# Tiruvaymoli

## First Centum

## 1.1 Uyarvara uyarnalam

## 1.1.1. Uyarvara uyarnalam

*uyarvaṟa uyarnalam udaiyavan yavan avan mayarvaṟa madinalam aruḷinan yavan avan ayarvaṟum amarargaḷ adipati yavan avan tuyaraṟu sudarodi toḻudeḷu en mananē*

**Пословный перевод:**

uyarvu – greatness (as explained in taittirīya upaniśat – ānandavalli); aṟa – non-existing; uyar – unexplainably high; nalam – that bliss; udaiyavan – being the one who has; yavanavan – one who is famously explained in authentic scriptures; mayarvu – ignorance (samsaya – doubt, viparyaya – error etc); aṟa – be destroyed; madinalam – true knowledge and devotion; aruḷinan – blessed (out of own mercy); yavanavan – one who is ancient; ayarvu – forgetting nature; aṟum – does not have; amarargaḷ – nityasūris who eternally enjoy bhagavān; adipati – infinite (uncallengable) master; yavan – one; avan – his; tuyaraṟu – removes the sufferings (of the dependants); sudar – eternal radiance; adi – to the divine feet; toḻudu – performing the act that fits a servant (as explained in baddānjali putā: – ones who are with folded hands); en mananē – oh my mind!; eḻu – rise and be uplifted

**Перевод:**

**Oh my mind! Bow down with folded hands at the lotus feet of emperumān and be uplifted. emperumān is the famous one highlighted in authentic scriptures  as one who has unexplainable greatness which makes all other greatness non-existing. He is the one who blessed me true knowledge and devotion, out of his unconditional grace that dispelled my ignorance completely. He is the indisputable master of the nityasūris who have no defects such as forgetful nature etc.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*nammāḻvār enjoys the most glorious bhagavān fully and out of great devotion caused by such experience, reveals his experience to others.*

[āḻvār](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/18/nammazhwar-english/) instructs his mind to engage in all types of kainkaryam at all places in all ways to [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) and be uplifted. [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is explained as having unlimited auspicious qualities such as bliss etc. He unconditionally and mercifully blessed [āḻvār](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/18/nammazhwar-english/) with divine blemiśless knowledge and triggered great devotion towards his lotus feet. [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is explained as the master of the infiinte divine souls in paramapadam such as ādi sēśan, viśvaksēnar, garudāḻvār et al who never fall from their position and already showering his mercy towards such nityasūris.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*bhagavān srīman nārāyaṇan who is opposite to all defects and the abode of all auspicious qualities, being the master of nityasūris (in paramapadam), out of his unconditional grace, blessed nammāḻvār with pristine knowledge and devotion towards him. Being blessed, nammāḻvār starts engaging in service of such bhagavān. Thus, at the beginning of the prabandam itself, (auspicious aspects such as ) the object of glorification and reverential bowing down are highlighted.*

- *uyarvaṟa uyarnalam udaiyavan* – Just like in the presence of Sun, the stars do not shine, in comparison to [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s glories, others’ glories do not shine at all.
- *madinalam* – bhaktirūpāpanna jñānam – knowledge enriched with devotion or knowledge matured into devotion.
- *amarargaḷ* – usage of plural indicates that there are infinite nityasūris.
- *tuyaraṟu sudaradi* – Is there agony for the lotus feet themselves? Yes – they consider the agony of the ones who are surrendered as their own and remove that agony.
- Why is [āḻvār](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/18/nammazhwar-english/) asking to worship the lotus feet instead of [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) himself? Just like a nursing child will look for the mother’s bosom, adiyavan (dāsa – servitor) will look for the lotus feet of the master.
- Many arguments such as “brahmam is sat only without any attributes” (auspicious qualities in the first line) and “the difference between [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) and [paramātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is artificial, on liberation they will become one” (master of nityasūris explained in the third line) are defeated easily and [āḻvār](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/18/nammazhwar-english/)‘s siddāntam \[philosophy\] is established.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*In this pāsuram, the summary of the first padigam (decad) is explained. In this first pāsuram, the existence of unlimited auspicious qualities, unconditional mercy, controlling the nityasūris and having eternal auspicious forms – all of which reveal the supremacy of emperumān, are revealed. Having said so, nammāḻvār directs his heart to always serve such emperumān.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*Very similar to nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

This reflects [nampiḷḷai](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/09/16/nampillai-english/)‘s vyākhyānam mostly.

- *amararagaḷ* – ones who are immortal. For them death means separation from [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) – there is no other death for them.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*nammāḻvār first highlights the 3 main favours which are done by emperumān towards him. First emperumān favoured āḻvār by showing his true nature of being filled with auspicious qualities. Then, even though āḻvār did not have anything on his side,  emperumān blessed him with divine knowledge and devotion towards him out of his causeless mercy. Then he showed that he is the master of nityasūris. Being favoured like this, āḻvār directs his heart to come and serve him eternally. āḻvār asks his heart to bow down to bhagavān to be uplifted. When a river starts flooding nearby fields, the trees which stay still will be uprooted while the plants etc., which bend and tackle the flood, will survive. In the same way, after understanding the glories of bhagavān, if one bows down in front of him, he will be uplifted. Just like lakśmaṇa said he is overwhelmed with srī rāma’s auspicious qualities and became a servant to him, āḻvār also reveals his attachment towards emperumān and thus becoming a servant to him. Since, bhagavān showed his auspicious qualities to āḻvār to win him, over āḻvār too engages in glorifiying bhagavān‘s auspicious qualities right in the beginning. உயர்வற உயர் நலம் உடையவன் யவனவன் மயர்வற மதி நலம் அருளினன் யவனவன் அயர்வறும் அமரர்கள் அதிபதி யவனவன் துயரறு சுடரடி தொழுதெழென் மனனே. uyarvaṟa uyarnalam udaiyavan yavan avan mayarvaṟa madinalam aruḷinan yavan avan ayarvaṟum amarargaḷ adipati yavan avan tuyaraṟu sudarodi toḻudeḷu en mananē*

- *uyaravaṟa uyarnalam* – When taittirīya upaniśat started enjoying [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s auspicious qualities, it could not even fully enjoy a single quality named “ānandam” (bliss) and declared “*yatō vācō nivartantē*“. Each quality of [emperumān](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/17/divya-dhampathi/) is infinitely great. āḷavandār explains that [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s greatness over all other entities is clearly explained here.
- *udaiyavan* – These qualities are natural for [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) instead of being accidental (acquired). [kūrattāḻvān](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2013/10/05/kurathazhwan/) explains to piḷḷai piḷḷai āḻvān that [āḻvār](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/18/nammazhwar-english/) establishes [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s auspicious qualities right upfront and easily defeats the ones who claim he is nirguṇam (without any qualities – according to them).
- *yavan* – that most famous and established personality. The personality on whom these auspicious qualities are naturally and fittingly visible. This means [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) by nature is great and does not depend on his qualities to prove his greatness. On the other hand, this also means that [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) who is with such great auspicious qualities.
- *mayarvaṟa* – removing the ajñānam (ignorance) completely. ajñānam is of 3 categories
   - jñāna anudaya (no knowledge at all) –  dēhātma abhimānam – considering body as the soul. This means, there is no knowledge about [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) and considering the body itself as everything.
   - anyatā jñānam – dēvatāntara sēśatvam – considering oneself as servitor of other dēvatās such as brahmā, rudran, indran et al.
   - viparīda jñānam – svātantriyam (considering oneself as independant) and svabhōjñam (considering oneself as the enjoyer) like kēvalan (one who desires kaivalya mōkśam).
- *madinalam* – some explain this as jñānam and bhakti. But [bhattar](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/09/11/parasara-bhattar/) explains this as jñānam enriched with bhakti (jñānam matured as bhakti). This bhakti was blessed by [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) himself and it induces kainkaryam to [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/). When some ask [embār](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/09/07/embar/) if [āḻvār](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/18/nammazhwar-english/) was a prapanna or bhakti yōga niśta, he replies “[āḻvār](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/18/nammazhwar-english/) is a prapanna; but performs bhakti to spend his time in this world”.
- *aruḷinan* – Being blessed by [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) unconditionally, āḻvār considers himself as [asat](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/09/thathva-thrayam-achith-what-is-matter/) (insentient) before being blessed.
- *ayarvaṟum …* – One who has a whole realm (parampadam) filled with devotees who cannot sustain themselves without bhagavān’s mercy. nityasūris are those who have no forgetfulness by the grace of bhagavān; muktātmās are those who were in samsāra before with forgetfulness but subsequently got relieved of the same during liberation, by the grace of bhagavān.
- *amarargaḷ* – the residents of paramapadam who cannot bear separation from [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/). All of them look similar to [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) – only in the grand assembly and by seeing his divine consorts and divine ornaments like srī kaustubam can bhagavān be easily identified.
- *adipati* – Though there are some similarities,  he is completely greater than they.
- *tuyaraṟu* – Previously ācāryas explained this as “*tuyaraṟukkum*” (that which dispels the agony of others). [emperumānār](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/09/06/emperumanar/) explained this as “*tuyaraṟu sudaradi*” (the lotus feet which dispel the agony of [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)). As explained in srī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 2.42 “*vyasanēśu ca manuśyāṇām brusam bhavati dukkita:*” (when his subjects suffered, srī rāma felt more agony than themselves) [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) was in pain seeing [āḻvār](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/18/nammazhwar-english/)‘s sufferings before, but seeing he has been blessed, his agony is dispelled.
- *toḻudu* – engaging in the devotional activity which is natural for the [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) considering the time lost in this samsāram since time immemorial.
- *eḻu* – rise and be uplifted. From the state of “*asannēva sa bhavati*” (taittirīya upaniśat ānandavalli – he is not even considered to be existing when he considers brahmam to be not existing), he became “*santamēnam tatō vidu:*” (taittirīya upaniśat ānandavalli  – others know him to be existing when he knows brahmam to be existing).
- *en mananē* – now only [āḻvār](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/18/nammazhwar-english/) is seeing himself. He relishes his relationship with his mind now having been blessed by [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/). As explained in srīviṣṇu purāṇam 6.7.28 “*mana Eva manuśyāṇām kāraṇam bandamōkśayō:” (*For a man, his mind is the cause for both attachment to this world and liberation from this world).
- Ones who claim that [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) does not have guṇam (qualities), vigraham (form), vibhūti (wealth) are all defeated in this pāsuram itself. One need not explain the opponents case and defeat it. If ones own philosophy is explained clearly, that will easily defeat the opponents philosophy.
- arta pancakam is explained in this pāsuram.
   - prāpyam – “[bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)” is explained by “*uyarvaṟa uyarnalam udaiyavan – ayaravaṟum amarargaḷ adipati*“
   - [virōdi](http://ponnadi.blogspot.in/p/virodhi-pariharangal.html) – “ignorance being dispelled” is explained by “*mayarvaṟa*“
   - sādanam (upāyam) – “[bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is the means” is explained by “*aruḷinan”*
   - palam (upēyam) – “kainkaryam is the goal” is explained by “*toḻudu eḻu*“
   - [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) – “the pure soul who is the qualified person to pursue the goal” is explained by “*en mananē*“

In the next article we will the next pāsuram.

adiyen saraty ramanuja dasan

## 1.1.2. Mananagamalamara

*mananagamalam aṟa malar misaiyeḻudarum mananuṇarvu aḷavilan poṟiyuṇarvu avaiyilan inanuṇar muḻunalam edir nigaḻ kaḻivinum inanilan enan uyir migu narai ilanē*

**Пословный перевод:**

mananagam – in the mind; malam – blemishes such as kāmam (lust), krōdam (anger) etc; aṟa – being removed; malar – being blossomed; misai – up; eḻudarum – rise and grow; manan uṇarvu – jñānam which is felt in the heart/mind through the practice of yōga; aḷavilan – immeasurable and thus distinct from cit (jīvatmā); poṟiyuṇarvu avaiyilan – distinct from acit (matter) which is experienced/understood through the external senses; inan – thus being different from cit and acit; uṇar muḻunalam – Identified with being full knowledge and full bliss; edir – in the future; nigaḻ – in the present; kaḻivinum – in the past; inanilan migunaraiyilan – having none who is equal to or higher than; enanuyir – my sustaining soul

**Перевод:**

**bhagavān is immeasurable by even well-blossomed mind which is free of blemishes such as kāmam, krōdam etc., that can understand the ātmā. He is immeasurable by the external senses which are used to comprehend acit (matter). Thus he is distinct from both cit and acit. He is identified as being full knowledge and full bliss and has none who is equal to or higher than him, in the past, present or future. He is my sustaining soul.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*The most distinct nature of bhagavān‘s svarūpam (true nature) which is the abode of the previously mentioned  auspicious qualities is explained in this pāsuram. Such bhagavat svarūpam is explained as the opposite of all blemishes and the abode of all auspiciousness.*

Very similar to the simple translation. [āḻvār](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/18/nammazhwar-english/) says to his mind that such [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) should be vorśipped (linking this with the last line of the 1st pāsuram).

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*Very similar to piḷḷān‘s introduction. Such bhagavān‘s svarūpam is explained in a step-by-step manner.*

- When it is sufficient to say that [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is different from all [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)s, why is it necessary to establish that he is different from [acit (matter)](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/09/thathva-thrayam-achith-what-is-matter/)? This is to establish that – looking at him, it is irrelevant whether it is [cit (sentients)](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) or [acit (insentients)](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/09/thathva-thrayam-achith-what-is-matter/) – none can match him.
- It is already explained that [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is distinct from (greater than) everyone/ everything. What is the need for saying that there is none equal/higher than him in past / present / future? This is to expain that no one is even qualified to be compared with him (let alone be compared).

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Next, nammāḻvār speaks about bhagavān (who is explained as “yavan” in previous pāsuram) being distinct from all other entities.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*Previously, bhagavān who is explained as “yavan” is further elaborated as distinct from all other entities and is made of jñānam (knowledge) and ānandam (bliss). This is explained in a step-by-step manner.*

This reflects [nampiḷḷai](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/09/16/nampillai-english/)‘s vyākhyānam mostly.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*bhagavān can be explained by explaining the result (this universe) first and then explaining the cause like it is done in taittirīya upaniśat “yatō vā imāni…“. He can also be explained by explaining his svarūpam first and then his wealth, etc. But āḻvār chooses to explain the auspicious qualities first and then bhagavān‘s svarūpam subsequently. This is because bhagavān attracted āḻvār by revealing his qualities to him. Thus āḻvār spoke about his qualities first. He simply stated the glorious nature of bhagavat svarūpam which is the abode of such qualities using the term “avan”. Here, he enjoys that svarūpam being most distinct due to his being distinct from all cētanam (sentients) and acētanam (insentients) as he is opposite of all blemishes/defects and the abode of all auspiciousness. மனனக மலமற மலர்மிசை யெழுதரும் மனனுணர் வளவிலன், பொறியுணர் வவையிலன் இனனுணர், முழுநலம், எதிர்நிகழ் கழிவினும் இனனிலன், னெனனுயிர், மிகு நரை யிலனே. mananagamalam aṟa malar misaiyeḻudarum mananuṇarvu aḷavilan poṟiyuṇarvu avaiyilan inanuṇar muḻunalam edir nigaḻ kaḻivinum inanilan enan uyir migu narai ilanē*

- *mananagam…* – nampiḷḷai questions the need for explaining about [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) in detail. This is [āḻvār](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/18/nammazhwar-english/)‘s real experience of his own self/heart being most purified (by [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s mercy).
- *malamaṟa* – blemishes in the heart/mind are avidyā etc. kāmam (lust), krōdam (anger), lōbam (desire for material aspects), harśa (happiness), mānamatā guṇā: (ahankāram, pride and lack of good qualities), viśādam (sorrow) are the eight defects for the mind. But since ātmā is eternal and is fully knovledgable naturally, these defects are not natural for the mind (since mind also gets subdued during praḷaya). Thus by following yōga sāstram, removing the detachment from external worldly pleasures and turning it inwards towards the ātmā, these defects can be removed.
- Here the mind is explained as the tool through which ātmā can be understood. But one may question, just like gold and charcoal may be different, they can be perceived by the same senses, why can’t [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) be perceived by mind which perceives ātmā? That cannot be applied here due to the infinite greatness of [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/). But then, why is it said that “…manasā tu visuddēna” (such [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is perceived by the pure mind)? In other words, [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) can be understood that he is supreme/great – but he cannot be fully understood as he is, due to his infinite greatness.
- *uṇarmuḻunalam –* fully made of knowledge and bliss. As explained in bruhadāraṇyaka upaniśat “*yatā saindavagana:*” (like a salt crystal is filled with salt, [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is filled with knowledge). taittirīya upaniśat says “*ānandō brahma*” (brahmam is bliss) and “*ānanda maya:*” (pervaded by ānandam). One can attempt to understand him through examples – even through those examples, he cannot be fully comprehended.
- *inanilan* – bhattar highlights that “*First* [*āḻvār*](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/18/nammazhwar-english/) *says that there is no sādarmya drustāntam, here he says that there is no vaidarmya drustāntam*“. That means first it is explained that [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) cannot be compared to [cit](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) and [acit](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/09/thathva-thrayam-achith-what-is-matter/). Here it is said that there is no one who is even qualified to be compared to [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/). kāncīpuram PB aṇṇangarācāryar svamy gives a nice example for this in his divyārta dīpikai. He says if some one says “A caṇḍāḷa (dog-eater) cannot be compared to vasiśta (famous sage)”, learned persons will say “No! dont say that”. That does not mean that they are comparable. It simply means that caṇḍāḷa is not even qualified to be compared to vasiśta.
- *enanuyir –* Such [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is my sustenance. Just as it is said in bruhadāraṇyaka upaniśat “*yasya ātmā sarīram*” ([bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is antaryāmi for the ātmā and the ātmā is the sarīram – body). [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is the dāraka (bearer) and ātmā is the dārya (held by [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)).
- *migunaraiyilanē* – Just like his being the antaryāmi and bearing/controlling the [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)s, there is no one else who is his antaryāmi and greater than him. This is explained in svētāsvatara upaniśat “*na tatsamasca abhyadikasca drusyatē*” (No one equal to or higher than that [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is seen).

In the next article we will the next pāsuram.

## 1.1.3. Ilanatu udaiyanitu

*ilanadu udaiyanidu ena ninaivu ariyavan nilanidai visumbidai uruvinan aruvinan pulanodu pulanalan oḻivilan paranda an nalanudai oruvanai naṇuginam nāmē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ilanadu – not owning because of being far-away from an object; udaiyanidu – owning because of being close to an object; ena – thus limiting by certain objects; ninaivu aṟiyavan – cannot be understood; nilanidai – in the earth; visumbidai – in the sky and higher realms; uruvinan aruvinan – having acit (insentients) which are visible to eyes (and other external senses) and having cit (sentients) which are not visible to eyes (and other external senses) as prakāram (attribute, body); pulanodu – existing amidst such cit and acit which are well established through pramāṇam (authentic source); pulanalan – not having their nature; oḻivilan paranda – pervading everywhere without missing out on any object/place; annalanudai – one having auspicious qualities as explained in first pāsuram; oruvanai – that most distinct person; nām naṇuginam – we are blessed to be able to approach him

**Перевод:**

**Simple transalation (based on vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar‘s 12000 padi)**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*In this pāsuram, the material realm which is fully owned/controlled by bhagavān who is distinct from all other entities is explained.*

We are fortunate to receive the shelter of [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) who is the master of everything/everyone, who is the in-dwelling soul of entire existence, one who is not touched by the defects of [cit](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) and [acit](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/09/thathva-thrayam-achith-what-is-matter/), who is having full control over everything being the in-dwelling soul and who is distinct from everything else that exists. āḻvār tells his mind to worship such [emperumān](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/17/divya-dhampathi/) and be uplifted.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In this pāsuram, the material realm which is present for the sport of bhagavān who was explained in the first pāsuram as the master of nitya vibhūti (paramapadam – spiritual realm) is explained.*

Very similar to [nampiḷḷai](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/09/16/nampillai-english/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*nammāḻvār explains bhagavān‘s connection with material realm to establish that he is not limited by any particular object or location.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*Same as nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

Very similar to [nampiḷḷai](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/09/16/nampillai-english/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*nammāḻvār enjoyed bhagavān‘s auspicious qualities, bhagavān‘s control over spiritual realm and his divine form (lotus feet) in the first pāsuram. In the second pāsuram, he explained the true nature of bhagavān being totally distinct from cit and acit. In continuing with that, he is explaining the material realm which is also belonging to bhagavān. Though cāndōjña upaniśat declares “nōpajanam smarannidam sarīram” (a muktātmā, after being liberated, will never contemplate about this material realm since he will be fully engaged in blissful activities in spiritual realm), muktātmās would still relish material realm as something that exists for the sport of bhagavān. āḻvār too, even though being present in this realm only, since he is blessed by bhagavān himself with blemiśless knowledge, relishes this world as the wealth of bhagavān. Just like a king and his wife may be engaged in making a garden and destroying it playfully even though they may have huge wealth (lands, palaces, etc), when srīman nārāyaṇan and srī mahālakśmi glance with their divine vision this material realm becomes manifested and when they glance away, the material realm becomes subtle. āḻvār is enjoying such material realm in this pāsuram. இலனது உடையனி தென நினைவரியவன் நிலனிடை விசும்பிடை உருவினன் அருவினன் புலனொடு புலனலன், ஒழிவிலன், பரந்த அந் நலனுடை யொருவனை நணுகினம் நாமே. ilanadu udaiyanidu ena ninaivu ariyavan nilanidai visumbidai uruvinan aruvinan pulanodu pulanalan oḻivilan paranda an nalanudai oruvanai naṇuginam nāmē*

- *ilanatu udaiyanatu en ninaivariyavan* – It is easy to understand when it is said that “[bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) cannot be be explained as not having/owning this object” since he owns everything. But why can we not say “[bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) cannot be explained as having/owning this object”? If we said “x person has this”, then immediately a thought may arise “x person may not have this other thing” –  to avoid such confusion [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) cannot be explained as having one particular object. Either way, one may misunderstand the vastness (infinite nature) of [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s wealth.
- *nilanidai visumbidai …* – Then how do we explain his wealth? It has to be done as done in sāstram – nārāyaṇa sūktam says “*patim visvasya*” (he is the owner of the entire existence). “nilan” (earth) indicates regions down to pātāḷam (lowest in a particular aṇḍam – universe) and “visumbu” (sky) indicates regions up to the border of paramapadam.
- *uruvinan aruvinan* – Does “inan” in tamḻ mean ownership? Yes, as explained in tiruvāimoḻi 9.3.1 “*kārāyina kāḷananmēniyinan*” ([bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) has cloud-like beautiful dark-hued body), “*inan*” will indicate ownership.
- *pulanodu* – Would such [emperumān](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/17/divya-dhampathi/) just stay in paramapadam enjoying endless bliss? No, he will exist inside everyone and protect everyone as the in-dwelling soul. He performs creation (subtle to gross manifestation), enters into all manifested matter through [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)s and thus is present as the in-dwelling soul of everything that is manifested.
- *pulanalan* – If he exists with them, will he be affected by the defects of [acit](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/09/thathva-thrayam-achith-what-is-matter/) (like complete transformation of state) and [cit](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) (like having joy and happiness based on karmā)? No, this principle is explained in rig vēdam “*dvā suparṇā sayujā sakhāyā samānam vrukśam pariśasvajātē \| tayōranya: pippalam svādvatti anaśnannanyō abicākasīti \|\|*” (There are two related (servant and master) birds ([jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) and paramātmā) residing in a tree (body). One bird ([jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)) enjoys the fruits of its actions (karmā) and the other one (paramātmā) being detached is radiantly witnessing that).
- *naṇuginam* – Not just being blessed by [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) with blemiśless knowledge, I have also taken shelter of him.
- *nāmē* – Instead of saying “nām”, āḻvār is saying “nāmē!” with exclamation. āḻvār doubts if he has really taken shelter of [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/). Considering how materialistic he was before being blessed by [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/), he cannot believe his fortune. When sītā pirātti was in agony in asōka vanam at lankā, she saw hanuman singing the glories of srī rāma and became very confused and could not believe what was happening. She questioned herself if it was her own bewilderment or madness or is this a wicked dream (srī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇṭam 34.23). Before, āḻvār was thinking “īsvarōham” – aham should lead up to [īsvara](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/), but āḻvār was considering his body as [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)/[īsvara](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) before being blessed by [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) with blemiśless knowledge. When bharadāḻvān went looking for srīrāma to srī bharadvāja riśi’s āsram, he was thinking himself “Am I truly entering the āsram here to see srī rāma? I am the most unfortunate person to have been called “Oh! king” by kaikēyi when srī rāma was the real king and was doubted by guhap perumāḷ that I was coming to hurt srī rāma further. How is this happening?”

In the next article we will the next pāsuram.

## 1.1.4. Nam avan

*nām avan ivan uvan avaḷ ivaḷ uvaḷ evḷ tām avar ivar uvar atu itu utu edu vīm avai ivai uvai avai nalam tīngu avai ām avai āy avai āy ninṟa avarē*

**Пословный перевод:**

nām – self (which is going to be the context for the other words to follow); avan – a male who is far away; ivan – a male who is nearby; uvan – a male who is neither far away nor nearby; avaḷ – a female who is far away; ivaḷ – a female who is nearby; uvaḷ – a female who is neither far away nor nearby; evaḷ – (being questioned as) which female?; tām – respectable person (first person – in front of us); avar – a respectable person who is far away; ivar – a respectable person who is nearby; uvar – a respectable person who is neither far away nor nearby; adu – an animal/bird/insentient that is far away; idu – an animal/bird/insentient that is neaby; udu – an animal/bird/insentient that is neither far away nor nearby; edu – (being questioned as) which animal/bird/insentient?; vīmavai – temporary objects that are subject to change; ivai uvai avai – such temporary objects which are nearby, neither far away nor nearby, far away; nalam tīngu avai – those virtuous and lowly actions/aspects; āmavai – future aspects; āyavai – all such (past) objects; āy ninṟa avar – one has become such objects

**Перевод:**

**bhagavān is the one who has become (is the antaryāmi of) all entities (male, female, insentient, temporary ones) which are identified by different words to indicate their proximity (nearby, faraway, in-between etc) which are good or bad and which existed in the past, exist now or will come to existence in the future.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*Starting with this pāsuram, the previous pāsuram is explained in detail.*

This pāsuram explains that [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) controls all entities that are referred by different words.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*It is explained that the svarūpam (true nature) and svabhāvam (characteristics) of different entities which are identified through different words are completely under the control of bhagavān according to sāmānādikaraṇyam.*

Very similar to [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2013/03/22/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar-english/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*In the next 3 pāsurams (starting with this one), the svarūpam (true nature), stiti (existence), pravrutti (actions) etc of the entities in this leelā vibhūti are explained as being totally controlled by bhagavān. In this pāsuram, nammāḻvār explains that the svarūpam of all the entities are explained as being totally controlled by bhagavān through sāmānādikaraṇyam.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*Very similar to vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar‘s introduction.*

Very similar to [nampiḷḷai](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/09/16/nampillai-english/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*In the previous pāsuram, āḻvār enjoyed bhagavān‘s wealth of leelā vibhūti. While only few pāsurams explained nitya vibhūti, why are there many pāsurams explaining leelā vibhūti? nitya vibhūti (paramapadam) fully follows bhagavān‘s heart as explained in tiruvāimoḻi 4.9.10 “oṇḍodiyāḷ tirumagaḷum nīyumē nilāniṟpa” (Only srīmahālakśmi and you are visible in parampadam – meaning others are so submissive and subdued in service to the two of you). So there is nothing special in saying that everything is under his full control there. But in this leelā vibhūti, jīvātmās acquire bodies according to their karmā and follow the will of bhagavān according to the circumstances here. Only in this vibhūti we see anya sēśatvam (being dependant on other dēvatās), sva svātantriyam (being fully independent) etc . Thus it is more important to establish that leelā vibhūti is under full control of bhagavān. In the next 3 pāsurams (starting with this),  the nature, characteristics and actions are established as being fully controlled by bhagavān. In the subsequent (7th) pāsuram the sarīra – ātma (sarīri) bhāvam between the universe and īsvara is explained. In the subsequent (8th) pāsuram kudruśtis (those who dont accept vēdam as authority) are defeated. In the 9th pāsuram, sūnyavādi (philosopher of voidness) is defeated. In the 10th pāsuram, his all-pervading nature is explained. In the 11th pāsuram, the fruits of reciting the decad are explained. In this pāsuram, sruśti (creation), aṇu pravēsam (all-pervading nature) etc are explained as fully dependent on bhagavān both in subtle (cause) and gross (effect) states. நாம் அவன் இவன் உவன் அவள் இவள் உவள் எவள் தாம் அவர் இவர் உவர் அது இது உது எது வீம் அவை இவை உவை அவை நலம் தீங்கு இவை ஆம் அவை ஆய் அவை ஆய் நின்ற அவரே nām avan ivan uvan avaḷ ivaḷ uvaḷ evḷ tām avar ivar uvar atu itu utu edu vīm avai ivai uvai avai nalam tīngu avai Am avai āy avai āy ninṟa avarē*

- *āmavai āyavai* – all past and future aspects. When past and future are explained, that includes present as well.
- *āyninṟa* – those entities that exist. When these entities are considered as they are, aikyam (sameness/oneness) can not be explained (since each entity is distinct naturally).
- Any word (relating to matter) represents three aspects – the [acit (insentient/body)](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/09/thathva-thrayam-achith-what-is-matter/), [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) who is the abhimāni of that [acit](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/09/thathva-thrayam-achith-what-is-matter/) (the [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) who controls that [acit](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/09/thathva-thrayam-achith-what-is-matter/)) and [paramātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) who is the antaryāmi (in-dwelling soul) of that [jīvatmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/). (For example, when we say “sheep” – that indicates the sheep’s [body](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/09/thathva-thrayam-achith-what-is-matter/), the [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) inside the sheep’s [body](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/09/thathva-thrayam-achith-what-is-matter/) which control’s the [body](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/09/thathva-thrayam-achith-what-is-matter/) and finally the [paramātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) which controls that [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/). It is explained by [emperumānār](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/09/06/emperumanar/) in vēdārtta sangraham that one who is not learned in vēdāntam will only see the sheep’s body but the learned ones will see all 3 entities through that word).
- This pāsuram reflects the same meaning of cāndōjña upaniśat vākyam (statement) “*idam sarvam brahma kalu*” (isn’t this all [brahmam](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)?) and “*tatvamasi*” (that [brahmam](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) which has the entire universe as its body is the same [brahmam](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) that has you ([ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)) as its body as well). Here the real meaning of tatvamasi is beautifully explained. In the [first pāsuram](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/?p=1903), [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s auspicious qualities, being in the spiritual realm and having divine form were explained. In the [second pāsuram](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/?p=1969), his glorious nature was explained. “*tat*” in “*tatvamasi*” refers to previously explained [brahmam](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) with such great qualities which is explained by the “*avar*” (respectable him) at the end of this pāsuram. “*āy ninṟa*” explains [paramātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) which exists along with the [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)s and [acit (matter)](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/09/thathva-thrayam-achith-what-is-matter/). Thus, oneness of [brahmam](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) and [cit](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)/[acit](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/09/thathva-thrayam-achith-what-is-matter/) is explained through sāmānadikaraṇyam – that the same [brahmam](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is the substratum for all [cit](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) and [acit](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/09/thathva-thrayam-achith-what-is-matter/).
- Thus, by expressly identifying all types of entities in relation to [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/), their true nature being fully controlled by [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is established in this pāsuram.

In the next article we will the next pāsuram.

## 1.1.5. Avaravar tamatamatu

*avaravar tamadamadu aṟivaṟi vagai vagai avaravar iṟaiyavar enavadi adaivargaḷ avaravar iṟaiyavar kuṟaivilar iṟaiyavar avaravar vidi vaḻi adaiya ninṟanarē*

**Пословный перевод:**

avaravar – those adikāris (qualified persons who are interested in certain goals); tamadamadu – their; aṟivaṟi vagaivagai – different levels/varieties of knowledge; avaravar – those dēvatās according to their desire; iṟaiyavar ena – assumed as the master who will fulfil their desires; adi adaivargaḷ – approach, take shelter; avaravar – those dēvatās; iṟaiyavar – being the master who fulfils such desires; kuṟaivilar – appropriate; iṟaiyavar – being sarva svāmy (supreme lord); avaravar – such adikāris; vidi vaḻi – per vidi (karmā/fate); adaiya – attaining the goal; ninṟanar – situated as the antarātmā

**Перевод:**

**Simple transalation (based on vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar‘s 12000 padi)**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*It is explained that bhagavān is the object of all vorśippable aspects.*

Persons worship indra et al through jyōtiśtōmam etc, according to their jñānam considering them as their benefactor. Those dēvatās are quite capable of fulfilling the desires of such persons who worship them as applicable for such worship. How is this possible? By following the principles of sāstram, if a dēvatā is worshiped, [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) being the antaryāmi of that dēvatā, facilitates the fulfillment of such results as he is the real object of worship.

Many pramāṇams  from bhagavat gītā etc., are highlighted to establish this principle. Since [emperumān](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/17/divya-dhampathi/), being the antarātmā of everything, is the true object of worship and the true benefactor of all fruits, protecting everything is also under his full disposal.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*It is explained that everything is sustained by emperumān.*

Very similar to [nampiḷḷai](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/09/16/nampillai-english/)‘s vyākhyānam.

*avaravar* is explained as individuals who are different based on their guṇam (quality) of satvam (goodness), rajas (passion) and tamas (ignorance).

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, emperumān sustaining everything in the form of protection is explained through vaiyadikaraṇyam (that he is the one who is related to all different entities).*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*Sustenance (of everything) is also under the disposal of bhagavān through vaiyadikaraṇyam.*

Very similar to [nampiḷḷai](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/09/16/nampillai-english/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*nammāḻvār says stiti (sustenance) is also under emperumān‘s disposal Just like the true nature is (explained in previous pāsuram). A person may control a house. Another person may control a village. Another may control a crowd. Another person (indra) may control 3 worlds (bhūr, bhūva:, suva:). Another person (brahmā) may control 14 worlds (from brahma lōkam to pātāḷa lōkam). Irrespective of the person protecting a house or the 14 worlds, it is because of bhagavān being the antarātmā (in-dwelling soul) that they are able to protect and they get protected. Without his presence, no one will have the independant ability to control/protect anything. This is explained in viṣṇu purāṇam “nahi pālanasāmartyam rutē sarvēsvaram harim”  (Other than the supreme lord hari, no one has the (natural) ability to protect others). As explained in taittirīya upaniśat “yadvēdādau svara: prōktō vēdāntē ca pratiśtita:” – whatever is created from bhagavān during sruśti (creation) will settle back into bhagavān himself during layam (devolution), just like jewels are taken out of a jewel box, worn and then placed back in the jewel box. That praṇavam, which has akāram as the first letter indicates bhagavān as the rakśaka (protector). That bhagavān is the sarvēsvaran – supreme lord. அவரவர் தமதமது அறிவறி வகை வகை அவரவர் இறையவர் எனவடி அடைவர்கள் அவரவர் இறையவர் குறைவிலர் இறையவர் அவரவர் விதி வழி அடைய நின்றனரே avaravar tamadamadu aṟivaṟi vagai vagai avaravar iṟaiyavar enavadi adaivargaḷ avaravar iṟaiyavar kuṟaivilar iṟaiyavar avaravar vidi vaḻi adaiya ninṟanarē*

- *avaravar* – In tamiḻ “*avaravar*” when casually said indicates “someone” (that means, not so important persons). nampiḷḷai explains that [āḻvār](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/18/nammazhwar-english/) does not give much importance to such vorśippers of other dēvatās. It also indicates different types of persons.
- *tamadamadu* – their goals which are different based on their quality (satvam, rajas, tamas).
- *aṟivaṟi* – the jñānam (knowledge) which leads to such goals.
- *vagaivagai* – due to the different types of desires, they may pursue different types of means to attain the goal
- Based on the guṇam, one has ruci (taste/desire) for the goals and such desire will lead to the particular means to attain such goals.  An individual may be filled with rajō guṇam (passion) or with tamō guṇam (ignorance, lethargy, etc) or misra satvam (tainted satvam – since sudda satvam is very rare to see) – so their jñānam will also be in the same mode.
- *avaravar iṟaiyavar ena adi adivargaḷ* – Those dēvatās are very difficult to worship and please. In some cases, they (rudra) insisted to their devotees to kill their own son and bring the flesh, (skandan) insisted his devotee to bring the flesh of a goat etc. But to please [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/), just an anjali (namaskāram – folded hands) is sufficient as explained in bharatvāja samhitai “*anjali: paramā mudrā kśipiram dēvaprasādinī*” (anjali is the ultimate act which induces the blessings of [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)). [nammāḻvār](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/18/nammazhwar-english/) says “*adi adaivargaḷ*” (will take shelter of lotus feet) as he is used to that in his group (of [āḻvārs](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/azhwars/)). When sugrīva did not help srī rāma and lakśmaṇa as promised, lakśmaṇa came and gave a huge roar and created fear in the hearts of sugrīva. On hearing that sugrīva asked hanumān what to do and hanumān said just perform an anjali and that will please lakśmaṇa (and srī rāma too).
- *avaravar iṟaiyavar kuṟaivilar* – the ones who are worshiping are doing according to their nature and the ones who are worshiped are being the benefactor according to their nature – everything is appropriate according to their situation.
- *iṟaiyavar* – Since [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is the supreme god for the vorśippers, the dēvatās and [nammāḻvār](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/18/nammazhwar-english/) himself as explained in nārāyaṇa sūktam “*patim visvasya*” (master of everyone).
- As explained in bhagavat gītā by [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) himself, whoever worships other dēvatās with bhakti will reach such dēvatā and get his/her desires fulfilled.
- When a son gets angry with his mother and leaves home, the mother will try to help him through others. Similarly, when jīvātmās are not mature enough to worship [srīman nārāyaṇan](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/17/divya-dhampathi/) directly, emperumān will help them through the dēvatās whom he has himself appointed. It is because of his existence that jīvātmās are able to approach such dēvatās and such dēvatās are able to protect them. If he does not allow that, these dēvatās are as good as a scarecrow which stands protecting the fields.

In the next article we will see the next pāsuram.

## 1.1.6. Ninranar irundanar

*ninṟanar irundanar kidandanar tirindanar ninṟilar irundilar kidandilar tirindilar enṟumoriyalvinar ena ninaivariyavar enṟumoriyalvodu ninṟa em tidarē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ninṟanar irundanar kidandanar tirindanar – entities which are the abode of the actions of standing, sitting, lying down and walking (are under the full control of emperumān); ninṟilar irundilar kidandilar tirindilar – entities which are the abode of the inaction (not standing, not sitting, not lying down, not walking) (are under the full control of emperumān); enṟum – always; oru iyalvinar – having such quality; ena – as; ninaivu ariyavar – inconceivable; enṟum – always; oru iyalvodu ninṟa – being distinct from all other entities; em tidar – our lord who is firmly established by sāstram (which is the strongest and most authentic evidence)

**Перевод:**

**Simple transalation (based on vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar‘s 12000 padi)**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

This pāsuram explains that the actions and inaction of all [cit (sentients)](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) and [acit (insentients)](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/09/thathva-thrayam-achith-what-is-matter/) are under the adīnam (control) of bhagavat sankalpam (divine will of [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)).

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*This pāsuram explains that the actions and inaction of all cit (sentients) and acit (insentients) are under the adīnam (control) of bhagavat sankalpam (divine will of bhagavān).*

- Since [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) has many prakārams (attributes/aspects), he cannot be limited to any one attribute/aspect.
- “*em*” emphasises personal favour received by āḻvār from [emperumān](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/17/divya-dhampathi/).

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*nammāḻvār explains that all actions/inaction are under bhagavān‘s control through sāmānādikaraṇyam.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*Same as vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar‘s introduction*

Similar to [nampiḷḷai](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/09/16/nampillai-english/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*nammāḻvār  explained previously that the sustenance of leelā vibhūti is under the control of bhagavān. In this pāsuram, he explains that leelā vibhūti’s pravrutti (actions) and nivrutti (inaction) are working under the divine will of bhagavān. நின்றனர் இருந்தனர் கிடந்தனர் திரிந்தனர்\* நின்றிலர் இருந்திலர் கிடந்திலர் திரிந்திலர்\* என்றுமோரியல்வினர் என நினைவரியவர்\* என்றுமோரியல்வொடு நின்ற எம் திடரே ninṟanar irundanar kidandanar tirindanar ninṟilar irundilar kidandilar tirindilar enṟumoriyalvinar ena ninaivariyavar enṟumoriyalvodu ninṟa em tidarē*

- Though ninṟanar (one who is standing) etc., are identified instead of niṟṟal (the action of standing) etc., this pāsuram is focussed on establishing that the actions (and inaction) of everyone are under the control of [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) since the individual entities themselves are under the control of [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) has been previously established. An example is cited for this aspect from yajur vēdam. “*aruṇayā pingākśayā sōmam krīṇāti*” (Purchase sōma plant by giving red colored cow with golden eyes). Already it is explained in other places that cow should be given in exchange for sōma plant. So, the important aspect is red color and golden eyes. Similarly, since the all sentient/insentient entities being under full control of [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) has already been explained, the focus is on the actions/inaction of such entities. But if we take this example, sāmānādikaraṇyam cannot be explained. So, in this case, it is explained that standing etc are the aspects of jīvātmā and that jīvātmā is fully dependent on [paramātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/). Thus, all actions/inaction are under the full control of [paramātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)/[bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/).
- *ninṟilar* … – When some one asks [embār](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/09/07/embar/) “It is understandable that one’s actions are dependent on [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/). But does inaction depend on [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)?” [embār](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/09/07/embar/) replies “When trisangu was pushed down from svargam, visvāmitra stopped him from falling. So, even for negating an action, unless [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s will is there, that will not happen”.
- *enṟumoriyalvinar ena ninaivu ariyavar* – Even if one keeps on trying as long as time exists (eternally) he cannot comprehend the true nature/attributes of [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/).
- *em tidar* – [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is emphasised greatly in vēdam which is most authentic due to its being apauruśēyam (Note: apauruśēyam means not written by any person – not even by [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) himself. [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) only reveals the eternal vēdam time and again).

In the next article we will see the next pāsuram.

## 1.1.7. Tidavisumbu erivali

*tidavisumbu eri vaḷi nīr nilam ivai misai padarporuḷ muḻuvadumāy avai avai toṟum udanmisai uyir enak karandengum paranduḷan sudarmigu surudiyuḷ ivai uṇḍa suranē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tidam – druda (more established – long lasting) – since ākāsa stays for a little longer than other elements in manifested state, it is explained as “established”; visumbu – ākāsam – ether; eri – agni – fire; vaḷi – vāyu – air; nīr – jalam – water; nilam – bhūmi – earth; ivai misai – having them as the source; padar – pervaded; poruḷ muḻuvadum – all worldly elements (matter); āy – being the upādānam (raw-material); udal-misai – in the body; uyir ena – like an ātmā pervading the body; karandu – hidden/concealed; engum parandu – thus being pervaded everywhere; sudar – radiant due to being svata:prāmāṇyam (self-evident); migu – abundant; surudiyuḷ – in sruti (which is heard); uḷan – being the essence; ivai uṇḍa – one who consumed everything during samhāram as explained in brahma sūtram 1.2.9 “attā carācara grahaṇāt”; suran – One who is identified by the word “dēva” (lord) as explained in subhāla upaniśat “tama: parē dēva ēkī bhavati” (tamas (mūla prakruti-matter) merges into paramātmā)

**Перевод:**

**bhagavān is the supreme lord who becomes (creates) all of the material realm having first created the strong ether, fire, air, water and earth as the source and pervades all of them. He is pervading in everything similar to ātmā is pervading in the body. Not only that, he is present inside and outside of everything. He is the main object of the most radiant vēdam, Such emperumān consumes everything during praḷayam and is glorified as “sura” (God).**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*In the previous 3 pāsurams, it is established that the svarūpam (true nature), stiti (existence) and pravrutti (actions) of jagat (material realm) are all under the full control of bhagavān through sāmānādikaraṇyam. In this pāsuram, it is explained that this sāmānādikaraṇyam is bound by the sarīra-ātma bhāvam of jagat and īsvara – that the entire realm (consisting of cit and acit) is the body and  bhagavān is the antaryāmi of everything.*

[bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) pervades everywhere and controls all entities just like the [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) controls the body. Thus being totally distinct from acit and three types of [cit](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) (nitya – eternally free, mukta – liberated, badda – bound), being free from all blemishes and full of all auspiciousness, being the one who creates, sustains and annihilates the whole of material realm as a sport, being the antarātmā of everything (other than him), being not affected by the defects of [cit](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) and [acit](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/09/thathva-thrayam-achith-what-is-matter/) since he is not bound by any karmā is explained as the supreme lord in detail through vēdam. vēdam is blemiśless due to its not being created by any individual, is understood through smruti, itihāsams and purāṇams and is unrefuted, radiant and authentic pramāṇam (source of knowledge). piḷḷān lists over 30 pramāṇams from vēdam, upaniśat, bhagavat gītā etc to establish this principle. With this, philosophies of lōkāyata (cāruvāka), māyāvāda, bhāskarīya, yādava prakāsa etc, which are contrary to vēdam, are refuted.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*After explaining the total control of bhagavān over the nature, existence and actions through sāmānādikaraṇyam and vaiyadikaraṇyam in the previous pāsurams, the sarīra-sarīri bhāva sambandam (the body – soul relationship) between the material realm and bhagavān is explained here. It is also explained that “since the material realm is totally under the control of bhagavān, it is his body” as the body is fully controlled by the in-dwelling soul.*

Similar to [nampiḷḷai](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/09/16/nampillai-english/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Next, this sāmānādikaraṇyam is explained as bound by the body-soul relationship between the material realm and bhagavān.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*Similar to nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

Similar to [nampiḷḷai](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/09/16/nampillai-english/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Previously nammāḻvār explained sāmānādikaraṇyam to explain it further in this pāsuram. The result of such sāmānādikaraṇyam is sarīra-ātma bhāvam (body-soul aspect of the material realm and bhagavān). It can also be said that the sāmānādikaraṇyam is bound by the sarīra-ātma bhāvam principle. It is explained in cāndōjña upaniśat “anēna jīvēna ātmanānupravisya nāmarūpē vyākaravāṇi”  (I enter into all matter through jīvātmās to give them distinct names/forms which signify creation). Instead of being like a clay pot which is just made of clay, bhagavān stays as the antaryāmi of all entities and controls those entities fully just like an ātmā (soul) stays as the dāraka (protector), niyāmaka (one who controls) and sēśi (the master). It is explained that this sarīra-ātma bhāvam is the driving force for the previously explained sāmānādikaraṇyam. When it is is said that “dēvadatta is standing on a tree”, there is no sarīra-ātma bhāvam (but when it is said that “bhagavān is everything”, there is sarīra-ātma bhāvam – bhagavān is the ātmā and everything is his body). திடவிசும்பு எரி வளி நீர் நிலம்  இவை மிசை படர்பொருள் முழுவதுமாய அவை யவை தொறும் உடல்மிசை உயிர் எனக் கரந்தெங்கும் பரந்துளன் சுடர்மிகு சுருதியுள்  இவை உண்ட சுரனே tidavisumbu eri vaḷi nīr nilam ivai misai padarporuḷ muḻuvadumāy avai avai toṟum udanmisai uyir enak karandengum paranduḷan sudarmigu surudiyuḷ ivai uṇḍa suranē*

- *tida visumbu* – tidam (drudam) indicates long lasting. This adjective can be given to all five elements, since they remain a little longer than the variegated material manifestation. Otherwise, it can be said only of ākāsam – which is created first even among the five elements and consumed in the end – so even among the five elements, ākāsam is more long lasting. This is also indicated to refute lōkāyata philosophy which accepts only 4 elements (except ether).
- *ivaimisai padar poruḷ muḻuvadumāy* – Having these five elements as cause and the variegated manifestation as the effect. Here “*āy*”  (become) should be understood as “*ākki*” (created). [nammāḻvār](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/18/nammazhwar-english/) uses the term “*āy*” due to his familiarity in vēdam (taittirīya upaniśat) which says “bahusyām” (he became many). This is how vaidikas establish their philosophy through vēdam.
- *avai avai toṟum* – Unlike many pillars which support a ceiling (where the pillars are separate from the ceiling), [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) pervades all entities like its said in “*jāti vyaktitōṟum parisamāpya vartikkumāpōlē*” (the category of an entity pervades all through the entity – here jāti indicates – dēva (godly), manuśya (human), tiryak (animal), stāvara (plant). If there is a human, humanness will pervade each human fully in all the parts of the human as well. Similarly, [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) pervades all entities everywhere).
- *udalmisai uyirena* – Similar to [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) being the protector, controller, master of the body, [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is the protector, controller, master of everything. (Note: Its important to also understand the distinction between ātmā pervading body which happens through jñānam (knowledge) and bhagavān pervading everything through svarūpam (himself existing in every thing)).
- *engum karandu* – Even though he is all pervading, the pervaded entities may not know him since he is hidden inside them. He is spread inside and outside – everywhere.
- *uḷan sudarmigu surudiyuḷ* – Such [emperumān](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/17/divya-dhampathi/) is explained in detail in vēdam which is apauruśēyam (not created by an individual) and nirdōśam (flawless).
- *sudarmigu* – It is so radiant and cannot be discarded through arguments as in the case of pratyakśam (perception) and anumānam (inference).
- *suruti* – sruti – that which is continually taught orally through generations. With this, all principles which are explained starting with the [first pāsuram](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/?p=1877) until now, are based on the flawless vēdam.
- *ivaiyuṇḍa suran* – one who consumed (annihilated) everything (in the material realm). Previously creation was attributed to [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/). If annihilation were attributed to some one else, that will minimize the glory of [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/). So, [nammāḻvār](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/18/nammazhwar-english/) establishes that samhāram is also under the control of [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/).
- Important aspects in this pāsuram
   - Through “*ivayiyuṇḍa suran*“, [nammāḻvār](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/18/nammazhwar-english/) refutes the kudruśtis (ones who misinterpret vēdam) who say sruśti/samhāram are conducted (independently) by other dēvatās.
   - Through “*tida visumbu*“, [nammāḻvār](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/18/nammazhwar-english/) refutes lōkāyatas (cāruvāka who dont accept vēdam as pramāṇam) who do not accept ākāsam as an element and only accept 4 elements.
   - Through “*udal misai uyir*“, [nammāḻvār](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/18/nammazhwar-english/) refutes advaitis who consider everything is one (as it is established that [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) controls all different entities).
   - Through “*sudarmigu surudiyuḷ*“, [nammāḻvār](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/18/nammazhwar-english/) acknowledges [srīman nārāyaṇan](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/17/divya-dhampathi/)‘s paratvam (supremacy), lakśmīsambandam (relationship with [srī mahālakśmi](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/17/divya-dhampathi/)) etc which are explained in puruśa sūktam etc.

In the next article we will see the next pāsuram.

## 1.1.8. Surar arivaru nilai

*surar aṟivaru nilai viṇ mutal muḻuvadum varan mudalāy avai muḻuduṇḍa paraparan puram oru mūnṟerittu amararkkum aṟivu iyandu aran ayan ena ulagu aḻittu amaittu uḷanē*

**Пословный перевод:**

surar – for dēvatās starting with brahmā; aṟivarum – difficult to know; nilai – having such position/stage; viṇ mudal – ākāsam etc; muḻuvadum – All entities in samaśti rūpam (panca bhūtams in aggregate state); varan mudalāy – being the largest cause; avai – those; muḻudu – without remainder/balance; uṇḍa – annihilating; para paran – one who is greater than great brahmā, rudra et al who are responsible for vyaśti (variegated) sruśti (creation) and samhāram (annihilation); aran – rudra; ayan – brahmā; ena – being well-known; puram oru mūnṟu – the unique 3 towns; erittu – burnt down; amararkku – to the dēvatās; aṟivu – jñānam/knowledge; iyandum – taught; ulagu – the different layers/planets of the egg shaped universe; aḻittu – annihilated; amaittu – created them; uḷan – being the antaryāmi of such brahmā, rudra et al

**Перевод:**

**bhagavān being the cause for mūla prakruti etc, which cannot be comprehended by brahmā, rudra et al, consumed (annihilated) all of the material realm being the supreme lord of such dēvatās, assumed the form of rudra to destroy the 3 towns (tripura samhāram), annihilated everything, created the variegated forms (again), gave the knowledge to dēvatās et al. He does all of these being the antaryāmi of dēvatās such as brahmā, rudra et al.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*This pāsuram refutes kudruśtis (those who misinterpret vēdam) who say that such sarvēsvaran popularly being established through vēdam is one amongst the dēvatās like brahmā who is involved in sruśti, rudra who is involved in samhāram etc.*

Quoting many pramāṇams from sāstram to establish that brahmā was born inside the universe (aṇḍam – sphere that contains the 14 planetary layers) and rudra was born as the son of brahmā (Note: There are innumerable such universes with each universe having one brahmā, one rudra and so on), [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s supremacy is established.

[nammāḻvār](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/18/nammazhwar-english/) says that those who are born inside the universe would not understand the mūla prakruti (primordial matter – unmanifested state), mahān (manifested matter), ahankāram (ego), etc which are beyond and outside the scope of such universes. [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) directly performs the samaśti sruśti first (initial creation of the five elements) and the ultimate samhāram (consuming the remaining items outside the universe). Also, svētāsvatāra upaniśat says “*yō brahmāṇam vidadāti pūrvam…*” ([bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) created brahmā and taught him vēdam) and mahābhāratam says “*viṣṇurātmā bhagavatō bhavasyāmitatējasa: …*” ([viṣṇu](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/17/divya-dhampathi/) is the antaryāmi of siva who is most glorifiable and has great radiance). Through these pramāṇams, we can understand that [emperumān](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/17/divya-dhampathi/) (who gave jñānam to dēvatās, who helped in tripura dahanam (burning of 3 towns) etc) is the lord of brahmā, rudra et al since he is the one who performs [samaśti sruśti/samhāram](https://granthams.koyil.org/readers-guide-english/) (which are beyond the reach of brahmā, rudra et al and who performs [vyaśti sruśti/samhāram](https://granthams.koyil.org/readers-guide-english/) by being the antaryāmi of brahmā, rudra et al.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*Similar to piḷḷān‘s introduction.*

Similar to [nampiḷḷai](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/09/16/nampillai-english/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, nammāḻvār says brahmā and rudra who are responsible for vyaśti sruśti (creation of variegated forms) and vyaśti samhāram (annihilation of variegated forms) respectively are under the full control of bhagavān.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*Similar to piḷḷān‘s introduction.*

Similar to [nampiḷḷai](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/09/16/nampillai-english/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Someone questions nammāḻvār “You say that bhagavān is established by vēdam and is the antarātmā for every thing.  But others are also responsible for certain aspects like brahmā being responsible for creation, rudra for annihilation etc. If you say that everything is controlled by one person, then you seem to be biased”. nammāḻvār replies “I am not biased towards a single person, but if we analyse the pramāṇams (scriptures), we can understand that those dēvatās are not (independantly) performing their responsibilities”. சுரர் அறிவரு நிலை விண் முதல் முழுவதும் வரன் முதலாய அவை முழுதுண்ட பரபரன் புரம் ஒரு மூன்றெரித்து  அமரர்க்கு அறிவு இயந்து அரன் அயன் என உலகு அழித்து அமைத்து உளனே surar aṟivaru nilai viṇ mutal muḻuvadum varan mudalāy avai muḻuduṇḍa paraparan puram oru mūnṟerittu amararkkum aṟivu iyandu aran ayan ena ulagu aḻittu amaittu uḷanē*

- *surar aṟivaru nilai* – As explained in brahma sūtram 1.3.9 “*akśaram ambarāntadrutē:*” (akśaram indicates [paramātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) only, since mūla prakruti which is the source of ākāsam is held by him) and  gārggi vidyai in bruhadāraṇyaka upaniśat says “*kasminnu kalvākāsa ōtasca prōtasca*” (mūla prakruti exists in many different forms), ākāsa indicates mūla prakruti here based on kāraṇa-kārya bhāvam (cause-effect relationship where mūla prakruti is the cause and ākāsam is the effect). dēvatās starting with brahmā do not understand the true nature of mūīa prakruti etc.
- *varan mudalāy* – [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) pervades everything in the subtle state of mūla prakruti (primordial nature) and the gross state of mahān (manifested matter), ahankāram  etc – as part of sruśti. Since he controls everything by pervading everything, he is explained as the ultimate cause of everything.
- *avai muḻuduṇḍa* – In samhāram too, he is the one who consumes everything. In katavallī 1.2, it is explained that “*yasya brahma ca kśtranca ubhē bhavata ōdana: \| mrutyur yasya upasēcanam \| ka ittā vēda yatra sa:* \|\|” (one who has all brāhmaṇas, kśatriyas (indicating all entities) as his food, one who has yama (the lord of death) himself as upasēcanam (like curd, pickle etc which are used as side-dish and eaten in the end as well). Who will know the greatness of that great person?).
- *paraparan* – brahmā,etc al who are qualified (in some ways) are greater than general population. [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is much greater than such devatās. This is explained in viṣṇu purāṇam 1.2.10 “*para: parāṇām …*” – Different from the great brahmā, rudra et al and greater than they. [nammāḻvār](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/18/nammazhwar-english/) himself says in tiruvāimoḻi 8.7.5 “*manisarkkut tēvar pōlat tēvarkkum dēvā*” (Just like dēvas are superior to humans, you are superior to such dēvas).
- *puram oru mūnṟērittu amararkku aṟivy iyandu* – It is popularly known that rudra performed tripura samhāram (destroying the 3 towns) and brahmā gave jñānam (knowledge) to dēvas. But if we analyse that, we will understand that, [srīman nārāyaṇa](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/17/divya-dhampathi/) is the one who creates these dēvatās and gives them the ability to perform various tasks.
   - In mahābhāratam karṇa parvam, learned scholars such as vyāsa said “*viṣṇurātmā bhagavatō bhavasyāmitatējasa: \| tasmāddanurjñāsam sparsam sa viśēhē mahēsvara:* \|\|” ([viṣṇu](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/17/divya-dhampathi/) is the antaryāmi for siva who is most courageous and vorśippable. It is because of [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s presence as antaryāmi that siva managed to tie the string and launch the bow during tripura samhāram). [tirumangai āḻvār](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2013/01/23/thirumangai-azhwar/) (who is one among the [āḻvārs](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/azhwars/) who were blessed by [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) himself with blemiśless knowledge) declared in periya tirumoḻi 6.1.3 “*naṇṇār nagaram viḻa nanimalai silai vaḷaivu seydu angaḻal niṟa ambu adu ānavanē*” ([emperumān](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/17/divya-dhampathi/) who became the arrow in the huge bow which is fiery, to knock down the 3 towns).
   - In svētāsvatāra upaniśat, it is said “*yō brahmāṇam viddāti pūrvam yōvai vēdāmsca prahiṇōti tasmai*” (that [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) who created brahmā first, that [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) who taught vēdam to him).
- *aran ayan ena ulagu aḻittu amaittu uḷān* – In mahābhāratam sānti parvam 169, it is said that “*ētau dvau vibudasrēśtau prasādakrōdajau smrutau \| tadādarsitapantānau sruśtisamhārakārakau \|\|*” (brahmā and rudra are best among dēvatās who were born out of [srīman nārāyaṇa](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/17/divya-dhampathi/)‘s mercy and anger (respectively). They are explained in smruti as the ones who perform creation and annihilation as learnt from [srīman nārāyaṇan](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/17/divya-dhampathi/) himself). So, as per pramāṇam (scriptures), they have involvement in creation and annihilation. Since it is [emperumān](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/17/divya-dhampathi/) who performs sruśti and samhāram being the antaryāmi of brahmā and rudra, I ([nammāḻvār](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/18/nammazhwar-english/)) told that [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is the real creator/annihilator and not because of my bias towards [srīman nārāyaṇa](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/17/divya-dhampathi/). Thus, [nammāḻvār](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/18/nammazhwar-english/) refutes the kudruśtis (ones who misinterpret vēdam) in this pāsuram.

In the next article we will the next pāsuram.
