## 1.1.9. Ulan enil ulan

*uḷan enil uḷan avan uruvam ivvuruvugaḷ uḷan alan enil avan aruvam ivvaruvugaḷ uḷan ena ilan ena ivai guṇam udaimaiyil uḷan iru tagailmaiyodu oḻivilan parantē*

**Пословный перевод:**

uḷan enil – if said to be existing as per own philosophy (vaidika philosophy); uḷan alan enil – if said to be non-existing as per other philosophy (avaidika philosophy); uḷan – Should be considered as existing since there should be an entity (substratum) for sat bhāvam (existence) or asat bhāvam (non-existence) while making a statement; thus; uḷan ena ilan ena ivai – that which is said as existing or non-existing; guṇamudaimaiyil – having as attribute; ivvuruvugaḷ ivvaruvugaḷ – those aspects with form or without form in this material realm; avanuruvam avanaruval – having them as prakāram (attribute) that shows or hides; iru tagaimaiyodu – having two different aspects; uḷan – being; parandu – pervading everywhere; oḻivilan – present without ever ceasing to exist

**Перевод:**

**bhagavān is the substratum for both existence (as per āḻvār‘s vaidika philosophy) or non-existence (as per avaidika philosophy) – so, bhagavān must be understood/accepted as existing  while making a statement about him. He is the one who pervades everywhere without ever ceasing to exist and has both with-form and form-less manifestation of this material realm as his two types of aspects which shows and hides him respectively.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*After rejecting kudruśtis who accept vēdam but misinterpret them, this pāsuram rejects sūnyavādis (philosophers of voidness) who say “there is no pramāṇam (scriptures), there is no pramēyam (goal/bhagavān); everything is sūnyam (void). Thus there is no vēdam, no bhagavān (who is the object of vēdam) and no existence of this realm (which is his wealth)”.*

[āḻvār](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/18/nammazhwar-english/) tells a sūnyavādi “You cannot prove [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s non-existence through his presence or absence. In general, bhāvam (presence) or abhāvam (absence) of an entity/attribute is based on the place, time and form. When we say [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is present, that means he is present within gross forms which are visible  and when say [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is absent, that means he is present within subtle forms which are invisible. Even for other entities ([cit](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) and [acit](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/09/thathva-thrayam-achith-what-is-matter/)), the same rule applies – they either are present in gross or subtle forms. Thus being with form (gross) or without form (subtle) are just his attributes. Thus in either case he exists”. Thus sūnyavādi is refuted.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*Similar to piḷḷān‘s introduction.*

Similar to [nampiḷḷai](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/09/16/nampillai-english/)‘s vyākhyānam. nanjīyar highlights that his pāsuram is explained according to [kūrattāḻvān](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2013/10/05/kurathazhwan/)‘s explanation.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, nammāḻvār refutes mādyamika baudda philosophers (a type of sūnyavādi – voidness philośopher) who is considered as the primary amongst vēda bhāhyas (the ones who reject vēdam).*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*Previously, nammāḻvār refuted those who partially took some aspects of pramāṇam (scriptures) and pramēyam (goal) and thus misunderstood bhagavān‘s svarūpam and his attributes/qualities. In this pāsuram, āḻvār refutes sūnyavādi who rejects both pramāṇam and pramēyam. Even before the sūnyavādi starts giving any reason for his argument, āḻvār himself declares the truth about bhagavān who is with vibhūti (great wealth of (spiritual realm and) material realm).*

Similar to [nampiḷḷai](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/09/16/nampillai-english/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*In this pāsuram, nammāḻvār refutes sarva sūnyavādi (one who says everything is void in all aspects). He refutes as done by srī bhāśyakārar (emperumānār) in srī bhāsyhyam. Since bhāśyakārar is after the times of āḻvār, we can conclude that bhāśyakārar writes his refutal in srī bhāśyam based on āḻvār‘s explanations. Previously kudruśtis argued that brahmā, rudra et al are supreme based on some pramāṇams. But āḻvār establishes that srīman nārāyaṇan is the supreme lord, the entire material realm is for his service just like body is for the ātmā and these are revealed in vēdam. When we say “something does not exist”, we first need to define that something and then only reject the existence of that thing. Due to the fact that “something” is defined first, it cannot be made void. Merely saying something does not exist (without defining the entity) will not explain complete voidness. sarva sūnyavādam (complete voidness) can never be established (If there is a proper word that will always indicate some entity. It can never point to non-existing entity. For example if we say “there is no rabbit” – that means rabbit generally exists but it does not exist here at this place. Even if we create composite words like “rabbit-horn” (which is contradictory since there is no horn for rabbit) and say that does not exist, it will only prove that there is no connection between rabbit and horn – but both rabbit and horn exist separately.Thus, sarva sūnyavādam can never be established). āḻvār tells the sūnyavādi that you can neither prove voidness by accepting bhagavān‘s existence nor by rejecting bhagavān‘s existence. In either case, your desire (of establishing voidness) will not be fulfilled. I will take your word of “bhagavān does not exist” and prove that bhagavān exists. Generally, we explain the meaning of a word that indicates the presence or absence of an entity (i.e., when we say something exists, that means that entity exists in a particular place, time and form. Similarly when we say an entity does not exist, that means that entity does not exist in particular place, time and form). If we do not agree to this common platform of debate, you do not have the qualification to participate in the debate. உளன் எனில் உளன் அவன் உருவம் இவ்வுருவுகள் உளன் அலன் எனில் அவன் அருவம் இவ்வருவுகள் உளன் என இலன் என இவை குணம் உடைமையில் உளன் இரு தகைமையொடு ஒழிவிலன் பரந்தே uḷan enil uḷan avan uruvam ivvuruvugaḷ uḷan alan enil avan aruvam ivvaruvugaḷ uḷan ena ilan ena ivai guṇam udaimaiyil uḷan iru tagailmaiyodu oḻivilan parantē*

- *avanuruvam ivvuruvugaḷ* – [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) exists with the universe which he controls as explained in bruhadāraṇyaka upaniśat “*yasya ātmā sarīram yaya prutivī sarīram*” (all [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)s are his body, earth is his body) and has this universe as his sarīram (body) and sēśam (subordinate) – this is the stūlarūpam (gross form). When it is said as uḷān alan (he does not exist) he exists in the unmanifested (sūkśma – subtle) form.
- *avanaruvam ivvarugaḷ* – This is explained as the meaning of the word “nāsti” (non-existence) which really explains a different state of existence. “*gatōsti*” (pot exists) indicates an object with an opening at the top with a rounded structure. “*gatō nāsti*” indicates a different state – when it is not here means it is present else where; when it is not present now means it is present at some other time; it cannot be said that pot does not exist in any form at all times.
- *uḷan ena ilan ena ivai guṇam udaimaiyil* – Having the existence (in gross form) and non-existence (existence in subtle form) as qualities indicate that both of them are his attributes.
- *uḷan iru tagaimaiyodu* – He has both types of behaviour of being in existence and being not in existence which are indicated by the words “*uḷan*” and “*ilan*“.
- *oḻivilan parandē* – I ([āḻvār](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/18/nammazhwar-english/)) established his existence through the word “*uḷan*“. You (sūnyavādi) established his existence through the word “*ilan*“. So, both of us have established the truth. [āḻvār](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/18/nammazhwar-english/) also says “Just like his existence is established, can we not understand that he exists with this wealth of nitya vibhūti (spiritual realm) and leelā vibhūti (material realm)?”.

Note: kāncī P.B aṇṇangarācāryar svamy says at the end of his detailed explanation for this pāsuram in his divyārtta dīpikai commentary – “It cannot be explained in any more detail – this should be heard in detail under learned scholars” – what to speak about this English translation? The translation here is to develop the taste in hearing word-by-word kālakśēpam of these wonderful grantams which are the only way to get reasonable understanding of these pāsurams.

In the next article we will see the next pāsuram.

## 1.1.10. Paranta tan paravai

*paranda taṇ paravai uḷ nīr toṟum paranduḷan paranda aṇḍam idu ena nila visumbu oḻivu aṟak karanda sil idam toṟum idam tigaḻ poruḷ toṟum karandu engum paranduḷan ivai uṇḍa karanē*

**Пословный перевод:**

paranda – spread everywhere; taṇ – Since its not mixed with other bhūtams, ocean is naturally cool (which is the natural quality of water); paravai uḷ – inside the ēkārṇava (singular water mass which is the source of everything); nīr toṟum – in each drop of water; paranda aṇḍam itu ena – Like being in the huge aṇḍam (egg shaped universe); parandu uḷan – being present without any limitation; nilam – in the earth; visumbu – in the higher planets; oḻivu aṟa – in every particle; karanda – in the most subtle manner (invisible); sil idam toṟum – Even in the most minute places; idam – in those places; tigaḻ – self-effulgent; poruḷ toṟum – in the jīvātmās; karandu – hiding inside in such a way that even those pervaded objects do not know his existence; engum – everywhere; parandu uḷan – being the omni-present one; ivai uṇḍa karan – one who consumed all these during samhāram and stayed firm

**Перевод:**

**Just like staying conveniently (all by himself) in the huge universe, he stays in each drop of the water in the naturally cool ocean in the most subtle matter. He is present even inside the most minute places and inside the self-effulgent jīvātmās who reside in those minute places in such a manner that the pervaded objects do not realise his presence. He, being the omni-present being, consumed everything during samhāram (annihilation) and remained firm.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*bhagavān pervades in each atom of the drops of water in the ocean, in the subtlest acit (matter) particles which exist from the earth to the sky and in the jīvātmās which exist inside each such particle. Even inside those jīvātmās, he pervades most casually/conveniently as if he is staying (all by himself) in a huge universe. Yet, he is invisible to others and he is the one who annihilates everything. nammāḻvār instructs his mind to worship the lotus feet of such emperumān who is clearly established in vēdam.*

Included in the introduction itself.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*nammāḻvār explains the convenience of bhagavān‘s vyāpti (omni-presence that was explained previously) in this pāsuram.*

Similar to [nampiḷḷai](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/09/16/nampillai-english/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Similar to nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*Similar to nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

Similar to [nampiḷḷai](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/09/16/nampillai-english/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Previously nammāḻvār explained that bhagavān has the material realm as his subordinate (like body for the soul), the one who is omni-present, the abode of everything, controller and the master. But when jīvātmā is bound inside a body, he becomes limited within the limitation of that body – would paramātmā also go through similar difficulties/limitations? No. He pervades without any limitations in the most convenient manner. பரந்த தண் பரவை யுள் நீர் தொறும் பரந்துளன் பரந்த அண்டம் இது என நில விசும்பு ஒழிவு அறக் கரந்த சில் இடம் தொறும் இடம் திகழ் பொருள் தொறும் கரந்து எங்கும் பரந்துளன் இவை உண்ட கரனே paranda taṇ paravai uḷ nīr toṟum paranduḷan paranda aṇḍam idu ena nila visumbu oḻivu aṟak karanda sil idam toṟum idam tigaḻ poruḷ toṟum karandu engum paranduḷan ivai uṇḍa karanē*

- *paranda taṇ paravai uḷ nīr toṟum parandu uḷan* –  In the cool and large ocean, [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) has pervaded in every drop of water which itself is made of minute atomic particles.
- *paranda aṇḍam idu ena* – One may question “Will the [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) who is explained in cāndōjña upaniśat 3.14 as ‘… *jyāyān antarikśāt …’* (though this [paramātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is in my heart, he is greater than the earth etc) be cramped within the minutest atomic particle?” – āḻvār answers that saying “No, he stays most conveniently in there just as he is staying in a huge universe by himself”.
- *nila visumbu oḻivaṟa* – Is he only pervading the minute particles of water? No, he is pervading earth, sky, this universe, all other universes, etc – everywhere which is explained further.
- *karanda sil idantoṟum* – everywhere – in the space between eye-lids where minute beings live (and die quickly even by the force of closing the eye-lids) – even in those subtlest beings, he is fully pervaded.
- *idam tigaḻ poruḷ toṟum* – Even inside the jīvātmās of those subtlest beings.
- *karandu* – hidden so that no one sees him, even those entities which were pervaded by him do not see/know him.
- *engum paranduḷan* – When a [cētana/jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) pervades the body in which he lives, he pervades through his knowledge – jñāna vyāpti (i.e., [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) exists in the heart and through the dharma bhūta jñāna understands and controls everything related to that body). But [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s vyāpti is not jñāna vyāpti – it is svarūpa vyāpti (pervaded naturally and fully in every place). [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is vibhu (great) and [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) is aṇu (atomic – minute).
- *ivai uṇḍa karanē* – if [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is so huge and these atomic particles are miniscule, how can he stay inside these comfortably without being cramped? He can do it because he is omni-potent (all-capable). As explained by [tirumangai āḻvār](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2013/01/23/thirumangai-azhwar/) in periya tirumoḻi 11.5.3 “*tayiruṇḍa pon vayiṟu ivvēḻulugumuṇḍum idamudaittāl*” (kriṣṇa’s golden (most-likable) stomach which contains the curd/yoghurt eaten by him, has more space even after consuming the 7 layers of planets) – Just like [emperumān](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/17/divya-dhampathi/) as a small child could consume all of the world and still have space left in his stomach, he can be great yet he can stay comfortably in the minutest particle.
- *karan* – who is firmly known by the most authoritative vēdam.

In the next article we will see the next pāsuram.

## 1.1.11. Kara visumbu

*kara visumbu eri vaḷi nīr nilam ivai misai varanavil tiṟalvali aḷi poṟai āy ninṟa paran adi mēl kurukūrc catakōpan sol niraniṟai āyirattu ivai pattum vīdē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kara – since ākāsam is more sūbtle than others, it is said as invisible or strong; visumbu – ākāsam – ether; eri – agni – fire; vaḷi – vāyu – air; nīr – jalam – water; nilam – bhūmi – earth; ivai misai – being the abode or having them as attributes; varan – best; navil – sabdam – words (attribute of ether); tiṟal – heat (attribute of fire); vali – bhalam – strength (attribute of air); aḷi – coolness (attribute of water); poṟai – forbearance (attribute of earth); āy ninṟa – being these darmi (elements) and darmams (their attributes); paran – the most supreme; adi mēl – on the lotus feet (which removes sorrows); kūrukūrc catakōpan – one who is born in āḻvārtirunagari and one who wins over bhāhyas and kudruśtis who are identified by sata (ignorance, etc); sol – mercifully spoken; niraniṟai āyirattu – enriched/complete due to the words, meanings, tunes, music etc coming together; ivai pattum – these 10 pāsurams which reveal his supremacy; vīdē – (vidappattana – submitted) offered to the lotus feet of emperumān. Since these 10 pāsurams lead one to mōkśam, vīdē (vīdu = mōkśam in tamiḻ) can also be taken as indicating the ultimate result

**Перевод:**

**These 10 pāsurams (which are mercifully spoken and which are most enriching/complete) are offered by nammāḻvār (who is born in āḻvārtirunagari) at the lotus feet of emperumān who is the supreme lord and is the abode of panca bhūtam (ākāsa, vāyu, agni, jalam and bhūmi) and their respective qualities (sound, strength, heat, coolness and forbearance) or has them as his attributes. Just like vālmīki is glorified in srī rāmāyaṇam bāla kaṇṭam 4.1 for his trustworthy nature, here āḻvār ‘s trustworthy nature is highlighted. Since the count 1000 is highlighted, bhagavān who is the divine force behind these pāsurams is established. This padgam (decad) falls under the tamiḻ poem category of “kali viruttam“.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

This tiruvāimoḻi (padigam/decad) explains [emperumān](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/17/divya-dhampathi/) who has two vibhūtis – [nitya vibhūti](http://granthams.koyil.org//readers-guide) (spiritual realm – bhōga upakaraṇa – tool for his joy) and [leelā vibhūti](https://granthams.koyil.org/readers-guide-english/) (material realm – leelā upakaraṇa – tool for his sport). [āḻvār](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/18/nammazhwar-english/) focusses this on his lotus feet since it is the most suitable object of worship. Looking at the beauty of the words, meaning, tune, truthful nature of the pāsurams etc [āḻvār](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/18/nammazhwar-english/) desires that 1000 such pāsurams are sung to glorify [emperumān](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/17/divya-dhampathi/).

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the end, nammāḻvār concludes that these 10 pāsurams are offered as devotional service at the lotus feet of emperumān who is explained in the 10 pāsurams in great detail (same is explained in nampiḷḷai‘s introduction).*

Similar to [nampiḷḷai](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/09/16/nampillai-english/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, summarizing the supremacy of bhagavān that is explained previously, āḻvār declares that the result of (learning/reciting/understanding) this decad is mōkśam.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*Similar to nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

Similar to [nampiḷḷai](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/09/16/nampillai-english/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*In the first pāsuram, bhagavān having auspicious qualities, being the master of nitya vibhūti (spiritual realm) and having beautiful and distinct form are explained. In the second pāsuram,  bhagavān‘s svarūpam (true nature) – the abode of the previously said aspects (auspicious qualities, being with spiritual realm and having divine body) – is explained as distinct from cit and acit. In the third pāsuram, āḻvār enjoys the leelā vibhūti (material realm) which is similar to nitya vibhūti in the sense that both are owned/controlled by him. In the fourth pāsuram, āḻvār says that the leelā vibhūti’s svarūpam (true nature) is under bhagavān‘s control. In the fifth pāsuram, āḻvār says that the existence of the material realm is also under bhagavān‘s control. In the sixth pāsuram, āḻvār says that action and inaction are under bhagavān’s control. In the seventh pāsuram āḻvār says that since jagat (material realm) and īsvara share body and soul relationship, the aikyam (union) explained between jagat and īsvara is based on sarīra-ātma bhāvam. In the eighth pāsuram, āḻvār refutes kudruśtis (ones who misinterpret vēdam). In the ninth pāsuram, āḻvār refutes sūnyavādis (ones who reject vēdam and say that everything is void). In the tenth pāsuram, āḻvār explains the convenient nature of emperumān‘s vyāpti (omni-presence). Thus, bhagavān‘s paratvam (supremacy) is elaborately established by āḻvār previously. In this pāsuram, āḻvār says that ones who engage in this decad, gets the same result (bhagavat kainkarya mōkśam) as he (āḻvār) had got. கர விசும்பு  எரி வளி நீர் நிலம் இவை மிசை வரனவில் திறல்வலி யளி பொறை யாய் நின்ற பரன் அடி மேல் குருகூர்ச் சடகோபன் சொல் நிரனிறை ஆயிரத்து இவை பத்தும் வீடே kara visumbu eri vaḷi nīr nilam ivai misai varanavil tiṟalvali aḷi poṟai āy ninṟa paran adi mēl kurukūrc catakōpan sol niraniṟai āyirattu ivai pattum vīdē*

- *kara visumbu … ivai misai* … *poṟai āy ninṟa* – By explaining the five elements and their qualities – leelā vibhūti is explained. leelā vibhūti is explained as upalakśaṇam (a sample) for nity vihūti. Thus, the supreme lord who is the master of both realms.
- *kurukūrc catakōpan* – As said in srī rāmāyaṇam bāla kāṇṭam 4.1 “*vālmīkir bhagavān ruśi:*” (the most knovledgable sage vālmīki), here [āḻvār](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/18/nammazhwar-english/)‘s name is revealed to highlight his trustworthy nature.
- *nira niṟai* – Can be “*niral niṟai*” (made of best words and filled with great meanings) or “*niran niṟai*” (Having 4 lines where line is similarly composed and matching the tunes of music etc in proper andādi (last word/letter in one pāsuram matching next pāsuram’s first word, letter etc.,) format as explained for srī rāmāyaṇam slōkams).
- *āyiram* – Similar to srī rāmāyaṇam bāla kāṇṭam 2.41 “…*kāvyam rāmāyaṇam krutsnamīdrusai: karavāṇyaham*” (Let me compose this epic called srī rāmāyaṇm in such manner) which was composed by vālmīki (by the blessings of brahmā), [āḻvār](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/18/nammazhwar-english/) who was fully blessed by [emperumān](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/17/divya-dhampathi/) with blemiśless knowledge declares that he is going to compile these pāsurams. Also, since his experiences cannot be revealed at once, he says he will reveal them in 1000 pāsurams in sequence. Also, it can be said that, since [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s greatness cannot be explained in a few words, [āḻvār](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/18/nammazhwar-english/) says he will explain them over 1000 pāsurams.
- *ivai pattum vīdē* – These are offered at the lotus feet of [emperumān](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/17/divya-dhampathi/). It can also be explained as – Just like when one looks at a field that has paddy crop and says “this field is filled with paddy” (even when it is not grown, yet indicating the result will be paddy), here, [āḻvār](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/18/nammazhwar-english/) says these 10 pāsurams will lead to vīdu (mōkśam).
- [āḻvār](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/18/nammazhwar-english/) mercifully explains that [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s mercy gave him blemiśless knowledge, that knowledge leads him to mōkśam and one who engages in this prabandam in any manner, will also get the same benefit.

Thus ends the English translation for tiruvāimoḻi 1st centum 1st decad.

## 1.2 Vidumin murravum

## 1.2.1. Vidumin murravum

*vīdumin muṟṟavum vīdu seydu ummuyir vīdu udaiyān idai vīdu seymminē*

**Пословный перевод:**

muṟṟavum – All (self-centered) means which are hurdles to worship emperumān; vīdumin – give up without any attachment; not only that; vīdu seytu – after giving up; um uyir – yourself; vīdu udaiyānidai – the master who is the controller of mōkśam (liberation); vīdu seymmin – submit unto him. It is also said as “vīdu isaiminē” which means “Agree to submit unto him”

**Перевод:**

**Simple transalation (based on vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar‘s 12000 padi)**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

Give up the association of all matters which are different from bhagavat viśayam. Submit oneself as a servant. Surrender unto the master. samarppaṇam (submitting) means communicating oneself that one is a servant to emperumān.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*nammāḻvār instructs us to give up attachments to all matters except bhagavat viśayam and submit oneself at the lotus feet of srīman nārāyaṇan who is the master of everyone.*

Similar to [nampiḷḷai](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/09/16/nampillai-english/)”s vyākhyānam.

- vīdumin – To highlight the importance of giving up that which is being held on, [nammāḻvār](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/18/nammazhwar-english/) first says “give up”.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*In this padigam (decad), in the first pāsuram, nammāḻvār orders everyone to perform ātma samarppaṇam (submitting oneself) to bhagavān with the prerequisite of giving up attachments to everything else.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*Similar to nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

Similar to [nampiḷḷai](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/09/16/nampillai-english/)”s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*nammāḻvār instructs to give up other matters and hold on to bhagavat viśayam which is appropriate for the nature of jīvātmās. வீடுமின் முற்றவும்–வீடுசெய்து உம்முயிர் வீடு உடையான் இடை–வீடு செய்ம்மினே vīdumin muṟṟavum vīdu seydu ummuyir vīdu udaiyān idai vīdu seymminē*

- *vīdumin* – vīdumin itself can mean “give up”. It can also be said that “vidumin” has been stretched to sound “vīdumin”. Why āḻvār is emphasising the “giving up” first without indicating what is to be given up? When a small child gets hold of a snake, the mother (or elders) out of fear will say “drop” first and then say “the snake”. Similarly, when a house is on fire, onlookers may scream “get out” first and then say that the house is on fire. Similarly, āḻvar says “give up” first. Also, as seen in vibhīśaṇa’s life in srī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam, “*tayktvā putrāmsca dārāmsca*” (Giving up the sons and wife) and “parityaktā mayā lankā” (lankā was fully given up me) – first vibhīśaṇa gave up everything and then surrendered to srī rāma – āḻvār is also instructing in the same order. “vīdumin” is a plural world – It is not that someone who was distressed by the worldly matters approached āḻvār and asked him for advise. āḻvār out of his eagerness, instructs everyone to relieve them from the suffering in this world.
- *muṟṟavum* – Everything. When a caṇḍāḷa’s (dog-eater) house is given to a brāhmaṇa, everything is cleared out and then given. Similarly, while giving up, everything should be given up since all world attachments are based on ahankāram (considering oneself as body) and mamakāram (considering oneself as the owner).
- *vīdu seytu* – The repetition here is to emphasise the importance of “giving up”. When a prince somehow is imprisoned even before being crowned, first being released from the prison would be the primary goal. Similarly, giving up everything itself is important first.
- *ummuyir vīdu udaiyānidai* – There are several explanations for this.
   - As explained in bruhadāraṇyaka upaniśat “*yasya ātmā sarīram, yasya prutvi sarīram*” (all [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)s are his body, earth is his body) – [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is the owner of both the [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) and its *vīdu* (house – residing place) which is the body.
   - The one who has yourself ([ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)) as the residing place.
   - The owner to whom yourself should be submitted.
   - vīdu (mōkhsam – paramapadam) – The one who is the owner of paramapadam.
- *ummuyir* – yourself. I am suggesting for the well-being of yourself, not your body. And it is not for the well-being of me but for you.
- *udaiyānidai* – Now, āḻvār is using general term “Owner/master”. When one develops taste towards bhagavat viśayam and asks “who is the master?”, āḻvār will say “*vaṇpugaḻ nāraṇan*” (the most glorious [srīman nārāyaṇan](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/17/divya-dhampathi/)) at that time. As the owner, he is trying to protect you all along. You too, accept his ownership without thinking “me, mine” and submit unto him. Since he is the owner, we cannot argue with him.
- manusmruti 8.92 is explained in detail by nampiḷḷai “*yamō vaivasvatō rāja ya stavaiśa hrudi stita: \| tēna cēdavivādas tē mā gangām mā kurūn gama: \|\|*” (The one who controls yama (the controller of death), one who is born in the sun dynasty  or one who is residing in the center of sun, the one who is liked by everyone, the one who is explained popularly in antaryāmi brāhamaṇam, he is residing in your heart. If you give up arguing with him, that is sufficient – you need not visit holy rivers and holy places).  nampiḷḷai highlights that [emperumān](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/17/divya-dhampathi/) is always within our heart to help us. Atonement without giving up ahankāram and mamakāram is like packing a condemned material in a nice package and offering it. Also, [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is the owner. [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) is the best object which is stolen by us (i.e., considering oneself to be independent instead of being dependent on [emperumān](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/17/divya-dhampathi/)). Before atoning (submitting) one should give up the stolen object – but that stolen object is oneself. But, there is no one else to submit. So, you just submit yourself to the master. Submitting means agreeing to his ownership and our servitorśip.

In the next article we will the next pāsuram.

## 1.2.2. Minnin nilaiyila

*minnin nilaiyila mannuyir ākkaigaḷ ennum idattu iṟai unnumin nīrē*

**Пословный перевод:**

uyir – ātmā (soul); man – filled with likeable aspects; ākkaigaḷ – bodies which are the cause for bondage; minnin – more than a lightning; nilai – state of appearing and disappearing immediately; ila – not having; ennum idattu – as explained in; nīrē – yourself; iṟai – the master; unnumin – meditate upon him

**Перевод:**

**Simple transalation (based on vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar‘s 12000 padi)**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*Can we give up things which we are used to for a very long time?*

āḻvār says when one analyses and understands the impermanent nature of the body etc which are related to the [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/), then those impermanent aspects can be easily given up.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*Can we give up things which we are used to for a very long time? nammāḻvār says that when we understand their defects such as impermanence, etc., they can be easily given up.*

Similar to [nampiḷḷai](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/09/16/nampillai-english/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, to facilitate the process of renunciation (giving up), nammāḻvār identifies the impermanent nature of the aspects which are to be given up.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*Similar to nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

Similar to [nampiḷḷai](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/09/16/nampillai-english/)‘s vyākhyānam.

Also, for the singular usage of uyir ([jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) – soul) and plural usage of ākkaigaḷ (sarīram – bodies), periyavāccān piḷḷai quotes bhagavat gītā 2.22 “*vāsāmsi jīrṇāni*” slōkam, where [emperumān](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/17/divya-dhampathi/) explains that just as a person acquires new clothes when the old ones are unusable, the [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) too will acquire a new body when the old one becomes unusable (at the time of death). So, the same [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/), continually acquires a new body birth after birth.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*In the first pāsuram, nammāḻvār instructs everyone to give up all aspects other than bhagavat viśayam and surrender unto emperumān. When some one questions “You are asking us to give up worldly attachments. But we have been used to it since time immemorial. How we can we give them up now?”. nammāḻvār replies through this pāsuram “when you understand the defects of the worldly aspects, they can be given up”. மின்னின் நிலையில–மன்னுயிர் ஆக்கைகள் என்னும் இடத்து இறை–உன்னுமின் நீரே minnin nilaiyila mannuyir ākkaigaḷ ennum idattu iṟai unnumin nīrē*

- *minnin nilaiyila* – In the case of lightning we, at the least, know that it exists only for a moment. It is both insignificant and impermanent. But, the body, even though impermanent, creates an illusion in the mind that it is permanent and leads to all kinds of troubles. Just like when someone places his hand on a snake thinking that it resembles sandalwood paste which has beautiful fragrance, coolness, softness etc and if he is informed that he is keeping his hand on a snake, he cannot resist taking his hand away (seeing the danger). Similarly, when the real defects of this temporary body (and material realm) such as insignificance and impermanence are highlighted, one can easily give it up.
- *mannuyir ākkaigaḷ* – the bodies in which the [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) is well seated; it is also explained as the different bodies pursued by the eternal [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/). nampiḷḷai gives a beautiful example – “*tiṟandu kidanda vāsalgaḷ tōṟum nuḻaindu tiriyum padārttam pōlēyiṟē ivan tirivadu*” (Just like a dog that will enter into any house that has an open door and come out, [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) enters so many bodies through the cycle of birth and death). Here, the usage of singular [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) is considered as a representative for all [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)s which pursue many bodies.
- *ennum idattu* – the defects are so much – even more than [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s auspicious qualities.
- nīrē – you can understand it just by observing yourself (since the impermanence is quite obvious). There is no need for pramāṇam (sāstram, etc) or ācārya upadēsam (instructions from an ācārya) to understand this.

In the next article we will the next pāsuram.

## 1.2.3. Nir numadu

*nīr numadu enṟu ivai vēr mudal māyttu iṟai sērmin uyirkku adan nēr niṟai illē*

**Пословный перевод:**

nīr numadu enṟu ivai – those which are known as ahankāram and mamakāram; vēr mudal māyttu – destroying them completely along with the ruci (taste) and vāsanā (habit/impressions) like pulling out a plant along with its root; iṟai – the master; sērmin – reach out to him; uyirkku – For the ātmā; adan nēr – fitting/suitable; niṟai illai – no fulfillment

**Перевод:**

**Give up ahankāram and mamakāram and reach out to the master. For the jīvātmā, there is nothing more fulfilling and suitable than that.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

Fully give up ahankāram and mamakāram (along with the ruci and vāsanā) which will destroy the [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) and reach out to [emperumān](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/17/divya-dhampathi/).  There is nothing more fulfilling for the nature of [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/).

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In this pāsuram, nammāḻvār briefly instructs as to what is to be given up.*

Similar to [nampiḷḷai](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/09/16/nampillai-english/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, nammāḻvār mercifully explains the process of renunciation briefly.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*Similar to nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

Similar to [nampiḷḷai](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/09/16/nampillai-english/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*A question is raised to āḻvār – “you are saying that if we understand the defects, we can give up (attachment to worldly aspects). We have already spent our time in this world since eternity. It looks endless too. Don’t we need a really long time to give up that which was accumulated over very long time?” nammāḻvār briefly explains that which is to be given up. He explains the cause for being in samsāram with worldly attachments and the remedy for the same. நீர் நுமது என்று இவை–வேர் முதல் மாய்த்து இறை சேர்மின் உயிர்க்கு அதன் –நேர் நிறை இல்லே nīr numadu enṟu ivai vēr mudal māyttu iṟai sērmin uyirkku adan nēr niṟai illē*

Both [periyavāccān piḷḷai](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2013/10/05/periyavachan-pillai-english/) and [nampiḷḷai](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/09/16/nampillai-english/) explain ahankāram and mamakāram nicely in their vyākhyānam using the following pramāṇa slōkam from srīviṣṇu purāṇam.

*anātmani ātma buddiryā asvē svamiti yā mati: \|*  
*avidyātarusambhūtibījamētat dvividā stittam \|\|*

Considering that which is not [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) (i.e., body) as [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) and considering that which is not one’s property (i.e., [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) and that which is owned by the [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) which are fully owned by [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)) as one’s own are the two seeds for this tree of samsāram (which is the cycle of birth and death based on ones actions). Here ahankāram is considering the [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) as body – dēhātma abhimānm. mamakāram is considering oneself as the owner – sva svātantriyam. Both need to be eradicated and one should understand that oneself is [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) (ahankāram eliminated) and oneself is totally owned by [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) (mamakāram eliminated).

- *nīr numadu enṟu* – You and yours. When instructing others, it is common to use “You and yours”. Also, āḻvār would not say “*nān ennadu*” (I and mine) – since even the thought of such ego will singe his tongue as he is fully realised that he belongs to [emperumān](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/17/divya-dhampathi/) only. Also, ahankāram (*nān*) indicates two aspects  – the egoistic thought of [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) as an independent entity and confusing it with the body. Once we understand that rāvaṇa et al were destroyed due to their egoistic attitude, we can easily give up that ego and independent thought and consider ourselves as subservient to [emperumān](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/17/divya-dhampathi/). We also need to not confuse ourselves with our body. Both aspects need to be eliminated.
- *ivai vēr mudal māyttu* – Eliminating completely. That means developing strong faith that these (ahankāram and mamakāram) are not real goals. When two trees stand bound together, if one tree is poisoned, that will eventually die out and the other tree will survive and grow. Similarly, if the ahankāram and mamakāram (first tree ) are destroyed, the [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) (second tree) will nicely blossom. It can also be explained that if the ahankāram and mamakāram (first tree) are destroyed, samsāram (second tree) will be automatically destroyed. We already saw the viṣṇu purāṇa slōkam which explains ahankāram and mamakāram as the cause for bondage. The remedy is also given in srīviṣṇu purāṇam itself in slōkam 6.7.11 “*acyutāham tavāsmīti saiva samsāra bhēśajam*” (Oh acyuta (one who does not let his devotees slip/fall)! I am being your servant. This thought alone is the remedy for the disease of samsāram/bondage). Since [emperumān](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/17/divya-dhampathi/) who is the rakśaka (protector) is always waiting to protect/uplift us, if only [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) has vilakkāmai (not refusing his help), all hurdles will be removed.
- *iṟai sērmin* – give up unfitting aspects and approach [emperumān](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/17/divya-dhampathi/) who is the true master. [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) approaching [emperumān](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/17/divya-dhampathi/) is like a ship that lost its way finding the shore.
- *uyirkku adan nēr nirai illē* – There is nothing more ideal for the [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) than taking shelter of [emperumān](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/17/divya-dhampathi/). Initially, bhagavat sambandam (realising one’s connection with [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)) will be hitam (like medicine, that which is good but may not be likable that much) and subsequently priyam (very likable). This is most fitting for the [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) which is eternal and known by its jñānam (knowledge), ānandam (bliss) etc.
- Finally, [nampiḷḷai](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/09/16/nampillai-english/) summarises – Just as it is explained in viṣṇu darmam “*samsārārṇava magnānām viśayākrānta cētasām \| viṣṇupōtam vinā nānyat kincidasti parāyaṇam \|\|*” (For the ones who are having the mind which is attached to worldly pleasures and is immersed in the ocean of samsāram, there is no means (to be uplifted) other than the boat of srīviṣṇu who is all pervading), the only means for being uplifted is [emperumān](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/17/divya-dhampathi/) who is explained as the boat that connects both the material and spiritual realm.

In the next article we will the next pāsuram.

## 1.2.4. Illatum ullatum

*illadum uḷḷadum alladu avan uru ellaiyil annalam pulgu paṟṟu aṟṟē*

**Пословный перевод:**

illadum – non-existing, due to constant transformation of the entity itself, acit (matter) is indicated using the word “asat”; uḷḷadum – existing, due to unchanging nature, cit (soul) is indicated using the word “sat”; alladu – not, different from; avan – his; uru – svarūpam (nature); ellaiyil – unlimited; annalam – having (the previously explained) quality of bliss; paṟṟu aṟṟu – giving up attachment towards other worldly pleasures; pullu (pulgu) – approach him with devotion

**Перевод:**

**Simple transalation (based on vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar‘s 12000 padi)**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

If someone says “We can pursue [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) only if he is distinct from and more glorious than the worldly pleasures which are to be given up”, āḻvār explains to them that [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is devoid of any defects, filled with all auspicious qualities, being distinct from [cit](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) and [acit](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/09/thathva-thrayam-achith-what-is-matter/) and because of all of these, he is most enjoyable. Thus, give up attachment to these faulty aspects and approach him.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*nammāḻvār explains the glories of emperumān who is being approached.*

Similar to [nampiḷḷai](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/09/16/nampillai-english/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, nammāḻvār explains the distinct nature of emperumān who is vorśipped after giving up worldly attachments.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*Same as nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

Similar to [nampiḷḷai](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/09/16/nampillai-english/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*nammāḻvār explains the most enjoyable nature of emperumān who is approached which is contrary to the not-so enjoyable nature and defective nature of worldly pleasures which are given up. இல்லதும் உள்ளதும்–அல்லது அவன் உரு எல்லையில் அந்நலம்–புல்கு பற்று அற்றே illadum uḷḷadum alladu avan uru ellaiyil annalam pulgu paṟṟu aṟṟē*

- *illadum* – non-existing – It is not said as non-existing because of lack of pramāṇam (authentic explanation) of [acit](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/09/thathva-thrayam-achith-what-is-matter/) or because of [acit](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/09/thathva-thrayam-achith-what-is-matter/) being an  illusory aspect (as explained by advaita/māyāvāda philosophers). It is due to the fact that [acit](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/09/thathva-thrayam-achith-what-is-matter/) is perishable (has total transformation of itself) that it is said as “*illadu*“.
- *uḷḷadum* – existing – due to the distinction from “*illadu*“, i.e., [cit](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) does not change itself ever, it is called “*uḷḷadu*“.
- *illadum uḷḷadum* – [cit](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) and [acit](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/09/thathva-thrayam-achith-what-is-matter/) are explained as sat and asat in srīviṣṇu purāṇam “*yadasti yannāsti*” (existing and non-existing)  and taittirīya upaniśad “*satyancca anrutanca*” (truth and false). It can also be explained as [acit](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/09/thathva-thrayam-achith-what-is-matter/) which is the abode of [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) and [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) which resides in [acit](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/09/thathva-thrayam-achith-what-is-matter/) – in this context “*il*” in tamiḻ is explained as house and “*uḷ*” is explained as “that which is inside”.
- *alladu avanuru* – his nature is different from [acit](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/09/thathva-thrayam-achith-what-is-matter/) which is perishable and [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) which becomes bound in [acit](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/09/thathva-thrayam-achith-what-is-matter/) (body) and considers “I am enjoying, I am suffering, etc”.
- ellaiyil annalam – Many pramāṇams are highlighted to explain [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s blissful nature. He is explained as such in taittirīya upaniśat “*ānandamaya:*” (filled with bliss), tiruvāimoḻi 1.1.2 “*uṇar muḻu nalam*” (filled with jñānam and ānandam), srīviṣṇu purāṇam 6.5.84 “*samastakalyāṇaguṇātmakōsau*” (naturally having all auspicious qualities) etc.
- pulgu – For one who fully knows the auspicious qualities, [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) who is filled with such auspicious qualities is most enjoyable, similar to embracing a beautiful woman for some one who is desiring worldly pleasure.
- paṟṟu aṟṟē – One should give up other attachments and then pursue emperumān. One cannot be “*iru karaiyan*” – i.e., one who holds on to both viśayāntaram (worldly pleasures) and bhagavat viśayam (devotion towards bhagavān). As explained in tiruvāimoḻi 7.2.7, “*paṟṟilār paṟṟa ninṟānē*“, [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is pursued by the ones who have given up all attachments to viśayāntaram (worldly pleasures) and sādanāntaram (other means to attain him).

In the next article we will the next pāsuram.

## 1.2.5. Arradu parru

*aṟṟadu paṟṟu enil uṟṟadu vīdu uyir seṟṟadu mannuṟil aṟṟu iṟai paṟṟē*

**Пословный перевод:**

paṟṟu – attachments towards aspects outside bhagavat viśayam; aṟṟadu enil – when given up; uyir – ātmā; vīdu – mōkśam; uṟṟadu – attained; adu – that kaivalya mōkśam which is enjoyment of oneself; seṟṟu – eradicate; manna uṟil – approaching bhagavat viśayam firmly to be well engaged; aṟṟu – giving up attachments towards other aspects; iṟai – īsvara; paṟṟu – submit to him

**Перевод:**

**When attachments towards aspects outside bhagavat viśayam are given up, ātmā is fit to attain (kaivalya) mōkśam (being free from samsāram and enjoying oneself).  Eradicating such thought of kaivalya mōkśam, giving up attachments towards everything else and approaching emperumān to be firmly engaged with him, submit to īsvara.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

When giving up attachments towards worldly pleasures, one will see the most shining [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) (self). Without getting trapped in that, one should approach [emperumān](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/17/divya-dhampathi/) at that stage itself to be fully positioned in one’s true nature.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In this 5th pāsuram, nammāḻvār identifies the internal hurdle and remedy for approaching bhagavān.*

Similar to [nampiḷḷai](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/09/16/nampillai-english/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, the venerable emperumān being the most apt goal to be attained is explained by nammāḻvār.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*Similar to nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

Similar to [nampiḷḷai](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/09/16/nampillai-english/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*While approaching emperumān (to be relieved from samsāram), an internal hurdle could arise. nammāḻvār is mercifully giving a remedy for that as well. One who desires indra’s position would not care for wealth in this earthly realm. One who desires for brahmā’s position would not care for indra’s position. One who desires for ātmānubhavam (enjoying one self in kaivalya mōkśam) would not care for any worldly pleasures. One who approaches emperumān who is filled with most auspicious qualities and having eternal divine forms, will not care for any of the previously mentioned aspects. Thus nammāḻvār highlights the internal hurdle and its remedy. அற்றது பற்று எனில்–உற்றது வீடு உயிர் செற்றது மன்னுறில்–அற்று இறை பற்றே aṟṟadu paṟṟu enil uṟṟadu vīdu uyir seṟṟadu mannuṟil aṟṟu iṟai paṟṟē*

- *aṟṟadu paṟṟu enil* – When attachment towards worldly pleasures in the material realm are given up
- *uṟṟadu vīdu uyir* – [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) attained liberation. Pure knowledge and nature of [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) are hidden from oneself due to attachment towards worldly pleasures. Once such attachment is given up through yōgābhyāsam (constant practice of aśtānga yōga), [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) will shine radiantly. Since that is realised as eternal, fully knovledgable and blissful, one may develop attachment towards enjoying oneself.
- *seṟṟu adu* – Completely defacing that thought
- *mannuṟil (manna uṟil)* – When approaching the ultimate goal (bhagavat kainkaryam) which has nothing higher than that
- *aṟṟu iṟai paṟṟē* – While approaching him, have full faith in him and submit to the supreme master. Its also explained as “*iṟai paṟṟi, ittai aṟap pār*” (submit to emperumān and try giving up the attachments to worldly pleasures) as explained in mūnṟām tiruvantādi 14 “*māṟpāl manam suḻippa mangaiyar tōḷ kaivittu*” (by having our mind focussed on [emperumān](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/17/divya-dhampathi/), attachment towards worldly attachments will fall out).

In the next article we will the next pāsuram.

## 1.2.6. Parru ilan

*paṟṟu ilan īsanum muṟṟavum ninṟanan paṟṟu ilai āy avan muṟṟil adangē*

**Пословный перевод:**

īsanum – Even though he is sarvēśvaran (supreme lord); paṟṟu ilan – he is not attached to his divine consorts, nitya sūris et al who are already attached to him; muṟṟavum – attached fully as dāraka (sustaining), pōśaka (nourishment), bhōjñam (enjoyment) etc to us who are newly approaching him; ninṟanan – firmly stood; paṟṟu ilai āy – you too, giving up worldly attachments; avan – towards him; muṟṟil – his qualities of being dāraka (sustaining), pōśaka (nourishment), bhōjñam (enjoyment), etc; adangu – be immersed

**Перевод:**

**Simple transalation (based on vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar‘s 12000 padi)**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*If we approach emperumān, would he accept us?  Is he not the supreme lord (too high to consider engaging with us)?*

Even though he is sarvēśvaran, whoever approaches him, he will manifest friendship. So, you too approach him with friendship and serve him by all means.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*Would īśvara who has many distinct followers accept some one like us who is just approaching emperumān now?*

Similar to [piḷḷān](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2013/04/14/thirukkurugaippiran-pillan-english/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, nammāḻvār explains emperumān‘s equality towards everyone.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*Even if we give up everything and approach him, since he is sarvēśvaran (supreme lord), would he acknowledge us? Considering his easy mingling nature with everyone, even his supremacy will look like vandēṟi (accidental – acquired) for him.*

Similar to [nampiḷḷai](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/09/16/nampillai-english/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*In the previous pāsuram, nammāḻvār explained remedy for internal hurdle. When asked “Since he is explained as the one who has no unfulfilled desires and the master of everyone, would he be attainable by us?” āḻvār replies “He is already naturally interested in engaging with others”. பற்று இலன் ஈசனும் முற்றவும் நின்றனன் பற்று இலை ஐ அவன் முற்றில் அடங்கே paṟṟu ilan īsanum muṟṟavum ninṟanan paṟṟu ilai āy avan muṟṟil adangē*

- *paṟṟilan* – one who has attachment. Its explained as paṟṟu + il (abode or residence of attachment). “*paṟṟilān*” is shortened to be “*paṟṟilan*“. It is like – “*innān ingu uṇḍō?*” (is that person here?). “*ingu illai avan. agattilān*” (He is not here. He is at home). This is based on  [piḷḷān](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2013/04/14/thirukkurugaippiran-pillan-english/)‘s second/alternative explanation of *paṟṟilan* being explained as “one who has attachment”.
- *īsanum* – īśvaratvam (Supremacy) is just natural for him. Great person being easily approachable is a distinct quality (if some one is not very great, being humble and easily approachable is not surprising, but a great person being humble is rare). [nampiḷḷai](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/09/16/nampillai-english/) beautifully quotes srīviṣṇu purāṇa slōkam 5.19.21 “*prasāda paramau nātau mama gēhamupāgatau \| danyōham arccayiśyāmi ityāha mālyōpajīvana: \|\|*” (balarāma and kriṣṇa who are naturally most compassionate have come to my home. Hence, the most humble me is going to worship him – says the one who makes a living by selling flowers).  [nampiḷḷai](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/09/16/nampillai-english/) explains this slōkam beautifully:
   - *prasāda paramau nātau* – you both are most compassionate and easily approachable – it looks very rare for such supreme persons.
   - *mama gēyamupāgatau* – When the great masters are served by their servants, your compassion is very clearly visible by your visit to this humble residence in a narrow lane.
   - *danyōham* – being most fortunate like some one finding a great treasure in the same street where he passes by everyday.
   - *arccayiśyāmi* – I will engage in what is natural servitude for me.
   - *ityāha* – riśi (sage – speaker) is being amazed at mālādara’s (flower vendor) words which resemble the words of nityasūris as explained by [nammāḻvār](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/18/nammazhwar-english/) himself in tiruviruttam 21 “*sūttu nanmālaigaḷ tūyana ēndi*” (nityasūris holding up the pure and good garlands).
   - *mālyōpajīvana:* – One who makes a living out of selling flowers. He was such (business minded) that he would look the other side while making garlands fearing that he may develop attachment to use some flowers for himself,
- *muṟṟavaum ninṟanan* – As explained in bhagavat gītā 9.24 “*samōham sarvabhūtēśu*” (I am equal to all entities), he treats all his devotees equally irrespective of the quality of the ones who approach him.
- *paṟṟilaiyāy* – you too with attachment
- *avan muṟṟil adangē* – As said by srī lakśmaṇa to srī rāma in srī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇṭam 31.25 “*aham sarvam kariśyāmi*” (I will serve in all ways), one should engage in kainkaryams to [emperumān](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/17/divya-dhampathi/).

[nampiḷḷai](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/09/16/nampillai-english/) also highlights [bhattar](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/09/11/parasara-bhattar/)‘s explanation which is also most elegant.

- *parrilan īsanum* – Though he is the abode of all auspicious qualities residing in paramapadam, he is not attached to even nityasūris.
- *muṟṟavum ninṟanan* – Does that bother him? No. He is greatly glorified while accepting a devotee who approaches him for the first time.  This is explained beautifully using srī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇṭam 41.4 “…*tvayi kincit samāpannē kim kāryam sītayā mama*” (srī rāma tells sugrīva (after sugrīva tries to hit rāvaṇa and returns) even if you are hurt a little bit, what is the use of getting sītā back?) – For an animal (sugrīva being a monkey), srī rāma is willing to give up his eternal companion (sītā pirātti).  When a cow gives birth to a new calf, to protect that calf, she will push her other calves away – similarly [emperumān](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/17/divya-dhampathi/) also greatly protects ones who approach him newly.
- *paṟṟilaiyāy* – He was ready to ignore nityasūris for you. Why can’t you give up everything else for him?
- *avan muṟṟil adangē* – accept him as everything. A few pramāṇams are  quoted here:
   - bhagavat gītā 7.19 “*vāsudēvas sarvam*” (everything is vāsudēva)
   - subhāla upaniśat “*mātā pitā brātā nivāsa: saraṇam suhrud gatir nārāyaṇa:*” (nārāyaṇa is Mother, Father, Brother, residence, refuge, well-wisher, goal)
   - “… *ēkaikapalalābhāya sarvalābhāya kēsava:*” (When attaining father, mother et al they fulfil one particular purpose; When attaining kēsava, all purposes are fulfilled).

In the next article we will the next pāsuram.

## 1.2.7. Adangu elil

*adangu eḻil sambattu adangak kaṇḍu īsan adangu eḻil ahdenṟu adanguga uḷḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

adangu eḻil – fully beautiful; sampattu – wealth; adanga – everything without leaving out even a single entity; kaṇḍu – meditating upon; īsan – to īśvara (supreme lord); ahdu – that; adangu eḻil – beautifully subservient; enṟu – thus knowing the relationship; uḷḷē – in that; adanguga – become a part of it

**Перевод:**

**Simple transalation (based on vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar‘s 12000 padi)**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*Though he has a friendly and welcoming attitude, seeing him being the owner of both nitya vibhūti (spiritual realm which exists for his true pleasure) and leelā vibhūti (material realm which exists for his sport), would we able to approach him?*

āḻvār says – Meditating on one’s relationship with [emperumān](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/17/divya-dhampathi/), knowing that “everything is owned by my master”, approach him and serve him without any shyness or hesitation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*Though he has a friendly and welcoming attitude, seeing his greatness of being the owner of the unlimited ubhaya vibhūti (material and spiritual realm), for some one like us, it will be difficult to approach him. So, if we say that we cannot approach him, nammāḻvār says “if we understand our eternal relationship with him, we can console ourselves and approach him without any worries”.*

Similar to [nampiḷḷai](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/09/16/nampillai-english/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, instead of shying away from him seeing his wealth (of ubhaya vibhūti), nammāḻvār says that one should meditate on the relationship between emperumān and his ubhaya vibhūti and one should understand that oneself is among the property of emperumān.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*Similar to nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

Similar to [nampiḷḷai](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/09/16/nampillai-english/)‘s vyākhyānam. [periyavāccān piḷḷai](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2013/10/05/periyavachan-pillai-english/) indicates that [bhattar](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/09/11/parasara-bhattar/) narrates the story of the father and son meeting at a distant place to explain this pāsuram’s meaning.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Previously nammāḻvār said emperumān has a friendly attitude towards everyone. Though he is friendly, he is still the owner of unlimited and great realms (material realm and spiritual realm). The one who is approaching him is too simple and has very inferior senses etc. With this, how can emperumān be approached? When a boat is being tossed around in the ocean, would it not naturally be pushed to the shore? Similarly, emperumān’s greatness will push the jīvātmā to the ultimate goal. But, what if the jīvātmā resists seeing his disqualification and emperumān‘s purity? At that time, the jīvātmā needs to meditate on the relationship between emperumān and himself and realize that he is also a part of emperumān‘s wealth – this sambanda jñānam (understanding the relationship between oneself and bhagavān) is all that is required to approach him. A merchant travels to a distant land while his wife was pregnant to earn money.  She gives birth to a child and he grows up as years pass by. Following the family tradition, the grown-up boy too travels to the same location and camps where his father is doing business. They do not know their father-son relationship yet. A dispute arises between them where they setup their shop and that leads to physical fight. At that time, another person who knows both of them arrives there and highlights their relationship. At once they give up their fight and feel sorry for the days lost in-between. The son submits all his wealth to the father and abides by his father’s desire. As explained in rig vēdam “dvā suparṇā … samānam vrukśam pariśasvajātē” (two birds exist in the same tree…), both jīvātmā and paramātmā exist in the body – while one (jīvātmā) enjoys the fruits of its action, the other one (paramātmā) remains shining, overseeing the activities of the first one. Once we realize that he is the controller and we are the controlled, we can easily approach him. A prince comes across a beautiful garden and hesitates to enter. At that time, if someone says “This is  your father’s property. Feel free to enter and enjoy yourself”, the prince will happily enter the garden. Similarly, one should understand everything is under the control of emperumān – then one can also become part of that. அடங்கு எழில் சம்பத்து அடங்கக் கண்டு ஈசன் அடங்கு எழில் அஃதென்று அடங்குக உள்ளே adangu eḻil sambattu adangak kaṇḍu īsan adangu eḻil ahdenṟu adanguga uḷḷē*

- *adangu eḻil sambattu adangak kaṇḍu* – nitya vibhūti is bhōga bhūmi (place of enjoyment). This (leelā) vibhūti is bound by karmā under his control. While nitya vibhūti can be explained as beautiful, why is leelā vibhūti too explained as beautiful? Considering it as his property and creation, it can also be said to be beautiful and the fact that it is bound by karmā will not be seen important at that stage when we see everything is [emperumān](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/17/divya-dhampathi/)‘s property.
- *adangu eḻil …* – Having seen all the beautiful wealth, meditating that this is the wealth of our apt/true master, one can consider oneself as part of that wealth as well.  By doing so, one can bring joy to one’s master. “*sēśa bhūtanudaiya svarūpa siddi sēśipakkal kincitkārattālēyāy irukkumē*” (The true nature of a servitor will be established only by performing (at least) some small kainkaryams for the master).
- *adanguga uḷḷē* – Based on having knowledge about sva-svāmi bhāvam (property – owner relationship), one can also engage as a part of [emperumān](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/17/divya-dhampathi/)‘s wealth. Though ocean is great/huge, the aquatics which live inside it, can freely swim in it. Similarly, by knowing our relationship with [emperumān](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/17/divya-dhampathi/), he can be easily approached. A grass which does not relate to the ocean is pushed out by the waves to the shore. gataka krutyam (the role of ācārya) is to make one realize his relationship with [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/).

In the next article we will the next pāsuram.

## 1.2.8. Ullam urai

*uḷḷam urai seyal uḷḷa im mūnṟaiyum uḷḷik keduttu iṟai uḷḷil odungē*

**Пословный перевод:**

uḷḷam – mind which is used for meditation, etc; urai – speech which is used for verbal glorification, etc; seyal – body which is used for prostrating, etc; uḷḷa – which we have from the beginning; im mūnṟaiyum – these three which are readily available to us; uḷḷi – understanding their purpose; keduttu – giving up attachment towards worldly pleasures; iṟai uḷḷil – towards the master who is apt for us; odungu – become totally subservient

**Перевод:**

**Simple transalation (based on vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar‘s 12000 padi)**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*What tools are to be used to perform kainkaryam?*

Instead of having to earn the tools, the tools to worship emperumān (mind, speech and body) are already given to us for engaging them in bhagavat viśayam. Meditating upon this aspect, give up attachments towards other aspects and engage them fully in bhagavat viśayam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the 8th pāsuram, nammāḻvār explains the method of worshiping/serving bhagavān.*

Similar to [nampiḷḷai](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/09/16/nampillai-english/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Similar to nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*Similar to nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

Similar to [nampiḷḷai](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/09/16/nampillai-english/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*When asked “when we consider ourselves as part of his wealth, we realise our existence and realise that we have our senses. Would we not need other tools to worship him?” nammāḻvār explains the method of worshiping/serving bhagavān. உள்ளம் உரை செயல் உள்ள இம் மூன்றையும் உள்ளிக் கெடுத்து இறை உள்ளில் ஒடுங்கே uḷḷam urai seyal uḷḷa im mūnṟaiyum uḷḷik keduttu iṟai uḷḷil odungē*

- *uḷḷam urai seyal* – When the mind which is attached to external pleasures is turned inwards (towards the true nature of [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)), it becomes favourable for meditating upon bhagavān. When such meditation deepens, it overflows through speech as explained in tiruvāimoḻi 8.10.4 “*pongēḻ pugaḻgaḷ vāyavāy*” (the glorification of his auspicious qualities that was an outcome of the overflowing experience in mind). The body facilitates falling on [emperumān](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/17/divya-dhampathi/)‘s lotus feet and vorśipping him as explained in srī rāmāyaṇam kiśkintā kāṇḍam 4.12 “*guṇair dāsyamupāgata:*” (serving srī rāma being overwhelmed by his auspicious qualities).
- *uḷḷa immūnṟaiyum* – already existing these three faculties. sēśi (master) himself gave this to the [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)s to serve him; hence the [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) need not look for external tools. Here, iraṇḍām tiruvantādi 21 “*tāmuḷarē*” and mudal tiruvantādi 95 “*nāvāyiluṇḍē*” pāsurams need to be remembered.
- *uḷḷik keduttu* – ānalysing the purpose of these senses and body which are engaged in worldly pleasures, one needs to pull them back from external pleasures and engage them in bhagavat viśayam.
- *iṟai uḷḷil odungē* – Like a farmer who diverts the water from being wasted into dry lands to being used in fertile crops, one should engage these senses and body in bhagavat viśayam which is apt for the true nature of the [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) instead of letting them go astray. *odukku* (control/engage) has become *odungu*.

nampiḷḷai beautifully explains iraṇḍām tiruvantādi 21 “*tāmuḷarē*” pāsuram here.

- *tāmuḷarē* – one exists – one need not go and search for oneself anywhere.
- *tamuḷḷam uḷḷulḷadē* – one need not go and acquire mind from elsewhere to meditate upon [emperumān](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/17/divya-dhampathi/). When one exists, one’s mind exists with oneself too.
- *tāmaraiyin pū uḷatē* – [emperumān](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/17/divya-dhampathi/) also created lotus flowers which can be easily plucked and offered to [emperumān](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/17/divya-dhampathi/). Considering [emperumān](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/17/divya-dhampathi/)‘s greatness and magnanimous nature, all flowers will be accepted by him as explained in periya tirumoḻi 11.7.6 “*kaḷḷār tuḻāy*” pāsuram.
- *ēttum poḻuduṇḍē* – [emperumān](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/17/divya-dhampathi/) created time as well. We need not purchase it from anywhere. We have all the time at our disposal.
- *vāman* – He became vāmana and begged for his own property from mahābali. So, he is willing to accept our offerings by all means.
- *tirumaruvu tāḷ* – His lotus feet which highlight his wealth. This tiruvadi which is so tender as explained tiruvāimoḻi 9.2.10 “*vadiviṇai illā malarmagaḷ maṟṟai nilamagaḷ pidikkum melladi*” (the most tender feet of emperumān which are massaged by the most beautiful srī dēvi and bhūdēvi).
- *maruvu senniyarē* – behold it in one’s head fully. This head is given by him to accept his lotus feet on it.
- *sevvē aru naragam sērvadu aridu* – When *vāman* (One who is so compassionate that he kept his lotus feet even on the heads of nitya samsāris who are fully immersed in worldly pleasures) is present, how can one give up this opportunity and seek out worldly pleasures? Here samsāram (this material realm) itself is identified as *aru naragam* (most difficult hell).

In the next article we will the next pāsuram.
