## 1.2.9. Odunga avan

*odunga avan kaṇ odungalum ellām vidum pinnum ākkai vidum poḻudu eṇṇē*

**Пословный перевод:**

avan kaṇ – unto the master; odunga – being bound to him as per aprutak siddam (inseparable aspect); odungalum – Contraction of ātmā’s knowledge etc; ellām – the cause for such contraction such as avidyā (ignorance) etc; vidum – will leave, will be eradicated; pinnum – After that, as explained in mahābhāratam “krutakrutyā pradīkśantē” (those learned persons who have completed all that is to be done and expecting); ākkai – the remaining life of the current body; vidum poḻudu – end; eṇ – look out for it

**Перевод:**

**As one gives up everything unto the master (bhagavān), avidyā (ignorance) etc and the contraction of ātmā’s knowledge will be eliminated. After that, one can surrender to emperumān and seek out for his kainkaryam at the end of this life itself.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

By engaging our senses in his kainkaryam always, all hurdles will be removed. After that, please wait until the current body dies – that is how long it takes to attain the ultimate result.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In this ninth pāsuram, nammāḻvār says that by approaching emperumān the hurdles which stop us from reaching emperumān will be destroyed. It is only delayed until the end of this body/life.*

Similar to [nampiḷḷai](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/09/16/nampillai-english/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, nammāḻvār explains the removal of hurdles which is the result of worshiping emperumān.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*In this ninth pāsuram – Though worshiping emperumān is easy, aren’t the anādikāla sancitamāna avidyā etc (ignorance, vāsanā, ruci, karmā etc which are accumulated since time immemorial) hurdles for worshiping emperumān? For having the thought “let us worship him” we only need sukrutam (virtue). By engaging in worshiping emperumān due to that sukrutam, the hurdles will be eradicated fully.*

Similar to [nampiḷḷai](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/09/16/nampillai-english/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*ninth pāsuram – In the previous 2 pāsurams, nammāḻvār explained that one should not shy away from emperumān since everyone is eternally related to emperumān (pāsuram 7) and worshiping him is by engaging the senses given by him in his service (pāsuram 8). Are we not worshiping him due to lack of knowledge? We are actually not serving him due to our hurdles. nammāḻvār says that by approaching emperumān, the hurdles will go away. ஒடுங்க அவன் கண் ஒடுங்கலும் எல்லாம் விடும் பின்னும் ஆக்கை விடும் பொழுது என்னே odunga avan kaṇ odungalum ellām vidum pinnum ākkai vidum poḻudu eṇṇē*

- *odunga avan kaṇ* – By you ([jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)) who are prakārabhūta (attribute/mode) becoming part of (approaching) [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) who is prakāri (substratum for all such [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)s). Here becoming part of him is explained as giving up svātantriyam (independence), accepting oneself as fully subservient to him.
- *odungalum ellām vidum* – When what is prāptam (apt/deserving) is pursued, aprāptam (inapt/undeserving) will be eradicated. When what is appropriate for the true nature is pursued, hurdles which are inappropriate for the true nature of [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) will naturally leave. “*odungal*” indicates that this independence is not natural for [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/). It can also be considered that “*odukkal*” became “*odungal*” – *odukkal* indicates binding [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)‘s senses in worldly pleasures.
- *ellām vidum* – avidyā (ignorance), karmā (action/reaction), vāsanā (impressions), ruci (taste) etc will all be removed. Remember periya tiruvandādi pāsurams 54 “*vānō maṟikadalō*” (where did my sins go after pursuing kaṇṇan [emperumān](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/17/divya-dhampathi/)) and 59 “*mādē varappeṟuvarāmenṟē valvinaiyār*” (Will great sins come close to me anymore?) If all hurdles leave him, what does he do?
- *pinnum ākkai vidum poḻudu eṇṇē* – Instead of staying calm thinking “being confident of the upāsanam(devotion), the result will come”, one would anxiously be thinking “since all hurdles are removed,  when would this body fall and achieve the ultimate result without any further obstruction”. Just like a beloved would clean herself of sweat etc and be prepared to engage with her beau, [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) will wait for the removal of the material body to engage with [emperumān](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/17/divya-dhampathi/) (in parampadam). [āṇḍāḷ](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/12/16/andal/) too decorated herself and said in nācciyār tirumoḻi 8.7 “*kongai mēl kungumattin kuḻambaḻiyap pugundu oru nāḷ tangumēl ennāvi tangum*” (When [emperumān](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/17/divya-dhampathi/) comes and embraces me such that the sandalwood paste applied on my bosom is effectively useful, my life will be sustained) and waited for [emperumān](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/17/divya-dhampathi/). As explained in tiruviruttam 1 “*aḻukkudambu*” (dirty/material body), when will this body be removed and the ultimate result be achieved? As explained in  mahābhāratam “*kruta krutyā: … mrutyum priyamivātidim*” (one who has performed what is to be done, waits eagerly for mrutyu dēvatā – the dēvatā for death). *kruta krutyā:* means one who has accepted that emperumān is the means to achieve him (pursued the siddā sādanam – established means). This is explained in  mahābhāratam also as “those who know kriṣṇa truly, are the ones who have performed all that is needed to be performed”. Once on ayanam (varuśa pravēsam – new year day), kunṟattu jīyar approached [emperumānār](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/09/06/emperumanar/) and worshiped his lotus feet. At that time emperumānār says “singappirān! today is an ayanam”. jīyar does not understand the emotions of [emperumānār](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/09/06/emperumanar/) and looks at him curiously. [emperumānār](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/09/06/emperumanar/) says “Once it is sure that the ultimate result will be achieved at the end of this life, a year of those days of waiting is gone! īsn’t this a happy aspect to celebrate for you?” Another time, [embār](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/09/07/embar/) gives a different view point for this – “When the cause of this samsāram, i.e. avidyā etc is eradicated, vouldnt the effect, i.e. the body be naturally eradicated? Wouldn’t the result be accomplished surely? So, what is there to worry about the eradication of this body?”

In the next article we will the next pāsuram.

## 1.2.10. En perukku

*eṇ perukku an nalattu oṇ poruḷ īṟila vaṇ pugaḻ nāraṇan tiṇ kaḻal sērē*

**Пословный перевод:**

eṇ – (As explained in taittirīya upaniśat – ānandavalli about the bliss of bhagavān) for count; perukku – grown infinitely; an nalattu – those auspicious qualities such as bliss etc which match that brahmānandam (bliss of brahmam explained in ānandavalli); oṇ poruḷ – the distinct group of all jīvātmās explained by the phrase (in ānandavalli) “akāmahata srōtriya” (unaffected by desire and most knovledgable); īṟila – innumerable and unlimited; vaṇ pugaḻ – auspicious qualities, having thus; nāraṇan – the master who is known as nārāyaṇan; tiṇ – firm (stable), such that those who approach him are fully protected; kaḻal – lotus feet; sēr – approach, surrender

**Перевод:**

**nārāyaṇan is the owner of infinite jīvātmās, who has auspicious qualities such as ānandam (bliss) etc. He has unlimited auspicious qualities. Surrender unto the firm lotus feet of that master known as nārāyaṇan.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*When asked who is this īsvara who is explained as approachable by everyone?*

īsvara is the one who owns infinite [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)s (who have auspicious qualities such as ānandam etc) and who has most auspicious qualities himself.  Surrender unto his lotus feet which continuously protect those who surrender.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In this 10th pāsuram, nammāḻvār explains tirumantram with its meaning and thus instructs everyone to approach emperumān.*

Similar to [piḷḷān](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2013/04/14/thirukkurugaippiran-pillan-english/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, nammāḻvār explains the complete nature of emperumān being the most apt goal.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*In this 10th pāsuram, nammāḻvār explains that while approaching emperumān, meditate upon tirumantram with its meanings.*

Similar to [piḷḷān](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2013/04/14/thirukkurugaippiran-pillan-english/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*10th pāsuram – Nice. We agree with your suggestions. What is the mantram that anchors our devotion? nammāḻvār explains that tirumantram (astākśaram) is the mantram and instructs that one should meditate on the meaning of that mantram. Others (other than prapannas) use this mantram in japam, hōmam etc to attain their objectives. Our ācāryas knowing that “the meaning of this mantram reminds one’s true nature and leads such persons who meditate on the true meanings to mōkśam”, themselves meditate upon the meanings of the same and also instruct/teach the same to the ones who approach them (for such true knowledge). Both vēdam and āḻvārs(s) realize this mantram, sometimes they explain the mantram and then its meaning; other times they explain the meaning of the mantram first and then the mantram itself. This is because meditating on the meaning always accompanies remembering/realising/reciting the mantram. nammāḻvār says in tiruvāimoḻi 1.3.3 “yāvarum yāvaiyum tānām amaivudai nāraṇan” (nārāyaṇan is such that everyone and everything is a manifestation of his – i.e., everything is his body)  and in tiruvāimoḻi 2.7.2 “nāraṇan muḻu ēḻu ulagukkum nādan” (nārāyaṇan is the lord of all the universes). vēdam too explains similarly as in nārāyaṇa sūktam “antar bahis ca tat sarvam vyāpya nārāyaṇas stita:” (inside, outside and everywhere nārāyaṇan is pervaded) and “nārāyaṇa parōjyōti:” (nārāyaṇan is the supreme light). என் பேருக்கு அந் நலத்து ஒண் பொருள் இறில வான் புகழ் நாரணன் தின் கழல் சேரே eṇ perukku an nalattu oṇ poruḷ īṟila vaṇ pugaḻ nāraṇan tiṇ kaḻal sērē*

- [nammāḻvār](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/18/nammazhwar-english/) explains tirumantram with its meaning through this pāsuram.
- When [kūrattāḻvān](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2013/10/05/kurathazhwan/) was explaining tiruvāimoḻi, for this pāsuram, [āḻvān](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2013/10/05/kurathazhwan/) tells his two sons [parāsara bhattar](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/09/11/parasara-bhattar/) and [srī rāma piḷḷai (vēda vyāsa bhattar)](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2013/04/16/vedha-vyasa-bhattar/) “You hear the meaning of this pāsuram from your ācāryan” (as tirumantram is traditionally explained by one’s own samāsrayaṇa ācārya – both bhattars are direct siśyas of [embār](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/09/07/embar/)). When bhattars get ready to leave, [āḻvān](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2013/10/05/kurathazhwan/) changes his mind and tells them “We never know who will survive even for a moment. So, while you are here you listen to the meaning”, explains the meaning of tirumantram and tells them “Remember this pāsuram as explaining tirumantram”.
- *eṇ perukku* – infinite number of [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)s
- *nalattu* – [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)s are abode of jñānam (knowledge). In the 3rd letter of praṇavam (makāram), [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)s are explained as the abode of jñānam and knover,
- *oṇ poruḷ* – distinct object (knovledgable object) – unlike [acit](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/09/thathva-thrayam-achith-what-is-matter/) (matter) which does not have knowledge, [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) (cit) knows himself through darmi jñānam (consciousness) and other objects through dharma bhūta jñānam (perceptive knowledge).
- *īṟila vaṇpugaḻ nāraṇan* – countless. īṟila is explained with both “*oṇporuḷ*” and “*vaṇpuguḻ*“, i.e., [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) having countless [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)s and countless great qualities. And this combination is the distinct quality of [nārāyaṇan](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/17/divya-dhampathi/). Having infinite eternal [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)s who are of three kinds (nitya – ever-liberated \[and not having any connection with materialistic realm\], mukta – liberated \[from materialistic realm\] and badda – bound souls) and eternal auspicious qualities is the main identity for [nārāyaṇan](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/17/divya-dhampathi/).
- *tiṇ kaḻal sērē* – Knowing that the relationship is eternal between [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) and [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)s, he will never let go of the ones who have clear knowledge about this eternal relationship. His lotus feet are explained as “*tiṇ kaḻal*” (firm feet) to indicate that they will always protect the ones who surrender.
- *sēr* – You surrender unto him. After knowing that he is your own master, surrender immediately. This is “*nama:*” in tirumantram (which explains emperumān is the means to attain him).

## 1.2.11. Sert tadam

*sērt tadat ten kurugūrc catakōpan sol sīrt todai āyirattu ōrtta ip pattē*

**Пословный перевод:**

sēr – abundance; tadam – ponds (water-bodies); then – beautiful; kurukūr – in āḻvārtirunagari; satakōpan – nammāḻvār; sol – word blessed by (āḻvār); sīr – words/phrases which have nice form and meanings; todai – poetic meter; āyirattu – in these 1000 pāsurams; ippattu – this decad which instructs those who surrender; ōrtta – well-analysed

**Перевод:**

**nammāḻvār of beautiful āḻvārtirunagari which has abundance of ponds (showing rich and beautiful environment) blessed words/phrases which have nice form and meanings with poetic meter in this well-analysed decad in these 1000 pāsurams. It is also explained as “ōrtta ippattai sēr” – pursue this well-analysed decad.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

This decad is well-thought-out about [emperumān](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/17/divya-dhampathi/) in these1000 pāsurams which reveal [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s auspicious qualities.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the end, nammāḻvār says that these 10 pāsurams are told by him after analysing the 1000 pāsurams in tiruvāimoḻi which reveal the auspicious qualities of bhagavān.*

Similar to [nampiḷḷai](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/09/16/nampillai-english/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, nammāḻvār says that the result is to understand the most admirable nature of this tiruvāimoḻi (decad) among the whole prabandam.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*Similar to piḷḷān‘s introduction*

Similar to [nampiḷḷai](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/09/16/nampillai-english/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*In the first pāsuram, nammāḻvār said that one should agree to submit oneself unto emperumān after giving up attachments to other aspects. In the second pāsuram, nammāḻvār said that after understanding the defects of other (worldly) aspects, one can easily give them up. In the third pāsuram, nammāḻvār highlighted the nature of what is to be given up briefly. In the fourth pāsuram, nammāḻvār highlighted the glories of emperumān who is to be pursued. In the fifth pāsuram, nammāḻvār highlighted the remedy for the internal hurdle which can occur while pursuing emperumān. In the sixth pāsuram, nammāḻvār explained that emperumān naturally likes to mix with others. In the seventh pāsuram, nammāḻvār said that once we have true knowledge about the relationship with emperumān, one can easily bond with him. In the eighth pāsuram, nammāḻvār explained that we need not seek out for separate tools to pursue him and we can simply use our body and senses which are given to us by him. In the ninth pāsuram, nammāḻvār explained that by engaging body and senses for him, the hurdles for devotion towards him will vanish. In the tenth pāsuram, nammāḻvār highlighted the mantram that is used to worship him. In this pāsuram, he says that these have not been said without analysing; they are said after analysing the well-being of the jīvātmā thoroughly. Alternatively, it is explained as something which is constantly meditated upon since it is for the well-being of the jīvātmā. சேர்த் தடத் தென் குருகூர்ச் சடகோபன் சொல் சீர்த்த தொடை ஆயிரத்து ஆர்த்த இப் பத்தே sērt tadat then kurugūrc catakōpan sol sīrt todai āyirattu ōrtta ip pattē*

- *sērttadam* – It is explained in 3 different ways
   - *sēr tadam* – ponds which are together
   - Since sērttadam is followed by tenkurukūr, it is explained as an adjective to the town, i.e., beautiful tirunagari which has many ponds
   - *sēr* is explained as a verb which indicates approach, bond with etc.
- *tenkurukūrc catakōpan sol* – It is the word of the most-trustworthy person (nammāḻvār)
- *sīrttodai āyiram* – poetic aspects such as words, tune etc. It is also explained as pāsurams which reveal collection (*todai*) of auspicious qualities (*sīr*).
- *āyirattu ōrtta ippattē* – Among the 1000 pāsurams, the most well-wishing decad. Also, it is explained as the decad which analyses what is best for the [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/). Also, it is explained as the decad that is to be constantly meditated upon due to its revealing the best instructions for the [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) among the 1000 pāsurams.

Thus ends the English translation for tiruvāimoḻi 1st centum 2nd decad.

[emperumānār](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/09/06/emperumanar/) tiruvadigaḷē caraṇam  
[piḷḷān](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2013/04/14/thirukkurugaippiran-pillan-english/) tiruvadigaḷē caraṇam  
[nanjīyar](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/09/14/nanjiyar-english/) tiruvadigaḷē caraṇam  
[nampiḷḷai](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/09/16/nampillai-english/) tiruvadigaḷē caraṇam  
[vadakkut tiruvīdip piḷḷai](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/09/17/vadakku-thiruveedhi-pillai-english/) tiruvadigaḷē caraṇam  
[periyavāccān piḷḷai](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2013/10/05/periyavachan-pillai-english/) tiruvadigaḷē caraṇam  
[vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2013/03/22/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar-english/) tiruvadigaḷē caraṇam  
[jīyar](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/09/23/azhagiya-manavala-mamunigal/) tiruvadigaḷē caraṇam

## 1.3 Pattudai adiyavar

## 1.3.1. Pattudai adiyavar

*pattudai adiyavarkku eḷiyavan piṟargaḷukku ariya vittagan malar magaḷ virumbum nam arum peṟal adigaḷ mattuṟu kadai veṇṇey kaḷavinil uravidai āppuṇḍu ettiṟam uralinōdu iṇaindu irundu ēngiya eḷivē*

**Пословный перевод:**

pattudai – having bhakti (devotion); adiyavarkku – for devotees; eḷiyavan – easily approachable; piṟargaḷukku – for those others (who lack devotion); ariya – difficult to reach; vittagan – very wise; malarmagaḷ – (being joyous about the two aspects of being eḷiyavan and ariyavan) one who is having the lotus flower as her residence; virumbum – being desired by; peṟal – to get; arum – difficult; nam adigaḷ – our svāmy (master); mattu – by the churning staff; uṟu – with great effort; kadai – churned; veṇṇey kaḷavinil – while stealing of butter; uravidai – in the chest; āppuṇḍu – being tied/bound; uralinodu iṇaindirundu – staying together with the mortar tirelessly; ēngiya – crying out of fear; eḷivu – simplicity; ettiṟam – how is it possible?

**Перевод:**

**Simple transalation (based on vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar‘s 12000 padi)**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

Such devotion (explained in previous padigam) will not develop unless we experience [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/). But such experience cannot be acquired by our limited senses since he is beyond our senses as explained in [*mananagam*](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/03/thiruvaimozhi-1-1-2-mananaga-malamara/) pāsuram. So, have we lost the opportunity for being uplifted? [āḻvār](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/18/nammazhwar-english/) starts explaining that for those who have the desire to see him, he is easily approachable and for those others he is difficult to be approached. Citing an example of his act of stealing butter, from kriṣṇāvatāram, [āḻvār](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/18/nammazhwar-english/) starts wondering and says “Is it not enough to have appeared as a human being so everyone can approach him? Why should he be bound to a mortar and shiver at the sight of his mother for stealing butter? Why did you he this?”.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*nammāḻvār desirous to cite some examples for emperumān‘s saulabhyam (simplicity), starts instructing based on kriṣṇāvatāram but thinking about his act of stealing butter, āḻvār becomes immersed in that.*

Similar to [piḷḷān](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2013/04/14/thirukkurugaippiran-pillan-english/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Similar to nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*Similar to nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

Similar to [nampiḷḷai](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/09/16/nampillai-english/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Similar to nanjīyar‘s introduction. பத்துடை அடியவர்க்கு எளியவன் பிரர்களுக்கு அறிய வித்தகன் மலர் மகள் விரும்பும் நம் அரும் பெறல் அடிகள் மத்துறு கடை வெண்ணெய் கலவினில் உறவிடை அப்புண்டு எத்திறம் உரலினோடு இனைந்து இருந்து ஏங்கிய எளிவே pattudai adiyavarkku eḷiyavan piṟargaḷukku ariya vittagan malar magaḷ virumbum nam arum peṟal adigaḷ mattuṟu kadai veṇṇey kaḷavinil uravidai āppuṇḍu ettiṟam uralinōdu iṇaindu irundu ēngiya eḷivē*

- *pattu* – Is [āḻvār](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/18/nammazhwar-english/) talking about bhakti (devotion) or para bhakti (the ultimate/full devotion? Here [āḻvār](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/18/nammazhwar-english/) is talking about very basic desire or even the act of not stopping [emperumān](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/17/divya-dhampathi/)‘s mercy. This is because, [āḻvār](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/18/nammazhwar-english/) is talking about [emperumān](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/17/divya-dhampathi/)‘s saulabhyam (simplicity) here and not paratvam (supremacy). As bhagavān himself says in srī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 18.3 “*mithra bhāvēna samprāptam na tyajēyam katancana…*” (When one approaches me with advēśam (no hatred), ābimukhyam (being friendly towards me), I will never give up such persons …). He is seeking out everyone to shower his mercy on that person- all he expects is that desire (which is a natural quality) from the [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/).
- *udai* – having. Having such advēśam, ābimukhyam itself is considered as a great trait. This is the greatest wealth – [emperumān](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/17/divya-dhampathi/) considers such persons who engage in bhagavat viśayam in this world to be greater than nityasūris. He takes on their responsibilities as his own burden. srī vibhiśaṇāḻvān was glorified as antarikśa gatas srīmān (the most wealthy person who has started his airborne journey towards srī rāma) after giving up the wealth of lankā. iḷaiya perumāḷ (srī lakśmaṇa) was glorified as “lakśmaṇō lakśmī sampanna:” (lakśmaṇa who has abundance of kainkarya srī).
- *adiyavarkku* – for the devotees. this is also per [emperumān](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/17/divya-dhampathi/)‘s consideration – he considers even those who have basic desire as equivalent to srī mahālakśmi et al.
- *eḷiyavan* – he presents himself completely under their control. When arjuna asked kriṣṇa “Why you are attached to your devotees even though I have heard about you as “*param brahma param dāma…*” (supreme brahmam, the supreme abode, etc)?” kaṇṇan [emperumān](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/17/divya-dhampathi/) replies “This is natural for me”. Unlike princes who give some commitments during difficult times to others but will take back their commitment when they become princely again, bhagavān always shows his simplicity towards his devotees – he would even go as a messenger for them.
- *piṟargaḷukku ariya vittagan* – vittagan in tamiḻ is the same as vismanīya (astonishing) in samskrutam. Here piṟar (others) are those who want to use [emperumān](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/17/divya-dhampathi/) for their personal benefits. He is uncontrollable for them. Here the astonishing aspect is that though he is totally under the control of yasōdā et al he was uncontrollable by pūtanā et al. When kriṣṇa was resting before the kurukśētra battle began, arjuna and duryōdana came to him – he gave himself to arjuna and gave pangaḷam (his soldiers – worthless in comparison to him) to duryōdana. Just like our ācāryas accepted only [emperumān](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/17/divya-dhampathi/) as upāyam (as in the case of arjuna) and others held other acētanams (insentient – karma, jñāna, bhakti yōgams etc) as upāyam (as in the case of duryōdana). When srī lakśmaṇa got hurt and fainted in the battlefield, rāvaṇa came along with his soldiers and tried to carry him – but he could not lift him due to the hatred he had. But hanuman came and lifted lakśmāṇa most casually since he was greatly devoted. It is not that lakśmaṇa tricked rāvaṇa – it was just natural that hanuman could lift him. Note: Whatever is said for lakśmaṇa applies to srī rāma as well.
- *malarmagaḷ virumbum* – His supremacy and simplicity are due to his connection with srī mahālakśmi.
- *nam arum peṟal adigaḷ* – nam (our) highlights his established supremacy as in puruśa sūktam etc. Here lakśmī sambandam (connection to srī mahālakśmī) is also established by vēdam.  Being dear to srī mahālakśmi is the main criterion for being the supreme lord.
- *mattuṟu kadai veṇṇey* – [āḻvār](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/18/nammazhwar-english/) further explains the simplicity which was highlighted in the beginning of the pāsuram. Its the same valiant bhagavān with great shoulders which churned the milk ocean – now being caught for stealing butter in this cow-herd community. “*kadai veṇṇey*” indicates past, present and future tenses. [piḷḷān](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2013/04/14/thirukkurugaippiran-pillan-english/) explains that when the curd is being churned (even before butter fully forms), kaṇṇan [emperumān](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/17/divya-dhampathi/) grabs it and eats it just like a hungry person would even grab half-boiled rice.
- *uravidai* *āppuṇḍu* – bound in the chest area. He was bound where [srī mahālakśmi](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/17/divya-dhampathi/) resides. ōr it can also be said as “the one who is majestic like bull is bound now”. It can also be considered as “*udaram*” being said as “*uram*” – udaram means waist as one of his names is dāmōdaran (one who is bound by rope in the waist area). When caught stealing butter, yasōdā māta binds him with the mortar and threatens him “if capable you can release yourself”.
   - That brahmam which is hailed in svētasvatāra upaniśat as “…*parāsya saktir vividaiva srūyatē…*” – that supreme bhagavān’s who has full ability is being bound here.
   - The one who is the cause for everything (being bound in samsāram, sustenance and liberation) is being bound here.
   - The one who controls brahmā et al merely by his will is being bound by a simple cow-herd girl.
   - As explained in bhagavat gītā 4.10 “…*tyaktvā dēham punar janma* *naitē māmēti…*” – one who said “you will reach me and never be bound in this samsāram” again is being bound here to relieve us from the samsāram.
- *uralinōdu iṇaindirundu* – he stood just like the mortar without any movement (out of fear).
- *ēngiya* – the stage before crying – seeing helplessly, lips quivering, etc.  This is the only difference between kriṣṇa and the mortar now.
- *ettiṟam* – One who was said in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.1.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/03/thiruvaimozhi-1-1-1-uyarvara-uyarnalam/) as “*uyarvaṟa uyarnalam udaiyavan*” is like this. He is glorified in taittiriya upaniśat as “*yatō vācō nivarttantē*” (beyond the reach of words) for his supremacy – now we are seeing that in his simplicity. [āḻvār](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/18/nammazhwar-english/) cannot comprehend as to how [emperumān](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/17/divya-dhampathi/) presents himself as such helpless child even after being the most supreme lord.

In the next article we will the next pāsuram.

## 1.3.2. Elivarum iyalvinan

*eḷivarum iyalvinan nilai varambila pala piṟappāi oḷivaru muḻunalam mudalila kēdila vīdām teḷidaru nilaimaiyadu oḻivilan muḻuvadum iṟaiyōn aḷivarum aruḷinōdu agattanan puṟattanan amaindē*

**Пословный перевод:**

nilai – a position (without discriminating based on birth, activities etc); varambu – boundary; ila – not having; pala – many different types of; piṟappāy – one who is with (such) births; mudalila kēdila muḻunalam – full auspicious attributes which are without beginning and ending; oḷivarum – radiant; eḷivarum iyalvinan – having natural simplicity; vīdām – (even being like this) mōkśam; teḷi tarum – that which gives clarity; adu – that; nilaimai – position; muḻuvadum – completely; oḻivilanāna – ever-existing; iṟaiyōn – svāmy (master); aḷivarum – naturally helpful; aruḷinōdu – with mercy; amaindu – present; agattanan – residing within the devotees; puṟattanan – staying away from the others

**Перевод:**

**emperumān appears in different types of life without any boundary with his full auspicious qualities which are without both a beginning and and end. Despite being supreme, he is naturally simple and is radiant because of that and though he is simple, he is still capable of liberating any one which leads to pristine knowledge about everything. Such ever-existing emperumān who is our master who is naturally helpful, is mercifully present within his devotees and stays away for the others. From this, it can be understood that his qualities shine radiantly in his incarnations (even more than in paramapadam).**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*nammāḻvār started speaking about bhagavān‘s simplicity in his avatārams, but after meditating on his unlimited simplicity of being bound in the mortar and trembling out of fear, āḻvār who is beyond the control of prakruti (matter/body), became controlled by prakruti (fainted and became unconsicous) and then after regaining consciousness started elaborating bhagavān‘s simplicity.*

Being simple means assuming different forms of life without discriminating between them (being born in human, animal, plant etc forms) and their activities. Even while being born in such forms, he carries along all his eternal auspicious qualities and abilities such as giving mōkśam to others etc. Being born like this, he presents himself to his devotees and for the others he is unapproachable.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*After enjoying emperumān‘s saulabhyam (simplicity), āḻvār starts instructing about his saulabhyam in a detailed manner.*

Similar to [piḷḷān](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2013/04/14/thirukkurugaippiran-pillan-english/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*śubseqently, āḻvār instructs about the speciality of emperumān‘s avatārams.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*Becoming bewildered after experiencing emperumān‘s saulabhyam, āḻvār faints and stays unconscious for 6 months. Subsequently, he becomes conscious again and starts instructing about his saulabhyam in detail.*

Similar to [nampiḷḷai](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/09/16/nampillai-english/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*It is well-known that hailing “ettiṟam” (how is this possible?) āḻvār fainted and remained unconscious for 6 months. When he was lying unconscious madurakavi āḻvār and his associates carefully took care of him just like srī guhap perumāḷ (guhan) watched sītā pirātti and srī rāma sleeping during their visit to his place. It looked similar to birds thronging a well-ripened fruit-bearing tree. When sītā pirātti and srī rāma were traveling, they rested at guha’s place and guha watched them carefully. When bharatāḻvān came looking for them, guha showed him the place where they rested. bharata became unconscious thinking about them (having had to rest with very minimal comforts contrary to the princely life they were used to) and later regained consciousness. Similarly, āḻvār too lost his consciousness thinking about emperumān‘s saulabhyam. As a great fortune for the sātvikas (good persons – fully devoted to emperumān) of āḻvārtirungari, as said in tiruviruttam 100 “nallār navil kurugūr” (āḻvārtirungari which is the abode of good persons), he regained conscious. When he asked where he stopped before losing consciousness, madurakavi āḻvār and others carefully told him, “You said ‘ettiṟam‘ and fainted” instead of reminding about “pattudai adiyavarkku eḷiyavan” which may cause him to faint again. In the first pāsuram, he experienced emperumān though he wanted to instruct others. In this pāsuram, he starts instructing others. எளிவரும் இயல்வினன் நிலை வரம்பில பல பிறப்பை ஒளிவரு முழுநலம் முதலில கேடில விடாம் தெளிதரு நிலைமையது ஒழிவிலான் முழுவதும் இறையோன் அழிவரும் அருளினோடு அகத்தனன் புறத்தனன் அமைந்தே eḷivarum iyalvinan nilai varambila pala piṟappāi oḷivaru muḻunalam mudalila kēdila vīdām teḷidaru nilaimaiyadu oḻivilan muḻuvadum iṟaiyōn aḷivarum aruḷinōdu agattanan puṟattanan amaindē*

- *eḷivarum iyalvinan* – Having simplicity as a natural quality. He is not simple towards his friends alone – even towards others he manifests his simplicity. Everyone is simple at times. For him its always present – it is svarūpam (natural) for him.
- *nilai varambila* – pūrvācāryas explained this as “there is no condition on the type of birth and type of activities”. But [bhattar](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/09/11/parasara-bhattar/) explained it as “there is no condition in any type of birth – but whatever may be the birth, he is not limited”. Even while being a charioteer for arjuna (which is considered very humble), he manifested visvarūpam. Similarly, he was going to rudran at kailāsam seeking offspring but on his way he gives mōkśam to gaṇṭā karṇan. He lifted gōvardana hill, being a seven year old boy. Thus there is no boundary for him even in humble situations – the only aim for him is to protect his devotees and he will do it in any situation.
- *pala piṟappāy* – Many many births. He himself (who is absolutely knovledgable) says in gītā 4.5 “*bahūni*” (many). vēdam which says truth as it is, says in puruśa sūktam “*bahudā vijāyatē*” (many births). āḻvārs who are blessed by [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) with flawless knowledge say “*pala piṟappu*” (many births). He likes to present himself in such forms (instead of showing his supremacy) and does not feel guilty about it.
- *oḷivaru muḻunalam* – Unlike [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) who acquires a body due to karmā which leads to hiding of his knowledge etc., [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s birth means “The humbler his form, the more radiant his auspicious qualities” (since he takes them on willingly to help others). In yajur vēdam its seen “…*sa u srēyān bhavati jāyamāna:*” (…that [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) takes birth. After taking birth, he acquires great radiance). Here “u” is explained as “Eva” (only) which means, he becomes great only by descending into this samsāram with various forms.
- *mudalila kēdila* – These qualities are eternal – they do not appear and disappear.
- *vīdām*… – mōkśa pradatvam (granting of mōkśam) is separately explained because the whole purpose of his births is to uplift others. *teḷi taru* – that which gives absolute knowledge – when the [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) reaches paramapadam, he gets full knowledge. This samsāram is such that, it is even capable of confusing [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) himself (In arumpadam, it is highlighted that, this is explained to show the difference between samsāram and paramapadam – not to say that [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) can be confused in this material world).
- *iṟaiyōn* – Only [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) has the quality of mōkśa pradatvam (granting of liberation). Even in avatārams, that quality is preserved by him.
- *aḷivarum aruḷinōdu* – compassion as necessary; unconditional compassion.
- *agattanan* – For his devotees (pāṇḍavas for example), he will present himself as a humble messenger who ties the envelope of message \[on a palm leaf\] around his neck and goes to the destination.
- *puṟattanan* – For others (kauravas for example), even in such state of being so humble, they cannot approach/accept him.

In the next article we will the next pāsuram.

## 1.3.3. Amaivudai araneri

*amaivudai aṟaneṟi muḻuvadum uyarvaṟa uyarndu amaivudai mudalkedal odividai aṟanilam aduvām amaivudai amararum yāvaiyum yāvarum tānām amaivudai nāraṇan māyaiyai aṟibavar yārē*

**Пословный перевод:**

amaivu – leading to result; udai – having; aṟam – darmam (virtuous path); neṟi – history; muḻuvadum – fully, in all; uyarvaṟa uyarnda – top most; amaivu – position; udai – having; mudal kedal – sruśti (creation) and samhāram (dissolution); idai odivu – avāntara samhāram (annihilation that happens in-between); aṟa – abundance; nilam aduvām – being able; amaivu – intelligent; udai – having; amararum – dēvas starting with brahmā; yāvaiyum – all acētanas (insentients); yāvarum – all cētanas (sentients); tānām – being himself; amaivu – position; udai – having; nāraṇan – srīman nārāyaṇan’s; māyaiyai – the magnificent aspect of his avatārams; yār aṟibavar – who knows?; amaivu – apt

**Перевод:**

**dēvas such as brahmā et al have darmam (virtuous path) that leads to proper result, have attained high position to be engaged in creation, annihilation etc and are very capable/intelligent. Even such dēvas starting with brahmā cannot comprehend the magnificent nature of the incarnations of the most apt (for being the supreme lord) srīman nārāyaṇan who sustains all cētanas (sentients) and acētanas (insentients).**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

Similar to [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2013/03/22/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar-english/)‘s vyākhyānam (simple translation).

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In this 3rd pāsuram, nammāḻvār says that the glories of the confidential nature of the birth/appearance of srīman nārāyaṇan, who is the supreme lord, are incomprehensible even for brahmā et al, who are greatly knovledegable.*

Similar to [nampiḷḷai](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/09/16/nampillai-english/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, nammāḻvār says that the avatāra rahasyam (the confidentiality of bhagavān‘s births) cannot be understood by anyone.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*Similar to nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

Similar to [nampiḷḷai](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/09/16/nampillai-english/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*In the first pāsuram, āḻvār said bhagavān is eḷiyan (very simple). In the next pāsuram, his simplicity was elaborated.  In this pāsuram, āḻvār says that his avatāra rahasyam cannot be comprehended by any one. amaivudai aṟaneṟi muḻuvadum uyarvaṟa uyarndu amaivudai mudalkedal odividai aṟanilam aduvām amaivudai amararum yāvaiyum yāvarum tānām amaivudai nāraṇan māyaiyai aṟibavar yārē*

- *amaivudai aṟaneṟi…* – The path of darmam which leads to the result surely like dasarata cakravarty performing yāgam and soon benefiting with 4 gems (4 children). Like [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is complete in auspicious qualities, brahmā et al are complete in virtues.
- *amaivudai mudal kedal…* – When brahmā creates, everyone wonders if creation was done by [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) himself – he is so meticulous. Similar is the case with samhāram etc. This also includes avāntara samhāram etc (intermediate annihilation, creation etc). **Note**: brahmā lives for 100 years of 360 days each. There are innumerable brahmās. Under each brahmā, 14 lōkams exist. In each day of brahmā \[12 hours\], there are 1000 catur yugams. At the end of brahmā’s day, viz. during the night \[12 hours\], there is no activity. At the end of brahmā’s life, there is mahā praḷayam (everything is consumed by [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)). The 1000 yugams are divided into 14 manvantarams (about 70 catur yugams approximately) – each manvantaram has one indra, one manu, sapta riśis (seven riśis) etc. At the end of each manvataram, 10 lōkas, up to svarga lōka (5th lōkam coming down from brahma lōka) are dissolved and a new set of 10 lōkas get created again. This could be called as avāntara praḷayam and avāntara sruśti. At the end of each catur yugam also, lots of annihilation occurs at various locations and dharma will be re-established through fresh progeny. This could also be called as avāntara praḷayam and avāntara sruśti.
- *aṟa nilam aduvām* – top-most virtue. brahmā et al are so capable that they need not hear the instructions from [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) even for a second time. They become very obedient and submissive on learning their tasks from [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/).
- *yāvaiyum yāvarum* – All [acētanas](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/09/thathva-thrayam-achith-what-is-matter/) (insentient entities) and [cētanas](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) (sentient entities)
- *tānām amaivudai nāraṇan* – being the antaryāmi for all [cit](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) and [acit](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/09/thathva-thrayam-achith-what-is-matter/) – [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is the prakāri (object or substrate) and they are all his prakāra (forms/attributes).
- *māyaiyai aṟibavar yārē* – It is so difficult to comprehend because he chose to be born as the son of nandagōpa who is one of his prakāram (form) and made him consider that “this is my son”.
- *aṟibavar yārē* – Who can comprehend this greatness? No one can.
   - nityasūris cannot comprehend this since they are fully engaged in enjoying [emperumān](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/17/divya-dhampathi/) in paramapadam.
   - samsāris cannot comprehend this since they don’t have faith in [emperumān](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/17/divya-dhampathi/).
   - brahmā et al are depending on self-effort, so they cannot comprehend this unlimited greatness of [emperumān](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/17/divya-dhampathi/).
   - āḻvārs who are blessed by [emperumān](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/17/divya-dhampathi/) himself, cannot comprehend this since they are immersed in enjoying such [emperumān](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/17/divya-dhampathi/) in these incarnations and they cannot come out of it to comprehend it.
   - The omniscient lord himself cannot comprehend this since he himself says in bhagavat gītā 4.9 “*janma karma ca mē divyam*” (my birth and activities are so divine that I myself am bewildered thinking about them).

In the next article we will the next pāsuram.

## 1.3.4. Yarumor nilaimaiyan

*yārum ōr nilaimaiyan ena aṟivaraiya emperumān yārum ōr nilaimaiyan ena aṟiveḷiya emperumān pērum ōr āyiram piṟa pala udaiya emperumān pērum ōr uruvamum uḷadillai iladillai piṇakkē*

**Пословный перевод:**

pērum – names which highlight the divine forms; piṟa – the many other forms which are highlighted by those names; pala āyiram – many thousands; udaiya – being visible having such names/forms; yārum – those unfavourable ones even though they may be greatly knovledegable; ōr nilaimaiyan – having a state; ena – thus; aṟivariya – difficult to know/understand; emperumān – the one who is my master accepting service from me; yārum – those devotees even though they may be very ignorant; ōr nilaimaiyan – having a state; ena – thus; aṟiveḷiya – easy to know/understand; emperumān – to the one who is my master accepting service from me; ōr pērum – a name; ōr uruvamum – a form; uḷadillai – not present for such unfavourable persons; iladillai – not absent for such favourable persons; piṇakku – eternal argument/doubt

**Перевод:**

**emperumān has many names which highlight his divine forms and many other forms which are highlighted by those names. He is visible through such many thousands of those forms. Such emperumān is having a state that is not understandable by those who are not devoted to him and is understandable by those devotees even though they may be very ignorant. For such unfavourable ones, he is never present with a form and name. For such favourable ones, he is never absent (implying always present) with a form and name.  Thus, there will be constant debate about his existence and non-existence. Here, āḻvār blissfully says emperumān many times in this pāsuram, realising the favours bhagavān has done to him.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

No matter how great one may be, if one is unfavourable towards [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/), they cannot understand “He is like this”. No matter how meek/ignorant one may be, if one is favourable towards [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/), they can understand “He is like this”. Knowing “He is like this” implies – [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) who has unlimited auspicious qualities assumes unlimited forms to protect his devotees. For the unfavourable ones, since they don’t understand this nature of his in a name and form, “He does not exist”. For the favourable ones, since they understand his nature properly, “He does exist”. Thus, there will always be this confusion about his existence.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In this 4th pāsuram, when asked if these incarnations of bhagavān are comprehensible by any one, nammāḻvār replies that they can be easily comprehended by the devotees and very difficult to comprehend for those who are not devotees.*

Similar to [nampiḷḷai](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/09/16/nampillai-english/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, nammāḻvār says bhagavān who has many forms and names through these incarnations, is not comprehensible to those who are unfavourable towards him and comprehensible to the favourable ones – this will continue forever.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*Similar to nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

Similar to [nampiḷḷai](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/09/16/nampillai-english/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Similar to nanjīyar‘s introduction. yārum ōr nilaimaiyan ena aṟivaraiya emperumān yārum ōr nilaimaiyan ena aṟiveḷiya emperumān pērum ōr āyiram piṟa pala udaiya emperumān pērum ōr uruvamum uḷadillai iladillai piṇakkē*

- *yārum…* – The first “yārum” (whoever) indicates the unfavourable ones – no matter how intelligent (most intelligent) they are, because they will try to understand [emperumān](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/17/divya-dhampathi/) (my master) with their self-efforts, they will fail to understand him. In arumpadam some pāsurams are shown to explain this – mudal tiruvandādi 56 “*nērē kadikkamalattuḷ irundum kāṇgilān*”  (despite being in the lotus flower from [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s navel, he \[brahmā\] does not see [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)), tiruvāimoḻi 7.7.11 “*katkariya piraman sivan indiran enṟivarkkum katkariya kaṇṇan*” (kriṣṇa is difficult to be seen/understood by brahmā, rudra, indra who are difficult to be seen by us)
- *yārum… –* The second “*yārum*” (whoever) indicates the favourable ones – no matter how ignorant (most ignorant) they are, because they understand his glories as revealed by him. We saw this in the lives of monkey (sugrīva), hunter girl (sabari), cow-herd girl (yasōdā).
- [*emperumān*](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/17/divya-dhampathi/) – Being amazed by this great quality of being understandable and not-understandable at the same time, āḻvār declares him to be [emperumān](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/17/divya-dhampathi/) (my master). [āḷavandār](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/09/01/alavandhar/) too glorifies [emperumān](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/17/divya-dhampathi/) in stōtra ratnam 21 “*namō namō vāngmanasāti bhūma yē namō namō vāngmanasaikabhūmayē…*” (I offer my obeisances to you who are beyond the mind and words; I offer my obeisances to you who are in reach of mind and words).
- *pērum ōr āyiram* – In mahābhāratam bhīśma declares “…*dēvo nāma sahasravān*” (that radiant vorśippable [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) has thousands of names). There is no limit for the words (names) which explain his guṇams (auspicious qualities) and svarūpam (true nature).
- *piṟa palavudaiya* – having many divine forms. How can “*piṟa*” (other) refer to forms? This is based on precedence seen in sāstram where nāma (name) is followed by rūpa (form). In viṣṇu purāṇam 1.5.6, it is said that “*nāma  rūpanca bhūtānām…*” (brahmā created names, forms and activities for entities such as dēvas et al). In cāndōjña upaniśat 6.3.178, it is said that “*…anēna jīvēna ātmanānupravisya nāma rūpē vyākaravāṇī…*” (I (brahmam) enter through these [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)s as antaryāmi and give them names and forms). Not only that, he himself says subsequently in this pāsuram itself “*pērum ōr uruvamum*” (name and form).
- *pērum oṟ uruvamum* – auspicious name and divine form
- *uḷadillai* – For those who are unfavourable, it will be difficult to understand even at a gross level (since they are not seeing any of the auspicious qualities and the divine forms as they are).
- *iladillai* – For those who are favourable, since they see him with his qualities and form, he cannot be made non-existent ever.
- *piṇakkē* – Since the devotees see everything, they will constantly be performing mangaḷāsāsanam. Since the others do not see anything, they will not even approach him. In between these, āḻvār is happy to see the [emperumān](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/17/divya-dhampathi/) eternally.

In the next article we will the next pāsuram.

## 1.3.5. Pinakkara aruvagai

*piṇakkaṟa aṟuvagaic camayamum neṟi uḷḷi uraitta kaṇakkaṟu nalattanan andamil ādi am pagavan vaṇakkudait tavaneṟi vaḻi ninṟu puṟaneṟi kaḷai kattu uṇakkumin pasai aṟa avanudai uṇarvu koṇḍu uṇarndē*

**Пословный перевод:**

aṟuvagaic camayamum piṇakku aṟa – Removing the confusions which are in the six philosophical systems and eliminating the debate of such philosophers with vaidikas (the followers of vēdam); neṟi – the path of vēdam; uḷḷi – analysed; uraitta – mercifully spoken/explained; kaṇakkaṟu nalattanan – unlimited auspicious qualities such as audārya (generosity), āsrita vātsalya (motherly forbearance towards the surrendered persons) etc; andamil – endless; ādi – eternal since he is the cause of everything; am – hēya pratibatan (rivalling all inauspicious aspects); pagavan – bhagavān who is the abode of auspicious qualities such as jñānam, sakti etc; vaṇakku – nama: etc (vorśipping); udai – having; tava neṟi vaḻi – bhakti mārgam (path of bhakti); ninṟu – being stable; puṟa neṟi – giving up useless paths as explained in muṇḍaka upaniśat “anyā vācō vimuncata” (give up talking about the other aspects); kaḷai – weed; kattu – removing; avanudai – in his matters; uṇarvu koṇḍu – through bhakti rūpa jñānam (knowledge matured into devotion); uṇarndu – having seen; pasai – attachment due to vāsanā (impressions); aṟa – to remove; uṇakkumin – eliminate it

**Перевод:**

**bhagavān who is eternal (being the cause), who is endless, who is filled with auspicious qualities such as audāryam, āsrita-vātsalyam etc., who is rivalling all inauspicious qualities, analysed the vēdam and compassionately eliminated the confusions which existed between avaidikas (followers of six philosophical systems mainly) and vaidikas.  Being situated in such bhakti yōgam explained in srī bhagavat gītā, understanding the glorious aspects of bhagavān, giving up attachments to other paths which are like weeds, giving up focus on everything other than emperumān, with the help of devotion towards him and seeing him, one should eliminate such attachments fully.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*When there is confusion about his existence, how to establish the truth about him?*

To eliminate the confusion between the unfavourable persons who follow the six philosophies and the favourable ones who follow vēdam, he \[bhagavān\] himself who is omniscient naturally, yet analyzed thoroughly and presented in srī bhagavat gītā that

- he ([bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)) is the object of all of vēdam
- the vēdam is blemiśless due to its being not created by any one and
- these six philosophies which speak contrary to vēdam are not authoritative source of information

So, giving up attachments to worldly pleasures, through bhakti yōgam, approach [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) who compassionately revealed the important principles of vēdam. How to give up worldly pleasures? Contemplate on the most auspicious qualities of [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) which are explained in gītā and after understanding his glories, give up the attachment to worldly pleasures which are insignificant.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In this 5th pāsuram, considering that he is unreachable for the ones desiring to approach him (due to his supremacy), nammāḻvār instructs everyone to approach emperumān through bhakti yōgam as presented by emperumān himself in srī bhagavat gītā.*

Similar to [nampiḷḷai](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/09/16/nampillai-english/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār explains that emperumān should be approached through bhakti as explained clearly in srī bhagavat gītā which was blessed by himself.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*Same as vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar‘s introduction*

Similar to [nampiḷḷai](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/09/16/nampillai-english/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*5th pāsuram. āḻvār! you said worship emperumān many times, But what is the method of such worship? āḻvār replies “Should I explain this separately? bhagavān himself explained the path of bhakti in srī bhagavat gītā. You follow that and approach him”. piṇakkaṟa aṟuvagaic camayamum neṟi uḷḷi uraitta kaṇakkaṟu nalattanan andamil ādi am pagavan vaṇakkudait tavaneṟi vaḻi ninṟu puṟaneṟi kaḷai kattu uṇakkumin pasai aṟa avanudai uṇarvu koṇḍu uṇarndē*

- *piṇakkaṟa aṟuvagaic camayamum* – In the arumpadam, the six systems are listed as sākya (baudda), ulūkya (vaisēśika), akśapāda (naiyyāyika), kśapaṇaka (jaina), kapila (sānkya), patanjali (yōga)
- *neṟi uḷḷi uraitta* – Just like someone who does not have full understanding will analyse it thoroughly and explain, [emperumān](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/17/divya-dhampathi/) too analysed the subject matter of vēdam deeply and then explained. Even though he can explain it instantaneously, out of great attachment towards the well-being of arjuna, if he says quickly, someone may complain that “kriṣṇa explained the principles quickly without thinking through”. To avoid such fault-finding by others, he analysed it thoroughly and explained the same.
- *kaṇakkaṟu nalattanan* – It can be said as – He has unlimited auspicious qualities or he has unlimited attachment towards arjuna (and his devotees). No one requested him to explain these principles – it was out of motherly affection that he revealed these important principles.
- *andamil* – endless. When someone says something just out of love/attachment, would that be true/beneficial? He is endless. Only when there is binding of karmā through birth/death, there is expansion/contraction of jñānam (knowledge). Since, he is endless, he is akarmavasyan (not controlled by karmā).
- am pagavan –  The word [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) truly rests on [srīman nārāyaṇan](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/17/divya-dhampathi/) only. It is attributed on persons who have some minor glories (brahmā, vyāsa bhagavān, vālmīki bhagavān et al) – those are just for praising such qualities as explained in srī viṣṇu purāṇam 6.5.77 “*anyatra hyupacārata*:” (In case of others such as dēvas et al the term ‘[bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘ is used as ceremonial glorification).
- *am pagavan vaṇakkudait tavaneṟi vaḻininṟu –* This bhakti yōgam explained by [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) in gītā is most enjoyable since bhakti is focussed on glorifying bhagavān’s auspicious qualities. Just as how materialists \[those who are not devoted to emperumān\] would enjoy embracing a woman (being fully immersed in it), devotees would enjoy glorifying bhagavān’s qualities. Here, [āḻvār](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/18/nammazhwar-english/) uses “*vaṇakkudai*” since kriṣṇa said in srī bhagavat gītā 9.34 “*mām namaskuru*” (offer obeisances to me). [āḻvār](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/18/nammazhwar-english/) indicates bhakti through the word “tava” (tapas) since
   - bhakti is a special state of jñānam.
   - It is also based on muṇḍaka upaniśat 1.1.10 “*yasya jñānamayam tapa:*” (brahmam’s tapas/sankalpam is filled with jñānam) – jñānam and tapas are thus related.
   - It is also based on [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) considering such devotee’s prēma (devotion) itself as tapasya (austerity).
- *puṟa neṟi kaḷai kattu* – Eliminating other aspects. In case of *neṟi* being considered as bhakti, one should eliminate all desires which are aimed at achieving something other than kainkaryam. In case of *neṟi* being considered as prapatti, all other upāyams should be eliminated.
- *uṇakkumin pasaiyaṟa* – give up such attachments with ruci (taste) and vāsanā (impressions).
- *avanudai uṇarvu koṇḍu uṇarndu* – How to give up such attachments?
   - Through gaining knowledge on him, or
   - Through knowledge explained by him, or
   - Through the path of devotion, or
   - Through holding on to the principle explained by him in carama slōkam.

In the next article we will the next pāsuram.

## 1.3.6. Unarndu unarndu

*uṇarndu uṇarndu iḻindu aganṟu uyarndu uruviyanda in nilaimai uṇarndu uṇarndu uṇarilum iṟai nilai uṇarvaridu uyirgāḷ uṇarndu uṇarndu uraittu uraittu ari ayan aran ennum ivarai uṇarndu uṇarndu uraittu uraittu iṟainjumin manappattadu onṟē*

**Пословный перевод:**

uṇarndu uṇarndu – Since jīvātmā is naturally knowledgeable, being the one who realises oneself constantly; iḻindu aganṟu uyarndu – since that jñānam (knowledge) is unlimited in its pure form, pervading in all directions; uru – unlike acit which can be in a form/shape; viyanda – being distinct; innilaimai – the state of such ātmā; uṇarndu – realising it through hearing; uṇarndu – further, realising it through contemplation; uṇarilum – Even when realised through yōgam; iṟai nilai – the nature of sarvēsvaran who is concealing his supremacy and presenting himself in between brahmā and rudran; uṇarvaridu – difficult to understand; uyirgāḷ – Oh cētanas who have the ability to discriminate between different aspects and understand the same!; ari ayan aran ennum ivarai – those who are popularly known as hari, ajan (brahmā) and rudran (siva); uṇarndu uṇarndu – analysing their qualities, wealth, nature etc; uraittu uraittu – reading through those pramāṇams which reveal their qualities, wealth etc; manappattadu onṟu – whoever is understood as īśvara; uṇarndu uṇarndu – meditating on such person’s guṇa (qualities), vigraha (forms) etc., constantly; uraittu uraittu – reciting mantrams and nāmams (names) of such sarvēsvaran constantly; iṟainjumin – you perform worship

**Перевод:**

**Oh cētanas who have the ability to discriminate between different aspects and understand the same! Since jīvātmā is naturally knowledgeable and that knowledge in its pure form is unlimited and expanding in all directions, one can understand that the ātmā is different from body by hearing and meditating and realise the self. Even if that is accomplished, it will be difficult to understand the nature of sarvēsvaran who descends amidst brahmā and rudran in a concealed manner. Knowing the three popular dēvatās brahmā, viṣṇu and rudran, analysing their qualities, abilities etc., through the pramāṇams which reveal them, understand the supreme being amongst them. Having understood that, meditating on his qualities, abilities, etc and reciting the mantrams and his names, approach him and worship him.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*Even though one can realise one’s own self which is jñāna svarūpam (being jñānam), having jñānam and free (different) from matter, one cannot easily understand sarvēsvaran who descends into many different forms to accept his devotees. One will be always confused as to whether this supreme lord is brahmā, rudran or srīman nārāyaṇan. How to understand the truth in such a case?*

Similar to simple translation based on [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2013/03/22/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar-english/)‘s commentary.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In this 6th pāsuram, when sarvēsvaran (supreme lord) assumes a form amidst brahmā and rudran (like them) to manifest his simplicity, that itself becomes the cause of confusion to determine as to who is the supreme lord. nammāḻvār clarifies that by clearly explaining mūrty trayam (three forms) and eliminates the difficulty in establishing his supremacy.*

Similar to [nampiḷḷai](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/09/16/nampillai-english/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, the first avatāram (incarnation as viṣṇu) amidst brahmā and rudran will lead to considering him as the same as the other two – it is difficult to understand the truth, so you contemplate it and approach the right person.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*Similar to nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

Similar to [nampiḷḷai](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/09/16/nampillai-english/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*āḻvār! you said approach emperumān‘s incarnations. It is explained in srīrangarāja stavam 2.81 “madyē virinca girisam pratamāvatāra:” (your first incarnation that was in-between brahmā and rudra…). Each of those 3 is engaged in equivalent roles (sruśti – creation, stiti – sustenance, samhāram – annihilation). In this situation, it is difficult to determine – “Are all these 3 primary? Is there one among the three who is primary? Is there another one who is higher than these 3?” and approach the right person. Can you not establish the supreme person so that we can approach him? āḻvār replies “Instead of considering the body as self, considering that the self is different from body is difficult to achieve. Even if this is understood after trying very hard, it is even more difficult to understand the true nature of sarvēsvaran who has brahmā, rudran, et al as his body. Thus, try to understand him properly though this manner (as explained in the pāsuram) and approach him”. He explains as to who is the approachable object and how to approach him. uṇarndu uṇarndu iḻindu aganṟu uyarndu uruviyanda in nilaimai uṇarndu uṇarndu uṇarilum iṟai nilai uṇarvaridu uyirgāḷ uṇarndu uṇarndu uraittu uraittu ari ayan aran ennum ivarai uṇarndu uṇarndu uraittu uraittu iṟainjumin manappattadu onṟē*

- *uṇarndu* – āḻvār uses the term “*uṇarndu*” (knowing/realising) instead of “*uṇarvu*” (knowledge/jñānam) – this rejects the philosophy of yōgācāra (baudda school) “knowledge only exists and there is no knover”. The repetition “*uṇarndu uṇarndu*” rejects the philosophy of naiyāyika/vaisēśika “conciousness is accidental (not natural). On liberation, [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) will become like stone etc., without any consciousness” – insisting that jñānam is a natural attribute of [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) which exists always – even in liberated state. Since “jñātrutvam nityam” is given (being knovledgable is eternal), this also rejects the philosophy of kriyāvādi (a school which believes in action/results) “knowing is the cause of action, since there is beginning and end for action, the cause of such action which is knowledge, is also not eternal”.
- *iḻindu aganṟu uyarndu* – spread in all directions. nampiḷḷai says “*īśvaran svarūpattālē engum vyāpittirukkumāpōlē jñānattālē engum vyāpittirukkum*” (Just as [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) has pervaded naturally himself everywhere, [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) has pervaded through his jñānam).
- *uru viyanda innilaimai* – this nature of [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) being different from [acit](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/09/thathva-thrayam-achith-what-is-matter/) which is with form. It is also explained as *“uruvu iyanta*” – [cit](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) which is beyond what is seen ([acit](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/09/thathva-thrayam-achith-what-is-matter/)). In any case, the self is different from the body. Though this can be understood by hearing, meditating on such matters (from sāstram), one may personally try hard and realise it through yōga sāstram.
- *iṟainilai uṇarvaridu* – Even if the self is truly realised through difficult means, [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) being the antaryāmi for brahmā, rudran et al cannot be understood easily.
- *uyirgāḷ* – Oh the conscious ones! Are you like [acit](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/09/thathva-thrayam-achith-what-is-matter/) (which lacks knowledge) to miss out on understanding this? Being a [cētana](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/), the objective should be achieved – if not, its not worth having knowledge.
- *ari ayan aran ennum ivarai* *uṇarndu uṇarndu uraittu uraittu* … – One person is the destroyer of enemies and protector ([hari](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/17/divya-dhampathi/)), one person was born directly from the navel of viṣṇu (brahmā), one person is in-charge only for annihilation (rudra). By neutrally analysing the authentic texts which explain about them and reciting them, you can understand who is truly superior. Instead of siding with one person just as it is done in (the beginning of) linga purāṇam “please give me a text that will explain the glories of lingam” (and then the riśi explains the glories of lingam in that purāṇam), you should analyse the svarūpam (true nature) and svabhāvam (attributes) of these persons. If that is done, you will understand that one person is supreme among the three. You can then hear about him and meditate on him and finally approach him to accomplish the ultimate goal (of being accepted by him to render service to him).

In the next article we will the next pāsuram.

## 1.3.7. Onrenap palavena

*onṟenap palavena aṟivarum vadivinuḷ ninṟa nanṟeḻil nāraṇan nānmugan aran ennum ivarai onṟa num manattu vaittu uḷḷi num iru pasai aṟuttu nanṟena nalam seyvadu avanidai nammudai nāḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

onṟenap palavena – Considering there is one chief controller or considering there are many chief controllers; aṟivarum – difficult to know; vadivinuḷ – in a form; ninṟa – residing; nanṟu – beautiful/distinct; eḻil – having radiance of auspicious qualities such as apahatapāpmatvam (being freed from all evils); nāraṇan – srīman nārāyaṇa who is explained in nārāyaṇa anuvākam and who is the in-dwelling supersoul of all cit and acit; nānmugan – catur-muka (four faced) brahmā who has four faces (a) to recite the four vēdams and (b) for the different types of creation; aran – hara (rudra/siva) who is focussed on samhāram (annihilation) only; ennum ivarai – these personalities who are explained in various pramāṇams to reveal their nature/activities; onṟa – being neutral instead of taking sides of any one (to identify the chief person); num manattu vaittu – contemplating in your heart/mind; uḷḷi – analysing their svarūpa (true nature) and svabhāva (qualities) through pramāṇams (sāstram); num irupasai aṟuttu – eliminating the concept of being supreme from the 2 persons you may be attached to; avanidai – on that auspicious srīman nārāyaṇan; nammudai – our; nāḷ – lifespan; nanṟena – well-matured as said in “ēka bhakti:” (single-focussed devotion); nalam – snēham/friendship; seyvadu – do it

**Перевод:**

**Simple transalation (based on vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar‘s 12000 padi)**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

Similar to the simple transalation based on [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2013/03/22/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar-english/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*nammāḻvār instructs “Oh ones who have limited life span! Determine the supreme lord amongst the three (brahmā, viṣṇu, rudra) through established means and surrender unto such supreme controller”.*

Similar to [nampiḷḷai](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/09/16/nampillai-english/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār explains the means to determine the supreme and then instructs everyone to quickly surrender unto that supreme.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*In this 7th pāsuram, āḻvār seeing that the samsāris are still reluctant to find out about the supreme, says “Oh ones who have limited lifespan! Analyze who is the supreme and surrender unto him”.*

Similar to [nampiḷḷai](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/09/16/nampillai-english/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*7th pāsuram. Even after hearing āḻvār‘s instructions, people were saying “we will do as you say” and were still lethargic. āḻvār says “you have limited life span; you are not realising the true and wonderful nature of bhagavān who is the ultimate object to attain; determine the supreme before you die, using proper means and devote yourself towards him” in this pāsuram which is a continuation of the previous pāsuram. onṟenap palavena aṟivarum vadivinuḷ ninṟa nanṟeḻil nāraṇan nānmugan aran ennum ivarai onṟa num manattu vaittu uḷḷi num iru pasai aṟuttu nanṟena nalam seyvadu avanidai nammudai nāḷē*

- *onṟenap palavena* – It is difficult to easily comprehend if there is a single controller who exists in three different forms or if there are three different chief controllers in three different forms. It makes one wonder if it is “*ēkātma adiśtānam*” (single ātmā being the controller) or “*anēkātma adiśtānam*” (multiple ātmās being the controllers).
- *nanṟeḻil* – [āḻvār](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/18/nammazhwar-english/) is meditating on nārāyaṇa anuvākam etc which are fully focussed on srīman nārāyaṇan. This is explained by [āḻvār](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/18/nammazhwar-english/) himself in tiruvāimoḻi 4.5.10 “*kaṇḍavāṟṟāl tanadē ulagena ninṟān*” (Just by seeing his radiant/commanding form, one can understand everything is owned by him).
- *nāraṇan* – The name “nārāyaṇa” itself explains that he is the prakāri (object) and everything else is his prakāram (attributes/forms).
- *nānmugan* – Having four faces indicating his involvement in sruśti (creation) only.
- *aran* – haran – the destroyer – indicating his involvement in samhāram only.
- *nāraṇan nānmugan aran* – As explained in srīviṣṇu purāṇam 1.2.23 “*sruśtistityantakarṇīm brahma viṣṇu sivātmikām \| sa samjñām yāti bhagavānēka Eva janārdana: \|\|*” (the distinct [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) janārdanan assumes three forms with the names of brahmā, viṣṇu and siva to perform creation, sustenance and annihilation) – while viṣṇu is placed in between brahmā and rudra (making them all look similar), while explaining [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/), the slōkam uses viṣṇu’s name of janārdana emphasising viṣṇu alone is supreme.
- *onṟa num manattu vaittu* – Instead of having favouritism towards the other two (brahmā, siva) or trying to bring up the glories of one individual without analysing, first contemplate the qualities of each of them, being neutral.
- *uḷḷi* – analyse through logic explained in sruti (vēdam). When such analysis is done, one person will look as the chief and other two will look as the subordinates.
- *num iru pasai aṟuttu* – eliminating the attachment towards the other two. There is no natural greatness for them – it is only because of your \[samsāris’\] praising that they look great.
- *nanṟena nalam seydu avanidai* – Having established his supremacy, realising how fortunate you are, perform unalloyed devotion towards him.
- *nammudai nāḷē* – When they said, we will take our time, [āḻvār](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/18/nammazhwar-english/) says “our lifespan is very short”. This is already explained in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.2.1 “](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/05/thiruvaimozhi-1-2-2-minnin-nilaiyila/)[*minnin nilaiyila*](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/05/thiruvaimozhi-1-2-2-minnin-nilaiyila/)[“](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/05/thiruvaimozhi-1-2-2-minnin-nilaiyila/) pāsuram. When a person is sleeping inside closed doors and the building catches fire, should the person try to escape the fire in a relaxed way? There is very limited time to escape the fire – similarly, there is very limited lifespan for us to realise our nature and surrender unto [emperumān](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/17/divya-dhampathi/). Our life is such that, when the day dawns, one relishes that its time to go earn money and when the sun sets, one relishes that its time to enjoy sex life – in the mean time a day is lost in the life. “s*ālil edutta nīr pōle tangaḷ āyussu kuṟaginṟatenṟu aṟiyādirā ninṟārgaḷ*” (A day in our lifespan is just like a pot of water fetched from the well – that water is gone and can never be brought back).

In the next article we will the next pāsuram.
