## 1.3.8. Nalum ninradu

*nāḷum ninṟadu nama paḻaimai am kodu vinai udanē māḷum ōr kuṟaivillai mananaga malamaṟak kaḻuvi nāḷu nam tiruvudai adigaḷ tam nalam kaḻal vaṇangi māḷumōr idattilum vaṇakkodu māḷvadu valamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

mananagam – in the heart; malam – dirt which is created due to confusion on trimūrti sāmyam (brahmā viṣṇu rudra being considered equal); aṟa – to remove; kaḻuvi – purified through knowledge; nāḷum – everyday which is dear to us; nam – for us; tiruvudai – srīmān (one who has srī mahālakśmi); adigaḷ tam – unto the svāmi (master); nalam – approachable by all, most enjoyable; kaḻal – lotus feet; vaṇangi – surrendering; nāḷum – everyday; ninṟu – always being with us; adum – torturing; nama – accumulated by us knowingly; paḻamai – eternal, always existing since time immemorial; am kodu – most cruel; vinai – pāpams (sins) such as akrutya karaṇa (indulging in the prohibited acts) etc; udanē – at the time of surrender; māḷum – will be destroyed; ōr kuṟaivillai – nothing to worry; māḷumōr idattilum – even while leaving the body; vaṇakkodu – with surrender; māḷvadu – dies; valam – strong

**Перевод:**

**By purifying one’s heart through knowledge eliminating the dirt of considering the three dēvatās (brahmā, viṣṇu, rudra) to be equal and surrendering unto the most enjoyable and easily approachable lotus feet of our svāmy (master) srīman nārāyaṇan who is the husband of srīmahālakśmi, we can eliminate the most cruel sins which were accumulated by us knowingly and which have tortured us every day, during such time of surrender. Even if we are able to surrender at the last moments of our life, it will be strong enough.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

Similar to [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation. In addition, piḷḷān says “Even if those who realise this at the last moments of their life are unable to engage in bhakti yōgam for even a small period of time, just an anjali (namaskāram with folded hands) or even a word or even a thought towards emperumān is better than such bhakti yōgam”.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*Eighth pāsuram. nammāḻvār explaining sriya:patitvam (being the husband of srī mahālakśmi) that is the basis for emperumān being vorśippable, says that in the beginning of such worship, all obstacles for such worship will be eliminated.*

Similar to [piḷḷān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/pillan/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says that on approaching the lotus feet of sarvēsvaran who is srīya:pati, the obstacles for such surrender and the ultimate materialising of the result will be destroyed.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*Similar to nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

Similar to [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Some people ask “You are saying at least surrender to emperumān now. But we have accumulated sins since time immemorial. How do we eliminate that? Do we have time to surrender unto him?” āḻvār replies “When you get ready to surrender, your obstacles will be destroyed. Since you are surrendering to sriya:pati (husband of srī mahālakśmi), don’t think that you have lost your opportunity. Even if you are too old and walking with a stick, you can fall at his lotus feet with the stick and will still be protected”. nāḷum ninṟadu nama paḻaimai am kodu vinai udanē māḷum ōr kuṟaivillai mananaga malamaṟak kaḻuvi nāḷu nam tiruvudai adigaḷ tam nalam kaḻal vaṇangi māḷumōr idattilum vaṇakkodu māḷvadu valamē*

- *nāḷum ninṟadum* – continuously torturing. Though [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s svarūpam (true nature) and guṇams (auspicious qualities) are existing eternally, his qualities are subservient to him. Similarly, though [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) is eternal and eternally subservient to [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)‘s connection with [acit (matter)](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/09/thathva-thrayam-achith-what-is-matter/) in samsāram is also going on since time immemorial.
- *nama* – our own. It is said in sātyāyana sākhā “*suhrudassādukrutyām dviśanta: pāpakrutyām*” (Friends receive the result of pious deeds and enemies receive the result of sinful deeds) – unlike that these were caused by our own deeds which were done knowingly. nampiḷḷai explains here [āḷavandār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/alavandhar/)‘s stōtra ratnam 25th pāsuram “*abhūtapūrvam…*” where [āḷavandār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/alavandhar/) says that he suffers the results of many sinful deeds from past and present and it is only inappropriate for [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) to allow such sufferings to happen to the ones who are surrendered unto him.
- *paḻamai* – this is not something from recent past, but ancient.
- *am* – krauryam – cruel nature. Explanation in arumpadam – “*am*” generally means beautiful. But this is called viparīta lakśaṇai – for example, in tamiḻ “*nalla pāmbu*” refers to cobra, a very poisonous snake, though “nalla” means good.
- *kodu vinai* – those which are only exhausted by experiencing the fruits of the actions.
- *udanē māḷum* – will be immediately eliminated while approaching emperumān. cāndōjña upaniśat 5.25 explains this principle “*yatēśīkatūlamagnau prōtam pradūyēta ēvam hāsya sarvē pāpmāna: pradūyantē*” (Just like cotton gets burnt fully in fire, all his sins are destroyed). Similar principle is explained in viṣṇu darmam 78th chapter ślōkam as well “*mērumantaramātrōpi…*” which explains that one who approaches kriṣṇa, even if his sins amount to the size of mēru mountain, they will be removed just like a disease is removed by the doctor. These 2 statements explain the removal of previously committed sins.
- *ōr kuṟaivillai* – \[aniśta nivrutti (removal of unfavourable aspects)\] There won’t be any further obstacles \[In the arumpadam, to establish that the future sins will be eliminated, the author quotes cāndōjña upaniśat 4.14.3 “*yatā puśkarapalāsa āpō na sliśyantē ēvam ēvamvidi pāpam karma na sliśyatē*” (Just like water does not stay on a lotus leaf and just slides down, for the one who has this brahma vidyā, the sins will not stay and he will be unaffected by them)\]. Subsequently it can also be said as all the favourable aspects will be attained. In gītā 9.31, [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) says “*kauntēya pratijñānīhi na mē bhakta: praṇasyati*” (arjuna! you declare that my devotee never perishes). Devotees and sins are like fire and soaking – unrelated. nampiḷḷai then explains mahābhārata sānti parva slōkam “*durācōpi sarvāsī krutagna: nāstika: purā samāsrayēd…prabhāvāt paramātmana:*” – Even when a person was previously having bad manners/discipline, eating that which is not to be eaten , ungrateful to those who helped him, disrespecting vaidika principles, etc., if he is surrendered to srīman nārāyaṇan, he is explained to be pure. Considering him to be lowly is to disrespect [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s glories. This is also explained in mahābhāratam (sahasranāma adyāyam – pala sruti) “*na vāsudēva bhaktānām asubham vidyatē kvacit*” (For the one who has devotion towards vāsudēva, there will be no inauspiciousness).
- *mananaga malamaṟak kaḻuvi* – should not be bewildered seeing viṣṇu in between brahmā and rudran and always having pure faith that [sarvēsvaran](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is our protector. One should have the faith as in nānmugan tiruvandādi 68 “*tiruvadi than nāmam maṟandehum puṟam toḻā māndar*” (Even if forgetting srīman nārāyaṇan, one should not worship others).
- *nāḷum* – every day, any day. One cannot touch ocean/sea on aparva kālam (parva kālam – ēkādasi, paurṇami, amāvāsyai, māsa pravēsam) \[Explanation in arumpadam – It is forbidden to see and touch peepal tree and ocean/sea everyday – peepal tree can only be seen on Tuesdays and ocean/sea can only be touched on parva kālam\] – this is in connection with next phrase, which says that emperumān’s relationship with tāyār is eternal/always.
- *nam tiruvadai adigaḷ tam* – unto our master who is always having srī mahālakśmi (on his chest) – this explains nityayōgam – eternal togetherness of perumāḷ and tāyār. [nanjīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nanjiyar/) asks [bhattar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/parasara-bhattar/) “When one surrenders to sarvēsvaran, he is going to be delivered by [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/). What is the need for the puruśakāram (recommendation) of tāyār?” bhattar replies “It is explained in this pāsuram by āḻvār that one should approach perumāḷ with the puruśakāram of tāyār”. He continues “This is because, when a [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) surrenders to emperumān, tāyār will keep him under her protection and when [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) turns towards her, she will make him ignore the faults of the [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) and accept him. Thus one should approach emperumān through tāyār”.
- *nalam kaḻal* – good feet – those lotus feet which will accept those who surrender with the puruśakāram of tāyār without seeing their defects.
- *māḷumōr idattilum* – Even at the last moment of one’s life.
- *vaṇakkodu māḷvatu valam* – Instead of being as rāvaṇa said in srī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 36.11 “*dvidā bhajyēyamapyēvam na namēyam…*” (Even if I am cut into two, I will not worship any one), even at the last moment if one dies with a bowed head, that will be better.
- *valamē* – strong/best. Instead of approaching him and others, even if he is approached at the end of one’s life, it will lead to fruitful result. From this we can understand that, even if one is surrendered to someone other than [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) throughout one’s life, there is no benefit; but if one surrenders even at the last moment to [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/), (best) result is certain to be accomplished.

In the next article we will the next pāsuram.

## 1.3.9. Valattanan tiripuram

*valattanan tiripuram erittavan idampeṟat tundit talatteḻu tisaimukan padaitta nal ulagamum tānum pulappada pinnum tan ulagattil agattanan tānē solappugil ivai pinnum vayiṟṟuḷa ivai avan tuyakkē*

**Пословный перевод:**

eḻu tisaimukan – brahmā (who has four faces for each of the four directions) who has greatness (of controlling fourteen layers of the universe); padaitta – created by; nallulagamum tānum – the beautiful universe and himself; tundittalattu idam peṟa – having in the broad naval; tiripuram erittavan – rudran who performed tripura dahanam (burning of the three towns); valattanan – one who is present on the right side of the body as mentioned in mōkśa darmam 167.51 “pasyaikādasa mē rudrān dakśiṇam pārsvamāsritān” (See the eleven rudras who are situated on my right side); pinnum – even after giving a place in his body for those who consider themselves as supreme and protecting them; pulappada – to be visible for those who long for him by saying as in tiruvāimoḻi 8.5.2 “kāṇavārāy” (please come in front of me so that I can see you); tānē – himself who is not bound by any karmā etc; than ulagattil – in his own world; agattanan – having descended/incarnated; solappugil – trying to highlight these; ivai – these many different qualities; pinnum – subsequently; vayiṟṟuḷa – there are many other different qualities which are still hidden (yet to be revealed); ivai avan tuyakku – he makes everyone become bewildered

**Перевод:**

**Simple transalation (based on vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar‘s 12000 padi)**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

Similar to [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation. Why is it difficult to understand and surrender to him then? Those who are not friendly to him cannot understand his nature. [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) keeps them chained in this samsāram due to their having no interest in him.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In ninth pāsuram, āḻvār explains that sarvēsvaran incarnates into this world (which is part of his wealth) for the pleasure of his devotees.*

Similar to [piḷḷān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/pillan/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says that while brahmā, rudran et al become established due to their dependence on emperumān, he descends into this world like a common man and makes them bewildered by his actions.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*ninth pāsuram – In previous pāsuram(s), āḻvār explained the inferior nature of brahmā, rudran et al and supremacy of sarvēsvaran (srīman nārāyaṇan). In this pāsuram, he explains that brahmā, rudran et al depend on sarvēsvaran and become successful in their tasks.*

Similar to [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Similar to periyavāccān piḷḷai‘s introduction. Though srīman nārāyaṇan is the cause for brahmā, rudran et al, he appears in this world where even those dēvatās will not step in. The reason for this is explained by himself as in bhagavat gītā 4.8 “paritrāṇāya sādūnām…” (to protect my devotees, to annihilate the miscreants and to establish darmam, I take birth again and again). He appears mainly to cultivate the devotion of his devotees and to create devotion in others; destroying the miscreants is just a side effect \[In arumpatam, it is explained further – This is based on emperumānār‘s explanation in gītā bhāśyam for this slōkam where he says “ānuśangikastu duśkrutām vināsa:” (destroying of miscreants is secondary, that which follows the primary aspect)\]. valattanan tiripuram erittavan idampeṟat tundit talatteḻu tisaimukan padaitta nal ulagamum tānum pulappada pinnum than ulagattil agattanan tānē solappugil ivai pinnum vayiṟṟuḷa ivai avan tuyakkē*

- *valattanan tiripuram erittavan* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is elaborating the points explained in [pāsuram 6](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/06/thiruvaimozhi-1-3-6-unarnthu-unarnthu/) and [pāsuram 7](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/07/thiruvaimozhi-1-3-7-onrenap-palavena/) in this pāsuram. Being proud after destroying the three towns, rudran realises his true nature after becoming a part on the right side of [srīman nārāyaṇan](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s body as mentioned in mōkśa darmam 167.51 “*pasyaikādasa mē rudrān dakśiṇam pārsvamāsritān*” (See the eleven rudras who are situated on my right side).
- *idampeṟat tundittalattu eḻutisaimukan padaitta nallulagamum tānum* –  having the great brahmā in the vast naval as explained in gītā 11.15 “*brahmāṇamīsam kamalāsanastam*” (rudran who is under the control of brahmā, who is sitting on a lotus flower).
- These are representative of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) protecting them in all manner. *eḻucci* means having the capability to control the universe containing fourteen layers . *nallulagam* – good world – since [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) himself descends here.
- As explained in tiruvāimoḻi 4.8.1 “*ēṟāḷum iṟaiyōnum tisaimukanum tirumagaḷum kūṟāḷum taniyudamban*” ([emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) gives different parts of his body to rudran – one who rides the bull, brahmā – who has four faces, [srī mahālakśmi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/) et al). Instead of giving the same place, i.e., his private quarters ([srī mahālakśmi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/)‘s residence) to every one, he allocates different places to each person. His divine form is the abode of everyone.
- Are these dēvatās (brahmā, rudran et al) present in the specific parts of the body of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) all the time (like [srī mahālakśmi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/) always staying in his chest)? When there is a danger, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) gives his body as a safe-haven to these dēvatās. Since this is a great quality of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), [āḻvārs](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/azhwars/) enjoy this quality always in him (as if they are there always). Small-town kings, ministers etc., may have their own palaces etc., but will always like to be honored in the emperor’s palace. Similarly, these dēvatās like their place on [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s divine body. Just as when there is flood/danger in srīrangam, everyone would move inside the adaiyavaḷaintān (seventh prākāram which is like a fort) and when the floods drain (or the dangers disappear) they will return to their location, these dēvatās would reside in [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s divine body sometimes and at other times they will be back in their places.
- *tannulagattil agattanan* – The one who has given place for brahmā, rudran et al in his body, will descend into this world, where even they don’t want to step in.
- *pulappada* – to be seen by his dear devotees as explained in tiruvāimoḻi 8.5.2 “*kāṇavārāyay enṟenṟu kaṇṇum vāyum tuvarndu*” (my eyes/mouth are dried up craving to see you). For such persons he cannot show his vision by just his sankalpam, he has to be physically present in front of them to satisfy their desires. This is explained in tiruvāimoḻi 3.1.9 “*maḻungāda jñānamē padaiyāga malarulagil toḻumbāyārkkaḷittāl un sudarccōdi maṟaiyum*” (if you just present your divine vision in their minds and not physically be present in front of such devotees, your radiance will decrease).
- *solappugil ivai pinnum vayiṟṟuḷa* – He is so great that he becomes the child of daśarata, nandagōpa et al, who were created by brahmā. Not only that, when daśarata said “I am giving you my kingdom” and later said “no kingdom, you have to go to the forest”, he accepted that. Similarly when nandagōpa gave him a stick and said “go, herd the cattle”, he happily accepted that too. Such are his unfathomable qualities. It can also be said as “his protecting everyone during praḷayam by keeping everyone inside his stomach/body”.
- *ivai avan tuyakkē* – As explained in gītā 7.14 “*mama māyā duratyayā*” (my material world is difficult to cross over) – for those who are unfortunate, he does not allow them close to him and when they try to move away from him, he lets them do that. Since he is indifferent towards you, you cannot understand his glories.

In the next article we will the next pāsuram.

## 1.3.10. Tuyakkaru madiyil

*tuyakkaṟu madiyil nal jñānattuḷ amarararait tuyakkum mayakkudai māyaigaḷ vānilum periyana vallan puyaṟkaru niṟattanan peru nilam kadanda nalladippōdu ayarppilan alaṟṟuvan taḻuvuvan vaṇanguvan amarndē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tuyakkaṟu – without any anxiety due to not having doubtful/erroneous understanding; madiyil – in the mind/intellect; nal jñānattuḷ – those who are having good knowledge; amararai – dēvas; tuyakkum – make them anxious/bewildered; mayakku – ability to cheat/deceive; udai – having; māyaigaḷ – amazing aspects; vānilum – even in the boundless sky; periyana vallan – one who is more capable than; puyal – like a dark cloud; karu niṟattanan – having blackish hue; peru nilam – vast earth; kadanda – easily measured/stretched over; nal – distinct/beautiful; adippōdu – lotus feet; amarndu – being situated firmly without expecting any other results; ayarppilan – not being forgetful; alaṟṟuvan – blabbering his qualities with my mouth; taḻuvuvan – embrace with great love; vaṇanguvan – offer obeisances bowing down my head

**Перевод:**

**emperumān has amazing capabilities to bewilder dēvas who have pristine knowledge due to not having any doubtful/erroneous understanding and can easily cheat/deceive them. Such emperumān who has a blackish hue which resembles dark clouds, casually measured the earth with his beautiful lotus feet. I will be firmly situated at his lotus feet, not forgetting him (meditating upon him constantly), blabber his glories with my mouth, embrace him with great love and offer obeisances bowing down my head – thus engaging all my three types of faculties (mind, speech and body) in his service.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

Similar to [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation. His incarnations can even bewilder brahmā, rudran et al who have pristine knowledge.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*āḻvār desires to enjoy the lotus feet of trivikraman emperumān (which do not discriminate  between any one, which were easily attained by him, which were most enjoyable) through mind, words and deeds.*

Similar to [piḷḷān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/pillan/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, leaving aside emperumān‘s unlimited deceitful aspects, āḻvār desires to enjoy his beauty.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*Similar to nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

Similar to [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*10th pāsuram. Leave aside his attitude towards the ones who are not turning towards him. āḻvār desires to enjoy emperumān‘s lotus feet (which  measured the three worlds to pacify us) through mind, words and deeds. tuyakkaṟu madiyil nal jñānattuḷ amarararait tuyakkum mayakkudai māyaigaḷ vānilum periyana vallan puyaṟkaru niṟattanan peru nilam kadanda nalladippōdu ayarppilan alaṟṟuvan taḻuvuvan vaṇanguvan amarndē*

- *nal jñānattuḷ amarar* – uḷ can mean manam (mind), idam (place), mēlum (great/better). In this case, it can be said to be “*mēlāna amarar*” (dēvas – celestial being who are better than manuśya – human). amarar refers to indra et al.
- *tuyakkum mayakkudai māyaigaḷ* – those incarnations with auspicious qualities and actions which bewilder dēvas.
- *vānilum periyana vallan* – Even if one can measure the size of sky, no one can measure his auspicious qualities.
- *nal jñānattuḷ amarar* – When the dēvas are in trouble, they will beg for his help – but the moment they regain their power they will start fighting with him. After losing his wealth, his women-folk being captured and himself insulted completely, indra requests [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) to help him. kriṣṇa goes and wins over narakāsura, rescues the women-folk and brings back the lost glory to indra, On his visit to dēva lōka, satyabāmā (kriṣṇa’s wife) wants the pārijāta tree from indra’s garden – indra’s wife refuses to give that, so kriṣṇa forcefully brings along the tree with him. Seeing this, indra forgetting all the help done by [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), shamelessly chases him with his vajrāyuda (and eventually gets taught a lesson by kriṣṇa). Here, amarar can mean nityasūris also. periya tiruvadi (garudāḻvār) once argued with kriṣṇa (when sumuka (a snake he was chasing) went under kriṣṇa’s protection) and told him “I am the one who carried you and your consorts” similar to someone who carries the palanquin will argue for wages – so even nityasūris can be bewildered by [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s actions. We cannot understand his amazing activities. Let us leave that aside.
- *perunilam kadanda…* – [piḷḷān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/pillan/) explains this as “[āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is enjoying through mind, words and deeds”. [nanjīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nanjiyar/) explains this as “[āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) desiring to enjoy him through these ways”.
- *perunilam kadanda* – placed  his lotus feet everywhere – be it on vasiśta (most advanced) or on caṇḍāḷa (most down-trodden). Instead of looking for the purity in them, he ensured that his purity benefited them.
- nalladippōdu – most desirable lotus feet. [āḷavandār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/alavandhar/) too prays in stōtra ratnam 31 “*kadāpuna:…*” (trivikrama! when will your beautiful lotus feet decorate my head?). This is similar to one who desires to decorate his head with fresh flowers.

In the next article we will the next pāsuram.

## 1.3.11. Amarargal toludu

*amarargaḷ toḻudu eḻa alai kadal kadaindavan tannai amar poḻil vaḷam kurukūrc catakōpan kuṟṟēvalgaḷ amar suvai āyirattu avaṟṟinuḷ ivai pattum vallār amararōdu uyarvil senṟu aṟuvar tam piṟavi am siṟaiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

amarargaḷ – those dēvas who wanted to get a medicine \[nectar\] to become immortal; toḻudu eḻu – performing anjali (namaskāram with folded hands) as he did in tiruvāimoḻi 1.1.1 “toḻudu eḻu”; alai kadal – the sea with waves; kadaindavan tannai – the one who churned to agitate it; amar – well-fit; poḻil vaḷam – being beautiful due to the presence of gardens; kurukūr – belongs to āḻvārtirunagari; satakōpan – nammāḻvār‘s; kuṟṟēvalgaḷ – confidential kainkaryams (reciting pāsurams); suvai – both sweet sound and meaning; āyirattu avaṟṟinuḷ – among those 1000 pāsurams; ivai pattum – this decad which is like the amrutam (nectar) which came out of tiruppāṟkadal (kśīrābdi – milk ocean); vallār – those who can repeatedly recite/understand; uyarvil – in greatness; amararōdu senṟu – equaling nityasūris; tam piṟavi – their birth; am siṟai aṟuvar – will destroy that prison

**Перевод:**

**The dēvas (celestial beings) who wanted to become immortal, vorśipped emperumān (like āḻvār himself vorśipped him) who churned the milk ocean. nammāḻvār who belongs to āḻvārtirunagari which is beautiful due to the presence of many gardens, sang such emperumān in this decad (among the 1000 pāsurams) which is like the nectar that came out of milk ocean. Those who can understand this decad will rise to the level of nityasūris and eliminate their birth in this world which is like being in a prison.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

Similar to [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*āḻvār says that those who practice (understand/recite) this decad will first be honoured by being in the line of nityasūris and have their relationship with this samsāram (material world) severed.*

Similar to [piḷḷān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/pillan/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Similar to nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*Similar to nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

Similar to [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Similar to nanjīyar‘s introduction. amarargaḷ toḻudu eḻa alai kadal kadaindavan tannai amar poḻil vaḷam kurukūrc catakōpan kuṟṟēvalgaḷ amar suvai āyirattu avaṟṟinuḷ ivai pattum vallār amararōdu uyarvil senṟu aṟuvar tam piṟavi am siṟaiyē*

- *amarargaḷ toḻudu eḻa* – “*‘uppuccāṟu kiḷaṟuvadeppōdō?’ enṟu kidakkiṟa dēvajāti’* – dēvas who were waiting for the salt-essence (amrutam – nectar is explained like this since it merely brings immortality for a longer period in comparison to human life, but its not going to liberate any one from the clutches of samsāram) to come out.
- *alai kadal kadaindavan tannai* – With garlanded beautiful/broad shoulders, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) was churning the ocean. “*oru kadal oru kadalai ninṟu kadaiyumāpōlē*” (like one ocean is churning another ocean) – [bhagavan](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is an ocean of mercy, kśīrābdi is milk ocean.
- *toḻudeḻa* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) offered himself being overwhelmed by [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s auspicious qualities, dēvas became mesmerized by the beauty of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/).
- *satakōpan kuṟṟēvalgaḷ* – serving [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) through words. In case of complete personalities, one cannot do anything more than glorifying through words (since they already have everything). Even nityasūris are engaged in glorifying [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) through words only, as explained in rig vēdam (viṣṇu sūktam) “…*tadviprāsō vipanyava:..*” (the most learned ones who are well-capable to glorify).
- *amar suvai āyiram* – those most enjoyable 1000 pāsurams – this indicates that one need not glorify [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) as duty-bound but glorify out of great desire (due to the most enjoyable nature of the pāsurams and [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)).
- *avaṟṟinuḷ ivai pattum* – Just as it is explained in periya tirumoḻi 6.1.2 “*viṇṇavar amuduṇa amudil varum peṇṇamuduṇḍa*” (while the dēvas were enjoying the nectar, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) accepted/enjoyed [srī mahālakśmi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/) who is the real nectar), this decad is the most reliśable among all of tiruvāimoḻi.
- *avaṟṟinuḷ ivai pattum vallār amararōdu uyarvil senṟu aṟuvar tam piṟavi am siṟaiyē* – Those who are able to meditate on this decad, will achieve the greatness of nityasūris and then will have the shackles of birth in this samsāram removed.
- When any one learns this decad, immediately they are considered as nitysūris. As soon as the body falls, the [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) will go to paramapadam. A coupe of examples are given:
   - When a king gifts something to someone, it will reach the person surely. Similarly, when [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) himself considers him \[a samsāri\] to be nityasūri, his existence in this samsāram will be terminated surely and he will reach paramapadam.
   - If a prince is imprisoned for some reason, when he needs to be released, he will first be crowned and then his shackles will be cut (to be freed). Similarly, first such persons who learn this decad will be considered as nityasūris and subsequently, their binding in this samsāram will be removed.
- *amararōdu uyarvil senṟu aṟuvar tam piṟavi am siṟaiyē –* This is also explained as “one will reach with the help of ādivāhikas (who are celestial beings, who help the [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) (after death of the gross body) travel through different layers of the material world and reach the banks of vrajā river) and have his subtle body also removed (to get a new spiritual body before entering paramapadam).  The result of this padigam (decad) is as explained by [gītācāryan](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) in gītā 4.9 “*tyaktvā dēham punar janma naiti māmēti*” (after giving up this body, there is no birth again in this material world and one will reach me).
- nampiḷḷai summarizes the whole decad in the end.
   - In the 1st pāsuram, āḻvār said emperumān is sulabhan (easily approachable).
   - In the 2nd pāsuram, āḻvār explained that saulabhyam in detail.
   - In the 3rd pāsuram, āḻvār said that his avatāra rahasyam cannot be understood by anyone.
   - In the 4th pāsuram, āḻvār said that his avatāra rahasyam can be understood by those who are surrendered unto him and not be understood by those who are not surrendered unto him.
   - In the 5th pāsuram, āḻvār instructed everyone to approach him through the bhakti mārgam (the path of devotion) that was explained by emperumān himself.
   - In the 6th pāsuram, āḻvār explained the nature of emperumān and how to approach him.
   - In the 7th pāsuram, āḻvār said since you are having short life span, surrender unto him quickly.
   - In the 8th pāsuram, āḻvār said while surrendering unto him, all the obstacles will be removed.
   - In the 9th pāsuram, āḻvār explained the reason for avatārams of emperumān who is the cause of brahmā, rudran et al.
   - In the 10th pāsuram, āḻvār tried to enjoy such emperumān with his mind, words and deeds.
   - In the last pāsuram, āḻvār explained the fruits of those who learn/practice this decad.

Thus ends the English translation for tiruvāimoḻi 1st centum 3rd decad.

## 1.4 1.4.1 anjiraiya madanaray

## 1.4.1. 1.4.1 Anjiraiya madanaray

*anjiṟaiya madanārāy aḷiyattāy nīyum nin anjiṟaiya sēvalumāy āvā enṟu enakkaruḷi venjiṟaip puḷ uyarttākku en vidu tūdāyc cenṟakkāl van siṟaiyil avan vaikkil vaippuṇḍāl en seyyumō*

**Пословный перевод:**

aḷiyattāy – one who has the characteristics to bless/give me; am siṟaiya – having beautiful wings/feathers which will help fulfil my desire; mada nārāy – tender/shy female crane being lethargic after the union with the male crane; nīyum – you who are inseparable from your partner; nin am siṟaiya sēvalumāy – your beautiful partner whose wings/feathers are shining due to the union with you; A A enṟu – Feeling for my separation and crying out “alas! alas!”; enakku aruḷi – blessing me; vem siṟai – the wings which are dreaded by the enemies; puḷ – periya tiruvadi (garuda); uyarttārkku – one who raised (garuda) as the flag to protect others; en vidu tūdāyc cenṟakkāl – while going as a messenger sent by me; van siṟaiyil – in a cruel prison (of ignoring your presence and words); avan vaikkil – if he keeps you; vaippuṇḍāl – if agreed to that; en seyyum – what is wrong with that?; O – is it even possible?

**Перевод:**

**Simple transalation (based on vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar‘s 12000 padi)**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

Similar to [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*This pirātti (āḻvār in feminine mood), seeing pairs of cranes having union in the garden, being a girl, approached a female crane and requests it to express her sufferings to emperumān.*

Similar to [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*parānkusa nāyaki requests the female crane which is enjoying with the male crane in the pond in the garden to go as a messenger to garudadvajan (srīman nārāyaṇan who has garuda as his flag).*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*In this first pāsuram, parānkusa nāyaki tells the female crane which is enjoying with her male crane to inform her state to emperumān.*

Similar to [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*First pāsuram. parānkusa nāyaki looks at a female crane which stays nearby and knowing well “the male crane should be approached through the female crane” \[arumpadam – Just like bhagavan is approached through srī mahālakśmi who does puruśakāram, ācārya too should be approached through other srīvaiṣṇavas – here crane is considered as the ācārya who establishes the link between āḻvār and bhagavan\]- parānkusa nāyaki requests the male crane through the female crane to inform her state to emperumān. அஞ்சிறைய மடனாராய் அளியத்தாய் நீயும் நின் அஞ்சிறைய சேவலுமாய் ஆவா என்று எனக்கருளி வெஞ்சிறைப் புள் உயர்த்தாக்கு என் விடு தூதாய்ச் சென்றக்கால் வன் சிறையில் அவன் வைக்கில் வைப்புண்டால் என் செய்யுமோ anjiṟaiya madanārāy aḷiyattāy nīyum nin anjiṟaiya sēvalumāy āvā enṟu enakkaruḷi venjiṟaip puḷ uyarttākku en vidu tūdāyc cenṟakkāl van siṟaiyil avan vaikkil vaippuṇḍāl en seyyumō*

- *am siṟaiya* – Just like an infant will focus on the bosom of the mother (which is the source of nutrition), [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) focusses on the wings which are the means to reach [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/). The beauty glows due to mutual bliss out of the union of the cranes. Just like siśya will focus on ācārya’s jñānam and serve him, [parānkusa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) focusses on the wings of the crane.
- *mada* – humble; being ready to serve; due to the union, feeling lethargic and thus ready to obey the orders; nāṇam (shyness), madam (humility) and accam (fear) are considered as very basic characteristics of women. [parānkusa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) calls out for the help of the female crane who will understand what she is going through in separation from [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/).
- *nārāy* – like calling ammā (mother), ammē!, she is calling nārai as nārāy!
- *aḷiyattāy* – bless me, help me. Your presence is so glorious – just coming here to help me.
- *nīyum* – As seen in srī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 31.12 “sa brātus caraṇau gādam  nipīdya raghunandana: sītāmuvāca” (iḷaiyaperumāḷ/lakśmaṇa held on tightly the lotus feet of his brother srī rāma, speaking at sītā pirātti first) – While srī rāma decided to go to the forest, lakśmaṇa prayed to him to go along with him as well – at that time he approached srī rāma through sītā pirātt. So, parānkusa nāyaki too first calls out for the female crane.
- *nin am siṟaiya sēvalumāy* – Like “*sriya:pati*“, our indulgence towards [bhagavan](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is due to his connection with [srī mahālakśmi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/). You both are made for each other.
- *A A enṟu* – cranes being together is to remove my suffering
- *enakku* – Like the riśis complained to srī rāma showing their wounded bodies in srī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 6.16 “*ēhi pasya sarīrāṇi*” (You come and see our wounded bodies), [parānkusa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) shows her body which is severely affected by the separation from [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/).
- *aruḷi* – Instead of helping me just because I asked, you should do this as your goal. In bhagavat viśayam (spiritual matters), ācāryas do not help in expectation of something in return; it is purely out of their compassion; when they help us attain [bhagavan](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) who is the owner of both spiritual/material worlds, the siśya has nothing to offer the ācārya in return which will match that. [parānkusa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) glorifies the cranes greatly. Seeing that, the cranes ask “He left you like this. Is he going to listen to us? Also, when we go there (parampadam), everyone will look similar as stated in muṇḍaka upaniśat 3.1.3 “*niranjana: paramam sāmyamupaiti*” (becoming pure, attains same qualities as [bhagavan](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)). How to distinguish [bhagavan](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) from nityasūris and muktas?”.
- *vem siṟaip puḷ uyarttārkku* – one who has the garuda dvaja (flag) – this is the distinguishing aspect between [bhagavan](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) and others.  Here garuda’s wings are having adjective of “cruel” for two reasons – a) he is capable of eliminating our enemies and help us reach there; b) he is the one who helped [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) leave us by carrying him – so he himself is described as cruel – just like ākrūra was accused as cruel by the gōpis due to his taking kriṣṇa away from them.
- *en vidu tūdāy* – it is actually his duty to send someone to me to protect me, but now I have to send a messenger to him. You are going on my request – I am not so strong/able like pāṇḍavas who sent kriṣṇa as a messenger.  I am such a helpless girl. Going as a messenger for others’ benefit is a rare opportunity.
- *senṟakkāl* – You are going to see [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) before I could see him. Is that not great?
- *van siṟaiyil* – [bhagavan](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) will not imprison a messenger from [parānkusa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/). But ignoring the messenger itself is considered as imprisonment. Like princes need to be pampered regularly – if they are not given betel leaves on time, they will become upset.
- *en vidu tūdāy senṟakkāl van siṟaiyil avan vaikkil –* When someone goes as a messenger of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), he may be imprisoned, tortured (by setting fire on the tail etc) – like hanumān went through. When you go as my messenger, he will embrace you as explained in srī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 1.13  “*pariśvangō hanūmata:*” (that hanumān was embraced by me – on carrying the return message from sītā pirātti to srī rāma). You will be embraced by the chest I would like to embrace.
- *avan vaikkil* – would he imprison you? As explained in srī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 2.42 “*vyasanēśu manuśyāṇām*” (He feels the pain of the suffering of the lowest of humans), he would never trouble you. In fact, he will hold your feet on his head.
- *vaippuṇḍāl en seyyumō* – Even if he imprisons you, is it not something noble? Like sītā pirātti who herself allowed to be imprisoned by rāvaṇa to release the dēva strīs (celestial women) from the prison of rāvaṇa – this will be greatly glorified as a noble gesture.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.4.2. Enseyya tamaraikkan

*en seyya tāmaraik kaṇ perumānārkku en tūdāyen seyyum uraittakkāl inakkuyilgāḷ nīralirēmun seyda muḻu vinaiyāl tiruvadikkīḻ kuṟṟēvalmun seyya muyalādēn agalvaduvō vidiyinamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

inakkuyilgāḷ – Oh group of cuckoos!; nīr alirē – don’t you who have beautiful voice?; en – for me whom he became bound to; seyya – reddish; tāmarai – like a lotus; kaṇ – having eyes; perumānārkku – one who is greater than every one else (unreachable for me); en tūdāy – being my messenger; uraittakkāl – if you speak; en seyyum – what is wrong?; mun seyda – previously committed; muḻu vinaiyāl – complete sins; tiruvadik kīḻ – at your divine feet; kuṟṟēval – confidential service; seyya – to perform; mun – previous; muyalādēn – me who did not engage in any means; inam – still; agalvaduvō vidi – Is staying away the right thing to do?

**Перевод:**

**Oh group of cuckoos! īsn’t it true that you who have beautiful voice!?When you speak on behalf of me (whom he is bound to) to the greatest lord who has beautiful reddish eyes, what is wrong with that? Due to my previously committed sins, I did not try to perform confidential service at the lotus feet through any means, but still should I stay away? Is that the right thing to do? Here the sweet speaking ability of the ācāryas and their presence in groups is indicated.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

Similar to [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the second pāsuram, parāngusa nāyaki speaks about what some cuckoos would tell on her behalf to emperumān.*

Similar to [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, since there are lot more cuckoos (a group of them) which can accomplish her objective, she requests some of those to go to her puṇḍarikākśan (lotus eyed lord) on her behalf as a messenger.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*Similar to nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

Similar to [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

[bhattar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/parasara-bhattar/) was staying in tirukkōśtiyūr and there were two siśyas of his who were also present there at that time. They were named teṟkāḻvān and kōḷariyāḻvān. kōḷariyāḻvān is very focused on ācāram (following disciplined lifestyle according to vaidika darmam).  teṟkāḻvān is more lenient on the ācāram. Once on a festive day, when they both met, kōḷariyāḻvān asks teṟkāḻvān “Won’t you take a holy dip at least today?” teṟkāḻvān replies “my sins are so huge that such holy dips are not helpful. Only [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s sudarsana chakra has the ability to destroy my sins. So, what is the use of such holy dip then?”. [bhattar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/parasara-bhattar/) overheard this and thought “I underestimated teṟkāḻvān based on his ācāram, but he is really knowledgeable” and felt blissful.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Previously, parāngusa nāyaki requested some cranes to go as her messenger. Now, she explains to cuckoos what to convey when they go there. She started with cranes but ended with cuckoos. This is how much bewildered she is. That is the greatness of bhagavān from whom she is separated now. When someone who is separated from worldly matters/experience, they get quite upset and bewildered – if that is the case for normal matters, how much bewilderment one should have when separated from the most distinguished bhagavān. If bhagavān does not bewilder her like this, that would be an insult to his most auspicious qualities. என் செய்ய தாமரைக் கண் பெருமானார்க்கு என் தூதாய் என் செய்யும் உரைத்தக்கால் இனக்குயில்காள். நீரலிரே?முன் செய்த முழு வினையால் திருவடிக்கீழ் குற்றேவல் முன் செய்ய முயலாதேன் அகல்வதுவோ விதியினமே en seyya tāmaraik kaṇ perumānārkku en tūdāyen seyyum uraittakkāl inakkuyilgāḷ nīralirēmun seyda muḻu vinaiyāl tiruvadikkīḻ kuṟṟēvalmun seyya muyalādēn agalvaduvō vidiyinamē*

- *en* – mine. emperumān was very subservient to [parāngusa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) that he makes her think that he belongs to her even in separation. Alternatively, to help her sustain herself during separation, while leaving her, he said “wherever I am, wherever I go, I am yours”; because of that, she considers “he is mine”.
- *en seyya tāmaraik kaṇ perumānārkku* – my lotus eyed lord. She has enjoyed his reddish eyes before. His eyes are red due to:
   - His svābāvika aisvaryam (natural control over everything else)
   - His vātsalyam (motherly forbearance) towards his subjects
   - Just like a drunken person’s eyes, after having enjoyed in union with [parāngusa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)
   - Due to suffering in separation from her
- Where did she enjoy these aspects? In the first tiruvāimoḻi, she experienced/explained  [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s aisvaryam. In the third tiruvāimoḻi, she experienced/explained his vātsalyam. Here, union and separation are explained.
- *perumānārkku* – While leaving, he gave her a blissful glance and got her to become fully surrendered to him (in connection with the lotus eyes).
- *en tūdāy* – Like the rising and receding of a sea – it feels so empty. Going as a messenger for me who is so lonely/helpless.
- *en seyyum uraittakkāl* – when you speak on behalf of me, he may even gift you ubhaya vibhūti (both spiritual and material realms).
- *inakkyuilgāḷ* – you are in a group unlike me who is alone.
- *nīralirē* – you are the embodiment of simplicity. Why are you not helping me now? You responded nicely when we were enjoying together.
- *mun* – Is there a beginning for the time when I started committing sins? Its anādi (without a beginning).
- *seyda* – Were those sins just planned but not committed? They were committed.
- *muḻu vinai* – Were they incomplete in any manner? Can I eliminate?   An incident from the life of [bhattar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/parasara-bhattar/) is cited by nampiḷḷai and is explained in detail by periyavāccān piḷḷai in his vyākhyānam.
- *tiruvadikkīḻ* – Just like a brāhmaṇa, even if he becomes retarded, will recite vēdam only, [nammāḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/), even in the state of [parāngusa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) will only want to embrace [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s lotus feet instead of his chest – serving the lotus feet is natural for nammāḻvār.
- *kuṟṟēval* – desiring to perform confidential services to the lotus feet.
- *tiruvadikkīḻ kuṟṟēval mun seyya muyalādēn* – I who did not try serving your lotus feet previously; It is also explained as said by lakśmaṇa in srī rāmāyaṇam “*kriyatām iti mām vada*” (do as I say), not serving even after hearing the orders.
- *agalvaduvō vidi* – Even after not engaging in self-efforts, would I miss out on the goal? For [āḻvārs](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/azhwars/), [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is the only means. [nammāḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says in tiruvāimoḻi 5.8.8 “*kaḷaigaṇ maṟṟilēn*” (I have no other means”); [kulasēkarāḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/kulasekarazhwar/) says in perumāḷ tirumoḻi 5.1 “*un caraṇallāl caraṇillai*” (there is no other means than your lotus feet) and in perumāḷ tirumoḻi 5.7 “*maitteḻunda māmugilē pārttirukkum maṟṟavai*” (Like the crops which only look up to the blackish-huge clouds), [poigai āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/poigai-azhwar/) says in mudal tiruvantādi 4 “*neṟivāsal tānēyāy ninṟānai*” ([emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is the means and goal), [periyāḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/periyazhwar/) says in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 5.1.2 “*viḻikkum kaṇṇilēn nin kaṇ maṟṟallāl*” (I will not take any other refuge than your blessing vision) and [toṇḍaradippodi āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/thondaradippodi-azhwar/) says in tirumālai 38 “*vāḻum sōmbar*” (living lazy person – one who only depends on [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) for one’s protection and will not engage in self-efforts).
- *vidiyinamē* – there is no other way (from our side). piḷḷai tirunaṟaiyūr araiyar says “[parāngusa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says ‘even though we have nothing in our side to achieve our desires (service to you), why are you hesitating?'”

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

adiyen saraty ramanuja dasan

## 1.4.3. Vidiyinal pedai

*vidiyināl pedai maṇakkum mennadaiya annangāḷ madiyināl kuṟaḷ māṇāy ulagu iranda kaḷvarkku madiyilēn valvinaiyē māḷādō enṟu orutti madiyellām uḷ kalangi mayangumāl ennīrē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vidiyināl – out of great fortune (unlike me who is alone); pedai – with the female swan; maṇakkum – enjoying the union; mennadaiya annangāḷ – swans which have tender steps (due to their enjoying); madiyināl – with great intelligence (fulfilling indra’s desire and preserving mahābali’s generosity); kuṟaḷ – vāmanan – dwarf; māṇāy – celibate boy; ulagu – the world; iranda – stood begging (showing small feet and measuring with huge feet in the guise of begging); kaḷvarkku – krutrima – for the cheat/falsifier; madiyilēn – me who is ignorant (about his cheating ways); valvinaiyēyō – those sins (which cannot be exhausted by experiencing the results); māḷādu enṟu – thinking that they are not destructible (like destroying the sins of cintayantī etal); orutti – one girl; madi ellām – her intelligence (that was given by you); uḷ kalangi – being bewildered totally; mayangum – losing consciousness; ennīr – please go and tell him

**Перевод:**

**Oh swans who out of great fortune of being with your female companions having tender steps (conduct)! emperumān assumed the disguise of a dwarf celibate boy and stood begging for the world, as a cheat. I am an ignorant girl who is unable to understand his acts and my mind is totally bewildered and losing consciousness – please go and tell him this. “orutti” (a girl) will make him realise exactly who it is (since he knows who would be in this state). Through this pāsuram, the glories of gatakas (ācāryas) with respect to their tender (perfect) conduct of gently dealing with each other and their greatness are revealed.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

Similar to [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*Seeing that emperumān is thinking “one has to experience the result of one’s sins surely”, āḻvār requests through some swans to emperumān “May be cintayanti could have exhausted her sins by experiencing \[acute suffering in separation from kriṣṇa\], but my sins are far too much that they cannot be exhausted by experiencing the results”.*

Similar to [piḷḷān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/pillan/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, parāngusa nāyaki requests some swans which have better conduct and purity than the cuckoos to go as messenger to emperumān who made her fully dependent on him.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*In this third pāsuram, parāngusa nāyaki requests some swans to inform emperumān “If my sins are not eliminated by your mercy, they cannot be exhausted by experiencing the results as well”.*

Similar to [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Similar to nanjīyar‘s introduction. விதியினால் பேடை மணக்கும் மென்னடைய அன்னங்காள் மதியினால் குறள் மாணாய்  உலகு  இரந்த கள்வற்கு மதியிலேன் வல்வினையே மாளாதோ என்று , ஒருத்தி மதியெல்லாம் உள் கலங்கி மயங்குமால் என்னீரே vidiyināl pedai maṇakkum mennadaiya annangāḷ madiyināl kuṟaḷ māṇāy ulagu iranda kaḷvarkku madiyilēn valvinaiyē māḷādō enṟu orutti madiyellām uḷ kalangi mayangumāl ennīrē*

- *vidiyināl* – vidi is explained in different ways:
   - vidi as sāstram, and [parāngusa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) say “since you are having union according to sāstram, you are not separated from each other. But I am trying to have union with him (without being married) – that is why I am separated”.
   - vidi as bhājñam (fortune) – you are being together due to your fortune or it can be said as my fortune.
      - swans’ fortune – Being together with one’s lover is the result of one’s puṇyam (virtues) and being separated is the result of one’s pāpam (vices).
      - [parānkusa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s fortune – When srī rāma was searching for sītā pirātti, he met sugrīva who had also lost his wife, kingdom etc. srī rāma ensured that sugrīva was well settled – then only he started to remedy his own sufferings.  So, should [parānkusa nāyagi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) also not be happy for the swans being together? For ones who are compassionate, sufferings of others are more important than their own sufferings. I am fortunate to not have to unite you with your spouse before going towards my lord.
- *pedai maṇakkum* – Being together with the female companion – satisfying the desires of the female companion.
- *mennadaiya annangāḷ* – Are you going to get my desires fulfilled with such tender walk/steps? As explained in srī rāmāyaṇam kiśkintā kāṇḍam 33.37 “*sā praskalantī*…” (the famous tārā arrived with a staggered walk…). nampiḷḷai beautifully explains the whole slōkam here. When sugrīva was enjoying with tārā after vāli was vanquished, and forgetting to help srī rāma as committed, srī rāma sends lakśmaṇa to check on him. lakśmaṇa arrives there with great fury on sugrīva’s attitude. Hearing lakśmaṇa’s roar at the entrance, sugrīva trembles, realises only tārā can pacify him and sends her to lakśmaṇa. That famous tāra comes out as it is after enjoying sensual pleasures with sugrīva with a staggered walk, blurred vision due to consumption of alcohol, with her dress in irregular manner. She, who looks like a beautifully bent creeper, approaches lakśmaṇa. nampiḷḷai says tārā has a motherly affection towards lakśmaṇa \[this is based on kambar’s view too\], so just like a mother would at times appear in front of the child in “not so perfect” condition casually, tārā approached lakśmaṇa. Similarly, [parāngusa nāyagi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) also thinks that the swans with their beautiful and tender steps, would convince [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) and fulfil her desire.
- *madiyināl* – Unlike rāvaṇa who had to be destroyed, mahābali had a good quality named audāryam (generosity). indran lost his kingdom. Both of them should be satisfied – so, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is glorified in srī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 21.8 as “*gōsahasra pradātāram*” (After gifting thousands of cows in charity…) – the one who has hands which are greatly known for their generosity – decided to beg. That was [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s intelligence.
- *kuṟaḷ* – When a huge quantity is condensed into a small quantity (like milk boiled to get guava which is too sweet), so it can be easily enjoyed.
- *māṇāy* – the form of  a brahmacāri (a celibate boy) who is equally smiling to people who arehappily giving alms and others who are shutting the door on him while begging for alms.
- *ulagu iranda* – Begged the world that was created by his own sankalpam (divine will).
- *kaḷvarkku* – [tirumālai āṇḍān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/thirumalai-andan/) explains this as a “cheat”. [emperumānār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/emperumanar/) explains it as “one who did something to accomplish something else”. [emperumānār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/emperumanar/)‘s explanation is based on āḻvār’s thinking that “He cheated mahābali to attract me”, since he himself said previously ([1.3.10](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/07/thiruvaimozhi-1-3-10-thuyakkaru-mathiyil/)) “*perunilam kadanda nalladippōdu*” (this divine lotus feet which measured the huge world). [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s nature is such that whatever [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) does, he will always be attracted to [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) only. He says in tiruvāimoḻi 5.3.5 “*ulagam koṇḍa adiyan aṟivarumēni māyattanāgilum kodiya ennenjam avan enṟē kidakkum*” (Though he grabbed the world (from mahābali) and his forms are difficult to grasp, my heart will always be for him) and in tiruvāimoḻi 5.4.10 “*anṟorugāl vaiyam aḷanda pirān vārānenṟu onṟorugāl sollādu ulagu*” (the (people in the) world are not even saying that the   [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who once measured the world will not come for you). [tirumangai āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/thirumangai-azhwar/) also says in periya tirumoḻi 9.4.2 “*munnam kuṟaḷuruvāy mūvadi maṇ koṇḍaḷanda mannan saridaikkē mālāgi ponpayandēn*” (my bodily complexion changed out of great love for [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) on hearing the history of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) becoming a dwarf, begging for three feet of land and measuring the worlds). All [āḻvārs](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/azhwars/) are thus attracted to [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s vāmana avatāram.
- *madiyilēn* – ignorant. I should have simply requested him when he was leaving – I was not even intelligent to do that.
- *valvinaiyē māḷādō* – [parāngusa nāyagi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is called dīrga cintayantī. cintayantī was a gōpi \[cow-herd girl\] who was once caught in a situation at her house where her in-laws were at the hallway. She heard the notes of kriṣṇa playing on the flute and wanted to go to him at once (but she could not go past her in-laws sitting the hallway). Her virtues were exhausted by constant/deep meditation of kriṣṇa at that moment. Her vices were exhausted by suffering in separation and not being able to leave at once. Since puṇyam/pāpam were nullified, she at once gave up her body and reached paramapadam.  But [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) goes through these emotions repeatedly and constantly – that is why he is glorified as dīrga cintayantī.
- *orutti* – a girl. How will [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) know that it is about [parāngusa nāyagi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)? Like a deer is hunted down by a hunter’s bow, and if the hunter had been told “in such and such place, a deer was hunted down”, the hunter will easily identify that it was his hunt – similarly, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) will know that only [parāngusa nāyagi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) will be suffering so much in separation.
- *orutti* – most distinct . She is different from samsāris (who are simply focused on material aspects), nitaysūris (who never have separation from [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)) and other [āḻvārs](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/azhwars/) (because they are [nammāḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s avayavam (parts)).
- *madi kalangi* -Tell him that she is bewildered. He will say “even if her knowledge is diminished, I have given her (special) knowledge”.
- *madiyellām kalangi* – He will say “With the knowledge I gave, she will wait for me to come and protect her”. Tell him “Since you gave that knowledge which made her understand you, it became the cause to become bewildered”. He will ask “She may have some confusion. But would she be totally confused since this is pure knowledge given by me?”
- *madiyellām uḷ kalangi* – Tell him “The unblemiśed knowledge you gave is totally lost in her and she is fully confused”.
- *mayangumāl* – Hearing that, he may say “Oh! Is that so? I will give her knowledge when I go there”. If you say “she has already died”, he may think “What is the use of going there if she has died?” So, tell him “She will die soon if you don’t go”.
- *ennīrē* – You do your duty of informing him – if he does not come it will be his fault. When he hears your tone, he will understand my suffering and come to me.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.4.4. En nirmai

*en nīrmai kaṇḍu irangi idu tagādu ennāda en neela mugil vaṇṇarkku en sol(l)i yān sollugēnō nannīrmai ini avar kaṇ tangādu enṟu oruvāyc col nanneela maganṟilkāḷ nalgudirō nalgīrō*

**Пословный перевод:**

en nīrmai – (while being together) my inability to cope with separation; kaṇḍu – seen (while observing changes in my body during our embrace, etc); irangi – having compassion (considering she is very tender natured); idu tagādu ennāda – not understanding/saying that this separation is unbearable; en neela mugil vaṇṇārkku – to the one who is having dark-cloud hued form (but not showing compassion like such dark-clouds which rain water); en solli – saying what words; yān – me; sollugēnō – can tell? (still); nal – venerable; nīrmai – her sustenance; ini – now onvards; avar kaṇ – to him; tangādu – will not be sustained; oru vāyc col – saying a word; nanneela maganṟilkāḷ – beautifully blue colored love birds; nalgudirō – will you help?; nalgīrō – will you not help?

**Перевод:**

**While being together, emperumān has seen my inability to cope with separation by observing my bodily changes during his embrace etc., and what words can be said to that dark-cloud hued emperumān? Still, oh beautifully blue colored love birds! Can you tell him or not that I cannot sustain myself in separation? Here “avar” is used as parāngusa nāyagi‘s venerable way of calling emperumān. In this pāsuram, the beautiful form of the gataka (ācārya) is also highlighted.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

Similar to [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In this fourth pāsuram, āḻvār feeling dejected “How can I inform emperumān who left me even after knowing my nature?”, again out of hope/desire, requests some maganṟil birds (a species of love birds where the male and female of the species will not separate from each other) “Would you go and tell him about me or not?”.*

Similar to [piḷḷān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/pillan/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, parāngusa nāyagi desiring to send a messenger to dark-cloud hued emperumān, speaks towards beautifully (similarly) coloured maganṟils (love birds).*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*Similar to nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

Similar to [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Fourth pāsuram – Previously parāngusa nāyagi stated “My sins are so much that they cannot be exhausted by enjoying the fruits of the same” in 2nd pāsuram. Did she experience any suffering? Yes – When emperumān turned his face away from her for a moment – she experienced great suffering (thereby exhausting the accumulated sins). At that time, she assumes that some love birds who came near her were asking her “how can he help you?”. She feels dejected and tells them “Even after seeing my pitiful state – he left me. What can I tell him?” But out of desire, as if telling to someone who does not listen, she asks them “will you go and tell him about my situation or not?” என் நீர்மை கண்டு இரங்கி இது தகாது என்னாத என் நீல முகில் வண்ணார்க்கு என் சொல்(ல்)லி யான் சொல்லுகேனோ நன்நீர்மை இனி அவர் காண் தங்காது என்று ஒருவாய்ச் சொல் நன்னீல மகன்றில்காள். நல்குதிரோ நல்கீரோ? en nīrmai kaṇḍu irangi idu tagādu ennāda en neela mugil vaṇṇarkku en sol(l)i yān sollugēnō nannīrmai ini avar kaṇ tangādu enṟu oruvāyc col nanneela maganṟilkāḷ nalgudirō nalgīrō*

- *en nīrmai* – my nature, my tender form/heart.
- *kaṇḍu irangi idu tagādu ennāda* – Instead of showing compassion on seeing my suffering, he left. Here a tamiḻ scholar asks [bhattar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/parasara-bhattar/) “Should it not be ‘*kēttu irangi*‘ (having compassion on hearing my suffering) instead of ‘*kaṇḍu irangi*‘ (having compassion on seeing my suffering)?” [bhattar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/parasara-bhattar/) (being an expert in tamiḻ grammar and literature) replies “When he relaxes the embrace, her body becomes pale out of separation”. The scholar again asks “Is it even possible?”.[bhattar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/parasara-bhattar/) asks “Don’t you know tirukkuṟaḷ 1187 ‘*pullik kidandēn*‘  and kuṟundogai 399 ‘*kādalar toduvuḻi*‘? Is that not sufficient reference?” \[The scholar’s question is – since [parāngusa nāyagi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is singing in separation, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) cannot see her suffering – but only can hear about her suffering. bhattar says that though the current situation is in separation, [parāngusa nāyagi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) reminds him of the time when they were together when he was observing her suffering in a moment of separation\].
- *en neela mugil vaṇṇarkku en solli yān sollugenō* – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) was so attached to her that even in separation she says “*ennudaiyavan*” (mine – owned by me). She says “What can I say to the one who left me?” When asked “Why are you saying like this?”,[parāngusa nāyagi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says “He did not show compassion even after seeing my sufferings. How do I expect him to show compassion on hearing my sufferings now?” When asked “When did he see your suffering?” [parānkusa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) replies “While being together, when he takes his hand away from me, that part of my body will become pale out of sufferings in separation”.
- *kaṇḍirangi* – Should he not know that I cannot sustain myself as he has seen me losing consciousness as soon as saying “[*ettiṟam*](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/06/thiruvaimozhi-1-3-1-paththudai-adiyavar/)” ? \[as in tiruvāimoḻi pāsuram 1.3.1\]
- *idu* – this state of mine – even she herself cannot fully express her state (which is beyond words).
- *en neela mugilvaṇṇarkku* – one who has a dark-bluish complexion like a cloud. He showed his beauty and got me to become fully dependent on him. But this radiance is not seen in his heart \[comparison with cloud is done for both bodily beauty and the generosity of cloud which rains over everywhere – here, [parāngusa nāyagi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says that [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) has beauty like cloud but does not have the compassion towards her\]. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) himself says in tiruvāimoḻi 8.9.5 “*yāmudai āyan than manam kal*” (our cow-herd boy’s heart is made of stone). Initially giving up thinking “if he can leave me even after seeing my suffering, what is the use of sending a message?” later out of hope/desire, she starts sending the messenger again. This is like the behaviour of gōpikās towards kriṣṇa as explained in srī viṣṇu purāṇam 5.24.15 “*atavā kim tadālābhai: parā kriyatām katā \| apyasau mātaram draśtum sakrudapyāgamiśyati \|\|*” (If there is no use of speaking about him, let other matters be discussed. Would this [kriṣṇa](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) not come to visit his mother at least once?) – here the gōpikās are first saying he does not need us (so won’t talk about him, then out of hope expects his visit saying), but he would need his mother.
- *avar kaṇ tangādu* – My life will only be sustained on/by you (who is my master). nampiḷḷai explains a similar conversation from srī rāmāyaṇam between [sītā pirātti](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/) and hanumān (who is the messenger from srī rāma). sītā pirātti is upset with srī rāma for not rescuing her quickly. At that time hanumān asks “But, if you are so attached to srī rāma, how have you sustained yourself thus far instead of immediately giving up your life?”.sītā pirātti replies as in srī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 36.30 “*na cāsya mātā…*“. nampiḷḷai explains this slōkam – perumāḷ showed all his love (like towards his father, mother et al) towards me. While he is searching for me if he finds me dead, he will be heart-broken like a thirsty person finding a broken pot (without water). That is why I sustained myself to protect him.
- *oru vāyc col* – Just one word/phrase is sufficient. Like sītā pirātti said to hanumān in srī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 39.10 “…*vācā darmamavāpnuhi*” (by conveying the message using the appropriate words to the illustrious srī rāma, so that he can console me while I am surviving, you become virtuous through speech).
- *nanneela maganṟilgāḷ nalgudirō nalgīrō* – Both [perumāḷ](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) and you have dark-complexion. So, are the actions also similar (both trying to not help me)? Out of sorrow, she asks “will you help or not?”.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.
