## 1.4.5. Nalgit tan

*nalgit tān kāttaḷikkum poḻilēḻum vinaiyēṟkē nalgat tān āgādō nāraṇanaik kaṇḍakkāl malgu nīrp punal padappai irai tēr vaṇ siṟu kurugē malgu nīrk kaṇṇēṟkōr vāsagam koṇḍu aruḷāyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

poḻil ēḻum – seven worlds; nalgi – being desirous without their seeking out for their well-being; tān – without their expecting his help; kāttu – removing their hurdles; aḷikkum – fulfilling their desires; tān – him; vinaiyēṟkēyō – for me who is very sinful; nalgal āgādu – being indifferent; nāraṇanai – nārāyaṇan who has exclusive relationship with everyone to protect everyone; kaṇḍakkāl – on seeing him; malgum – flowing abundantly; nīr – having the nature; punal – having water; padappai – gardens; irai – prey; tēr – searching for; vaṇ siṟu kurugē – pleasing to the eyes and young kurugu; malgum – abundant; nīr – having tears; kaṇṇēṟku – me who is having (teary) eyes; ōr vāsagam – a sentence (a message); koṇḍu – taking from me; aruḷāy – help me by informing him

**Перевод:**

**Oh young kurugu who searches for prey in gardens which have abundance of water and who is pleasing to eyes! When you see emperumān who has exclusive relationship with everyone to protect everyone and who with great desire himself removes the hurdles and fulfills the desires of the (people in the) worlds without their expecting so, you give him the message taken from me who is with tearful eyes. nārāyaṇan indicates antaryāmitvam (being the in-dwelling super-soul of everyone) and samudrasāyitvam (lying down in the causal ocean). As said in tiruvāimoḻi 8.10.3 “siṟu mā manisar” (ācāryas with small form but great characteristics), ācāryas forms being small is highlighted.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

[āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says to some kurugus to inform [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) “[bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) who is most merciful, forgives the offenses of all [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)s, removes what is unfavourable for them and protects them in a friendly manner. Why can’t he forgive my mistakes and accept me and mingle with me?” and requests them to get the response from him.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*parāngusa nāyagi requests a few kurugu (heron/stork/pelican) birds to relay back emperumān‘s reply after telling him that if he does not protect her, his nārāyaṇatvam which includes protecting everyone will become questionable.*

Similar to [piḷḷān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/pillan/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, parāngusa nāyagi requests a young kurugu which has a small body which makes it easy to travel (far), to go to emperumān who is sarvarakhsakan (protector of all) to inform about her.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*Similar to nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

Similar to [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*parāngusa nāyagi says (to emperumān) “Forget about us who are going to die any way; But you are trying to live  – Don’t you want to save yourself?” She tells (the kurugu) to inform emperumān to preserve his title of nārāyaṇatvam (being the protector of all). நல்கித் தான் காத்தளிக்கும் பொழிலேழும் வினையேற்கே, நல்கத் தான் ஆகாதொ? நாரணனைக் கண்டக்கால் மல்கு நீர்ப் புனல் படப்பை இரை தேர் வண் சிறு குருகே. மல்கு நீர்க் கண்ணேற்கோர் வாசகம் கொண்டு அருளாயே nalgit tān kāttaḷikkum poḻilēḻum vinaiyēṟkē nalgat tān āgādō nāraṇanaik kaṇḍakkāl malgu nīrp punal padappai irai tēr vaṇ siṟu kurugē malgu nīrk kaṇṇēṟkōr vāsagam koṇḍu aruḷāyē*

- *nalgi* – While protecting his vibhūti (wealth), instead of doing it as a duty, he does it as a desirable result for himself. Just like I have so much attachment towards [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), he has so much attachment towards his subjects.
- *tān* – without their expecting, he himself is going and protecting them.
- *poḻil ēḻum* – poḻil generally means bhūmi. Here it is indicates all fourteen layers where the seventh layer from the top-down is Earth. It can also indicate Earth which has seven islands.
- *nalgittān kāttaḷikkum …* – *nalgi* – Since all of these worlds are considered as [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s body, just like one will take care of his body with great desire, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) too takes care of these worlds with great care. *nalgi* means snēham (with desire) as well as sruśti (creation). When the entire creation was in subtle state, who requested him to transform it to gross/manifested state (these worlds etc)? It was out of his own desire he does these. “*kāttu*” and “*aḷikkum*” both mean protection – these are explained in context of the two meanings of nalgi.
   - When *nalgi* is considered as snēham – *kāttu* means aniśta nivrutti (removing the unfavourable aspects) and *aḷikkum* means iśta prāpti (fulfilling the favourable aspects).
   - When *nalgi* is considered as sruśti – After creating the worlds, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) sustains them and also consumes them in the end to protect them safely. Here *kāttu* means samhāram (where he protects everything by absorbing them within himself) and *aḷikkum* means stiti (sustenance).
- *vinaiyēṟkē nalgattānāgādō* – (*nalgi – sruśti*) When the worlds were not present (they were in subtle state), you created them. But after creating, we start accumulating karma (good and bad) – should you give up on us citing such karma? (*nalgi – snēham*) Should you not protect your dependents? When you are protecting everyone, why not protect your spouse (me) as well?
- *nāraṇanaik kaṇḍakkāl* – He is the ultimate controller of the existence etc., of all jīvātmās. He is the prakāri (substratum) and everything else is prakāram (attributes/forms). Even if one ātmā is not protected, it is a loss to him. This is the meaning of the title “nārāyaṇa”. Go and ask him “We thought this name referred to you as per yaugika (etymological meaning) as well as rūdi (general prevalence) meanings. But, is this like cactus having the name ‘mahāvrukśa’ (great tree – when it is really neither huge nor useful)?” \[The name nārāyaṇa is asādāraṇa (most-distinct) and is only applicable for [srīman nārāyaṇan or viṣṇu](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) – no other dēvatā can claim that name, because only [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) fulfills both yaugika and rūdi principles. For example: mahēśvara indicates rudran by rūdi (general prevalence), but [srīman nārāyaṇan](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) by yaugika (etymological meaning) since he is the only supreme controller\].
- *malgu nīr punal padappai* – garden having abundance of water. your action is for the benefit of others…
- *irai tēr* – Searching for a prey that is suitable for the female companion. Like it is said in periya tirumoḻi 5.1.2 “*puḷḷup piḷḷaikku irai tēdum*” (searching for fish to feed the hatcling) – though big fish are passing by, its waiting for small fish that will fit in the hatcling’s mouth.
- *vaṇ siṟu kurugē* – kurugu is vaṇḍānam or koyyadinārai (types of stork). vaṇmai – beauty, generosity. You are generous unlike [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is feasting (enjoying) while I am starving (suffering) here in separation. Hopefully, your are not like him.
- *malgu nīrk kaṇṇēṟku* – My eyes are also filled with water (tears) and they look like beautiful fish (which attract storks). Teary eyes is [parāngusa nāyagi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s identity it seems. While being together, her eyes are filled with joyful tears and in separation they are filled with sorrowful tears.
- *ōr vāsagam koṇḍu* – Just pass my message to him. [parāngusa nāyagi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is fearful of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) rejecting her. But she just wants a reply from him – whether it is yes or no. In siṟiya tirumadal, [tirumangai āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/thirumangai-azhwar/) says “*tārān tarum enṟu iraṇḍattil onṟadanai*” (he will say yes or no – either way). [āṇḍāḷ](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/andal/) says in nācciyār tirumoḻi 13.9 “*meymmai solli mugam nōkki vidaidān tarumēl miga nanṟu*” (Even if he looks at me and says “I dont want you”, that is very much acceptable – at least at that time he will look at me and I will try to convince him in other ways). [nammāḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) himself says in tiruvāimoḻi 4.7.3 “*pāvi nī enṟu onṟu sollāy*” (Even if you accuse me as a sinner – just open your mouth and speak to me something).
- *aruḷāyē* – bless me – When she considers herself as [sītā pirātti](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/), these birds as her messenger and the result they bring is bhagavat viśayam, then she has to speak to these birds respectfully.  [bhattar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/parasara-bhattar/) was informed “*nambi ēṟutiruvudaiyān dāsar tirunāttukku nadandār*” (nambi ēṟutiruvudaiyān dāsar left/walked to paramapadam). He was startled and then replied “*avar srīvaiṣṇavargaḷudan parimāṟumpadikku, tirunāttukku eḻundaruḷinār ennavēṇum kāṇ*” (for the way he interacted with other srīvaiṣṇavas, you should say ‘he ascended to paramapadam’ in a venerable way) \[srīvaiṣṇavas should speak to other srīvaiṣṇavas with great respect/reverence irrespective of their age, birth, wealth, intelligence etc\].

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.4.6. Arulata nir

*aruḷāda nīr aruḷi avar āvi tuvarā mun aruḷ āḻip puḷ kadavīr avar vīdi oru nāḷ enṟu aruḷ āḻi ammānaik kaṇḍakkāl idu solli  aruḷ āḻi vari vaṇḍē yāmum en piḻaittōme*

**Пословный перевод:**

āḻi – circle shaped; vari vaṇḍē – Oh beetle that has stripes in your body!; aruḷ – Having mercy more than emperumān himself; āḻi – having cakkarattāḻvār (sudarśana cakram); ammānai – that master; kaṇḍakkāl – on seeing; aruḷāda nīr – You who have vowed not to show your mercy on parāngusa nāyagi since she has committed many sins/mistakes; aruḷi – breaking such sankalpam and showing compassion once; avar – her; āvi – ātmā (soul); tuvarāmun – Before her existence dries up; aruḷāḻi – ocean of mercy; puḷ – periya tiruvadi (garudāḻvār); avar vīdi – In the street where she resides; oru nāḷ – at least one day; kadavīr enṟu – take a stroll like you did to protect gajēndrāḻvān; idu solli aruḷ – please tell him this; yāmum – (If you don’t come) we; en piḻaittōm – what mistake was committed?

**Перевод:**

**Oh circle shaped beetle who has stripes on your body! When you go and see the master who has sudarśana cakram (who is even more merciful than emperumān himself) in his hand, please tell him “Oh you who have vowed not to show your compassion on parāngusa nāyagi since she has committed many sins/mistakes! You break your vow and show your compassion once by taking a stroll on the street where she lives on garudāḻvār (who is an ocean of mercy) at least one day – before she loses her existence”. If he refuses to do so, she would wonder “What mistake did we commit that he does not even pass by our street?”.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*Though emperumān is ready to forgive the mistakes of everyone and protect them all, if he is not willing to forgive parāngusa nāyagi (who is special unlike anyone else) and mix with her and thereby not wanting to manifest his kāruṇyam (compassion) etc., what can we tell him?*

Similar to [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*If emperumān feels “If I mix with persons who are with offenses my reputation/greatness will be minimized – even if my nārāyaṇatvam (being the protector of every one) becomes questionable, that is fine” – parāngusa nāyagi requests a beetle (bumble bee) to go “I will suggest an idea that will not cause any damage to his reputation – you ask him to do like that” .*

Similar to [piḷḷān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/pillan/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, parāngusa nāyagi tells a beautiful, radiant beetle (bumble bee) “Give a message to sarvēsvaran who has beautiful cakram in his hand”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*Similar to nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

Similar to [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Previously, parāngusa nāyagi said “Even if you don’t want to eliminate our sufferings in separation, at least ensure that your nārāyaṇatvam is not challenged”. For that, emperumān replied “Even if my nārāyaṇatvam is challenged, I do not want to be accused of mixing with unqualified persons”. Understanding this, parāngusa nāyagi requests a beetle “There is a way where he does not get accused of mixing with unqualified persons yet ensuring we sustain ourselves; he can take a stroll for a sport or to protect an elephant (gajēndran) etc; at such times, if he passes through our streets, that will not hurt his reputation. We would also sustain ourselves by seeing him through the window. Since this is possible, ask him to do that”. அருளாத நீர் அருளி அவர் ஆவி துவரா முன் அருள் ஆழிப் புள் கடவீர் அவர் வீதி ஒரு நாள் என்று அருள் ஆழி அம்மானைக் கண்டக்கால் இது சொல்லி அருள் ஆழி வரி வண்டே. யாமும் என் பிழைத்தோமே? aruḷāda nīr aruḷi avar āvi tuvarā mun aruḷ āḻip puḷ kadavīr avar vīdi oru nāḷ enṟu aruḷ āḻi ammānaik kaṇḍakkāl idu solli  aruḷ āḻi vari vaṇḍē yāmum en piḻaittōme*

- *aruḷāda nīr* – Just like you once vowed as srī rāma in srī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 29.10 “*…ētat vratam mama*” (this is my vow to protect those who surrender unto me), now you have vowed to not shower your mercy upon me. We (nampiḷḷai) cannot understand the current state of āḻvār, who once said “[*mayarvaṟa madinalam aruḷinan*](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/03/thiruvaimozhi-1-1-1-uyarvara-uyarnalam/)” (he blessed me with unblemiśed knowledge), who is now saying “*aruḷāda nīr*” (you who are not blessing me). Here, [parāngusa nāyagi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is giving a name/title “*aruḷāda nīr*“.
- *aruḷi* – blessing me – Compassion is your intrinsic nature. parāngusa nāyagi’s state is so pitiable that even the most unkind person would feel compassion for her. So, why are you not blessing her?
- *avarāvi tuvarāmun* – Bless [parāngusa nāyagi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) before she loses her existence. Just like sītā pirātti requested hanumān to inform srī rāma about her state in srī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 39.10 “*jīvantīm mām yatā rāmassambāvayati kīrtimān…*” (by conveying the message using the appropriate words to the illustrious srī rāma, so that he can console me while I am surviving, you become virtuous through speech), here parāngusa nāyagi is requesting the beetle and the beetle is informing the message to [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/).
- *aruḷāḻip puḷ* – garudāḻvār who is an ocean of mercy; earlier, when garuda carried [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) away from her, she said “*vem ciṟaip puḷ*” (garuda with cruel wings); now that garuda will bring [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) to him, she says “*aruḷāḻip puḷ*“.
- *kadavīr* – “*kadattal*” in tamiḻ is used to indicate driving a vehicle etc (which is [acētanam](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/09/thathva-thrayam-achith-what-is-matter/) – without knowledge) with the effort of the driver. But here, though garuda is [cētanam](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) (knovledgable), he may sometimes be a little bit lethargic/slow (desiring to enjoy [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who has a tender body being seated on him) and [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) desiring to help his devotees quickly, drives garuda by poking him etc., to increase garuda’s speed.
- *avar vīdi* – Where should he take a stroll on garuda? In the street where [parānkusa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) lives. Would it not be suspicious if a person regularly strolls in a street where a girl lives?
- *orunāḷ* – To help us sustain ourselves, he Just needs to visit for one day.
- *aruḷāḻi ammānai* – Multiple explanations given by nampiḷḷai.
   - Our master who is ocean of mercy as stated in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 4.9.2 “*tāmaraiyāḷāgilum sidaguraikkumēl ennadiyār adu seyyār*” (Even if srī mahālakśmi herself finds fault in his devotees, he would say “My devotees would not do anything wrong”). His mercy is even greater than the mercy of periya tiruvadi (garudāḻvār).
   - Considering “*aruḷ*” (compassion) as adjective for “*āḻi*” (sudarśana cakram) – our master who has the most merciful sudarsana cakram in his hands. He is already glorified by [nammāḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) in tiruviruttam 33 “*aruḷār tiruccakkaram*” (sudarśana cakram who has abundance of mercy). [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) himself borrows his mercy from sudarśana cakram. Even if [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) refuses to show mercy, his sudarśana cakram will show mercy towards the devotees.
- *idu solli aruḷ* – you tell him “*aruḷāḻip puḷ kadavīr avar vīdi orunāḷ*“
- *āḻi varivaṇḍē* – beautiful beetle which eliminates our fatigue on seeing it. It can also be said that though the beetle is small, it is most generous/helpful – willing to fulfil the desire of [parāngusa nāyagi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/). This indicates that both the form and qualities of gataka (ācārya) are to be cherished.
- *yāmum en piḻaittōmē* – What mistake did I commit? “*yāmum*” (us also – um in the end indicates “also”) – Just like you let us suffer after separating from us, did we also wait for you to come at your pace? While you are the one who surrendered to an animal (sugrīva) and sent an animal (hanumān) as messenger – now we have reversed that role (surrendering to crane, beetle etc., and sending them as messengers). Even after this, you not coming here – is it your fault or ours?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

adiyen saraty ramanuja dasan

## 1.4.7. Enbu ilai

*enbu iḻai kōppadu pōlap pani vādai īrginṟadu en piḻaiyē ninaindu aruḷi aruḷāda tirumālārkku en piḻaittāḷ tiruvadiyin tagavinukku enṟu oru vāyc col enbu iḻaikkum iḷam kiḷiyē yān vaḷārtta nīyalaiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

enbu iḻaikkum iḷam kiḷiyē – Oh parrot who is piercing my bones with your brimming youth and beauty! enbu = elumbu – bone; yān vaḷartta nīyalaiyē – Were you not raised by me (as appropriate)?; enbu – in the bone; iḻai – string; kōppatu pōla – like piercing it through; pani vādai – freezing wind; īrginṟa – torturing; en piḻaiyē ninaindu aruḷi – mercifully thinking about my mistakes only instead of thinking of his own; aruḷāda – not blessing me; tirumālārkku – to the emperumān who is good towards pirātti who triggers his compassion; tiruvadiyin – for you who are the master; tagavinukku – for the compassion that is your intrinsic nature; en – what; piḻaittāḷ enṟu – mistake that was committed; oru vāy – one word; sol – have to tell

**Перевод:**

**Oh parrot who is piercing my bones with your brimming youth and beauty! The freezing wind is piercing my bones like a string (in separation). To the emperumān who is seeing my mistakes instead of seeing his own mistakes and mercifully not blessing me, you go and tell him “what mistake did parāngusa nāyagi do that cannot be forgiven by you who are the master of pirātti (srī mahālakśmi who triggers his compassion) and who has compassion as your intrinsic nature”.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

parāngusa nāyagi requests her parrot – You go and tell him “On top of my sufferings in separation, I am also tortured by the freezing wind. Instead of thinking of his compassion, he is thinking about my mistakes and not blessing me . Even if I committed mistakes, can they not be dispelled by his compassion?” Oh young parrot! You are piercing my bones by showing your beauty and by reciting his names. When you tell him this message, you tell this in front of srī mahālakśmi – is her relationship not sufficient (to convince him to accept me)?

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In this seventh pāsuram – parāngusa nāyagi meditates on emperumān‘s characteristic of “aparāda sahatvam” (tolerating mistakes) which is the highlight of this padigam (decad) and speaks to her parrot “Tell him ‘Am I falling outside the limits of your aparāda sahatvam?'”.*

Similar to [piḷḷān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/pillan/)‘s vyākhyānam. “*yān vaḷartta nīyalaiyē*” (were you not raised by me?) – would the children torture their mother (who raised them)?

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, parāngusa nāyagi speaks to the parrot which she raised “you go and ask him ‘has she done any mistake that cannot be pardoned by your unlimited compassion?'”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*Similar to nanjīyar‘s introduction. This pāsuram is the highlight of this padigam (decad).*

Similar to [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Considering “Instead of seeing one’s own mistakes, why is she asking me to take a stroll in her street” is emperumān‘s view, parāngusa nāyagi requests her parrot “you tell him ‘should you be seeing our mistakes only? Should you instead not be seeing your aparāda sahatvam?'” என்பு இழை கோப்பது போலப் பனி வாடை ஈர்கின்றது என் பிழையே நினைந்து அருளி அருளாத திருமாலார்க்கு என் பிழைத்தல் திருவடியின் தகவினுக்கு என்று ஒரு வாய்ச சொல் என்பு இழைக்கும் இளம் கிளியே யான் வளர்த்த நீயலையே? enbu iḻai kōppadu pōlap pani vādai īrginṟadu en piḻaiyē ninaindu aruḷi aruḷāda tirumālārkku en piḻaittāḷ tiruvadiyin tagavinukku enṟu oru vāyc col enbu iḻaikkum iḷam kiḷiyē yān vaḷārtta nīyalaiyē*

- *enbu iḻai kōppadu pōl* – The body has become so thin that bones and nerves are visible. Also, cool wind piercing the bone and sending a string through it – here [parāngusa nāyagi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s body can be considered as bone and cool wind as a string. nampiḷḷai explains this using srī rāmāyaṇam kiśkintā kāṇḍam 1.105 where srī rāma says to lakśmaṇa “*padmasaugandikavaham sivam sōkavināsanam \| danyā lakśmaṇa sēvantē pampōpavanamārutam \|\|*” (Oh lakśmaṇa! Those (couples) who receive the soft breeze which is bringing beautiful fragrance from various flowers in ponds etc from the woods near pampā river are fortunate  (i.e., the separated ones are unfortunate and they can’t stand the soft breeze). nampiḷḷai says, for the separated ones, such mild breeze is like form of fire. Seeing the wife suffering in separation, is he gathering the (monkey) armies? Building the bridge? etc.
- *en piḻaiyē ninaindu aruḷi* – thinking about my mistakes. Considering that my sufferings in separation are not enough, he is checking old balances (of my sins etc). Instead of being *avijñātā* (sahasranāmam – one who does not know any mistakes in his devotees), he is being *sahasrāmsu:* (sahasranāmam – having unbounded knowledge (in my mistakes)).
- *aruḷāda tirumālārkku* – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) (husband of srī mahālakśmi) who is not blessing me. One can be upset where there is privileged relationship. [nanjīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nanjiyar/) explains this as – even when [pirātti](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/) (the one who said in srī rāmāyaṇam 116.45 “*na kascinnāparādyati*” (there is no one who does not commit mistakes)) is nearby, he is not blessing me. Does he think that pirātti will speak to him after that? [piḷḷān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/pillan/) explains this as – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is enjoying with pirātti and ignoring me.
- *en piḻaittāḷ tiruvadiyin tagavinukku* – When you (parrot) ask him “Why are you not blessing [parāngusa nāyagi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)?” and he thinks to say “instead of looking at her mistakes, should she be asking me to show compassion?” you reply to him “What mistake did she do that cannot be forgiven by your supremacy?” If he thinks about punishing me for my mistakes, you remind him about his compassion. Can we ever commit mistakes that will overtake the compassion of our master? We commit mistakes within our capability and you forgive within your capability.
- *tiruvadiyin tagavukku en piḻaittāḷ* – nampiḷai explains this as “*dēvarīr krupaikku taṇṇīrt turumbāga ēdēnum pradakśiṇa namaskārādigaḷ paṇṇiṟṟuṇḍō?*” (Did I engage in upāyāntarams which emphasise on self-effort such as doing pradakśiṇam (circumambulation), namaskāram (obeisances) etc., that will be an insult to your krupai (mercy) which is the only protection for us?)
- *tagavinukku* – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is always benevolent towards others as explained in srī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 40.41 “*ānrusamsyam parōdarma:*” – what mistake did she commit that will affect such nature of emperumān? nampiḷḷai quotes srī rāmāyaṇam kiśkintā kāṇḍam 33.40 “*kim kōpamūlam manujēndraputra kastē na santiśtati vāngnidēsē…*” (Oh son of cakravarty! What is the reason for your anger? Who is not following the orders here?…) – tārā enquired lakśmaṇa about the reason for his anger ignoring the fact that they let srī rāma and lakśmaṇa suffer through the rainy season in the caves of the mountain – the reason she dared to ask such questions was due to having faith in their benevolence (that they will forgive her). She calls him *manujēndraputra* (son of cakravarty) to indicate that dasarata cakravarty ruled 60000 years without punishing anyone for his/her mistakes – being his son, she expects them to be merciful as well. She also indicates to him that it was they who killed vāli and asked them to enjoy freely after suffering for a long period – now they themselves cannot feel angry at the action of monkeys who do not understand śāstram etc.
- *enbu iḻaikkum iḷam kiḷiyē* – the parrot that is youthful, humble, fresh, having red mouth and attracting the nāyaka (master) through these – such parrot is melting my bones (by such attraction). It can also be said as “*en piḻaikkum*” – what is wrong in informing my state to [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)?
- *yān vaḷartta nīyalaiyē* – You are raised/nurtured by me (like my child) – would you also do the same that is done by [sriya:pati](https://vedarama.com/en/books/tiruvaymozhi/%20http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) (husband of [srī mahālakhsmi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/)) who was not-born to any one? Would my own offspring do the same thing that is done by those who mixed with me and left me in separation? Since I have raised you, you also would behave like me only – is there any fault in you?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.4.8. Niyalaiye sirupuvay

*nīyalaiyē siṟupūvāy nedumālārkku en tūdāynōy enadu nuvalenna nuvalādē irundoḻindāysāyalodu maṇimāmai taḷarndēn nān ini unaduvāy alagil innadisil vaippārai nādāyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

siṟu pūvāy – Oh bird that is small due to your tender age!; nedumālārkku – One who is greatly mad (Out of unbounded vātsalyam towards his devotees); en tūdāy – going as my messenger; enadu – my; nōy – disease of separation; nuval enna – having requested you to tell; nuvalādē – not telling him; irundu oḻindāy – ignored me out out of pride (of not desiring to go on my behalf); nīyalaiyē – isn’t that you?; nān – I; sāyalodu – radiance; maṇi – worthy of praise; māmai – color; taḷarndēn – lost; ini – after being engrossed in him like this; unatu – your; vāy alagil – inside your beak; in – sweet; adisil – rice/food; vaippārai – one who would feed; nādāy – search for them outside

**Перевод:**

**Oh myna that is small due to your tender age! Having requested you to go as my messenger and tell emperumān who is greatly mad (Out of unbounded vātsalyam towards his devotees) about my disease in separation, you ignored my request out of pride despite your being raised by me. I have lost my radiant lustre and colour from my body. After this, you have to search for someone who can comfortably feed you sweet food that fits your beak/mouth.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

Similar to [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the eighth pāsuram – looking at a pūvai (myna) bird, parāngusa nāyagi tells about her great fatigue (exhaustion) that was caused due to separation from emperumān.*

Similar to [piḷḷān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/pillan/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, parāngusa nāyagi tells her young pet myna which was raised by her, “Go and tell the one who has endless vātsalyam (motherly forbearance) about my disease (in separation)”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*In the Eighth pāsuram, parāngusa nāyagi tells about her disease to her pet myna which is exhausted seeing her state of fatigue.*

Similar to [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Eighth pāsuram – Previously when parāngusa nāyagi was discussing and sharing her emotion, the pūvai (myna) also sustained itself – but when she was exhausted, it also became exhausted. Looking at that myna, parāngusa nāyagi says “‘Previously I told you to inform my state to him’ – you ignored my requests out of pride, now I am going to die soon. So, you find some one who can take care of you”. pūvai – nāgaṇavāippuḷ – a type of bird \[resembling our myna\]. நீயலையே சிறுபூவாய் நெடுமாலார்க்கு என் தூதாய் நோய் எனது நுவலென்ன நுவலாதே இருந்தொழிந்தாய்சாயலோடு மணிமாமை தளர்ந்தேன் நான் இனி உனது வாய் அலகில் இன்னடிசில் வைப்பாரை நாடாயே nīyalaiyē siṟupūvāy nedumālārkku en tūdāynōy enadu nuvalenna nuvalādē irundoḻindāysāyalodu maṇimāmai taḷarndēn nān ini unaduvāy alagil innadisil vaippārai nādāyē*

- *nīyalaiyē* – īsn’t this you? I requested you to inform my state to him – but you have ignored my request. So, we have come to this situation because of your inaction. If you informed him and he did not turn up, it is his fault – but now we cannot say that it is his fault since you have not gone and informed him. [parāngusa nāyagi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) establishes that bhagavallābam (achieving [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)) is by the efforts of gataka (ācārya). Even though one has eternal relationship with [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/), ācārya is cherished due to the favour (of reminding about that eternal relationship) done by him. As explained in “*ādadīta yatō jñānam tam pūrvam abivādayēt*” – one shall first offer obeisances to ācārya from whom one grasps different types of knowledge.
- *sīṟu pūvāy* – youthful myna – your immaturity caused this difficulty for us.
- *nedumālārkku* – you don’t need to create vyāmōha (bewilderment) in him (he is already greatly mad about his devotees). In tamiḻ, *māl* means mad.
- *en tūdāy* – if both were equally longing for each other, there is no need for the messenger.
- *nōy enadu –* my disease. It is like the disease of bharatāḻvān – this is explained as something which lasts for long time unlike cāturtikam (a type of fever which is considered fatal) – this is not a real disease but it is the disease of separation. nampiḷḷai beautifully quotes srī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 100.1 “*jatilam ciravasanam prānjalim patitam bhuvi\| dadarśa rāmō durdarśam yugāntē bhāskaram yatā \|\|*” (Having matted hair, wearing tree-bark-robes, having joined palms, lying flat on the earth. [srī rāma](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)  is unable to bear that vision that is like the radiant sun during dissolution). This slōkam explains the state of [parāngusa nāyagi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) and [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/) explains the slōkam word-by-word:
   - *jatilam* – When daśarata sees beautiful garlands, he immediately says “this will be nice for bharata’s hair” – such hair is matted now
   - *ciravasanam* – When daśarata sees beautiful clothes, he says “this is for our son” – such bharata is wearing tree-bark-robes.
   - *prānjalim* – one who always performs charity to those who join their palms towards him – he now has joined palms.
   - *patitam bhuvi* – the bharata who is said as “*ankē bharatam āropya*” (srī rāma placing bharata on his lap), one who sleeps on lap since he is so tender that even sleeping on bed could be irritating – he is now lying on the ground.
   - *dadarśa rāmō durdarśam* – srī rāma never takes his eyes off his younger brother bharata – now srī rāma is incapable of seeing him due to his state
   - *yugāntē bhāskaram yatā* – Not only that, it seemed like ultimate dissolution was dawning on him.
- *sāyalodu maṇimāmai taḷarndēn nān* – What is the result of your not informing my state to him? I lost both my lustre and colour. The myna said “I will inform him at once”; but what is the use of building a dam after the floods had drained? Similarly, what is the use of informing now after my losing everything?
- *ini unadu vāyalagil innadisil vaippārai nādāyē* – Even if he comes now, the lost lustre and colour will not be back. You go and seek out your caretaker now. [periya tirumalai nambi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/periya-thirumalai-nambi/) had a small arccā vigraham (idol) of kriṣṇa named “veṇṇeykkādum piḷḷai” (one who dances for butter) in his tiruvārādanam. In his last moments, he asked to remove the screen in front of the tiruvārādana perumāḷ and said to the [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) “*sāyalodu maṇimāmai taḷarndēn nān, ini unadu vāyalagil innadisil vaippārai nādāyē”* (My time is up here, you have to find someone who will worship you in this world).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.4.9. Nadada malar

*nādāda malar nādi nāḷ tōṟum nāraṇan tan vādāda malar adik kīḻ vaikkavē vagukkinṟu vīdādi vīṟṟiruttal vinai aṟṟadu en seyvadō ūdādu pani vādāy uraittīrāy enadu udalē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ūdu – In between (emperumān and me); ādu – occurring/travelling; pani vādāy – Oh cool wind!; nādāda – rare (difficult to find); malar – flowers; nādi – seek out; nāḷ tōṟum – daily; nāraṇan than – unto nārāyaṇa (who has eternal relationship with everyone as master); vādāda malar adik kīḻ – unto the fresh lotus feet of emperumān; vaikkavē – on offering; vagukkinṟu – engaging (the senses); vīdu – in separation; ādi – occurring; vīṟṟiruttal – being alone; vinai aṟṟadu – unfortunate situation; en seyvadō – what is the result of it?; uraittu – telling him (and if he gives unfavourable answer); enadu udal – my body; īrāy – kill it so it does not exist

**Перевод:**

**Simple transalation (based on vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar‘s 12000 padi)**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

Similar to [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the ninth pāsuram – āḻvār requests the cool wind: after informing emperumān “Can you let your subservient person die down like this?” if he still ignores me, you should surely put me to my end.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, parānkusa nāyaki looks at the cool wind which returns from emperumān to finish her unlike previous occasions and tells it “After informing him who is naturally related to me, you can come and harm me”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*Similar to nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

Similar to [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Ninth pāsuram – When parāngusa nāyagi was thinking as in (the previous pāsuram) “sāyalodu maṇi māmai taḷarntēn nān” (I have become tired losing my colour, lustre etc), a cool wind touches her body. Seeing its nature, she thought that there is something to it, just like tārai said “sugrīva was struggling till a little while ago being beaten up by vāli – but the same sugrīva has returned with a great roar – there must be something to it (i.e., having the support of srī rāma))”. When a king sends his servants to torture those who disobey (or defame) the king, those persons may try to give some wealth etc to the servants to avoid the torture. In the same way parāngusa nāyagi tells the cool wind “you go and inform him about my plight and if he does not care about my offerings, then you can return to put me to my end”. நாடாத மலர் நாடி நாள் தோறும் நாரணன் தான், வாடாத மலர் அடிக் கீழ் வைக்கவே வகுக்கின்று, வீடாடி வீற்றிருத்தல் வினை அற்றது என் செய்வதோ? ஊடாது பனி வாடாய். உரைத்தீராய் எனது உடலே. nādāda malar nādi nāḷ tōṟum nāraṇan than vādāda malar adik kīḻ vaikkavē vagukkinṟu vīdādi vīṟṟiruttal vinai aṟṟadu en seyvadō ūdādu pani vādāy uraittīrāy enadu udalē*

- *nādāda malar nādi* – Some say this (flower) relates to “*ātma puśpam*” (the flower of [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) which has certain auspicious qualities). Instead of that, nanjīyar explains this as highlighted in tiruvāimoḻi 4.7.8 “*eṇḍhisaiyum uḷḷa pūk koṇḍu*” (bringing flowers from eight directions) – bringing flowers which are rare to find.
- *nāḷ tōṟum* – Without any break. For the [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) whose true nature (of servitude) is established by kincitkāram (a little service), break in such service is an obstacle.
- *nāraṇan* – One who is [sarvasvāmy](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) (master of all) who deserves to be served always
- *vādāda malar adik kīḻ* – unto the lotus feet which look like fresh flowers. Even while being separated (in suffering), the lotus feet are so reliśable and thus cannot be given up.
- *vaikkavē* – to keep
- *vagukkinṟu* – present for that only. Just as it is explained in srī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 40.5 “*sruśtastvam vanavāsāya*” (sumitrai says to lakśmaṇa – “you are created to accompany (and serve) srī rāma in the forest”. Similarly, the purpose of [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)‘s existence is to serve the most appropriate/deserving, easily approachable and ever reliśable lotus feet of emperumān.
- *vīdu ādi vīṟṟiruttal vinai aṟṟadu en seyvadō* – Just like sēśabhūta’s ([jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)/servitor) true nature is established by rendering service, sēśi’s ([bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)/master) true nature is established by accepting such service. *vīdu* – leaving/separating. *vīṟṟiruttal* – being seated comfortably (in separation). *vinai aṟukkai* – terminating my good fortunes.  Two explanations are given:
   - Instead of accepting my service, he is enjoying in separation from me. What can I do seeing this act of his?
   - Being separated from him and also being given up by my relatives (and thus separated from them too), what can I do?
- *ūdādu pani vādāy* – Just like a servant/messenger will convey messages between two persons, the cool wind is travelling back and forth between me and emperumān. Also explained as: *ūdu* – inside, *ādugai* – travelling. Reaching up to the inner quarters of emperumān or you who were near us during the times we were together.
- *uraittu* – When you tell him “this [parāngusa nāyagi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) ([jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)) is born only to serve you eternally”, if he says “I don’t even want the kainkaryam from her”, you return and put an end to my body which cannot bear the separation from him.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.4.10. Udal ali

*udal āḻip piṟappu vīdu uyir mudalā muṟṟumāy kadal āḻi nīr tōṟṟi adanuḷḷē kaṇ vaḷarum adal āḻi ammānaik kaṇḍakkāl idu solli vidal āḻi mada nenjē vinaiyōm onṟām aḷavē*

**Пословный перевод:**

āḻi – deep; mada nenjē – Oh (my) humble mind!; udal – in body; āḻi – in the form of a cakram (disc/cyclic); piṟappu – the material realm which is the abode of birth after birth; vīdu – mōkśam (liberation) which is being relieved from previously explained cycle of birth; uyir – ātmā which is the enjoyer of bhōgam (in material realm) and mōkśam (in spiritual realm); mudalāy – being the controller of ātmā etc; muṟṟumāy – being the prakāri (substratum) for the protection of everything; āḻi nīr – deep water; kadal – in the kśīrārṇavam (milk ocean); tōṟṟi – being visible; adanuḷḷē – inside that; kaṇ vaḷarum – lying down; adal – being war-ready (towards the enemies of the devotees); āḻi – cakkarattāḻvār’s; ammānai – master; kaṇḍakkāl – on seeing him; idu – (present) suffering; solli – informing (him); vinaiyōm – us who are having sins (that is the cause for this separation); onṟāmaḷavu – until I become united (with him); vidal – don’t leave

**Перевод:**

**Oh my deep mind! When you see the master (emperumān) of the war-ready cakkarattāḻvār, who is lying down in the milk ocean, who is the controller of ātmās who take birth in this cycle of samsāram to be free from the cycle, and who has become the different forms etc., tell him about my present suffering due to my sins and don’t leave him until I become united with him.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

Similar to [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the tenth pāsuram – Looking at her mind which is restless on contemplating the servitude towards emperumān which was discussed in previous pāsuram, parāngusa nāyagi requests her mind “you sustain me until emperumān is informed about our state and fulfils our desire”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, she affirms her desires through her mind which goes out of its own volition to kśīrābdinātan (emperumān in milk-ocean which is in the material realm) who is close-by in comparison to paramapadanātan (emperumān in parampadam which is in the spiritual realm).*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*Similar to nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Tenth pāsuram – Some say that “leaving aside other messengers, parāngusa nāyagi is sending her own mind as messenger”. In such case “vidal” means “hold on to emperumān“.  Instead, another explanation is given – In the previous pāsuram, after inherent servitude towards him is identified in “vaikkavē vagukkinṟu“, just like a calf that would run towards its mother’s udder, parāngusa nāyagi‘s mind restlessly starts moving towards emperumān giving up on the body; at that time, parāngusa nāyagi says “don’t leave me until our desire is fulfilled”. உடல் ஆழிப் பிறப்பு வீடு உயிர் முதலா முற்றுமாய் கடல் ஆழி நீர் தொற்றி அதனுள்ளே கண் வளரும் அடல் ஆழி அம்மானைக் கண்டக்கால் இது சொல்லி விடல் ஆழி மட நெஞ்சே வினையோம் ஒன்றாம் அளவே udal āḻip piṟappu vīdu uyir mudalā muṟṟumāy kadal āḻi nīr tōṟṟi adanuḷḷē kaṇ vaḷarum adal āḻi ammānaik kaṇḍakkāl idu solli vidal āḻi mada nenjē vinaiyōm onṟām aḷavē*

- *udal āḻip piṟappu vīdu –* ātmā acquiring different bodies through repeated births – to attain the puruśārttams (goals) such as mōkśam etc. Cyclic births – the beginning and end is unknown. āḻi is also explained as ocean – very deep and countless births. vīdu – mōkśam (liberation). It is said like this since the goal of creation (by [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)) is to facilitate the jīvātmās towards mōkśam.
- *vīduyir* – another explanation starting with *vīdu*. *vīdu* (house) – sarīram. ātmās residing in the bodies.
- *āy* – become. As explained in taittirya upaniśat “*bahu syām*” (let me become many) – it is the transformation of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s own body \[cit and acit – from sūkśma (subtle) state to stūla (gross) state\].
- *kadal āḻi nīr tōṟṟi* – creating the single huge deep ocean (water body) and lying down there to perform creation etc.
- *adal āḻi ammānai* – To protect the ones who are created by him from their predators, he is lying down alert with his hands holding on to the cakram.
- *kaṇḍakkāl* – on seeing him – You will be fortunate to attain the goal (of seeing him) before I do.
- *idu solli* – Tell him “*vaikkavē vagukkiṇru*” (created to serve you). Ask him “Is it not the goal of creation/birth to perform kainkaryam to you?” as mentioned in srī viṣṇu darmam “*vicitrā dēhasampattir īśvarāya nivēditum \| pūrvamēva krutā brahman hastapādādisamyutā \|\|*” (Oh brāhmaṇa! To offer oneself and other materials, ātmā previously got connected to the amazing body with hands and legs).
- *āḻi mada nenjē* – knowledgeable, humble mind. It is also explained as ignorant mind.
- *vinaiyōm onṟām aḷavum vidal* – While the whole purpose of creation is to reach him and perform kainkaryam to him, I am being separated due to my sins; you have to hold on to him until I reach him.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.4.11. Alavu iyanra

*aḷavu iyanṟa ēḻulagattavar perumān kaṇṇanai vaḷa vayal sūḻ vaṇ kurugūrc catakōpan vāyndu uraitta aḷavu iyanṟa andādi āyirattuḷ ippattin vaḷa vuraiyāl peṟal āgum vān ōngu peru vaḷamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

aḷavu – boundary; iyanṟa – crossed/beyond; ēḻu – seven types of; ulagattavar – cētanas (sentients) who are residents of world; perumān – one who is glorified as the master; kaṇṇanai – kriṣṇa (who is easily approachable by his devotees); vaḷam – abundant/rich; vayal – fertile fields; sūḻ – surrounded by; vaṇ – beautiful; kurugūr – controller of āḻvārtirunagari; satakōpan – nammāḻvār; vāyndu – approached (with jñānam (knowledge) and prēmam (devotion)); uraitta – mercifully spoken by; aḷavu – in pramāṇams (which are decorated properly in poetic metrics); iyanṟa – being present; andādi – in andādi type of poem (last word/letter of one pāsuram remains consistent with the first word/letter of the next pāsuram); āyirattu – in the thousand pāsurams; uḷ – those which reveal āḻvār‘s bhāva (mood) and banda (relationship); ippattin – of these 10 pāsurams; vaḷam – sweet; uraiyāl – words alone; vān – in paramapadam; ōngu – lofty; peru vaḷam – kainkarya sāmrājyam (the kingdom of servitude); peṟalām – can be achieved

**Перевод:**

**nammāḻvār, who is the controller of beautiful āḻvārtirunagari which is surrounded with fertile fields, approached and mercifully spoke about kaṇṇan emperumān who is the master of cētanas who are the residents of the seven types of worlds in these 1000 pāsurams of tiruvāimoḻi in andādi style. For those who recite this padigam (decad – 10 pāsurams) which reveals āḻvār‘s devotional mood and relationship with emperumān, lofty wealth of kainkaryam in parampadam is achievable.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

Similar to [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the end, āḻvār says those who learned this tiruvāimoḻi (padigam/decad) will get the unlimited wealth of the liberated souls in paramapadam.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says that the result of this tiruvāimoḻi is the wealth and enjoyment of liberation.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*Similar to nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*In the end, āḻvār says that just by reciting the pāsurams in this tiruvāimoḻi (padigam/decad), one will reach paramapadam. அளவு இயன்ற ஏழுலகத்தவர் பெருமான் கண்ணனை வள வயல் சூழ் வான் குருகுற்ச சடகோபன் வாய்ந்து உரைத்த அளவு இயன்ற அந்தாதி ஆயிரத்துள் இப்பத்தின் வள உரையால் பேரால் ஆகும் வான் ஓங்கு பெரு வளமே aḷavu iyanṟa ēḻulagattavar perumān kaṇṇanai vaḷa vayal sūḻ vaṇ kurugūrc catakōpan vāyndu uraitta aḷavu iyanṟa andādi āyirattuḷ ippattin vaḷa vuraiyāl peṟal āgum vān ōngu peru vaḷamē*

- *aḷaviyanṟa* – “viyanda” has become “viyanṟa”. viyattal means kadattal (crossing) which means beyond measurement. [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is “*apariccēdya mahiman*” (one with unlimited glories). This indicates that he is filled with auspicious qualities such as jñānam etc to bless us.
- *ēḻulagattavar perumān* – Being the master of everyone without giving up his nārāyaṇatvam (being the protector of everyone). [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) too is inside the 7 worlds – thus indicating his own dependence on him.
- *kaṇṇanai* – One who freely mixed with his devotees – thus eliminating the defect of not showing mercy. As [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) greatly desired to enjoy kriṣṇa in “[*pattudai adiyavar*](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/05/thiruvaimozhi-1-3-paththudai/)“, he sends a messenger – so when [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) becomes visible to him now, he says its kriṣṇa. From this, we can understand that [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s mēnmai (greatness) and saulabhyam (easy approacability) got established after showing mercy to [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/).
- *vaḷāvayal* – rich fields.  Jut as it is said in srī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 127.17 and 127.18 “*akālapaliṇō vrukśā:…*” (srī rāma requests bharadvāja riśi – Oh bharadvāja bhagavān! When we reach ayōdya, on our way, let the trees blossom even during non-season and give us fruits and honey-giving-flowers).
- *vāyndu uraitta* – Reciting in great suffering/pain in separation.
- *aḷavu iyanṟa andādi* – Since the pāsurams talk about [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who has unlimited glories, the pāsurams too have unlimited glories.
- *vānōngu peru vaḷam peṟalām* – Just like milk (which is tasty) itself is medicine for certain diseases, this pāsuram (which is sweet) leads to paramapadam. By reciting these pāsurams without any expectation, one can give up the limited state in this material realm, reach paramapadam, attain real inherent nature of [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) and enjoy endless pleasure of servitude to [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/).

Two summaries given by nampiḷḷai in the end.

First summary – explaining the message in each pāsuram:

- In the first pāsuram, [parāngusa nāyagi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) sends a nārai (crane) as messenger to [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/).
- In the second pāsuram, she teaches to some cuckoos as to what to say when they go to him.
- In the third pāsuram, she requests some swans to go and tell him “my sins are endless (may be that is holding you up)”.
- In the fourth pāsuram, she asks some love birds, “would you go and inform him about my state or not?”.
- In the fifth pāsuram, she tells some herons “Tell him to preserve his nārāyaṇatvam (by protecting me also)”.
- In the sixth pāsuram, she tells a bumble bee “you go and tell him to take a stroll in my street so we can sustain ourselves and his nārāyaṇatvam can be preserved”.
- In the seventh pāsuram, she speaks to a parrot “Ask him if he will just look only at my defects. Ask him to look at his aparāda sahatvam (quality of forgiving defects) also”.
- In the eighth pāsuram, she speaks to a pūvai which becomes exhausted seeing her exhaustion “I am going to die soon; you go and seek out someone who can protect you”
- In the ninth pāsuram, she tells the cool wind “When you go and inform my suffering to him and if he rejects me, you return to put me to my end”.
- In the tenth pāsuram, she sends her mind/heart to him telling “Don’t leave him until our desire is fulfilled”.
- In the end, he declares the result for those who recited this padigam and completes the padigam.

Second summary – explaining the attributes of gataka (ācārya) as seen in the pāsurams:

- In the first pāsuram, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) explains the greatness of ācārya’s knowledge.
- In the second pāsuram, he explains that the ācārya speaks sweet language.
- In the third pāsuram, he says ācārya is sāra asāra vivēkajña (one who can intelligently distinguish between essence and residue).
- In the fourth pāsuram, he recollects ācārya’s beautiful form.
- In the fifth pāsuram, he explains that ācārya is so pure that he will have patience to attain the desired goal.
- In the sixth pāsuram, he explains that ācārya only enjoys [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/); his form is beautiful, he is also merciful and grave.
- In the seventh pāsuram, he explains that though the ācārya may be all-knowing, he would not say something which is not heard from his ācāryas. Thus ācārya’s trustworthiness is established.
- In the eighth pāsuram, he says that taking care of ācārya’s bodily needs is the most important spiritual duty of the siśya.
- In the ninth pāsuram, he explains that relationship with ācārya is the only thing that sustains the siśya.
- In the tenth pāsuram, he explains that anything other than ācārya sambandam is an impediment for the siśya’s sustenance.
- Thus, the siśya being situated in the manner explained in each pāsuram in relationship with ācārya and serving such ācārya, his desire in kainkaryam to [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) becomes nurtured and will reach [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) in paramapadam.

Thus ends the English translation for tiruvāimoḻi 1st centum 4th decad.

## 1.5 Valavel ulagin

## 1.5.1. Valavel ulagin

*vaḷavēḻ ulagin mudalāya vānōr iṟaiyai aruvinaiyēn kaḷavēḻ veṇṇey toduvuṇḍa kaḷvā enban pinnaiyumtaḷavēḻ muṟuval pinnaikkāy vallān āyar talaivanāyiḷa ēṟ ēḻum taḻuviya endāy enban ninaindu naindē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vaḷam – big/spacious (great); ēḻulagin – for the seven worlds; mudalāya – etc (and other areas of the material realm); vānōr – residents of paramapadam (spiritual realm) – nityasūris and muktātmās; iṟaiyai – that supreme lord who is the master of both spiritual and material realm; aruvinaiyēn – I who have inexhaustible sins; ninaindu – having meditated upon (with my mind); naindu – (body becoming) depleted; kaḷavēḻ – being interested in stealing; veṇṇey – butter; todu uṇḍa – eating secretly; kaḷvā! – Oh thief!; enban – will say (the words of mother yasōdā); pinnaiyum – further; taḷavu – (mullai) jasmine; ēḻ – looking like; muṟuval – having gentle smile; pinnaikku – for nappinnai (neeḷā dēvi who is one of the primary consorts of srīman nārāyaṇan appeared as satyā/nappinnai, as the daughter of kumba (nagnajit)); āy – keeping you at her disposal; val – famous; ānāyar – of the gōpas (covherd persons); talaivanāy – coming as the leader; iḷam – youthfully arrogant; ēṟu – bulls; ēḻum – seven of them; taḻuviya – embraced and killed them (wanting to engage with nappinnai after winning over the bulls); endāy – Oh my master!; enban – I will say (the words of those who are dear to you)

**Перевод:**

**I, having inexhaustible sins, meditated upon the supreme lord of both material and spiritual reams, became depleted and said “Oh thief! You are stealing butter with great interest and eating it secretly” as said by mother yasōdā. Further, as said by those who are dear to you (nappinnai), I said “Oh my master! To marry nappinnai,  being at her disposal, you came as the leader of the covherd clan, embraced the seven youthful bulls and killed them”.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

Why is love/devotion towards [bhagavān,](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) which is explained as the “ultimate goal”, highlighted by [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) as pāpam (sin)? pāpam (sin) is that which causes sorrow. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) thinks “my glorification of  [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) does not suit emperumān’s greatness and thus will diśonour him”.  Such diśonour of emperumān will bring sorrow to āḻvār – and thus he considers his devotion towards emperumān as a sin.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the first pāsuram – āḻvār is grieving saying “I, who am most abominable, have diśonoured the most distinct emperumān with my mind, words and deeds”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*In the first pāsuram – āḻvār says he diśonoured sarvēsvaran (who sustains/cures everyone) through his three karaṇams (instruments – mind, words and deeds) like mixing of poison in nectar.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

ninaintu – mānasa (by mind); naintu – kāyika (by actions); enban – vācika (by words);

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*First pāsuram – āḻvār says he diśonoured that emperumān who is enjoyed by nityasūris with his mind, words and deeds. வளவேழ் உலகின் முதலாய வானோர் இறையை அருவினையென் களவேழ் வெண்ணெய் தொடுவுண்ட கள்வா. என்பன் பின்னையும்தளவேழ் முறுவல் பின்னைக்காய் வல்லான் ஆயர் தலைவனாய்,இள ஏற் ஏழும் தழுவிய எந்தாய். என்பன் நினைந்து நைந்தே. vaḷavēḻ ulagin mudalāya vānōr iṟaiyai aruvinaiyēn kaḷavēḻ veṇṇey toduvuṇḍa kaḷvā enban pinnaiyumtaḷavēḻ muṟuval pinnaikkāy vallān āyar talaivanāyiḷa ēṟ ēḻum taḻuviya endāy enban ninaindu naindē*

- *vaḷa ēḻ ulagu mudalāya* – vaḷam (greatness) is explained as an attribute of the *ēḻ ulagu* (material realm), *vānōr* (nityasūris) and *iṟai* ([bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)). Also, by highlighting *ēḻ ulagu* (material realm) and vānōr (residents of spiritual realm) – [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s ubhaya vibhūti nātatvam (being the controller of both material and spiritual realm) is established. While explaining this as nityasūris being the cause of creation, a doubt arises if they are involved in creation (as only bhagavān is said as the singular cause of everything) and this doubt is explained using srī. In srīviṣṇu purāṇam astra bhūśaṇa adyāyam (the section where bhagavān’s weapons, ornaments etc., are explained in detail). Here it is explained that “bhagavān bears the collection of [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)s on his kaustuba jewel” and “bhagavān bears the [insentient matter](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/09/thathva-thrayam-achith-what-is-matter/) on his srīvatsa mole”.
- *vānōr iṟaiyai* – Since nityasūris are dēsikas (ones who know the truth) they know well that [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is their svāmy (master). [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) wanted to say “*vānōr iṟaiyaik kaḷvā enban*” (I will call master of [nityasūris](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) as thief), but before completing the sentence, he started thinking about himself and said “*aruvinaiyēn*” (most sinful me). Just like a virtuous person would set fire to his house due to moods of passion/ignorance and later when good sense prevails will atone for that, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) too thinks he called [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) kaḷvā (thief) out of love and then realises he did a mistake and worries for that.
- *aruvinaiyēn* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is calling himself most sinful – here, the love which induced him to call [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) as “kaḷvā” is the sin. Since it is said “*aniśtāvaham pāpam*” (that which produces unfavourable result is sin), āḻvār’s love is highlighted by him as sin, since it brings disrepute to [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) (according to āḻvār’s thinking out of humility).
- *kaḷavēḻ veṇṇey toduvuṇḍa kaḷvā enban* – kaḷavēḻ – One who enjoys stealing, one who steals so that others know about it. With this, āḻvār is saying that he is repeating the words of mother yasōdā.
- *taḷavēḻ* … – I also spoke the words of (his dear consort) nappinnai to whom [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) revealed even more than what was revealed to mother yasōdā.
- *taḷavēḻ muṟuval* – jasmine buds are no comparison to the beauty of nappinnai’s teeth (her teeth are so much more beautiful) – yet just like when one sees a wild cow, he gets reminded about the domestic cow, nappinnai’s teeth are compared to jasmine buds.
- *pinnaikku āy* – Being flattened by nappinnai’s smile, kriṣṇa came under her control fully.
- *vallāṇāyar talaivanāy* – two explanations:
   - valla (great/strong) is explained as an attribute of āyar – As said in mahābhāratam drōṇa parvam 183.24 “*kriṣṇāsrayā: kriṣṇabalā: kriṣṇānātāsca pāṇḍavā:*” (pāṇḍavas – surrendered to kriṣṇa, kriṣṇa is their strength, kriṣṇa is their master) pāṇḍavas were walking around with great self-belief and confidence due to their dependence on kriṣṇa and were thus winning over everyone easily – similarly the covherd clan was great/strong due to their dependence on kriṣṇa.
   - vallāṇ is explained as an attribute of “talaivan of ānāyar” (kriṣṇa – leader of covherd clan) – He would not even take bath properly (as it is common for covherd clan). Even if some covherds take bath on certain festive occasions, kriṣṇa would not bathe  even on such days (proving his covherd nature even more than others). Only such grooms will find good brides in covherd clan. sundara bāhu stavam 7 “… *kulēna sadrusi …*” (kriṣṇa being born in kśatriya kula and being raised in vaisya kula, married rukmiṇi and nappinnai matching the respective clan he was associated with) and srī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 16.5 “*tulya seela vayō vruttām…*” (sītā pirātti is equally great in nature, age, actions etc with respect to srī rāma) are to be remembered.
- *iḷa ēṟu* *ēḻum taḻuvi* – He embraced the seven deadly bulls by combining their necks together. The word “*taḻuvi*” (embrace) is used since, after killing the bulls, he embraced nappinnai pirātti.
- *endāy enban* – I repeated those words said by nappinnai pirātti after she was won over by kriṣṇa by defeating the seven bulls.
- *ninaindu* – I even caused disrepute to him by mind.
- *naindē* – by becoming emaciated, which others came to know about, I caused disrepute through body/actions as well.
- [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is feeling sorry for saying “[*ayarvaṟum amarargaḷ adipadi*](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/03/thiruvaimozhi-1-1-1-uyarvara-uyarnalam/)” (which matches “*vaḷavēḻulagin mudalāya vānōr iṟaiyai*“), “[*ettiṟam*](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/06/thiruvaimozhi-1-3-1-paththudai-adiyavar/)*“* (which relates to “*kaḷavēḻ veṇṇey toduvuṇḍa kaḷvā*“) and sending messenger assuming the form of his consort in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.4](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/07/thiruvaimozhi-1-4-anjiraiya/) (which relates to “*iḷavēṟēḻum taḻuviya entāy*“).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.5.2. Ninaindu naindu

*ninanidu naindu uḷ karaindu urugi imaiyōr palarum munivarum punainda kaṇṇi nīr sāndam pugaiyōdu ēndi vaṇangināl ninainda ellāp poruḷgatkum vittāy mudalil sidaiyāmē manam sey jñānttu un perumai māsūṇādō māyōnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

imaiyōr – dēvas starting with brahmā, who don’t blink their eyes (ever); munivarum – those great sages who are constantly meditating on you – such as sanaka kumāras; palarum – many more; ninaindu – thinking (about your auspicious qualities in their hearts/minds); naindu – body becoming weak/depleted due to such constant meditation; uḷ karaindu – being heart-broken; urugi – becoming melted; punainda – prepared/made (with such great love); kaṇṇi – garland; nīr – water for arghyam (washing hands), etc; sāndam – sandalwood paste; pugaiyōdu – with fragrant incense sticks; ēndi – holding them (for your acceptance); vaṇangināl – when they worship (you for having accepted their offerings); māyōnē – Oh the one who is always present together with the magnificent and distinct realm!; ninainda – (out of mercy during creation) thought upon; ellāp poruḷgatkum – for all entities; vittāy – being the upādāna kāraṇa (raw-material cause); mudalil sidaiyāmē – without any change in your true nature; manam – in heart/mind; sey – performed; jñānattu – having knowledge in the form of sankalpam (vow); un – your; perumai – glories; māsūṇādō? – would they not be tarnished?

**Перевод:**

**Oh the one who is always present together with the magnificent and distinct wealth (realm)! dēvas who don’t blink their eyes, the sanakādi (sanaka et al) riśis who are always meditating upon you, and many more, are on constant meditation upon your auspicious qualities, becoming depleted (due to great emotions out of such meditation) and becoming heart-broken and totally melted for you. They stand seeking your acceptance holding garlands which were prepared with great love/affection, water (for washing hands etc), sandalwood paste, fragrant incense sticks and worship you gratefully on your acceptance. But even when such great personalities worship you, who out of great compassion became the material-cause for all entities through your knowledge in the form of a vow, without any transformation to your true nature, would that not tarnish your glories?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the second pāsuram – āḻvār says “Who am I to say I am not qualified to glorify you? Only brahmā, rudra et al can say that they are not qualified to glorify you”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently – āḻvār considering that emperumān is asking him “How would your relationship with me cause disrepute to me?” replies “Even if the great dēvas et al approach you with the sole aim of serving you \[which in itself is a rarity\], for your distinct greatness, it is a disgrace” (even if they come with pure thoughts, that is no match for your greatness).*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

For [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s compassion during sruśti (creation), periyavāccān piḷḷai quotes srīrangarāja stavam uttara satakam 41 “*acidavisēśitān praḷayasīmani samsarata: karaṇakaḷēbarair gatayitum dayamānamanā: …*” (During praḷayam (annihilated state), ātmās were in the state of acit (matter), i.e., in a subdued/inactive state; out of your compssion, to engage them in activities (which will lead them to mōkśam), you provided them body and senses by mercifully transforming subtle matter into gross matter, just out of your sankalpam (vow)).

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Second pāsuram – Previously , āḻvār said “I committed a mistake (causing disrepute to you) by thinking in my mind (about you), by speaking (about you) and by becoming physically depleted”. Here he says “I committed the mistake of saying that I caused disrepute to you. My saying that I am unqualified and leaving you is like a caṇḍāḷa (abominable person) saying that he is not qualified (he is not even qualified to say that). Because, only brahmā et al who have overflowing love for emperumān can say that they are not qualified to glorify him”. āḻvār is now cursing himself for claiming his disqualification and leaving emperumān (since he considers himself most lowly even to do that). நினைந்து நைந்து உள் கரைந்து உருகி இமையோர் பலரும் முனிவரும் புனைந்த கண்ணி நிர் சந்தம் புகையோடு ஏந்தி வணங்கினால், நினைந்த எல்லாப் பொருள்கட்கும் வித்தாய் முதலில் சிதையாமே மனம் செய் ஞானத்து உன் பெருமை மாசூணதோ மாயோனே ninanidu naindu uḷ karaindu urugi imaiyōr palarum munivarum punainda kaṇṇi nīr sāndam pugaiyōdu ēndi vaṇangināl ninainda ellāp poruḷgatkum vittāy mudalil sidaiyāmē manam sey jñānttu un perumai māsūṇādō māyōnē*

- *ninaindu*… – When brahmā et al come to worship [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), they come prepared with garland etc.
- *ninaindu* – They think “When we bring these items for worship, he will mercifully glance at us”. First they will think just as it is said in srīviṣṇu purāṇam 5.17.12 “*māmakrūra vakśyati*” (he will enquire me with care calling me ‘*you faultless akrūra*‘”).
- *naindu* – subsequently, unable to sustain themselves, they become emaciated
- *uḷ karaindu* – will become totally melted for you
- *urugi* – become completely depleted that they cannot even regain their composure
- *imaiyōr palarum munivarum …* – Who are they? dēvas starting with brahmā and the four kumāras (sanaka, sanandana, sanātana and sanat kumāra). Just as when they are engulfed in the qualities of rajas (passion) and tamas (ignorance) they think so high of themselves, when their satva (goodness) guṇam (quality) is predominant, they would melt by meditating on the auspicious qualities of [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/). In such times, they prepare garland, water for washing [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s hands, sandalwood paste to anoint [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) and fragrant incense sticks etc. With these, they come and fall at the divine feet of emperumān without an iota of pride.
- *ēndi vaṇangināl* – They feel great satisfaction when emperumān accepts those offerings with great interest. emperumān feels great satisfaction in just seeing them carrying those offerings to solely satisfy him. Just like it is explained in tiruviruttam 21 “*sūttu nanmālaigaḷ tūyana ēndi*” (Holding pure garlands which are to be worn by [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)) with respect to nityasūris, here too, same logic is applied.
- *ninainda* … – While subsequently [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says “*manam sey jñānam*” (knowledge in the form of vow) – what does this term “*ninainda*” (thinking) indicate? Here this thinking relates to [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s merciful thought to help [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)s. When everything was in subtle state as mentioned in cāndōjña upaniśat 6.2.1 “*sadēva*” (sat/[bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) only existed at that time of praḷayam), like a person who lost his children or a person who is in separation from his son who has travelled to a different country, [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) too is thinking about the loss of [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)s (being in subtle state unable to perform any action towards liberation).
- *ninainda ellāp poruḷkatkum vittāy* – ninaittal also indicates kalattal, kūdal etc., in tamiḻ which means being together – so this indicates the cit ([jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)s/souls) and [acit](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/09/thathva-thrayam-achith-what-is-matter/) (matter) which are attached to him and [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) being the cause for the same – this is the explanation given by piḷḷai amudanār. Another explanation – being the cause for such [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)s which are mercifully thought about.
- *mudalil sidaiyāmē …* – While engaging in creation, there is no impact on his true nature. When clay becomes pot, lamp etc.,  clay itself has transformed to pot, lamp etc., and the clay is no longer existing in its original form. But here, emperumān’s prakāram (attribute/form) has only changed – emperumān (the substratum) has remained without any change. This indicates that, what is seen here in this world as “material cause” (where the raw material itself becomes the object and the raw material is no longer existing) is no comparison for [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) being upādāna kāraṇam (material cause). Another question arises here. In that case, is the sankalpam (vow) the cause? Is sūkśma cidacidvisiśta brahmam (brahmam with souls and matter in subtle form) not the cause? Though [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) with sankalpam is (the efficient) cause, since it is said as in taittiriya upaniśat “*bahu syām*” (let me become many), the sankalpa visiśta brahmam (bhagavān with the knowledge in the form of vow) is the efficient cause – but the material cause is sūkśma cidacidvisiśta brahmam (bhagavān with souls and matter in subtle form). So [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is both upādāna kāraṇam (material cause) and nimitta kāraṇam (efficient cause) (In fact, he is also the sahakārikā kāraṇam – ancillary cause). [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) has this greatness of creating everything through his sankalpam (vow) in an effortless manner – for such greatness, brahmā et al can think “How can we, who are created simply by his vow, be qualified to worship him, to justify his greatness?”. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) thinks “I am not qualified even to be considering my disqualification”.
- *māyōnē* – Most amazing person. āḻvār tells [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) “You are so fascinating that even brahmā et al are seen in front of you as commoners”.

Note: To understand the mood of [āḻvārs](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/azhwars/) towards other dēvatās, the following articles would be very helpful.

- part 1 – [http://ponnadi.blogspot.in/2013/02/divya-prabhanda-pramanya-samartanam-1.html](http://ponnadi.blogspot.in/2013/02/dhivya-prabhandha-pramanya-samarthanam-1.html)
- part 2 – [http://ponnadi.blogspot.com/2013/02/divya-prabhanda-pramanya-samartanam-2.html](http://ponnadi.blogspot.com/2013/02/dhivya-prabhandha-pramanya-samarthanam-2.html)

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.
