## 1.5.3. Mayonigalay

*māyōnigaḷāy nadai kaṟṟa vānōr palarum munivarum nīyōnigaḷaip padai enṟu niṟai nānmuganaip padaittavan sēyōn ellā aṟivukkum tisaigaḷ ellām tiruvadiyāl  tāyōn ellā evvuyirkkum tāyōn tānōr uruvanē*

**Пословный перевод:**

māyōnigaḷāy – having distinguished birth; nadai – suitable actions; kaṟṟa – learned; palarum – many different; vānōr – dēvatās (celestial beings); munivarum – riśis (sages); yōnigaḷai – living beings; nī padai enṟu – saying “you create”; niṟai – having completeness (in jñānām (knowledge) etc., that is required for vyaśti sruśti (variegated creation)); nānmuganai – catur muka brahmā; padaittavan – one who created; ellā aṟivukkum – the knowledge of all jīvātmās starting with brahmā; sēyōn – having greatness which is beyond the reach of; tisaigaḷ ellām – all worlds indicated by dik (directions); tiruvadiyāl – with the tender divine feet; tāyōn – who touched; ellā evvuyirkkum – all beings of different species; tāyōn – having motherly affection; tān – him (bhagavān); ōr uruvanē – his qualities are so enjoyable!

**Перевод:**

**srīman nārāyaṇan created brahmā who is complete (as necessary to perform vyaśti sruśti) and tells him “you create the great dēvas, riśis et al who have learned their suitably great actions”. emperumān who is beyond the reach of the intelligence of such great persons, who measured all directions (which indicate all worlds) with his tender divine feet, who is having motherly affection towards all entities – such emperumān‘s qualities are so enjoyable. The essence is – Just like his supremacy, his simplicity (of touching everyone with his lotus feet etc) is also unbounded.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the 3rd pāsuram – When āḻvār declared that he was unqualified to even say that he has no qualification and moved too far away from serving bhagavān, āḻvār says that emperumān showed him the measuring (winning over) of three worlds which highlights bhagavān’s sauseelyam (mixing with everyone freely), vātsalyam (motherly forbearance) etc., and mercifully attracts āḻvār towards him.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār becomes astonished when emperumān says “Not just unlimited greatness, I also have the simplicity which lets me freely mingle with everyone without discimination” and shows him the trivikrama avatāram where he touched everyone with his lotus feet.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Third pāsuram – in the first pāsuram āḻvār said “I did a mistake by thinking, speaking and becoming depleted”; He said in the second pāsuram “I did a mistake in saying that I did a mistake”; At this time, emperumān says “Don’t see my supremacy and shy away from me. For once, see my simplicity in mixing freely with everyone” and shows his act of measuring the three worlds (and touching everyone’s head with his lotus feet). Meditating upon this, āḻvār stays stunned, neither coming close nor moving far. When asked “Can āḻvār spend his time like this without approaching him?” it is explained that as highlighted in periya tiruvantādi 86 “sīr kalanda sol ninaindu pōkkuvar ippōdu” (those devotees spend their time meditating on the pāsurams which glorify the auspicious qualities of emperumān), āḻvār could meditate on emperumān’s quality of simplicity and spend his time. மாயோனிகளாய் நடை கற்ற வானோர் பலரும் முனிவரும் நியோனிகளைப் படை என்று நிறை நான்முகனைப் படைத்தவன் சேயோன் எல்லா அறிவுக்கும் திசைகள் எல்லாம் திருவடியால் தாயோன் எல்லா எவ்வுயிர்க்கும் தாயோன் தானோர் உருவனே māyōnigaḷāy nadai kaṟṟa vānōr palarum munivarum nīyōnigaḷaip padai enṟu niṟai nānmuganaip padaittavan sēyōn ellā aṟivukkum tisaigaḷ ellām tiruvadiyāl  tāyōn ellā evvuyirkkum tāyōn tānōr uruvanē*

- *māyōnigaḷāy …* – Persons having distinct birth. When it comes to sruśti (creation) etc., which are their responsibilities, these dēvatās, riśis et al  are so intelligent that in whatever they were taught by [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), they will not have any doubt and will not go back to emperumān for clarification again. These include – sapta riśis (the seven primary sages), dasa prajāpatis (the ten progenitors), ēkādasa rudras (the eleven rudras), dvādasa ādityas (the twelve sons of aditi – the main dēvas), asta vasus (the eight dēvatās who assist indra) et al. [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) creates brahmā, imparts him the vēdas and orders him to engage in vyaśti sruśti (variegated creation). As explained in svētāsvatara upaniśat “*yō brahmāṇam vidadāti pūrvam*“, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) imparts vēdam unto brahmā initially. brahmā is so complete that, after learning once, he would never return to bhagavān for any clarification and would function perfectly.
- *sēyōn ellā aṟivukkum* – [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is beyond comprehension for even brahmā who is born directly from him and learned vēdam directly from him (what to speak of others who were created by brahmā?).
- *tisaigaḷ ellām tiruvadiyāl tāyōn* – Though he is beyond the reach of the most intelligent beings, when he desires to reveal himself, he effortlessly does it. He measured the bhūmi (earth) which has different directions with his divine feet. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is being amazed at [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s gesture since he touched the forests, water bodies etc with his lotus feet which  are so tender that even his divine consorts would touch them as if they were touching a flower.
- *ellā evvuyirkkum tāyōn* – Why did he touch everyone without discrimination based on their quality etc? That is because he has motherly affection towards all beings.
- *tān ōr uruvanē* – In the first two lines [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) enjoyed [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s ultimate supremacy and in the next two lines āḻvār enjoyed bhagavān’s ultimate simplicity – in both cases āḻvār becomes amazed. āḻvār who was walking away fast from [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) slows down a bit thinking about his simplicity.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.5.4. Tan or uruve

*tān ōr uruvē tani vittāyt tannil mūvar mudalāya vānōr palarum munivarum maṟṟum maṟṟum muṟṟumāy tān ōr peru nīr tannuḷḷē tōṟṟi adan uḷ kaṇ vaḷarum vānōr perumān māmāyan vaikundan emperumānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tān – He (who is indicated by the word “sat”); ōr uruvē – Having single form/substratum (sahakāri nirapēkśatvam – since he does not expect any assistance from any one – he is the ancillary cause); tani – singular (nimittāntara rahitan – one who does not depend on the desire of any one else – he is the efficient cause); vittu āy – being the seed (upādāna – seeking no other raw-material – since he is the material cause); tannil – (thus being the all three types of causes) his own inherent nature having sankalpam (vow); mūvar – the three (brahmā, rudra, indra); mudalāya – et al, starting with; vānōr – dēvatās (celestial beings); munivarum – riśis (sages); palarum – many forms of jīvātmās; maṟṟum – other human forms; maṟṟum – other animal forms and plant forms; muṟṟumāy – all; tān – He (who has the sankalpam/vow); tannuḷḷē – as part of his inherent nature (within himself); ōr – without second entity (since there is no other entity); peru nīr – Singular causal ocean; tōṟṟi – created; adan uḷ – (to create brahmā et al) inside that; kaṇ vaḷarum – lying down; vaikundan – resident of paramapadam; vānōr perumān – controller of nityasūris; māmāyan – (being without any expectation) with his amazing qualities and actions, having unlimited simplicity; em perumānē – my master

**Перевод:**

**bhagavān who is indicated by the word “sat” having a single form (being the instrumental cause), being the singular (being the efficient cause) seed (being the material cause), out of his sankalpam (vow) became dēvatās (starting with brahmā, rudra, indra), riśis, many forms of jīvātmās, human forms, animal/plant forms and all forms. emperumān created a singular causal ocean within himself and lay down in that ocean (to create brahmā et al). Such emperumān who is the resident of paramapadam (spiritual realm) and the controller of the nityasūris (eternally liberated souls), with amazing qualities and actions, is my master.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fourth pāsuram – āḻvār thinks “emperumān who has taken many efforts such as sruśti etc without any expectation and attracted me, will not let me go due to his sauseelyam (simplicity) even if I said ‘no’ to him” and becomes convinced.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār accepts bhagavān‘s relationship saying “bhagavān who is the controller of both spiritual and material realms and who has no expectation, attracted me through his auspicious qualities such as seelam (simplicity) etc and became my master”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Fourth pāsuram – When asked “This is bhagavān‘s nature. Now, what are you going to do?”   āḻvār says “Even if we try to leave, would the owner let go of us?” āḻvār says “emperumān who has taken many efforts such as sruśti etc., without any expectation and attracted me, will not let me go due to his sauseelyam (simplicity) even if I said ‘no’ to him” and becomes convinced. தான் ஓர் உருவே தனி வித்தாய்த் தன்னில் மூவர் முதலாய வானோர் பலரும் முனிவரும் மற்றும் மற்றும் முற்றுமாய் தான் ஓர் பெரு நீர் தன்னுள்ளே தொற்றி அதன் உள் கண் வளரும் வானோர் பெருமான் மாமாயன் வைகுந்தன் எம்பெருமானே tān ōr uruvē tani vittāyt tannil mūvar mudalāya vānōr palarum munivarum maṟṟum maṟṟum muṟṟumāy tān ōr peru nīr tannuḷḷē tōṟṟi adan uḷ kaṇ vaḷarum vānōr perumān māmāyan vaikundan emperumānē*

\[Note: For any object, generally, three types of causes are explained. upādāna kāraṇam – material cause – that which transformed to become the object; nimitta kāraṇam – efficient cause – that which caused the transformation; sahakāri kāraṇam – ancillary cause – tools which are used for the creation. For example, when a pot is made – soil is the material cause, potter(‘s desire/will) is the efficient cause; stick and wheel are the instrumental cause\].

- *tān ōr uruvē tani vittāy* – This phrase explains/matches cāndōjña upaniśat 6.2.1 “*sadēva sōmya idamagra āsīdēkamēva advitīyam*” (Oh svētakētu who is eligible to drink sōmapānam! This universe, before creation was called “sat” was existing; it was existing alone since there was no name and form, and was singular (since there was no other substratum for it)). Here, three words (sadēva, ēkamēva, advitīyam) indicate the distinct nature of brahmam and also indicate that brahmam is the three types of causes for creation. vittu (seed/cause) is to be read as  “*tān vittu*“, “*oru vittu*” and “*tani vittu*“.  “*tān*” indicates that there is no other upādānam (raw-material) \[cit (souls)/acit (matter) which are brahmam’s body in sūkśma state is the raw-material\]; “*ōr*” indicates that there is no additional tools/instruments in creation \[brahmam’s knowledge, power etc are the tools\]; “*tani*” indicates that there is no additional instigator for creation \[brahmam is the only instigator and his sankalpam/vow is the trigger for creation\]. “*uru*” indicates beauty, i.e., brahmam beautifully being the three types of causes himself.
- *tannil mūvar mudalāya* – Two explanations are given here:
   - first, [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is explained as the primary deity among brahmā, viṣṇu, rudra – Just like srī rāma was born amidst ikśvāku clan descendants and is counted along as one of them and just like kriṣṇa was born in the yādava clan and was counted amongst them, bhagavān too was born in between brahmā and rudra and was counted as one among the trimūrtis (three deities) – yet, he remains with his distinct qualities, protects everyone and also performs creation/annihilation being the antaryāmi for the other two.
   - second, “*tannil*” is explained as “(dependent) on him” – as explained in nārāyaṇa anuvākam “*sa brahmā: sasivas sēndras sōkśara: parama: svarāt*” (that [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is the antaryāmi of brahmā, rudra, indra; he is sinless, supreme and fully independent (untouched by karmās)”; so, here mūvar is explained as brahmā, rudra and indra.
- *vānōr palarum* – dēvatās starting with brahmā
- *munivarum* – riśis starting with sanaka
- *maṟṟum* – plants
- *maṟṟum* – animals
- *muṟṟum* – all those which are not stated
- *āy* – to create
- *tānōr peru nīr tannuḷḷē tōṟṟi adan uḷ kaṇ vaḷarum* – Thus having thought about creation, he first creates a huge ocean to lie down.
- *vānōr perumān* – master of nityasūris
- *māmāyan* – who has amazing qualities and activities
- *vaikundan* – being comfortably seated in srīvaikuṇṭam
- *emperumānē* – He is my Lord. When a property is slipping way, would the owner leave it? A mother who gives birth to a child after many difficult vratams (sacrifices etc.), when the boy grows up and says “I want to go overseas”, can she bear that? Similarly, when I was suffering long time in this samsāram without knowledge, he is the one who gave me true knowledge and made me realise who I am. But if I try to leave him using that knowledge (saying he is supreme and I am very lowly), can he bear it?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.5.5. Maney nokki

*mānēy nōkki madavāḷai mārvil koṇḍāy mādavā kūnē sidaiya uṇḍai vil niṟattil teṟittāy gōvindā vānōr sōdi maṇivaṇṇā madusūdā nī aruḷāy un tēnē(y) malarum tiruppādam sērumāṟu vinaiyēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

mānēy – similar to deer; nōkkin – having eyes; madavāḷai – the greatest lady who is an embodiment of humility; mārbil – in your chest; koṇḍāy – you who are keeping/having; mādava – and thus being called as mādava; kūnē – hunch-back; sidaiya – breaking; uṇḍai vil niṟattil – in the form of a bow (which is used to shoot clay-balls); teṟittāy – straightened it (effortlessly); gōvindā – one who protected the ignorant cows (with great joy); vān – the land of the wise persons; Ar – filled; sōdi – having radiance; maṇivaṇṇā – having form of carbuncle; madusūdā – the destroyer of madu (who is an enemy of devotees); nī – you; un – your; tēnē – honey; malarum – blossoming; tiruppādam – divine feet; vinaiyēn – I who have sins (which make me wait even after your accepting me); sērumāṟu – to approach/surrender; aruḷāy – bless me

**Перевод:**

**Oh emperumān! You are called as mādava since you have srī mahālakśmi, who has eyes which resemble the eyes of deer and who is the embodiment of humility and the greatest femininity,  in your chest. Oh gōvinda (who protected ignorant cows with great joy)! You straightened the hunch-back by hitting it with clay-balls shot from (playful) bow. Oh maṇivaṇṇa! – one who has beautiful form like a carbuncle – the radiance of which (gem) reaches the land of the wise persons. Oh madusūdana! – who is the destroyer of the enemies (such as madu) of your devotees! You bless me such that I, who have sins (which make me wait even after your accepting me), surrender unto your lotus feet.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fifth pāsuram – emperumān thinks “if I suddenly show my face to āḻvār (who is thus convinced), he may again try to leave; Let me wait to approach him until he prays for the same” and waits – āḻvār then prays “You ensure that I serve your lotus feet”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār prays to emperumān who performs many actions to please his devotees “based on our (eternal) relationship, bless me the union in the form of blissful experience”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*Similar to nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Fifth pāsuram – 2 introductions: āḻvār, after turning towards emperumān, prays to him to engage him in kainkaryam as explained in srī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 15.7 “kriyatāmiti mām vada” (lakśmaṇa to srī rāma – order me in what is to be done). After āḻvār turned towards him, since emperumān delays a little to appear. unable to bear that, āḻvār says “Please bless me”. மானே நோக்கி மடவாளை மார்வில் கொண்டாய். மாதவா. கூனே சிதைய உண்டை வில் நிறத்தில் தெறித்தாய் கோவிந்தா வானோர் சோதி மணிவண்ணா மதுசூதா நீ அருளாய் உன் தேனே(ய) மலரும் திருப்பாதம் சேருமாறு வினையேனே mānēy nōkki madavāḷai mārvil koṇḍāy mādavā kūnē sidaiya uṇḍai vil niṟattil teṟittāy gōvindā vānōr sōdi maṇivaṇṇā madusūdā nī aruḷāy un tēnē(y) malarum tiruppādam sērumāṟu vinaiyēnē*

- *mānēy nōkki* … – Why should I (separately) pray for his blessings when the one who triggers his mercy ([srī mahālakśmi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/)) is right next to him?
- *mānēy nōkki* – having eyes similar to those of deer
- *madavāḷai* – [srī mahālakśmi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/) who is endowed with all auspicious qualities. Two explanations:
   - madappam is explained as auspicious quality – she is so ideal that the moment she glances at [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), without any significance, emperumān will fully shower his mercy on us immediately.
   - madappam is explained as being very weak/humble – the moment he looks at her, she becomes fully withered like a flower that had its honey sucked out by bee.
- *mārbil koṇḍāy mādavā* – [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is named mādava due to his eternal relationship with [śrī mahālakśmi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/) and having her in his chest always. There are those, other than emperumān, who are also called as śrīmān, without any connection to śrī mahālakśmi, just like an insect that is named “māmbaḻa uṇṇi” has no relationship with “māmbaḻam” (mango).  But unlike them,  [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s eternal relationship with tāyār is well-established. Another explanation – Oh the one who is called mādava, since srī mahālakśmi is eternally residing in your chest as explained in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 1.9.104 “*viṣṇu vakśasstalastayā*” (srī mahālakśmi who resides in the chest of srī mahāviṣṇu who never fails his devotees).
- *kūnē sidaiya* – two explanations one with respect to srī rāma and another with respect to kriṣṇa.
   - Explaining srī rāma’s childhood play, where he would hit mantarā’s hunched-back without hurting any other part. It was this act of srī rāma which infuriated mantarā and led her to cause srī rāma to go to vanavāsam (forest dwelling) and to ultimately destroy rāvaṇa. In this context, gōvinda means “one who protects the earth” – he protected the earth by killing rāvaṇa and other demoniac persons. It can also be said that “pōm pahḻiyellām amaṇan talaiyōdē” (whoever commits mistake, only one person is accused) – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) doing mischief in whichever avatāram (in this case, srī rāmāvatāram), only kriṣṇa (gōvinda) is accused for that. A funny story is narrated in arumpadam to explain this statement of nampiḷḷai. Once a robber tries to drill a hole in a brāhmaṇa’s house to steal materials and in the process the wall collapses and the robber gets killed. The robber’s relatives come to the brāhmaṇa and ask for compensation. The brāmaṇa refuses to pay any compensation and they complain to the king. The king says the brāhmaṇa needs to compensate since it was his fault in not building the wall properly. brāhmaṇ thinks for a moment and says “It was the builder’s fault for having too much water in the mix that led to the wall collapsing”. The king brings the builder and charges him. The builder knowing the situation, says “It was the potter who gave bigger pot than usual which caused more water to be added in the mix and thus it was his fault”. The potter is brought to the king’s court and he says “It was because I was attracted to a prostitute who was roaming here and there and I lost focus in making the pot”. The prostitute is brought to the king’s court and she says “The vaśerman delayed returning my saree, which is why I was roaming here and there, waiting for it”. The vaśerman is brought to the king’s court and he says “The place where I usually dry the saree was taken by a monk and thus it got delayed to dry the saree”. Finally the monk was brought to the court and he was charged. Since the monk had taken a vow of silence, he never refuted the charge verbally. The foolish king ordered the killing of the monk as punishment for him. Similarly, whoever commits mischief, kaṇṇan [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) gets blamed for those mischief.
   - Explaining this as kriṣṇa’s leelā – when kubjā (hunched-back lady) gave him pure sandalwood, kriṣṇa became mighty pleased and straightened her back effortlessly. Here his having “*vil*” (bow) is questioned – but other pāsurams are quoted where kriṣṇa having bow is highlighted such as periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 2.6.1 “*vēlikkōl vetti viḷaiyādu* ***vil****lēṟṟi*“, nācciyār tirumoḻi 14.6 “*tarumam aṟiyāk kuṟumbanait than kaic****cārngam*** *aduvē pōl*“.
- *vānār sōdi maṇivaṇṇā* – having the forms which please your devotees! Like a precious gem in a beautiful glass box – even in paramapadam the radiance arising out of his divine form is uncontrollable.
- *madusūdā* – For those who desire to enjoy your divine form, you are the remover of their hurdles. Just like how you eliminated madu, you eliminated my hurdles too.
- *un tēnē(y) malarum tiruppādam* – Even if we don’t see your divine form, pastimes and qualities – your divine feet, which are so enjoyable, are enough to not give up on you. yajur vēdam – viṣṇu sūktam says “*viṣṇō: padē paramē madva utsa:*” (honey is overflowing from your great lotus feet). āḻvār desired in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.3.10](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/07/thiruvaimozhi-1-3-10-thuyakkaru-mathiyil/) for “*peru nilam kadanda nalladippōdu*” (the divine lotus feet which measured the great world). So, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) showed him “*tisaigaḷ ellām tiruvadiyāl tāyōn*” ([tiruvāimoḻi 1.5.3](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/08/thiruvaimozhi-1-5-3-mayonigalay/) – he measured all the directions with his lotus feet) and [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) also requests for the same here.
- *sērumāṟu vinaiyēnē* – Please bless me to be at your lotus feet – I am so sinful like someone who is served food but disallowed to eat the same. Here, āḻvār says “*vinaiyēn*” to indicate his sinful nature which stops him from enjoying emperumān even after approaching him.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.5.6. Vinaiyen vinai

*vinaiyēn vinai tīr marundu ānāy viṇṇōr talaivā kēsavā manai sēr āyar kula mudalē māmāyanē mādavā sinaiyēy tazaiya marāmarangaḷ ēḻum eydā sirīdarā inaiyāy inaiya peyarināy enṟu naivan adiyēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vinaiyēn – most qualified to be called as “most sinful”; vinai – for the sins (which make me shy away from emperumān though having great love towards him, seeing my lowly nature); tīr – that will rid; marundu ānāy – being the medicine (that is in the form of simplicity/auspicious qualities); viṇṇōr – sūris – the residents of paramapadam (where there are no such obstacles to enjoy you); talaivā – Oh controller/leader!; kēsavā – Oh one who is having the name kēsava (which means – not only is he the leader of the residents of parampadam, he is also the leader of brahmā, rudra et al who seek him for worldly benefits – for he is the one who sustains them); manai sēr – land which is attached to; āyar – covherd; kula – for the clan; mudalē – Oh the primary one!; māmāyanē – having amazing activities (stealing butter etc); mādavā – Having the name mādava! (as said in popular pramāṇam “ēśa nārāyaṇa śrīmān” (nārāyaṇan who is the husband of srī mahālakśmi) which is the cause for the amazing activities); sinai – with branches; ēy – joined; taḻaiya – having well-sprouted leaves as well; marāmarangaḷ ēḻum – 7 peepal trees; eydāy – Oh one who shot; siridarā – Oh one who is having the name śrīdara (after attaining vīraśrī-bravery due to shooting down those trees); inaiyāy – Oh one having such qualities!; inaiya peyarināy enṟu – Oh one who is having such auspicious names!; adiyēn – I who have (unconditional/eternal) relationship (with you); naivan – becoming emaciated

**Перевод:**

**I have become emaciated after having said “Oh the one who is the medicine for my sins which stop you from accepting my kainkaryam! Oh the controller of the residents of parampadam (spiritual realm)! Oh the lord of brahmā, rudra et al ! Oh the primary one of the covherd clan! Oh the one who has amazing activities due to the eternal relationship with śrī mahālakśmi! Oh the one who shot down the well-grown seven peepal trees (and achieved valour due to that)! Oh the one having such qualities! Oh the one who is having such auspicious names!”**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In sixth pāsuram – Since emperumān did not fulfil his desire immediately,  āḻvār meditates on emperumān‘s enjoyable nature and his divine names in order to get his desire fulfilled and  becomes heart-broken.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Similar to nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*Similar to nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Sixth pāsuram – āḻvār turns towards emperumān, but emperumān delays a little bit (in accepting āḻvār’s kainkaryam). āḻvār says to emperumān “you have lost me”. வினையேன் வினை தீர் மருந்து அனைய விண்ணோர் தலைவா கேசவ மனை சேர் ஆயர் குல முதலே மாமாயனே மாதவா சினையேய் தழைய மராமரங்கள் ஏழும் எய்தாய். சிரீதரா. இணையாய் இணைய பெயரினாய் என்று நைவன் அடியேன் vinaiyēn vinai tīr marundu ānāy viṇṇōr talaivā kēsavā manai sēr āyar kula mudalē māmāyanē mādavā sinaiyēy tazaiya marāmarangaḷ ēḻum eydā sirīdarā inaiyāy inaiya peyarināy enṟu naivan adiyēnē*

- *vinaiyēn …* – Don’t you see your stature (of being great/magnanimous) and my stature (of being meek/sinful) \[if you do, you will surely help me\].
- *vinaiyēn vinai* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s sins are unlike other [cētanas](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)‘ sins. Other cētanas like to have union with [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/), but āḻvār wants separation now.
- *tīr marundānāy* – You are the medicine that will remedy my thought of “my approaching [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) will cause disrepute to him”.

From where did the quality of being the medicine come?

- *viṇṇōr talaivā* – Because, though he is the leader of nityasūris and eternally enjoying in paramapadam and he is facilitating himself such that, those who think and shy away from seeing his greatness, would also be attracted towards him.
- kēsavā – descending to vyūha state from parampadam and being the master of brahmā, rudra et al as highlighted in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 5.3.14 “*ka iti brahmaṇō nāma īsōham sarvadēhinām \| āvām tavāngē sambhūtau tasmāt kēsavanāmavān \|\|*” (ka indicates brahmā; I am (rudra) the lord of all entities (in the material world); both of us appeared from your body as a part; thus you have the name kēsava which means that ka and īsa were born from you – as said by siva towards [srīman nārāyaṇan](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)).
- *manisēr āyar kula mudalē* – descending from vyūha state to vibhavan (avatāram – here kriṣṇāvatāram) and coming close to us. manai generally means land/house. Three explanations given:
   - Since it is explained to have five lakh families in nandagōpāla’s town, the houses are laid touching each other. Being the leader of such clan.
   - Arriving at the houses of the covherds and being the leader of their clan.
   - Bringing along some bamboo sticks always and joining them to make a hut wherever they go. Being the leader of such clan.
- *māmāyanē* – one who performs amazing activities – being born in the covherd clan, having that which is prepared by them (butter) to sustain himself, even that – consuming the stolen butter, still being dissatisfied – gets caught with the butter red-handed and gets punished for the same.

What is the cause for this simplicity of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)?

- mādavā – Oh the who is eternally together with śrī mahālkśmi (the cause for [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s simplicity)!
- *sinai ēy* … – the act that was performed by srī rāma to bring confidence of his valour in the mind of sugrīva mahārāja; The seven peepal trees where filled with branches having abundance of leaves which make it difficult to take an aim and shoot them down in one shot. From this it can be understood that when a devotee doubts [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s abilities, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) will go to the extent of clearing the doubts of the devotee and protecting the devotee.
- *sirīdarā* – Hailing the vīra lakshmi (the wealth of valour) that was visible even as srī rāma was taking aim at the trees.
- *inaiyāy* – \[inaiyāy means describing someone based on one’s qualities\] Oh the one who is having such qualities and activities!
- *inaiya peyarināy* – Oh the one who is having suitable names for such qualities and activities!
- *enṟu naivan* – I am becoming emaciated thinking as mentioned here.
- *adiyēnē* – Whose wealth is getting lost? [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying that he is [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s wealth and bhagavān should ensure that he does not lose it.
   - Am I looking/suffering as an independent entity? \[No – I am fully dependent on you\]
   - Am I becoming weak due to dependence on some one else? \[No – I am fully dependent on you\]
   - Am I suffering since you are unable to protect me? \[No – You have all the ability to protect me\]
   - Am I suffering since I can protect myself? \[No – I have no ability to protect myself. You have to protect me\]

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.5.7. Adiyen siriya

*adiyēn siṟiya jñānattan aṟidal ārkkum ariyānai kadisēr taṇṇanduḻāyk kaṇṇi punaindān tannaik kaṇṇanai sediyār ākkai adiyāraic cērdal tīrkkum tirumālai adiyēn kāṇbān alaṟṟuvan idanin mikkōr ayarvu uṇḍē*

**Пословный перевод:**

siṟiya jñānattan – having a little knowledge; adiyēn – me; ārkkum aṟidal ariyānai – emperumān who is difficult to know even for the wisest; kadi – fragrance; sēr – abundant; taṇ – cool; am tuḻāyk kaṇṇi punaindān tannai – the one who is having the attribute of wearing beautiful tuḷasi garland; kaṇṇanai – Being born as kriṣṇa (who is shining with greatness, being most enjoyable); sediyār – filled with sins (in this samsāram which is like a dense forest); ākkai – relationship with the body; adiyārai – for his inseparable devotees; sērdal tīrkkum – stopping them from engulfing and protecting; tirumālai – srīya:pati (divine consort of śrī mahālakśmi); adiyēn – being his servitor; kāṇbān – to see him; alaṟṟuvan – long for it (so it will cause disrepute for him); idanil – than this; mikku – greater; ōr ayarvu – foolishness; uṇḍē – is it there?

**Перевод:**

**emperumān is the one who appeared as kriṣṇa, who is difficult to know for even the wisest, who is wearing cool/beautiful tuḷasi garland which has abundant fragrance, who removes the abundant sins of his devotees and protects them. I, who have very little knowledge, long to see such emperumān and call out for him – what is greater foolishness than this?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In seventh pāsuram – āḻvār, thus desiring to see emperumān, when emperumān showed interest in being together, again thinks about emperumān’s great stature and his own lowly stature and leaves emperumān again.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*āḻvār having reminded about previous consideration of himself being lowly, thinks “I am so ignorant, how can I long to see emperumān who is so simple, so enjoyable and great? What foolishness on my part?” and again tries to shy away.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Seventh pāsuram – āḻvār said “naivan“; not letting him to suffer, emperumān appeared to him; seeing him, āḻvār says “I need not add any more glories to him” and leaves him. அடியேன் சிறிய ஞானத்தன் அறிதல் யார்க்கும் அரியானை கடிசேர் தண்ணந்துழாய்க் கண்ணி புனைந்தான் தன்னைக் கண்ணனை செடியார் ஆக்கை அடியாரைச் சேர்தல் தீர்க்கும் திருமாலை அடியேன் காண்பான் அலற்றுவன் இதனில் மிக்கோர் அயர்வு உண்டே? adiyēn siṟiya jñānattan aṟidal ārkkum ariyānai kadisēr taṇṇanduḻāyk kaṇṇi punaindān tannaik kaṇṇanai sediyār ākkai adiyāraic cērdal tīrkkum tirumālai adiyēn kāṇbān alaṟṟuvan idanin mikkōr ayarvu uṇḍē*

- *adiyēn siṟiya jñānattan* –  āmongst samsāris (materialistic persons), there are some ignorant persons. I am so ignorant that, in comparison with me, they would look like all-knowing.
- *adiyēn* – Two explanations given*:*
   - Even while shying away from [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), he calls himself “*adiyēn*” (servitor)
   - [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is not saying *adiyēn* desiring to perform service, but based on the realisation that ātmā’s true nature is to be a servant as much as to be knover and enjoyer.
- *siṟiya jñānattan* – having very little knowledge.
- *aṟidalārkkum ariyānai* – Even for the wisest person, he is difficult to comprehend; even for himself \]emperumān\] who is “*svatassarvajña”* (naturally fully knovledegable), his glories are not comprehensible as explained in tiruvāimoḻi 8.4.6 “*tanakkum than tanmai aṟivariyān*” (he himself does not know his full glories \[this is not a limitation since his glories have no upper limit\]). Combination of myself (*adiyēn siṟiya jñānattan*) and [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) (*aṟidalārkkum ariyān*) is like tamas (darkness) and prakāsam (brightness) mingling.
- *kadi sēr taṇṇanduḻāyk kaṇṇi punaindān tannai* – rich in fragrance – this tuḷasi garland is a key identity for [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) (who is difficult to be comprehended). “*sēr*” is explained in present tense that “day after day the fragrance increases” and one who wears such garland.
- *kaṇṇanai* – though being incomprehensible, he made himself easily approachable by covherd boys and girls.
- *sediyār ākkai adiyārai sērdal tīrkkum tirumālai* – Body which is filled with sins. It is explained in periya tirumoḻi 9.7.7 “*nōyalām peydatōr ākkai*” (body which is affected with all types of diseases). As explained in bhagavat gītā 7.14 “*jarāmaraṇa mōkśāya māmāsritya yatanti yē…*” (Those who surrender unto me and try to be free from birth, death etc., realise everything about the ātmā) – kēvala (one who desire for kaivalya mōkśam of enjoying oneself eternally) is also protected/delivered by śrīmān (the divine consort of [srī mahālakhsmi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/)).  Are they adiyārs (devotees)? In [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s opinion, they are the true adiyārs. How is that? śēśa bhūta (servitor) means one who brings glories to śēśi (master). Unlike me who approaches [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) and brings disrepute to him, they get relieved from samsāram (by his grace) and stay away from him (without causing disrepute to him) – so they are true adiyārs.

So, what happened to you now?

- *adiyēn kāṇbān alaṟṟuvan* – I am crying out “*adiyēn*” (I am a servitor), “*kāṇbān*” (want to see him).
- *idanin mikkōr ayarvuṇḍē* – When I was a samsāri (materialistic – in previous births), being ignorant was blissful. How was that good? At least, back then, I stayed away from [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) without causing disrepute to him. Now, I am trying to approach him and causing disrepute to him. What is more foolish than this?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.5.8. Unday ulagu

*uṇḍāy ulagu ēḻ munnamē umiḻndu māyaiyāl pukku uṇḍāy veṇṇey siṟu manisar uvalai ākkai nilai eydi maṇ tān sōrndu atu uṇḍēlum manisarkku āgum bīr siṟidum aṇḍā vaṇṇam maṇ karaiya ney ūṇ marundō māyōnē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

māyōnē – Oh amazing person (who does not get impacted negatively even while mixing with everyone in all aspects); munnamē – once upon a time; ulagēḻ – the seven worlds (which is a sample of all creation); uṇḍāy – you consumed; umiḻndu – (without any residue) spat them out; siṟu manisar – insignificant humans; uvalai – to be avoided/abandoned; ākkai – body; nilai – position/situation; eydi – descended/took; māyaiyāl – in cunning ways; pukku – entered; veṇṇey – butter; uṇḍāy – ate; maṇḍhān – some residue from the earth that was consumed before; sōrndu adu uṇḍēlum – remaining that is present; manisarkku – for the humans; āgum – that occur; bīr – indigestion; siṟidum – even a little; aṇḍā vaṇṇam – kept away; maṇ – that soil; karaiya – to dissolve; ney ūṇ – (in a different incarnation) eating ghee; marundō – is that a medicine? no

**Перевод:**

**Oh amazing person (who does not get impacted negatively even while mixing with everyone in all aspects)! Once upon a time, you consumed all the worlds and spat them out. Subsequently, you descended as an insignificant human being bound in a body (that is generally considered to be avoided). You ate butter to keep away the indigestion that occurs to humans. Is eating ghee a medicine to dissolve the residual soil? (No).**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*āḻvār curses himself and moves away from emperumān. Seeing that, emperumān shows his true nature as the one having the quality of sustaining himself by being together with his devotees and consoles āḻvār.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the eighth pāsuram – Seeing āḻvār leave, to bring āḻvār towards him, emperumān shows his inability to sustain himself in separation from his devotees – āḻvār becomes amazed at that.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently – āḻvār thus tries to move away losing hope. Seeing that, emperumān shows his great attachment towards his devotees saying “I will not fail those who are bound to me; I cannot sustain myself without them; there is no disrepute for me in being with you and you can see that yourself in my history” and āḻvār becomes consoled after seeing that.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Eighth pāsuram – When āḻvār tries to leave like this, emperumān thinks “He is quite brave; he should be made to understand” and asks āḻvār “Oh āḻvīr! Have you not heard about the incidents in tiruvāyppādi (gōkulam)?”  āḻvār replies “I am unaware of that” desiing to hear about it from emperumān. emperumān says “Once upon a time, I rescued the earth and protected it by keeping in my stomach; Subsequently, I released it; I then thought that there may be residue in my stomach – so to have them digested properly, I consumed some butter in gōkulam”. āḻvār questions “Both events happened at different times. What is the relationship?” emperumān then asks “So, you tell me – why did I do that?” āḻvār replies “Because you sustain yourself with the things which are touched by your devotees \[butter churned by the covherd girls\], you consumed the butter”. emperumān says “Just like that butter, you too are very dear to me. In that case, if you don’t present yourself to me, you will reach the same hell as those who hid the butter away from me”. In this pāsuram, āḻvār repeats emperumān’s words thinking that he has understood emperumān’s desire. உண்டாய் உலகு ஏழ் முன்னமே உமிழ்ந்து மாயையால் புக்கு உண்டாய் வெண்ணெய் சிறு மனிசர் உவலை ஆக்கை நிலை எய்தி மண் தான் சோர்ந்து அது உண்டெழும் மனிசர்க்கு ஆகும் பீர் சிறிதும் ஆண்ட வண்ணம் மண் கரைய நெய் ஊன் மருந்தோ மாயோனே! uṇḍāy ulagu ēḻ munnamē umiḻndu māyaiyāl pukku uṇḍāy veṇṇey siṟu manisar uvalai ākkai nilai eydi maṇ tān sōrndu atu uṇḍēlum manisarkku āgum bīr siṟidum aṇḍā vaṇṇam maṇ karaiya ney ūṇ marundō māyōnē!*

- *māyaiyāl pukku uṇḍāy veṇṇey –* As explained in *vēda nigaṇḍu* (vēda dictionary), “*māyā vayunam jñānam*” (māyā is synonymous with wisdom, knowledge) – consumed butter (which is a form of knowledge) with desire.

It would not suit well if we say [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) was born as srī rāma, stole butter and consumed the same. So,

- *siṟu manisar uvalai ākkai nilai eydi* – He took up the body (that is to be avoided) of lowly humans. He presented his own aprākruta (divine) form as a lowly human form. As explained in tiruvāimoḻi “*kaṟaiynār tuvar udukkai*” (wearing dirty clothes), he was born amongst covherd boys and enjoyed butter. While it is said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 5.3.14 “*sapalam dēvi sanjātam jātōham yat tavōdarāt*” (the result of your prayers in previous births, led to the result of me entering your womb – kriṣṇa to dēvaki), it is also said in mahābhāratam “*naiśa garbbatvamāpēdē na yōnyāmavasat prabhu:*” (This kriṣṇa does not have the quality of staying in someone’s womb and never stayed in anyone’s womb). How is this possible that without being in the womb of the mother, he is born? It is purely by his śakti (power).  A king descending in the ikśvāku vamsam was once performing a yāgam. He became thirsty and consumed the water that was sanctified with mantras and that led to him becoming pregnant. Though only the union of man and woman generally leads to pregnancy – in this case it was the special power of the mantram which got him pregnant. If this can be said for a normal king who drinks sanctified water, why should it not be possible for [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) to appear in the form which he likes?

Consuming the soil is for the sustenance of the worlds. Consuming the butter was to sustain yourself (by being in contact with your devotees).

- *maṇḍhān …* – Here consuming ghee is explained in two ways.
   - *bīr* is explained as *vaivarṇyam* (becoming pale) – If there is any residual soil remaining in the stomach, for common men, it leads to becoming pale (due to indigestion etc). So, to avoid that, he is eating butter to dissolve the soil.
   - *bīr* is explained as “a little” here – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is consuming butter without leaving behind even a little portion for others.
- *marundō?* – Is that a medicine? No. You are not consuming it as medicine, but you are consuming it since it was touched by covherd girls who are very dear to you – and you are so mad for your devotees that you cannot sustain yourself without things which are touched by them.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.5.9. Mayom tiya

*māyōm tīya alavalai perumā vanjap pēy vīyat tūya kuḻaviyāy vidappāl amudā amudu seyditta māyan vānōr tanit talaivan malarāḷ maindan evvuyirkkum tāyōn tammān ennammān ammā mūrttiyaic cārndē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tīya – having ill-intentions; alavalai – one who is a constant chatter; peru – beyond measurement; mā – big; vanjam – deceitful; pēy – devil; vīya – to finish her; tūya – unblemiśed; kuḻviyāy – being a child; vidappāl – poisonous milk; amudā – accepting it as nectar; amudu seyditta – ate; māyan – one with amazing nature; vānōr – for the nityasūris; tanit talaivan – singular controller; malarāḷ – to śrī mahālakśmi who resides in the lotus flower; maindan – one who has most enjoyable youth; evvuyirkkum – for all jīvātmās; tāyōn – having motherly affection; tammān – being the controller of himself; en ammān – my master who is not letting me leave him; ammā mūrttiyai – one who has that distinct and beautiful form; sārntu – approached; māyōm – cannot finish both emperumān and myself. If not separated, both perumāḷ and āḻvār can sustain themselves

**Перевод:**

**emperumān has an amazing nature where he being a pure hearted child, accepted  the poisonous milk of the devil pūtanā (who was having ill-intentions, who was constantly chattering, who was having immeasurable deceitfulness) as nectar to kill her. He is the singular controller of nityasūris (eternally liberated), who has the enjoyable youth for śrī mahālakśmi’s pleasure, who has motherly affection towards all beings and who is my master (for not failing me). I approached such emperumān who has distinct and great form, so both he and I can sustain ourselves.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the ninth pāsuram – nammāḻvār says “The butter given by yasōda et al (gōpikās) are nectarean for you. But my association with you will be poisonous for you. So, my leaving you is appropriate”. emperumān replies “The poison of pūtanā is unfavourable for me, but your faults are not”.  Hearing this āḻvār says “in that case, I won’t leave” and becomes satisfied.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says he will be uplifted by approaching bhagavān who is the lord and master of all jīvātmās and who has motherly affection towards them all.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Ninth pāsuram – emperumān says to āḻvār “Your body which you consider as lowly is that which would sustain me like the butter given by yasōdā et al in tiruvāyppādi (gōkulam)”;  āḻvār replies “The butter given by those who have great attachment towards you would sustain you. But association with me who doesn’t have such attachment is poisonous for you”. emperumān says “Oh! is it poison? Nothing wrong even if it is poison”. āḻvār too says “Yes – it is poison and nothing less than poison”. emperumān then says “In that case, I accepted pūtanā’s poison – so there is nothing that will be rejected by me”. Hearing this āḻvār becomes satisfied. It is also explained as “Just like kriṣṇa killed pūtanā, emperumān terminated my thought of leaving from him”. மாயோம் தீய அலவலை பெருமா வஞ்சப் பேய் வீயத் தூய குழவியை விடப்பால் அமுதா அமுது செய்திட்ட மாயன் வானோர் தனித் தலைவன் மலராள் மைந்தன் எவ்வுயிர்க்கும் தாயோன் தம்மான் என்னம்மான் அம்மா மூர்த்தியைச் சார்ந்தே māyōm tīya alavalai perumā vanjap pēy vīyat tūya kuḻaviyāy vidappāl amudā amudu seyditta māyan vānōr tanit talaivan malarāḷ maindan evvuyirkkum tāyōn tammān ennammān ammā mūrttiyaic cārndē*

- *māyōm* – Since [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s state is “separation means death”, āḻvār says we will not leave and die. Here “we” (plural) indicates āḻvār and his friends/relatives/dependents. It can also refer to āḻvār and [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) both of whom cannot bear the separation.
- *tīya alavalaip perumā vanjap pēy vīya* – As explained in hari vamsam 53 “*stanyam tadviśasammisram rasyamāsījjagadgurō:*” (For the one who killed pūtanā to save the universe and thus was called universal preceptor (kriṣṇa), the poisonous breast milk became nectar) – pūtanā who came to kill kriṣṇa, the root cause of everything (if kriṣṇa is killed the whole universe will cease to exist), who was saying sweet words like yasōdā – she disguised as yasōdā with ill-intentions and even made [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) who is svatassarvajña (naturally fully knovledegable) himself wonder if she was yasōdā herself.
- *tūya kuḻaviyāy* – Even though he has all the wealth and opulence, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) behaved like an innocent child.

But if he is an innocent child, why was not he killed by the poison?

- *vidappālamudā* – The poison became nectarean to him – but his birth itself causes destruction to the asuras.
- *māyan* – He is so amazing that he converts poison to nectar, protects himself, thus protecting all of us (if he died, we also would have died). Since pūtaṇa was offering the poisonous milk purely for kriṣṇa (not for herself and not for others), it became nectar – since anything that was offered exclusively to [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/), he will accept that happily.

Who was the one who changed pūtanā’s poison to nectar?

- *vānōr tanit talaivan* – The exclusive leader of ayarvaṟum amarargaḷ (nityasūris)
- *malarāḷ maindan* – the divine couple who is served by nityasūris as explained in tiruvāimoḻi 8.1.4 “d*hēvimārāvār tirumagaḷ bhūmi Eva maṟṟamarar ātceyvār*” (nityasūris serve [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) with his divine consorts as ordered by them). maindan indicates one who is suitable for śrī mahālakśmi. Due to his connection with her, he is eternally youthful.
- *evvuyirkkum tāyōn* – One who has motherly affection towards all [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)s.
- *tammān* – [sarvēsvaran](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)
- *ennammān* – One who ensured that I did not leave him and give up my life. Keeping me in a higher position than nityasūris and all other [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)s and giving me special blessings.
- *am mā mūrttiyaic cārndē* – surrendering unto such great personality who has a distinctly beautiful form and thus be protected.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.5.10. Sarnda iru

*sārnda iru val vinaigaḷum sarittu māyap paṟṟu aṟuttut tīrndu tanpāl manam vaikkat tirutti vīdu tiruttuvān ārnda jñānac cudarāgi agalam kīḻ mēl aḷavu iṟandu nērnda uruvāy aruvāgum ivaṟṟin uyirām nedumālē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ārnda – complete; jñānac cudarāgi – (one who is) having naturally shining knowledge; agalam – around; kīḻ – below; mēl – above (all ten directions); aḷavu iṟandu – being naturally unlimited; nērnda – very subtle; uruvāy aruvāgum – cit and acit; ivaṟṟin – for these; uyirām – being the antarātmā (in-dwelling super soul); nedumāl – one who has boundless vātsalyam (motherly affection) towards me; sārnda – being together (with me); iru – two types (virtues and vices); val – strong – irremovable; vinaigaḷum – karmas; sarittu – pushed over (completely without any remainder); māyam – done out of ignorance; paṟṟu – attachment with material pleasures; aṟuttu – cut off; tīrndu – having full faith (existing for his pleasure only); tanpāl – towards him; manam – mind/heart; vaikka – to be situated; tirutti – reformed (me); vīdu – in the mōkśastalam (paramapadam – the residence of freed persons); tiruttuvān – will freshen it up

**Перевод:**

**emperumān is complete with naturally shining knowledge, having permeated in all directions, being the in-dwelling super-soul for all cit and acit which are very subtle and has great attachment towards me. Such emperumān removes my two types of karma (puṇyam and pāpam), cuts off the attachment towards worldly pleasures, reforms me to be totally existing for his pleasure and freshens up the parampadam (to welcome me).**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the tenth pāsuram – āḻvār speaks about emperumān’s great attachment towards himself (āḻvār) in triggering the desire to serve him and emperumān being ready to carry āḻvār to tirunādu (paramapadam – spiritual realm).*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently – seeing āḻvār being convinced, emperumān becomes pleased. Seeing that, āḻvār shows great gratitude towards emperumān for his favours and becomes delighted.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*Tenth pāsuram – āḻvār says – When he said “māyōm” (we won’t die) emperumān becomes pleased and starts decorating paramapadam (where everyone will be interested to do kainkaryam and no one would call himself disqualified to do kainkaryam) to welcome āḻvār there.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Tenth pāsuram – Having convinced āḻvār, emperumān started decorating parampadam which already does not need any more beautification. சார்ந்த இரு வல் வினைகளும் சரித்து மாயப் பற்று அறுத்துத் தீர்ந்து தன்பால் மனம் வைக்கத் திருத்தி வீடு திருத்துவான், ஆர்ந்த ஞானச் சுடராகி அகலம் கீழ் மேல் அளவு இறந்து, நேர்ந்த உருவாய் அருவாகும்  இவற்றின் உயிரம் நெடுமாலே. sārnda iru val vinaigaḷum sarittu māyap paṟṟu aṟuttut tīrndu tanpāl manam vaikkat tirutti vīdu tiruttuvān ārnda jñānac cudarāgi agalam kīḻ mēl aḷavu iṟandu nērnda uruvāy aruvāgum ivaṟṟin uyirām nedumālē*

- *sārnda iru valvinaigaḷum sarittu* – As explained in srīranga gadyam “*tilatailavaddāruvahnivat…*” (Like oil inside sesame seeds, fire inside wood), karmas are so attached to [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) – these karmas have grown like dense branches which are most difficult to remove even for [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is sarvaśaktimayan (omnipotent). [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) removes them like a very knovledegable builder who easily pulls down a huge wall – nampiḷḷai uses a beautiful sentence “*viragar nedunjuvar taḷḷumāpōlē pōkki*“.
- *māyap paṟṟu aṟuttu* – Cutting off māyam – ruci (taste) and paṟṟu – vāsanā (impressions).
- *tīrntu* – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is said to be krutakrutyan – one who has performed the necessary duties. It is also explained as [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) saying he has become fully available at the disposal of emperumān from previously saying “I will leave you”.
- *vīdu tiruttuvān* – spiritual realm is explained in mūnṟām tiruvandādi 51 as “*kalangāp perunagaram*” (huge town which never gets disturbed for anything) – even that becomes excited to welcome [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/).
- *ārnda jñānac cudarāgi* – being complete with shining knowledge
- *agalam kīḻ mēl aḷaviṟandu* – spread in all 10 directions.
- *nērnda uruvāy aruvāgum ivaṟṟinuyirām* – nērndu is explained as “subtle” and “nearby”.
   - Being the soul of the most subtle [cit](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) and [acit](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/09/thathva-thrayam-achith-what-is-matter/).
   - Being the soul of those which can be easily perceived – prakruti ([acit](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/09/thathva-thrayam-achith-what-is-matter/)) and [cit](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/).
- *nedumāl* – Such [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) (who is nedu \[great\] māl) engages in decorating the paramapadam. Two explanations for nedumāl – His greatness acquired more beauty after accepting [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/). He became great (and spread everywhere) to acquire āḻvār like a king who surrounds the town with his army to catch a single thief.
- *nedumālē* – Starting from here until “*muniyē nānmuganē*” (tiruvāimoḻi’s last decad), [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is speaking about the great favours done by [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) to him. He is calling out for emperumān constantly until the last decad when emperumān finally takes him to paramapadam.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.5.11. Male maya

*mālē! māyap perumānē! mā māyanē! enṟu enṟu mālē ēṟi māl aruḷāl mannu kurukūrc catakōpan pālēy tamiḻar isaikārar pattar paravum āyirattin pālē patta ivai pattum vallārkku illai parivadē*

**Пословный перевод:**

mālē – Oh the one who has natural greatness due to being superior to everyone!; māyap perumānē! – Oh the one who has unlimited amazing qualities (which are capable of placing an eternally materialistic person amidst the eternally liberated souls)!; mā māyanē! – Oh the one who has unlimited wealth, forms and activities!; enṟu enṟu – thus meditating (the greatness of being the master, being the means and being the goal); mālē ēṟi – being bewildered (that we will leave meditating upon one’s own lowly nature); māl – of the sarvēsvaran who has unsurpassed motherly affection; aruḷāl – out of infinite mercy; mannu – approaching after being convinced; kurukūrc catakōpan – nammāḻvār‘s; pālēy – sweet like milk; tamiḻar – ones who are learned in tamiḻ prose; isaikārar – ones who are learned in music and can sing; pattar – ones who are devotees who understand and relish the meanings; paravum – celebrating; āyirattin pālē – in these 1000 pāsurams of tiruvāimoḻi; patta – in (like “kadalilē muttup pattadu” \[pearls are in the ocean\]); ivai pattum – this decad which explains emperumān‘s auspicious qualities; vallārkku – those can recite it with the appropriate mood; parivatu – sorrow (out of separation due to considering oneself as lowly and shying away from perumāḷ); illai – not there

**Перевод:**

**āḻvār, being bewildered (out of his own humility), calls out to emperumān – Oh the one who has natural greatness due to being superior to everyone! Oh the one who has unlimited amazing qualities! Oh the one who has unlimited wealth, forms and activities! – and meditates upon his auspicious qualities. After being bewildered and desiring to leave emperumān, he was convinced by the infinite mercy of emperumān (to be together) in this decad which is part of āḻvār‘s tiruvāimoḻi (1000 pāsurams) which are celebrated by those who are well-versed in tamiḻ, those who are well-versed in music and can sing this and those devotees who understand the meaning. For such persons who can recite this decad with the proper attitude/mood, they do not need to go through the sufferings in separation like āḻvār had to go through.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the end – āḻvār identifies the result for the ones who learned this decad.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār mercifully says that the result of this decad is that for those who are engaged in this padigam, there is no sorrow in contemplating their own lowly nature.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*In the end – āḻvār says that for those who learned this decad, there is no sorrow of saying “I am unqualified” and leaving emperumān.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*In the end – āḻvār says that for those who can recite and meditate on this decad, they need not go through the suffering of not having emperumān, considering oneself unqualified and leaving him like āḻvār had to go through. மாலே! மாயப் பெருமானே! மா மாயனே. என்று என்று மாலே ஏறி மால் அருளால் மன்னு குருகூர்ச் சடகோபன் பாலேய் தமிழர் இசைகாரர் பத்தர் பரவும் ஆயிரத்தின் பாலே பட்ட இவை பத்தும் வல்லார்க்கு இல்லை பரிவதே. mālē! māyap perumānē! mā māyanē! enṟu enṟu mālē ēṟi māl aruḷāl mannu kurukūrc catakōpan pālēy tamiḻar isaikārar pattar paravum āyirattin pālē patta ivai pattum vallārkku illai parivadē*

- *mālē* – natural omnipresence (greatness).
- *māyap perumānē* – greatness due to auspicious qualities.
- *māmāyanē* – greatness due to his divine activities.
- *enṟu enṟu mālēyēṟi* – Becoming bewildered, saying “I am unqualified” and leaving him after contemplating on such greatness of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/).
- *māl aruḷāl mannu kurukūrc catakōpan* – Just like someonevho is  trying to hang himself is saved by cutting off the rope, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) who tried to leave emperumān, was saved by [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s unlimited mercy. Just like princely persons cannot eat every handful of food without ghee, āḻvār cannot proceed at every stage without emperumān’s mercy.
- *pālēy tamiḻar* – Ones who are well-versed in tamiḻ that is like sweet milk.
- isaikārar – Ones who can add music to poems – like [srī madurakavigaḷ](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/madhurakavi-azhwar/) and [nātamunigaḷ](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nathamunigal/) \[who were experts in music\].
- *pattar* – those bhaktas (devotees) who are similar to [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) himself who is always engaged in enjoying bhagavā’s auspicious qualities. Those who are like “*kālāḻum nenjaḻiym kaṇsuḻalum*” (legs are becoming weak, heart is melting, eyes are feeling heavy – periya tiruvantādi 34) – bodily changes due to great devotion.
- *pālēy tamiḻar isaikārar pattar* – [kūrattāḻvān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/kuraththazhwan/) once explained that [periya nambi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/periya-nambi/) is “*pālēy tamiḻar*“, [āḻvār tiruvarangap perumāḷ araiyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/thiruvarangapperumal-araiyar/) is “*isaikārar*” and [piḷḷai uṟangā villi dāsar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/pillai-urangavilli-dhasar/) is “*pattar*“; [āḷavandār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/alavandhar/) explained that mudalāḻvārgaḷ ([poigai āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/poigai-azhwar/), [bhūtattāḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/bhuthaththazhwar/), [pēyāḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/peyazhwar/)) are “*pālēy tamiḻar*“, [tiruppāṇāḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/thiruppanazhwar/) is “*isaikārar*” and [periyāḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/periyazhwar/) is “*pattar*“. These three terms are explained as “*pālēy tamiḻar*” (those who know the pāsurams), “*isaikārar*” (those who know the tunes for the pāsurams) and “*pattar*” (those who are engrossed in enjoying bhagavān’s auspicious qualities in those pāsurams).
- *paravum* – The whole world appreciates these pāsurams after [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) removed the thought of leaving from [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/).
- *āyirattin pālē patta* – Just like a pearl is present in beautiful ocean, this decad is present in the beautiful tiruvāimoḻi prabandam.
- *illai parivadu* – no sorrow. āḻvār, after sending messenger in “[*anjiṟaiya mada nārāy*](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/07/thiruvaimozhi-1-4-anjiraiya/)“and [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) arrives, said “I am unqualified” and suffered in separation – such sorrows will not affect those who recite these pāsurams.

Final summary from nampiḷḷai:

- In the first pāsuram, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) said “I am unqualified” and left [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/).
- In the second pāsuram, āḻvār said that he is not qualified to leave [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/).
- In the third pāsuram, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) showed his simplicity and āḻvār became mesmerised.
- In the fourth pāsuram, āḻvār said that the owner of the property will not let the property from slipping.
- In the fifth pāsuram, āḻvār prays emperumān to ensure that āḻvār is surrendered at his lotus feet.
- In the sixth pāsuram, on seeing emperumān delaying a little bit, āḻvār says he is finished.
- In the seventh pāsuram, emperumān rushes to āḻvār and āḻvār again says that he is unqualified.
- In the eighth pāsuram, emperumān says that being together with āḻvār is like eating butter in gōkulam.
- In the ninth pāsuram, āḻvār says that his association with [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) will be poisonous for emperumān and emperumān says he would sustain with that poison.
- In the tenth pāsuram, āḻvār says that [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) convinced him (to remain with him) and started decorating paramapadam to welcome him.
- Finally, āḻvār explains the result for those who learned this decade.

Thus ends the English translation for tiruvāimoḻi 1st centum 5th decad.

[āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) tiruvadigaḷē caraṇam  
[emperumānār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/emperumanar/) tiruvadigaḷē caraṇam  
[piḷḷān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/pillan/) tiruvadigaḷē caraṇam  
[nanjīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nanjiyar/) tiruvadigaḷē caraṇam  
[nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/) tiruvadigaḷē caraṇam  
[vadakkut tiruvīdip piḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadakku-thiruvidhi-pillai/) tiruvadigaḷē caraṇam  
[periyavāccān piḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/periyavachchan-pillai/) tiruvadigaḷē caraṇam  
[vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/) tiruvadigaḷē caraṇam  
[jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/mamunigal/) tiruvadigaḷē caraṇam

## 1.6 Parivadil isanai

## 1.6.1. Parivadil isanai

*parivadil īsanaip pādi virivadu mēval uṟuvīr pirivagai inṟi nal nīr tūy purivaduvum pugai pūvē*

**Пословный перевод:**

parivadil – one who rivals all inauspicious qualities; īsanai – sarvēśvaran (who is the controller of all and who is complete in all auspicious qualities); pādi – singing (in the form of sāma gānam which is an outcome of love due to divine experience); virivadu – blossoming of true nature; mēval – on acquiring; uṟuvīr – Oh those who have strong conviction!; piri vagai – passing over (with ulterior motives); inṟi – not doing that; nal nīr – pure water; tūy – offering it (with love) even irregularly; purivaduvum – submitting that; pugai pūvē – simply some fragrance stick and flower

**Перевод:**

**Oh those who have strong conviction on singing (the glories) of sarvēśvaran who rivals all inauspicious qualities and acquiring natural blossoming of oneself (self-realisation)! Instead of moving away from emperumān (after getting your desires fulfilled), just offer pure water (even irregularly but with love) and submit some incense and flowers.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

piḷḷān calls out for those bhakti yōga niśtas (those who are practicing bhakti yōgam) and tells them that it is difficult to perform bhakti yōga incessantly and thus give up such efforts and take up to performing some tiny little kainkaryam  to [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) which will be accepted by him happily.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In first pāsuram – āḻvār says that since emperumān is fully complete and very simple, he will be satisfied with leaf, flowers etc.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*In first pāsuram – āḻvār explains the practicability in vorśipping emperumān.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*In first pāsuram – āḻvār explains that no specific offerings are expected from those who approach emperumān.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. பரிவது இல் ஈசனைப் பாடி விரிவது மேவல் உறுவீர் பிரிவகை இன்றி நல் நீர் தூய் புரிவதுவும் புகை பூவே parivadil īsanaip pādi virivadu mēval uṟuvīr pirivagai inṟi nal nīr tūy purivaduvum pugai pūvē*

- *parivadu* – explained as both dukkam (sorrow) and pakśapādam (partiality)
- *il* – (short form of illai) not present.
   - there is no sorrow – when the devotee feels sorrow thinking “will he accept my offering or not”, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) feels sorrow for that. So, the devotee need not feel sorrow about the offering.
   - there is no partiality – having partiality means favouring a person since he offered lots (or something of higher value). If he has such partiality, that will be a defect for [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/). So, there is no such partiality. Because of not having sorrow/partiality, he is called “*hēyapratyanīkan*” (opposite of all defects).

Why does he not show any partiality?

- *īsanai* – Because he is the real master (for everyone). When hēyapratyanīkatā (opposite of defects) is explained, it also indicates kalyāṇaguṇayōgam (being the abode of all auspicious qualities). When we offer a feast to an outsider, even if we did it with great care, we would still wonder “How is he going to like it?” But when we offer a feast to our own father, even if there are any defects, the father will consider it as his own – so we need not have any worry about our offerings – such is the relationship between [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) and [paramātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/).
- *pādi* – To let out the emotions by singing about him on approaching him.
- *pādi virvadu mēval uṟuvīr* – Just as it is explained in taittirya upaniśat “*ētat sāmagāyannāstē*” (He is singing the mantra which is mentioned subsequently), those who want to have their knowledge expanded by singing the glories of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/).

That is a great result (having full expansion of knowledge). What do we have to do?

- *pirivagai inṟi* – Instead of saying as in tiruvāimoḻi 1.5.2 “*imaiyōr palarum munivarum punainda kaṇṇi nīr sāndam pugaiyōdu ēndi vaṇangināl … un perumāi māsuṇādō*” (Even if the dēvas, riśis et al came with pure garlands, water, incense to worship you – would that not cause disrepute to your glories?) and leaving him.
- *nal nīr* – Just pure water is sufficient. No need to even add cardamom etc.
- *tūy* – throw at him (even if not offered humbly) – as explained in stōtra ratnam 28 “yatā tatā vāpi” (in any manner).
- *purivaduvum* – offering those which are already given to him by [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) out of his mercy only.
- *pugai pūvē* – Instead of special fragrance, flower etc. – any flower or any incense.

[bhattar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/parasara-bhattar/) explains “one can even burn some dry leaves and offer that smoke; one can even offer kaṇṭakārikā (nightshade) flower”. Hearing this [nanjīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nanjiyar/) highlights a pramāṇam which says “*na kaṇṭakārikā puśpam dēvāya vinivēdayēt*” (one should not offer nightshade flower to [sarvēsvaran](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)). bhattar explains for that saying “It is not because it is unacceptable for him. It is rejected due to itsz having thorns which may hurt the devotee who plucks that flower”.

[bhattar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/parasara-bhattar/) further explains periya tirumoḻi 11.7.6 pāsuram here “*kaḷḷāṟ tuḻāyum kaṇavalarum kūviḷaiyum muḷḷār muḷariyum āmbalum”* – different kinds of flowers soft or thorny are cited here without any discrimination – this is to highlight that [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) does not distinguish between the variety of offerings. In the same pāsuram it is explained “*puḷḷāy ōr ēnamumāyp pukkidandān*” – If he thought that he wanted pure offerings, would he not have stayed in paramapadam itself? But he descended as a bird (swan), a wild boar etc (to accept the offerings of his devotees without any discrimination). Once when nanjīyar was reading vārāha kalpam (varāha purāṇam), it is noted there that varāha [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) accepts muttakkāsu (a type of root which is liked by pigs) – [nanjīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nanjiyar/) became astonished by [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s true association with the form he accepts. The pāsuram ends with “*uḷḷātār uḷḷattai uḷḷamāk koḷḷōmē*” (we will not consider the hearts of such persons as hearts) – the plural in “we will not consider” indicates [tirumangai āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/thirumangai-azhwar/) is including all the other [āḻvārs](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/azhwars/) as well and indicates that all 10 [āḻvārs](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/azhwars/) are in the same mood.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.
