## 1.6.2. Madu ar

*maduvār taṇ am tuḻāyān mudu vēda mutalvanukku edu ēdu en paṇi ennādu aduvē āḷ ceyyum īdē*

**Пословный перевод:**

am – (beautiful) highlighting the supremacy; madu Ar – abundance of honey; taṇ – cool; tuḻāyān – one who wears tuḷasi garland; mudu – ancient; vēdam – vēdams; mudalvan – for the one who is explicitly explained in; edu – (matching his caliber) what?; en paṇi ēdu – what is my service?; ennādu aduvē – instead of saying that (what can I do to match his greatness?); saying “aham sarvam kariśyāmi” (I will serve him in all ways); āḷ seyyum – to serve; īdu – qualification

**Перевод:**

**For the sarvēsvaran who is wearing beautiful tuḷasi garland (which reveals his supremacy) and who is explicitly explained in the ancient vēdam, instead of saying “I am unqualified to serve him matching his greatness”, one should consider the desire to serve him in all ways as the qualification.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In second pāsuram – āḻvār says that no specific qualification is required for those who approach emperumān.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently – āḻvār mercifully explains the practicability of the one who is approaching emperumān.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Second pāsuram – āḻvār explained in the first pāsuram that no specific offerings are required while approaching emperumān. In this pāsuram, he explains one need not say “I am unqualified” and leave emperumān. மதுவார் தண் அம் துழாயான் முது வேத முதலவனுக்கு எது ஏது என் பணி என்னாது அதுவே ஆள் செய்யும் ஈடே maduvār taṇ am tuḻāyān mudu vēda mutalvanukku edu ēdu en paṇi ennādu aduvē āḷ ceyyum īdē*

- *maduvār taṇṇantuḻāyān* – In the previous pāsuram, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) said “*purivaduvum pugai pūvē*” in the end; Here, he starts with “*maduvār taṇṇantuḻāyān*“; How does this conform to andādi rule? Experts in tamiḻ say that “Since pū (flower) always is with madu (honey), it is reasonable”; there is a different version to the text”*vaduvār taṇṇantuḻāyān*” which will be most appropriate; vaduvai means fragrance and ārtal means “filled with”. vaduvai has become vadu and this indicates most fragrant tuḷasi; Experts in tamiḻ accept this explanation too.
- *maduvār taṇṇantuḻāyān* –  [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s hair-locks are so potent that even when a dry garland is placed on his hair, due to its contact with the hair, the garland becomes fresh, filled with honey and honey will start overflowing.
- *muduvēda mudalvanukku* – While talking about this beautiful decoration of [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/), it should be supported with the ancient vēdam. “*vēda mudalvan*” means one who is explained through vēdam as highlighted in brahma sūtram 1.1.3 “*sāstrayōnitvāt*” (sāstram is the source to know about [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)). “*maduvār taṇṇantuḻāyān”* indicates that he is sarvādikan (superior to everyone); “*muduvēda mudalvan*“  indicates that he is paripūrṇan (complete in all aspects). Both facilitate him to be easily vorśippable.
- *edu ēdu …* – The qualification to serve him is not to ask “What is his duty? What is my duty?” One cannot say “Only nityasūris can serve him; what can I do?” It is also explained as instead of assuming that we cannot engage in certain kainkaryams, desiring to serve him in all manners is the qualification to serve him.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.6.3. Idum eduppum

*īdum eduppum il īsan mādu vidādu en mananē pādum en nā avan pādal ādum en angam aṇangē*

**Пословный перевод:**

īdum – (Due to the defects) leaving behind; eduppum – (Due to the good qualities) accepting; il – not present; īsan – īśvaran’s (one who has eternal relationship with everyone); mādu – proximity; en manan – my mind/heart; vidādu – will not give up; en nā – my tongue; avan pādal – this tiruvāimoḻi that glorifies him; pādum – will sing; en angam – my body; aṇangu – like possessed by some divine force; ādum – will dance

**Перевод:**

**Meditating upon bhagavān’s quality of not rejecting anyone due to his/her defects and not accepting any one due his/her qualities (i.e., being neutral towards everyone), my mind will not leave his proximity; my tongue will sing this tiruvāimoḻi; my body will dance like being possessed by a divine force.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*When asked “Why no qualification is expected by him?” āḻvār says that emperumān naturally does not have the attitude to reject those who have the desire to serve him in spite of their inferior birth, qualities and actions.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In third pāsuram – āḻvār contemplates the qualities of emperumān which are explained in the previous two pāsurams and mercifully explains how his mind, speech and body are happily engaged in the service of sarvēsvaran.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Third pāsuram – meditating upon emperumān‘s qualities (as explained previously), forgetting his purpose (of parōpadēsam – advising others), āḻvār mercifully explains how his mind, speech and body are happily engaged in emperumān’s service. ஈடும் எடுப்பும் இல் ஈசன் மாடு விடாது என் மனனே பாடும் என் நா அவன் பாடல் ஆடும் என் அங்கம் அணங்கே īdum eduppum il īsan mādu vidādu en mananē pādum en nā avan pādal ādum en angam aṇangē*

- *īdum eduppumil īsan* – sarvēśvaran who does not accept some people and reject some others, Since his relationship with everyone is the same, he cannot reject some. jitantē 1.2 “*dēvānām dānvānām ca sāmānyamadidaivatam*” (Oh the one who is the common lord for dēvas and asuras!) – he has the same relationship with the ones whom he accepts and the ones he rejects.
- *īsan mādu vidādu en mananē* – My mind will not give up his proximity. Only when he is approached for attaining ulterior goals, could be forgotten after the goals are accomplished. I cannot even engage in the activity I started (advising others about his easily vorśippable nature) – my mind is fully focussed on him.

It is explained by [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) himself in tiruvāimoḻi 4.5.4 “*nāviyalāl isai mālaigaḷētti*” (making garlands of poems and singing them with the tongue). Why don’t you just explain that to us with your words? No need for your mind’s involvement (let it be engaged in enjoying [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)).

- *pādum en nā avan pādal* – My tongue too started following the mind’s way \[So, I am not even able to talk to you\].

At the least, show your hand in upadēsa mudrā (instructing posture) – that will make us understand the meanings.

- *ādum en angam aṇangē* – My body too started dancing out of bliss \[So, I can’t even show you the hasta mudrā\].

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.6.4. Anangu ena

*aṇangu ena ādum en angam vaṇangi vaḻipadum īsan piṇangi amarar pidaṟṟum guṇagkeḻu koḷgaiyinānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

aṇangu ena – like being divinely possessed; ādum – dancing up and down (out of love); en – my; angam – body; vaṇangi vaḻipadum – worshiping in the form of offering obeisance, etc; īsan – the one who is the master; amarar – nityasūris – residents of parampadam who eternally enjoy bhagavān; piṇangi pidaṟṟum – (based on the qualities enjoyed by them) happily arguing etc; guṇam keḻu – abundance of qualities; koḷgaiyinān – one who has these as a natural phenomenon

**Перевод:**

**emperumān, the one who has amazing qualities in abundance, is discussed by nityasūris (based on his various qualities). Such emperumān is my master who is worshiped by me by offering obeisance etc., by my body that is dancing up and down like divinely possessed.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In fourth pāsuram – āḻvār says he too developed eternal love for bhagavān like nityasūris. It is also said as āḻvār saying that his body will worship and glorify bhagavān who has many qualities.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says, bhagavān who acknowledged āḻvār, has glorious qualities which are eternally enjoyed by nityasūris.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Fourth pāsuram – āḻvār says that the love developed in his mind, words and body towards emperumān is not transient and is eternal like that of nityasūirs. அணங்கு என ஆடும் என் அங்கம் வணங்கி வழிபடும் ஈசன் பிணங்கி அமரர் பிதற்றும் குணங்கெழு கொள்கையினானே aṇangu ena ādum en angam vaṇangi vaḻipadum īsan piṇangi amarar pidaṟṟum guṇagkeḻu koḷgaiyinānē*

- It is explained in two ways:
   - [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is “*aṇangena ādum en angam vaṇangi vaḻipadum īsan piṇangi amarar pidaṟṟum guṇam keḻu koḷgaiynān*”  (my body dancing like divinely possessed, worships the sarvēsvaran, in the form of obeisance etc, whose qualities are discussed by nityasūris”.
   - “*piṇangi amarar pidaṟṟum guṇam keḻu koḷgaiyinānāna īsanai anubavittu aṇangu ena ādum en angam vaṇangi vaḻipadum*” (On enjoying [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) whose qualities are discussed by nituasūris, my body like being possessed will dance and will worship him).
- *aṇangu ena ādum en angam* – dancing like being possessed; worshiping [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) as if that is the only work.
- *piṇangi amarar pidaṟṟum* – While debating the various qualities, one starts with glorifying one’s own favourite quality, but ends up glorifying the quality that is favoured by the others; they become upset with each other desiring to glorify each of their favourite qualities – the one who is the abode of such auspicious qualities;
- *guṇam keḻu koḷgaiyinānē* – Just like an ocean having unlimited precious stones/gems/pearls in it, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is having unlimited auspicious qualities. One who has such auspicious qualities naturally in full. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says he is going through the same emotions like nityasūris who are sarvajñas (omniscient).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.6.5. Kolgai kolamai

*koḷgai koḷāmai ilādān eḷgal irāgam ilādān viḷgai viḷḷāmai virumbi uḷ kalandārkku ōr amudē*

**Пословный перевод:**

koḷgai – quality of accepting (seeing good qualities); koḷāmai – quality of rejecting (seeing bad qualities); ilādān – one who does not have; eḷgal – emotion (that leads to rejecting); irāgam – desire (that leads to accepting); ilādān – neutral person who does not have; viḷgai – (accepting ulterior benefits and) leaving; viḷḷāmai – (being fully focussed on serving emperumān and) staying together; virumbi – seeing that; uḷ kalandārkku – for those (who are inseparable from him) who entered (his heart); ōr – distinct; amudu – eternally nectarean (reliśable)

**Перевод:**

**bhagavān who does not accept some (seeing their good qualities) and reject others (seeing their bad qualities), who is neutral and does not have emotions and desires, sees that he is distinctly reliśable for those who seek out him alone (and not for the others who seek out ulterior benefits).**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*Thus speaking about being blessed unconditionally by emperumān with abundance (of devotion) for a while (in-between), subsequently, āḻvār speaks towards those who consider themselves unqualified to serve emperumān to remove their shyness and explains emperumān‘s glorious qualities to them.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation. piḷḷān highlights that [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) gives himself to those who desire him alone and he gives ulterior benefits to those who seek out such benefits from him (thus he being neutral in providing what each individual seeks out from him).

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In fifth pāsuram – āḻvār explains that for those who are fully existing for emperumān‘s pleasure, emperumān is infinitely enjoyable.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Fifth pāsuram – Again, āḻvār starts engaging in his original initiative – When someone approaches sarvēsvaran, he analyses “Will they seek out ulterior benefits and leave? Will they seek out for me only?” and says that emperumān remains infinitely enjoyable for those who seek out him alone. கொள்கை கொளாமை இலாதான் எள்கல் இராகம் இலாதான் விள்கை விள்ளாமை விரும்பி உள் கலந்தார்க்கு ஓர் அமுதே koḷgai koḷāmai ilādān eḷgal irāgam ilādān viḷgai viḷḷāmai virumbi uḷ kalandārkku ōr amudē*

- *koḷgai koḷāmai ilādān* – [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) does not engage individuals in service based on “this person is great in birth, actions, knowledge etc., so I will engage him in confidential service; this other person is not so great in birth, actions, knowledge etc., so I will engage him in insignificant external service”.

Though he does not discriminate while engaging individuals in service, does he think about them like that?

- *eḷgal irāgam ilādān* – Even in his divine heart, he does not discriminate. In “[*īdum eduppumil īsan*](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/08/thiruvaimozhi-1-6-3-idum-eduppum/)” – his neutral nature while they approach him is explained. Here his neutrality while engaging them in service is highlighted.
- *viḷgai viḷḷāmai virumbi* – He only expects this aspect (explained further).
- *viḷgai* – Leaving, after achieving ulterior motives.
- *viḷḷāmai* – Being together always with kainkaryam as the only motive.
- *virumbi* – encouraging.
- *uḷ kalandārkku* – Those who approach him with serving him alone as the goal – ones who has seamlessly mixed with him.
- *ōramudē* – he will be distinct nectar; [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) himself says in tiruvāimoḻi 5.8.1 “*ārāvamudu*” (unflinching nectar).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.6.6. Amutam amarargatku

*amudam amaragatku īnda nimir sudar āḻi nedumāl amudilum āṟṟa iniyan nimir tirai nīḷ kadalānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

amarargatku – for the dēvas (who desired immortality); amudam – amrutam (nectar which is the medicine that bestows immortality); īnda – one who bestowed it; nimir sudar – glowing (growing) radiance; āḻi – one who beholds sudarsana cakram; nedumāl – one who is always with unlimited glories; nimir – raising (due to his touch); tirai – having the waves; nīḷ – broad (matching his glories); kadalān – one who lies down in kśīrābdi (milk ocean); amudilum – more than amrutam (which was retrieved from the milk ocean); āṟṟa iniyan – very sweet

**Перевод:**

**emperumān who bestowed the nectar (which in-turn bestows immortality) to dēvas (celestial beings who desired immortality) has sudarsana cakram (disc) which has glowing radiance. Such emperumān has infinite glories, lies down in kśīrābdi (milk ocean) which is very broad (matching emperumān‘s glories) and having raising waves (due to his touch).  He is sweeter than the amrutam which was retrieved from the milk ocean.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation. piḷḷān also says that [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) becomes distressed seeing the loss of those prayōjanāntaraparars who were highlighted in previous pāsuram.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In sixth pāsuram – āḻvār derides those who pursue the infinitely enjoyable emperumān as means but leave him after having their ulterior goals fulfilled.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says that emperumān fulfils the ulterior motives of those who seek him out and presents himself as most enjoyable for those who are fully seeking him out.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*piḷḷai Sixth pāsuram – āḻvār says “When he is like this (being most enjoyable), these people are getting ulterior benefits and leaving him!” and derides dēvas who are prayōjanāntarapara (those who seek out ulterior benefits from him). அமுதம் அமரர்கட்கு ஈந்த நிமிர் சுடர் ஆழி நெடுமால் அமுதிலும் ஆற்ற இனியன் நிமிர் திரை நீள் கடலானே amudam amaragatku īnda nimir sudar āḻi nedumāl amudilum āṟṟa iniyan nimir tirai nīḷ kadalānē*

- *amudam amaragatku īnda* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is wondering “How generous [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is?” Even when dēvas ask “We don’t want you. Just arrange for our immortality”, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) still fulfils their desires.

Deriding their motives, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) explains the distinction between their goal and his own.

- *nimir sudarāḻi nedumāl* – This is [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s nectar. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s nectar is “*nāltōḷamudu*” (the nectar with 4 shoulders) \[tiruvāimoḻi 6.10.9\]; iraṇḍām tiruvantādi 85 “*amudenṟum tēnenṟum āḻiyānenṟum*” (He is relished as nectar, honey, the one who beholds sudarsana cakram). The sudarsana cakram is glowing with radiance due to [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) fulfilling their desires.
- *nedumāl* – the who is greatly mesmerised – due to the fact that even if the dēvas were seeking out for ulterior motives, they got them accomplished with the help of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) himself \[instead of going to someone else\].
- *amudilum āṟṟa iniyan* –  sweeter than nectar. If they knew the distinction between [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) and the nectar, they would have not desired for ulterior motives. It is said that nambi tiruvaḻutinādu dāsar said “Are these dēvas like deer/foolhardy? They are so focussed on seeing this salt-water \[sarcastically saying about the amutam/nectar\] coming out of the ocean?”
- *nimir tirai nīḷ kadalānē* – Are they giving him up due to lack of proximity? He is lying down in the same ocean where the nectar is found. Even for those who don’t understand his glories, he is readily available to be woken up and engaged in resolving their issues. The ocean is broad as explained in tiruvāimoḻi 8.10.8 “*tāḷum tōḷum mudigaḷum samanilāta pala parappi*” (spread out his feet, shoulders and heads which are incomparable) and with high tides (due to his touch). It is said in mudal tiruvandādi 19 “*mālum karungadalē en nōṟṟāy*” (Oh dark ocean! what penance did you do to have [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) lying in such a mesmerized state in you?).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.6.7. Nil kadal

*nīḷ kadal sūḻ ilangaik kōn tōḷgaḷ talai tuṇi seydān tāḷgaḷ talaiyil vaṇangi nāḷ kadalaikkaḻiminē*

**Пословный перевод:**

nīḷ – broad; kadal – by the ocean; sūḻ – surrounded; ilangai – for lankā; kōn – leader whose; tōḷgaḷ – 20 shoulders; talai – 10 heads; tuṇi seydān – one who destroyed; tāḷgaḷ – divine feet (which entered the battle-field); talaiyil vaṇangi – worship by bowing by head; nāḷ kadalai – the ocean of time; kaḻimin – spend

**Перевод:**

**Spend the time which is as long as the ocean, by bowing down your head at the divine feet of srī rāma who destroyed the 20 shoulders and 10 heads of the leader of lankā, which is surrounded by the broad ocean.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In seventh pāsuram – āḻvār says that for those who are devoted to him, if a day feels like an ocean due to their great desire in seeing him and being unable to spend the time, they should think about srī rāma’s brave history and worship his lotus feet with their head. It is also explained as – meditate upon srī rāma who is dasarta’s son and who is the destroyer of the enemies of the devotees and be free from grief.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Seventh pāsuram – When asked “You told he is infinitely enjoyable; But until we reach him, how would we spend our time? “, āḻvār replies “that is what manattukkiniyān’s (srī rāma, who is dear to my heart) \[tiruppāvai 12\] auspicious qualities are there for”. நீள் கடல் சூழ் இலங்கைக் கோன் தோள்கள் தலை துணிசெய்தான் தாள்கள் தலையில் வணங்கி நாள்கள் தலைக்கழிமின்னே nīḷ kadal sūḻ ilangaik kōn tōḷgaḷ talai tuṇi seydān tāḷgaḷ talaiyil vaṇangi nāḷ kadalaikkaḻiminē*

- *nīḷ kadal sūḻ ilangaik kōn* – Due to having the ocean as a moat and due to that, as a  protective layer for lankā, rāvaṇa considered himself as great and out of his ego, he ignored the greatness of [srī rāma](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) and fought with him like an imbecile.
- *tōḷgaḷ talai tuṇi seydān* – [srī rāma](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) casually destroyed the shoulders and heads of rāvaṇa like a sport instead of doing it with vengeance etc.

Like tiruvadi (hanumān) who always meditates upon srī rāma’s acts of valour.

- *nāḷ kadalaik kaḻiminē* – two explanations:
   - If we think about his most enjoyable nature, the time between now and when we reach him looks like a lengthy ocean. In such case, spend the time thinking about the valour of srī rāma.
   - Approach srī rāma (who is the son of dasarata cakravarty) and remove the ocean of samsāram (here nāḷ is explained as time in samsāram \[material realm\]).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.6.8. Kalimin tondirgal

*kaḻimin toṇḍīrgaḷ kaḻittut toḻumin avanai toḻudāl vaḻi ninṟa valvinai māḷvittu aḻivinṟi ākkam tarumē*

**Пословный перевод:**

toṇḍīrgaḷ – Oh those who are desirous (to serve bhagavān)!; kaḻimin – give up (your attachment); kaḻittu – after giving up (that); avanai – cakkaravarttit tirumagan (srī rāma) who was explained in the previous pāsuram; toḻumin – worship him; toḻudāl – merely by carrying out an anjali; val – difficult (to exhaust and existing since time-immemorial); vaḻininṟa vinai – sins which are obstacles in attaining the goal; māḷvittu – eliminating them; aḻivinṟi – (eternally) without returning; ākkam – growing wealth; tarumē – certainly he will give

**Перевод:**

**Oh those who are desirous (to serve bhagavān)! Give up your attachments and worship bhagavān. By merely carrying out an anjali towards him, even those sins which are difficult to exhaust will be eliminated and he will certainly bestow the growing wealth of eternal servitude.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the eighth pāsuram – āḻvār says that for those who worship emperumān for his exclusive pleasure, emperumān removes the obstacles and bestows them with the wealth of perpetual servitude.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says that just an anjali (praying with joined palms) towards him will remove the time-immemorial obstacles and bestow the eternal goal.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Eighth pāsuram – On meditating upon the valiant history of srī rāma and giving up attachment towards worldly pleasures, bhagavān himself will remove the obstacles and bestow eternal servitude to him. கழிமின் தொண்டீர்கள் கழித்துத் தொழுமின் அவனை தொழுதால் வழி நின்ற வல்வினை மாள்வித்து அழிவின்றி ஆக்கம் தருமே kaḻimin toṇḍīrgaḷ kaḻittut toḻumin avanai toḻudāl vaḻi ninṟa valvinai māḷvittu aḻivinṟi ākkam tarumē*

- *kaḻimin toṇḍīrgaḷ* – give up the taste for worldly pleasures. “kaḻikkai” means understanding that they are bad. Those who are seeking for worldly pleasures will not give up the attachment towards them – so *toṇḍīrgaḷ* indicates those who are desirous for bhagavat viśayam.
- *kaḻittut toḻumin* – Instead of being “If we keep worshiping him, these attachments will gradually disappear”, certainly first give up the attachments and then worship him. Saying “*kaḻimin*” (give up) first and then “*kaḻittu*” (after giving up) indicates that giving up worldly pleasure by itself is a goal. Saying “*toḻumin*” (worship him) and then “*toḻudāl*” (if you worship) indicates that even if there is no other result, worshiping itself is the result – like it is said in tamiḻ “*karumbu tinnak kūlipōlē*” (if there is a wage for eating sugarcane) – if there were a separate result for worshiping that is great, but worshiping itself is the enjoyable objective.

If it were done,

- *vaḻi ninṟa val vinai māḷvittu* – Removing those karmas (puṇya \[virtues\] and pāpa \[vices\]) which seem like naturally bound to the [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/), with their vāsanā (impressions).
- *aḻivinṟi ākkam tarumē* – [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) will bestow *apunarāvrutti lakśaṇa mōkśam* (liberation that has no return – once reaching paramapadam, the soul never returns to this material realm) as explained in cāṇḍhōjña upaniśat 8.15 “…*na ca punarāvartatē*” (he does not return after reaching brahmam).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.6.9. Taruma arum

*taruma arum payan āya tirumagaḷār tanik kēḷvan perumai udaiya pirānār irumai vinai kadivārē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tarumam – darmams (virtuous processes/means); arum – difficult to attain; payanāya – the goal that is; tirumagaḷār – srī mahālakśmi who is the best among women; tanikkēḷvan – being the unique beloved/intimate husband; perumai udaiya – having the greatness; pirānār – sarvēsvaran (srīman nārāyaṇan who is the supreme lord); irumai – puṇya (virtue) and pāpa (vice) – two types of; vinai – karmas; kadivār – he will destroy

**Перевод:**

**sarvēsvaran srīman nārāyaṇan is the unique beloved/intimate husband of srī mahālakśmi who is the ultimate manifestation of femininity. emperumān who has such greatness of lakśmī sambandam will bestow the goal which is difficult to accomplish even by most virtuous means and will destroy the karmas which are in the form of puṇyam and pāpam.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the ninth pāsuram – āḻvār says that while removing the obstacles and bestowing the eternal kainkaryam for those who approach him, emperumān does that being together with periya pirāttiyār (srī mahālakśmi), with fondness.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, bhagavān who is sriya:pati (husband of srī mahālakśmi) removes the obstacles out of his will.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Ninth pāsuram – When asked “Just for surrendering unto him, would he remove the obstacles and bestow the result?” āḻvār says “Should we just see him? Should we not see who is accompanying him? īsn’t one who said ‘na kascinnāparādyati‘ (there is no one who does not commit mistakes – srī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 116.45) right next to him?” தரும அரும் பயன் ஆய திருமகளார் தனிக் கேள்வன் பெருமை உடைய பிரானார் இருமை வினை கடிவாரே taruma arum payan āya tirumagaḷār tanik kēḷvan perumai udaiya pirānār irumai vinai kadivārē*

- *tarum* – he will give. There is no doubt.
- *avvarum payanāya* – two explanations:
   - the goal that is explained in sāstram as very difficult to accomplish.
   - [srī mahālakśmi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/) – the embodiment of the ultimate goal attained through virtuous means; since he is the unique/beloved husband of such srī mahālakśmi – he is the most distinct master. As explained in srī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 37.108 “*apramēyam hi tattējō yasya sā janakātmajā …*” (that srī rāma’s valour that is inconceivable, that srī rāma who is the dear consort of sītā dēvi who is the daughter of janaka mahārāja) – only [srīman nārāyaṇan](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) has the glory of being the husband of srī mahālakśmi.
- *perumai udaiya pirānār* – pirān – upakāraka (one who does favours) – one who is the embodiment of blessing his devotees; pirān who is great due to being lakśmīpati (husband of [srī mahālakśmi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/)).
- *irumai vinai kadivārē* – puṇyam and pāpam are only different in namesake for those who are seeking mōkśam (liberation – eternal kainkaryam in paramapadam), since both bind them in this samsāram. So, [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) removes both of them \[arumpadam – In his varadarāja pancāsat slōkam 29 “*sadyas tyajanti varada*“, [vēdāntācāryar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vedhanthacharyar/) explains that puṇyam and pāpam are like gold and iron shackles respectively since puṇyam leads one to svargam and pāpam leads one to narakam – as both svargam and narakam are bindings within this material realm, they both are to be given up by mumukśus\].

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.6.10. Kadivar tiya

*kadivār tīya vinaigaḷ nodiyārum aḷavaik kaṇ kodiyā adu puḷ uyartta vadivār mādavanārē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tīya vinaigaḷ – cruel karmas; nodi ārum – the moment that is filled by a second; aḷaviakkaṇ – measurement of; kadivār – one who destroys; adu – destroying (enemies of his devotees); puḷ – garudāḻvār; kodiyā – as flag; uyartta – having; vadivār – one who is with a beautiful form; mādavanār – sriya:pati (husband of srī mahālakśmi)

**Перевод:**

**emperumān who has garudāḻvār (who destroys the enemies of bhagavān’s devotees) in his flag, who is with a beautiful form, who is the husband of srī mahālakhsmi, will destroy the cruel karmas (puṇyam/pāpam accumulated since time immemorial) within a second.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In tenth pāsuram, āḻvār says that emperumān will arrive with periya pirāttiyār and quickly remove the obstacles mercifully.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says while removing the obstacles, he will do it very quickly.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

periyavāccān piḷḷai says while commenting on “*kodiyā adu puḷ uyartta vadivār*” that the reason [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) quoted garudāḻvār here is to highlight that [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) considers the ones who surrenders now to be the same as nityasūris.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Tenth pāsuram – When asked “When will emperumān and tāyār \[mother – śrī mahālahmi\] eliminate the obstacles?”, āḻvār replies that they will do it as soon as one bows at the lotus feet of emperumān. கடிவார் தீய வினைகள் நொடியாரும் அளவைக் கண் கொடியா அடு புள் உயர்த்த வடிவு ஆர் மாதவனாரே kadivār tīya vinaigaḷ nodiyārum aḷavaik kaṇ kodiyā adu puḷ uyartta vadivār mādavanārē*

- *kadivār tīya vinaigaḷ* – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who has the quality of removing the cruel sins which cannot be eliminated by an individual’s self-effort even when tried perpetually.

In [8th pāsuram](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/08/thiruvaimozhi-1-6-8-kazhimin-thondirgal/), [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says “*vaḻininṟa valvinai māḷvittu*” – once surrendered, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) will remove the sins. In [9th pāsuram](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/08/thiruvaimozhi-1-6-9-tharuma-arum/), [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says “*irumai vinai kadivār*” – since he is with srī māhālakśm, he will remove the sins. When asked “How long will it take for him to remove the sins?”, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says “in a second”.

- *nodiyārum aḷāvaikkan* – the time measurement that lasts a second – indicates “immediately”.
- *kodiyā adu puḷ uyartta vadivār* – vadivu is explained as svabhāvam (nature/characteristic) and rūpam (form). ēvenas one sees the garuda flag from the di’/stance,  one can understand the nature of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) having garudāḻvār (who destroys the enemies) as/in his flag. *vadivār* also means “having a beautiful form”.
- *vadivārmā* – mā indicates srī mahālakśmi. Here vadivār is an adjective for tāyār – the one who has complete form, beautiful form, suitable form.
- mādavanār – Only if [pirātti](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/) is advising him by being nearby, he will remove the sins.  [pirātti](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/) says “On one side, there is birth and on the other side, there is death. In between there are diseases. How can you see his (the one who surrenders) mistakes? If you have to cite the mistakes and ignore him (to suffer in this samsāram), you have to give up on every one. Forgive him” and [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) says “forgiven” to satisfy her.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.6.11. Madavan pal

*mādavan pāl satakōpan tīdu avam inṟi uraitta ēdam il āyirattu ippattu ōda vallār piṟavāṟē*

**Пословный перевод:**

satakōpan – nammāḻvār; mādavan pāl – towards sarvēsvaran srīman nārāyaṇan; tīdu – defect (of hesitating on seeing his own greatness); avam – defect (of failing the devotees seeing their faults); inṟi – not having; uraitta – told; ēdam – defects (of poetic structure etc); il – not having; āyirattu – among the 1000 pāsurams; ippattu – this decad (which explains the easily vorśipable nature of emperumān); ōda vallār – those who are capable of learning/reciting (through an ācāryan); piṟavār – won’t be born (in this samsāram)

**Перевод:**

**This decad is explained by āḻvār in the pristine manner (without any defect) about emperumān who does not have the defects of hesitating (to bless the devotees)  on seeing his own greatness and failing them on seeing their faults. Those who can learn this decad among the thousand pāsurams from tiruvāimoḻi will not be born in material realm.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the end, āḻvār mercifully highlights the result for those who learn this decad.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār mercifully explains the result of this decad as elimination of birth (in this material realm).*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*In the end, āḻvār says that those who learn this decad will not be born in this samsāram where it is an up-hill task to experience bhagavān.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

- *piṟavār* – This samsāram is such that we have to say “approaching [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is easy” like “serving one’s mother is nice”.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*In the end, āḻvār says that those who are capable of practicing (the principles explained in) this decad will not be born in samsāram (material realm). மாதவன் பால் சடகோபன் தீது அவம் இன்றி உரைத்த ஏதம் இல் ஆயிரத்து இப்பத்து ஓத வல்லார் பிறவாரே mādavan pāl satakōpan tīdu avam inṟi uraitta ēdam il āyirattu ippattu ōda vallār piṟavāṟē*

- *mādavan* … – While tīdu, avam and ēdam are explained by some ācāryas in the context of pratipādyan (object of the pāsurams), vaktā (speaker of the pāsurams) and prabandam (pāsurams) respectively, [bhattar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/parasara-bhattar/) explained it differently. “*ēdamil āyiram*” (faultless 1000) itself is sufficient to explain that there is no defect in all three – pramēyam, pramāta and pramāṇam. So, what is the purpose of tīdu and avam? It is based on “satakōpan mādavanpāl tīdu avam inṟi uraitta” (satakōpan recited these pāsurams explaining that [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) does not have tīdu and avam). tīdu – considering his own greatness of “I am the husband of [srī mahālakśmi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/)” and staying away from his devotees; avam – Looking at the lowly nature – “The one who is surrendering unto me is nitya samsāri (who has been perpetually bound in this material realm)” and failing the devotee. These two defects are not present in [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/).
- *piṟavār* – This samsāram is such that we have to say “approaching [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is easy” like “being protected by mother is nice” \[i.e., even the most obvious principle is difficult to understand due to the high level of ignorance\]. Those who understand this decad, will give up the connection in this material realm and will enjoy [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) in the assembly of nityasūris (eternally free) and muktas (liberated) who fully spend their time in experiencing [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) only.

Final summary from nampiḷḷai:

- In the first pāsuram, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says that for the one who approaches [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), there is no specific restriction on the offerings.
- In the second pāsuram, he says that there is no specific qualification required for the one who approaches [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/).
- In the third pāsuram, he says that all his three faculties (mind, speech and body) are engaged in bhagavat viśayam.
- In the fourth pāsuram, he says that such engagement in bhagavat viśayam became his activity always, like that of nityasūris.
- In the fifth pāsuram, he says that for those who approach [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) for emperumān’s pleasure only, emperumān becomes most enjoyable.
- In the sixth pāsuram, he becomes angry at the materialistic persons saying “why they are missing out on this most-enjoyable [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) and running behind worldly pleasures?”.
- In the seventh pāsuram,  he explains the activities for those who are fully existing for the pleasure of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/).
- In the eighth pāsuram, he  explains that [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) himself will eliminate the hurdles which stop the result from being acquired.
- In the ninth pāsuram, when a doubt is raised on him removing the obstacles, he says “Don’t just see his nature, see the nature of his divine consort”.
- In the tenth pāsuram, when asked “How long will the divine couple take to remove the obstacles?”, he says “at once”.
- Finally, he says that those who practice this decad will no longer be connected to the material realm after this life.

Thus ends the English translation for tiruvāimoḻi 1st centum 6th decad.

[āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) tiruvadigaḷē caraṇam  
[emperumānār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/emperumanar/) tiruvadigaḷē caraṇam  
[piḷḷān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/pillan/) tiruvadigaḷē caraṇam  
[nanjīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nanjiyar/) tiruvadigaḷē caraṇam  
[nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/) tiruvadigaḷē caraṇam  
[vadakkut tiruvīdip piḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadakku-thiruvidhi-pillai/) tiruvadigaḷē caraṇam  
[periyavāccān piḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/periyavachchan-pillai/) tiruvadigaḷē caraṇam

[jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/mamunigal/) tiruvadigaḷē caraṇam

## 1.7 Piravit tuyar

## 1.7.1. Piravit tuyar

*piṟavit tuyar aṟa jñānattuḷ ninṟu tuṟavic cudar viḷakkam talaip peyvār aṟavanai āḻippadai andaṇanai maṟaviyai inṟi manattu vaippārē*

**Пословный перевод:**

piṟavit tuyar – sufferings which arise out of birth; aṟa – to remove; jñānattil – in knowledge (to see ātmā); ninṟu – having conviction; tuṟavi – being discharged from all bindings; cudar – the radiant ātmā‘s; viḷakkam – manifestation; talaippeyvār – ones who are interested in; aṟavanai – most benevolent (due to his bestowing the results for such persons); āḻippadai – one having the sudarsana cakram (which purifies the heart); antaṇanai – the purest īsvara (supreme lord); maṟaviyai inṟi – having him as means; manattu vaippār – how they are meditating! (accuses them)

**Перевод:**

**To remove the sufferings which arise from birth, those who are situated in knowledge (on ātmā), giving up all attachments, seeking out for self-realisation, meditate upon emperumān who is most benevolent, who carries the sudarsana cakram and who is the purest supreme lord! Here, āḻvār is censuring such kaivalyārttis (those who seek out self-enjoyment after being liberated) for accepting emperumān as the means but not as the goal too.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*āḻvār becomes mesmerised seeing emperumān who fulfils the desires of mumukśus who just seek liberation from the pains of material realm to be seated in self-enjoyment even after approaching emperumān who is infinitely enjoyable.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*In first pāsuram, āḻvār explains the pure nature of bhagavān who is being worshiped.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*First pāsuram – āḻvār censures the kēvalar (one who desires self-enjoyment) for giving up bhagavān and seeking out ulterior benefits (of enjoying oneself) and leaving him. பிறவித் துயர் அற ஞானத்துள் நின்று துறவிச் சுடர் விளக்கம் தலைப் பெய்வார் அறவனை ஆழிப்படை அந்தணனை மறவியை இன்றி மனத்து வைப்பாரே piṟavit tuyar aṟa jñānattuḷ ninṟu tuṟavic cudar viḷakkam talaip peyvār aṟavanai āḻippadai andaṇanai maṟaviyai inṟi manattu vaippārē*

- *piṟavit tuyar aṟa jñānattuḷ ninṟu* – kēvalar is explained in bhagavat gītā 7.14 “jarā maraṇa mōkśāya …” (to be free from old-age, death etc). Here, they are being explained. For all three types of samsāris – aisvaryārtti (one who desires for worldly wealth/pleasures), ātmaprāpti kāman (one who desires for self-realisation) and bhagavatprāpti kāman (one who desires for kainkaryam to [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)), upāsana (worshiping [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)) and antimasmruti (meditating upon their desired aspect during the last moments) are common. But why is there difference in the result? That is because, while worshiping [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), they desire for different results, i.e., instead of desiring kainkaryam to him, stopping short. This is what is explained in tiruppallāṇḍu 4th pāsuram “*varamboḻi vandu*” (remove the boundaries and come). The cause for such interest in different results is their sukruta tāratamyam (difference in level of piety). [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) himself declares in gītā 7.16 “*caturvidā bhajantē mām janāssukrutinōrjuna*” (Oh arjuna! there are four types of pious persons who worship me). It is based on their virtue that they develop the taste for different results. For such results, they carry out upāsanam (worship). Based on their upāsanam, the results will occur.
- *piṟavit tuyar …* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) wonders “Why do they approach [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) and simply stop with insignificant results?”. piṟavi – janmam – here this term also includes the other five aspects viz – asti (existence), pariṇamatē (change), vivartdatē (growth), apakśīyatē (decline) and vinasyati (cease to exist). To eliminate all of these (they worship [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)). He too prays to emperumān in tiruviruttam 1 “*inninṟa nīrmai ini yām uṟāmai*” (I cannot bear this suffering any more) – what is the reason for [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) censuring these persons here? For āḻvār, when samsāram (material suffering) is eliminated, he is naturally leaning towards kainkaryam. But for the kaivalyārttis, eliminating material suffering is the only goal – so, there is a distinction.
- *jñānattuḷ ninṟu* – The result of “*piṟavit tuyar aṟa*” (eliminating of material suffering) leads to “*jñānattuḷ ninṟu*” (being situated in proper knowledge). [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) is both jñāna guṇakam (one who has knowledge as an attribute/quality) and jñātā (one who knows).\]
- *tuṟavic cudar viḷakkam talaip peyvār* – The contraction of knowledge for the [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) that is seen in material situation does not exist in the liberated state where the knowledge is fully expanded. When we look at “*piṟavit tuyar aṟa jñānattuḷ ninṟu*” from upāsana perspective, “*tuṟavic cudar viḷakkam*” (giving up attachments and self-realisation) are the result.
- *aṟavanai* – dārmika – the most benevolent. [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) only looks for the quality of approaching him even for insignificant results – he becomes pleased by that and bestows the results. Even when they don’t want him and pray for insignificant fruits, he mercifully bestows them those results.
- *āḻippadai andaṇanai* – One who holds sudarsana cakram which will remove the obstacles for self-realisation. Here, [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is treated by kaivalyārttis as cow-dung which is a purifier but once purified the cow-dung that was used to purify gets thrown out. They only looked at [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) as “*suddan*” (pure/purifier) but their hearts did not understand his bhōjñatā (most enjoyable nature). [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying “Instead of becoming mesmerized in the divine posture of emperumān holding the cakram in his hand, they simply hold him as the one who purifies them”.
- *maṟaviyai inṟi* *manattu vaippārē* – without forgetting, they will meditate upon him. For [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/), when he sees the beautiful form of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) with his cakram, he does not remember the first line (where its explained that emperumān is the one who relieves us from samsāram). [tirumangai āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/thirumangai-azhwar/) too said in periya tirumoḻi 10.10.9 “*āḻiyodum ponnār sārngamudaiya adigaḷai innār enṟu aṟiyēn*” (I don’t recognize this master \[of mine\] who has the cakram and golden bow in his hands) – [āḻvārs](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/azhwars/) become bewildered seeing [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s beautiful form. If his divine form can even make his devotees forget the good aspects (real identity etc), how come it does not make these kaivalyārttis forget the bad aspect (their attachment to self enjoyment)? They will pursue him (meditate upon him) for self-enjoyment even after seeing his divine form. In case of upāsakar (bhakti yōga niśtar), the same is explained as – even after experiencing his most enjoyable nature, how they are staying steady instead of losing their consciousness – they are pretty strong-hearted.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.7.2. Vaippam maruntam

*vaippu ām marundu ām adiyarai valvinait tuppu ām pulan aindum tunjak kodān avan eppāl evarkku(m) nalattāl uyarndu uyarndu appālavan engaḷ āyar koḻundē*

**Пословный перевод:**

adiyarai – (bhagavān‘s distinctive) sēśabhūtar (servitors); val – popular; vinai – karmas; tuppām – capable; pulan aindum – senses (which control); tunjak kodān – one who does not let them perish; vaippām – being the wealth (that is their puruśārttam \[goal\]); marundām – medicine (that is the means to remove the obstacles to accomplish that goal); eppāl – all places (starting from ānandam of humans up to brahmā); evarkkum – all cētanas (jīvātmās); nalattāl – bliss; uyarndu uyarndu – in large quantity; appāl avan – unreachable (for the words and mind); engaḷ – being for us (who are fully for him) alone; āyar – (ignorant) cow-herd clan; koḻundu – leader

**Перевод:**

**bhagavān is the wealth (that is the goal) and the medicine (that removes the obstacles in attaining the goal) for his servitors and he protects them from being perished by being caught in the powerful senses which are controlled by the popular karmas (puṇyam and pāpam). How is that? Though his bliss is unreachable by words/mind compared to all jīvātmās in all places, he became the leader of our cow-herd clan (to protect us).**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*Further, āḻvār explains emperumān‘s affection towards those who have surrendered unto him and accepted his divine feet as the ultimate goal.*

[āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) being much greater than dēvatās starting with brahmā et al with respect to his auspicious qualities such as ānandam (bliss) etc., took birth in the clan of his devotees, and removes their obstacles which stop them from being with him by being their wealth and medicine.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In second pāsuram, āḻvār mercifully explains emperumān‘s attitude towards ananyaprayōjanar (ones who expect nothing other than kainkaryam towards him).*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār tells that emperumān is very blissful towards those special individuals who accept emperumān only as the ultimate goal and emperumān only as the means to attain him.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

*āyar koḻundu* – the main person in the cow-herd clan. Just like [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is happy to be the primary deity among the dēvatās starting with brahmā, he is also happy to be the primary cow-herd boy among the cow-herd clan. In indiscipline etc., he is the leader among cow-herd boys.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Second pāsuram – In the first pāsuram, āḻvār censured those kēvalar who surrendered to emperumān but left after fulfilling their goal of self-enjoyment; in this pāsuram, āḻvār explains emperumān’s attitude towards those who are fully surrendered to him. வைப்பு ஆம் மருந்து ஆம் அடியரை வல்வினைத் துப்பு ஆம் புலன் ஐந்தும் துஞ்சக் கொடான் அவன் எப்பால் எவர்க்கும் நலத்தால் உயர்ந்து உயர்ந்து அப்பாலவன் எங்கள் ஆயர் கொழுந்தே vaippu Am marundu Am adiyarai valvinait tuppu Am pulan aindum tunjak kodān avan eppāl evarkku(m) nalattāl uyarndu uyarndu appālavan engaḷ āyar koḻundē*

- *vaippām* – Just like having some money in a leather pouch which is prepared by taking the skin of a goat and keeping it safely in our waist, that can be used as we desire, [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) too becomes submissive towards his devotees so that they can enjoy him as they please – this explains “prāpyatvam” (being the goal) of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/).
- *marundām* – Still, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is the greatest of all, makes himself available for the bound souls. In such a case, how can they enjoy him? [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) himself removes the hurdles which stop them from enjoying him and gives them the ability to enjoy him – this explains the “prāpakatvam” (being the means) of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/).

For whom is he the prāpakam (means) and prāpyam (goal)?

- *adiyarai* – those who have eliminated the thought of “*na namēyam*” (I will not worship srī rāma – srī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 36.11)
- *valvinait tuppām tunjak kodān avan* – For those who approach him and exist for him alone, instead of leaving him after getting ulterior benefits; he protects them from the senses which could finish them off (by engaging them in worldly pleasures). tuppu – sāmartyam (ability).

Where did he do this?

- *eppāl …* – Greatness is present based on the place of existence and the species; svargam \[heaven\] is different from bhūmi \[earth\]; dēvas \[celestial entities\] are different from manuśyas (humans);  eppāl – in all these places; pāl means place in tamiḻ as in “appāl” (there), “ippāl” (here); evarkku – all entities; “eppāl evarkkum” means everywhere, everyone.
- *nalattāl uyarndu uyarndu* – As explained in taittiriya upaniśat ānanda valli “*yatō vācō nivarttantē*” – even by increasing the bliss 100 folds at each level (humans, dēvas … brahmā), the bliss (among other qualities) of [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) cannot be comprehended. That is why he is explained in taittiriya upaniśat as “*ānandamaya:*” (filled with abundance of bliss).
- *engaḷ āyar koḻundē* – supreme person taking birth as one among the cow-herd boys – is this to give up on his devotees? \[No – it is to uplift them\]. Did he experience sorrow, bewilderment etc., (in avatārams) to let his devotees go through sorrow, bewilderment etc? \[No – it is to free them from such sufferings\]. The ultimate supreme being, becoming ultimately ignorant cow-herd boy – was this to let his devotees perish? \[No – it is to help them\].
- *engaḷ* – **our** – couple of explanations:
   - [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) cherishes his relationship with the residents of the place where kriṣṇa was born (by saying “leader of **our** cow-herd clan”\].
   - avatārams are for the devotees. Though his stealing butter etc., have already happened, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) previously said “[ettiṟam](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/06/thiruvaimozhi-1-3-1-paththudai-adiyavar/)” and fainted. Similarly, here too, āḻvār is saying kriṣṇāvatāram is for him only.
- *āyar koḻundu* – the primary in the cow-herd clan. Such [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) will protect his devotees.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.7.3. Ayar kolunday

*āyar koḻundāy avarāl pudaiyuṇṇum māyap pirānai en māṇikkac cōtiyai tūya amudaip parugip parugi en māyap piṟavi mayarvu aṟuttēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

āyar – for the cow-herd boys; koḻundāy – being the leader; avarāl – (for stealing butter etc) by those; pudaiyuṇṇum – beaten; māyap pirānai – performing amazing acts (such as crying due to being beaten etc) and giving them joy; en māṇikkac cōtiyai – one who presented his (well polished) carbuncle-like radiantly shining form (due to his being submissive towards cow-herd boys) for me; tūya amudai – pure nectar (which is not mixed with supremacy and only presenting simplicity); parugip parugi – eternally enjoying; en – (just like for the one who drinks milk as a medicine will be cured of indigestion) my; māyam – that which is caused by prakruti; piṟavi – due to the birth; mayarvu – ignorance; aṟuttēn – finished

**Перевод:**

**Being the leader of the cow-herd boys, he got beaten by them (for stealing butter etc) and performed amazing acts (like crying like a helpless child after getting beaten) and thus presented his carbuncle-like radiantly shining form to me. By eternally enjoying that pure nectar (which is not mixed with even a tinge of supremacy), I eliminated my ignorance that was due to my birth (in this material realm) which was caused by prakruti (material activities etc).**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In third pāsuram – āḻvār says that while sweetly enjoying emperumān, his sorrows of this samsāram vanished.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says the humility shown by emperumān towards his devotees in his avatārams is more enjoyable than the bliss enjoyed with paramapadanātan.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. āḻvār says “I did not surrender unto him seeking ulterior benefits; I did not surrender unto him for eternal kainkaryam; I desired to enjoy him seeing his sweet nature; the hurdles got eliminated themselves”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Third pāsuram – āḻvār censured kēvalars who seek out self-enjoyment (in the first pāsuram); he explained the attitude of bhagavān towards his pure devotees (in the second pāsuram); When asked which category he belongs to, āḻvār replies “I am not a prayōjanāntaraparan (one who seeks out ulterior benefits); I cannot be clearly identified as ananyaprayōjanan (one who purely desires kainkaryam); I simply enjoyed him and he eliminated my hurdles”. ஆயர் கொழுந்தாய் அவரால் புடையுண்ணும் மாயப் பிரானை என் மாணிக்கச் சோதியை தூய அமுதைப் பருகிப் பருகி என் மாயப் பிறவி மயர்வு அறுத்தேனே āyar koḻundāy avarāl pudaiyuṇṇum māyap pirānai en māṇikkac cōtiyai tūya amudaip parugip parugi en māyap piṟavi mayarvu aṟuttēnē*

- *āyar koḻundāy* – Previously, his primary nature among the cow-herds was explained; here his being the singular focus is explained, i.e., they are the root and he is the tender leaf – when the cow-herd boys graze the cows in the forest and become tired, kaṇṇan [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s face will show the fatigue, just like when the root lacks water, the leaf will reflect that.
- *avarāl pudaiyuṇṇum* – being beaten by them – irrespective of being men or women, all of them beat kriṣṇa – all the men and women of the five lakh families of āyarpādi (gōkulam) had so much control over him. As [bhattar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/parasara-bhattar/) says “they used to beat kaṇṇan using the churning staff, casually”.
- *māyap pirānai* – [sarvēsvaran](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) who is avāpta samastakāman (having no unfulfilled desires), born in the cow-herd clan as if he is missing something, unable to sustain himself without that (butter) which was touched by his devotees, stealing it since that was not readily given to him, unable to complete the task properly, being caught red-handed and being beaten – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) meditates on this and becomes amazed at [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s qualities.
- *en māṇikkac cōtiyai* – Just a like a carbuncle shines more with more polishing, the more he gets beaten, more his glories become multi-fold.
- *en* – the one who gave me that radiance as full fledged meals (full enjoyment).
- *tūya dparugip parugi* – that nectar churned out of kśīrābdi (milk-ocean) for dēvas was restricted to dēvas and was given only once. This nectar ([bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)) is consumable by all as many times as they desire.
- *en māyap piṟavi mayarvu aṟuttēnē* – I eliminated the ignorance (with the impressions) that came out of amazing birth – birth is amazing because it is different for different persons (and even for the same person in different births).
- *mayarvaṟuttēnē* – Because he is the one who is enjoying the results as said in tiruviruttam 1 “*inninṟa nīrmai ini yām uṟāmai*” (I am unable to bear this life in samsāram) , he says he eliminated them.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.7.4. Mayarvu ara

*mayarvu aṟa en manattē manninān tannai uyarvinaiyē tarum oṇ sudark kaṟṟaiyai ayarvu il amarargaḷ ādik koḻundai en isaivinai en solli yān viduvēnō?*

**Пословный перевод:**

mayarvu – ignorance; aṟa – to remove; en manattē – into my heart/mind; manninān tannai – residing eternally; uyarvinaiyē – increasing my jñānam, bhakti etc; tarum – one who gives; oṇ – being infinitely enjoyable; sudark kaṟṟaiyai – having a radiantly shining form; ayarvu – forgetfulness; il – not having; amarargaḷ – for the nitya sūris; ādik koḻundai – being the leader (who sustains them etc); en isaivinai – one who has full control over my acceptance (to approach him); en solli – what reason can I say; yān – me (who knows about him); viduvēn – give up

**Перевод:**

**What reason can I say to leave emperumān who is residing in my heart removing my ignorance, who bestowed me increase in my knowledge, devotion etc., who has a radiantly shining form, who is the leader of nityasūris who do not have forgetfulness etc., and thus sustaining them and who controls my mind in accepting him also?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*āḻvār says that there is no termination of his communion with emperumān in any manner.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In fourth pāsuram – āḻvār says that he does not have any reason to give up the association of mahōpakārakan (the one who has done great favours) who convinced āḻvār by showing his divine form/nature and mingled with āḻvār like he would mingle with nityasūris.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says there is no reason to give up on emperumān who is enjoyable.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*Fourth pāsuram – See nanjīyar”s introduction. Because, previously he said “ayōjñan” (unqualified) and shied away from emperumān, now he is saying “ini vidēn” (I won’t leave him any more).*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Fourth pāsuram – Some ask āḻvār – First you said in tiruviruttam 1 “inninṟa nīrmai ini yām uṟāmai” (I cannot bear this samsāram \[material life\] any more) and your desire was fulfilled (in arumpadam, previous pāsuram “māyap piṟavi mayarvaṟuttēnē” \[I eliminated any further births in this samsāram\] is highlighted). Should you not stay calm/relaxed (let him go free now and hold on to him later) now? āḻvār replies “How can I give up on him?”. மயர்வு அற என் மனத்தே மன்னினான் தன்னை உயர்வினையே தரும் ஒண் சுடர்க் கற்றையை அயர்வு இல் அமரர்கள் ஆதிக் கொழுந்தை என் இசைவினை என் சொல்லி யான் விடுவேனோ? mayarvu aṟa en manattē manninān tannai uyarvinaiyē tarum oṇ sudark kaṟṟaiyai ayarvu il amarargaḷ ādik koḻundai en isaivinai en solli yān viduvēnō?*

- *mayarvu aṟa* – eliminating ajñānam (ignorance) along with its vāsanā (impressions)
- *en manattē manninān tannai* – to prevent ignorance entering my mind, he entered in my heart and positioned himself like an immovable plant/tree. Just like an emperor will not leave his main centres of the kingdom, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) stays in my heart as if there is no other place to stay for him.

Being situated there, what does he do?

- *uyarvinaiyē tarum* – he will bestow me jñānam (knowledge), visramba (confidence/conviction) and bhakti (devotion). Also explained as – he gives such greatness to even walk on the heads of yama darmarāja et al.
- *tarum* – not satisfied with giving once, he will be giving eternally. Many pāsurams are quoted to establish that [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) gives great devotion to [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) – tiruvāimoḻi 5.3.4 “*kādal kadal puraiya*” (so much love like an ocean), tiruvāimoḻi 7.3.6 “*kādal kadalin migap peridāl*” (āḻvār’s love towards [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is bigger than ocean), tiruvāimoḻi 7.3.8 “*nīḷ visumbum kaḻiyap peridāl*” (my love for emperumān is greater than the space which accommodates all of material creation), tiruvāimoḻi 10.10.10 “*sūzndadanil periya*” (greater than all 3 tatvams – [cit](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/), [acit](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/09/thathva-thrayam-achith-what-is-matter/) and [īsvara](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)) \[This also shows the progressive development of āḻvār’s devotion/love towards [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)\].
- *oṇ sudark kaṟṟaiyai* – showing great radiance by doing this (bestowing knowledge etc) and thinking that I ([āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)) helped him ([emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)) instead of his helping me. it can also be explained as āḻvār revealing the beauty of emperumān which attracted him. This is similar to srīviṣṇu purāṇam 1.9.63 “*tējasām rāsimūrjitam*” (one who shines like collection of radiant rays and who has the valour to demolish his enemies).

Such [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who helped me as if its a favour to himself – does he not have anyone who would enjoy him?

- *ayarvil amarargaḷ ādik koḻundai* – there is abundant number of persons (nityasūris) who cannot sustain themselves, when [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) does not show his favours (mercy). bhagavān is the one who sustains nityasūris who cannot ever forget him for even a moment and undoubtedly enjoy him all the time.
- *en isaivinai* – he himself entered my heart and ensured that I will not leave him saying I am unqualified.
- *en solli yān viduvēnō* – Why should I leave him?
   - Should I leave him saying there is a little bit of ignorance left? (*mayarvaṟa*)
   - Should I leave him since he eliminated my ignorance, yet stayed away from me? (*en manattē manninan*)
   - Should I leave him since he did not continue to bestow good things? (*uyarvinaiyē tarum*)
   - Should I leave him since he expected some thing back from me for his favours? (*oṇ sudark kaṟṟaiyai – explaining this as auspicious quality*)
   - Should I leave him since he does not have physical beauty? (*oṇ sudark kaṟṟaiyai – explaining this as physical form*)
   - Should I leave him since he does not have enough supremacy? (*ayarvil amarargaḷ ādik kozundai*)
   - Should I leave him since I attained him out of my own efforts? (*en isaivinai*)

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.7.5. Viduveno en vilakkai

*viduvēnō en viḷakkai en āviyai naduvē vandu uyyak koḷginṟa nādanai toduvē seydu iḷa āycciyar kaṇṇinuḷ vidavē seydu viḻikkum pirānaiyē?*

**Пословный перевод:**

en viḷakkai – One who lights up the lamp of knowledge which makes me understand the nature of my true self; en āviyai – my soul; naduvē – in-between; vandu – entered (seeing the right time/opportunity); uyyak koḷginṟa – uplifting me (so I don’t perish); nādanai – being the master; toduvē – mischievous pastimes; seydu – performed; iḷam – having youthful state (which is not qualified to be used by anyone); āycciyar – cow-herd girls’; kaṇṇinuḷ – inside \[their\] eyes; vidavē seydu – engaged in cunning/subtle acts (which are known to kriṣṇa and gōpis only); viḻikkum – glancing/meeting of eyes; pirānai – the one who gives favours; viduvēnō – can I leave him?

**Перевод:**

**How can I leave emperumān who is the one who lights my true knowledge, who entered my soul at the opportune time to uplift me, who is the one performing favours such as the mischievous pastimes with the youthful cow-herd girls by exchanging subtle glances, etc, with them \[and there by attracting them to be totally dependent on him\]?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In fifth pāsuram – āḻvār asks “How can I leave emperumān who attracted me through his causeless mercy by showing his beautiful divine eyes just like he did with the cow-herd girls even though I was ignorant about him and was attached to matters other than him?”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says that after knowing about the favours done by emperumān to him, he cannot leave him.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Fifth pāsuram – āḻvār says that he will leave emperumān when the gōpis of āyarpādi (gōkulam) will give up kriṣṇa and desire for paramapadam \[which does not happen – they are so attached to kriṣṇa only\]. விடுவேனோ என் விளக்கை என் ஆவியை நடுவே வந்து உய்யக் கொள்கின்ற நாதனை தொடுவே செய்து இள ஆய்ச்சியர் கண்ணினுள் விடவே செய்து விழிக்கும் பிரானையே? viduvēnō en viḷakkai en āviyai naduvē vandu uyyak koḷginṟa nādanai toduvē seydu iḷa āycciyar kaṇṇinuḷ vidavē seydu viḻikkum pirānaiyē?*

- *viduvēnō en viḷakkai* – [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/), due to his causeless mercy, who revealed his true nature, forms, qualities and wealth to remove my ignorance about my own self. Why is he saying “*en viḷakkai*” (my lamp)? Would he not shine for others and remove their ignorance? No one has attachment towards [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) like [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) has. Only when there is attachment, [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) will shine. *viḷakku* (lamp) is that which shows itself as well as other things – bhagavān too showed him para svarūpam (nature of bhagavān), svasvarūpam (nature of [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) – [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) who is subservient to [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)) and virōdi svarūpam (nature of the obstacles) \[In arumpadam, it is explained that this highlights arta pancakam – by explaining para svarūpam – upāya svarūpam (he, being the means) is also explained and by explaining svasvarūpam – kainkaryam (service as the goal) is also explained\].
- *ennāviyai …* – my soul (me) which neither realised the existence of the self nor has attachment towards [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/).
- *naduvē vandu* – arriving without any reason (causeless mercy). Though I was running behind worldly pleasures, he came to my rescue.
- *uyyakkoḷginṟa* – he does not give up after accepting me, he nurtures me. As explained in taittiriya upaniśat, ānandavalli, previously I was in the state of “*asannēva sa bhavati*” \[as good as non-existing\] and transformed as in “*santamēnam tatō vidu:*” (due to knowing brahmam, others know him to be existing).

[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) asks [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/), “You told ‘*en āvi*‘ (my ātmā), why should I uplift your ātmā?”.

- *nādanai* – Whose property is being destroyed here? Is there anything like “me”? Because you are the owner, you uplifted me.

When asked “Why should anyone try for the benefit of someone else?”, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says “who tried for the uplifting of the cow-herd girls in āyarpādi?”.

- *toduvē seydu* – Steals etc., and gets caught intentionally so that many girls (who got affected by him) will come and see him get caught.
- *iḷa āycciyar* – By saying *āycciyar* (cow-herd girls), [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) differentiates them from men; By saying *iḷavāycciyar* (young cow-herd girls), [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) differentiates them from older-women. Men can protect themselves and older-women are protected by their children \[young girls are helpless and thus protected by kriṣṇa himself\]. Also men and older-women have less attachment towards kriṣṇa in comparison to the young cow-herd girls of āyarpādi.
- *kaṇṇinuḷ vidavē seydu viḻikkum* – glancing at the girls which can only be understood by them. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) himself says in tiruvāimoḻi 9.10.9 “*tūdu sey kaṇgaḷ*” (eyes which can transmit messages).
- *pirānaiyē* – just like he mesmerized those girls and made them to be totally surrendered to him, he did the same to me. How can I leave him?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.
