## 1.7.6. Piran perunilam

*pirā an peru nilam kīṇḍavan piunnum virā ay malart tuḻāy vēynda mudiyan marāmaram eyda māyavan ennuḷ irān enil pinnai yān ottuvēnō?*

**Пословный перевод:**

pirān – being a upakāraka (benefactor); peru nilam – great earth; kīṇḍavan – one who dug it up; pinnum – combined (prepared as a garland); virāy – mixed; malar – with flowers; tuḻāy – using tuḷasi leaves; vēynda – covered fully; mudiyan – one who has a crown; marāmaram eyda – shot the peepal tree (to instill confidence in sugrīva mahārāja); māyavan – amazing personality; en – my; uḷ – in the heart; irān enil – when he would not stay; pinnai – subsequently; yān – me (who cannot sustain without him); ottuvēnō – will I allow? will I sustain (being separated)?

**Перевод:**

**When emperumān, being the benefactor, who lifted the earth, whose crown is covered with tuḷasi leaves mixed with flowers, who amazingly shot down the peepal tree, would not stay in my heart, subsequently, how will I allow him to leave?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In sixth pāsuram – When asked “what if he himself wants to leave?” āḻvār replies “Will I let him (who showed his divine activities, won over me and mingled with me) leave?”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says that even if emperumān tries to leave, āḻvār will not accept that.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Sixth pāsuram – In the previous pāsuram, when asked “Though you are saying you won’t leave him now, you are the same one who tried to leave him before – how can we believe you?” āḻvār replied “being acknowledge by him, how will I leave him?” In this pāsuram, some people ask “What if he leaves you?” and āḻvār replies “he showed his \[divine\] qualities and activities, won over me and mingled with me. How will I allow him to leave me?” பிரா அன் பெரு நிலம் கீண்டவன் பின்னும் விரா அய் மலர்த் துழாய் வேய்ந்த முடியன் மராமரம் எய்த மாயவன் என்னுள் இரான் எனில் பின்னை யான் ஒட்டுவேனோ? pirā an peru nilam kīṇḍavan piunnum virā ay malart tuḻāy vēynda mudiyan marāmaram eyda māyavan ennuḷ irān enil pinnai yān ottuvēnō?*

- *pirān* – Just like moon, soft-breeze and sandalwood, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) makes himself fully available for others.

[āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) recollects his help towards everyone as well as specifically towards his devotees which will be explained further.

- *peru nilam kīṇḍavan* – this is how he helped everyone. Just like [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) dug up earth from the causal ocean assuming a form (boar) that does not shy away from water and mud, he picked me up from this ocean of samsāram.
- *pinnum virāy malart tuḻāy vēynda mudiyan* – He jumped into the ocean \[in the form of boar\] with all decorations. Having  a crown covered with fresh tuḷasi garland which is closely knit with flowers, having abundance of fragrance.
- *marāmaram eyda māyavan* – this is how he helped his devotee. sugrīva, observing vāli’s valour and srī rāma’s tender nature, said “you can’t kill vāli” and srī rāma at once out of great attachment (towards his devotees) drew his bow and prepared to prove his capability.
- *ennuḷ irān enil* – If he, who pursues his devotees and works for their goal, does not wish to stay in my heart. “*enil*” –  \[since āḻvār says\] *even* if he \[emperumān\] wants to \[leave\], there is no reason for me to leave him.
- *pinnai yān ottuvēnō* – When he is prepared to leave in any case, why would I agree to his wish? Just like my karma pāratantriyam (being bound by karma), is there any imperfection in his āśrita pāratantriyam (being bound to his devotees)? When I don’t let him leave, can he leave? piḷḷān explains it  as “How can I sustain myself if I let him leave?”.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.7.7. Yan otti

*yān otti ennuḷ iruttuvam enrilan tān otti vandu en tani nenjai vanjittu ūn otti ninṟu en uyiril kalandu iyal vān ottumō ini ennai negiḻkkavē?*

**Пословный перевод:**

yān – I; otti – with acceptance; ennuḷ iruttuvam – will keep inside; enṟu ilan – did not think like that; tān – He; otti vantu – arrived with a vow; en – my; tani – independent; nenjai – heart; vanjittu – attracted without my knowing it; Un – in the body; otti – being together; ninṟu – entered and stayed; en uyiruḷ – in my ātmā; kalantu – mixed; iyalvān – (as if existing due to that) sustained himself; ini – now; ennai – me; negiḻkka – to leave; ottumō – is it possible?

**Перевод:**

**I did not think about keeping him inside my heart with acceptance, but he himself arrived with a vow and entered my independent heart attracting it without my knowing about that. He became mixed with me (the soul) and entered in my body and sustained himself. Now, is it possible for him to leave me?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the seventh pāsuram – āḻvār says “though I did not accept him, he himself accepted me at his lotus feet; in such case, even if I want to leave, he would not let me leave”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Seventh pāsuram – When asked “You are bound by the three types of qualities \[satvam, rajas, tamas\]; occasionally you are saying ‘I will not leave him’; can we trust your words?” āḻvār replies “Even if I leave him, he will not leave me”. யான் ஒட்டி என்னுள் இருத்துவன் என்றிலன் தான் ஒட்டி வந்து என் தனி நெஞ்சை வஞ்சித்து ஊன் ஒட்டி நின்று என் உயிரில் கலந்து இயல் வான் ஒட்டுமோ இனி என்னை நெகிழ்க்கவே? yān otti ennuḷ iruttuvam enrilan tān otti vandu en tani nenjai vanjittu Un otti ninṟu en uyiril kalandu iyal vān ottumō ini ennai negiḻkkavē?*

- *yān …* – Only if my acceptance \[of him to stay inside me\] was chosen by me, could I choose to let go of him. If [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) says “[āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)! I will stay with you” and [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) would say “No!” he simply vowed to be with āḻvār and entered his heart. āḻvār says “I did not request him to be in my heart”.
- *tān otti vandu* – Just as it is said in srī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 18.34 “*adyamē maraṇam vāpi taraṇam sāgarasya vā*” (Either I should cross the ocean or destroy the ocean), here too emperumān arrived with the vow to be with me. \[In arumpadam, a nice story is narrated to explain this aspect of emperumān forcefully accepting [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/). Once, there was a brāhmaṇa who was very miserly. Another brāhmaṇa was planning to go and ask him for food and the on-lookers warned him that he would not get anything. He said to them that somehow he will get some food. He went to the miserly brāhmaṇa’s house and asked him for even a little bit of food. The miserly brāhmaṇa refused to give even that. When this person persisted, the miserly brāhmaṇa said “ōK, I can give food, but unfortunately there is no plantain leaf to serve food on”. Hearing that, the guest brāhmaṇa said, “Here! I have a leaf, now you serve me food”. The miserly brāhmaṇa said “When coming to kill some one, would they not come with a knife?” and gave him food in the end. Like this, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) vowed to have [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) and pursued him voluntarily\].
- *en tani nenjai* – independent heart that cannot be reformed.
- *vanjittu* – showed his seela (simplicity) etc qualities and tamed my heart to be surrendered to him.

What did he do after that?

- *Un otti ninṟu en uyiril kalandu* – Some explained this as “mixing with my [self](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) which is together with the body”. [nanjīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nanjiyar/) mercifully explained this as “Just like a person would enjoy the impurities of his beloved, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) accepted my body, and once I did not push him away, he mixed with my self/soul”.
- *iyalvān* – one who has such benevolence as a natural quality; one who is prepared to pursue his devotees.
- *ottumō ini ennai negiḻkkavē* – Such [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who showered his grace on me unconditionally, even if I said ‘I want to leave’ would he let me go? After working so hard to give knowledge to me, and when the acquired knowledge started yielding result, if I said that I will leave, would he agree to that? \[No\].

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.7.8. Ennai negilkkilum

*ennai negiḻkkilum ennudai nan nenjam  tannai agalvikkat tānum killān ini pinnai nedum paṇait tōḷ magiḻ pīdu udai munnai amarar muḻu mudalānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ennai – me (who was bestowed with jñānam (knowledge), prēmam (love) by bhagavān himself and one who cannot look at anyone else); negiḻkkilum – push me aside; nal – well-wishing (captured by emperumān to be partial towards him); ennudai nenjam tannai – my heart; agalvikka – to separate from him; tānum – himself (who is sarvasakti (omnipotent)); ini killān – will not do it; pinnai – (he is) nappinnai pirātti’s \[nappinnai is an incarnation of nīḷā dēvi and is one of the foremost wives of kriṣṇa\]; nedum – wide; paṇai – well-rounded; tōḷ – being embraced with such shoulder; magiḻ – joyful; pīdu udai – having the greatness; munnai – ancient; amarar – nityasūris; muḻu – for their sustenance etc; mudalānē – isn’t he the only primary person?

**Перевод:**

**Even if I can be convinced to leave him, it will be impossible for he himself to separate from my heart which has become partial towards him. īsn’t he the leader of nityasūris, being the one who has the greatness of enjoying the embracing of the wide, well-rounded shoulder of nappinnai?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, When asked “What if such emperumān leaves you?”, āḻvār replies “Even if he wants to separate from me, he cannot separate my heart from him”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

- *pinnai nedum paṇait tōḷ magiḻ pīdu udai* – Similar to srī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 37.38 “apramēyam hi tattēja: yasya sā janakātmajā” (srī rāma who is with unbelievable radiance due to having janaka’s daughter on his side).

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Eighth pāsuram – Why should we say “I will leave him, he will leave me”? No, even if he wants to leave me, more than me, my heart which is fully captured by his auspicious qualities, cannot be separated from him, even if he himself tried. என்னை நெகிழ்க்கிலும் என்னுடை நன் நெஞ்சம் தன்னை அகல்விக்கத் தானும் கில்லான் இனி பின்னை நெடும் பணைத் தோள் மகிழ் பீடு உடை முன்னை அமரர் முழு முதல் தானே ennai negiḻkkilum ennudai nan nenjam  tannai agalvikkat tānum killān ini pinnai nedum paṇait tōḷ magiḻ pīdu udai munnai amarar muḻu mudalānē*

- *ennai negiḻkkilum* – It is very difficult to separate me (who has been bestowed with faultless knowledge/bhakti by [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) himself); even if he can do that,
- *ennudai nal nenjam tannai agalvikka* – How can he separate my heart which was immersed in him as explained in periya tiruvantādi 1 “*nenjē! iyaṟṟuvāy emmodu nī kūdi*” (Oh heart! being together with me, work with me) and in tiruvāimoḻi 1.1.1 “*toḻudu eḻu en mananē*” (Oh mind! worship and be uplifted)?
- *tānum killān* – He is sarvasakti (omnipotent), would he not be able to dispose of your heart? No, he cannot.

Did he not keep you in samsāram until now? Why would not he do that again?

- *ini* – No, he will not do that any more.

What is the reason for [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) saying “*ini*” confidently?

- *pinnai …* – How can [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) dispose of those who surrender unto him with the puruśakāram (recommendation) of nappinnai in the assembly of nityasūris (eternally liberated souls)?
- *pinnai nedum paṇait tōḷ magiḻ pīdu udai* – One whose glories are celebrated for embracing the wide, well-rounded and fresh bamboo like shoulder.
- *amarar muḻu mudalānē* – As explained in yajur vēdam accitram “*yatrarśaya: pratamajā yē purāṇā:*” (those nityasūris – the residents of paramapadam, ones who can visualize everything, ones who have no beginning and ones who have most enjoyable fresh forms though they are ancient), [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is the sustenance, activities etc for nityasūris.
- *tānum killān* – srī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 51.32 “…*haryarukhsagaṇa sannidau…*” (srī rāma vowed in the assembly of vānaras (monkeys) that he will destroy those who kidnapped sītā). When nappinnai’s puruśakāram is there, why would he dispose me of? \[Just like srī rāma protected sītā per his vow, he will protect me too\].

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.7.9. Amarar mulumudal

*amarar muḻu mudal āgiya ādiyai amararkku amudu īnda āyar koḻundai amara aḻumbat tuḻāvi en āvi amarat taḻuviṟṟu ini agalumō?*

**Пословный перевод:**

amarar – nityasūris’; muḻu – (svarūpa – true nature, stiti – existence, pravrutti – actions etc) all; mudalāgiya – have it as cause; ādiyai – being the primary/leader; amararkku – for the dēvas; amudu – nectar (which they desired for); īnda – one who gave; āyar – for the cow-herd boys (who were related to him); koḻundai – one who is the leader; en āvi – my ātmā (soul); amara – becoming fit (to be only existing for emperumān); aḻumba – mixing with him (to eliminate the hurdles such as svātantriyam (independence) etc); tuḻāvi – analysed (through many aspects such as svarūpam etc); amara – being together (without separation); taḻuviṟṟu – embraced him; ini agalumō – is there any scope for separation?

**Перевод:**

**Once my ātmā became fit to be fully existing for him after analysing many aspects and embraced emperumān, on whom nityasūris fully depend for their sustenance, existence, activities etc., who is the leader of such nityasūris, who gave the nectar to the dēvas and who is the leader of cow-herd clan, is there any question of separation?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In ninth pāsuram – āḻvār realizing the abundance of his communion with emperumān, says that there is no question of separation.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār asks “is there any reason for my ātmā to think about separation, after having communion with him in all possible ways?”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

- *āyar koḻundai* – [bhagavat gītā](http://githa.koyil.org/) 4.8 “*paritrāṇāya sādūnām …*” (Time after time, I descend to protect my devotees…).

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Ninth pāsuram – What is the reason for saying “tānum killān” (even he is not capable to leave me)? āḻvār asks “When emperumān and I look like a single entity, where is the question of separation?” அமரர் முழு முதல் ஆகிய ஆதியை அமரர்க்கு அமுது ஈந்த ஆயர் கொழுந்தை அமர அழும்பத் துழாவி என் ஆவி அமரத் தழுவிற்று இனி அகலும்மோ? amarar muḻu mudal āgiya ādiyai amararkku amudu īnda āyar koḻundai amara aḻumbat tuḻāvi en āvi amarat taḻuviṟṟu ini agalumō?*

- *amarar muḻu mudal āgiya* – nityasūris have [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) as the reason for their svarūpam, stiti etc.
- *ādiyai* – starting with this, leelā vibhūti (material realm) is explained. [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is the one who bestows the senses, body etc to even those are not fully devoted to him.
- *amararkku amudu īnda* – dēvas who accepted the senses/body which were given by him said “We don’t want you; just the salt-water (amudu-nectar) is enough” \[since this nectar only elongates the life-span for a longer duration in this material realm\] – for such dēvas too, he churned the milky ocean and gave the amrutam.
- *āyar koḻundai* – He descended as kriṣṇa to those who said they want [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) only and not the amrutam and gave himself to them.
- *amara …* – Approached such [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is with both spiritual realm and material realm, enjoyed him in several ways and mixed with him so much that it became difficult for me to distinguish myself from him.
- *ini agalumō* – Only when two entities are visible, could they be separated. Once prakāra (body) and prakāri (substratum) are understood as one, can they be separated? \[[bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is the substratum \[that which beholds everything\] and [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) is a body/attribute of [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)\]. Just like a form and its attributes are inseparable, when an entity ([jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)) becomes fully attached to another entity ([bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)), those also become inseparable.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.7.10. Agalil agalum

*agalil agalum aṇugil aṇugum pugalum ariyan poru allan emmān nigar il avan pugaḻ pādi iḷaippilam pagalum iravum padindu kudaindē*

**Пословный перевод:**

agalil – for those who leave him (after being fulfilled with ulterior benefits); agalum – he also will be interested in leaving them (since there is nothing more to do); aṇugil – for those who pursue him (without any other benefit); aṇugum – he will mix with those (just like water mixes with water); pugalum ariyan – (for those with ulterior motives) he is difficult to reach; poruvallan – (for those who want him alone) there are no obstacles to reach him; emmān – (for such auspicious quality) being my master; nigaril avan – (for such quality) having none comparable to him; pugaḻ – his glories; pagalum iravum – day and night without break; padindu – entered in me; kudaindu – mixing everywhere; pādi – singing (with love); iḷaippilam – never stops doing it (not taking rest at all)

**Перевод:**

**For those who leave him, he will leave them too; For those who pursue him, he will mix with them freely. He is difficult to reach (for those with ulterior motives) and (at the same time) there are no obstacles to reach him (for those who are surrendered to him). Being my master (for such great qualities), having none comparable to him and having entered in me mixing everywhere freely, I will sing his glories day and night without any break and will never get tired of doing that.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In tenth pāsuram – āḻvār says “Even if I enjoy the communion of emperumān with me forever, I will not be satisfied”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says that since enjoying such emperumān forever will not give full satisfaction, he cannot leave him.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. அகலில் அகலும் அணுகில் அணுகும் புகலும் அரியன் பொரு அல்லன் எம்மான் நிகர் இல் அவன் புகழ் பாடி இளைப்பு இலம் பகலும் இரவும் படிந்து குடைந்தே agalil agalum aṇugil aṇugum pugalum ariyan poru allan emmān nigar il avan pugaḻ pādi iḷaippilam pagalum iravum padindu kudaindē*

- *agalil agalum* – As seen in srī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 18.34 “*ānayainam harisrēśta dattamasyābhayam mayā \| vibhīśaṇō vā sugrīva yadi vā rāvaṇassvayam \|\|*” (Oh sugrīva, the best among monkeys! I give protection to vibhiśaṇa (who gave up his relatives);  Whether it is vibhīśaṇa or even rāvaṇa, bring him in front of me) – when the [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)s leave [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), he would feel sorry for them and leave them too with teary eyes. As said in srī rāmāyaṇam 36.11 “*dvidā bhajyēyamapyēvam na namēyam*” (even I am cut into two pieces, I will not worship him) – for those who say that to [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/), without any choice, he will destroy them too.
- *aṇugil aṇugum* – As seen in srī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 19.6 “*ākyāhi mama tatvēna rākśaānām balābalam*” (srī rāma requested vibiśaṇa to explain the strengths and weaknesses of rākśasa army), only when one takes a few steps towards [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), he starts discussing even most confidential matters with him. Here, srī rāma considered vibhīśaṇa as a descendant of ikśvāku vamsam instead of a rākśasa (just for him turning towards [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)). In this decad, the [first pāsuram](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/09/thiruvaimozhi-1-7-1-piravith-thuyar/) explains the meaning of “*agalil agalum*” and the [second pāsuram](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/09/thiruvaimozhi-1-7-2-vaippam-maruntham/) explains the meaning of “*aṇugil aṇugum*“.
- *pugalum ariyan* – When both arjuna and duryōdana approached him (before the battle), he gave himself to arjuna and pangaḷam (heap of chaff which remains after beating paddy – worthless aspects – his army) to duryōdana. So, for those who don’t enjoy him, he would be difficult to acquire.
- *poruvallan* – When devotees approach him, there are no obstacles. As seen in mahābhāratam udyōga parvam 49 “*yatra kruṣṇau ca kruṣṇā ca satyabhāmā ca bhāminī …*” (where kriṣṇa, arjuna, draupati and the beautiful satyabhāmā are (intimately) present, where even abhimanyu or nakula/sahādēva have not even gone – sanjaya (after seeing it) says to drudrāśtra), kaṇṇan [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) showed that divine vision (without any obstacles) to sanjaya (who is a pure-hearted devotee) which cannot be seen by one’s own sons.
- *emmān* – by showing these qualities, he transformed me to be totally existing for him only.
- *nigaril avan pugaḻ pādi iḷaippilam* – I have no reason to take a break from glorifying his incomparable auspicious qualities.

Is there any limit in when you would do that?

- *pagalum iravum* – day and night – always

Is it because you are enjoying him partially?

- *padindu kudaindē* – enjoy him in all manners deeply – still I am unable to stop enjoying him.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.7.11. Kudaindu vandunnum

*kudaindu vaṇḍu uṇṇum tuḻāy mudiyānai adainda ten kurukūrc catakōpan midainda sol todai āyirattu ip pattu udaindu nōygaḷai ōduvikkumē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vaṇḍu – beetle; kudaindu – submerged; uṇṇum – eating the honey; tuḻāy – tuḷasi; mudiyānai – sarvēsvaran who is having it on his head; adainda – (by all means) rich; then – most benevolent; kurukūrc catakōpan – nammāḻvār‘s; midainda – closely knit; sol – words; todai – having poetic meter; āyirattu ippattu – this decad among the thousand pāsurams of tiruvāimoḻi; nōygaḷai – great disease (of actions which are result of ahankāra, wealth, lust); udaindu – breaking them; ōduvikkum – will make them leave instantaneously

**Перевод:**

**emperumān‘s divine head is decorated with closely placed tuḷasi leaves that are filled with honey in which beetles are submerged while drinking it. The most benevolent nammāḻvār who is from āḻvārtirunagari  glorified such emperumān in this decad which is among the thousand pāsurams of tiruvāimoḻi which are compiled with beautiful words and poetic meter. Such decad will eradicate the great disease of samsāram after breaking it into pieces.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the end – āḻvār says that this decad will eradicate all the difficulties which are obstacles for bhakti.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār explains removal of the great disease of samsāram (material life) as the result of this decad.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*In the end – āḻvār says that this decad will eradicate the attachment for ulterior benefits which are obstacles for experiencing bhagavān.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Similar to nanjīyar‘s introduction. குடைந்து வண்டு உண்ணும் துழாய் முடியானை அடைந்த தென் குருகூர்ச் சடகோபன் மிடைந்த சொல் தொடை ஆயிரத்து இப் பத்து உடைந்து நோய்களை ஓடுவிக்குமே kudaindu vaṇḍu uṇṇum tuḻāy mudiyānai adainda then kurukūrc catakōpan midainda sol todai āyirattu ip pattu udaindu nōygaḷai ōduvikkumē*

- *kudaindu vaṇḍuṇṇum tuḻāy mudiyānai* – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is wearing divine crown which is decorated with tuḷasi garland – the beetles which entered the garland seeking honey (like delving into an ocean), happily consumed the honey and even after all the honey was extracted, stay there not wishing to leave. Such [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is glorified here.
- *adainda tenkurukūrc catakōpan* – Just like those beetles were unable to back out of the honey in tuḷasi leaves, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is unable to withdraw from enjoying [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/). Such āḻvār mercifully compiled this decad.
- *midainda sol todai āyirattu ippattu* – Though the pāsurams are an outpouring of overflowing emotions of [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/), the words too want to participate in the service and request āḻvār to use them in his pāsurams.  For those who can recite this decad among the thousand pāsurams, their sins which make them think aisvaryam (wealth – worldly pleasures), kaivalyam (self-enjoyment) as the goal, will scoot.
- *nōygaḷai udaindu ōduvikkum* – Even while (the effect of) those sins leave him – they won’t leave as a whole. They will be broken into pieces and driven out as explained in periya tirumoḻi 8.10.7 “*vaḷḷalē! un tamarkku enṟum naman tamar kaḷḷar pōl*” (Oh most benevolent! for your devotees, yama darmarāja’s assistants are like totally unwanted \[they won’t even approach them\]).

Final summary from nampiḷḷai:

- In the first pāsuram, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) censured the kēvalar \[those desiring for self-enjoyment\].
- In the second pāsuram, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) explained the attitude of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) towards those who are fully existing for him.
- In the third pāsuram, when asked “Of these two categories, which one do you belong to?”, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) replied “I just enjoyed you and my obstacles got removed”.
- In the fourth pāsuram, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) asked “What reason can I give to leave [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who transformed me like this?”.
- In the fifth pāsuram, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) said “when the gōpis of āyarpādi leave [kriṣṇa](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), I will leave him”.
- In the sixth pāsuram, when asked “What if he leaves?”, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) replied “I will not allow that”.
- In the seventh pāsuram, when asked “What if you leave him?”, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) replied “He will not let me leave him”.
- In the eighth pāsuram, when asked “did he not let you be separated from him in samsāram until now?”, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) replied “now that I have approached him with nappinnai pirātti’s \[nīḷā dēvi’s\] recommendation, even he himself cannot leave me”.
- In the ninth pāsuram, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) said “why does this question \[of leaving him\] even arise? Once we have mixed together, it will be impossible to separate us”.
- In the tenth pāsuram, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) said “I will eternally enjoy the auspicious qualities and will not become tired”.
- Finally, he explains the result for those who practices this decad.

Thus ends the English translation for tiruvāimoḻi 1st centum 7th decad.

[emperumānār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/emperumanar/) tiruvadigaḷē caraṇam  
[piḷḷān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/pillan/) tiruvadigaḷē caraṇam  
[nanjīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nanjiyar/) tiruvadigaḷē caraṇam  
[nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/) tiruvadigaḷē caraṇam  
[vadakkut tiruvīdip piḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadakku-thiruvidhi-pillai/) tiruvadigaḷē caraṇam  
[periyavāccān piḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/periyavachchan-pillai/) tiruvadigaḷē caraṇam

[jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/mamunigal/) tiruvadigaḷē caraṇam

## 1.8 Odum pulleri

## 1.8.1. Odum pulleri

*ōdum puḷ ēṟi sūdum taṇ tuḻāy nīdu ninṟu avai ādum ammānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ammān – nirupādika svāmy (unconditional master); puḷ ēṟi – climbing on periya tiruvadi (garudāḻvār) fulfilling his desire (to carry emperumān); ōdum – wander around; taṇ – cool (stress-busting); tuḻāy – tiruttuḻāy (tuḷasi); sūdum – wearing (on his divine limbs maintaining the freshness of tuḷasi); nīdu ninṟu avai – with those entities which will live eternally; ādum – be joyfully engaged

**Перевод:**

**bhagavān, the unconditional master (of all), climbing on garudāḻvār vandesr around (fulfilling garuda’s desire to serve him), wearing cool tuḷasi garland and joyfully engaging with those entities who are eternal.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In first pāsuram – āḻvār talks about emperumān bonding with nityasiddas (nityasūris – eternally free souls in paramapadam).*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*First pāsuram – this pāsuram explains emperumān‘s sincere engagement with the residents of paramapadam. There is no lack of sincerity in nityasūris \[so, where is the question of emperumān having to deal with them sincerely?\] – but still, since they are many with each one having different desires/tastes, emperumān understands their desire and engages with them per that desire – this is where his ārjavam (sincerity/honesty) is manifested. ஓடும் புள் ஏறி சூடும் தண் துழாய் நீடு நின்றவை ஆடும் அம்மானே ōdum puḷ ēṟi sūdum taṇ tuḻāy nīdu ninṟu avai ādum ammānē*

- *ōdum puḷḷēṟi* – “*puḷḷēṟi ōdum” –* climb the bird (garudāḻvār) and wander around; \[arumpadam – would it not be a pain to carry some one?\] Just like the queen would enjoy the touch of the king on her bosom, garudāḻvār desires [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) climbing and riding on him. Him climbing garudāḻvār solves two purposes – to bless the residents of paramapadam with that divine darśan and to fulfil the nature (servitude) of garudāḻvār. [āḷavandār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/alavandhar/) highlights in stōtra ratnam 41 “*tvadangri sammartdakiṇāngasōbhinā*” \[shining radiantly due to the scars which were received by the pressing of [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s divine feet\] – just like a kāmini (beloved) sustains herself by seeing the love-marks on her body, garudāḻvār sustains himself by the scars from the divine feet of [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/).
- *sūdum taṇ tuḷāy* – Wearing fresh tuḷasi where the freshness will be lost even if there is a slight delay by [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) (out of tuḷasi’s anxiety on not being able to serve [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)) . Do they (garudāḻvār (bird), tuḷasi (leaves) etc) have consciousness? Yes – as explained in pauśkara samhitā “…*cinmayais svaprakāsaisca…*” ([bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is with flower garlands, pearl necklaces, clothes etc which have knowledge/consciousness, which are self-luminous etc and are increasing the radiance to each other) – some cētanas assume the form of garudāḻvār, tuḷasi etc., as required for [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s sport/pleasure. But then, should these not have the quality of ignorance (not-so-developed intelligence, ) etc which are seen in these species? No, these are like the hunch-backs, dwarfs etc who are seen in a king’s court (for his joy). In the spiritual realm, all forms are assumed by [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)s based on desire and not based on karma as in material realm. In samsāram (this material realm), plant/animal forms are due to one’s karma \[In arumpadam, famous verse “*vācikai: pakśimrugatām mānasairantyajātitām \| sarīrajai: karmadōśair yāti stāvaratām nara:*” is quoted – A human being  who commits offence/sins through words will be born as birds/animals (their speech will be curtailed); those who commit sins through mind will be born as lowly beings (their purity in mind will be curtailed); those who commit offence/sins through body will be born as plants (their physical movement will be curtailed)\] but in paramapadam (the spiritual realm), all forms are based on the desire (of the [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)s who are there). Only samsāris (bound souls in this material realm) have differences in desires and dishonesty. For nityasūris, since the goal is only to serve [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), there is no difference in desires and no dishonesty. Why then is there a need to specifically say that [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) deals with them honestly/sincerely? Though everyone’s goal is to serve bhagavān, since bhagavān has different activities/manifestations, the tastes will be different for different individuals in spiritual realm.
- *nīdu ninṟu* – Only when something happens due to karma, its temporary. Since these engagements (in paramapadam etc) are befitting the nature of [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) and [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)s, they will be permanent – eternal. [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) cannot sustain himself without them and they cannot sustain themselves without him.
- *avai* – Since, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) said “*puḷ*” and “*tuḻāy*” before, he is now saying “*avai*” (indicating insentients – plural).
- *ādum* – Instead of saying [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) will engage with them, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying they will enjoy him sportingly – just like a very tired/thirsty person jumps into a cool pond and enjoys it, all of them will be immersed in enjoying bhagavān.
- *ammānē* – Though, he is the master for all irrespective of one being nityasūri (eternally free soul) or nityasamsāri (bound soul), he still engages with them like this.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.8.2. Ammanay

*ammānāyp pinnum em māṇbum ānān vem mā vāy kīṇḍa sem mā kaṇṇanē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ammānāy – being sarvasmātaparan (supreme compared to everyone else) svāmi (master); vem – harsh/fierce; mā – horse; vāy – mouth; kīṇḍa – tore; sem – reddish; mā – big; kaṇṇan – kriṣṇa who has such (reddish big) eyes; pinnum – further, not stopping with that; emmāṇbum ānān – became great; became beautiful in various avatārams

**Перевод:**

**Being the supreme master, kriṣṇa who has reddish big eyes, tore the mouth of the harsh/fierce horse and further acquired greatness/beauty in various avatārams. māṇbu – It can also be explained that in kriṣṇāvatāram, he manifested most enjoyable activities.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In second pāsuram, āḻvār mercifully explains emperumān‘s bonding with  his devotees in this samsāram (material realm).*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār mercifully explains the speciality of avatārams \[incarnations\] which are aimed at bonding with his devotees in this leelā vibhūti (material realm).*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

- *māṇbu* – beauty in avatārams is multifold compared to paratvam (in paramapadam) – In yajur vēdam it is seen “…*sa u srēyān bhavati jāyamāna:*” (…that [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) takes birth. After taking birth, he acquires great radiance).

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Second pāsuram – this pāsuram explains how emperumān descends from nitya vibhūti (spiritual realm) into this leelā vibhūti (material realm), eliminates the enemies of the residents and bonds with them sincerely. அம்மானாய்ப் பின்னும் எம் மாண்பும் ஆனான் வெம் மா வாய் கீண்ட செம் மா கண்ணனே ammānāyp pinnum em māṇbum ānān vem mā vāy kīṇḍa sem mā kaṇṇanē*

- *ammānāy* – thus being the supreme person
- *vemmā vāy kīṇḍa semmā kaṇṇan pinnum emmāṇbum ānān* – there was a fierce animal – kēsi the horse; the one who tore its mouth. When kēsi appeared with an open mouth in front of kaṇṇan [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), srī nārada bhagavān seav that, became frightened and fell unconscious screaming  “*jagadastamitam*” (the world is coming to an end). The fear nārada bhagavān went through at that time, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) goes through the same just by remembering that incident.
- *semmā kaṇṇanē* – kriṣṇa who is having the eyes which have blossomed big and habe become reddish on the joy of destroying the enemy.
- *pinnum emmāṇbum ānān* – Not just stopping with that avatāram, he assumed many other avatārms as explained in [srī bhagavat gītā](http://githa.koyil.org/) 4.5  “*bahūni mē vyatītāni…*” (Oh destroyer of enemies (arjuna)! I have also taken many births and you have too. I remember all my births but you do not). *māṇbu* means beauty; the beauty of manifesting supremacy in human form is glorified here.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.8.3. Kannavan

*kaṇ āvān enṟum maṇṇōr viṇṇōṟkku taṇ ār vēnkada viṇṇōr veṟpanē*

**Пословный перевод:**

maṇṇōr – (as explained in yajur vēdam – “cakśurdēvānāmuta marttyānām” – one who blesses knowledge to the residents of higher realms and earthly realms) for the residents of the material realm; viṇṇōrkkum – for the residents of the spiritual realm; enṟum – always; kaṇṇāvān – being the controller; taṇ – with coolness; Ar – abundant; vēnkadam – the place which is named as tiruvēnkadam; viṇṇōr veṟpan – one who has tirumalai which is vorśippable by nityasūris

**Перевод:**

**bhagavān who has tirumalai which is vorśippable by nityasūris, being the controller, resides in the abundantly cool tiruvēnkadam always for the residents of material and spiritual realms.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.,

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the third pāsuram – āḻvār explains that bhagavān mercifully arrived at tirumalai to bond with both badda (bound souls in material realm) and mukta entities (liberated souls in spiritual realm).*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār mercifully explains the position of emperumān in tirumalai which is common for both nitya vibhūti (spiritual realm) and leelā vibhūti (material realm).*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Third pāsuram – āḻvār mercifully explains the simplicity which which emperumān mercifully presents himself in tirumalai to both nityasūris (eternally free souls) and samsāris (bound souls), just like a mother of twins will position herself to breast-feed both of them, கண் ஆவான் என்றும் மண்ணோர் விண்ணோர்க்கு தண் ஆர் வேங்கட விண்ணோர் வெற்பனே kaṇ āvān enṟum maṇṇōr viṇṇōṟkku taṇ Ar vēnkada viṇṇōr veṟpanē*

- *kaṇṇāvān* – two meanings – being the controller; to become visible (through knowledge). Explaining 2nd meaning further, nampiḷḷai says that [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) mercifully reveals the principle explained in śruti (yajur vēdam 4.6.8) – “*cakśurdēvānāmuta marttyānām*”  – one who blesses knowledge to the residents of higher realms and earthly realms.
- *maṇṇōr viṇṇōrkku enṟum kaṇṇāvān* – Explaining 1st meaning further, nampiḷḷai says that [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is the controller for all whether it is nityasūri or samsāri – here, a question is raised as to why he should be the controller of nityasūris (and muktas) who are fully knovledgable. nampiḷḷai answers – though they are fully knovledgable, they are also fully dependent on [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) and consider him as their controller – so he obliges.
- *taṇṇār vēnkadam* – As explained in nācciyār tirumoḻi 8.3 “*kuḷir aruvi vēnkadam*” (tiruvēngadam which has cool waterfalls), the place that can remove the distress of both [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) not having someone to be protected and these ātmās not having someone to protect them.
- *viṇṇōr veṟpanē* – Though he is presenting himself equally for both nityasūris and samsāris, tirumalai is owned by nityasūris. As in the case of paramapadam which is called as “*vānavar nādu*” (land of the nityasūris/muktas – tiruvāimoḻi 3.9.9), here it is said “*viṇṇōr veṟpu*” (the mountain of the nityasūris/muktas). nityasūris meditate upon [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s simplicity in presenting himself for the monkeys etc., in the forest as highlighted in nānmugan tiruvantādi 47 “*kānamum vānaramum*” (forests, monkeys) and become immersed in him – thus [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) declares tirumalai belongs to such nityasūris.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.8.4. Verpai onreduttu

*veṟpai onṟu eduttu oṟkam inṟiyē niṟkum ammān sīr kaṟpan vaigalē*

**Пословный перевод:**

onṟu – one; veṟpai – the hill; eduttu – lifted up; oṟkam – becoming tired; inṟiyē – not having; niṟkum – standing; ammān – master’s; sīr – glories (āpatsakatva – timely help); vaigal – for eternity; kaṟpan – will remember/recite

**Перевод:**

**I will remember/recite for eternity the glories of the lord/master who is standing without feeling tired after lifting up the gōvardana hill (to protect his devotees from the hailstorm instigated by indra).**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In fourth pāsuram – āḻvār says that he will always enjoy the qualities of emperumān who lifted gōvardanam.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār mercifully explains bhagavān‘s protecting of his devotees when they are in danger.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Fourth pāsuram – āḻvār explains how bhagavān‘s ārjavam (sincerity) was beneficial for him. வெற்பை ஒன்று எடுத்து ஒற்கம் இன்றியே நிற்கும் அம்மான் சீர் கற்பன் வைகலே veṟpai onṟu eduttu oṟkam inṟiyē niṟkum ammān sīr kaṟpan vaigalē*

- *veṟpai onṟu eduttu* – When indra effected a hailstorm to attack the cows and cow-herd boys,  [kaṇṇan emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), in order to shield them from that, picked up a hill (gōvardanam) nearby and protected them.

Since he was only seven years old, did he not get tired holding the hill up?

- *oṟkam inṟiyē niṟkum* – stood there holding the hill up, without getting tired.

Why did he not get tired even after standing up for seven days holding up the hill?

- *ammān* – natural lord and master – due to the natural/eternal relationship, he stood there without getting tired, just like a mother who would never get tired taking care of her child.
- *sīr kaṟpan* – I will meditate upon his caring act of lifting up the hill and protecting those who are to be protected by him. As said in srī rāmāyaṇam kiśkintā kāṇḍam 4.12 “*guṇairdāsyamupāgata:*” (I am serving him, being overwhelmed by his qualities says lakśmaṇa about srī rāma), [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) becomes a servitor to [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) on seeing his nīrmai (simplicity).
- *vaigalē* – daily/always. I will not say this now and then leave to do something else after a while. Like nityasūris, this (enjoying his auspicious qualities) will be my eternal activity as said in rig vēdam (viṣṇu sūktam) “…*vipanyava:…*” (ones who are glorifying [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) naturally).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.8.5. Vaigalum venney

*vaigalum veṇṇey kai kalandu uṇḍān poy kalavādu en mey kalandānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vaigalum – always; veṇṇey – butter; kai kalandu – stretching the hand fully; uṇḍān – one who ate; poy kalavādu – being truthful (without deceit); en – my; mey – body (which is to be rejected); kalandān – became immersed in me

**Перевод:**

**One who stretched his hands fully (to fetch the butter) and ate the butter, without any deceit, immersed in my body (that is to be rejected). kai kalandu – also explained as eating butter with both hands.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In fifth pāsuram – āḻvār mercifully explains how emperumān persevered with him seeing āḻvār starting to sing emperumān‘s qualities and glories.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār mercifully explains how such (glorious) kriṣṇa bonded with him.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Fifth pāsuram – when asked “if you meditate upon his qualities, what does he do?”, āḻvār replies “Just like I focussed on emperumān‘s qualities more than him, he too is liking my body more than me”. வைகலும் வெண்ணெய் கை கலந்து உண்டான் பொய் கலவாது என் மெய் கலந்தானே vaigalum veṇṇey kai kalandu uṇḍān poy kalavādu en mey kalandānē*

- *vaigalum* – Just like his qualities are the ones which sustain me as I mentioned in “*kaṟpan vaigalē*” in previous pāsuram, he sustains himself by accepting those things which have been touched by his devotees.
- *veṇṇey kai kalandu uṇḍān* – 3 explanations given:
   - Out of great desire for the butter, he accepted the butter in both his hands and consumed that.
   - As explained in siṟiya tirumadal “*tārār tadantōḷgaḷ uḷḷaḷavum kai nītti*” (put his hand fully up to his shoulder in the pot to dig out as much butter as possible), [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) due to being a small child, considered that his stomach will be filled by fetching as much butter in his hands as possible and ate the same.
   - When he was blamed for stealing butter, he mingled with those who were searching for the thief and at the same time consumed the butter smartly.

Does it make sense to say that [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) who is sarvādikan (greater than all) desired for the body of [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) who was eternally in samsāram (material realm) just as [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) desired for the butter in āyarpādi (gōkulam)?

- *poy kalavādu en mey kalandānē* – Just like he had true desire for that butter, his bonding with my body is also most truthful – says [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/).
- *en mey* – my body – this shows that [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is showing great interest in āḻvār but [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is shying away from him. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying – that which I reject as “*aḻukkudambu*” (dirty body – tiruviruttam 1) is desired greatly by him.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.8.6. Kalandu ennavi

*kalandu en āvi nalam koḷ nādan pulan koḷ māṇāy nilam koṇḍānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kalandu – mixing (like water); en āvi – my ātmā‘s; nalam – vellness (of being distinguished subservient to bhagavān); koḷ – had (as his benefit); nādan – one who is sēśi (master); pulan – for the senses; koḷ – ākarśaka (enchanting); māṇāy – having the form of vāmana – a dwarf, celibate youth; nilam – earth; koṇḍān – accepted it

**Перевод:**

**vāmana emperumān, with a youthful celibate dwarf form that is enchanting for the senses (of the on-looker), accepted earth as his. That same master mixed with my ātmā and established my servitude towards him. Here earth is indicated as a sample for other parts of the world which were measured/accepted by vāmana at that time.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

[āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says “after winning over me, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) desiring to give more pleasure to me, shows his beautiful form, attracts mahābali and grabs the world from him”.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the sixth pāsuram – āḻvār vividly explains how emperumān transformed him to be fully subservient, after bonding with him.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says that emperumān transformed his ātmā (self) to be subservient just like how he brought the whole world to be subservient.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Sixth pāsuram – When asked “what did he do after bonding with you?” āḻvār replies “He is not stopping with liking my body, he enjoyed my ātmā as well”. கலந்து என் ஆவி நலம் கொள் நாதன் புலன் கொள் மாணாய் நிலம் கொண்டானே kalandu en āvi nalam koḷ nādan pulan koḷ māṇāy nilam koṇḍānē*

- *kalandu ennāvi nalam koḷ* – Bonded with me like water mixing with water (so they cannot be separated) and subsequently established my [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)‘s eternal servitude towards him.

Did he stop with that?

- *nādan* – As explained in tirunedundāṇḍagam 25 “*ennai āḷum koṇḍu*” (ruling over me), eliminated the thought of my existing for my own pleasures (and made me exist fully for his pleasure).

Are you the only one who was caught by him like that?

- *pulan koḷ māṇāy nilam koṇḍānē* – mahābali too was captured by him; he did not give himself to [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) (like me), but only gave a little bit of land. Assuming a form that will enchant all the senses, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) grabbed the earth which was considered by mahābali as his own.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.8.7. Kondan elvidai

*koṇḍān ēḻ vidai uṇḍān ēḻ vaiyam taṇ tāmam seydu en eṇ tān ānānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ēḻ vidai – seven bulls (which were hurdles which stop from achieving the goal of marrying nappinnai); koṇḍān – one who took their vital air, i.e., killed them; ēḻ vaiyam – all the worlds; uṇḍān – one who protected them by keeping them in his stomach; taṇ – that which eliminates the heat of samsāram (material realm); tāmam – attachment towards paramapadam; seydu – showed (towards me); en – my; eṇ – ambition/desire; tān – he; ānān – started desiring

**Перевод:**

**emperumān killed the seven bulls (which were stopping him from marrying nappinnai) and protected all the worlds by consuming them. Such emperumān showed towards me the desire that he shows towards paramapadam, which is also what I desire for.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the seventh pāsuram – āḻvār says “Whatever ambitions I had towards emperumān, he manifested the same towards me”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “He held my thoughts as his own”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Seventh pāsuram – āḻvār says “Not only he established my subservience towards him, he manifested towards me the same attachment he has towards nitya vibhūti (paramapadam – spiritual realm)”. கொண்டான் ஏழ் விடை உண்டான் ஏழ் வையம் தண் தாமம் செய்து என் எண் தான் ஆனானே koṇḍān ēḻ vidai uṇḍān ēḻ vaiyam taṇ tāmam seydu en eṇ tān ānānē*

- *koṇḍān ēḻ vidai* – kriṣṇa killed the seven bulls which were stopping him from being united with nappinnaip pirātti (satyā, the daughter of kumba who is the brother of yasōdā).
- *uṇḍān ēḻ vaiyam* – Just as he could not bear the worlds tormenting during deluge and so consumed them to protect them, he united with me as if he could not bear the separation from me .

Further more,

- *taṇ tāmam seydu* – paramapadam is a place which has a pleasing coolness. Whatever attachment he has towards paramapadam, he manifested the same towards me. Also explained as, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) saying “though I am in this samsāram (material realm), he treated me as a resident of paramapadam”.
- *en eṇ tān ānānē* – two explanations:
   - He fulfilled my goal as I desired.
   - He assumed my desires as his own. In other words, just like āḻvār wants to enjoy [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) in paramapadam as he says in tiruvāimoḻi 9.3.7 “*māga vaikundam kāṇbadaṟku en manam ēkameṇṇum*” (my heart constantly desires to see paramapadam), tiruviruttam 47 “*kaṇṇan viṇṇūr toḻavē sariginṟadu sangam*” (due to my longing to see [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s paramapadam, I am becoming weak and my bangles are falling off as I become leaner), [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) too desires “Let us go to [āḻvārtirunagari](http://azhwarthirunagari.koyil.org/) and enjoy [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) there”.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.8.8. Anan anayan

*ānān ān āyan mīnōdu ēnamum tān ānān ennil tānāya sangē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ānān An āyan – Became a cow-herd boy who is naturally inclined towards protecting cows; tān – he; mīnōdu ēnamum – (to protect his devotees) in the forms of fish, boar etc; ānān – he incarnated; ennil – while saying that; tānāya – (naturally most distinct) incarnations of his; sangu – no sankyā (no limits)

**Перевод:**

**emperumān who descended as kriṣṇa (a cow-herd by who is naturally inclined towards protecting cows) also descended as fish, boar etc – while saying this we can see his most distinct incarnations are infinite. sangu – is explained as infinity as well as attachment. When explained as attachment – āḻvār is saying “due to his attachment towards me, he assumed the forms of fish, boar etc.”.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the eighth pāsuram, āḻvār says “sarvēśvaran mercifully descended into dēva (celestial), manuśya (human) etc forms out of great attachment towards me”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says that there is no limit to the incarnations of emperumān which are focussed on his devotees.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Eighth pāsuram – āḻvār says “there is no limit to his incarnations that are aimed at me”. ஆனான் ஆன் ஆயன் மீனோடு ஏனமும் தான் ஆனான் என்னில் தான் ஆய சங்கே ānān An āyan mīnōdu ēnamum tān ānān ennil tānāya sangē*

- *ānān An āyan* – Born in a cow-herd family, out of great commitment towards the birth, he engaged in herding the cattle instead of desiring to be crowned in the kingdom.

Did he stop with that?

- *mīnōdu ēnamum tān ānān* – previously [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) spoke about kriṣṇāvatāram. When compared with these avatārams such as matsya (fish) and varāha (boar), kriṣṇāvatāram is like nityasūris (in-front of samsāris). [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) who is sarvādika (greater than all), became one amongst these species (of fish and boar). Though these two incarnations appeared in sequence, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/), out of hurry, recites them together as if they appeared at the same time.
- *ānān* – his form, act etc match the particular species’ form, act etc. The purpose of these three incarnations is to impart knowledge \[matsyāvatāram was taken to protect/retrieve vēdam, varāha emperumān is known as jñānappirān and kriṣṇa is gītācāryan\].

And the purpose of these incarnations is

- *ennil tānāya sangē* – three explanations:
   - sangam is explained as bonding; the great desire of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) to be united with me.
   - sangē – mahā sankyā – a special measurement of identifying great number such as lakhs, crore etc; his incarnations are countless/infinite.
   - sangē – mahā sankyā? – it is asked like a question; is it limited to mahā sankyā? Is there an end to his incarnations? This is explained in [srī bhagavat gītā](http://githa.koyil.org/) 4.5  “*bahūni mē vyatītāni…*” (Oh destroyer of enemies (arjuna)! I have also taken many births and you have too. I remember all my births but you do not).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.8.9. Sangu cakkaram

*sangu cakkaram angkaiyil koṇḍān engum tānāya nangaḷ nādanē*

**Пословный перевод:**

engum – in all places; tānāya – (through his incarnations) manifesting himself; nangaḷ – our; nādan – master; am – (naturally) beautiful; kaiyil – divine hands; sangu cakkaram – disc and conch (which are enjoyed by his devotees); koṇḍān – having them

**Перевод:**

**While manifesting himself (through his incarnations), our master has disc and conch (which are enjoyed by his devotees) in his divine hands (which are naturally beautiful on their own).**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In ninth pāsuram – āḻvār says that when bhagavān descends at various places to engage with his devotees, he would do so manifesting his distinct symbols which show his wealth/control over everyone else.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. சங்கு சக்கரம் அங்கையில் கொண்டான் எங்கும் தானாய நங்கள் நாதனே sangu cakkaram angkaiyil koṇḍān engum tānāya nangaḷ nādanē*

- *sangu cakkaram am kaiyil koṇḍān* – Just like those who try to attract someone carry some medicines/substances (which will mesmerise or cast a spell”) in their hand, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) carries his divine weapons while incarnating. Does he carry his ornaments in all incarnations? Yes. When kings go on disguise to check on the state of their kingdom secretly, his confidantes too will follow him from distance; similarly, the weapons too, sometimes will be visible and other times be hidden – but they are always there. For [āḻvārs](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/azhwars/), these fierce weapons appear as ornaments as said in tiruvāimoḻi 6.9.1 “*kūrārāḻi veṇ sangēndi vārāy*” (Appear in front of me holding your sharp disc and white conch).
- *sangu cakkaram* – In those divine hands which looks most enchanting on their own, he placed the weapons.
- *engum tānāya* – One who appeared in many species such as dēva (celestial), manuśya (human) etc. It is also explained as [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s omnipresence – just like an army rounds up a whole town to capture a thief/criminal, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is existing everywhere to capture [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/).
- *nangaḷ nādanē* – his whole aim is to accept us as his servitors.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.8.10. Natan jnalam

*nādan jñālam koḷ pādan en ammān ōdam pōl kiḷar vēda nīranē*

**Пословный перевод:**

nādan – being unconditional master for all; jñālam – (to sustain his lordship over) all worlds; koḷ – accepted/spread-over (without discriminating); pādan – one with the divine feet; ennammān – (due to that) being my distinct master; ōdam pōl – like an ocean; kiḷar – rising high (glorifying and revealing its heart); vēdam – one who is spoken by vēdam; nīran – one who has the quality of nīrmai (ārjavam – sincerity in this case)

**Перевод:**

**emperumān, being the lord of all, having the divine feet which spread over all worlds without discrimination to establish his lordship over them, the one who is my master due to that, is the most sincere one who is spoken by vēdam like the rising tides of an ocean.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In tenth pāsuram – āḻvār says that such emperumān‘s greatness is only (to be) revealed through vēdam.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Tenth pāsuram – āḻvār started talking about emperumān‘s nīrmai (ārjavam/sincerity in this case) and said “Am I qualified to speak about that? Should it not be spoken by vēdam fiercely like great tides rising out of an ocean?”. நாதன் ஞாலம் கொள் பாதன் என் அம்மான் ஓதம் போல் கிளர் வேத நீரனே nādan jñālam koḷ pādan en ammān ōdam pōl kiḷar vēda nīranē*

- *nādan* – Controller of all.
- *jñālam koḷ pādan* – One who spread his lotus feet over the heads of all, irrespective of their being vasiśta (most learned/disciplined) or caṇḍāḷa (most ignorant/indisciplined).
- *ennammān* – one who transformed me to be totally existing for him by manifesting these two qualities of supremacy and simplicity.

Another explanation:

- *nādan* – The one who has mēnmai (supremacy/lordship) over all as explained in the [first pāsuram](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/09/thiruvaimozhi-1-8-1-odum-pulleri/).
- *jñālam koḷ pādan* – The one who has nīrmai (simplicity/easy -approacability) in his avatārams as explained in the [second pāsuram](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/09/thiruvaimozhi-1-8-2-ammanay/).
- *ennammān* – One who is present in tirumalai so that I too can approach him. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is thinking about [third pāsuram](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/09/thiruvaimozhi-1-8-3-kannavan/) where he said “*kaṇṇāvān*” (one who is visible).
- *ōdam pōl kiḷar vēda nīranē* – While speaking about his glories such as these, one should depend on vēdam which speaks about his nīrmai (ārjavam) just like a fierce ocean with rising tides \[i.e., vēdam establishing the glories most clearly and loudly\]. nīrmai – ārjavam – honesty/sincerity.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.8.11. Nir purai

*nīr purai vaṇṇan sīr satakōpan nērdal āyirattu ōrdal ivaiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

nīr purai – Like water in honesty/sincerity (as it will flow where it is directed); vaṇṇan – one who is having such nature; sīr – ārjava guṇam (quality of honesty/sincerity); satakōpan – nammāḻvār; nērdal – analysed and mercifully revealed; āyirattu – among the 1000 pāsurams; ivai – these (10 pāsurams); ōrdal – to be learned/understood

**Перевод:**

**nammāḻvār analysed emperumān‘s water-like ārjavam (sincerity) in all of tiruvāimoḻi and mercifully revealed in this decad, what is to be understood.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the end, āḻvār says that this decad is spoken after analysing all decads.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says that the purpose of this decad is to prove bhagavān‘s ārjavam (honesty/sincerity).*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. நீர் புரை வண்ணன் சீர் சடகோபன் நேர்தல் ஆயிரத்து ஓர்தல் இவையே nīr purai vaṇṇan sīr satakōpan nērdal āyirattu ōrdal ivaiyē*

- *nīr purai vaṇṇan* – Thus, sarvēsvaran’s ārjava guṇam (honesty/sincerity) is explained in this decad. It talks about the sincerity of the one who is similar to water in quality. Here ārjavam means – when samsāris (materially bound [soul](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)s) avoid [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), his following them (without giving up on them).
- *satakōpan nērdal* – Sung by [nammāḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/). Instead of some one disconnected from this singing, nammāḻvār who became the target of [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s ārjavam mercifully revealed this.
- *āyirattu ōrtal ivaiyē* – analysed the whole of tiruvāimoḻi and mercifully explained by [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/), i.e., on meditating upon the insincere nature of samsāris (bound [soul](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)s) and thus the possibility of losing out on [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/), [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) analysed bhagavān’s sincere nature and revealed that. It is also explained as – that which is to be analysed and understood by samsāris.

Final summary from [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/):

- In the first pāsuram, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) mercifully explained [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s sincere engagement with the residents of nitya vibhūti (spiritual realm).
- In the second pāsuram, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) mercifully explained [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s sincere engagement with the residents of leelā vibhūti (material realm).
- In the third pāsuram, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) mercifully explained [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s presence in tiruvēnkatam tirumalā to present himself for the residents of both nitya and leelā vibhūtis.
- In the fourth pāsuram, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) mercifully explained [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s sincerity manifesting on him personally.
- In the fifth pāsuram, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) said “Just like I like his qualities, [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) likes my body”.
- In the sixth pāsuram, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) said “Not stopping with my body, [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) also accepted my self ([soul](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/))”.
- In the seventh pāsuram, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) said “Not stopping with that, [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) also showed great attachments towards as he shows towards paramapadam”.
- In the eighth pāsuram, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) said “there is no limit for the incarnations [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) took to convince me”.
- In the ninth pāsuram, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) said “While incarnating as such, [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) descends with the symbols of his greatness over everyone else”.
- In the tenth pāsuram, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) said “vēdam should speak about [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s ārjavam (sincerity)”.
- Finally, he said that this decad is to be meditated upon by bound [soul](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)s always.

Thus ends the English translation for tiruvāimoḻi 1st centum 8th decad.
