## 1.9 Ivaiyum avaiyum

## 1.9.1. Ivaiyum avaiyum

*ivaiyum avaiyum uvaiyum ivarum avarum uvarum yavaiyum yavarum tan uḷḷē āgiyum ākkiyum kākkum avai uḷ tani mudal emmān kaṇṇa pirān en amudam suvaiyan tiruvin maṇāḷan ennudaic cūḻal uḷānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ivaiyum avaiyum uvaiyum – those acētana (insentient) entities which are near, far and in-between; ivarum avarum uvarum – those cētana (sentient) entities which are near, far and in-between; yavaiyum yāvarum – everything; tannuḷḷē – within himself (during annihilation); āgiyum – being their existence (by sustaining them); ākkiyum – creating them (during creation); kākkum – protecting (those which/who are created by eliminating the obstacles and fulfilling their desires); avaiyuḷ – being the in-dwelling soul in them; tani mudal – being the independent cause (without looking for anyone’s assistance); ammān – being the lord; kaṇṇa pirān – manifesting easy approacability in kriṣṇāvatāram; en amudam – being my enjoyable entity; suvaiyan – being a great enjoyer (due to that); tiruvin maṇāḷan – with srī mahālakśmi; ennudai – in my; sūḻal uḷān – present in the surroundings

**Перевод:**

**bhagavān who creates, protects and annihilates (consuming) all the acētanas (insentientn entities) and cētanas (sentient entities), being the in-dwelling soul of everything, being the supremely independent cause of everything, being the lord, showed his easy approacability in the form of kriṣṇa, being a great enjoyer, having given me great joy, is in my surroundings along with srī mahālakśmi.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the first pāsuram – āḻvār becomes delighted saying that kaṇṇan emperumān who is the cause of the creation etc of the universe, being the sustainer of all by being the antarātmā (in-dwelling super-soul) in everything, being sriya:pati (spouse of srī mahālakśmi), being a great enjoyer, being his lord, mercifully arrives in his vicinity to give him the pleasure of being together with emperumān.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*In the first pāsuram – āḻvār says that srīman nārāyaṇan who is the most supreme due to his being the cause of everything and being the in-dwelling soul of everything, who is most easily approachable, arrives in his vicinity.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*First pāsuram – āḻvār says that kaṇṇan emperumān who is the cause of creation etc, who is the in-dwelling soul of everything, could not leave his vicinity. For āḻvār, enjoying bhagavān‘s qualities and his wealth are not different from each other (Here āḻvār is enjoying various aspects of bhagavān‘s creation in this material realm also). āḻvār is recollecting the aspect he enjoyed in great detail in first decad (in 1.1.4 “nām avan“ pāsuram) and is enjoying the same in brief here. இவையும் அவையும் உவையும் இவரும் அவரும் உவரும் எவையும் எவரும் தன்னுளே ஆகியும் ஆக்கியும் காக்கும் அவையுள் தனிமுதல் எம்மான் கண்ண பிரான் என் அமுதம் சுவையன் திருவின் மணாளன் என்னுடைச் சூழல் உளானே ivaiyum avaiyum uvaiyum ivarum avarum uvarum yavaiyum yavarum than uḷḷē āgiyum ākkiyum kākkum avai uḷ tani mudal emmān kaṇṇa pirān en amudam suvaiyan tiruvin maṇāḷan ennudaic cūḻal uḷānē*

- *ivaiyum avaiyum …* – Collectively identifying acētana (insentient) and cētana (sentient) entities which/who are near, far and in-between.
- *tannuḷḷē āgiyum* – As explained in cāndōjña upaniśat 6.2.1 “*sadēva*” (sat/truth alone) – Out of his own will, [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) bearing [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) to ensure the sustenance of [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/).
- *ākkiyum* – As explained in taittirīya upaniśat “*bahu syām*” (let me become many), separating the [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)s from him and make them eligible to be distinguished, by their names and forms.
- *kākkum* – Mercifully protecting those entities which are were created \[creation means transformation from subtle form to gross form\].
- *avaiyuḷ tanimudal* – [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s presence as [antarātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) (in-dwelling soul) is that which gives the cētanas (sentients) eligibility for pravrutti (action) and nivrutti (inaction). īsn’t that already explained as part of “*ākkiyum*” (sruśti)? “*ākkiyum*” explains taittirīya upaniśat “*tadanupravisya*” – [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s entering into them (being present in them) as antaryāmi, to establish their identity and to acquire a name. Here,  the state of bhagavān being the antaryāmi, which means all words identifying the entity (cētana/acētana) will lead up to the antaryāmi ([emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)), is explained.
- *emmān* – He made me fully exist for him by showing his preference towards his own wealth.
- *kaṇṇapirān –* Such [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is kriṣṇa and he bestows great favours being visible in front of us.
- *en amudam* – Unlike the amrutam which was retrieved by churning milky ocean (tiruppāṟkadal) which expects its consumer to have big qualifications (like being a dēvatā etc), my amrutam ([bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)) is easily approachable by all.
- *suvaiyan* – That amrutam cannot be enjoyer (it can only be enjoyed by others). But [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is a parama-rasika (great enjoyer).

The reason for his enjoying attitude is highlighted:

- *tiruvin maṇāḷan* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s amrutam (nectar) is a (divine) couple \[srī mahālakśmi and srīman nārāyaṇan\].
- *ennudaic cūḻaluḷānē* – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is inseparable from [periya pirāttiyār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/) as explained in tiruvāimoḻi 6.10.10 “*agalagillēn iṟaiyum*” (I will not leave [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) even for a moment – tāyār’s words), approached me as if it is a great benefit for him to be in my vicinity. As explained in srī rāmāyaṇam kiśkintā kāṇḍam 4.21 “*yasya prasādē satatam prasīdēyurimā: prajā: \| sa rāmō vānarēndrasya prasādamabhikānkśatē \|\|*” (That srī rāma whose blessings which keep the residents of ayōdyā with pure-heart, was looking for sugrīva’s blessings out of his pure-heart) and srī rāmāyaṇam kiśkintā kāṇḍam 4.18 “… *lōkanāta: purā bhūtvā sugrīvam nātamiccti*” (though he is the ancient master of all of universe, he desires to have sugrīva as his master), such great emperumān would not want to let go of me and constantly stays in my vicinity.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.9.2. Sulal palapala

*sūḻal palapala vallān tollai am kālattu ulagai kēḻal onṟu āgi idanda kēsavan ennudai ammān vēḻa maruppai osittān viṇṇavarkku eṇṇal ariyān āḻa nedum kadal sērndān avan en arugalilānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

sūḻal – deceitful incarnations (for the purpose of attracting his devotees); pala pala – many; vallān – capable of assuming (out of his will); tollai – ancient; am – beautiful (due to its assisting in incarnations); kālattu – in the beginning of varāha kalpam; ulagai – the universe (submerged in the causal ocean); kēḻal onṟu āgi – becoming a unique boar; idanda – dug out; kēsavan – having beautiful kēsam (hair) (that has become wet due to contact with the causal water); ennudai ammān – being my master; vēḻam – (having incarnated as kriṣṇa), elephant named kuvalayāpīdam (which was an obstacle); maruppai osittān – one who broke its tusks; viṇṇavarkku – dēvatās (who are most knowledgeable); eṇṇil – to comprehend; ariyān – being very difficult; āḻam – (again to help his devotees) being very deep; nedum – wide; kadal – kśīrārṇavam – ocean of milk; sērndān avan – lying down there mercifully; en arugalilān – arrived at a place which is close to me

**Перевод:**

**emperumān who is capable, purely out of his will, of assuming deceitful incarnations which will attract his devotees, who assumed the form of a wild boar with beautiful locks during the ancient beautiful time to rescue the universe from the causal ocean, who broke the tusk of kuvalayāpīdam elephant, who is mercifully lying down in the deep and wide kśīrārṇavam to help the  most knowledgeable  dēvatās (those who cannot comprehend such acts of emperumān)  arrived at a place which is close to me.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the second pāsuram – āḻvār feels satisfied that bhagavān, beyond comprehension through the faculties of speech and mind of dēvatās such as brahmā, rudra et al, descended into the milk ocean for them. Such emperumān mesmerised āḻvār by his incarnations, qualities and activities and transformed him to be his servitor. Such emperumān arrived at his close proximity to give him the joy of his companionship.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says that emperumān who performed great favours for his devotees through his incarnations arrived at his close proximity.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Second pāsuram – āḻvār says “once I grasped emperumān‘s presence in the vicinity and digested the impact of that, he arrived closer to me”. சூழல் பலபல வல்லான் தொல்லை அம் காலத்து உலகைக் கேழல் ஒன்று ஆகி இடந்த கேசவன் என்னுடை அம்மான் வேழ மருப்பை ஒசித்தான் விண்ணவர்க்கு எண்ணல் அரியான் ஆழ நெடுங் கடல் சேர்ந்தான் அவன் என் அருகவிலானே sūḻal palapala vallān tollai am kālattu ulagai kēḻal onṟu āgi idanda kēsavan ennudai ammān vēḻa maruppai osittān viṇṇavarkku eṇṇal ariyān āḻa nedum kadal sērndān avan en arugalilānē*

- *sūḻal pala pala vallān* – Here the term sūḻal (surrounding/deceit) indicates avatāram. Why is avatāram indicated as surrounding/deceit? Because he captures the [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)s by surrounding them through his incarnations.
- *pala pala* – Indicates jāti bhēdam (distinct species) and avāntara bhēdam (different categories within the species).
- *vallān* – He is capable of assuming forms which cannot even be assumed by [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)s who acquire different forms based on their karma. \[[jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)s’\] karmam is limited but \[[bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s\] is capable of doing anything.

Here, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is explaining one such avatāram.

- *tollai* – ancient. In the beginning of varāha kalpam \[kalpam is a day in brahmā containing 1000 catur (krita, trētā, dvāpara and kali) yugas. The current kalpa is named as svētavarāha kalpa which is highlighted as part of sankalpams we perform during vaidika karmānuśtānam\].
- *am kālattu* – the time when he manifested his form to all – that is why [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says “beautiful time”.
- *ulagai* – Did he do this for tiruvadi (garudāḻvār) or tiruvanantāḻvān (ādi sēśan)? No, he did it for the earth which is not at all qualified to even be thought about.
- *kēḻal onṟu āgi* – Should he not have assumed a form which fits his greatness? \[No, he assumed the form of a boar\].
- *onṟu āgi* – The form is so unique that, even if he (who is supreme) wants to assume the form again, he will not be able to do that. He assumed a form that would not shy away from water and mud. Since it was a form assumed by him, even if it seems lowly, it becomes radiant because of him. nācciyār tirumoḻi 11.8 “*panṟiyām tēsu*” (boar with radiance).
- *idanda* – boars are naturally prideful. Since [srīman nārāyaṇan](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) (husband of [srī mahālakśmi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/)) assumed that form, the pride in that form is most explicit. He dug out the earth from the wall of the aṇḍam \[oval shaped universe that contains 14 layers starting from pātāḷam up to brahma lōkam\].
- *kēsavan* – prasasta kēsan (one who has beautiful locks). The beautiful form with nicely flowing hair.
- *ennudai ammān* – one who rescued me from this samsāram (which itself is annihilation).
- *vēḻa maruppai osittān* – One who effortlessly broke the tusk of the elephant named kuvalayāpīdam. Similarly he who destroyed my senses (which are like elephants). This indicates that he is the destroyer of obstacles.
- *viṇṇavarkku eṇṇal ariyān* – The one who fought the elephant alone, is beyond the comprehension of brahmā, rudran, etc.
- *āḻa nedum kadam sērndān* – Arrived in the milk ocean and lay down there to hear the complaints of such brahmā, rudra et al.
- *avan en arugalilānē* – Unlike staying in-between \[kśīrābdi is not as far as paramapadam, but it is not very close either\], [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) came very close to me.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.9.3. Arugalilaya

*arugal ilāya perum sīr amaragaḷ ādi mudalvan karugiya neela nal mēni vaṇṇan sendāmaraik kaṇṇan poru siṟaip puḷ uvandu ēṟum pūmagaḷār tanik kēḷvan oru gatiyin suvai tandittu oḻivu ilan ennōdu udanē*

**Пословный перевод:**

arugal il – not having defects such as apakśa (decline), etc; āya – Eternal, Due to permanent existence; perum – unlimited; sīr – one who is having auspicious qualities; amarargaḷ – for the nityasūris; ādi – one who is the cause for their existence etc; mudalvan – leader; karugiya – very blackish; neelam – like a blue gem; nal – good; mēni vaṇṇan – one who is having bodily complexion; sem – reddish (being contrary to such bodily complexion); tāmarai – lotus like; kaṇṇan – having divine eyes; poru – abundant; siṟai – having feathers; puḷ – periya tiruvadi (garudāḻvār); uvandu – with great desire; ēṟum – one who climbs on; pū magaḷār – most enjoyable srī mahālakśmi who is like the embodiment of flower’s fragrance; tanik kēḷvan – singular enjoyer; ennōdu udanē – being together with me; oru gatiyin – in one aspect; suvai – taste; tandittu – giving; oḻivu ilan – does not leave

**Перевод:**

**emperumān who has no defects such as decline etc., who is eternal, who has unlimited auspicious qualities, who is the leader of nityasūris and the cause for their existence etc., who has nice blackish bluish bodily complexion, one who has a reddish lotus like divine eyes (that looks contrasting to the blackish form), one who climbs with great desire on garudāḻvār who has abundant feathers, who is the singular enjoyer of the most enjoyable srī mahālakśmi who is like the embodiment of flower’s fragrance, after being with me giving one particular aspect of enjoyment, does not leave me.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the third pāsuram – āḻvār says “Unlike the divine consorts of emperumān who enjoy different dealings with him,  emperumān gave me all kinds of blissful union and became so attached to me that he can never be separated from me”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “emperumān bonded with me and gave me many blissful experiences”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Third pāsuram – āḻvār says “emperumān who engages differently with tiruvadi (garudāḻvār), tiruvanantāḻvān (ādi sēśan), his divine consorts et al, does not leave me after engaging me in just one aspect”. அருகல் இலாய பெரும் சீர் அமரர்கள் ஆதி முதல்வன் கருகிய நீல நன் மேனி வண்ணன் செந்தாமரைக் கண்ணன் பொரு சிறைப் புள் உவந்து ஏறும் பூமகளார் தனிக் கேள்வன் ஒருகதியின் சுவை தந்திட்டு ஒழிவு இலன் என்னோடு உடனே arugal ilāya perum sīr amaragaḷ ādi mudalvan karugiya neela nal mēni vaṇṇan sendāmaraik kaṇṇan poru siṟaip puḷ uvandu ēṟum pūmagaḷār tanik kēḷvan oru gatiyin suvai tandittu oḻivu ilan ennōdu udanē*

- *arugal il āya perum sīr amaragaḷ ādi mudalvan* – arugal – reduction, defect, blemish; il – absence; āya – good. Being free from any blemish, having unlimited auspicious qualities, and presenting such qualities for the enjoyment of nityasūris, and being the cause for their existence etc.
- *karugiya neela nal mēni vaṇṇan* – Having most blackish beautiful bodily complexion which is beyond expression in words. Having beautiful complexion in most distinct, divine form. nityasūris sustain themselves by constantly enjoying this divine form.
- *sendāmaraik kaṇṇan* – eyes which reveal the internal qualities such as kindness, compassion etc.
- *poru siṟaip puḷ uvandu ēṟum* – When [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) invites garudāḻvār (to go for a ride), garudāḻvār feels delighted seeing [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s acknovledgement of his service and his feathers start rising due to that joy. [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) too feels great joy to accept his service.
- *pū magaḷār tanik kēḷvan* – Like the embodiment of flower’s fragrance. When explained as the singular enjoyer of most enjoyable srī mahālakśmi, it establishes that there is no comparable person for [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/).
- *oru gatiyin suvai tandittu oḻivilan ennōdu udanē* – Unlike engaging with them (nityasūris) he engages with me in just one aspect and does not leave me; he engages with me in all different ways by which he engages with all of them.
- *udanē* – He does not treat me differently thinking that he is supreme etc. He even addresses the concerns of nityasūris from my close proximity.  In previous decad, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)  said [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) showed his attachment towards me just as he shows his attachment towards paramapadam; now, he says emperumān engages with him in all the different ways by which he engages with all the residents of srī vaikuṇṭam.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.9.4. Udan amar

*udan amar kādal magaḷir tirumagaḷ maṇmagaḷ āyar madamagaḷ enṟu ivar mūvar āḷum ulagamum mūnṟē udan avai okka viḻungi ālilaic cērndavan emmān kadal mali māyap perumān kaṇṇan en okkalaiyānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

udan – being together; amar – having; kādal – love; magaḷir – his consorts; tirumagaḷ – lakshmi (who has amazing rich form); maṇmagaḷ – bhūmi dēvi (who is embodiment of forbearance); āyar mada magaḷ – (most-suitable) nappinnai who is having great family heritage and great qualities; enṟu – being the main and well known; ivar – these divine consorts; mūvar – three; āḷum – ruling over (protecting); ulagamum – universe/world; mūnṟē – three layers – 1) from pātāḷa lōka to svarga lōkam, 2) jana lōkam, tapa lōkam, satya lōkam, 3) mahar lōkam; avai – (during praḷayam/annihilation) those; udan – without any distinction; okka – evenly; viḻungi – consumed; ālilai – on banyan leaf; sērndavan – lying down; emmān – (by doing this) being my lord and master; kadal – in kśīrārṇavam (milk ocean); mali – having the glories of resting; māyam – with amazing qualities/activities; perumān – one with naturally unlimited qualities; kaṇṇan – kriṣṇa; en okkalaiyān – (like on yasōdā) sat on my hip

**Перевод:**

**bhagavān kriṣṇa is seated with his three well-known, primary and divine/lovable consorts srī mahālakśmi, srī bhūmi dēvi and srī neeḷā dēvi (nappinnai), who rule over the three worlds. He consumed those three worlds evenly during (total) annihilation without any distinction and lay down on a banyan leaf and thus won over me and became my master. Such kaṇṇan emperumān who is having the glories of resting in kśīrārṇavam (milk ocean) with naturally unlimited qualities, sat on my hip (like he sat on mother yasōdā’s hip).**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār explains in the manner in which emperumān engaged with him.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In fourth pāsuram – āḻvār says that kriṣṇa who is sarvēsvaran, atyāscarya bhūtan (most amazing person) and my master, climbed up my hip and sat there.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says that bhagavān who is complete and the protector of all sat on my hip.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Fourth pāsuram – āḻvār says that emperumān is supreme; he is capable of performing impossible tasks; such emperumān sat on my hip just like he sat on mother yasōdā’s hip and considered that as his fortune. உடன் அமர் காதல் மகளிர் திருமகள் மண்மகள் ஆயர் மட மகள் என்று இவர் மூவர் ஆளும் உலகமும் மூன்றே உடன் அவை ஒக்க விழுங்கி ஆல் இலைச் சேர்ந்தவன் எம்மான் கடல் மலி மாயப் பெருமான் கண்ணன் என் ஒக்கலையானே udan amar kādal magaḷir tirumagaḷ maṇmagaḷ āyar madamagaḷ enṟu ivar mūvar āḷum ulagamum mūnṟē udan avai okka viḻungi ālilaic cērndavan emmān kadal mali māyap perumān kaṇṇan en okkalaiyānē*

- *udan amara kātal magaḷir* – divine consorts who have great love to be always with [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/). They always feel as stated in tiruvāimoḻi 6.10.10 “*agalagillēn iṟaiyum*” (I will not leave even for a moment).

Who are they?

- *tirumagaḷ* – periya pirāttiyār ([srī mahālakśmi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/)) – the principal consort of [sarvēsvaran](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/), the empress and the one who says as stated in srī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 116.45 “*na kascinnāparādayti*” (there is no one who does not commit mistakes).
- *maṇmagaḷ* – srī bhūmi pirāttiyār (bhūdēvi) – the one who teaches [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) “should you even see the mistakes?” and the one who is the origin of forbearance.
- *āyar madamagaḷ* – nappinnai pirāttiyār (neeḷā dēvi) – the one who keeps [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) engaged by her beauty etc., and hides the mistakes of others.
- Another explanation – *tirumagaḷ* is his wealth; *maṇmagaḷ* is the place where it (the wealth) grows; *āyar madamagaḷ* – the one who enjoys that wealth.
- *ivar mūvar* – Individuals who are separately available to establish [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s supremacy and to be the puruśakāram (mediator).
- *āḷum ulagamum mūnṟē* – lōkam could indicate the residents of the lōkam and three indicates the three types of cētana ([jīvāmtmās](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)) \[viz nitya – eternally free souls, mukta – liberated souls, badda – bound souls\]. It could also mean the top, middle and the bottom layers of a single universe.
- *udan avai okka viḻungi* – Without missing anything, consuming them all at once and protecting them inside his stomach. Since paramapadam is eternal, this only applies to the bound souls in the material realm.
- *ālilaic cērndavan* – After consuming everything and having them in his stomach, he rested on a banyan leaf. This means he has agadita gatanā sāmartyam (achieving the impossible) \[i.e., consuming everything which is huge and then lying down on a banyan leaf which is so small\].
- *emmān* – by such act, he won over me. He acquired me through patrālambanam (dual meaning – by climbing on a leaf, by writing in a document to be my master). This act of accepting is even more impossible in comparison to the act of lying down on a banyan leaf since I was completely staying away from [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/). He transformed me to be totally existing for him only.
- *kadal mali māyap perumān* – Descending into the kśīrābdi (milk ocean) and resting there without any defects and having amazing qualities/activities. Also explained as one who is having more amazing aspects than an ocean.
- *kaṇṇan* – manifesting all those aspects in this form of [kriṣṇa](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)
- *en okkalaiyānē* – He sat on my hip Just like he sat on mother yasōdā’s hip.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.9.5. Okkalai vaittu

*okkalai vaittu mulap pāl uṇ enṟu tandida vāngisekkam sega anṟu avaḷ pāl uyir sega uṇḍa perumānnakka pirānōdu ayanum indiranum mudalāgaokkavum tōṟṟiya īsan māyan en nenjin uḷānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

nakka pirānōdu – one who wears ākāsam (space/ether) as clothes (i.e., nagna – being naked), who is popularly known as īsvara; ayanum – brahmā who is popularly known as aja (unborn) since he is not born from a woman’s uterus (he was directly born from bhagavān out of bhagavān‘s will/desire); indiranum – indra who considers himself as the most wealthy entity; mudalāgavum – and all such beings; okka – at once; tōṟṟiya – created; īśanum – being the sarvēśvaran; okkalai vaittu – (during kriṣṇāvatāram) placing him on her hip (like mother yasōdā does); mulaip pāl uṇ enṟu – (with loving intentions) saying drink my breast-milk; tandida – (exclusively) gave; vāngi – (without any doubt) accepting it; sekkam – the thought of killing kriṣṇa; sega – to be destroyed (within her, without anyone else knowing); anṟu – that day (when she came to kill him); avaḷ pāl – in her; uyir – vital-air; sega – to be finished; uṇḍa – consumed (the milk she gave); perumān – sarvādika (who is greater than all and who retained himself as the master of the universe); māyan – most amazing person; en – my; nenjin uḷān – became contained in my heart (which is a part in my body

**Перевод:**

**sarvēśvaran who is the creator of rudra, brahmā, indra and all beings, when appeared as kriṣṇa, pūtanā (the demon) picked him up like mother yasōdā would do and placed him on her hip. She then fed kriṣṇa her \[poisonous\] breast-milk that was kept exclusively for him and emperumān accepted it without any doubt. He consumed the vital-air of pūtanā while accepting the milk and destroyed her thought of killing kriṣṇa along with her (without anyone knowing about that). Such most amazing emperumān entered my heart and became contained in there.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*āḻvār says “īśvara who is the creator of even brahmā, rudran et al, removed my obstacles and entered my heart”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār explains “kriṣṇa who is greater than all, who is eliminator of obstacles became contained within my heart”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. ஒக்கலை வைத்து முலைப் பால் உண் என்று தந்திட வாங்கிச்செக்கம் செக அன்று அவள் பால் உயிர் செக உண்ட பெருமான்நக்க பிரானோடு அயனும் இந்திரனும் முதலாகஒக்கவும் தோற்றிய ஈசன் மாயன் என் நெஞ்சின் உளானே okkalai vaittu mulap pāl uṇ enṟu tandida vāngisekkam sega anṟu avaḷ pāl uyir sega uṇḍa perumānnakka pirānōdu ayanum indiranum mudalāgaokkavum tōṟṟiya īsan māyan en nenjin uḷānē*

- *okkalai vaittu* – Placing kriṣṇa on her hip, just like the most loving yasōdā does.
- *mulaip pāl uṇ enṟu* – saying forcefully “I am having pain in my breasts since you have not consumed the milk. So, please drink now”.
- *tandida* – as she gave – This is similar to what was said by sugrīva on seeing vibhīśaṇa with his assistants in srī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 17.5 “*asmān hantum*” (to kill us), [āḻvār](http://srunu/) for a moment feels that pūtanā is trying kill āḻvār (by taking the life of kriṣṇa). It also simply means, she gave.
- *sekkam sega* – 3 explanations:
   - sekkam means death. The death she desired for kriṣṇa, occurred to her.
   - sekkam means red – which indicates anger. The anger she had on kriṣṇa that turned towards her. [tirumangai āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/thirumangai-azhwar/) too used red to indicate anger in periya tirumoḻi 8.6.6 “*ilangai sentī uṇṇac civandu*“.
   - sekkam also means lips. “sekkam sega” means “lips turning red”. Smiling with his lips showing gratitude towards pūtanā for her act of nursing him.
- *anṟu* – That day when she planned to destroy the universe \[if kriṣṇa is killed, the whole universe will cease to exist\]. That day when pūtanā came to destroy kriṣṇa in a secluded place.
- *avaḷ pāl uyir* – her vital-force that clings on to her deplorable body.
- *sega* – to destroy that.
- “*avaḷ pāl uyir sega*” is also explained as “Her milk, life (both) destroyed”. In periya tirumoḻi, it is said “*mulai ūdu uyirai vāngi uṇḍa vāyān*” (one who consumed the breast and her life) – here breast indicates breast-milk. “*mulai uṇḍān*” (he ate the breast) means “*mulaippāl uṇḍān*” (he ate the breast-milk).
- *uṇḍa perumān* – by consuming the breast-milk and destroying pūtanā, he (himself) gave the master for the universe.
- *nakka pirān …* – rudra who is popularly known to be favourable towards his devotees, his father caturmuka brahmā (4 headed brahmā), indra who is closer to us in proximity (in comparison with brahmā) and all those beings who are present in this side (material realm) etc., are consumed at once like easily destroyable mosquitoes.
- *māyan* –  one who is capable of entering into the universe which was created by him.
- *en nenjinil uḷānē* – arrived into a (special) part (heart) of my body.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.9.6. Mayan en

*māyan en nenjin uḷḷān maṟṟum yavarkkum aduvē kāyamum seevanum tānē kālum eriyum avanē sēyan aṇiyan yavarkkum sindaikkum gōcaram allan tūyan tuyakkan mayakkan ennudait tōḷiṇaiyānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

en – my; nenjin uḷḷān – one who resides in (my) heart; māyan – amazing person; maṟṟum yavarkkum – for others; aduvē – can he do that?; kāyamum – sarīram/body; seevanum – ātmā/soul; tānē – having everything as his prakāram (form) and thus being seemingly identical to them; kālum – wind; eriyum – fire; avanē – having them as prakāram (form); sēyan – being distant (for those who are not his devotees); aṇiyan – being close (for his devotees); yavarkkum – even for those great persons; sindaikkum – to meditate upon (trying on their own efforts); gōcaram allan – not within the grasp; tūyan – having purity (to be approachable by his devotees); tuyakkan mayakkan – one who creates doubts/errors in the minds (of those non-devotees); ennudai – my (like how he climbs garudāḻvār); tōḷiṇaiyān – stayed on my two shoulders

**Перевод:**

**Can the amazing emperumān stay in others’ hearts like he stays in my heart? Having all types of bodies (acit) and souls (cit) as his prakāram, having wind, fire as his prakāram, he is difficult to understand for those non-devotees and easy to understand for his devotees. He is not comprehensible for even the greatest persons. He is pure (to be approachable by his devotees) and the one who creates doubts/errors in those who are not devoted to him. Such emperumān stayed on my two shoulders just like he stays on garudāḻvār’s shoulders.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In sixth pāsuram – āḻvār says “bhagavān who is sarvāntarātmā (in-dwelling super soul of everyone), who is unreachable for non-devotees and very much reachable for devotees, gets hold of my shoulders and that is his overflowing mercy towards me”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Sixth pāsuram – āḻvār says “one who is sarvāntarātmā held on to my shoulder and engaged with me”. மாயன் என் நெஞ்சின் உள்ளான் மற்றும் எவர்க்கும் அதுவே காயமும் சீவனும் தானே காலும் எரியும் அவனே சேயன் அணியன் எவர்க்கும் சிந்தைக்கும் கோசரம் அல்லன் தூயன் துயக்கன் மயக்கன் என்னுடைத் தோளிணையானே māyan en nenjin uḷḷān maṟṟum yavarkkum aduvē kāyamum seevanum tānē kālum eriyum avanē sēyan aṇiyan yavarkkum sindaikkum gōcaram allan tūyan tuyakkan mayakkan ennudait tōḷiṇaiyānē*

- *māyan en nenjin uḷḷān* – What a great blessing! Such great [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) with amazing qualities and activities entered my heart. What a union is this which is impossible!
- *maṟṟum yavarkkum aduvē* – No one else has received what has been received by me.

When questioned as to what is the benefit which you got?

- *kāyamum seevanum tānē –* All types of beings (in various forms) and the ātmās which control those bodies are under his control.
- *kālum eriyum avanē* – wind and agni indicate all 5 elements (earth, water, fire, air ether); they are also his form.
- *sēyan* – For those who try to see him with self-efforts, he is very difficult to reach.
- *aṇiyan* – For those who approach him through him,  he becomes a tool in their hands to reveal himself.
- *yavarkkum sindaikkum gōcaramallan* – showing the limits for the difficulty in reaching him. Even for the most intelligent persons, not only is he invisible for the eyes but also incomprehensible for the mind.
- *tūyan* – such pure [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/), for yasōdā et al, presents himself as said in srīviṣṇu purāṇam 4.6.15 “*yadi saknōśi…*” (if you are capable, free yourself) \[so they can even bind him and threaten him with love\].
- *tuyakkan mayakkan* – For those who are not attached to him, he creates doubts, errors in their mind. Even with me, when I first said in tiruvāimoḻi 1.5.1 “*aruvinaiyēn*” (most sinful), he let my mind wander around and then mingled with me and made me say in tiruvāimoḻi 1.5.5 “*un tēnē malarum tiruppādam serumāṟu*” (let me be at your lotus feet which is the source of honey).
- *ennudait tōḷiṇaiyānē* – He stayed on my shoulder like staying on garudāḻvār’s shoulder.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.9.7. Tolinai melum

*tōḷiṇai mēlum nal mārbin mēlum sudar mudi mēlumtāḷ iṇai mēlum punainda taṇ am tuḻāy udai ammānkēḷ iṇai onṟum ilādān kiḷarum sudarōli mūrttināḷaṇaindu onṟum agalān ennudai nāvin uḷānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tōḷiṇai mēlum – On the divine shoulders (which) give protection); nal – that which is desirable for the beloved; mārbin mēlum – on the divine chest; sudar – having radiance indicating the lordship; mudi mēlum – on the divine head; tāḷiṇai mēlum – on the divine, lotus feet which are held by the servitors; punainda – worn; taṇ am tuḻāy udai – having cool/beautiful tuḷasi; ammān – being the master; kēḷ – matching (such decoration); iṇai – comparable example; onṟum – even in a single aspect; ilādān – having none; kiḷarum sudar – having abundant radiance (natural radiance and the radiance of tuḷasi added); oḷi mūrtty – having a resplendent divine form; nāḷ – everyday; aṇaindu – approached; onṟum – even a little; agalān – being inseparable; en udai nāvinuḷān – entered my tongue

**Перевод:**

**emperumān who is wearing cool/beautiful tuḷasi on his divine shoulders, divine chest, divine head and divine lotus feet, being the master, having none comparable to him even in a single aspect, having an abundantly radiant resplendent divine form, approached me forever, being inseparable from me and entered my tongue.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the seventh pāsuram – āḻvār says “To unite with me, emperumān has decorated his divine form with tuḷasi and entered my tongue”. It can also be explained as āḻvār saying “he came to be praised by me”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “the most enjoyable emperumān became permanently seated in my tongue”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Seventh pāsuram – āḻvār says “emperumān decorated himself to my delight and entered my tongue”. தோள் இணை மேலும் நன் மார்பின் மேலும் சுடர் முடி மேலும்தாள் இணை மேலும் புனைந்த தண் அம் துழாய் உடை அம்மான்கேள் இணை ஒன்றும் இலாதான் கிளரும் சுடர் ஒளி மூர்த்திநாள் அணைந்து ஒன்றும் அகலான் என்னுடை நாவின் உளானே tōḷiṇai mēlum nal mārbin mēlum sudar mudi mēlumtāḷ iṇai mēlum punainda taṇ am tuḻāy udai ammānkēḷ iṇai onṟum ilādān kiḷarum sudarōli mūrttināḷaṇaindu onṟum agalān ennudai nāvin uḷānē*

- *tōḷiṇai* … – When one goes to meet his beloved, he would decorate himself to please her. Similarly when [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) goes to visit [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/), he wears tuḷasi everywhere. āḻvār desires for tuḷasi and emperumān too gives him that. Many pāsurams are quoted citing [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s love for emperumān wearing tuḷasi and his presenting that to āḻvār.
- *tōḷiṇai mēlum* – As explained in srīviṣṇu purāṇam 5.18.2 “*…sugādam pariśasvajē*” (kriṣṇa embraced akrūra tightly), those shoulders which make one long for their embrace.
- *nal mārbin mēlum* – divine chest where the one who facilitates such embrace ([srī mahālakśmi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/)) resides
- *sudar mudi mēlum* – After the embrace, if we lift up the face and look up, (on) the crown which indicates [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s lordship
- *tāḷiṇai mēlum punainda taṇṇan tuḻāyudai ammān* – sarvēsvaran whose lordship is established by his divine lotus feet and who is wearing tuḷasi in all these parts of his divine form.
- For this section, [bhattar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/parasara-bhattar/) gives a nice explanation. Brave men would first decorate their weapons. So, he placed tuḷasi on his divine shoulders. Those who are in love would decorate their beloved. So, he placed tuḷasi on his divine chest where his dearest consort lives. After giving to the weapons and beloved, they would decorate themselves. So, he wore it on his crown. The remnants are given to adiyārs (dual meaning – lotus feet and devotees). So he gives tuḷasi to his lotus feet. It is those devotees who come for the rescue when one is in danger. Just as  his divine lotus feet protect us, they protect him too (when sakataāsura came to attack kriṣṇa, kriṣṇa’s feet kicked him to death and protected him).
- *kēḷ iṇai onṟum ilādān* – When kēḷ is treated as kēḻ, kēḻ and iṇai both mean comparable. In this case, it means there is none comparable to [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) individually or even collectively. Alternatively, kēḷ means śadrusam (like) and iṇai means comparable. In this case, it means there is none like him to compare with him.
- *kiḷarum* – raising like a flood
- *sudar oḷi* – having unlimited resplendent, auspicious form
- *mūrtti* – having a form which does not need any additional decorations which were described previously
- *nāḷ aṇaindu* – Will not give up until he is with me every day (eternally, ever after)
- *ennudai nāvinuḷānē* – Became an identity to be praised by me; became the controller of my speech.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.9.8. Navinul ninru

*nāvinuḷ ninṟu malarum jñānak kalaigaḷukku ellām āviyum ākkaiyum tānē aḻippōdu aḷippavan tānē pū iyal nāl tadam tōḷan poru padai āḻi sangu ēndum kāvi nal mēnik kamalak kaṇṇan en kaṇṇin uḷānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

nāvinuḷ ninṟu – from the tongue; malarum – permeate/spread; jñānam – tools for knowledge; kalaigaḷukku ellām – for all those abodes (pramāṇams/śāstram/scriptures); āviyum – essential meaning which is the soul; ākkaiyum – the word which is the body; tānē – having them under his disposal; aḻippōdu aḷippavan tānē – having their creation and annihilation at his full disposal; pūviyal – fresh like a flower; nāl tadam tōḷan – one who is having four wide shoulders; poru – to destroy the enemies of devotees; padai – weapons; āḻi – sudarsana cakram – disc; sangu – pāncajanyam – conch; ēndum – holding them; kāvi – a dark-coloured flower; nal – good-looking; mēni – divine bodily complexion; kamalam – lotus like; kaṇṇan – having the eyes; en kaṇṇin uḷḷān – (with this beauty) entered my eyes

**Перевод:**

**bhagavān has the tools for knowledge, which spread everywhere from the words and meanings that emanate from the tongue, at his full disposal. He also has their creation and annihilation at his full disposal.  Such emperumān who is having four wide and fresh shoulders, who is having the sudarasana cakram and pāncajanyam in his hands to destroy the enemies of his devotees, who is having the divine bodily complexion of kāvi flower and who is having lotus-like eyes, entered into my eyes.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the eighth pāsuram – āḻvār says “emperumān who establishes the relationship for the words and their meanings for all types of knowledge, who handles the sustenance and annihilation of the same, entered into my eyes”. It is also explained as āḻvār saying “emperumān became visible to my eyes”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “emperumān entered into my eyes with a most beautiful form”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*In the eighth pāsuram – āḻvār says “Once my tongue consumed the experience, he became visible to my eyes”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Eighth pāsuram – āḻvār says “sarvēsvaran, who is the object of all knowledge, manifested his form that is visible through pramāṇams (śāstram) to my eyes”. நாவினுள் நின்று மலரும் ஞானக் கலைகளுக்கு எல்லாம் ஆவியும் ஆக்கையும் தானே அழிப்போடு அளிப்பவன் தானே பூ இயல் நால் தடம் தோளன் பொரு படை ஆழி சங்கு ஏந்தும் காவி நன் மேனிக் கமலக் கண்ணன் என் கண்ணின் உளானே nāvinuḷ ninṟu malarum jñānak kalaigaḷukku ellām āviyum ākkaiyum tānē aḻippōdu aḷippavan tānē pū iyal nāl tadam tōḷan poru padai āḻi sangu ēndum kāvi nal mēnik kamalak kaṇṇan en kaṇṇin uḷānē*

- *nāvinuḷ …* – For all the vidyā stānams (abodes of knowledge – śāstram) which are the tools which reveal knowledge that shines/emanates from the tip of the tongue.
- *āviyum ākkaiyum tānē* – āvi (soul) – meaning; ākkai (body) – word. It is [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) who establishes “Let this word will reveal this meaning”. Thus, he is the full controller of the relationship between the words and their meanings.
- *aḻippōdu aḷippavan tānē* – When the real meanings of words diminish due to the lack of faith in the people with ignorant intellect, writing/recording mistakes \[when someone writes down something, he/she may make a mistake\] and pātabhēdams (differences in recordings – a word/phrase may be recorded/recited in different ways due to different ways of understanding the same), he destroys such words. He then creates those words (with the proper meanings) again when he desires so. Alternatively, some explain this as generally talking about creation, annihilation of the universe.
- *pūviyal* … – Shoulders which have the tender quality of flowers or which are decorated with flowers. And, shoulders which are well expanded like kalpaka taru (kalpaka tree, a celestial tree) and four in numbers.
- *poru padai* – weapons which are used in wars. After having the shoulders expanded, they are decorated with the weapons.
- *kāvi nal mēni* – After having eliminated the hurdles, one can enjoy the beautiful form of emperumān.
- *nal mēni* – Since kāvi flower is not a direct comparison for mēni (form), nal (good/beautiful) is also added as an adjective.
- *kamalak kaṇṇan en kaṇṇin uḷānē* – If [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) stays away from [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s eyes, he will be named “*kaṇ vattak kaḷḷan*” (like a friend who does not help in need tries to stay away from sight). The eyes are like a swirl in a great flood.
- *en kaṇṇin uḷānē* – emperumān became visible to **me** who was seeing (enjoying) worldly pleasures.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.9.9. Kamalak kannan

*kamalak kaṇṇan en kaṇṇin uḷḷān kāṇbavan avan kaṇgaḷālē amalangaḷ āga viḻikkum aim pulanum avan mūrtti kamalattu ayan nambi tannaik kaṇṇudalānōdum tōṟṟi amalat teyvattōdu ulagam ākki en neṟṟi uḷḷānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kamalak kaṇṇan – one who is lotus-eyed; en kaṇṇin uḷḷān – becomes the object of my vision; kāṇban – (With that, after eliminating the state of “na cakśuśā pasyati” (cannot be seen by the eyes),) I saw him; avan – (that is because) that lotus-eyed emperumān; than kaṇgaḷālē – with his eyes; amalangaḷāga – eliminating the dirt such as ignorance etc; viḻikkum – glance at me; aim pulanum – (with that,) eyes and all other senses (totally five – eyes, ears nose, skin, tongue); avan mūrtti – became forms of his (he is the substratum) and his servitors; kamalattu – (Who is the one who did this to me?) being born in lotus flower; ayan – brahmā who is known as aja; nambi tannai – Being complete to fulfil his tasks such as creation etc; kaṇ nudalānōdum – along with visibly powerful rudra due to having the third eye in his forehead; tōṟṟi – creating them; amalam – (starting with them) having abundant goodness; teyvattōdu – along with the dēvatās; ulagam – universes; ākki – one who naturally creates; en – (preserving these qualities,) in one of my body parts; neṟṟi uḷān – became placed in my forehead

**Перевод:**

**emperumān who is lotus-eyed, became visible to me and I saw him because he glanced at me mercifully eliminating my ignorance, etc and thus my senses became subservient to him. This is the same emperumān who is the creator of the most complete brahmā who is born in the lotus flower (from the navel of bhagavān), the most capable rudra who has the third eye, many other dēvatās who are filled with goodness and the universes. With all these qualities, he became seated in my forehead.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the ninth pāsuram – āḻvār says “emperumān who is the creator of all, arrived on my forehead”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “Even while shining in my eyes, he who is the creator of all, became seated in the middle of my forehead”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*In the ninth pāsuram – āḻvār says “emperumān who created everything by a fraction (small portion) of his will, became seated in one of my body parts (forehead) and sustained himself”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Ninth pāsuram – āḻvār says “After feeling satisfied with being present in the eyes, emperumān arrived at my forehead”. கமலக் கண்ணன் என் கண்ணின் உள்ளான் காண்பன் அவன் கண்களாலே அமலங்கள் ஆக விழிக்கும் ஐம் புலனும் அவன் மூர்த்தி கமலத்து அயன் நம்பி தன்னைக் கண்ணுதலானொடும் தோற்றி அமலத் தெய்வத்தொடு உலகம் ஆக்கி என் நெற்றி உளானே kamalak kaṇṇan en kaṇṇin uḷḷān kāṇbavan avan kaṇgaḷālē amalangaḷ āga viḻikkum aim pulanum avan mūrtti kamalattu ayan nambi tannaik kaṇṇudalānōdum tōṟṟi amalat teyvattōdu ulagam ākki en neṟṟi uḷḷānē*

- *kamalak kaṇṇan en kaṇṇin uḷḷān* – puṇḍarikākśan (lotus-eyed lord) became visible to my eyes. This destroys the view point of bruhadāraṇyaka upaniśat 4.6.62 “*na cakśuśā gruhyatē*” (not graspable by eyes).

When he manifested his form to your eyes, what did you do?

- *kāṇban* – I saw and enjoyed that.

How were you able to see and enjoy his form?

- *avan kaṇgaḷālē amangaḷāga viḻikkum* – He mercifully glanced over me with his divine eyes and removed my blemishes (which are obstacles to see him) and facilitated me to see him.

But don’t your senses stop you from seeing him (being attached to worldly pleasures)?

- *aim pulanum avan mūrtti* – Even those senses became completely subservient to him like a body to the soul.
- *kamalattu ayan* … – brahmā who was born directly from the navel of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), one who is having such distinct birth from all others (generally everyone is born from a woman), one never goes back to [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) with any doubts etc., while creating other beings, created rudra who has the third eye in his forehead, other dēvatās with abundance of goodness and other universes. “*ākki*” indicates that [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is the natural creator of all.
- *en neṟṟi uḷānē* – He created the universe according to the karma and let it take care of itself. But he arrived at my forehead, without any expectation to stay here permanently.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.9.10. Nerriyul ninru

*neṟṟi uḷ ninṟu ennai āḷum niṟai malarp pādangaḷ sūdi kaṟṟait tuḻāy mudik kōlak kaṇṇa pirānait toḻuvār oṟṟaip piṟai aṇindānum nānmuganum indiranum maṟṟai amararum ellām vandu enadu ucci uḷānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

neṟṟiyuḷ ninṟu – being friendly; ennai – me; āḷum – accepting service; nirai malar – having rows of flowers submitted by devotees; pādangaḷ – divine feet; sūdi – wearing (on their heads); kaṟṟai – abundant/bunch of; tuḻāy – tuḷasi; mudik kōlam – having decorated head/crown; kaṇṇa pirānai – kriṣṇa who has favoured me (and most humble towards his devotees); toḻuvār – (by joining palms etc) worshipers; oṟṟaip piṟai – moon which is just a day into waxing; aṇindānum – rudra who is decorated with; nānmuganum – four headed brahmā; indiranum – indra; maṟṟai – other; amararum ellām – all dēvatās; vandu – (such emperumān who was vorśipped by all) arrived (from that forehead); en ucci uḷān – seated on my head

**Перевод:**

**kriṣṇa who is being friendly towards me, who is willing to accept my service, whose divine, lotus feet are decorated with rows of flowers submitted by devotees, who is having his head/crown decorated with abundant tuḷasi leaves, who has favoured me, is vorśipped by rudra whose head is decorated with a crescent moon, four headed brahmā, indra and all other dēvatās. Such emperumān climbed up to my head.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the tenth pāsuram – āḻvār says “emperumān who is difficult to reach for brahmā, rudra et al, while they worship and glorify his lotus feet, ignored them and climbed my head”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “emperumān who is the refuge for brahmā et al,arrived at the top-most part of my body”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. நெற்றியுள் நின்று என்னை ஆளும் நிரை மலர்ப் பாதங்கள் சூடிக் கற்றைத் துழாய் முடிக் கோலக் கண்ண பிரானைத் தொழுவார் ஒற்றைப் பிறை அணிந்தானும் நான்முகனும் இந்திரனும் மற்றை அமரரும் எல்லாம் வந்து எனது உச்சியுளானே neṟṟi uḷ ninṟu ennai āḷum niṟai malarp pādangaḷ sūdi kaṟṟait tuḻāy mudik kōlak kaṇṇa pirānait toḻuvār oṟṟaip piṟai aṇindānum nānmuganum indiranum maṟṟai amararum ellām vandu enadu ucci uḷānē*

- neṟṟi … – Accepting my service being seated on my forehead.
- *nirai malarp pādangaḷ sūdi* – holding his divine, lotus feet that look like a row of flowers
- *kaṟṟait tuḻāy* … – Even if a dry flower is placed on his head, due to the connection with his divine hair, it will become fresh and grow abundantly. Unto the most magnanimous kriṣṇa who is wearing a divine crown which is decorated with fresh tuḷasi garlands/leaves.
- *oṟṟaip piṟai aṇindānum* … – rudra who wears a crescent moon in his matted hair and who gives happiness, brahmā who is the father of such rudra, indra who manages the dēvatās and all other dēvatās are longing to serve [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) and to attain him; he himself tries to capture me and climbs my head. When the kings travel inside their pleasure/private quarters from one area to another (when they are in happy mood), the confidantes will request and get their tasks done. Similarly, when [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) goes from [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s forehead to head, brahmā et al approach emperumān and get their tasks completed.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.9.11. Ucciyulle nirkum

*ucciuḷḷē niṟkum dēva dēvaṟkuk kaṇṇa pirāṟku iccaiyuḷ sella uṇartti vaṇ kurukūrc catakōpan ic conna āyirattuḷe ivaiyum ōr pattu em pirāṟku niccalum viṇṇappam seyya nīḷ kaḻal senni porumē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ucci uḷḷē niṟkum – (thus) staying on my head; dēva dēvaṟku – for the god of gods; kaṇṇa pirāṟku – maganimous kriṣṇa who has both supremacy (pirān) and simplicity (kriṣṇa); iccai – (his) affection (towards āḻvār); uḷ – inside (āḻvār); sella – occur, having realised; uṇartti – informing that (to him); vaṇ kurukūrc catakōpan – nammāḻvār (who is the most liberal leader of the place named āḻvārtirunagari); icconna āyirattuḷ – In the thousand pāsurams mercifully given by him; ivai – these (which talk about emperumān‘s union with āḻvār); ōr – distinct, incomparable; pattu – ten pāsurams; em pirāṟku – to emperumān; viṇṇappam seyya – recite to him; nīḷ – those which are so long that they reach up to his devotees; kaḻal – his divine, lotus feet; senni – in the heads of those (who recite); niccalum – every day, always; porum – will be fixed

**Перевод:**

**For those who recite to emperumān these ten pāsurams which are in the mood of enjoying emperumān’s union among the thousand pāsurams, the divine, lotus feet (which reach up to his devotees) of kaṇṇan emperumān who has both supremacy and simplicity, will be on their head forever.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the end, āḻvār says “when one recites this decad to emperumān, emperumān’s lotus feet will eternally be placed on his head”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār explains eternal experience with bhagavān as the result of this decad.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. உச்சியுள்ளே நிற்கும் தேவ தேவற்குக் கண்ண பிரானர்க்கு இச்சையுள் செல்ல உணர்த்தி வண் குருகூர்ச் சடகோபன் இச் சொன்ன ஆயிரத்துள்ளே இவையும் ஓர் பத்து எம் பிராற்கு நிச்சலும் விண்ணப்பம் செய்ய நீள் கழல் சென்னி பொருமே ucciuḷḷē niṟkum dēva dēvaṟkuk kaṇṇa pirāṟku iccaiyuḷ sella uṇartti vaṇ kurukūrc catakōpan ic conna āyirattuḷe ivaiyum ōr pattu em pirāṟku niccalum viṇṇappam seyya nīḷ kaḻal senni porumē*

Where was bhagavān planning to go next?

- *ucci uḷḷē niṟkum* – He,  who is the flower that decorates the head of nityasūris (eternally free souls), realising that there is nothing more fragrant than my head, stayed right there. It is also explained as “since he is staying in my head, he becomes dēva dēva (god of gods).
- *uḷḷē niṟkum* – there is nowhere else better than my head.
- *dēva dēvaṟku* – Being the lord of nityasūris is considered insignificant by him (in comparison to staying on [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s head).
- *kaṇṇa pirāṟku* – kriṣṇa who is most helpful.
- *iccai uḷ sella uṇartti* – Informing to [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) that he realised how affectionate emperumān is towards him.
- *vaṇ kurukūrc catakōpan* – the magnanimous [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/), who did not stop with just informing to sarvēśvaran, but also made this available even for samsāris/materialists  (by being born in [āḻvārtirunagari](http://azhwarthirunagari.koyil.org/) and giving tiruvāimoḻi to every one).
- *icconna …* – the ten pāsurams among the thousand which were recited with this mood (of union)
- *em pirāṟku …* – On reciting this to [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), his divine feet will stay connected with the head forever. “*em pirān*” indicates, emperumān’s magnanimous act of approaching āḻvār step-by-step and making āḻvār forget about the lost time (until he was blessed). Unlike [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) who received this mercy step-by-step, those who recite this decad, will receive the mercy immediately. There is no separate fruit for this decad as “*ucciyuḷḷē niṟkum*“, bhagavān staying on the head itself is the result.

Final summary from [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/):

- In the first pāsuram, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) said that [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) arrived in his vicinity.
- In the second pāsuram, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) said that [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) approached his close proximity, after āḻvār was able to understood the first stage.
- In the third pāsuram, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) said that [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) stayed right next to him.
- In the fourth pāsuram, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) said that [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) climbed his hip and stayed there.
- In the fifth pāsuram, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) said that [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) entered his heart.
- In the sixth pāsuram, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) said that [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) climbed his shoulders and stayed there.
- In the seventh pāsuram, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) said that [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) entered his tongue.
- In the eighth pāsuram, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) said that [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) entered his eyes and stayed there.
- In the ninth pāsuram, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) said that [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) stayed in his forehead.
- In the tenth pāsuram, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) said that [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) climbed his head.
- Finally, he said that since emperumān bonded with him step-by-step, he placed emperumān on his head. He completes the decad with (that) result.

Thus ends the English translation for tiruvāimoḻi 1st centum 9th decad.

## 1.10 Poruma nilpadai

## 1.10.1. Poruma nilpadai

*poru mā nīḷ padai āḻi sangattodutiru mā nīḷ kaḻal ēḻ ulagum toḻaoru māṇik kuṟaḷāgi nimirnda akkarumāṇikkam en kaṇṇuḷadu āgumē*

**Пословный перевод:**

poru – to destroy the enemies; mā – (because of that) being great; nīḷ – that which grows (along with his form); padai – weapons; āḻi sangattodu – with sangu (conch), cakkaram (disc); tiru – having the symbols indicating that he is the master of srī mahālakśmi; mā – being great; nīḷ – reaching (up to the devotees); kaḻal – lotus feet; ēḻ ulagum – (without any discrimination between learned and ignorant) all universes; toḻa – performing service joyfully which is fitting for a servitor; oru – distinct; māṇik kuṟaḷāy – assuming the form of a celibate dwarf (who has the quality of taking alms); nimirnda – mercifully grew (after accomplishing the goal); a(k) – one with such glories; karumāṇikkam – one who is beautiful to the sight like a blue gem; en kaṇṇuḷadu – become visible for my eyes; āgum – happens

**Перевод:**

**emperumān appeared as a celibate dwarf who is beautiful to the sight like a blue gem, mercifully grew into a great form with the weapons such as conch and disc that also grew along with him and are great because of that. Having great lotus feet which have the symbols indicating that he is the master of srī mahālakśmi, that stretched all the way to the devotees to be served by every one in all universes (matching their nature of being servitors), he manifested this form to my eyes.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the first pāsuram, āḻvār repeats how emperumān manifested his qualities such as saundarya (beauty), sauseelya (simplicity) etc., and attracted āḻvār, made āḻvār fully exist for him, and mixed with him up to the top.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*In the first pāsuram, āḻvār says “emperumān, just like favouring everyone through his trivikrama incarnation, manifested that form to my eyes”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*First pāsuram – āḻvār briefly explains the meanings of this whole decad in this pāsuram. āḻvār contemplates “While mahābali was not expecting to see emperumān, he went to him as a mendicant and received ownership of something which already belonged to him. Similarly, though I was not thinking about emperumān, he himself came to me and manifested his beautiful form to my eyes” and becomes pleased. பொரு மா நீள் படை ஆழி சங்கத்தொடுதிரு மா நீள் கழல் ஏழ் உலகும் தொழஒரு மாணிக் குறள் ஆகி நிமிர்ந்த அக்கரு மாணிக்கம் என் கண்ணுளது ஆகுமே poru mā nīḷ padai āḻi sangattodutiru mā nīḷ kaḻal ēḻ ulagum toḻaoru māṇik kuṟaḷāgi nimirnda akkarumāṇikkam en kaṇṇuḷadu āgumē*

- *poru* – fight – While measuring the worlds, the divine weapons showed their anger over namuci (mahābali’s son) et al. It is also explained that the different weapons competed against each other. But first explanation is more apt. iraṇḍām tiruvandādi 71st pāsuram “*idangai valampuri ninṟārppa … vidangālum tīvāyaravaṇai mēl tōnṟal …*” which reveals similar meaning is explained by nampiḷḷai. “*idangai valampuri ninṟārppa*” – srī pāncajanyam hailed [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s victory; srī sudarasanam spew fire and drove away the enemies. “*vidangālum tīvāyaravaṇai*” – tiruvanantāḻvān  (ādi sēśan) too is always spewing hot fire to keep the enemies away from [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/). This is explained further in nānmugan tiruvandādi 10 “*āngu āravāram adu kēttu aḻal umiḻum pūngāraravaṇai…*” – Place is āngu (there – paramapadam); Sound is adu (that – āravāram – recital of sāma vēdam) where nitya sūris are happily saying “ahamannam ahamannam ahamannam, ahamannādōhamannādōahammnāda:” (I am enjoyed by him repeatedly and I am the enjoyer who is enjoying his enjoying me, repeatedly). For such devotees who care for [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) in paramapadam, what to speak of this material realm? And the reason for such fear in nityasūris is due to “*aravaṇai mēl tōnṟal*” – One who is having ādiśēśan (the softest bed) as his bed, is now measuring all the forests etc., with his very tender lotus feet – so his dear devotees are fearing for his well-being. This is called “*astānē bhaya sankai”* (having fear unnecessarily) – one need not fear for [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) who is all capable, yet the devotees fear for him due to great overwhelming love. Even after vibhīśaṇa surrendering to srī rāma saying “*rāgavam saraṇam gata:*” (I surrender unto srī rāma – srī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 17.14), sugrīva doubts him and tells srī rāma to destroy him by saying “*vadyatām*” (let him be killed – srī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 17.27). Similarly, srī lakhmaṇa said “*bharatasya vadē dōśam nāham pasyāmi*” (there is nothing wrong in killing bharata – srī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 96.24) – he doubted bharatāḻvān’s intentions out of great love for srī rāma.
- *mā* – the greatness of the divine form of the weapons; it is also explained as their partiality towards the devotees even more than [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) himself. It is explained in viṣṇu darmam 78th adyāyam, “*avyāhatāni kriṣṇasya cakrādīnyāydāni tam \| rakśanti sakalāpadbhyō yēna viṣṇurupāsita: \|\|*” That prapanna who worships kriṣṇa is protected from all dangers by [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s weapons such as tiruvāḻi (cakram)” etc) – even if emperumān becomes their enemy, they will try to protect such devotees (who had vorśipped him before). When it protects such persons, it is obvious that emperumān’s devotees would always be protected.
- *nīḷ padai* – The weapons try to over-do [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) in his efforts, by competitively growing along with him.
- *tiru mā nīḷ kaḻal ēḻ ulagum toḻa* – As stated in stōtra ratnam 31 “*kadā puna:*” (when) – you placed your lotus feet which are desired by me, on the heads of those who have no such desire.
- *tiru* – having auspicious symbols such as flag, lotus flower etc., which indicate [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s wealth/control
- *mā* – most vorśippable
- *nīḷ kaḻal* – the divine feet that will stretch up to those who have even a little bit of desire for that
- *ēḻ ulagum toḻa* – to be vorśipped by the people of universe who have not even performed any other sādanam such as karma, jñāna, bhakti yōgams.
- *oru* – distinct – even if [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) desires to assume such beautiful form, it will be impossible for him
- *māṇi* – brahmacāri (celibate) – assuming a form that matches the quality of taking alms, hiding that he is the master of srī mahālakśmi herself (who is the top-most wealth)
- kuṟaḷāgi – became very dwarfish such that the4 huge form could be seen by the eyes
- *nimirnda* – As soon as water was poured (to complete the charity of three feet of land), he grew. This is because, he is known as “*vāsudēva taru*” (the tree known as vāsudēva who gives shadow to everyone). The whole sky was filled with his form’s divine beauty.
- *ak karumāṇikkam* – “That” black gem – Even [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) who was blessed with defect-less knowledge by [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) could not comprehend “that” (there are so much glories).
- *en kaṇṇuḷadāgumē* – The people of the universes don’t know his glories. But since āḻvār knows his glories he says “*en kaṇṇuḷadāgumē*” (visible to my eyes). “kaṇ” also means “idam” meaning that he is in me. Since he compared [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) to “*karumāṇikkam*” (an insentient), he is saying “*kaṇṇuḷadu āgum*” (instead of saying *kaṇṇuḷānāgum*).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.10.2. Kannulle nirkum

*kaṇuḷḷē niṟkum kādanmaiyāl toḻil eṇṇilum varum en ini vēṇḍuvam maṇṇum nīrum eriyum nal vāyuvum viṇṇum āy viriyum em pirānaiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

maṇṇum nīrum eriyum nal vāyuvum viṇṇum āy – Having the five elements – prutivi (earth), ap (water), agni (fire), vāyu (air) and ākāśam (ether) as prakāram (forms); viriyum – expand into the form of universe; empirānai – my master; kādanmaiyāl – attachment out of devotion; toḻil – while doing praṇāmam (obeisances), arcanā (glorification) etc; kaṇ uḷḷē – not leaving their vision as said in bhagavat gītā 4.11 “tāms tataiva bhajāmi aham” (I reciprocate appropriately for those devoted persons); niṟkum – eternally exist; eṇṇilum – merely by contemplating his existence as said in taittiriya upaniśat “asti brahmēti cēdvēda” (when he knows that brahmam exists); varum – arrive at him (at his disposal); ini – after emperumān being easily approachable in both difficult and easy means; en vēṇḍuvam – (for us who have no other refuge) is there anything to be done?

**Перевод:**

**For those who worship emperumān with attachment derived out of bhakti, emperumān who has the five elements as his form, who is my master, becomes eternally placed in front of them. For those who accept his existence too, he is at their disposal. After this, is there anything to be done by us?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the second pāsuram, āḻvār becomes absorbed in emperumān‘s quality of ultimate easy approacability for the most devoted towards him and the ones who just contemplate upon him.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says that sarvēśvaran who is the cause of everything is accessible for those who are completely devoted towards him and those who just accept his existence.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Second pāsuram – āḻvār says emperumān becomes available equally for both paramabhakti (ultimate devotion) and parigaṇanā (counting). கண்ணுள்ளே நிற்கும் காதன்மையால் தொழில் எண்ணிலும் வரும் என் இனி வேண்டுவம் மண்ணும் நீரும் எரியும் நல் வாயுவும் விண்ணும் ஆய் விரியும் எம் பிரானையே? kaṇuḷḷē niṟkum kādanmaiyāl toḻil eṇṇilum varum en ini vēṇḍuvam maṇṇum nīrum eriyum nal vāyuvum viṇṇum āy viriyum em pirānaiyē*

- *kaṇṇuḷḷē niṟkum kādanmaiyāl toḻil* – When one worships with paramabhakti (ultimate devotion), [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) will eternally stay in their vicinity. When they cannot exist without him, he too will not be able to separate from them and will always stay in front of them.
- *eṇṇilum varum* – Few explanations:
   - Even if one counts [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) along with other objects like gatam (pot), patam (cloth), [īśvara (bhagavān),](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) will arrive in front of him thinking “at least he did not deny my existence and counted me along with these objects”.
   - If one says “there are [24 insentient entities](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/09/thathva-thrayam-achith-what-is-matter/), [jīvātmā (sentient)](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) is 25th entity and [īśvaran](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is 26th element”, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) will say “At least he accepted my existence along with these entities” and arrive in front of him.
   - He would arrive even one is not thinking about him (out of his own will).
   - When one counts 21, 22, 23, 24, 25, 26, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) will say “I am 26” and come in front of him.
- *varum* – will come – It does not mean that he will always be there. If someone says “go” on seeing [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), he would be prepared to do that as well.
- *en ini vēṇḍuvam* – When [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) arrives equally for ultimate devotion and mere contemplation/counting, is there any worry for me? When emperumān is simply looking for apratiśēdam (non-prohibition) and arrive at him at an opportune time, what does the [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) need to do for his own welfare? A prapanna simply means one, who understands this true nature of [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) \[being most compassionate\]. Just like emperumān explained about his nature and said in bhagavat gītā 18.66 “*mā suca:*” (do not worry) to say “you do not have to fear for the losses occurred due to your own defects”, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) too thinks about [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s true nature and says “*en ini vēṇḍuvam*“. For the goal to be accomplished, non-prohibition (not stopping emperumān from bestowing that goal) is only required. Any other qualification or disqualification is insignificant. vēl vetti nambiyār enquires [nampiḷḷai](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/09/16/nampillai-english/) “When perumāḷ (srī rāma) surrendered unto the ocean (samudrarāja), he did that facing east etc. Does saraṇāgati also have certain rules/regulations like other means?” [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/) replies “vibhīśaṇāḻvān instructed perumāḷ to surrender to samudrarāja. But he himself did not even take a holy-dip in the ocean before surrendering unto perumāḷ. From this we can understand that since perumāḷ was born in ikśvāku vamsam and is one who gives great importance to such ācāram (purification etc), he followed such rules. Since vibhīśaṇāḻvān was born in rākśasa family, he did not follow any rules before surrendering. So, a qualified person need not give up his qualification and unqualified person need not earn qualification. Thus, this upāyam (saraṇāgati) is sarvādikāram (can be pursued by all without discrimination)”. Those who understand [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s greatness, will have faith in this.Others who think that the result is given by the rituals themselves, will not have clear understanding of this principle.
- *maṇṇum …* – [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is the most magnanimous person and the antaryāmi (in-dwelling soul) of the five great elements which are the manifested form of his as explained in taittiriya upaniśat “*bahusyām*” (let me be many). [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says “When such sarvēśvaran who is the sustaining force for all entities other than himself, thinks that he exists for those who have even a little bit of attachment towards him, what is there to worry for this [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)?” vāyu is stated as nal vāyu (good air) since it helps sustaining everyone.
- *viṇṇumāy* – being the antaryāmi for ākāśam (ether) etc.
- *viriyum* – expands, becomes manifested as stated in “*bahusyām*“.
- *empirān* – one who helps me

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.
