## 1.10.3. Em piranai

*em pirānai endai tandai tandaikkum tam pirānait taṇ tāmaraik kaṇṇanai kombu arāvu nuṇ nēr idai mārbanai em pirānait toḻāy mada nenjamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

madam – having humility to obey the instructions; nenjamē – Oh heart!; em – my; pirānai – One who favours (by bestowing advēśam (not having hatred), ābhimukyam (friendliness) etc); endai tandai tandaikkum – for our clan (instead of stopping with just us); tam pirānai – being the master; taṇ – cool vision (due to this relationship between us); tāmaraik kaṇṇanai – having lotus eyes; kombu – a type of wind instrument (like a horn); arāvu – snake; nuṇ – leaner than; nēr – honest/straight; idai – srī mahālakśmi who is having such waist; mārbanai – having in the chest; em pirānai – master; toḻāy – worship him

**Перевод:**

**Oh humble/obedient heart! Please attempt to worship emperumān who favours us with advēśam, ābhimukyam etc., towards him, who is the master of our entire clan, one who is having lotus-like eyes which shed coolness towards all, who has in his chest srī mahālakhmi who has very thin straight waist (which is leaner than a kombu and snake).**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the third pāsuram, āḻvār contemplates emperumān‘s relationship with srī mahālakśmi which is the cause of his easy approachable nature towards his devotees and instructs his mind “Oh humble heart! worship him”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār instructs his heart to enjoy emperumān who has most enjoyable qualities such as being the master of srī mahālakśmi etc.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Third pāsuram – āḻvār tells his heart “You have seen his nature \[of being equal towards all in helping them\]; you too should behave according to your nature \[of servitude towards him\]”. எம் பிரானை எந்தை தந்தை தந்தைக்கும் தம் பிரானை தண் தாமரைக் கண்ணனை கொம்பு அராவு நுண் நேர் இடை மார்பனை எம்பிரானைத் தொழாய் மட நெஞ்சமே em pirānai endai tandai tandaikkum tam pirānait taṇ tāmaraik kaṇṇanai kombu arāvu nuṇ nēr idai mārbanai em pirānait toḻāy mada nenjamē*

- *em pirānai* – contemplating on the simplicity of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) which was highlighted in the previous pāsuram, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says “my master”.
- *endai tandai tandaikkum tam pirānai* – āḻvār says “Not only [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) helped me with causeless grace, but he is the master for my entire clan”.

On hearing [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s praises, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who knows the distinction of the praising of prayōjanāntarapara (one who desires for ulterior goals) and ananyaprayōjana (one who is fully situated in servitude only), blessed him with his merciful glance.

- *taṇ tāmaraik kaṇṇanai* – cool lotus-eyed [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/).

[āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) wondered, why is [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) blessing him (since he considers himself as not having done anything favourable towards emperumān), when emperumān himself said in [srī bhagavat gītā](http://githa.koyil.org/) 16.19 “*tānaham dviśata: krūrān samsārēśu narādamān \| kśipāmi …* ” (Those who offend me, who hate me, who are cruel in nature, who are dirty, who are lowest among mankind, I place such persons repeatedly in this ocean of birth and in demoniac births which are unfavourable to attain me) and realised the one who triggers such blessing is seated in close proximity of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/).

- *kombarāvu nuṇ nēridai mārbanai* – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) having [srī mahālakśmi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/) in his chest. two explanations for [tāyār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/)‘s waist:
   - [tāyār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/)‘s waist looking like kombu and aravu, yet leaner than those.  aravu is expanded as arāvu.
   - arāvu also means reducing/sharpening. Here it means, her waist appears to be even reduced in size in comparison to kombu.
- *em pirānai* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) saying “*em pirānai*” once specifically to glorify the togetherness of perumāḷ and tāyār.
- *toḻāy* – The vorśippable object is a [divine couple](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/08/17/divya-dhampathi/) \[so, you worship\].
- *mada nenjamē* – My heart is so obedient/qualified to receive the instruction “[*toḻudu eḻu*](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/03/thiruvaimozhi-1-1-1-uyarvara-uyarnalam/)” (worship and arise)

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.10.4. Nenjame nallai

*nenjamē nallai nallai unnaip peṟṟāl en seyyōm ini enna kuṟaivinam maindanai malarāḷ maṇavāḷanait tunjum pōdum vidādu todar kaṇḍāy*

**Пословный перевод:**

nenjamē – Oh heart (which is the abode of knowledge)!; nallai nallai – (what you have done is) very good; unnaip peṟṟāl – when I have you; en seyyōm – what can I not accomplish?; ini – after having acquired your acceptance; enna kuṟaivinam – is there anything that is impossible for us? What deficiency do we have?; maindanai – (then) one who is eternally youthful; malarāḷ – to śrī mahālkśmi who is infinitely enjoyable; maṇavāḷanai – one who is the enjoyer; tunjum pōdum – even while we are finished; vidādu – without leaving; todar kaṇḍāy – try to engage with him

**Перевод:**

**Oh heart! What you have done is very good. When I have you, what can I not accomplish? After having your acceptance, is there anything impossible for us? Thus, even if we are being finished (due to separation from emperumān), you keep engaging with him who is the eternally youthful enjoyer of the infinitely enjoyable śrī mahālakśmi.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In fourth pāsuram – āḻvār contemplates his own lowly nature and mercifully instructs his heart “Even if you are unable to sustain yourself in separation from emperumān, you have to hold on to him”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār being delighted on seeing that his heart is following his orders, tells it “You try to enjoy him incessantly”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

- *tunjum pōdum vidādu todar kaṇḍāy* – Here two slōkams are quoted – srī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 31.5 “*na ca sītā tvayā hīnā*” (sītā who is separated from you will not survive) and srī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 27.17 “*yastvayā saha …*” (When I am with you it is heaven and when I am separated from you it is hell).

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Fourth pāsuram – āḻvār glorifies his heart on seeing it following his orders and vorśipping emperumān, instructs his heart “Even if I leave him citing my lowly nature, you hold on to him”. நெஞ்சமே நல்லை நல்லை உன்னைப் பெற்றால் என் செய்யோம்? இனி என்ன குறைவினம்? மைந்தனை மலராள் மணவாளனைத் துஞ்சும் போதும் விடாது தொடர் கண்டாய் nenjamē nallai nallai unnaip peṟṟāl en seyyōm ini enna kuṟaivinam maindanai malarāḷ maṇavāḷanait tunjum pōdum vidādu todar kaṇḍāy*

- *nenjamē nallai nallai* – Just like parents embrace their children who obediently completed a task, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) embraces his heart and glorifies it.
- *nenjamē nallai nallai* – Why is the repetition in appreciating his heart? Just like [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) sends a messenger to [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/), it appears to him that he also needs to send a messenger to his own heart which already reached [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) leaving āḻvār behind as explained in tiruviruttam 30 “*en nenjināraik kaṇḍāl ennaic colli avaridai nīr innam selleerō*” (If you see my respectable heart, you ask on behalf of me why he has not reached bhagavān with my message yet?). Since it is “*munduṟṟa nenju*” (the heart which headed towards emperumān even before me), [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) glorifies it repeatedly.

When the heart asks “Why are you praising me like this?”

- *unnaip peṟṟāl en seyyōm* – When you are in sync with me and speak the same principles, what can I not accomplish? [īśvaran](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is there to bless the result; you are there to not push it aside; thus, is there anything not possible to accomplish?
- *ini enna kuṟaivinam* – In previous phrase, it looked like I mistakenly said that “**I** can accomplish anything” . But when [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is ready to unconditionally help us, what is it that we can do? When he is the means eternally without any expectation, there is nothing for us to independently pursue.

When asked “But, is there nothing we need to do?” [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says “Yes, there is something for us to do” \[Further explaining, that when [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) pursues us, we have to hold on to him instead of ignoring the great opportunity\].

- *maindanai* – can any one leave this \[eternally youthful\] [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)?. maindu – sweetness, beauty, strength.
- *malarāḷ maṇavāḷanai* – I am telling you to never leave [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is inseparable from periya pirāttiyār herself as she said in tiruvāimoḻi 6.10.10 “*agalagillēn iṟaiyum*” (I will never leave even for a moment).
- *tunjum pōdum vidādu todar kaṇḍāy* – Even if I say I am “unqualified” and try to leave, you have to hold on to him. vislēśam (separation) is explained as vināsam (destruction). For him tunjudal (getting destroyed) means separation as explained in srī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 31.5 “*muhūrttamapi jīvāva:*” (we will stay alive for only a moment after separating from you – said by srī lakśmaṇa to srī rāma). [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says “even I  tell you leave him, you don’t leave him”.  He further says “You drink [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) just like drinking medicine” and “You enjoy [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) from whom [pirātti](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/) is saying ‘*agalagillēn iṟaiyum*‘”.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.10.5. Kandaye nenje

*kaṇḍāyē nenjē! karumangaḷ vāykkinṟu ōr eṇ tānum inṟiyē vandu iyalumāṟu uṇḍānai ulagēḻum ōr adi koṇḍānaik kaṇḍu koṇḍanai nīyumē*

**Пословный перевод:**

nenjē – Oh mind!; karumangaḷ – actions (such as advēśam (not having enmity), ābhimukyam (friendliness), āsrayaṇam (surrendering), aṟivu (knowledge), nalam (bhakti/devotion) etc); vāykkinṟu – fructifying; ōr – a; eṇḍhānum inṟiyē – even without contemplation; vandiyalum – happening for us; āṟu – way/means; kaṇḍāyē – have you seen?; ulagu ēḻum – all universes; uṇḍānai – safely placed in his stomach (during praḷayam (annihilation)); ōr – unique/distinct; mūvadi koṇḍānai – established them as subservient to him by assuming the form of trivikrama; nīyum – you too (who don’t have ābhimukyam (friendliness) towards him); kaṇḍu koṇḍanai – received it

**Перевод:**

**Oh mind! Did you see how the results are fructified for us even without contemplating on actions (such as advēśam, ābimukhyam, āsrayaṇam etc)? Like he consumed and safely placed all the universes in his stomach (without their expecting him to do so) and how he established their subservience by measuring the worlds marking his victory over them, you too received his benevolence.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fifth pāsuram, āḻvār says that though he did not even think about emperumān, emperumān pursued him without any reason.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār tells his mind “Seeing us getting the results without even desiring for that, you too, can see us approaching him”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Fifth pāsuram – āḻvār explains to his heart – What we said previously “eṇṇilum varum” (mere contemplation will bring him) is even too much! His nature is such \[that he will appear to us even without our contemplation\]. கண்டாயே நெஞ்சே! கருமங்கள் வாய்க்கின்று ஓர் எண் தானும் இன்றியே வந்து இயலுமாறு உண்டானை உலகு ஏழும் ஓர் மூவடி கொண்டானைக் கண்டுகொண்டனை நீயுமே kaṇḍāyē nenjē! karumangaḷ vāykkinṟu ōr eṇ tānum inṟiyē vandu iyalumāṟu uṇḍānai ulagēḻum ōr adi koṇḍānaik kaṇḍu koṇḍanai nīyumē*

- *kaṇḍāyē nenjē* – See that what I have said about fructified results is true \[In arumpadam, it is highlighted that one of the explanations for “[*eṇṇilum varum*](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/10/thiruvaimozhi-1-10-2-kannulle-nirkum/)” – “even without our effort [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) will come” is the focus here\].
- *nenjē* – Oh heart/mind! I don’t need to explicitly tell you since you are the origin of knowledge.
- *karumangaḷ vāykkinṟu* – While the actions fructify.
- *ōr eṇ tānum inṟiyē vandiyalumāṟu kaṇḍāyē* – You see that [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) appeared even without our thinking about him, where he considers “eṇṇilum varum” (when contemplated, he will appear) is even too much to expect. His supremacy can be explained, but his simplicity is beyond the expression of words.

[āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is showing examples to establish that results fructify even without desire in us.

- *uṇḍānai …* – Does the universe ([acit](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/09/thathva-thrayam-achith-what-is-matter/) – insentient) have the ability to think that “[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) will protect by placing me in his stomach”? “*ulagēḻum*” is to be applied for both in “*uṇḍānai*” ([emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) consuming all universes) and “*ōr mūvadi koṇḍānai*” (measuring all universes). Similarly, when he was measuring the universe, would the universe realise that emperumān is placing his lotus feet on my head?
- *kaṇḍu koṇḍānai nīyumē* – You, who have the ability to reject his favour, are seeing it now. During praḷayam (annihilation), the universe does not have the ability to reject his favour. But here, we have no reason to reject his favours. Since in those cases (measuring worlds etc), they received his mercy unexpectedly, they could not reject \[But you (heart/mind) having knowledge, could have rejected his favour, but you did not – so you are to be appreciated\].

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.10.6. Niyum nanum

*nīyum nānum in nēr niṟkil mēl maṟṟōr nōyum sār kodān nenjamē! sonnēn tāyum tandaiyum āy iv vulaginil vāyum īsan maṇivaṇṇan endaiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tāyāyum – being affectionate like mother; tandaiyāyum – looking after the well-being like father; ivvulaginil – in this world (which does not understand his glories); vāyum – descended; īsan – out of his eternal lordship; maṇivaṇṇan – manifesting his beautiful bluish gem like form to me, benevolently; endai – being my master accepting my service (by doing all which had been said thus far); nenjamē – Oh heart!; nīyum – you (who are humble to be ordained to worship) also; nānum – me (who is having you as my tool); i – in this manner explained thus far; nēr – not reject his favour; niṟkil – if we stand by; mēl – future; maṟṟu – anything else (other than what is natural); ōr nōyum – any disease; sārkodān – will not let them approach us; sonnēn – told you (this most important meaning)

**Перевод:**

**bhagavān who is like mother who looks after the desires of the children and father who looks after the well-being of the children, descended into this world solely due to his eternal relationship and favoured me with his bluish gem like form and thus became my master. Oh heart! If you and I stand by the aspect of not rejecting his help as explained thus far, I tell you that emperumān will ensure that no diseases would approach us for eternity.**

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the sixth pāsuram – When the heart said “such easily approachable emperumān will not leave us”, āḻvār says to his heart “If we stop leaving him citing our disqualification and acknowledge his help, he will never leave us”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says to his heart “if both of us are aligned in our speech, emperumān who has most distinct relationship with us, will never let us grieve”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. நீயும் நானும் இந் நேர் நிற்கில் மேல் மற்றோர் நோயும் சார் கொடான் நெஞ்சமே! சொன்னேன் தாயும் தந்தையும் ஆய் இவ் உலகினில் வாயும் ஈசன் மணிவண்ணன் எந்தையே nīyum nānum in nēr niṟkil mēl maṟṟōr nōyum sār kodān nenjamē! sonnēn tāyum tandaiyum āy iv vulaginil vāyum īsan maṇivaṇṇan endaiyē*

- *nīyum nānum innēr niṟkil* – If you, who went behind garudāḻvār (in search of [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)) and I, having you as my assistant. who are going to enjoy the results, remain without excluding his help, i.e., as long as we are not like it is stated in srī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 36.11 “*na namēyam*” ( I will not worship).
- *mēl maṟṟōr nōyum sārkodān* – he will protect from following types of diseases of leaving [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/):
   - considering oneself very lowly and leaving [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)
   - praying for ulterior benefits from [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) and on acquiring them, leaving him after that
   - considering oneself as disqualified to approach [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) and thus leaving him
   - pursuing other means (like karma jñāna bhakti yōgams etc) and leaving [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) \[It would take a really long time to reach [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) by these means\]
   - reaping the results of previous sins which will lead to leaving [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)
- *nenjamē sonnēn* – In this situation, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is like [tirukkōśtiyūr nambi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/thirukkoshtiyur-nambi/) who preserved the confidentiality of bhagavat viśayam from others \[Even to instruct the meanings of carama slōkam, he made [emperumānār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/emperumanar/) walk 18 times and he instructed only after [emperumānār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/emperumanar/) vowed not to reveal it to unqualified persons\]! After explaining to his heart, āḻvār regrets/censures like kriṣṇa who said in [bhagavat gītā](http://githa.koyil.org/) 18.67 “*idam tē na atapaskāya*” (Do not reveal to those who are not austere). kriṣṇa revealed carama slōkam ([bhagavat gītā](http://githa.koyil.org/) 18.66) to arjuna after seeing draupati’s pitiful state of disheveled hair. But after revealing that, thinking about the greatness of carama slōkam, he thinks “I have thrown a very expensive gem into the sea” and said “*padaṇ padaṇ*” (alas! alas!). Second explanation is: my instruction is valuable, but those who do not have faith in this will not benefit.
- *tāyum tandaiyumāy* – Caring like mother and father, but is much greater than they are.
- *ivvulaginil vāyum īsan* – When a child falls into a well, the mother will jump in there as well to rescue the child – similarly, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) jumps into samsāram to rescue the [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)s from here.

What is the reason for him descending here?

- *īsan* – Since he is the rightful master. Alternatively it can be explained that he descends into the material realm, eliminates the lordship of others and thus establishes his supremacy over all.
- *maṇivaṇṇan endaiyē* – By showing his physical beauty, he eliminated my material desires, he showed his lordship and established my servitude towards him.

As declared \[by vēda vyāsa bhagavān\] “…*satyam satyam…*” (There is no sāstram greater than vēdam, there is no God superior to kēsava – this is truth, truth and truth again), this is truth.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.10.7. Entaiye enrum

*endaiyē enṟum em perumān enṟum sindaiyuḷ vaippan solluvan pāviyēn endai emperumān enṟu vānavar sindaiyuḷ vaittuc collum selvanaiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vānavar – residents of paramapadam (srīvaikuṇṭam); endai – one who is our sustenance etc; emperumān enṟu – our supreme master; sindaiyuḷ vaittu – contemplating thus; sollum – one who is said like that; selvanai – one who has such wealth; pāviyēn – sinful me; endaiyē enṟum – saying “Oh the one who looks after my well-being!”; emperumān enṟum – saying “Oh my master!”; sindaiyuḷ – in my heart too; vaippan – keeping; solluvan – will say as well

**Перевод:**

**emperumān is having the wealth of being contemplated by the nityasūris as the one who sustains them etc., and as their supreme master. I, who am very sinful, too have kept such emperumān as the one who looks after my well being, my master in my heart and spoken the same as well.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is upset on himself for thinking/speaking like nityasūris though he himself was very sinful, thereby causing disrepute to [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/).

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the seventh pāsuram – āḻvār says “I who am most fallen, committed a mistake by trying to meditate upon and speak about emperumān who is most distinct \[distinctly great\]” and leaves emperumān.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār, meditating upon emperumān‘s greatness which is enjoyed by nityasūris, and considering his own fallen nature, tries to leave emperumān.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*In the seventh pāsuram – āḻvār \[previously\] glorified emperumān as “maṇivaṇṇan endai” (my father/master who has a precious-gem-hued form) and considering his own lowly nature,  leaves emperumān. What he feared in “tunjum pōdum vidādu todar kaṇḍāy” became reality here.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Seventh pāsuram – What he feared previously, became reality now – i.e., he claims himself to be “ayōjña” (unqualified) and leaves emperumān. எந்தையே என்றும் எம் பெருமான் என்றும் சிந்தையுள் வைப்பன் சொல்லுவன் பாவியேன் எந்தை எம் பெருமான் என்று வானவர் சிந்தையுள் வைத்துச் சொல்லும் செல்வனையே endaiyē enṟum em perumān enṟum sindaiyuḷ vaippan solluvan pāviyēn endai emperumān enṟu vānavar sindaiyuḷ vaittuc collum selvanaiyē*

- *endaiyē enṟum* – saying “Oh the one who cares \[like a father\] for me!”
- *emperumān enṟum* – saying “Oh rightful master!”
- *sindaiyuḷ vaippan* – I am keeping this in my heart wherein I have contemplated about many \[lowly/materialistic\] things.

Did I stop with just contemplating about him (which is known only to me)?

- *solluvan* – I brought disrepute to him by speaking about him which becomes known to others.
- *pāviyēn* – two explanations:
   - I am such a sinful person who had taken birth to simply bring disrepute to the one who is enjoyed by great personalities.
   - Just as when a sātvika (person in the mode of goodness), out of rage sets fire in a house and when he regains his goodness, will feel distressed for his act – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) glorified [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) and thinks that it is not fitting for him to glorify and thus scolds himself.

Why are you saying this? Are contemplating upon [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) and speaking about him results from previous sins? It is like a dog touching the offerings which are kept for a yajña (ritual) – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) considers himself lowly and says that [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is to be enjoyed by nityasūris (eternally free souls) should not be touched by him.

- *endai …* – nityasūris who cannot sustain themselves even for a moment without thinking about [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/), out of such overflowing experience say out of their heart “Oh the one who cares for us! Oh our master!” What have I done by glorifying [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) with such wealth!

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.10.8. Selva naranan

*selva(n) nāraṇan enṟa sol kēttatum malgum kaṇ pani nāduvan māyamē allu nal pagalum idai vīdu inṟi nalgi ennai vidān nambi nambiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

selva(n) nāraṇan enṟa – “srīman nārāyaṇan”; sol – divine name; kēttalum – on hearing; kaṇ – eye; pani – tears; malgum – flowing; nāduvan – started searching (from where is this coming); māyamē – this is amazing; nambi – bhagavān who is complete; nal – having goodness (to be approached); allum – in the night; pagalum – in the day; idai vīdinṟi – without any break; nalgi – being friendly; ennai – me; nambi – considering me as his property; vidān – will not leave me

**Перевод:**

**As soon as I heard the name “srīman nārāyaṇan”, tears started flowing from my eyes and I started searching for him.  How amazing is this! The complete bhagavān who has the goodness (to be approached by all), being friendly during day and night without any break, considers me as his own, would not leave me.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the eighth pāsuram – āḻvār says “When I left emperumān. considering \[me\] to be unqualified, I accidentally heard bhagavān‘s names and hence I am incapable of moving away from him; He too is attached to me and hence not leaving me. How amazing!”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “Even as I was thus thinking to leave him, bhagavān who is complete, made me fall head over heels on hearing his names; such emperumān will not leave me”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Eighth pāsuram – āḻvār says “I committed a mistake by contemplating upon him and speaking about him. I need to avoid that” and “I need to go to a place where his qualities are not discussed and stay there” and goes to a secluded location and stays there with his head covered with a cloth to conceal his identity. A passer-by who carries heavy weight, being unable to bear that weight, unloaded that there and sighed saying “sriman nārāyaṇan“. āḻvār becomes astonished that his senses have become mesmerized on hearing those words. செல்வ(ன்) நாரணன் என்ற சொல் கேட்டலும் மல்கும் கண் பனி நாடுவன் மாயமே அல்லும் நன் பகலும் இடை வீடு இன்றி நல்கி என்னை விடான் நம்பி நம்பியே selva(n) nāraṇan enṟa sol kēttatum malgum kaṇ pani nāduvan māyamē allu nal pagalum idai vīdu inṟi nalgi ennai vidān nambi nambiyē*

- *selva(n) nāraṇan enṟa sol kēttalum* – Due to [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s influence over others, no one talks about brahmacāri nārāyaṇan in his proximity but only talks about “srīman nārāyaṇan” \[literal translation of selva nāraṇan\]. He does not even need to analyze the meaning of this word – just hearing that word will bring out great distress for him \[thinking about separation from such [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)\]. Is that possible? Yes, just like some mantrams have an effect in removing the poison from one’s body just on hearing them, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) becomes distressed just on hearing [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s name.
- *malgum kaṇpani nāduvan* – His eyes spontaneously shed tears and his heart too spontaneously searches for [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/).
- *māyamē* – This is astonishing; To leave emperumān I \[my consent\] was required, but to unite with [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), I am \[my consent is\] not required.

What did [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) do after that?

- *allum nal pagalum …* –  Since this is the time when [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) himself made [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) captivated towards him, āḻvār says “*nalla allum nalla pagalum*” (the good night and the good day). [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) being friendly towards [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) day and night, being complete and pursuing/accepting me, will not give up on me. āḻvār says “As soon as I heard his name, my eyes were filled with tears and my heart started searching for him. How amazing is this!”.
- *idai vīdinṟi* – I searched for him and gave up. But he continuously pursued me in a friendly manner.
- *ennai vidān nambi nambiyē* – Since I am incomplete,  the complete [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) will not leave me knowing my abilities.
- *nambi* – he will consider me as worthy and hence will not give up on me.
- *nambiyē* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says “For acquiring a [samsāri cētana](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) (bound soul who is imperfect) and yet considering as if its a great achievement, only [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is called paripūrṇa (most complete) by all”.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.10.9. Nambiyait tenkurungudi

*nambiyait tenkuṟungudi ninṟa ac cemponē tigaḻum tiru mūrttiyai umbar vānavar ādi am sōdiyai empirānai en solli maṟappanō?*

**Пословный перевод:**

then kuṟungudi – In tirukkuṟungudi \[then – south/beautiful\]; ninṟa – due to him standing there; nambiyai – one who is filled with all auspicious qualities; a – such (even more beautiful than in paramapadam); cempon – like molten-red gold; tigaḻum – radiant; tirumūrttiyai – having divine form; umbar – great; vānavar – for nityasūris; ādi – being the cause for their sustenance, etc; am – most beautiful that makes others see him always; sōdiyai – one who is known by the term “paramjyōti” (supremely effulgent); em pirānai – one who accepted my servitude after making me experience (such wonderful form); en solli – what will I say; maṟappan – to forget

**Перевод:**

**What reason can I say to forget emperumān who is complete due to his standing in tirukkuṟungudi, who has a molten-reddish golden form (in tirukkuṟungudi) which is even more radiant than his form in paramapadam, who is the cause for the sustenance etc of the great nityasūris, who is always a feast to the vision of all, who is known by the term “paramjyōti” and who made me his servant by showing such divine form?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the ninth pāsuram – When asked “Though he would not leave you, what if you forget him being focussed elsewhere?”, āḻvār replies “After seeing nambi who is mercifully stationed in tirukkuṟungudi, how can I forget him?”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār asks “How can we forget his helping nature?”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Ninth pāsuram – When asked “Instead of feeling like this for emperumān, would you not forget him and just eat, dress-up, and roam around along with samsāris?”, āḻvār replies “What reason can I cite to forget him?”. நம்பியை தென் குறுங்குடி நின்ற அச் செம்பொனே திகழும் திரு மூர்த்தியை உம்பர் வானவர் ஆதி அம் சோதியை எம் பிரானை என் சொல்லி மறப்பனோ? nambiyait tenkuṟungudi ninṟa ac cemponē tigaḻum tiru mūrttiyai umbar vānavar ādi am sōdiyai empirānai en solli maṟappanō?*

- *nambiyai* – One who is complete in auspicious qualities. In paramapdam (spiritual realm), he has all qualities, but it is only here, in samsāram (material realm), that they are manifested and visible fully.
- *then kuṟungudi ninṟa* – One who has paramapadam which is highlighted as in mūnrām tiruvantādi 51 “*kalangāp perunagaram*” (the land where there is no confusion), gave that up and descended to tirukkuṟungudi to capture me waiting for an opportune time in this stationary form.
- *nambiyait then kuṟungudi ninṟa* – I can forget him if he is incomplete in qualities or staying in a far-away place \[but he is not\].
- *ac cemponē tigaḻum tirumūrttiyai* – If there is some defect/limitation in his form, I can forget him \[but it is not so\].
- *ac cempon* – One who has a divine auspicious form which cannot be comprehended by mind, speech, having an unlimited radiant form, which is like incomparably shining molten-reddish gold.
- *umbar vānavar ādi am sōdiyai* – nityasūris who exist simply to enjoy such beauty. [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is having his divine form purely for the enjoyment of nityasūris who are having [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) as the cause for their sustenance unlike the dēvas of this material realm.
- *em pirānai* – One who has presented such divine form (which was enjoyed by nityasūris) to me.
- *en solli maṟappanō* – what reason will I cite to forget him?
   - *apūrnan enṟu maṟakkavō* – Can I forget him saying he is incomplete? \[No – he is nambi – complete\]
   - *asannihitan enṟu maṟakkavō* – Can I forget him saying he is staying far-away? \[No – he is right here in [tirukkuṟungudi](http://thirukkurungudi.koyil.org/)\]
   - *vadivaḻagu illai enṟu maṟakkavō* – Can I forget him saying he has no physical beauty? \[No – he is the most beautiful with molten-reddish golden radiant form\]
   - *mēnmai illai enṟu maṟakkavō* – Can I forget him saying he has no supremacy? \[No – he is even vorśipped/enjoyed by nityasūris\]
   - *enakku upakārakan anṟu enṟu maṟappanō* – Can I forget him saying he has not favoured me? \[No – he is my lord who favoured such beautiful form to me\]

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.10.10. Marappum jnanamum

*maṟappum jñānamum nān onṟu uṇarndilan maṟakkum enṟu sendāmaraik kaṇṇodu maṟappu aṟa en uḷḷē manninān tannai maṟappanō ini yān en maṇiyaiyē?*

**Пословный перевод:**

maṟappum – forgetfulness; jñānamum – remembrance/knowledge; onṟu – one; uṇarndilan – when I don’t know; maṟakkum – that “āḻvār will forget”; enṟu – considering; sem – reddish; tāmarai – Like a lotus; kaṇṇodu – with the eye(s); maṟappaṟa – ensuring that forgetfulness does not occur; en uḷḷē – inside my heart; manninān tannai – one who arrived to stay eternally; en maṇiyai – the most easily approachable emperumān who can be tied in a cloth like a precious gem and enjoyed; ini – now on; yān – I; maṟappanō – how to forget?

**Перевод:**

**When I don’t know about forgetfulness and remembrance, emperumān, after blessing the knowledge about him, considering that “āḻvār may forget about this”, with his merciful reddish lotus-like eyes, entered my heart to stay there eternally to ensure that I never forget him. How can I forget such emperumān who is like a precious gem which can be enjoyed fully?\[he is so simple that he places himself under the full control of his devotees for their enjoyment\]**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the tenth pāsuram – When asked “What if you tried hard to forget him?” āḻvār replies “How can I forget the one who watchfully glances at me always and resides in me eternally to ensure that I don’t forget him?”*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “When he is trying hard to ensure that I don’t forget him, how can I forget him?”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*In tenth pāsuram – āḻvār says “When he is making efforts to ensure that I don’t forget him, how can I forget him?”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. மறப்பும் ஞானமும் நான் ஒன்று உணர்ந்திலன் மறக்கும் என்று செந்தாமரைக் கண்ணொடு மறப்பு அற என் உள்ளே மன்னினான் தன்னை மறப்பனோ இனி யான் என் மணியையே? maṟappum jñānamum nān onṟu uṇarndilan maṟakkum enṟu sendāmaraik kaṇṇodu maṟappu aṟa en uḷḷē manninān tannai maṟappanō ini yān en maṇiyaiyē?*

- *maṟappum jñānamum nān onṟu uṇarndilan* – two explanations:
   - Only If I considered myself as a [cētana (sentient)](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/), could I forget. Only if I thought about him, could I forget him \[I had never contemplated upon him before\].
   - ātmā is the abode for both jñānam (knowledge) and ajñānam (ignorance). Before I was like [acit (insentient](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/09/thathva-thrayam-achith-what-is-matter/) – which had no knowledge).
- *maṟakkum enṟu sen tāmaraik kaṇṇodu maṟappaṟa en uḷḷē manninān* – Thinking about me (who is so ignorant), he pretended as if I contemplated upon him with my own efforts, said “Now that he has become knowledge about me, I cannot let him forget me”, glanced me with his cool beautiful divine eyes, stayed in my heart eternally ensuring that I never forget him.
- *manninān* – Staying in me, as if there is nothing else existing outside.
- *maṟappanō ini yān en maṇiyaiyē* – When one gets a precious gem, would they throw it out instead of tying it tightly to their cloth and preserving it?
- *maṟappanō ini* – When he has the tool \[his beautiful divine reddish lotus-like eyes\] to keep me always remembering about him, how can I forget him? Since time immemorial, I could never think about you; similarly, going forward, I can never forget you.
- *yān* – I who never remembered you before.
- *en maṇiyaiyē* – After [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) makes himself available to me, like a radiant precious gem handed over, which can be enjoyed fully, will I ignore him?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 1.10.11. Maniyai vanavar

*maṇiyai vānavar kaṇṇanait tannadu ōr  aṇiyait ten kurukūrc catakōpan sol paṇi sey āyirattuḷ ivai pattudan taṇivilar kaṟparēl kalvi vāyumē*

**Пословный перевод:**

maṇiyai – One who has a form like (radiant) ruby; vānavar – For those residents of paramapadam; kaṇṇanai – being the controller; tannadōr aṇiyai – the distinct one who himself is a decoration for him; then – obedient; kurukūr – the leader of āḻvārtirunagari; satakōpan – āḻvār; sol – by his word; paṇisey – served; āyirattuḷ – among the thousand pāsurams; ivai pattu – this decad; udan – agreeing in principle; taṇivilar – those who are being disturbed; kaṟparēl – if learnt (with great desire through an ācārya); kalvi – that learning/knowledge; vāyum – will lead to the result in the form of kainkaryam

**Перевод:**

**For those who learn this decad among the thousand pāsurams (through an ācārya with great desire), agreeing to the principles spoken in the mood of service by nammāḻvār who is the leader of āḻvārtirunagari (which is being obedient towards āḻvār), on bhagavān who has a form which resembles radiant ruby, who is the controller of nityasūris, and who is decorated naturally having none to compare against him, this decade will lead to the ultimate result in the form of kainkarayam.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the end, āḻvār says that those who learn this decad will get kainkaryam to bhagavān which is the unsurpassed and ultimate result to be achieved. It can also be understood as, those who learn this decad will acquire this true knowledge naturally.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*āḻvār says “the result of this decad – studying this by itself is a kainkaryam”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. மணியை வானவர் கண்ணனைத் தன்னது ஓர் அணியை தென் குருகூர்ச் சடகோபன் சொல் பணிசெய் ஆயிரத்துள் இவை பத்துடன் தணிவிலர் கற்பரேல் கல்வி வாயுமே maṇiyai vānavar kaṇṇanait tannadu ōr  aṇiyait then kurukūrc catakōpan sol paṇi sey āyirattuḷ ivai pattudan taṇivilar kaṟparēl kalvi vāyumē*

- *maṇiyai* – Here, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s saulabhyam (simplicity) of being able to be tied in one’s cloth (as a precious gem) is explained. This is the same saulabhyam which was explained in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.10.9](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/10/thiruvaimozhi-1-10-9-nambiyaith-thenkurungudi/) “*tenkuṟungudi ninṟa*” (one who is standing in [tirukkuṟungudi](http://thirukkurungudi.koyil.org/)).
- *vānavar kaṇṇanai* – Here [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s supremacy is explained. Already seen in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.10.9](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/10/thiruvaimozhi-1-10-9-nambiyaith-thenkurungudi/) “*umbar vānavar ādi am sōdi*” (the leader of nityasūris).
- *tannadōr aṇiyai* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is thinking about the divine form which was highlighted in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.10.9](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/10/thiruvaimozhi-1-10-9-nambiyaith-thenkurungudi/) “*accemponē tigaḻum tirumūrtti*” (the divine form which is in molten-reddish golden form). [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s supremacy is a fresh collection of these three aspects.
- *tenkurukūrc catakōpan* – Seeing [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) compiling the verses, the words come forward and request him “Please accept me! Please accept me!” to be engaged in kainkaryam. It can also be explained as vācika kainkaryam (service through words/speech) – kainkaryam in the form of thousand pāsurams.
- *udan taṇivilar kaṟparēl* – When learnt with agreement to the principles. taṇivu means māndyam (feeling feeble, being without faith), taṇivilar means being faithful. Instead of being “If I get it, I will not leave it; if I don’t get it, I won’t seek out for it”, learning it with total faith.
- *kalvi vāyumē* – As said in mudal tiruvandādi 67 “*oṇ tāmaraiyāḷ kēḷvan oruvanaiyē nōkkum uṇarvu*” (knowledge/consciousness which is fully focussed on srīman nārāyaṇan only) – jñānam means that which is rooted in bhagavat viśayam (spiritual matters centered on [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)). So,learning this decad will, by itself, lead to the result which is kainkaryam.
- *kalvi vāyum* – Alternatively, it is explained as, this learning/knowledge, by itself is the result.

Final summary from [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/) (for this decad):

- In the first pāsuram, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) briefly explained the meanings which were to be elaborated in the subsequent pāsurams.
- In the second pāsuram, he said that [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) will be friendly towards those who have parama bhakti (ultimate devotion) and those who just think about him.
- In the third pāsuram, he said to his heart “since you have seen [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s nature, you also behave according to your nature”.
- In the fourth pāsuram, on seeing his heart vorśipping [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/), he praised it.
- In the fifth pāsuram, he mercifully explained to his heart that his previous saying of “[*eṇṇilum*](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/10/thiruvaimozhi-1-10-2-kannulle-nirkum/)” became manifested in result.
- In the sixth pāsuram, he said to his heart that if both he and his heart stayed like this, there will be no defect.
- In the seventh pāsuram, he said that whatever he feared previously came true.
- In the eighth pāsuram, he explained the bodily changes that occurred to him on hearing the divine names of [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/).
- In the ninth pāsuram, when asked “what if you forget [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)?” he said “there is no way to forget [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)“.
- In the tenth pāsuram, when asked “what if you tried hard to forget [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)?” he replied “How can I forget [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) who is in my heart?”
- Finally, he explained the result for those who learnt this decad.

[nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/) gives a summary for the whole of 1st centum.

[āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) said [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is sarvasmātparan (greater than every one else – [1st decad](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/03/thiruvaimozhi-1-1-uyarvara/)), bhajanīyan (vorśippable – [2nd decad](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/04/thiruvaimozhi-1-2-vidumin/)), sulabhan (easily approachable – [3rd decad](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/05/thiruvaimozhi-1-3-paththudai/)), aparādasahan (one who tolerates offenses – [4th decad](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/07/thiruvaimozhi-1-4-anjiraiya/)), seelavān (who has the qualities of simplicity etc. – [5th decad](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/08/thiruvaimozhi-1-5-valavezh/)), svārādan (easily vorśippable – [6th decad](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/08/thiruvaimozhi-1-6-parivathil/)), niratisaya bhōjñan (most enjoyable – [7th decad](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/09/thiruvaimozhi-1-7-piraviththuyar/)), has ārjavam (honesty – [8th decad](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/09/thiruvaimozhi-1-8-odumpul/)) and is sātmyabhōgapradan (one who gives joy in a step-by-step manner – [9th decad](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/09/thiruvaimozhi-1-9-ivaiyum/)). Such [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) accepts \[me/us\] out of his causeless mercy ([10th decad](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/10/thiruvaimozhi-1-10-poruma/)). Thus, he instructs his heart to worship him as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.1.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/03/thiruvaimozhi-1-1-1-uyarvara-uyarnalam/) “*avan tuyaraṟu sudaradi toḻudu eḻu en mananē*“.

[nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/) goes on to summarize each centum of [tiruvāimoḻi](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/thiruvaimozhi/) here:

- In the first centum, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) established that the ultimate goal is to perform bhagavat kainkaryam (service to [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)).
- In the second centum, he eliminated the weeds in such kainkaryam.
- In the third centum, he explained that kainkaryam where the weeds are eliminated is bhagavat kainkaryam which leads all the way to bhāgavata kainkaryam (serving [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s devotees).
- In the fourth centum, he explained that aiśvaryam (worldly wealth) and kaivalyam (self-enjoyment) are the hurdles for such kainkaryam.
- In the fifth centum, he explained that [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is the only one who can remove those hurdles.
- In the sixth centum, he surrenders unto the lotus feet of such [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who eliminates the hurdles.
- In the seventh centum, seeing that even after surrendering to [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) with the puruśakāram (recommendation) of [srī mahālakśmi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/), as in the case of “dagdapata nyāya” (a cloth which is burnt, but seemingly looks alright), he is still in samsāram (material world), he becomes very dejected.
- In the eighth centum, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) thinks “I may be suffering in samsāram even after becoming a surrendered person as in the case of “dagdapata nyāya”, due to my attachments to myself and the objects owned by me” and declares that he is detached from everything \[other than [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)\].
- In the ninth centum, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) wonders why he is still not protected (liberated); [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) says “I am nārāyaṇan; one who has all capabilities; I will fulfil all your desires” and he becomes overwhelmed by [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s qualities.
- In the tenth centum, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) mercifully explains how [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) seeing his urgency, descends to tirumōgūr, shows arcirādi gati (the path that starts with arcis and leads up to paramapadam) and fulfills his desires.

Thus ends the English translation for tiruvāimoḻi 1st centum 10th decad.

[āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) tiruvadigaḷē caraṇam  
[emperumānār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/emperumanar/) tiruvadigaḷē caraṇam  
[piḷḷān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/pillan/) tiruvadigaḷē caraṇam  
[nanjīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nanjiyar/) tiruvadigaḷē caraṇam  
[nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/) tiruvadigaḷē caraṇam  
[vadakkut tiruvīdip piḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadakku-thiruvidhi-pillai/) tiruvadigaḷē caraṇam  
[periyavāccān piḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/periyavachchan-pillai/) tiruvadigaḷē caraṇam

[jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/mamunigal/) tiruvadigaḷē caraṇam

## Second Centum

## 2.1 Vayum tirai

## 2.1.1. Vayum tirai

*vāyum tirai ugaḷum kānal mada nārāy! āyum amar ulagum tunjilum nī tunjāyāl nōyum payalamaiyum mīdūra emmē pōl nīyum tirumālāl nenjam kōḷ pattāyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vāyum – approaching closely; tirai – in the tide; ugaḷum – carefully walking; kānal – in the seashore; madam – majestic; nārāy – Oh crane!; āyum – (sleepless) mother; amar ulagum – dēva lōkam – celestial world (where sleep is nonexistent); tunjilum – even if they sleep; nī – you; tunjāy – are not sleeping; Al – thus; nōyum – the pain/disease inside; payalaimaiyum – (which causes) the pale complexion due to love-sickness; mīdūra – raising; emmē pōl – (being caught in dear one) like us; nīyum – you too; tirumālāl – by śrīman nārāyaṇan who is the consort of śrī mahālakśmi; nenjam – heart; kōtpattāyē – have been stolen?

**Перевод:**

**Oh crane that carefully walks on the closely approaching tides! Even if those sleepless mother, dēvas in dēvalōkam (where there sleep is nonexistent) sleep, you are not sleeping. It seems that this is because you are in pain inside (due to separation) as a result of which your body has become pale, due to that love-sickness like us whose hearts have been stolen by śrīman nārāyaṇan.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the first pāsuram, parānkuśa nāyaki (āḻvār in feminine mood), looking at a crane which is single-mindedly waiting for its prey, thinks that it is in distress like herself and says “Alas! you too are suffering like this”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*In the first pāsuram,  meditating upon the union of śrī mahālakśmi with śrīman nārāyaṇan which is the cause of increased enjoyableness as highlighted previously in tiruvāimoḻi 1.10.10 “maṇiyai vānavar kaṇṇanai” and becoming immersed in that experience, she sees a crane in her garden which is near the seashore and asks it “Did you also lose your heart to emperumān?”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*First pāsuram – Since those who are in separation seek out neydal land (sea and seashore), parānkusa nāyaki too reaches a garden on the seashore to cheer herself up while in distress of separation from emperumān. She notices a crane there. On seeing the white/pale complexion of the crane’s body, she thinks that the crane too has become pale due to the love-sickness in separation and tells it “Oh poor thing! You too have been caught in the matter of same emperumān like I am and lost your heart to him”. வாயும் திரை உகளும் கானல் மட நாராய் ஆயும் அமர் உலகும் துஞ்சிலும் நீ துஞ்சாயால் நோயும் பயலைமையும் மீது ஊர எம்மே போல் நீயும் திருமாலால் நெஞ்சம் கோள் பட்டாயே? vāyum tirai ugaḷum kānal mada nārāy! āyum amar ulagum tunjilum nī tunjāyāl nōyum payalamaiyum mīdūra emmē pōl nīyum tirumālāl nenjam kōḷ pattāyē*

- *vāyum tirai ugaḷum* – Even when great tides go over the head, the crane does not leave the seashore until its prey is caught. This is like those who are fully meditating upon [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) (who do not give up in any circumstance). Just as it is said in [periya tirumoḻi](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/periya-thirumozhi/) 11.4.1, one who does not forget “*alaikadalnīr kuḻamba agadādavōdi agalvānurinja mudugil malaigaḷai mīdu koṇḍu varumīnai*” (the fish \[matsyāvatāram\] which brings great mountains on its back in the ocean with great tides), this crane too is not forgetting the fish it preys for. As explained in srī bhāgavatam 10.20.15 “*girayō varśadārābhihanyamānā na vivyatu: abhibhūyamānā vyasanairyatādōkśajacētasa:*” – even when great rains fall on a mountain, the mountain stays fixed – this is similar to those who are fixated on “sarvēsvaran is the protector” will stay strong and not become caught in miseries of this world.
- *kānal madanārāy* – Oh crane that carefully walks into the tides! Like the village-heads who wear auspicious pavitram (darba grass), perform yāgam etc., and pretend to be virtuous while harming others, even if some lean fish pass by, you ignore them and wait for the best prey.
- *āyum* – my ([parānkusa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s) mother who has not slept since her birth worrying for my  well-being.
- *amar ulagum tunjilum* – even if the nityasūris (who never sleep) sleep, you are not sleeping. Why is her mother sleepless? Initially, she was sleepless thinking “we have to get her a fitting husband”; subsequently, on seeing her suffer in separation from [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), she is sleepless. sītā pirātti said in srī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 119.36 “*patisamyōgasulabham vayō druśtvā ca mē pitā \| cintārṇavagata:*” – my father became very worried thinking “Her age is ripe that she should be married to a suitable groom and I am not finding that suitable person”. Similarly, [parānkusa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s parents are having sleepless nights in such worry. nityasūris do not sleep since their eye-lids never close and are always having the divine vision of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/).
- *nōyum payalaimaiyum* – the internal suffering and the impact of such internal suffering on her body.
- *mīdūra* – Like poison spreading in the body, this paleness has spread all over the body.
- *emmē pōl* – I thought I was alone in this suffering but you are there too. Like me, you are also tolerating the sorrow, insults etc., still waiting for [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) and having pale complexion.
- *nīyum* – you too who are so tender for not being able to handle the suffering in separation. Are both of us unable to uphold the principle explained in srī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 9.30 “*tat tasya sadrusam bhavēt*” (he coming over to lankā and rescuing me (without any of my efforts) is the suitable action for srī rāma’s greatness).
- *tirumālāl nenjam kōtpattāyē* – Are you also suffering in your heart and physically, by losing bodily complexion like me? Did you \[also\] desire for “*maintanai malarāḷ maṇavāḷanai*” (the eternally youthful husband of [śrī mahālakśmi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/)) \[even after his being with [srī mahālakśmi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/) who helps everyone to unite with him, how can he make us suffer like this?\].
- *nenjam kōtpattāyē* – You also lost your heart! Not just bodily suffering – you are suffering in your heart too!

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.1.2. Kotpatta sintaiyaiyay

*kōḷ patta sintaiyaiyāyk kūrvāya anṟilē! sēṇ patta yāmangaḷ sērādu irangudiyāl āḷ patta emmē pōl nīyum aravu aṇaiyān tātpatta taṇ tuḻāyt tāmam kāmuṟṟāyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kōtpatta – stolen; sintaiyaiyāy – having (been stolen of) heart; kūrvāya – (reflecting such sorrow in a stammering way) with loud voice; anṟilē – oh ibis!; sētpatta – lengthy; yāmangaḷ – night time; sērādu – not having associated; irangudi – being sorrowful; Al – thus; ātpatta – being servitors; emmē pōl – like us; nīyum – you too (whose suffering in separation is physically visible); aravaṇaiyān – one who has ādi sēśa bed as his identity; tāḷ – in his lotus feet; patta – having been stepped on (while enjoying); taṇ – having freśnesss; tuḻāyt tāmam – tuḷasi garland; kāmuṟṟāyē – did you desire for that?

**Перевод:**

**Oh ibis whose heart is stolen and crying out loud due to that! Your suffering in separation for long duration (in the night) is visibly manifested. Did you also desire for the fresh tuḷasi garland which was stepped on (touched) by the divine feet of emperumān who is identified by his ādi sēśa bed?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the second pāsuram – On hearing the sorrowful cry of an ibis which is separated from its partner, parānkusa nāyaki becomes sad.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, parānkusa nāyaki sees an ibis and asks it “did you also desire to get the tuḷasi from the lotus feet of sēśasāyi (one who is resting on ādi sēśa)?*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

- *nīyum* – Though you don’t have vēdānta jñānam (knowledge in sāstram) and have not been blessed by [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) directly, you are so attached to him. It is amazing that there is no qualification for developing great love for emperumān!
- *tāmam kāmuṟṟayē* – [bhagavat gītā](http://githa.koyil.org/) 2.62 “*sangāt sanjāyatē kāma:*” (attachment leads to great desire) is quoted here.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Second pāsuram – While thus speaking to the crane, āḻvār hears the sorrowful cry of an ibis bird on a near-by palmyra on having its beak separated from its partner’s and says “Alas! You too have been caught like me (in sorrow)” கோள் பட்ட சிந்தையையாய்க் கூர்வாய அன்றிலே சேண் பட்ட யாமங்கள் சேராது இரங்குதியால் ஆள் பட்ட எம்மே போல் நீயும் அரவு அணையான் தாள் பட்ட தண் துழாய்த் தாமம் காமுற்றாயே? kōḷ patta sintaiyaiyāyk kūrvāya anṟilē! sēṇ patta yāmangaḷ sērādu irangudiyāl āḷ patta emmē pōl nīyum aravu aṇaiyān tātpatta taṇ tuḻāyt tāmam kāmuṟṟāyē*

- *kōtpatta sintaiyaiyāy* – One whose heart is stolen. How did she know? [parānkusa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) knew it from the helpless cry of the heart.
- *kūrvāya anṟilē* – This cry would break those who are in separation into pieces.
- *sētpatta yāmangaḷ* – Its not just the night itself is long, but each yāmam (each quarter/part of night) is long.
- *sērādu irangudiyāl* – In such a lengthy night, at least if one is with the partner in the bed, one can sustain. But here, you are breaking into pieces due to separation (from your partner).
- *ātpatta emmē pōl* – Having lost the heart to him and not having him along in the bed like me, are you also caught in the fragrance for serving his divine feet?
- *nīyum* – You, who are distinct from the worldly persons. You are neither learned in nārāyaṇa sūktam which says “*patim visvasya*” ([bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is the master of all), yajur aśtakam “*yasyāsmi*” (I belong to [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)) etc. Nor are you blessed with “[*mayarvaṟa madinalam*](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/03/thiruvaimozhi-1-1-1-uyarvara-uyarnalam/)” (faultless knowledge/devotion) by [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/). Though you are not up to my level of knowledge/blessing, still you are suffering like me.
- *aravaṇaiyān* … – Earlier, she said “*tirumālāl*” (by [srīman nārāyaṇan](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is dear to [srī mahālakśmi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/)); That means, they both should be lying on the bed (ādisēśa). Did you desire for the tuḷasi garland which was crushed by both of them during their intimate dealings?
- *tāḷ patta taṇ tuḻāy* – Instead of desiring for the tuḷasi garland which is worn by [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) in his head/crown, you are desiring for the garland which was crushed by their divine feet. How do you know that the garland was enjoyed by both of them? The fragrance from the civet perfume, flowers etc., are reflecting in that garland.
- *tāmam* – radiance, garland. Here it is explained as garland.
- *kāmuṟṟāyē* – You have reached a stage where you just don’t have the desire to get that garland, but you will live if you get that and you will perish if you don’t get that.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.1.3. Kamurra

*kāmuṟṟa kaiyaṟavōdu ellē! irāp pagal nīmuṟṟak kaṇ tuyilāy nenju urugi ēngudiyāl tī muṟṟat ten ilangai ūttinān tāḷ nayanda yām uṟṟadu uṟṟāyō? vāḻi kanai kadalē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

kāmuṟṟa – enjoyment that was desired for; kaiyaṟavōdu – being sad for not accomplishing them; nī – you; irāp pagal – night and day; muṟṟa – fully; kaṇ tuyilāy – not sleeping; nenju – even inside your heart; urugi – melted; ēngudi – calling out; Al – thus; tennilangai – lankā; muṟṟa – fully; tī ūttinān – one who set fire; tāḷ – divine feet; nayanda – desired; yām – us; uṟṟadu – whatever happened; uṟṟāyō – did you also experience?; kanai – making noise; kadalē – Oh sea!; vāḻi – may you live long (after having your sorrow eliminated)

**Перевод:**

**Oh noisy sea! Like one who did not accomplish his/her desires fulfilled, you are not sleeping night and day; you are also calling out from your heart; thus, I ask you “Like us, did you also desire for the divine feet of srī rāma who set fire in lankā and become affected by that?”. May you live long (after having your sorrows removed).**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In third pāsuram, parānkusa nāyaki, on seeing the sea with noisy tides asks “Did you also become captivated by the qualities of srī rāma and suffer due to that?”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, on seeing the noisy sea, she tells “Did you also become like me who desired for the divine feet of the one who eliminates the enemies?”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Third pāsuram – While feeling bad for the cry of ibis, she sees the sea which is a great entity, losing its composure, trying to reach the shore and retracting from there, and making noise which does not have any meaning, like a dumb-person’s speech, and asks “Are you also suffering like me after being captivated in the qualities of srī rāma?”. காமுற்ற கையறவோடு எல்லே! இராப் பகல் நீ முற்றக் கண் துயிலாய் நெஞ்சு உருகி ஏங்குதியால் தீ முற்றத் தென் இலங்கை ஊட்டினான் தாள் நயந்த யாம் உற்றது உற்றாயோ? வாழி கனை கடலே kāmuṟṟa kaiyaṟavōdu ellē! irāp pagal nīmuṟṟak kaṇ tuyilāy nenju urugi ēngudiyāl tī muṟṟat then ilangai ūttinān tāḷ nayanda yām uṟṟadu uṟṟāyō? vāḻi kanai kadalē!*

- *kāmuṟṟa kaiyaṟavōdu* – This is recited along with “*nenjurugi ēngudiyāl*” (crying out from the heart since your desires did not fructify). Feeling distressed for not having the desires fulfilled. While both desires and distress for not having such desires fulfilled are not applicable for the sea, since she, who quotes the sea as an example for her state of mind, has that, she assumes that the sea too has those aspects.
- *ellē* – calling out – Since the state/behaviour of the sea looks similar to her own with respect to making noise night and day, [parānkusa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) calls out the sea just like she would call her (girl) friend – this is like friendship in jail (when two prisoners would share each other’s agony) \[this samsāram (material realm) itself is like a prison\]. [tirumangai āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/thirumangai-azhwar/) too says in periya tirumoḻi 9.4.9 “*ōdamum nānum uṟangādirundēnē*” (tides and I were not sleeping). Alternatively, “*ellē*” can also be explained as “*ennē!*” as exclamation out of amazement.
- *irāp pagal nī muṟṟak kaṇ tuyilāy* – in your case, we see no distinction between night (which is meant for sleeping) and day (which is meant for being awake).
- *nī* – Where did **your** composure go? \[Sea is very composed without tides inside and with tides at the shore\].
- *nenjurugi ēngudiyāl* – When there is no sleep, obviously the heart will melt.
- *tī muṟṟat tennilangai ūttinān* – Oh poor thing! You did not desire for [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s paratvam (form in paramapadam) but for [srī rāma](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who could not bear the separation of his wife. He burnt down lankā fully. But what about vibhīśaṇa’s palace? Was it not inside lankā? Just like vibhīśaṇa did not fit in the group of rākśasa’s (even though he was physically present there), his palace too did not belong in lankā (though it was physically present there) – his palace is the place of a servitor.
- *tī muṟṟat tennilangai ūttinān* – Alternatively, Earlier, due to fear for rāvaṇa, agni (fire-god) did not function properly; but now with [srī rāma](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s arrival/strength, he fiercely acted upon lankā and burnt it down as said in [periya tirumoḻi](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/periya-thirumozhi/) 10.9.1 “*oḷḷeri maṇḍi uṇṇa*” (shining fire pervades and consumes). [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/) quotes “*sendīyuṇḍu tēkkittadē*” a phrase that resembles kamba rāmāyaṇam, sundara kāṇḍam, eriyūttup padalam 46th pāsuram – which highlights his deep knowledge of tamiḻ literature.
- *tāḷ nayanda yām uṟṟadu uṟṟāyō* – You too desired for the divine feet of cakkaravartti tirumagan (emperor’s son) who is most attached to his wife. To be distressed in separation – it does not matter if one desires for [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s lotus feet or his shoulder. Both [sītā pirātti](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/) (who desires [srī rāma](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s embrace) and bharatāḻvān (who wanted to serve srī rāma’s lotus feet) felt equally distressed in separation.
- *vāḻi* – you live long after this suffering is removed.
- *kanai kadalē* – instead of calling out, you are stuttering in sorrow! It is also explained as “sea which makes loud noise”.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.
