## 2.1.4. Kadalum malaiyum

*kadalum malaiyum visumbum tuḻāy em pōl sudar koḷ irāp pagal tunjāyāl taṇ vādāy! adal koḷ padai āḻi ammānaik kāṇbān nī udalam nōy uṟṟāyō ūḻi tōṟūḻiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

taṇ – cool (like a body cured of fever); vādāy – Oh northerly wind!; kadalum – sea; malaiyum – and mountain; visumbum – and sky; tuḻāy – touching; em pōl – Like us who seek out for him in milk ocean, tirumalā and paramapadam (paramākāsam – the ultimate sky) as stated in taittiriya upaniśat “ambasyapārē bhuvanasya madyē nāgasya pruśtē”; sudar – radiance of moon, sun, etc; koḷ – as identity; irā – in the night; pagalum – in the day; tunjāy – not sleeping (being stationed in a single place); Al – thus; adal – in the mahābhārata war; koḷ – took up (after saying “I won’t pick up any weapons”); padai āḻi – having the divine sudarśana cakram; ammānai – sarvēśvaran; kāṇbān – desiring to see (like how bhīśma wanted to see kriṣṇa); nī – you (who are helping all); ūḻidōṟūḻi – time after time (even if the yuga cycles change), forever (thinking about him); udalam – pervaded all through the body, until the body exists; nōy – disease; uṟṟāyō – did you have?

**Перевод:**

**Oh cool northerly wind! Like us, you are also seeking emperumān in the ocean (kśīrābdi – milk ocean), mountain (tirumalā) and sky (paramapadam which is called as the great/ultimate sky) and not sleeping in night and day which are identified with moon and sun respectively; Thus, did you also desire to see kriṣṇa who took up the sudarsana cakram during the mahābhārata war and acquired the disease (of separation) in your body that will last forever even beyond the yuga cycles?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fourth pāsuram, on seeing the blowing wind, parānkusa nāyaki asks “Did you also desire to see the divine hands and the disc in the hands of kriṣṇa and become anguished?”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, she tells seeing the northerly wind, “Did you go through the suffering of desiring to see the one with the weapon that will destroy the enemies?”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Fourth pāsuram – Wind being an entity which pervades, not being stationary due to separation from its dear ones, hiding/covering its body with dust, just like those who are in separation who send messages to their beloved, was cool like those whose fever was cured. Seeing that, she asks “Are you also going through the same suffering as I?” கடலும் மலையும் விசும்பும் துழாய் எம் போல் சுடர் கொள் இராப்பகல் துஞ்சாயால் தண் வாடாய் அடல் கொள் படை ஆழி அம்மானைக் காண்பான் நீ உடலம் நோய் உற்றாயோ ஊழி தோறு ஊழியே? kadalum malaiyum visumbum tuḻāy em pōl sudar koḷ irāp pagal tunjāyāl taṇ vādāy! adal koḷ padai āḻi ammānaik kāṇbān nī udalam nōy uṟṟāyō ūḻi tōṟūḻiyē*

- *kadalum malaiyum visumbum tuḻāy* – Few explanations:
   - As said in siṟiya tirumadal “*kārār tirumēni kāṇum aḷavum pōy*” (seeking out the blacking cloud divine form of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)), the wind is similar to those \[[āḻvārs](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/azhwars/)\] who seek out [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s forms in kśīrābdi (milk ocean), tirumalā (mountain) and paramapadam (great sky). As said in siṟiya tirumadal “*ūrāya ellām oḻiyāmē*“, the wind is similar to such persons who seek out in all towns/places.
   - The wind is similar to the sons of dasarata – srī rāma and lakśmaṇa, who searched for sītā everywhere as said in srī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 61.20 “*tau vanāni girīmscaiva saritasca \| nikilēna vicinvanau sītām dasartātmajau \|\|*” (Those sons of dasarata – srī rāma and lakśmaṇa walked around in forests, mountains, rivers, ponds and everywhere searching for sītā pirātti). sītā pirātti who is searched for is too great/beautiful to be given up. The sons of dasarata (the great emperor) are not born to search \[they are born as princes who are tender and to be cared by others\]. From this, it is explained that the wind is unable to bear the separation of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/).
- *kadalum malaiyum* *visumbum* – unlimited ocean, endless mountain, Ether/Sky which provides space or sky which causes fear.
- *em pōl sudar koḷ irāp pagal  tunjāyāl taṇ vādāy* – Cool like the one who cured of fever; sudar koḷ irāp pagal – night which consumed sun and day which has the sun – irrespective of the time, you are not sleeping, Oh northerly wind!
- *adal koḷ* … – adal means pride – one who consumes the pride of the enemy or one who is prideful. You are captivated by the one who became asatya pratijñan (kriṣṇa who did not keep up his promise) for his devotee (arjuna who was severely assaulted by bhīśma) unlike srī rāma who said in srī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 29.10 “*…ētat vratam mama*” (this is my vow to protect those who surrender unto me). In the mahābhāratam battle, when arjuna retracted after being assaulted by bhīśma, kriṣṇa ignoring his own vow of not taking up arms, brought forward his sudarśana cakram and chased bhīśma. Quoting mahābhāratam bhīśma parvam 59.98 – when kriṣṇa approached bhīśma, instead of running for his life, bhīśma stopped and said “*ēhi ēhi*” (come! come!), “come and see our mother/father walking beautifully towards me”. He says “*pullāmbhuja patra nētra*” – what is the loss for him ignoring his own vow – we can still enjoy his beautiful reddish eyes brimming with anger! “*prahasya mām pādaya*” (you knock me down). Even after your declaring that you won’t take up arms and even if I had weapons in my hand, I will be defeated by your supremacy. You kindly order me to drop my weapons and cut my head. “*lōkanāta*” (master of the universe) – I am not being defeated by you or your valour, but by your lordship.
- *adal koḷ padai āḻi* – sudarśana cakram which is a prideful weapon.
- *āḻi ammānai* – Did you also desire to see the [sarvēśvaran](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) with the divine chakra in his hand?
- *udalam nōyuṟṟāyō* – You who are helping everyone without expecting anything in return, are having pain in your body. [parānkusa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) (nammāḻvār)  is not realizing that movement of wind is a natural phenomenon but considers it as an outcome of its suffering in separation from [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/).
- *ūḻi tōṟūḻiyē* – She is saying “you are suffering kalpa after kalpa continuously” \[kalpa is a day of brahmā where 1000 four-yuga cycles occur\]. It is also explained as suffering which leads to perishing of the body.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.1.5. Ulidoruli

*ūḻidōṟu ūḻi  ulagukku nīrkoṇḍu tōḻiyarum yāmum pōl nīrāy negiḻginṟa vāḻiya vānamē! nīyum madusūdan pāḻimaiyil pattu avan kaṇ pāsattāl naivāyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tōḻiyarum – girl-friends (who are equally pained as I am); yāmum pōl – like us (who are in pain); ulagukku – to fill the world; nīr koṇḍu – with the water; ūḻidōṟūḻi – forever; nīrāy – in the form of water; negiḻginṟa – falling down; vānamē – Oh cloud!; nīyum – you who are most generous; madusūdan – one who killed madu; pāḻimaiyil – great valour; pattu – being captivated; avankaṇ – towards him; pāsattāl – out of affection; naivāyē – become weak; vāḻiya – may you live long after being relieved from this pain

**Перевод:**

**Oh cloud which is falling down as rain to fill the world like my friends and I \[who are also longing and falling into pieces\]! It appears that you have also been captivated by madusūdanan emperumān‘s valour and become weak. Those who are generous, when in separation from bhagavān, will become weak.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fifth pāsuram, looking at the clouds which are falling down as rain, parānkusa nāyaki becomes sad saying “you too are captivated like me by emperumān‘s qualities, activities etc., and are suffering  due to that”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, parānkusa nāyaki asks a cloud “did you also become caught in bhagavān‘s abilities and become weak?”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*In the fifth pāsuram, seeing a cloud which is falling down as rain, parānkusa nāyaki says “did you also become captivated in his valour?”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Fifth pāsuram – At that time, a cloud falls down as rain; She asks it “did you also become captivated in his ability to destroy the enemies?”. ஊழிதோறு ஊழி உலகுக்கு நீர்கொண்டு தோழியரும் யாமும் போல் நீராய் நெகிழ்கின்ற வாழிய வானமே நீயும் மதுசூதன் பாழிமையில் பட்டு அவன் கண் பாசத்தால் நைவாயே? ūḻidōṟu ūḻi  ulagukku nīrkoṇḍu tōḻiyarum yāmum pōl nīrāy negiḻginṟa vāḻiya vānamē! nīyum madusūdan pāḻimaiyil pattu avan kaṇ pāsattāl naivāyē*

- *ūḻidōṟūḻi – nīrāy negiḻginṟa* – kalpa after kalpa, cloud falls as rain.
- *ulagukku nīr koṇḍu* – having abundance of water (that was fetched from an ocean) to fill the world with lots of water.

You have good examples \[in us\].

- *tōḻiyarum yāmum pōl* – Like my girl-friends who are attached to [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) much more than I am; and I.
- *nīrāy negiḻginṟa* – melting and falling down as rain.
- *vāḻiya* – you who are so generous/helpful towards the universe, may you live long after being removed of tears from your eyes.
- *vānamē* – It can indicate both cloud and sky.  [parānkusa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is thinking that the sky/ether which is a subtle entity, absorbs water from the ocean and discharges it as rain. vānam is also another name for mēgam (cloud) in tamiḻ. This is seen in iraṇḍām tiruvandādi 75 “***vān*** *kalanda vaṇṇan*” ([emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is in the color of cloud). tamiḻ scholars too said “***vānam*** *vaḻangāvidil*” \[tirukkuṟaḷ – 19: if the cloud does not bestow\].
- *nīyum* – You who have assumed a form to help the universe.
- *madusūdan pāḻimaiyil pattu* – Being captivated in the valour of one who can destroy the enemies, due to the attachment towards him, neither being able to live nor being able to die, you are suffering. pāḻimai – strength; great desire to protect.
- *avan kaṇ pāsattāl* – attachment towards him. Attachment towards something is depending on the \[greatness of the\] object; suffering too would be proportionate if that object is not acquired.
- *naivāyē* – suffering is the only result.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.1.6. Naivaya emmepol

*naivāya emmē pōl nāḷ madiyē! nī in nāḷ mai vān iruḷ agaṟṟāy māḻāndu tēmbudiyāl ai vāy aravu aṇaimēl āḻip perumānār mey vāsagam kēttum un meyn nīrmai tōṟṟāyē?*

**Пословный перевод:**

naivu – becoming weak only; āya – having it as nature; emmē pōl – like us; nāḷ – crescent shaped (1/16th of the size of full moon); madiyē – oh chandra!; nī – you (who are radiant); innāḷ – on this day (right now); mai – like very dark color paste; vān – in the sky; iruḷ – darkness; agaṟṟāy – unable to eradicate it; māḻāndu – losing the shine; tēmbudi – you have waned; Al – thus; aivāy – having many faces and two tongues (to lie); aravaṇai mēl – on the serpent bed; āḻi – one how has the divine sudarśana cakram; perumnānār – having great glories (who teaches them to lie); mey – big lie; vāsagam – words; kēttu – after hearing; un – your; mey – in the form; nīrmai – the ability to uplift; tōṟṟāyē – have you lost?

**Перевод:**

**Oh crescent shaped moon! You have also naturally become weak like us. You (who are shining) are not removing the darkness in the sky now, which looks very black in color; you have also lost your shine. Thus, did you also lose the shine in your form on hearing (believing) the false promises of emperumān who is resting on the serpent bed having the sudarśana cakram in his hand?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the sixth pāsuram, on seeing the crescent moon (which is in its minimal size), parānkusa nāyaki says “did you also believe in the false promises of emperumān and suffer like me?”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Sixth pāsuram – Crescent moon (in its minimal size) appeared next to the cloud; parānkusa nāyaki says to him “it appears that you have become weak”. நைவாய எம்மே போல் நாள் மதியே! நீ இந் நாள் மை வான் இருள் அகற்றாய் மாழாந்து தேம்புதியால் ஐ வாய் அரவு அணைமேல் ஆழிப் பெருமானார் மெய் வாசகம் கேட்டு உன் மெய்ந் நீர்மை தோற்றாயே? naivāya emmē pōl nāḷ madiyē! nī in nāḷ mai vān iruḷ agaṟṟāy māḻāndu tēmbudiyāl ai vāy aravu aṇaimēl āḻip perumānār mey vāsagam kēttum un meyn nīrmai tōṟṟāyē?*

- *naivāya emmē pōl* – having weakness like us; embodiment of weakness. srī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 15.22 “*sabankām analankārām vipadmāmiva padminīm \| …*” which describes sītā pirātti’s form is quoted here. sabankām – raised from the earth – dusty; analankārām – having no decoration – since she is in separation, she did not clean and decorate herself; vipadmāmiva padminīm – a pond which is without the lotus flower – she looks in so much sorrow that even if srī rāma arrives, her sorrow will not be removed. srī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 15.26 “*avyaktalēkāmiva candralēkām pāmsupradigdāmiva hēmalēkām \| kśataprarūdāmiva bāṇalēkām vāyuprabhagnāmiva mēgalēkām* \|\|” (sītā pirātti looks like a moon without the shine, pure gold with a dust cover, a wound which is covered with a layer of skin on top and group of clouds devastated by a great wind) is also quoted here.
- *nāḷ madiyē* – Oh full moon! Oh moon that was full before (now waned)! Just as it is said in “*nātpū*” young/fresh flower, here it also means young moon (not full in size).
- *nī* – you who are pleasant for our sight.
- innāḷ – now
- *mai vān iruḷ agaṟṟāy* – explained as, you, who are without any defect, are not removing the darkness in the sky; also explained as, you are not removing such black dense darkness. Just as a weak enemy would be crushed by a strong person, the darkness is crushing you who are weak now.
- *māḻāndu tēmbutiyāl* – you have waned now and lost your shine.
- *aivāy …* – Did you get caught in his big lies? As said in nācciyār tirumoḻi 10.3 “*tam pāmbu pōl nāvum iraṇḍuḷavāyiṟṟu*” (like his serpent \[bed\], he too has two tongues \[which means he does not speak the same way all the time\]) – if he has one mouth to lie, his servants have 5 mouths to lie. He learns to lie from his bed.
- *āḻip perumānār* – Even the serpent (ādi sēśa) looks a little better in comparison to sudarśana cakram. When [kriṣṇa](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) wanted to turn day into night, it was the sudarśana cakram which made it happen. When these servants of emperuān are glorified for helping, no wonder they are chastised when the desires are not fulfilled.
- *perumānār* –  He is such a great master in telling lies that all these servants of his learn the art of telling lies from him.
- *āḻip perumānār* *mey vāsagam* – When it is said as “*mey vāsagam*” (truthful words), why it is explained as “poy” (lie)? “*mey vāsagam*” is used to distinguish the commoners’ lies from emperumān’s lies \[viparīta lakśaṇā – satirically using the opposite word\]. He said “*ētat vratam mama*” (this is my vow) in srī rāmāyaṇam and you believed his words. Since those words are not fulfilled yet, she says that “it is a lie”. His truthful words in srī rāmāvatāram and his lies in kriṣṇāvatāram are the refuge for the devotees \[In [4th pāsuram](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/11/thiruvaimozhi-2-1-4-kadalum-malaiyum/), his lies are explained\].
- *un meyn nīrmai tōṟṟāyē* – you lost your beauty! You, who mercifully help remove darkness of the world, have lost your shine yourself.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.1.7. Torrom madanenjam

*tōṟṟōm mada nenjam emperumān nāraṇaṟku em āṟṟāmai solli aḻuvōmai nī naduvē vēṟṟōr vagaiyil kodidāy enai ūḻi māṟṟāṇmai niṟṟiyō? vāḻi kanai iruḷē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

em – our; perumān – master; nāraṇan – to srīman nārāyaṇan; madam – that which is humble towards us; nenjam – heart; tōṟṟōm – having lost it; em āṟṟāmai – (due to that) our sorrow; solli – spoke out loudly; aḻuvōmai – with respect to us who are crying; nī – you; naduvē – having entered in-between; vēṟṟōr vagaiyil – than the nature of enemies; kodiyadāy – more cruel; enai ūḻi – until eternity (forever); māṟṟāṇmai – being the one who can remove our suffering; niṟṟiyō – are you standing firm?; kanai – dense; iruḷē – Oh darkness!; vāḻi – instead of manifesting your presence and torturing us, let the sufferings vanish and live long

**Перевод:**

**Oh dense darkness! We are crying out loud having lost our humble heart to our master srīman nārāyaṇan. Being more cruel than enemies and having entered in between us (and emperumān), are you planning to stand firm forever? Instead of manifesting yourself, please be removed of your darkness and live long.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the seventh pāsuram, on seeing the darkness which blocks the vision of each other, parānkusa nāyaki asks “how long will you torture us?”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, parānkusa nāyaki asks the darkness “how long are you going to show your influence and torture me who is in sorrow of separation from bhagavān who is eternally related to me?”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s and  nampiḷḷai‘s introductions.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Seventh pāsuram – parānkusa nāyaki says “as the mind became bewildered, darkness (ignorance) took over it”. தோற்றோம் மட நெஞ்சம் எம் பெருமான் நாரணற்கு எம் ஆற்றாமை சொல்லி அழுவோமை நீ நடுவே வேற்றோர் வகையில் கொடிதாய் எனை ஊழி மாற்றாண்மை நிற்றியோ? வாழி கனை இருளே tōṟṟōm mada nenjam emperumān nāraṇaṟku em āṟṟāmai solli aḻuvōmai nī naduvē vēṟṟōr vagaiyil kodidāy enai ūḻi māṟṟāṇmai niṟṟiyō? vāḻi kanai iruḷē!*

- *tōṟṟōm …* (full pāsuram summary) – [emperumānār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/emperumanar/) focussed on the coining of words and explained it as – When I am suffering along with crane etc., (on seeing their suffering), instead of consoling me, you too are showing your suffering (of being dark) and increasing my sorrow. ammangi ammāḷ too insists on the same meaning.
- *tōṟṟōm* ***mada*** *nenjam* – We lost our heart which is greatly attached to bhagavat viśayam (matters relating to [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)). Alternatively, it is explained as – we lost our humble heart.
- *emperumān nāraṇaṟku* – Have we not lost our heart to the appropriate person? We have lost it to [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who shows motherly forbearance towards his dependents. nāraṇan is also explained as sulabhan – easily approachable \[one who dwells in everyone’s heart as antaryāmi\].
- *em āṟṟāmai solli aḻuvōmai* – īsn’t it natural for those who are desperate to cry out to accomplish what they want? What should we cry for? Should we cry to get him, should we cry to get back the lost heat? ōr should we cry for our helpless nature?
- *nī naduvē* – Unlike others who are crying with us, you are trying to block our union.  That too when there is no reason for you to torture (block) us.
- *vēṟṟōr vagaiyil kodidāy* – vēṟṟōr – satru (enemy). You are torturing even more than how enemies would do. Alternatively, even enemies should be forgiven \[arumpadam – Like srī rāma gave reprieve to rāvaṇa when rāvaṇa lost all his weapons\] – but you are not even doing that.
- *enai ūḻi māṟṟāṇmai niṟṟiyō* – Would you have this enmity forever? Your activities are different from those who are showing pity towards us and those who are showing enmity.
- *vāḻi* – Live long – It is like calling out a butcher as “brother” \[expecting some mercy out of him\].
- *kanai iruḷē* – dense darkness! Also explained as – darkness which shows anger.

An alternative explanation fitting the sequence of pāsurams is also given at the end – Without realising that there is an entity named tamas (darkness) which is naturally lacking light, [parānkusa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) thinks that due to separation from [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/), it has lost its shine and is unable to even call out to [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/). Seeing that, she says “your suffering is more than ours; at least after losing our heart we are calling out for [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)! But you are not even able to do that and that gives us more agony! Let your difficulties disappear and may you live long”.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.1.8. Irulin tinivannam

*iruḷin tiṇi vaṇṇam mā nīrk kaḻiyē! pōy maruḷuṟṟu irāp pagal tunjilum nī tunjāyāl uruḷum sagadam udaitta perumānār aruḷin peru nasaiyāl āḻāndu nondāyē ?*

**Пословный перевод:**

iruḷin – of the darkness; tiṇi – dense; vaṇṇam – having the color; mā – big; nīr – having water; kaḻiyē – Oh salt-pan!; pōy – very; maruḷ uṟṟu – bewildered; irāp pagal – during night and day; tunjilum – even if \[they\] end; nī – you; tunjāy – not sleeping; Al – thus; uruḷum – rolling; sagadam – wheel; udaitta – kicked (with his lotus feet); perumānār – great person’s; aruḷin – quality of compassion; peru – big; nasaiyāl – attachment/desire; āḻāndu – immersed; nondāyē – feeling pain?

**Перевод:**

**Oh salt-pan that has huge water which resembles dense darkness! You look bewildered and are not sleeping even if night and day end (change).  Thus, did you become captivated with the compassion of the great person (kriṣṇa), who kicked the rolling wheel (sakatāsura) with his lotus feet, and did you feel pained?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the eighth pāsuram, not knowing the difference between land and water due to darkness, parānkusa nāyaki reaches a salt-pan (where sea-salt is prepared) and asks it “did you also become flattened and are suffering for showing attachment towards emperumān like me?”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, parānkusa nāyaki sorrowfully asks a salt-pan “did you become attached towards emperumān‘s compassion?”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Eighth pāsuram – Retracting from the darkness, parānkusa nāyaki walked aimlessly and reached a salt-pan, which too is dark and walked in to it. Seeing it overflowing like those who cross the boundaries and send messages to their beloved, she asks “Oh poor thing! Did you get captivated in kriṣṇa’s act of killing sakatāsura?”. இருளின் திணி வண்ணம் மா நீர்க் கழியே போய் மருளுற்று இராப் பகல் துஞ்சிலும் நீ துஞ்சாயால் உருளும் சகடம் உதைத்த பெருமானார் அருளின் பெரு நசையால் ஆழாந்து நொந்தாயே? iruḷin tiṇi vaṇṇam mā nīrk kaḻiyē! pōy maruḷuṟṟu irāp pagal tunjilum nī tunjāyāl uruḷum sagadam udaitta perumānār aruḷin peru nasaiyāl āḻāndu nondāyē ?*

- iruḷin tiṇi vaṇṇam – fearsome darkness; not darkness mixed with some light – after extracting all light and making it as dense as a diamond. It is also explained as – Oh salt-pan that has the color of dense darkness and lots of water!
- *pōy maruḷ uṟṟu* – greatly bewildered. Your bewilderment matches that of those \[[āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) et al\] who are blessed with unblemiśed knowledge/devotion.
- *irāp pagal* … –  Even time which is endless may end; but we are not sighting an end for your suffering.
- *uruḷum sagadam udaitta* – The wheel of  the same cart which was kept as protection for kriṣṇa, being possessed by an asura, started rolling towards [kriṣṇa](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/). Even his own mother was not there to protect him; angered by not having been nursed (out of such anger), kriṣṇa kicked the wheel and killed the asura and thus gave the lord to the universe \[by protecting himself, he gave himself to us\]. Hoping that such upakāraka (great saviour), will also help his beloved.
- *aruḷin peru nasaiyāl* – \[our\] attachment is correspondingly greater with respect to \[his\] compassion.
- *āḻāndu nondāyē* – did you become flattened by his compassion and thus feel pained \[due to separation from such compassionate [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)\]?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.1.9. Nondarak kadalnoy

*nondu ārāk kādal nōy mel āvi uḷ ulartta nandā viḷakkamē! nīyum aḷiyattāy sendāmarait tadam kaṇ senganivāy em perumān am dāmam taṇ tuḻāy āsaiyāl vēvāyē?*

**Пословный перевод:**

nandā – continuous, without any break; viḷakkamē – Oh lamp!; aḷiyattāy – (such) distinct; nīyum – you too; nondu ārā – not being satisfied though being already engaged; kādal – love; nōy – sickness; mel – tender (like your body); āvi – prāṇa (vital air); uḷ – inside; ulartta – to dry it up; sem – reddish; tāmarai – like a lotus; tadam – huge; kaṇ – eyes; sem – reddish; kani – like a fruit; vāy – having the mouth; emperumān – my master; am – beautiful; taṇ tuḻāyt tāmam – cool tuḷasi garland’s; āsaiyāl – attachment/desire; vēvāyē – are you suffering in anguish?

**Перевод:**

**Oh distinct lamp that is constantly burning! Your love-sickness (that is not removed even after being already engaged in bhagavān) is drying up the life. Are you suffering in anguish of separation from my master who has reddish lotus like big eyes and reddish fruit like mouth?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the ninth pāsuram, parānkusa nāyaki returns to her palace and sees the oil-lamp which is burning there. She assumes that the lamp is burning out of separation from bhagavān and tells it “you too are suffering like me”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, parānkusa nāyaki says to an oil-lamp “Are you burning out of desire to enjoy bhagavān who has a form which attracts others?”*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Ninth pāsuram – Since the salt-pan does not unite with the sea (like herself who is not united with emperumān), she returns to her home and falls on her bed. She sees the oil-lamp which is burning there. Assuming that the oil-lamp too is burning out of virahajvaram (anguish of separation), she asks it “are you also suffering?”. நொந்து ஆராக் காதல் நோய் மெல் ஆவி உள் உலர்த்த நந்தா விளக்கமே! நீயும் அளியத்தாய் செந்தாமரைத் தடம் கண் செங்கனி வாய் எம் பெருமான் அம் தாமம் தண் துழாய் ஆசையால் வேவாயே? nondu ārāk kādal nōy mel āvi uḷ ulartta nandā viḷakkamē! nīyum aḷiyattāy sendāmarait tadam kaṇ senganivāy em perumān am dāmam taṇ tuḻāy āsaiyāl vēvāyē?*

- *nondu ārāk kādal nōy* – the suffering never ends in love-sickness which desiccates (dehydrates) the [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) which is very tender.
- *mellāvi* – [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) which is very meek due to being immersed in [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s qualities; [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) which cannot even bear the touch of air.
- *nandā viḷakkamē* – the lamp which never turns off. Though the flame is changing every moment by continuous burning, [parānkusa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/), who is in disturbed state of mind \[due to separation from [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)\], does not see the subtle change in the flame and says the \[same\] flame is alive for ever \[arumpadam – the main meaning is – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says that even if the flame dies, the suffering would end immediately – instead it keeps on burning and seeking union with [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s like [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) who himself is seeking the same\].
- *nīyum aḷiyattāy* – You who are the one who helps others by providing light, are suffering yourself.
- *aḷiyattāy* – you who are to be shown compassion by all. You, who exist purely for others, are yourself suffering from disease!
- *sendāmarai …* – Did you desire to have the tuḷasi garland from [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), just like [sītā pirātti](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/) (as seen in srī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 16.21) “*patisammānitā sītā bharttāram asitēkśaṇā …*” (one who was honoured \[with a garland\] by srī rāma and one who has beautiful black eyes followed [srī rāma](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) up to the gate praying for his well-being)?
- *sem tāmarait tadam kaṇ* – highlighting the freshness of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s eyes when he glanced lovingly
- *sem kani vāy* – highlighting the reddish nature of his divine lips when he speaks sweet words
- *emperumān …* – with the desire to acquire the tuḷasi garland of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who captured me fully through his glances and sweet words.
- *vēvāyē* – the flame which will go off easily even for the air from fan – you are burning fiercely now!

In the ne xt article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.1.10. Vevara vetkainoy

*vēvu ārā vētkai nōy mel āvi uḷ ulartta ōvādu irāp pagal unpālē vīḻttu oḻindāy mā vāy piḷandu marudidai pōy maṇ aḷanda mūvā mudalvā! ini emmaic cōrēlē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vēvārā – not satisfied with torturing; nōy – disease (love-sickness); mel – weak (due to separation); āvi – ātmā; uḷ – like dried leaf; ulartta – to dry it completely; irāp pagal – night and day; ōvādu – incessantly; un pālē – in your qualities; vīḻtu oḻindāy – one who captivated me; mā – the horse’s (that was the enemy of those who approach you); vāy – mouth; piḷandu – tore; marudu – (twin) arjuna tree; idai – in between; pōy – entered; maṇ – the earth (to make it fully subservient); aḷandu – measured; mūvā – being every youthful; mudalvā – Oh the cause of all!; ini – going forward; emmai – us; cōrēl – never leave us

**Перевод:**

**Oh emperumān who tore the mouth of kēsi (horse), who crawled in between the twin trees and measured the earth, who is the cause of all! My already tender/meek ātmā has further fully dried up by being tortured by love-sickness and you made me fully subservient to you by showing your qualities! Now onvards, please don’t fail \[leave\] me ever. In this, āḻvār contemplates how emperumān eliminated the obstacles and sustained him.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the tenth pāsuram – On seeing emperumān who united with her to remove her fatigue, parānkusa nāyaki prays to him “You should never leave me”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, emperumān who is sarvakāraṇabhūtan (the cause of all) arrives there on seeing parānkusa nāyaki‘s suffering and parānkusa nāyaki prays to him “you should never leave me”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. வேவு ஆரா வேட்கை நோய் மெல் ஆவி உள் உலர்த்த ஓவாது இராப் பகல் உன்பாலே வீழ்த்து ஒழிந்தாய் மா வாய் பிளந்து மருதிடை போய் மண் அளந்த மூவா முதல்வா! இனி எம்மைச் சோரேலே vēvu ārā vētkai nōy mel āvi uḷ ulartta ōvādu irāp pagal unpālē vīḻttu oḻindāy mā vāy piḷandu marudidai pōy maṇ aḷanda mūvā mudalvā! ini emmaic cōrēlē*

- *vēvārā vētkai nōy* – If it started torturing, it will not stop with just torturing once. Unlike other diseases (of the body), this love-disease (of love-sickness of separation from [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)) is never ending \[since this affects the [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) which is eternal\].
- *mellāvi* – Like her tender body, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s self too is very tender in nature.
- *uḷ ulartta* – As said in srī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 85.17 “… *gūdōgniriva pādapam*” (like drying of the leaves in a tree by the fire inside the tree-hole), it tortures from inside ([ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)) to outside (body). [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) is said to be adāhyam (incombustible – unable to be burnt – [srī bhagavat gītā](http://githa.koyil.org/) 2.24), yet it cannot be burnt only by material fire \[the anguish of separation from [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) will hurt the [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)\]. As said in srī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 35.44 “… *mahatā jvalatā nityamagninēvāgni parvata:*” \[Oh revered sītā! Having not seen you, [srī rāma](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is in anguish like a huge/burning mountain of fire\].
- *ōvādu irāp pagal* – Just like the eternal disease, the night and day also seem to be so long.
- *un pālē vīḻtu oḻindāy* – two explanations:
   - You captivated me towards you from whom no one can return.
   - You captivated me towards you and yet you are staying far away without being friendly.
- *māvāy …* – two explanations:
   - \[Focus on mūvā – being still energetic, looking to help\] Having casually torn kēsi’s mouth, having entered in between the twin-trees, having recovered the land by conquering \[measuring\] over that land that was grabbed by mahābali – after having done so much favours, feeling that you have not done enough, you are looking forward to help everyone.
   - \[Focus on mudalvā – cause\] Having done all of these, as if you have not done anything, you performed creation etc., of the universe etc.
- *ini emmai cōrēlē* – two explanations:
   - [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) requesting [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) to arrive at him just by eliminating the obstacles like he eliminated kēsi et al.
   - [parānkusa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) faithfully requesting [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), seeing the great dangers she is facing in not uniting with him.
- *ini* – Even if the past is gone, at least in future she wants to be united with [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/). It is also explained that – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is feeling for the time lost with emperumān until now. srī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 5.5 is quoted here: “*na mē dukkam priyā dūrē*” – I am not grieving for my dear (sītā) being far away; if I took up a journey, I can easily reach her; “*na mē dukkam hrutēti vā*” – I am not grieving that this separation was caused by a rākśasa, by cutting off his head, that grief will be eliminated; “*ētadēvānusōcāmi*”  – this is my only grief; “*vayōsyā hyativarttatē*” – \[that is,\] I can never bring back the lost time. So, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s state of separation from [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is like [srī rāma](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s separation from [sītā pirātti](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.1.11. Sorada epporutkum

*sōrāda ep porutkum ādiyām sōdikkē ārāda kādal kurukūrc catakōpan ōrāyiram sonna avaṟṟuḷ ivai pattum sōrār vidār kaṇḍīr vaikundam tiṇṇanavē*

**Пословный перевод:**

sōrāda – without leaving out even a single entity; epporutkum – for all entities; ādiyām – being the cause; sōdikkē – one who is known by the term “paramjyōti” \[supreme effulgence\]; ārāda – insatiable; kādal – having affection; kurukūrc catakōpan – nammāḻvār; ōr – unique; āyiram – in thousand pāsurams; sonna avaṟṟuḷ – among those which are spoken; ivai pattum – these 10 pāsurams (which are filled with great love); sōrār – ones who stick to (these pāsurams); vaikundam – that paramapadam; tiṇṇana – certainly; vidār kaṇḍīr – those who will never miss it

**Перевод:**

**Those who stick to these ten pāsurams amongst the unique thousand pāsurams which are spoken by āḻvār who has insatiable affection towards bhagavān who is known as paramjyōti and who is the cause of everything, will certainly never miss to reach paramapadam.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the end, āḻvār says “those who learned this decade will eternally live in paramapadam; this is certain”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār mercifully says that the result of (learning) this decad is the attainment of paramapadam.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*In the end – āḻvār says “Those who learned this decad, instead of staying in samsāram (material realm) where everything that is visible is suffering in separation from bhagavān, will enter paramapadam (spiritual realm) where everyone who is visible is blissfully living in union with bhagavān”. சோராத எப் பொருட்கும் ஆதியாம் சோதிக்கே ஆராத காதல் குருகூர்ச் சடகோபன் ஓராயிரம் சொன்ன அவற்றுள் இவை பத்தும் சோரார் விடார் கண்டீர் வைகுந்தம் திண்ணனவே sōrāda ep porutkum ādiyām sōdikkē ārāda kādal kurukūrc catakōpan ōrāyiram sonna avaṟṟuḷ ivai pattum sōrār vidār kaṇḍīr vaikundam tiṇṇanavē*

- *sōrāda epporutkum ādiyām sōdikkē* – For descending upto [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) and helping āḻvār sustain himself, bhagavān is highlighted as the [īsvara (controller)](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) of all and because of bonding with [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/), he became radiant \[jyōti\]. Before bonding with āḻvār, his [sarvēśvara](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)tvam (being the controller of all) seemed to have disappeared. If [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) fails āḻvār, then his [sarvēśvara](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)tvam will completely vanish. But, after bonding with [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) to the full satisfaction of āḻvār, he becomes controller of all.
- *sōdikkē* – Instead of considering the loss/gain as [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s, [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) considers fulfilling āḻvār’s desires as his own gain and not doing so is his own loss – so after āḻvār’s desire was fulfilled, [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s form became radiant \[out of happiness\]. He became as explained in samkśēpa rāmāyaṇam “… *krutakrutya: …*” (After crowning vibhīśaṇa as the king of lankā, srī rāma felt as one who has performed all his duties and one who was relieved from fever).
- *ārāda kādal* – It is explained in this decad – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s great affection towards [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), which makes him think that all the entities he sees are suffering in separation from [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) like he himself is going through.
- *kādal kurukūrc catakōpan* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is identified by his love/affection \[kriṣṇa truṣṇā tatvam\]. Only he himself can explain his nature.
- *sonna* – He spoke tiruvāimoḻi with this great love.
- *avaṟṟuḷ ivai pattum* – if we compare this decad with the rest of tiruvāimoḻi, this decad reveals [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s love fully (unlike other decads).
- *ivai pattum sōrār vidār kaṇḍīr vaikundam* – those who suffered here for all entities which were seen that they are suffering in separation, will give up this place and reach paramapadam where every visible person is fully and joyfully engaging with [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) and eternally be blissful there. By saying “*kaṇḍīr*“, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is raising his hands and showing “see for yourself”.
- *tiṇṇanavē* – this is most-certain; if we say something based on the matters/persons of this material realm, there is room for doubt, but when it is said based on [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s abilities/greatness, there is no doubt.

From the first pāsuram, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) grieved for crane, ibis, sea, wind, cloud, moon, darkness, salt-pan, oil-lamp and became very week. At that time, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) arrives there and [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says to him “Never leave me hereafter” and explains the result for those who learned this decad.

[āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) tiruvadigaḷē caraṇam  
[emperumānār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/emperumanar/) tiruvadigaḷē caraṇam  
[piḷḷān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/pillan/) tiruvadigaḷē caraṇam  
[nanjīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nanjiyar/) tiruvadigaḷē caraṇam

[vadakkut tiruvīdip piḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadakku-thiruvidhi-pillai/) tiruvadigaḷē caraṇam  
[periyavāccān piḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/periyavachchan-pillai/) tiruvadigaḷē caraṇam  
[vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/) tiruvadigaḷē caraṇam

## 2.2 Tinnan vidu

## 2.2.1. Tinnan vidu

*tiṇṇan vīdu mudal muḻudum āy eṇṇin mīdiyan em perumān maṇṇum viṇṇum ellām udan uṇḍa nam kaṇṇan kaṇṇalladu illai ōr kaṇṇē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tiṇ – having strength; nal – unique; vīdu – mōkśam; mudal – etc; muḻudumāy – being the controller for all results; eṇṇin mīdiyan – having incomprehensible nature that is beyond our thoughts; emperumān – master who lorded me (by showing such supremacy); maṇṇum – earth; viṇṇum – higher regions; ellām – without missing anything; udan – in single effort (without discrimination); uṇḍa – protecting them by keeping them in the stomach; nam kaṇṇan – the most simple emperumān in the form of kriṣṇa who gave himself to us; kaṇ – the controller of the entire creation; alladu – other than him; ōr – one; kaṇ – controlling entity; illai – does not exist

**Перевод:**

**emperumān who is the controller of all results/goals such as the strong, unique mōkśam (liberation) etc., whose incomprehensible nature is beyond our thoughts, my master who lorded me (by showing such supremacy) , who protected all by keeping everyone/everything in his stomach during annihilation, is the same kriṣṇa who appeared and presented himself to us. He is the supreme controller for the universe and there is no other controlling entity that exists. kaṇ means kaḷaigaṇ – protection. tiṇṇan is also explained as tiṇṇam (niścitam – certainty).**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In first pāsuram – āḻvār says kriṣṇa is the controller of the universe.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*In the first pāsuram – āḻvār says kriṣṇa is the only controller of everyone.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction. āḻvār says kriṣṇa, who is filled with auspicious qualities and who is the one who protects everyone during annihilation, is the controller.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*First pāsuram – āḻvār briefly explains bhagavān‘s supremacy, which is further elaborated in this decad. திண்ணன் வீடு முதல் முழுதும் ஆய் எண்ணின் மீதியன் எம் பெருமான் மண்ணும் விண்ணும் எல்லாம் உடன் உண்ட நம் கண்ணன் கண் அல்லது இல்லை ஓர் கண்ணே tiṇṇan vīdu mudal muḻudum āy eṇṇin mīdiyan em perumān maṇṇum viṇṇum ellām udan uṇḍa nam kaṇṇan kaṇṇalladu illai ōr kaṇṇē*

- *tiṇṇan vīdu mudal muḻudumāy* – tiṇṇan means tiṇṇam, i.e., drudam – firm. Firmness is an adjective to vīdu (mōkśam) which is nitya vibhūti (paramapadam – spiritual realm). Firmness here indicates the absence of birth/death, creation/annihilation cycles which are due to karma – but changes do happen due to [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s desire in paramapadam. Even if there is some destruction it is not to be seen like that – it is only part of [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s sport since there are no defects which are based on karma (puṇyam and pāpam of individuals) as seen in samsāram (material realm). mudal – etc. So, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is the master of nitya vibhūti and leelā vibhūti. *vīdu mudal muḻudumāy* – [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) who is having the quality of granting different goals such as aiśvaryam (worldly wealth), kaivalyam (self-realisation and enjoyment) and mōkśam (vīdu – liberation) (explaining this one quality is a sample for his multifarious qualities).
- *eṇṇin mīdiyan* – one who is having innumerable auspicious qualities. If the previous phrase is explained in the context of vibhūti (spiritual and material realms), this is explained in the context of auspicious qualities. If the previous phrase is explained in the context of auspicious qualities, this is explained in the context of vibhūti. If “*vīdu mudal muḻudumāy”* is only explained for that single quality, *eṇṇin mīdiyan* explains the previously unspoken auspicious qualities of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/). “eṇṇin mīdiyan” means beyond count.
- *emperumān* – one who became my master by showing such greatness.
- *maṇṇum viṇṇum ellām* – Since kaṇṇan (kriṣṇa) is the natural owner, when the great annihilation covers earth, sky etc, he picks them all up and places them carefully in his stomach and protects them all at once.
- *udan uṇḍa* – Since he cannot sustain himself without protecting his subjects, “*uṇḍa*” (ate) is used. If he was simply protecting (like a king), using the word “kākkum” (protection) could have been sufficient.
- *nam kaṇṇan kaṇ* – Did kriṣṇa consume the universe? Yes – kriṣṇa only. As said in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 1.1.6 “‘angāndida vaiymēḻum kaṇḍāḷ’iṟē yaśōdai” (mother yaśōdā saw the entire creation when kriṣṇa opened his month). So, kriṣṇa is the protector for the entire creation. This is established in well known source of mahābhāratam bhīśma parvam “*kriṣṇa Eva hi lōkānāmutpattirap cāpyaya: \| kriṣṇasya hi krutē …*” (It is well known that all creation is done by krikṣṇa, annihilation is also done by kriṣṇa and the existence of everything is for kriṣṇa).
- *alladu illai ōr kaṇṇē* – “*ōr kaṇ*” (one \[unique\] protection) – if we try to explain this in any other manner (that someone else is protector) it will not make any sense, like the eyes in the peacock feathers (which don’t see). \[for example, we see some other controllers like brahmā et al, in this world\]. For those who see māl (śrīman nārāyaṇan) as protector, others will be seen as dependents only.  This is tiṇṇam – drudam – certain. Like it is said in itihāsams/purāṇams “*satyam satyam punas satyam …*” (I declare the truth again and again). [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) declares [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s supremacy positively in “*nam kaṇṇan kaṇ*” and rejects others’ supremacy in “*alladu illai*“.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.2.2. Epavam parame

*ē! pāvam paramē ēḻ ulagum ee pāvam seydu aruḷāl aḷippār ār mā pāvam vida araṟkup piccai pey gōpāla kōḷari ēṟu anṟiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

mā – very big; pāvam – sin (against one’s own preceptor); vida – to be erased; araṟku – for rudra; piccai pey – one who offered alms; gōpāla kōḷ ari ēṟu – the lion amongst those who are born in covherd clan; anṟiyē – if not; ēḻulagum – all worlds; eepāvam seydu – to be with eradicated (eliminated) sins; aruḷāl – out of his compassion; aḷippār – one who protects (by fulfilling the desires); Ar – who?; ēpāvam – how sad!; paramē – become my responsibility (to establish the supremacy of emperumān); E – showing dislike

**Перевод:**

**āḻvār asks “Who else can protect all the worlds out of compassion other than kriṣṇa who is the lion amongst those are born in covherd clan and the one who offered alms to rudra to erase the effects of a very big sin?”. With dislike he says “How sad! It has become my responsibility (to establish the supremacy of emperumān) \[which is already well established\]”.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says kriṣṇa is the cause for aniśta nivrutti (removal of unwanted aspects) and iśta prāpti (bestowing the desired aspects).*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction. periyavāccān piḷḷai nicely coins the question as asked by āḻvār “Is ‘others being non-controllers (dependents)’ not obvious that it needs to be separately discussed and established?”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Second pāsuram – When asked “Why are you saying ‘alladu illai’ (there is no other controller)? āren’t brahmā, rudra et al also explained as controllers in some scriptures?”, āḻvār says that when their situations are analysed one person gets his head cut off, and another person cut the head off; emperumān is the one who removed the defects of both of them and so you tell me if they are controllers or he is the controller? ஏ! பாவம் பரமே ஏழ் உலகும் ஈ பாவம் செய்து அருளால் அளிப்பார் ஆர் மா பாவம் விட அரற்குப் பிச்சை பெய் கோபால கோளரி ஏறு அன்றியே? E! pāvam paramē ēḻ ulagum ee pāvam seydu aruḷāl aḷippār Ar mā pāvam vida araṟkup piccai pey gōpāla kōḷari ēṟu anṟiyē*

- *ēpāvam* – “E!” indicates “O!” (alas!) – abundance of distress.
- *ēpāvam* – āḻvār says “We are forced to explicitly speak about the differences between diamond and dung”. He says “How sad! People have become so foolish that we are forced to try and establish the well-known supremacy of [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)“.
- *paramē* – bharam – responsibility; Instead of enjoying the divine auspicious qualities of [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/), I am forced to explain his supremacy to others \[By definition, āḻvār means one who is immersed in [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s qualities etc and has less inclination towards instructing others – It is only out of compassion to uplift others that they engage in instructing others\].
- *ēḻulagum* – While the residents of the seven worlds engage in accumulating more and more sins,
- *īpāvam seydu* – to eradicate their sins

Without the [jīvātmās](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) requesting [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) to help them,

- *aruḷāl* – out of his unconditional unsolicited grace
- *aḷippār Ar* – Who will protect these souls? These sins can be eradicated only by his grace and not by their self-effort or atonement. When they try on their own, they will only end up increasing the sins. Instead of saying “*aḷippān ivan*” ([emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is the protector), āḻvār is saying “Who will protect?” – this is to convince them when they are situated in satvam (goodness) so that they would accept saying “Only the one about whom you are speaking about” . This is explained in śrī rāmāyaṇam uttara kāṇḍam “*pāvanssarvalōkanām tvamēva*” (śrī rāma! You are the one capable of removing the sins and purifying every one) and śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 1.22.19 “*nahi pālana sāmartyam rutē*” (No one has the ability to protect other than viṣṇu who is the supreme controller of everyone). His helping everyone is well-known.
- *mā pāvam vida* – to eradicate the great sin. “*ānaikkum tanakkut takka vādamiṟē*” (an elephant would have problem that matches its size – this is to identify the nature of sins committed by great personalities). In comparison with others, rudra is distinct when it comes to jñānam (knowledge) and śakti (capability); But using such knowledge and ability, he became a sinner by plucking the head of brahmā who is the master of the (material) universe \[the universe which is under his control – there are innumerable universes each one having a brahmā as the leader\]. To be relieved of the great sin that is identified in matsya purāṇam “… *vāmānguśtanakāgrēṇa cinnam tasya śirō mayā*” (Siva says – “the head of brahmā was plucked by me using my left hand thumb finger nail”).
- *araṟkup piccai pey gōpāla kōḷari ēṟu* – Though rudra is the annihilator \[appointed by [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) with great authority/responsibility\], he committed a sin and still [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) rescued him from that situation during [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s incarnations in this mortal world.  gōpāla (kriṣṇa as cow-herd boy) term is used here to indicate that irrespective of the greatness of these dēvatās and whatever humble form [śrīman nārāyaṇan](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) assumes, śrīman nārāyaṇan is the only protector.
- *gōpāla kōḷ ari ēṟu* – kōḷ – pride; kōḷ (extension of koḷ) – one who overrules the detractors. The pride of being the leader of cow-herds even though he is the leader of nityasūris (eternally servitors in paramapadam). Should we call those who get trapped in danger as īśvara (controller) or should we call the one who rescues them from such danger as īśvara?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.2.3. Eranaip puvanai

*ēṟanai pūvanai pūmagaḷ tannai vēṟinṟi viṇ toḻat tannuḷ vaittu mēl tannai mīdida nimirndu maṇ koṇḍa māl tanil mikkum ōr tēvum uḷadē?*

**Пословный перевод:**

ēṟanai – rudra who rides a riśaba (bull); pūvanai – brahmā who is seated on a lotus; pūmagaḷ tannai – śrī mahālakśmi who is part of his distinct identity and who is seated in a lotus flower; vēṟu inṟi – without any other opinion (than having her in his divine chest); than uḷ – inside his divine body; viṇ – the residents of paramapadam (who know such excellent disposition of emperumān with all); toḻa – to worship him; vaittu – having kept; mēl tannai – the higher world; mīdida – stepping over; nimirndu – grew; maṇ – the earth; koṇḍa – measured and accepted; māl tanil – than the great person; mikkum – anything greater; ōr – one/any; tēvum – God; uḷadē – exist?

**Перевод:**

**Is there any one greater than the great (emperumān) who keeps 1) rudra who rides a bull, 2) brahmā who is seated on a lotus and 3) śrīmahālakśmi who is inseparable and seated on a lotus in his divine chest – in his divine body to be vorśipped by the residents of paramapadam (who know emperumān’s excellent disposition towards all). and who measured the higher (celestial) world by running his feet over the earth, measuring it and accepting it?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the third pāsuram – āḻvār says that due to emperumān‘s sauseelyam (excellent disposition) and super-human activities such as measuring the three worlds, he is the īśvara (controller).*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says emperumān is the greatest of all.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. ஏறனை பூவனை பூமகள் தன்னை வேறுஇன்றி விண் தொழத் தன்னுள் வைத்து மேல் தன்னை மீதிட நிமிர்ந்து மண் கொண்ட மால் தனின் மிக்கும் ஓர் தேவும் உளதே? ēṟanai pūvanai pūmagaḷ tannai vēṟinṟi viṇ toḻat tannuḷ vaittu mēl tannai mīdida nimirndu maṇ koṇḍa māl tanil mikkum ōr tēvum uḷadē?*

- *ēṟanai* – Just like [sarvēśvaran](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is proud about his having garuda as his vehicle, rudra is proud about having the bull as his vehicle (like a covherd who would be proud about his cattle).
- *pūvanai* – brahmā who is proud about his direct connection with [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/). It is because of this direct birth in the lotus flower that he is called as “aja”.
- *pūmagaḷ tannai* – one who is made of the fragrance of the lotus flower, who is the embodiment of sweetness (most enjoyable)  and who has equal importance to [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) himself as mentioned in tiruvāimoḻi 10.10.6 “*unakku ēṟkum*” (one who fits your stature). “*tannai*” after “*pūmagaḷ*” highlights her importance over others. While they are mentioned casually as “*ēṟanai*“, “*pūvanai*” – she is mentioned with great emphasis in “*pūmagaḷ tannai*“.
- *viṇ toḻa vēṟu inṟit tannuḷ vaittu* – the residents of paramapadam worship emperumān with great astonishment for his quality of accommodating rudra, brahmā et al who are not firm in their devotion along with [śrī mahālakśm](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/)i who exists purely for emperumān’s pleasure. [nanjīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nanjiyar/) asks [bhattar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/parasara-bhattar/) “Do brahmā, rudra  et al hold on the emperumān’s divine form always?” and bhattar replies “No, they are accommodated in a place by emperumān in his divine body during grave dangers. āḻvārs, holding on to such quality, always  speak about it”.
- *vēṟu inṟi* – As said in tiruvāimoḻi 4.8.1 “*kūṟāḷum tani udamban*” ([emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who has a divine body where each one takes over a particular part and lives there), handing over his divine body parts in proper order to others.
- *viṇ toḻa* – As in “*manjā: krōśanti*” (bed making noise means one lying on the bed is making noise) – here (spiritual) sky (paramapadam) vorśipping means the residents of paramapadam are vorśipping. The residents of this material world are amazed with bhagavān’s supremacy and the residents of the spiritual world are amazed with his simplicity.
- *mēl tannai mīdida nimirndu maṇ koṇḍa* – *mēl tannai* – the higher worlds. As said in tiruneduntāṇḍagam 5 “*appāl mikku*” (greater than the higher places), all parts of earth came under his stretched out lotus feet.
- *māl tanil* – greater than [sarvēśvaran](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) who manifested such super-human activity
- *mikkumōr tēvum uḷadē* – is there any one greater who exists? Even when [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is mixing freely with all dēvatās, is there any one who can be compared with him? Should I declare [śrīman nārāyaṇan](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who touched everyone with his lotus feet as supreme or should I declare those who were touched on their heads by that lotus feet as supreme?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.2.4. Tevum epporulum

*tēvum ep poruḷum padaikkap pūvil nānmuganaip padaitta tēvan emperumānukku allāl pūvum pūsanaiyum tagumē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tēvum – the celestial beings; epporuḷum – all beings starting with the human beings; padaikka – to create; pūvil – in the lotus flower positioned in his navel; nānmuganai – catur muka brahmā (four headed brahmā); padaitta – one who created; tēvan – dēva (supreme God); emperumān – my master; allāl – if not (for him); pūvum – offerings such as flower; pūsanaiyum – ārādana upacāram (worshiping and attending); tagumē – does it fit? It does not

**Перевод:**

**Would worshiping and attending, offerings such as flowers be a fit for anyone other than emperumān who created four headed brahmā in the lotus flower positioned in his navel in order to create celestial beings, human beings and all other types of beings?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fourth pāsuram – āḻvār says “since there is no one other than emperumān who has matching beauty/tenderness of the flower and the predominance to accept worship, he alone is the sarvēśvaran (supreme controller)”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says none has predominance to accept worship like him (bhagavān).*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Fourth pāsuram – āḻvār says emperumān is the īśvara due to his tender nature and his predominance. தேவும் எப் பொருளும் படைக்கப் பூவில் நான்முகனைப் படைத்த தேவன் எம் பெருமானுக்கு அல்லால் பூவும் பூசனையும் தகுமே? tēvum ep poruḷum padaikkap pūvil nānmuganaip padaitta tēvan emperumānukku allāl pūvum pūsanaiyum tagumē*

- *tēvum epporuḷum padaikkap pūvil nānmukanaip padaitta* – To create celestial beings and all other entities, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) created four headed brahmā in the lotus flower in his navel (like 4 flowers in a flower).
- *tēvan* – dēva – The word dēva has many meanings in samskrutam. a) Majesty due to creating brahmā, b) one who does creation as a sport (effortlessly), c) one who is radiant due to his beauty etc.
- *emperumānukku allāl* – if not for [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who overwhelmed me through great favours such as creation \[Only through creation, a bound soul gets an opportunity to reach [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)\] and through those (supreme) qualities which make him the creator
- *pūvum pūsanaiyum tagumē* – For the one with matted hair, flowers are not applicable;  worshiping does not fit for one who begs for alms. Flowers are to be offered to one who is tender natured; worshiping befits the one who is predominant; [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says that except for [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), no one else is qualified to accept worship.  In mahābhāratam, during rājasūya yāgam, bhīśma explains [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s supremacy and concludes in the end to pāṇḍavas “yaśca dēvō mayā druśta: purā padmāyatēkśaṇa: \| *sa ēśa prutudīrgākśas sambandī tē janārdana: \|\|*”  (The lotus-eyed lord ([kriṣṇa](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)) who is explained in śruti as supreme has now appeared as your father’s sister’s son). But when sahadēva (one among the pāṇḍavas) declared “*arcyamarccitumiccāmas sarvē sammantumarhata*” (We consider [kriṣṇa](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) as vorśipable – you (those who are in this assembly) are capable of acknowledging his glories to facilitate his worship); hearing this vow, the celestial beings rained flowers on sahadēva in joy. From this we can understand that, vairājñam \[sahadēva declaring [kriṣṇa](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) as vorśippable and encouraging others to accept that\] is more important than jñānam \[bhīśma merely highlighting kriṣṇa’s supremacy\].

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.2.5. Tagum sir

*tagum sīrt tan tani mudalinuḷḷē migum dēvum ep poruḷum padaikka tagum kōlat tāmaraik kaṇṇan emmān migum sōdi mēl aṟivār yavarē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tagum – suitable (for creation etc); sīr – one who is having qualities such as jñānam (knowledge), śakti (capability) etc; than – his; tani – distinct; mudalin uḷḷē – in the vow which is the cause (for the world); migum – greater (which leads to the doubt of being controller); tēvum – celestial beings such as brahmā, rudra et al; epporuḷum – all beings/objects starting with humans; padaikka – to create; tagum – that which highlights that “he is suitable”; kōlam – beautiful; tāmarai – like a lotus flower; kaṇṇan – with the eyes; emmān – than my master; migum sōti – param jyōti (supreme radiance); mēl – greater than this; aṟivār – knovers (among vaidikas); yavar – who?

**Перевод:**

**Are there any vaidikas who know someone greater in radiance than emperumān who has lotus like beautiful eyes which highlight the ability to create great dēvas (brahmā, rudra et al), human beings and all other entities just with his distinct will/vow and who has suitable qualities such as knowledge, ability etc for creation etc?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fifth pāsuram – āḻvār says “Due to his having lotus-eyes, he alone is supreme”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār explains the lotus-eyed nature of emperumān which reveals his supremacy.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. தகும் சீர்த் தன் தனி முதலினுள்ளே மிகும் தேவும் எப் பொருளும் படைக்கத் தகும் கோலத் தாமரைக் கண்ணன் எம்மான் மிகும் சோதி மேல் அறிவார் எவரே? tagum sīrt than tani mudalinuḷḷē migum dēvum ep poruḷum padaikka tagum kōlat tāmaraik kaṇṇan emmān migum sōdi mēl aṟivār yavarē*

- *tagum* … *padaikka* – One who is having those qualities such as jñānam, śakti etc., which are used in creation
- *than tani mudalinuḷḷē* – primordial matter which is the cause for all material effects; it can also be said as the sankalpa jñānam (divine will) of [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) as said in taittiriya upaniśat “*bahusyām*” (let me become many) which is the cause for creation.
- *tani mudal* – Singular cause; differentiating from philosophers such as those who present paramāṇu (atomic particles) as kāraṇam (cause)
- *migum dēvum*  … – dēvatās (celestial beings) who are at times confused to be supreme. Their supremacy is only visible until the doubt is cleared as seen in śrī rāmāyaṇam bāla kāṇḍam 75.19 “…adikam mēnirē viṣṇum…” (once the dēvas saw viṣṇu breaking Siva’s bow, they understood the greatness of viṣṇu).
- *epporuḷum* – All objects. His eyes reveal that he is the one who is qualified to create everything. Even if he does not have the ability to protect \[hypothetically speaking\], he has eyes which are most beautiful, cool and those which won over me. He is the most radiant. He too was won over in a similar manner as in the case of tiruvadi (hanuman). nampiḷḷai explains śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 53.8 here. *rāma:* – One who is completely beautiful; *kamalapatrākśa: –* his eyes are like a swirl in a river (to get sucked in); what is the ability of those eyes? *sarvasatvamanōhara:* – They could even steal the heart of mine (who is born as an animal that jumps from branch to branch). *rūpadākśiṇyasampanna: prasūta:* – one who has unlimited bodily qualities and spiritual qualities has appeared as śrī rāma; *janktmajē* – Oh śītā! you too are equally great (hanuman speaking towards her in most eloquent manner).
- *migum sōti* – As seen in cāndōhya upaniśat “*paramjyōtirupa sampadya:*” (reaching brahmam who is explained by the term paramjyōti:), nārāyaṇa sūktam “*nārāyaṇana parōjyōti:*” (nārāyaṇa, the supreme radiance) etc., [śrīman nārāyaṇan](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) alone is explained as paramjyōti.
- *mēlaṟivār yavarē* – Is there anyone who knows “Except [śrīman nārāyaṇan](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), there is someone else talked about and established through nārāyaṇa anuvākam (sūktam)”?
- *yavarē* – This is similar to [āḷavandār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/alavandhar/) challenging everyone in stōtra ratnam 11 “*vaidika: ka:*” (which vēdānta scholar who rejects your supremacy over all other dēvatās? – implies no one will do that). Is there any vēdānta scholar who shows jealousy towards you who is clearly glorified in nārāyaṇa anuvākam etc? If such a person exists, he can be declared as avaidika (one who is ignorant of vēdānta). This is explained in pādma purāṇam “*viṣṇu bhakti vihīnō … tasya utpattir nirūpyatām*” (Even though one is well learned in all śāstram, if he does not accept the supremacy of [viṣṇu](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/), he is not entitled to be called a brāhmaṇa and his birth is questionable).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.2.6. Yavarum yavaiyum

*yavarum yāvaiyum ellāp poruḷum kavarvu inṟit tannuḷ odunga ninṟa pavar koḷ jñāna veḷḷac cudar mūrtti avar em āḻi ampaḷḷiyārē*

**Пословный перевод:**

yavarum – all cētanas (sentient beings); yāvaiyum – all acētnas (insentient objects); ellāp poruḷum – all such objects; kavarvinṟi – effortlessly; tannuḷ – within a part of him; odunga – being subdued; ninṟa – stayed; pavarkoḷ – having vastness; jñānaveḷḷam – abundance of knowledge; sudar – having it as a glow; mūrti – one who is the master; avar – that emperumān who is greater than all; em – being enjoyable for us; am – spectacular; āḻi – in the milk ocean; paḷḷiyār – resting there

**Перевод:**

**Our lord and master, who effortlessly consumes all objects – cētanas and acētanas, and keeps them inside (his stomach) and stays having vast and abundant knowledge as his glow, who is enjoyable for us, is resting in the spectacular milk ocean.  sudar mūrti can also be explained as vigraham (divine form).**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the sixth pāsuram – āḻvār says bhagavān alone is the īśvara (controller) since he protects all cit (sentient) and acit (insentient) by keeping them in his stomach (during praḷayam – dissolution).*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says emperumān is resting in kśīrārṇavam (milk-ocean) to protect his devotees.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Sixth pāsuram – since he is the one who helps during difficulties, āḻvār says that he is the īsvara (controller). எவரும் யாவையும் எல்லாப் பொருளும் கவர்வு இன்றித் தன்னுள் ஒடுங்க நின்ற பவர் கொள் ஞான வெள்ளச் சுடர் மூர்த்தி அவர் எம் ஆழி அம் பள்ளியாரே yavarum yāvaiyum ellāp poruḷum kavarvu inṟit tannuḷ odunga ninṟa pavar koḷ jñāna veḷḷac cudar mūrtti avar em āḻi ampaḷḷiyārē*

- *yavarum yāvaiyum ellāp poruḷum* – During praḷayam, consuming all such entities such as cētanas (sentient) and acētanas (insentient) and keeping them in his stomach
- *kavarvinṟi* – without crushing/troubling them (in his stomach)
- *tannuḷ odunga ninṟa* – As explained by mārkaṇḍēya riśi to yudiśtra in mahābhāratam āraṇya parvam “*tadapaśyam aham sarvam tasya kukśau mahātmana:*” (I have seen inside viṣṇu’s stomach all movable/immovable objects which are seen here now). It can also be explained as within a small portion of his divine will.
- *pavarkoḷ jñānaveḷḷac cudar mūrti* – Having the vast abundant knowledge that is required to protect them, and having a divine form that manifests his emotions “I am so happy to protect them”.
- *em āḻi am paḷḷiyārē* – Since he is in this samsāram (material realm), he speaks on behalf of all the residents here and says “to protect us, you have descended here and having this kśīrārṇavam as a beautiful bed”. It is explained in tamiḻ nigaṇḍu (grammar book) “*pāyalum paḷḷiyum pāḻiyum padukkai*” (Bed is indicated by the following words pāyal, paḷḷi, pāḻi). Thus, he is the īśvara (lord and master) because he is the one who helps during difficulties and he is most beautiful.

## 2.2.7. Palli alilai

*paḷḷi ālilai ēḻ ulagum koḷḷum vaḷḷal val vayiṟṟup perumān uḷ uḷ ār aṟivār avan tan kaḷḷa māy manak karuttē*

**Пословный перевод:**

paḷḷi – bed; Al ilai – as banyan leaf; ēḻ ulagum – all worlds; koḷḷum – provide space to accommodate them; vaḷḷal – having generosity; val – and śakti (power); vayiṟu – having stomach; perumān – greater than all; kaḷḷam – without anyone knowing; māyam – spectacular; manak karuttu – contemplation (for protecting the worlds); uḷḷuḷ – contemplation; aṟivār – those who know; Ar – who?

**Перевод:**

**Having the banyan leaf as his bed, emperumān who is greater than all, having a stomach which is both generous and capable of holding all worlds, is contemplating spectacularly without any one knowing about it. Who can comprehend this act of his? It can be said that it is difficult for anyone to know about it.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the seventh pāsuram – āḻvār explains emperumān’s vatadaḷaśayana (lying down on banyan leaf during praḷayam) which is impossible (for anyone else) and says that due to this reason too, he is supreme.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. பள்ளி ஆல் இலை ஏழ் உலகும் கொள்ளும் வள்ளல் வல் வயிற்றுப் பெருமான் உள் உள் ஆர் அறிவார் அவன் தன் கள்ள மாய மனக் கருத்தே? paḷḷi ālilai ēḻ ulagum koḷḷum vaḷḷal val vayiṟṟup perumān uḷ uḷ Ar aṟivār avan than kaḷḷa māy manak karuttē*

- *paḷḷi Al ilai* – banyan leaf being the resting place
- *ēḻ ulagum koḷḷum* – resting in this bed having the seven worlds in his stomach
- *vaḷḷal* – having space to accommodate more such worlds
- *val vayiṟṟup perumān* – having power/pride so that the entities which entered the stomach have no fear inside
- perumān – the natural protector – the owner.
- *uḷḷuḷ … karuttē* – I have told whatever I have seen, but there is much more which cannot be known by anyone in his mind. Who will know that?
