## 2.2.8. Karuttil tevum

*karuttil tēvum ellap poruḷum varuttitta māyap pirānai anṟi ārē tiruttit tiṇ ṇilai mūvulagum tammuḷ iruttik kākkum iyalvinarē*

**Пословный перевод:**

karuttil – with his will/thoughts; tēvum – dēvas (celestial beings); ellāp poruḷum – all beings such as manuśya (humans) etc; varuttitta – created (to have their sustenance); māyam – one who is having spectacular abilities etc; pirānai – īśvara; anṟi – else; ārē – who is; mūvulagum – all worlds; tiṇ – strong; nilai – to have such state; tirutti – reform (through eliminating undesirable aspects); tam uḷ – in his thoughts; irutti – firmly placing (them); kākkum – protecting; iyalvinar – (who is) having such nature?

**Перевод:**

**Other than the spectacularly capable supreme emperumān who created dēvas and all other beings through his sankalpam, who else is having such nature to reform all worlds to such strong state and protect them by firmly placing them in his thoughts? emperumān’s protective nature is emphasised.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the eighth pāsuram – āḻvār says “since emperumān performs creation, protection etc., through his mere will, he is the īśvara (supreme controller)”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “emperumān is the only protector in all manners”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Eighth pāsuram – āḻvār says “Since emperumān has creation and protection under his full control, he is the īśvara (supreme controller)“. கருத்தில் தேவும் எல்லாப் பொருளும் வருத்தித்த மாயப் பிரான் அன்றி யாரே திருத்தித் திண் நிலை மூவுலகும் தம்முள் இருத்திக் காக்கும் இயல்வினரே? karuttil tēvum ellap poruḷum varuttitta māyap pirānai anṟi ārē tiruttit tiṇ ṇilai mūvulagum tammuḷ iruttik kākkum iyalvinarē*

- *karuttil … kākkum* – The spectacularly capable [sarvēśvaran](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) out of his own will, creates all dēvas and other beings; who else other than he, reforms the three worlds (sample for all worlds) to have a strong stable state, keeps them in himself (his mind) and aptly protects them? He protects as stated in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 1.22.19 “*nahi pālana sāmartyam rutē sarvēśvaram harim \| …*” (No one other than [hari (viṣṇu)](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) has the ability to protect – this is well known fact).
- *iyalvinarē* – Who has this as true nature?

## 2.2.9. Kakkum iyalvinan

*kākkum iyalvinan kaṇṇa perumān sērkkai seydu tan undiyuḷḷē vāytta tisai mugan indiran vāanavar ākkinān teyva ulagugaḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kākkum iyalvinan – has “protecting (others)” as a natural quality; kaṇṇan – who is kriṣṇa; perumān – sarvēśvaran (supreme lord); sērkkai seydu – (during annihilation, the unmanifest matter as said in “tama ēkībhavati“) to merge; than undi uḷḷē – inside his divine navel; vāytta – fit (for creation); tisai mugan – catur muka (four headed) brahmā; indiran – indra; vānavar – dēvas; teyva ulagaugaḷ – their celestial worlds; ākkinān – created them

**Перевод:**

**sarvēśvaran kriṣṇa who has “protecting others” as a natural quality, lets the matter which is in unmanifest state without names/forms during annihilation to submerge in him; he subsequently creates brahmā, indra, other dēvatās, the celestial worlds which are their habitats, inside his divine navel.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the ninth pāsuram – āḻvār says “Since emperumān has creation, sustenance and annihilation under his full control, he is supreme”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “In addition to sustenance, creation and annihilation are also under his control”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

- *sērkkai seydu* – “*tama ēkī bhavati*” (everything becomes unmanifest matter) is quoted.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. காக்கும் இயல்வினன் கண்ண பெருமான் சேர்க்கை செய்து தன் உந்தியுள்ளே வாய்த்த திசை முகன் இந்திரன் வானவர் ஆக்கினான் தெய்வ உலகுகளே kākkum iyalvinan kaṇṇa perumān sērkkai seydu than undiyuḷḷē vāytta tisai mugan indiran vāanavar ākkinān teyva ulagugaḷē*

- *kākkum iyalvinan* – As said in “*na sampadām samāhārē*”  (no one other than [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) has the talent to save/protect wealth), emperumān is the one who has the action of protecting others as a natural aspect.
- *kaṇṇa perumān* – it is for this specific purpose of protecting (his devotees and earth), supreme lord  descended as [kriṣṇa](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)
- *sērkkai seydu* – During annihilation, he submerges the visible material realm which is an effect (from the cause – [primordial matter)](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/09/thathva-thrayam-achith-what-is-matter/) into his body.
- *than … ulagugaḷē* – In the lotus flower in his divine navel, he creates brahmā and explains him the process of creation; brahmā who is most intelligent (and blessed) then creates indra, the other dēvatās, their residences etc., in proper order/structure.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.2.10. Kalva! emmaiyum

*kaḷvā! emmaiyum ēḻulagum nin uḷḷē tōṟṟiya iṟaiva! enṟu veḷ ēṟan nānmugan indiran vānavar puḷḷūrdi kaḻal paṇindu ēttuvarē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kaḷvā – Oh cheat (who hides your supremacy/dominance in the guise of an incarnation); emmaiyum – me and; ēḻulagum – all worlds; nin uḷḷē – in your thoughts/will; tōṟṟiya – created; iṟaiva – my lord!; enṟu – saying so; veḷ – pristine white; ēṟan – rudra who is having (such white) bull; nānmugan – caturmukha (four-headed) brahmā; indiran – indra; vānavar – the residents of heaven; puḷ ūrdi – one who rides garuda, his; kaḻal – divine feet; paṇindu – offering obeisances; ēttuvar – and offer prayers

**Перевод:**

**rudra who rides white bull, four-headed brahmā, indra and the residents of heaven would offer obeisances to the divine feet of emperumān, the rider of gaurda and offer him prayers saying “Oh mischievous lord (who hide your dominance in the name of being in an incarnation) who created us and all worlds through your will!”**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the tenth pāsuram – āḻvār says “The proof for what was said previously, that is, ‘only emperumān is supreme, others are not’,  is their own words”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvar says “Since  emperumān is greater than all, he is the vorśippable person for all dēvatās”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. கள்வா எம்மையும் ஏழ் உலகும் நின் உள்ளே தோற்றிய இறைவ என்று வெள் ஏறன் நான்முகன் இந்திரன் வானவர் புள் ஊர்தி கழல் பணிந்து ஏத்துவரே kaḷvā! emmaiyum ēḻulagum nin uḷḷē tōṟṟiya iṟaiva! enṟu veḷ ēṟan nānmugan indiran vānavar puḷḷūrdi kaḻal paṇindu ēttuvarē*

- *kaḷvā* – Once when rudra was asking for a boon from [sarvēśvaran](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) [śrīman nārāyaṇan](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), he asked “Your highness! You need to give me another special boon, that is, you have to come and request me to grant you a boon which will be remembered by everyone” \[In arumpadam, it is explained that, rudra was performing a great yajña, and he was about to cut his head and place it as an offering. At that time [viṣṇu](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) appears and gives him many boons and rudra finally asks one more boon in the end\]; [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) agrees to that and during his kriṣṇāvatāram, he goes to kailāsa, glorifies rudra as \[he\] said in śrīharivamśam “*namō gaṇṭāya karṇāya*“, asks him to bless his wife rukmiṇi to give birth to nice offsprings; rudra arrives there and says “kaḷvā (Oh misceivous lord)! When you come and do this during your incarnations which hide your supremacy, do you think that people will believe this?” Hiding his svātantriyam (independence) and standing as a paratantran (dependent seeking a boon) is called mischief here. When a brāhmaṇa heard [kriṣṇa](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s prayers to rudra, he said “since [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is not used to glorifying others, he does not even praise rudra properly and his lips are stuttering like fish’s mouth due to his inexperience”. Unlike others, his tongue is not used to praising others as stated in periya tirumoḻi 1.7.8 “*nāttaḻumba nānmuganum īśanumāy muṟaiyāl ētta*” (With great emotions, brahmā and rudra praised \[emperumān\] properly).

The mischief here is  – His taking a dependent position and praising others – this is explained further.

- *emmaiyum … tōṟṟiya* – During creation, did you not create these dēvatās and then only created animals etc?
- *iṟaiva* – they will call him “Oh lord!”.

Who are those persons who call him “lord”?

- *veḷḷēṟan nānmugan indiran vānavar* – Just like a king’s servants will come with their unique identities (uniform, stick etc) to serve the king, these dēvatās too, come with their unique identities (riding the bull, having four heads etc). This is also explained in [tiruppaḷḷiyeḻucci 6 “](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/01/thiruppalliyezhuchchi-6-iraviyar/)[*iraviyar maṇinedum tērodum*](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/01/thiruppalliyezhuchchi-6-iraviyar/)[“](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/01/thiruppalliyezhuchchi-6-iraviyar/).
- *puḷ ūrdi kaḻal paṇindu ēttuvarē* – Since these people cannot enter the quarters of [sarvēśvaran](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) where he enjoys with [periya pirāttiyār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/), to bestow his presence when these dēvatās call out from this side of milk ocean, he will appear in his playground where he takes a stroll on his garuda’s shoulders.  dēvatās will wait for  him to appear and then praise his glories there.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.2.11. Etta elulagum

*ētta ēḻ ulagum koṇḍa kōlak kūttanaik kurukūrc catakōpan sol vāytta āyirattuḷ ivai pattudan ētta vallavarkku illai ōr ūnamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ētta – having the glorification by the residents of the world as water that helps him grow; ēḻulagum – all worlds; koṇḍa – measured and accepted; kōlam – bodily beauty; kūttanai – measuring as a talented dancer will dance effortlessly; kurukūrc catakōpan – nammāḻvār; sol – mercifully spoken; vāytta – rare/unexpected gain (for the universe); ivai pattu – these 10 pāsurams; udan – accepting (the meanings); ētta – speaking in the form of praise; vallavarkku – those who are capable; ōr ūnam – defects (considering other dēvatās as great, considering them as equal to emperumān or considering emperumān to be lower than they); illai – not present

**Перевод:**

**These 10 pāsurams are mercifully blessed by āḻvār as most rare/unexpected gain (for the universe) in glorification of the most beautiful emperumān who measured all worlds effortlessly like a talented dancer dances. For those who are well versed in this decad (accepting the principles) there is no defect of considering other dēvatās as great, considering them as equal to emperumān or considering emperumān to be lower than they.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the end, āḻvār says that those who learn this pāsuram with meanings clearly, will not have the misunderstandings such as “emperumān is not supreme”, “other dēvatās are supreme” etc.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār mercifully explains elimination of all doubts as the result of (learning) this decad.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*In the end, āḻvārsays that for those who know/recite this decad, they do not have the defect of considering other dēvatās as supreme. ஏத்த ஏழ் உலகும் கொண்ட கோலக் கூத்தனைக் குருகூர்ச் சடகோபன் சொல் வாய்த்த ஆயிரத்துள் இவை பத்துடன் ஏத்த வல்லவர்க்கு இல்லை ஓர் ஊனமே ētta ēḻ ulagum koṇḍa kōlak kūttanaik kurukūrc catakōpan sol vāytta āyirattuḷ ivai pattudan ētta vallavarkku illai ōr ūnamē*

- *ētta ēḻulagum koṇḍa* – Glorified as in viṣṇu darmam “*sangaissurāṇām …*” (groups of dēvas from the heavenly planets, groups of humans from earth, dwellers from celstial vehicles in the sky glorified trivikrama. Let such trivikrama who measured the world be there for my auspiciousness), [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) placed all the worlds under his feet out of happiness of being glorified like that.
- *kōlak kūttanai* – When he measured the world, it looked so gracious like a well-talented dancer’s dance. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) does not desire for getting his kingdom back like indra – instead, he is simply enjoying the beauty of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/).
- *kurukūrc catakōpan sol* – for trustworthiness, it is said “spoken by so and so”.
- *satakōpan* – In comparison to vēdāntam (which is apauruśēyam – not created by anyone), the greatness of tiruvāimoḻi in coming out of [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s mouth.
- *vāytta āyiram* – Just like the greatness of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), this prabandam is also great; also explained as, tiruvāimoḻi is greater than [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/). That is, this tiruvāimoḻi explains [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) as he is – hence the greatness.
- *ivai pattudan ētta vallavarkku* – For those who can sing this decad, accepting its meanings fully.
- *illai ōr ūnamē* – Defect for the [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) is considering other dēvatās as supreme and not considering the [supreme lord](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) to be supreme. Such defects are not present for those who learn this decad.

[nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/), gives a brief summary of the whole decad at the end.

In the first pāsuram, the principle explained in this decad is briefly highlighted. From the second pāsuram, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s many qualities such as he being the remover of sorrows, being the one with auspicious qualities, being most tender, being lotus eyed, being the helper in danger, having great abilities to accomplish the unimaginable tasks, being the creator and sustainer, being the annihilator, being the object of praising of those who consider themselves to be supreme – thus establishing his supremacy through various examples and finally declares the result of those who learn this decad and completes the decad.

[āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) tiruvadigaḷē śaraṇam  
[emperumānār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/emperumanar/) tiruvadigaḷē śaraṇam  
[piḷḷān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/pillan/) tiruvadigaḷē śaraṇam  
[nanjīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nanjiyar/) tiruvadigaḷē śaraṇam  
[nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/) tiruvadigaḷē śaraṇam  
[vadakkut tiruvīdip piḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadakku-thiruvidhi-pillai/) tiruvadigaḷē śaraṇam  
[periyavāccān piḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/periyavachchan-pillai/) tiruvadigaḷē śaraṇam

## 2.3 Unil val

## 2.3.1. Unil val

*ūnil vāḻ uyirē! nallai pō unnaip peṟṟu vān uḷār perumān madusūdan en ammān tānum yānum ellām tanuḷḷē kalandoḻindōm tēnum palum neyyum kannalum amudum ottē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ūnil – body which is made of flesh; vāḻ – living (gloriously with bhagavat anubhvam in this body which is rare like a lotus blooming on a stove); uyirē – Oh mind/heart!; nallai pō – this is good!; unnai – you; peṟṟu – getting (as subservient to me); vānuḷār – more than the nityasūris who are residents of paramapadam; perumān – having greater glory; madusūdan – one who finished my hurdles (since I have the desire to enjoy him) like he finished the demon madu; en ammān tānum – he who has the quality of being my master, accepting my services; yānum – I (who desired to enjoy him and surrendered to him for that); than uḷḷē – within himself; ellām – being all sweet; tēnum – like honey and honey; pālum – like milk and milk; neyyum – like ghee and ghee; kannalum – like sugar and sugar; amudum ottu – like nectar and nectar; kalandu oḻindōm – we have mixed

**Перевод:**

**Oh mind/heart which lives in this body! This is good! Due to having you (as subservient to me),  emperumān who is greater than nityasūris, finished my hurdles in enjoying him like he finished the demon madu. Such emperumān who is my master and I, who am desirous of serving him, mixed like honey and honey, milk and milk, ghee and ghee, sugar and sugar and nectar and nectar.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the first pāsuram – āḻvār praises his heart saying “emperumān and I united and as a result we enjoyed continuous bliss; this abundance of bliss is because of you”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*In the first pāsuram – When a prince lost his kingdom and someone helps him regain it, the prince will praise that person who helped saying “I got this because of you”; Similarly, āḻvār praises his divine heart thinking “ātmā (Self) who is rightfully qualified for kainkarya sāmrājyam (the kingdom of servitude) had lost it for so long, it was this heart which got it now”. ஊனில் வாழ் உயிரே நல்லை போ உன்னைப் பெற்று வான் உளார் பெருமான் மதுசூதன் என் அம்மான் தானும் யானும் எல்லாம் தன்னுள்ளே கலந்தொழிந்தோம் தேனும் பாலும் நெய்யும் கன்னலும் அமுதும் ஒத்தே ūnil vāḻ uyirē! nallai pō unnaip peṟṟu vān uḷār perumān madusūdan en ammān tānum yānum ellām tanuḷḷē kalandoḻindōm tēnum palum neyyum kannalum amudum ottē*

- *ūnil vāḻ uyirē* – Un – śarīram (body); vāḻ – living/residing; uyir (ātmā) that resides in body; Also explained as, living in the body without knowing anything else. vāḻ – explained as living gloriously now; living gloriously in this body itself which is made of flesh. You have favoured me to reach paramapadam and enjoy variegated experiences. In this body which is made of flesh, blood, bones, stool, urine etc., you have helped me achieve great bliss. From this, vāḻ is explained as living gloriously – since time immemorial you enjoyed material/worldly pleasures, you have now favoured me to acquire divine bliss. manas (mind) is indicated with the term “*uyir*” (vital air – life) since even though ātmā’s darmabhūta jñānam (knowledge) is eternal, the importance of mind is explained in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 6.7.28 “*mana Eva manuśyāṇām kāraṇam banda mōkśayō*” (mind is the main cause for bondage to and liberation from \[samsāram\] for people). He is calling out for his own mind as “*uyirē!*“.
- *nallaipō* – pō generally indicates go. Here [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is addressing his mind, saying “come, good mind!” (pō (go) is to be treated as vā (come) – viparīta lakśaṇai – Opposite meaning). bō! is also *sambōdana* (addressing). nallaipō can also be treated as a single world indicating “nallai nallai” (good good).

Why are you praising me in between (while enjoying divine union with [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/))?

- *unnaip perṟṟu* – You, who are generally the cause for bondage, are now the cause for liberation. [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is eternal (always existing); relationship with him is also anādi (without a beginning). Even though he tried to help you in many ways, you did not turn towards him until now and lost the great opportunity to serve him. Since you have turned towards him today, you have got this great result.

[āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) explaining further, the great result he got.

- *vānuḷār perumān madusūdan ennammān tānum yānum* – multiple explanations:
   - Though being the leader of nityasūris, just like he incarnated and finished the demon named madu, he finished the hurdles which were stopping my divine union with him, overwhelmed me and engaged me in his service; *tānum* – I who am the performer of kainkaryam.
   - I who suffered in seeing all visible entities to be suffering in pain of separation in “[vāyum tiruayugaḷ (tiruvāimoḻi 2.1)](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/11/thiruvaimozhi-2-1-vayum/)” and [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who removed my suffering through his many efforts.
   - [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who put in efforts (to get me); me who became the target of his efforts.
- *ellām than uḷḷē kalandu oḻindōm* – Just like one \[the numeral\] is contained in thousand and a puddle of water is contained in sea, we had divine union in which all different tastes/flavours manifested.
- *oḻindōm* – to the maximum – eternal experience. Even when I enter nitya vibhūti (paramapadam – spiritual realm), I will be ruminating this experience. There is nothing separate (for [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)) in paramapadam; it is the continuation of his blissful experience from here (here it happens with break, there it happens without any break). So, even after having such divine union, the reasons for [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) to seek out to reach paramapadam are – to have proper companionship (with like-minded persons) and to have this experience without any break.

How did they mix?

- *tēnum pālum kannalum …* – For this, [tirumālai āṇḍān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/thirumalai-andan) explains it saying he heard it this way from [āḷavandār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/alavandhar/) – Like two objects of the same species mixed (seamlessly); that is, honey and honey mixing, milk and milk mixing, ghee and ghee mixing, sugar and sugar mixing, necatar and nectar mixing”. But [emperumānār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/emperumanar/) gives a different explanation – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) takes these sweet objects as samples for all different flavours and says “we enjoyed all such flavours in our union”. As explained in cāndōjña upaniśat “*sarvagndas sarvarasa:*”  ([bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is the source of all fragrances and flavours), [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) mixed with such (tasteful) [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/). When two entities ([paramātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) and [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)) who have jñānam (knowledge), ānandam (bliss) unite, they unite in such a way that all flavours are manifested. Even in [āḷavandār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/alavandhar/)‘s explanation, when two objects of the same species mix, the quantity increases – so , here āḻvār is not talking about merging (eliminating of individual identity of [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)/[paramātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) as explained in advaita philosophy) – he is only highlighting the seamless union.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

adiyen saraty ramanuja dasan

## 2.3.2. Ottar mikkarai

*ottār mikkārai ilaiyāya mā māya! ottāy ep poruktum uyir āy ennaip peṟṟa at tāy āy tandai āy aṟiyadana aṟivittu attā! nī seydana adiyēn aṟiyēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ottār mikkārai ilaiyāya – not having anyone equal or greater (for such tasteful nature); māmāya – being very spectacular (even if enjoyed every moment, each moment being so new and reliśable); ottāy epporutkum – descending in all forms to give joy; uyirāy – being the bearer of everything (like the ātmā bearing the body); ennai – me; peṟṟa – created; a – having such distinct relationship; tāyāy – being mother who looks after the desires of the child; a – being the cause for such creation; tandaiyāy – being father who looks after the well-being of the child; aṟiyādana – those experiences which one is ignorant about; aṟivittu – taught; attā! – Oh one who has the natural relationship (to do such favours)!; nī – you (who have natural relationship unlike the mother/father of this world who have a relationship due to specific reason of being born to them due to karma); seydana – favours done; adiyēn – being a servitor; aṟiyēn – would not know fully

**Перевод:**

**Oh one who has natural relationship with me! You have none equal or greater than you (in your tasteful nature) and are most spectacular every moment; you descend in all forms to give joy to us and you are the bearer of all entities; you are the mother who cares for my desires and the father who cares for my well-being; you are the ācārya (teacher) who taught what I don’t know; Even though I am your servitor, I don’t fully know the limitless favours done by you.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*After praising his heart, āḻvār relishes emperumān’s merciful favours towards him by informing emperumān about that.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the second pāsuram – āḻvār says to emperumān “I cannot count the number of favours you, who are without any expectations, have done to me with much expectations towards me, reforming my heart to be favourable towards you and so on”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s v**hlights from** [**periyavāccān piḷḷai**](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/periyavachchan-pillai/)**‘s vyākhyānam**

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says that such tasteful emperumān has done countless favours towards him.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Second pāsuram. When this pāsuram was discussed once in the assembly of embār, a question was asked “Who is the pratamaguru (first guru) for the ātmā?” Some śrīvaiṣṇavas said “it must be the ācārya”; others said “that would be the śrīvaiṣṇava who led the ātmā to the ācārya”; at that time embār said “No! It is bhagavān only; even when a śrīvaiṣṇava invites an ātmā to approach an ācārya, it is sarvēśvaran who ensures that the ātmā accepts the proposal without rejecting it. In previous pāsuram, āḻvār praised his heart saying that it was his heart which united him with emperumān. At that time the heart asks “Why are you praising a passer-by without knowing the root cause?” āḻvār then says “if I contemplate deeper, I understand that emperumān is the cause for my heart leading me to emperumān and without realising that I simply praised my heart” and starts praising sarvēśvaran. ஒத்தார் மிக்காரை இலையாய மா மாய ஒத்தாய் எப் பொருட்கும் உயிர் ஆய் என்னைப் பெற்ற அத் தாய் ஆய் தந்தை ஆய் அறியாதன அறிவித்து அத்தா! நீ செய்தன அடியேன் அறியேனே ottār mikkārai ilaiyāya mā māya! ottāy ep poruktum uyir āy ennaip peṟṟa at tāy āy tandai āy aṟiyadana aṟivittu attā! nī seydana adiyēn aṟiyēnē*

- *ottār mikkārai ilaiyāya māmāya!* – Did you accept me because you are lacking in something? Even for the master of śrī mahālakśmi, there is one dāridryam (poorness/poverty) – as explained in śvētāśvatara upaniśat “*na tatsamaścyābhyadikaśca druśyatē*” (for that [paramātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/), no one equal or greater is seen) – he too is lacking in having someone equal or greater.
- *māmāya* – this is so spectacular!
- *ottāy epporutkum* – You are so great, but what did you go through? One who has no one equal or greater, takes birth in different forms.
- *epporutkum ottāy* – you descended as viṣṇu amidst brahmā and rudra; you became the brother of indra (as vāmana); you descended as humans in rāma, kriṣṇa avatārams; you were born in animal species as mahāvarāha (great boar); you descended in plant species as kubjāmaram (dwarf mango tree). Even while taking a plant form, he assumes to be a dwarf tree so that even women and ignorant can climb (reach out easily). Why is he assuming these forms? If he takes birth maintaining his supremacy, they will leave him out of fear; if he makes himself too lowly, they will ignore him; so he assumes many different species to attract them. [kūrattāḻvān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/kuraththazhwan/)‘s atimānuśa stavam 15th ślōkam is quoted here which reflects this meaning.

What did he do by assuming such incarnations?

- *uyirāy* – emperumān will care for the [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) as the [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) himself cares; it is also explained as emperumān being the dāraka (bearer).
- *ennaip peṟṟa attāyāy* – instead of just being foster mother, being real mother who longs for a child, gives birth from her own body and cares for all his desires.
- *tandaiyāy* – the mother is just the one who carries the child; but the father is the seed-giver and one who cares for his well-being.

not only that;

- *aṟiyādana aṟivittu* – As explained in āpastamba dharma sūtram, “*śarīramēva mātāpitarau janayata:*” (the mother and father only give birth to the body), not just being mother/father, but also being the ācārya who nurtures knowledge; “*sa hi vidyāstam janayati tatśrēśtam janma*” (that ācārya triggers the (second) birth of the śiśya through knowledge). He has vowed to help [jīvātmās](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) as in śrī rāmāyṇam “*ētat vrattam mama*” (this is my vow) and [bhagavat gītā](http://githa.koyil.org/) “*māmēkam śaraṇam vraja*” (surrender unto me only).
- *attā* – Oh the one who has done great favours! Since he is the owner, he is bound to help us in these ways. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says as said in subāla upaniśat “*mātā pitā bhrātā nivāsaśśaraṇam suhrudgatirnārāyaṇa:*” ([śrīman nārāyaṇan](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is mother, father, brother, abode, refuge, friend, goal). He himself said in periya tiruvantādi 5 “*peṟṟa tāy nīyē piṟappitta tantai nī maṟṟaiyārāvārum nī*” (you are my mother, father and every relationship).
- *nī seydana* – if it is one or two favours, we can list them out; since there are too many, he just says “favours done by you”. Those favours done by svāmi (master) to me who is śēśabhūta (servitor).
- *adiyēn aṟiyēnē* – you who bestowed such favours may know what was done by you; I can only experience the bliss and be submerged into it instead of counting those favours.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.3.3. Ariyak kalattulle

*aṟiyāk kālattuḷḷē adimaikkaṇ anbu seyvittu aṟiyā mā māyattu adiyēnai vaittāyāl aṟiyāmaik kuraḷāy nilam māvali! mūvadi enṟu aṟiyāmai vanjittāy enadu āviuḷ kalandē*

**Пословный перевод:**

aṟiyāmai – one who mesmerised (through his physical beauty so that others cannot know his true nature); kuṟaḷāy – one who became vāmana (dwarf); nilam māvali mūvadi enṟu – saying “land mahābali three feet” (even without proper sentence formation); aṟiyāmai – not understanding (the instructions given by śukrācārya who said “this is supreme lord himself”); vanjittāy – Oh one who cheated (and grabbed the world which he considered as his own)!; enadu āvi uḷ kalandu – entering into my heart (by revealing this incident); aṟiyā – that which will nurture ignorance; mā – having insurmountable glories; māyattu – samsāra which is the result of māyā (ignorance); adiyēnai – me (just considering our relationship as master-servant); aṟiyāk kālattu uḷḷē – when there was no scope to know about such relationship; adimaik kaṇ – in such servitude; anbu – attachment; seyvittu vaittāyāl – created that

**Перевод:**

**Oh one who mesmerised (through your physical beauty so others cannot know your true nature) by becoming vāmana (dwarf) saying “land mahābali three feet” (even without proper sentence formation) and making mahābali not understand the instructions of śukrācārya and thus cheated (and grabbed the world which mahābali considered as his own! Entering into my heart (by revealing this incident) when I was in this insurmountably glorious samsāram which is the result of māyā which will nurture ignorance and when there was no scope to know about such relationship in me, (just considering our relationship as master-servant) you created that attachment towards such servitude.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the third pāsuram – emperumān asks “What favour did I do to you?” and āḻvār says “though I have no qualification, you prepared me to unite with you”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār mercifully explains how emperumān nurtured āḻvār‘s devotion towards him.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Third pāsuram – tirumālai āṇḍān explains as heard from āḷavandār “āḻvār says with sorrow ‘emperumān bestowed me sambanda jñānam (knowledge about emperumān–āḻvār relationship) and then he placed me in a body which hides that knowledge'”. emperumānār mercifully heard this and said “previous pāsuram and next pāsuram are spoken by āḻvār with joy and hence this pāsuram cannot be spoken in sorrow. So āḻvār is speaking ‘When I was in ignorance – emperumān gave me knowledge and engaged me in his service’ in this pāsuram as a favour done by emperumān”. When emperumān says to āḻvār “You said, attā nī seydana (the many favours you have done); tell me one such favour which you value most” and āḻvār starts speaking about that. அறியாக் காலத்துள்ளே அடிமைக்கண் அன்பு செய்வித்து அறியா மா மாயத்து அடியேனை வைத்தாயால் அறியாமைக் குறள் ஆய் நிலம் மாவலி! மூவடி என்று அறியாமை வஞ்சித்தாய் எனது ஆவியுள் கலந்தே aṟiyāk kālattuḷḷē adimaikkaṇ anbu seyvittu aṟiyā mā māyattu adiyēnai vaittāyāl aṟiyāmaik kuraḷāy nilam māvali! mūvadi enṟu aṟiyāmai vanjittāy enadu āviuḷ kalandē*

- *aṟiyāk kālattu uḷḷē* – As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam bāla kāṇḍam 18.27 “*bālyāt prabhruti susnigda:*” (lakśmaṇa being very attached to śrī rāma from early child hood), in early days when knowledge is not developed.
- *adimaikkaṇ anbu seyvittu* – adimaikkaṇ – in servitude. As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 31.25 “*aham sarvam kariśyāmi*” (let me serve you in all manner) – you engaged me in the tasks which are done by nityasūris who are never touched by samsāram.
- *anbu seyvittu* – Instead of remaining with the attitude “will not leave it, if it comes to me and will not search for it, if I don’t get it”, you made me such that I cannot sustain without serving you as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 31.22 “*kuruśva…*” (bless me to accompany you).
- *arīyā …* –  Like someone who ate an intoxicating plant and became bewildered, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) became bewildered and asked “you have blessed me (who is so fallen)”. \[Explaining [āḷavandār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/alavandhar/)‘s view point – \] Even if something is captured in samsāram, it is still mine and so I will engage it in service. \[Explaining [emperumānār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/emperumanar/)‘s view point – \] You placed this water source \[when I am in ignorance, you blessed me with opportunity to do service, like providing water for a thirsty person\].

Here is an example for this (engaging me in service without my knowledge).

- *aṟiyāmai …* – Like someone who acts without the knowledge of his own heart (so mischievous), assuming the form of a vāmana even without the knowledge of śrī mahālakśmi who resides in his own heart, as said in tiruvāimoḻi 3.8.9 “*koḷvan nān māvali*” (mahābali, I will accept), he spoke incoherent sentence “*nilam māvali mūvadi*” (land mahābali three feet). Only if he had begged before, could he have spoken coherently and asked for something.
- *aṟiyāmai vanjittāy* – He cheated mahābali with his sweet words even when śukrācārya et al tried to convince him that “He is sarvēśvaran, arrived to fulfil the desires of dēvas, arrived to grab all your properties”. Similarly, he entered my heart, captured it too and united with me. He arrived into me who was totally shying away from him and captured me by manifesting his auspicious qualities and activities. Just like he cheated mahābali as a mischievous dwarf, he entered into me, who was ignorant and from early days engaged me in his devotion.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.3.4. Enadu aviyul

*enadu āvi uḷ kalanda peru nal udavik kaimmāṟu enadu āvi tandoḻindēn ini mīḷvadu enbadu uṇḍē? enadu āvi āviyum nī poḻil ēḻum uṇḍa endāy enadu āvi ār? yān ār? tanda nī koṇḍākkinaiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

poḻil ēḻum – all worlds; uṇḍa – (while being destroyed during praḷayam (annihilation)) placed in your stomach and protected them; endāy – Oh lord/master!; enadāvi uḷ – inside my ātmā (which is to be rejected due its fallen nature); kalanda – mixed seamlessly (like water mixing with water); peru – (considering that as his benefit) huge; nal – good (since its nirhētukam – without any effort from āḻvār); udavi – for the favour; kaimmāṟu – as return of favour; enadāvi – my ātmā; tandu oḻindēn – submitted (to you); ini – now; mīḷvadu – (for that) return; uṇḍē – is not there; enadu āviyum – for my ātmā (soul); āvi – ātmā; nī – you; enadu āvi Ar? – the actions of ātmā (which is submitted) are not under my control; yān Ar – the doerśip of mine (who is submitting) is not under my control; tanda – one who created (the existence of this ātmā which has the ability to give, act etc); nī – you only; koṇḍākkināy – subsequently accepted

**Перевод:**

**Oh lord who placed all worlds (while being destroyed during praḷayam (annihilation)) in your stomach and protected them! You mixed seamlessly inside my ātmā (which is to be rejected due to its fallen nature) and did huge good favour; as a return for such favour, I submitted my self unto you which cannot be revoked; on analysing deeper, you are my soul (ātmā‘s ātmā), neither the actions of the ātmā (that is submitted) and nor the doerśip of the ātmā that is submitting is under my control; (really) you (who) created (the existence of this ātmā which has the ability to give, act etc) have subsequently accepted this ātmā.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fourth pāsuram – āḻvār being unable to return emperumān‘s favour, becomes perplexed.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says he cannot return emperumān‘s favours.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Fourth pāsuram – āḻvār recollects emperumān‘s favour which he mentioned in “vaittāyāl” and becomes perplexed. When asked “Can you not submit something you own and be satisfied?” he agrees and submits his own self but then repents for doing so. எனது ஆவி யுள் கலந்த பெரு நல் உதவிக் கைம்மாறு எனது ஆவி தந்தொழிந்தேன் இனி மீள்வது என்பது உண்டே? எனது ஆவி ஆவியும் நீ பொழில் ஏழும் உண்ட எந்தாய் எனது ஆவி யார்? யான் ஆர்? தந்த நீ கொண்டாக்கினையே enadu āvi uḷ kalanda peru nal udavik kaimmāṟu enadu āvi tandoḻindēn ini mīḷvadu enbadu uṇḍē? enadu āvi āviyum nī poḻil ēḻum uṇḍa endāy enadu āvi Ar? yān Ar? tanda nī koṇḍākkinaiyē*

- *enadu āvi uḷ kalanda* – You have entered into me (ātmā) who has toiled in this samsāram since time immemorial.
- *enadu āvi* – (like saying “my ātmā” with much shame) showing an example – Like vaśiśta (great sage) entering caṇḍāḷa’s (outcast) place. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) always considers himself as highlighted in tiruvāimoḻi 3.3.4 “*nīcanēn*” (I am the most fallen).
- *uḷ kalanda* – Not just bestowing enjoyment and liberation for my ātmā; as highlighted in first pāsuram “*ellām tanuḷḷē kalandoḻindōm*“, uniting/bonding fully with me.
- *udavi*, *nal udavi*, *peru nal udavi* – udavi – favouring; nal udavi – favouring without any effort from āḻvār, peru nal udavi – favouring others as if it is a favour for oneself. *kaimmāṟu* – *pratyupakāram* – in return for such huge favour.
- *enadu āvi tandu oḻindēn* – I submitted my self under the lotus feet of your highness.

[bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) asks “For how many baths (days), this will last?”

- *ini mīḷvadu enbadu uṇḍē* – Given it as *sadyō daśāham* – those 10 days completed too; When selling goods, the seller would say you can return the product within 10 days from the date of purchase, but not after that. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) saying even those 10 days are gone now – so there is no option for revoking his submission.

[bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) says “Good! Now, you analyse and see whose you have submitted and to whom”. When [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) analyses it, he realises that he has submitted something to bhagavān, which is already owned by bhagavān.

- *enadu āviyum nī* – you are the in-dwelling super soul of my soul too. We have considered the ātmā as ours for long (since time immemorial), though it is already owned by [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/). Today, we submitted that to him. What would [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), who is omniscient, think about this act of ours? Once realising  [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s reaction, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) feels ashamed of his submission. If we don’t perform ātmasamarpaṇam (submitting oneself), that will lead to *sarva mukti prasangam* (everyone irrespective of surrendering or not, should have become liberated); but if we submit ourselves to him, that would mean that we offered something which is already owned by him; so, what is to done? When perplexed one should submit oneself; but when one acquires clarity, one cannot be satisfied that “I have offered myself”; [āḷavandār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/alavandhar/) too said in stōtra ratnam ślōkams 52 and 53 “… *mayā samarpita: , … atavā kinnu samarpayāmi tē*” (I have offered myself, (After knowing that everything is yours) what can I offer to you?) \[In arumpadam, there is detailed explanation for this section, since this is a very in-depth principle to understand\].
- *poḻil ēḻum uṇḍa endāy* – should we have to say this based on your natural lordship over everyone? Is it not sufficient to say you are the lord of everyone since you have protected everyone by placing everyone in your stomach during annihilation?
- *endāy* – Just like you protected the world during annihilation, you bonded with me and protected me from destruction due to separation from you
- *enadu āvi Ar? yān Ar?* – Who owns the entity that is being submitted? Who owns the submitter?  How can I say “I have submitted my [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) (when it is really not owned by me)”?
- *tanda nī koṇḍu ākkinaiyē* – you who first created the [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/), accepted it too. How can ātmā be created when it is eternal? It is because of his eternal desire that the ātmās are eternally existing as explained by [kūrattāḻvān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/kuraththazhwan/) in Śrīvaikuṇṭha stavam 36 “*iccāta Eva viśvapadārtasattā…*” (the creation of all entities is based on your vow/desire).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

adiyen saraty ramanuja dasan

## 2.3.5. Iniyar jnanangalal

*ini yār jñānangaḷāl edukkal eḻāda endāy! kanivār vīttu inbamē! en kadal padā amudē! taniyēn vāḻ mudalē! poḻil ēḻum ēnam onṟāy nuni ār kōttil vaittāy un pādam sērndēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

yār – even those who are great; jñānangaḷāl – with the knowledge; edukkal – to grasp; eḻāda – cannot grasp; endāy – my lord; kanivār – those with well matured heart (due to their attachment towards you); vīttu inbamē – one who is like the bliss in liberation; en – for me (who neither has knowledge nor has a matured heart); kadal – in the ocean; padā – not created from; amudē – being (divine) nectar; taniyēn – lonely me (due to not fitting in this material realm); vāḻ – (glorious) living (matching my nature); mudalē – (due to his triggering the attachment, etc) the primary cause; poḻil ēḻum – (to demonstrate lifting me up from the material world) the universe which is structured as seven islands; onṟu – distinct; ēnamāy – being mahāvarāha (great wild-boar); nuniyār – sharp; kōttil – in the tusk; vaittāy – Oh one who placed it!; ini – now (after your being my controller); un pādam – your divine feet; sērndēnē – reached (certainly)

**Перевод:**

**Oh lord who cannot be grasped even by great persons! Oh divine nectar which is not sourced from the ocean (like the worldly nectar which came out of churning milk ocean)! Oh the one who is primary cause for the glorious life of mine who is lonely here in this material world! Oh distinct great varāha who lifted up the seven-island universe and placed it in your sharp tusk (to demonstrate that you will lift me up from this samsāram as well)! Now (after your being my controller), I have certainly reached your divine feet.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fifth pāsuram – āḻvār becomes satisfied saying “Just like you lifted up the world from praḷayārṇavam (causal ocean), you have also lifted me up from the samsāra sāgaram (ocean of material realm) by mercifully showing my relationship with your lotus feet; so, I have now attained your lotus feet”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “Since you have shown your divine reliśable nature and have been the one who triggered my attachment towards you, have I not attained your lotus feet? (yes, I have)”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Fifth pāsuram – When asked “Is it sufficient to have knowledge? Should the result be not accomplished?” āḻvār says “you being my first well wisher, having transformed me to be different from samsāris (worldly people), I have attained the result then and there”. இனி யார் ஞானங்களால் எடுக்கல் எழாத எந்தாய்! கனிவார் வீட்டு இன்பமே! என் கடல் படா அமுதே! தனியேன் வாழ் முதலே! பொழில் ஏழும் ஏனம் ஒன்றாய் நுனி ஆர் கோட்டில் வைத்தாய் உன் பாதம் சேர்ந்தேனே ini yār jñānangaḷāl edukkal eḻāda endāy! kanivār vīttu inbamē! en kadal padā amudē! taniyēn vāḻ mudalē! poḻil ēḻum ēnam onṟāy nuni Ar kōttil vaittāy un pādam sērndēnē*

- *ini* – explained further…
- *Ar jñānangaḷāl edukkal eḻāda endāy* – Oh my lord who cannot be understood by the  self-effort of one who may be however greatly knowledgeable! That is, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) could not be comprehended by duryōdana and could not be lifted up by rāvaṇa.
- *kanivār vīttu inbamē* – For those who melt for you, you are their bliss of liberation; also explained as, for those who melt for you, you descend to their own place and give them bliss. Where did we see this? Mother yaśōdā enjoyed ultimate bliss at her own residence (given by kriṣṇa) as explained in perumāḷ tirumoḻi 7.8 “*tollai inbattu iṟudi kaṇḍāḷē*” (she enjoyed that ancient ultimate bliss).
- *en kadal padā amudē* – Oh most enjoyable lord who I got without my effort! I am not counted in either group – enemies (like rāvaṇa) or devotees (like yaśōdā) – since I only have advēśam (no hatred towards you when you try to help).
- *taniyēn vāḻ mudalē* – the primary cause (well-wisher) for such experience of lonely me. Like sītā pirātti who felt lonely amidst the rākśasis (demoniac servants of rāvaṇa), [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) feels lonely in this samsāram.
- *poḻil ēḻum ēnam onṟāy* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is explaining [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s help when he was feeling lonely. Assuming the most distinct form of a great varāha (wild-boar), he rescued the seven worlds which were consumed by the praḷayam (annihilation).
- *nuniyār kōttil vaittāy* – nuni – sharpness;  Ar – abundance; placing it in the abundantly sharp tusk.  This implies [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s desire for protecting everything which is a lot greater than that of those who need to be protected.
- *ini una pādam sērndēnē* – Just like lifting up the world from the praḷayam, when you rescued me from the ocean of samsāram, I have attained the divine feet of your highness. Right at the time when you gave knowledge to me to say in tiruviruttam 1st pāsuram “*imaiyōr talaivā – in ninṟa nīrmai ini yām uṟāmai*” (1st prabandam of [nammāḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)), I have attained your divine feet.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.3.6. Serndar tivinaigatku

*sērndār tīvinaigatku aru nanjait tiṇ madiyait tīrndār tam manattup piriyādu avar uyiraic cōrndē pōgal kodāc cudarai arakkiyai mūkku īrndāyai adiyēn adaindēn mudal munnamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

sērndār – those who have reached (you); tī – cruel; vinaigatku – sins; aru – unbearable; nanjai – being the poison; tiṇ madiyai – one who bestows strong mind which has complete faith; tīrndār tam – for those who have such faith; manattu – in their mind; piriyādu – without being separated; avar uyirai – their ātmā; sōrndē – moving/dying away (by engaging in worldly matters); pōgal kodā – without letting them; sudarai – the naturally radiant emperumān (who manifests his divine form to them); arakkiyai – sūrpaṇakā; mūkku īrndāyai – you who can destroy (their worldly attachments) like you cut off the nose (of sūrpaṇakā); adiyēn – me who is naturally a servant of you; mudal munnamē – since time immemorial; adaindēnē – have I not reached?

**Перевод:**

**You are being the unbearable poison to the cruel sins of those who have reached you; you are the bestover of a strong mind which has total faith in you; you stay without separating from those who have such total faith in you; you manifest your divine form to them and keep them from moving/dying away from you (by engaging in worldly matters); you are capable of destroying the vorldy attachments of such persons, like you cut off the nose of sūrpaṇakā; Have I (who am your natural servant) not reached you since time immemorial?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the sixth pāsuram – As emperumān unites with āḻvār and makes āḻvār totally forget about the separation from emperumān since time immemorial, āḻvār says “Did I get you just today, have I not been united with your highness since time immemorial?”*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, since being united with bhagavān is natural for the ātmā, āḻvār says that his being united with emperumān is always the case.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Sixth pāsuram – āḻvār said “ini una pādam sērndēnē” (now, I have reached your divine feet); Two explanations are given: Why should I specially say “ini” (now)? I have reached your feet, when you specially blessed me and made me sing “poy ninṟa jñānam” (tiruviruttam 1 – first pāsuram of his first prabandam). Thinking about his true nature, natural servitorśip towards emperumān is the permanent state. Since he feels his situation of being away from emperumān is accidental, he says this (that he has been united with emperumān since time immemorial). சேர்ந்தார் தீவினைகட்கு அரு நஞ்சை திண் மதியை தீர்ந்தார் தம் மனத்துப் பிரியாது அவர் உயிரைச் சோர்ந்தே புகல் கொடாச் சுடரை அரக்கியை மூக்கு ஈர்ந்தாயை அடியேன் அடைந்தேன் முதல் முன்னமே sērndār tīvinaigatku aru nanjait tiṇ madiyait tīrndār tam manattup piriyādu avar uyiraic cōrndē pōgal kodāc cudarai arakkiyai mūkku īrndāyai adiyēn adaindēn mudal munnamē*

- *sērndāruṇḍu* (those who are united with emperumān are present) – Those who don’t follow the principle as said by rāvaṇa in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 36.11 “*dvidā bhajyēyamapyēvam na namēyam tu kasyacit*” (Let me be cut in to two pieces; even at that time I will not worship any one).
- *sērndār* – Those who have reached him like a ship that was lost, reaching the shore. [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) which is in this samsāram (material realm) since time immemorial, reaching [sarvēśvaran](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is like reaching the shore. *ikkarai ēṟinārgaḷiṟē avargaḷ* – Those are the ones who reached the shore (nampiḷḷai quoting periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 5.3.7, where [periyāḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/periyazhwar/) says he reached the shore of paramapadam).
- *tī vinaigatku aru nanjai* – He is like an unbearable poison for the hurdles which stop them from attaining him.
- *tiṇ madiyai* – He is the bestover of strong intellect on those who are already surrendered unto him. When ambarīśa was performing penance, [sarvēśvaran](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) assumes the form of indra, goes to him and tells him “You ask me for any boon”; ambarīśa replies “I don’t worship you; don’t disturb my penance; I pray to you that you leave immediately”. This is explained in śrīviṣṇu darmam second chapter “*nāham āradayāmi tvām tava baddōyamanjali:*” – he gives such strong intellect that even if he himself tries to shake it, it will not be disturbed.
- *tīrndār …* – He will not leave the hearts of those who cannot bear his separation as explained in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 31.5 “*jalān matsyāvivōddrutau*” (like a fish taken out of water); he will not let them melt fully out of separation and manifests radiance highlighting that it is his benefit that they are with him. tīrndāruṇḍu (such resigned people are present) – those who have full faith in [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) being the upāyam (means). Those people would consider emperumān as prāpyam (goal) and prāpakam (means). He will stay in their hearts such that they don’t suffer in separation.
- *arakkiyai mūkku īrndāyai* – Just like eliminating the hurdles which came to disrupt his union with sītā pirātti, he would eliminate the hurdles of such fully dedicated devotees too. But did [śrī rāma](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) cut off the nose of sūrpaṇakā (it was actually lakśmaṇa)? Yes – one should use their hand to cut off the nose and lakhsmaṇa is explained as śrī rāma’s right hand in śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 34.13 and 34.14 “*rāmāsya dakśiṇō bāhu:*” (lakhsmaṇa is śrī rāma’s right shoulder) – so there is nothing wrong in saying “śrī rāma cut off sūrpaṇakā’s nose)
- *adiyēn …* – I, who am your servitor, have reached you long ago – isn’t it?
- *adiyēn adaindēn mudal munnamē* – Since you have given such blissful experience which made me forget the loss that was there since time immemorial, it cannot be said that “I just got it today”. Just like [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) forgot the union he had before he composed “*vāyum tiraiyugaḷum*” and subsequently remembered the separation only, here the abundant experience from the union makes him wonder if he had this experience forever.  *mudal munnamē* – very ancient.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.3.7. Munnal yal

*mun nal yāḻ payil nūl narambin mudir suvaiyē! pal nalār payilum paranē! pavittiranē! kannalē! amudē! kārmugilē en kaṇṇā! ninnalāl ilēn kāṇ ennai nī kuṟikkoḷḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

mun – since time immemorial; nal – distinct/beautiful; yāḻ – in the musical instrument named yāḻ \[similar to modern day vīṇā\]; payil – practiced (by those who want to acquire proficiency); nūl – as laid out in gīta śāstram (literature related to music); narambil – sourced from the nerve (String); mudir – matured; suvaiyē – ūnlimitedly enjoyable like music; pal – multitude (of persons who enjoy as mentioned); nalār – those with greatness (which never slips); payilum – to enjoy eternally; paranē – one who is supreme; pavittiranē – one who purifies (those who don’t have such state of mind by eliminating their defects such as ignorance etc and giving them such joyful experience); kannalē – Having unlimited sweetness like sweet food item which has sweetness everywhere; amudē – nectar (which can give life to even dead ones); kārmugilē – Having a magnanimous form like a cloud during rainy season (who is being the abode of such tastes); en – to give blissful experience to me (with such divine form); kaṇṇā – Oh kriṣṇa!; ninnalāl – without you (who are so unlimitedly sweet); ilēn kāṇ – I have no existence; ennai – me (who will die in separation); nī – you (who have so much sweetness that will make others die while in separation); kuṟikkoḷ – consider in your divine heart (after analysing the nature of us both)

**Перевод:**

**Oh one who is like the most enjoyable/matured music which is sourced from the nerve (String) and which is practiced in the musical instrument named yāḻ and that follows the rules laid in the music literature! Oh one who exists as the supreme for the joy of those multitude of great persons! Oh one who can purify even those who  don’t have such state of mind by eliminating their defects such as ignorance etc and giving them such joyful experience! Oh one who is having unlimited sweetness like sweet food item which has sweetness everywhere! Oh one who is the nectar which can give life to even dead ones! Oh the one who is having a magnanimous form like a cloud during rainy season (who is being the abode of such tastes)! Oh one who assumed the form of kriṣṇa to give blissful experience to me (with such divine form)! You (who have so much sweetness that will make others die if separated) keep me (who will die in separation) in your heart since I have no existence without you.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the seventh pāsuram – āḻvār doubts if the togetherness with emperumān will break and says “I cannot bear the separation” and requests emperumān to keep him in emperumān’s heart.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “How can I sustain myself without you who are so generous and most enjoyable?”*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Seventh pāsuram – Contemplating the great favour which he got and the most enjoyable nature of the union with emperumān, āḻvār doubts that this cannot be sustained and says “if your highness leaves me, I will not even exist; please never leave me”. முன் நல் யாழ் பயில் நூல் நரம்பின் முதிர் சுவையே பல் நலார் பயிலும் பரனே! பவித்திரனே கன்னலே! அமுதே கார் முகிலே என் கண்ணா! நின் அலால் இலேன் காண் என்னை நீ குறிக்கொள்ளே mun nal yāḻ payil nūl narambin mudir suvaiyē! pal nalār payilum paranē! pavittiranē! kannalē! amudē! kārmugilē en kaṇṇā! ninnalāl ilēn kāṇ ennai nī kuṟikkoḷḷē*

- *munnal* … – Some explain munnal by removing “*n*“, saying it as “*munal*” which indicates “*mural*” (making sound). Alternatively, munnal also is explained as unnal, which means contemplation – due to its sweetness, it makes one contemplate and blabber about it constantly. Otherwise, mun – oldness of the literature – due to the ancient nature of the literature, that too “*nal*” (good/distinct), yāḻ payil nūl – the śāstram which is studied about yāḻ. *nūl – śāstram*. So, as mentioned in śāstram. *narambin mudir suvaiyē* – sourced from the nerve, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is most enjoyable like the matured music which came from the nerve (String) of the musical instrument. Here nerve (String of the instrument) is indicated instead of *midaṟu* (throat) because, throat may have limitations due to infections etc due to one’s own karma; but nerve always remains perfect.

If there is unlimited joy like this, there should be some who enjoy that; they are explained further.

- *pannalār payilum paranē* – As highlighted in nācciyār tirumoḻi 4.1 “*teḷḷiyār palar kai toḻum dēvanār*” (Many intellectuals worship [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)) – there are many of them, even if nityasūris who are leaders in enjoying bhagavān try to enjoy him, what is enjoyed will be less and what is to be enjoyed will be more.
- *pavittiranē* – two explanations:
   - Even for those who have been eternally in this samsāram (material realm), he purifies them to bring them to the level of nityasūris.
   - *pannalār* indicates mumukśus; even when they enjoy him forever, his sweetness does not reduce, and he has the ability to eliminate the hurdles which stop them from enjoying him.
- *kannalē* – you who are unlimitedly enjoyable for me!
- *amudē* – you who keep me alive!
- *kārmugilē* – magnanimous
- *en kaṇṇā* – one who gave himself to me (as kriṣṇa, which is ultimate state of magnanimity).

Up till this, the reasons for [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s doubt are listed.

- *ninnalāl ilēn kāṇ* – I cannot even sustain for a fraction of a moment in your separation; it can also be explained as “no one other than you can protect me”.
- *ennai nī kuṟikkoḷḷē* – you have to throw your glance at me; you have to consider me in your divine heart;
- *ennai* – me who is like [acit (insentient)](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/09/thathva-thrayam-achith-what-is-matter/) in your separation
- *nī* – you who are the bearer of me

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.3.8. Kurikkol jnanangalal

*kuṟikkoḷ jñānangaḷāl enai ūḻi sey tavamum kiṟikkoṇḍu ip piṟappē sila nāḷil eydinan yān uṟikkoṇḍa veṇṇey pāl oḷittu uṇṇum ammān pin neṟikkoṇḍa nenjanāyp piṟavit tuyar kadindē*

**Пословный перевод:**

uṟi – in a pot (hung down from the ceiling in a rope to preserve milk, curd (yoghurt), butter etc); koṇḍa – preserved; veṇṇey – butter; pāl – milk; oḷittu – entered mischievously (without the knowledge of the owners); uṇṇum – since he eats; ammān – kriṣṇa who is the master (since he accepted the service); pin – subsequently; neṟi – path (which he took); koṇḍa – following; nenjanāy – having such heart; piṟavit tuyar – difficulties caused by birth; kadindu – discarding them through detachment; kuṟikkoḷ – those which are pursued (through renunciation and control of senses); jñānangaḷāl – many different types of jñāna yōgam (which vary in form as in vēdana, dhyāna, upāasana and in the process such as sadvidyā, dahara vidyā etc); enai ūḻi – in a long span of time; sey – performed; tavamum – the result of tapasyā (penance – bhakti yōgam); kiṟikkoṇḍu – through good means (which is the mercy of bhagavān); ippiṟappē – in this life itself; sila nāḷil – in a short span of time; yān – me (who is not qualified for such experience); eydinan – attained

**Перевод:**

**kriṣṇa entered (the house) mischievously, eats the butter and milk which are preserved in the pots that are hanging in a rope in the ceiling. By accepting this service, he shows that he is the master. I, being won-over by his act of stealing butter etc., having a heart which follows him, have attained the goal effortlessly through good means (that is, the mercy of bhagavān) in this life itself in a short span of time. This is otherwise attained by discarding difficulties which are caused by birth through detachment and pursuing jñāna yōgam (which vary in form as in vēdana, dhyāna, upāasana and in the process such as sadvidyā, dahara vidyā etc), and after a very long time, as said in lagvatri smruti “janmāntara saharēśu” (After many many thousands of births) and bhagavat gītā 7.19 “bahunām janmanām antē” (after many many births) in a long span of time through the result of tapasyā (bhakti yōgam).**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the eighth pāsuram – emperumān mercifully asks “is there a possibility of the separation you spoke about in the previous pāsuram?”. āḻvār consoles himself hearing that and becomes pleased thinking “I have effortlessly attained in this life itself in a short time frame, the unsurpassed goal which cannot be attained in a very long period”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār mercifully explains how he attained this experience.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*In the eighth pāsuram – emperumān asks “Are my favours such that you doubt them and say ‘keep me in your heart’?” and āḻvār contemplates on emperumān’s such favours and becomes pleased.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Eighth pāsuram – When āḻvār said “ennai nī kuṟikkoḷḷē” (keep me in your heart – don’t leave me), emperumān mercifully glances at āḻvār. On receiving that merciful glance, all sufferings of āḻvār are removed and he enjoys emperumān. குறிக்கொள் ஞானங்களால் எனை ஊழி செய் தவமும் கிறிக்கொண்டு இப் பிறப்பே சில நாளில் எய்தினன் யான் உறிக்கொண்ட வெண்ணெய் பால் ஒளித்து உண்ணும் அம்மான் பின் நெறிக்கொண்ட நெஞ்சனாய்ப் பிறவித் துயர் கடிந்தே kuṟikkoḷ jñānangaḷāl enai ūḻi sey tavamum kiṟikkoṇḍu ip piṟappē sila nāḷil eydinan yān uṟikkoṇḍa veṇṇey pāl oḷittu uṇṇum ammān pin neṟikkoṇḍa nenjanāyp piṟavit tuyar kadindē*

- *kuṟikkoḷ jñānangaḷāl* – Special kind of knowledge (jñāna viśēśam – bhakti) which is earned by practising aśtānga yōgam (yama, niyama, Asana, prāṇāyāma, pratyāhāra, dāraṇa, dhyāna, samādi). Such knowledge/devotion is indicated by vēdana, dhyāna, upāsana etc.
- *enai ūḻi sey tavamum* – The result of penance which is acquired through śravaṇam (hearing), mananam (meditation), druvānusmruti (continuous thinking) which is done for many kalpams (kalpa – 1 day of brahmā which is many crores of years).
- *kiṟikkoṇḍu* – Effortless means; that is, [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) himself being the means. Does kiṟi mean bhagavān? He is explained in tiruviruttam 91 as “*perungiṟiyān*” (greatest means).

When asked “In how many births did you accomplish this?”

- *sila nāḷil* – in a very short span of time.

Nice, did you accomplish yourself?

- *eydinan* – I got it (by the mercy of [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)).
- *yān* – I, who did not put any effort for this result.
- *uṟikkoṇḍa ….* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) explains the result which is explained in “*tavameydinan*” and the means which is explained in “*kiṟikkoṇḍu*“.
- *uṟi* … – One who won over the universe by manifesting the activity of stealing butter and milk which were preserved carefully in pots (hanging in the ceiling) and made people wonder “How did the butter disappear? Was it consumed by God without our knowledge?”.
- *pin neṟikkoṇḍa nenjanāy* – Having a heart which follows him as said in “*yēna yēna dātā gaccati, tēna tēna saha gaccati*” (wherever [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) goes, [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) follows him in those ways). Alternatively, prapatti (surrender) is explained in “*pin neṟi*“. *“pin neṟi*” means that which was explained later (that is, carama ślōkam which was spoken at the end of [bhagavat gītā](http://githa.koyil.org/)) – so having a heart which is focused on carama ślōkam.
- *piṟavit tuyar kadindē* – While speaking about the result (in carama ślōkam), removal of hurdles is also explained – that is explained here (the eradication of birth in this material realm). Alternative explanation – “*pin neṟik koṇḍa nenjanāy*” – in the mahābhārata battle, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) created a sorrowful situation and instructed the means to arjuna; but here, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) followed kriṣṇa where he went to steal butter, locked the door (so kriṣṇa cannot escape) and learned the meanings.
- *piṟavittuyar kadindē* – bhagavāan explained in gītā as “*sarvapāpēbhyō mōkśayiśyāmi*” (I will eradicate all your sins).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.3.9. Kadivar tannantulay

*kadi vār taṇ am tuḻāyk kaṇṇan viṇṇavar perumān padi vānam iṟanda paraman pavittiran sīr sedi ār nōygaḷ kedap padindu kudaindu ādi adiyēn vāy maduttup parugik kaḷittēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kadi – fragrance; vār – flowing; taṇ am tuḻāy – one who is wearing fresh tuḷasi (garland); kaṇṇan – kriṣṇa (who is submissive towards his devotees); viṇṇavar perumān – for him who has supremacy (which is enjoyed by) nityasūris who are matching in glory; vānam – in paramapadam (spiritual sky); padi – match; iṟanda – since (it is) not there; paraman – the supreme who has no one greater than him; pavittiran – one who is so pure (that he purifies even those who are ignorant and don’t have this proper understanding and gives them divine experience); sīr – in the qualities (which manifest his supremacy, simplicity, purity etc); sediyār – densely populated, abundant; nōygaḷ – great diseases (starting with worldly attachments); keda – to destroy; padindu – approached; kudaindu – completely immersed; ādi – bathed (drenched/drowned); adiyēn – I who am fully existing for bhagavān; vāy maduttu – keeping my mouth (which is the desire that is the tool to enjoy) ready; parugi – consumed it (like a very thirsty person drinking water) for full satisfaction; kaḷitttēn – attained unsurpassed bliss

**Перевод:**

**One who is wearing fresh tuḷasi which has flowing fragrance, one who is kriṣṇa (who is submissive towards his devotees), one who is the undisputed supreme lord since he does not have a match even in paramapadam where he is the master of nityasūris (who have matching glory), one who is so pure (that he he purifies even those who are ignorant and don’t have this proper understanding and gives them divine experience); in order to destroy the great diseases (starting with worldly attachments), I have approached emperumān, fully submerged, bathed, prepared the mouth and fully consumed emperumān and acquired unsurpassed joy.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the ninth pāsuram – āḻvār says that he enjoyed emperumān‘s guṇams (qualities) with great thirst and felt blissful.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Ninth pāsuram – As said in taittirya upaniśad ānandavalli “sōśnutē sarvān kāman saha brahmaṇā vipaścitā” (He experiences all auspicious qualities of bhagavān who is omniscient), āḻvār says that he experienced bhagavān and eliminated all his difficulties and becomes delighted. கடி வார் தண் அம் துழாய்க் கண்ணன் விண்ணவர் பெருமான் படி வானம் இறந்த பரமன் பவித்திரன் சீர் செடி ஆர் நோய்கள் கெட படிந்து குடைந்து ஆடி அடியேன் வாய் மடுத்துப் பருகிக் களித்தேனே kadi vār taṇ am tuḻāyk kaṇṇan viṇṇavar perumān padi vānam iṟanda paraman pavittiran sīr sedi Ar nōygaḷ kedap padindu kudaindu ādi adiyēn vāy maduttup parugik kaḷittēnē*

- *kadivār taṇṇantuḻāyk kaṇṇan* – kriṣṇa who is wearing tuḷasi garland which has abundance of fragrance; kriṣṇa who is wearing tuḷasi garland which has honey flowing.
- *viṇṇavar perumān* – With this mesmerising form, he wins over nityasūris such as ananta (ādiśēśa), garuda et al.
- *padi vānam iṟanda paraman* – 3 explanations:
   - the supreme lord to whom even those nityasūris are no match
   - having supremacy such that even those nityasūris who are at par with [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) are not a match for his true nature
   - for his divine form (padi), even cloud (vānam (sky) represents mēgam (cloud)) is not a match
- *pavittiran sīr* – having purity to make such divine beautiful form available for samsāris (worldly people) too; *sīr* – such [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s auspicious qualities;
- *sediyār ….* – the dense/abundant difficulties (such as avidyā (ignorance) etc) of this material realm which block my experience of such qualities; approached such [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), experienced him in all directions, deeply immersed in him; I, who am fully existing for him, fully experienced him, placed my feet on the heads of yama et al (won-over death) and became blissful. *vāy maduttup parugi* – quenched my great thirst.
- *kaḷittēnē* – Just like worldly matters are filled with sorrow, experience of [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is fully joyful.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.
