## 2.3.10. Kalippum kavarvum

*kaḷippum kavarvum aṟṟup piṟappup piṇi mūppu iṟappu aṟṟu oḷikkoṇḍa sōdiyamāy udan kūduvadu enṟu kolō tuḷikkinṟa vān in nilam  sudar āḻi sangu ēndi aḷikkinṟa māyap pirān adiyārgaḷ kuḻāngaḷaiyē?*

**Пословный перевод:**

kaḷippum – joy (in worldly gains); kavarvum – craving (in the lack of such gains); aṟṟu – without; piṟappup piṇi mūppu iṟappu aṟṟu – without janma (birth), vyādi (disease), jarā (old age), maraṇa (death) which are the cause for such gains and lack of them; oḷik koṇḍa – that which shines the flame (of knowledge etc); sōdiyamāy – having beautiful effulgent form; tuḷikkinṟa – raining; vān – sky; innilam – earth (which sustains by that rain); sudar – greatly radiant; āḻi – chakra (disc); sangu – Sanka (conch); ēndi – holding; aḷikkinṟa – mercifully protecting; māyappirān – the great benefactor’s; adiyārgaḷ – nityasūris who are engaged with eternal servitude; kuḻāngaḷai – assemblies; udan – with agreement (to mix as water with water); kūduvadu – joining; enṟu kolō? – When

**Перевод:**

**Simple translation (based on vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar‘s 12000 padi)**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the tenth pāsuram – āḻvār searches for good company to share the divine experience of bhagavān‘s qualities thinking “When will I have my worldly difficulties removed and enter the assembly of nityaśuris (in paramapadam)?”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Tenth pāsuram – After saying “kaḷittēnē” (enjoyed), āḻvār says “instead of again being with samsāris (worldly people), when will I enter the assembly of nityasūris who are leaders for such blissful experience?”. களிப்பும் கவர்வும் அற்று பிறப்புப் பிணி மூப்பு இறப்பு அற்று ஒளிக்கொண்ட சோதியுமாய் உடன் கூடுவது என்று கொலோ துளிக்கின்ற வான் இந் நிலம் சுடர் ஆழி சங்கு ஏந்தி அளிக்கின்ற மாயப் பிரான் அடியார்கள் குழாங்களையே? kaḷippum kavarvum aṟṟup piṟappup piṇi mūppu iṟappu aṟṟu oḷikkoṇḍa sōdiyamāy udan kūduvadu enṟu kolō tuḷikkinṟa vān in nilam  sudar āḻi sangu ēndi aḷikkinṟa māyap pirān adiyārgaḷ kuḻāngaḷaiyē?*

- *kaḷippum* – joy derived out of enjoying matters other than that which is related to [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)
- *kavarvum* – the sorrow derived out of craving for such matters when they are not attained
- *aṟṟu* – eliminating
- *piṟappup piṇi mūppu iṟappu aṟṟu* – birth which is the cause for such joy/sorrow; disease which naturally follows birth at each stage of life; old age which occurs when one is thinking “at least we can survive with this disease” and finally the death; eliminating all of these
- *oḷikkoṇḍa sōdiyamāy* – having infinitely radiant body/form which is fully made of pure goodness unlike the body here which is mixed in satvam (goodness), rajas (passion) and tamas (ignorance)
- *udan kūduvadu enṟu kolō* – When will I join (that assembly)? Even after knowing that the assembly of bhāgavatas (devotees) is our goal, here one may hesitate to join the assembly due to ahankāram, mamakāram. But nityasūris (who have pure forms) are not like that – they always enjoy in groups. When will I jostle in the crowd of such nityasūris?
- *tuḷikkinṟa …* – By nature, sky pours down rain; earth flourishes by that; the spectacular [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who protects these with his divine weapons, just like he protected in the seashore (During śrī rāmāyaṇa battle, the monkey army went around the camp of śrī rāma and protected him. When in the night they slept due to fatigue, śrī rāma went around all of them with his bow and arrow and protected them mercifully. So whether awake or sleeping, it is [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is protecting all).
- *sudar āḻi sangu ēndi aḷikkinṟa māyap pirān* – In paramapadam, his weapons look like ornaments (since there is no use for weapons there); but here in this material realm, they act like weapons.
- *adiyārgaḷ kuḻāngaḷaiyē* – For such devotee who are won over by such protector, those who are the goal like he himself is, those leaders in (enjoying) [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s qualities, those who are company for *bhōdayanta:parasparam* ([bhagavat gītā](http://githa.koyil.org/) 10.9). In the assembly of such devotees. Like a very hungry person saying “When will I get food?”, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying with great desire “When will I join those assemblies?”

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.3.11. Kulam kol

*kuḻām koḷ pēr arakkan kulam vīya munindavanai kuḻām koḷ ten kurugūrc catakōpan terindu uraitta kuḻām koḷ āyirattuḷ ivai pattum udan pādi kuḻāngaḷāy adiyīr udan kūdi ninṟu āduminē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kuḻām koḷ – having many groups(of rākśasas who are hindering (others)); pēr – rāvaṇa who has greatness (of having such armies of rākśasas); arakkkan – rākśasa’s; kulam – whole clan; vīya – to be destroyed; munindavanai – one who mercifully showed his anger; kuḻām koḷ – having many groups (of śrīvaiṣṇavas); tenkurugūr – the controller of tirunagari; śatakōpan – nammāḻvār; terindu – analysed; uraitta – mercifully spoke; kuḻām koḷ – in the form of decads (collection of 10 pāsurams); āyirattuḷ – in the thousand pāsurams of tiruvāimoḻi; ivai pattum – these ten pāsurams; udan – agreeing (to the meanings); pādi – sing (to reveal the joy); kuḻāngaḷāy – in many groups (sharing the joy with each other); adiyīrudan – being like minded devotees matching your true nature; kūdi – associate; ninṟu – staying together (without break); ādumin – try to dance

**Перевод:**

**śrī rāma destroyed the clan of rāvaṇa who has the greatness of having many groups of rākśasas (who are hindering others); nammāḻvār who is the leader of āḻvārtirunagari which is filled with many groups of śrīvaiṣṇavas has analysed and mercifully spoken/sung this decad which is in one among the thousand pāsurams which have many such decads.  You sing this decad (to reveal your joy) agreeing with the meanings (of the pāsurams) in many groups of devotees together and try to dance in joy.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the end – āḻvār says “Those who are exclusively involved in enjoying bhagavān, should enjoy this decad together unlike me who enjoyed it alone”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār explains the result saying “Sing this decad together in association with mutual affection”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. குழாம் கொள் பேர் அரக்கன் குலம் வீய முனிந்தவனை குழாம் கொள் தென் குருகூர்ச் சடகோபன் தெரிந்து உரைத்த குழாம் கொள் ஆயிரத்துள் இவை பத்தும் உடன் பாடி குழாங்களாய் அடியீர் உடன் கூடி நின்று ஆடுமினே kuḻām koḷ pēr arakkan kulam vīya munindavanai kuḻām koḷ then kurugūrc catakōpan terindu uraitta kuḻām koḷ āyirattuḷ ivai pattum udan pādi kuḻāngaḷāy adiyīr udan kūdi ninṟu āduminē*

- *kuḻām koḷ ….* – rāvaṇa had many groups of sons, grand sons, relatives et al to support him; he was also well established due to his own strength and the strength acquired through boons. Such rāvaṇa was destroyed along with his clan by cakravarati tirumagan (son of emperor daśarata). This is explained by śrī rāma himself in śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 64.66 “*kariśyē maitileehētōr apiśācam arākśasam*” (Having śitā as reason, I will free this earth from devils and demons).
- *kuḻām koḷ tenkurugūrc catakōpan* – Just like the riśis entered daṇḍakāraṇyam after the rākśasas (kara, dūśaṇa et al) were destroyed in janastānam, many śrīvaiṣṇavas arrived at [āḻvārtirungari](http://azhwarthirunagari.koyil.org/) to see [nammāḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) who survived the agony of separation in “*vāyum tiraiyugaḷum*” padigam (decad). āḻvār himself declares in tiruviruttam 100 “*nallār navil kurugūr*” (āḻvārtirungari where many good persons reside).  If there is a place where there are many good persons (devotees) who are engaged in glorifying ([emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)), would they not assemble there together?
- *terinduraitta* – meditated and spoke as it is
- *ivai pattum* – these ten pāsurams, with which the assembled devotees sustain themselves
- *kuḻām koḷ āyiram* – As said in tiruvāimoḻi 9.4.9 “*toṇḍarkku amuduṇṇa*” (to be consumed as nectar for the devotees), ten pāsurams make one decad, ten decads make one centum and ten such centums make this tiruvāimoḻi which has thousand pāsurams. This tiruvāimoḻi is the livelihood for the devotees.
- *ivai pattum udanpādi* – singing along, agreeing with the principles
- *kuḻāngaḷāy* – Instead of saying “*kaḷittēnē*” (I enjoyed – singular) like me and subsequently searching for the assembly of devotees, be in the assembly first and sing along together.
- *adiyīrudan kūdi ninṟu āduminē* – You who are all fully pledged to him, who are quite few in numbers (in comparison to those who are not devotees) are going to be here in this world for a short span of time; in such time, instead of holding on to worldly wealth and desire and fighting with each other, enjoy this experience together here until you reach the great assembly in paramapadam.

[nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/), gives a brief summary of the whole decad at the end.

- In the first pāsuram, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) praised his divine heart.
- In the second pāsuram, he praised sarvēśvaran who convinced his divine heart (to surrender).
- In the third pāsuram, he highlighted a favour that was done by [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/).
- In the fourth pāsuram, he submitted his own self as a return to such favour and subsequently repented for that.
- In the fifth pāsuram, he said that since [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is the primary good-deed for him, he already attained [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s lotus feet.
- In the sixth pāsuram, he said “Did I achieve this today? When you first blessed me – at that time itself I have attained your lotus feet”.
- In the seventh pāsuram, he meditated upon his sweet nature and said “I cannot sustain separation from you”.
- In the eighth pāsuram, he said “I attained such unsurpassed sweet person through easy means”; it can also be said as, “I followed him and easily attained him instead of having to perform austere penance for a long time to get that great result”.
- In the ninth pāsuram, he said “I enjoyed so that all my difficulties are eliminated and became blissful”.
- In the tenth pāsuram, he asked “when will I be in the assembly of such persons who enjoy [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) so much?”.
- In the end, he said “Meditate upon and recite this tiruvāimoḻi with its meaning;  you are few in numbers and are going to live for a short span of time only, so try to experience it (instead of fighting among yourselves)”.

## 2.4 Adi adi

## 2.4.1. Adi adi

*ādi ādi agam karaindu isai pādip pādik kaṇṇīr malgi engum nādi nādi narasingā enṟu vādi vādum iv vāḷ nudalē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ivvāḷ nudal (ivvāṇudal) – one who is having a shining forehead; ādi ādi – running around many times (like a trained dancer whose dance is a treat to watch, out of her grief unable to stay in one place); agam karaindu – having a broken heart; isai pādip pādi – (out of that grief) lamenting by singing in many different ways; kaṇṇīr malgi – (like a melted heart will shed) tears from eyes; engum – everywhere; nādi nādi – looking out for him; narasingā enṟu – calling out as narasimha! (who is present everywhere); vādi vādum – (since he did not arrive even after that) became very exhausted

**Перевод:**

**My daughter who is having a shining forehead, is running around many times (like a trained dancer whose dance is a treat to watch, out of her grief unable to stay in one place), and is having a broken heart; she is thus lamenting by singing in many different ways and shedding tears from her eyes; she is looking for emperumān calling out as narasimha! (who is present everywhere) and (since he did not arrive even after that) became very exhausted.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the first pāsuram – parānkusa nāyaki‘s (āḻvār in feminine mood) divine mother is grieving saying that my daughter is feeling sunken saying “emperumān who incarnated as narasimha and helped śrī prahlādāḻvān, is not helping me”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*In the first pāsuram – She is saying that parānkusa nāyaki is feeling depressed saying “He has not helped me like he did for prahlāda”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*In the first pāsuram – parānkusa nāyaki‘s mother is saying that her daughter is calling out for emperumān who is of the nature of helping his devotees when they called for him keeping their danger itself as the reason (for his arrival). ஆடி ஆடி அகம் கரைந்து, இசை பாடிப் பாடிக் கண்ணீர் மல்கி, எங்கும் நாடி நாடி நரசிங்கா என்று, வாடி வாடும் இவ் வாள் நுதலே ādi ādi agam karaindu isai pādip pādik kaṇṇīr malgi engum nādi nādi narasingā enṟu vādi vādum iv vāḷ nudalē*

- *ādi ādi* – The divine mother of [parānkusa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) became attracted to her daughter’s restlessness/anxiety (in separation from [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)) which was manifested in her irregular state, walking and sleeping. Like śrī kausalyā suffering in (thinking about the) separation from śrī rāma as explained in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 40.45 “… *nrutyantīmiva mātaram*” (Seeing kausalyā starting to cry constantly, in thinking about the separation of śrī rāma, lakśmaṇa and sītā – śrī rāma watched her like seeing a dancer). When someone is beautiful, all their actions would also be beautiful (and enjoyable for others). When sītā was in separation from śrī rāma and not decorated, vālmīki bhagavān narrated her in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 29.1 “… *subhām* …” (the one with an auspicious form).
- *ādi* – Second “*ādi*” is not the same as first “*ādi*” (the tone becomes much lower due to her inability). Initially, though unable to sustain oneself, one would walk about waiting for perumāḷ \[But subsequently, even that would not be possible, since one will be totally exhaused\]. Since [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is filled with auspicious qualities, one cannot easily give up on him. This is explained by quoting bharata’s situation in śrī rāmāyaṇam bāla kāṇḍam 1.38 “*rāmāgamanakāngśayā*” (desiring for śrī rāma’s arrival) – bharata thinks “if I can see śrī rāma’s face one more time, why should I give up this life in a useless manner?” administered the kingdom, waiting for śrī rāma. Second “*ādi*” is recited in half the volume of first “*ādi*” – this can be understood based on the sound of the cymbal (like a sound being echoed).
- *agam karaindu* – Like the walk (action) is irregular, heart/mind too became weak like ice melting to become water. How did the mother know the daughter’s heart is melting? Just like the daughter’s actions are observed through her eyes, the daughter’s heart is  understood by her own heart. While it is said that “*mana: pūrvō vāguttara:*” (whatever is conceived in mind manifests in action subsequently), there is no such order in her behaviour. Her crying out in anxiety has naturally turned into a song. Just as it is said in tiruccanta viruttam 105 “*paṇṇai venṟa insol mangai*” (girl whose words are better than music), śrī rāma said to hanuman about sītā in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 64.15 “*madurā madurālāpā*” (the beautiful one with beautiful voice). Just like her actions out of anxiety became a dance, her words out of anxiety became a song. Unlike the first time crying, subsequent crying will be a lot weaker.
- *kaṇṇīr malgi* – Once the heart melted, it flowed like music and came out as tears.
- *malgi* – abundance. śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 33.4  “*kimartam tava nētrābhyām vārisravati śōkajam*” (Why are sad tears coming out of your eyes (which resemble lotus flower) where there should only be tears of joy?) – [bhattar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/parasara-bhattar/) explained the meaning of this ślōkam and mercifully asked “Whose clan is going to be destroyed by these tears?”; [piḷḷān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/pillan/) asked “Who is there to enjoy this form (no one)?” focusing more on “lotus like eyes shedding tears” (since [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is not present there). [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/) says “Oh sinful me! I have not seen perumāḷ arriving to see my form”.
- *engum nādi nādi* – having her danger (separation) alone as tāmrasāsanam (charter written on copper plate as evidence/reason), she would look around in all directions. śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 31.19 is explained by nampiḷḷai here:
   - *sā tiryakūrdvanca tatāpyadastāt* (sītā pirātti looked across, up and down) – though she was unconscious, when she heard the divine names (of śrī rāma recited by hanuman), she started looking around everywhere across lankā, up and down. Why did she look down? Three explanations are given: 1) If one can come out of earth and recite the names, he can come out of everywhere – so she looked around everywhere; 2) one who was fasting for a month, upon hearing the word “food”, will look around everywhere with great desire – similarly she looked around everywhere; 3) it can be said as sītā pirātti looking at the śimśupā tree everywhere (across, top and bottom).
   - *tamacintyabhuddim dadarśa* – Before seeing hanuman’s form, she analysed his heart, thinking that he has arrived where she is and with the kind heart to help her.
   - *pingādipatēr amātyam* – she understood that he is not independent and he is here on the orders of his king
   - *vātātmajam* – he looked like “the son of vāyu who is the one who provides life sustaining air to all” since he is going to help sustain pirātti who is the life of śrī rāma
   - *sūryamivōdayastam* – he laid the foundation for sunrise in lankā; like the aruṇōdayam (the early morning time before sunrise), hanuman was the aruṇōdayam before śrī rāma who is the sūryōdayam. That is why inside lankā’s fort, it sounds “hari hari” (double meaning – hari means viṣṇu; hari also means monkey; the name “hari” is recited in the morning as soon as one wakes up to ward off their sins). So, why is she searching in places from where [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) may not arrive? Because, emperumān arrives from any place; why is she not calling out for viṣṇu (generally)? After singing “[*pattudai adiyavar*](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/06/thiruvaimozhi-1-3-1-paththudai-adiyavar/)“, she would always stop at avatārams (incarnations) and not go beyond that.
   - *engum nādi nādi* – [bhattar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/parasara-bhattar/) explained this as “she searched even in her own koysakam (saree-fold)” – this is based on [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) having [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s waist as his residing place as āḻvār himself said in tiruvāimoḻi 1.9.4 “*kaṇṇan en okkalaiyānē*” (kriṣṇa is on my waist).
   - *narasingā enṟu* – Since she did not have a pillar like prahlāda had. The one who appeared in front of prahlāda who had pristine knowledge and said “*mattassarvam aham sarvam*” (śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 1.19.85 – everything is created from me, everything is me) – he is not appearing before this poor girl! Would you help only if the father becomes enemy? Would you not help if you yourself become enemy (by not uniting with her)? While you helped the one who is firm in jñānam (knowledge), would you not help me who is firm in bhakti (devotion)? While you helped men, would you not help girls (like me)? While you helped assuming form which is unnatural, would you not help with your natural form? Should she develop some qualification (like prahlāda should be protected with a unique narasimha form), approach you at a particular time (since hiraṇyakaśipu could not be killed at day, night etc), expect you to help her with a particular tool (like [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) was forced to use his nails to kill hiraṇyakaśipu and protect prahlāda)? Should you have to assume a particular face to protect her (like he assumed lion face to protect prahlāda)?
   - *vādi vādum* – Like a stem which lost its supporting stick. First “*vādi*” (sulking) is fresh, when we compare the second “*vādum*” with that (she deteriorated quickly).
   - *vādum* – It is in future tense. So she is sure that she will not die and will just crave for his arrival.
   - *ivvāṇudalē (ivvāḷ nudalē)* – having a shining forehead. She is going through such suffering which those who become attracted to her will go through. Are you staying away from her thinking that you can create someone like her if she dies? Are you planning to create (someone like her) again as said in taittirya upaniśad nārāyaṇavalli “*dātā yatāpūrvamakalpayat*” (brahmā created like it was present in previous times (before praḷayam))? The signs of the union you had with her in “[*ūnil vāḻuyir*](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/02/thiruvaimozhi-2-3-unil-vazh/)” has still not disappeared. Just like one who was destroyed by arrows and one who drowned in water will be clearly identified, she is suffering due to separation from [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who has abundance of auspicious qualities.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

adiyen saraty ramanuja dasan

## 2.4.2. Val nudal

*vāḷ nudal im madavaral ummaik kāṇum āsaiyuḷ naiginṟāḷ viṟal vāṇān āyiram tōḷ tuṇittīr ummaik kāṇa nīr irakkam ileerē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vāḷ – shining; nudal – having forehead; immadavaral – this girl with abundance of humility; ummai – you (who are a treat to eyes); kāṇum āsaiyuḷ – with the desire to see; naiginṟāḷ – becoming weak; viṟal – very prideful; vāṇan – bāṇāsura’s; āyiram tōḷ tuṇittīr – oh the one who cut of the thousand shoulders!; ummai – you; kāṇa – to see; nīr – you; irakkam ileer – are merciless

**Перевод:**

**This girl with shining forehead and abundance of humility is becoming weak due to desire to see you (who are a treat to eyes). Oh the one who cut off the thousand shoulders of the prideful bāṇāsura! You have no mercy to show your form (to her).**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the second pāsuram – parānkuśa nāyaki‘s mother says “you who cut off the many shoulders (hands) of bāṇāsura and helped aniruddāḻvāne, ar not helping her even in her such pitiful state”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Second pāsuram – emperumān asks “While you have lots of hurdles, is her craving enough?” and parānkuśa nāyaki‘s mother says “are her hurdles greater than the bāhuvanam (many shoulders) of bāṇāsura?”. வாள் நுதல் இம் மடவரல், உம்மைக் காணும் ஆசையுள் நைகின்றாள், விறல் வாணன் ஆயிரம் தோள் துணித்தீர், உம்மைக் காண நீர் இரக்கம் இலீரே vāḷ nudal im madavaral ummaik kāṇum āsaiyuḷ naiginṟāḷ viṟal vāṇān āyiram tōḷ tuṇittīr ummaik kāṇa nīr irakkam ileerē*

- *vāḷ nudal* – this beauty of the forehead is the cause for grief instead of joy (for the mother).. That which is attractive to me who gave birth to this girl, is that which is causing you to ignore her. nampiḷḷai quotes śrī rāmāyaṇam bāla kāṇḍam 73.24 “*iyam sītā mama sutā sahadarmacarī tava \| pratīccacainām bhadram tē pāṇim gruhṇīśva pāṇinā* \|\|” (this sītā, my daughter is well qualified to accompany you in the righteous path; you accept her; let there be all auspiciousness; you hold on to her hands with your hands) comparing [parānkuśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) to [sītā pirātti](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/).
- *im madavaral* – having a very tender nature; cannot bear separation. The state of this divine mother of parānkuśa nāyaki is the same as when tiruvadi (hanuman) saw sītā pirātti (in aśōka vanam). nampiḷḷai beautifully explains śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 15.53 here. *duśkaram krutavān rāma:* – perumāḷ (śrī rāma) performed very difficult tasks while sustaining himself in her separation. *hīnō yadanayā prabhu:* – that is he sustained himself – which by itself is a great task. *prabhu: –* in his early days, he learned to ride horse, elephant etc and how to rule the kingdom; In separation from his beloved, he did not enjoy anything. When [perumāḷ](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) was in mālyavān, hanuman observed his agony in separation and since he was a renunciate, he thought about śrī rāma “he is śiśya of vaśiśta (who is a great scholar/sage), but is suffering for a woman like this” and laughed \[within himself\] at perumāḷ; but on seeing sītā pirātti, since he is greatly knowledgeable, he thought “how can one sustain oneself in separation from sītā pirātti?”. *dārayatyātmanō dēham* – is this a body which is acquired on loan (not one’s own) so that it can be sustained like this? is this body not present for enjoyment? is this body present for suffering? Her quality is not such that one can say “in separation, I will wait for the apt process to unite with her”.
- *ummai* – I only need to explain her state to you; you know about yourself quite well such that you should know “those who are in separation from me will not survive”.
- *vāḷ nudal immadavaral ummai* – you both are as explained in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 16.5 “*tulya śīla vayō vruttām*” (śitā and śrī rāma are perfect match in qualities, age, activities etc).
- *ummaik kāṇum āsaiyuḷ naiginṟāḷ* – one’s desire will match the object of such desire (you are great, so the desire is also great).
- *kāṇum āsaiyuḷ* – Did she desire to embrace you? Why are you not even showing your form?
- *ummaik kāṇum āsaiyuḷ naiginṟāḷ* – Like being submerged in an ocean; desire is the ocean here; this craving is also acceptable.
- *viṟal vāṇan āyiram tōḷ tuṇittīr* – if you are asking “is such craving sufficient when there are hurdles?”, let me say “are her hurdles not greater than the many shoulders of bāṇāsura?”. You are the one who united uśā and anirudda. Would you only help if it is your grandson or male? Should you not help this poor girl who united with you (previously)?
- *ummaik kāṇa* – When someone desires for a karumugai garland \[an exotic flower\], it is to wear it, not to make it as summādu (a cloth which is rolled up and kept on head to support heavy objects). Similarly, when she wants to see you, seeing is the purpose; she is not going to ask for something more after seeing. [tirumaḻisai āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/thirumazhisai-azhwar/) says in nānmugan tiruvantādi 39 “*aḻaippan tiruvēnkatattānaik kāṇa*” (I call out for śrīnivāsa to see him); [tirumangai āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/thirumangai-azhwar/) says in siṟiya tirumadal “*kārār tirumēni kāṇumaḷavum*” (to see his cloud-like divine form); [nammāḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) too said in tiruvāimoḻi 3.8.5 “*kaṇgaḷāl kāṇa varungolenṟu*” (arrive to be seen by my eyes). You are not having the mercy to make yourself visible.
- *nīr irakkam ileerē* – As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 36.42 “…*naiva damśān…*” (in separation from you, śrī rāma was not even driving away forest-flies etc from his body) – you were so attached to sītā pirātti; but here you are not even showing basic compassion towards [parānkuśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) who is suffering in separation from you. parānkuśa nāyaki’s mother feels “her agony/craving is not the means for the goal; his mercy is the means for the goal”. She also thinks “her agony/craving is part of the entourage for his mercy; his mercy is the means for the goal”. As said in katavalli upaniśad “*nāyamātmā pravacanēna labhyō na mēdayā na bahunā śrutēna \| yamaivēśa vruṇutē tēna labhayastasyaiśa ātmā vivruṇutē tanūm svām \|\|*” (This [paramātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) cannot be attained through contemplation, profound and repetitive meditation, lots of hearing etc; only those who are accepted by such [paramātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) can attain him; for such [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/), this paramātmā  shows his true nature) – one can see him only when he himself makes him visible.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.4.3. Irakka manattodu

*irakka manattōdu eri aṇai arakkum meḻugum okkum ivaḷ irakkam eḻīr idarku en seygēn arakkan ilangai seṟṟirukkē*

**Пословный перевод:**

irakkam – filled with sorrow; manattōdu – having such heart; ivaḷ – she; arakkum – sealing lacquer (a type of wax) – firm; meḻugum – soft wax; eri aṇai okkum – just like they (firm and soft wax) will melt when contacted with fire, she lost her chastity and shyness; irakkam ileer – you are not manifesting your mercy; idaṟku – for this; arakkan – rākśasa named rāvaṇa’s; ilangai – lankā; seṟṟirukku – you who destroyed; en – what; seygēn – (I) will do?

**Перевод:**

**Having a heart filled with sorrow, she lost her chastity and shyness (after uniting with you) like firm or soft wax will melt when contacted with fire; but you who destroyed lankā, belonging to a rākśasa named rāvaṇa, are not manifesting your mercy; what will I do for this?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the third pāsuram – parānkuśa nāyaki‘s mother is saying helplessly “My daughter desired you thinking about the acts you did towards King śrī janaka’s divine daughter and is suffering due to that; still you are not helping her; what can I do?”*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, parānkuśa nāyaki‘s mother says “You who destroyed rāvaṇa and lankā for sītā pirātti are not helping my daughter; what can be done?”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Third pāsuram – parānkuśa nāyaki‘s mother says “Today, you have decided not to show your mercy to my daughter; but why did you spend sleepless nights, crossed over the sea and do such acts (like destroying lankā etc) then (as śrī rāma)?”. இரக்க மனத்தோடு எரி அணை, அரக்கும் மெழுகும் ஒக்கும் இவள், இரக்கம் எழீர் இதற்கு என் செய்கேன், அரக்கன் இலங்கை செற்றீருக்கே irakka manattōdu eri aṇai arakkum meḻugum okkum ivaḷ irakkam eḻīr idarku en seygēn arakkan ilangai seṟṟirukkē*

- *irakkam* … – irakkam means melting of heart, attachment, friendship; having a weak heart, she melted like firm/soft wax in contact with fire. piḷḷai tirunaṟaiyūr araiyar explains Firm wax as an adjective to her heart and soft wax as an adjective to her. [bhattar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/parasara-bhattar/) explains both firm and soft wax as adjectives to her since her heart is in her control also. As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam bāla kāṇḍam 1.18 “*viṣṇunā sadruśō vīryē…*” (He is like [viṣṇu](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) in valour, like moon to be a treat to the eyes – Each aspect of śrī rāma has one example), there can be many examples for her situation (this is explanation for bhattar’s view). Wax will disappear when placed in fire; it will become hard when taken away from fire and will melt when in proximity of fire. She can neither die (and be relieved) nor can sustain herself – you are torturing her like this – this is her state.
- *irakkam eḻīr* – Are we asking you to also melt like her? You are not even showing mercy towards those who are suffering. She is with a suffering heart; your compassion is not manifesting; if you are not showing mercy, at least give her a heart like yours (which does not have any attachment).
- *idaṟku en seygēn* – Can there be any means other than your mercy for this goal?
- *en seygēn* – Can I make you show mercy to her? Can I make her not long for you?
- *arakkan ilangai seṟṟirukkē* – If you don’t have mercy, why did you perform an act which developed her attachment towards you? She became attached to you thinking “Would one who helped his beloved, not help me too?” She misunderstood your act (as if it were your genuine help to a dear one) like someone misunderstanding the marks of a worm to be writing and thus became very agonised.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.4.4. Ilangai serravane

*ilangai seṟṟavanē ennum pinnum valam koḷ puḷ uyarttāy! ennum uḷḷam malanga vevvuyirkkum  kaṇṇir migak kalangi kai toḻum ninṟu ivaḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ivaḷ – she; pinnum – (with more distress than before) again; ilangai – lankā (where māli et al lived); seṟṟavanē – Oh one who destroyed!; ennum – said; valam koḷ – having strength; puḷ – periya tiruvadi (garudāḻvār); uyarttāy – Oh one who is having as flag and vehicle!; ennum – said; uḷḷam – heart; malanga – becoming vexed; vem – hot; uyirkkum – breathe; kaṇṇīr – tears; miga – abundance; kalangi – with bewildered knowledge; ninṟu – thinking (that he is coming); kai toḻum – performs anjali (joining the palms to pray)

**Перевод:**

**She again said with great distress “Oh one who destroyed lankā! Oh one who is having the strong garuda as flag and vehicle!”; But since he did not arrive, her heart became vexed, started breathing out hot air, with abundance of tears and becoming bewildered, she performed anjali (joining the palms to pray) thinking that he is coming.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fourth pāsuram – parānkuśa nāyaki‘s mother says “after sustaining herself for a little while on hearing from me about śrī rāma, again unable to bear the sorrow, she started blabbering and praying”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, she felt distressed speaking about his favours to everyone.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*In the fourth pāsuram – parānkuśa nāyaki‘s mother says “She called out to him highlighting his favours to people in historical times and since such emperumān did not come to help her, she became pained”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Fourth pāsuram – parānkuśa nāyaki‘s mother says”that he destroyed rāvaṇa’s lankā” is not his natural quality; it only happens some times; unable to bear that parānkuśa nāyaki repeats the same incident. இலங்கை செற்றவனே, என்னும், பின்னும் வலம் கொள் புள் உயர்த்தாய்! என்னும், உள்ளம் மலங்க வெவ்வுயிர்க்கும், கண்ணீர் மிகக் கலங்கி கை தொழும் நின்று இவளே ilangai seṟṟavanē ennum pinnum valam koḷ puḷ uyarttāy! ennum uḷḷam malanga vevvuyirkkum  kaṇṇir migak kalangi kai toḻum ninṟu ivaḷē*

- *ilangai seṟṟavanē ennum* – two explanations:
   - parānkuśa nāyaki said “Oh one who helped me before!” (She is saying this to her mother to emphasise that helping others is natural quality for him). She is calling out to him as if he helped her before and not helping now.
   - parānkuśa nāyaki said “Do you have to build a bridge, lift a mountain (to bring herbs to bring back lakśmaṇa’s consciousness) or draw an arrow (to fight) on the bow? What hurdle is there to come to me?” Whatever her mother said to get her to leave [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), she is using the same for holding on to him further.
- *pinnum …* – Further, she said “you are having the entourage (garuda) to help like someone having a water jug at a higher level to feed water for thirsty persons”. This indicates – having the able garuda in his flag or having garuda as his vehicle. Even though garuda is present (who can bring him to her), since he is not coming, as if her heart is taken away from her, she is heaving very hot air as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 17.29 “*dahantīmiva ni:śvāsairvrukśāt pallava dāriṇa: …* ” (hanuman saw sītā pirātti who looked like burning down the trees, which are having fresh leaves and are in neck deep water, with her hot breath …).
- *kaṇṇīr miga* – Whatever started as heavy breathing, turned into tears.
- *kalangit toḻum* – beloved (while in separation) would usually not be praying with pristine knowledge (she will be bewildered).
- *ivaḷē* – she, who is so great to be prayed by him, is now herself praying for him.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.4.5. Ival irap pagal

*ivaḷ irāp pagal vāy verīit tana kuvaḷai oṇ kaṇṇa nīr koṇḍāḷ vaṇḍu tivaḷum taṇ am tuḻāy kodīr ena tavaḷa vaṇṇar tagavugaḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ivaḷ – (such distinct) she; irāp pagal – without distinguishing between day and night; vāy vereei – blabbering (to get tuḷasi); tana – her; kuvaḷai – water-lily like; oṇ – beautiful; kaṇ – eyes; nīr – sad tears; koṇḍāḷ – had; vaṇḍu – bees; tivaḷum – (having drunk honey and) shining (like someone who applied chemicals); taṇ am tuḻāy – divine tuḷasi; kodīr – not giving; tavaḷa vaṇṇar – you who is pure natured (towards your devotees); tagavugaḷ – qualities such as compassion etc; ena – In what manner they exist?

**Перевод:**

**My distinct daughter without distinguishing between day and night was blabbering (to get tuḷasi); when she did not get that, her water-lily like beautiful eyes became filled with tears; you, who are pure natured (towards your devotees), are not giving your divinely shining tuḷasi which has shining bees; In what manner your qualities such as compassion etc exist?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fifth pāsuram – parānkuśa nāyaki‘s mother censures emperumān saying “You are not showing your mercy for this girl who is in such grief; is this the nature of your mercy?”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, parānkuśa nāyaki‘s mother is saying “You are so pure, yet you are like this!”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Fifth pāsuram – parānkuśa nāyaki‘s mother says that emperumān is merciless since he is not coming  even after seeing her suffering. இவள் இராப் பகல் வாய் வெரீத் தன குவளை ஒண் கண்ண நீர் கொண்டாள் வண்டு திவளும் தண் அம் துழாய் கொடீர் என தவள வண்ணர் தகவுகளே? ivaḷ irāp pagal vāy verīit tana kuvaḷai oṇ kaṇṇa nīr koṇḍāḷ vaṇḍu tivaḷum taṇ am tuḻāy kodīr ena tavaḷa vaṇṇar tagavugaḷē*

- *ivaḷ irāp pagal vāy vereei* – As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 36.44 “*anidras satatam rāma: suptōpica narōttama: \| sītēti madurām vāṇīm vyāharan pratibudyatē \|\|*” (śrī rāma never sleeps, and even if he sleeps he blabbers the sweet word “sītā” and wakes up), [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) should be the one blabbering your name. nampiḷḷai gives further explanation of this ślōkam beautifully. *anidras satatam rāma:* – śrī rāma who is having the wealth of being always engaged in nidrā (deep meditation – yōga nidrā – thinking about his own beauty since he is so attractive to all others), became sleepless. *suptōpi ca* – First saying “*satatam anidra:*” (always sleepless) and then saying “*suptōpi ca*” (if he sleeps) indicates that whether sleeping or awake, he is always thinking about sītā. *narōttama:* – best among men means being very attached to his dear lover.
- *irāp pagal* – Speaking like this since he \[āḻvār\] first spoke in tiruviruttam 1 “*poynninṟa jñānamum*” (first prabandam first pāsuram).
- *vāy vereei* – Not cogent speech (just blabbering); her impressions are from her teacher and she simply repeats the teacher’s words.
- *tana kuvaḷai oṇ kaṇṇa nīr koṇḍāḷ* – the eyes which are supposed to have tears of joy are now having tears of sorrow. She is having tears which would normally be seen in the eyes of those who are caught in her glance. Having tears in her water-lily like beautiful eyes.

What should I do? (asks [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/))

- *vaṇḍu tivaḷum taṇ am tuḻāy kodīr* – you are not giving the fresh tuḷasi garland from your chest after accepting the dry garland from her who is suffering in separation (you should give). Did you accept the tears of the bees to give them your garland? “*tivaḷum*” means being there, moving around, shining.
- *ena* – what are these qualities?
- *tavaḷa vaṇṇar tagavugaḷē* – [embār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/embar/) explains it as [parānkuśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) saying “You who are pure! Where did your compassion etc go?” [bhattar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/parasara-bhattar/) explains it as parānkuśa nāyaki saying (censuring [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) on his lack of compassion) “A few persons like you will be sufficient for weak women to perish”.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.4.6. Tagavudaiyavane

*tagavu udaiyavanē! ennum pinnum miga virumbum pirān! ennum enadu aga uyirkku amudē! ennum uḷḷam uga urugi ninṟu uḷ ulē*

**Пословный перевод:**

uḷḷam – heart; uga – to be broken; urugi – (her true nature becoming) melted like water; uḷ uḷē – in her; ninṟu – being such; tagavu – qualities such as krupā etc (to give me joy); udaiyavanē – one who has; ennum – says; pinnum – not stopping with that; miga – more and more; virumbum – liked by; pirān – one who bestows favours; ennum – says; enadu – my; aga uyirkku – for antarātmā (soul); amudē – eternal unsurpassed sweet (nectar); ennum – says

**Перевод:**

**Being herself who is melted like water to have a broken heart, parānkusa nāyaki says “Oh one who has qualities like krupā (mercy) etc to be enjoyed by me!” Not stopping with that, she says “Oh one who is very likable and who bestows favours (to all)!”and “Oh one who is eternal unsurpassed sweet nectar for me! (soul)”.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the sixth pāsuram – parānkuśa nāyaki‘s mother says “I started finding faults in emperumān‘s qualities and unable to bear it she started speaking about his qualities and became immersed in them”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, parānkuśa nāyaki‘s mother says “my daughter being very weak, starts speaking about your most enjoyable nature and keeps repeating about that”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Sixth pāsuram – Seeing her daughter’s exhaustion, parānkuśa nāyaki‘s mother said “emperumān is merciless”; unable to bear that, parānkuśa nāyaki said “tagavudaiyavanē” (merciful) – mercy is his intrinsic quality. தகவு உடையவனே! என்னும் பின்னும் மிக விரும்பும் பிரான்! என்னும் எனது அக உயிர்க்கு அமுதே! என்னும் உள்ளம் உக உருகி நின்று உள் உளே tagavu udaiyavanē! ennum pinnum miga virumbum pirān! ennum enadu aga uyirkku amudē! ennum uḷḷam uga urugi ninṟu uḷ ulē*

- *tagavu udaiyavanē ennum* – Alas! How can we say that there is no mercy deep in his heart? It is only our fault (that he is not coming). parānkuśa nāyaki is so attached to [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) that she shows her love for him as if he comes at once in front of her to shut the mouth of the mother who was saying “*tagavillai*” (he has no mercy).
- *pinnum miga virumbum* – she is saying as if [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is in front of her (uru veḷippādu – visualizing the form of emperumān being in front of āḻvār even in his absence).
- *pirān ennum* – What is the favour done by him in separation? He did not give an opportunity for the mother to further worry about her separation and appeared in front of her. parānkuśa nāyaki wonders “What a great favour is this!”
- *enadu aga uyirkku amudē ennum* – uyir is explained as ātmā here. She says “One who is enjoyable for my ātmā”. amudu – amruta – nectar which gives immortality. Here [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is explained as the nectar which saves the eternal jīvātmā from being destroyed. She is speaking the words which are generally spoken while being together enjoying each other.
- *uḷḷam uga urugi ninṟu* – Mind which does not have a form, assumed a form and melted and became lost fully. This is understood from the expressions.
- *uḷ uḷē* – vācā magōcaram (beyond the capacity of words). It can also be explained as “melting more and more”.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.4.7. Ullul avi

*uḷ uḷ āvi ularndu ularndu ena vaḷḷalē! kaṇṇanē! ennum pinnum veḷḷa nīrk kidandāy! ennum ena kaḷvi tān patta vanjanaiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ena kaḷvi – she who has deceit (of concealing the changes of her heart); tān patta – the acts of emperumān which trapped her; vanjanai – the deceptive actions; uḷ uḷ – that which is staying inside the heart; āvi – in-dwelling soul (which cannot be dried); ularndu ularndu – became very dry; ena – for me to whom you have given yourself fully; vaḷḷalē – Oh most generous person!; kaṇṇanē – Oh kriṣṇa (who is epitome of easily accessibility); ennum – says; pinnum – further; veḷḷa nīr – (to readily incarnate) in the ocean filled with water; kidandāy – Oh one who rested!; ennum – says

**Перевод:**

**parānkuśa nāyaki who is deceptive in hiding the acts of emperumān which trapped her through his deceitful actions and her ātmā which resides inside her heart became very dry; she calls out “Oh most generous person who has given yourself fully to me! Oh kriṣṇa who is epitome of easily accessibility” and further says “Oh one who rested in the ocean filled with water”. She is saying that emperumān‘s bed (where he is resting) belongs to her (as his beloved).**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the seventh pāsuram – parānkuśa nāyaki‘s mother speaks about her daughter’s exhaustion and how emperumān showed his qualities and cheated her.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, parānkuśa nāyaki‘s mother quotes her daughter saying “Oh one who is readily available to help those who request such help!”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Seventh pāsuram – parānkuśa nāyaki‘s mother says “By showing his qualities, emperumān cheated my daughter who conceals her heart from everyone and made her call out for him loudly”. உள் உள் ஆவி உலர்ந்து உலர்ந்து என வள்ளலே! கண்ணனே! என்னும் பின்னும் வெள்ள நீர்க் கிடந்தாய் என்னும் என கள்வி தான் பட்ட வஞ்சனையே uḷ uḷ āvi ularndu ularndu ena vaḷḷalē! kaṇṇanē! ennum pinnum veḷḷa nīrk kidandāy! ennum ena kaḷvi tān patta vanjanaiyē*

- *uḷḷuḷ āvi* – ātmā which bears/holds the heart which is an internal part; Such [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) ([parānkuśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)) dried up like a leaf in separation from [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/). It is said in [bhagavat gītā](http://githa.koyil.org/) 2.24 “*accēdyōyam adāhyōyam aklēdya: aśōśya Eva ca*” (ātmā cannot be cut, cannot be burnt, cannot be soaked in water, cannot be dried) – parānkuśa nāyaki says that even such quality of ātmā is lost (since she (herself) has dried up in separation). Does it mean that her body dried first and then her soul dried later? No – since this is based on intrinsic love for [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) and separation from him, first ātmā became dry which reflected in her body later.

Like a thirsty person, swallows camphor block to quench the thirst ([parānkuśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/), speaks about [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s qualities to subdue her suffering),

- *ena vaḷḷalē kaṇṇanē ennum* – She says “in such condition, you ([kriṣṇa](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)) who will present yourself at my disposal (since kriṣṇa presented himself to the covherd boys and girls)”.
- *pinnum veḷḷa nīrk kidandāy ennum* – Further, as said  in śrī viṣṇu darmam 40th adyāyam “…*tāpārtō jalaśāyanam…*” (those who are trapped in difficulties, will be relieved from miseries by meditating upon kśīrābdi nātan – one who is resting in the ocean) – you have arrived and mercifully rested in kśīrābdi to help me. This posture makes her think that they are in bed together (out of great attachment).
- *ena kaḷvi* – She is going through much distress by hiding what is happening in her heart!
- *tān patta* – One who said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 66.10 “*na jīvēyam kśaṇamapi*” (I cannot even survive for a moment in separation from sītā) is without any emotional change and she ([parānkuśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)) has become so emotionally affected!
- *vanjanai* – Big army (kaurava army) loses to small army (pāṇḍava army) by mischief only. Just like he (kriṣṇa) changed day into night, declared “I won’t touch any weapons” and used it (during mahābhārata battle), here he deceived parānkuśa nāyaki.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.4.8. Vanjane ennum

*vanjanē! ennum kai toḻum ena nenjam vēva nedidu uyirkkum viṟal kanjanai vanjanai seydīr ummait tanjam enṟu ivaḷ pattanavē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vanjanē – Oh deceptive one (one pretends to be humble)!; ennum – says; kai toḻum – (Considering out of love-anger “should I not worship him for such deception?”) folds her palms and worships; tana nenjam – her heart; vēva – to burn; nedidu uyirkkum – breathes deeply/heavily; viṟal – prideful; kanjanai – kamsa; vanjanai seydīr – Oh one who killed him and finished his deception along with him!; ummai – you (who helped the girls in maturā); tanjam enṟu – considering as refuge (for her); ivaḷ – she; pattana – much suffering; E – How!

**Перевод:**

**parānkuśa nāyaki‘s mother looks at her daughter’s suffering – parānkuśa nāyaki says “Oh deceptive one (one pretends to be humble)!” and folds her palms and worships; thinking about their previous togetherness, her heart burns out of her heavy / deep breathing; parānkuśa nāyaki‘s mother says “Oh one who killed the prideful kamsa and finished his deception along with him!” and wonders as to why she is going through much suffering for considering you (who helped the girls in maturā) as refuge (for her)!.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the eighth pāsuram – parānkuśa nāyaki‘s mother asks emperumān “How can my daughter, who accepted you as the refuge, suffer like your enemies?”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, parānkuśa nāyaki‘s mother wonders “even after being fully faithful to emperumān who removes the hurdles of those who are close to him, what kind of suffering she is going through!”*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Eighth pāsuram – parānkuśa nāyaki‘s mother says “Neither you gave her your blissful experience nor you finished her like you finished kamsa; this is the suffering she got for thinking that you are her protector”. வஞ்சனே! என்னும் கை தொழும் என நெஞ்சம் வேவ நெடிது உயிர்க்கும் விறல் கஞ்சனை வஞ்சனை செய்தீர் உம்மைத் தஞ்சம் என்று இவள் பட்டனவே vanjanē! ennum kai toḻum ena nenjam vēva nedidu uyirkkum viṟal kanjanai vanjanai seydīr ummait tanjam enṟu ivaḷ pattanavē*

- *vanjanē ennum* – When the mother says “he cheated you”, parākuśa nāyaki cannot bear that; she said “even when I said ‘no’, you deceived me and being most generous, accepted me at your divine feet”.  His nature is explained in tiruvāimoḻi 1.7.7 “*tānotti vandu en tani nenjai vanjittu ūnotti ninṟu en uyiril kalandu iyal*” (approaching me, deceiving my heart, staying close to my body, he mixed inside me). Thus she said “Oh generous one who deceived me even without my knowledge and accepted me at your divine feet!”.
- *kai toḻum* – Being grateful for being cheated, she salutes him.
- *tana nenjam vēva nediduyirkkum* – Still she is unable to bear the situation even after convincing her mother who was finding faults in [emperumān.](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) She breathes heavily such that her heart burns (due to intense emotions); śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 15.18 “*tatō malinasamvītām rākśasībhis samāvrutām \|  upavāsakruśām dīnām ni:śvasantīm puna: puna: \|\|*” (Thereafter, (hanuman saw) sītā pirātti who was wearing ragged clothes, surrounded well by rākśasis, looking lean due to abstaining from eating, fearful and frequently breathing heavily). Previously she said in 4th pāsuram “*uḷḷam malanga*” – cutting into pieces; in 7th pāsuram she said “*uḷḷuḷ āvi ularndu ularndu*” – drying; here she says “*nenjam vēva*” – burning with fire; \[These relate to [bhagavat gītā](http://githa.koyil.org/) 2.24 “*accēdyōyam adāhyōyam aklēdya: aśōśya Eva ca*” ([ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) cannot be cut, cannot be burnt, cannot be soaked in water, cannot be dried) – i.e., her ātmā is suffering so much\].
- *viṟal kanjanai vanjanai seydīr* – you destroyed the prideful kamsa. You defeated the one who wanted to defeat you. Would you act the same way with devotees and others? \[i.e., you get defeated by devotees like mother yaśodā and you defeat your enemies like kamsa – but now you seem to be desirous to defeat my daughter who is your devotee\].
- *ummait tanjan enṟu* – [parānkuśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s mother is quoting her daughter “being fully surrendered to [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)” – but the mood of parānkusa nāyaki is such that she is saying “I have unfortunately surrendered unto you”. Looking at her daughter’s state, it looks as though she is saying that she has surrendered to a cruel person though she has surrendered to [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is the protector of all.
- *ivaḷ pattanavē* – The torture you are giving to her seems as lengthy as mahābhāratam (which is a huge epic). You have not made her to be like samsāris (since she feels even your deception is a great favour); you have not given yourself to her like you have done with nityasūris (since her heart is still burning in separation); you have not made her to be like us who have patience and full faith as said by sītā pirātti in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 9.30 “… *tat tasya sadruśam bhavēt*“(śrī rāma himself destroying lankā and rescuing me is that which will fit his nature – so I will wait for his arrival) \[Generally, mothers are supposed to be focused on upāyam (means) – where they wait for [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) to protect us at his will, friends are focused on sambhandam/svarūpam (one’s relationship with bhagavān) and beloved-girl is focused on upēyam (goal of being with bhagavān)\]; you have not killed her like you killed kamsa. Instead of accepting my approach, she has taken up to you directly – how long are you going to make her suffer?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

adiyen saraty ramanuja dasan

## 2.4.9. Patta podu

*patta pōdu eḻu pōdu aṟiyāḷ virai mattu alar taṇ tuḻāy ennum sudar vatta vāy nudi nēmiyīr! numadu ittam enkol iv ēḻaikkē?*

**Пословный перевод:**

patta pōdu – sunset; eḻu pōdu – sunrise; aṟiyāḷ – she does not know; virai – fragrance; mattu – honey; alar – spread well; taṇ tuḻāy – fresh tuḷasi; ennum – says; sudar – radiant; vattam – round; vāy – mouth; nudi – sharpness; nēmiyīr – Oh the one having sudarśana chakra!; numadu – for you (who has the tool to eliminate hurdles and allow in close proximity); ittam – thoughts; ivvēḻaikku – for this poor girl who is desirous; en kol – what?

**Перевод:**

**parānkuśa nāyaki does not know sunset or sunrise (due to lack of sleep, and not having woken up from sound sleep with clear mind). She joyfully says “fresh tuḷasi with well spread fragrance and honey”. Oh one who holds the radiant sudarśana chakra which has round mouth and sharpness! What are your (who has the tool to eliminate hurdles and allow in close proximity) thoughts for this poor girl who is desirous \[of attaining you\]?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the ninth pāsuram – parānkuśa nāyaki‘s mother asks “what are you planning to do in the case of parānkuśa nāyaki who is desiring for you and is suffering permanently, due to separation from you?”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, parānkuśa nāyaki‘s mother asks “You have the tools to protect others – what are your thoughts on her?”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*In the ninth pāsuram – When asked what was parānkuśa nāyaki‘s suffering?, parānkusa nāyaki’s mother explains that suffering in this pāsuram; It is also explained as parānkuśa nāyaki’s mother asking emperumān “What are you planning to do for her who is desiring to see your beautiful hand and the divine disc (in your hand), who did not even know sunrise or sunset and is desiring for you?”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

- *sudar vatta vāy nudi nēmiyīr* –  [periyavāccān piḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/periyavachchan-pillai/) quotes [nanjīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nanjiyar/) saying “sudarśana chakra would keep away from those who like it and finish them by showing its beauty; and it would finish those who hate it by getting close to them and destroying them”.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Ninth pāsuram – When parānkuśa nāyaki‘s mother said “her daughter suffered”, she was asked “What type of suffering?”. She replies to that “She has suffered so much and there is nothing more to suffer further”. பட்ட போது எழு போது அறியாள் விரை மட்டு அலர் தண் துழாய் என்னும் சுடர் வட்ட வாய் நுதி நேமியீர்! நுமது இட்டம் என்கொல் இவ் ஏழைக்கே? patta pōdu eḻu pōdu aṟiyāḷ virai mattu alar taṇ tuḻāy ennum sudar vatta vāy nudi nēmiyīr! numadu ittam enkol iv ēḻaikkē?*

- *patta pōdu eḻu pōdu aṟiyāḷ* – She does not know sunrise and sunset. When asked if she knew anything,
- *virai mattalar taṇ tuḻāy ennum* – She would speak joyfully about the tuḷasi \[which [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is wearing\]; virai – what wonderful fragrance! mattu – what wonderful honey! alar – what wonderful flower! taṇ – what wonderful coolness! and so on. She is saying as said in tiruvāimoḻi 6.7.2 “*ummudaiya pērum tārum oḻiya – aṟiyāḷ*” (She would not know anything beyond your name, garland etc).

Hearing this [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) became too joyful and raised his sudarśana chakra thinking “\[finally\] there is someone who is so attached to me” \[In arumpadam, [bhagavat gītā](http://githa.koyil.org/) ślōkams 7.18 “*udārās sarva ēvaitē*” (all those approach me are generous – for letting me manifest my generosity towards them) and 7.19 “*bahunām janmanām … sa mahātmā sa durlabha:*” (those who accept vāsudēva as everything are great souls and are rare to find)\].

- *sudar vatta vāy nudi nēmiyīr* – Oh one who has radiant, round mouthed, sharp sudarśana chakra in your hand! Why so much adjective for the chakra (when in depressed mood)? Even more than parānkuśa nāyaki, her mother herself became attracted to the beautiful hand holding the chakra and glorifies that with adjectives. Do you use the same tool to finish both your devotees and others? āḻvār himself said in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.7.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/09/thiruvaimozhi-1-7-1-piravith-thuyar/) “*āḻippadai andaṇanai maṟaviyai inṟi manattu vaippārē*” (without forgetting, they keep that pure [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) (who holds the weapon named chakra) in their mind). [āḻvārs](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/azhwars/) are of the nature that they melt on seeing emperumān with his divine hand and chakra.
- *numadu ittam en kol* – Are you planning to finish her like you finished rāvaṇa, hiraṇya et al? Are you planning to let her enjoy the beauty of the divine disc and the divine hand, just like nityasūris? Are you planning to make her forget about her own true nature and about you (bhagavān), and let her roam around like samsāris (worldly people) taking care of their stomachs \[feeding it fully\] and wearing nice clothes ? What are you thinking about her attaining her goal?
- *ivvēḻaikkē* – What are you thinking about this girl who is completely desirous to attain you?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.4.10. Elai pedai

*ēḻai pēdai irāp pagal tana kēḻ il oṇ kaṇṇa nīr koṇḍāḷ kiḷar vāḻvai vēva ilangai seṟṟīr! ivaḷ māḻai nōkku onṟum vāttēnminē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ēḻai – being desirous (even if the goal is unattainable); pēdai – innocent/adolescent girl (who does not listen to my instructions); irāp pagal – without distinguishing between night and day; tana – her; kēḻ – match; il – not having; oṇ – beautiful; kaṇ – eyes; nīr koṇḍāḷ – became tearful; kiḷar – having great superiority (by troubling others); vāḻvu – wealth of rāvaṇa; vēva – like burnt into ashes; ilangai – lankā; seṟṟīr – Oh one who destroyed it!; ivaḷ – parānkuśa nāyaki‘s; māḻai – eyes which look like those of a tender deer; nōkkonṟum – eyes alone; vāttēnmin – please do not destroy them

**Перевод:**

**Being desirous, the beautiful matchless eyes of my innocent (adolescent) daughter who is not distinguishing between day and night have become tearful; Oh one (śrī rāma) who destroyed lankā and burnt the greatly superior rāvaṇa’s wealth into ashes! Just like you helped sītā pirātti, you at least ensure that parānkuśa nāyaki‘s eyes which look like those of a tender deer are protected.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the tenth pāsuram – parānkuśa nāyaki‘s mother lost everything but the beautiful innocent eyes of her daughter; she requests those divine eyes to be retained and not vanquished at the least.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, parānkuśa nāyaki‘s mother says to emperumān “Oh one who has great valour,  who destroys the enemies! I am sustaining myself just by seeing her divine eyes; at least do not vanquish them”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Tenth pāsuram – parānkuśa nāyaki‘s mother gave up everything but her divine daughter’s eyes/form; she requests emperumān to protect them at least. ஏழை பேதை இராப் பகல் தன கேழ் இல் ஒண் கண்ண நீர் கொண்டாள் கிளர் வாழ்வை வேவ இலங்கை செற்றீர்! இவள் மாழை நோக்கு ஒன்றும் வாட்டேன்மினே ēḻai pēdai irāp pagal tana kēḻ il oṇ kaṇṇa nīr koṇḍāḷ kiḷar vāḻvai vēva ilangai seṟṟīr! ivaḷ māḻai nōkku onṟum vāttēnminē*

- *ēḻai* – Even if it is established authentically that the goal is not attainable, still not giving up on it.
- *pēdai* – the state (stage of girl) where one cannot understand that the goal is unattainable; even if I (mother) advise her, her state (adolescence) will not let her accept.
- *irāp pagal than kēḻil oṇ kaṇṇa nīr koṇḍāḷ* – eyes which are meant to have tears of joy only; kēḻ – match, il – not present; so matchless eyes; the eyes, which are so beautiful that after being seen by others, the evil-eye should be removed (druśti removal through hārati) – such eyes have become filled with tears. Like a water-drop in lotus flower, such beautiful form is wasted like “*kāttil eṟitta nilavu*” (moonlight in forest which is not useful for anyone unlike that which is shining in the town which is useful/enjoyable for the residents)! After trying so hard (to get a jīvatmā), losing that at the time of reaping the result! As said in tiruviruttam 11 “*ponnum muttum*” (pon – gold – disease of separation; muttu – pearl – tears) are the result of the hard work (of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/))! Now, she is crying for the loss of emperumān (i.e., losing her by not accepting her) and not for her own.

When there are hurdles to accepting, is just crying for me sufficient (to attain me)?

- *kiḷar …* – Are her hurdles greater than rāvaṇa’s?  As explained in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 1.7 “*udīrṇasya rāvaṇasya*” (powerful rāvaṇa) – his wealth is such that he kept mother (sītā pirātti) and father (śrī rāma) in separation; you destroyed lankā to eliminate such wealth/power. When you think of destroying something, you destroy it completely without any trace.
- *ivaḷ māḻai nōkku onṟum vāttēnminē* – Now, you have to ensure that her tender eyes are protected.
- *nōkku onṟum vāttēnminē* – she only will die (if you don’t accept her); we only are the losers; if you are going to survive, you ensure that you protect your life and soul (that is [parānkuśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.4.11. Vattamil pugal

*vāttam il pugaḻ vāmananai – isai kūtti vaṇ satakōpan sol – amai pāttu ōr āyirattu ip pattāl – adi sūttal āgum am dāmamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vāttam – (since emperumān appeared in front of her, his worries disappeared) worries; il – not having; pugaḻ – having auspicious qualities; vāmananai – to vāmana; vaṇ – generous; satakōpan – āḻvār; isai – with music; kūtti – added; sol – spoke; amai – having peace (due to fullness in definition); ōr – unique; pāttu – pāsurams (songs); āyirattu – in the thousand; ippattāl – through this decad; adi – at the lotus feet of such vāmana; am – beautiful; dāmam – garland; sūttalāgum – can be submitted

**Перевод:**

**vāmanan emperumān, who has no worries (since his worries got eliminated by appearing in front of āḻvār) and has many auspicious qualities, was spoken with music by nammāḻvār in this peaceful decad among the unique thousand pāsurams; such decad facilitates those who recite it to submit beautiful garland (as service) at the lotus feet of such vāmanan emperumān.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the end – āḻvār says that those who learn this decad can perform kainkaryam of offering garlands to the divine feet of emperumān without having to go through the difficulties which he himself went through.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār mercifully explains that the result of this decad is kainkaryam to emperumān in the form of worshiping him.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*In the end – āḻvār says that those who are able to recite this decad will enter the assembly of nityasūris as he himself prayed and will engage in kainkaryam at the divine feet of sarvēśvaran as explained in tiruviruttam 21 “sūttu namālai” (offering pure garland). வாட்டம் இல் புகழ் வாமனனை – இசை கூட்டி வண் சடகோபன் சொல் – அமை பாட்டு ஓர் ஆயிரத்து இப் பத்தால் – அடி சூட்டல் ஆகும் அம் தாமமே vāttam il pugaḻ vāmananai – isai kūtti vaṇ satakōpan sol – amai pāttu ōr āyirattu ip pattāl – adi sūttal āgum am dāmamē*

- *vāttamil pugaḻ vāmananai* – If he does not appear in front of āḻvār, his glories will be minimised.
- *vāmananai* – One who begged to (mahābali to) get back his own property.
- *isai kūtti* – Just like a flower blossoms with fragrance, these pāsurams blossomed with music/tune.
- *vaṇ satakōpan sol* – Like śrī vālmīki is glorified in śrī rāmāyaṇam bāla kāṇḍam 2.12 “*udāradīr muni:*” (the sage who is having great intelligence) – [nammāḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is most generous – instead of stopping at just enjoying emperumān in his heart, he sang them as pāsurams so that others too can experience the same.
- *amai pāttu ōr āyirattu* – being wholesome in proper words and meanings
- *ippattāl …* – Those who can recite this decad, can perform eternal kainkaryam of offering fresh garlands at emperumān’s divine feet. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s sufferings are due to his desiring to perform kainkaryam and not being able to perform that; just like father’s wealth will automatically be inherited by the son, those who learn this decad need not suffer like āḻvār, and will enter the assembly of nityasūris and experience the bliss (of kainkaryam) as desired (and achieved by āḻvār).

Finally, nampiḷḷai summarizes the contents of this decad briefly.

- In the first pāsuram, [parānkuśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s mother said that [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is naturally helpful towards his devotees considering their danger alone as the trigger for his help, did not come to help her daughter when she was suffering.
- In the second pāsuram, when reminded about the hurdles, she asks “are the hurdles more powerful than bāṇāsura’s thousand arms (which you destroyed)?”.
- In the third pāsuram, she asks “when you are not ready to help my daughter now, why did you help sītā pirātti in a similar manner before?”.
- In the fourth pāsuram, she says “unable to bear the thought of her finding fault in [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), her daughter quotes the same incident to highlight his generosity”.
- In the fifth pāsuram, she says that [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is merciless since he had not arrived even then.
- In the sixth pāsuram, she quotes her daughter “is he not merciful by nature? it is due to our fault that he is not coming now”.
- In the seventh pāsuram, she says “emperumān has mesmerised my daughter so much that, she considers his faults themselves as good qualities”.
- In the eighth pāsuram, she says to emperumān “Look at her sufferings for taking refuge of you”.
- In the ninth pāsuram, she asks emperumān “what are you thinking for her attainment of the goal?”.
- In the tenth pāsuram, she says to emperumān “her beautiful eyes are the only remaining aspect in her; please protect them at the least”.
- In the end, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) explains the result for those who recite this decad and completes the same.
