## 2.5 Andamattu anbu

## 2.5.1. Andamattu anbu

*am dāmatu anbu seydu en āvi sēr ammānukku am dāmam vāḻ mudi sangu āḻi nūl āram uḷa sendāmarait tadangaṇ sengani vāy sengamalam sendāmarai akikkaḷ sempon tiru udambē*

**Пословный перевод:**

andāmattu – in paramapadam; anbu – attachment; seydu – having; en āvi – in my heart (me who is not favourable); sēr – well-placed; ammānukku – to the natural master; am – beautiful; dāmam – having garland; vāḷ – radiant; mudi – crown; sangu āḻi – divine weapons chakra (disc) and Sanka (conch); nūl – yajñōpavītam (sacred thread); āram – divine garland; uḷa – they appeared; kaṇ – divine eyes; sem tāmarait tadam – like a pond with red lotus flowers; sem – reddish; kani – like a ripened fruit; vāy – mouth/lips; sem – reddish; kamalam – like a lotus flower; adikkaḷ – divine feet; sem – reddish; tāmarai – like a lotus flower; tiru udambu – divine body; sem pon – like reddish gold

**Перевод:**

**bhagavān who is the natural master and has attachment towards paramapadam, became well-placed in my heart; manifesting his supremacy, radiant crown having beautiful garland, divine weapons, sacred thread and garland appeared clearly; his eyes look like a pond of reddish lotus flowers; his reddish ripened fruit like mouth/lips resemble a lotus flower; his divine feet look like a lotus flower; his divine body shines like reddish gold.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the first pāsuram, āḻvār speaks about the splendour acquired by emperumān after arriving with all his entourage and uniting with āḻvār as desired by āḻvār himself.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*In the first pāsuram, āḻvār enjoys emperumān‘s beautiful form that is decorated with divine ornaments.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*First pāsuram – āḻvār says that emperumān came and united with him as he desired in tiruvāimoḻi 2.3.10 “adiyārgaḷ kuḻāngaḷai – udan kūduvadu enṟu kolō” (when will I join the assembly of nityasūris agreeing with their principles?) \[Since emperumān’s chakra, thread, garland etc are all nityaśuris, āḻvār’s desire of being together with them is thus fulfilled\]. அம் தாமத்து அன்பு செய்து என் ஆவி சேர் அம்மானுக்கு அம் தாமம் வாழ் முடி சங்கு ஆழி நூல் ஆரம் உள செந்தாமரைத் தடம் கண் செங்கனி வாய் செங்கமலம் செந்தாமரை அடிகள் செம்பொன் திரு உடம்பே am dāmatu anbu seydu en āvi sēr ammānukku am dāmam vāḻ mudi sangu āḻi nūl āram uḷa sendāmarait tadangaṇ sengani vāy sengamalam sendāmarai akikkaḷ sempon tiru udambē*

- *andāmattu anbu seydu* – Showing the same affection to me as shown towards the beautiful land (parampadam). dāmam – stānam \[place\]. Also explained as – As in *mancā: krōśanti* (bed making noise which implies those who are lying on the bed making noise), showing the same affection to me as shown towards nityasūris who are the residents of paramapadam. He showed me the total affection that was shown towards all the residents of nitya vibhūti (paramapadam). [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) himself mercifully said in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.2.6](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/05/thiruvaimozhi-1-2-6-parru-ilan/) “*muṟṟavum ninṟanan*” (firmly attached towards me).
- *en āvi* – it shows that [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) reaches out to him, but [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) shies away from him. Thinking about his previous state, he shied away; but emperumān approaches him with that itself as the reason. Like pouring water on a drought stricken land, emperumān united with my soul which was explained in tiruvāimoḻi 2.4.7 as “*uḷḷuḷ āvi ularndu ularndu*” (ātmā inside the heart which is dried up).
- *sēr* – Like a thirsty person who jumps into a pond, he united with me.

What is the reason for his uniting with me like this?

- *ammānukku* – because he is the natural lord/master; he has natural entitlement to mingle with the residents of both realms viz., nitya vibhūti (paramapadam) and leelā vibhūti (samsāram). Only after accepting [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) as his servant, he became sarvēśvaran (master of all).
- *andāma …* – two explanations:
   - [āḷavandār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/alavandhar/)‘s explanation presented by [tirumālai āṇḍān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/thirumalai-andan) – As desired by āḻvār in [tiruvāimoḻi 2.3.10](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/02/thiruvaimozhi-2-3-10-kalippum-kavarvum/) “*adiyār kuḻāngaḷai udan kūduvadu enṟu kolō*” (when will I be united with nityasūris accepting their principles?) [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) arrived with nityasūris to unite with āḻvār. But how is it that “*āḻi nūī āram*” (chakra, sacred thread, garland) are identified as nityasūris? These nityasūris who are filled with knowledge, assume these forms to manifest their pāratantriyam (total dependence on [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)).
   - [emperumānār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/emperumanar/) presents a different explanation – Before uniting with āḻvār, like [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), his weapons/ornaments too were lacking splendour. On uniting with him, they all became radiant and their existence was well established. Just like when a tree dries up, the leaves, flowers etc will also dry up (when emperumān lacks splendour, his weapons, ornaments etc also lack splendour).
- *andāma vāḻ mudi* – beautiful garland became crowned and lively. Another explanation – vāṇmudi – vāḷ + mudi – vāḷ means radiance, thus it means infinitely radiant crown. dāmam also means tējas (glow). Glowing pāncajanyam (conch), glowing tiruvāḻi (chakra – disc), glowing yajñōpavītam (sacred thread), glowing tiruvāram (garland); In this ways glow is an adjective for all nityasūris.
- *uḷa* – How do they acquire “existence” now? As said in mahōpaniśad “*sa ēkākī na ramēta*” (that śrīman nārāyaṇa was not joyful alone during praḷayam when all ātmās were submerged in him) , before uniting with [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/), emperumān does not even feel the existence of paramapadam.
- *sem tāmarait tadam kaṇ* – the state of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) seeing him to his heart’s full satisfaction. Only after uniting with [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/), his eyes became fresh and expanded/brightened. That which is explained as “*ēkarūpa*” (unchanging) is changing like this. It is said in śrī viṣṇu purāṇam 1.2.1 “*sadaikarūparūpāya*” (having a divine form which matches his true nature) – he does not acquire any change due to karma (like us) \[His changes are due to his divine desire\].
- *sem kani vāy sem kamalam* – the mouth/lips which speak hundreds of sweet words. Beautiful tender (like ripened fruit) lips looked like red lotus flower.
- *sem tāmarai adikkaḷ* – after becoming overwhelmed with the glance (of the eyes) and smile (of the lips), one will naturally fall at the lotus feet.
- *tiru udambē* – after falling at the lotus feet, one will naturally (get to) enjoy the divine body of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/). As said in manu smriti 12.122 “…*rukmābham*…” (one who has a golden form) – his body started shining like gold after uniting with [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.5.2. Tiru udambu

*tiru udambu vān sudar sendāmarai kaṇ kai kamalam tiru idamē mārvam ayan idamē koppūḻ oru idamum endai perumāṟku aranē ō oruvidam onṟu inṟi ennuḷ kalandānukkē*

**Пословный перевод:**

oru(vu) idam onṟu inṟi – without leaving anything; en uḷ – inside me; kalandānukku – one who united; endai perumāṟku – lord of my clan; tiru – laudable; udambu – body/form; vān sudar – in the colour of āditya (sun); kaṇ kai kamalam – divine hands and divine eyes; sem – reddish; tāmarai – fresh like a lotus; mārvam – divine chest; tiru idamē – the abode of śrī mahālakśmi; koppūḻ – navel; ayan – for brahmā; idamē – abode; oruvu idam – the other part; aranē – is rudra himself; Oh! – how amazing!

**Перевод:**

**The laudable form of emperumān who is the lord of my clan, without leaving anything, came inside me and united with me, has sun-like complexion; his divine hands and eyes are reddish and fresh like lotus flower; his divine chest is the abode of śrī mahālakśmi; his navel is the abode of brahmā; his other part is rudra himself; how amazing is this!**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the second pāsuram, āḻvār says “śrī mahālakśmi et al fully depend on sarvēśvaran resting on him; such sarvēśvaran came, united with me with all his limbs and hence became luminous”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār explains the aujjvalyam (radiance) of emperumān who has such beautiful limbs (as explained in previous pāsuram) and who gives his limbs as the abode for brahmā, rudra et al like he is doing to śrī mahālakśmi.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Second pāsuram – āḻvār, after explaining how emperumān became radiant after uniting with him, says “He who sustains brahmā, īśāna (rudra) by giving his body as resting place for them, is sustaining himself by having my body as his (resting place)”. திரு உடம்பு வான் சுடர் செந்தாமரை கண் கை கமலம் திரு இடமே மார்வம் அயன் இடமே கொப்பூழ் ஒருவு இடமும் எந்தை பெருமாற்கு அரனே ஓ ஒருவு இடம் ஒன்று இன்றி என்னுள் கலந்தானுக்கே tiru udambu vān sudar sendāmarai kaṇ kai kamalam tiru idamē mārvam ayan idamē koppūḻ oru idamum endai perumāṟku aranē O oruvidam onṟu inṟi ennuḷ kalandānukkē*

- *tiru udambu vān sudar* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying this based on his observation when [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)  embraced him. Unlike those who say that the supreme lord has no physical body, no wealth/control, āḻvār who is a most-trustworthy person, says “*tiru udambu vān sudar*” (explaining his divine body and opulence). nanjīyar (realising bhattar’s great efforts to transform him) mercifully said “Many engage in sinning by saying that the lord is formless, attribute-less; what a great favour śrī ranganāta has done (through parāśara bhattar) by making sure that I no longer listen to those people!” \[When authenticity of āḻvār is questioned\] [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) divinely blessed āḻvār with pristine knowledge and bhagavān’s form is that which mesmerises āḻvār. As explained in śrī viṣṇu purāṇam 6.5.84 “*iccāgruhītābhimatōrudēha:*” (many forms assumed by bhagavān out of his own desire) – his forms are most dear to himself. To those he values/respects (devotees/jñānis), he presents his divine forms only, as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 1.13 “*ēśa sarvasvabhūtastu …*” (this embrace given to hanuman (by śrī rāma) is equivalent to giving all of himself).
- *vān sudar* – Originally radiant divine form acquired more radiance due to uniting with [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/). It is not like just shining outside and dull inside; it is like thick/dense ghee (which is fully made of ghee) – having abundance of radiance inside and out. As explained in  
   śrī viṣṇu purāṇam 1.9.63 “*tējasām rāsimūrjitam*” (one who shines like collection of radiant rays and who has the valour to demolish his enemies). While [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s divine body is made of pancaśakti (panca upaniśad – divine matter – paramēśti, pumān, visvam, nivrutti, śarvam), here he is glorified as *śādguṇya vigrahan* (divine form made of 6 qualities), to highlight that his qualities are well-revealed in his divine form.
- *sem tāmaraik kaṇ* – Being blessed with divine eyes, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) speaking with his teeth chattering (due to that cool vision).
- *kai kamalam* – As said in hari vamśam “…*karēṇa mrudunā…*” (with the tender hand), the hands which embraced. Why is [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) being repetitive? One who is an expert in stringing pearls, will do it in many different ways. Similarly āḻvār too is enjoying [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) in different ways. \[When one feels cold, automatically the other person would embrace to give warmth – so, emperumān embraces āḻvār seeing his teeth chattering\].
- *tiru idamē mārvam* – the place where [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is embraced by [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) with his hand is his chest – the abode of periya pirāttiyār ([śrī mahālakśmi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/)).
- *ayanidamē koppūḻ* – brahmā who is the creator of the 14 layered planetary system has [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s navel as his abode.
- *oruvidamum endai perumāṟku aranē* – Instead of saying ōridam (one place), [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) said oruvidam (oruvu – leaving/separating) – a place which is separated. The place which is not fit for my lord will be the abode of rudra. Since it is the part where rudra, who is a tāmasa dēvatā (a deity in the mode of ignorance) is, āḻvār is saying it in a manner which indicates that he does not care for his abode.
- *oru idam onṟu inṟi ennuḷ kalandānukkē* – When uniting with me, he united without leaving any part.
- *O* \[as in araṇēyō\] – Before, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) was amazed at [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s śilaguṇam (simplicity) in giving a part of his body to periya pirāttiyār ([śrī mahālakśmi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/)) who fully exists for him and for those dēvatās like brahma, rudra who are focused on worldly aspects. But after seeing emperumān giving himself to āḻvār, āḻvār becomes even more amazed and thinks that emperumān’s previous action of giving his limbs to brahmā, rudra is like supremacy, when compared with him giving his body to āḻvār (which is the top most manifestation of his simplicity).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.5.3. Ennul kalandavan

*ennuḷ kalandavan sengani vāy sengamalam minnu m sudar malaikkuk kaṇ pādam kai kamalam mannu muḻu ēḻ ulagum vayiṟṟin uḷa tannuḷ kalavādadu ep poruḷum tān i(l)laiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

en uḷ – inside me; kalandavan – being united; minnum – shining (due to that bonding); sudar – having radiance; malaikku – one who is like a mountain; sem kani vāy sem kamalam kaṇ pādam kai kamalam – (as explained previously) all his exalted bodily features are shining radiantly; mannum – firmly; muḻu – full; ēḻ ulagum – seven (all) worlds; vayiṟṟin – being in his stomach; uḷa – sustaining; than uḷ – inside him; kalavādadu – those which are not related; ep poruḷum tān – any object; illai – not present

**Перевод:**

**emperumān who united inside me, who is shining radiantly like a mountain, has beautiful exalted bodily features (as previously explained – reddish fruit like mouth, lotus like eyes, feet and hand); all the worlds sustain themselves by firmly and fully being positioned in his stomach; there is no object that exists which is not related with him.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the third pāsuram, āḻvār says “not just rudra et al, emperumān is the abode for all worlds; Such emperumān suffered in separation from me, as all these worlds would suffer in his separation; he united with me and became very splendorous”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says ““just like no entity would exist when removed from him, he thought he did not exist while separated from me; he then united with me and became radiant”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Third pāsuram – āḻvār says “sarvēśvaran who sustains all entities other than himself, sustained himself by holding on to me and united with me”. என்னுள் கலந்தவன் செங்கனி வாய் செங்கமலம் மின்னும் சுடர் மலைக்குக் கண் பாதம் கை கமலம் மன்னும் முழு ஏழ் உலகும் வயிற்றின் உள தன்னுள் கலவாதது எப் பொருளும் தான் இலையே ennuḷ kalandavan sengani vāy sengamalam minnu m sudar malaikkuk kaṇ pādam kai kamalam mannu muḻu ēḻ ulagum vayiṟṟin uḷa tannuḷ kalavādadu ep poruḷum tān i(l)laiyē*

- *en uḷ kalandavan* – Just as it is said in samkśēpa rāmāyaṇam “*agastya brātā*” (brother of sage agastya – is a well-recognisable identity for his brother even over his own name) – being united with [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is the unique identity for [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/). Like “*nārāyaṇan*” and “*vāsudēvan*” (which highlight his supremacy), “*en uḷ kalandavan*” is his name (which highlights his simplicity).
- *sem kani vāy sem kamalam* – the reddish ripened mouth looked like a reddish/fresh lotus flower.
- *minnum sudar malaikku* – Like a huge mountain – as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 2.4.11](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/03/thiruvaimozhi-2-4-11-vattamil-pugazh/) “*vāttamil pugaḻ vāmanan*” (vāmana who has no worries and has auspicious qualities) – when vāmana grew, he became like a mountain and acquired radiance too; [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is identifying [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) as mountain due to his sustaining himself by being firmly placed in the ground and his strong nature.
- *kaṇ pādam kai kamalam* – Like pearl necklace, prepared by an expert in stringing the pearls, will sell for good price, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) too being an expert in such matters, is enjoying [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) feature by feature.
- *mannu muḻu ēḻ ulagum than vayiṟṟin uḷa* – All worlds are depending fully on his sankalpam (divine will) and thus are eternally existing. Though material realm keeps changing, there is continuous existence of this realm in one form or the other, so material realm is eternal too – this is called *pravāha rūpa nityatvam*.
- *than uḷ …* – The object that does not depend on his divine will (if it exists), comes to be called as nāsti (non-existing). But there is no object, that is abrahmātmakam (not having [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) as antaryāmi). He himself said in [śrī bhagavat gītā](http://githa.koyil.org/) 10.39 “… *na tadasti vinā yat syāt …*” (whatever exists, if it does not depend on me, that ceases to exist).
- *than uḷ kalavādadu epporuḷum tān ilaiyē* – When those objects do not depend on him, they are as good as non-existing due to the true nature of all objects (being dependent on him); he feels to be non-existing when separated from [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) due to their loving relationship.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.5.4. Epporulum tanay

*ep poruḷum tān āy maradagak kunṟam okkum appoḻudait tāmaraippūk kaṇ pādam kai kamalam eppoḻudum nāḷ tingaḷ āṇḍu ūḻi ūḻi toṟum appoḻudaikku appoḻudu en ārā amudamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

eppoḻudum – all moments; ennāḷ – all days; ettingaḷ – all months; evvāṇḍu – all years; evvūḻi ūḻi toṟum – all yuga cycles; appoḻudaikku appoḻudu – every such moment; en – being united with me; ārā – unquenchable; amudam – nectar; epporuḷum – all objects; tānāy – feeling satisfied for being the ātmā of everything; maradagak kunṟam okkum – having greatness (in height), complexion and strength like an emerald mountain; appoḻudai – freshly blossomed; tāmaraip pū – like a lotus flower; kaṇ – eyes; appoḻudaik kamala – freshly blossomed lotus flower like; pādam – divine feet; kai – divine hands acquired freshness

**Перевод:**

**Simple transalation (based on vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar‘s 12000 padi)**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fourth pāsuram, āḻvār says “emperumān who united with me has unlimited sweetness which can be enjoyed every moment forever” and becomes delighted.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “such unlimited sweet emperumān became steady after entering my heart”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Fourth pāsuram – When asked “Why are you repeating the same thing (beauty of emperumān) several times?” āḻvār says “I will stop. But could you make emperumān remain the same way always?” எப் பொருளும் தான் ஆய் மரகதக் குன்றம் ஒக்கும் அப்பொழுதைத் தாமரைப்பூக் கண் பாதம் கை கமலம் எப்பொழுதும் நாள் திங்கள் ஆண்டு ஊழி ஊழிதொறும் அப்பொழுதைக்கு அப்பொழுது என் ஆரா அமுதமே ep poruḷum tān āy maradagak kunṟam okkum appoḻudait tāmaraippūk kaṇ pādam kai kamalam eppoḻudum nāḷ tingaḷ āṇḍu ūḻi ūḻi toṟum appoḻudaikku appoḻudu en ārā amudamē*

- *epporuḷum tānāy* – [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is the prakāri (Entity) and all other entities are prakāra (form/attribute) to him and thus all entities are contained in bhagavān. Is he getting affected by an entity which he has no control over? \[No, he is getting affected by [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) who is well within his control, as are all other entities\]
- *maradagak kunṟam okkum* – Previous term (*epporuḷum tānāy*) explains generally that everything is sustained by [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) and everything is his body; here – his specific divine form is explained. In [previous pāsuram](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/03/thiruvaimozhi-2-5-3-ennul-kalandhavan/) “*minnum sudar*“, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) explained the radiance acquired by bhagavān after uniting with him; here, āḻvār explains the divine/distinct form/body which is the abode for that radiance.
- *appoḻudai* – Here [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is repenting for showing lotus flower asan  example previously. If we just compare with lotus flower, even dry flower may be thought about. Here he is emphasising that it is freshly blossomed lotus flower.
- *kaṇ pādam* – *kāṇ* – eyes which induce the relationship with him; *pādam* – divine feet – when the relationship is realised, this is where the focus would be.
- *kai kamalam* – (hands) became fresh when they came in contact with [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/). All of these will resemble freshly blossomed lotus flower.
- *eppoḻudum* – momentary joyful experience, joyful experience for a day, joyful experience for a month, joyful experience for a year, joyful experience kalpa (day of brahmā) after kalpa. Even if one enjoys [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) forever, as said previously, emperumān is like nectar which cannot be consumed just once; we would want to consume him again and again. The experience of one moment is unlike the experience next moment. It is not just the experience of oneself which is acquired based on the change in time, place etc., based on the knowledge of the one who is experiencing; here, emperumān himself looks new/fresh every moment.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.5.5. Ara amudamay

*ārā amudamāy al āvi uḷ kalanda kār ār karumugil pōl en ammān kaṇṇanukku nērā vāy sembavaḷam kaṇ pādam kai kamalam pēr āram nīḷ mudi nāṇ pinnum iḻai palavē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ārā amudamāy – being unsurpassed sweet person; al – having nothing (useless); āvi uḷ – in my heart; kalandu – mingled/united; kār – in rainy season; Ar – full; karu mugil pōl – like a dark cloud; en ammān – one who is my lord; kaṇṇanukku – for kriṣṇa; sem – reddish; pavaḷam – coral; vāy – lips; nērādu – incomparable; kamalam – lotus flowers; kaṇ pādam kai – eyes, feet and hands; nērā – incomparable; pēr – huge; āram – garland; nīḷ – tall; mudi – crown; nāṇ – waist string etc; pinnum – and other; iḻai – ornaments; pala – countless

**Перевод:**

**emperumān entered into my heart and mingled with useless me as an unsurpassed sweet person; because of that, my lord kriṣṇa is shining like laden dark cloud in the rainy season; reddish corals are no match for his lips; lotus flowers are no match for his eyes, feet and hands; further, he is wearing countless ornaments such as huge garland, tall crown, waist string and many more.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fifth pāsuram, āḻvār says “There is no comparison for emperumān‘s beauty which was acquired after uniting with me”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Fifth pāsuram – āḻvār was explaining emperumān‘s beauty by citing lotus flower as an example until now; but as he started experiencing emperumān, he realised that lotus flower is no comparison for emperumān; so he now skips the examples and directly explains emperumān. ஆரா அமுதமாய் அல் ஆவியுள் கலந்த கார் ஆர் கருமுகில் போல் என் அம்மான் கண்ணனுக்கு நேரா வாய் செம்பவளம் கண் பாதம் கை கமலம் பேர் ஆரம் நீள் முடி நாண் பின்னும் இழை பலவே ārā amudamāy al āvi uḷ kalanda kār Ar karumugil pōl en ammān kaṇṇanukku nērā vāy sembavaḷam kaṇ pādam kai kamalam pēr āram nīḷ mudi nāṇ pinnum iḻai palavē*

- *ārā amudamāy* – Even if consumed eternally, it will only increase our desire to consume more – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is like such sweet nectar.
- *al āviyuḷ kalanda* – If he is so enjoyable, are those, who enjoy him, equally qualified? \[No\].
- *al āvi* – non-existing entity – You united with me who cannot even be considered as an entity! He neither knows himself \[his greatness\] nor does he know about me \[my lowly nature\].
- *al āvi* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is considering himself lower than [acit (insentient)](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/09/thathva-thrayam-achith-what-is-matter/). Since insentient objects don’t have knowledge, they would not know even if they are separated from [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/); but being a [sentient](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/), which has knowledge, and not achieving the true goal of having that knowledge (true goal being realisation about [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)), [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) considers himself as even lower than insentient.
- *uḷ kalanda* – Did he unite with me like uniting with nityasūris who are best among people? Another explanation – he considered me to be the sweetest nectar and himself as lowly and hence united with me!
- *uḷ kalanda* – united with me so deep that, both of us have merged in each other and looked like a single entity.

When [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) was asked “How did you know that he united with you like this?” āḻvār says that he found that out by observing the divine form of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/).

- *kār Ar karu mugil pōl* – He manifested great joy highlighting that uniting with me is his goal. This is explained as “laden dark cloud in rainy season”. kār – black, it means blackish cloud. [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) with such beautiful form came and united with me.
- *en ammān kaṇṇanukku* – kriṣṇa who acquired me by showing such beautiful form.
- *nērā vāy sem pavaḷam* – īsn’t pavaḷam (pravāḷam – coral) red in complexion? Yes – but to understand the real reddish complexion of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s lips – emperumān’s lips are so red that if we compare his lips’ color with pavaḷam’s color, pavaḷam will look like white. So, no pavaḷam can match emperumān’s lips in complexion.
- *kaṇ pādam kai kamalam nērā* – eyes which gave cool glance, the lotus feet at which one will fall being defeated by such glance, the hands which would lift up and embrace those who fall at his divine feet – for all these, no lotus flower will be a match.
- *pēr āram* – As said in mūnṟām tiruvandādi 55 “*periya varai mārvil pērāram*” (huge garland in mountain-like big chest), the garland which needs to be folded into two to be placed on his divine neck.
- *nīḷ mudi* – his divine crown which is as said in varadarāja stavam 25 “*ādirājya sūcakam”* (that which highlights his supremacy).
- *nāṇ* – a type of gadi sūtram (waist string).
- *pinnum iḻai palavē* – I can only experience these – How can I complete explaining about these?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.5.6. Pala palave

*pala palavē ābharaṇam pērum pala palavē pala palavē sōdi vadivu paṇbu eṇṇil pala pala kaṇḍu uṇḍu kēttu uṟṟu mōndu inbam pala palavē jñānamum pāmbaṇai mēlāṟkēyō*

**Пословный перевод:**

pāmbaṇai mēlāṟku – for the emperumān who united with me, just like having tiruvanantāḻvān (ādiśēśan) as his bed (thus being united with him); paṇbu eṇṇil – when analysing his nature; ābharaṇam – ornaments; pala pala – having many ornaments like crown etc and having many varieties of each of such ornaments; pērum – names; pala pala – many due to his being present as different entities, having many different objects in each category; sōdi – radiantly shining; vadivu – divine spiritual forms; pala pala – many forms such as para (in śrīvaikuṇṭam), vyūha (kśīrābdi – milk ocean) etc and multiple forms in each such category; kaṇḍu uṇḍu kēttu uṟṟu mōndu inbam – all pleasures acquired through the different senses such as eyes, mouth, ears, skin, nose; pala pala – many due to the presence of different entities and different objects in each category; jñānamum – knowledge acquired through such senses; pala pala – also many (like previously explained)

**Перевод:**

**For the emperumān who united with me, just like having tiruvanantāḻvān (ādiśēśan) as his bed (thus being united with him), when analysing his nature, \[we would understand that\] he is having many ornaments like crown etc and having many varieties of each of such ornaments; many names due to his being present as different entities, having many different objects in each category; many radiantly shining divine forms such as para (in śrīvaikuṇṭam), vyūha (kśīrābdi – milk ocean) etc and multiple forms in each such category; many pleasures acquired through the different senses such as eyes, mouth, ears, skin, nose due to the presence of different entities and different objects in each category; and knowledge acquired through such senses are also many (like previously explained).**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the sixth pāsuram – āḻvār enjoys the countless divine ornaments etc of emperumān who united with him.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Sixth pāsuram – āḻvār says “having united with me and not being satisfied, he assumed multiple forms to enjoy me”. பல பலவே ஆபரணம் பேரும் பல பலவே பல பலவே சோதி வடிவு பண்பு எண்ணில் பல பல கண்டு உண்டு கேட்டு உற்று மோந்து இன்பம் பல பலவே ஞானமும் பாம்பு அணை மேலாற்கேயோ pala palavē ābharaṇam pērum pala palavē pala palavē sōdi vadivu paṇbu eṇṇil pala pala kaṇḍu uṇḍu kēttu uṟṟu mōndu inbam pala palavē jñānamum pāmbaṇai mēlāṟkēyō*

- *pala palavē ābharaṇam* – jāti bhēdam (different categories) and vyakti bhēdam (different objects in each category) are present. \[For example: \] Ornaments for hands are many. Even in each category (bracelet) – there may be the one for forehand, another one for upper part of the hand and so on.
- *pērum pala palavē* – While enjoying different qualities/activities of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), different names will come up – some names which highlight his simplicity, other names which highlight his valour and so on.
- *pala palavē sōdi vadivu* – The names lead to many different forms. Since he makes his divine form manifest among many different species \[plant, animal, human, celestial forms\], all such forms would shine radiantly \[*sa u śrēyān bhavati jāyamāna:* – [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) becomes radiant by taking birth since his birth is out of his desire and not out of force\]. Like saubhari riśi \[who assumed 50 different forms to marry 50 different girls\], [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) assumed many different forms to enjoy [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/). Like a [muktātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) would assume many different forms to enjoy [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) \[*sa ēkadā bhavati* …. – muktātmā assumes one form, two form, multiple forms\], bhagavān here assumes many different forms to enjoy me \[role reversal\]
- *paṇbeṇṇil* – while analysing his qualities/states,
- *pala pala …* – pleasures derived through senses by rūpa (seeing), rasa (tasting), śabda (hearing), sparśa (feeling the touch) and grāṇa/ganda (smelling) are many. Also explained as – those which are desirable for eyes, mouth, ear, skin and nose are many.
- *pala palavē jñānamum* – here jñānam can indicate the object of knowledge – i.e., pleasures acquired through the senses as well as the senses themselves which are the tools to acquire the pleasure \[this is explained based on the root meaning of jñānam\]. But can this knowledge be many too? Yes – knowledge will differ based on the object of such knowledge. emperumān being the enjoyer of all matters other than himself, being the knover of such matters and having the greatness of enjoying such matters are explained here.
- *pāmbaṇai mēlāṟkēyō* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is showing an example of an aspect where emperumān is enjoying all such variety of pleasures. ādiśeśan (serpent) is soft (sparśa indriyam – touch); has nice fragrance (grāṇa indriyam – smell), delight to watch (rūpa indriyam – eyes). Like this, all pleasures are present. \[Oh! indicates the manifestation of delight\].

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.5.7. Pambanai mel

*pāmbu aṇai mēl pāṟkadaluḷ paḷḷi amarndaduvum kāmbu aṇai tōḷ pinnaikku āy ēṟu udan ēḻ seṟṟaduvum tēm paṇaiya sōlai marāmaram ēḻ eydaduvum pūm piṇaiya taṇ tuḻāyp pon mudi am pōr ēṟē*

**Пословный перевод:**

pāṟkadaluḷ – In the milk ocean; pāmbu aṇai mēl – on the serpent bed; paḷḷi – resting; amarndaduvum – firmly placed; kāmbu aṇai – Like bamboo; tōḷ – having shoulders; pinnaikkāy – for nappinnaip pirātti; ēṟu ēḻu – seven bulls; udan – at the same time; seṟṟaduvum – killed; tēn – honey; paṇaiya – having branches; sōlai – (due to that) grown like a garden; marāmaram – pipal (peepal) tree; ēḻ – seven; eydaduvum – shot; pū – beautiful; piṇaiya – woven; taṇ – cool; tuḻāy – decorated by tuḷasi; pon – very radiant; mudi – having crown; am – delight to watch; pōr – prideful, being focused on destroying the enemies; ēṟu – Like a bull

**Перевод:**

**emperumān is like a beautiful (delightful to our eyes), prideful bull that is focused on destroying the enemies, wearing a very radiant crown which is decorated by cool, beautifully woven tuḷasi. He is firmly resting on the serpent bed in the milk ocean. He killed the seven bulls at once to marry nappinnaip pirātti. He shot down the seven pipal trees which had honey and many branches which made them look like a garden by themselves.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the seventh pāsuram – āḻvār enjoys the divine activities which were mercifully manifested by emperumān.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār enjoys the divine activities of emperumān which shone nicely after uniting with him.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*In seventh pāsuram – āḻvār enjoys emperumān‘s divine activities.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Seventh pāsuram – āḻvār says “You being the master of nityasūris who have unblemiśed knowledge, rested in kśīrābdi (milk ocean) and assumed the forms of śrī rāma, kriṣṇa et al for me”. பாம்பு அணை மேல் பாற்கடலுள் பள்ளி அமர்ந்ததுவும் காம்பு அணை தோள் பின்னைக்கு ஆய் ஏறு உடன் ஏழ் செற்றதுவும் தேம் பணைய சோலை மராமரம் ஏழ் எய்ததுவும் பூம் பிணைய தண் துழாய்ப் பொன் முடி அம் போர் ஏறே pāmbu aṇai mēl pāṟkadaluḷ paḷḷi amarndaduvum kāmbu aṇai tōḷ pinnaikku āy ēṟu udan ēḻ seṟṟaduvum tēm paṇaiya sōlai marāmaram ēḻ eydaduvum pūm piṇaiya taṇ tuḻāyp pon mudi am pōr ēṟē*

- *pāmbaṇai* – To protect his devotees, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is resting in the milk ocean. \[As he is most tender\] not wanting to be affected by the fluids in the ocean, he is resting on tiruvantāḻvān (ādi śēśan) who has coolness, nice fragrance and is most tender.
- *kāmbu …* – Beautiful shoulder of nappinnaip pirātti resembles bamboo for the circumference and smoothness. To marry such nappinnaip pirātti, kriṣṇa killed the bulls (which were the hurdles for marrying her) together, at once.
- *tēn paṇaiya (tēmbaṇaiya)* – sugrīva mahāraja said “You cannot kill vāli” and to instill confidence in him, he shot down the seven pipal trees which had honey, lots of large branches and grown like a bush which make them difficult to take aim.
- *pū …* – Having nicely woven flowers; being decorated with nicely decorated tuḷasi garland, wearing beautiful divine crown which signifies his supremacy, and after bestowing such wonderful experience to nityasūris and feeling prideful due to that, he is looking like a bull which is ready for a fight. It is also like [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) saying “all of these are done by [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) for me (to enjoy)”.

## 2.5.8. Ponmudi amporerrai

*pon mudi am pōr ēṟṟai emmānai – nāl tadam tōḷ tan mudivu onṟu illāda taṇ tuḻāy mālaiyanai en mudivu kāṇādē ennuḷ kalandānai sol mudivu kāṇēn nān solluvadu en? solleerē*

**Пословный перевод:**

pon – radiant; mudi – having a crown; am pōr ēṟṟai – being very prideful; emmānai – the master who accepted my service (by showing such pride of full independence); nāl – four types of; tadam – huge; tōḷ – having divine shoulders; than – for his greatness; mudivu onṟillāda – having no end; taṇ – cool; tuḻāy mālaiyanai – one who is wearing a divine tuḷasi garland; en mudivu kāṇādē – (like there is no end for his greatness) without seeing my lowliness; en uḷ – in my heart; kalandānai – one who mingled/united; nān – me; sol – to explain through words; mudivu – method; kāṇēn – not seeing; solluvadu – explaining this; en – how?; solleer – (if possible) please do that (he is saying this to worldly people)

**Перевод:**

**emperumān is wearing a radiant crown; showing such prideful form he turned me into his servitor and became my master; he is having four (types of) divine shoulders and has no end to his greatness; his greatness and sweetness are highlighted by his cool divine tuḷasi garland; just like there is no end to his greatness, there is no end to my lowliness too – he entered into the heart of of such lowly me and mingled with me; (while I can understand his glories) I cannot see any method to speak about his glories; āḻvār says to worldly people “like you glorify material joyful aspects, you speak about emperumān‘s glories if possible”.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the eighth pāsuram – āḻvār says “You being unique and beyond the capacity of mind/words and still uniting with me – I cannot explain this great quality of yours”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār mercifully explains the greatness of uniting with emperumān which is beyond the capacity of explanation through words.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Eighth pāsuram. āḻvār says “I cannot speak about this great quality of yours, where you being the leader of the nityasūris who have unblemiśed knowledge, still united with me without checking my lowly nature”. பொன் முடி அம் போர் ஏற்றை எம்மானை – நால் தடம் தோள் தன் முடிவு ஒன்று இல்லாத தண் துழாய் மாலையனை என் முடிவு காணாதே என்னுள் கலந்தானை சொல் முடிவு காணேன் நான் சொல்லுவது என்? சொல்லீரே pon mudi am pōr ēṟṟai emmānai – nāl tadam tōḷ than mudivu onṟu illāda taṇ tuḻāy mālaiyanai en mudivu kāṇādē ennuḷ kalandānai sol mudivu kāṇēn nān solluvadu en? solleerē*

- *pon mudi am pōr ēṟṟai* – Having a crown which shows his control over both vibhūtis (realms – paramapadam and samsāram) that manifests his lordship over all.
- *emmānai* – by showing his ultimate lordship, he placed me in my ultimate servitude.
- *nāl tadam tōḷ …* – four, flourishing shoulders; while speaking about [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is wearing tuḷasi garland, even the vēdam gives up saying “*yatō vācō nivartantē*” (unable to comprehend the glories of paramātmā, speech and mind give up and return). tuḷasi garland is the identity of the entity whose glories cannot be comprehended.
- *en mudivu ….* – Like there is no limit for the goodness in [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), there is no limit to the faults in [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/).
- *en mudivu kāṇādē* – Not seeing my level. As said in śrīviṣṇu sahasranāmam “*avijñātā*” (ignorant), ignoring my faults and closing his eyes, he came and mingled with me. Another explanation – unable to witness me trying to finish myself in separation that was highlighted in [tiruvāimoḻi 2.4](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/03/thiruvaimozhi-2-4-adiyadi/) “*ādiyādi*“, he came and united with me.
- *sol mudivu kāṇēn nān* – Trying to explain this quality of mingling with me (sauśeelyam), I went through the same difficulty as vēdam which tried to explain [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s quality named “*ānandam*” (bliss) \[in taittirīya upaniśad ānandavalli\]. Also explained as [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) saying “When he allows me to experience him, the taste which I acquire out of this can only be experienced and cannot be explained to others”.
- *solluvadu en solleerē* – Oh \[worldly\] people! You who are able to share your worldly experiences! Are you able to explain his glories?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.5.9. Solleer en ammanai

*solleer en ammānai en āvi āvi tanai ellai il sīr en karumāṇikkac cudarai nalla amudam peṟaṟku ariya vīdum āy alli malar virai ottu āṇ allan peṇ allanē*

**Пословный перевод:**

en – for me; ammānai – being the lord; en āvi – for my soul; āvi tanai – being the soul; ellai il – boundless; sīr – having qualities such as saukumāryam (beauty) etc; en karumāṇikkac cudarai – one who allowed me to experience his blue emerald like form; solleer – speak (if it is possible to do so for all of you together); nalla – being distinct (from worldly nectar); amudam – eternally sweet nectar; peṟaṟku – to attain; ariya – difficult; vīdumāy – the controller of the eternal land (of paramapadam – spiritual realm); alli malar – in water lily flower; virai ottu – most enjoyable like the fragrance; peṇ allan – like he is different from women (due to his being a man); āṇ allan – he is different from all men other than himself (due to his being puruśōttama – supreme man)

**Перевод:**

**Do so if you can speak about emperumān who is my lord, who is the soul of my soul (paramātmā – in-dwelling super soul), who is having boundless qualities such as beauty etc and who allowed me to experience his blue emerald like form; (when asked, the reason(s) for being unable to speak about him) he is eternally sweet nectar which is distinct from worldly nectar; he is the controller of paramapadam (spiritual realm) which is difficult to attain (even for great yōgis); he is most enjoyable like the fragrance in water lily flower; just as he is different from women (due to his being a man), he is also different from all men other than himself (due to his being puruśōttama – supreme man) .**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the ninth pāsuram – As āḻvār was unable to speak about emperumān, he completely stopped speaking; subsequently, out of desire (to speak about him), he calls everyone and starts engaging in a conversation with them.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “If you are able to speak about the unsurpassed sweet emperumān, please do so”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*In the ninth pāsuram – āḻvār who withdrew after deciding that he cannot speak about emperumān, out of utmost desire calls everyone and starts speaking to them.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Ninth pāsuram. āḻvār will not stop speaking about him saying “I cannot”.  He says to samsāris (worldly people) “Can you all together speak about my lord?” \[Previously āḻvār said no one can speak about emperumān; now he is calling out again to see if there is some intelligent ones who may be capable of doing that\]. சொல்லீர் என் அம்மானை என் ஆவி ஆவி தனை எல்லை இல் சீர் என் கருமாணிக்கச் சுடரை நல்ல அமுதம் பெறற்கு அரிய வீடும் ஆய் அல்லி மலர் விரை ஒத்து ஆண் அல்லன் பெண் அலனே solleer en ammānai en āvi āvi tanai ellai il sīr en karumāṇikkac cudarai nalla amudam peṟaṟku ariya vīdum āy alli malar virai ottu āṇ allan peṇ allanē*

- *solleer en ammānai* – Oh ones who are able to enjoy worldly (lowly) pleasures and explain about that! Can you speak about him?
- *en ammānai* – [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) who manifested his divine qualities and activities and thus engaged me in proper servitude towards him.
- *en āvi āvi tanai* – one who is the antarātmā (in-dwelling super soul) of my [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) (soul).
- *ellai …* – Even if one can understand the limit of the qualities of his divine svarūpam (true nature) \[such as jñānam, ānandam etc\], one can never understand the limit of the qualities of his divine vigraham (form) \[such as saukumāryam etc\]. Also explained as [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) saying “[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who allowed me to experience his unlimited auspicious qualities of the divine svarūpam (true nature) and  his cool divine blue emerald like beautiful form”.
- *nalla amudam* – eternal and most enjoyable nectar. Also explained as best among available nectar.
- *peṟaṟku ariya vīdumāy* – being the mōkśa puruśārtam (liberation – the fourth goal desired by [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)s \[dharma (righteousness), arta (wealth); kāma (enjoyment) and mōkśa (liberation) are the four goals desired by ātmā\].
- *alli malar virai ottu* – For his sweetness, he is comparable to the fragrance of the water lily flower.
- *āṇ allan peṇ allan* – Not like any other man.  Just like he is unlike any other woman, he is also unlike any other man. This indicates that he cannot be compared to any one.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.5.10. An allan

*āṇ allan peṇ allan allā aliyum allan kāṇalum āgān uḷan allan illai allan pēṇungāl pēṇum uru āgum allanum ām kōṇai peridu udaittu em pemmānaik kūṟudalē*

**Пословный перевод:**

āṇ – male; allan – not being; peṇ – female; allan – not being; allā – useless; aliyum – gender-less; allan – not being; kāṇalum – to be seen (using the pramāṇams that show them); āgān – unable; uḷan allan – does not exist (for those who are unfavourable); illai allan – exists – he is not void (for those who are favourable); pēṇum – when being devoted (as devotees); kāl – at times; pēṇum – desired (by those); uru āgum – assuming a form; allanum āy – (for those who don’t have such desire) he will not manifest his form; em pemmānai – my master; kūṟudal – while explaining (me who has seen this nature of him as shown by him); peridu – very; kōṇai udaittu – difficult

**Перевод:**

**He is unlike male; he is unlike female; He is unlike the gender-less individuals who are not of any use \[in the context of procreation\]. He is also unable to be seen (using the pramāṇams/tools such as eyes that show these differences such as male, female and so on); He does not exist (for those who are unfavourable). He exists and is not void (for those who are favourable); for those devotees who desire to see him in specific forms, he assumes those forms; for those others (who don’t desire to see him) he will not manifest his form; While \[I am\] explaining about my master \[who showed his such nature to me\], I feel great difficulty in doing so due to these aforementioned reasons.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the tenth pāsuram – āḻvār highlights emperumān‘s distinct nature which is different from all entities such as male, female, gender-less individuals and says that he cannot speak about the bonding of such emperumān with him.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says that it is very difficult to explain emperumān‘s nature.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*In the tenth pāsuram – āḻvār says “even if I can speak about his greatness, I cannot speak about such emperumān uniting with me”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Tenth pāsuram. āḻvār says “It is very difficult to speak about the nature of emperumān who united with me”. ஆண் அல்லன் பெண் அல்லன் அல்லா அலியும் அல்லன் காணலும் ஆகான் உளன் அல்லன் இல்லை அல்லன் பேணுங்கால் பேணும் உரு ஆகும் அல்லனும் ஆம் கோணை பெரிது உடைத்து எம் பெம்மானைக் கூறுதலே āṇ allan peṇ allan allā aliyum allan kāṇalum āgān uḷan allan illai allan pēṇungāl pēṇum uru āgum allanum Am kōṇai peridu udaittu em pemmānaik kūṟudalē*

- *āṇ allan …* – He is unlike the worldly men; similarly he unlike the worldly women; he is unlike the gender-less individuals who are not of any use. This is explained in rig vēdam āraṇyam 2.2 “*nainam vācā striyam bruvannainamastrīpumān bruvan \| pumāmsam na bruvannainam vadan vadati kaścana \|\| a iti brahma \|\|*” (A man who explains this [paramātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/), cannot explain him in feminine terms. He cannot explain paramātmā as gender-less individual who is different from male and female. He cannot explain paramātmā in masculine terms; in this manner, [parabrahmam (bhagavān)](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is identified as “a” (akāram)). This is also explained in śrī bhāgavatam 8.3.24 “*sa vai na dēvāsuramartyatiryangna strī na śaṇḍō na pumānna jantu: \| nāyam guṇa: karma na sanna cāsanniśēdaśēśō jayatādaśēśa: \|\|*” (That [paramātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is not present as dēva (celestial beings), asura (demoniac beings), martya (human beings), tiryang (animals); He is not present as a woman; he is not present as a gender-less individual; he is not present as any other object outside these three types (male, female and gender-less). He is not present as a quality; he is not present as an activity. He is not sat ([jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) \[who does not change but\] whose knowledge can reduce); he is not present as asat ([acētanam](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/09/thathva-thrayam-achith-what-is-matter/) – matter which itself transforms). That [sarvēśvaran](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) who is different from all these aforementioned entities and who is also present as everything due to his immense potency, has to appear for my liberation). When [bhattar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/parasara-bhattar/) was thus explaining, a tamiḻan (a person who is proficient in tamiḻ language) questioned “jīyā (Oh great personality)! if he is not like any of the 3 types (male, female, gender-less) which are seen in this world, is he śūnyam (void – non-existing)?”. [bhattar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/parasara-bhattar/) mercifully replied “Oh son! you seem to be ignorant about the grammar in the word construction of the pāsuram. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is not saying ‘*āṇ allan* (He is not a man), *peṇ allaḷ* (She is not a woman), *allā aliyum alladu* (It is not a gender-less entity)’; Since [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying ‘*allan, allan, allan*‘ (all of which indicate masculine nature) – here, the word puruśōttaman (best among men – supreme man) is indicated. isn’t it?”. By saying “*āṇ allan peṇ allan …*“, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) establishes that bhagavān is neither like some other entity within each type (not like any other male) nor is he like another type (not like another female).
- *kāṇalum āgān* – He cannot be understood through the pramāṇams (tools – eyes etc) which make us see these differences such as male, female etc. This also establishes that there is no equality between the tools that show him and these other aspects.
- *uḷan allan* – for those who have not surrendered unto him – he is not existing.
- *illai allan* – for those who have surrendered unto him – he is not void. This is explained further.
- *pēṇum kāl pēṇum uru āgum* – When some one prays to him “Please take birth as our son”, he does so and says “… *sapalam dēvi sajjātam jātōham yat tavōdarāt*” (As prayed by you desiring for a son previously, Oh mother dēvaki! That desire has been fulfilled for you now; by that reason I have been born through your womb). Also explained as – when someone desires for him, he will appear in a manner that those who prayed for him will have to carefully protect him or take care of him.
- *allanum Am* – Even when he makes himself available like this, those unfavourable persons such as śisupāla will not be able to understand/approach him.
- *kōṇai peridu …* – To speak about [sarvēśvaran](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s nature of revealing so much to me, is very difficult.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

adiyen saraty ramanuja dasan

## 2.5.11. Kurudal onru

*kūṟudal onṟu ārāk kudak kūtta ammānai kūṟudalē mēvik kurugūrc catakōpan kūṟina andādi ōr āyirattuḷ ip pattum kūṟudal vallār uḷarēl kūduvar vaikundamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

onṟu – one quality; kūṟudal – if spoken; ārā – cannot be fully spoken; kudak kūttu – \[emperumān who is having\] auspicious qualities such as śeeḷa (simplicity) which is manifested by him dancing like a cow-herd boy with pots; ammānai – master; kūṟudal – to explain (as is); mēvi – set out; kurugūrc catakōpan – āḻvār (who became knowledgeable and devoted to emperumān by the grace of emperumān); kūṟina – mercifully explained; andādi – antādi style (First word/sentence of a pāsuram relates to the last word/sentence of previous pāsuram) in which the structure of the pāsurams cannot be corrupted; ōr – unique/matchless; āyirattuḷ – among the thousand pāsurams; ip pattum – this decad; kūṟudal – to recite/speak; vallār – able; uḷarēl – if present; vaikundam – paramapadam (spiritual realm); kūduvar – reach

**Перевод:**

**Even if attempted, our lord emperumān‘s qualities such as śeeḷam (simplicity) which are manifested through kudak kūttu etc, cannot be spoken of fully. nammāḻvār who was blessed by emperumān with knowledge and devotion, set out to speak (as it is) about such emperumān’s qualities; āḻvār thus sang this decad among the distinct/matchless thousand pāsurams which are in antādi style which cannot be corrupted. Those who are able to recite these 10 pāsurams will reach paramapadam.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*āḻvār says “those who practice this decad will enjoy emperumān in paramapadam as highlighted in this decad”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*āḻvār explains attaining parampadam as the result for reciting this decad.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*In the end – āḻvār says “if there are people who can practice this decad, they will reach parampadam and enjoy eternally”. கூறுதல் ஒன்று ஆராக் குடக் கூத்த அம்மானைக் கூறுதலே மேவிக் குருகூர்ச் சடகோபன் கூறின அந்தாதி ஓர் ஆயிரத்துள் இப் பத்தும் கூறுதல் வல்லார் உளரேல் கூடுவர் வைகுந்தமே kūṟudal onṟu ārāk kudak kūtta ammānai kūṟudalē mēvik kurugūrc catakōpan kūṟina andādi ōr āyirattuḷ ip pattum kūṟudal vallār uḷarēl kūduvar vaikundamē*

- *kūṟudal …* – When set out to speak about his nature, as mentioned in taittiriya upaniśat ānandavalli, it is impossible to completely explain his nature. Here [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is not speaking about his supremacy which cannot be explained; āḻvār is actually saying that [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s act of dancing with pots as a cow-herd boy cannot be explained fully.
- *ammānai* – One who manifested his kudak kūttu, thereby making me fully exist for him. mahābhāratam bhīśma parva “*viśnōr jiṣṇōr vasudēvātmajasya*” (viṣṇu (omni-present), jiṣṇu (victorious) who appeared as the divine son of vasudēva).
- *kūṟudalē mēvi* – vēdam withdrew itself highlighting inability to speak about [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) – but [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) pursues such task and sets out to do it nicely. In the [eighth pāsuram](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/03/thiruvaimozhi-2-5-8-ponmudi-amporerrai/) he said “*nān solluvaden? solleerē*” (How can I speak? You speak if possible) and immediately in the  [ninth pāsuram](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/03/thiruvaimozhi-2-5-9-solleer-en-ammanai/) he said “*solleer en ammānai*” (speak about my lord) – that is āḻvār’s nature.

Did he just attempt to speak or did he succeed speaking about [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)?

- *kurugūrc catakōpan* – Since he is [nammāḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) who was blessed divinely by [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), there is no doubt about his ability to glorify emperumān.
- *kūṟina andādi …* – The 10 pāsurams in this prabandam which are as glorious as the object of this prabandam – which is emperumān himself.
- *kūduvar vaikundamē* – Instead of not achieving the goal as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 2.3.10](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/02/thiruvaimozhi-2-3-10-kalippum-kavarvum/) “*adiyār kuḻāngaḷai udan kūduvadu enṟukolō?*” (when I will reach the divine assembly of nityasūris agreeing to their principles?) and instead of suffering in separation as in [tiruvāimoḻi 2.4](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/03/thiruvaimozhi-2-4-adiyadi/) “*ādiyādi*“, immediately on reciting these pāsurams, they will attain the goal which I attained by tiresome prayers. When father’s wealth is present (which was acquired by him with great difficulty), the son would simply enjoy the wealth. No need to suffer like [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/); those who learn/practice this decad, can simply participate in āḻvār’s result.

Finally, nampiḷḷai summarizes the contents of this decad briefly.

- In the first pāsuram, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) explained how [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) came along with his entourage and united with him.
- In the second pāsuram, he said “after uniting with me, his divine form, divine features and divine weapons became radiant”.
- In the third pāsuram, he said “emperumān united with me in such a manner that he would feel existing when being together with me and in separation he would feel as though non-existing”.
- In the fourth pāsuram, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) ridiculed the metaphors given to him (his features) since they are no match for him.
- In the fifth pāsuram, he skipped the metaphors and directly enjoyed [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/).
- In the sixth pāsuram, he said “Such distinct [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) enjoyed me like muktātmās (liberated souls) would enjoy him”.
- In the seventh pāsuram, āḻvār said “[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) assumed the forms of śrī rāma, kriṣṇa et al for my sake”.
- In the eighth pāsuram, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) said “He does not have the ability to speak about emperumān”.
- In the ninth pāsuram, āḻvār, seeking out for company, set out to speak about [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/).
- In the tenth pāsuram, āḻvār said “Even to speak about a single quality of emperumān united with me thus, is very difficult”.
- In the end, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) explains the result for those who recite this decad and completes the same.

[āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) tiruvadigaḷē śaraṇam  
[emperumānār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/emperumanar/) tiruvadigaḷē śaraṇam  
[piḷḷān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/pillan/) tiruvadigaḷē śaraṇam  
[nanjīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nanjiyar/) tiruvadigaḷē śaraṇam  
[nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/) tiruvadigaḷē śaraṇam  
[vadakkut tiruvīdip piḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadakku-thiruvidhi-pillai/) tiruvadigaḷē śaraṇam  
[periyavāccān piḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/periyavachchan-pillai/) tiruvadigaḷē śaraṇam  
[vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/) tiruvadigaḷē śaraṇam

## 2.6 Vaikunda manivannane

## 2.6.1. Vaikunda manivannane

*vaikundā! maṇivaṇṇanē! en pollāt tirukkuṟaḷā! – ennuḷ manni vaigum vaigal tōṟum amudāya vān ēṟē!sey gundā arum dīmai un adiyārkkut tīrttu asurarkkut tīmaigaḷsey gundā! – unnai nān pidittēn koḷ sikkenavē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vaikundā – being the unmatched leader due to having parampadam as the residence; maṇivaṇṇanē – sulabha (easily approachable) due to having blue-emerald like complexion; en pollāt tirukkuṟaḷā – having beautiful vāmana form and thus being most enjoyable; en uḷ – in my heart; manni – staying there firmly and bonding; vaigum vaigal tōṟum – at all times (forever); amudāya – as eternal nectar; vānēṟē – having greatness of giving the experience of nityasūris \[to me\]; sey – being done; kundā – not hesitating while bestowing results; arum – difficult to avoid; tīmai – cruel sins; un adiyārkku – for those who are your servitors; tīrttu – destroying them; asurarkku – for those (demons); tīmaigaḷ – disaster; sey – causing; kundā – oh one who has the weapon named kunda!; unnai – you (who are enjoyable, removing the hurdles, being favourable towards your devotees); nān – I (who knows your sweetness and cannot sustain myself without you); sikkena – firmly; pidittēn – holding on; koḷ – you realise that

**Перевод:**

**emperumān resides in my heart bonding with me eternally as the unmatched leader due to having parampadam as the residence, sulabha (easily approachable) due to having blue-emerald like complexion (when some one is attractive, we will approach them), having beautiful vāmana form and thus being most enjoyable, having greatness of giving the experience of nityasūris \[to me\]. He destroys the cruel sins (which do not hesitate in giving results and are difficult to destroy) for those who are his servitors, passes them on to those demoniac individuals causing them disaster. Oh one who has the weapon named kunda! Realize that I am firmly holding on to you.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the first pāsuram – emperumān doubts “What if he leaves?” āḻvār eliminates that doubt.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*In the first pāsuram – āḻvār requests emperumān to keep in his divine heart saying “I am holding on firmly to you who are unsurpassedly sweet and removing the hurdles”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*In the first pāsuram – emperumān united with āḻvār in “andāmattanbu” and considered himself to have accomplished an improbable task; āḻvār started considering himself unworthy as previously said in tiruvāimoḻi 2.5.5 “allāvi uḷ kalanda” (one who united with this unworthy soul) and tiruvāimoḻi 2.5.8 “en mudivu kāṇādē ennuḷ kalandān” (He united with me ignoring my fallen nature); seeing this emperumān started doubting “what if he again starts thinking as in ‘vaḷavēḻ ulagu‘ (where āḻvār shies away from emperumān thinking about his own fallen nature) and leaves me?” āḻvār eliminates emperumān’s doubt. வைகுந்தா! மணிவண்ணனே! என் பொல்லாத் திருக்குறளா! – என்னுள் மன்னிவைகும் வைகல் தோறும் அமுது ஆய வான் ஏறே!செய் குந்தா அரும் தீமை உன் அடியார்க்குத் தீர்த்து அசுரர்க்குத் தீமைகள்செய் குந்தா! – உன்னை நான் பிடித்தேன் கொள் சிக்கெனவே. vaikundā! maṇivaṇṇanē! en pollāt tirukkuṟaḷā! – ennuḷ manni vaigum vaigal tōṟum amudāya vān ēṟē!sey gundā arum dīmai un adiyārkkut tīrttu asurarkkut tīmaigaḷsey gundā! – unnai nān pidittēn koḷ sikkenavē*

- *vaikundā* – It appears that [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) becomes delighted thinking “the lord of nitya vibhūti (spiritual realm) arrived and bonded with me”. āḻvār says [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s primary name. Like the divine daughter of king janaka, śitā said “*āryaputra*“, the cow-herd girls of āyarpādi (gōkulam) said “*kriṣṇa*“, āḻvār said “*vaikundā*“. When joy overflows (between dear ones), they call out each other’s name and pacify themselves.
- *maṇivaṇṇanē* – Feeling his embrace, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) blissfully says this name. Oh. one who is having a cool form like a blue emerald!
- *en pollāt tirukkuṟaḷā* – Just he stood in front of mahābali as a mendicant, here [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is standing in front of āḻvār seeking his service. Here beauty is not just worldly beauty – a beauty which cannot be found in anything else. It can also be explained as – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is using “*pollā*” (bad), to shed druśti-dōśam (evil eyes – jinx). *vaikundā* speaks about supremacy; *maṇivaṇṇanē* explains physical beauty; *en pollāt tirukkuṟaḷā* explains his simplicity; supreme entity is that which has all the three qualities.
- *en uḷ manni* – indra benefited by getting his kingdom back; mahābali benefited by being called generous; but [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s heart is most suitable to enjoy [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s divine beauty. Entering my heart and staying here eternally.
- *vaigum vaigal tōṟum amudāya* – being eternally enjoyable nectar every moment
- *vānēṟē* – Like being prideful after mingling with nityasūris and winning over them, he bonded with [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) and won over him. “*ēṟu*” indicates that his experience/greatness supersedes everything else.

[āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) explains how [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) removed his hurdles to enjoy him.

- *sey kundā varum tīmai* – those sins which are committed and the results of which have to be personally experienced; alternatively explained as – those sins for which, the results are most difficult to evade.
- *un adiyār …* – Oh the pure one who ensures that, those who are surrendered to you do not endure the results of such sins and pass them on to the demoniac ones! Those who committed sins before, when they become favourable towards you and approach you, you take their sins and distribute them to their enemies. This is explained in śādyāyana śākā “*dviśanta: pāpa krutyām*” (those who are enemies, receive the evil activities); \[before crossing the ocean to lankā\] śrī rāma mounted his arrow on his bow towards samudrarājan (king of the ocean); but when samudrarājan realised his mistake and surrendered to śrī rāma, he diverted the arrow towards the demoniac individuals in the northern desert. When he sees no such option, as said in mahābhāratam “… *urasā dārayāmāsa pārttam sanjādya mādava:*” (Protecting arjuna, kriṣṇa accepted in his chest the powerful śakti astram which was sent by bhagadatta) – he pushed away arjuna and accepted the powerful arrow on his anta:puram (chest which is the private quarters of śrī mahālakśmi) – thus he himself takes up the suffering of his devotees.  Sins are certain type of acts, which will disappear when the results are experienced; since the [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) (soul – doer) is ignorant, he may forget; sarvajñan (omniscient [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)) remembers and ensures that the ātmā experiences the fruits of such activities. His accepting them in his heart implies his forgiving them and when he forgives, naturally those results get exhausted (without the [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) having to experience the results). Some other schools of thought say that “*apūrvam*“, “*śakti*” are the principles which make sure that the doer experiences the result of his actions; but [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) clearly establishes that [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is the controller of these actions; this is the true/beautiful philosophy.
- kundam – kurundu tree – the flower is white in color; this whiteness indicates purity; another explanation – kundā is an auspicious name of emperumān as seen in śrīviṣṇu sahasranāmam “*kumuda: kundara: kunda:*” (one who enjoys in earth with his devotees, one who brings joy to earth by eliminating the evils, one who bestows vaikuntam).
- *unnai* – you who are partial towards your devotees
- *nān* – I who suffered in separation in [*ādiyādi*](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/03/thiruvaimozhi-2-4-adiyadi/). By your uplifting me, I came to exist \[until then, though I was there, I was not worthy to be called as “existing”\].
- *pidittēn koḷ* – realise that I caught hold of you.

Have these words not been uttered before? Those were not the same.

- *sikkenavē pidittēn koḷ* – You have to realise that even if you (who caused me to surrender unto you) leave me, I will not leave you. Here, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying “*mā suca:”* (don’t grieve) \[kriṣṇa said “*mā suca:*” in [bhagavat gītā](http://githa.koyil.org/) 18.66 comforting arjuna that once he fully surrenders, he need not grieve about the hurdles; here, āḻvār is comforting emperumān that he will not leave him\].

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

adiyen saraty ramanuja dasan
