## 2.6.2. Sikkenac ciridoridamum

*sikkenac ciridu ōr idamum puṟappadāt tanuuḷḷē – ulagugaḷ okkavē viḻungip pugundān pugundadaṟpin mikka jñāna veḷḷac cudar viḷakku āyt tuḷakku aṟṟu amudam āy – engum pakkam nōkku aṟiyān paindāmaraik kaṇṇanē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ciridu ōr – negligible; idamum – space; puṟappadā – to exist outside the scope; ulagugaḷ – worlds; than uḷḷē – in his divine will; okkavē – in a singular manner; viḻungi – subdued; cikkena (sikkena) – firmly so that they never leave; pugundān – entered (inside me); pugundadan pin – after entering; mikka – abundant; jñāna veḷḷam – completeness of knowledge; cudar (sudar) – that which is the abode for splendor; viḷakkāy – his svarūpam which is the source of light; tuḷakku – shivering (which came out of doubts in separation from me); aṟṟu – being removed; amudamāy – being unsurpassedly sweet; en – one who is constantly looking at me; paim – beautiful; tāmarai – like a lotus; kaṇṇan – having eyes; engum – any place; pakkam – in; nōkka – see; aṟiyān – does not know

**Перевод:**

**emperumān who consumed (subdued) all worlds within his divine will, in a single manner not leaving even very negligible space outside the scope, entered into me; after entering me, being the source of light (that is his true nature) which has abundant splendour of knowledge, having removed his doubts (about separation from me), being unsurpassed sweetness, he is having beautiful lotus like eyes which are constantly looking at me; such emperumān can not see anywhere else now other than me.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the second pāsuram – āḻvār speaks about the completeness emperumān acquired after uniting with him.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says that after uniting with him, emperumān became radiant and did not focus on anything else.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*In the second pāsuram – āḻvār speaks about how emperumān enjoyed him and the splendour emperumān acquired through such experience.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Second pāsuram. In the previous pāsuram, emperumān‘s doubt of “what can I do if āḻvār leaves me?; the completeness acquired by emperumān, after hearing āḻvār say “I won’t leave you”, is explained in this pāsuram. சிக்கெனச் சிறிது ஓர் இடமும் புறப்படாத் தன்னுள்ளே – உலகுகள் ஒக்கவே விழுங்கிப் புகுந்தான் புகுந்ததற்பின் மிக்க ஞான வெள்ளச் சுடர் விளக்குஆய் துளக்கு அற்று அமுதம் ஆய் – எங்கும் பக்கம் நோக்கு அறியான் என் பைந்தாமரைக் கண்ணனே sikkenac ciridu ōr idamum puṟappadāt tanuuḷḷē – ulagugaḷ okkavē viḻungip pugundān pugundadaṟpin mikka jñāna veḷḷac cudar viḷakku āyt tuḷakku aṟṟu amudam āy – engum pakkam nōkku aṟiyān paindāmaraik kaṇṇanē*

- *siridōridamum puṟappadāt than uḷḷē ulagugaḷ okkavē viḻungic cikkenap pugundān* – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) thought “while enjoying [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) I should not be like someone who left his sandals/shoes outside the temple and thinking about that while worshiping inside the temple” \[nampiḷḷai uses a beautiful phrase “*seruppu vaittut tiruvadi toḻappukkāṟpōlē*” – in arumpadam, this is explained nicely. Once a śrīvaiṣṇava entered śrīrangam temple, leaving his sandals outside the temple. It is customary not to wear sandals/shoes inside the saptaprākāram (seven layers around śrīrangam temple). But when someone has health issues in the feet, he would wear sandals. The śrīvaiṣṇava left the sandals outside and went inside. Since he kept thinking about the sandals due to fear of losing them, when he went inside the sannidi, instead of saying “please give tīrtam”, he asked “please give sandals”. The message here is – there should be single focus of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) instead of thinking about petty things. emperumān is manifesting this in the matter of āḻvār – he is having single focus on āḻvār only, arranged for protecting the universe and fully enjoyed āḻvār without leaving him; the kings will enter the private quarters of their consorts after completing their duties for the kingdom (so there is no disturbance). He ensured that even the smallest particle is protected without being separated from him by placing them in his divine will and then entered āḻvār.
- *sikkenap pugundān* – Also explained as “entering into [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) simply to enjoy āḻvār without any other expectation”.
- *pugundadan pin* … – Only after uniting with him and having eliminated his own doubts about [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) leaving him again, [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s knowledge fully blossomed and his shivering stopped. For [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) who has knowledge as an eternal quality, being bound in this world due to its karma, accepts a body, depends on the senses to acquire knowledge; on a fine day, out of bhagavān’s blessings, the ātmā’s knowledge’s contraction gets eliminated; for bhagavān there is no such restriction; still, only after uniting with [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/), bhagavān’s knowledge became fully blossomed and abundant; his bodily splendour too became great now only.
- *tuḷakku aṟṟu* – having already witnessed [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s suffering in separation in “[*ādiyādi*](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/03/thiruvaimozhi-2-4-adiyadi/)“, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) was shivering (thinking about āḻvār going through the same again if he separates) – but his shivering got eliminated as āḻvār ensured that he would not leave him. He is explained in samkśēpa rāmāyaṇam 85 “… *vijvara: …*” (having his fever removed) \[After crowning vibhīśaṇa as the king of lankā, śrī rāma felt that he has completed his task, having his fever (of fear of vibhīśaṇa rejecting the throne) eliminated and felt happy – saying this vālmīkī riśi too feels joyful\]. His fear of “what if āḻvār leaves me?” is eliminated now.
- *amudamāy* – As explained in samkśēpa rāmāyaṇam 85 ” … *pramumōda ha*” (riśi joyfully saying “śrī rāma is happy”). āḻvār feels joyful that [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) accepts him with great affection and joy.
- *engum pakkam nōkkaṟiyān* – Even if his divine consorts embrace him tightly thinking “we should reduce his great attachment towards [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)“, he would not look at them. Here, an incident from the lives of [āḷavandār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/alavandhar/) and [kurugaik kāvalappan](https://guruparamparai.wordpress.com/2013/02/03/kurugai-kavalappan/) is cited. [maṇakkāl nambi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/manakkal-nambi/) tells āḷavandār that kurugaik kāvalappan has a secret. āḷavandār goes to appan to learn that from him at a place called “gangai koṇḍa cōḷapuram” where appan was meditating sitting on a raised platform. āḷavandār, not wanting to disturb his meditation, hid behind a wall; appan opened his eyes while in the middle of meditation and asked “is there any one from sottaik kulam (śrēśta kulam – the clan of [nātamunigaḷ](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nathamunigal/))?”. āḷavandār comes out of the hiding saying “*adiyēn*” (dāsan) and asked “while we hid behind the wall, how did you find out about our arrival?”. appan mercifully replies “when I blissfully enjoy with [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) during my meditation, even if [śrī mahālakśmi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/) embraces him, he would not care for her, but now he pressed upon my shoulders and looked over my back to see who is present; I understood that there must be someone who is from the sottaik kulam which is very dear to him” \[Similarly, when [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) enjoys with āḻvār, he would not even look anywhere else\].
- *en paim tāmaraik kaṇṇanē* – His divine eyes became cool, after the heat they acquired looking at the suffering of [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) in “[*ādiyādi*](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/03/thiruvaimozhi-2-4-adiyadi/)“.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.6.3. Tamaraik kannanai

*tāmaraik kaṇṇanai viṇṇōr paravum talai maganait – tuḻāy viraip pū maruvu kaṇṇi em pirānaip ponmalaiyai nām maruvi nangu ētti uḷḷi vaṇangi nām magiḻndu āda – nāvu alar pā maruvi niṟkat tanda pānmaiyē vaḷḷalē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tāmarai – like a lotus flower; kaṇṇanai – having eyes; viṇṇōr – nityasūris; paravum – being eternally glorified; talai maganai – having greatness; virai – buds; pū – flowers; maruvu – filled; tuḻāyk kaṇṇi – being the one who is decorated with tuḷasi garland; em – for us; pirānai – being the lord; ponmalaiyai – (due to that togetherness) one who is shining like a golden mountain; nām – we (without leaving, seeing our own lowly nature); maruvi – approached; nangu – (like nityasūris, to be qualified for paramapadam) in a fine manner; ētti – glorifying; uḷḷi – meditating like them (nityasūris) in our mind; vaṇangi – falling at his lotus feet; nām – we; magiḻndu – being joyful; Ada – to dance; nā – in the tongue; alar – born; pā – in the poem; maruvi – being attached; niṟka – to be singing tiruvāimoḻi; tanda – one who bestowed; pānmai – svabhāvam (nature/quality); ēy – fitting; vaḷḷal – one who is with generosity

**Перевод:**

**emperumān is having lotus like eyes; (due to that beauty) he is eternally glorified by nityasūris and is wearing tuḷasi garland that is filled with buds and flowers; he is being our lord and (due to the togetherness with us) is shining like a golden mountain; we (instead of leaving him, seeing our lowly nature) approached him and in proper manner (engaged all our three senses) glorified him, meditated upon him and fell at his lotus feet; (due to this experience in all three senses) the most generous emperumān having such svabhāvam (quality) of magnanimity, bestowed us to have beautiful poems arising from our tongue, that led us to joy and dancing – Such generous emperumān would be single-focused on me (āḻvār).**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the third pāsuram – āḻvār becomes delighted thinking “emperumān has blessed me with the ability to describe his saundaryam (beauty) etc like nityasūris (who have great ability);  how generous he is!”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “the most generous emperumān who made me experience him through his three types of senses (mind, speech, body) does not know (focus on) anyone but me”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Third pāsuram – āḻvār says “How generous emperumān is! He is so generous that he made me a dēśika (highly capable leader) to enjoy him who is even beyond the abilities of nityasūris”. தாமரைக் கண்ணனை விண்ணோர் பரவும் தலைமகனை – துழாய் விரைப் பூ மருவு கண்ணி எம் பிரானை பொன்மலையை நாம் மருவி நன்கு ஏத்தி உள்ளி வணங்கி நாம் மகிழ்ந்து ஆட – நாவு அலர் பா மருவி நிற்கத் தந்த பான்மையே வள்ளலே tāmaraik kaṇṇanai viṇṇōr paravum talai maganait – tuḻāy viraip pū maruvu kaṇṇi em pirānaip ponmalaiyai nām maruvi nangu ētti uḷḷi vaṇangi nām magiḻndu Ada – nāvu alar pā maruvi niṟkat tanda pānmaiyē vaḷḷalē*

- *tāmaraik kaṇṇanai …* – nityasūris are of such nature that when [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) glances at them once, they would feel totally defeated and start glorifying emperumān like someone  blabbering while being affected with fever. This is as explained in mōkśa darmam “*śrutōyamartō rāmasya jāmadagnyasya jalpata: …*” (This meaning is heard from paraśurāma and vyāsa in a disorderly manner).
- *talai maganai* – Though they glorify him, as said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 5.1.48 “*niravadya: para: prāptē:*” (excellent and unreachable), he remains supreme.
- *tuḻāy …* – He won over the nityasūris by showing his beautiful eyes; he caught [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) through his garland. He got āḻvār to become bewildered by showing his garland. [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is having a garland which has abundance of fragrance and flowers.
- *ponmalaiayai* – he who has become beautiful after uniting with me and who keeps growing. He grew in stature by my glorification. Thus – it is established that  [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) became radiant after acquiring [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/).
- nām maruvi – we, who said “*aruvinaiyēn*” (very sinful) and shied away, are now approaching him.
- *nangu ētti* – Glorifying such [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is glorified by nityasūris; [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) previously said in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.10.7](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/10/thiruvaimozhi-1-10-7-enthaiye-enrum/) “*vānavar sindaiyuḷ vaittuc collum selvanai, endaiyē enban*” (I call him my father – he is the wealthy one who is meditated upon and glorified by nityasūris) and shied away. Even when vēdam itself gave up on glorifying [bhagavān](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/10/thiruvaimozhi-1-10-7-enthaiye-enrum/) as said in taittiriya upaniśat “*yatō vācō nivartantē*” (the words are returning from glorifying that brahmam), āḻvār followed him and glorified him.
- *uḷḷi* – meditating upon; instead of trying to leave [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) thought about [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/).
- *vaṇangi* – worshiped him without any ego, after being forced by bhagavān’s auspicious qualities. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) who said in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.5.2](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/08/thiruvaimozhi-1-5-2-ninainthu-nainthu/) “*vaṇangināl un perumai māsūṇādō*” (If I worship you, would that be an insult), fell at [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s lotus feet now.
- *nām magiḻndāda* – we who did not have any idea about this divine joy derived from experience with bhagavān, are now dancing out of great joy.
- *nāvalar …* – Like a fresh flower arising, the pāsuram which arises out of my tongue and stayed firm in me – Oh such generous [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is having such generosity as a natural quality!
- *nā alar pā* – simply arising out of the tongue – even without the help of mind.

It is also explained as [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) saying “Oh lotus eyed lord! Oh you who resemble golden mountain! You have such quality which made us approach you and sing your glories! What a beautiful quality this is! Oh generous one!”.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.6.4. Vallale madusudana

*vaḷḷalē! madusūdanā! en maragada malaiyē! unai ninaindu eḷgal tanda endāy unnai enganam vidugēn veḷḷamē purai nin pugaḻ kudaindu ādip pādik kaḷittu ugandu ugandu uḷḷa nōygaḷ ellām turandu uyndu pōndirundē?*

**Пословный перевод:**

vaḷḷalē – being most generous (irrespective of whether being asked or not); madusūdanā – being the destroyer of my hurdles like you destroyed the demon named madu; en – for me; maragada malaiyē – one who makes me experience his (tall radiant) emerald hill-like beautiful form; unnai – you; ninaindu – on meditating upon; eḷgal – having acquired detachment (for worldly pleasures); tanda – bestowed; endāy – Oh lord!; veḷḷamē purai – countless like an ocean; nin – your; pugaḻ – qualities; kudaindu – immerse in you and experience you; ādip pādi – (out of great joy) dancing and singing; kaḷittu – becoming joyful; ugandu ugandu – (not stopping at some point) increasing more and more; uḷḷa nōygaḷ ellām – all diseases (such as ahankāram (considering body as oneself), artam (wealth), kāmam (lust), anubhava viślēśam (break in divine experience), nikarśa anusandānam (considering oneself to be worthy) etc); turandu – eliminating them to keep them far away; uyndu – having achieved the goal; pōndu – (leaving the state of existence in this material realm and) reaching unto you; irundu – staying there with permanent experience; unnai – you (who are such generous lord); enganam – how; vidugēn – will I leave?

**Перевод:**

**Oh lord who is being most generous (irrespective of whether being asked or not), who is being the destroyer of my hurdles, just like you destroyed the demon named madu, who is the one who makes me experience your (tall radiant) emerald hill-like beautiful form! As said in mūnṟām tiruvandādi “māṟpāl manam suḻippa mangaiyar tōḷ kaivittu” (as the mind becomes attached towards śrīman nārāyaṇa, it withdraws itself from worldly pleasures), my lord, you bestowed me detachment (from worldly pleasures) on meditating upon you! You made me immerse in you and experience your ocean-like countless qualities, made me dance and sing (out of great joy), made me become joyful, increasing my joy more and more, eliminating all my diseases (such as ahankāram (considering body as oneself), artam (wealth), kāmam (lust), anubhava viślēśam (break in divine experience), nikarśa anusandānam (considering oneself to be worthy) etc) and keeping them far away,  having achieved the goal (of leaving the state of existence in this material realm and) reaching unto you and staying there with permanent experience; how will I leave you (who are such a generous lord)?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fourth pāsuram – āḻvār asks emperumān “you are of such nature that you give yourself to us, you have all auspicious qualities led by the quality of destroying my hurdles; after experiencing you (who are of such nature), is there any reason for me to leave you?”*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār asks emperumān “is there any reasons for me to leave you who are benevolent in all manners?”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*In fourth pāsuram – when āḻvār was asked by emperumān “how long will this love last?”, āḻvār replies “After experiencing your nature, is there any reason to leave you?”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Fourth pāsuram – On āḻvār manifesting his humility by saying “nām maruvi nangētti uḷḷi vaṇangi nām magizndu Ada” (we, who are very lowly, approached you, glorified you with our speech, meditated upon you, worshiped you and danced in great joy), emperumān doubts “what if he leaves me?” āḻvār says “On experiencing your divine beauty as shown by you and becoming weak, is there any reason for me to leave you?” வள்ளலே! மதுசூதனா! என் மரகத மலையே! உனை நினைந்து எள்கல் தந்த எந்தாய் உன்னை எங்ஙனம் விடுகேன் வெள்ளமே புரை நின் புகழ் குடைந்து ஆடிப் பாடிக் களித்து உகந்து உகந்து உள்ள நோய்கள் எல்லாம் துரந்து உய்ந்து போந்திருந்தே? vaḷḷalē! madusūdanā! en maragada malaiyē! unai ninaindu eḷgal tanda endāy unnai enganam vidugēn veḷḷamē purai nin pugaḻ kudaindu ādip pādik kaḷittu ugandu ugandu uḷḷa nōygaḷ ellām turandu uyndu pōndirundē?*

- *vaḷḷalē* – Oh most generous one who bestowed yourself to me unconditionally!
- *madusūdanā* – While you gave yourself to me, you removed the hurdles which stop me from reaching you, just like you destroyed the demon named madu
- *en maradaga malaiyē* – you bestowed upon me your unlimited divine beautiful form which brings glories to you, is greater than your true nature and that eliminates the fatigue of the beholder.
- *unai ninaindu eḷgal tanda endāy* – Oh the one who made me give up on worldly pleasures on meditating upon you! Also explained as – eḷgal – attachment; [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) saying – on mediating upon you my lord, you mesmerised me and made me become unconscious as said in periya tiruvandādi 34 “*kālāḻum nenjaḻiyum kaṇsuḻalum*” (legs become weak, heart becomes broken, eyes get dizzy)
- *unnai enganam vidugēn* – Should I leave you because you have no generosity? Should I leave you because you cannot eliminate the hurdles? Should I leave you because you are not beautiful? After having engaged in you, is there any reason to leave you? Also explained as [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) saying – Once I meditate upon you and have become detached from worldly pleasures, is there any reason to leave you?

Further, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) removes [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s doubts,

- *veḷḷamē …* – having entered into your ocean-like auspicious qualities in all directions, having immersed in them, singing with great love, becoming prideful due to that and becoming greatly attached to you
- *uḷḷa nōygaḷ ellām turandu* – driving out all types of diseases such as those which are experienced due to karma, those sufferings due to separation from you, those sufferings due to considering myself unworthy and leaving you etc.
- *uyndu* – having uplifted/revived myself as said in taittiriya upaniśat “*santamēnam tatō vidu:*” (they know him as existing due to his having true knowledge)
- *pōndu* – being different from samsāris (materialistic people)
- *irundu* – being free from burden – Oh most generous! Oh destroyer of madu! How (Why) will I leave you?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.6.5. Uyndu pondu

*uyndu pōndu en ulappilāda vem tīvinaigaḷai nāsam seydu unadu andam il adimai adaindēn viduvēnō? aindu paindalaiyādaravaṇai mēvip pāṟkadal yōga nittirai sindai seyda endāy unnaic cindai seydu seydē*

**Пословный перевод:**

pāṟkadal – in the milk ocean; aindu – in five types; pai – expanded; talai – having hoods; ādu – with mild rhythmic rocking movements; aravaṇai – in the divine serpent bed; mēvi – fitting nicely in the serpent bed and resting; yōgam – meditating for the welfare of the universe; nittirai – like sleeping; sindai seydu – thinking (about the protection of all); endāy – my lord!; unnai – you (who manifested this quality of protecting others); sindai seydu seydu – by constantly meditating upon; uyndu – having achieved the goal; pōndu – being different from materialistic people who are focused on other worldly matters; en – my (which are caused by me); ulappilāda – countless; vem – cruel; tī – having the nature of fire; vinaigaḷai – sins; nāsam seydu – destroyed; unadu – (the apt) you; andam il – boundless; adimai – the joy of serving; adaindēn – I, who attained it; viduvēnō – there is no reason for me to leave it

**Перевод:**

**Oh my lord and master who is firmly resting in the milk ocean in the five-hooded ādiśēśan (serpent bed), pretending to be sleeping but really thinking about protection of all entities of the universe! On constantly meditating upon you and having attained the goal, being different from samsāris (materialistic people), you have destroyed the countless cruel fire-like sins which I myself have accumulated; after acquiring boundless joyful servitude towards you, there is no reason to leave you.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fifth pāsuram – āḻvār asks emperumān “Having achieved eternal kainkaryam to you, is there any reason to leave you?”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār asks emperumān “Having achieved eternal joyful kainkaryam to you after experiencing you, why would I leave you?”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. உய்ந்து போந்து என் உலப்பு இலாத வெம் தீவினைகளை நாசம் செய்து உனது அந்தம் இல் அடிமை அடைந்தேன் விடுவேனோ? ஐந்து பைந்தலை ஆடு அரவு அணை மேவிப் பாற்கடல் யோக நித்திரை சிந்தை செய்த எந்தாய் உன்னைச் சிந்தை செய்து செய்தே uyndu pōndu en ulappilāda vem tīvinaigaḷai nāsam seydu unadu andam il adimai adaindēn viduvēnō? aindu paindalaiyādaravaṇai mēvip pāṟkadal yōga nittirai sindai seyda endāy unnaic cindai seydu seydē*

- *uyndu pōndu* – having come to exist, being different from samsāris.
- *en ulappilāda* … – (you) having eliminated my endless cruel sins without a trace and I, engaging in selfless servitude at your lotus feet, is there any reason for me to leave you?
- *viduvēnō* – Would I leave you because I am interested in worldly matters? Would I leave you because I don’t understand my true nature? Would I leave you because I don’t relish the fragrance of servitude towards you? Would I leave you because I am dissatisfied with serving you?
- *aindu …* – Only if tiruvanantāḻvān (ādiśēśan) who is well-aware of servitude towards you, leaves you, will I leave you. Just like a great flood will seep out through many exits, ādiśēśan has many hoods to express his great joy of serving you; his head would rock like being drunk with honey; oh my master, who is resting in the milk ocean, on such ādiśēśan, who is cool, tender and fragrant and meditating on “how to uplift all living entities”!
- *yōga nittirai* – deep trance – as said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 6.4.6 “…*ātmānam vāsudēvākyam cintayan…*” ([bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) started meditating upon vāsudēva who is himself and attained divine trance of yōga nidrā), he is meditating on himself.
- *endāy* – you made me completely exist for you by manifesting your simplicity.
- *unnaic cindai seydu seydu* – on meditating upon you, who worked hard to make me think about you, is there any reason for me to leave you?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.6.6. Unnaic cindai

*unnaic cindai seydu seydu un nedu mā moḻi isai pādi ādi – en munnait tīvinaigaḷ muḻu vēr arindanan yān unnaic cindaiyināl igaḻnda iraṇiyan agal mārvam kīṇḍa – en munnaik kōḷ ariyē! mudiyādaden enakkē*

**Пословный перевод:**

unnai – you (who are apt lord and helper); sindaiyināl – by his heart/mind; igaḻnda – ignored/insulted; iraṇiyan – hiraṇyakaśipu’s; agal – wide, spacious; mārvam – chest; kīṇḍa – one who effortlessly tore; en – my (who is the best example for wanting hurdles to be removed); munnai – superceded (his devotee prahlāda’s thoughts); kōḷariyē – Oh one who appeared as narasimha (half-lion half-man incarnation)!; unnai – you (who are helper of the needy, apt and sweet); sindai seydu seydu – constantly meditating upon; nedu – (out of such devotion) great; un – words that highlight your qualities; moḻi – tiruvāimoḻi; mā – having greatness (matching it); isai – with music; pādi – singing; ādi – dancing (to the tunes of the singing); en – my; munnait tīvinaigaḷ – sins accumulated since time immemorial; yān – I; muḻu vērarindanan – eliminated completely from the root (once nature of self is realised as completely dependent on bhagavān, as the joy is for the ātmā, elimination of hurdles can also be attributed to self); enakku – for me; mudiyādadu – impossible; en – what is there?

**Перевод:**

**Oh you (who are apt lord and helper) who superceded your devotee prahlāda’s thought and appeared as narasimha, effortlessly tore the wide chest of hiraṇyakaśipu who insulted you with his heart! By constantly meditating upon your great qualities, (out of such devotion) I started singing the great tiruvāimoḻi  which has the words which highlight your greatness with matching great music and dancing; by thus engaging all my three senses (mind – meditating, speech – singing, body – dancing), my sins which have been accumulated since time immemorial were eliminated completely from the root. For such me, what is impossible to achieve?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the sixth pāsuram – when emperumān mercifully asked āḻvār “What more shall I do for you?” āḻvār replies “Have I not acquired anything? I have acquired everything”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says that by acquiring this servitude towards emperumān, all his desires are fulfilled.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Sixth pāsuram – āḻvār says “After emperumān being someone who would appear instantaneously on the request/vow of his devotee, do I have anything to do?” உன்னைச் சிந்தை செய்து செய்து உன் நெடு மா மொழி இசை பாடி ஆடி – என் முன்னைத் தீவினைகள் முழு வேர் அரிந்தனன் யான் உன்னைச் சிந்தையினால் இகழ்ந்த இரணியன் அகல் மார்வம் கீண்ட – என் முன்னைக் கோளரியே முடியாதது என் எனக்கே unnaic cindai seydu seydu un nedu mā moḻi isai pādi ādi – en munnait tīvinaigaḷ muḻu vēr arindanan yān unnaic cindaiyināl igaḻnda iraṇiyan agal mārvam kīṇḍa – en munnaik kōḷ ariyē! mudiyādaden enakkē*

- *unnaic cindai seydu seydu* – meditating upon you without any break due to your sweet nature
- *unnai* – you, who iare enjoyable and apt \[master\] for me
- *sindai seydu seydu* – Instead of meditating upon you as a matter of following orders in bruhadāraṇyaka upaniśat “*nididyāsitavya:*“, I am constantly meditating upon you due to your sweetness.
- *un nedu mā moḻi isai* – greatness (indicated by nedu and mā) is adjective to moḻi (pāsuram) and isai (tune) respectively. Greatness of the poem and the tune are explained here. Singing the pāsuram where the words and tune are boundless and such tune/words make one dance.
- *en* … – I eliminated all my accumulated sins without any trace. *muḻu vēr* – down to the root. It is also explained as eliminating even along with the side roots (which grew along).
- *arindanan yān* – though, [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) eliminates those sins, since [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is the enjoyer of the result, he says he himself removed the hurdles too.
- *unnai* … – Oh you who helped long ago!
- *unnaic cindaiyināl igaḻnda* – hiraṇyakaśipu did not insult [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) with words alone – deep down his heart, he insulted [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/). From this, it can be understood that – to give up on someone, emperumān sees if they commit mistake from deep tinside heir heart; but to pursue someone, he just looks for them even pretending as friends.
- *iraṇiyan agal mārvam kīṇḍa* – Since the well-fed body of hiraṇyakaśipu is no match for narasimha’s nails, he effortlessly tore hiraṇya’s chest.
- *en munnaik kōḷariyē* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) thinks that [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s incarnation as narasimha is to help him specifically. kōḷ – pride, radiance. As said in narasimha dhyāna ślōkam “*mahāviṣṇum*“, it indicates pride; as said in the same ślōkam “*jvalantam*“, it indicates radiance. When one does not consider a favour done to emperumān’s devotees as something that was done to themselves, there is no bhagavat sambandam (relationship with [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)).
- *mudiyādadu en enakkē* – When you are readily appearing to fulfil the vow of your devotee, what is impossible for me? \[nothing is impossible\].

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.6.7. Mudiyadadu en

*mudiyādadu en enakkēl ini muḻuvēḻ ulagum uṇḍān – ugandu vandu adiyēn uḷ pugundān agalvānum allan ini sediyār nōygaḷ ellām turandu emar kīḻ mēl eḻu piṟappum vidiyā ven naragattu enṟum sērdal māṟinarē*

**Пословный перевод:**

muḻu ēḻ ulagum – all worlds; uṇḍān – (since he cannot exist without protecting them) one who consumed them \[during praḷayam\]; ugandu – (further, since he has the same attachment towards me) having great affection; adiyēn – considering my relationship as a servitor to him as the only reason; uḷ – inside; vandu – arrived; pugundān – entered; ini – further; agalvānum – one who lets them go \[during sruśti\]; allan – not; kīḻ – previous (ancestors); mēl – subsequent (descendants); eḻu piṟappum – seven generations; emar – those who are related to me; sedi – like a dense bush; Ar – abundant; nōygaḷ ellām – all diseases (such as avidyā (ignorance), karma (virtues/vices), vāsanā (impressions) etc); turandu – driving them away; vidiyā – no relief; vem – very hot; naragattu – hell named samsāram (material realm – where we live now); enṟum – forever; sērdal – reach, be present; māṟinar – avoided; ini – thus, after emperumān showing his partiality towards my whole clan and those who are related to that clan; enakkēl – for me; mudiyādadu – impossible; en – is it there?

**Перевод:**

**emperumān who consumed all worlds \[during praḷayam\] (as he cannot exist without protecting them), (further, since he has the same attachment towards me) having great affection, arrived at me and entered into me considering my relationship as a servitor to him as the only reason and did not leave me unlike those worlds are let out by him \[during sruśti\]; due to this reason, he would drive away the densely available abundant diseases (such as avidyā (ignorance), karma (virtues/vices), vāsanā (impressions) etc) for those who are related to me in seven generations before me (ancestors) and after me (descendants); such relatives will ever avoid reaching this hot hell named samsāram (material realm) where there is no relief; thus, after emperumān showed his partiality towards my whole clan and those who are related to that clan, is there anything impossible for me to do?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the seventh pāsuram – when asked “Are you satisfied with having acquired everything?”, āḻvār replies “due to the special attention/mercy given by emperumān to me, even my relatives and their relatives became uplifted from this samsāram (material realm); after this, is there anything left for me to attain?”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “emperumān‘s help towards me reached up to all those who are related to my clan and uplifted them all”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Seventh pāsuram – āḻvār says “emperumān‘s favouring towards me reached to my relatives and their relatives too”. முடியாதது என் எனக்கேல் இனி? முழு ஏழ் உலகும் உண்டான் – உகந்து வந்து அடியேன் உட்புகுந்தான் அகல்வானும் அல்லன் இனி செடி ஆர் நோய்கள் எல்லாம் துரந்து எமர் கீழ் மேல் எழு பிறப்பும் விடியா வெம் நரகத்து என்றும் சேர்தல் மாறினரே mudiyādadu en enakkēl ini muḻuvēḻ ulagum uṇḍān – ugandu vandu adiyēn uḷ pugundān agalvānum allan ini sediyār nōygaḷ ellām turandu emar kīḻ mēl eḻu piṟappum vidiyā ven naragattu enṟum sērdal māṟinarē*

- *mudiyādadu en enakkēl ini* – is there anything impossible for me?

When asked “How are you saying this?”, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says

- *muḻu* … – Whatever turmoil universe goes through when caught in the danger of praḷayam (annihilation) until it enters his stomach, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) goes through the same until he enters my heart. Even after this, is there anything impossible for me?
- *adiyēn uḷ pugundān* – he entered me seeing our relationship \[as [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) the master – me the servant\]
- *uḷ pugundān* – mixed like water mixing with water seamlessly; unlike the universe entering him without any real desire, he entered in me with great desire. In the example of [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) and universe – bhagavān needs to protect the universe and the universe needs to be protected by bhagavān – so bhagavān consumes the universe to protect it; but in the case of [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/), bhagavān has great desire towards āḻvār and enters into āḻvār (without āḻvar having same attachment towards bhagavān).
- *agalvānum allan ini* – For the universe, once the praḷayam is over \[and sruśti begins\], it will be spat out again; but for [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) there is no such restriction \[he would be there in [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s heart permanently\] – He will not even contemplate about separation to start with. He is not bound by karma like [cētanas (jīvātmās)](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) who separate due to pāpa (sins) and be together due to sukrutam (virtues).

When asked “If [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) has so much affection towards you, would he only protect you like a palm tree that gives shade only to itself?” [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) replies,

- *sedi Ar …* – sedi – pāpam – sins. Sorrows which are abundantly filled with sins. Eliminating densely abundant sins \[here sedi is explained as dense like a bush\]. Diseases/sufferings which arise from attachment to worldly pleasures, considering oneself as unworthy and separation from experiencing [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/). Driving them away with their traces. Was it not explained already in tiruvāimoḻi 2.6.4 “*uḷḷa nōygaḷ ellām turandu*” (eliminating all diseases)? There, it was explained in the context of [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/); now its explained in the context of his relatives and their relatives.

How did they drive out these diseases?

- *emar* – nothing else; just by being related to me, their diseases are driven away.

What type of relations?

- *kīḻ mēl eḻu piṟappum* – 21 generations. 7 generations including him – 3 generations before him, himself and 3 generations after him; 7 generations before that and 7 generations after that.
- *vidiyā vennaragattu* – In the naraka lōkam of yama, when the (pāpa/sinful) karma is exhausted, there is relief. But there is no relief in this material realm. In narakam (hell), the sufferings are obvious, but here the sufferings are not obvious \[we get deceived to think that these actual sufferings are not so bad\].
- *enṟum sērdal māṟinarē* – forever they avoid reaching this material realm. Neither do I need to pray for that, nor does he need to specifically think about that. It is due to special affection (partiality) shown towards me that all those who are related to me also get benefited. So, nothing is impossible for me.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.6.8. Mari mari

*māṟi māṟip pala piṟappum piṟandu adiyai adaindu uḷḷam tēṟi īṟu il inbattu iru veḷḷam yān mūḻginan pāṟip pāṟi asurar tam pal kuḻāngaḷ nīṟ eḻa pāy paravai onṟu ēṟi vīṟṟirundāy – unnai en uḷ nīkkēl endāy*

**Пословный перевод:**

pala piṟappum – in many births (such as dēva (celestial), tiryak (animal), manuśya (human), stāvara (plant) forms); māṟi māṟip piṟantu – while being born again and again (in the same form of birth too); adiyai – your divine feet; adaindu – reached (with knowledge about servitude); uḷḷam tēṟi – having clarity in heart (that you are my means); īṟu – end; il – not existing; inbam – bliss; iru – big; veḷḷam – flood; yān – I (who am indicated by the word “aham”); mūḻginan – drowned; asurar tam – demons’; pal – many different; kuḻāngaḷ – groups; pāṟip pāṟi – to break them in many ways; nīṟu – to turn them into dust; eḻa – and rise; pāy – one who could crash into (amidst their army); onṟu – one who is distinct; paṟavai – on the garuda; ēṟi – riding; vīṟu – manifesting your superiority; irundāy – being present; endāy – my lord!; unnai – you (who are my apt master, refuge, enjoyable entity and eliminator of enemies); ennuḷ – from inside me (who is subservient to you in all manners); nīkkēl – never leave

**Перевод:**

**While being born again and again (in the same form of birth too) in many births (such as dēva (celestial), tiryak (animal), manuśya (human), stāvara (plant) forms), I reached your divine feet (with knowledge about servitude) having clarity in my heart (that you are my means); being triggered by experiencing you, I drowned in the bliss which is like an endless big flood; oh lord who is riding on the distinct garuda who can crash amidst the army of demons, manifesting your supremacy and break the many groups of demons and turn them into rising dust, never should you (who are my apt master, refuge, enjoyable entity and eliminator of enemies) leave from inside me (who is subservient to you in all manners).**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the eighth pāsuram – āḻvār prays to emperumān “Such greatness acquired by your causeless mercy should continue forever without any break; this is what I need”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says that this result that he got should continue forever without any break.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

Some aspects are explained in a clearer manner here.

- *māṟi māṟi* … – [āḻvār](https://guruparamparaihindi.wordpress.com/2013/09/17/nammazhwar/) says “Since time immemorial I was suffering in this material realm; there is no way I could have either exhausted my karma or by atoning for the same, and be delivered”. Since he does not see any effort from his side to attain such great result, he is clearly spelling that out \[and thus highlighting it is purely [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s grace which brought this upon him\].

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Eighth pāsuram – When asked “What virtuous act did you do to achieve this great result?” āḻvār replies “this is not acquired by any of my good virtues – it was acquired after taking birth in this life”; he also says “there is one uninterrupted act; I have been continuously taking birth \[since time immemorial\] in this material realm”. மாறி மாறிப் பல பிறப்பும் பிறந்து அடியை அடைந்து உள்ளம் தேறி ஈறு இல் இன்பத்து இரு வெள்ளம் யான் மூழ்கினன் பாறிப் பாறி அசுரர் தம் பல் குழாங்கள் நீறு எழ பாய் பறவை ஒன்று ஏறி வீற்றிருந்தாய் உன்னை என்னுள் நீக்கேல் எந்தாய் māṟi māṟip pala piṟappum piṟandu adiyai adaindu uḷḷam tēṟi īṟu il inbattu iru veḷḷam yān mūḻginan pāṟip pāṟi asurar tam pal kuḻāngaḷ nīṟ eḻa pāy paravai onṟu ēṟi vīṟṟirundāy – unnai en uḷ nīkkēl endāy*

- *māṟi māṟi* … – When asked “what is the reason for [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) pursuing you along with your related ones?” [āḻvār](https://guruparamparaihindi.wordpress.com/2013/09/17/nammazhwar/) says “Like a boat in an ocean which would get pushed around by the waves and reach the shore, as I was being born again and again, I suddenly saw myself taking refuge in your divine feet. There is no way I can exhaust my karma by experiencing the results and be delivered; neither is there an option for me to atone for my sins and be delivered (only way to be delivered is by your causeless grace).
- *adiyai adaindu uḷḷam tēṟi* – He is not of the type  where “he acquired clarity about self and then reached [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s divine feet”; it is the reverse in [āḻvār](https://guruparamparaihindi.wordpress.com/2013/09/17/nammazhwar/)‘s case where “he first reached emperumān’s feet and then acquired clarity about self”.
- *uḷḷam tēṟi* – heart became purified after eliminating the dirt accumulated due to lengthy impressions of worldly pleasures and not having attained [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/);

Not just purification, further more,

- *īṟil inbattu iru veḷḷam yān mūḻginan* – I submerged and drowned into the endless ocean of bliss. I enjoyed the matter (related to [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)) which is enjoyed by garuda, ādiśēśa and they themselves become consumed by such experience too.

When asked “But what happened to the hurdles which were stopping you from enjoying him?” [āḻvār](https://guruparamparaihindi.wordpress.com/2013/09/17/nammazhwar/) replies “You ask this question to the one who takes care of those” \[explaining it further\].

- *pāṟi* … – Oh lord who manifests your distinct supremacy by riding on garuda who can crash into the midst of the army of groups of demons, and destroy them down to dust! The distinction for garuda is that he is the leader amongst those who \[spontaneously\] act according to your will. The only act done by [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) to destroy the enemies is to comfortably be seated on garuda \[and garudāḻvār will take care of the rest\].
- *unnai* … – oh my lord! You should never take yourself away from me.
- *unnai ennuḷ nīkkēl* – After making yourself present here to unite with me, you should ensure that I too understand your greatness and never think of leaving you. Previously \[in [fourth pāsuram](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/04/thiruvaimozhi-2-6-4-vallale-madhusudhana/)\], [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) doubted that [āḻvār](https://guruparamparaihindi.wordpress.com/2013/09/17/nammazhwar/) may leave him; here, out of great affection towards emperumān, āḻvār doubts himself that he may leave emperumān and thus prays to emperumān that he makes sure to eliminate such thoughts from him.
- *endāy* – āḻvār is identifying the (fatherly/lordly) relationship of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) with him, that ensures that emperumān eliminates the hurdles and unites with [āḻvār](https://guruparamparaihindi.wordpress.com/2013/09/17/nammazhwar/).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.6.9. Enday

*endāy! taṇ tiruvēngadattuḷ ninṟāy! ilangai seṟṟāy! marā maram – paindāḷ ēḻ uruva oru vāḷi kōtta villā! kondu ār taṇ am tuḻāyināy amudē! unnai enuḷḷē kuḻainda em – maindā! vān ēṟē! ini engup pōginṟadē?*

**Пословный перевод:**

endāy – being my categorical lord; taṇ – cool – giving relief from fatigue; tiruvēngadattuḷ – in tirumalā; ninṟāy – arrived and stayed there, being very simple to approach; ilangai – lankā (which is the abode of the enemies of emperumān‘s devotees); seṟṟāy – one who destroyed; marāmaram – pipal (peepal) trees’; paim – well-rounded; tāḷ – bottom portion; ēḻu – seven; uruva – to pierce; oru vāḷi – an arrow; kōtta – (effortlessly) launched; villā – one who is having the bow; kottu – bunches; Ar – abundance; taṇ – cool; am tuḻāyināy – being decorated with tuḷasi garland; em amudē – being eternally sweet (for me); unnai – you with such qualities/aspects; en uḷḷē – inside me; kuḻaitta – completely united (like water mixing in water); maindā – being eternally youthful; vān – for the nityasūris; ēṟē – being their prideful leader; ini – now; engu – where; pōginṟadu – going? This implies that āḻvār is saying “don’t go anywhere”

**Перевод:**

**Oh one who is being my categorical lord! Oh one who has arrived and stayed in cool tirumalā being very simple to approach! Oh one who destroyed lankā (which is the abode of the enemies of emperumān‘s devotees)! Oh one who is having the bow from which you effortlessly launched an arrow to pierce the well-rounded bottom portion of the seven pipal (peepal) trees! One who is being decorated with abundant bunches of cool tuḷasi garland! Being eternally sweet for me, being ever youthful with such qualities/aspects completely united with me inside me; due to this reason, being the prideful leader of nityasūris (You having shown special/distinct relationship (towards me), simplicity, ability to eliminate enemies and instilled faith in me like you did in the case of sugrīva mahārāja, having shown your divine beauty and united with me being very sweet to me, being even greater than the nityasūris who are residents of nitya vibhūti (paramapadam)), now, giving up this togetherness, where are you going? This implies that  āḻvār is saying “don’t go anywhere”.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the ninth pāsuram – āḻvār says to emperumān “After attracting me by showing your qualities and activities, and becoming inseparably together, there is no reason for you to leave me”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says to emperumān “After you yourself put in efforts and united with me, how can you leave me?”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*In the ninth pāsuram – After inseparably uniting with me, why are you wandering in utter perplexity as if you have done nothing \[to uplift me\]? Also explained as – emperumān trying to leave saying “I would like to know what you think”, āḻvār says “How can you go now?”*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Ninth pāsuram. āḻvār says to emperumān “When initially I was unaware of you, you made me aware about yourself and your qualities, transformed me to a state where I cannot exist without you; \[after doing all of this\] you should not leave me”. எந்தாய்! தண் திருவேங்கடத்துள் நின்றாய்! இலங்கை செற்றாய்! மரா மரம் – பைந்தாள் ஏழ் உருவ ஒரு வாளி கோத்த வில்லா! கொந்து ஆர் தண் அம் துழாயினாய் அமுதே! உன்னை என்னுள்ளே குழைத்த எம் – மைந்தா! வான் ஏறே! இனி எங்குப் போகின்றதே? endāy! taṇ tiruvēngadattuḷ ninṟāy! ilangai seṟṟāy! marā maram – paindāḷ ēḻ uruva oru vāḷi kōtta villā! kondu Ar taṇ am tuḻāyināy amudē! unnai enuḷḷē kuḻainda em – maindā! vān ēṟē! ini engup pōginṟadē?*

- *endāy* – Oh lord who arrived in the cool tirumalā, manifested your lordship and engaged me in my servitude towards you!
- *ilangai seṟṟāy* – Just like you eliminated the hurdle that was stopping sītā pirātti from uniting with you, you eliminated those hurdles which were stopping my servitude towards you.
- *marāmaram* … – Here, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) demonstrated that he would take up weapons to help his devotees. He pierced through the seven peepal trees which have broad base and knocked them down completely – Oh one who has such great archery skills!
- *kondār taṇ am tuḻāyināy* – He destroyed the peepal trees while having the garlands decorating him \[i.e., he destroyed them effortlessly without even having the garlands disturbed\]. Even if [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is wearing any garland matching the particular incarnation \[emperumān may be wearing different types of flower garlands in different incarnations\], they will appear as tuḷasi garland only for [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/). kondār – densely spread.
- *amudē* – the form of śrī rāma aiming for the peepal trees is most reliśable to [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/).
- *unnai* … – While uniting he mixed seamlessly (like water mixing in water) and now if he says “I am leaving”, can that be allowed? Even if he leaves, he should take me along.
- *maindā* – Due to uniting with me, you have acquired this new youthful charm!
- *vān ēṟē* – Like being supreme after having given his experience to nityasūris, here [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is giving experience to [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) and manifesting his supremacy.
- *ini engup pōginṟadē* – Are you leaving me who cannot sustain without you and going to those who can sustain without you? If you can leave nityasūris, you can leave me too. While āḻvār was removing [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s doubt of “what if [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) leaves me?” why is āḻvār saying “Don’t leave me”? emperumān being distinct/great,  he would doubt and would also make the other person ([āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)) doubt about the togetherness \[due to extreme love for each other\].

nampiḷḷai beautifully explains that [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) should not leave [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) by giving context for each word/phrase in the end.

- *endāy* – Would you leave because you are not my lord? (No, you are my lord and thus cannot leave me – in this same way, each point to be concluded).
- *taṇ tiruvēngadattuḷ ninṟāy* – Would you leave because you are far away from me?
- *ilangai seṟṟāy* – Would you leave because you do not have the ability to destroy the hurdles/enemies?
- *marāmaram …* – Would you leave because you would not take up weapons to help your devotees?
- *kondār taṇ am tuḻāyināy* – Would you leave because you have not decorated yourself with a garland \[vowing\] to protect your devotee?
- *amudē* – Would you leave because you are not sweet by nature?
- *unnai en uḷḷē kuḻaitta* – Would you leave because you have not united with me seamlessly?
- *en maindā* – Would you leave because you are not youthful?
- *vānēṟē* – Would you leave because you are lacking supremacy?
- *ini engup pōginṟadē* – Even if you leave, you have to take me along with you. Would you unite with me seamlessly and still leave alone?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.6.10. Poginra kalangal

*pōginṟa kālangaḷ pōya kālangaḷ pōgu kālangaḷ – tāy tandai uyir āginṟāy unnai nān adaindēn viduvēnō? pāginṟa tol pugaḻ mūvulagukkum nādanē! paramā! taṇ vēngadam mēginṟāy! taṇ tuḻāy virai nāṟu kaṇṇiyanē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

pōginṟa kālangaḷ pōya kālangaḷ pōgu kālangaḷ – present, past and future times; tāy tandai uyirāginṟāy – one who is caring for me like my mother, father and self; pāginṟa – spreading thus to protect all; tol – eternally present; pugaḻ – having \[auspicious\] qualities; mūvulagukkum – for the three types of cētana \[sentient – nityāatmās (eternally free), muktātmās (liberated), baddātmās (bound in material realm)\] and acētana \[insentient – śudda satva (pure goodness), miśra satva (mixed goodness – satva/rajas/tamas), satva śūnya (kālam – time)\]; nādanē – being the lord; paramā – having no one superior for such greatness; taṇ – cool (giving relief from fatigue); vēngadam – in tirumalā; mēginṟāy – staying there out of love, being easily approachable; taṇ – cool; tuḻāy – having tuḷasi leaves; virai – fragrance; nāṟu – spreading; kaṇṇiyanē – oh one who is wearing garlands!; unnai – you who are of such qualities; adaindēn – having united; nān – I; viduvēnō – will \[I\] leave?

**Перевод:**

**Simple translation (based on vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar‘s 12000 padi)**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the tenth pāsuram  – āḻvār says “After visualizing/experiencing you who favoured me in all manners in all times (past, present and future), is there any reason for me to leave you?”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “Having attained you and seen your favours, would I leave you?”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Tenth pāsuram. When emperumān says “I won’t leave you; but you have to see that you don’t leave me”, āḻvār replies “after seeing your favours, is there any reason for me to leave you?” He says that since you are related to me in all manners in all times (past, present and future), there is no reason to leave you. போகின்ற காலங்கள் போய காலங்கள் போகு காலங்கள் – தாய் தந்தை உயிர் ஆகின்றாய் உன்னை நான் அடைந்தேன் விடுவேனோ? பாகின்ற தொல் புகழ் மூவுலகுக்கும் நாதனே! பரமா! தண் வேங்கடம் மேகின்றாய் தண் துழாய் விரை நாறு கண்ணியனே pōginṟa kālangaḷ pōya kālangaḷ pōgu kālangaḷ – tāy tandai uyir āginṟāy unnai nān adaindēn viduvēnō? pāginṟa tol pugaḻ mūvulagukkum nādanē! paramā! taṇ vēngadam mēginṟāy! taṇ tuḻāy virai nāṟu kaṇṇiyanē!*

- *pōginṟa* … –  Taking care of me in all three times (past, present and future) like a mother, doing what a father who is focused on the well-being of the child would do and even if they give up as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 38.33 “*sa pitrā ca parityakta:*” (being given up by his (kākāsura) own mother and father), like ones’ own ātmā would care for oneself, after attaining you who are being the apt lord and the one who favoured, how can I, who has gratitude, leave you?
- *pāginṟa …* – As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 21.20 “*vidita: …*” (known by everyone popularly as virtuous and one who is affectionate towards the surrendered ones), [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) being famous and pervaded even in the enemy camp, naturally having auspicious qualities, being the lord of the three worlds (all worlds and the residents of such worlds).
- *paramā* – if we think about you for auspicious qualities and protection, not having anyone else matching such greatness, and being greater than all. To be understood as – having such greatness, to accept my service, you have arrived into the cool tirumalā; I have attained you, would I leave you now?
- *taṇ tuḻāy virai nāṟu kaṇṇiyanē* – Having accepted [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) and eliminated all his sufferings, giving him wonderful experience and having his own doubts of “what if āḻvār leaves?” also eliminated, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is gracefully standing there with the beautiful garlands which have wonderful fragrance and design.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.6.11. Kannit tannandulay

*kaṇṇit taṇ am tuḻāy mudik kamalat tadam perum kaṇṇanaip – pugaḻ naṇṇit ten kurugūrc catakōpan māṟan sonna eṇṇil sōrvu il andādi āyirattuḷ ivaiyum ōr pattu isaiyodum paṇṇil pāda vallār avar kēśavan tamarē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kaṇṇi – in the form of a garland; taṇ – cool; am tuḻāy – being decorated with tuḷasi; mudi – crown; kamalam – delight to watch like a lotus flower; tadam – broad; perum – wide; kaṇṇanai – one who is having divine eyes; pugaḻ – qualities (which make him unite with his devotees); naṇṇi – reach; then – beautiful; kurugūr – being the leader of āḻvārtirunagari; māṟan – having “māṟan” as his family name; satakōpan – nammāḻvār; sonna – mercifully compiled; eṇṇil – bhagavān‘s wishes; sōrvil – without missing; andādi – in the form of antādi (last word of one pāsuram, being connected to the first word of next pāsuram); āyirattuḷ – in the thousand pāsurams; ōr – distinct/unique; ivai pattum – these ten pāsurams; isaiyodum – with music; paṇṇil – with proper tune; pāda vallār avar – those who can sing; kēśavan tamar – will become inseparably related to sarvēśvaran who is greater than all

**Перевод:**

**emperumān is wearing a crown which is decorated with cool and beautiful tuḷasi in the form of a garland and he has broad and wide divine eyes; nammāḻvār, the leader of āḻvārtirunagari, who has the family name “māṟan”, approached such emperumān’s qualities (which make him unite with his devotees); those who can sing these distinct/unique ten pāsurams, which are revealing bhagavān‘s wishes and are part of the thousand pāsurams which are mercifully compiled by such āḻvār, with music in a proper tune, will be inseparably related to sarvēśvaran who is greater than all.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the end, āḻvār says “those who joyfully recite or meditate upon this decad will be accepted by bhagavān“.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār explains becoming a servitor of bhagavān as the result of this decad.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*In the end, āḻvār says “those who practice this decad, whoever they may be, their kula (family tree), caraṇa (śākā – subdivision – the vēda they belong to), gōtram (clan) etc will become irrelevant; due to their being engaged in singing these pāsurams, they will be identified as servitors of bhagavān”. கண்ணித் தண் அம் துழாய் முடிக் கமலத் தடம் பெருங் கண்ணனைப் – புகழ் நண்ணி தென் குருகூர்ச் சடகோபன் மாறன் சொன்ன எண்ணில் சோர்வு இல் அந்தாதி ஆயிரத்துள் இவையும் ஓர் பத்து இசையொடும் பண்ணில் பாட வல்லார் அவர் கேசவன் தமரே kaṇṇit taṇ am tuḻāy mudik kamalat tadam perum kaṇṇanaip – pugaḻ naṇṇit then kurugūrc catakōpan māṟan sonna eṇṇil sōrvu il andādi āyirattuḷ ivaiyum ōr pattu isaiyodum paṇṇil pāda vallār avar kēśavan tamarē*

- *kaṇṇi* … – Only now (after hearing [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) saying that he will not leave [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)), emperumān’s garlands became fresh, crown became well decorated and eyes became broad and shining.
- *pugaḻ naṇṇi* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) being drenched in the love that was shown by [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) towards himself
- *then kurugūrc catakōpan māṟan* – one is his divine name (māṟan); another explains him as being a terror for the enemies.
- *eṇṇil sōrvil andādi* – after contemplating upon the love [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) has shown towards him, this decad which is part of the thousand pāsurams that reveals without missing any of such aspects that were enjoyed by [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)
- *isaiyodum paṇṇil pāda vallār* – those who are able to lovingly sing these pāsurams with music and tune. paṇ – music; isai – pitch variation – high pitch, low pitch etc, matching nicely.
- *avar kēśavan tamarē* – Whoever they are, their kula, caraṇa, gōtra etc become irrelevant; just as it is said in “*viṇṇappam seyvārgaḷ*” (aṟaiyars who sing pāsurams with tune, i.e., without specifically identifying their name, surname etc., as they are simply identified by their title), due to this reason of singing these pāsurams, they will become [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s servitors.

Finally, nampiḷḷai summarizes the contents of this decad briefly.

- In the first pāsuram, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) eliminated [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s doubt “what if āḻvār leaves me?”
- In the second pāsuram, he explained the freshness acquired by [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) after having such doubt eliminated.
- In the third pāsuram, he became delighted thinking about [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s generosity towards him.
- In the fourth pāsuram, when asked “what was his generosity towards you?”, he replies “he created detachment for matters other than [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)“.
- In the fifth pāsuram, he said “after having detachment towards matters other than [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/), having engaged in ultimate servitorśip towards bhagavān, I will never leave you”.
- In the sixth pāsuram, he said “You being the helper of your devotees, is there any worry for me?”.
- In the seventh pāsuram, he said “there is no worry for my relatives and their relatives”.
- In the eighth pāsuram, he explained the means that got him this result.
- In the ninth pāsuram,  [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) desiring to know his heart, moves away a little bit and āḻvār says “you cannot leave me”.
- In the tenth pāsuram, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) says “I won’t leave you; but you need to ensure that you don’t leave me” and āḻvār replies “there is no reason to leave you, who are related to me in all times (past, present and future) and in all manners”.
- In the end, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) explains the result for those who learnt this decad and completes the same.

[āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) tiruvadigaḷē śaraṇam  
[emperumānār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/emperumanar/) tiruvadigaḷē śaraṇam  
[piḷḷān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/pillan/) tiruvadigaḷē śaraṇam  
[nanjīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nanjiyar/) tiruvadigaḷē śaraṇam  
[nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/) tiruvadigaḷē śaraṇam  
[vadakkut tiruvīdip piḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadakku-thiruvidhi-pillai/) tiruvadigaḷē śaraṇam  
[periyavāccān piḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/periyavachchan-pillai/) tiruvadigaḷē śaraṇam  
[vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/) tiruvadigaḷē śaraṇam  
[jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/mamunigal/) tiruvadigaḷē śaraṇam

In the next article we will enjoy the next decad.

## 2.7 Kesavan tamar

## 2.7.1. Kesavan tamar

*kēśavan tamar kīḻ mēl emar ēḻ eḻu piṟappum māsadir idu peṟṟu nammudai vāḻvu vāykkinṟavā! īsan en karu māṇikkam en sengōlak kaṇṇan viṇṇōr nāyagan em pirān emmān nārāyaṇanālē*

**Пословный перевод:**

īsan – having lordship (towards everyone); en karumāṇikkam – (instead of such common aspect towards everyone) showing his blue-emerald like form; en sem kōlak kaṇṇan – (contrasting his bluish form) making me exist fully for him with his reddish beautiful divine eyes; viṇṇōr nāyagan – acknowledged by the nityasūris too; empirān – giving me joy; emmān – due to being my lord; nārāyaṇālē – by śrīman nārāyaṇan (who has unlimited vātsalyam (motherly forbearance); kīḻ mēl ēḻ eḻu piṟappum – seven generations of ancestors and descendants; kēśavan tamar – devotees of kēśava (who is greater than all); emar – mine; idu – this (unconditional acknovledgement of bhagavān); mā – great; sadir – glory; peṟṟu – having acquired; nammudaiya – our; vāḻvu – this wealth of śrīvaiṣṇavam; vāykkinṟavā – flourishing!

**Перевод:**

**śrīman nārāyaṇan (who has unlimited vātsalyam (motherly forbearance) who is having lordship (towards everyone) and who is (instead of such common aspect towards everyone) showing his blue-emerald like form and (contrasting his bluish form) making me exist fully for him with his reddish beautiful divine eyes, acknowledged by the nityasūris too, is giving his experience; By such emperumān, due to being my lord, those devotees of kēśava (who is greater than all) who are my seven generations of ancestors and descendants acquired this great glory which is our wealth of śrīvaiṣṇavam and are flourishing.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In first pāsuram – āḻvār becomes delighted seeing emperumān becoming attached to his relatives also due to great attachment towards āḻvār himself.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*In first pāsuram – āḻvār mercifully explains how his clan members became the target of bhagavān‘s affection.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. கேசவன் தமர் கீழ் மேல் எமர் ஏழ் எழு பிறப்பும் மா சதிர் இது பெற்று நம்முடை வாழ்வு வாய்க்கின்றவா! ஈசன் என் கரு மாணிக்கம் என் செங்கோலக் கண்ணன் விண்ணோர் நாயகன் எம் பிரான் எம்மான் நாராயணனாலே kēśavan tamar kīḻ mēl emar ēḻ eḻu piṟappum māsadir idu peṟṟu nammudai vāḻvu vāykkinṟavā! īsan en karu māṇikkam en sengōlak kaṇṇan viṇṇōr nāyagan em pirān emmān nārāyaṇanālē*

- *kēśavan tamar* – \[3 explanations\] those devotees who are attracted to [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who has beautiful hair locks; those devotees who are attracted to [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) being engaged in destroying enemies \[like killing the horse demon kēśi\]; those devotees who are attracted to emperumān being the controller of all as said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 5.3.14 “*ka iti brahmaṇō nāma īsōham sarvadēhinām \| āvām tavāngē sambhūtau tasmāt kēsavanāmavān \|\|*” (ka indicates brahmā; I am (rudra) the lord of all entities (in the material world); Both of us appeared from your body as a part; Thus you have the name kēśava which means ka and īśa were born from you – as said by Siva towards [śrīman nārāyaṇan](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)). [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) likes them because they are devotees of sarvēśvaran. emperumān likes them because āḻvār calls them “*emar*” (mine). From this we can understand that – to be pursued by emperumān, one needs to have the affection of a śrīvaiṣṇava.
- *kēśavan tamar* – śrīvaiṣṇavas who are won over by [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s divine bodily beauty.
- *kīḻ mēl* … – my ancestors, descendants of seven (many) generations became his devotees. This is explained in following pramāṇams \[For ordinary virtuous acts, great benefits are explained in śāstram – what to speak of being related to a śrīvaiṣṇava\]:
   - mahābhāratam – bhīśma saying to darmaputra (yudiśtra) – “*ēkāhamapi kauntēya bhūmistam udagam kuru \| kulam tārayatē tāta! sapta saptaca sapta ca*” (Oh yudiśtra, my dear child! at least one day offer water to earth; that will help uplift your 21 generations of family members).
   - bōdāyana darmam *– “daśapūrvān daśāparātmānam ca”* (10 generations  before, self and 10 generations after) \[will be purified\]
- *mā sadir idu peṟṟu* – acquiring great glory – tiruvāimoḻi 2.7.6 “*vidi sūḻndadāl*” (due to being drenched in his unconditional grace) or tiruvāimoḻi 2.7.3 “*mādavan enṟadē koṇḍu*” (just for saying mādava) or achieving such glory that whatever result he got, the same result was bestowed to his relatives too.
- *mā sadir idu peṟṟu* – achieving great glory. Having acquired “*tadakkai caturan*” ([emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who has highly capable (generous) wide hands); if something is acquired by one’s own efforts, there would be an end to the result \[hence, the result was bestowed by [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) himself, there is no end to the joy/experience for [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)\].
- *idu peṟṟu* – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is showing his great affection.
- *nammudai vāḻvu vāykkinṟavā* – this is my fortune that he is caring for all those who are related to me.
- *nammudai vāḻvu* – śrīvaiṣṇava sampat – wealth of śrīvaiṣṇavam.
- *vāykkinṟavā* – like a flood which continuously flows without losing its strength. Before it was said “seven (twenty one) generations” – is this not contradicting by saying “continuous without losing strength”? No – that number is just a sample of the full mercy. \[nampiḷḷai saying\] See, it has even reached us.

What is the reason for such mercy of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)?

- *īsan* – he is the apt/natural lord (so he is caring).
- *viṇṇōr nāyagan empirān emmān* – Just like winning over nityasūris by showing his beauty, he would do the same to me and let me experience his beauty – such generous lord.
- *nārāyaṇanālē* – Disregarding his own supremacy, not giving up even those who don’t accept him – since he is the one with vātsalyam (motherly forbearance). Instead of saying “*samitai pādi sāvitri pādi*” (Half samit (wooden blocks/sticks used in fire sacrifices) and Half sāvitri (gāyatri mantram), it is purely out of [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s nirhētuka krupai (unconditional grace) \[brahmācāris while performing samitādānam, need to recite gāyatri mantram 1008 times and also place 1008 samit in the hōmam – it cannot be substituted by half count of mantram and samit. Similarly, this can be accomplished only by unconditional grace – not based on the combination of [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s self effort and his mercy\].

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.
