## 2.7.2. Naranan

*nāraṇan muḻu ēḻ ulagukkum nādan vēda mayan kāraṇam kirisai karumam ivai mudalvan endai sīr aṇangu amarar piṟar palarum toḻudu ētta ninṟu vāraṇattai maruppu ositta pirān en mādavanē*

**Пословный перевод:**

nāraṇan – one who has the name nārāyaṇa; muḻu ēḻ ulagukkum – for all worlds; nādan – being the svāmi (nāta, lord); vēdamayan – he being revealed by vēdam (which primarily speaks about this name); kāraṇam – cause for kriyā (activity); kirisai – kriyā, activity; karumam – kāryam, which is the result of such activity; ivai – for these; mudalvan – being the prime cause; sīr – one who is having \[auspicious\] qualities; aṇangu – divine; amarar – dēvas (celestial beings); piṟar – riśis (sages), manuśyas (humans) et al; palarum – all; toḻudu – vorśipping; ētta – to be praised; ninṟu – stood; vāraṇattai – elephant named kuvalyāpīdam; maruppu – tusk; ositta – broke; pirān – being the most generous lord; en – revealing to me (that all these aspects which fall under the category of nāra (groups of eternal entities) are his wealth); mādavan – kriṣṇa who is śriya:pati (lord of śrī mahālakśmi); endai – is my master who made me fully exist for him

**Перевод:**

**emperumān who has the name nārāyaṇa which means he is the lord of all worlds and is the one who is being revealed by vēdam (which primarily speaks about this name); he is the cause for all activities; he is the activities themselves and he is the result of all such activities; he stood being vorśipped and praised by the divine celestial beings, sages and humans; he appeared as kriṣṇa, being the most generous lord, broke the tusk of the elephant named kuvalayāpīdam; he revealed to me (that all these aspects which fall under the category of nāra (groups of eternal entities) are his wealth); he is kriṣṇa, śriya:pati (lord of śrī mahālakśmi), my master who made me fully exist for him.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār wants to explain the meaning for the name “nārāyaṇa” which was cited in the previous pāsuram and mercifully explains emperumān‘s partiality towards him.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*In the second pāsuram – āḻvār speaks about the meaning of the term “nārāyaṇa” which was cited \[in the previous pāsuram\].*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Second pāsuram. The name “nārāyaṇa” became the subject matter as cited in “nārāyaṇānālē” – here āḻvār ventures into mercifully explaining its meaning. நாரணன் முழு ஏழ் உலகுக்கும் நாதன் வேத மயன் காரணம் கிரிசை கருமம் இவை முதல்வன் எந்தை சீர் அணங்கு அமரர் பிறர் பலரும் தொழுது ஏத்த நின்று வாரணத்தை மருப்பு ஒசித்த பிரான் என் மாதவனே nāraṇan muḻu ēḻ ulagukkum nādan vēda mayan kāraṇam kirisai karumam ivai mudalvan endai sīr aṇangu amarar piṟar palarum toḻudu ētta ninṟu vāraṇattai maruppu ositta pirān en mādavanē*

- *nāraṇan* – when asked, what is the meaning of nāraṇan \[[āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) explains further\] …
- *muḻu ēḻ ulagukkum nādan* – He is the lord of all. What is the authority for that \[How can we validate that\]?
- *vēdamayan* – through many statements such as nārāyāṇa sūktam “*nārāyaṇa parambrahma*” ([nārāyaṇan](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is the supreme brahmam), he is explained as sarvasvāmi (lord of all) \[in vēdam\].
- *kāraṇam kirisai karumam ivai mudalvan* – In all the worlds, he is the controller for all causes \[such as raw-materials – example: five great elements\], results \[the result of such causes – example: the universes\] and activities related to such results \[example: the activities of the residents of universes\]. Also explained as the controller for kriyā sādanam \[the three types of causes – nimitta kāraṇam (instrumental cause), upādāna kāraṇam (raw-material cause) and sahākārikā karaṇam (ancillary cause)\], kriyā \[the activity that arises of such cause\] and the kāryam \[the result of such cause\].
- *endai* – my father
- *sīraṇangu* – The divine lady named [śrī mahālakśmi – periya pirāttiyār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/).
- *sīraṇangamarar …* – Alternatively, *sīraṇangu* is an adjective for amarar (nityasūris – eternally free souls) – i.e., those nityasūris who have divine qualities. Thus irrespective of being insignificant individuals of this material realm or nityasūris who have auspicious qualities and divine nature, everyone accepts his supremacy and praises him; such [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is the most generous person who broke the tusk of the elephant named kuvalayāpīdam as explained in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam “*… na samam yuddamityāhu:…* ” (this is not a fair battle between śrī rāma who is positioned on the ground and the rākśasas who are positioned in their chariots).
- *en mādavanē* – the aspect of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) \[husband of śrī mahālakśmi\] which won him over me. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying “[śrīman nārāyaṇan](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is my lord”.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.7.3. Madavan

*mādavan enṟadē koṇḍu ennai ini ippāl pattadu yādu avangaḷum sēr kodēn enṟu ennuḷ pugundu irundu tīdu avam kedukkum amudam sendāmaraik kaṇ kunṟam kōdu avam il en kannal katti emmān en gōvindanē*

**Пословный перевод:**

en – for me; gōvindan – one who appeared as kriṣṇa; emmān – one who is my svāmi (lord); mādavan – śrīmān (mādava – the lord of lakshmi); enṟadē – considering that word (which was uttered without heart’s intent) alone; koṇḍu – having that as the reason; ennai – me (who does not know the difference between different utterings); ini – after uttering; ippāl pattadu – for the subsequent times; avangaḷ – (avam – sin/defect) defects such as avidyā (ignorance); yādum – completely; sērkodēn – will not let them approach/affect; enṟu – vowing that; en uḷ – in my heart; pugundu – entered; irundu – stayed there without any other thought; tīdu – vices (which were committed knowingly); avam – (incidental) vices; kedukkum – destroying; amudam – eternally sweet; sem – reddish; tāmarai – lotus like; kaṇ – divine eyes; kunṟam – letting me experience his well established divine form; kōdu – the type of defect that arises due to mixing with other objects; avam – the type of defect that arises due to being cooked; il – not having; en kannal katti – sweet like a block of sugar

**Перевод:**

**emperumān who appeared as kriṣṇa for me, who is my lord, considered my uttering (which was uttered without heart’s intent) of “śrīmān” (mādava – the lord of śrī mahālakśmi) alone as the reason and saved me from being approached by defects such as avidyā (ignorance) after uttering that word; vowing this, he entered into my heart, stayed there without any other thought, being eternally sweet, eliminated all my defects (which were committed knowingly or unknowingly); due to this union, he allowed me to experience his divine reddish lotus-like eyes and well-established divine form like a block of sugar without having any defects (that arise due to mixing with other objects or being cooked).**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*(mādavan) āḻvār wonders to himself “What is the aspect in me which caused emperumān to transform me to become a vaiṣṇava and pursue those who are related with me too?” and explains that in this pāsuram.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the third pāsuram – āḻvār says “emperumān eliminated all my defects and accepted me just for saying the name mādava”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār mercifully explains the favours done by emperumān being partial towards him merely for his (āḻvār’s) word \[of saying mādava\].*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Third pāsuram. Previously āḻvār said “mā sadir idu peṟṟu” (acquired this great glory); when asked the reason for this, āḻvār says “unknowingly I had spoken the words the residents of anta:puram (private quarters of the queens)”. bhattar said in śrī guṇaratna kōśam 52 “… jāmātā dayitastavēti bhavatīsambandadruśtyā harim paśyēma …” (Oh mother lakshmi! Like the residents of mitilā who loved śrī rāma due to your relationship with him, in the same manner, we who are engaged in your beautiful service too, approach sarvēśvaran (lord of all) namperumāḷ who is called as jāmātā (aḻagiya maṇavāḷan) and who is your lord, look at him, serve him etc. On seeing his joy during those times, we too would feel blissful \[This ślōkam is quoted to establish that the residents of anta:puram (those who serve tāyār) would glorify perumāḷ\]. மாதவன் என்றதே கொண்டு என்னை இனி இப்பால் பட்டது யாது அவங்களும் சேர் கொடேன் என்று என்னுள் புகுந்து இருந்து தீது அவம் கெடுக்கும் அமுதம் செந்தாமரைக் கண் குன்றம் கோது அவம் இல் என் கன்னல் கட்டி எம்மான் என் கோவிந்தனே mādavan enṟadē koṇḍu ennai ini ippāl pattadu yādu avangaḷum sēr kodēn enṟu ennuḷ pugundu irundu tīdu avam kedukkum amudam sendāmaraik kaṇ kunṟam kōdu avam il en kannal katti emmān en gōvindanē*

- *mādavan enṟadē koṇḍu* – For me, merely uttering the word “*mādava*“; he considered this itself as a great act of commitment. Considering that “[āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) knows the difference between the other names and this name” and treats that as a great thing.
- *ennai* – me who does not know the difference between other names of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) and this name.
- *ini* – whatever time that is gone cannot be retrieved; the remaining times looked like a short duration for [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/). Like a cētana ([jīvātmā – soul](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)) feels towards [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) after taking refuge of bhagavān as said in mudal tiruvandādi 16 “*paḻudē pala pagalum pōyina*” (I have wasted all these times), bhagavān is having that same feeling towards me ([āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)) now. This is like how śrī rāma felt in śrī rāmāyaṇam kiśkintā kāṇḍam 30.3 “… *buddvā kālamatītanca mumōha …*” (śrī rāma fell unconscious thinking about how sugrīva is attached to his sense of enjoyment and the time lost in rescuing sītā pirātti).
- *ippāl pattadu* – Lost time is like water that crossed the dam, at least the water that is still there should be preserved.
- *yādu avangaḷum sēr kodēn enṟu* – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) vowing “I will not let you go through any difficult penance and suffer \[to attain me\]”. Holding on to upāyāntarams (other means such as karma yōga, jñāna yōga, bhakti yōga etc) instead of emperumān himself, is like entering into a river with a heavy rock tied on to oneself \[it will only drown the individual\]. avam – avidyā (ignorance) etc., that lead to narakam (hell). emperumān is vowing that he will not let [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) leave him by (a) making him pursue other goals, (b) making him shy away considering himself to be unworthy and (c) letting him pursue other means.
- *enṟu* – vowing as done in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 29.10 “…*ētat vratam mama*” (this is my vow).
- *pugundu* – After vowing, instead of staying away from me, he entered into my heart.
- *irundu* – After entering too, since there may be option to leave, like “sugrīva mahāraja mischievously closed the entrance of the cave in which vāli entered”, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) stood there firmly closing all options to leave.
- *pugundu irundu* – instead of having [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) try to reach him, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) himself entered āḻvār’s heart and stayed there firmly.

What did he do after entering?

- *tīdu avam kedukkum* – two explanations:
   - tīdu – all vices which were knowingly committed before tiruviruttam 1 “*poy ninṟa jñānam*“, i.e., all vices which were committed before being blessed by [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) with true knowledge. avam – all mistakes which were unknowingly committed after acquiring knowledge.  By these two, the hurdles which stop one from attaining [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) are explained.
   - As explained in śrī rāmāyaṇam kiśkintā kāṇḍam 33.12 “*gōgnē caiva surāpē ca cōrē bhagnavratē tatā \| niśkrutirvihitā sadbhi: krutagnē nāsti niśkruti: \|\|*” (Atonement is explained by elders for killing cows, consuming liquor, stealing and those who slip in their vows; but there is no atonement explained for those who are ungrateful), tīdu and avam could indicate those sins/vices which can be atoned and those which cannot be atoned \[need to be experienced without fail\].

Would he give a bitter medicine to eliminate these?

- *amudam* – he eliminated those vices by making me experience his sweetness.
- *sem tāmaraik kaṇ kunṟam* – Not sweet just for the tongue, he is sweet/delightful to the eyes as well.
- *kunṟam* – Having tall/radiant form which shines as if he has eliminated his own defects instead of eliminating [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s defects. As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 2.42 “*vyasanēśu manuśyāṇām bhruśam bhavati dukkita:*” (He feels the pain of the suffering of lowest of humans) \[similarly, any joy acquired for his devotees, he would consider that joy for himself as well\].
- *kōdu avam il en kannal katti* – kōdu – an object getting spoiled after mixing with another object \[like if sugar is on its own, it will stay fresh, but when it comes in contact with water, it will start deteriorating\]. avam – an object getting spoiled when it is cooked \[sugar, when it gets cooked, will start deteriorating\]. In the case of [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) \[who is explained through this example of sugar\], kōdu – favouring [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) to manifest (show off) his own mercy \[it should instead be done to fulfil the natural relationship\]; avam – doing it as a help to the [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) \[it should instead be done purely for [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s pleasure\]. He would be so sweet that one cannot imagine any other sweet object.
- *emmān* – my lord, who won over me fully and made me think that “there is nothing sweeter than him”.
- *en gōvindanē* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) thinks that kriṣṇāvatāram was done for [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) only. periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 1.7.11 “*ātkoḷḷat tōnṟiya āyar tam kō*” ([emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who appeared to win over others as the leader of covherd clan).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.7.4. Govindan

*gōvindan kudak kūttan kōvalan enṟu enṟē kunittu tēvum tannaiyum pādi ādat tirutti ennaik koṇḍu en – pāvam tannaiyum pāṟak kaittu emar ēḻ eḻu piṟappum mēvum tanmaiyam ākkinān vallan em pirān vittuvē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vallan – being capable (of completing any task he desires); vittu – pervading all objects \[as viṣṇu\]; empirān – my lord who acknowledged me (like rounding up a town to catch a single person\]; gōvindan – (suiting his birth) having abundance of cows; kudak kūttan – (expressing the joy of such abundance of cattle through) being a dancer (with pots); kōvalan – having a birth in covherd clan (which matches such wealth and activities); enṟu enṟē – saying these aspects individually; kunittu – dancing out of great joy; tēvum – dēvatvam – supremacy (which is the cause for such simplicity); tannaiyum – his special aspect of simplicity; pādi – singing (to express the joy); Ada – to dance; tirutti – reformed me (to be on a par with nityasūris like an alchemist who would change iron to gold); ennai – me; koṇḍu – accepting (me as his own); en – my; pāvam tannaiyum – sins; pāṟa – to run away; kaittu – drove; emar – those who are related to me; ēḻ eḻu piṟappum – seven times seven births; mēvum tanmaiyum – made us to desire for him and attain him; ākkinān – done

**Перевод:**

**emperumān being capable (of completing any task he desires), pervading all objects \[as viṣṇu\] is my lord who acknowledged me (like rounding up a town to catch a single person\]; he is having abundance of cows, (expressing the joy of such abundance of cattle through) being a dancer (with pots) matching his birth in the covherd clan. He made me dance and sing out of great joy saying individually his aspects such as his supremacy (which is the cause for simplicity) and his special aspect of simplicity. He reformed me (to be on a par with nityasūris like an alchemist who would change iron to gold) and accepted me. He also drove my sins to run away from me and reformed my relatives of seven times seven births \[many many ancestors/descendants\]. How great is his capability!**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fourth pāsuram, āḻvār becomes amazed thinking “How ingenious is he! He has changed those who are related to me like myself”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār explains the ingenuity of emperumān for bestowing the same favour to all his relatives and their families too.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. கோவிந்தன் குடக் கூத்தன் கோவலன் என்று என்றே குனித்துத் தேவும் தன்னையும் பாடி ஆடத் திருத்தி என்னைக் கொண்டு என் – பாவம் தன்னையும் பாறக் கைத்து எமர் ஏழ் எழு பிறப்பும் மேவும் தன்மையம் ஆக்கினான் வல்லன் எம் பிரான் விட்டுவே gōvindan kudak kūttan kōvalan enṟu enṟē kunittu tēvum tannaiyum pādi ādat tirutti ennaik koṇḍu en – pāvam tannaiyum pāṟak kaittu emar ēḻ eḻu piṟappum mēvum tanmaiyam ākkinān vallan em pirān vittuvē*

- *gōvindan* – This wealth is not even seen in śrīvaikuṇṭam (spiritual realm). Wealth due to abundance of cows is only seen here \[in vrindāvanam\].
- *kudak kūttan* – Like brāhmaṇas would perform fire sacrifices when there is abundance of wealth, when covherds get abundance of wealth, they would spend it by dancing with pots. [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) who is explained in cāndōjña upaniśat as “*avākyanādara:*” (anādara: – not caring for anyone since he has no desires left to be fulfilled;  avākī – he maintains silence considering everything else as unworthy of conversation – this is [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s state in śrīvaikuṇṭam), dancing crazily like well-grown crop swinging in heavy wind.
- *kōvalan* – gōpāla (covherd) – having birth which matches aforementioned qualities / activities. This wealth was earned by [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) taking birth in this covherd clan.
- *enṟu enṟē kunittu* – contemplating such aspects, \[[āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)\] naturally started dancing; when āḻvār thinks about bhagavān’s dependence on his devotees \[as in kriṣṇāvatāram\], he cannot stop glorifying it.
- *tēvum* – Here *dēvatvam* (supremacy) indicates aisvaryam \[ability to control all\]; *tannai* (self – natural aspect) indicates being controlled by his devotees; this dependence towards his devotees is his natural quality; vaśiśta said to śrī rāma in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 111.7 “… *ātmānam nātivartētā: …*” (You accept bharata’s words and ensure that your true nature of being dependent on your devotees is retained). Some would say it as “*ātmabhūtam bharatam* *nātivartētā*:” (Don’t lose bharata who is like your ātmā). But [bhattar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/parasara-bhattar/) would explain it as “vaśiśta is saying ‘your natural quality is to be dependent on your devotees. By discarding your brother’s request, don’t lose your such natural quality'”.
- *pādi ādat tirutti* – What is the difference between “*enṟu enṟē kunittu*” and here (also speaking about dancing and singing)? Previously his simplicity was glorified while dancing/singing; here both supremacy and simplicity are glorified while dancing/singing. So, it can be explained that the object of singing/dancing is different in two places. Alternative explanation: Previously, it can be said as [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) just starting to dance/sing without full intent of his heart and now he is fully engrossed into it with full intent of his heart.
- *tirutti* – Like a barren land is refined to be fertile, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is transformed to have the behaviour/activities of nityasūris.
- *ennaik koṇḍu* – accepting me. If [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says “now he made me pursue him through some means”, that will not match āḻvār’s philosophy which emphasises on his acquiring this glory due to [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s grace only. So, what is āḻvār saying here? Like a person would pick-up a precious gem from mud, wash it thoroughly and use it to his heart’s content, bhagavān accepted him, destroyed āḻvār’s sins which cannot be destroyed by self efforts and drove those sins away.
- *emar* … – Not only he did this for me, but he bestowed the same mercy of reaching him naturally for my ancestors/descendants for many generations.
- *empirān vittu vallan* – sarvēsvaran who is my saviour, who can do whatever he pleases. Is there anything that cannot be done by the omnipotent lord? [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) considers [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s omnipresence also is for him only.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.7.5. Vittilangu

*vittu ilangu senjōdit tāmarai pādam kaigaḷ kaṇgaḷ vittu ilangu karunjudar malaiyē tiruvudambu vittu ilangu madiyam sīr sangu cakkaram paridi vittu ilangu mudi ammān madusūdanan tanakkē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vittu – being viṣṇu; vittu – spread; ilangu – shining; mudi – having a crown; ammān – being the lord/master; madusūdanan tanakku – for madusūdana; ilangu – adding splendour; sem – reddish; sōdi – having radiance; tāmaraiyē – like a lotus flower; pādam – divine feet; kaigaḷ – divine hands; kaṇgaḷ – divine eyes; vittu – well expanded; ilangu – shining; karum – bluish; sudar – having rays; malaiyē – like a mountain; tiru – beautiful; udambu – form; sīr – beautiful; sangu – his pāncajanyam – conch; vittu – expanded; ilangu – shining; madiyamē – like the moon; cakkaram – sudarśana cakram – disc (wheel); vittilangu – similar (expanded and shining); paridiyē – like the sun

**Перевод:**

**Being viṣṇu, my lord madusūdanan who is having well-spread shining crown, has reddish radiant divine feet, divine hands and divine eyes which are adding splendour to him;his divine body looks like a shining bluish mountain with bright rays; his beautiful conch looks like the well-expanded shining moon; his disc looks like similarly shining sun.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fifth pāsuram – āḻvār says “emperumān reformed me and those who are related to me to enjoy emperumān, only by showing his beauty”. This also explains āḻvār saying “emperumān acquired unsurpassed radiance by accepting āḻvār and those who are related to āḻvār”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Fifth pāsuram. When emperumānār was listening to the meanings of tiruvāimoḻi from tirumālai āṇḍān, emperumānār would give explanations to pāsurams and would ask āṇḍān “is this meaning apt?”. āṇḍān would reply “this is like viśvāmitra sruśti \[viśvāmitra created a new heavenly planet for trisangu; āṇḍān used to say emperumānār is explaining pāsurams in a newer way which is not explained by elders\]; I have not heard this from āḷavandār“; When explaining this pāsuram, āṇḍān asked emperumānār “Is there any viśvāmitra sruśti (new explanation) for this pāsuram?”, emperumānār replied “āḻvār is saying in this pāsuram ’emperumān showed his physical beauty and made me to be fully subservient to him'”. In addition, bhattar also mercifully explains a meaning for this pāsuram – emperumān acquired new radiance in his body after accepting āḻvār and those who are related to āḻvār”; it is like as explained in śrī rāmāyaṇam 131.15 “viśōditajata: snātaścitramālyānulēpana: \| mahārhavasanō rāmastastau tatra śriyā jvalan \|\|” (having washed his locks of hair, having mercifully bathed, wearing many different flower garlands, sandalwood paste, expensive clothes, śrī rāma shone radiantly along with the wealth of beauty in that throne – in this ślōkam, it is explained that śrī rāma acquired new radiance after accepting bharata). விட்டு இலங்கு செஞ்சோதித் தாமரை பாதம் கைகள் கண்கள் விட்டு இலங்கு கருஞ்சுடர் மலையே திரு உடம்பு விட்டு இலங்கு மதியம் சீர் சங்கு சக்கரம் பரிதி விட்டு இலங்கு முடி அம்மான் மதுசூதனன் தனக்கே vittu ilangu senjōdit tāmarai pādam kaigaḷ kaṇgaḷ vittu ilangu karunjudar malaiyē tiruvudambu vittu ilangu madiyam sīr sangu cakkaram paridi vittu ilangu mudi ammān madusūdanan tanakkē*

- *vittilangu* … (1st line) – The divine feet at which [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) offers obeisances after [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) wins over āḻvār, the divine hands that embrace āḻvār, the divine eyes that shower cool glance towards āḻvār – all these look reddish splendorous lotus flower having radiance that is like greatly flowing like water from a dam. Since the example (lotus) is not a direct match for the object (emperumān), āḻvār is saying “*tāmarai pādam…*” (lotus feet) instead of saying “*tāmarai pōnṟa pādam*” (lotus like feet). Alternatively, it is explained as viṣṇu’s radiant reddish divine feet, hands, eyes \[This alternative explanation is similar to 12000 padi vyākhyānam\].
- *vittilangu* … (upto end of the pāsuram) – His bodily beauty is as explained in śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 38.15 “*śōbhayan daṇḍakāraṇyam …*” (śrī rāma through his radiant appearance made the whole daṇḍakāraṇyam shine and he looked like a freshly radiant moon); [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) felt the cool comfort of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) when emperumān embraced him. pāncajanyam (his conch) looked like a radiantly shining moon.
- *sīr sangu* – Wealth acquired due to close proximity of [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/). nāciyār tirumoḻi 7.8 “*uṇbadu sollil ulagaḷandān vāyamudam kaṇpadai koḷḷil kadalvaṇṇan kaittalattē*” (He \[pāncajanya, the divine conch\] eats the nectar from the mouth of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who measured the worlds; he rests on the hands of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) whose complexion resembles sea-water). Like those devotees who simply eat [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s food remnants and rest inside the temple, pāncajanyam gets fed directly from bhagavān’s mouth and rests on his hand enjoying his beauty (from close proximity).
- *sīr sangu* – As said in nāciyār tirumoḻi 7.7 “*un selvam sāla aḻagiyadu*” (your wealth is most worthy) – this is the real wealth.
- *cakkaram paridi* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is citing sun as example to explain sudarśana chakra’s radiance though sudarśana chakra’s radiance is unlimited in comparison to the limited radiance of sun.
- *vittilangu mudi* – the radiance of his crown will subside the radiance of all of these.
- *ammān madusūdanan tanakkē* – for the one who is sarvēśvaran (supreme lord) and being the destroyer of enemies.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.7.6. Madusudanai anri

*madusūdanai anṟi maṟṟu ilēn enṟu ettālum karumam inṟi tudi sūḻnda pādalgaḷ pādi āda ninṟu ūḻi ūḻi toṟum edir sūḻal pukku enaittōr piṟappum enakkē aruḷgaḷ seyya vidi sūḻndadāl enakkēl ammān tirivikkiramanaiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

madusūdanai anṟi – Other than madusūdanan (who removed my obstacles); maṟṟu – any other goal; ilēn – I don’t have; enṟu – saying thus; ettālum – with anything; karumam – expectation for a result; inṟi – not having; tudi – in the form of stōtram (praises); sūḻnda – covering (his countless qualities); pādalgaḷai – songs; ninṟu – staying firm (without attachment for ulterior motives); pādi – sing; ādi – dance; ūḻi ūḻi toṟum – kalpa (a day of brahmā) after kalpa; enaittu – many; ōr – unique/distinct; piṟappum – in births; edir – to be friendly with me; sūḻal pukku – appearing with tricks; enakkē – exclusively for me; aruḷgaḷ – favours (from initial merciful blessing to total devotion towards him); seyya – to do; enakku – for me; ēl – position himself; ammān – being my lord; tirivikkiramanai – trivikrama; vidi – mercy in the form of unavoidable destiny; sūḻndadu – wrapped

**Перевод:**

**Saying “I don’t have any goal other than madusūdanan (who removed my obstacles)” without any expectation for any results, I sing and dance covering his countless qualities in the form of stōtrams (praises); to transform me to such state, he took many many distinct/unique births in kalpa (day of brahmā) after kalpa, assuming different forms to do different tricks to become friendly with me; such lord trivikrama of mine who positioned himself to favour me exclusively, became overwhelmed/wrapped with mercy in the form of unavoidable destiny.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the sixth pāsuram – āḻvār says “emperumān out of his compassion worked hard, for a long time, to develop my devotion towards him”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār explains emperumān‘s binding to his compassion which is the trigger for the favours done by him, which caused him this great splendour.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. மதுசூதனை அன்றி மற்று இலேன் என்று எத்தாலும் கருமம் இன்றி துதி சூழ்ந்த பாடல்கள் பாடி ஆட நின்று ஊழி ஊழி தொறும் எதிர் சூழல் புக்கு எனைத்தோர் பிறப்பும் எனக்கே அருள்கள் செய்ய விதி சூழ்ந்ததால் எனக்கேல் அம்மான் திரிவிக்கிரமனையே madusūdanai anṟi maṟṟu ilēn enṟu ettālum karumam inṟi tudi sūḻnda pādalgaḷ pādi Ada ninṟu ūḻi ūḻi toṟum edir sūḻal pukku enaittōr piṟappum enakkē aruḷgaḷ seyya vidi sūḻndadāl enakkēl ammān tirivikkiramanaiyē*

- *madusūdanai anṟi maṟṟu ilēn enṟu* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s state is such that he will not have anyone, other than the one who has the quality of eliminating the hurdles, as his refuge.

What is the difference between us who say the same thing when our mind is in satva guṇam (goodness) and āhvār?

- *ettālum karumam inṟi* – His actions would be in line with his words. He would discard fake-goals and fake-means and would consider that anything other than \[emperumān\] himself is of no use to him.
- *tudi sūḻnda* … –  two explanations – songs in the form of praises; songs which will consume his qualities which are to be praised. He made me such that I sing his glories kalpa after kalpa.
- *ninṟu* – Instead of looking for favours in return as said in yajur vēdam 1.8 “*dēhimē …*” (you give me something and I will give you something back) and leaving you, staying firmly.

When asked “what is the reason for his favours?”, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says “*vidi sūḻndadāl*” (because he was wrapped with compassion):

- *edir sūḻal pukku* – When someone tries to catch a person, he would come from the opposite direction; similarly, whenever [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) took birth in this material realm, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) too appeared to catch him. āḻvār was born due to his karma (virtues/vices) and emperumān was born due to his compassion. *sūḻal* also means avatāram (incarnation). āḻvār says “*enaittōr piṟappum edir sūḻal pukku enakkē aruḷgaḷ seyya vidi sūḻndadāl*” (all these births of emperumān while I was born is due to his being wrapped in compassion and wanting to shower his mercy on me). vidi means [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s krupā (mercy). Why is bhagavān’s krupā said as vidi (destiny)? This is because he cannot avoid showing his compassion (he is bound by it); like we cannot fulfil all our desires freely due to our karma, he too cannot fulfil his desires due to his own compassion; śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 38.34 “*… vadārhamapi kākutsta: krupayā parypālayat \|\|*” (śrī rāma who is a descendant of kakutsta, saved kākāsura due to compassion) – their heritage is such that they will protect others even at the cost of harming themselves. He even avoided killing kākāsura who was worthy to be killed \[Here it is explained that though he wanted to kill kākāsura (indra’s demoniac son who assumed the form of a crow) for hurting sītā pirātti, he was overwhelmed with compassion and ended up forgiving kākāsura\].
- *enakkēl …* – [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) being [sarvēśvaran](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) (lord of all), took birth as a dwarf, measured the worlds in three feet and placed all the worlds under his lotus feet and mingled with everyone; that act of simplicity looks like supremacy when compared to his being wrapped with compassion to accept me.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.7.7. Tirivikkiraman

*tirivikkiraman sendāmaraik kaṇ emmān en sengani vāy uruvil polinda veḷḷaip paḷingu niṟattan(an) enṟu enṟu uḷḷip paravip paṇindu pal ūḻi ūḻi nin pāda pangayamē maruvit toḻum manamē tandāy vallai kāṇ en vāmananē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

tirivikkiraman – one who measured the worlds and won over them; sem – reddish; tāmarai – lotus flower like; kaṇ – with the eyes; emmān – my lord who accepted my service to say “jitam” (victory to him); en sem kani vāy uruvil polinda veḷḷaip paḷingu niṟattan – one who let me experience the beautiful row of white pearl like teeth inside the reddish mouth (lips) and made me exist for him exclusively; enṟu enṟu – thus saying each aspect individually; uḷḷi – contemplating in the heart; paravi – (as the experience is not subdued in the heart, it is expressed by) speaking in a disorderly manner; paṇindu – (due to that overwhelming love) bowing (at the lotus feet); pal – many; ūḻi ūḻi – until time exists in different types of kalpa (i.e., forever); nin – your; pāda pangayamē – enjoyable lotus feet; maruvi – fitting well (without any other expectation); toḻum – serving; manamē – mind; tandāy – you bestowed; en vāmananē – Oh my vāmana!; vallai kāṇ – you are very capable

**Перевод:**

**Like he measured the worlds and won over them, he, my lord showed his reddish lotus flower like eyes, won over me and accepted my service; he let me experience the beautiful row of white pearl like teeth inside the reddish mouth (lips) and made me exist for him exclusively. “You thus made me contemplate these aspects individually in the heart and speak about them in a disorderly manner, made me bow at your lotus feet (due to that great love) and bestowed me the mind that made me fit well (without any other expectation) at your enjoyable lotus feet until time exists in different types of kalpa (i.e., forever). Oh vāmana! You are very capable!”.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the seventh pāsuram – āḻvār says “You have bestowed me a mind which aims only to experience you by glorifying and worshiping you. Is anything difficult for you, who are śrī vāmana?”*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says that emperumān bestowed a pure mind which is suitable to worship him.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

- *vallai kāṇ en vāmananē* – Like you tricked mahābali by your beauty so that he did not heed to the advice of śukrācārya et al, you have tricked me to fully exist for you.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. திரிவிக்கிரமன் செந்தாமரைக் கண் எம்மான் என் செங்கனி வாய் உருவில் பொலிந்த வெள்ளைப் பளிங்கு நிறத்தனன் என்று என்று உள்ளி பரவிப் பணிந்து பல் ஊழி ஊழி நின் பாத பங்கயமே மருவித் தொழும் மனமே தந்தாய் வல்லை காண் என் வாமனனே tirivikkiraman sendāmaraik kaṇ emmān en sengani vāy uruvil polinda veḷḷaip paḷingu niṟattan(an) enṟu enṟu uḷḷip paravip paṇindu pal ūḻi ūḻi nin pāda pangayamē maruvit toḻum manamē tandāy vallai kāṇ en vāmananē!*

- *tirivikkiraman* – With three steps, he brought all the worlds under his lotus feet.
- *sem tāmaraik kaṇ emmān* – through his glance, he brought me under his lotus feet.
- *en sem kanivāy* … – After [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) said as in jitantē stōtram 1 “*jitam …*” (victory), emperumān smiled \[revealing his row of pearl like teeth\]. His lips became red after transforming āḻvar to be fully existing for him – in such lips. Due to the visible contrast (red lips – white teeth), one who is having the row of pure white teeth.
- *enṟu enṟu uḷḷi* – In the worldly pleasures (bodily beauty of opposite sex), one can contemplate upon that only when the inside is not seen (i.e., thought externally someone may look beautiful, the inside of the body is still made of flesh, blood etc., which look disgusting only\]; but bhagavat viśayam can be continuously meditated upon \[since bhagavān’s body is pure and divine\].
- *paravip paṇindu* – calling him out without any order, falling at his lotus feet without any self-esteem.

This joy is not limited for one day and gone the next day –

- *pal ūḻi ūḻi* – kalpa (day of brahmā which is several million years) after kalpa; you bestowed me a mind to worship your most enjoyable lotus feet forever without any expectation. Also explained as – since worldly pleasures are temporary and not enjoyable, the mind will not be fixated on any single thing for a longer duration as mentioned by arjuna in bhagavad gītā 6.34 “*cancalam hi mana:*” (the wavering mind); but since you are permanent and most enjoyable, you bestowed me a mind that will fit well in your lotus feet. You did not just reform my old mind – you have given me a new mind from the store room as said by kriṣṇa in bhagavad gītā 11.8 “… *divyam dadāmi …*” (I am giving you a divine set of eyes to behold my universal form which cannot be seen by your material eyes). On seeing the mind, one cannot say that it was the same old mind which got transformed – it looked like a brand new mind.
- *en vāmananē vallai kāṇ* – Is this vāmana form the tool for you to give and take? By showing this vāmana form you have reformed my mind and given a new look to it; it is this same beauty through which you took away the worlds which mahābali considered as his own; [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) becomes delighted saying “*vallai kāṇ*” (you are very capable).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.7.8. Vamanan

*vāmanan en maradaga vaṇṇan tāmaraik kaṇṇinan kāmanaip payandāy! enṟu enṟu un kaḻal pādiyē paṇindu tū manattananāyp piṟavit tuḻadi nīnga ennait tī manam keduttāy unakken seygēn? en sirīdaranē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

vāmanan – Oh (most easily approachable) vāmana!; en – for me to experience; maradaga vaṇṇan – Oh one who is having a beautiful form resembling emerald!; tāmarai – like lotus flower; kaṇṇinan – Oh one who is having such eyes!; kāmanai – for cupid (who is loved by all); payandāy – Oh one who is the creator!; enṟu enṟu – saying so; un kaḻal – your divine feet; pādiyē – sing; paṇindu – bow to them; tū manattananāy – having pure mind (which does not hanker for ulterior goals); piṟavi – caused by birth; tuḻadi – sufferings; nīnga – to eradicate; ennait tīmanam keduttāy – reformed my evil mind (which was focussed on worldly pleasures); en – being the helper for such me; sirīdaranē – Oh śrīmān (lord of śrī mahālakśmi)!; unakku – for you (who are complete); en – what; seygēn – can I do?

**Перевод:**

**Oh (most easily approachable) vāmana! Oh one who is having a beautiful form resembling emerald, for me to experience! Oh one who is having lotus flower like eyes which would happily and completely bless those who enjoy them! Oh one who is the creator of cupid (who is loved by all)! You reformed my evil mind to say these, sing your divine feet, bow to them, to have a pure mind and to eliminate the sufferings caused by birth \[in material realm\]; Oh you who are śrīmān (husband of śrī mahālakśmi) who is complete in all manners and who has done such favours to me! What can I do in return?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the eighth pāsuram – āḻvār says “There can be no reciprocation for the favours done by emperumān“.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār asks “is there a reciprocation for emperumān‘s favour of eliminating the mind which is not useful to enjoy him?”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Eighth pāsuram. āḻvār struggles due to not finding a way to reciprocate the favour done by emperumān to him. வாமனன் என் மரகத வண்ணன் தாமரைக் கண்ணினன் காமனைப் பயந்தாய்! என்று என்று உன் கழல் பாடியே பணிந்து தூ மனத்தனனாய்ப் பிறவித் துழதி நீங்க என்னைத் தீ மனம் கெடுத்தாய் உனக்கு என் செய்கேன்? என் சிரீதரனே! vāmanan en maradaga vaṇṇan tāmaraik kaṇṇinan kāmanaip payandāy! enṟu enṟu un kaḻal pādiyē paṇindu tū manattananāyp piṟavit tuḻadi nīnga ennait tī manam keduttāy unakken seygēn? en sirīdaranē!*

- *vāmanan* – this explains his divine bodily beauty; also explains him as the well-wisher who does good to others.
- *en maradaga vaṇṇan* – one who let me enjoy his divine form which removes all fatigue.
- *tāmaraik kaṇṇinan* – Not just external beauty, his mercy dripping heart is exposed through his divine eyes.
- *kāmanaip payandāy* – oh the creator of manmata (cupid) who threatens/bewilders everyone with his extreme beauty! On meditating upon [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), sometimes [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) speaks in first person with emperumān (you, here etc – as if he is in front of him); but when he further desires for affectionate exchanges which would not happen, he will speak in third person \[he, there etc\] to him; his great attachment to emperumān is the reason for both types of dealings.
- *enṟu enṟu  …* – reciting these divine names and falling at his lotus feet
- *tū manattananāy* – mind is generally explained as the cause for both bondage and liberation; leaving that aside, having a heart which is fully focussed on liberation; that is, having pure internal sense (mind). As a result, one need not take birth again \[in this material realm\]; piṟavit tuḻadi – sufferings in birth, eliminating that.
- *ennait tīmanam keduttāy* – You reformed the mind which would desire for both you and worldly pleasures like a person who would desire for both nectar (which would give immortality) and poison (which would kill). Not only you bestowed me a good mind, you also eliminated my evil mind (explained in previous pāsuram).
- *unakku* … – Seeing the favours done by you, I cannot bear myself not reciprocating the same; but I am not finding ways to reciprocate; Neither am I able to reject your favour nor are you in need of something. What can I do to you who is already complete in all aspects?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.7.9. Sireeidaran

*sireeidaran seyya tāmaraik kaṇṇn enṟu enṟu irāp pagal vāy vereei alamandu kaṇgaḷ nīr malgi vevvuyirttu uyirttu mareeiya tīvinai māḷa inbam vaḷara vaigal vaigal ireei unnai ennuḷ vaittanai en irudīkēśanē !*

**Пословный перевод:**

sireeidaran – one who is śriya:pati (husband of śrī mahālakśmi); seyya – fresh (due to the joy acquired after uniting with her); tāmarai – like a lotus flower; kaṇṇan – one who has eyes; enṟu enṟu – saying so; irāp pagal – night and day; vāy vereei – repeatedly saying/blabbering; alamandu – (as said in tiruvāimoḻi 2.4.1 “engum nādi nādi“) looking blank and confused; kaṇgaḷ nīr malgi – (as said in tiruvāimoḻi 2.4.5 “kuvaḷai oṇ kaṇṇa nīr koṇḍāḷ” and tiruvāimoḻi 2.4.10 “kēḻil oṇ kaṇṇa nīr koṇḍāḷ“) shedding tears; vevvuyirttu uyirttu – (as said in tiruvāimoḻi 2.4.4 “uḷḷam malanga vevvuyirkkum” and tiruvāimoḻi 2.4.8 “nenjam vēva nedituyirkkum“) breathing hot and long, continuously; mareeiya – suffered (as in tiruvāimoḻi 2.4 “ādiyādi“); tīvinai – vices; māḷa – to eradicate; inbam vaḷara – to increase the joy (starting from tiruvāimoḻi 2.5 “andāmattanbu“); vaigal vaigal – always; en irudīkēśanē – since you are the controller of my senses; en uḷ – in my heart (which is submissive towards you); unnai – you (who are the controller, enjoyer); ireei – (as said in tiruvāimoḻi 2.6.2 “pakka nōkkaṟiyān“) keeping; vaittanai – placed

**Перевод:**

**You made me repeatedly say “śrīdara” and “seyya tāmaraik kaṇṇan” (one with fresh lotus flower like eyes (due to the joy acquired after uniting with her)) night and day and blabber that,  looking blank and confused, shedding tears, breathing hot and long, continuously and suffered; to eradicate such vices and to increase the joy always, you placed yourself by keeping you in my heart since you are the controller of my senses.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the ninth pāsuram – āḻvār becomes pleased saying “You mercifully entered into me and stayed firmly and removed my sufferings which were highlighted in ādiyādi, made me devoted to you and took charge of my senses fully”. It is also explained as āḻvār becoming pleased saying “After I enjoyed you with devotion, you eliminated my hurdles, bestowing on me unsurpassed joy by placing yourself in me”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. சிரீதரன் செய்ய தாமரைக் கண்ணன் என்று என்று இராப்பகல் வாய் வெரீஇ அலமந்து கண்கள் நீர் மல்கி வெவ்வுயிர்த்து உயிர்த்து மரீஇய தீவினை மாள இன்பம் வளர வைகல் வைகல் இரீஇ உன்னை என்னுள் வைத்தனை என் இருடீகேசனே! sireeidaran seyya tāmaraik kaṇṇn enṟu enṟu irāp pagal vāy vereei alamandu kaṇgaḷ nīr malgi vevvuyirttu uyirttu mareeiya tīvinai māḷa inbam vaḷara vaigal vaigal ireei unnai ennuḷ vaittanai en irudīkēśanē !*

- *sireeidaran* – one who has periya pirāttiyār in his chest.
- *seyya tāmaraik kaṇṇan* – Like crops which look fresh when watered, having cool beautiful eyes due to her presence in his chest. This is explained in viṣṇu daramam – mangalyastavam “… *vakśastalēna śriyamudvahan vibhu: \| vistāri padmōtpala patralōcana: …*” (one who is having śrī mahālakśmi in his chest, who is sarvēśvara and whose divine eyes resemble lotus leaf or vaterlily flower).
- *enṟu enṟu* – saying thus
- *irāp pagal* … – Previous ācāryas explained this as “Since he is overwhelmed with devotion, this is how his activities would be \[constantly crying, longing for [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) etc\]”. But, [bhattar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/parasara-bhattar/) explained it as “upto ‘*mareeiya tīvinai māḷa*‘ as the state of [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) which was elaborated in ‘[*ādiyādi*](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/03/thiruvaimozhi-2-4-adiyadi/)‘ decad and ‘*inbam vaḷara*‘ explains the loving devotion which flourished in āḻvār starting from ‘[*andāmattanbu*](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/03/thiruvaimozhi-2-5-andhamaththanbu/)‘ decad up to ‘[*kēśavan tamar*](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/04/thiruvaimozhi-2-7-kesavan-thamar/)‘ decad”. “*irāp pagal vāy vereei*” indicates [tiruvāimoḻi 2.4.5](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/03/thiruvaimozhi-2-4-5-ival-irap-pagal/) “*ivaḷ irāp pagal vāy vereei*“. “*alamandu*” indicates [tiruvāimoḻi 2.4.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/03/thiruvaimozhi-2-4-1-adi-adi/) “*engum nādi nādi*“. “*kaṇgaḷ nīr malgi*” indicates [tiruvāimoḻi 2.4.5](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/03/thiruvaimozhi-2-4-5-ival-irap-pagal/) “*tana kuvaḷai oṇ kaṇṇa nīr koṇḍāḷ*“. “*vevvuyirttuyirttu*” indicates [tiruvāimoḻi 2.4.4](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/03/thiruvaimozhi-2-4-4-ilangai-serravane/) “*uḷḷam malanga vevvuyirkkum*“.
- *mareeiya tīvinai māḷa* – His suffering in “*ādiyādi*” was like the suffering of gajēndrāḻvān (elephant) due to the crocodile. To eradicate such well established sufferings.
- *inbam vaḷara* – the joyful love which started from “*andāmattanbu*“.
- vaigal vaigal – every moment that has passed
- *unnai en uḷ irīi vaittanai* – you placed yourself within me.
- *en irudīkēśanē* – Those senses which were mine and did harm to me by opposing me, gave up their arms (surrendered to you). Would the ones (senses) which have seen parama śēśi (ultimate master – [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)) stop at dvāra śēśi (local master – [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/))? \[No – they will become subservient to bhagavān.\]

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.7.10. Irudikesan

*irudīkēśan em pirān ilangai arakkar kulam murudu tīrtta pirān emmān amarar pemmān enṟu enṟu terudiyāgil nenjē! vaṇangu tiṇṇam aṟi aṟindu marudiyēlum vidēl kaṇḍāy nambi paṟpanābanaiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

irudīkēśan – controlling my mind (which is the entrance for all my 10 senses); empirān – my saviour (who favoured me); ilangai – in lankā; arakkar kulam – for the clan of rākśasas; murudu – most cruel rāvaṇa; tīrtta – destroyed; pirān – one who helped (the citizens); amarar pemmān – like nityasūris (their leader); emmān – my lord who let me enjoy him (like nityasūris enjoy him); enṟu enṟu – meditating like this in many ways; nenjē! – oh mind!; terudiyāgil – if you are wise; vaṇangu – see that you worship (him); tiṇṇam – firmly; aṟi – know; aṟindu – even after having such knowledge; marudiyēlum – if you get disturbed (due to your unworthiness); nambi – being complete in all qualities; paṟpanābanai – this great saviour who has divine lotus flower in his navel (which is the cause for everything); vidēl kaṇḍāy – don’t let go of him – so says āḻvār to his heart

**Перевод:**

**Oh mind! Meditate upon emperumān again and again, who is being the controller of my mind (which is the entrance for my 10 senses) and one who favours me like he favoured the citizens by destroying the cruel rāvaṇa of the rākśasa clan of lankā, who is my lord who let me enjoy him like the nityasūris do; if you are wise, see that you worship him; you firmly know this and even after having such knowledge, if you get disturbed (due to your unworthiness), don’t let go of this great saviour who is being complete in all qualities and who has divine lotus flower in his navel (which is the cause for everything).**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the tenth pāsuram – āḻvār again instructs his mind “Don’t ever leave emperumān who has done us great favours”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār mercifully explains the desire to not let go of emperumān who favours him in all ways.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. இருடீகேசன் எம் பிரான் இலங்கை அரக்கர் குலம் முருடு தீர்த்த பிரான் எம்மான் அமரர் பெம்மான் என்று என்று தெருடியாகில் நெஞ்சே! வணங்கு திண்ணம் அறி அறிந்து மருடியேலும் விடேல் கண்டாய் நம்பி பற்பநாபனையே irudīkēśan em pirān ilangai arakkar kulam murudu tīrtta pirān emmān amarar pemmān enṟu enṟu terudiyāgil nenjē! vaṇangu tiṇṇam aṟi aṟindu marudiyēlum vidēl kaṇḍāy nambi paṟpanābanaiyē*

- *irudīkēśan empirān* – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is most generous in making me use the senses to know him, instead of letting me engage them in worldly pleasures and go astray.
- *ilangai …* – How did he eliminate his attachment to his senses? Like in lankā, he destroyed the cruel rāvaṇa et al with the help of vibhīśaṇa et al (who too are born in the same clan).
- *emmān amarar pemmān* – Not only he eliminated the attachment of my senses to worldly pleasures, he also let me enjoy him like the nityasūris enjoy him. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying so \[repeatedly\].
- *terudiyāgil* – if you grasp this knowledge; he says this to the mind/heart, since mind is the entrance to grasp the knowledge.
- *nenjē vaṇangu* – if you really have the greatness of being the entry point for jñāna indriyams (organs of knowledge) and knowledge, you fall at the divine feet of the one who favours you \[with such qualities\].
- *tiṇṇam aṟi* – You understand this firmly instead of superficially understanding it as said in an assembly.
- *aṟindu* – knowing this is the goal; there is no separate goal to pursue.

Further,

- *marudiyēlum vidēl kaṇḍāy* – You have a piccu (maruḷ – ajñānam – ignorance); when you see his exceptional greatness, you would think “why should I insult him \[in the name of glorifying him\]?” and consider yourself unworthy and try to leave him; try to give that up.
- *nambi paṟpanābanaiyē* – Are you going to eat sand leaving him \[saying – what else can you do in a worthy manner after leaving [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)\]? See his completeness of auspicious qualities; see his bodily beauty; you have already seen how he favoured us.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.7.11. Parpanaban

*paṟpanāban uyarvu aṟa uyarum perum tiṟalōn eṟparan ennai ākkik koṇḍu enakkē tannait tanda kaṟpagam en amudam kār mugil pōlum vēngada nal veṟpan visumbōr pirān endai dāmōdaranē*

**Пословный перевод:**

paṟpanāban – being the one who has divine lotus flower in his navel (which is the cause for creation of the material worlds); uyarvaṟa uyarum – being very tall; perum – boundless; tiṟalōn – having the ability; eṟparan – (having such greatness) being focussed towards me; ennai – me; ākki – created; koṇḍu – acknowledged me; enakkē – exclusively for me; tannai – him; tanda – gave; kaṟpagam – kalpaka tree (which fulfils the wishes of one who seeks); en – for me; amudam – being sweet like nectar; kār mugil pōlum – resembling a dark cloud (which would rain without checking the ground status); vēngadam – having the name tiruvēngadam (which is suitable abode for such dark cloud); nal – exceptional; veṟpan – having tirumalā as his abode; visumbōr – nityasūris, the residents of paramapadam; pirān – one who has subservience towards his devotees to let them enjoy him; dāmōdaran – dāmōdara; endai – accepted me as his servitor

**Перевод:**

**emperumān, having divine lotus flower in his navel (which is the cause for creation of the material worlds), having very tall and boundless ability, (having such greatness) being focussed towards me, due to that \[supremacy\], created me, acknowledged and exclusively gave himself to me like a kalpaka tree (which fulfils the wishes), being enjoyable to me, resembling a dark cloud (which would rain without checking the ground status)  having the exceptional tirumalā which is known as tiruvēngadam as his abode; such emperumān who has subservience towards nityasūris (his devotees, residing in paramapadam) to let them enjoy him, accepted me as his servitor.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the eleventh pāsuram – āḻvār says emperumān, being most distinct, still accepted me as his servitor out of most simplicity and does not know any one other than me.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “for me who has acquired this knowledge, he is the favourer in all ways”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. பற்பநாபன் உயர்வு அற உயரும் பெரும் திறலோன் எற்பரன் என்னை ஆக்கிக் கொண்டு எனக்கே தன்னைத் தந்த கற்பகம் என் அமுதம் கார் முகில் போலும் வேங்கட நல் வெற்பன் விசும்போர் பிரான் எந்தை தாமோதரனே paṟpanāban uyarvu aṟa uyarum perum tiṟalōn eṟparan ennai ākkik koṇḍu enakkē tannait tanda kaṟpagam en amudam kār mugil pōlum vēngada nal veṟpan visumbōr pirān endai dāmōdaranē*

- *paṟpanāban* – One who has the divine lotus flower like (in) navel which is the root cause for all of creation.
- *uyarvaṟa* … –  One who has great qualities such as valour, bravery etc which cannot be easily explained through words. tiṟal – ability to command respect even from enemies. This (tiṟal) is a sample for all other qualities. That (paṟpanāban – padmanābhan) indicates his supremacy due to being the creator/cause of everything.

Such [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/),

- eṟparan – is exclusively focussed on me
- *ennai* … – kalpaka vrukśa (desire fulfilling tree) is the most popular object for audāryam (generosity).

The differences between kalpaka tree and [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) are explained further.

- *ennai ākkik koṇḍu* – kalpaka tree would not create the person who would ask for wishes \[[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) first created me and then fulfilled my desires too\].
- *enakkē* – kalpaka tree would not help one person exclusively \[[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is focussing on me exclusively\].
- *tannait tanda* – kalpaka tree would fulfil the desires but would never offer itself to the one who desires \[[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) gave himself to me\].
- *en amudam* – kalpaka tree is in itself not enjoyable \[while it can present enjoyable aspects\] – but [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is most enjoyable for me.
- *kārmugilpōlum vēngada nal veṟpan* – his audāryam (generosity) is due to his connection with tirumalā; isn’t this generosity founded from (mountain named) sahya \[the river which originates from sahya mountain is perennial – citing that as an example\]? [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is having tirumalā as his abode – tirumalā is like a generous cloud which showers the rain and does not even think that it has helped others.
- *visumbōr pirān* … – Though [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is the controller/leader of nityasūris, he descended as kriṣṇa to be bound/beaten by covherd boys and girls and thus won over me and accepted me as his servitor through such acts.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.7.12. Damodaranai

*dāmōdaranait tani mudalvanai jñālam uṇḍavanai āmō taram aṟiya oruvarkku? enṟē toḻum avargaḷ dāmōdaran uru āgiya sivaṟkum tisai mugaṟkum āmō taram aṟiya emmānai en āḻi vaṇṇanaiyē ?*

**Пословный перевод:**

dāmōdaranai – having the simplicity of showing total subservience towards his devotees \[as kriṣṇa – dāmōdara\]; tani mudalvanai – having the greatness of being the singular cause for all worlds; jñālam uṇḍavanai – one who has the ability to protect all during praḷayam (annihilation); taram – analyse; aṟiya – know; oruvarkku – for anyone; āmō – is it possible?; enṟu – saying thus; toḻum avargaḷ – those who worship; dāmōdaran – for such dāmōdara; uru āgiya – servitors who are the prakāram (mode/form) of emperumān; sivaṟkum – for rudra; tisai mugaṟkum – for brahmā; en – in me; āḻi vaṇṇan – placing his ocean of auspicious qualities; emmān – my lord who accepted my service; taram – measure; aṟiya āmō – is it possible to know?

**Перевод:**

**rudra, brahmā et al , the servitors who are the prakāram (mode/form) of emperumān, worship emperumān saying “is it possible for any one to analyse and know bhagavān who is having the simplicity of showing total subservience towards his devotees \[as kriṣṇa – dāmōdara\], the greatness of being the singular cause for all worlds and who has the ability to protect all during praḷayam (annihilation)?” For such rudra, brahmā et al is it possible to measure and know how my lord, who accepted my service, placed his ocean of auspicious qualities in me (like storing an ocean in a mustard seed)?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the twelfth pāsuram – āḻvār says “Even for brahmā et al who are desirous to gain true knowledge about bhagavān, it is difficult to know emperumān“.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says that the favours done by emperumān to him cannot be comprehended by even the most knovledegable persons.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Twelfth pāsuram. āḻvār says “as said in ‘eṟparan‘ (fully focussed on me) – only those who were favoured  like me by emperumān can see him and it is not possible to see him for those \[brahmā et al\] who think that they can know bhagavān through their own efforts”. தாமோதரனை தனி முதல்வனை ஞாலம் உண்டவனை ஆமோ தரம் அறிய ஒருவர்க்கு? என்றே தொழும் அவர்கள் தாமோதரன் உரு ஆகிய சிவற்கும் திசைமுகற்கும் ஆமோ தரம் அறிய எம்மானை என் ஆழி வண்ணனையே? dāmōdaranait tani mudalvanai jñālam uṇḍavanai āmō taram aṟiya oruvarkku? enṟē toḻum avargaḷ dāmōdaran uru āgiya sivaṟkum tisai mugaṟkum āmō taram aṟiya emmānai en āḻi vaṇṇanaiyē ?*

brahmā et al glorify emperumān by saying “Who can know ‘dāmōdaran’, ‘tani mudalvan’ and “jñālam uṇḍavan’?”

- *dāmōdaranai* – Is it possible to understand as to how he stays totally subservient to his devotees \[like being bound and beaten by mother yaśōdā\]?
- *tani mudalvanai* – As said in cāndōjña upaniśat “*sadēva sōmya idamagra āsīt …*” (Oh śvētakētu who is qualified to drink sōma juice! Before creation, sat only existed alone \[since there is no name/form\] without anything else to bear it), [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is the three types of causes \[upādāna kāraṇam – material cause, nimitta kāraṇam – instrumental cause, sahakārikā kāraṇam – ancillary cause\] – is it possible to understand this state of bhagavān?
- *jñālam uṇḍavanai* – Not just creating them and leaving them alone, he also stands as the protector when everyone is in danger during annihilation. Is it possible to understand this state of [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)?
- *āmō taram aṟiya oruvarkku* … – They (brahmā et al) would think that they know everything and say “Would anyone else understand these aspects of [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)?” Is it possible to understand for brahmā, rudra et al who are subservient to bhagavān like body is subservient to soul and who worship saying “Is it possible to understand these for any one?” Is it possible to understand bhagavān for brahmā and rudra who think that they are different from others and that they know bhagavān better?

When asked as to who are they trying to understand,

- *emmānai en āḻi vaṇṇanai* – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who revealed his nature of being filled with auspicious qualities to me like placing an ocean in a small area created by a foot step. Thus, one can understand emperumān only when he reveals himself and those who try with their own efforts cannot understand him.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.7.13. Vannamamani

*vaṇṇa mā maṇic cōdiyai amarar talai maganai kaṇṇanai nedumālait ten kurugūrc catakōpan paṇṇiya tamiḻ mālai āyirattuḷ ivai panniraṇḍum paṇṇil panniru nāmap pāttu aṇṇal tāḷ aṇaivikkumē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vaṇṇam – having beautiful complexion; mā – most expensive; maṇi – blue gem’s; cōdiyai – having radiance like a bright light; amarar – for nityasūris (eternally free souls who are residents of paramapadam); talai maganai – being the great leader who is incomprehensible (even for such nityasūris); kaṇṇanai – being the one (as kriṣṇa) who enjoys his own devotees; nedumālai – to reach emperumān who is having great love (which is the cause for enjoying his devotees); then – beautiful; kurugūr – leader of āḻvārtirunagari; satakōpan – nammāḻvār; paṇṇiya – sung by; tamiḻ mālai – woven together in tamiḻ (drāvida) language which can be pursued by all without any restriction; āyirattuḷ – in the thousand pāsurams; paṇṇil – fitting in the tune; panniru nāmap pāttu – which are focussed on the twelve divine names of emperumān; ivai panniraṇḍum – these twelve pāsurams; aṇṇal – sarvēśvaran (supreme lord); tāḷ – divine feet; aṇaivikkum – will facilitate attainment

**Перевод:**

**nammāḻvār, leader of the beautiful āḻvārtirunagari has sung, among the thousand pāsurams which are woven together in tamiḻ (drāvida) language which can be pursued by all without any restriction – these twelve pāsurams which are nicely fitting in tune and are focussed on the twelve divine names of emperumān who resembles an expensive radiant blue gem that is having beautiful complexion and brightness for the joy of nityasūris; these pāsurams themselves will facilitate one to attain the divine feet of emperumān.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the end – āḻvār says “This decad (tiruvāimoḻi) itself will facilitate those who learnt it to reach the divine feet of emperumān“.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār explains attainment of bhagavān as the result of this decad.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. வண்ண மா மணிச் சோதியை அமரர் தலை மகனை கண்ணனை நெடுமாலைத் தென் குருகூர்ச் சடகோபன் பண்ணிய தமிழ் மாலை ஆயிரத்துள் இவை பன்னிரண்டும் பண்ணில் பன்னிரு நாமப் பாட்டு அண்ணல் தாள் அணைவிக்குமே vaṇṇa mā maṇic cōdiyai amarar talai maganai kaṇṇanai nedumālait then kurugūrc catakōpan paṇṇiya tamiḻ mālai āyirattuḷ ivai panniraṇḍum paṇṇil panniru nāmap pāttu aṇṇal tāḷ aṇaivikkumē*

- *vaṇṇam …* – One who is having a form which resembles an expensive precious gem which has beautiful complexion.
- *vaṇṇa mā maṇic cōdiyai* – vaṇṇam – colour; mā – blackish blue; it can also indicate [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) having the radiance of a blackish-blue gem.

Further, those who enjoy this beauty is explained.

- *amarar talaimaganai* – Even if the whole of paramapadam try to enjoy his beauty, his beauty cannot be comprehended – such great [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/).
- *kaṇṇanai* – He appeared as kriṣṇa so that the residents of this material realm too can enjoy.
- *nedumālai* – He has such great love that when he pursues someone, he does not stop at that individual, but extends his love to all those who are related to that individual.
- *then kurugūrc catakōpan paṇṇiya* – This is unlike *vēdam* which has no creator; this has greater glories even compared to vēdam which is considered as apauruśēyam (not created by an individual) due to the greatness of the author, that is [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) \[In arumpadam, some pramāṇams are cited which highlight the importance of a literature based on the author. “*brahmavādinō vadanti*” (spoken by the knovers of brahmam), “*sa hōvāca vyāsa: pārāśarya:*” (thus spoke vyāsa, the famous son of parāśara), “*yadvai kinca manuravadat tadbhēśajam*” (whatever spoken by manu is medicine) – if that is the case for riśis et al, what to speak of the words of [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)?\]. These pāsurams thrive in divine music.
- *panniru nāmap pāttu* – These pāsurams are sung based on the divine names of viṣṇu which are an important symbol for vaiṣṇavas \[Divine names are recited/remembered while applying the tirumaṇ/tilak on twelve parts of our body\].

What do these twelve pāsurams lead to?

- *aṇṇal tāḷ aṇaivikkum* – will help one be united with the divine feet of sarvēśvaran; one’s relationship with this decad, will make one “*kēśavan tamar*” (devotee of kēśava).

Finally, nampiḷḷai summarizes the contents of this decad briefly.

- In the first pāsuram, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) explained that all those who are related to him and those who are related to them are pursued by bhagavān like he himself was pursued by [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/).
- In the second pāsuram, he mercifully explained that bhagvān’s action was due to his being [nārāyaṇa](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) (being connected to everyone as the lord) and explained the meaning of that “*nārāyaṇa*” word.
- In the third pāsuram, he explained the reason for [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) pursuing them.
- In the fourth pāsuram, he explained that emperumān transformed āḻvār to constantly enjoy him.
- In the fifth pāsuram, he explained that because of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) making āḻvār enjoy him, emperumān’s splendour grew.
- In the sixth pāsuram, he explained that emperumān pursued āḻvār due to his nirhētuka krupai (unconditional grace).
- In the seventh pāsuram, he explained that emperumān bestowed a mind/heart that will constantly enjoy him.
- In the eighth pāsuram, he explained that [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) bestowed not only a pure mind, he also removed the earlier evil mind/heart.
- In the ninth pāsuram, he explained that emperumān entered āḻvār’s heart so that āḻvār can enjoy his auspicious qualities always.
- In the tenth pāsuram, he explained that emperumān engaged āḻvār’s senses too which are the hurdles in enjoying emperumān.
- In the eleventh pāsuram, he explained that such [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) became fully focussed on him.
- In the twelfth pāsuram, he explained that only those like āḻvār who saw emperumān by emperumān’s grace can see him and those who try with their own efforts cannot see him.
- In the end, he explained the result for this decad and completes the decad.

[emperumānār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/emperumanar/) tiruvadigaḷē śaraṇam
