## 2.8 Anaivadu aravanaimel

## 2.8.1. Anaivadu aravanaimel

*aṇaivadu aravaṇai mēl pūm pāvai āgam puṇarvadu iruvar avar mudalum tānē iṇaivanām epporutkum vīdu mudalām puṇaivan piṟavik kadal nīnduvārkkē*

**Пословный перевод:**

aravu – tiruvanantāḻvān (ādiśēśan); aṇai mēl – on the bed; aṇaivadu – lovingly lie down; pū – most tender person like a budding flower; pāvai – pirātti’s (śrī mahālakśmi‘s); āgam – divine body; puṇarvadu – embracing joyfully; avar – popularly known (for their controlling ability); iruvar – creation and sustenance of brahmā, rudra; tānē – himself; mudalum – is the cause; epporutkum – all objects (in the universe which is protected); iṇaivanām – (through his incarnations) being born in the species; vīdu – mōkśam (liberation which is the top-most form of protection); mudalām – is the cause; piṟavi – this existence in material realm; kadal – ocean; nīnduvārkku – to those who want to cross over; puṇaivan – is the boat

**Перевод:**

**emperumān lovingly lies down on tiruvanantāḻvān (ādiśēśan) in the form of a bed and joyfully embraces the divine body of śrī mahālakśmi who is most tender person like a budding flower – this explains his control over nitya vibhūti (spiritual realm). In the leelā vibhūti (material realm), he himself is the cause for the creation and sustenance of brahmā and rudra who are popularly known (for their controlling ability). He takes birth in the various species (through his incarnations) in the universe that is protected. He is the cause for mōkśam (liberation which is the top-most form of protection). (To avoid the question of why everyone is not liberated then) He is the boat for those who want to cross over this existence in the ocean of material realm.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the first pāsuram – āḻvār explains briefly the principles which are explained in this decad.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*In the first pāsuram – āḻvār mercifully explains briefly emperumān‘s control over all that is explained in this decad.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*First pāsuram. āḻvār explains the joy acquired by liberated souls. First pāsuram is the short summary of the whole decad, where each word is further explained in the subsequent pāsurams. aṇaivadu aravaṇai mēl pūm pāvai āgam puṇarvadu iruvar avar mudalum tānē iṇaivanām epporutkum vīdu mudalām puṇaivan piṟavik kadal nīnduvārkkē*

- *aṇaivadu aravaṇai mēl*  – this is the joy acquired by liberated persons; As explained in paryanka vidyā, when a [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) becomes mukta (liberated) and approaches [śrī mahālakśmi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/) and [śrīman nārāyaṇan](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who are lying on tiruvanantāḻvān (ādiśeśan), he would say “*aham brahmāsmi*” \[as explained in sāmānādikaraṇyam, since brahmam sustains everyone, everyone is indicated by the word “brahmam”\] – I am a prince, a mode/form of brahmam; hearing that, [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) would say “if that is the case, come to me” and having acknowledged, the [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) would climb on the bed like a child that would climb its parents’ bed as explained in “*tamēmvamvit pādēnādyārōhati*” (knowing him thus, he sets foot on ādiśeśa and climbs there) – this result acquired by the jīvātmā is explained here.
- *aṇaivadu* – Like a [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) who is turmoiled by tāpa trayam (three types of sufferings – ādyātmika, ādi baudika and ādi daivika, that is, those sufferings which are caused by self, other creatures and natural forces) would immerse in brahmam as said in mahābhāratam mōkśa darmam 4.50 “…*ēśa brahma praviśtōsmi*…” (like immersing in a cool pond during a hot summer day, ātmā stays satisfied on attaining [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)), bhagavān who does not have any such sufferings, still lies down on ādiśēśa as if he had such sufferings and then feels so satisfied as if being relieved from such sufferings. Like a thirsty person would jump into a cool pond, bhagavān would jump on ādiśēśan to rest.
- *aravaṇai mēl* – Would lie down on tiruvanantāḻvān (ādiśēśan) who has fragrance, coolness and tenderness as natural qualities; ādiśēśa is explained in mudal tiruvandādi 53 “*pulgum aṇaiyām*” (the bed that he embraces). Like a śēśa bhūta (servant) who cannot sustain himself without rendering service, the śēśi (master) cannot sustain himself without accepting the servant’s service.
- *pūm pāvai āgam puṇarvadu* – He unites and enjoys with [śrī mahālakśmi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/) who is the embodiment of pleasure and who has natural femininity.
- *āgam puṇarvadu* – Her auspicious qualities becomes irrelevant since he is too overwhelmed just by her physical beauty itself. Here we can understand that ādiśēśa too acquires the same pleasure as perumāḷ and pirātti, since the words “*aṇaivadu, puṇarvadu*” are used in the same manner – this is explained through “*agryaprāya nyāyam*“. This is masterfully explained through a ślōkam from śrī rāmāyaṇam bāla kāṇḍam 1.31 by nampiḷḷai. *ramyamā vasatam krutvā* – the āśramam (hermitage) constructed by iḷaiya perumāḷ (lakśmaṇa) in the forest was more beautiful and fitting than the palace built by daśarata with great efforts. *trayayō  ramamāṇā:* – [tāyār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/)‘s joy is the same as her lord [perumāḷ](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s joy; perumāḷ’s joy is the same as that which was acquired by pirātti. lakśmaṇa is the one who becomes greatly joyful seeing the divine couple enjoying there. *vanē* – they seemed to fit in so well there as if they are forest-dwellers instead of palace-dwellers. With this, it is explained that the real joy for muktātmā (liberated person) is to enjoy and serve [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) and [pirātti](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/) joyfully being together on ādiśēśan.
- *iruvar avar mudalum tānē* – He is the creator of brahmā and rudra. As known popularly from nārāyaṇa sūktam “*sa brahmā sa Siva:*” (he is brahmā, he is Siva)
- *iruvar avar* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says both are [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) (his prakāram/form, śarīram/body) only \[āḻvār is using the same method as in vēdam\]. While explaining nitya vibhūti, he explains it as “*aṇaivadu puṇaivadu*” – since that realm exists for his pleasure eternally. Here, he explains it as “*mudal*” (cause) to highlight that there is cause ([bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)) – effect (material realm) relationship and that there is continuous creation/dissolution.  He also explains through this that brahmā and rudra are materially bound in this realm and īśvara is the only one who is capable of bestowing liberation. It is also explained that bhagavān is the only refuge and brahmā/rudra should not be considered as refuge. This is explaind in śrīviṣṇu darmam “*ābrahmastamba paryantā jagadantarvyavastitā: \| prāṇina: karmajanitasamsāravaśavartina:* \|\|” (From brahmā down to a worm, all entities of this realm are bound in this samsāram (material realm) which is created through \[their collective\] puṇya/pāpa (virtues/vices)).

Such [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) who is having the greatness acquired due to being the cause of brahmā, rudra,

- *epporutkum iṇaivanām* – He would be born among all types of species such as dēva (celestial) et al. That is – being born amidst brahmā and rudra, being born as upēndra (younger brother of indra) \[up to this is in dēva/celestial form\], being born as the son of daśarata cakravarti and śrī nandagōpa \[up to this in manuśya/human form\], being born as mahāvarāham \[the great wild boar in animal form\], being born as kupjā tree \[plant form\].

Why is he reducing his own glories and taking birth in these worldly species?

- *vīdu mudalām* – to bestow liberation; wherever he took birth, he bestowed mōkśam to bird (jatāyu mahārāja), piśāca (demoniac person – gaṇṭā karṇan\].

If he is descending to bestow liberation, should everyone not become liberated?

- *piṟavik kadal nīnduvārkkup puṇaivan* – For those who say “This samsāram (material realm) is a great ocean and we cannot cross it on our own. You who are all powerful, should help us cross over”, he would be the one who takes responsibility for them (puṇai – bailing them out and liberating them). puṇai is also explained as boat; he would be the one who controls all their aspects \[relieves them from their burdens\]. He would help cross over this samsāram for those who think as said in jitantē stōtram “*samsārasāgaram gōramanantaklēśabhājanam \| tvāmēva śaraṇam prāpya \|\|*” (Those intelligent persons surrender unto you and cross over this cruel ocean of samsāram (material realm) which has unbounded sufferings). puṇaivan is also explained as boat, as explained in śrīviṣṇu darmam “*viṣṇupōtam*” (the boat named viṣṇu); unlike the boat which is seen in this world which resides in a single place, this boat of viṣṇu is spread from spiritual realm to material realm \[This is explained based on the root meaning for viṣṇu which means “all pervading”, “omnipresent”\].

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.8.2. Nindum tuyar

*nīndum tuyarp piṟavi utpada maṟṟu evvevaiyum nīndum tuyar illā vīdu mudalām pūm taṇ punal poygai yānai idar kadinda pūm taṇ tuḻāy en tani nāyagan puṇarppē*

**Пословный перевод:**

pū – having flower; taṇ – cool; punal – having water; poygai – in the pond; yānai – for the elephant (gajēndrāḻvān); idar – trouble (caused by the crocodile); kadinda – one who eliminated; pūm – fresh; taṇ – cool; tuḻāy – wearing tiruttuḻāy (tuḷasi); en – for me; tani nāyagan – unique/singular lord; puṇarppu – relationship; nīndum – for the jīvātmā who is finding it difficult to cross-over; tuyar – sorrowful; piṟavai – birth; utpada – including; maṟṟu – other; nīndum – to cross over; evvevai – all types of aspects (such as old-age, death etc); tuyarum – sorrows; illā – untouched by; vīdu – liberation; mudalām – cause

**Перевод:**

**My unique/singular lord who is wearing fresh and cool tiruttuḻāy (tuḷasi) is the one who eliminated the trouble (caused by the crocodile) for the elephant (gajēndrāḻvān). The relationship with such emperumān is the cause for liberation that is untouched by the sorrows (of this material realm) for the jīvātmā who is finding it difficult to cross-over the sorrowful samsāram which has all types of sorrowful aspects such as birth, old-age, death etc. This pāsuram explains “vīdu mudalām” which is mentioned in the first pāsuram.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the second pāsuram, āḻvār starts explaining “vīdu mudalām” (cause of liberation) and says “Is he needed to give liberation? Is the relationship with him alone not sufficient?”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “the relationship with emperumān is the cause for liberation after eliminating the relationship with samsāram (material realm)”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Second pāsuram. āḻvār says, “Is emperumān needed to bestow liberation? īsn’t the relationship with him sufficient?” by saying “en tani nāyagan puṇarppē” (the relationship with my singular master alone). nīndum tuyarp piṟavi utpada maṟṟu evvevaiyum nīndum tuyar illā vīdu mudalām pūm taṇ punal poygai yānai idar kadinda pūm taṇ tuḻāy en tani nāyagan puṇarppē*

- *nīndum …* – This pāsuram is explanation of “*piṟavik kadal nīnduvārkku*“. It should be understood as “*nīndum tuyarp piṟavi utpada maṟṟu evvevaiyum nīndum; tuyarillā vīdu mudalām*“; Alternatively “*nīndum … tuyarillā*” could be considered as adjective for *vīdu*.
- *nīndum …* – Since “*nīndum*” is a word in present tense, it implies that all sorrowful aspects which are difficult to overcome such as birth, decay, death etc will be eliminated.
- *tuyarillā vīdu mudalām* – he is the cause for mōkśam (liberation) where there is no trace of sorrow.  This implies that [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is the cause for the liberation which has no trace of any sufferings such as birth etc which are difficult to overcome. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is not just implying elimination of samsāram (engagement in material realm) by saying “vīdu”, he implies attainment of [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) which is filled with joy only. This is explained in nigaṇḍu (dictionary) as “*muktirmōkśō mahānanda:*” (mukti (liberation), mōkśam (liberation and mahānandam (great joy) are synonyms).

Where did we see him eliminating sorrows and bestowing joy?

- *pūm taṇ …* – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is the one who completely removed the sufferings of the elephant which was caught by the crocodile while entering the pond that is filled everywhere with blossomed cool flowers. gajēndrāḻvān (elephant) desired that he would submit the flower without losing its freshness at the lotus feet of emperumān – he was suffering since his desire was not fulfilled – it was emperumān who removed that suffering and facilitated him to fulfil his desire.
- *pūm taṇ tuḻāy en tani nāyagan* – he flew and jumped near the pond with the tuḷasi bunch placed on his head! Just like fragrance is natural for tuḷasi, removing the sorrows of the elephant (devotee) is natural for [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/). The suffering of elephant can also be explained as thinking – What if some one thinks “We believed that [sarvēśvaran](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) will protect us during dangers; but he is unfortunately not helping! Why is he behaving like someone who is devoid of good qualities?”.
- *en tani nāyagan* –  [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) feels that [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) removed his (āḻvār’s) own suffering instead of elephant’s suffering \[focussing on “*en*” – my\].
- *puṇarppu* – relationship with [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/). The connection with his divine feet will remove the sufferings and also bestow the blissful result \[of service to bhagavān in paramapadam\].

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.8.3. Punarkkum ayanam

*puṇarkkum ayanām aḻikkum aranām puṇartta tan undiyōdu āgattu manni puṇartta tiruvāgit tan mārvil tān sēr puṇarppan perum puṇarppu engum pulanē*

**Пословный перевод:**

than – him; puṇartta – created; undiyōdu – with the navel; āgattu – in one portion of his divine body; manni – eternally residing; puṇarkkum – one who creates the universe; ayanām – being aja (brahmā); aḻikkum – one who annihilates; aranām – being hara (rudra); than mārvil – in his chest; puṇartta – kept together (to be identity); tiruvāgi – having śrī mahālakśmi; tān – he himself; sēr – matching for his stature; puṇarppan – being the one with naturally beautiful activities; perum – boundless; puṇarppu – divine activities; engum – everywhere; pulan – popular as seen and enjoyed

**Перевод:**

**Simple translation (based on vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar‘s 12000 padi)**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the third pāsuram, āḻvār desiring to explain “iruvar avar mudalum tānē” says “The husband of śrī mahālakśmi, emperumān‘s \[immortal\] activities revealing his control \[over others\] is visible everywhere”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “His divine activities are well-known to everyone”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. puṇarkkum ayanām aḻikkum aranām puṇartta than undiyōdu āgattu manni puṇartta tiruvāgit than mārvil tān sēr puṇarppan perum puṇarppu engum pulanē*

- *puṇarkkum ayanām* – brahmā whose only job is to create the universe.
- *aḻikkum aranām* – Like a hot stick \[which is used to destroy others\], he stays as rudra destroying the universe. By having [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) as antarātmā (in-dwelling super-soul) they perform these activities. This is explained in mahābhāratam śānti parvam 169 “… *tadāśrita pantānau sruśtisamhārakārakau …*” (the top most of dēvas (celestial beings), brahmā and rudra who were born from bhagavān’s mercy and anger respectively, being guided by him, perform creation and annihilation – this is explained in smruti) and śrīviṣṇu darmam “… *sruśtim tata: kariśyāmi tvāmāviśya prajāpatē \|\|*” (Oh brahmā! I am going to create and place the earth as before, enter you and create subsequently).
- *puṇartta than undiyōdu āgattu manni puṇarkkum ayanām aḻikkum aranām* – They can only perform their tasks when they are connected with his divine body, just like a suckling baby cannot sustain itself when the mother withdraws her bosom from its mouth. With this, [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s antaryāmitvam (being the in-dwelling soul) is explained through sāmānādikaraṇyam (one entity being the common bearer of multiple entities which perform different tasks). By saying “*puṇartta than undi*” (created in his navel), his kāraṇatvam (being the cause) is established; by saying “*āgattu manni*” (eternally residing in his divine body), their existence depending on his divine body is established.
- *puṇartta tiruvāgit than mārvil* – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is the one who has [śrī mahālakśmi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/) in his chest eternally being united with him. Why is this explained now? Just like his being the creator reveals his control over everyone, the relationship with lakshmi is also an important factor that shows his control/wealth. His togetherness with periya pirāttiyār ([śrī mahālakśmi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/)) is the reason for his simplicity and supremacy.
- *tān sēr puṇarppan* – two explanations – he lies down in the causal ocean to initiate creation; he is the one who is having matching activities for his stature.
- *perum puṇarppu engum pulanē* – His activities which are conducted via brahmā et al (creation etc) and his great activities which he himself performs; such great activities are well known everywhere.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.8.4. Pulan aindum

*pulan aindu mēyum poṟi aindu nīngi nalam andam illadōr nādu puguvīr! alamandu vīya asuraraic ceṟṟān palamundu sīril padiminōvādē*

**Пословный перевод:**

pulan – visible matters; aindum – in those five; mēyum – well-fitting; poṟi – like a trap which catches him; aindum – from the five senses; nīngi – detaching; nalam – bliss; andamilladu – being unlimited; ōr – distinct/unique; nādu – in the abode; puguvīr – Oh the ones who desire to enter!; alamandu – toiling; vīya – be destroyed; asurarai – demons; seṟṟān – of the one who killed; mundu – from the beginning; palam – being the result (due to its sweetness); sīril – in the auspicious qualities; ōvādē – always; padimin – be immersed

**Перевод:**

**Oh the ones who desire to be detached from the five sense organs (ears, skin, eyes, nose and tongue) which trap him (ātmā) completely in the five matters (sound, touch, vision, smell and taste) and to enter the abode of unlimited bliss! emperumān who killed the demons that were destroyed after toiling hard – you always be immersed in the auspicious qualities of such emperumān which can be explained as the result (due to its sweetness) from the beginning.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fourth pāsuram – āḻvār says “Oh ones who desire eternal goal of liberation in the form of unsurpassed happiness after giving up attachment to petty worldly pleasures! You take refuge of emperumān“.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “To attain bhagavān after being relieved from this samsāram (material realm), you immerse in the auspicious qualities of such emperumān always”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*In the fourth pāsuram – āḻvār says “Oh ones who desire for liberation after cutting off the ties in this material realm on meditating upon emperumān of such nature! You immerse in his auspicious qualities”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Fourth pāsuram. There was no defect in bhagavān‘s supremacy \[as seen in previous pāsuram\]. Now, āḻvār says “Oh ones who wish to attain a benefit which has no equal! See that you quickly accept him as refuge”. pulan aindu mēyum poṟi aindu nīngi nalam andam illadōr nādu puguvīr! alamandu vīya asuraraic ceṟṟān palamundu sīril padiminōvādē*

- *pulan …* – pulan aindu means the five different matters (sound, touch, vision, smell and taste) and poṟi aindu are the sense organs (ears, skin, eyes, nose and tongue) which get trapped in those matters; being detached from them. Rats etc are killed by keeping a trap of certain fragrant substances; similarly the sense organs get trapped in the matters and become finished – so the sense organs are called trap. This implies that one is getting detached from being attached to the sense organs which can only perceive visible (physical) matters.
- *nalam …* – Oh ones who desire to enter the abode where there is no end of bliss/goodness! [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) being the most authoritative person mercifully explains that there is a divine abode which has endless bliss that is to be attained to discard the philosophy which advocates “becoming void as liberation”.
- *puguvīr* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says that our acceptance is the only qualification \[for liberation\].

Even if there is a divine abode and if an [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) has the desire to enter that divine abode, if there are strong obstacles, how would one reach the divine abode?

- *alamandu vīya asuraraic ceṟṟān* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) asks “Is it our job to remove the obstacles?”. [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) destroyed the demons so that they suffer and fall down \[Similarly, he will remove our obstacles\].
- *palamundu sīril padimin* – You engage in his auspicious activities which are enjoyable right from the beginning, viz., right when we start pursuing them. This is explained in bhagavat gītā 9.2 “… *susukam kartumavyayam*” (imperishable and very joyful to perform) – due to the object of meditation ([bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)), from the beginning, it is enjoyable to perform.
- *ōvādē* – There is no rule that one can come in contact with sea/ocean only during special days (month beginning, paurṇami (full-moon day) etc) – try to engage in bhagavān’s qualities always without any distraction. It can also be said as [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) encouraging others to engage in bhagavān’s qualities continuously since he enjoyed them very much. Just as it is said in periya tirumoḻi 6.10.6 “*nānum sonnēn namarum uraimin*” (as I have recited, let my friends/relatives also recite).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.8.5. Ovat tuyar

*ōvāt tuyar piṟavi utpada maṟṟu evvevaiyum mūvāt tani mudalāy mūvalgum kāvalōn māvāgi āmaiyāy mīnāgi mānidamām dēvādi dēva perumān en tīrttanē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ōvā – continuous (without break); tuyar – one that gives distress; piṟavi – creation which binds ātmā to birth; utpada – including; maṟṟu – others such as sustenance, annihilation etc; evvevaiyum – all other activities; mūvā – effortlessly; tani mudalāy – being the singular cause who does not expect anyone’s help; mūvulagum – of the (created) universe; kāvalōn – being the protector; dēva – for the dēvas (celestial beings) starting with brahmā et al; ādi dēvar – for those nityasūris who are beyond the reach (of such dēvatās); perumān – being the lord; en – for me; tīrttan – like a river bank, that is easily approachable; māvāgi – incarnating as hayagrīva (horse-headed form, who is the propagator of vēdam); āmaiyāy mīnāgi – incarnating as kūrma (tortoise) and matsya (fish) (who are propagators of purāṇas); mānidamām – and also incarnated as human form (who is the propagator of gītōpaniśat – bhagavat gītā)

**Перевод:**

**emperumān is the effortless singular cause of the created universe, without expecting anyone’s help. He is the protector of such universe which gives continuous  distress for the ātmā, continuously by binding it to the universe. He is also in control of all other activities including  sustenance, annihilation etc. He is the lord for those nityasūris who are beyond the reach of the dēvas (celestial beings) starting with brahmā et al and is like a river bank that is easily approachable by me. Such emperumān (for the protection of such universe) incarnates as hayagrīva (horse-headed form, who is the propagator of vēdam), as kūrma (tortoise) and matsya (fish) (who are propagators of purāṇas) and also incarnated as human form (who is the propagator of gītōpaniśat – bhagavat gītā). This pāsuram elaborates tiruvāimoḻi 2.8.1 “iṇaivanām epportkum” (would be born among all species).**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fifth pāsuram – āḻvār elaborates emperumān‘s sarvasajātīyatvam (being born in all species) saying “emperumān would mercifully incarnate as hayagrīva et al to protect the universes created by him”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār mercifully explains the unique nature of the many incarnations assumed by emperumān who is the cause of all to protect the result of his creation.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Fifth pāsuram. āḻvār explains previously highlighted tiruvāimoḻi 2.8.1 “iṇaivanām epportkum” (would be born among all species). ōvāt tuyar piṟavi utpada maṟṟu evvevaiyum mūvāt tani mudalāy mūvalgum kāvalōn māvāgi āmaiyāy mīnāgi mānidamām dēvādi dēva perumān en tīrttanē*

- *ōvāt tuyar piṟavi utpada …* – Before he said in [tiruvāimoḻi 2.8.2](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/05/thiruvaimozhi-2-8-2-nindhum-thuyar/) “*nīndum tuyarp piṟavi*” (sorrowful birth etc which are difficult to cross-over); here he says – it is not just something that gives us opportunities to recoup and escape – it is those six aspects (jāyatē – birth, asti – existence, pariṇamatē – change, vivardatē – growth, apakśīyatē – decay, naśyati – disappearance) and the objects of such aspects which cause continuous sorrows.
- *mūvāt tanimudal – mūvā* – without laziness, effortlessly; this is explained as adjective for both “*ōvāt tuyar piṟavi utpada*” and *“tani mudal*“, that is, [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) being the singular cause without laziness for these six aspects which go on eternally in continuity (*pravāha rūpattālē nityam*) and being the effortless singular cause of these entire creations. Though [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) gives body/senses to ātmās to facilitate them to worship him, if they misuse the tools, he would think “if they do like this, let me develop their taste towards me over time”, will allow them to continue in their path and be neutral/indifferent towards them. Thus, even if they digress from his own desire (of accepting all of them), like a farmer who would try growing crops again and again instead of giving up, he keeps engaging in creation again and again. This is explained in periya tiruvantādi 18 “*sōmbādu ippal uruvai ellām padarvitta vittā*” (without laziness, you, who are the original cause who created this universe that has variegated aspects).

What is he creating and protecting?

- *mūvulagum kāvalōn* – whatever that is in the boundary of the material realm. Two explanations for mūvulagam:
   - 3 layers – Lower layer (seven worlds below bhūmi (earth) – atala, vitala, …, pātāla), middle layer (Earth), upper layer (six worlds above earth – bhuva:, svarga, maha:, jana:, tapa:, satya).
   - 3 types of worlds – krutakam (3 worlds below mahar lōkam – bhū: (earth), bhūva:, svarga) – these are recreated as part of each manvantra (life of manu – 71 catur yugams approximately), akrutakam (3 worlds above mahar lōkam) – jana:, tapa:, satya – these remain undisturbed even during the dissolution of a manvantra, krutakākrutakam (maharlōkam) – this gets recreated at a lesser frequency \[during the beginning of brahmā’s day which contains 1000 catur yugams\] \[Here the context of recreation is within the boundary of brahmā’s one day\].
- *kāvalōn* – Protecting by propagating śāstram etc.

Does he protect without minimizing his supremacy?

- *māvāgi …* – akarmavaśya (one who is not bound by karma) being born amongst / like karmavaśya (one who is bound by karma).
- *māvāgi* – incarnated as hayagrīva mūrtti (horse headed form).
- *āmaiyāy mīnāgi* – incarnations which are focussed on revealing sacred/true knowledge.
- *mānidamām* – incarnations such as śrī rāma, kriṣṇa et al. As explained in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 35.11 “*maryādānām ca lōkasya kartā kārayitā ca sa:*” (That śrī rāma is the epitome of maintaining honour/dignity and one who engages others to be honourable/dignified) and in bhagavat gītā 3.21 “*yadyadācarati śrēśta: …*” (whatever performed by great person, common men will follow…”.

Who is the person who makes himself available in such mortal forms?

- *dēvādi dēva perumān* – He is beyond the reach of nityasūris who cannot handle the smell/acquaintance of dēvas (celestial beings) who cannot handle the smell/acquaintance of humans.
- *en tīrttanē* – two explanations:
   - pure – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who has the purity to purify me; he changed my desire from worldly matters, towards him (I was like those who desire for cheap foods when most delicious foods are available).
   - easily approachable – he is like the banks of a river where we can step in and immerse.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.8.6. Tirttan

*tīrttan ulagaḷanda sēvadi mēl pūndāmam sērtti avaiyē sivan mudimēl tān kaṇḍu pārttan teḷindu oḻinda painduḻāyān perumai pērttum oruvarāl pēsak kidandadē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tīrttan – In the previous incarnation of pure kriṣṇa; ulagu – the three worlds; aḷanda – measured; sē – having freshness; adimēl – on the divine feet; pūm – beautiful; dāmam – garlands; sērtti – offered; avaiyē – the same garlands; sivan – Siva’s; mudimēl – on matted hair; tān – he himself; kaṇḍu – seen; pārttan – arjuna; teḷindu oḻinda – established; paim – fresh/green; tuḻāyān – of the one who is having tuḷasi; perumai – supremacy; pērttum – other than arjuna; oruvarāl – anyone else; pēsa – to narrate; kidandadē – is there any aspect that remains to be clarified?

**Перевод:**

**arjuna offered fresh garlands on the lotus feet of pure kriṣṇa who measured the three worlds in his previous incarnation \[as vāmana/trivikrama\]; he then saw the same flowers on the matted hair of Siva; this is the supremacy of the one who is having fresh/green tuḷasi garlands on him that is established by arjuna; can anyone else other than arjuna narrate this supremacy and is there any aspect of this supremacy that remains to be clarified still? It implies that bhagavān‘s supremacy is already well established.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the sixth pāsuram, āḻvār asks “Is there a need to analyse the supremacy of bhagavān by any more persons after having been analysed by arjuna?”*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “the supremacy in his incarnations is very famous”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Sixth pāsuram. When asked “Does the bhagavān you speak about, have all these greatness?” āḻvār replies “Already arjuna analysed and established this principle (supremacy of bhagavān). Is there any doubt remaining in that which needs to be analysed by us?”. tīrttan ulagaḷanda sēvadi mēl pūndāmam sērtti avaiyē sivan mudimēl tān kaṇḍu pārttan teḷindu oḻinda painduḻāyān perumai pērttum oruvarāl pēsak kidandadē*

- *tīrttan* – As said in stōtra ratnam 13 “… *pādōdakēna sa Siva: svaśirōdrudēna*” (by beholding the water from whose feet, he became Siva (pure)?” and in īśvara samhitai “… *pāvanārttam jatāmadyē yōjñōsmītyavadāraṇāt*” (Siva, seeing the gangā water falling from the divine feet of [śrīman nārāyaṇan](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), knowing well that he is qualified, for his purification, held it in his matted locks), [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/), through the connection with his divine feet, is able to purify even the impure ones.

When asked when did this incident happen?

- *ulagu aḷanda sēvadi* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) reminds us that this incident happened during the time when [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) measured the worlds. nampiḷḷai explains this through nānmugan tiruvantādi 9th pāsuram beautifully. *kuṟai koṇḍu* – with his ākincanyam (unworthiness – having nothing). *nānmugan kuṇḍigai nīr peydu* – On brahmā’s desire, dharma tatvam (the deity for righteousness) assumes the form of water and enters brahmā’s kamaṇḍalam (water pot). *maṟai koṇḍa mandirattāl vāḻtti* – Praising him through śrī puruśa sūktam etc. *kaṟai koṇḍa kaṇḍattān senni mēl ēṟak kaḻuvinān* – Thinking “without analysing the instructions, he (Siva) pursued unrighteousness (considering himself to be independent); that should be gone”, brahmā washes the lotus feet of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) so that the water falls onto Siva’s matted locks, just like a father will sprinkle the śrīpāda tīrttam (holy water) on the heads of evil children. While the current pāsuram is talking about kriṣṇāvatāram, why is he suddenly citing an incident from vāmanāvatāram? Because both kriṣṇa and vāmana mingled with everyone freely without discrimination, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) narrates an incident from vāmana’s caritram while explaining about kriṣṇāvatāram.
- *pūndāmam sērtti* – Here [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is explaining the incident from mahābhārata yuddam (battle). When arjuna once desired to acquire a weapon from a dēvatā (Siva) and set out to ask for that, kriṣṇa mercifully told him to reduce his troubles “You place those flowers at my lotus feet and you will succeed”. arjuna followed kriṣṇa’s words and did the same. In the night, Siva appears in arjuna’s dream beholding those same flowers in his head and bestows the weapons to arjuna. pūndāmam means both pūmālai (flower garland) and aḻagiya mālai (beautiful garland).
- *avaiyē* – they were not other flowers of the same kind \[they were the same flowers\].
- *sivan mudi mēl tān kaṇḍu* – Not on the side, but he saw them directly on Siva’s head.
- *tān kaṇḍu* – Not heard from some trustworthy person, not seen in some scriptures such as śruti or smruti, he himself saw that. He saw it so that he can remember it clearly.
- *pārttan* … – arjuna, who did not get confused about kriṣṇa’s supremacy even though he assumed the role of the charioteer. As said in gītā bhāśyam by [emperumānār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/emperumanar/) “*sa tu pārtō mahāmanā:*” (that most intelligent arjuna), the wisest arjuna analysed and established the supremacy of kriṣṇa and worshiped him as in [bhagavat gītā](http://githa.koyil.org/) 11.40 “*nama: purastādata pruśtatastē*” (I worship in front of you and behind you).
- *paim tuḻāyān perumai* – The supremacy of sarvēśvara is highlighted by his wearing fresh/green tirutuḻāy (tuḷasi) garlands; is that needed to be analysed by any less-intelligent people now?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.8.7. Kidandirundu

*kidandu irundu ninṟu aḷandu kēḻalāyk kīḻpukku – idandidum tannuḷ karakkum umiḻum tadam perum tōḷ ārat taḻuvum pārennum madandaiyai māl seyginṟa māl ār kāṇbārē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kidandu – lay down (on the seashore, praying to \[samudrarāja, the King of oceans to\] give way (to protect) as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam “pratiśiśyē mahōdadim“); irundu – sat (in citrakūta as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam “utajē rāmamāsīnam“); ninṟu – stood (amidst the celestial deities holding his bow after killing rāvaṇa); aḷandu – measured \[as trivikrama to win over the universe\]; kēḻalāy – in the form of a wild boar; kīḻ – underneath the causal water; pukku – entered; idandidum – separated from the walls of the universe and rescued; tannuḷ – during mahāpraḷayam (total annihilation in the form of a baby lying down on a leaf and holding the universe) in his stomach; than uḷ – inside him; karakkum – hide it inside (so no one can see); umiḻum – spit it out to let them see outside; tadam – spacious; perum – big; tōḷ – divine shoulders; Ara – to fulfil; taḻuvum – embrace (with his divine form); pār ennum – known as bhūmi; madandaiyai – girl; māl – īsvara who is greater than all; seyginṟa – performing; māl – affection; kāṇbār – can see/know; Ar – who?

**Перевод:**

**emperumān lay down (on the seashore praying to give way (to protect) as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam “pratiśiśyē mahōdadim“), sat (in citrakūta as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam “utajē rāmamāsīnam“) and stood (amidst the celestial deities holding his bow after killing rāvaṇa); alternatively, this could be explained as emperumān assuming different forms (lying, sitting, standing) in arcāvatāram (deity forms) as explained in tiruvāimoḻi 9.2.4 “puḷingudik kidandu varaguṇamangai irundu vaikuntattuḷ ninṟu” (lying down in tiruppuḷingudi, sitting in varaguṇamangai and standing in śrīvaikuṇṭam divya dēśams). He measured \[as trivikrama to win over the universe\]; in the form of a wild boar he entered underneath the causal water, separated earth from the walls of the universe and rescued it; during mahāpraḷayam (total annihilation), he hid the universe inside him (so no one can see it) in his stomach (assuming the form of a baby lying down on a leaf); he would spit the universe out so the residents can see outside; he would embrace bhūmi dēvi fully with his broad shoulders (in his special form). Who can understand these loving interactions of bhagavān who is greater than all with the girl named bhūmi dēvi? It is implied that even the most intelligent ones cannot understand it.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the seventh pāsuram, āḻvār starts to explain that bhagavān‘s supremacy itself should prove his unconditional help in the form of lying down and resting in milk ocean \[for the protection of all\], but says that it is impossible to understand them due to the innumerable nature of such acts.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says that emperumān, out of motherly forbearance towards the universe that is protected,would perform many acts.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Seventh pāsuram. Should we determine his supremacy based on one individual’s praising? This universe fully exists for his sport. Is this not enough proof to show his supremacy? kidandu irundu ninṟu aḷandu kēḻalāyk kīḻpukku – idandidum tannuḷ karakkum umiḻum tadam perum tōḷ ārat taḻuvum pārennum madandaiyai māl seyginṟa māl Ar kāṇbārē*

- *kidandu* – lying down in tiruppāṟkadal (milk ocean); or lying down in the seashore as explained in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 21.1 “*pratiśiśyē*” (lay down); his lying down with his hand supporting his head would look like him lying down on tiruvanantāḻvān (ādiśēśa – serpent bed) as said in the same ślōkam “*bāhum bhujagabhōgābham*” (hand resembling the body of a serpent). As further explained in the same ślōkam “*arisūdana:*” (one who destroys the enemies), seeing his comfortable/commanding form of resting, the demoniac residents of lankā would fearfully leave their residences. “*pratiśiśyē mahōdadē*” (lay down next to the great sea) – it appears as if one sea is lying down next to another sea.
- *irundu* – sitting in paramapadam; or sitting in the hermitage of the sages as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 99.25 “*utajē rāmamāsīnam*” (rāma seated in the hermitage).
- *ninṟu* – standing in tirumalā (tiruvēnkatam); or standing victoriously at the entrance of lankā with his bow, after killing rāvaṇa; standing after killing vāli. As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam kiśkintā kāṇḍam 19.25 “*avaśtabhya ca tiśtantam dadarśa danurūrjitam \| rāmam rāmānujam caiva bhartuścaivānujam śubhā \|\|*” (The good-hearted tārā (wife of vāli) saw rāma who is leaning on his strong bow, lakśmaṇa and her own husband’s brother sugrīva), his supremacy can be heard from the wives of those who were defeated by him. śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 114.15 “*tamasa: paramō dātā śankacakragadādara:*” (maṇḍōdari, the wife of rāvaṇa says about śrī rāma – the lord of śrīvaikuṇṭam which is beyond the material realm, who holds conch, disc and maze). śrī rāmāyaṇam kiśkintā kāṇḍam 24.31 “*tvamapramēyaśca*” (tārā says to śrī rāma – you cannot be measured even by vēdam).
- *aḷandu* – when the likes of mahābali claim ownership of earth, which is [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s property, he redeems it by measuring it.
- *kēḻalāyk kīḻ pukku idandidum* – he would assume the form of a varāham (wild boar) which would not hesitate jumping into water/mud, jump into the causal ocean, separate the earth from the walls of the universe under water and rescue the same.
- *than uḷ karakkum* – Instead of kicking/knocking the earth in the name of protection, he would place it safely in his stomach. Also explained as, knowing that there will be praḷayam (total annihilation), he would conceal the universe inside his stomach and pretend as if nothing existed to be destroyed even during praḷayam.
- *umiḻum* – he would spit them out to see what happened to them inside his stomach and to let them see the outside.
- *tadam perum tōḷ ārat taḻuvum* – He would embrace with his well-developed shoulders to his full satisfaction.
- *pār ennum madandaiyai* – śrī bhūmip pirātti (bhūdēvi). Since earth is a prakāram (mode/form) of bhūdēvi, she is indicated by that term (pār – bhūmi). When [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) takes so much effort in protecting his property, bhūdēvi who is the abhimānini dēvatā (controlling deity) for earth, with great love, would embrace him; he too will embrace her in return.
- *māl* – sarvēśvaran who is greater than all \[Here, māl means svāmi – lord\]
- *seyginṟa māl* – the great attachment he shows \[Here, māl means attachment\] towards bhūdēvi
- *Ar kāṇbārē* – can anyone comprehend it?

## 2.8.8. Kanbar ar

*kāṇbār ār em īsan kaṇṇanai en kāṇumāṟu ūṇ pēsil ellā ulagum ōr tuṟṟāṟṟā sēṇpāla vīdō uyirō maṟṟu epporutkum ēṇpālum sōrān parandu uḷanāam engumē*

**Пословный перевод:**

em – my; īsan – being lord; kaṇṇanai – kriṣṇa who is easily approachable; kāṇbār – one who can know; Ar – who?; kāṇumāṟu – to know; en – how?; ūṇ – food; pēsil – if we try to say; ellā ulagum – all worlds (which are filled with movable/immovable objects); ōr tuṟṟu – even for a handful; āṟṟā – not sufficient; vīdō – his residence (where he lives); sēṇpāla – As explained in cāndōjña upaniśad “viśvata: pruśtēśu sarvata: pruśtēśu” (beyond everything else in this material world), in the paramapadam (spiritual realm) that is much beyond all of the material realm; avanō – him; maṟṟu – other than him; epporutkum – all objects; uyir – antarātmā (in-dwelling super soul); ēṇpālum – even a small place; sōrān – without losing; engum – in all places; parandu – pervaded; uḷanām – exists

**Перевод:**

**Simple translation (based on vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar‘s 12000 padi)**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the eighth pāsuram – āḻvār says “His magnificent activities, even individually, cannot be comprehended by the wisest persons”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “his divine aspects which were revealed by him to me, cannot be easily understood/taught for any one”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*In the eighth pāsuram – āḻvār says “For those who depend on self-effort to see/understand him, how can they even comprehend one among his many magnificent activities?”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. kāṇbār Ar em īsan kaṇṇanai en kāṇumāṟu ūṇ pēsil ellā ulagum ōr tuṟṟāṟṟā sēṇpāla vīdō uyirō maṟṟu epporutkum ēṇpālum sōrān parandu uḷanāam engumē*

- *kāṇbār Ar em īsan kaṇṇanai* – Being the supreme lord,  he still appeared as [kriṣṇa](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) and became controllable by me. Unlike me who saw him after he himself decided to reveal about him, others who try with their own efforts cannot see him. Is there anyone who can know/see him with his/her own self-efforts? Leaving that aside, is there anyone who has known/seen him?
- *en kāṇumāṟu* – Which aspects can they know? Even if intelligent persons set out to know him, his aspects are unlimited to know. Why are they difficult to understand? His activities are such that they are difficult to understand. If we try to explain how he eats, all of the worlds will not even be a handful for him. How can anyone comprehend [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who has such activities?

After saying his activities are difficult to understand, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) further says that his nature too is not easy to understand.

- *sēṇpāla vīdō* – He is owning the paramapadam which is naturally great, muktātmās (liberated souls) and nityātmās (ever-free souls) and all other dēvatās (celestial beings) et al \[sēṇ – greatness, pāl – having\].
- *ēṇpālum sōrān* – *ēṇpālum –* two explanations – a) all conceivable places, b) eight directions. He is pervading in all these places.
- *parandu uḷanām engumē* – When he is pervading, he pervades everywhere without leaving any space. This being the case, how can any of the objects which are pervaded by [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/),  comprehend [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is pervaded everywhere?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.8.9. Engumulan kannan

*engum uḷan kaṇṇan enṟa maganaik kāyndu ingillaiyā enṟu iraṇiyan tūṇ pudaippa angappoḻudē avan vīyat tōnṟiya en – singap pirān perumai ārāyum sīrmaittē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kaṇṇan – as said in “sarvam vyāpya stita:” (everywhere pervaded and well situated), sarvēśvaran who is the controller of all; engum – everywhere; uḷan – one who is present; enṟa – thus said; maganai – son; kāyndu – shunned or showing anger; ingu – here; illai – not present; enṟu – saying so; tūṇ – pillar (which was declared by himself as the place devoid of emperumān); iraṇiyan – hiraṇya kaśipu; pudaippa – hit; angu – in that pillar itself; appoḻudē – instantaneously; avan – hiraṇya kaśipu; vīya – to be destroyed; tōnṟiya – presented his form; en – my; singam – half human and half lion form; pirān – great saviour’s; perumai – greatness (of being partial towards his devotees); ārāyum – analysing (through the heart); sīrmaittē – is it of that nature?

**Перевод:**

**hiraṇya kaśipu showed his anger on his son śrī prahlādāḻvān who said sarvēśvran who is the controller of all is present everywhere as said in “sarvam vyāpya stita:” (everywhere pervaded and well situated), saying “He is not here” and hit the pillar (which was declared by himself as the place devoid of emperumān); emperumān appeared in that pillar itself instantaneously in a half human and half lion form; Is the greatness  (of being partial towards his devotees) of such narasimhan emperumān who is a great saviour of the nature that it can be analysed and understood?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the ninth pāsuram – āḻvār says “it is impossible to comprehend the greatness of śrī narasimha, who appeared instantaneously on request of śrī prahlādāḻvān to prove his all-pervasive nature even to convince those who don’t believe that”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says that his mingling freely with his devotees is difficult to comprehend.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Ninth pāsuram. When asked “What you are saying is inconclusive. How can the same object pervade many objects without losing any of its aspects? Is it possible?” āḻvār says “Oh losers! You will also suffer the same fate as hiraṇyakaśipu who did not accept emperumān’s omnipresence”. engum uḷan kaṇṇan enṟa maganaik kāyndu ingillaiyā enṟu iraṇiyan tūṇ pudaippa angappoḻudē avan vīyat tōnṟiya en – singap pirān perumai ārāyum sīrmaittē*

- *engum uḷan kaṇṇan* – This is the mistake he committed; he said “*sarvēśvaran is omnipresent*“. He simply repeated the words of kriṣṇa himself. bhagavat gītā 9.4 “*mayā tatamidam sarvam* …” (this universe is pervaded by me). bhagavat gītā 10.39 “*na tadasti vinā yat syānmayā*” (whatever exists, it does not exist without me).
- *enṟa maganaik kāyndu* – Even if an enemy utters these words, one should fall at the enemy’s feet too (due to the great meaning of the words); considering the relationship (his own son), he should only praise his son for uttering such wise words; even considering the age too, he should praise due to a young boy saying such wise words; nampiḷḷai explains this using periya tirumoḻi 2.3.8 pāsuram. As it is school-going age as said in “*paḷḷiyil ōdi vanda*” (learning in school), whatever recited will be praiseworthy. Further, “*than siṟuvan*” (his own son) – since he is his own progeny, his words should be dear to him. More over,”*vāyil ōr āyira nāmam*” (1000 names in his mouth) – what he said is the divine name of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/). “*oḷḷiyavāgip pōda*” (recited in a sweet manner) – even if the words are not worthy, since they are said sweetly, they should be praised. “*āngu adanukku onṟum ōr poṟuppilanāgi*” (unable to bear those words, right there) – this is called asahyāpacāram (offense without any specific reason). “*piḷḷaiyaic cīṟi*” – he disowned his own son citing the recital of divine names as the only reason. But [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) proclaims such prahlādāḻvān as \[his own\] “piḷḷai” (magan – son).
- *maganaik kāyndu* – Though his own son, because of recital of divine names of emperumān, he showed his anger towards prahlādāḻvān.
- *ingu …* – He pats the nearby pillar and says “if he is everywhere, he should not be absent here” and hits it. As said in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 1.7.9 “*aḷanditta tūṇai avan tatta*” (he hit the pillar that was built by himself) – since it was built directly under his supervision, one cannot say that “narasimha was placed inside pillar previously while constructing the pillar”. “*avan tatta*” (he himself hit the pillar) – if some one else hit the pillar, one may say “the one who hit the pillar hid the narasimhan [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) in his hand and sneaked him inside the pillar before breaking it”.
- *angu appoḻudē* – inside the pillar itself, in the same place. instantaneously – right when prahlādāḻvān vowed the presence of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) everywhere.
- *avan vīyat tōnṟiya* – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) appeared fiercely such that his appearance itself will kill hiraṇya kaśipu (due to the fearsome appearance). Seeing narasimha emperumān’s roar, angrily folded tongue on top of the lip, reddish angry eyes, raised eyebrows, hiraṇya kaśipu melted like a roasted pig since he is gold (hiraṇya means gold which melts in heat).
- *en singap pirān perumai* – Can the supremacy of narasimha [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who favoured his devotees, be analysed by someone now?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.8.10. Sirmai kol

*sīrmai koḷ vīdu suvargga naragīrā īrmai koḷ dēvar naduvā maṟṟu epporutkum vēr mudalāy vittāyp parandu tani ninṟa kār mugil pōl vaṇṇan en kaṇṇanai nān kaṇḍēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

sīrmai koḷ – having greatness (of being accomplished by bhagavān‘s mercy instead of being achievable by one’s own virtues/vices); vīdu – mōkśam – liberation (paramapadam – spiritual realm); suvargga naragu – svarga (heaven) and naraka (hell) (which are resulting from virtues and vices); īṟā – having as upper boundary; īrmai koḷ – kind-hearted; dēvar – celestial beings; naduvā – being the intermediary (between the means and the result); maṟṟu – \[other\] primary forms; epporutkum – all entities/aspects such as sādanam (means) etc; vēr – being the sahakāri kāraṇa (ancillary cause); mudalāy – being the nimitta kāraṇa (instrumental cause); vittāy – being the upādāna kāraṇa (material cause); parandu – pervading everywhere; tani – being different (from all objects he pervades); ninṟa – being situated; kār – in the rainy season; mugil pōl – like a cloud; vaṇṇan – having the form; en – being easily approachable by me; kaṇṇanai – kriṣṇa; nān – I; kaṇḍēnē – enjoyed him – saying this he becomes delighted

**Перевод:**

**bhagavān is the all three causes viz., upādāna kāraṇam (material cause), nimitta kāraṇam (instrumental cause) and sahakāri kāraṇam (ancillary cause) for the great mōkśam (liberation – paramapadam – spiritual realm which can only be accomplished by bhagavān’s mercy instead of one’s own virtues/vices), for all objects/aspects starting with the primary forms, means etc., having the kind-hearted celestial beings who are the intermediary (between the means and the result) in the middle and svargam (heaven)/narakam (hell) as the upper boundary; he is all-pervading omnipresent. āḻvār becomes delighted that he enjoys such kaṇṇan emperumān who is having a beautiful cloud like form in rainy season.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the tenth pāsuram – āḻvār says “Let others do whatever they want; I am glad to have enjoyed emperumān who is the lord of both spiritual realm and material realm”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār becomes delighted that he enjoyed bhagavān who is the saviour in all manners and is the one who bestows mōkśam.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*In the tenth pāsuram – āḻvār becomes delighted like someone who escaped with his belongings in a mass robbery saying “I am happy to enjoy him”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Tenth pāsuram. āḻvār becomes delighted meditating upon the benefit for self thinking “Leave the others. Instead of becoming like them, at least we are able to enjoy him”. sīrmai koḷ vīdu suvargga naragīrā īrmai koḷ dēvar naduvā maṟṟu epporutkum vēr mudalāy vittāyp parandu tani ninṟa kār mugil pōl vaṇṇan en kaṇṇanai nān kaṇḍēnē*

- *sīrmai koḷ* … – For the paramapadam (spiritual realm) which is best in all manners, heaven which has limited pleasures, hell which has exclusive suffering at the end, kind-hearted celestial beings in the middle, other animal forms etc
- *vēr mudalāy vittāy* – he is exclusively the three types of causes
- *parandu* – As said in taittirīya upaniśat “*tat sruśtvā tadēvānuprāviśat tadanupraviśya sacca tyaccābhavat*” (He created it (universe); he entered in there; after entering he became (assumed the forms of) cētana (sentient) and acētana (insentient)) – first he created the universe and the entities, subsequently entered into them to give them names and forms and thus being the cause of everything \[anu pravēśam – [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is already present everywhere; he is entering into the objects means that he is transforming the entities from a subtle (unmanifest) state to gross (manifest) state\].
- *tani ninṟa …* – Not only he stayed as jagaccarīra (having the universe as his body), highlighting his distinct nature, though he remained in paramapadam with a beautiful laden cloud (in rainy season) like dark-hued form, he descended as kriṣṇa to be controlled by me – I enjoyed such [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) happily, says [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/).

## 2.8.11. Kan talangal

*kaṇ talangaḷ seyya karumēni ammānai vaṇḍalambum sōlai vaḻudi vaḷa nādan paṇ talaiyil sonna tamiḻ āyirattippattum vallār viṇḍalaiyil vīṟṟirundu āḷvar emmā vīdē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kaṇ – in the eye; talangaḷ – fully; seyya – reddish; karu – (contrasting it) blackish; mēni – having divine form; ammānai – lord of all; vaṇḍu – beetles; alambum – moving around in the flood of honey; sōlai – having gardens; vaḻudi vaḷa nādan – āḻvār who owns tiruvaḻudi vaḷanādu; paṇ talaiyil – keeping the tune as the foundation; sonna – mercifully sang; tamiḻ āyirattu – thousand pāsurams of tiruvāimoḻi; ippattum – this decad; vallār – those who are well-versed; viṇ talaiyil – on top of the paramākāśam (spiritual sky); vīṟṟu irundu – As said in “sa svarātbhavati” (he has become the emperor), being seated distinctly; e (em) – being together in all manner; mā – having unlimited joy; vīdu – the bliss of mōkśam (liberation); āḷvar – will experience with full control

**Перевод:**

**nammāḻvār who owns tiruvaḻudi vaḷanādu which has gardens, having beetles moving around in flood of honey, mercifully sang this decad in the thousand pāsurams having tune as the foundation, about emperumān who is the lord of all, who has blackish divine body contrasting his fully reddish eyes; those who are well-versed in this decad, will be seated distinctly as said in “sa svarātbhavati” (he has become the emperor) on top of the paramākāśam (spiritual sky) and will experience the bliss of mōkśam being together in all manner having unlimited joy with full control. emmā vīdu is also explained as the great abode (parampadam) which he has decided to bestow to me and those who are related to me.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the end – āḻvār says “Those who learn this decad, will achieve the most distinct wealth of the liberated individuals, as explained in this decad”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār mercifully explains sovereign control over all as the result of this decad.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. kaṇ talangaḷ seyya karumēni ammānai vaṇḍalambum sōlai vaḻudi vaḷa nādan paṇ talaiyil sonna tamiḻ āyirattippattum vallār viṇḍalaiyil vīṟṟirundu āḷvar emmā vīdē*

- *kaṇ talangaḷ* … – Like it is said in “*bhūtalangaḷ*” (the vast lands), here “*talangaḷ*” explains the vastness of “*kaṇ*” (eye). āḻvār praised sarvēśvaran who has vast reddish eyes and a contrasting divine blackish body, through his poetry.
- *vaṇḍu …* – Like one is tossed around in a flood,  beetles are tossed around in the flood in the gardens which are present in tiruvaḻudi vaḷanādu (āḻvārtirunagari and its surroundings) which is owned by nammāḻvār. pāsurams sung by such āḻvār. This prabandam is sung in talaiyāna paṇ (top-most tune). Alternatively, it is explained as pāsuram sung with a tune. Among the thousand pāsurams, those who are well-versed in this decad, as said in taittiriya upaniśad “*nāgasya pruśtē*” (seated on ādi śēśa in śrīvaikuṇṭam), will be seated in paramapadam in a distinct manner having mōkśam fully under their disposal.
- *viṇ talai* – explained as *talaiyāna viṇ* (top-most sky), *viṇṇin mēlē* (on top of the sky). They will achieve a stature where the residents of paramapadam will follow their orders. They will achieve not just ātmalābham (self-realization), but will achieve *paramapuruśārtalakśaṇa mōkśam* (ultimate goal of engaging at emperumān’s kainkaryam forever).
- *vīṟṟu irundu* – Staying relaxed, being freed from all the turmoils of the material realm.
- *āḷvar emmā vīdē* – As explained in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.5.10](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/08/thiruvaimozhi-1-5-10-sarntha-iru/) “*than pāl manam vaikkat tirutti vīdu tiruttuvān*” (reform the jīvātmā to be fully engaged with him and freshen up paramapadam too), they will rule the paramapadam (spiritual realm) which is prepared for the pleasure of me (āḻvār) and those who are related to me.

Finally, nampiḷḷai summarizes the contents of this decad briefly.

- In the first pāsuram, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) started explaining the principles of the decad briefly by saying “emperumān would help cross-over this ocean of material world for those who desire to do so”.
- In the second pāsuram, he said “He is not needed to that; relationship with him will itself do that”.
- In the third pāsuram, he said “bhagavān’s immortal activities are visibly seen”.
- In the fourth pāsuram, he said “Oh those who want to enjoy boundless bliss! Take shelter of him”.
- In the fifth pāsuram, he elaborated tiruvāimoḻi 2.8.1 “*iṇaivanām epporutkum*” (he will be born among all species) phrase.
- In the sixth pāsuram, when asked “Does he have all these greatness?”, he said “arjuna already analysed and established so that we don’t have to do that again”.
- In the seventh pāsuram, he said “Is this something we need to know by someone’s words? We can see that the whole universe exists for his sport”.
- In the eighth pāsuram, he said “his omnipresence etc cannot be comprehended by any one”.
- In the ninth pāsuram,  he said “those who do not agree with his omnipresence will suffer like hiraṇya kaśipu”.
- In the tenth pāsuram, he said “I have seen/known such emperumān”.
- In the end, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) explains the result for those who learnt this decad and completes the same.

## 2.9 Emma vittu

## 2.9.1. Emma vittu

*emmā vīttut tiṟamum seppam – nin semmā pāda paṟput talai sērttu – ollai kaimmā tunbam kadinda pirānē! ammā adiyēn vēṇḍuvadu īdē*

**Пословный перевод:**

e – in all ways; mā – great; vīttut tiṟam – form of liberation; seppam – won’t say/ask; nin – your; sem – reddish; mā – apt; pāda paṟpu – divine lotus feet; talai – on my head; ollai – immediately; sērttu – to be joined/placed; kaimmā – the elephant who had drowned into the pond along with its trunk; tunbam – suffering; kadinda – one who eliminated; pirānē – being most magnanimous; ammā – the lord who accepted my servitude (manifesting this incident); adiyēn – I who am servant (of you); vēṇḍuvadu – praying for (the result which matches my nature); īdē – this only

**Перевод:**

**I won’t ask for the form of liberation that is great in all ways; I only want to have your divine reddish feet which are apt for me, immediately placed on my head. Oh my lord who eliminated the sufferings of the elephant who had drowned into the pond along with its trunk! Oh my lord who magnanimously accepted my service! I, who am servant (of you), am praying to you for this (result which matches my nature) only. Implies that, that which is desired by puruśa is puruśārtam (goal).**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*In the first pāsuram – āḻvār desires for the goal which is connection with emperumān‘s divine feet over fully qualified liberation.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the first pāsuram – āḻvār says “I am not desiring even for the top-most goal of reaching śrīvaikuṇṭam; my goal is only to have your divine feet placed on my head”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See piḷḷān‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. emmā vīttut tiṟamum seppam – nin semmā pāda paṟput talai sērttu – ollai kaimmā tunbam kadinda pirānē! ammā adiyēn vēṇḍuvadu īdē*

- *em mā vīttut tiṟamum* – īśvaran said “[āḻvīr](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)! Here, accept mōkśam”; āḻvār said “No! I don’t want”; [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) said “this is *mā vīdu* – distinct/special mōkśam”; āḻvār said “I don’t want that too”; emperumān further said “this is *em mā vīdu* – don’t think that is *aiśvaryam* (joy in this world) or *ātma lābham* (*kaivalyam* – eternal self enjoyment); this is *parama puruśārta lakśaṇa mōkśam* (attainment of the ultimate liberation of eternal joyful service in śrīvaikuṇṭam)” āḻvār says “I don’t want even that”. I don’t want to hear any discussion on any form of liberation (however great it may be).
- *seppam* – we won’t speak about it. You need not bring up that discussion and I need not discard your suggestion.
- *emmā vīttut tiṟamum seppam* – An expert in tamiḻ explained “*tiṟamum seppam*” as “*vikalpamum sevviyum*“. vikapam means choice/diverse – here, it explains the different aspects of mōkśam (sālōkya – residing in the same place as [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/), sārūpya – having similar form to bhagavān, sāmīpya – being in close proximity to bhagavān and sāyujya – being connected to bhagavān). seppam – semmai – best (all inclusive) – in this, all types of mōkśam are contained.

When asked “but, what is it that you need?”,

- *nin semmā pāda paṟput talai sērttu* – This is what I need. sem – reddish and mā – blackish; you have to place your divine feet which is reddish on the inside and blackish on the outside that resemble a lotus flower which has broadness, freshness, coolness and fragrance. Alternatively, *semmai* implies *sevvai – ārjavam* (honesty) which ensures that the devotees don’t need to worry. *mā* indicates greatness and most vorśippable divine feet. sērttu – to be joined. Your divine feet and my head should be joined like a hook and a loop-head. Here *sērttu* is not a request, but an order. śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 98.8 “*yāvanna śaraṇau bhrātu: pārttivavyanjanānvitau \| śirasā dārayiśyāmi  na mē śāntirbhaviśyati \|\|*” (Until I behold the divine feet of my brother śrī rāma who has all qualities of being a king, I will not have peace) – When bharata was asked “Oh son! when will your internal sorrows be eliminated?”, he replied “When perumāḷ (śrī rāma) is crowned aptly \[as the emperor\] and I am crowned aptly \[as his servitor\], my sufferings will be removed”.
- *nin semmā pāda paṟput talai sērttu* – Like those who desire to decorate their hairs (in head) with flower after washing the hair cleanly, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) too wants to be drowned in the endless flood of joy and have his head decorated with the flower (divine feet of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)).

[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) agreed and said “I will do so”. I cannot wait for your leisurely pace.

- *ollai* – You should do it while you are saying “Here, I am doing it”.

Is there any place where there was such desperation/hurry?

- *kaimmā tunbam kadinda pirānē* – Don’t you know how to rush quickly? nampiḷḷai explains part of a beautiful ślōkam from viṣṇu darmam 68. “*paramāpadamāpanna:*” (fell in great danger) – It was such a great danger that sarvēśvaran rushed in without checking his own situation. “*manasācintayat*” (thought in its mind) – even stopped crying out \[only thinking in the mind\].
- *kaimmā tunbam* – Elephant suffers to its stature – it was such suffering that even its trunk had drowned \[unable to breathe\]. [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) asks [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) “Are you in such danger?” āḻvār replies “it was one crocodile there; here, I have five crocodiles \[five senses which try to swallow me\]; it was 1000 celestial years; here, I have been in this material realm since time immemorial; it is a small pond there; here it is a great ocean named samsāram \[material realm\]; it is danger for the body there; here, it is danger for the soul; the crocodile caught the leg of the elephant; here, the senses are catching and torturing my heart. So, see the difference between there and here”.
- *pirānē* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) feels that the help of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) removing the sufferings of śrī gajēndrāḻvān is help for āḻvār himself.

[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) says “There is a reason for my help to the elephant. But, why should I help you?”,

- *ammā* – The relationship with your highness is the same for the elephant and me. āren’t you the lord?

When, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) says “Who are you?”,

- *adiyēn* – I am a śēśabhūta (servitor).

When [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) asks “Do you insist upon this simply as a duty due to our master-servant relationship?”,

- *vēṇḍuvadu* – rāga prāptam (desire to achieve). No, this is my desire too \[not just mechanical activity\].

When [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) asks “You want this and what more?”

*īdē* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says “*nin semmā pāda paṟput talai sērttu*” (Placing your divine lotus feet on my head) only is desired.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.
