## 2.9.2. Ide yan

*īdē yān unnaik koḷvadu enjñānṟum – en mai tōy sōdi maṇivaṇṇa endāy! eydā nin kaḻal yān eyda – jñānak kai tā kālak kaḻivu seyyēlē*

**Пословный перевод:**

en – for me, this taste-inducing; mai – black/dark; tōy – abundant; sōdi – having radiance; maṇi – like a precious gem; vaṇṇam – having beautiful form; endāy – Oh my lord!; unnai – you; yān – I; enjñānṟum – at all times; koḷvadu – the result of having; īdē – this only; eydā – difficult to achieve; nin – your; kaḻal – divine feet; yān – I; eyda – to attain; jñānak kai – the helping-hand of knowledge that gives clarity; tā – you give; kālak kaḻivu – delay; seyyēl – don’t do

**Перевод:**

**Oh my lord who is having abundantly blackish form resembling a radiant beautiful precious gem which induces my attachment towards you! This is the result of having you all the times. What is this? It is your divine feet which are difficult to achieve for me. You give the helping hand of knowledge that gives clarity to attain them without making any delay. jñānam (knowledge) is explained as kai (helping hand), since that is his hold.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the second pāsuram – āḻvār requests emperumān to mercifully bless him quickly to be fulfilled to say “I have attained the goal \[that was explained in previous pāsuram\]”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār requests emperumān to bless him with the knowledge that matches this relationship (between himself and emperumān).*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Second pāsuram. In the first pāsuram, he desired for the goal for his body; here, he desires for the goal for the mind. īdē yān unnaik koḷvadu enjñānṟum – en mai tōy sōdi maṇivaṇṇa endāy! eydā nin kaḻal yān eyda – jñānak kai tā kālak kaḻivu seyyēlē*

Though in the previous pāsuram [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) said “*īdē*” (only this – being connected to your lotus feet), [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) thought “Sometimes if we hear the same matter repeatedly, mind may desire for something else; so, I should confirm if āḻvār is well engaged in this goal” and asked “What do you need in addition to this?”

- *īdē* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says “this only”.

How will I know that you are engaged in this goal only?

- *yān unnaik koḷvadu* – Our nature is the proof. I, the servitor, will have only this from you, the master.

[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) says “Though my svāmitvam (lordship) and your śēśatvam (servitude) existed forever, you had missed out on the opportunity to serve; that is why I have this doubt; how many days will this firmness last?”

- *enjñānṟum* – As long as the ātmā exists (that is, forever), this will be my request.

[īśvaran](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) asks “Who trained/educated you to be firm in this goal?” [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) asks “Is there anything else? Your physical beauty only”…

- *en mai tōy …* – Oh my lord who revealed your lordship by showing the complexion which resembles a precious gem which has radiant black hue.

[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) says “Good. What shall I do for you?”

- *eydā nin kaḻal yān eyda* – You make me attain your divine feet which are difficult to attain by anyone’s self effort. I should attain it with the thought that “You blessed me that favour”.

[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) asks “Did you not get that when you were blessed “*mayarvaṟa madinalam*” (pure knowledge/devotion without any fault)”?

- *jñānak kai tā* – It is not as sufficient as you think; you have to make me realize that “I have attained it”. The favour of knowledge is like giving a helping hand to a drowning person. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says “*jñānamāna kaiyait tā*” (give me knowledge that is the helping hand). Here, we should recollect the words of [mudaliyāṇḍān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/mudhaliyandan/) to [embār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/embar/) which is “when someone falls in a well, if two persons give their hand, it will be easy on both those who are helping and the one being helped; so be it” \[A śiśya of [mudaliyāṇḍān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/mudhaliyandan/) goes to [embār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/embar/) and serves him when mudaliyāṇḍān was away. embār thinks he has not had panca samskāram (initiation) and performs the same to him without realizing [āṇḍān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/mudhaliyandan/) is already his ācārya, but later comes to know about it. When āṇḍān returns, the śiśya returns to āṇḍān and informs about the incident. At that time āṇḍān tells embār not to worry saying the aforementioned words – such was his magnanimity\].
- *jñānak kai tā* – Alternatively, when [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) asks “Is that goal not achieved only by those who have para bhakti, para jñānam and parama bhakti?”,
- *jñānak kai tā* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says “even those, you need to bestow them to me and accept me at your lotus feet”.

When [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) said “I will do so”,

- *kālak kaḻivu seyyēl* – āḻvr says “Don’t delay. My word/request has always been ‘immediately’ “.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.9.3. Seyyel tivinai

*seyyēl tīvinai enṟu aruḷ seyyum – en kaiyār cakkarak kaṇṇa pirānē ! aiyār kaṇḍam adaikkilum nin kaḻal eyyādu ētta aruḷ sey enakkē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tīvinai – sins (those which are forbidden in śāstram etc); seyyēl – ensure that I don’t do; enṟu – saying so; en – towards me; aruḷ – mercy in the form of an order; seyyum – to do; kai – with the divine hand; Ar – well fitting; cakkaram – having sudarśana chakra (divine disc); kaṇṇan – with his simplicity in the form of kriṣṇa; pirānē – oh one who favoured!; ai – mucus; Ar – filled; kaṇḍam – throat; adaikkilum – even if it becomes speechless; nin – your (you who are the eliminator of hurdles, who are simple and apt); kaḻal – divine feet; eyyādu – being tireless; ētta – to praise; enakkē – for me exclusively; aruḷ sey – mercifully you should bless

**Перевод:**

**Oh emperumān who appeared as kriṣṇa with saulabhyam (simplicity) and having well-fitting sudarśana chakra in your hand to show your mercy in the form of an order saying “don’t engage in sins which are forbidden in śāstram”! Even when my throat is filled with mucus and I become speechless, you should mercifully bless me exclusively to praise your divine feet, without getting tired.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the third pāsuram – āḻvār says to emperumān “You should bless me that I praise your divine feet even during the most difficult times in my death bed”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “You should bless me to praise you even in the most dangerous situations that could subdue the knowledge \[that was prayed for in the previous pāsuram\]”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*In the third pāsuram – āḻvār prayed for service through his body in the first pāsuram; then, he prayed for service through his mind; in this pāsuram, he is praying for service through his speech.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Third pāsuram. Here, āḻvār is praying for the result of praising through his speech. seyyēl tīvinai enṟu aruḷ seyyum – en kaiyār cakkarak kaṇṇa pirānē ! aiyār kaṇḍam adaikkilum nin kaḻal eyyādu ētta aruḷ sey enakkē*

- *seyyēl* … – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) says “You have seen my beauty of well-fitting sudarśana chakra in my hand; you have seen my bhavaytā (suitableness – as kriṣṇa being very easily approachable); is it good to engage in me or is it good to go astray by engaging in worldly pleasures \[*tīvinai* – sins\]?” and eliminated [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s attachment to worldly pleasures by showing his divine beauty and easily approachable nature; āḻvār’s attachment to worldly pleasures were not  eliminated through the teachings of śāstram etc.
- *aiyār* … – I am not asking to eliminate the sorrows; As explained in jitantē stōtram “*durgatāvapi …*” (Even when great danger occurs if my attachment towards you is not reduced, I will be grateful to you forever) – even in my death-bed, you should bless me that I praise your lotus feet without getting tired. Even when my throat is filled with mucus, you should bless me that I praise your ever-charming divine feet continuously.  “*aiyār kaṇḍam adaikkilum*” can also be explained sarcastically as “Even if that cruel boy named ‘mucus’ comes and gets hold of my throat while I am in my death-bed \[when I am too weak to defend myself\]”.

When [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) says “that \[thinking me always\] is the result of a good deed”,

- *aruḷ sey* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says – you show your compassion and mercifully vow that “Let him have it”.

[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) says “But should I not bless everyone like that?”

- *enakkē* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says – you bestow this on me only, who is standing in front of you and praying for that.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.9.4. Enakke atcey

*enakkē ātcey ekkālattum enṟu – en manakkē vandu idai vīdinṟi manni tanakkēyāga enaik koḷḷum īdē enakkē kaṇṇanai yān koḷ siṟappē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ekkālattum – always; enakkē – exclusively for me; āḷ – serve; cey – do; enṟu – mercifully saying so; en – my; manakkē – in my mind; vandu – arrived; idaivīdu – break; inṟi – without; manni – residing forever; tanakkē – (not for others, not for me, not jointly for him and me) exclusively for him; āga – to be fully dependent; enai – me; koḷḷum – acknovledgement; īdē – this only; enakkē – fitting my nature; kaṇṇanai – kriṣṇa; yān – I; koḷ – desiring; siṟappu – result

**Перевод:**

**The only result I desire from kriṣṇa is his mercifully saying “always exclusively serve me” and not stopping with that, arriving in my heart and residing there forever without any break, and acknowledging me, fitting my nature, to be fully dependent (not for others, not for me, not jointly for him and me, but) exclusively for him.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*āḻvār teaches to emperumān how he should be engaged in service.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fourth pāsuram – āḻvār says that he needs pāratantriyam (total dependence) which is the most confidential aspect of upaniśats.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See periyavāccān piḷḷai‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*In the fourth pāsuram – āḻvār is establishing “tadēka pāratantriyam” (exclusive dependence on  bhagavān) as the goal, after praying for servitude towards bhagavān through his body, mind and speech in the previous three pāsurams.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Fourth pāsuram. The goal established by āḻvār in this decad is “bhagavān should engage āḻvār exclusively for his own pleasure like garland, sandalwood paste etc \[garland, sandalwood etc have no self-interest, they only exist for the pleasure of bhagavān; āḻvār desires for similar state\]”. Here, embār explains – “sarvēśvaran engages all three types of cētanas (sentients) according to their nature; āḻvār says ‘let me also attain the same thing \[according to my nature\]’ “. muktas (liberated souls) and nityas (eternally free souls) enjoy themselves and bring joy to bhagavān;  baddas \[bound souls\] bring joy to bhagavān without themselves enjoying \[as they are suffering in material realm\]. emperumān is explained as in tiruvāimoḻi 3.10.7 “inbuṟum ivviḷaiyāttudaiyān” (one who enjoys this sport of creation, sustenance, annihilation etc in the material realm). When piḷḷai tirunaṟaiyūr araiyar asked embār “Why is āḻvār who is blessed with ‘mayarvaṟa madinalam’ (pristine knowledge/devotion) praying in this pāsuram ‘tanakkēyāga enaik kōḷḷumīdē’ (he should engage me for his exclusive pleasure) instead of letting emperumān deal with him as to his satisfaction?” embār mercifully explained “Good question; śrī māhālakśmi never separated from emperumān in the past; nor will she ever separate from him in the future; yet, even though she is staying right in his chest, she says as in tiruvāimoḻi 6.10.10 ‘agalagillēn, agalagillēn‘ (I will not leave, I will not leave) – this is because of the greatness of emperumān; similarly, the desire in the goal (of being engaged for exclusive pleasure of emperumān) makes āḻvār say these words”. āḻvār requests emperumān this (exclusive and total dependence on emperumān) which is “emmā vīttil emmā vīdu” (emmā vīdu decad is the most important decad in tiruvāimoḻi, and this pāsuram is the most important pāsuram in the decad), the great wealth for vaiṣṇavas, the most confidential principle expounded in the upaniśats, that which is prayed from emperumān and attained, that which is apt for the jīvātmā. enakkē ātcey ekkālattum enṟu – en manakkē vandu idai vīdinṟi manni tanakkēyāga enaik koḷḷum īdē enakkē kaṇṇanai yān koḷ siṟappē*

- *enakkē ātcey* … – First he should say “*ātcey*” (serve); serving eliminates svātantriyam (independence). After that he should say “*enakku ātcey*” (serve me); by saying “serve me”, \[attachment to\] worldly matters are eliminated. Then he should say “*enakk****E*** *ātcey*” (serve me exclusively); this eliminates serving the interest of both his and mine.
- *ekkālattum* – This too, as said in tiruvāimoḻi 3.3.1 “*oḻivil kālamellām udanāy manni*” (I should be with you all times). As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 15.7 “*kriyatāmiti mām vada*” (lakśmaṇa to śrī rāma – order me in what should be done), he should engage me in his service. To order me like that, he should not be staying far away from me.
- *en manakkē vandu* – you should enter my heart.
- *idai vīdinṟi manni* – you cannot be going back and forth; like an immovable object, you should stay there permanently.

What is the purpose of staying in the heart?

- *tanakkē āga enaik koḷḷum īdē* – Engage me in service like garland, sandalwood paste etc. \[When asked, are these only for the pleasure of the user?\] garland and sandalwood paste give pleasure to one who wears these and applies these respectively and when discarded, they are of no other use; when two persons enjoy in union, the joy is shared, I don’t want such share in the joy \[it should be exclusively for you only\]. Until the start of this line, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) was using the words “*nin*” (you), “*ammā*” (oh my lord!) which are all in first person. In this line, why is he using “*tanakkē*” (for **him** only), which is in third person? If āḻvār looks at the beautiful face of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) which will mesmerize him, he would be unable to firmly establish the ultimate goal \[being attracted by emperumān’s beauty and divine smile, āḻvar would start deriving pleasure already, which is against the philosophy\] – so āḻvār is looking away and stating his goal.
- *enakkē kaṇṇanai* – After explaining “for him ([emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)) exclusively”, the obvious next is to identify “for me ([āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)) only”; now, he is saying this to highlight it as his puruśārtam (goal). emperumān says “Only a cētana (sentient – who has knowledge) will have desire. If I fulfil your desire, I should also be fulfilling everyone’s desire”.
- *yān koḷ* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says “Do it for me who acquired true knowledge about the self which was given by you”.

[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) says “For you, I cannot do it always”.

- *siṟappē* – It is not required many times; just do it once. Even that, even if you shut the doors and do it to me behind the doors in seclusion without the knowledge of any one else. *siṟappu* – ēṟṟam (greatness), that is puruśārtam (goal). That you should engage me in the goal that fits my true nature. Three more explanations – *siṟappu* means mukti (liberation), sampat (wealth of kainkaryam) and nanṟi (gratitude). mukti – In this, the liberation I accept from you is placing me exclusively for your service. sampat – the wealth of kainkaryam towards you. nanṟi – my gratitude towards you.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.9.5. Sirappil vidu

*siṟappil vīdu suvarkka naragam iṟappil eyduga eydaṟka – yānum piṟappil pal piṟavip perumānai maṟapponṟu inṟi enṟum magiḻvēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

iṟappil – after leaving this body; siṟappil – having goodness (of bliss); vīdu – mōkśam (liberation); suvarkkam – svarga – heaven (which is fictitious joy or a misconceived joy); naragam – naraka – hell (which is filled with sorrow); eyduga – reach there (when considering the body to be different from the soul); eydaṟka – does not reach and get finished (when considering the body to be the same as the soul); piṟappu – cause for birth; il – when not there; pal – in many forms; piṟavi – one who is born; perumānai – sarvēsvaran; onṟu – any (of these qualities which win over his devotees and make them fully depend on him); maṟappu inṟi – not forgetting; enṟum – always; magiḻvēn – let me have the bliss (caused by such continuous remembrance)

**Перевод:**

**After leaving this body, let me reach (when considering the body to be different from the soul) mōkśam (spiritual realm) which is having the goodness (of bliss) or heaven (which is fictitious joy or a misconceived joy) or naraka – hell (which is filled with sorrow), or let me not go anywhere and get finished (when considering the body to be the same as the soul) here itself. But let me always have the bliss (caused by continuous remembrance) of not forgetting sarvēsvaran‘s any of these qualities (which win over his devotees and make them fully depend on him) of the various forms in which he is born though he has no reason to take birth \[one is assuming a particular birth due to his or her karma – since bhagavān is not bound by any karma, he is not forced into any birth – but he assumes different births due to his own desire\]. Both previous pāsuram and this pāsuram are āḻvār‘s monologue (instead of speaking face to face with perumāḷ).**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fifth pāsuram – āḻvār says “Let the soul be the same as body; ōr let the one who is different from body be the soul; it is irrelevant; my goal is to enjoy all the various incarnations which were taken by bhagavān for his devotees’ sake”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “I want the happiness of not forgetting this īśvaran who reveals this total dependence to me”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*In the fifth pāsuram – when asked “What is your true nature? The goal should match your nature”, āḻvār replies “It does not matter who I am; what matters is that, whoever I am, I should exist for his sake only”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Fifth pāsuram. āḻvār first desired for service through mind, speech and body and said “You should eliminate everything that is for “me” and simply engage my these three faculties (mind, speech and body) for your pleasure alone”; emperumān thinks “this kind of dealings cannot be had with samsāris (worldly people); so let us investigate what āḻvār thinks of himself while praying for this” and asked “Who are you desiring this favour from me?” āḻvār replied “Some say ‘dēham (body) is the same as ātmā (soul)’; others say ‘since without indriyams (senses), the body cannot do anything, the senses are the soul’; few others say ‘even those senses cannot grasp and understand the objects when not supported by manas (mind), so mind is the soul’; few others say ‘even the mind works only with the support of prāṇas (vital airs – prāṇa, apāna etc), so vital air is the soul’; few others say even if all are present, unless adyavasāyam (firm knowledge) is there, there is no use; so, buddi (intellect) is the soul’; finally, some say ‘some thing is beyond all of these, having jñānam as an attribute and being made of jñānam – this is ātmā (soul)'” āḻvār says “there is no specific binding for me in any of these; whoever I am, I want to be an object which exists purely for your sake”. This is like āḷavandār saying in stōtra ratnam 52 “vapurādisu yōpi kōpi vā …” (Let me be anything starting with body). siṟappil vīdu suvarkka naragam iṟappil eyduga eydaṟka – yānum piṟappil pal piṟavip perumānai maṟapponṟu inṟi enṟum magiḻvēnē*

- *siṟappil vīdu …* – mōkśam (liberation) which is explained as the unlimited bliss acquired by nitya samsāri (eternally bound soul in this world) which matches that of nityasūris (eternally free souls), svargam which has limited bliss, naraka which has pure suffering only – let me achieve any of these at the time of my death or not achieve. This means – let the [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) (soul) be different from dēham (body) and thus progress to a different place after death or let the ātmā and dēham be the same and be finished at the time of death. It is irrelevant (for [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)). Only the ātmā, which is different from the body, goes on to acquire a new body and enjoys in svargam etc; the body is obviously burnt down to ashes after death as we see for ourselves.
- *yānum* – Here [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says “me too, who is unqualified for any of these”. Also explained as āḻvār saying “whoever I am, without having to analyse my nature”.
- *piṟappu il pal piṟavip perumānai* – sarvādika (one who is greater than all), though he has no karma which binds him to a particular birth, takes birth in those forms which are even looked down upon by those bound in this material realm. yajur vēdam “*ajāyamānō bahudā vijāyatē*” (the unborn (one who has no necessity to take birth due to karma), assumes many births).
- *maṟappu onṟu inṟi* – not forgetting any of those incarnations and the divine activities of those incarnations.
- *maṟappu onṟu inṟi* – we can forget anything related to us; but we cannot forget anything related to [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/).
- *enṟum magiḻvēnē* – magiḻcci (joy) and anubhavam (experience) are synonyms; [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says, “I will experience him”. Thus, through this pāsuram, āḻvār reveals his own nature. Through “*perumān*” (lord), he reveals his *śēśatvam* (subservience); through “*maṟapponṟinṟi*” (without forgetting anything), he reveals *jñātrutvam* (being a sentient); through “*enṟum*” (always), he reveals *nityatvam* (eternal nature); through “*magiḻvu*” (joy), he reveals *bhōktrutvam* (being the enjoyer).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.9.6. Magilkol deyvam

*magiḻ koḷ deyvam ulōgam alōgam magiḻ koḷ sōdi malarnda ammānē ! magiḻ koḷ sindai sol seygai koṇḍu – enṟum magiḻvuṟṟu unnai vaṇanga vārāyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

magiḻ koḷ – abundance of joy; deyvam – dēvatās (celestial beings); ulōgam – humans who have shining knowledge; alōgam – animals and plants which lack shining of knowledge; magiḻ – joy (acquired through lustre); koḷ – having; sōdi – being radiant objects; malarnda – one who is expanded (as said in taittiriya upaniśad “bahu syām” (let me become many)); ammānē – Oh one who is the lord!; magiḻ koḷ – with love (due to being friendly with you); sindai – mind/thoughts; sol – speech; seygai – action; koṇḍu – having; enṟum – always; magiḻvuṟṟu – being blissful without any worries; unnai – you (who created such aspects for all my three faculties of mind, speech, body); vaṇanga – to experience; vārāy – mercifully come here

**Перевод:**

**Oh lord who expanded (as said in taittiriya upaniśad “bahu syām” (let me become many)) as dēvatās (celestial beings) who have abundance of joy, humans who have shining knowledge, animals and plants which lack shining of knowledge and other radiant objects which have joy (that is acquired through lustre)! You made me blissful without any worries to have mind, speech and action which are attached to you and you should mercifully come here to let me experience you. ulōgam and alōgam also indicate cētana (sentient) and acētana (insentient) entities \[ulōgam – cit, alōgam – acit\].**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*āḻvār says to emperumān “Just like you have created these dēvas et al (celestial beings, humans, animals, plants etc) to have their own qualities, you should make me enjoy with pleasing words and mind, speech and body which are attached to you”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār desires for external experience based on this internal experience.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. Also explained as – āḻvār asking  emperumān “Having created dēvas et al, you should help me enjoy this experience of enjoying you (which is the purpose of creation) externally instead of stopping with internal experience”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

[periyavāccān piḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/periyavachchan-pillai/) beautifully connects “*magiḻ koḷ sindai sol seygai*“.

- *magiḻ koḷ sindai* – my heart should be filled with love when I hear about you.
- *sol* – the overflowing words reflecting such love
- seygai – the action that follows those loving words

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Sixth pāsuram. āḻvār says to emperumān “Just like you have created dēvas et al, you should make me enjoy you”. Also explained as āḻvār saying “Just like you have established a particular aspect in dēva et al, you should establish the aspect of enjoying you in me”. magiḻ koḷ deyvam ulōgam alōgam magiḻ koḷ sōdi malarnda ammānē ! magiḻ koḷ sindai sol seygai koṇḍu – enṟum magiḻvuṟṟu unnai vaṇanga vārāyē*

- *magiḻ koḷ deyvam* – celestial beings (residing in heaven etc) who have better bhōjña (joy), bhōgōprakaraṇa (tools for enjoyment) and bhōga stānam (abodes of enjoyment) in comparison with those of humans.
- *ulōgam* – As said in “*lōkyata iti lōka:*” (because it is seen, it is called lōka), acit (insentient matter), which is perceivable through our five senses (eyes, ears, nose, tongue, skin).
- *alōgam* – alōka – cit (sentient – soul), that which cannot be perceived by our senses and can only be understood through śāstram.
- *magiḻ koḷ sōdi* – Those radiant objects. It can be explained as candra (moon), sūrya (sun). Oh [sarvēśvara](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) who created these!
- *malarnda* – Since it is his own expansion as said in taittiriya upaniśad “*bahu syām*“, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says “*malarnda*” (blossomed). [brahmam (bhagavān)](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) with [cit (sentients)](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) and [acit (insentient)](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/09/thathva-thrayam-achith-what-is-matter/) is both cause and effect \[In causal state (before creation), brahmam has cit and acit in subtle state and after creation, cit and acit become manifested in gross state\].

When asked by [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) “Whatever you have said is done by me! What should I do now for you?”,

- *magiḻ koḷ* … – you should make my heart become joyful by experiencing you; you should make the same to my speech too; my actions should become loving service to you; I too should exclusively experience you and feel blissful; you should arrive here for me to experience you always.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.9.7. Varay

*vārāy un tiruppāda malark kīḻ pērādē yān vandadaiyum padi tārādāy! unnai ennuḷ vaippil enṟum ārādāy enakku enṟum ekkālē*

**Пословный перевод:**

unnai – you (who are to be enjoyed always); en uḷ – in my heart; enṟum – eternally; vaippil – while placing; enakku ārādāy – having not satisfied me; enṟum – all days; ekkāl – all times; un – (the apt) your; tiru – laudable; malar – enjoyable; pādam – in the lotus feet; kīḻ – being fully dependent; pērādē – being inseparable; yān – I; vandu – come; adaiyum padi – to reach; tārādāy – Oh one who is not giving opportunity!; un tiruppāda malark kīḻ pērādē yān vandu adaiyum padi – to make me reach as explained; vārāy – you come

**Перевод:**

**After my not feeling satisfied while placing (the apt)  you in my heart eternally, oh one who is not giving opportunity for me to reach your laudable enjoyable lotus feet and be fully dependent and inseparable for all days and at all times!  You come to me to make me reach you as explained.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the seventh pāsuram – āḻvār tells emperumān out of overflowing affection “you should come here to engage me in your service at all times”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār is sorrowfully desiring for external experience \[with bhagavān\] after not being fulfilled with the internal experience.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*In the seventh pāsuram – āḻvār, feeling sad for not seeing emperumān‘s arrival even after calling out for him (“vārāy“), again out of affection says “You come so that I can reach you”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. vārāy un tiruppāda malark kīḻ pērādē yān vandadaiyum padi tārādāy! unnai ennuḷ vaippil enṟum ārādāy enakku enṟum ekkālē*

- *vārāy … tārādāy!* – Oh one who is not blessing me the opportunity to reach your unlimitedly enjoyable exalted feet and stay there without ever returning \[to previous state\]! Due to feeling upset for the non-arrival of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying “*tārādāy*” (one who is not giving the opportunity) as emperumān’s identity. āḻvār is establishing his desire (that is, reaching emperumān’s lotus feet) using a round-about way. If he is not planning to give that opportunity, at least he can remove the desire from my heart. My heart is thinking about this as it happens during *periya tirunāḷ* \[adyayana utsavam or panguni utsavam – where there used to be 24 hour activities at śrīrangam; āḻvār’s heart is also longing for this throughout the day without any break\].
- *unnai ennuḷ vaippil enṟum ārādāy* – Oh [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)! you are so enjoyable and I am unable to bear the thought of not having external experience with you; how can I be satisfied just with internal experience with you being in my heart?
- *enakku enṟum ekkālē* – For me on all days and in all situations, “*vārāy*” – please come.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.9.8. Ekkalattu endaiyay

*ekkālattu endaiyāy ennuḷ mannil – maṟṟu ekkālattilum yādonṟum vēṇḍēn mikkār vēda vimalar viḻungum – en akkārak kaniyē ! unnai yānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

mikkār – being greatly exalted; vēda vimalar – the purest leaders of vaidika path; viḻungum – (due to their great attachment) consume and enjoy him; en – for me; akkāram – soaked in sugar; kaniyē – one who is filled with sweetness like a fruit; ekkālattu – even a fleeting moment; endaiyāy – visibly manifesting your lordship over me; en uḷ – in my heart; mannil – if residing firmly; maṟṟu – except this; ekkālattilum – at all times; yādu – anything; onṟum – other; unnai – you; yān – I; vēṇḍēn – won’t ask

**Перевод:**

**Oh one who is filled with sweetness like a fruit soaked in sugar for me, in a way similar to the experience of the purest exalted leaders of vaidika path who consume and enjoy you! If you reside firmly in my heart and visibly manifest your lordship over me even for a fleeting moment, I will never ask your for anything other than that.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the eighth pāsuram – āḻvār mercifully says out of his great thirst in serving emperumān “even if it is a fleeting moment, if you spend with me as my master, I won’t even ask that (small moment of togetherness) afterwards”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār mercifully reveals his great affection by saying “if I get to be with you even for a fleeting moment, I won’t need anything else”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. ekkālattu endaiyāy ennuḷ mannil – maṟṟu ekkālattilum yādonṟum vēṇḍēn mikkār vēda vimalar viḻungum – en akkārak kaniyē ! unnai yānē*

[āḷavandār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/alavandhar/) explains this as follows:

- *ekkālam* … – Even if it is for a very very fleeting moment which cannot even be explained by me in the future, if you arrive in my heart with your proper stature as the lord, at all times – i.e., all times other than this time when you arrive, I won’t ask for anything; I won’t even ask for the same thing (very very fleeting moment of togetherness) in the future. This is just like someone who is suffering from fever would crave for a drop of water.

When asked “Is there anything that can just be enjoyed for a fleeting moment but can still give full satisfaction?”

- *mikkār …* – *mikkār* – nityasūris who are immersed in enjoying [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/), who are explained as purest in vēdam as said in yajur vēdam accitram “*yatrarśaya: pratamajā yē purāṇā:*” (those nityasūris – the residents of paramapadam, ones who can visualise everything, ones who have no beginning and ones who have most enjoyable fresh forms though they are ancient). Oh [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is enjoyed by such nityasūris, who is manifesting your sugar like and fruit like abundance of sweetness! Oh one who is like the well-ripened fruit in the tree of sugar! akkārak kani (sweet fruit) implies that he is the enjoyable object for them in all manners.
- *unnai yānē* – I, who knovsyour nature, would never ask for anything in the future ever if you, who have unsurpassed sweetness, arrive and stay in my heart once, even for a small moment.

[emperumānār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/emperumanar/) mercifully heard this \[from [tirumālai āṇḍān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/thirumalai-andan/)\] and said “This explanation is nice; but, it does not exactly match [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s nature; whether he gets or not, he would not ask for anything small (or momentary); it should be explained like this” \[he re-arranges the words slightly – instead of taking it as “*maṟṟu ekkālattilum yādu onṟum vēṇḍēn*“, he takes it as “*ekkālattilum maṟṟu yādu onṟum vēṇḍēn*“.

- *ekkālattu* … – You who are my lord at all times, if you arrive in my heart accepting me as a servitor,
- *ekkālattilum* – at all times
- *maṟṟu yādu onṟum vēṇḍēn* – I will not ask for anything other than this \[you being in my heart in the proper manner\].

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.9.9. Yane ennai

*yānē ennai aṟiyagilādē yānē enṟanadē enṟirundēn yānē nī en udaimaiyum nīyē vānē ēttum em vānavar ēṟē*

**Пословный перевод:**

yānē – I myself; ennai – in the matters relating to me; aṟiyagilādē – due to not having true knowledge; yānē – considering myself as independent; en tanadē – considering everything but myself as my belongings; enṟu – engaged in ahankāram (considering myself as independent) and mamakāram (considering the belongings of bhagavān as mine); irundēn – merely existed (without manifesting ātmā‘s eternal nature); vānē – all of paramapadam (where true knowledge is practiced without this ignorance); ēttum – praising (your relationship with them); avvānavar – those residents of the paramapadam; ēṟē – Oh one who resides there manifesting the pride of lordship!; yān – I; nīyē – being prakāra (attribute) of you which is inseparable and thus can be said as “You”; en udaimaiyum – those which are my belongings; nīyē – (in the same manner, being attributes) are such that they can be said as “You”

**Перевод:**

**Due to my not having true knowledge in the matters relating to me, I considered myself as independent and considered everything but myself as my belongings, engaged in ahankāram (considering myself as independent) and mamakāram (considering the belongings of bhagavān as mine) and merely existed (without manifesting ātmā‘s eternal nature); Oh one who resides in paramapadam manifesting the pride of lordship, being praised in all of paramapadam (where true knowledge is practiced without this ignorance) by those residents of the paramapadam praising (your relationship with them)! Once this true knowledge is understood, I realise that “I” can be said as “You”, due to my being prakāra (attribute) of you which is inseparable and in the same manner being your attributes, my belongings can also be called as “You”.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the ninth pāsuram  – āḻvār feels sorry for having lost this most enjoyable servitude since time immemorial.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “though the relationship \[between jīvātmā and paramātmā\] is inseparable, due to ignorance that has no beginning, being polluted by ahankāram and mamakāram, I have lost it”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*In the ninth pāsuram – āḻvār says “I have lost this sambandam and the joy (explained in previous pāsuram) since time immemorial”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Ninth pāsuram. āḻvār meditated upon the manner in which nityasūris enjoy emperumān eternally saying “mikkār vēdavimalar viḻungum“; āḻvār then thinks about his own nature (of the ātmā) which matches the śēśatvam (servitude) of the nityasūris and says “\[Yet\] I have been unworthy \[having lost that opportunity to serve\]”. yānē ennai aṟiyagilādē yānē enṟanadē enṟirundēn yānē nī en udaimaiyum nīyē vānē ēttum em vānavar ēṟē*

- *yānē* – My loss is not due to his deeds \[This is explaining the avadāraṇārtam “E” in end of yānē which says I alone am the cause\]; while he is trying to come in front of me and help me, I myself caused my own destruction.
- *ennai aṟiyagilādē* – Just like a prince who gets lost in the forest, found by a hunter and being raised by him, he will eventually come to think that he too is a hunter, I who do not realise that I am a prakārabhūta (an attribute, a form) of sarvēśvaran.
- *yānē en tanadē enṟu irundēn* – Instead of thinking “[bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) and his belongings”, I misunderstood “I and my belongings”.
- *irundēn* – If this goes on for a long time, some day, one should repent for such situation; even that did not occur – I lived as if I am complete and without any worries. Just as it is said in periya tiruvantādi 82 “*tīvinaiyēn vāḷā irundu oḻindēn*” (I, who am this sinner, stayed without acting upon those sins). Though I was fit to do everything as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 31.25 “*aham sarvam kariśyāmi*” (Let me serve you in all ways), I stayed as if I had nothing to do. It sounds like [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying “*oḻindēn*” (I am finished). While it is said that “even a moment of separation from [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is unbearable”, āḻvār says that he has lost this all along (until now) since time immemorial.

When asked “Is this not the way that this should be understood?”, he says

- *yānē nī* – muktātmās would say as in bruhadāraṇyaka upaniśad “*aham manurabhavam sūryaśca*” (vāma dēva riśi who worships brahmam says “I am manu, I am sūrya”); those who have pristine knowledge in this samsāram would say as in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 1.19.85 “*mattas sarvamaham sarvam*” (prahlāda says “everything came out of me, I am everything”; What makes them say these? “*aham brahmāsmi*” – Like one says “I am the prince (son of the king)”, one’s relationship with brahmam makes one say “I am brahmam”. When it is said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam “*sa vāsudēva:*” (that object is [vāsudēva](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)), isn’t it explained as a śarīram (body) of [vāsudēva](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)?
- *en udaimaiyum nīyē* – Just as it is said in mahābhāratam udyōga parvam by vidura to dritarāśtra “*yasyaitē taddanam*” (for those who own him, those persons are that wealth for him).

Where did we observe this?

- *vānē ēttum* – nityasūris enjoy you this way. As in “*manjā krōśanti*” (bed is making noise) which means the persons on the bed are making noise, here *vān* (paramapadam) indicates the residents of the paramapadam.
- *em vānavar ēṟē* – This is the place where the nityasūris and muktātmās serve him matching their serving nature and he accepts their service matching his lordship over them. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says “*em*” to indicate that he (baddātmā – bound soul) is as qualified as they are (nitasūris – ever free soul), yet, he lost and became worthless.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.9.10. Erel elum

*ēṟēl ēḻum venṟu ēr koḷ ilangaiyai nīṟē seyda nedum sudarc cōdi! tēṟēl ennai un ponnadic cērttu ollai vēṟē pōga enjñānṟum vidalē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ēl – Opposed; ēṟu – bull; ēḻum – seven; venṟu – won; ēr – beautiful; koḷ – having; ilangaiyai – lankā; nīṟē seyda – due to burning into ashes; nedum – great; sudar – one who is having splendour; sōdi – one who is having radiant form; ennai – me; tēṟēl – not having faith (that I know what is good for me); un – your; pon – radiant; adi – in divine feet; ollai – immediately; sērttu – accept; vēṟē pōga – going astray (thinking about worldly pleasures); enjñānṟum – at all times; vidal – don’t leave me

**Перевод:**

**Oh emperumān who won over the seven bulls which opposed him, who burnt the beautiful lankā into ashes and who is the one with the radiant form that acquired great splendour by these actions! You should accept me at all times in your radiant divine feet, without letting me to go astray (thinking about worldly pleasures) immediately, knowing well that that I don’t know what is good for me.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the tenth pāsuram – āḻvār says to emperumān “Instead of giving up on me thinking ‘let him try himself and achieve his goal’, you should remove the obstacles and quickly accept me at your divine feet”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says to emperumān “Accept me and ensure that our relationship is not broken”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Tenth pāsuram. When emperumān asked āḻvār “After making you repent saying ‘yānē endandē enṟu irundēn‘, is there anything more for me to do? Why are you worrying like this?” āḻvār says “It is for this \[which is to be explained in this pāsuram\]” ēṟēl ēḻum venṟu ēr koḷ ilangaiyai nīṟē seyda nedum sudarc cōdi! tēṟēl ennai un ponnadic cērttu ollai vēṟē pōga enjñānṟum vidalē*

- *ēṟu ēl ēḻum venṟu* – Winning over the seven bulls \[“*ēl*” is just a slang and no specific meaning\]. Winning over the bulls which are the obstacles to unite with nappinnaip pirātti.
- *ēr koḷ ilangaiyai* – lankā which has beauty and protection \[ēr – beauty, protection\]. As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 49.17 “*ahō vīryamahō dairyam*” (What bravery! What valour!) – this is the lankā which was respected by tiruvadi (hanumān) \[hanumān is a brahmacāri and a great personality who was totally detached from worldly pleasures – lankā was so beautiful/organised that even he himself started admiring it for a moment\]. nampiḷḷai beautifully explains the situation in lankā through śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 9.12 ślōkam. *babhūva buddistu harīśvarasya* (hanumān started thinking) – On seeing the setup of rāvaṇa and his wives, since he is also a leader of a group, he started thinking like this. *yadīdruśī rāgava darmapatnī* (if sītā were like this) – If only this fellow (rāvaṇa) had allowed [perumāḷ (śrī rāma)](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) and [pirātti (sītā)](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/) to be like how he is enjoying with his wives, this whole lankā would not get destroyed. *imā yatā rākśasarāja bhāryāssujātamasyēti hi sādubuddē:* (is it now good for rāvaṇa (if sītā were like) these wives of rāvaṇa) – For hanumān who looks after the well-being of enemies too.
- *nīṟē seyda* – burnt into ashes as sītā pirātti mercifully said.
- *nedum sudarc cōdi* – It is the divine victorious form of śrī rāma who annihilated rāvaṇa along with entourage. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says that [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) should remove his obstacles just as he removed them as śrī rāma.
- *tēṟēl ennai* – In case of nappinnaip pirātti, it is enough to eliminate the obstacles; in the case of the divine daughter of king janaka, it is enough to kill rāvaṇa who separated her; you don’t specifically strive to make them for you; because they are already your consorts; but in my case, you cannot eliminate the obstacles and stop with that. Alternative explanation – when it is read as “*tēṟēn*” – it means “*teḷiyēn*” (I don’t have full faith in you), “*dariyēn*” (I cannot bear this situation).

When asked “What should I do now?” [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says,

- *un ponnadic cērttu ollai* – He concludes with the principle he highlighted in [tiruvāimoḻi 2.9.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/06/thiruvaimozhi-2-9-1-emma-vittu/) “*nin semmā pāda paṟput talai sērttu*” (place my head on your reddish great lotus feet).
- *un ponnadi* – your divine feet are capable of giving knowledge even to stone \[śrī rāma relieving ahalyā from stone form, which she acquired due to a curse, by touching that \].
- *sērttu* – mercifully accept.
- *ollai* – Right now when I am agreeing to do so, please accept me and make me like the divine lines in your feet.
- vidal – That is not sufficient. You should not think that “I have bestowed all honours on [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/). What more is needed?” Even if you bestow me all honours, I will still cause all diśonours for myself; so you should never leave me to fend for myself.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.9.11. Vidalil cakkarattu

*vidalil cakkarattu aṇṇalai mēval vidalil vaṇ kurugūrc catakōpan sol kedalil āyirattuḷ ivai pattum kedalil vīdu seyyum kiḷarvārkkē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vidal – putting away; il – not; cakkarattu – having divine chakra (disc); aṇṇal – master/lord; mēval – approached; vidalil – one who cannot bear leaving; vaṇ – most magnanimous; kurugūrc catakōpan – nammāḻvār; sol – mercifully said; kedal – disaster; il – that which will not occur; āyirattuḷ – among the thousand pāsurams; ivai pattum – these 10 pāsurams; kiḷarvārkku – for those who recite with desire; kedalil – not having disasters such as avidyā etc; vīdu – blissful mōkśam; seyyum – will facilitate

**Перевод:**

**The most magnanimous nammāḻvār who cannot bear leaving emperumān, approached his lord/master emperumān who never puts away his divine chakra; these ten pāsurams among the thousand pāsurams sung \[by such āzvār\], ensure that those who recite them with desire will not be affected by any disaster; the pāsurams will themselves lead those persons to blissful mōkśam where there are no disasters such as avidyā etc.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the end, āḻvār says “those who have faith in this decad will achieve the goal explained in it”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “mōkśam (liberation) is the result of this decad”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. vidalil cakkarattu aṇṇalai mēval vidalil vaṇ kurugūrc catakōpan sol kedalil āyirattuḷ ivai pattum kedalil vīdu seyyum kiḷarvārkkē*

[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) showed his divine chakra saying “Why are you doubting unnecessarily that I will leave you? See I never leave anyone”,

- *vidalil cakkarattu aṇṇalai* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) praised [sarvēśvaran](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) who never puts away his divine chakra.
- *mēval vidalil …* – The most magnanimous [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) who approached him due to his nature (of never putting his chakra away), who cannot handle the separation from [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/).  mercifully sang these pāsurams. Here, *vaṇmai* (magnanimity) is the aspect of revealing his experience in the form of these pāsurams to help others.
- *kedalil āyiram* – These pāsurams which are giving good instructions to avert the disaster for the [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) (self).
- *avaṟṟil ippattum* *kiḷarvārkku kedalil vīdu seyyum* – for those who are faithful on these pāsurams instead of being “I won’t give up if I get it, but I won’t try for it hard if I don’t get it”, these pāsurams will facilitate the result which is natural for the self, that has no evil aspects, as prayed in “*tanakkēyāga vēṇum*” (should exist without any ahankāram and mamakāram for the pleasure of [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) exclusively) by [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) .

Finally, nampiḷḷai summarizes the contents of this decad briefly.

- In the first pāsuram, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) prayed for service to [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) through his body/action.
- In the second pāsuram, he prayed for service to emperumān through his mind.
- In the third pāsuram, he prayed for service to emperumān through his speech/words.
- In the fourth pāsuram, he established the goal which fits his true nature.
- In the fifth pāsuram, when emperumān asked “who are you asking for this result as”, he replied “whoever I may be, you should bless me that I experience you and become blissful”.
- In the sixth pāsuram, he asked emperumān to bless him to experience him with all three faculties (body, mind, speech) with love.
- In the seventh pāsuram, he became upset since [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) did not bless him like that immediately.
- In the eighth pāsuram, he said “if you unite with me matching my nature even for a moment, I won’t ask for that ever”.
- In the ninth pāsuram,  he said “though I am qualified \[as a soul\] to enjoy you, I have caused disaster to myself in not achieving that”.
- In the tenth pāsuram, he said “Don’t ever let me fend for myself saying ‘I have given him sufficient special knowledge’”
- In the end, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) explains the result for those who learn this decad and completes the same.

## 2.10 Kilaroli ilamai

## 2.10.1. Kilaroli ilamai

*kiḷaroḷi iḷamai keduvadan munnam vaḷaroḷi māyōn maruviya kōyil vaḷariḷam poḻil sūḻ mālirunjōlai taḷarvilarāgil sārvadu sadirē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kiḷar – rising; oḷi – qualified for jñānam (knowledge) and aujvalyam (radiance); iḷamai – (beginning of) youth; keduvadan munnam – before going astray (in worldly matters); vaḷar – increasing (after descending here for his devotees); oḷi – radiance of auspicious qualities (such as simplicity etc); māyōn – sarvēśvaran who has amazing abilities; maruviya – staying firmly; kōyil – being the divine abode; vaḷar – though growing; iḷam – yet youthful; poḻil – gardens; sūḻ – surrounded by; mālirunjōlai – tirumalai which is being called “mālirunjōlai” due to that (being surrounded by gardens); taḷarvu – sorrow (in the form of relationship with ulterior motives); ilarāgi – being free from; sārvadē – to reach only that, is; sadir – best

**Перевод:**

**tirumalai which is known as tirumālirunjōlai due to being surrounded by gardens which are growing yet youthful, is the divine abode of increasingly radiant sarvēśvaran who has amazing abilities (his radiance increasing after descending here for his devotees) and who is staying here firmly; being in the (beginning of) one’s youth, which is qualified for rising knowledge and radiance and being free from sorrow, it is best to reach such tirumalai.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the first pāsuram – āḻvār says “To attain tirumalai (the divine hill of tirumālirunjōlai) is the unsurpassed goal”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*In the first pāsuram – āḻvār says “The goal is tirumalai which is dear to sarvēśvaran who has unsurpassed radiance”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. kiḷaroḷi iḷamai keduvadan munnam vaḷaroḷi māyōn maruviya kōyil vaḷariḷam poḻil sūḻ mālirunjōlai taḷarvilarāgil sārvadu sadirē*

- *kiḷaroḷi iḷamai* … – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) said “take shelter of tirumalai”; worldly people said “yes” and remained indifferent; seeing that, āḻvār asked “What makes you stay relaxed? Have you not heard about śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 5.5 “*vayōsyā hyativartatē*” (sītā’s age is passing by without being enjoyed \[by me (śrī rāma)\])? You are being relaxed only to waste the days which pass by; can you regain the days which were lost?
- *kiḷaroḷi iḷamai* – when the mind becomes faithful \[in matters related to [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)\], before that faith disappears and becomes attached to worldly matters. Second explanation – a person may become faithful in something at one time; he may become unfaithful in the same thing after some time; so – before that attachment fades away. Third explanation – Though people may understand tirumalai as the goal, they may not have the physical ability (in old age) to pursue; so – when their body and senses are in tact and before they become old. This is explained by prahlādāḻvān in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 17.74 and 17.75. *bālyē krīdanakāsaktā: …* – in their childhood, they are attached to playing sports etc and in their youth they are attached to worldly pleasures. *tasmādbālyē vivēkātmā yatēta* – thus, one should pursue \[spiritual matters\] in childhood with intelligence.
- *vaḷaroḷi* – The divine abode of tirumalai is such that it will bring in vikāra (changes) in [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) who has no growth/decay naturally \[he is popularly glorified in śrīviṣṇu saharsnāmam as “*avikārāya…*“\]. [sarvēśvaran](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) who has amazing abilities, having growing radiance, resides eternally in tirumālirunjōlai unlike his vibhava incarnations, where he returns to his divine abode of parampadam after some time in the material realm.
- *vaḷar iḷam poḻil sūḻ mālirunjōlai* – Those who serve are with rising youthfulness; one who accepts the service is with rising radiance and amazing abilities; the divine abode where they serve is surrounded by well-grown and fresh gardens; thus, those who serve, one who accepts the service and the divine abode are all matching in qualities; though they grow, the youthfulness is still maintained.
- *taḷarvilarāgil* – “*yanmuhūrtam kśaṇam vāpi vāsudēvō na cintyatē …*” (even if one does not think about vāsudēva for a moment, that is great loss, great evil etc). [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) feels that if one does not approach tirumalai – that is disaster in all respects. Also explained as – after having acquired the knowledge of “tirumalai being the goal”, being relieved from the sorrow of not reaching tirumalai.
- *sārvadu sadirē* – for the [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/), reaching tirumalai is the best option; everything else is foolishness. Your thought of “instead of pursuing those \[worldly\] pleasures which are perceivable by the senses, you \[spiritualists\] are pursuing something that is not perceivable by the senses” is foolishness; this \[attaining tirumalai\] is the most intelligent goal.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.10.2. Sadirila madavar

*sadiriḷa madavār tāḻcciyai madiyādu adirkural sangattu aḻagar tam kōyil madi tavaḻ kudumi mālirunjōlai padi adu ētti eḻuvadu payanē*

**Пословный перевод:**

sadir – intelligent (in providing their body based on wealth and their own self-defects); iḷam – mesmerising through their youth; madavār – damsels; tāḻcciyai – the words and acts which reveal their fallen nature; madiyādē – not being attached to; adir kural – blowing (due to the joy acquired from the togetherness); sangattu – one who has unsurpassed beauty due to having śrī pāncajanyam (Sanka – divine conch); aḻagar – for aḻagar; tam kōyil – being the divine/special abode; madi – chandra (moon); tavaḻ – tall, being touched by; kudumi – having many peaks; mālirunjōlai – in tirumālirunjōlai; padi – divine abode; adu – well known; ētti – praise; eḻuvadē – to rise; payan – is the goal

**Перевод:**

**One should not be attached to the words and actions (which reveal their fallen nature) of intelligent (in providing their body to acquire wealth and based on their own self-defects) and youthful damsels who mesmerise others; instead one’s goal should be to praise the well-known place of tirumālirunjōlai and rise; this tirumālirunjōlai is the divine mountainous abode of aḻagar emperumān, having many tall peaks which are touched by the moon; aḻagar emperumān has unsurpassed beauty due to having śrī pāncajanyam (Sanka – divine conch) that is blowing (due to the joy acquired from the togetherness). This pāsuram is spoken by āḻvār towards his mind/heart.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the second pāsuram – āḻvār says “More than the tirumalai (divine hill), enjoying the divya dēśam that is attached to it (tirumālirunjōlai) is the ultimate goal”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. Alternatively, this can be taken as āḻvār speaking about tirumalai itself. sadiriḷa madavār tāḻcciyai madiyādu adirkural sangattu aḻagar tam kōyil madi tavaḻ kudumi mālirunjōlai padi adu ētti eḻuvadu payanē*

- *sadiriḷa madavār tāḻcciyai madiyādu* – Give up your lowly acts towards intelligent youthful damsels; alternative explanation – not being attached to the intelligent youthful damsels who have lowly activitie. If one considers these aspects, there are certain results; in the after-life, one will go to hell; in the current life, this is looked-down by learned persons. These worldly pleasures are unlike the bhagavān’s aspects which are fully existing for the pleasure of his devotees and are most enjoyable as explained in jitantē stōtram “… *bhaktānām*” (His names, forms etc exist for his devotees). These damsels are very intelligent to know how to capture others and keep them trapped. They would even pretend that they would die in separation. They capture others by showing their intelligence and youthful charm. Previously [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) said “*kiḷaroḷi iḷamai*” (rising youth) – these are like crocodiles which will capture the young men of this particular age.
- *adir kural …* – Due to being in constant touch with the divine hands of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), pāncajanyam, the divine conch is always making joyful sounds. Due to the togetherness, he (emperumān) too is named as sangattaḻagar (sangam means togetherness and conch in tamiḻ). emperumān considers in his divine heart that tirumālirunjōlai is an ideal place to stay and takes care of his devotees. Thus he considers this divine abode as “mine”.
- *madi tavaḻ kudumi* – tirumalai which has peaks which are being touched by the floating moon like pregnant women would climb a hill (slowly and elegantly). padi (abode) can be explained as mālirunjōlai itself or the divine abode **in** mālirunjōlai.
- *padi adu ētti eḻuvadu payanē* – Engaging in actions which are fitting to the nature of the ātmā and being uplifted is the goal; others are non-goals. payan – prayōjanam (goal) – prāpyam (goal to be reached).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.10.3. Payanalla seydu

*payan alla seydu payanillai nenjē puyal maḻai vaṇṇar purinduṟai kōyil mayal migu poḻil sūḻ mālirunjōlai ayal malaiadaivadu adu karumamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

nenjē – Oh my heart!; payanalla – useless actions; seydu – performing; payan – use; illai – no; puyal – drizzles and drops; maḻai – like a black cloud; vaṇṇar – one who is like cloud that showers rain without discriminating between land and water (sea); purindu – being friendly; uṟai – residing eternally; kōyil – abode; mayal migu – that place which captivates the one who sees; poḻil – garden; sūḻ – surrounded by; mālirunjōlai – in tirumalai; ayal – nearby; malai – mountain; adaivadu aduvē – reaching it alone exclusively; karumam – it is natural activity – must be done

**Перевод:**

**Oh heart! There is no use in performing useless activities. emperumān is like a black cloud that  holds drizzles and droplets of water and showers rain without discriminating between land and water (sea); being friendly, he is residing eternally in the beautiful abode of mālirunjōlai surrounded by garden that captivates; reaching a mountain near tirumalai is a natural activity \[for the ātmā\] and must be done.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the third pāsuram – āḻvār says “one should consider ayan malai (nearby hill) which is part of tirumalai as the goal”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “To desire for the hill nearby tirumalai where the most generous emperumān resides, is the goal”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Third pāsuram. āḻvār says “Do we need all these goals? The hill nearby tirumalai itself can be considered as the goal”. payan alla seydu payanillai nenjē puyal maḻai vaṇṇar purinduṟai kōyil mayal migu poḻil sūḻ mālirunjōlai ayal malaiadaivadu adu karumamē*

- *payanalla …* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) considers [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s presence in paramapadam (spiritual realm) and incarnations as useless \[since they are unreachable due to the place (too distant) and time (past);  he considers aḻagar [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s presence here and now as the most worthy aspect\]. Alternatively, this is explained as engaging in activities which are of no use. In āḻvār’s case \[i.e., emperumān’s presence here\], both the process and the result are of real use; this is what is explained in [bhagavat gītā](http://githa.koyil.org/) 9.2 “*susukam kartum*” (joyful to perform); [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is really thinking here about ascending to heaven (where there is joy that is still mixed with sorrow) and the process for that is difficult too.
- *nenjē* – Oh heart! You understand well, the difference between viśayāntaram (worldly pleasures) and bhagavat viśayam (transcendental pleasures). Alternative explanation – mind/heart is the common aspect that leads one to bondage and liberation; knowing well about this, you only tried to shy away from [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/).
- *puyal maḻai vaṇṇar purinduṟai kōyil* – Now, describing the nature of the result. Two explanations – 1) the temple that is the residence of the one who is as beautiful as a laden cloud, who fully manifests such beauty for the sake of others; 2) the temple that is the residence of the one who is as merciful as a laden cloud which showers the rain irrespective of land or water and who fully manifests such mercy for the sake of others. From these two explanations, we can understand that both the means \[his mercy\] and end \[his beauty\] are bhagavān only.
- *mayal migu poḻil sūḻ* – the dark place due to the coverings of the gardens; alternatively – due to its abundantly beautiful/enjoyable scenery, it will mesmerise those who see it.
- *mālirunjōlai ayan malai* – the hill that is glorified, only due to its proximity to tirumalai. Just as it is said in samkśēpa rāmāyaṇam “*agastya bhrātā*” (brother of sage agastya – is a well-recognizable identity for his brother even over his own name), this hill is known as the neighbouring hill of tirumalai.
- *adaivadu adu karumamē* – this is the only action that is to be done; all other actions are to be given up.

## 2.10.4. Karumavan pasam

*karumavan pāsam kaḻittu uḻanṟuyyavē perumalai eduttānpīduṟai kōyil varumaḻai tavaḻum mālirunjōlai tirumalai aduvē adaivadu tiṟamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

karumam – karmas which are bondage; van – difficult to eliminate; pāsam – attachments; kaḻittu – removed; uḻanṟu – perform (services); uyyavē – for the uplifting (of jīvātmās); peru – big; malai – hill; eduttān – one who lifted and protected; pīdu – (his) glories of protecting others; uṟai – residing eternally manifesting his radiance; kōyil – abode; varu – arriving (to rain) – laden; maḻai – clouds; tavaḻum – floating; māl – very tall; irum – wide; cōlai – having gardens; tirumalai aduvē – tirumalai itself; adaivadē – to reach; tiṟam – to be done

**Перевод:**

**emperumān who lifted the big (gōvardana) hill and protected the covherd girls/boys, eternally resides manifesting his radiance in the divine abode of mālirunjōlai that has very tall and wide gardens which are touched by the floating, laden clouds; he resides there to remove the karmas which are bondage and which are difficult to remove, and to accept the services of the jīvātmās; thus, to reach that tirumalai itself is that which is to be done \[by all\]. Since āḻvār emphasises tirumalai with the adjective of mālirunjōlai (tall, wide gardens), the beautiful gardens of tirumalai being the goal is highlighted.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fourth pāsuram – āḻvār says “the tirumalai (divine hill) where sarvēśvaran mercifully resides to remove the bondage of karma and let the devotees serve and live \[happily\], is the apt refuge”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “to attain tirumalai which is surrounded by huge gardens and which is the abode of rakśaka (protector) , is the apt action \[for devotees\]”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. karumavan pāsam kaḻittu uḻanṟuyyavē perumalai eduttānpīduṟai kōyil varumaḻai tavaḻum mālirunjōlai tirumalai aduvē adaivadu tiṟamē*

- *karumavan pāsam kaḻittu uḻanṟu uyyavē* – [kūrattāḻvān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/kurathazhwan/) explained once “Can we do anything other than approaching tirumalai to remove the bondage?”; that is also a nice explanation. Alternatively – [emperumānār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/emperumanar/) explains this as “emperumān descended here to remove our bondage and accept our service”. Just like murāsura who built a fort covered by pāsam (ropes) and tried to protect himself (eventually to be killed by kriṣṇa), the karmas which are covered by avidyā (ignorance) etc.  To remove the karma in the form of strong ropes and to uplift the jīvātmās by accepting their services towards him. It is the objective of his incarnations to remove the enemies and uplift others as explained in bhagavad gītā 4.8 “*paritrāṇāya sādūnām*” (to protect the devotees).
- *peru malai eduttān* – He would perform impossible tasks to protect his devotees. As the gōpas (covherd boys) and gōpis (covherd girls) suffered as explained in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 5.11.13 “*gōgōpījanasankulam”* (cows, covherd boys and girls are all suffering), he protected them by lifting the gōvardana hill. With such glories, he arrived in tirumālirunjōlai to reside here.
- *peru malai* – the hill is so wide that all 5 lakh families who are residents of the town \[āyarpādi\] can take shelter underneath it.
- *pīdu udai kōyil* – pīdu – perumai – aiśvaryam – wealth/greatness, quality of helping while in danger etc. [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who protected having a hill as ādēyam (one that is held), is now having a hill as ādāram (one that holds) to protect \[his devotees\]. The temple where he manifests the greatness acquired by protecting cows and covherd boys/men
- *varu maḻai tavaḻum mālirum cōlai* – As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam kiśkintā kāṇḍam 28.22 “*samudvahantassalilātibhāram balākinō vāridarā nadanta: \| mahatsu śrungēśu mahītarāṇām viśramya viśramya puna: prayānti \|\|*” (Clouds which are laden with abundance of water, which have nicely formed rows like a group of cranes which make sounds, are resting on the great peaks of the mountains and travelling subsequently), the clouds are travelling like pregnant ladies elegantly climbing the hills. Clouds too are of kinds – those which stay at the top and rain and those which keep travelling; here [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is compared to clouds as he was referred to as “*puyal maḻai vaṇṇar*” previously.
- *tirumalai aduvē adaivadu tiṟamē* – it is the duty for every one to reach tirumalai which is known as mālirunjōlai; this is to be done. Also explained as – take shelter of tirumalai which has mālirunjōlai (māl – tall, irum – wide, cōlai – garden).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.
