## 2.10.5. Tiramudai valattal

*tiṟamudai valattāl tīvinai perukkādu aṟamuyal āḻip padai avan kōyil maṟuvil vaṇ sunai sūḻ mālirunjōlai puṟa malai sārap pōvdu kiṟiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tiṟam udai – many types of; valattāl – strengths, abilities; tī – cruel; vinai – sins; perukkādu – instead of increasing; aṟam – righteous acts (such as protecting his devotees); muyal – being engaged; āḻi – divine chakra; padai avan – having it as weapon; kōyil – being the abode; maṟu – blemish; il – without; vaṇ – helping in all ways for those who approached; sunai – ponds; sūḻ – surrounded by; mālirunjōlai – tirumalai; puṟa malai – the hill that is in the outer ring; sāra – to approach; pōvadu – to go; kiṟi – best method/means

**Перевод:**

**Instead of increasing cruel sins (such as engaging in those acts which are forbidden etc) through one’s many types of abilities, the best means is to go and approach the hill that is in the outer ring of mālirunjōlai (tirumalai) that is surrounded by unblemiśed ponds which help those  who approached them in all ways; such tirumalai is the abode of aḻagar emperumān who is holding the divine chakra as a weapon, that is engaged in righteous acts (such as protecting his devotees).**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fifth pāsuram – āḻvār says “The best means is to approach a hill that is outside (in the vicinity) of tirumalai”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “The best means is to approach a hill that is outside (in the vicinity) of tirumalai which is the abode of the one who holds the divine chakra to protect \[others\]”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. tiṟamudai valattāl tīvinai perukkādu aṟamuyal āḻip padai avan kōyil maṟuvil vaṇ sunai sūḻ mālirunjōlai puṟa malai sārap pōvdu kiṟiyē*

- *tiṟamudai valattāl* – tiṟam – group; valam – balam – strength/ability. Instead of accumulating the sins through our groups of strengths.
- *aṟamuyal …* – As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 16.4 “… *lakśmaṇasya ca dīmata: …*” (sītā pirātti found out the opinion of śrī rāma and the intelligent lakśmaṇa) – even more than sarvēśvaran, the divine chakra which is more interested in protecting his devotees \[lakśmaṇa is cited as an example for sudarśana chakra who is also his devotee\], the divine abode of such [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who holds the divine chakra. When sarvēśvaran looked at him (sudarśana chakra), in a moment he went and burnt down varaṇāsi \[When pauṇḍarīka vāsudēva was killed, the king of kāśi, sent a demon to attack kriṣṇa. But kriṣṇa sent his sudarśana chakra and he promptly destroyed all the enemies and protected [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s devotees\].
- *maṟuvil …* – For those who desire to reach [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/), the best means which has no difficulty is to approach the outer hill of mālirunjōlai which is surrounded by beautiful ponds which are  without blemish, which has absolute clarity like [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s divine heart, which is pleasing to the eyes and perennial as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam bāla kāṇḍam 2 “*ramaṇīyam prasannāmbu sanmanuśyamanō yatā*” (This water is beautiful like the pristine minds of the learned elders).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.10.6. Kiriyena ninaimin

*kiṟiyena ninaimin kīḻmai seyyādē uṟiyamar veṇṇey uṇḍavan kōyil maṟiyodu piṇaisēr mālirunjōlai neṟipada aduvē ninaivadu nalamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kīḻmai – inferior aspects (of being attached to worldly pleasures); seyyādē – instead of engaging in; kiṟi – best means; ena – to be; ninaimin – consider; uṟi – in the (pot from the) suspended rope; amar – accumulated and safely kept; veṇṇey – butter; uṇḍavan – the one who consumed, kriṣṇa’s; kōyil – being the temple; maṟiyodu – with the calves; piṇai – female deer; sēr – unite; mālirunjōlai – in the tirumalai; neṟi – path; pada – to enter; aduvē – that (thought) itself; ninaivadu – to meditate upon; nalam – puruśārtam (goal)

**Перевод:**

**Instead of engaging in inferior aspects (of being attached to worldly pleasures), consider this as the best means; (that is because, ) this is the temple of kriṣṇa who consumed the butter that was accumulated and safely kept in the (pot from the) suspended rope. Also, this mālirunjōlai is where the female deer are united with their calves; to meditate upon entering the path to such tirumalai is the goal.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the sixth pāsuram – āḻvār says “Contemplating on the path that leads to tirumalai (divine hill) is good”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “Contemplating on the path that leads to tirumalai (divine hill) that is the abode of emperumān who is greatly attached to his devotees, in itself is good”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*In the sixth pāsuram – āḻvār says “Contemplating on the path that leads to tirumalai is the good means”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. kiṟiyena ninaimin kīḻmai seyyādē uṟiyamar veṇṇey uṇḍavan kōyil maṟiyodu piṇaisēr mālirunjōlai neṟipada aduvē ninaivadu nalamē*

- *kiṟiyena ninaimin* – Make your intellect realise that this (what I am saying now) is the correct means.
- *kīḻmai seyyādē* – Indulge in what I am suggesting and not in anything other than this; i.e., attachment towards worldly pleasures.
- *uṟi* … – the abode of emperumān who consumed the butter that was accumulated in the pots and kept safely in the tightly strung ropes; it made people wonder “did some gods consume this butter which is impossible to be retrieved by any ordinary person”. This highlights that he cannot sustain himself without those objects which are touched by his devotees.
- *maṟiyodu piṇai sēr mālirunjōlai* – the place where the mother and calves are not separated. This implies that it is the abode where the protected ones (devotees) and the protector ([bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)) are living together.
- *neṟi* … – the best means is to meditate upon tirumalai so that it is well understood in the mind/heart; alternative explanation – the best means is to contemplate upon entering the path leading to tirumalai.
- *aduvē ninaivadu nalam* – contemplating on that alone is good \[for the [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)\]; everything else is bad.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.10.7. Nalamena ninaimin

*nalamena ninaimin naragaḻundādē nilamunam idandān nīduṟai kōyil malamaṟu madisēr mālirunjōlai valamuṟai eydi maruvudal valamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

naragu – (being outside) in this hell named samsāram (material realm); aḻundādē – instead of being immersed; nalam – ultimate goal; ena – as; ninaimin – keep it in your intellect; munam – once upon a time (during praḷayam (destruction)); nilam – earth; idandān – lifted up (in the form of varāha); nīduṟai – eternally residing; kōyil – being the temple; malamaṟu – having no blemish (due to rubbing on the peaks); madi – chandra; sēr – well placed; mālirunjōlai – tirumalai; muṟai – due to the relationship (as śēśa/servant and śēśi/master); valam – ānukūlyam – favourable aspects; eydi – acquire; maruvudalē – being well placed; valam – ultimate goal

**Перевод:**

**Instead of being immersed in this hell named samsāram (material realm), keep this as the ultimate goal in your intellect: to acquire the favourable aspects of the relationship (as śēśa/servant and śēśi/master) in tirumalai which is having the well placed moon with no blemish (due to rubbing on the peaks). This tirumalai is the eternally residing temple of emperumān who lifted up the earth (as varāha perumāḷ) once upon a time (during praḷayam (destruction)).**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the seventh pāsuram – āḻvār says “It is victorious when one acts favourably on hearing the word ‘tirumalai'”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “It is best to be favourable towards tirumalai which is the abode of emperumān who helps during praḷayam (deluge)”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Seventh pāsuram. āḻvār says “It is victorious for the ātmā to approach tirumalai and reside there permanently”. nalamena ninaimin naragaḻundādē nilamunam idandān nīduṟai kōyil malamaṟu madisēr mālirunjōlai valamuṟai eydi maruvudal valamē*

- *nalam ena ninaimin* – You keep my instructions as the most valuable advice in your intellect. Also explained as – keep this as the ultimate/best goal in your intellect.
- *naragu aḻundādē* – For [āḻvārs](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/azhwars/), naraka (hell) is well defined \[i.e., separation from [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is hellish for them\]; this is explained through the beautiful śrī rāmāyaṇa ślōkam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 30.18 “*yastvayā saha sa svarga: nirayō yastvayā vinā \| iti jānan parām prītim gacca rāmamayāsaha \|\|*” ([sītā pirātti](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/) says to [śrī rāma](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) – To be with you is heaven for me and to be separated from you is hell for me; knowing this great love of mine towards you, you go along with me to the forest); *yastvayā saha sa svarga: …* – śrī rāma said to sītā “To be in the forest is sorrowful and to be in the palace is very comfortable”. But it is not like that; sukam and dukkam are determined based on the individual who goes through the situations; \[sītā pirātti says\] whatever experience I get with you \[even in the forest\] – that is joyful for me and if I am separated from you \[even if I am in the palace\], it is sorrowful for me. *iti jānan* – If you don’t have such feelings \[towards me\], you have to learn it from others \[me\]! *parām prītim* –  my love towards you is not the same as your love towards me \[my love towards you is greater\]. śrī rāma asks “You are saying that you have greater love towards me. What should I do now?” *gacca rāma mayā saha* (Oh rāma! Just come along with me to the forest) – as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 27.9 “*agratastē gamiśyāmi*” (I will go before you), as I start towards the forest, you let me go first and just follow me. iḷaiya perumāḷ (lakśmaṇa) also said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 53.31 “*na ca sītā tvayā hīnā …*” (Just as sītā cannot live in separation from you, I too cannot live in separation from you. We will only survive for a moment in separation from you just like a fish can only live for a moment when separated from water) \[It is not just females (his consorts) who cannot bear his separation, even males (all his devotees irrespective of their gender) cannot handle his separation\].
- *nilam …* – In the beginning of varāha kalpam (kalpa is one day of brahmā), [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) assumed the form of a huge wild-boar, dived into the causal ocean and rescued the earth that was attached to the walls of the aṇḍam (universe); [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) has such kind heart as a natural quality; such emperumān’s eternal residence unlike those incarnations who live for a short period (in the material realm) and return to paramapadam (spiritual realm).
- *malam aṟu* – since the hill is very tall touching the sky, whenever the moon passes by, he rubs on the peaks and becomes radiant like a knife that is sharpened by rubbing it on a sharpener. Alternatively, [piḷḷān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/pillan/) explains this as “the divine hill itself will bestow pure knowledge”.
- *valamuṟai eydi* – Approaching [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) in a favourable manner unlike kālayavana, jarāsanda et al \[who approached emperumān to fight with him\].
- *maruvudal valamē* – to do so will give strength; also explained as *maruvudal va****r****amē* which means, to do so is the best thing.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.10.8. Valam seydu

*valam seydu vaigal valam kaḻiyādē valam seyyum āya māyavan kōyil valam seyyum vānōr mālirunjōlai valam seydu nāḷum maruvudal vaḻakkē*

**Пословный перевод:**

valam – strength (for the senses); seydu – create; vaigal – forever; valam – that strength; kaḻiyādē – instead of wasting it by spending in worldly matters; valam – favourable aspect of being dependent on the devotees; seyyum – one who does; āyan – kriṣṇa; māyavan – amazing lord; kōyil – temple; vānōr – nityasūris, the residents of paramapadam; valam – favourable acts; seyyum – do; mālirunjōlai – towards tirumalai; valam – favourable acts such as circumambulation; seydu – do; nāḷum – forever; maruvudal – to be together; vaḻakku – proper

**Перевод:**

**tirumalai is the abode of the temple of amazing lord kriṣṇa who does favourable aspect of being dependent on the devotees; such tirumalai is favourably served by nityasūris, the residents of paramapadam. It is proper for the ātmā to acquire strength (for the senses) and engage in favourable acts such as circumambulation etc towards tirumalai and be together forever \[with emperumān\] instead of wasting such strength on worldly matters.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the eighth pāsuram – āḻvār says “It is proper to go to tirumalai and circumambulate the divine hill forever”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār say “It is natural fit for the ātmā to eternally act favourably in tirumalai which is the abode of kriṣṇa who is favourable towards his devotees”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. valam seydu vaigal valam kaḻiyādē valam seyyum āya māyavan kōyil valam seyyum vānōr mālirunjōlai valam seydu nāḷum maruvudal vaḻakkē*

- *valam seydu …* – Instead of going astray by engaging in worldly matters, one should acquire strength and approach [sarvēśvaran](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) using the humanly body that was bestowed by him.
- *valam seyyum* … – Just as in citrakūtam,  where śrī rāma walked around holding sītā pirātti’s hands, this is the abode, where aḻagar [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) walks around with pirātti holding her hands affectionately \[mā + yavan – mā means [śrī mahālakśmi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/)\]. Second explanation – as said in yajur vēdam kātakam 7.5.36 “*ya ātmadā baladā:*” (sarvēśvara who gives himself to them to enjoy and who removes the hurdles to enjoy him as well), the abode of amazing kaṇṇan [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who gives himself to their (his devotees) joy and also gives the ability for them to enjoy him.
- *valam seyyum vānōr mālirunjōlai* – Earlier, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) said in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.8.3](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/09/thiruvaimozhi-1-8-3-kannavan/) “*viṇṇōr veṟpan*” (one who has the tirumalai (tiruvēnkatam) which is vorśippable by nityasūris); here he says “*vānōr mālirunjōlai*” which has similar meaning. Why are the nityasūris attached to these two divya dēśams specifically, while there are so many? Just like a suckling toddler will focus only on the mother’s bosom while there are so many organs in her body,  nityasūris (who are children of bhagavān) are focussed on these two divya dēśams which are explained as bosoms in periya tirumadal “*tennan uyar poruppum deyva vada malaiyum*” (the two divine hills – tirumālirunjōlai in the south and tirumalai in the north of tamiḻnādu); so, these two hills exist for the nityasūris exclusively.
- *vānōr mālirunjōlai* – Just like lakhmaṇa, bharata et al followed śrī rāma when he went to the forest, when [sarvēśvaran](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) goes to reside in tirumālirunjōlai, the nityasūris too followed him.
- *valam seydu* – We too engage in favourable acts along with them (nityasūris). [nanjīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nanjiyar/) mercifully explained “piḷḷai tirunaṟaiyūr araiyar and [bhattar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/parasara-bhattar/) were circumambulating periya kōyil (śrīrangam temple); I was following them; when others were circumambulating at the speed of a wild horse, these two were fully enjoying the divine gōpurams, divine buildings etc and were slowly moving” \[It is highlighted that one should go around the temple meditating upon [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), [āḻvārs](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/azhwars/) and [ācāryas](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/full-list) while seeing the wonderful sannidis, sculptures etc. instead of just running/walking around quickly/mechanically\].
- *nāḷum maruvudal vaḻakkē* – if we too follow the acts of nityasūris, there is no deviation for us. This is the proper method.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.10.9. Valakkena ninaimin

*vaḻakkena ninaimin valvinai mūḻgādu aḻakkodi attān amar perum kōyil maḻakkaḷiṟṟinam sēr mālirunjōlai toḻak karuduvadē tuṇivadu sūdē*

**Пословный перевод:**

val – very powerful (that is difficult to cross over); vinai – sins; mūḻgādu – not drowning; vaḻakku – this is fitting for the nature \[of soul\]; ena – as; ninaimin – you think; aḻan – demoniac; kodi – girl; attān – one who killed; amar – well-settled; perum – huge; kōyil – being the temple; maḻa – calves; kaḷiṟṟinam – herds of elephants; sēr – reaching; mālirunōlai – tirumalai; toḻa – to worship; karuduvadē – in the mind; tuṇivadē – having faith; sūdu – cause (to win over the samsāram (material realm))

**Перевод:**

**You think that this is fitting to the nature \[of the soul\] instead of getting drowned in very powerful sins; mālirunjōlai is the divine huge temple where emperumān, who killed the demoniac girl (pūtanā), is well-settled; herds of elephant calves reach such tirumalai; the cause (to win over the samsāram) is to have full faith in the mind to worship such tirumalai.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the ninth pāsuram – āḻvār says “The cause for victory is to have firm faith that it will be beneficial to think about vorśipping tirumalai (tirumālirunjōlai – divine hill)”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “The firm faith in thinking ‘I should worship the abode of emperumān who killed pūtanā’ is the cause for victory”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. vaḻakkena ninaimin valvinai mūḻgādu aḻakkodi attān amar perum kōyil maḻakkaḷiṟṟinam sēr mālirunjōlai toḻak karuduvadē tuṇivadu sūdē*

- *vaḻakkena ninaimin* – You emphasise in your intellect (mind) that my suggestion is the proper one.
- *valvinai mūḻgādu* – if you want to eradicate your huge sins that cannot be eradicated by your own efforts.
- *aḻk kodi attān* *amar perum kōyil* – aḻan indicates demon; kodi indicates girl; aḻakkodi means demoniac girl. aḻan means dead-body, thus it indicates demon \[since dead-body and demons are related\]. [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who killed pūtanā thought “when such enemies come, I cannot be far away” and resided here forever – thus it is *perum kōyil* (great temple).
- *maḻa* … – All the animals reside along with [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) as a single clan. Alternative explanation – tirumalai where groups of young elephant calves have reached. \[Further explanation of both ideas together\] when a most beautiful elephant is present in a place, naturally many elephants will come and join there. emperumān who is standing there is also explained as an elephant in periya tirumoḻi 4.9.2 “*sōlai maḻa kaḷiṟiṟē*” (young elephant of the garden) and in tiruneduntāṇḍagam 10 “*tennānāy*” (elephant in the south side).
- *toḻak karuduvadē tuṇivadu sūdē* – Cause for victory for the [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is to firmly believe in the mind that ‘I should worship tirumalai”.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.10.10. Sudenru kalavum

*sūdenṟu kaḷavum sūdum seyyādē vēdamun virittān virumbiya kōyil māduṟu mayil sēr mālirunjōlai pōdaviḻ malaiyē puguvadu poruḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

sūdu – simple means to achieve wealth; enṟu – thinking so; kaḷavum – stealing (without the knowledge of the victim); sūdum – taking away (while the victim is watching); seyyādē – instead of doing that; mun – long ago; vēdam – the principles of vēdam (through gītōpaniśat etc); virittān – explained; virumbiya – residing joyfully; kōyil – being the temple; mādu – softness; uṟu – having; mayil – peacocks; sēr – residing together; māl – tall; irum – wide; sōlai – in the gardens; pōdu – flower; aviḻ – blossoming; malai – in the tirumalai; puguvadē – to enter; poruḷ – puruśārtam – goal

**Перевод:**

**Thinking that stealing (without the knowledge of the victim) and taking away (while the victim is watching) wealth are simple means to earn wealth, one should not engage in such activities; instead one should consider entering tirumalai (tirumālirunjōlai) as the goal; this tirumalai is the joyful abode of emperumān who explained the principles of vēdam (through gītā etc) long ago; it is also the place which has tall, wide gardens which are populated by peacocks having softness and which have blossoming flowers. māduṟu is also explained as peacocks living together with their female-counterparts.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the tenth pāsuram – āḻvār concludes that tirumalai is the ultimate goal as explained in many ways \[in previous pāsurams\].*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār concludes saying “the goal is to enter tirumalai which is the abode of emperumān who is the propagator of vaidika jñānam (knowledge \[based\] on vēdam)” as he started.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. sūdenṟu kaḷavum sūdum seyyādē vēdamun virittān virumbiya kōyil māduṟu mayil sēr mālirunjōlai pōdaviḻ malaiyē puguvadu poruḷē*

- *sūdenṟu* …
   - One should not engage in gambling and stealing because of there being good opportunity for doing those activities.
   - Second explanation – Since śāstram forbids one from engaging ins gambling and stealing, one should not engage in them.
   - Third explanation – kaḷavu means \[sva svātantriyam – considering oneself as independent\] stealing the ātmā from bhagavān as explained in “*cōrēṇa ātmāpahāriṇā*” (stealing the ātmā is the biggest theft); sūdu means \[dēhātmābhimānam – considering the self to be the same as body\] when someone is being sātvika (faithful, in the mode of goodness) and believes in śāstram thinking “sarVēśvaran is my protector”, going to such person and telling him that “there is no [īśvara (God)](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) beyond the body that is present for you; there is no [ātmā (soul)](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) too” and stealing \[his knowledge\] as he is watching.
- *vēdam …* – the divine abode of *gītōpaniśadācārya* (the author of bhagavat gītā), kriṣṇa, who explained the principles of vēdam to eliminate such habits (kaḷavu, sūdū) from everyone.
- *māduṟu mayil* – mādu can be considered as tenderness indicating the peacocks which are feast to the sight; mādu can also mean female indicating the peacocks which live in pairs. All the residents of this abode are couples only \[like the divine couple, [śrīman nārāyaṇan](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) and [śrī mahālakśmi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/)\].
- *pōdaviḻ malaiyē* – It is not that there would be some flowers in between shrubs, leaves, bushes etc., the whole tirumalai is filled with blossomed flowers.
- *pugavadu poruḷē* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is concluding that reaching tirumalai is the only goal for the ātmā. āḻvār describes all other activities as useless acts.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 2.10.11. Porul enru

*poruḷ enṟu ivvulagam padaittavan pugaḻ mēl maruḷil vaṇ kurugūr vaṇ śatakōpan teruḷ koḷḷac conna ōrāyirattuḷ ippattu aruḷ udaiyavan tāḷ aṇaivikkum mudittē*

**Пословный перевод:**

poruḷ – result (to have friendship of his devotees); enṟu – as; i – inda – this; ulagam – lōkam – world; padaittavan – one who created; pugaḻ mēl – on the qualities (such as dayā (mercy), kśamā (patience), audārya (generosity) etc); maruḷ il – being devoid of ignorance; vaṇ – distinct/beautiful; kurugūr – being the leader of āḻvārtirunagari; vaṇ – being most generous; śatakōpan – nammāḻvār; teruḷ – true knowledge; koḷḷa – (for the jīvātmās to) accept; sonna – mercifully explained; ōr – distinct; āyirattuḷ – among the thousand pāsurams; ippattum – this decad; mudittu – will eradicate samsāram (bondage in this material realm); aruḷ udaiyavan – aḻagar emperumān who is completely merciful; tāḷ – divine feet; aṇaivikkum – will enable reaching that

**Перевод:**

**The most generous nammāḻvār who is the leader of the distinct/beautiful āḻvārtirunagari, being devoid of ignorance, mercifully explained the true knowledge to the jīvātmās, in this decad which is among the distinct thousand pāsurams, glorifying the qualities (such as dayā (mercy), kśamā (patience), audārya (generosity) etc) of emperumān who created this world, to have the result (of getting the friendship of his devotees); such decad itself will eradicate samsāram (bondage in this material realm) and enable reaching the divine feet of aḻagar emperumān who is completely merciful.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the end – āḻvār says “This tiruvāimoḻi (decad) itself will end the bondage (to this materialistic realm) of those who learned it and will unite them with the divine feet of aḻagar emperumān“.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār explains reaching bhagavān as the result of this decad.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. poruḷ enṟu ivvulagam padaittavan pugaḻ mēl maruḷil vaṇ kurugūr vaṇ śatakōpan teruḷ koḷḷac conna ōrāyirattuḷ ippattu aruḷ udaiyavan tāḷ aṇaivikkum mudittē*

- *poruḷ* … – This decad was mercifully sung by [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) who doesn’t have even a trace of ignorance, in the matter of the auspicious qualities of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who created the universes thinking that they will be of use \[i.e., the people of these universes will try to learn the truth and reach him\]. emperumān, after creating the universes and bestowing body/senses to the [jīvātmās](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/), if they become attached to worldly pleasures and go astray, instead of thinking “my goal is not accomplished” and stopping doing it, will repeatedly do this creation \[creation, sustenance and annihilation\] thinking “if not today, some day, someone will reach me”;
- *maruḷ il …* – Since [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) was bestowed pristine knowledge/devotion by [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) himself, he would have no confusion about the auspicious qualities of bhagavān.

And the prabandam is,

- *teruḷ koḷḷac conna ōrāyiram* – For [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/), there was ignorance \[in infinite number of previous lives\] and it was eliminated \[by [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) in this life\]; but for those who learn āḻvār’s prabandam, their ignorance will be immediately eliminated and they will acquire pure knowledge. īśvara is the source for his knowledge; he is the source for our knowledge.

What does the prabandam do?

- *aruḷ udaiyavan* … – bhagavān is identified by his mercy \[that is the unique differentiating factor for him from others\]. This decad will unite the [jīvātmās](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) with the divine feet of the one who is filled with mercy.

While doing so,

- *mudittē* – It will eradicate the bondage in this samsāram (material realm) with its impressions (any trace of subconscious attachment) and unite them with the divine feet of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/). It is not just a tool to instil knowledge, it will literally be in action, uniting us with the divine feet of emperumān.

Finally, nampiḷḷai summarizes the contents of this decad briefly.

- In the [first pāsuram](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/06/thiruvaimozhi-2-10-1-kilaroli-ilamai/), [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) said “quickly take shelter of tirumalai (divine hill)”.
- In the [second pāsuram](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/06/thiruvaimozhi-2-10-2-sadhirila-madavar/), he said “take shelter of the divyadēśam attached to the divine hill”.
- In the [third pāsuram](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/06/thiruvaimozhi-2-10-3-payanalla-seydhu/), he said “even the neighbouring hill of the tirumalai is sufficient \[for our being uplifted\]”.
- In the [fourth pāsuram](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/06/thiruvaimozhi-2-10-4-karumavan-pasam/), he instructed us to take shelter of tirumalai again as done in [kaṇṇinuṇ ciṟut tāmbu 3](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/01/kanninun-chiru-thambu-3-thirithanthagilum/) “*tiridandāgilum*” (even if done again).
- In the [fifth pāsuram](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/06/thiruvaimozhi-2-10-5-thiramudai-valaththal/),  he said “take shelter of the outer hill around the tirumalai”.
- In the [sixth pāsuram](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/06/thiruvaimozhi-2-10-6-kiriyena-ninaimin/), he said “it is sufficient to think about the path that leads to tirumalai”.
- In the [seventh pāsuram](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/06/thiruvaimozhi-2-10-7-nalamena-ninaimin/), he instructed us to take shelter of the hill that is attached to the path that leads to tirumalai.
- In the [eighth pāsuram](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/06/thiruvaimozhi-2-10-8-valam-seydhu/), he said “tirumalai is the ultimate goal since it is the goal for nityasūris too”.
- In the [ninth pāsuram](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/06/thiruvaimozhi-2-10-9-vazhakkena-ninaimin/),  he insisted that the firm belief in “We will worship tirumalai” is required.
- In the [tenth pāsuram](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/07/thiruvaimozhi-2-10-10-sudhenru-kalavum/), he concluded that taking shelter of tirumalai is the goal with respect to all aspects.
- In the end, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) mercifully explained the result for those who learn this decad.

nampiḷḷai also briefly summarizes each decad of this centum in the end.

- In the [first decad](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/11/thiruvaimozhi-2-1-vayum/), [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) said that since [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is most distinct/beautiful as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.10.11](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/10/thiruvaimozhi-1-10-11-maniyai-vanavar/) “*maṇiyai vānavar kaṇṇānait tannadōr aṇiyai*“, he will make those who are separated from him to crave for him.
- In the [second decad](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/01/thiruvaimozhi-2-2-thinnan/), he said “Even when united with him, he will make others fully forget about everything else”.
- In the [third decad](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/02/thiruvaimozhi-2-3-unil-vazh/), he said “emperumān with whom he united is greatly joyful”.
- In the [fourth decad](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/03/thiruvaimozhi-2-4-adiyadi/), he became bewildered since he did not unite and enjoy [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) with those great leaders (nityasūris) who are experts in emperumān’s aspects.
- In the [fifth decad](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/03/thiruvaimozhi-2-5-andhamaththanbu/), he explained emperumān uniting with him as he desired.
- In the [sixth decad](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/03/thiruvaimozhi-2-6-vaikundha/), he said “[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) would doubt unnecessarily that [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) may leave”.
- In the [seventh decad](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/04/thiruvaimozhi-2-7-kesavan-thamar/), he explained how [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) pursued those who are related to [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) and his relatives.
- In the [eighth decad](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/05/thiruvaimozhi-2-8-anaivadhu/), he explained [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s mōkśa pradatvam (ability to bestow liberation).
- In the [ninth decad](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/06/thiruvaimozhi-2-9-emmavidu/), he established the goal clearly.
- In the [tenth decad](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/06/thiruvaimozhi-2-10-kilaroli/), he advised everyone to take shelter of tirumalai (the divine hill of tirumālirunjōlai) to acquire the goal established previously.

## Third Centum

## 3.1 Mudiccodiyay

## 3.1.1. Mudiccodiyay

*mudiccōdiyāy unadu mugaccōdi malarndaduvō adiccōdi nī ninṟa tāmaraiyāy alarndaduvō padiccōdi ādaiyodum palakalanāy nin paim pon kadiccōdi kalandaduvō tirumālē katturaiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

unadu – your; mugam – divine face’s; cōdi – radiance; mudi – in the divine crown; cōdi – radiance; malarndaduvō – did it rise upwards?; adi – the divine feet’s; cōdi – radiance; nī ninṟa – where you stand; tāmaraiyāy – the lotus seat; alarndaduvō – did it spread downwards?; pai – well spread; pon – having beauty; nin – your; kadi – waist’s; cōdi – radiance; padi – natural; cōdi – having radiance; ādaiyodum – with the divine clothes; pal – many; kalanāy – being divine ornaments; kalandaduvō – did it spread upwards and downwards?; tirumālē – since you are the lord of śrī mahālakśmi; katturai – mercifully explain this to remove my doubts

**Перевод:**

**Did the radiance of your divine face rise upwards to become the radiance in your divine crown? Did the radiance of your divine feet spread downwards to become the radiance in the lotus flower where you stand? Did the radiance of your well spread beautiful waist spread downwards and upwards with the naturally radiant cloth and the divine ornaments you wear? Since you are the lord of śrī mahālakśmi, as said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 1.8.18 “artō viṣṇuriyam vāṇi” (śrī viṣṇu is the meaning and śrī mahālakśmi is the word), as you are the one who is the controller of words and meanings, mercifully explain this to remove my doubts.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the first pāsuram – āḻvār becomes delighted thinking about the perfect match between the divine limbs and the divine ornaments.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*In the first pāsuram – based on the perfect match between the divine ornaments and divine limbs of lord śrīman nārāyaṇan, āḻvār gets doubts that could not be comprehended by him and hence he asks emperumān himself to clarify that doubt.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. mudiccōdiyāy unadu mugaccōdi malarndaduvō adiccōdi nī ninṟa tāmaraiyāy alarndaduvō padiccōdi ādaiyodum palakalanāy nin paim pon kadiccōdi kalandaduvō tirumālē katturaiyē*

- *mudiccōdiyāy unadu mugaccōdi malarndaduvō* – Did your divine face’s radiance extend up to the divine crown and become splendorous? ōr it can also be explained as – did your divine crown’s radiance extend down to the divine face and become splendorous? For a śēśabhūta (servant), the first thing that will be seen is emperumān’s śēśitvam (that which highlights the supremacy – i.e., his unique and divine crown); the beauty of the crown that highlights his supremacy leads [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) to his divine feet.
- *adiccōdi* – Did the radiance of the divine feet spread over the lotus seat of your highness and become splendorous? ōr did the lotus on which you are standing spread to your radiant divine feet and become splendorous \[like a lotus flower would be fresh when in contact with water, your lotus feet are looking fresh due to the contact with the lotus seat\]?
- *nī ninṟa* – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is called ēkarūpa (unchanging), stood with great attachment like someone performing penance standing in water. Since this is the ultimate goal, there is nothing beyond \[below\]. So, the radiance of the divine feet rises up \[leading [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) to other aspects in emperumān’s divine form\]; like a wooden block in an ocean that is pushed from one tide to another, the beauty of different aspects of emperumān pushes āḻvār and āḻvār enjoys them.
- *padiccōdi* – \[padi – tirumēni – divine form\] Did the beauty of the divine form spread into the many divine ornaments or did the beauty of the many ornaments spread into the divine form? Did the radiance of the divine clothes spread into the divine waist or did the radiance of the divine waist spread into the divine clothes?
- *nin paim pon kadiccōdi padiccōdi ādaiyodum pal kalanāyk koṇḍu kalandaduvō* – Did the radiance of your beautiful gold-like waist spread into the naturally radiant divine clothes and other divine ornaments? Just as we cannot differentiate when water gets mixed with water, it is impossible to differentiate between the radiance/beauty of these various aspects. Alternatively, padi is also explained as “inherent quality” \[i.e., all of these aspects are natural for [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)\].
- *tirumālē* – This divine togetherness of [śrī mahālakśmi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/) and [śrīman nārāyaṇan](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is also another beautiful aspect. Both [śrī mahālakśmi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/) who says as in tiruvāimoḻi 6.10.10 “*agalagillēn*” (will never separate from him) and naturally all-knowing yourself should analyse these and give clarification to me. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) who started enjoying [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) recently \[i.e., new to bhagavat viśayam\] would say as in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.1.6](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/04/thiruvaimozhi-1-1-6-ninranar-irunthanar/) “*enṟum ōriyalvinar ena ninaivu ariyavar*” ([emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) cannot be understood as having such and such qualities). Those who enjoy him eternally (his divine consorts) would say as in periya tirumoḻi 8.1.9 “*paṇḍivaraik kaṇḍaṟivadu evvūril yām*” (where did we see him before?). emperumān himself who is naturally omniscient as explained in tiruvāimoḻi 8.4.6 “*tanakkum than tanmai aṟivariyān*” (he himself does not fully know his glories). Thus, these doubts remain for āḻvār who started experiencing [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) recently, as they do for those who eternally experience emperumān and āzjvār himself – without any difference. āḻvār is thinking that just like he is having these doubts, they would also be having such doubts.
- *katturaiyē* – please explain.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.1.2. Katturaikkil

*katturaikkil tāmarai nin kaṇ pādam kai ovvā sutturaitta nan pon un tirumēni oḷi ovvādu otturaittu ivvulagu tanaip pugaḻvellām perumbālum patturaiyāyp puṟkenṟē kāttumāl paranjōdi*

**Пословный перевод:**

paranjōdi – Oh supreme light (bhagavān)!; katturaikkil – when clearly said; tāmarai – lotus flower; nin – your; kaṇ pādam kai – divine eyes, divine feet and divine hands; ovvā – does not compare to; suttu – molten; uraitta – prepared; nan – good/best; pon – gold; un – your; tirumēni – divine (spiritual) body/form’s; oḷi – collective radiance; ovvādu – does not compare to; i – inda – this; ulagu – world; ottu – as matching example; uraittu – told; unnai – you; pugaḻvu – glorifying; ellām – all; perumbālum – mostly; patturaiyāy – explained as seen/understood; puṟkenṟē – as something inferior; kāttum – will show

**Перевод:**

**Oh supreme light! When clearly said, lotus flower does not compare to your divine eyes, divine feet and divine hands; the best molten gold that is prepared does not compare to the collective radiance of your divine (spiritual) body/form. Thus, whatever is told in this world as matching example in glorifying you, are all  mostly explained as seen/understood \[by the individuals\] and will only lead to showing bhagavān (the object of such examples\] in poor light \[Lotus flower, gold etc., have acquired greatness; but emperumān has natural greatness; hence, comparing such objects to bhagavān will make one think that emperumān is only as great/beautiful as those examples, but in reality his greatness/beauty is too great\].**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the second pāsuram – āḻvār says “Since there is nothing comparable to aḻagar emperumān‘s beauty, the praises of the worldly people are not going to add more glories to emperumān and in reality it would only cause insult to his greatness \[since his greatness cannot be fully comprehended and glorified\]”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār mercifully explains the lack of examples for the beauty of emperumān which is spoken about.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*In the second pāsuram – āḻvār investigates if there are any examples for aḻagar emperumān‘s beauty; since there are no such examples, he says “it is incomparable”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. katturaikkil tāmarai nin kaṇ pādam kai ovvā sutturaitta nan pon un tirumēni oḷi ovvādu otturaittu ivvulagu tanaip pugaḻvellām perumbālum patturaiyāyp puṟkenṟē kāttumāl paranjōdi*

- *katturaikkil* – One can experience [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) and only be immersed in him and cannot speak about such experience \[kattu – experience and uraikkil – if it is possible to explain\].
- *katturaikkil* – katturai – a full/single word meaning “if it can be explained”. Even if all of the \[best\] lotus flowers are compared to your divine eyes, divine feet and divine hands collectively, they are no match. Even individually the eyes, feet and hands cannot be compared to all the lotus flowers. \[Why did [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) not sing from the divine feet to hands going upwards as we are suppose to do?\] Two explanations – 1) The reason for the order eyes, feet and hands is, eyes which gave the cool \[merciful\] glance, the divine feet at which we will fall after being won over by him and the hands that will lift us up and embrace us. 2) Since it is said in “*na śāstram naiva ca krama:*” (for those with unlimited devotion towards śrīman nārāyaṇan, the rules of śāstram do not apply), [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is just sharing his divine experiences \[which are beyond the ordinary rules of śāstram\] through his pāsurams. His experiences in previous pāsuram lead to the words in this pāsuram, i.e., “*nin kaṇ*” relates to “*mudiccōdi*“, “*pādam*” relates to “*adiccōdi*” and “*kai*” is a sample of his experience in between the crown and the divine feet.
- *sutturaitta …* – Explains this to highlight that gold is not a match for [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) .
- *sutturaitta* – The best gold which was molten and then purified further will not match the radiance of your natural divine form. Only if “gold” were explained with so many adjectives (molten, purified, best), it can at least be discarded as incomparable (without those, we cannot even start comparing the gold with [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s radiance). His divine form is explained in manu smruti 12.122 as “*rukmābham*” (having the complexion of molten gold).
- *otturaittu* – ottu – sadruśam – matching. They (people who compared) explained it as comparable to you.
- *ivvulagu* – As said in “*manjā: krōśanti*” (bed is making noise), those worldly people who do not understand anything beyond their perception. It is also explained as those people who cannot even comprehend these worldly matters properly.
- *unnai* – One who is known from śāstram alone and even when such śāstram tries to glorify you, it declares its inability as in taittiriya upaniśat “*yatō vācō nivartantē*” (the words are returning from glorifying that [brahmam](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)) – such you ([emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)).
- *pugaḻvellām* – even if told as the true glories and additional non-existing glories
- *perumbālum* – greatly, mostly
- *patturaiyāy* – what is felt in the heart, if said as it is (without thinking through). Alternative explanation – speaking casually without analysing.
- *puṟkenṟē kāttumāl* – it is showing him in poor light only. If he tells something that does not match [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/), how would that show bhagavān in poor light? If someone who does not know about the structure of gems looks at a precious gem and says “this looks like a salt crystal”, the one who listens to that will believe it as a salt crystal only and due to that the gem will become worthless too. Similarly, any praising done by anyone here towards bhagavān will only lead to such disgrace.

What is the basis for the cause of such disgrace?

- *paranjōdi* – As said in nārāyaṇa sūktam “*nārāyaṇa parōjyōti:*” (śrīman nārāyaṇan, the supreme light), he is different from all other entities \[so, worldly praises will not be able to do justice to his greatness\].

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.1.3. Paranjodi

*paranjōdi nī paramāy nin igaḻndu pin maṟṟōr paranjōdi inmaiyil padiyōvi nigaḻginṟa paranjōdi nin uḷḷē padar ulagam padaitta – em paranjōdi gōvindā! paṇburaikka māttēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

paramāy – being supreme; paranjōdi – one who is having unlimited radiant form; nī – you; nin – you; igaḻndu – except; pin maṟṟu – any other; ōr paranjōdi – a radiant entity who is supreme; inmaiyil – due to non-existence; padi ōvi – not having example; nigaḻginṟa – present; paranjōdi – being glorified as “paranjyōti”; nin uḷḷē – in your will; padar – vast; ulagam – world; padaitta – created; em paranjōdi – one who manifested to me the unsurpassed radiance of not being touched by the qualities of the created world; gōvindā – Oh one who is having radiance of tending to cows which is even greater than your supremacy!; paṇbu – your radiant nature that is due to your supreme unique forms, you having no example, your supreme nature of being the cause for this world and your unlimited simplicity; uraikka – to sing/glorify; māttēn – I am incapable

**Перевод:**

**You are the supreme one who is having unlimited radiant form; you are glorified as “paranjyōti” due to non-existence of any other supreme radiant entity except you; you created this vast world by your will, still remain untouched by the qualities of the created world and manifested to me this aspect which is of unsurpassed radiance; oh one who is having radiance of tending to cows, which is even greater than your supremacy! I am incapable of singing/ glorifying your radiant nature that is due to your supreme unique forms, you having no example, your supreme nature of being the cause for this world and your unlimited simplicity.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the third pāsuram – when emperumān asked āḻvār “if you say that my glories cannot be explained by certain others, can you do it?” āḻvār says “It is not possible for me too”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “your nature which is radiant from all aspects cannot be explained by me too”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Third pāsuram. When emperumān says “Leave those worldly people who have not started approaching me; but can you, who are different from them, speak about my glories?” āḻvār says “even I cannot speak about your glories”. paranjōdi nī paramāy nin igaḻndu pin maṟṟōr paranjōdi inmaiyil padiyōvi nigaḻginṟa paranjōdi nin uḷḷē padar ulagam padaitta – em paranjōdi gōvindā! paṇburaikka māttēnē*

- *paranjōdi nī paramāy* – Being supreme – you are the supreme light. \[The reason for paramāy – being supreme\] When someone has a little bit of beauty and wealth, others will glorify saying “there is none more beautiful than you; there is none wealthier than you”; but in [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s case it is so complete that there is no other entity which has such beauty, wealth etc – thus you are the supreme light in the true sense of supremacy as said in katōpaniśat “*tasya bhāsā sarvamidam vibhāti*” (Due to the radiance of that [brahmam](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/), all other radiant objects are shining).
- *nin …* – In this world, even though one may have beauty and wealth as comparable or greater, still he may be glorified saying “is there any one equal or greater than you?” Unlike that, since there is no supreme radiance like you, you cannot be compared to any one else and none can be cited as example for you. You are such a supremely radiant person \[who cannot be explained by any other example\].
- *nin uḷḷē …* – Though one may not even have full control over oneself, he may be glorified saying “you are the controller of all” Unlike that, it is your minute will that resulted in the creation of this vast world – you are my radiant lord. As said in “*putrastē jāta:*” (you have given birth to a son), this radiance is acquired after creating this world \[like the radiance acquired by a woman who gives birth to a child\]. The initial “paranjōdi” (supreme radiance) is the natural radiance of bhagavān. Here, it is the radiance acquired due to being the cause.

Even if the radiance of his supremacy can be understood/comprehended,

- *gōvindā* – the radiance of your simplicity is beyond comprehension.
- *paṇbu* – your attributes. While I can experience it, I cannot explain it.
- *gōVindā paṇburaikka māttēnē* – As said in tiruviruttam 98 “*nenjāl ninaipparidāl veṇṇey ūṇennum īnac col*” (That he was insulted saying that he stole and ate butter, cannot be comprehended in the heart), if it cannot be comprehended in the heart, how can it be explained?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.1.4. Mattade agilum

*māttādē āgilum im malar talai mā jñālam – nin māttāya malar puraiyum tiru uruvam manam vaikka māttāda pala samaya madi koduttāy – malarttuḻāy māttē nī manam vaittāy(l) mā jñālam varundādē?*

**Пословный перевод:**

malar – the lotus flower in the divine navel; talai – having it as (its) head; i – inda – this; mā – huge; jñālam – world; nin – (the apt) your; māttāya – in the true nature; malar puraiyum – tender like a flower; tiru uruvam – divine form; manam – in the heart; vaikka – to keep; māttādē āgilum – though not having done it since time immemorial (forever); māttāda – unqualified for meditating upon the divine form; pala samaya madi – knowledge about many different philosophies; koduttāy – you bestowed; nī – you; malar – blossomed; tuḻāy māttē – in the divine tuḷasi; manam – your heart; vaittāl – enjoying continuously; mā jñālam – this great world; varundādē – would it not worry?

**Перевод:**

**You bestowed knowledge on this world about many different philosophies (other than the one which should be used for reaching you). This world is unqualified for meditating upon your true nature and your tender flower-like divine form. It has as its head, the lotus flower in your divine navel. It has not meditated upon you from time immemorial. If you keep your heart in the divine tuḷasi and enjoy it continuously, would this great world not be put to difficulties?  Implies that it will be put to difficulties as bhagavān is not even looking at it with his mercy. malar talai also means that the world is on top of the lotus flower.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fourth pāsuram – āḻvār, being induced by aḻagar emperumān‘s abundant divine beauty, explains the same thinking “All the jīvātmās should not miss out on you (emperumān) who are distinctly greater than every one and are the confidential subject of upaniśats”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār asks emperumān “If you become fully engaged in enjoying this \[explained in the pāsuram\], would this insentient world not become worried?”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Fourth pāsuram. āḻvār said “I won’t explain” in the previous pāsuram. emperumān’s greatly reliśable nature is not attainable by some \[worldly people\]; feeling that these worldly people should not miss out and thereby not suffer in this material realm, being induced by aḻagar emperumān‘s abundant divine beauty, āḻvār speaks. māttādē āgilum im malar talai mā jñālam – nin māttāya malar puraiyum tiru uruvam manam vaikka māttāda pala samaya madi koduttāy – malarttuḻāy māttē nī manam vaittāy(l) mā jñālam varundādē?*

- *māttādē* … – \[To be read as\] *nin māttāya malar puraiyum tiru uruvam manam vaikka immalar talai mā jñālam – māttādē āgilum*.
- *nin māttāya* – Three explanations – 1) in you. 2) near you. 3) mattai (honey) has become māttu. As said in viṣṇu sūktam “*madva utsa:*” (honey is greatly flowing), since it is the source of honey, his divine form is very enjoyable/sweet. “*immalar talai mā jñālam”* is said due to It (the world) being unable to think about bhagavān, since it is created and bound by karma. māttai also means mādu (wealth), nidi (treasure). This great world, that is having the lotus flower in the divine navel as the base, is unable to meditate upon your treasure like great, flower like tender divine form. *āgilum* means “while the world is not mediating upon (you)”. This itself is disaster. For [cētanas (souls)](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) who are bound by karma, it is impossible to keep their heart on the divine form, which is enjoyable when karma is eradicated.

More than that disaster,

- *nin tiru uruvam manam vaikka māttāda pala samaya madi koduttāy* – Those which don’t engage their hearts in your divine form – there are many philosophies – i.e., other philosophies; you guided their hearts towards such philosophies. “*tiru uruvam manam vaikka*” is to be read with both the sections before and after that phrase. You have created these various philosophies which are outside vaidika philosophy, so that these cētanas can be diverted from you and thus they cannot have you in their hearts.

For those souls who have been in ignorance, you have created many philosophies, but since these souls are like [acit](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/09/thathva-thrayam-achith-what-is-matter/) (matter without any trace of knowledge) due to such ignorant philosophies, at least if you reside in close proximity to them such that they can approach you…

- *malart tuḻāy māttē nī manam vaittāy* – You started enjoying the enjoyable aspects like divine tuḷasi etc which will mesmerise even you. With this, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) implies “Is your sweet nature facilitating some people to approach you \[or stopping you from helping others\]?” \[While [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) was thinking to instruct others about [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s joy-filled nature, he sees that the sweet nature of emperumān which attracts everyone is so mesmerising to emperumān himself that even emperumān becomes too immersed in it and forgets his duty of uplifting others. So, he feels sorry for those [jīvātmās](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) who are missing out on emperumān’s mercy\]. mādu means place. Here it means “in” \[i.e., emperumān placed his heart in tuḷasi\].
- *mā jñālam* – This great world cannot suffer like this! Since they ([jīvātmās](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)) are bound by their karma, they are unable to meditate upon you; on top of that, you have created these various philosophies which detract them from you; and you are enjoying groups of objects which give unsurpassed pleasure; \[[āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) saying with great grief\] if you are not there to help them, they will clearly suffer by engaging in worldly pleasures as said in śrī bhagavat gītā 2.63 “*buddināśāt praṇaśyati*” (gets destroyed, having lost the intelligence).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.1.5. Varundada

*varundāda arundavatta malar kadirin sudar udambāy varundāda jñānamāy varambinṟi muḻudiyanṟāy varungālam nigaḻkālam kaḻikālamāy – ulagai orungāga aḷippāy sīr engulakka ōduvanē*

**Пословный перевод:**

varundāda – not attainable without great efforts; aru(m) – difficult to attain; tavatta – to be said as the result of (such) penances; malar – blossomed; kadirin – having rays; sudar – radiant; udambai – having as form; varundāda – natural instead of attaining through efforts; jñānamāy – being the one which (such) knowledge; varambu – limit; inṟi – not having; muḻudu – all entities; iyanṟāy – one who is residing; varungālam nigaḻkālam kaḻikālamāy – being present in all times (future, present and past); ulagai – world; orungāga – to stabilize; aḷippāy – Oh one who protects!; sīr – qualities (which are there due to your natural radiance, radiance in your knowledge, omnipresence and protection); engu – where (how); ulakka – comprehensively; ōduvan – can I speak?

**Перевод:**

**emperumān who has radiant light with blossomed rays as his form – a form which is the most difficult to attain even as a result of penance and cannot be attained without great efforts; emperumān who resides in all entities without any limits and has natural knowledge instead of knowledge acquired through self-efforts; emperumān who exists in past, present and future times; Oh such emperumān who stabilizes and protects the world! How can I comprehensively speak about your qualities (which are there due to your natural radiance, radiance in your knowledge, omnipresence and protection)?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fifth pāsuram – emperumān mercifully says “If the ignorant world does not speak, why don’t you speak?” āḻvār replies “I cannot speak about you, who are having endless auspicious qualities and wealth”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār asks “How can I comprehensively explain about you who are having such distinct greatness?”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Fifth pāsuram. Third pāsuram and this pāsuram are directly connected; in the fourth pāsuram, the loss to worldly people was highlighted by āḻvār since he happened to think about it. emperumān asks “Why are you saying ‘gōvindā paṇburaikka māttēnē‘? Leave aside the loss to worldly people, since you are blessed with pristine knowledge by me, you are different from them (and much wiser) ; not only are you different from worldly people, you are also different from the residents of paramapadam; why don’t you speak about me?” and āḻvār replies “you have bestowed pristine knowledge to me, but you have not converted yourself to be ‘limited’ \[i.e., emperumān‘s greatness is unlimited and cannot be spoken comprehensively\]”. varundāda arundavatta malar kadirin sudar udambāy varundāda jñānamāy varambinṟi muḻudiyanṟāy varungālam nigaḻkālam kaḻikālamāy – ulagai orungāga aḷippāy sīr engulakka ōduvanē*

- *varundāda* … – Is this beauty of his divine form explainable by me?
- *varundāda arum tavatta* – natural, radiant form of well-expanded rays. tava – abundance. As soon as people see the divine form, they will think “is this the result of great penance?” but once they immerse in it, they will realize “this is not acquired by any penance; but naturally gifted strength”.
- *malar kadirin sudar udambāy* – Having divine radiant form with clear rays. \[Like a diamond\] having removed the dirt, i.e., instead of being mixed with rajas (passion) and tamas (ignorance), this is pure satvam (goodness), the form of infinite splendour. [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) with the divine form which reveals his internal qualities clearly – unlike those bodies which are bound by karma \[in the mixed mode of satvam, rajas, tamas\], his divine body is acquired by him based on his iccā (desire) and thus is very pure. Our bodies are made of karma – some are made of pāpam (sins), some are made of puṇyam (virtues) and some are made of both puṇyam and pāpam. śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 5.1.50 “*na akāraṇāt kāraṇādvā kāraṇākāraṇānna ca*” is explained here. *akāraṇam* – result \[variegated forms of matter\]; *kāraṇam* – mūlaprakruti (primordial matter – cause); *kāraṇākāraṇam* – mahat etc (intermediary forms of matter which are both cause (for variegated forms) and effect (of primordial matter)) \[these are worldly elements, but [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s divine forms are made of spiritual elements and their purpose is explained further\]; *śarīra grahaṇam vyāpin* – you who are omnipresent, having the world itself as your body, assume these forms. *darmatrāṇāya kēvalam* – your forms are like water-shelter (A place where water is provided for the thirsty persons) for the pleasure of those who long for your vision as said in tiruvāimoḻi 8.5.2 “*kāṇa vārāy*” (please come here to see me). This is explained in jitantē stōtram 5 “… *na cākāra: bhaktānām …*” (your nature, forms, ornaments, weapons etc are all for the pleasure of your devotees).
- *varundāda jñānamāy* – Being naturally omniscient instead of acquiring this knowledge by great penances or acquiring it by the blessing of some one else.
- *varambu inṟi muḻudu iyanṟāy* – You control everything without any limitation. It is natural for the owner to control everything that is owned by him.
- *iyanṟāy* – iyalugai means controlling. Being the owner, instead of staying elsewhere and overseeing it, he is present everywhere and protecting each entity \[by his presence as antaryāmi\].
- *varungālam* … – How is it possible for me to comprehensively explain the auspicious qualities of yours, protecting all the worlds in a stable manner, being the controller at all times (past, present and future)? First two lines explain the greatness of your divine forms. Subsequently your presence as the one who can visualize everything at once and you being the protector are explained. Among these what can I speak about comprehensively?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.1.6. Oduvar ottellam

*ōduvār ōttellām evvulagattu evvevaiyum sāduvāy nin pugaḻin tagaiyallāl piṟidillai pōduvāḻ punanduḻāy mudiyināy! pūvinmēl māduvāḻ mārbināy! en solli yān vāḻttuvanē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ōduvār – having classification such as rig, yajur, sāma etc to be pursued by the qualified persons belonging to such branches of vēdam; ōttu ellām – all of vēdams; evvulagattu – in all worlds; evvevaiyum – having all branches; sāduvāy – having the goodness (of teaching the meanings as it is); nin – your; pugaḻin – qualities’; tagai allāl – will stop with a little engagement; piṟidu – explaining completely or beyond; illai – not there; pōdu – having flower; punam vāḻ tuḻāy – being decorated with divine tuḷasi which is fresh as if it is staying in its natural base; mudiyināy – having the divine crown; pūvin mēl – eternally residing on top of the lotus flower; mādu – śrī mahālakśmi; vāḻ – (leaving that) eternally residing; mārbināy – Oh one who is having the divine chest!; en solli – saying what (can I sing your sweetness? can I sing your attachment towards śrī mahālakśmi?); yān – I; vāḻttuvan – will praise?

**Перевод:**

**vēdams are having classification such as rig, yajur, sāma etc to be pursued by the qualified persons belonging to such branches of vēdam; even such vēdams which are present in all worlds having all branches, having the goodness of teaching the meanings as they are, will stop with a little engagement in explaining your qualities and cannot explain them completely or beyond that; you are decorated with a divine crown that has fresh divine tuḷasi with flowers; Oh one who is having the divine chest which is the eternal abode of śrī mahālakśmi, who was eternally residing in the lotus flower! What will I say and how will I praise you (Can I sing your sweetness? Can I sing your attachment towards śrī mahālakśmi)?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the sixth pāsuram – emperumān tells āḻvār “Like the vēdams which praise  me, you too can do it” and āḻvār says “Even vēdams tried to praise you, but after beginning to do so, they withdrew from doing the same. Is there any way for me, who is totally unworthy, to glorify you who are having such unlimited greatness?”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “What will I sing in glorification of you, who cannot be glorified by all of vēdams?”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. ōduvār ōttellām evvulagattu evvevaiyum sāduvāy nin pugaḻin tagaiyallāl piṟidillai pōduvāḻ punanduḻāy mudiyināy! pūvinmēl māduvāḻ mārbināy! en solli yān vāḻttuvanē*

- *ōduvār ōttu ellām* – By saying ōduvār, the diversity of qualified individuals is highlighted.
- *ōttu + ellām* – rig, yajur, sāma and atarva vēdams. Thus, all of vēdams which are classified into multiple branches based on the diversity of students.
- *evvulagattu evvevaiyum* – All manifestations in all worlds. Even in svarga lōkam (heaven – abode of indra) and brahma lōkam (abode of brahmā), vēdam would exist based on the intellect of the residents of those places. For example, śrī rāmāyaṇam in brahma lōkam contains unlimited ślōkams, while in our earthly abode, it has 24000 ślōkams.
- *sāduvāy* – being good. goodness for śabdam (vēdam, word) means revealing the meaning as it is. Alternatively, sāduvāy (goodness) could be seen as adjective for pugaḻ (qualities of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)).
- *sāduvāy nin pugaḻin tagai allāl piṟidu illai* – neither does it go beyond your auspicious qualities nor can it experience [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) fully. \[Another explanation\] As said in śrīrangarāja stavam 1.20 “*… varśabindōrivābdau sabandāt svātmalābha: …*” (when rain-drop falls into the ocean, it becomes worthy), when a rain-drop falls into the ocean, it does not pervade all of the ocean! It does not become extinct either \[By reaching the ocean, the rain-drop’s goal is reached; similarly by praising [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), one’s true nature is established\].
- *pōdu …* – Even while the vēdams are trying and giving up, how can I praise this togetherness \[of the divine couple\]? Oh the one who is having flower and divine tuḷasi, which is fresh as if it is staying in its natural base \[when flowers are attached to the tree/plant, they would remain fresh\], on your divine crown! The tuḷasi flower is living gloriously being crowned! Is this divinely decorated appearance within the limits of my praise?
- *pūvin mēl …* – Only when pirātti (śrī mahālakśmi) is separated, the decorated flowers would be dried. Her togetherness with [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) which is a decoration on top of the decoration (that was explained previously) – is that within the limits of my praise? Oh one who has the divine chest which is the abode of śrī mahālakśmi who felt the lotus flower to be too hot (in comparison to your divine chest)! If only sītā pirātti had ever returned to mitilā after marrying śrī rāma \[which never happened\], śrī mahālakśmi would consider leaving his divine chest and returning to the lotus flower which was her birth place.
- *en solli yān vāḻttuvanē* – Is this decoration and togetherness singable in praise by me?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.1.7. Valttuvar palaraga

*vāzttuvār palarāga nin uḷḷē nānmuganai mūḻtta nīr ulagellām padai enṟu mudal padaittāy kēztta sīr aran mudalāga kiḷar deyvamāyk kiḷarndu sūḻttamarar tudittāl un tol pugaḻ māsūṇādē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vāḻttuvār – those who praise you; palar – many; āga – to exist; nin uḷḷē – in your will; nānmuganai – four headed brahmā; mūḻtta nīr – in the causal ocean; ulagellām – all the worlds; padai – you create; enṟu – saying thus; mudal – as the primary entity; padaittavanē – oh one who created!; kēḻtta – abundance; sīr – having qualities such as jñānam etc; aran – rudra; mudalā – starting with; kiḷar – those who are with risen divine powers; amarar – having immortality \[to a limited extent\]; deyvamāy – dēvatās; kiḷarndu – zealously; sūḻttu – covering (the qualities which reap benefits \[for them\]); tudittāl – if they praise; un – your; tol – natural (ancient); pugaḻ – radiant qualities; māsūṇādē – would they not become tainted?

**Перевод:**

**Oh one who being the primary entity, created the four headed brahmā in the causal ocean saying to him “you create all the worlds” so that many of those who praise you exist! Even if such dēvatās starting with rudra et al who are having immorality \[to a limited extent\], who are with risen divine powers, praise you, covering those qualities which reap benefits \[for them\], would your naturally radiant qualities not become tainted?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the seventh pāsuram – when asked “What if everyone praises you together, or if most intelligent rudra et al praise you \[would that be possible\]?” āḻvār replies “Because rudra was created by brahmā who was created by you, the praise by those with narrow knowledge will only conceal your auspicious qualities”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Seventh pāsuram. emperumān says “Leave aside vēdam. There are certain individuals who are known as vaidika puruśas (well versed in vēdam such as vyāsa et al). What about their praising me?” āḻvār replies “Even that will only minimize your glories”. vāzttuvār palarāga nin uḷḷē nānmuganai mūḻtta nīr ulagellām padai enṟu mudal padaittāy kēztta sīr aran mudalāga kiḷar deyvamāyk kiḷarndu sūḻttamarar tudittāl un tol pugaḻ māsūṇādē*

- *vāḻttuvār palarāga* – [bhattar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/parasara-bhattar/) explains this as “Yes, there are many who can praise [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/). But what greatness do they have over vēdam \[which is eternal and free from blemish\]?” Alternatively, this is explained as – to create many who can praise [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/).
- *nin* … – With a very small fraction of your will, you created brahmā telling him “you create these worlds which are surrounded by water”. It can also be explained as – you created brahmā saying to him “mūḻtta nīrilē” (in the great causal ocean), “lōkangaḷai uṇḍākku” (you create the worlds). Is there any way for those created by brahmā, who was created by you, to praise you? \[this explains [bhattar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/parasara-bhattar/)‘s view point\]

When asked “But apart from those (vaidika puruśas such as vyāsa et al), what if we also included dēvatās rudra et al? Can they praise your glories?”, further it is explained that, even for them “it is not possible to do so”.

- *kēḻtta …* – If we leave aside these helpless group, is it possible for greatly powerful personalities to comprehensively glorify you? kiḷarnda sīr – qualities such as jñānam etc; if each of those dēvatās starting with rudra, who are at times confused to be supreme, who have such great knowledge, who have a very long life, attempts to praise different qualities which reap different benefits, would such praising cause disgrace to your naturally auspicious qualities? \[yes they will, in the sense that\] “his  qualities are only as great as they are able to praise \[while in reality the greatness of his qualities are unlimited\]”. In that sense, will their praising you not become a disgrace for you ([emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/))?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.
