## 3.1.8. Masuna

*māsūṇāc cudar udambāy malarādu kuviyādu māsūṇā jñānamāy muḻudumāy muḻudiyanṟāy māsūṇā vān kōlattu amarar kōn vaḻippattāl māsūṇā una pāda malarc cōdi maḻungādē*

**Пословный перевод:**

māsūṇā – without a trace of blemish; sudar – in the form of radiant light; udambāy – having divine form; malarādu kuviyādu – without expansion and contraction; māsūṇā – devoid of blemishes such as doubt, error etc; jñānamāy – having such knowledge as a natural quality; muḻudumāy – having all qualities and wealth/realms as attributes; muḻudu – all of those; iyanṟāy – oh one who is the abode for all of them to exist on you!; māsūṇā – devoid of blemishes; vān kōlattu – being decorated with great knowledge etc; amarar kōn – brahmā who is served by the dēvatās; vaḻip pattāl – if he engages in serving you in the form of praising your greatness; māsūṇā – being the opposite of all defects; un – your; pāda malar – divine lotus feet’s; sōdi – radiance; maḻungādē – will it not be reduced?

**Перевод:**

**Oh one who has a divine form which is devoid of any blemishes and that is in the form of a radiant light, who has knowledge that does not expand/contract and has no blemishes such as doubt, error etc., as a natural quality, who has all qualities and wealth/realms as attributes and being the abode for all of them to exist on you! \[Considering that there is a\] brahmā who is decorated with great knowledge etc which is devoid of any blemishes and who is being served by dēvatās, if he engages in serving you in the form of praising your greatness, will that not reduce the radiance of your divine lotus feet that is the opposite of all defects? It is implied that brahmā who is a created being (with acquired good qualities) approaching naturally radiant divine feet, is not of great value \[for the divine feet\].**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the eighth pāsuram – āḻvār considers brahmā who has ubhaya bhāvanā \[both karma bhāvanā – engaging in worldly activities and brahma bhāvanā – engaging in meditation etc upon bhagavān\] as good as vanaspati (plant) and says “if there were a greatly wise brahmā who has ultimate intelligence and even if he praises you, that will only conceal your greatness”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “even if brahmā becomes reformed to have ultimate knowledge and starts praising you, would your radiance not be concealed \[by that\]?”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Eighth pāsuram. Some explain this as – In previous pāsuram, āḻvār said that “those dēvatās starting with rudra cannot praise emperumān” and in this pāsuram, he says “even if brahmā who is the father of rudra praised you, that will only cause you disgrace”. bhattar mercifully explains this as –  Even brahmā was included in previous pāsuram. Here, āḻvār is saying “instead of this brahmā who has ubhaya bhāvanā, if there is a brahmā who is fully engaged with brahma bhāvanā alone, even his praising will lead to blemish for your highness”. māsūṇāc cudar udambāy malarādu kuviyādu māsūṇā jñānamāy muḻudumāy muḻudiyanṟāy māsūṇā vān kōlattu amarar kōn vaḻippattāl māsūṇā una pāda malarc cōdi maḻungādē*

- *māsūṇāc cudar udambāy* – Since you are being the opposite of defects, being in the mode of sudda satva (pure goodness), you are having infinitely radiant divine form.
- *malarādu kuviyādu* – He is as said in periya tirumoḻi 7.10.1 “*arumbinai alarai*” (sprouting flower); As said in “*yuvākumāra:*” (youth and adolescent), he would manifest both states at the same time. Also explained as said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 1.2.1 “*sadaikarūparūpāya*” (having a divine form which matches his divine nature), he would neither have growth or decay.
- *māsūṇā jñānamāy* – You who is having knowledge which cannot become blemished due to a particular reason \[karma\]. *malarādu kuviyādu* (expansion/contraction) is applicable to both his divine form (before the phrase) and his knowledge (after the phrase). His divine form does not acquire expansion/contraction as in the case of the changes that manifest in the bodies of samsāris (bound souls) which are acquired by their karma \[bodies -\> acit – matter – goes through changes to its nature itself\]; nor his knowledge goes through changes like in the case of samsāris whose knowledge expands/contracts \[cit – souls – does not change itself, but its knowledge expands/contracts\] \[Thus, it is established that [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is cangeless both in his nature and qualities and hence he is different from both [cit](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) and [acit](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/09/thathva-thrayam-achith-what-is-matter/)\].
- *muḻudumāy* – having all other qualities which are not explicitly highlighted here.
- *muḻudumāy* – his state of being the soul of the entire creation.
- *muḻudu iyanṟāy* – This is re-establishing the same concept that was highlighted in  [tiruvāimoḻi 3.1.5](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/07/thiruvaimozhi-3-1-5-varundhadha/) “*varambinṟi muḻudiyanṟāy*“, one who controls everything \[by being the antaryāmi (in-dwelling super soul\].
- *māsūṇā …* – As said in varāha purāṇam “*caturmukāyu: …*” (If there is some one who has the life span of brahmā with crores of faces and very pure mind, we are not sure if he can explain 1/10000th of your qualities. Oh supreme among Gods! kindly show your mercy”, even if there is such a brahmā who is the leader of dēvatās, his praises would also cause blemish only to you. Only [āḻvārs](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/azhwars/) perform mangaḷāśāsanam knowing his greatness. A brahmā who has no blemishes should be created. This is what is implied by “*utprēkśitanāna brahmā*” (an invented brahmā). Here, for the brahmā, at the end of his life, his knowledge will end too; for this \[invented\] brahmā, there should be no such defect. Since “*kōla*” (decoration) is seen as an adjective for “*vaḻippadugai”* (praising/vorśipping), it relates to the knowledge \[that is used to praise\]. If such brahmā praises you, the radiance of your divine feet that does not get reduced by the touch of anything else, will that not become minimized when considered “are his divine feet only as great as explained by brahmā \[instead of knowing their unlimited greatness\]?”. Due to his nature of servitude, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying “*una pādam*” (your feet) instead of “*un tirumēni*” (your divine form).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.1.9. Malungada

*maḻungāda vainnudiya cakkara nal valattaiyāy toḻum kādal kaḷirṟaḷippān puḷḷūrndu tōnṟinaiyē maḻungāda jñānamē padaiyāga – malarulagil toḻumbāyārkku aḷittāl un sudarc cōdi maṟaiyādē*

**Пословный перевод:**

maḻungāda – not blunt; vai – having sharpness; nudiya – having mouth; cakkaram – divine disc (sudarśana chakra); nal – beautiful; valattaiyāy – one who is having it in his right \[hand\]; toḻum – due to rendering service; kādal – having attachment; kaḷiṟu – elephant; aḷippān – to protect; puḷ – periya tiruvadi (garudāḻvār); ūrndu – rode him with great urgency; tōnṟinaiyē – you appeared in front of that elephant; maḻungāda – unfailing; jñānamē – jñānam (knowledge) in the form of sankalpam (divine will); padaiyāga – as entourage; malar – blossomed/expanded; ulagil – in the world; toḻumbāyārkku – to those who worship (you); aḷittāl – if you helped them; un – your; sudar – greatly radiant; sōdi – lustre; maṟaiyādē – will it not be reduced?

**Перевод:**

**You appeared in front of the elephant (gajēndrāḻvān) that is having attachment due to rendering services, to protect it by riding the garudāḻvār with great urgency, having the beautiful sudarśana chakra (disc) which has sharpness and does not become blunt and has a sharp mouth, in your right hand. In such case, for those who worship you in this blossomed/expanded world, if you helped them with unfailing jñānam (knowledge) in the form of sankalpam (divine will) as your entourage, would that not reduce your greatly radiant lustre (of urgently arriving at the banks of the pond to protect his devotee)?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*Subsequently, since āḻvār cannot sustain himself without praising emperumān, he highlights emperumān’s qualities and praises him.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In ninth pāsuram – āḻvār explains emperumān‘s vātsalyam (motherly affection) towards his devotees, with an example.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, your supremacy of protecting your devotees just with your will is inferior when compared to the great motherly affection you have towards your devotees.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*In ninth pāsuram – āḻvār mercifully explains emperumān‘s motherly affection that easily wins over his supremacy \[that was explained in previous pāsurams\].*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Ninth pāsuram. āḻvār says “If we say that your supremacy cannot be explained, does it mean that your simplicity is within the boundary of words?”. maḻungāda vainnudiya cakkara nal valattaiyāy toḻum kādal kaḷirṟaḷippān puḷḷūrndu tōnṟinaiyē maḻungāda jñānamē padaiyāga – malarulagil toḻumbāyārkku aḷittāl un sudarc cōdi maṟaiyādē*

- *maḻungāda …* – As it hits the bodies of the enemies, like a knife which gets sharpness/shining by being touched by knife-sharpener, the divine sudarśana chakra becomes sharper and more radiant. Instead of being blunt, the divine chakra with sharp edges, having such chakra in your right side as said in [tiruppallāṇḍu 2](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/06/thiruppallandu-2-adiyomodum/) “*vadivār sōdi valatturaiyum sudarāḻiyum pallāṇḍu*“.
- *nal valattaiyāy … tōnṟinaiyē* – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) forgot that he had his divine chakra in his hand; had he remembered, he would have sent that and finished the job right from where he was. As soon as he heard the sorrowful cry of his devotee, he forgot himself. But, even if he realized his position, he could not remove the sorrows right from where he is; because the elephant is “*toḻum kādal kaḷiṟu*” (elephant that has great attachment due to rendering services) – gajēndra is such an elephant who had the desire to see [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) with his divine chakra in the hand.
- *kādal kaḷiṟu* – Like airāvata is known as “*caturdanti*” (elephant with 4 tusks), gajēndra is called as “the loving elephant” – where love for [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is his identity.
- *aḷippān* – To accept the flower held by the elephant before it loses its freshness at his lotus feet \[this is explained as the cause of sorrow for gajēndra – he wants to offer the lotus flower at [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s lotus feet before it loses its freshness\].
- *puḷ ūrndu tōnṟinaiyē* – garudāḻvār’s speed is usually faster than [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s sankalpam (divine will); but this time, even such speed was not enough for emperumān, so he tucked garudāḻvār under his arm (carrying him all along) and jumped at the banks of the pond.
- *tōnṟinaiyē* – it looks like not gajēndra, but [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) was himself suffering – āḻvār is saying as if emperumān appeared in front of him!
- *maḻungāda jñānamē padaiyāga …* – To explain that he forgot the presence of his own divine chakra. Is he thinking about his knowledge in the form of his divine will which is even closer to him than his chakra? Even if his knowledge is used in many activities, instead of losing its quality, it gains lustre – having such divine will as entourage.
- *malarulagil toḻumbāyārkku aḷittāl un sudarc cōdi maṟaiyādē* – *toḻumbāyārkkum* – those who are [śēśabhūtas](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) (servitors). Those who are his servitors in this samsāram (material realm) which has the lotus flower in his navel as the base.  If you protect those devotees from wherever you are using your divine will, you will not be known for great lustre as in “one who urgently jumped without caring for his appearance, clothes etc., at the banks of the pond where the elephant was caught in trouble”.
- *maṟaiyādē* – When this was recited, an ācārya named siṟṟātkoṇḍān screamed “*maṟaiyum, maṟaiyum*” \[Yes, if he does not physically appear to protect the elephant, his lustre will be reduced\].

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.1.10. Maraiyaya

*maṟaiyāya nāl vēdattuḷ ninṟa malarc cudarē muṟaiyāl ivvulagellām  padaittidanduṇḍumiḻndaḷandāy piṟai ēṟu sadaiyānum nānmuganum indiranum iṟai ādal aṟindētta vīṟṟiruttal idu viyappē?*

**Пословный перевод:**

maṟaiyāya – that which conceals (its meanings for those who are filled with rajas (passion) and tamas (ignorance)); nāl vēdattu – vēdams which are four-fold (starting with rig vēdam etc which reveals its meaning to those who are situated in satvam (goodness)); uḷ ninṟa – being the intrinsic essence; malar – having blossomed; sudarē! – being in the form of a radiant light; muṟaiyāl – at every (creation) cycle; i – inda – this; ulagellām – worlds; padaittu – created; idandu – lifting them up (by entering into the causal ocean); uṇḍu – consuming them (during total deluge); umiḻndu – spitting them out again; aḷandāy – oh one who measured them (so that others cannot claim ownership)!; iṟaiyādal – being the lord (being revealed by vēdam only and engaging in creation etc); aṟindu – knowing thus (about you); piṟai ēṟu sadaiyānum – rudra who is engaged in enjoyment and austerity due to having candrakalā (crescent moon) in his head and having matted hair respectively; nānmuganum – brahmā (who has all the abilities to engage in creation); indiranum – indra (who is the lord of 3 worlds namely svarga lōka, bhuvar lōka and bhūlōka); ētta – to take shelter of you (by praising you); vīṟu – being great/distinct (since he is the one who gives shelter to all); iruttal idu – such stature; viyappē – is it surprising?

**Перевод:**

**Oh one who is in the form of a blossomed radiant light, being the intrinsic essence of vēdams which conceal (its meanings for those who are filled with rajas (passion) and tamas (ignorance)) and which are being four-fold (starting with rig vēdam etc which reveals its meaning to those who are situated in satvam (goodness))! Oh one who time and again creates the worlds,  lifts them up (by entering into the causal ocean), consumes them (during total deluge), spits them out again, and measures them (so others cannot claim ownership)! In such case, is it surprising to see such stature of being the great shelter (since he is the one who gives shelter to all) for rudra who is engaged in enjoyment and austerity due to having candrakalā (crescent moon) in his head and having matted hair respectively, brahmā (who has all the abilities to engage in creation), indra (who is the lord of 3 worlds namely svarga lōka, bhuvar lōka and bhūlōka) et al and being praised by them knowing that you are the lord.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In tenth pāsuram – āḻvār says “For you who is known only through vēdam and the lord of all, is it surprising that brahmā et al, who are created and bestowed knowledge by you, know you as “īsvara” (lord) and praise you?”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “Even those who consider themselves to be the lords, since it is apt for them, knowing your lordship and taking shelter of you is not at all surprising”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. maṟaiyāya nāl vēdattuḷ ninṟa malarc cudarē muṟaiyāl ivvulagellām  padaittidanduṇḍumiḻndaḷandāy piṟai ēṟu sadaiyānum nānmuganum indiranum iṟai ādal aṟindētta vīṟṟiruttal idu viyappē?*

- *maṟaiyāya* – śrī rangarāja stavam 1.19 “*ādau vēdā: pramāṇam smrutirupakurutē sētihāsai: purāṇair nyāyaissārdam tvadarcāvidimupari parikśīyatē pūrvabhāga: \| ūrdvō bhāgastvadīhāguṇavibhavaparijñāpanaistvatpadāptau vēdyō vēdaiśca sarvairahamiti bhagavan! svēna ca vyācakarta: \|\|*” (Oh [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)! vēdams are primary pramāṇam (authentic source of knowledge, without need for external validation). manu smruti is helping along with itihāsams and purāṇams, pūrva and uttara mīmāmsā. The karma kāṇḍa (pūrva bhāgam) reveals everything about how to worship you. The glorious uttara kāṇḍa (ūrdva bhāgam) leads to your divine feet by revealing your activities such as creation etc, the qualities that are required for such activities, the realms that are under your control etc. Also, you yourself have revealed \[in bhagavat gītā etc\] that you are only known through vēdam which is divided in to pūrva and uttara kāṇḍam). Here vēdam is highlighted by two words – maṟai (one that conceals) and vēdam (one that reveals) – this is because, for those who are outside vēdam without any faith in it, it hides itself and for those who are faithful, it reveals its meanings. pūrvā bhāgam (karma kāṇḍam) explains the process of worship and uttara bhāgam (uttara kāṇḍam) explains the nature of the object of worship (bhagavān). The lustre acquired due to being revealed by all of vēdam as said in bhagavat gītā 15.15 “*vēdaiśca sarvair ahamēva vēdya:*“. Oh one who is shining in the vēdams as the lord of everyone and has unsurpassed sweetness.
- *muṟaiyāl* … – vēdams explain that he is the protector of all.
- *muṟaiyāl* – two meanings – 1) relationship – due to him being the lord, 2) repeatedly in every cycle of creation. During deluge, when the [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) was devoid of karaṇa (body) and kaḷēbara (senses) and without any means to enjoyment in this world or for liberation, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) creates them \[i.e., gives the body, senses, ability to act etc\], assuming the form of mahāvarāham (great wild-boar/pig) and rescued the created world that was consumed by the causal ocean, protecting the world by keeping it safely in his stomach when there is a deluge again, then spitting it out again, when people like mahābali steals (claims) [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s wealth like an eagle plucking its prey, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) rescues the world from him by measuring it up to the boundary. Oh one who is protecting in so many ways like this! \[Here a question arises, is this not the karma which leads an [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) into a particular birth? why are these actions highlighted as favours to the [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)?\] The karma of the [cētana](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) is the viśēśa kāraṇam (special cause) that leads to the variegated bodies one may acquire. *yaugapadyam anugraha kāryam* \[But, the whole universe(s) is created at once out of [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s mercy on seeing the plight of [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)s without any body/senses\] – bhagavān is thus the sāmānya kāraṇam (common cause) for whole of creation.
- *piṟai ēṟu sadaiyānum* … – rudra who is having matted hair in the form of doing penance, yet, having the \[cool\] crescent moon on his head and being the prime enjoyer; brahmā who is the father of such rudra; indra who is \[having greatness to be\] counted along with those two; by them glorifying you and you manifesting your distinct nature due to that, is there anything great for you? Like a person making a doll, decorating it to look great, keeping his feet on its head and pridefully claiming “it vorśipped me”, like it is said in tiruvāimoḻi 7.5.4 “*nanmaip punal paṇṇi nānmuganaip paṇṇi*” (creating the good causal ocean and creating the brahmā), if brahmā who was created by you and these other dēvatās who are created by brahmā praise you and if you become proud about that, is there any greatness in it? would you not be a laughing-stock by doing this?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.1.11. Viyappaya viyappilla

*viyappāya viyappillā meyjñāna vēdiyanai sayap pugaḻār palar vāḻum tadam kurugūrc catakōpan tuyakkinṟit toḻuduraitta āyirattuḷ ippattum uyak koṇḍu piṟappaṟukkum oli munnīr jñālattē*

**Пословный перевод:**

viyappāya – surprising to see qualities, activities etc (when seen in others); viyappillā – nothing unusual (in bhagavān‘s case); mey jñānam – that which explains such true knowledge; vēdiyanai – one who is known through vēdams; sayam – jayam – victory (over samsāram (worldly bondage)) leading to; pugaḻār – one who has glories (such as jñānam (knowledge), vairājñam (detachment)); palar – many; vāḻum – living (enjoying āḻvār’s greatness); tadam – vast; kurugūr – leader of āḻvārtirunagari; śatakōpan – nammāḻvār; tuyakku – confusion of mind (in the form samśaya (doubt), viparyaya (error)); inṟi – without; toḻudu – rendering service (which is the natural act of true knowledge); uraitta – mercifully spoken; āyirattuḷ ippattum – this decad among the thousand pāsurams; oli – joyful noise; munnīr – having the ocean which has three types of water (river water, ground water and rain water); jñālattu – in the world; uyak koṇḍu – uplifting (by bestowing knowledge etc); piṟappu – relationship with \[further worldly\] births; aṟukkum – will eradicate

**Перевод:**

**emperumān in whom the amazing qualities etc are natural (nothing unusual) whereas in others it is surprising to see any qualities, activities etc; such emperumān is revealed by vēdams that shine due to being related to bhagavān and that which explain such true knowledge. nammāḻvār, who is the leader of āḻvārtirunagari, where many glorious personalities who have won over the worldly bondage, live enjoying greatness of nammāḻvār. This decad among the thousand pāsurams, which is mercifully spoken by such nammāḻvār without any confusion in his mind (in the form of doubt, error) and rendering service (which is the natural act of true knowledge). Such decad will uplift (by bestowing knowledge etc) those jīvātmās in this world which is having the ocean that makes joyful noise and that has three types of water (river water, ground water and rain water) and will eradicate the relationship with \[further worldly\] births.**

*No specific introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the end, āḻvār says “This decad will uplift those who learn it and also will eradicate the worldly sorrow”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār explains elimination of this worldly birth as the result of this decad.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. viyappāya viyappillā meyjñāna vēdiyanai sayap pugaḻār palar vāḻum tadam kurugūrc catakōpan tuyakkinṟit toḻuduraitta āyirattuḷ ippattum uyak koṇḍu piṟappaṟukkum oli munnīr jñālattē*

- *viyappāya viyappillā* – \[Those qualities, activities etc\] When observed in others, we will be surprised, but when seen in [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/), it will seem normal. When some one donates four (a few) cows in charity, it will make us wonder. But when we hear that “śrī rāma gave in charity”, it will sound quite normal. When śrī rāma was giving away wealth in charity and completed it, a brāhmaṇa named trijada arrived there, Since śrī rāma wondered what to give, he said “You throw your stick as far as possible, and I will give you cows fitting that distance”. The brāhmaṇa obliged and went away with so many cows \[that fit within the boundary\].
- *mey jñāna vēdiyanai* – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who has the greatness of being revealed by vēdam which speaks the truth as it is.
- *sayam* … – Like āḻvār himself who said in tiruviruttam 1 “*inninṟa nīrmai ini yām uṟāmai*” (I cannot bear this lowly life in this material realm), many śrīvaiṣṇavas live here enjoying āḻvār – [āḻvārtirunagari](http://azhwarthirunagari.koyil.org/) which is the vast abode that accommodates all such śrīvaiṣṇavas.
- *tuyakku inṟi* – tuyakku means confusion in mind. This decad which is among the thousand pāsurams, which was composed after āḻvār fully visualized the truth without any doubt, error.
- *oli munnīr jñālattē* – In this world which has the noisy ocean which has the three types of water, this decad will uplift those who were as said in taittiya upaniśat  “*asannēva sa bhavati*” (as good as non-existing) to become as in taittiya upaniśat “*santamēnam tatō vidu:*” (due to knowing brahmam, others know him to be existing) and will also eliminate the hurdles. Like when a kingdom becomes leaderless, \[if there were a prince who was imprisoned for some reason\] the prince would first be crowned and then his shackles will be broken, this decad would first engage one in kainkaryam at the divine feet of aḻagar [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) and then the bondage in this material world which is a hurdle for such kainkaryam, would be eliminated.

Finally, nampiḷḷai summarizes the contents of this decad briefly.

- In the [first pāsuram](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/06/thiruvaimozhi-2-10-1-kilaroli-ilamai/), [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) meditated upon the perfect match between aḻagar [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s divine ornaments and divine form.
- In the [second pāsuram](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/06/thiruvaimozhi-2-10-2-sadhirila-madavar/), he said “For such perfect match, those examples given by worldly people will only cause blemish to you”.
- In the [third pāsuram](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/06/thiruvaimozhi-2-10-3-payanalla-seydhu/), [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) said “forget about worldly people, why can’t you explain that?”, āḻvār replied “I won’t be able to completely explain that”.
- In the [fourth pāsuram](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/06/thiruvaimozhi-2-10-4-karumavan-pasam/),  “you, who is great and infinitely sweet, confused the worldly people so that they lose you”.
- In the [fifth pāsuram](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/06/thiruvaimozhi-2-10-5-thiramudai-valaththal/),  emperumān said “you are different from worldly people, why can’t you speak?” and āḻvār replied “You have transformed me to be different from worldly people, but you have not made yourself to be limited \[you are still unlimited\]”.
- In the [sixth pāsuram](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/06/thiruvaimozhi-2-10-6-kiriyena-ninaimin/), [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) said “why don’t you along with vēdams speak about me?” and āḻvār replied “Even vēdams cannot fully understand you”.
- In the [seventh pāsuram](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/06/thiruvaimozhi-2-10-7-nalamena-ninaimin/), emperumān said “Leave aside vēdams; there are some vaidika puruśas (those who are well-versed in vēdam). What is the problem in them glorifying me?” and āḻvār replied “Even that will cause blemish only to you”.
- In the [eighth pāsuram](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/06/thiruvaimozhi-2-10-8-valam-seydhu/), āḻvār said “even if we imagined a brahmā who is not in karma bhāvanā (engaging in worldly creation etc) and is fully in brahma bhāvanā (total devotion towards [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)), even such brahmā’s glorification would cause blemish only to you”.
- In the [ninth pāsuram](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/06/thiruvaimozhi-2-10-9-vazhakkena-ninaimin/),  āḻvār said “as we are not able to speak about his supremacy, is his simplicity easy to speak about?”.
- In the [tenth pāsuram](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/07/thiruvaimozhi-2-10-10-sudhenru-kalavum/), āḻvār said “īsn’t it a blemish if those who are created by brahmā who was created by you, glorify you?”.
- In the end, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) mercifully explained that, this decad by itself will give the ultimate result.

## 3.2 Munnir jnalam

## 3.2.1. Munnir jnalam

*munnīr jñālam padaitta em mugil vaṇṇanē anṇāḷ nī tanda ākkaiyin vaḻi uḻalvēn vennāḷ nōy vīya vinaigaḷai vēr aṟap pāyndu ennāḷ yān unnai ini vandu kūduvanē*

**Пословный перевод:**

munnīr – having 3 types of water; jñālam – universe; padaitta em mugil vaṇṇanē – created and because of such magnanimous act similar to that of dark clouds (that shower the rain irrespective of land or water), you became my saviour!; annāḷ – during the time of such sruśti (creation); nī – you; tanda – gave (to reach you); ākkaiyin – body’s; vaḻi – going in its ways (that adds bondage); uḻalvēn – me who is suffering (in garbha (womb), naraka (hell) etc); vem – that which leads to a pitiable state (after having acquired knowledge); nāḷ – in such day; nōy – diseases (in the form of ahankāram (considering oneself to be body), arta (worldly wealth), kāma (worldly pleasure) etc); vīya – to destroy; vinaigaḷai – karmas (which cause them); vēr – with its traces; aṟappāyndu – plucked and thrown away; yān – I (who used the senses which were supposed to be favourable towards you, against you); unnai – you (who is the primary saviour); ini – after being ungrateful; vandu – come (giving up this situation); kūduvan – unite; en nāḷ – when is that?

**Перевод:**

**Oh emperumān who created the universe that has 3 types of water and because of such magnanimous act similar to that of dark clouds (that shower the rain irrespective of land or water), you became my saviour! During the time of such sruśti (creation), having merciful heart, you gave me (to reach you) a body; but in such day when I have become pitiable having gone in such body’s ways (that adds bondage) and am suffering (in garbha (womb), naraka (hell) etc), for such me, plucking and throwing out my karmas with its traces, to destroy the diseases (in the form of ahankāram (considering oneself to be body), arta (worldly wealth), kāma (worldly pleasure) etc) which are caused by such karmas, after me being ungrateful, when will I (who used the senses that were supposed to be favourable towards you, against you) unite with you (who is the primary saviour)?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*First pāsuram – āḻvār cries out with grief saying “You gave me the body which is to be used to surrender unto you; but I have instead gone in its (bodily) ways and gone astray; when will I see you?”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*First pāsuram. āḻvār says “You have created this universe and bestowed me body and senses to worship you; I am using those for worldly pleasures and gone astray; you have to tell me, who is in this situation , as to when I will reach you”. munnīr jñālam padaitta em mugil vaṇṇanē anṇāḷ nī tanda ākkaiyin vaḻi uḻalvēn vennāḷ nōy vīya vinaigaḷai vēr aṟap pāyndu ennāḷ yān unnai ini vandu kūduvanē*

- *munnīr* – River water, ground water and rain water. As said in manu smruti 1.8 “*apa Eva sasarjādau*” (that supreme being first created water), first created water and then created the aṇḍa (universe containing 14 layers from brahma lōkam at the top till pātāḷa lōkam at the bottom).
- *jñālam padaitta* – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who created this universe with diverse forms. Seeing the [jīvātmās](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) in a helpless state, being overwhelmed by compassion, he created the universe thinking “let them acquire body and senses to be uplifted”.
- *em mugil vaṇṇanē* – Though [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) creates to help every one, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) considers it as “*madartam*” (for me). Like if a person performs great penances and brings the rains, many will reap the benefit, āḻvār thinks, because [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) created the universe for me, all the [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)s in the universe benefited too. āḻvār says “*mugil vaṇṇan*” (cloud like) to highlight the qualities of cloud such as helping everyone and helping without expecting anything in return.
- *an nāḷ* – That time when the [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) was without any body/senses, being covered by subtle matter (the state of matter during deluge) and being qualified to accept the mercy.
- *nī* – At that time, you who helped, since you consider it (the loss of ātmās) as your own loss as said in mahōpaniśat “*sa ēkāki na ramēta*” (he is not happy when being alone \[as the [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)s are in subtle state, without any means to express themselves, they are as good as non-existing\].
- *tanda* – you bestowed the body so that it can bow at your divine feet and attain you.
- *nī tanda* – bestowed by you, who is very compassionate. Instead of the ātmās requesting you, you yourself bestowed out of your compassion. The rarity of acquiring human body is explained in śrī bhāgavatam 11.2.28 “*durlabhō mānuśō dēha:*” (It is very difficult to acquire human body) etc. Why is this (act of bestowing bodies/senses) explained as a favour? Is creation not happening based on karma? Though creation happens based on karma as said in “*yaugapadyam anugraha kāryam*” (the whole universe(s) is created at once out of [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s mercy on seeing the plight of [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)s without any body/senses). śrīrangarāja stavam 2.41 “*acidaviśēśitān praḷayasīmani samsarata: karaṇakaḷēbararirgatayitum dayamānamanā: …*” (In the state of deluge, seeing the plight of cētanas (souls) who are as good as acētana (matter) \[due to lack of body/senses\], you, with compassionate heart, to bestow them body and senses, with your divine will, transformed the primordial (subtle) matter into gross forms such as mahān, ahankāram,  panca bhūtams etc). Like an emperor would release the prisoners on special occasions, you out of your mercy, blessed the souls with bodies and senses.
- *ākkaiyin vaḻi uḻalvēn* – You bestowed me the body with a particular intent; but I went with the ways of the body \[instead of following your will\]. [embār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/embar/) explained this as “When we are supposed to push the boat to reach [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) and enjoy him, like those who don’t understand the value of the boat and move along with the flow to end up in the ocean, I went along with worldly pleasures and caused disaster to self”.
- *vennāḷ* – Once knowledge about the true nature of the self is acquired, the time spent in this material realm would feel like sītā pirātti’s \[unbearable\] stay in lankā in separation from śrī rāma. For [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/), when in separation from [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/), it feels like he is being burnt – so he says “*vem nāḷ*” (hot day).
- *nōy* – birth \[birth itself is considered as a disease that is to be cured\]. śrī bharatāḻvān’s disease was unlike cāturtikam (a type of fever which is considered deadly that will kill very quickly), it is due to separation from śrī rāma \[which lasted for 14 long years\]; in the same manner, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s disease (of separation from [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)) is also well-known.
- *vīya* – to eradicate.
- *vinaigaḷai vēraṟap pāyndu* – śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 37.6 “*rākśasānām kśayam krutvā sūdayitvā ca rāvaṇam \| lankāmunmūlitām krutvā kadādrakśyati mām pati: \|\|*” (My husband śrī rām will cause destruction for the rākśasas, kill rāvaṇa and destroy lankā completely and will see me always” – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) too desires that his hurdles are eradicated like this – i.e., eradicating the avidyā (ignorance) etc along with their impressions, that cause the grief of separation. From “*pāyndu*“, we can understand the anger of āḻvār towards such hurdles. āḻvār is saying “How can I do this (eliminating hurdles) which can only be done by [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/), who is all capable?”.
- *ennāḷ* – I am not saying that “I want this now”. I will be happy if you tell me when you will bestow that to me. As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 127.1 “*pūrṇē caturdaśē varśē …*” (after completing 14 full years śrī rāma, elder brother of śrī lakśmaṇa arrived at bharadvāja maharishi’s āśramam on a pancami day and vorśipped the maharishi).
- *yān* – me who used the body and senses for worldly pleasures and inflicted this disaster on myself.
- *unnai* – You who can be requested to give a solution for the disaster I have caused upon myself.
- *ini* – After having destroyed the tools/mercy that was given by you.
- *ini vandu kūduvanē* – Previous [ācāryas](http://acharyas.koyil.org/) would explain this as [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) giving up thinking “Is it even possible to reach him?”. But [emperumānār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/emperumanar/) explains “āḻvār is of the nature that if he gives up, he will be finished. He would give up in ninth pāsuram and [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) will appear immediately and convince him in the tenth pāsuram”. So here āḻvār is saying “Tell me the day when you have arranged for me to reach you”.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.2.2. Vanma vaiyam

*vanmā vaiyam aḷanda em vāmanā! nin panmā māyap piṟaviyil padiginṟa yān tonmā valvinait todargaḷai mudalarindu nin mā tāḷ sērndu niṟpadu enjñānṟukolō*

**Пословный перевод:**

val – being tight due to firmness; mā – vast; vaiyam – world; aḷanda – measured (with your tender divine feet); em – made me exist fully for him by such act; vāmanā – Oh vāmana!; nin – for your sport; pal – variegated (due to the qualities and resulting forms); mā – very difficult to cross over; māyam – in prakruti (material realm) which is amazing; pal piṟaviyil – many different forms (such as dēva, manuśya etc); padiginṟa – living in a well fitting manner; yān – I; tol – since time immemorial; mā – countless; val – difficult to eradicate; vinai – sins; todargaḷai – chains; mudal – with their cause; arindu – cut them off; nin – your (who is apt to be attained); mā – having great glories (that are to be attained); tāḷ – divine feet; sērndu – reach; niṟpatu – stay there firmly (without moving away); enjñānṟu kol – when will that be?

**Перевод:**

**Oh vāmana who measured (with your tender divine feet) the tight (due to firmness) and vast world and made me exist for you fully by that act! I am living in a well fitting manner assuming many  different forms (such as dēva, manuśya etc) in prakruti (material realm) which is amazing, that is variegated (due to the qualities and resulting forms), is very difficult to cross over and that which exists for your sport. When will I cut off the countless chains of sins that are difficult to eradicate and that exist since time immemorial, reach your (who is apt to be attained) divine feet that are having great glories (that are to be attained) and stay there firmly (without moving away)?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In second pāsuram – āḻvār calls out for emperumān saying “I escaped from having your divine feet on my head when you touched everyone’s head without discriminating land/water; in such case, when will I reach your divine feet?”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār asks “You came to  take alms like a mendicant and won over the universe completely; when will I reach your exalted divine feet?”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Second pāsuram. emperumān says “If you are not coming to my place with your body and unite with me, when I assumed the form of vāmana and stood in front of mahābali; why did you not approach me there?”, āḻvār replies “I missed that opportunity also”. vanmā vaiyam aḷanda em vāmanā! nin panmā māyap piṟaviyil padiginṟa yān tonmā valvinait todargaḷai mudalarindu nin mā tāḷ sērndu niṟpadu enjñānṟukolō*

- *vanmā vaiyam aḷanda* – This world \[people of world\] was so hard that even when he himself came and manifested his beautiful form, it did not feel any emotion. It did not even have the tenderness of mahābali who is born in demoniac clan. He did not heed to the advice of śukrācārya et al \[to ignore vāmana\]. It is also explained as – due to the righteousness of mahābali, the world was difficult to be measured at that time. Another explanation – He measured the world which had harsh forests and mountainous terrains with his tender divine feet which are touched by the most tender [śrī mahālakśmi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/) and [bhūdēvi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/andal/) with utmost care. Here vanmai (hardness) is explained as the hard nature of the heart of materialistic people, the hard nature of earth and the “hard to enter” nature of the world that was due to being protected by mahābali’s strong shoulders.
- *em vāmanā* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) considers vāmanāvatāram is for [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) himself and not for indra who lost his kingdom.
- *nin* – What was said by [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) in śrī bhagavat gītā 7.14 “*mama māyā duratyayā*” (this material realm which is mine is difficult to cross over) has become true in my case.
- *pal mā māyam* – *māyam* means mūlaprakruti (primordial matter). Here variegated nature is – the resulting variegated forms is applied on the primordial matter which is the cause for the same. Alternatively, it can be explained as – since prakruti is the abode of three types of guṇas (satva, rajas, tamas), due to this difference in qualities, it can be explained as variegated.
- *pal piṟaviyil* – Due to the connection of prakruti (matter), ātmā assumes many different births.

In such births,

- *padiginṟa* – being submerged completely. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying “*padiginṟa*” (fitting well) instead of “*viḻuginṟa*” (falling into) because, the ātmā is happily living in these births without any discomfort. Due to padiginṟa being in present tense, it implies that the ātmā is submerging (like in a ocean without hitting the bottom).
- yān – me who is roaming in this material realm
- *tol mā* *val vinai* – the sins that have been present since the presence of ātmā (*tol* – without a beginning), inexhaustible even if the results of the sins are experienced (mā – great), very strong such that even if [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is to eradicate them, he needs to position himself firmly and eradicate them (val – strong) – eliminating such sins that are together, along with the traces.
- *todar* – chain
- *nin mā tāḷ sērttu* – attaining your divine feet that are most apt to be attained and are infinitely enjoyable.
- *niṟpadu* – The nitya samsāri (one who has been eternally bound in this material realm) surrendering unto [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is like placing heavy object on a leaf \[that was used to eat, considered impure\] so that it does not fly \[and spread its impurity\]. This is explained in taittiriya upaniśat “*ata sō ‘bhayangatō bhavati*” (thus \[by being firm in bhagavān\], he reaches the fearless state).
- *niṟpadu enjñānṟu kolō* – Let it be this day \[ennāḷ (which day) is considered as innāḷ (this day)\] . As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 24.37 “*apīdānīm sa kāla: syāt*” (kausalyā tells śrī rāma – let the day when I see you be this day). Alternatively, it is considered as a question – “which day will I firmly stay at your lotus feet?”.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.2.3. Kolla makkol

*kollā mākkōl kolai seydu bhāradap pōr ellāc cēnaiyum iru nilattavitta endāy pollā ākkaiyin puṇarvinai aṟukkalaṟā sollāy yān unnaic cārvadōr sūḻcciyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kollā – tool which is not meant to kill; mā – that which drives a horse; kōl – stick with thorn; kolai – killing; seydu – done; bhāradap pōr – in the mahābhārata yuddam (battle); ellāc cēnaiyum – all the armies (irrespective of them belonging to the enemies or pāṇḍavas, those who are causing burden to the earth); iru nilattu – in the vast land (of darmakśētra – the righteous place of kurukśētra); avitta – destroyed; endāy – my svāmy (lord and master)!; pollā – that which causes disaster; ākkaiyin – with the body; puṇarvinai – connection; aṟukkal – (if I tried) to cut off; aṟā – unable to do so; yān – me (who is caught in this); unnai – you (who can eliminate my hurdles); cārvadu – to reach; ōr – distinct; sūḻcci – method; sollāy – please tell (like you explained to arjuna)

**Перевод:**

**Oh my lord and master who destroyed all the armies (irrespective of them belonging to the enemies or pāṇḍavas, those who are causing burden to the earth) in the mahābhārata yuddam (battle) in the vast land (of darmakśētra – the righteous place of kurukśētra) with the thorny stick (as said in “mayaivaitē nihatā:“, purely through his will) which is meant to drive the horse and not to kill! even if I tried to cut off the connection with the body I am unable to do so; (like you explained to arjuna,) please tell me (who is caught in this) a distinct method to reach you (who can eliminate my hurdles).**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In third pāsuram – āḻvār says “You took birth as kriṣṇa to accept those who missed out when you appeared as vāmana; I missed out that opportunity as well; you have to find the ways for such person (me) to reach you”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “You who is capable of eliminating the enemies of your devotees, have to mercifully tell me a way through which I can reach you”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Third pāsuram. emperumān asks āḻvār “Since vāmanāvatāram happened in ancient times, and since you are after that time and have missed out the opportunity there, I descended as kriṣṇa, and obeyed the words of pāṇḍavas to protect the mangaḷasūtram of a lady (the ornament which identifies a married woman); can you not come and take shelter there?” and āḻvār replies “I missed out the opportunity there too”. kollā mākkōl kolai seydu bhāradap pōr ellāc cēnaiyum iru nilattavitta endāy pollā ākkaiyin puṇarvinai aṟukkalaṟā sollāy yān unnaic cārvadōr sūḻcciyē*

- *kollā* – When kriṣṇa was mercifully resting, duryōdana and arjuna arrived there to request for his help; duryōdana stayed at the side of kriṣṇa’s divine head and arjuna stayed at the side of kriṣṇa’s divine feet; when kriṣṇa woke up, he asked “How are the kings?” \[looking at arjuna\]; duryōdan says “I came first” and kriṣṇa replies “It is alright that you came first; but I saw arjuna first \[since he was standing at his divine feet\]” as said in mahābhāratam udyōga parvam 6 “*bhavānabhigata: pūrvamatra mē nāsti samśaya:…*” (I have not doubt that you came here first, but arjuna was seen by me first) and argues in favour of arjuna thus; then he enquires “what do you both need?” and both say “we need help for our battle”; hearing that, kriṣṇa says “Alright; one of you can have my army; and the other can have me”; Like those who think the actions themselves will bear fruits \[instead of knowing, [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) who is pleased/pained by actions will give the results\], duryōdan chose to accept kriṣṇa’s army and bhīśma, drōṇa et al condemned him for his mistake and instructed him to go back to kriṣṇa and request him not to take up arms during the battle; he comes back and asks “you should not take up arms” and kriṣṇa replies “Agreed. I won’t take up weapons”, and then uses his thorny stick which is used to drive the horse, to finish everyone \[simply by driving around the horse\].
- *bhāradap pōr* – in the battle of mahābhārata
- *ellāc cēnaiyum* – In both the armies, there were many evil persons. He finished all of them except a few here (pāṇḍavas) and a very few there (aśvattāmā, krupācārya et al).
- *iru nilattu* – the place where the battle happened was such a holy site that even if those who lost their lives did not have anything good in them, they would still reach heaven for their valour.
- *avitta* – dampened. When bhīśma et al came like forest fire to attack, he dampened them like a dark-cloud pouring heavy rain. His arrival is explained in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 3.4.1 as “*maḻaikolō varuginṟadu*” (is it rain that is coming?).
- *endāy* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) feels that whatever help done for pāṇḍavas back then is like help done to āḻvār himself.
- *pollā ākkai …* – This (body) is not as cool as those duryōdana et al who were killed by you \[it is more cruel than them\]. While it looks like it is favourable, in reality it is dangerous. It will create enjoyableness in it and will thus conceal the enjoyableness of [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/). When some one has many blemishes, the learned elders would consider him as downtrodden and give up on him. Similarly, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) considers all the blemishes of the body and says “*pollā ākkai*” (disastrous body). The sins sins that are combined with each other, that caused this body. *puṇarvinai* means the connection with such a body.
- *aṟukkalaṟā* – it will repeatedly reappear like rāvaṇa’s head \[everytime śrī rāma knocked off rāvaṇa’s head, it will grow again due to the mystical power rāvaṇa had; similarly the karmas are not easy to eliminate\].
- *sollāy* – You should mercifully tell me a method through which I can eliminate these karmas and reach you. If I know that method, I will try to escape \[and be bound still in this material realm\]. So, you have to find a method which I won’t know. But you also have to tell me \[so, I am pacified that I will escape\].
- *yān* – Like some one who is held in prison, me who is tied in this material realm.
- *unnai* – You who is enjoyed by the nityasūris in the special abode of śrīvaikuṇṭam.
- *cārvadōr sūḻcciyē* – Tell me a method to reach you. i.e., mercifully saying as in śrī bhagavat gītā 18.66 “*sarvapāpēbhyō mōkśayiśyāmi*” (I will make you relieved of all sins).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.2.4. Sulcci

*sūḻcci jñānac cudaroḷyāgi enṟum ēḻccik kēdinṟi engaṇum niṟainda endāy! tāḻcci maṟṟengu tavirndu nin tāḷiṇaik kīḻ vāḻcci yān sērum vagai aruḷāy vandē*

**Пословный перевод:**

sūḻcci – surrounding (everything); jñānac cudar – having the rays of knowledge; oḷiyāgi – being naturally self-effulgent; enṟum – at all times; ēḻcci – expansion; kēdu – contraction; inṟi – not having; engaṇum – everywhere; niṟainda – fully pervading; endāy – Oh the lord who accepted me (like surrounding a town to capture a single person)!; maṟṟu – except (you); engum – in all aspects; tāḻcci – engagement in; tavirndu – skipped; nin – your (apt); tāḷ – (enjoyable) divine feet; iṇai – two; kīḻ – underneath; vāḻcci – living such life (of being subservient to you); yān – I (who have not done this before); sērum – attaining; vagai – method; vandu – coming and standing (in front of me assuming a particular form); aruḷāy – mercifully tell me

**Перевод:**

**Oh the lord who accepted me (like surrounding a town to capture a single person) by fully pervading everywhere, having a self-effulgent form which is surrounded by rays of knowledge which are neither expanding nor contracting! Coming and standing (in front of me, assuming a particular form), please mercifully tell me  (who has not done this before) the method of attaining your (apt) two (enjoyable) divine feet and living such life underneath them, after skipping engagement in all aspects except you.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In fourth pāsuram – āḻvār says “Even your omnipresence which is for the protection of all, did not help me. You have to mercifully see that I attain you”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār say “You have to appear in front of me and tell me the method by which I can attain divine feet of you, who pervades everywhere to protect all”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*In fourth pāsuram – āḻvār says “Did I just miss out the opportunity during your incarnations? As said in śrī bhagavat gītā 10.10 “dadāmi buddiyōgam tam” (I give them the intellect), even when you enter in my heart which is the source of the thought process, to help me, I have not reaped the benefit”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Fourth pāsuram. emperumān asks “Even if you missed the opportunity, when I myself descend (by assuming various incarnations) to wherever you are, unlike those incarnations that stay only for a specific period of time, when I am present as in-dwelling super soul in the hearts of even those who don’t like me, why don’t you be favourable towards such antaryāmi emperumān and fulfill your desire?”, āḻvār says “I missed out the opportunity in there too”. sūḻcci jñānac cudaroḷyāgi enṟum ēḻccik kēdinṟi engaṇum niṟainda endāy! tāḻcci maṟṟengu tavirndu nin tāḷiṇaik kīḻ vāḻcci yān sērum vagai aruḷāy vandē*

- *sūḻcci …* – Since he catches the cētanas (jīvātmās) by his vyāpti (pervading), it is called sūḻcci (trick). Pervading everywhere, with well expanded radiant ray of knowledge. Here it (*jñānac cudaroḷiyāgi engum ēzccik kēdinṟi engaṇum niṟainda*) is explaining both the svarūpam of [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) which is the abode of knowledge and the knowledge itself. In bhagavān’s case both svarūpa vyāpti (his true nature being pervaded everywhere) and jñāna vyāpti (his knowledge being pervaded everywhere, i.e., he is cognizant of everything) can be explained \[In jīvātmā’s case, the ātmā does not physically pervade everywhere, only its knowledge is spread over certain scope\], since both are done for the sake of (helping) others.
- *enṟum ēḻccik kēdinṟi* – At all times, no expansion and contraction. There is no expansion/contraction based on karma (bondage). ēḻcci – expansion. kēdu – contraction.
- *engaṇum niṟainda* – Is he pervading in a single spot? No. It is everywhere. kaṇ – place. As said in tiruvāimoḻi 1.1.10 “*idam tigaḻ poruḷtoṟum karandu*” (hiding in all places), at all places in all entities. Like an entity will be pervaded by its category (for example, a cow has the “quality of being a cow” throughout its body), [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) completely pervades  everything.
- *endāy* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) considers his omnipresence is also for āḻvār himself as it is seen in an army surrounding a whole town to catch a single person. Even after you enter my heart to protect me, I, being attached to worldly pleasures, escaped you.
- *tāḻcci maṟṟu engum tavirndu* – Avoiding the disgrace that will be acquired by engaging in all aspects other than you. As said in tiruviruttam 95 “*yādānum paṟṟi*” (holding on to anything), for me to be attracted, your absence is the only thing that is needed.
- *nin tāḷ iṇaik kīḻ vāḻcci* – Service at your apt, infinitely enjoyable lotus feet. You have to mercifully show a new path to me. Though the attachment is same in both (spiritual matters and worldly matters), [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says one as “*tāḻcci*” (disgrace – worldly matters) and the other as “*vāḻcci*” (glory – spiritual matters). Attachment to worldly matters is explained in “*sarvam paravaśam dukkam*” (being subservient to others is sorrowful) and in manu smruti 4.6 “*sēvā śvavrutti:*” (to serve others is inferior); attachment to spiritual matters is ordained in mūla samhitā “*cāyāvā satvam anugaccēt*” (like a shadow following its owner). You have to mercifully explain me the ways to attain such glorious life for me who is born for such a life, yet have lost it so far.
- *vandē* – You cannot tell that without appearing in front of me; you have to come in front of me. You have to mercifully assume an incarnation specifically for me like you descended as śrī rāma, kriṣṇa et al.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.2.5. Vanday pole

*vandāy pōlē vandum en manattinai nī sindāmal seyyāy iduvē idu āgil kondār kāyāvin koḻumalart tiru niṟatta endāy! yān unnai engu vandu aṇugiṟpanē?*

**Пословный перевод:**

vandāy pōlē – as you came (for prahlāda, gajēndra); vandum – even if appeared; en – my (me who desired to approach you); manattinai – heart; nī – you (who helped when in danger); sindāmal – from becoming weak (thinking about the hurdles); seyyāy – not doing; iduvē – this (being unhelpful ); idu – your true nature; āgil – if it is; kondu – bunches; Ar – filled; kāyāvin – kāyām (flax – a bluish flower); koḻu malar – fresh flowers; tiruniṟatta – having such complexion; endāy – oh the master who won over me (by manifesting such beauty)!; yān – I (who cannot survive without your beauty); unnai – you (who showed this beauty); engu – where (how); vandu – come; aṇugiṟpan – will be able to approach?

**Перевод:**

**Even if you came and appeared as you came (for prahlāda, gajēndra), you (who helped when in danger) are not protecting my (me who desired to approach you) heart from becoming weak and if this (being unhelpful) is your true nature, Oh the master who won over me (by manifesting the beauty of) bunch of fresh kāyām (flax – a bluish flower) flowers! where (how) will I (who cannot survive without your beauty) be able to come and approach you (who showed this beauty)?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In fifth pāsuram – āḻvār says “If you yourself pursue me and sustain me, I don’t have to approach you with my intelligence. Also, this will ensure that I will not miss out on your ultimately enjoyable beauty”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Fifth pāsuram. emperumān tells āḻvār “You said ‘I should definitely come and bless you’; but this is difficult for me; once I descended and stayed for 11000 years (as śrī rāma); once I descended and stayed for 100 years (as kriṣṇa); it takes efforts for me to descend” and āḻvār replies “yes – you should come and bless me for some days like such incarnations; if that is not your divine desire, you should atleast appear for a few moments like you did for  the elephant (gajēndrāḻvān) and prahlādāḻvān and help me”. vandāy pōlē vandum en manattinai nī sindāmal seyyāy iduvē idu āgil kondār kāyāvin koḻumalart tiru niṟatta endāy! yān unnai engu vandu aṇugiṟpanē?*

- *vandāy pōlē vandum* – Not like appearing and staying only for a few days.
- *en manattinai nī* – You who knows exactly the state of my heart and how to sustain it; you who is capable of re-creating that which lost its stature.
- *sindāmal seyyāy* – you are not protecting it from melting it into a fluid state.

[āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying “*iduvē idu āgil … engu vandu aṇugiṟpan”* (if this is his nature, how can I approach him?).

- *iduvēn idu āgil* – If it happens that – without you my heart loses its shine and merely watching that (without helping) is your nature.
- *kondu Ar …* – If you are not going to help me, why did you show your beauty (and attracted me)? *kondārndu* – Oh one who showed your cool complexion which resembles that of bunch of fresh flax flowers and won over me!
- *yān* … – (*yān*) I, who does not have anything worthy in me to reach you; I, who knows the enjoyable nature of your divine form. (*unnai*) You who is having the form that will make others unable to sustain themselves in separation from you. You who presents yourself to others as said in muṇḍaka upaniśat 3.2.3 “… *tasyaiśa ātmā vivruṇutē tanūm svām*” (For such [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) who [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) pursues, he himself shows his true nature). What sādanam (means) will I perform and where (how) will I reach you? Is there even something like “I can reach you \[on my own efforts\]”.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.2.6. Kirpan killen

*kiṟpan killēn enṟilan muna nāḷāl aṟpa sārangaḷ avai suvaittu aganṟoḻindēn paṟpal āyiram uyir seyda paramā! nin naṟpoṟsōdit tāḷ naṇuguvadu enjñānṟē*

**Пословный перевод:**

muna nāḷ Al – in previous times; kiṟpan enṟu ilan – (if told to “do” – that is for the well-being) I will disagree saying ‘I am incapable’; killēn enṟu ilan – (if told to “refrain” – that it is not good to engage in evil activities) I will not avoid engaging in such activities; aṟpam – very insignificant; sārangaḷ – having attractions; avai – those diverse evil aspects; suvaittu – enjoyed them (wrongly thinking that they have real attraction); aganṟu oḻindēn – (due to that) I have gone far away \[from emperumān\]; pal pal – many many; āyiram – countless; uyir – types of life forms; seyda – able to create (as desired); paramā – oh one who has great ability!; nin – your (you who is apt master); nal – spiritual (not made of worldly matter); pon – very reliśable; sōdi – radiant; tāḷ – divine feet; naṇuguvadu – to attain; enjñānru – when?

**Перевод:**

**In previous times, (if told to “do” – that is for the well-being) I will disagree saying ‘I am incapable’; (if told to “refrain” – that it is not good to engage in evil activities) I will not avoid engaging in such activities; thus being, indifferent towards vidi and niśēdam, I enjoyed those diverse evil aspects that are having very insignificant attractions (wrongly thinking that they have real attraction) and (due to that) I have gone far away \[from emperumān\]. oh one who has great ability to create (as desired) many many countless types of life forms! When will I attain your (you who is apt master) spiritual (not made of worldly matter), very reliśable, radiant divine feet? Implies that, when highly capable you are present who can facilitate me attaining you, there is no way I \[who is insignificane/powerless\] can attain you \[independently\].**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In sixth pāsuram, āḻvār, due to attachment towards the goal, again asks “when will I attain your divine feet which are perfectly enjoyable?”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “When will I who moved away from you being attached to worldly pleasures since time immemorial, attain you who has infinite abilities?”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Sixth pāsuram. āḻvār says “Considering me, there is no way to reach him. Considering you, there is no way I can escape you \[your grace\]. This being the case, when will I reach your  perfectly enjoyable divine feet?”. \[Also explained as\] āḻvār saying “When will I who went astray being attached to worldly pleasures, Ignoring the vidi (do’s) and niśēdam (dont’s ) \[that are mentioned in śāstram\], attain your divine feet?”. kiṟpan killēn enṟilan muna nāḷāl aṟpa sārangaḷ avai suvaittu aganṟoḻindēn paṟpal āyiram uyir seyda paramā! nin naṟpoṟsōdit tāḷ naṇuguvadu enjñānṟē*

nampiḷḷai explains this as a conversation between [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) and [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/).

- *kiṟpan killēn enṟu ilan* – When [he](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) says “[āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)! in case of bhagavat viśayam (spiritual goals), nothing more than ‘iccā’ (desire)  is required; and the result is, ‘*apunarāvrutti lakśaṇa mōkśam*‘ (eternal joyful kainkaryam in paramapadam, with no return to sufferings in material realm) ; why can’t you do something \[advēśam – not having hatred towards [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/), ābhimukyam – being friendly towards [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/), etc\] for this?” and I would not say “Alright, I will do as you say”. When he says “Attachment to worldly pleasures, efforts are difficult to do and the results are not permanent. So, why don’t you refrain from engaging in such activities?” and I would not say “Alright, I will refrain from such aspects”.

When asked “Since when are you not following the orders and refraining from prohibited activities?”, āḻvār says,

- *muna nāḷāl* – Forever (since time immemorial), this is my way of life.

When asked, “Are there very attractive aspects that keep you away from me?”, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says,

- *aṟpa sārangaḷ* – Yes. There are some aspects which keep me away from you. There is nothing worthy in them. Like the honey in muḷḷi (a type of jasmine flower) which is very very little. There are many such aspects. I submerged into those aspects which have acquired taste \[not having natural taste\] and lost your highness as said in periya tirumoḻi 1.1.1 “*ōdinēn*” (ran).

When asked “If you had lost me for so long, what do you want me to do now?”, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says,

- *pal pal āyiram uyir seyda paramā!* – Creating life forms means – connecting [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) with [bodies](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/09/thathva-thrayam-achith-what-is-matter/) so that they have the ability to stand firm, move around, make progress etc. Oh one who created countless entities! if you can create entities that did not exist before \[here, as said before, the transformation of subtle matter to gross matter and connecting that gross matter with ātmā is highlighted as creating entities that did not exist before\], is it difficult for you to bless me with a quality \[to have attachment towards you\]?
- *nin* … – When will I come and attain your beautiful, attractive, radiant divine feet?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.2.7. Enjnanru

*enjñānṟum nām irundirundu irangi nenjē! mey jñānam inṟi vinai iyal piṟappaḻundi enjñānṟum engum oḻivaṟa niṟaindu ninṟa mey jñānac cōdik kaṇṇanai mēvudumē*

**Пословный перевод:**

nenjē! – Oh heart!; enjñānṟum – always; irundu irundu – being; irangi – grieving (due to desire for the goal); mey jñānam – true knowledge (which is the tool for attaining such goal); inṟi – not having; vinai – due to the sins (that are the hurdles for attaining such goal); iyal – leading to; piṟappu – births; aḻundi – trapped; nām – we (who have this as the routine); enjñānṟum – all times; engum – in all entities; oḻivaṟa – without leaving anything; niṟaindu – fully pervading; ninṟa – stayed; mey jñānam – eternal knowledge; sōdi – having radiance of; kaṇṇanai – kriṣṇa (who appeared to be easily approachable by his devotees); mēvudumē – when will we reach?

**Перевод:**

**Oh heart! We are having the routine of always grieving (due to desire for the goal), without having the true knowledge (which is the tool for attaining such goal) and due to the sins (that are the hurdles for attaining such goal) that lead to births; when will (such) we  reach kriṣṇa (who appeared to be easily approachable by his devotees) who is fully pervading at all times in all entities without leaving anything and is having the radiance of eternal knowledge?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In seventh pāsuram – āḻvār pacifies his heart which is longing, with grief, thinking about the enjoyable nature of emperumān‘s divine feet saying “if we, who are unqualified, desire for him, is there any benefit in that?”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “Though the all pervading emperumān is easily approachable, if we have no means to attain the goal, can we attain him?”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Seventh pāsuram. On thinking about the enjoyable nature of the divine feet on reciting “nin naṟpoṟcōdittāḷ” (your beautiful enjoyable radiant divine feet), āḻvār‘s divine heart starts longing for it with great grief; seeing that, āḻvār says “Without knowing your nature, if you desire for something good, would you achieve it?”. enjñānṟum nām irundirundu irangi nenjē! mey jñānam inṟi vinai iyal piṟappaḻundi enjñānṟum engum oḻivaṟa niṟaindu ninṟa mey jñānac cōdik kaṇṇanai mēvudumē*

- *enjñānṟum …* – What is the use even if cry greatly life after life?
- *nenjē!* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says to his heart “Don’t you know you? Previously, were you not always the cause for bondage?” and the heart replies “But, why should we not attain the goal? Is a slightly favourable attitude \[towards [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)\] sufficient to attain the goal?”.
- *mey jñānam inṟi vinaiy iyal piṟappu aḻundi* – īsn’t this our previous state? We don’t have true knowledge. As said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 6.5.87 “*tadjñānam ajñānamatō ‘nyaduktam*” (that knowledge which leads to brahmam is true knowledge, all other knowledge are as good as ignorance), “*vidyānyā śilpanaipuṇam*” (Other knowledge are like mundane skills which are useless for self/god realization) – we had some knowledge but we do not have true knowledge. Did we just lack true knowledge? Our state is such that we are assuming births that will lead to sins and again be trapped in bondage.
- *enjñānṟum engum oḻivaṟa niṟaindu ninṟa* – pervading at all times in all entities without missing even a single entity.
- *mey jñānac cōdik kaṇṇanai* – Are we trying to reach some one who does not know our situation? Though [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) is eternal, its knowledge is subject to expansion and contraction. Unlike that, kriṣṇa is the one who has radiant true knowledge \[at all times\]; as said by śakuntalā towards duśyanta in mahābhāratam sambhava parvam 38.29 “*ēkō’hamasmīti ca manyasē tvam…* ” (You think I am alone here, forgetting that [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is present everywhere and you are committing sins in his presence).
- *nenjē! mey jñānac cōdik kaṇṇanai mēvudumē –* Two explanations for kaṇṇan (sulabhan (easily approachable), nirvāhakan (controller)) Should we try to reach him thinking that he is easily approachable? Can we reach kriṣṇa who is the controller?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.
