## 3.2.8. Mevu tunba

*mēvu tunba vinaigaḷai viduttum ilēn ōvudal inṟi un kaḻal vaṇangiṟṟilēn pāvu tol sīrk kaṇṇā en paranjudarē! kūvuginṟēn kāṇbān engu eydak kūvuvanē?*

**Пословный перевод:**

mēvu tunbam – having inseparable sorrows; vinaigaḷai – sins; viduttum ilēn – did not give up (by engaging in tapa (penance), jñāna (knowledge), sama (good qualities) etc); ōvudal inṟi – constantly; un – your (the apt you); kaḻal – divine feet; vaṇangiṟṟilēn – did not worship (as said in tiruvāimoḻi 1.3.5 “vaṇakkudait tavaneṟi”); pāvu – pervaded (everywhere); tol – natural; sīr – having qualities (for protection \[of his devotees\]); kaṇṇā – being kriṣṇa; en – for me whose desires are triggered by; param sudarē – oh one who is having infinitely radiant form!; kāṇbān – to see; kūvuginṟēn – crying out (like those who engaged in various processes and called out for you since you did not appear even after such efforts); engu – where; eyda – to reach; kūvuvan – will I call?

**Перевод:**

**I did not give up  (by engaging in tapa (penance), jñāna (knowledge), sama (good qualities) etc) sins that cause inseparable sorrows; I did not constantly worship (as said in tiruvāimoḻi 1.3.5 “vaṇakkudait tavaneṟi”) your (the apt you) divine feet; Oh one who is having infinitely radiant form which triggers my desires, by being kriṣṇa with natural qualities (for protection \[of his devotees\]) that have pervaded (everywhere)!  I am crying out (like those who engaged in various processes and called out for you since you did not appear even after such efforts) to see you; where will I call to reach you?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In eighth pāsuram – āḻvār says “Though I have no means to attain you, I am crying out for you to see you; How am I going to have my desire fulfilled?”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār meditating upon emperumān‘s divine qualities, forms and radiance which are a result of his saulabhyam (simplicity of being born as kriṣṇa) says “How can I, who has nothing in me, call out for you to see you?”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Eighth pāsuram. āḻvār is saying “How can I, who has no qualification matching the result to be attained, call out and attain the goal, like those who are engaged in certain means/process to attain a result would call out if their results are delayed?”. mēvu tunba vinaigaḷai viduttum ilēn ōvudal inṟi un kaḻal vaṇangiṟṟilēn pāvu tol sīrk kaṇṇā en paranjudarē! kūvuginṟēn kāṇbān engu eydak kūvuvanē?*

- *mēvu* – Sins that cause inseparable sorrows for the ātmā as said in [śrīranga gadyam](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/02/sriranga-gadhyam/) “*tilatailavat dāruvahnivat*” (like oil inside sesame seed and fire inside firewood). I did not eliminate such sins by engaging in ordained activities as said in taittiriya upaniśat “*darmēṇā pāpamapanudati*” (by engaging in righteous acts, he eliminates the sins).
- *ōvudal inṟi un kaḻal vaṇangiṟṟilēn* – I did not look out for the means to visualize you by engaging in constant meditation as said in bruhadāraṇya upaniśat 4.5 “*nididyāsitvya:*” (to be meditated upon). [embār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/embar/) would explain this as “***ōvudalinṟi*** *mēvu tunba vinaigaḷai viduttumilēn*” (I did not constantly try to give up sinful activities) and “***ōvudalinṟi*** *un kaḻal vaṇangiṟṟilēn*” (I did not constantly try to worship your divine feet). Like a newly wed girl would not even have time for food (she will be constantly pursued by her husband), I lived by feeding my sense organs well and never looked after my well-being.
- *pāvu tol sīrk kaṇṇā* – This being the case, once I meditated upon you, I am unable to leave you. Oh kriṣṇa who is popular for your natural auspicious qualities even in opposing groups as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 21.20 “*vidita:*” (śrī rāma is well known as one who is well situated in dharma (specifically śaraṇāgati darmam) …)!
- *en param sudarē* – Oh one who revealed your greatness in all aspects!
- *kaṇṇā en param sudarē* – Also explained as – Oh one who made yourself available as very humble kriṣṇa and let me fully enjoy your beauty! It is said in tiruvāimoḻi 6.3.7 “*param cudar udambāy*” (having radiant form).
- *kūvuginṟēn kāṇbān* – Those who engage in specific means \[like karma yōga, jñāna yōga, bhakti yōga etc\] and still not attain, will call out for you when their goal is not attained. Similarly I am calling you \[without engaging in any such means\].
- *engu eydak kūvuvanē* – Would a mosquito’s call be heard in brahmā’s assembly? How I am going to make you come by my crying out?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.2.9. Kuvik kuvi

*kūvik kūvik koduvinait tūṟṟuḷ ninṟu pāviyēn pala kālam vaḻi tigaittu alamaruginṟēn mēvi anṟu ānirai kāttavan ulagamellām tāviya ammānai enginit talaip peyvanē?*

**Пословный перевод:**

kodu – cruel; vinai – source for sins; tūṟṟuḷ – being caught in the quagmire (samsāram – material realm, where one cannot escape from); ninṟu – staying here; pala kālam – for long time; vaḻi – way (to escape); tigaittu – being confused; alamaruginṟēn – toiled (in such situation); pāviyēn – me who is very sinful; anṟu – back when (you helped by giving sticks to the covherd boys to herd the cows); mēvi – with full heart (instead of just to accomplish the task); ānirai – cows; kāttavan – you who protected; ulagamellām – towards all worlds (unlike limiting to a single place \[like in kriṣṇāvatāram\]); tāviya – you who performed the act of traivikrama (being victorious over the three worlds); ammānai – sarva svāmy (the master of all); ini – after missing out back then; kūvik kūvi – crying out again and again with great grief; engu – where; talaip peyvan – will I reach?

**Перевод:**

**Being very sinful, I am being confused about the way (to escape), toiling and staying here for a long time, being caught in the quagmire (samsāram – material realm, where one cannot escape from) which is the source for cruel sins; I (who is in such situation) missed out on the grace of you back then (when you helped by giving sticks to the covherd boys to herd the cows), when you protected the cows with full heart (instead of just to accomplish the task) and when you, who is the master of all, performed the act of traivikrama (being victorious over the three worlds) towards all worlds (unlike limiting to a single place \[like in kriṣṇāvatāram\]); In such case, by crying out again and again with great grief, where will I reach you?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In ninth pāsuram – āḻvār says “I missed out on your great favours as bestowed in the form of kriṣṇa and śrī vāmana; is there anything like me attaining you any more?” and becomes hopeless.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “After missing out on your favours for both the wise and the ignorant without discrimination, how will I attain the goal?”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Ninth pāsuram. āḻvār asks “Is there anything like me attaining you any more after having missed the opportunity when you descended in incarnations that were helping everyone without discrimination?”. kūvik kūvik koduvinait tūṟṟuḷ ninṟu pāviyēn pala kālam vaḻi tigaittu alamaruginṟēn mēvi anṟu ānirai kāttavan ulagamellām tāviya ammānai enginit talaip peyvanē?*

- *kūvi* – Having understood the true nature of [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) \[being fully dependent on [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s will\], [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) would cry out for [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) from this material realm instead of calmly waiting for him to come and help him.
- *kūvi* – Instead of stopping and atoning after crying out once \[for not being calm knowing one’s dependence on [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘\], he will cry out again and again.
- *kodu vinait tūṟṟuḷ ninṟu* – Staying in the material realm, where even if [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) extends his hand to help on hearing [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s cry, the place is so deep that emperumān needs to keep extending his hand, and crying out from such place.
- *pāviyēn* – Did I cry out being in the proximity of vālmeeki \[I am so sinful that I don’t have the shelter of any saintly person\]?
- *pala kālam vaḻi tigaittu alamaruginṟēn* – I who have been suffering all along, due to ignorance.
- *mēvi* … – Am I suffering due to not having someone who would not help those who are suffering? As said in  śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 4.11.13 “*gōgōpījanasangulam atīvārtam*” (for the suffering cows, covherd boys and girls) the lord looked at the suffering of cows and covherds and ensured that not a single drop of rain fell on them by lifting up the hill that was in front of him.
- *mēvi* – When bhagavān who is the lord of nityasūris (eternally free souls of paramapadam) was given a stick and asked to tend cows, instead of thinking it was something ordained, he would think that it is a great fortune to be tending cows and would engage in it with great love.
- *anṟu* – what a time it was!
- *vaḻi tigaittu alamaruginṟēn – mēvi anṟu ānirai kāttavan* – Like the one who showed the directions for those covherds who were lost in the forest. He is the one who showed the path in [śrī bhagavat gītā](http://githa.koyil.org/) 18.66 “*māmēkam śaraṇam vraja*” (accept me as the only refuge). He will not show any other path. Standing on the chariot, he showed the path for uplifting all [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)s.
- *ulagam …* – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who declared himself as the lord of all by keeping his divine feet on everyone/everything instead of just helping one town \[unlike in kriṣṇāvatāram, where emperumān only helped āyarpādi (gōkulam), in śrī vāmanāvatāram, he helped everyone\].
- *engu init talaip peyvanē* – How am I going to reach him? After having missed such “*dūḷi dānam*” (favour in the form of the dust of his lotus feet – which is an easy way to reach him), will I be able to reach him by undergoing any test? [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is asking “After having missed out on the opportunity when he himself came and helped, how am I going to engage in any sādanam (karma yōgam, jñāna yōgam, bhakti yōgam etc) and reach him?” and becoming hopeless.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.2.10. Talaippey kalam

*talaip pey kālam naman tamar pāsam vittāl alaippūṇ uṇṇum avvallal ellām agalak kalaip pal jñānatten kaṇṇanaik kaṇḍu koṇḍu nilaip peṟṟen nenjam peṟṟadu nīduyirē*

**Пословный перевод:**

naman tamar – the servitors of yama; talaip pey kālam – in the last moments; pāsam – rope; vittāl – throw; alaippūṇ – being tortured; uṇṇum – such as experiencing it (due to seeing enemies); a – that; allal ellām – sorrows; agala – to eliminate; pal – many types of; kalai – vēdams; jñānam – having known; en – \[emperumān\] who is easily approachable by me; kaṇṇanai – kriṣṇa; kaṇḍu koṇḍu – having seen; en nenjam – my heart (which is broken); nilai – stability; peṟṟu – acquired; uyir – ātmā (which was going to be finished due to grief); nīdu – eternity; peṟṟadu – acquired

**Перевод:**

**In the last moments, when the servitors of yama throw their rope and will torture \[the ātmā\], that will lead to experiencing great sorrows (due to seeing enemies – i.e, the servitors of yama); after seeing kriṣṇa who is known by many types of vēdam, eliminating such sorrows, my broken heart acquired stability and the ātmā (which was going to be finished due to grief) acquired eternity.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In tenth pāsuram – āḻvār becomes hopeless and is unable to survive the grief; seeing that emperumān manifests his divine form in tirumalā (tiruvēnkatam) to āḻvār’s total satisfaction and makes āḻvār sustain himself.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, kriṣṇa seeing āḻvār hopelessness in “engu init talaip peyvan” (How I am I going to attain the goal?), manifests his form in well known vicinity where he is present to help the people of future generation \[in the form of deity in a temple\] and āḻvār having his sorrows removed becomes satisfied.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Tenth pāsuram. Seeing āḻvār‘s hopeless state, emperumān thinking that “āḻvār cannot wait patiently for the result” says “Knowing you are greatly desirous, I am standing in north tirumalā specifically for you” to sustain him and āḻvār becomes pleased by sustaining himself. talaip pey kālam naman tamar pāsam vittāl alaippūṇ uṇṇum avvallal ellām agalak kalaip pal jñānatten kaṇṇanaik kaṇḍu koṇḍu nilaip peṟṟen nenjam peṟṟadu nīduyirē*

- *talaip pey kālam naman tamar* – talaip pey kālam – the time when the servitors of yama reach us \[to take our life\]. When one was alive and engaging in whatever sins he liked, they will keep noting them down and will arrive and manifest themselves when one is about to reap the fruits of their activities.
- *pāsam vittāl* – when they throw the ropes from their hands towards such a person in his last moments \[to strangle him and pull him\]
- *alaippūṇ uṇṇum* – There is no end to their suffering, as the [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) will try to pull the rope towards his side since he likes his mundane life and the servitors of yama will pull the rope towards their side.
- *avvallal ellām agala* – “*avvallal*” can only be said as “that suffering” – there is no example to explain that suffering. Will these be applicable for śrīvaiṣṇavas as there are certain pramāṇams which say that it is not applicable for śrīvaiṣṇavas? [embār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/embar/) explains that these sufferings \[of [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)\] are similar to [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)s suffering in the hands of the servitors of yama. i.e., the sufferings in separation from [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is the same as the sufferings of [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)‘s final moments. Alternatively – [āṇḍān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/mudhaliyandan/) explains this as – once we have not attained [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/), naturally we will end up with the servitors of yama – to eliminate such sorrows.
- *kalai* … – As said in śrī bhagavat gītā 15.15 “*vēdaiśca sarvair ahamēva vēdya:*” (from all of vēdams, I am only known), having the glories of being known from many \[parts of\] vēdams; instead of being in too far away place and only heard from pramāṇams (śāstrams), having seen his appearance as kriṣṇa.
- *nilaip peṟṟu en nenjam* – The heart that was said in tiruvāimoḻi 3.2.5 “sindāmal seyyāy” (you are not protecting my heart from being broken), also became stable somehow.
- *uyir nīdu peṟṟadu* – That [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) which is explained in [śrī bhagavat gītā 2.24](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/2-24/) as “*accēdyō ’yam adāhyō*” (This ātmā cannot be cut, burnt) was going to be finished. Only now, it acquired permanence. But is there destruction for [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) which is eternal while it is explained as “*cēdyādi visajātīyam*” (distinguished category which cannot be cut etc)? There is no destruction to [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s qualities which can enter subtly into the ātmā and destroy it \[by fully taking over the ātmā\]. Destruction for the eternal ātmā is dāsya asiddi (not having servitude). When śēśatvam (being a servitor) is the true identity of ātmā, there is no identity other than this.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.2.11. Uyirgal ella

*uyirgaḷ ellā ulagamum udaiyavanaik kuyil koḷ sōlait ten kurugūrc catakōpan seyiril sol isai mālai āyirattuḷ ippattum uyirin mēl ākkai ūnidai oḻivikkumē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ellā uyirgaḷ – all living beings; ellā ulagamum – all worlds; udaiyavanai – one who owns; kuyil koḷ – having cuckoos; sōlai – having gardens; then – beautiful; kurugūrc catakōpan – mercifully spoken by nammāḻvār who is the leader of āḻvārtirunagari; seyir – poetic defects; il – without; sol – having words; isai – with music/tune; mālai – having garland; āyirattuḷ – among the thousand; ippattum – this decad; uyirin mēl – that which is unnatural and cause of bondage for the ātmā; Un ākkai idai – from the body which is made of flesh etc; oḻivikkum – will free

**Перевод:**

**āḻvārtirunagari is the place that has gardens that have cuckoos in them; nammāḻvār who is the leader of such āḻvārtirunagari mercifully spoke about the one who owns all living beings and worlds, with words that have no poetic defects and music/tune in a garland of thousand pāsurams; among such thousand pāsurams, this decad will free the ātmā from the \[material\] body which is unnatural, cause of bondage for the ātmā and made of flesh etc.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the end, āḻvār says that those who learn this decad would not suffer like him and would be freed from bondage.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār mercifully explains the elimination of bodily connection that he desired for, as the result of this decad.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*In the end, āḻvār says that this decad will cut off the bodily connection for those who practice it. uyirgaḷ ellā ulagamum udaiyavanaik kuyil koḷ sōlait then kurugūrc catakōpan seyiril sol isai mālai āyirattuḷ ippattum uyirin mēl ākkai ūnidai oḻivikkumē*

āḻvār said “[*nilaip peṟṟu en nenjam peṟṟadu nīduyir*](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/07/thiruvaimozhi-3-2-10-thalaippey-kalam/)” (My broken heart became stable and my ātmā became permanent) when [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) appeared in front of him to relieve him from all his sorrows; But looking at emperumān’s face, it looked like, it was his ātmā that became permanent \[after satisfying nammāḻvār\].

- *uyirgaḷ* … – Only after [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) sustaining himself, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) became the owner of all worlds and living beings; emperumān would have only lost āḻvār; but āḻvār would have lost emperumān who is the owner of both spiritual and material realms. Even if one part is lost, he becomes incomplete. Thus, only after having āḻvār, his lordship/supremacy acquired completeness.
- *kuyil* … – After the prakāri (bhagavān – object) survives, nammāḻvār who is the prakārabhūtar (ātmā – a form, mode, attribute) survives, āḻvartirunagari too survives, the gardens that are present there also survive,  the joyful sounds of the birds that live in those gardens are heard. It happened as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 127.17 and 127.18 “*akālapaliṇō vrukśā:…*” (śrī rāma requests bharadvāja riśi – Oh bharadvāja bhagavān! When we reach ayōdya, on our way, let the trees blossom even during non-season and give us fruits and honey-giving-flowers).
- *seyir il sol* … – A literary garland made of words and tunes without any defect. These words are not focussed on suggesting us to tactfully work with the bodily connection or continue to lead the life conveniently even when don’t achieve bhagavān. If the actions don’t match “[*engu init talaip peyvan*](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/07/thiruvaimozhi-3-2-9-kuvik-kuvi/)“, that will be a defect.

When asked “What does this decad do?”,

- *uyirin mē ūnidai ākkai oḻivikkumē* – Like a prince and hunter were placed together \[when a prince gets lost in the forest and a hunter picks him up and raises him, they develop a bondage, though it is unnatural and when the king finds out about the prince, he will someday reinstate him as the prince, breaking the bondage between the hunter and prince\], [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) which is eternal, having jñānam (knowledge) and ānandam (bliss) as its identity and being subservient to [īsvara](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) and [acit](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/09/thathva-thrayam-achith-what-is-matter/) which constantly changes are together bonded by avidyā (ignorance) etc; Such ignorance will be eradicated along with its traces. It is not that, āḻvār still has igorance and it will be removed now. When he says “[*pollā ākkaiyin puṇarvinai aṟukkalaṟā*](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/07/thiruvaimozhi-3-2-3-kolla-makkol/)“, it is due to the repeated remembrance of the dangers of this material realm; when āḻvār said in tiruviruttam 1 “*inninṟa nīrmai ini yām uṟāmai*“, [īsvaran](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) decided to remove all his hurdles. Still, there should be some result for his crying out; for that, it is explained that the hurdles of those who are related to āḻvār will be removed.

Finally, nampiḷḷai summarizes the contents of this decad briefly.

- In the first pāsuram, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) said “How will I reach you after using the senses you gave me in causing disaster to myself?”.
- In the second pāsuram, he said “When will I reach your highness after eliminating these sins that have surrounded me?”.
- In the third pāsuram, he said “It is not possible to eliminate the sins myself after myself surrounding me with those sins with the senses you have given me. So, you have to find a means that I dont’t know, but you know and tell me that”.
- In the fourth pāsuram, he said “You have to eliminate my attachment towards lowly aspects which are different from you and you have to bring me glories by being attached to your divine feet”.
- In the fifth pāsuram,  he said “if you were not going to do that \[uplift me\], why did you reveal your greatness to me?”.
- In the sixth pāsuram, he said “what is so great about creating the ātmā \[i.e., giving it body and senses\]? now, you have to bestow the qualities \[that are required to reach you\]”.
- In the seventh pāsuram, he said “What is the use of blaming him without knowing our own position?”.
- In the eighth pāsuram, he said “Have I engaged in any great means to cry out for you like this?”.
- In the ninth pāsuram,  āḻvār said “How am I going to achieve him after missing him during traivikrama incident \[where he touched everyone’s head with his divine feet\]?”.
- In the tenth pāsuram, at that stage, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) manifests himself in front of āḻvār and sustains him.
- In the end, he explains the result and concludes the decad.

[āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) tiruvadigaḷē śaraṇam  
[emperumānār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/emperumanar/) tiruvadigaḷē śaraṇam  
[piḷḷān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/pillan/) tiruvadigaḷē śaraṇam  
[nanjīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nanjiyar/) tiruvadigaḷē śaraṇam  
[nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/) tiruvadigaḷē śaraṇam  
[vadakkut tiruvīdip piḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadakku-thiruvidhi-pillai/) tiruvadigaḷē śaraṇam  
[periyavāccān piḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/periyavachchan-pillai/) tiruvadigaḷē śaraṇam  
[vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/) tiruvadigaḷē śaraṇam  
[jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/mamunigal/) tiruvadigaḷē śaraṇam

In the next article we will enjoy the next decad.

## 3.3 Olivil kalam

## 3.3.1. Olivil kalam

*oḻivil kālam ellām udanāy manni vaḻuvilā adimai seyya vēṇḍunām teḻikural aruvit tiruvēnkatattu eḻilkoḷ sōdi endai tandai tandaikkē*

**Пословный перевод:**

teḻikural – making great noise; aruvi – having waterfalls; tiruvēnkatattu – in tirumalā tiruvēnkatam; eḻil – beauty; koḷ – having; sōdi – having fully radiant form; endai tandai tandaikku – to the leader of our clan of successive ancestors; nām – we (who are distinguished servants); oḻivil – without break/rest; kālamellām – all times; udanāy – being together (in all places); manni – being inseparable (in all forms); vaḻuvilā – without leaving anything; adimai – all types of services; seyya vēṇḍum – should perform

**Перевод:**

**We should perform all types of services without leaving anything at all times without break/rest, being together (in all places), being inseparable (in all forms) to the leader of our clan of successive ancestors, that is, tiruvēnkatamudaiyān (śrīnivāsan) who is having a fully radiant form and is beautiful due to being present in tirumalā tiruvēnkatam which is having waterfalls that are making great noise.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In first pāsuram – āḻvār says “should engage in all types of kainkaryams to tiruvēnkatamudaiyān“.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*In first pāsuram – āḻvār longs along with those who are related to him to engage in all types of services to tiruvēnkatamudaiyān who is the lord and greater than all.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*In first pāsuram – āḻvār says “At all places all times and in all forms, should engage in service at the divine feet of tiruvēnkatamudaiyān”. oḻivil kālam ellām udanāy manni vaḻuvilā adimai seyya vēṇḍunām teḻikural aruvit tiruvēnkatattu eḻilkoḷ sōdi endai tandai tandaikkē*

- *oḻivil kālamellām* – endless time \[i.e., for eternity\]. Some would extrapolate “*oḻivil kālamellām*” as “[āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) desiring for even the past times”. That is – there is no way lost time can be retrieved.  The only possible option is to make one forget about what has happened in the past as said in cāndōjña upaniśat “*nōpajanam smaran*” (ātmā will not contemplate about the material realm after reaching the spiritual realm). Also seen in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 5.5 “na mē dukkam … *vayōsyā hyativartatē*” (My biggest sorrow is … sītā’s age is passing by without being enjoyed \[by me (śrī rāma)\]) etc. Thus, this should be understood as all times in the future. \[this highlights service at all times\]
- *udanāy* – Like he desired to be present at all times, he also desires to be present at all places. Like iḷaiya perumāḷ (lakśmaṇa) served \[sītā – rāma\] in the palace as well as forest. \[this highlights service in all places\]
- *manni* – Even when [sarvēśvaran](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) and [pirātti (śrī mahālakśmi)](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/) draw down their curtains and enjoy in private, one should desire to be in the form of a vessel, lamp etc that are engaged in their confidential service. In this – service in all forms/states is highlighted. It is said in śrī rāmāyaṇam bāla kāṇḍam 1.31 “*ramamāṇā vanē traya:*” (all 3 – śrī rāma, sītā and lakśmaṇa enjoyed together in the forest); Why is lakśmaṇa associated with a share of the enjoyment, when it was really [sītā](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/) and [śrī rāma](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) enjoyed? It is because, whatever joy they get by enjoying together, one who witnesses that would also acquire the same joy.
- *oḻivil kālam* … – This speaks about sarva kālam (all times), sarva dēśam (all places) and sarva avastā (all forms/states). Whenever [āḻvār tiruvarangapperumāḷ araiyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/thiruvarangapperumal-araiyar/) starts singing this pāsuram, he would keep singing “*oḻivil kālamellām, kālamellām, kālamellām*” and would stop at that \[being overwhelmed with emotions\].
- *vaḻuvilā adimai seyya vēṇḍum* – one’s service cannot be shared with others. Should serve like iḷaiya perumāḷ (lakśamaṇa) who went along with śrī rāma and served him in the forest without separating; should also perform the kainkaryams done by śrī bharatāḻvān who stayed behind in the capital (ayōdyā). When kaikēyi called śrī bharatāḻvān \[in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 72.24\] as “*rājan*” (Oh king), he was unable to bear it, became completely broken and cried out \[in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 82.11 “*vilalāpa*” (cried out); for those who understand the flavour of pāratantriyam (total subservience), svātantriyam (independence) would feel like disaster. nampiḷḷai beautifully explains śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 101.12 here.
   - “*ēpiśca sacivaissārdam*” (with these ministers who are here … I (bharata) pray unto you (śrī rāma) …) – there were many along with bharata who were more anguished than him. He brought along many who were grieving like him. He thought “If it was just me, he could think ‘he is my brother only’ and exercise his independence. But with them, he cannot simply do that. For such elders, he needs to obey their orders. If they themselves enquired what happened and suggested him solution “you do this”, he will have no choice. If bharata wanted to highlight his suffering in separation from śrī rāma, he could have gone alone. Why did he bring everyone along? bharata thinks “If he does not return to ayōdyā seeing the tears in my eyes, he may at least return on seeing the tears of everyone assembled here”. Like a person who goes to battle, would bring along elephants, horses etc., bharata too brought them along, since they too feel the anguish in separation from śrī rāma.
   - *śirasā yācita:* – śrī rāma is the one who tries hard to help me. In such case, if I bow down and beg him, would he refuse?
   - *mayā* – If the roles are reversed (as explained in previous phrase), would he not help me?
   - *bhrātu: –* As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 97.8 “… *bhasmātkurutām śikī*” (śrī rāma saying – If I get even little pleasure without bharata, you (lakśmaṇa) and śatrugna, let that pleasure be burnt by fire), am I not born after him? He himself said “let my properties that are not useful for my brothers be burnt down to ashes”.
   - *śiśyasya* – Am I laying my claim for the throne citing that I am his brother? Did I not learn all the confidential meanings from you \[as a disciple would learn from his teacher\]?
   - *dāsasya* – Did I just stay as a disciple? Did I not commit myself as a full servitor so that you can even sell me? This being the case, would he refuse my request? This is the state of those who are desirous of kainkaryam.
- *vaḻuvilā adimai* – Even if he missed out on a single service, that will reflect on his physical form \[i.e., the grief would reflect on his body\].
- *seyya* – Even previously he had such desire \[which were reflected in many pāsurams previously\]. But now, it cannot just stop with the desire. He needs to practically engage in service now.
- *adimai seyya vēṇḍum* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s desire for service itself is part of the goal for āḻvār. When set out to enjoy “sensual pleasures” in this world, a mutually enjoyable aspect would be identified for both parties, the aspect would be enjoyed until the particular time and once done, the aspect will be discarded \[the enjoyable aspects are temporary\]. When set out to enjoy “heavenly pleasures”, as said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 6.5.50 “*svargē’pi pātabhītasya kśayiṣṇōr nāsti nirvruti:*” (Since even in heaven, there is the fear of falling down, there is no real joy); from there one can see others suffering in hell, so even while enjoying, one would not fully manifest the joy; also, the puṇyam (virtues) that keeps one there, will reduce like water fetched from pot \[which will eventually dry out\], they too will be pushed down eventually; instead of these temporary pleasures which are the result of ahankāram (considering body as soul) and mamakāram (considering oneself to be independent) and are contrary to the nature of the ātmā, this \[adimai – servitude, towards [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)\] is fitting to the true nature of the ātmā, the one who accepts such service \[bhagavān\] is also eternal and the one serves \[ātmā\] is also eternal, time is also eternal, the place is also eternal (paramapadam which is indestructible), the result is apunarāvrutti mōkśam (liberated state, from where there is no return to material realm), this is perfectly joyful unlike sensual pleasures which are mixed with pain.
- *nām* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) saying “*nām*” in plural by including his heart along with him. It can also be explained that after “[*kēśavan tamar*](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/04/thiruvaimozhi-2-7-kesavan-thamar/)“, he is not alone and is always with devotees of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), he is also including those devotees who are as dear as his own heart to him.
- *teḻi kural* … – Further it is explained that – more than the excitement of [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) who wants to serve, the excitement of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is going to accept his service is greater. āḻvār is desiring from wherever he is; but emperumān gave up the great assembly in “*kalangāp perunakaram*” (the unshakable paramapadam)) and descended all the way down to tirumalā and exhibited his excitement by his actions.
- *teḻi kural …* – The waterfalls that have a great sound. Because of the presence in this divine abode, even the sound of the waterfalls is pursuable for him. For [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/), the sound resembles “those who are interested to serve, please come here”. Do we need to explain this sound being enjoyable for [nammāḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) as [tirumangai āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/thirumangai-azhwar/) sang in periya tirumoḻi 1.7.2 “*silaikkai vēdar teḻipparāda*” (the abode where the sound of those hunters with bows never subsides) and enjoyed even those hunters who rob? Even the sounds of the robbing hunters are enjoyable, if it is present in the divine abodes.
- *tiruvēnkatattu eḻil koḷ sōdi* – This is the divine abode of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) which he considers to be the apt place to accept service. It is the place where one can serve emperumān the same service that is done after giving up one’s body, traveling in the arcirādi gati (the path of light) and reaching paramapadam (spiritual realm).
- *eḻil koḷ sōdi* – Even if he is not present in close proximity, his bodily beauty is so attracting that one will naturally fall in love with him.
- *vēnkatattu eḻil koḷ sōdi* – Differentiates “*vānār sōdi*” (the radiant light in spiritual sky – paramapadam) and “*neelāḻic cōdi*” (the radiant light in the milk ocean  – kśīrābdi). The light in spiritual sky is like a light in the midst of brightly illuminated day, The light in the milk ocean is consumed by the ocean. But the light in tiruvēnkatam is alike a lamp on the top of a hill which shines clearly everywhere. His beauty improved due to the contact with the divine hill.
- *endai* – The (fatherly) relationship is such that, even if he is ugly, we cannot leave him. Also explained that – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) won over [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) by showing his simplicity (by descending in tiruvēnkatam) and his beauty.
- *tandai tandaikkē* – Supreme lord. In this pāsuram, [tirumantram (aśtākśram)](http://ponnadi.blogspot.in/2015/12/rahasya-thrayam.html) which is focussed on kainkaryam as the goal, is explained. caturti (āya in tirumantram, “*adimai seyya vēṇḍum*“) explains the prayer/request. “*nām*” explains jīvātmā’s nature. “*teḻi kural …*” explains the meaning of the word “nārāyaṇa”. The kainkaryam (service) that is done towards the apt entity is the goal. Now, saulabhyam (*vēnkatattu*), physical beauty (*eḻil koḷ sōdi*), svāmitvam (*endai tandai tandai*) explain the meaning of the word nārāyaṇa \[Note: all of these are explained as part of mumukśuppadi and other grantams which give detailed explanation for tirumantram. It can be learned from elders precisely\].

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.3.2. Endai tandai

*endai tandai tandai tandai tandaikku mundai vānavar vānavar kōnodum sindupū magiḻum tiruvēnkatattu andamil pugaḻk kār eḻil aṇṇalē*

**Пословный перевод:**

endai tandai tandai tandai tandaikkum mundai – one who is having the primary relationship with us in our ancestral chain; vānavar – nityasūris; vānavar kōnodum – along with (their leader) sēnai mudaliyār (viśvaksēnar); sindu – spread out; pū – flowers; magiḻum – blossom (due to the connection with the hill); tiruvēnkatattu – due to residing in tirumalā; andam – anta – end; il – not having; pugaḻ – having qualities; kār – dark; eḻil – having beautiful form; aṇṇal – sarvādika (greater than all)

**Перевод:**

**emperumān is the primary relative in our ancestral chain; he is vorśipped by the nityasūris along with (their leader) sēnai mudaliyār (viśvaksēnar) by spreading flowers that blossom (due to the connection with the hill); due to sarvādika (greater than all) residing in tirumalā, he has endless auspicious qualities and dark beautiful form.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In second pāsuram – When asked “Is going to paramapadam and serving emperumān there not the ultimate goal for all?”, āḻvār replies “tiruvēnkatamudaiyān has endless beauty, simplicity etc and is desired even by nityasūris due to this, made me his confidential servitor. This being the case, I want to perform all services to him”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār mercifully explains the distinguished qualities and forms of such master who is greater than all.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. endai tandai tandai tandai tandaikku mundai vānavar vānavar kōnodum sindupū magiḻum tiruvēnkatattu andamil pugaḻk kār eḻil aṇṇalē*

- *endai …* – Just like while establishing svasvarūpam (nature of self), [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says as in tiruvāimoḻi 3.7.10 “*adiyār adiyār tam adiyār adiyār tamakku adiyār adiyōngaḷ*” (servant of servant of servant of …. of [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)), he started from bhagavān and ended with himself, while establishing parasvarūpam (bhagavān’s nature) he starts from himself and goes all the way up to him. It is explained in śvētāśvatara upaniśat “*tamīśvarāṇām paramam mahēśvaram*” (supreme lord of all lords).
- *vānavar* … – vānavar – nityasūris, vānavarkōn – [śrī sēnāpati āḻvān (viśvaksēnar)](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vishwaksenar/). Along with him, they bring spiritual flowers and wonder “[bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) who is unreachable even for us, now is manifesting himself for this forest, monkeys etc – How simple he is?” and become weak \[due to overwhelming emotions\] meditating upon such qualities, would spread the flowers in a disorderly manner \[sindu – drop\]. Just like [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)s who become liberated and reach paramapadam would become overwhelmed by bhagavān’s supremacy there, nityasūris who come here become overwhelmed by his simplicity. His supremacy is to be enjoyed in that (spiritual) realm; his simplicity is to be enjoyed in this (material) realm.
- *sindu pū magiḻum* – Due to the divine nature of tiruvēnkatam hill, the flower would look more blossomed after falling into the ground than while they were in the branch \[usually, flowers remain fresh when they are in the tree/plant\].
- *andamil pugaḻ* – Looks like in śrīvaikuṇṭam there is an end to [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s qualities. Since he himself is having a spiritual form, and is prepared for those who approach him with suitable \[spiritual\] senses, perhaps his glories are limited; but here since he manifests himself for the sake of yāḷi (a huge lion-headed animal with a trunk like elephant), lion, precious stones, pearls, flower bearing trees etc., there is no end to his glories. Thus, it is as said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 6.5.84 “*samastakalyāṇaguṇātmakō’sau*” ([bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is the one who naturally has all auspicious qualities).
- *kār eḻil* – dark physical beauty – His beauty is such that, even if devoid of any good qualities, we cannot leave him.
- *aṇṇal* – Even if there is no beauty, the relationship is binding. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says “nityasūris along with viśvaksēnar worship the resident of tiruvēnkatam who is the dark, beautiful [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) with unlimited glories – he is the primary personality in my clan; So, I should perform all kainkaryams to him”.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.3.3. Annal mayan

*aṇṇal māyan aṇi koḷ sendāmaraik kaṇṇan sengani vāyk karumāṇikkam teṇṇiṟaic cunai nīrt tiruvēnkatattu eṇṇil tol pugaḻ vānavar īsanē*

**Пословный перевод:**

aṇṇal – manifesting his supremacy in his divine form; māyan – having amazing qualities (matching such supremacy); aṇi – the beauty (which reveals such wealth/control); koḷ – having; sem tāmaraik kaṇṇan – being puṇḍarikākśa (reddish lotus like eyes); sem – reddish; kani – fruit like; vāy – having lips; karu māṇikkam – having a radiant form which shines like blackish blue gem stone; teḷ – with pristine shine (like his own complexion); niṟam (niṟai) – having complexion; sunai nīr – having water in ponds; tiruvēnkatattu – due to standing in tirumalai; eṇṇil – countless; tol – natural; pugaḻ – having auspicious qualities; vānavar – of the nityasūris (who came there to enjoy such qualities); īsan – is the lord (having greatness of giving them joy)

**Перевод:**

**emperumān is manifesting his supremacy in his divine form, having amazing qualities (matching such supremacy) and the beauty (which reveals such wealth/control), being puṇḍarikākśa, having reddish fruit like lips (to comfort those who are won over by such sight), having a radiant form which shines like blackish blue gem stone (to bestow experience for those who are caught by these beautiful divine parts). Due to standing in tirumalai that is having water with pristine shine (like his own complexion) in the ponds, such emperumān, is having countless naturally auspicious qualities and is the lord (having greatness of giving joy to nityasūris) of the nityasūris (who came there to enjoy such qualities), ,**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In third pāsuram – When asked “Would he give us this abundant experience of him?”, āḻvār replies – īsn’t bhagavān the most merciful in giving his perfect beauty and countless auspicious qualities for the enjoyment of countless exalted personalities? Hence, he would let us also enjoy him”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “Such emperumān who has distinguished forms, qualities etc is served by nityasūris (eternally free souls of paramapadam)”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Third pāsuram. When asked “Would we only have the desire to serve him like this? Would he himself bestow us this abundance of joy in experiencing him?”, āḻvār replies “When he is giving himself to those who are desireless \[since nityasūris’ desires are already fulfilled, they are not particularly desirous of anything specific\], why would he not give himself to us who are desirous \[to achieve him\]?” . aṇṇal māyan aṇi koḷ sendāmaraik kaṇṇan sengani vāyk karumāṇikkam teṇṇiṟaic cunai nīrt tiruvēnkatattu eṇṇil tol pugaḻ vānavar īsanē*

- *aṇṇal* – aṇṇal means leader of kurinji (hill/mountains) region. It also means sarvasvāmi – lord of all.
- *māyan* – Amazing person due to having beauty, simplicity etc.

When asked “Identify an ammānpodi (powder that will mesmerize others) in him”, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says,

- *aṇi koḷ sem tāmaraik kaṇṇan* – His eyes are such that “For one who has such beautiful eyes, no need for any other makeup or decoration”. It is an ornament by itself, and can somehow (not perfectly) be explained by a lotus with broadness/full blossom, freshness, coolness and fragrance – having such beautiful eyes. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is talking about the eyes that establish the initial contact \[with those who are liked by him\].
- *sem kani vāy* – His smile will imprison even those who escape his glance. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) was also won over by his gentle smile only.
- *karu māṇikkam* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is talking about his physical beauty that will deeply immerse those who are caught by his smile, in him.
- *teḷ niṟaic cunai nīrt tiruvēnkatam* – In tirumalai which has ponds that have abundance of pristine water. For [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/), not just [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s form, even tirumalai itself is soothing. For him, “*aṇikoḷ sendāmaraik kaṇṇan*” (one with beautiful reddish lotus like eyes), “*senganivāy*” (beautiful reddish lips), “*karumāṇikkam*” (blackish blue gem like physical form) and “*teṇṇiṟaic cunainīr*” (ponds with pristine, abundant water) are all the same. Because, all of these are seen in tirumalai.
- *eṇṇil tol pugaḻ* – One who is having countless and natural qualities as said in matsya purāṇam 20 “*yatā ratnāni jaladē: asankyēyāni putraka! …*” (Oh child! like how the ocean contains countless gems and precious stones, [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) has countless auspicious qualities).
- *vānavar īsanē* – One who sustains the nityasūris by giving his joyful experience of his auspicious qualities. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) explains that [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) would give his joyful experience to those nityasūris who are always attached to him.

## 3.3.4. Isan vanavarkku

*īsan vānavarkku enban enṟāl adu tēsamō tiruvēnkatattānukku nīsanēn niṟai onṟum ilēn en kaṇ pāsam vaitta paranjudarc cōdikkē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vānavarkku – of nityaśūris; īsan – controller, leader; enban – will say; enṟal – if I say so; nīsanēn – downtrodden (being filled with inauspicious qualities); niṟaivu – completeness (acquired through auspicious qualities); onṟum ilēn – due to having none; en kaṇ – towards me (who is directly opposite to him being the abode of auspicious qualities only and being opposite of all blemishes); pāsam – infinite attachment; vaitta – placed; param sudar – (due to that) being with perfect radiance; sōdikku – having fully radiant form; tiruvēnkattānukku – one who is firmly staying in tirumalai (where his simplicity is revealed); adu – that (being the leader of nityasūris); tēsamō – tējas? – Is that anything great?

**Перевод:**

**I will say “emperumān is the controller/leader of nityasūris”. If I say so, is that anything great? \[No. Because \] He has placed his infinite attachment towards me (who is directly opposite to him being the abode of auspicious qualities only and being opposite of all blemishes) who is downtrodden (being filled with inauspicious qualities)  and having no completeness (acquired through auspicious qualities). (Due to that) one who is firmly staying in tirumalai (where his simplicity is revealed) acquired perfect radiance and is having fully radiant form \[Blessing me who is downtrodden, brings him so much more glories than blessing nityasūris who are already pure\].**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In fourth pāsuram – āḻvār asks “For emperumān who has united with me who is very downtrodden, is there anything great in saying ‘he gave himself to nityasūris who have pristine knowledge’?”*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. īsan vānavarkku enban enṟāl adu tēsamō tiruvēnkatattānukku nīsanēn niṟai onṟum ilēn en kaṇ pāsam vaitta paranjudarc cōdikkē*

- *īsan vānavarkku enban* – I said “He is the controller of nityasūris”.
- *enṟāl* – if I said so
- *adu tēsamō tiruvēnkatattānukku* – For the one who has descended to tirumalai, and standing here manifesting his simplicity, is “being the leader of nityasūris” something great? I became confused and started glorifying śrīvaikuṇṭanātan since that (being the controller of nityasūris) is great for śrīvaikuṇṭanātan and not tiruvēnkatamudaiyān \[he has some other greatness\]. For the one who left paramapadam to be identified with this divine hill, who is presenting himself for the forest, monkeys and hunters, giving his presence for nityasūris is not something admirable. While bringing out the glories of an emperor, he cannot be glorified citing his visits to jail \[to supervise etc\] \[So, śrīvaikuṇṭanātan cannot be glorified citing his presence in tirumalai\].

When asked “What were you thinking to glorify tiruvēntattān as?”, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says,

- Should I not be saying “*nīsanēn niṟai onṟum ilēn enkaṇ pāsam vaitta param sudarc cōdi*“? Instead of saying this, should I be saying that \[that, he is the controller of nityasūris\]?
- *nīsanēn niṟai onṟum ilēn* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying that if a form is made with “inferiority and not having any good qualities”, that will be him. nampiḷḷai beautifully brings out [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s divine emotions through stōtra ratnam 62nd ślōkam.
   - *amaryāda:* *nrupaśu:* – As a *nrupaśu:* (animal in the form of human) that would not distinguish between the mother that gave birth and other beings \[when it comes to having physical relationship, (some) animals don’t distinguish\].  (amaryāda:) I practiced those activities that were forbidden in śāstram and became immersed in such activities.
   - *kśudra:* – When some one says “you cannot ignore śāstram maryādai (the orders of śāstram)”, I don’t have the heart to accept that.
   - *calamati:* – If there was some one to advice and even if that advice is understood by the heart at that time, my heart would lose faith in it soon as said in periya tirumoḻi 1.1.4 “*ninṟavā nillā nenju*” (heart without firm conviction),
   - *asūyā prasavabhū:* – I cannot even tolerate the person who advised for my well-being.
   - *krutagna:* – For such persons who helped me, instead of being grateful, I caused them suffering.
   - *durmānī* – Not only I caused them suffering, I also considered myself greater than them.
   - *smara paravaśa:* – While I considered myself greater than the wise people, I also considered myself subservient to lusty women.
   - *vancanapara:* – I would steal from others and bring that to a woman; once a lump sum is accumulated at the woman’s place, I would steal that too.
   - *nruśamsa:* – Not even feeling bad thinking “I have cheated those who trusted me”.
   - *pāpiśta:* – I would repeatedly do this. I would be immersed in sins.
- *nīsanēn niṟai onṟum ilēn* – [anantāḻvān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/ananthazhwan/) would say “Though this ślōkam was blessed by [āḷavandār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/alavandhar/), I would not dare saying it \[since I may accidentally come to think that a tiny little bit of these blemishes may be present in āḷavandār\].
- *nīsanēn niṟai onṟum ilēn* – Two explanations.
   - I only have anātmaguṇams (bodily/inferior qualities) and no ātmaguṇams (natural/superior qualities) \[so being my lord, adds to his glories of accepting even the most downtrodden\] \[This explanation focusses on “For tiruvēnkatattān who is paranjudarccōdi who placed his attachment on me who is inferior and has no good qualities – if I said ‘*vānavarkku īsanenban*‘ (he is the lord of nityasūris) – is there anything great in that?”\].
   - piḷḷai tirunaṟaiyūr araiyar would say that [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is explaining this as “It is because of my inferior nature and not having any good qualities, I am saying this \[*īsan vānavarkkenban* (he is lord of nityasūris)” \[since it is better to be the lord of nityasūris than me\]. \[This explanation focusses on “Because I am inferior and have no good qualities, I proclaim him to be the lord of nityasūris. For tiruvēnkatattān who is the paranjudarccōdi who placed his attachment towards me, is there any glory in me saying that?”\].
- *en kaṇ pāsam vaitta* – One who placed his love towards me. He placed his control over nityasūris. But he had his attachment towards me.  He united with them to sustain them. He united with me to sustain himself. They are like the first wife (crowned-queen) – who is given priority \[in official circles\], given some wealth etc., to avoid being blamed if she wears saffron robes and goes for begging. But I am like his dear wife in whom he has placed his heart, body. Alternatively, it is also explained by some as [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) saying that [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) triggered my attachment towards him. That is, “*enkaṇ* (in me) *pāsam* (attachment towards him) *vaitta* (placed)”.
- *param cudarc cōdikkē* – His bodily radiance shows that he did not unite with me without real interest in his heart just to convince others, he engaged with me with all his heart. He was shining. After uniting with me, he acquired new radiance. He stood shining like he would after uniting with [śrī mahālakśmi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.3.5. Sodiyagi

*sōdiyāgi ellā ulagum toḻum ādi mūrtti enṟāl aḷavāgumō vēdiyar muḻu vēdattamudattait tīdil sīrt tiruvēnkatattānaiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vēdiyar – vaidika’s \[those who go by the vēdas andn śāstras\]; muḻu vēdattu – in all of vēdams; amudattai – (As revealed in taittiriya upaniśat as “ānandō brahma” (supreme brahmam is bliss), “rasō vai sa:” (he is the source of all tastes)) having greatly enjoyable aspects; tīdu – defect (of bestowing the sweetness based on the qualification of the enjoyer); il – not having; sīr – having auspicious qualities (of giving joy to lowly forest, monkeys, hunters etc); tiruvēnkatattānai – tiruvēnkatamudaiyān; sōdiyāgi – being the one with a radiant form; ellā ulagum – everyone (without any discrimination in greatness etc); toḻum – being approached; ādi – being the cause of everything; mūrtti – sarvēśvaran (supreme lord); enṟāl – if we said so; aḷavāgumō – is there any greatness?

**Перевод:**

**If tiruvēnkatamudaiyān who is (as revealed in taittiriya upaniśat as “ānandō brahma” (supreme brahmam is bliss), “rasō vai sa:” (he is filled with all tastes)) having greatly enjoyable aspects as highlighted in vaidika’s all of vēdams, not having the defect (of bestowing the sweetness based on the qualification of the enjoyer) and having auspicious qualities (of giving joy to lowly forest, monkeys, hunters etc), is hailed as sarvēśvaran with a radiant form, being the cause of everything and presents himself to be vorśipped by everyone (without any discrimination in greatness etc), is there any greatness in that? Implies that – his supremacy and being the shelter for everyone is no match for his simplicity and sweetness.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In fifth pāsuram – āḻvār says “For tiruvēnkatamudaiyān’s nature, is accepting me such a great quality?”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “Is he just śeelavān (simple, one with good qualities)? For such emperumān, who is also perfectly enjoyable in addition to being simple, is praising him as sarvēśvaran (lord of all) adding to his glories?”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Fifth pāsuram. Previously āḻvār said – For one who gave himself to me, is hailing him as one who gave himself to nityasūris, adding to his glories?; Is hailing him for giving himself to me adding to his glories, if he has searched and helped those who are even lower than me? sōdiyāgi ellā ulagum toḻum ādi mūrtti enṟāl aḷavāgumō vēdiyar muḻu vēdattamudattait tīdil sīrt tiruvēnkatattānaiyē*

- *sōdiyāgi* – Having a divine form that is infinitely radiant. While his divine form is glorified as in nārāyaṇa sūktam “*neelatōyadamadyastā*” (Like a bright lightning in a dark cloud), he is also said as “*pītābhā*” (like the radiance of molten gold). His pleasant form is subdued by his radiance and his radiance is contained in his pleasant form too. This implies that both aspects are together and both need nothing more (either one is sufficient) to bring out his glories. He is also explained in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 1.9.63 as “*tējasām rāsimūrjitam*” (one who shines like collection of radiant rays and who has the valour to demolish his enemies).
- *ellā ulagum toḻum ādi mūrtti enṟāl aḷavāgumō* – Previously, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) first said “*eṇṇil tol pugaḻ vānavar īsan*” and repeated the same in “*īsan vānavarkku enban*“. Is he doing the same here? No. Here he is explaining [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s greatness by artāpatti (inference from circumstances). How so? Before, he said “*nīsanēn niṟai onṟum ilēn*” (I am downtrodden and have no good qualities). He identified himself as the lowest of all. When he himself vorśipped, it means that everyone (who is lowly) in all worlds have also vorśipped. When one says “the top most step in a tank is now submerged into the water”, it implies that the lower steps are submerged and need not be explicitly stated.
- *toḻum* – Even those who vowed not to worship kriṣṇa, vorśipped him as soon as they saw him as seen in mahābhāratam sabhā parvam 75 “*yadārham kēśavē vruttimavaśā: pratibēdirē*” (with great enchantment towards kēśava, they performed obeisances etc).
- *ādi mūrtti* – On being told “*brahma jijñāsyam*” (Know brahmā), when asked what is the identity of brahmam, being the cause etc of universe is highlighted as the identity. kāraṇa vākyams (those phrases in vēdam etc that identify the root cause of everything) are explained through taittirya upaniśat bruguvalli “*yatō vā imāni bhūtāni jāyantē … tadvijijñāsasva tadbrahma*” (From which, the universe is created, on which, the universe is sustained, in which the universe dissolves, that is to be known and that is brahma). When asked “Which entity should be approached?”, it is said as in cāndōjña upaniśat “*kāraṇam tu dyēya:*” (the object of meditation is that which is the cause of everything) and as in śvētāśvatāra upaniśat “*yō brahmāṇam vitadāti pūrvam .. mumukśurvai śaraṇam aham prapadyē*” (That śrīman nārāyaṇan who blessed brahmā with all the knowledge during creation … I am surrendering unto that brahmam). Similarly, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) also is saying “*ellā ulagum toḻum*” (that which is vorśipped by all) and “*ādi mūrtti*” (one who is to be surrendered) in the same manner \[as in upaniśats\]. Even to explain that there is nothing matching brahmam’s greatness, we need to do it using vēdam as said in taittiriya upaniśat “*yatō vācō nivartantē*” (the words returned (being unable to glorify [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) fully).
- *vēdiyar muḻu vēdattu amudattai* – Having unlimited sweetness as glorified in all vēdams of brāhmaṇas as explained in yajuśi “*sā hi śrīramrutā sadām*” (For the scholars/elders, this vēdam is the eternal wealth), \[brāhmaṇas\] who are the givers of vēdam, As said in kata upaniśat 1.2.15 “*sarvē vēdā yatpadamāmananti*” (that goal which is explained by all vēdams), taittirya “*sarvē vēdā: yatraikam bhavanti*”  (that vēdam which subsides in brahmam), śrī bhagavat gītā 15.15 “*vēdaiśca sarvair ahamēva vēdya:*” (All vēdams reveal me only), [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) who is glorified in all vēdams as having the quality of “bliss”. He is also glorified in taittiriya upaniśat as “*ānandō brahma*” (supreme brahmam is bliss), “*rasō vai sa:*” (he is filled with all tastes).
- *tīdil sīrt tiruvēnkattānaiyē* – tīdu – defects. il – absence. Having auspicious qualities which have no defects. While pursuing individuals, absence of defect means not choosing as in “this person is ōK. this person is not” and so on. What is greater in this “*tīdil sīr*” that is more than “*ellā ulagum toḻum ādi mūrtti ennum aḷavāgumō?*“. Previously we saw “*enkaṇ pāsam vaitta*” (placing your attachment in such lowly me) as greater than “*īsan vānavrkku enban*” (the leader of nityasūris). Similarly, the greatness of “*tīdil sīrt”* more than “*ellā ulagum toḻum*” is – pursuing/accepting me is not such a great aspect while he searched for the most downtrodden persons and not found one. He is such that, he would do hunger-fast and wait for such downtrodden persons as explained in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 59.3 “… *āśayā yadi vā rāma: …*” (I was waiting here (banks of gangā) with guhap perumāḷ thinking that perumāḷ (śrī rāma) would call him some day). After accepting [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) who said “*nīsanēn niṟai onṟum ilēn*“, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is looking for even more downtrodden persons and since he has not found them, he is just waiting. For one who is protecting, if he gets the protected entity and becomes satisfied immediately, it is a defect \[he should wait and care for him instead\]. This is explained in “…*santuśta: kśatriyas tadā…*” (A brāhmaṇa would become lost if he is not satisfied with what he gets. On the other hand, if a kśatriya becomes satisfied with what he gets, he will become lost \[kśatriya should constantly strive for more\]). The defect in quality is to discriminate between those who surrender.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.3.6. Venkatangal

*vēnkatangaḷ meym mēl vinai muṟṟavum tāngaḷ tangatku nallanavē seyvār vēnkatattuṟaivārkku namavennal ām kadamai adu sumandārgatkē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vēnkatattu – in tirumalai; uṟaivārkku – for the lord who resides eternally (to be pursued by everyone); nama ennalām – the word “nama:” (which highlights the eradication of independence, indicates total dependence, easy means, that which matches one’s true nature); adu – that (which is emphasised by śruti (vēdam) saying “bhūyiśtām tē nama uktim vidēma“); kadamai – activity; sumandārgatku – those who carried in their heads (to highlight their qualification); kadangaḷ – previously accumulated sins in the form of debts (that can be exhausted by consuming the results); mēl vinai – uttarāgams (sins that are accumulated after surrendering); muṟṟavum vēm – will be burnt into ashes (as said in tiruppāvai 5 “tīyinil tūsāgum” (like dust in fire)); mey – satyam – this is truth (since this is conclusion of the faultless vēdāntam); tāngaḷ – those (who have surrendered); tangatku – for their true nature; nallanavē – experience of bhagavān which leads to bliss; seyvār – only engage in

**Перевод:**

**For those who performed the activity of carrying the word “nama:” (which highlights the eradication of independence, indicates total dependence, easy means, that which matches one’s true nature) in their heads (to highlight their qualification) towards the lord who resides eternally in tirumalai (to be pursued by everyone) , their previously accumulated sins in the form of debts (that can be exhausted by consuming the results) and uttarāgams (sins that are accumulated after surrendering) will be burnt into ashes (as said in tiruppāvai 5 “tīyinil tūsāgum” (like dust in fire)); this is truth (since this is conclusion of the faultless vēdāntam). Since the unfavourable aspects disappear themselves, those (who have surrendered) would only engage in experience of bhagavān which leads to bliss for their true nature.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In sixth pāsuram – when asked “Would those karmas (virtues/vices) be hurdles for our kainkaryam (service)?”, āḻvār says “as soon as we agree to serve, those would disappear themselves”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār mercifully explains the easy nature of taking refuge of emperumān which is helpful in blissful experience of bhagavān which is acquired after the unfavourable aspects are eliminated.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Sixth pāsuram. Previously (in the first pāsuram), āḻvār explained the meaning of tirumantram. But “nama:” was not explained in that pāsuram. (that is, elimination of hurdles such as ignorance etc); he is explaining that here. When asked “Though he may not be satisfied until every jīvātmā is protected, and though we may be determined to reach him, what are we going to do with the karmas which have been accumulated by us since time immemorial and are the hurdles for us to achieve bhagavān?”, āḻvār says “as we engage in kainkaryam (service), they will themselves disappear”. vēnkatangaḷ meym mēl vinai muṟṟavum tāngaḷ tangatku nallanavē seyvār vēnkatattuṟaivārkku namavennal Am kadamai adu sumandārgatkē*

- *vēnkatangaḷ* – katam – kadan (debt). kadangaḷ means debts (obligations). Those are as explained in yajuśi kāṇḍam 6 “*tribhir ruṇavā jāyatē*” (one is born with 3 debts) \[they are debts to riśis (sages), dēvas (celestial beings) and pitrus (ancestors)\]; Further as explained (in same ślōkam) “*brahmacaryēṇa ruśibhya: yajñēna dēvēbhya: prajayā pitrubhya:*“, by brahmacaryam (pursuit of brahmam), his obligation to sages will be fulfilled; by engaging in yāgams, his obligation to dēvas will be fulfilled and by prajōtpatti (progeny), his obligation to ancestors will be fulfilled. It is said in manu smriti 6.35 “*ruṇāni trīṇyapākrutya …*” (One should fulfill these 3 obligations and pursue sanyāsāśramam (renounced order); if sanyāsāśramam were pursued without fulfilling the obligations, one will fall).
- *meym mēl vinai muṟṟavum* – The sins that are acquired due to engagement in this [prakruti](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/09/thathva-thrayam-achith-what-is-matter/) (material aspects) \[here mey is explained as body\]. Thus, “the three debts and the sins acquired will be burnt/destroyed \[when nama: is recited\]” – up to this is [āḷavandār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/alavandhar/)‘s explanation. [emperumānār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/emperumanar/) heard this and said “can we not explain this in line with vēdāntam?” and mercifully explained it as follows. That is as said in brahma sūtram 4.1.13 “*uttarapūrvāgayōraślēśavināśau*” (as said in śruti (vēdam), due to the greatness of the vidyā (upāsanam, means), the uttārāgam (the sins that were committed after acquiring knowledge) will not stick to the pursuer and the pūrvāgam (the sins that were committed before acquiring knowledge) will be burnt to ashes); and cāndōjña upaniśat 5.25 “*ēvam hāsya sarvē pāpmāna: pradūyantē*” (For one with such true knowledge in vēdāntam, all his sins will be destroyed like dust thrown in to fire). vēm (destroyed) implies destruction for past sins and dissociation from future sins. Alternatively, it can be said that both past and future sins would be dissociated. pūrvāgam means all unfavourable acts which were done **intentionally** before acquiring true knowledge. uttarāgam means all unfavourable acts which were done **unintentionally** after acquiring true knowledge. Even after acquiring true knowledge, due to being bound in bodily condition, one may end up engaging in forbidden acts. Subsequently, on realizing the mistake, one would (should) withdraw immediately from such acts and atone/suffer thinking “what great mistake I have committed?”. \[[emperumānār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/emperumanar/)‘s explanation is\] past sins and future sins will be destroyed – this is truth \[here mey is explained as satyam – truth\]. This is explained in cāndōjña upaniśat 5.25 “*ēvam hāsya sarvē pāpmāna: pradūyantē*” (For one with such true knowledge in vēdāntam, all his sins will be destroyed like dust thrown in to fire). \[Is it truth just because it is explained in śāśtram?\] pramāṇams (authentic source of knowledge) such as pratyakśam (sense perception) and anumānam (inference) would cause both confusion and clarification \[Some times they confuse and other times they reveal the truth\]. But if it is explained in śāstram \[śabda pramāṇam\], it will always be truth as said in “*yatābhūtavādi hi śāstram*” (śāstram explains the truth as it is). śrī rāma launched his bow/arrow to destroy the ocean; but when samudrarājan (king of ocean) realized his mistake and came out humbly in front of śrī rāma, śrī rāma \[with his anger subdued\] asked samudrarājan “Tell me who are your enemies, I will send this arrow towards them”.  Here bhattar explains a humorous incident. Once there was a bald and wealthy land owner who was measuring his harvest. A poet comes by that side and \[desiring to win some prize money\] asked him “Instead of taking care of your curly hair, why are you working hard in measuring this?”. The land owner asked “Why did you come?” and the poet replied “I came to just see you”. Being pleased, the land owner gave him a sack of paddy. The poet accepted it gleefully and started walking away. Another poet ran into him and asked “where did you get this sack of paddy from?” and the first poet sarcastically said “that mottait talaiyan (the bald headed person) gave me”. The second poet runs to the land owner and complains to him that the first person called him bald headed and asked “why was he awarding such persons?”. The land owner became furious and started running towards the first poet to retrieve the sack of paddy. The first poet noticed the land owner coming towards him furiously and realized what could have happened. As the land owner got closer, the first poet praised him saying “why are you running towards me so hard with your curly hairs diśevelling here and there?”. The land owner again became pleased on hearing the praise and told “I came to give you another sack of paddy” and gives the same. Similarly, śrī rāma,  first himself surrendered to samudrarājan (king of ocean) and then on his non-arrival, threatened to destroy him with his bow/arrow. But on his arrival and surrender, he himself felt embarrassed for having raised his bow/arrow and with care, asked him “Tell me who are your enemies, I will aim this at them” \[This passage is highlighted to explain, how [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)  will willingly remove all the sins of those who are surrendered to him\].

In the first pāsuram, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) missed to explain one aspect (*nama:*). He is explaining it here.

- *tāngaḷ* … – When asked “For the one who is to enjoy the results, like he is praying for kainkaryam, would he also have to pray to have the hurdles/sins removed?”, āḻvār says “No. It is not necessary to separately pray for elimination of hurdles. As they engage in kainkaryams, their hurdles will be automatically removed”. [anantāḻvān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/ananthazhwan/) used to emphasise on “*tāngaḷ tangatku*” (those (qualified persons), for them) since this is focussed on those who desire to perform all types of kainkaryams as said in “*vaḻuvilā adimai seyya vēṇḍum nām*” in the first pāsuram.
- *tāngaḷ* – those who are detached from worldly pleasures and attached to performing kainkaryam.
- *tangatku* – For them, who have such taste towards kainkaryam.
- *nallanavē seyvār* – They would only engage in kainkaryams that are matching their true nature.

What were they thought about when said “*tāngaḷ tangatku nallanavē seyvār*“?

- *vēnkattu uṟaivārkku* – Here the meaning of caturti (āya in tirumantram) is explained.
- *nama* – nama: means “for him and not for me”.
- *ennal* – It need not come from the heart. It can just be said (without deep interest/understanding). Even though this may be a very small act (of saying the word), would it be good for him? Yes, susukam \[kriṣṇa explains in śrī bhagavat gītā 9.2 that bhakti yōgam is something very pleasing for the self to engage in\].

If it is said to be very easy to do, would it match the true nature of the self?

- *kadamai* – prāptam (naturally fitting).
- *adu sumandārgatkē* – Looking at the greatness of the result and the insignificant act of the [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/), like it is said in “would he have to carry a mountain to accomplish this task?”, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says “*adu sumandārgatku*” (those who carry this *nama:* on their heads) as it would be considered by [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) himself. ōr it could have been said in āḻvār’s own opinion who knows the greatness of the result and bhagavān’s mercy; or it could have been said based on bhagavān’s consideration of any small effort of ātmā to be great; it is explained in yajuśi “*bhūyiśtām* …” (We are reciting the word nama: which is considered great by you). When draupati cried out “gōvinda!”, bhagavān became greatly hurt thinking “She cried out my name \[and I am not with her to help her immediately\]”. He praised her (for crying out for him) and condemned himself for not being with her at that time of suffering for her. As said in mahābhāratam udyōga parvam 58.22 “*… kriṣṇā mām dūravāsinam …*” (My heart is still not relieved from the debt (which is accumulated now) of letting draupati cry out “*gōvinda!*” for me, who was staying far away from her). Even though she was rescued from the insult that occurred in the assembly, he was always feeling sorry for not being present physically with her while she called out for him. He felt “while my name did its job in protecting those who called out, I have not specifically done anything for her”. \[When asked if the name itself can protect\] if two unrelated words are recited together \[in the form of garuda mantram\], it cures the poison of snake bite just by the power of the mantram, why vouldn’t [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s name protect those who recited it?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.
