## 3.3.7. Sumandu mamalar

*sumandu mā malar nīr sudar dūpam koṇḍu amarndu vānavar vānavar kōnodum namanṟeḻum tiruvēnkatam nangatkuc caman koḷ vīdu tarum tadam kunṟamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

mā – best; malar – flowers; mā – good; nīr – water; mā – distinguished; sudar – lamp; mā dūpam – incense; sumand koṇḍu – carrying them with attachment; amarndu – being seated as ananyaprayōjana (one who is focussed exclusively in serving bhagavān without any interest in worldly favours); vānavar – nityasūris (eternally free souls of parampadam); vānavar kōnodum – with sēnai mudaliyār (viśvaksēna – who is their leader); namanṟu – bowing (which highlights their total dependence); eḻum – feeling accomplished (having realized their true nature); tiruvēnkatam – having the name tiruvēnkatam; tadam – very vast (the hill that will cause emotional changes in sarvēśvara who is with śrī mahālakśmi); kunṟam – tirumalai – divine hill; nangatku – for us (who have taste in attaining the goal); saman – parama sāmyāpatti (equivalence to bhagavān in eight qualities); koḷ – having; vīdu – bliss of liberation; tarum – will bestow

**Перевод:**

**nityasūris along with their leader sēnai mudaliyār, with attachment, carrying the best flowers, good water, distinguished lamp and incense, being seated as ananyaprayōjana (one who is focussed exclusively in serving bhagavān without any interest in worldly favours) bowed (which highlights their total dependence) towards very vast (the hill that causes emotional changes in sarvēśvaran who is with śrī mahālakśmi) tirumalai (divine hill) which is named tiruvēnkatam and felt accomplished (having realized their true nature). Such tirumalai would bestow us  (who have taste in attaining the goal) the bliss of liberation which leads to parama sāmyāpatti (equivalence to bhagavān in eight qualities).**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In seventh pāsuram – āḻvār says “To engage in all services we desire, we need not surrender unto tiruvēnkatamudaiyān; tirumalai itself will bestow that”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “the tirumalai where he resides will itself bestow the ultimate sāmyāpatti \[equivalence to bhagavān himself in eight qualities\], as the result of surrender since it came up \[in previous pāsuram\]”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Seventh pāsuram. āḻvār says “tirumalai itself will bestow the kainkaryam which was prayed for in the first pāsuram”. kainkaryam \[carrying flowers, water, lamp, incense etc\] is the result of prāpti \[reaching parampadam\]. sumandu mā malar nīr sudar dūpam koṇḍu amarndu vānavar vānavar kōnodum namanṟeḻum tiruvēnkatam nangatkuc caman koḷ vīdu tarum tadam kunṟamē*

- *sumandu* … – It can be explained as “*māmalar, nīr, sudar, dūpam ivaṟṟaic cumandu koṇḍu”* (holding best flower, water, lamp and incense). Alternatively, it is explained as “*māmalar sumandu, nīr sudar dūpam koṇḍu*” (holding best flower and having water, lamp and incense). Even if it is a karumugai (sampangi) flower \[which is very light weight\], due to desire/attachment of the devotees thinking “Hope he accepts it, hope he wears it, hope he blesses us specially”, it will feel very heavy \[to [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)\]. Alternatively, it feels heavy for sarvēsvaran because it was offered by one who is favourable towards him. Remember the incident of a prince offering śeṇbaga (campak) flower to śrī puruśōttamamudaiyān (puri jagannāta). puruśōttama usually accepts campak flower with great satisfaction. Once, a few princes visited puri kśētram. At that time, all the flowers except one were sold out. The princes out of pride, bid against each other and one prince won the flower for great expense \[he traded his own kingdom for the flower with the flower vendor\] and offered that flower to jagannātan [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/). In the night, jagannātan emperumān appeared in the dream of that prince and mercifully told him “the flower you offered is very heavy and I cannot carry it”.
- *amarndu …* – Explained in context of nityasūris and sēnai mudaliyār. Also explained in context of dēvas and brahmā.
- *amarndu* – well seated. Though brahmā et al (dēvas) are prayōjanāntaraparars (desirous of worldly pleasures), the nature of this divine hill is such that, it will even transform them to ananyaprayōjanar (those who exclusively desire for kainkaryam). Having such raw materials for their worship, they would bow in front of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) and rise. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) considers them to have his own attitude which he highlighted in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.1.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/03/thiruvaimozhi-1-1-1-uyarvara-uyarnalam/) “*tuyaraṟu sudaradi toḻudu eḻu*” (worship his divine feet that will remove the sorrows and rise).
- *nangatku* – for us who are interested in kainkarayam.
- *saman koḷ vīdu tarum* – Three explanations:
   - Explained as bestowing mōkśam in the form of sāmyāpatti as explained in muṇḍaka upaniśat 3.2 “*brahma vēda brahmaiva bhavati*” (one who know brahmam becomes like brahmam), muṇḍaka upaniśat 3.1.3 “*niranjana: paramam sāmyam upaiti*” (having all blemishes eliminated through bramha vidyā becomes fully equivalent (in eight qualities) to brahmam), [śrī bhagavat gītā](http://githa.koyil.org/) 14.2 “*mama sādarmyamāgatā:*” (those who have this knowledge, will acquire form etc that equals mine), periya tirumoḻi 11.3.5 “*tammaiyē okka aruḷ seyvar*” ([emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) will bless the devotee to become exactly like himself).
   - Alternatively explained as bestowing the liberation that matches the true nature of the ātmā as said in cāndōjña upaniśat “*svēnarūpēṇābhiniśpadyatē*” (the ātmā acquires a distinguished form matching his true nature and shines).
   - Another explanation – tirumalai itself will bestow the result matching its own status. tirumalai āḻvār (this divine hill) is fortunate in having tiruvēnkatamudaiyān himself on its head. In the same manner, tirumalai āḻvār himself will bestow such result as prayed by [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) himself in [tiruvāimoḻi 2.9.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/06/thiruvaimozhi-2-9-1-emma-vittu/) “*nin semmā pāda paṟput talai sērttu*” (you place your fresh divine lotus feet on my head) as said in “*tadam kunṟamē tarum*” (the hill itself will bestow).
- *tadam kunṟam* – Having vast space so that tiruvēnkatamudaiyān can roam around as much as he desires. nampiḷḷai explains śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 98.12 ślōkam to explain the vastness of tiruvēnkatam.
   - *subhaga: –* gracious
   - *girirājōpama:* – comparable to tirumalai (girirāja – king of hills)
   - *yasmin vasati* – explaining the reason for the aforementioned aspects
   - *kākutsta:* – the reason is, śrī rāma who was born in the lineage of kakutsta, the lineage that always seeks out secluded places for enjoyment, resided here happily (so it is gracious and comparable to tirumalai).
   - *kubēra iva nandanē* – Like kubēra would leave his palace and wander around pridefully in his gardens in the forests which are inhabited by dangerous beasts, śrī rāma was wandering around in citrakūta forests leaving his palace in ayōdyā.

## 3.3.8. Kunram endi

*kunṟam ēndik kuḷir maḻai kāttavan anṟu jñālam aḷanda pirān – paran senṟu sēr tiruvēnkata mā malai onṟumē toḻa nam vinai ōyumē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kuḷir maḻai – hailstorm (which troubled the cows and covherd clan); kunṟam – a hill; ēndi – lifted up; kāttavan – being the protector; anṟu – back then (when the world was mischievously taken by mahābali); jñālam – earth; aḷanda – measured; pirān – one who is the saviour (by entirely owning it); paran – supreme lord; senṟu – went; sēr – reached; tiruvēnkatam – tiruvēnkatam; mā – huge; malai – divine hill; onṟumē – that alone; toḻa – experience (not having to follow any regulation such as reaching up to the dēśika (leader/lord)); nam – our; vinai – hurdles that are sins (that stop experiencing the leader); ōyum – will naturally disappear

**Перевод:**

**emperumān, the supreme lord, who lifted up a hill to protect from hailstorm (which troubled the cows and covherd clan) and who is the saviour (by entirely owning the earth) back then (when the world was mischievously taken by mahābali) by measuring the earth, went and reached tiruvēnkatam which is a huge divine hill; On experiencing  (not having to follow any regulation such as reaching up to the dēśika (leader/lord)) that (divine hill) alone, our hurdles that are sins (that stop experiencing the leader), will naturally disappear.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In eighth pāsuram, āḻvār says “tirumalai is the ultimate goal for emperumān who is most enjoyable by his acts of lifting up the gōvardana hill etc; does it need to give us something? It is in itself the ultimate goal”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “By experiencing such tirumalai, the hurdles for the goal will naturally disappear”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Eighth pāsuram. āḻvār says “tirumalai āḻvār (the divine hill) himself will eliminate the hurdles that were identified in ‘vēnkatangaḷ‘ pāsuram”. Also explained as āḻvār saying “Should it fulfill a particular goal? tirumalai itself is the goal; does it need to be separately mentioned as the goal for śēśabhūta (servitor), when it is the goal for śēśi (lord) himself?”. kunṟam ēndik kuḷir maḻai kāttavan anṟu jñālam aḷanda pirān – paran senṟu sēr tiruvēnkata mā malai onṟumē toḻa nam vinai ōyumē*

- *kunṟam ēndik kuḷir maḻai kāttavan* – Always, hill is used by [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) as an instrument to eliminate the hurdles. As said in  śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 4.11.13 “*gōgōpījanasangulam atīvārtam*” (for the suffering cows, covherd boys and girls), when the cows and covherd clan were targeted to be destroyed, he picked up a hill that was visible right in front of him and held it effortlessly for seven days and protected them.
- *anṟu* … – Previously, his help for a small village was explained. Now, his help for the entire world is explained. When the earth was taken over by the enemy mahābali, he, the saviour, walked over its boundaries and reclaimed it back. His being sarvarakśaka (protector of all) and āśritarakśaka (protector of indra, his devotee) is explained.
- *paran* – [sarvasmātparan](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) – greater than all.
- *senṟu sēr tiruvēnkata māmalai* – He himself arrived considering it as “my goal” and living here.
- *onṟumē toḻa* – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is dwelling inside the hill is also not needed; tirumalai āḻvār (divine hill) himself is sufficient.
- *nam vinai ōyumē* – Two explanations.
   - The sin of thinking “We have not attained our goal yet”.
   - The sins that are identified in “*vēnkatangaḷ*” pāsuram as the hurdles in attaining the goal. Both types of sins will be removed.

## 3.3.9. Oyumuppu

*ōyumūppup piṟappiṟappup piṇi vīyumāṟu seyvān tiruvēnkatattu āyan nāḷmalarām adit tāmarai vāyuḷḷum manattuḷḷum vaippārgatkē*

**Пословный перевод:**

nāḷ malarām – very tender (like a flower that has just blossomed today); adit tāmarai – lotus feet; vāy uḷḷum – in speech; manattuḷḷum – in the heart/mind; vaippārgatku – to those who place; ōyum – that would cause disturbance in attaining the result; mūppu – old age; piṟappu – birth (the basis for the body); iṟappu – destruction (of such body); piṇi – diseases (which come along with the old age); vīyumāṟu – to destroy; seyvān – one who does; tiruvēnkatattu – residing in tiruvēnkatam; āyan – kriṣṇa

**Перевод:**

**kriṣṇa who is residing in tiruvēnkatam is the one who destroys old age  that would cause disturbance in attaining the result, birth (basis for the body),  destruction (of such body) and diseases (which come along with the old age), to those who place his very tender (like a flower that has just blossomed today) lotus feet in their speech and mind.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In ninth pāsuram – āḻvār says “To bestow us the kainkaryam and to remove our hurdles, tirumalai is not needed; tiruvēnkatamudaiyān who is a part of tirumalai, himself is sufficient”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “the ability to remove the hurdles by tiruvēnkatamudaiyān who is dēśikan (leader), is due to his relationship with the dēśam (divine abode), tirumalai”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Ninth pāsuram. āḻvār explained in the previous two pāsurams that tirumalai āḻvār (divine hill) himself will remove his hurdles and bestow the goal. Here he asks “Is tirumalai āḻvār required to remove my hurdles and bestow the goal? Is a part of tirumalai āḻvār not sufficient to accomplish that?”. Here “a part” indicates “tirumalai appan” (śrīnivāsan). tiruvēnkatamudaiyān is glorified in periya tirumoḻi 7.10.3 as “vadamāmalai ucci” (the peak of the great northern hill). ōyumūppup piṟappiṟappup piṇi vīyumāṟu seyvān tiruvēnkatattu āyan nāḷmalarām adit tāmarai vāyuḷḷum manattuḷḷum vaippārgatkē*

- *ōyumūppup piṟappu iṟappu* – janma (birth), jarā (old age), maraṇa (death) and vyādi (disease) will disappear. Since it is saying “ōyum” (will be gone) now, we understand that since time immemorial they have continuously troubled us without giving any break.
- *piṇi vīyumāṟu sevyān tiruvēnkatattu āyan*–  Should be read as “*piṇi vīyumāṟu sevyān tiruvēnkatattu āyan*” (kriṣṇa residing in tiruvēnkatam will remove the diseases/sufferings) \[“*piṇi vīymāṟu seyvān*” (one who eliminates hurdles) is an adjective for “*tiruvēnkatattu āyan*“\]. One who is now residing in tiruvēnkatam to eliminate our sufferings, would he not have stayed in “*kalangāp perunagaram*” (unśakeable paramapadam) if were to let us continue to toil here? Here *piṇi* includes all types of sufferings which arise from bodily bondage (birth, old age, disease. death). But why is it said “*piṇi vīyumāṟu seyvān*” (will remove all diseases” here? It is to indicate that he has descended here to eliminate the sufferings of this world. Thus, it indicates that [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s nature is to eliminate others’ sufferings. Unless he himself descends and removes these hurdles, for this [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) who is *eli elumban* (very meek and incapable), there is no way to eliminate them.
- *nāḷ malarām adit tāmarai* … – On seeing his feet, “old age, birth, death, disease” will be destroyed. To eliminate the hurdles, one is asked to drink this bitter pill (sarcasm – it should be read as “the most enjoyable divine feet”). Like the ones who keep fresh flowers on their head, to carry heavy burden.
- *vāy uḷḷum* … – vāy (speech) and manas (mind) is indicated as a sample for speech, mind and body. For those who pursue the divine feet through their mind, speech and body. Placing in speech means as said in mudal tiruvandādi 95 “*ōvāduraikkum urai*” (constant recital without any break). Placing in mind means not forgetting subsequently. Thus by engaging in the natural duty of the senses, the hurdles that are contrary to the nature of the self and those that come about incidentally, will disappear.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.3.10. Vaitta nal

*vaitta nāḷ varai ellai kuṟugic cenṟu eyttiḷaippadan munnam adaiminō paitta pāmbaṇaiyām tiruvēnkatam moytta sōlai moy pūm tadam tāḻvarē*

**Пословный перевод:**

paitta – having expanded hoods; pāmbu – anantan (ādiśēśan); aṇaiyān – sarvēśvaran who is having ādiśēśan as his bed; tiruvēnkatam – in tirumalai (that is glorified for its similarity in form to ādiśeśan); moytta – enriched; sōlai – garden; moy – beautiful; pū – having flowers; tadam – having space; tāḻvar – divine foot hills; vaitta – determined (for you); nāḷ – life span; varai – end; ellai – the beginning (of such end); kuṟugi – approach you; eyttu – (senses) wane; iḷaippadan munnam – (due to that) before (the heart) dies; senṟu – go (as said in nānmugan tiruvandādi 44 “pōm kumarar uḷḷeer purindu“); adaimin – reach

**Перевод:**

**tirumalai is glorified due to its similarity in its form to anantan (ādiśēśan) who is having expanded hoods and is the bed of sarvēśvaran; the spacious divine foot hills of such tirumalai is having enriched garden with beautiful flowers; before your senses wane and your heart dies (due to that) when the beginning of the end of your determined life span approaches you, go and reach such divine foot hills of tirumalai.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In tenth pāsuram, out of abundant joy, āḻvār requests everyone to take shelter of the divine foot hills of tirumalai.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār tells his own people “Accept tirumalai which is perfectly enjoyable, as the ultimate goal”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*In tenth pāsuram – āḻvār says “Since tirumalai is the goal, all of you take shelter of its foot hills when your senses are functioning well”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Tenth pāsuram. āḻvār says “Since tirumai āḻvār is the goal for everyone, all of you take shelter of the divine hill”. vaitta nāḷ varai ellai kuṟugic cenṟu eyttiḷaippadan munnam adaiminō paitta pāmbaṇaiyām tiruvēnkatam moytta sōlai moy pūm tadam tāḻvarē*

- *vaitt nāḷ varai ellai kuṟugi* – It is explained that [sarvēśvaran](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) gave this good body to the [cētana](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) (sentient being) to go to tirumalai and not to go to those worldly aspects which lead him to hell. It is explained in śrī viṣṇu darmam “*vicitrā dēhasampattir īśvarāya nivēditum \| pūrvamēva krutā brahman hastapādādisamyutā \|\|*” (Oh brāhmaṇa! To offer oneself and other materials, ātmā previously got connected to the amazing body with hands and legs). nampiḷḷai beautifully explains śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 40.5 “*sruśtastvam vanavāsāya*” (sumitrā says to lakśmaṇa – “you are given birth to accompany (and serve) śrī rāma in the forest”).
   - *sruśtatvam vanavāsāya* – lakśmaṇa said to sumitrā “perumāḷ (śrī rāma) is going to the forest to obey the orders of our father. I too will go along with him” and sumitrā replies “Did I give birth to you for you to stay in the palace while he is toiling in the forest? If you did this (go with śrī rāma), my purpose of giving birth to you is fulfilled. I gave birth to you to accompany him whenever he needs support”.
   - *svanuraktassurujjanē* – Are you not truly devoted to saintly people? So you protect śrī rāma who is like the heart for everyone. Also explained as “*suhrujjanē – rāmē*” – as you are truly devoted to śrī rāma since time immemorial, do I even have to tell you to go along with him?
   - *rāmē pramādam mā kārśī:* – But I have to instruct you in one thing. Don’t ever be forgetful. When lakśmaṇa asked “forgetful in what sense?”, sumitrā says
   - *putra bhrātari gaccati* – your brother would walk. By his stylish walk, he will steal our heart. By getting mesmerized in such walk, don’t forget your duty of protecting him. Similarly, this [cētana](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) was also placed in this material realm, to make him go to tirumalai \[and serve there\].
- *vaitta nāḷ varai ellai kuṟugic cenṟu* – Reaching the end of the life span which is determined by [īśvara](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/).
- *eyttu iḷaippadan munnam adaiminō* – Go to tirumalai while the desire to go there exists and before reaching the state “how pitiful! my senses are not allowing me to travel”.
- *paitta* … – [sarvēśvaran](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) who is having tiruvanantāḻvān (ādiśēśan) whose hoods are expanded due to the touch of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), as his bed. The abode which is dearer to emperumān even more than ādiśēśan. Alternatively, tirumalai āḻvār (the divine hill) himself is explained as tiruvanantāḻvān (ādiśēśan).
- *moytta* … – Before becoming weak, reach the divine foot hills which has enriched garden and ponds which have well blossomed flowers. Here weakness is of two types – becoming weak in heart \[losing the attachment for [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)\] and becoming weak in body \[old age etc\].

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.3.11. Tal parappi

*tāḷ parappi maṇ tāviya īsanai nīḷ poḻil kurugūrc catakōpan sol kēḻil āyirattu ippattum vallavar vāḻvar vāḻveydi jñālam pugaḻavē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tāḷ – divine feet; parappi – spread; maṇ – earth; tāviya – measured; īsanai – sarvēśvaran; nīḷ – high (well-grown); poḻil – having gardens; kurugūr – leader of āḻvārtirunagari; śatakōpan – nammāḻvār; sol – mercifully spoken by; kēḻ – match; il – not having; āyirattu – thousand pāsurams; ippattum – this decad also; vallavar – one who can recite (along with meditating upon the meanings); vāḻvu – the glorious wealth of kainkaryam (which āḻvār prayed for); eydi – attain; jñālam – the whole world; pugaḻ – praise; vāḻvar – live gloriously (in such servitude)

**Перевод:**

**nammāḻvār, the leader of āḻvārtirunagari which is having high (well-grown) gardens mercifully spoke about sarvēśvaran who spread his divine feet and measured the earth, in this thousand pāsurams; one who can recite (along with meditating upon the meanings) this decad also, will attain the glorious wealth of kainkaryam (which āḻvār prayed for) and will live gloriously (in such servitude) being praised by the whole world.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the end, āḻvār explains “those who practice this decad, will get all kinds of kainkaryams desired by me”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār explains acquiring the wealth of kainkaryam as the result of this decad.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*In the end, āḻvār explains “those who practice this decad, will get all kinds of kainkaryams at the divine feet of tiruvēnkatamudaiyān as desired by me”. tāḷ parappi maṇ tāviya īsanai nīḷ poḻil kurugūrc catakōpan sol kēḻil āyirattu ippattum vallavar vāḻvar vāḻveydi jñālam pugaḻavē*

- *tāḷ parappi maṇ tāviya īsanai* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) glorified [sarvēśvaran](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) who measured the rough terrain of earth that has forests and mountains, with his tender divine feet, like spreading soft flowers over a rough surface. But when asked “Did he not glorify tiruvēnkatamudaiyān \[why speak about vāmana/trivikrama here\]?”, āḻvārs have mercifully glorified tiruvēnkatamudaiyān as vāmanan as in periya tirumoḻji 1.10.4 “*koṇḍāy kuṟaḷāy nilam īradiyālē viṇ tōy sigarat turvēnkatamēya aṇḍā*” (Oh God of gods tiruvēnkatamudaiyān who is residing in tiruvēnkatam which has very tall peaks! you accepted the world by measuring them with your divine feet as a dwarf), tiruvāimoḻi 6.10.6 “*maṇ aḷanda iṇait tāmaraigaḷ*” (the divine lotus feet \[of tiruvēkankatamudaiyān\] which measured the earth) and in periya tirumoḻi 5.8.9 “*ulagam aḷanda ponnadiyē adainduyndu*” (reached the golden feet that measured the world and got uplifted); Also seeing at his posture which welcomes everyone to take shelter of his divine feet \[like trivikrama\] and because he gives himself to forest and monkeys \[the simplicity which is a quality of vāmana\], [tiruvēnkatamudaiyān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is explained as śrī vāmana.
- *nīḷ poḻil* … – Mercifully composed by [nammāḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) who is the leader of [āḻvārtirunagari](http://azhwarthirunagari.koyil.org/) which has well-grown shade-giving trees like a shelter for the divine feet which mercifully measured the world.
- *kēḻil āyiram …* – kēḻ – oppu (match). Those who can recite this matchless decad. The speciality of this decad is due to it being the decad where [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) prays for the kainkaryam that is suitable for the true nature of the [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/).
- *vāḻvar vāḻvu eydi* – Instead of it being just a desire/dream, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s desire of the wealth of servitude will materialize \[for those who recite this decad\] and they will enjoy the same.
- *jñālam pugaḻavē – vāḻvar* – \[They will also be glorified\] Like whole of ayōdyā praised lakśmaṇa “How special iḷaiya perumāḷ (lakśamaṇa) is! What great kainkaryam he got \[to serve śrī rāma\]!”.

Also explained as,

- *vāḻvu eydi – jñālam pugaḻa – vāḻvar* – Unlike glorifying a wealthy person even though his cruelty may still be in the heart, just to earn their livelihood, those who recite this decad will glorify [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) with great love \[after attaining great kainkaryam\], thinking “We are fortunate to glorify emperumān! what a life we have!”. Not just the most knovledgable persons, everyone one will affectionately glorify such devotees \[who practice this decad\].

Finally, nampiḷḷai summarizes the contents of this decad briefly.

- In the first pāsuram, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) longed to perform all kinds of kainkaryams to the divine feet of [tiruvēnkatamudaiyān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) at all times in all forms.
- In the second pāsuram, when asked “Is that not done in the special abode of paramapadam?”, he replied “Even those residents of paramapadam come here and serve him. So, we too can get that here”.
- In the third pāsuram, he said “If he can give himself to those who are filled with good qualities (nityasūris – eternally free souls), why would not he give himself to those who are filled with defects (samsāris – worldly people)?”.
- In the fourth pāsuram, he said “Giving himself to those nityasūris is nothing great for him in comparison to giving himself to me”.
- In the fifth pāsuram,  he said “Giving himself to me is not something great, when he cannot find anyone lower than me”.
- In the sixth pāsuram, he said “as we engage in servitude towards him, our hurdles will be naturally eliminated”.
- In the seventh pāsuram, he said “tirumalai āḻvār (divine hill) himself will bestow this kainkaryam to us”.
- In the eighth pāsuram, he said “this tirumalai āḻvār would eliminate our hurdles and also will bestow himself to us”.
- In the ninth pāsuram,  āḻvār said “is tirumalai āḻvār required to do this? relationship to the one who is related to tirumalai āḻvār (i.e., [tiruvēnkatamudaiyān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)) is sufficient”.
- In the tenth pāsuram, he said “Since the lord himself desires for tirumalai, all the servants of the lord should also take shelter of tirumalai”.
- In the end, he explains the result and concludes the decad.

## 3.4 Pugalum nal oruvan

## 3.4.1. Pugalum nal oruvan

*pugaḻum nal oruvan enkō poruvil sīr bhūmi enkō tigaḻum taṇ paravai enkō tī enkō vāyu enkō nigaḻum ākāsam enkō nīḷ sudar iraṇḍum enkō igaḻvil ivvanaittum enkō kaṇṇanaik kūvumāṟē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kaṇṇanai – kriṣṇa; kūvumāṟu – the method of explaining him; pugaḻum – praised by (vēdams and vaidikas); nal – having distinguished forms and wealth; oruvan – advitīya – unparalleled one; enkō – should I say?; poru – match; il – not having; sīr – having completeness in all qualities (such as bearing everything etc); bhūmi enkō – should I say earth?; tigaḻum – radiant (due to its purity); taṇ – naturally cool; paravai enkō – should I say water forms?; tī enkō – should I say fire (that removes coolness)?; vāyu enkō – should I say air (which is the cause for prāṇa (vital air) etc)?; nigaḻum – proximate (surrounding all those that were born out of it); ākāsam enkō – should I say ether?; nīḷ – (through the rays) reaching radiantly everywhere; sudar iraṇḍum enkō – should I say the two luminous objects (moon and sun); igaḻvil – without leaving out anything; ivai – these; anaittum enkō – should I say all?

**Перевод:**

**While speaking about the method of explaining the unparalleled kriṣṇa who is praised (by vēdams and vaidikas) and is having distinguished forms and wealth – should I say he is the matchless one who is having completeness in all qualities (such as bearing everything etc)? should I say he is the radiant (due to its purity) naturally cool water forms? should I say he is fire (that removes coolness)? should I say he is air (which is the cause for prāṇa (vital air) etc)? Should I say he is proximate ether (surrounding all those that were born out of it)? should I say he is the two luminous objects (moon and sun) which are reaching radiantly everywhere (through the rays)? should I say he is all of these without leaving out anything?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In first pāsuram – āḻvār briefly and mercifully explains the principles that are explained in this decad.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*In first pāsuram – āḻvār briefly and mercifully explains emperumān being the prakāri (ātmā) of the great elements and their variegated forms.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*In first pāsuram – āḻvār captures bhagavān‘s qualities and panca bhūtams which are the cause for the material realm and briefly and mercifully explains the principles that are explained in detail in this decad. pugaḻum nal oruvan enkō poruvil sīr bhūmi enkō tigaḻum taṇ paravai enkō tī enkō vāyu enkō nigaḻum ākāsam enkō nīḷ sudar iraṇḍum enkō igaḻvil ivvanaittum enkō kaṇṇanaik kūvumāṟē*

- *pugaḻum nal oruvan enkō* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) mercifully explains the meanings that were propounded from [tiruvāimoḻi 1.1.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/03/thiruvaimozhi-1-1-1-uyarvara-uyarnalam/) “*uyarvaṟa uyar nalam*” until now, in a single phrase. Should I say that he is the unique person who has distinguished qualities and is praised by śruti (vēdam), smruti, itihāsa etc? enkō means “should I say?”. First āḻvār explains the glories of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) due to being with auspicious qualities and further explains his wealth.
- *pugaḻum nal oruvan enkō* – *nal* – ānandam (bliss) – Should I say one who is having auspicious qualities such as bliss etc? *oruvan* – unique – Should I say one who has none equal or greater?
- *poruvil …* – Like [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) enjoyed the beauty of his divine face and divine crown as in [tiruvāimoḻi 3.1.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/07/thiruvaimozhi-3-1-1-mudichchodhiyay/) “*mudiccōdiyāy unadu mugaccōdi malarndaduvō*“, since there is match between his auspicious qualities and wealth, after enjoying his qualities, he is enjoying [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s wealth. *poru* – *oppu* – match. *il* – not present. Should I say he is the matchless earth which has qualities such as patience etc? Since it is said in “*padbhyām bhūmi:*” (Earth was created from the divine feet of [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)), āḻvār is saying it to be matchless.
- *tigaḻum* … – bhūmi which was explained before is hard by nature. To use it effectively, it should be loosened up. So, water which will loosen up earth is explained. Should I call him as water which has the radiance of being the cause and also being the one which removes fatigue?
- *tī enkō* – If that loosened up earth is still not usable, fire will help prepare it better. Should I call him as fire which has flames that rise up?
- *vāyu enkō* – If that is too hot, we need air to dry it. Should I call him as air which dries?
- *nigaḻum* – To breathe, everyone needs space. nigaḻum – present. Two explanations – 1) even when the four elements (earth, water, fire, air) are destroyed, ether exists (consuming all other elements); 2) alternatively, ether is present such that all other elements rest on it. Thus, the panca bhūtams (five great elements) which are cause, are explained.
- *nīḷ sudara iraṇḍum enkō* – Now, as a sample to the effect \[of the five great elements\], moon and sun are explained. Sun is present to extract the water from everything \[sucks the water and evaporates\] and moon is present to eliminate the fatigue for everyone \[pleasant\].
- *igaḻvil* – Should I say [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is everything without leaving anything? kriṣṇa himself said in [śrī bhagavat gītā](http://githa.koyil.org/) 10.39 “… *mayā vinā yatasyāt na tadasti …*” (I am the seed for everything, movable/immovable does not exist without me). Alternatively – Since all these appear as his wealth instead of just some objects, should I say all of these are acceptable instead of being dismissible?
- *kaṇṇanaik kūvumāṟē* – For [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/), saying “*poruvil bhūmi*” \[etc\] is not different from arjuna saying “*hē kriṣṇa*” (Oh [kriṣṇa](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)!).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.4.2. Kuvumaru

*kūvumāṟaṟiya māttēn kunṟangaḷ anaittum enkō mēvu sīr māri enkō viḷangu tāragaigaḷ enkō nāviyal kalaigaḷ enkō jñāna nal āvi enkō pāvu sīrk kaṇṇan emmān pangayak kaṇṇanaiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kunṟangaḷ anaittum – all mountains (that are effects of earth due to their hard nature); mēvu sīr – having glorifiable qualities (due to helping all living beings) and an effect of water; māri – rain; viḷangu – effect of fire (due to its radiance); tāragaigaḷ – stars etc; (effect of air) nā – in the tongue; iyal – being created; kalaigaḷ – vidyāstānams (fields of knowledge); jñānam – for in-depth knowledge; nallāvi – being the śarīra (body/tool), the sounds which are effects of ākāśa (ether); enkō – Should I say or call him?; pāvu – vast; sīr – having qualities and wealth; kaṇṇan – one who is easily accessible for me; pangayak kaṇṇan emmānai – my lord who won over me by the beauty of his lotus eyes; kūvumāṟu – method of speaking about him; aṟiya māttēn – I am not knowing

**Перевод:**

**I am not knowing the method of speaking about my lord who won over me by the beauty of his lotus eyes, who is easily accessible for me, who is having vast (number of) qualities and wealth. Should I call him as all mountains (that are effects of earth due to their hard nature)? Should I call him as rain that is having glorifiable qualities (due to helping all living beings) and an effect of water? Should I call him as stars etc that are effect of fire (due to its radiance)? Should I call him vidyāstānams (fields of knowledge) that are created in the tongue? Should I call him the sounds which are the śarīra (body/tool) for in-depth knowledge and effects of ākāśa (ether)?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In second pāsuram – āḻvār explains the (transformed) effects of five great elements in proper order and explains bhagavān being owner of those.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār explains the effects of the five great elements which were discussed in previous pāsuram.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. kūvumāṟaṟiya māttēn kunṟangaḷ anaittum enkō mēvu sīr māri enkō viḷangu tāragaigaḷ enkō nāviyal kalaigaḷ enkō jñāna nal āvi enkō pāvu sīrk kaṇṇan emmān pangayak kaṇṇanaiyē*

- *kūvarmāṟu* – I don’t know how to compile a song on him to call him. kūvudal – calling. It is said in periyāḻvār tiruvāimoḻi 1.4.5 “*kūvak kūva nī pōdiyēl*” (even as I am calling, you keep going). Since [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) acquired his fully expanded knowledge by the causeless grace of [bhagvān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) \[instead of self-effort\] all aspects are known to him. It is due to overwhelming devotion he is unable to speak; ōr, he is unable to speak since [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s wealth is boundless and cannot be easily spoken.
- *kunṟangaḷ* – Mountains are the effect of Earth (cause) that was mentioned as “*poruvil sīr bhūmi*” \[in previous pāsuram\]. It looks like all the hardness of earth came together to be as the mountain. Should I call him as the mountains that support the earth?
- *mēvu sīr māri enkō* – This is the effect of water that was identified in previous pāsuram as “*taṇ paravai*“. Should I call him as the cloud which has beauty and coolness that attract those who see it. Clouds are desirable for [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) in two ways – first, they are wealth of [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) and second, they are also comparable \[in some sense\] to physical form and compassion.
- *viḷangu tāragaigaḷ enkō* – Should I call him as the shining stars etc which are effect of fire that was explained in previous pāsuram as “*tī enkō*“? Stars are a sample for all illuminous objects.
- *nāviyal kalaigaḷ enkō* – This the effect of vāyu (air) as highlighted in previous pāsuram as “*vāyu enkō*“. The 64 branches of knowledge which were derived (spoken/taught) using the tongue. \[īsn’t sound an effect of ether? Yes. But \] Manifestation of sound happens as an effect of air \[different frequency of air manifests different sounds\]. All efforts depend on air to succeed.
- *jñāna nal āvi enkō* – śabdam (śāstram) is the quality of ether which is said in previous pāsuram as “*ākāsam enkō*“. The quality in the cause is the cause for the quality in the effect. īsn’t the whiteness in the thread the cause for the whiteness in the cloth \[produced from that thread\]? Also, since ākāśam (ether) is the only element remaining \[among the five great elements\], this should point to ether only. When it says āvi (ātmā), it indicates body (sounds, the effect) through lakśaṇā (indication). śabdam (word, śāstram) is laden with artam (meanings). [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says “*nallāvi*” (good sound), since there is no defect in śabdam unlike our senses.
- *pāvu sīrk kaṇṇan* – kriṣṇa who is filled with auspicious qualities that are spread everywhere as said in rī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 21.20 “*vidita:*” (śrī rāma is well known as one who is well anchored in dharma).
- *emmān* … – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) keeps [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) attracted towards him by showing his beautiful eyes. For āḻvār, there is no distinction between “*pangayak kaṇṇan*” (*lotus eyed lord*) and “*kunṟangaḷ anaittum*” (all mountains) \[he sees everything as belonging to [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)\]. Here “*kunṟangaḷ anaittum*” is explained as a comparison of bhagavān’s form to the the form of mountains and “*mēvu sīr māri*” is explained as a comparison of bhagavān’s complexion to the color of clouds – this is similar to how it is explained in periya tirumoḻi 7.10.1 “*perumpuṟakkadal*” (bhakta vatsalan emperumān in [tirukkaṇṇamangai](http://thirukkannamangai.koyil.org/) divya dēśam is explained in one point of view to be looking similar to a great ocean instead of explaining him as the ocean itself by sāmānādikaraṇa nyāyam\].

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.4.3. Pangayak kannan

*pangayak kaṇṇan enkō pavaḷac cevvāyan enkō angadir adiyan enkō anjana vaṇṇan enkō sengadir mudiyan enkō tirumaṟu mārban enkō sangu sakkarattan enkō sādi māṇikkattaiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

sādi – produced from a mine; māṇikkattai – having a precious-gem like (very radiant) form; pangayam – like a lotus; kaṇṇan – having eye; pavaḷam – like a coral; sem – reddish; vāyan – one who is having lips/mouth; am – beautiful; kadir – radiant; adiyan – having divine feet; anjana(m) – like black pigment; vaṇṇan – one who is having complexion; sem – reddish; kadir – having rays; mudiyan – one who is having divine crown; tiru – in the abode of lakśmī; maṟu – scar (caused by śrīvatsa mole); mārban – one who is having divine chest; sangu cakkarattan – having completeness in weapons (to protect the private quarters of his divine consort); enkō – should I call him?

**Перевод:**

**Should I call emperumān as one who is having a precious-gem (that was  produced from a mine) like (very radiant) form? Should I call him as the one who is having a lotus like eye? Should I call him as the one who is having coral like reddish lips/mouth? Should I call him as the one who is having beautiful radiant divine feet? Should I call him as the one who is having black pigment like complexion? Should I call him as the one who is having  divine crown that is having reddish rays? Should I call him as the one who is having the divine chest which is the abode of śrī mahālakśmi, that is having a scar (caused by śrīvatsa mole)? Should I call him as the one who is having completeness in weapons (to protect the private quarters of his divine consort)?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In third pāsuram – To equate bhagavān‘s wealth of material realm with his spiritual divine form that is decorated with divine ornaments etc, āḻvār speaks about the beauty of emperumān‘s divine form amidst speaking about the material realm. It is the same purpose when he speaks about his distinguished/special nature in other pāsurams also. kadir means oḷi (radiance).*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār meditates upon emperumān‘s distinguished form amidst these prakārams (material forms) and the similarity in them.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Third pāsuram. Since there is no difference between bhagavān having the whole creation as his body and having distinguished divine form, āḻvār enjoys him being the cause of the universe and his divine form. pangayak kaṇṇan enkō pavaḷac cevvāyan enkō angadir adiyan enkō anjana vaṇṇan enkō sengadir mudiyan enkō tirumaṟu mārban enkō sangu sakkarattan enkō sādi māṇikkattaiyē*

- *pangayak kaṇṇan enkō* – He engages with the cētanas (sentient beings) through his eyes. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is identifying the beauty of the eyes which made first contact with him.
- *pavaḷac cevvāyan enkō* – Even if someone escapes such glance, they will be captured by his smile – that is explained here.
- *am kadir adiyan enkō* – Those who are captivated by his glance and smile, will fall at his divine feet – that is explained here. Should I call him as the one who is having beautifully shining divine feet?
- *anjana vaṇṇan enkō* – Those who fall at those divine feet get to enjoy the beautiful form – that is explained here.
- *sem kadir mudiyan enkō* – īsn’t it the divine crown that highlights his supremacy and thus the experience with such supreme person is apt \[for the jīvātmā\]?
- *tiru maṟu mārban enkō* – When one observes the divine crown, one may shy away from [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) thinking about his supremely independent nature. īsn’t it the relationship with śrī mahālakśmi that eliminates that fear \[from the jīvātmā and lets him approach with confidence that tāyār would facilitate his union with bhagavān\]? Should I call him as the one with śrī mahālakśmi and the mole in his chest?
- *sangu cakkarattan enkō* – For those who fear unnecessarily for the safety of the divine couple, aren’t the divine weapons \[conch and disc\] the ones which instill confidence in them and remove their fear, by protecting the divine couple? Even they \[[periyāḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/periyazhwar/) in [tiruppallāṇḍu 2](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/06/thiruppallandu-2-adiyomodum/)\] said “*vadivāy nin vala mārbinil vāḻginṟa mangaiyum pallāṇḍu*” (Let tāyār who resides in the right side of your chest live forever) and immediately followed it up with “*sudarāḻiyum pallāṇḍu*” (Let the radiant disc live forever).
- *sādi māṇikkattaiyē* – Instead of a counterfeit gem, it is real gem which was fetched from a mine. Like that real gem, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) too has no defects and has natural beauty.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.4.4. Sadi manikkam

*sādi māṇikkam enkō savi koḷ pon muttam enkō sādi nal vairam enkō tavivil sīr viḷakkam enkō ādiyam sōdi enkō ādiyam purudan enkō ādumil kālattendai accudan amalanaiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ādum – anything; il – not there; kālattu – during the time of deluge; endai – due to the causeless/eternal relationship, being the ātmā of cit and acit that are in unmanifested state; accudan – not having any loss/decay (in his nature, qualities etc); amalanai – one who is the opposite of all defects (i.e., not being affected by the defects of cit and acit, though he pervades them all); sādi – having the distinguished quality of being born/found in a mine; māṇikkam – precious gem; savi – radiance; koḷ – having; pon – golden; muttam – pearls; sādi – found in mines; nal – distinguished in comparison to other ratnams (gems); vayiram – diamond; tavi(r)vil – indestructible; sīr – having shining qualities; viḷakkam – lamp; ādi – being the primordial; am – having qualities such as beauty etc; sōdi – having a radiant divine form; ādi – being the primary person; am – having qualities such as ānandam (bliss) etc; purudan – supreme lord; enkō – Should I say/call?

**Перевод:**

**emperumān is the one who is the ātmā of cit and acit that are in unmanifested state due to the causeless/eternal relationship during the time of deluge without having any loss/decay (in his nature, qualities etc) when nothing else is there; he is the opposite of all defects (i.e., not being affected by the defects of cit and acit, though he pervades them all). Should I call such emperumān as precious gem having the distinguished quality of being born/found in a mine? Should I call him as radiant golden pearls that are found in mines \[i.e., best quality\]? Should I call him as diamond that is distinguished in comparison to other ratnams (gems)? Should I call him an indestructible lamp that is having shining qualities? Should I call him the primordial radiant divine form that is having qualities such as beauty etc? Should I call him the primary/supreme lord who is having qualities such as ānandam (bliss) etc?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In fourth pāsuram – āḻvār explains emperumān having radiant gems etc as his wealth.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Fourth pāsuram. When one of our pūrvācāryas asked another one \[presumably māṟanēri nambi since similar incident is identified in mudal tiruvandādi 1st pāsuram with reference to him\] “Please tell me a way to remember emperumān” and he replies “I will do that. But can you tell me a way to forget him?”. This means anything other than bhagavān does not acquire its form and name without his presence, anything that is seen is seen as a wealth/form of him. Just like for jāti (species/category) and guṇam (quality), there is no stiti (existence) and upalambha (recognition) without the \[particular\] entity \[that bears the category and quality\], though dravya \[separate objects – sentient and insentient beings\], without bhagavān there is no existence and recognition – this is based on pramāṇam \[authentic quotes from śāstram such as “yasya ātmā śarīram, yasya prutvī śarīram” (ātmā is bhagavān’s body, Earth is bhagavān’s body) – without the soul, the bodies cannot exist\],. While others are focussed on the viśēśaṇam (attributes/forms – sentient and insentient beings), our āḻvārs/ācāryas are focussed on viśēśyam (object/paramātmā – bhagavān). Because of importance for viśēśyam (bhagavān), only he is seen in everything. This is the nature of one who has heard vēdāntam. emperumānār too explained this in vēdārta sangraham “vēdānta śravaṇē na hi vyutpatti: pūryatē” (Only by hearing vēdāntam, one’s knowledge becomes complete). With this, all objects being prakāram (form) and bhagavān being prakāri (entity) is explained. In this too, as explained in śrī bhagavat gītā 10.41 “yadyadvibhūtimat satvam śrīmadūrjitamēva vā \| tattadēvāvagacca tvam mama tējōmśa sambhavam” (You shall know that any object that has wealth/form, glories, efforts in engaging in auspicious activities, all of them came from a fraction of my radiance), though everything is his wealth, he selected the best among them and highlighted them as his wealth; similarly āḻvār too is enjoying priceless gems etc being his wealth. sādi māṇikkam enkō savi koḷ pon muttam enkō sādi nal vairam enkō tavivil sīr viḷakkam enkō ādiyam sōdi enkō ādiyam purudan enkō ādumil kālattendai accudan amalanaiyē*

- *sādi māṇikkam enkō* – Should I call him as a gem that was fetched from the best source/mine?
- *savi koḷ pon muttam enkō* – If savi is taken as an adjective for pon (gold), it means radiance; if taken as an adjective for muttam (pearls), it means beauty and coolness. Should I call him as radiant gold or beautiful pearl?
- *sādi nal vayiram enkō* – Should I call him as the best diamond that was fetched from the best source/mine?
- *tavivil sīr viḷakkam enkō* – tavivu means viccēdam (break/end). Should I call him as the lamp that is having endless beauty? This can be taken as explaining the source of light and the light itself – for example, both āditya (sun) etc and their radiance.
- *ādi am sōdi enkō* – As said in jitantē stōtram “*kāryāṇām kāraṇam pūrvam …*” (They know that your paramapadam is the cause of all effects …), Should I call you as the owner of paramapadam that is being present even before the creation of these \[radiant objects in material realm\], is itself being in a singular/unchanging form, and is infinitely radiant as said in mahābhāratam āraṇya parvam “*atyarkānaladīptam tat stānam …*” (śrīman nārāyaṇan’s divine abode parampadam is many thousands of times more radiant than the sun and moon)? When asked “How is paramapadam the cause?”, it is explained that “when something exists exactly before the effect, that is called the cause” \[since paramapadam always existed, when the material realm is created (transformed from subtle to gross manifestation), the paramapadam is seen as cause here\]. Alternatively (second explanation), ādi refers to [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) being īśvara (controller) too. Here ādi (cause) is also explained based on astrabhūśaṇa adyāyam in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam. There it is explained that śrīvatsa \[divine mole in bhagavān’s chest\] bears the primordial matter, śrīkaustuba \[jewel in his chest\] bears the collection of all ātmās. Third explanation – That divine radiant form is also part of the nitya vibhūti (paramapadam). But why is nitya vibhūti (spiritual realm) mentioned here while talking about the gems etc which are in leelā vibhūti (material realm)? That is because, for [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) both feel the same \[since he considers both to be the wealth of emperumān\].
- *ādi am purudan enkō* – Now, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is talking about the vibhūtimān (owner of the vibhūti (wealth)).  Should I call him as [sarvēśvaran](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) who is the cause of all, is together with both vibhūtis (spiritual and material realms), and is known by the names/words puruśa and puruśōttama \[in śāstram\]?
- *ādum il …* – ādumil kālam – samsāra kālam (that time when I did not have anything good in me like advēśam (no hatred), ābhimukhyam (friendliness) towards [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)). That is, \[*ādumil kālattu*\] at that time when I had nothing in me to attain him, \[endai\] he himself announced his eternal fatherly relationship with me, \[*accudan*\] protected me without leaving me ever, \[*amalan*\] doing all these unconditionally without expecting anything from me in return and uplifted me as if it is his fortune; Alternative explanation – \[*ādumil kālattu*\] during praḷaya kālam (the time of deluge when nothing exists) when everything is in subtle state \[where I cannot do anything\], \[*endai*\] considering that he is the lord, when there is no name or form for these ātmās, \[*accudan*\] bearing them and protecting them, \[*amalan*\] though he mingled with everyone as one with these [cit](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) and [acit](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/09/thathva-thrayam-achith-what-is-matter/), still their defects did not touch him. bhagavān when pervaded in all cit (sentient) and acit (insentient) whether they are in gross (manifested) forms or in subtle (unmanifested) forms, their defects don’t touch him. This is due to the fact that bhagavān is present in them out of his own will/desire \[unlike jīvātmās who enter into a material body due to being pushed by their karma – so their knowledge gets impacted by the type of their body and the bodily activities\].

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.4.5. Accudan amalan

*accudan amalan enkō adiyavar vinai kedukkum naccu mā marundam enkō nalam kadal amudam enkō accuvaik katti enkō aṟusuvai adisil enkō neyccuvait tēṟal enkō kani enkō pāl enkēnō?*

**Пословный перевод:**

accudan – one who is having sweetness that never lets go of those who enjoy him; amalan – having purity (of letting us enjoy him, as a fortune for him); adiyavar – those who are related to him; vinai – suffering of not attaining the desired results; kedukkum – that which eliminates; naccum – that which is desired (due to its taste); mā marundam – medicine acquired from cow; nal – (due to the connection of milk) being distinguished; am – (due to connection with bhagavān) being pleasant to the eyes; kadal – in the ocean; amudam – nectar (which was churned and fetched by him); a – that nectar’s; suvai – having taste; katti – sugar (cane) block; aṟusuvai – having six types of tastes (madura (sweet), amla (sour), lavaṇa (salty), katu (pungent), kaśāya (astringent), tikta (bitter)); adisil – rice; ney – of ghee; suvai – having taste; tēṟal – honey; kani – fruit (which cannot be left unconsumed due to its ripened state); pāl – milk (which has natural taste); enkō (enkēnō) – should I say/call?

**Перевод:**

**Should I call emperumān as the one who is having sweetness that never lets go of those who enjoy him? Should I call him as having purity (of letting us enjoy him, as a fortune for him)? Should I call him as the medicine acquired from cow which is desired (due to its taste) and which eliminates the suffering of not attaining the desired results for those who are related to him? Should I call him as the nectar (which was churned and fetched by him) that was found in the (due to the connection of milk) distinguished ocean that is (due to connection with bhagavān) pleasant to the eyes? Should I call him as sugar (cane) block that is having the taste of that nectar \[found in the milk ocean\]? Should I call him as rice having six types of tastes (madura (sweet), amla (sour), lavaṇa (salty), katu (pungent), kaśāya (astringent), tikta (bitter))? Should I call him as honey having the taste of ghee? Should I call him fruit (which cannot be left unconsumed due to its ripened state)? Should I call him milk (which has natural taste)?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In fifth pāsuram – āḻvār says “All tasty objects are his wealth”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. accudan amalan enkō adiyavar vinai kedukkum naccu mā marundam enkō nalam kadal amudam enkō accuvaik katti enkō aṟusuvai adisil enkō neyccuvait tēṟal enkō kani enkō pāl enkēnō?*

- *accudan amalan enkō* – Should I call him as the one who never loses his state of being with nitya vibhūti (spiritual realm)? ōr as the one who is the opposite of all inauspicious qualities and the abode of all auspicious qualities?
- *adiyavar …* – For his devotees, not having to grieve that he is too far away (in a distant abode named śrīvaikuṇṭam), he is of the nature that he will jump right at the banks of the pond when the elephant was in trouble.
- *adiyavar vinai kedukkum* – one who protects by eliminating the troubles of those who are fully dependent on him.
- *naccu mā marundam* – We can be faithful that he will come and protect us when we are in danger, instead of having to go and search for a solution at the time of danger \[like how hanumān had to go and search for herbs in the mountains when indrajit downed śrī rāma and lakśmaṇa into an unconscious state using brahmāstram\].
- *naccu mā marundam* – the medicine that is desired.
- *mā marundam* – Great medicine. Three explanations:
   - The medicine is far more powerful than the disease. That is, just by smelling the medicine, the disease will be cured.
   - Being a single medicine that needs to be fed only once to cure the disease.
   - The medicine which does not demand any strict diet from the patient. That is, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) would ignore those sins that were committed by his devotees unknowingly. If a devotee \[surrendered person\] knowingly commits a sin, it will contradict the knowledge he acquired \[about his own nature, [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s nature etc\]. After knowing the true nature of [self](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/), one will not engage in such \[sinful, worldly\] activities; still, since the  body, that is a hurdle to one’s spirituality, continues to exist, being bewildered by ignorance, he may engage in such activities \[like sugrīva who ignored his promise to help śrī rāma, but [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) forgave him at that time since he realized his mistake subsequently\]; subsequently, if he realizes his mistake, he will atone and withdraw from such activities; instead, if he continues to commit mistakes knowingly, it can be concluded that he has not acquired the true knowledge.
   - *nalam kadal amudam enkō* – Should I call him as the nectar that came out without churning the ocean?
   - *accuvaik katti enkō* – Since this “*katti*” (block) is indicated after nectar, this should be a sugar block. Should I call him as a sweet sugar block?
   - *aṟusuvai* – The six tastes are sweet, sour, salty, pungent, astringent and bitter. Should I call him as the rice porridge that has all these six tastes?
   - *neyccuvait tēṟal enkō* – *ney* – abundance. Abundantly tasty honey. Should I call him as tasty ghee \[here *ney* is considered directly as ghee\]?  Should I call him abundantly tasty honey?
   - *kani* *enkō pāl enkēnō* – Should I call him a fruit that is very sweet? Should I call him milk?

## 3.4.6. Palenko

*pāl enkō nāngu vēdap payan enkō samaya nīdi nūl enkō nudangu kēḷvi isai enkō ivaṟṟuḷ nalla mēl enkō vinaiyin mikka payan enkō kaṇṇan enkō māl enkō māyan enkō vānavar ādiyaiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vānavar – for all dēvas; ādiyai – one who is the cause for their existence etc; nāngu vēdam – vēdams’; pāl – classifications such as śākā (branch) etc; nāngu vēdam – such four vēdams’; payan – result; samayam – establishing the meanings; nīdi – explaining logic; nūl – mīmāmsā śāstram; nudangu – engaging (the listeners); kēḷvi – having sounds; isai – songs/tunes; ivaṟṟuḷ – in these (which have been discussed); nalla – distinguished; mēl – unlimited, wondrous enjoyment; vinaiyil – not matching the effort; mikka – great; payan – result; kaṇṇan – kriṣṇa (who is blissful, in the form of such result); māl – who enjoys (those who enjoy him) with great love; māyan – having matching amazing activities; enkō – should I call?

**Перевод:**

**What should I call emperumān who is the cause for existence etc of all dēvas? Should I call him as classifications such as śākā (branch) etc of vēdams? Should I call him as the result of such four vēdams? Should I call him as mīmāmsā śāstram which explains logic and establishes the meanings? Should I call him as songs/tunes that are having sounds that engage (the listeners)? Should I call him as the distinguished unlimited, wondrous enjoyment in these (which have been discussed)? Should I call him as the great result that does not match the \[minimal\] effort? Should I call him as kriṣṇa (who is blissful, in the form of such result) who enjoys (those who enjoy him) with great love and has matching amazing activities?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In sixth pāsuram – āḻvār speaks about emperumān having the wealth of all sound forms, be it prose or musical poetry, starting with vēdam.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. pāl enkō nāngu vēdap payan enkō samaya nīdi nūl enkō nudangu kēḷvi isai enkō ivaṟṟuḷ nalla mēl enkō vinaiyin mikka payan enkō kaṇṇan enkō māl enkō māyan enkō vānavar ādiyaiyē*

- *pāl enkō* – Reminded of the taste that was discussed in the previous pāsuram.
- *nāngu vēdap payan enkō* – Should I call him as vēdam which is the essence of all authentic scriptures? Only if there is a portion of vēdam which glorifies any one else, it should be said “result of four vēdams”. Since that is not there, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying “the result of vēdam which has four different aspects”. Alternatively, it is explained as – since [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is fully explained while explaining the nature of worship and the object of worship, since there is nothing except him in vēdam in all four corners of it, he says so. emperumān himself said in [śrī bhagavat gītā](http://githa.koyil.org/) 15.15 “*vēdaiśca sarvair ahamēva vēdya:*” (In all of vēdams, I am only fully explained).
- *samaya nīdi nūl enkō* – Should I call him as the itihāsas (epics) and purāṇas (ancient history) which establish the principles of vaidika samayam (vēdic religion)? It is said in bārhaspatya smruti “*itihāsapurāṇābhyām vēdam samupabrumhayēt*” (vēdam should be explained through itihāsams and purāṇams).
- *nudangu kēḷvi isai enkō* – Should I call him as tunes/songs having sounds which mesmerize those who heard them?
- *ivaṟṟuḷ nalla mēl enkō* – Should I call him as something that is beyond these great aspects that have been highlighted? He should tell about all, but will not do so \[since he is going to explain further that he is greater than the means that help achieve him\].
- *vinaiyil mikka payan enkō* – Should I call him as many great results which are accomplished by insignificant efforts? Like planting a handful of paddy seeds and reaping a huge harvest as result. \[As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 18.3\] In this side \[of [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)\], there is “*mithra bhāva”* (pretending to be friend) and in that side \[of [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)\], there is “*na tyajēyam*” (I will never leave you).
- *kaṇṇan enkō* – Should I call him as kriṣṇa who said “I am there for you”, as in [śrī bhagavat gītā](http://githa.koyil.org/) 18.66 “mā suca:” (do not grieve)? kriṣṇa is the one who tells “All you need to do is to not reject what I provide you and accept the same. I will be there for you”.
- *māl enkō* – Should I call him as totally mad for his devotees? While reciting this ślōkam ([śrī bhagavat gītā](http://githa.koyil.org/) 18.66), he did not say before “*idam tē nātapaskāya*” (Do not reveal this to those who are not austere … – [śrī bhagavat gītā](http://githa.koyil.org/) 18.67). Like he warned in śrī bhagavat gītā 9.1 “*idam tu tē guhya tamam pravakśyāmi*” (I am speaking to you this most confidential knowledge about bhakti yōgam) \[before instructing bhakti yōgam\], it should have been proper to speak “*idam tē nātapaskāya*” before revealing it \[i.e., the principle of surrender in carama ślōkam, that is śrī bhagavat gītā 18.66\]. Instead, he first spoke about surrender and then said “*idam tē nātapaskāya*” after that. When [nanjīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nanjiyar/) asked [bhattar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/parasara-bhattar/) “Why did he do like this?”, bhattar mercifully explained “Unable to bear witnessing draupati’s untied hair \[she vowed to knot her hair only after the kauravas were killed and it is generally considered inauspicious to have the hair left untied. Also draupati is so very dear to kriṣṇa that he could not bear her grief at all\], wanting to have it tied, without knowing what to do, he brought out the great principle in the open battle field; after doing so, he contemplated about the confidentiality of the principle, and thought ‘who is qualified to hear this? I have thrown a priceless gem in the ocean’ and said ‘pataṇ pataṇ’ \[a phrase that identifies he worried greatly\]”.
- *māyan enkō* – Should I call him as some one who performs amazing activities for his devotees such as going as messenger and being their charioteer? mahābhāratam udyōka parvam “*krutārtā bhunjatē dūtā:*” (kriṣṇa to duryōdana – Messenger will eat in the home and accept the worship (of the host) after completing their task. If you fulfill my desire, I will accept your food/worship).
- *vānavar ādiyaiyē* – What can I say about [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is the cause for existence etc of brahmā et al, who considers me as the cause for his existence etc?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.4.7. Vanavar adi

*vānavar ādi enkō  vānavar deyvam enkō vānavar bōgam enkō vānavar muṟṟum enkō ūnamil selvam enkō ūnamil suvarggam enkō ūnamil mōkkam enkō oḷi maṇivaṇṇanaiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

oḷi – radiant; maṇi – like a ruby; vaṇṇanai – having form; vānavar – dēvas (who are engaged in enjoyment); ādi – creator; vānavar – their; deyvam – vorśippable god; vānavar – their; bōgam – enjoyment (which is the result of their worship); vānavar – their; muṟṟum – all types of protection; ūnamil – perennial; selvam – wealth; ūnamil – that which lasts till the end of world; suvarggam – heavenly abode; ūnamil – vast (unlike kaivalyam which is limited); mōkkam – blissful mōkśam (liberation); enkō – should I say/call?

**Перевод:**

**What should I call that emperumān who has a radiant ruby like form? Should I call him the creator of dēvas (who are engaged in enjoyment)? Should I call him their vorśippable god? Should I call him their enjoyment (which is the result of their worship)? Should I call him their all types of protection? Should I call him the perennial wealth? Should I call him the heavenly abode which lasts till the end of world? Should I call him the vast (unlike kaivalyam which is limited) blissful mōkśam (liberation)? Some explain vānavar as nityasūris also.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In seventh pāsuram – āḻvār speaks about emperumān being the owner of puruśārtams (goals) such as aiśvaryam etc.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār mercifully explains bhagavān‘s wealth of worldly enjoyment and liberation.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. vānavar ādi enkō  vānavar deyvam enkō vānavar bōgam enkō vānavar muṟṟum enkō ūnamil selvam enkō ūnamil suvarggam enkō ūnamil mōkkam enkō oḷi maṇivaṇṇanaiyē*

- *vānavar ādi enkō* – In previous pāsuram, “*vānavar ādi*” was explained as creator of brahmā et al; here it is explained as the controller of nityasūris (eternally free souls of paramapadam) and [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) being the cause of their existence etc. While the words are same, why is it explained differently in the two pāsurams? For brahmā et al, he helps them during their creation and subsequently lets them go and do their activities; but for nityasūris, as said in tiruvāimoḻi 6.7.1 “*ellām kaṇṇan*” (everything is kriṣṇa), he remains everything for them. They too consider kriṣṇa as everything as said in śrī bhagavat gītā 7.19 “*vāsudēvassarvam*” (vāsudēva is everything).
- *vānavar ādi enkō* – Should I call him the sattāhētu (cause for the existence) of nityasūris? What does it mean to be the cause for their existence? Are they not eternal already? Whether they are eternal or not, it is only his eternal desire that makes them eternal; if that desire changes, even those nityasūris’ eternity will be lost. As said in nānmugan tiruvantādi 38 “*ettēvar vālāttum evvāṟu seygaiyum appodu oḻiyum*” (any dēva’s pride or existence will be destroyed when he ignores them), if he changes his desire, then their existence will also be in jeopardy.
- *vānavar deyvam enkō* – Should I call him as the refuge for them?
- *vānavar bōgam enkō* – Should I call him as \[as in tiruvāimoḻi 6.7.1\] “*uṇṇum sōṟu parugunīr tinnum veṟṟilai ellām \[ānavan\]*” (one who is food (which gives nutrition), water (which sustains) and betel leaves (which give enjoyment))?
- *vānavar muṟṟum enkō* – Is he everything that are not identified here so far, for them?
- *ūnamil selvam enkō* – Should I call him as perennial wealth instead of temporary wealth which disappears after a while?
- *ūnamil suvarggam enkō* – Should I call him as eternal heavenly abode unlike the worldly heaven where a person will be kicked out once his accumulated pious karma is exhausted? Are these defective heaven etc also not his wealth? Why is he specifically spelling out real heaven that has no defects here? It is similar to kriṣṇa specifically highlighting in [śrī bhagavat gītā](http://githa.koyil.org/) 10.41 “*śrīmadūrjitamēva vā*” (anything that is auspicious, they are a miniscule part of my radiance).
- *ūnamil mōkkam enkō* – Should I call him as parama puruśārta lakśaṇa mōkśam (ultimate liberation of engaging in loving devotional service in paramapadam) which is going upto the prakāri ([bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) – entity) instead of stopping at ātmānubhavam (enjoying oneself) which is at the level of prakāram ([jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) – attribute, aspect)?
- *oḷi maṇivaṇṇanaiyē* – The aforementioned aspects look similar to the distinguished form of [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.
