## 3.4.8. Oli manivannan

*oḷi maṇivaṇṇan enkō oruvan enṟētta ninṟa naḷir madic cadaiyan enkō nānmugak kadavuḷ enkō aḷi magiḻndulagam ellām padaittavai ētta ninṟa kaḷi malart tuḷavan emmān kaṇṇanai māyanaiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

aḷi – for the favour of protecting; magiḻndu – having joy; ulagam ellām – all the worlds; padaittu – created; avai – those \[worlds\]; ētta – praise; ninṟa – standing (feeling accomplished); kaḷi – with flowing honey; malar – blossomed flower; tuḷavan – due to the beauty of the tuḷasi garland; emmān – one who completely won over me; māyanai – one who carried out amazing activities such as stealing butter etc; kaṇṇanai – kriṣṇa; maṇi – like a ruby (which is polished well); oḷi – best due to its radiance; vaṇṇan – having complexion; oruvan enṟu – that he is the one; ētta – being praised; ninṟa – one who is standing; taḷir – cool; madi – due to having crescent moon; sadaiyan – due to having matted hair, rudra who is engaged in enjoyment (having cool crescent moon) as well as penance (having matted hair); nānmugan – four headed brahmā (who is vorśipped by all dēvatās); enkō – Should I call him?

**Перевод:**

**What should I call kriṣṇa who completely won over me by his beauty of wearing blossomed tuḷasi flower garland that has flowing honey, who carried out amazing activities such as stealing butter etc and who is standing (feeling accomplished) being joyfully praised by all worlds which he created to do the favour of protecting them? As said in tiruvāimoḻi 1.7.1 “āyar koḻundāy avarāl pudaiyuṇṇum māyappirānai en māṇikkac cōdiyai” (my amazing ruby like radiant lord who was born in the covherd clan and was beaten by them), should I call him as the one who is having the complexion like the ruby (which is polished well) which is the best due to its radiance? Should I call him as rudra who is standing being praised as the one (as said in yajur vēdam “ēka Eva rudra:” (he is the only supreme) by his dependents), who is engaged in in enjoyment due to having cool crescent moon as well as in penance due to having matted hair? Should I call him as four headed brahmā (who is vorśipped by all dēvatās)?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In eighth pāsuram – āḻvār speaks about emperumān having primary personalities such as brahmā, rudra etc, as his wealth.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. oḷi maṇivaṇṇan enkō oruvan enṟētta ninṟa naḷir madic cadaiyan enkō nānmugak kadavuḷ enkō aḷi magiḻndulagam ellām padaittavai ētta ninṟa kaḷi malart tuḷavan emmān kaṇṇanai māyanaiyē*

- *oḷi maṇi vaṇṇan enkō* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is recollecting the beauty of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) which he described in previous pāsuram.
- *oruvan* … – Should I call him as rudra who is considered as the primordial lord by ignorant people, who is having cool crescent moon \[on his head\] and matted hair?
- *naḷir madic cadaiyan enkō …* – Should I call him as the one who is having the best knowledge? \[Double meaning – Here, madi is explained as knowledge (talaiyāna madi – best knowledge); talaiyāna madi also means crescent moon on his head\]. If ignorance of his followers were removed, he would have nothing great.  Should I call him as brahmā who is the father of such rudra?
- *aḷi magiḻndu* – He created the worlds only to protect them and in turn they praise him. He stood satisfied after the purpose of his creation got fulfilled.
- *kaḷi malar* … – kaḷi – honey; malar – flower. [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is wearing a tuḷasi garland which has both honey and flowers, and capturing me fully by manifesting that beautiful garland, being easily approachable by me and having amazing qualities and activities.

## 3.4.9. Kannanai mayan

*kaṇṇanai māyan tannai kadal kadaindu amudam koṇḍa aṇṇalai accudanai anantanai anantan tan mēl naṇṇi nanguṟaiginṟānai jñālam uṇḍumiḻnda mālai eṇṇumāṟu aṟiya māttēn yāvaiyum yavarum tānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

yāvaiyum – all acētana (insentient objects); yavarum – all cētana (sentient entities); tān – being himself; kaṇṇanai – being easily approachable for his devotees; māyan tannai – one who is identified by his amazing qualities and activities; kadal – ocean; kadaindu – churned; amudam koṇḍa – work for them; aṇṇalai – being sarvasvāmy (lord of all); accudanai – being the one who never leaves his devotees; anantanai – being the one with unlimited glories in his true nature etc; anantan tanmēl – on tiruvanantāḻvān (ādiśēśan) (who is capable of securing everything inside him); naṇṇi – fitting well; nangu – happily; uṟaiginṟānai – one who is resting; jñālam – when there is danger for the world that is protected by him; uṇḍu – protecting by placing it in his stomach; umiḻnda – and then let it out free \[when safe to do so\]; mālai – one who is having vātsalyam (motherly affection); eṇṇumāṟu – to (comprehensively) think; aṟiya māttēn – I don’t know

**Перевод:**

**I don’t know how to (comprehensively) think about emperumān who is himself being all acētana (insentient objects) and cētana (sentient entities), being easily approachable for his devotees, being the one who is identified by his amazing qualities and activities, being the sarvasvāmy (lord of all) who churned the ocean and worked (even for those  who are looking for ulterior goals), being the one who never leaves his devotees, being the one with unlimited glories in his true nature etc and the the one who is happily fitting well on tiruvanantāḻvān (ādiśēśan) (who is capable of securing everything inside him) and resting there, who would with motherly affection, protect the world when there is danger by placing it in his stomach and would then let it out free \[when safe to do so\].**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In ninth pāsuram – āḻvār says “His vast wealth cannot be individually spoken about; we can only briefly speak about his wealth as cētana (sentient) and acētana (insentient) in the form of cause and effect respectively”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “Not just those which have been spoken thus far, I am unable to comprehend bhagavān‘s nature of being all sentient and insentient beings”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. kaṇṇanai māyan tannai kadal kadaindu amudam koṇḍa aṇṇalai accudanai anantanai anantan than mēl naṇṇi nanguṟaiginṟānai jñālam uṇḍumiḻnda mālai eṇṇumāṟu aṟiya māttēn yāvaiyum yavarum tānē*

- *kaṇṇanai māyan tannai* – kriṣṇa whose qualities and activities amaze everyone as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.3.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/06/thiruvaimozhi-1-3-1-paththudai-adiyavar/) “*ettiṟam*” (how is it possible?).
- *kadal …* – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), who is the lord of all, who would take pains in churning the ocean even for those who have ulterior goals \[the goal of dēvas is not to serve emperumān, but immortality to enjoy worldly pleasures\].
- *accudanai* – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who has the natural quality of protecting those who are surrendered to him, always without fail.
- *anantan* … – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) rests on ādiśēśan comfortably, not waking up even when his divine consorts engage with him by pressing their breasts on him. \[Would there be two entities with the quality of ananta (unlimited)? emperumān and ādiśēśa both are called ananta\] Since ādiśēśan is situated in ultimate servitude, he even secures the supreme lord within him out of great love.
- *jñālam uṇḍu umiḻnda mālai* – \[He is of such kind nature that \] When there are people in danger, he cannot comfortably rest in there \[he would immediately rush to their help\].
- *eṇṇumāṟu aṟiya māttēn* – Even he (kriṣṇa) when elaborating his vibhūti yōga (his great wealth), said in śrī bhagavat gītā 10.19 “*nāstyantō vistarasya mē*” (there is no limit to my wealth); similarly, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) too is saying “I don’t know how to speak about him” after highlighting certain aspects previously.

When asked “can that be explained briefly?”, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says,

- *yāvaiyum yavarum tānē* – [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is the prakāri (underlying entity) and all cētana and acētana (sentient and insentient objects) are his prakāram (form/attribute).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.4.10. Yavaiyum yavarum

*yāvaiyum yavarum tānāy avar avar samayam tōṟum tōyvilan pulan aindukkum solappadān uṇarvin mūrtti āvi sēr uyirin uḷḷāl ādum ōr paṟṟilāda bāvanai adanaik kūdil avanaiyum kūdalāmē*

**Пословный перевод:**

yāvaiyum – all acētana (insentient objects); yavarum – all cētana (sentient entities); tānāy – being himself; avar avar – those sentient entity’s; samayam tōṟum – in their various situations \[bodies\] such as being dēva (celestial) et al (when united with acit (matter)); tōyvilan – has no binding unlike them; pulan aindukkum – through the five sensory organs; solappadān – is not spoken \[understood\]; uṇarvin mūrtti – one who is naturally self-illuminating; āvi – body which is the abode of prāṇa (vital air); sēr – together with; uyirin – ātmā’s; uḷ – in the nature; ādum – qualities such as jadatva (being inanimate), pariṇāmitva (changes) etc; ōr – in any one; paṟṟu – attachment; ilāda – not applicable; bāvanai – aspect; adanai – that true nature; kūdil – if affected; ādumōr paṟṟilāda – the aspect of not being affected (in the attributes of all cētana and acētana); avanaiyum – īsvara (who was spoken about previously and is explained as self-illuminating); kūdalām – will be applicable; E – certainly

**Перевод:**

**bhagavān is the one who is himself being all acētana (insentient objects) and cētana (sentient entities); though he is \[present along with the souls\] in various situations \[bodies\] such as being dēva (celestial) et al (when united with acit (matter)), he has no binding unlike those souls; he is is not spoken \[understood\] through the five sensory organs and is naturally self-illuminating; Hence, it is certain that, if the true nature of ātmā that is  together with body which is the abode of prāṇa (vital air), is not affected by qualities such as jadatva (being inanimate), pariṇāmitva (changes) etc which are not attached to it \[the true nature of the ātmā\], the aspect of īsvara (who was spoken about previously and is explained as self-illuminating) not being affected (in the attributes of all cētana and acētana) will be applicable.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In tenth pāsuram – āḻvār says “though bhagavān is pervading all cētana (sentient entities) and acētana (insentient objects), their defects do not touch him”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. yāvaiyum yavarum tānāy avar avar samayam tōṟum tōyvilan pulan aindukkum solappadān uṇarvin mūrtti āvi sēr uyirin uḷḷāl ādum ōr paṟṟilāda bāvanai adanaik kūdil avanaiyum kūdalāmē*

- *yāvaiyum yavarum tānāy* – [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) being prakāri (entity) and all [cētana](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) and [acētana](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/09/thathva-thrayam-achith-what-is-matter/) being prakāra (attribute/form), such that they are contained in the word “tān” (I – bhagavān) \[bhagavān means the paramātmā who has the entire spiritual realm and material realm, as his body\].
- *avar avar …* – “*avar avar*” implies the plurality of [jīvātmās](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/). Since previously both sentient and insentient are identified as “*yāvaiyum* \[plurality of insentient\] and *yavarum* \[plurality of sentient\]”, here too “*avai avai*” should be assumed to be implicitly present, since this is reinforcing previous phrase. But why is not explicitly stated? That is because acētana is not as important as cētana and also since in the context of what is being discussed, it is automatically implied \[so need to explicitly state it\]. samayam means vyavastā \[states\]. This highlights the ever changing nature of acētana and the feeling of joy and sorrow in cētana.
- *tōyvilan* – Though [cētana](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) and [acētana](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/09/thathva-thrayam-achith-what-is-matter/) are so inseparable from him that they are identified by the word “*tān*” (I – bhagavān), still, their faults which do not affect him. Though cētanas (souls) do not have the defect of pariṇāma (change/transformation) etc., which are natural for acit, yet the souls acquire joy and sorrow due to being together with acit; so, when [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is pervaded in all these cētana and acētana, would their defects not affect him? No, they would not affect him. Though there is no joy/sorrow for ātmā independently, only because of ātmā being together with acit, he acquires joy/sorrow. Would that same principle be applicable for bhagavān too? No, that principle cannot be applied to him. That is due to the reason for the presence of bhagavān and ātmā within acit \[any particular body\]. bhagavān is not present inside a body due to his karma unlike a jīvātmā; instead he is present due to his mercy \[to sustain the body, since nothing exists without bhagavān’s presence and to help/guide the jīvātmā by accompanying him everywhere\]. In a prison, both the prisoner and the prince (of the kingdom) are present. Since the prisoner entered the prison due to his karma (unlawful activity) he is suffering. But since the prince entered the prison out of his own desire, it is joyful for him. This principle is explained in rig vēdam “*dvā suparṇā sayujā sakhāyā samānam vrukśam pariśasvajātē \| tayōranya: pippalam svādvatti anaśnannanyō abicākaśīti \|\|*” (There are two related (servant and master) birds ([jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) and [paramātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)) residing in a tree (body). One bird ([jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)) enjoys the fruits of its actions (karma) and the other one (paramātmā) being detached is radiantly witnessing that).
- *pulan aindukkum solappadān* – He cannot be comprehended by the five sensory organs starting with ears etc. Alternatively explained as – only if we can think about him, we can go on to explain. He cannot be comprehended by such thoughts.

Then, what is his nature?

- *uṇarvin mūrtti* – He is the embodiment of radiance.

But since the connection between these \[[cētana](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) and [acētana](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/09/thathva-thrayam-achith-what-is-matter/)\] and [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is real, how is that their defects do not affect him?

- *āvi sēr* … – āvi – body which is the abode of prāṇa (vital air), is present. uyir – ātmā (soul), that is connected to the body is also present, When it is considered that the childhood, youth, old age etc that are related to the body, are unrelated to the ātmā, there is nothing wrong in applying similar principle to bhagavān \[being unaffected by the defects of cit and acit\].

Beyond this, two other explanations are given for the second half of the pāsuram.

- If one has devotion towards bhagavān, one can attain him.
- If one gives up all other means and fully surrender unto him, one can attain him.

Another explanation is also given – if one meditates upon him during his final moments, one  can attain him.

[emperumānār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/emperumanar/) heard these different explanations and said “Since previously [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s all pervading nature is explained, this must be explained in the context of the defects of the pervaded entities not affecting emperumān who is pervading them all; so, this should be the best explanation”.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

adiyen saraty ramanuja dasan

## 3.4.11. Kudi vandaraiyum

*kūdi vaṇḍaṟaiyum taṇḍār koṇḍalpōl vaṇṇan tannai mādalar poḻil kurugūr vaṇ śatakōpan sonna pādal ōr āyirattuḷ ivaiyum oru pattum vallār vīdila bōgam eydi virumbuvar amarar moyttē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vaṇḍu – bumble bees; kūdi – grouped; aṟaiyum – buzzing (due to the joy of drinking honey); taṇ – cool; tār – wearing divine garland; koṇḍal pōl – like a black cloud; vaṇṇan tannai – being the one with such complexion; mādu – on all sides; alar – blossomed; poḻil – having gardens; kurugūr – leader of āḻvārtirunagari; vaṇ śatakōpan – nammāḻvār; sonna – mercifully spoke; pādal – with music; ōr – distinguished; āyirattuḷ – in the thousand pāsurams; oru – distinguished; ivaiyum pattum – this decad also (which explained bhagavān having all worlds as his wealth like having distinguished form); vallār – those who can practice; vīdila – uninterrupted; bōgam – experience of bhagavān; eydi – attain; amarar – nityasūris; moyttu – surround; virumbuvar – be desired

**Перевод:**

**nammāḻvār, the leader of āḻvārtirunagari which is having gardens that are filled on all sides with blossomed flowers, mercifully spoke with music in this distinguished decad (which explained bhagavān having all worlds as his wealth like having distinguished form) in the distinguished thousand pāsurams about emperumān who is the one with black cloud like complexion and wearing cool divine garland that has groups of bumble bees buzzing (due to the joy of drinking honey); those who can practice this decad \[which has such greatness\] will attain uninterrupted experience of bhagavān and will be surrounded and desired by nityasūris.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the end – āḻvār says “those who learn this decad, will attain eternal service and be liked by nityasūris (eternally free souls of paramapadam)”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār mercifully explains uninterrupted experience of bhagavān as the result of this decad.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. kūdi vaṇḍaṟaiyum taṇḍār koṇḍalpōl vaṇṇan tannai mādalar poḻil kurugūr vaṇ śatakōpan sonna pādal ōr āyirattuḷ ivaiyum oru pattum vallār vīdila bōgam eydi virumbuvar amarar moyttē*

- *kūdi vaṇḍaṟaiyum* … – Here [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is explaining the matching beauty of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s shoulders and the garland which decorates them, similar to his wealth which was explained in detail previously. āḻvār praised [sarvēśvaran](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) who is having a pleasant cloud like form and a pleasant garland which is entered by bumble bees as a group like it is done while stepping into a flowing river \[when entering a flowing river, usually people would enter as a group to secure each other\] and which are buzzing after drinking the honey.
- *mādalar* … – Mercifully sung by the most magnanimous nammāḻvār who is the leader of [āḻvārtirunagari](http://azhwarthirunagari.koyil.org/) which has well blossomed \[flower bearing\] gardens.
- *pādal ōr āyiram* … – Those who can practice this thousand pāsurams with music which resembles a flower which blossoms with fragrance.
- *vīdila bōgam eydi* – attaining the blissful liberation where there is no question of break.
- *virumbuvar amarar moyttē* – Will be greatly desired by nityasūris. \[Why would nityasūris desire for those who practice these pāsurams?\] Since nityasūris consider the material realm as owned by [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) and since they lovingly and greatly admire [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) thinking “whatever we enjoy being in this spiritual realm \[which is favourable for bhagavat viśayam\], āḻvār being in material realm \[which is unfavourable for bhagavat viśayam\], having acquired this pristine knowledge and enjoying the same experience”, they would approach and greatly enjoy those who recite such āḻvār’s prabandams even at the expense of not enjoying [sarvēśvaran](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) \[This is in context of nityasūris desiring those who practice these pāsurams even in this material realm\].

Finally, nampiḷḷai summarizes the contents of this decad briefly.

- In the first pāsuram, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) explained briefly in this pāsuram, the principle that was explained in detail in this decad.
- In the second pāsuram,  he spoke about the effect/result of \[panca\] bhūtams (5 great elements) in order.
- In the third pāsuram, he enjoyed [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) being the sustainer of entire universe and his distinguished form together.
- In the fourth pāsuram, he said “emperumān is the owner of radiant precious gems such as ruby etc”.
- In the fifth pāsuram,  he mercifully spoke about emperumān having tasteful objects as wealth.
- In the sixth pāsuram, he said “emperumān is the owner of varieties of sounds in the form of prose and music/tune such as vēdam”.
- In the seventh pāsuram, he said “emperumān is the owner of puruśārtams (goals) such as aiśvarya (worldly wealth) etc”.
- In the eighth pāsuram, he said “emperumān is the owner of primary entities of the material realm such as brahmā, rudra et al”.
- In the ninth pāsuram, he briefly spoke about [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) having [cētana](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) and [acētana](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/09/thathva-thrayam-achith-what-is-matter/) as wealth, since his vast wealth cannot be spoken about individually.
- In the tenth pāsuram, he said “though he pervades all of these \[cētana and acētana\], he is unaffected by their defects”.
- In the end, he explains the result for those who learned this decad and concludes the same.

## 3.5 Moymmam pumpolil

## 3.5.1. Moymmam pumpolil

*moymmām pūm poḻil poygai mudalaic ciṟaippattu ninṟa kaimmāvukkaruḷ seyda kārmugil pōl vaṇṇan kaṇṇan emmānaic collip pādi eḻundum parandum tuḷḷādār tammāl karumam en solleer taṇ kadal vattattuḷḷīrē*

**Пословный перевод:**

moy – tightly packed; mā – well-grown; pū – blossomed \[flowers\]; poḻil – having gardens; poygai – in the pond; mudalai – by the crocodile; siṟaippattu – captured; ninṟa – stood (standing still, being unable to reach the shore); kaimmāvukku – for the elephant; aruḷ seyda – bestowed his mercy (of accepting the flower from its trunk before it loses its freshness and decorating himself with it); kār – pleasant (that which removes the fatigue of the one who sees); mugil pōl – like a dark cloud; vaṇṇan – form; kaṇṇan – saulabhyam (simplicity) (of descending down to help uplift); emmānai – having \[eternal\] relationship (which is the cause for removing the fatigue and helping); solli – speak with the mouth; pādi – sing (out of joy); eḻundum – instead of being seated; paṟandum – flying high without having the feet touching the ground; tuḷḷādār – by those who do not jump up and down doing somersaults; en – what; karumam – is the purpose?; taṇ – cool; kadal – surrounded by ocean; vattattu – earth; uḷḷīrē – those who are residing with the intention to enjoy bhagavān; solleer – please tell

**Перевод:**

**emperumān is the one who bestowed his mercy  (of accepting the flower from the elephant’s trunk before it loses its freshness and decorating himself with it) upon the elephant  which stood (standing still, being unable to reach the shore) captured by the crocodile in the pond which is having gardens \[around it\] which have tightly packed, well-grown, blossomed flowers; (to be enjoyed by such elephant after having its suffering eliminated,) he has pleasant (that which removes the fatigue of the one who sees), dark cloud like form, saulabhyam (simplicity) (of descending down to help uplift) and \[eternal\] relationship (which is the cause for removing the fatigue and helping). Oh those who are residing in the earth which is surrounded by cool ocean, with the intention to enjoy bhagavān! please tell, what is the purpose of those who do not speak with the mouth, sing (out of joy), flying high without having the feet touching the ground instead of being seated and jumping up and down doing somersaults?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In first pāsuram – āḻvār says “Worthless are those who remain indifferent even after observing emperumān‘s vātsalyam (motherly affection) of mercifully protecting śrī gajēndrāḻvān”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*In first pāsuram – āḻvār says “Worthless are those who remain indifferent even after observing emperumān‘s compassion of rushing from \[mūnṟām tiruvantādi 51\] ‘kalangāp perunagaram‘ (paramapadam which is unshakable) to the banks of the pond where his devotee (gajēndra the elephant) was in danger”. moymmām pūm poḻil poygai mudalaic ciṟaippattu ninṟa kaimmāvukkaruḷ seyda kārmugil pōl vaṇṇan kaṇṇan emmānaic collip pādi eḻundum parandum tuḷḷādār tammāl karumam en solleer taṇ kadal vattattuḷḷīrē*

- *moymmām pūm poḻil* – *mā* – bumble bee. Gardens swarmed by bumble bees. Another explanation. moy – tightly packed – denseness of the garden; that denseness will capture the heart. mā – \[two meanings\] mango tree, vastness; pūm poḻil – well blossomed garden. If denseness was only taken as meaning previously, here, heart-captivating aspect is explained.
- *poygai* … – gajēndraāḻvān who wanted to serve the lotus feet of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) with flowers, was worried since he did not find any; he saw the cool garden and blossomed-flower filled pond from a distance and ran in to it without realizing that there is a beast waiting inside; [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) greatly enjoys the garden and pond as enjoyed by gajēndrāḻvān  back then; this pond resembles emperumān as explained in tiruvāimoḻi 10.1.8 “*tayaratan peṟṟa maṇittadam*” (the precious-gem like pond (śrī rāma) who was the son of daśarata). As explained in tiruvāsiriyam 5 “*tāmaraikkādu malarkkaṇṇodu kanivāyudaiyadumāy*” (one who is having eyes which resembled a forest of blossomed lotus flowers, reddish fruit like mouth/lips), since these examples resemble emperumān, āḻvār enjoys them and becomes captivated. gajēndrāḻvān was captured by the crocodile in the pond. Since pond is not a natural habitat for the elephant, it was easily captured by the crocodile. If it was land, elephant would easily defeat the crocodile; the elephant is neither fighting with another elephant nor a lion \[both are comparable in strength\], but it is fighting with a lowly water worm \[a slang for crocodile\].
- *siṟaippattu ninṟa* – The crocodile pulled the elephant into the pond and the elephant pulled the crocodile to the shore and it was going on for many years as said in śrī viṣṇu darmam 68th chapter “*divyam varśasaharakam*” (1000 dēva (celestial) years i.e., 360000 human years) and in the same ślōkam “*gaja ākarśatē tīrē grāha ākarśatē jalē*” (gajēndrāḻvān the elephant, pulls towards the banks of the pond and the crocodile pulls towards the water); subsequently, the elephant’s efforts stopped and the crocodile started winning; since water is not the natural habitat, the elephant’s strength will eventually reduce; and since water is the natural habitat and also the crocodile is inching towards victory, it’s strength gets doubled; the crocodile is explained in periya tirumoḻi 5.8.3 as “*muḻuvali mudalai*” (crocodile with full strength); previously, the crocodile’s strength would have been reduced since achieving it’s desire was not in sight; now that the victory is in sight, it acquires full strength. The crocodile knowing well, caught hold of the foot of the elephant which was not done before. For a long time, the crocodile was thinking “I have not seen an elephant to be relieved of my current condition” \[a gandarva was previously cursed to become a crocodile and was told at that time that his relief will come from [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) through an elephant\] and held on to the elephant’s foot as soon as it entered the pond.
- *kaimmāvukku* – kai means hand, mā means animal. kaimmā means elephant (which has a trunk/hand). Two explanations for using the name kaimmā – a) elephant being a tall/strong animal, would think that even if there is danger for other animals, I cannot be troubled – such elephant suffered here. b) even if there is a danger (in water), the elephant would keep its trunk outside and can breathe for long time – but here, even the trunk almost submerged into the water. As said in periya tiumoḻi 2.3.9 “*ānaiyin tuyaram*” (elephant’s suffering), when an elephant is in danger, it must be really grave danger.
- *aruḷ seyda* – even when the trunk was getting submerged, gajēndrāḻvān kept the flower above water to preserve freshness; \[the mercy here is\] [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) accepting such flower without losing its freshness. It can also be explained as emperumān caringly holding the foot that was caught by the crocodile, with his divine hand and mercifully glancing at the elephant. To ensure that gajēndrāḻvān does not think that emperumān is in a distant abode of paramapadam, emperumān quickly arrived riding his garuda and accepted the flower from it.
- *aruḷ seyda* – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) broke the shackles from the elephant’s foot. The crocodile was described in periya tirumoḻi 5.8.3 as “*kodiyavāy vilangu*” (animal with cruel mouth, shackle of cruel mouth). \[it is the merciful\] posture of emperumān touching the elephant’s foot that was caught by the crocodile, with his divine hand. This is explained in “… *grāham cakrēṇa mādava:*” (The husband of śrī mahālakśmi cut the crocodile into two using his chakra). nampiḷḷai explains nācciyār tirumoḻi 3.5 “*kālaik kaduviduginṟa*” pāsuram here. When the gōpikās placed their clothes in the banks of the pond and entered the pond, kriṣṇa grabbed the clothes and climbed a tree on the banks of the pond. The gōpikās find out about [kriṣṇa](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s mischief and request him to return their clothes in many different ways, but they did not succeed. One among them, who knew the secrets of [īśvara](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/), said “fishes such as kayal, vāḷai are biting our feet. emperumān had rushed to the help of the elephant which had surrendered to him, when the elephant was attacked by the crocodile; why is he not coming to our help when we are suffering? There the elephant was troubled by one crocodile only, here we, who are helpless, are being troubled by both kayal and vāḷai”. The gōpikā thinks that kriṣṇa would at once hand over the clothes hearing this. Since she was born in vaiṣṇava family \[[āṇḍāḷ](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/andal/) who is the daughter of [periyāḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/periyazhwar/), sang this pāsuram\] would know the secrets of [īśvara](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) – they would know that [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) would come and help on saying certain words.
- *kār mugil* … – The amazing reaction in [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s form as well as qualities while helping the elephant. emperumān let the elephant enjoy him and stood subserviently \[by holding it’s foot caringly etc\]; it is well known that kriṣṇa means one who becomes subservient to those who enjoy him. emperumān’s beautiful form and simplicity are the viśalya karaṇi (that which heals wounds created by weapons) and sandāna karaṇi (the medicine which will re-fit the limbs which were cut off). He eliminated the sufferings of the elephant by letting the elephant enjoy him when he remained subserviently.
- *emmānai* – Elephant was removed of it’s shackles by his help. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) became captivated by emperumān’s such compassion/simplicity. āḻvār thinks how emperumān helped śrī gajēndrāḻvān which is not of great birth, knowledge or activity, but only having taste \[towards serving [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)\], and became completely taken over by emperumān. When [bhattar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/parasara-bhattar/) heard up to this line, he asked the reciter to recite the remaining part of the pāsuram \[where āḻvār says one would dance, sing etc\] and mercifully said “How much ever emperumān does, to be indifferent, we are needed; and when there is a danger for us, being emotionally affected and rushing to help us, he is needed”.
- *solli* … – Those who are not speaking about the compassion of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) helping the elephant, singing after being overwhelmed by love, standing up unable to stay still, flying high unable to keep the feet on ground and performing somersaults.
- *tammāl karumam en* – As [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is supposed to engage them in his service, what is the purpose of emperumān’s creation \[if they are not doing that\]? What is the purpose of emperumān assuming a form and doing this (to protect gajēndrāḻvān) \[and still these people are not engaging in his service\]?
- *taṇ kadal vattattuḷḷīr solleer* – Though you are unlike us \[who are knowledgeable\], after assuming a \[human\] form and still not engaging in devotion towards [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/), you being similar to those who are engaged in mundane pleasures – please tell me. In this world that is surrounded by ocean, both wise and unwise people will be present; [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says that this principle is easy to understand for both wise and unwise people.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.5.2. Tan kadal

*taṇ kadal vattattuḷḷārait tamakkiraiyāt tadinduṇṇum tiṇ kaḻaṟkāl asurarkkut tīngiḻaikkum tirumālaip paṇgaḷ talaik koḷḷap pādip paṟandum kunittuḻalādār maṇ koḷ ulagil piṟappār valvinai mōda malaindē*

**Пословный перевод:**

taṇ – having coolness as a quality; kadal – surrounded by ocean; vattattu – in earth; uḷḷārai – the residents; tamakku iraiyā – to merely fulfill their appetite; tadindu – kill; uṇṇum – live by eating; tiṇ – strong; kaḻal – anklet highlighting valour; kāl – having in their feet; asurarkku – for the asuras (demons); tīngu – hurting (in the form of destroying them); iḻaikkum – caused; tirumālai – on the one who is being dear to pirātti (śrī mahālakśmi) (because of such destruction of demons); paṇgaḷ – tunes; talaik koḷḷa – to be overwhelmed; pādi – sing; paṟandum – rising into the sky (like flying); kunittu – dance; uḻalādār – those who don’t go around everywhere; maṇ koḷ – having abundant of soil/land; ulagil – in the world; val – difficult to exhaust; vinai – great sins; malaindu – being inflicted with; mōda – to be smashed on the ground; piṟappār – will be born

**Перевод:**

**asuras (demons) who have strong anklet in their feet highlighting their valour that help them kill and live by eating the residents of the earth which is surrounded by the cool ocean, merely to fulfill their appetite. emperumān hurts (in the form of destroying) them and due to that is dear to pirātti (śrī mahālakśmi). Those who don’t overwhelmingly sing tunes, praising emperumān, rising into the sky (like flying), dance and go around everywhere, will be born in this world which is having abundant of soil/land, to be smashed on the ground, being inflicted with the great sins which are difficult to exhaust.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In  second pāsuram – āḻvār says that those who are not captivated by śriya:pati‘s natural compassion with which he eliminates the hurdles of everyone and protects them, will be born in this samsāram (material realm) to experience great suffering.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Second pāsuram. āḻvār says “If we look at bhagavān‘s compassion of eliminating the hurdles of samsāris who are unaware that ‘they have sufferings’, his helping of gajēndrāḻvān looks like helping of nityasūris. taṇ kadal vattattuḷḷārait tamakkiraiyāt tadinduṇṇum tiṇ kaḻaṟkāl asurarkkut tīngiḻaikkum tirumālaip paṇgaḷ talaik koḷḷap pādip paṟandum kunittuḻalādār maṇ koḷ ulagil piṟappār valvinai mōda malaindē*

- *taṇ kadal* – The demons would hurt the creatures and live off that.

What caused the demons to hurt them?

- *taṇ kadal vattattuḷḷār* – The bondage due to residing in the same place is the only cause for the demons hurting others. The same reason that makes sarvēśvaran protect them \[because they are staying in the place owned by him\] , is causing the demons to hurt them. nampiḷḷai explains śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 1.20 “*tē vayam bhavatā rakśyā:*” (we are qualified to be protected by you) here.  “*tē vayam bhavatā rakśyā:*” – the maharishis in the daṇḍakāraṇyam said “We who are suffering is the apt target for the protection of your highness who has vowed to protect the sufferers” and śrī rāma asked them “Why should I protect you? Are you trying to convince me by your upāsanam (worship)?”, the maharishis say “there can be defects in our worship”; “*bhavadviśaya vāsina:*” (we are living in your kingdom) – \[but\] we belong to your kingdom. In this aspect, there is no option to escape \[from protecting us\]. You may say “this is beyond the boundary of my protection” like it was said in tiruviruttam 33 “*ivaṟṟin puṟattāḷ enṟeṇṇō*” (are you thinking that parānkuśa nāyaki is outside the boundary of your protection?) \[in this ślōkam, the maharishis continue to say “both towns and forests, they are all under śrī rāma’s control only\]. So, the demons would hurt them just because they live and move around in their vicinity.
- *tamakkiraiyā* – to nourish their bodies.
- *tadinduṇṇum* – living by hurting others.
- *tiṇ kaḻaṟkāl asurarkku* – The demons who have the anklet of valour in their feet. Like śrī rāma has taken a vow to protect others saying as in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 29.10 “…*ētat vratam mama*” (this is my vow), they are wearing this anklet highlighting their desire to hurt others. Even if one can escape the vow of śrī rāma’s protection, one cannot escape the vow of the demons to hurt others.
- *tīngiḻaikkum tirumālai* – If we consider “these demons were also created by us” and see their \[eternal\] bondage, our own wealth \[people of the world etc\] will be destroyed by them. Thinking “How can we protect our world even if it takes to destroy these demons?”, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) would say as in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 18.3 “*mitrabhāvēna …*” (even if they pretend to be friends, I will protect them) and pirātti would say as in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 58.44 “… *bhavēyam śaraṇam hi va:*” (sītā pirātti to the lady-demons who are guarding her – I will protect you all) and thus would discuss/inquire ways to protect the devotees by pulling out the weeds only.
- *tirumālai – paṇgaḷ talai koḷḷap pādi* – \[Singing the glories of [śriman nārāyaṇan](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) with tunes\] Five explanations:
   - Knowing that the devotees are singing about śrīman nārāyaṇan, the tunes would come up and say “please use me, please use me”, i.e., singing with abundance of tunes.
   - Singing with importance to tunes.
   - Singing with the best tune.
   - Singing out of devotion, without proper tunes.
   - Singing in a tune which manifests various tunes.
- *paṟandum* … – Those who are not dancing in a manner that their feet do not touch the ground and spend their time travelling and doing this only.  Those who are not jumping up and down and dancing as their routine.
- *maṇ koḷ* … – “*valvinai malaindu mōda maṇkoḷ ulagil piṟappār*” (they will take birth in the world which has land, being forcefully pushed by their sins). Those who remain stiff and indifferent without showing any emotions while experiencing [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/), cannot do anything when they are severely affected by cāturtikam (a type of deadly fever). Here “*piṟappu*” (birth) is indicated for other sorrows such as old age, disease and death.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.5.3. Malaiyai eduttu

*malaiyai eduttuk kal māri kāttup pasu nirai tannait tolaivu tavirtta pirānaic collic colli ninṟeppōdum talaiyinōdādanam tattat tadu kuttamāyp paṟavādār alai koḷ naragattaḻundik kidanduḻaikkinṟa vambarē*

**Пословный перевод:**

malaiyai – gōvardana hill; eduttu – lifted; kal māri – hail storm (which was caused by indra since his worship was interrupted); kāttu – protected; pasu nirai tannai – herd of cows (which don’t even know to request to be protected); tolaivu – from destruction; tavirtta – averted; pirānai – one who favoured; collic colli – repeatedly saying \[praising\]; eppōdum – always; ninṟu – staying without break; ādanattōdu – ground; talai – head; tatta – to hit; tadu kuttamāy – doing somersaults; paṟavādār – dance with their feet not touching the ground; alai koḷ – having many sorrows; naragattu – in the great hell; aḻundi – drowned (so they cannot reach the shore); kidandu – staying there; uḻaikkinṟa – suffering; vambar – those who never lose their freshness

**Перевод:**

**kriṣṇa is the one who favoured the herd of cows (which don’t even know to request to be protected) by lifting up the gōvardana hill, protecting them and averted their destruction when hailstorm (which was caused by indra since his worship was interrupted) occurred; those who never lose their freshness, who are not repeatedly saying \[praising\] such emperumān, doing somersaults such that their heads hit the ground and dancing with their feet not touching the ground, are drowned (so they cannot reach the shore) in the great hell which is having many sorrows and stay there suffering.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In third pāsuram – āḻvār says “Hellish experience is \[nothing but\] being indifferent after meditating upon the great quality of emperumān lifting up the gōvardana hill to eliminate the danger for the cows that cannot even realize the favour done \[by emperumān\] and those who are similar to those cows \[the covherds\]”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “those who do not get excited on meditating upon emperumān protecting the cows that were in trouble,  would suffer becoming residents of hell”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Third pāsuram. āḻvār says “Those who are being indifferent after meditating upon the great quality of emperumān lifting up the gōvardana hill to eliminate the danger for the cows that cannot even realize the favour done \[by emperumān\] and those who are similar to those cows \[the covherds\], will eternally suffer in this material realm”. malaiyai eduttuk kal māri kāttup pasu nirai tannait tolaivu tavirtta pirānaic collic colli ninṟeppōdum talaiyinōdādanam tattat tadu kuttamāyp paṟavādār alai koḷ naragattaḻundik kidanduḻaikkinṟa vambarē*

- *malaiyai …* – indra would be honoured once a year with great feasts by the covherd men; seeing their great enthusiasm, kriṣṇa asked them “what are you doing?” and they reply “we offer this feast to indra to get rains properly”; kriṣṇa thinks “In the land where I am \[supreme lord\] born and raised, offering something to a dēvatātntaram \[some demigod other than himself\] is like the sweat of the emperor’s wife being attended by some one other than the emperor himself” and said “Why should we offer anything to the resident of sky? should we not be offering this feast to this gōvardana hill which provides us the vast land to receive the rain and wind, being the shelter for our cows and having lots of greenery and water?” Since they are simple covherds, they at once agreed to his words. They brought huge quantity of food stuffs and placed them in front of the hill; kriṣṇa then assumed the form of the hill itself as said in “gōvardanō’smi” (I am this gōvardana hill) and consumed everything; since indra who was waiting for the feast did not get it, and due to the anger out of hunger, he started the hailstorm.
- *malaiyai eduttu* – He protected by lifting up the hill that was highlighted by him as the shelter previously. Real fighter would use the weapons \[strategy\] of the enemy when the battle approaches the end. Similarly, kaṇṇan [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) lifted up the hill that was in front of him and protected everyone from the hailstorm. For the mistake committed by indra, kriṣṇa should have cut off his hands. But he thinks “This idiot is doing this due to anger out of hunger; I cannot treat him like demoniac people; let him give up himself after a while” and patiently kept lifting up the hill for seven days.
- *kal māri kāttu* – \[This is bhattar’s interesting perspective\] If indra caused \[regular\] rain with water, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) would have protected by stopping it with water \[but since indra rained with hail (hard object), kriṣṇa protected with stones\].
- *pasu nirai tannai* – When we look at the state \[intelligence\] of covherds and cows, the elephant ([first pāsuram](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/08/thiruvaimozhi-3-5-1-moymmam-pumpozhil/)) and samsāris ([second pāsuram](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/08/thiruvaimozhi-3-5-2-than-kadal/)) look like nityasūris. Why is it said “*pasu nirai tannait tolaivu tavirtta*” (averting the disaster for the herd of cows) \[while the covherds are superior\]? That is to identify who is the main target of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s protection \[cows would not reject emperumān’s help unlike covherds who may reject some times\].  Another explanation – that is to identify the ones who realise the protection \[and be grateful\]; it is the cows that smile when seeing the ignorance of the covherds. kirātārjunīyam chapter 4 “… *krutānukārāniva gōbhirārjavē*” (looked like the cows were making fun of the covherds’ activities).
- *tolaivu tavirtta* – protected the cows and covherds from getting destroyed.
- *pirānai* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) thinks that he himself was the one caught in that hailstorm and suffered and he thinks that [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) helped for him only.
- *collic colli* – only when it is said for a particular purpose, it stops with one time \[when he is praised for the sake of praising only, such praises never stop\].
- *ninṟu* – Not just stopping after praising once, but also not stopping after repeating the praise many times.
- *eppōdum* – praising always, not just when some one is looking.
- *talaiyinōdu ādanam tatta* – such that the head hits the ground
- *tadu kuttamāyp paṟavādār* – *tadu kuttam* – irregular movements. That is, doing things in no proper sequence. Those who dance without having their feet touching the ground.
- *alaikoḷ …* – Will suffer by drowning deep in the hell which has waves of sorrows.
- *vambar* – For the servants of yama, they will look ever fresh. vambu – pudumai (new). After torturing one day, when they return the next day, instead of showing mercy thinking “we just tortured this person yesterday”, like receiving a very fragrant fruit which makes them smell it again and again, the servants of yama would say “come on! we are just looking for you” – such freshness.

nampiḷḷai is now repeating the meaning once more \[a śrīvaiṣṇava arrived late to the lecture and nampiḷḷai is repeating the meanings specifically for him\].

- *malaiayai eduttuk kal māri kāttu* – He likes to act for his devotees. Even if he performed the most difficult task, it would feel easy for him \[[āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) would have used the word “*sumandu*”  (holding it with difficulty) otherwise\].
- *pasu nirai tannai* – While performing difficult task and protecting, one just needs to not reject his help. \[By saying “*pasu nirai*“\] it implies that there is no such capability in them.
- *pirānai* – \[one who does great favours\] it is the nature of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) to exist for helping others, to be like moon, cool breeze, sandalwood paste and water \[all of which exist exclusively for the pleasure of others\].
- *solli …* – [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) who is said in cāndōjña upaniśat as “*avākyanādara:*” (anādara: – not caring for anyone since he has no desires left to be fulfilled;  avākī – he maintains silence considering everything else as unworthy of conversation – this is [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s state in śrīvaikuṇṭam), places himself for them \[covherds, devotees\] and chatters continuously as said in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 2.1.2 “*alavalai vandu appūcci kāttuginṟān*” (kriṣṇa who is like a chatter box, comes and scares me); similarly, \[his devotees too\] instead of glorifying mortal humans as said in tiruvāimoḻi 3.9.9 “*vāykoṇḍu mānidam pādādē*“, should think “the purpose of having the mouth is fulfilled by praising him” as said in tiruvāimoḻi 3.8.2 “*en tanjanē-nanjanē-vanjanē ennum eppōdumen vāsakam*” (my speech will always say ‘my shelter, the one who is like poison for hurdles, mischievous one” ; those who are not like this,
- *alai koḷ* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says that they will enter \[remain\] in the hell of samsāram \[material realm\]. Another explanation – being not engaged in such dancing and jumping around itself is hell. \[īsn’t there a separate place called naraka (hell)?\] śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 30.18 “*yastvayā saha sa svarga: nirayō yastvayā vinā \| iti jānan parām prītim gacca rāmamayāsaha \|\|*” ([sītā pirātti](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/) says to [śrī rāma](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) – To be with you is heaven for me and to be separated from you is hell for me; knowing this great love of mine towards you, you go along with me to the forest) – svarga and naraka will be different for each individual. Since āḻvār feels like being in hell when not dancing like that, he says so.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.5.4. Vambavalil kodai

*vambaviḻ kōtai poruttā māl vidai ēḻum adartta sem pavaḷat tiraḷ vāyan sirīdaran tol pugaḻ pādik kumbidu nattam ittādik kōgukattuṇḍuḻalādār tam piṟappāl payanennē sādu sanangaḷ idaiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vambu – having freshness; aviḻ – blossomed; kōdai poruttā – considering attaining of nappinnaip pirātti who is wearing a garland as the only goal; māl – huge; vidai – bull; ēḻum – seven; adartta – due to killing them; sem – reddish; pavaḷam – like a coral; tiraḷ – large; vāyan – having gentle smile in the lips; sirīdaran – kriṣṇa who stood having vīraśrī (wealth of valour); tol – natural; pugaḻ – qualities; pādi – sing; kumbidu nattam ittādi – dancing upside down; kōgu – in chaotic manner; ugattu – noise; uṇḍu – make; uḻalārtām – those who do not; piṟappāl – having born; sādu sanangaḷ – in sātvika sangam (assembly of devotees); idaiyē – amidst; en – what; payan – use?

**Перевод:**

**Considering attaining of nappinnaip pirātti who is wearing a fresh blossomed garland as the only goal, emperumān killed the seven huge bulls; due to killing them kriṣṇa who stood having vīraśrī (wealth of valour) and having gentle smile in the large, coral like reddish lips; what is the use of being born amidst sātvika sangam (assembly of devotees) for those who do not sing the natural qualities of such kriṣṇa, dance upside down and make noise in chaotic manner?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In fourth pāsuram – āḻvār says “If after meditating upon emperumān‘s quality of love which caused him to kill the seven bulls and marry \[his divine consort\] nappinnaip pirātti, one remains still, for what purpose were they born in vaiṣṇava family?”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. vambaviḻ kōtai poruttā māl vidai ēḻum adartta sem pavaḷat tiraḷ vāyan sirīdaran tol pugaḻ pādik kumbidu nattam ittādik kōgukattuṇḍuḻalādār tam piṟappāl payanennē sādu sanangaḷ idaiyē*

- *vambaviḻ kōdai poruttā* – vambu – fragrance. aviḻgai – spreading everywhere. kōdai – garland, it is used to indicate the hair \[which has the garland\]. It means – one who is wearing \[in her hair\] a garland, the fragrance of which is spreading everywhere. Presenting the well decorated nappinnaip pirātti and declared “she will be married to the one who wins over the seven bulls”; looking at her well decorated beauty and beautiful hair, ignoring his own safety, kriṣṇa presented \[risked\] himself for her as said in “*tavāsmi*” (I am for you).
- *māl vidai* – huge bulls. Seeing the hugeness, one will naturally take a step back out of fear.
- *ēḻum* – seven. As said in “*śrēyāmsi bahuvignāni*” (even for great persons, when doing noble tasks, there will be many hurdles), not one or two, but seven bulls that are hurdles.
- *adartta* – Since the result of winning them over is nappinnaip pirātti’s embrace, he crushed the necks of the bulls at once instead of handling them one at a time.
- *sem pavaḷat tiraḷ vāyan* – Since the hurdles are eliminated, he smiled. It can also be explained as kriṣṇa smiling, since the seven bulls are no match for his strong shoulders.
- *sirīdaran* – He stood with *vīra lakshmi* (wealth of valour) after killing the bulls. Another explanation – Stood there ready for nappinnaip pirātti’s embrace as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 30.39 and 30.40  “*bharttāram pariśasvajē*“. \[nampiḷḷai explains this ślōkam beautifully.\]
   - *tam druśtvā* – Previously she (sītā pirātti) only observed romantic exchanges. Now only she observed “he is capable of those who cause hurdles for such enjoyable exchanges”. Before, when he goes for hunting, she hears from his companions “he killed this beast, that rākśasa etc”; now she is personally witnessing him taking on the enemies.
   - *śatru hantāram* – one who completely destroyed the enemies instead of just sending them back with cuts and bruises. He did this without himself sweating much.
   - *maharśīṇām sukhāvaham* – Like a man will bring his child along to engage with his wife, śrī rāma killed the rākśasas who were the enemies of the riśis (sages), and presented himself in front of pirātti to accept her embrace.
   - *babhūva* – She was worried seeing the cruelty of the rākśasas and tenderness of śrī rāma and considered herself to have ceased to exist. Now, after seeing him victorious, she regained her existence.
   - *hruśtā* – If darmi (entity) exists, darmams (attributes and those which are supported by the entity), will also exist.
   - *vaidēhi* – sītā is one who is born in a family which is well aware of bravery \[vaidēhi – daughter of vidēha (janaka’s ancestor) clan\]. Another explanation – My father who gave you in marriage for launching and breaking one bow; what will he do if he saw your valour of killing 14000 rākśasa single-handed?
   - *bharttāram* – As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam bāla kāṇḍam 77.26 “*dārā: pitrukrutā:*” (given in marriage to you by her father), she loved śrī rāma, since it was her father who arranged the marriage; but, only now, she embraced him considering him to be a “real man”; previously it was sītā who said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 30.3 “*striyam puruśavigraham*” (you are a woman in the disguise of a man) \[when śrī rāma suggests sītā to not accompany her to the forest\].
   - *pariśasvajē* – She comforted śrī rāma, by pressing her divine breasts on the wounds caused in the battle. In the same way, kriṣṇa stood there waiting for nappinnai’s embrace.
- *tol pugaḻ* – Like those who are serving in the private quarters, singing about his qualities of loving affection which is part of his nature; they will sing as in [tiruppallāṇḍu 2](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/06/thiruppallandu-2-adiyomodum/) “*mangaiyum pallāṇḍu*“.
- *kumbidu* … – will do praṇāmams (worship) and dance. Also explained as – dancing with anjali (folded palms).
- *kōgu kattu* – dancing in a chaotic/disorderly manner
- *uṇḍu* – having that as their daily routine
- *uḻalādār* – those who don’t conduct this on a daily basis
- *tam piṟappāl* – having been born amidst those who dance in a disorderly manner, what is the purpose of such birth? What is the purpose of them accepting a body amidst vaiṣṇavas? piḷḷaip piḷḷai āḻvān (a disciple of [kūrattāḻvān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/kurathazhwan/)) explained “\[The presence of such uninterested persons among vaiṣṇavas would be like – when it is raining\] When many śrīvaiṣṇavas stand squeezed under a *tiruppunnai* (a divine tree), if strong village leaders with hairy shoulders and head covered with clothes \[like turban\] squeeze them further \[it will be very uncomfortable\]”.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.5.5. Sadu sanattai

*sādu sanattai naliyum kanjanaic cādippadaṟku ādiyanjōdi uruvai angu vaittingup piṟandu vēda mudalvanaip pādi vīdigaḷ tōṟum tuḷḷādār ōdi uṇarndavar munnā en savippār manisarē*

**Пословный перевод:**

sādu sanattai – Good natured people such as dēvaki, vasudēva et al; naliyum – hurting; kanjanai – kamsa; cādippadaṟku – to control; ādi – primordial; am – spiritual; sōdi – having divine splendour; uruvai – form; angu – in paramapadam (spiritual realm); (vaittu) – as had there; ingu vaittu – having it here also; piṟanda – one who was born; vēdam mudalvanai – the primary lord whose distinguished incarnations are revealed in vēdam \[as said in puruśa sūktam “ajāyamāna: … ” (the unborn, assumes many births) etc\]; pādi – singing (such glories); vīdigaḷ tōṟum – in all streets; tuḷḷādār – those who do not dance; ōdi – having studied śāstram; uṇarndavar – wise; munnā – in their presence; manisar – like humans; en – what; savippār – chanting they do?

**Перевод:**

**The primary lord whose distinguished incarnations are revealed in vēdam \[as said in puruśa sūktam “ajāyamāna: … ” (the unborn, assumes many births) etc\] was born with his primordial spirital form which is having divine splendour as in paramapadam, to control kamsa who was hurting good-natured people such as dēvaki, vasudēva et al. Those who do not sing (such glories) such emperumān and dance in all streets, what is the use, even if they chant like a human being in front of wise scholars who have studied vēdam? Implies that they are neither qualified to be called human beings nor their japam (chanting) is worthy.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In fifth pāsuram – āḻvār says “Those who remain indifferent after listening to emperumān‘s quality of incarnating, with his most distinguished divine form for the purpose of eliminating the enemies of his devotees, are not even considered worthy of existing”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “Those who  are not attracted towards incarnations of emperumān, for the purpose of eliminating the enemies of his devotees, what japa (chanting) etc would they do?”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. sādu sanattai naliyum kanjanaic cādippadaṟku ādiyanjōdi uruvai angu vaittingup piṟandu vēda mudalvanaip pādi vīdigaḷ tōṟum tuḷḷādār ōdi uṇarndavar munnā en savippār manisarē*

- *sādu sanattai naliyum* – śrī vasudēva and dēvaki indicated by sādu janam (sātvika, good-natured people). kamsa tortured and imprisoned the ones who he wanted to have as his parents as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam bāla kāṇḍam 77.26 “… *pitaram rōcayāmasa …*” ([bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) decided to accept daśarata as his father). śrī bhagavat gītā 4.8 “*paritrāṇāya sādūnām …* ” (I descend time and again to protect the sādus …) \[sādu is explained as one who is dear to bhagavān – i.e., his devotees\]. Also to kill kamsa.
- *ādi am sōdi uruvai* – His divine form is such that everyone will be amazed at it being the source of all the effects (material manifestation) here \[as indicated in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam astrabhūśaṇa adyāyam where each aspect of the creation such as [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)s (souls), [prakruti](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/09/thathva-thrayam-achith-what-is-matter/) (matter) etc are related to a divine part, ornament or weapon of [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)\], that which reveals his jñānam (knowledge) etc., making one thing his form seems to be made of his auspicious qualities.
- *angu vaittu ingup piṟanda* – Born here with the same features as in paramapadam. In śrī bhagavat gītā 4.6, he himself said “*prakrutim svāmadiśtāya*” (I am born … with my divine body). He took birth so that the residents of leelā vibhūti (material realm) can enjoy him the same way as the residents of nitya vibhūti (spiritual realm) would do. [āḻvārs](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/azhwars/) mercifully explained in mudal tiruvantādi 85 “*padi kaṇḍaṟidiyē*” (Have you seen his divine form and known him?) and iraṇḍām tiruvantādi 82 “*sevvip padikkōlam*” (the beauty of his fresh divine form). When he incarnates thinking “I should appear in many ways and many forms to protect them”, their \[samsāris – materialistic people\] nature/form is such that they refuse to reform and be protected. puruśa sūktam “*ajāyamānō bahudā vijāyatē*” (the unborn (one who has no necessity to take birth due to karma), assumes many births). mahābhāratam “*na bhūtasangasamstānō dēhō’sya paramātmana:*” (The divine body of [paramātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is not made of five gross elements) and “*na tasya prākrutā mūrti: …*” (The divine body of paramātmā is not made of worldly matter such as blood, flesh, bones etc). mahābhāratam mausala parvam “… *kalpē kalpē jāyamāna: svamūrtyā*” (In every kalpa (day of brahmā), you should appear with your divine original form and protect us). He appears in many different forms as said in periya tirumoḻi 4.9.8 “*munnai vaṇṇam pālin vaṇṇam muḻudum nilai ninṟa, pinnai vaṇṇam koṇḍal vaṇṇam*” (first in sat yugam, you appeared in milky white complexion and subsequently you appeared in dark cloud-like complexion which remains firmly since it happens in kaliyugam) and tiruccanda viruttam 44 “*pālinīrmai semponīrmai pāsiyin pasumpuṟam pōlunīrmai poṟpudait tadattu vaṇḍu viṇḍulām neelanīrmai*” ([emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) appears assuming different forms having various complexions such as milky white, molten gold like red, green, blackish-blue which is the color of a flower surrounded by golden colored bumble bees in a pond). \[appearing\] In different forms. Though he is born \[like this in this world\], there is no direct involvement of him in a mother’s womb as said in mahābhāratam “*naiśa garbatvamāpēdē na yōnyāvasat prabhu:*” (this kriṣṇa did not acquire the binding of being in a womb and did not reside in a womb). One should not wonder “How is this possible?”. In ikśvāku vamśam (clan), a king named “yuvanāśva”, drank sanctified water and became pregnant due to special powers \[of the sanctified water\]. There he did not give birth as a result of union of a man and woman. Similarly \[if it can be said in a normal human being, why not in case of supreme lord\], this principle could be understood by [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s omnipotent nature.

For this, śruti (vēdam) declaring “*ajāyamānō:*” is the authentic proof. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is explaining this further.

- *vēda mudalvanai* – Singing the one who is known from vēdam only. Singing the one who is highlighted as the supreme lord in vēdam. After saying “*piṟandavāṟu*” as in tiruvāimoḻi 5.10.1 \[since previously “*piṟanda*“, his birth is highlighted\], [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)  would be like “*ettiṟam*” (how is this possible?) as in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.3.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/06/thiruvaimozhi-1-3-1-paththudai-adiyavar/) and will not be able to move to his subsequent activities which are highlighted in tiruvāimoḻi 5.10.1 “*vaḷarndavāṟu*“. After saying “*ettiṟam*“, one can only repeat “*ettiṟam*” again and cannot move any further \[due to overwhelming emotions\]. As said in puruśa sūktam “*tasya dīrā: parijānanti yōnim*” (the upāsakas (devotees) would keep going around [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s birth), they will keep focussing on it \[his birth\].
- *vīdigaḷ tōṟum tuḷḷādār* – miḷagāḻvān’s words should be remembered \[in the eighth pāsuram, it is explained that when miḷagāḻvān was asked if we dance like this, would the on-lookers not laugh at us? he replies “their laughing will be our ornaments/decoration\]. Not just in big streets where there is lot of people, but in all streets/lanes. Those who don’t dance in every such streets.

Are you condemning such people who are not dancing and ignorant?, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says

- *ōdi uṇarndavar munnā* – Starting with those fully knowledgeable scholars who have studied \[learned the vēdam\] and heard \[the meanings of vēdam\]. \[But why are scholars condemned?\] “*viduśō’dikramē daṇḍabhūyastvam*” (when the learned scholars cross the boundaries of vēdam, don’t they deserve greater punishment?\].
- *en savippār* – What is the use of their existence? What is the purpose learning the mantram secretly and chanting it \[savippār – japippār\]?. Also explained as – Are they capable of cursing \[savippār – sabippār\] or blessing others?
- *manisarē* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is clarifying that though they are born in human form which is bound by śāstram, they will not be considered as humans. periya tirumoḻi 11.7.9 “*mānidavar allar enṟu en manattē vaittēnē*” (I placed in my mind that they are not to be considered as humans). Since the purpose of human birth is to surrender unto [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/), those who don’t do that will not be considered as humans. *en manattē vaittēnē* – Even [īśvara](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) cannot help him now. Like it is inscribed on copper plate or stone,  I, who will not give up easily on those even if īśvara gave up on them, myself have given up on them.

In the previous decad, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) enjoyed this material realm considering it to be a property of [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/). In this decad, as said in periya tirumoḻi 11.6.7 “*eṇṇāda mānidattai eṇṇāda pōdellām iniyavāṟē*” (when I don’t think about those who don’t think about bhagavān, it is very pleasant) and periya tirumoḻi 7.4.4 “*pērāḷan pērōdum periyōrai oru kālum pirigilēnē*” (I will never separate from those great souls who constantly recite the names of supreme lord), āḻvār accepted some and rejected others. Why is this contradiction? Previously, though he realized his position of being in this material realm, he was overwhelmed with considering everything as owned by bhagavān and expressed his emotions liked that. āḻvār has different states \[at different times\]. \[[pūrvācāryas](http://acharyas.koyil.org/)\] would explain that āḻvār can be said to have the state of mukta (liberated soul) by seeing the previous decad; He can be said to have the state of mumukśu (desirous to be liberated) by seeing this decad.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.
