## 3.5.6. Manisarum marrum

*manisarum maṟṟum muṟṟumāy māyap piṟavi piṟanda taniyan piṟappili tannait tadam kadal sērnda pirānai kaniyaik karumbin insāṟṟaik kattiyait tēnai amudai munivinṟi ēttik kunippār muḻuduṇar nīrmaiyinārē*

**Пословный перевод:**

manisarum – as humans; maṟṟum – other celestial forms; muṟṟumāy – assuming other animal forms; māyam – amazing; piṟavi – incarnations; piṟanda – assuming; taniyan – (though born in same species) one who is totally distinguished, incomparable person; piṟappili tannai – one who is not having births (not being bound by karma, which is the reason for this distinction); tadam – vast; kadal – in the milk ocean; sērnda – one who is resting; pirānai – one who does favours; kaniyai – like a fruit (which tempts every one to eat as soon as it is seen); in – faultless sweet; karumbin sāṟṟai – sugarcane juice; kattiyai – and the block of sugar (which is tasteful in every particle); tēn – honey (which is fully tasteful); amudai – most enjoyable like nectar (which gives immortality to the one who drinks it); munivu – hatred (in considering the incarnations to be inferior); inṟi – without; ētti – praising (the qualities of such incarnations such as simplicity, easy approacability etc); kunippār – those who dance with somersaults (out of that joy); muḻudu – all śāstrams; uṇar – knowing; nīrmaiyinār – having the nature

**Перевод:**

**emperumān, (though born in same species) one who is totally distinguished, incomparable person, one who is not having births (not being bound by karma, which is the reason for this distinction) assumes amazing incarnations \[In the forms of \[human\] śrī rāma, kriṣṇa et al, \[celestial\] upēndra (vāmana), \[animal\] matsya (fish), kūrma (tortoise) etc\] as humans, other celestial forms and other animal forms. One who does favours is resting in the milk ocean (for such incarnations); he is like a fruit (which tempts every one to eat as soon as it is seen); he is like sugarcane juice which has faultless sweetness and the block of sugar (which is tasteful in every particle); he is like honey (which is fully tasteful); he is most enjoyable like nectar (which gives immortality to the one who drinks it); those who praise (the qualities of such incarnations such as simplicity, easy approacability etc) without hatred (in considering the incarnations to be inferior, dance with somersaults (out of that joy) are having the nature of know all śāstrams.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In sixth pāsuram – āḻvār says “Those who enjoy thinking about emperumān‘s enjoyability of incarnating in human forms etc and stay blissful, are realized of all results of \[true\] knowledge”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. manisarum maṟṟum muṟṟumāy māyap piṟavi piṟanda taniyan piṟappili tannait tadam kadal sērnda pirānai kaniyaik karumbin insāṟṟaik kattiyait tēnai amudai munivinṟi ēttik kunippār muḻuduṇar nīrmaiyinārē*

- *manisarum maṟṟum muṟṟumāy* – human forms, celestial forms and all other forms that are not spelt out such as animal forms, plant forms. varadarāja stavam 18 “*suranaratiraścāmavataran*” (born amidst celestial beings, humans, animals and plants).
- *māyap piṟavi piṟanda* – Though there is no binding for him, he would assume the forms that are hated even by those who are bound. One who assumes many amazing incarnations.
- *taniyan* – While incarnating, he would go with the clothes he was wearing \[as in the case of śrī rāma going to forest giving up everything\]. In rāmāvatāram, we have heard that only a few accompanied him to the forest.  They not only forget to think “[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) appeared for our upliftment”, they also explain his birth as a fault in him \[like, people saying “he incarnated in a particular form due to the curse of a riśi” etc., without understanding his true nature\].
- *piṟappili tannai* – \[Though unborn\] While being born for others’ benefit like this, even if he does not succeed in his mission, instead of giving up thinking “though we are taking so much efforts, there is no success”, he again takes birth.
- *tadam kadal sērnda pirānai* – His form of performing penance to be born again. The anirudda form which is lying/resting on milk ocean is the root of all incarnations. He is explained in tiruppāvai 6 as “*veḷḷattaravil tuyil amarnda vittu*” ([emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is the seed who is resting on ādiśēśan in the ocean). To remove the ocean of birth/samsāram of the bound souls, he descends and rests on the ocean,
- *kaniyai …* – Like the ocean became a fruit; ōr, it has become a fruit having soaked in milk. The sweetness due to the beauty acquired as a result of resting in the milk ocean. Unlike it is said in cāndōjña upaniśat “*sarvarasa:*” (all the tastes), [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) cannot say it in one word. He cannot stop glorifying [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) while attempting to do so. He is just describing in a few ways based on his personal experience \[of emperumān\]. Thus, he is praising emperumān as “fruit”. The fruit which is so tempting to be eaten as soon as it is seen \[kani – fruit\], the juice of such fruit after removing all the pulp etc \[karumbin sāṟu – juice\], the block which is made of such juice \[katti – sugar block\], that which can be drunk \[tēn – honey\] and not just enjoyable but also can give immortality (amudu – nectar\]. āḻvār is reminded by his sweetness which he enjoyed in previous decad – [tiruvāimoḻi 3.4.3](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/08/thiruvaimozhi-3-4-5-achchudhan-amalan/) “*nalam kadal amudam enkō*“.
- *munivinṟi ēttik kunippār* – *munivu inṟi* means without jealousy. When hearing about [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/), those who praise him without jealousy. People may be jealous when a co-human is praised. Would they be jealous if the supreme lord is glorified? Yes, there are many who are jealous of bhagavān’s great quality \[of avatāra saulabhyam – his simplicity in his incarnations\], not only that, they also find faults in him \[in his incarnations, that they are mere mortal forms and not the forms of supreme\]. kriṣṇa told arjuna in [śrī bhagavat gītā](http://githa.koyil.org/) 9.1 “*idam tu tē guhyatamam pravakśyāmi anasūyavē*” (I am talking to you this most secret knowledge, since you are not jealous of me) “When I explained to you my true nature, forms, qualities and wealth, you did not show any jealousy, and I have not seen any one who is (receptive) like you. So, I will reveal you more which I have not explained to you previously, please come near me”. \[Would there be jealousy/hatred towards [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) in his devotees or favourable persons?\] kriṣṇa performed many great tasks to help/protect pāṇḍavas such as presenting sanganidi and padmanidi (great wealth), building a palace/capital inside the ocean (dvārakā) and accepting the arrows of their enemies on his own chest. Even after doing that, for very insignificant matters, they would say “who is this kriṣṇa? what is he doing?”. kriṣṇa himself said in mahābhāratam “*dāsyamaiśvaryavādēna*” (I am serving them (pāṇḍavas) in the name of protecting them) – in the name of rakśakatvam (protecting them), I served them in various ways; when I received something good, I shared with them; still whatever harsh words they say, I bear them. When a precious gem was lost, being stolen by some one else, kriṣṇa was blamed for it and nambi mūtta pirān (balarāma) went on a pilgrimage citing this insult \[syamantaka jewel was taken by a lion which eventually reached jāmbavān – but kriṣṇa was blamed by his own relatives that he stole the jewel\]. Alternatively, munivu means munitvam (being a muni – one who has clear state of mind due to constant meditation); so munivu inṟi means having disturbed mind. This is explained as those who sing and dance in a disorderly manner.
- *muḻuduṇar nīrmaiyinārē* – As said in “*ēka vijñānēna sarva vijñānām*” (one who knows that one \[supreme\] thing, he knows everything), they become all-knowing; i.e., omniscient. Once they know the result of true knowledge \[[bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) and his qualities\], there is nothing they don’t know. Just by the emotional manifestation in their body, their great knowledge can be understood. They become fully knowledgeable.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.5.7. Nirmaiyil nurruvar

*nīrmaiyil nūṟṟuvar vīya aivarkkaruḷ seydu ninṟu pār malgu sēnai avitta param sudarai ninaindādi nīr malgu kaṇṇinarāgi nenjam kuḻaindu naiyādē ūn malgi mōdu paruppār uttamargatken seyvārē*

**Пословный перевод:**

nīrmai – compassion (of wanting to share with relatives); il – not having; nūṟṟuvar – starting with duryōdana, the hundred brothers; vīya – to be killed; aivarkku – for the pāṇḍavas; aruḷ – unlimited mercy; seydu – gave; ninṟu – standing there for them (as all types of relative for them as said in mahābhāratam drōṇa parvam 183.24 “kriṣṇāśrayā: kriṣṇabalā: kriṣṇanātāśca pāṇḍavā:” (pāṇḍavas are surrendered to kriṣṇa; kriṣṇa is their strength and kriṣṇa is their lord)); pār – earth; malgu – filled; sēnai – army; avitta – destroyed (effortlessly like turning off the wick in an oil lamp); param sudarai – having beautiful form which has infinite splendor; ninaindu – think (as having such beauty etc); ādi – dance (due to overwhelming love); nīr – happy-tears; malgu – filled; kaṇṇinarāgi – having eyes; nenjam – heart (that thought about him); kuḻaindu – losing its hardness; naiyādē – instead of having weak body (with goose bumps etc); Un malgi – having more muscles; mōdu paruppār – growing their bodies which are having huge shoulders; uttamargatku – for the best bhāgavatas (who are most knowledgeable); en seyvār – what purpose will they serve?

**Перевод:**

**emperumān who is having beautiful form which has infinite splendor, destroyed (effortlessly like turning off the wick in an oil lamp) the army which filled the earth, standing there for pāṇḍavas (as all types of relative for them as said in mahābhāratam drōṇa parvam 183.24 “kriṣṇāśrayā: kriṣṇabalā: kriṣṇanātāśca pāṇḍavā:” (pāṇḍavas are surrendered to kriṣṇa; kriṣṇa is their strength and kriṣṇa is their lord)) and gave them unlimited mercy to have the hundred brothers starting with duryōdana killed, for not having compassion (of wanting to share with relatives). Those who do not think about such emperumān (as having such beauty etc), dance (due to overwhelming love), have eyes filled with happy-tears, lose hardness of heart (that thought about him), have weak body (with goose bumps etc) and instead have more muscles, growing their bodies which are having huge shoulders – what purpose will they serve for the best bhāgavatas (who are most knowledgeable)?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In seventh pāsuram – āḻvār says “Those who do not melt thinking about the qualities of emperumān who eliminated the enemies of pāṇḍavas who are his devotes, are the ones who cause pain to their mothers”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “What use is to bhāgavatas of such persons who do not become attracted to emperumān‘s partiality towards his devotees?”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Seventh pāsuram. āḻvār says “Those who are not attracted to emperumān‘s great quality of partiality towards his devotees and just roam around feeding their own bodies – what purpose do they serve being born for vaiṣṇavas?”. nīrmaiyil nūṟṟuvar vīya aivarkkaruḷ seydu ninṟu pār malgu sēnai avitta param sudarai ninaindādi nīr malgu kaṇṇinarāgi nenjam kuḻaindu naiyādē Un malgi mōdu paruppār uttamargatken seyvārē*

- *nīrmai* … – kriṣṇa first sent sanjaya and subsequently he himself went and tried to unite pāṇḍavas and kauravas. But kaurava did not agree in any manner and arrogantly said “If they live, we cannot live. We will not give them any land. Since we are many, we need the whole earth for our own use. They have kriṣṇa and darmam (virtuous ways) and will enjoy heaven as a result of that \[kauravas thought – when they come fight us considering their own virtue, we will eventually kill them and they will attain vīra svargam (heaven for those who fought in battle with valour and died) – they were very confident in this manner\] and we will continue to rule the earth”. kriṣṇa observed that they absolutely have no compassion and decided to kill them. kriṣṇa protected pāṇḍavas \[for their compassion\] since they said “we cannot live without our relatives”; as said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 1.33](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/1-33/) “*yēśām artē kānkśitam nō rājyam bhōgā:sukānica …*” (For the purpose of those teachers et al we are desiring kingdom, pleasures, joy etc., those teachers et al are standing here willing to give up their lives, wealth etc.), “people seek out for wealth and win over kingdoms, to enjoy the result with their relatives. In that case, we will not kill our relatives and desire to enjoy” – such was their compassion. But duryōdana et al said “we will not even give a small piece of land, if they live, we can’t live”. Seeing this, kriṣṇa thought “They are demoniac. If we don’t kill them, the whole world will be destroyed” and set out to kill them. To have duryōdana et al who don’t have any compassion, killed.
- *aivarkku aruḷ seydu ninṟu* – for the pāṇḍavas who have no other refuge than himself. They are as said in mahābhāratam drōṇa parvam 183.24 “*kriṣṇāśrayā: kriṣṇabalā: kriṣṇanātāśca pāṇḍavā:*” (pāṇḍavas are surrendered to kriṣṇa; kriṣṇa is their strength and kriṣṇa is their lord). *ninṟu* – Standing for them in all aspects as said in mahābhāratam rājasūya yāga parvam “*yasya mantrī ca gōptā ca suhruccaiva janārdana:*” (sanjaya said “since kriṣṇa, the lord of all worlds, is the minister, protector and friend for yudiśtra, what can yudiśtra not achieve?”).
- *pār malgu sēnai avitta* – He burnt the demoniac persons who were causing great burden to the earth, like turning off the wick of a lamp, so that even their dead bodies are not traceable.
- *param sudarai* – They requested him not to take up arms; to fulfil that he assumed the form of a charioteer with the dust of the army on his head, a stick to drive the horses of the chariot, a small rope to keep the horses in control, having his feet firm on the ground under the chariot, with beautiful anklets in his feet \[In [piḷḷai lōkācāryar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/pillai-lokacharyar/)‘s mumukśuppadi, 218th sūtram resembles these words of nampiḷḷai in a very similar manner\].
- *ninaindu ādi* – Thinking about his subservience towards his devotees, and such thinking leading to not staying in one place, and dancing.
- *nīrmalgu kaṇṇinarāgi* – As said in śrīviṣṇu tatvam “*āhlādaśītanētrāmbu:*” (Having happy-tear filled eyes due to meditating upon [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)), they are having eyes that are identified by the tears.
- *nenjam kuḻaindu* – Not just external weakness, even the heart has become weak.
- *Un malgi mōdu paruppar* – They grow their body which is muscular, having strong shoulders and strong physique.
- *uttamargatku en seyvārē* – Will they be companions for those great personalities who have lean body due to constant meditation of [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s qualities? [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says – the purpose of taking birth is to help/serve vaiṣṇavas. [īsvara](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) makes himself and his wealth available for his devotees. \[An incident where āḻvān explains this principle of everything existing for devotees\] When krimikaṇḍa cōḷa king in āyirattaḷi (the town) tortured and drove out [periya nambi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/periya-nambi/) and [kūrattāḻvān](https://guruparamparaitamil.wordpress.com/2016/07/20/kurathazhwan/), periya nambi ascends to the spiritual realm (giving up his body) placing his head on āḻvān’s lap. At that time, some people who usually say “we will help those orphans who die without help in cremating them” came there and saw āḻvān with periya nambi’s remains and said “there is one person to help” and started leaving. At that time āḻvān who never has the habit of blaming any one, said “Come on sons! are you seeking out for a vaiṣṇava who is orphan who needs to be cremated? While [īsvara](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) and his whole wealth (worlds) exist to do menial services to vaiṣṇavas, where are you going to find vaiṣṇavas who are orphans/helpless?”.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.5.8. Var punal

*vār punal andaṇ aruvi vada tiruvēnkatattendai pēr pala sollip pidaṟṟip pittar enṟē piṟar kūṟa ūr pala pukkum pugādum ulōgar sirikka ninṟādi ārvam perugik kunippār amarar toḻap paduvāṟē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vār – falling; punal – having water; am – beautiful; taṇ – cool; aruvi – having water falls; vada – (for tamiḻ land) the northern boundary; tiruvēntattu – standing on the great tirumalā; endai – my lord’s; pēr – divine names (which reflect his true nature, forms, qualities and wealth); pala – many; solli – speak; pidaṟṟi – blabber in a disorderly manner; piṟar – others (who lack devotion towards bhagavān); pittar enṟu – as mad; kūṟa – to be said; pala Ur – in many towns (which are inhabited by people); pukkum – entered; pugādum – even in those places which are not inhabited by people; ulōgar – worldly people; sirikka – to laugh at; ninṟu – standing (with overwhelming emotions); ādi – dance around; ārvam – enthusiasm; perugi – abundance; kunippār – dance with somersaults; amarar – sūris who are eternally enjoying bhagavān; toḻap paduvār – will be glorified

**Перевод:**

**My lord (tiruvēnkatamudaiyān) is standing on the great tirumalā which is (for tamiḻ land) the northern boundary and is having water falls with beautiful cool falling water. The devotees speak and blabber in a disorderly manner, such emperumān‘s many divine names (which reflect his true nature, forms, qualities and wealth)). Due to that, they enter in to many towns (which are inhabited by people) and even in those places which are not inhabited by people, to be called as mad by others (who lack devotion towards bhagavān) and to be laughed at by worldly people and still standing (with overwhelming emotions) and dance around doing somersaults with abundance of enthusiasm; such devotees will be glorified by sūris who are eternally enjoying bhagavān.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In eighth pāsuram – āḻvār says “Those who are always attached to the qualities of tiruvēnkatamudaiyān who is approached by every one, though being in samsāram (material realm), they are greater than nityasūris (eternally free souls of paramapadam)”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “Those who perform acts which are in deep attachment to sarvēśvaran who is in arcā (deity) form with simplicity in tirumalā, they will be honored by nityasūris”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Eighth pāsuram. āḻvār says “Who are we to glorify those who are attached to the simplicity of tiruvēnkatamudaiyān? nityasūris themselves are glorifying them”. vār punal andaṇ aruvi vada tiruvēnkatattendai pēr pala sollip pidaṟṟip pittar enṟē piṟar kūṟa Ur pala pukkum pugādum ulōgar sirikka ninṟādi ārvam perugik kunippār amarar toḻap paduvāṟē*

- *vār punal* … – My lord descended into northern tirumalā which has beautiful, invigorating water falls which have dripping water.
- *pēr …* – Speaking his many divine names in a disorderly manner. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is highlighting his own experience in “[*oḻivil kālam*](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/08/thiruvaimozhi-3-3-ozhivil/)*“* \[tiruvāimoḻi 3.3.1\] and “[*pugaḻu nal oruvan*](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/08/thiruvaimozhi-3-4-pugazhum/)” \[tiruvāimoḻi 3.4.1\].
- *pala solli* – Speaking those phrases which relate to his true nature, forms, qualities and his wealth in great detail.
- *pittar enṟē piṟar kūṟa* – Those who are indifferent (disinterested) on hearing [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s divine names would watch [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) saying [“](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/08/thiruvaimozhi-3-4-1-pugazhum-nal-oruvan/)[*poruvil sīr būmi enkō*](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/08/thiruvaimozhi-3-4-1-pugazhum-nal-oruvan/)[“, “](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/08/thiruvaimozhi-3-4-1-pugazhum-nal-oruvan/)[*kaṇṇanaik kūvumāṟē*](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/08/thiruvaimozhi-3-4-1-pugazhum-nal-oruvan/)[“](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/08/thiruvaimozhi-3-4-1-pugazhum-nal-oruvan/), [“](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/08/thiruvaimozhi-3-4-2-kuvumaru/)[*kunṟangaḷ anaittum enkō*](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/08/thiruvaimozhi-3-4-2-kuvumaru/)[“, “](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/08/thiruvaimozhi-3-4-2-kuvumaru/)[*pangayak kaṇṇanaiyē*](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/08/thiruvaimozhi-3-4-2-kuvumaru/)[“](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/08/thiruvaimozhi-3-4-2-kuvumaru/), [“jñālam uṇḍumiḻnda mālai eṇṇumāṟu aṟiya māttēn yāvaiyum yavarum tānē”](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/08/thiruvaimozhi-3-4-9-kannanai-mayan/) \[The concept of bhagavān as the substratum/bearer of all objects/entities, which is explained in these pāsurams of previous decad, is not possible to understand for those who have not heard/understood vēdāntam. So, they look at āḻvār as a mad person who is talking unrelated things\]. Others would think “āḻvār is mad” and āḻvār would \[know and\] say “they are mad”. As said in periya tirumoḻi 7.1.8 “*attā ariyē enṟunnai aḻaikkap pittāvenṟu pēsuginṟār piṟar ennai*” (When I call you (bhagavān) as father, hari, they speak about me as a mad person), perumāḷ tirumoḻi 3.8 “*pēyarē enakku yāvarum yānumōr pēyanē yavarkkum*” (Others look like mad people to me and I look like a mad person to them), just like their \[worldly people\] acts would look disorderly to āḻvār, āḻvār’s acts would look disorderly to them.
- *piṟar kūṟa* – More than vaiṣṇavas acknowledging us, avaiṣṇavas declaring “he is not fit for us” and giving up is most desired; vibhīśaṇāḻvān considered rāvaṇa saying as in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 16.15 “*tvām tu dik kulapāmsanam*” (you are an outcast from our rākśasa clan), as desirable. An ācārya named miḷagaḻvān once heard about a king \[who was unfavourable towards vaiṣṇavas\] giving gifts and went there. The king said “we won’t give you anything” and miḷagāḻvān said “Why so? if you want to test competenece in vēdam or overall śāstram, you can do so and then give me gifts”. The king said “You are well qualified in those. I won’t disagree”. miḷagāḻvān asked “Then why are you refusing me gifts?” and the king replied “That is because, you are a vaiṣṇava”. Hearing this miḷagāḻvān took off his upper cloth, threw it up and danced for being given up by an avaiṣṇava. *prātikūlya varjanam* (giving up unfavourable aspects) alone is required.
- *Ur pala* … – Entering in places which are inhabited and not inhabited by humans. When those who don’t understand the greatness of such efforts see this and laugh at them, they would consider that as the music/tune and dance for that, and will be filled with enthusiasm and dance more.
- *amarar toḻap paduvārē* – They will be glorified by nityasūris. Those nityasūris who are always in the presence of [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) and sing/dance as said in taittiriya upaniśat “*ahamannam ahamannam ahamannam*” (I am enjoyed by him – emphasised 3 times), will glorify them \[who are singing and dancing for [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) in this material relam\].

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.5.9. Amarar tolappaduvanai

*amarar toḻap paduvānai anaittulagukkum pirānai amara manattinuḷ yōgu puṇarndavan tannōdonṟāga amarat tuṇiya vallārgaḷ oḻiya allādavarellām amara ninaindeḻundādi alaṟṟuvadē karumamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

amarar – for nityasūris; toḻap paduvānai – being perfectly enjoyable; anaittu ulagukkum – for all worlds; pirānai – sarvēśvara who is the lord; amara – firmly; manattinuḷ – in the mind; yōgu – through yōga; puṇarndu – filled; avan tannōdu onṟāga – to attain parama sāmyāpatti (supreme equality to him \[in eight qualities\]); amara tuṇiya vallārgaḷ – those bhaktas who are able to have firm faith; oḻiya – instead; allādavar ellām – those who others who have not acquired (bhakti caused by such yōga); amara – to be situated in this; ninaindu – thinking; eḻundu – pursuing it; ādi alaṟṟuvadē – (like them) dancing and blabbering; karumam – is to be done

**Перевод:**

**bhaktas are able to have firm faith on sarvēśvara who is the lord for all worlds and who is being perfectly enjoyable for nityasūris, to have him in their minds, have their heart filled with him through yōga, and are thus able to attain parama sāmyāpatti (supreme equality to him \[in eight qualities\]); For those who are unlike those bhaktas, the others (who have not acquired (bhakti caused by such yōga), should be situated in this thinking about him, pursuing (like them) dancing and blabbering. This is to be done.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In ninth pāsuram – āḻvār condemns those who are situated in kaivalya puruśārta niśtā (seeking self realization/enjoyment eternally ignoring service to bhagavān) and requests all others to enjoy bhagavān’s qualities with great love which he identifies as the puruśārtam (true goal).*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār tells those who are not bhakti yōga niśtars who are deeply attached to bhagavān who is the lord of spiritual and material realms, “you look at them (bhakti yōga niśtars) and follow what they do – this is to be done” \[vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar differs from other commentators in this pāsuram\].*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Ninth pāsuram. āḻvār tells kavailya puruśārta niśtar “Instead of attaining bhagavān who is with many auspicious qualities such as śeela (simplicity) etc, you are holding on to ātmānubhavam (self enjoyment) which is similar to firefly” and condemns them, and tells the others “Instead of considering matters outside bhagavān as goal, you meditate upon bhagavān’s qualities and blissfully sing and dance. This is the duty”. amarar toḻap paduvānai anaittulagukkum pirānai amara manattinuḷ yōgu puṇarndavan tannōdonṟāga amarat tuṇiya vallārgaḷ oḻiya allādavarellām amara ninaindeḻundādi alaṟṟuvadē karumamē*

- *amarar toḻap paduvānai* – Being vorśipped by nityasūris who are greater than brahmā rudra et al.
- *anaittulagukkum pirānai*  – sarvalōkēśvara (lord of all worlds).
- *amara manattinuḷ yōgu puṇarndu* – Performing yōgābhyāsam \[practice of aśtāngayōga – eight limbed yōga – yama, niyama, Asana, prāṇāyāma, pratyāhāra, dāraṇa, dhyāna, samādi\] deeply to have him firmly seated in the mind/heart.
- *avan tannōdu onṟāga amarat tuṇiya vallārgaḷ oḻiya* – Other than those inferior persons who consider their own self to be equal to [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/), during the final moments (before liberation), Does “*onṟāga*” (union, being one) indicate equality? kriṣṇa explained the union in śrī bhagavat gītā 6.31 “*sarvabhūtastitam yō mām bhajatyēkatvamāstita:*” (One who worships me who is all pervading, in union) and when the same principle was repeated again \[by arjuna\], it was said to be in equanimous state in śrī bhagavat gītā 6.33 as “*yō’yam yōgastvayā prōkta: sāmyēna madusūdana:*” (madusūdana! that yōga which was explained by you as being in an equanimous state). Thus, other than those who are bold enough to consider [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) to be as pure as [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/), during the final moments. Can we consider these to be vilakśaṇa adikāris (bhakti yōga niśtar) and “*allādavar ellām*” (all others) to be “those who are not qualified to engage in bhakti yōga, you think about him, sing and dance”? No, that cannot be done. That is because, the current context is as explained previously in 5th pāsuram “*ōdi uṇarndavar munnā*“, it is said that “those who are indifferent after hearing the glories of [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/), however great may be their birth or activities, they are inferior, not even considered to be existing” and “even if they are inferior by their birth or activities, if they become emotional hearing the glories of bhagavān, they are said to be ‘*muḻuduṇar nīrmaiyinār*‘ (having the nature of omniscience)” in 6th pāsuram glorifying these persons and condemning those persons as in 5th pāsuram “*en savippār manisarē*” (what worth is their chanting); in this context, we should consider the meaning to be “those who surrender to [sarvēśvaran](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) and yet leave him after getting insignificant result \[ātmānubhavam – self enjoyment\], are considered as not worthy of existing” itself.
- *allādavar ellām* – Others who are different from those inferior persons who meditate upon their own self and hold back their heart from getting attached to [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) who is with auspicious qualities.
- *amara ninaindu eḻundādi* – Being ananya prayōjana (focussed exclusively on serving [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)), meditating upon him firmly, out of the bliss acquired from such meditation, dance and praise him in a disorderly manner – this is to be done.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.5.10. Karumamum

*karumamum karuma palanum āgiya kāraṇan tannait tirumaṇi vaṇṇanaic cengaṇ mālinait tēva pirānai orumai manattinuḷ vaittuḷḷam kuḻaindeḻundādi perumiayu(m) nāṇum tavirndu pidaṟṟumin pēdaimai tīrndē*

**Пословный перевод:**

karumamum – karma (in the form of sādana (means)); karuma palanum – the fruits of such karma; āgiya kāraṇan tannai – being the cause of all of them which occur according to his will; tiru – beautiful (for those who pursue him as the means and goal); maṇi – like a māṇikkam (precious stone); vaṇṇanan – having form (which is śubhāśrayam (auspicious refuge)); sem – reddish; kaṇ – eyes; mālinai – having vātsalyam (motherly affection); dēvapirānai – enjoyable for them as enjoyed by nityasūris; orumai – singular (so there is no difference between means and goal); manattinuḷ – in the heart/mind; vaittu – placing; uḷḷam kuḻaindu – having melted heart (for these two aspects of emperumān); eḻundu – rise; ādi – dance; perumaiyum – pride (which leads to arrogance); nāṇum – shyness (which is the cause for such pride, which makes one think “why should I dance in front of other humans?”); tavirndu – giving up; pēdaimai – foolishness (of considering such emotional reaction to be inferior); pidaṟṟumin – chant (his groups of qualities) in a disorderly manner

**Перевод:**

**emperumān is the cause of all the karma (in the form of sādana (means)) and the fruits of such karma, which occur according to his will; he is having a beautiful (for those who pursue him as the means and goal) māṇikkam (precious stone) like form (which is śubhāśrayam (auspicious refuge)); (to bless them fully) he is having reddish eyes and vātsalyam (motherly affection); he is enjoyable for them as enjoyed by nityasūris; \[all of you should\] be placing such emperumān in the heart/mind in a singular manner, having melted heart (for these two aspects of emperumān), should rise and dance giving up pride (which leads to arrogance), shyness (which is the cause for such pride, which makes one think “why should I dance in front of other humans?”) and foolishness (of considering such emotional reaction to be inferior) and chant (his groups of qualities) in a disorderly manner.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In tenth pāsuram – āḻvār says “Giving up the foolishness of being indifferent when hearing bhagavān’s qualities, all of you meditate upon his qualities, being blissful, giving up shyness and pride, come and glorify him”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently; previously āḻvār said that the great devotion of upāsakas (bhakti yōgis) in the matter of bhagavān who has distinguished forms, even those who had not engaged in such great devotion, should obediently follow the upāsakas; here – he is telling those ananya sādana (who pursue emperumān only as means) and ananya prayōjana (who consider emperumān only as goal) to be blissfully engaged in great devotion and emotionally charged \[vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar differs from other commentators in this pāsuram\].*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Tenth pāsuram. Previously, āḻvār condemned kēvalar \[those who are focussed in kaivalya or self-enjoyment\]; here – he says “Being ananya prayōjana, you meditate upon his qualities and be emotionally charged; this is your goal”. karumamum karuma palanum āgiya kāraṇan tannait tirumaṇi vaṇṇanaic cengaṇ mālinait tēva pirānai orumai manattinuḷ vaittuḷḷam kuḻaindeḻundādi perumiayu(m) nāṇum tavirndu pidaṟṟumin pēdaimai tīrndē*

- *karumamum …* – being the controller for karma in the form of puṇya (virtue) and pāpa (sin) and the results of such karma. Though there is karma, there must be someone who performs such karma. Being the one who performs karma. Being the controller through the one who performs work.
- *karuma palanum āgiya* – Though one performs karma, unless some one bestows the results, those karma are useless, since the karma themselves are acit (insentient). Being the one who gives the result \[karma itself is not knowledgeable to give the result, [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is the one who gives the result, seeing the performance of karma\].
- *kāraṇan tannai* – A kartā \[controller, in this context\] is required to engage [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)s into puṇya (virtuous acts), to eliminate the pāpa (sins) and to bestow the results; being the controller of all of that.
- tiru maṇi vaṇṇanai – For an upāsaka (one who engages in meditation/worship), a vigraha (form) is explained as śubhāśrayam (auspicious refuge). One who is the having the divine form which is the object of such meditation. tiru – kānti (radiance). One who is having an invigorating form which has abundant radiance.
- *sem kaṇ mālinai* – Having divine eyes which showcase his motherly affection. puṇḍarikākśatvam (lotus eyes) is a distinguished identity for the supreme cause ([bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)).
- *dēva pirānai* – He became my saviour, by making me enjoy the beauty of his divine form and divine eyes, as the nityasūris would enjoy them.
- *orumai manattinuḷ vaittu* – Instead of placing bhagavān in the heart to achieve something else, placing him in the heart simply to have him there as the result. From this, we can understand that [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) condemned prayōjanāntaraparar (one who seeks out other benefits \[specifically kaivalya niśtars who meditated upon [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/), yet wanted only self-enjoyment in the end\]).
- *uḷḷam …* – Having placed bhagavān in the heart in this manner as an ananyaprayōjanar (one who is exclusively focussed on bhagavān), the heart melts, unable to stand still; dance with that melted heart, giving up 1) superiority complex which is a result pride which makes one think “Is it fit for us to show our emotions when we hear about [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)?”, 2) shyness of thinking “How can we show our emotions in public?” and 3) foolishness of thinking “Should we not control our emotions in all situations and not show them in front of others?”, and praise him in a disorderly manner. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says “this is the true goal”.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.5.11. Tirnda adiyavar

*tīrnda adiyavar tammait tiruttip paṇikoḷḷa valla ārnda pugaḻ accudanai amarar pirānai emmānai vāynda vaḷa vayal sūḻ taṇ vaḷam kurugūrc catakōpan nērnda ōr āyirattippattu aruvinai nīṟu seyyumē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tīrnda – determined (in īśvara being the upāya (means) and upēya (goal)); adiyavar tammai – devotees; tirutti – reform them (first by eliminating their hurdles and bestowing them parabhakti, parajñānam etc); paṇi – eternal service; koḷḷavalla – one who is able to engage; ārnda – being complete (since he is omnipotent); pugaḻ – having groups of qualities; accudanai – being the one who never leaves his devotees; amarar pirānai – one who accepts their service as he would accept the service of nityasūris; ammānai – sarvēśvara; vāynda – good; vaḷam – having richness; vayal – crop-fields; sūḻ – surrounded; taṇ – invigorating; vaḷam – having abundant wealth; kurugūr – being the controller of āḻvārtirunagari; śatakōpan – nammāḻvār; nērnda – spoke (about the greatness of the ones who have overwhelming devotion and condemnation of ones who lack that); ōr – distinguished; āyirattu – in the thousand pāsurams; i – this; pattu – decad; aruvinai – great sins (which stop one from getting emotionally charged while meditating upon the qualities of bhagavān); nīṟu seyyum – will burn them into ashes

**Перевод:**

**emperumān reforms those devotees of him who are determined (in īśvara being the upāya (means) and upēya (goal), first by eliminating their hurdles and bestowing them parabhakti, parajñānam etc) and is able to engage them in eternal service; he is complete (since he is omnipotent); he is having groups of qualities; he is the one who never leaves his devotees; he is the one who accepts their service as he would accept the service of nityasūris; nammāḻvār who is the controller of āḻvārtirunagari which is having abundant wealth and is surrounded by good rich invigorating crop-fields, spoke (about the greatness of the ones who have overwhelming devotion and condemnation of ones who lack that) such emperumān in this decad as part of the distinguished thousand pāsurams; such decad will burn the great  sins (which stop one from getting emotionally charged while meditating upon the qualities of bhagavān) into ashes.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the end, āḻvār says “For those who learn this decad, this decad itself will completely eradicate the great sin of not being emotionally charged by thinking about bhagavān“.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār explains the eradication of the hurdles for enjoying bhagavān as the result of this decad.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. tīrnda adiyavar tammait tiruttip paṇikoḷḷa valla ārnda pugaḻ accudanai amarar pirānai emmānai vāynda vaḷa vayal sūḻ taṇ vaḷam kurugūrc catakōpan nērnda ōr āyirattippattu aruvinai nīṟu seyyumē*

- *tīrnda adiyavar tammai* – “*tīrnda adiyavar*” (determined devotees) are those who considers [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) to be the prāpakam (means) and prāpyam (goal).
- *tiruttip paṇi koḷḷa valla* – Reforming them means eliminating their hurdles in their \[pursuing of the\] prāpakam and prāpyam. Though one is in the state as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 31.25 “*aham sarvam kariśyāmi*” (Let me serve you in all ways), one should be as said in āraṇya kāṇḍam 15.7 “*kriyatāmiti mām vada*” (lakśmaṇa to śrī rāma – order me in what should be done) \[[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) should engage them in service when requested\].
- *ārnda pugaḻ accudanai* – Being with abundant auspicious qualities, one who has never heard the words “he abandoned the ones who surrendered unto him”.
- *amarar pirānai emmānai* – Accepting service from me who has no attachment towards him, as he would accept service from nityasūris who are never touched by samsāram (material realm). āḻvār is speaking based on his own experience of [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s acyutatvam (quality of not abandoning his devotees) instead of speaking based on what he heard from others.
- *vāynda* – vāygai – attaining. Not just thinking about bhagavān’s qualities and being unable to sustain without such meditation, āḻvār spoke being immersed in bhagavān’s qualities that he condemned those who are indifferent when hearing about [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s qualities and praised those who are emotionally charged when hearing about bhagavān’s qualities.
- *vaḷa vayal* … – Mercifully spoken by [nammāḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) who is the controller of [āḻvārtirunagari](http://azhwarthirunagari.koyil.org/) which has the greatness of crop-fields (countryside) and cities. taṇ – coolness. nērnda – spoken. The decad among the thousand pāsurams which were spoken by āḻvār being emotionally charged due to meditating upon [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s qualities.
- *aruvinai nīṟu seyyum* – The great sins which make one remain hard and indifferent when hearing about the qualities of bhagavān, will be burnt to ashes.

[āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) tiruvadigaḷē śaraṇam

## 3.6 Seyya tamarai

## 3.6.1. Seyya tamarai

*seyya tāmaraik kaṇṇanāy ulagēḻum uṇḍa avan kaṇḍīr vaiyam vānam manisar deyvam maṟṟum maṟṟum maṟṟum muṟṟumāyc ceyya sūḻ sudar jñānamāy veḷippattivai padaittān pinnum moykoḷ sōdiyōdāyinān oru mūvar āgiya mūrttiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

seyya – reddish (revealing the wealth/control of bhagavān due to his being greater than all); tāmarai – like a lotus; kaṇṇanāy – having beautiful eyes; ulagēḻum – all worlds; uṇḍa – drew them inside him; avan kaṇḍīr – he is; oru – distinguished; mūvar āgiya – having the three forms of brahmā, viṣṇu and Siva; vaiyam – earth; vānam – upper regions; manisar – humans; deyvam – celestial beings; maṟṟum – animals; maṟṟum – plants; maṟṟum – five great elements \[earth, water, fire, air, ether\]; muṟṟum – mahat etc (which are primary elements of creation); āy – being the raw material to create \[them\]; seyya – (since amōgha (unerring)) being honest; sūḻ – to surround (all created objects); sudar – radiant; jñānamāy – being embodiment of knowledge in the form of sankalpam (divine will/vow); veḷip pattu – appearing with inclination to create; ivai – all these aforementioned objects; padaittān – (being the nimitta (instrumental cause)) created; pinnum – further; moy koḷ – abundant; sōdiyōdu – with divine radiance; āyinān – remained with

**Перевод:**

**emperumān has lotus-like reddish beautiful eyes; at the time of deluge he drew all worlds inside him. After the deluge at the time of re-creating, he, with distinguished three forms of brahmā, viṣṇu and Siva, with himself as raw material, created earth and the upper regions, as well as residents of such places such as humans, celestial beings, animals and plants, five great elements \[earth, water, fire, air, ether\] and mahat etc (which are primary elements of creation). Being honest, he surrounded \[permeated\] all created objects; being embodiment of radiant knowledge in the form of sankalpam, appearing with inclination to create all these aforementioned objects, he created them. Further, he remained with abundant divine radiance.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In first pāsuram – Looking at emperumān who is having the qualities of being the creator etc of universe, highlighting his puṇḍarīkākśatvam (having lotus eyes) etc, explains the nature of the personality who is to be surrendered.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*In first pāsuram – āḻvār says apyaya (deluge) followed by sruśti (creation) is under bhagavān‘s control.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. Is he not talking about saulabhyam (simplicity)? Why is he talking about paratvam (supremacy)? – When the supreme lord who is greater than everyone, minimizes his stature \[voluntarily\], it counts as a \[auspicious\] quality. If a simpleton is in an inferior position, it is natural \[there is nothing great about it\].*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. seyya tāmaraik kaṇṇanāy ulagēḻum uṇḍa avan kaṇḍīr vaiyam vānam manisar deyvam maṟṟum maṟṟum maṟṟum muṟṟumāyc ceyya sūḻ sudar jñānamāy veḷippattivai padaittān pinnum moykoḷ sōdiyōdāyinān oru mūvar āgiya mūrttiyē*

- *seyya tāmaraik kaṇṇanāy* – As said in śruti (vēdam) and smriti – cāndōjña upaniśat 1.6 “*tasya yatā kapyāsam puṇḍarīkam ēvamakśiṇī*” (The two divine eyes of śrīman nārāyaṇan who is parabrahamam, resemble a lotus flower that was blossomed by morning sun’s rays) and śrī viṣṇu darmam 22 “*yajñēśō yajñapuruśa: puṇḍarīkākśa samgita:*” (being the lord of sacrifices, being yajña personified, having the name of puṇḍarīkākśa), one who is having divine eyes which resemble fresh lotus flower which just blossomed.
- *ulagēḻum* … – Like the lotus eyes for beauty \[which is distinct and special\], praḷaya āpatsakatvam (protecting during deluge) is \[the highlight\] in \[his\] qualities.
- *vaiyam* … – vaiyam – bhūmi (earth); vānam – higher planets. manisar – residents of earth. deyvam – residents of higher planets. maṟṟum – animals and plants. Second maṟṟum – the five great elements which are the initial phase of variegated forms \[such as humans, celestial beings, animals, plants\]. Third maṟṟum – mahat (the great) which is the initial phase of five great elements. muṟṟum – all the aforementioned objects. To say “one who appeared as embodiment of radiant knowledge to create everything”. Alternatively – As said in tiruvāimoḻi 8.10.7 “*tanimāppugaḻē enjñānṟum niṟkumpadiyāyt tāntōnṟi*” (appearing himself as brahmā, with his glories standing firm forever showcased in vēdāntam) and in taittiriya upaniśat “*bahu syām*” (let me become many), to create everything, he appeared as them and created them. In this alternative point of view, veḷippattu means he appeared with inclination to create.
- *seyya* – seyya (sevvai) for jñānam is being effortless. Alternatively – sevvai means as said in taittiriya nārāyaṇa upaniśat “*dātā yatā pūrvamakalpayat*” (brahmā \[with [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) as antaryāmi\] created everything as it were before), honestly creating all creatures based on their previous karma.
- *sūḻ* – pervading all the objects that are created.
- *sudar* – Well expanded as stated in [tiruvāimoḻi 3.1.9](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/07/thiruvaimozhi-3-1-9-mazhungadha/) “*maḻungāda jñānam*” (unfailing knowledge).
- *jñānamāy* – one who is having such knowledge in the form of sankalpam (vow/will).
- *veḷippattu ivai* – These which are revealed from pramāṇam (authentic source).

With this, [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s jagat kāraṇatvam (being the creator/cause of universe) is explained. Further, his being together with nitya vibhūti (spiritual realm) is explained.

- *pinnum* … – Beyond being together with leelā vibhūti (material realm), as said in mahābhāratam āraṇya parvam “*atyarkānaladīptam tat stānam*” (śrīman nārāyaṇan’s divine abode parampadam is many thousands of times more radiant than the sun and moon), this explains [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s abundantly radiant presence with nitya vibhūti.
- *moy koḷ sōdi* – Also explained as one who is having auspicious qualities such as tējas (radiance). tējas is a sample for all of his qualities. Why are his qualities spoken about now? That is because, one who is abundant with auspicious qualities, is to be accepted as refuge.
- *oru mūvarāgiya mūrttiyē* – [sarvēśvaran](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) who is creating/annihilating by being the antarātmā (in-dwelling super soul) of the bodies and souls of brahmā and rudra, and performing the sustenance himself. The word “*mūrti*” denotes supremacy. Alternatively, mūvar (trio) indicates brahmā, rudra and indra.

This pāsuram should be read as “The supreme lord with abundant radiance and who became the trio – further – appearing as everything such as earth, higher planets, humans, celestial beings, animals, planets, five great elements, primary matter – with fully pervaded radiant knowledge – reddish lotus-eyed lord who consumed all the worlds – created them – this being the case, surrender unto him”.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.6.2. Muvar agiya

*mūvar āgiya mūrttiyai mudal mūvarkku(m) mudalvan tannaic cāv(p)am uḷḷana nīkkuvānait tadam kadal kidandān tannait tēva tēvanait ten ilangai eri eḻac ceṟṟa villiyaip pāva nāsanaip pangayat tadam kaṇṇanaip paravuminō*

**Пословный перевод:**

mūvar āgiya mūrttiyai – As said in nārāyaṇa sūktam “sa brahmā sa śivassēndra:” (he \[bhagavān\] is brahmā, he is Siva, he is indra), bhagavān who is the śarīrī (ātmā) of brahmā, rudra and indra, \[yet\] they are seen as himself; mudal – lōka pradāna (prime personalities of the world); mūvarkku – (for those) three personalities; mudalvan tannai – being the causal entity; sāvam – curses (for them which are caused by hurting own guru etc); uḷḷana – that are present; nīkkuvānai – one who removes them; tadam – vast; kadal – in kśīrābdi (milk ocean); kidandān tannai – resting \[there\]; tēva tēvanai – appearing as the shelter for dēvas (celestial beings, who wanted to kill rāvaṇa); then ilangai – in lankā; eri – gruesome fire; eḻa – to rise; seṟṟa – destroyed the enemies; villiyai – the archer; pāva nāsanai – (in sētu, through boons and charity) one who destroys the sins; pangayat tadam kaṇṇanai – puṇḍarikākśa (lotus-eyed lord); paravumin – take shelter by praising him

**Перевод:**

**bhagavān is the śarīrī (ātmā) of brahmā, rudra and indra, \[yet\] they are seen as himself; he is the causal entity for those three primary personalities and the one who removes the curses that are present \[for them\]. Further to hear the complaints, he is resting in the vast milk ocean. Such emperumān appearing as the shelter for dēvas (celestial beings, who wanted to kill rāvaṇa), being an archer (śrī rāma), destroyed the enemies in lankā by gruesome rising fire. You take shelter of such lotus eyed lord who destroys the sins, by praising him.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*From second pāsuram onvards, emperumān‘s saulabhyam is spoken. In second pāsuram – though being sarvēśvaran, he appeared as the son of śrī daśarata cakravarti, as one among them \[the humans\] to be easily approached by them. āḻvār says “take shelter of such emperumān”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “Take shelter of kśīrārṇava sāyi (one who is resting in milk ocean) who is the source of all incarnations and is there to protect the created universe”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

- *pangayat tadam kaṇṇananai* – In addition to [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam, periyavāccān piḷḷai aptly quotes a pramāṇam from śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 53.8 where śrī rāma is glorified as lotus-eyed. “*rāma: kamalapatrākśa:*” (śrī rāma, having eyes that resemble lotus leaf).

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Second pāsuram. When asked “āḻvār , you highlighted jagat kāraṇatvam (being the cause of universe), puṇḍarikākśatvam (having lotus eyes) etc and asked us to take shelter of him; those are specific qualities that highlight his supremacy; how can we approach him in that case? \[if he is supreme, and we are very insignificant, how can we approach him?\]”, āḻvār replies “Such supreme lord has appeared as one among you, that is as cakravartit tirumagan (son of daśarata cakravarti). You can surrender there”. mūvar āgiya mūrttiyai mudal mūvarkku(m) mudalvan tannaic cāv(p)am uḷḷana nīkkuvānait tadam kadal kidandān tannait tēva tēvanait then ilangai eri eḻac ceṟṟa villiyaip pāva nāsanaip pangayat tadam kaṇṇanaip paravuminō*

- *mūvar āgiya mūrttiyai* – āḻvār is explaining further to clarify the sāmānadikaraṇyam \[To know more about sāmānadikaraṇyam, please see at the end of this link [https://grantams.koyil.org/readers-guide-english/](https://granthams.koyil.org/readers-guide-english/) \] which came up in the end of previous pāsuram \[in *mūvar āgiya mūrtti*\].
- *mudal* … – This sāmānādikaraṇyam is not something based on “all being one” \[as explained by māyāvādis\], but it is in the form of cause and effect. \[śrīman nārāyaṇan\] Being the cause for the three personalities including himself who is the cause of the universe. While he is the cause for brahmā and rudra, how can he be the cause for himself? Like he is the cause for brahmā and rudra, there is no one else apart from himself, who is the cause for him; this is explained in nārāyaṇa sūktam “*ātmēśvaram*” (he is the master of himself). Alternatively, including indra \[in place of viṣṇu\] and explains it as the causal entity for the primary personalities of universe namely brahmā, rudra and indra.
- *sāvamuḷḷana nīkkuvānai* – One who removes the curses as explained in stōtra ratnam 13 “*vēdāpahāra guru pādaka daitya pīdā*” (\[brahmā\] lost vēdams, \[rudra\] committed offense to his teacher \[who is brahmā\], \[indra\] being hounded by demoniac persons).
- *uḷḷana* – These are negligible considering the eagerness/ability of [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) to remove \[even greater\] sins.
- *tadam kadal …* – Proactively waiting in the ocean thinking “They cannot go search for me when they get into danger”.
- *tēva tēvanai* – Resting there being the refuge for dēvas starting with brahmā.
- *then ilangai eri eḻac ceṟṟa villiyai* – Explaining [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s action on hearing their cries. In lankā where agni (fire god) would not enter fearing rāvaṇa \[śrī rāma burnt the lankā with the same fire which was fearing rāvaṇa before\]. śri rāma whose archery skills are such that he has full control over the bow and arrow to do anything.
- *tēva tēvanait then ilangai eri eḻac ceṟṟa villiyai* – This can be taken as explaining his supremacy even in human form. ōr, it can be taken as saying “take shelter of the one who is glorified by nityasūris” \[dēva indicates nityasūri and dēva dēva indicates one who is the lord of nityasūris\].
- *pāva nāsanai* – On seeing the beauty of śrī rāma with the bow in his hand, sins of everyone will disappear. One who has the natural quality of eliminating the sins of the [cētana](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) in such state as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam uttara kāṇḍam 82.9 “*pāvanassarvalōkānām tvamēva raghunandana*” (Oh descendant of raghu dynasty! you eliminate the sins of everyone).
- *pangayat tadam kaṇṇananai* – Having such beautiful eyes, that even if were to add to our sins \[instead of removing them\], we cannot forget/leave him.
- *paravuminō* – Being captivated with the beauty of his eyes, praise him in a disorderly manner saying as in jitantē stōtram 1 “*jitantē puṇḍarīkāskha*” (Let there be victory for the lotus eyed lord).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.6.3. Paravi vanavar etta

*paravi vānavar ētta ninṟa paramanaip param sōdiyaik kuravai kōtta kuḻaganai maṇivaṇṇananik kudak kūttanai aravam ēṟi alai kadal amarum tuyil koṇḍa aṇṇalai iravu nan pagalum vidādenṟum ēttudal manam vaimminō*

**Пословный перевод:**

paravi – speaking (his collection of qualities) clearly; vānavar – dēvas (celestial beings); ētta – to be praised; ninṟa – stood (in front of them); paramanai – one who is having supremacy; param sōdiyai – (In his incarnations, as said in “dēva dēVēśa“) having unsurpassed radiance; kuravai kōtta – through the divine rāsa krīdā (romantic sport); kuḻaganai – one who is being subservient to be fully at the disposal \[of the covherd girls\]; maṇi – Very simple like a precious gem that can be secured in one’s cloth; vaṇṇanai – having the form; kudak kūttanai – being the one who danced with pots; aravam – on tiruvanantāḻvān (ādi śēśan); ēṟi – climbed; alai – (due to his presence, being agitated) and throwing the waves up in the air; kadal – in the ocean; amarum – fit in well (thinking about their protection); tuyil – sleep; koṇḍa – accepted; aṇṇalai – lord; nan – good (due to being used in praising); iravum pagalum – without knowing the difference between day and night; vidādu – without any break; enṟum – always; ēttudal – to engage in praising; manam – mind; vaimmin – keep

**Перевод:**

**emperumān who is having supremacy and unsurpassed radiance, stood in front of dēvas to be praised in speaking his glories by them (who are praying to eliminate the burden on earth). He climbed on ādi śēśan and slept there in a fitting manner thinking about the protection of all, in the milk ocean which is having agitated waves. Such emperumān  descends as kriṣṇa who remained subservient to the covherd girls by performing the divine rāsa krīdā with those girls who were captivated by his beauty, He is having a very simple form like a \[priceless\] precious gem which can be easily secured in one’s waist cloth. He also performed the dance with pots to be enjoyed by the whole town, not just the girls. You keep your mind on praising such lord, without break during day and night.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In third pāsuram – āḻvār says “Permanently take shelter of the divine son of śrī nandagōpa who is easier to approach than the divine son of daśarata”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār meditating upon the simplicity of kśīrārṇavaśāyi’s (one who is resting in milk ocean) kriṣṇāvatāram and the activities he carried out for his devotees where his simplicity is more than rāmāvatāram (incarnation as śrī rāma), says “Take shelter of him”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Third pāsuram. āḻvār says “Take shelter of kriṣṇāvatāram when compared to which, rāmāvatāram looks like paratvam (bhagavān’s form in paramapadam) \[i.e., kriṣṇāvatāram is way too easy to approach in comparison with rāmāvatāram”. paravi vānavar ētta ninṟa paramanaip param sōdiyaik kuravai kōtta kuḻaganai maṇivaṇṇananik kudak kūttanai aravam ēṟi alai kadal amarum tuyil koṇḍa aṇṇalai iravu nan pagalum vidādenṟum ēttudal manam vaimminō*

- *paravi vānavar ētta ninṟa paramanai* – Being glorified by nityasūris \[eternally free souls residing in parampadam\] without any specific order, due to which, stood lacking some one equal or greater to him. Alternative explanation – stood in such a manner that his glories cannot be comprehended even if glorified by nityasūris.
- *param sōdiyai* – Shining radiantly due to their glorification; As said in viṣṇu sūktam “*vipanyavō jāgruvāmsasamindatē*” (those who are wise and have the nature of praising \[him\] constantly, reach that supreme abode of viṣṇu), he considers their praising as his benefit and reflects that in his form. cāndōjña upaniśat “*param jyōtir upasampadya*” (attaining bhagavān who is known as param jyōti) – it is the svarūpam (nature) of śēśabhūta (servitor) to bring glories to śēśi (master).
- *kuravai kōtta kuḻaganai* – While interacting with the covherd girls, he would do so without any discrimination/restraint, as he would interact with nityasūris. kuḻagan – bhavyan – subservient.
- *maṇi vaṇṇanai* – one who has the tool to attract them (covherd girls). Having an invigorating blue-gem like form.
- *kudak kūttanai* – To satisfy those who missed out in the confidential rāsa krīdā, he presented his beauty fully to be enjoyed by everyone in the four-way junction \[like a street-performer performing in a crowded place to attract everyone\].
- *aravm ēṟi* – To relax from the performance of hectic dance, he went and lay down in milk ocean.
- *alai kadal* – They ocean becomes agitated seeing his presence.
- *amarum tuyil* – \[resting/contemplating deeply that\] even his divine consorts cannot awaken him.
- *aṇṇalai* – Having the strong feeling of supremacy due to anantaśāyitvam (lying down on the serpent bed is a unique identity of the supreme lord).
- *iravum* … – I am asking you to enjoy bhagavān in this material realm where time has controlling power, the same experience that is enjoyed in spiritual realm where time has no controlling power. Since it is time for praising [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying “*nal iravum, nal pagal*” (good night and good day).
- *enṟum ēttudal* – As said in viṣṇu sūktam “*vipanyava:*” (have the nature of praising him constantly).
- *manam vaimminō* – All you need to do is to place your mind/heart \[on him\]. You will naturally become immersed in his experience.  All you need to do is to set out to praise him. You would not even need to have some one instructing you on it subsequently \[it will become natural\].
- *manam vaimminō* – Pull back the mind from worldly pleasures and try to place it on him.

\[nampiḷḷai summarizes the whole pāsuram beautifully with a series of questions.\]

- \[*vānavar ētta ninṟa*\] I am asking you to glorify bhagavān who is glorified by nityasūris.
- \[*paramanai*\] I am asking you to glorify the supreme lord who is greater than all.
- \[*param sōdi*\] I am asking you to glorify the one who considers your praising as his benefit and reveals the same in his form.
- \[*kuravai kōtta kuḻaganai*\] I am asking you to glorify the one who descended to mingle with you expecting your non-rejection as the only criterion.
- \[*maṇi vaṇṇanai*\] I am asking you to glorify the one who has such divine beauty which will be pursued by whatever possible ways by everyone.
- \[*kudak kūttanai*\] I am asking you to glorify the one who is pridefully dancing due to having united with you.
- \[*aravam ēṟi alaikadal amarum tuyil aṇṇal*\] I am asking you to glorify the one who is lying on the serpent bed.
- \[*aṇṇal*\] I am asking you to glorify the lord of all.
- \[*iravum nan pagalum*\] Are you constrained by time limits?
- \[*manam*\] Are you lacking the tool \[don’t you have your own mind\]?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.6.4. Vaimmin nummanattu

*vaimmin num manattenṟu yān uraikkinṟa māyavan sīrmaiyai emmanōrgaḷ uraippaden adu niṟka nāḷ toṟum vānavar tammai āḷum avanum nānmuganum sadai mudi aṇṇalum semmaiyāl avan pāda pangayam sindittēttit tirivarē*

**Пословный перевод:**

num – your; manattu – in mind/heart; vaimmin – keep; enṟu – as; yān – I; uraikkinṟa – saying; māyavan – one who is having amazing qualities and activities; sīrmaiyai – great qualities such as excellent disposition; emmanōrgaḷ – like me (who are greatly attached to him); uraippadu – saying; en – what is surprising about it?; adu niṟka – that aside; vānavar tammai – celestial beings (who have their individual positions); āḷum avanum – indra who rules them; nānmuganum – brahmā (who creates, teaches etc); sadai mudi – due to his greatness in penance which is highlighted by his having matted hair; aṇṇalum – rudra, who is lord of this world; semmaiyāl – out of honesty (understanding the master/servitor relationship between bhagavān and themselves, after giving up their false pride); avan – his (i.e., bhagavān who is the master); pangayam – unsurpassed enjoyability; pādam – divine feet; nāḷ toṟum – daily/always; sindittu – meditating on; ētti – praising; tirivar – will do (as their routine)

**Перевод:**

**What is surprising in some one like me (who are greatly attached to him) saying “keep the great qualities such as excellent disposition of one who is having amazing qualities and activities in your mind/heart “? That aside; indra who rules the celestial beings, brahmā (who creates, teaches etc), rudra who is lord of this world due to his greatness in penance which is highlighted by his having matted hair, out of honesty are always meditating on and praising bhagavān’s divine feet which has unsurpassed enjoyability.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In fourth pāsuram – āḻvār speaks about emperumān‘s qualities (such as śeela (excellent disposition) etc) which makes him approachable for very prideful brahmā, īśāna (rudra) et al without hesitation.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. vaimmin num manattenṟu yān uraikkinṟa māyavan sīrmaiyai emmanōrgaḷ uraippaden adu niṟka nāḷ toṟum vānavar tammai āḷum avanum nānmuganum sadai mudi aṇṇalum semmaiyāl avan pāda pangayam sindittēttit tirivarē*

- *vaimmin* … – The śeelam (excellent disposition) of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is having amazing qualities and activities, and who is said by me as “Keep in your heart”. Alternatively – it is explaining the supremacy of emperumān which makes it easier as in “he is so great to be taken shelter by qualified personalities such as brahmā, rudra et al”.
- *emmanōrgaḷ uraippadu en* – What is the point of people like us speaking about it? Even if we spoke about it, others will simply disregard our words saying they were spoken due to great devotion \[instead of real glories\].
- *adu niṟka* – \[so\] leave that aside.
- *nāḷ toṟum* … – His excellent disposition is such that even qualified personalities such as brahmā, rudra et al, come to him as ananyaprayōjana (those who are exclusively serving [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) without any other expectation than such service) and accept his refuge. Alternatively – it is explaining the supremacy of emperumān which makes it easier as in “he is so great to be taken shelter by qualified personalities such as brahmā, rudra et al”. Further, it is to be read as “*nāḷ toṟum … sindittu ēttit tirivarē*“.
- *vānavar tammai āḷum avanum* – indra who counts his subordinate dēvas on Saturdays and Wednesdays, and who enquires their complaints etc.
- *nānmuganum* – caturmuka (four-headed) brahmā who is the creator of the 14 layers of the world.
- *sadai mudi aṇṇalum* – rudra, though having the form of a sādaka (practising devotee), considers himself to be the supreme.
- *semmaiyāl* … – Though they have ulterior motives in their heart, they would take shelter of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) like an ananyaprayōjana. Though their heart is impure with ulterior motives, they would pretend to be like those who are exclusively devoted to him – emperumān’s nature is such that he would even let them visit him, leave and roam around \[like pure devotees would do\]! semmai – sevvai – ārjavam – honesty. That is, as they meditate  upon his divine feet like ananyaprayōjana, they would praise him to reveal that those praises are a result of such meditation, and sustain them with that and would roam around \[singing his glories\] as said in [kaṇṇinuṇ ciṟut tāmbu 2](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/01/kanninun-chiru-thambu-2-navinal/) “*pādit tirivanē*” (I \[[madurakavi āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/madhurakavi-azhwar/)\] roam around singing [nammāḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s glories)

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.6.5. Tiriyum karru

*tiriyum kāṟṟōdagal visumbu tiṇinda maṇ kidanda kadal eriyum tīyōdiru sudar deyvam maṟṟum maṟṟum muṟṟumāyk kariya mēniyan seyya tāmaraik kaṇṇan kaṇṇan viṇṇōr iṟai suriyum pal karum kunji engaḷ sudar mudi aṇṇal tōṟṟamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kariya – blackish; mēniyan – having form; seyya – (contrasting with that) reddish; tāmarai – lotus like; kaṇṇan – having eyes; viṇṇōr – eternally enjoyable for nityasūris (eternally free residents of paramapadam); iṟai – having supremacy; suriyum – curly; pal – many, wavy; karum – blackish; kunji – hairs; engaḷ – one who accepts our service; sudar – having radiance; mudi – one who is having divine crown; aṇṇal – being the master/lord; kaṇṇan – kriṣṇa’s; tōṟṟam – appearance; tiriyum – constantly moving; kāṟṟōdu – with vāyu (air); agal – vast; visumbu – ākāśam (ether/space); tiṇinda – hard; maṇ – bhūmi (earth); kidanda – staying, without breaching the shore; kadal – ocean; eriyum – with rising flames; tīyōdu – with agni (fire); iru sudar – starting with candra (moon) and āditya (sun); deyvam – groups of dēvatās (celestial beings); maṟṟum – and manuśyas (human beings); maṟṟum – and tiryak (animals) muṟṟumāy – and will be with stāvara (plants)

**Перевод:**

**kriṣṇa is the one with blackish form and with reddish lotus like eyes; is having the supremacy to be eternally enjoyable for nityasūris; is having curly, many wavy blackish hairs; who is having divine radiant crown which makes him accept our service. Such kriṣṇa’s appearance is together with the five great elements (which are part of samaśti śruśti) viz vāyu (air) which is constantly moving, vast ākāśam (ether/space), hard bhūmi (earth), ocean which is staying without breaching the shore and agni (fire) with rising flames, and (which are part of vyaśti śruśti) groups of dēvatās (celestial beings) starting with candra (moon) and āditya (sun), manuśyas (human beings), tiryak (animals)  and stāvara (plants).**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In fifth pāsuram – āḻvār says “Since emperumān cannot survive even without one of his wealth, I am seeing emperumān with all his wealth always”. Also explained as, emperumān appearing with his wealth etc in his incarnations as said in śrī bhagavat gītā 4.6 “bhūtānām īśvarō’pi san” (I am the lord of all beings).*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Fifth pāsuram. Explained as “due to his vātsalyam (motherly affection) he is always present with all his wealth and appears \[in manifested form\] like a peacock with spread out feathers. Also explained as, emperumān appearing with his wealth etc in his incarnations as said in śrī bhagavat gītā 4.6 “bhūtānām īśvarō’pi san” (I am the lord of all beings). tiriyum kāṟṟōdagal visumbu tiṇinda maṇ kidanda kadal eriyum tīyōdiru sudar deyvam maṟṟum maṟṟum muṟṟumāyk kariya mēniyan seyya tāmaraik kaṇṇan kaṇṇan viṇṇōr iṟai suriyum pal karum kunji engaḷ sudar mudi aṇṇal tōṟṟamē*

- *tiriryum* … – air which is constantly on the move, ether which provides space for all other entities, earth which is hard by nature, ocean which is not breaching the shores due to bhagavān’s order, fire which rises up in flames by nature, radiant moon and sun.
- *deyvam* … – Celestial beings who are present to give refuge to those who are other than themselves and fulfil their desires. Humans who take shelter of such celestial beings. Animals. Plants.
- *muṟṟum āy* – His appearance is explained to be with all of these. āy – being the ātmā of all of these. From this, bhagavān’s sustenance of the universe is explained.

Subsequently, his presence with distinguished form is explained.

- *kariya mēniyan* – One who is having divine invigorating form which eliminates the tāpa trayam (three types of distresses) of those who see him.
- *seyya tāmaraik kaṇṇan* – One who is having beautiful eyes which reveals his vātsalyam (motherly affection).
- *kaṇṇan* – one who is subservient towards his devotees.
- *viṇṇōr iṟai* – even in such form as kriṣṇa, he is having supremacy in human form, which makes the nityasūris come and glorify him.
- *suriyum* … – One who is having hairs which are curly, wavy, blackish which makes the one who sees him feel the coolness.
- *engaḷ sudar mudi aṇṇal tōṟṟamē* – tōṟṟam – prakāśam (glow), avatāram (appearance). [sarvēśvaran](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s appearance having divine radiant crown which reveals his supremacy and is enjoyable by ananyaprayōjanar (those who are exclusively devoted to [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) without any expectation in return).
