## 3.6.6. Torrak kedu

*tōṟṟak kēdavai illavan udaiyān avan oru mūrttiyāyc cīṟṟattōdaruḷ peṟṟavan adik kīḻp puga ninṟa sengaṇmāl nāṟṟat tōṟṟac cuvai oli uṟal āgi ninṟa em vānavar ēṟṟaiyē anṟi maṟṟoruvarai yān ilēn eḻumaikkumē*

**Пословный перевод:**

avai – as in the other entities; tōṟṟak kēdu – birth and demise; illavan – being the one who is not having; udaiyān – being the one who is having (appearance and disappearance during specific times as required for his devotees); avan – one who is well established in pramāṇams (authentic scriptures); oru – distinguished (which is not seen in this world); mūrttiyāy – in the form of narasimha; sīṟṟāttōdu – with anger (for hiraṇya kaśyap); aruḷ peṟṟavan – prahlāda who received his blessing; adik kīḻ – under his divine feet; puga – to take shelter; ninṟa – stood (in an easily approachable manner for prahlāda); sem kaṇ – reddish eyes; māl – having vātsalyam (motherly affection); nāṟṟat tōṟṟac cuvai oli uṟal āgi ninṟa – being the controller of all entities which have ganda (fragrance), rūpa (form), rasa (taste), śabda (sound) and sparśa (touch sensation); em vānavar ēṟṟaiyē anṟi – other than the one who is enjoyable for us in the same way he is enjoyed by the nityasūris; yān – I; eḻumaikkum – forever; maṟṟu oruvarai – any other person; ilēn – won’t have (as the goal)

**Перевод:**

**emperumān is the one who is having (appearance and disappearance during specific times as required for his devotees) and is not having birth and demise as in all other entities; he is well established in pramāṇams (authentic scriptures); such emperumān stood (in an easily approachable manner for prahlāda) in the distinguished form of narasimha with reddish eyes, motherly affection \[towards prahlāda\] and anger (for hiraṇya kaśyap) to prahlāda who was blessed by him and was looking to take shelter under his lotus feet. Other than the emperumān who is the controller of all entities which have ganda (fragrance), rūpa (form), rasa (taste), śabda (sound) and sparśa (touch sensation), who is enjoyable for us in the same way he is enjoyed by the nityasūris, I won’t forever have any other person \[as my goal\].**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In sixth pāsuram – āḻvār becomes delighted saying “narasimha is enjoyable  for me in all manner like he is enjoyed by nityasūris \[eternally free souls of paramapadam\]; I will not have any one other than him as my dāraka (that which sustains) etc forever”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “I will not have any one other than the one \[narasimha\] who has no hesitance/lethargy in helping his devotees, as my goal at all times and in all manner”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*nampiḷḷai says “Instead of being like samsāris, who wait for advice from others, I will be like nityasūris who do not wait for others’ advice \[to serve/enjoy emperumān\], will not consider any one other than narasimha \[as done by nityasūris\] as my dāraka etc., forever”. tōṟṟak kēdavai illavan udaiyān avan oru mūrttiyāyc cīṟṟattōdaruḷ peṟṟavan adik kīḻp puga ninṟa sengaṇmāl nāṟṟat tōṟṟac cuvai oli uṟal āgi ninṟa em vānavar ēṟṟaiyē anṟi maṟṟoruvarai yān ilēn eḻumaikkumē*

- *tōṟṟak kēdu avai illavan* – One who does not have utpatti (birth), vināśam (demise). This is a sample for śadbhāva vikāram (six types of changes).
- *udaiyān* – One who has all those entities which undergo birth and demise, at his disposal. nirūpādika śēśi (the unconditional \[supreme\] lord \[of everyone\]).
- *avan oru mūrttiyāy* – One who does not have birth which is triggered based on karma (virtues/vices), assuming distinguished forms (incarnations) for the purpose of his devotees.
- *oru mūrtti* – unparallelled, \[and due to being unparallelled\] very distinguished  narasimha \[with human body and lion head\]. īsn’t he glorified as in nānmugan tiruvantādi 22 “*aḻagiyān tānē ari uruvan tānē*” (He is the most beautiful one, he is the lion-headed one).
- *sīṟṟattōdu aruḷ peṟṟavan* – Having anger and mercy at the same time is even more amazing than a unique form with a mixture of naratvam (being a human) and simhatvam (being a lion).
- *sīṟṟām* … – While he is manifesting anger towards hiraṇya, he stood so that śrī prahlādāḻvān who is the target of his mercy can take shelter of his divine feet. It means prahlāda received bhagavān’s mercy, while bhagavān was angry. Like hiraṇya was the target of bhagavān’s hatred, prahlāda was the target of his mercy. It is also explained as “*avan oru mūrttiyāyc cīṟṟattodu*” ([emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) in a distinguished form, with anger).
- *adik kīḻp puga ninṟa sem kaṇ māl* – When [emperumānār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/emperumanar/) was questioned by some “While emperumān was angry towards hiraṇya, how was he approachable for śrī prahlādāḻvān?”, he mercifully explained “though a lioness would be angry towards an elephant, it will still be nursing its cubs at the same time \[similarly [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) showing anger and mercy at the same time towards different individuals\]”. He also explained “If [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) out of motherly affection towards his devotees, became angry towards the enemies of his devotees, would he show that anger towards his devotees themselves?”.
- *sem kaṇ māl* – \[reddish eyes\] is due to both reasons \[anger and mercy\]. It will be reddish due to anger towards hiraṇya and also due to motherly affection towards śrī prahlādāḻvān.
- *māl* – \[two meanings – greatness, affection\] Explaining the supremacy of [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) which makes him unapproachable for hiraṇya as said in narasimha mantram “… *mahāviṣṇum* …” (The supreme lord – mahāviṣṇu); it also explains his mad affection towards śrī prahlādaḻvān who can easily approach him.
- *nāṟṟam* … – nāṟṟam – gandam (fragrance). tōṟṟam – rūpam (form). suvai – rasam (taste). oli – śabdam (sound). uṟal – sparśam (touch).
- *āgi ninṟa* – He became all these śabdam etc, for me.

Like for whom?

- *em vānavar* … – Like he is every enjoyable aspect for nityasūris.
- *maṟṟu* … – I will not have any one else as the goal.

How many baths (days) will this last?

- *eḻumaikkumē* – Forever. When he behaves with me as he would behave with nityasūris, would I consider anything else as enjoyable? Only if they consider some one other than him as enjoyable, I would do the same.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.6.7. Elumaikkum

*eḻumaikkum enadāvikkinnamudattinai enadāruyir keḻumiya kadirc cōdiyai maṇivaṇṇanaik kudak kūttanai viḻumiya amarar munivar viḻungum kannal kaniyinait toḻumin tūya manattarāy iṟaiyum nillā tuyarangaḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

eḻumaikkum – in all situations; enadu āvikku – for my ātmā; in amudattinai – being perfectly enjoyable; enadu Ar uyir – being fully united in my true nature; keḻumiya kadir – shining radiantly due to such union; sōdiyai – having radiance; maṇivaṇṇanaik kudak kūttanai – having physical beauty and activities (to unite with me); viḻumiya – best; amarar – the immortal personalities of śrīvaikuṇṭam; munivarum – and the sages (of śrīvaikuṇṭam) as said in tiruvāimoḻi 10.9.9 “vaikundattamarum munivarm”; viḻungum – consuming \[enjoying\]; kannal kaniyinai – one who is perfectly sweet like a fruit mixed with sugar; tūya manattarāy – being ananyaprayōjana (exclusively devoted without any ulterior motives, instead of keeping their mind in something other than bhagavān); toḻumin – you surrender unto him; tuyarangaḷ – difficulties (that block such blissful experience); iṟaiyum – even a little bit; nillā – will not remain

**Перевод:**

**You surrender being ananyaprayōjana (exclusively devoted without any ulterior motives, instead of keeping their mind in other than bhagavān) unto emperumān who is perfectly enjoyable at all times for my ātmā, who is fully united in my true nature and shining radiantly due to such union, who is having radiance, physical beauty and activities (to unite with me), one who is consumed (enjoyed) by the best immortal personalities and sages of śrīvaikuṇṭam, who is perfectly sweet like a fruit mixed with sugar. Even a little bit of your difficulties (that block such blissful experience) will not remain.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In seventh pāsuram – āḻvār says “After emperumān manifesting simplicity towards his devotees, you give up the doubts in difficulty in approaching him, and take shelter of him. Your sorrows will be eliminated without a trace”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “You take shelter of such easily approachable emperumān who is perfectly enjoyable”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. eḻumaikkum enadāvikkinnamudattinai enadāruyir keḻumiya kadirc cōdiyai maṇivaṇṇanaik kudak kūttanai viḻumiya amarar munivar viḻungum kannal kaniyinait toḻumin tūya manattarāy iṟaiyum nillā tuyarangaḷē*

- *eḻumaikkum enadu āvikku in amudattinai* – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who became enjoyable to my heart which was eternally immersed in worldly pleasures without even a trace of attachment towards him. eḻumai means count of seven \[seven lives, seven yugas etc\]. Since anything big is explained using the count of seven, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) used the word eḻumaikkum to indicate a very long period of time.
- *enadu Ar uyir* … – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who became radiant by uniting with my [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) which suffered in this material realm since time immemorial. āḻvār considered his approach towards him will cause blemish to [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/); but emperumān became more radiant as he approached āḻvār.
- *maṇivaṇṇanai* … – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is having the tools \[physical beauty etc\] to capture the [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)s ([āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) here) without even them knowing about his tricks. One who has physical beauty and activities that steal the heart. *vaṇṇam* – color. It can also be explained as emperumān presenting himself to be controlled and enjoyed like one will do so with a precious blue stone.
- *viḻumiya amarar* … – Perfectly enjoyable like sugar and fruit for the best amarar (immortal – eternally free souls) and munivar (sages) of paramapadam, who are unlike these dēvas \[of this material realm\] who are created. He is explained in cāndōjña upaniśat as “*sarvagandas sarvarasa:*” (source of all fragrance and all taste).
- *kannal kaniyinait toḻumin* – Like “*māngani*” (mango fruit), “*kannal kani*” means sugar riped into becoming a fruit. This is the medicine I am giving you \[to be cured of the disease of existence in material realm\]; am I not falling at your feet to drink \[sweet\] milk?
- *tūya manattarāy* – Instead of having doubts \[in the mind\] such as “Is he difficult to approach? or easy to approach? Is he difficult to understand? or easy to understand? Would I reach him?”, surrender unto him keeping him as the goal.
- *iṟaiyum nillā tuyarangaḷē* – The great sins which cause such doubts will be eradicated along with their traces. Also explained as – the worldly sorrows will be eliminated with their traces.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.6.8. Tuyarame taru

*tuyarmē taru tunba inba vinaigaḷāy avai allanāy uyara ninṟadōr sōdiyāy ulagēḻum uṇḍumiḻndān tannai ayara vāngum naman tamarkku aru nanjinai accudan tannait tayaradaṟku magan tannai anṟi maṟṟilēn tanjam āgavē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tuyaramē taru – that which will give (exclusive distress); tunbam – sorrows; inbam – cause for happiness (which is also exclusive distress since it is attained by difficult process, the resulting happiness is missed with distress, is ultimately ending with distress); vinaigaḷāy – being the controller of karmas in the form of puṇya (virtue) and pāpa (vice); avai – by them; allanāy – not being bound; uyara – having greatness (as said in cāndōjña upaniśat “viśvata: pruśtēśu sarvata: pruśtēśu” (paramapadam which is greater than vyaśti sruśti and samaśti sruśti)); ninṟadu ōr – eternal, unparalleled; sōdiyāy – having a divine body which is filled with radiance; ulagu ēḻum – when all the worlds (which are bound by karma) are endangered during deluge; uṇḍu – consuming them; umiḻndān tannai – one who \[subsequently\] lets them out and protects them; ayara – for the bewilderment; vāngum – take away the life; naman tamarkku – for the servitors of yama; aru – difficult to rescue; nanjinai – being poison; accudan tannai – one who is having the nature of not abandoning his devotees; tayaradaṟku magan tannai – śrī rāma, the son of daśarata cakravarti; anṟi – other than him; maṟṟu – any one, even another form of bhagavān; tanjamāga ilēn – will not have as my refuge

**Перевод:**

**emperumān is the controller of karmas in the form of puṇya (virtue) and pāpa (vice) which will give (exclusive distress) out of happiness (which is also exclusive distress since it is attained by difficult process, the resulting happiness is missed with distress, is ultimately ending with distress) and sorrow; \[yet\] he is not bound by them \[karmas\]; he is having a divine body which is filled with radiance, is eternal, unparalleled and  having greatness; when all the worlds (which are bound by karma) are endangered during deluge, he consumes them and \[subsequently\] lets them out and protects them; he is the poison which is difficult to rescue for the servitors of yama who take away the life for the bewilderment \[of ātmās\] and hence having the nature of not abandoning his devotees; other than such śrī rāma, who appeared as the son of daśarati cakravarti, I will not have any one, even another form of bhagavān, as my refuge. tanjam – being a companion when one is in danger.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In eighth pāsuram – āḻvār explains his own philosophy \[conviction\] to help others \[samsāris (materialistic persons)\] know about it and develop taste in it saying “I will not consider any one other than \[śrī rāma, \] the son of daśarata cakravarti as my āpaddanam (wealth during hard times)”*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “there is no refuge other than the son of daśarata cakravarti who never abandons his devotees”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. tuyarmē taru tunba inba vinaigaḷāy avai allanāy uyara ninṟadōr sōdiyāy ulagēḻum uṇḍumiḻndān tannai ayara vāngum naman tamarkku aru nanjinai accudan tannait tayaradaṟku magan tannai anṟi maṟṟilēn tanjam āgavē*

- *tuyaram* … – Being the controller of karmas in the form of puṇya/pāpa which lead to exclusive suffering. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s thinking is that both pāpa and puṇya lead to suffering only; since both are hurdles for one’s servitude towards [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/), both have “leading to bondage” in common; it is said in muṇḍaka upaniśat “… *puṇya pāpē vidūya* …” (one sheds both puṇya and pāpa and then attains liberation).
- *avai allanāy* – akarma vaśya (one who is not bound by karma). As said in rig vēdam “*dvā suparṇā sayujā sakhāyā samānam vrukśam pariśasvajātē \| tayōranya: pippalam svādvatti anaśnannanyō abicākaśīti \|\|*” (There are two related (servant and master) birds ([jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) and [paramātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)) residing in a tree (body). One bird ([jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)) enjoys the fruits of its actions (karma) and the other one (paramātmā) being detached is radiantly witnessing that), not being bound by these karma and shining due to having control over them.
- *uyara* … – As said in yajur vēdam 2.2.12 “… *kśayantamasya rajasa:parākē*” (residing in the supreme realm of paramapadam which is beyond this material realm which is filled with rajas (passion)) and puruśa sūktam “*tamsa: parastāt*” (paramātmā is superior to material nature), the same emperumān who cannot be reached by the residents of the material realm, is present in this material realm itself, with a divine form which has infinite radiance – this is explained here. Also explained as, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) having the eternal unparalleled fully radiant spiritual abode (paramapadam) which is having greatness (as said in cāndōjña upaniśat “*viśvata: pruśtēśu sarvata: pruśtēśu*” (paramapadam which is greater than vyaśti sruśti and samaśti sruśti)).
- *ulagu* … – Though he is complete, when a small portion of his wealth, that is samsāram (material realm) is consumed by deluge, he would descend here, protect the worlds by placing them in his stomach and would subsequently let them out thinking “what would they have gone through inside my stomach,  not having seen the outside?”; as those who cross through a stretch of land which is known for robbery would swallow their expensive properties \[gold, precious stones etc\] and would spit them out when they reach safety, emperumān too consumes and spits out the worlds.
- *ayara* – For those who have taken shelter of his divine feet, when the servitors of yama try to grab them \[at the time of their death\] with such force which will bewilder the person, he is the poison that will ensure that they \[devotees\] cannot be taken away by them \[servitors of yama\].
- *accudan tannai* – acyuta – one who does not abandon those who are surrendered unto him, to be taken away by the servitors of yama. This is explained in nānmugan tiruvantādi 88 “*uyirkoṇḍu udal oḻiya ōdumpōdu ōdi ayavenṟa tīrppān*”  (when the servitors of yama grab the [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) leaving the body and start running, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) will himself chase them and eliminate all the sufferings of the ātmā).

Where did we see such act from emperumān?

- *tayaradaṟku magan tannai* – When śrī rāma was ruling the kingdom, a brāhmaṇa’s son dies unexpectedly at a very young age, he brought him back by the sword \[śampūka, being śūdra was performing penance which he was not supposed to do, which caused the tragedy. śrī rāma killed śampūka and thereby gave life the brāhmaṇa’s son\]; after killing rāvaṇa, śrī rāma was checking his army and found out some leaders \[monkey soldiers etc\] were missing/dead, he summoned indra, asked him for a boon to recover those soldiers and brought them along to ayōdyā; when a riśiputra (son of a sage) died accidentally at a young age, he (kriṣṇa) recovered him too \[Here based on darmi aikyam – same [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) in the form of śrī rāma and kriṣṇa, this incident of śāndīpani riśi is also highlighted\]. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) said “*tayaradaṟku magan*” (being a fully obedient son of daśarata) instead of “*tayaradan magan*” (son of daśarata) \[subtle grammatical difference\], to emphasise how subservient śrī rāma was towards his father. śrī rāma manifested the same subservience both when daśarata said out of pride “You will be the crown prince” from tomorrow and when he said “No, I am not crowning you, You have to go to forest” being overwhelmed with affection for his wife kaikēyi.
- *anṟi maṟṟu ilēn tanjam āgavē* – When [parāśara bhattar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/parasara-bhattar/) was explaining this, [nanjīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nanjiyar/) said “[āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s nature is such that, he would say the same thing \[tiruviruttam 99 – *jñānappirān allāl illai nān kaṇḍa nalladuvē* (there is nothing better than varāhap perumāḷ in what I have seen), [tiruvāimoḻi 3.6.6](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/09/thiruvaimozhi-3-6-6-thorrak-kedu/) “*tōṟṟak kēdu … maṟṟoruvari yān ilēn eḻumaikkumē*” (I will not consider anyone as the goal other than my supreme lord in the form of narasimha), tiruvāimoḻi 9.1.10 “*kaṇṇan allāl illai kaṇḍīr śaraṇ*” (there is no refuge other than kriṣṇa)\] wherever \[whichever [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)\] he surrenders to” and [bhattar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/parasara-bhattar/) mercifully explained “He surrenders to other forms of emperumān considering them to be purifying, but he considers śrī rāma as the most enjoyable lord”; But is śrī rāma also not glorified as the one who gives purity as in śrī rāmāyaṇam uttara kāṇḍam 82.9 “*pāvanas sarvalōkānām tvamēva*” (agastya says “śrī rāma! you are the one who removes the sins of every one”)? agastya is also similar to [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/). Just like āḻvār considers no one other than śrī rāma as enjoyable, agastya considers no one other than śrī rāma as purifying. siṟiyāttān wanting to hear [bhattar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/parasara-bhattar/)‘s partiality towards śrī rāma, asked “Though śrī rāma is glorified in all aspects, he does not have the simplicity of kriṣṇa who went as a messenger for pāṇḍavas hanging their message on his neck \[as a necklace, as messengers would normally do those days\]” and bhattar replied “Well! śrī rāma would not have refused to go as a messenger; but since he was the emperor of the great ikśvāku dynasty, no one asked him to go as a messenger”. Only to satisfy such desire which was unfulfilled in rāmāvatāram, he appeared as kriṣṇa and went as a messenger”; this is explained in periya tirumoḻi 2.2.3 “*avanē pinnōr tūdu ādi mannarkkāgip perunilattār innār tūdan ena ninṟan*” (that same śrī rāma, subsequently became \[kriṣṇa\] the messenger of yudiśtra and stood to be said by the residents of the big world ‘he is the messenger of pāṇḍavas’). \[Should he appear as kriṣṇa to specifically fulfill this desire?\] Having decided to enjoy pāratantriya rasam (the feeling of being subservient), that one aspect will be unfulfilled \[thus he appeared to satisfy that desire\].

[emperumānār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/emperumanar/) had veṇṇeykkādum piḷḷai (nardana kriṣṇa – kriṣṇa who would dance for butter) in his tiruvārādanam (personal worship); one day, a śrīvaiṣṇava brought a deity of cakravartit tirumagan (śrī rāma) and presented the same to emperumānār; seeing him, emperumānār said “one who did not demand ‘*māmēkam śaraṇam vraja*‘ (surrender unto me only), has arrived). \[Generally ābhimukhyam \[being friendly\] in the form of allowing [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) to protect/rescue us, is explained as prapatti.\] When we look at *ābhimukhyam* as the cause \[for emperumān’s protection\], for the cētana \[who is bound in this material realm\], even such ābhimukhyam is as difficult as parama bhakti to perform – so saying “there is nothing more than ābhimukhyam which is needed in him” is due to the simplicity \[magnanimity\] of śaraṇyan (emperumān who is giving shelter); but if we look at what is required, it is explained as “*māhaviśvāsa pūrvakam*” (with complete faith). \[Would we need such faith as a prerequisite on our side?\] When some one goes on a sea voyage, he has faith in the ship and carries food, water etc in the hope of managing with that for six months; for those who surrender to [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/), would they at least not need such faith?”.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.6.9. Tanjam agiya

*tanjam āgiya tandai tāyodu tānumāy avai allanāy enjalil amarar kula mudal mūvar tam uḷḷum ādiyai anji nīr ulagattuḷḷīrgaḷ avan ivan enṟu kūḻēnmin nenjināl ninaippān yavan avan āgum nīḷ kdal vaṇṇanē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tanjam āgiya – being the refuge (unlike biological mother and father who may abandon their child in specific situations, emperumān who will never abandon); tandai tāyodu – (due to seeking for the well-being and to fulfil the desires) being father and mother, with them; tānum āy – being self (who will always seek out the well-being of oneself); avai allan āy – not just that, being all types of relation; enjal il – those who have no limit in their experience; amarar kula mudal – being the cause for the existence of nityasūris; mūvar tam uḷḷum – in the trio of primary deities namely brahmā et al; ādiyai – to hold on to the principal one; ulagattu uḷḷīrgaḷ – worldly people; nīr – you; anji – (looking at his supremacy) being afraid; avan – he (who is having unlimited greatness \[such bhagavān in paramapadam\]); ivan – him (who assumed the \[arcā/deity\] form which we desired); enṟu – thinking of superiority and inferiority \[of these forms\]; kūḻēnmin – instead of doubting (if he is to be surrendered to or not?); nenjināl – with the heart; ninaippān – thought about and joyfully consecrated; yavan – that emperumān; avan – him; kadal – like ocean; nīḷ – vast/boundless; vaṇṇan – sarvēśvaran, having such nature; āgum – he is

**Перевод:**

**emperumān is the refuge, father and mother, along with them, the self and not just that, he is all types of relation; he is the cause for the existence of nityasūris who have no limit in their experience and is the principal one in the trio of primary deities namely brahmā et al; Oh worldly people! instead of doubting if he (who is the supreme person is the same in deity form) is to be surrendered unto or not due to considering them \[those forms\] superior \[bhagavān in paramapadam\] and inferior \[bhagavān in deity form\], \[know that\] he who is thought about and joyfully consecrated \[in deity form\] is the same sarvēśvaran who has ocean-like vast nature.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In ninth pāsuram – when asked “For us, emperumān‘s presence in śrīvaikuṇṭam is incomprehensible. We were not favoured by him when he descended with utmost simplicity in many incarnations. How will we approach him?”, āḻvār says “You approach him requesting him to be present in a form you desire \[arcā (deity) form\]; since it is too easy for the devotees to approach, he likes such form as much as he likes his spiritual divine form”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “Instead of shying away from emperumān thinking ‘paratvam (supremacy) and incarnations are unreachable for us’, you take shelter of arcāvatāra emperumān who is present to be easily approached by those are after the time of incarnations and who is all types of relationships for you”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. This pāsuram is the main one for this decad. tanjam āgiya tandai tāyodu tānumāy avai allanāy enjalil amarar kula mudal mūvar tam uḷḷum ādiyai anji nīr ulagattuḷḷīrgaḷ avan ivan enṟu kūḻēnmin nenjināl ninaippān yavan avan āgum nīḷ kdal vaṇṇanē*

- *tanjam āgiya tandai tāyodu tānumāy* – Those who claim to be mother and father, would abandon him when there is a danger \[like indra abandoned his own son jayanta who offended sītā pirātti and śrī rāma\]; even when he is in danger, it is [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) alone who protects him. There are some parents who consider “the time of his birth is inauspicious” and abandon him in a four road junction \[public place\] due to that \[as seen in the life of jarāsanda\]; some would sell their children during difficult times \[as seen in the life of śunaśśēpa, the nephew of viśvāmitra\]; unlike them \[emperumān would be like \] those parents who would protect their children even at the cost of self-sacrifices. Second explanation – since the bondage with worldly parents are based on karma, when the karma is exhausted, the bondage with them will also be cut off; in emperumān’s case, as he is the cause for everyone’s existence, he will be the father for everyone as said in mahābhāratam – śrīviṣṇu sahasranāmam “*bhūtānām yō’vyaya:pitā*” (the imperishable father for all creatures) and in mahābhāratam “*sarvēśāmēva lōkānām pitā mātā ca mādava:*” (for all creatures of the world, śriya:pati (husband of śrī mahālakśmi) is the mother and father); That too, he is the father for whom one need not cry for his departure \[since he is indestructible\].
- *tānumāy* – Father cannot be mother; mother cannot be father; both of them cannot be himself; he cannot be both his parents \[each has his/her own role\]; [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) will assume all these roles \[in caring for him\].
- *tānumāy* – When mother and father abandon him, one would think “I need to survive; Something good should happen to me”. bhagavān is such that he would always look out for the well-being. “tanjam” (refuge) is applicable for all of these – “*tanjamāgiya tandai*“, “*tanjamāgiya tāy*“, “*tanjamāgiya tān*“. Mother and father may not be true refuge; but would oneself not be true refuge \[looking out for the true well-being of self\]? No. Not even self is true refuge. This is because even though [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) blesses one with body and senses as said in śrī viṣṇu darmam “*vicitrā dēhasampattir īśvarāya nivēditum \| pūrvamēva krutā brahman hastapādādisamyutā \|\|*” (Oh brāhmaṇa! To offer oneself and other materials, ātmā previously got connected to the amazing body with hands and legs), the individual engages in useless activities as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 3.2.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/07/thiruvaimozhi-3-2-1-munnir-gyalam/) “*annāḷ nī tanda ākkaiyin vaḻi uḻalvēn*” (I will go in the ways of the body that was given by you); thus one is not one’s own refuge.
- *avai allanāy* – Not just father, mother and self, but he is the only one who bestows all types of upakāram (favour) and is the one who is all types of bandu (relation) as said in subhāla upaniśat “*mātā pitā brātā nivāsa: śaraṇam suhrud gatir nārāyaṇa:*” (nārāyaṇa is Mother, Father, Brother, residence, refuge, well-wisher, goal) and “*pitru mātru suta bhrātrudāramitrādayōpi vā*\| *ēkaikapalalābhāya sarvalābhāya kēśava: \|\|*” (When attaining father, mother, etc., they fulfil one particular purpose; When attaining kēsava, all purposes are fulfilled).
- *enjalil amarar* … – Who is such a person? [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says that he is the cause of the existence for nityasūris. enjal – contraction. il – not having. There is a clan of nityasūris who have no contraction in experiencing [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) – he is the leader/controller of them.
- *mūvar tam uḷḷum ādiyai* – When written as “*mūvartām uḷḷum ādiyai*” (one who is meditated by the trio of primary deities), this is explained as [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) being the antaryāmi of brahmā, rudra and indra and is meditated upon by them as said in cāndōjña upaniśat “*kāraṇam tu dyēya:*” (meditate upon the one who is the cause). ādi – dyēya vastu (object of meditation). Second explanation – “the antaryāmi (in-dwelling soul) and controller of brahmā, rudra and indra”. Third explanation – the principal one among the trio of primary deities. In this case, indra needs to be replaced with viṣṇu. Here mūvar means trio (count of three). It means one who is the cause among the three dēvatās.
- *anji* – All these aforementioned aspects are reason to be afraid. Can we approach the one who is all types of relation to the entire creation? Can we approach the one who is the cause for existence for the nityasūris? Can we approach the controller of brahmā and rudra? – fearing in this manner.
- *nīr ulagattuḷḷīrgaḷ* – you who are worldly people.
- *avan ivan enṟu kūḻēnmin* – avan (he who is in a distant place) – [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) who is not limited by dēśa (place), kāla (time) and vastu (objects), who is having distinguished form and who is being enjoyed by nityasūris \[in paramapadam\]. ivan (he who is in close proximity to us) – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is in a specific place, time and object, who accepted as divine form that which is made by materials that we desired \[for him\], and is dependent on our thoughts. \[That avan is the same as ivan.\] This being the case, don’t be bewildered that avan is apariccinna (unlimited) and ivan is pariccinna (limited).
- *nenjināl ninaippān yavan* – what you desired as his divine form in your mind.
- *avan āgum nīḷ kadal vaṇṇanē* – sarvēśvara who has unlimited greatness, would accept that with great desire as his divine form. Unable to spell out like riśis who said “… *pratimāsvaprabuddānām*” (for the ignorant, he appears in deity form), [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says “*avan ivan*” (that [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is in this deity form). [mudaliyāṇḍān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/mudhaliyandan/) used to say “Do not think that these diyva dēśams/kśētrams are wealth of paramapadanātan; instead you think that paramapadam is the wealth of [arcāvatāra emperumān](http://ponnadi.blogspot.in/p/archavathara-anubhavam.html)“. This is explained in śrī bhagavat gītā 4.11 “*yē yatā mām prapadyantē*” (whichever individuals pray to me to assume any forms, I will present to them in such forms to be pursued by them), taittirya nārāyaṇa upaniśat “*manasābhiklupta:*” (even one can worship through their mind), śrī viṣṇu purāṇam 5.17 “*smrutam sankalpanāmayam*” (viṣṇu who is considered based on one’s desires/will) and śrī viṣṇu darmam “*suvarṇa rajatādibhi:*” (one can worship the deity of viṣṇu in gold, silver etc in the manner that pleases oneself). Even his asādāraṇa vigraham (his divine distinguished form in paramapadam) is vorśipped by us due to “his accepting it as his form”; similarly, even his arcā (deity) forms, if he accepts them, there is nothing limiting us from vorśipping them. Primarily, his acceptance of a divine form is for the purpose of his devotees as said in jitantē stōtram 5 “*bhaktānām*” (Your everything (nature, form, ornaments etc) is for your devotees). It shines well where it can have full impact (in material realm, in deity form). Hence, he is nīḷ kadal vaṇṇan (one who is of the vast ocean-like nature).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.6.10. Kadal vannan

*kadal vaṇṇan kaṇṇan viṇṇavar karu māṇikkam enadāruyir padavaravin aṇaik kidanda paranjudar paṇḍu nūṟṟuvar adavarum padia manga aivargatkāgi venjamattu anṟu tēr tadaviya perumān kanai kaḻal kāṇbadenṟu kol kaṇgaḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

viṇṇavar – for the residents of paramapadam; karu māṇikkam – being enjoyable like a blue gem, not changing his form; padam – having hoods (which are expanded due to his touch); aravin – ananta (ādiśēśa) \[who has natural softness, coolness and fragrance\]; aṇaik kidanda – on the bed; param sudar – having bright glow (which establishes his supremacy); kadal vaṇṇan – having endless auspicious qualities and invigorating physical form; enadu – for me; Ar uyir – being the sustainer without whom I cannot live; paṇḍu – previously; nūṟṟuvar – of the hundred brothers (starting with duryōdana); ada varum – those who wanted to harm and marched towards him; padai – army; manga – to be destroyed; aivargatku – for the five pāṇḍavas; āgi – became the protector in all manner; vem samattu – in the heated battle; anṟu – at that time (back when the enemies came in large numbers); tēr kadaviya – who rode the chariot (as the charioteer); perumān – one who is filled with the quality of simplicity; kanai kaḻal – the divine feet which are decorated with anklets which make loud victorious noise; kaṇgaḷ – eyes; kāṇbadu – seeing (to my heart’s content); enṟu kol – when?

**Перевод:**

**kriṣṇa is enjoyable like a blue gem, not changing his form, being an object to be enjoyed \[by nityasūris\]; \[he descends to the milk ocean and\] is resting on the bed ananta (ādiśēśa) \[who has natural softness, coolness and fragrance\] who is having hoods, is having endless auspicious qualities and invigorating physical form and is the sustainer for me, without whom I cannot live; previously he became the protector in all manner for the five pāṇḍavas to destroy the army of those hundred brothers (starting with duryōdana) who wanted to harm and marched towards him, rode the chariot (as the charioteer) in the heated battle; when am I going to see with my eyes (to my heart’s content), the divine feet which are  decorated with anklets of such emperumān, which make loud victorious sound ?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In tenth pāsuram – After explaining the ultimate simplicity \[arcāvatāram\] of bhagavān \[in previous pāsuram\], being reminded by kriṣṇa, āḻvār says “When will I see the perfectly enjoyable divine feet of one who was present in the divine chariot and performed the role of charioteer?”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār meditates upon kriṣṇa’s activities where he tried hard to be subservient towards his devotees, wants to enjoy \[such activities\] after instructing others \[in previous pāsuram\].*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Tenth pāsuram. After mercifully explaining the saulabhyam (simplicity) which he started instructing, up to arcāvatāram \[his ultimate simplicity\], subsequently, went on to his favourite aspect of kriṣṇāvatāram and says “When will I see and experience \[such kriṣṇa\]?”, concluding thus with disappointment in not attaining the goal. \[Why would he go from arcāvatāram (which was explained as ultimate simplicity of emperumān) to kriṣṇa?\] When some one likes something, they won’t see whether it is difficult or easy to attain. Though there is lots of greatness in paratvam (supremacy in paramapadam), and there are many who reach there, tiruvadi (hanuman) said as in śrī rāmāyaṇam uttara kāṇḍam 40.16 “bhāvō nānyatra gaccati” (my heart does not desire any other form \[than this form of śrī rāma\]). Similarly, though arcāvatāram (deity form) is easier to approach compared to kriṣṇāvatāram, he became immersed saying “ettiṟam” (how is this possible?) in kriṣṇāvatāram only. But what happened to āḻvār previously saying “tayaradaṟku magan tannai anṟi maṟṟilēn” (I will not consider any one else as my goal other than the son of daśarata cakravarti)? He will only say that until he sees kriṣṇa’s simplicity.  But is arcāvatāram simpler than kriṣṇa? \[So, why is āḻvār going to kriṣṇa after seeing arcāvatāram?\] For this, we have already given explanation \[previously about hanuman’s attachment to śrī rāma and so on\]. kadal vaṇṇan kaṇṇan viṇṇavar karu māṇikkam enadāruyir padavaravin aṇaik kidanda paranjudar paṇḍu nūṟṟuvar adavarum padia manga aivargatkāgi venjamattu anṟu tēr tadaviya perumān kanai kaḻal kāṇbadenṟu kol kaṇgaḷē*

- *kadal vaṇṇan … viṇṇavar karumāṇikkam* – One who has divine form which is enjoyable for the nityasūris.
- *padavaravin aṇaik kidanda param sudar* – Leaving paramapadam, he descended to milk ocean to hear the complaints of brahmā et al in close proximity and resting there.
- *kadal vaṇṇan kaṇṇan* – Leaving milk ocean, he appeared as kriṣṇa to be enjoyed by all. \[Summarizing up to here\] The immeasurably great kriṣṇa who is enjoyed by nityasūris, leaving *kalangāp perunagaram* (unśakeable great abode of paramapadam), descended to *kśīrābdi* (milk ocean) to hear the complaints of brahmā et al, resting on tirvanantāḻvān (ādi śēśan) who has expanded hoods due to his physical contact and resting there, shining like a precious stone embossed on a gold plate due to the contact with ādiśeśan \[due to resting on him\], having an invigorating form which reveals his supremacy over all.
- *enadu Ar uyir* – He is everything for me such as dāraka (that which sustains) etc \[that which nourishes and that which gives pleasure\].
- *padavaravu* … – ādiśēśan whose hoods are expanded due to being in contact with [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/). This explains that emperumān greatly enjoys being in contact with ādiśēśan. Since the word “aravu” (sarpa – serpent) is used, we can understand that ādiśēśa has natural fragrance, coolness, softness etc.
- *param sudar* – Only when he is lying on ādiśēṣa, his supremacy is visible.
- *paṇḍu* – Long ago
- *nūṟṟuvar …* – All the evil-minded people joined hands with duryōdana and his brothers.
- *adavarum padai manga* – To destroy the army which marches to kill emperumān. Those evil boys would march towards him screaming “sāratee! sāratee!”.  As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 17.5 “*asmāt hantum*” (sugrīva and the monkeys say “vibhīśaṇa is coming along with his 4 soldiers to kill us”), [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) feels as if the army is coming to kill āḻvār himself \[that is why he is saying “*varu padai*” (the army which is coming) instead of “*cenṟa padai*” (the army which is going towards kriṣṇa)\].
- *aivargatku āgi* – As said in mahābhāratam drōṇa parvam 183.24 “*kriṣṇāśrayā: …*” (pāṇḍavas are surrendered to kriṣṇa; kriṣṇa is their strength and kriṣṇa is their lord), for those pāṇḍavas who have no other refuge than kriṣṇa himself.
- *vem samattu* – In the battle. Wanting to present his subservience towards his devotees to be seen by everyone as highlighted by [emperumānār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/emperumanar/) in [śrī gītā bhāśyam](http://githa.koyil.org/) “*pārtam ratinam ātmānam ca sāratim sarvalōka sākśikam cakāra*” (Having arjuna as the master of the chariot and himself as sārati (charioteer), he made it visible for the eyes of everyone in the world).
- *anṟu* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) becomes grief-stricken thinking even those who hated [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) had the fortune to see him and I have missed it then. Is there any way I will get this opportunity again?
- *tēr* … – On hearing the sound of the ornaments in his divine feet, he wants to see them. \[[nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s beautiful words of explaining kriṣṇa’s posture which is quoted/paraphrased by [piḷḷai lōkācāryar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/pillai-lokacharyar/) in other grantams\] *sēnādūḷiyum uḷavukōlum siṟuvāykkayiṟum tērukkīḻē nāṟṟina tiruvadigaḷum adilē sāṟṟina siṟuc cadangaiyumāy sāratyavēśattōdē ninṟa pōdait tiruvadigaḷil ābaraṇa dvani sevippadavum avvadivaik kāṇavum kāṇum āsai – The dust of the army \[on his body\], having a stick and small rope to control the horse, having his divine feet firmly placed on the ground underneath the chariot, the divine anklets which decorate those divine feet – as* [*āḻvār*](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) *hears the sound of the anklets, he wants to see the divine form behind that sound.*
- *kanai kaḻal* – kanai – *seṟinda* (well shaped), *dvanikkiṟa* (that which makes sound) \[*kaḻal* – divine feet\].
- *kāṇbadu* … – When will my eyes meet \[see\] his lotus feet? Until now, the eyes have been refused its food \[of enjoying his lotus feet\], when will this refusal stop? When will those eyes which long for that vision get that?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.6.11. Kangal kandarku

*kaṇgaḷ kāṇḍaṟkariyanāyk karuttukku nanṟum eḷiyanāy maṇ koḷ jñālattuyirkkellām aruḷ seyyum vānavar īsanaip paṇ koḷ sōlai vaḻudi nādan kurugaik kōn śatakōpan sol paṇ koḷ āyirattip pattāl pattarāgak kūdum payiluminē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kaṇgaḷ – eyes; kāṇḍaṟku – to perceive; ariyanāy – being difficult; karuttukku – for the heart; nanṟum eḷiyanāy – being the target of elaborate experience; maṇ koḷ jñālattu – in the world which is dominated by land; uyirkku – for creatures; ellām – all; aruḷ seyyum – doing favours (through arcāvatāram); vānavar īsanai – the lord who gives out the same experience that is given to nityasūris; paṇ koḷ – (due to the buzz of the bees) having abundant noise; sōlai – having garden; vaḻudi nādan – being the leader of tiruvaḻudi nādu (āḻvārtirunagari region); kurugaik kōn – the lord of āḻvārtirunagari town; śatakōpan – nammāḻvār; sol – mercifully spoke; paṇ koḷ – with meter; āyirattu – among the thousand pāsurams; ip pattāl – this decad (which highlights the simplicity of arcāvatāra emperumān); pattar – having bhakti \[as said in śrī bhagavat gītā 7.19 “sa mahātmā sudurlabha:” (such greatly devoted souls are very rare to find), very difficult to see\]; āgak kūdum – would become; payilumin – practice \[this decad\]

**Перевод:**

**emperumān is difficult for the eyes to perceive and is the target of elaborate experience for the heart; he is the lord who gives out the same experience that is given to nityasūris, doing favours (through arcāvatāram) for all creatures in this world which is dominated by land; nammāḻvār who is the leader of tiruvaḻudi nādu (āḻvārtirunagari region) which is having garden with abundant noise (due to the buzz of the bees)  and the lord of āḻvārtirunagari town, mercifully spoke with meter on such emperumān in this decad (which highlights the simplicity of arcāvatāra emperumān) among the thousand pāsurams; by \[practicing\] this decad, one would have bhakti (great devotion); \[hence, you\]  practice \[this decad\].**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In eleventh pāsuram – āḻvār says “On practicing this decad, one will surely become a faultless devotee; knowing this, practice this decad”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār mercifully explains gain of devotion towards bhagavān as the result of this decad.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. kaṇgaḷ kāṇḍaṟkariyanāyk karuttukku nanṟum eḷiyanāy maṇ koḷ jñālattuyirkkellām aruḷ seyyum vānavar īsanaip paṇ koḷ sōlai vaḻudi nādan kurugaik kōn śatakōpan sol paṇ koḷ āyirattip pattāl pattarāgak kūdum payiluminē*

- *kaṇgaḷ kāṇḍaṟkariyanāyk karuttukku nanṟum eḷiyanāy* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying with the distaste of not having seen [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/). Being difficult to be seen by eyes, yet always in the forefront of the heart and hence unable to save oneself by accepting the fact “yes, he cannot be seen” \[At least if we can forget, there will be less grief. Neither he can be seen, nor he can be forgotten\]. For āḻvār, viślēśam (separation) is – agony due to the disturbance in internal togetherness as a result of not being able to see him externally (physically). samslēṣam (union) is – internal visualization which is as good as seeing him physically.
- *maṇ koḷ* … – As he was enjoyed by nityasūris, the easily approachable [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) due to his presenting himself in arcāvatāram to favour samsāris (worldly people) without discriminating them.
- *paṇ koḷ sōlai* – Very noisy/musical garden due to the buzzing of the bees. The sōlai resembles mukkōttai \[mukkōttai is a temple of dēvatāntarams such as durgā, vināyaka – which will induce even a layman to sing great poems. Here, the garden of āḻvārtirunagari is such that, it will even make bees to sing beautiful tunes. Also explained as – the garden is inducing [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) to sing beautiful tunes\].
- *vaḻudi nādan* – Mercifully spoken by nammāḻvār who is the leader of tiruvaḻudi nādu (bigger region) and [āḻvārtirunagari](http://azhwarthirunagari.koyil.org/) (smaller town inside the bigger region).
- *paṇ koḷ āyiram* – Just like the buzzing of bees became beautiful tunes without their knowledge, the overflowing devotion in the speech of nammāḻvār became set in meter naturally.
- *pattarāgak kūdum payiluminē* – [cētana](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)s (sentient beings) may achieve many different things, but it is very difficult for them to attain devotion towards [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/); even that will be attained by practicing this decad. Even for those who don’t have sukrutam (virtues), śāstra jñānam (knowledge in śāstram), sadācārya upadēśam (instructions from a genuine teacher) and unconditional mercy of bhagavān, when they meditate upon the simplicity of [arcāvatāra emperumān](http://ponnadi.blogspot.in/p/archavathara-anubhavam.html), they will acquire devotion towards bhagavān; one will start thinking “Should we \[at least\] not be friendly towards [sarvēśvaran](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) who has no unfulfilled desires out of motherly affection towards his devotees, assumes a form that is desired by his devotee, accepts what he is fed as food, enters different homes and never abandons his devotees?”. As soon as one hears “there is treasure buried here \[in one’s house\]”, he/she will feel very blissful and pursue it; similarly when [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) mercifully says “*pattar āgak kūdum*” (one will become devotee \[instead of ordering “You practice this decad to become a devotee”\]), they will start practicing the decad.

[āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) tiruvadigaḷē śaraṇam

## 3.7 Payilum sudaroli

## 3.7.1. Payilum sudaroli

*payilum sudar oḷi mūrttiyaip pangayak kaṇṇanaip payila iniya nam pāṟkadal sērnda paramanaip payilum tiru udaiyār evarēlum avar kaṇḍīr payilum piṟappidai tōru emmai āḷum paramarē*

**Пословный перевод:**

payilum – abundant; sudar – having radiance (such as saundaryam (overall beauty), lāvaṇyam (beauty of specific parts) etc); oḷi mūrttiyai – having divine form which is an embodiment of splendour; pangayak kaṇṇanai – having pūṇḍarīkākśatvam (being lotus-eyed which is indication of supremacy over all); payila iniya – being perfectly enjoyable for those who are fully engaged (in this beauty); nam – for the devotees; pāṟkadal – in the divine milk ocean; sērnda – one who mercifully rests; paramanai – having supremacy in the enjoyable nature of form and qualities; payilum – being together and eternally engaged in; tiru – wealth; udaiyār – those who have; evarēlum – even if they lack (high birth, knowledge, actions); avar – in that same state; payilum – (for us, in ever repeating) many; piṟappidai tōṟu – in births; emmai – us; āḷum – having as servitors; paramar kaṇḍīr – they are the supreme masters

**Перевод:**

**emperumān is one who is having abundant radiant divine form which is an embodiment of splendour, having lotus-eyes which indicate supremacy, having supremacy in the enjoyable nature of form and qualities, mercifully rests in the divine milk ocean being perfectly enjoyable for his devotees who are fully engaged (in this beauty); those who have the wealth of being together with him to be eternally engaged in him, even if they lack (high birth, knowledge, actions), even in that same state, they are the supreme masters having us as servitors in many births.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In first pāsuram – āḻvār explains the essence of this decad saying ” all those who become attracted towards emperumān‘s beauty and qualities and serve him, whoever they may be, they are my masters”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*In first pāsuram – āḻvār says “bhāgavatas who have the wealth of associating with the lord of all, who is resting in milk ocean with distinguished form and qualities, even if they are considered inferior due to their birth, actions etc., they are my masters”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. payilum sudar oḷi mūrttiyaip pangayak kaṇṇanaip payila iniya nam pāṟkadal sērnda paramanaip payilum tiru udaiyār evarēlum avar kaṇḍīr payilum piṟappidai tōru emmai āḷum paramarē*

- *payilum* – payilugai – seṟigai (growing abundantly); since it is in present continuous tense, it will constantly be glowing unlike in worldly aspects where the radiance may grow for some time only to be reduced eventually since they are driven by karma \[here, payilum is explained as adjective for the radiance\].
- *sudar oḷi mūrttiyai* – one who is having a form is which is embodiment of perfect splendour.
- *payilum sudar* – Alternatively, payilum is explained as nityatva (eternal) – that is the radiance existing eternally at all times.
- *sudar oḷi mūrttiyai* – sudar and oḷi implies tējas (splendour) – great splendour. Alternatively – oḷi means beauty \[sudar oḷi – shining beauty\]. One who is having divine form which is embodiment of pure goodness revealing his true nature. His divine form is of pure goodness such that it reveals his auspicious qualities such as jñānam etc and his true nature as said in śrī bhagavat gītā 14.6 “*tatra satvam nirmalatvāt prakāśakam*” (that satva guṇam (goodness) which reveals the purity), śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 1.9.63 “*tējasām rāśimūrjitam*” (one who shines like collection of radiant rays and who has the valour to demolish his enemies), śrī bhagavat gītā 11.12 “*divisūrya sahasrasya*” (Like a thousand sun shining at the same time in the sky) being perfectly radiant and captivating as said in “*śādguṇya vigraham*” (divine form with six qualities) for those who want to be captivated.
- *pangayak kaṇṇanai* – All his bodily beauty will be matched with the beauty of his eyes. This is explained in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 53.8 “*rāma: kamalapatrākśa:*” (śrī rāma, having eyes that resemble lotus petal). Those who are attracted towards his bodily beauty, would be kept captivated by the beauty of his eyes. His bodily beauty is like a radiant ocean. The beauty of his eyes resembles well spread lotus flower in that radiant ocean. His physical beauty itself attracts everyone. Moreover his eyes would reveal his internal qualities such as motherly affection etc.
- *payilum* … – \[from the beginning\] One who is having eternal perfectly radiant form and more beautiful eyes.
- *payila iniya* – Due to his ever lasting physical beauty and beautiful eyes, he is enjoyable. Other \[worldly\] matters are of the nature that – they look nice from a distance \[or before attaining\], but once approached closely \[or attained\], one would want to leave them \[since they don’t look the same beautiful way in all aspects\]; when [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is approached closely, we will understand the defects of worldly aspects; at the same time \[when emperumān is approached closely\], we will understand the nature of emperumān being the eternal goal. This is why emperumān is the nitya prāpyam (eternal goal). Once [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s beauty is enjoyed, even subsequently, the experience will be afresh as said in cāndōjña upaniśat 8.12.3 “*nōpajanam smaran*” (ātmā will not contemplate about the material body after reaching the spiritual realm), like a liberated person will forget about his worldly existence \[eternally enjoyable means even if we repeatedly enjoy emperumān, there will never be boredom and there will always be a new type of experience every time forever\]. As explained in periya tirumoḻi 8.1.9 “*paṇḍu ivarai* …” \[Have I seen tirukkaṇṇapuram emperumān before somewhere else?” wonders parakāla nāyaki, says her mother\] – When meeting [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) the first time, due to natural lordship and the coolness/mercy in the face, even though one may not have seen him before, one would wonder “He looks familiar; have I seen him before?”; but even after getting to know each other for a few days, one will wonder “Have I seen him before \[He looks different now\]”. I (nampiḷḷai) asked \[nanjīyar\] – As the words “*paṇḍu ivarai yām kaṇḍu*” are the same – why is there two different meanings in two different situations? nanjīyar replied to me saying – In both situations (initial and subsequent), the same word “*payilginṟāḷāl*” (repeatedly reciting) is used \[so one way or other, parakāla nāyaki is always wondering about the identity of emperumān\].
- *nam* … – Can he be ignored due to lack of good qualities though he is very beautiful? No. The one who has “kalangāp perunagaram” (unśakeable big city – paramapadam) as his abode, descends to the milk ocean to address his devotees \[out of great compassion – so, he is filled with auspicious qualities too\].
- *nam* – implies “for his devotees”. Others, who are beautiful, when desired to be approached, will make it difficult to do so \[out of pride etc\]; but such beautiful [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) himself descended to milk ocean which is nearer \[for us\] in comparison to paramapadam to be enjoyed by his devotees.
- *paramanai* – You extolled his physical beauty and qualities over others; is there any one as great as he? No. There is no one superior to him \[He is the most supreme lord\].
- *paramanaip payilum tiru udaiyār* – Considering his presence to be a good opportunity, instead of begging for worldly favours, those who approach him having the wealth of considering himself as the goal. Those who approach him for specific ulterior goals, will leave him after their goal is accomplished; but those who approach him considering him as the goal, will get closer and closer.
- *tiru* – Like he has the crown of supremacy, these devotees have the crown of servitude; \[three personalities/incidents are cited to explain to tiru/śrī/wealth\] As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 16.17 “*antarikśa gatas śrīmān*” (śrī vibhīśaṇāḻvān, the most wealthy person who has started his airborne journey towards śrī rāma); viṣṇu darmam 68th chapter “*satu nāgavaraś śrīmān*” (that gajēndrāḻvān is endowed with wealth of kainkaryam); śrī rāmāyaṇam bāla kāṇḍam 1.18.29 “*lakśmaṇō lakśmī sampanna:*” (lakśmaṇa who is endowed with kainkarya śrī); \[explaining each personality in detail now\] “*antarikśa gatas śrīmān*” – As soon as took one step considering śrī rāma’s lotus feet as the goal, giving up lankā, his poverty of being associated with rāvaṇa got eradicated and real wealth matching his true nature was acquired. “*satu nāgavaraś śrīmān*” – Here śrī gajēndrāḻvān’s great desire to serve [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) which made the sarvēśvaran arrive hurriedly without checking his personal looks etc., is explained as the wealth; “*lakśmaṇō lakśmī sampanna:*” – lakśmaṇa’s servitude was such that, even when perumāḷ (śrī rāma) forced him to accept the throne of the prince and was told as in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 131.88 “*sarvātmanā paryanunīyamāna:*” (Only if you became a prince, I will become the emperor), lakśmaṇa simply rejected any post and remained as a servitor only. When bharatāḻvān was asked “when will you be relieved of internal agony?”, he replied as in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 98.8 “*yāvanna caraṇau bhrātu: pārtivavyanjanānvidau śirasā dārayiśyāmi…*” (Until I behold the divine feet of my brother śrī rāma who has all qualities of being a king, I will not have peace), “When perumāḷ is crowned with suitable throne for him \[being the lord\], and I being crowned with suitable throne for me \[being the servitor\], my distress will be removed”. This is explained in perumāḷ tirumoḻi 10.7 “*arasamarndān adi sūdum arasu*” (the crown of the lotus feet of śrī rāma being the emperor). [kulaśēkarāḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/kulasekarazhwar/) desires to be living at the divine feet of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/).
- *udaiyār* – As seen in “vaiśravaṇan” (who is the son of viciravasu), those who have the wealth of pāratantriyam (total subservience), are known as udaiyār \[in tamiḻ, udaiyār means those who possess/have\].

What other glories should they have to be praised/supported by us?

- *yavarēlum* – Whatever may be their birth, actions and knowledge; such subservience only is required.
- *avar kaṇḍīr* – Since the pride which is acquired through high birth, best actions and great knowledge are hurdles for one’s servitude towards [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/), [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says “those who are devoid of such pride” are desired. āḻvār says “those want to identify themselves as ‘tadīyar’ (bhagavān’s devotee) only, and those who are devoid of the pride of high birth etc., which are contrary to vaiṣṇavatvam (the quality of being a vaiṣṇava) are my favourites”.

When asked “How long will they remain dear to you?”, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says,

- *payilum piṟappidai tōru* – In all births which occur one after another. Now, āḻvār is desiring for the same births which he wanted to give up previously in [tiruvāimoḻi 3.2.2](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/07/thiruvaimozhi-3-2-2-vanma-vaiyam/) “*nin pal mā māyap pal piṟaviyil padiginṟa yān*” (me who is suffering in many different births which is facilitated by your amazing abilities), since those births are used to serve bhāgavatas. āḻvār says that he is ready to take many more births if he will be serving at the divine feet of a bhāgavata (devotee).
- *emmai āḷum paramar* – The lords who can enslave me. When asked “previously you said [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is ‘paraman’ (supreme) and now you are seeing his devotees are ‘paramar’; why is it like this?”, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says “There, he was glorified due to his great qualities; here, those who are captivated by his such great qualities are glorified”. If individuals are glorified independently without their relationship with [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/), that means āḻvār’s relationship with bhagavān will become void.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.7.2. Alum paramanai

*āḷum paramanaik kaṇṇanai āḻip pirān tannait tōḷum ōr nāngudait tūmaṇi vaṇṇan emmān tannait tāḷum tadakkaiyum kūppip paṇiyum avar kaṇḍīr nāḷum piṟappidai tōṟu emmai āḷudai nādarē*

**Пословный перевод:**

āḷum paramanai – being the one who has the superior qualities such as śeelam (disposition) etc to enslave (his devotees); kaṇṇanai – being the one who has simplicity in his incarnations which reveal that; āḻip pirān tannai – (to protect his devotees, even in his incarnations) being the one who has the sudarśana chakra (disc); ōr – unparalleled; nāngu tōḷum udai – being the one with four shoulders; tū – enjoyable (for them); maṇi – distinguished like a blue gem stone (which can be tied in one’s cloth and controlled); vaṇṇan – being the one with the form; emmān tannai – my lord who enslaved me (by manifesting such form); tadam tāḷum kaiyum kūppi – folding their hands and legs revealing their submissive nature; paṇiyum avar kaṇḍīr – those who offer their obeisances; nāḷum – forever; piṟappidai tōru – in many births to come; emmai āḷ udai – those who have me as their servant; nādar – nātabhūtar (lord)

**Перевод:**

**emperumān is the one who has the superior qualities such as śeelam (disposition) etc to enslave (his devotees); who has simplicity in his incarnations which reveal such qualities; who has the sudarśana chakra (disc) (to protect his devotees, even in his incarnations); (further, as a shade for his devotees to take shelter,) he is the one with four unparalleled shoulders; is the one with the form which is distinguished like a blue gem stone (which can be tied in one’s cloth and controlled); is my lord who enslaved me (by manifesting such form). Those who offer their obeisances folding their hands and legs revealing their submissive nature towards emperumān, are my lords who would have me as their servant forever in many births to come.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In second pāsuram – āḻvār says “śrīvaiṣṇavas who are fascinated by the beauty of emperumān‘s divine body parts, are my lords”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. āḷum paramanaik kaṇṇanai āḻip pirān tannait tōḷum ōr nāngudait tūmaṇi vaṇṇan emmān tannait tāḷum tadakkaiyum kūppip paṇiyum avar kaṇḍīr nāḷum piṟappidai tōṟu emmai āḷudai nādarē*

- *āḷum paramanai* – \[Why is [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) saying “[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is paraman” here after saying “bhāgavatas are paramar” in previous pāsuram?\] emperumān is of the nature that even if we are attached to bhāgavatas ignoring him, he would rule us by engaging us in the service of bhāgavatas as desired by us; \[Is he surely of that nature?\] He is as said in amalanādipirān 1st pāsuram “*adiyārkku ennai ātpadutta vimalan*” (the pure lord who will engage me in the service of his devotees); āḻvār is saying that [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is the cause for such joy \[of being engaged in the service of bhāgavatas since he is the one who facilitated that\]; also, we are attached to bhāgavatas only due to their relationship with him.
- *kaṇṇanai* – \[kriṣṇa\] there is no one comparable to him for engaging his devotees in service; he enslaves his devotees by performing the role of messenger for them, riding their chariot as the driver etc. He assumes various incarnations and roams around to enslave the jīvātmā in his life time by doing as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 2.7.6](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/05/thiruvaimozhi-2-7-6-madhusudhanai-anri/) “*edir sūḻal pukku*” (coming from the opposite side to catch the jīvātmā), and as said in periya tirumoḻi 8.9.6 “*anjēl enṟu adiyēnai ātkoḷḷa vallānai*” (one who can enslave me, eliminating my fears) and periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 1.6.11 “*ātkoḷḷat tōnṟiya āyar tam kōvinai*” (the leader of the covherd clan, kriṣṇa, who appeared to enslave me).
- *āḻip pirān tannai* – Even while assuming inferior roles, he carries the tool to change day to night, pick up arms after vowing not to do so etc. mahābhāratam bhīśma parvam – “*sudarśanam cititamātramāśu tasyāgrahastam svayamārurōha*” (As soon as he thought about him, sudarśana at once seated himself on the hand of kriṣṇa) – sudaraśanāḻvān will climb on his hand and will destroy the enemies. sudarśana is capable of acting merely based on [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s will. [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is the upakāraka (pirān – one who performs great favour) by manifesting the divine beautiful combination of his hand and sudarśana chakra for his devotees, eliminating the enemies with that for those who need their enemies to be removed and will let those who want to enjoy the beauty to enjoy the same.
- *tōḷum* … – The shoulders are present to eliminate the enemies as well as to let the devotees enjoy them, so that nothing additional is required. śrī rāmāyaṇam kiśkintā kāṇḍam 3.14 “*āyatāśca suvrutāśca  … kimartam …*” (For what reason, your (śrī rāma’s) divine shoulders that are well stretched, well rounded, resembling an iron beam and qualified to be decorated by all ornaments, are not decorated?). This implies [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) does not stop with manifesting divine beauty which is what is expected by the devotees \[but also use the same to destroy their enemies\].
- *nāngu* – When [bhattar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/parasara-bhattar/) was in tirukkōśtiyūr, [anantāḻvān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/ananthazhwan/) asked him “In paramapadam, does [sarvēśvaran](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) have two hands or four hands?” and bhattar replied “ēkāyanar (those who follow dvaita philosophy) say ‘he is dvibhujan (two handed)’ and our ācāryas say ‘he is caturbhujan (four handed)'”; anantāḻvān further asked “what is the pramāṇam (source) for these?” and [bhattar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/parasara-bhattar/) mercifully replied “if he is two-handed he would resemble [periya perumāḷ](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) (śrīrangam mūlavar); if he is four-handed, he would resemble [namperumāḷ](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) (śrīrangam utsavar) \[implying ‘in either case, he is enjoyable’\]”. \[Is there anyone who has seen [periya perumāḷ](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) with four hands?\] Unlike us, those who had divine vision \[[tiruppāṇāḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/thiruppanazhwar/)\] saw periya perumāḷ and glorified him as in amalanādipirān 7 “*kaiyinār surisangu anal āḻiyār*” (one who is having curved conch and fiery disc \[in additional two hands\]); As kriṣṇa would appear with four hands for the cow-herd girls \[who were dear to him\] and would appear with two hands for kamsa et al who were unfavourable towards him; [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) when appearing as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 3.5.5](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/09/thiruvaimozhi-3-5-5-sadhu-sanaththai/) “*ādi am sōdi uruvai angu vaittu ingup piṟandu*” (he appeared in this world with the same radiant primordial form as in paramapadam), appeared with four-hands; when vasudēva requested as in śrī bhāgavatam 5.3 “*… upasamhara*” (Oh lord of nityasūris who is having conch, disc, and mace, you have taken birth here with this divine form; oh my lord! out of compassion, please conceal this form \[and assume a human form\]), he assumed a human form. nilāttukkuṟi pagavar asked [bhattar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/parasara-bhattar/) “Is there any pramāṇam (authentic evidence) to say that emperumān is four-handed in paramapadam?” and bhattar replied “Yes, it is highlighted in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 114.15 ‘*tamasa: paramō dātā śankacakragadādara:*‘ (the lord of śrīvaikuṇṭam which is beyond the material realm is holding Sanka (conch), chakra (disc) and gadā (mace)), he is the provider”. nilāttukkuṟi pagavar becomes stunned with anger on hearing the evidence, bhattar mercifully said “Can’t you accept it even after hearing the pramāṇam?”. [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) resembles a kalpaka tree branched with four unparalleled shoulders.
- *tūmaṇi* … – To capture certain people, his bodily beauty itself is sufficient and his beautiful shoulders are extravagant. One who enslaved me showing his beautiful form which resembles faultless blue gem. One who has beautiful form that will steal the heart of those whose hearts are already stolen by his devotees. Even they became attached to his devotees seeing his beauty only.
- *tāḷum tadak kaiyum kūppi* – To worship such beauty, they would be happy to have well grown legs and hands. Folding the legs means becoming ananyagati (have no other refuge) and folding the hands means becoming akincana (having nothing in oneself to offer). Thus, the result of these two is to becoming bhagnābhimāna (completely free from pride). \[hanuman offering his respects humbly towards sītā pirātti while meeting her after śrī rāma’s victory is highlighted as an example for humility\] śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 113.4 \[it is indicated as 116.3\] “*nibhruta:*” – to have all parts subdued in one part \[being fully silent\]. “*praṇata:*” – fallen down unable to lift oneself up \[being very humble\]. “*prahva:*” – staying there even without thinking that “I am offering obeisances so humbly \[even that could lead to pride\]”.
- *nāḷum piṟappidai tōṟu* – In every birth. And in every day of those births.
- *emmai āḷudai nādarē* – Only in the case of [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/), he needs to enslave us by manifesting his beauty, qualities etc; but in case of bhāgavatas, they are our lords unconditionally. \[Do we at least not need permission of bhagavān to become a servitor of his devotees?\] As we are owned by him \[which means we are also owned by his devotees\], one need not get the permission of bhagavān to become servant of his devotees, oneself need not also be consciously be aware of becoming a servitor. All of these will happen naturally. This is already explained in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 4.4.10 “*endammai viṟkavum peṟuvārgaḷē*” (the devotes can even sell me as a commodity).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.
