## 3.7.3. Nadanai jnalamum

*nādanai jñālamum vānamum ēttum naṟunduḻāyp pōdanaip ponnedum cakkarattendai pirān tannaip pādam paṇiya vallāraip paṇiyum avar kaṇḍīr ōdum piṟappidai tōṟu emmai āḷudaiyārgaḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

nādanai – being the unconditional master; jñālamum – (the ignorant) samsāris \[worldly people who are residents of the material realm\]; vānamum – (the wise) nityasūris \[eternally free souls who are residents of the spiritual realm\], without any distinction; ēttum – as glorified by; naṟum tuḻāyp pōdanai – being decorated with very fragrant tiruttuḻāy (tuḷasi) garland; pon – good-looking; nedum – overwhelming (with sweetness); cakkarattu – with the beauty of his divine hands and sudarśana chakra (disc); endai pirān tannai – one who is my infinite lord; pādam – in the lotus feet; paṇiya vallārai – those who bow; paṇiyum avar kaṇḍīr – those who bow and serve them; ōdum – spoken (in śāstram); piṟappu idai tōṟu – in various births; emmai – us; āḷudaiyārgaḷ – who have as servitors

**Перевод:**

**emperumān being the unconditional master, who is glorified without any distinction by both samsāris and nityasūris, who is decorated with very fragrant tiruttuḻāy (tuḷasi) garland, is my infinite lord due to the beauty of his good-looking overwhelming (with sweetness) combination of his divine hands and sudarśana chakra (disc); those who bow and serve those who bow at his lotus feet, are the ones who have us as servitors in various births, which are spoken in śāstram.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In third pāsuram – āḻvār says “śrīvaiṣṇavas who are attached to the beauty of emperumān who is decorated with tuḷasi, are my lords”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “Those who are surrendered to bhāgavatas who are attached to emperumān‘s enjoyable nature which is enjoyed by both spiritual and material realms, they are the lords who enslave me”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Third pāsuram. āḻvār says “Those who are surrendered to those who are won over by the beauty of emperumān‘s shoulders and the matching garland on the shoulders, are my lords”. nādanai jñālamum vānamum ēttum naṟunduḻāyp pōdanaip ponnedum cakkarattendai pirān tannaip pādam paṇiya vallāraip paṇiyum avar kaṇḍīr ōdum piṟappidai tōṟu emmai āḷudaiyārgaḷē*

- *nādanai* – one who is my unconditional lord.
- *jñālam* … – On seeing the combination of his shoulders and the garlands on the shoulders, like how people cry out and worship when the screen is opened \[we can relate to this by imagining how the whole crowd in front of the sannidi cry out “gōvindā! gōvindā!” these days when [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) becomes visible after the screen in front of him is removed\], without any distinction, both nityasūris and nitya samsāris glorify emperumān. śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 130.32 “*strībālayuvavruddānām*” – those women who think that they will lose their chastity if they spoke a word in glorification of men, children who cannot speak, youth who won’t reveal their mind, elderly people who cannot speak cohesively – śrī rāma’s beauty was such that, it is glorified loudly by all of these.
- *naṟum tuḻāyp pōdanai* – One who is decorated by fresh tuḷasi flower which acquired divine fragrance due to coming into contact with his divine body.
- *pon* … – one who is having the divine sudarśana chakra which is attractive like gold, being incomparable for his beauty, decorated ornament and gait, with abundance of joy. He is the one who performed the favour of enslaving me by manifesting such beautiful chakra. Like those princes (who are focussed on enjoyment) will take ghee for every handful of rice, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) repeatedly enjoys the combination of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s divine hand and the tiruvāḻi (sudarśana chakra). “*āḻip pirān*” in previous pāsuram is explained as “*pon nedum cakkarattu endai pirān*“.
- *pādam* … – Those who can become captivated in the beauty and fall at his divine feet instead of feeling jealous about it. \[Who would manifest jealousy on the supreme lord?\] They are manifesting jealousy without understanding his greatness. sarvēśvaran himself mercifully said in [śrī bhagavat gītā](http://githa.koyil.org/) 9.1 “*idam tu tē guhyatamam pravakśyāmi anasūyavē*” (I am talking to you this most secret knowledge, since you are not jealous of me) and [śrī bhagavat gītā](http://githa.koyil.org/) 18.67 “… *na ca mām yōbhyasūyati*” (this carama ślōkam is not to be revealed to the one who hates me). \[Is it difficult to worship [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) without jealousy?\] Since our pūrvācāryas have demonstrated it, it is easy for us to follow; only when we look at others \[who don’t do it\], we can understand the difficult in doing it.
- *vallāraip paṇiyum avar kaṇḍīr* – \[those who are able to worship such devotees.\] If one can be envious towards īśvaran himself, what to speak of envy towards his devotees? In case of [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) one may look at his supremacy and worship him or one may consider oneself to be independent and refuse to do so as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 36.11 “… *na namēyam …*” (rāvaṇa – I will never worship śrī rāma, even if I am cut into two pieces); but devotees who sustain themselves by food and water are more difficult to be surrendered \[since they will be considered as good as oneself\]. Ignoring their physical constraints and looking at the devotees purely by their dependence on [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) and accepting them as their master, one should have very good maturity. \[But, is being simple, a cause for jealousy?\] Yes. For śisupāla et al, emperumān’s saulabhyam itself became the cause for their envy and led to their destruction \[since they abused him considering him to be a normal human and thus paid the price for that\]. \[nampiḷḷai narrates an incident from his own life to demonstrate how difficult it is for one to accept another devotee as superior\] There was a good śrīvaiṣṇava named piḷḷai āttān. He approached the divine feet of jīyar ([nanjīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nanjiyar/)) and requested him to teach tiruvāimoḻi once fully. nanjīyar said to him “You learn it from piḷḷai (nampiḷḷai) who will explain it to you in great detail”. piḷḷai āttān asked nanjīyar “But do I have to offer my obeisances to him” \[He was ready to offer obeisances to nanjīyar who was a sanyāsi (renouncer) and senior, but was hesitant to offer obeisances to nampiḷḷai who was a gruhasta (householder) and younger too\]. Hearing that, nanjīyar said “That is not compulsory. You can do it if you desire to do so”. nanjīyar then called me and instructed me to explain tiruvāimoḻi to him even if he wants to sit on a higher platform and learn. I started doing that and when I explained this decad, he started respecting me greatly \[after understanding the glories of śrīvaiṣṇavas\], and I withdrew myself from teaching him. He then went to nanjīyar and told him “Since I did not know the importance of this principle \[of being devoted to devotees\], I previously told like that. You please mercifully instruct him to accept my respects” and forcefully served me by the orders of nanjīyar \[which I could not refuse\].
- *ōdum* … – If we get this servitude towards devotees, I will not mind even births where I am mentioned just as “*piṟandān, settān*” (he was born, he died). Alternatively, I will accept any birth which is explained in śāstram as inferior.
- *emmai āḷudaiyārgaḷē* – As said in [tiruvāimoḻi 2.3.10](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/02/thiruvaimozhi-2-3-10-kalippum-kavarvum/) “*adiyārgaḷ kuḻāngaḷ*” and tiruvāimoḻi 10.9.11 “*andam il pērinbattu adiyarōdirundamai*” (being together with the devotees in paramapadam which has endless joy) – one serves in the special place of paramapadam to devotees only; let them accept that service \[from me\] here itself.
- *emmai* – His lordship is common towards all as mentioned in jitantā 1.2 “*dēvānām dānvānām ca sāmānyamadidaivatam*” (Oh the one who is the common lord for dēvas and asuras!); but bhāgavtas are lords for those who acquired special knowledge as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.1.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/03/thiruvaimozhi-1-1-1-uyarvara-uyarnalam/) “*mayarvaṟa madi nalam*” (faultless knowledge and devotion) like myself ([āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)). When we look at [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s glories, it will overshadow the worldly aspects \[of bhāgavatas\]; As said in mahābhāratam śānti parvam “*durācārōpi …*” (even if he has bad conduct etc., if one is fully faithful to śrīman nārāyaṇan who is the cause of everything, he is to be known as faultless), even if a devotee is seen to have certain faults, if he is surrendered to [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), he should be considered as faultless. Why should he be considered faultless when there are faults? As said in the same “*durācārōpi*” ślōkam, “*prabhāvāt paramātmana:*” (by the greatness of [paramātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)), after being a devotee, if we consider inferior \[due to the faults\], it is equal to considering bhagavān to be incapable of purifying him. Two dear śiśyas of [nanjīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nanjiyar/) named vīrap piḷḷai and pāligaivāḷip piḷḷai who were always together, went to a different town, became angry at each other due to a fight and did not talk to each other. Seeing that nanjīyar said to them “Dear sons! only if material wealth and lust are not to be given up, only if bhagavat viśayan is not sufficient / conclusive, a śrīvaiṣṇava can be angry at another śrīvaiṣṇava and avoid talking to him”. Hearing that, they both offered obeisances to nanjīyar and became friendly again.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.7.4. Udai arnda

*udai ārnda ādaiyan kaṇḍigaiyan udai nāṇinan pudaiyār pon nūlinan pon mudiyan maṟṟum pal kalan nadaiyā udait tirunāraṇan toṇḍar toṇḍar kaṇḍīr idaiyār piṟappidai tōṟu emakkem peru makkalē*

**Пословный перевод:**

udai ārnda – fitting with the waist; ādaiyan – having divine garment; kaṇḍigaiyan – being the one wearing ornaments in the neck; udai nāṇinan – being the one who is wearing a waist string on top of the garment; pudai Ar – placed on one side; pon nūlinan – being the one with golden yajñōpavītam (sacred thread); pon mudiyan – wearing an attractive crown; maṟṟum – and; pal kalan – many different ornaments; nadaiyā udai – having them naturally; tirunāraṇan – nārāyaṇan who is śrīmān; toṇḍar – for those who are servitors; toṇḍar kaṇḍīr – those who are servitors of; idai Ar – permanent; piṟappu idai tōṟu – in every moment of every birth; emakku – for us; em perumakkaḷ – distinguished supreme lords

**Перевод:**

**nārāyaṇan who is śrīmān (husband of śrī mahālakśmi) is having garment/dress which fits well with his waist \[perfect fit\]; is wearing ornaments in the neck; is wearing a waist string on top of the garment; is adorned with golden yajñōpavītam placed on one side; is wearing an attractive crown and having many different ornaments naturally; those who are servitors of the servitors of such emperumān, are our distinguished supreme lords permanently in every moment of every birth.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In fourth pāsuram – āḻvār says “Those who are servitors of śrīvaiṣṇavas who are attached to the divine ornaments of emperumān, are my lords”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. udai ārnda ādaiyan kaṇḍigaiyan udai nāṇinan pudaiyār pon nūlinan pon mudiyan maṟṟum pal kalan nadaiyā udait tirunāraṇan toṇḍar toṇḍar kaṇḍīr idaiyār piṟappidai tōṟu emakkem peru makkalē*

- *udai ārnda ādaiyan* – Looks like the waist blossomed into the waist garment. “*kauśēya puśpita katītatam*” (the silk garment in the waist appears to have blossomed from the waist). śrīmat bhāgavatam kāṇḍam 10 “*pītāmbaradara:*” (one who is wearing yellow garment) \[nampiḷḷai goes on to explain the whole ślōkam. This ślōkam is usually recited as part of tiruvārādanam during mantra puśpam\]. *tāsāmāvirabhūt* – While roaming around in śrī brindāvanam, he hid himself to see how restless they \[covherd girls\] become. When he realized that “they cannot sustain the separation anymore”, he appeared in front of them. *tāsām* – Like a drought-stricken land blessed with heavy rain. *smayamāna mukhāmbuja:* – his lotus like face would be like this \[with a beautiful smile\] when he sees them \[the covherd girls\] cannot sustain in his absence. *pītmābaradara:* – His yellow garment is so soothing that it relieves the girls from their anger out of separation \[love-fights\]. The yellow garment is such that, after having the wounds in the heart healed, there will be constant meditation/discussion about the beauty of the yellow garment itself. This is the main routine as explained in [tiruvāimoḻi 3.1.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/07/thiruvaimozhi-3-1-1-mudichchodhiyay/) “*padiccōdi ādaiyodum palkalanāy nin paim pon kadiccōdi kalandaduvō*“. *sākśānmanmatamanmata:* – As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam “*pumsām druśti cittāpahāriṇam*” (śrī rāma who captures the eyes and heart of men too).
- *kaṇḍigaiyan* – To stop the beauty of the garment escaping through the top, there is a ornament in the divine neck. It pulls [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) upto the neck and makes him enjoy the beauty there. kaṇḍigai – necklace which is worn on the neck.
- *udai nāṇinan* – waist string. When enjoyed fully, the waves of beauty from the neck push down, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) stops and enjoys the middle portion \[of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s divine body\].
- *pudaiyār pon nūlinan* – Not needing another ornament in its side, like a lightning in a dark-cloud, one who is having the divine sacred thread. As āḻvār immerses in the ocean of beauty, he holds on to the sacred thread as a support.
- *pon mudiyan* – As said in tiruvāimoḻi 3.6.10 “*tēr kadaviya perumān*” (emperumān who rode the chariot), one who is crowned to serve his devotees. \[double-meaning\] If one holds on to a nūl \[nūl also means śāstram\], he is sure to reach the head \[being liberated\]. ponmudi – attractive crown.
- *maṟṟum pal kalan nadaiyā udai* – one who wears many other ornaments naturally. Once the head is reached, all other enjoyments will naturally follow.
- *maṟṟum pal kalan* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) becomes speechless \[stunned due to the joy and thus unable to further elaborate in detail about each ornaments\]. Since there are infinite ornaments, he cannot completely list them; but he cannot stop glorifying his beauty. This is āḻvār’s trouble.
- *tiru nāraṇan* – The relationship with [śrī mahālakśmi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/) is like the perfect fit of those ornaments to [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/). It is said as in tiruvāimoḻi 10.10.2 “*mārvattu mālai*” (garland in the chest). As the tiruvābharaṇāḻvārs \[divine ornaments\] are eternal free souls of paramapadam, one who controls/owns them is called tirunāraṇan.  [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying “*the lords of this world is this divine couple”* .
- *toṇḍar toṇḍara kaṇḍīr* – Like the divine togetherness of tāyār and perumāḷ being the ultimate state of śēśitvam (lorśip), these bhāgavatas are staying in the ultimate state of śēśatvam (servitorśip).
- *idai Ar* … – In every moment of every birth, without any break. Instead of manifesting decorated beauty externally \[as done by emperumān\] and enslaving us, they are our natural \[without any such condition\] lords. Alternatively – For those who are surrendered to [śrīman nārāyaṇan](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), I am wondering “how amazing it is to see them taking shelter of the divine couple together” and declaring that I am their servant. Even if they don’t think themselves as my lords, they are our lords \[in my opinion\]. Our distinguished lords.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.7.5. Peru makkal

*peru makkaḷ uḷḷavar tam perumānai amarargatku arumai oḻiya anṟāramudūttiya appanaip perumai pidaṟṟa vallāraip pidaṟṟum avar kaṇḍīr varumaiyum immaiyum nammai aḷikkum pirākkaḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

peru makkaḷ uḷḷavar – for the nityasūris who have greatness of having parama sāmyāpatti (having similar qualities that are of bhagavān‘s); tam perumānai – the distinguished emperor; amarargatku – for the dēvas (celestial beings) who desire for immortality; arumai oḻiya – eliminating difficulty; anṟu – previously (when they were cursed by durvāsa muni); Ar amudu ūttiya – feeding them the nectar fully; appanai – towards the one who ensured their existence; perumai – his greatness of favouring others; pidaṟṟa vallārai – those who can speak about it (in a disorderly manner due to overflowing love); pidaṟṟum avar kaṇḍīr – those who speak about them (in turn being overwhelmed with love); varumaiyum immaiyum – in aihika (of this world – material realm – samsāram) and āmuśmika (belonging to the other world – spiritual realm – paramapadam); pirākkaḷ – those who provide us favours

**Перевод:**

**emperumān is the distinguished emperor for the nityasūris who have greatness of having parama sāmyāpatti (having similar qualities that are of bhagavān‘s) and fed the nectar fully to the dēvas (celestial beings) who desired for immortality previously (when they were cursed by durvāsa muni) and ensured their existence; śrīvaiṣṇavas can speak (in a disorderly manner due to overflowing love) about his greatness of favouring others; those who speak about such śrīvaiṣṇavas (in turn being overwhelmed with love) are the ones who provide us favours in this (material) world and the other (spiritual) world.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In fifth pāsuram – āḻvār says “Those who meditate upon, become emotional and glorify emperumān who is having the nature of fulfilling the desires of prayōjanāntaraparar (those who worship him with ulterior motives), are the masters who protect us in this world and higher world”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Fifth pāsuram. āḻvār says “My masters are those who are won over by those who are won over by emperumān‘s audāryam (generosity) of fulfilling the desires of prayōjanāntaraparar too” peru makkaḷ uḷḷavar tam perumānai amarargatku arumai oḻiya anṟāramudūttiya appanaip perumai pidaṟṟa vallāraip pidaṟṟum avar kaṇḍīr varumaiyum immaiyum nammai aḷikkum pirākkaḷē*

- *peru makkaḷ* – nityasūris; As said in “*periyōr*” (respected elders). They are said as in periya tirumoḻi 7.4.4 “*pērāḷan pērōdum periyōr*” (the respected persons who recite the names of the great lord). The words of śēśi (the lord) also glorify them as in [śrī bhagavat gītā](http://githa.koyil.org/) 9.13 “*mahātmanas tu*” (but those great souls), 7.19 “*sa mahātmā su durlabha:*” (such great souls are rare to find) and “*ētē vai sumahātmana:*” (these are great souls). If these can be said for those mumukśus (desirous of mōkśam) in this samsāram (material realm) who become favourable towards [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), there is no surprise for nityasūris to be called in this way.
- *uḷḷavar* – Always present instead of as in taittiriya upaniśat “*asannēva*” (as good as non-existing) until one day and became “*santamēnam*” (existing) one day \[for those who are ignorant of true knowledge about their servitude towards [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/), they are said to be as good as non-existing and when they realize that true knowledge, they exist\]. That is, since their true nature of servitude is never lost. When nirūpaka \[the attribute which is used to identify an entity – here, the servitude which identifies the [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)\] is not present, nirūpyam \[the entity which is identified through the attribute – here, the [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) which is identified by the servitude\] is considered to be non-existing too. Those whose servitude is never diminished.
- *tam perumānai* – [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) who being the reason for their existence and the one who conducts such existence.
- *amaragatku* – \[amarar means immortal – really indicates nityasūris\] for indra et al – though they live a few days \[years\] longer than us, they carry the name “amarar” \[pretending to be really immortal\].
- *arumai oḻiya* – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) churned the ocean and gave the results to them to relieve them from the insults of being tortured by the asuras (demons). Also explained as, he took up the difficulty of churning the ocean himself and engaged them in enjoying the resulting nectar.
- *anṟu* – when they were suffering due to the curse of durvāsa muni.
- *ūttiya appanai* – He is known as in periya tirumoḻi 2.6.1 “*vānavarip peṇṇāgi amudūttum perumān*” ([emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who assumed a feminine form and fed the dēvas). appan – upakārakan – one who bestows favours. The favour done by the mother to her children is to nourish the child and raise him/her.
- *perumai* … – As said by himself in [śrī bhagavat gītā](http://githa.koyil.org/) 7.8 “*udārā:*” (they are generous). His generosity of being magnanimous towards those who desire for worldly wealth etc., as we would be towards those who desire for [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) himself. He would think “At least I am able to help them in this manner; they are doing sarvasvadānam \[offering themselves – emperumān magnanimously thinking like this\]!”. His greatness is not the same as the greatness of worldly people. In this world, those who give are considered to be generous. But here, those who accept \[from emperumān\] are considered (by emperumān\] to be generous. If one eliminates others’ suffering, are they not said to be generous? \[Since only if some one accepts, he can be glorified of being generous – so he glorifies them to be generous to make him generous.\]
- *pidaṟṟa vallārai* – As said in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.7.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/09/thiruvaimozhi-1-7-1-piravith-thuyar/) “*aṟavanai*” (most benevolent), those who can meditate in their heart upon his greatness of even helping prayōjanāntaraparar and glorify him in a disorderly manner.
- *pidaṟṟum avar kaṇḍīr* – The manner in which those devotees feel “how magnanimous [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is even towards those who are desiring for ulterior motives!” and be attached to him, for those who have the same kind of attachment towards such devotees.

How long will you desire for them?

- *varumaiyum immaiyum* – As said in stōtra ratnam 2 “*atra paratra cāpi*” (in both this material realm and spiritual realm) – both here and in paramapadam. In this world, they would be as said in tiruvāimoḻi 10.6.2 “*nāttārōdu iyalvoḻittu nāraṇanai naṇṇuvittu*” (eliminating the relationship with worldly people and bringing closer to śrīman nārāyaṇan) and in paramapadam they are the ones who bestow favours as said in tiruvāimoḻi 2.3.10 “*adiyārgaḷ kuḻāngaḷilē udankūttum*” (will make us unite with the groups of devotees in paramapadam).
- *nammai aḷikkum pirākkaḷ* – The lords who uplift us. sarvēśvaran would keep us inside him \[in subtle form\] some times \[during deluge\] and also would keep us in samsāram as said in perumāḷ tirumoḻi 5.1 “*taru tuyaram tadāyēl*” (not removing the sufferings which were given by you); the nature of śrīvaiṣṇavas is such that, when associating with them, we would think that “even samsāram (material realm) is a fine place to be”. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) himself said in tiruvāimoḻi 8.10.3 “… *naṟumāvirai nāḷ malar adik kīḻ  pugudaluṟumō*” (When śrīvaiṣṇavas are present here, would it be apt for me to reach the very fragrant fresh lotus feet of vāmanan [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)?).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.7.6. Alikkum paramanai

*aḷikkum paramanaik kaṇṇanai āḻip pirān tannait tuḷikkum naṟum kaṇṇit tūmaṇi vaṇṇan emmān tannai oḷik koṇḍa sōdiyai uḷḷattuk koḷḷumavar kaṇḍīr salippinṟi āṇḍu emmaic canma canmāntaram kāpparē*

**Пословный перевод:**

aḷikkum paramanai – (while helping others) there is none greater than him in giving (himself); kaṇṇanai – being subservient (to be at the disposal of his devotees); āḻip pirān tannai – the beautiful combination of his divine hand and the sudarśana chakra (disc); tuḷikkum naṟum kaṇṇi – the beauty of the fragrant garland with flowing honey; tū maṇi – like a flawless precious stone; vaṇṇam – form; pirān tannai – bestowing (manifesting); emmān tannai – being the master who enslaved me; oḷik koṇḍa – acquiring shine (as a result of that); sōdiyai – one who is having splendour; uḷḷattu – through the heart; koḷḷumavar kaṇḍīr – those who enjoy; emmai – us; salippu inṟi – firmly (ensuring that we don’t seek ulterior benefits); āṇḍu – engaging us in their service; sanmam – in this birth; sanmāntaram – in the subsequent births; kāppar – they will protect

**Перевод:**

**emperumān (while helping others) has none greater than him in giving (himself) and is subservient (to be at the disposal of his devotees); he became my master by manifesting the beautiful combination of his divine hand and the sudarśana chakra (disc), his form which resembles a flawless precious stone and as a result of that acquired shining splendour. Those who enjoy him through their heart will protect us firmly (ensuring that we don’t seek ulterior benefits) both in this birth and in the subsequent births.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In sixth pāsuram – āḻvār says “Those who enjoy in heart, all the previously mentioned qualities such as saundaryam (beauty) etc. collectively, are my protectors always”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “Those who enjoy the radiant emperumān who lets the ananyaprayōjanars (devotees who are exclusively focussed on kainkaryam) enjoy his divine bodily beauty are my protectors”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. aḷikkum paramanaik kaṇṇanai āḻip pirān tannait tuḷikkum naṟum kaṇṇit tūmaṇi vaṇṇan emmān tannai oḷik koṇḍa sōdiyai uḷḷattuk koḷḷumavar kaṇḍīr salippinṟi āṇḍu emmaic canma canmāntaram kāpparē*

- *aḷikkum paramanai* – When it comes to protecting these ātmās, there is none matching his ability to do so. Alternatively, when it comes to bestowing, there is none matching his ability to do so. aḷikkai – rakśikkai (protecting) and kodukkai (bestowing).
- kaṇṇanai – He gives himself. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) himself said in [tiruvāimoḻi 2.7.11](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/05/thiruvaimozhi-2-7-11-parpanaban/) “*enakkē tannait tanda kaṟpagam*” ([emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is the kalpaka tree which gave itself to me).
- *āḻip pirān tannai* – As said in jitantē stōtram 5 “*… nāyudāni …*” (Your everything (nature, form, ornaments etc) is for your devotees), emperumān considers his weapons as well as himself existing for his devotees only as said in the same ślōkam “*bhaktānām*” (for his devotees only). Here, āḻvār is thinking about [tiruvāimoḻi 3.7.2](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/09/thiruvaimozhi-3-7-2-alum-paramanai/) “*āḷum paramanai*” pāsuram.
- *tuḷikkum* … – His garland is present to trap those who have not been captured by his beautiful weapons \[kaṇṇi means both garland and trap\].
- *tuḷikkum naṟum kaṇṇi* – One who is adorning tiruttuḻāy (tuḷasi) garland which acquired freshness due to coming in contact with his divine body, which is having flowing honey and beautiful fragrance; Here, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is thinking about [tiruvāimoḻi 3.7.3](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/09/thiruvaimozhi-3-7-3-nadhanai-gyalamum/) “*naṟum tuḻāyp pōdanai*” (one who is adorning fragrant tuḷasi garland).
- *tūmaṇi vaṇṇan emmān tannai* – One who showed his divine form which resembles a blue gem which is free of any impurity and enslaved me; as said in tiruvāimoḻi 1.10.10 “*maṇiyai vānavar kaṇṇanai*” , like he enslaved nityasūris, he also enslaved [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) \[by showing his beautiful form\]. It is said in mudal tiruvantādi 85 “*padi kaṇḍaṟidiyē*” (Have you seen his divine form and known about him). Here, āḻvār thinks about [tiruvāimoḻi 3.7.2](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/09/thiruvaimozhi-3-7-2-alum-paramanai/) “*tōḷum ōr nāngudait tūmaṇi vaṇṇan*” ([emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who has pure gem like form with four shoulders).
- *oḷik koṇḍa sōdiyai* – One who has infinitely radiant form. Here, āḻvār thinks about [tiruvāimoḻi 3.7.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/09/thiruvaimozhi-3-7-1-payilum-sudaroli/) “*payilum sudaroḷi*” (emperumān with abundant radiance).
- *uḷḷattuk koḷḷumavar kaṇḍīr* – Those who meditate upon [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s auspicious qualities, become emotional and unable to speak out due to the overwhelming emotions.
- *salippu inṟi āṇḍu emmai* – When one takes refuge of bhagavān, one may still move away from bhagavān by being attracted to great wealth of brahmā et al. Only when one becomes a servitor of a tadīya (bhāgavata/devotee), one will remain firm. Even if they moved away from bhagavān, they will be as said in [kaṇṇinuṇ ciṟut tāmbu 3](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/01/kanninun-chiru-thambu-3-thirithanthagilum/) “*tiritantāgilum dēva pirānudaik kariya kōlat tiruvuruk kāṇban*” (Even if I slipped (giving up) nammāḻvār, I will see the divine blackish form of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is the master of nityasūris). As said in periya tirumoḻi 1.1.3 “*terivaimār uruvamē maruvi*” (being attached with the forms of women), bhāgavatas ensure that we are focussed on [madurakavi āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/madhurakavi-azhwar/)‘s stature of being focussed on one form ([nammāḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)) instead of [tirumangai āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/thirumangai-azhwar/)‘s stature of being engaged in many different forms of emperumān \[Here, uru is explained as form\]. Also, explained as – emperumān will have to teach this many times, but āḻvār (bhāgavatas) will make us understand in one time \[Here, uru is explained as repetition\].
- *sanma sanmāntaram kāpparē* – They will protect us from not taking subsequent births. In previous pāsurams, out of attachment towards śrīvaiṣṇavas, he favoured more births; in this birth, he is explaining their action \[in stopping our worldly births\].

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.7.7. Sanma sanmantaram

*sanma sanmāntaram kāttu adiyārgaḷaik koṇḍupōyt tanmai peṟuttit tan tāḷiṇaik kīḻk koḷḷum appanait tonmai pidaṟṟa vallāraip pidaṟṟumavar kaṇḍīr nanmai peṟuttu emmai nāḷ uyyak koḷginṟa nambarē*

**Пословный перевод:**

sanma sanmāntaram – many births; kāttu – (protecting by) relieving them; adiyārgaḷai – those who have the knowledge about servitude; koṇḍu pōy – carry them (to paramapadam); tanmai peṟutti – making them realize their true nature; than tāḷiṇaik kīḻ – under his divine feet; koḷḷum – mercifully accepting service; appanai – one who is the master; tonmai – natural helping tendency; pidaṟṟa vallārai – those who can praise in a disorderly manner; pidaṟṟumavar kaṇḍīr – those who glorify them being overwhelmed with love; emmai – us; nanmai peṟuttu – making us acquire the excellence (of being in paramapadam with devotees as said in tiruvāimoḻi 10.9.11 “andamil pēr inbattu adiyarōdu“); nāḷ – forever; uyyak koḷginṟa – one who would uplift; nambar – would be believed

**Перевод:**

**emperumān is the master who protects those who have the knowledge about servitude by relieving them of many births, carrying them (to paramapadam), making them realize their true nature and mercifully accepting their service under his divine feet; śrīvaiṣṇavas are those who can praise his natural helping tendency in a disorderly manner; those who glorify such śrīvaiṣṇavas being overwhelmed with love are the ones who would make us acquire the excellence and are believed to uplift us forever.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In seventh pāsuram – āḻvār says “Those who glorify the śrīvaiṣṇavas who meditate emperumān‘s great favours towards his devotees and glorify him, are my eternal masters”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*sanma sanmāntaram kāttu adiyārgaḷaik koṇḍupōyt tanmai peṟuttit than tāḷiṇaik kīḻk koḷḷum appanait tonmai pidaṟṟa vallāraip pidaṟṟumavar kaṇḍīr nanmai peṟuttu emmai nāḷ uyyak koḷginṟa nambarē*

- *sanma sanmāntaram kāttu* – As explained in pancāgni vidyai \[This is the process which facilitates the transmigration of a soul from one body to another. This is explained in detail in cāndōjña upaniśat. Here agni and āhuti are synonyms – the five oblations which carry through the soul are ākāśa (ether), Cloud, Earth, Male and Female\], [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) \[after leaving a body, the ātmā goes to svarga (heaven) or naraka (hell) based on the karma, after the karma is exhausted, the ātmā enters the ākāśa (ether) and from there the sun picks up the ātmā and places it in a cloud\] enters a cloud, from there it falls into the earth as part of rain, enters into paddy seed from the earth, enters into a man in the form of food, from the man it reaches the fifth āhuti (oblation) which is the female and finally becomes part of the womb. Decimating such process of births. Making the current body as the final material birth and ensuring that the soul does not acquire another birth here in the material realm.

To whom is this done?

- *adiyārgaḷai* – those who have placed all their burdens \[fully faithful\] at [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s divine feet.
- *koṇḍu pōy* – \[nampiḷḷai narrates how emperumān carries the [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) from here to paramapadam beautifully\]
   - As said in tiruvāimoḻi 9.10.5 “*maraṇamānāl*” (when death occurs), he patiently waits until the current body falls down,
   - without mandating *antima smruti* (remembering the lord at the final moments) and bhakti (devotion) as a requirement, he himself thinks about such person as said in śrī varāha purāṇam, śrī varāha carama ślōkam “*aham smarāmi*” (If one surrenders to me when he/she is stable-minded, I will remember him/her when he/she lies as a log of wood or stone without any consciousness during their last moments and deliver him/her),
   - guide him through the 101st nādi \[suśumnā nādi – a specific nerve/vein which reaches up to the top of the head\] and accompanying him,
   - giving a divine experience to relieve from all the pains that occurred during death, pamper the ātmā to help facilitate the smooth journey like a mother who would pamper her child when the child is in agony,
   - as said in nānmugan tiruvantādi 88 “*uyirkoṇḍu udal oḻiya ōdumpōdu ōdi ayavenṟa tīrppān*”  (when the servitors of yama grab the [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) leaving the body and start running, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) will himself chase them and eliminate all the sufferings of the ātmā) emperumān would be friendly with the ātmā,
   - preserves the subtle body until the ātmā reaches the virajā river even though the connection with karma is eliminated \[along with the last body\] by vidyā māhātmyam (the greatness of the process of liberation),
   - instead of sending some divine messengers he himself personally accompanies him as said in śrī varāha carama ślōkam “*nayāmi*” (I will ensure they reach)
   - taken along under his protection as said in periya tirumoḻi 3.7.4 “*mādavan tuṇaiyā nadandāḷ*” (walked along under the protection of śrīman nārāyaṇan), like the “kaḷvankol pirātti” \[[parakāla nāyaki’s (tirumangai āḻvār in feminine form)](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/thirumangai-azhwar/) experience of walking with perumāḷ safely in late night when everyone was asleep – periya tirumoḻi 3.7\] who was carefully taken along by perumāḷ,
   - carrying the soul to paramapadam after eliminating all the material aspects \[at the virajā river\] to be honoured by the great souls who reside along the path that leads to paramapadam,
   - facilitating the ātmā to realize its shining true nature as said in cāndōjña upaniśat “*svēna rūpēṇābhiniśpadyatē*” (with its true form, the ātmā attained paramapadam),
   - still not leaving the ātmā \[independently\], placing the ātmā under his divine feet supported by the divine feet themselves,
   - the great benefactor who thinks that he has done a favour for himself even after doing so much for the ātmā. All of these is precisely explained in “*sāyujyam pratipannā yē*” (those who fully devote themselves to me and attain sāyujya mōkśam (being together with [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) always in paramapadam and serving him), they become my eternal servants).
- *tanmai peṟutti* – Making the ātmā realize its true nature,
- *appanai* – \[all these that were done to \] ātmā, since he is a cētana (sentient), he would consider this as a favour \[done by [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)\]; but in reality due to pāratantriyam (the nature of ātmā being fully dependant on bhagavān), bhagavān has done this for his own sake \[Here since bhagavān is appan (svāmy – master\], he has done all this to acquire his own property\].
- *tonmai pidaṟṟa vallārai* – those who become attracted to his natural generosity and glorify him in a disorderly manner. His natural state is to protect the ātmās; but it is aupādikam (due to specific reasons) he pushes down those who are evil due to their vices as said in śrī bhagavat gītā 16.19 “*tānaham dviśata:*” (those who insult me, hate me etc, I push them into births that make it difficult for them to attain me).
- *pidaṟṟumavar kaṇḍīr* – Those who are attached to them (śrīvaiṣṇavas) thinking “How they are able to understand and the most confidential aspects \[such as travelling to paramapadam etc\]” and glorify them.
- *nanmai peṟuttu* – Instilling servitude towards [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) which stretches upto servitude towards bhāgavatas.
- *emmai nāḷ uyyak koḷginṟa nambarē* – those trustworthy persons who will conduct our servitude towards his divine feet forever; it can indicate our mudaligaḷ (ācaryas).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.7.8. Nambanai

*nambanai jñālam padaittavanait tirumārbanai umbar ulaginil yārkkum uṇarvariyān tannaik kumbi naragargaḷ ēttuvarēlum avar kaṇḍīr em pal piṟappidai tōṟu em toḻu kulam tāngaḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

nambanai – being the refuge (unconditionally); jñālam padaittavanai – one who performs creation of the universe (to let others take refuge of him and enjoy him); tirumārbanai – having śrīya:patitvam (at all stages such as during creation, while taking refuge and while being enjoyed as the goal); umbar ulaginil – in higher worlds (which were created by him); yārkkum – even for the most knowledgeable persons; uṇarvu aṟiyān tannai – one who is too great to be known by them; kumbi naragargaḷum – even the most sinful persons who reside in kumbī naraka (a region in the hell which is gruesome); ēttuvarēl – if (they) glorify; avar tāngaḷ kaṇḍīr – those persons; em pal piṟappidai tōṟu – in our many different births; em toḻu kulam – the clan which is the recipient of our servitude

**Перевод:**

**emperumān is the (unconditional) refuge; performs creation of the universe (to let others take refuge of him and enjoy him); is having śrīya:patitvam (at all stages such as during creation, while taking refuge and while being enjoyed as the goal); is too great to be known by even the most knowledgeable persons residing in higher worlds (which were created by him); even if the most sinful persons who reside in kumbī naraka (a region in the hell which is gruesome) glorify him, the clan of such persons will be the recipient of our servitude in our many different births.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In eighth pāsuram – āḻvār says “Those who meditate upon his śrīya:patitvam (being the consort of śrī mahālakśmi) which is the cause of all his opulence, along with their descendants, are vorśippable to me, in all my births”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nampiḷḷais introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷais introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Eighth pāsuram. āḻvār says “My masters are those who are won over by his śrīya:patitvam (being the consort of śrī mahālakśmi)”. nambanai jñālam padaittavanait tirumārbanai umbar ulaginil yārkkum uṇarvariyān tannaik kumbi naragargaḷ ēttuvarēlum avar kaṇḍīr em pal piṟappidai tōṟu em toḻu kulam tāngaḷē*

- *nambanai* – one who is trustworthy. Even in the most difficult times, he is the refuge for the soul \[Even when kākāsura was at the receiving end from śrī rāma, kākāsura only had to surrender to him and be protected by him in the end. ōr even if one is harming the self, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is the only one who can protect\]. Even for the previously identified śrīvaiṣṇavas, their trustworthiness is based on emperumān’s trustworthiness. Those relatives other than him are not to be trusted.  \[nampiḷḷai goes on to explain śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kaṇḍam 38.33 to explain emperumān’s trustworthy nature – kākāsura hurt sītā pirātti and śrī rāma became very angry and fired the brahmāstram towards him which chases him everywhere\]
   - *sa pitrā ca* – \[nampiḷḷai explaining the essence of this ślōkam – that emperumān is the only protector even when the individual cannot help himself.\] periya tirumoḻi 8.9.7 “*peṟṟār peṟṟoḻindār*” (the parents abandoned). As a doctor/neighbour would help a patient who is suffering from great disease who declared “at a particular point of time, I will be suffering the ill-effects of this great disease; I will not be conscious of myself at that time; oh my lord! please come and protect me”, \[Similarly\] emperumān would help those who can’t protect themselves too.
   - *sa pitrā ca* – even when one is opposed to [īśvaran](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/), īśvaran himself is the protector. On seeing his offense against śrī rāma, kākāsura’s father indra abandoned him. “ca” (also) indicates that his mother also abandoned him. \[why is mother abandoning the child after father?\] As mother helps before father, if father abandons the child, she too needs to abandon. Where there is vātsalyam (motherly affection), one will take refuge first; that is why kākāsura approached his mother first; she (mother) stood decorating herself and ignoring her child; and he (father) too abandoned his child.
   - *parityakta: –* Seeing his action \[of hurting mother sītā\], everyone said “Have we not abandoned him already? \[Yes, We have\]”.
   - *suraiśca* – even when parents abandon a child, the relatives will support him. Even if dēvas give up, would the compassionate sages not help them?
   - *sa maharśibhi:* – Even those sages who are focussed on helping others abandoned him. But there is restriction on who can be shown mercy. When the parents disown their child, it is not the responsibility of the others to take care of the child. Thus,
   - *trīn lōkān samparikramya* – He went around the world many times trying to enter any open house thinking “if not the first time, at least subsequently they may show mercy and save me”; but they shut the doors as he tried to enter their houses.
   - *tamēva śaraṇam gata:* – He came back and fell at the divine feet of the one who fired the brahmāstram at him as said in perumāḷ tirumoḻi 5.1 “*arisinattāl īnra tāy agaṟṟidinum maṟṟavaḷ than aruḷ ninaindē aḻum kuḻavi*” (even if the mother with great anger pushes away the child, the child will cry seeking her mercy only), except for his divine feet, there is no other refuge \[in the end, śrī rāma pardons kākāsura and lets him go after piercing one of his eyes\]. In this way, [sarvēśvaran](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is the trustworthy person in all situations.

Where did we see such help from [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)?

- jñālam padaittavanai – When the [ātmā (sentient)](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) was in [acit (insentient)](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/09/thathva-thrayam-achith-what-is-matter/) like state during total deluge without any help from self or others, emperumān created the body \[and bestowed it to the ātmā\] which can be used to attain the puruśārtam (goal).

For whose pleasure was this done?

- *tirumārbanai* – For the pleasure of her ([śrī mahālakśmi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/)). [kūrattāḻvān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/kurathazhwan/) in his śrī stavam 1 says “*yasyā vīkśya mukham tadingitaparādīna:*” ([emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) looking at the face of śrī mahālakśmi and performs creation etc per her facial expressions).
- *umbar* … – One who cannot be known even by the most knowledgeable persons in the higher worlds.
- *kumbi naragargaḷ* … – Even if those who have entered the kumbī region of hell which is the destination of most sinful persons, recite the divine names of [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/),
- *avar kaṇḍīr* – Even if a śrīvaiṣṇava is in the most abominable state, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying that they are our goal \[to be pursued\], even in that state.
- *em pal piṟappidai tōṟu em toḻu kulam tāṇgaḷē* – In our many types of births and in every moment of such births, not just those who recited the divine names, are our desired target; but even the descendants of such persons are the ācāryas (master) for our clan. Is it possible for some one to recite the divine names when they are going through so much suffering in hell? [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) hopes “Even at that stage, shall they at least not scream ‘*ammā! appā*” (mother! father!) \[since [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is the natural mother and father, that will indicate him\]?”.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.7.9. Kulam tangu

*kulam tāngu sādigaḷ nālilum kīḻ iḻindu ettanai nalam tān ilāda saṇḍāḷa saṇḍaḷargaḷ āgilum valam tāngu sakkarattaṇṇal maṇivaṇṇaṟkāḷenṟu uḷ kalandār adiyār tam adiyār em adigaḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kulam – (by anulōma vivāham (brāhmaṇa man marrying khsatriya/vaiśya/śūdra woman, kśatriya man marrying vaiśya/śūdra woman, vaiśya man marrying śūdra woman) and pratilōma vivāham (śūdra man marrying vaiśya/kśatriya/brāhmaṇa woman, vaiśya man marrying kśatriya/brāhmaṇa woman, kśatriya man marrying brāmaṇa woman)) for all clans; tāngu – being the anchor; sādigaḷ – varṇams (classes); nālilum – in four of them; kīḻ iḻindu – below them; ettanai nalam tān ilāda – being totally ignorant (that “we are very low by birth”); saṇḍāḷar – caṇḍāḷa (considering this first caṇḍāḷa to be brāhmaṇa); saṇḍāḷargaḷ āgilum – those who are abandoned by (even such caṇḍāḷa highlighted in previous word); valam tāngu – being carried on the right side; sakkarattu – (As said in “śaraṇam pavitram” (pure refuge)) very pure/sacred \[sudarśana\] āḻvān’s; aṇṇal – being the lord; maṇi – pure like a precious gem (which will purify others who come into contact with it); vaṇṇaṟku – for the who is having (radiant) form; āḷ – (we are) śēśabhūtar (servitors); enṟu – thinking that; uḷ kalandār – united with him as ananyaprayōjanar; adiyār tam – for their servitors; adiyār – those who are servitors; em – for us; adigaḷ – lords

**Перевод:**

**emperumān is the lord of very pure/sacred \[sudarśana\] āḻvān who is carried on the right side \[by emperumān\]; he is having a (radiant) form which is pure like a precious gem (which will purify others who come into contact with it); even for those caṇḍāḷas who are abandoned by some caṇḍāḷas (who are considered better among them), who are totally ignorant (that “we are very low by birth”), who descended below the four varṇams due to anulōma, pratilōma marriages. if they think themselves as the śēśabhūtar (servitors) of such emperumān and unite with him as ananyaprayōjanar, those who are servitors for their servitors, are our lords.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In ninth pāsuram – āḻvār says “Those who are servitors of the śrīvaiṣṇavas who serve emperumān seeing the divine combination of his hand and the sudarśana chakra in the hand, are our masters”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “emperumān who has the utmost purity to eliminate the defects that arise out of their birth etc; those who enjoy such emperumān as ananyaprayōjanar (those who are without any expectation) are my lords for 3 levels \[i.e., we will serve the servitors of servitors of servitors of emperumān\]”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. kulam tāngu sādigaḷ nālilum kīḻ iḻindu ettanai nalam tān ilāda saṇḍāḷa saṇḍaḷargaḷ āgilum valam tāngu sakkarattaṇṇal maṇivaṇṇaṟkāḷenṟu uḷ kalandār adiyār tam adiyār em adigaḷē*

- kulam … – when we keep going below the various clans that are of krama vivāham (intra-class marriage within brāmaṇa, kśatriya, vaiśya, śudra), anulōma vivāham (brāhmaṇa man marrying khsatriya/vaiśya/śūdra woman, kśatriya man marrying vaiśya/śūdra woman, vaiśya man marrying śūdra woman) and pratilōma vivāham (śūdra man marrying vaiśya/kśatriya/brāhmaṇa woman, vaiśya man marrying kśatriya/brāhmaṇa woman, kśatriya man marrying brāmaṇa woman) \[ruśyaśrunga and yayāti are the ones who are examples for anulōma and pratilōma marriages\] and are anchored by the four varṇams;
- ettanai … – Among the caṇḍāḷa clan, there are those who don’t even have the knowledge and follow the principles of that clan, like we don’t see caṇḍāḷas, they are not even seen by their own community and are even considered as out-caste by the caṇḍāḷas themselves. Such lowly people.

What strength/identity they have which makes them also desirable \[for [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)\]? āḻvār explains further saying they have such conduct and also they have the mark of sudarśana chakra and explains it clearly to us.

- valam tāngu sakkaram – Like [periyāḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/periyazhwar/) said in [tiruppallāṇḍu 2](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/06/thiruppallandu-2-adiyomodum/) “*vadivāy nin vala mārbinil vāḻginṟa mangaiyum pallāṇḍu*” (long live śrī mahālakśmi who resides in your divine chest) followed by “*vadivār sōdi valattuṟaiyum sudar āḻiyum pallāṇḍu*” (long live the radiant sudarśana chakra which resides in your radiant right side), [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) too said “*tirumārbanai*” (one who has [śrī mahālakśmi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/) in his chest) in previous pāsuram and here he says “*valam tāngu sakkaram*“. For the sarvēśvara who is having the divine sudarśana chakra on his right side and the invigorating blue-gem like beautiful form which is the abode for that chakra.
- āḷ enṟu – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says that the servitors of those who consider “serving him with true knowledge is the goal” are my lords. Taking shelter under the one who has the best conduct (of being the servitor) is the only aspect that is required. They are even more desirable than [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) himself.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.7.10. Adiyarnda

*adiyārnda vaiyam uṇḍu ālilai anna vasam seyyum padiyādumil kuḻavippadi endai pirān tanakku adiyār adiyār tam adiyār adiyār tamakku adiyār adiyār tam adiyār adiyōngaḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

adi – with his divine feet; ārnda – united/merged; vaiyam – bhūmi (earth); uṇḍu – consuming it (when the danger of deluge occurred); ālilai – in a banyan leaf; anna vasam seyyum – resting (ensuring that the consumed world does not get digested); padi yādum il – incomparable; kuḻavip padi – having the form of a toddler; pirān endai tanakku – (due to that nature) one who is master for us; adiyār adiyār tam adiyār adiyār tamakku adiyār adiyār tam adiyār – to the lowest level in the descendants of those who are servitors; adiyōngaḷ – servitors (us)

**Перевод:**

**emperumān is the master for us due to the nature of having the incomparable form of a toddler and resting in a banyan leaf after consuming the bhūmi earth) which was united/merged with his divine feet (by his action of measuring the world during the trivikrama avatāram); we are the servitors to the lowest level in the descendants of those who are servitors of such emperumān,**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In tenth pāsuram – āḻvār desires for the ultimate state of servitude starting with the servitude of those who are attached to the amazing aspects of vatataḷaśāyi (emperumān lying in banyan tree leaf during total deluge), like those who desire for wealth will desire for the top most opulence.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*In tenth pāsuram, Like those who desire for material wealth will desire for the position of brahmā which has the top most material wealth, āḻvār too desires for the ultimate stage of servitude.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Tenth pāsuram. āḻvār says “I am the ultimate servitor \[at the bottom of the chain of servitors\] of śrīvaiṣṇavas who are won over by emperumān‘s agatitagatanā sāmartyam \[the ability of making the impossible happen – i.e., lying down in a small banyan leaf in the causal ocean after consuming the entire world\]”. adiyārnda vaiyam uṇḍu ālilai anna vasam seyyum padiyādumil kuḻavippadi endai pirān tanakku adiyār adiyār tam adiyār adiyār tamakku adiyār adiyār tam adiyār adiyōngaḷē*

- *adiyārnda vaiyam uṇḍu* – To consume the world, he first measured it. He consumed that which will not even be partly enough for him. Another explanation, consumed the world which is matching the size of tiruvadi (divine feet) \[this is based on pādam meaning feet and quarter – since material realm is said to be 1 quarter in size and spiritual realm to be 3 quarters in size\].
- *Al ilai anna vasam seyyum* – Two explanations. 1) lying down in a banyan leaf, to match the \[amount of\] food consumed. 2) lying down on the right side to ensure the consumed food is not digested. Every one tries to preserve his food. tiruppallāṇḍu 3 “*kūḻāḷ pattu*” (being attached to food) is applicable even for [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/).
- *padi yādumil kuḻavip padi* – his infancy has no match; not even his infancy under yaśōdā is a match; there \[yaśōdā’s residence\], his infancy is such that “while being in the cradle, he would not know/fear that he may fall off the cradle”; but here his infancy is such that, he would not know/fear that he may fall off the leaf into the causal ocean.
- *endai pirān* – the benefactor who won over me by manifesting such agatita gatanā sāmartyam \[combination of contrary aspects – consuming the entire world and yet lying down as a child on the leaf\].
- *adiyār* … – As said in śvētāśvatara upaniśat “*tamīśvarāṇam paramam mahēśvaram*” (that [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is the supreme lord for those who are considered as lords here \[in the material realm\]”, like there is no one superior to bhagavān in lordship, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) takes up a position where there is no one superior to him in servitude. Like one who desires for wealth would want to have more wealth than other persons of his clan, more wealth than kśatriyas \[who rule huge kingdoms\], then the position of indra \[being the lord of celestial world\] and finally even the position of brahmā \[being the lord of a whole material world containing 14 layers\], āḻvār too desires for the ultimate state of servitude. \[Is he desiring for a particular level of servitude?\] Even now he is not stopping \[with seven level of adiyārs\] due to his preference/desire; but he is stopping since the poetic meter does not allow any more words in this pāsuram. \[Would it not be contrary to worldly understanding if we wanted to be servitors of the lowest of caṇḍāḷas if they are devoted to [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)?\] [nanjīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nanjiyar/) said “If we manifest servitude towards vaiṣṇavas against the worldly understanding, then we will be regarded as being faithful to [nammāḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s desire”.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.7.11. Adiyongu

*adiyōngu nūṟṟuvar vīya anṟu aivarkkaruḷ seyda nediyōnait ten kurugūrc catakōpan kuṟṟēvalgaḷ adiyārnda āyirattuḷ ivai pattu avan toṇḍar mēl mudivu ārak kaṟkiṟkil sanmam seyyāmai mudiyumē*

**Пословный перевод:**

adi ōngu – the rise of their kingdom/reign; nūṟṟuvar – the hundred brothers starting with duryōdana; vīya – to be finished; anṟu – at that time (when they were banished); aivarkku – for the five pāṇḍavas; aruḷ seyda – helping them in all ways; nediyōnai – on the one who remained very eager (as if he has done nothing); then kurugūr – the leader of the orderly āḻvārtirunagari; śatakōpan – nammāḻvār‘s; kuṟṟēvalgaḷ – in the form of confidential activity; adi ārnda – being complete due to the pāda bhandam (connection with the divine feet of emperumān. It can also mean, the proper sequence/connection of the words/lines); āyirattuḷḷum – among the thousand pāsurams; avan toṇḍar mēl – on his servitors; mudivu – focussed; ivai pattu – these ten pāsurams; Ara – to grasp it well (in the heart); kaṟkiṟkil – if one can practice it well; sanmam seyyāmai – birth (which blocks one’s servitude); mudiyum – will be finished

**Перевод:**

**emperumān still remained eager even after helping the five pāṇḍavas in all ways at that time (when they were banished) to finish the hundred brothers starting with duryōdana who had their kingdom/reign on the rise; nammāḻvār, the leader of the orderly āḻvārtirunagari, sung these complete ten pāsurams among the thousand pāsurams which are complete due to the pāda bhandam, focussed on such emperumān’s servitors; if one can practice this decad to grasp it well in their heart, his/her birth (which blocks one’s servitude) will be finished.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the end – āḻvār says “Those who recite this decad which reveals about servitude towards bhāgavatas, will surely cross over the samsāram (material realm) which is a hurdle for this goal \[of servitude towards bhāgavatas\]”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār explains eradication of birth \[in this material realm\] as the result for this decad.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. adiyōngu nūṟṟuvar vīya anṟu aivarkkaruḷ seyda nediyōnait then kurugūrc catakōpan kuṟṟēvalgaḷ adiyārnda āyirattuḷ ivai pattu avan toṇḍar mēl mudivu ārak kaṟkiṟkil sanmam seyyāmai mudiyumē*

- *adiyōngu nūṟṟuvar vīya* – To finish the duryōdana and brothers, who trapped the pāṇḍavas in the wax palace, won them over in gambling by deceit, driving them out of the kingdom and making them stay in the forest etc., and themselves growing their families in great numbers, and rooted strongly in the kingdom.
- *anṟu* – at that time when the pāṇḍavas where banished by the kauravas.
- *aivarkku aruḷ seyda nediyōnai* – Helping the five, is applicable in both cases. Here \[in [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s case\], he blessed such that he is not suffering the impact of the five senses and there, he helped the five pāṇḍavas who were affected by the impact of five senses.
- *aivarkku* – When they (duryōdana et al) took over the elephants, horses etc, kriṣṇa himself became everything they lost as said in mahābhāratam rājasūya parvam “*yasya mantrī ca gōptā ca*” (for whom kriṣṇa is the minister, protector et al).
- *nediyōnai* – Even after engaging in actions for pāṇḍavas, he claimed that he had not done anything for them as said in mahābhāratam “*nātisvastamanā:*” (My heart is not satisfied).
- *then kurugūr* … – Since [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is performing kainkaryam by speech that goes up to servitude towards bhāgavatas, this is a confidential service to sarvēśvaran.
- *adi ārnda āyirattuḷ* – The thousand pāsurams which are complete in the poetic word/line structure as in rig vēdam and śrī rāmāyaṇam which is said as in śrī rāmāyaṇam bāla kāṇḍam 2.18 “*pādabatdō’kśarasama:*” (with four lines, and matching letters in each line).
- *avan toṇḍar mēl mudivu* – Wherever [sarvēśvaran](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is mentioned \[in this decad\], those are secondary in nature \[the primary purpose is to highlight the importance of bhāgavatas, who are his devotees\].
- *ārak kaṟkiṟkil* – If they can learn to have the meanings well established in their heart. Also, explained as, without leaving even a single pāsuram.
- *sanmam seyyāmai mudiyum* – births which are impediment to serve his devotees, will be eradicated.

## 3.8 Mudiyane

## 3.8.1. Mudiyane

*mudiyānēe! mūvulagum toḻudēttum sīr adiyanēe! āḻkadalaik kadaindāy! puḷḷūr kodiyānēe! koṇḍal vaṇṇā! aṇḍattumbaril nediyānēe! enṟu kidakkum en nenjamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

mudiyānē – Oh one with the crown (which highlights your supremacy of being the lord of both spiritual and material realm)!; mūvulagum – all the worlds; toḻudu ēttum – will approach and praise; sīr adiyānē – Oh one who is having the divine feet which have the complete qualities of being the apt refuge!; āḻ kadal – the deep ocean; kadaindāy – Oh one who helped them by churning!; puḷ Ur kodiyānē – Oh one who is having periya tiruvadi (garudāḻvār) as his vehicle and the flag (so he can visit his devotees and give them pleasure when they see him from distance)!; koṇḍal – Like a black cloud (to be enjoyed by those devotees and to invigorate them); vaṇṇā! – oh one who is having the form!; aṇḍattu – the residents of paramapadam; umbaril – the leader of nityasūris; nediyānē – Oh the great!; enṟu – meditating upon these (qualities individually); en nenjam – my heart; kidakkum – will remain still (being very weak without engagement in any activity)

**Перевод:**

**Oh one with the crown (which highlights your supremacy of being the lord of both spiritual and material realm)! Oh one who is having the divine feet which have the complete qualities of being the apt refuge, which are approached and praised by all the worlds! Oh one who helped the dēvatās by churning the deep ocean! Oh one who is having periya tiruvadi (garudāḻvār) as his vehicle and the flag (so he can visit his devotees and give them pleasure when they see him from distance)! oh one who is having blackish cloud like form! Oh the great leader of the nityasūris who are the residents of paramapadam! My heart will remain still (being very weak without engagement in any activity) meditating upon these qualities.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In first pāsuram – āḻvār mercifully explains how his divine heart is unhappy due to not having seen emperumān after having desired for that.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*In first pāsuram – āḻvār mercifully explains the great attachment of his divine heart towards emperumān who is the apt \[lord\], the refuge and the goal.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*First pāsuram. āḻvār speaks about the great desire of his divine heart to attain him. mudiyānēe! mūvulagum toḻudēttum sīr adiyanēe! āḻkadalaik kadaindāy! puḷḷūr kodiyānēe! koṇḍal vaṇṇā! aṇḍattumbaril nediyānēe! enṟu kidakkum en nenjamē*

- *mudiyānē* – His crown is the one which reveals his primordial lordship and his ownership over both spiritual and material realms; [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) first sights the divine crown which highlights his supremacy. His crown is so great that it will make others’ crowns fake. His crown is such that, it controls both spiritual and material realms.
- *mudiyānē****e*** – The depth of āḻvār’s anxiety can be identified by the tone of the lengthy cry. There is no specific order of starting with low pitch and reaching high pitch; it (his cry) right away starts in high pitch \[It is also explained as – āḻvār is directly focussing on the highest spot – the crown on the head instead of starting from lower parts of his divine body\].
- *mudiyānē****e*** – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) referred “*ponmudiyan*” previously (tiruvāimoḻi 3.7.4) and is re-emphasising it here.
- *mūvulagum* … – Oh one who has the divine feet which are the refuge for all worlds without discriminating based on the qualities or the lack of them \[in those who are surrendering\]! After being captivated by the divine crown, āḻvār falls at the divine feet of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/). [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) never leaves the divine feet of emperumān. He is being triggered by his previous statement in tiruvāimoḻi 3.7.7 “*than tāḷiṇaik kīḻ koḷḷum*”  (one who places under his divine feet). This implies that āḻvār is requesting emperumān to place his divine feet which is common to all worlds, on his head.
- *āḻ kadalaik kadaindāy* – He is reminded by tiruvāimoḻi 3.7.5 “*āramudūttiya appanai*” (the lord who fed the nectar). Oh [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who painstakingly helps even those who desire for worldly benefits after leaving the enjoyment in such divine feet. As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 19.31 “*apramēyō mahōdadi:*” (immeasurable great ocean), emperumān who took on the immeasurable great ocean and made it look like a small pit of water and churned it.
- *puḷ Ur kodiyānē****e*** – Oh one who has periya tiruvadi (garudāḻvār) as vehicle and flag to visit those who are affectionate towards you! Vehicle helps him reach where his devotees are and garudāḻvār becomes the flag to help the devotees know his arrival from distance and sustain themselves. \[In connection with previous phrase of “*āḻ kadalaik kadaindāy*“\] This is also explained as [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) arriving on garuda to present the nectar in a jug like container when the dēvas (celestial beings) became tired churning the ocean to fetch the nectar from it.
- *koṇḍal vaṇṇā* – When he appeared on garuda, he resembled a blackish cloud trying to devour mēru mountain. mahābhāratam “*neelam mērāvivāmbhudam*” (Like a water laden cloud on top of the mēru mountain).
- *aṇḍattu umbaril* – Looking at his sitting posture on garudāḻvār, he surely is to be believed as the supreme lord. From his posture, it is clear that his \[immeasurable\] wealth is greater than the measurable wealth of brahmā et al. Like his beauty, his wealth is attractive too.
- *enṟu kidakkum* – When one starts saying “*nediyānē*“, one cannot stop saying that they desire to see him or hear him. Rather one would keep saying “*nediyānē****e***!” \[with a long syllable\] extending the tone continuously, like staying in the same posture and getting bed-sours. His heart is said to be like śrī bharatāḻvān who cried out in a meek voice “āryā!” and remained silent as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 99.88 “*uktvāryēti sakrut dīnam punarnōvāca kincana*“.
- *en nenjamē* – Unlike in tiruvāimoḻi 5.3.5 “*kodiya en nenjam*” (my cruel heart) \[where āḻvār praises his heart\], he is not praising his heart here. He says “While my heart do what I did \[desire for [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)\], what can I do to relieve it’s agony?”. When asked “Should you not wait for your husband \[lord\] to bless you with his visit?”, āḻvār replies “How can I pacify my heart which is very eager to see him?”.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.
