## 3.8.2. Nenjame

*nenjamē nīḷ nagarāga irunda en tanjanē! taṇṇilangaikkiṟaiyaic ceṟṟa nanjanē! jñālam koḷvān kuṟaḷāgiya vanjanē! ennum eppōdum en vāsagamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

en vāsagam – my speech; eppōdum – always; nenjamē – heart; nīḷ nagarāga – considering it as a big divine city; irunda – (due to his) residing; en tanjanē – Oh one who is a good companion!; taṇ – cool (like a bee-hive which is filled with bees, the place which is filled with rākśasas); ilangaikku – for lankā; iṟaiyai – rāvaṇa who is the leader; ceṟṟa – finished; nanjanē – Oh one who became like a poison!; jñālam – earth; koḷvān – to make it fully exist for him; kuṟaḷ āgiya – one assumed the form of a vāmana; vanjanē – Oh mischievous one!; ennum – will keep saying

**Перевод:**

**My speech will always keep saying “Oh one who is a good companion due to his residing in my heart, considering it as a big divine city! Oh one who became like a poison and finished rāvaṇa, the leader of cool lankā! Oh mischievous one who assumed the form of a vāmana to make the earth fully exist for him (after eliminating the pride of mahābali)”.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In second pāsuram – āḻvār mercifully explains the desire of his vāk indriyam (organ for speech) which is subsequent to manas (mind) as said in “mana: pūrvō vāguttara:” (thoughts in mind culminate into speech).*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “My speech always explains his nature of eliminating the hurdles and making me exist fully for him”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Second pāsuram. āḻvār says “As said in ‘mana: pūrvō vāguttara:‘, vāk (speech) which is subsequent to manas \[thoughts in mind\], speech desired for the actions of mind and itself”. nenjamē nīḷ nagarāga irunda en tanjanē! taṇṇilangaikkiṟaiyaic ceṟṟa nanjanē! jñālam koḷvān kuṟaḷāgiya vanjanē! ennum eppōdum en vāsagamē*

- *nenjamē* … – This is the word of speech. Speech said “Would you always stay in the heart? Why don’t you spend some time with me too?”.  By saying nenjamē (exclusively in heart), [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) wonders “How other senses, paramapadam, kśīrābdi etc abodes, long for him in his absence?”. As said in periya tiruvantādi 68 “*kallum kanai kadalum vaikiunda vānādum pul enṟu oḻindanakol ēpāvam*” (Alas! (after entering my heart) looks like he is considering tiruvēnkatam, kśīrābdi, the upper world called as paramapadam etc as insignificant), what is happening to paramapadam and his presence there? Whatever attachment he has in “*kalangāp perunagar*” (big city which is never disturbed – mūnṟām tiruvantādi 51), he shows the same in āḻvār’s heart. His unfulfilled desires in paramapadam are fulfilled here only. He considered āḻvār’s heart as the deficit-less abode. Only due to that \[residing in the heart with full satisfaction and ignoring other abodes\], his speech calls out for him.
- *en tanjanē* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) shows gratitude to [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) for making him call out in this manner. Among samsāris (materialistic people), there is none who calls out for emperumān like this. Because of this thoughts in his heart, he cries out for emperumān like this.
- *taṇ ilangai* … – Oh one who became a poison to rāvaṇa who is the leader of beautiful lankā, by destroying him! tiruvadi (hanuman), who is never attracted and is totally detached to anything materialistic, himself saw the beauty of lankā and said as in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 49.17 “*ahō vīryam ahō dairyam ahō satvam ahō dyuti:*” (How valiant! How brave! How strong! How radiant!) \[nampiḷḷai’s words “tiruvadi maditta aiśvaryamiṟē” (opulence respected by hanuman himself)\]. taṇmai indicates beauty.
- *jñālam* … – Oh one who knows the knack to retrieve the earth which was snatched by mahābali! [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) did not cut off his head like he did to rāvaṇa since mahābali had a little bit of audāryam (generosity). It is the knack of sarvēśvaran (supreme lord) himself assuming the form of a needy person and getting back the kingdom to indra considering “he (mahābali) had a pseudo virtue (of generosity)”.
- *vanjanē* – The mischief of assuming the form of a dwarf and cheating mahābali, showing his small feet asking as in tiruvāimoḻi 3.8.9 “*mūvadi*” (just three steps), measuring with huge feet, covering everything in two steps, imprisoned mahābali using the third step. Here [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says “*koḷvān*” (emperumān will keep it) since emperumān considers indra’s gain as his own. My speech is repeatedly speaking about this mischief. After meditating upon this mischief, my heart is not even desiring for śrī rāma’s honesty. In rāmāvatāram, emperumān ensured that his greatness is not compromised; here (in vāmanāvatāram) he gave up his own greatness \[to help indra\].
- *eppōdum* – Like a hungry person will say “food! food!” \[[āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying this always\].

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.8.3. Vasagame etta

*vāsagamē ētta aruḷ seyyum vānavar tam nāyaganēe! nāḷ iḷam tingaḷaik kōḷ viduttu vēyagam pāl veṇṇey toduvuṇḍa ān āyar tāyavanēe! enṟu tadavum en kaigaḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vāsagamē – speech only; ētta – to praise; (adukkē) aruḷ seyyum – one who blesses (that only); vānavar tam – (as a result of that) to be glorified by nityasūris; nāyaganē – Oh one who is the controller!; nāḷ – being fresh every day; iḷam tingaḷ – young rising moon; kōḷ – pleasing radiance; viduttu – revealing (like the moon will rise softly, releasing the beautiful shining smile (of the intact teeth) and the beauty of the lips); vēyagam pāl – placed inside bamboo hut; veṇṇey – butter; toduvu uṇḍa – due to stealing and consuming it; An āyar – covherds; tāyavanē – one who nurtures their existence etc; enṟu – saying so; en kaigaḷ – my hands; tadavum – (where he performed his act of stealing) will seek out to touch him

**Перевод:**

**Oh controller of nityasūris who glorify you, due to your blessing my mouth/speech to praise you! Oh nurturer of the existence etc of covherds by stealing and consuming the butter placed inside bamboo hut with the light generated by the pleasing radiance of the young rising moon which is fresh everyday \[here fresh young rising moon is an example for kriṣṇa’s shining teeth\]! Saying these, my hands will seek out to touch you.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In third pāsuram – āḻvār mercifully explains the desire of his hands for his activities and the activities of his mouth/speech.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “My hands analyze kriṣṇa who likes the possessions of his devotees due to great love towards them”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. vāsagamē ētta aruḷ seyyum vānavar tam nāyaganēe! nāḷ iḷam tingaḷaik kōḷ viduttu vēyagam pāl veṇṇey toduvuṇḍa An āyar tāyavanēe! enṟu tadavum en kaigaḷē*

- *vāsagamē ētta* … – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s hands thought “Why should speech alone praise? Can I not praise once?”. Did my speech offer anything special to you to be able to praise you who remains detached \[without any expectation\] even after being praised by nityasūris as said in rig vēdam \[viṣṇu sūktam\] “… *vipanyava:* …” (those who are wise and have the nature of praising \[him\] constantly, reach that supreme abode of viṣṇu). Though he has no expectation, he became desirous to be praised by speech. Is he manifesting that detachment towards me now? Also explained as – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who blessed the speech to naturally praise him as done by nityasūris.
- *nāḷ iḷam tingaḷaik kōḷ viduttu* – He entered in to the huts to steal cow’s butter as said in periya tirumoḻi 4.4.3 “*padaladaitta siṟu kurambai nuḻaindu pukkup pasu veṇṇey kaḷavu kāṇa*“. Butter is usually preserved in a container that is secured in a rope hanging from the ceiling; due to his own dark complexion and the darkness of the place, he would search for the pots by touch – when his hand touches the pot, he would feel excited and smile – at that time his shining teeth would help him as the lamp and would eat the butter joyfully. When some one arrives, he would immediately close his mouth and darkness will surround the place again. \[Why would he close his mouth?\] Since the presence of others is unfavourable for him, he would become upset and stop smiling by closing his mouth. \[What happens to the shining kaustuba jewel in his chest?\] He would cover that with his hands too. His smile (teeth) resembles a fresh moon. periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 1.7.2 “*sekkaridai nunik kombil tōnṟum siṟupiṟai muḷaip pōl nakka senduvar vāyt tiṇṇai mīdē naḷir veṇpal muḷaiyilaga*” ([emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s cool white teeth inside the raised lips which resemble a crescent which appears on a stick In the reddish sky (early evening)). Instead of saying “*tingaḷ pōl*“, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) just said “*tingaḷ*” – this type of usage is called muṟṟuvamai in tamiḻ \[where the example is super-imposed in the object that is explained\]; this is similar to tiruvāimoḻi 6.9.9 “*tāvi vaiyam koṇḍa tadam tāmarai*” (the vast lotus \[instead of saying lotus like feet\] that stretched and accepted the earth).
- *kōl viduttu* – releasing the radiance; stops covering the teeth with his lips.
- *vēy agam* – house/hut built using bamboo.
- *pāl veṇṇēy toduvuṇḍa* – Mercifully stole and ate the milk and butter from those places \[pāl – milk\].  Also explained as – the butter in the house \[pāl – place\].
- *vēy agam pāl veṇṇey toduvuṇḍa* – After spying the place, he went in to the house, stole the butter and mercifully consumed it. vēyttu – spying and checking the situation. Naturally, one will first spy the place before stealing from there \[so vēyttu as spying seems more appropriate than vēy as bamboo\]. His stealing of butter is explained in detail by [tirumangai āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/thirumangai-azhwar/) in siṟiya tirumadal starting with “*pōrār vēḷ*“.
- *An āyar tāyavanē enṟu* – Saying “Oh one who is caring like a mother for the covherds!”.
- *tadavum en kaigaḷ* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) searching to catch [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) red-handed while he enters the house for stealing. Alternatively – when āḻvār starts meditating upon emperumān’s butter stealing act, his hands are not able to locate his eye. śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 42.34 “*rāmam mē anugatā druśti:*” (daśarata says to kausalyā – My vision followed rāma to the forest). Can we retrieve that which was consumed by the ocean? How will my eyes which waited for 60000 years \[to see rāma\] return to me? \[Still, are they not your eyes?\] When something gets attached to an apt target, is there any point arguing based on ownership? “*adyāpi*” (even now) when their (eyes’) help is needed, they are not here to help. Even if I cannot see him, at least I will touch you who gave birth to him and feel his presence.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.8.4. Kaigalal ara

*kaigaḷāl ārat toḻudu toḻudunnai vaigalum māttiraip pōdum ōr vīdinṟip pai koḷ pāmbēṟi uṟai paranē! unnai mey koḷḷak kāṇa virumbum en kaṇgaḷē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

en kaṇgaḷ – my eyes; kaigaḷāl – with my hands; unnai – you; Ara toḻudu toḻudu – worship you fully many times; vaigalum – forever; ōr māttiraip pōdum – even a moment; vīdu inṟi – without break; paikoḷ – having expanded hoods; pāmbu ēṟi uṟai – one who is permanently lying on tiruvanantāḻvān (ādiśēśa); paranē – oh supreme lord!; unnai – you; mey koḷḷak kāṇa – to see in front of me; virumbum – desire

**Перевод:**

**Oh supreme lord who is permanently lying on tiruvanantāḻvān (ādiśēśa) having expanded hoods! My eyes worship you with my hands fully many times forever without a break even for a moment and desire to see you in front of me.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In fourth pāsuram – āḻvār says “My eyes say ‘we want the activities of hands and our own activity of seeing'”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “my eyes desire to see the anantaśāyi (one who is lying on ādiśēśa) root of such incarnations”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. kaigaḷāl ārat toḻudu toḻudunnai vaigalum māttiraip pōdum ōr vīdinṟip pai koḷ pāmbēṟi uṟai paranē! unnai mey koḷḷak kāṇa virumbum en kaṇgaḷē!*

- *kaigaḷāl* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s hands not vorśipping [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is like a lover-girl with well-developed breasts which were not touched by her lover-boy. He desires to perform the natural activity of his hands \[which is vorśipping emperumān\]. śrī viṣṇu darmam “*vicitrā dēhasampattir īśvarāya nivēditum \| pūrvamēva krutā brahman hastapādādisamyutā \|\|*” (Oh brāhmaṇa! To offer oneself and other materials, [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) previously got connected to the amazing body with hands and legs).
- *ārat toḻudu* – Like it is said “*pasiyar vayiṟ* ***Ara*** *uṇṇa*” (a hungry man ate to his **full satisfaction**), The hands that desire to worship you but remain grief-stricken with that unfulfilled desire, worship you to their full satisfaction. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) desires to praise to the mouth’s satisfaction and serve to the hands’ satisfaction. Like it is natural for the mouth to praise, it is natural for the hands to worship [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/).
- *toḻudu toḻudu* – \[keep vorśipping\] When an act is done to accomplish a particular ulterior goal, the act will stop once the goal is accomplished. When an act is performed with the thought that it is the means, it will stop when the goal is accomplished. Instead, this is done as the main routine activity. When explaining the nature of muktātmās (liberated souls), nārāyaṇīyam “*muktānām lakśaṇam hyētat*” is the same as the residents of śvēta dvīpam (milk ocean) as said in the same ślōkam “*nityānjali putā:*” (having hands in anjali posture always). Their state would be similar to the joyful state of a hungry man eating as said in the same ślōkam “*hruśtā:*” (joyful). “*nama ityēva vādina:*” – they will always be saying “*nama:*“.
- *unnai* – Like the [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) which sustains by vorśipping you, who sustains by having them worship you. You who made my hands worship you. You who is apt to be vorśipped. manu smriti 4.6 “*sēvā śvavrutti:*” (serving others is dog’s job) is explained for serving worldly people. \[But here\] You who cannot sustain yourself without the worship from me, who cannot sustain without vorśipping you.
- *vaigalum* … – Daily. In every day, without a break for even a moment. Instead of vorśipping once a day and remaining free other times, vorśipping every moment. This is not like nityāgnihōtri (one who performs agnihōtram every day – but this ritual is only done at specific time and not always) \[here nitya/vaigalum means every moment of every day\].
- *pai koḷ* … – Here the greatness and attraction to accept the worship and the nature of the vorśipper are explained. Due to lying on tiruvanantāḻvān (ādiśēśa) whose hoods are expanded due to coming in contact with the divine body of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), emperumān resembles a precious stone pressed on a gold plate – as a result, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) calls him “*paran*” (supreme). anantaśāyi (one lying on ādiśēśa) is the [sarvēśvaran](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) (supreme lord). āḻvār desires for the result explained in paryanka vidyā (a type of upāsanam).
- *unnai* – You who is apt and enjoyable.
- *mey koḷḷāk kāṇa* – To see you truly. Unlike previous instances where [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s divine internal vision is feeling as though emperumān is right in front of him and when āḻvār seeks out to embrace him, he is not present and thus cries out, here āḻvār seeks for [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s real presence.
- *virumbum* – desired for that.
- *en kaṇgaḷē* – My eyes desired to worship him and to see him. Like śrī bharatāḻvān praised iḷaiya perumāḷ (lakśmaṇa) for following śrī rāma, and himself desired for lakśmaṇa’s activities too.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.8.5. Kangalal kana

*kaṇgaḷāl kāṇa varum kolen(ṟu) āsaiyāl maṇ koṇḍa vāmanan ēṟa magiḻndu sel paṇ koṇḍa puḷḷin siṟagoli bāvittut tiṇ koḷḷa ōrkkum kidandu en sevigaḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kaṇgaḷāl – with eyes (which are the faculty for seeing); kāṇa – to see in front; varum kol – would he come?; enṟu – that; āsaiyāl – with desire; maṇ koṇḍa – accepting earth (going as a needy person to accept his own property); vāmanan – śrī vamānan; ēṟa – climbing (to show himself to those who desire to see him); magiḻndu – (as a result of that) being pleased; sel – one who can move around; puḷḷin – periya tiruvadi’s (garuda’s); paṇ koḷ – that which has the tune of sāma vēdam; siṟagoli – sound of the flapping of the wings; bāvittu – meditating upon; en sevigaḷ – my ears; kidandu – remaining (attracted); tiṇ koḷḷa – firmly; ōrkkum – think about that

**Перевод:**

**śrī vāmanan who accepted the earth, climbs on garudāḻvār who is pleased \[due to that climbing\] and moves around with his wings flapping with the tune of sāma vēdam; meditating upon that sound, my ears firmly remain thinking about that desire “would he come in front of me to be seen by my eyes?”. “paṇ koṇḍa” is also explained as “adorned with ornaments” \[paṇ also means ornaments\].**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In fifth pāsuram – āḻvār says “The ear, sensory organ for hearing says ‘I want to see and hear'”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “My ears desire to see him and when he arrives to bless me with his audience, they also desire to hear the flapping sound of the wings of periya tiruvadi (garudāḻvār)”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*kaṇgaḷāl kāṇa varum kolen(ṟu) āsaiyāl maṇ koṇḍa vāmanan ēṟa magiḻndu sel paṇ koṇḍa puḷḷin siṟagoli bāvittut tiṇ koḷḷa ōrkkum kidandu en sevigaḷē*

- *kaṇgaḷāl …* – Due to the desire of his eyes which longed to see [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), would he come to be seen by those eyes? emperumān’s distinguished greatness such that everyone will patiently wait to see him. “Will the apt object for the sight arrive to be seen?” as said in subālōpaniśat “*cakśuśca draśtavyanca nārāyaṇa:*” (the eyes which are seeing and that which is seen are nārāyaṇa).

Will he come as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 40.3 “*gātraiśśōkābhikarśitai:*” (sītā pirātti said “you bless me so that I who is greatly attached to śrī rāma, can touch the tiger among men śrī rāma, with my body parts which are very weak) \[Will the insentient sensory organs crave for his arrival?\]. No.

- *āsaiyāl* – It is due to my desire. Alternatively, it is explained as [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) being confident that [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) will arrive seeing āḻvār’s desire. \[Is the desire sufficient to make him come?\] In bhagavat viśayam, whatever is done, that is sufficient; this is explained in [śrī bhagavat gītā 2.40](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/2-40/) “*nēhābhikramanāśōsti*” (no loss for the efforts that are begun).
- *maṇ koṇḍa vāmanan* – āḻvār is saying “vāmana” even after accepting the earth \[while he became trivikrama at that time\]; like confidential associates would call a crowned king with his pet names which were there before being crowned, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says vāmana even after his transformation into trivikrama, due to his great attachment in that form.
- *ēṟa magiḻndu sel* – garudāḻvār moving around blissfully to express his joy after [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) climbing on him.
- *paṇ koṇḍa puḷ* – paṇ indicates “decoration for the vāhanam (vehicle)”; also, since he is vēdātmā (embodiment of vēdam), paṇ also indicates the musical portions of sāma vēdam such as bruhadrantara etc.
- *siṟagoli bāvittu* – meditating upon the flapping sound of the wings
- *tiṇ koḷḷa ōrkkum* – Even if some one staying in front of him and say something, his ears do not hear them; they only hear the flapping sound of the wings. pakhsapātam towards that is the reason \[double meaning – pakśapātam means partiality; pakśa also indicates wings, so attachment towards wings\].

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.8.6. Sevigalal ara

*sevigaḷāl āra nin kīrttik kani ennum kavigaḷē kālap paṇ tēn uṟaippat tuṟṟup puviyin mēl pon nedum sakkarattunnaiyē avivinṟi ādarikkum enadāviyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

enadu – impatient due to the delay, my; āvi – prāṇa (vital air); nin – your; kīrtti kani – the ripen fruit of your glories; ennum – explained as; kavigaḷē – poems; kālam paṇ – tune/music matching the season; tēn – in honey; uṟaippa – in abundance; tuṟṟu – enjoyed; sevigaḷālē – through the ears; Ara – to fully enjoy; puviyiun mēl – on earth; pon – attractive; nedu – unsurpassed enjoyment; sakkarattu – having divine chakra; unnaiyē – you only; avivu inṟi – without any break; ādarikkum – will engage

**Перевод:**

**emperumān has attractive sudarśana chakra which has unsurpassed enjoyment; my prāṇa (vital air) which is impatient due to the delay \[in your (emperumān’s) arrival\] will engage in you to enjoy the poems which are said as the ripen fruit of your glories and are enjoyed with abundance of honey which is the tune/music matching the season, through the ears.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In sixth pāsuram – āḻvār says “My prāṇa (vital air) desires to hear your glories”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “My prāṇa desires to enjoy the combination of his beautiful hand and tiruvāḻi (sudarśana chakra)”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. bhagavān‘s glories is such that one would patiently wait and hear it. sevigaḷāl Ara nin kīrttik kani ennum kavigaḷē kālap paṇ tēn uṟaippat tuṟṟup puviyin mēl pon nedum sakkarattunnaiyē avivinṟi ādarikkum enadāviyē*

- *sevigaḷāl Ara* – for the full satisfaction of the ears.
- *nin kīrttik kani ennum kavigaḷē* – the poems which are like ripen fruits which are in the form of glorification. Due to the extreme enjoyment, instead of saying the poems which are like fruits, it is said that, ripen fruit became a poem.
- *kālam* … – Like proud princes will eat the best fruits soaked in honey, mixing your glories in the form of a fruit with the music matching the season in the form of honey, so that there is more honey than fruit.
- *tuṟṟu* – enjoying that.

When asked “īsn’t this experience found in paramapadam only?”,

- *puviyin mēl* – \[In this earth itself.\] When some one is hungry in one place, he cannot be fed elsewhere. One should be given food, where he is hungry.
- *pon nedum sakkaram* – As the place was set to be here, the matter of joy should also remain the same \[bhagavān from paramapadam\]. \[But would bhagavān have chakra in his hand in paramapadam?\] śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 114.15 “*tamasa: paramō dātā śankacakragadādara:*” (the one who resides in paramapadam which is beyond the material realm, the one who holds Sanka (conch), chakra (disc), gadā (maze)) – only you who is identified as having the attractive, endlessly enjoyable divine chakra.
- *avivinṟi ādarikkum* – engaged in him without any break. Instead of realizing you are difficult to attain, my prāṇa desired for you like an easily attainable aspect.
- *enadu āviyē* – My prāṇa will not listen when said “we should wait for [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) to come at his own will”. It is of the nature as said in tiruvāimoḻi 9.9.6 “*avan aruḷ perum aḷavil nillādu*” (My prāṇa cannot wait for him to come and give his mercy).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.8.7. Aviye aramude

*āviyē! āramudē! ennai āḷudait tūvi am puḷ udaiyāy! sudar nēmiyāy! pāviyēn nenjam pulambap pala kālum kūviyum kāṇap peṟēn una kōlamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

āviyē – being the (sustaining) prāṇa (vital air) (which will finish in separation); Ar – fully; amudē – eternally enjoyable; ennai āḷudai – one who is fit to enslave me; am tūvi – having beautiful wings; puḷ – periya tiruvadi (garudāḻvār); udaiyāy – having as vehicle; sudar – (that which will eliminate the enemies) radiant; nēmiyāya – one who holds the tiruvāḻi (divine sudarśana chakra); un – your; kōlam – (endlessly enjoyable) beautiful form; pāviyēn – greatly sinful me; nenjam – my heart; pulamba – call out with desire; pala kālam – many times; kūviyum – when I called out; kāṇap peṟēn – have not seen and enjoyed

**Перевод:**

**Oh one who is my prāṇa, one who is fully and eternally enjoyable, one who has beautifully winged periya tiruvadi (garudāḻvār) as his vehicle to enslave me, who holds the radiant divine chakra! The heart of greatly sinful me calls out for you and due to that great desire, even after calling out many times, I have not seen and enjoyed you.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In seventh pāsuram – āḻvār says “Being a great sinner, I who is not even able to fulfil the craving of my heart, could not see your beauty even after calling out for many days”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār explains about his loss like the loss of his sensory organs in not experiencing emperumān saying “I am unable to enjoy such easily approachable, enjoyable you”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. Previously āḻvār explained the craving of his senses; here, he explains his own craving and the craving of his senses. āviyē! āramudē! ennai āḷudait tūvi am puḷ udaiyāy! sudar nēmiyāy! pāviyēn nenjam pulambap pala kālum kūviyum kāṇap peṟēn una kōlamē*

- *āviyē* – When asked “Even if the desire is so much, should you not bear the agony until the lord arrives?”, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says “How can I be without my prāṇa (vital air)?”. As said in [tiruvāimoḻi 2.3.4](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/02/thiruvaimozhi-2-3-4-enadhu-aviyul/) “*āviyāviyum nī*” (You are the sustaining soul for myself), he is the ātmā \[sustaining force\].
- *āramudē* – When he is both dāraka (sustaining aspect) and bhōjña (reliśable aspect), how can I be without him? āramudu – fully pure nectar. This nectar is different from the nectar acquired by dēvas \[while churning the milk ocean\]; thinking about him every moment is nectarean; he is explained in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.6.6](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/08/thiruvaimozhi-1-6-6-amutham-amarargatku/) as “*amudilum āṟṟa iniyan*” (sweeter than nectar).
- *ennai* … – The same garudāḻvār who brought nectar for his mother vinatā, brings this nectar ([emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)) too. One who enslaved me by manifesting his posture on periya tiruvadi. Alternatively – it can also be explained as “*ennai āḷudait tūvi am puḷ*” (the beautiful garuda who can rule me). This is because he considers himself as a servitor of those who unites him with [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) \[as garuda brings bhagavān to [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/), āḻvār feels indebted to garuda\]. When there is some one ready to bring emperumān who sustains and gives utmost joy, is there any reason to be patient?
- *sudar nēmiyāy* – sudarśana chakra is the tool both for his beauty and to eliminate the enemies. While coming \[on garuda\], he has the tool right on his hand to eliminate any hurdle that come in the way.
- *pāviyēn* – Those who desire for bhagavān have no loss as said in mūnṟām tiruvantādi 27 “*ārē tuyar uḻandār*” (Those devotees of kśīrābdi nātan, even if they had committed sins which cause sorrow, they have not experienced the results of such sorrows) \[Still since I am very sinful, I lost the opportunity to see emperumān and am suffering\].
- *pāviyēn nenjam* – Due to being my \[I who am very sinful\] heart, it lost the experience of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/). As said in perumāḷ tirumoḻi 7.3 “*nandan peṟṟanan nal vinai illā nangaḷ kōn vasudēvan peṟṟilanē*” (nandagōpa had the fortune of raising you and vasudēva who is the husband of me who has no virtues, lost that) – though both nandagōpa and vasudēva are both fathers to kriṣṇa, due to being married to me who has no virtues, śrī vasudēva lost the opportunity to raise kriṣṇa – similarly due to the heart being mine, it lost the opportunity to enjoy emperumān. It is said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 38.48 “… *mamaiva duśkrutam kincit …*” (sītā pirātti telling hanuman – It is due to my  great misdeeds, I am being neglected by the great warriors śrī rāma and lakśmaṇa).
- *pulamba* – Heart crying out due to the loss of not having seen [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/). Like it is said in mudal tiruvantādi 56 “*kadik kamalattuḷ irundum kāṇgilān*” (brahmā who is sitting right inside the lotus flower which is rooted in [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s naval, is not seeing bhagavān), the heart is crying out for the emperumān who is seated in the heart as said in mūnṟām tiruvantādi 81 “*nenjattup pērādu niṟkum perumān*” (the great lord who stays in the heart firmly).
- *palakālum* – emperumān who arrived just on hearing the single scream of gajēndrāḻvān, did not arrive even after my heart crying out many times.
- *kūviyum kāṇap peṟēn* – Neither my desire was fulfilled; nor my svarūpam (true nature) was preserved. I did not conduct myself as stated in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 9.30 “… *tat tasya sadruśam bhavēt*“; I also did not acquire the result of reaching out to my dear lover \[as done by uśā who united with anirudda by reaching out to him\]. I destroyed both my nature \[by crossing my limits and calling out for him\] and his nature also \[since he did not come on hearing my call\]. I destroyed his nīrmai \[that he is very merciful and will arrive on hearing the cry of his devotees\] and my śēśatvam \[of being surrendered to him fully\]. I destroyed his īśvaratva \[being the controller\] and my īśitavyatva \[being the controlled\] is also lost. Now, What is there to accept? Who is there to give?
- *una kōlamē* – The distinguished beauty of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), which makes [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) conduct himself in such a way that damages the nature of both [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) and himself \[as explained in the previous point in detail\]. Is bhagavān so cheap that, while in separation from him, we can easily spend our time by sleeping, playing chess etc? It is difficult to sleep or spend the time being awake as said in tiruviruttam 97 “*uṇḍō kaṇgaḷ tunjudal*” (will the eyes close ever?) and in periya tiruvantādi 86 “*en ninaindu pōkkuvar ippōdu*” (how will they spend their time?) respectively.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.8.8. Kolame

*kōlamē(y) tāmaraik kaṇṇādōr anjana neelamē! niṟu enadāviyai īrginṟa seelamē! senṟu sellādana munnilām kālamē! unnai ennāḷ kaṇḍu koḷvanē?*

**Пословный перевод:**

kōlamē – very pleasant (like having specifically decorated form); tāmarai – like a lotus flower; kaṇṇadu – having eyes; ōr – unparalleled; anjanam – black pigment; neelamē – having form which is an embodiment of blackish-blue complexion; ninṟu – firmly standing; enadu āviyai – my soul; īrginṟa – cuts; seelamē – having qualities \[such as simplicity\] as his identity; senṟu – past times which are gone; sellādana – future times which are yet to occur; munnilām kālamē – one who is the controller of the present times as well; unnai – (such) you; ennāḷ – when; kaṇḍu koḷvan – will I see and enjoy?

**Перевод:**

**Oh emperumān who is very pleasant to see, who has lotus like flowers, who is having an unparalleled form which is an embodiment of blackish-blue complexion of black pigment, having as his identity, qualities \[such as simplicity\] of cutting my soul by standing firmly, who is the controller of past, future and present times! when will I see and enjoy (such) you?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In eighth pāsuram – āḻvār says “Even if you ask ‘should the time not be right for me to fulfil your desire?’, that time is also under your control. Such being the case, how can I miss out on this experience?”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār asks “When will I see and enjoy you who have enjoyable beauty etc?”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. kōlamē(y) tāmaraik kaṇṇādōr anjana neelamē! niṟu enadāviyai īrginṟa seelamē! senṟu sellādana munnilām kālamē! unnai ennāḷ kaṇḍu koḷvanē?*

- *kōlamē* – Instead of being two aspects – beauty and the object which hosts such beauty, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is being the embodiment of beauty. In śāstram, jñātā \[knover\] is said as jñānam \[knowledge\] due to *tadguṇasāratvam* \[when an entity is fully pervaded by a particular attribute, the entity is called as the attribute itself – when [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)‘s primary quality is jñānam, ātmā itself is at times cited in śāstram as jñānam\]; in such manner, when there is abundance of beauty, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) wanting to identify emperumān with his beauty, calls him “kōlamē!” (Oh beauty!).
- *tāmarai* … – The nature of the divine body of emperumān which is the abode of such beauty. That too, the beautiful nature of each part of the divine body \[since lotus like eyes are specifically addressed\]. Oh one who has beautiful eyes which is in some sense comparable to the lotus flower due to the reddish colour, blossomed form and tenderness.
- *anjana neelamē* – anjanamē (oh one who is like black pigment)! neelamē (Oh one who is having dark blue complexion)! Since one example is not sufficient to explain his beauty, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is highlighting with various aspects. \[Alternatively\] One who is having the dark blue complexion of black pigment as his divine body.

Though he has beautiful form, would he not have attachment in his heart?

- *ninṟu* … – One who is having qualities such as simplicity which cuts my heart in separation – even if I can forget his divine beauty, I cannot forget his qualities! [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is thinking about the simplicity of [arcāvatāram](http://ponnadi.blogspot.in/p/archavathara-anubhavam.html) which was identified by him in tiruvāimoḻi 3.6.9 “*nenjināl ninaippān yavan avan āgum nīḷ kadal vaṇṇan*” (sea (blackish blue) coloured [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who assumes the forms sought out by his devotees) in tiruvāimoḻi 3.6 “*seyya tāmaraik kaṇṇan*” decad. Alternatively, āḻvār can be said to be thinking about emperumān’s simplicity which let āḻvār unite with emperumān in tiruvāimoḻi 1.5 “*vaḷavēḻulagu*” decad.

Though emperumān has beauty and auspicious qualities, is there not a right time to attain him?

- *senṟu* … – īsn’t time under your control too? mahābhāratam udyōga parvam 68.13 “*kālasya ca hi mrutyōśca jangamastāvarasya ca \| īśatē bhagavānēka: satyamētadbravīmi tē*” (sanjaya says – [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is the only controller for time, yama, movable and immovable entities; I am telling you “this is truth only”). [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) was present before creation of objects, he is the controller for the kāla (time) which remains even after the destruction of all these objects and the creators and destroyers of such objects; \[does mrutyu indicate all destroyers or only yama\] all destroyers are indicated by the term mrutyu as said in katavallī 1.2 “*mrutyur yasyōpasēcanam*” (even the destroyers are consumed like pickle is consumed in the end) – mrutyu indicates destroyers. emperumān is the only one who is present before the creation of all objects during sruśti, being present even after destruction, being aware of everything always, controls the creators, created entities and the destroyers. There is no exaggeration in bhagavat viśayam as said in “*satyam …*“; When one is believed to be āpta (trustworthy), he/she won’t lie to those who believe in him/her. senṟu – past; sellādana – future; munnilām kālam – present.
- *kālamē* – Oh one who has the three times (past, present and future) at his disposal!
- *unnai* … – Your beauty and qualities does not let me leave you; you cannot avoid by saying “the time is not right”. This being the case, tell me, when will I see you? As promised for bharatāḻvān and arrived after 14 years as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 127.1 “*pūrṇē caturdaśē varśē pancamyām…*” (after completing 14 full years śrī rāma, elder brother of śrī lakśmaṇa arrived at bharadvāja maharishi’s āśramam on a pancami day and vorśipped the maharishi) – tell me that “You will see me on this particular day”.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.8.9. Kolvan nan

*koḷvan nān māvali! mūvadi tā enṟa kaḷvanē! kanjanai vanjittu vāṇanai uḷ vanmai tīra ōr āyiram tōḷ tuṇitta puḷ vallāy! unnai enjñānṟu porunduvanē?*

**Пословный перевод:**

māvali – ‘Oh mahābali!; nān – I; mūvadi koḷvan – will accept three feet \[of land\]; tā – give’; enṟa – saying so (attracted him by his childish speech); kaḷvanē – being mischievous; kanjanai vanjittu – cheating kamsa so that his mischievous thoughts will die with him; vāṇanai – bāṇa; uḷ vanmai tīra – to destroy his inner strength; ōr tōḷ āyiram – unparalleled thousand shoulders/hands; tuṇitta – cut off; puḷ vallāy – Oh rider of garuda!; unnai – you (who is able to eliminate the enemies of your devotees); enjñānṟu porunduvan – when will I reach?

**Перевод:**

**Oh rider of garuda who mischievously said to mahābali “Oh mahābali! I will accept three feet \[of land\]; give”, who was cheating kamsa so that his mischievous thoughts will die with him, who cut off the unparalleled thousand shoulders/hands of bāṇa to destroy his inner strength! When will reach you?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In ninth pāsuram – āḻvār says “When will I unite with you who knows how to protect his devotees and how to eliminate their hurdles?”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “When will reach you who is the eliminator of all hurdles?”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. koḷvan nān māvali! mūvadi tā enṟa kaḷvanē! kanjanai vanjittu vāṇanai uḷ vanmai tīra ōr āyiram tōḷ tuṇitta puḷ vallāy! unnai enjñānṟu porunduvanē?*

- *koḷvan* – Like the intelligent ways of people of kēraḷa, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) (going in to that region) said “I will not leave without accepting from you”. Alternatively – Looking at vāmana’s humble appearance, mahābali thought “It will be nice if he accepts something from me” and knowing mahābali’s thought, vāmana said “I will accept”. Another explanation – Looking at vāmana’s appearance which manifested nairapēkśyam (disregard, not expecting anything), mahābali thought “Would he not accept something from me?” and vāmana said “Don’t think like that. I am expecting something from you”.
- *nān* – Me who will not leave without accepting from you.
- *māvali* – Since he came to beg for alms on the same day he was born, vāmana does not know how to address benevolent kings \[so he calls out “māvali” by name\]. Before his birth, \[since there is no one greater than him\] there is no reason for him to glorify others; after taking birth, since he immediately arrived here for alms, he did not have time to learn \[so he called the king just by his name\]. As mahābali was only praised by others and never called by name, hearing his name, he noticed the beautiful child, and joyfully asked “What do you need?”.
- *mūvadi* – \[three feet of land\] Since those who accept from him never asked for such insignificant gift, he remained indifferent; vāmana said “Don’t be like that. Give me now”.
- *enṟa kaḷvanē* – indra surrendered to [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/). A generous person have snatched his kingdom; thinking “I cannot destroy him like I destroyed rāvaṇa et al since he is having some pseudo virtue \[of being generous\]. But indra is begging for my help; how can we solve this issue?”, he assumed the form of a needy person, and attracted mahābali by his beautiful appearance and sweet talks, even though mahābali advised by sukrācārya et al saying “he has arrived to fulfil the desire of dēvas” – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying “*kaḷvanē*” due to all these mischievous activities.
- *kanjanai vanjittu* – kamsa being kriṣṇa’s maternal uncle, placed the kuvalayāpīda elephant and the wrestlers at the gates as if they stood there by mistake, and stood there pretending to be crying for kriṣṇa; destroying all of those and such kamsa so that his evil thoughts are buried with him.
- *vāṇan* … – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who arrived for vaiyāḷi (a joy ride) on periya tiruvadi (garudāḻvār) and eliminated the inner strength immediately for bāṇa who held on to a kśudra dēvatā \[petty deity – rudra, the subordinate deity of emperumān for annihilation\]; bāṇāsura remained fearless after surrendering to rudra as pure devotees would be fearless after surrendering to [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) as said in taittiriya upaniśat “*ata sō’bhayangatō bhavati*” ([jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) remains fearless after attaining paramātmā).
- *āyiram tōḷ tuṇitta* – Since bāṇa became prideful, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) abandoned him \[and thereby his hands were cut off\].
- *puḷ vallāy* – Like *vāḷ vallāy* (expert in using the sword), *tōḷ vallāy* (expert in using the shoulder strength) etc., puḷ vallāy means one who is expert in riding the garuda.
- *unnai enjñānṟu porunduvanē* – After acquiring knowledge about the true nature of the self, it appears that we \[were once united with him and now we\] have separated from him. After acquiring true knowledge about self, being with the material body is like pirātti (sītā) remained in separation in aśōka vana (forest) as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 21.15 “*ananyā rāgavēṇāham*” (I am not different from śrī rāma, like the rays of the sun). After acquiring true knowledge, the state of being in this material world since time eternal, looks like something which occurred accidentally. One should not lose this opportunity looking at your nature of being omniscient, omnipotent and having many auspicious qualities; and my nature is such that I should not lose you; in this case, please tell me “when will I unite with you?”. While servitude is inseparably present in all ātmās, they are categorized as nitya (eternally free), mukta (once bound, now liberated) and badda (bound in the material relam) – similarly there is categorization in the divine consorts of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) also. “*ananyā*” (not different) can be said to all ātmās when the true nature of self is realized.  Once, he \[nanjīyar/nampiḷḷai\] casually explained this – \[When [śrī mahālakśmi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/) is explained as part of [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) in some parts of śāśtram, why is she identified as part of [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)s?\] When bhēdam (difference) is explained between [īśvara](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) and his consorts, it explains that like all jīvātmās who are different from bhagavān, the consorts are also different; where aikyam (unity/similarity) is explained, the ultimate state of pāratantriyam (total dependence) is explained \[i.e., their thoughts/speech/actions are perfectly harmonious with emperumān that there is no difference between them\].
- *āyiram tōḷ* … – bāṇāsura was bewildered and considered himself very strong due to having thousand hands. Oh emperumān who removed those extraneous hands and left him with just the apt (two) hands!”. He is said in tiruccanda viruttam as “*āyiram karam kaḻitta āadi māl*” (the primordial lord who eliminated the thousand hands).
- *unnai enjñānṟu porunduvanē* – When will I reach you who eliminated the hands of bāṇa and made him helpless?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.8.10. Porundiya ma marudu

*porundiya mā marudin idai pōya em perundagāy! un kaḻal kāṇiya pēduṟṟu varundi nān vāsaga mālai koṇḍu unnaiyē irundirun(du) ettanai kālam pulambuvanē?*

**Пословный перевод:**

porundiya – bushy; mā marudin idai – in between two huge arjuna (terminalia arjuna) trees; pōya – entered and effortlessly crushed them; em perum tagāy – oh great entity, who gave yourself to us!; un – your; kaḻal – reddish divine feet; kāṇiya – to see; pēdu – attachment; uṟṟu – one who is having; varundi – grieving; nān – I (who cannot wait any longer); vāsagam – words in praise of your glories; mālai koṇḍu – with a garland of such words; unnaiyē – exclusively towards you (who is perfectly enjoyable); irundu irundu – being weak; ettanai kālam – how long; pulambuvan – will call out?

**Перевод:**

**Oh great entity, who gave yourself to us by entering between the two arjuna trees and effortlessly crushing them! Being weak and having great attachment to see your reddish divine feet, feeling grieved \[due to not seeing them\], I submitted exclusively towards you, a garland of words in praise of your qualities. How long will I do this?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In tenth pāsuram – āḻvār says “How long will I who is won-over by your qualities, who is suffering due to not being able to see you, have to suffer?”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “How long will I have to call out to see the divine feet which effortlessly eliminate the hurdles?”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Tenth pāsuram. āḻvār says “How long will I, who is suffering in not being able to see you, have to call out for you?”. porundiya mā marudin idai pōya em perundagāy! un kaḻal kāṇiya pēduṟṟu varundi nān vāsaga mālai koṇḍu unnaiyē irundirun(du) ettanai kālam pulambuvanē?*

- *porundiya mā marudu* – marudu (arjuna tree), mā marudu (big arjuna tree), porundiya mā marudu (big bushy tree). By *marudu*, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) indicates a tree; as said in tirumālai 27 “*marangaḷ pōl valiya nenjam*” (hardened heart like trees), for hardness, tree is usually cited as example; by this – āḻvār indicates the hardness of the heart; mā indicates black color which highlights anger. Alternatively mā indicates hugeness. That is, without anyone doing anything, it is ready to fall \[and kill\]. porundiya is also explained as awaiting patiently to complete the particular task – the great arjuna tree which is waiting to complete its task. The like mindedness of both the trees \[the asuras who are standing in the form of the two trees\]  is explained.  Thus, being uniformly focussed on their task, having anger, and having hardened hearts which do not soften even after seeing kriṣṇa.
- *idai pōy* – While it is fearful to even approach them, he entered them casually as if it is an open hole in a single tree.
- *pōya em perum tagāy* – Oh the great one who gave yourself who is the lord by entering the trees!
- *un kaḻal* … – As said in “*tata: katakatāśabdsamākarṇanatatpara:*” (being joyful after hearing the sound of the trees falling), \[[āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)\] desiring to see the divine feet of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) which resemble the complexion of his reddish eyes which was expanded \[in amazement\] in seeing the falling trees after hearing the sound of the same. The sage parāśara greatly desired to see the divine reddish eyes as said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 5.6 “… *jagāma kamalēkśaṇa:*” (When yaśōdā was busy with household chores, lotus-eyed kriṣṇa went through the arjuna trees); āḻvār desires to see the divine feet of the crawling kriṣṇa. He never leaves the divine feet of emperumān in all states. Everyone will search for their lifeline; āḻvār too searches for his lifeline \[emperumān’s lotus feet\].
- *pēduṟṟu* – being bewildered.
- *varundi* – the amount of grief will match the object which was lost \[since [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is great, the agony in missing him is also great\].
- *nān* – I who sustained myself by depending on your divine feet. I who will not sustain myself in separation of the same and will survive when I attain them as said in tiruvāimoḻi 2.9.1 “*nin semmā pāda paṟput talai sērttu ollai*” (At once, you place your divine lotus feet on my head).
- *vāsaga mālai koṇḍu* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) feels as if he is lifting and holding a mountain, by speaking a word in praise \[he is so weak and tender that he cannot even do that\].
- *unnai* – You, who cannot be comprehensively spoken about. taittiriya upaniśat ānandavalli “*yat vācō nivartantē aprāpya manasā saha*” (the words returned being unable to glorify [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) fully and even the mind cannot comprehend him).
- *irundu irundu* – When starting to say a word, before completing it, he needs to think about [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) for long time.
- *ettanai kālam pulambuvanē* – He will not utter a word as means to attain him; but he cannot stop speaking about him as part of the goal \[kainkaryam\]; āḻvār asks “what is the end for this?”.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.8.11. Pulambu sir

*pulambu sīr būmi aḷanda perumānai nalam koḷ sīr nan kurugūrc catakōpan sol valam koṇḍa āyirattuḷ ivaiyum ōr pattu ilangu vān yāvarum ēṟuvar sonnālē*

**Пословный перевод:**

pulambu sīr – having qualities that are praised (by everyone); būmi – world; aḷanda – measured; perumānai – sarvaēśvara; nalam koḷ – having auspiciousness (of attachment towards experiencing bhagavān); sīr – having qualities such as jñāna (knowledge) etc; nal – wonderful; kurugūr – leader of āḻvārtirungari; śatakōpan – nammāḻvār; sol – mercifully spoken by; valam koṇḍa āyirattuḷ – among the thousand pāsurams which have the strength of conveying the meanings; ōr – unparalleled; ivai pattum – this decad; sonnāl – if recited; yāvarum – everyone; ilangu vān – in radiant paramapadam; ēṟuvar – will ascend

**Перевод:**

**sarvēśvara (supreme lord) who is having qualities that are praised (by everyone) measured the world; nammāḻvār who is having auspicious qualities such as jñāna etc and is the leader of the wonderful āḻvārtirungari, mercifully spoke the thousand pāsurams which have the strength of conveying the meanings on such emperumān; if this unparalleled decad among those thousand pāsurams is recited, everyone (who recites them) will ascend to the radiant paramapadam.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In  the end – āḻvār says “Any one who learned and memorized just the pāsurams in this decad, as desired in this decad, will reach the divine abode of parampadam where there is no hurdle in the endlessly joyful experience”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār explains attaining of paramapadam as the result for this decad.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. pulambu sīr būmi aḷanda perumānai nalam koḷ sīr nan kurugūrc catakōpan sol valam koṇḍa āyirattuḷ ivaiyum ōr pattu ilangu vān yāvarum ēṟuvar sonnālē*

- *pulambu sīr* – His qualities are such that they are glorified by everyone like done by [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/).
- *būmi aḷanda perumān* – āḻvār praised the sarvasvāmy (supreme lord of all) \[not some ordinary person\] who measured the world \[by stretching his foot\] and eliminated its anya śēśatvam (being ruled by some one other than [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)) and svasvātantryam (independence) through his pāsurams.
- *nalam koḷ sīr* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) who has the śrīvaiṣṇavaśrī (wealth of being a śrīvaiṣṇava) due to craving greatly for bhagavān. That is, his sensory organs craving like [cētana (sentient),](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) that too each sense craving for the activity of all other senses, himself craving for all of those activities. The words of nammāḻvār who is the leader of the wonderful āḻvārtirunagari, who is having the goodness of desiring for experience of bhagavān and who is with qualities such as jñāna etc.
- *valam koṇḍa* … – \[valam is explained as surrounding/circumambulating and balam (strength)\] Circumambulating and consuming [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) who is revealed in these pāsurams \[i.e., clearly explaining about bhagavān\]. Also explained as having the ability (strength) to explain the meanings clearly.
- *ilangu vān …* – When this unparalleled decad is recited, irrespective of the nature and qualities of the individual, one will attain paramapadam which has the distinguishing aspect of experience of bhagavān without any break. As said in cāndōjña upaniśat “*sa ēkadā bhavati* …” (that liberated person will assume one form, three forms, many forms and serve [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)), they will enter paramapadam where they will assume many forms and the sensory organs in each of those \[divine\] forms can enjoy emperumān fully.

## 3.9 Sonnal virodam

## 3.9.1. Sonnal virodam

*sonnāl virōdam idu āgilum solluvan kēṇminō en nāvil in kavi yān oruvarkkum kodukkilēn tennā tenā enṟu vaṇḍu mural tiruvēnkatattu en ānai en appan emperumān uḷan āgavē*

**Пословный перевод:**

idu – this good advice (which is focussed on eliminating your praising of others); sonnāl – when spoken; virōdam – inimical (to your desire); āgilum – in spite of that; solluvan – I will say (unable to bear your disastrous situation); kēṇmin – (you) listen; vaṇḍu – beetles; tennā tenā enṟu – (being joyful as a result of consuming honey) sweet humming; mural – making sound; tiruvēnkatattu – being present in tirumalā (tiruvēnkatam); en ānai – being eligible to be praised by me; en appan – being the benefactor who gives himself (as the prize for the pāsuram in his praise); emperumān – the apt lord; uḷan āga – sustaining himself (by these pāsurams in praise); en nāvil – fulfilling the purpose of my tongue; in kavi – sweet pāsurams (to īśvara who accepts these pāsurams); yān – I (who is exclusive servitor of him); oruvarkkum – to anyone else; kodukkilēn – unable to submit

**Перевод:**

**When spoken, this good advice (which is focussed on eliminating your praising of others) is inimical (to your desire); in spite of that I will say (unable to bear your disastrous situation); (you) listen; the apt lord who is eligible to be praised by me, the benefactor who gives himself (as the prize for the pāsuram in his praise), who is present in tirumalā (tiruvēnkatam) where the beetles are making sweet humming sound, is sustaining himself (by these pāsurams in praise); I am unable to submit the sweet pāsurams coming out of tongue fulfilling its (tongue’s purpose) to anyone else (other than tiruvēnkatamudaiyān).**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In first pāsuram – āḻvār who set out to give advice for their well-being to those who praise others, explains his own philosophy to develop the taste in them.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*In first pāsuram – āḻvār explains his own philosophy saying “I will not praise any one other than the upakāraka (benefactor) who is present in tirumalā to accept my praises”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*In first pāsuram – āḻvār who set out to advice “it is not good for you to praise petty persons”, to develop the taste in them, mercifully explains his own philosophy saying “See my stature”. sonnāl virōdam idu āgilum solluvan kēṇminō en nāvil in kavi yān oruvarkkum kodukkilēn tennā tenā enṟu vaṇḍu mural tiruvēnkatattu en ānai en appan emperumān uḷan āgavē*

- *sonnāl virōdam idu* – Three explanations:
   - Towards you who are interested in ulterior benefits , me telling “do not praise \[others\]” implies I am blocking the benefits you desire for; you will develop hatred towards me thinking “he is speaking contrary to our objectives”. Still, I am saying this \[out of great compassion unable to bear your pathetic situation\].
   - Alternatively – As said in “*… yō’vasādassa ucyatām*” (Let the defects of those who recite [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s names during morning, noon, evening be revealed \[implies, there is no defects for such person\]), prahlāda said to the asura children recite the divine names of bhagavān either by saying “if we say the divine name, thunder will strike” \[i.e., reciting the divine names even in a negative connotation\] or by saying the divine names themselves \[either way, one should recite the divine names\]; similarly, even if you think this to be meaningless, I will tell you.
   - Another explanation – As said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 3.7.14 “*svapuruśam … karṇamūlē …*” (yama tells his servitor secretly in his ears “I am the master for all common people but not for the vaiṣṇavas, leave those who are surrendered to devotees of bhagavān”), like “some one who is desiring for the queen” should not be discussed in public \[as both the speaker and the person who is being discussed will be in trouble\]. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) feels disgusted to even say “it is very lowly to serve undeserving persons”; this being the case, you are so pathetic that I have to advice you; thus, if I say something now, it will be bad for me as well \[as explained in the example\].
- *āgilum solluvan* – Still I am telling you. Why are you telling us even in this situation? āḻvār says “I am not telling you since you have come with internal/external sense control, with samit (sticks that are used in yajñas) \[as dedicated brahmacāris (students) would have\]; but I am telling you looking at your pathetic situation; thus, I will not stop until you are relieved from this suffering.  Like you are not retracting from worldly desires, I will not retract from giving you good advice”.
- *kēṇminō* – \[listen\] Don’t think that after listening to me you have to follow the instructions fully; just listening to me is sufficient; no need to follow. \[Why is [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) not telling them to put the advice in practice?\] On hearing the good advice, since they are cētanas (sentient beings), they will like it very much; for that which happens out of natural attachment, we need not specifically tell them to do; thus āḻvār says “what is the point in forcing them to follow the instructions? just listen”. One would not close their ears when hearing the sound of the ocean; at least hear like that. By the plural in “*kēṇmin*“, āḻvār implies that the pathetic situation is common for everyone and thus he is telling everyone. His pain \[in seeing them suffer\] is so much that, he is falling at the feet of everyone and requesting them to worship [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) like falling at someone’s feet to make them drink sweet milk.
- *en nāvil* … – If you are truly a cētana (sentient – knovledgable person), as you are going in the wrong path, when you see someone who is going on the right path, should you not say “I should also go in the same path”? So, you have seen my conduct; why don’t you also follow the same conduct?
- *en nā* – As said in mahābhāratam udyōga parvam “*yasyaitē tasya taddanam*” (to the one who owns a person, his property also belongs to the same owner), as I am a servitor of bhagavān, my tongue which is a faculty for me, is a servitor of him too – such tongue. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says “Is there any one who has used his tongue in a better manner than me?”; my tongue is as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 3.8.2](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/10/thiruvaimozhi-3-8-2-nenjame/) “*vanjanē ennum eppōdum en vāsagam*” (my speech **will always** say “Oh misceivous one!”).
- *in kavi* – [īśvara](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) hears his pāsurams of praise, becomes pleased and cheerful, and āḻvār in turn becomes cheerful. In whichever way śēśi (lord) becomes pleased, the śēśabhūta (servitor) also becomes pleased. Whatever pleasure is acquired when śrīman nārāyaṇan and śrī mahālakśmi are united as a couple, the same pleasure is acquired when śēśi ([bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) – lord) and śēśa ([ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) – servitor) unite. The unique aspect of śēśabhūta is to be pleased by the same thing that pleases the lord.
- *yān* – me who is considering myself as exclusively devoted to bhagavān. With this thought only, previously “*yasyaitē*” was explained.
- *oruvarkkum kodukkilēn* – This \[phrase\] is not in line with the previously explained atyanta pāratantriyam \[total dependence\]. When one says “I will not give to any one else”, it implies “I will give to [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)“; will it fit the true nature of ātmā to consider owning something, giving to others and accepting from others? If [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) himself has bestowed the ability to think, act and withdraw from actions, one can say “I have submitted mine”. The relationship of ātmā with bhagavān is very deep that one can say “I have submitted mine”. Like during gōdānam (donating a cow) a father will pour water for the offering in the hands of his son, give his own cow to his son and accept that back from him \[as if the cow was owned by the son\]; \[similarly,\] [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) explains this from [īśvara](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s view point, where the ātmā presents something as if it’s one’s own property, emperumān will accept it as if the ātmā has given everything.  As said in tiruvāimoḻi 7.9.1 “*ennāl tannai in tamiḻ pādiya*” (emperumān sung about himself in beautiful pāsurams through me), emperumān is of the nature that he made āḻvār sing about him and then considered “āḻvār sung about me”. Since worldly people praise other worldly people, āḻvār is emphasising that he will not praise others.
- *tennā* … – This is how he composed his pāsurams in praise of emperumān. That is  – like the humming noise made by the beetles out of the joy of drinking honey fell in line with musical note, āḻvār’s divine experience of bhagavān which leads to the great joy was released as the pāsurams. tiryak \[insects – beetles\], mumukśus (liberation seekers) and [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) himself – everyone is blissfully enjoying the music/pāsurams. If those who are close to bhagavān sing these pāsurams, it is natural that [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is also attached to them; he is said as “*tennā ennum en ammān*” (my lord who is enjoying).
- *tiruvēnkatattu en ānai* – Like śrī rāmāyaṇam is glorified greater than vēdam, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) highlights the greatness of the target of his praises \[[tiruvēnkatamudaiyān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) – arcāvatāram\] in comparison to the target of śrī vālmīki bhagavān’s praises \[śrī rāma – vibhavāvatāram\].
- *tiruvēnkatattu en ānai* – āḻvār is so great that he gets an elephant as prize for singing praises; tiruvēnkatamudaiyān, the elephant acquired fame by āḻvār’s praises \[in his pāsurams\]. āḻvār enjoys as sagōtri \[belonging to the same gōtra – here gōtra means hill/mountain\] for the beetles \[who are residents of tirumalā\]. emperumān is unlike others, who would give a different elephant for those who praise them \[as prize\]. emperumān is a pleasure to watch \[like an elephant which is always watched with great joy\] and deserves to be praised at all times. [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is enjoyable for me like an elephant and is residing in tirumalā where beetles out of joy due to drinking honey make sound like those who perform elaborate vocal musical rendering.
- *en appan* – My great benefactor who made me capable of advising others, while the people of this world are busy in glorifying others.
- *emperumān* – Even if he caused harm \[instead of doing favour as explained previously\], he has the apt relationship \[of being my lord\].
- *uḷan āgavē* – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is said to sustain others by his arrival as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 59.3 “… *āśayā yadivā rāma: …*” (sumantra says – hoping that śrī rāma will return, I stayed with guha for many days) – when such emperumān sustains himself by hearing my pāsurams, will I sing any one else? Like it is said in taittiriya upaniśat “*asannēva*” (similar to acit) – when a samsāri ātmā (bound soul) does not reach bhagavān, it is as good as acit (insentient), emperumān considers himself to be non-existing when he is not with me – thus he arrived here \[to accept me\]. What will happen to him who descended here to make me sing his praises, if I go and praise some one else? That being the case, it is apt for you to be like me.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

adiyen saraty ramanuja dasan
