## 3.9.2. Ulan agave

*uḷan āgavē eṇṇit tannai onṟāgat tan selvattai vaḷanā madikkum im mānidattaik kavi pādi en? kuḷan ār kaḻani sūḻ kaṇṇan kuṟungudi meymmaiyē uḷan āya endaiyai endai pemmānai oḻiyavē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kuḷan Ar – filled with water-bodies (ponds, lakes etc); kaḻani sūḻ – surrounded by fields; kaṇ – having vast space; nal – beautiful; kuṟungudiyē – in tirukkuṟungudi; meymmaiyē – revealing the ultimate benefit of auspicious qualities such as saulabhya; uḷan āya – one who permanently presented himself; endaiyai – my benefactor; endai pemmānai – the lord of my clan; oḻiya – other than him; tannai – oneself (who is as good as asat (acit) due to lack of knowledge about bhagavān); uḷan āgavē – to be existing; onṟāga – as an entity; eṇṇi – considering; than selvattai – the lowly wealth which is considered as one’s own though not belonging to oneself; vaḷanā – greatly distinguished; madikkum – oneself respecting/considering; i mānidattai – this human species which is very lowly; kavi pādi en – what is the benefit of singing their praises?

**Перевод:**

**What is the benefit of glorifying this human species which is very lowly where one is considering oneself to be an entity that is existing, considering the lowly wealth which is considered as one’s own though not belonging to oneself, respecting/considering oneself to be greatly distinguished, instead of glorifying the lord of my clan, my benefactor who permanently presented himself revealing the ultimate benefit of auspicious qualities such as saulabhya in beautiful tirukkuṟungudi having vast space surrounded by fields which are filled with water-bodies?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In second pāsuram – āḻvār condemns those who sing praises of the ones who are as good as acit (matter which lacks knowledge), who are having worthless wealth instead of praising emperumān who is eternal, who is complete in all auspicious qualities and wealth.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “What is the benefit of singing the praises of mortal persons instead of singing the praises of the lord of my clan who is standing in tirukkuṟungudi with these qualities such as saulabhyam (easy approacability) etc.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Second pāsuram. āḻvār says “What is the benefit of singing the praise of lowly persons who have wealth which is not worth of even a word of praise, when such wealth is analysed it is false due to its impermanent nature, and the one who owns that wealth is also not worthy, instead of praising sarvēśvara who is eternal, having complete wealth, being perfect with respect to true nature, forms and qualities and apt lord \[for everyone\]?”. uḷan āgavē eṇṇit tannai onṟāgat than selvattai vaḷanā madikkum im mānidattaik kavi pādi en? kuḷan Ar kaḻani sūḻ kaṇṇan kuṟungudi meymmaiyē uḷan āya endaiyai endai pemmānai oḻiyavē*

- *uḷan āgavē eṇṇi* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) considers them to be “*ilan*” (non-existing) \[though worldly persons consider themselves to be existing\]. Since it is said in katavalli upaniśat “*nēha nānāsti*” (there is nothing but that supreme brahmam) that there is nothing beyond bhagavān \[All sentient and insentient beings are contained in bhagavān himself\]. If one considers bhagavān to be non-existing that persons is to be considered non-existing as said in taittiriya upaniśat “*asannēva*” (as good as non-existing). One is said to exist only when one has knowledge about brahmam. While one should think about the existence of brahmam and exist oneself, there is no way to be existing while denying bhagavān’s existence. When tied down and taken to the court of rāvaṇa, hanuman said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 43.25 “*nēyam asti purī lankā na yūyam na ca rāvaṇa: \| yasmādikśvākunātēna baddam vairam mahātmanā \|\|*” (For the reason you became inimical with the great śrī rāma, for the same reason all of you, rāvaṇa and lankā will cease to exist) \[āḻvār too saying that worldly persons are non-existing due to their lack of acceptance of bhagavān\].
- *eṇṇi* – themselves thinking \[to be existing\], like imagining the great mēru mountain standing on a needle \[which is impossible\].
- *tannai* – Is this person thinking about some one who remains fearless and rests without anxiety after hearing “[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is there for us” as said in mudal tiruvantādi 99 “*uḷan kaṇḍāy nan nenjē uttaman enṟum uḷan kaṇḍāy*” (Oh noble heart! emperumān is present, the best lord is always present)? \[No\] He is thinking about himself who is like it is said in “*asannēva*“, where his existence depends on [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s existence.
- *onṟāga* – thinking intensely
- *than selvattai* – as said in “*sati darmiṇi darmā:*” (if the righteous entity exists righteous will exist), only when his ([ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)) existence is truth, his attributes will exist; when his existence itself is questionable, he thinks that he has some wealth.
- *vaḷanā* – this means beauty and greatness. He thinks that his wealth is greater than [īśvara](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s wealth.
- *madikkum* – he himself would think highly of his wealth; to consider his wealth to be worthy, there is no one lower than him \[i.e. he must first be worthy to consider his wealth to be worthy\]. \[An incident explains how one may consider himself very worthy\] In a place called kal brahmadēśam, there was a person named karikāl cōḷa brahmarāyan \[probably a minister\]  who said to nanjīyar “I have written a commentary for tiruvāimoḻi” and submitted the same to him. Considering the favours done by him \[towards sampradāyam and śrīvaiṣṇavas\], he calls nampiḷḷai and mercifully tells him to listen to that and praise him accordingly \[to keep him encouraged\]. nampiḷḷai too obliges and tells the person “your commentary closely follows āḻvār’s divine heart”. Hearing that the person \[pridefully\] says to nampiḷḷai “Oh piḷḷai! Can’t you identify the difference between [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) and me? I did this while I was also taking care of my official duties \[unlike āḻvār who was engaged in this full time – hence, my work is more appreciable since I did both official duties and writing commentary\].
- *immānidattai* – already āḻvār explained the true nature of such worldly people
- *immānidattai* – āḻvār does not even want to call them humans; he treats them like [acētana (insentient objects)](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/09/thathva-thrayam-achith-what-is-matter/). \[mey – truth, body.\] One who does not know the true nature of oneself is as good as “matter” \[which lacks knowledge\]; Also explained as – one who does not know that he is the body of bhagavān, he is as good as matter.
- *kavi pādi en* – What is the benefit of revealing their defects which they have concealed, in clear writings?
- *kuḷan Ar* – There is more water-bodies than fertile lands; otherwise the fields will dry out and die.  This implies, that the town where rakśaka (protector) is present more than the rakśya (protected).
- *kaṇṇan kuṟungudi* – This is the abode which is considered as his own with great attachment by sarvēśvara himself. tamiḻ scholars explained this as “*kaṇ nal kuṟungudi*” – this means spacious, beautiful [tirukkuṟungudi](http://thirukkurungudi.koyil.org/).
- *meymmaiyē uḷan āya* – The lord who has all the qualities that are revealed in the verses praising him unlike those who are praised without any real standing and their praises are merely heard in the verses submitted to them. There is no artavāda (exaggeration or mere praise without fact) in [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s case. In other matters/entities there is nothing but artavāda. In bhagavān’s case, one cannot fully glorify all the aspects and in others’ case, there is nothing to glorify.
- *endaiyai* – The benefactor who revealed his qualities to be praised by me. He is apt to be praised. Having all qualities in full in [tirukkuṟungudi](http://thirukkurungudi.koyil.org/) and one who is being our lord.
- *endai* … – Since the result does not stop with [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/), he says “[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is the lord of my entire clan”. What is the benefit of glorifying mortal beings who lack good qualities, who are very lowly and who are not apt goals, instead of glorifying the apt lord who has all auspicious qualities?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

adiyen saraty ramanuja dasan

## 3.9.3. Olivonrillada

*oḻivonṟillāda pal ūḻi tōṟūḻi nilāvappōm vaḻiyait tarum nangaḷ vānavar īsanai niṟkap pōyk kaḻiya miga nalla vān kavi koṇḍu pulavīrgāḷ! iḻiyak karudi ōr mānidam pādal ennāvadē?*

**Пословный перевод:**

oḻivu onṟu illāda – without any break; pal ūḻi tōṟūḻi – forever (in every kalpa (day of brahmā)); nilāva – stand firm and enjoy; pōm – that goes on; vaḻiyai – kainkaryam (service) which is the path; tarum – bestow; nangaḷ vānavar īsanai – our lord who is served by nityasūris; niṟka – other than him; pōy – seeking outside; kaḻiya – very great; miga nalla – very noble; vān kavi koṇḍu – with best poems; pulavīrgāḷ – you who are wise!; iḻiyak karudi – wanting to lower yourself (like foolish persons); ōr mānidam – the human race which has no specific glories; pādal – by singing \[the praises\]; en āvadu – what is the benefit?

**Перевод:**

**Oh you who are wise! What is the benefit in seeking out others and singing \[the praises\] of the human race, which has no specific glories, with very great noble, best poems instead of singing our lord who is served by nityasūris and bestows the path of performing kainkaryam (service) to him forever, without any break?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In third pāsuram – āḻvār says “What is the benefit of praising lowly human beings instead of praising emperumān who is very distinguished and greatly benevolent?”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. oḻivonṟillāda pal ūḻi tōṟūḻi nilāvappōm vaḻiyait tarum nangaḷ vānavar īsanai niṟkap pōyk kaḻiya miga nalla vān kavi koṇḍu pulavīrgāḷ! iḻiyak karudi ōr mānidam pādal ennāvadē?*

- *oḻivu …* – Forever without break. nilāva – to live. As said in cāndōjña upaniśat 8.15 “*na ca punarāvartatē*” (there is no return), forever being free from bondage in material realm. Though, for kainkaryam without any break, experience in paramapadam where time has no control, is explained, since āḻvār is residing in this material world which is controlled/changed by time, he speaks about such kainkaryam in this context \[of time in this material realm\].
- *pōm vaḻiyait tarum* – Three explanations – 1) [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) will give the arcirādi gati (path which takes one to śrīvaikuṇṭam) which has endless bliss and will make the ātmā think “even the joy in paramapadam cannot match the joy in this journey”; 2) alternatively, he will bestow the means through which one can attain him; the routine will involve constant engagement with [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/). 3) *vaḻi* is also explained as prāpyam (goal). Bestowing the goal, means he himself becoming upāyam (means). When *vaḻi* is explained as prāpyam (goal), here it talks about natural servitude towards bhagavān.
- *nangaḷ vānavar īsanai niṟka* – The \[joyful\] result which is explained as in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 4.5.2 “*puṇaikkodukkilum pōga vottār*” (nityasūris will not let those liberated souls to return to material realm, even if some one from material realm guarantees that we will return those liberated souls to paramapadam in a few days). Two explanations  for niṟka – giving up, standing. 1) giving up emperumān who would give to those who sing his praises, think “would this be sufficient for what he has done to me?” and give more. 2) emperumān patiently waiting for the [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) to sing his praises thinking “he is capable of glorifying me”.
- *pōy* – Seeking out to glorify something else beyond bhagavān. When the one who is being praised hears that some one is coming to praise him, he runs away. The one who praises is also determined to get some prize from the one who is being praised; so, the one who praises too chases that person (who is to be praised) to fulfil his requirement; so, every one is going. In bhagavat viśayam (matters related to [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)), as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 17.1 “*ājagāma*” (he came), when one takes a step towards bhagavān, it will be said as coming to one’s own residence from others’ residence; but in the case of others, even if one is in close proximity \[from one’s own place\], it will feel like an unnatural residence \[which is why the word “*pōy*” (going) is used instead of “coming”\].
- *kaḻiya* … – Since the one who praises adds non-existing glories about the one who is praised, it will be beyond comprehension; the person being praised will be confused thinking “Who is he really talking about? Is that really me?”; thus, the praises will not stay with the one who is praised. When a poem speaks about the glories which do not exist in a person, such poem points to the person \[bhagavān\] who really has \[all\] such glories.
- *miga nalla* – very good. vān kavi – intense poem. As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam bāla kāṇḍam 2.48 “*tadupagata samāsa sandiyōgam*” (joined words and compound words), having enriched words. With very beautiful, orderly poems.
- *pulavīrgāḷ* – The ones who can differentiate between the poem and the bhagavān who is the target of the poem. Why did you, who are wise, do this?
- *iḻiyak karudi* – If one is intelligent, would one not try to improve ones stature? Is there anyone who will want to fall down from his stature very much?
- *ōr mānidam pādal* – Praising a lowly person.
- *en āvadu* – Will it fit your special intelligence? Will it lead to any benefit for them \[who are ignorant humans\]? Will it benefit you? Is it matching for the poem itself? What are you singing for?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.9.4. Ennavadu

*ennāvadu? ettanai nāḷaikkup pōdum pulavīrgāḷ! mannā manisaraip pādip padaikkum perum poruḷ minnār maṇi mudi viṇṇavar tādaiyaip pādināl tannāgavē koṇḍu sanmam seyyāmaiyum koḷḷumē*

**Пословный перевод:**

pulavīrgāḷ – Oh poets (who know words and their meanings)!; mannā – impermanent (they are not even guaranteed to live until you complete your praises); manisarai – humans; pādi – singing their praises; padaikkum – achieve as great reward; perum poruḷ – of great wealth (based on your desire); ettanai nāḷaikkup pōdum – how long will they be of use?; min Ar – having great radiance; maṇi mudi – one who is having precious gem studded crown; viṇṇavar tādaiyai – the supreme lord who is the cause of sustenance for nityasūris; pādināl – if you sing; tannāgavē koṇḍu – considering you to be fully existing for him; sanmam seyyāmaiyum – eliminate birth (which leads to praising others); koḷḷum – will acknowledge

**Перевод:**

**Oh poets! How long will the great reward of great wealth which was achieved by singing the praises of impermanent humans, be of use? If you sing \[praises of\] the supreme lord who is the cause of sustenance for nityasūris, who is having radiant precious gem studded crown, he will acknowledge the elimination of birth, considering you to be fully existing for him.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In fourth pāsuram – āḻvār says “Instead of praising emperumān who would give a reward which is comparable to himself to those who praise him, singing mortal humans who have limited life span will yield petty reward only”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “What is the benefit of praising mortal humans instead of the superior lord of all?”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. ennāvadu? ettanai nāḷaikkup pōdum pulavīrgāḷ! mannā manisaraip pādip padaikkum perum poruḷ minnār maṇi mudi viṇṇavar tādaiyaip pādināl tannāgavē koṇḍu sanmam seyyāmaiyum koḷḷumē*

- *en āvadu* – Nothing will come out \[of praising mortal beings\]. Are you not praising with expectation of some benefit? But, whatever you desire will not be achieved. So, what is achieved? You will only achieve the lowly nature which was explained in previous pāsuram.
- *en āvadu* – You think that you are getting some reward; I think that you are becoming lowly;

How do you say there is no benefit? Don’t you see people singing praises and people rewarding in return for such praises?

- *ettanai nāḷaikkup pōdum* – It is as good as not getting anything \[since the reward won’t last long\]. If we analyze “the reward was forcefully acquired for the praises”. The cost of bringing people along while praising some one, the loans acquired during the time of preparing/singing the praises \[until the reward was given\] etc cannot be compensated by the reward.
- *pulavīrgāḷ* – Does it match your intelligence? Should you not yourselves know “this is the nature of the poem, this is the reward – whether the poem and the reward match or not”?
- *pulavīrgāḷ* – Ones who know the words and meanings \[and their worth\]!
- *mannā manisarai* – Should you at least not be getting some small reward? The ones you praise should at least remain until you complete your praises. When you go to submit your praises, some one will come towards you saying as in periya tirumoḻi 6.2.5 “*avarē māṇḍār*” (that person has already died).
- *pādip padaikkum perum poruḷ* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) accuses them saying “Will śriya:pati not give you enough?”.
- *min Ar* … – Those who praise him are crowned for their praises towards [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/); nityasūris who have radiant crowns which are precious gem studded. As said in rig vēdam \[viṣṇu sūktam\] “… *vipanyava:* …” (those who are wise and have the nature of praising \[him\] constantly, reach that supreme abode of viṣṇu). They \[nityasūris\] are also the ones who provide the assembly to those who praise [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) and make emperumān hear them. They are said in tiruvāimoḻi 10.6.11 as “*kēttārār vānavargaḷ*” (the residents of paramapadam will want to hear tiruvāimoḻi again and again as they are not satisfied just hearing it once).
- *viṇṇavar tādaiyaip pādināl* – If the leader of nityasūris is praised. If the crown is considered as an adjective for [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/), it means “the crown which he adorns to reward the ones who praise him”.
- *pādināl* – This praising itself is a reward.

Further,

- *tannāgavē  koṇḍu* – accepting the praises for himself; Also explained as [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) making the [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) to resemble bhagavān himself as said in [śrī bhagavat gītā](http://githa.koyil.org/) 14.2 “*mama sādarmyamāgatā:*” (acquire my nature), muṇḍaka upaniśat “*paramam sāmyamupaiti*” (attain the supreme similarity) and periya tirumoḻi 11.3.5 “*tammaiyē okka aruḷ seyvar*” ([emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) will bless those who worship him to become similar to him).
- *sanmam seyyāmaiyum koḷḷumē* – He will then eliminate the worldly birth which makes one to be submissive and to praise others. The birth in this material realm is the cause for praising worldly people. First he gives the qualities/enjoyment of nityasūris and then only he removes the connection from this samsāram as an imprisoned prince is first crowned and then his shackles are broken and as śrī vibhīśaṇāḻvān was first crowned \[even before the war\] and then rāvaṇa was killed.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.9.5. Kollum payanillai

*koḷḷum payan illai kuppai kiḷarttanna selvattai vaḷḷal pugaḻndu num vāymai iḻakkum pulavīrgāḷ! koḷḷak kuṟaivilan vēṇḍiṟṟellām tarum kōdil en vaḷḷal maṇivaṇṇan tannaik kavi solla vamminē*

**Пословный перевод:**

koḷḷum payan – a benefit that is acquired; illai – not there; kuppai kiḷarttu anna – like digging out the waste/garbage which will only reveal faults; selvattai – the lowly people who are having wealth; vaḷḷal – as greatly generous persons; pugaḻndu – praising; num vāymai – your truthfulness; iḻakkum – losing; pulavīrgāḷ – Oh poets!; koḷḷa – to accept (as the object of the praise and the benefit of the praising); kuṟaivilan – complete without any limitation; vēṇḍiṟṟu ellām – whatever we prayed for; tarum – while giving; kōdu il – being without any defect (like discriminating between the recipients or giving with an expectation in return); en vaḷḷal – being the great benefactor who gave himself to me; maṇivaṇṇan tannai – one who is having the best form which resembles a blue gem; kavi solla – to praise; vammin – come

**Перевод:**

**Oh poets! Don’t lose your truthfulness by praising the lowly people who are having wealth which is like digging out the waste/garbage which will only reveal faults and which has no real benefit when acquired, as greatly generous persons. Come and praise emperumān who is completely qualified to accept all praises, who is without any defect (like discriminating between the recipients or giving with an expectation in return) while giving whatever we prayed for, who is the great benefactor who gave himself to me and who is having the best form which resembles a blue gem.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In fifth pāsuram – āḻvār says “Come and sing emperumān who is the abode of all auspicious qualities and the bestover of all desires instead of singing those who are not doing any favours and will cause insult to those who sing their praises”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “Instead of praising of others which is of no use, come and praise the great benefactor and the one gives all benedictions”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. koḷḷum payan illai kuppai kiḷarttanna selvattai vaḷḷal pugaḻndu num vāymai iḻakkum pulavīrgāḷ! koḷḷak kuṟaivilan vēṇḍiṟṟellām tarum kōdil en vaḷḷal maṇivaṇṇan tannaik kavi solla vamminē*

- *koḷḷum payan illai* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says “One ventures to praise others not because they are worthy of being praised but because there is some worldly benefit; but there is no such benefit”. They are not singing their praises for the sake of it. There are only doing this because there is some reward in doing so; hence, āḻvār starts with saying “there is no such benefit” – hearing which they may give up such praising.
- *koḷḷum payan illai* – This is the great reward of singing their praises with great dedication, i.e., no reward – there is no reward that is worthy to be accepted. Thus, there is no benefit for you.

Though there is no benefit for self, one may perform certain acts for the well-being of others. Is there anything like that in this?

- *kuppai* … – This wealth which resembles the effect of digging out the waste/garbage. That is, exposing the faults/defects/dirt which is disgraceful for those who are praised. When we dig the garbage we will end up bringing out soiled clothes etc. Not only it is disgraceful for them, it is also that which causes impurity for the ones who are singing such \[false\] praises.
- *vaḷḷal pugaḻndu* – Singing them as very generous. Though such praises do nothing good to the one who is praised and have no value for others, praising him well to bring auspiciousness for him and to show that it is done purely for the sake of praising without any expectation.
- *num vāymai iḻakkum* – This is the reward you get. He said previously that both good aspects are not present (there is no benefit and exposes the dirt); thus, you give up your title of “*vāgmi*” (eloquent speaker). Alternatively – vāymai is explained as mey (truth), and since you are telling those aspects which are contrary to well-known facts, you will be called as a liar.
- *pulavīrgāḷ* – Is this matching the stature of you who know about losing great things? I am in this unfortunate situation of instructing what is good for you; will your praises match varṇāśrama dharma \[To acquire wealth, a person of higher standing may need to praise some one of lower standing\]? As [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is the sarvaśabdavācyan (indicated by all words), would the words in praise indicate anyone else?

When they ask “Whoever you speak about ([emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)), is there greater glory than whom we are praising now?”, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says,

- *koḷḷak kuṟaivilan* – āḻvār is explaining the opposite of what was explained previously. There is real benefit. And there is no garbage in this wealth. Whatever praises you have rendered, emperumān is fully qualified to receive those praises; he is the abode of all auspicious qualities.
- *vēṇḍiṟṟu ellām tarum* – The reward is great. Whatever you pray for – bhōga (enjoyment in this world), mōkśa (ultimate enjoyment after liberation), he will bestow them. Others, when they bestow worldly enjoyment and if the recipient wants liberation, they cannot bestow that; \[but, would everyone who seeks out bhōga and mōkśa get them from [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) after surrendering unto him?\] In [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s case, only due to incapability of the recipient, they may miss out; they will not miss out on them because bhagavān is not able to give to them \[bhagavān is always ready and able to give\]. viṣṇu darmam “*bhaumam manōratam svarjñam svargivandyanca yatpadam\| dadāti dāyinām nityam apavargapradō hari:*” (bhagavān who is liberation giver, bestows worldly pleasures, pleasures in celestial worlds and paramapadam which is desired by the residents of celestial worlds, for those who meditate upon him); viṣṇu darmam “*sakala pala: pradō hi viṣṇu:*” (viṣṇu who is bestover of all results).
- *kōdil* – While giving reward to some one, there will be no faults. Faults in charity/gift – giving according to time, place and recipient \[discrimination\], giving with the pride that “I gave”, making the recipient worry “How am I going to repay this great reward?”.

When asked, “How did you know?”, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says,

- *en vaḷḷal* – I am sharing my own experience \[with the most generous [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)\].
- *maṇivaṇṇan* – His divine bodily beauty which is so attractive even if his rewards are worthless and he has no opulence. Previously, people were singing praises by being attracted to fake beauty; even if one were to sing the beauty, it is [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) only who deserves such praises. Just like his qualities are complete to be praised, his beauty is also complete to be praised.
- *maṇivaṇṇan tannaik kavi solla vamminō* – Come and sing the one who is of the nature which I have explained.
- *vammin* – instead of hesitating, join fast.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.9.6. Vammin pulavir

*vammin pulavīr! num mey varuttik kai seyduymminō im mannulagi(ni)l selvar ippōdillai nōkkinōm num in kavi koṇḍu num num ittā deyvam ēttināl semmin sudar mudi en tirumālukkuc cērumē*

**Пословный перевод:**

pulavīr – Oh knowledgeable persons due to being a poet!; vammin – come here (giving up praising others); num mey varutti – toiling your body; kai seydu – engaging in craft works; uymminō – survive; man – eternal due to the continuity \[of repeated material creation\]; i – this; ulaginil – world; selvar – śrīmān (wealthy person); ippōdu – at this time; illai – not there; nōkkinōm – we have analysed; num – your; in kavi koṇḍu – with your best poems; num num – matching your taste; ittā deyvam – favourite dēvatās; ēttināl – if praised; sem min sudar mudi – having a divine crown with unstoppable radiant glow; en tirumālukkē – divine lord of śrī mahālakśmi, who is my lord; sērum – will belong to him

**Перевод:**

**Oh knowledgeable persons who are wise due to being a poet, come here (giving up praising others)!  For your livelihood, you can survive by toiling your body and engaging in craft works; we have analysed that at this time there is no śrīmān (wealthy person) in this world which is eternal due to the continuity \[of repeated material creation\]; now, if you praised your favourite dēvatās matching your taste with your best poems, (since those praises don’t befit them, instead of belonging to them) they will belong to the divine lord of śrī mahālakśmi, who is my lord, who is having a divine crown with unstoppable radiant glow.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In sixth pāsuram – They (those who praise worldly people) say “We are praising mortal humans et al for our livelihood”. āḻvār replies to them “Instead of surrendering unto such lowly humans and make a living, it is better to toil physically by doing hard labour or engage in craft works to make a living”. They say “But that won’t fulfil our desires; thus we are vorśipping our favourite dēvatās and have our desires fulfilled”. āḻvār replies “Since they don’t have the auspicious qualities which can be praised you, you praise emperumān who have such auspicious qualities who is the recipient of all praises anyway. If you don’t, you will be blamed of robbery \[of stealing emperumān’s qualities/glories and giving them to others\]; thus you come and worship emperumān”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “Whoever you praise, that will reach the supreme lord of all, the divine master of śrī mahālakśmi only”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. vammin pulavīr! num mey varuttik kai seyduymminō im mannulagi(ni)l selvar ippōdillai nōkkinōm num in kavi koṇḍu num num ittā deyvam ēttināl semmin sudar mudi en tirumālukkuc cērumē*

- *vammin* – Like inviting those who are caught in a wild fire by showing a pond, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is inviting these persons \[who are caught in the wild fire of material realm by showing bhagavān\].
- *pulavīr* – Oh ones who know what is good! come here. They ask āḻvār “Why are you calling us? Even if we have to manage our livelihood by praising others, don’t we need to do that?”, āḻvār replies “Even if you want to truly take care of your livelihood, do you have to reduce yourself for that? can you not take care of your livelihood, without lowering your stature?”.
- *num mey* … – You can toil your body or engage in craft works to manage your livelihood. [embār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/embar/) explains this as – would you not engage in carrying heavy loads, cutting grass etc?

When they said “But we won’t get sufficient funds to manage our livelihood! if we praise others we can get whatever we want”, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says “Yes – if that happens \[if you get the appropriate rewards\]”,

- *immannulagil selvar ippōdillai nōkkinōm* – In this world which is pravāharūpēṇa nityam \[unlike spiritual realm which is factually eternal, this material realm is eternal due to the continuity in creation after creation\], there is no śrīmān (wealthy persons) who will reward you matching your praises.
- *ippōdu nōkkinōm* – We (āḻvār) analyzed now seeing “These people are putting their heart in praising others – is there any benefit?”; but there is no one. Another explanation – Why say “no one present now” – there was also no one previously? Since āḻvār was not focussed on this worldly aspects \[initially  he was engaged in enjoying [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) fully and subsequently he turned towards the suffering souls and started advising them\], he is seeing them now thinking “Are they unnecessarily toiling? Is there any benefit for their efforts?”.

They say “Alright. We accept that there is no human being who is capable of rewarding us properly. But dēvatās (celestial beings – demigods) are different from manuśyas (humans); so, we will praise our favourite dēvatās using these poems” and [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) replies,

- *num* … – With your sweet praises, if you who are in rājasa (passionate) or tāmasa (ignorant) mode, praise respective rājasa or tāmasa dēvatās, that,
- *sem min* … – You praise with certain glorification in your poems; those glorification will not be applicable for them; when you say “*puṇḍarikākśa*” (lotus-eyed), it will belong to the one who lotus eyes; it will not apply to a “*virūpākśa*” (one who is having deformed eyes); thus, those praises will reach śriya:pati (lord of śrī mahālakśmi) who is having the divine crown which reveals his supremacy over everyone else. As a result, you only get called as robbers (since you rob off the qualities of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) and try to give it to others). While praising some one, you would normally say “sarvādika (greater than all), samasta kalyāṇa guṇātmaka (abode of all auspicious qualities), sarvarakśaka (protector of all and so on”; that will only apply to emperumān who really has those qualities. emperumān who has the divine crown with unstoppable radiant glow.
- *en tirumālukkuc cērum* – Even without your intentions, based on the nature/content of the poem, they will reach śriya:pati only. Alternate explanation – As said in mudal tiruvantādi 67 “*oṇḍāmaraiyāḷ kēḷvan oruvanaiyē nōkkum uṇarvu*” ((knowledge of) ātmā will only focus on śrīman nārāyaṇan who is the lord of [śrī mahālakśmi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/)), as true knowledge will only be focussed on [śrīman nārāyaṇan](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), as poems are garlands of words and since [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is indicated by all words, they will reach him only. \[Words that directly mean could indicate him, but how could all words which point to cit (sentient) and acit (insentient) will indicate him?\] That is – as all words indicate the combination of [acit](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/09/thathva-thrayam-achith-what-is-matter/) (matter/form that is visible), the [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) who controls that form and the [antāryāmi](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) (in-dwelling super soul – bhagavān), due to the primary importance of being the viśēśya (primary entity), the words primarily indicate him \[For example – when we say goat – it indicates the body of goat (matter – acit), the ātmā inside that body which is controlling the activities of the goat and the paramātmā who is the antaryāmi. Similarly, “table” indicates the physical form of table, the ātmā which is inside the table and the [paramātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) who is the antaryāmi. This principle applies to every form/body which is perceivable by our senses\]. dakśa smruti “*yē yajanti* …” (Whoever worships pitrus (ancestors), dēvatās (celestial beings), brāhmaṇas with agni, it implies that they worship [viṣṇu](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is the [antāryāmi](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) of all beings).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.9.7. Serum kodai

*sērum kodai pugaḻ ellaiyilānai ōrāyiram pērum udaiya pirānai allāl maṟṟu yān kilēn māri anaiya kai māl varai okkum tiṇ tōḷ enṟu pāril ōr paṟṟaiyaip paccaip pasum poygaḷ pēsavē*

**Пословный перевод:**

sērum – matching (for his stature); kodai – generosity; pugaḻ – the fame (acquired by such generosity); ellai ilānai – being boundless; ōr āyiram – unparalleled thousand; pērum udaiya – having divine names; pirānai – great benefactor; allāl – other than; maṟṟu – some one; pāril – in the earth; ōr paṟṟaiyai – an entity which is as useless as a blade of grass; kai – his hand deeds; māri anaiya enṟu – like the clouds; tiṇ tōḷ – his strong shoulders; māl varai – like huge mountains; okkum enṟu – similar; paccaip pasum poygaḷ – fresh falsehoods without a trace of truth; pēsa – to speak; yān – I (who has taken refuge of the complete lord); kilēn – incapable

**Перевод:**

**I am incapable to speak fresh falsehoods without a trace of truth as in saying “the deeds of your hands is similar to that of clouds”, “your strong shoulders are like huge mountains” in praise of an earthly entity which is as useless as a blade of grass; I can only of glorify the great benefactor who has boundless generosity and fame (matching his stature\] and having unparalleled thousand divine names.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In seventh pāsuram – āḻvār becomes pleased saying “I am unable to sing the praises of any one other than emperumān“.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “I have no strength to sing false praises of any one other than emperumān who has fully praiseworthy qualities and divine names”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Seventh pāsuram. Like a person who escaped with his belongings from a place where there is rampant robbery, āḻvār becomes pleased saying “Unlike these people \[who are praising worldly persons, dēvatās et al\], I am unable to sing the praises of any one other than emperumān“. sērum kodai pugaḻ ellaiyilānai ōrāyiram pērum udaiya pirānai allāl maṟṟu yān kilēn māri anaiya kai māl varai okkum tiṇ tōḷ enṟu pāril ōr paṟṟaiyaip paccaip pasum poygaḷ pēsavē*

- *sērum* … – having boundless fame which was acquired by his generosity; Alternatively – having boundless fame due to having generosity which matches his stature; that is – when a person gives a cow in charity to another person, others would wonder “what is the reason for this charity \[there must be some expectation\]”; perumāḷ (śrī rāma) gave everything including his own simhāsanam (throne) and śrī satrunjayan (his celebrated lead elephant) and stood without anything else to offer, a brāhmaṇa named trijada came and requested for some wealth. śrī rāma said “you can take all my cows which are living up to the banks of sarayu river” and gave them all, and others hearing this said “śrī rāma is quite capable to do that” \[it is nothing unusual for [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) to be greatly generous\]. In this manner, he is the one who has boundless fame acquired by his matching generosity. Only such emperumān is praiseworthy.
- *ōr āyiram* … – When we want to praise some one, instead of having one or two names, that too as in “jalapila:” \[some random name\] which does not fit in poetic meter easily, emperumān is greatly generous in presenting us countless names which can be nicely blended in to poetry.
- *ōr āyiram* – Every one of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s divine names is unparalleled to highlight his glories and to be praised.
- *pirānai* – The great benefactor who revealed them to me.
- *allāl* … – I am not capable of singing any one other than such emperumān.

When asked what would you not do?, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says,

- *māri anaiya kai* – Glorifying some one who has nothing to offer as “generous like clouds”. That is – giving without any expectation \[clouds don’t expect anything in return for dropping the rain\], becoming pale when unable to give \[clouds which do not rain become pale and shy away\] etc. Here kai indicates kodai (charity/generosity).
- *māl varai okkum* … – Looking at the shoulders which become weak thinking about giving charity, saying “your shoulders have expanded by giving charity, and your shoulder gives the shadow for everyone to take rest”.
- *pāril ōr paṟṟaiyai* – At least if one is to glorify the dēvatās of the bhōga bhūmi (celestial worlds fully focussed on enjoyment), that is acceptable; but here in this pār \[earth\], those who are like grass which simply grow and die; there is no use right from the time of taking birth and getting destroyed, they do good neither for oneself nor for others. Alternatively – pār indicates place. That is, without a place to stay. A tamiḻ scholar explained, paṟṟai (based on paṟṟu – holding on, attaching) as some one who holds on to whatever he has and does not engage in any charity. It is apt to say paṟṟai as *truṇa saman* (as good as grass).
- *paccaip pasum poygaḷ pēsavē* – Speak falsehoods which have no trace of truth.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.9.8. Veyin mali

*vēyin mali purai tōḷi pinnaikku maṇāḷanai āgiya perum pugaḻ ellai ilādana pādip pōyk kāyam kaḻittu avan tāḷinṇaik kīḻp pugum kādalan māya manisarai en solla vallēn en vāy koṇḍē?*

**Пословный перевод:**

vēyin – when compared to bamboo (for freshness, roundness, smoothness); mali – being greater; purai – shining; tōḷi – one who is having shoulders; pinnai – for nappinnai; maṇāḷanai – kriṣṇa who is always desired by her; āya – befitting his nature; perum – individually unlimited; ellai ilādana – countless; pugaḻ – qualities; pādi – singing; pōy – spending long time; kāyam – body; kaḻittu – shedding; avan tāḷ iṇaik kīḻ – at the lotus feet of him (who is the ultimate goal); pugum – taking shelter; kādalan – I who have desire; māyam manisarai – men who are bound in material bondage; en vāy koṇḍu – with my speech (which is qualified to praise bhagavān); en solla vallēn – what can I say?

**Перевод:**

**What can I say with my speech (which is qualified to praise bhagavān) about men who bound in material bondage? I am desirous of shedding my body and taking shelter at the lotus feet of kriṣṇa (who is the ultimate goal) by spending long time in singing the individually unlimited countless qualities of him which matching his nature, and who is always desired by nappinnai who is having shining shoulders which are greater in comparison to bamboo (for freshness, roundness, smoothness).**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In eighth pāsuram – āḻvār says “Even if I set out to glorify other lowly persons my speech will not co-operate; I can only praise emperumān who is opposite of all inauspicious aspects, abode of all auspicious qualities and the dear consort of nappinnaip pirātti \[incarnation of neeḷā dēvi who is one of the primary divine consorts of bhagavān\]”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, Can I who is desirous of praise kriṣṇa who is the ultimate goal and get him, praise lowly persons?*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. vēyin mali purai tōḷi pinnaikku maṇāḷanai āgiya perum pugaḻ ellai ilādana pādip pōyk kāyam kaḻittu avan tāḷinṇaik kīḻp pugum kādalan māya manisarai en solla vallēn en vāy koṇḍē?*

- *vēyin* … – \[Summary meaning\] [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says – I am desirous of praising sarvēśvaran who is dear to nappinnaip pirātti, who is abode of all auspicious qualities, shed my body, subsequent to that, acquire a spiritual body which is useful in serving [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) and serve them; In such case, how can I sing with my speech, the praises of lowly persons who are like a bubble in the water \[which will burst any time\]?
- *vēyin …* – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is dear to nappinnaip pirātti who has shoulders which are comparable only to themselves, and are greater in freshness \[beauty\], roundness and smoothness when compared to bamboo. malidal – abundance. purai – comparison. It is said that – napinnaip pirātti is doing puruśakāram (recommendation) \[to bhagavān\] to eliminate the connection with this material body which makes one praise others and to acquire a distinguished body to engage in service at the lotus feet of [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/). How can I who praised such divine couple, will engage in praising others? Would [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) who sings the praises of such pirātti and perumāḷ being close to pirātti, be abandoned by them?
- *pinnaikku maṇāḷanai* – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is specifically born to enjoy nappinnai’s beauty etc.

\[*āya, perum pugaḻ, ellai ilādana* are adjectives for his auspicious qualities.\]

- *āya* – Well analyzed. Also explained as, being opposite of all inauspicious aspects. Alternatively – āya means Ana, which is befitting the nature of [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/).
- *perum pugaḻ* – Whether it is the rūpa guṇa (qualities of divine form) or ātma guṇa (qualities of his true nature), each one of those qualities are infinite in nature.
- *ellai ilādana* – there are such countless qualities.
- *pādip pōyk kāyam kaḻittu* – As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 2.7 “*pāṇḍarasyātapatrasya cāyāyām jaritam mayā*” – daśarata cakravarti kept going around the kingdom in protection of the citizens and became old staying under the pearl studded ceremonial umbrella, speaking about the auspicious qualities of bhagavān as the regular routine and finally shedding the body.
- *avan* … – I who have the desire to take shelter of his divine feet as a breast-feeding child will take shelter of mother’s breast, after shedding this body, instead of engaging in self-enjoyment (kaivalya mōkśam) or accepting other worldly pleasures, accepting a spiritual body which is apt for serving [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/),
- *māya manisarai* – Those persons death which is earmarked as soon as they were born. That is, those who could die even before completing the song in praise of them.
- *en vāy koṇḍu en solla vallēn* – Even to praise them with the mouth (without the heart’s involvement) is not possible.
- *en vāy koṇḍu* – May be others speech can praise them \[not my speech\]. “*mana: pūrvō vāguttara:*” (whatever occurs in mind first is then spoken by mouth). After having great devotion towards [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/), how can I praise others? Would we desire for one thing and speak about some thing else? For all sensory organs, mind is the root; all sensory organs would follow the mind only. What is the reason for [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) highlighting this? That is because – though everyone has the same privilege to serve bhagavān, it is seen that some people are glorifying mortal beings, āḻvār says “I have fortunately escaped from such situation from the beginning”.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.9.9. Vay kondu

*vāy koṇḍu mānidam pāda vanda kaviyēn allēn āy koṇḍa sīr vaḷḷal āḻip pirān enakkē uḷan sāy koṇḍa immaiyum sādittu vānavar nāttaiyum nī kaṇḍu koḷ enṟu vīdum tarum ninṟu ninṟē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vāy koṇḍu – with my mouth which is the sensory organ for speech (which is meant to praise the apt emperumān); mānidam – manuśya (mortal humans who are not apt to be praised); pāda – to sing; vanda – come; kaviyēn allēn – not a poet; āy – examined (in vēdāntam); sīr – qualities such as ānandam (bliss) etc; koṇḍa – having; vaḷḷal – most generous; āḻi – having divine chakra (which will ensure that the hearts of those poets will be captivated in emperumān); pirān – great benefactor; enakkē uḷan – is present for me exclusively as the distinguished one; sāy koṇḍa – having great radiance; immaiyum – arcāvatāra anubhavam in this material realm; sādittu – create and present; vānavar nāttaiyum – the spiritual realm which is owned by nityasūris; nī kaṇḍu koḷ enṟu – saying “you analyse and manage”; vīdum – mōkśānandam (the bliss of liberation which is acquired by serving him); ninṟu – in the proper methods; tarum – will give

**Перевод:**

**I am not a poet who have come to sing manuśya (mortal humans who are not apt to be praised) with my mouth which is the sensory organ for speech (which is meant to praise the apt emperumān); the most generous emperumān whose qualities such as ānandam (bliss) etc are examined in vēdāntam, who is a great benefactor having divine chakra (which will ensure that the hearts of those poets will be captivated in emperumān) is present for me exclusively as the distinguished one; he will create and present us the greatly radiant arcāvatāra anubhavam (enjoyment in deity form of emperumān) in this material realm and the spiritual realm which is owned by nityasūris, and will say “you analyse and manage (like sēnai mudaliyār, who is chief administrator of all operations)” and also give mōkśānandam (the bliss of liberation which is acquired by serving him) in proper methods.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In ninth pāsuram – āḻvār says “I who was made by the most generous emperumān only by him, am not qualified to praise others”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. vāy koṇḍu mānidam pāda vanda kaviyēn allēn āy koṇḍa sīr vaḷḷal āḻip pirān enakkē uḷan sāy koṇḍa immaiyum sādittu vānavar nāttaiyum nī kaṇḍu koḷ enṟu vīdum tarum ninṟu ninṟē*

- *vāy koṇḍu* … – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is the only one who can naturally praise [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) \[His speech/mouth is present specifically to praise emperumān which is explained by this ślōkam\].  śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 40.5 “*sruśtastvam vanavāsāya*” (sumitrā says to lakśmaṇa – “you are given birth to accompany (and serve) śrī rāma in the forest”); “*sruśtastvam vanavāsāya”* – iḷaiya perumāḷ (lakśmaṇa informed his mother sumitrā, “perumāḷ (śrī rāma) is leaving to forest as per the orders of father and mother (daśarata and kaikēyi); I am following him too”, and sumitrā replies “if you have the desire to be crowned to rule the kingdom \[which you don’t have\], that could have been due to me praying to give birth to a son with such qualities; I have given birth to you to have you fully serving śrī rāma”; “*suhrujjanē rāmē – svanurakta:”* – you care for the divine feet of śrī rāma without anyone instructing you to do so; is there anything for me to specifically advise you now? you serve emperumān with great taste in serving him and seeing him through your ears \[since ādiśēśa, the serpent has both seeing and hearing through the same sensory organ\]. Alternatively – it is explained as “*svanurakta: suhrujjanē*” – You are dear to those who good people who care for perumāḷ (śrī rāma) thinking “Like a soft garland was placed under hot sun, perumāḷ ignoring his tender nature, left to the forest to fulfil his father’s order – what is going to happen now \[for him\]?” – śrī rāma’s mothers and others in ayōdyā request lakśmaṇa to care for śrī rāma who is like the root (which sustains them all) for them. “*rāmē*” – One who is beautiful as it is, and walking a few steps elegantly will increase his beauty manifold.  “*rāmē pramādam mākārśī:*” – There is no reason for lakśmaṇa who since birth as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam bāla kāṇḍam 18.27 “*bālyāt prabruti susnigda:*” (friendship from childhood) sustained himself by being together with śrī rāma and suffered in separation from him, to become forgetful now; she must be saying some thing specifically for the current context \[of going to the forest\]. “*bhrātari gaccati”* – śrī rāma will be walking in front of you; You be alert that you don’t become captivated by his beauty \[while walking in front of you\]; his elegant walk makes him deserve a ceremonial umbrella as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 11.1 “*agrata: prayayau*” (śrī rāma walks first).  [periyaḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/periyazhwar/) too explains the beauty of his walk/steps in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 3.6.4 “*ādal pādal*” pāsuram.
- *vāy koṇḍu* – I am not born to glorify lowly persons with my mouth/speech. If I praise some one else, how will your creation of me be fulfilled? sruśti (creation) is for self as said in śrī rangarāja stavm “*svamuddisya*” (for himself).
- *āy koṇḍa* – When asked “Though you are set out to praise him, is he not beyond words as vēdam itself returned unable to glorify him as in taittiriya upaniśat ‘*yatō vācō nivartantē*‘ (the words returned being unable to glorify [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) fully and even the mind cannot comprehend him)?”, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says he presents himself for me as said in jitantē stōtram “*bhaktānām*” (My names, forms etc (everything) are for my devotees only).
- *āy koṇḍa sīr* – His auspicious qualities which are well analyzed already \[by vēdāntam etc\] and are opposite to all defects.
- *vaḷḷal* – Very generous
- *āḻip pirān* – One who is having the tool (sudarśana chakra) which preserves these qualities in him.
- *enakkē uḷan* – he presented himself to be glorified by my poems exclusively.
- *āḻip pirān* … – He presented the divine combination of himself and his tools (sudarśana chakra etc) to be praised by me as said in tiruvāimoḻi 6.4.9 “*valakkai āḻi*” (having sudarśana chakra in the right hand) etc.
- *sāy koṇḍa immaiyum sādittu* – Bestowing me with radiant joy in this material ream. sāy – radiance. koḷgai – having. Making the present life such that it is more enjoyable than liberation too.
- *sādittu* – By having [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) as the sādanam (means),  [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) achieves everything in this material realm and in subsequent life in paramapadam (spiritual realm).
- *vānavar nāttaiyum* – śrīvaikuṇṭanātan (the lord of spiritual realm) is considered as one among the residents of paramapadam (though he is the lord); the ultimate abode is fully under the control of nityasūris (the eternally liberated servitors in paramapadam). As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 1.20 “*bhavadviśayavāsina:*” (the sages tell śrī rāma “we reside in the same kingdom as you”), the same concept applies for [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) too \[where he would joyfully say that he is residing in the same abode as the nityasūris\].
- *nī kaṇḍu koḷ enṟu* – śrī bharatāḻvān managed ayōdyā’s treasury during śrī rāma’s exile, grew it greatly and returned it with much greater wealth as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 127.55 “*krutam daśaguṇam mayā*” (śrī bharatāḻvān to śrī rāma “By your grace, this treasury is worth ten times now in comparison to when you managed it”). By saying “*vānavar nāttaiyum nī kaṇḍu koḷ*“, it is implied that [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) does not discriminate between a nityasūri and a newly liberated individual as a cow would ignore her previous calves after giving birth to a new calf \[if at all, newly liberated individuals are showered with more love by emperumān\]. This is explained in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 41.4 “*tvayi kincit samāpannē*” (śrī rāma to śrī vibhīśaṇāḻvān – even if you are suffering a little bit, what is the use of regaining sītā?).
- *enṟu* – saying with attachment like this
- *vīdum tarum* – will bestow kainkaryam (service); nigaṇḍu (dictionary) says “*mukti: mōkśō mahānanda:*” (mukti (liberation), mōkśam (liberation), mahānandam (great bliss) are synonyms).
- *ninṟu ninṟē* – Three explanations:
   - Our ācāryas explained this as – Even after giving everything, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) would feel “I have not done anything to him”, with agony in his divine heart as said in mahābhāratam udyōga parvam 58.22 “*ruṇam pravruttam iva mē*” (kriṣṇa thinking about draupati – I am worried like a borrower who is unable to repay the debt).
   - A tamiḻ scholar explained this as – emperumān would bestow the aforementioned aspects one by one – i.e., first he will let the individual enjoy worldly pleasures, then show him paramapadam and then give him the joy of kainkaryam.
   - Also explained as – emperumān will give sufficient experience of himself here in this material realm, attainment of parampadam and the joy of kainkaryam in small/adequate portions.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

adiyen saraty ramanuja dasan

## 3.9.10. Ninru ninru

*ninṟu ninṟu pala nāḷ uykkum ivvudal nīngip pōyc cenṟu cenṟāgilum kaṇḍu sanmam kaḻippān eṇṇi onṟi onṟi ulagam padaittān kavi āyinēṟku enṟum enṟum ini maṟṟoruvar kavi ēṟkumē?*

**Пословный перевод:**

pala nāḷ – forever; ninṟu ninṟu – remaining steadfast without any break; uykkum – will make (the cētana (sentient being) exist for); iv udal – this body; nīngip pōy – leaving; senṟu senṟu āgilum – even if a long period of time had elapsed; kaṇḍu – seeing (this cētana) in front; sanmam kaḻippān – to eliminate worldly birth; eṇṇi – having his divine will; onṟi onṟi – in every sruśti (creation), carefully with his full heart; ulagam padaittān – of the one who created the world; kavi āyinēṟku – for me (āḻvār) who is the poet; ini – further; enṟum enṟum – ever; maṟṟu oruvar kavi – praising any one else; ēṟkumō? – would it be suitable?

**Перевод:**

**emperumān is the one who carefully created the world in every sruśti (creation), with his full heart, having his divine will to eliminate worldly birth, seeing this (this cētana) in front, even if a long period of time had elapsed after leaving the body which will remain steadfast without any break in making the cētana exist for the body forever. Would it suitable for me (āḻvār) who is the poet of such emperumān, to praise any one else ever?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In tenth pāsuram – āḻvār says “For me who is sarvēśvaran kavi (poet who exclusively glorifies the supreme lord), it does not fit to praise others”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. ninṟu ninṟu pala nāḷ uykkum ivvudal nīngip pōyc cenṟu cenṟāgilum kaṇḍu sanmam kaḻippān eṇṇi onṟi onṟi ulagam padaittān kavi āyinēṟku enṟum enṟum ini maṟṟoruvar kavi ēṟkumē?*

- *ninṟu ninṟu* … – since time eternal without any break.
- *uykkum* – will conduct. \[The body\] will cause hindrance for the [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) \[in it’s spiritual progress\].
- *iv vudal* – \[this body\] [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) feels great fear in seeing the body like seeing death. This body and the previous bodies which are all same in category \[that they are all made of worldly matter\]. For āḻvār, even the previous bodies \[births\] feel connected with the current body \[like a train which has many compartments which are all connected\] and appear like present.
- *nīngip pōy* – leaving/shedding it
- *senṟu senṟu āgilum* – if not in one birth at least in some future birth
- *kaṇḍu* – this cētana will see me ([bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)) \[as thought by bhagavān “this [cētana](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) will realize me some day”\]
- *sanmam kaḻippān eṇṇi* – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) desiring “let him be relieved from the bondage in this world \[by realizing me\]”. Alternative explanation – considering “*senṟu senṟāgilum kaṇḍu*” as a single connected phrase – he contemplates “even if it takes a very long time, I should make sure that these souls do not take birth again”.
- *onṟi onṟi ulagam padaittān* – As said in periya tiruvantādi 18 “*sōmbādu ippal uruvai ellām padarvitta vittā*” (Oh the primordial lord who expanded the variegated manifestation without any lethargy repeatedly), instead of giving up if there is no result in one creation, emperumān who is putting his full heart engages in creation; as a farmer would plant the seeds and if it does not give a proper yield, do it over and over again until he gets the result, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) too creates with the thought that “if not today, some one will reach me some day”; this material realm is as said in nānmugan tiruvantādi 23 “*patti uḻavan perum punam*” (the great field of [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) who is the farmer who plants the seed of devotion in the heart of [jīvātmās](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)). \[summarizing, \] emperumān carefully creates the world (again and again) to free the ātmās from the bodies which keep hindering the ātmās by making them realize about bhagavān.
- *ulagam padaittān kavi āyinēṟku* – For me who became a poet of him by his efforts as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 2.7.6](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/05/thiruvaimozhi-2-7-6-madhusudhanai-anri/) “*edir sūḻal pukku*” (comes across from the opposite side and catches).
- *enṟum enṟum* … – Can I praise anyone else ever (until eternity)? It is his sauhārdam (kind heart) which made this happen \[for me\]. If that is the case, should it not happen for everyone? His sankalpam (divine will) will take effect over a period of time and it will not happen \[for everyone\] at once; thus, he will keep seeing (blessing) as [jīvātmās](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) are uplifted.
- *enṟum enṟum* … – From now on, this \[praising of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)\] is my routine forever in this body. Subsequently, for me who is going to praise him \[in paramapadam\] as said in taittiriya upaniśat “*ētat sāma gāyan nāstē*” (they are singing the sāma gānam) and in same upaniśat “*aham annam aham annam aham annam*” (I am the food enjoyed by [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) (repeated three times for emphasis)).
- *maṟṟu oruvar kavi ēṟkumē* – After being like this, can I praise anyone other than bhagavān? Also explained as – Am I fit to being the poet who praise others? Another explanation – Will I engage in hearing the praises of other poets?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.9.11. Erkum perum pugal

*ēṟkum perum pugaḻ vānavar īsan kaṇṇan tanakku ēṟkum perum pugaḻ vaṇ kurugūrc catakōpan sol ēṟkum perum pugaḻ āyirattuḷ ivaiyum ōr pattu ēṟkum perum pugaḻ solla vallārkkillai sanmamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ēṟkum – matching/apt (for paratvam (supremacy) and saulabhyam (easy approacability)); perum pugaḻ – being the one with great qualities; vānavar īsan – with the supremacy to rule over the nityasūris (eternal residents of paramapadam); kaṇṇan tanakku – for kriṣṇa (who appeared as sulabha (easily approachable)); ēṟkum – matching (among the ones who are great in praising bhagavān); perum pugaḻ – having great qualities such as jñāna (knowledge) etc; vaṇ kurugūrc catakōpan – nammāḻvār, the leader of beautiful āḻvārtirunagari; sol – mercifully spoken; ēṟkum – matching (to reveal the qualities etc of bhagavān); perum pugaḻ – having great characteristics; āyirattuḷ – among the thousand pāsurams; ēṟkum – which matches one’s true nature (in eliminating praising of others and explaining the praising of bhagavān); perum pugaḻ – having great qualities; ōr – unparalelled; ivai pattum – this decad; solla vallārkku – those who can recite; sanmam – birth (which causes praising of others); illai – not there

**Перевод:**

**kriṣṇa (who appeared as sulabha who is being the one with matching/apt great qualities with the supremacy to rule over the nityasūris;  nammāḻvār, the leader of beautiful āḻvārtirunagari, who is having matching great qualities such as jñāna (knowledge) etc (which are required to be counted among the ones praising bhagavān) mercifully spoke thousand pāsurams which are having matching great characteristics (to reveal the qualities etc of bhagavān); for those who can recite this unparalelled decad having great qualities which matches one’s true nature, among those thousand pāsurams, there is no birth (which causes praising of others).**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the end – āḻvār says “Even for those who simply memorize and recite this decad, there is no birth in this samsāram (material relam) where one should be taught ‘we need not praise any one other than bhagavān‘ \[in parampadam (spiritual realm), one will naturally praise bhagavān only\]”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār mercifully explains that there is no birth \[in this material realm\] for those who can recite this decad.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*In the end, āḻvār says “For those who have simply learned the pāsurams, there is no birth where one is qualified to praise any one other than emperumān“. ēṟkum perum pugaḻ vānavar īsan kaṇṇan tanakku ēṟkum perum pugaḻ vaṇ kurugūrc catakōpan sol ēṟkum perum pugaḻ āyirattuḷ ivaiyum ōr pattu ēṟkum perum pugaḻ solla vallārkkillai sanmamē*

- *ēṟkum* … – Being the one with great fame matching his nature. for [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is the leader of nityasūris, who appeared with the same supremacy and manifested such supremacy in the human form \[as kriṣṇa\]; in śrī bhagavat gītā ninth chapter his supremacy while being in a human form is elaborately explained by himself.
- *ēṟkum* … – As emperumān is aptly said as “*ubhaya vibhūti yuktan*” (one who is together with both spiritual and material realms), when said as “*sarvēśvaran kavigaḷ ivar*” (he is a poet of the supreme lord), he will be qualified to say so; mercifully spoken by such [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/).
- *ēṟkum perum pugaḻ āyiram* – This thousand pāsurams which is matching to have consumed [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) whose qualities can not be even measured by vēdam as said in taittiriya upaniśat *“yatō vācō nivartantē*” (the words returned being unable to glorify [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) fully and even the mind cannot comprehend him).
- *ivaiyum ōr pattu ēṟkum perum pugaḻ* – This decad among the thousand pāsurams. Having matching great fame. That is – since this decad instructed “Do not praise others which is not matching for the true nature of the ātmā” and “Come and praise the apt lord matching the true nature of the ātmā”, it will bestow all glories which is explained so far.
- *illai sanmamē* – nityasūris need not be trained by saying “Don’t praise others” \[they are naturally inclined to praise bhagavān only\]; only due to birth in this material realm, one sets out to praise others. Such persons who recite this pāsurams will not be born in lowly births where one is to trained explicitly saying “Don’t praise others”.
