## 3.10 Sanmam pala pala

## 3.10.1. Sanmam pala pala

*sanmam pala pala seydu veḷippattuc cangodu cakkaram vil oṇmai udaiya ulakkai oḷ vāḷ taṇḍu koṇḍu puḷ ūrndu( u)lagil vaṇmai udaiya arakkar asurarai māḷp padai poruda nanmai udaiyavan sīr paravap peṟṟa nānōr kuṟaivilanē*

**Пословный перевод:**

pala – in different species such as dēva (celestial), manuśya (human), tiryak (animal) and stāvara (plant); pala – in different inner categories of those species; sanmam – different births; seydu – assuming (not just with his vow, but physically being born amidst the particular species); veḷippattu – manifesting himself (so that his divine form which is beyond perception becomes visible for samsāris (worldly people)); sangodu sakkaram – Sanka (conch) and chakra (disc) which are inseparable from him; vil – śrī śārnga bow; oṇmaiyudaiya ulakkai – the club which breaks the enemies; oḷ vāḷ – nandaka sword which never gives up while destroying the enemies; taṇḍu – gadā (mace); koṇḍu – having these as tools/weapons; puḷ – periya tiruvadi (garudāḻvār); ūrndu – ride; ulagil – in this world (which is protected by him); vanmai udaiya – having hardness (without being attracted to such beautiful emperumān); arakkarai – rākśasas (demoniac persons among humans); asurarai – asuras (demoniac persons among celestial beings); māḷa – to kill; padai poruda – to march as an army against; nanmai – the goodness of honesty/straightness; udaiyavan – one who has; sīr – śaurya (valour), vīrya (bravery), parākrama (courage) and svāmitva (lordship), vātsalya (motherly affection) towards his devotees; paravap peṟṟa – to praise and speak about them elaborately; nān – I; ōr kuṟaivu ilan – have no dissatisfaction (in enjoying any aspect of bhagavat viśayam (matters relating to bhagavān) in any place, any time and any body)

**Перевод:**

**emperumān (who is said in puruśa sūktam “ajāyamāna: … ” (the unborn, assumes many births), being akarma vaśya (not bound by karma to take birth), ) assumes different births in different species such as dēva (celestial), manuśya (human), tiryak (animal) and stāvara (plant) and in different inner categories of those species and manifests himself (so that his divine form which is beyond perception becomes visible for samsāris (worldly people)) along with his weapons (the tools that help him protecting the devotees and destroying the demoniac which is the purpose of his incarnations) such as Sanka (conch) and chakra (disc) which are inseparable from him, śrī śārnga bow, the club which breaks the enemies, nandaka sword which never gives up while destroying the enemies and gadā (mace); with all of these, he rides garudāḻvār; he is the one who is having the goodness of honesty/straightness to kill by marching as an army against the rākśasas (demoniac persons among humans) and the asuras (demoniac persons among celestial beings) who are having hardness (without being attracted to such beautiful emperumān); for I who got to  praise and elaborately speak about śaurya (valour), vīrya (bravery), parākrama (courage) and svāmitva (lordship), vātsalya (motherly affection) towards his devotees, there is no dissatisfaction (in enjoying any aspect of bhagavat viśayam (matters relating to bhagavān) in any place, any time and any body).**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In first pāsuram – āḻvār explains the principles which are explained in this decad in short in this pāsuram saying “I enjoyed with loving devotion, the auspicious qualities of emperumān who incarnates many times to protect his devotees and who destroyed their enemies”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*In first pāsuram – āḻvār says “I who praised the multifarious qualities of emperumān who destroyed the enemies of his devotees through his incarnations, have no dissatisfaction”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*In first pāsuram – āḻvār explains the principles which are explained in this decad in short in this pāsuram.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*In first pāsuram – āḻvār explains the principles which are explained in this decad in short in this pāsuram; āḻvār says “I who enjoyed his incarnations, where he appeared with his divine weapons, have no dissatisfaction”;  āḻvār says “I who praised the auspicious qualities of emperumān who destroyed the enemies of his devotees through his incarnations to protect them, have no dissatisfaction”;  (sanmam pala pala) āḻvār says “I who meditated upon emperumān’s nature of assuming different forms even after being akarma vaśya (not bound by karma) which are despised even by those who are karma vaśya (bound by karma), have no dissatisfaction”;   āḻvār says “I who meditate upon emperumān who is being sarvēśvara, instead of feeling supreme and not mingling with the worldly people, assuming the forms where he goes through the same suffering like those worldly people and protect them, have no dissatisfaction”. sanmam pala pala seydu veḷippattuc cangodu cakkaram vil oṇmai udaiya ulakkai oḷ vāḷ taṇḍu koṇḍu puḷ ūrndu( u)lagil vaṇmai udaiya arakkar asurarai māḷp padai poruda nanmai udaiyavan sīr paravap peṟṟa nānōr kuṟaivilanē*

- *sanmam pala pala* – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) would assume several incarnations. Those who know that his nirhētuka krupā (unconditional grace) \[instead of karma, as in the case of bound jīvātmār\] is the cause for incarnations, would not pursue his supremacy \[in paramapaadam\] ignoring his incarnations. \[vēdam – scripture\] puruśa sūktam “*ajāyamāna: bahudā vijāyatē \| tasya dīrā: parijānanti yōnim”* (the intelligent persons know the reason of his births very well); \[vēdyan – [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) who is revealed through the vēdam\] he himself is very attracted towards his incarnations as said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 4.9](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/4-9/) “*janma karma ca mē divyam*” (my birth and activities are divine); \[vaidikar – those who are faithful towards vēdam\] [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) too who is the best among the intelligent persons is delighted saying in tiruvāimoḻi 5.10.1 “*piṟandavāṟum*” (his births …). The reason for āḻvār being immersed in devotion is due to his great knowledge about bhagavān. When there is abundance of sweetness in something, it is natural to become immersed in it.
- *pala* – āḻvār who become delightedly bewildered as in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.3.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/06/thiruvaimozhi-1-3-1-paththudai-adiyavar/) “*ettiṟam*” (how is this possible?) when thinking about one incarnation, what to speak of many incarnations?
- *pala pala* – It is said that – there is a boundary/end for the births of karma vaśya (one who is bound by karma) \[i.e., when the ātmā is liberated, there is no more births in the material realm\]; but there is no end to the births of akarma vaśya ([emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is not bound by karma) \[his incarnations are based on his desire to help bound souls, and will keep occurring for eternity\]. There is a limit to karma (cycle of birth/death) but no limit to anugraha (blessings). Even when he himself explained his births, he said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 4.5](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/4-5/) “*bahūni*” (countless).
- *pala pala* – differences in species such as dēva etc and the different internal categories in each of those species.
- *seydu* – While incarnating, instead of just appearing (out of nowhere), if a karma vaśya (bound soul) will remain in the womb for 10 months before coming out, emperumān would be born after remaining in the womb of 12 months as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam bāla kāṇḍam “*tataśca dvādaśē māsē*” (kausalyā gave birth to śrī rāma in the 12th month of caitrā on the navami titi). [periyāḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/periyazhwar/) (who assumed motherly mood towards [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)) highlighted in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 3.2.8 “*panniru tingaḷ vayiṟṟil koṇḍa appāngināl*” (yaśōdā saying – due to lovingly caring for kriṣṇa in my womb for 12 months). As said in yajur vēdam kātakam 3.9 “*pitā putrēṇa pitrumān yōniyōnau \| nāvēdavinmanutē tam bruhantam \|\|*” ([sarvēśvara](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) who is the father of the whole world, in his every birth, he accept one of his children as his father; the foolish people will not understand the glories of such incarnations of emperumān), emperumān who is the sarva kāraṇa bhūtan (cause of all), appeared as the kārya (effect) of one among his effects.
- *veḷippattu* – emperumān who is imperceptible as said in muṇḍaka upaniśat 3.1 “*na cakśuśā gruhyatē*” (not seen by the \[material\] eyes), makes himself visible. As a treasure which is buried under a place where one roams around becomes visible, emperumān incarnates and makes his divine form along with his paraphernalia visible for everyone. Presenting the form which is constantly seen by the spiritual eyes \[of nityasūris and muktas in paramapadam\], to the material eyes \[of worldly people\]. emperumān is making the material eyes see the divine form which is explained in periya tiruvantādi 28 as “*enṟēnum katkāṇṇāl kāṇāda avvuru*” (your divine form which cannot be seen with this material eyes).
- *sangodu* … – the brotherly inseparable relationship \[between [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) and his conch/disc\]. As in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 1.1 “*gaccatā mātulakulam bharatēna*” (one who is going along with bharata to his maternal uncle’s place as a sword will be take along by the owner). When he incarnates, he incarnates with his divine weapons \[who are all nityasūris\]. For those who desire to leave this samsāram \[material realm\], he descends along with those who are part of the goal. After seeing and enjoying [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), they would say as in tiruvāimoḻi 2.3.10 “*adiyārgaḷ kuḻāngaḷai udan kūduvadu enṟu kolō*” (when will I unite with your devotees in paramapadam?); to fulfil their desire immediately, he descends with his eternal associates in the form of his weapons.
- *sangodu sakkaram* – When one is sufficient \[to please the devotees and eliminate their enemies, emperumān out of great affection brings them all along\].
- *vil* – instead of just bring one per category \[of weapons, he brings them all along\]
- *oṇmaiyudaiya ulakkai* – oṇmai – knowledge. As said in tiruvāimoḻi 10.6.8 “*karudum idam porudu*” (whatever emperumān thinks, they will execute the task without even verbally being ordered), they are most intelligent.
- *oḷ vāḷ taṇḍu koṇḍu* – samsāris are the ones who see the divine divine weapons in his hands and think that he is having them to hurt others; unlike them, nityasūris would think that he is having them to add to his beauty; since [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is also one among them, he also enjoys them as adding beauty to him. He along with his weapons resemble a beautiful kalpaka tree with well expanded branches.
- *puḷ ūrndu* – this is another beautiful combination; as said in tiruvāimoḻi 9.2.6 “*ponmalaiyin mīmisaik kārmugil pōl*” (like a black cloud on top of a golden mountain \[[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) on garudāḻvār\]).
- *ulagil* – this beauty is enjoyed in the divine abode of paramapadam by nityasūris. That being the case, he presented the same experience in this material realm itself.
- *vanmai* … – The rākśasas and asuras whose heart don’t melt seeing this beauty. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) longs that everyone is tender like him in this matter \[relating to [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)\].  For him, as said in tiruvāimoḻi 9.6.2 “*ninai toṟum sollum toṟum nenju idindugum*” (every thought, every word, āḻvār’s heart becomes shattered). \[āḻvār becomes amazed at people for not being attracted towards such beauty and says \] One can remain “I am supreme” until they see [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/); but these rascals, after seeing the beautiful form of emperumān with divine weapons, are fighting him instead of surrendering unto him and serve him. He says “Instead of being captivated by his beauty, they are getting finished by his arrows”.
- *māḷap padai poruda* – To hurt them with weapons to finish them. After entering into the battle field, instead of speaking about non-violence or compassion about relatives \[like arjuna did\], emperumān has the goodness of destroying them since they are enemies to his devotees. Alternatively – his goodness of incarnating and physically fighting to kill them instead of killing them out of his sankalpa (divine will). [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) himself said in [tiruvāimoḻi 3.1.9](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/07/thiruvaimozhi-3-1-9-mazhungadha/) “*maḻungāda jñānamē padaiyāga – malarulagil*  
   *toḻumbāyārkku aḷittāl un sudarc cōdi maṟaiyādē*” (For those who worship you in this blossomed/expanded world, if you helped them with unfailing jñānam (knowledge) in the form of sankalpam (divine will) as your entourage, would that not reduce your greatly radiant lustre (of urgently arriving at the banks of the pond to protect your devotee)?). \[Is killing not violence, even if he kills the enemies of devotees?\] When one hesitates/skips performing animal sacrifices \[which are performed by well qualified persons for the upliftment of the animal being sacrificed\] as part of agnīśōmīya \[vaidika yajñas or hōmas – fire sacrifices\], one should atone for that \[i.e., one cannot go to a war and hesitate to fight. If one does so, then that is a mistake. Hence, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) killing the enemies of devotees in war is not wrong\].
- *nanmai udaiyavan sīr paravap peṟṟa nān* – I who spoke his auspicious qualities in a disorderly manner.
- *ōr kuṟaivu ilanē* – Two explanations:
   - I do not have the following dissatisfaction:
      - Like samsāris, not knowing [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) to start with.
      - Being unable to praise him in pāsurams after seeing his incarnations.
      - Being finished like śisupāla et all for considering [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) as “one among us” and insulting him.
      - Being bewildered like arjuna after seeing śrī viśvarūpam \[unable to comprehend bhagavān’s qualities fully\].
   - Do I have the dissatisfaction of  “not having this experience in paramapadam” after enjoying that same experience of his divine qualities in this material realm, which is explained in taittiriya upaniśat “*sō’śnutē sarvān kāmān*” (the [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) enjoys all auspicious qualities with [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/))?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.10.2. Kuraivil tadam kadal

*kuṟaivil tadam kadal kōḷ aravēṟit tan kōlac cendāmaraikkaṇ uṟaibavaan pōla ōr yōgu  puṇarnda oḷi maṇi vaṇṇan kaṇṇan kaṟai aṇi mūkkudaip puḷḷaik kadāvi asuraraik kāynda ammān niṟai pugaḻ ēttiyum pādiyum ādiyum yānoru muttilanē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kuṟaivu il – being complete in his togetherness; tadam kadal – in the ocean which is spacious (for reclining); kōḷ aravu – on very strong tiruvanantāḻvān (ādiśēśan); ēṟi – climb; than kōlam – having his beauty which highlights his supremacy; sem tāmaraik kaṇ uṟaibavan pōla – pretending to sleep such that his reddish lotus like eyes blossom; ōr yōgu puṇarnda – meditating upon his own unparalleled divine nature and the protection of all; maṇi – like a precious gem embossed on a gold plate; oḷi – having great radiance; vaṇṇan – having a form; kaṇṇan – (giving up such reclining posture as said in Hari vamśam “āgatō maturām purīm” (arrived at the city of maturā)) appeared as kriṣṇa; kaṟai aṇi – having a stain as ornamental decoration (due to breaking of the egg prematurely); mūkkudai – having divine beak; puḷḷai – periya tiruvadi (garudāḻvār); kadāvi – ride; asuraraik kāynda – destroying the asuras with his power; ammān – supreme person’s; niṟai pugaḻ – complete victorious nature; ēttiyum – (with devotion) praise; pādiyum – sing with music; ādiyum – (out of joy) dance; yān – I; oru muttu ilan – have no break/hurdle

**Перевод:**

**In the ocean which is spacious (for reclining) due to being complete in togetherness with emperumān, he climbed and reclined on the very strong tiruvanantāḻvān (ādiśēśan) with his beauty which highlights his supremacy and pretending to sleep such that his reddish lotus like eyes blossom and meditating upon his own unparalleled divine nature and the protection of all; in this posture, his form resembled a precious gem having great radiance, embossed on a gold plate; (giving up such reclining posture as said in Hari vamśam “āgatō maturām purīm” (arrived at the city of maturā)) appeared as kriṣṇa and rode garudāḻvār who is having a divine beak having the stain (due to breaking of the egg prematurely) which looks like ornamental decoration and  destroyed the asuras with his power; for me who is praising and singing with music the complete nature of such supreme person and dancing (out of joy), there is no break/hurdle \[in such experience\].**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In second pāsuram – āḻvār says “Since I am able to enjoy with great love, the glories of kriṣṇa who incarnates as the divine son of śrī vasudēva and eliminates the enemies of his devotees, after reclining in the tiruppāṟkadal (kśīrābdi – milk ocean) as the root for incarnations, I have no break/hurdle in such joy”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. kuṟaivil tadam kadal kōḷ aravēṟit than kōlac cendāmaraikkaṇ uṟaibavaan pōla ōr yōgu  puṇarnda oḷi maṇi vaṇṇan kaṇṇan kaṟai aṇi mūkkudaip puḷḷaik kadāvi asuraraik kāynda ammān niṟai pugaḻ ēttiyum pādiyum ādiyum yānoru muttilanē*

- *kuṟaivil tadam kadal* – Not just me – there are others who have no end \[says the āḻvār\]. While saying “*tadam kadal*” itself is sufficient to explain the vastness of ocean, the usage of *kuṟaivil* (endless) is not repetition, rather it is to indicate that the ocean is having endless bliss due to being in contact with [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) as explained in mudal tiruvantādi 19 “*tirumēni nī tīṇḍap peṟṟu – mālum karum kadalē en nōṟṟāy*” (To have the fortune of touching the divine form of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) – Oh ocean who is dizzy (due to the overwhelming bliss in such contact), what penance did you perform \[to achieve this\]?). As mother yaśōdā would place kriṣṇa in her lap and be blissful by pampering him, the ocean is having [sarvēśvaran](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) within itself and is blissful with endless joy.
- *tadam kadal* – the vast ocean where emperumān can rest in an expansive manner.
- *kōḷ aravu ēṟi* – kōḷ means radiance. Reclining on tiruvanantāḻvān (ādiśēśan) who has great radiance due to being in contact with [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/); Alternatively – kōḷ means strong, that is, having the strength to behold [sarvēśvaran](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) and [sarvēśvari](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/) together and handle their sports on him as said in stōtra ratnam 39 “*prakruśta vijñāna balaika dāmani*” (ādiśēśan who is the abode of great knowledge and ability).
- *aravu* – ādiśēśan who has tenderness, coolness, fragrance as natural attributes \[like a serpent has\].
- *than* … – emperumān’s reddish divine eyes which naturally \[without any additional decoration\] deserve to be performed the ritual of warding off evil-eyes, highlighting his ownership of everything, highlighting the joy of uniting with periya pirātti, which can be \[vaguely\] compared to fresh reddish lotus flower. *kaṇ uṟaigai* means sleeping. In the guise of sleeping emperumān is contemplating on the protection of all created beings \[in this material realm\].
- *ōr yōgu puṇarnda* – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) would be thinking “What is the means by which all creatures will cross-over the samsāram and reach me?”; when contemplating about their well-being, his tongue will become dry due to grief; at that time, like placing camphor on the tongue of a thirsty person, he thinks about himself as said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 6.4.7 “*ātmānam vāsudēvājñam cintayan*” (vāsudēvan emperumān meditates about himself). By contemplating about himself he will realize the means to protect everyone \[which is the avatārams (incarnations)\].
- *oḷi maṇi vaṇṇan kaṇṇan* – One who appeared as kriṣṇa to show his physical beauty and uplift those who are to be protected. periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 1.6.11 “*ātkoḷḷat tōnṟiya āyar tam kō*” ([emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) appeared as the leader of covherd clan to enslave them). kriṣṇa who is having the form which resembles a radiant precious blue gem.
- *kaṟai aṇi* … – Having a beak which is having blood stains after killing enemies and those stains looking like decoration; Alternative explanation – when garudāḻvār was inside the egg before birth, vinatā, his mother, wanted to see his face sooner and performed an action which caused a scar in his beak and that remained as an identity for garudāḻvār like [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) having the śrīvatsa mole in his chest as his identity. garudāḻvār having that scar/mole as an ornament.
- *kadāvi* – Like one would ride chariot etc. Due to the constant contact with emperumān’s divine form, having extended shoulder muscles and being kicked by emperumān \[to speed up\] while riding. stōtra ratnam 41 “*tvadangri sammartda giṇānga śōbhinā*” (garudāḻvār having beautiful scars caused by emperumān’s kicks while riding him).
- *asuraraik kāynda* – Destroyed the demoniac people by riding the garudāḻvār in this manner. It is explained here that the tool which pleases emperumān’s devotees \[garudāḻvār), is the same tool which destroys the enemies of the devotees too.
- *ammān* – The unconditional lord who ensures that the weak are not tortured by the strong.
- *niṟai pugaḻ …* – I who out of great loving devotion praise and sing [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) having endless fame due to such protection of his devotees, and dance out of great bliss. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says he has no break in enjoying [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/). muttu – vilakku (break).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.10.3. Muttil pal

*muttil pal bōgattoru tani nāyagan mūvulagukkuriya kattiyait tēnai amudai nan pālaik kaniyaik karumbu tannai mattaviḻ taṇṇan tuḻāy mudiyānai vaṇangi avan tiṟattup patta pinnai iṟai āgilum yān en manattup parivilanē*

**Пословный перевод:**

mūvulagukku uriya – being the distinguished lord for three types of cētana (nitya, mukta and badda) and acētana (sudda satvam, miśra satvam, kālam); muttu il – without break; pal bōgam – having multifarious enjoyable aspects; oru – unparalleled; tani nāyagan – being the distinguished leader; nal kattiyai – block of sugar which is sweet inside and outside; nal tēnai – honey which has collection of all tastes; nal amudai – eternally sweet nectar; nal pālai – milk which has the goodness of natural sweetness; nal kaniyai – well ripened fruit which is tempting to be eaten immediately; nal karumbu tannai – sugarcane which is sweet in each piece (thus emperumān who is having all kinds of enjoyable aspects); mattu – with honey; aviḻ – blossoming; taṇ – cool; am – beauiful; tuḻāy – being decorated with divine tuḷasi; mudiyānai – having divine crown; vaṇangi – (being won over by these enjoyable aspects) vorśipping him; avan tiṟattu – in his matters; patta pinnai – being totally surrendered (as ananyārha – not existing for any one other than bhagavān); yān – I (who am immersed in bhagavān, who is complete); iṟai āgilum – even a little bit; parivu – continuous craving (for sorrows due to unfulfilled worldly desires); manattu – in my mind; ilan – not having

**Перевод:**

**emperumān, being the distinguished lord for three types of cētana (nitya, mukta and badda) and acētana (sudda satvam, miśra satvam, kālam); being the unparalleled primmordial leader having varieties of joy; he resembles block of sugar which is sweet inside and outside, honey which has collection of all tastes,  eternally sweet nectar, milk which has the goodness of natural sweetness, well ripened fruit which is tempting to be eaten immediately and is sweet in each piece (thus emperumān who is having all kinds of enjoyable aspects); after becoming emperumān’s devotee who has very nice divine crown which is well decorated with divine tuḷasi; (being won over by these enjoyable aspects) I am vorśipping him and becoming totally surrendered (as ananyārha – not existing for any one other than bhagavān); this being the case, I (who am immersed in bhagavān, who is complete in bhagavat viśayam) have not even a little bit of continuous craving in my mind (that arises due to sorrows from unfulfilled worldly desires).**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In third pāsuram – āḻvār says “For me who is forced into serving sarvēśvaran as a result of meditating upon his sweetness, there is no sorrow in my mind”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*In third pāsuram – āḻvār says “For me who is forced into serving sarvēśvaran as a result of meditating upon his sweetness, there is no sorrow in my mind which arises out of attachment to lowly pleasures”. muttil pal bōgattoru tani nāyagan mūvulagukkuriya kattiyait tēnai amudai nan pālaik kaniyaik karumbu tannai mattaviḻ taṇṇan tuḻāy mudiyānai vaṇangi avan tiṟattup patta pinnai iṟai āgilum yān en manattup parivilanē*

- *muttu il* … – Unlike having hurdles/break after a few days, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is the unparalleled distinguished leader who has countless enjoyable aspects. That is, when he is said as the “leader”, there is no second person to be counted along with him in his capacity. Even brahmā et al are glorified as “leader”; to distinguish from them, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says “*advitīyanāna \[oru\] tani nāyagan*” (unparalleled distinguished leader). It should be read as “*mūvulugakku uriya – oru tani nāyagan*” (for the 3 types of both cētana and acētana – the unparalleled distinguished leader). *muttil pal bōgam* – Differentiates this pleasure from the pleasure acquired from aisvarya (worldly wealth) and kaivalyam (enjoying oneself). āḻvār feels – As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 2.13 “*trailōkyamapi nātēna yēna syānnātavattaram*” (In śrī rāma, all the three worlds have an apt leader) and in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 17 “*sarvalōka śaraṇyāya*” (rāgava, the refuge for all worlds) – can anyone praise emperumān like me \[without any break\]? Alternatively – “*mūvulagukkuriya – kattiyait tēnai*” – his enjoyable nature is also common for everyone to be enjoyed.
- *kattiyai* – being rasagana (filled with taste) inside and outside; taittirīya upaniśat “*rasōvai sa:*” ([bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is embodiment of taste).
- *tēnai* – same sweetness without the hardness of the katti (sugar block).
- *amudai* – that which gives immortality and has a distinguished taste.
- *nan pālai* – enjoyable for even ordinary persons. “nanmai” adjective is applicable for all these aspects.
- *kaniyai* – well ripened such that one would want to eat as soon as seeing it
- *karumbu tannai* – \[sugarcane\] being free from the defect of having to process it to sweeten it – naturally sweet without any additional process. Thus, as said in vēdam “*sarvarasa:”,* since none of these can fully explain his nature, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) himself (“*tannai*” on its own mean “himself”). This is āḻvār’s *śadrasam* (*aṟusuvai* – six tastes).
- *mattu aviḻ* … – Having a divine crown that is decorated with tiruttuḻāy (tuḷasi) which has abundance of honey in it. With these, the nature of emperumān who is the refuge, is established.
- *vaṇangi avan tiṟattup patta pinnai* – It is the intrinsic nature of śēśa bhūta (servitor) to worship him and approach his divine feet. After approaching him properly unlike kāla yavana, jarāsanda et al who surrounded his town with their armies and approached him.
- *iṟai āgilum* – even little bit.
- *yān* – I who am averse to worldly/sensual pleasures.
- *en manattup parivilanē* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says – Do I have any sorrow in my mind for “If I reach paramapadam I can enjoy him fully as said in taittirīya upaniśat “*rasam hyēvāyam labdvānandī bhavati*” (this [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) reaches [paramātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) who is embodiment of all tastes, and acquires joy) but here in samsāram I can enjoy only a portion of it”? \[No. He is already enjoying here like he would in paramapadam\].

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.10.4. Parivinri

*parivinṟi vāṇanaik kāttumen(ṟu) anṟu padaiyodum vandedirnda tiripuram seṟṟavanum maganum pinnum angiyum pōr tolaiyap poru siṟaip puḷḷaik kadāviya māyanai āyanaip poṟcakkarat(tu) ariyinai accudanaip paṟṟi yān iṟaiyēnum idar ilanē*

**Пословный перевод:**

anṟu – that day (when kriṣṇa himself arrived for anirudda, his grand son); vāṇanai – of bāṇāsura; parivu inṟi – removing the sorrows; kāttum – will protect’; enṟu – saying flowery words; padiyodum – with weapons; vandu edirnda – came and stood against; tiripuram seṟṟavanum – rudra who is proud about destroying tripura (the three towns); maganum – his son, subrahmaṇya who is having the greatness of being the commander-in-chief of the army of dēvatās (celestial beings); pinnum – further; angiyum – agni (who resembles rudra in his anger); pōr tolaiya – run away saying “we will never fight again”; poru – attacking; siṟai – having divine wings; puḷḷai – periya tiruvadi (garudāḻvār); kadāviya – rode; māyanai – amazing personality; āyanai – in the guise of incarnation, one who positions himself in a lowly stature (as a covherd boy); pon – attractive \[like gold\]; sakkarattu – having divine disc; ariyinai – destroying the enemies; accudanai – acyuta (one who does not abandon his devotees); paṟṟi – attain; yān – I (who am enjoying); iṟaiyēnum – even a little bit; idar ilan – have no sorrows

**Перевод:**

**On that day (when kriṣṇa himself arrived for anirudda, his grand son), rudra who is proud about destroying tripura (the three towns) came and stood against kriṣṇa saying “I will protect bāṇāsura removing his sorrows” along with his son subrahmaṇya who is having the greatness of being the commander-in-chief of the army of dēvatās (celestial beings) and agni (who resembles rudra in his anger), and kriṣṇa the amazing personality in the guise of incarnation, one who positions himself in a lowly stature (as a covherd boy)  having the attractive divine disc and riding periya tiruvadi (garudāḻvār) who is having attacking divine wings, made them all (rudra et al) run away saying “we will never fight again”; I who enjoy such emperumān who destroys the enemies and never abandons his devotees, have not even a little bit of sorrow.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In fourth pāsuram – āḻvār says “I approached emperumān who showed that the dēvatāntarams (other dēvatās) are not real protectors of those who took shelter of them, and became completely free from all sorrows”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “I who have taken shelter of emperumān who is the eliminator of hurdles that stop our enjoyment and who never abandons his devotees, am free from all sorrows”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Fourth pāsuram – āḻvār says “I approached emperumān who showed that the dēvatāntarams (other dēvatās) are not real protectors of those who took shelter of them and emperumān himself will never abandon those who took shelter of him, and I have no sorrows”. parivinṟi vāṇanaik kāttumen(ṟu) anṟu padaiyodum vandedirnda tiripuram seṟṟavanum maganum pinnum angiyum pōr tolaiyap poru siṟaip puḷḷaik kadāviya māyanai āyanaip poṟcakkarat(tu) ariyinai accudanaip paṟṟi yān iṟaiyēnum idar ilanē*

- *parivu inṟi …* – When kriṣṇa brought his army to rescue aniruddāḻvān, bāṇa went to rudra and said “kriṣṇa has arrived to fight us”. rudra replied “I will protect you to ensure that even the flower on your head does not lose its freshness”. He said that like a person who would speak about his chivalry from inside his own house \[instead of being in the battle field\]; is he saying like śrī rāma who vowed in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 18.33 “*ētat vratam mama*” (this is my vow)?
- *anṟu* – when aniruddāḻvān was imprisoned.
- *padaiyodum vandedirnda* – rudra as said in tiruccanda viruttam 71 “*muṇḍanīṟan*” (bald headed, having applied ashes all over his body), thinking that he is sure to win, brought along his army to see his victory. padai also means weapons. śrīviṣṇu purāṇam “*pāravaśyam samāyātaś śūlee*” (rudra who is holding the trident became unconscious on hearing the various sounds made by kriṣṇa).

Why did rudra come with weapons to fight kriṣṇa who should be vorśipped by performing an anjali (folded palms) to manifest one’s emptiness \[when it comes to protecting oneself\]?

- *tiripuram seṟṟavanum* – Due to rudra having great pride from tripura dahana (burning down the three towns) incident. As [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) took 8 forms while churning the ocean and helped dēvas, he also helped rudra during tripura dahana incident by being the strength in the bow, firmness in the bow-string, sharpness in the arrow and the antarātmā (in-dwelling supersoul) for rudra himself, won over the enemies and destroyed the three towns. Ignorant persons who did not understand all of these, praised rudra saying that he burnt down the three towns and rudra became bewildered hearing that, came to fight kriṣṇa thinking “If I can burn down the three towns, why can’t I defeat kriṣṇa?”. By this it is explained that rudra will abandon his devotees and run away when in danger \[what is said for rudra applies to all other dēvatās\] and [sarvēśvaran](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) will protect his devotees at all times.
- *maganum* – subrahmaṇya who is the son of rudra and who performed brave acts while being very young unlike his father \[who performed brave acts at a matured age\], who is like a brave young commander-in-chief of celestial beings.
- *pinnum angiyum* – Further 49 agni (fire dēvatās).
- *pōr tolaiya* – to be destroyed in the battle
- *poru siṟaip puḷ* … – The amazing lord who can ride garudāḻvār whose wings attack the enemies. Here “amazing” aspect is – kriṣṇa severing bāṇa’s hands, making him lord-less \[by driving away rudra\] and himself becoming the lord for bāṇa and his country. He is glorified in tiruccandaviruttam as “*vāṇan āyiram karam kaḻitta ādimāl*” (the primordial lord who severed bāṇāsura’s thousand hands).
- *āyanai* – rudra lost without giving up his stature \[as dēvatā\]; [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) won even in a lowered stature as a covherd boy.
- *poṟcakkarattu ariyinai* – holding the divine disc which is attractive to favourable ones \[devotees\] and being invincible for enemies. śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 5.33.41 “*kriṣṇa kriṣṇa mahābāhō jānē tvām puruśōttamam*” (rudra says – Oh kriṣṇa! Oh kriṣṇa! mighty-shouldered! I know your nature of being the puruśōttama and controller of all). rudra understood kriṣṇa’s supremacy only after seeing his mighty shoulders \[and their act in battle\].
- *accudanai* – One who does not abandon his devotees. rudra abandoned his devotee bāṇa and ran away from the battle field. But emperumān is explained in periya tirumoḻi 5.1.7 as “*sadaiyānōda adal vāṇan tadam tōḷ tuṇitta talaivan*” (the leader who severed the wide shoulders of bāṇa while rudra (one who is with matted hair) ran away). talaimai (greatness) indicates emperumān’s severing of hands and not taking his life. Since kriṣṇa took the arrows on his chest for aniruddāḻvān, there is nothing wrong in saying “[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is the refuge for his devotees”.
- *paṟṟi yān iṟaiyēnum idarilanē* – After holding on to him, I don’t even have a little bit of sorrow \[unlike anirudda who had a little bit of sorrow for being imprisoned for a few days\]; Since, anirudda is his grandson, he was imprisoned for few days; since I took shelter of him saying “*adiyēn*” (dāsan – servitor), I don’t even have to go through such suffering.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.10.5. Idar inriye

*idar inṟiyē oru nāḷ oru pōḻdil ellā ulagum kaḻiyap padar pugaḻp pārttanum vaidikanum udan ēṟat tiṇ tēr kadavic cudar oḷiyāy ninṟa tannudaic cōdiyil vaidikan piḷḷaigaḷai udalodum koṇḍu koduttavanaip paṟṟi onṟum tuyar ilanē.*

**Пословный перевод:**

idar inṟiyē – without difficulty; oru nāḷ – one day; oru pōḻdil – at a time (which is in between the completion of one karma (task) and the beginning of the next karma); ellā ulagum – for all worlds; kaḻiya – to go away from; padar pugaḻ – very famous (due to being surrendered to kriṣṇa); pārttanum – arjuna; vaidikanum – and the brāhmaṇa; udan ēṟa – climb along and go with; tiṇ tēr – the firm chariot (which does not go through any change even while reaching the causal region \[paramapadam\]); kadavi – ride; sudar oḷiyāy ninṟa – standing, greatly radiant, cangeless; tannudaic cōdiyil – his own abode which is indicated by the term “param jyōti” (supremely radiant abode); vaidikan piḷḷaigaḷai – the four sons of that brāhmaṇa; udalodum – with their unchanged bodies (since paramapadam does not get affected by change in time); koṇḍu koduttavanai – brought back and gave them to him \[brāhmhaṇa\]; paṟṟi – approached and enjoyed; onṟum – in any manner; tuyar ilan – remain free from worldly sorrows

**Перевод:**

**emperumān, one day at a particular time (which was in between the completion of one karma (task) and the beginning of the next karma), to go away from all \[material\] worlds, having the greatly famous arjuna and the brāhmaṇa climbing along in the firm chariot, rode it without any difficulty, reached his own greatly radiant abode which is indicated by the term “param jyōti” (supremely radiant abode), brought back the four sons of that brāhmaṇa with their unchanged bodies (since paramapadam does not get affected by change in time) and gave them to him \[brāhmaṇa\]; I approached and enjoyed such emperumān and (as a result of that) remain free from worldly sorrows in any manner.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In fifth pāsuram – āḻvār meditates upon the great incident of kriṣṇa rescuing vaidika putra (son of a brāhmaṇa) and becomes satisfied.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*In fifth pāsuram – āḻvār meditates upon the great incident of kriṣṇa rescuing vaidika putra (son of a brāhmaṇa) and says “For me who has taken refuge of such emperumān, there is no sorrow”. idar inṟiyē oru nāḷ oru pōḻdil ellā ulagum kaḻiyap padar pugaḻp pārttanum vaidikanum udan ēṟat tiṇ tēr kadavic cudar oḷiyāy ninṟa tannudaic cōdiyil vaidikan piḷḷaigaḷai udalodum koṇḍu koduttavanaip paṟṟi onṟum tuyar ilanē.*

- *idar inṟiyē* – without any difficulty
- *oru nāḷ* – On a day when the brāhmaṇa had taken a vow in a yajña which lasts just one day
- *oru pōḻdil* – After completing the morning rituals and before starting the noon rituals
- *ellā ulagum kaḻiya* – to go beyond the *āvaraṇa saptaka* (the seven layers which surround the material realm)
- *padar pugaḻp pārttanum* – arjuna who is greatly famous for accepting kriṣṇa as all types of relatives as said in mahābhāratam rājasūya parvam “*yasya mantrī ca gōptā ca suhrutcaiva janārdana:*” (janārdana who is the lord of all the worlds and is the minister, protector and friend of arjuna).
- *vaidikanum* – A brāhmaṇa who has endless attachments towards the divine feet of kriṣṇa
- *udan ēṟa* – climb along with him
- *tiṇ tēr kadavi* – Having them in the chariot, without disturbing the kāryākāram (state of being the effect), riding the chariot up to mūla prakruti (ultimate layer of primordial matter) by giving strength; like even when soil is in the state of a block, the structure of a pot is subtly present \[this is an example to explain how [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) managed to bring through the chariot (which is the state of effect) up to mūla prakruti (which is the state of cause) – an impossible task which is only possible by bhagavān\].
- *sudar oḷiyāy ninṟa* – oḷi means beauty. the abode which remained infinitely radiant and cangeless.
- *tannudaic cōdiyil* – His distinguished abode, where his radiance is well spread out. The abode cannot be seen by arjuna and brāhmaṇa due to it being the embodiment of the radiance of many millions of sun and moon as said in mahābhāratam āraṇya parvam “*atyarkkānaladīptam tat stānam viṣṇōr mahātmana:*” (the divine abode of the great viṣṇu which shines like many millions of sun/moon lit together). So, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) stops them at tamas (mūla prakruti – at the edge of the material realm), and since it is his own abode, he entered there alone; this abode is such that only dēśika (qualified visionary persons) can enter as fish swims in water.
- *vaidikan piḷḷaigaḷai* – the sons of the brāhmaṇa.
- *udalodum* … – He brought back the children without any change from the time they left the material realm, since time does not alter anything in the spiritual realm \[the children remained the same way\].
- *udalodum* … – Also explained as – He brought them back with the turmeric which was applied on them, the silk garment they wore, waist string and yajñōpavītam (sacred thread), decorations in their ears etc. [nanjīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nanjiyar/) asked [bhattar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/parasara-bhattar/) “If they were taken away as they were born, would these decorations have been applied?” and bhattar replied “since they are riśiputrar (children of a sage \[the brāhmaṇa is explained as a sage who has special powers\]), they can be born with these decorations”.
- *paṟṟi* … – It is difficult to bring water from ocean to a higher place, but is easy to bring water from a higher place to ocean. Similarly, to bring back any one from paramapadam  (spiritual realm) to samsāram (material realm) is not acceptable for [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s divine heart. His desire is to bring those in this material realm to the spiritual realm. Unlike the brāhmaṇa who forced emperumān to act against his will, for me who desired to go to paramapadam which is natural for me and pleasing to him – is there any sorrow? The children had to return since their karma (virtues/vices) were not exhausted yet. How did these children enter paramapadam where those who have exhausted their karma can only enter? This is because, the divine consorts wanted to manifest their independence \[to see kriṣṇa\] and thus brought them over there. Unlike them \[he is desiring with full heart to go to paramapadam unlike the children who were forcefully taken there\], [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says “I started in tiruviruttam 1 ‘*inninṟa nīrmai iniyām uṟāmai*‘ (I cannot tolerate this lowly samsāram any more) and concluded in tiruvāimoḻi 10.7.10 ‘*mangavottu’* (Please agree to remove all my material attachments) – manifesting my detachment in samsāram; my devotion towards [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) has grown as in tiruvāimoḻi 7.3.6 ‘*kādal kadalin migap peridāl*‘ (my love is greater than the ocean), tiruvāimoḻi 7.3.8 ‘*maṇ tiṇi jñālamum ēḻ kadalum nīḷ visumbum kaḻiyap peridāl*‘ (my love is greater than the world, seven oceans and great sky) and tiruvāimoḻi 10.10.10 ‘*adanil periya ennavā*‘ (my love which is greater than [cit (sentient beings)](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/), [acit (insentient beings)](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/09/thathva-thrayam-achith-what-is-matter/) and [īśvara (supreme lord)](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)). As I desire to go to paramapahdam with great love, I have no sorrow”.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.10.6. Tuyaril sudaroli

*tuyaril sudar oḷi tannudaic cōdi ninṟa vaṇṇam niṟkavē tuyarin maliyum manisar piṟaviyil tōnṟik kaṇ kāṇa vandu tuyarangaḷ seydu tan deyva nilai ulagil puga uykkum ammān tuyaramil sīrk kaṇṇan māyan pugaḻ tuṟṟa yān ōr tunbam ilanē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tuyar il – (since it is spiritual) being opposite to sorrow etc; sudar oḷi – (since it is sudda satvam (pure goodness)) very radiant resplendent form; tannudaic cōdi – his distinguished form which is termed as param jyōti (supreme light); ninṟa vaṇṇamē – in the same original state; niṟka – retaining; tuyaril – in sorrow; maliyum – subsisted; manisar piṟaviyil – in human birth; tōnṟi – appear/incarnate; kaṇ kāṇa vandu – presenting (his spiritual form which is imperceptible) to the human eyes; tuyarangaḷ seydu – engage (devotees and others in his qualities (physical, magnanimity, bravery etc)); than – his distinguished; deyvam nilai – divine supreme state; ulagil – in this world (which does not understand his greatness); puga uykkum – place firmly; ammān – one who is greater than all; tuyaram il sīr – one who is opposite to all bad aspects and the abode of all auspicious qualities; kaṇṇan – kriṣṇa; māyan – amazing person’s; pugaḻ – qualities and activities; tuṟṟa – closely enjoyed; yān – I; ōr tunbam – an undesirable aspect; ilan – not having

**Перевод:**

**emperumān retaining his distinguished form which is termed as param jyōti (supreme light) and is opposite to sorrow etc and is very radiant resplendent form, appeared in human birth which is subsisted with sorrow, presenting (his spiritual form which is imperceptible) to the human eyes and engaged in his qualities; he is placing firmly his distinguished divine supreme state in this world; he is greater than all and is opposite to all bad aspects and the abode of all auspicious qualities; after closely enjoying such amazing personality kriṣṇa‘s qualities and activities, I am not having any undesirable aspect.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In sixth pāsuram – āḻvār says “I who have enjoyed kriṣṇa‘s infinite beauty, have no trace of sorrow”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Sixth pāsuram. āḻvār says “I who have enjoyed the qualities of kriṣṇa who presented his spiritual form in a human form to be seen by samsāris (materialistic people), have no trace of sorrow”. tuyaril sudar oḷi tannudaic cōdi ninṟa vaṇṇam niṟkavē tuyarin maliyum manisar piṟaviyil tōnṟik kaṇ kāṇa vandu tuyarangaḷ seydu than deyva nilai ulagil puga uykkum ammān tuyaramil sīrk kaṇṇan māyan pugaḻ tuṟṟa yān ōr tunbam ilanē*

- *tuyaril* … – Being opposite of all defects, being infinitely radiant due to being fully in the mode of pure goodness, his divine form which is exclusive for him unlike that of anyone else.
- *ninṟa vaṇṇam niṟkavē* – Without losing anything from the form in paramapadam, like a lamp lit from another lamp, presenting himself here \[in samsāram\] as found there \[in paramapadam\]. Explained in śrī bhagavat gītā 4.6 “*svām prakrutim adiśtāya*” (I am situated in my own divine nature).
- *tuyaril* … – Appearing in the human births which are immersed in ocean of sorrow. śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 5.3.2 “*dēvakī pūrvasandyāyām āvirbhūtam*” ([kriṣṇa](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), the sun, appeared in dēvaki, the eastern direction).
- *kaṇ kāṇa vandu* – He, who is always seen by nityasūris and not qualified to be seen by material eyes, makes himself visible for these material eyes.
- *tuyarangaḷ seydu* – Hurt the favourable ones with his beauty and the unfavourable ones with his weapons. mahābhāratam “*krutvā pārāvataraṇam prutivyā: prutulōcana: \| mōhayitvā jagat sarvam gatas svam stānamuttamam \|\|*” (The beautiful eyed kriṣṇa relieved the burden of earth, bewildered the people of all worlds and ascended to his supreme abode) – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) hurt his enemies with thorn-edged stick and favourable ones with his beautiful eyes. As said by [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) himself in tiruvāimoḻi 7.7.1 “*iṇaik kūṟṟam kolō*” (pair of death-personified), emperumān’s eyes hurt his devotees with their beauty.
- *than deyva nilai* – his divine nature.
- *ulagil* – samsāram (material realm) which is undeserving
- *puga uykkum* – making the entry \[of his form into this world\]
- *ammān* – Here [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s prāpti (aptness) of revealing his nature without any expectation to the samsāris (materialistic people) is explained. He revealed his divine form/nature to samsāris because both the residents of paramapadam and the residents of samsāram have equal right to enjoy [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/). Also explained as – emperumān winning over the materialistic people by performing acts of going as messenger, being the charioteer etc.
- *tuyarm il sīrk kaṇṇan* – [kriṣṇa](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is devoid of bad aspects and abode of auspicious qualities.
- *māyan* – one who is having amazing qualities and activities.
- *pugaḻ tuṟṟa yān* – I who enjoyed his auspicious qualities at close proximity.
- *ōr tunbam ilanē* – If he blesses me to embrace and enjoy his spiritual divine auspicious form when I am in this material body, when I shed this body and go to paramapadam seeking the same thing, would he make that difficult to attain? \[So, I have no such sorrows\].

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.10.7. Tunbamum inbamum

*tunbamum inbamum āgiya sey vinaiyāy ulagangaḷumāy inbam il vennaragāgi iniya nal vān suvarggangaḷumāy man pal uyirgaḷumāgip pala pala māya mayakkukkaḷāl inbuṟum iv viḷaiyāttudaiyānaip peṟ(ṟu) ēdum allal ilanē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tunbamum – sorrow (in the form of dislikes); inbamum – joy (in the form of likes); āgiya – to occur; sey – done by (cētanas – sentient beings); vinai – karma (in the form of puṇya and pāpa); āy – being the controller; ulagangaḷum – for the worlds (where these can be performed); āy – being the controller; inbam il vem naragu – for hell where there is no trace of joy; āgi – being the controller; iniya – with pleasing enjoyable aspects; nal – nice; vān – best; suvarggangaḷum – regions of heaven; āy – being the controller; man – eternal (due to being present at all times such as the time when the karma is performed, the time when the results are reaped); pal uyirgaḷum – countless beings; āgi – being the controller; pala pala – countless (in different qualities, different intellectual levels, different tastes); māyam mayakkukkaḷāl – cētanas who are bewildered due to effects of prakruti (material nature); inbuṟum – causing enjoyment; iv viḷaiyāttudaiyānai – one who has leelās (sports) in this material realm; peṟṟu – attaining truly; ēdum – even a little bit; allal – suffering (in this material realm which is bound by karma); ilan – I don’t have

**Перевод:**

**emperumān is the controller of puṇya/pāpa karma which leads to sorrow and joy; he is the controller for the worlds where these puṇya/pāpa are performed; he is the controller for hell where there is no trace of joy and regions of heaven which have nice best pleasing enjoyable aspects (which are the result of such puṇya/pāpa); he is the controller of countless eternal beings; he is the one who is having countless cētanas who are bewildered due to effects of prakruti and thus having enjoyable leelās (sports) in this material realm; after attaining such emperumān truly, I don’t have even a little bit of suffering in this material realm.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In seventh pāsuram – āḻvār says “I enjoyed the joy acquired for emperumān through leelā upakaraṇam \[the tool for his sport – material realm\] and became free from sorrow”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Seventh pāsuram. āḻvār says “Since īśvara is akarma vaśya (not bound by karma \[virtues/vices\]) and since everything in this leelā vibhūti (material realm) is only for his sport, for me who meditated upon that, there is no binding in karma; I also don’t have to be involved in this material realm”. tunbamum inbamum āgiya sey vinaiyāy ulagangaḷumāy inbam il vennaragāgi iniya nal vān suvarggangaḷumāy man pal uyirgaḷumāgip pala pala māya mayakkukkaḷāl inbuṟum iv viḷaiyāttudaiyānaip peṟ(ṟu) ēdum allal ilanē*

- *tunbam* … – being the controller of puṇya/pāpa karma (virtues and vices) which cause happiness/joy
- *ulagangaḷumāy* – Explains the world where such puṇya/pāpa are earned. Also explains the abode of enjoyment.
- *inbam il vem naragāgi* – being the controller of hell where there is not even a trace of joy
- *iniya nal vān suvarggangaḷumāy* – being the controller of heaven which has a little bit of joy when compared to hell. When “*ulagangaḷumāy*” is explained as the abode where puṇya/pāpa is earned, this is explained as the abode of enjoying those effects of puṇya/pāpa; alternatively – if that was explained as enjoyable abodes, here, they simply speak about the joy and sorrow.
- *man pal uyirgaḷum āgi* – being the controller of the unlimited group of ātmās who are the kartā (performer) for the karma (action) and the bhōktā (enjoyer) of the result. Being the controller of the eternal countless ātmās.
- *pala pala* … – Having sports that are caused by the various intellects due to unlimited changes in material nature. How is this suffering of [jīvātmās](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) in separation from him, enjoyable \[as a sport\] for sarvēśvaran who is well wisher of everyone and most merciful? When he tries to protect them out of compassion, and if that \[protection\] is undesirable for them, that becomes amusing for him, and thus becomes part of his sport; this is the direct essence of why such suffering of cētanas becomes part of his sport. When the knowledge/consciousness that was given by him gets misused and causes disaster, he looks at śrī mahālakśmi thinking “I gave them knowledge/consciousness with a particular purpose, but they have used it for other reasons” and smiles, naturally it becomes part of sport.
- *ēdum allal ilanē* – For me who meditated upon his akarma vaśyatā (not being bound by karma), there is no karma vaśyatā (binding by karma); for me who meditated upon his creation etc as part of his sport, there is no sorrow of being involved in this material realm. [śrī bhagavat gītā 4.14](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/4-14/) “*na mām karmāṇi limpanti na mē karmapalē spruhā \| iti mām yō ’bhijānāti karmabhir na sa badyatē \|\|*” (Activities such as creation etc do not bind me (who is sarvēśvara); There is no desire for me in the fruits of the activities such as creation etc; Whosoever knows me well in this manner, he is not bound by the sins). śrī bhagavat gītā 7.14 “… *mama māyā duratyayā \| māmēvayē prapadyantē māyāmētām taranti tē \|\|*” (My material nature is difficult to crossover; those who surrender unto me, will cross over this material realm). As said by [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) himself “one who knows me thus, will not be bound by karma” and “Only those who surrender unto me to remove the bindings, are the ones who can cross over the material realm”, for me who fully depend on him to be relieved, there is no suffering.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.10.8. Allalil inbam

*allalil inbam aḷaviṟan(du) engum aḻagamar sūḻoḷiyan alli malar magaḷ bōga mayakkukkaḷāgiyum  niṟkum ammān ellaiyil jñānattan jñānamahdē koṇ(du) ellāk karumangaḷum sey ellaiyil māyanaik kaaṇṇanait tāḷ paṟṟi yānōr dukkam ilanē*

**Пословный перевод:**

allal – without any sorrow; inbam – quality of bliss; aḷavu iṟandu – without end; engum amar – pervaded everywhere; aḻagu – with beauty in all parts \[of his divine body\]; sūḻ – with; oḷiyan – being with overall beauty; alli malar magaḷ – with śrī mahālakśmi, the best among women, who is infinitely enjoyable due to having lotus flower as her abode; bōgam – due to the union; mayakkukkaḷāgiyum – (unable to distinguish between the two) being with blissful joyful form; niṟkum – standing; ammān – greater than all; ellai il – (like previously explained bliss, beauty and joy) boundless; jñānattan – having great knowledge; ahdu – that (which does not expect anything else); jñānamē – knowledge; koṇḍu – having; ellāk karumangaḷum – all worlds which are part of the effect; sey – (just with his divine will) being the controller; ellai il – boundless; māyanai – having amazing activities; kaṇṇanai – kriṣṇa; tāḷ paṟṟi – holding on to his divine feet tightly; yān – I; ōr dukkam – any sorrow; ilan – not having

**Перевод:**

**emperumān is with the overall physical beauty with the quality of bliss without a trace of sorrow and endless beauty which is pervaded in all his \[divine body\] parts; he is greater than all, standing with blissful joyful form due to union with śrī mahālakśmi, the best among women,  who is infinitely enjoyable due to having lotus flower as her abode; he is having boundless great knowledge with which he controls all of the worlds (which are part of effect); for me who is holding on tightly to the divine feet of kriṣṇa who is having boundless amazing activities, there is no sorrow.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In eighth pāsuram – āḻvār enjoys speaking about emperumān‘s experience in nitya vibhūti (paramapadam – spiritual realm).*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “I who have taken refuge at the divine feet of emperumān who is greater than all, divine master of śrī mahālakśmi and who controls everything just by his divine will, have no sorrow”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction. Also explained as āḻvār saying “I who have taken refuge of kriṣṇa who said ‘māmēkam‘ (me only) with pirātti’s puruśakāram (recommendation), have no sorrow”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Eighth pāsuram. āḻvār says “I who enjoyed emperumān‘s quality (simplicity) of protecting everyone in the world even after having the supremacy of enjoying the nitya vibhūti (paramapadam), have no sorrow”. allalil inbam aḷaviṟan(du) engum aḻagamar sūḻoḷiyan alli malar magaḷ bōga mayakkukkaḷāgiyum  niṟkum ammān ellaiyil jñānattan jñānamahdē koṇ(du) ellāk karumangaḷum sey ellaiyil māyanaik kaaṇṇanait tāḷ paṟṟi yānōr dukkam ilanē*

- *allal* … – Unlike svarga where there is joy mixed with sorrow and there is a limit to the enjoyment, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) has sorrow-less joy, complete happiness and unlimited bliss.
- *engum aḻagamar* – his lustre spreads all over the tripād vibhūti (paramapadam  – spiritual realm).
- *sūḻoḷiyan* – aḻagu explains avayava śōbhā (individual part-by-part beauty) and sūḻoḷi explains samudāya śōbhā (collective beauty).

Alternative explanation,

- *engum aḻagamar* – If we analyse from his divine feet to head individually, each part will be without any defect as one would say “Oh this part is nice! Oh this other part is nice!” and so on.
- *sūḻoḷiyan* – the whole of tripād vibhūti is flooded with his lustre. lāvaṇyam means pervading everywhere and visible everywhere.
- *alli malar magaḷ* … – Instead of this beauty being wasted like moon shining in forest, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) explains how his beauty is deeply enjoyed by śrī mahālakśmi who remains right in his chest. [sarvēśvaran](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) who is having amazing bliss due to union with infinitely enjoyable [śrī mahālakśmi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/), like flower and its fragrance together. mayakku – ānandam – bliss. mayakku also means union.
- *āgiyum niṟkum* – On top of the self-evident bliss, he would also have the bliss that is acquired due to being śrīya:pati (the master of [śrī mahālakśmi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/)).
- *ammān* – sarvēśvaran is embodiment of bliss and the master of śrī mahālakśmi.
- *ellaiyil jñānattan* – As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam bāla kāṇḍam “*manasvī*” (One who has his heart on her), in romantic aspects, his knowledge is much greater than her knowledge as a horse is much faster when compared to an elephant.
- *jñānam ahdē koṇḍu …* – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) will create these worlds in the material realm having jñānam (knowledge) that arises out of the union with śrī mahālakśmi as the only means without expecting anything else. [kūrattāḻvān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/kurathazhwan/) too explained this in śrī stavam 1 “*yasyā vīkśya mukham tadingita parādīnō vidattē’kilam*” (emperumān who looks at the facial reactions of śrī mahālakśmi and engages in creation based on such reactions). It is by this, taittirīya upaniśat’s “*bahu syām*” (let me be many) happens. For everyone else, union with worldly matters will lead to loss of knowledge, strength and form. But the union of emperumān and pirātti leads to the opposite \[i.e., leads to the well-being of entire creation\].
- *ellaiyil māyanai* – The amazing person who can perform sruśti (creation) etc just by his knowledge in the form of divine will.

Who is such person?

- *kaṇṇanai* – kriṣṇa. mahābhāratam rājasūya parvam “*kriṣṇa ēvahi lōkānām*” (kriṣṇa is the cause for creation etc).
- *kaṇṇanait tāḷ paṟṟi yān ōr dukkam ilanē* – With pirātti’s presence, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who would take care off our requirements with her recommendation and without assistance of anyone else, one who is filled with bliss as said in taittirīya upaniśat “*ēśa hyēvānandayāti*” (this [paramātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) bestows bliss) – for me who is surrendered to such emperumān, there is no sorrow.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.10.9. Dukkamil

*dukkamil jñānac cudaroḷi mūrtti tuḻāy alangal perumān mikka pal mā māyangaḷāl vigirudam seydu vēṇḍumuruvu koṇḍu nakka pirānōdu ayan mudalāga ellārum evaiyum tannuḷ okka odunga viḻunga vallānaip peṟṟu onṟum taḷarvilanē*

**Пословный перевод:**

dukkam il – without trace of sorrow; jñānam – one who is having knowledge; sudar oḷi – very radiant; mūrtti – having form; tuḻāy alangal – decorated with tiruttuḻāy (tuḷasi) garland; perumān – sarvādika (greater than all); mikka – (as said in śvētāśvatara upaniśat as “… parāsya saktir vividaiva srūyatē …” (that supreme bhagavān who has full ability)) greatly excellent; pal māyangaḷāl – multifarious amazing abilities; vēṇḍum uruvu – forms (as desired by him) that are dear to him; koṇḍu – accepting; vikirutam seydu – performs \[wondrous\] activities (to make others think of him to be one among those species he is born in); nakka pirānōdu – rudra who has directions as cloth (naked) and who considers himself to be supreme; ayan – brahmā who is popularly known as aja (who is creator of such rudra); mudalāga – starting with; ellārum – every cētana (sentient being); evaiyum – acētana (insentient objects); okka – without any difference; tannuḷ odunga – to have them rest in a small portion inside him; viḻunga vallānai – one who has the power to protect them by swallowing them; peṟṟu – having attained; onṟum taḷarvu – any weakness (loss of strength); ilan – do not have

**Перевод:**

**emperumān is having knowledge without any trace of sorrow; he is having a very radiant divine form; he is greater than all, decorated with tiruttuḻāy (tuḷasi) garland, with  greatly excellent multifarious amazing abilities, accepts forms that are dear to him and performs \[wondrous\] activities. Not only that, he has the power to protect by swallowing all sentient beings starting with rudra who has directions as cloth (naked) and who considers himself to be supreme, brahmā who is popularly known as aja and insentient beings without any difference to have them rest in a small portion inside him. Having attained such emperumān, I do not have any weakness (loss of strength).**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In ninth pāsuram – āḻvār says “I who enjoyed the ultimately amazing vatataḷaśāyi (emperumān lying in banyan tree leaf during total deluge), have no weakness”. It can also be said that āḻvār is meditating upon total deluge.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “I who am surrendered to emperumān who is the protector in all manner and who is the companion when in danger,  have not weakness”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. dukkamil jñānac cudaroḷi mūrtti tuḻāy alangal perumān mikka pal mā māyangaḷāl vigirudam seydu vēṇḍumuruvu koṇḍu nakka pirānōdu ayan mudalāga ellārum evaiyum tannuḷ okka odunga viḻunga vallānaip peṟṟu onṟum taḷarvilanē*

- *dukkam il* … – sarvēśvara who is having knowledge which is opposite to all defects, infinitely radiant form and decorated with tiruttuḻāy (tuḷasi) garland which matches such beautiful form. alangal – garland.
- *mikka* … – with unlimited multifarious amazing abilities
- *vēṇḍum uruvu koṇḍu vikirutam seydu* – Accepting the forms that he desires and engaging in wondrous activities. That is – explaining the agatita gatanā sāmartyam (making the impossible happen) such as accepting a small form, swallowing the big worlds and resting in a banyan leaf.
- *nakka pirān* … – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is sarva rakśaka (protector of all) who has the ability to place all cētana and acētana to save them from praḷaya (total deluge). cētanas include rudra who is popularly known as a favourer for his devotees, brahmā who has the fame of being the father of such rudra. “*odunga viḻungugai*” means – as said in periya tirumoḻi 11.5.3 “*ēḻulaguṇḍum idam udaittu*” (there is lot of space in his stomach even after consuming all the worlds), the worlds settling down nicely instead of appearing like cluster fig strung in a stick (without any sequence/match). Such emperumān …
- *peṟṟu onṟum taḷarvilanē* – Do I have any sorrow after taking shelter of sarvaśakti (omnipotent lord) without any expectation? During naimittika praḷayam (partial deluge), since [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) protects the 3 worlds which are to be protected by the dēvatās, he is the real protector of all (including those dēvatās).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 3.10.10. Talarvinriye

*taḷarvinṟiyē enṟum engum paranda tani mudal jñānam onṟāy aḷavudai aim pulangaḷ aṟiyā vagaiyāl aruvāgi niṟkum vaḷaroḷi īsanai mūrttiyaip pūdangaḷ aindai iru sudaraik kiḷaroḷi māyanaik kaṇṇanait tāḷ paṟṟi yān onṟum kēdilanē*

**Пословный перевод:**

enṟum – at all times; engum – in all places; taḷarvu inṟiyē – being complete without relaxing (from his ability to control); paranda – being all pervading; tani – unparalleled; mudal – the cause for everything; jñānam onṟāy – identified exclusively by knowledge; aḷavudai – limited in capacity; aim pulangaḷ – for the five senses; aṟiyā vagai – being imperceptible; aruvāgi – being without any avayava (parts/limbs); niṟkum – present \[as antaryāmi (in-dwelling super soul\]; vaḷar – grown (due to having control by pervading); oḷi – having radiance; īsanai – being the lord; mūrttiyai – with distinguished divine form; pūdangaḷ aindai – panca bhūtas (five great elements), in samaśti sruśti stage (initial creation); iru sudarai – candra (moon) and āditya (sun), in vyaśti sruśti stage (subsequent variegated creation) (since having them as śarīra (body), they can be said as him); kiḷar – grown due to incarnating; oḷi – greatly radiant; māyanai – having amazing qualities; kaṇṇanai – kriṣṇa; tāḷ paṟṟi – being surrendered to the divine feet; yān – I; enṟum – always; kēdu ilan – am free from destruction/disaster

**Перевод:**

**emperumān is all pervading being complete without relaxing (from his ability to control) at all times in all places; he is identified exclusively by unparalleled knowledge which is the cause for everything; he is present \[as antaryāmi\] without any avayava (parts/limbs) being imperceptible for the five senses which are limited in capacity; he is the lord with well grown radiance and with distinguished form; he is panca bhūtas, candra and āditya (since having them as śarīra (body), they can be said as him);kriṣṇa who has greatly grown radiance due to incarnating, who is having amazing qualities; I am always free from destruction/disaster, having surrendered to the divine feet of such emperumān.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In tenth pāsuram – āḻvār says “There is no disaster for me who vorśipped kriṣṇa who is having the entire creation as his body, who has pervaded as the antaryāmi in every entity and still cannot be perceived by their senses”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Tenth pāsuram. āḻvār says “There is no disaster for me who is surrendered to emperumān who is the antarātmā of entire creation, who sustains everyone and who protects those who are friendly towards him by incarnating with distinguished form”. taḷarvinṟiyē enṟum engum paranda tani mudal jñānam onṟāy aḷavudai aim pulangaḷ aṟiyā vagaiyāl aruvāgi niṟkum vaḷaroḷi īsanai mūrttiyaip pūdangaḷ aindai iru sudaraik kiḷaroḷi māyanaik kaṇṇanait tāḷ paṟṟi yān onṟum kēdilanē*

- *taḷarvu inṟiyē …* – Two explanations.
   - Without any ***loss*** while being present everywhere at all times, and while engaging in sruśti (creation), having unparalleled knowledge in the form of sankalpa (will).
   - Pervading at all places without skipping any place at all times in a singular form, being the trivida kāraṇa (three types of causes upādāna kāraṇa (material cause), sahākārika kāraṇa (ancillary cause) and nimitta kāraṇa (instrumental cause)) while creating everything, being an embodiment of distinguished knowledge.
- *aḷavudai* … – Just as it is not possible to measure an ocean with a measuring can, sensory organs which only perceive matter (which is perceivable), cannot perceive the imperceptible bhagavān.
- *aruvāgi niṟkum* – bhagavān will remain imperceptible by those sensory organs.
- *vaḷar oḷi īsanai* – When he remains the antarātmā of [cētana (sentient](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) entity) and [acētana (insentient entity)](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/09/thathva-thrayam-achith-what-is-matter/) in this manner, would their defects not contaminate him? No. As said in rig vēdam “*dvā suparṇā sayujā sakhāyā samānam vrukśam pariśasvajātē \| tayōranya: pippalam svādvatti anaśnannanyō abicākasīti \|\|*” (There are two related (servant and master) birds ([jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) and [paramātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)) residing in a tree (body). One bird ([jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)) enjoys the fruits of its actions (karma) and the other one (paramātmā) being detached is radiantly witnessing that), being untouched by their defects, he would have the radiance acquired by his niyantrutva (controlling ability).
- *mūrttiyai* – While being jagat śarīri (having entire creation as his body), he is also present with spiritual divine form in nitya vibhūti (paramapadam – spiritual realm).
- *pūtangaḷ aindai iru sudarai* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) enjoys [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s both aspects – that is, being with divine form and being with the entire creation as his body. To indicate that, āḻvār said “*pūtangaḷ aindai iru sudarai*” – his being the controller of leelā vibhūti (material realm) is explained by highlighting panca bhūta (five great elements) which are part of kāraṇa (intermediary cause) and candra/sūrya (moon/sun) which are part of the final effect.
- *kiḷar oḷi māyanaik kaṇṇanai* – emperumān who descended as kriṣṇa into this material realm bringing along his spiritual divine paraphernalia/form.
- *kaṇṇanait tāḷ paṟṟi* – Holding on to the divine feet of emperumān who said as in śrī bhagavat gītā 18.66 “*mām ēkam śaraṇam vraja*” (surrender unto me only).
- *yān enṟum kēdilanē* – There is no disaster for me who properly held on to the divine feet of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who sustains due to the eternal relationship with the [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/), even when the ātmā is shying away from him and when that ātmā becomes friendly towards him, he appears in front and protects the ātmā.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.
