## 3.10.11. Kedil viluppugal

*kēdil viḻuppugaḻk kēsavanaik kurugūrc catakōpan sonna pādal ōr āyirattuḷ ivaiyum oru pattum payiṟṟa vallārgatku avan nādum nagaramum nagudan kāṇa nalanidai ūrdi paṇṇi vīdum peṟuttit tan mūvulagukkum tarum oru nāyagamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kēdu il – (since opposite to all defects) being imperishable; viḻu – excellent (since auspicious); pugaḻ – having qualities; kēsavanai – kriṣṇa who is the destroyer of kēśi (the demoniac horse); kurugūr – leader of āḻvārtirunagari; satakōpan – nammāḻvār; sonna – mercifully spoke; pādal – in the form of song; ōr – unparalleled; āyirattuḷ – among the thousand pāsurams; oru – the one which bestows experience of bhagavān; ivai pattum – this decad; payiṟṟa vallārgatku – those who can recite to reflect the richness of the words and the meanings; avan – such kriṣṇa; nādum – the country side (which has more illiterate people); nagaramum – the cities (which have more knowledgeable people); nangudan – with fame; kāṇa – to see; nalanidai – with the wealth of servitude towards bhagavān and bhāgavatas; ūrdi paṇṇi – conduct; vīdum – mōkśānandam (bliss of liberation); peṟutti – bestow; than mūvulagukkum – due to the relationship with him, to independently enjoy the three types of cētana and acētana, like he would do; (avaṟṟukku – for them); oru nāyagam – being the unparalleled leader; tarum – will bestow

**Перевод:**

**nammāḻvār, the leader of āḻvārtirunagari, mercifully spoke in the form of a song this decad which bestows experience of bhagavān among the unparalleled thousand pāsurams about kriṣṇa who is the destroyer of kēśi (the demoniac horse) and is having imperishable excellent qualities; such kriṣṇa would conduct those who can recite to reflect the richness of the words and the meanings, with great fame to be seen by the people of country side and cities, with them having the wealth of servitude towards bhagavān and bhāgavatas, bestow them mōkśānandam (bliss of liberation) and let them independently enjoy the three types of cētana and acētana, like he would do and would bestow them unparalleled leadership.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the end – āḻvār says “Those who practice this decad, emperumān would conduct them with great fame with vaiṣṇavaśrī (the wealth of being a vaiṣṇava) in this material realm, bring them along to tirunādu (paramapadam – spiritual realm) and will present all his wealth at their disposal”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār explains the attainment of self-rule as result of this decad.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. kēdil viḻuppugaḻk kēsavanaik kurugūrc catakōpan sonna pādal ōr āyirattuḷ ivaiyum oru pattum payiṟṟa vallārgatku avan nādum nagaramum nagudan kāṇa nalanidai ūrdi paṇṇi vīdum peṟuttit than mūvulagukkum tarum oru nāyagamē*

- *kēdu il* – Without any defect and having excellence.
- *pugaḻ* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) glorified the kēśihantā (destroyer of kēśi), kriṣṇa, who is having eternally present auspicious qualities.
- *kurugūrc catakōpan sonna* – As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam bāla kāṇḍam “*raghuvara caritam muni praṇītam*” (History of śrī rāghava (śrī rāma) spoken by the sage vālmīkī bhagavān \[who only speaks about śrī rāma\]), this is spoken by nammāḻvār who is fixated on \[kriṣṇa\] avatāram.
- *pādal ōr āyiram* – As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam bāla kāṇḍam 4.8 “*pātyē gēyē ca maduram*” (both words and music are sweet), the pāsurams were born (sung) with music.
- *ivaiyum oru pattum* – Like an expert in pearl makes a string of pearls, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says “this unparalleled decad”.
- *payiṟṟa vallārgatku* – those who can recite. payiṟṟa = payila which means those who can practice. “*avan tarum*” (he will bestow) is to be added here to frame the sentence properly.
- *nādu* – aviśēśajñar (non-experts, simple-minded people)
- *nagaramum* – those who are experts in principles
- *nangudan kāṇa* – to see them with goodness. To glorify him saying “what a great person!”.
- *nalanidai ūrdi paṇṇi* – to make him conduct in goodness. goodness is śrīvaiṣṇavaśrī (wealth of being a śrīvaiṣṇava).
- *vīdum peṟutti* – bestow him parama puruśārta mōkśam (the ultimate liberation of engage in uninterrupted pure kainkaryam).
- *than mūvulagukkum tarum oru nāyagam* – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) will make this ātmā as the unparalleled leader of the three types of jīvātmās (nitya – eternally free souls in paramapadam, mukta – liberated souls in paramapadam and badda – bound souls in samsāram) who are subservient to emperumān himself. emperumān will present his wealth/control to the ātmā to make him think that it is his (ātmā’s) own wealth. That is – when emperumān presents his wealth to this ātmā, instead of staying aloof from it, the ātmā will also clearly think that he is also part of that wealth of emperumān.

## Fourth Centum

## 4.1 Oru nayagamay

## 4.1.1. Oru nayagamay

*oru nāyagamāy ōda ulagudan āṇḍavar karu nāy kavarnda kālar sidaigiya pānaiyar peru nādu kāṇa immaiyilē piccai tām koḷvar tirunāraṇan tāḷ kālam peṟac cindittuymminō*

**Пословный перевод:**

oru nāyagamāy – having supremely independent empire; ōda – to conduct (for a lengthy period of time); ulagu – with the world; udan – fitting firmly; āṇḍavar – those who protected their kingdom; karu – black (unable to distinguish from the darkness); nāy – by a dog; kavarnda – bitten; kālar – having leg; sidaigiya – (useless) broken and discarded; pānaiyar – having that as the pot for begging; peru nādu – by the people of this great earth (which was once ruled by them); kāṇa – to be seen; immaiyilē – in this birth itself; piccai – alms; tām – themselves (asking after giving up their shame); koḷvar – will accept; tiru – being nityaśrī (eternally wealthy); nāraṇan – (the natural lord) nārāyaṇan’s; tāḷ – divine feet; kālam peṟa – immediately, without wasting any time; sindittu – meditate upon; uymmin – be uplifted

**Перевод:**

**Those emperors who are conducting supremely independent empire, fitting firmly in the world and protecting their kingdom, (when their wealth gets destroyed, would beg in the night) have their leg bitten by black dog , having a broken and discarded pot (shell/skull) for begging, will accept alms themselves to be seen by the people of this great earth (which was once ruled by them). (Since aiśvaryam (worldly wealth) is temporary,) meditate upon the eternally wealthy lord nārāyaṇan’s divine feet immediately, without wasting any time and be uplifted.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In first pāsuram – āḻvār says “Emperors will \[one day\] lose their kingdom and miserably live by begging. This being the case,  approach the divine feet of tirunārāyaṇan (śrīman nārāyaṇan) who is eternally wealthy, and be uplifted”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam – maṇḍōdari’s words “śrīvatsavakśānityaśrī:” (the eternally wealthy lord with śrīvatsa mole in his chest) is quoted to highlight emperumān‘s eternal wealth. oru nāyagamāy ōda ulagudan āṇḍavar karu nāy kavarnda kālar sidaigiya pānaiyar peru nādu kāṇa immaiyilē piccai tām koḷvar tirunāraṇan tāḷ kālam peṟac cindittuymminō*

- *oru nāyagamāy* – humans who hold on to impermanent wealth and burst like bubbles; these kings, like pauṇḍraka vāsudēva (who imitated kriṣṇa, to be killed by kriṣṇa in the end) – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying “*oru nāyagamāy*“, as they think their wealth is similar to [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s wealth as said in nārāyaṇa sūktam “*patim viśvasya*” (the lord of the entire creation); being singular emperor.
- *ōda* – How long this \[ruling\] goes on? for a very lengthy period of time. As said in “60000 years, 70000 years”.

What is being ruled?

- *ulagu* – the whole earth which is surrounded by the ocean. As said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 4.2.65 “*māndātu: kśētramucyatē*” (māndātā’s kingdom spreads from where the sun rises to where it sets); they would rule it effortlessly like managing a small field.
- *udan āṇḍavar* – Two explanations:
   - Those who ruled the earth fully having no place outside their regime.
   - Those who ruled with authority over every single person as in the case of kārtavīryārjuna who would at once appear with his bow and arrow in front of those who think to engage in sinful activities (even before they set out to performing such activities) as said in raghu vamśam 6 “*akārya cintā sama kālam Eva prāturbhavamś cāpadara: purastāt*“.

What will such independent emperors, who ruled the world for too long,  do? [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says they will suffer after losing their kingdoms as said in “*rājyam nāma mahā vyādi racikitsyō vināśana: \| bhrātaram vāsutamvāpityajanti bhūmipā: \|\|*” (kingdom is an uncurable and disaster-causing disease; don’t people even give up brothers and sons for the sake of kingdom?).

- *karu nāy kavarnda kālar* – After living a royal life for a very long time, one would not tolerate hunger \[while living a simple life, after losing the kingdom\] and say “let me fast today”; with great desire to live, he would set out to beg; but since he lived a royal life, out of shame, he will not go in the day time; he would instead go in the dark night and in dark areas; black dogs would be present in some places like a collection of darkness; not seeing them, he will step into their mouth; they will bite.
- *karu nāy* – karu indicates anger – angry dog; karu also means pregnant/nursing mother; since its a dog which gave birth to pups, it is protecting them and when it sees people nearby, it will chase and bite those who come near by.
- *kālar* – they were previously identified as “those who are wearing anklets of bravery”; now they are identified as “those whose legs are bitten by dog”.
- *sidaigiya pānaiyar* – Searching everywhere, they will only find a useless broken pot. Previously they ate in a golden pot, but now their state is such that they can not even find a new earthen pot. That too, when some one gives some alms, that will fall through the holes in the pot.
- *peru nādu kāṇa* – Previously, everyone will bring offerings to them and wait at their entrance for 6 months, 1 year and so on, unable to gain entry; in contrast, now everyone can see them. Another explanation – since they lived a royal life previously and then became poor, everyone will come to see their transformation.

Does this transformation happen in a subsequent birth?

- *immaiyilē* – in the same birth where they lived a royal life before.
- *piccai* – Previously they would give smaller kingdoms to other regional kings; now all they expect is little bit of alms.
- *tām koḷvar* – Previously, when regional kings bring them gifts, they will collect those gifts through their representatives, since it hurts their ego to accept from certain people; now, they accept themselves without seeing who is giving.

This being the worth of worldly kingdoms,

- *tirunāraṇan tāḷ* – periya tirumoḻi 6.9.1 “*idar kedutta tiruvāḷan iṇaiyadi*” (the divine feet of śrīman nārāyaṇan who removed the sorrows of rudra). Approach the divine feet of śrīman nārāyaṇan and be uplifted. matsya purāṇam “*tatra nārāyaṇa śrīmān mayā bhikśām prayācita:*” (rudra says – I begged that śrīman nārāyaṇan for alms). Other than emperumān, there is no other refuge for those who beg with a pot (shell/skull) in their hand; periya tirumoḻi 3.4.2 “*ōttūṇoḻitta*“van (one who eliminated the need to beg with pot/shell).
- *tāḷ* – When bharatāḻvān was asked “when will you be relieved of internal agony?”, he replied as in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 98.8 “*yāvanna caraṇau bhrātu: pārtivavyanjanānvidau śirasā dārayiśyāmi…*” (Until I behold the divine feet of my brother śrī rāma who has all qualities of being a king, I will not have peace), “When perumāḷ is crowned with suitable throne for him \[being the lord\], and I being crowned with suitable throne for me \[being the servitor\], my distress will be removed” – such divine feet. This is explained in perumāḷ tirumoḻi 10.7 “*arasamarndān adi sūdum arasu*” (the crown of the lotus feet of śrī rāma being the emperor). [kulaśēkarāḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/kulasekarazhwar/) desires to be living at the divine feet of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/).
- *kālam peṟa* – Even if it is a small moment, one should come as early as possible. One cannot postpone this to the next day since “*jīvitam maraṇāntam hi jarāntē rūpa yauvanē \| sampadaśca vināśāntājānan kōdrutimāpnuyāt \|\|*” (life ends with death, youth ends with old age, wealth ends with destruction – how can the one who knows this be fearless?). Thus one should not say “I will surrender unto emperumān tomorrow”; garuda purāṇam pūrva 222.22 “*yanmuhūrtam kśaṇam vāpi vāsudēvō na cintyatē \|  sā hānistanmahaccidram sā bhrāntis sā ca vikriyā \|\|*” (if in a muhūrta \[48 minutes of our time\] or in a moment vāsudēva is not thought of, that is a great loss; that is great sorrow; that becomes illusory; that is deterioration) – such lapse in thinking for a moment leads to the disaster of making him to be non-existing as said in taittirīya upaniśat “*asannēva*“. “*tanmahaccidram*” (great sorrow) – this leads to disaster. “*sā bhrānti*:” (confusion) – this is *viparīta jñānam* (adverse knowledge). “*sā vikriyā*” (deterioration) – this is prohibited conduct.
- *sindittu* – Don’t give reason that there is nothing \[no tool\] to reach him \[mind is present\]; Use the faculty (mind) that was given by him for him; when this is understood in the heart, one can meditate; śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 1.17.78 “*smrutōyaccatiśōbanam*” (what is the difficulty in thinking about [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)?).
- *uymminō* – such meditation ends with the goal \[of upliftment\]. Since [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) thinks that all should get this benefit, he is telling this to all \[in plural\].
- *uymminō* – If there is no \[care for\] *adi* (feet, root), one (devotee, plant) will become dry; so one should care for the *adi* (feet, root) and be uplifted/revived.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.1.2. Uymmin

*uymmin tiṟai koṇarndenṟulagaṇḍavar immaiyē tammin suvai madavāraip piṟar koḷḷat tām vittu vemmin oḷi veyil kānagam pōyk kumai tinbargaḷ semmin mudit tirumālai viraindadi sērminō*

**Пословный перевод:**

tiṟai – tribute; koṇarndu – bringing along; uymmin – survive; enṟu – saying this (just words, not even action); ulagu – world; āṇḍavar – who ruled over; immaiyē – in the same life; tam – their exclusive; in – dear; suvai – pleasure giving; madavārai – wives (who are totally dependent on them and cannot live without them); piṟar – others; koḷḷa – to grab; tām – they themselves; vittu – abandon; vem – very hot; min oḷi – (having a blinding effect for the one who saw ) such expansive brightness; veyil – sunshine; kānagam – in forest; pōy – go; kumaitinbargaḷ – will be tortured (by other kings, there too); sem min – unstoppably radiant; mudi – having crown; tirumālai – divine husband of śrī mahālakśmi; viraindu – quickly with goodness; adi sērmin – surrender unto the divine feet

**Перевод:**

**Those kings who rule over the world saying \[to regional kings and others\] “you survive by bringing along the tribute”, in the same life, would abandon their exclusive, dear, pleasure giving wives to be grabbed by others; unable to stay in their kingdom, they would go into the forest where there is very hot sunshine, only to be tortured (by other kings, there too). Thus, you quickly with goodness, surrender unto the divine feet of the divine husband of śrīmahālakśmi, who is having unstoppably radiant crown.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In second pāsuram – āḻvār says “they (these emperors) will even lose their queens to those who defeated them”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “Since you may lose even your wife on top of losing your wealth, you take shelter of emperumān, the lord of śrī mahālakśmi, who is the supreme lord of all”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Second pāsuram. āḻvār says “These kings will not only lose their kingdom, but their enemies will even grab their queens with whom they enjoyed while ruling over everyone and will thus be in a pathetic state”. uymmin tiṟai koṇarndenṟulagaṇḍavar immaiyē tammin suvai madavāraip piṟar koḷḷat tām vittu vemmin oḷi veyil kānagam pōyk kumai tinbargaḷ semmin mudit tirumālai viraindadi sērminō*

- *uymmin tiṟai koṇarndu* – Instead of taking over kingdoms of their enemies by battling in wars, these emperors would tell other kings “if you want to save yourself, bring all your wealth and surrender that to me” and take over others’ kingdom. These great rulers need not fight battles, but can win over others just by their warning message of asking for tribute.
- *immaiyē* – in the same life where they ruled over others like this
- *tam in suvai madavāraip piṟar koḷḷa* – During his regime, such emperor would bring the women folks and wealth of other kingdoms and keep them; as he collected them, some one else would take over later; we have seen this when the town of narakāsura was destroyed \[kriṣṇa came and rescued all the women folks and eventually married them all too\]; proof for this is draupati’s insult in the great assembly, though pāṇḍavas had performed rājasūya yajña and were prideful before. To have their infinitely enjoyable women grabbed by their enemies.
- *tām vittu* – To save their own life, they will themselves carry the luggage of their women-folks and leave them willingly \[at the enemies’ place\].  As said in “*āpadartam danam rakśēt …*” (One should save wealth for emergency situations; even by spending such wealth, one should protect his wives; even at the cost of such wealth and wives, one should save oneself).
- *vem min* … – Thinking that “The enemy will torture me if I still remain in this place”, one would go to the forest which lacks water and human habitat. He will go to a forest where there is only mirage and hot sunshine. Alternative explanation – He will go to a forest where there is very hot sunshine.
- *kumai tinbargaḷ* – When one is wealthy, he will have assistants to finish any task; the current kings’ servants would say “we will go and destroy them wherever they are; give us the orders” and the kings too will order them to do that and fulfil their needs; so, even in such forests, they will not be spared.
- *kumaitinbargaḷ* – will be tortured. They started suffering with dog-bites first.

This being the case,

- *sem min* … – Quickly surrender unto the divine husband of [śrī mahālakśmi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/) who is adorning reddish shining crown. He has the crown which signifies his ability to fulfil the desires of those who surrender unto him; right next to him, the one who makes him give \[śrī mahālakśmi\] is also present; the loss \[for the ātmā\] is only due to not reaching there quickly.
- *ai sērminō* – Though he wants to give his crown to you, you seek out only his divine feet. You expect/accept what is apt for you.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.1.3. Adi ser

*adi sēr mudiyinarāgi arasargaḷ tām toḻa idi sēr murasangaḷ muṟṟattiyamba irundavar podi sēr tugaḷāyp pōvargaḷ ādalil nokkenak kadi sēr tuḻāy mudik kaṇṇan kaḻalgaḷ ninaiminō*

**Пословный перевод:**

adi – at their feet; sēr – united; mudiyinarāgi – having crown; arasargaḷ – kings; tām – themselves; toḻa – worship; idi sēr – thunderous; murasangaḷ – drums; muṟṟattu – in the yard outside; iyamba – making noise; irundavar – staying (with least bother for those who surrendered and hearing that noise); podi – with a small portion of an object; sēr – united; tugaḷāy – to become a piece of dust; pōvargaḷ – become worthless; ādalil – thus; nokkena – immediately; kadi sēr – having fragrance; tuḻāy – decorated with tiruttuḻāy (tuḷasi); mudi – adorning crown; kaṇṇan – kriṣṇa’s; kaḻalgaḷ – divine feet; ninaimin – meditate

**Перевод:**

**Those (emperors) who have at their feet the other kings themselves vorśipping, will stay (with least bother for those who surrendered) hearing the thunderous noise of drums \[being played\] outside; such emperors would become worthless to become a piece of dust in a small portion of an object. Thus, meditate upon the divine feet of kriṣṇa vhos is adorning a crown which is decorated with fragrant tuḷasi.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In third pāsuram – āḻvār says “Those emperors who lived without caring for the other kings who surrendered to them, will lose their wealth and live without being respected by others”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. āḻvār says “Thus , surrender unto the divine feet of the enjoyable kriṣṇa”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. adi sēr mudiyinarāgi arasargaḷ tām toḻa idi sēr murasangaḷ muṟṟattiyamba irundavar podi sēr tugaḷāyp pōvargaḷ ādalil nokkenak kadi sēr tuḻāy mudik kaṇṇan kaḻalgaḷ ninaiminō*

- *adi sēr mudiyanarāgi* – This emperor who was prideful that those other kings who considered equal to him, placed their crown at their feet \[bowed in front of them\] .
- *arasargaḷ* – kings
- *tām toḻa* – They worship fully understanding the situation, but he does not even bother to think “this person has vorśipped me with great reverence”. The other kings only think “we are fortunate to bow down at his exalted feet”. They are not vorśipping [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who was stuck with agony when thinking about bharatāḻvān who begged śrī rāma to return and he did not fulfil that desire as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 24.19 “*śirasā yacanastasyavacanam nakrutam mayā*” (Even after bharata begged having his head at my feet, I was unable to fulfil his desire).

When the king bowed at the emperor’s feet, what did he do?

- *idi sēr* … – The emperor would announce that “this particular king will offer me tribute on this day”, would welcome everyone to the grand assembly, prepare a big drum using the trees and spreading animal skin over it, will have that drum sound thunderously and (being focussed on the music band) will least bother for the king who is vorśipping. The emperor feels that he should be famously known as the one who conquered many kings, invited them to his court and insulted them by watching music/dance programs.
- *irundavar* – He remained indifferent with those vorśipping kings as if they are indistinct from the pillars in the court.

What would happen to such emperors? [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says “they will become a particle of dust eventually”.

- *podi sērt tugaḷāyp pōvargaḷ* – They will become so fallen that they will not even have their own space, and will be like a piece of dust attached to another piece of dust. Those respected emperors who did not care for the kings who vorśipped them, will become so lowly that, when some one steps over them, those who stepped on them  will not even bother to think “Oh! I have placed my foot on his head by mistake”.
- *ādalil* – As this is the nature of worldly wealth,
- *nokkena* – immediately
- *kadi* … – When crown is given, that should be accompanied with the garland which decorates the crown. Meditate upon the divine feet of kriṣṇa who is having very fragrant tuḷasi garland (the fragrance of which increases as days go by) on his divine crown and who is easily approachable by his devotees. \[Is meditating sufficient? Is it not necessary to worship?\]  The sweetness of the divine feet is such that, it will make one drown in such experience just by thinking about it \[this explains [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s divine feet being the goal\]. By thinking about the divine feet, one’s bondage will be completely severed \[this explains bhagavān’s divine feet being the means\]. As said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 3.71.14 “*madusūdana prapannān*” (those who are surrendered to madusūdanan emperumān), they will acquire great respect which is feared by yama (controlling deity of death) and his followers.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.1.4. Ninaippan pugin

*ninaippān pugil kadal ekkalin nuṇ maṇalin palar enaittōrugangaḷum ivvulagāṇḍu kaḻindavar manaippāl marungaṟa māydal allāl maṟṟuk kaṇḍilam panaittāḷ mada kaḷiṟattavan pādam paṇiminō*

**Пословный перевод:**

ninaippān – to speak (about kings who died giving up bhagavat anubhavam (experience of bhagavān)); pugil – set out; enaittōrugangaḷum – many yugas; i ulagu – this world; āṇḍu – ruled; kaḻindavar – who passed away; kadal ekkalil – in the ocean, sand dunes; nuṇ maṇalil – than very tiny sand particles; palar – many; manaip pāl – residence (where they lived); marungu – and their surroundings; aṟa – without any distinction \[everything would be flattened\]; māydal allāl – will only be destroyed; maṟṟu – any remainder; kaṇḍilam – we have not seen; panai – well-rounded like a palm tree; tāḷ – having feet; mada kaḷiṟu – mad elephant; attavan – one who destroyed; pādam – divine feet; paṇimin – you all worship

**Перевод:**

**If we set out to speak about (about kings who died giving up bhagavat anubhavam), more than the very many tiny sand particles in the sand dunes in the ocean, there are many who passed away in the many yugas; they will be destroyed in a manner that there would be no distinction between their residence and the surroundings \[everything would be flattened\] and we have not seen any remainder of them; thus, you all worship the divine feet of the one \[kriṣṇa\] who destroyed the mad elephant \[kuvalayāpīdam\] which had well rounded palm tree like feet.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In fourth pāsuram – āḻvār says “It is not just the wealth that is temporary, even the enjoyer of such wealth will be finished along with their paraphernalia”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “Since the life span is also short (temporary),you worship the divine feet of kriṣṇa who is the eliminator of hurdles”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Fourth pāsuram. āḻvār says “While the wealth is temporary and will lose its worth in time, even due to the temporary nature of the enjoyer of such wealth, one should approach bhagavān“. ninaippān pugil kadal ekkalin nuṇ maṇalin palar enaittōrugangaḷum ivvulagāṇḍu kaḻindavar manaippāl marungaṟa māydal allāl maṟṟuk kaṇḍilam panaittāḷ mada kaḷiṟattavan pādam paṇiminō*

- *ninaippān pugil* – While starting to think about. Like venturing into the ocean, the state where one cannot complete thinking about it and also implies that [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) would not think about worldly matters; still, āḻvār thinks about them for their well being.
- *kadal ekkalil nuṇ maṇalil palar* – More in number than the tiny sand particles in the wavy sand dunes of the ocean. When analysed about those who lived and died like this – they are not lowly humans, but they are brahmā et al who live for 100 years which are divided in to two parts \[first 50 years and second 50 years\], where each day has 1000  catur yugams \[a cycle of 4 yugas lasting for about 43,20,000 human years\] and the night has the same duration too \[where there is no activity\]. While they rule for many years \[and die eventually\] like this as the world remains eternal \[in continuous existence\], they would be finished with the thought of “this is mine”. vaiṣṇava dharma śāstram “*gangāyāssikatādārā yadāvarśadivāsavē \| śakyāgaṇayitum lōkēnavayatītā: pitāmahā: \|\|*” (The brahmās who have come and gone in this world are countless like the sand particles in gangā and the rain droplets showered by indra).
- *manaippāl marungaṟa* – if one has little wealth, it will go along with him; if he has great wealth, when he goes, it will take along all who are near him; when a big tree falls, it will affect the whole surrounding. Just because of the proximity, the neighbours will also be affected.
- *māydal allāl maṟṟuk kaṇḍilam* – We have seen only this destruction and not seen any one staying put.

So, what should be done?

- *panait tāḷ* … – kuvalāypīdam is an elephant whose feet resembled palm trees; try to approach the divine feet of the one who killed that elephant. To have him eliminate your well-known hurdles, see that you place your head at his divine feet. \[Based on [carama ślōkam](http://ponnadi.blogspot.in/2015/12/rahasya-thrayam.html)\] In the previous pāsuram the meaning of “*mām*” \[saulabhyam – easily approachable nature\] is explained; in this pāsuram, the meaning of “*aham*” \[paratvam – supremacy\] is explained.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.1.5. Panimin tiruvarul

*paṇimin tiruvaruḷ ennum am sīdap paim pūm paḷḷi aṇi men kuḻalār inbak kalavi amuduṇḍār tuṇi munbu nālap pal ēḻaiyar tāmiḻippac celvar maṇi minnu mēni nām māyavan pēr solli vāḻminō*

**Пословный перевод:**

am – beautiful; sīdam – cool; pai – huge; pū paḷḷi – in flower bed; tiruvaruḷ – divine grace; paṇimin – to bestow; ennum – having attachment; aṇi – with decorations; mel – very tender; kuḻalār – those who have hairs; inbak kalavi amudu – the nectar of blissful union; uṇḍār – those who enjoyed; tuṇi – cloth; munbu – in front; nāla – hanging; pal – many; ēḻaiyar – those damsels who were desirous previously; tām – themselves; iḻippa – speak insulting words; selvar – will go (back there due to their desire); maṇi – like a blue gem; minnu – having radiance; mēni – having divine form; nam – one who lets us (devotees) enjoy him; māyavan – amazing lord; pēr – divine names; solli – reciting; vāḻmin – live happily

**Перевод:**

**Those \[kings, wealthy folks\] who enjoyed the nectar of blissful union of damsels who have tender hairs with decorations, lying in a beautiful cool huge flower bed to receive the divine grace, subsequently with their cloth hanging in the front side, will themselves go back to those damsels who were desirous previously, in spite of those girls speaking insulting words towards them; thus, you live happily by reciting the divine names of the amazing lord who is having a blue-gem like radiant divine form and who lets (us devotees) enjoy him.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In fifth pāsuram – āḻvār says “Like wealth, the pleasure of union with women also has the defects such as temporary etc”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. So, recite the divine names of sarvēśvara and be uplifted.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. paṇimin tiruvaruḷ ennum am sīdap paim pūm paḷḷi aṇi men kuḻalār inbak kalavi amuduṇḍār tuṇi munbu nālap pal ēḻaiyar tāmiḻippac celvar maṇi minnu mēni nām māyavan pēr solli vāḻminō*

Previous ācaryas would explain this as “*paṇimin tiruvaruḷ ennum – am sīdap paim pūm paḷḷi aṇi men kuḻalār*” – where the damsels look for the grace of the wealthy folks; [bhattar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/parasara-bhattar/), explains it differently by reading “*paṇimin tiruvaruḷ ennum*” with “*inbak kalavi amuduṇḍār*” in the context of those who enjoyed such union looking for the grace of those damsels. When those kings were ruling, they will make their kingdom at the disposal of those damsels, and,

- *paṇimin tiruvaruḷ ennum* – will say “Would you kindly reveal what is in your divine heart?” \[towards those damsels\]. There are many who are waiting to serve those kings outside; real romance is – those great kings waiting for the mercy of those damsels.
- *am sīdap paim pūm paḷḷi* – On the beautiful cool huge bed spread with flowers.

When he places her on such bed and says “*tiruvaruḷ paṇimin*” (reveal your divine orders), what would such damsels do?

- *aṇi men kuḻalār* – Being indifferent towards their praises, they will adjust their decorations, hair etc.
- *inbak kalavi amuduṇḍār* – Those who relished such nectarean union followed by such indifference \[love-fights\] towards them; alternatively – those who relished such nectarean indifference \[love-fights\]. They are \[superficially\] enacting śrīmahālakśmi’s romantic dealings \[with śrīman nārāyaṇan\] which was explained in [tiruvāimoḻi 3.10.8](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/11/thiruvaimozhi-3-10-8-allalil-inbam/) “*alli malar magaḷ bōga mayakku*” (the romantic acts of [śrī mahālakśmi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/) who resides in the lotus flower).

\[After those kings lose their wealth/youth\] Subsequently some one else will snatch those damsels and start enjoying them; still, he will go and beg from them to sustain himself.

- *tuṇi munbu nāla* – As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 32.32 “*śātīm āccādya duścadām*” (that brāmaṇa, based on his wife’s advice, wore a cloth which was not sufficient to tie up to the back side and went to [śrī rāma](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s place), his cloth would stop-short to tie all the way to the back side \[falling from richness to such poverty\].
- *pal ēḻaiyar tām iḻippa* – they are many; previously they would say that they cannot live without him; but now, to please the one who pampers them, they would insult him about his lack of qualification to enjoy them and his misery.
- *selvar* – They will go to those damsels thinking ignorantly “it is only due to our close relationship with her which makes her speak rightfully with us like this”. They would think that the damsel is doing this similar to what she was doing previously during love-fights. This is explained in “… *truṣṇaikā nirupadravā*”  (An old man loses hairs, teeth, vision etc; but his desire never diminishes).

This being the case, try to hold on to the divine form which is explained as in jitantē stōtram 5 “*bhaktānām*” (Your grace’s divine nature, divine auspicious form, divine weapons etc … are not for your sake; yet you appear with the divine auspicious forms for your devotees).

- *maṇi* … – Divine form which has radiance like blue gem and is more attractive than such gem. \[nampiḷḷai goes on to explain\] śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 1.13 “*ēśa sarvasvabhūtastu …*” (this embrace given to hanuman (by [śrī rāma](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)) is equivalent to giving all of himself).
   - *ēśa:* – When one enjoys some thing, they would give it to others. śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 6.5.84 “*iccā gruhītābhimatōru dēha:*” (the forms such as śrī rāma, kriṣṇa which were willingly and joyfully accepted by [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)). Since this says “*iccā gruhītam*” (accepted willingly), it implies that there is no binding of karma; “*abhimatam*” indicates that they are enjoyable for bhagavān himself.
   - *sarvasvabhūta:* – If he gave anything else other than his own divine body, there will always be dissatisfaction of not having that! by giving his own body \[in embrace to hanuman\], everything is given; the divine body is the abode of all auspicious aspects. The difference between giving his divine body and others is clearly visible – “*pariśvankō hanumata:*” (embraced hanuman) – for the one who desires for nectar, one cannot feed grass. hanuman desired for [śrī rāma](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) only as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam uttara kāṇḍam 40.16 “*snēhō mē parama:*” (for me, great devotion towards you is only needed) and so he should be given that only.
   - *mayā kālam imam prāpya datta:* – śrī rāma was dissatisfied that “hanuman will not expect/accept anything;  How will I give some thing to him?” and when an opportunity arose he bestowed himself \[in embrace\] which hanuman cannot refuse.
   - *tasya mahātmana:* – For hanuman who saved two bodies (lives), giving one body \[in embrace\] is no match. When sītāp pirātti was preparing to commit suicide \[in aśōka vanam\], hanuman saved her \[by singing the glories of śrī rāma and subsequently explaining her about his mission\]; \[By bringing the good news about sītāp pirātti’s location\] He also saved śrī rāma who was suffering in separation from sītāp pirātti as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 5.9 “*avagāhyārṇavam svapsyē …*” (Oh lakśmaṇa! let me dive deep into the ocean without you and sleep there, so I can cool down the scorching love \[of separation\]). Thus hanuman gave two bodies for [śrī rāma](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) \[saved two of them\]. Since he helped in many forms/ways, śrī rāma too bestowed him in this \[one\] way.
- *nam māyavan* – Can the greatness of his attitude towards his devotees, be understood?

What should we do to get his mercy?

- *pēr solli* – One should just do this \[recite his names\]; it will lead to the great result of upliftment. A name which leads to upliftment! The enjoyable nature of his divine names is as explained in [tirumālai 2](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/08/thirumalai-2-part-2/) “*accuvai peṟinum vēṇḍēn*” (I will not want paramapadam too).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.1.6. Valndargal

*vāḻndārgaḷ vāḻndadu mā maḻai mokkuḷin māyndu māyndu āḻndār enṟallāl anṟu mudal inṟaṟudiyā vāḻndārgaḷ vāḻndē niṟpar enbadillai niṟkuṟil āḻndār kadal paḷḷi aṇṇal adiyavarāminō.*

**Пословный перевод:**

vāḻndārgaḷ – those who think that they are living; vāḻndadu – their life; mā maḻai – in heavy rain; mokkuḷin – like a bubble; māyndu māyndu – crushed again and again; āḻndār – became very fallen; enṟu allāl – other than this; anṟu mudal – from the time of creation; inṟu aṟudiyā – until today; vāḻndārgaḷ – those who lived; vāḻndē niṟpar – will live in the same manner; enbadu – the principle; illai – is not present; niṟkuṟil – to have an eternal life; āḻndu – deep; Ar – abundance; kadal – ocean; paḷḷi – having as bed; aṇṇal – to the lord; adiyavar – devotee/servitor; āmin – become

**Перевод:**

**Those who think that they are living, are like a bubble in the heavy rain which gets crushed again and again and becomes fallen; other than this, the principle of any one who had lived in the same manner \[forever\] is not present from the time of creation until today; to have an eternal life, \[you\] become a devotee/servitor to the lord who is having the deep, abundant ocean as his bed. Ar also indicates vastness.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In sixth pāsuram – āḻvār says “From the time of sruśti (creation) till date, I have not seen anyone who has survived being a wealthy person”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Sixth pāsuram. While asked “Like doctors would count those who survived, why are you counting \[speaking about\] those who died? Is there no one who lived for long?”, āḻvār  says “You should hear about those”. vāḻndārgaḷ vāḻndadu mā maḻai mokkuḷin māyndu māyndu āḻndār enṟallāl anṟu mudal inṟaṟudiyā vāḻndārgaḷ vāḻndē niṟpar enbadillai niṟkuṟil āḻndār kadal paḷḷi aṇṇal adiyavarāminō.*

- *vāḻndārgaḷ* … – The life of those who think that they lived. They think that they lived a great life; [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) thinks that their lives were disastrous. Whatever they think as glorious life, āḻvār thinks about them as disastrous as said in tiruvāimoḻi 6.9.8 “*innam keduppāyō*” (would you spoil me further?).
- *mā maḻai mokkuḷil* – In a bubble in a heavy rain; *jalabudbudavatsamam* (Like a water bubble which appears and disappears very quickly). āḻvār is saying “*mā maḻai*” (heavy rain) to imply that the droplet will be crushed very quickly.
- *māyndu māyndu* – crushed again and again.
- *āḻndār enṟallāl* – For the sins committed during their life, falling to the lowest state – there is no other option.
- *anṟu* … – There is no question of any one surviving/living in the same manner continuously from the time of sruśti (creation) until today.
- *niṟkuṟil* – if you desire for the eternal goal.
- *āḻndār* … – sarvēśvara who has the deep/vast ocean as his bed. Having depth which ensures that there is no trouble for his divine tender body and having vastness which allows him to spread his divine limbs and rest comfortably. [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) descends to tiruppāṟkadal (milk ocean) and rests there to provide refuge to others, not being bound by karma (virtues/vices); this being the case, to fulfil his desire, you pursue the goal which is apt for your true nature.
- *adiyavar āminō* – When he is being the śēśi (lord), you try to accept your servitude towards him \[Become a servitor, is an order\]. Alternative explanation – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is speaking based on [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s opinion of accepting the ātmā who was not a servitor before, as a servitor now. \[[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is considering that the [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) has become a servitor, by showing the inclination to do so\].

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.1.7. Amin suvai

*āmin suvai avai āṟōdadisiluṇḍārnda pin tū men moḻi madavār irakkap pinnum tuṟṟuvār īmin emakkoru tuṟṟenṟu idaṟuvar ādalin kōmin tuḻāy mudi ādi am sōdi guṇangaḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

Am – Matching the nature; in – pleasing; avai – world renowned; āṟu suvaiyōdu – having six types of tastes (madura (sweet), amla (sour), lavaṇa (salty), katu (pungent), kaśāya (astringent), tikta (bitter)); adisil – (distinguished) food; uṇḍu – ate; ārnda pin – after feeling full \[filled with such food\]; tū – pure (due to affectionate attitude); men – soft (audible); moḻi – having speech; madavār – (humble) damsels; irakka – due to their desire; pinnum – again; tuṟṟuvār – will eat, with difficulty; (after losing such wealth, they will go to the places of those damsels and tell them – you too,); emakku – for us; oru tuṟṟu – a handful of food; īmin – give; enṟu – asking so; idaṟuvar – (even if they don’t get that, at every house) knock around; ādalil – thus; tuḻāy – decorated by tiruttuḻāy (tuḷasi); mudi – the infinitely enjoyable lord, due to having the divine crown; ādi – being the cause of all; am – beautiful; sōdi – one who has radiant divine form, sarvēśvaran’s; guṇangaḷ – qualities; kōmin – enjoy together

**Перевод:**

**\[The rich folks\] after eating (distinguished) food which is matching the nature \[of oneself\], pleasing, world renowned and having six types of tastes, and feeling full, they will again eat with difficulty, unable to refuse the desire of pure (due to the affectionate attitude) and soft-spoken, damsels; after losing such wealth, they will go to the places of those damsels asking “you too give us a handful of food” and knock around (their entrances); thus, together you enjoy the qualities of beautiful sarvēśvaran who has radiant divine form, who is infinitely enjoyable lord due to having the divine crown which is decorated by tiruttuḻāy (tuḷasi) and who is the cause of all.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In seventh pāsuram – āḻvār explains the temporary nature of food, drinks and similar pleasures.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. Thus, meditate upon the qualities of emperumān who is the cause of all and who is greater than all.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Seventh pāsuram. When asked “Though wealth has the defects which you highlight, food, drinks etc have the quality of being dāraka (that which sustains), bhōjña (that which gives pleasure)”, āḻvār replies “even they are not permanent”. āmin suvai avai āṟōdadisiluṇḍārnda pin tū men moḻi madavār irakkap pinnum tuṟṟuvār īmin emakkoru tuṟṟenṟu idaṟuvar ādalin kōmin tuḻāy mudi ādi am sōdi guṇangaḷē*

- *āmin suvai* – Apt and good taste.
- *avai āṟōdu* – the well-known śat-rasam (six types of tastes)
- *adisil uṇḍu* – the one who begged for food previously, once he got some money, will appoint a maid-servant, call himself “mudaliyār” (Honourable person, landlord) and will use the term “*adisil uṇḍār*” (ate food) \[Usually, food/rice is mentioned as sōṟu in tamiḻ in colloquial language, but elegant way of saying is “adisil”\].
- *ārnda pin …* – filling the stomach with whatever is available, remained like a leech which can neither leave nor stay attached, after sucking the blood; at that time some of his damsel friends would come and tell him “you look very weak; how are you going to protect us if you are like this?”; he will then wonder “have I not eaten before?”. First when they tell, he will refuse; but then, they will take a handful of food and feed him lovingly. He will not refuse at that time; being captivated by their sweet-talks he will eat again.
- *īmin* … – In the same manner, some one else will own these damsels. They will feed such \[new\] person in the same way; at that time, he will go there and ask them to give at least a handful of food.
- *emakku* – The same person who would offer anything good to them instead of eating/using himself, out of helpless situation, is saying “for me”. But these damsels will not even look at him, to keep the new person satisfied.
- *idaṟuvar* – They will again go around, knocking.
- *ādalin* – Thus, this being the truth of life.
- *kōmin* … – Enjoy the auspicious qualities of [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) who has tiruttuḻāy (tuḷasi) garland which signifies him as the owner of all wealth, who is the cause of entire creation, who is having infinitely radiant form.
- *ādi am sōdi guṇangaḷaik kōmin* – Enjoy the qualities of his svarūpam (true nature) and vigraham (form) together. Enjoy them as said in cāndōjña upaniśat “*aham annāda:*” (bhagavān is the food and I am the enjoyer), taittirīya upaniśat “*sōśnutē …*” ([jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) enjoys all the auspicious qualities of [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/), along with him) and in periya tiruvantādi 78 “*ōvāda ūṇāga uṇ*” (enjoy as eternal bliss).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.1.8. Gunam kol

*guṇam koḷ niṟai pugaḻ mannar kodaik kadan pūṇḍirundu iṇangi ulagudan ākkilum āngavanai illār maṇam koṇḍa bōgattu manniyum mīḷvargaḷ mīḷvillai paṇam koḷ aravaṇaiyān tirunāmam padiminō*

**Пословный перевод:**

guṇam – for qualities such as seelam (simplicity) etc; koḷ – being the abode; niṟai – being complete (since everyone praises these qualities); pugaḻ – famous; mannar – crowned princes; kodai – magnanimity (of making their wealth available for the welfare of all); kadan – nature; pūṇḍu – assuming; irundu – well established; iṇangi – fitting well together; ulagu – world; udan ākkilum – even while protecting harmoniously; āngu – in matters relating to such aiśvarya (wealth/control); avanai – sarvēśvara; illār – those who are not subservient to; maṇam – freshness of daily celebrations; koṇḍa – having; bōgattu – joy of wealth; manniyum – though staying firm in this manner; mīḷvargaḷ – will become bankrupt; mīḷvu illai – you will attain the goal from where there is no return; paṇam koḷ – with hoods which are expanded (due to coming in contact with him); aravu – ādiśēśa; aṇaiyān – one who is inclined to be united with his devotees, since he is having as bed; tirunāmam – divine names; padimin – recite/practice

**Перевод:**

**Those kings who are the abode of qualities such as seelam (simplicity) etc, who are having complete fame, who are crowned princes, who are well established having assumed the nature of magnanimity (of making their wealth available for the welfare of all); even if they are fitting well together with the world and protecting harmoniously, those who are not subservient to sarvēśvara in matters relating to such wealth, though staying firm in this manner having freshness of daily celebrations and joy of wealth, they will become bankrupt; if you recite/practice the divine names of one who is inclined to be united with his devotees, since he is having ādiśēśa with expanded hoods as bed, you will attain the goal from where there is no return.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In eighth pāsuram – āḻvār says “Without approaching emperumān, one cannot get the enjoyments such as ruling an empire etc; even if one gets them by approaching emperumān, such aspects will not remain permanent”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently āḻvār says “Since these acquired kingdoms will not be long lasting without the grace of bhagavān, you recite the divine names of anantaśāyi (emperumān reclining on ādiśēśa)”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Eighth pāsuram. When asked “rājyaśrī (wealth of ruling over the kingdom) is temporary only when there is no harmony with the citizens; if there is harmony, would it not remain permanent?”, āḻvār says “Even if there is harmony, without approaching emperumān, one will not acquire such wealth; even if it was acquired by pursuing him, due to their \[worldly aspects\] nature, they will not remain forever; this being the case, approach him having himself as the goal”. guṇam koḷ niṟai pugaḻ mannar kodaik kadan pūṇḍirundu iṇangi ulagudan ākkilum āngavanai illār maṇam koṇḍa bōgattu manniyum mīḷvargaḷ mīḷvillai paṇam koḷ aravaṇaiyān tirunāmam padiminō*

- *guṇam koḷ* … – Those who are having good qualities – in abundance; having complete fame; \[also explained as\] being famous for having good qualities.

Even with such qualities, one will not be liked, if they are not apt –

- mannar – crowned princes \[who are liked by their citizens\].

Even such apt kings with good qualities will not be approached if they are misers.

- *kodaik kadan pūṇḍu irundu* – they are having natural magnanimity.

Even in that case, if they consider themselves to be powerful, people will be afraid to approach them.

- *iṇangi* – being a sulabha (easily approachable) person, fitting well together with the citizens.
- *ulagudan ākkilum* – even if they worked together with the world; working together as said in śamkśēpa rāmāyaṇam “*rāmōrājyam upāsitvā*” (śrī rāma ruled the kingdom, working with everyone in a harmonious manner).
- *āngu avanai illār* – If [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s mercy is not there in this matter, one will not get such rājyaśrī (wealth of kingdom).
- *maṇam koṇḍa* … – Such wealth is acquired by bhagavān’s mercy.
- *maṇam koṇḍa bōgam* – Ever-fresh wealth. Even if one acquires such wealth, due to its temporary nature, they will lose it.
- *mīḷvillai* – This being the case, one can attain the goal which is explained in cāndōjña upaniśat as “*na ca punar āvartatē*” (there is no return).

How is that attained?

- *paṇam koḷ* … – Engage in reciting the divine names of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is identified by tiruvanantāḻvān (ādiśēśa) who has expanded hoods due to coming in contact with him. It implies that those who are engaged in reciting his divine names will be treated by him as he treats ādiśēśa. Alternative explanation – One who is having a bed which can handle very rough usage as said in “*ēvamvidpādēnanādyhārōhati*” (Those who know him, climb his bed by stepping on it).
- *mīḷvillai* – \[Another explanation establishing “not just pleasures in this earth, even pleasures in heaven are temporary”\] Instead of performing virtuous actions without attachment in the result and having emperumān as goal, if one performs actions with the expectation of enjoyment such as life in heaven etc., that is also not permanent \[even if acquired by emperumān’s grace\].

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.1.9. Padi mannu

*padi mannu palkalan paṟṟōdaṟuttu aimpulan venṟu sedi mannu kāyam seṟṟārgaḷum āngavanai illār kudi mannum in suvargam eydiyum mīḷvargaḷ mīḷvillai kodi mannu puḷḷudai aṇṇal kaḻalgaḷ kuṟuguminō*

**Пословный перевод:**

padi – lands/properties; mannu – wearing always (without removing); pal – many types of; kalan – ornaments; paṟṟōdu – with the attachment; aṟuttu – giving up; aim pulan – the five sensory organs (which are attached to worldly pleasures); venṟu – winning over (to have full control over them); sedi mannu – (due to lengthy penance) bushes formed around them; kāyam – body; seṟṟārgaḷum – troubled (through fasting etc); mannum – permanent (existing for a long time, as a result of their penance); kudi – having settlements; in – very enjoyable; suvargam – svarga (heaven); eydiyum – even if they attained; avanai – bhagavān (who is the benefactor); āngu – staying there; illār – those who don’t take shelter of him; mīḷvargaḷ – will lose such heavenly life; mīḷvillai – to acquire ever-lasting result; kodi – in the dvaja (flag); mannu – staying eternally; puḷ – periya tiruvadi (garudāḻvār); udai – one who has; aṇṇal – sarvēśvaran’s (supreme lord’s); kaḻalgaḷ – divine feet; kuṟugumin – try to reach

**Перевод:**

**Even if they attained the svarga which is having very enjoyable settlements and  is \[seemingly\] permanent (due to their existence for a long time) by giving up lands/properties and the many types of ornaments which are always worn, by winning over the sensory organs and by troubling the bodies \[in penance\] and having bushes formed around them, if they don’t take shelter of bhagavān while staying there, they will lose such heavenly life; to acquire ever-lasting result, you should try to reach out to the divine feet of sarvēśvaran who has periya tiruvadi staying eternally in his dvaja (flag). “padi mannu” also indicates “Those \[ornaments\] which are well fitting with the body”.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In ninth pāsuram – āḻvār says “Not just earthly kingdom etc, even the wealth of ascending to heaven etc which are acquired through bodily penance, are also temporary”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “Since the other-worldly joy in heaven etc are temporary, you take shelter of īśvara who will establish the goal which is ever-lasting”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Ninth pāsuram. In the previous eight pāsurams, āḻvār explained that the earthly joy is temporary; in this, he says “after performing difficult penance by troubling one’s body, when that penance leads to heaven, bhagavān‘s mercy is required to sanction that; even if such heavenly life is attained by the mercy of bhagavān, due to its nature, such joy will not last long”. padi mannu palkalan paṟṟōdaṟuttu aimpulan venṟu sedi mannu kāyam seṟṟārgaḷum āngavanai illār kudi mannum in suvargam eydiyum mīḷvargaḷ mīḷvillai kodi mannu puḷḷudai aṇṇal kaḻalgaḷ kuṟuguminō*

- *padi* – Talking about what he gives up while engaging in penance. padi – bhūmi (land).
- *mannu palkalan* – The ornaments which were acquired properly.

Alternatively,

- *padi mannu palkalan* – The ornaments which were passed along in a heriditary manner from the ancestors. Here padi is considered as paramparā.
- *paṟṟōdu aṟuttu* – Not just living without them, but also giving up the attachment towards them.
- *aim pulan venṟu* – Winning over the sensory organs such as ears which are the source for such attachment, so that they don’t go behind the sensual pleasures. śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 114.18 “*indriyāṇi purājitvā*” (maṇḍōdari tells rāvaṇa “you were able to rule over the worlds, since you had full control over your senses”).
- *sedi mannu kāyam seṟṟārgaḷum* – Those who troubled their body by staying in penance in a particular Asana for a long time, so that bushes grow around them. iraṇḍām tiruvantādi 53 “*neṟiyār kuḻaṟkaṟṟai munninṟu pin tāḻndu aṟiyādu iḷangiri enṟeṇṇip piṟiyādu, pūngodigaḷ vaigum*” (The flowers would remain permanently, after growing in the front portion of the hair and hanging in the back side, of people, thinking that their heads are like a little hillock, without knowing that they are fully focussed on the path to tirumalā).
- *āngu avanai illār* – Without his mercy, it will not materialize. If his mercy is there,
- *kudi mannum in suvarggam eydiyum* – [bhattar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/parasara-bhattar/) would say “there are people who are pursuing this goal too”. Even if he attains svarga, which is having closely knit communities, having joy, which is different from what is observed in naraka” \[it will not last long\].
- *mīḷvargaḷ* – Once their virtues are exhausted, they will be pushed out \[of svarga\] saying “*dvamsa*” (you fall down).
- *mīḷvillai* – Such fall is not present \[in this eternal goal\]. There is no decrease for [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s virtues. periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 4.5.2 “*puṇaikkodukkilum pōga ottārē*” (In paramapadam, even if the nityasūris (eternally free souls) give surety to bring back the muktas (liberated persons), [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) will not allow them to go to the material realm again).
- *kodi mannu puḷ* – garudāḻvār eternally staying as the flag. emperumān is so magnanimous that he will have those who take shelter of him \[in this case, garudāḻvār\], as his identity or distinguishing factor from others. Why should he have garudāḻvār as his identity instead of having others? It is because of his beak strength and having wings \[both of which will facilitate quick elimination of hurdles of his devotees\].
- *puḷḷudaiya aṇṇal* – Like “*śriya:pati*” (lord of śrī mahālakśmi), he (garudāḻvar) also uniquely identifies īśvara.
- *aṇṇal* – śēśi – lord.
- *kaḻalgaḷ kuṟuguminō* – To be freed from worldly bondage, approach [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s divine feet. In the first pāsuram, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) said “*tirunāraṇan tāḷ kālam peṟac cindittuymminō*” (Quickly meditate upon the divine feet of [śrīman narāyaṇan](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)) and here he says “*puḷḷudai aṇṇal kaḻalgaḷ kuṟuguminō*” (Reach out to the divine feet of the lord who has garudāḻvār as his vehicle) – this implies that just like śrī mahālakśmi being his unique identity, garudāḻvār is also his unique identity.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.1.10. Kuruga miga

*kuṟuga miga uṇarvattodu nōkki ellām vitta iṟugal iṟappennum jñānikkum appayan illaiyēl siṟuga ninaivadōr pāsam uṇḍām pinnum vīdillai maṟugalil īsanaip paṟṟi vidā vidil vīdahdē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kuṟuga – in proximity (of self instead of going astray in worldly pleasures); uṇarvattodu – with the ātmā who is identified by his jñānam (knowledge); miga nōkki – meditating upon it intensely (to attain vision of self); ellām – all goals (other than ātmā); vitta – the one who has given up; iṟugal – exclusively ending on ātmā; iṟappu – mōkśa (liberation); ennum – considering as the goal; jñānikkum – for the jñāni (wise); appayan – accepting (bhagavān, who is the ultimate exclusive goal) as the means; illaiyēl – if not present; siṟuga – lowly goals; ninaivadu – to think about; ōr pāsam – attachment; uṇḍām – will exist; pinnum – further; vīdu – mōkśam (in the form of attaining self-enjoyment); illai – will not be attained; maṟugal il – being the opposite of all defects; īsanai – (natural) controller of all and the lord who is the abode of all auspicious qualities; paṟṟi – surrendering unto him (considering him as the goal and the means); vidā vidil – not leaving him ever (like the others who accept ulterior benefits from bhagavān \[and leave him\]); ahdē – that itself; vīdu – is parama puruśārtam (the ultimate goal)

**Перевод:**

**The jñāni (wise) who has given up all goals (other than ātmā), meditating upon the ātmā intensely being in close proximity of the self who is identified by his jñānam, is considering mōkśa which ends in ātmā exclusively as the goal; for such jñāni, if accepting bhagavān as the means is not present \[in him\], attachment to think about lowly goals will exist; further mōkśam (in the form of attaining self-enjoyment) will also not be attained. This being the case, surrendering unto bhagavān who is the opposite of all defects, who is the controller of all and the lord who is the abode of all auspicious qualities and not leaving him ever in itself is parama puruśārtam (the ultimate goal).**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In tenth pāsuram – āḻvār explains that kaivalya puruśārtam (the goal of self-enjoyment) is very difficult to attain and an inapt goal \[for the nature of jīvātmā who is an eternal servitor of bhagavān\].*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “kaivalyam though is not temporary \[as in the case of worldly pleasures which are temporary\], since it is not as enriching as parama puruśārtam (the ultimate goal of serving bhagavān eternally), attaining of bhagavān who is the all controlling supreme lord, is the most wonderful puruśārtam (goal)”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Tenth pāsuram. āḻvār previously explained that both the earthly wealth and experience in heaven are temporary; when asked “unlike these, isn’t self-enjoyment a permanent goal?”, āḻvār replies “While it is better in comparison to worldly pleasures \[in the sense that kaivalyam is permanent while the worldly pleasures are temporary\], since it is inferior when compared to the bliss of bhagavān, kaivalyam is also very lowly; this being the case, try to hold on to bhagavān”. kuṟuga miga uṇarvattodu nōkki ellām vitta iṟugal iṟappennum jñānikkum appayan illaiyēl siṟuga ninaivadōr pāsam uṇḍām pinnum vīdillai maṟugalil īsanaip paṟṟi vidā vidil vīdahdē*

- *kuṟuga* … – To start with, only for the one who has his mind fully focussed on the internal self is qualified for Self-enjoyment. The mind which grasps which go far away and engage in external matters, should be focussed on [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/). That is, seeing eyes with ones own eyes \[eye indicates jñānam – here first jñānam indicates dharma bhūta jñānam \[knowledge of ātmā\] and the second jñānam indicates darmi jñānam \[ātmā – Self which itself is knowledge/consciousness. So with the knowledge one sees/knows ātmā\]. To focus one’s intent/attachment which was focussed on worldly pleasures for a very long time, into the self.
- *ellām vitta* – Giving up everything including śrīman nārāyaṇa – even if he arrives with beautiful garlands on his shoulders, on garudāḻvār, without the mind getting attached to his enjoyable nature, just using him like cow dung which is used to purify a contaminated place but thrown out after the use \[using [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) to purify the self and achieve self-enjoyment instead of achieving servitude at his lotus feet\].
- *iṟugal iṟappu ennum jñānikkum* – For the ātma jñāni (the wise person who is focussed on ātmā), who considers this contraction (of enjoying the miniscule ātmā) as mōkśam (liberation). Though self-enjoyment is considered to be greater than worldly enjoyment, since [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) has seen the bliss of bhagavān, he considers this to be very lowly. iṟappu – mōkśam (liberation).
- *appayan illaiyēl* – If one does not engage in bhagavat upāsanam \[engaging the mind in [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/), by considering him as the means\], one cannot meditate upon [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/). Since upāsanam is a joyful act, it is said as “*payan*” (goal). bhagavān, who is the means, is the goal for [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/).
- *siṟuga* … – \[when such bhagavat upāsanam is not present\] One will become more fallen than even before \[starting the pursuit of ātmā\], ignorance which is the cause for bondage will grow like hundreds of branches in a tree; the bondage which will lead one to think “I am dēva (celestial being); I am manuśya (human)” \[which is opposite to the truth of “I am the soul, servitor of [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)“\], will occur.
- *pinnum vīdillai maṟugalil īsanaip paṟṟi vidā vidil* – Even for the one who has full control of his senses, performed bhagavat upāsanam, exhausting the karmas (virtues/vices), at the time of attaining [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/), unless he focusses his thoughts on bhagavān during his last moments while shedding the body, such (kaivalya) mōkśam will not be achieved.
- *maṟugal il īsanai* – sarvēśvara who is opposite of all evil aspects. Alternatively, “*maṟugal il*” indicates the agony one goes through at the time of death.
- *īsanaip paṟṟi vidāvidil* – If there is no antima smruti (remembering [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) during the last moment), one will be born as the object that one thought of at the end, just as in in the case of ādi bharata who was born as a deer since he thought of a deer at the last moment.
- *vīdu ahdē* – What I ([āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)) explained in pāsuram 1 “*tirunāraṇan tāḷ kālam peṟac cindittu uymminō*” (Quickly meditate upon the divine feet of [śrīman nārāyaṇan](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) and be uplifted) is the real goal.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.1.11. Ahde uyya

*ahdē uyyap pugumāṟenṟu kaṇṇan kaḻalgaḷ mēl koy pūm poḻil sūḻ kurugūrc catakōpan kuṟṟēval sey kōlattāyiram sīrt todaip pādal ivai pattum ahkāmal kaṟpavar āḻ tuyar pōy uyyaṟpālarē*

**Пословный перевод:**

uyya – to be uplifted; pugum – approach; āṟu – upāyam (means); ahdē – only that (saying firmly so); kaṇṇan – kriṣṇa’s; kaḻalgaḷ mēl – on the divine feet; koy – pluckable; pū – having abundance of flowers; poḻil – having garden; kurugūr – the leader of āḻvārtirunagari; śatakōpan – nammāḻvār; kuṟṟēvalgaḷ – in the form of confidential services; sey – performed; kōlam – decorated to perfection; āyiram – thousand; sīrt todai – having sīr and todai (grammatical aspects in composing verse); pādal – tiruvāimoḻi in the form of a song; ivai pattum – this decad; ahkāmal – without losing; kaṟpavar – those who learn; āḻ – being immersed (in worldly wealth and self-enjoyment); tuyar – grief; pōy – having eradicated; uyyaṟpālar – will be engaged in upliftment of self (leading to devotion towards bhagavān)

**Перевод:**

**nammāḻvār, the leader of āḻvārtirunagari ,which has gardens having abundance of pluckable flowers, sang thousand pāsurams having sīr and todai in the form of confidential services performed to kriṣṇa’s divine feet, firmly saying those are the only means to be approached for ātmā‘s upliftment. Those who learn this decad among those thousand pāsurams without losing \[any part of them\], will have their grief of being immersed in worldly wealth and self-enjoyment, eradicated and will be engaged in upliftment of self (leading to devotion towards bhagavān).**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the end – āḻvār says “Those who learned this decad will discard lowly goals such as worldly wealth and will exclusively enjoy service to bhagavān“.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār explains upliftment of ātmā after elimination of all sorrows as the result of this decad.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. ahdē uyyap pugumāṟenṟu kaṇṇan kaḻalgaḷ mēl koy pūm poḻil sūḻ kurugūrc catakōpan kuṟṟēval sey kōlattāyiram sīrt todaip pādal ivai pattum ahkāmal kaṟpavar āḻ tuyar pōy uyyaṟpālarē*

- *ahdē uyyap pugumāṟenṟu* – Saying that the divine feet of śrīman nārāyaṇan as I said \[in first pāsuram\] “*tirunāraṇan tāḷ*“, is the means for upliftment \[of [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)s\] and the goal.
- *kaṇṇan kaḻalgaḷ mēl* – He himself said in [tiruvāimoḻi 3.10.10](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/11/thiruvaimozhi-3-10-10-thalarvinriye/) “*kaṇṇanait tāḷ paṟṟi*” (being surrendered to the divine feet of kriṣṇa) and instructed others in [tiruvāimoḻi 4.1.3](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/11/thiruvaimozhi-4-1-3-adi-ser/) “*kaṇṇan kaḻalgaḷ ninaiminō*” (meditate upon the divine feet of kriṣṇa); he is repeating the same instruction here. Considering that there is no one else who has completely taken shelter of his divine feet, he himself surrendered to them. \[Where did we see that?\] First [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) instructed to his divine heart in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.1.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/03/thiruvaimozhi-1-1-1-uyarvara-uyarnalam/) “*tuyar aṟu sudar adi toḻudeḻu*” (Worship the radiant feet which remove the agony, and rise); he then instructed to others in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.2.10](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/05/thiruvaimozhi-1-2-10-en-perukku/) “*vaṇ pugaḻ nāraṇan tiṇ kaḻal sēr*” (Reach out to the divine firm feet of śrīman nārāyaṇan who is having auspicious qualities). Here, he said in [tiruvāimoḻi 3.10.10](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/11/thiruvaimozhi-3-10-10-thalarvinriye/) “*kaṇṇanait tāḷ paṟṟi yān enṟum kēdilanē*” \[after having surrendered to the divine feet of kriṣṇa, I am never in any ruins\] and also instructed others in tiruvāimoḻi 4.1.3 “*kaṇṇan kaḻalgaḷ ninaiminō*” (mediate upon the divine feet of kriṣṇa); What great devotion! In the end too [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) instructs others saying in tiruvāimoḻi 9.1.10 “*kaṇṇan allāl illai kaṇḍīr śaraṇ*” (There is no one other than kriṣṇa who can provide shelter) \[Instructions relating to virōdi (hurdles) completed in tiruvāimoḻi 9.1 decad\].
- *koy pū …* – [nammāḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) who is the leader of [āḻvārtirunagari](http://azhwarthirunagari.koyil.org/) which is surrounded by ever-fragrant divine gardens. Such āḻvār performs confidential services in the form of singing this decad, at the divine feet of sarvēśvaran. *sey* \[in past tense\] – poem that is compiled; it also indicates service by speech when read as “*satakōpan kuṟṟēval sey*” ([nammāḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s confidential service by speech).
- *kōlattāyiram* – The thousand pāsurams which have no deficiency in the decorations for the poem.
- *sīr* … – Those who learn, without losing anything, this decad which is strung with [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s qualities, will be rid of disastrous goals such as aiśvaryam (worldly pleasures) and kaivalyam (self-enjoyment) which are devoid of service to bhagavān and will be uplifted. *ahkal* – shrinking (losing some aspects).
- *uyyaṟpālar* – They will have upliftment as a natural aspect. That is, they will have what [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) explained in “*kālam peṟac cindittuymminō*” (quickly meditate upon his divine feet and be uplifted).
