## 4.2 Balanay elulagundu

## 4.2.1. Balanay elulagundu

*bālanāy ēḻulaguṇḍu parivinṟi ālilai anna vasam seyyum aṇṇalār tāḷ iṇai mēlaṇi taṇṇantuḻāy enṟē mālumāl valvinaiyēn mada valliyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

bālanāy – having a very infant-like form; ēḻ ulagu – all worlds; uṇḍu – consumed; (attāl – as a result of that); parivu inṟi – without any discomfort; Al ilai – on a tender banyan leaf; anna vasam seyyum – resting after consumption of \[heavy\] food; aṇṇalār – the lord’s; tāḷ iṇai mēl – on the two divine feet; aṇi – decorated (by the nityasūris who were captivated by this act of emperumān); taṇ – cool; am – having freshness; tuḻāy – (desiring to get the) tiruttuḻāy (tuḷasi); enṟē – only that; mālum – bewildered without realising (that the incident happened way back in time and she cannot get the tuḷasi from that time); valvinaiyēn – for me who has the sins to witness such agony \[of my daughter\]; madam – exhaustion due to not giving up on the desire; valli – she \[my daughter\] who resembles a creeper which needs support

**Перевод:**

**sarvēśvaran, having a very infant-like form, is resting on a tender banyan leaf after consuming all the worlds (without any discomfort after consuming such heavy food); his two divine feet are decorated with cool fresh tuḷasi; my daughter desires to get that tuḷasi only, remains bewildered without realising (that the incident happened way back in time and she cannot get the tuḷasi from that time) and is exhausted due to not giving up on the desire, resembles a creeper which needs support; I have the sins to witness such agony \[of my daughter\].**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In first pāsuram – parānkuśa nāyaki‘s mother is agonised that her daughter desires to immediately get the tiruttuḻāy (tuḷasi) which is decorating the divine feet of sarvēśvaran who is in the form of vata taḷa śāyi (one who is resting on the banyan leaf).*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. bālanāy ēḻulaguṇḍu parivinṟi ālilai anna vasam seyyum aṇṇalār tāḷ iṇai mēlaṇi taṇṇantuḻāy enṟē mālumāl valvinaiyēn mada valliyē*

- bālanāy – My daughter won’t be as worried, if [emperumān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) consumed the worlds and rested on the banyan leaf, after becoming a youth \[but since he is a toddler, she is worried\]; I can console her, if he is at least grown up saying “at this particular age, he has the duty to protect the worlds when they are in danger”.
- *āy* – As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 120.11 “*ātmānam mānuśam manyē*” (śrī rāma – I consider myself as a human only), other than his toddler state, his previous \[supreme\] states are not visible; it is said as in [tiruvāimoḻi 3.10.10](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/10/thiruvaimozhi-3-7-10-adiyarndha/) “*padiyādumil kuḻavippadi*” (incomparable toddle form); having pure infancy.
- *ēḻulaguṇḍu* – His age is such that, without thinking whether something will digest or not, \[toddlers\] will pick up something they can lay their hands on and put in their mouth. \[Does eating of a toddler count as protecting?\] Since it is the act of the protector, it ends up being an act of protection. If empersumān performs an act which is acceptable, she too will desire for reasonable aspects \[Since emperumān performed an impossible task, [parānkuśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) too desires now for the impossible aspect of getting the tuḷasi from that time\].
- *ēḻulaguṇḍu* – When there is a danger, he does not discriminate and consumes all the worlds and protects them.
- *parivu inṟi* – without any discomfort; when placing the worlds in his stomach, he does not have any discomfort.
- *ālilai* – on a banyan leaf; the pure leaf given by a banyan tree.
- *anna vasam seyyum* – Instead of having control over self, he became overwhelmed by food which is explained in tatittirīya upaniśat “*aham annam*” (I am the enjoyed). He reclined on his right side, to preserve what he consumed instead of digesting them.
- *aṇṇalār* – Like emperumān’s nature is to carefully protect everyone even when he is a toddler, she remembers his lordship even when she is bewildered/unconscious.
- *aṇṇalār* – He is the sarvarakśaka (protector of all) and sarva svāmy (lord of all). She \[[parānkuśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)\] is asking “Since you are the protector of all, is there any trouble for you to fulfil the desire of helpless me \[to attain you\]?”.
- *aṇṇalār tāḷiṇai* – śēśa bhūta (servitor) will naturally hold on to the divine feet of śēśi (lord).
- *tāḷiṇai mēl aṇi taṇ am tuḻāy* – She first offered tiruttuḻāy (also explained as – she offered tiruttuḻāy (tuḷasi) at his divine feet) which resulted in such desire \[of desiring to have that  tuḷasi\]. As a brāhmaṇa would constantly recite vēdam even if he becomes mad, she will repeat the same thing which she previously learned/said as in [tiruvāimoḻi 2.1.2](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/11/thiruvaimozhi-2-1-2-kotpatta-sinthaiyaiyay/) “*tāḷ patta taṇ tuḻāy dāmam kāmuṟṟāyē*” (you have the great desire to have the tuḷasi which was crushed by the divine feet of emperumān).
- *tuḻāy enṟē* – She will constantly repeat the same thing. Even if I told her “Oh poor thing! It is impossible. The incident happened in the past \[and we cannot get the tuḷasi from that past incident now\]”, she will not hear.
- *mālum* – becomes bewildered. She is not just blabbering these words, even inside her she has become very weak/bewildered. When some one thinks that the rays of a shining gem is fire, should that also burn him \[when touched\]? \[When she realized that it is difficult to get the tuḷasi from the past, should she also become bewildered?\].
- *valvinaiyēn* – For her \[[parānkuśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)\], who is bewildered/unconscious, there is no agony, but for me who is well aware of the situation, there is agony due to my own sins.
- *mada valliyē* – \[two meanings\] stubborn, humble. Her age is such that, she should be supported by [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) like a creeper is supported by a stick.
- *valli* – She is in the state as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 119.36 “*pati samyōga sulabham vaya:*” (janaka, the father of sītā, drowned in an ocean of sorrow thinking about his daughter ready to be married \[and yet not finding the right groom for her\]).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.2.2. Valli ser

*valli sēr nuṇṇidai āycciyar tammodum kollaimai seydu kuravai piṇaindavar nalladi mēlaṇi nāṟu tuḻāy enṟē sollumāl sūḻ vinai āttinēn pāvaiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

valli – creeper; sēr – like; nuṇ – thin; idai – having waist; āycciyar tammodum – with the covherd girls, mingling freely; kollaimai – actions which cross the limits; seydu – performed; kuravai – rāsa leelā \[divine interactions between kriṣṇa and gōpikās\]; piṇaindavar – the one who engaged, his; nal – beautiful (having steps that follow the dance); adimēl – on the divine feet; aṇi – worn; nāṟu – very fragrant; tuḻāy enṟē – “tiruttuḻāy” (tuḷasi) only; sollum – tells/recites; sūḻ – surrounded (to see her without any escape route); vinaiyāttiyēn – I am having sins, my; pāvai – daughter

**Перевод:**

**kriṣṇa engaged in rāsa leelā mingling with the covherd girls who have creeper like thin waist, performing actions which cross the limits; my daughter keeps reciting the very fragrant tuḷasi which were on the beautiful divine feet of such emperumān; I am having sins which have surrounded me to make me witness such state of my daughter.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In second pāsuram – Mother says “parānkuśa nāyaki desires to witness the divine activities of kriṣṇa with the gōpikās (covherd girls) in rāsa leelā”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, mother says “She (my daughter) is constantly and incoherently reciting \[about\] the tiruttuḻāy at the divine feet of kriṣṇa who performed rāsa leelā”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Second pāsuram. Mother says – When she \[my daughter\] was asked “if sarvēśvaran who is sarva rakśaka (protector of all), protected his own wealth \[the material realm\] during total deluge, would that be a reason for \[me to have faith in\] me attaining the goal \[with his help\]?”, she replies “that may not be the reason, but since he helped \[the covherd\] girls of my age, why should he not help me?”. valli sēr nuṇṇidai āycciyar tammodum kollaimai seydu kuravai piṇaindavar nalladi mēlaṇi nāṟu tuḻāy enṟē sollumāl sūḻ vinai āttinēn pāvaiyē*

- *valli sēr nuṇ idai* – As said in periya tirumoḻi 3.7.1 “*vaḷḷi marungul*” (having creeper-like thin waist), the girls who are having “vaḷḷi” (a type of creeper) like thin waist; Having a form like valli (creeper) and since there is no exact example for their waist, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying “*nuṇ idai*” (very thin waist).
- *āycciyar tammodum* – My daughter said – if he can help many girls of my age, why can’t he help me who has all their cravings put together? In tirvāyppādi (śrī gōkulam), [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) helped many girls of her age.
   - *kollaimai seydu* – engaging in activities that cross the limits of decency; ridding of their limits by manifesting his beauty etc.
- *kuravai piṇaindavar* – he strung himself in between them.
- *nalladi* – My daughter is desiring to get the tuḷasi which were repeatedly trampled by the covherd girls and kriṣṇa. She is not of the nature of desiring for the tuḷasi from the divine feet of brahmacāri [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/).
- *nāṟu tuḻāy* – By smelling the fragrance of the tuḷasi, she can tell whether it was trampled by both of them or not. \[How does she know?\] “*kalambagan*” (a term to identify a garland made of two different flowers\] has a unique fragrance \[That is, when tuḷasi comes in contact with *lotus* feet of the girls and the *lotus* feet of kriṣṇa, it will have a special fragrance\].
- *enṟē sollumāl* – Chaste women would think about their dear consort but will not speak out their emotions. What happened to such chastity?
- *sūḻ vinaiyāttiyēn* – I have sins which will surely keep me entrapped in this situation. It is due to my sin, I am revealing the words of her who is as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam 58.85 “*naivamām kincit abhravīt*” (sumantra’s words after leaving perumaḷ (śrī rāma), pirātti (sītā) and iḷaiya perumāḷ (lakśmaṇa) – sītāp pirātti was overwhelmed with grief and could not speak a word).
- *pāvaiyē* – My daughter who has the nirupādika strītvam (top-most, unconditional chastity) who will never reveal her mind, is not in a situation where she needs to express herself vocally to attain her goal.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.2.3. Paviyal veda

*pāviyal vēda nan mālai pala koṇḍu dēvargaḷ māmunivar iṟainja ninṟa sēvadi mēlaṇi sempon tuḻāy enṟē kūvumāl kōḷ vinaiyāttiyēn kōdaiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

pā – in candas (poetic meter); iyal – existing; vēdam – vēda sūktams (sacred hymns); nal – divinely; pal – many; mālai – garlands; koṇḍu – having; dēvargaḷ – dēvas; mā munivar – eminent sages like sanaka et al; iṟainja – to be vorśipped; ninṟa – (measured the world and) stood; cē adi mēl – on the reddish divine feet; aṇi – adorned (by them); sem – reddish; pon – desirable like gold; kūvum – she is calling out; kōḷ vinaiyāttiyēn – I have very strong/well-known sins, my; kōdai – flower garland like daughter, or daughter who is wearing a flower garland

**Перевод:**

**emperumān (measured the world and) stood to be vorśipped by dēvas and eminent sages like sanaka et al, who are having vēda sūktams which are existing in candas, with many divine garlands; I, a great sinner, have a daughter who is herself \[tender like\] a flower garland, and who is calling out only for the tiruttuḻāy which is desirable like reddish gold and is adorned on the reddish divine feet of such emperumān.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In third pāsuram – mother says “My daughter (parānkuśa nāyaki) desires for the tiruttuḻāy (tuḷasi) from the divine feet of emperumān who divinely measured the worlds”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, mother says “My daughter calls out for the tiruttuḻāy from the divine feet of trivikrama who is glorified by all worlds”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Third pāsuram. mother says “My daughter is saying – What is the impediment in getting that which is held by the one who helped the whole world instead of the one who helped just a town?”. pāviyal vēda nan mālai pala koṇḍu dēvargaḷ māmunivar iṟainja ninṟa sēvadi mēlaṇi sempon tuḻāy enṟē kūvumāl kōḷ vinaiyāttiyēn kōdaiyē*

- *pā iyal vēdam* – vēdam which is composed of hymns. \[Alternatively\] vēdam which is spoken with poetic meter, i.e., vēdam which has different meters such as anuśtup, triśtup, bruhatī etc. \[depending on the number of words in a line\]
- *nal mālai* – with the best garlands among such vēdam – that is with śrī puruśa sūktam etc. \[Why specifically hymns from vēdam?\] Though bhagavān is glorified in other places too, since his nature and qualities are clearly revealed in vēdam, using \[such vēdam which says\] katavalli upaniśat 1.2.15 “*sarvē vēdā yat padamāmananti*” (the vēdams which speak about the nature of paramātmā who is the ultimate goal) and in [śri bhagavat gītā](http://githa.koyil.org/) 15.15 “*vēdaiśca sarvair ahamēva vēdya:*” (I am the object of knowledge in all vēdams). Alternatively, reading vēdam and nanmālai separately, it is explained as – with vēdam which speaks about worship of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) and śrī puruśa sūktam which speaks about his nitya vibhūti and leelā vibhūti.
- *dēvargaḷ mā munivar iṟainja ninṟa* – emperumān standing as the refuge, after divinely measuring the world, to be vorśipped by dēvas (celestial beings) and sages like sanaka et al as said in śrīviṣṇu darmam “*sankaissurāṇām*” (When trivikram measured the world with his foot, he was vorśipped by dēvas, humans and other celestial beings).
- *sēvadi* – as said in tiruvāsiriyam 5 “*mā mudal adip pōdu onṟu kaviḻttalartti*” (a great lotus flower, placed in an upside-down posture), when the divine foot appears like a flower on the head, āḻvār lifts his head and sees the enjoyable reddish colour of the foot. It is the rāgam (redness indicates attachment) in the beginning/feet which changed [parānkuśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) to be in her current situation. Alternatively – it is explained as feet with sevvai (ārjava – honesty). Honesty for the foot is being neutral towards devotees and others and touching all as said in mūnṟām tirvantādi 88 “*podu ninṟa ponnam kaḻal*” (the attractive, beautiful divine feet which are common for everyone). The ārjavam (honesty) of his divine feet makes everyone engage in them as said in tiruneduntāṇḍagam 1 “*taḷir puraiyum tiruvadi en talai mēlavē*” (His blossoming divine feet are on my head).
- *sēvadi mēlaṇi sem pon tuḻāy* – She was calling out for the gold-like attractive tiruttuḻāy (tuḷasi) on such divine feet.
- *enṟē kūvumāl* – Even if she was given the garland which he wore on his shoulders, she would not accept. Al – exclamation, additional word for poetic sound.
- *kōḷ vinaiyāttiyēn* – I who have sins which will finish me surely. Alternatively – kōl – strong. Sins which can only be exhausted by experiencing the results \[of such strong\] sins.
- *kōdaiyē* – \[kōdai means flower garland, lock \[hair\] and a girl who is wearing garland\] Four explanations – 1) She, who will torment those who see her garland and lock, is herself being tormented now! 2) She who is having such lock is desiring for another garland \[that is worn by [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)\]. 3) She herself, being a garland on \[emperumān’s\] chest, is desiring for another garland! 4) emperumān is crazy about the garland on his chest and she is crazy on such emperumān.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.2.4. Kodila van pugal

*kōdila vaṇ pugaḻ koṇḍu samayigaḷ bēdangaḷ sollip pidaṟṟum pirān paran pādangaḷ mēlaṇi paim pon tuḻāy enṟē ōdumāl ūḻ vinaiyēn tadam tōḷiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kōdu – defect (of looking for self praise); ila – without that (purely existing for others’ enjoyment); vaṇ – distinguished; pugaḻ – qualities; koṇḍu – having; samayigaḷ – \[philosophers, thinkers\] focussed on groups of qualities such as śeelam (simplicity) etc , śauryam (valour) etc, ānandam (bliss) etc; bēdangaḷ – differences (in greatness of such qualities); solli – saying them; pidaṟṟum – one who gives experience to make them speak in a (very reliśable) disorderly manner; pirān – great benefactor; paran – greater than all; pādangaḷ mēl – at the divine feet; aṇi – decorated (by nityasūris)\_; pai – greenish \[fresh\]; pon – attractive; tuḻāy enṟē – “tiruttuḻāy (tuḷasi)” only; ōdum – (always) recites \[desiring it\]; ūḻ vinaiyēn – I who have great sins which are existing with me since time immemorial; tadam – rounded; tōḷi – having shoulders

**Перевод:**

**emperumān (in paramapadam) is without any defect having distinguished qualities; he gives experience to make the nityasūris speak in a (very reliśable) disorderly manner, \[each one is\] focussed on the differences of groups of qualities such as śeelam (simplicity) etc , śauryam (valour) etc, ānandam (bliss) etc; such great benefactor who is greater than all, has his divine feet decorated with greenish \[fresh\] attractive tiruttuḻāy (tuḷasi); I who have great sins which are existing with me since time immemorial; my daughter who has well rounded shoulders, always recites such tuḷasi \[desiring it\].**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In fourth pāsuram – Mother says “Her daughter is desiring for the tiruttuḻāy from the divine feet of sarvēśvaran who is greater than all and residing in tirunādu (paramapadam)”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Fourth pāsuram. When asked “Where will I search for the tuḷasi from avatārams which helped everyone long ago and disappeared like a river in floods which dried up?”, parānkuśa nāyaki replies “Leave that aside. What is the hurdle in getting the tuḷasi from the divine feet of paramapadanātan (emperumān in śrīvaikuṇṭam) who remains unchanged forever?”. kōdila vaṇ pugaḻ koṇḍu samayigaḷ bēdangaḷ sollip pidaṟṟum pirān paran pādangaḷ mēlaṇi paim pon tuḻāy enṟē ōdumāl ūḻ vinaiyēn tadam tōḷiyē*

- *kōdu ila* – faultless; opposite to all faults. Qualities of emperumān being faultless implies, when one meditates upon a particular quality, it will bind the person who meditates into that quality and would not let him/her move on to the next quality. If that is not the case, there is no difference between this (emperumān’s qualities) and other worldly pleasures \[where one will be constantly seeking new things\].
- *vaṇ pugaḻ* – auspicious qualities. Meditating upon them.
- *samayigaḷ* – Those \[nityasūris (eternally free souls) and muktas (liberated souls)\] who engage in one quality and will not move on to the next one. Those who are focussed on different qualities saying “emperumān’s sauśeelyam \[simplicity\] is very attractive; his valour is more attractive than that; the qualities of his form such as beauty etc are even more attractive”. Further, it can also indicate different types of upāsakas who are engaged in different types of practices such as sadvidyā (focussing on bhagavān’s nature along with his qualities such as omniscience etc), dahara vidyā (focussing on both his qualities and his nature), upakōśala vidyā (focussing on bhagavān who resides in everyone’s eyes), śāṇḍilya vidyā (focussing on bhagavān in his viśvarūpam) etc.
- *bēdangaḷ solli* – Glorifying the qualities they enjoy. For example – one who enjoys his sauśeelyam will say “There is no comparison of this quality. Can his valour match his simplicity?” and so on.
- *pidaṟṟum* – Being immersed in such qualities, they would call him out speaking incoherently like a person affected with high fever would do.
- *pirān paran* – śrīvaikuṇṭanātan who blessed them this situation. Being a benefactor for them means – as said in tiruviruttam 98 “*imaiyōr tamakkum sevvē nenjāl ninaipparidāl veṇṇey ūṇennum īnac col*” (this amazing incident of kriṣṇa accepting butter as his food, is difficult to comprehend even for nityasūris), he presented such qualities within their reach for them to enjoy – so āḻvār calls him “*pirān*“.
- *paran pādangaḷ mēl aṇi paim pon tuḻāy enṟē ōdumāl* – She always speaks about the fresh and attractive tiruttuḻāy (tuḷasi) which was offered at his divine feet by nityasūris who are great servitors as said in tiruviruttam 21 “*sūttu nan mālaigaḷ tūyana ēndi*” (carrying beautiful pure garlands which are ready to be worn).
- *ūḻ vinaiyēn* – I who have sins which have properly reached me. ūḻ – in proper sequence.
- *tadam tōḷiyē* – My daughter who is extremely beautiful is desiring for the tiruttuḻāy from the divine feet of emperumān, which is the abode of auspicious qualities. Who will babble in such incoherent manner – the one who is the target of these beautiful shoulders (emperumān) or she herself? \[He should be longing for her instead\].

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.2.5. Toli ser

*tōḷi sēr pinnai poruttu erudēḻ taḻeeik kōḷiyār kōvalanār kudak kūttanār tāḷ iṇai mēl aṇi taṇ am tuḻāy enṟē nāḷu nāḷ naiginṟadāl endan mādarē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tōḷi – having shoulders (that are dear to him); sēr – who is comparable to him (in her qualities such as śeelam etc); pinnai poruttu – for nappinnai; erudu ēḻ – seven bulls; taḻeeik kōḷiyār – embracing them (all at once); kōvalanār – belonging to the covherd clan; kudak kūttanār – one who captivates the heart through his dance with pots; tāḷ iṇai mēl – on the two divine feet; aṇi – offered (being won over by such brave act); taṇ – cool; am – beautiful; tuḻāy enṟē – \[saying\] “tiruttuḻāy” only; nāḷum nāḷ – day after day; endan mādar – my daughter; naiginṟadu – is becoming weak

**Перевод:**

**kriṣṇa who belongs to the covherd clan, who captivates the heart through his dance with pots, embraced the bulls (at once) for nappinnai who is having shoulders which are dear to him and who has qualities comparable to his; day after day, my daughter is becoming weak, only saying “tiruttuḻāy” which is cool and beautiful, and which are offered at the two divine feet of such kriṣṇa.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In fifth pāsuram – Mother says “My daughter (parānkuśa nāyaki) desires for the tiruttuḻāy (tuḷasi) from the divine feet of kriṣṇa who mercifully killed the seven bulls to marry nappinnaip pirātti”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Fifth pāsuram. Mother says – When asked “Is it possible to search for the tuḷasi which decorated the divine feet of bhagaān who is greater than all, who is residing in paramapadam and is impossible to attain?”, parānkuśa nāyaki says “In that case, what is the difficulty in getting the tuḷasi which decorated the divine feet of kriṣṇa who killed the bulls disregarding safety of himself, for a girl like me?”. tōḷi sēr pinnai poruttu erudēḻ taḻeeik kōḷiyār kōvalanār kudak kūttanār tāḷ iṇai mēl aṇi taṇ am tuḻāy enṟē nāḷu nāḷ naiginṟadāl endan mādarē*

- *tōḷi sēr pinnai* – As explained in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 16.5 “*tulya śeela vayō vruttām*” (śitā and śrī rāma are perfect match in qualities, age, activities etc), while sītā is a perfect match in family heritage etc for śrī rāma, as explained in the same ślōkam “*asitēkśaṇā*” (black-eyed sītā) \[Since only sītā’s eyes are specifically explained, it is implied that her eyes are more beautiful than śrī rāma’s\]. Similarly, while nappinnaip pirātti’s beauty is a perfect match for kriṣṇa’s, the beauty of her shoulders is greater than kriṣṇa’s. This is to make him lose \[his heart\] to those shoulders and to embrace them.
- *erudu ēḻ taḻeeik kōḷiyār* – One who embraced the seven bulls. Since he subsequently wants to  embrace her, his fighting with the bulls appeared like embracing her. That is why, it is said “*erudu ēḻ taḻeei*” (embracing the seven bulls). Since this is the means to get her, he fought with the bulls’ *kombu* (horn), as if he is joyfully embracing this *kombu*  (nappinnai who resembles a kombu (slender stick)
- *kōvalanār kudak kūttanār* – One who is having an equivalent family heritage and pride (of being an expert in dancing with pots), in order to get nappinnai. Just like janaka who would not marry his daughter to any one other than a prince from the ikśvāku clan even if he broke the prized bow, parents of nappinnai would not marry their daughter to any one who has shortcomings in covherd habits even if he killed the seven bulls \[dancing with the pots is also a unique aspect of covherd clan, and kriṣṇa was an expert in it\].
- *tāḷ iṇai* … – [parānkuśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is desiring for the tuḷasi which decorated the divine feet of kriṣṇa who helped nappinnai.
- *nāḷu nāḷ naiginṟadāl* – She, who is so tender that she cannot handle becoming weak for even a single day, is becoming weak day after day. [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is the one who bestows the body and then weakens it too.
- *endan mādar* – My daughter. Is my daughter as strong as he (kriṣṇa) who took birth \[in a prison cell\], broke the shackles and escaped from there, fought and killed pūtanā, śakatāsura, yamaḷārjuna et al, having scarred feet as said in mudal tiruvantādi 21 “*taḻumbu irunda tāḷ sakatam sādi*” (having a scar in the feet due to kicking the śakatāsura)? She is like a tender deer, who has a slender waist which will break simply if touched.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.2.6. Madar ma man madandai

*mādar mā maṇ madandai poruttu ēnamāy ādi am kālattu agalidam kīṇḍavar pādangaḷ mēlaṇi paim pon tuḻāy enṟē ōdum māl eydinaḷ endan madandaiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

mādar – being best among women; mā – laudable; maṇ madandai poruttu – for śrī bhūmip pirātti; ēnam āy – assuming the form of śrī varāha (a pig, which does not shy away from water and mud); ādi – beginning of kalpa (brahmā’s day); am – having goodness; kālattu – at that time; agal idam – the vast earth; kīṇḍavar – emperumān who separated (from the wall of the 14 layered aṇḍam \[deep in the causal ocean\]) and rose; pādangaḷ mēl – on the divine feet; aṇi – decorated (by sages such as sanaka et al); pai – greenish; pon – attractive; tuḻāy enṟē – “tiruttuḻāy” only; ōdum – (always) reciting; māl – bewilderment; eydinaḷ – acquired; endan madandai – my daughter who has distinguished humility

**Перевод:**

**At that good time during the beginning of kalpa (brahmā’s day), emperumān assuming the form of śrī varāha for the laudable śrī bhūmip pirātti who is best among women, separated the vast earth (from the wall of the 14 layered aṇḍam \[deep in the causal ocean\]) and rose; my daughter who has distinguished humility,  (always) reciting only the greenish attractive “tiruttuḻāy” which was decorated by sages such as sanaka et al – the divine feet of such varāha bhagavān and she acquired bewilderment.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In sixth pāsuram – Mother explains how her daughter (parānkuśa nāyaki) desires for the tiruttuḻāy (tuḷasi) from the divine feet of emperumān when he mercifully rescued bhūmi (earth) from the causal ocean as śrī varāha.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Sixth pāsuram. Mother says – My daughter desires for the tiruttuḻāy from the divine feet of śrī varāha who reduced his stature to help śrī bhūmip pirātti, unlike kriṣṇa who helped nappinnaip pirātti, without reducing his human stature. mādar mā maṇ madandai poruttu ēnamāy ādi am kālattu agalidam kīṇḍavar pādangaḷ mēlaṇi paim pon tuḻāy enṟē ōdum māl eydinaḷ endan madandaiyē*

- *mādar* – Having beauty, nirupādika strītvam (unconditional quality of being a lady); mādar indicates being loving and friendly.
- *mā maṇ madandai poruttu* – for the sake of the laudable śrī bhūmip pirātti.
- *ēnamāy* – As said in nācciyār tirumoḻi 11.8 “*pāsi tūrttuk kidanda pārmagaḷ*” (bhūmi dēvi who was covered with moss), when the beloved girl is in physically dirty situation, the beloved boy looking clean and nice, does not fit their loving relationship; as said in the same pāsuram “*māsudambil nīr vārā mānamilāp panṟiyām tēsu*” (the radiance of being a humble pig with muddy water all over it’s body), having a form which does not shy away from mud and water.
- *ādi* – at the beginning of \[śvēta\] varāha kalpa (the day of brahmā which is known by that name\].
- *am kālattu* – Beautiful time. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) celebrates this as beautiful time, since it is time where one could enjoy the beautiful form assumed, by [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is the protector, in order to protect his possession (earth).
- *agalidam kīṇḍavar* … – On the divine feet of emperumān who rescued the great earth which got stuck to the wall of the aṇḍam \[deep in the ocean of 14 layered sphere\] and rose \[above the water level\], the tiruttuḻāy (tuḷasi) which was offered by sages such as sanaka et al as said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 1.4.29 “*rōmāntarastā munayas stuvanti*” (the riśis (sages) who are at the pores of the root of the hairs, are singing his praises) – she desired for such tuḷasi.
- *ōdum māl eydinaḷ* – She became mad to recite this always.
- *endan madandaiyē* – My daughter \[is so innocent that she\] thinks “he should be becoming mad \[thinking about me\]”. The torment one who goes through when looking at her stage, she is going through the same torment now \[In tamiḻ literature, seven stages of womanhood are explained – among those, madandai indicates the age from 14 to 19\].

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.2.7. Madandaiyai

*madandaiyai vaṇ kamalat tirumādinait tadam koḷ tār mārbinil vaittavar tāḷin mēl vadam koḷ pūntaṇṇantuḻāy malarkkē ivaḷ madangumāl vāṇudaleer! en madak kombē*

**Пословный перевод:**

madandaiyai – one who is having (eternally enjoyable) stage of womanhood \[girl between 14 and 19 years of age\]; vaṇ – attractive; kamalam – having the lotus flower as her seat; tiru – (as said in “śrīdēvi”) having the divine name of “tiru”; mādinai – having saundaryam (beauty) etc as a result of \[perfect\] femininity; tadam koḷ – huge; tār – having garland (which reveals his supremacy); mārbinil – in the divine chest; vaittavar – mercifully keeping it ready (for her to climb and be seated there); tāḷin mēl – on the divine feet (offered by the dēvas of that time); vadam – strung; koḷ – having; pū – attractive; taṇ – cool; am – fresh; tuḻāy malarkku – for the tiruttuḻāy (tuḷasi) garland; vāḷ nudaleer – Oh girls who are having radiant forehead!; en – my; madam – humble; kombu – attractive like a slender twig; ivaḷ – my daughter; madangum – withers (being distressed)

**Перевод:**

**emperumān is having huge garland in his divine chest, keeping it ready for the attractive śri mahālakśmi who is having the divine name of “tiru” (śrī), who is having eternally enjoyable stage of womanhood, who is having saundaryam (beauty) etc as a result of \[perfect\] femininity and is having the lotus flower as her seat; Oh girls who are having radiant forehead! my humble daughter who is attractive like a slender twig is desiring for the strung attractive cool fresh tiruttuḻāy (tuḷasi) garland which is on the divine feet of such emperumān and withers (being distressed).**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In seventh pāsuram – Mother says “My daughter desires for the tiruttuḻāy (tuḷasi) from the divine feet of emperumān who placed periya pirātti (śri mahālakśmi) on his divine chest during the churning of the ocean to get nectar”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. madandaiyai vaṇ kamalat tirumādinait tadam koḷ tār mārbinil vaittavar tāḷin mēl vadam koḷ pūntaṇṇantuḻāy malarkkē ivaḷ madangumāl vāṇudaleer! en madak kombē*

- *madandaiyai* – being in the stage of womanhood which is always enjoyable.
- *vaṇ kamalat tirumādinai* – [śri mahālakśmi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/) who is having beautiful lotus flower as her residence.
- *tadam koḷ* … – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who placed śrī mahālakśmi in his chest which is spacious to be the private quarters for her, and is having garland which is indicative of his control/wealth. As said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 1.9.105 “*paśyatām sarvadēvānām yayau vakśastalam harē:*” (āmidst all the dēvas (celestial beings) who were watching, śrī mahālakśmi ascended the divine chest of śrī hari), during the churning of ocean to get nectar, that mahālakśmi desires to climb his divine chest, emperumān accepts her. My daughter \[says āḻvār’s mother\] desired for the richly strung attractive cool fresh tuḷasi flower from the divine feet of such emperumān, and due to not getting it, she fell down and remained in a withered posture.
- *vāḷ nudaleer* – Oh girls who have forehead which has radiance! when will I see her in your splendour?
- *en madak kombē* – Without separating from me, she remains steadfast in her goal and suffering as a result of that.

## 4.2.8. Kombu pol

*kombu pōl sītai poruttu  ilangai nagar amberi uyttavar tāḷ iṇai mēl aṇi vambaviḻ taṇ am tuḻāy malarkkē ival nambumāl nān idaṟku en seygēn? nangaimīr!*

**Пословный перевод:**

kombu pōl – extremely beautiful like a slender twig; sītai poruttu – for sītā, the daughter of śrī janakarāja; ilangai nagar – in the town of lankā; ambu eri – fiery arrows; uyttavar – one who made them enter; tāḷ iṇai mēl – on the divine feet; aṇi – submitted (by brahmā et al after praising śrī rāma); vambu aviḻ – freshly blossomed with fragrance; taṇ – cool; am – beautiful; tuḻāy – tiruttuḻāy’s (tuḷasi); malarkku – flower garland; ivaḷ – my daughter; nambum – desires; nangai mīr – Oh girls who are complete in all aspects!; idaṟku – this great attachment; nān – I; en seygēn – what shall I do?

**Перевод:**

**śrī rāma shot the fiery arrows to make them enter the town of lankā for the daughter of śrī janakarāja, sītā, who is extremely beautiful like a slender twig. Oh girls, who are complete in all aspects! My daughter desires for the cool beautiful flower garland of tuḷasi which is freshly blossomed with fragrance and submitted (by brahmā et al after praising śrī rāma) on the divine feet of such śrī rāma; what shall I do for this great attachment \[of my daughter towards emperumān\]?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In eighth pāsuram – Mother says “My daughter (parānkuśa nāyaki) desires for the tiruttuḻāy (tuḷasi) from the divine feet of cakravarati tirumagan (śrī rāma, the son of emperor daśarata) who burnt down lankā for sītā, the daughter of śrī janakarāja”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

- *ambu eri uyttavar* – Fire (agni dēvatā) will only cook food in this town. It will not manifest its fiery nature. Even when hanuman entered lankā, he was sent by śrī rāma, like sending an arrow only.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. kombu pōl sītai poruttu  ilangai nagar amberi uyttavar tāḷ iṇai mēl aṇi vambaviḻ taṇ am tuḻāy malarkkē ival nambumāl nān idaṟku en seygēn? nangaimīr!*

- *kombu pōl* – Like a *“vanjik kombu”* (a variety of slender twig); also explained as a part of the singular whole (bhagavān) as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 21.15 “*ananyā …*” (sītā – Like sun’s rays never separate from the sun, I never separate from śrī rāghava).
- *sītai poruttu* –  for sītā.
- *ilangai nagar* – the town which was feared by sun and moon to freely move around \[due to rāvaṇa’s rule\].
- *ambu eri uyttavar* – He sent the collection of fiery arrows and made them enter there. \[How did fire enter the town when sun and moon were fearful?\] śrī rāma touched the arrows and sent them along with fire after giving them enough power/force; this is why, they entered with that strength given by śrī rāma. That which adorns the divine feet of such śrī rāma who can give strength to even those who are fearful.
- *vambu aviḻ taṇ am tuḻāy malarkkē* – Fragrant flower, ever fresh flower. śrī rāma, even though being the son of emperor \[in a human form\], he is present along with all his glories as in paramapadam (spiritual realm) – similarly, whatever garland he wears, that appears as tiruttuḻāy only for his devotees.
- *nambumāl* – she always desires for that.
- *nān idaṟku en seygēn nangaimīr* – Unlike kriṣṇa who was commonly accessible for everyone, śrī rāma is an ēkadāravratan (strictly attached to a single wife). How can I go and search for the tiruttuḻāy from the divine feet of such [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)? Please tell.
- *nangaimīr* – While you all are complete, please see her suffering.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.2.9. Nangaimir nirum

*nangaimīr nīrum ōr peṇ peṟṟu nalginīr enganē sollugēn yān peṟṟa ēḻaiyaic cangennum cakkaram ennum tuḻāy ennum inganē sollum irāp pagal en seygēn?*

**Пословный перевод:**

nangaimīr – Oh girls who are complete in all aspects!; nīrum – all of you; ōr peṇ – a daughter; peṟṟu – gave birth; nalginīr – raised them; yān – I; peṟṟa – gave birth; ēḻaiyai – this girl who is desirous \[of attaining emperumān\]; engan – how; sollugēn – to speak?; sangu ennum – saying Sanka (which is his unique symbol); cakkaram ennum – saying chakra; tuḻāy ennum – saying tiruttuḻāy (tuḷasi from his divine feet); irāp pagal – day and night, without any difference; inganē – individually in this manner; sollum – she is saying; en seygēn – what shall I do for this!

**Перевод:**

**Oh girls who are complete in all aspects! All of you have given birth to a daughter and raised them too. How can I speak about my daughter who is desirous \[of attaining emperumān\]? She is individually saying Sanka, chakra (which are his unique symbols) and tuḷasi (from his divine feet) day and night, without any difference. What shall I do for this!**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In ninth pāsuram – Mother says “My daughter (parānkuśa nāyaki) tries to speak about emperumān‘s weapons but being unable to speak fully about them, becomes anguished”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, mother says “She keeps reciting emperumān‘s distinguished symbols”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. nangaimīr nīrum ōr peṇ peṟṟu nalginīr enganē sollugēn yān peṟṟa ēḻaiyaic cangennum cakkaram ennum tuḻāy ennum inganē sollum irāp pagal en seygēn?*

- *nangaimīr* – You are so complete \[in knowledge etc\], yet you have to hear about the sufferings of my daughter.
- *nīrum ōr peṇ peṟṟu nalginīr* – All of you too gave birth to a daughter and raised them! Did anyone suffer like my daughter?

When asked “What is the difference between our daughters and your daughter?”, mother says,

- *enganē sollugēn* – I can only speak about her state if it can be expressed through words. Even  if one can speak about bhagavān’s qualities which are themselves explained in taittirīya upaniśat as “*yatō vācō nivartantē aprāpya manasā saha*” (the words returned being unable to glorify [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s quality of bliss fully and even the mind cannot comprehend that), the qualities of those \[[āḻvārs](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/azhwars/)\] who are immersed in [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s qualities cannot be comprehended. As said in śrīviṣṇu tatvam “*sadā para guṇa viśtō draśtavyas sarva dēhibhi:*” (being engaged in the qualities of bhagavān and thus qualified to be seen always by others), such devotees can be seen but cannot be spoken about. bhagavān himself declared in śrī bhagavat gītā 7.17 “*priyōhi jñāninōtyartam*” (such jñāni (devotee) is very dear to me). How can I speak about her state of desiring to get the objects from different place/time at this place and now?

When told “Still, you are much closer to her than us. Why don’t you tell as much as you know?”, she says,

- *sangu ennum* – As if lifting a mountain, she says with great difficulty “Sanka” (conch). When that sets in, she says *cakkaram ennum* – \[Since she is desirous\] she is neither withdrawing; nor saying \[since she is weak\]. Thinking about the garland, which is placed in between the conch and disc on either hand of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), *tuḻāy ennum*. She is not saying \[calling out loudly\] as in tiruvāimoḻi 7.2.1 “*sangu cakkarangaḷ*” (conch and disc) or as in 6.9.1 “*kūr Ar āḻi veṇ sangu*” (the sharp disc and the white conch). \[When there is great danger one will call out like that. Is there any one who did that?\] When draupati was in great danger, she called out in mahābhāratam “*Sanka chakra gadā pāṇē*” (Oh one who has conch, disc and mace in his hands) \[Since my daughter is in even greater dangerous situation, she is unable to even call out like that\].
- *inganē sollum* – She is anguishing by starting to say but unable to complete the words and repeating the same again and again.

For how long is this going on?

- *irāp pagal* – always.
- *en seygēn* – Should I make her complete what she started to tell? ōr should I see her strītvam (femininity) and withdraw from calling out?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.2.10. En seygen

*en seygēn ennudaip pēdai en kōmaḷam en sollum en vasamum allaḷ nangaimīr min sey pūṇ mārbinan kaṇṇan kaḻal tuḻāy pon sey pūṇ men mulaikkenṟu meliyumē*

**Пословный перевод:**

nangaimīr – Oh girls, who are complete in all aspects!; ennudai – my; pēdai – being ignorant (having not attained the stage to listen to my advice) \[pēdai refers to a girl in the age group of 5 to 7\]; en kōmaḷam – having a tender-heart (which does not allow her to listen to my advice); en sollum – whatever I say; en vasamum – whatever I think; allaḷ – she is not obeying; en seygēn – what shall I do (for this)?; min sey – having radiance; pūṇ – decorated with ornaments such as kaustubha gem etc; mārbinan – having chest; kaṇṇan – kriṣṇa; kaḻal – divine feet; tuḻāy – tiruttuḻāy (tuḷasi); pon – pale complexion (due to separation); sey – made; pūṇ – decorated with ornaments; mel – withered (due to agony in separation); mulaikku – for breast (to be a decoration); enṟu – desiring so; meliyum – has become weak (since her desire is not fulfilled)

**Перевод:**

**Oh girls, who are complete in all aspects! my ignorant tender-hearted daughter is not obeying whatever I say and whatever I think. What shall I do for this? She is desiring for the tuḷasi from the divine feet of kriṣṇa who is having a chest which is decorated with radiant ornaments such as kaustubha gem etc. She desires such tuḷasi to decorate her withered breast (as decoration) which has pale complexion (which occurs due to separation from the beloved one); since her desire is not fulfilled, she has become weak.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

- *pon sey men mulai* – The breast decorated with golden ornaments in anticipation of uniting with [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/).

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In tenth pāsuram – When asked “īsn’t your daughter under your control? Why don’t you give her good advice?”, mother responds to them “She does not listen to me and is very distressed due to desiring for him”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, Mother says “Being disobedient towards me and being captivated by the beauty of ornaments worn by kriṣṇa, my daughter has become weak, desiring for the tiruttuḻāy (tuḷasi) from the divine feet of kriṣṇa to decorate her breast”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. en seygēn ennudaip pēdai en kōmaḷam en sollum en vasamum allaḷ nangaimīr min sey pūṇ mārbinan kaṇṇan kaḻal tuḻāy pon sey pūṇ men mulaikkenṟu meliyumē*

- *en seygēn* – Looking at her state, it appears that I have lost her; what shall I do?
- *ennudaip pēdai* – She is too young to listen to my good advice.
- *en kōmaḷam* – Nor can I give her up saying “she is not listening to my advice”; she is very tender-hearted.
- *en sollum allaḷ en vasamum allaḷ* – Neither she listens to my advice; nor is she prepared to listen to my advice.
- *nangaimīr* – I don’t need to explain this to you \[you are already completely knowledgeable to know all of these\].
- *min sey* … – The tuḷasi from the divine feet of [kriṣṇa](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who has radiant śrī kaustubha gem in his chest. To be decorated with such tuḷasi on her breast which is decorated with golden ornaments and which cannot bear the separation \[from such [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)\]; alternatively, it is explained as breast which has pale complexion \[due to separation from emperumān\]; periya tirumoḻi 2.7.6 “*men mulai pon payandirunda*” (tender breasts acquiring pale complexion due to separation). Another explanation – the breast which has such pale complexion as an ornament as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 29.1 “*aninditām*” (sītāp pirātti withered form in separation from [śrī rāma](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), is explained by śrī vālmīki bhagavān as “irreproachable” (faultless)).
- *min sey pūṇ mārbinan – pon sey pūṇ men mulai* – As [śrīman nārāyaṇan](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s \[supreme\] masculinity is identified by his kaustubha gem, [parānkuśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s femininity is identified by her pale compelxion \[in separation\]; it is an ideal quality to become pale in separation from her beloved person. No one’s tanam (stana – breast) \[generally breast indicates bhakti\] is comparable to parānkusa nāyaki’s; also explained as no one’s danam \[wealth of kainkaryam\] is comparable to parānkusa nāyaki’s.
- *men mulai* – Due to the separation from her beloved, she is decorating her breast with golden ornaments \[to be seen by him\].

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.2.11. Meliyum noy

*meliyum nōy tīrkkum nam kaṇṇan kaḻalgaḷ mēl mali pugaḻ vaṇ kurugūrc catakōpan sol oli pugaḻ āyirattu ippattum vallavar mali pugaḻ vānavarkkāvar naṟkōvaiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

meliyum – the cause for such weakness; nōy – separation; tīrkkum – one who will cure; nam – who is easily approachable for devotees; kaṇṇan – kriṣṇa; kaḻalgaḷ mēl – on the divine feet; mali – well developed (persevering even in separation); pugaḻ – having fame; vaṇ – laudable; kurugūr – leader of āḻvārtirunagari; satakōpan – nammāḻvār; sol – mercifully spoke; oli – glorious; pugaḻ – completeness of all attributes; āyirattu – among the thousand pāsurams; ippattum – this decad as well; vallavar – those who can understand the mood and recite/practice; mali – abundance; pugaḻ – having bhagavat anubhavam (experience of bhagavān); vānavarkku – for nityasūris; nal – laudable; kōvai āvar – become united

**Перевод:**

**nammāḻvār, the leader of the laudable āḻvārtirunagari, mercifully spoke thousand pāsurams which have completeness of all glorious attributes on the divine feet of kriṣṇa who is easily approachable for his devotees and who will cure the separation which causes such weakness in āḻvār. Those who can understand the mood and recite/practice this decad as well, will become laudable and united with nityasūris who are having abundance of bhagavat anubhavam.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the end – āḻvār says that those who are well versed in this decad, among the thousand pāsurams, mercifully spoken by him on the divine feet of kriṣṇa, who united with him to relieve him of his unbearable anguish, will be comparable to ayarvaṟum amarargaḷ (nityasūris – eternal residents of paramapadam).*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār mercifully says “those who learn this decad will attain the result of uniting with nityasūris”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Eleventh pāsuram. In the end – āḻvār says “Those who can recite this decad, will become comparable to nityasūris”. meliyum nōy tīrkkum nam kaṇṇan kaḻalgaḷ mēl mali pugaḻ vaṇ kurugūrc catakōpan sol oli pugaḻ āyirattu ippattum vallavar mali pugaḻ vānavarkkāvar naṟkōvaiyē*

- *meliyum nōy tīrkkum* – Mother withdraws her support thinking that it will “weaken” her daughter \[Mother’s words stop after “*meliyum*” – after that it is [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s words in his natural mood\], but the \[real\] owner ([emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)) will not abandon \[his property\]. periya tirumoḻi 8.9.7 “*peṟṟār peṟṟoḻindār*” (My parents gave birth to me and abandoned me subsequently) etc.
- *nam kaṇṇan* – It is well established in sacred texts that emperumān will come for help whenever there is danger as said in śrī bhāgavatam kāṇḍam 10 “*tāsāmārāvirabhūc cauri:*” (kriṣṇa arrived amidst the covherd girls with a smiling beautiful lotus like face and yellow garment like a cupid for cupid himself). On the divine feet of kriṣṇa who can cure the disease of separation which is the cause for her weakened state.
- *mali pugaḻ …* – The glory acquired by [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) due to longing for emperumān as in “I want to experience his forms which are from distant place/time”. Mercifully spoken by such glorious āḻvār.
- *oli pugaḻ āyirattu ippattum vallavar* – Those who can recite this decad which expressively explains the auspicious qualities of emperumān who caused such longing in [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) and who also drove away such longing without a trace by accepting āḻvār.
- *mali pugaḻ vānarkku āvar naṟkōvaiyē* – \[It is not that āḻvār becomes comparable to nityasūris, instead\] They will become comparable to āḻvār. nityasūris long for [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) while eternally/fully enjoying him \[desiring for more such experience\]; āḻvār longs for bhagavān in the abode where people have no such longing in separation of bhagavān; so, “longing for bhagavān” is common for both nityasūris and āḻvār – thus they both are comparable.
- *naṟ kōvai āvar* – He will be a good combination with *vānavar* \[i.e., āḻvār will fit in perfectly among nityasūris\].

## 4.3 Kovai vayal

## 4.3.1. Kovai vayal

*kōvai vāyāḷ poruttu ēṟṟin eruttam iṟuttāy madiḷ ilangaik kōvai vīyac cilai kunittāy kula nal yānai marupposittāy pūvai vīyā nīr tūvip pōdāl vaṇangēnēlum nin pūvai vīyām mēnikkup pūsum sāndu en nenjamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kōvai – reddish like a kōvai fruit (a type of reddish force); vāyāḷ poruttu – for nappinnai who has lips; ēṟṟin – bulls’; eruttam – nape (the back of the neck); iṟuttāy – one who broke; madiḷ – having forts; ilangai – for lankā; kōvai – rāvaṇa who is the kō (ruler); vīya – to finish; silai – bow; kunittāy – one who drew; kulam – having high birth (best breed); nal – having best abilities; yānai – kuvalayāpīda’s; maruppu – tusk; osittāy – Oh one who (effortlessly) broke!; pūvai – flowers; vīyā – inseparable from; nīr – water; tūvi – offering unto you in a disorderly manner (due to love); pōdu – at those times; vaṇangēnēlum – though I did not worship; nin – your; pūvai vīyām – having the complexion of pūvaippū (a dark-blue coloured flower); mēnikku – for the divine form; pūsum – qualified to apply; sāndu – angarāga (scented cosmetic); en nenjamē – let it be my heart!

**Перевод:**

**Oh emperumān who broke the nape of the bulls for nappinnai who has lips which are reddish like a kōvai fruit, who bent your bow to finish rāvaṇa who is the kō (ruler) of lankā which has forts, who (effortlessly) broke the tusk of  kuvalayāpīda which is having high birth and best abilities! though I did not worship you (in this manner, you who eliminated the hurdles of nappinnai, sītā, girls of maturā) at those times offering flowers, which are inseparable from water, unto you in a disorderly manner (due to love), let my heart be the angarāga (scented cosmetic) which is qualified to be applied on your divine form, which is having the complexion of pūvaippū.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In first pāsuram – āḻvār says “Though I did not get to pamper emperumān to relieve him of his fatigue after defeating enemies of his devotees, survival/sustenance of my heart itself became pampering for him”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*In first pāsuram, āḻvār looks at emperumān who destroys the hurdles which stop one from achieving the goal and says “you have my heart as your angarāga (scented cosmetic)”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*In first pāsuram – āḻvār says “When the likes of nappinnaip pirātti, sītāp pirātti who is the divine daughter of śrī janakarāja are your most dear lovers, my existence has become everything for you such that you manifest the divine love you have for them, towards me”. Alternatively – same as nanjīyar‘s introduction. kōvai vāyāḷ poruttu ēṟṟin eruttam iṟuttāy madiḷ ilangaik kōvai vīyac cilai kunittāy kula nal yānai marupposittāy pūvai vīyā nīr tūvip pōdāl vaṇangēnēlum nin pūvai vīyām mēnikkup pūsum sāndu en nenjamē*

- *kōvai vāyāḷ poruttu* – Highlighting the beauty of nappinnai’s lips which made [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) go up against the fierce bulls disregarding his own safety. They decorated her and showcased her saying “the one who wins over the bulls can marry her”; kriṣṇa went up against the bulls thinking “Why śouldn’t I fight the bulls, if I can embrace her?”. nappinnai was upset seeing nambi mūtta pirān (balarāma) first stepping up thinking “what if he controls the bulls?”; but as kriṣṇa pushes away balarāma and takes charge, out of great joy, she smiles; the reddish lips appeared at that time. Being captivated by that sight, he made himself her’s.
- *ēṟṟin eruttam iṟuttāy* – broke the nape of the bull; eruttam – pidar – high nape; it is the cause for the bull’s pride. He broke that pride. A real brave fighter would go weaponless against an enemy who has weapon in his hand and snatch that – this is what kriṣṇa did; the bulls have top weapons (on their upper body). When perumāḷ (śrī rāma) started chasing the māyāmrugam (the mysterious deer), iḷaiya perumāḷ (lakśmaṇa) understood the situation and warned him about it saying “there is something mysterious; it is a rākśasa in the form of a deer”; I too should have gone to kriṣṇa when he was getting ready to fight the bulls and should have warned him that they are possessed by some demoniac force; but I did not do that – says [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/).
- *madiḷ ilangai* – rāvaṇa opposed cakravarati tirumagan (śrī rāma) thinking “I have this great town and the fort surrounding it”. Leaving perumāḷ who is the sarvarakśaka (protector of all), he considered this fort as protection; this is the only thing one can do to protect oneself \[i.e., considering [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) as protector\].
- *ilangaik kōvai vīya* – śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 1.39 “*lankām rāvaṇa pālitām*” (to lankā which is ruled by rāvaṇa). The town is so well protected that no one can easily enter there. On top of that, the ruler’s strength is also great. To finish rāvaṇa who pridefully thinks “I have this well protected lankā”.
- *silai kunittāy* – Just like rākśasas only know māyāprayōgam (covert attacks), you \[referring to emperumān\] only know honest way of fighting. Like śrī vibhīśaṇāḻvān who advised you “rākśasas only know to attack covertly as you only know to attack directly”, I could not inform you about such aspects.
- *kula nal yānai maruppu osittāy* – Oh one who effortlessly broke the tusk of the elephant which is best right from birth to its nature. At that time I could not stand along with the girls of maturā and say as in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam “*… na samam yuddamityāhu:…* ” (this is not a fair battle between śrī rāma who is positioned on the ground and the rākśasas who are positioned in their chariots).
- *pūvai vīyā nīr tūvi* – Explained as placing the flowers at his divine feet and sprinkling water; also explained as flower which is \[fresh\] with water – placing that at his divine feet.
- *pōdu* – Though I did not worship him at those times with flowers and water; though I did not pamper him to eliminate his fatigue at those times when he won over the bulls and so on.
- *nin pūvi vīyā mēnikku* – The divine body/form of yours which can only be pampered with \[soft\] flowers; alternatively – the divine body/form that has the complexion of pūvaippū (dark-coloured flower). vī is a synonymous noun for pū (flower). For his body which is as tender as a flower.
- *mēnikkup pūsum sāndu* – As said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam kāṇḍam 5 “*āvayōrgātra sadruśam*” (matching the body), when nambi mūtta pirān (balarāma) and he (kriṣṇa) entered śrī maturā, they looked at kūni (the hunched-back lady) and told her “can you apply sandalwood paste on my elder brother and me, which is suitable for us?”, she first gave very inferior quality sandalwood paste; “*sugandamētat”* – he said “this may be suitable for you”; she then presented little better quality paste; “*rājārham*” – he said “this may be suitable for kamsa”; she then presented even better quality paste; “*ruciram*” – he said “this can be applied on us”. Hearing his merciful words, kūni wondered “How is that these young covherd boys who are engaged with butter, know about the different qualities of sandalwood pastes?” and smiled due to that;  “*rucirānēna*” – he says “this is a beautiful face suitable to provide best quality sandalwood paste!”. Thus, kriṣṇa says “Those who supply best quality sandalwood paste, should know about the bodies of the consumer of the same; thus you provide the suitable \[best\] sandalwood paste for my elder brother and myself”. For such body which is applied with the best sandalwood paste, let my \[[āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s\] heart be the sandalwood paste.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.3.2. Pusum sandu

*pūsum sāndu en nenjamē punaiyum kaṇṇi enadudaiya vāsagam sey mālaiyē vān pattādaiyum ahdē tēsamāna aṇikalanum en kai kūppuc ceygaiyē īsan jñālam uṇḍumiḻnda endai ēka mūrttikkē*

**Пословный перевод:**

īsan – being natural controller; jñālam uṇḍu umiḻnda – being the protector of all since he consumes everything and spits them out again (during the danger of praḷayam (deluge)); endai – being my lord (enslaving me by manifesting this activity); ēkam – matchless; mūrttikku – for the one who has form; pūsum – suitable (as given by kūni \[vendor of sandal paste\]); sāndu – sāttuppadi (sandalwood paste); en nenjam – my heart; punaiyum – adorning (as joyfully offered by śrīmālākārar \[vendor of garlands\]); kaṇṇi – divine garland; enadudaiya – my; vāsagam – the words which are the result of my speech; sey – strung; mālai – garland; vān – best; pattādaiyum – garment; ahdē – those words only; tēsamāna – adding tējas (radiance); aṇi – worn; kalanum – ābharaṇams (ornaments); en – my; kai kūppuc ceygaiyē – the anjali (salutation with joined palms)

**Перевод:**

**For the emperumān who is the natural controller, the protector of all since he consumes everything and spits  them out again, and hence my lord, and who has matchless form, my heart is the suitable sandalwood paste; the garland strung with the words which are the result of my speech is the divine garland; only those words make the best garment; my anjali is the ornaments worn by him adding radiance to him.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In second pāsuram – āḻvār becomes pleased thinking “my remembrance etc are his angarāga (scented cosmetic) etc”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “For the lord who is sarvaniyantā (controller of all) and sarvarakśaka (protector of all), my karaṇatrayam (three faculties – mind, speech, body) became enjoyable”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*My remembrance etc which are the effects of faculties became enjoyable tools for emperumān who is paripūrṇa (complete). pūsum sāndu en nenjamē punaiyum kaṇṇi enadudaiya vāsagam sey mālaiyē vān pattādaiyum ahdē tēsamāna aṇikalanum en kai kūppuc ceygaiyē īsan jñālam uṇḍumiḻnda endai ēka mūrttikkē*

- *pūsum sāndu en nenjamē* – After meditating upon the distinguished nature of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s divine form, and emperumān’s attachment towards him, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) repeats this sequence \[these were the last few words of previous pāsuram\].
- *punaiyum kaṇṇi* – Not some inferior garland, but the best garland.
- *enadudaiya vāsagam sey mālaiyē* – He need not specifically say “*vāsagam sey avar \[emperumān’s\] mālaiyē*“; whatever belongs to āḻvār naturally belongs to emperumān.
- *vāsagam sey mālaiyē* – Seems that his words are more fragrant than his heart. sandalwood paste’s fragrance is increased by the presence of fragrant garlands.
- *vān pattādaiyum ahdē* – The same words are the garments which manifest his supreme masculinity. Since his pā (poems) are of best nūl (double meaning in tamiḻ – thread as well as śāstram), they make the best silk garment. He prayed in the beginning itself that his poems should come out as best.
- *tēsamāna aṇikalanum* – the ornaments which bring about radiance to him.
- *en kai kūppuc ceygaiyē* – His anjali (joined palms) brought about radiance as done by the ornament named cēra pāṇḍiyan \[namperumāḷ’s unique ornament\].

Does [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who has acquired great radiance through these, have any limitations?

- *īsan* – sarvēsvaran.

Since he is the rakśaka (protector), would he let his belongings suffer?

- *jñālam uṇḍumiḻnda* – he is the protector in all ways for the jagat (worlds).
- *endai* – one who enslaved me by showing such protection.
- *ēka mūrttikku* – for the one who has matchless divine form.
- *ēka mūrttikku – pūsum sāndu en nenjamē* – For his divine form which is known as in cāndōjña upaniśat “*sarvaganda:*” (source of all fragrances), would my heart be suitable?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.3.3. Eka murtti

*ēka mūrtti iru mūrtti mūnṟu mūrtti pala mūrtti āgi aindu būtamāy iraṇḍu sudarāy aruvāgi nāgam ēṟi naduk kadaluḷ tuyinṟa nārāyaṇanē! un āgamuṟṟum agattadakki āvi allal māyttadē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ēka mūrtti – Having the causal form (as said in cāndōjña upaniśat “ēkamēva” (Only him) with the cit (sentient entities) and acit (insentient entities) in their subtle form); iru mūrtti – having the forms of mahat and ahankāram (both of which are sequential manifested states of the primordial matter which is avyakta (unmanifest)); mūnṟu mūrtti – having the variations based on satvam (goodness), rajas (passion) and tamas (ignorance) qualities, as attributes; pala mūrtti āgi – having the 11 senses (panca karmēndriyam (5 sense organs of action), panca jñānēndriyam (5 sense organs of knowledge) and manas (mind)) as attributes (these 11 senses are an effect of vaikārika, one of the three types of ahankāram), as attributes; aindu būtamāy – having panca bhūtams (five great elements, which are effects of bhūtādi, which is the tāmasa ahankāram, one of the three types of ahankāram) as attributes; iraṇḍu sudarāy – having sun and moon (which are cited as a sample for the entities inside the aṇḍam (oval shaped universe), which are part of vyaśti sruśti (variegated creation)) as his forms; aru āgi – being in a subtle form (as the in-dwelling super soul of such entities); nāgam – on tiruvanantāḻvān (ādiśēśan); ēṟi – climb; naduk kadal uḷ – in the tiruppāṟkadal (milk ocean); tuyinṟa – resting; nārāyaṇanē – Oh one who is known by the word nārāyaṇa (which is established by such antarātmatva (being the in-dwelling super-soul) and samudrasāyitva (resting in ocean))!; un – your; āgam – form; muṟṟum – all beauty (of having all of my faculties as all of your decorations); agattu – in my heart; adakki – consumed and enjoyed; āvi – my ātmā; allal – the sorrows (which occurred to me in previous decad); māyttadē – are gone

**Перевод:**

**emperumān is having the \[singular\] causal form, having the forms of mahat and ahankāram, having the variations based on satvam (goodness), rajas (passion) and tamas (ignorance) qualities as attributes, having the 11 senses as attributes, having panca bhūtams as attributes, having sun and moon as forms, being in a subtle form; Oh one who is known by the word nārāyaṇa, who climbed on tiruvanantāḻvān (ādiśēśan) in the tiruppāṟkadal (milk ocean) and resting there! After having consumed and enjoyed all your beautiful form (which is having all my faculties as all your decorations), the sorrows of my ātmā are gone.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In third pāsuram – āḻvār speaks about the fulfilment acquired by emperumān through this loving relationship with him.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “My ātmā, after enjoying your beauty which has relationship with all due to you being the ātmā of all, was relieved from worldly sorrows”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Third pāsuram. āḻvār says “By making me exist fully for you, you became fulfilled \[completing what is to be completed\]”. ēka mūrtti iru mūrtti mūnṟu mūrtti pala mūrtti āgi aindu būtamāy iraṇḍu sudarāy aruvāgi nāgam ēṟi naduk kadaluḷ tuyinṟa nārāyaṇanē! un āgamuṟṟum agattadakki āvi allal māyttadē*

- *ēka mūrtti* – As said in cāndōjña upaniśat “*sadēva sōmya idam agra āsīt*” (Oh śvētakētu who is qualified to drink sōma juice! before creation, sat only existed), before creation, the whole material realm which is indicated by the term “*idam*” was in a subtle state, and [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) existed having everything subdued in him – this state is discussed here as the singular form. It also explains, the distinguished form of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) before sruśti (creation). Thus, his form where he is set out to create, is explained here.
- *iru mūrtti* – His witnessing prakruti (primordial matter – unmanifested form) and mahān (manifested form) and having them as his forms is explained. Thus, bhagavān having both cause (prakruti) and effect (mahān) as his forms is explained; the proximity of both principles is explained here \[as cause and effect\]; mahān is the manifested state of the unmanifested prakruti.
- *mūnṟu mūrtti* – [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) being with three different ahankārams as his forms is explained. ahankāram exists in the mode of sātvika (goodness), rājasa (passion) and tāmasa (ignorance).
- *pala mūrtti aindu būtamāy* – Now, the previously followed order is not being followed here \[Previously, the cause – effect relationship was explained in a step-by-step manner. Now, the effects are collectively explained\]. Effect of sātvika ahankāram is the 11 indriyams (senses); the effect of tāmasa ahankāram is panca bhūtams \[earth, water, fire, air, ether\]; rājasa ahankāram facilitates both sātvika and tāmasa ahankāram in their transformation. Thus explaining the 11 senses and 5 great elements and highlighting that emperumān is having these as his \[many\] forms.
- *iraṇḍu sudarāy* – As said in taittiriya nārāyaṇa upaniśat “*sūryācandramasau dātā yatā pūrvamakalpayat*” (brahmā \[with [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) as antaryāmi\] created sun, moon \[and everything\] as they were before), sun and moon are examples for the effect \[created objects\].
- *aru āgi* – After creating them, entering into them to sustain them as said in taittirīya upaniśat “*tat sruśtvā tadēvānuprāviśat tadanupraviśya sacca tyaccābhavat*” (He created it (universe); he entered in there; after entering he became (assumed the forms of) cētana (sentient) and acētana (insentient)) – this subtle form is explained. After explaining [acit](http://ponnadi.blogspot.in/2013/03/thathva-thrayam-achith-what-is-matter.html) (matter) previously \[up to *iraṇḍu sudar*\], should aru (formless – i.e. subtle form) not indicate [cit](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) (sentient beings)? As said in cāndōjña upaniśat 6.3.178, it is said that “*…anēna jīvēna ātmanānupravisya nāma rūpē vyākaravāṇī…*” (I (brahmam) enter through this [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)(s) as antaryāmi and give them names and forms), as [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) enters as antaryāmi through [jīvātmās](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/), that principle \[i.e., jīvātmā\] is also explained.
- *nāgam ēṟi* – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) arrived at tiruppāṟkadal (milk ocean) and reclined on tiruvantāḻvān (ādiśēśa) to be approached by brahmā et al who were thus created. Also explained as – like a farmer would build a hut and stay right there in the field after planting the seeds, emperumān reclined in milk ocean for the protection of the created entities.
- *nārāyaṇanē* – The natural quality of emperumān being the goal which makes him constantly giving out his mercy at all times, is explained here.
- *un āgamuṟṟum agattadakki* – āgam – body. For your divine body, these are the sandalwood paste, garland, garments, ornaments etc that are suitable; *agattadakki* – making them exist in me. This is the purpose of creation \[for [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) to enter along with all of these aspects into [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s heart\].

Who becomes relieved from sorrows by this? [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) only.

- *āviyallal māyttadē* – “Somehow the distress in your heart got eliminated. You became krutakrutya (fulfilled that the task is completed) by uplifting me”. Alternatively – my soul became freed from sorrow.

Some explain this as – *ēka mūrtti* indicates paratva \[his form as para vāsudēva in spiritual realm\], *iru mūrtti* indicates vyūha state of vāsudēva and sankarśaṇa, *mūnṟu mūrtti* indicates – vāsudēva, sankarśaṇa and pradyumna, *pala mūrtti* indicates \[many\] incarnations and “*aindu būtamāy iraṇḍu sudarāy*” indicates the classification of this person is responsible for creation, this other person is responsible for sustenance and so on.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.
