## 4.3.4. Mayttal enni

*māyttal eṇṇi vāy mulai tanda māyap pēy uyir māytta āya māyanē! vāmananē! mādavā! pūttaṇ mālai koṇḍu unnaip pōdāl vaṇangēnēlum nin pūttaṇ mālai nedu mudikkup punaiyum kaṇṇi enaduyirē*

**Пословный перевод:**

māyttal – to finish; eṇṇi – thinking; vāy – in the divine mouth; mulai tanda – placed her breast; māyam – having a motherly form (which is favourable); pēy – evil demon’s; uyir – prāṇa (vital air); māytta – finished; āyan – without any deficiency in “covherd child” qualities; māyanē – Oh amazing emperumān!; vāmananē – blessing me to see vāmanāvatāram (where he manifested his lordship over the whole universe and showed that everything is fully dependent on him); mādavā – Oh one who established (your natural) śriya:patitvam (being the lord of śrī mahālakśmi)!; unnai – you (who is the destroyer of enemy in disguise); pū – with distinguished flowers; taṇ – cool; mālai koṇḍu – with garlands; pōdu – according to the situation; vaṇangēnēlum – even though I did not get to worship you; nin – your; pū – abundant flowers; taṇ – fresh; mālai – decorated with garland; nedu – tall (revealing the supremacy over everyone); mudikku – for the divine crown; punaiyum – worn as decoration; kaṇṇi – garland; enadu uyirē – my prāṇa (vital air, life)!

**Перевод:**

**Oh amazing emperumān who finished the life of the evil demon who was having a (favourable) motherly form and place her breast in your divine mouth thinking to finish you, who is without any deficiency in “covherd child” qualities! Oh you who is blessing me to see vāmanāvatāram! Oh one who established (your natural) śriya:patitvam! Even though I did not get to worship you with cool garlands and flowers, my prāṇa (vital air, life) is the garland which is worn as decoration for your tall divine crown which is decorated with garland made of abundance of flowers!**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In fourth pāsuram – āḻvār becomes pleased thinking “My prāṇa (vital air) has become the suitable pampering tool for your fatigue after performing activities such as accepting milk from \[demoniac\] pūtanā and so on, and for the tenderness of yours, who is śriya:pati (lord of śrī mahālakśmi)”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “For you who is śriya:pati, who has enslaved me completely by killing pūtanā who is anukūla śatru (enemy in disguise), my prāṇa became the distinguished decoration on your divine head”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Fourth pāsuram. āḻvār says “Though I could not pamper you to remove your fatigue during the killing of pūtanā et al, for your tender divine body which cannot survive without pampering, my existence itself is the suitable garland”. māyttal eṇṇi vāy mulai tanda māyap pēy uyir māytta āya māyanē! vāmananē! mādavā! pūttaṇ mālai koṇḍu unnaip pōdāl vaṇangēnēlum nin pūttaṇ mālai nedu mudikkup punaiyum kaṇṇi enaduyirē*

- *māyattal eṇṇi* – Looking at her intentions while approaching kriṣṇa, it is natural that there is need for some one to care for him. Since there is no mention of who is to be finished in “*māyttal eṇṇi*” (thinking to finish), [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying “She came to finish the whole universe”; when the soul is destroyed, the body will naturally be destroyed; when the life itself is attacked, one need not attack each limb; he is the singular soul of the entire universe. sugrīva on seeing vibhīśaṇa with his assistants said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 17.5 “*asmān hantum na samśaya:*” (to kill us, there is no doubt).
- *vāy mulai tanda* – āḻvār is saying “*tanda*” (gave) since pūtanā trying to breast-feed the poison to kriṣṇa made āḻvār feel as if she gave it to āḻvār himself; alternatively, “*tanda*” and “*kodutta*” can be simply treated as synonyms and is simply explaining that she breast-fed poison to kriṣṇa.
- *māyap pēy* – Not just evil by birth, she also came in disguise. That is, instead of coming in her real form, she came in a motherly form as said in periya tirumoḻi 1.5.6 “*tāyāy vanda pēy*” (the demon which came in the disguise of mother).
- *uyir māyttu* – Whatever she came to take \[kriṣṇa’s life\], he did that \[took away her life\] to herself.
- *āya māyanē* – Oh amazingly capable covherd! He accepted the milk as a toddler; she too gave him milk like a mother; just by the nature of things \[bhagavān and her enmity towards him\], she died.
- *vāmananē* – At least in kriṣṇāvatāram, if pūtanā breast-feeds poison, there is a real mother who can give antidote to him there. mūnṟām tiruvantādi 74 “*vengongai uṇḍānai mīttu āycci ūttuvān, than kongai vāy vaittāḷ sārndu*” (Mother yaśōdā rescuing kriṣṇa from pūtanā who gave her hot \[evil\] breast, placed her breast in his mouth\], mūnṟām tiruvantādi 29 “*pēycci pāl uṇḍa perumānaip pērttu eduttu, āycci mulai koduttāḷ anjādē*” (grabbing kriṣṇa from the demon from whom he was drinking milk, without any fear, mother yaśōdā gave milk”. Another explanation – after giving birth to kriṣṇa, his mother and father were engaged in tapas \[were not paying attention\], so he himself chases down the demons \[and kills them\]. When he goes after the enemies, it creates fear in the devotees’ hearts. This is what is done in periya tiruvantādi 16 “*sīrāl piṟandu siṟppāl vaḷarādu, pēr vāmanan āgākkāl pērāḷā!*” (Oh great personality! if you did not take birth as vāmana who did not have wealthy traditions while being born …).
- *mādavā* – As said in a proverb “*tīnāḷ tiruvaudaiyārkku illai*” (those who have [śrī mahālakśmi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/), have no inauspicious days\], he escaped these dangers to embrace her. Even when there is no danger, they like to sing mangaḷāśāsanam (well-wishes) to the togetherness of [periya pirāttiyār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/) and [periya perumāḷ](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/); those caring persons \[[āḻvārs](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/azhwars/)\] said in [tiruppallāṇḍu 2](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/06/thiruppallandu-2-adiyomodum/) “*vadivāy nin vala mārbinil vāḻginṟa mangaiyum pallāṇḍu*” (Long live, you who is having śrī mahālakśmi in your beautiful right chest).
- *pūt taṇ mālai koṇḍu* – With cool flower garlands. Though I did not get to fall at your divine feet and serve you during the times of pūtanā et al.
- *ni pūt taṇ mālai nedu mudikku* – For your divine crown which reveals your supremacy over everyone which cannot survive without cool flower garland, my prāṇa/sattai (life/existence) is the desired garland.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.3.5. Kanni enaduyir

*kaṇṇi enaduyir kādal kanagac cōdi mudi mudalā eṇṇil palkalangaḷum ēlum ādaiyum ahdē naṇṇi mūvulagum naviṟṟum kīrttiyum ahdē kaṇṇan empirān emmān kāla cakkarattānukkē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kālam – to control the time; cakkarattān – having the tiruvāḻi (divine chakra \[disc\]); emmān – (by showing such beauty) being the lord who enslaved me; empirān – my great benefactor (one who lets me enjoy such beauty eternally); kaṇṇanukku – kriṣṇa (who incarnated with simplicity synchronous with the time); enadu – my dear; uyir – ātmā; kaṇṇi – became the garland (which is placed on his head); kādal – prēma \[love\] (which is the natural expression of this ātmā); kanagam – golden; sōdi – radiance (which reveals his supremacy over all); mudi mudalā – crown etc; eṇ il pal – innumerable; kalangaḷum – became ornaments; ēlum – matching (revealing his supremacy over all); ādaiyum – his divine pītāmbaram (garment); ahdē – the same; mū ulagum – three types of ātmās \[nitya (eternally free), mukta (liberated), badda (bound) souls\]; naṇṇi – approach; naviṟṟum – continuously recite; kīrttiyum – eulogies; ahdē – the same

**Перевод:**

**For kriṣṇa who is having the divine chakra to control the time, who is the lord who enslaved me and who is my my great benefactor, my dear ātmā became the garland; my prēma (love) became his innumerable ornaments such as the golden radiant crown etc; the same \[prēma\] became his divine pītāmbaram (garment); the eulogies which were continuously recited by the three types of ātmās who approach him, also are the same \[his ornaments\].**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In fifth pāsuram – āḻvār says that each one of his qualities such as snēham (friendship) etc towards emperumān is an ornament and other appendage for emperumān.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “For kriṣṇa who is enjoyable, the lord, the benefactor and is easily approachable, my prēma (love) etc are the ornaments etc”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. kaṇṇi enaduyir kādal kanagac cōdi mudi mudalā eṇṇil palkalangaḷum ēlum ādaiyum ahdē naṇṇi mūvulagum naviṟṟum kīrttiyum ahdē kaṇṇan empirān emmān kāla cakkarattānukkē*

- *kaṇṇi enaduyir* – Whatever I considered as mine, he accepted that as his garland \[what a great quality\]! It is apt for him to have śrī mahālakśmi who is said as in tiruvāimoḻi 10.10.2 “*mārvattu mālai*” (the garland of his chest); instead he is having my existence as his garland.
- *kādal* … – My love is his attractive, supremacy revealing divine crown and many other divine ornaments. How can [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s friendship become [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s ornaments? emperumān after becoming the target of āḻvār’s love, considers that he acquired all the radiance that would be acquired by wearing many divine ornaments – thus based on emperumān’s opinion, āḻvār’s love is considered as the many ornaments for emperumān.
- *ēlum ādaiyum ahdē* – The same love is the matching divine garment for his waist. Once when a śrīvaiṣṇava vaṇṇattān (vaśerman), washed \[periya perumāḷ’s\] clothes perfectly and presented to [emperumānār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/emperumanar/), being very pleased, he held vaśerman’s hands and took him in front of periya perrumāḷ and said “nāyantē! please bestow your divine glance for the clothes he washed to match your divine waist” and mercifully showed the clothes to periya perumāḷ. [periya perumāḷ](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) became very pleased and mercifully spoke to [udaiyavar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/emperumanar/) “For the sake of this vaśerman, I have forgiven the vaśerman who committed offense towards me in kriṣṇāvatāram \[When kriṣṇa and balarāma entered maturā, they first met a vaśerman who refused to give freshly washed clothes to them and insulted them, to be killed by kriṣṇa\]”.
- *ēlum ādaiyum ahdē* – Not just one type of object, but all types of objects for him. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s love is the divine pītāmbaram (yellow garment) which highlights his supremacy also. This \[love\] is the long time effort which becomes [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s divine ornaments and garments. His love is what sustains him as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 2.3.3](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/02/thiruvaimozhi-2-3-3-ariyak-kalaththulle/) “*aṟiyāk kālattuḷḷē adimaikkaṇ anbu seyvittu*” (when there was no scope to know about such relationship, you engaged me in servitude towards you). bruhadāraṇyaka upaniśat 4.3 “*mahārajatamvāsa:*” (the best golden garment). Since āḻvār’s pāsurams are as said in tiruvāimoḻi 4.3.11 “*poyyil pādal*” (songs which have no lies), no need to doubt his words.
- *naṇṇi mū ulagum* … – Not just greatly knowledgeable devotees, but all come and approach him and glorify him like waves rising from ocean – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s love is such glorification. After accepting āḻvār’s love, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) started thinking “even those anyaparar (devotees with ulterior expectations) became ananyaparar (exclusive devotees)”.

Subsequently, emperumān’s efforts to kindle such love in [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/), is explained; he showed already serving devotees and converted āḻvār to be like them.

- *kāla cakkarattān em pirān emmān kaṇṇanukku* – For my lord, kriṣṇa, who manifested his divine combination of beautiful hand and divine chakra and bestowed me ananyaparatvam (exclusive existence for [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)) and made me to be as said in tiruviruttam 97 “*kaḻivadōr kādal uṟṟārkkum uṇḍō kaṇgaḷ tunjudal*” (can those who have great love towards emperumān, close their eyes and ever sleep?).
- *kāla cakkaram* – He \[sudarśana cakkarattāḻvār\] can turn day into night. tiruvāḻi (divine cakram) which controls time. Also explained as the divine cakram that can eliminate our binding to time. In the dark times as said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 6.1.41 “… *nārcayiśyanti*” (In the kaliyuga, by the influence of crooked persons, people will stop vorśipping viṣṇu, the sarvēśvara) and in the samsāram \[material realm\] which is said as in tiruvāimoḻi 10.6.1 “*iruḷ taru mā jñālam*” (this world which gives us ignorance), the divine chakra which drives out the darkness as said in tiruviruttam 33 “*aruḷār tiruccakkaram*” (the divine chakra which is filled with mercy), which kindles my taste \[towards him\] and keeps me inseparable at his divine feet as he resides inseparable in his hand. cakkarattāḻvār will stay in his hand and make everyone fall at [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s divine feet.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.3.6. Kala cakkarattodu

*kāla cakkarattodu veṇ sangam kai ēndināy jñālamuṟṟum uṇḍumiḻnda nārāyaṇanē enṟenṟu ōlamittu nān aḻaittāl onṟum vārāyāgilum kōlamām en sennikku un kamalam anna kurai kaḻalē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kālan – having the nature of becoming kāla (the destroyer) (to destroy the enemies); cakkarattodu – with tiruvāḻi (divine chakra, disc); veḷ sangu – śrī pāncajanya conch which has (contrasting) white colour; am – beautiful (adding grace to them); kai – in the divine hand; ēndināy – one who held; jñālam – for the world (which is protected); muṟṟum – without a trace; uṇḍu – placing it in his stomach and protecting it; umiḻnda – (after the deluge) spitting it out to let it see the outside; nārāyaṇanē – Oh nārāyaṇa (who has natural relationship)!; enṟu enṟu – saying these aspects repeatedly; ōlamittu – crying out; nān – I (who is not worthy of your arrival); aḻaittāl – even if I called; onṟum – without any indication (of your arrival, as said in periya tiruvantādi 8 “arugum suvadum terivuṇarōm” (we don’t have the ability to approach you or know the means to approach you)); vārāy āgilum – even if you don’t arrive; en sennikku – for my head (for me who cannot sustain without you); un – your (the master); kamalam anna – infinitely enjoyable like a lotus flower; kurai – making sounds of bravery (which highlight the protection for your devotees); kaḻal – divine feet; kōlam Am – shining radiantly as decoration

**Перевод:**

**Even if I said “Oh nārāyaṇa who is holding in the beautiful divine hands, the tiruvāḻi which is having the nature of becoming kāla (the destroyer) and śrī pāncajanya conch which has (contrasting) white colour, and who places the world in your stomach, protecting it and then spitting it out to let it see the outside!” repeatedly, cried out and I called you, and if you don’t arrive or don’t show any indication of your arrival, your infinitely enjoyable lotus flower like divine feet which make sounds of bravery are the shining radiant decoration for my head.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In sixth pāsuram – āḻvār says “Oh emperumān who has such love towards me! even if you don’t unite with me, your existence itself is my sustenance etc”. Why is āḻvār now talking about his own love towards emperumān \[as this decad is about emperumān’s love towards āḻvār\]? It is to indicate that the great love of emperumān towards āḻvār, caught on to āḻvār and made āḻvār also reciprocate such love towards emperumān.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Sixth pāsuram. āḻvār says “even if you, who has such love towards me, do not come to me, your existence only is my sustenance etc”. āḻvār says “Though I did not help you, just as my existence is your sustenance etc, even if you don’t come, your existence is my sustenance etc”. While, āḻvār is talking about emperumān‘s love, why did he mention about his own love here? When two people unite and enjoy, the joy which is derived is common for both; in this, previously āḻvār spoke about emperumān’s love; now, he is saying that emperumān’s overflowing love made him to manifest such love towards emperumān as well. kāla cakkarattodu veṇ sangam kai ēndināy jñālamuṟṟum uṇḍumiḻnda nārāyaṇanē enṟenṟu ōlamittu nān aḻaittāl onṟum vārāyāgilum kōlamām en sennikku un kamalam anna kurai kaḻalē*

- *kāla cakkaram* … – This is how [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) calls out. Oh one who gently holds \[like holding a flower\] the divine chakra which is an enemy for the opponents and white Sanka which is a contrast for your dark complexion, in your beautiful hand, which should be checked for evil-eyes even when there is nothing on them \[what to speak, when the conch and disc are present in them?\]! Like pristine whiteness is the identity for pāncajanya, destroying the enemies is the identity for tiruvāḻi (sudarśana chakra).
- *jñāla muṟṟum …* – When he is decorated with these weapons as ornaments, instead of remaining indifferent when his vibhūti (belongings) is suffering, he would help when needed. During total deluge, he would place the world in his stomach and protect it, and when the deluge is over, he would let it out – in this manner he will completely protect all.
- *nārāyaṇanē* – Protecting fully in this manner, and the protected ones not having to feel “He protected me, how am I going to payback?”, he is naturally related. One does not feel “My mother cared for me when I was in her stomach, what can I do for her in return?” – that is due to natural relationship; [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is also similar to mother as said in periya tirumoḻi 11.6.6 “*tāy irukkum vaṇṇam ummait than vayiṟṟirutti uyyak koṇḍavan*” (Like a mother, he kept you \[all\] in his stomach and protected you).
- *enṟu enṟu* – Speaking about the combination of the divine hand and the āḻvārs (weapons, Sanka and chakra, who are indicated as śangattāḻvār and cakkarattāḻvār), his protection as required at specific times, the natural relationship even if such beauty and helping tendency was there. By repetition, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s individual engagement in each aspect is highlighted.
- *ōlamittu nān aḻaittāl* – When I who is powerless, call out for you. When I call out in high pitch so that you hear my cry and are shaken so much that you have to come, even when you are in paramapadam.
- *ōnṟum vārāy āgilum* – As said in mahābhāratam udyōga parvam “… *kuśastalē nivasati sa ca prātarihaiśyati*” (Oh vidura! kriṣṇa who came from upaplāvya, is now staying in kuśastalam. In the morning, he will arrive here), even if there is no scope for “he had left from his abode and have arrived here”. “*nāmagrāhanca nātasya śītala: kāhaḷadvani:*” (The trumpet sound which resembles the name of kriṣṇa, will have a cooling effect).
- *kōlamām en sennikku* – For my head which considers as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 98.8 “*yāvanna śaraṇau bhrātu: pārtivavyanjanānvitau \| śirasā dārayiśyāmi  na mē śāntirbhaviśyati \|\|*” (Until I behold the divine feet of my brother śrī rāma who has all qualities of being a king, I will not have peace), \[your divine feet as\] decoration.
- *un kamalam anna* – As people would desire to wear fresh flowers \[[āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is desiring the lotus like divine feet of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)\].
- *kurai kaḻalē* – kurai can mean vastness, which indicates enjoyable nature of the divine feet; it can also mean the sound of ornaments \[decorating the feet\]. Why is āḻvār saying “*vārāyāgilum kōlamām*” (even if you don’t come, your divine feet are my decoration)? [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says “You should not avoid coming here. But if that happened \[you did not arrive\], this is my thinking”. āḻvār is saying “you have pushed me to such a state \[of deep attachment towards you\]”. Naturally, āḻvār would say “*ninnalāl ilēn kāṇ*” (I won’t exist without you).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.3.7. Kurai kalalgal

*kurai kaḻalgaḷ nītti maṇ koṇḍa kōla vāmanā! kurai kaḻal kai kūppuvārgaḷ kūda ninṟa māyanē! virai koḷ pūvum nīrum koṇḍu ēttamāttēnēlum un urai koḷ sōdit tiruvuruvam ennadāvi mēladē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kurai – having brave ornaments (which were added for his activities which make others exist exclusively for him); kaḻalgaḷ – divine feet; nītti – lifted; maṇ – universe; koṇḍa – measured and accepted; kōlam – having beauty; vāmanā – being vāmana; kurai kaḻal – towards those divine feet; kai kūppuvārgaḷ – those who perform anjali; kūda – to attain (only him); ninṟa – stood (as upāyam (means) and upēyam (goal)); māyanē – Oh amazing lord!; virai koḷ – abundantly fragrant; pūvum – flower; nīrum – and water; koṇḍu – having; ētta māttēnēlum – even if I am incapable of praising you (to worship you); urai – through words of vēdānta; koḷ – unlimited; sōdi – having tējas (radiance); un – your; tiru uruvam – divine form; ennadu āvi mēladu – intent on my ātmā

**Перевод:**

**Oh amazing lord who lifted your divine feet with brave ornaments and measured and accepted the universe as vāmana and stood for those who perform anjali towards those divine feet to attain (you)! Even if I am incapable of praising you (to worship you) with abundantly fragrant flower and water, your divine form which is having unlimited tējas through the words of vēdānta, became intent on my ātmā.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In seventh pāsuram – āḻvār becomes astonished thinking “Though I don’t have the friendship or activities matching such friendship, my existence is the cause for your life! How great is your praṇayitva (love towards me)!”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “Though I did not do anything for you, the nature of your divine form enslaves me and makes me exist exclusively for you; it has accepted my soul”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. kurai kaḻalgaḷ nītti maṇ koṇḍa kōla vāmanā! kurai kaḻal kai kūppuvārgaḷ kūda ninṟa māyanē! virai koḷ pūvum nīrum koṇḍu ēttamāttēnēlum un urai koḷ sōdit tiruvuruvam ennadāvi mēladē*

- *kurai kaḻalgaḷ nītti* – As said in tiruneduntāṇḍagam 5 “*maṇ muḻudum agappadutta ninṟa*” (stood capturing all the worlds), lifting his divine feet to have the full vastness of the world under his divine feet. kurai indicates parappu (vastness) and ōsai (sound).
- *maṇ koṇḍa kōla vāmanā* – Even after [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) completing the measurement \[and had become trivikrama\], [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s divine heart is attached to the [vāmana](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) form. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) feels that emperumān assumed the form of vāmana to please him and not to redeem indra’s lost kingdom.

Previously, the attainable goal is explained. Further, the nature of such goal, i.e., being easily attainable simply by an anjali (joined palms) is explained.

- *kurai kaḻal kai kūppavārgaḷ* – You stood to be united with those who performed anjali towards your divine feet. Alternative explanation – oh amazing person who is united with those who performed anjali having their feet held together \[without going anywhere else\]! The divine feet are attained \[easily\] by anjali \[upāyam/means\] and the target of that anjali \[upēyam/goal\]. Like indra is attached to his rājyam (kingdom), āḻvār is attached to the beautiful divine feet \[kurai indicates beauty\]. The divine feet which were the means for indra \[to redeem his kingdom\], are the goal for [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/).
- *māyanē* – How amazing! you are attainable by a simple anjali! – says āḻvār.
- *virai* … – When you are attainable simply by an anjali, it is naturally fitting for the cētana (sentient entity) to serve you with puśpa (flowers) etc; even if I did not get do that. Even if I did not engage in natural service towards you with fragrant flowers and water as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 130.6 “*sincantu vasudām krutsnāmhimaśitēnavāriṇā*” (Let the earth be covered with cool water; then, let them throw rice flakes and flowers).
- *un urai koḷ sōdit tiru uruvam* – “*urai koḷḷugai*” means continuously reciting it; the residents of ayōdyā were like that as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 131.7 “*rāmōrāmōrāma iti prajānāmabhavankatā: \| rāma bhūtam jagatabhūt rāmē rājyam praśāsati \|\|*” (When cakravarti tirumagan ([śrī rāma](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), son of daśarata cakravarti) was ruling the kingdom, every one was constantly reciting “rāma rāma rāma”; everything in the world was seen as śrī rāma only). Alternatively – the divine form which is beyond words; another meaning – divine form which has no match or words to explain. It is said as in [tiruvāimoḻi 3.1.2](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/07/thiruvaimozhi-3-1-2-katturaikkil/) “*sutturaitta nan pon un tirumēni oḷi ovvādu*” (best molten gold will not match your divine form’s radiance).
- *ennadu āvi mēladē* – Such distinguished divine form of yours is all over my existence. The divine form that is enjoyed by nityasūris is now sustained by my existence! As said in “*kaliyar sōṟṟin mēl manam*” (hungry person’s mind is all over food). [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s nature is as said in taittirīya upaniśat bhrugu valli “*aham annam aham annam aham annam*” (I am the food \[for bhagavān\] – repeated three times for emphasis).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.3.8. Ennadavi

*ennadāvi mēlaiyāy ērkoḷ ēḻulagamum tunni muṟṟum āgi ninṟa sōdi jñāna mūrttiyāy unnadennadāviyum ennadunnadāviyum inna vaṇṇamē ninṟāy enṟuraikka vallēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ennadu āvi mēlaiyāy – intent on my ātmā; ērkoḷ – having natural radiance; ēḻ ulagamum – all worlds which are classified into seven categories; tunni – completely pervading; muṟṟum – all objects; āgi – having them as \[your\] prakāra (attributes/modes); ninṟa – stood; sōdi – naturally lustrous; jñānam – knowledge; mūrttiyāy – oh one who is having as true nature!; ennadu āvi – my ātmā’s nature; unnadum – enjoyable for you; unnadu āvi – your divine ātmā’s nature; ennadum – enjoyable for me; inna vaṇṇamē – in this manner; ninṟāy – you stood; enṟu uraikka vallēnē – how will I sing/praise this?

**Перевод:**

**Oh emperumān who is intent on my ātmā, you are completely pervading all naturally radiant worlds which are classified into seven categories, having all objects as \[your\] prakāra (attributes/modes) and having naturally lustrous knowledge as your true nature! My ātmā’s nature is enjoyable for you and your divine ātmā’s nature is enjoyable for me; how will i sing/praise this situation? Thus, the love of both emperumān and āḻvār is explained.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In eighth pāsuram – āḻvār says “The union between emperumān and me, by which one person’s nature, existence, actions etc are fully dependent on the other person, is beyond words”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār asks “Can I speak about your nature when you have pervaded all the worlds for me and accepted me?”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. ennadāvi mēlaiyāy ērkoḷ ēḻulagamum tunni muṟṟum āgi ninṟa sōdi jñāna mūrttiyāy unnadennadāviyum ennadunnadāviyum inna vaṇṇamē ninṟāy enṟuraikka vallēnē*

- *ennadu āvi mēlaiyāy* – Accepting my existence, and having great joy due to that; also explained as – one who is intent on attaining me. Also, “*ennadu āvi mēlaiyāy*” is *sambōdanam* (calling out).
- *ēr koḷ* … – Due to the joy of acquiring [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/), even his omnipresence is appearing fresh; alternative explanation – when some one \[king\] wants to capture a person \[his lady love\], he would surround the whole town, similarly, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) pervades everywhere to capture āḻvār \[Usually, this is explained with the following example – when a thief/terrorist hides in a town and the military wants to capture him, they will surround the entire town. Similarly, emperumān pervades everywhere to capture his dear devotees\] .
- *ēr koḷ ēḻ ulagamum* – Only after uniting with āḻvār, the jagat (universe) appears new/fresh. As said in “*uṇḍi udal kāttum*” (when some one eats to his full satisfaction, his body will reflect that), when śarīri \[emperumān who is the ātmā of all\] feels complete \[by uniting with [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)\], the śarīra (body) will also reflect that; he is jagat śarīri (one who has the universe as his body).
- *tunni muṟṟum āgi ninṟa* – As the jāti (the species) is all pervading in every vyakti (a creature of that species) \[For example: humanness is all pervading in a human being, in every single part of that person\], [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is pervading all objects without any limitation.
- *sōdi jñāna mūrttiyāy* – Having knowledge in the form of lustre as your true nature.
- *unnadu ennadu āviyum ennadu unnadu āviyum* – My ātmā is yours and your ātmā is mine. \[That is\] I am under your full control and you are under my full control. When [āḷavandār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/alavandhar/) was explaining this, some śrīvaiṣṇavas asked “It is understandable that this ātmā is under [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s full control; but how come he is under full control of this [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)?”. [āḷavandār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/alavandhar/) explained – When the ātmā says “Let me be under his control fully”, he may not fulfil that due to his own bondage; but when [sarvēśvara](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) places himself under an [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)‘s control, there is no possibility of violating that; thus, his vow of making himself under the control of his devotee, is that which will be long-lasting. And hence, one needs to only doubt “if the ātmā can fully be under the control of sarvēśvara?”.
- *inna vaṇṇamē ninṟāy* – you remained in this manner.
- *enṟu uraikka vallēnē* – How can I sing such praṇayitva (great love) of yours?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.3.9. Uraikka vallen

*uraikka vallēn allēn un ulappil kīrtti veḷḷattin karaikkaṇ enṟu selvan nān kādal mayalēṟinēn puraippilāda param paranē poyyilāda param sudarē iraittu nalla mēn makkaḷ ētta yānum ēttinēn*

**Пословный перевод:**

uraikka vallēn allēn – not capable (to sing your loving attitude towards your devotees); ulappu il – endless; un – your; kīrtti – overwhelming love; veḷḷattin – ocean’s; karaikkaṇ – shore; nān – I; enṟu – when; selvan – will reach?; kādal – out of love; maiyalēṟinēn – became bewildered; puraippu ilāda – without any falsehood; param paranē – having supremacy over all; poy ilāda – without any falsehood; param sudarē – oh one who is having infinite radiance!; nalla – having distinguished knowledge; mēl – having supremacy over all; makkaḷ – nityasūris; iraittu – making noise (like rising tides in the ocean); ētta – praising saying “hā’hū hā’hū”; yānum – I too; ēttinēn – praised

**Перевод:**

**I am not capable (to sing your loving attitude towards your devotees); when will I reach the shore of the ocean which is your endless love? Out of love I became bewildered; Oh one who is having infinite radiance due to having supremacy without falsehood, over all, and not having any falsehood (while uniting with me)! Just as nityasūris who are having distinguished knowledge and supremacy over all, are making noise and praising you saying “hā’hū hā’hū“, I too praised.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In ninth pāsuram – āḻvār says “Your intense love \[towards me\] is beyond my words”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “Can I complete speaking about your nature of supremacy and supreme radiance?”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Ninth pāsuram. When asked “Why can’t you speak about what you have perceived/understood?”, āḻvār replies “Your intense love \[towards me\] is beyond my words”. uraikka vallēn allēn un ulappil kīrtti veḷḷattin karaikkaṇ enṟu selvan nān kādal mayalēṟinēn puraippilāda param paranē poyyilāda param sudarē iraittu nalla mēn makkaḷ ētta yānum ēttinēn*

- *uraikka vallēn allēn* – I can only drown in enjoying your praṇayitva (loving attitude), but cannot conclude speaking about it.

When asked “You may not be able to speak fully. But can you not explain a little bit?”, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) replies

- *un* … – Can I even enter the shore of the ocean of greatness which came about due to your endless love?

When asked “If you cannot even enter the shore, why do you set out to talk about it?”, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) replies

- *kādal maiyal ēṟinēn* – I became bewildered due to my love \[towards you\]. Would any one ask a mad person “Why are you behaving like this?”?

When asked “Why did you get mad in this matter? Don’t you have some support?”, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) replies “I saw the nityasūris madly praising him; I too followed them”. This matter \[greatness of [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)\] is no different when it comes to nityasūris, or āḻvār or bhagavān himself. Even if [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is sarvajña (omniscient) and sarvaśakta (omnipotent) tries to understand himself, he cannot understand that. He will meet with the same fate as vēdams which set out to comprehend his qualities and failed \[taittirīya upaniśat “*yatō vācō nivartantē”* (mind/speech returned unable to comprehend [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s quality of bliss)\].

- *puraippu ilāda param paranē poy ilāda param sudarē* – Oh one who does not have any falsehood in the radiance acquired due to uniting with me just as there is no falsehood in your being the supreme lord of all! Alternative explanation – Just as there is no falsehood in your perfect love, Oh one who reveals the radiance acquired by uniting with me without any falsehood!
- *iraittu* … – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says “Did I praise him considering myself capable \[of praising him\]? \[No\] As I saw the nityasūris who have parama bhakti praise [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) like an ocean with rising tides, I too praised him”.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.3.10. Yanum etti

*yānum ētti ēḻulagum muṟṟum ēttip pinnaiyum tānum ēttilum tannai ētta ētta engeydum tēnum pālum kannalum amudumāgit tittippa yānum empirānaiyē ēttinēn yān uyvānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

yānum – I (who was fully blessed by him with faultless knowledge and devotion); ētti – glorify; muṟṟum – without distinction between ignorant and wise; ēḻulagum – all the worlds; ētti – glorify; pinnaiyum – further more; tānum – he himself (who is sarvajña (omniscient) and bestows knowledge to everyone); ēttilum – even if glorifies; tannai – him (who is incomprehensible); ētta ētta – repeatedly glorify (without repeating the same aspect); engu – where (How); eydum – can we complete?; tēnum – honey; pālum – milk; kannalum – sugar; amudumāgi – like nectar; tittippa – reliśable/sweet (in all manners); em – one who bestowed me such enjoyment \[of him\]; pirānaiyē – great benefactor only; yān – I; uyvān – for my uplifting; yānum – I too; ēttinēn – glorified

**Перевод:**

**Even if I glorify emperumān, even if all the \[residents of the\] worlds irrespective of ignorant or wise ones glorify him, and furthermore if he himself glorifies him repeatedly, how can we complete \[glorifying him\]? Still, I too glorified emperumān who is great benefactor and is reliśable/sweet like honey, milk, sugar and nectar, for my uplifting.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In tenth pāsuram – āḻvār says “I glorify emperumān, who has praṇayitva (love) which cannot be fully glorified by me or the whole world or emperumān himself, out of great attachment to sustain myself”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. yānum ētti ēḻulagum muṟṟum ēttip pinnaiyum tānum ēttilum tannai ētta ētta engeydum tēnum pālum kannalum amudumāgit tittippa yānum empirānaiyē ēttinēn yān uyvānē*

- *yānum ētti* –  I, who was blessed by [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) with pristine knowledge and devotion, glorifying
- *ēḻulagum muṟṟum ētti* – Everyone irrespective of having or not having distinguished knowledge, glorifying.
- *pinnaiyum tānum ēttilum …* – Being svatassarvajña (naturally omniscient), sarvaśakti (omnipotent) to complete any task he commenced, glorifying. Even if all such persons glorify him at once, the glorified aspects remain small and the remaining aspects to be glorified remain large. There is no distinction between anyaparar (those who are devoted to [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) and other matters also), ananyaparar (those who are exclusively devoted to bhagavān), those who have limited knowledge and those who have unlimited knowledge, when it comes to seeing the boundary of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s qualities.

When asked “But, why are you engaged in glorifying him?”,

- *tēnum pālum* … – I glorified him due to the sweet nature of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) as said in “*sarvarasa:*” (the source of all taste), and due to emperumān being the benefactor of manifesting his love towards me and making me engage in glorifying him.

When asked “Just because he is sweet and the benefactor, are you capable of glorifying him?”,

- *yān uyvānē* – If I don’t glorify him, how can I survive?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.3.11. Uyvupayam

*uyvupāyam maṟṟinmai tēṟik kaṇṇan oṇ kaḻalgaḷ mēl seyya tāmaraip paḻanat tennan kurugūrc catakōpan poyyil pādal āyirattuḷ ivaiyum pattum vallārgaḷ vaiyam manni vīṟṟirundu viṇṇum āḷvar maṇṇūdē*

**Пословный перевод:**

uyvu upāyam – means for uplifting; maṟṟu inmai – nothing else existing; tēṟi – established; kaṇṇan – (the one who is so attached towards his devotees,) kriṣṇa’s; oḷ – most enjoyable; kaḻalgaḷ mēl – on the divine feet; seyya – reddish; tāmarai – having lotus flower; paḻanam – having water bodies; then – in south direction; nal – praiseworthy; kurugūr – leader of āḻvārtirunagari; satakōpan – nammāḻvār‘s; poy il – without any falsehood (in his love towards emperumān); pādal – sung; āyirattuḷ – in the thousand pāsurams; ivai pattum – this decad; vallārgaḷ – those who can recite (along with meditating upon their meanings); vaiyam – in this world; manni – firmly for a long time; vīṟṟirundu – remain (in a distinguished manner); maṇṇōdē – with this world (material realm); viṇṇum – paramapadam also (spiritual realm); āḷvar – will rule over (under their control)

**Перевод:**

**nammāḻvār, the leader of praiseworthy āḻvārtirunagari which is located in south direction with water bodies having reddish lotus flowers, established that there is no other means for uplifting and among the thousand pāsurams, sang this decad without any falsehood, on the most enjoyable divine feet of kriṣṇa; those who can recite this decad (along with meditating upon its meanings), will firmly remain for a long time in this world in a distinguished manner and will rule over this world and paramapadam too.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

*poyyil pādal* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says “The manner in which [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) united with me with unlimited desire and with such pleasant interactions between us, is all true”.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the end – āḻvār says “Those who recite this decad will have the ubhaya vibhūti (spiritual realm and material realm) of īśvara, under their disposal”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. uyvupāyam maṟṟinmai tēṟik kaṇṇan oṇ kaḻalgaḷ mēl seyya tāmaraip paḻanat tennan kurugūrc catakōpan poyyil pādal āyirattuḷ ivaiyum pattum vallārgaḷ vaiyam manni vīṟṟirundu viṇṇum āḷvar maṇṇūdē*

- *uyvu upāyam maṟṟinmai tēṟi* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) did not speak about [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s praṇayitvam (love) thinking that he can fully speak about it; he spoke about it knowing that he has no other means than speaking about it to sustain himself.
- *kaṇṇan oḷ kaḻalgaḷ mēl* – At the lotus feet of kriṣṇa who incarnated to manifest such great love.
- *seyya* … – As [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) sustained himself by meditating upon his praṇayitva, the town (āḻvārtirunagari) too flourished as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 127.17 “*akāla palinō vrukśā:*” (let the trees blossom even during non-season). Mercifully sung by [nammāḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) of praiseworthy [āḻvārtirunagari](http://azhwarthirunagari.koyil.org/) of the southern direction, which is having water bodies with reddish lotus flowers.
- *poyyil pādal* … – there is no falsehood in the whole tiruvāimoḻi as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam bāla kāṇḍam 2.37 “*na tē vāk anrutā kāvyē kācit atra bhaviśyati*” (brahmā tells vālmīkī – Your words in this epic will never be false); Alternative explanation – the decad highlights that there is no falsehood in the praṇayitva (love) of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), who is avāpta samastakāma (one without any unfulfilled desires) and [sarvēśvara](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) (lord of all), as he eagerly descended and united with [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/), who was a nityasamsāri (bound soul, before), making āḻvār’s sustenance as a means of his enjoyment. When it is said as “*poyyillāda āyiram*” (the thousand pāsurams without falsehood), it includes this decad too.
- *vaiyam manni* … – In this world, like [emperumānār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/emperumanar/) who lived a long/complete life with śrīvaiṣṇavaśrī (wealth of kainkaryam, jñānam, bhakti, vairājñam etc).
- *viṇṇum āḷvar maṇṇūdē* – While being in this world itself, they will rule over paramapadam; not only when they go to parampadam as said in tiruvāimoḻi 10.9.6 “*āṇmingaḷ vānagam āḻiyān tamar*” (Oh servants of the one who is holding sudarśana chakra! you rule over the heavenly abodes), but while being right here, they will rule over there.

While explaining “*vaiyam manni vīṟṟirundu*” everytime, [nanjīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nanjiyar/) would say “Unlike us who were like those who lost the food which was so close to their mouth, those who recite this decad will remain in this world with śrīvaiṣṇavaśrī, manifesting their distinction as said in tiruvāimoḻi 10.6.2 ‘*nāttārōdiyalvoḻinhu*‘ (cutting off ties from worldly people)”. He lost \[his ācārya\] [bhattar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/parasara-bhattar/) at a very young age \[which is why he said “Unlike us who were like those who lost the food which was so close to their mouth”\].

## 4.4 Mannai irundu

## 4.4.1. Mannai irundu

*maṇṇai irundu tuḻāvi vāmanan maṇ idu ennum viṇṇait toḻudu avan mēvu vaikuntam enṟu kai kāttum kaṇṇaiyuṇṇīr malga ninṟu kadal vaṇṇan ennum annē! en peṇṇaip perum mayal seydārkku en seygēn peyvaḷaiyīrē*

**Пословный перевод:**

maṇṇai – earth; irundu – sitting; tuḻāvi – searching with the hands; idu – this; vāmanan – as vāmana who begged, measured and accepted (so others cannot claim ownership); maṇ – earth; ennum – says; viṇṇai – sky (which is high up); toḻudu – performing anjali (joined palms); avan – he (bhagavān); mēvu – eternally residing; vaikuntam – śrīvaikuṇṭam (which indicates paramavyōma – supreme/spiritual sky); enṟu – saying so; kai – indicating with her hand; kāttum – will show (to others); uḷ – inside (her heart); nīr – tears; kaṇṇai – beyond eyes; malga – to flow; ninṟu – staying; kadal – invigorating like ocean; vaṇṇan – emperumān showing, with unlimited aspects, his beautiful form, making me experience him; ennum – says; annē – Oh mother!; en – my; peṇṇai – (young) daughter; peru – in this amazing way; mayal – madness; seydārkku – one who caused; pey vaḷaiyīrē – Oh ones with fitting bangles! (unlike my daughter’s bangles which keep slipping); en – what; seygēn – shall I do?

**Перевод:**

**\[my daughter\] sitting down, searching for with the hands on earth, says “this is the earth which was begged, measured and accepted by vāmana”; performing anjali towards the sky, she is saying “that is śrīvaikuṇṭam, where bhagavān is residing eternally” and indicating with her hand, shows it to others; with the tears from inside flowing beyond her eyes, she says “emperumān with unlimited aspects, who made me experience his beautiful invigorating form, (manifesting his two vibhūtis)”; Oh mother! Oh ones with fitting  bangles! What shall I do to the one who caused madness to my young daughter in this amazing way?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In first pāsuram – The divine mother (of parānkuśa nāyaki) feels sorrowful saying “emperumān has made her go mad; what shall I do?” while explaining her daughter’s situation to those who came to enquire about her daughter.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*In first pāsuram, the mother says to those neighbours who came to enquire about her daughter “My daughter became disturbed meditating upon bhagavān‘s relationship with spiritual realm and material realm and on seeing the earth and the sky”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. maṇṇai irundu tuḻāvi vāmanan maṇ idu ennum viṇṇait toḻudu avan mēvu vaikuntam enṟu kai kāttum kaṇṇaiyuṇṇīr malga ninṟu kadal vaṇṇan ennum annē! en peṇṇaip perum mayal seydārkku en seygēn peyvaḷaiyīrē*

- *maṇṇai irundu tuḻāvi* – She will search with her hands, for all the vastness of earth which was under his divine feet as said in tiruneduntāṇḍagam 5 “*maṇ muḻudum agappaduttu ninṟa endai*” (my father who stood having all earth under his divine feet). She likes the earth only due to its relationship with [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/); but his relationship is not specific to single entity/object. \[Was there anyone who was attached to places related to bhagavān?\] śrī rāmāyaṇam bāla kāṇḍam 29.22 “*mayātu bhaktyā tasyaiva vāmanasya upabhujyatē*” (Due to my devotion to vāmana, I have an attachment to this land). śrī rāma asked sage viśvāmitra “What is this beautiful hermitage which is in front of us?” and sage viśvāmitra replied “Previously, this place known as siddāśrama, was inhabited by śrī vāmana; after he arrived here, out of devotion towards him, I would often just stay here with great attachment to this land”. Those who have attachment towards bhagavān will not let go \[of such objects that are related to him\] as said in mahābhāratam āraṇya parvam “*viṣṇur mānuśa rūpēṇa cacāra vasudātalē*” (viṣṇu assumed the human form of cakravarti tirumagan (son of daśarata cakravarti) and wandered on this earth).
- *irundu* – It appears that, before this state \[of being seated\], she was going through agony and was standing, walking etc in a disorderly manner.
- *tuḻāvi* – It appears that she cannot let go of the earth; Like a person with pitta (a type of imbalance in bile fluid) cannot take his hands off sandalwood paste \[which gives coolness to the body\]; if takes his hands off, he will be affected with over-heating of his body.

While they are looking at her and thinking “she looks confused”, she is looking at them and saying “are you confused?” \[she is properly engaged thinking about vāmana and has become bewildered, while they are not thinking about [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) and being clear\].

- *vāmanan maṇ idu ennum* – She says “īsn’t this vāmana’s earth?”. She says “isn’t this ganda (fragrance) from the divine feet \[of vāmana\]?”. Earth is famously known as “*gandavati prutivī*” (Earth has fragrance); but she (parānkuśa nāyaki) knows that it is due to the relationship with [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) who is known as “*sarvaganda:*” (source of all fragrance). She says “He begged and made it his own”. When it is his, he need not give it to her as he gave it to indra; when it is his, it naturally belongs to her too. It is not possible to get her away from searching the earth saying “It does not belong to him”.
- *idu ennum* – When it is pratayakśam (perceivable by the eyes), do you still have doubt about the ownership of the earth? While she can perceive now, what happened in the past \[vāmana measuring the world\], she cannot \[physically\] see emperumān, who measured it, now.
- *viṇṇait toḻudu* – As she was able to perceive now, what happened in the past, she is also able to perceive the interactions of the other \[spiritual\] world right here. As said in “akkarai, ikkarai” (there, here), for them \[āḻvārs\], even here \[in this material realm\], the other \[spiritual\] world will be visible clearly; just like, for us, even there \[spiritual realm\], this material realm will be clearly visible. Some (darmaputra/yudiśtra and others) saw paramapadam when they were in the āśramam of sage ārśtiśēṇa. Due to having same name \[vyōma (sky), paramavyōma (spiritual sky)\] and ūrdvākāram (being in higher position), parānkuśa nāyaki worships this sky as paramapadam.
- *avan mēvu vaikuntam* – Unlike this place where he united with me and separated, śrīvaikuṇṭam is an abode where he never leaves. Highlights the difference between avatārams \[which have specific time frame\] and his presence in paramapadam \[which is eternal\]; and her not wanting to lose him \[like he is always in paramapadam\].
- *kai kāttum* – Thinking about his singular form there and her state of not being to enjoy him there, becoming weak, unable to speak, she will simply point to that direction. Thinking about the presence of nityasūris \[eternally free souls\] in paramapadam and about her own nature to be like them, yet not having that, becoming weak, becomes incapable of speaking further \[and just shows by sign language\].
- *kaṇṇai uṇṇīr malga ninṟu* – Tears start flowing from her eyes when she thinks about not being able to enjoy him eternally in paramapadam unlike avatārams \[which are time bound\].
- *kadal vaṇṇan ennum* – He made her go mad by manifesting his \[beautiful\] form; she too highlights how he made her go crazy. His presence there resembles the embodiment of a dark sea properly – she talks about that.
- *annē* – She is crying out “Oh mother!” out of great agony. It can also be “mannē”.
- *en peṇṇai* – As said in “*yuvatiścakumāriṇi*” (one who is both a youth and child – the transition stage), she is not yet matured to be united with [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/).
- *peru mayal seydārkku* – He gave more agony to her than the agony of those who are in separation from him. She only looked at objects similar to him and grieved \[Here, the distinction between [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) and other nācciyārs like [sītā](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/), [āṇḍāḷ](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/andal/) is highlighted. They did not suffer as much as āḻvār did in separation\].
- *en seygēn* – Shall I bring him to her to relieve her from her agony? Shall I make her realize that she should wait until he arrives?
- *pey vaḷaiyīrē* – Oh ones with bangles! Like those who remain without wetting their feet even in great flood, you are remaining firmly with your bangles! Can you tell me how you retain your bangles? I will also try to apply that to my daughter \[In traditional literature, it is shown that when in sorrow of separation, one becomes weak and the bangles will slip from the hands\].

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.4.2. Pey valai

*pey vaḷaik kaigaḷaik kūppip pirān kidakkum kadal ennum seyyadōr jñāiṟṟaik kāttic cirīdaran mūrtti īdennum naiyum kaṇṇīr malga ninṟu nāraṇanennumannē! en deyva uruviṟciṟumān seyginṟadonṟaṟiyēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

pey – adorned (after slipping many times); vaḷai – with bangles; kaigaḷai – hands; kūppi – performing anjali (joined palms); pirān – benefactor (for dēvas who surrendered unto him); kidakkum – resting (to befriend me); kadal – ocean; ennum – says; seyyadu – with reddish light; ōr – unique; jñāiṟṟai – āditya (Sun); kātti – pointing with hands; sirīdaran – as said in “vidyāsahāyavantam māmādyastam sanātanam“, one who is vorśipped along with periya pirāttiyār; mūrtti – form; īdu – this; ennum – says; naiyum – becomes weak (since she was unable to approach and enjoy emperumān who is śaraṇya (refuge) and upāsya (vorśippable)); kaṇṇīr – tears; malga – flowing; ninṟu – stays; nāraṇan – nārāyaṇa (who is with natural relationship towards us); ennum – says; annē – Oh mother!; en – my; deyva uruvil – having a divine spiritual form which is similar to that of the nityasūris; siṟu – childish; mān – at youthful stage like a doe; seyginṟadu – actions; onṟu – any; aṟiyēn – don’t understand

**Перевод:**

**Performing anjali with hands adorned with bangles, looking at the noisy ocean, she says “this is the ocean where the benefactor is resting”; pointing with the hands at the unique sun with reddish light, she says “this is the form of the one who is vorśipped along with periya pirāttiyār”; she becomes weak (since she was unable to approach and enjoy emperumān who is śaraṇya (refuge) and upāsya (vorśippable)); she stays with tears flowing and says “nārāyaṇa”; Oh mother! I don’t understand any of the actions of my daughter who is having  a divine spiritual form which is similar to that of the nityasūris and is at a youthful stage like a doe.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In second pāsuram – the mother says “I cannot understand the actions of my daughter (parānkuśa nāyaki) who has a divine form”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, the mother says “She sees the ocean and sun which are related to him (bhagavān) and becomes weak”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. pey vaḷaik kaigaḷaik kūppip pirān kidakkum kadal ennum seyyadōr jñāiṟṟaik kāttic cirīdaran mūrtti īdennum naiyum kaṇṇīr malga ninṟu nāraṇanennumannē! en deyva uruviṟciṟumān seyginṟadonṟaṟiyēnē*

- *pey vaḷaik kaigaḷaik kūppi* – One who is having the form that is vorśippable even by [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), vorśipped him herself. She adorned the bangles in her hands to be vorśipped by him \[i.e., she would not normally have bangles in her hands while in separation\]. When she said “*kadalvaṇṇan*“, those bangles which were still falling, other than ones which had already fallen, remained \[as she heard the name and gained strength\]. She is suffering despite having brahmāstram (the bangles, the ultimate weapon) in her hands. Like a brave soldier had fallen with his valorous anklet, she has fallen with her bangles.

When she was lying like this, she heard the noise of the ocean.

- *pirān kidakkum kadal ennum* – She is saying “[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) became great benefactor as he descended into the near-by ocean since had he just stayed in tiruppāṟkadal (milk ocean) he cannot arrive quickly to help eliminate my sorrow”.

In this manner, she spends the night listening to the noise of the ocean and in the morning sees the arrival of sun.

- *seyya* … – In the morning, seeing the sun, she says “this is śrīdara’s form”. For her to become bewildered, there was no need for similarity in all aspects, but just a small similarity is sufficient. When she saw the “prabhā and prabhāvān” (sun’s rays and sun), she is reminded about the togetherness of [śrī mahālakśmi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/) and [śrīman nārāyaṇan](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/); śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 21.15 “*bhāskarēṇa prabhāyatā*” (sītā says – Like the sun’s rays which never get separated from the sun, I never get separated from śrī rāma).
- *naiyum* – She became weak like a hungry child in front of the parents (mother and father) together. She became weak thinking “When puruśakāra bhūtā (pirātti who recommends our situation to perumāḷ) is with him and still not having fulfilled my desire, who will do puruśakāram for me?”.
- *kaṇṇīr malga ninṟu* – Due to the weakness, her eyes became flooded with tears.
- *nāraṇan ennum* – Not having strength to say “*śrīman nārāyaṇan*” like one would cry out “*ammē*“, washing her hands with the \[overflowing\] tears \[When performing vaidika activities, one will wash the hands and then perform the act, similarly, she is doing that\] and called out “*nārāyaṇa*“.
- *annē* – Like saying “*maitrēya!*“, she is looking for a support for her.
- *en deyva uruvil* – Meditating upon sadruśa padārtams (similar objects) and sambandi padārtams (related objects), she acquired the radiance of nityasūris \[eternally free souls\] who eternally enjoy [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/);

but there is a difference between her and them,

- *siṟumān* – \[Unlike my daughter who is a very young child\] they are ancient as said in yajur vēdam accitram “*purāṇā:*” and tiruviruttam 2 “*viṇṇāttavar mūdūvar*” (those elderly residents of paramapadam).
- *seyginṟadu onṟaṟiyēnē* – I am unable to understand what she is starting and what she is ending.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.4.3. Ariyum sendiyai

*aṟiyum sendīyait taḻuvi accudan ennum mey vēvāḷ eṟiyum taṇ kāṟṟait taḻuvi ennudaik kōvindan ennum veṟikoḷ tuḻāy malar nāṟum vinai udai āttiyēn peṟṟa seṟivaḷai mun kaic ciṟu mān seyginṟaden kaṇṇukkonṟē*

**Пословный перевод:**

aṟiyum – known to burn; sem – having reddish color; tīyai – fire; taḻuvi – embracing (thinking it to be the emperumān with abundantly radiant form); accudan – he will not abandon me!; ennum – says; mey – body; vēvāḷ – did not burn (the fire did not affect her); (though she is bewildered, since fire fears bhagavān, it will not hurt her); eṟiyum – blowing; taṇ – cool; kāṟṟai – southerly breeze; taḻuvi – (since it is cool, considering it to be bhagavān) embracing; ennudai – one who is obedient towards me; gōvindan – gōvinda; ennum – says (you said that you were going to herd the cattle, but why have you come back as quick as wind?); veṟi koḷ – having abundance of fragrance; tuḻāy malar – tiruttuḻāy (tuḷasi); nāṟum – emitting pleasant smell; (as said in tiruviruttam 56 “ōr taṇ tenṟal vandu … ampūntuḻāyin intēn puyaludai nīrmaiyināl tadaviṟṟu en pulan kalanē” (a cool breeze approached me and gently touched my body and ornaments with the tuḷasi’s honey it carried); vinai udai āttiyēn – me who is being sinful (to see this bewilderment); peṟṟa – being the mother; seṟi – became enriched (due to thinking that the substitutes fire and breeze are him); vaḷai – having bangles; mun kai – having forehand; siṟu – young; mān – my daughter who resembles a deer; seyginṟadu – the activities performed; en kaṇṇukku – for my eyes; onṟē – does not appear as one (it appears to be many)

**Перевод:**

**While embracing reddish fire which is known to burn, my daughter says “he will not abandon me!”; her body did not burn (like prahlāda’s body did not burn); embracing the blowing cool southerly breeze, she says “he is my obedient gōvinda”; tiruttuḻāy from her is emitting abundance of fragrance; being the sinful mother of my young daughter who is having enriched forehand with bangles, her activities appear to be many for my eyes.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In third pāsuram – parānkuśa nāyaki‘s mother, looks speak about her many activities and says “they are innumerable”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, the mother says “parānkuśa nāyaki thinks about emperumān‘s pratāpam (valour) and anugraham (kindness) and considers agni (fire) and vāyu (air) to be him and worships them”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. aṟiyum sendīyait taḻuvi accudan ennum mey vēvāḷ eṟiyum taṇ kāṟṟait taḻuvi ennudaik kōvindan ennum veṟikoḷ tuḻāy malar nāṟum vinai udai āttiyēn peṟṟa seṟivaḷai mun kaic ciṟu mān seyginṟaden kaṇṇukkonṟē*

- *aṟiyum sendīyait taḻuvi* –  She embraced fire knowing well that it will burn and cannot be extinguished easily.  Alternatively – before when she was not bewildered, she would know that fire would burn and thus avoid it. She embraced the reddish fire which burns. Is she embracing fire thinking that “The power of fire is subdued by some mantrams/herbs”?
- *sendīyait taḻuvi* – Seeing that the fire is shining as [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) as said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 1.9.63 “*tējasām rāśimūrjitam*” (one who shines like collection of radiant rays and who has the valour to demolish his enemies), she embraces it. As said in tiruvāimoḻi 8.9.3 “*porunīrk kadal tīppattengum tigaḻum eriyodu selvadoppa*” (Like a wavy ocean set on fire approaching), she thinks that [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is wearing a shining diamond garment and coming to embrace her.
- *accudan ennum* – she says “he has come to safeguard his belonging \[me\]”.
- *mey vēvāḷ* – While she is embracing the fire out of bewilderment, why is the fire not burning her? That is because it is coming through acyuta as said in puruśa sūktam “*mukhādindraścāgniśca*” (From the mouth of the virāt puruśa (supreme lord), indra and agni appeared).
- *sendīyait taḻuvi accudan ennum mey vēvāḷ* – This \[recital of “*acyuta*” name\] is her mantram to arrest the fire.
- *mey vēvāḷ* – As said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 1.17.39 “*tat smrutyāhlāda samstita:*” (being the one with joy due to thinking about [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)), due to being wet \[sweat etc\] on thinking about bhagavān, the fire does not burn her; prahlāda said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 1.17.47 “*paśyāmi padmāstaraṇāstrutāni śītāni sāvāni diśām mukhāni*” (Oh father! Though this fire is burning fiercely due to the presence of wind, it is not burning me; I see the presence of a spread of lotus flowers in all my directions). Alternatively – there is no one for me to say as in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 53.28 “*śītōbhava*” (let there be coolness). Since the one who orders the fire to be cool, herself is embracing the fire, it will not burn her \[Here [parānkuśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is considered as a divine consort of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)\].

To embrace vāyuputra (son of vāyu, hanumān) \[or vāyu\] is the duty of the lord and his beloved consort while in separation; śrī rāmāyaṇam 1.13 “*pariśvangōhanūmata:*” (I am embracing hanumān as a present to him); Since it is said in taittirīya upaniśat “*vāyōragni:*” (From vāyu comes agni, and hence agni is seen as son of vāyu).

- *eṟiyum* … – Embracing the cool breeze. This is the amazing aspect. For the one who is suffering in separation, even cool breeze will burn. But since the air is [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s life, it also will not burn her; puruśa sūktam “*prāṇatvāyurajāyata*” (air appeared in prāṇa).
- *ennudaik kōvindan ennum* – \[Explanation in context of śrī rāma\] Can I bear his separation as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 66.10 “*najīvēyam kśaṇamapi*” (I will not survive even a moment without sītā)? [parānkuśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says – his existence is for others only.
- *ennudaik kōvindan ennum* – \[Explanation in context of kriṣṇa\] parānkuśa nāyaki says “He appeared in the form of a covherd, to embrace me and relieve me of all my suffering”. She is different from worldly people and women in separation; for worldly people, fire should burn and for women in separation, breeze should burn. She is not seen to be affected by either.
- *veṟi koḷ tuḻāy malar nārum* – The fragrance acquired from the union in “[*kōvai vāyāḷ*](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/01/thiruvaimozhi-4-3-kovai-vayal/)” will remain for some days \[that is why she is having the fragrance in her body still\]; alternative explanation – since if the incidental body is eliminated, the ātmā is naturally existing for bhagavān \[that knowledge about bhagavān is seen as the fragrance\]; another explanation – it can be said that [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) hid in the breeze and embraced her through that \[thus transmitting his fragrance to her\]. It is said in tiruvāimoḻi 8.9.10 “*anṟi maṟṟōr upāyam en ivaḷ antaṇṇantuḻāy kamaḻdal*” (What other reason can we say for the fragrance of beautiful tiruttuḻāy being emitted from her?).
- *vinai udai āttiyēn peṟṟa* – It is due to being born to me who is sinful, she is going through so much suffering. The mother identifies the puṇya (virtue) accumulated over many births as pāpa \[it is due to such puṇya, she is engaged in bhagavat viśayam\], due to the current loss. Due to my sin, she was engaged so much with him that even in separation the fragrance of tiruttuḻāy is present on her and she looks at similar objects and considers them to be him and then gives them up. Those who become engaged in bhagavat viśayam, will obviously not get along with their \[worldly\] parents; it is said in periya tirumoḻi 3.7.7 “*annaiyum attanum enṟu adiyōmukku ingu irangiṟṟilaḷ*” (she did not show mercy even though we are her parents).
- *seṟi vaḷai munkaic ciṟumān* – this is the current unfortunate situation! instead of seeing the marks of the bangles of her hand \[due to their union\] on him, we are just seeing his divine tuḷasi on her.
- *siṟu mān* – One who has many bangles in her forehand. This was her previous state, she is fit to be like that even now \[but now due to separation, her bangles slipped out\].
- *siṟu mān* – Is she matured enough to handle these? She is very young!
- *seyginṟadu en kaṇṇukku onṟē* – She is saying “It is not one; many”. Embracing fire, embracing breeze, \[her body\] smelling divine tuḷasi etc. We cannot identify her as a worldly girl since she is unaffected by fire; she cannot be said to be in union with [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) since she is seeking out the objects which resemble him; she cannot be said to be in separation since tiruttuḻāy fragrance is present on her; thus, can her nature be described as one?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.4.4. Onriya tingalai

*onṟiya tingaḷaik kātti oḷi maṇi vaṇṇanē ennum ninṟa kunṟattinai nōkki nedumālē! vā enṟu kūvum nanṟu peyyum maḻai kāṇil nāraṇan vandān enṟu ālum enṟina maiyalgaḷ seydār ennudaik kōmaḷattaiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

onṟiya – perfectly full (with all aspects); tingaḷai – moon; kātti – pointing at it (for those who are near-by); oḷi – having lustre; maṇi – like a spatika jewel \[crystal\]; vaṇṇanē – oh one who is having the form!; ennum – says; ninṟa – standing (in front, rising up to that moon); kunṟattinai – mountain; nōkki – seeing; nedu mālē – one who is having great friendship (like your form)!; vā – come on (why are you hesitating like someone who committed an offense? While you left me without seeking my permission, whose permission are you waiting for to come?); enṟu – saying so; kūvum – will call out (revealing her love in separation); nanṟu – nicely (to cater to the planted crop); peyyum – raining; maḻai – cloud; kāṇil – seeing; nāraṇan – nārāyaṇa who is the abode of water which is indicated by the word “nāra”; vandān – arrived (eliminating our sufferings); enṟu – saying so; Alum – will dance (like peacock dances with delightful sounds when seeing the clouds); ennudai – my; kōmaḷattai – tender-natured daughter; enṟu – when; ina – this type of; maiyalgaḷ – bewilderment; seydār – did he inflict?

**Перевод:**

**parānkuśa nāyaki points at the perfect full moon and says “oh one who is having a lustrous spatika jewel like form!”; seeing the mountain in front and says “one who is having great friendship (like your form)!’; will call out saying “come on”; seeing the nicely raining cloud, she will dance saying “nārāyaṇa who is the abode of water which is indicated by the word “nāra”, has arrived”; when did he \[bhagavān\] inflict this type of bewilderment on my tender-natured daughter?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In fourth pāsuram – parānkuśa nāyaki‘s mother grieves thinking “emperumān is torturing my daughter who has no support in sorrow of separation”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, the mother says “Meditating upon emperumān‘s radiant, splendid, invigorating and distinguished form, she looks at the moon, mountain and cloud and confuses them to be him”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. onṟiya tingaḷaik kātti oḷi maṇi vaṇṇanē ennum ninṟa kunṟattinai nōkki nedumālē! vā enṟu kūvum nanṟu peyyum maḻai kāṇil nāraṇan vandān enṟu Alum enṟina maiyalgaḷ seydār ennudaik kōmaḷattaiyē*

- *onṟiya tingaḷaik kātti* – Showing the perfect full moon to those who are standing by.
- *oḷi maṇi vaṇṇanē ennum* – She calls out “*oḷi maṇi vaṇṇanē!*“. She says “you have come to embrace me with a cool form resembling a lustrous jewel”. Alternative explanation – She says to those who are standing by, “this is the most lustrous [sarvēśvaran](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)“.

But those people will ask, “How can you say this dull moon is [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)?”,

- *oḷi maṇi vaṇṇanē ennum* – She will confidently say – that is bhagavān only.
- *ninṟa kunṟattinai nōkki* – By that time, she will see some mountain coming by her way; seeing that,
- *nedumālē vā enṟu kūvum* – Two explanations.
   - [piḷḷān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/pillan/) explains – Looking at the hugeness of the mountain, she will think “This must be [sarvēśvaran](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) who divinely measured the world with his divine feet with a huge form to cover the whole universe” and will call out “please come to me”.
   - [nanjīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nanjiyar/) explains – seeing a mountain which stayed immovable for long time in rains, being fresh/green, she thinks “since he is shy about his offenses, he is covering himself with a green shawl” and says “who can stop elephants from mating? why don’t you come here without hesitation?”.
- *nanṟu* … – Like the peacocks will dance in the rainy season when rains arrive at proper season instead of damaging rains, she dances seeing the rains.
- *enṟu* – saying these aspects.
- *ina maiyalgaḷ seydār* – In this manner, he \[emperumān\] drove her mad. Also implies “When did he drive her mad like this?”. After my daughter became disobedient towards me, do I have time for these? When did this happen as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 4.2.10](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/12/thiruvaimozhi-4-2-10-en-seygen/) “*en sollum en vasam allaḷ*” (she is not obedient towards my words; nor is she under my control)? When did she drive her mad like this?
- *ennudaik kōmaḷattaiyē* – Should he not see if she is capable of handling it? While she is so young that she cannot even handle togetherness, how can she handle separation?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.
