## 4.4.5. Komala van kanrai

*kōmaḷa vān kanṟaip pulgik kōvindan mēyttana ennum pōm iḷa nāgattin pin pōy avan kidakkai īdennum ām aḷavonṟum aṟiyēn aruvinaiyāttiyēn peṟṟa kōmaḷa valliyai māyōn māl seydu seyginṟa kūttē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kōmaḷam – young; vān – big; kanṟai – calves; pulgi – embracing; gōvindan – gōvinda (who was crowned for herding the cows); mēyttana – herded (with great love); ennum – says; pōm – moving; iḷam nāgattin – young serpent; pin – behind; pōy – going (thinking that “wherever it goes, we can see emperumān there”); avan kidakkai – the bed where he rests; īdu – this; ennum – says; aru – difficult (to fully exhaust by experiencing the results); vinaiyāttiyēn – me who is having sins; peṟṟa – gave birth (to suffer like this); kōmaḷam – tender natured; valliyai – creeper which spreads on the ground (due to not having a supporting stick); māyōn – one who is having amazing qualities and activities; māl seydu – made her go mad; seyginṟa – doing; kūttu – dramas; Am aḷavu – to what extent; onṟum – anything; aṟiyēn – I don’t know

**Перевод:**

**My daughter, embracing the young \[but\] big calves says “these cows were herded by gōvinda”; going behind the young serpent which is moving, she says “this is the bed where he rests”; tender-natured creeper like parānkuśa nāyaki who is born to me, having sins which are difficult to exhaust by experiencing the results, is driven mad by emperumān who is having amazing qualities and activities; I don’t know up to what extent his dramas will go on!**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In fifth pāsuram – parānkuśa nāyaki‘s mother says “I do not know when my daughter’s suffering will come to an end”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, the mother says “My daughter thinks about his actions of protection \[for others\], sees calves and a serpent and says ‘these \[calves\] are the ones he protected and this \[serpent\] is his bed while he protects'”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. kōmaḷa vān kanṟaip pulgik kōvindan mēyttana ennum pōm iḷa nāgattin pin pōy avan kidakkai īdennum Am aḷavonṟum aṟiyēn aruvinaiyāttiyēn peṟṟa kōmaḷa valliyai māyōn māl seydu seyginṟa kūttē*

- *kōmaḷa vān kanṟaip pulgi* – By age they are young, but physically they are well built – embracing such calves; calves which are shining in a distinguished manner like a ruby – embracing such calves; kōmaḷa indicates māṇikka (ruby) and youthfulness. Thus, embracing such attractive and tender calves. Their age matches kriṣṇa’s age; for those who reached him, they get sāmyāpatti (equality) \[since the calves took shelter of kriṣṇa, they too became like him\].
- *gōvindan mēyttana ennum* – Crowned for protecting the calves with great desire as said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 5.17.19 “*vatsamadyagatambālam*” (kriṣṇa who is amidst the calves and looking youthful) and in tiruneduntāṇḍagam 16 “*kanṟu mēyttu iniduguanda kāḷāy*” (the bull like kriṣṇa who lovingly herded the calves). Their well-nourished state is physically visible indicating that they were lovingly cared by the apt-lord. When she embraces the calf’s neck, it will jump and run – she will say “the calf is as active and youthful as kriṣṇa”.

At that time, a serpent goes by; she starts following it. That is the bhōga prāvaṇayam (bhōga means enjoyment and serpent; desire for enjoyment, desire for serpent) for her.

- *iḷa nāgam* – muktātmās will always remain 25 years old, due to constant engagement with [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/); she considers that youthful state to be present in the serpent too. Is she thinking properly to embrace the calves and go behind serpent? since the calves remain in one place, she embraces them and since the serpent keeps moving, she chases it. Since she thinks “wherever it goes, he will come there”, she went behind it. He is known to be paramabhōgi (most enjoyable; the supreme person on the serpent).
- *avan kidakkai īdu ennum* – It will go inside ant-hill, its resting place; she will keep looking at that ant-hill, in order to see him when he comes there.
- *Am aḷavu onṟum aṟiyēn* – Is the world going to end? I don’t know; she is not withdrawing realizing it to be a serpent; what will happen now? For the divine mother, it appears that her daughter is residing with a serpent \[which is very dangerous\]. If she dies, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), who is the cause of whole universe, will also be gone; if the cause \[[bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)\] is gone, the effect \[universe\] will also be gone.
- *aru vinai āttiyēn peṟṟa* – My sins are the cause for her thoughts and sufferings. Alternatively – it is explained as – my tender daughter who is born to me due to my endless puṇyas (virtues) as said in tiruviruttam 37 “*nedungālamum kaṇṇan nīḷ malarppādam paravip peṟṟa*” (acquired by vorśipping kriṣṇa’s big lotus feet for a long time).
- *peṟṟa* – Though she is born to her, she is beyond her reach/control as she became completely belonging to [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s spiritual world.
- *kōmaḷa valliyai* – Not just any creeper, but very young creeper. She is in a childish stage where she needs the support of bhagavān.
- *māyōn* – One who is having amazing praṇayitva (greatly loving) guṇam which can make one forget oneself on seeing him.
- *māl seydu* – driving her mad.
- *seyginṟa kūttu* – dramas he plays.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.4.6. Kuttar

*kūttar kudameduttādil gōvindanāmenā ōdum vāytta kuḻal ōsai kētkil māyavan enṟu maiyākkum āycciyar veṇṇeygaḷ kāṇil avan uṇḍa veṇṇey īdennum pēycci mulai suvaittārkku en peṇ kodi ēṟiya pittē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

kūttar – dancers; kudam eduttu – lifting pots; ādil – if they dance; gōvindan – kriṣṇa (who dances out of pride of having abundance of cows); Am – yes; enā – as; ōdum – will run (to see); vāytta – that which torments the heart; kuḻal ōsai – sound of the flute; kētkil – if she hears; māyavan – kriṣṇa (who is amazing at playing the flute to console the covherd girls from their suffering in separation); enṟu – as; maiyākkum – will become bewildered; aāycciyar – in the hands of covherd girls; veṇṇeygaḷ – butter; kāṇil – if she sees; avan uṇḍa – he mercifully consumed; veṇṇey – similar butter; īdu – this; ennum – says; pēycci – pūtanā’s \[a demoniacal woman\]; mulai – breast; suvaittārkku – for the great benefactor who consumed along with her prāṇa (life) and gave himself to the world; kodi – having a slim form like a creeper; en peṇ – my daughter; ēṟiya – totally affected; pittu – madness

**Перевод:**

**If the dancers dance with the pots, my daughter will say “he is kriṣṇa” and run to see;  if she hears the sound of flute which torments the heart, she will think that to be kriṣṇa \[playing the flute\] and become bewildered; if she sees butter in the hands of the covherd girls, she says it is similar butter which was mercifully consumed by kriṣṇa; my daughter who is having a slim form like a creeper is totally affected by madness towards the great benefactor who consumed \[milk\] from pūtanā’s breast along with her prāṇa (life) and gave himself to the world.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In sixth pāsuram – parānkuśa nāyaki‘s mother explains the cause for her daughter’s madness.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, the mother says “Meditating upon bhagavān‘s heart-captivating activities, she becomes bewildered on seeing similar objects”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. kūttar kudameduttādil gōvindanāmenā ōdum vāytta kuḻal ōsai kētkil māyavan enṟu maiyākkum āycciyar veṇṇeygaḷ kāṇil avan uṇḍa veṇṇey īdennum pēycci mulai suvaittārkku en peṇ kodi ēṟiya pittē!*

- *kūttar kudam eduttu ādil* – Knowing her nature, she is isolated from watching the dancers. The covherds express their pride by engaging in dances, specifically kudak kūttu – dancing with pots. But, without knowing the result, some strangers would start dancing.

Seeing that,

- *gōvindanām enā ōdum* – When she sees them dancing, she will run to see kriṣṇa who has abundance of cows.

Some will ask “How can these dancers who beg for their living, be kriṣṇa?”, she replies

- *Am enā ōdum* – She will run to see them saying “it must be kriṣṇa”.
- *vāytta kuḻal ōsai kētkil* – When the sweet music from the flute which mesmerizes irrespective of whether one is viśēśajñar (wise) or aviśēśajñar (ignorant) is heard.
- *māyavan enṟu maiyākkum* – He himself is said as in [tiruvāimoḻi 3.4.6](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/08/thiruvaimozhi-3-4-6-palenko/) “*nudangu kēḷvi isai*” (songs/tunes that are having engaging sounds). She will be bewildered thinking about his lowly words \[of cribbing in separation\] which are expressed through his flute in the form of music, saying that “Since morning I was out in the forest to let the cattle gaze the grass, served the elders, was in separation from you and I cannot bear that – this day long separation felt like many eons”.
- *āycciyar veṇṇeygaḷ kāṇil* – She will reject the butter if told “this butter was prepared by brāhmaṇi (female counterpart of a brāhmaṇa)”; but when seeing butter which still has the odour of covherd girls …
- *avan uṇḍa veṇṇēy īdu ennum* – She says that this is the butter of the same kind which remained after he went, stole and got caught red handed.

Why does she get bewildered like this?

- *pēycci mulai suvaittārkku* – He already did a favour; from the day she got captivated by such favour, she started going mad for him. Even when the mother was not looking, pūtanā (the demon which came in the disguise of a beautiful covherd girl) tried to breast feed him, he realized the danger, finished her and saved himself for the benefit of everyone; for that favour, starting from that day, she was mad for him. For union (of a girl and her beloved boy), there are different reasons \[identified in ancient literature\] such as “*pūttaru puṇarcci*” (boy approaching the girl with a flower), “*punal taru puṇarcci*” (boy saving the girl from drowning in a river), “*kaḷiṟu taru puṇarcci*” (boy saving the girl from an elephant) etc. When a girl desires for a flower from a tall tree, boy climbing disregarding his own safety and gifting that flower for her. The girl thinks “he took all this efforts disregarding his own safety” and presenting herself to him – this is *pūttaru puṇarcci*. Presenting herself to him, for saving her while drowning in the river is called *punal taru puṇarcci*. When saving her who was unexpectedly caught in front of an elephant, if she presents herself to him – that is *kaḷiṟu taru puṇarcci*. None of these is a reason \[for [parānkuśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) presenting herself to [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)\]; she presents herself to him, for his saving himself from pūtanā.
- *en peṇ kodi* – \[Thus\] My daughter is different from all others \[explained in the different types of unions, since the girls presented themselves to the boys for a reason\]; she has natural strītvam (femininity).
- *ēṟiya pittu* – the madness of her.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.4.7. Eriya pittinodu

*ēṟiya pittinōdu ellā ulagum kaṇṇan padaippennum nīṟu sevvēyidak kāṇil nedumāl adiyārenṟōdum nāṟutuḻāy malarkāṇil nāraṇan kaṇṇi īdennum tēṟiyum tēṟādum māyōn tiṟattanaḷē ittiruvē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ēṟiya – greatly; pittinōdu – being bewildered; ellā ulagum – the whole world; kaṇṇan – kriṣṇa’s; padaippu – creation; ennum – says; nīṟu – \[some one\] with ashes; sevvē – straight up \[vertically\]; ida – applied; kāṇil – if she sees; nedumāl – to sarvēśvaran who has great attachment (towards his devotees); adiyār – devotee; enṟu – being bewildered; ōdum – runs (towards the place where they are present); nāṟu – very fragrant; tuḻāy malar – tiruttuḻāy (tuḷasi) garland; kāṇil – if she sees; nāraṇan – nārāyaṇa who is sarvasvāmi (lord of all); kaṇṇi – garland; īdu – this; ennum – says; tēṟiyum – when in stable state of mind; tēṟādum – as well as in confused state of mind; ittiru – (Unlike the other divine consort sītā who was very stable minded and said “nānyārtam kśubhyatē” and “taddasya sadruśam bhavēt“) this consort (who is bewildered in separation and seeking out for similar entities and related entities); māyōn – on emperumān who has amazing symbols of supremacy; tiṟattanaḷ – is engaged in his features

**Перевод:**

**Being greatly bewildered, my daughter says “the whole world is kriṣṇa’s creation”; if she sees some one with ashes applied vertically, she runs behind that person, thinking that person to be a devotee of sarvēśvaran who has great attachment (towards his devotees); if she sees very fragrant tiruttuḻāy (tuḷasi) garland, she says this is nārāyaṇa, the sarvasvāmi’s garland; when in stable state of mind as well as in confused state of mind, this consort is engaged in his features.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In seventh pāsuram – parānkuśa nāyaki‘s mother says “My daughter is saying that she does not know anything but emperumān‘s features whether she is stable or bewildered”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, the mother says “Whether my daughter is bewildered thinking about emperumān‘s symbols of supremacy or stable, she is always engaged in his features only”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. ēṟiya pittinōdu ellā ulagum kaṇṇan padaippennum nīṟu sevvēyidak kāṇil nedumāl adiyārenṟōdum nāṟutuḻāy malarkāṇil nāraṇan kaṇṇi īdennum tēṟiyum tēṟādum māyōn tiṟattanaḷē ittiruvē*

- *ēṟiya* … – To hear her bewildered words, like maitrēya et al \[who posed questions to other great sages which resulted in viṣṇu purāṇam etc\], the divine mother needs to follow her around. She quotes śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 1.1.32 “*viṣṇōssakāśādudbhūtamajagat*” (Everything springs from close proximity of viṣṇu; everything submerges into viṣṇu). Like a brāhmaṇa will continuously recite vēdam even if he becomes bewildered, her nature is such that she will constantly speak about kriṣṇa. In mahābhāratam, during rājasūya yāgam bhīśma says “*kriṣṇa Eva hi lōkānām utpattirapicāpyaya:*” (kriṣṇa \[is the cause for\] creation and kriṣṇa \[is the cause for\] deluge; this is well-known) – there is no confusion for her in this principle \[whatever may be her state\]; even while being bewildered, she will say everything is created by kriṣṇa.
- *nīṟu sevvē idak kāṇil* – As part of sections explaining atonement for sins, for those tāmasa puruśas (ignorant persons) who have committed great offense like killing a brāhmaṇa, it is explained that ashes should be applied and such persons will apply that; instead of looking at the material (ashes), she simply looks at the vertical manner in which they applied it and becomes bewildered; she does not realize the true nature of the substance. Would they apply it vertically? Yes, those who are totally ignorant (as intelligent as a mosquito), will apply ashes in vertical manner \[It is explained that ashes should be applied in a horizontal manner and tirumaṇ (sacred soil) should be applied in a vertical manner – some people don’t even know this\]. Considering ūrdvatā matram (only the vertical application) of the ashes, she thinks that it is devotees who have applied the soil from divine abode of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) as said in “*udrudāsivarāhēṇa*” (you \[bhūmip pirātti\] were lifted by emperumān who assumed the mahā varāha (great wild boar) form), and runs behind them.
- *nāṟu tuḻāy malar kāṇil* – One who confuses fake with real, will not leave when she sees the real thing. He wears that \[tuḷasi garland\] on his head and then gives that to his devotees. That is, he presents it to śrīsatakōpam (śatāri). [tiruvāimoḻi 1.9.7](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/10/thiruvaimozhi-1-9-7-tholinai-melum/) “… *sudarmudi mēlum tāḷiṇai mēlum punainda taṇ am tuḻāy*” (the cool beautiful tuḷasi which was at his radiant head, his shoulders and his divine feet). If she sees fragrant tuḷasi garland, she says this is a fitting garland for sarvēśvara who is the lord of ubhaya vibhūtis (both spiritual and material realms).
- *tēṟiyum …* – tēṟiyum (stable minded stated) applies to “*tuḻāy malar kāṇil*” (when she sees the tuḷasi garland); tēṟādum (bewildered state) applies to “*nīṟu sevvē idak kāṇil*” (when she sees some one with vertically applied ashes). Alternative explanation – these two indicate her state in [tiruvāimoḻi 4.3](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/01/thiruvaimozhi-4-3-kovai-vayal/) “*kōvai vāyāḷ*” decad and this decad.
- *māyōn* – The amazing lord who can cause bewilderment through the knowledge acquired \[i.e., the more one knows about him, the more bewildered one becomes\]. This consort who is engaged in such [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/).
- *it tiru* – Her characteristics are such that, she can be distinguished from [śrī mahālakśmi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/) who never separates from him. For śrī mahālakśmi, he is the goal; for parānkuśa nāyaki, both [śrī mahālakśmi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/) and [śrīman nārāyaṇan](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) are the goal.

## 4.4.8. Tiruvudai mannarai

*tiruvudai mannaraik kāṇil tirumālaik kaṇḍēnē ennum uruvudai vaṇṇangaḷ kāṇil ulagaḷandān enṟu tuḷḷum karuvudait tēvilgaḷ ellām kadal vaṇṇan kōyilē ennum veruvilum vīḻvilum ōvāk kaṇṇan kaḻalgaḷ virumbumē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tiru – complete wealth; udai – having; mannarai – kings; kāṇil – while seeing; tirumālai – śriya:pati (śrīman nārāyaṇa, who has the most complete wealth); kaṇḍēnē – have seen; ennum – says; uru – distinct forms; udai – having; vaṇṇangaḷ – entities; kāṇil – while seeing; ulagaḷandān – one who is having divine fresh physical beauty while divinely measuring the worlds with his divine feet; enṟu – saying so; tuḷḷum – joyfully dance; karu – garbagruham (inner sanctum); udai – having; tēvu ilgaḷ ellām – all temples; kadal vaṇṇan – sarvēśvara who has attractive form like that of an ocean; kōyilē – temples only; ennum – says; veruvilum – while being fearful (due to the presence of bodily relatives); vīḻvilum – while being unconscious due to the grief; ōvāḷ – without any break; kaṇṇan – kriṣṇa; kaḻalgaḷ – divine feet; virumbum – desires

**Перевод:**

**While seeing kings who have complete wealth, she says she has seen śriya:pati; while seeing \[dark-coloured\] entities, she dances saying “one who is having divine fresh physical beauty while divinely measuring the worlds with his divine feet”; she says that all temples that are having garbagruham are the temples of sarvēśvara who has attractive form like that of an ocean, only; without any break while being fearful or unconscious due to grief, she desires only kriṣṇa’s divine feet.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In eighth pāsuram – parānkuśa nāyaki‘s mother says “Even if my daughter is in a distressed state, she will exist only for emperumān“.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, the mother says “Meditating upon his aiśvarya (wealth/control), beauty and venerable nature, my daughter remembers only him at all states, even while looking at objects which resemble him”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. tiruvudai mannaraik kāṇil tirumālaik kaṇḍēnē ennum uruvudai vaṇṇangaḷ kāṇil ulagaḷandān enṟu tuḷḷum karuvudait tēvilgaḷ ellām kadal vaṇṇan kōyilē ennum veruvilum vīḻvilum ōvāk kaṇṇan kaḻalgaḷ virumbumē*

- *tiruvudai mannaraik kāṇil* – When she sees kings with faultless wealth, she would say “I have seen a form of [śriya:pati](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) (consort of [śrīmahālakśmi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/))”. It is well known that [nātamunigaḷ](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nathamunigal/) saw a king placing his feet on his assistant’s head and climbing up the elephant, and said “This resembles [sarvēśvaran](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) placing his divine feet on the heads of brahmā et al and climbing up on periya tiruvadi \[garuda\]” and fainted. Subsequently, in gangaikoṇḍa cōḻapuram, when the king arrives with his entourage, [periya mudaliyār (nātamunigaḷ)](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nathamunigal/) was vorśipping mannanār ([emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)) at the \[[kāttu mannār kōyil](http://kattumannarkoyil.koyil.org/)\] temple. His daughter comes and tells him that two archers, a lady and a monkey came to our home. Hearing this nātamunigaḷ thinks that “perumāḷ (śrī rāma), iḷaiya perumāḷ (lakśmaṇa), pirātti (sītā) and aindravyākaraṇa paṇḍita (hanumān) must have come”, and starts running towards them. He tried to locate them by going in the direction they went and at the eastern entrance \[of the town\], he asks those who were there about the whereabouts of the four persons. When those on-lookers mention that they have not seen any one like that, out of great sorrow, he leaves his body at once and ascends to paramapadam \[śrīvaikuṇṭam\].
- *uru udai vaṇṇangaḷ kāṇil* – When seeing well drawn paintings of dark-coloured flowers such as neelam, kuvaḷai, kāyām etc, considering similarity in the complexion and the aspect of being perceived by worldly eyes, she thinks about them as [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who placed his divine feet on the head of everyone without checking their qualities, and jumps around with joy, like a calf who is near its mother-cow.
- *karu udai* … – Wherever she sees the presence of a stone \[statue/deity\], she considers those places as śrīrangam, where periya perumāḷ is reclining. Since the in-dwelling super-soul for all these deities (statues and other dēvatās too) is [sarvēśvaran](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/), [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) identifies them as “*karu*” (womb) (karu indicates garbha (womb) as well as garbhādāra (the progenitor) who is [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) himself). tiruvāimoḻi 5.10.8 “*tisaimugan karuvuḷ vīṟṟirundu padaittitta karumangaḷum*” (the acts done by [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) by being the in-dwelling soul of brahmā). tēvil – dēvālyam – temple.
- *veruvilum* … –  She constantly desires for kriṣṇa’s divine feet whether she is fearful seeing her relatives or she is ignorant while being unconscious. Her state of mind remains the same always. The change is in whether she is being conscious or unconscious. With this, it is established that, for [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/), bhagavat prāvaṇyam (attachment to [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)) is that which sustains him.

## 4.4.9. Virumbip pagavarai

*virumbip pagavaraik kāṇil viyal idam uṇḍānē ennum karum perum mēgangaḷ kāṇil kaṇṇanenṟēṟap paṟakkum perumbula ānirai kāṇil pirān uḷan enṟu pin sellum arum peṟal peṇṇinai māyōn alaṟṟi ayarppikkinṟānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

pagavarai – mōkśāśramis (sanyāsis) who are manifestations of bhagavān (who are complete with qualities such as knowledge etc and who can attract devotees and protect them); kāṇil – if she sees; virumbi – with great attachment; viyal idam – the vast universe; uṇḍānē – the sarvarakśaka (protector of all), who kept everything in his stomach and protected (this is confirmed); ennum – says; karu – dark; peru – huge; mēgangaḷ – clouds; kāṇil – if she sees; kaṇṇan – kriṣṇa (who manifests his beautiful form and captivates everyone without discriminating between the wise and unwise); enṟu – thinking so; ēṟa – to go up; paṟakkum – will try to fly/jump; peru – very abundant; pulam – attractive; ānirai – herd of cows; kāṇil – if she sees; pirān – great benefactor (who lets them gaze the grass to their fulfillment); uḷan – is accompanying; enṟu – thinking so; pin – behind them; sellum – will follow; peṟal arum – gem of a, very rare to beget; peṇṇinai – this daughter; māyōn – amazing lord (who has such activities manifesting his benevolence); alaṟṟi – making her muttering; ayarppikkinṟān – (further) bewilders her

**Перевод:**

**If my daughter parānkuśa nāyaki sees mōkśāśramis (sanyāsis) who are manifestations of bhagavān, with great attachment towards them, she says “they are the sarvarakśaka (protector of all), who kept the vast universe in his stomach and protected (this is confirmed)”; if she sees dark clouds thinking that they are kriṣṇa, she tries to go up by jumping; if she sees abundant very attractive herd of cows, she will follow behind them thinking that kriṣṇa, the great benefactor is accompanying them; the amazing lord is making my daughter, who is gem of a person and very rare to beget, mutter and further bewilders her.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In ninth pāsuram – parānkuśa nāyaki‘s mother says “emperumān is endlessly torturing my daughter who is a gem of a girl”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, the mother says “emperumān made her daughter meditate upon the favours done by him to his devotees and as a result made her go bewildered constantly muttering \[about him\] while looking at entities which are similar/related to him.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Ninth pāsuram. The mother says “emperumān made my gem of a daughter, to constantly mutter about him and become bewildered”. virumbip pagavaraik kāṇil viyal idam uṇḍānē ennum karum perum mēgangaḷ kāṇil kaṇṇanenṟēṟap paṟakkum perumbula ānirai kāṇil pirān uḷan enṟu pin sellum arum peṟal peṇṇinai māyōn alaṟṟi ayarppikkinṟānē*

- *virumbip pagavaraik kāṇil* – If my daughter sees sanyāsis (ascetics) who are complete in jñānam etc and are detached from worldly matters, she would say that they are sarvēśvaran himself who keeps the universe in his stomach during total deluge, protects those who are to be protected and thus manifesting the quality of nairapēkśyam (neutral towards everyone).
- *viyal idam …* – vast earth. Like she confused ninṟa kunṟam (standing mountain) to be nedumāl (bhagavān), here too she confused śēśa bhūta (servitors) to be śēśi (lord) himself.
- *karum peru mēgam …* – On seeing dark huge invigorating clouds, she will think them to be kriṣṇa who has a similar form, will jump up/down and dance. On seeing the clouds, naturally the wings will lift up \[and the birds will fly\]. In a village named rājēndra cōḻa, there was a śrīvaiṣṇava named “tiruvāyk kulattu āḻvān”; once on a rainy day, he went to check the crop in the fields and fell unconscious on seeing the clouds; the farmer who was there at that time, brought him home and told those in his home “Would anyone send him out during rainy season, knowing his \[devotional\] nature?”.
- *perum pulam …* – Seeing the huge attractive herd of cows, she thinks that kriṣṇa will be coming to help me and thus would go to the last batch of the cows and will look for his presence there. Alternative explanation – she would go behind the herd of cows to see if he is amidst the cows.
- *arum peṟal peṇṇinai* – My penances/sacrifices are greater than those of daśarata cakravarti acquiring śrī rāma as his son as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 66.3 “*mahatā tapasā rāma*” (śrī rāma! you were born to daśarata cakravarti due to the great penances and sacrifices he performed), From the beginning she had undertaken lot of penances to beget [parānkuśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/). It is also explained as – she showed great attachment towards the divinity of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) and as a result she got parānkuśa nāyaki as her daughter.
- *māyōn* – He is capable of making one give up one’s parents as said in śrī viṣṇu purāṇam 5.6.27 “*kurava: kim kariśyati*” (what will our tribal parents do to us?).
- *alaṟṟi ayarppikkinṟān* – He made her constantly mutter about himself. Further, he bewildered her.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.4.10. Ayarkkum

*ayarkkum suṟṟum paṟṟi nōkkum agalavē nīḷ nōkkuk koḷḷum viryarkkum maḻaikkaṇ tuḷumba vevvuyir koḷḷum mey sōrum peyarttum kaṇṇā enṟu pēsum perumānē vā enṟu kūvum mayal perum kādal en pēdaikkum en seygēn valvinaiyēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ayarkkum – (unable to see objects which resemble or relate to him, she) faints; suṟṟum – in all directions; paṟṟi nōkkum – repeatedly sees; agala – stretching (the eyes); nīḷ nōkkuk koḷḷum – sees for long; viyarkkum – (unable to locate him even there, out of anger in love) sweats a lot; maḻai pōlē – like rain; kaṇ – upto the eyes; tuḷumba – filled with; vem – revealing the inner heat; uyir koḷḷum – breathes heavily; mey – (unable to bear the heat) the body, unable to sustain; sōrum – becomes very tired; peyarttum – further; kaṇṇā – Oh kriṣṇa (who is easily approachable by ladies at all times); enṟu – as; pēsum – calls out; perumānē – Oh my lord (who favours me more than I can imagine); vā – shall you come?; enṟu – as; kūvum – calls out; mayal – (in this manner) causing madness; peru kādal – having great love; en pēdaikku – for my disobedient daughter; val vinaiyēn – most sinful me (who sees her in such suffering); en seygēn – what shall I do? Implies – Shall I bring the lord who refuses to come? or shall I tolerate this suffering of my daughter?

**Перевод:**

**\[My daughter\] faints; \[gaining consciousness\] repeatedly sees in all directions; stretching the eyes, she sees for a long time; she sweats a lot; her eyes become filled with tears like rain; revealing the inner heat, she breathes heavily; unable to sustain the body, she becomes tired; further, she calls out “kriṣṇa”; \[thinking he has arrived\] she calls out “Oh my lord, shall you come?”; what shall I do for my disobedient daughter who is having great love and has become mad? I am most sinful having to witness her such suffering. Implies – Shall I bring the lord who refuses to come? or shall I tolerate this suffering of my daughter?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In tenth pāsuram – parānkuśa nāyaki‘s mother speaking about the transformations in her daughter who is unable to meditate upon emperumān and suffering due to that, says “What shall I do?”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, the mother sees her daughter meditating upon his qualities such as saulabhyam (simplicity) etc, becoming filled with grief of being unable to see objects that resemble or related to him and says “What shall I do for her?”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. ayarkkum suṟṟum paṟṟi nōkkum agalavē nīḷ nōkkuk koḷḷum viryarkkum maḻaikkaṇ tuḷumba vevvuyir koḷḷum mey sōrum peyarttum kaṇṇā enṟu pēsum perumānē vā enṟu kūvum mayal perum kādal en pēdaikkum en seygēn valvinaiyēnē*

- *ayarkkum* – Being unstable, she will faint losing all consciousness.
- *suṟṟum paṟṟi nōkkum …* – After regaining consciousness, thinking that [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) will arrive seeing her distressed state, she looks around confidently in the near-by locations. As she does not find his presence, thinking that “By now, he would have started from his abode” and stretches her eyes to see up to paramapadam. As she does not find him there too, she becomes grieved and thinks “Why is he not coming yet?”,
- *viyarkkum* – Out of fatigue, she starts sweating.
- *maḻai* … – Whatever did not come out as sweat, will come out as tears. Whatever did not come out as tears, will come out as her heavy-breathing. Tears which flow as rain, will come out from the eyes, and revealing the fire of anger, she will breathe heavily.
- *mey sōrum* – As she loses all her inner strength, she becomes very tired. Would she be finished in this state? No, her attachment to [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) will keep her alive.
- *peyarttum kaṇṇā enṟu pēsum* – Again, she will call out “kriṣṇa!” and as a result of the bliss acquired by reciting that name, she will consider that he is present in front,
- *perumānē vā enṟu kūvum* – She will call out to him “come”, thinking “How can the owner lose his property? He must be hiding somewhere close by to accept me”.
- *mayal* … – For my daughter who is having great love towards him which bewilders her.
- *en seygēn* – Shall I stop her from fainting? Shall I make him come? Shall I tolerate this \[suffering of my daughter\]?
- *val vinaiyēnē* – I have committed great sins to see her in this state. Like [emperumānār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/emperumanar/) grieved after [kūrattāḻvān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/kUraththAzhwAn/) lost his eyes, the divine mother is grieving on seeing the state of her daughter.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.4.11. Valvinai tirkkum

*valvinai tīrkkum kaṇṇanai vaṇ kurugūrc catakōpan sol vinaiyāl sonna pādal āyirattuḷ ivai pattum nal vinai enṟu kaṟpārgaḷ nalanidai vaikuntam naṇṇit tol vinai tīra ellārum toḻudeḻa vīṟṟiruppārē*

**Пословный перевод:**

val – hurdles which prevent devotees to be with him (emperumān); vinai – all sins; tīrkkum – of the nature of driving out (as said in śrī bhagavat gītā 18.66 “sarva pāpēbhyō mōkśayiśyāmi”); kaṇṇanai – kriṣṇa; vaṇ – abundant with all wealth; kurugūr – leader of āḻvārtirunagari; śatakōpan – nammāḻvār; sol vinaiyāl – service in the form of words; sonna – mercifully spoke; pādal – verses in the form of songs; āyirattuḷ – among the thousand; ivai pattum – this decad; nal vinai – distinguished deeds; enṟu – considering them; kaṟpārgaḷ – those who learn; nalan – bliss of experiencing bhagavān; udai – having; vaikuntam – paramapadam (spiritual realm); naṇṇi – reach; tol – ancient; vinai – faults such as ignorance etc; tīra – not affected; ellārum – all the residents of paramapadam, i.e. nityasūris; toḻudu – humbly worship (to manifest their devotion towards devotees); eḻa – rising very briskly; vīṟṟu iruppār – will be seated in a distinguished manner (manifesting their śēśatva sāmrājyam (the kingdom of servitude towards bhagavān))

**Перевод:**

**nammāḻvār, the leader of āḻvārtirunagari which is abundant with all wealth, engaged in service in the form of words about kriṣṇa, who is of the nature of driving out all sins which put hurdles for the devotees to be with him, mercifully spoke this decad among the thousand verses in the form of songs; those who learn this decad considering them to be distinguished deeds, will reach paramapadam, which is having bliss of experiencing bhagavān. Such individuals will not be affected by faults such as ignorance etc; they will be vorśipped humbly by all the residents of paramapadam (nityasūris), rising very briskly, and will be seated in a distinguished manner.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the end, āḻvār says “Those who learn this decad will be relieved from the difficulties of samsāram (material realm) and will remain in tirunādu (paramapadam, spiritual realm) where there is no question of separation from bhagavān”, with great glories to be respected by all.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. valvinai tīrkkum kaṇṇanai vaṇ kurugūrc catakōpan sol vinaiyāl sonna pādal āyirattuḷ ivai pattum nal vinai enṟu kaṟpārgaḷ nalanidai vaikuntam naṇṇit tol vinai tīra ellārum toḻudeḻa vīṟṟiruppārē*

- *valvinai tīrkkum kaṇṇanai* – Even if the parents abandon children, those who are dear will not abandon them. kriṣṇa who is of that nature,  removes the hurdles for his devotees which cause separation from him.
- *vaṇ kurugūrc catakōpan* – Most magnanimous [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/). It is his magnanimity which is helping even us today, to enjoy bhagavān’s qualities.
- *sol vinaiyāl sonna pādal* – Service by speech. Three explanations – 1) out of overflowing devotion, āḻvār cannot just stop speaking about him, 2) āḻvār spoke being forced by bhagavān’s qualities, and 3) by the act of speaking.
- *āyirattuḷ ivai pattum* – Among the thousand pāsurams, this decad where āḻvār looked at objects resembling emperumān and became mad considering them to be him. Such madness, does not occur in everyone; that being the case,
- *nal vinai enṟu kaṟpārgaḷ* – Those who learn/practice this only for its purifying ability \[i.e., considering it only as the means and not knowing it to be the sweetest goal\]; also explained as – those who learn this considering it to be a distinguished decad.
- *nalanidai vaikuntam naṇṇi* – Reaching the paramapadam where there is no question of separation from bhagavān.
- *tol vinai tīra* – being relieved from sins that follow since time immemorial.
- *ellārum toḻudu eḻa* – to be vorśipped by nityasūris who are *aspruśta samsāra ganda* (those who are never touched by samsāram (bondage)). They will be served and revered by even those *paṇiyā amarar* (those who do not bow infront of anyone other than bhagavān and bhāgavatas), and be honoured as said in tiruvāimoḻi 10.9.10 “*padiyinil pānginil pādangaḷ kaḻuvinar*” (in their residences, with all the upacārams (reverences), they washed the feet of the muktātmā who is arriving newly). Like it is said in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.1.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/03/thiruvaimozhi-1-1-1-uyarvara-uyarnalam/) “*toḻudeḻen mananē*” (Oh my mind! worship him and rise), As āḻvār who was as said in taittirīya upaniśat “*asannēva*” (When a person does not know about God, he is as good as matter), became uplifted by vorśipping him, nityasūris uplift themselves by vorśipping those who sing [nammāḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s tiruvāimoḻi.
- *vīṟṟiruppārē* – As bhagavān has the throne of supremacy, these devotees have the throne of servitude. vēdam says “*sasvarāt bhavati*” (that muktātmā becomes independent). *vīṟṟu* – distinguishing factor.

## 4.5 Virrirundu

## 4.5.1. Virrirundu

*vīṟṟirundu ēḻulagum tanik kōl sella vīvil sīr āṟṟal mikkāḷum ammānai vemmā piḷandān tannaip pōṟṟi enṟē kaigaḷārat toḻudu sol mālaigaḷ ēṟṟa nōṟṟēṟku ini enna kuṟai eḻumaiyumē?*

**Пословный перевод:**

vīṟṟu – being distinct from every other entity (in being the substratum of all, controller of all, lord of all and pervading everywhere); irundu – seated (in the divine throne in the divine realm); ēḻulagum – seven types of worlds (representing seven types of entities; four types of acētana (matter) – vyakta (manifested), avyakta (unmanifested), kāla (time) and śudda satva (divine matter) and three types of cētana (soul) – badda (bound souls in material realm), mukta (liberated souls in spiritual realm) and nitya (ever-free souls in spiritual realm)); tani – matchless (in the form of his divine will); kōl – sceptre; sella – to conduct; vīvil – endless; sīr – being with groups of auspicious qualities (such as jñāna, śakti etc); āṟṟal mikku – being with (natural) infinite śānti (peace); āḷum – conducting with great natural glories; ammānai – lord of all; vem – naturally very cruel (which are hurdles for the protected ones as said in “mahāraudra:‘ (very fierce)); mā – horse (named kēśi, which is possessed by a demon); piḷandān tannai – sarvēśvara who tore its mouth (as said in “nipapātadvidābhūta:“); pōṟṟi enṟē – performing mangaḷāśāsanam saying “pōṟṟi, pōṟṟi” \[long live\]; kaigaḷ – hands (which were as said in tiruvāimoḻi 4.4.1 “viṇṇait toḻudu” (vorśipping the sky)); Ara – to the full satisfaction; toḻudu – performing anjali (joined palms); sol – in the form of a collection strung with words; mālaigaḷ – garlands \[poems\]; ēṟṟa – to submit (so he can wear them on his head); nōṟṟēṟku – for me who has the puṇya (virtue) of his (nirhētuka (unconditional)) krupā (mercy) (as said in tiruvāimoḻi 10.6.1 “vidi vāykkinṟu” (his mercy occurring)); ini – going forward; eḻumaiyum – (as said in “saptasaptacasaptaca” (twenty one births)) even if I am to be born many more times; enna kuṟai – what worries do I have? \[implies – no worries\]

**Перевод:**

**sarvēśvaran, the lord of all, being distinct from every other entity, seated to conduct seven types of worlds with his matchless sceptre, being with groups of auspicious qualities, being with infinite peace, is conducting \[all these\] with great natural glories; such emperumān tore the mouth of kēśi, the very cruel horse; for me who has the virtue of his mercy to perform mangaḷāśāsanam to him saying “pōṟṟi, pōṟṟi“, to perform anjali to my full satisfaction and to submit collection of words as garlands, going forward, even if I am to be born many more times, what worries do I have? \[implies – no worries\]**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In first pāsuram – āḻvār says “I have no worries ever, after singing praises of kriṣṇa who being the sarvēśvara, divinely and mercifully incarnated as a human being and mercifully protected his devotees”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*In first pāsuram, āḻvār says “I who got to sing the praises and mangaḷāśāsanam \[well-wishes\] for sarvēśvara who is the controller of all the worlds, have no worries ever”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. vīṟṟirundu ēḻulagum tanik kōl sella vīvil sīr āṟṟal mikkāḷum ammānai vemmā piḷandān tannaip pōṟṟi enṟē kaigaḷārat toḻudu sol mālaigaḷ ēṟṟa nōṟṟēṟku ini enna kuṟai eḻumaiyumē?*

- *vīṟṟirundu* – vīṟu – distinction/differentiation. Being present, manifesting all his distinctions. Being present, manifesting his difference from all other entities since he is the lord for all of them and they are all his dependents; each entity is different from others \[but this distinction of his being the lord and others being dependents is special\]. Though all [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)s are equal with him when seen as “a product of jñānam”, qualities such as vibhutva (omnipresence), śēśitva (lordship) and niyantrutva (control over all) are unique to [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/). bhagavān having everyone other than himself as his servitors, himself pervading everywhere as jāti (the particular species) pervades throughout all vyaktis (entity of that species) and not like the pervading of āKāśa (ether) \[though it pervades everywhere, it does not control the objects it pervades\], pervades to control \[all entities\]. Here it reveals [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s blissful seated posture due to being the owner of all entities. *vīṟṟirundu* implies his majestic seated posture on the divine throne which rules over the ajñāna (ignorance) etc which frightens all the residents of this material realm.
- *ēḻulagum tanik kōl sella* – Instead of going around the worlds to rule over them, he rules them all with his sceptre from right where he is seated. When “*ēḻulagu*” indicates his spiritual and material realms, “*vīvil sīr*” (endless) is an adjective for his auspicious qualities; if “*ēḻulagu*” is taken as indicating the leelā vibhūti (material realm) only, “*vīvil sīr*” will imply nitya vibhūti (spiritual realm). When “*ēḻulagu*” indicates ubhaya vibhūti (both spiritual and material realms), it includes the three types of [cētana](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)s (souls) and four types of prakruti ([acētana](http://ponnadi.blogspot.in/2013/03/thathva-thrayam-achith-what-is-matter.html) – matter). Four types of prakruti are – kārya prakruti (cause) and kāraṇa prakruti (effect) in both paramapadam (spiritual realm) and samsāram (material realm). When “*ēḻulagu*” only indicates leelā vibhūti, from bhūmi down to pātāḷa (lowest region) is considered as one layer, and including the 6 layers above bhūmi, totally seven layers of worlds in this (our) side (samsāram) is explained.
- *vīvil sīr* – This indicates both the eternal qualities and eternal vibhūti (paramapadam).

Would he remain unattainable due to the pride of ruling over both realms?

- *āṟṟal mikkāḷum* – He rules with humility; as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam bāla kāṇḍam 1.97 “*rāmō rājyam upāsitvā*” (śrī rāma rules the kingdom …); since śrī rāma ruled the kingdom with humility, the word “*upāsitvā*” is used. When some one earns wealth in illegal means, he would conduct himself in a careless manner; since this wealth is owned by him, its apt for him to rule over it carefully. Alternatively – āṟṟal indicates strength/ability, and some explain this as “emperumān having the ability to support/rule over the wealth”.
- *ammānai* – sarvēśvaran who appears with the wealth acquired by his control \[over everything\].
- *vem mā piḷandān tannai* – bhattar explains it as “sarvēśvara who looks opulent due to having control over everything”. ammangi ammāḷ explains it as “When asked ‘who has the ability to rule this?’, at once, we will hear ‘it is [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) only'”. Since he is the owner of everything, instead of being seated in the throne and ruling them over by saying “*daha paca*” (burn them, cook them), he takes birth as one among them, tolerates all the insults thrown at him, protects them by taking out the weeds. In the incidents such as “syamantaka maṇi getting stolen” etc., others insulting him are well-known; you yourself declared in mahābhāratam “*dāsyamaiśvaryavādēna jñātīnāncakarōmyaham*” (I am serving them (pāṇḍavas) in the name of protecting them) and in the same ślōkam “*artabhōktāca bhōgānām vākduruktānicakśamē*” (For good enjoyments, I shared with them and I tolerated their insulting words).
- *vem mā piḷandān tannai* – Though kēśi \[already\] died, out of anger āḻvār says “*vemmā*” (cruel horse). śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 5.16.7 “*vyāditāsyō mahāraudras sōsura:kriṣṇabhāhunā \| nipapātadvidābhūtō vaidyutētātruma: \|\|”* (With widely opened mouth and very cruel looking asura named kēśi, tore by kriṣṇa’s hands like a tree hit by lightning, fell down); when kēśi came targeting kriṣṇa with open mouth, as small children would have tendency to pick in any hole, due to childish nature, kriṣṇa placed his hand in it’s mouth. Due to the unseen animal, the child’s hand expanded in joy and that broke the horse into two and knocked it down.
- *pōṟṟi* – āḻvār’s care matches his svarūpam (true nature). Even after kēśi’s death, āḻvār thinks that it is happening right now and feels frightened.
- *enṟē* – When some one says “*pallāṇḍu*“, naturally it will be followed by “*pallāṇḍu pallāṇḍu*“. As said in “*nama ityēva vādina:*” (they will always be saying “*nama:*“).
- *kaigaḷārat toḻudu* – The hands which vorśipped the empty sky as in [tiruvāimoḻi 4.4.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/02/thiruvaimozhi-4-4-1-mannai-irundhu/) “*vaikuntam enṟu kai kāttum*” (hand will point to śrīvaikuṇṭam), are now vorśipping to the full satisfaction, after having been relieved from the sufferings.
- *sol mālaigaḷ* – The \[word\] garlands which will never wither. Like the ever-fresh garland strung by anusūyā \[the chaste wife of atri riśi\].
- *ēṟṟa* – The garlands which are to be worn on his divine head. As said in śrī sātvatam “*kriṣṇāti sirasāsvayam*” (kriṣṇa himself accepts them on his head).
- *nōṟṟēṟku* – His efforts which are highlighted here are nothing but his craving / suffering in “*maṇṇai irundu tuḻāvi*” or it can be said as [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s krupā; that which exists in the previous step is called the means \[for accomplishing something\].
- *in enna kuṟai* – Even there \[in paramapadam\], one’s nature is to engage in small kainkaryams \[services\]; for me who has attained such kainkaryam right here, is there any worry?

How long will this remain?

- *eḻumaiyumē* – Whatever is eternal, they are generally explained in counts of sevens. bōdāyana darmam *“daśapūrvān daśāparātmānam ca”* (10 generations  before, self and 10 generations after) \[will be purified\]. mahābhāratam – bhīśma saying to darmaputra (yudiśtra) – “*ēkāhamapi kauntēya bhūmistam udagam kuru \| kulam tārayatē tāta! sapta saptaca sapta ca*” (Oh yudiśtra, my dear child! at least one day offer water to earth; that will help uplift your 21 generations of family members). Do I have the worry of “not reaching paramapadam”, when I have enjoyed the same experience right here? Even after going there, “doesn’t one engage in singing pallāṇḍu for him?”, as said in [tiruppallāṇḍu 12](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/11/thiruppallandu-12-pallandu-enru/) “*sūḻndirundu ēttuvar pallāṇḍē*“.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

adiyen saraty ramanuja dasan

## 4.5.2. Maiya kannal

*maiya kaṇṇāḷ malar mēl uṟaivāḷ uṟai mārbinan seyya kōlat tadam kaṇṇan viṇṇōr perumān tannai moyya sollāl isai mālaigaḷ ētti uḷḷap peṟṟēn veyya nōygaḷ muḻudum viyan jñālattu vīyavē*

**Пословный перевод:**

maiya – (as she is always residing in his chest \[and looking at him\] his black complexion got transferred to her eyes and being naturally known as asitēkśaṇā (black-eyed), beyond all of these) as if applied with black pigment; kaṇṇāḷ – having eyes; malar mēl uṟaivāḷ – most enjoyable lakshmi having been born in and residing in the lotus flower, and having high heritage and a form which is embodiment of the fragrance of the flower; uṟai – most enjoyable abode where she eternally resides; mārbinan – having the chest; seyya – (by constantly enjoying the lotus coloured mahālakśmi through his eyes, acquiring more redness on top of the naturally) reddish; kōlam – having beauty; tadam – expansive (out of great excitement in love); kaṇṇan – having divine eyes; viṇṇōr – letting nityasūris (eternally free souls of paramapadam) experience (such mutual and enjoyable togetherness); perumān tannai – sarvēśvara, who is their lord; moyya – collected together (like when they recite sāma gānam \[that part of vēda which is sung as hymns\]); sollāl – made with words; isai – having tune; mālaigaḷ – with garlands; viyal – vast; jñālattu – while being in this world; veyya – (as said in “na tatra sancariśyanti“) that which causes grief; nōygaḷ muḻudum – all sorrows (such as avidyā (ignorance), karma (actions), vāsanā (impressions), ruci (taste), prakruti sambandam (bondage)); vīya – to be destroyed (so they don’t ever occur); ētti – praise; uḷḷa – experience in my heart (his happiness revealed in his face, the one who is known as stavapriya (one who likes to be praised)); peṟṟēn – got

**Перевод:**

**Most enjoyable lakshmi who is born in and residing in the lotus flower, and since having high heritage and a form which is embodiment of the fragrance of the flower, who is having eyes which look as if they are applied with black pigment; sarvēśvara is having the chest which is the most enjoyable abode where she eternally resides and having reddish, beautiful, expansive, divine eyes and who is the lord of nityasūris, is letting them experience \[such mutual and enjoyable togetherness of him and śrī mahālakśmi\]; I got to praise such emperumān to destroy all sorrows which cause grief, with garlands of words collected together, while being in this vast world, and experience in my heart, his happiness.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In second pāsuram, āḻvār mercifully explains emperumān‘s lakśmīnātatva (being the divine lord of śrī mahālakśmi) which is the cause for this great wealth.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “I sang the praises of emperumān who is having the relationship with śrī mahālakśmi which is the cause for this greatness, to remove all troubles which are related to this material realm”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Second pāsuram. āḻvār mercifully explains emperumān‘s śriya:patitva (being the lord of śrī mahālakśmi) which is the cause for this great wealth. By the grace of brahmā who conducts the world by the grace of emperumān as per emperumān’s desire, through nārada et al, śrīmat rāmāyaṇam came about; here, āḻvār mercifully highlights the greatness of his prabandam over such great śrī rāmāyaṇam. As said in tiruvāimoḻi 8.8.11 “tirumālāl aruḷappatta śatakōpan” (nammāḻvār, who was blessed by śrīman nārāyaṇa), these prabandams of āḻvār came about as a result the mercy of the divine couple. “sītāyāścaritam mahat” (the epic which narrates sītā’s greatness) is equally applicable for both (śrī rāmāyaṇam and tiruvāimoḻi); āḻvār too said in tiruviruttam 48 “tirumālavan kavi yādu kaṟṟēn” (In what way will I know śrīman nārāyaṇa’s glories?). vālmīki composed \[śrī rāmāyaṇam\] and made śrī rāma listen to it alone \[without the presence of sītā\]; āḻvār made him listen along with śrī mahālakśmi and performed mangaḷāśāsanam to the couple \[praising them\]; āḻvār glorified “maiya kaṇṇāḷ malar mēl uṟaivāḷ uṟai mārbinan” (one who who is having on his chest, the dark-eyed śrī mahālakśmi, seated on a lotus flower). maiya kaṇṇāḷ malar mēl uṟaivāḷ uṟai mārbinan seyya kōlat tadam kaṇṇan viṇṇōr perumān tannai moyya sollāl isai mālaigaḷ ētti uḷḷap peṟṟēn veyya nōygaḷ muḻudum viyan jñālattu vīyavē*

- *maiya kaṇṇāḷ* – She is said as śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 16.5 “*asitēkśaṇā”* (black-eyed). If [periya pirāttiyār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/) glances at [sarvēśvaran](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) with her divine eyes once, he will cool down as if drenched in heavy rain; she is said in tiruviruttam 52 as “*maḻaik kaṇ madandai*” (lady having cool rain like eyes). Those who are not seen by her become virūpakśa (having deformed-eyes like rudra). śrīrangarāja stavam “*nama: śrīranganāyakyai yat bhrū vibhrama bhētata: \| īsēsitavya vaiśamya nimnōnnatam idam jagat \|\|”* (I worship śrī ranganācciyār whose eyebrow movements (her desire and reaction revealed through that) determine the fate of [jīvātmās](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) (whether one is rich or poor, learned or illiterate, etc).); one being [aḻagiya maṇavāḷap perumāḷ (śrī ranganātan)](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) and another being bikśuka (rudra, who begs for alms) \[are based on her divine glance\].
- *malar mēl uṟaivāḷ* – One who is born in the fresh lotus flower, having the buds/fragrance of the flower as the raw material. Previously (maiya kaṇṇāḷ) explains her beautiful features; here her tenderness is explained.
- *uṟai mārbinan* – One who has the chest which is the permanent residence of [śrī mahālakśmi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/), for whom even residing on a flower is difficult to handle \[she is so tender\]. Just as śrī janaka rāja’s divine daughter (sītā) never once thought about \[going to\] mitilā after marrying perumāḷ \[śrī rāma\], she never thought about the lotus flower after realizing the nature of his chest; as said in as said in cāndōjña upaniśat 8.12.3 “*nōpajanam smaran idam śarīram*” (ātmā will not contemplate about the material body after reaching the spiritual realm), she would not think about the lotus flower as muktātmās would not think about their \[previous\] lives in the material realm.
- *seyya kōlat tadam kaṇṇan* – When heavy rains fall on a particular region, the whole region will cool down; similarly, her eyes become drenched in his black-coloured form, and she becomes black-eyed; his form is known, as in tiruviruttam 94 “*maippadi mēni*” (black-coloured form). She is constantly seeing that form. \[In the same way\] [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is constantly glancing at her reddish form and that reddish complexion gets transferred to his eyes and he becomes puṇḍarikākśa (\[red\] lotus-eyed); she is known, as in tiruvāimoḻi 9.4.1 “*seyyāḷ tirumārbinil sēr tirumāl*” (śrīman nārāyaṇan who is united in his chest with the reddish [śrī mahālakśmi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/)). In this manner, in both their eyes, the form of each other can be seen; his form/complexion can be seen in her eyes and vice versa. This is their eye-body contact. One who is having reddish, attractive, wide divine eyes. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) recites his poems in praise of emperumān, to express his great joy, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) looks at [pirātti](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/) and pirātti tells “Why don’t you hear [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s pāsuram without getting diverted?” – they both heard āḻvār’s pāsurams in this manner.
- *viṇṇōr perumān tannai* – The abode which is nurtured under the protection of these eyes is explained here. Having those who enjoy these beautiful eyes and their \[divine couple’s\] togetherness instead of these being wasted like a moon shining in the forest; as said in tiruvāimoḻi 2.6.3 “*tāmaraik kaṇṇanai viṇṇōr paravum talai maganai*” (Lotus-eyed lord, the leader who is vorśipped by nityasūris). [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), [periya pirāttiyār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/) and the assembly of nityasūris heard [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s pāsurams together.
- *moyya sollāl* – Being amazed by the distinct nature of [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/), vēdam set out to praise but returned unable to do so saying as in taittirīya upaniśat “*yatō vācō nivartantē”* (mind/speech returned unable to comprehend [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s quality of bliss); unlike such vēdam, I got to sing emperumān’s glories. moy indicates collection/abundance and greatness; the poem which is with tightly connected words instead of loosely connected words and the poem which is strong enough to consume \[glorify\] [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/).
- *isai mālaigaḷ* – Like garlands with abundant fragrance, having tune/music which will mesmerize those who listen to the pāsurams.
- *ētti uḷḷap peṟṟēn –* The rule of “*mana:pūrva: vāguttara:*” (first conceptualize in the mind and then speak through the mouth) does not apply in [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s case. He does not need to think for the words of praise; since [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s thoughts control āḻvār, the words will naturally fit in well; āḻvār himself said in tiruvāimoḻi 7.9.2 “*en mun sollum*” (bhagavān who remains inside me and teaches me the words first, as an ācārya would do \[which I will repeat\]). Since these pāsurams are explained in tiruvāimoḻi 7.9.3 “*nā mudal vandu pugundu nal in kavi tū mudal pattarkkut tān tannaic conna*” (Entering my tongue, he sings beautiful pāsurams about himself for the enjoyment of mumukśus (those who are focussed on liberation)), the words will naturally form nice pāsurams. As happened in [tiruvāimoḻi 3.8](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/10/thiruvaimozhi-3-8-mudiyane/) “*mudiyānē*” decad where the different faculties of [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) craved for [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) individually, here āḻvār enjoys emperumān individually. \[Explaining [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s state through this pāsuram\] periya tirumoḻi 8.10.9 “*nāttināy ennai unakku mun toṇḍāga*” (you placed me in front you as your servitor), you engaged me who had no experience / interest in servitude and said  “He is mine”; with your acknovledgement, I drove away may accumulated sins, along with their traces. “*pāttināl …*” – through those pāsurams, you revealed your presence in my heart as sarvajña (omniscient), sarvaśakta (omnipotent). “*kaṇṇapurattuṟai ammānē*” – the divya dēśam which made me sing is tirukkaṇṇapuram. This is “*mukkōttai*” of [tirumangai āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/thirumangai-azhwar/) \[mukkōttai is a temple of a dēvatāntaram, where anyone who goes and prays sincerely will be blessed with great knowledge and ability such as singing etc. Similar to that, tirumāliruncōlai is said to be the mukkōttai of [nammāḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)\]. In this way, as his mouth sings the glories, just like us, āḻvār too meditated upon those pāsurams.
- *veyya nōygaḷ muḻudum* – “*avaśyam anubhōktavyam*” (one must experience the effects of one’s karma), even those karmas are destroyed.
- *viyan jñālattu vīyavē* – The clarity acquired through the bhagavat anubhavam (experience of [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)) made āḻvār say that even while being in this material realm, all my sins are eradicated. Another explanation – unlike the shadow of palm tree which is only useful for itself, all the karmas of everyone in this material realm where I live are destroyed. Yet another explanation – since āḻvār says “*viyal jñālam*” (vast world) as if it is a different place, some say that “āḻvār mercifully recites ‘*vīṟṟindu ēḻulagu*‘ as if he is speaking from paramapadam (spiritual realm)”. Due to his mood, it appears that he is one among those residents of paramapadam as his divine heart is always attached there. *viyal jñālam* means wonderful world and vast world.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.5.3. Vivil inbam

*vīvil inbam miga ellai nigaḻnda nam accudan vīvil sīran malark kaṇṇan viṇṇōr perumān tannai vivil kālam isai mālaigaḷ ētti mēvap peṟṟēn vīvil inbam miga ellai nigaḻndanan mēviyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vīvu il inbam – continuous bliss; miga ellai nigaḻnda – (as said in ānandavalli, being beyond comprehension of mind and speech) being in the ultimate state; nam accudan – one who is of apracyuta svabhāva (nature of never deviating) who gives enjoyment to persons like me; vīvu il – endless; sīran – having distinguished qualities such as yuvatva (youth) etc and wealth; malark kaṇṇan – being lotus-eyed (which reveals this greatness); viṇṇōr – vorśipped by the residents of paramapadam; perumān tannai – the leader; vīvu il – without any break; kālam – time; isai – in the form of songs; mālaigaḷ – collection \[of words\]; ētti – praised; mēvap peṟṟēn – attained; mēvi – having attained (the one who is filled with bliss as said in taittirīya upaniśat “labdvānandī bhavati“); vīvu il – endless; inbam – bliss; miga ellai – continuous \[joyful\] aspects; nigaḻndana – occurred

**Перевод:**

**emperumān is in the ultimate continuous blissful state who gives enjoyment to persons like me; is having endless distinguished qualities such as yuvatva (youth) etc and wealth; is lotus-eyed and is the leader of the residents of paramapadam;  I attained by praising him continuously with collection of words in the form of songs;  having attained \[him\], continuous \[joyful\] endless aspects occurred.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In third pāsuram, āḻvār says “The bliss I acquired by singing tiruvāimoḻi and performing services \[through speech\], is greater than the bliss of sarvēśvara which is explained in \[taittirīya upaniśat\] ānandavalli”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “I became completely blissful after vorśipping and attaining emperumān who has qualitiies such as ānanda etc, due to his supremacy and śriya:patitva (being the lord of śrī mahālakśmi)”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. vīvil inbam miga ellai nigaḻnda nam accudan vīvil sīran malark kaṇṇan viṇṇōr perumān tannai vivil kālam isai mālaigaḷ ētti mēvap peṟṟēn vīvil inbam miga ellai nigaḻndanan mēviyē*

- *vīvu il inbam* – *vīvu il* – Without any break; *inbam* – bliss.

How far will this extend?

- *miga ellai nigaḻnda* – At the ultimate state, where “there is nothing beyond this”.
- *nam* – well known in ānandavalli.
- *accudan* – Do we need to explain this using another pramāṇam (authentic text)? The divine name itself explains that there is no break \[acyuta here indicates imperishable, permanent bliss\].
- *vīvu il sīran* – Having the nitya vibhūti (spiritual realm) which is the cause for such bliss. Also explained as having eternal \[auspicious\] qualities. His qualities and wealth lead to bliss.
- *malark kaṇṇan* – His divine eyes will highlight that he has natural bliss.
- *viṇṇōr perumān tannai* – One who has a whole realm which is captivated by his beautiful eyes and says “*jitam*” (victory). tiruvāimoḻi 2.6.3 “*tāmaraik kaṇṇanai viṇṇōr paravum talai maganai*” (Lotus-eyed lord, the leader who is vorśipped by nityasūris).
- *vīvu il kālam* … – When one sets out to enjoy insignificant worldly aspects, since they have faults such as alpatva (being insignificant), astiratva (temporary) etc., the enjoyment will also not last long; here, with respect to [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/), since he is huge (without limit), the time of enjoyment is also forever. One would say as in [tiruvāimoḻi 3.3.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/08/thiruvaimozhi-3-3-1-ozhivil-kalam/) “*oḻivil kālamellām*” (forever without any break).
- *isai mālaigaḷ* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is serving [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) through words. Like it is said in “*karumugai mālai*” (flower garland), this garland is made of music.
- *ētti mēvap peṟṟēn* – Praised and attained him.

What is the result of attaining him?

- *vīvu il inbam miga ellai nigaḻndanan* – I attained eternal unsurpassed bliss.

You explained his bliss and your bliss to be at par; that being so, what is special about you?  [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says “there is a small difference”.

- *mēviyē* – His bliss is natural; but my bliss a result of vorśipping / attaining him; there is no cause for his bliss \[it’s natural\]; but mine has a cause \[he is the cause\]. I have the greatness as said in taittirīya upaniśat ānandavalli 7 “*ēśa hyēvānandayāti*” (bhagavān only gives pleasure to [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)); for him it is “*tān tōnṟi*” (causeless).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.5.4. Mevi ninru

*mēvi ninṟu toḻuvār vinai pōga mēvum pirān tūvi am puḷ udaiyān adal āḻi ammān tannai nāviyalāl isai mālaigaḷ ētti naṇṇap peṟṟēn āvi en āviyai yān aṟiyēn seyda āṟṟaiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

mēvi – (being ananya prayōjana) united; ninṟu – staying firmly; toḻuvār – those who enjoy; vinai – sins (which are hurdles for such enjoyment); pōga – to be destroyed (naturally); mēvum – (he) uniting (with them); pirān – great benefactor; tūvi – wings (to bring him to where they were as said in periya tirumoḻi 9.2.8 “anjiṟaip puḷḷum onṟu ēṟi vandār“); am – having beauty; puḷ – periya tiruvadi (garudāḻvār); udaiyān – having as vehicle; adal – for battle (as said in periya tiruvantādi 87 “kaikaḻalā nēmiyān nam mēl vinai kadivān” (one who has the sudarśana chakra in his hands to eliminate our sins), having it for destruction of the enemies of the devotees); āḻi – having tiruvāḻi (divine chakra); ammān tannai – sarvēśvara; nā – for the tongue; iyalāl – action; isai – in the form of a song; mālaigaḷ – with collections (garlands); ētti – glorifying; naṇṇa – activity; peṟṟēn – I got; āvi – my antaryāmi (indvelling super soul), who sustains me; en – my (body’s); āviyai – ātmā (soul – me); seyda āṟṟai – manner in which he made me praise him, made me enjoy that and desire for that; yān – I; aṟiyēn – (as “ēvam vidam” (in this manner)) cannot examine and know

**Перевод:**

**emperumān , a great benefactor unites with those who are united and are firmly staying and enjoying him, to have their sins destroyed; he is having beautiful winged periya tiruvadi as vehicle, having the tiruvāḻi to help him in battle; I got to engaging in glorifying through my mouth by offering the collections of the words which come out in the form of songs from my tongue; I cannot examine and know his being my antaryāmi and sustaining me and favouring me in making me praise him, making me enjoy that and desire for that.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In fourth pāsuram, āḻvār meditates upon emperumān being the leader of nityasūris (eternally free souls of paramapadam) yet accepted āḻvār who is very lowly and becomes emotional thinking about emperumān’s great favour.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “I praised emperumān who has the vehicle, weapons etc to protect/nurture those who are exclusively focussed on him, and attained him”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Fourth pāsuram. āḻvār says “emperrumān who is having ananya prayōjanars (who exist for exclusive enjoyment of emperumān) and nityasūris who never engage in any act of ulterior benefits, and who is beyond the reach of nityasūris, performed great favour towards me who is a nitya samsāri (fully materialistic). I cannot comprehend such great favour of his”. mēvi ninṟu toḻuvār vinai pōga mēvum pirān tūvi am puḷ udaiyān adal āḻi ammān tannai nāviyalāl isai mālaigaḷ ētti naṇṇap peṟṟēn āvi en āviyai yān aṟiyēn seyda āṟṟaiyē*

- *mēvi ninṟu toḻuvār* – After approaching him, instead of begging for ulterior results and leaving as said in “*dēhimē dadāmi tē*” (You fulfil my desires, I will give you this \[in return\]), these are the ones who worship [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), having him as the result/goal exclusively as said in mudal tiruvantādi 26 “*vaḻuvā vagai ninaindu vaigal toḻuvār*” (continuously thinking about him and vorśipping him every day). Those who worship him saying as in nācciyār tirumoḻi 9.7 “*inṟu vandu ittanaiyum seydidap peṟil …*” (If I am able to serve you in this manner, I will desire for more such service).
- *vinai pōga* – Would they still have sin \[after approaching emperumān\]? Yes, to be freed from sins that lead their heart to ulterior benefits.
- *mēvum pirān* – Just as the ātmā pursued [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) without any other expectation, emperumān too pursued the ātmā without any other expectation; in the mean time, since there is no place to rest for the sins, they will naturally vanish. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) himself said in periya tiruvantādi 30 “*valvinaiyār tām – madi adakki niṟpadanil – mīṇḍu adi eduppadanṟō aḻagu*” (Those sins – instead of staying here where there is no space – isn’t it better for them to leave this place?).
- *pirān* – One who is having such helping of others as his natural quality.

Previously, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) explained about those who were initially focussed on ulterior benefits and then became focussed on bhagavān himself; now, he explains about those who never focussed on anything other than emperumān; he is talking about emperumān having ananta \[ādiśēśan\] , vainatēya \[garudan\] et al \[as his servitors\].

- *tūvi* – Wings. This implies that emperumān has the means which will carry him, wherever he desires.
- *am puḷ* – Having the greatness of being beautiful as explained in [stōtra ratnam 41](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/01/sthothra-rathnam-41/) “*tvadanghrisammardagiṇāngaśōbhinā*” (shining due to being identified by the scars caused by pressing of your divine feet).
- *adal āḻi* – Since his devotees have always unnecessary fear (for [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s safety), he always carry his weapons. adal – midukku – pride.
- *ammān tannai* – As he is sarvādika (greater than all), he is expert in remaining seated on periya tiruvadi (garudāḻvār) always and in holding the tiruvāḻi āḻvān (sudarśana chakra) always.
- *nā iyalāl isai mālaigaḷ ētti* – Without the engagement of the mind, his actions of speech themselves became a garland of words. Whenever he twists his tongue, it will result in beautiful poem and tune.
- *ētti naṇṇap peṟṟēn* – He did not perform something and sing his praises; his praises were the activities.
- *āvi en āviyai seyda āṟṟai yān aṟiyēn* – āvi – nirūpādika sarvātmā (unconditionally present in every entity as antaryāmi). tiruvāimoḻi 8.1.5 “*ulagangetkellām ōruyir*” (he is the soul of entire world), taittirīya upaniśat “*ātmana ākāśa: sambhuta:*” (ether appears from paramātmā), “*sarvātmā*” (ātmā of all).
- *en āviyai* – Me who is very lowly.
- *seyda āṟṟai aṟiyēn* – He who is vibhu (omnipresent), made that me who is aṇu (miniscule) attain bliss which matches his, as said in taittirīya upaniśat ānandavalli 7 “*ēśa hyēvānandayāti*” (He only gives pleasure to [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)) and [tiruvāimoḻi 4.5.3](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/02/thiruvaimozhi-4-5-3-vivil-inbam/) “*vīvil inbam miga ellai nigaḻndanan*” (endless bliss of continuous \[joyful\] aspects occurred). How amazing that [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is sarvaśarīrī (soul of all), selects one of his forms/bodies and blesses great results to him.
- *yān aṟiyēn* – We can only get drowned in the experience and cannot speak about it. Even upakāra smruti (remembering the favour with gratitude) is his.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.
