## 4.5.5. Arra nalla

*āṟṟa nalla vagai kāttum ammānai amarar tam ēṟṟai ellāp poruḷum virittānai emmān tannai māṟṟa mālai punaindētti nāḷum magiḻveydinēn kāṟṟin munnam kadugi vinai nōygaḷ kariyavē*

**Пословный перевод:**

āṟṟa – as much as acceptable; nalla – (as tool for the enjoyment) distinct; vagai – attributes (such as jñāna (knowledge), bhakti (devotion, \[advanced stages of bhakti such as\] parabhakti, parajñāna, paramabhakti); kāttum – reveals (to the ātmās who enjoy); ammānai – being natural lord; amarar tam – (those who have such attributes are facilitated to enjoy like) nityasūris are facilitated to enjoy him; ēṟṟai – having pride; ellāp poruḷum – all such distinct principles; virittānai – elaborately explained; emmān tannai – my lord who unconditionally bestowed these; vinai – sins (which are hurdles for knowledge, devotion etc); nōygaḷ – great diseases (such as rāga (desire), dvēśa (hatred) etc); kāṟṟin – wind (which can move fast); munnam – faster than; kadugi – flee; kariya – (as said in “agnau prōtam“) to burn; māṟṟam mālai – garland of words; punaindu – strung; ētti – praised; nāḷum – always; magiḻvu eydinēn – attained happiness

**Перевод:**

**emperumān, being the natural lord, having the pride of revealing \[the ātmās’\] distinct attributes as much as acceptable \[by them\] and facilitating them just as nityasūris are facilitated to enjoy him, elaborately explained all such principles; I attained happiness by stringing garland of words and praising my \[such\] lord who unconditionally bestowed these to me, to make the sins, great diseases flee faster than wind and to have them burned.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In fifth pāsuram, āḻvar says “I became very pleased on enjoying emperumān who accepted me by manifesting his qualities and activities step by step, just as he mercifully explained all the principles to arjuna, while being the leader of nityasūris (eternally free souls of paramapadam) and sarvēśvara (being the lord of all)”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvar says “I got to praise sarvēśvara who bestowed me with jñāna (knowledge) etc, which are tools to enjoy him, and had all my sorrows naturally vanish at once”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Fifth pāsuram. āḻvar says “I acquired unsurpassed bliss by singing tiruvāimoḻi to have all my hurdles removed in enjoying emperumān who manifested his nature step by step just as he explained all the principles step by step to arjuna while being sarvādika (greater than all)”. āṟṟa nalla vagai kāttum ammānai amarar tam ēṟṟai ellāp poruḷum virittānai emmān tannai māṟṟa mālai punaindētti nāḷum magiḻveydinēn kāṟṟin munnam kadugi vinai nōygaḷ kariyavē*

- *āṟṟa* – Step by step. As much as one can accept. Instead of letting the ocean flow into a small pit, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) letting [āḻvar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) experience his auspicious qualities step by step. \[āḻvār says\] After saying in tiruviruttam 1 “*inninṟa nīrmai iniyām uṟāmai*“, had emperumān given the experience of “*vīṟṟirundu ēḻulagu*” \[current decad\], I would not have handled it and probably be dead by now \[out of overwhelming emotions\].
- *nalla vagai kāttum* – He would let me experience/enjoy his qualities and activities.
- *ammānai* – The owner naturally will make his possession know about the same.
- *amarar tam ēṟṟai* – emperumān let me, who cannot completely enjoy petty pleasures, enjoy himself, who is eternally enjoyed by nityasūris. Neither is he lacking in qualities, nor is he lacking those who enjoy him; he is sarvēśvara (lord of all) and has the nityasūris to enjoy him; even after this, he let me enjoy him.
- *ellāp poruḷum* – [āḻvar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) explains how [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) facilitated āḻvār to enjoy him. emperumān manifested his qualities and activities and helped āḻvār step by step, just as he did in the case of arjuna who first said I do not know what is virtue and what is vice as in [śrī bhagavat gītā 2.7](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/2-7/) “*śiśyas tēham śādimām tvām prapannam*” (I am becoming your disciple. Please instruct me that which will be good for (me). Please reform me who has surrendered unto you).
   - First, kriṣṇa made arjuna aware of the differences between [prakruti (matter)](http://ponnadi.blogspot.in/2013/03/thathva-thrayam-achith-what-is-matter.html) and [puruśa (soul)](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/).
   - Then, he instructed him karma yōga.
   - Then, he instructed him to give up the status of performer in such karma yōga and work without any attachment in the results.
   - Then, he instructed him about ātma jñānam (knowledge about soul/self).
   - Then, he instructed him knowledge about [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/).
   - Then, he instructed him about upāsana kramam (bhakti – devotion) of constantly engaging in bhagavān.
   - After explaining all these and having instilled full faith in arjuna’s heart, and when arjuna worried thinking “these are impossible to practice”, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) concluded saying “depend fully upon me and be free from worries”.
- *emmān tannai* – \[[āḻvar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says\] I don’t know if arjuna benefited from the discourse; but I got the benefit of those instructions. arjuna, after hearing the instructions, even after saying in śrī bhagavat gītā 18.73 “*stitōsmi*” (I am well situated \[in the principles\]), did he not say “*nūnam samśayōsti*” (I have some doubts again)? \[Though arjuna did not say this in gītā, in anugītā (mahābhāratam), kriṣṇa tells arjuna, “It appears that you still have some doubts” and repeats the gītā to him once more\]; since [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) who instructed \[gītā\] is common for all and the principles which he explained are also common for all, there is nothing wrong in saying “āḻvār benefited after knowing the principles”; it is said in nācciyār tirumoḻi 11.10 “*vittucittar kēttiruppar*” ([periyāḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/periyazhwar/) heard the principles of [śrī bhagavat gītā](http://githa.koyil.org/) and lived according to those principles). It appears that kriṣṇa stayed in āḻvār’s manōratam (heart) and instructed.
- *māṟṟa mālai punaindu ētti* – Stringing garland of words. Being captivated by [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), [āḻvar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) praised out of gratitude and those praises became tiruvāimoḻi.
- *nāḷum magiḻveydinēn* – Became eternally blissful.

If you attained such great result, what happened to your hurdles?

- *kāṟṟin munnam kadugi vinai nōygaḷ kariyavē* – The sins and the births which are results of such sins, ran away faster than wind and were burnt down. Like a new cloth is purified step by step, if we try to remove the hurdles, we have to do it step by step; but if [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) removes it, it does not take all that effort for him; as said in periya tiruvantādi 76 “*vinaip padalam viḷḷa viḻittu*” (By staring at the collection of sins, they will be removed). viṣṇu darmam chapter 78 “*mēru mantara …*” (Even if one’s sins are as high as mēru mountain, by taking shelter of kriṣṇa, those sins get destroyed). Just as the disease of a patient disappears on approaching a learned doctor, the sins of those who are surrendered to sarvēśvara, will be destroyed. periya tiruvantādi 54 “*vānō maṟikadalō …*” (I took shelter of the divine feet of kriṣṇa who killed vatsāsura; I have not seen my cruel sins anywhere near by; did they reach the sky, ocean, air, fire or forest? Alas!).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.5.6. Kariya meni

*kariya mēni misai veḷiya nīṟu siṟidē idum periya kōlat tadam kaṇṇan viṇṇōr perumān tannai uriya sollāl isai mālaigaḷ ētti uḷḷap peṟṟēṟku ariyaduṇḍō enakku inṟu tottum ini enṟumē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kariya – blackish; mēni misai – on top of the beautiful form; veḷiya nīṟu – black pigment; siṟidē – to the extent required; idum – wearing; periya kōlam – with unsurpassed beauty; tadam – large; kaṇṇan – having beautiful eyes; viṇṇōr perumān tannai – sarvēśvara who has the greatness of drowning the nityasūris; uriya – matching (such beauty); sollāl – made with words; isai mālaigaḷ – with garlands of songs; ētti – praise; uḷḷa – to enjoy; peṟṟēṟku enakku – for me who got; inṟu tottum – starting today (when the enjoyment commenced); ini – going forward; enṟum – forever in the future; ariyadu – difficult to attain; uṇḍō – is there anything?

**Перевод:**

**sarvēśvaran who has beautiful blackish form and on top of that having beautiful large eyes with unsurpassed beauty which are applied with as much black pigment as required, has the greatness of drowning the nityasūris \[with such beauty\]; for me who got to enjoy such emperumān by praising him with matching words of garlands of songs, is there anything difficult to attain starting today and going forward forever in the future?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In sixth pāsuram, emperumān asks “What do you need?” and āḻvār says “Is there something to be accomplished which I don’t have?”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “Is there anything difficult for me to accomplish after having enjoyed emperumān by praising him who has ultimate beauty to be enjoyed by those who have unfailing knowledge and devotion?”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Sixth pāsuram. Previously āḻvār said “I had the opportunity to serve the divine feet of sarvēśvara and was relieved from the hurdles”; when īśvara asked “But, is there anything I can do for you?”; āḻvār says “Is there anything which I have not got already which needs to be attained now?”. kariya mēni misai veḷiya nīṟu siṟidē idum periya kōlat tadam kaṇṇan viṇṇōr perumān tannai uriya sollāl isai mālaigaḷ ētti uḷḷap peṟṟēṟku ariyaduṇḍō enakku inṟu tottum ini enṟumē*

- *kariya mēni misai* – *mēni* indicates colour; on top of the black colour in the black pupils of the divine eyes. It is said in amalanādipirān 8 “*kariyavāgip pudai parandu*” (blackish expansive eyes).
- *veḷiya nīṟu* – anjana cūrṇam (black pigment). Decorating with pigment as much as required. It is said in siṟiya tirumadal “*ārār ayil vēṟkaṇ anjanattin nīṟaṇindu*” (decorating the beautiful spear like eyes with black pigment).
- *siṟidē idum* – It is not necessary to apply this to add further beauty. But since it is applied for auspiciousness, it is only applied a little bit.
- *periya kōlam* – There is abundance of natural beauty which doesn’t require any additional decoration.
- *tadam kaṇṇan* – The eyes are much larger than the availability of those who enjoy \[those eyes\].

Alternative explanation.

- *kariya* … *tadam kaṇṇan* – For the divine reddish eyes which are a contrast for the blackish body, on top of the natural beauty, black pigment is applied.

Another explanation

- *kariya* … *tadam kaṇṇan* – A tamiḻ scholar explained – kari indicates elephant, that is kuvalyāpīdam. kuvalayāpīdam angrily targetted (*veḷiya – sīṟa*) his divine form and in turn [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) breaks it into pieces (*nīṟu siṟidē idum*).

- *viṇṇōr perumān* – nityasūris are the ones who enjoy the beauty of his divine eyes.
- *perumān* – Even if the whole tripādvibhūti (paramapadam, spiritual realm) together sets out to enjoy [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), the aspect to be enjoyed remains greater than the aspect that was enjoyed already.
- *uriya sollāl* – One will think “The beauty of emperumān is great; nityasūris are the ones who enjoy; how can we glorify him with our poems?” and refrain from glorifying; still, \[[āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) sings\] using words that match emperumān.
- *isai mālaigaḷ* – They are pleasing to hear as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 31.1 “*samśravē maduram vākhyam*” (words that are sweet to hear).
- *ētti uḷḷap peṟṟēṟku* – For me who praised and enjoyed him.
- *ariyadu uṇḍō* – As said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 3.22](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/3-22/) “*nānavāptam avāptavyam*” (there is nothing which is not fulfilled or to be attained, presently). Is there anything which is not attained by me already, and is to be attained now?
- *enakku* – For me who became attracted to śēśatvam (servitude) in this samsāram where everyone thinks “*īśvarō’ham*” (I am the lord), who engaged in vācika kainkaryam (service through words) which is natural for the self, and who has the hurdles removed as said in the [tiruvāimoḻi 4.5.5](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/02/thiruvaimozhi-4-5-5-arra-nalla/) “*vinai nōygaḷ kariya*“.
- *inṟu tottum ini enṟumē* – Starting today when I commenced my servitude and forever going forward. As said in taittirīya upaniśat “*atasō’bhayangatō bhavati*” (Subsequently, he (jīvātmā) becomes fearless). [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying this without realizing what is coming in the next decad “*tīrppāraiyāmini*” \[In this next decad, āḻvār again grieves in separation\].

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.5.7. Enrum onragi

*enṟum onṟāgi ottārum mikkārgaḷum tan tanakku inṟi ninṟānai ellā ulagum udaiyān tannai kunṟam onṟal maḻai kātta pirānaic col mālaigaḷ nanṟu sūttum vidi eydinam enna kuṟai namakkē*

**Пословный перевод:**

enṟum – in all states (whether it is paratvam (in paramapadam) or in his avatārams (incarnations)); onṟu āgi – having a prakāra (form); ottārum – equal; mikkārgaḷum – greater; than tanakku – for his unsurpassedly enjoyable distinct aspects such as saulabhya (simplicity) etc; inṟi – without; ninṟānai – remained; ellā ulagum – all worlds; udaiyān tannai – having subservient to him; maḻai – the danger in the form of heavy rain (with which indra threatened emperumān’s dependents); kunṟam onṟāl – with a mountain (which he set his sight on); kātta – protected; pirānai – great benefactor; sol mālaigaḷ – garlands with abundance of words; nanṟu sūttum – to prepare so that he wears them with great liking; vidi – fortune (in the form of his mercy); eydinam – got; namakku – for us; enna kuṟai – is there any worry?

**Перевод:**

**emperumān remained in a form without an equal or greater person in all states for his unsurpassedly enjoyable distinct aspects such as saulabhya (simplicity) etc; \[during kriṣṇāvatāram\] while having all worlds subservient to him, when there was the danger in the form of heavy rain, he, the great benefactor protected \[his dependents\] with a mountain; is there any worry for us who got the fortune to prepare garlands with abundance of words so that he wears them with great liking?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In seventh pāsuram, āḻvār says “I got all these wealth due to his mercy”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “What worries are there for me who got to praise kriṣṇa whose enjoyment has none equal or greater?”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Seventh pāsuram. When asked “How did you attain this perfection of saying ‘there is nothing unattainable by me’?”, āḻvār replies “I got that by the mercy of bhagavān“. enṟum onṟāgi ottārum mikkārgaḷum than tanakku inṟi ninṟānai ellā ulagum udaiyān tannai kunṟam onṟal maḻai kātta pirānaic col mālaigaḷ nanṟu sūttum vidi eydinam enna kuṟai namakkē*

- *enṟum* – at all times.
- *onṟāgi ottārum mikkārgaḷum* – It is not that there is no match for his form of having all aspects of the world \[such as virāt rūpa (universal form)\], even for a single aspect of his, there is no equal or greater entity. As said in śvētāsvatara upaniśat “*na tatsamaśca abhyadikaśca drusyatē*” (No one equal to or higher than [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)  is seen); some one with a form/aspect which is equal to or greater than [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/).
- *than tanakku inṟi ninṟānai* – When [emperumānār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/emperumanar/) visited southern region, [āḷavandār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/alavandhar/)‘s son sottai nambi mercifully explained – “*than tanakku*” means “*tānāna tanakku*” ([bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s form/incarnation). When \[śāstram is\] saying “there is no equal/greater entity for emperumān, it is not talking about emperumān’s paratvam (supreme state); but in his incarnations where he assumes human forms as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 120.11 ‘*ātmānam mānuśam manyē*‘ (I am only a human being)”.
- *ellā ulagum udaiyān tannai* – kriṣṇa who is sarva lōkēśvara (lord of all worlds). It is said in mahābhāratam bhīśma parvam “*kriṣṇa Eva hi lōkānām*” (Creation and annihilation of the worlds are in kriṣṇa).

In this manner, being the prideful owner of everything, would he let his dependents suffer?

- *kunṟam* … – The saviour who protected the cattle and covherds when angry indra out of hunger \[since covherds stopped their offerings to indra\] showered heavy rains on them,  \[[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)\] lifted up the hill which he set his sight on and averted the disaster. tiruvāimoḻi 7.4.10 “*tīmaḻai*” (rain of fire).
- *sol mālaigaḷ* … – In paratvam (supremacy), the qualities simply exist; only in avatārams, those qualities shine; as emperumān is perfect, instead of withdrawing from my praises saying “it’s impossible to speak about him”, I became consumed by such qualities and spoke. I got the great fortune of offering these words to be worn by him. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) now indicates bhagavat krupā ([bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s mercy) by “*vidi*“. Since it fructified in him and bhagavān could not avoid \[showering his mercy\], he is using the term “*vidi*” (destiny). He already said in [tiruvāimoḻi 2.7.6](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/05/thiruvaimozhi-2-7-6-madhusudhanai-anri/) “*vidi sūḻndadāl*” (wrapped by mercy in the form of unavoidable destiny).
- *enna kuṟai namakkē* – For us who have become the target of his krupā (mercy) instead of his wrath as said in “*nakśamāmi*” (śrī varāha [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) – I will not forgive), is there any worry? If we have any worries, that means, we are limiting his mercy. \[śrī rāmāyaṇa ślōkam sundara kāṇḍam 38.34 is explained elaborately to highlight how emperumān is bound by his mercy\]
   - *sa:* – emperumān who is having protection of all, as his nature.
   - *tam* – kākāsura, who was situated in ultimate unfavourable attitude.
   - *nipatitam bhūmau* – he who would not have his feet touch the earth due to pride of being a dēva (celestial being) is now fallen on the ground; just as a child, caught doing mischief, will go and fall at the feet of its mother when its father chases to punish it, \[kākāsura\] fell on \[mother\] earth.
   - śaraṇya: – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is the refuge in any situation.
   - *śaraṇāgatam* – one who sought protection with no other refuge to go.
   - *vadārham api* – Even by \[the most merciful\] śrī rāma’s principle, he deserves to be killed \[for his mistake\].
   - *kākutsta:* – He protected due to his hereditary compassion. But, would his lineage not make him punish those who are worthy to be punished?
   - *krupayā* – just as we cannot successfully complete the actions which we take up due to our karma \[which stops them\], he too, since is bound by his krupā, would not complete what he desired \[i.e., he cannot punish even if desires to do so\]. kākāsura reached \[fell on\] the \[mother\] earth which is the origin of mercy, since that triggered [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s krupā; how will he punish?
   - \[parya pālaya: – \[emperumān\] protected\].
- *enna kuṟai namakkē* – \[Hence\] If I have worries, that implies that his mercy is limited.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.5.8. Namakkum

*namakkum pūvin misai nangaikkum inbanai jñālattār tamakkum vānattavarkkum perumānait taṇ tāmarai sumakkum pādap perumānaic col mālaigaḷ sollumāṟu amaikka vallēṟku iniyāvar nigar agal vānattē*

**Пословный перевод:**

namakkum – for us (who are lower than nitya samsāris (eternally bound souls), due to our involvement with ignorance etc since time immemorial); pūvin misai nangaikkum – for pirātti (śrī mahālakśmi) who is greater than nityasūris (eternally free souls) due to her enjoyable aspect of being born in a lotus flower and her completeness in all auspicious qualities; inbanai – one who gives bliss (due to his ultimately enjoyable nature); jñālattār tamakkum – the residents of material realm (who are not greatly knowledgeable); vānattavarkkum – residents of paramapadam (who are greatly knowledgeable), without any difference; perumānai – one who is having natural lordship for all; taṇ – having freshness; tāmarai – lotus flower; sumakkum – carrying; pādam – one who is having divine feet; perumānai – the supreme lord; sol mālaigaḷ – garlands of words; sollumāṟu – to praise; amaikka vallēṟku – to remain firm; agal – vast; vānattu – in tripād vibhūti (paramapadam, spiritual realm); yāvar – who (can enjoy without becoming emotional); ini – now; nigar – match?

**Перевод:**

**emperumān gives bliss for both us and śrī mahālakśmi, is having natural lordship for both the residents of material realm and spiritual realm and is the supreme lord carried by fresh lotus flower; who can match me in the spiritual realm to remain firm after praising him with garlands of words?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In eighth pāsuram, āḻvār thinks about emperumān‘s attachment towards him and says “There is no one comparable to me even in paramapadam, to praise such sarvēśvaran“.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “Is there any one equivalent to me in paramapadam to praise sarvēśvaran who is the lord of both spiritual and material realms?”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Eighth pāsuram. āḻvār thinks about emperumān‘s attachment towards him and says “there is no one comparable to me even in paramapadam, to praise emperumān matching his lordship over the two realms and his tenderness”. namakkum pūvin misai nangaikkum inbanai jñālattār tamakkum vānattavarkkum perumānait taṇ tāmarai sumakkum pādap perumānaic col mālaigaḷ sollumāṟu amaikka vallēṟku iniyāvar nigar agal vānattē*

- *namakkum* – For us who took shelter of his divine feet today. For us who are lower than nitya samsāris (eternally bound souls). [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) already said in [tiruvāimoḻi 3.3.4](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/08/thiruvaimozhi-3-3-4-isan-vanavarkku/) “*nīsanēn niṟai onṟum ilēn*” (I am very lowly and have no good qualities).
- *pūvin misai nangaikkum* – For pirātti who is greater than nityasūris and who is complete in qualities of her form and nature.
- *pūvin misai nangai* – She is tender and enjoyable like the fragrance in the flower. Just as we have no good qualities, she has no shortcomings.
- *inbanai* – While giving bliss, first he will associate with us and then only with her. śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 41.4 “*tvayi kincit samāpannē kim kāryam sītayā mama*” (even if you were insulted a little bit, what is the use of my getting back sītā?). When śrī rāma arrived, rāvaṇa appeared on the top of the tower. Looking at that \[sugrīva\] mahāraja thinks “How dare you lowly person stand atop in front of śrī rāma?”, jumps on him \[knocks his crown\] and returns back. Seeing that śrī rāma says “*ēvam sāhasa yuktāni kurvanti janēśvara:*” (Kings should not do such daring acts themselves) – when some one needs to be attacked, should the king himself go and do that while the servitors are waiting for the king’s orders \[śrī rāma considers himself to be a servitor of sugrīva\]? śrī rāmāyaṇam kiśkintā kāṇḍam 4.18 “*lōkanāta: purā bhūtvā sugrīva nātamiccati*” (śrī rāma who is the lord himself, desires sugrīva as his lord) – whether his desire is fulfilled or not, he desired for that. śrī rāmāyaṇam kiśkintā kāṇḍam 4.17 “*sugrīvam śaraṇam gata:*” (śrī rāma surrendered to sugrīva). \[Expanding further on the relationship between śrī rāma and sugrīva\] When śrī vibhīśaṇa āḻvān came to surrender to śrī rāma, sugrīva said “I won’t allow him to come to our side” and śrī rāma said “I won’t consider myself to exist, if I don’t accept him”. [nanjīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nanjiyar/) asked \[his ācārya, bhattar\] “Why do they have such differing view points?” and [bhattar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/parasara-bhattar/) mercifully said “Both are differing, since both want to protect the one who surrendered to each of them”. sugrīva tried to fulfil the aspect of “*sugrīvam śaraṇam gata:*” and śrī rāma tried to fulfil the aspect of “*rāghavam śaraṇam gata:*” (vibhīśaṇa surrendered to śrī rāma). That is why śrī rāma said “*ānaya*” (bring him over) to sugrīva \[himself, who opposed\] and accepted vibhīśaṇa. śrī rāma said “*tvayi kincit samāpannē”* – If he \[rāvaṇa\] causes even the slightest insult to your stature of being the king, of what use to me is the object (sītā) which you went searching for?

What is the cause for his such attachment towards us?

- *jñālattār* … – The reason for his equal attachment towards distinctly different entities \[those in material realm and those in spiritual realm\], though his relationship with everyone is common, is that [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is on the earth (bhūmip pirātti), which is his mattress; hence there is special attachment.  While his being the Lord is congruent with their \[nityasūris, in paramapadam\] being the servitors, just as parents would show more compassion towards their children who have shortcomings, emperumān also shows more attachment towards samsāris \[as their abilities, intelligence etc are less in comparison with nityasūris\]. As said in mahōpaniśat, “*sa ēkāki na ramēta*” ([śrīman nārāyaṇa](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), who was alone during deluge, was not joyful) emperumān was not happy even though śrīvaikuṇṭam was very much existing.
- *taṇ tāmarai sumakkum pādap perumānai* – The sarvasvāmi (lord of all) who is having divine feet which are held by cool lotus flower. It appears that the lotus flower lost the competition with the lotus feet in coolness, fragrance and freshness and in turn, are carrying the lotus feet. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) already said in [tiruvāimoḻi 3.1.2](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/07/thiruvaimozhi-3-1-2-katturaikkil/) “*tāmarai nin kaṇ pādam kai ovvā*” (lotus flower does not compare to your divine eyes, divine feet and divine hands).
- *sol mālaigaḷ* – Previous [ācāryas](http://acharyas.koyil.org/) explained this as āḻvār saying – When [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) said to me “Why don’t you praise me with a poem?” I would at once compile a poem, for such competent me \[This is called āsukavi – one who is able to instantaneously write a poem\]; But, [bhattar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/parasara-bhattar/) explained it as āḻvār saying – As said in tiruvāimoḻi 7.9.4 “*ennāgiyē tappudal inṟit tanaik kavi tān solli*” (Through me, you praised yourself with poems which have no defects), since it is [sarvēśvaran](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) who is singing \[through me\], there is no surprise in  instantaneously singing his praises; but when he acknowledges and mercifully glances at me and says “You sing a poem in praise of me”, I can stay firm without becoming overwhelmed and recite a poem in praise of him – for such me. For me who can recite poems which match his wealth and tenderness which are acquired as a result of his lordship over the spiritual and material realms.
- *ini yāvar nigar agal vānattē* – Are those who stay firm in paramapadam and sing as in taittirīya upaniśat “*aham annam aham annam aham annam*” (I am the food to be enjoyed by [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) \[repeated thrice\]), a match for me? Even if everyone from the vast spiritual realm were compared with me, are they a match for me? Since paramapadam (spiritual realm) is known as “*teḷi visumbu*” (the spiritual realm where every one is perfectly wise), it will naturally make them recite \[perfectly\]; but since this samsāram (material realm) is known as “*iruḷ tarumā jñālam*” (the world which gives ignorance), this will deviate everyone from such recitals \[as I stay in this material realm and recite firmly, I am greater than them\]. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) already said in tiruviruttam 79 “*sīdanaiyē toḻuvār viṇṇuḷārilum sīriyarē*” (those who worship cool natured [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) only \[in this realm\], are better than the residents of paramapadam).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.5.9. Vanattum

*vānattum vānattuḷ umbarum maṇṇuḷḷum maṇṇin kīḻt tānattum eṇ tisaiyum tavirādu ninṟān tannai kūnaṟsangat tadakkaiyavanaik kudamādiyai vānak kōnaik kavi solla vallēṟku ini māṟuṇḍē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vānattum – in svarga (heaven) which is indicated by the word “ākāśa” (sky); uḷ vānattu – residing inside the sky; umbarum – in the higher regions; maṇṇuḷḷum – in the earth; maṇṇin kīḻ tānattum – the lower regions below earth such as pātāḷa etc; eṇ tisaiyum – eight type of entities (which exist in these different regions, classified by categories such as dēva (celestial), manuśya (human), tiryak (animal), stāvara (plant) and varṇa such as brāhmaṇa, kśatriya, vaiśya and śūdra); tavirādu – without missing anything; ninṟān tannai – one who has the nature of pervading everything; kūn – bent; nal – attractive; sangam – having śrī pāncajanya (the divine conch); tada – large; kaiyavanai – one who is having divine hands; kudamādiyai – one who performs activities such as dancing with pots, which captivate the hearts of everyone; vānam kōnai – emperumān who has the greatness of being enjoyed by nityasūris (eternally free souls); kavi solla vallēṟku – for me who can sing his praises; ini – now; māṟu – \[matching\] opponent; uṇḍē – is there any?

**Перевод:**

**emperumān has the nature of pervading everything such as svarga (heaven) which is indicated by the word “ākāśa” (sky), those who are residing in the higher regions, the earth, the lower regions below earth such as pātāḷa etc and in the eight type of entities, without missing anything; is having large divine hands where he is having attractive bent śrī pāncajanyam (the divine conch); he performs activities such as dancing with pots, which captivate the hearts of everyone; now, is there any \[matching\] opponent for me who can sing the praises of such emperumān who has the greatness of being enjoyed by nityasūris (eternally free souls)?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In ninth pāsuram, āḻvār becomes blissful saying “I can praise him in all his states such as all-pervading antaryāmi, and avatārams (incarnations)”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “Is there anyone like me who can praise him in all his states such as all-pervading antaryāmi, and avatārams (incarnations)?”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Ninth pāsuram. āḻvār says “Is there anyone like me who can praise him in all his states such as all-pervading antaryāmi, and avatārams (incarnations)?”. nityasūris (eternally free souls) being engrossed in the unlimited pleasure in paramapadam, would not know anything else; since muktar (liberated souls) would not think about the material realm as said in cāndōjña upaniśat 8.12.3 “nōpajanam smaran idam śarīram” (ātmā will not contemplate about the material body after reaching the spiritual realm), they are comparable to nityar (nityasūris); sages like parāśara, pārāśarya (vyāsa) et al would each be engaged in different aspects; śrī vālmīki bhagavān would not think about anything other than śrī rāmāvatāram; śrī parāśara bhagavān and śrī vēda vyāsa bhagavān would not think about anything other than kriṣṇāvatāram; śrī śaunaka bhagavān would be greatly attached to arcāvatāram; unlike all of these personalities, I can sing about any aspect of emperumān – is there any one comparable to me? vānattum vānattuḷ umbarum maṇṇuḷḷum maṇṇin kīḻt tānattum eṇ tisaiyum tavirādu ninṟān tannai kūnaṟsangat tadakkaiyavanaik kudamādiyai vānak kōnaik kavi solla vallēṟku ini māṟuṇḍē*

- *vānattum* – In svarga.
- *vānattuḷ umbarum* – in those regions which are higher than such svarga, i.e., mahar lōkam etc.
- maṇṇuḷḷum – on the earth
- *maṇṇin kīḻt tānattum* – in the lower regions such as pātāḷam etc.
- *eṇ tisaiyum* – eight directions.
- *tavirādu ninṟān tannai* – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who fully pervades all these regions and the residents of these regions such as dēva (celestial beings) etc, like the presence of \[water in\] ocean. With this, the difference between aṇu dravyam (objects of minuteness) and vibhu dravyam (objects of hugeness) is explained. [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) which is aṇu (miniscule) will not pervade the whole body; ākāsa (ether) which is huge and all pervading, does not control the entities which it is pervading.

Alternative explanation,

- *vānattum* … – Higher regions such as svarga etc and the great brahmā et al who reside in such higher regions.
- *kūnal sangat tadakkaiyavanai* – Such [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is pervading everywhere, incarnates among those pervaded objects to be with them – that is being explained here. When asked “Such emperumān who is incarnating, is he descending with a mortal body?”, as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 3.5.5](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/09/thiruvaimozhi-3-5-5-sadhu-sanaththai/) “*ādi am sōdi uruvai angu vaittu ingup piṟanda*” (having the same primordial spiritual splendorous form here as present in paramapadam), he brought in his auspicious spiritual form and presented the same as a human body.  It is said in śrī bhāgavatam 5.3 “*jātōsi dēva dēvē śaśanka chakra gadādara*” (Oh lord of nityasūris who are the controllers of dēvas (celestial beings)! you have taken birth with your conch, disc and mace).

- *kūnal sangam* – As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 4.42 “*prānjalim prahvamāśīnam*” (humbly sitting with folded palms), pāncajanyam which resembles lakśmaṇa who is bowing out of enjoying [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/). śrī pāncajanyāḻvān is known for enjoying [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s hands and mouth.
- *tadak kaiyavanai* – The hands are so huge that, even if both the realms (spiritual and material realm) rest on them, there is lot more space remaining to accommodate more.
- *kudamādiyai* – Just as he pervaded everywhere, he danced with pots to be seen by everyone in the town. This is an example for all his divine activities.
- *vānak kōnai* – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is bestowing his presence not just for a town, but for the whole \[spiritual\] realm.
- *kavi solla vallēṟku* – For me who can glorify such emperumān in all of his forms/states.
- *ini māṟu uṇḍē* –  Should I say specifically “*agal vānam*” (the spiritual realm) \[as in previous pāsuram\]? There is no one in both the realms \[spiritual and material realm\].

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.5.10. Undum umilndum

*uṇḍum umiḻndum kadandum idandum kidandum ninṟum koṇḍa kōlattodu vīṟṟirundum maṇam kūdiyum kaṇḍavāṟṟāl tanadē ulagena ninṟān tannai vaṇ tamiḻ nūṟka nōṟṟēn adiyārkku inba māriyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

uṇḍum – placed in \[his\] stomach (during total deluge); umiḻndum – (subsequently) spat out; kadandum – measured and placed under his foot (to remove any thought of any other person being the owner); idandum – lifted up (during intermediary deluge, in the form of varāha); kidandum – (as said in “pratiśiśyē mahōdadē:“, at the seashore) laid down; ninṟum – stood (giving darśan to the dēvatās after killing rāvaṇa as said in “avaśtabhya ca tiśtantam“); koṇḍa – returned \[to ayōdyā\] and accepted the throne; kōlattodu – with that divine attire; vīṟṟirundum – sat; maṇam – daily festivities; kūdiyum – being united (with mother earth) and ruled over; kaṇḍa – as visibly seen in these cases; āṟṟāl – his activities; ulagu – world; tanadē – subservient to him; ena – as praised by the whole world; ninṟān tannai – on sarvēśvara who stood; vaṇ tamiḻ – the drāvida prabandam which is distinguished and practicable by all; nūṟka – to compile; nōṟṟēn – acquired the puṇya (virtue) (of his acknovledgement); adiyārkku – for the \[pleasure of the\] bhāgavatas who are his servitors; inba māri – cloud which rains joy

**Перевод:**

**emperumān placed the world in \[his\] stomach, spat it out, measured it and placed it under his foot, lifted it up, laid down \[as śrī rāma\], stood \[victorious against rāvaṇa\], returned \[to ayōdyā\] and accepted the throne, sat with that divine attire, being united (with mother earth) and ruled over the world with daily festivities; as visibly seen in these cases, his activities showcase that the world is fully subservient to him; I acquired the puṇya (virtue) (of his acknovledgement) to compile the drāvida prabandam which is distinguished and practicable by all, on sarvēśvara who stood praised by all the world, for the \[pleasure of the\] bhāgavatas who are his servitors.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In tenth pāsuram, āḻvār enjoys the sweetness of his own pāsurams and says “Those śrīvaiṣṇavas who are dear to emperumān, How joyful they will be on hearing these pāsurams!”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “I am fortunate to sing the praises of emperumān who has heart-captivating activities for the protection of the entities he is pervading, for the pleasure of his devotees”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Tenth pāsuram. āḻvār says “Being capable of singing his praises to have all his activities contained in my words, not only did I serve in the apt matter \[singing emperumān‘s glories\], I also brought happiness for śrīvaiṣṇavas”. uṇḍum umiḻndum kadandum idandum kidandum ninṟum koṇḍa kōlattodu vīṟṟirundum maṇam kūdiyum kaṇḍavāṟṟāl tanadē ulagena ninṟān tannai vaṇ tamiḻ nūṟka nōṟṟēn adiyārkku inba māriyē*

- *uṇḍum* – Protecting the world by placing it in his stomach during total deluge.
- *umiḻndum* – Releasing them outside so that they don’t get cramped inside his divine stomach forever.
- *kadandum* – When persons like mahābali steal the earth like an eagle catching its prey, he crosses the boundaries and rescues it.
- *idandum* – When deluge consumes the earth, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) assumed the form of mahā varāha and lifted up the earth from the walls of the aṇḍam (oval shaped universe of 14 layers).
- *kidandum* – As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 21.6 “*bāhum bhujagabhōgābhamudāyārisūdana: \| anjalim prāngmukha: krutvā pratiśiśyē mahōdadē: \|\|*” (śrī rāma, annihilator of his enemies, saluted the ocean facing east, placed his arm which resembles the body of a snake, as support/pillow for his head, laid down in front of the ocean), laid down in a posture which in itself will destroy lankā, like one ocean is angry with another, stayed in the seashore.
- *ninṟum* – He stood as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam kiśkintā kāṇḍam 19.25 “*avaśtabhya ca tiśtantam dadarśa danurūrjitam*” (tārā saw śrī rāma who stood with the majestic bow).
- *koṇḍa kōlattodu vīṟṟirundum* – his presence as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 99.25 “… *utajē rāmamāsīnam …*” (śrī bharatāḻvān saw śrī rāma wearing clothes of bark of tree, having matted hair etc in the hermitage). Alternatively, it explains – śrī rāma ruling over in the form of an emperor for 11000 years.
- *maṇam kūdiyūm* – As he protected śrī bhūmi dēvi who is his divine companion, for those 11000 years, being united with her.
- *kaṇḍa āṟṟāl* … – We don’t need any pramāṇams (authentic texts) to establish his supremacy; just his personal command over the world is sufficient to understand that “this world is under his control”; when a person \[farmer\] ploughs the land, sows seeds in it, waters them and takes care of them \[for a period of time\], one can understand that “he is the owner”; [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) himself says in tiruvāimoḻi 6.3.5 “*peyda kāvu kaṇḍīr perundēvudai mūvulagu*” (the three worlds (upper, middle and lower worlds) which are having great dēvatās like brahmā, rudra et al, is the creation of tiruviṇṇagar [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)).
- *vaṇ tamiḻ nōṟka nōṟṟēn* – I am blessed to sing tiruvāimoḻi. vaṇ tamiḻ – udāra (magnanimous); those who recite the pāsurams will be blessed with all benefits. Alternatively – though these pāsurams are ancient, due to being revealed through āḻvār, they appear fresh and clear. śrī rāmāyaṇam bāla kāṇḍam 4.7 “*ciranirvruttamapyētat pratyakśamiva darśitam*” (Though this happened long ago, it appears as if it is happening now). kaṇḍa āṟṟāl implies “This is visible in front of our own eyes”.
- *adiyārkku inba māriyē* – āren’t these pāsurams sung to praise [sarvēśvara](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) \[yes\]? They are also giving joy to śrīvaiṣṇavas.
- *inba māri* – Cloud which showers happiness. Seeing how enjoyable this is for me, how enjoyable will this be for those who are favourable towards [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)? He himself said in tiruvāimoḻi 9.4.9 “*toṇḍarkkamuduṇṇāc col mālaigaḷ sonnēn*” (I have sung these garlands of words, to be drunk as nectar for the devotees).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.5.11. Mari marada

*māri māṟāda taṇ am malai vēnkatattaṇṇalai vāri māṟāda paim pūm poḻil sūḻ kurugūr nagark kārimāṟan satakōpan sollāyirattu ippattāl vēri māṟāda pūmēl iruppāḷ vinai tīrkkumē*

**Пословный перевод:**

māri māṟāda – due to non-stop rains; taṇ – cool; am – attractive; vēnkatam – having the divine name tiruvēnkatam; malai – in tirumalai; aṇṇalai – natural lord; vāri māṟāda – having abundance of water (for services at his divine feet etc); paim pūm poḻil – attractive gardens with abundance of flowers; sūḻ – surrounded by; kurugūr nagar – in āḻvārtirunagari; kāri – having the relationship with kāri (who is his father); māṟan – having the family name of māṟan; satakōpan – nammāḻvār; sol – mercifully spoke; āyirattu – in the thousand pāsurams; ippattāl – through this decad; vēri māṟāda – having continuous flow of honey; pū mēl – in the lotus flower; iruppāḷ – lakshmi who eternally resides; vinai – all sins (which are hurdles for enjoying bhagavān); tīrkkum – eliminate (by her divine glance)

**Перевод:**

**emperumān is in tirumalai which has the divine name tiruvēnkatam, which is attractive and cool due to non-stop rains; nammāḻvār who is having relationship with kāri (his father) and has the family name “māṟan”, residing in āḻvārtirunagari, which is surrounded by attractive gardens with abundance of flowers and water, mercifully spoke about such emperumān in this decad among the thousand pāsurams; through \[learning/practicing\] this decad, lakshmi who eternally resides in the lotus flower which has continuous flow of honey, will eliminate all sins.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the end, periya pirāttiyār who is engrossed in this great quality “namakkum pūvin misai nangaikkum” (for us and śrī mahālakśmi) of emperumān, feels joyful that she got the company of nammāḻvār who understood and mercifully explained this quality \[to others\], removes all the sufferings of those who learned this decad which reveals this quality considering such act as her responsibility and protects them.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār explains as the result of this decad – just by engaging in this decad, lakshmi will eliminate all sins that are hurdles, by her merciful glance.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*In the end – āḻvār says ” periya pirāttiyār will consider those who learned this decad as her dependents and eliminate all their sufferings”. māri māṟāda taṇ am malai vēnkatattaṇṇalai vāri māṟāda paim pūm poḻil sūḻ kurugūr nagark kārimāṟan satakōpan sollāyirattu ippattāl vēri māṟāda pūmēl iruppāḷ vinai tīrkkumē*

- *māri* … – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) praised [sarvēśvaran](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) who is having tirumalai which is cool and attractive since it is always raining. As it is said in tiruviruttam 50 “*viṇmudal nāyagan nīḷmudi veṇmutta vāsigaittāy maṇ mudal sērvuṟṟu aruvi seyyā niṟkum malai*” (The tirumalai which has waterfalls starting from the peak regions flowing down to the foothills which resemble white pearl garland decorating the divine crown of paramapadanātan), it appears attractive with flowing water. Since āḻvār glorified [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s śeelam (simplicity) of showing preferential treatment towards nitya samsāris (eternally bound souls) even ahead of the ever inseparable [śrī mahālakśmi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/), he is glorifying tiruvēnkatamudaiyān (śrīnivāsan) who is the ultimate manifestation of such simplicity.
- *vāri* … – As the rain never stops in tirumalai, tirunagari is also always with water, since tirumalai is the origin for tirunagari (like rain water in the mountain being the source of flowing water). [āḻvārtirunagari](http://azhwarthirunagari.koyil.org/) which is surrounded by beautiful attractive garden.
- *kāṟimāṟan* … – To avoid any doubts/misgivings in the explained principles, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is explaining the trustworthy nature of himself.
- *vēri* … – It is explained that [periya pirāttiyār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/) will bestow the benefits for those who learn this decad. Since rain never stops in tirumalai, water never recedes in tirunagari. Since it is a perennial pond, honey never stops flowing in [pirātti](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/)‘s seat, that is the lotus flower. Why should pirātti give the benefits for those who learned this decad? This decad explains the śeela guṇam of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) which facilitates him like the samsāri (bound soul) who was recommended by pirātti; this śeela guṇam is incomprehensible for anyone; only she can comprehend it and those who were divinely blessed with knowledge/devotion by emperumān (like [āḻvārs](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/azhwars/)) can comprehend it; out of great mercy thinking “[āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) understood this quality and revealed it”, when emperumān sets out to give the benefits, pirātti pushes him aside and takes up such bestowing of the benefit as her responsibility saying “Only I should bestow the benefits”.
- *vinai tīrkkumē* – She will remove the hurdles for the bhagavat anubhavam of those who learned this decad. Also explains that – those who learn this decad can enter the private quarters of [śrī mahālakśmi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/).

[āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) tiruvadigaḷē śaraṇam  
[emperumānār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/emperumanar/) tiruvadigaḷē śaraṇam  
[piḷḷān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/pillan/) tiruvadigaḷē śaraṇam  
[nanjīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nanjiyar/) tiruvadigaḷē śaraṇam  
[nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/) tiruvadigaḷē śaraṇam  
[vadakkut tiruvīdip piḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadakku-thiruvidhi-pillai/) tiruvadigaḷē śaraṇam  
[periyavāccān piḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/periyavachchan-pillai/) tiruvadigaḷē śaraṇam  
[vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/) tiruvadigaḷē śaraṇam  
[jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/mamunigal/) tiruvadigaḷē śaraṇam

## 4.6 Tirpparai yam

## 4.6.1. Tirpparai yam

*tīrppārai yām ini enganam nādudum? annaimīr! ōrppāl ivvoṇṇudal uṟṟa nal nōy idu tēṟinōm pōrppāgu tān seydu anṟaivarai velvitta māyappōrt tērppāganārkku ivaḷ sindai tuḻāyt tisaikkinṟadē*

**Пословный перевод:**

annaimīr – (due to love towards her, you who think “somehow or other her disease should be cured”) mother!; ini – after the disease is not being cured; tīrppārai – those who can cure (this disease); yām – we (you all and I, who cannot understand the nature of the disease); enganam – how; nādudum – to find?; ōrppāl – by checking now; i oḷ nudal – this girl with beautiful forehead; uṟṟa – affected with; nal – laudable; idu – this; nōy – disease; tēṟinōm – clearly understood (by seeing her nature and bodily beauty and as it appears to have internally affected her, this is not a bodily disease, but a distinguished disease of attachment towards bhagavān himself); pōr – for the warfare; pāgu – having abilities; tān – himself (as said in “yasya mantrī cagōptā ca suhruccaiva janārdana:“); seydu – engaged; anṟu – that day (when duryōdana and his brothers dominated pāṇḍavars); aivarai – those five; velvitta – to be victorious; māyam – having amazing activities in the form of deceit (such as vowing not to take up weapons and took up the same, changing day into night); pōr – in the battle; tēr – in arjuna’s chariot; pāganārkku – for the one who stood as the charioteer (in front \[of arjuna\], as said in “pārtam sancādya“, to accept the enemies arrows’ on himself); ivaḷ – her; sindai – heart; tuḻāy – bewildered; tisaikkinṟadu – losing her mind

**Перевод:**

**\[The friend says\] Oh mother! After her (parānkuśa nāyaki‘s) disease is not being cured, how to find those who can cure (this disease)? By checking now, I clearly understood that this girl with beautiful forehead is affected with this laudable disease. Her heart became bewildered and she lost her mind for the one \[kriṣṇa\] who stood as the charioteer in arjuna’s chariot during the battle; on that day, kriṣṇa who has the abilities for the warfare and performed amazing activities in the form of deceit, himself engaged to have those five pāṇḍavas victorious.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In first pāsuram, the friend of this pirātti (parānkuśa nāyaki) explains the cause of her disease \[to her relatives\] and tells them “Whatever you are doing as the remedy is not the true remedy” and stops them.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*In first pāsuram, the friend of parānkuśa nāyaki tells her mother “We analysed and found out that she is attached to kriṣṇa who was partial to pāṇḍavas; hence, where will we find the one who will cure her disease”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. tīrppārai yām ini enganam nādudum? annaimīr! ōrppāl ivvoṇṇudal uṟṟa nal nōy idu tēṟinōm pōrppāgu tān seydu anṟaivarai velvitta māyappōrt tērppāganārkku ivaḷ sindai tuḻāyt tisaikkinṟadē*

\[The disease explained in this pāsuram/padigam is the exclusive devotion towards [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) and the subsequent sorrow in separation of emperumān.\]

- *tīrppārai yām ini enganam nādudum* – This is mercifully explained in three different ways.
   - Since it is said “*tīrppārai – enganam nādudum*” (where to find those who can cure this?), the crux is to negate their actions saying “Whatever you are doing is not the remedy”; when they are trying to find a cure, if it is said “where to find those who can cure?”, it implies that whatever they are not doing is not the cure.
   - We will only find those who will become bewildered like herself and where can we find those who can cure her? As said in tiruvāimoḻi 6.7.2 “*ūrum nādum ulagamum tannaip pōl*” ([āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is transforming everyone to become like him), she keeps transforming others to be like her.
   - It appears that her friend too is now looking for those who can cure the disease.
   - \[A fourth explanation is given too – probably spontaneously thought about it as the first 3 explanations were given; alternatively, this is given as explanation for “*ini*” in some manuscripts\] As said in tiruneduntāṇḍagam 11 “*kadalvaṇṇar idu seydāl kāppārār*” (if [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) himself does this, who can save her?), if the medicine itself becomes unsuitable, what is the remedy? That which is said as in [tiruvāimoḻi 3.4.5](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/08/thiruvaimozhi-3-4-5-achchudhan-amalan/) “*naccu mā marundam*” (the desirable medicine acquired from cow) itself becomes unsuitable; He who is said as in viṣṇu sahasranāmam “*nirvāṇam bhēśajam bhiśak*” (bliss, medicine and doctor), himself becomes harmful.
- *yām* – After addressing specifically “*annaimīr*” (you, mother), here, she is saying “*yām*” (we); this means that there is no difference between mother and friends \[with regard to the sorrow\]. When the mothers wished well for śrī rāma and returned, the friends could not even do that as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 41st sargam “*śōkabhārēṇa cākrantāśśayanamnajahustatā*” (śrī rāma’s friends being afflicted with sorrow, remained in their beds being unable to stand up); hence, this sorrow, would eliminate the difference between mother and friends; it can also be considered as highlighting the greatness of the friend \[yām, as in respectable yān. that is, using we to say “I” with reverence “the royal we”\].
- *ini* – After knowing the nature of the disease.
- *enganam nādudum* – When she said “Is there any remedy? where can we search?”, all the relatives thought “she must have the solution” and turned towards her; she thinks “If I told them that I already knew the issue, they will blame me only; let me pretend to analyse the situation now”,
- *ōrppāl* – She said “I think about the situation now; as you also analysed and I too have analysed, this is what I feel now”. She (this friend) is like [kūrattāḻvān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/kUraththAzhwAn/) (in her jñānam); when she thinks inward, she can visualise the [tatva trayam](http://ponnadi.blogspot.com/p/thathva-thrayam.html) ([cit](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/), [acit](http://ponnadi.blogspot.in/2013/03/thathva-thrayam-achith-what-is-matter.html) and [īśvara](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)) part by part, in great detail.
- *ivavoṇṇudal* – This girl ([parānkuśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)) who has a distinguished forehead. For the one who has such distinguished face, can she be affected with a disease through any other means? Should she not be affected by [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s face only, as said in tiruvāimoḻi 7.7.8 “*kaṇṇan kōḷiḻai vāḷ mugamāyk kodiyēn uyirk koḷginṟadu*” (kriṣṇa’s glow having his own beautiful face which is like an ornament for him, through such face captivates the heart of me who is very bad)? If she has a disease, should it not be caused by emperumān only? If bharatāḻvān gets affected with a disease will it be cāturtikam (a type of deadly fever)? īsn’t it well known that he was affected due to separation from śrī rāma? If some thing is troubling her, should it not be a distinct matter \[emperumān\]? Can we not distinguish between one who died being killed by an arrow and one who died by drowning in water? Due to desiring for emperumān who has great qualities and got bewildered due to not getting what she wanted, her fresh face demanded to rid of evil eyes.
- *uṟṟa* – the disease which has penetrated very deep and has no cure.
- *nal nōy* – This disease is not be cured. \[Instead\] one should pay some money and be affected with this disease. The mumukśus (those who desire for liberation) put in many efforts to acquire this disease. Instead of accepting such disease, I am trying to give a remedy! After acquiring true knowledge, until the body is shed, for the dēha yātrai (daily conduct of oneself), this disease exists and subsequently it continues eternally \[after shedding the body as well\]. When \[this bhakti (devotion) is\] considered as a means which is different from prapatti, when that thought it be being the means \[instead of [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) being the means\] is eliminated, such devotion will become part of the goal. viṣṇu darmam 68 “*paramāpadamāpanna:*” (fell in great danger) – this is a distinguished danger. This danger will make [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) himself rush to protect in a chaotic manner. When this which is explained as in [śrī bhagavat gītā](http://githa.koyil.org/) 11.54 “*bhaktyā tvananyayā śakya:*” (I cannot be attained without devotion), is acquired, emperumān will also be \[easily\] attained.
- *tēṟinōm* – In their \[[āḻvārs](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/azhwars/)\] group, clarity is rare to find, just like bewilderment is rare to find in the group of riśis (sages). For the riśis, they only have the clarity “one should not be attached to worldly matters”; but in the case of āḻvārs they are bewildered due to bhagavat viśayam (matters related to [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)).

“If you have understood, why don’t you explain it to us” query the relatives of [parānkuśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/).

- *pōrp pāgu* … – Though kriṣṇa was related to both \[kauravas and pāṇḍavas\], when it was time for action, as said in mahābhāratam rājasūya parvam “*yasya mantrī ca gōptā ca suhrutcaiva janārdana:*” (janārdana who is the lord of all the worlds and is the minister, protector and friend of arjuna), for pāṇḍavas, kriṣṇa remained everything which was taken away by kauravas from them. He himself managed all aspects of the war. pāgu – the act of the manager/controller.
- *tān seydu* – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who remained seated ruling over all the worlds, himself did. Instead of making it happen based on his powerful position, he personally engaged and completed the task. “*tān*” indicates his supremacy. She is captivated by his saulabhyam (simplicity). If a lowly person manifests simplicity, she will not be attracted by that. When such supreme lord manifests simplicity, she becomes captivated.
- *tān seydu anṟu aivarai velvitta* – On that day when those hundred brothers along with all the evil forces stood together and when these five pāṇḍavas stood without much help; this explains – how emperumān himself arranged the soldiers, drove the chariot, gave rest and water to the horses when they became tired, tended/managed the horses and won the battle for the pāṇḍavas himself. He took up all responsibilities of arjuna on himself.
- *aivarai velvitta* – To make the pāṇḍavas victorious was more difficult than defeating the duryōdana and his group \[and [parānkuśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)\]. Since duryōdana and group were prideful, it was difficult to defeat them; it is difficult to defeat parānkuśa nāyaki due to her strītva abhimānam (pride of considering herself to be a perfect woman); similarly as arjuna said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 1.32](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/1-32/) “*na kānkśē vijayam kriṣṇa*” (Oh kriṣṇa! I have no desire for victory), it was difficult to make the pāṇḍavas win \[since they had no desire for that\].
- *māyap pōr* – Amazing war; also explained as deceitful war. That is, in the pāṇḍavas side, changing of day into night, kriṣṇa declaring that he will not take up weapons and taking it up subsequently were done; in the kauravas side many atiratas (great charioteers) together attacked abhimanyu \[when he was unarmed\].
- *tērp pāganārkku* – Whenever anyone attacked arjuna, kriṣṇa stood there to take the attack on himself, ignoring his \[tender\] body, drove the chariot, sitting in front of arjuna, without any weapons. He would say as in mahābhāratam “*ayamasmi*” (I am yours) – Am I not your servitor? Why don’t you engage me in your service?
- *ivaḷ …* – [parānkuśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) who was captivated by such act of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/). As said in mahābhāratam when bhīma tells hanumān “*nirguṇa: paramātmā saudēhantē vyāpyatisttati*” (the paramātmā (śrī rāma) who has no inauspicious qualities is well pervaded and manifested in your body), is the sāratya vēśam (the form of emperumān being a charioteer) not visible in her body? Her heart was shaken and she became bewildered for the one who controlled the chariot; if an ocean shakes, should it not be by the mantara mountain \[when the dēvas and asuras churned the ocean, it became wild\]? She who is blessed with “*mayarvaṟa madi nalam*” (faultless knowledge and devotion), does not become bewildered for his supremacy in paramapadam, but only for his simplicity as the charioteer. When those who are blessed with faultless knowledge and devotion become bewildered, would it not be for [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s *āśrita pāratantriyam* (his subservience towards his devotees)? One who eliminated the sorrows of arjuna is now causing sorrow for parānkuśa nāyaki. He removed the sorrow of a man, but is causing sorrow for a helpless woman.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.6.2. Tisaikkinrade

*tisaikkinṟadē ivaḷ nōy idu mikka perum deyvam isaippinṟi nīr aṇangādum iḷam deyvam anṟidu tisaippinṟiyē sangu cakkaram enṟivaḷ kētka nīr isaikkiṟṟirāgil nanṟēyil peṟum idu kāṇminē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tisaikkinṟadu – (both she and you) are losing your mind; ivaḷ nōy – caused by her disease; idu – this situation; mikka perum deyvam – caused by sarvēśvara who is greater than all, with incomprehensible greatness; idu – this \[activity\]; isaippu inṟi – not fitting (to the nature of yours, hers and the disease); nīr – you all; aṇangādum – being engaged for the; iḷam dēvatā – petty dēvatā (deity); anṟu – is not \[caused by\]; tisaippu inṟiyē – without getting confused (by the words of the others who advice you otherwise); sangu cakkaram – Sanka and chakra (which are distinguished symbols of that supreme lord); enṟu – as; ivaḷ – she (parānkuśa nāyaki, who is bewildered); kētka – to hear; nīr – you all; isaikkiṟṟir āgil – if you can say; nanṟē – well; il pērum – be sustained; itu – this state; kāṇmin – (imagine and) see

**Перевод:**

**Both she and you are losing your mind; this situation caused by her disease is caused by sarvēśvara who is greater than all, with incomprehensible greatness; this \[activity\] you all are engaged for the petty dēvatā (deity) is not fitting (to the nature of yours, hers and the disease); without getting confused, if you all can say Sanka and chakra and make her hear, she can be well sustained; (imagine and) see this state \[of her being redeemed\].**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In second pāsuram, parānkuśa nāyaki‘s friend says “This disease cannot be cured by pacifying kśudra dēvatās (lowly deities); if you explain emperumān‘s greatness without getting bewildered, we can redeem her”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, parānkuśa nāyaki‘s friend says “Her disease is not caused by kśudra dēvatās but by the greatest dēvatā (emperumān); hence, if you tell her about his distinguished symbols, she can be redeemed”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. tisaikkinṟadē ivaḷ nōy idu mikka perum deyvam isaippinṟi nīr aṇangādum iḷam deyvam anṟidu tisaippinṟiyē sangu cakkaram enṟivaḷ kētka nīr isaikkiṟṟirāgil nanṟēyil peṟum idu kāṇminē*

- *tisaikkinṟadē ivaḷ nōy* – She ([parānkuśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)) lost her mind for [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s qualities; you all lost your mind seeing her disease. You all are not realising that this disease is due to emperumān. She is using the word “*tisaikkinṟadē*” \[which is a respectful term to say that you have lost your mind\], since the mother \[of parānkuśa nāyaki\] needs to be treated with respect.

The mother and relatives say “Alright. We are confused about her disease. If you know the cause for this, why don’t you tell us?”,

- *idu mikka perum deyvam* – As said in “*gambhīra: paramōdēva:*” (he is profound (deep); he is the supreme lord) and tiruviruttam 53 “*vānōr talaimaganām sīrāyina deva nal nōy*” (This divine disease in the matter of the auspicious qualities of the lord of the nityasūris), this disease was acquired by the grace of [sarvēśvara](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/); considering the disease \[great devotion\] and the cause of the disease \[[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) himself\] to be the same, she calls the disease itself as “*idu mikka perum deyvam*“.
- *isaippinṟi* … – There is no consonance between you and your remedy; there is no consonance between this disease and [parānkuśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/). For those who are engaged in bhagavat viśayam in the initial stages, they cannot bear such pain. So there is no match for any of these. This \[action\] is not a match for you; the disease which has affected your daughter is not a match for her; it \[the disease\] does not match emperumān who is the cause of such disease \[since such pain is acquired due to emperumān’s anger\]; since other dēvatās cannot enter here, this does not match the dēvatās you are thinking about. An incident is mercifully explained \[by nampiḷḷai\] to demonstrate this – once an assistant \[a śrīvaiṣṇava too\] of piḷḷai uṟangā villi dāsar \[a disciple of bhagavad śrī rāmānuja\],  became possessed with aiyanār (śāstā – a deity which protects the town borders) and tortured him. When the relatives asked him what he wanted, he said “bring me some milk and fruits; want to apply some good sandalwood paste and perfume; want to wear some new clothes; want to wear some beautiful ornaments; want to be carried in a palanquin; some one should hold an umbrella for me” and they all agreed to fulfil the desires of that deity. They came to piḷḷai uṟangā villi dāsar’s residence and collected these materials, brought them over, offered all of them to the possessed person. In the night, the śāstā started troubling the assistant twice the torture which was previously done. When asked why he was troubling more, śāstā replied “Well, it appears that you have brought the paraphernalia of piḷḷai (uṟangā villi dāsar). You offered his umbreall to me; how can I go under that? you applied the sandal paste which was applied to him to cause me severe burns as if I am exposed to hot sun, his ornaments are like shackles for me. For what you have done, I will kill this man \[whom I have entered\]” and tortured more. Thus, for śrīvaiṣṇavas, these other dēvatās’ effects will not match.
- *nīr* – You who are supposed to be deeply engaged in bhagavat viśayam.
- *aṇangādum iḷam deyvam anṟu idu* – This is not a disease which is acquired from lowly dēvatā which is worthless for anything else.
- *tisaippinṟiyē* – Instead of getting bewildered in the remedy, as you got bewildered in the cause of the disease. Even if the cause is confusing, the disease will only be cured, if the remedy is properly identified.

They all ask “In what aspect, we lost our mind in determining the cause of the disease? In what way can we not lose our mind in the remedy?”,

- *sangu* … – Her disease makes her say as in [tiruvāimoḻi 4.2.9](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/12/thiruvaimozhi-4-2-9-nangaimir-nirum/) “*sangennum cakkaramennum*” (says “Sanka, chakra”); you too try to do the same to cure her. Don’t you want to know how she got the disease, to cure the same? I have also known you saying “*sangennum cakkaramennum*“; but when it comes to curing her, why are you losing your mind? When you do that \[saying “*sangennum cakkaramennum*“\], do not do it in a negligible manner so that it gets sounded out like a small pit in the ocean, but say it in the same manner as [parānkuśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says.
- *ivaḷ kētka nīr isaigiṟṟiyāgil* – Only when the bewildered parānkuśa nāyaki can listen, the clear-minded mother and relatives can speak; that is why, the friend says “*tisaippinṟiyē*” (without any confusion). She will only hear about [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s divine symbols and anything else will not enter her ears. If you can stabilize yourself and tell this once to make her hear that. \[An incident from the life of [bhattar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/parasara-bhattar/) is highlighted here to explain how they should make her listen\] During the final moments of āyccimagan (a śrīvaiṣṇava) when he was unconscious, bhattar arrived there to see him. bhattar knowing āyccimagan’s attachment towards [\[aḻagiya maṇavāḷap\] perumāḷ (śrī rangānāta)](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), whispers in his ear “*aḻagiya maṇavaḷap perumāḷē śaraṇam*” so that he hears that; āyccimagan hears those words and whenever he regained conscious he keeps reciting “*aḻagiya maṇavaḷap perumāḷē śaraṇam*” and subsequently ascended to tirunādu (paramapadam). \[Explaining to highlight the importance/rarity of hearing bhagavān’s names during the last moments\] As said in periya tirumoḻi 6.2.4 “*peṟṟa makkaḷ peṇḍir enṟivar pin udavādaṟindēn – pirindēn*” (Knowing that my children, wife et al will not help me in my final moments, I gave them up) – in the final moments, one can see the children/relatives asking “Where did you keep your gold, money etc?” and cannot see anyone reciting the divine names of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/); periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 4.5.3 “*sōrvināl poruḷ vaittadu uṇḍāgil sollu sollenṟu suṟṟum irundu*” (Surrounding the person on the death bed, people will ask “can you recollect and tell us if you have kept any valuable anywhere?”).
- *nanṟē* – This is very nice.

What is the goodness in it?

- *il peṟum* – \[Three exlanations\] 1) She will have \[matching\] body which can sustain the ātmā; 2) a tamiḻ scholar explained this as “*il – kiḻatti – gruhiṇi* (wife)” – “She will become the wife of emperumān”; 3) also explained as “*nanṟu*” + “*ēyil peṟum*“, where “*ēyil*” means gānam (song), since she is said as in tiruccanda viruttam 105 “*paṇṇai venṟa insol mangai*” (the lady, whose voice is sweeter than music), she will speak \[on hearing your words\]; śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 66.15 “*madurāmadurālābā*” (sweet person, who speaks sweet words). Thus, “she will retain her body; she will be the wife; she will become capable of speaking” are explained.
- *idu kāṇminē* – You allowed those who are connected to dēvatāntarams (other dēvatās) to come and touch her; in that manner, would you not try the remedy I am suggesting? I am giving this suggestion based on visible results; why don’t you try this also? Is there only one remedy? This is like a river-nourished fertile land, the results will be well known.
- *idu kāṇminē* – Another explanation – as said in tiruvāimoḻi 7.3.1 “*veḷḷaic curisangodāḻi ēndit tāmaraik kaṇṇan en nenjinūdē, puḷḷaik kadāginṟa āṟṟaik kāṇīr*” (lotus eyed [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s riding his garuda in my heart, holding his white curved conch), the friend is showing the form that is shining in her ([parānkuśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s) heart, “Whether you give the remedy I suggested to her or not; if done in the proper way, you can see the result now”. In this explanation, the pāsuram ends with “*nanṟēyil peṟum*” and “*idu kāṇminē*” will be considered as a separate sentence.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.
