## 4.6.3. Idu kanmin

*idu kāṇmin annaimīr! ikkattuvicci sol koṇḍu nīr eduvānum seydu angōr kaḷḷum iṟaicciyum tūvēnmin maduvār tuḻāy mudi māyappirān kaḻal vāzttināl aduvē ivaḷ uṟṟa nōykkum aru marundāgumē*

**Пословный перевод:**

annaimīr – Oh mother!; idu – doing the remedy (I suggested); kāṇmin – see (the results for yourself); i – this lowly; kattuvicci – psychic reader’s; sol – (inferior) words; koṇḍu – accepting them; nīr – instead of seeing your own nature; eduvānum – any act (for the appeasement of the dēvatās who are to be rejected); seydu – engaging in; angu – there; ōr – a (forbidden); kaḷḷum – alcohol; iṟaicciyum – meat; tūvēnmin – do not offer them; maduvār – with flowing honey; tuḻāy – decorated with tiruttuḻāy (tuḷasi); mudi – having divine crown; māyam – amazing qualities and activities; pirān – The great benefactor who lets those who desire for him, to enjoy him; kaḻal – for the divine feet; vāḻtināl – if mangaḷāśāsanams (well-wishing praises) are done; aduvē – not only such praising is befitting your true nature; ivaḷ uṟṟa – she is affected with; nōykku – for the disease; aru – difficult to attain; marundumāgum – be the medicine as well as the enjoyable aspect, and be the relief for you who are suffering seeing her disease

**Перевод:**

**Oh mother! By doing the remedy (I suggested), see (the results for yourself); accepting this lowly psychic reader’s words, instead of seeing your own nature, there, do not engage in any act (for the appeasement of the dēvatās who are to be rejected) and do not offer the dēvatās any forbidden things such as alcohol and meat; emperumān who is having divine crown which is decorated with tiruttuḻāy (tuḷasi) with flowing honey, is the great benefactor who lets those who desire for him, to enjoy him; if mangaḷāśāsanams are done for such emperumān’s divine feet, not only would such praising be befitting your true nature; it would also be the medicine as well as the enjoyable aspect, and be the relief for you who are suffering seeing the disease she is affected with.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In third pāsuram, parānkuśa nāyaki‘s friend says “Instead of doing unsuitable acts, just praise emperumān‘s divine feet; by doing that, her sorrows will go away”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, parānkuśa nāyaki‘s friend says “Instead of pleasing other dēvatās with the forbidden alcohol and meat, if you praise the infinitely enjoyable emperumān’s divine feet, that itself will be the medicine and enjoyable aspect for her disease”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. idu kāṇmin annaimīr! ikkattuvicci sol koṇḍu nīr eduvānum seydu angōr kaḷḷum iṟaicciyum tūvēnmin maduvār tuḻāy mudi māyappirān kaḻal vāzttināl aduvē ivaḷ uṟṟa nōykkum aru marundāgumē*

- *idu kāṇmin annaimīr* – Just because we are born to you, that does not warranty that you should not listen to our advice. Do you want some one older/superior to give advice? Even if it is one’s own child, if the advice is good, one should accept it. As said in tiruneduntāṇḍagam 14 “*tirumālaip pādak kēttu ‘vaḷarttadanāl payan peṟṟēn varuga’ enṟu madakkiḷiyaik kai kūppi vaṇangināḷē*” (On hearing my daughter sing about śrīman nārāyaṇa, I said “I feel accomplished having raised you, come here” and saluted her who was like a humble parrot), don’t you belong to the group of those \[āḻvārs\] who saluted their own children? \[Not only in your āḻvārs group, even among riśis, this is seen\] Further, isn’t it said “*putrakā itihōvāca*” “Did they not say ‘Oh children!’ \[When brahmā condemned pidira et al, they went to śukrācārya, and he welcomed them all\]?” – Whoever may have said it, if the advice is good, should we not accept it?
- *ik kattuvicci* – tiruccanda viruttam 64 “*kāṇilum uruppolār*” (not even qualified to be seen).
- *sol koṇḍu* – tiruccanda viruttam 64 “*sevikkināda kīrttiyār*” (unpleasant to hear about).
- *ik kattuvicci sol koṇḍu* – This psychic reader who is suggesting you the remedy – you have seen her form and you have heard her speech, are you accepting her? Even if she says the same words as I, are they acceptable? And, if I say the same words she uttered, I should be given up – such is the evil nature of her words.
- *nīr* –  You who remain as said in mudal tiruvantādi 11 “*pēy mulai nanjūṇāga uṇḍān uruvodu pēr allāl kāṇā kaṇ kēḷā sevi*” ([emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who consumed the poison from the demoniac pūtanā’s breast – my eyes will not see any form other than his, my ears will not hear any name other than his). Even bauddas, ārhatas (jainas) would say “we should not hurt others; alcohol is forbidden”; are we going to accept these teachings? \[If we are to follow the aforementioned teachings\] while it is said in “*nahimsāt sarvabhūtāni*” (no creature should be hurt), vēdam also ordains certain sacrifices etc – should we not pursue such sacrifices following these others’ teachings?
- *ikkattuvicci …* – As said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 4.33](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/4-34/) “*jñāninas tatvadarśina:*” (those jñānis who have realized the knowledge about self), should you not be instructed by such great jñānis?
- *eduvānum seydu* – Only those activities which match your practice. Another explanation – Doing any activity. Your niśtai (faith/stature) is as explained in [tiruppāvai 2](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2014/12/thiruppavai-02-vaiyaththu/) “*seyyādana seyyōm*” (Will not do what is not done by our elders) and in [tiruppāvai 26](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/01/thiruppavai-26-male-manivanna/) “*mēlaiyār seyvanagaḷ*” (as done by the elders).
- *angu ōr* … – Do not spoil this vaiṣṇava residence with forbidden items. She is saying “angu” (there), turning her face away from there \[not wanting to see those items\].

Alright, we will stop. Why don’t you give us the remedy?

- *maduvār* … – I have heard in [tiruvāimoḻi 2.4.9](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/03/thiruvaimozhi-2-4-9-patta-podhu/) “*virai mattalar taṇ tuḻāy*” (fresh tuḷasi with well spread fragrance and honey) from you only. \[Full meaning of the sentence\] Due to coming in contact with the divine hair of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), tiruttuḻāy is having overflowing honey; such honey laden tuḷasi is decorating his divine crown; he is being an amazing personality due to such saundaryam (beauty), śeelam (simplicity) etc; the benefactor, who is manifesting such qualities for his devotees; if we praised such emperumān’s divine feet. They \[āḻvārs\] recite the divine names through mangaḷāśāsanam \[Thus, we can understand that tirunāma sankīrtanam is thus contained in divya prabandam recital itself\]. They praise him saying as in [tiruppallāṇḍu 1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/06/thiruppallandu-1-pallandu/) “*un sēvadi sevvi tirukkāppu*” (let the reddish fresh beauty of your divine feet be protected). periya tirumoḻi 11.1.9 is explained here. “*keṇḍaiyoṇ kaṇum tyilum*” – The young tender eyes will sleep, unable to do anything other than sleeping. “*enniṟam paṇḍu paṇḍu pōl okkum*” – that is, my bodily complexion will resemble that of the time before our union \[*paṇḍu paṇḍu* – First paṇḍu indicates the time before separation, and second paṇḍu indicates the time even before that, when she was a child without any of these awareness, with normal complexion\]. Union always leads to unbearable separation. When a person does not know about something, one would be free from desire for that thing \[But once it is acquired, it makes one desire for it repeatedly\]. What makes her sleep and get back to previous bodily complexion? “*mikkasīr toṇḍar itta pūndaḷavin vāsamē vaṇḍu koṇḍu vandu ūdumāgilē*” – When the bumble bee brings and softly blows the fragrance of the tuḷasi that was offered by śrīvaiṣṇavas who are ananya prayōjanas (exclusively serving for [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s happiness). When nanjīyar mercifully explained this pāsuram in this manner, I (nampiḷḷai) asked “Is saying ‘*tuḷavin vāsam*‘ (the fragrance of tuḷasi) not sufficient? What is the need for the adjective ‘*mikka sīrt toṇḍar*‘ (śrīvaiṣṇavas who are ananya prayōjanas)?”. nanjīyar mercifully replied “She is grieving due to thinking that there is no one to care for him; but if she knows that there are ananya prayōjanas who are serving there, even those sleepless eyes \[feeling relieved\] will start sleeping and she will regain her previous bodily complexion”.
- *aduvē* – this is the aptly enjoyable aspect as well.
- *ivaḷ uṟṟa nōykkum aru marundāgum* – It is the rare medicine too for her disease. Just by bringing it closer, she will be cured.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.6.4. Marundagum

*marundāgum enṟu angōr māya valavai sol koṇḍu nīr karunjōṟum maṟṟaic cenjōrum kaḷan iḻaitten payan? orungāgavē ulagēḻum viḻungi umiḻnditta perundēvan pēr sollagiṟkil ivaḷaip peṟudirē*

**Пословный перевод:**

marundāgum enṟu – believing it to be the remedy; angu ōr – one who cannot be said to be “from this place, of this nature”; māyam – deceitful; valavai – one who keeps speaking in a flattering way, her; sol – words; koṇḍu – believing; nīr – you all (who are not qualified to be in contact with dēvatāntarams); karum sōṟum – black rice \[tāmasa food\]; maṟṟai – different from that; sem sōṟum – with red rice \[rājasa food\]; kaḷan – in front of the dēvatāntarams (other dēvatās); iḻaittu – placing them (to please them); en payan – what is the use?; ulagu ēḻum – all worlds (without differentiating between devotees and others); orungāgavē – at once; viḻungi – himself consumed to protect (to save them from being consumed by the deluge); umiḻnditta – spat them out again (after the deluge completes); perum dēvan – para dēvatā’s (supreme lord’s); pēr – divine name; sollagiṟkil – if you can recite; ivaḷai – (distinguished) parānkuśa nāyaki; peṟudir – will have her alive

**Перевод:**

**Believing something which is not a remedy to be the remedy, believing the words of the deceitful one \[psychic reader\] who cannot be said to be “from this place, of this nature” and one who keeps speaking in a flattering way, you all are placing the black rice and red rice which is different from the black rice in front of those other dēvatās – what is the use of this? If you can recite the divine name of para dēvatā (supreme lord) who himself consumed all worlds at once to protect and spat them out again, you will have this distinguished parānkuśa nāyaki alive.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In fourth pāsuram, parānkuśa nāyaki‘s friend says “What is the use of offering different coloured ric varieties to dēvatās who are abundant with rajō guṇam (passion) and tamō guṇam (ignorance), based on the words of the kattuvicci (psychic reader) who can speak mischievously? If you can engage in the divine nāma sankīrtanam \[chanting the divine names\] of sarvēśvara who is the friend in need, you can redeem her”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Fourth pāsuram. parānkuśa nāyaki‘s friend says “If you give up the repeated chattering of this kattuvicci (psychic reader) who speaks whatever comes to her mind, and if you can recite the divine names of sarvēśvara who is a friend in need, you will have her alive”. marundāgum enṟu angōr māya valavai sol koṇḍu nīr karunjōṟum maṟṟaic cenjōrum kaḷan iḻaitten payan? orungāgavē ulagēḻum viḻungi umiḻnditta perundēvan pēr sollagiṟkil ivaḷaip peṟudirē*

- *marundāgum enṟu* – Should one who does not have a strict diet claim to be on diet? “*marundām*” – as if it is medicine.
- *angu ōr* – Saying that “some one is there” with disregard for that person.
- *māya valavai sol koṇḍu* – One who deceitfully speaks whatever she thinks about. Listening to the words of such person.
- *nīr* – What a shame for you who are qualified to hear from those who are sātvika (goodness personified), honest persons who only speak about bhagavat viśayam.
- *nīr* – You who realize the value of the food remnants of sātvika śrīvaiṣṇavas as said in tirumālai 41 “*pōnagam seyda sēdam taruvarēl punidam*” (if a śrīvaiṣṇava gives his food remnants, that will be very purifying); you who cannot touch anything but sātvika annam (prasādam).
- *karum sōṟum …* – tāmasa food and rājasa food which is close \[in quality\] to that tāmasa food.
- *kaḷan iḻaittu en payan* – kaḷan – field, iḻaikkai – offering. That is, the places where kśudra dēvatās (petty deities) reside such as four way junctions, iḻaittu – offering with the regulations ordained for such dēvatās. What is the use of placing rājasa and tāmasa food as per the ordained regulations for those rājasa and tāmasa deities in their places of worship? Implies that there is no benefit; it will end with destruction only. Only if one can be saved from the total deluge by any one other than sarvēśvara who is sarva rakśaka (protector of all), she ([parānkuśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)) can be protected with the help of petty deities.

When asked “If there is no benefit \[in doing what we are doing\], you tell us what you consider as the means to get the benefit” and parānkuśa nāyaki’s friend says “If you will follow my suggestion, I will only tell you one name \[to recite\]”.

- *orungāgavē* – You approach the one who voluntarily protects without any restriction, even if he is not vorśipped with offerings. Even when no one is praying \[for protection\], he will come and protect considering the danger as the only reason.
- *ulagēḻum* – That too, instead of differentiating between devotees and others, he will place everyone in his divine stomach and protect them, and will release them out after the deluge.
- *perum dēvan* – para dēvatā (supreme deity). Since he is the protector of all, he is the supreme lord; he is the protector for those who are suffering; even though he did not manifest himself previously, when there is imminent danger, he will appear and protect. Due to his such nature, he is svārādakan (easily vorśippable); unlike the dēvatās (deities) you worship who are difficult to worship due to saying “*attadoḻiyac cuttadu kodu vā*” \[In the incident where rudra appears as a mendicant, goes to his devotee’s place and asks to kill and cook a young boy, and after eating the body of the boy, he asks for the head too – finally, he brings back the child to life being pleased with his devotees faith\]. [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), while protecting his devotees, only expects apratiśēdam (non rejection) which is a hint for the devotee’s ānukūlya (favourable nature) \[towards emperumān\].
- *ulagēḻum* … – That lord who finished \[protected\] during that praḷayam (deluge) is the one who can finish my praḷayam (suffering). How can we take shelter of the kśudra dēvatās (petty deities) who also suffer along with us during the deluge? Should we not take shelter of the sarva rakśaka?
- *pēr sollagiṟkil* – If you can recite the divine names.

If it is so effortless \[like just reciting the divine names\], would the benefit also be limited/small?

- *ivaḷaip peṟudirē* – There \[with respect to petty deities\], whatever may be the effort, the benefit is small/nothing; here, the effort is just reciting the divine names, and the benefit is great in redeeming her. If you recite the names, you will get her, otherwise you will lose her.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.6.5. Ivalaip perum parisu

*ivaḷaip peṟum parisu ivvaṇangādudal anṟandō kuvaḷait tadam kaṇṇum kōvaic cevvāyum payandanaḷ kavaḷaik kadāk kaḷiṟatta pirān tirunāmattāl tavaḷap podik koṇḍu nīr ittidumin tanṇiyumē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ivaḷai – she (who is having unsurpassed greatness), her; peṟum – to redeem; parisu – method; i aṇangādudal anṟu – it is not this activity for this dēvatā; andō – alas! (how her disease has worsened!); kuvaḷai tada kaṇṇum – eyes which are dark/large like kuvaḷai (blue-lotus) flower; kōvai sem vāyum – kōvaikkāy (ivy gourd) like reddish lips/mouth; payandanaḷ – lost complexion and have become pale; kavaḷam – (consuming) handful of \[intoxicating\] food; kadām – with water coming out of it’s trunk etc; kaḷiṟu – elephant (named kuvalayāpīdam); atta – killed; pirān – great benefactor’s; tirunāmattāl – by reciting the divine names (to be rid of the hurdles); tavaḷam – pristine; podi – dust of the divine feet; koṇḍu – taking; nīr – you all (who are seeking out even unsuitable ways to cure her disease, due to attachment towards her); ittidumin – offer it quickly (so she can come in contact with it); taṇiyum – (the paleness in her body) will be reduced \[by doing that\]

**Перевод:**

**This activity for this dēvatā is not the method to redeem this parānkuśa nāyaki; alas! her eyes which were dark/large like kuvaḷai (blue-lotus) flower and reddish lips/mouth which are like kōvaikkāy (ivy gourd) have lost their complexion and have become pale; (now the remedy for this is) by taking the pristine dust of the divine feet of those bhāgavatas who are reciting the divine names of kriṣṇa, the great benefactor who killed the elephant which ate handful of \[intoxicating\] food and which has water coming out of it’s trunk etc, and offer it quickly to her (so she can come in contact with it); (the paleness in her body) will be reduced \[by doing that\].**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In fifth pāsuram, parānkuśa nāyaki‘s friend tells a befitting remedy for parānkuśa nāyaki’s disease.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, parānkuśa nāyaki‘s friend says “The remedy you are giving is worsening her disease; you recite the divine names of kriṣṇa who is the eliminator of popular hurdles and apply pure white powder on her”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Fifth pāsuram. parānkuśa nāyaki‘s friend says “The remedy you are giving is worsening her disease; giving that up, please perform a befitting remedy for parānkuśa nāyaki’s disease”. ivaḷaip peṟum parisu ivvaṇangādudal anṟandō kuvaḷait tadam kaṇṇum kōvaic cevvāyum payandanaḷ kavaḷaik kadāk kaḷiṟatta pirān tirunāmattāl tavaḷap podik koṇḍu nīr ittidumin tanṇiyumē*

- *ivaḷāip peṟum parisu ivvaṇangādudal anṟu* – Those who want to redeem this best entity ([parānkuśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)), would they do so through this forbidden/lowly means? Engaging in activities to please this dēvatā will not redeem this distinguished parānkuśa nāyaki.

Since, they did not withdraw from their efforts, even after the friend saying this,

- *andō* – alas! we cannot lose her.

They ask “Do you think we will lose her, even after our efforts?” and she replies “Can’t you see?”,

- *kuvaḷait tadam kaṇṇum kōvaic cevvāyum payandanaḷ* – His \[[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s\] food \[enjoyable aspect\] is being taken away. As said in periya tirumoḻi 3.7.2 “*toṇḍai am sengani vāy nugarndānai*” (emperumān who consumed her reddish fruit like lips) and periya tirumoḻi 8.10.1 “*maṇa nōkkam uṇḍān*” (one who consumed her glance), these are his enjoyable food. She is said as in periya tirumoḻi 2.7.1 “*kuvaḷai am kaṇṇi*” (one who has beautiful eyes like kuvaḷai (dark coloured) flower); kuvaḷai flower like eyes which are far larger than any one can enjoy; she is said as in [tiruvāimoḻi 4.3.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/01/thiruvaimozhi-4-3-1-kovai-vayal/) “*kōvai vāyāḷ*” (reddish lips like kōvai fruit); her kōvai fruit like lips (along with her eyes) became pale. Those limbs which did not become pale even in separation from emperumān, became pale when they came in contact with dēvatāntarams and devotees of such dēvatāntarams.

When they say “Alright, why don’t you suggest the remedy?”, the friend says “You only said previously in tiruviruttam 37 ‘*nedum kālamum kaṇṇan nīḷ malarp pādam paravip peṟṟa iḷamān*‘ (my young child who was born as a result of our lengthy prayer at the divine feet of kriṣṇa); according to this, you should take shelter of kriṣṇa and be cured by him”.

- *kavaḷam* … – Two mistakes have occurred here \[contact with other dēvatās and contact with devotees of other dēvatās\]; you atone in two different ways to remedy those two mistakes \[nāma sankīrtanam and the dust of the divine feet of the devotees of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) respectively are identified as the remedies\]. An elephant which had consumed food and had been intoxicated through certain beverages, was placed in front of him. The great benefactor who killed the kuvalayāpīdam elephant which had water coming out of its body. You try to cure her by the divine names of the one can effortlessly eliminated the strongest of enemies/hurdles.
- *tavaḷap podik koṇḍu* – with the pure dust/powder.
- *nīr* – Should not the persons who assisted her in her sinful deeds \[taking help from dēvatāntarams\] be now bound to assist her in providing atonement for the same?
- *ittidumin* – You apply on her. For her contact with dēvatāntaram, you try to cure that by reciting [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s divine names; for her coming in contact with devotees of those dēvatāntarams, you try to cure her with the dust from the divine feet of śrīvaiṣṇavas.

When they ask “Would this cure her?”, the friend says

- *taṇiyumē* – I guarantee that she will regain consciousness and her original complexion.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.6.6. Taniyum poludillai

*taṇiyum poḻudillai nīraṇangādudir annaimīr piṇiyum oḻiginṟadillai perugum idu allāl maṇiyin aṇi niṟa māyan tamaradi nīṟu koṇḍu aṇiya muyalin maṟṟillai kaṇḍīr ivvaṇangukkē*

**Пословный перевод:**

annaimīr – Oh mothers!; taṇiyum poḻudu – break; inṟi – without; nīr – you all; aṇangādudir – engaging in vorśipping this \[petty\] dēvatā; idu – having this as the reason; piṇiyum – her disease; perugum allāl – is only worsening; oḻiginṟadu illai – not getting cured; maṇiyin – more than a blue jewel; aṇi – unsurpassed, distinguished; niṟam – having complexion; māyan – in the matters of kriṣṇa who is an amazing personality; tamar – bhāgavatas who are well aware of their subordinate relationship with kriṣṇa; adi nīṟu – dust from the divine feet (which was explained as “tavaḷap podi“); koṇḍu aṇiya – to apply on her; muyalin – if you try; i aṇangukku – for this divine natured girl (parānkuśa nāyaki); maṟṟu – another remedy matching this one; illai kaṇḍīr – you would see that it does not exist

**Перевод:**

**Oh mothers! Without break you are all engaging in vorśipping this \[petty\] dēvatā; having that as the reason her disease is only worsening and not getting cured; if you try  to apply on her, dust from the divine feet of bhāgavatas who are well aware of their subordinate relationship with kriṣṇa who is having unsurpassed distinguished complexion more than a blue jewel,you would see that there is no other matching remedy existing for this divine natured girl (parānkuśa nāyaki).**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In sixth pāsuram, parānkuśa nāyaki‘s friend says “If you set out to apply just the dust from the lotus feet of śrīvaiṣṇavas, that will be the remedy; there is no other remedy for her disease”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, parānkuśa nāyaki‘s friend says “By your constant engagement with these other dēvatās, her disease is only worsening and not improving; hence, you set out to apply the dust from the divine feet of bhāgavatas who are related to sarvēśvara, who has distinguished forms”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Sixth pāsuram. parānkuśa nāyaki‘s friend says “These huge efforts are not required; knowing exactly what is said as “tavaḷap podi” and starting to engage with that will cure her disease”. taṇiyum poḻudillai nīraṇangādudir annaimīr piṇiyum oḻiginṟadillai perugum idu allāl maṇiyin aṇi niṟa māyan tamaradi nīṟu koṇḍu aṇiya muyalin maṟṟillai kaṇḍīr ivvaṇangukkē*

- *taṇiyum …* – As there are those who would stop them from engaging in the worship of such petty dēvatā, and since they did not know when they will be asked to stop, they continued their worship without a break.
- *piṇiyum …* – With more engagement in the cause \[association with other dēvatā\], the effect \[disease\] also became worse.
- *perugum idu allāl* – Like an overflowing flood, the disease worsened.
   - *maṇiyin …* – If you set out to apply the dust from the divine feet of devotees of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is having beautiful complexion as that of a blue jewel, is amazing due to his qualities and activities. Since this is a mistake which happened to the one who is born in viśiśta (prapanna) kulam (the clan of surrendered persons, which is most disciplined), we suggested the atonement with great intent; but if you look at the greatness of the process \[dust from the divine feet of bhāgavatas\], just starting to pursue it in itself is sufficient. kulaśēkara āḻvār too said in perumāḷ tirumoḻi 2.2 “*toṇḍaradip podi Ada nām peṟil gangai nīr kudaindādadum vētkai ennāvadē*” (When we can bathe in the dust from the divine feet of devotees of [śrīman nārāyaṇan](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), why    would we have the desire to bathe in gangā?). ahirbhudnya samhitā 37.27 and 37.28 “ānukūlyasya sankalpa: prātikūlyasya varjanam … ” (six aspects of śaraṇāgati are explained in these ślōkams, the first two being – vowing to act favourably and refraining from unfavourable acts) – for favourable aspects just vowing to engage is sufficient \[here to accept the dust from the divine feet of the devotees, just the vow is sufficient\], but for unfavourable aspects, one must physically give those up.
- *māyan tamar adi nīṟu koṇḍu* – Recollect piḷḷai uṟangā villi dāsar’s remedy for his nephews vaṇḍar and soṇḍar when they were misled by the king. That is – when agaḷanga nāttāḻvān mischievously showed vaṇḍar and soṇḍar the lions placed on the towers of a jain temple and told them “*tirumuṟṟam; tiruvadi toḻungōḷ*” (this is a divine abode of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/); offer your obeisances), they believed him to be telling the truth and at once offered obeisance. But soon they realized that it was a jain temple and fell unconscious. Hearing about the situation, piḷḷai uṟangā villi dāsar \[arrived there and\] applied the dust from his divine feet on their heads and they regained consciousness. \[nampiḷḷai says\] When nanjīyar was explaining this pāsuram in a protected area near the tirukkottāram (store room) \[During dangerous times, lectures are given in secluded/secret locations\], when this line was explained by him, I asked “When the cause for the disease is explained as ‘[*tērppāganārkku*](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/03/thiruvaimozhi-4-6-1-thirpparai-yam/)*‘* (for kriṣṇa, the charioteer), why is ‘*māyan tamar adi nīṟu koṇḍu aṇiya muyalin*‘ (if you try to apply the dust from the divine feet of the devotees of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)) explained as the remedy?”. He mercifully explained “When a person with some disease cannot consume curd which is the medicine, he will first be given dry ginger to prepare him and will then be given curd. Since, when “[*tērppāganārkku*](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/03/thiruvaimozhi-4-6-1-thirpparai-yam/)” was said, she could not bring emperumān there, so initially, she is pacified by applying the dust from the divine feet and will subsequently be shown [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)“.
- *maṇiyin …* – She became unconscious thinking about emperumān’s saundaryam (beauty), śeelam (simplicity) etc; you too bring the dust from the lotus feet of the śrīvaiṣṇavas who are captivated by emperumān’s beauty, simplicity etc., and try to give the remedy for her. The disease will break into pieces; when the *podi* (dust) is applied, the disease will be cured.
- *maṟṟa* … – For [parānkuśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) who is distinguished to be cured only by this remedy, you try to apply only this as the remedy.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.6.7. Anangukku

*aṇangukkarumarundenṟu angōr ādum kaḷḷum parāyc cuṇangai eṟindu num tōḷ kulaikkap padum annaimīr! uṇangal kedak kaḻudai udadāttam kaṇḍu en payan? vaṇangīrgaḷ māyap pirān tamar vēdam vallāraiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

annaimīr – Oh mothers!; aṇangukku – for this divine daughter of yours; aru marundu enṟu – considering to be a rare medicine; angu – for the other dēvatā; ōr ādum – to cut a goat, the act of which is prohibited; kaḷḷum – to offer alcohol; parāy – praying; suṇangai eṟindu – having goose bumps; num tōḷ – your shoulders; kulaikka – swaying; padum – occurred; uṇangal – paddy which is being dried; keda – to be wasted; kaḻudai – donkey’s (which is eating that paddy); udadu āttam – the lips that are chewing; kaṇḍu – watching; en payan – what is the benefit?; māyam – amazing qualities and activities; pirān – the benefactor who manifested them to her and let her enjoy them; tamar – devotees; vēdam vallārai – bhāgavatas who are best among vaidikas (knowledgeable in vēdam and practicing the principles); vaṇangīrgaḷ – start vorśipping them

**Перевод:**

**Oh mothers! What is the benefit of your praying to the other dēvatā to cut a goat, the act of which is prohibited and to offer alcohol, considering these acts to be a rare medicine? Your body is having goose bumps and your shoulders are swaying; what is the benefit of watching the donkey’s lips which are chewing the paddy which is being dried while it (paddy) is being wasted (similarly, as she is losing her existence, the engagement with the other dēvatā is of no benefit)? You start vorśipping the bhāgavatas who are best among vaidikas and who are the devotees of emperumān, the benefactor who manifested his amazing qualities and activities to her and let her enjoy those.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In seventh pāsuram, parānkuśa nāyaki‘s friend says “If you take shelter of other dēvatās, that will only lead to her destruction; if you want to save her, take shelter of śrīvaiṣṇavas”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. aṇangukkarumarundenṟu angōr ādum kaḷḷum parāyc cuṇangai eṟindu num tōḷ kulaikkap padum annaimīr! uṇangal kedak kaḻudai udadāttam kaṇḍu en payan? vaṇangīrgaḷ māyap pirān tamar vēdam vallāraiyē*

- *aṇangukku aru marundu enṟu* – aṇangu – divine girl. tamiḻ meaning “*sūrum aṇangum deyvap peṇ peyar*” (divine girl is called sūru and aṇangu). Considering it to be a matching and rare medicine for her divine nature. Neither you know her distinguished nature nor you understand the lowly nature of your activity.
- *angu ōr ādum kaḷḷum parāy* – Offering forbidden \[food\] items. parāy – prārtana (prayer).
- *tuṇangai eṟindu* – tuṇangai is a type of dance. eṟidal – offering/performing. Engaging in a particular type of dance. *tuṇangaik kūttu* means a type of dance with clapping of hands – here that may also be highlighted; there is a type of dance where they throw turmeric powder at each other – that may also be highlighted here \[tuṇangai eṟindu is an accepted variation in the pāsuram, for cuṇangai eṟindu\] .
- *num tōḷ* … – You who know very well that even an anjali (joined palms) performed towards [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is considered to be great due to the simplicity of śaraṇyan (one who gives shelter), have engaged in such lowly activities. [āḻvārs](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/azhwars/) think that “*toḻudu … eḻudum ennum idu migai*” (\[devotees\] offering obeisances and rising are considered too much \[for [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) to handle due to his overwhelming attachment for them\]).
- *uṇangal* … – The paddy \[which is to be turned into rice\] which is the source of sustenance is eaten away by a donkey – what is the benefit of watching the donkey’s mouth/lips chewing the paddy? Similarly, you who have to sustain yourself by having her alive, are letting her become destroyed by engaging in activities with those who are the devotees of other dēvatās – what is the benefit in doing that? Not only is there no benefit, it also leads to her destruction. Alternative explanation given by aiyan tirukkurugaip perumāḷ araiyar – uṇangal – suffering. To eliminate her suffering; kaḻudu – ghost. When you offer the goat and alcohol to the ghost \[which has entered her body – according to you\], and when it consumes those food items, what is the benefit of watching it chew on them? tamiḻ scholars explain in nigaṇḍu (dictionary) “*kaḻudum pēyum paraṇum*” (kaḻudu, pēy, paraṇ are synonyms for ghost).

If there is no benefit in these activities, tell us what will bestow us the benefit.

- *vaṇangīrgaḷ* – Try to fall at their divine feet.

Who are “they”?

- *māyap pirān …* –  The śrīvaiṣṇavas who are engaged in the qualities of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who has amazing qualities and activities. As said in śrī bhagavat gītā 15.15 “*vēdaiśca sarvair ahamēva vēdya:*” (All of the vēdams reveal about me only), katavalli upaniśat 1.2.5 “*sarvē vēdā yatraikam bhavanti*” (the supreme lord about whom all vēdams talk in unison) and śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 1.14.23 “*natāssmasarvavacasām pratiśtā yatraśāsvatī*” (we worship gōvinda who is the essence of all words), those who have understood the essence of vēdam. What is meaning of this adjective “*vēdam vallāraiyē*” (only those who are expert in vēdam)? [parānkuśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s friend set out to highlight the remedy for being treated by the devotees of other dēvatā; while doing that she says fall at the divine feet of those who feel “Without emperumān, no dēvatā has independent capability; He is the only goal”. Instead of falling at the feet of those who think “each dēvatā has its own duties”, take shelter of those who think that all words are ultimately indicating emperumān.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

adiyen saraty ramanuja dasan

## 4.6.8. Vedam vallargalai

*vēdam vallārgaḷaik koṇḍu viṇṇōr perumān tirup pādam paṇindu ivaḷ nōy idu tīrttuk koḷḷādu pōy ēdam paṟaindu alla seydu kaḷḷudu kalāyttūyk kīdamuḻavittu nīr aṇangādudal kīḻmaiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vēdam vallārgaḷai – bhāgavatas who are experts in the essence of all vēdams; koṇḍu – having them (as puruśakāram (recommendation)); viṇṇōr perumān – sarvēśvaran who is vorśipped by nityasūris, his; tiru pādam – divine feet which are most enjoyable; paṇindu – surrendering; ivaḷ – (greatly distinguished) parānkuśa nāyaki‘s; idu nōy – this disease which is different \[from other diseases\] in this world; tīrttuk koḷḷādu – instead of curing it; pōy – going (towards other dēvatās as their devotees); ēdam – the words indicating other dēvatās (which hurt the true nature of self); paṟaindu – speaking; alla seydu – engaging in forbidden activities towards them; ūdu – in between; kaḷ – surā (alcohol); kalāy – mix; tūy – throwing/offering; gīdam – matching the songs (glorifying them); muḻavu ittu – making noises with musical instruments; nīr – you (who are related to her); aṇangu ādudal – dancing, being possessed by those dēvatās; kīḻmaiyē – is an insult (for your family heritage)

**Перевод:**

**Instead of curing parānkuśa nāyaki‘s disease which is different in this world, by having bhāgavatas who are experts in the essence of all vēdams as puruśakāram and surrendering unto the divine feet of sarvēśvaran, you are going towards other dēvatās as their devotees, speaking the words indicating other dēvatās and engaging in forbidden activities towards them; in between, you are also throwing/offering the mix of alcohol and making noises with musical instruments matching the songs (glorifying them) and are dancing being possessed by those dēvatās – these acts of yours are an insult (for your family heritage).**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In eighth pāsuram, parānkuśa nāyaki‘s friend says “Instead of having śrīvaiṣṇavas as puruśakāram (recommendation), surrendering unto the divine feet of sarvēśvaran and curing her disease, taking shelter of kśudra dēvatās (petty deities) will lead to your being considered inferior”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. vēdam vallārgaḷaik koṇḍu viṇṇōr perumān tirup pādam paṇindu ivaḷ nōy idu tīrttuk koḷḷādu pōy ēdam paṟaindu alla seydu kaḷḷudu kalāyttūyk kīdamuḻavittu nīr aṇangādudal kīḻmaiyē*

- *vēdam vallārgaḷaik koṇḍu* – Pursuing those who have mastered the essence of vēdam that is “sarvēśvara is the prāpya (goal) and prāpaka (means)”. As said in nānumugan tiruvantādi 18 “*vēṟāga ētti iruppārai vellumē maṟṟavaraic cārtti iruppār tavam*” (those (group A) who are surrendered to the vaiṣṇavas (group B) who constantly praise [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) in a distinguished manner – the stature of group A will be greater than that of group B), if one falls at the divine feet of such śrivasihṇavas, the disease will be cured. But it is difficult to acquire that faith \[to be fully surrendered to śrīvaiṣṇavas\]; since we consider them to be equal mortals like ourselves, great attachment and faith towards them are difficult to achieve; hence, you consider them \[at least\] as puruśakāram (recommendation) and surrender unto emperumān. For the days we are in this material realm, mumukśus \[those who are desirous of mōkśam\] are present for puruśakāram; in the spiritual realm, nityasūris are present for puruśakāram. As said in cāndōjña upaniśat 4.15 “*sa ēnān brahma gamayati*” (That amānava brings the muktātmās to bhagavān), with their help only one enters the divine assembly \[in parampadam\]. With the help of those who have understood \[and practice\] the essence of vēdam.
- *viṇṇōr perumān tiruppādam paṇindu* – Bowing at the divine feet of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is the lord of nityasūris, who is said in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.1.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/03/thiruvaimozhi-1-1-1-uyarvara-uyarnalam/) as “*ayarvaṟum amarargaḷ adipati*” (the singular lord of the nityasūris who have no faults).
- *ivaḷ nōy idu tīrttuk koḷḷādu* – She ([parānkuśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)) is the one who is having the disease and the disease is this \[suffering in separation due to deep devotion\]; instead of engaging in a remedy which is suitable for these.
- *pōy* – Venturing into a remedy which is too distant for our nature and unsuitable for our stature.
- *ēdam paṟaindu* – Speaking those words which cause you blemish.
- *alla seydu* – Engaging in activities which are forbidden.
- *kaḷ ūdu kalāyt tūy* – Spreading the lowly/forbidden alcohol everywhere in the home. dēvatāntara sparśam (coming in contact with other dēvatās) is like coming in contact \[or consuming\] forbidden foods or beverages. Since it is saying “*viṇṇōr perumān tiruppādam paṇindu ivaḷ nōy idu tīrttuk koḷḷādu*” (Instead of surrendering unto the lord of nityasūris and curing her disease) here, even trying to attain him using the means which includes ahankāram (ego) and mamakāram (doer-ship), instead of attaining [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) through himself, is considered to be the same as vorśipping dēvatāntarams \[or consuming forbidden foods/beverages\]. [parānkuśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is suggesting the top-most medicine and that is what is ignored by the relatives of parānkuśa nāyaki .
- *gīdam …* – Playing musical instruments with forbidden songs.
- *nīr* … –  You who have to say as in tiruvāimoḻi 10.8.7 “*uṇḍu kaḷittēṟkumbar en kuṟai*” (For us who have enjoyed this, is there anything left to be enjoyed in paramapadam?) after enjoying bhagavān’s qualities, are now engaged in vorśipping these \[lowly\] dēvatās.
- *kīḻmaiyē* – This is very lowly/insulting. This insult would not stop at you but would also harm the reputation of your descendants.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.6.9. Kilmaiyinal

*kīḻmaiyināl angu ōr kīḻ magan itta muḻavin kīḻ nāḻmai pala solli nīr aṇangādum poy kāṇgilēn ēḻmaip piṟappukkum sēmam innōykkum īdē marundu ūḻmaiyil kaṇṇa pirān kaḻal vāḻttumin unnittē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kīḻmaiyināl – lowliness (due to non-definability); angu ōr – one who cannot be explained as “He is from this place, of this nature”; kīḻmagan – lowly person; itta – promoted by; muḻavin kīḻ – playing the musical instruments; nāḻmai pala – praising the greatness of other dēvatās in many ways; solli – speaking; nīr – you all; aṇangu ādum – engaged in vorśipping those dēvatās being engrossed in them; poy – useless activity; kāṇgilēn – I cannot witness; ēḻmaip piṟappukkum – (as said in “saptasaptacasaptaca” (twenty one births)), all births which can be one among the seven types; sēmam – comforting; īdē – this; innōykkum marundu – the medicine for this disease; ūḻmaiyil – befitting the true nature of self and following the ancient practice; kaṇṇapirān – kriṣṇa who is a benefactor through his saulabhyam (simplicity); kaḻal – divine feet; unnittu – meditating upon; vāḻttumin – perform mangaḷāśāsanam (wishing well)

**Перевод:**

**I cannot witness you all speaking about and praising the greatness of other dēvatās in many ways such as playing the musical instruments, which are promoted by a lowly person whose lowliness cannot be explained as “He is from this place, of this nature” and engaged in the useless activity of vorśipping those dēvatās, being engrossed in them;  befitting the true nature of self and following the ancient practice, you perform mangaḷāśāsanam to the divine feet of kriṣṇa who is a benefactor through his saulabhyam; this is the comforting aspect for all births which can be one among the seven types and the medicine for this disease.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In ninth pāsuram, parānkuśa nāyaki‘s friend says “I cannot witness your worship of this petty dēvatā, which does not lead to any benefit; if you want parānkuśa nāyaki to be saved, you think about kriṣṇa’s divine feet and perform mangaḷāśāsanam to them”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. kīḻmaiyināl angu ōr kīḻ magan itta muḻavin kīḻ nāḻmai pala solli nīr aṇangādum poy kāṇgilēn ēḻmaip piṟappukkum sēmam innōykkum īdē marundu ūḻmaiyil kaṇṇa pirān kaḻal vāḻttumin unnittē*

- *kīḻmaiyināl* – Due to your lowly nature. Being lowly in their case is, being consumed by rajō guṇam (passion) and tamō guṇam (ignorance). It is due to this reason, they are engaged in such \[inferior\] activities.
- *angu ōr* … – Playing the musical instruments which are promoted by a caṇḍāḷa (very lowly person) who cannot be said “He is from this place, of this nature” \[his identity, nature are not worthy of discussion\].
- *nāḻmai pala solli* – nāḻmai – faults; praising those dēvatās with non-existing greatness in them. They would praise those dēvatās saying “He did this, he did that” as sarvēsvaran is \[naturally\] glorified as in [tiruvāimoḻi 4.5.10](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/02/thiruvaimozhi-4-5-10-undum-umizhndhum/) “*uṇḍum umiḻndum kadandum idandum*” ([emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) placed the world in \[his\] stomach, spat it out, measured it and placed it under his foot, lifted it up, laid down \[as śrī rāma\]). nāḻ indicates faults, speaking of non-existing greatness and considering oneself to be great.
- *nīr* … – Your fake engagement being possessed by this dēvatā does not appear as a \[worthy\] matter for me. As said in katavalli upaniśat 2.4.11 “*nēhanānāsti kincana*” (There is no plurality of entities), only when one considers “any other dēvatā has existence independent of [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)“, can think that their act is in line with truth.

The relatives ask “If you consider our acts to be fake, until when will your prediction/suggestion be true?”. She replies,

- *ēḻmaip piṟappukkum sēmam* – When something good happens, it is usually multiplied by 7 and presented. This is the protection in all births. “*ēḻmaip piṟappu*” is also explained as lowly birth – i.e., it is the protection even in lowly births.

They ask “Are we seeking for protection in our births? Are we not simply seeking the cure for her disease? Why are you speaking about some thing other than that?”, she says “After having the grass cut by one person, do we seek some one else to organize it?”,

- *innōykkum īdē marundu* – This is the medicine which holds on to the divine feet of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/). ūḻmaiyil – in proper way. Instead of what you are doing now, this process is done as per the norms.
- *kaṇṇa pirān …* – Praise and sing mangaḷāśāsanam to the divine feet of kriṣṇa. This medicine is very worthy.

While doing that,

- *unnittu* – As said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 1.17.78 “*smrutōyaccatiśōpanam*” (As soon as one thinks about [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/), bhagavān brings auspiciousness to them), all of you together meditate and perform mangaḷāśāsanam to him. By doing this, it will be the protection for all births; and the cure for her disease too; it is also done in the proper way.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.6.10. Unnittu

*unnittu maṟṟoru deyvam toḻāḷ avanai allāl num iccai solli num tōḷ kulaikkap padum annaimīr! mannap padu maṟai vāṇanai vaṇ tuvarāpati mannanai ēttumin ēttudalum toḻudādumē*

**Пословный перевод:**

avanai allāl – other than him (kriṣṇa); maṟṟu oru deyvam – any other dēvatā; unnittu – meditate upon; toḻāḷ – will not worship; annaimīr – Oh mothers you have given birth to her (being bewildered due to having attachment towards her)!; num iccai – your desires; solli – explained; num tōḷ – your shoulders (which are to be engaged in service to bhagavān); kulaikka – to be engaged in (worship of other dēvatās); padum – occurred; manna – eternally; padum – thought about (in heart); maṟai vāṇanai – who is exclusively explained in vēdam; vaṇ tuvarāpati mannanai – kriṣṇa who is the emperor of śrīmad dvārakā; ēttumin – praise; ēttudalum – being awakened at the time of such praising; toḻudu – pray (unto him); ādum – will dance with excitement

**Перевод:**

**parānkuśa nāyaki will not meditate upon and worship any dēvatā other than kriṣṇa. Oh mothers you have given birth to her! You have explained your desires and have your shoulders to be engaged in (worship of other dēvatās); you praise kriṣṇa who is the emperor of śrīmad dvārakā and who is exclusively explained in vēdam which eternally is thought about in the heart. Being awakened at the time of such praising, she will pray (unto him) and will dance with excitement.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In tenth pāsuram, parānkuśa nāyaki‘s friend says “Considering parānkuśa nāyaki‘s exclusive attachment to kriṣṇa’s divine feet, you perform mangaḷāśāsanam to him; by doing so, she will be saved”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. unnittu maṟṟoru deyvam toḻāḷ avanai allāl num iccai solli num tōḷ kulaikkap padum annaimīr! mannap padu maṟai vāṇanai vaṇ tuvarāpati mannanai ēttumin ēttudalum toḻudādumē*

- *unnittu maṟṟoṟu deyvam toḻāḷ avanai allāl* – Is there not a remedy based on the type of the person? Should that not be known and applied accordingly? Your act is like, if one gets hurt in the knee, he is being treated in the nose for that. ṣouldn’t you know that “She cannot handle coming in contact with other dēvatās”? She has never vorśipped any other dēvatā before. As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam bāla kāṇḍam 18.27 “*bālyāt prabruti susnigda:*” (right from the cradle stage lakśmaṇa was a dear friend of śrī rāma), even in the infant stage when children will see moon with reverence, she never revered the moon \[or any other dēvatās\] too. Even in that stage, her conduct was to your amazement as said in tiruviruttam 60 “*mulaiyō muḻu muṟṟum pōndila … perumān malaiyō tiruvēnkatam enṟu kaṟkinṟa vāsagam – ivaḷ paramē*” (her nature is such that –  \[when she was so young that\] when her breasts were not developed, etc., she was always focussed on speaking about the divine hill abode of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), i.e., tiruvēnkatam); now, would she disregard the mountain \[of tiruvēnkatam\] and pursue a bundle of chaff? \[nampiḷḷai explains śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 28.12 ślōkam here to establish that she does not look out for any other dēvatā even in dire situations\]
   - *ananya daivatvam* (there is no other god) – \[sītā says\] I cannot even think “There is another dēvatā who is the refuge. He will protect”. Even while accompanying śrī rāma to assist him as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam “*saha patnyā*” (chaste wife who is accompanying), while he worships periya perumāḷ, I would accompany him only to assist him and would not even look at periya perumāḷ \[periya perumāḷ was known as nārāyaṇa before and was vorśipped by the raghu dynasty kings in ayōdyā, until the period of śrī rāma\].
   - *iyamkśamāca* – I tolerated the words of rāvaṇa and the tortures of the rākśasis (demoniac assistants of rāvaṇa) thinking that “One day, I will hear his (śrī rāma’s) sweet words”.
   - *bhūmau caśayyā* – Even resting on ground here is due to longing to lay down in his lap one day as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 38.12 “*tavāngēsamupāviśam*” (I rested on your lap). “*niyamaśca darmē*” – since I considered “my protection is his duty”, I remained steadfast in that faith. I said “*natvā kurmidaśagrīva bhasmabhasmārhatējasā*” (Oh ten headed rāvaṇa! Even though I have the power to burn you down to ashes with my chastity) seeing \[knowing\] śrī rāma. *pativratātvam* (my chastity) is based on śrī rāma’s vow śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 18.33 “*ētat vratam mama*” (This is my vow) and I have never thought of vowing myself and destroying these.
   - *vipalam mamētam* – Even his firm vow became shaken \[in my case, in not protecting me yet\]. As in the case of, “*mānuśāṇam krutagnēśu krutamiva”* – Even for śrī rāma who said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 120.11 “*ātmānam mānuśam manyē*” (I am also a human), there are human qualities; it happened in śrī rāma’s case as it would happen in others’ case. \[But\] his firm vow failed \[in my case\] – what is the reason for that? *mamētam* – It is not his fault, but must be my fault only.
- *num iccai solli* – Telling what you desire. If you look at the underlying principle or if you see her \[nature\], you can understand that coming in contact with other dēvatās is unsuitable for her. This being the case, you have to be informed about your obstacles.
- *num tōḷ kulaikka* – Are you so emotional to be engaged in the worship of other dēvatās? Would people of good conduct \[devotees\] engage in activities of people of bad conduct \[those who have no attachment towards [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)\]?  Don’t you usually say as in mudal tiruvantādi 63 “*tōḷ avanai allāl toḻā*” (my shoulders/hands will not pray anyone other than bhagavān).

When they ask “So, what is to be done?”, [parānkuśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s friend,

- *mannap padu maṟai vāṇanai* – Try to surrender unto [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is explained fully in vēdam. Should you pursue the methods explained in āgamas (religious texts for temple worship)? \[*mannap padu maṟai*\] *mannugai* – comes by abhyāsa (practice); learned from teachers through proper training; alternatively – it also means, \[vēdam\] being eternal \[with no beginning/end\], not having the defects such as vipralambha (deceit) etc due to not having originated from the minds of individuals, and coming by the ways of previous recitals heard and recited by others \[and propagated thereof\]. [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is having the greatness of being revealed by the eternal vēdam.
- *vaṇ tuvarāpati mannanai* – Instead of just being hear-say, one who incarnated to be physically perceived and enjoyed \[as the lord of dvārakā\]. Just as someone drowned in water is brought back to conscious state by sprinkling water on that person’s face, you try to awaken [parānkuśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) who fainted thinking about the tērppāgan (kaṇṇan emperumān as the charioteer for arjuna), by reciting the divine names of vaṇ tuvarāpati mannan \[lord of śrī dvārākā\].
- *ēttumin* – To fulfil the purpose of being provided the mouth, you praise him. Don’t you say as in periya tiruvantādi 52 “*sīr paravādu uṇṇa, vāy tānuṟumō onṟu*” (Will my mouth desire for consuming anything other than [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s divine qualities?).
- *ēttudalum* – Not only will you be satisfied, she will also be awakened immediately after such praising of emperumān as said in taittirīya upaniśat “*atasōbhayngatō bhavati*” ([ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) then becomes fearless).
- *toḻudādumē* – Once she regains conscious, this is what she will do. She will gain the strength to sustain herself and dance with joy.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.6.11. Toludadi

*toḻudādit tūmaṇi vaṇṇanukku ātceydu nōy tīrnda vaḻuvāda tol pugaḻ vaṇ kurugūrc catakōpan sol vaḻuvāda āyirattuḷ ivai pattu veṟigaḷum toḻudādip pāda vallār dukka seelam ilargaḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

toḻudu – performing anjali (joined palms – which befits the śēśatva (servitude)); ādi – (out of that joy) dancing up and down; tū maṇi – resembling a radiant blue jewel; vaṇṇanukku – kriṣṇa who is having such complexion; āḷ seydu – doing this as kainkaryam (service); nōy tīrnda – to cure the disease of sorrow of separation from emperumān; vaḻuvāda – without faults (of any contact with other dēvatās in any manner); tol pugaḻ – one who is having the greatness of natural servitude( towards bhagavān; vaṇ kurugūr – the leader of distinguished āḻvārtirunagari; satakōpan – nammāḻvār; sol – mercifully spoken by; vaḻuvāda – revealing without missing any aspect of bhagavat svarūrpam etc; āyirattuḷ – among thousand pāsurams; veṟigaḷ – sang to eliminate the worship of dēvatās; ivai pattum – this decad; toḻudu – vorśipping (being engrossed in the meanings and becoming blissful); ādi – dance; pāda – sing (out of overwhelming love); vallār – experts; dukkam – sorrow born out of separation from bhagavān and the sorrow caused by vorśipping dēvatās as a remedy to cure such suffering; seelam – character; ilargaḷ – will be devoid of

**Перевод:**

**nammāḻvār, the faultless leader of distinguished āḻvārtirunagari,  who has no faults and who is performing anjali and dancing up and down, towards kriṣṇa who is having divine complexion resembling a radiant blue jewel, doing all of these as kainkaryam (service) to cure the disease in the form of sorrow of separation from emperumān. Such nammāḻvār explains the ways to eliminate the worshiping of other dēvatās in this decad among these thousand pāsurams revealing without missing any aspect of bhagavat svarūrpam etc. Those who are experts in such decad who can pray, dance and sing this decad will attain the character of being free from sorrow born out of separation from emperumān and sorrow caused by pursuing other dēvatās.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the end, āḻvār says “Those who recite/practice this decad with their heart’s involvement, will not suffer in separation from emperumān that I suffered”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār mercifully explains the fruits of this decad saying “Those who recite this decad being emotionally charged with love will be free from the sorrow of separation from bhagavān“.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. toḻudādit tūmaṇi vaṇṇanukku ātceydu nōy tīrnda vaḻuvāda tol pugaḻ vaṇ kurugūrc catakōpan sol vaḻuvāda āyirattuḷ ivai pattu veṟigaḷum toḻudādip pāda vallār dukka seelam ilargaḷē*

- *toḻudu ādit tūmaṇi vaṇṇanukku ātceydu nōy tīrnda* – For this, ammangi ammāḷ \[a disciple of bhagavad rāmānuja\] explains – When an unconscious person regains consciousness slightly, others will say “she drank curd, stabilized herself, opened her eyes and spoke a few words”; similarly, here also done \[that parānkuśa nāyaki prayed, danced, sang etc\]. Due to the previously experienced great grief, even the awakening is rejoiced greatly; since next decad is “*seelamillāc ciṟiyēn*” (very humble person with no good qualities), she only regained as much consciousness as required to be called out.
- *toḻudu* … – even this friend of parānkuśa nāyaki does not understand [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s greatness; she told others to praise [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/); but for parānkuśa nāyaki to be awakened even that is not required and just her telling others to praise him is sufficient. Just as outsiders will not understand bhagavān’s greatness, even those who are insiders find it difficult to comprehend his greatness.
- *vaḻuvāda tol pugaḻ* – Even in unconscious/bewildered state, dēvatāntara sparśam (contact with other dēvatās) and tadīya sparśam (contact with the devotees of other dēvatās) lead to destruction of one’s existence and even in such state, [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s names and tadīya sparśam (contact with devotees of bhagavān) lead to sustaining oneself – greatness of being situated in such śrīvaiṣṇavaśrī. This is what makes one a vaiṣṇava; after hearing the instruction “sarvēśvaran is rakśaka (protector)” \[based on dvayam or carama ślōkam\] from some one (i.e., ācārya), if one comes in contact with other dēvatās and abhāgavatas (non-devotees), one cannot be called as vaiṣṇava. If one meditates upon the first half of dvayam, one cannot engage in any self-effort \[even cutting grass\]; if one meditates upon the second half of dvayam, one cannot even sleep for a moment like iḷaiya perumāḷ \[lakśmaṇa who accompanied śrī rāma and served him\]. One’s state would be as explained in tiruviruttam 97 “*kaḻivadōr kādal uṟṟārkkum uṇḍō kaṇgaḷ tunjudal*” (For one who is very attached to [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/), can he/she even sleep for a moment?”. When one realizes “this is the svarūpam (true nature)”, if the activities befitting that svarūpam are not pursued and if the obstacles for such activities are not avoided, it implies that true knowledge has not dawned in that person. If one does not follow this fully, he cannot be said to be following the path of āḻvārs; āḻvārs’ nature is explained in nānmugan tiruvantādi 68 “*tiruvadi than nāmam maṟandum puṟam toḻā māndar*” (A śrīvaiṣṇava may even forget emperumān’s name, but will never worship other dēvatās), nānmugan tiruvantādi 53 “*tiruvillāt tēvarait tēṟēnmin dēvu*” (I will not consider a dēvatā who is without śrī mahālakśmi as dēvatā), periya tirumoḻi 11.6.7 “*eṇṇāda mānidattai eṇṇāda pōdellām iniyavāṟu*” (It is pleasing whenever I don’t think about those who don’t think about [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)), periya tirumoḻi 7.4.4 “*pērāḷan pērōdum periyōrai orukālum pirigilēn*” (I will never separate from those great personalities who recite the names of the great lord). Should one at least not do this, being grateful to be freed from sins which were carried out since time immemorial and to attain eternal kainkaryam?
- *vaḻuvāda* *āyirattuḷ* … – This decad which explains all the principles that are to be known by the [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/), without missing any aspect and which relate to veṟi (removing the attachment towards other dēvatās\].  In tamiḻ culture, there is a tradition named “*veṟi vilakku*“; when a girl is suffering from viraha jvaram (fever of separation from her beloved), the relatives would start engaging a psychic reader in cutting goat, offering alcohol and sacrifices, and a friend of the girl would say “This is a disease which occurred due to attachment with her beloved and not because of anything else” and stop their activities.
- *toḻudu ādip pāda vallār* – As the relatives would feel rejoice on having the bewilderment of the girl eliminated, the same joy would be present for those who learn this decad – that is how āḻvār feels.
- *dukka seelam ilargaḷē* – The sorrow is – coming in contact with other dēvatās and losing contact with bhāgavatas, when being bewildered. They will acquire the character of not having such sorrow. seelam – svabhāvam (character).

## 4.7 Seelamillac ciriyan

## 4.7.1. Seelamillac ciriyan

*seelam illāc ciṟiyanēlum seyvinaiyō peridāl jñālam uṇḍāy jñān mūrttī! nārāyaṇā! enṟenṟu kālam tōṟum yānirundu kaitalai pūsalittāl kōla mēni kāṇa vārāy kūvyium koḷḷāyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

jñālam – all entities \[of the world\]; uṇḍāy – consumed and protected them; jñānam – having distinguished knowledge to protect such world; mūrttī – Oh emperumān who is an embodiment \[of such knowledge\]!; nārāyaṇā – Oh one who is having the inseparable relationship to know the means for protection!; enṟenṟu – repeatedly speaking about your characteristics; kālam tōṟum – at all times without any break; yān – I (who will cease to exist in separation from you); irundu – staying with grief (with the desire to see you); kaitalai pūsalittāl – calling out loudly with my hand on my head \[a sign of great sorrow\]; kōlam mēni – your physical form which is very attractive to see; kāṇa – to be seen by me; vārāy – you are not coming; kūviyum koḷḷāy – you did not call me to your place either; seelam illāc ciṟiyanēlum – Even though I am ignorant and lowly without any good background; seyvinai – sins committed by physical actions (unlike you creation of the worlds by your divine vow, mine are committed by bodily engagement in sins)

**Перевод:**

**Oh emperumān who is an embodiment of distinguished knowledge by consuming and protecting all entities! Oh one who is having the inseparable relationship to know the means for protection! repeatedly speaking about your characteristics, at all times without any break, I am calling out loudly with my hand on my head; \[but\] you are not coming to show your physical form which is very attractive to see; you did not call me to your place either; even though I am ignorant and lowly without any good background, sins accrued by my actions are very great.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In first pāsuram, āḻvār says “What abundance of sins committed by me which make you not accept me even after calling out for a long time?”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. seelam illāc ciṟiyanēlum seyvinaiyō peridāl jñālam uṇḍāy jñān mūrttī! nārāyaṇā! enṟenṟu kālam tōṟum yānirundu kaitalai pūsalittāl kōla mēni kāṇa vārāy kūvyium koḷḷāyē*

- *seelam illā* – seelam means goodness. That is vruttam (good conduct). Good conduct is indicated by the word seelam. It is not that I have anything good in me now, but I have no basis for having any future goodness in me.
- *siṟiyanēlum* – ātmā is miniscule in nature and its jñānam is all-pervading \[in the bodies where the ātmā can reach out\]; due to the sorrow, having the all-pervasive nature subdued, ātmā \[[āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)\] merely existed \[as a miniscule entity\]. Even though I am very small without any goodness now and not having any basis to acquire goodness in the future.
- *sey vinaiyō peridāl* – \[But\] looking at the accrued sins, it appears that it has grown over and above the [three entities](http://ponnadi.blogspot.com/p/thathva-thrayam.html) namely [cit](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) (sentient entities), [acit](http://ponnadi.blogspot.in/2013/03/thathva-thrayam-achith-what-is-matter.html) (insentient entities) and īśvara ([bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)) and consumes all 3 of them. It appears to have become bigger than īśvara’s qualities which tolerate samsāris (materialistic people) and the knowledge in the form of devotion which was bestowed by [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/); \[this is because\] even that knowledge is useless and even while his qualities are manifested, my sins are accumulating. In this world tatva trayam (the collection of three entities) is huge; greater than that is [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s jñānam; the greatness of his sins is bigger than such jñānam.
- *sey vinai* – These were physically committed by one unlike emperumān’s sankalapam \[which occurs just by his thinking about those\].
- *O* – How amazing! Also explained as [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s great sorrow being revealed in this \[as “alas!”\]. When asked “If he can be awakened just by the discussion on divine names, what sins does he have?” – It is that \[time immemorial\] sin which causes him to miss out on the experience to his heart’s content such [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) who makes him sustain himself. sītā pirātti too said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 38.48 “*mamaiva duśkrutam kincit mahadasti …*” (My little bit abundant sins are the cause for my current situation even while śrī rāma and lakśmaṇa who could protect me were present). They (śrī rāma and lakśmaṇa) are capable of completely uprooting all the enemies and protecting me; they grew up strong and made their enemies bite the dust previously; and I am suffering so much that they should have protected me even at the cost of themselves; this being the case, they did not mercifully glance at me \[and protect me\]; the reason for this is due to some fault \[sins\] either in them or in me; I cannot find any fault in them; so this must be my own sins. “*kincit*” – as we are not sarvajña (omniscient) to know everything, there should be some sin in us which we are not aware off; this must be deduced by the result \[suffering we are going through now\].
- *jñālam uṇḍāy* – When contemplating on the abundance of sins, those who depend on self efforts will start thinking about atonement for the same; but [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is firmly of the belief that “[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) has got the remedy for this in his hands”; āḻvār himself said in periya tiruvantādi 87 “*eppōdum kai kaḻalā nēmiyān nam mēl vinai kadivān*” (emperumān who always has sudarśana chakra attached to his hand, will drive away our sins); this is  “*sudarśana*” \[the chakra which brings auspiciousness by its sight\] as said in jitantē stōtram “*bhagavatō balēna*” \[with [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s strength\]; hence āḻvār is contemplating emperumān’s nature. śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 62.20 “*gajamvāvīkśya*” \[sītā pirātti did not fear seeing elephants, tigers and lions, since she was under the protection of śrī rāma\] and so on.
- *jñālam uṇḍāy* – Is emperumān not of the nature that he will come and help when there is great danger which has no other protection? Would he protect only if the whole word is under a deluge? Would he not help if all the dangers that envelop all the persons, fall on one person? Would be only help those who do not realise their danger and who do not call out? Is there any compulsion for him not to help those who realise their danger and call out to him? It is only on that day when the word, under deluge, makes an attempt to lift itself can one have the means to remedy one’s own sins. For you to protect, you only need a relationship and a person in danger.

[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) says “Though my nature is to help others, since the benefit is for you, you should have the knowledge befitting such benefit”, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) replies

- *jñāna mūrttī* – I have knowledge to make myself a nitya samsāri (eternally bound in this world). Don’t you have the knowledge to eliminate such thoughts from me and engage me in good path? As said in tiruvāimoḻi 4.9.2 “*āmāṟu onṟu aṟiyēn nān*” (I don’t know the path which is beneficial), periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 2.7.8 “*āmāṟu aṟiyum pirānē*” (Oh benefactor who knows the proper path), jitantē stōtram “*naiva kincit parōkśantē*” (there is nothing that is not known to your highness) – there is nothing that I know and there is nothing that you don’t know; if there is nothing that I can do, and nothing that you cannot do, then for whom is a task difficult to achieve? When a person \[[āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)\] is both blind and lame and another person \[[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)\] has good vision and walking ability, who will lead whom in the proper path? Oh one who is having the knowledge of one’s disease and its remedy as true nature!

emperumān says “Though I help during danger and have the knowledge to know and provide remedy, I will only help those who are aptly related to me”, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) replies

- *nārāyaṇā* – Oh [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is aptly related to me to protect me! By saying “*nārāyaṇa*“, it implies that ātmā is subservient to [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) like body to soul. But would śarīra (body) or śarīrī (soul) try to attain the benefit? only the owner will try to acquire his belongings \[bhagavān is the owner of everything which is also indicated by the word “nārāyaṇa”\].
- *enṟu enṟu* – The reason for repetition of “*enṟu*” – since nārāyaṇa word is focussed on qualities such as vātsalyam (motherly affection) etc which make him the upāyam (means) and qualities such as śēśitva (lordship) etc which make him the upēyam (goal). Now, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is not of the nature that he would say something to get something and after acquiring it stopping to say so; as the present tense in upāyam \[here, it is talking about *prapadyē* (surrendering) in dvaya mahā mantram\], this continuous calling out in itself is the goal for him. This is explained in mudal tiruvantādi 95 “*namō nārāyaṇā enṟu ōvāduraikkum urai*” (the words of “namō nārāyaṇā” which is constantly recited).
- *kālam tōṟum* – Am I reciting this now and subsequently saying “there is some other vorśippable aspect” and engaging in that? \[No – always engaged in [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)\].
- *yān irundu* – Even after suffering do I have to live long for 100 years? When separated from emperumān who is abundant with auspicious qualities, the desire will not let one die and make one think “Can we see him one more time?”.
- *kai talai pūsal ittāl* – Three explanations – 1) When I keep my hands \[in anjali mudrā – joined palms\] on my head, should you not manifest yourself? 2) When I keep my hand on my head \[with sorrow\] and call you out loudly; 3) When I have my hands on my head forever and call you out.
- *kōla mēni* – If that divine form is not presented for those who are desirous to see, what for is that form? īsn’t it said as in jitantē stōtram “*bhaktānām*” \[his forms, etc are for his devotees\]? As cool water is kept out of reach for thirsty person; this water is not useful for those who are desirous; \[is he water?\] he is said as in tiruvāimoḻi 10.1.8 “*maradaga maṇit tadam*” (emerald pond).
- *kāṇa* – Would those who are searching for karumugai mālai (garland of dark coloured flowers), do so for wearing it or for keeping it as a base to carry some weight on it? Even after attaining, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is said as “*sadā paśyanti*” (nityasūris are always seeing emperumān); here also it is as said in siṟiya tirumadal 69 “*kārār tirumēni kāṇum aḷavu*” (to see emperumān’s cloud like divine form); he is said in nānmugan tiruvantādi 39 “*aḻaippan tiruvēnkatattānaik kāṇa*” (Calling tiruvēnkatamudaiyān (śrīnivāsa) to see him); as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kaṇḍam 25.16 “*danyā paśyanti mē nātam*” (Many pious great souls are seeing my husband); sītā pirātti said “The whole world is stealing my belonging”.
- *vārāy* – When seeing such divine form, it is apt to know that only by his grace, he is coming. *kāṇa* (to see) – prāpyam (goal); *vārāy* (come) – prāpakam (means). Alternative explanation – *vārāy* – not coming; if you are not coming, we cannot force you to do so. Even if you are not willing to fulfil my desire, it is required for me to have my sorrow eliminated.
- *kūviyum koḷḷāyē* – You are not accepting, even if I call you out, which is not proper \[you should have come yourself instead of me calling\].

Even if I pray continuously, you are not appearing with your divine form; even if I call out, you are not accepting and coming; reason for this is, even though I am miniscule without any good qualities, my sins are great;. \[[arta pancakam](http://ponnadi.blogspot.in/2015/12/artha-panchakam.html) explanation\] By saying “*nārāyaṇa*“, prāpyam ([bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)) is explained. “*siṟiyan*” explains ātma svarūpam (nature of ātmā); “*vārāy*” explains upāyam (means); “*kāṇa*” explains palam (goal); “*seyvinaiyō peridu*” explains virōdi (obstacle); thus arta pancakam is explained.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.
