## 4.7.2. Kolla mala

*koḷḷa māḷā inba veḷḷam kōdila tandidum en vaḷḷalēyō! vaiyam koṇḍa vāmanāvō! enṟenṟu naḷḷirāvum nanpagalum  nānirundōlamittāl kaḷḷa māyā! unnai en kaṇ kāṇa vandīyāyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vaiyam – bhūmi (which was considered to be owned by some one else); koṇḍa – who measured it with intent (to have it exist for him); vāmanāvō – Oh vāmana!; koḷḷa – enjoying repeatedly; māḷā – unable to see the limit; inba veḷḷam – ocean of bliss; kōdu ila – not having faults (of having satisfaction while enjoying and seeking out other enjoyment); tandidum – truly bestowing; en vaḷḷalēyō – Oh my great benefactor!; enṟu enṟu – saying with dejection; naḷ irāvum – in the middle of the night; nanpagalum – daytime when objects are clearly visible; nān – I (who cannot live without you); irundu – being present (without engagement in any other aspect); ōlamittāl – if I call out; kaḷḷam māyā – Oh amazing person who is present in the heart (being invisible like a cheat)!; unnai – you (without seeing whom, I cannot sustain myself); en kaṇ kāṇa – to be seen by my eyes (which desired to see you); vandu īyāy – have not arrived and given yourself

**Перевод:**

**Oh vāmana who measured bhūmi with intent! Oh my great benefactor who is truly bestowing the limitless ocean of bliss which is without any faults, for my enjoyment! Saying these with dejection in the middle of the night and in the daytime when objects are clearly visible, if I call out “Oh amazing person who is present in the heart!”, you have not arrived  to be seen by my eyes and given yourself. āḻvār implies “come and give yourself to me”. The “O” in the words “vaḷḷalēyō!” and “vāmanāvō!” indicates the sorrow of āḻvār.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In second pāsuram, āḻvār highlights the favours done by emperumān for him and becomes displeased thinking “You, who is such benefactor, have not arrived even after my calling out with sorrow”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “If I call you out highlighting your magnanimity of making me exist fully for you and enjoy you, you have not arrived to be seen by me and have not presented yourself to me”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Second pāsuram. āḻvār highlighting emperumān‘s previous favours, says “Is it reasonable for you who favoured me and revealed your nature to me, to not arrive in front of me when I call out for you now?”. koḷḷa māḷā inba veḷḷam kōdila tandidum en vaḷḷalēyō! vaiyam koṇḍa vāmanāvō! enṟenṟu naḷḷirāvum nanpagalum  nānirundōlamittāl kaḷḷa māyā! unnai en kaṇ kāṇa vandīyāyē*

- *koḷḷa māḷā inba veḷḷam* – Ocean of bliss which never saturates even after enjoying repeatedly. \[Did [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) give bliss to [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)?\] He is explaining what was explained in [tiruvāimoḻi 4.5.3](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/02/thiruvaimozhi-4-5-3-vivil-inbam/) “*vīvil inbam miga ellai nigaḻndanan*” (being in the ultimate state of continuous bliss).
- *kōdila tandidum* – Fault in the bliss is – leading one to be satisfied after enjoying once, causing one to desire for other matters; this bliss is unlike that; it increases the desire for enjoying repeatedly and also causes detachment towards other enjoyments; thus, bestowing faultless and limitless ocean of bliss.
- *en vaḷḷalēyō* – While bestowing you gave it as if it is for your benefit, but now you have made it appear that it is for my benefit and are you waiting for me to call out for you? vaḷḷal (magnanimous person) means favouring others as if it is a benefit for oneself. The nature of him who bestowed himself is explained in “*ānandamaya:*” (embodiment of bliss), “*ānandōbrahma:*” (brahmam is bliss). If you were planning to make me call out \[with agony\] like this, why did you give such enjoyment in [tiruvāimoḻi 4.5](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/02/thiruvaimozhi-4-5-virrirundhu/) “*vīṟṟirundēḻulagu*“? It appears that [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) gave some joy for the little [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)  – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) referred to himself as “*siṟiyan*” in previous pāsuram.
- *vaiyam koṇḍa vāmanāvō* – Are you not of the nature that you will \[even\] beg for those who beg to you? To eliminate the tears of indra who fell at his feet saying “I lost all my three worlds”, he who is śriya:pati (lord of śrī mahālakśmi) himself took up the form of a seeker; alas! instead of you eagerly bestowing yourself to me, you are making me call out for you!
- *enṟu enṟu* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is not like indra who left after getting his kingdom back; nor is he like mahābali who manifested audāryam (generosity) \[towards emperumān himself\]; instead he keeps repeating this \[vāmana avatāram\] only. Even after measuring and accepting the worlds \[as trivikrama\], āḻvār’s divine heart was still engrossed in the \[previous state of\] vāmana form only.
- *naḷḷirāvum nanpagalum* – naḷ indicates middle and abundance/darkness; it also indicates the unique sound in the night when all other sounds subdue. By all of these, it indicates the middle of the night. As said in katavalli upaniśat 2.5 “*ya ēśu suptēśu*” (one who is awake \[and protecting\] when everyone is fast asleep), you are making me aware and call out for you, while you are the one who is awake and caring for everyone!
- *nanpagal* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying “good day” since his contact/relationship with [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is unchanging whether it is [tiruvāimoḻi 4.6](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/02/thiruvaimozhi-4-6-thirpparai/) “*tīrppāraiyāmini*” or [tiruvāimoḻi 4.5](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/02/thiruvaimozhi-4-5-virrirundhu/) “*vīṟṟirundēḻulagu*“. \[Only\] when other matters are experienced, when [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is not seen, the mind/heart will think about the other matters. Alternatively, “*nanpagal*” is like *cevvāykkiḻamai* (Tuesday) \[which is usually considered to be inauspicious\] being called “*mangaḷavāram*” (auspicious day) \[This is called viparīta lakśaṇā – contrary identification\], since he was not seen, this time is considered as empty/useless time.
- *nān irundu* – Me who is very weak and not having ability to call you.
- *nān irundu* – Me who enjoyed ultimate bliss previously.
- *ōlamittāl* – if I call out.
- *kaḷḷa māyā* – Oh amazing lord who is invisible to the eyes, but unforgettable in the heart!
- *unnai* – Distinguished you without whom I cannot sustain myself; because you have a beautiful form.
- *en kaṇ kāṇa* – to be seen by my eyes which desire to see you.
- *vandu īyāyē* – You have to come and walk in front of me for me to witness that beautiful walk and sustain myself. As said \[by śrī rāma\] in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 66.10 “*najīvēyam …*” (I cannot sustain in your separation even for a moment) and śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 10.9 “… *hrīrēśāhi …*” (I am ashamed to have made you wait \[to the sages\]), when he appears, he makes other think “there is nothing wrong with him” \[even if he comes late\]. You should come and present yourself to us.

When [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) says “I have already given myself to you; when others are calling out for me, I have made you call only for me”, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says “that is not sufficient”,

- *kaṇ kāṇa vandu īyāy* – Just the experience in mind is not sufficient; you have to physically appear in front of me. It can also be read as “*īgiṟilai*” which means “you are not appearing in front of me” and this goes along well with “*seyvinaiyō peridāl*” (my sins are huge). Another explanation – Please come and give.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.7.3. Ivilada tivinaigal

*īvilāda tīvinaigaḷ ettanai seydanan kol? tāvi vaiyam koṇḍa endāy! dāmōdarā! enṟenṟu kūvik kūvi nenjurugik kaṇ pani sōra ninṟāl pāvi nī enṟonṟu sollāy pāviyēn kāṇa vandē*

**Пословный перевод:**

(as said in Śrīvaikuṇṭha stavam 60 “yadbrahmakalpaniyutānubhavē’pyanāśyam” (sins committed by this jīvātmā in half a moment cannot be atoned even over a period of 1000s of days of brahmā), even if experienced for many kalpas (kalpa – a day of brahmā)); īvu ilāda – indestructible; tīvinaigaḷ – cruel sins (which lead to agony); ettanai – countless; seydanan kol – have I committed?; tāvi – measured (with his divine feet); vaiyam koṇḍa – captured the universe to fully exist for you; endāy – oh my lord!; dāmōdarā – Oh one who is having the scar of the rope on your waist (which was tied by yaśōśā to show that you are obedient towards those who are fully existing for you); enṟu enṟu – saying so; kūvik kūvi – calling out many times without break; nenju urugi – heart melting as water; kaṇ pani sōra – that water flowing out as tears; ninṟāl – if I stood (with agony); pāviyēn – me, who is having sins (which stop me from seeing you); kāṇa – to see; vandu – appear in front of me; nī – you; pāvi – are a sinner; enṟu – that; onṟu sollāy – you are not telling

**Перевод:**

**Have I committed indestructible countless cruel sins? Oh my lord who measured and captured the universe to fully exist for you! Oh one who is having the scar of the rope on your waist! If I who is having sins that are stopping me to see you, stood and called out to you saying these, with my heart melting as water and that water flowing out as tears, you are not appearing in front of me and telling “You are a sinner”. āḻvār implies that emperumān appearing to say that āḻvār is a sinner is also sufficient. īvu – destruction.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In third pāsuram, āḻvār becomes displeased saying “You are not presenting yourself in front of me, at least you can come in front of me and say ‘You are not virtuous enough to see me’ to make me become devoid of such desire to see you; you are not even doing that”*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “If I call out for you who is very humble/obedient towards those who exclusively exist for you, you are not even coming in front of me and telling ‘Why are you, who has committed sins, calling out to me?'”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. īvilāda tīvinaigaḷ ettanai seydanan kol? tāvi vaiyam koṇḍa endāy! dāmōdarā! enṟenṟu kūvik kūvi nenjurugik kaṇ pani sōra ninṟāl pāvi nī enṟonṟu sollāy pāviyēn kāṇa vandē*

- *īvilāda tīviinaigaḷ* – I am committing big sin; should I commit sins which cannot be exhausted even by experiencing the effects of it? Would “*nābhuktam kśīyatēkarma*” (if the effects of the actions are not experienced, they don’t get exhausted) be false in my case \[i.e., some effects are already experienced, at least those karma should be exhausted by now; but it appears that I have so much karma left\]; even after experiencing the effects, should \[a large portion of\] it remain? \[But\] Did [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) experience the effect of his sins? Yes – he experienced the effect of all his sins \[the great agony\], when [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) turned away from [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) for half a moment.
- *tīvinaigaḷ ettanai seydanan kol* – Does “*seyvinai*” just indicate one sin? How many crores of sins have I done?
- *tāvi* … – Are you not capable of doing difficult tasks effortlessly? Don’t you protect everyone at that time without limiting yourself? He set out his divine feet to protect them and [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) too being fully captivated by that act, said “*endāy*“.
- *dāmōdarā* – When some persons \[dēvaki and nandagōpa in previous births\] prayed to have you as their child, did you not appear as their child and become submissive to them to be disciplined by them? She \[yaśōdā\] saw your act of stealing the butter, tied you to the mortar and beat you up, to starve you also.
- *enṟu enṟu* – He is not of the nature of saying this \[incident\] once and speaking about something else subsequently.
- *kūvik kūvi* – Repeatedly calling out speaking about these incidents.
- *nenju urugi* – The first calling out leads to subsequent calling out, the sound from his throat entering his ear and causing the heart to melt like fluid matter.
- *kaṇ pani sōra ninṟāl* – As the eyes will act on behalf of the heart, they shed overflowing tears. When that happens,
- *pāvi* … – To sustain myself by becoming free from desire \[to see you\]; Can [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) not come in front of me and say “Why are you desiring to be helped by me like I helped indra, yaśōdā et al? indra was satva niśta \[situated in satva guṇam (goodness)\], yaśōdā was my mother, \[but\] you are a sinner”? \[Is indra a satva niśta?\] Since emperumān divided dēvas (celestial deities) and asuras (demons) based on their qualities, indra can be said to have satva guṇam since he is counted along in dēvas.
- *onṟu sollāy* – You can tell me “You are fortunate \[or you are a sinner\]”. I don’t care about the meaning of your words, I just want to hear you speak.

But there is restriction while you say that.

- *pāviyēn kāṇa vandu* – You have to appear in front of me and say that. You are capable of being present in my heart and speaking to me – but I will not be satisfied with that.
- *pāviyēn* – While the whole world is happily living its life, I am so sinful that I cannot sustain myself without hearing you speak in this manner.
- *kāṇa vandu* – This is śabdādi viśaya prāvaṇyam \[attachment towards sense enjoyment\] of [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) \[i.e., his senses too are attached to [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) only\]; sollāy is explained in two ways – “come and tell me” as well as “you are not even coming and telling me this”.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.7.4. Kana vandu

*kāṇa vandu en kaṇ mugappē tāmaraik kaṇ piṟaḻa āṇi sem pon mēni endāy! ninṟaruḷāy enṟenṟu nāṇam illāc ciṟu tagaiyēn nāningalaṟṟuvaden? pēṇi vānōr kāṇa māttāp pīdudai appaniyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vānōr – dēvas such as brahmā et al; pēṇi – with desire as per their knowledge and love; kāṇamāttā – not having the ability to see him; pīdu udai – having greatness; appanai – lord; āṇi sem pon – attractive like pure, best gold \[āṇip pon means the best gold, which is used as benchmark to compare other gold and determine the other gold’s quality\]; mēni – having form; endāy – my father/lord!; tāmarai – like a lotus (which is infinitely enjoyable); kaṇ – eye; piṟaḻa – lighting up; kāṇa – to be seen (by me, from the beginning); vandu – come; en kaṇ mugappē – in front of me; ninṟaruḷāy – kindly stand; enṟu enṟu – saying repeatedly; nāṇam illā – shamelessly; siṟu tagaiyēn – having lowly nature; nān – I; ingu – in this world which takes me away from bhagavat viśayam (bhagavān related matters); alaṟṟuvadu – to lament; en – what is the use?

**Перевод:**

**Oh my father/lord who is having such greatness that even dēvas such as brahmā et al with desire as per their knowledge and love, are not having the ability to see him and having a form which is attractive like pure, best gold! What is the use of me who is having lowly nature, shamelessly saying “You kindly come and stand in front of me with your lotus like eyes lighting up, to be seen by me” repeatedly and lamenting in this world which takes me away from bhagavat viśayam?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In fourth pāsuram, āḻvār says “I, who is very lowly, am calling out to see sarvēśvara who is desired to be seen by brahmā et al and cannot be seen by even them; How shameless of me!”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “What is the use of me shamelessly calling out for emperumān who cannot be seen by dēvatās such as brahmā et al, to appear in front of me with his attractive, beautiful form?”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Fourth pāsuram. āḻvār calls out for emperumān to be seen by him; he says – What is the use of desiring “I want to see the divine form which is enjoyed by nityasūris (eternally free souls of paramapadam) who are never touched by samsāram, and which cannot be seen by brahmā, indra et al”? The reason for this  \[desire\] is – my śamelessness and lack of knowledge. kāṇa vandu en kaṇ mugappē tāmaraik kaṇ piṟaḻa āṇi sem pon mēni endāy! ninṟaruḷāy enṟenṟu nāṇam illāc ciṟu tagaiyēn nāningalaṟṟuvaden? pēṇi vānōr kāṇa māttāp pīdudai appaniyē*

- *kāṇa vandu* – Not merely experiencing your form in the mind, but you should appear physically to be seen by my eyes – says [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/); another explanation – I should see and enjoy your arrival right from when your commence your journey towards me.  āḻvār says “*āṇic chem pon mēni endāy – en kaṇ mugappē – ninṟaruḷāy*” (my lord who has pure, best gold like form, kindly stand in front of me). As said in tiruviruttam 85 “*maṟṟōppārai illā āṇip ponnē*” (the best gold like lord, who has no one comparable to him), even the best gold of this world which is said in [tiruvāimoḻi 3.1.2](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/07/thiruvaimozhi-3-1-2-katturaikkil/) “*sutturaitta nan pon un tirumēni oḷi ovvādu*”  (Even the shine of the best molten gold is not comparable to your divine form’s shine) appears without shine when compared to him. If the best gold is rubbed on the rubbing stone of the tongue (of āḻvār) and placed in the wax of the heart (of āḻvār), it will fail the test.
- *sem pon mēni endāy* – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) enslaved [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) by showing his form which is said as in tiruneduntāṇḍagam 10 “*ponnānāy*” (You are gold). This is explaining the changes which happen in emperumān’s form which remains ēkarūpa (cangeless), when he sees āḻvār.
- *tāmaraik kaṇ piṟaḻa* – His divine eyes light up \[with loving agitation\] on seeing him, like an agitated ocean rising with topsy-turvy waves; another explanation – shining brightly. Oh emperumān who made me exist exclusively for you by manifesting your divine form which resembles the best gold!
- *ninṟu aruḷāy* – You have to stand in the vicinity of my eyes.
- *enṟu enṟu* – When he arrives in front, those who are with ulterior motives as explained in “*dēhi mē dadami tē*” (*quid pro quo* – you give me something and I will give you this) will say \[whatever is to be said\] once \[But [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) will keep praising [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), since he is not seeking for any ulterior benefits\].
- *nāṇam illā* – Who is saying the words that are to be said by whom \[āḻvār is saying the words of nityasūris here which he feels as inapt\]? I who is not contemplating my own previous state and thus being shameless.
- *siṟu tagaiyēn* – Me who is very lowly. tagai – aḷavu – knowledge/greatness. siṟu tagai – means lack of knowledge/greatness.
- *nān ingu alaṟṟuvaden* – What is the use of calling out to him from a place where he cannot place his divine feet? \[ōr, What is use of calling out to him from a place where he cannot be served properly?\].
- *pēṇi* … – Can he be seen by those (dēvatās) who do not place their feet on the earth? As said in uttara mīmāmsā 1.3.25 “*taduparyapibādarāyaṇassambhavāt*“, even brahmā et al engage in upāsanam (worship) of lord. pēṇugai – desiring, which indicates upāsanam. There is greatness of not being seen by even those celestial beings who worship him; How can I, such shameless, ignorant person, lament to see him? āḻvār considers himself very inferior that when compared to him even brahmā et al (dēvatās) appear to be like nityasūris.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.7.5. Appane adalaliyane

*appanē adal āḻiyānē āḻ kadalaik kadainda tuppanē un tōḷgaḷ nāngum kaṇḍidak kūdungol enṟu eppoḻudum kaṇṇa nīr koṇḍu āvi tuvarndu tuvarndu ippoḻudē vandidāy enṟu ēḻaiyēn nōkkuvanē*

**Пословный перевод:**

appanē – Oh one who has the nature to bestow favours (to devotees starting with making them exist)!; adal āḻiyānē – Oh one who is having the divine chakra which is of the nature of destroying their \[devotees’\] enemies!; āḻ kadalai – deep ocean; kadainda – churned and fulfilled their \[devotees’ – here dēvas’\] desires; tuppanē – Oh very majestic lord!; un tōḷgaḷ nāngum – your four shoulders; kaṇḍidak kūdum kol – is it possible to see?; enṟu – thinking in this manner; eppoḻudum – always; kaṇṇa nīr koṇḍu – with tearful eyes; āvi – prāṇa (life); tuvarndu tuvarndu – drying up more and more; ippoḻudē – right now (before existence ceases); vandidāy – you should come; enṟu – looking forward with great eagerness; ēḻaiyēn – the desirous me; nōkkuvan – seeing (in the direction from where he may come seeing my current state of existence)

**Перевод:**

**Oh one who has the nature to bestow favours! Oh one who is having the divine chakra which is of the nature of destroying their \[devotees’\] enemies! Oh very majestic lord who  churned the deep ocean and fulfilled their \[devotees’ – here dēvas’\] desires! I am always thinking “Is it possible to see your four shoulders?”, with tearful eyes and my prāṇa drying up more and more; I, who is desirous, am looking forward with great eagerness, am seeing in the direction thinking “you should come right now”.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In fifth pāsuram, āḻvār says “As I cannot sustain myself after desiring to see your beauty that cannot be seen even by brahmā et al, I said ‘Come right now’ and will wait to see you when you arrive without missing that. How desirous am I!”*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “Though you are difficult to attain for dēvas, for your devotees, you fulfilled their desires by engaging in great efforts – thinking about this, I eagerly desired to see you”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. appanē adal āḻiyānē āḻ kadalaik kadainda tuppanē un tōḷgaḷ nāngum kaṇḍidak kūdungol enṟu eppoḻudum kaṇṇa nīr koṇḍu āvi tuvarndu tuvarndu ippoḻudē vandidāy enṟu ēḻaiyēn nōkkuvanē*

- *appanē* – Oh lord who has done such great favour to me that I call out to you only even if you don’t turn towards me!
- *adal* … – adal – midukku – majestic. Always being alert and ready to fight to destroy the enemies. Oh lord who carries the disc which can eliminate my hurdles!
- *āḻ kadal …* – Oh lord who has the ability to churn the great ocean which is described as in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 14.31 “*apramēyō mahōdadi*” (immeasurably deep ocean) and helped even those who do not desire for you and just desire for other worldly aspects!
- *un* … – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is unlike those dēvas who accept the salt water \[amrutam – nectar\]. Instead, he is desiring to see the shoulders which churned that ocean. [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is explained in nācciyār tirumoḻi 9.1 as “*madurak koḻunjāṟu koṇḍa sundarat tōḷaniṟē*” (emperumān with beautiful shoulders who accepted the divine nectar). āḻvār is saying “Shall I see your four shoulders?”.
- *eppoḻudum* – Like a low-level land which is ready to accept flowing waters always, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s eyes are always with tears.
- āvi – my prāṇa (life).
- *tuvarndu tuvarndu* – drying up totally; neither dying after drying up nor living due to having faith that our desire to see [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) with great qualities will be fulfilled; some times āḻvār sustains and other times he becomes totally agonised – this keeps repeating.
- *ippoḻudē tandidāy enṟu* – emperumān should only consider [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s agony as the proof and should arrive without even wasting a fraction of a moment.
- *nōkkuvanē* – I will be looking at the direction from where you can arrive.

Is he doing like this since emperumān is having some intention to arrive?

- *ēḻaiyēn* – No. I am only having the desire. \[[emperumānār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/emperumanar/) orders [kūrattāḻvān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/kUraththAzhwAn/) to compile varadarāja stavam in praise of dēVap perumāḷ and pray for regaining his eyesight. āḻvān compiles the prabandam too\] When emperumānār listens to one of the ślōkams, he tells āḻvān “[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) will surely bestow his mercy on hearing this ślōkam; you just show your face \[eyes\] to him \[and get it cured\]” \[āḻvān eventually prays to emperumān to have the vision to see perumāḷ and emperumānār only\].

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.7.6. Nokki nokki

*nōkki nōkki unnaik kāṇbān yān enadāvi uḷḷē nākku nīḷvan jñānam illai nāḷtōṟum ennudaiya ākkai uḷḷum āvi uḷḷum all puṟattin uḷḷum nīkkam inṟi engum ninṟāy ninnai aṟindaṟindē*

**Пословный перевод:**

nāḷ tōṟum – everyday; ennudaiya – my; ākkai uḷḷum – in the heart which is inside my body; āvi uḷḷum – inside the ātmā (soul) (which is the controller of that body); alla – beyond these two (and being the faculties of such ātmā); puṟattin uḷḷum – indriyas (senses) etc (which are outside the true self); nīkkam inṟi – without missing anything; engum – everywhere; ninṟāy – Oh one who stood (as the antarātmā (in-dwelling super soul))!; ninnai – you; unnai – you (who is having enjoyable form); kāṇbān – to see with my eyes; nōkki nōkki – looking forward constantly; yān – I (who is desirous); enadu – my; āvi uḷḷē – in my heart; nākku nīḷvan – will desire for that; jñānam – knowledge (that “antarātmā is beyond the reach of our senses”); illai – due to not having

**Перевод:**

**Oh one who stood everyday as the antarātmā in my heart which is inside my body, inside the ātmā and beyond these two, in my indriyas (senses) and everywhere else without missing anything! Always knowing you (as omnipresent), I will desire in my heart and look forward constantly to see you with my eyes, due to not having the knowledge (that “antarātmā is beyond the reach of our senses”).**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In sixth pāsuram, āḻvār says “Though I know that you are not presenting yourself in front of me, despite being present always around me, due to your not having the intention for that, I desired to see you every moment; this is due to my own ignorance”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. nōkki nōkki unnaik kāṇbān yān enadāvi uḷḷē nākku nīḷvan jñānam illai nāḷtōṟum ennudaiya ākkai uḷḷum āvi uḷḷum all puṟattin uḷḷum nīkkam inṟi engum ninṟāy ninnai aṟindaṟindē*

- *nōkki nōkki* – I will repeatedly look in the direction of your arrival.

What is reason for his constant looking there?

- *unnaik kāṇbān* – Due to the desire to see you.
- *yān* … – When a person is desirous of something, it is said that “*ivan ivviśayattilē nākku nīttā ninṟān*” (Having the tongue stretched out for that matter \[keenly interested in it\]); in this manner, I desired for him in my heart.

What is the reason for not revealing that desire?

- *jñānam illai* – There is no one more ignorant than I due to this desire.

But why is this “desire to see [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)” considered as ignorance?

- *nāḷ tōṟum* … – You have permeated everywhere without missing any place such as my body which is a hurdle to reach you at all times, in the ātmā which will be the recipient \[of your vision\], and the others such as the senses which too are hurdles to see you. When there is treasure in the bag, some will run around searching for it to only end up with swelling in their leg – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is like that now.
- *ninnai aṟindu aṟindu* – It is only my ignorance that I am not remaining peacefully without realizing that [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) does not have the intention to be present in front of me even after being 1) the apt protector for me, 2) one who is omniscient to know the cause of this situation and provide a remedy, 3) being omnipotent to fulfil the task which is taken up, 4) having compassion to show his mercy to me and 5) is omnipresent. It is not that I am apt (to protect myself) and you are not; it is not that I am omniscient and you are ignorant; its not that I am omnipotent and you are incapable; it is not that I am omnipresent and you are miniscule; it is not that you are cruel to let me suffer; being the owner and not caring for your belonging only implies that you don’t have the intention to do so – not being  at peace \[knowing all these\] is purely due to my ignorance only.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.7.7. Arindu arindu

*aṟindaṟindu tēṟit tēṟi yān enadāvi uḷḷē niṟainda jñāna mūrttiyāyai ninmalamāga vaittup piṟandum settum ninṟidaṟum pēdaimai tīrndoḻindēn naṟuntuḻāyin kaṇṇi ammā! nān unnaik kaṇḍu koṇḍē*

**Пословный перевод:**

naṟu – abundantly fragrant; tuḻāy – having tiruttuḻāy (tuḷasi); kaṇṇi – wearing divine garland; ammā – Oh sarvādika (greater than all)!; nān – I (who is desirous of your enjoyability); unnai – you (who is apt and infinitely enjoyable); kaṇḍu koṇḍu – seeing (with my heart, as you revealed yourself); aṟindu aṟindu – by this mayarvaṟa madinalam (blemiśless knowledge/devotion) blessed by you, knowing you to be the prāpyam (goal) and prāpakam (means); tēṟit tēṟi – having clarity (about the in-depth aspects of such prāpyam and prāpakam); yān – I (who is with firm knowledge \[bestowed by you\]); enadu āvi uḷḷē – in my heart which is substratum for my prāṇa (life); niṟainda jñāna mūrttiyāyai – you who is the embodiment of complete knowledge; ninmalamāga – to be freed from any doubt, error; vaittu – placing (firmly); piṟandum settum – going through birth and death; ninṟu – remaining to be; idaṟum – lamenting; pēdaimai – ignorance; tīrndu oḻindēn – became free from

**Перевод:**

**Oh sarvādika who is wearing divine garland which is having abundantly fragrant tiruttuḻāy (tuḷasi)! I am seeing you through my heart and having clarity by the mayarvaṟa madinalam (blemiśless knowledge/devotion) blessed by you, knowing you to be the prāpyam (goal) and prāpakam (means), placing you who is the embodiment of complete knowledge, in my heart which is substratum for my prāṇa, to be freed from any doubt and error, became free from the ignorance of going through birth and death and remaining to be lamenting. “I have not had the fortune of physically seeing you” is the remainder which needs to be assumed.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In seventh pāsuram, emperumān says “Why are you calling me out? I have revealed about me to you and eliminated all your worldly sorrows” and āḻvār says “That is not sufficient”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “While you remained in my heart, I meditated upon your beautiful form which you revealed to me and became free from worldly ignorance; now, I am desiring to see that beauty with my eyes physically”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Seventh pāsuram. emperumān says “You are greatly disliking me now;  Did I not do any favour for you? Do you think that I have not helped you in anyway?”, āḻvār replies “you have done some favours; I have got a little bit now; but I am not satisfied”. aṟindaṟindu tēṟit tēṟi yān enadāvi uḷḷē niṟainda jñāna mūrttiyāyai ninmalamāga vaittup piṟandum settum ninṟidaṟum pēdaimai tīrndoḻindēn naṟuntuḻāyin kaṇṇi ammā! nān unnaik kaṇḍu koṇḍē*

- *aṟindu aṟindu tēṟit tēṟi* – \[First explanation – explaining it as progressive acquiring of clarity\] In the [\[first centum\] first decad](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/03/thiruvaimozhi-1-1-uyarvara/), [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) meditated upon [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s supremacy; there is a clarity which is acquired when that is grasped; subsequent to that, there is clarity acquired by meditating upon him to be vorśippable \[in second decad\], there is clarity acquired by meditating upon him to be simple \[in third decad\], and there is clarity acquired by meditating upon him to be tolerating the mistakes \[of his devotees\] \[in fourth decad\] and so on; in this manner only, āḻvār’s clarity increased throughout tiruvāimoḻi; all of these are mānasa anubhavam (experience in the mind).
- *aṟindu aṟindu tēṟit tēṟi* – \[Alternative explanation – explaining this in the context of [arta pancakam](http://ponnadi.blogspot.in/2015/12/artha-panchakam.html)\] By your bestowing of *mayarvaṟa madinalam*, I acquired clarity \[in the five essential principles\].
   - *para svarūpam* (nature of [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)) – the clarity acquired by knowing that [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.1.2](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/03/thiruvaimozhi-1-1-2-mananaga-malamara/) “… *manuṇarvaḷavilan poṟi uṇarvavaiyilan, edir nigaḻ kaḻivinum inanilan, migu naraiyilan, uṇar muḻu nalam, inan …*” ([bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is immeasurable by even well blossomed mind which is free of blemishes such as kāmam, krōdam, etc., that can understand the ātmā. He is immeasurable by the external senses which are used to comprehend [acit (matter)](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/09/thathva-thrayam-achith-what-is-matter/). Thus he is distinct from both [cit](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) and [acit](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/09/thathva-thrayam-achith-what-is-matter/). He is identified as full knowledge and full bliss and has none who is equal or higher in the past, present or future. He is my sustaining soul); further knowing the ultimate state of this para svarūpam is [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s total dependence in his arcāvatāram \[on his devotees\] as mentioned in tiruvāimoḻi 10.6.1 “*adu namadu vidi vagaiyē*” (his mercy is based on the desire of his devotees) and [tiruvāimoḻi 3.6.9](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/09/thiruvaimozhi-3-6-9-thanjam-agiya/) “*nenjināl ninaippāva yavan avanāgum nīḷ kadal vaṇṇan*” (he who is thought about and joyfully consecrated \[in deity form\] is the same sarvēśvaran who has ocean-like vast nature).
   - *sva svarūpam* (nature of self) – the clarity acquired by knowing that ātmā is as said in tiruvāimoḻi 8.8.5 “*senṟu senṟu param paramāy yādum inṟit tēyndaṟṟu, nanṟu tīdu enṟu aṟivu aridāy nānṟāy jñānam kadandirukkum*” (Pursuing beyond different \[material\] entities (like body, mind, intelligence etc), unable to distinguish if it is good or bad, being distinguished and beyond the comprehension of mind); further knowing the ultimate state of this ātmā is to be totally surrendered to [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s devotees as said in tiruvāimoḻi 8.10.3 “*siṟu mā manisarāy ennai āṇḍār ingē tiriya – naṟu mā virai  nāḷ malar adikkīḻ pugudal – uṟumō*” (While the devotees who may be physically small but are great in their heart, are present here, should I seek out and reach the divine, fragrant, fresh, lotus feet of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)?) and [tiruvāimoḻi 3.7.10](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/10/thiruvaimozhi-3-7-10-adiyarndha/) “*tam adiyār adiyōngaḷē*” (being the servitor of the servitors of lord).
   - *upāya svarūpam* (nature of the means) – the clarity acquired by knowing that the means (process) is as said in tiruvāimoḻi 5.10.11 “*nāgaṇai misai nampirān saraṇē \[caraṇau – the divine feet\] saraṇ \[śaraṇam – refuge\] namakku*” (the divine feet of the lord who is reclining on ādi śēśa is the refuge/means for us); further knowing the ultimate state of this upāyam is – [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s sahākāri nirapēkśyam (not expecting any other support while being the upāyam) which cannot even tolerate the svīkāram (prapatti/surrender) which is an adikāri viśēśaṇam (a quality of a person who realizes his true nature) \[this implies that, even the surrender performed by the ātmā is not the means, bhagavān is the exclusive means\].
   - *pala svarūpam* (nature of the goal) – the clarity acquired by knowing that the goal is as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 3.3.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/08/thiruvaimozhi-3-3-1-ozhivil-kalam/) “*oḻivil kālam ellām udanāy manni vaḻuvilā adimai seyya vēṇḍum*” (Being together with [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) at all times, in all places and in all forms and serving him); further, knowing the ultimate state of this palam is – tiruvāimoḻi 10.3.9 “*undan tiruvuḷḷam idar kedum tōṟum nāngaḷ viyakka inbuṟudum*” (your divine heart should attain bliss and seeing that we should also feel the bliss) \[More than us getting kainkaryam (and feeling joyful first – which is self-centered), his acquiring bliss is more important. As a natural result, we will also feel joyful seeing his joy\].
   - *virōdi svarūpam* (nature of the obstacles) – the clarity acquired by knowing that the obstacle is as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 2.9.9](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/06/thiruvaimozhi-2-9-9-yane-ennai/) “*yānē entanadē enṟu irundēn*” (merely existing considering myself as independent and considering everything but myself as my belongings); further knowing the ultimate state of this virōdi is – “*kainkaryattil ahankāra garbamāna mamakāram*” (While performing kainkaryam, the ownership triggered by the ego) \[When performing kainkaryam, it should be done for the pleasure of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) and not to satisfy one’s own ego\].
- *yān* – I who learned these by you teaching these principles to me.
- *enadu āvi uḷḷē* – In my heart.
- *niṟainda jñāna mūrttiyāyai* – You who is an embodiment of complete knowledge. You who is so distinguished that I can never be satisfied with what I have enjoyed in you \[and still craving for more\].
- *ninmalamāga vaittu* – meditating upon you in the most expansive manner.
- *piṟandum* … – Immediately after acquiring knowledge \[mayarvaṟa madinalam\], I acquired what I prayed for in tiruviruttam 1 “*inninṟa nīrmai ini yām uṟāmai*” (I cannot tolerate this lowly samsāram). \[That is\] I got rid of the ignorance which makes one die, be born again and suffer in this samsāram.
- *naṟum tuḻāy …* – This is his effort to make this knowledge dawn in me. That is, by manifesting his tuḷasi decoration, and making me study in that school of his beautiful form, he bestowed me knowledge and enslaved me.
- *nān unnaik kaṇḍu koṇḍu* – I who understands your enjoyable nature, having seen your infinite enjoyability. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is explaining the essence that he acquired “*naṟuntuḻāyin kaṇṇi ammā! nān unnaik kaṇḍu koṇḍu – aṟindaṟindu tēṟittēṟi yān enadāviyuḷḷē niṟainda jñāna mūrttiyāyai ninmalamāga vaittu, piṟandum settum ninṟidaṟum pēdaimai tīrndoḻindēn*“.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.7.8. Kandu kondu

*kaṇḍu koṇḍu en kaigaḷāra nin tiruppādangaḷ mēl eṇḍisaiyum uḷḷa pūk koṇḍu ētti ugandugandu toṇḍarōngaḷ pādiyādac cūḻkadal jñālattuḷḷē vaṇḍuḻāyin kaṇṇi vēndē! vandidagillāyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kaṇḍu koṇḍu – fully seeing and enjoying (with the eyes and not just in the heart as said in “nān unnaik kaṇḍu koṇḍu” (I seeing you)); en kaigaḷ – my hands (which are as said in “tāyavanē enṟu tadavum” (searching for the one who measured the worlds)); Ara – to the full satisfaction; nin – (the apt) your; tiruppādangaḷ mēl – on your divine feet; eṇ tisaiyum – in all directions; uḷḷa – present; pūkkoṇḍu – bringing the flowers; ētti – offering with praises; ugandu ugandu – being joyful in each of those activities; toṇḍarōngaḷ – us who are having great devotion in the form of affection towards you; pādi Ada – singing and dancing (to reveal our love); kadal sūḻ jñālattuḷḷē – in this material realm, which is the earth surrounded by the ocean; vaḷ – distinguished; tuḻāyk kaṇṇi – wearing tiruttuḻāy (tuḷasi) garland; vēndē – Oh my lord!; vandida killāy – you are not coming

**Перевод:**

**Oh my lord who is wearing distinguished tiruttuḻāy garland! You are not coming here to be fully seen and enjoyed \[by me\], to bring the flowers from all directions and offer them on your divine feet with my hands to their full satisfaction, being joyful in each of those activities, to sing and dance for us who are having great devotion in the form of affection, in this material realm, which is the earth surrounded by the ocean.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In eighth pāsuram, emperumān asks “Now, what is that I have not done for you?” and āḻvār replies “You have not arrived for us to see your highness in this samsāram (material realm), to render all services and be uplifted”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār, out of attachment towards the enjoyable nature of emperumān, desires to see emperumān, enjoy him and serve him.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Eighth pāsuram. As āḻvār explained \[in the previous pāsuram\] the aspect which he attained, in this pāsuram, he explains what is not yet attained. kaṇḍu koṇḍu en kaigaḷāra nin tiruppādangaḷ mēl eṇḍisaiyum uḷḷa pūk koṇḍu ētti ugandugandu toṇḍarōngaḷ pādiyādac cūḻkadal jñālattuḷḷē vaṇḍuḻāyin kaṇṇi vēndē! vandidagillāyē*

- *kaṇḍu koṇḍu* – To see you to satisfy the hunger of my eyes which were left to starve as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 3.8.4](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/10/thiruvaimozhi-3-8-4-kaigalal-ara/) “*kāṇa virumbum en kaṇgaḷ*” (my eyes desire to see). As said in periya tirumoḻi 2.5.8 “*aravindam pōnṟu nīṇḍa kaṇṇānaik kaṇṇārak kaṇḍu koṇḍu*” (to the full satisfaction of my eyes to see the one whose eyes resemble lotus flower).
- *en kaigaḷ Ara* – As said in [tiruvāimoḻi 3.8.3](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/10/thiruvaimozhi-3-8-3-vasagame-eththa/) “*tāyavanē enṟu tadavum en kaigaḷ*” (Oh hands will seek out for him saying “Oh one who measured the world!”), to satisfy the need of my hands; as a hungry person would say “*vayiṟāra uṇḍu*” (eat to the full satisfaction of the stomach).
- *nin tiruppādangaḷ mēl* – On the divine feet which sustain you and give pleasure to you. It is said in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 1.2.1 as “*pidittuc cuvaittuṇṇum pādak kamalam*” (the divine lotus feet you behold and suck on – as a toddler kriṣṇa), they also sustain you. Alternative explanation –  On your divine feet which are apt and enjoyable for me. On your divine feet which is said in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.5.5](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/08/thiruvaimozhi-1-5-5-maney-nokki/) as “*un tēnē malarum tiruppādam*” (Your divine feet which is the origin of honey). Previously too, I was engaged like this in worldly matters; instead of that, to be engaged in the divine feet of you who is the apt lord. For the words from mālatī mādava drama “*tvat pāda pankaja parigrahadanya janmābhūyāsam*” (By reaching your lotus like feet, my purpose of life is fulfilled), [āḷavandār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/alavandhar/) mercifully explained “The words are nice; but it is not in the proper/apt matter” \[as the context was not in relation to [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) and was in worldly dealings\].
- *eṇ tisaiyum* … – Matching the greatness of [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) who is the target and matching my own desire. Matching his own desire, āḻvār says “I want to bring everything I desire \[for emperumān\]”. His desire spreads in all directions \[āsai means both desire and direction in tamiḻ\]. This is how the words of those who are desirous to serve, will be; like a hungry person would say “want to eat a whole pot of rice”. Devotees would be as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 31.25 “*aham sarvam kariśyāmi*” (lakśmaṇa says – I will carry out all kainkaryams).
- *ugandu ugandu* – To go on without diminishing the love.
- *toṇḍarōngaḷ* – We, who know the intricacies of this kainkaryam (service). After [tiruvāimoḻi 2.7](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/04/thiruvaimozhi-2-7-kesavan-thamar/) “*kēsavan tamar*“, āḻvār is not alone.
- *pādi Ada* – To be singing and dancing out of love.

[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) says “This is what I was also planning to do. Once you shed this body, I will bring you to paramapadam and get you engaged in that as said in taittirīya upaniśat “*ētat sāmagāyannāstē*” (the [muktātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) is singing the sāma gānam which is explained subsequently)”, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) replies “That is not what I want”.

- *sūḻ kadal jñālattuḷḷē* – If some one is thirsty in one place, should that person’s thirst be quenched in some other place? I want you to come in to this world surrounded by ocean, to be seen by me, right here.
- *vaṇ tuḻāyin kaṇṇi vēndē* – While appearing in this samsāram (material realm), you should bless me with that same form which is seen by the residents of paramapadam; you should appear with the same decorations that is shown to nityasūris.
- *vandidagillāyē* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying that it is not sufficient to just say “*kūviyum koḷḷāy*” (even after calling, you have not accepted me). You are not coming. This is the aspect I have not attained yet. What is the nature of this? Neither has āḻvār been freed from this material world; nor has he attained \[eternal\] kainkaryam \[in paramapadam\]; this being the case, how can he say “I have attained this aspect; I am yet to attain this other aspect”? Here, one \[kainkaryam\] is the goal, and the other \[being freed from material bondage\] is ancillary to that goal.  āḻvār considers to have attained freedom from bondage thinking “As I have said in the beginning itself in tiruviruttam 1 ‘*inninṟa nīrmai iniyāmuṟāmai’* (I cannot bear this existence in this lowly samsārm) and as he is fully capable \[of liberating me\], this bondage must have been extinguished \[by him\]”; and since [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) cannot sustain himself without being engaged in kainkaryam, and since he has not achieved it \[in paramapadam\] yet, he is longing for that.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.7.9. Idagilen

*idagilēn onṟattagillēn aimpulan vellagillēn kadavanāgik kālam tōṟum pūppaṟittēttagillēn mada vannenjam kādal kūra valvinaiyēn ayarppāyt tadavuginṟēn enguk kāṇban cakkarattaṇṇalaiyē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

onṟu idagilēn onṟu attagillēn – I will not give a handful of food or a glass of water for some one who is hungry or thirsty, respectively; aimpulan – the five senses; vellagillēn – unable to control them (from straying away into worldly pleasures); kadavanāgi – (based on these, to be engaged in bhakti yōgam) being an obedient person \[devotee\]; kālam tōṟum – at appropriate times (suitable for worship); pūppaṟittu – gathering flowers; ēttagillēn – not vorśipping and praising \[emperumān\]; madam – being desirous (of the goal); val – very firm attachment which cannot be shaken by any one; nenjam – heart; kādal kūra – with overflowing affection; val vinaiyēn – I who am having strong sins (which stop me from having enjoyment which matches such desire); ayarppāy – being ignorant; cakkaram – having enjoyable divine chakra; aṇṇalai – lord; tadavuginṟēn – searched (to see him); enguk kāṇban – where will I see him?

**Перевод:**

**I will not give a handful of food or a glass of water for some one who is hungry or thirsty, respectively; I am unable to control my five senses; I am not being an obedient person who gathers flowers at appropriate times for vorśipping and praising emperumān; \[Still\]  having a heart with desire, very firm attachment which cannot be shaken by any one and with overflowing affection, I who am having strong sins, being ignorant, searched to see the lord who is having enjoyable divine chakra; where will I see him?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In ninth pāsuram, āḻvār says “If I who don’t have the means such as karma yōga etc to see emperumān, desire to see him, is there any means to see him?”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “How will I being empty handed, yet desirous of seeing my lord who is carrying the enjoyable divine chakra, see him?”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*In ninth pāsuram, āḻvār says “Having nothing in me, if I desirously call him out to see him, is there any means for me to see him?”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. idagilēn onṟattagillēn aimpulan vellagillēn kadavanāgik kālam tōṟum pūppaṟittēttagillēn mada vannenjam kādal kūra valvinaiyēn ayarppāyt tadavuginṟēn enguk kāṇban cakkarattaṇṇalaiyē!*

- *idagilēn* – When one sees a person who is suffering and offers him something after feeling bad for his state, that will very much please [sarvēśvara](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s divine heart; I have not done anything like that.
- *onṟu attagillēn* – Even if one does not desire to spend any wealth for others, at least one can physically work by carrying water and offer that \[to a thirsty person\]; I did not do that as well.
- *aimpulan vellagillēn* – Even if one does not engage in helping others, should not one at least avoid what is hazardous for one’s own self? I did not restrain my senses from engaging in worldly pleasures.
- *kadavanāgi* … – I did not gather flowers and other materials matching the times, and vorśipped the divine feet of your highness, as ordained in śāstram. But, has [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) not engaged in vorśipping [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)? He has never engaged in sādana bhakti (bhakti yōga as a means to attain emperumān) which is explained in śāśtram; but he is only engaged in bhakti which is the only way for him to spend his life. If these were present, they can be counted as part of bhakti yōga; but āḻvār is saying, he has none of these. Here, āḻvār is not rejecting the activity itself \[like karma, jñāna, bhakti\], but the upāyatva (considering those acts as means) \[It is explained in mumukśuppadi sūtram 271 that, for a prapanna (surrendered person), karma becomes part of kainkaryam, jñāna becomes part of svarūpa prakāśa (realising the true nature clearly), bhakti becomes part of prāpya ruci (taste for attaining the goal) and prapatti (surrender) becomes part of svarūpa yādātmya jñāna (knowing the ultimate nature of the self)\].
- *mada val nenjam* – madappam indicates the tender nature of the heart – that is, when hearing “*bhagavat viśayam*” (matters about bhagavān), becoming engrossed in it at once. vanmai indicates that once a person becomes engrossed, it is difficult to take the heart away from it.
- kādalkūra – with such a heart, full of love
- *valvinaiyēn* … – I have sins which stop me from seeing him befitting my eagerness. I did not have my love fulfilled. Neither am I able to control my love towards him nor have I totally lost him since he will manifest himself to even those who slightly desire for him.

What was the nature of my sins?

- *ayarppāy* – Me who is foolish, ignorant.
- *tadavuginṟēn* – I am searching for him even if he appears in front of me. As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 42.24 “… *na tvā paśyāmi kausalyē! …*” (my eyes went behind rāma and have not returned till now. Oh kausalyē! Touch me with your hands).
- *enguk kāṇban* – How can I who is empty handed, see him?
- *cakkarattaṇṇalaiyē* – How can I see [sarvēśvara](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) who is holding the divine chakra in his hand? Like mother yaśōdā held kriṣṇa with butter in his hands, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) desires to see [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) with the sharp chakra in his hands.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.7.10. Cakkarattannale

*cakkarattaṇṇalē enṟu tāḻndu kaṇṇīr tadumba pakkam nōkki ninṟalandēn pāviyēn kāṇginṟilēn mikka jñāna mūrttiyāya vēda viḷakkinai en takka jñānak kaṇgaḷālē kaṇḍu taḻuvuvanē*

**Пословный перевод:**

cakkaram – manifesting the beautiful combination of your divine hand and the chakra; aṇṇalē – Oh my lord who enslaved me!; enṟu – saying this; tāḻndu – falling down on the ground (due to not being able to enjoy him); kaṇ nīr tadumba – having overflowing tears; pakkam nōkki – looking around; ninṟu – remained; alandēn – anguished; pāviyēn – I who am a sinner (sins, which stop me from seeing him); kāṇginṟilēn – unable to see him; mikka jñāna mūrttiyāya – being natural embodiment of boundless knowledge; vēdam viḷakkinai – one who is seen through the lamp of vēdam; en – for me (who desires to see him physically and anguishing due to that); takka – matching; jñānam – jñānam (wisdom); kaṇgaḷālē – eyes; kaṇḍu – see; taḻuvuvan – will embrace him

**Перевод:**

**Saying “Oh my lord who enslaved me by manifesting the beautiful combination of your divine hand and the chakra!”, falling down on the ground and having overflowing tears, I remained anguished; I who am a sinner, was unable to see him; with my matching jñānam as the \[internal\] eyes, I will embrace emperumān who is the natural embodiment of boundless knowledge and is seen through the lamp of vēdam. As the love became the cause for anguish due to not being able to see him, the internal shining wisdom also became the cause for anguish.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In tenth pāsuram, āḻvār becomes distressed thinking “How is this internal vision occurring which affects my joy of being forgetful of him when he is not seen physically?”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “When I desired to see emperumān who is known from vēdam, with his divine hand and chakra, and did not get that physical vision, should he shine in my internal vision, making it impossible for me to forget him and sustain myself?”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. cakkarattaṇṇalē enṟu tāḻndu kaṇṇīr tadumba pakkam nōkki ninṟalandēn pāviyēn kāṇginṟilēn mikka jñāna mūrttiyāya vēda viḷakkinai en takka jñānak kaṇgaḷālē kaṇḍu taḻuvuvanē*

- *cakkarattaṇṇalē enṟu tāḻndu* – Falling on the ground saying “Oh lord who enslaved me showing your divine chakra!”.
- *kaṇ nīr tadumba* – To have overflowing tears in the eyes. The limit of āḻvār’s sorrow is known from his tears.
- *pakkam nōkki ninṟu alandēn* – Looked eagerly at the direction from where he is likely to come and became vexed \[due to his not coming\]. As described in viṣṇu darmam 68 “*paramāpadamāpanna:*” (fell in great danger).
- *pāviyēn kāṇginṟilēn* – Though in great danger \[deserving to be helped by him\], since I was a great sinner, I did not get to see him.

Though I am unable to see him, did I at least become saved by forgetting him due to his not shining in my heart?

- *mikka jñāna mūrttiyāya* – one who is the embodiment of complete knowledge.
- *vēda viḷakkinai* – One who is seen through the lamp of vēdam; also explained as – one who is revealed in vēdam.
- *en takka* … – Matching my nature, I will have an internal vision and through that I will see [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) and enjoy him. As the love became the cause for anguish due to not being able to see him, the internal shining wisdom in the heart also became the cause for anguish. The jñānam (knowledge) and bhakti (devotion) explained in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.1.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/03/thiruvaimozhi-1-1-1-uyarvara-uyarnalam/) “*mayarvaṟa madi nalam aruḷinan*” (emperumān blessed faultless jñānam and bhakti), became the hurdles themselves. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says “Do I even need this knowledge which matches my stature, which stops me from forgetting him and sustaining myself?”.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.7.11. Taluvi ninra

*taḻuvi ninṟa kādal tannāl tāmaraikkaṇṇan tannaik kuḻuvu mādat ten kurugūr māṟan satakōpan sol vaḻuvilāda oṇ tamiḻgaḷ āyirattuḷ ippattum taḻuvap pādi āda vallār vaikuntam ēṟuvarē*

**Пословный перевод:**

taḻuvi – being an inherent aspect of the svarūpam (true nature); ninṟa – firm; kādal tannāl – due to great desire to enjoy; tāmaraik kaṇṇan tannai – on sarvēśvara who is having infinitely enjoyable divine eyes which are the cause for such great desire; kuḻuvum – group of; mādam – having mansions; then kurugūr – the leader of āḻvārtirunagari; māṟan – having great family lineage; satakōpan – nammāḻvār‘s; vaḻu ilāda – without missing (any of bhagavān’s qualities); oḷ tamiḻgaḷ – in drāvida (tamiḻ) language which is available to pursue for all, in the form of distinguished teachings; āyirattuḷ – among the thousand pāsurams; ippattum – this decad; taḻuva – to be fixated in the heart; pādi – sing; Ada – to dance with great emotions (out of overwhelming love); vallār – those who are able to; vaikuntam ēṟuvar – will ascend to paramapadam (where there is unlimited enjoyment)

**Перевод:**

**nammāḻvār, who is having great family lineage, who is the leader of āḻvārtirunagari, which is having group of mansions, due to great desire to enjoy, which is an inherent aspect of the svarūpam and is firm, sang thousand pāsurams in drāvida (tamiḻ) language which is available to be pursued by all, in the form of distinguished teachings, on sarvēśvara who is having infinitely enjoyable divine eyes which are the cause for such desire to enjoy him; those who have this decad among those thousand pāsurams without missing anything, fixated in their heart, who are able to sing and dance with great emotions will ascend to paramapadam.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the end, āḻvār says “Those who learn this decad can enter paramapadam (spiritual realm) where they can eternally be united with emperumān“.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār mercifully explains that the result of meditating upon this decad and becoming overwhelmed with joy is to ascend to paramapadam.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. taḻuvi ninṟa kādal tannāl tāmaraikkaṇṇan tannaik kuḻuvu mādat then kurugūr māṟan satakōpan sol vaḻuvilāda oṇ tamiḻgaḷ āyirattuḷ ippattum taḻuvap pādi Ada vallār vaikuntam ēṟuvarē*

- *taḻuvi ninṟa kādal tannāl* – My love which cannot be given up even if said “I will give up”, which always accompanies me.
- *tāmaraik kaṇṇan tannai* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is identifying the eyes which worked to cultivate this love in him for [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/).
- *kuḻuvu mādat then kurugūr* – As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 127.5 “*sarvanca kuśalam gruhē*” (everyone is well at home), the whole of [āḻvārtirunagari](http://azhwarthirunagari.koyil.org/) was overflowing with many who consoled each other saying “As [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s desire/sorrow is increasing, it is only a matter of time before [sarvēśvara](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) arrives here”.
- *māṟan* – One who changed samsāram (material realm) \[to become devoted to [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)\].
- *satakōpan* – One who is enemy for those who turn away from bhagavān.
- *sol vaḻuvilāda* – Among thousand pāsurams, this decad which is spoken (as good instructions to be heard by everyone without discrimination) without missing anything in this auspicious calling out in separation from bhagavān.
- *taḻuvap pādi Ada vallār* – āḻvār’s pure mood and actions cannot occur in anyone else; if one can recite this decad even with slight emulation of such mood (those who can dance with such emotions).
- *vaikuntam ēṟuvarē* – Giving up this samsāram where one can only call out with desire to see him, will ascend to nitya vibhūti (paramapadam) where there is eternal enjoyment.

*kuḻuvu mādam* – closely built mansions. *tenkurugūr* – also explained as, beautiful [āḻvārtirunagari](http://azhwarthirunagari.koyil.org/).

## 4.8 Eralum iraiyonum

## 4.8.1. Eralum iraiyonum

*ēṟāḷum iṟaiyōnum tisaimuganum tirumagaḷum kūṟāḷum tani udamban kulangulamā asurargaḷai nīṟāgum padiyāga nirumittup padai totta māṟāḷan kavarāda maṇi māmai kuṟaivilamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ēṟu āḷum – having ruśabha vāhanam (bull as his vehicle); iṟaiyōnum – rudra who considers himself to be the īśvara (lord) (of the world as said in “īśōham sarvadēhinām” (lord of all creatures)); tisai muganum – catur mukha (four headed) brahmā who is qualified to engage in variegated creation; tirumagaḷum – lakshmi, who is inseparable from him and who is his wealth; kūṟu – individually (part by part); āḷum – enjoy and consider to be their own abode; tani – unique, and having spiritually distinguished; udamban – having divine body; kulam kulamā – groups and groups of; asurargaḷai – asuras (demoniac people); nīṟu āgum padiyāga – to transform them into particles of dust; nirumittu – vowing in his divine heart; padai totta – one who took up weapons and fought; māṟāḷan – hostile controller; kavarāda – not desired; maṇi māmai – radiant complexion; kuṟaivu ilam – there is no use

**Перевод:**

**emperumān is having a unique and spiritually distinguished divine body which is individually enjoyed and considered to be their own abode by rudra who considers himself to be the īśvara and is having the bull as his vehicle, catur mukha brahmā who is qualified to engage in variegated creation and śrī mahālakśmi who is inseparable from him and who is his wealth; there is no use of my radiant complexion when it is not desired by emperumān who is hostile controller and who, vowing in his divine heart, took up weapons and fought groups and groups of asuras to transform them into partices of dust.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In first pāsuram, parānkuśa nāyaki \[āḻvār in feminine mood\] says “There is no use with my best bodily complexion which is not desired by emperumān who is a great guṇavān (one with good qualities) and who is capable of destroying the enemies”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. ēṟāḷum iṟaiyōnum tisaimuganum tirumagaḷum kūṟāḷum tani udamban kulangulamā asurargaḷai nīṟāgum padiyāga nirumittup padai totta māṟāḷan kavarāda maṇi māmai kuṟaivilamē*

- *ēṟāḷum …* – parānkuśa nāyaki tells “I have lost the divine form \[body of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)\] which is the abode for even those who are very prideful”. She says “I am unable to attain what is attained even by a kāpāli and kandan \[Both indicating rudra – kāpali – one who is having skull in his hand, kandan – one who is wearing torn clothes; another explanation kandan indicates brahmā who is born in the lotus in the divine naval of emperumān\]”.
- *ēṟāḷum* – When [sarvēśvara](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) has periya tiruvadi (garuda) who is vēdātmā (the soul of vēdam) as his vehicle, rudra too, like wandering mendicants, pridefully thinks ‘I have a bull as my vehicle’.
- *āḷum* – This is his \[rudra’s\] ubhaya vibhūti \[sarcasm – as [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is ruling over spiritual and material realms, here rudra is said to be ruling over the bull\].
- *iṟaiyōnum* – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is the [sarvēśvara](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) controlling ubhaya vibhūti; as \[a small/useless\] kaḷḷi (spurge) plant is mistaken as mahā vrukśa (great tree), he \[rudra\] considers himself to be īśvara. \[This is to explain that bhagavān is not the same as other dēvatās ever\] While dharma \[form/attribute\] and darmi \[soul/substratum\] have aikyam \[indicated in unison\], two darmis \[souls\] have no aikyam \[cannot be indicated as the same\] \[Here it is only talking about aikyam at the śarīra-śarīri level, that is, a soul and body are considered to be united and always indicated together. But there is no svarūpa aikyam, that is, the entities themselves (soul and body) are different from each other\].
- *tisai muganum* – One who is having four heads to recite four vēdams through each mouth to engage in creation and who pridefully thinks that he is the creator.
- *tirumagaḷum* – And [periya pirāttiyār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/) who is as explained in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 21.15 “*ananyā rāghavēṇāham*” (I am inseparable from śrī rāma).
- *kūṟāḷum* … – Having a unique body which can individually (part-by-part) be occupied by aforementioned personalities. They have full control over their own regions so that pirātti’s assistants will not come and disturb those dēvatās’ regions and those dēvatās’ assistants will not come and disturb pirātti’s region. His divine form is even more glorious than his divine nature. His divine form is the abode for everyone. And I have lost such easily approachable/attainable [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/).
- *kulam kulamā* – Have I lost him due to having hurdles in embracing him? Previous section is similar to samkśēpa rāmāyaṇam “*kōnvasmin sāmpradam lōkē guṇavān*” (Who is the one with the most auspicious qualities in this world at this time?); this \[section\] is similar to “*vīryavān*” (who is the one with valour?). Groups and groups of demoniac people.
- *nīṟāgum padiyāga nirumittu* – As said in śrī bhagavat gītā 11.33 “*nihitā:pūrvamēva*” (They have been already killed by me \[through my will\]). When \[duryōdana\] declared he does not need any of you \[pāṇḍavas\], I vowed that they will be burnt to ashes.
- *padai totta* – The same [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who creates the universe through his divine will, physically jumps out with his weapons when it comes to destroying the enemies of his devotees. During sruśti (creation) etc, he would remain satya sankalpa (one who has accomplished will/vow) and for the enemies of his devotees, he vourld remain asatya sankalpan (would even lie to have them destroyed).
- *nīṟāgum padiyāga* – As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 94.22 “*cinnam binnam śarair dagdam*” (one who was cut, cleaved or burnt by the arrows), he will vow to turn them into dust and take up arms \[to accomplish that\]. As said in “*yajñavignakaram hanyām pāṇḍavānāncadurhrutam*” (I will torture those who create hurdles for yāgams (fire sacrifices) and who trouble pāṇḍavas), he will attack those who strangle my neck \[causing hurdles for yagāms\] and those who attack my life-spot \[pāṇḍavas, his devotees are like his life\].
- *māṟāḷan* – majestic/firm; enemy. When duryōdana invited kriṣṇa to eat at his residence he refused saying as in mahābhāratam udyōga parvam 74.27 “*dviśadannam na bhoktavyam ca dviśantam naiva bhōjayēt*” (Neither can one consume the food given by one’s enemy, nor can one feed one’s enemy), will argue considering his devotees’ enemies as his own.
- *kavarāda* – After the enemies have been killed \[in the fight\], when he is thirsty and needs water, if he does not arrive and embrace me, I have no desire for my beautiful complexion. Only when he likes my complexion, there is use for it; when that liking is not there in him, it is only a hurdle.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.
