## 4.8.2. Manimamai

*maṇimāmai kuṟaivillā malar mādar uṟai mārban aṇimānat tavarait tōḷ adal āḻit tadakkaiyan paṇimānam piḻaiyāmē adiyēnaip paṇi koṇḍa maṇimāyan kavarāda mada nenjāl kuṟaivilamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

maṇi – infinitely radiant (due to eternal union with emperumān); māmai – in the complexion; kuṟaivillā – one who is having no shortcoming; malar mādar – the best among women, śrī mahālkśmi, who is having enjoyability due to the tender nature etc as a result of having the high birth of being born in a flower; uṟai – eternally residing; mārban – having the divine chest; aṇi – decorated by ornaments; mānam – elongated; tada – well rounded; varai – like perfectly carved out of a mountain; tōḷ – having shoulders; adal – capable of destroying the enemies; āḻi – having divine chakra; tadakkaiyan – having huge hands; paṇi mānam – aspects in rendering service; piḻaiyāmē – without missing; adiyēnai – me who has the nature of a servitor; paṇi koṇḍa – engaging in matching service; maṇi māyan – one who has black complexion like a bluish precious stone; kavarāda – not desiring; mada nenjāl – obedient heart; kuṟaivu ilam – there is no use

**Перевод:**

**The best among women, śrī mahālakśmi who is having no shortcoming in her infinitely radiant complexion, who is having enjoyability due to the tender nature etc as a result of having the high birth of being born in a flower; emperumān who is having such pirātti eternally residing in his chest, who is having the shoulders which are decorated by ornaments, elongated, well rounded and appear to be perfectly carved out of a mountain, who is having huge hands where he is having the divine chakra which is capable of destroying the enemies,  who engaged me  who has the nature of a servitor, in service that matches my nature without missing any aspect in rendering services to him; if such emperumān who has black complexion like a bluish precious stone is not desiring for my obedient heart, there is no use of that heart.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, parānkuśa nāyaki says “There is no use of my heart which is not desired by emperumān, the ultimate goal, who enslaved me by showing his divine form which is united with pirātti (śrī mahālakśmi)”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Second pāsuram. parānkuśa nāyaki says “What is the use of my obedient heart which is not desired by emperumān, who enslaved me by showing his divine form which is united with pirātti (śrī mahālakśmi), which is the cause for his auspicious qualities”. maṇimāmai kuṟaivillā malar mādar uṟai mārban aṇimānat tavarait tōḷ adal āḻit tadakkaiyan paṇimānam piḻaiyāmē adiyēnaip paṇi koṇḍa maṇimāyan kavarāda mada nenjāl kuṟaivilamē*

- *maṇi māmai kuṟaivillā* – One who need not say “*maṇi māmai kuṟaivilamē*” \[as I said in the previous pāsuram\]. [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who enslaved me by her \[śrī mahālakśmi\] eternal presence with him. Even when śrī mahālakśmi who said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 116.45 “*na kascinnāparādayti*” (there is no one who does not commit mistakes) was with him, if he disregards me, what is the use of my belongings \[like my heart\]?
- *malar mādar* – Not just the complexion, she is having tenderness which never lets emperumān separate from her. Being like the embodiment of the buds/fragrance of the flower.
- *uṟai mārban* – One who has the divine chest where she \[pirātti\] eternally resides. Born in the lotus flower and eternally residing in his divine chest. He who is having the divine chest which makes her think that the flower, in which she took birth, is like a thorny forest. tiruvaḷḷuvar too said in tirukkuṟaḷ 1120 “*aniccamum annattin tūviyum mādar adikku nerunjip paḻam*” (When compared to the tender feet of damsels, the anicca flowers and the feathers of swan appear like thorns). Like the muktātmā who would not think about his lives in samsāra (material realm), śrī mahālakśmi never thinks about the flower where she was born – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is having such divine chest. Only if sītā pirātti thought about śrī mitilā after marrying śrī rāma, she will think about the flower. I am missing out on the form which she says in tiruvāimoḻi 6.10.10 “*agalagillēn*” (I will never leave).
- *aṇi mānat tada varait tōḷ* – aṇi means ornaments. mānam means length. As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam kiśkintā kāṇḍam 3.14 “*sarva bhūsaṇa bhūśārhā:*” (the shoulders which deserve to be decorated by all ornaments), nanjīyar mercifully explains this as “the shoulders which are ornaments to ornaments themselves”. A tamiḻ poet/scholar explained this as “aṇi means beauty, mānam means greatness – thus, shoulders which have great beauty”. By this definition also, it implies that the shoulders themselves are decoration for the ornaments. As said in the same ślōkam, “*āyatāśca suvrutāśca …*“, one who is having the shoulders which are long, well rounded and cannot be overcome by anyone.
- *adal āḻit tadak kaiyan* – One who is having the divine chakra in his perfect hand; the divine chakra is of the nature that, being unnecessarily fearful about the divine togetherness of [pirātti](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/) and [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), he is always alert for battles, and will destroy the enemies. His actions can be seen on top of emperumān’s hands.
- *paṇi mānam piḻaiyāmē* – paṇi means kainkaryam (service), mānam means measurement – without missing even the smallest services. As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 31.25 “*aham sarvam kariśyāmi*” (lakśmaṇa says – I will carry out all kainkaryams).
- *adiyēnaip paṇi koṇḍa* – Like emperumān accepted the kainkaryam of iḷaiya perumāḷ (lakśamaṇa), he accepted the kainkaryam of āḻvār too, while being together with pirātti.
- *adiyēnai* – As said in “*kumarirundu pōgamē*” (without getting my śēśatvam wasted, engaging me fully). That is, being an entity which is fully subservient to bhagavān, not being used in the service of him who is the apt lord. An incident is mercifully explained here – Once during a tadīyārādanam (distribution of prasādam to śrīvaiṣṇavas) in the mutt where [emperumānār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/emperumanar/) was residing, [kidāmbi āccān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/kidambi-achchan/) was serving water to the śrīvaiṣṇavas while they were eating \[In those days, offering water, i.e., pouring water directly into the mouth of those who need water, was a separate service. Since one should not eat/drink anything with the left hand, this practice of some one pouring water directly into the mouth of those who needed it, existed\]. When a śrīvaiṣṇava wanted water, kidāmbi āccān goes to him, stands by his side and poured the water. Seeing this from a distance, emperumānār rushed to āccān and banged on his back and chastised āccān saying “Should you not be pouring water standing across the person to ensure regulated flow of water?”. Hearing this, āccān said “*paṇi mānam piḻaiyāmē adiyēnaip paṇi koṇḍa*” (engaging me in service without seeing my faults, and reforming me as necessary).
- *paṇi koṇḍa maṇi māyan* – He did not engage me in kainkaryam saying “daha, paca” (burn him, eat him); but by relaxing his upper body cloth (shawl) \[manifesting his divine form\]. Having a dark complexion like that of a blue gem.
- *kavarāda* – If he does not show his divine form and let me enjoy him, what is the use of my obedient heart? nanjīyar mercifully explains this here – Since [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who desired for my heart then as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 4.3.2](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/01/thiruvaimozhi-4-3-2-pusum-sandhu/) “*pūsum sāndu en nenjamē*” (my heart is the sandalwood paste he applies), is disregarding it now – as a beloved consort would break the container with the sandalwood paste inside it, in front of her beloved husband  when he comes late, here āḻvār also says “I don’t want my heart”. Will I not be patient, had pirātti not been with him? Will I not be patient, had he not manifested his beautiful shoulders to me? Will I not be patient thinking that he is not the apt goal, had he not manifested the beautiful combination of his divine hand and chakra? Will I not be patient, had he attracted me through his qualities \[so I can think about various aspects of him and engage in them\] instead of his divine beautiful form \[which cannot be forgotten\]?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.8.3. Mada nenjal

*mada nenjāl kuṟaivillā magaḷ tāy seydoru pēycci vida nanja mulai suvaitta migu jñānc ciṟu kuḻavi pada nāgaṇaik kidanda paruvarait tōḷ param purudan nedumāyan kavarāda niṟaivināl kuṟaivilamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

madam nenjāl – having an affectionate heart (towards the nursing baby); kuṟaivillā – without any shortcoming; tāy magaḷ – mother (yaśōdā); seydu – arriving in the form; oru – distinguished to defeat (the opponent); pēycci – the lady devil’s; vidam nanjam mulai – the breast which is covered with strong poison (where the poison of this world appears like nectar, when compared to her poison); suvaitta – completely sucked out; migu jñānam – knowledgeable about different tastes; siṟu kuḻavi – being an innocent toddler; padam nāgattu aṇai – on the serpent bed (where the serpent’s hoods are expanded due to coming in contact with emperumān); kidanda – one who rests; paru varai tōḷ – one who is having mountain like huge shoulders; param purudan – (as said in “uttama:puruśa:“) being the supreme lord; nedu māyan – kriṣṇa who is having infinitely amazing qualities and activities; kavarāda – not desired by; niṟaivināl – completeness in my feminine nature; kuṟaivu ilam – what use is there?

**Перевод:**

**pūtanā (the lady devil) arrived in the form of mother yaśōdā who has no shortcoming in her affectionate heart; kaṇṇan emperumān, being an innocent toddler, knowledgeable about different tastes, completely sucked \[her vital air\] from her breast which is covered with strong poison; what is the use of my completeness in my feminine nature when it is not desired by such emperumān who rests on the serpent bed, who is having mountain like huge shoulders, who is the supreme lord and who is having infinitely amazing qualities and activities?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In third pāsuram, parānkuśa nāyaki says “I don’t need my modesty which is not desired by the greatly distinguished emperumān who showed great affection towards me previously”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, parānkuśa nāyaki desiring to explain aniśta nivrutti (removal of unfavourable aspects) etc which make emperumān the upāyam (means), in the subsequent pāsurams fully, first starts explaining the killing of pūtanā who appeared as an anūkūla śatru (enemy in disguise), and says “There is no use of my modesty when it is not desired by kriṣṇa who descended from the serpent bed”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Third pāsuram. parānkuśa nāyaki says “I don’t need my modesty which is not desired by emperumān who is capable of destroying the enemies, who is greatly distinguished and who was greatly affectionate towards me previously”. mada nenjāl kuṟaivillā magaḷ tāy seydoru pēycci vida nanja mulai suvaitta migu jñānc ciṟu kuḻavi pada nāgaṇaik kidanda paruvarait tōḷ param purudan nedumāyan kavarāda niṟaivināl kuṟaivilamē*

- *mada nenjāl kuṟaivillā* – madappam – tenderness; that is having a soft heart. pūtanā assumed the care which is usually shown by mother yaśōdā while she nurses [kriṣṇa](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/). While she had hatred inside her towards kriṣṇa, externally she manifested favourable intent.
- *magaḷ tāy seydu* – makkaḷ has become magaḷ – it indicates human being. Though she was a devil, she assumed the form of a human being, that too assuming kriṣṇa’s mother’s form as said in periya tirumoḻi 1.3.1 “*peṟṟa tāy pōl*” (like his own mother).
- *oru pēycci* – How wicked! Implying “ūnparallel wickedness”. It can also be considered as disregard for her as saying “some devil”, due to [parānkuśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) having anger on pūtanā’s act of trying to kill kriṣṇa.
- *vida nanjam* – Repetition of poison by saying “viśam” and “nanjam” – this implies the heavy nature of the poison; when compared to this, other poisons appear to be nectar.
- *pēycci vida* – To have her life taken away.
- *nanja mulai suvaitta* – One who consumed \[through\] the poison-afflicted breast. As said in periya tirumoḻi 1.3.1 “*uyirai vaṟṟa vāngi uṇḍa vāyan*” ([emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who sucked her life), he sucked in such a manner that along with milk, her life too came out; to get her life out of her, as said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 4.5.5 “*prānasahitam papau*” (along with the life).
- *migu jñānac ciṟu kuḻavi* – Though he was an infant, due to knowing the different tastes, he spotted that “this is not my mother’s breast; it is someone else’s breast” and fed on it. Alternative explanation – though she comes as his mother, and though he may consider her to be his mother, the nature of the object \[poisonous milk\] will have its effect.
- *pada nāgaṇaik kidanda* – His resting place also matches what he consumes. He consumes poison and reclines on a poisonous serpent. Poison is the antidote for another poison. Two explanations – after killing the enemy, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) goes and rests on the serpent; another explanation – as said in hari vamsam 113.62 “*nāgaparyankamutsrujya*” (he descends from the serpent bed), he steps out from his bed and kills the enemy. When he hears the cry of his devotee, his heart will not be satisfied with “*bhōga*” (bhōga means enjoyment as well as serpent). Due to the joy of sarvēśvara resting on him, his (ādi śēśan’s) hoods will be expanded. Just as demoniac entities will be killed when they approach \[emperumān\] as said in mūnṟām tiruvantādi 66 “*vāynda madu kaidaparum vayiṟurugi māṇḍār*” (even the brave madu and kaitap got killed), when devotees approach emperumān, they will end up with a joyful life.
- *paru varait tōḷ* – The changes in the ēkarūpa (unchanging form) of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) after coming in contact with tiruvanantāḻvān (ādi śēśan) is explained. For emperumān, except for no changes/impacts due to karma \[puṇya, pāpa\], if we say that there is no change at all, then there is no point in desiring to embrace such emperumān.
- *param purudan* – As a diamond pressed on a gold plate will shine more than ever before, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), after reclining on ādi śēśa, appears to be “*sarvādika*” (greater than all).
- *nedu māyan* – After knowing the flavour of resting on my lap, he does not rest on the lap of ādi śēśan with satisfaction. (One who has huge mountain like shoulders; being the supreme lord as said in “*uttama:puruśa:*‘; [kriṣṇa](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who has infinitely amazing qualities and activities.)
- *kavarāda* – If one who showed great attachment like this before, disregards me now, what is the use of my strītva (feminine nature)?
- *niṟaivu* – modesty. That is, the feminine nature, where a woman does not reveal to others, what is in her mind.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.8.4. Niraivinal

*niṟaivināl kuṟaivillā nedum paṇait tōḷ madap pinnai poṟaiyinān mulai aṇaivān poru vidai ēḻ adarttuganda kaṟaiyinār tuvarudukkaik kadaiyāvin kaḻikōṟkaic caṟaiyinār kavarāda taḷir niṟattāl kuṟaivilamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

niṟaivināl – completeness in strītvam (femininity); kuṟaivillā – without any shortcoming; nedum paṇait tōḷ – having long and well grown shoulder; madam – being modest with respect to her beloved consort; pinnai – nappinnaip pirātti; mulai – bosom; aṇaivān – to embrace; poṟaiyināl – with pride (along with sorrow); poru vidai ēḻ – the seven bulls which were all set to fight him; adarttu uganda – killed them (and considering “I have now fulfilled my desire”) and became happy about it; kaṟaiyinār – his clothes having stains \[due to gathering fruits in the forest); tuvar – tree bark; udukkai – garments; kadaiyāvin – bamboo container (which is used to collect the milk from cow); kaḻikōlum – stick which is carried by covherd boys; kai – having them in his hands; caṟaiyinār – one who is wearing the waist string with bells (on his waist); kavarāda – not liked; taḷir niṟattāl – sprout like reddish complexion; kuṟaivilam – no use (for us)

**Перевод:**

**emperumān pridefully killed the seven bulls which were all set to fight him, to embrace the bosom of nappinnaip pirātti who has completeness in strītvam without any shortcoming in it, who has long and well grown shoulder and who is modest with respect to her beloved consort, and became happy about it. There is no use of my sprout like reddish complexion if that is not liked by emperumān whose tree bark garments are having stains, who is having bamboo container and stick which is carried by covherd boys in his hands, and who is wearing the waist string with bells.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In fourth pāsuram, parānkuśa nāyaki says “I have no use for my tender sprout like complexion which is not liked by kriṣṇa who enjoys his activities which are performed by him for the sake of his devotees”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, parānkuśa nāyaki says “There is no use of my reddish complexion which is not liked by kriṣṇa who killed the seven bulls to enjoy his beloved nappinnai”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Fourth pāsuram. parānkuśa nāyaki says “I don’t need this complexion of mine which is not liked by kriṣṇa who pampered the girls instead of caring for himself”. niṟaivināl kuṟaivillā nedum paṇait tōḷ madap pinnai poṟaiyinān mulai aṇaivān poru vidai ēḻ adarttuganda kaṟaiyinār tuvarudukkaik kadaiyāvin kaḻikōṟkaic caṟaiyinār kavarāda taḷir niṟattāl kuṟaivilamē*

- *niṟaivināl kuṟaivillā* – nappinnai who is having no shortcoming in her strītvam (modesty), i.e., being without any reaction even after seeing kriṣṇa taking on the bulls to marry her. When there is reason to show reaction, she remained reactionless \[that is real modesty\].
- *nedum paṇait tōḷ* – Previously her ātma guṇam (internal quality – modesty) was explained. Now her physical quality is explained.
- *nedum paṇai …* – Long, well grown shoulder. Long bamboo shoot like shoulder. Her beauty is such that, even by engaging in great tasks, one will desire to get her.
- *madap pinnai* – very tender natured nappinnai.
- *mulai aṇaivān* – to embrace her.
- *poṟaiyināl* – Tolerating patiently. When the bulls banged on him with their horns and hooves, he considered them to be coming in contact with nappinnai’s bosom.
- *poru vidai* – Not any ordinary bull. They were possessed with demoniac forces and were rearing to fight with kriṣṇa. Not one or two; he held the neck of all the seven bulls and strangled them.
- *uganda* – He became joyous thinking that he now got nappinnai.
- *kaṟaiyinār tuvarudukkai* – He wears tree-barks which had lots of stains. Here it is talking about the garment which is worn by covherds to avoid getting them torn by thorns when they go to the forest. While it is saying “*tuvar*” (reddish colour), it is also saying “*kaṟaiyinār*” (stained), since they collect wild fruits from the forest and the essence which drips from them will lead to lot of stains on their garment; so it is a stained garment. She does not even desire for nice yellow garments as said in nācciyār tirumoḻi 13.1 “*pītaka vaṇṇa ādai*“, and she ([parānkuśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)) wants to embrace kriṣṇa with his garment which he wore while protecting cows.
- *kadaiyā* – The covherds will always carry a bamboo container, which they can use at suitable times to milk the cows.
- *kaḻi kōl kai* – *kaḻi kōl –* the stick which is used to throw and mark the distance where the cows can reach up to. Covherds who carry the bamboo container and stick.
- *kadaiyāvin kaḻi kōl kai* – Also explained as – the covherds who carry the stick to control wild cows and milk them \[Here kadaiyā is explained as wild cow\].
- *kaḻi kōl* – When the calves go along with the cow, to stop them from feeding on their mother cows, they will be tied with a stick in front of their face – it is talking about that stick. As sanyāsis do not have a permanent residence, they will carry their plate (container) etc along with them; the covherds too will carry these along with them and will rest where they find grass and water.
- *caṟaiyinār* – Three explanations 1) caṟai means a type of bell; the covherds usually will tie a bell on their waist string so that when they lead, the cows and calves will follow them obediently based on that sound. 2) Alternative explanation – caṟai means lowly. Those who are born in lowly covherd families which cannot be compared with other higher varṇas. 3) caṟai means lazy. While other covherds may partially bathe during special occasions such as viśu etc., due to running behind the cows, kriṣṇa would not even do that. nappinnai desires to embrace this form of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), where he does not bother about himself while protecting those who need to be protected. śrī rāmāyaṇanam “*dīkśitam vrata sampannam varājinataramśucim \| kurankaśrungapāṇinca paśyantītvā bhajāmyaham*“.
- *kavarāda taḷir niṟam* – What is the use of divine complexion which is not desired by him? What is the use of the complexion/glow of sītāp pirātti who arrived after the killing of rāvaṇa, the complexion of which was not liked by śrī rāma himself? There is no other consorts of emperumān who have spoken like [parānkuśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) with respect to complexion/method. What is the difference between “*maṇi māmai kuṟaivilam*” which was said in first pāsuram and “*taḷir niṟattāl kuṟaivilam*” which is explained here? There, maṇi māmai speaks about her beauty and tenderness. and here it speaks about her complexion; if we consider that complexion was explained in that pāsuram, here it may be said that parānkuśa nāyaki is explaining about the beautiful complexion. Explains the śrī rāmāyaṇa ślōkam here:
   - *dīkśitam* … – As pirātti was born in janaka kulam (clan) which is very strict in following customs/practices, she liked śrī rāma’s form; as nappinnai was born in covherd clan where there is no requirement for strictly following customs/practices, she desired for the divine form of kriṣṇa.
   - *dīkśitam* – She is saying “I am desiring to see kriṣṇa as the lord, who is having special garment, having butter applied all over his body”.
   - *vrata sampannam* – When riśi (vaśiśsta – the sage and mentor) tells him to fast one session, śrī rāma would think “He is caring for our tender body and diluting it” and would continue fasting for four days – that is due to his total obedience in śāstram.
   - *varājinataram* – His special garments are even more attractive than silk garments.
   - *śucim* – When \[sage vaśiśta\] says “You cannot come in contact with any woman; but when you come in contact with your obedient wife, there is nothing wrong with it; so, you can not come in contact with any other woman”; and he gets unnecessary doubt whether sītā’s clothes touched his and will bathe fully to purify him \[Here, kriṣṇa is opposite to these discipline\].
   - *kurankaśrunga pāṇinca* – Even more than “*ēka vastraradarōdanvī”* (wearing one garment and holding the bow), I prefer seeing him with deer horn.
   - *paśyantītvā bhajāmyaham* – As she prays for the ultimate goal, incidentals \[like performing mangaḷāśāsanam\] will naturally occur in between. Whatever one prays, that is for what is visible only; so, she prays to see him. Even there \[spiritual realm\], it is said as “*sadā paśyanti*” (always seeing [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)). In between she is performing mangaḷāśāsanam to avert evil-eyes during the process; as the ultimate goal is prayed for, the incidentals such as mangaḷāśāsanam will happen naturally. \[An example from the life of sāvitri is cited here to establish how one goal is attained while another goal is desired\] sāvitri showed her husband and prayed that he begets many children through him \[sāvitri desired to marry satyavān; nārada muni appeared there and told her that his life span is short; yet she insisted to marry him. Soon after her marriage, the servitors of yama came and took away satyavān and sāvitri followed them. When yama enquired what she wanted saying that he will fulfil her desire, she said “I want to have many children with my husband”. yama did not have any choice other than letting satyavān live long\].

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.8.5. Talir nirattal

*taḷir niṟattāl kuṟaivillāt tanic ciṟaiyil viḷappuṟṟa kiḷi moḻiyāḷ kāraṇamāk kiḷar arakkan nagar eritta kaḷi malart tuḻāy alangal kamaḻ mudiyan kadal jñālattu aḷi mikkān kavarāda aṟivināl kuṟaivilamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

taḷir niṟattāl – with the attractive tender sprout like complexion; kuṟaivillā – being complete; tanic ciṟaiyil – (like the rays which were separated from the sun) alone (amidst the rākśasis) in a confined manner; viḷappuṟṟa – being famous (to be glorified all over the world as the one who became imprisoned to protect others); kiḷi moḻiyāḷ – sītāp pirātti who has a sweet voice like that of a parrot; kāraṇamā – for her sake; kiḷar – being tumultuous out of being unjust; arrakkan – rāvaṇa’s; kiḷar nagar – wealthy city; eritta – one who burnt it down; kaḷi malar – having honey, well blossomed; tuḻāy alangal – by the tiruttuḻāy (tuḷasi) garland; kamaḻ – best fragrance; mudiyan – wearing the crown; kadal jñālattu – the earth which is surrounded by ocean; aḷi mikkān – mercifully lived manifesting his cool mercy; kavarāda – not liked; aṟivināl – knowledge; kuṟaivilam – we have no use

**Перевод:**

**śrī rāma burnt down the unjust tumultuous rāvana’s wealthy city for the sake of sītāp pirātti who is complete with the attractive tender sprout like complexion, who remained alone in a confined manner, was famous \[for her mercy to being imprisoned to protect others\] and who has a sweet voice like that of a parrot. Such emperumān, after ascending the throne in ayōdyā, who was wearing the crown which is given best fragrance by the well blossomed tuḷasi garland on it which is having honey, mercifully lived manifesting his cool mercy in the earth which is surrounded by ocean. We have no use of our knowledge which is not liked by such emperumān.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In fifth pāsuram, parānkuśa nāyaki says “There is no use of my knowledge which is not desired by my greatly beloved śrī rāma, the son of daśarata”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, parānkuśa nāyaki says “What is the use of my knowledge when it is not desired by cakravarti tirumagan (the son of emperor daśarata) śrī rāma, who killed rāvaṇa et al who committed needless offenses towards sītā, the divine daughter of king janaka”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. taḷir niṟattāl kuṟaivillāt tanic ciṟaiyil viḷappuṟṟa kiḷi moḻiyāḷ kāraṇamāk kiḷar arakkan nagar eritta kaḷi malart tuḻāy alangal kamaḻ mudiyan kadal jñālattu aḷi mikkān kavarāda aṟivināl kuṟaivilamē*

- *taḷir niṟattāl kuṟaivillā* – As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 15.28 “*kurvantīm prabhayādēvīm sarvāvitimirādiśa:*” (One who drives away the darkness in all directions by her bodily radiance) – due to not bathing for ten months of separation from śrī rāma, the radiance in her body got reduced, still was enough to drive away the darkness of all ten directions; raghuvamsam 10.2 “*śōkatamōpaham*” (radiance which drives darkness away).
- *tanic ciṟaiyil* – Her constrained stay amidst the rākśasis (demoniac women) is like the separation of sun and his rays.
- *viḷappuṟṟa* – As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 15.23 “*kruśāmanaśanēnaca*” (she was with tearful eyes, in a pitiable state, due to not having food), as explained by hanumān to śrī rāma “she was not caring for herself”; another explanation – she remained famous in the world for having imprisoned herself in rāvaṇa’s city by taking up the shackles on her own without caring for herself, to remove the shackles from the legs of dēva strīs (celestial damsels).
- *kiḷi moḻiyāḷ kāraṇamā* – Reminded by her words through hanumān’s words, śrī rama said in sundara kāṇḍam 64.15 “*madurā madurā lābhā*” (the sweet person, with sweet words); for the sake of the one who has such sweet voice.
- *kiḷar arakkan* – His anger is so tumultuous that he cannot bear the togetherness of the mother and father \[[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) and [pirātti](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/), are the real divine parents for every living entity\]; as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 1.7 “*udīrṇasya rāvaṇasya*” (well nourished rāvaṇa).
- *nagar eritta* – Destroying the residence of rāvaṇa and flattening the city \[so that one can easily cross from one end to another without any hurdle\]. Burning down rāvaṇa’s well groomed city.
- *kaḷi malar* … – kaḷi – honey. One who is having divine crown which has the fragrance of tirruttuḻāy (tuḷasi) garland with flowers having honey. When he descends like a mortal being, his divine servitors would also appear as part of his entourage; thus, even if he is decorated with kalambagam (collection of flowers), they ([āḻvārs](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/azhwars/), [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s devotees) will praise him as being decorated with tiruttuḻāy only; \[giving a worldly example for this\] even when pāṇḍiya and other (cēra, cōḷa) kings are decorated with karumugai flower, the poets will praise them with their appropriate \[favourite\] flowers such as vēmbu etc only.
- *kadal jñālattu aḷi mikkān* – Having cool mercy in this samsāram itself. Looking at the sufferings of the samsāris (worldly people), his divine heart became fixated here; he then had to be sent off to paramapdam by separating pirātti from him \[[sītāp pirātti](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/) first ascended to paramapadam\], separating iḷaiya perumāḷ from him \[lakśmaṇa also ascended to paramapadam citing the violation śrī rāma’s order as a reason\] and by informing “the purpose of your avatāram (incarnation) is complete; you have to ascend to paramapadam now”.
- *kavarāda* … – There is no use of my knowledge which is not liked by such [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/). What is the use of this knowledge which is similar to the vanvāsa jñānam \[knowledge/thoughts of sītāp pirātti, where she desired to stay under the guidance of riśis (sages) in their hermitage, during her pregnancy\], which led to her second separation from śrī rāma? Such knowledge only leads to separation \[from him\].

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.8.6. Arivinal kuraivilla

*aṟivināl kuṟaivillā agal jñālattavar aṟiya neṟi ellām edutturaitta niṟai jñānattoru mūrtti kuṟiya māṇ uruvāgik kodum kōḷāl nilam koṇḍa kiṟiyammān kavarāda kiḷar oḷiyāl kuṟaivilamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

aṟivināl – not having desire for knowledge; kuṟaivillā – without any limitation; agal jñālattavar – those who are in the vast earth; aṟiya – to be known; neṟiyellām – all means (starting from karma yōga upto prapatti (surrender)); eduttu uraitta – (himself) mercifully explained (to be clear); niṟai jñānattu – one who is complete in knowledge; oru mūrtti – one who is having unmatched nature; kuṟiya – Like bringing the whole mēru mountain into a small stone, being very attractive in vāmana (dwarf) form; māṇ uruvāgi – having brahmacāri (celibate) form (which is identified by accepting alms); kodum kōḷāl – deceiving in a wicked manner (by showing his physical beauty and captivating mahābali’s attention, by showing the small feet and convincing mahābali); nilam koṇḍa – one who made the earth to be his own; kiṟi – having good abilities; ammān – sarvēśvara (supreme lord); kavarāda – not liked; kiḷar oḷiyāl – glowing radiance; kuṟaivilam – what is the use?

**Перевод:**

**emperumān \[gītācāryan\] who is complete in knowledge and who is having unmatched nature, mercifully explained all the means to be known by those who are in this vast earth which has no limitation. What is the use of my glowing radiance which is not liked by sarvēśvaran who is having good abilities and who is being very attractive in a vāmana (dwarf) form which is like bringing the \[beauty of the\] whole mēru mountain into a small stone, and having a brahmacāri (celibate) form, deceiving \[mahābali\] in a wicked manner?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In sixth pāsuram, parānkuśa nāyaki says “emperumān, after mercifully explaining the different means to attain him \[as gītācārya\], reformed/captivated those who were unable to be reformed by good advice, by showing his divine beauty as śrī vāmana; there is no use of my overall beauty which is not desired by such emperumān”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, parānkuśa nāyaki says “There is no use of my radiance when not desired by sarvajña (omniscient lord) who makes one exist for himself exclusively by giving advice and seeking out”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Sixth pāsuram. parānkuśa nāyaki says “What is the use of my beauty which is not desired by emperumān who gives knowledge through instructions to those who are ignorant and who enslaves those who are unqualified to acquire knowledge by manifesting his overall physical beauty?”. aṟivināl kuṟaivillā agal jñālattavar aṟiya neṟi ellām edutturaitta niṟai jñānattoru mūrtti kuṟiya māṇ uruvāgik kodum kōḷāl nilam koṇḍa kiṟiyammān kavarāda kiḷar oḷiyāl kuṟaivilamē*

- *aṟivināl kuṟaivillā* – People of this world are well aware and knowledgeable in matters of food, beverages etc; but when it comes to real knowledge they are not even aware that their knowledge is very limited. That is, they are not even worried that they are ignorant \[when it comes to bhagavat viśayam\]. They have no interest in real knowledge.
- *agal jñālattavar* – In this vast world, there is no one who is full in knowledge without any shortcoming.
- *avar aṟiya* – To impress this in their heart is similar to drilling a hole in rock and preserving water in it \[very much impossible\].
- *neṟi ellām edutturaitta* – As there are differences among cētanas (sentient beings), there are as many different upāyams (means). Explaining clearly starting from karma yōgam up to prapatti (surrender). That is, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who mercifully explained \[many such means\] in great detail – karma yōgam, jñāna yōgam, bhakti yōgam, avatāra rahasya jñānam (confidential knowledge about his incarnations),  puruśōttama vidyā (knowledge about the supreme lord), the true nature of the self, surrender to remove the obstacles, surrender to realize oneself, surrender to realize [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) etc. When kriṣṇa explained karma yōga, arjuna said “it is difficult to overcome the senses”, and kriṣṇa says “in that case, you place your heart in me” and incidentally explain those who practiced karma yōga, and at that time explained the confidential knowledge about his own incarnations, and subsequently jñāna yōga and said “as part of jñāna yōga, place your heart in me”, and subsequently explained bhakti yōga and said “to destroy the sins which are hurdles and to develop your bhakti, place your heart in me”; subsequently he advised prapatti (surrender) as an ancillary step for those (karma, jñāna, bhakti yōgams) as said in śrī bhagavat gītā 15.4 “*yata:pravrutti:prasrutā purānī*” (the lord, from whom the connection in this material world have existed since time immemorial), śrī bhagavat gītā 18.62 “*tamēva śaraṇam gacca*” (You surrender unto that supreme lord only), śrī bhagavat gītā 7.14 “*māmēvayē prapadyantē*” (Only by surrendering unto me) and ignited the knowledge about self \[in arjuna\]; explaining all sentient beings and insentient entities as his own bodies, starting with [śrī bhagavat gītā 7.4](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/7-4/) “*bhūmirāpōnalōvāyu:*” ([earth, water, fire wind etc](http://ponnadi.blogspot.in/2013/03/thathva-thrayam-achith-what-is-matter.html) are my bodies) and up to [śrī bhagavat gītā 7.5](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/7-5/) “*jīvabhūtām*” ([jīvātmās](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) are also controlled by me) and through that explaining that one cannot engage in any means on one’s own to achieve \[the goal of eternal service to [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)\]; firmly impressing upon arjuna’s heart that none of these means is doable, giving a solution for what he already enquired, and also voluntarily explaining about what arjuna does not know and does not ask \[i.e., explaining the [carama ślōkam](http://ponnadi.blogspot.in/2015/12/rahasya-thrayam.html) voluntarily, which explains the method/greatness of śaraṇāgati\] – thus highlighting his explanation from karma yōga up to prapatti.
- *niṟai jñānattu oru mūrtti* – When “someone says”, does it become authentic? Should it not be trustworthy? – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is having such complete knowledge that even the ignorance of the [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) is ineffective \[to cause any harm to [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)\]; even the nityatva (eternal nature), apauruśēyatva (not authored by any individual) of vēdam which gives elaborate knowledge to everyone by being authentic source of knowledge, remains under his full control such that he can recollect it and recite it \[without any flaw\] and explain the meanings of vēdam elaborately. One who is having unmatched nature of having complete knowledge.
- *kuṟiya …* – emperumān enslaves those who don’t listen to his instructions by manifesting his beauty.
- *kuṟiya* – Like shrinking a vast land into a small place, the (vāmana) dwarf form is even more attractive than the well grown trivikrama form.
- *māṇuruvāgi* – Since vāmana started accepting alms immediately after taking birth and continued doing that, it makes one think “has he known this \[accepting alms\] even before taking birth?”. He has mastered the art of accepting alms such that, he smiles beautifully in the same way when some one gives him alms or drives him away shutting the door on him.
- *kodum kōḷāl* – Showing his beauty and captivating him \[mahābali, to give whatever asked for\]. Alternative explanation – kōdu has become kodu. That is, deception. Such as asking for three foot-length of land and measuring with two feet, showing small foot and measuring with huge foot. As some one who has taken unrighteous path should be dealt with accordingly, to deal with mahābali’s dishonesty, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) also took up dishonest means.
- *kiṟi ammān* – sarvēśvara who has great ability to accept knowing well how mahābali will give. He is known as “*perum kiṟiyān*” as said in tiruviruttam 91.
- *kavarāda* … – Even by dishonest means, he will accept his belonging for himself; while he is not manifesting in front of me who is already desiring for him and not accepting me for himself, what is the use of this \[radiance\] for me? kiḷaroḷi – great radiance, collective beauty.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.8.7. Kilaroliyal kuraivilla

*kiḷaroḷiyāl kuṟaivillā ari uruvāyk kiḷarndeḻundu kiḷaroḷiya iraṇiyanadu agal mārbam kiḻittuganda vaḷaroḷiya kanal āḻi valampuriyan maṇi neela vaḷaroḷiyān kavarāda vari vaḷaiyāl kuṟaivilamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

maṇi – best; neelam – very radiant like blue gem; vaḷar – distinguished; oḷiyān – one who is having vigraha tējas (glowing divine form); kiḷar – (as said in “jvalantam” (blazing)) abundant; oḷiyāl – with radiance; kuṟaivillā – complete; ari uruvāy – assuming a lion’s form; kiḷarndu eḻundu – set out to kill the enemy; kiḷar oḷiya – very radiant; iraṇiyanadu – hiraṇya’s \[hiraṇyakaśyap\]; agal mārbam – broad chest; kiḻittu – (effortlessly) tearing; uganda – became joyful (as the enemy of his devotee was finished); vaḷar oḷiya – having increasing flames; kanal āḻi – fire-like divine sudarśana chakra; valam puriyan – one who has śrī pāncajanyam \[divine conch\]; kavarāda – not supported (liked); vari vaḷaiyāl – bangle which has lines in it; kuṟaivilam – what is the use?

**Перевод:**

**emperumān who is having distinguished vigraha tējas, which is very radiant like the best blue gem, assumed a lion’s form which is complete with abundant radiance, set out to kill the very radiant enemy, hiraṇya, tore his chest and became joyful. What is the use of my bangle which has lines in it, and which is not supported (liked) by such emperumān who is having fire-like divine sudarśana chakra which has increasing flames and who is having śrī pāncajanyam?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In seventh pāsuram, parānkuśa nāyaki says “There is no use of my distinguished bangle which is not liked by emperumān \[as narasimhan\] who kills hiraṇya, an enemy of emperumān’s devotee, by manifesting anger which is beyond hiraṇya’s ability to handle, while destroying him”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Seventh pāsuram. parānkuśa nāyaki says “For whom is my decoration with ornaments if he, who helped the child who became enemy for his own father, is not helping me who seeks his help only”. kiḷaroḷiyāl kuṟaivillā ari uruvāyk kiḷarndeḻundu kiḷaroḷiya iraṇiyanadu agal mārbam kiḻittuganda vaḷaroḷiya kanal āḻi valampuriyan maṇi neela vaḷaroḷiyān kavarāda vari vaḷaiyāl kuṟaivilamē*

- *kiḷar ōḷi* … – Explaining the meaning of the narasimha mantram which says “*jvalantam*“. Being narasimha who has no shortcoming in blazing radiance.
- *kiḷarndu eḻundu* – Appearing with anger. As said in periya tirumoḻi 2.5.8 “*piṟai eyiṟṟu anṟu adal ariyāyp peruginānai*” ([emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who appeared as a fighting lion with crescent like teeth), as hiraṇya started chastising his son, prahlāda, emperumān appeared with anger.
- *kiḷar oḷiya iraṇiyan* – Very radiant hiraṇya. That is, demoniac radiance. The evil hiraṇya’s radiance was such that, even narasimhan [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) himself stepped back for a moment .
- *agal mārbam* – hiraṇya’s broad chest, which was nourished with many dēvatās’ boons as food to be given as a deserving prey for the divine lion form.
- *kiḻittu* – Seeing narasimha’s open face (mouth), folded tongue/lips, fist which was ready to punch him and the ostentatious laughter, he melted like a roasted pig; emperumān, then just tore him effortlessly. When emperumān appeared with fearsome lion form with big open eyes and eye-brows, like the fire inside wood, the fire inside one’s own body will burn the insides due to fear.
- *uganda* – Became joyful thinking “the enemy of this child is finished”.  As said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 1.20.21 “*math pitus tat krutam pāpam dēvatasya praṇaśyatu*” (Oh lord! let the sins committed by my father towards me who vorśipped you, be destroyed) – he became joyful that he did not have to beg prahlāda to get his orders \[to kill him\], rather prahlāda himself prayed for that.
- *vaḷar oḷiya kanal āḻi valam puriyan* – As beasts will be well fed In the guarded fields, hiraṇya who was nourished and well fed by the boons of dēvatās, became partly fulfilling food for the divine nails of narasimha; when there are many servitors depending on an individual \[master/[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)\], if a few \[the nails\] make a pact with the master, destroy the prey and consume it fully, others \[sudarśana chakra (disc), śārnga (bow) etc\] will be very angry and rise. So, the other divine weapons of emperumān became angry.
- *maṇi neela vaḷar oḷiyān* – Having radiance of a blue gem which is increasingly radiant. For those who did not get their food, they should be given their share every day; when that does not happen, they will not be patient even for half a moment \[for those who are desirous of seeing [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s divine form, they should be given that darśan\]; as said in mudal tiruvantādi 85 “*padi kaṇḍaṟidiyē*” (Have you seen and enjoyed his divine form?). They \[devotees\] sustain themselves by seeing emperumān’s form. It is said in viṣṇu sūktam “*sadā paśyanti*” (always seeing emperumān). Why is it said “*maṇi neela vaḷāroḷi*“? Would his form not be pale in complexion? No, the divine form will be cooled down, thinking “happy to see the end of prahlāda’s suffering”.
- *kavarāda* … – [parānkuśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says “What is the use of such bangle which is worn when [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) with such divine form himself does not come and pursue me?”.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.8.8. Varivalaiyal kuraivilla

*vari vaḷaiyāl kuṟaivillāp peru muḻakkāl adangārai eri aḻalam pugavūdi irunilamun tuyar tavirtta terivariya sivan biraman amarar kōn paṇindēttum viri pugaḻān kavarāda mēgalaiyāl kuṟaivilamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vari – having lines (on its face); vaḷaiyāl – made by śrī pāncajanyam (conch); kuṟaivillāp peru muḻakkāl – great battle-cry; adangārai – enemies who did not surrender; eri – rising; aḻalam – the fire of fear; puga – to enter inside; ūdi – blew; mun – in the olden days; iru nilam – the great earth’s; tuyar – the burden of suffering; tavirtta – eliminated; terivariya – having incomprehensible importance (of bewilderment as they consider themselves to be equal to emperumān himself); sivan – rudra; biraman – bramhā; amarar kōn – indra, the leader of dēvas; paṇindu ēttum – to praise him out of great gratitude; viri pugaḻān – one who is having vast fame; kavarāda – not liked; mēgalaiyāl – kāncīguṇa (girdle, waist string); kuṟaivilam – what is the use?

**Перевод:**

**emperumān eliminated the burden of suffering of the great earth in the olden days by the great battle-cry made by blowing the śrī pāncajanyam which is having lines, to make the fire of fear enter inside the enemies who did not surrender. What is the use of my girdle which is not liked by such emperumān  who is having vast fame and is praised by rudra, brahmā, indra who is the leader of dēvas et al who are having incomprehensible importance, out of great gratitude? mēgalai indicates both waist string which holds the garment, and the garment itself.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In eighth pāsuram, parānkuśa nāyaki says “There is no use of my girdle (a waist string worn by women) which is not liked by emperumān who is praised by dēvatās such as brahmā, rudra et al, for eliminating all the troubles of the world by finishing the unfavourable \[demoniac\] persons”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, parānkuśa nāyaki says “What is the use of my girdle which is not liked by emperumān who is having infinite greatness and who finished the hundred enemies, duryōdana and his brothers, to reduce the burden on earth”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Eighth pāsuram. parānkuśa nāyaki says “What is the use of my girdle which is not liked by emperumān who favours the whole world but disregards me who exclusively exists for him?”. vari vaḷaiyāl kuṟaivillāp peru muḻakkāl adangārai eri aḻalam pugavūdi irunilamun tuyar tavirtta terivariya sivan biraman amarar kōn paṇindēttum viri pugaḻān kavarāda mēgalaiyāl kuṟaivilamē*

- *vari vaḷaiyāl* – vaḷai means conch. By śrī pāncajanyam (which has lines on its face (upper part)).
- *kuṟaivillāp peru muḻakkāl* – By great battle-cry which is beyond the abilities of the enemies. As said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 1.19](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/1-19/) “*sa ghōśō dārtarāśtrāṇām*” (The sound of the conces blown together that filled the sky and the entire earth, broke the hearts of the sons of drutarāśtra) and mahābhāratam drōṇa parvam “*jagat sa pātāla viyaddigīśvaram prakampayāmāsa*” (The sound of that pāncajanyam shook the hearts of the protectors of pātāla \[nether world\], sky and all directions).
- *varivaḷaiyāl … peru muḻakkāl* – Similar to “*hastēna rāmēṇa” (*By hand, by śrī rāma).
- *adangārai* – those enemies who did not surrender.
- *eri aḻalam puga ūdi* – Blowing \[the conch\] in such a manner that, blazing fire entered their hearts. Made the fire of fear burn them. He blew the conch to eliminate the enemies of his devotees \[second explanation – He blew the conch to eliminate the enemies of devotees, to please parānkuśa nāyaki\].
- *irunila mun tuyar tavirtta* – In the vast earth, one who eliminated the previously existing suffering. If the one who previously was eliminating sufferings of others, lets me suffer now, what is the use of my belongings? The sound of śrī pāncajanyam is dear for the favourable ones, and is the cause for the annihilation of the unfavourable ones, as explained in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 5.23.26 “*dēvānām vavrudētēja: prasādaścaiva yōginām*” (The dēvas’ strength increased and the yōgis’ minds became clearer) and [śrī bhagavat gītā 1.19](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/1-19/) “*sa ghōśō dārtarāśtrāṇām*” (The sound of the conces blown together that filled the sky and the entire earth, broke the hearts of the sons of drutarāśtra). This is specifically life saving for the divine daughter of [periyāḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/periyazhwar/) \[i.e., [āṇḍāḷ](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/andal/)\]. nācciyār tirumoḻi 9.9 “*pūkkoḷ …*” – as āṇḍāḷ has the desire of the divine daughter of śrī jankarāja \[sītā\] and rukimṇip pirātti, put together, she says, “I should get what was achieved by both of them”; [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/) says “I have heard this principle, mercifully explained by [bhattar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/parasara-bhattar/)“. When śiśupāla set out to marry rukmiṇi during her svayamvaram, she became perplexed thinking “if kriṣṇa does not appear now, I cannot live anymore” – at that time kriṣṇa blew his pāncajanya \[conch\] from the garden outside and she survived; when rāvaṇa showed the māyāśiras (fake head) of śrī rāma, sītāp pirātti became perplexed and at that time śrī rāma’s victorious blowing of the conch was heard by her and she survived too; since āṇḍāḷ has the anguish of both of them, she desires for both to happen for her too.
- *terivariya* … – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) having vast glories for being surrendered by dēvatās who give up their arrogance, fall at his feet and sing his praises; previously, these same dēvatās consider themselves not understandable by others, who don’t place their feet on this earth \[considering it to be dirty\] and were prideful. Just due to the presence of a group of mosquitoes, even a small portion of the milk ocean will not be fully occupied; similarly, even by their praises, his glories to be praised will remain at large and his glories which were praised remain a small portion \[that is how vast his glories are\].
- *kavarāda …* – What is the use of such mēgalai which is not liked by him and worn by me just out of self-desire? What is the use of the garment which does not have shrinkage \[by putting it into use\]? if [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who appears as rakśaka \[protector\] and becomes famous due to that, remains “I don’t want the fame of protecting you, and it is ok to be condemned for not protecting you”, should I care for my garments where such act only leads to a shame for me?
- *vari vaḷaiyāl* – \[First two lines are explained again\] śrī pāncajanyam, who stays at the tip of emperumān’s mouth, burned down enemies. When the enemies set out to attack him, he stays at the tip of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s mouth and makes such noise that the enemies will be roasted fully. When the residents (divine consorts) of emperumān’s private quarters complain to emperumān “śrī pāncajanyam is stealing our food \[your nectar of lips\]”, he would say “\[what can I do?\] he is always attached to my mouth”. He is with sound and radiance, he will just blow away the enemies. Though the other āḻvārs \[weapons are also nityasūris who are fully engrossed in emperumān, so they are called āḻvārs\] are sharper, and are known as tadiyar (heavy – mace etc), kaḻundar (bent – bow), but no one else is known as “*suśi*” (knowledgeable, having holes). Since they \[enemies\] are as said in tirumālai 27 “*marangaḷ pōl valiya nenjyu*” (hardened heart like a tree), they are burned by blowing fire into them. What is the use of my mēgalai which is not like by such emperumān who protected his devotees?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.8.9. Megalaiyal kuraivilla

*mēgalaiyāl kuṟaivillā melivuṟṟa agalalgul bōga magaḷ pugaḻt tandai viṟal vāṇan tuyar tuṇittu nāgamisait tuyilvānpōl ulagellām nangodunga yōgaṇaivān kavarāda udambināl kuṟaivilamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

mēgalaiyāl – her beautiful clothes; kuṟaivu illā – perfect; melivu uṟṟa – having śrinkages (due to the union with anirudda); agal algul – having wide distinguished waist region; bōgam magaḷ – for uśā who is having enjoyable femininity; tandai – father; pugaḻ – having fame; viṟal – without any shortcoming in valour, bravery etc; vāṇan – bāṇāsura’s; buyam – shoulders (which have the itch to fight); tuṇittu – severed; nāgamisai – reclining on the ancient serpent bed; tuyilvānpōl – pretending to sleep; ulagellām – all worlds; nangu odunga – to give shelter in the goodness (of attaining him); yōgu aṇivān – one who contemplates the means; kavarāda – not liked; udambināl – body; kuṟaivilam – what is the use?

**Перевод:**

**kaṇṇan emperumān severed the shoulders of bāṇāsura who has no shortcoming in his valour, bravery etc and is having the fame of being the father of uśā who is having enjoyable femininity, who is having wide distinguished waist region and is having śrinkages in her perfectly beautiful clothes; \[such emperumān, after fulfilling the purpose of his avatāram\] reclined on the ancient serpent bed, pretending to sleep and contemplates the means to give shelter in the goodness (of attaining him) for all worlds; what is use of my body which is not liked by such emperumān? yōgu – upāyam (means).**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In ninth pāsuram, parānkuśa nāyaki says “There is no use of my body which is not liked by emperumān who is meditating upon the ways to uplift all beings as he eliminated the many shoulders of the enemy of his devotees, bāṇāsura, and reclined on tiruvanantāḻvān (ādiśēśan)”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, parānkuśa nāyaki says “What is the use of my body which is not liked by kriṣṇa who eliminated the hands of bāṇāsura who is an enemy of his devotees?”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Ninth pāsuram. parānkuśa nāyaki says “What is the use of my body which is not liked by kriṣṇa who eliminated the hands of bāṇāsura who is an enemy of his devotees, and who contemplates the means to uplift everyone?”. mēgalaiyāl kuṟaivillā melivuṟṟa agalalgul bōga magaḷ pugaḻt tandai viṟal vāṇan tuyar tuṇittu nāgamisait tuyilvānpōl ulagellām nangodunga yōgaṇaivān kavarāda udambināl kuṟaivilamē*

- *mēgalaiyāl kuṟaivillā* – [vangip purattu nambi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vangi-puraththu-nambi/) \[a disciple of bhagavad rāmānuja\] said “uśā’s dress makes her look very beautiful”.
- *melivuṟṟa* – Having a tender nature. One cannot bear the loneliness during separation \[from perumāḷ\]”.
- *agal algul* – having wide waist.
- *bōga magaḷ* – Girl who is qualified to be enjoyed.
- *pugaḻt tandai* – bāṇāsura, who is famous to be known as the father of uśā. ōr he is famous for his valour, bravery etc.
- *viṟal vāṇan* – majestic/prideful bāṇāsura. While one should have his satva guṇam (mode of goodness) prominently visible in the presence of a dēvatā ([emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)), even that time, itching to fight, bāṇāsura is quite prideful that he was seeking for a matching enemy for him – he is such a majestic person.
- *buyam tuṇittu* – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) eliminated his hands thinking that he has crossed all the boundaries. Even though bāṇāsuram has committed enough mistakes and deserved to have his head cut off, kriṣṇa did not kill him thinking that “uśā cannot become fatherless”.
- *nāgam* … – Only after eliminating the very many hands of bāṇāsura, emperumān reclined or enjoyed.

Why is it said “*tuyilvānpōl*” (pretending to be sleeping)? Is he not really sleeping?

- *ulagellām nangodunga yōgaṇaivān* – After intending to eliminate others like bāṇāsura who could oppose him, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) will remain in yōga nidrā (meditation) thinking “What is the means for these worldly people to reach me by being surrendered to me?”.
- *kavarāda* – While emperumān cares for everyone else but me, what will I do with my body? Her body is meant for him. She also likes her own body because it belongs to him. Just as emperumān himself remains as said in jitantē stōtram “*bhaktānām*” (my forms etc are for the sake of my devotees), her body is meant for the lord.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.8.10. Udambinal kuraivilla

*udambināl kuṟaivillā uyir pirinda malait tuṇḍam kidandana pōl tuṇi palavā asurar kuḻām tuṇittuganda tadam punala sadai mudiyan tani oru kūṟamarnduṟaiyum udambudaiyān kavarāda uyirināl kuṟaivilamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

udambināl kuṟaivillā – being well built due to nurturing their bodies well; asurar kuḻām – groups of asuras (evil persons); uyir pirinda – (breaking into pieces) their lives taken out; malait tuṇḍam – pieces of mountain; kidandanapōl – as present; pala tuṇiyā – to be broken into many pieces; tuṇittu uganda – destroy them and (thinking that the enemy of the universe is gone) being jubilant; tadam punala – holding gangā which is a vast water source \[on his head\]; sadai mudiyan – rudra who considers himself to be highly capable since he is having matted hair; tani amarndu – accepting emperumān as the support; oru kūṟu – on one side; uṟaiyum – eternally residing; udambu udaiyān – one who is having divine body; kavarāda – not liked; uyirināl – ātmā; kuṟaivilam – there is no use

**Перевод:**

**emperumān destroyed groups of asuras who were well built due to nurturing their bodies well, by taking their lives out of their bodies and breaking them into pieces and leaving them on the ground like pieces of mountain, and became jubilant. There is no use of my ātmā (self) which is not liked by such emperumān who is having the divine body which is eternally occupied on one side by rudra, holding gangā which is a vast water source, who considers himself to be greatly capable due to having matted hair.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In tenth pāsuram, parānkuśa nāyaki says “No matter how great the enemy force is, emperumān is having great qualities to eliminate them; there is no use of my self which is not liked by such emperumān”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, parānkuśa nāyaki says “What is the use of my self which is not liked by sarvēśvara who eliminates all the enemies without a trace?”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Tenth pāsuram. parānkuśa nāyaki, highlighting the śeela guṇam (simplicity) and virōdi nirsanam (eliminating the enemies) which were explained in the first pāsuram, says “What is the use of my existence which is not desired by him?” concludes matching the initial description. By “udambināl kuṟaivillā uyir pirinda malait tuṇḍam kidandana pōl tuṇi palavā asurar kuḻām tuṇittu“, “nīṟāgumpadiyāga nirumittup padai totta” is re-explained. “kūṟāḷum tani udamban” is re-explained by “tadam punala sadai mudiyan tani oru kūṟamarnduṟaiyum udambudaiyān“. udambināl kuṟaivillā uyir pirinda malait tuṇḍam kidandana pōl tuṇi palavā asurar kuḻām tuṇittuganda tadam punala sadai mudiyan tani oru kūṟamarnduṟaiyum udambudaiyān kavarāda uyirināl kuṟaivilamē*

- *udambināl kuṟaivillā* – There is no shortage in both the groups of asuras and the souls \[which are bound\]; those who ignore the soul/self and nurture the body, will only end up as nitya samsāris (eternally bound souls).
- *uyir* … [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) became jubilant after destroying groups of asuras by breaking them into pieces and let them lay on the ground like the movable mountains were attacked and broken into pieces by indra’s vajrāyuda. While he is commonly related to all as said in jitantē stōtram “*dēvānām dānavānānca sāmānyam*” (common to dēvas and asuras), due to they being enemies of his devotees, he finished them and became joyful thinking “enemies of my devotees are gone”.
- *tadam punala* – Their durmāna (pride) is such that, even [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) giving a place in his body for them is praised as a good quality. He is giving space for those egoistic persons in his body which is supposed to be the abode of those who are devoid of any ego. emperumān who is having a divine form, where rudra who is having gangā which has overflowing water, in his matted hair, and having pride due to that, claims a particular portion of emperumān’s divine form as his own just as śrī mahālakśmi has emperumān’s divine chest as her abode.
- *kavarāda* … – [parānkuśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says “Such [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who makes his divine form available for everyone, does not help me; in this case what is the use of having this [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)?”. Previously she discarded her body and other bodily belongings, all of which are anyway temporary and will leave on their own at some point – so it would mean that parānkuśa nāyaki was just discarding the temporary aspects; to make things clear, she now says that she does not even want her eternal self here. Why is she saying “I don’t want this ātmā too”? If the [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) remains, as time progresses, she will acquire another birth and will acquire the previously discarded belongings again, and will have her bosom well developed and cause suffering \[in separation from emperumān\]. The eternal nature of ātmā is due to emperumān’s eternal desire \[for such aspect\]; if he himself has no liking for my ātmā, what is the use of this ātmā then?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

adiyen saraty ramanuja dasan

## 4.8.11. Uyirinal kuraivilla

*uyirināl kuṟaivillā ulagēḻ tannuḷ odukkit tayir veṇṇey uṇḍānait tadam kurugūrc catakōpan seyiril sol isai mālai āyirattuḷ ippattāl vayiram sēr piṟappaṟuttu vaikundam naṇṇuvarē*

**Пословный перевод:**

uyirināl – ātmās; kuṟaivillā – without shortage; ēḻulagu – all worlds; than uḷ odukki – having the supremacy to protect them to become subdued in his sankalpa (will); tayir – curd; veṇṇey – butter; uṇḍānai – on emperumān who is having saulabhyam (simplicity) of consuming; tadam kurugūr – the leader of very spacious āḻvārtirunagari; satakōpan – nammāḻvār’s; seyir il – flawless (in both poetry and its meaning); sol – words; isai – with music; mālai – garland; āyirattuḷ – among the thousand pāsurams; ippattāl – by this decad; vayiram sēr – deep-rooted since time immemorial; piṟappu – bondage in this material realm; aṟuttu – severing; vaikundam – paramapadam; naṇṇuvar – will attain

**Перевод:**

**emperumān who is having the supremacy to protect innumerable ātmās of all \[material\] worlds to become subdued in his sankalpa, is having saulabhyam (simplicity) of consuming curd and butter; by this decad which is among the thousand flawless pāsurams which is a garland of words with music, by nammāḻvār, the leader of very spacious āḻvārtirunagari, on such emperumān, one will sever the bondage in this material realm which is deep-rooted since time immemorial and will attain paramapadam.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the end, āḻvār says “Those who are well versed in this decad which explains emperumān, who is sarvēśvara yet easily approachable by his devotees, will be freed from this deep rooted material realm and will enter the tirunādu (paramapadam – spiritual realm)”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār explains paramapada prāpti (ascending to paramapadam) which is a precursor for eternal service to bhagavān, as the result of this decad.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. uyirināl kuṟaivillā ulagēḻ tannuḷ odukkit tayir veṇṇey uṇḍānait tadam kurugūrc catakōpan seyiril sol isai mālai āyirattuḷ ippattāl vayiram sēr piṟappaṟuttu vaikundam naṇṇuvarē*

- *uyrirināl* … – The seven worlds which are complete with countless [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)s.
- *than uḷ odukkit tayir veṇṇey uṇḍānai* – While setting out to steal curd and butter, to avoid other distractions, i.e., as in “leaving the slippers/sandals outside and going into the temple for worship, one may be thinking of the safety of the sandals while vorśipping the [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) inside \[i.e., not having full focus on emperumān\]”, he fulfilled the needs of all worlds with his will and then proceeded to steal them.
- *ulagēḻ* *than uḷ odukkit tayir veṇṇey uṇḍānai* – Like a pregnant woman would consume foods to suit the child in the womb, emperumān consumed curd and butter to suit the worlds he already consumed. Though he is the [sarvēśvara](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/), he cannot sustain himself without the items that have connection with his devotee; as explained in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 5.6.34 “*sarvasyajagata:pālau vatsapālau babhūvatu:*” (kriṣṇa and balarāma who protect all worlds, are now protecting the cows).
- *tadam kurugūrc catakōpan* – As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 5.16 “*brundam brundam ayōdyāyām*” (in ayōdyā, groups and groups of people), as people came and waited to see the divine coronation ceremony of śrī rāma in ayōdyā, having enough space for śrīvaiṣṇavas from all over the place to come and see nammāḻvār’s state of giving up [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) and its belongings – nammāḻvār who is the leader of such [āḻvārtirunagari](http://azhwarthirunagari.koyil.org/).
- *seyir il sol isai mālai* – seyir is flaw; il is lack of such flaw; i.e., being flawless. That is, there is no falsity in saying “I don’t want my [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) and its belongings”.
- *vayiram sēr piṟappu aṟuttu* – The deep-rooted samsāram which will not leave him, even if āḻvār declares that he does not belong to it and leaves it.
- *vaikundam naṇṇuvarē* – Giving up this body which is to be given up, they \[those who are well versed in this decad\] will enter paramapadam where one can accept many bodies as said in cāndōjña upaniśat “*sa ēkadā bhavati tridā bhavati*” (He assumes one form, three forms and so on), based on [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s desire and his own desire which follows bhagavān’s desire, and serves with many bodies. Though [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) likes [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s body, without realising that, āḻvār says “I don’t want it”.

[āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) tiruvadigaḷē śaraṇam  
[emperumānār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/emperumanar/) tiruvadigaḷē śaraṇam  
[piḷḷān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/pillan/) tiruvadigaḷē śaraṇam
