## 4.9 Nannadar muruvalippa

## 4.9.1. Nannadar muruvalippa

*naṇṇādār muṟuvalippa nalluṟṟār karaindēnga eṇṇārāt tuyar viḷaikkum ivai enna ulagiyaṟkai kaṇṇāḷā! kadal kadaindāy! un kaḻaṟkē varum parisu? taṇṇāvādadiyēnaip paṇi kaṇḍāy sāmāṟē*

**Пословный перевод:**

naṇṇādār – those who do not stay by one’s side, due to enmity; muṟuvalippa – to smile (joyfully seeing his suffering); nal uṟṟār – those relatives who stay by one’s side, out of friendship; karaindu ēnga – seeing his suffering, being weakened and to worry for his suffering; eṇ ārā – innumerable; tuyar – sufferings; viḷaikkum – which causes; ivai ulagiyaṟkai – these worldly aspects; enna – how \[strange\] are they?; kaṇṇāḷā – (due to being natural controller,) being merciful; kadal kadaindāy – oh one who has the helping tendency of churning the ocean (even when requested by those with ulterior motives)!; una kaḻaṟkē – for the sake of the divine feet of you, who are apt \[lord\]; varum parisu – for my attainment; taṇṇāvādu – without delaying any further; adiyēnai – me (who is your exclusive servitor); sāmāṟu – to die (and shed my body); paṇi kaṇḍāy – you have to mercifully speak a word (as in the case of śrī bhagavat gītā 18.66 “mōkśayiśyāmi” (I will free you))

**Перевод:**

**How strange are these worldly aspects which cause innumerable sufferings and which make those who do not stay by one’s side, due to enmity, to smile and make those relatives who stay by one’s side, out of friendship, to feel weakened and to worry for one’s suffering? Oh merciful one who has the helping tendency to churn the ocean! You have to mercifully speak a word (as in the case of śrī bhagavat gītā 18.66 “mōkśayiśyāmi” (I will free you)), without delaying any further, to let me die for the sake of the attainment of the divine feet of you who are apt \[lord\]. It is implied that, the body is also part of “sarvapāpa” (all sins) which is explained in the gītā carama ślōkam.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In first pāsuram, āḻvār requests emperumān “while you are capable of protecting all, and are the controller of all, these samsāris (bound souls) are going through great sufferings – I am unable to bear the sight of this; either you remove their suffering or finish me so that I don’t have to think about it”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*In first pāsuram, āḻvār says “I am unable to witness the sufferings of the samsāris; this being the case, you who engages in difficult tasks for your devotees to fulfil their desires, should make me leave my body so that I don’t have to witness this suffering \[of samsāris\]”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*First pāsuram. āḻvār says “You should mercifully facilitate shedding of my body to reach your divine feet, from the midst of these \[samsāris\] who have their gain/pain outside you”. naṇṇādār muṟuvalippa nalluṟṟār karaindēnga eṇṇārāt tuyar viḷaikkum ivai enna ulagiyaṟkai kaṇṇāḷā! kadal kadaindāy! un kaḻaṟkē varum parisu? taṇṇāvādadiyēnaip paṇi kaṇḍāy sāmāṟē*

- *naṇṇādār muṟuvalippa* – How sad that some see the suffering of others and feel joyful! [śrī bhagavat gītā 5.29](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/5-29/) “*suhrudam sarvabhūtānām*” (being the friend of all creatures) – arjuna asked “when will my likes/dislikes disappear?” and kriṣṇa said “If you realize that I am well-wisher of all, you too will start seeking good for my wealth”. naṇṇādār indicates enemies. When some one goes through suffering, even if they \[enemies of the sufferer\] had never consumed betel leaves and nuts (which are considered as an enjoyable food item), they would seek out for such enjoyments on that day \[of others’ suffering\]; they would buy new clothes and wear them; they would laugh out loud.
- *nal uṟṟār* – While one should consider [sarvēśvaran](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) as the natural relative and should remain inseparable from those who are fully surrendered to [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) as said in mudal tiruvantādi 55 “*avan tamar evvinaiyarāgilum en kōn avan tamarē*” (Whatever may be the conduct of emperumān’s devotees, they are my rulers), instead considering the bodily relatives as natural relatives, these people would feel very bad when something bad occurs to them as said in tiruvāimoḻi 9.6.2 “*ninaitoṟum sollum toṟum nenjidindugum*” (my thoughts, words and mind will tremble) – that is, whatever [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) goes through in bhagavat viśayam (emperumān related matters), they will go through that in worldly matters. \[While enmity is bad, is feeling bad for other sufferings bad?\] As said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 1.19.31 “*sarva bhutātmakē*” (kēśava who has all [ātmās](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) as his body, has no enmity/friendship with anyone). What is said in “karaindēnga, muṟuvalippa”, is reflected in the same ślōkam “*mitrāmitrakadakuta:*” (who is friend and who is enemy?). Since all of these are based on \[worldly\] rāga dvēśam (likes, dislikes), there is no difference between friendship and enmity. As said in śrī bhagavat gītā 15.5 “*dvantvair vimuktās sukhadu:kha samjñai:*” (those who are free from joy and sorrow), the joy and sorrow are for namesake only. In the material realm, both are sorrow only in reality, which is what is explained here. In śrī ayōdyā, though there is scope for enmity, they all prayed to śrī rāma in the same manner as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 131.95 “*rāmamēva*” (as they were only thinking about śrī rāma, they did not harm each other); what is the reason for that? Though at times inimical feelings may arise in their minds , they would think “that will hurt śrī rāma’s feelings” and such inimical feelings will not lead to actions. In bhagavat viśayam, one will be as said in śrīguṇaratna kōśam  “*puśpānkāragaissamam*” \[not just in this world, even in paramapadam, devotees will remain like garland etc\]. When [sarvēśvaran](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) engages with periya pirāttiyār, other consorts will become part of the enjoyable aspects such as garland, sandalwood paste etc; and when [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) engages with those other consorts, it will be like his engaging with periya pirātti’s bosom, waist etc \[they are all like her limbs\]. As said in mudal tiruvantādi 42 “*tirumagaḷum maṇmagaḷum āymagaḷum sērndāl tirumagatkē tīrndavāṟen kol*” (When all his three primary divine consorts are present, he would be fully attached to śrī mahālakśmi) – he will be fully focussed on śrī mahālakśmi only \[others will not consider themselves to be equal consorts and will be subservient to the divine couple\]; this is because, the joy of such togetherness is witnessed in śrī mahālakśmi’s face. As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 12.68 “*yatāyatāhi kausalyā*” (kausalyā conducted herself along with the other wives, for the pleasure of daśarata), if such conduct can be seen in material realm, where someone like kausalyā who had some basic good qualities conducted herself in a superior manner over the other wives with daśarata cakravarti, what to speak of śrī mahālakśmi in spiritual realm. *yatā yatāhi* – kausalyā presented herself to daśarta according to each season, without any specific identity for herself \[fully dedicated to her husband\].
- *eṇṇārāt tuyarviḷaikkum* – For [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/), both the reaction of feeling pained or joyful appears as suffering only. Even if one can find the boundary of the joy of paramapadam, one cannot find the boundary of the suffering in this realm. Just as there is pure bliss in the spiritual realm, there is infinite suffering in this material realm. \[The commentator becomes emotional thinking about [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s suffering in this realm\] śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 67.24 “*rājyāt bramśa: …*” (My sufferings such as leaving behind my kingdom, forest dwelling with sītā, losing her, seeing jatāyu mahārāja die etc, will even burn down fire). emperumān himself suffered in this material realm, when he gave a helping hand to the suffering souls of this material realm. When he was set to be crowned on the throne, someone else said that they need the throne. Even if he was not crowned, at least he could have lived in the palace in the capital city. śrī kausalyā said “let my son not rule the kingdom, but even if he has to beg, let him do it in my sight” \[but that also did not happen\]. “*sītā naśtā”* – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) thought that he can enjoy some private moments in the forest, but alas, they were separated from each other and lived in different locations. periya udaiyāra (jatāyu mahārāja) \[who was a father-figure for śrī rāma\] who came to the rescue of pirātti, also lost his life. Why is it that what was glorified previously as “*rājyanāśōbakarśati*” and “*vanavāsō mahōdaya:*“, is now explained as suffering? Originally, he left for the forest looking to mingle with his devotees and to help the sages – but since there were hurdles for those expected joys, now they feel like sorrows. As he ended up separating from pirātti and losing jatāyu mahārāja, the loss of the kingdom and the forest-dwelling (which felt joyful before) are appearing to be sufferings. By these two, all the sufferings of this world are contemplated. “*nirda hēdapipāvakam*” – It \[samsāram\] is so powerful that it even separated the inseparable lakśmaṇa from him.
- *ivai enna ulagiyaṟkai* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) asks “Oh lord! Why did you create this world where there is gain/pain outside you?”

empeumān’s replies “What shall I do? All of these are based on the effect of their actions. They are not caused by me”; and [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) speaks further.

- *kaṇṇāḷā* – If they simply have to reap the results of their actions, what is the use of your compassion? Compassionate person is generally explained as “*kaṇṇudaiyavan*” (one with eyes). Alternatively – kaṇ also means place, implying the vast world. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is asking “Is this an independent place? While you are the controller of everyone in this world, why are they engaging in activities that are contrary to their nature?”. kaṇ also implies controller.

[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) asks “where did you see me help anyone so that he doesn’t have to reap the results of his karma (actions)?”. āḻvār says “there is plenty of such incidents” and gives an example.

- *kadal kadaindāy* – ḍidn’t you take up great task to even help the prayōjanāntaraparar (those with ulterior motives – here, dēvas), to be freed from the sufferings caused by the curse of durvāsa? emperumān says “They (dēvas) had the desire to approach me; for those who don’t have the desire, what can I do?”. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says “In that case, you have to ensure that I reach your divine feet, so that I am not in the midst of these samsāris”.
- *una kaḻaṟkē varum parisu* – The state of being at your divine feet which are apt and enjoyable, instead of going behind distractions \[such as aiśvaryam (worldly pleasures), kaivalyam (self-enjoyment) etc\]. As āḻvār had a little bit of desire, [īśvara](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) agreed to fulfil his desire.
- *taṇṇāvādu* – Without delay. I cannot be satisfied by you saying “I will do”, you have to do now.

[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) asks “Why should I do it immediately?”.

- *adiyēnai* – Due to my self-realised state, I cannot co-exist along with samsāris.
- *paṇi kaṇḍāy sāmāṟē* – paṇikkai – speaking/saying. Word is related to thought. For you it is a simple word, but for me, it is my sustenance.
- *sāmāṟē paṇi* – You should ensure that I am freed from my body; emperumān asks “Why are you just praying to be freed from your body like a kēvalar \[one who is focussed on kaivalyam\]?”. That is because, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s desire is to first be freed from being in the midst of samsāris, as said in śaunaka samhitā “*varamhutavahajvālā pancarāntarvyavastiti: \| naśauricintāvimukha jana samvāsavaiśasam \|\|*” (It is better to be in the midst of a forest fire than to be present in the midst of those who are not interested in meditating upon kriṣṇa). For one who is caught in a forest fire, he will first seek out for water and shade, then only will he look for enjoyable aspects; similarly, āḻvār too requests to be first freed from his body to avoid being present amidst samsāris.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.9.2. Samarum kedumarum

*sāmāṟum kedumāṟum tamar uṟṟār talait talaip peydu ēmāṟik kidandalaṟṟum ivai enna ulagiyaṟkai? āmāṟonṟaṟiyēn nān aravaṇaiyāy ammānē! kūmāṟē virai kaṇḍāy adiyēnaik kuṟik koṇḍē*

**Пословный перевод:**

sāmāṟum – to die (while setting out to live long); kedumāṟum – to lose (the wealth, while setting out to increase it); tamar – the paternal relatives; uṟṟār – other relatives; talait talaip peydu – all of them showing their attachment; ēmāṟi – without any break; kidandu – staying; alaṟṟum – crying; ivai enna ulagiyaṟkai – what is the nature of these worldly activities?; nān – I; Am āṟu – to finish these \[sufferings\] within my ability; onṟu – any means; aṟiyēn – I don’t know; aravaṇaiyāy – one who engages ananta, your servitor, in your service; ammānē – Oh lord who has similar relationship with everyone!; adiyēnai – me, who is a servitor; kuṟikkoṇḍu – considering me (to be not deserving to go through sufferings); kūmāṟu – call me; virai kaṇḍāy – rush to do so

**Перевод:**

**What is the nature of these worldly activities where seeing the death and loss of wealth of one, his paternal relatives and other relatives showing their attachment, staying without any break and crying? I don’t know any means to finish these \[sufferings\] within my ability. Oh one who engages ananta, your servitor, in your service! Oh lord who has similar relationship with everyone! considering me, who is a servitor, rush to call me \[towards you\].**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In second pāsuram, āḻvār becomes sorrowful speaking about sufferings such as death etc of cētanas \[sentient beings\] and says “if you are not removing their sufferings, at least you should accept me quickly at your divine feet, so that I need not think about that”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “I don’t know when the worldly suffering will end. So you, my natural lord, should rush to accept me”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Second pāsuram. In the previous pāsuram, āḻvār collectively said “eṇṇārāt tuyar” (boundless sufferings); becoming sorrowful on highlighting a few of them, he says “if you are not removing their sorrows, you should at least accept me at your divine feet”. sāmāṟum kedumāṟum tamar uṟṟār talait talaip peydu ēmāṟik kidandalaṟṟum ivai enna ulagiyaṟkai? āmāṟonṟaṟiyēn nān aravaṇaiyāy ammānē! kūmāṟē virai kaṇḍāy adiyēnaik kuṟik koṇḍē*

- *sāmāṟum kedumāṟum* – to die and face loss of wealth; \[focussing on the “āṟu”, the process/method\] are there any more details in these?  while one is considering oneself to live long happily, and planning to destroy those who co-exist with him \[for his own joy\], he will be consumed by death without even realising; while acquiring a little bit of wealth, he will start thinking “I have no more worries”, he will lose that and cry out with sorrow. There are other reasons for their \[āḻvārs’\] anguish; āḻvār thinks that not attaining bhagavān is death as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 2.3.7](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/02/thiruvaimozhi-2-3-7-munnal-yazh/) “*ninnalāl ilēn kāṇ*” (I have no existence without you), tiruvāimoḻi 6.9.9 “*pala nī kāttip paduppāyō*” (will you push me showing various other pleasures) and tiruvāimoḻi 6.9.8 “*innam keduppāyō*” (will you push me down further?), and he considers seeing other worldly pleasures as disastrous. What else did āḻvārs consider as death and loss? They are of such nature that they say as in mudal tiruvantādi 95 “*ennoruvar tīkkadikkaṇ sellum tiṟam*” (How can one follow evil paths when serving [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is so easy?). They consider death and disaster as seen in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 31.22 “*kuruśva*” (lakhsmaṇa to śrī rāma – You should make me follow you \[otherwise I will not be able to live\]) and śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 30.18 “*yastvayā sahasa svarga:*” (sītā to śrī rāma – Being together with you is heaven, and getting separated from you is hell).
- *kedumāṟum* – when wealth is lost; since one considers wealth as the refuge. \[in comparison to loss of wealth, even death will look better – an example is explained here\] When some soldiers were set out to cut off the hands and legs of a traitor, some others see that and question the soldiers. The soldiers said to those on-lookers if anyone of you pays the fine, we will leave him and some one in the crowd said “you are kind enough not to kill him, you are quite compassionate” and left the place \[not wanting to pay any money\].
- *tamar uṟṟār* – For āḻvār, the relatives are as said in tiruvāimoḻi 8.10.9 “*tamargaḷ tamargaḷ tamargaḷ*” (devotees of devotees of devotees of emperumān). Instead of considering such devotees \[as relatives\], worldly people will consider bodily relatives and other relatives acquired through marriage etc and be free from worries.
- *talait talaip peydu* – showing too much attachment.
- *ēmāṟik kidandu alaṟṟum* – “*E*” means longing, “*māṟugai”* – not having; that is, calling out without any longing; alternatively – ēmāṟṟam can be explained as a single word – that is sorrow, implying “calling out with sorrow”. piḷḷai amudanār explains this as – “*E*” means clarity, “*ēmāṟugai*” means losing clarity. It is said in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 2.7.8 “*ēmāṟṟam ennait tavirttāy*” (You eliminated my lack of clarity).
- *ivai enna ulagiyaṟkai* – How sad is this worldly existence? āḻvār says “Oh my lord! nature of this worldly existence is such that – dying while longing to live; losing the wealth while acquiring it and happily thinking to live with that; while considering bodily relatives as everything, when something happens to self, crying out”.

[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) asks “Why do you care about others? I have made you call out for me only! your calling out has already been seen in ‘[*seelamillāc ciṟiyan*](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/03/thiruvaimozhi-4-7-seelamilla/)*‘ “.*

- *āmāṟu onṟu aṟiyēn nān* – Are they calling out because of not having relationship with you? īsn’t it because of their existence in this material realm and have you freed me from this material realm? Is it due to me having a body in this realm, I do not know what I am calling out for? Alternative explanation – I don’t know the means to eliminate the sufferings of these samsāris (materialistic people). Third explanation – i don’t know the means to give what you have given to me \[i.e., blessing of pristine knowledge/devotion\].
- *aravaṇaiyāy ammānē* – Oh [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who has motherly relationship with all these samsāris, who has reclined on tiruvanantāḻvān in milky ocean, for their protection and who considers their well-being as your benefit! He has true/motherly relationship with all of them. His protection of all of these beings will occur irrespective of his truthfulness \[in śrī rāmāvatāram\] or deception \[in kriṣṇāvatāram\].
- *kūmāṟē virai* – You, who are easily approachable in being present in tiruppāṟkadal (milky ocean) to hear their complaints, should quickly call me and accept me at your divine feet.

[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) asks “Why should I rush to do so?”,

- *kaṇḍāy* – After seeing me \[my state\], can you still remain relaxed? He shows his form \[which was weakened/consumed by separation from emperumān\] to emperumān for his seeing as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 6.16 “*ēhi paśya śarīrāṇi*” (riśis of daṇḍakāraṇya to śrī rāma – See our bodies which were tortured by the demons).

[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) says “But would you not feel anguished when separated from your body and relatives who have followed you since time immemorial?”.

- *adiyēnaik kuṟikkoṇḍē* – You should consider my nature \[of being blessed by you with pristine knowledge/devotion\] which cannot cope with the activities of this material realm. Also explained as – after having realised my relationship with your divine feet, like yourself, I too am concerned about the sufferings of others – you should mercifully consider that. When āḻvār says “*kūmāṟē virai kaṇḍāy*” (Please accept me quickly at your divine feet), how does that highlight the fact that āḻvār cannot tolerate suffering of others? From his saying “*ivai enna ulagiyaṟkai*” (How sad is the situation here) and requesting [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) to accept him in paramapadam, it is understood that he cannot tolerate seeing others suffering.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.9.3. Kondattum kulampunaivum

*koṇḍāttum kulam punaivum tamar uṟṟār viḻu nidiyum vaṇḍār pūm kuḻalāḷum manai oḻiya uyir māydal kaṇḍāṟṟēn ulagiyaṟkai kadal vaṇṇā! adiyēnaip paṇḍē pōl karudādu un adikkē kūyp paṇi koḷḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

koṇḍāttum – due to having wealth, the praises done by the \[people of the\] world; kulam punaivum – pride of being born in high family heritage (which was not there, but assumed); tamar – the paternal relatives (who arrived seeing the wealth); uṟṟār – other relatives; viḻu nidiyum – the glorious wealth; vaṇḍu Ar pū kuḻalāḷum – the enjoyable damsel who is having hair-locks, filled with beetles; manai – the distinguished residence which is where the damsel is enjoyed; oḻiya – while all these remain; uyir māydal – losing one’s life; ulagiyaṟkai – this worldly nature; kaṇḍu – seeing; āṟṟēn – I am unable to tolerate; kadal vaṇṇā – Oh one who is having ocean-like boundless physical beauty!; adiyēnai – me who became enslaved to you (losing to your beauty); paṇḍē pōl – like previously (when I called for you in separation); karudādu – instead of thinking; un adikkē – to exist exclusively for your divine feet; kūvi – invite; paṇi koḷ – mercifully accept my service

**Перевод:**

**While \[worldly people have\] glorious wealth, and due to having such wealth, are praised by the world,the pride of being born in high family heritage, the enjoyable damsel who is having hair-locks filled with beetles \[coming to drink the honey in hair-locks\], the distinguished residence which is where the damsel is enjoyed etc, remain, one loses one’s life – such is the nature of this world and I am unable to tolerate seeing it. Oh one who is having ocean-like boundless physical beauty! Instead of thinking about me like previously, you invite me to exist exclusively for your divine feet and mercifully accept my service.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In third pāsuram, āḻvār says “Even while entities are having high birth etc, I am unable to tolerate seeing their death; please accept me at your divine feet and engage me in your service so that I won’t have to meditate upon these sufferings”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. koṇḍāttum kulam punaivum tamar uṟṟār viḻu nidiyum vaṇḍār pūm kuḻalāḷum manai oḻiya uyir māydal kaṇḍāṟṟēn ulagiyaṟkai kadal vaṇṇā! adiyēnaip paṇḍē pōl karudādu un adikkē kūyp paṇi koḷḷē*

- *koṇḍāttum* – Previously one would be a nobody, but after acquiring little bit of wealth, he would be known as “*mudaliyār*” (master). [āḻvārs](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/azhwars/) only glorify as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 3.7.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/09/thiruvaimozhi-3-7-1-payilum-sudaroli/) “*payilum tiruvadaiyār*” (those who have the wealth of being together with [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) eternally).
- *kulam punaivum* – Once he acquired some wealth, others will praise him as if he was born in a great family heritage.
- *tamar* – For such people, their blood relatives would be others \[not those who are interested in bhagavān\]. Previously \[before acquiring wealth\], those who considered identifying him to be a relative as lowly, would now claim close relationship.
- *uṟṟār* – Previously those who said as in “It is not worthy to have a relationship \[like marital engagement between sons/daughters\] with him; it will be an insult for us” are now saying “It would be nice to have some relationship with him” and are eagerly approaching him.
- *viḻu nidiyum …* – Just like dry leaves will accumulate without anyone realising, he will acquire some great wealth; not knowing how to spend such wealth, he will use that to attract a damsel towards him without knowing what he is doing. She is explained as – *vaṇḍār pūm kuḻalāḷ*. Her \[hair’s\] freshness will be enjoyed by the beetles and not him. He accepts at an \[old\] age when he is no longer fit to enjoy her. \[But\] for [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/), every enjoyment is [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) only as said in tiruvāimoḻi 5.1.8 “*sēlēy kaṇṇiyarum perum selvamum nan makkaḷum mēlāt tāy tandaiyarum*” (beautiful fish-eyed girls, great wealth, good children, praiseworthy parents).
- *manai oḻiya* – To enjoy along with her, he will build with great efforts, multi-storeyed building in his land.
- *uyir māydal* – While all of these remain, and eagerly waiting to enjoy her, he will suddenly die.
- *kaṇḍu āṟṟēn ulagiyaṟkai* – I cannot tolerate such activities of the world.
- *kadal vaṇṇā* – There is a form which can be enjoyed which is different from this worldly sufferings. Mercifully show your invigorating form to eliminate the stress of meditating upon their suffering.
- *adiyēnaip paṇḍē pōl karudādu* – Don’t consider about me in your divine heart as seen before in tiruviruttam 1 “*poyn ninṟa jñānam*” – there I only looked at the faults of myself in this samsāram (material realm) and said “*inninṟa nīrmai ini yām uṟāmai*” (I cannot tolerate this lowly nature anymore). But now, I am saying this after being fully engaged in bhagavat viśayam (matters related to [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)). siṟṟāḷ koṇḍār (a śrīvaiṣṇava) said “emperumān cannot remain indifferent towards [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) who keeps repeating the same thing \[requesting to accept him in paramapadam\] like a lizard which keeps making the same noise”. Alternative explanation – Previously I requested to be freed from this samsāram only seeing my own suffering and now I am requesting based on the suffering of others.
- *un* … – You should invite me at your divine feet and engage me in kainkaryam. Even after reaching your divine feet, only if I am engaged in kainkaryam, will I remain there without returning; this being the case, you should engage me in eternal service.
- *kūyp paṇi koḷḷē* – Like saying “Give some food and engage in work” \[[āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying “invite me and engage me in kainkaryam”\].

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.9.4. Kol enru

*koḷ enṟu kiḷarndeḻunda perum selvam neruppāgak                    koḷ enṟu tamam mūdum ivai enna ulagiyaṟkai vaḷḷalē maṇivaṇṇā! unakaḻaṟkē varum parisu vaḷḷal seydadiyēnai unadaruḷāl vāngāyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

koḷ enṟu – saying “pursue me, pursue me”; kiḷarndu eḻunda – rising and visible in an appealing manner; peru selvam – great wealth; neruppāga – while being like fire (due to leading to destruction etc and to be defeated by enemies); koḷ enṟu – (again) saying “pursue” (this); tamam mūdum – to be consumed by the darkness of ignorance; ivai – these; enna ulagiyaṟkai – How sad are \[these\] worldly incidents?; vaḷḷalē – having unsurpassed magnanimity; maṇi vaṇṇā – Oh one who is having divine form which resembles blue gem!; una kaḻaṟkē – at your divine feet; varum parisu – to reach; vaḷḷal seydu – show your magnanimity for this; adiyēnai – me (who exist exclusively for you); unadu aruḷāl – by your grace; vāngāy – mercifully accept me

**Перевод:**

**Great wealth which is rising and visible in an appealing manner, saying “pursue me, pursue me”, while being like fire and people get consumed by the darkness of ignorance of such wealth saying “pursue \[me\]” – How sad are these worldly incidents? Oh one who is having divine form which resembles blue gem, who is having unsurpassed magnanimity! Show your magnanimity to have me reach your divine feet and mercifully accept me by your grace.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In fourth pāsuram, āḻvār thinking about abundance of wealth being the cause for disaster, and the craziness of the people of this world desiring for that, says “you should accept me in your lotus feet where there is no scope for meditating upon such sufferings”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “You should manifest your magnanimity and accept me just as you manifested your beautiful form so that I don’t have to see the worldly activities of people being attached to this wealth which is temporary”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. koḷ enṟu kiḷarndeḻunda perum selvam neruppāgak                    koḷ enṟu tamam mūdum ivai enna ulagiyaṟkai vaḷḷalē maṇivaṇṇā! unakaḻaṟkē varum parisu vaḷḷal seydadiyēnai unadaruḷāl vāngāyē*

- *koḷ enṟu* … – Though one does not desire for the unsurpassed wealth, it will rise like a pot/container which is used in farming to fetch water.
   - *neruppāga* – to destroy without any trace; also explained as – that which causes destruction of the self. Why is it that wealth leads to destruction? Hearing that “one is living a wealthy life”, others would like to finish him out of jealousy.  Though wealth leads to destruction, since others force him to pursue wealth, being covered with ignorance, out of greed, one will pursue wealth which was deemed to cause destruction previously. Again one pursues wealth due to being covered with ignorance.  Alternative explanation – here the mind is explained as the instigator to pursue wealth; another explanation – the strength of the wealth is such that, though one knows that it leads to destruction, the heart, being covered with ignorance, will instigate him to pursue the wealth. mahābhāratam śalya parvam “*hatē bhīśmatē drōṇē hatē karṇē mahāratē āśābalavatī rājan śalyōjyēśyati pāṇḍavān*” (Even after the death of great warriors like bhīśma, drōṇa and karṇa, duryōdana, out of greed, thought, he can defeat pāṇḍavas using the help of śalya).
- *ivai enna ulagiyaṟkai* – How sad are these worldly incidents!
- *vaḷḷalē* – Oh the magnanimous one who impressed upon my heart that the worldly wealth would lead to destruction!
- *maṇivaṇṇā* – You magnanimously gave the abode (your divine form) which resembles a priceless gem. sādanānuśtānam (practicing of other means) will not lead to extra benefits \[such as getting instructions from ācārya etc. Only [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s magnanimity will bestow those\]. Alternative explanation – censuring the desire for worldly wealth, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), relaxed his shawl (outer covering), revealed his divine beauty \[to [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)\].
- *una kaḻal* … – Is it sufficient to bestow knowledge? Don’t you also bestow the ultimate goal? Is it sufficient to bestow “[*mayarvaṟa madinalam*](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/03/thiruvaimozhi-1-1-1-uyarvara-uyarnalam/)” (bestowing faultless knowledge, devotion)?  Should you also not make me “[*tuyaraṟu sudaradi toḻudeḻa*](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/03/thiruvaimozhi-1-1-1-uyarvara-uyarnalam/)” (bow down at the radiant feet which removes the sufferings, and rise)? When you create hunger, should you also not feed me sufficiently?
- *vaḷḷal seydu* – Showing your magnanimity to reach your divine feet. Pursuing the [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) ([āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)) thinking “let him get this ultimate goal”.
- *adiyēnai* – Me who is praying to retain your own belonging \[at your divine feet\].
- *undaruḷāl* – As you blessed me to acquire faultless knowledge and devotion, you should also bless me to attain the benefit.
- *vāngāyē* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says “*vāngāy*” considering himself to be a insentient entity \[which cannot do anything on its own\]. This is because – even if one acquires up to paramabhakti, looking at the greatness of the benefit, it appears that everything was acquired by [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s mercy only.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.9.5. Vangu nir

*vāngu nīr malar ulagil niṟpanavum tirivanavum ānguyirgaḷ piṟappiṟappup piṇi mūppāl tagarppuṇṇum īngidan mēl vennaragam ivai enna ulagiyaṟkai vāngenai nī maṇivaṇṇā! adiyēnai maṟukkēlē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vāngum – that which will consume (those objects which are caught in the tides); nīr – having oceanic water; malar ulagil – in the vast earth; niṟpanavum – immovable; tirivanavum – and movable entities; āngu – in those abodes; uyirgaḷ – ātmās which are attached to the prāṇa (vital-air in body); īngu – here; piṟappu iṟappu piṇi mūppāl – by birth, death, disease and old-age; tagarppuṇṇum – are tortured; idan mēl – moreover; ven naragam – very cruel raurava narakam (hell) etc; ivai – these; enna ulagiyaṟkai – How said are these worldly situations?; maṇi – (to be at the disposal of his devotees) attractive and easily manageable like a blue gem; vaṇṇā – Oh one who is having a form!; nī – you; enai – me (who cannot bear this suffering); vāngu – mercifully acknowledge me; adiyēnai – me (who is your servitor); maṟukkēl – don’t bewilder

**Перевод:**

**ātmās which are attached to the prāṇa (life-air in body) of immovable and movable entities in the vast earth having oceanic water which will consume (those objects which are caught in the tides), are tortured here by birth, death, disease and old-age and moreover in very cruel raurava narakam (hell) etc; How sad are these worldly situations? Oh one who is having a blue-gem like form which is attractive and easily manageable! you mercifully acknowledge me and don’t bewilder me.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In fifth pāsuram, āḻvār says “You should mercifully withdraw me from this world by showing its nature of being filled with ātmās who are suffering through janma (birth), jarā (old age) etc”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. vāngu nīr malar ulagil niṟpanavum tirivanavum ānguyirgaḷ piṟappiṟappup piṇi mūppāl tagarppuṇṇum īngidan mēl vennaragam ivai enna ulagiyaṟkai vāngenai nī maṇivaṇṇā! adiyēnai maṟukkēlē*

- *vāngu nīr malar ulagil* – effect will submerge in the cause \[among the five great elements, water is considered as the cause for earth\]; in the vast earth which is consumed by the water; sruśti (creation) is preceded by layam (deluge).  Alternative explanation – vāngudal – curved, the world which is born from the lotus from the divine naval of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) which is covered with water.
- *niṟpanavum tirivanavum* – immovable (plants, mountains etc) and movable entities (humans, animals).
- *āngu uyirgaḷ* – [ātmās](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) which are present in those different bodies. Alternative explanation – “*āngu*” is explained subequently, and just explaining the ātmās which are in immovable and movable entities.
- *piṟappu* … – They will be tortured in birth, death, disease and old-age. This goes on as long as they exist in samsāram (material realm).
- *idan mēl ven naragam* – On top of this, there is the cruel hell. When compared to the life in hell, the life here looks a lot happier enjoying all sorts of pleasures. Here in the earth, at least there is fake joy, but there in hell, it is pure sorrow. Here, it is like a person who is to be hanged momentarily, becomes thirsty and given water which leads to momentary satisfaction; even that short relief is not present in hell. This is how sad this worldly situations is!

[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) asks “So, what shall I do for you?”,

- *āngu vāngu enai* – You should pull me into the spiritual abode where you are seated on the divine throne and independently ruling over all worlds as said in Siva \[linga\] purāṇam “*vaikuṇṭē tu parē lōkē śriyā sārdam jagatpati: \| āstē viṣṇuracityātmā bhaktair bhāgavatais saha\|\|*” (The inconceivable lord of the universe, viṣṇu, mercifully resides along with śrī mahālakśmi, in the supreme abode, śrī vaikuṇṭam, along with bhkatas (devotees) and bhāgavtas (his followers).
- *maṇi vaṇṇā* – You should manifest your divine form to me who is attracted and attached to worldly pleasures like “giving such great form to a dog”.  As said in iraṇḍām tiruvantādi 42 “*manaippāl – piṟandār piṟandeydum pērinbam ellām tuṟandār toḻdār attōḷ*” (Those who worship [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s divine shoulders will hate all these petty pleasures which are acquired in this material realm by taking birth here), after seeing his form, one will not like anything else.
- *adiyēnai* – me who knows your form/nature, me who knows your divine form in that great assembly \[in paramapadam\].
- *maṟukkēlē* – You should ensure that I don’t get bewildered staying amidst these samsāris who are being tortured by birth, old-age, death etc. Don’t confuse me. \[Instead\] Accept me in teḷivisumbu (clear spiritual sky – paramapadam).
- *adiyēnai maṟukkēlē* – Can you enjoy even those who are exclusively engaged in service for you, in your leelās (sports)?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.9.6. Marukki valvalaip padutti

*maṟukki val valaip paduttik kumaittittuk konṟuṇbar aṟap poruḷai aṟindōrār ivai enna ulagiyaṟkai? veṟittuḷava mudiyānē! vinaiyēnai unakkadimai aṟak koṇḍāy, ini en āramudē! kūyaruḷāyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

maṟukki – (speaking fearsome words and making his heart to) be afraid; valvalaip padutti – captivating him in the net \[of fear\]; kumaittittu – catching him (so that he himself hands over his belongings); konṟu – killing him so that there is no trace \[of such incident\]; uṇbar – will live their life; aṟam poruḷai – dharma, the first goal; aṟindu – knowing; ōrār – those who don’t determine (that “this is the way for our uplifting”); ivai enna ulagiyaṟkai – How sad are these worldly situations?; veṟi tuḷavam – having very fragrant tiruttuḻāy (tulasi); mudiyānē – oh one who is wearing divine crown!; vinaiyēnai – me who is an embodiment of sins; unakku – for you; aṟa – to exist exclusively; adimai koṇḍāy – Oh one who enslaved me!; en – for me; Ar – perfect and most enjoyable; amudē – Oh divine nectar!; kūyaruḷāy – mercifully invite me and accept me

**Перевод:**

**How sad are these worldly situations where those who don’t know and determine that dharma is the first goal, will make one to be afraid, captivate him in the net of fear, catch him and kill him so that there is no trace of any such incident, and live their life \[in this manner\]!  Oh one who is wearing divine crown which is having very fragrant tiruttuḻāy (tulasi)! Oh one who enslaved me, an embodiment of sins, to exist exclusively for you! Oh perfect and most enjoyable divine nectar for me! mercifully invite me and accept me at your divine abode. aṟap poruḷai aṟindōrār also means those who know wealth only and do not care for anything else.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In sixth pāsuram, āḻvār meditates upon the faults of the samsāris (worldly people) such as not being interested towards bhagavān etc and avoids being upset with emperumān \[for not helping them\], prays to emperumān “please accept me at your divine feet to be relieved from my association with them”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. maṟukki val valaip paduttik kumaittittuk konṟuṇbar aṟap poruḷai aṟindōrār ivai enna ulagiyaṟkai? veṟittuḷava mudiyānē! vinaiyēnai unakkadimai aṟak koṇḍāy, ini en āramudē! kūyaruḷāyē*

- *maṟukki* … – This is how village heads make their earnings; an individual will appear \[to the village head\] like a “sādu” (kind hearted, good person) and will think “if we live in a town, we should have some trustworthy support” and will go to the village head; the village head, realizing the innocent nature of the individual, will tell him “many are speaking about you in different ways”; hearing that, the individual will become fearful and believe “only the village head can protect me” and ask the village head himself what needs to be done to protect himself; the village head will then say “you place your wealth in my house and give ownership of your properties to me, so that if something happens to you, I will protect you”; bewildering one’s mind in this manner.
- *val valaip padutti* – making the individual fully depend on him \[the village head\], so that the individual can never escape.
- *kumaittittu* – he \[the village head\] will then write off all wealth for his own expenses but will actually give it out for high interest \[to earn wealth\].
- *konṟu* – he \[the village head\] will then think “if he continues to live, some day he may take shelter of some one else and come at me” and will kill him.
- *uṇbar* – this is how he \[the village head\] makes his living.
- *aṟap poruḷai aṟindu* – Knowing the truth about dharma as “there is an ātmā (soul) which is different from the dēham (body); our current actions are contrary to the nature of the soul”.
- *ōrār* – Not determining this \[principle of dharma\] to start with. Alternative explanation – Not giving up harming others. orudal – oruvudal – leaving; i.e., not leaving the act of harming others. Another explanation – such people would only know the goal of arta (wealth), being greatly interested in that, they will not see what is good or bad \[and just act as they please\]. Oh lord! What kind of worldly activities are these?
- *veṟi* .. – Oh lord with divine crown having fragrant tiruttuḻāy! you manifested your enjoyable nature and enslaved me who am in the midst of these samsāris.
- *vinaiyēnai* – Me who am  having sins to be born amidst these persons who are attracted to worldly pleasures. You accepted my service at your divine feet out of your causeless mercy, even though I am not qualified for such service.
- *ini* – after having enslaved me.
- *en āramudē* – Oh one who is perfectly enjoyable for me! you should accept me so that I reach your divine feet after giving up the existence in the midst of these samsāris.

Alternative explanation –

- *ini en* – As they have not interest in the adruśtam (the unseen – paramapadam), what is the use of my worrying for their disaster? Can I not give it up? First, mercifully accept me at your divine abode, paramapadam.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.9.7. Aye ivvulagattu

*āyē ivvulagattu niṟpanavum tirivanavum nīyē maṟṟoru poruḷum inṟi nī ninṟamaiyāl nōyē mūppiṟappiṟappup piṇiyē enṟivai oḻiyak kūyē koḷ adiyēnaik kodu ulagam kāttēlē*

**Пословный перевод:**

i uvalagattu – in this world; niṟpanavum – immovable entities; tirivanavum – movable entities; nīyē āy – you yourself; maṟṟu oru poruḷum – any other entity; inṟi – without; nī – you; ninṟamaiyāl – as you exist; nōyē – disease; mūppē – old-age; piṟappē – birth; iṟappē – death; piṇiyē – pain (also, indicates poverty); enṟa – these individual aspects which are cause for sorrow; ivai – these; oḻiya – to eliminate; adiyēnai – me who is a servitor (of you); kūyē koḷ – mercifully call and accept me; kodu – cruel; ulagam – world; kāttēl – hide them from me (my eyes)

**Перевод:**

**As you exist yourself \[i.e., the in-dwelling super soul\] as the movable and immovable entities without any other entity in this world, mercifully call and accept me who am a servitor (of you) to eliminate these disease, old-age, birth, death, pain (also poverty) which are cause for sorrow; hide the cruel world from me.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In seventh pāsuram, as āḻvār‘s desire was not fulfilled immediately, he thought emperumān remains silent thinking “you yourself try and reach me” and says to emperumān “as the identity, existence etc of all entities are fully under your disposal, instead of showing this samsāram which is turning away from you, mercifully see that I reach your divine feet”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “You who are the antaryāmi of everyone should accept me so that I don’t see this cruel sorrow-filled world”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. āyē ivvulagattu niṟpanavum tirivanavum nīyē maṟṟoru poruḷum inṟi nī ninṟamaiyāl nōyē mūppiṟappiṟappup piṇiyē enṟivai oḻiyak kūyē koḷ adiyēnaik kodu ulagam kāttēlē*

- *āyē* – Can be considered as “tāyē” (Oh mother!), as said in [stōtra ratnam 5](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/12/sthothra-rathnam-5/) “*mātā pitā*” (Mother, Father …), Oh one who is all kinds of relationships to me! Alternative explanation,
- *ivvulagattu niṟpanavum tiriuvanavum nīyē – āyē* – You are the prakāri (substratum) and all the movable and immovable entities of this world are the prakāram (attribute) and thus they all are indicated as “you”.
- *maṟṟoru poruḷum inṟi* – Explaining that there is no entity which is not pervaded by [brahmam (bhagavān)](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) and existing independently as said in katavalli upaniśat 2.4.11 “*nēhanānāsti kincana*” (There is no plurality of entities) and in bruhadāraṇyaka upaniśat 6.5 “*ātmaivābhūt tatkēnakampaśyēt*” (once one realises that the world is the body of paramātmā, he can independently see that one [paramātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)).
- *nī ninṟamaiyāl* – after you exist in such manner.
- *nōy* … – An [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) (soul) will feel joyful or sorrowful for the occurrences on its dēham (body); since you are having such relationship with me, you \[should\] eliminate these anguishes which are caused by birth. nōy and piṇi are synonyms – here they are used to identify mental and physical diseases.
- *kūyē koḷ* – You should mercifully call for and accept me instead of thinking “let him come on his own”.
- *kodu ulagam* – This world which is engaged in worldly pleasures based on sound, touch etc, leaving you aside.
- *kāttēlē* – Like druśti viśam (the poison which kills on seeing it), if [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) sees this world, he will die. Since āḻvār is requesting [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) to hide this world from his vision, it is to be understood that he is not seeing it. But when emperumān shows the world to him just as he mercifully bestowed faultless knowledge and devotion to āḻvār, āḻvār will see it. But how does it match with āḻvār saying “*ivai enna ulagiyaṟkai*” (How sad are these worldly situations!) – due to “parahitam” (well-wishing for others), āḻvār meditated upon that before; here, āḻvār is saying “You should make sure that such worldly situations do not touch me”.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.9.8. Katti ni

*kātti nī karandumiḻum nilam nīr tī visumbu kāl ītti nī vaittamaitta imaiyōr vāḻ tani muttaik kōttaiyinil kaḻittennai un koḻum sōdi uyarattuk kūttariya tiruvadikkaḷ enjñānṟu kūttudiyē?*

**Пословный перевод:**

kātti – (in previous creation) revealing; nī – you who are unconditional cause; karandu – (during samhāram (deluge), conceal as said in “tama: ēkībhavati” (everything becomes merged into primordial matter)); umiḻum – (during sruśti (creation), create as spitting out what was consumed before, without any change as said in “yatāpūrvamakalpayat” (everything gets created as before); nilam nīr tī visumbu kāl – the five great elements starting with prutvi (earth); ītti – collecting them (through the process of pancīkaraṇam); vaittu – placing them (in the outside \[of the oval shaped world\] as layers of protection); imaiyōīr – brahmā et al, who don’t blink their eyes; vāḻ – to be their abodes; amaitta – prepared; tani muttai – unparalelled world; kōttaiyinai – unbreakable fort; kaḻittu – freeing; ennai – me who am desirous (to reach you, since the existence in this world is sorrowful for me); un koḻum sōdi – greatly radiant, which is distinguished/special for you; uyarattu – the most supreme abode, paramapadam, as said in “viśvata:pruśtēśu sarvata: pruśtēśu” (higher than the \[material\] world, beyond everything \[material\]); kūdu ariya – difficult to attain; tiruvadikkaḷ – divine feet; enjñānṟu – when; kūttudi – will you unite me?

**Перевод:**

**You who are the unconditional cause, revealed (in previous creation) concealment as said in “tama: ēkībhavati” and creation as spitting out what was consumed before, without any change as said in “yatāpūrvamakalpayat“, collecting the five great elements starting with prutvi (earth) and placing them in outside (as layers) and inside as abodes for those who don’t blink their eyes such as brahmā et al – this unparalelled oval-shaped world which is an unbreakable fort is created in this manner; when will you free me from this world and unite me who am desirous to attain your divine feet (which is difficult to attain) in the greatly radiant, most supreme distinguished/special abode, paramapadam, as said in “viśvata:pruśtēśu sarvata: pruśtēśu” ?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In eigt pāsuram, emperumān says “Alright. I will fulfil your desire” and āḻvār asks “When?”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “When will you, who are the antaryāmi of the entire world, eliminate my presence inside this material world and accept me at your divine feet?”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Eighth pāsuram. emperumān says “I was ready to take you to paramapadam, but as you said ‘no’, I stopped short of doing it; do you have to beg me to get this done?”; āḻvār asks “if you are ready to do it, when will you do it”. \[Did āḻvār refuse to go to paramapadam?\] āḻvār said in tiruvāimoḻi 2.9.1 “emmā vīttut tiṟamum seppam” (won’t ask the great benefit of paramapadam). kātti nī karandumiḻum nilam nīr tī visumbu kāl ītti nī vaittamaitta imaiyōr vāḻ tani muttaik kōttaiyinil kaḻittennai un koḻum sōdi uyarattuk kūttariya tiruvadikkaḷ enjñānṟu kūttudiyē?*

- *kātti* – Like a magician; [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) manifested how he previously consumed everything as part of deluge and made them to be identical with him and made the jagat (material world) exist \[as a lump\] and how he subsequently created them as said in taittirīya upaniśat nārāyaṇavalli “*dātā yatāpūrvamakalpayat*” (\[[bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) through\] brahmā created like it was present in previous times (before praḷayam)).
- *nī karandu umiḻum* – You who are the creator, yourself protected everyone by placing them inside you during deluge, and once the deluge was over, you let them out. Alternative explanation – you will manifest the concealing and you will manifest the spitting out. Through the five great elements which are consumed and spat out.
- *ītti* – collecting them. Here trivrut karaṇam (process of creating, using the three great elements – earth, water and fire) is explained \[Highlighting trivrut karaṇam is a sample for explaining pancī karaṇam (process of creating using the five great elements)\]. As said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 1.2.54 “*samēdyānyōnya samyōgam paraspara samāśrayā:*” (the five elements starting with earth are mixed with each other and are present in every object), these five elements cannot create any object on their own; even when together in equal measures, they will not lead to any visible object; like a potter will mix dust, mud and water in different proportion to create pots etc \[[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) creates these objects by mixing the elements in different proportions\]; if the mutual causes remain in a singular form, the effect will also remain singular \[indistinguishable from each other\]; these five elements remain the primary raw materials and secondary raw material to create different forms such as dēva (celestial), manuśya (human), stāvara (plant) and jangama (animals). In this manner, emperumān collects them and creates, using them.
- *nī vaittu amaitta* – You created and placed.
- *imaiyōr* … – To let me leave from this fort which is the unparalleled world where brahmā et al engage in mischievous acts. A fort is where one cannot enter from outside (easily) and one cannot exit from inside (easily) – it would be like a maze where the entry and exit points are difficult to ascertain. [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) himself said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 7.14](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/7-14/) “*duratyayā*” (difficult to cross over).
- *ennai* – Me who am caught in this fort and who do not know the way to escape. Me who am surrendered to you as you instructed in [śrī bhagavat gītā 7.14](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/7-14/) “*māmēvayē prapadyantē māyām ētām taranti tē*” (Only those who are surrendered to me, can cross over).

[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) asks “after freeing you from this, where should I take you?”

- *un koḻum sōdi uyarattu* – To the infinitely radiant paramapadam which is untouched by material aspects and which is in the mode of pure tranquility.
- *kūttariya tiruvadikkaḷ* – The divine feet which are unreachable based on one’s own self-effort.
- *enjñānṟu* – At least if you said as in śrī bhagavat gītā 18.66 “*māsuca:*” (do not worry), I can be content as said in śrī bhagavat gītā 18.73 “*stitōsmi*” (I am well situated); so, you should just mercifully say “I will accept you at my divine feet”. You should mercifully say that you will come in 14 years to make bharata happy as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 112.25 “*ārurōha ratam hruśta:*” (bharata climbed the chariot happily along with śatrugna). You should place me who want to be freed from here, in the abode where you place those who are dear to you – when will you, who are omnipotent, do it? You who created this fort, yourself should free me from it. One should surrender to [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) only to have the hurdles removed and to attain him also, he should be attained through him only; śrī bhagavat gītā 7.14 “*māmēvayē prapadyantē*” (surrender unto me only) and śrī bhagavat gītā 18.62 “*tamēva śaraṇam gacca*” (surrender unto him only). piḷḷai tirunaraiyūr araiyar explains “No one can dismantle a nest created by a sparrow; how can the weakest samsāri break the nest/web created by sarvaśakti ([bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) who is omnipotent) based on the karma of each individual, without surrendering unto him?”.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.9.9. Kuttudi

*kūttudi nin kurai kaḻalgaḷ imaiyōrum toḻā vagai seydu āttudi nī aravaṇaiyāy adiyēnum adu aṟivan vētkai ellām viduttennai un tiruvadiyē sumanduḻalak kūttariya tiruvadikkaḷ kūttinai nān kaṇḍēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

nī – you (who is omnipotent); kurai – perfectly enjoyable; nin kaḻalgaḷ – at your divine feet; kūttudi – please accept me; imaiyōrum – (greatly knowledgeable) dēvas; toḻā vagai – to not see and enjoy you; seydu – doing; āttudi – agitate them; aravu – tiruvanantāḻvān (the leader among devotees); aṇaiyāy – Oh one who is having as bed!; adu – your nature of being easy to be attained and difficult to be attained with respect to devotees and others respectively; adiyēnum – I too who am a servitor; aṟivan – knows; vētkai ellām – affection in worldly matters; viduttu – eliminating with the trace; ennai – me who have great desire towards you and cannot live without you; tiru – perfectly enjoyable; un adi – your divine feet; sumandu – holding them on my head; uḻala – to follow you as said in “yēna yēna dātā gaccati” (wherever the master goes); kūtta – to reach (even for the most knowledgeable); ariya – difficult; tiruvadikkaḷ – at the divine feet; kūttinai – you accepted; nān kaṇḍēn – I saw (it in front of me) and enjoyed; E – certainly

**Перевод:**

**You please accept me at your perfectly enjoyable divine feet. If one tried to see, by one’s own effort, you make sure that even dēvas do not see and enjoy you and agitate them; oh one who is having tiruvanantāḻvān as bed! I too who am a servitor, know your nature of being easy to be attained and difficult to be attained with respect to devotees and others respectively.  Eliminating my affection in worldly matters with all traces, you made me, who have great desire towards you and cannot live without you, hold your perfectly enjoyable divine feet on my head and follow you as said in “yēna yēna dātā gaccati” and accepted me at the divine feet which are difficult to reach; I certainly saw (it in front of me) and enjoyed this.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In ninth pāsuram, emperumān mercifully manifests his divine presence in tirunādu (paramapadam) to āḻvār to eliminate all of āḻvār’s grief; āḻvār, having seen it and having mercifully given up his attachment for all other matters says “you have presented your divine feet which are difficult to attain; I have enjoyed that” and feels satisfied.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. kūttudi nin kurai kaḻalgaḷ imaiyōrum toḻā vagai seydu āttudi nī aravaṇaiyāy adiyēnum adu aṟivan vētkai ellām viduttennai un tiruvadiyē sumanduḻalak kūttariya tiruvadikkaḷ kūttinai nān kaṇḍēnē*

- *kūttudi nin kurai kaḻalgaḷ* – Even if unqualified, you accept those who are dear to you, at your divine feet. kurai – greatness or the sound of the ornament.
- *imaiyōr* … – Even brahmā et al, if you don’t consider them to be acceptable, you will agitate them so that they don’t reach you.
- *aravaṇaiyāy* – This is an example for “*kūttudi*” \[those who are with him irrespective of their knowledge – since ādiśēśa is in a reptile form, he is considered as less intelligent in layman terms\].
- *adiyēnum adu aṟivan* – I know your nature which is well revealed in scriptures of this world (itihāsams and purāṇams).

How did you know \[Did you know through śāstram\]?

- *vētkai ellām viduttu* – Before, whatever that was not related to you, did I not desire for all of them? Is there anything that I have not desired in your \[material\] world? Did you not remove my attachments as said in tiruviruttam 95 “*yādānum paṟṟi nīngum viradattai nalvīdu seydu*” (my attitude of leaving you citing any reason, was reformed by you)?
- *un tiruvadiyē sumandu uḻala* – To have all the attachments I had in worldly matters (before), at you (now), holding on to your divine feet only and having that only as my routine.
- *kūttariya* … – You accepted me at your divine feet which are difficult to attain by self-effort of even great personalities. I am not saying these based on hearsay, but based on personal experience \[nān kaṇḍēn\].

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.9.10. Kandu kettu

*kaṇḍu kēttuṟṟu mōndu uṇḍuḻalum aingaruvi kaṇḍa inbam terivariya aḷavillāc ciṟṟinbam oṇḍodiyāḷ  tirumagaḷum nīyumē nilā niṟpak kaṇḍa sadir kaṇḍoḻindēn adaindēn un tiruvadiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kaṇḍu – seeing (the quality of form); kēttu – hearing (the quality of sound); uṟṟu – contacting (the quality of touch); mōndu – smelling (the quality of fragrance); uṇḍu – eating (the quality of taste); uḻalum – agitate (not being satisfied with what was acquired and will make one long for more of the same kind); aim karuvi – through the five senses; kaṇḍa – enjoyed by analysing individually; inbam – the joy of worldly pleasure; terivu – to be comprehended by these senses and enjoy; ariya – difficult; aḷavillā – incomprehensible (in comparison to worldly pleasures in terms of being eternal etc); ciṟu inbam – the joy of self-enjoyment which is very insignificant when compared to the joy of experiencing bhagavān; oṇ todiyāḷ – one who is having distinguished curved forearms; tirumagaḷum – the best among women, who is known as śrī due to being the collection of all wealth; nīyumē – you only (who is the best among men); nilā niṟpa – remaining together (to manifest the wealth and the true nature); kaṇḍa – determined; sadir – the best means; kaṇḍu – seeing it in front of me; oḻindēn – gave up (worldly pleasure and self-enjoyment); un tiruvadi – (to have all entities present in you, being śriya:pati and the ultimate goal) your divine feet; adaindēn – attained (in the form of visual experience)

**Перевод:**

**After seeing in front of me \[the three different goals namely\] a) the joy of worldly pleasure enjoyed by analysing individually through the five senses of seeing,  hearing, contacting, smelling  and eating and feeling agitated by these b) the joy of self-enjoyment which is incomprehensible, which is difficult to be comprehended by these senses and enjoy and which is very insignificant when compared to joy of experiencing bhagavān and c) the togetherness of you and the one who is having distinguished forearms with ornaments like bangles, the best among women, who is known as śrī due to being the collection of all wealth, and determined the best means, gave up worldly pleasure and self-enjoyment and attained your divine feet.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In tenth pāsuram, out of great love, āḻvār clearly explains “what was given up and what was pursued”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, emperumān asks “How did I eliminate the other benefits for you and bestow you the ultimate benefit?”, āḻvār replies “I am blessed to give up aiśvarya (worldly pleasures) and kaivalya (eternal self-enjoyment), determined you who are śriya:pati (lord of śrī mahālakśmi) as the goal and attained you too”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. kaṇḍu kēttuṟṟu mōndu uṇḍuḻalum aingaruvi kaṇḍa inbam terivariya aḷavillāc ciṟṟinbam oṇḍodiyāḷ  tirumagaḷum nīyumē nilā niṟpak kaṇḍa sadir kaṇḍoḻindēn adaindēn un tiruvadiyē*

- *kaṇḍu* … – Eye which is a tool to see, ear which is a tool to hear, skin which is a tool to feel touch, nose which is a tool to smell and tongue which is a tool to taste. The senses facilitate one to spend his/her life by just seeing, hearing, feeling, smelling and touching \[worldly pleasures\].
- *aim karuvi kaṇḍa inbam* – The worldly pleasure which is enjoyed by senses which are limited in capability like a measuring cup. The jñānam (knowledge, consciousness) which is an eternal quality of ātmā, is contracted due to being bound by karma \[puṇya, pāpa\], comes out through the mind, and absorbs the pleasure/pain through external sense organs.
- *terivariya aḷavillāc ciṟṟinbam* – While compared to worldly pleasure, the ātmānubhavam (kaivalyam, self-enjoyment) is difficult to attain, and when compared to bhagavat anubhavam (experiencing bhagavān) it is worthless; since ātmānubhavam is enjoyment based on the atomic ātmā, the enjoyment is also comprehensible.
- *oḻindēn* – gave up these.
- *siṟṟinbam* – It is the opposite of “*antamil pērinbam*” (endless great joy).
- *oṇ todiyāḷ* … – When periya pirāttiyār and you are together, the whole of nitya vibhūti became subdued in your affection – I have seen this divine togetherness. todi – bangle worn in forearm. The greatness for those bangles is, not to ever slip from her hands. Since she is *nityānapayini* (always inseparable \[from emperumān\]), there is no reason for those bangles to slip once and be worn again. She is said in tiruccanda viruttam 57 “*sangu tangu munkai nangai*” (The perfect lady who has beautiful bangles in her forearm).
- *tirumagaḷum nīyumē* – You who are desired by such pirātti as said in tiruvāimoḻi 6.10.10 “*iṟaiyum agalagillēn*“.
- *nīyumē nilā niṟpa* – In both of your abhimānam (affection/care), the whole tripād vibhūti (3 parts – spiritual realm – paramapadam) will be present in a subdued manner. While it is said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 1.8.35 “*nānyōr vidyatē param*” (Except for śrīman nārāyaṇan and śrī mahālakśmī, there is no one else independently existing), everywhere people consider themselves to be the lords in this material realm.
- *nilā niṟpak kaṇḍa sadir* – The proper situation of being under the shelter of you both, which is arranged by you; as said in Siva \[linga\] purāṇam “*vaikuṇṭē tu parē lōkē śriyāsārdam jagat patē*” (In the divine world of vaikuṇṭam, viṣṇu is present with śrī mahākśmi, being served by nityasūris), the arrangement you have done. Have seen that.
- *un tiruvadiyē adaindēn* – I approached those divine feet thinking “I should be present along with those nityasūris and serve your divine feet”. This is what I am holding on to; whatever I have explained previously, have been given by me.

By saying “*ondodiyāḷ tirumagaḷum nīyumē*“, does it explain the togetherness in nitya vibhūti (spiritual realm) \[being served with many devotees\]? As āḻvār himself has said in [tiruvāimoḻi – 2.3.10](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/02/thiruvaimozhi-2-3-10-kalippum-kavarvum/) “*adiyārgaḷ kuḻāngaḷai udan kūduvadu enṟu kolō*” (When will I be amidst the nityasūris?), and there are other pramāṇams such as in Siva \[linga\] purāṇam “*vaikuṇṭē tu* … *bhaktai: bhāgavatais saha:*” (be along with bhaktas and bhāgavatas). Also, as he said in “*niṟpanavum tirivanavum nīyē maṟṟoru poruḷuminṟi*” (all immovable and movable objects are your manifestation only) and then said “*kodu ulagam kāttēl*” (don’t show me this cruel world) \[where āḻvār is saying there are innumerable entities in this material realm but all are pervaded and controlled by bhagavān\]; similarly when it is said “only pirātti and perumāḷ”, it would imply the \[spiritual\] realm which is fully under the full care of that divine couple. But can emperumān accept such servitude from āḻvār in this material realm itself? No, it will be in paramapadam with emperumān’s distinguished form, as lakśmaṇa prayed to śrī rāma in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 31.25 “*bhavāms tu saha vaidēhyā*” (I want to serve you along with sītāp pirātti) and śrī rāma accepted lakśmaṇa’s service as requested by him in śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 15.7 “*kriyatāmiti mām vada*” (lakśmaṇa to śrī rāma – order me in what should be done) \[In case of śrī rāma, sītā and lakśmaṇa, they were all present together and so lakśmaṇa could serve there as he desired. Here, āḻvār specifically prays to be freed from this world and engage in kainkaryam in paramapadam, so emperumān gives him kainkaryam in paramapadam as āḻvār desired\].

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.9.11. Tiruvadiyai narananai

*tiruvadiyai nāraṇanai kēsvanaip param sudarait tiruvadi sērvadu karudic ceḻum kurugūrc catakōpan tiruvadi mēl uraitta tamiḻ āyiarattuḷ ippattum tiruvadiyē adaivikkum tiruvadi sērndonṟuminē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tiruvadiyai – being sarvaśēśi (master of all); nāraṇanai – having the ability to be present as in-dwelling soul in every entity, to lord over every entity; kēsavanai – eliminating the hurdles of his devotees just as he killed kēśi, the demoniac horse; param sudarai – on kriṣṇa who is having unsurpassed radiance (due to having the relationship with all, having vātsalyam (motherly forbearance) and having the ability to eliminate the enemies); tiruvadi – his divine feet; sērvadu – to attain; karudi – having the intention; seḻum kurugūr – being the leader of āḻvārtirunagari which is having unsurpassed enjoyability; śatakōpan – nammāḻvār; tiruvadi mēl – on his divine feet; uraitta – mercifully spoke; tamiḻ āyirattuḷ – among the thousand tamiḻ pāsurams; ip pattum – this decad; tiruvadiyē – those divine feet themselves; adaivikkum – help attain; tiruvadi – those divine feet; sērndu – attain; onṟumin – (being inseparable) try to serve them

**Перевод:**

**nammāḻvār, the leader of āḻvārtirunagari which is having unsurpassed enjoyability, having the intention to attain the divine feet of kriṣṇa, mercifully spoke about him who is the sarvaśēśi, who is having the ability to be present as in-dwelling soul in every entity, to lord over every entity and who eliminates the hurdles of his devotees just as he killed kēśi, the demoniac horse; mercifully spoke in this decad among the thousand tamiḻ pāsurams on his divine feet; such decad will help one attain those divine feet themselves; you, who are engaged in this decad, attain those divine feet and try to serve them (being inseparable).**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the end, āḻvār says “This decad will help those who practice (learn/recite) it to attain the divine feet of emperumān; hence,  you practice it, reach his divine feet and be uplifted”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. tiruvadiyai nāraṇanai kēsvanaip param sudarait tiruvadi sērvadu karudic ceḻum kurugūrc catakōpan tiruvadi mēl uraitta tamiḻ āyiarattuḷ ippattum tiruvadiyē adaivikkum tiruvadi sērndonṟuminē*

- [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) meditates upon [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s act of eliminating the attachment towards other aspects and nurturing attachment towards emperumān himself, and praises emperumān;
- *tiruvadiyai* – one who is the lord of all.
- *nāraṇanai* – Not just the having lordship, but even when one rejects such lordship, emperumān has the vātsalyam (motherly forbearance) which makes him not give up on anyone.
- *kēsavanai* – Instead of merely showing motherly affection from outside, he appeared as a human \[covherd boy\] and eliminated the enemies of them \[the covherd clan\].
- *param sudarai* – His supremacy which was visible even while assuming a human form.
- *tiruvadi sērvadu karudi* – One who has the desire to reach his divine feet. From the beginning this is [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s desire, as seen in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.1.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/03/thiruvaimozhi-1-1-1-uyarvara-uyarnalam/) “*tuyaraṟu sudaradi toḻudu eḻu*” (bow at the divine feet which removes the sorrows and rise).
- *seḻum kurugūrc catakōpan* – It is the birth in this town which caused this great love in āḻvār \[towards [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)\] – similar to the nature of the land in śrī ayōdyā will nurture rāma bhakti.
- *tiruvadi mēl uraitta .*.. – Among the thousand pāsurams, this decad will help one reach his divine feet; you too, for this, please go and pursue his divine feet. As you approach his divine feet, like a rice pot \[which is totally dependent on its owner\], giving up all enjoyment for self, try to serve his divine feet eternally. You serve him to his divine heart’s content, by being inseparable like iḷaiya perumāḷ (lakśmaṇa) and serve him, as said in “*sāyujyam pratipannāyē*” (having attained an equal position, and having their hurdles eliminated, they remain eternal servitors) and as said in parama samhitā “*yēna yēna dātā gaccati tēna tēna saha gaccati*” (wherever the lord goes, the servitor follows). For those who serve in this manner, do they have to give up what was given up by [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) and pursue what was pursued by āḻvār? This decad, on being meditated and practiced upon, will nurture detachment in worldly pleasures and will also help one reach his divine feet.
