## 4.10 Onrum devum

## 4.10.1. Onrum devum

*onṟum dēvum ulagum uyirum maṟṟum yādum illā anṟu nānmugan tannodu dēvar ulagōdu uyir padaittān kunṟam pōl maṇi māda nīdu tirukkurugūr adanuḷ ninṟa ādip pirān niṟka maṟṟait teyvam nādudirē*

**Пословный перевод:**

onṟum – (as said in “tama: ēkī bhavati“, in his nature) became subdued; dēvum – dēva (celestial) species; ulagum – the world (where they reside); uyirum – other species (such as manuśya (human) etc); maṟṟum – all entities (mahat etc, which are in samaśti (collective) form); yādum – all entities; illā anṟu – when they were annihilated; nānmugan tannodu – with brahmā who is the samaśti puruśa (one who is created at the end of samaśti sruśti (creation up to five great elements)); dēvar – dēvatās; ulagu – world; uyir – other different species; padaittān – having created (to have them accept his refuge); kunṟam pōl – like mountains; maṇi – with abundance of precious stones; mādam – mansions; nīdu – tall; tirukkurugūr adanuḷ – in \[āḻvār\]tirunagari; ninṟa – standing (in an easily approachable manner for those who want to surrender unto him); ādi – the cause of everything; pirān – great benefactor; niṟka – when he is present well; maṟṟai – those who are affected by creation and annihilation; deyvam – dēvatās; nādudirē – you are approaching (as shelter)

**Перевод:**

**When dēva species, their world, other species, all entities (in collective form or in no name/form) were all annihilated and became subdued \[in bhagavān\], emperumān created brahmā who is the samaśti puruśa, dēvatās, their world and other different species; when such emperumān is standing well in āḻvārtirunagari that is having tall mountain like mansions, he being the cause of everything and the great benefactor, you are approaching these dēvatās who are \[also\] affected by creation and annihilation.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

piḷḷān gives an elaborate list of pramāṇams from śāstram citing [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s supremacy. Please refer to the original commentary for the same.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In first pāsuram, āḻvār, in line with mahōpaniśat statement “ēkōhavai nārāyaṇa āsīt” (Only nārāyaṇa existed before creation), says “when the kāryarūpaprapancam (the universe in the form of effect) was completely non-existing, sarvēśvaran who is the cause of the universe, created the universe through caturmukha (four-headed) brahmā; such emperumān is mercifully standing to be seen and surrendered by you all in \[āḻvār\]tirunagari which has mountain like tall mansions; instead of taking shelter of him, you are searching for other dependable dēvatās”, and condemns them.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār in line with statements which establish emperumān’s causal nature, asks \[the materialistic people\] “while sarvēśvaran who is the cause for everything is present, which other dēvatā are you searching for?”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. It is also highlighted that emperumān is present in tirunagari with motherly affection towards the suffering souls to help them. onṟum dēvum ulagum uyirum maṟṟum yādum illā anṟu nānmugan tannodu dēvar ulagōdu uyir padaittān kunṟam pōl maṇi māda nīdu tirukkurugūr adanuḷ ninṟa ādip pirān niṟka maṟṟait teyvam nādudirē*

- *onṟum dēvum* … – dēvatās and their worlds, ātmās who have assumed forms such as manuśya (human) etc, mahat etc which are causes for oval shaped universes, and all others – at the time when they were not present – “*onṟum*” (none of these) is recited at the end of this section.  Alternative explanation – since effect becomes subdued in cause \[during deluge\], as bhagavān is the cause, dēvas, worlds, and all other entities are subdued in him and are thus not visibly present.  It is said in cāndōjña upaniśat “*sadēva*” (only sat remained).
- *nānmugan* … – When others set out to protect/help the rest, they will see some reason and think “there will be some use by them some day” and then only help; sarvēśvaran is the only one who protects without expecting anything from anyone.
- *nānmugan tannodu dēvar ulagōdu uyir padaittān* – Through caturmukha (four-headed) brahmā, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) created their worlds and the different forms accepted by cētanas (sentient beings). sarvēśvara created caturmukha (four headed brahmā); caturmukha created pancamukha (five headed rudra); pancamukha created śaṇmukha (six headed skanda) – this way creation became variegated. Though worldly people give great importance to rudra and become confused, since [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) did not see anything special in rudra, instead cites brahmā who was born directly from the divine naval lotus of bhagavān and includes rudra in the group of \[remaining\] dēvatās. In samhāram (annihilation), āḻvār cited mahat tatvam etc; in sruśti (creation), he cited brahmā; the reason for this is – no one considers mahat to be supreme; but common people consider brahmā as supreme – so, to eliminate such doubts, āḻvār cites brahmā and discards him saying he is also part of the created entourage. emperumān created without any difference, brahmā who creates the 14 layered oval shaped universe, the ten prajāpatis (progenitors) who are created by brahmā to manage routine/subsequent creation, the worlds which are the abodes for their enjoyment, the citizens of such worlds etc; he also bestowed them body and senses, to let them seek enjoyment and liberation.
- *kunṟam …* – Such [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), after creating these, instead of being away from those created places, stood in āḻvārtirunagari which has tall mansions which appear like mountains that are filled with precious stones. As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 50.3 “*āśayāyadivārāma: punaśśabdāpayētiti*” (sumantra said – I waited along with guha there with the desire of śrī rāma calling for me again), emperumān is waiting there thinking “with the body and senses I have given them, would they come to me instead of saying ‘*na namēyam*‘ (I will not worship him)”. Alternative explanation – emperumān waiting there thinking “even if I myself tried to accept them, would they at least not reject me?”. There \[in śrī rāmāyaṇam\], the śēśabhūta (servitor) waited to be accepted by śēśi (the lord); here the lord is waiting to be accepted by the servitors.
- *ādip pirān niṟka* – Giving up such [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who has arrived with affection towards you all and reside permanently in tirunagari.
- *maṟṟait teyvam nādudirē* – You can only search for other dēvatās but cannot find the proper refuge. As said in “*vāsudēvam parityajya yōnyam dēvamupāsatē \| truśitō jāhnavītīrē kūpamganatidurmati: \|\|*” (one who leaves aside kriṣṇa, who is the son of vasudēva, and worships other dēvatās, that fool is like a thirsty person who is digging a well at the banks of river gangā), \[one who is seeking other dēvatās is like \] a thirsty person, while river gangā is flowing nicely, instead of drinking water directly from that and quenching his thirst, is digging a well to quench his thirst; [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is condemning those who are giving up [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is natural/apt lord, easily approachable, easily vorśippable and with great qualities, and are seeking out other dēvatās who are inapt, difficult to attain, difficult to worship and with no great qualities, and even if vorśipped, it is as said in tirumālai 10 “*sēttai than madi agattu selvam pāṟttu*” (trying to get wealth from the inauspicious mūdēvi deity), those dēvatās who are lacking [śrī mahālakśmi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/) in them.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.10.2. Nadi nir

*nādi nīr vaṇangum deyvamum ummaiyum mun padaittān vīdil sīrp pugaḻ ādippirān avan mēvi uṟai kōyil māda māḷigai sūḻndaḻagāya tirukkurugūradanaip pādi ādip paravic cenmingaḷ pallulagīr parandē*

**Пословный перевод:**

nīr – you (who are filled with rajas (passion) and tamas (ignorance)); nādi – determine (based on your own quality); vaṇangum – surrender; deyvamum – dēvatās; ummaiyum – you as well (who are intent on surrendering to such dēvatās); mun – during sruśti (creation); padaittān – one who created; vīdil sīr – having eternal auspicious qualities such as jñānam (knowledge), śakti (ability) etc (for such creation); pugaḻ – greatness (as per vēdāntam); ādip pirān avan – the first benefactor; mēvi – well fixed (to be friendly towards his devotees); uṟai – reside; kōyil – \[divine\] abode; mādam – mansions; māḷigai – palaces; sūḻndu – surrounded; aḻagāya – beautiful to these; tirukkurugūr adanai – tirunagari; pal ulagīr – Oh those who are residing in different worlds (due to your quality and taste)!; pādi – sing; ādi – dance (out of joyful emotions); paravi – praise (in many ways); parandu senmingaḷ – engage everywhere

**Перевод:**

**sarvēśvaran, the first benefactor who created the dēvatās you determine \[to be vorśippable\] and surrender unto, and you as well, during the creation, who is having eternal auspicious qualities such as jñānam (knowledge), śakti (ability) etc and greatness, is residing well fixed in this divine abode tirunagari which is beautiful due to being surrounded by mansions and palaces; oh those who are residing in different worlds! you engage in singing, dancing and praising him everywhere.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In second pāsuram, āḻvār says to those who are created by emperumān “You and the dēvatās you worship are the same \[when it comes to being created by bhagavān\]; hence, you take shelter of tirunagari where sarvēśvaran who is eternal wealth, is standing mercifully”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. nādi nīr vaṇangum deyvamum ummaiyum mun padaittān vīdil sīrp pugaḻ ādippirān avan mēvi uṟai kōyil māda māḷigai sūḻndaḻagāya tirukkurugūradanaip pādi ādip paravic cenmingaḷ pallulagīr parandē*

- *nādi nīr vaṇangum deyvamum* – While the dēvatās themselves withdraw them from being glorified due to not having true glories but glories which are built only through fake statements and fake speeches, you try hard and make them stand upright by false praises which are not present in them – such dēvatās.
- *nādi* – Like a thief is searched and caught, these dēvatās are to be searched and found. They are the one who stole goat; since they brought a goat for sacrifice as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 4.6.7](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/03/thiruvaimozhi-4-6-7-anangukku/) “*aṇangukku aru marundu angu ōr ādum kaḷḷum*” (What is the benefit of your praying to the other dēvatā to cut a goat). As said in “*kaḷḷar accam kādu koḷḷādu*” (the fear of the thieves is beyond the capacity of the forest), the dēvatās will fear for those who come to surrender unto them to be those who have come to catch them.
- *nīr* – You who are having rājasa and tāmasa quality. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying “You” to highlight that he cannot co-exist with them. They (those dēvatās) have nothing to sustain themselves other than your faith in them.
- *nīr vaṇangum deyvamum ummaiyum* – While creating the dēvatās you worship who are having rājasa and tāmasa quality, along with yourself.
- *mun padaittān* – During creation, he first created them and then created you. As said in svētāsvatara upaniśat “*yō brahmāṇam vidadāti pūrvam*“ (first [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) created brahmā), bhagavān created brahmā first followed by everyone else here.
- *nīr vaṇangum deyvamum ummaiyum* *mun padaittān* – Unless he created those dēvatās how would you all worship them?
- *padaittān* – If he does not create those dēvatās who will you worship? Only when you worship, they become vorśippable deities.
- *vīdil sīr …* – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is having natural opulence unlike those dēvatās whose wealth are under the disposal/control of an individual ([bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)), based on their own past karma and when that karma is exhausted, their wealth will also be exhausted.
- *vīdil sīr* – bhagavān’s wealth is unlike the wealth of the dēvatās you worship which have a boundary/limit; their wealth is based on their karma and when the puṇya (virtues) diminishes, their wealth too will decrease; or when the mercy of emperumān who benedicts the opulence reduces, their wealth will decrease too. uttara mīmāmsā 3.2.37 “*pala mata:*” (all benefits are received from that supreme lord).
- *vīdil sīr* – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is having eternally auspicious qualities. As said in “*tasmin yat antas tadupāsitavyam*” (that which is inside him is also to be meditated upon), just as we meditate upon emperumān, we shall also meditate upon his auspicious qualities.
- *pugaḻ* – Being famous for protecting everyone. Would he who protects everyone be not considered as the protector? śrī rāmāyaṇam kiśkintā kāṇḍam 15.19 “*yaśasaścaikabhājanam*” (one who is the abode of glories).
- *ādip pirān* – Not only he is famous for protecting others, he also has natural relationship with everyone.
- *pirān* – Not just naturally related to everyone, but also the benefactor for everyone. One who is benefactor; naturally related and famous; one can surrender unto some one who has all the opulence and eternally auspicious qualities only; it is not apt to surrender unto some one who does not have these. That which is the cause for everything is to be meditated upon – cāndōjña upaniśat “*kāraṇam tu dyēya:*”.
- *avan mēvi uṟai kōyil* – [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) remains with anguish in paramapadam. Considering the sufferings of samsāris, he remains in paramapadam thinking “what are they going through?”. Only for the liberated souls who were previously suffering in this material realm, there is no necessity to think about the sorrows of this material realm, as said in cāndōjña upaniśat 8.12.3 “*nōpajanam smaran idam śarīram*” ([ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) will not contemplate about the material body after reaching the spiritual realm). bhagavān does not have the shortcoming of “when enjoying, by thinking about sorrows, one’s joy may be reduced”. While bhattar mercifully explained “[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) mercifully resides in paramapadam thinking about the suffering of the samsāris, in his divine heart with anguish”, a person named “*paṇḍitar*” presented a question to him saying “āccān and piḷḷai āḻvān heard this and asked if it is appropriate to consider emperumān who is with great joy in paramapadam to be in anguish?”. bhattar mercifully explained “Did you not ask them if the śrī rāmāyaṇa ślōkam in ayōdyā kāṇḍam 2.42 ‘*vyasanēṣu ca manuśyānām*‘ (śrī rāma becomes anguished seeing others suffer) explained in context of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s glorification or in his shortcoming? If something is explained as an auspicious quality \[here\], would it not be present there too?”. He is explained as said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 6.5.84 “*samasta kalyāṇa guṇātmakōsau*” (one who is having all auspicious qualities naturally). Other than saying that he does not experience anything based on karma without his own desire and If there is no personal experience for him based on his own mercy \[towards others\], it will indicate that [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is not even a [cētana (sentient being)](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) \[since any cētana will have personal experience/emotions\]. It is said in mahōpaniśat, “*sa ēkāki na ramēta*” ([śrīman nārāyaṇa](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), who was alone during deluge, was not joyful) while he has nitya vibhūti (spiritual realm) and auspicious qualities.
- *ādip pirān avan mēvi uṟai kōyil* – As there is none who is lesser than him in paramapadam (to protect), [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) happily comes and resides in this abode ([āḻvārtirunagari](http://azhwarthirunagari.koyil.org/)) where samsāris seek protection, like a mother would give up the comforts of her own bed etc and lie down next to the cradle of her child.
- *māda māḷigai …* – Anyway, you like beautiful towns; doesn’t this place appear to be similar to that which is desired by liberated souls? Being surrounded with mansions and palaces and hence looking very beautiful.
- *adanaip pādi ādi* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying – “*adanuḷ ninṟa ādip pirān*” (the ādip pirān who resides in this town) is also extraneous. The abode itself is the attainable goal as said in garuda purāṇam 11th chapter “*viṣṇōrāyatanēvasēt*” (one should live in the divine abode of viṣṇu) and “*dēśōyamsarvakāmaduk*” (the abode which can fulfill all desires).
- *pādi ādi …* – Singing out of overwhelming love, dancing by swaying the body and calling out [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s names in a disorderly manner. āḻvār thinks that like himself others would also behave the same way as soon as they hear the name of emperumān’s abode.
- *pal ulagīr* – It is not that some one is approaching [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) with very humble and obedient attitude and āḻvār is instructing him; looking at the suffering everywhere in the world as said in “*ivai enna ulagiyaṟkai*” (How sad is the situation here), āḻvār is instructing everyone.
- *parandē* – Like how everyone would arrive from all directions to śrīrangam for periya tirunāḷ (adyayana utsavam), āḻvār is saying “go over in all directions and sing the glories everywhere”.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.10.3. Paranda deyvamum

*paranda deyvamum pallulagum padaittu anṟudanē viḻungik karandumiḻndu kadandidandadu kaṇḍum teḷiyagilleer sirangaḷāl amarar vaṇangum tirukkurugūr adanuḷ paran tiṟam anṟip pallulagīr! deyvam maṟṟillai pēsuminē*

**Пословный перевод:**

paranda – being vast (due to being appointed by emperumān himself, and being took as supreme); deyvamum – different dēvatās; pal ulagum – many different worlds (which are their wealth); padaittu – creating; anṟu – back then (during deluge); udanē – immediately (without giving importance to the process/order); viḻungi – consuming; karandu – concealing (so the worlds can be protected from praḷayam (deluge)); umiḻndu – (after the deluge, to see the outside) spitting them out; kadandu – owning them up fully (to eliminate the ownership/pride of mahābali, measuring it); idandadu – (during avāntara praḷayam (intermediate deluge), in the form of varāha) rescuing it; kaṇḍum – even after seeing clearly (through pramāṇams (authentic texts)); teḷiyagilleer – you are unable to have clarity; amarar – dēvas (starting with brahmā et al); sirangaḷāl – with their heads; vaṇangum – bowing and vorśipping; tirukkurugūr adanuḷ – standing in tirunagari; paran – for the sarvasmātaparan (the supreme lord of all); tiṟam anṟi – not being the prakāra (mode/form); maṟṟu – any other independent; deyvam – dēvatā; illai – not present; pal – different (having different levels of intellect); ulagīr – the residents of worlds; pēsumin – tell me (if there is any one)

**Перевод:**

**Even after seeing clearly emperumān creating many different dēvatās and their many different vast worlds, back then consuming all the worlds immediately (during deluge) concealing them from the deluge, spitting them out (after the deluge), owning them up fully and rescuing them, you are unable to have clarity; there is no independent dēvatā present that is not a prakāram (form) of the supreme lord who is standing in tirunagari and who is being bowed and vorśipped by all dēvatās; oh the residents of different worlds! tell me if there is any such dēvatā.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

piḷḷān gives an elaborate list of pramāṇams from śāstram citing [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s supremacy. Please refer to the original commentary for the same.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In third pāsuram, āḻvār says “Even by his divine activities related to the universe such as annihilation etc, emperumān is the supreme lord; those who do not agree with this can come and debate with me”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “The protection etc of the universe which is an effect \[from the cause\], is that which reveals the lord’s supremacy”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. paranda deyvamum pallulagum padaittu anṟudanē viḻungik karandumiḻndu kadandidandadu kaṇḍum teḷiyagilleer sirangaḷāl amarar vaṇangum tirukkurugūr adanuḷ paran tiṟam anṟip pallulagīr! deyvam maṟṟillai pēsuminē*

- *paranda deyvamum* – The different dēvatās who have grown vast and covering the supreme lord, like a fruit will be covered by the creeper. These dēvatās are highlighted \[to show their celestial powers\] and then discarded \[saying that they are not the supreme lord\].
- *pal ulagum* – The vast worlds which can behold the vastness of those dēvatās. The other controlled cētanas (sentient beings) who make these dēvatās controllers.
- *padaittu* – creating the. Having no distinction between the dēvatās and others, when it comes to creation.
- *anṟu udanē viḻungi …* – While creating, emperumān did that in an order; svētāsvatara upaniśat “*yō brahmāṇam vidadāti pūrvam*“ (first [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) created brahmā); but when there is imminent danger \[of deluge\], he cannot protect in a particular order \[he immediately protects\]. Placing the worlds inside him during deluge, and concealing their presence to protect them further from the deluge, and thinking that the worlds are suffering inside and releasing them out at the appropriate time, and amidst all this if the likes of mahābali snatches the worlds like an eagle catching its prey, then measuring them up and recapturing them, and when the world became submerged during \[intermediate\] deluge and became attached to the wall of the material realm, assuming the form of varāha and rescuing it. These various activities \[are\] performed by emperumān.
- *kaṇḍum* – For āḻvār, śāstram is more clearly visible than pratyakśam (perception). Seeing these super-human abilities, while it is easy to understand that emperumān is the one to be surrendered unto, you are not knowing that.
- *teḷiyagilleer* – Except for their clarity or lack of the same, there is no change in the underlying principle \[of emperumān’s supremacy\]. Except for your clarity or the lack of the same, no one can make emperumān the supreme lord or not \[he is always the supreme lord\].
- *sirangaḷ* … – Though you remain indifferent and think that “emperumān is not the creator of all and he is not the one who helps everyone in danger”, at least if you first see the activities of the dēvatās you worship, you will acquire clarity. At least by seeing their attitude of bowing to emperumān thinking “the purpose of having a head is fulfilled by bowing in front of emperumān’, you surrender unto emperumān. mahābhāratam rāja darmam “*pādēna kamalāpēna brahma rudraārcitēnā*” (emperumān gently touched with his divine feet which were vorśipped by brahmā, rudra et al); perumāḷ tirumoḻi 4.3 “*pinnitta sadaiyānum piramanum indiranum tunnittup pugalariya*” (tiruvēnkatam, the divine abode, which is difficult to enter for rudra who has matted hair, brahmā and indra); periya tirumoḻi 1.7.8 “*nāttaḻumba nānmuganum īsanumāy muṟaiyāl ētta*” (brahmā and rudra are emotionally praising emperumān in an orderly manner).
- *tirukkurugūr adanuḷ paran* – This is even beyond emperumān’s manifestation of supremacy in a human form. As one approaches this side \[from supremacy to simplicity\], his greatness increases manifold. An entity is glorified based on its qualities; only here in arcāvatāram, his qualities are well present.
- *adanuḷ paran* – As said in rig vēdam “*dvā suparṇā sayujā sakhāyā samānam vrukśam pariśasvajātē \| tayōranya: pippalam svādvatti anaśnannanyō abicākasīti \|\|*” (There are two related (servant and master) birds ([jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) and [paramātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)) residing in a tree (body). One bird ([jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)) enjoys the fruits of its actions (karma) and the other one (paramātmā) being detached is radiantly witnessing that), as the cētanas (ātmās – souls) become dimmer the more they engage in worldly activities and emperumān’s radiance will increase due to his controlling nature while residing with them, his supremacy too becomes radiant the more he engages with samsāris (worldly people) \[in his arcā form\].
- *tiṟam anṟi* – Anything which is not his prakāram (form).
- *deyvam maṟṟillai* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is not discarding/rejecting the existence of dēvatās; since he desires to see emperumān’s vibhūti (wealth/opulence) \[which the dēvatās are also part of\]; he is simply rejecting their independence \[and establishing that they are all dependent on [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)\]. There is no dēvatā which is fully independent and exists for its own self. If you consider them to be his prakāram (form) and surrender, that will imply that you are surrendered unto him; but if you consider them to be independent and surrender unto them, there is nothing purposeful in that; “*nēhanānāsti*” (there is nothing independently existing) etc.
- *pēsuminē* – I said “there is no dēvatā who is independently existing without being his prakāram”; if there is anyone who is capable of saying “there is a dēvatā who is having as his prakāram, such emperumān who is not ruled over by anyone and who controls everyone,”, then they can come and tell that in front of me.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.10.4. Pesa ninra

*pēsa ninṟa sivanukkum piraman tanakkum piṟarkkum nāyagan avanē kabāla nan mōkkattuk kaṇḍu koṇmin tēsamāmadiḷ sūḻndaḻagāya tirukkurugūr adanuḷ īsan pāl ōr avam paṟaidal ennāvadu ilingiyarkkē*

**Пословный перевод:**

pēsa ninṟa – spoken (through fake pramāṇams and arguments, doubting (misunderstanding) to be the īśvara); sivanukkum – for rudra; piraman tanakkum – for brahmā (who is the creator of such rudra and who is with the vast world which was created by him); piṟarkkum – for the other dēvatās (who follow the orders of such brahmā and rudra); nāyagan – the lord; avanē – sarvēśvaran only (who is revealed through the faultless vēdānta); kabālam – the skull (which became the begging bowl in the hands of rudra after severing the head of brahmā); nal – well (to break into thousand pieces); mōkkattu – in mahābhāratam (which is known as fifth vēdam, and is having documented) this elimination; kaṇḍu koṇmin – please see for yourself; tēsam – being radiant; mā – very great; madiḷ – fort; sūḻndu – surrounded by; aḻagāya – being beautiful due to that; tirukkurugūr adanuḷ – inside tirunagari; īsanpāl – towards the natural sarvēśvaran (who clearly manifests such elimination of kapālam from rudra’s hand); ōr avam – any lowly aspects such as his not being the lord; paṟaidal – committing \[speaking\]; ilingiyarkku – for those ānumānikas who consider linga puraṇam etc as the pramāṇam (as authentic source of knowledge); ennāvadu – what is the benefit?

**Перевод:**

**sarvēśvaran (śrīman nārāyaṇan) is the only lord for rudra who is spoken \[as lord in some statements\], brahmā and other dēvatās; please see for yourself as revealed in mahābhāratam, how the skull was eliminated from rudra’s hands; what is the benefit for those ānumānikas who consider linga puraṇam etc as the pramāṇam, while committing \[speaking\] any lowly aspects (talks) such as sarvēśvaran not being the lord, towards emperumān who is the natural lord and who is residing inside tirunagari which is beautiful due its radiance and being surrounded by very great fort.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In fourth pāsuram, opposing āḻvār, vyōmātīta, naiyāyika, vaiśēśika etc philosophers come and say “the universe which has avayava (parts) is an effect, and since it is an effect, there must be a creator, and when we look into the upaniśats to find out who this creator is, it uses the terms ‘īśa‘ and ‘īśāna‘ to identify that creator; based on this, and previously explained inference and the supporting evidences for this, rudra tatvam (the principle of Siva/rudra) is supreme”. When a person (brahmā) was still alive, he got his head severed; another person (rudra – the one who cut the head) become affected with the kapāla (skull) attached in his hand and sustained by begging for alms; sarvēśvaran out of his compassion gave kapāla mōkśam (freed rudra from the affect of having the kapāla attached to his hand) and protected rudra – identifying this famous incident from itihāsams and purāṇams and showing the statements which say that the meaning of akāram is explained to be sarvēśvara, and further āḻvār is saying that in front of this evidence from śruti (vēdam), these weak arguments will not stand, and rejects the kudruśtis (misinterpreters of vēdam) and establishes that emperumān is sarvēśvaran through upaniśats.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār asks “What is the benefit for those naiyāiyika et al (who determine īśvara by inference) for rejecting the supreme nature of sarvēśvaran who is revealed by the faultless vēdam and who is the lord of the dēvatāntarams (other dēvatās) that are confused to be supreme?*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. pēsa ninṟa sivanukkum piraman tanakkum piṟarkkum nāyagan avanē kabāla nan mōkkattuk kaṇḍu koṇmin tēsamāmadiḷ sūḻndaḻagāya tirukkurugūr adanuḷ īsan pāl ōr avam paṟaidal ennāvadu ilingiyarkkē*

- *pēsa ninṟa sivanukkum* – They say “if you cite śruti (vēdam), we will do that as well”; that is – if I explain that [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s supremacy is revealed by nārāyaṇa anuvākam (puruśa sūktam, nārāyaṇa sūktam etc), you will also cite certain tāmasa (mode of ignorance) purāṇams and other arguments and help rudra stand his ground; also explained as – rudra who is spoken as supreme by you. That principle will not stand – it can only be supported \[temporarily\] to speak in this manner. Unlike other dēvatās, this rudra has the greatness to be called as “īśvara” (supreme).
- *piraman tanakkum* – for brahmā who is the creator of rudra; it is explained in sāma vēdam “*brahmaṇa:putrāya jyēśtāya śrēśtāya*” (rudra who attained fame by being born as brahmā’s first son) and “*brahmaṇaścābhisambhūtaśśiva:*” (Siva was born as brahmā’s son). rudra’s īśvaratvam (supremacy) is acquired by the mercy of [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) as said in māhābhāratam rāja darmam “*mahādēvas sarvamētē mahātmā hūtvātmānam dēvadēvōbabhūva*” (The great soul Siva offered his own self in the sarvamēta hōma, and became dēva dēva).
- *piṟarkkum* – In [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s divine heart, there is no difference between brahmā, rudra and other dēvatās. They too think along the same lines as brahmā said to rudra “*tavāntarātmā mama ca yē ca anyē dēhisamjitā:*” (viṣṇu is the antaryāmi \[in-dwelling soul\] for you and I; whoever is having body, that viṣṇu remains the witness \[by being the antaryāmi\]).
- *pēsa ninṟa sivanukkum piraman tanakkum nāyagan avanē* – Even if one can can imagine a reason for such supremacy, empermān is the only lord. This is because of the well established fact in śruti (vēdam). [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is thinking about nārāyaṇa anuvākam, which cannot be attributed to any other dēvatā and being known as the popular meaning of akāram (the first syllable in praṇavam) which is explained in nārāyaṇa anuvākam as “*ya: parassa mahēśvara:*“.

When asked “Why are you saying ‘*avanē*‘ ([emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) only)? At times, rudra is also explained as equal for emperumān – what do you say for that?”,

- *kabāla nal mōkkattuk kaṇḍu koṇmin* – saying this, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is showing it explicitly \[catching rudra red-handed with the kapāla mōkśam incident\]. If you claim supremacy for rudra, we have a counter argument to reject such claim. mātsa purāṇam “*tatra nārāyaṇa:śrīmān mayā bhikśām prayācita:*” (There, nārāyaṇa who was accompanied by śrīmahālakśmi, was begged by me) – rudra says “[śrī mahālakśmi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/) who is said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 116.45 ‘*na kaścin nāparādyati*‘ (who does not commit mistakes), who makes [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) give up his independence of his saying ‘whatever deeds they have done, they have to reap the results; what can I do?’, was also with him”. mātsa purāṇam ślōkam continuation “*viṣṇu prasādāt suśrōṇi kapālam sahasradā \| sputitam bahudāyā tam svapna labdam danam yatā*” (He then scrapped his skin with his nail, picked up some blood from there and sprinkled that on the skull which was attached to my hand. Oh pārvati! By the mercy of viṣṇu, that skull broke in to thousand pieces and disappeared like wealth which was acquired in a dream). *suśrōṇi* – The fortune I got from your beauty helped me while approaching [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) \[It is generally said that, if the wife is beautiful, it brings fortune to the husband\]. *svapna labdam* – while one was experiencing in the dream, the whole experience suddenly stopped when woken up; that is why, it is said “*nal mōkkam*” (distinguished freedom/liberation from the suffering of having the skull attached to the hand). [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying “I have this to counter argue your claim” or he is saying his supremacy too disappeared as the wealth acquired in dream will disappear on waking up. This is the state of those who are considered as īśvara (supreme lord) by you all; one person (brahmā) lost his head; another person (rudra) had skull attached to his hand and was atoning for his sin. Like a boat with a hole trying to rescue a boat with a crack, should you who are having some shortcoming, surrender to those who are having bigger shortcoming than you? After yourself saying “being an offender, he roamed around begging”, now you are claiming supremacy for him. One dēvatā’s (brahmā) īśvaratvam (supremacy) was lost with his head; now āḻvār is highlighting the lack of īśvaratvam in another dēvatā (rudra) by showing his hand.
- *kaṇḍu koḷmin* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying “instead of blabbering in front of me, why don’t you check the grantams (books) which were written by your own people and are available in your own house?”.
- *tēsamā madiḷ …* – The fort that is having tējas (radiance/strength) to be not overcome by enemies, having fort which is a protective layer, and is beautiful.
- *tirukkurugūr adanuḷ īsanpāl* – As [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) never leaves \[anyone\], even in his saulabhyam (simplicity in arcā form), he retains that supremacy.
- *īsan pāl* – towards such sarvēśvara who is said in “*ya:parassa mahēśvara:*“. Speaking about the meaning of the word nārāyaṇa first, since it says the one who is indicated by “*akāram*” and who is supreme is indicated by the word “mahēśvara”, it is established in vēdam that nārāyaṇa is only indicated by the word mahēśvara; since this is established in śruti, your \[the other person debating\] inference becomes void; [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying that the effect “*kaṇḍu koḷmin*” will easily overcome any contrary principles; thus, śrīman nārāyaṇan alone is supreme.
- *ōr avam paṟaidal* – Comparing other kśētrajña ([jīvātmās – souls](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)) with [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) and presenting some arguments which nullifies his supremacy. As āḻvār does not want to say it, he simply says “*avam*” (fault).
- *paṟaidal* – If at all, such discussions can be done only secretly in privacy and not to be discussed in public. “*yatā mē śirasaścēdādam kurutaram vaca:*” (you have made a statement which is worse than severing my head); mahābali said to śrī prahlādāḻvān (bali’s grand father) “the lustre is reducing in the kingdom and my strength is diminishing; what is the reason for this?” and prahlādāḻvān says “it is due to the offenses you committed against [sarvēśvara](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)“; mahābali then says “*kōyam viṣṇu*” (who is that viṣṇu?) and other disrespectful words; hearing that prahlādāḻvān tells him “\[instead of speaking like this\] if you cut my head and give it to me, I will say ‘this is the favour done by my grand son’ ” and then curses mahābali saying “you have insulted bhagavān in front of me; so you shall lose your kingdom”. When [bhattar](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/09/11/parasara-bhattar/) mercifully explained this, he was asked “Why did prahlādāḻvān who very well knows the difference between [prakruti (matter)](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/09/thathva-thrayam-achith-what-is-matter/) and [puruśa (soul)](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/), curse him with respect to the body and not with respect to the soul?”. [bhattar](https://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/2012/09/11/parasara-bhattar/) mercifully explains “When you punish a dog, you have to take away the dirty thing it likes since taking away some sandalwood paste does not affect the dog in any way; similarly, mahābali was attached to his wealth/opulence; so prahlādāḻvān curses mahābali in that aspect”.
- *ennāvadu ilingiyarkkē* –  What is the benefit of those ānumānikas (followers of Siva)? [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says “Did you bring any greatness to that dēvatā? Did you get any result for surrendering unto him? Did you at least acquire any greatness by doing this?”.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.10.5. Ilingattitta

*ilingattitta purāṇattīrum samaṇarum sākkiyarum valindu vādu seyvīrgaḷum maṟṟu num deyvamum āgi ninṟān malindu sen nel kavari vīsum tirukkurugūr adanuḷ polindu ninṟa pirān kaṇḍīr onṟum poy illai pōṟṟuminē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ilingattu itta – that which highlights worship of lingam; purāṇattīrum – you who are kudruśtis due to being faithful to tāmasa (mode of ignorance) purāṇams; samaṇarum – jainas (who are faithful to texts which are outside vēdam); sākkiyarum – bauddas; valindu – through dry arguments; vādu seyvīrgaḷum – you vaiśēśikas, who are debating; maṟṟum – further; num – those you have considered as goal; deyvamum – the different dēvatās; āgi – promoting them to be at his (emperumān‘s) disposal; ninṟān – stood; sen nel – fresh paddy; malindu – abundantly available; kavari vīsum – due to the rich crops, swaying like a cāmara (a fan made with fur); tirukkurugūr – in tirunagari; polindu ninṟa – standing with completeness (where his qualities of paratvam (supremacy) and śeelam (simplicity), saulabhyam (easy approacability) etc shine well); pirān kaṇḍīr – see the sarvēśvaran himself; onṟum – any; poy illai – no falsity; pōṟṟumin – (thus, giving up your bāhya and kudruśti aspects) and praise him

**Перевод:**

**Oh you who are kudruśtis due to being faithful to tāmasa (mode of ignorance) purāṇams! Oh jainas! Oh bauddas! Oh you vaiśēśikas, who are debating through dry arguments! emperumān is promoting those different dēvatās, you have considered as goal, to be at his (emperumān‘s) disposal and standing in tirunagari where fresh paddy is available abundantly and the crops are appearing to be swaying like a cāmara (a fan made with fur) with completeness, is sarvēśvaran himself; there is no falsity in this principle and thus you all praise him.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In fifth pāsuram, āḻvār says “All of you who are faithful to linga purāṇam, and your dēvatās are pervaded by nārāyaṇa; this being the case, all of you surrender unto him”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, rejecting bāhya (those who reject vēdam) and kudruśtis (those who misinterpret vēdam0, āḻvār says “emperumān who resides in tirunagari is superior to all”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Fifth pāsuram. āḻvār rejects those who bring kudruśti smrutis (the texts which misinterpret vēdam) such as linga purāṇam and bāhya smrutis (the texts which reject vēdam) as authentic texts. ilingattitta purāṇattīrum samaṇarum sākkiyarum valindu vādu seyvīrgaḷum maṟṟu num deyvamum āgi ninṟān malindu sen nel kavari vīsum tirukkurugūr adanuḷ polindu ninṟa pirān kaṇḍīr onṟum poy illai pōṟṟuminē*

- *ilingattitta purāṇattīrum* – This is the difference between sātvika purāṇam and rājasa/tāmasa purāṇam \[that is, sātvika purāṇams speaks the truth of viṣṇu’s supremacy as it is; other purāṇams exaggerate the greatness of a particular dēvatā\]. The crux of the purāṇam can be observed right at the beginning of the purāṇam; \[in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam\] as a general question is posed as in “*yanmayam jagat brahman*” (Oh best among brāhmaṇas! who is pervading this universe as antarātmā? From where did these universe appear? In where did they become subdued during deluge? and so on) and the answer is given specifically and naturally as in “*viṣṇōs sakāśāt udbhūtam*” (Everything appeared from viṣṇu, everything goes back to viṣṇu, that viṣṇu is the one who bestows birth and death; and he is the antaryāmi of everything); unlike this, in the rājasa/tāmasa purāṇams, both the speaker and the listener being filled with tamō guṇam, this purāṇam was written specifically to glorify lingam. This purāṇam is like the praising of a poet who obliges when requested to praise “a dirty eyed person to be a lotus eyed person” and when requested to sing “an buffalo as an elephant”; they are praised falsely just for the sake of praising without them having any such greatness; these praise would neither bring glory to the entity which lacks glorification nor will it reduce the glory of the truly glorious entity.
- *samaṇarum* – ārhata (jaina)
- *sākkiyarum* – baudda
- *maṟṟum valindu vādu seyvīrgaḷum* – Those remaining bāhyas (those who reject vēdam), who try to establish their principles using dry/vague arguments instead of arguments based on the top most pramāṇams (authentic texts). As said in manu dharma śāstram “*yā vēda bāhyās smrutaya:*” (Those texts which are outside vēdam and those texts which misinterpret vēdam – they are useless for this life and the after life; they are filled with ignorance); ignorance is part of everything \[outside vēda śāstram\]; that is why bāhyas and kudruśtis are treated at par.
- *num deyvamum āgi ninṟān* – He is the ātmā of both you all and the dēvatās you worship. When you glorify them, you should do that recognizing bhagavān’s supremacy. This is because, their nature, existence etc are at his full disposal. Now, in every sect, they will glorify their own leader/prime as “sarvajña” (omniscient), “īsvara” (lord) etc. . When it is said “their nature, existence etc are at his full disposal”, is this based on our own philosophy or their philosophy? it is neither one’s philosophy – but it is said based on pramāṇam (authentic sacred texts). When some one observed superhuman attributes in a dēvatā (rudra destroying the three towns) and was asked “what is the reason for his super human abilities?”, it was said in mahābhāratam karṇa parvam “*viṣṇurātmā bhagavatō bhavasya*” (viṣṇu is the antaryāmi of rudra who is very radiant and vorśippable); In atarva śiras, as rudra started explaining his own supremacy like [sarvēśvaran](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) would do, he was asked “how are you saying this?” and he said in atarva śikhā “*sa: antarātantaramprāviśat*” (I am speaking like this because paramātmā is inside me); prahlādāḻvān said “*mattassarvam aham sarvam*” (Everything comes from me; everything rests back in me; I am everything); only when prahlāda has supremacy, these dēvatās would also have that \[obviously, prahlādāḻvān is a devoted servitor of [śrīman nārāyaṇa](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)\].
- *malindu …* – Such [sarvēśvaran](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) who is the antarātmā of all, arrived and presented himself in āḻvārtirunagari to eliminate the question of “he is not present here”. Only due to his arrival here, without any differentiation between cētana (sentient) and acētana (insentient), everyone/everything could serve him as performed by iḷaiyaperumāḷ (lakśmaṇa) as sumitra said in śrī rāmāyaṇam 40.5 “you were given birth to serve śrī rāma in the forest” \[here both humans as well as the crops are said to be serving [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) – that is what is said by [cētana](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) and [acētana](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/09/thathva-thrayam-achith-what-is-matter/)\]. When the fresh paddy crops sway, it appears as if they are performing the fanning kainkaryam to [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/).
- *polindu ninṟa pirān kaṇḍīr* – When he descends in to samsāram giving up paramapadam, instead of suffering like them, his glories based on his svarūpam (true nature), rūpam (form), guṇam (qualities) and vibhavam (activities) shine greatly. Whatever praises done by anyone, his glories are beyond those praises.
- *onṟum poy illai* – As all the praises done for other dēvatās will remain false, there is no falsity in the praises done for [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/). As the other dēvatās don’t have any natural greatness, there is no truth in the praises done towards them; and as there is no limit to the greatness of emperumān, there is no room for falsity in his case.
- *pōṟṟuminē* – It is my great mercy towards you which makes me request you to praise him while you don’t desire for this; such mercy should fructify; instead of saying “it will happen over time” just try to surrender unto him immediately.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.10.6. Porri marror

*pōṟṟi maṟṟōr deyvam pēṇap puṟattittu ummai innē tēṟṟi vaittadu elleerum vīdu peṟṟāl ulagillai enṟē sēṟṟil sennel kamalam ōngu tirukkurugūr adanuḷ āṟṟa vallavan māyam kaṇḍīr adaṟindaṟindōduminē*

**Пословный перевод:**

maṟṟu ōr – another; deyvam – dēvatā; pōṟṟi – praise; pēṇa – to serve/support; puṟattittu – keeping away (from him); ummai – you all (who are attached to those dēvatās); innē – in this manner (like I am faithful towards emperumān, you are faithful towards those dēvatās); tēṟṟi vaittadu – made you remain faithful (in those dēvatās); elleerum – everyone; vīdu peṟṟāl – if attained mōkśam (liberation) of serving bhagavān; ulagu – the injunctions/order of the world (where it is said that “emperumān will conduct the world based on the individual’s karma giving them the apt results); illai – will be lost; enṟē – will remain like that; sēṟṟil – in marshes; sennel – fresh paddy; kamalam – lotus; ōngu – grow nicely; tirukkurugūr adanuḷ – residing in āḻvārtirunagari; āṟṟavallavan – the one being greatly capable and making others enjoy the results of their deeds, his; māyam kaṇḍīr – being related to prakruti (material realm) which is said as “māyā” (which is part of his sport and is difficult to cross over); adu – that; aṟindu aṟindu – having knowledge about it (the process of prapatti (surrender) which helps cross over the material realm); ōdumin – try to cross over (that material realm)

**Перевод:**

**The reason for keeping you all away from him to praise and serve another dēvatā in this manner and made you remain faithful towards them is, if everyone attained mōkśam (liberation) of serving bhagavān, the injunctions/order of the world will be lost. The reason for this is – emperumān who is residing in āḻvārtirunagari where fresh paddy and lotus flowers grow nicely in marshes, who is greatly capable and making others enjoy the results of their deeds – such emperumān’s relation with prakruti (material realm) which is said as “māyā” ; having knowledge about it, try to cross over the material realm.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In sixth pāsuram, āḻvār was asked “If emperumān is the supreme lord, why did he make us to be devoted towards dēvatāntarams (other dēvatās)?” and he replies “This is done to not let the injunctions of śāstram which indicates ‘all the creatures who are engaged in good/bad deeds to reap the results according to their deeds’, fail; knowing this, you all escape his deception”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “It is emperumān’s skill which makes you not realize how he manages the material realm based on one’s karma (deeds)”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Sixth pāsuram. When asked “We have good clarity about bhagavān’s supremacy when you mercifully explain the same and at other times we have great desire towards other dēvatās; what is the reason for this?”, āḻvār replies “that is due to your own sins”. Also, see nanjīyar‘s introduction. pōṟṟi maṟṟōr deyvam pēṇap puṟattittu ummai innē tēṟṟi vaittadu elleerum vīdu peṟṟāl ulagillai enṟē sēṟṟil sennel kamalam ōngu tirukkurugūr adanuḷ āṟṟa vallavan māyam kaṇḍīr adaṟindaṟindōduminē*

- *pōṟṟi* – Whatever I am doing towards bhagavān, you are doing the same towards other dēvatās; there is no fault in your side; it is just that your object of worship is unsuitable \[to be vorśipped\].
- *maṟṟōr deyvam* – As said in śrī bhagavat gītā 9.23 “*yē pi anya dēvatā bhaktā:*” (even those who worship other dēvatās, are vorśipping me but in a wrong way).
- *pēṇa* – Since they do not have any specific greatness, it is your responsibility to bring about some glories for them.
- *puṟattittu* – Keeping away from emperumān himself.
- *ummai innē tēṟṟi vaittadu* – The way he managed to keep you with clear knowledge \[in whatever you were doing\].  As I remain free and fearless for the future disasters as said in taittirīya upaniśat “*nabibheti kutaścana*” (He will not fear anywhere), he made you surrender unto other dēvatās who are like boats with holes and cracks \[which cannot even save themselves\] and remain faithful and attached towards them.
- *elleerum* … – If the whole residents of the material realm become liberated, śāstram which is meant for leelā (sport) will become useless. The world has people who engage in virtuous deeds and people who engage in sinful deeds; when those who performed pious and sinful deeds reap the results of their deeds, the injunctions/order of śāstram as said in “*puṇya:puṇyēkarmaṇā – pāpa:pāpēna*” (those who engage in pious deeds become pious and those who engage in sinful deeds become sinful), will become nullified. \[Citing a pramāṇam where the word “lōka” indicates śāstram\] In bhagavat gītā 15.14 “*atōsmi lōkē vēdēcapratita: puruśōttama:*” (I am famously known in śruti \[vēda\] and smruti \[lōka\] as puruśōttama), lōka is explained as pramāṇam (smruti) \[and not world or the residents of the world\]. Similarly here too lōka indicates śāstram.
- *sēṟṟil* … – The objects of this sacred town are competent to each other \[in their glories\]. As explained in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 4.8 “*uram peṟṟa malark kamalam*” (The distinct lotus flower) etc, every object will touch each other and grow together.
- *āṟṟa vallavan* – emperumān who is capable of making those who engaged in virtuous deeds and sinful deeds to enjoy the results of those deeds respectively.
- *māyam kaṇḍīr* – You see how he is deceiving and keeping the ones whom he does not want to accept, away from in this prakruti (material realm) as said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 7.14](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/7-14/) “*mama māyā duratyayā*” (my material realm is very difficult to cross over).
- *adu aṟindu* – Knowing that it is his māyā (amazing ability).
- *aṟindu ōduminē* – As said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 7.14](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/7-14/) “*māmēvaya prapadyantē māyām ētām taranti tē*” (Those who surrender unto me, cross over this material realm), he himself mercifully explained the path of surrender to cross over; knowing that path/means, try to escape from this material realm by surrendering unto him. This material realm being a creation of him, instead of trying to win over him by keeping away from him, try to hold on to his divine feet and escape from here.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.10.7. Odi odi

*ōdi ōdip pala piṟappum piṟandu maṟṟōr devam pādi ādip paṇindu pal padigāl vaḻi ēṟik kaṇḍīr kūdi vānavar ētta ninṟa tirukkurugūr adanuḷ ādu putkodi ādi mūrttikku adimai puguvaduvē*

**Пословный перевод:**

maṟṟu ōr deyvam – another dēvatā who cannot be named; pādi ādi – singing and dancing (being devoted towards that dēvatā); paṇindu – worship; pal padigāl – in many different ways; vaḻi – through the śāstram (which instructs one to surrender); ēṟi – taking shelter of that dēvatā more and more; ōdi ōdi – (as a result, in garbha (womb), naraka (hell) etc which are results of such activities) running/moving around; pala piṟappum piṟandu – taking different births; kaṇḍīr – you have seen in front of you; vānavar – all those dēvatās (whom you are surrendered to); kūdi – together; ētta – to be praised and to be surrendered unto (to be relieved of their dangers); tirukkurugūr adanuḷ – in āḻvārtirunagari; ninṟa – one who is standing; ādu – swaying (due to devotion towards bhagavān); puḷ – periya tiruvadi (garudāḻvār); kodi – having as his flag (which highlights his supremacy); ādi mūrttikku – for the sarvēśvara, who is the cause of all; adimai puguvadu – become his servitor

**Перевод:**

**Singing and dancing another dēvatā who cannot be named, vorśipping him in many different ways, taking shelter of him more and more through the śāstram, running/moving around taking different births, and seen all these in front of you. You become the servitor of sarvēśvara, who is the cause of all, who is having the swaying garuda as his flag, and is standing in āḻvārtirunagari, to be praised and to be surrendered unto, by all those dēvatās together.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In seventh pāsuram, when asked “Shall we pursue other dēvatās to acquire certain unseen benefits?”, āḻvār replies “You will only get whatever you have already got praying un to them; hence, give up those aspects and surrender unto polindu ninṟa pirān”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “You will only get whatever you have already got from those dēvatās; hence, you become a servitor of emperumān who is the cause of all and who is having garuda dvajam (flag)”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Seventh pāsuram. Those who heard āḻvār in previous pāsuram said “Alright. We will do that \[surrender unto emperumān\]. But considering ‘these other dēvatās too have some greatness, we have served them; to not waste such efforts and we will wait for those efforts to fructify and finally we will surrender unto empeurumān” and āḻvār says “You have already seen the results of vorśipping those dēvatās; now you do what is required”. ōdi ōdip pala piṟappum piṟandu maṟṟōr devam pādi ādip paṇindu pal padigāl vaḻi ēṟik kaṇḍīr kūdi vānavar ētta ninṟa tirukkurugūr adanuḷ ādu putkodi ādi mūrttikku adimai puguvaduvē*

- *ōdi ōdi* … – As said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 9.21](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/9-21/) “*gatāgatam kāmakāmā labhantē*” (having desires in the desirable svargam etc (which are mentioned in them), they attain (the insignificant, temporary) svargam etc and again and again return \[to the material world\]), they roamed around in this samsāram assuming many births.
- *pala piṟappum piṟandu* – ātmā is eternal; acit is also eternal; the connection with acit \[for ātmā\] is also eternal, and through the continuous flow of karma, one assumes different types of births; without knowing the past and future, you are thinking “this is the only birth/life I have”.
- *maṟṟu ōr …* – In this countless births, in every birth, you have vorśipped other dēvatās. While doing so, you were engaged with all your three faculties – mind, speech and body, yet due to the shortcoming of the dēvatā, you did not get the real benefit – there is nothing surprising in it \[since they cannot bestow the real benefit\]. You were deeply engaged in those dēvatās as ordered in his matters by bhagavān in śrī bhagavat gītā 9.34 “*mām namaskuru*” (worship me).
- *pal padi kāl* – Did you just worship those dēvatās in one particular way? No, you engaged in their worship in several ways.
- *vaḻi ēṟik kaṇḍīr* – Have you yourself not seen the result of vorśipping those dēvatās as explained in śāstram? For “*palpadikāl vaḻiyēṟikkaṇḍīr*“, how did āḻvār know that they have not surrendered to bhagavān in any of their births? On seeing their current state where āḻvār had to instruct them in this way, it is obvious that they did not surrender to bhagavān previously. As said in brahmāṇḍa purāṇam “*mōkśam iccēt janārdanāt*” (those who desire mōkśam should approach janārdana (śrīman nārāyaṇa), had they surrendered to bhagavān, they would have become mukta (liberated soul). Since you had surrendered to other dēvatās, you are toiling in this samsāram. mahābhāratam mōkśa darmam 169.35 “*brahmāṇam śitikaṇṭam ca yācca anyā: dēvatā: smrutā: \| pratibuddā na sēvantē yasmāt parimitam palam \|\|*” (Those who are desirous of liberation will not worship brahmā, Siva and other dēvatās who are highlighted in smrutis), those who are desirous of mōkśam, will not follow inferior dēvatās; this is because – they can only give temporary results. It is said that “*skanda rudra mahēndrādyā: pratiśiddāstu pūjanē*” (vorśipping of dēvatās such as skanda, Siva, indra is forbidden). vaiṣṇava darmam “*tvayābiprāptam …*“. ambarīśa was meditating upon bhagavān. sarvēśvaran wanted to know his faith; he assumed the form of indra and arrived in front of ambarīśa on the airāvata elephant and asked “What do you desire for?”; ambarīśa said “Who are you, who have appeared on a worm \[indicating the elephant as worm, due to his disregard for the same\]?”. As emperumān assumed this form of indra, ambarīśa did not realize that it was emperumān himself appearing in this form of indra along with his garuda in the form of airāvata. ambarīśa spoke “I am performing this penance to see whoever you have taken shelter to acquire this wealth; I am not of the nature of vorśipping and serving strangers; so you can leave now my lord; my salutations to you”. [tirumaḻisai āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/thirumazhisai-azhwar/), a great devotee of śrīman nārāyaṇa was once stitching his cloth. At that time, rudra and pārvati were passing by on the aerial route. tirumaḻisai āḻvār did not care for their passing by; pārvati became offended and told rudra “While you are greater than all, this person is disregarding you \[and thus disrespecting you\]”. rudra said “He appears to be a devotee of bhagavān” and both said “Let us find out who he is” and approached him. rudra asked “What is this? Humans when seeing the dēvas (celestial beings), will worship them and ask for boons; on the other hand, you, on seeing us, have not respectfully folded your stretched legs, and did not render any service and did not ask for any boons”. tirumaḻisai āḻvārs said “Alright. Can you give mōkśam?”. rudra replied “I have no capacity to give that. That can only be accomplished by the mercy of bhagavān by surrendering unto him”. āḻvār further asked “In that case, can you postpone the death of a person who is suppose to die today?”, rudra replied “That is also not possible for me to do since it is based on one’s karma (puṇya and pāpa)”. āḻvār sarcastically said “That being the case, can you mercifully make the thread go through the path of the needle?”. rudra became very angry and opened his third eye on his forehead and āḻvār showed many eyes on his foot in response \[which made rudra and pārvati understand the greatness of āḻvār and they respectfully left that place after apologising to āḻvār\].
- *kūdi* … – Those dēvatās whom you have surrendered unto, will accept your worship and then they will go and worship emperumān. At least, by seeing their acts, you surrender unto emperumān; irrespective of the one who severed the head (rudra) and the one who lost the head (brahmā), as village heads who have great enmity with each other, yet have common danger, all of those dēvatās will surrender unto bhagavān only. Though they have mutual enmity, they will come together when it comes to vorśipping emperumān.
- *ādu puḷ kodi* – Victorious garuda flag. ādu – victory. One who has victorious garuda as/in his flag. Also explained as – the bird (garuda) who is swaying/dancing out of joy of being the vehicle of sarvēśvaran. To destroy the enemies of devotees, one need not hurt sarvēśvaran; emperumān just need to remain on the shoulders of tiruvadi (garudāḻvār). One who is known as “garudadvaja”, “garudavāhana” is mōkśaprada (one who can bestow mōkśam).
- *ādi mūrttikku* – As said in cāndōjña upaniśat “*kāraṇam tu dyēya:*” (meditating upon the one who is the cause of everything). jagatkāraṇavastu (one who is the cause of universe) is the one who is to be meditated upon and vorśipped. sarvēśvaran who is the one who can bestow mōkśam and one who controls everyone.
- *adimai puguvaduvē* – It is the duty of each ātmā to serve bhagavān. You need not do anything \[additional\]; all you need to do is offer his belongings \[our self, body etc\] to him. While he considers us as “my belongings”, instead of you considering these to be “my belongings”, you should accept that these are “his belongings”. “*adimai puguvadu*” is an order/rule to follow, and “*kaṇḍīr*” indicates that you have seen the result of surrendering to other dēvatās; so, āḻvār says “now you try surrendering unto bhagavān”. When bhattar explained yayāti caritram \[yayāti being a very pious king ascends to svarga to share the throne with indra and he was tricked by indra to fall from that position\], piḷḷai viḻupparaiyar and āppān tiruvaḻundūr araiyar asked “Which concept of vēdam and its elaboration, is explained in this incident?”. bhattar mercifully explained “Inferior dēvatās, even when someone prays to them and achieves some greatness, they cannot tolerate that and only sarvēśvaran considers ‘the greatness achieved by others is as good as greatness of himself’ and hence, this incident explains that the other dēvatās are not be surrendered unto  and only sarvēśvaran is to be surrendered unto”. As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam bāla kāṇḍam 31.4 “*imausma*” (śrī rāma to viśvāmitra – we are available to execute your orders), only emperumān can assume very humble position. \[What about yādavas who were surrendered to kriṣṇa and still did not get liberated?\] On hearing that the yādavas \[kriṣṇa’s clan\] killed each other using wild grass, it was asked with fear “there is nothing that kriṣṇa has not done for them; yet, in the end, they killed each other; we think that our surrender to bhagavān also may lead to this end” and \[nampiḷḷai\] mercifully explained “Do not fear; we will not meet with that end; they simply considered kriṣṇa as ‘my friend’, ‘my in-law’ and so on and liked him only due to their bodily relationship with him and so their relationship with him ended with their current lives; but as we are knowledgeable about our true nature and surrender unto bhagavān thinking that we should achieve the real goal, we will achieve the eternal result”.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.10.8. Pukkadimaiyinal

*pukkadimaiyināl tannaik kaṇḍa mārkaṇḍēyan avanai nakka pirānum anṟuyyak koṇḍadu nārāyaṇan aruḷē kokkalar tadam tāḻai vēlit tirukkurugūr adanuḷ mikka ādippirān niṟka maṟṟait teyvam viḷambudirē*

**Пословный перевод:**

adimaiyināl – through servitude; pukku – entered; tannai – self (who is to be surrendered); kaṇḍa – seen in front; mārkaṇḍēyan – known as mārkaṇḍēya; avanai – famous through purāṇams; nakkan – known as nagna (naked) due to being digambara (having the directions as garments); pirānum – benefactor (for helping his devotee defeat death and become immortal); anṟu – during praḷaya (deluge); uyyak koṇḍadu – rescued and made him a devotee of bhagavān for his upliftment; nārāyaṇan – nārāyaṇa (who is the antarātmā); aruḷē – by the mercy (of making rudra to be the benefactor for mārkaṇḍēya); kokku – like the complexion of a crane; alar – blossoming flower; tadam – vast; tāḻai – leaves; vēli – having a protective layer; tirukkurugūr adanul – standing in āḻvārtirunagari; mikka – being greater than all; ādi – natural cause; pirān – great benefactor; niṟka – while standing; e maṟṟu deyvam – which other dēvatā who is with expectation; viḷambudir – speaking?

**Перевод:**

**rudra, the benefactor, who is known as nagna, due to being digambara, during praḷaya, rescued mārkaṇḍēya who is famously known through purāṇams and entered by servitude and seen him in front, and made mārkaṇḍēya a devotee of bhagavān for his upliftment by the mercy of nārāyaṇa; thus, while emperumān who is greater than all, the natural cause and the great benefactor is standing in āḻvārtirunagari which has a protective layer of blossoming flowers with the complexion of a crane \[white colour\] and vast leaves, which other dēvatā who is with expectation, are you speaking about?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In eighth pāsuram, when asked “Did mārkaṇḍēya riśi not pray to rudra and achieved his desire?”, āḻvār says “There, rudra was only doing puruśakāram (recommendation). It was emperumān who mercifully bestowed his desired goal”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār explains “even for other dēvatās, emperumān is the one who gives them the ability to fulfll the desires of those who pray to them”, through the example of rudra fulfilling the desires of mārkaṇḍēya, through the mercy of īśvara (bhagavān).*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Eighth pāsuram. When said “Though these principles are understood, mārkaṇḍēya et al got their desires fulfilled by approaching other dēvatās”, āḻvār says “Would you like to hear, how that happened?”. pukkadimaiyināl tannaik kaṇḍa mārkaṇḍēyan avanai nakka pirānum anṟuyyak koṇḍadu nārāyaṇan aruḷē kokkalar tadam tāḻai vēlit tirukkurugūr adanuḷ mikka ādippirān niṟka maṟṟait teyvam viḷambudirē*

- *pukku adimaiyināl* – Entering with servitude. He did not enter as “the servitor of [sarvēśvara](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)“; but entered as “the servitor of rudra”.
- *tannaik kaṇḍa* – He did not lose anything by not seeing rudra as such.
- *pukku* … – Neither there is loss due to the target of surrender \[rudra\]; nor there is any loss due to not seeing.
- *mārkaṇḍēyan avanai* – one who is known as mārkaṇḍēya.
- *nakka pirān* – nakkan means nagna. He is known as pirān (benefactor) since he helps his followers and since he bestows knowledge. Since “nārāyaṇa” is highlighted subsequently, it is said that rudra pointed mārkaṇḍēya towards [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s divine feet saying “when it comes to being a servitor, there is no distinction between you and me”.
- *uyyak koṇḍadu* – rescued when in danger.
- *nārāyaṇan aruḷē* – rudra said to mārkaṇḍēya “You served me for many days; that should not become useless. I also got this position by surrendering unto emperumān. Now, feeding you means giving you advice on from where you can get food \[i.e., desires fulfilled\] \[when a hungry person knocks on someone’s door and if he does not have food but is caring/courteous, he will direct the hungry person to the house where food is given\]” and lead him to sarvēśvaran. “*aruḷ*” (mercy) should be read as “*aruḷālē*” (by the mercy); also explained as – rudra protected him by making him receive the mercy of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/).
- *kokkalar* … – [āḻvārtirunagari](http://azhwarthirunagari.koyil.org/) which is having flowers which are having the white complexion of crane and the vast leaves as a protective layer. This is the nature of the land \[very pure and vast\].
- *mikka ādip pirān niṟka* – While emperumān who is greater than all and the cause of the universe is standing.
- *mikka* – Glorified greatly but having shortcomings while approached – unlike this. \[Explained further\] After accepting service for a long time, when it is time to bestow the goal, not having to lead to some one else \[like rudra had to do\].
- *maṟṟait teyvam viḷambudirē* – You are highlighting one among the many prakārams (forms) as īśvara \[[bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)\]; oh losers! while nothing which is not his prakāra can even exist, you are highlighting such prakāra as prakāri (substratum – bhagavān) and are looking nonsensical.
- *viḷāmbudirē* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) feels that these dēvatās are not even qualified to be discussed about.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.10.9. Vilambum

*viḷambum āṟu samayamum avai āgiyum maṟṟum tan pāl aḷandu kāṇḍaṟkariyanāgiya ādip pirān amarum vaḷam koḷ taṇ paṇai sūḻndaḻagāya tirukkurugūr adanai uḷam koḷ jñānattu vaimmin ummai uyyak koṇḍu pōguṟilē*

**Пословный перевод:**

viḷambum – being essence just by words (of great debating skills); āṟu samayamum – the six schools of philosophy which reject vēdam (namely cārvāka, śākhya (baudda), kśapaṇaka (jaina), vaiśēśika, śānkhya and pāśupata); maṟṟum – other kudruśti philosophies (which misinterpret vēdam); avai āgiyum – collectively group together; than pāl – in his own matters (where he is beyond limits); aḷandu – determine; kāṇḍaṟku – to see; ariyan āgiya – having nature which is difficult; ādip pirān – great benefactor who is the cause of all; amarum – the abode where he resides well; vaḷam koḷ – attractive; taṇ – invigorating; paṇai – water bodies; sūḻndu – surrounded; aḻagāya – perfectly enjoyable; tirukkurugūr adanai – āḻvārtirunagari; ummai – you; uyyak koṇḍu – to uplift; pōguṟil – if you want; uḷam koḷ jñānattu – in your internal knowledge (of the mind); vaimmin – place it

**Перевод:**

**emperumān, the great benefactor who is the cause of all, who is having the nature where his matters are difficult to see and determine by the collective group of six schools of philosophy which reject vēdam and are being essence just by words \[no real stuff\] and other kudruśti philosophies. If you want to uplift yourself, place āḻvārtirunagari, the perfectly enjoyable abode of such emperumān which is surrounded by attractive and invigorating water bodies, in your internal knowledge.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In ninth pāsuram, āḻvār says “If you want to be saved, take shelter of āḻvārtirunagari which is mercifully occupied by emperumān whose wealth cannot be destroyed by the wrong debates of vēda bāhya (those who reject vēdas) and kudruśtis (those who misinterpret vēdas)”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Ninth pāsuram. āḻvār says “You don’t even need to go to great heights (emperumān) for your upliftment. It is sufficient if you focus your knowledge on tirunagari where he resides”. viḷambum āṟu samayamum avai āgiyum maṟṟum than pāl aḷandu kāṇḍaṟkariyanāgiya ādip pirān amarum vaḷam koḷ taṇ paṇai sūḻndaḻagāya tirukkurugūr adanai uḷam koḷ jñānattu vaimmin ummai uyyak koṇḍu pōguṟilē*

- *viḷambum āṟu samayamum* – The bāhya philosophies (which reject vēdam) which have the essence just in words since they are not based on pramāṇam (vēdam) and are merely sustained by dry arguments countering certain points raised by vēdāntis. [bhāśyakārar (emperumānār)](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/emperumanar/) mercifully explained these as “*śākhya ulūkya akśapāda kśapaṇa kapila patanjali matānusāriṇa:*” (śākhya – baudda, ulūkya – cārvāka, akśapāda – gautama, kśapaṇa – jaina, kapila – sēśvara sānkhya (sānkhya philosophy which accepts īśvara’s existence), patanjali mata – yōga śāstram)).
- *avai āgiyum maṟṟum* – The kudruśti philosophies which are comparable to the bāhya philosophies. “*tamōniśtāhitāssmrutā:*” (those who follow philosophies which reject vēdam and those who follow philosophies which misinterpret vēdam will not qualify for mōkśam. They are situated in tamō (ignorance) guṇam).
- *than pāl* … – In [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s matters, even to say that “he does not exist”, one should understand his nature – but understanding his nature is impossible. That is, for bāhyas and kudruśtis, his svarūpa (nature), rūpa (forms), guṇa (qualities) and vibhava (activities) are unśakeable.
- *ādip pirān* – One cannot say “*mēmātāvandyā*” (my mother is barren) \[[bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) being the cause of everything/everyone, one cannot easily reject his existence/greatness\].
- *aḷandu* … – emperumān, the cause of the universe, who cannot be measured, lovingly resides.
- *vaḷam koḷ* – Having wealth and being surrounded by invigorating water bodies and very attractive [āḻvārtirunagari](http://azhwarthirunagari.koyil.org/).
- *uḷam koḷ jñānattu vaimmin* – uḷam koḷ jñānam – Internal knowledge. Before the knowledge dawns and grasps external aspects through the external senses, make tirunagari the focus of your internal knowledge. Instead of focussing the knowledge in external matters, turn it towards internal aspects \[ātmā and bhagavān who are in the heart\].
- *ummai uyyak koṇḍu pōguṟilē* – As said in taittirīya upaniśat “*santamēnam*” (they know him to be existing), if you want to retain your existence. As said in taittirīya upaniśat “*asannēva*” (he becomes non-existing), [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) thinks these people who reject/misinterpret vēdam, to be non-existing. śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 43.25 “*nēyamasti* … *mahātmanā*” (You manifest enmity with the great śrī rāma and for this the lankā will cease to exist. Neither you or rāvaṇa will survive), as hanuman said “perumāḷ (śrī rāma) is only comparable to himself in his paratva form (in paramapadam) and there is no one else who is comparable to him”.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.
