## 4.10.10. Uruvadavadu

*uṟuvadāvadu ettēvum evvulagangaḷum maṟṟum tanpāl maṟuvil mūrttiyōdu ottu ittanaiyum ninṟa vaṇṇam niṟkavē seṟuvil sennel karumbodōngu tirukkurugūr adanuḷ kuṟiya māṇuruvāgiya nīḷ kudak kūttanukkātceyvadē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ettēvum – all categories of dēvatās; evvulagangaḷum – all worlds; maṟṟum – other cit (sentient beings) and acit (insentient entities); ittanaiyum – all these; than pāl – in his svarūpam; maṟu il – unblamable; mūrttiyōdu ottu – considering them to be distinguished forms as comparable to his divine/special forms; ninṟa vaṇṇam – without losing his identity as well as his characteristics; niṟkavē – while standing; seṟuvil – in fertile lands; sennel – fresh paddy; karumbodu – sugarcane etc; ōngu – growing well; tirukkurugūr adanuḷ – standing in tirukkurugūr; kuṟiya – being vāmana (who can be well enjoyed by the devotees); māṇuruvē – assuming the form of brahmacāri (celibate student, who is having the identity of being needy); nīḷ – having great enjoyability forever (which captivates everyone who hears about him); kudak kūttanukku – to kriṣṇa who performed kudak kūttu \[type of dance with having multiple pots on oneself\]; āḷ seyvadē – to serve; uṟuvadu āvadu – the puruśārtam (goa) that is destiny and apt

**Перевод:**

**emperumān is standing in such a manner that all categories of dēvatās, all worlds, other cit (sentient beings) and acit (insentient entities) and all of these remain in his svarūpam, considering them to be distinguished forms as comparable to his divine/special forms, without losing his identity as well as his characteristics; he is also standing in tirukkurugūr which has fertile lands having well growing fresh paddy, sugarcane etc; to serve such emperumān who having great enjoyability forever as vāmana, assuming the form of brahmacāri and as kriṣṇa who performed kudak kūttu, is the puruśārtam (goal) that is destiny and apt.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In tenth pāsuram, āḻvār says “It is apt to serve polindu ninṟa pirān who has mercifully descended without losing any of his aiśvarya (wealth/control) and standing \[here in āḻvārtirunagari\]”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “It is both destiny and apt to serve emperumān who is the śarīri (soul) of all, very easy to mingle with and is having heart captivating activities”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. uṟuvadāvadu ettēvum evvulagangaḷum maṟṟum tanpāl maṟuvil mūrttiyōdu ottu ittanaiyum ninṟa vaṇṇam niṟkavē seṟuvil sennel karumbodōngu tirukkurugūr adanuḷ kuṟiya māṇuruvāgiya nīḷ kudak kūttanukkātceyvadē*

- *uṟuvadāvadu* … – It is apt to serve the one who performs great kudak kūttu (pot dance). This \[servitude\] is apt, suitable, best and joyful; it can simply mean “this is apt”.
- *ettēvum* … – All the dēvatās and the worlds which are their abodes.
- *maṟṟum* – the remaining [cētanas (sentient beings)](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) and [acētanas (insentient entities)](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/09/thathva-thrayam-achith-what-is-matter/).
- *than pāl maṟuvil mūrttiyōdu ottu* – When they arrive at him, they will be considered as his faultless forms. When they become his forms, they will be as good as his divine/spiritual forms, and remain faultless. *maṟu* – fault; *maṟu il* – not having fault. That is not having the possibility of being separable from him and so on. Another explanation – maṟu – mole – śrīvatsam; the form of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) which is having the śrīvatsa mole; \[these entities when united with emperumān\] will resemble the divine form of emperumān which is having the śrīvatsa mole. Another explanation – there is a form of empeurmān which is opposite to all faults; matching such form. How are they comparable to his śarīram (form)?  This is due to them a) being inseparable b) having ādāra (emperumān being the support) – ādēya (other entities being supported) relationship c) having niyantru (other entities being controlled) – niyāmya (emperumān being the controller) relationship, having śēśa (other entities being servitors) – śēśi (emperumān being lord) relationship, all of which are characteristics of śarīra (body/form) and are present in these entities with respect to [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/). When dēvadatta (an imaginary person) stands on a tree, that tree does not become his body – here it is not like that \[[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is pervading everything, so everything is his form\].
- *ittanaiyum* … – While all of these remain in him as they are. emperumān descending into [āḻvārtirunagari](http://azhwarthirunagari.koyil.org/) having all entities other than himself being servitors in the form of śarīra (body), and without losing any of this wealth/opulence. Since [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is together with ubhaya vibhūti (nitya vibhūti (spiritual realm) and leelā vibhūti (material realm)), he is standing here manifesting all those wealth. A prince, even while wearing a small garment and appears modest, it will manifest his wealth without any shortcoming.
- *seṟuvil* … – In the fertile fields of tirukkurugūr, the fresh paddy crop grows as high as sugarcane crop. In this town, the entities are equally great and have no shortcomings; just like in paramapadam, everyone will have the same greatness.
- *kuṟiya* – Just like a huge land is shortened into a small space, he presented himself in a short form which can be fully absorbed and enjoyed by one’s eyes.
- *māṇuruvāgiya* – He is an expert in begging that he will have the same fresh smiling face whether some one gives alms or not.
- *nīḷ kudak kūttanukku* – Even after performing the kudak kūttu long back, he danced in such a manner that, even those who hear about his dance, will completely be captivated as if they saw it right in front of them and start loving him.
- *āḷ seyvadē* – That kudak kūttu cēśtitam (leelā, activity) will itself engage you in servitude; you just need to oblige.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 4.10.11. Atceydu

*ātceydu āḻip pirānaic cērndavan vaṇ kurugūr nagarān nātkamaḻ magiḻ mālai mārbinan māṟan satakōpan vētkaiyāl sonna pādal āyirattuḷ ippattum vallār mītci inṟi vaikunda mānagar maṟṟadu kai aduvē*

**Пословный перевод:**

āḷ seydu – engaging in service through speech (of parōpadēśam (instructing others)); āḻip pirānai – benefactor who has the divine chakra in his hand (which is enjoyed by his devotees); sērndavan – having attained; vaṇ kurugūr nagarān – being the leader of the distinguished āḻvārtirunagari; nāḷ kamaḻ – having very fresh fragrance; magiḻ mālai – divine magiḻa garland; mārbinan – having on his chest; māṟan – having the family name “māṟan”; satakōpan – āḻvār who is having the divine name “śatakōpa” (due to defeating the bāhyas (those who reject vēdam) and kudruśtis (those who misinterpret vēdam)); vētkaiyāl – out of great desire (in bhagavat viśayam); sonna – mercifully spoke; pādal – in the form of a song; āyirattuḷ – among the thousand pāsurams; ippattum – these 10 pāsurams (which are focussed on instructing others); vallār – those who can recite (along with meditating upon the meanings); kaiyadu – in their hands’ reach; maṟṟu – on top of the recital itself \[which is a greatly joyful result\]; adu – being present in the other side \[of material realm\]; mītci inṟi – with no return; vaikundam – śrīvaikuṇṭam; mānagar – the great abode

**Перевод:**

**āḻvār who is having the divine name “śatakōpa” and the family name “māṟan”, who is having attained emperumān, the benefactor who has the divine chakra in his hand, by  engaging in service through speech,  is the leader of the distinguished āḻvārtirunagari and is having divine and very freshly fragrant magiḻa garland on his chest, out of great desire, mercifully spoke these 10 pāsurams among the thousand pāsurams in the form of a song. Those who can recite them, will have the great abode śrīvaikuṇṭam which is present in the other side, from where there is no return, in their hands’ reach, on top of the recital itself.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the end, āḻvār says “paramapadam is easy to attain for those who learn this decad”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. ātceydu āḻip pirānaic cērndavan vaṇ kurugūr nagarān nātkamaḻ magiḻ mālai mārbinan māṟan satakōpan vētkaiyāl sonna pādal āyirattuḷ ippattum vallār mītci inṟi vaikunda mānagar maṟṟadu kai aduvē*

- *ātceydu āḻippirānaic cērndavan* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) who attained [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) by serving him. He surrendered to sarvēśvaran in the proper manner. That is, as said in śrī viṣṇu darmam “*vicitrā dēhasampattir īśvarāya nivēditum \| pūrvamēva krutā brahman hastapādādisamyutā \|\|*” (Oh brāhmaṇa! To offer oneself and other materials, [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) previously got connected to the amazing body with hands and legs), instead of misusing the faculties bestowed by emperumān, engaging them in the apt matter as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 2.3.4](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/02/thiruvaimozhi-2-3-4-enadhu-aviyul/) “*tanda nī koṇḍākkinai*” (You who created me, accepted me subsequently) and attaining him. The means for accepting the servitude is in emperumān’s hands \[the divine chakra\]. As he \[sudarśana cakkarattāḻvār\] is engaged in servitude, he engaged āḻvār also in servitude.  As the divine chakra is united with emperumān’s hands, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) too united with him.
- *sērnda* – Like a broken ship reaching the shore. ātceygai means rendering service. Service can be of 3 types – mānasa (by mind), vācika (by speech) and kāyika (by body/actions). Among these, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is not the one for mānasa and kāyika kainkaryams. This is because, his nature is as explained in periya tiruvantādi 34 “*kālāḻum nenjaḻiyum kaṇsuḻalum*” (my feet does not remain stable, my heart is melting and my eyes are spinning). So, his service can only be through speech. \[Here is a detailed analysis of the nature of the service done by āḻvār in this decad/pāsuram\] Does it say that āḻvār served by singing tiruvāimoḻi? No. If that is the case, this pāsuram should be in the last decad, that is in “*muniyē nānmuganē*“; or it should have been part of the first pāsuram of tiruvāimoḻi which is the essence of the whole prabandam; or, it should have been part of “*pugaḻu nal oruvan*” decad ([tiruvāimoḻi 3.4](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/08/thiruvaimozhi-3-4-pugazhum/)), where āḻvār performed kainkaryam by speech. Alright, shall we say that āḻvār served by speech by mercifully explaining [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s supremacy after eliminating any doubts of supremacy for other dēvatās? No. That was already done in first pāsuram itself. Shall we say that āḻvār is determining who is supreme and instructing the same to others? No. That was already done in [tiruvāimoḻi 2.2](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/01/thiruvaimozhi-2-2-thinnan/) “*tiṇṇan vīdu*” and [tiruvāimoḻi 2.8](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/05/thiruvaimozhi-2-8-anaivadhu/) “*aṇaivadu aravaṇai mēl*“. Shall we say that this is explaining [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s supremacy in arcāvatāram? No. That was already done in [tiruvāimoḻi 3.6](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/09/thiruvaimozhi-3-6-seyya-thamarai/) “*seyya tāmaraik kaṇṇan*“. Shall we simply say that āḻvār is instructing others? No. That was also already done in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.2](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/04/thiruvaimozhi-1-2-vidumin/) “*vīdu min muṟṟavum*” and many other places. So, what is the scope of this decad “*onṟum dēvum*“? On hearing āḻvār mercifully saying “*tirukkurugūr adanuḷ paran tiṟam anṟip pallulagīr deyvam maṟṟillai pēsuminē*” ([tiruvāimoḻi 4.10.3](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/04/thiruvaimozhi-4-10-3-parandha-dheyvamum/)), that is “polindu ninṟa pirān” is the supreme lord, and seeing what is shown in “*kabāla nan mōkkattuk kaṇḍu koṇmin*” ([tiruvāimoḻi 4.10.4](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/04/thiruvaimozhi-4-10-4-pesa-ninra/)), everyone in this universe was reformed and became śrīvaiṣṇavas; they became reformed to be performed mangaḷāśāsanam by [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/). He dedicates a separate decad “poliga poliga” for such mangaḷāśāsanam. This samsāram which was unable to reform even by sarvēśvara through his incarnations, was reformed by āḻvār’s efforts. So āḻvār is saying “*ātceydu āḻip pirānai cērndvan*” (having attained [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) through his servitude) since by his instructions he has reformed the entire universe so that he need not try to establish who is the supreme anymore \[since everyone accepted his instructions and became śrīvaiṣṇavas already\] as said in tiruvāimoḻi 5.2.4 “*idam koḷ samayattai ellām eduttuk kaḷaivana pōlē tadam kadal paḷḷip perumān tannudaip pūdangaḷē*” (To eliminate all the wrong philosophies, the devotees of the lord who is reclining in milk ocean, are spread everywhere).
- *vaṇ kurugūr nagarān* – The cause for all these auspiciousness is the birth in this divyadēśam.
- *nāḷ kamaḻ magiḻ mālai mārbinan* – In “*naṇṇādār muṟuvalippa*” decad, previously āḻvār’s garland had become dry on seeing the sufferings of the samsāris (worldly people); now – on explaining the supremacy of [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/), and becoming confident that there is no more sufferings for them, the garland became fresh.
- *māṟan satakōpan* – He is the mrutyu (agent of death) for the hurdles in attaining bhagavān.
- *vētkai* … – He is not of the nature, where he is advising those who humbly approached him to learn these; it is out of his desire \[and compassion\], he is mercifully explaining this decad among the thousand pāsurams; for those who are well versed in this decad, the great abode of śrīvaikuṇṭam is within their hands reach and there is no return from there too.
- *maṟṟadu …* – Both śrīvaikuṇṭam and leelā vibhūti are at their disposal. maṟṟu is just an avyaya (no meaning, a word to just fulfil the poetic meter), the return-less paramapadam is within their hands. paramapadam is in their hands completely. Another explanation – the ultimate goal is knowledge about [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/); the abode which matches such knowledge is also easy to attain for them. Another explanation – The great abode of śrīvaikuṇṭam is the other world, which is opposite to this samsāram. That is in their hands.

## Fifth Centum

## 5.1 Kaiyar cakkarattu

## 5.1.1. Kaiyar cakkarattu

*kaiyār cakkarattu en karu māṇikkamē enṟenṟu poyyē kaimmai sollip puṟamē puṟamē ādi meyyē peṟṟoḻindēn vidi vāykkinṟu kāppārār aiyō kaṇṇa pirān aṟaiyō inip pōnālē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kai – with the divine hand; Ar – well fixed; cakkaram – having divine chakra; en karu māṇikkamē – one who made me enjoy your attractive blue gem like divine form!; enṟu enṟu – saying this repeatedly like those who are devoted to higher aspect (bhagavān); poyyē – while that love is absent \[in me\]; kaimmai – (to have even the enemy to believe) saying deceptive words; solli – saying; puṟamē puṟamē – jumping from one thing to another in worldly pleasures; ādi – engaged constantly; meyyē – the benefit attained by those who have great love towards bhagavān; peṟṟu oḻindēn – have attained; vidi – by your mercy (which is being the cause for such benefit, which makes you consider my lie to be truth, and which is indicated by the term “vidi” which makes you bless me even if you do not want to do that); vāykkinṟu – this (when materializing); Ar – who can; kāppār – avert?; kaṇṇan – being very easily approachable; pirān – you who favoured me; ini – after your mercy leading to the benefit; pōnālē – can you withdraw?; aiyō – alas!; aṟaiyō – if you are capable, try to leave me

**Перевод:**

**Simple translation (based on vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar‘s 12000 padi)**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In first pāsuram, āḻvār becomes pleased thinking “While I was very much looking away from emperumān and falsely said those words that are said by those who are attracted by his beauty etc, out of his own mercy, he mercifully bestowed me the benefit which is attained  by his great devotees”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. pāsuram kaiyār cakkarattu en karu māṇikkamē enṟenṟu poyyē kaimmai sollip puṟamē puṟamē ādi meyyē peṟṟoḻindēn vidi vāykkinṟu kāppārār aiyō kaṇṇa pirān aṟaiyō inip pōnālē*

- *kaiyār cakkarattu* – He held up the divine chakra in the divine hand which should be rid of evil eyes even as it is. This acts as both weapon when there is danger and ornament \[otherwise\]. In one hand, it is like an army \[on its own\]. This the cause for the love of favourable persons \[devotees\] towards [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) as said in tiruvāimoḻi 6.9.1 “*kūrār āḻi veṇ sangēndi vārāy*” (Come to us carrying the sharp chakra and white conch), and it is also the one which destroys the enemies.
- *kaiyār cakkarattu en karu māṇikkamē* – “attu” is an extraneous suffix and has no specific meaning. Same can be understood wherever it occurs.
- *en karu māṇikkamē* – After enjoying the beautiful combination of the divine hand and the chakra, he is not able to move on to the divine conch in sequence, yet he fell in love with the beauty of the divine form. He would not crossover the divine form and go to something else. Oh one who fully gave your invigorating, blue gem like invaluable divine form for my enjoyment.
- *enṟu enṟu* – Did I tell this once and leave it? Everything is good in [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s matters. Why is [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) feeling bad for repeating this multiple times? Since he feels that “there is not enough love in it”. āḻvār saying – If I were telling this with true emotions, it is good \[but I was only faking it\].
- *poyyē kaimmai solli* – poy and kaimmai are synonyms for lie. This implies – Not that, I was making others believe what I say, I was able to convince sarvajñan (omniscient lord) himself to make him think that “This is truth”. I did not even speak partial truth and partial lie \[it was pure lie\].
- *puṟamē puṟamē ādi* – Here puṟam (external) means worldly pleasures acquired through śabda (sound) etc. Even after saying that “I don’t have enough love towards bhagavān” and declaring that his love is fake, worldly pleasures seem external to āḻvār; \[it is because\] āḻvār is of the nature in saying in tiruvāimoḻi 6.9.9 “*pāviyēnaip pala nī kāttip paduppāyō*” (will you divert this sinner from you by showing worldly pleasures). As a species is pervading all the forms of that species, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying that his love for worldly pleasures is spread over every aspect of them. If we enquire “which state of his, is he talking about?”, we can either say – as he says past, present and future clearly, he is talking about his past. ōr, it can be said that – as he has acquired full knowledge and devotion towards [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), he considers his love is not matching emperumān’s greatness and saying this.

When asked  “If this is the case, what is the nature of the benefit/result you attained?”, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says,

- *meyyē* – Just as whatever comes from me is false only, whatever comes from him is truth only. There is no shortcoming in the benefit/result.
- *peṟṟu oḻindēn* – Even after reaching paramapadam, I will keep recalling this result.  [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) cannot do anything more than this to me.

When asked “You said that there is no reason, but the result is great; what is the reason for this?”, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says,

- *vidi vāykkinṟu* – If [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s mercy crosses over the boundaries, what can we do? vidi – bhagavān’s mercy. After tiruvāimoḻi 2.8 “*kēsavan tamar*” decad, whenever [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says “vidi”, he means bhagavān’s krupā (mercy). Reason for saying so is – he cannot escape that mercy.
- *vāykkinṟu* – When the flood of bhagavān’s mercy crosses over the dam of his independence.
- *kāppār Ar* – Who can stop that? Why is āḻvār saying “kāppār Ar” instead of saying “kāppadu edu \[what can stop\]” \[kāppār and Ar indicate cētanas \[sentient beings\]? That is to indicate that, neither the jīvātmā, who is subservient, nor the paramātmā, who is independent, can stop this mercy from flowing. Neither the enjoyer of the benefit (jīvātmā), nor the provider of the benefit (paramātmā) can stop the mercy from flowing.
- *kāppār Ar* – Can she who is the instigator of \[[bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)’s\] krupā (mercy) stop it? Can you who are bound by your own mercy stop it? Can I who am the target of your mercy stop it? While explaining śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 18.3 “*mithra bhāvēna*” (even if you (rāvaṇa) approach śrī rāma as a friend) ślōkam, [embār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/embar/) mercifully explains “Even for [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is sarvajña (omniscient), there is one ignorance and forgetfulness, even for him who is sarvaśakta (omnipotent), there is one incapability”. When some one surrenders to emperumān, emperumān will forget his previously committed intentional offenses, in the mistakes committed unintentionally after acquiring true knowledge, emperumān manifests ignorance and when it comes to giving up such person, emperumān manifests incapability; the reason for this behaviour of emperumān is his eternal motherly relationship with all ātmās.

emperumān asks “Why are you saying ‘Ar’? Me being independent, why can’t I stop the flow of my mercy?”,and [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says

- aiyō – You can try to do it if it is possible for you. It is said out of great joy.
- kaṇṇa pirān – Oh kriṣṇa who is a benefactor! Are you, who did not leave being bound by bodily relationship, going to leave me due to my fake words? Are you, who did not know how to escape when tied by a covherd girl, going to leave me now? (Implies that [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who did not untie the honest bondage, will also not untie the deceptive bondage).
- *aṟaiyō inip pōnālē* – If you go now, that is it \[“*aṟaiyō aṟai*” is a victorious chant recited by the winner usually\]. After accepting my fake words as truth, if you leave me, that will be victory for me. Depending upon [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s krupā, he is challenging īśvara’s svātāntriyam (independence). “kaṇṇa pirān” is treated as sambuddi (calling out); alternative explanation – if kaṇṇa pirān leaves me, then it is victory.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.1.2. Ponay mamarudin

*pōnāy mā marudin naduvē en pollā maṇiyē tēnē in amudē enṟenṟē sila kūttuc collat tānēl emperumān avan en āgi oḻindān vānē mānilamē maṟṟumuṟṟum en uḷḷanavē*

**Пословный перевод:**

mā – having huge bodies, being possessed by demon, and was well prepared to kill; marudin – \[two\] maruda (arjuna) trees; naduvē – in between; pōnāy – Oh one who went!; pollā – not pierced; en maṇiyē – (having great radiance like a precious gem) who attracted me with your form!; tēnē – Oh one who is having an enjoyable and beautiful form like honey!; in amudē – Oh one who saves (me who lost my existence due to thinking about the strength of the enemy), like a nectar!; enṟu enṟē – individually in this manner; sila – few which are spoken (out of great love); kūṟṟu – words; solla – speaking repeatedly with emotions; em – for me; perumān – one who is the lord; avan – him; tānēl – what he did; en – in my care; āgi oḻindān – came to be; vān – sky; mānilam – the five great elements starting with bhūmi (earth) and the whole leelā vibhūti (material realm) which is an effect of those elements; maṟṟum – nityavibhūti (spiritual realm) which is having incomprehensible glory; muṟṟum – all; en – me; uḷḷana – conducted from being within

**Перевод:**

**Oh one who went in between the \[two\] maruda (arjuna) trees which were having huge bodies, being possessed by demons, and was well prepared to kill! Oh one who attracted me with your form which resembles a precious gem which is not pierced! Oh one who is having an enjoyable and beautiful form like honey! Oh one who saves me like a nectar! In this manner, individually I spoke about different aspects with emotions as spoken by your loving devotees. What did my lord do to me for that? He came to exist in my care/disposal; he conducted the five great elements starting with bhūmi (earth) and the whole leelā vibhūti (material realm) which is an effect of those elements, nityavibhūti (spiritual realm) which is having incomprehensible glory and all, from being within me.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In second pāsuram, āḻvār says “While I was unfriendly towards emperumān, and spoke the words of those astānēbhayaśankis (those who fear for his safety even after him being the most supreme), he who is sarvēśvara along with his wealth/opulences, entered me”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. pōnāy mā marudin naduvē en pollā maṇiyē tēnē in amudē enṟenṟē sila kūttuc collat tānēl emperumān avan en āgi oḻindān vānē mānilamē maṟṟumuṟṟum en uḷḷanavē*

- *pōnāy mā marudin naduvē* – I repeated the deeply emotional words of mother yaśōdā who was witnessing the incident of kriṣṇa going in between the yamaḷārjuna trees, without such emotions. Due to [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s knowledge being well blossomed, he does not realize that, this incident happened in the past. The full expansion of knowledge became the cause for worrying for [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/).
- *mā marudin naduvē* – They are demons with huge forms who are standing there \[as the trees\]. Knowing his childishness, they stand there with huge, stout and attractive forms, talking to each other \[knowing the intent clearly\], without leaving any gap between them. He went through them as if he went through a single tree. śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 5.6.16 “*yamaḷārjunayōr madyē jagāma*” (He went through the arjuna trees) is highlighting the danger.
- *en pollā maṇiyē* – As said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 5.6.18 “*tata: katakatāśabdasamākarṇatatpara: – jagāmakamalēkśaṇa:*” (Hearing the noise of the tree falling apart, the covherd boys came joyfully running to see that), having escaped them and hearing the falling tree and seeing the unseen vision, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s divine appearance with reddish and broadly expanded eyes. He is explained as in periya tirumoḻi “*puṇar marudam iṟa nadanda poṟkunṟinai*” (kriṣṇa, the golden hillock, who walked through the arjuna trees breaking them). \[Why is [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) saying “pollā” (crazy/wild) instead of saying “aḻagiya” (beautiful)?\] To highlight the difference between worldly beauty and emperumān’s beauty, he is saying “pollā maṇi”; another explanation – he is condemning kriṣṇa so that the evil eyes of the worldly people \[looking at kriṣṇa’s divine beauty\] will be cancelled out by the condemning of āḻvār. Another explanation – *pollal* – piercing; *pollā maṇi* – unpierced gem; the gem which was never enjoyed by anyone. This too – mother yaśōdā’s words in kriṣṇa’s presence.
- *tēnē* – When she came and picked him up, due to coming in contact with him and the childish blabbering, she is praising kriṣṇa.
- *in amudē* – Words which came out of enjoyment at that moment. Also, that which is enjoyable forever, and the nectar, which can bring back lost life. As said in iraṇḍām tiruvantādi 85 “*amudenṟum tēn enṟum āḻiyān enṟum*” ([emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is like nectar, honey and having divine chakra), being infinitely enjoyable.
- *enṟu enṟē* – Could I stop myself after saying these once thinking “Oh I have committed a mistake of reciting emperumān’s glories”?
- *sila kūttuc colla* – kūttu means one person performing the thoughts and actions of another person. I who don’t have the affection of mother yaśōdā, am saying her loving words.
- *tānēl emperumān* – He is, sarvajña (omniscient) and sarva niyantā (controller of all). He is not the one who does not know the inner heart of all \[he knows the inner heart of all\], and having known, he can abandon \[those who lie\].
- *avan* – Such omniscient and omnipotent lord.
- *en āgi oḻindān* – He is fully at my disposal. One who owns me became owned by me. The roles have reversed – the owner has become owned. What did his wealth do? As said in mahābhāratam udyōga parvam “*yasyaitē tasya taddanam*” (to the one who owns a person, his property also belongs to the same owner), he made his wealth also to be at my disposal. He entered me along with all his wealth.
- *vānē mānilamē* – upalakśaṇam (sample) for panca bhūtams (five great elements).
- *maṟṟum* – The effects of the five great elements, that is, the oval shaped universes.
- *muṟṟum* – nitya vibhūti (spiritual realm) too.
- *en uḷḷanavē* – He managed both spiritual and material realms from being within me.

Another explanation:

- *vānē* … – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying “the wealth of spiritual and material realms came to me”. Just as one who is attached to worldly pleasures thinks that his object of liking is every wealth in this world, āḻvār is thinking [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is every wealth for him. As said in [tiruvāimoḻi 4.3.3](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/01/thiruvaimozhi-4-3-3-eka-murththi/) “*un āgamuṟṟum agattadakki*” (consumed and enjoyed all your beautiful form).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.1.3. Ullana marrulavay

*uḷḷana maṟṟuḷavāp puṟamē sila māyam solli vaḷḷal maṇi vaṇṇanē enṟenṟē unnaiyum vanjikkum kaḷḷa manam tavirndē unnaik kaṇḍu koṇḍuyndoḻindēn veḷḷattaṇaik kidandāy ini unnai vitten koḷvanē*

**Пословный перевод:**

uḷḷana – internal aspects \[senses\]; maṟṟu – worldly aspects other than you; uḷavā – while being engaged; puṟamē – outside, just in the mouth \[without heart’s intent\]; vaḷḷal – Oh generous one!; maṇi vaṇṇanē – Oh one with distinguished form!; enṟu enṟu – repeatedly saying so; sila – some; māyam – deceptive speeches; solli – engaging; unnaiyum – you who are sarvajña (omniscient); vanjikkum – to bewilder; kaḷḷam – artificial nature; manam – heart; tavirndu – having eliminated; unnai – you (who acknowledge just the favourable presentation); kaṇḍu koṇḍu – having enjoyed in front; uyndu oḻiundēn – I who was as good as asat (matter) have become uplifted; veḷḷam – in the milky ocean; aṇaik kidandāy – Oh one who rested!; ini – now that your efforts have fructified; unnai – you (who are always ready to help and perfectly enjoyable); vittu – leaving aside; en – which temporary and difficult to attain goal; koḷvan – will pursue?

**Перевод:**

**While my internal aspects were engaged in worldly aspects other than you, outside, just from the lips, I was repeatedly saying “Oh generous one! Oh one with distinguished form!” and engaging in some deceptive speeches to bewilder you who are a sarvajña; such artificial nature of my heart was eliminated and having enjoyed you in front, I who was as good as asat (matter) have become uplifted. Oh one who rested in the milky ocean! now that your efforts have fructified, leaving you aside, which temporary and difficult to attain goal will I pursue?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the third pāsuram, āḻvār says “I who attained you by praising you through my speech while my heart was elsewhere, will not desire for any other puruśārtam (goal)”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “The artificial nature in my heart which deceived even you, the omniscient, is gone and I have seen you; is there any shelter other than you who are such a benefactor?”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. uḷḷana maṟṟuḷavāp puṟamē sila māyam solli vaḷḷal maṇi vaṇṇanē enṟenṟē unnaiyum vanjikkum kaḷḷa manam tavirndē unnaik kaṇḍu koṇḍuyndoḻindēn veḷḷattaṇaik kidandāy ini unnai vitten koḷvanē*

- *uḷḷana* – that which is inside the heart.
- *maṟṟuḷavā* – while focussed on elsewhere. That is, internal heart is attached to worldly pleasures.
- *puṟamē sila māyam solli* – Externally speaking some flowery words. Here “*kūttuccolla*” (from [previous pāsuram](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/05/thiruvaimozhi-5-1-2-ponay-mamarudhin/)) is explained.
- *vaḷḷal maṇivaṇṇanē* – Oh great benefactor! Oh one who gave me your priceless gem like adorable form!
- *enṟu enṟē* – Repeatedly saying it in such a manner that even though it is said without heart’s intent, it appeared that [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is speaking with true emotions.
- *unnaiyum vanjikkum kaḷḷa manam* – My mischievous mind which makes you think that I am saying the truth and bewilders even you who are sarvajña (omniscient) and sarvāntaryāmi (omnipresent), knowing every thought of everyone due to being present everywhere.
- *tavirndē* – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is of the nature that, even those who pursue him without heart’s intent, will become fully attached to him.
- *unnai* – You who say “*na tyajēyam*” (śrī rāma – I will not abandon) even if some one approaches you with “*mithra bhāva*” (as a friend). You who are a suitable master and enjoyable.
- *kaṇḍu koṇḍu* – I who said “Can I see him once some how?”, got to see you, like finding treasure.
- *uyndu oḻindēn* – I who was as said in taittirīya upaniśat “*asannēva*” (he becomes non-existing), became uplifted. cāndōjña upaniśat *“druśtvā truptyanti” (*become satisfied on just seeing).

When asked “What are you going to do now?”, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says,

- *veḷḷattu aṇaik kidandāy* – Oh emperumān who left paramapadam (spiritual realm), arrived at kśīrābdi (milky ocean) and is mercifully resting there being ready to protect me!
- *ini* – After leaving paramapadam which is a perfect match for you and mercifully resting in this samsāram (material realm) which is no match for you, for protecting me.
- *unnai vittu* – Other than you who will not leave me even if I left you.
- *en koḷvanē* – Will I pursue those aspects which accept the pursual but fail while giving the results? Will I pursue those who are difficult to worship and cannot bestow anything? \[No – I will pursue nothing/none other than you\].

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.1.4. En kolvan

*en koḷvan unnai vittennum vāsagangaḷ solliyum van kaḷvanēn manattai valittuk kaṇṇa nīr karandu nin kaṇ nerunga vaittē enadāviyai nīkkagillēn en kaṇ malinam aṟuttu ennaik kūvi aruḷay kaṇṇanē*

**Пословный перевод:**

unnai – you (who is the ultimate benefit/goal); vittu – leaving aside; en – which benefit/goal; koḷvan – will I have?; ennum – that; vāsagangaḷ – verses of praises; solliyum – saying in many ways; val – since time immemorial, stealing the ātmā; kaḷvanēn – I, the mischievous; manattai – heart/mind (which went behind worldly pleasures); valittu – pulling; kaṇṇa nīr – the tears (which come out due to not having attained such pleasures); karandu – changed (by eliminating the scent); manattai – that heart; nin kaṇ – in you (who is perfectly enjoyable); nerunga vaittu – bring it closer; enadu āviyai – my ātmā; nīkka killēn – I am unable to release from the samsāram (material realm); en kaṇ – my; malinam – defects such as ignorance; aṟuttu – removing; ennai – I, who am incapable; kaṇṇanē – Oh kriṣṇa who says “mā suca:” to those who are in sorrow!; kūvi aruḷāy – accept me (close to you); van – since time immemorial; kaḷvanēn – I, who am mischievous; unnai – you; vittu – leaving aside; en – which other benefit?; koḷvan – will have; ennum – that; vāsagangaḷ solliyum – speaking unable to sustain myself; manattai – my heart which is broken due to not having attained you; valittu – prepare it well to be united with you; kaṇṇa nīr – tears due to not experiencing \[you\]; karandu – changing; nin kaṇ – in you; nerunga – to be fully subdued in you; vaittu – placing; enadu āviyai – my ātmā; nīkka – to liberate through upāsana (bhakti yōgam); killēn – I am unable; en kaṇ malinam aṟuttu ennaik kūvi aruḷāy – you only can mercifully do that

**Перевод:**

**First explanation**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fourth pāsuram, āḻvār says “Previously I pretended \[to love you\] due to my relationship with this prakruti (material realm); hence you have to mercifully eliminate my relationship with this prakruti”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Fourth pāsuram. Two introductions. en koḷvan unnai vittennum vāsagangaḷ solliyum van kaḷvanēn manattai valittuk kaṇṇa nīr karandu nin kaṇ nerunga vaittē enadāviyai nīkkagillēn en kaṇ malinam aṟuttu ennaik kūvi aruḷay kaṇṇanē*

**First Explanation**

- *en koḷvan unnai vittu ennum* – Though I am speaking like paramaikāntis (those who are fully surrendered to [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)), that is, my lips saying “What else other than you, will I have?”,
- *van kaḷvanēn* – kaḷavu mean para dravya apahāram (stealing others’ belongings). valiya kaḷavu (great robbery) means, as said in “*cōrēṇa ātmāpahāriṇā*” (stealing the [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) is the biggest theft), considering the ātmā, which is a property of [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/), to be “I, mine”. The severity of stealing a diamond is different from that of stealing wood. \[Is ātmā a dravya (object)?\] While \[sages like vyāsa were\] explaining different types of objects, ātmā was explained as the first one. The object \[ātmā\] is distinguished, and the owner is sarvēśvara himself, what more needs to be said about the theft?
- *manattai valittu* – Withdrawing the mind which is attached to worldly pleasures from them. The term “*valittu*” (pulling back strongly) is used to highlight the nature of the mind’s strong attachment towards those pleasures. While I try to overcome them, they end up winning over me. [śrī bhagavat gītā 2.60](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/2-60/) “*indriyāṇi pramātīni haranti prasabham mana:”* (his strong senses pull his mind forcefully \[towards them\]).
- *kaṇṇa nīr karandu* – Changing/stopping the tears which were flowing due to not getting those pleasures.
- *nin kaṇ nerunga vaittē* – Turning that mind towards you and bringing closer to you.
- *enadu āviyai nīkka killēn* – I am unable to consider the [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) (soul) to be separate from the body.
- *en kaṇ malinam aṟuttu* – The reason for my inability is due to the defects in me. That is being connected to this material realm \[specifically the physical body\]. I am suffering due to my connection with my “*mey*” (body). [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is praying to [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) “Please eliminate that \[body\] and mercifully accept me at your divine feet”.
- *kaṇṇanē* – āren’t you the one who removes others’ sorrows? All you need to do for me is to show your beautiful form and tell me “*mā suca:*” (do not feel sad). Once I see that form, I would be as said in amalanādipirān 10 “*maṟṟonṟinaik kāṇāvē*” (I will not see anything else).

**Second Explanation**

- *en koḷvan* … – Though I am reciting the words which match my svarūpam (true nature).
- *van kaḷvanēn* – As some one who did not acquire the suitable object would become upset and say “I am a great sinner”, āḻvār is saying this.
- *manattai valittu* … – Redeeming the mind which is broken due to bhakti pāravaśyam (overwhelming devotion) and making it strong; and stopping the tears which were explained in [tiruvāimoḻi 2.4.10](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/03/thiruvaimozhi-2-4-10-ezhai-pedhai/) “*tana kēḻil oṇ kaṇṇa nīr koṇḍāḷ*” (her beautiful matchless eyes became tearful).
- *nin kaṇ nerunga vaittē* – I am unable to a) make the mind which becomes broken on approaching you closely as said in periya tiruvantādi 34 “*kālāḻum nenjaḻiyum*” (my legs become weak and my heart becomes weak), to be strong and meditating upon you and b) consider that the [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) is different from body. Instead of being relaxed thinking “Let him eliminate his hurdles, and reach me in due course of time”, you who can accomplish whatever you think, should eliminate my hurdles and mercifully accept me.
- *kaṇṇanē* – Are you \[as kriṣṇa\] not the one who gave good advice \[as part of [gītā](http://githa.koyil.org/) carama ślōkam\] to the one who considered “bhakti is not upāyam”?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.1.5. Kanna piranai

*kaṇṇa pirānai viṇṇōr karu māṇikkattai amudai naṇṇiyum naṇṇagillēn naduvē ōr udambil ittut tiṇṇam aḻundak kattip pala seyvinai van kayiṟṟāl puṇṇai maṟaiya varindu ennaip pōra vaittāy puṟamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kaṇṇan – Having incarnated as kriṣṇa; pirānai – favouring the advice with regard to the upāyam (means) (as in “mām ēkam śaraṇam vraja“); viṇṇōr – that which is attractive and seen by nityasūris (eternally free souls of paramapadam); karu māṇikkattai – letting them enjoy the distinguished form; amudai – you who are eternally enjoyable; naṇṇiyum – though I remain situated close to you by the knowledge given by you; naṇṇa killēn – remained like those who have not attained you; naduvē – staying in between (to not have the connection with the ātmā and you who are opposite of all faults, to push away both); ōr – a; udambil – in body; ittu – placing and establishing the connection; pala – in many ways; sey – to be performed due to the bondage in body; vinai – karmas; val kayiṟṟāl – with strong ropes (bondage); tiṇṇam – to be firm; aḻunda – difficult to examine; katti – tie; puṇṇai – external faults; maṟaiya – to conceal; varindu – surrounding forever; ennai – me (who is incapable and unsuitable to remove this bondage); puṟamē – samsāram which is external to you and is filled with superficial pleasures; pōra – to go; vaittāy – placed me

**Перевод:**

**Even after remaining close to you by the knowledge given by you who incarnated as kriṣṇa, who are favouring the advice with regard to the upāyam and who are letting those who are surrendered to the eternally enjoyable you to enjoy the distinguished form which is attractive and seen by nityasūris, I remain like those who have not attained you; (the reason for that is) you have placed me in between in a body and established the connection, tied me with strong ropes in karmas which are to be performed in many ways due to the bondage in body, to be firm in that body, are concealing the external faults, are surrounding me forever and are placing me to go into samsāram which is external to you and is filled with superficial pleasures. āḻvār implies that “If you desire, you can release me from this bondage”.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fifth pāsuram, āḻvār mercifully and clearly explains that his fault is prakruti sambandam (relation to material realm).*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār saying to emperumān “You are the one who bound me into the prakruti” and explaining that eradication of such relationship with material realm is fully at emperumān’s disposal.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. kaṇṇa pirānai viṇṇōr karu māṇikkattai amudai naṇṇiyum naṇṇagillēn naduvē ōr udambil ittut tiṇṇam aḻundak kattip pala seyvinai van kayiṟṟāl puṇṇai maṟaiya varindu ennaip pōra vaittāy puṟamē*

- *viṇṇōr karu māṇikkattai …* – Oh you who appeared as kriṣṇa to present to me,  the form which is enjoyed by nityasūris, as said in śrīviṣṇu sūktam “*tadviprāsōvipanyavō jāgruvāmsasamindatē*” (in that paramapadam, the wisest and those who are always engaged in praising you are carefully present and are shining)!
- *amudai* – by incarnating, he made [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) enjoy his sweetness.
- *naṇṇiiyum …* – Though I have attained him, I am counted among those who have not attained him. Here, āḻvār indicates his jñāna lābham (acquiring pure knowledge) as attainment of emperumān; and he indicates his presence in this material body as non-attainment of him.
- *naduvē oru udambil ittu* – As [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) observes the unnatural aspect of this body, he says that he acquired it in-between, though [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)‘s relationship with [acit](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/09/thathva-thrayam-achith-what-is-matter/) is since anādi (time immemorial, without a beginning). For the pearl and gold in its shell, no one knows when they became dirty, yet as it is seen that the dirt is removed at some point, we understand that “the dirt” is unnatural; similarly, as we see that by surrendering unto [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) the connection with material realm is eradicated, the connection with material nature appears to be “unnatural” \[though ātmā and acit have been together thus far\]. As a prince who becomes lost in a forest, and found and raised by a hunter, will consider himself to be a hunter too, cētana (ātmā – sentient being) will consider the body to be self and think himself as “*dēvōham*” (I am dēva) etc.
- *tiṇṇam aḻundak katti* – Keeping it firmly tied by avidyā (ignorance) etc.
- *pala sey vinai …* – Keeping it bound to the strong ropes , that is, the karmas which are performed in many ways.
- *puṇṇai maṟaiya varindu* – Like a ditch which is covered with hay, and placed with a plank on top with decoration \[similarly, the body is covered with nice layer of skin\]. Without such decoration, if that which is inside gets exposed, one will not have time to drive away the crows which come to feast on it.
- *ennai* – me who am incapable and unsuitable to save the self.
- *pōra vaittāy puṟamē* – Being in this \[material\] body after acquiring svarūpa jñānam (true knowledge) appears to [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) like sītā pirātti’s case, where she went along with śrī rāma to enjoy in seclusion with him, but ended up in aśōka vanam (in lankā) on her own.
- *puṟamē* – You placed me in samsāram where your qualities are not well known. āḻvār being parama vaidika (fully faithful towards vēdam), tells “[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) placed him in samsāram”, as he considers his karma also to be fully under emperumān’s disposal, as his \[āḻvār’s\] svarūpam is.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.1.6. Puramara

*puṟam aṟak kattik koṇḍu iru val vinaiyār kumaikkum muṟai muṟai ākkai pugal oḻiyak kaṇḍu koṇḍoḻindēn niṟamudai nāl tadam tōḷ seyya vāy seyya tāmaraik kaṇ aṟamuyalāḻiyangaik karu mēni ammān tannaiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

puṟam – anything external; aṟa – to forget; kattik koṇḍu – binding; iru – two types (in the form of puṇya (virtues) and pāpa (vices)); val – very strong; vinaiyār – karmas; kumaikkum – the abode which is affected; muṟai muṟai – dēva (celestial) etc \[human, animal, plant\]; ākkai – in bodies; pugal – entering in many ways; oḻiya – to eliminate; niṟam – attractive form; udai – having; nāl – four types; tadam – rounded; tōḷ – shoulders; seyya – reddish; vāy – divine lips; seyya – reddish; tāmarai – lotus like; kaṇ – eyes; aṟam – in the virtual act of protection; muyal – engaged in; āḻi – due to having divine chakra; am – having great beauty; kai – having divine hand; karu – blackish; mēni – having form; ammān – the lord; kaṇḍu koṇḍu oḻindēn – I have seen him in front of me and enjoyed to eliminate all my losses

**Перевод:**

**One enters in many ways into bodies such as dēva (celestial) etc which are the abodes which are affected by very strong two types of karmas which bind one to forget about anything else; I have seen in front of me, the lord who is having attractive form having four types of rounded shoulders, reddish divine lips, reddish lotus like eyes, having greatly beautiful divine hand which is having divine chakra which is engaged in the virtual act of protecting \[everyone\] and blackish form, and eliminated all such losses \[of going through different bodies and sufferings\],**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the sixth pāsuram, āḻvār becomes pleased after emperumān manifesting his divine beauty to make āḻvār forget the anguish acquired by meditating upon the material realm.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Sixth pāsuram.  On seeing āḻvār saying “pōra vaittāy puṟamē” and becoming anguished, emperumān decided “we should make him forget of about his loss and redeem him” and manifests his physical beauty; on seeing that divine beauty, āḻvār becomes pleased forgetting his own body and says “I have seen him”. emperumān’s form mesmerized āḻvār and made āḻvār forget his own body. puṟam aṟak kattik koṇḍu iru val vinaiyār kumaikkum muṟai muṟai ākkai pugal oḻiyak kaṇḍu koṇḍoḻindēn niṟamudai nāl tadam tōḷ seyya vāy seyya tāmaraik kaṇ aṟamuyalāḻiyangaik karu mēni ammān tannaiyē*

- *puṟam aṟak kattik koṇḍu* – Having it tied in such a very complex manner that the ātmā cannot untie the binding. [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) himself said that the knot which is tied by him who is sarvaśakti (omnipotent) cannot be untied by any one else in [śrī bhagavat gītā 7.14](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/7-14/) “*mama māyā duratyayā*” (my material realm is very difficult to cross over).
- *iru val vinaiyār* – will effect both types of great sins \[puṇya and pāpa, both are considered as sins, since both of them bind us in this material realm\]. *vinaiyār* indicates respectful way of  saying *vinai* (karma) due to being tortured by it, or it can indicate the plural of *vinai*.
- *kumaikkum muṟai muṟai ākkai* – By doing \[more\] puṇya (virtue), one will acquire dēva (celestial) form, by doing \[more\] pāpa (vice), one will acquire animal and plant bodies, and when there is equal measure of puṇya and pāpa, one will acquire human form – in this manner there is no end to the sufferings here. Like a dog which will enter and exit any open door, the ātmā will enter different forms such as dēva (celestial), manuśya (human), tiryak (animal) and stāvara (plant) forms,  based on its karma and keep moving on.
- *pugal oḻiya* – to eliminate acquiring such births. ātmā which is known by its jñānam (knowledge) and ānandam (bliss) is the one which is going through different bodies and suffering, to go through six types of changes (birth, growth, … death) . To eliminate such sufferings.
- *kaṇḍu koṇḍu oḻindēn* – I have seen and enjoyed the apt lord; and hence eliminated the need to enter any more bodies.
- *niṟamudai* … – As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam kiśkintā kāṇḍam 3.14 “*sarva bhūsaṇa bhūśārhā:*” (the shoulders which deserve to be decorated by all ornaments), having divine shoulders which are being an ornament for the ornament, in count of four and being rounded; as said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 5.17.21 “*savilāsasmitādāram bibrāṇam mukhapankhajam*” (one who is having the divine face to support the broad smile) – having the smile which maintains the freshness of the divine face, the divine eyes which are glancing in a cool manner to make one forget their losses; having the divine hand which carries the divine chakra which is more focussed in the parama dharma (supreme virtue) of protecting the devotees, and the divine cool beauty which will capture anyone even if (s)he is not captivated by that \[divine hand/chakra combination\], and the aptness to enjoy saying “all of these are for me” – I have seen such [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/). \[Has [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) seen that form? Yes.\] This is the form that is seen in one’s own heart as explained in taittirīya upaniśat “*neelatōyada madyastā*” (like a lightning amidst a dark cloud). Just as previously this \[material\] body made me forget the divine form \[of emperumān\], now, that divine form made me forget this body.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.1.7. Amman alippiran

*ammān āḻip pirān avan evvidattān yān ār emmā pāviyarkkum vidi vāykkinṟu vāykkum kaṇḍīr kaimmā tunboḻittāy enṟu kaitalai pūsalittē meymmālāy oḻindēn em pirānum en mēlānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

āḻi – with the divine hand and divine chakra; pirān – the great benefactor who lets his devotees enjoy him; ammān – natural lord; avan – he; evvidattān – where is he standing (to be not measured and enjoyed even by nityasūris who have unlimited knowledge); yān – (the lowly) I (who am doing mischievous aspects in this matter); Ar – what is my capacity?; kaimmā – not seeing the inferior birth of the elephant (which set out to worship your divine feet); tunbu – suffering; oḻittāy – Oh one who eliminated!; enṟu – saying that; kai – hand; talai – placing on top of the head; pūsalittē – calling out well; meymmāl – having superior love; āyoḻindēn – have become; em – reforming me, ignoring my inferior nature; pirān – benefactor; en mēlān – become intent on pursuing me; e – any; mā pāviyarkkum – great sinners; vidi – destiny in the form of unmissable mercy of bhagavān; vāykkinṟu – when it sets out to bestow the result; vāykkum kaṇḍīr – will certainly bring the result

**Перевод:**

**Where is emperumān who is with the divine hand and divine chakra, the great benefactor who lets his devotees enjoy him, the natural lord standing? What is my capacity? I am calling out well saying “Oh one who eliminated the suffering of the elephant not seeing its inferior birth!” and have become a person with superior love \[towards you\] to have my hands placed on my head \[saluting you\]; such benefactor who reformed me, ignoring my inferior nature, has also become intent on pursuing me; thus, even for the greatest sinners, when the destiny in the form of unmissable mercy of bhagavān sets out to bestow the result, it will certainly bring the result.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the seventh pāsuram, āḻvār, becoming joyful as a result of the benefit he acquired, says “Even for worst sinners, emperumān‘s krupā is there, and hence, everyone will get the benefit”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. ammān āḻip pirān avan evvidattān yān Ar emmā pāviyarkkum vidi vāykkinṟu vāykkum kaṇḍīr kaimmā tunboḻittāy enṟu kaitalai pūsalittē meymmālāy oḻindēn em pirānum en mēlānē*

- *ammān* – sarvēśvaran.
- *āḻip pirān* – He who is manifesting the beautiful combination of his hand and the chakra to the nityasūris.
- *avan evvidattān* – which capable persons can interact with him?
- yān Ar – I am even lower than nitya samsāris (eternally bound souls). piḷḷai amudanār used to point high while reciting “ammān āḻip pirān” and low while reciting “yān Ar”.
- *em mā pāviyarkkum* … – If [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s krupā (mercy) sets out to flow towards even the most horrible sinners, that cannot be stopped. If the flood of his mercy starts flowing, one cannot say “I remain on the shore and I can escape it”.

When asked “How did you surrender to [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)?”, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says

- *kaimmā* … – The elephant which has no high birth, conduct or knowledge, due to impressions from previous birth, remembered the divine feet of emperumān when harmed, just like when some one steps on a thorn will naturally cry out “*ammē*” (Oh mother!); emperumān disregarding his supremacy, at once flew on garuda with diśevelled attire/decorations and protected the elephant; thinking about this mercy of emperumān saying “what a benefactor he is!”, I \[[āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)\] recited these words, which are recited with great emotions by those who are associated with emperumān, without any such emotion.
- *kai talai pūsalittē* – Three explanations – a) placing my hand on my head, I called out from my mouth b) performing anjali \[joined palms\] continuously c) not changing the hand which was placed on the head. On reciting the emotionless words which are recited with great emotions by those who consider the help to elephant as helping themselves being won over by gratitude towards [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), those words penetrated my heart and my fake devotion became real devotion.

When asked “What did he do to you?”, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says,

- *em pirān en mēlānē* – Would emperumān who truly pursues me (whether I am speaking truth or lies), ever leave me? emperumān, pursued me as a benefactor and as a hungry person who saw food.

Due to this reason,

- *em mā pāviyarkkum vidi vāykkinṟu vāykkum kaṇḍīr* – However great sinner one may be, where [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s krupā flows, one cannot escape.

pūsalidugai means calling out well, and joining together.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.1.8. Melat tevargalum

*mēlāt tēvargaḷum nilat tēvarum mēvit toḻum mālār vandina nāḷ adiyēn manattē manninār sēlēy kaṇṇiyarum perum selvamum nanmakkaḷum mēlāt tāy tandaiyum avarē ini āvārē*

**Пословный перевод:**

mēlām – superior in all manners; dēvargaḷum – surīs \[nityasūris of spiritual realm\]; nilam – in this material realm; tēvarum – bhāgavatas radiantly natured due to their knowledge about bhagavān, love towards bhagavān etc; mēvi – fully focussed being ananyaprayōjana (those who are don’t seek ulterior motives); toḻum – to enjoy; mālār – one who is greater than all; ina nāḷ – now; vandu – approaching me in a friendly manner; adiyēn – only considering my subordinate relationship with him; manattē – in my heart; manninār – became well settled; ini – subsequently; sēlēy kaṇṇiyarum – damsels with beautiful eyes; perum – great; selvamum – wealth; nal – with very good qualities; makkaḷum – sons; mēlām – considered great due to their priyam (love) and hitam (concern for the well-being); tāy tandaiyum – mother and father; avarē – he only; āvār – becomes

**Перевод:**

**emperumān who is greater than all, is enjoyed with full focus by being ananyaprayōjana by the nityasūris of the spiritual realm, who are superior in all manners and the bhāgavatas radiantly natured due to their knowledge about bhagavān, love towards bhagavān etc., in this material realm; such emperumān, now approaching me in a friendly manner and only considering my subordinate relationship with him, became well settled in my heart; subsequently, for me, he only becomes damsels with beautiful eyes, great wealth, sons with very good qualities, mother and father who are considered great due to their priyam and hitam. āḻvār Implies, whatever joy one may get from these persons, āḻvār will get the same joy from emperumān.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the eighth pāsuram, āḻvār says “While emperumān has many qualified persons to enjoy him, now he entered me; henceforth he is my all types of enjoyment”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “emperumān who is having the greatness of being the lord of both spiritual and material realms, entered my heart and allowed me to enjoy all types of relationships with him”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Eighth pāsuram. āḻvār says “emperumān who is the lord of spiritual and material realms pursued me with great intent and entered my heart; like nityasūris, I too, giving up this material realm, am trying to hold on to him as all my relationships”. mēlāt tēvargaḷum nilat tēvarum mēvit toḻum mālār vandina nāḷ adiyēn manattē manninār sēlēy kaṇṇiyarum perum selvamum nanmakkaḷum mēlāt tāy tandaiyum avarē ini āvārē*

- *mēlāt tēvargaḷum* – nityasūris.
- *nilat tēvarum* – śrīvaiṣṇavas who are known as bhūsuras (the celestial beings of this earth).
- *mēvit toḻum mālār* – Just as iḷaiya perumāḷ (lakśmaṇa) and monkeys which do not know to distinguish between left and right hands, served [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) together, emperumān, who is greater than all, is served by the residents of both spiritual and material realms together.
- *ina nāḷ* – Now. While I was unaware in the previous moment, now, I see the dawn.

When asked “what is the reason for his arrival?”, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says,

- *adiyēn* – He came due to the relationship which is not possible to be severed.

When asked “what did he do after coming?”, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says,

- *manattē manninār* – As said in mūnṟām tiruvantādi 3 “*manattuḷḷān mā kadal nīruḷḷān malarāḷ tanattuḷḷān*“, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who resides in the heart of great yōgis, milky ocean and the divine bosom of [periya pirāttiyār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/), became well settled in my heart, me who am a nityasamsāri (eternally suffering soul).

When asked “what are you going to do now?”, āḻvār says “Is there anything other than emperumān for me to engage in”,

- *sēlēy …* – Damsels who can captivate other by their glance, unlimited wealth, well behaved sons, parents who take care of the children even at the cost of their own sufferings – I tried holding on to [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) as all of these persons.
- *avarē ini āvārē* – I don’t need to worry about such relationships which cause suffering. subāla upaniśat “*mātā pitā …*” (śrīman nārāyaṇa is the mother, father, brother etc). śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 58.31 “*aham tāvat …*” (lakśmaṇa to sumantra – I do not consider daśarata cakravarti as my father. I consider śrī rāma to be my brother, master, all relatives and father).

## 5.1.9. Avarar tunai

*āvār ār tuṇai enṟu alai nīr kadaluḷ aḻundum nāvāy pōl piṟavik kadaluḷ ninṟu nān tuḷangat tēvār kōlattodum tiruccakkaram sanginodum āvā enṟaruḷ seydu adiyēnodum ānānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tuṇai – saviour; āvār – be; Ar – who will; enṟu – saying; alai – currents; nīr – having water; kadal uḷ – in the ocean; aḻundum – drowning; nāvāy pōl – like a boat; piṟavik kadal uḷ – in the middle of samsāra sāgaram (ocean of nescience); ninṟu – standing; nān – I (who cannot reach the shore); tuḷanga – shiver; tēvu – with divine beauty etc; Ar – being complete; kōlattodum – with the form; tiruccakkaram sanginodum – with the divine weapons which add lustre to that form; A A enṟu – considering “alas! (feeling sympathetic)” \[for my pitiable state\]; aruḷ seydu – bestowing his mercy; adiyēnodum – with me who is his belonging; ānān – united

**Перевод:**

**Saying “Who will be my saviour?”, I am shivering while standing in the middle of samsāra sāgaram, like a drowning boat in the ocean having water currents. (At that time) emperumān came with his complete divine beautiful form and with the divine weapons which add lustre to that form, feeling sympathetic and bestowing his mercy, united with me who is his belonging. āḻvār revealed whatever he mentioned as “vidi” previously to be “aruḷ” (mercy) explicitly now. tēvu \[divu in samskrutam\] – beauty; divine, spiritual.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the ninth pāsuram, āḻvār says “emperumān, out of his infinite mercy, came with his divine form and united with me, to remove all my sufferings in this samsāram (material realm)”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “emperumān, who is related to me in all these ways, came with his distinguished form and united with me”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. āvār Ar tuṇai enṟu alai nīr kadaluḷ aḻundum nāvāy pōl piṟavik kadaluḷ ninṟu nān tuḷangat tēvār kōlattodum tiruccakkaram sanginodum āvā enṟaruḷ seydu adiyēnodum ānānē*

- *āvār Ar tuṇai enṟu* – Who will be the saviour?
- *alai nīr* … – Like a boat drowning in an agitated ocean, I was shivering in this ocean of nescience. Here, if the term “*nāvāy*” is just taken to mean the boat, “*āvār Ar tuṇai*” should be considered as the words of those who are looking at the boat from the shore. Alternatively, it could be seen as “*manjā: krōśanti*” (the cot is making noise – i.e., the persons on the cot are making noise), where the individuals on the boat are saying “who will be our saviour?”. For, first explanation, where the focus is on the boat, nadungugai indicates “swaying while coming along in the ocean”.

When asked “What did [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) do seeing my shivering?”, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says,

- *dēvār …* – (dēvu \[divu in samskrutam\] – beauty; divine, spiritual) With great compassion towards me, coming along with his divine paraphernalia \[the spiritual realm\], and his divine weapons, bestowing his mercy upon me and united with me. As heard from [āḷavandār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/alavandhar/), [tirumālai āṇḍān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/thirumalai-andan/) explained this to [emperumānār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/emperumanar/) (*tiruccakkaram sanginodum – adiyēnodumānān – enṟu*), “[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) united with me as he is united with the āḻvārs (cakkarattāḻvār and sangāḻvār) in his hands”. Hearing that, emperumānār mercifully said “\[Instead\] It can be explained like this. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) desired to see emperumān along with his disc and conch as in tiruvāimoḻi 6.9.1 ‘*kūrārāḻi veṇsengēndi – vārāy*‘ (Please come to me, holding the sharp disc and pure white conch), and thus, emperumān appeared with his divine weapons to fulfil āḻvār’s desire”. āḻvār is like those servitors of kings who would kill themselves when the king is not pampered with flowers pertaining to the seasons/times. When he does not see the divine weapons of emperumān on his hands, he would at once cease to exist.
- *aruḷ seydu adiyēnodum ānān* – Starting from tiruvāimoḻi 2.7 decad “*kēsavan tamar*” \[specifically in [tiruvāimoḻi 2.7.6](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/05/thiruvaimozhi-2-7-6-madhusudhanai-anri/) “*madusūdanai anṟi … vidi sūḻndadāl*“\], out of misery, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) indicated [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s mercy using the word “*vidi*“, but now \[out of magnanimity\], he reveals it explicitly as “*aruḷ*” \[which is a direct translation for krupā\].
- *adiyēnodum ānān* – Matching his nature and my nature, he came as the lord and master, and united with me.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.1.10. Anan aludaiyan

*ānān āḷudaiyān enṟu ahdē koṇḍugandu vandu tānē in aruḷ seydu ennai muṟṟavum tān ānān mīnāy āmaiyumāy narasingamumāyk kuṟaḷāy kānār ēnamumāyk kaṟkiyām innam kārvaṇṇanē*

**Пословный перевод:**

mīn – matsya (fish); āy – becoming; āmaiyum – kūrma (turtle); āy – becoming; narasingamum – narasimha (lion-headed human); āy – becoming; kuṟaḷ – vāmana (dwarf); āy – becoming; kānār ēnamum – vana varāha (wild pig/boar); āy – becoming; innamum – further; kaṟkiyum – kalki; Am – become; kār – blackish like a dark-cloud; vaṇṇan – having distinguished form; (ennai – me); āḷ – as a servitor; udaiyān – one who is having; ānān – became; enṟu – this; ahdē – just the word; koṇḍu – considering; ugandu – being very pleased; vandu – came; tānē – himself, without any expectation; in – infinitely enjoyable; aruḷ – mercy; seydu – giving; ennai – to capture me; tān – he; muṟṟavum – with all incarnations; ānān – united with me

**Перевод:**

**Just considering my words of saying “emperumān who became matsya, kūrma, narasimha, vāmana, vana varāha, and further kalki, who is having distinguished blackish form like that of a dark-cloud, became the one who is having me as his servitor”, emperumān, being very pleased came himself without any expectation, gave his infinitely enjoyable mercy to capture me and united with me, manifesting and making me enjoy all his incarnations.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the tenth pāsuram, āḻvār says “emperumān gave his divine union with me just on seeing my observance of gratitude for his great favour”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “Such emperumān who has distinguished form made me enjoy all his incarnations and united with me”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Tenth pāsuram. āḻvār says “emperumān gave his divine union with me just on seeing my observance of gratitude for his great favour of creating taste towards him after mercifully eradicating my attachment to worldly pleasures”. ānān āḷudaiyān enṟu ahdē koṇḍugandu vandu tānē in aruḷ seydu ennai muṟṟavum tān ānān mīnāy āmaiyumāy narasingamumāyk kuṟaḷāy kānār ēnamumāyk kaṟkiyām innam kārvaṇṇanē*

- *ānān āḷ udaiyān* – Without realizing the meaning, I said “[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) will have me as his servitor”; just considering those words only, he forgot all his efforts which led me to say these words and just considered me saying them as a great thing.
- *ugandu* – Instead of me being the enjoyer of the result, he himself is the sole enjoyer.
- *vandu* – Here too, the roles were reversed \[instead of me approaching him, he came to me\].
- *tānē in aruḷ seydu* – He bestowed his grace as a benefit for him, while I did not even request to do so.
- *ennai muṟṟavum tān ānān* – Two explanations – a) he united with me so well without any differentiation, b) he became all types of enjoyment for me. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) already said in [tiruvāimoḻi 4.3.3](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/01/thiruvaimozhi-4-3-3-eka-murththi/) “*āgamuṟṟum agattadakki*” (having your form fully in me).
- *mīnāy* … – One who is different from all species, assumed a form in the aquatic species to bestow knowledge, assumed the form of turtle to sustain \[the mantara mountain\], assumed the human/lion combination form to immediately destroy the enemy, \[as vāmana\] became a seeker with the hands that only grew by giving to others, and assumed the form of wild pig to uplift me from the ocean of nescience.
- *kānār ēnam* – He assumed a varāha form which brings beauty to the whole forest as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 38.15 “*śōbhayandaṇḍakāraṇyam*” (the daṇḍaka forest acquired glow), the whole forest acquired the glow of śrī rāma’s peacock green color. Also explained as, varāha lives in a forest where there is no human habitat.
- *kaṟkiyām innam* – Even after fulfilling my desire, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) remains steadfast in his objective thinking “Until he remains in this samsāram, what danger he may face”. He remains prepared to assume the form of kaṟki, to protect [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) in the future. Like the births I took to escape him, he has had many births to protect me. Just like I assumed many births out of karma \[puṇya/pāpa\], he assumed many births out of mercy.
- *kār vaṇṇanē* – He appears like a laden cloud which is ready to rain. He does not appear like an empty cloud which already had shed the rain.
