## 5.3.10. Yamadalurndum

*yāmadalūrndum em āḻiyangaip pirānudait tūmadal taṇṇantuḻāy malar koṇḍu sūduvōm yāmadaminṟit teruvu tōṟayal taiyalār nāmadangāp paḻi tūṟṟi nādum iraikkavē*

**Пословный перевод:**

yā – matching the femininity, in any manner; madam – shyness; inṟi – without; teruvu tōṟu – in every street; ayal – neighbouring; taiyalār – women; nā – tongue; madangā – saying continuously; paḻi – accusations; tūṟṟi – hurling; nādum – all of the world; iraikka – to call out in an angry/agitated manner; yām – we (who have femininity and hence cannot engage in madal); madal – madal (which does not match our nature); ūrndum – even by engaging in; āḻi am kai – one who lets us enjoy the combination of his hand and chakra; em – attracted us; pirānudai – benefactor’s; tū – pure due to its freshness; madal – having leaf; taṇ – invigorating; am – attractive; tuḻāy – tuḷasi; malar – garland; koṇḍu – accepting it from him; sūduvōm – will wear it in our head

**Перевод:**

**Without shyness matching our femininity in any manner, we will even engage in madal by entering every street and by engaging in hurling accusations continuously with the tongue as done by the neighbouring women, to have all of the world call out in an angry/agitated manner for emperumān, the benefactor, who let us enjoy the combination of his hand and chakra and attracted us by that and will accept his invigorating and attractive tuḷasi garland which is pure due to the freshness of its leaves, and will wear it in our head. parānguśa nāyaki is addressing herself as “we/us” (the royal we) due to her pride in engaging in madal.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the tenth pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki says “Even if I have to engage in madal to jolt him severely, we will see that emperumān who is perfectly enjoyable”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, parānguśa nāyaki says “We will wear the garland of emperumān who is having distinguished symbols which are perfectly enjoyable, even by engaging in madal to jolt him in this world by accusing him everywhere”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. yāmadalūrndum em āḻiyangaip pirānudait tūmadal taṇṇantuḻāy malar koṇḍu sūduvōm yāmadaminṟit teruvu tōṟayal taiyalār nāmadangāp paḻi tūṟṟi nādum iraikkavē*

- *yā madal ūrndum* – Even doing by what is forbidden. We who are to remain fully dependent on [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 9.30 “… *tat tasya sadruśam bhavēt*“ (śrī rāma himself destroying lankā and rescuing me is that which will fit his nature – so I will wait for his arrival), even by engaging in madal. Here madal is thought to be – 1) the greatness of upēyam (goal), i.e., [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/), who must be attained for survival 2) meditating upon the greatness of the upāyam (means), i.e., bhagavān only, which can help one attain the goal 3) the confidence in “the goal is attained only through him” 4) not considering any thing else as upāyam and 5) not being able to wait for attaining emperumān in due course of time. Previously, she said “*madalūrdum*” (I will engage in madal); [parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s friend tells her “you cannot say this; to start with, it is forbidden for women to engage in madal; further more, you are a well-wisher for him even at the cost of hurting yourself as said in sankśēpa rāmāyaṇam bāla kāṇḍam ‘*nityam prāṇa samhitā’* (always focussed on the well-being of her beloved consort); he is more eager to attain you than you desiring to attain him; you are just not patient enough to attain him in due course of time; this adventurous act of yours does not fit your nature” and parṇaguśa nāyaki says “my love towards him is so much that I cannot see these”.
- *yā madal ūrndum* – I will not give up in pursuing him, even at the cost of hurting my own nature.
- *madal ūrndum* – Even if by engaging in this act \[of madal\]. I will attain him even by engaging in forbidden acts. Even by engaging in activity which does not match the meaning of “*aham*” (I). aham in praṇavam is explained in “yām”. ātmā is explained with reference to [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) only \[as bhagavān’s servitor\].
- *em āḻi* … – This is the explanation of the word “*nārāyaṇa*” \[in tirumantram, aśtākśaram\]. bhagavān is explained with reference to ātmā only \[as ātmā’s master\].
- *em* … – Just as he appears with the divine chakra in his hand, I appear with the madal in my hand. When I set out with the madal in my hand, if he places the ornaments in his hands, on my hands and if he places the garland on his shoulder, on my shoulder, he will survive; otherwise everything will be finished.
- *tū madal* – [parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) tells her friend – You look at the garland on my shoulder, I would like to wear a fresh garland.  Her garland is withered due to suffering in separation, and fresh garland is available on [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/).

Her friend says “You can speak like this, but can you do anything about it? Your femininity will block you from engaging in such acts”, parānguśa nāyaki replies,

- *yā madam inṟi* – Oh! let me first do what is done by those who don’t have such femininity \[those who are independent\].
- *teruvu tōṟu …* – Previously she said “*ulagu tōṟu alar tūṟṟi*” (accusing him in all worlds); when all the people of the world assemble, would I just say something about him and leave him? I will go to every street and make everyone aware of his defects by hurling accusations about him to those who don’t know about him. \[inner meaning of going to every street\] People may be thinking that “arcā vigrahams (deities at home) are fully at the disposal of those who worship them \[it is considered as [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s ultimate simplicity\]”, and will I let them continue to think like that? \[I will make everyone realise that emperumān is not truly fulfilling my desire and will drive out their attachment towards arcāvatāra emperumān too\]. *ayal taiyalār* – women who consider them to be independent \[inner meaning – śisupāla et al who consider themselves to be independent from [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)\]; I will make such accusations that \[even\] those women cannot speak anything. emperumān is going to hear those words of accusations which are not even heard from śisupāla et al. Alternative explanation \[*nā madangādē*\] – like the continuous accusations of those who cannot stop their tongues. Another explanation \[*nām adangādē*\] – us, overstepping you, setting out to engage in madal and accusing him.
- *nādum iraikkavē* – If he does not eliminate the “*ūravar kavvai*” (the noisy accusations of the people of the town), I will make him be accused by the whole kingdom. I will ensure that the whole world is tormented. I will ensure that it is known to everyone “a woman tormented a man! \[since\] he did not acknowledge her”. She is setting out to invalidate all the pramāṇams which glorify him and the means to attain him; I will ensure that it is known everywhere “if [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is present, will he let a woman who desired for him suffer like this? This being the case, this universe is devoid of īśvara (lord)”. Would anyone disregard the words of me who united with emperumān previously and believe in the autorless words of vēdam? As I have destroyed the best of pramēyams (goals) \[i.e., emperumān\], how will the best of pramāṇams (authentic texts) have any standing now? I will ensure that the whole world becomes nāstika (non-believers) making them say ‘when this is the result for those who desired emperumān, there is no use of upāsanam \[bhakti yōgam and other such means\]’ “.
- *nādum iraikkavē* *– yāmadalūrndum* – The accusations of the people are those which sustain her. She herself said in [tiruvāimoḻi 5.3.4](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/06/thiruvaimozhi-5-3-4-uravar-kavvai/) “*ūravar kavvai eru*” (the accusations of people of the town are the manure), she sustains by firmly rooting in them.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.3.11. Iraikkum karungadal

*iraikkum karungadal vaṇṇan kaṇṇa pirān tannai viraik koḷ poḻil kurugūrc catakōpan sonna niraik koḷ andādi ōr āyirattuḷ ippattum uraikka vallārkku vaigundam āgum tam ūrellām*

**Пословный перевод:**

iraikkum – noisy due to rising tides; karum kadal – abundant like blackish sea; vaṇṇan – one who is having beautiful form; pirān – one who is of the nature of letting his devotees enjoy such beauty; kaṇṇan tannai – kriṣṇa; viraik koḷ – greatly fragrant; poḻil – having garden; kurugūravar – leader of those who dwell in \[āḻvār\]tirunagari; satakōpan – āḻvār; sonna – mercifully spoke; nirai – Poetic aspects such eḻuttu, asai, sīr, taḷai, adi, todai, pā, isai, tāḷam and other decorative aspects; koḷ – having; andādi – being in andādi \[antam + ādi, a type of poem where the last word of one pāsuram is used as the first word in the next pāsuram\]; ōr – distinguished; āyirattuḷ – among the thousand pāsurams; ippattum – this decad; uraikka vallārkku – for those who can recite just the pāsurams (without understanding anything more); tam – where they are located; Ur ellām – the towns/abodes; vaigundam – to be said as paramapadam; āgum – have bliss

**Перевод:**

**āḻvār, the leader of those who dwell in \[āḻvār\]tirunagari which is having greatly fragrant garden, mercifully spoke about kriṣṇa who is having beautiful form, abundant like blackish sea which is noisy due to rising tides, in this distinguished decad which is having poetic aspects such as eḻuttu, asai, sīr, taḷai, adi, todai, pā, isai, tāḷam and other decorative aspects and is in andādi meter, among the thousand pāsurams; for those who can recite just the pāsurams (without understanding anything more) of this decad, the towns/abodes where they are located are to be said to have the bliss of paramapadam.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In  the end, āḻvār says “In the abodes where there are those who are well versed in reciting this decad, emperumān will himself descend and be eternally together \[with such devotees\]”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār declares the result as “the abode where those who are well versed in reciting this decad, will become paramapadam (spiritual realm)”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. iraikkum karungadal vaṇṇan kaṇṇa pirān tannai viraik koḷ poḻil kurugūrc catakōpan sonna niraik koḷ andādi ōr āyirattuḷ ippattum uraikka vallārkku vaigundam āgum tam ūrellām*

- *iraikkum karum kadal vaṇṇan* – [nanjīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nanjiyar/) came \[from tirunārāyaṇapuram\] and mercifully mentioned to [bhattar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/parasara-bhattar/) saying that he heard this from [anantāḻvān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/ananthazhwan/) – As the ocean heard śrī rāma’s \[angry\] words in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 21.22 “*cāpamānaya*” (Oh lakśmaṇa! bring my arrows), it became greatly agitated; in the same way [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s supremacy got agitated on hearing her firm decision to engage in madal.  vaṇṇan implies one who has such nature.
- *kadal vaṇṇan* – His great beauty which is to pursued even by engaging in madal, is explained here. One who is having an invigorating form like that of an ocean with rising tides.
- *kaṇṇa pirān tannai* – kriṣṇa, who gave that form as a favour to me. Thus his beautiful form and his nature are explained.
- *viraik koḷ poḻil* – As she set out to engage in madal, the town became filled with fragrance of freshly blossomed flowers, expecting his arrival.
- *niraik koḷ andādi* – Though he engages in madal without any specific plan, the various poetic aspects fell in place in the prabandam naturally. As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam bāla kāṇḍam 2.40 “*śōkaśślōkatvamāgata:*” (as the ślōkam followed the śōkam (sorrow)), though śrī rāmāyaṇam was started out of sorrow, by brahmā’s grace, all aspects fell in place for it; similarly, though [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) was grieved and could not even start the prabandam, the prabandam started flowing by [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s grace and thus there is nothing wrong in saying that every poetic aspect fell in place naturally.
- *uraikka vallārkku* – One need not engage in madal, it is sufficient to recite this pāsuram.
- *vaigundam āgum tam ūrellām* – Their target abode is paramapadam. Alternative explanation – not to have them set out to engage in madal to be known by everyone, he himself descends to wherever they are and remains together with them eternally; hence, their abodes can be called as paramapadam. There is nothing wrong in saying that wherever his presence is, that abode is śrīvaikuṇṭam. One cannot doubt “Is it possible to attain this just for \[reciting\] this pāsuram?”; if we consider the qualities of [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) explained in this decad, one can understand that he is of the nature where even this singing is extraneous \[to get his mercy\]; and if he will not show his mercy for reciting this pāsuram, it can be said that there is no use of paripūrṇa āsrayaṇa \[complete surrender – paramabhakti stage\] too; if this is not the case, even puruśōttama can be considered as any other mortal being.

## 5.4 Urellam tunji

## 5.4.1. Urellam tunji

*ūr ellām tunji ulagellām naḷḷiruḷāy nīr ellām tēṟi ōr nīḷ iravāay nīṇḍadāl pār ellām uṇḍa nam pāmbaṇaiyān vārānāl ār ellē valvinaiyēn āvi kāppār iniyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

Ur – the whole town; ellām – everyone; tunji – is sleep; ulagellām – the whole world; naḷ – abundant; iruḷāy – being dark; nīr – water; ellām – all; tēṟi – quiet, without any tides (as the living beings that live in water have slept); ōr – just being night, without any difference between day and night; nīḷ – extended; iravāy – night; nīṇḍadu – stretched so that there appears no end to it; pār – earth which was in danger due to praḷaya (total deluge); ellām – the whole; uṇḍa – one who kept it in his stomach and protected it; pāmbu – tiruvantāḻvān (ādi śēśa), the servitor; aṇaiyān – having as bed and protecting him; nam – one who is the refuge for us; vārān – have not arrived and protected us; ellē – alas!; ini – now, when the protector has not helped; val – very strong (that which cannot be exhausted by experiencing the fruits of); vinaiyēn – I, who am a sinner, my; āvi – ātmā (self); kāppār – protector/saviour; Ar – who?

**Перевод:**

**The whole town is asleep; the whole world is filled with abundant darkness; the water bodies are all quiet, without any tides; there is just night with no difference between day and night, where the night is extended and stretched so that there appears no end to it; emperumān who kept the whole earth which was in danger due to praḷaya, in his stomach and protected it, who is having tiruvantāḻvān, his servitor as his bed and protecting him, who is the refuge for us have not arrived and protected us; alas! now, when the protector has not helped, who is the protector for this ātmā, that is, I who am a sinner who have very strong sins? Will the people of the town who are sleeping help me? Will the world which is consumed by the darkness help me? Will the insentient water help me? ōr will the tormenting and never-ending night help me? ellē implies “ennē”, crying out in suffering.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the first pāsuram – parānguśa nāyaki says “while this dangerous night is going on, emperumān who is the protector when one is in danger, has not arrived. Now, who will be my protector?”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*In the first pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki says “This night is stretching to have the whole universe to be dark, sarvēśvaran who is the protector of all, now who will protect this ātmā?”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*First pāsuram. parānguśa nāyaki says “emperumān who helped during the danger of total deluge, has not helped me during the deluge of separation; now, can I survive?” and gives up attachment in her living. Ur ellām tunji ulagellām naḷḷiruḷāy nīr ellām tēṟi ōr nīḷ iravāay nīṇḍadāl pār ellām uṇḍa nam pāmbaṇaiyān vārānāl Ar ellē valvinaiyēn āvi kāppār iniyē*

- *Ur ellām tunji* – We were hoping to engage in madal having the accusations of the people of the town as the support; now whose accusations will we have as support to engage in madal? It is not just some people are sleeping and others are awake – everyone is fast asleep. When tiruvadi (hanuman) visited lankā, all the rākśasis (demoniac women) were all sleeping there, similarly, all those who hurl accusations were sleeping. Alternative explanation – since it is her birth place, seeing her plight, everyone became sad and were all sleeping in sadness like wild grass had fallen down. When brahmāstram attacked and made everyone lose consciousness in śrī rāma’s army, at least there were śrī jāmbavān, sugrīva mahārāja, tiruvadi (hanuman) who were unharmed and awake; here, even such few people are not awake. Thus, those who hurl accusations (people of the town), those who give advice (mothers) and those good companions (friends) were all sleeping. By this, it is explained that – since everyone is sleeping including those who torment by hurling accusations, [parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s state of not being able to share her thoughts with anyone and spend her time.

Even if the whole town is asleep, when looked around for good companions in the world,

- *ulagellām naḷḷiruḷāy* – As during praḷayam (total deluge), the whole world was just dark. naḷ – middle, abundance. That is midnight darkness, and abundant darkness. Alternative explanation – when everything becomes quiet, the night has an unique sound, “*naḷ iruḷ*” may indicate such state of the night too. Thus, it is explained that there is nothing which is visible to the eyes.
- *nīr ellām tēṟi* – As all the living beings in the water stay deep in sleeping state, the noise became subdued there too. By saying “ūrellām tunji” – it is explained that she does not engage in conversation with some people \[no use of vāk (sensory organ of speech)). By saying “*ulagellām*” – it is explained that she does not have anything \[worthy\] for her vision and does not spend her time seeing anything \[worldly\].  *nīrellām tēṟi* implies that there is nothing worthy available for her hearing to start with. This is a sample for all her senses – that there is nothing worthy in this world for the consumption of her senses. Since the senses would be active in the morning in their own activities, the anguish is less; but in the night, as they are fully focussed on [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is separated from her, the anguish is unbearable.
- *ōr nīḷiravāy nīṇḍadāl* – Even previously, there were times when the night was felt very long, yet day and night will occur in a cycle; now it feels like unending night.
- *nīṇḍadāl* – The nights of dēvas (celestial beings) are longer than the nights of manuśyas (humans) – yet, even those dēvas’ nights have an end; here it is endless.
- *pār ellām uṇḍa* – During the great danger of total deluge, he protected everyone without any discrimination. It appears the collective danger faced by everyone during total deluge, is singularly faced by [parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/). During deluge too, During deluge, does [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) only help those who set out to engage in madal and give up being unable to do so? No, he helps anyone who cannot protect themselves.
- *nam pāmbaṇaiyān* – One who gives his body to those who consider him very dear. One who is having tiruvanantāḻvān (ādi śēśan) as his bed. parānguśa nāyaki says we are neither like aspruśta samsāragandar (one who is not touched by samsāram – the nityasūris) nor like samsāris (worldly people). He lets the nityasūris enjoy him eternally; he protects the samsāris when they are in danger though they don’t request for help, due to his \[natural\] relationship with everyone.
- *nam* – She is saying “*nam*” (Our – with proximity), since he first united, and gave her what was required to call him.
- *vārānāl* – You need not protect me by keeping me in your stomach, you need not embrace me, just come and show your face to me. śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 83.9 “*druśta ēvahi naśśōkamapanēśyatirāghava: – tamassarvasyalōkasya samudyannivabhāskara:*” (Just like the rising sun will dispel the darkness of the world, śrī rāma will dispel our sorrows as soon as we see him).
- *ini* – now
- *āvi kāppār Ar* – Shall I who is in danger like being caught in deluge, rescue myself? Should my friend who suffer for my result even before me, as said in tiruvāimoḻi 9.9.5 “*emmin mun avanukku māyvarālō*“, rescue me? Should the mother who give good advice protect me? ōr should the people of the town who hurl accusations protect me?
- *ellē* – Saying “alas!” out of amazement, or it can be said as [parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) calling out her friend. Though parānguśa nāyaki says subsequently “*annaiyarum tōḻiyarum*” (mothers and friends) highlighting that the friends too will be sleeping, considering the dangerous situation she is in, she thinks that her friend will be awake and hence calling her out.
- *val vinaiyēn* – I have committed great sin that even [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is sarvarakśaka (protector of all) and who does not separate from those who embrace him, is not coming and helping me.
- *val vianaiyēn āvi* – My self which is destined to live for 100 years even while being separated; she is thinking “is this [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) which is not becoming weakened even after being separated, going to finish?”. The protector has not arrived, my friend is more anguished than me, now, are those harmful ones (the ones who hurl accusations), the protectors?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

adiyen saraty ramanuja dasan

## 5.4.2. Avi kappar

*āvi kāppār iniyār? āḻ kadal maṇ viṇ mūdi māvikāramāy ōr val iravāy nīṇḍadāl kāvi sēr vaṇṇan en kaṇṇanum vārānāl pāviyēn nenjamē! nīyum pāngallaiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

āḻ – deep; kadal – ocean; maṇ – earth; viṇ – sky; mūdi – covering; mā – huge; vikāramāy – having a well developed state; val – dense (even many suns cannot break the darkness); ōr iravāy – lengthy night filled with darkness; nīṇḍadu – extended without an end; kāvi – with neydal (blue nelumbo) flower; sēr – matching; vaṇṇan – having complexion; en – obedient to have such complexion as my wealth; kaṇṇanum – kriṣṇa; vārān – have not come so far; pāviyēn – one who is having sins (which makes the obedient kriṣṇa to disobey me), my; nenjamē – oh heart!; nīyum – you too; pāngallai – are not favourable; ini – when kriṣṇa, the protector is not helping and you, the companion are not helping; āvi – my life; kāppār – protector; Ar – who?

**Перевод:**

**The lengthy night filled with darkness which is covering the deep ocean, the earth, the sky and which is having a well developed state and is very dense, extended without an end; kriṣṇa who is having a complexion which matches neydal flower and who is obedient to have such complexion as my wealth, have not come so far; oh heart of a sinner (me)! you are not favourable; when kriṣṇa, the protector is not helping and you, the companion are not helping, who is the protector for my life?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the second pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki says “In such state of mine, even kriṣṇa is not coming, and due to being related to I who am a great sinner, oh heart! you too are not obedient towards me”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, parānguśa nāyaki says to her heart “kriṣṇa who revealed his beautiful form and became obedient, is not coming; oh heart! you too are not obedient towards me, now who will save my life?”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. āvi kāppār iniyār? āḻ kadal maṇ viṇ mūdi māvikāramāy ōr val iravāy nīṇḍadāl kāvi sēr vaṇṇan en kaṇṇanum vārānāl pāviyēn nenjamē! nīyum pāngallaiyē*

- *āvi kāppār iniyār* – One who is supposed to help, has not helped; the heart too became unfavourable; now who is the protector/saviour? kriṣṇa has not come, and oh heart! you too are not favourable – who will save my life?
- *āḻ kadal* … – The objects which are pervading (i.e., the five great elements) are covered by one of those objects which is pervaded (tamas – darkness). The immeasurable ocean, the earth which supports all objects, the ether which gives space to earth – covering all of these.
- *mā vikāramāy* – (the darkness) Subsequently, not stopping with that, having great growth, appeared to be aiming to cover even the nitya vibhūti (spiritual realm). It is attempting do what is done by the omnipotent [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) while manifesting the viśvarūpam (universal form).
- *ōr val iravāy* – Since she is unable to have the intelligence to distinguish between the night and darkness, she is highlighting darkness as night.
- *ōr val iravāy* – It is so densely dark that, even emperumān sends his divine sudarśana chakra to cut the darkness, it cannot be broken.
- *nīṇḍadāl* – unable to see the end.
- *kāvi sēr vaṇṇan* – Having the complexion as explained in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 5.3.8 “*pullēndīvarapatrāpam*” (one who is having the complexion of blossomed blue nelumbo flower). He is said to be having a divine form with dark complexion as in periya tiruvantādi 26 “*iruḷ anna mā mēni*“. He can come like those who wear dark clothes to conceal their identity and comes.
- *en kaṇṇan* – One who came in the dark and helped, where kamsa had his evil assistants \[waiting for him\]. periya tirumoḻi 7.5.1 “*naḷ irutkaṇ vanda endai perumānār*” (my father and great lord who arrived in the midnight darkness).
- *vārānāl* – Would it not be good if [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who comes to destroy tāmasa prakruti (demoniac persons), come and destroy tamas (darkness) itself? If he arrives, that will lead to her dawn at once. It is said in iraṇḍām tiruvantādi 81 “*pagal kaṇḍēn nāraṇanaik kaṇḍēn*” (I saw the day (brightness) which implies seeing śrīman nārāyaṇa).
- *pāviyēn nenjamē* – You too are similar to him. He did not help me not because of lacking the ability to help, but due to being related to me and being embraced by me – you too have both the qualifications \[so you are also not going to help me\].
- *nīyum pāngallaiyē* – Though you both have some similarity, would it not be nice if you there were some differences \[i.e., even if he did not help, at least you could help\]? Should you who are naturally dependent behave like [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is independent but assume dependency \[due to romantic mood\]? If he gives up his romantic mood, he will be left with fully independent attitude only, but that is not the case for you \[because you are naturally dependent\]. When there are two obedient entities \[emperumān and the heart\], if one \[emperumān\] becomes disobedient, should the other entity \[my heart\] too become disobedient? Here, emperumān and her heart are mentioned \[and to be recited\] in the same tone in “*en kaṇṇanum vārānāl*” and “*en nenjamē*“.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.4.3. Niyum pangallai

*nīyum pāngallai kāṇ nenjamē! nīḷiravum ōyum poḻidilllai ūḻiyāy nīṇḍadāl kāyum kadunjilai en kāguttan vārānāl māyum vagai aṟiyēn val vinaiyēn peṇ piṟandē*

**Пословный перевод:**

nenjamē – Oh heart!; niyum – you who are the main cause for all actions; pāngu allai – are not obedient; nīḷ – already extending; iravum – night; ōyum poḻudu – ending time; inṟi – not having; ūḻiyāy – like a kalpa (a day of brahmā); nīṇḍadu – stretched; kāyum – roasting the enemies of his devotees; kadu – cruel; silai – having śrī śārnga \[divine bow\]; en kāguttan – \[kākutsta\] śrī rāma, cakravarti tirumangan (divine son of emperor daśarata), who is born in the family heritage which gives great importance to helping others; vārān – has not helped me like he helped sītā, the divine daughter of king śrī janaka; val vinaiyēn – I who am having great sins (which stop even emperumān from helping); peṇ – woman (who does not even have the independence to kill herself); piṟandu – having been born; māyum vagai – ways to finish myself; aṟiyēn – I don’t know

**Перевод:**

**Oh heart! you, the main cause for all actions, are not obedient; the already extending night is not having the ending time and is appearing to be stretched like a kalpa; śrī rāma, cakravarti tirumangan who is having the cruel śrī śārnga \[bow\] which roasts the enemies of his devotees and who is born in the family heritage which gives great importance to helping others, has not helped me like he helped sītā, the divine daughter of king śrī janaka; I who am having great sins, having been born as a woman, don’t know the ways to finish myself.**

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the third pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki becomes sad thinking “kākutsta (śrī rāma) who is of the nature of eliminating all sorrows and uplifting, has not come; and I, being a dependent, do not know the means to finish myself”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. nīyum pāngallai kāṇ nenjamē! nīḷiravum ōyum poḻidilllai ūḻiyāy nīṇḍadāl kāyum kadunjilai en kāguttan vārānāl māyum vagai aṟiyēn val vinaiyēn peṇ piṟandē*

- *nīyum pāngallai kāṇ nenjamē* – śrī rāma, after reaching the other side of gangā, saw iḷaiya perumāḷ (lakśmaṇa) and told him “Son! you too go back to our capital (ayōdyā)”, being bewildered that he can complete his vanavāsam (exile from the kingdom to the forest) without him; similarly, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying to his divine heart “*nīyum pāngallai kāṇ*” (you too are not obedient towards me). As said in “*mana Eva …*” (mind (heart) is the cause for one’s bondage and liberation), he can attain everything only with the help of his heart. Still, out of sadness, āḻvār is saying this.
- *nīḷ iravu* … – Initially, it was just lengthy night; subsequently, it became endless. It appeared to be both without a beginning and endless. There are some cases where there would have been a beginning which ceased to exist (like creating a product from a raw material – the raw material existed before but is gone now), but yet is endless – this night is not like that \[there was no beginning to start with\].
- *ūḻiyāy* – Ordinary persons such as “*sāttan, kūttan*” (common names), when they acquire wealth, they will leave aside their common names and will live with special titles such as “*cōḻak kōnār, toṇḍamānār*” (respectable names); in the same way, the night acquired the name “kalpam”  (a day of brahmā).
- *nīṇḍadāl* – Even for the kalpa, there is an end, but there is no end for this \[night\].
- *kāyum kadum silai* … – Even the one who has the strength of the bow which eliminated the lengthy night of a woman (sītāp pirātti), has not come. One who is having the bow which roasts the enemies, which would show no mercy towards the enemies even if perumāḷ (śrī rāma) wants to show mercy. I have not seen his śāngam (bow, favouritism) towards me.
- *en kāguttan* – [parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) considers his help to sītāp pirātti as help to her own self. Even the one she considered as refuge as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 3.6.8](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/09/thiruvaimozhi-3-6-8-thuyarame-tharu/) “*tayarataṟku magan tannai anṟi maṟṟilēn tanjam*” (I will not have anyone other than the divine son of daśarata as my refuge), has not come. [tiruppāvai 12](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2014/12/thiruppavai-12-kanaiththilam-karrerumai/) “*sinattināl …*” (out of anger) – while eliminating the hurdles/enemies of pirātti, instead of thinking that he is doing a favour to her, he considers him having his own anger subdued \[by killing the demons\].
- *kāguttan* – Previously, she said “*kaṇṇanum vārānāl*” (kriṣṇa has not come); that son of king who was not crowned, did not come \[kriṣṇa coming in the clan of yayāti, where yayāti refused to crown his son \[who is the ancestor of kriṣṇa\] for not helping him\]; but I was not helped by even those who are born in the family of crowned kings who have protected others. Even the descendant of kakutstaa has not come \[kakutsta is well known to have helped others\].
- *vārānāl* – The one who does not wait for enemies to come to him and rather would go to his enemies, has not come. śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 1.29 is explained here. *abhiyātā* – He considers it his duty to go to the enemies’ place \[to defeat them\] instead of waiting for them to come. *prahartā ca* – While standing in the front row of the battle field, when asked “who will hit first?”, that will be his (śrī rāma’s). *sēnānaya viśārada:* – Even while he is not physically present, he is able to arrange the army perfectly, and win the battle easily.
- *māyum vagai aṟiyēn* – After knowing that he has not come, the only way to attain joy is by finishing myself, but I do not know how to do it.
- *val vinaiyēn* – I have committed such sin that, I cannot even attain death, if such death is considered joyful. How strange that, my sin is making me live instead of making me die! It is only my sin which is causing this unfavourable state for me that makes both living and dying difficult to attain.
- *peṇ piṟandē* – Is it possible to dies as and when they desire, having been born in a dependent birth? I have committed great sin to be born in this female birth, where one is to live for others. It is said in mahābhāratam “*pāpānāmākarasstriya:*” (this female form is considered as embodiment of sins). śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 36.30 is explained here. *nacāsya mātā* – After sītāp pirātti saw tiruvadi (hanuman), out of praṇaya rōśam (romantic anger) towards [perumāḷ (śrī rāma)](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), considering hanuman to be sent by him, she spoke to hanuman angrily;  hanuman pacified her saying “only due to not knowing the location of your highness, śrī rāma did not come for your rescue. It is not due to lack of attachment towards you; you can only blame him if he delays coming to you even after knowing your location”; further hanuman said “it has been ten months since you separated from him, you too have survived until now, without finishing yourself”.  sītā said “Oh! is that what you think? Now listen to me. For people, their attachment would be split among many entities such as mother, father, brother, relatives; but perumāḷ has all those attachment towards me; so he will do whatever it takes like building a bridge across the ocean etc and will come to me seeking for me like a thirsty person crying ‘water! water!’; when a thirsty person arrives in a water shelter with great difficulty and finds the water pots broken he will not survive; similarly, if he arrives here only to find me dead, he will not live either; so, I sustained myself for him. You can make this statement, only if you see me alive after meeting him”. *dūta* – previously, she addressed hanuman as “*vānara*” (monkey) etc, and now her anger is turned towards hanuman \[dūta – [śrī rāma](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s messenger\] and said “you are sent by śrī rāma \[so you too would have the same attitude\]”.
- *val vinaiyēn peṇ piṟandē – māyum vagai aṟiyēn* – One can as and when they desire, if they are men like daśarata, bhīśma et al; either jñānavān (very wise) \[like bhīśma\] or svatantra (one who considers themselves to be independent) \[like daśarata\] to die as and when they desire; would it be possible for ignorant persons who are born as women?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.4.4. Pen pirandar

*peṇ piṟandār eydum perum tuyar kāṇgilēn enṟu oṇsudarōn vārādoḷittān im maṇṇaḷanda kaṇ periya sevvāy em kārēṟu vārānāl eṇ periya sindai nōy tīrppārār ennaiyē?*

**Пословный перевод:**

peṇ – as a female; piṟandār – born; eydum – gets; perum tuyar – unbearable great sorrow; kāṇgilēn – unable to witness; enṟu – saying so; oṇ – attractive during the time of dawn; sudarōn – radiant sun; vārādu – not coming; oḷittān – hid himself (so that he is not found, even if searched for); i – this; maṇ – earth; aḷanda – as a result of joy due to measuring it to keep it for himself; periya – vast; kaṇ – divine eyes; sem – reddish; vāy – having divine lips; em – (like that earth, with his beautiful features) making us exist exclusively for him; kār – having cloud like blackish form; ēṟu – trivikrama who appears like a prideful bull (having accomplished his desired task); vārān – has not come; periya – great (to be out of reach, not conceivable through speech and mind); sindai nōy – mental anguish; ennai – me; tīrppār – will eliminate; Ar – who?

**Перевод:**

**The radiant sun which is attractive during the time of dawn is not coming and hid himself saying that he cannot witness the unbearable great sorrow one gets being born as female; trivikrama who appears like a prideful bull, who is having vast divine eyes and reddish divine lips as a result of the joy of measuring the earth to keep it for himself, who is having cloud like blackish form, has not come; who will eliminate the great mental anguish of mine which is beyond the conception of thoughts?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fourth pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki says “While I am suffering so much that it cannot be tolerated by anyone who sees that, emperumān who divinely measured the worlds to remove the dangers of everyone, has not arrived. Who will eliminate my endless mental suffering?”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, parānguśa nāyaki says “trivikraman emperumān looks prideful with beautiful features due to the joy of having measured the earth which he desired to; who will remove my endless mental suffering now?”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. peṇ piṟandār eydum perum tuyar kāṇgilēn enṟu oṇsudarōn vārādoḷittān im maṇṇaḷanda kaṇ periya sevvāy em kārēṟu vārānāl eṇ periya sindai nōy tīrppārār ennaiyē?*

- *peṇ piṟandār* … – Saying that I cannot witness the great sorrow experienced by women who are naturally dependent and hence unable to kill themselves, and being tender natured and hence unable to bear the separation.
- *oṇ sudarōn vārādu oḷittān* – While sarvarakśaka (protector of all) can witness \[tolerate\] such sufferings, can one (sun) who is engaged in a small act of protection, witness that? While puruśōttaman (supreme lord) can witness that, can a puruśa (sun, a mortal being) witness that? Even the sun who can dispel sorrows just by his arrival, hid himself and did not show up. Instead of saying “vandilan” (has not come), it is said “*oḷittān*” (hid himself) – this is because, as said in taittirīya upaniśat “*bhīśāsmāt vāta:pavatē*” (fearing [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s orders, wind is blowing), due to bhagavān’s orders, he should be circling every day \[present every day\]; such sun too thinks “If I violate bhagavān’s orders, they may cut my head, which is even alright in comparison to seeing this suffering of the women in separation” and hides himself from the servitors of bhagvān when they come searching for him. periya tirumoḻi 8.5.2 “*oḷiyavan visumbiyangum tērum pōyiṟṟu*”  (the chariot of the sun which travels in the sky, disappeared). It disappeared in such a manner that it’s arrival is not to be guessed; as said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 5.18.31 “*sōbhirēṇur na lakśyatē*” (even the dust (of the chariot) is not visible) and in periya tirumoḻi 9.4.6 “*suḻanṟilangu vem katirōn tērodum pōy maṟaindān*” (the revolving hot sun disappeared with his chariot).
- *im maṇ aḷanda* – What suffering engulfed the earth, which made him measure it and accept it? Is the suffering caused by mahābali to the earth a match for the suffering caused by the night to me? [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who protects without discriminating any one.
- *kaṇ periya sevvāy …* – Out of his mercy, assuming a huge form and measuring the earth, mercifully showering his cool glance to eliminate the anguish of the dwellers of the earth, and smiling out of joy due to such acts – and thus manifesting his reddish lips.
- *em* – One who is having as his nature, the protection given for all.
- *kār* – Having his natural complexion, due to protecting them.
- *ēṟu* – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who pridefully thinks that “doing all of this, is a benefit for me”, has not come. She is saying “*em*” (our) to indicate that she is also part of the protected persons by the sarvarakśaka (protector of all). When it is recited as “*en*” (my), it implies – one who has acquired his natural complexion as a resulting of being united with me previously.
- *vārānāl* – He need not beg from me; he need not measure the world, he just needs to manifest his form in front of me.
- *eṇ periya sindai nōy* – Until now, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) spoke about bhagavat viśayam (matters about [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)) which is given up to be impossible to speak about by vēdāntam as said in kēnōpaniśat “*yasyāmatam tasya matam*” (one who thinks he knows does not know); but his own mental anguish (suffering in separation) is difficult to conceive even with the unblemiśed knowledge acquired by the blessings of bhagavān. It can only be said as “*eṇ periyadu*” (difficult to conceive in the mind) and cannot be said “how much”. The mental anguish will match the entity \[bhagavān\] from whom she is separated. Since bhagavān has no boundary, the anguish acquired in separation from him also has no boundary. śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 5.13.21 and 5.13.22 “*tataprāpti mahādu:kha*” (Having acquired great sorrow due to not attaining kriṣṇa, citayantī was relieved of all her sins).
- *sindai nōy tīrppār Ar* – All I need is to have this mental anguish eliminated, even if it means forgetting [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), it is fine. These \[āḻvārs\] are of the nature to say as in periya tirumoḻi 9.3.3 “*ēdu seydāl maṟakkēn*” (What can I do to forget him?); it does no matter we remember him or forget him, we need to get the anguish eliminated. Here, saying “forget him” is not done with desire, but only to highlight the great anguish. In separation, the remembrance of emperumān will increase the suffering as seen in tiruvāimoḻi 9.5.8 “*kaṇṇan nāmamē kuḻaṟik konṟīr*” (you recited kriṣṇa’s name and killed me) and in tiruvāimoḻi 9.5.7 “*kāttēnmin num uru em uyirkkadu kālan*” (Do not show your form, as that is death to my life).
- *ennaiyē* – This anguish is unique to this [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) (me) alone. People (bhakti yōga followers) can meditate upon him and eliminate their anguish; it is possible for those who engage in bhakti considering it as the means \[to attain him\], since such smruti (remembrance) is ordained in śāstram as in bruhadāraṇyaka upaniśat “*nididyāsitavya:*” (to be constantly meditated upon); but for those who are fully immersed in his nature/form, this situation \[suffering in separation\] is present.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.4.5. Ar ennai

*ār ennai ārāyvār annaiyarum tōḻiyarum nīr ennē ennādē nīḷiravum tunjuvarāl kār anna mēni nam kaṇṇanum vārānāl pēr ennai māyādāl val vinaiyēn pin ninṟē*

**Пословный перевод:**

annaiyarum – mothers (who protect with affection); tōḻiyarum – friends (who protect due to well-wishing heart); nīr – her condition; ennē – how is it; ennādē – instead of determining; nīḷ – lengthy; iravum – the whole night; tunjuvar – are sleeping; kār anna – like a dark cloud (which is having the quality to greatly help others); mēni – having a divine form; nam – one who is obedient towards us; kaṇṇanum – kriṣṇa too; vārān – has not come to protect; val vinaiyēn – for me who is having very strong sins (which stops even those who protect, not to protect); pin – behind; ninṟu – standing; pēr – for name sake; ennai – me; māyādu – not allowing to die; ennai – me; ārāyvār – one who protects; Ar – who?

**Перевод:**

**the mothers and friends are sleeping through the whole lengthy night instead of determining her (my) condition; kriṣṇa too, who is having a dark cloud like divine form and who is obedient towards us, has not come to protect; standing behind me, the very strong sins are not allowing me to die and making me exist only for name sake; this being the case, who will protect me? Implies – no one. Implies that – her state of just being present for name sake even in dire situations reveals just her eternal nature.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fifth pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki says “The friends and mothers who help in difficult times, are not concerned about me and kriṣṇa who helps even when they give up, has not come. Now, I exist only for name sake”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, parānguśa nāyaki says “kriṣṇa who has a form which manifests his helping tendency has not come; I exist only for name sake, who will protect me?”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. Ar ennai ārāyvār annaiyarum tōḻiyarum nīr ennē ennādē nīḷiravum tunjuvarāl kār anna mēni nam kaṇṇanum vārānāl pēr ennai māyādāl val vinaiyēn pin ninṟē*

- *Ar ennai ārāyvār* – śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 116.40 “*dāsīnām rāvaṇasyāham marśayāmīhadurbalā*” (I, the fearless, forgive the mistakes of rāvaṇa’s servants) – when tiruvadi (hanuman) set out to harm the rākśasis (demoniac maid-servants of rāvaṇa), sītāp pirātti asked him “1) since these rākśasis were fully dependent on rāvaṇa and harmed me based on his orders, or 2) even if they harmed me out of their own will, but since I have said ‘I have forgiven you all’ and given them refuge, how can you harm them?”; hanuman asked “as rāvaṇa is killed now \[we need not fear anymore\], why should these evil women who harmed you for so long, be forgiven now?”; \[and sītā said\] *durbalā* – just because some one harmed us before, if we harm them back, what will those who see their pathetic state do? After rāvaṇa’s death and perumāḷ (śrī rāma) becoming victorious , they have already become weakened (both physically and mentally). sītāp pirātti who gave refuge to even those who harmed her, as stated in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 58.90 “*bavēyam śaraṇam hiva:*” (I will protect you all), is looking for a saviour and saying “who will protect me?” \[Here, [parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is compared to sītāp pirātti – there pirātti gave protection to others, here pirātti is seeking protection from others\].
- *annaiyarum tōḻiyarum* – Both those who lost their sleep on seeing my state (friends) and those who condemn me saying “you cannot lose sleep over this” (mothers). Both of those who follow my thoughts (friends) and those who have their own ideas and hence ordering me (mothers) are not helping me.
- *annaiyarum tōḻiyarum nīr ennai ennādē nīḷ iravum tunjuvarāl* -There are some who say that “*tunjuvarāl*” (sleeping) implies “*tunjudirāl*” (sleeping, in a slightly different tone). \[nīr is explained as “you”\] They are not asking \[with care\] “*ennē*” (how is this?) or “*en pattāy*” (what happened to you?). Alternative explanation – \[nīr is explained as nīrmai – svabhāvam – nature\] Mothers and friends are not asking me “why are you like this?” \[They should have asked\]. Even after his leaving her and engaging in other activities and forgetting her, you are not engaging in anything other than him! How amazing! \[When asked “Does nīr imply nīrmai?”, nampiḷḷai quotes kuṟaḷ 782\] “*niṟai nīra nīravar kēṇmai piṟaimadip pinnīra pēdaiyār natpu*” (The friendship of the wise waxes like the full moon; (but) that of fools wanes like the new moon).
- *nīḷ iravum tunjuvarāl* – Just as sleeplessness is my nature, sleeping the whole lengthy night is their nature.
- *kār anna mēni* – One who is having a cool form like a heavy rainfall on a drought-hit land, and one who has helped previously as said in śrī bhāgavatam “*tāsāmāvirabhūt* …” (he appeared amidst the gōpikās), has not come. *tāsām* (for those girls) is said based on their previous state \[of longing for him\].
- *nam kaṇṇanum vārānāl* – Even the one who always helped girls, has not come.
- *pēr ennai māyādāl* – My name does not match [bhagavān’s](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/). He is not coming and my name is not going. Though I am finished, my name is making me still exist. Just as [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s divine name is that which sustains the śrīvaiṣṇavas, he too is sustained by his name. Since the name has “*adi*” (bhagavān’s divine feet, bhagavān’s blessing), it will sustain everyone. Everyone accepts this \[śatāri\] on his head due to this reason.
- *pēr ennai māyādāl* – just living for name sake.
- *val vinaiyēn* – I have committed great sins to have a name which does not let me die even after physically having died.
- *pin ninṟu* – Even while I die, this name remains after me and does not let me die fully. As they (name and form) come along during birth, should they not be finished at the time of death? They are recited together as in cāndōjña upaniśat 6.3 “*nāma rūpē vyākaravāṇi*” (Let me create names and forms), śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 1.5.63 “*nāma rūpam ca bhūtānām*” ([paramātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) gave names and forms to the many creatures). Those who came first, should go first too, but why are they not going even later?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.4.6. Pin ninra

*pin ninṟa kādal nōy nenjam peritadumāl munninṟirā ūḻi kaṇ pudaiya mūdiṟṟāl manninṟa cakkarattu em māyavanum vārānāl inninṟa nīḷāvi kāppār ār ivvidattē*

**Пословный перевод:**

pin – following; ninṟa – not leaving; kādal – love; nōy – disease; nenjam – heart (which is its originating place); peritu – very; adum – destroyed; mun – in front; ninṟu – standing; irā – night; ūḻi – kalpa (day of brahma, eon); kaṇ – eye \[vision\]; pudaiya – to cover; mūdiṟṟu – concealed; manninṟa – present eternally (to eliminate the enemies of devotees); cakkaram – being the one with divine \[sudarśana\] chakra (disc); em māyavanum – kriṣṇa who made himself as our wealth by manifesting his amazing qualities; vārān – has not come; ninṟa – that which is not weakened even after experiencing sorrows eternally; en – my; nīḷ – eternal; i – this; āvi – ātmā (soul); ivvidattu – in this situation; kāppār – protector; Ar – who?

**Перевод:**

**The love disease is following without leaving me and is destroying the heart; the night which is like a kalpa, is standing in front of me to conceal my vision by covering my eye; kriṣṇa who made himself as our wealth by manifesting his amazing qualities, who is eternally with divine chakra, has not come; in this situation who is the protector for this eternal ātmā which is not weakened even after experiencing sorrows eternally.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the sixth pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki says “While I am suffering in separation and the night is on, who will protect me who is unable to die, if emperumān who is the protector does not come?”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, parānguśa nāyaki says “While my love and the night torture me, emperumān who has firm tools for protection has not arrived, who will protect my ātmā?”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. pin ninṟa kādal nōy nenjam peritadumāl munninṟirā ūḻi kaṇ pudaiya mūdiṟṟāl manninṟa cakkarattu em māyavanum vārānāl inninṟa nīḷāvi kāppār Ar ivvidattē*

- *pin ninṟa kādal nōy* – The love disease which follows everywhere and tortures. There is no shade where one can take shelter and rest \[it follows everywhere\].
- *nenjam peridadumāl* – It is severely tormenting the heart. \[Why is the heart instead of body mentioned to be tormented by the disease first?\] Fire will first burn the internals and then burn the externals \[in same cases\]; similarly, the disease hurts the place where it remains \[love is in the heart\] very much.
- *mun ninṟu* … – It appears that the love disease and the night have discussed with each other and are tormenting me together. They both come like those who say “I will come and attack him from behind and you attack him from the front side”. When the enemy is weak, some will insult them by grabbing their bow etc; similarly, seeing my helpless nature, the night which appears like an eon, conceals the vision, standing in front. Internal vision was covered by the love disease and the external vision was covered by the night.
- *kaṇ pudaiya mūdiṟṟāl* – The sense of vision which grasps and reveals \[other objects\] is covered by the darkness which is one of the grasped entities. Alternative explanation – the eon of night covers the vision in a manner that even if [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is having dark complexion appears in front, he cannot be seen.
- *manninṟa* … – As said in periya tiruvantādi 87 “*eppōdum kai kaḻalā nēmiyān*” ([emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) whose chakra is never separated from his hand), it is not that emperumān searches for his weapons when his devotees are faced with enemies, he has the chakra readily available with him.
- *em māyavanum* – The amazing [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who can invite darkness using his chakra which is the source of radiance \[kriṣṇa hid the sun using his chakra to bring out jayadrada to have him killed by arjuna\]. For the one who can bring about the nivartyam \[that which is to be eliminated – darkness\] using nivartakam \[that which eliminates – brightness which eliminates darkness\], is it not possible to use nivartakam \[here, chakra\] to eliminate the nivartyam \[darkness\]?
- *vārānāl* – Here, his vow need not be broken \[like in the case of mahābhārata battle, where he took up arms after vowing not to do so\], just he needs to desire to come. As said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 4.6](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/4-6/) “*sambhavāmi ātma māyayā*” (I incarnate out of my own desire), just desiring to come is sufficient. No need to pick up arms after vowing not to do so or no need to break the limit by driving out darkness using brightness, but he just needs to come; by the nature of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), darkness will automatically disappear.
- *in ninṟa nīḷ āvi kāppār Ar* – Who will kill this [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) and protect it, when it tries to live fully when it is at the state of death? \[Since it is eternal\] ātmā started debating citing [śrī bhagavat gītā 2.24](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/2-24/) “*accēdyōyamadāhyōyam*” (ātmā cannot be cut, it cannot be burnt). A tamiḻ scholar observed these harsh words “Who will kill this ātmā and protect me?” and had written a verse explaining the same meaning in tamiḻ “*pirivilum mudiyāda en uyirp pagaiyai nīkki ennai nōkkuvār Ar?*” (Who will destroy the enemy of my life which stops me from dying in separation and save me?).
- *ivvidattē* – In this situation when even [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is the sarvarakśaka (protector of all) does not help, giving up my life and be protected is the joy.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.4.7. Kappar ar

*kāppār ār ivvidattuk kangiruḷin nuṇ tuḷiyāyc cētpāla tūḻiyāyc celginṟa kangul vāyt tūppāla veṇ sangu cakkarattan tōnṟānāl tīppāla val vinaiyēn deyvangāḷ en seygēnō?*

**Пословный перевод:**

ivvidattu – in this condition (when the protector is not helping); kāppār – protector; Ar – who?; kangu – abundant to be in the ultimate state; iruḷ – darkness; nuṇ – tiny; tuḷi – misty droplet; āy – having; sēṇ – very lengthy; pāladu – having the nature; ūḻiyāy – kalpa (eon); selginṟa – passing; kangulvāy – in the night; tū – pure; pāla – having nature; veṇ – white; sangu – śrīpāncajanya; cakkarattan – one who is having divine sudarśana chakra; tōnṟān – not appearing; tī – like fire; pāla – burning nature; val – very strong; vinaiyēn – I, who am having sins; deyvangāḷ – Oh dēvatās (who are watching my suffering without even blinking the eyes); en – what; seygēn – shall do?

**Перевод:**

**Who is my protector in this condition? emperumān who is having divine śudarśana chakra and pure white śrīpāncajanya is not appearing in this very lengthy passing night which is like a kalpa having abundant darkness and tiny misty droplets; Oh dēvatās! What shall I, who am having very strong sins which are burning like fire, do?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the seventh pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki feeling helpless since emperumān did not arrive even as the eon like night was passing, looking at the dēvatās who are animiśars (who don’t blink their eyes), considering them to be related, not sleeping and being merciful, says to them “deyvangāḷ en seygēn” (Oh dēvatās! what will I do!”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, parānguśa nāyaki calls out to those sleepless dēvatās “what will I do in this very dark night”, when sarvēśvaran who has attractive distinguished symbols does not arrive.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. kāppār Ar ivvidattuk kangiruḷin nuṇ tuḷiyāyc cētpāla tūḻiyāyc celginṟa kangul vāyt tūppāla veṇ sangu cakkarattan tōnṟānāl tīppāla val vinaiyēn deyvangāḷ en seygēnō?*

- *kāppār Ar ivvidattu* – While the real protector is not helping, in this condition, will those who harm us, be protectors? Her state/condition is so pitiable that she, who would never ever think about other persons as protectors even if he delays his arrival, is saying these words. śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 39.30 is explained here. *śaraistu sankulām krutvālankām –* tiruvadi (hanuman) asked \[sītā\] pirātti “Should you not go to perumāḷ (śrī rāma) now?”; sītā replies “I can only go there when this lankā which is filled with rākśasas (demons) becomes filled with the arrows of śrī rāma; how can I go to him when seen by others? *parapurārdana: –* Is there any town which survived after earning his enmity? *māmnayētyadi* – Will the one who said in śrī varāha carama ślōkam “*nayāmi paramām gatim*” (I will bring him to higher abode), say two different things \[“I will protect” and “I won’t protect”\]? *kākutsta:* – Will the one who is born as a descendant of those \[kakutsta, one of the brave ancestors of śrī rāma\] who eliminated the enemies of indra et al, be helpless in his own matter? *tattasya sadruśam bhavēt* – Can we who do what is not matching his nature and die, do what will cause disrepute to to him, just to eliminate our suffering? It will be an insult to his abilities if it happened to be “A rākśasa separated śrī rāma’s consort, she cursed him and returned” or “a monkey brought her back”; is it not an insult to his heritage? Should I do what was done by rāvaṇa? Those who take up his responsibility of his protectorśip, will be considered to be the same as those who consider śrī rāma’s wealth to be one’s own. [parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) who is generally fearless even in fear infusing situation, out of great suffering became fearful and spoke these words \[kāppār Ar?\]. śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 60.20 “*gajam vētyāni nāhāra yati santrāsam*” (As sītā was under the shelter of śrī rāma, she did not fear seeing the herds of elephants, lions and tigers) – her true nature of strītvam (femininity \[i.e., being fearful\]) disappeared. *bāhūrāmasyasamśritā* – Will those who are in a fort, fear even when there is reason to fear? The current situation \[suffering in separation\] is not just like seeing herds of elephants/lions \[it is much more than that\].
- *kāppār Ar ivvidattu* – It is the same [parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) \[originally, as [nammāḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)\] who clearly knew “this is the protected entity \[[ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)\]; this is the protector \[[īśvara](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)\]” and was pridefully roaring “*amma*” (joyful cry), is now saying “who is the protector?” fearfully; it is the severity of the suffering. His sarvarakśakatvam \[protecting everying\] is present in “*accu*” (in a clear singular form, “a” in praṇavam); she is suffering in “*allu*” (night, hal letter in samskrutam – i.e., “ma” in praṇavam). When he is present \[as the protector\] in praṇavam, there is no danger.
- *kangiruḷil* – kangu – boundary; implies the epitome of darkness. \[kangu\] As marungul is sometimes shortened as marungu, here kangul (night time) is considered to be shortened to kangu, i.e., it is explained as darkness in night. In this case, it explains the duration. For example, when it is said “*daśa rātram, sapta rātram*” (ten nights, seven nights), it means ten days, seven days and so on.
- *nuṇ tuḷiyāy* – dense night and misty droplets.
- *sēt pāla* … – In the night which stretches to be very long appearing like an eon which is long by nature. A tamiḻ teacher (learned scholar) who is compared to agastya (in knowledge) explained “*kangul vāy*” as “*nāḷagattu*” \[this is to prove that kangul (night) is counted as a day\].
- *tūppāla* … – The one who has divine weapons which resemble both moon and sun appearing at the same time while driving out the darkness, has not come; to remove this darkness, we need moon and sun. It is said in mudal tiruvantādi 51 “*āngaittigiri sudarennum veṇ saṇgam vānil pagarumadi enṟum*” (Looking at the divine disc and pure white conch in his hands, and considering them as sun and moon). Previously, she first hand enjoyed these in his hands. The one who angrily dispels darkness \[sun\] and the one who mingles freely with darkness \[moon\].
- *tūppāla veṇ sangu* – The white conch which has purity as its nature. Alternative explanation – pāl indicates space; having faultless space. It is said as “*perumuḻakku*” (great war cry) and in mahābhāratam drōṇa parvam “*supūrṇōtaranissruta dvani:*” (śrīpāncajanya which releases great sound from the well rounded middle layer). Does tūymai (purity) indicate faultless? When someone is said to be pure, that implies that he is faultless,
- *veṇ sangu* – Alternative explanation – both this and tūymai indicate the abundant nature of the white colour. But this meaning does not fit well due to the existence of “*pāla*” in between “*tū”* and “*veṇ”*.
- *tīppāla val vinaiyēn* – I, who have committed sins which are of cruel nature and which cannot be eliminated. That is, my sins are so strong that, [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) has vowed to protect, I am qualified to be protected and he has the tools to protect me – yet I am not being helped.
- *deyvangāḷ en seygēnō* – There is similarity between the dēvatās and [parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/). The are animiśar (those who don’t blink) by birth, and she remains as in tiruviruttam 97 “*undō kaṇgaḷ tunjudalē*” (will my eyes sleep?). Now, she is not sleeping fearing the darkness; she thinks that they (mothers, friends) are watching her condition and remaining sleepless and considering the dēvatās as the refuge. Since they (animiśar) are not sleeping even when the friends are sleeping, she considers them to be close confidantes and tells them. The dēvatās are recited along with the mothers in “*āyum amarulagum tunjilum*” (if the mothers and the dēvatās slept). When the suffering increases, one will call “Oh mother! what will I do!” – this appears like that.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.4.8. Deyvangal

*deyvangāḷ en seygēn? ōriravu ēḻūḻiyāy mey vandu ninṟu enadāvi melivikkum kai vanda cakkarattu en kaṇṇanum vārānāl tai vanda taṇ tenṟal venjudaril  tān adumē*

**Пословный перевод:**

deyvangāḷ – Oh dēvatās (celestial beings, who are awake)!; en – what; seygēn – can (I) do?; ōr – one; iravu – night; ēḻu – seven; ūḻiyāy – feeling like kalpa (brahmā’s day, eon); mey – truthfully; vandu – coming in forefront; ninṟu – standing; enadu – my; āvi – prāṇa (life, vital air); melivikkum – weakens; kai vanda – obedient (to act knowing the inner thoughts fully); cakkaram – having divine disc; en kaṇṇanum – kriṣṇa; vārān – has not come (to eliminate this night with the help of that chakra); thai vanda – caressing (like those who come to torture); taṇ – cool; tenṟal – \[southerly\] breeze; vem – hot; sudaril – more than fire; adum – burning

**Перевод:**

**Oh dēvatās! What can I do? One night comes to the forefront and stands, and makes me feel like seven kalpa and weakens my prāṇa; kriṣṇa who has the obedient divine disc, has not come. Knowing that he has not come, the caressing cool breeze is burning more than hot fire. Also explained as burning like hot fire.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the eighth pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki says “A single night feels like many eons and is hurting very much; emperumān has also not come; and moreover even the breeze is torturing me”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, parānguśa nāyaki tells those dēvatās \[who were called out in previous pāsuram\] “kriṣṇa who eliminates the enemies by taking up arms, has not come; moreover even the breeze is torturing; what can I do?”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. deyvangāḷ en seygēn? ōriravu ēḻūḻiyāy mey vandu ninṟu enadāvi melivikkum kai vanda cakkarattu en kaṇṇanum vārānāl thai vanda taṇ tenṟal venjudaril  tān adumē*

- *deyvangāḷ en seygēn* – She can only inform those who are awake, if present.
- *ōr iravu ēḻ ūḻiyāy* – Previously, when she said “*ūḻiyāy*“, she meant “the night alone tortured her”, and here, she is saying “it is torturing in many eons”. As saubhari assumed many forms to enjoy, the night assumed many forms to torture [parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/).
- *mey vandu ninṟu* – As rāvaṇa came at the right time \[to capture sītā when she was alone\], the night came knowing well that [parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is suffering in separation. Not just it has come to obey the rules laid out by [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) \[that night sets out naturally at the end of the day\], it appears as though it specifically wants to torture me and appeared in front of me.
- *enadu āvi melivikkum* – It brings back my life and tortures it; the life which is declared to be “dead”, is brought back and tortured; similar to the case of those who steady the already tired persons by giving them some nutrition and then beating them severely again.
- *kai vanda cakkarattu* – Is he without the tool which is required to eliminate this suffering? He has the divine chakra in his hand which follows his thoughts and stays in his hand even if does not invite it. That is, he has the tool which is most obedient towards him. He has the tool which acts according to his mood. śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 15.29 is explained here. *bhāvajñēna* – When iḷaiya perumāḷ (lakśmaṇa) was building the hermitage for śrī rāma and sītā to stay in the forest, śrī rāma told him to have an assembly hall to meet with riśis and a hall to perform fire rituals; he did not mention specifically to build a private quarters for him to spend with sītā; but lakśmaṇa built that as well, knowing śrī rāma’s heart. He says something through his eyes, he too listens to them through his eyes and completes the task. *krutajñēna* – not just following śrī rāma’s thoughts; lakśmaṇa also knows the heart of daśarata cakravarti who remained childless for 60000 years and begot śrī rāma, and built palaces which satisfy his desires. *darmajñēna* – He did not do these tasks just as being a brother, but did them as “duty which must be done”. He performs these tasks considering them to be those duties which are the cause for uplifting himself. *tvayā putrēṇa* – You (lakhsmaṇa) are the one who delivers daśarata from hell, after his death. daśarata always worried “I will protect rāma as long as I am present; but after me, who will protect him; what shall I do?”; since you fulfil his responsibilities, you are the one who relieves him from his sorrows. *darmātmā* – How great of our father! He is a very righteous person; he took care of my protection while he was alive, and like those who establish water shelters for the benefit of others even after their death, he arranged you for my protection. *nasamvrutta:pitāmama* – You may have lost your father but I have not \[since you are there as my father\]. He is having the obedient tool which will complete all tasks as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 28.25 “*rāmasya dakśinō bāhu:*” (lakśmaṇa is like the right arm of śrī rāma).
- *kaṇṇan* – When kriṣṇa set out to attack śrī bhīśma, the divine chakra appeared at once in his hand. As śrī bhīśma attacked arjuna relentlessly for long time, arjuna became weakened; when sarvēśvaran saw that, he forgot his own vow \[of not taking up arms\], jumped out of the chariot and chased bhīśma with his divine chakra and bhīśma said “come and mercifully kill me”. He said in mahābhāratam bhīśma parvam 59.98 “*ēhi ēhi pullāmbhuja patra nētra ..*” (Come on! come on! Oh one with blossomed lotus petal like eyes) – if I get to enjoy your beautiful eyes shining with anger, even if you discard your vow, there is no loss! *prasahya* – Mercifully severe my head ordering me to lay down my arms, as I am not fearful of you or your bravery. *lōkanāta* – Though I won’t be defeated by your bravery, I will be defeated by your supremacy.
- *en kaṇṇan* – One who gives up his own vow for the benefit of his devotees. Whatever is done for one devotee is as good as doing it for all of them. Everyone who surrenders to him is doing so thinking “he will even give up his own vow for the benefit of his devotees”. If it is said that [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) has some rules which never breaks, there is no guarantee for those who surrender unto him.
- *thai vanda taṇ tenṟal* – The cool breeze which came in cool season \[January-February\]; thai varugai – caressing, the cool breeze which reminds the touch of her beloved lord. It is commonly used in the sentence “*tān senṟu maṇ magaḷait taivandān*” (he went and gently caressed the bhūmi dēvi).
- *vem sudaril tān adumē* – Explained as burning more than hot fire as well as burning like hot fire. The favourable aspect \[cool breeze\] appears different during separation, like the difference between ordinary fire and hellish fire.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.
