## 5.4.9. Venjudaril

*venjudaril tān adumāl vīngiruḷinuṇ tuḷiyāy anjudara veyyōn aṇi neduntēr tōnṟādāl senjudart tāmaraik kaṇ selvanum vārānāl nenjidar tīrppār iniyār? ninṟuruguginṟēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vīngu – huge; iruḷ – having darkness; nuṇ – tiny; tuḷi – mist droplet; āy – having; vem – hot; sudaril – more than fire; adum – burning; am – beautiful; sudar – having rays; veyyōn – āditya who is the hot sun, his; aṇi – beautiful; nedu – tall; tēr – chariot; tōnṟādu – not appearing; sem – reddish (highlighting his great opulence); sudar – having radiance; tāmarai – like a lotus flower; kaṇ – one who is having eye; selvanum – śrīmān \[one who has śrī mahālakśmi\]; vārān – has not come; ninṟu – standing steadily; uruguginṟēn – I am melting; ini – now; nenjidar – the suffering in my mind; tīrppār – destroyer; Ar – who?

**Перевод:**

**The current night which is having huge darkness and tiny mist droplet(s), is burning more than hot fire; the beautiful tall chariot of āditya, the hot sun, who is having beautiful rays, is not appearing; emperumān, who is śrīmān and is having lotus flower like,  radiant reddish eye(s) has not come; I am standing steadily and melting; now, who is the destroyer of the suffering in my mind?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the ninth pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki says “The night is torturing me. The sunrise which supposed to happen has not occurred since it is desired by me; emperumān too has not arrived; other than the suffering of mine, is there any one who will come and protect me?”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. venjudaril tān adumāl vīngiruḷinuṇ tuḷiyāy anjudara veyyōn aṇi neduntēr tōnṟādāl senjudart tāmaraik kaṇ selvanum vārānāl nenjidar tīrppār iniyār? ninṟuruguginṟēnē*

- *vem sudaril …* – The appearance of huge darkness along with the tiny mist droplets resembles rāvaṇa appearing along with mārīca. Both \[darkness and mist droplets\] are favourable for enjoyment \[during union with the beloved person\]. \[Darkness is favourable for enjoyment; are mist droplets too the same?\] as said in periya tirumoḻi 8.5.8 “*oḻugu nuṇpani*” (dripping tiny mist droplets), during rainy season, the beloved woman should be embraced by the beloved man tightly. Darkness is naturally favourable for enjoyment.
- *vīngiruḷin nuṇ tuḷiyāy .. vem sudaril tān adumāl* – Well developed darkness and tiny mist droplets are burning more than hot fire; also said as burning like hot fire. What is more important among these two? – Do we need to explicitly say that? Is it not sufficient to say there are two tormentors? Now, this decad is specifically speaking about the suffering in the night; so there is more importance for the darkness.
- *am sudar* … – Just as iḷaiya perumāḷ (lakhsmaṇa) stayed away \[while rāvaṇa came to capture sītā\], the sun stayed away here. The sun  which has beautiful rays which will dispel the sufferings at once on their arrival, did not come.
- *tōnṟādāl* – Just as some one miraculously escaped in the total deluge and will see “have I reached the shore? have I reached the shore?”, throughout the night, she is seeing “Has it dawned? Has it dawned?” \[repetition highlights the severity of the suffering\].
- *sem sudar* … – As said in cāndōjña upaniśat 1.6 “*tasya yatā kapyāsam puṇḍarīkam ēvam akśinī*” (The divine eyes of śrīman nārāyaṇa, the supreme lord, resemble the lotus flower which has been freshly blossomed by the rays of the sun), one who is residing in the sun planet has not come; just as the aruṇōdayam (the arrival of aruṇa, the charioteer of sun god) signifies the subsequent arrival of sun, the sun’s arrival signifies the subsequent arrival of bhagavān. The śrīmān (the one who beholds [śrī mahālakśmi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/) on his chest) who has lotus like eyes which shine like red glow, has not come. Even if sun comes, there is scope for the arrival of darkness too; the never-setting sun ([bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)) too has not come; the sun’s glow is limited to certain regions; but bhagavān illuminates both nitya vibhūti (spiritual realm) and leelā vibhūti (material realm). It is said in iraṇḍām tiruvantādi 81 “*pagal kaṇḍēn nāraṇanaik kaṇḍēn*” (I have seen the sun (which sets) and the nārāyaṇa (the sun which never sets)).
- *nenjidar tīrppāriniyār* – Who will cure the internal darkness \[suffering\]? Sun is the one who dispels external darkness; but internal darkness is well-rooted suffering; only a visionary and confidante person \[[bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) who is greatly capable and is present as antaryāmi (in-dwelling super soul)\] can remove it. He is said in tiruccanta viruttam 114 “*jñānamāgi jñāiṟāgi*” (he is knowledge, he is sun).
- *ninṟurugiginṟēnē … nenjidar tīrpār ini Ar* – Separation from distinguished [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), having melted, the entity (suffering in separation) will neither be finished nor be able to sustain itself. The desire to see the beloved person who is separated, once more, will not let the person in separation die, and since the beloved person is not seen at once, that loss will not let the person live.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.4.10. Ninruruginrene

*ninṟuruguginṟēnē pōla nedu vānam senṟurugi nun tuḷiyāyc celginṟa kangulvāy anṟor kāl vaiyam aḷanda pirān vārān enṟu onṟorukāl sollādu ulagō uṟangumē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ninṟu – staying (instead of leaving); uruguginṟēnē pōla – like me who is melting; nedu – the vastly spacious; vānam – sky; senṟu – waning; urugum – melting; nuṇ – tiny; tuḷi – droplets; āy – having; selginṟa – (continuously) going on; kangul vāy – in the night; anṟu – that day (when mahābali encroached upon); orukāl – back then; vaiyam – earth; aḷanda – measured; pirān – the one who benefits the whole world; vārān – is he coming today; enṟu – at least saying so; onṟu – a word; orukāl – once; sollādu – without saying so; ulagu – world; uṟangum – sleeping; O! – parānguśa nāyaki saying with disgust “what kind of attitude is this?”

**Перевод:**

**In the night which is continuing where the vastly spacious sky is waning with tiny droplets melting, as I am staying here melting, the whole world is sleeping without even saying “is emperumān, the great benefactor of the whole world who measured the earth back then, coming?”. parānguśa nāyaki saying this with disgust “what kind of attitude is this?”.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the tenth pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki says “Even after seeing my suffering in this night, \[alas!\] the whole world is sleeping instead of saying something about emperumān!”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, parānguśa nāyaki says “While I am suffering in this night, \[alas!\] the whole world is sleeping instead of saying something about emperumān, the great benefactor, who accepted the earth fully for him!”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. ninṟuruguginṟēnē pōla nedu vānam senṟurugi nun tuḷiyāyc celginṟa kangulvāy anṟor kāl vaiyam aḷanda pirān vārān enṟu onṟorukāl sollādu ulagō uṟangumē*

- *ninṟu* … – The sky which is vast and provides space for all the entities to stay, became tiny droplets and started falling down.

When asked “like whom?”, [parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says,

- *ninṟu uruguginṟēnē pōla* – An example must be perceivable/visible – so, she is highlighting herself as the example. As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 37.18 “*yasya sā janakātmajā … apramēyam hi tat tēja:*” (The greatness of the one (śrī rāma) who is married to the daughter of janaka, is beyond comprehension), parānguśa nāyaki, brings about greatness for even those who are already great. It is said that “due to being śriya:pati (lord of śrī mahālakśmi), he is greater than all”. In such a \[lengthy, tormenting\] night.
- *anṟu orukāl* … – The reason for my survival even in his separation is his nature – that is, will he who protected everyone \[as vāmana/trivikrama\], not protect me, that too, from the suffering caused by himself? No one says “it is not natural for him to protect others, but it happens rarely, as the path laid out by a moving worm sometimes ends up as an art”.
- *anṟu orukāl* – No one is there \[even\] to say “He did it once long ago, it is not a natural quality of him” \[everyone is sleeping\].
- *pirān* – while saying *pirān* \[benefactor\],
- *vārān* – she is also saying “he is not coming”. \[īsn’t this contradictory?\] No one is there \[even\] to say “If you are thinking that he is the benefactor who measured the whole world \[so he will help you also who is part of this world\], that happened once like a flood, his nature is to not come \[and give protection\]”.
- *onṟu* – Should we say “*vārān*” (not coming), or should we say “*varum*” (will come)? Only for those who have the desire to see him and survive, it will be possible to say “*varum*“. \[I am more focussed on you all saying something, instead of sleeping\] you can say either “*vārān*” or “*varum*“.
- *orukāl –* \[Just saying once is enough\] Only for those who can survive after hearing once that he will not come, it is required to say twice or more times. She will die as soon as she hears that he will not come.
- *ulagu O! uṟangumē* – Initially she was anguished that the mothers and friends were sleeping; subsequently she became so anguished that the whole world is sleeping. The world became similar to the [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who separated from me \[both are not speaking at all\].

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.4.11. Uranguvan pol

*uṟanguvān pōl yōgu seyda perumānaic ciṟanda poḻil sūḻ kurugūrc catakōpan sol niṟam kiḷarnda andādi āyirattuḷ ippattāl iṟandu pōy vaigundam sērāvāṟu enganēyō?*

**Пословный перевод:**

uṟanguvān pōl – pretending to be sleeping (when getting an opportunity to do so); yōgu – the meditation of thinking about protecting the world; seyda – engaged in; perumānai – about sarvēśvaran; siṟanda – rich; poḻil – garden; sūḻ – surrounded; kurugūr – leader of āḻvārtirunagari; satakōpan – āḻvār; sol – mercifully compiled; niṟam – paṇ (tune); kiḷarnda – abundant; andādi – in antādi style (beginning of a pāsuram matching the ending of previous pāsuram); āyirattuḷ – among the thousand pāsurams; ip pattāl – by this decad; iṟandu – shedding the body; pōy – travelling in the arcirādi (the illuminated) path; vaigundam – in paramapadam (spiritual realm); sērāvāṟu – not reaching; enganē – how?

**Перевод:**

**āḻvār, the leader of āḻvārtirunagari which is surrounded by rich garden(s), mercifully compiled this decad among the thousand pāsuarams which have abundant tune, on sarvēśvaran who is pretending to be sleeping  but \[actually\] engaged in meditating about protecting the world; by singing this decad how will one not go on the arcirādi path after shedding the body and reach paramapadam? It is certain that one will reach the spiritual realm. niṟam – paṇ (tune); it can also mean candas (meter).**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the end, āḻvār is asking “How can those who meditated upon āḻvār’s suffering in this decad, sustain themselves?”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār explains attainment of paramapadam as the result of \[learning/reciting\] this decad.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*In the end, āḻvār says “Those who heard āḻvār’s pāsurams, and those who meditated upon āḻvār’s condition, will not survive. Since those who die \[after hearing āḻvār’s words and meditating upon him\] are sure to reach paramapadam, this explains attainment of paramapadam” uṟanguvān pōl yōgu seyda perumānaic ciṟanda poḻil sūḻ kurugūrc catakōpan sol niṟam kiḷarnda andādi āyirattuḷ ippattāl iṟandu pōy vaigundam sērāvāṟu enganēyō?*

- *uṟanguvān pōl yōgu seyda perumānai* – Since his arrival was delayed, as earlier [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) wondered “if he has forgotten me and sleeping”, now he says “he is not sleeping; he is just thinking about our protection”; śrī rangarāja stavam uttara śatakam 75 “*nidrāsi jākaryayā*” (you are divinely sleeping with the thought to protect everyone in this world). He is not sleeping, instead he is fully meditating upon our protection, leaving aside all other thoughts. sarvēśvaran who is going to subsequently protect us, reminded us about his glories in this manner.
- *siṟanda poḻil* – As [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) sustained himself thinking about [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s divine sleep with thoughts about his protection, the whole town sustained itself too. The situation is such that, during separation one will say as in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 59.4 “*apivrukśā:*” (even trees have withered) and on seeing his arrival, one will say “*akāla palinō vrukśā:*” (the trees blossom in non-season too).
- *niṟam kiḷarnda andādi* – antādi style poems which are abundant in tune.
- *ippattāl* … – Those who recited \[or meditated upon\] this decad, need not suffer in separation from [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) like [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) who desired for death saying as in [tiruvāimoḻi 5.4.5](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/06/thiruvaimozhi-5-4-5-ar-ennai/) “*pēr ennai māyādāl*” (I am only living for name sake and even death is not helping me); those who recited this decad will not survive. Here it is said like this since those who die hearing this decad will enter paramapadam. There should be some result which is highlighted here, and what is that result? For those who heard the words of those who are engrossed in bhagavat viśayam (matters related to [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)), after leaving their body, their desired goal of attaining paramapadam will not elude them. For those who heard the words of those who are engrossed in bhagavān, became intolerant of existence in this material world and gave up their body, is there any reason for not reaching paramapadam which is the apt abode?
- *ippattāl iṟandu pōy vaigundam sērāvāṟu enganēyō* – Instead of suffering here saying as in [tiruvāimoḻi 5.4.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/06/thiruvaimozhi-5-4-1-urellam-thunji/) “*nīḷiravāy nīṇḍadāl*” (as the lengthy night extends without an end) and as in [tiruvāimoḻi 5.4.4](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/06/thiruvaimozhi-5-4-4-pen-pirandhar/) “*oṇsudarōn vārādu oḷittān*” (the sun not appearing and went into hiding), will reach the \[divine\] abode \[of paramapadam\] where the sun never sets and the day never ends.

## 5.5 Enganeyo annaimirgal

## 5.5.1. Enganeyo annaimirgal

*enganēyō annaimīrgāḷ! ennai munivadu nīr nangaḷ kōlat tirukkuṟungudi nambiyai nān kaṇḍa pin sanginōdum nēmiyōdum tāmaraik kaṇgaḷōdum senganivāy onṟinōdum selginṟaden nenjamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

annimīrgāḷ – Oh mothers!; nīr – You all; O – instead of showing your love; ennai – me (who became attached to apt matter); O – when you are supposed to be joyful; munivadu – showing anger; enganē – why?; nangaḷ – a distinguished person, matching the greatness of our clan; kōlam – attractive; tirukkuṟungudi – of tirukkuṟungudi; nambiyai – nambi who is complete with all auspicious qualities; nān – I; kaṇḍa pin – after enjoying; sanginōdum – with śrī pāncajanyam (conch); nēmiyōdum – with the divine chakra (disc); tāmarai – lotus like attractive; kaṇgaḷōdum – with divine eyes; sem – reddish; kani – fruit like; onṟu – unique; vāyinōdum – divine lips; en – my; nenjam – heart; selginṟadu – becoming attached

**Перевод:**

**Oh mothers! Why are you all showing anger towards me instead of showing your love when you are supposed to be joyful? After having enjoyed the attractive nambi of tirukkuṟungudi, who is a distinguished person matching the greatness of our clan and who is complete with all auspicious qualities, along with śrī pāncajanyam, the divine cakram, lotus like attractive divine eyes and reddish fruit like unique divine lips, my heart has become attached \[to him\]. kōlam (attractive) is also explained as an adjective for tirukkuṟungudi.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the first pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki says “On meditating upon the beauty of your divine face which is together with the āḻvārs (nityasūris in the form of śankam, cakram etc), my internal sense (heart/mind) becomes very attached towards it”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*In the first pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki says “My heart is attached to the āḻvārs (nityasūris in the form of śankam, cakram etc) which are nambi’s distinguished symbols and his predominant physical beauty”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. enganēyō annaimīrgāḷ! ennai munivadu nīr nangaḷ kōlat tirukkuṟungudi nambiyai nān kaṇḍa pin sanginōdum nēmiyōdum tāmaraik kaṇgaḷōdum senganivāy onṟinōdum selginṟaden nenjamē*

- *enganēyō* … – When some one starts advising others they will forget their own situation. Should one not understand the nature of something which they are trying to eliminate? If you are trying to eliminate my attachment, should you not be angry at the beauty of nambi which caused such attachment in me? What is the match between my current condition and your good advice? Why are you all who have enjoyed the physical beauty of nambi, trying to withdraw me who is engrossed in it?
- *annaimīrgāḷ* – Have I ever caused disgrace to our family heritage? Did I not grow up hearing your good words as said in periya tirumoḻi 7.4.4 “*pērāḷan pērōdum periyōr*” (the noble devotees who recite the names of the great lord) and in tiruvāimoḻi 3.7.1 “*yavarēlum avar*” (anyone who is a devotee)? The same activity which was done by you, if performed by your children, does it become a mistake? Whether it is children or disciples, if they pursue a few steps in bhagavat viśayam, should they not be celebrated? When the wife of kūrattāḻvār \[the father of [kūrattāḻvān/kūrēśa](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/kuraththazhwan/)\] shed her body and left for the divine abode, some one asked him “Shall we arrange to have you married again?”, he replied “that will end up being a hurdle for [āḻvān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/kuraththazhwan/); now, śāstram says ‘*anāśrami na tiśtēt’* (one should not be devoid of a proper āśramam \[brahmcaryra (celibate bacelorhood), gruhasta (married life), vānaprasta (retired life in seclusion) and sanyāsa (mendicant life) are the four āśramams. One should be situated in a proper āśrama. Once having entered gruhasta life, being without wife is considered as inappropriate\]); analysing the situation ‘shall I follow śāstram or shall I engage in caring for a bhāgavata \[āḻvān here\]’, he decided, instead of focussing on sāmānya darmam (normal rules of śāstram), this viśēśa darmam (special situation) is stronger \[and hence, is given more importance\]” and avoids second marriage.
- *ennai munivadu nīr* – Should you not show your anger on nambi, who made me not listen to your advice?
- *ennai* – Why are all of you who are fully engaged in nambi [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s beauty yourselves, showing your anger on me who is fully engrossed in the beauty of nambi?
- *nangaḷ …* – If you don’t know your own nature, should you also not know about nambi too?
- *nangaḷ* – nambi’s beauty is like a complete diet for this clan \[of this\]. Unlike those who engaged in countless austerities towards [sarvēśvaran](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/), [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) was begotten by surrendering unto nambi. It is well known that “udaiyanangaiyār (mother of āḻvār) surrendered to nambi \[prayed him\] and became divinely pregnant with āḻvār in her womb”. āḻvār too himself says in tiruviruttam 37 “*nedungālamum kaṇṇan nīḷ malarp pādam paravip peṟṟa*” (āḻvār was begotten by praying to kriṣṇa’s long lotus like divine feet). kōlam (attractive) is an adjective to explain how the tirukkuṟungudi town is decorated well in all aspects; or it can be considered as an adjective for nambi’s beauty.
- *nambiyai* – Why are you trying to withdraw me who is captivated by nambi who is complete with auspicious qualities?
- *nambiyai nān* – Just as there is no shortcoming in [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) in his beauty etc to captivate others, I have no shortcoming in desire to be captivated.
- *kaṇḍa pin –* You too are advising after seeing emperumān.
- *kaṇḍa pin* – You are doing “*gatē jalē sētu bandanam*” (building a bridge/dam after the floods have passed). You should have stopped me before I saw him, is it possible to do so now?

When asked “What has happened that will not allow us to withdraw you from him?”, she explains how she is captivated by what is on [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s hand and his face.

- *sangu* … – Your advice will work only for those who have a heart.
- *sanginōdum* – As said in nācciyār tirumoḻi 7.7 “*sengamala nāṇmalarmēl tēnugarum annam pōl*” (like a swan sucking the honey from red lotus flower), \[nambi\] has a white śrī pāncajanyam (divine conch) which is contrasting the dark complexion of his divine form; if this is an ornament for this hand, the nēmi (divine chakra, the weapon) appears as the ornament for the other hand, without the need for any other decoration.
- *tāmaraik kaṇgaḷōdum* – On seeing the eyes, she lost focus from the hands. The eyes which resembled lotus flower due to their expanded state etc.
- *sem kani vāy* – With the smile which says “*tavāsmi*” (I am yours) and makes one think “he is ours”.
- *onṟinōdum* – \[Explaining collectively, how [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s heart is reaching out to all aspects of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)\] With the divine lips which will make one forget everything as the [muktātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) will forget the material experience. Alternative explanation – the heart reaches out to all beautiful aspects of nambi, as jāti (species) pervades the whole vyakti (entity). It appears that āḻvār’s heart has become equivalent to [sarvēśvaran](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/). When he pervades, he does so fully unlike the normally pervasive nature of ākāśam (ether). Similarly, āḻvār’s heart too has reached all different beautiful aspects of nambi.
- *selginṟadu* – It is still going and has not reached the end. When they (the mothers) say “We have also enjoyed nambi’s beauty fully; you cannot refuse our advice”, she replies “I can refuse your advice, but I cannot refuse nambi’s divine face”.

They ask “Why are we not having such feelings?”, she says,

- *en nenjamē* – Unlike you all, my heart has enjoyed him, as he himself revealed about his nature to my heart.

\[It appears that a śrīvaiṣṇava may have entered the assembly, and hence nampiḷḷai is explaining the pāsuram again\]

- *enganēyō* … – Why are they showing their anger towards me instead of showing it towards nambi, whose beauty is the cause for my attachment towards him? How come they raised me so that I have natural attachment towards nambi, but now showing anger towards me \[for having such attafhment\]? While you yourself have taught these previously, when I set out to enjoy him, why are you condemning me?
- *kōlam* – He is having such beauty that it will stop me from withdrawing from him.
- *tirukkuṟungudi nambiyai* – Did I get captivated in the supremacy, to be withdrawn? \[No, I am captivated in his saulabhyam (simplicity)\].
- *nambiyai* – Can I withdraw citing lack of qualities in him? \[No, he is nambi, filled with auspicious qualities\].
- *nān kaṇḍa pin* – Can I withdraw citing lack of desire in me? \[No\].
- *sanginōdum* – She has special association with śrī pāncajanyam, the divine conch \[which is why she is highlighting it first\], since both \[the conch and [parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)\] understand the taste of his lips; like those who consume from the same container.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.5.2. En nenjinal

*en nenjināl nōkkik kāṇīr ennai muniyādē tennan sōlait tirukkuṟungudi nambiyai nān kaṇḍa pin minnu nūlum kuṇḍalamum mārbil tirumaṟuvum mannu pūṇum nāngu tōḷum vandengum ninṟidumē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ennai – me; muniyādē – instead of ordering; en nenjināl – (unlike your heart which does not transform even after enjoying him) through my heart (which is emotionally attached to him); nōkki – experience; kāṇīr – see; then – in south direction; nan – nice; sōlai – having garden; tirukkuṟungudi – in tirukkuṟungudi; nambiyai – nambi (complete with all auspicious qualities); nān – I; kaṇḍa pin – after seeing; minnum – (matching his form) revealing (his splendour); nūlum – divine yajñōpavīdam (sacred thread); kuṇḍalamum – his divine ear rings (which are swaying in both ears); mārbil – in the (distinguished) divine chest; tiru – inseparable ornament; maṟuvum – śrīvatsa (molehill); mannu – fixed permanently; pūṇum – various ornaments; nāngu – four; tōḷum – divine shoulders; engum – wherever I go; vandu – following me; ninṟidum – stood

**Перевод:**

**Instead of ordering me you should experience nambi through my heart and see; after seeing nambi in tirukkuṟungudi which is located in south direction and  is having nice garden \[around it\], his divine yajñōpavīdam which reveals his splendour, his divine ear rings, the inseparable ornament in his chest named śrīvatsa, various other ornaments which are permanently fixed and his four divine shoulders are following me and stand with me where I go.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the second pāsuram, parāguśa nāyaki says “nambi’s natural beauty in his divine chest and divine shoulders and his divine ornaments, surround me and torment me”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. en nenjināl nōkkik kāṇīr ennai muniyādē tennan sōlait tirukkuṟungudi nambiyai nān kaṇḍa pin minnu nūlum kuṇḍalamum mārbil tirumaṟuvum mannu pūṇum nāngu tōḷum vandengum ninṟidumē*

- *en nenjināl …* – The mothers say “we too have enjoyed nambi, yet have not lost our strītvam (femininity)” and parānguśa nāyaki replies,
- *en nenjināl nōkkik kāṇīr* – Can you borrow my heart and see through it? If you did that, you will scold yourself instead of scolding me.
- *ennai* – \[after seeing through my heart\] You will scold yourself saying “Have we been scolding her all these days!”.
- *muniyādē* – As said in periya tirumoḻi 8.2.9 “*kaṇapuram kai toḻum piḷḷaiyaip piḷḷai enṟu eṇṇap peṟuvarē*” (a child who worships tirukkaṇṇapuram sourirājap perumāḷ, even if it is one’s own child, it should be revered instead of being treated like a small child), only due to considering her to be our child, we scolded her instead of seeing her condition and will scold yourself subsequently.
- *en nenjināl nōkkik kāṇīr* – As said in mahābhāratam udyōka parvam 68.5 “*bhaktyā śāstratvēdmi janārdanam*” (With devotion, I learn about kriṣṇa through śāstram) – drutarāśtra asked sanjaya “While both of us learned śāstram together, how are you so distinguished that I have to learn these from you \[again\]”, sanjaya said “Hear the difference now” – “*māyām nasēvē*” – I am not deceptive. Since he is highlighting the fault of the king and the greatness of the self he says “*bhadram tē*” (let there be auspiciousness for you). “*navrudādarmamācarē*” – I never engage in useless activities. “*śuddabhāvamgata:*” – my mind, speech and actions are always in harmony. “*bhaktyā*” – I did not learn śāstram word-by-word to learn about bhagavān, but learned about him through śāstram accompanied by my devotion – so said sanjaya. “*nābhijānāsi kēśavam*” – for those who think they can learn on their own, they will not be able to know about him. Hence, you too try to know him through my heart.
- *tennan* … – Just as the ornaments were for nambi’s form, the garden is for the town. Explained as nice (nan) garden in south (then) direction; alternative explanation – as said in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 4.2.7 “*tennan koṇḍādum*” (glorified by the great pāṇḍiya king named “*tennan*“), tirukkuṟungudi which is praised by king tennan.
- *nān kaṇḍa pin* – After I, who know about the combination of divine ornaments and the distinguished nature of the garden, have seen him.
- *minnu nūlum* – The divine sacred thread which appears like a lightning amidst a cloud.
- *kuṇḍalamum* – The ear ring which appears like a twist of the lightning which struck; and the divine śrīvatsa mole on the chest which makes one desirous to ward off evil eye on seeing it at once.
- *mannu pūṇum* – The divine ornaments which are never taken off even while embracing his divine consorts. That is, they are naturally very enjoyable.
- *nāngu tōḷum* – The divine four shoulders which appear like ornaments for the ornaments which decorate [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) and those which appear like branches of kalpaka taru (celestial desire fulfilling tree). As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam kiśkintā kāṇḍam 3.15 “*sarvabhūśaṇa bhūśārhā:*” (the shoulders which bring about beauty for the ornaments which are worn by him).
- *vandu engum ninṟidumē* – Even when I step aside thinking “I will obey your good advice”, they come around and follow me there too. As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 39.14 “*vrukśē vrukśē paśyāmi*” (mārīca says to rāvaṇa – I am seeing śrī rāma in every tree), for both favourable persons \[[āḻvārs](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/azhwars/) et al\] and unfavourable persons \[asuras et al\], it is the same result \[both are seeing [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) everywhere – while the devotees see him everywhere due to overwhelming love towards him, others see him everywhere due to fear\]. You tell me, where will I go now?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.5.3. Ninridum tisaikkum

*ninṟidum tisaikkum naiyumenṟu annaiyarum munidir kunṟa mādat tirukkuṟungudi nambiyai nān kaṇḍa pin venṟi villum taṇḍum vāḷum cakkaramum sangamum ninṟu tōnṟik kaṇṇuḷ nīngā nenjuḷḷum nīngāvē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ninṟidum – standing dumbfounded (being unable to do anything else); tisaikkum – remain bewildered (not to understand what is said to her); naiyum – becomes weakened (due to internal thinking); enṟu – saying that; annaiyarum – the mothers who first instigated me into this love; munidir – you are talking unsavoury words; kunṟam – like a hill; mādam – having mansions; tirukkuṟungudi nambiyai – tirukkuṟungudi nambi; nān – I (who enjoy seeing his brave form as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam “tam druśtvā“); kaṇḍa pin – after enjoying; venṟi – victorious; villum – bow; taṇḍum – mace; vāḷum – sword; cakkaramum – disc; sangamum – conch; ninṟu – standing together; kaṇṇuḷ – inside my eyes; tōnṟi – appear; nīngā – do not leave; nenjuḷḷum – from inside my heart too; nīngā – do not leave

**Перевод:**

**You, the mothers who first instigated me into this love, are talking unsavoury words saying that I am standing dumbfounded, I remain bewildered and have become weakened; after enjoying tirukkuṟungudi nambi who is having hill-like mansions \[in the holy-abode\], his victorious bow, mace, sword, disc and conch are standing together inside my eyes and do not leave; similarly, they do not leave from inside my heart too.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In  pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki says “nambi’s divine weapons starting with śrī śārngam (bow) appear eternally inside and outside me everywhere”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. ninṟidum tisaikkum naiyumenṟu annaiyarum munidir kunṟa mādat tirukkuṟungudi nambiyai nān kaṇḍa pin venṟi villum taṇḍum vāḷum cakkaramum sangamum ninṟu tōnṟik kaṇṇuḷ nīngā nenjuḷḷum nīngāvē*

- *ninṟidum* – The different beautiful aspects of [nambi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) are also like śrī rāma’s arrows where each arrow will attack differently as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 94.22 “*cinnam binnam śarair dagdam*” (The rākśasas were cut, blown away, burnt and destroyed by the arrows of śrī rāma); one will make her dumbfounded; another will take away her intelligence and another will bestow intelligence and make her suffer. You are scolding me when I am dumbfounded, bewildered or weakened, considering them to be my mistake.
- *annaiyarum munidir* – Is it apt for you who have clarity in these matters, to scold me! How can you who are the mothers, be angry on me for showing such affection towards [nambi!](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) You who were previously having clarity and bewilderment \[during your youth\], are angry on me. \[Do they have bewilderment?\] You are the ones who say as in periya tirumoḻi 10.10.9 “*āḻiyodum ponnār sārngam udaiya adigaḷai innār enṟaṟiyēn*” (I am unable to identify this revered lord who is having disc, golden bow). Whatever you have done in your youth, if I did the same in my youth, is that wrong? The whole clan is engaged in attachment/affection towards bhagavān.
- *kunṟam* … – Having tall mansions which appear like hills placed next to each other.
- *nān kaṇḍa pin* – After I, who knows the nature of a person based on how they hold the weapon, have seen him. Since [parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is vīrapatni (the consort of a brave man, i.e., supreme lord), she knows the difference \[Equating parānguśa nāyaki to sītāp pirātti\]. Since (sītāp) pirātti is the one who brings the bow to perumāḷ (śrī rāma). \[Narrates the incident which happened in daṇḍakāraṇyam, where pirātti instigated śrī rāma to fight for the riśis\] When perumāḷ asked “bring me the bow”, she brought it and gave it to him and observing his stature with the bow, she said “If you roam around with the weapon in this manner, the riśis will come and surrender unto you \[asking for help\]; you will have to fight the rākśasas, who are their enemies, which will lead to long lasting rivalry, and will eventually lead to us living in separation; hence you can drop the bow here and we can move around with the guise of those who are engaged in penance”. It is the śāngam (two meanings – her partiality and the bow) which made her say this.
- *venṟi vil* … – The divine weapons, are identified as both weapons and ornaments. Only when they are used in battle, they are considered as weapons \[otherwise, they are considered as ornaments only\].
- *venṟi villum –* The divine bow which is victorious over those who are favourable and others who are unfavourable. As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam kiśkintā kāṇḍam 3.9 “*śakracāpa nibhē cāpē gruhītvā śatru nāśanē*” (hanuman to śrī rāma and lakśmaṇa – you who are holding the bows which will destroy the enemies and resemble indra’s bow) – the favourable ones will sustain on seeing the bow and the enemies will die on seeing the way you hold the bow.
- *taṇḍum* … – The other weapons which are of the same nature.
- *ninṟu tōnṟik kaṇṇuḷ nīngā* – Staying in front of my eyes and not moving aside. Since they tormented me by staying in front of my eyes, I closed my eyes and they appeared in my heart shining brightly.
- *nenjuḷḷum nīngāvē* – Previously, they were “*vandengum ninṟidumē*” (following me everywhere and present before me), here they are tormenting me both inside and outside. \[What is the difference between these two?\] She too became similar to [nambi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s beauty. Just as nambi’s beauty torments her everywhere, she too is enjoying him both through internal and external eyes.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.5.4. Ninga nilla

*nīnga nillā kaṇṇa nīrgaḷ enṟu annaiyarum munidir tēn koḷ sōlait tirukkuṟungudi nambiyai nān kaṇḍa pin pūndaṇ mālait taṇḍuḻāyum pon mudiyum vadivum pāngu tōnṟum pattum nāṇum pāviyēn pakkattavē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kaṇṇā nīrgaḷ – (her) tears; nīnga – flow; nillā – not stopping; enṟu – saying that; annaiyarum – you who engaged me in nambi to start with; munidir – are scolding; tēn – honey; koḷ – containing; sōlai – having gardens; tirukkuṟungudi nambiyai – tirukkuṟungudi nambi; nān – I (who rejoice his supremacy); kaṇḍa pin – after enjoying; pū – enjoyable; taṇ – invigorating; mālai – in the form of a garland; taṇ tuḻāyum – fresh tuḷasi; pon – attractive, highlighting his supremacy; mudiyum – crown; vadivum – form (which matches that garland and crown); pāngu – fitting (the divine waist); tōnṟum – appearing; pattu – silk garment; nāṇum – waist string (which is worn on top of the garment); pāviyēn – having me who is having the sin (of not attaining and enjoying the same, while they shine inside); pakkatta – came in close proximity

**Перевод:**

**You who engaged me in nambi to start with, are scolding me saying “her flowing tears are not stopping”; after enjoying nambi of tirukkuṟungudi which is having gardens containing honey, his fresh tuḷasi which is in the form of an enjoyable invigorating garland, his attractive crown which is highlighting his supremacy, his silk garment which is appearing to be fitting well for his form, his waist string etc came in close proximity to me,who is a sinner.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fourth pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki says “The divine garland on his divine shoulders, his garments etc are staying close to me and tormenting me”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, parānguśa nāyaki says “nambi‘s divine and distinguished attire which reveals his supremacy, stays close to me”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Fourth pāsuram. parānguśa nāyaki says “The crown which he adorns for the protection \[of others\], his garland, the way he is wearing his garments etc are staying close to me and tormenting me”. nīnga nillā kaṇṇa nīrgaḷ enṟu annaiyarum munidir tēn koḷ sōlait tirukkuṟungudi nambiyai nān kaṇḍa pin pūndaṇ mālait taṇḍuḻāyum pon mudiyum vadivum pāngu tōnṟum pattum nāṇum pāviyēn pakkattavē*

- *nīnga nillā  kaṇṇa nīrgaḷ* – While he left, the tears are not leaving. Alternative explanation – Not stopping. Another explanation – “*nīkka nillā*” (to be wiped off by the mothers) has become “*nīnga nillā*” – i.e., as they wipe the tears off, it keeps flowing.
- *annaiyarum munidir* – Have your eyes not shed happy tears? \[Why are you scolding me for shedding happy tears?\]
- *tēn koḷ* … – Only if you can stop the flow of honey in those gardens, I can stop my tears. It appears that the cause for these tears is the enjoyability of this divine abode of tirukkuṟungudi.
- *nān kaṇḍa pin* – After I who know his natural supremacy, have seen it.
- *pūn taṇ* … – Highlighting that he is the lord of both spiritual and material realms, attractive cool fresh tuḷasi garland, the divine crown which is worn to highlight that he conducts both the realms, and the form which matches that garland and crown; it is easy to determine that “he is the deserving person for this garland and crown”. nanjīyar with great emotions would mercifully say “*vadivum enbadē*” (she is counting his form amidst enjoying the ornaments).
- *pāngu tōnṟum pattum* – The divine pītāmbaram (yellow garment) which appears to have naturally grown out of the waist in the most fitting manner.
- *nāṇum* – waist string.
- *pāviyēn pakkatavē* – I have committed a great sin that he is neither presenting me himself to enjoy nor hiding himself in such realistic visualization. While he is appearing in close proximity, I am unable to enjoy him. He is neither letting me embrace him nor moving away from me.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.5.5. Pakkam nokki

*pakkam nōkki niṟkum naiyum enṟu annaiyarum munidir takka kīrttit tirukkuṟungudi nambiyai nān kaṇḍapin tokka sōdit toṇḍai vāyum nīṇḍa puruvangaḷum takka tāmaraik kaṇṇum pāviyēn āviyin mēlanavē*

**Пословный перевод:**

pakkam – side (from where he may arrive); nōkki – seeing; niṟkum – standing; naiyum – becomes weakened (due to his non-arrival); enṟu – saying that; annaiyarum – you \[mothers\] (who first established our friendship); munidir – angrily scolding me (to eliminate the friendship); takka – matching (his completeness); kīrtti – having fame; tirukkuṟungudi nambiyai – tirukkuṟungudi nambi; nān – I (who is captivated by his fame); kaṇḍa pin – after enjoying; tokka – abundant; sōdi – having radiance; toṇḍai – like toṇḍai (a reddish) fruit; vāyum – divine lips; nīṇḍa – long; puruvangaḷum – divine eyebrows; takka – having matching length (of those eyebrows); tāmarai – lotus like attractive; kaṇṇum – divine eyes; pāviyēn – me who is having the sin not to enjoy him as desired; āviyin mēlana – reaches up to my self\[soul\]

**Перевод:**

**You \[mothers\] are angrily scolding me saying that I am standing and seeing the side \[from where he may arrive\] and becoming weakened \[due to his non-arrival\]; after enjoying tirukkuṟungudi nambi who is having matching fame, his divine lips which resemble toṇḍai (a reddish) fruit with abundant radiance, his long divine eyebrows and lotus like attractive divine eyes which are equally long (like the eyebrows) are reaching to my self, who is having the sin to not enjoy him as desired.**

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In  pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki says “Just as matching fame for tirukkuṟungudi, the beauty of the matching divine lips, divine face etc hurt my soul”*

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, parānguśa nāyaki says “nambi‘s facial beauty etc appears to be reaching my ātmā”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. pakkam nōkki niṟkum naiyum enṟu annaiyarum munidir takka kīrttit tirukkuṟungudi nambiyai nān kaṇḍapin tokka sōdit toṇḍai vāyum nīṇḍa puruvangaḷum takka tāmaraik kaṇṇum pāviyēn āviyin mēlanavē*

- *pakkam nōkki niṟkum* – She will be watching the side from where he may come; śrī rāmāyaṇam 16.25 “*naiśā paśyati rākśasyōnēmān puśpapaladrumān \| ēkasta hrudayānūnam rāmavēvānupaśyati \|\|*” (This sītā, is not noticing the demoniac ladies, and these trees with flowers and fruits do not have her attention; she is fully focussed on seeing śrī rāma only). “*naiśā paśyati …*” – For sītā, there is no difference when she sees the demoniac ladies or the flowers. “*ēkasta* …” – She is not seeing those who are near her. She becomes weakened since [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is not appearing in that direction \[where she is seeing\].
- *enṟu annaiyarum munidir* – You who very well know how you engaged me in his service when I was totally ignorant, as said in tiruvāimoḻi 3.3.3 “*aṟiyāk kālattuḷḷē adimaik kaṇ anbu seyvittu*“, are now scolding me. Her nature is as explained in śrī rāmāyaṇam bāla kāṇḍam 18.27 “*bālyāt prabruti susnigda:*” (right from childhood, lakśmaṇa was friendly towards śrī rāma).
- *takka* … – tirukkuṟungudi nambi who has fame as highlighted in every manner.
- *nān kaṇḍa pin* – After I, who has such fame of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) as my sustenance, have seen him.
- *tokka sōdit toṇḍai vāyum* – The divine lips which appear like a reddish fruit and having abundance of radiance. As said in tiruvāimoḻi 7.7.3 “*kōlam tiraḷ pavaḷak koḻum tuṇḍam*” (a piece of shining pearl with enriched beauty), the divine mouth/lips which appear like a ball of radiance and a toṇḍai/kōvai (a reddish) fruit. Usually, toṇḍai/kōvai fruit is compared to the mouth/lips \[though the divine mouth/lips have no match really\].
- *nīṇḍa puruvangaḷum* – The divine eyebrows which has no match, and is having unique fame due to not having any limit.
- *takka tāmaraik kaṇṇum* – Similar to the eyebrows which have no end to their length, the divine eyes which are inconceivable and are matching those eyebrows. The lotus flower can only be highlighted as a   sample, but is not really comparable to the eyes.
- *pāviyēn āviyin mēlanavē* – They are hurting the soul.
- *pāviyēn* – I am sinner – while the divine vision is nicely visible internally, I am not having the same externally.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.5.6. Melum van pali

*mēlum van paḻi nam kudikkivaḷ enṟu annai kāṇa kodāḷ sōlai sūḻ taṇ tirukkuṟungudi nambiyai nān kaṇḍa pin kōla nīḷ kodi mūkkum tāmaraik kaṇṇum kani vāyum neela mēniyum nāngu tōḷum en nenjam niṟaindanavē*

**Пословный перевод:**

nam kudikku – for our clan (which is waiting to see him come); ivaḷ – she (who is in haste to see him); mēlum – forever (not just today); van – tight (which is difficult to eliminate); paḻi – embodiment of ridicule; enṟu – saying that; annai – mother; kāṇa – to see nambi; kodāḷ – does not allow; sōlai – garden; sūḻ – surround; taṇ – invigorating; tirukkuṟungudi – of tirukkuṟungudi; nambiyai – nambi; nān – I (who has attachment which makes me consider those ridicules to be praises); kaṇḍa pin – after seeing; kōlam – beautiful; nīḷ – long; kodi – like a kalpaka (celestial plant/tree) creeper; mūkkum – divine nose; tāmarai – (like the flower of such creeper) resembling a lotus; kaṇṇum – divine eyes; kani – (like the fruit in that flower) ripened; vāyum – divine lips; neelam – (contrasting such reddish lips) having a blue complexion; mēniyum – divine form; nāngu – four; tōḷum – divine shoulders; en – my; nenjam – heart; niṟaindana – filled

**Перевод:**

**Mother of parānguśa nāyaki does not allow her to see nambi saying that she is an embodiment of ridicule forever; after seeing nambi of tirukkuṟungudi which is surrounded by invigorating garden, his beautiful long divine nose which resembles a kalpaka creeper, his divine eyes which resemble a lotus, his divine lips which resemble ripened fruit, his divine form which is having a blue complexion and his four divine shoulders filled my heart.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In  pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki says “nambi’s beauty of the divine limbs fully entered my heart and are hurting me”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, parānguśa nāyaki says “His distinguished physical features and shoulders along with his facial beauty, entered my heart and filled it”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*In  pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki says “nambi‘s beauty of his divine face and facial parts fully entered my heart and are hurting me”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. mēlum van paḻi nam kudikkivaḷ enṟu annai kāṇa kodāḷ sōlai sūḻ taṇ tirukkuṟungudi nambiyai nān kaṇḍa pin kōla nīḷ kodi mūkkum tāmaraik kaṇṇum kani vāyum neela mēniyum nāngu tōḷum en nenjam niṟaindanavē*

- *mēlum* … – Saying that “she will cause eternal blame to our clan, not just a few people blaming us, for now”.
- *annai kāṇa kodāḷ* – My own mother who prayed too long to beget me is saying like this, not those other mothers who helped her to raise me.
- *sōlai* … –  [nambi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)  of tirukkuṟungudi which is surrounded by invigorating garden.
- *nān kaṇḍa pin* – After I, who am engaged in him fully to consider ridicules as praises, have seen him. After I, who cannot be frightened by saying “others will ridicule you”, have seen.
- *kōla nīḷ* … – The divine nose which looks like an abundantly beautiful creeper, the divine eyes which are similar \[to the same beautiful creeper\]. The divine eyes appear like a flower blossomed out of the creeper.
- *kani vāyum* – The divine lips/mouth which appear like a fruit ripened out of that flower and the divine form which appears like the bluish leaf of that lotus flower; the divine form/body appears like a flood and the divine shoulders appear like floats on that flood.
- *en nenjam niṟindanavē* – I have no room in my heart for your advice \[since it is already filled with [nambi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) emperumān’s bodily features\].

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.5.7. Nirainda van pali

*niṟainda van paḻi nam kudikkivaḷ enṟu annai kāṇa kodāḷ siṟanda kīrttit tirukkuṟungudi nambiyai nān kaṇḍa pin niṟainda sōdi veḷḷam sūḻnda nīṇḍa pon mēniyodum niṟaindennuḷḷē ninṟoḻindān nēmi angaiyuḷadē*

**Пословный перевод:**

nam – our; kudikku – clan; ivaḷ – she (parānguśa nāyaki); niṟainda – complete; van – very strong; paḻi – ridicule; enṟu – saying that; annai – mother; kāṇa – to see; kodāḷ – not allowing; siṟanda – glorious; kīrtti – having fame; tirukkuṟungudi nambiyai – tirukkuṟungudi nambi; nān – I (who am captivated in such great fame); kaṇḍa pin – after enjoying; niṟainda – complete; sōdi veḷḷam – flood of radiance; sūḻnda – being surrounded; nīṇḍa – splendid; pon – attractive; mēniyōdum – with divine form; en uḷḷē – in my heart; niṟaindu – filled; ninṟu oḻindān – stood; nēmi – divine chakra (which is a unique symbol); am – beautiful; kai – in the divine hand; uḷadu – is present

**Перевод:**

**The mother is not allowing parānguśa nāyaki to see nambi saying “she is a complete and very strong ridicule to the whole clan”; after enjoying tirukkuṟungudi nambi who is having glorious fame, he stood in my heart with his splendid attractive divine form which is surrounded by complete flood of radiance; the divine chakra is also present in his beautiful divine hand.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the seventh pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki says “the total beauty of nambi‘s divine form took roots in my heart”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, parānguśa nāyaki says “nambi, along with his divine form which is infinitely radiant, splendid and attractive, stood in my heart with his divine chakra in his hand”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. niṟainda van paḻi nam kudikkivaḷ enṟu annai kāṇa kodāḷ siṟanda kīrttit tirukkuṟungudi nambiyai nān kaṇḍa pin niṟainda sōdi veḷḷam sūḻnda nīṇḍa pon mēniyodum niṟaindennuḷḷē ninṟoḻindān nēmi angaiyuḷadē*

- *niṟainda van paḻi* – āṇḍāḷ (the revered wife of [kūrattāḻvān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/kuraththazhwan/)) pointed [parāśara bhattar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/parasara-bhattar/) and [sīrāmap piḷḷai (vēda vyāsa bhattar)](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vedha-vyasa-bhattar/) to āḻvān and said to him “They have attained the right age for marriage; why are you not doing anything?”, and āḻvān said  “Alright! When I go to have darśan of [periya perumāḷ](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) tomorrow, you send them along with me”. On the next day, they all went to periya perumāḷ and stood in his divine presence; periya perumāḷ gave aruḷappādu (invitation to speak, through arcaka) and asked “āḻvān, it looks like you want to say something”. āḻvān mercifully replied “Others are saying that these two are ready for marriage”. Subsequently, their marriage got fixed \[by divine arrangement, with [periya nambi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/periya-nambi/) family\]. Thus, this clan remains “We should get the goal attained with [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s effort only and our desiring for something in itself is a ridicule”. mahābhāratam viṣṇu darmam ślokam is explained here to establish that bhagavān is the only upāyam (means) and other upāyams are actually hurdles in attaining the goal. *ata pātaka bītastvam* – It is well known that darmaputra lied once and had to visit naraka. He is known to have performed rājasūya yajñams and is not known to have committed any forbidden activities.  *ata pātaka bītastvam* – If you thought your previous activities were detrimental and became frightened, once you understand “All activities which are done with ahankāram (ego) and mamakāram (possessiveness) are detrimental when considered that kriṣṇa is the only refuge for all our goals”, you will understand that those activities are detrimental too. *vimukta* … – Instead of you yourself trying in different ways, giving up everything else, see that you place all the responsibility on emperumān thinking “let the lord fulfil our goals”. Now, the mother is trying to restrain [parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) saying “*paḻi*” (ridicule) which is nothing but attachment towards [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/); both the states of being the divine mother who tries to restrain her daughter saying “paḻi” and being parānguśa nāyaki, the daughter who says “*paḻi enṟu mīḷēn*” (I will not withdraw thinking that it is a ridicule), are different states of āḻvār himself; the instructions of the divine mother trying to withdraw parānguśa nāyaki resemble the first part of carama ślōkam in [śrī bhagavat gītā](http://githa.koyil.org/) where bhagavān is explained as the only means; parānguśa nāyaki’s words of saying “I won’t withdraw considering my effort to be a ridicule”, resemble the *niśkarśam* \[that one will surely attain kainkaryam\] in the second part of carama ślōkam. The mother tries to restrain her saying “*paḻi*” eliminates the defects in one’s pursuit of the means \[here, the defect is self-effort; one should fully depend on the lord\]; parānguśa nāyaki’s firm state saying “*paḻi enṟu mīḷēn*” eliminates the defects in one’s attainment of the goal \[here the defect is to be patient to attain the goal; one should have haste/urge in attaining the goal\]. Should the para bhakti (the state of knowing [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) as everything) which is part of the nature of the self, be renounced \[No\]! There is nothing extraneous or to be given up \[with regard to para bhakti\] in the true nature of the self which is explained in cāndōjña upaniśat 8.12 “*svēnarūpēṇa abiniśpadyatē*” (he attains his natural and distinguished state). When we look at the upāyam (means) \[i.e., bhagavān\], one will start fearing to consider even what is ordained to be done as means; when we look at the upēyam (goal) \[i.e., kainkaryam to bhagavān\], one cannot stop doing anything as in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 31.25 “*aham sarvam kariśyāmi*” (lakśmaṇa says – I will carry out all kainkaryams). One should not say “I gave these up fearing that they will become upāyam (my own effort)” for lazily giving up ordained activities due to old habits of nāstikyam (disbelief in śāstram); nor should one give up those activities \[kainkaryams\] which are done out of attachment towards [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) saying “what if these were considered to be upāyams (my own effort)?”. Our ācāryas/elders would engage in all activities \[kainkaryams\] like laukīka (worldly people) and yet will have no upāya buddi (the thought of those activities being means to attain something) \[It is important to note that kainkaryam in itself is the goal and not a means to achieve something else\]. Thus restraining oneself from pursuit of emperumān saying “*paḻi*” is the meaning of the first half of carama ślōkam; not giving up the pursuit saying “*paḻi*” is the meaning of the second half of carama ślōkam.
- *siṟanda* … – tirukkuṟungudi [nambi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who has matching fame.
- *nān kaṇḍa pin* – After I, who is as matching as such fame to him, have seen it. As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 37.18 “*yasya sā janakātmajā … apramēyam hi tat tēja:*” (The greatness of the one (śrī rāma) who is married to the daughter of janaka, is beyond comprehension), for emperumān, just like the fame, the relationship with her too is glory in itself – such [parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/).
- *niṟainda* … – Like those who reside amidst the tides of river gangā, his form is appearing amidst the flood of his radiance. One who has to assume the presence of his form amidst the radiance. And his form is so lofty to be conceived and great.
- *niṟaindu en uḷḷē ninṟu oḻindān* – Once when nanjīyar was going to the temple and met piḷḷān on the way. [nanjīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nanjiyar/) asked [piḷḷān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/pillan/) “Does īśvara have svarūpa vyāpti (pervading in a subtle form) only? does he also vigraha vyāpti (present in the heart, with a divine form)?”. piḷḷān explained “Generally \[with respect to every entity\], he is pervading with a subtle form only; but for devotees, out of his grace towards them, he is present in their heart with the form which they considered as auspicious target; now, wherever you observe pramāṇams (references in sacred texts) for svarūpa vyāpti, they highlight his general omnipresence and wherever you observe pramāṇams for vigraha vyāpti, they highlight his special presence in the hearts of his devotees”.
- *nēmi am kai uḷadē* – If the whole bodily beauty is of one scale, the beautiful combination of his divine hand and divine chakra is on a higher scale. Would I not give up my attachment, had he not held the divine chakra in his hand? As he is having the divine chakra in his hand, would it be possible for me to withdraw my attachment for him fearing ridicule \[of others\]?.
- *niṟaindu en uḷḷē ninṟu oḻindān* – He filled my heart and stood there so that I cannot listen to your advice.
- *ninṟu oḻindān* – As he arrives in to my heart giving up his travels, am I able to move around now? Can you not ask him to leave from my heart, so that I can avoid this ridicule? As he is beautiful on his own to be warded of evil eyes, if he has the divine chakra in his hand, can I restrain my attachment towards him? Can I minimize his completeness or the complete ridicule in me?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.5.8. Kaiyul nanmugam

*kaiyuḷ nanmugam vaikkum naiyum enṟu annaiyarum munidir mai koḷ mādat tirukkuṟungudi nambiyai nān kaṇḍa pin seyya tāmaraik kaṇṇum alkulum siṟṟidaiyum vadivum moyya nīḷ kuḻal tāḻnda tōḷgaḷum pāviyēn mun niṟkumē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kaiyuḷ – in the hand; nal – beautiful; mugam – face; vaikkum – placing; naiyum – (moreover) becomes weakened; enṟu – saying that; annaiyarum – you mothers who put in the efforts initially leading to this weakness in me; munidir – showing your anger; mai – blackish complexion; koḷ – having; mādam – having mansions; tirukkuṟungudi nambiyai – tirukkuṟungudi nambi; nān – I (who am naturally weak); kaṇḍa pin – after seeing; seyya – reddish; tāmarai – lotus like; kaṇṇum – divine eyes; alkulum – (enjoyable) hip; siṟu – thin (to be contained in a fist); idaiyum – waist; vadivum – the form (which is the abode for these beautiful aspects); moy – density; koḷ – having; nīḷ – lengthy; kuḻal – hair; tāḻnda – lowering; tōḷgaḷum – shoulders; pāviyēn – I who am having sin (which stops me from enjoying those desirable aspects); mun – in front of me; niṟkum – stood

**Перевод:**

**Saying that I am placing my beautiful face in my hand and becoming weakened, you mothers who put in the efforts initially leading to this weakness in me are showing your anger; after seeing nambi of tirukkuṟungudi which is having black coloured mansions, his reddish lotus like divine eyes, hip, thin waist, his form, his dense lengthy hair which are lowering on his shoulders are all standing in front of me who is a sinner.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the eighth pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki says “His shoulders which are touched by his beautiful hair and his other beautiful features appear in front of me and hurt me”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Eighth pāsuram. parānguśa nāyaki says “His wholesome physical beauty appears in front of me and hurts me”. kaiyuḷ nanmugam vaikkum naiyum enṟu annaiyarum munidir mai koḷ mādat tirukkuṟungudi nambiyai nān kaṇḍa pin seyya tāmaraik kaṇṇum alkulum siṟṟidaiyum vadivum moyya nīḷ kuḻal tāḻnda tōḷgaḷum pāviyēn mun niṟkumē*

- *kai uḷ nan mugam vaikkum* – Due to the suffering in separation from him, she placed her face in her hand (palm). She has become so adventurous. Should she not know the distinguished nature of her own face? śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 21.19 “*bhujam anyasya kasyacit*” (This arm was given as pillow-rest for the lord of the universe śrī rāma. How can I present this arm as pillow-rest for anyone else?). My face can only tolerate the touch of my beloved lord’s hand. By this, the pāratantriyam (ultimate subservience) which excludes self also, is explained. This is the exact meaning of the word “*nama:*” (not for me – only for [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)). Since the *ukāram* (“*u*” in praṇavam) which is the shortened version of this “*nama:*” explains this pāratantriyam, the same principle is applicable here in “*nama:*” too \[ukāram explains exclusive servitude/subservience for emperumān, and “*nama:”* extends it to further eliminate servitude/subservience to self\].
- *naiyum* – She becomes weakened since she cannot tolerate her own enjoyment.
- *enṟu annaiyarum munidir* – Why am I hating the accusations of the people of the town? \[mother is showing that first of all I should not be enjoying my own face\].
- *mai koḷ mādam* – \[Dark coloured mansions\] Due to the ancient nature and also due to nambi’s shadow falling on them as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 38.15 “*śobayan daṇḍakāraṇyam*” (śrī rāma’s divine form’s radiance spread through the forest and lit up the whole forest).
- *nān kaṇḍa pin* – After I, who am similar to those ancient mansions to become weakened, have seen him. She is said as in tiruvāimoḻi 2.1.6 “*naivāya emmē pōl*” (You are also weak like me).
- *seyya tāmaraik kaṇṇum* – The eyes which make one exist exclusively for [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/).
- *alkulum* – The lap where those who are captivated will rest and sustain themselves.
- *siṟṟidaiyum* – The waist portion which is so thin that it is assumed to exist as a connecting point between the upper and lower parts of the body.
- *vadivum* – His form which does not allow restraining myself. It is his form which does not allow her to restrain herself.
- *moyya* … – The divine attractive hair which is attractive and lowers itself into the shoulders which deserve to be embraced.
- *pāviyēn munniṟkumē* – When that which cannot be enjoyed appears in front, it leads to more anguish. As she is saying “*munniṟkum*” (standing in front), she is also saying “*pāviyēn*” (sinner \[who cannot enjoy it\]). It appears like a horse for an elephant, which runs just in reach of the elephant, yet can never be reached.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.5.9. Mun ninray

*mun ninṟāy enṟu tōḻimārgaḷum annaiyarum munidir mannu mādat tirukkuṟungudi nambiyai nān kaṇḍa pin senni nīḷ mudi ādiyāya ulappil aṇigalattan kannal pāl amudāgi vandu en nenjam kaḻiyānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

mun – in front; ninṟāy – stood; enṟu – saying that; tōḻimārgaḷum – the friends (who suffer along); annaiyarum – mothers (who seek out the well-being); munidir – were angry \[on me\]; mannum – firmly rooted; mādam – having mansions; tirukkuṟungudi nambiyai – tirukkuṟungudi nambi; nān – I (who am setting out to go without caring for my femininity); kaṇḍa pin – after seeing; senni – on the head; nīḷ – tall (which indicates supremacy over everyone); mudi – divine crown; ādiyāy – etc; ulappil – countless; aṇi – wore; kalattan – has ornaments; kannal – sugar; pāl – milk; amudu – like nectar; āgi – being infinitely enjoyable; vandu – came; en – my; nenjam – heart; kaḻiyān – is not leaving

**Перевод:**

**Friends and mothers are angry at me saying that I am standing in front; after seeing nambi of tirukkuṟungudi which is having firmly rooted tall mansions, he came with his tall divine crown on the head and countless ornaments, being infinitely enjoyable like sugar, milk and nectar, into my heart and is not leaving \[from there\].**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the ninth pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki says “nambi has entered my heart with all his beauty and never leaves there even for a moment so that I don’t forget him”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. mun ninṟāy enṟu tōḻimārgaḷum annaiyarum munidir mannu mādat tirukkuṟungudi nambiyai nān kaṇḍa pin senni nīḷ mudi ādiyāya ulappil aṇigalattan kannal pāl amudāgi vandu en nenjam kaḻiyānē*

- *mun ninṟāy enṟu* – It seems that [parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) has not even stood in front of her friends. She is like sītāp pirātti as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 33.8 “*yānaśakyāpurādraśtum būtairākāśakairapi*” (That sītā who could not be seen by the great elements too). Seeing her boldness \[in pursuing [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) by coming out\], irrespective of those who like her \[friends\] or who censure her \[mothers\], start censuring her.
- *mannu mādam* – As said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 5.38.9 “*vāsudēvagruham tvēkam  na plāvayati sāgara:*” (kriṣṇa’s palace cannot be destroyed even by the ocean), she is saying that these mansions will remain in tact even during praḷayam (deluge).
- *nān kaṇḍa pin* – I who will not withdraw. I who am free of any shyness.
- *senni* … – Starting with the crown on the top of his head, one who is having countless ornaments. One who is having countless divine ornaments starting with the divine crown on his head which reveals his supremacy.
- *aṇi kalan* – the divinely beautiful combination of ornaments.
- *kannal pāl amudu āgi* – This implies all types of tastes.
- *vandu* … – After arriving in my heart, he is not leaving. They cannot censure the one who brought me out in to the fore front \[emperumān\]; they are only capable of censuring me saying “*mun ninṟāy*” (you stood in front). I too desire to forget him, but am unable to do so \[you can suggest a way to forget him\].

## 5.5.10. Kaliya mikkadu

*kaḻiya mikkadōr kādalaḷ ivaḷ enṟu annai kāṇa kodāḷ vaḻuvil kīrttit tirukkuṟungudi nambiyai nān kaṇḍa pin kuḻumit tēvar kuḻāngaḷ kai toḻac cōdi veḷḷattin uḷḷē eḻuvadōr uru en nenjuḷ eḻum ārkkum aṟivaridē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ivaḷ – she; kaḻiya – to eliminate; mikkadu ōr – great; kādalaḷ – one who has love; enṟu – saying that; annai – mother; kāṇa – to see (nambi); kodāḷ – does not allow; vaḻuvil – unimpaired; kīrtti – having glories; tirukkuṟungudi nambiyai – tirukkuṟungudi nambi; nān – I (who am having overwhelming affection); kaṇḍa pin – after seeing; dēvar kuḻāngaḷ – groups of nityasūris; kuḻumi – associating with each other; kai toḻa – to be served and enjoyed; sōdi veḷḷattin uḷḷē – amidst a flood of radiance; eḻuvadu – appearing in a raised manner; ōr – unique; uru – the divine form, which is the apt destiny; en – my; nenjuḷ – in the heart; eḻum – appeared; ārkkum – for even those who are very wise; aṟivu – to know (through self effort); aridu – difficult

**Перевод:**

**My mother does not allow me to see nambi saying that she is having great love which cannot be eliminated; after seeing tirukkuṟungudi nambi who is having unimpaired glories, his divine form which is the apt destiny to be served and enjoyed by groups of nityasūris associating with each other and which appears in a raised manner amidst a flood of radiance, appeared in my heart; it is difficult to know for even those who are very wise.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In  pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki says “The manner in which nambi’s divine form shines in my heart is beyond the comprehension of anyone”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, parānguśa nāyaki says “The divine form which is enjoyed by nityasūris (eternal residents of paramapadam), is very radiant and apt goal, is shining in my heart to be comprehended by none”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. kaḻiya mikkadōr kādalaḷ ivaḷ enṟu annai kāṇa kodāḷ vaḻuvil kīrttit tirukkuṟungudi nambiyai nān kaṇḍa pin kuḻumit tēvar kuḻāngaḷ kai toḻac cōdi veḷḷattin uḷḷē eḻuvadōr uru en nenjuḷ eḻum ārkkum aṟivaridē*

- *kaḻiya mikkadu ōr kādalaḷ ivaḷ* – The love which does not have a match and cannot be seen in anyone else; alternative explanation – the love which keeps increasing as days go by; śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 5.4 “*śōkaścakila kālēna gaccatāhyabagaccati \| mamacāpaśyata:kāntāmahanyaha nivartatē \|\|*” (People in general will forget the sorrows as time goes by; but for me, as time goes by the sorrow increases) – people in general, will be very sad on the day of getting separated from their beloved person, and will recover subsequently and forget about that; but for me, as days go by, the sorrow keeps increasing.
- *annai kāṇa kodāḷ* – The mother who first thought “I should see her falling in love”, does not allow me to see him now. So why is she \[mother\] doing like this now? She would not let [parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) to have so much love to have herself finished \[in suffering\] and would like her to reach [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) and see them together. kāṇgai (seeing) means meditating here. It is said in periya tiruvantādi 28 “*nenjennum utkaṇ*” (the heart/mind which is known as the internal eye). The mother even controlled the heart of parānguśa nāyaki.
- *vaḻuvil …* – one who is having faultless glories.
- *nān* – Just as the glories have no separate existence from him, I who have no separate existence from him.
- *kaṇḍa pin* – What is it that [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is seeing? From tiruviruttam 1st pāsuram “*poyn ninṟa jñānamum*” upto \[just before\] tiruvāimoḻi 10.10.1 “*muniyē nānmuganē*“, everything is part of a single stream of consciousness. All the others in between these two are just the visualisations in his heart.
- *kuḻumi* … – The groups of nityasūris will engage in [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) as people will form a human chain \[to hold each other for safety\] and step in to a flood.
- *sōdi veḷḷattin uḷḷē eḻuvadu ōr uru* – As said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 1.9.67 “*tējasām rāśimūrjitam*” (collection of radiance), the form is to be assumed amidst the flood of radiance.
- *en nenjuḷ eḻum* – He will shine in my heart, as he is shining amidst the nityasūris.

When mother asks “But we are not seeing that”, she replies,

- *ārkkum aṟivu aridē* – Just as I cannot forget him, he cannot be known \[seen\] by one’s own self effort.
