## 5.7 Norra nonbilen

## 5.7.1. Norra nonbilen

*nōṟṟa nōnbilēn nuṇṇaṟivilēn āgilum ini unnai vittonṟum āṟṟagiṟkinṟilēn aravin aṇai ammānē! sēṟṟut tāmarai sennel ūdu malar sirīvaramangala nagar vīṟṟirunda endāy! unakku migai allēn angē*

**Пословный перевод:**

nōṟṟa – performed to attain the result; nōnbu – karma yōgam; ilēn – I do not have; nuṇ – in subtle form; aṟivu – jñāna yōgam which is focussed on knowledge about self and god; ilēn – I do not have; āgilum – though not having bhakti yōgam which is possible by having these two, i.e., karma yōgam and jñāna yōgam; ini – after meditating upon your qualities; unnai – you (who are the saviour); vittu – other than; onṟum – even for a moment; āṟṟa – to survive; kiṟkinṟilēn – unable; aravu – ādiśēśa who is your servitor; aṇai – as mattress and favouring him by placing your divine body on him; ammānē – being the distinguished lord; sēṟu – muddy field; tāmarai – lotus flower; sennel ūdu – mingled with paddy crop; malar – attractive to be blossoming; sirīvaramangala nagar – in śrīvaramangala nagar; vīṟṟu – being distinguished, manifesting your readiness to protect well your devotees; irunda – being seated; endāy – Oh benefactor for me!; angu – in your presence there; unakku – you who are the saviour; migai – outside the savable souls; allēn – I am not

**Перевод:**

**I have not performed karma yōgam to attain the result; I have not performed jñāna yōgam which is in subtle form and is focussed on knowledge about self and god; though not having bhakti yōgam which is possible by having these two, i.e., karma yōgam and jñāna yōgam, I am unable to survive even for a moment without you after meditating upon your qualities; Oh benefactor for me who is seated in a distinguished manner manifesting your readiness to protect well your devotees in śrīvaramangala nagar \[vānamāmalai/tōtādri, also known as nāngunēri\] where attractive lotus flower is blossoming while being mingled with paddy crop in muddy fields! In your presence there, I am not an outsider to the savable souls who are to be saved by you who are the saviour.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the first pāsuram, āḻvār who is devoid of upāyams (means) such as karma yōgam etc and who is desirous of a saviour, sees emperumān who is complete and is seeking those who seek his protection, and sets out to have his desire fulfilled.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*In the first pāsuram, āḻvār says “I am devoid of upāyams mentioned in śāstram to attain you, and cannot survive without you; am I outside the purview of you who are a favourer in being together with your devotees and who are ready to help others?”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. nōṟṟa nōnbilēn nuṇṇaṟivilēn āgilum ini unnai vittonṟum āṟṟagiṟkinṟilēn aravin aṇai ammānē! sēṟṟut tāmarai sennel ūdu malar sirīvaramangala nagar vīṟṟirunda endāy! unakku migai allēn angē*

- *nōṟṟa nōnbilēn nuṇṇaṟivilēn* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying similar to what is said in [stōtra ratnam 22](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/01/sthothra-rathnam-22/) “*na dharma niśtōsmi na cātmavēdī na bhaktimāmstvaccaraṇāravindē*” \[Though āḷavandār appears after āḻvār, here the commentator has stated that āḻvār is stating similar to what is stated by āḷavandār, to make us understand the similarity. In reality, āḷavandār explained what is already explained by āḻvār\]. *na dharma niśtōsmi* – There are certain aspects which make people think “he is engaging in some pursuit on his own”, which in turn makes me bewildered thinking “we will attain something by this” and will lead you to give up on me \[since you are the real means to attain you, you cannot tolerate any other means\], but will not lead to the result \[i.e., there is no guarantee that the result will be achieved by karma yōgam etc\]. *na ca ātma vēdi* – those who pursue jñāna yōgam will know about self – I don’t even have such knowledge. I don’t have knowledge about īśvara which is preceded by true knowledge about self as said in śrī viṣṇu purāṇam 6.5.57 “*tat jñānam ajñānam ata: anyat uktam*” (Knowledge about [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is only identified as knowledge; everything else is ignorance only). *na bhaktimān* – No need to separately say “I have no bhakti” – only with karma yōgam and jñāna yōgam, bhakti yōgam can be present.
- *nōṟṟa nōnbilēn* – Is it not sufficient to say *nōnbilēn* \[to indicate that he is not engaged in karma yōgam\]? Should [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) say *nōṟṟa nōnbilēn*? This is to indicate “I do not have any karma yōgam, which is performed perfectly to lead to the desired result”. \[was there any one who waited for results after engaging in karma yōgam\] I do not have karma yōgam like that which was practiced by daśarata cakravarty or śrī vasudēva which leads to the result.
- *nuṇṇaṟivilēn* – In “*na dharma niśtōsmi*“, āḷavandār says that he does not have “*dharma niśtai*” \[faith in dharma\] instead of saying “*dharma*” \[dharma itself\]. Similarly, here, āḻvār says “*nuṇṇaṟivilēn*” instead of saying “*aṟivilēn*“. I do not have the knowledge through which one can first understand the true nature of the self and then go on to understand the true nature of [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/). Why is āḻvār not first highlighting and then discarding bhakti as done in “na bhaktimān” or in [tirumālai 25](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/10/thirumalai-25/) “*nin kaṇum pattan allēn*” (I am not your devotee)? bhakti only occurs when karma yōgam and jñāna yōgam are present as said in ātma siddi “*ubhaya parikrimitasvāntasya*” (for the one whose mind is decorated with karma and jñāna); since both of those are not present, there is no need to first highlight it and then discard it. Now, in the same manner, when it is said that “there is no karma yōgam”, what is the need for separately saying “there is no jñāna yōgam”? Well, if one performs karma yōgam to its perfection in one birth and dies before starting jñāna yōgam, it will continue in the next birth. Can the same not be said for bhakti yōgam? No – when karma and jñāna are practiced to their perfection, they will culminate in bhakti immediately, and hence it is necessary to highlight karma and jñāna separately, but bhakti need not be highlighted separately. When he says “*unnai vittu onṟum āṟṟagiṟkinṟilēn*“, does it not mean bhakti, since it is said “*snēha pūrvam anudyānam bhakti:*” (meditation with affection is bhakti); in this case, can this statement be considered as upāyam \[[āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s own pursuit to attain [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)\]? That cannot be said. The parabhakti (ultimate state of bhakti) which is acquired by one who has perfected karma and jñāna yōgams is only called as sādanam (means) in śāstram; but āḻvār’s state of mind is acquired based on [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s mercy and hence it is just svarūpam \[his nature is to be greatly devoted towards bhagavān, and not as means to pursue him\]. Alternative explanation – since karma and jñāna yōgams are explained as independent upāyams in purāṇams (ancient sacred texts), these statements can simply mean that āḻvār does not have any of those means independently. \[āḻvār pursuing emperumān here is explained generally as adikāri viśēśaṇam (a natural attribute of a [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) who has realized emperumān as the master). It should not be treated as upāyam. As such, a jīvātmā cannot pursue any upāyam other than emperumān to attain emperumān. So, here the desire to attain emperumān is to be treated as natural attribute only and not otherwise\]

When asked, like those who do not have any principal will not get any interest, if these don’t exist how would you get the result?

- *āgilum* – Even if this is the case. Even if you \[[bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)\] considered “*āṟṟagiṟkinṟilēn*” as my upāyam (means), there is no meaning for my using the word “*āgilum*” \[in spite of not having any means\].

When [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) asked [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) “But were you not patient all along?”, āḻvār says,

- *ini* – Is it not appropriate for me to miss out on you when I did not know you and myself? But should I still miss out on you after knowing your completeness and my defects? When a person has food in his hands and is willing to share it with others, and another person is needing food and is hungry, should the hungry person miss out?
- *ini* – Am I having something in my hand and waiting for it to culminate in result? You may consider my sattai (that which sustains me) as upāyam (means) and discard me. Since time immemorial, I had forgotten my nature and lost the opportunity to serve you. Now that I have truly accepted your lordship, should I still miss out on the opportunity to serve you eternally?
- *unnai vittu* – If you too are \[incomplete\] like me, will I not be relaxed \[and not think about attaining you immediately\]? Are you such that, I have to do something to attain you?
- *unnai vittu* – How can the body sustain itself without the soul?
- *onṟum āṟṟagiṟkinṟilēn* – The knowledge about you, is not letting me sustain myself. sītāp pirātti had a way to sustain herself saying as in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 39.30 “*tatdasya sadruśam bhavēt”* (śrī rāma saving me and accepting me will match his stature) and relax, but for [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/), [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) need not build a bridge on the ocean and kill rāvaṇa \[so he must come immediately\].
- *aravin aṇai ammānē* – Until now, āḻvār highlighted his own incompleteness; from now on, he is highlighting emperumān’s completeness.
- *aravin aṇai* – Can I be relaxed seeing your attachment towards bhōgam (bhōga means enjoyment as well as serpent)? While you are paramabhōgi (supreme enjoyer, supreme being on the serpent bed), can I be relaxed? anantaśāyitvam (reclining on ādiśēśa) is an indication of supremacy. Oh [sarvēśvara](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) who is having serpent as your bed!
- *sēṟṟut tāmarai …* – I can be relaxed and be patient if you are simply reclining on ādiśēśan.
- *sēṟṟut tāmarai* – The abode which will make one forget even paramapadam. In the muddy swamps, the lotus flowers standing close to the paddy crop, blossom appearing like umbrella to the crop. As the king descends to a place, his associates will follow \[similarly, as [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) descended from paramapadam to śrīvaramangala nagar, nityasūris too followed him and assumed various forms\].
- *sirīvaramangala nagar* – As said in “*dēvanāmbhū: ayōdyā*” (ayōdyā \[another name for paramapdam\] is the abode of nityasūris). emperumān residing in this abode with more joy than in paramapadam. The abode where he permanently resides for the protection of the samsāris (worldly people).
- *vīṟṟirunda* – Instead of residing with disgust thinking “I who resided in that great paramapadam, have to reside here now”, residing joyfully in a distinguished manner as a prisoner who was crowned in a kingdom would be.
- *endāy* – Just as his stay there is meant for the nityasūris, the stay here is specifically meant for me. My father who is residing in sirīvaramangala nagar.
- *unakku migai allēn* – If you resided in the distant abode of paramapadam, I can be patient and sustain myself, but you have specifically descended here for me, and hence, how can I miss out on you any more?
- angē vīṟṟirunda unakku migai allēn – I am not outside the reach of you who are desirous of protection seekers. Alternatively,
- *unakku migai allēn* – As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 31.32 “*vaidarmyam nēhavidyatē*” (there is no unrighteousness in this), I am not here for anything else. When I am beyond your reach, I will cease to exist.

When asked “what is the benefit for me?”, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says,

- *angē* – As said in “*tavacārta prakalpatē*” (it is a gain for your highness only), the benefit is also for your highness only. As a nursing mother will be happy to see the satisfied face of a fully fed baby, the master will gain when the servitor realizes his true nature and engages in servitude.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.7.2. Angurren allen

*anguṟṟēn allēn inguṟṟēn allēn unnaik kāṇum avāvil vīḻndu nān enguṟṟēnum allēn ilangai seṟṟa ammānē tingaḷ sēr maṇi māda nīdu sirīvaramangala nagar uṟai sangu cakkarattāy tamiyēnukkaruḷāyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

anguṟṟēn – entered into your apt abode, having you as ready means; allēn – I have not; inguṟṟēn – remaining patiently where I am now; allēn – I am not; unnai – you (who are infinitely enjoyable); kāṇum – to enjoy; avāvil – due to love; vīḻndu – being captivated; nān – I (who am grieving); enguṟṟēnum – in the state of worldly people too; allēn – not present; ilangai – lankā which was a hurdle for your devotee (sītāp pirātti); seṟṟa – destroyed and attained; ammānē – Oh my distinguished lord!; tingaḷ – moon; sēr – to reach; maṇi – abundance of emeralds; mādam – mansions; nīdu – rising; sirīvaramangala nagar – in śrīvaramangala nagar; uṟai – residing eternally; sangu cakkarattāy – one who is having special weapons which are both meant to destroy the enemies of the devotees and being enjoyable for the devotees; tamiyēnukku – I who am lonely without anyone other than you as companion; aruḷāy – mercifully bless me

**Перевод:**

**I have not entered into your apt abode, having you as ready means; I am not remaining patiently where I am now; being captivated in love to enjoy you, I am not present in the state of worldly people too; Oh my distinguished lord who destroyed lankā which was a hurdle for your devotee (sītāp pirātti) and attained her! Oh one who is having special weapons which are both meant to destroy the enemies of the devotees and being enjoyable for the devotees and who is residing eternally in śrīvaramangala nagar which has rising mansions which are with abundance of emeralds and reach up to the moon! Mercifully bless me who is lonely without anyone other than you as companion.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the second pāsuram, āḻvār says “If there are hurdles in attaining your divine feet, you have to remove those yourself and protect me out of your own mercy”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Second pāsuram. emperumān says “Just by saying ‘āṟṟēn’, what will you get? Hurdles still exist”; āḻvār says “As you eliminated the hurdles for sītāp pirātti, you should mercifully eliminate my hurdles too”. anguṟṟēn allēn inguṟṟēn allēn unnaik kāṇum avāvil vīḻndu nān enguṟṟēnum allēn ilangai seṟṟa ammānē tingaḷ sēr maṇi māda nīdu sirīvaramangala nagar uṟai sangu cakkarattāy tamiyēnukkaruḷāyē*

- *anguṟṟēn allēn* – I am not walking around \[confidently\] in this world as a sidda sādanan (one who is fully considering [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) as the means) just as muktātmās were walking around in this material realm.
- *inguṟṟēunum allēn* – I am also unlike those people of this realm who are engaged in sādanā \[bhakti yōgam\].

Alternative explanation:

- *anguṟṟēn allēn* – I am not the one who is fully enjoying you and not thinking about the worldly aspects as said in cāndōjña upaniśat 8.12.3 “*nōpajanam smaran idam śarīram*” ([ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) will not contemplate about the material body after reaching the spiritual realm).
- *inguṟṟēn allēn* – I am also not living as said in periya tirumoḻi 6.2.2 “*maṟandēn unnai munnam*” (I forgot you previously), forgetting you and considering sensual pleasures as the goal as said in periya tirumoḻi 1.1.1 “*avar tarum kalaviyē karudi*” (considering the embrace of woman only). Since [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is protected by [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) as said in tiruviruttam 95 “*yādānum paṟṟi nīngum virdattai nalvīdu seyyum*” (emperumān will relieve jīvātmā who has vowed to leave emperumān by pursuing any other materialistic aspects), he would be forgetful of emperumān.
- *unnai …* – emperumān asks “But in future, are you capable of doing anything?”, āḻvār replies – I have already mentioned to you \[in pāsuram 1\] “*unnai vittu onṟum āṟṟagiṟkinṟilēn*” (I am unable to sustain myself in separation from you). One who is able to do something will have strength to do so. Having become weakened as a result of the desire to see you, I cannot pursue any other upāyam now. This is the explanation given by pūrvācāryas.

\[This is explanation given by nampiḷḷai\]

- *anguṟṟēn allēn* – I am not amidst nityasūris \[in paramapadam\] being at par with them.
- *inguṟṟēnum allēn* – I am not just eating, wearing different clothes etc like the samsāris would do.
- *unnai* … – This being the case, I cannot remain sustaining myself until you come and appear in front of me.
- *avāvil vīḻndu nān* – I have fallen in this ocean of love \[towards you\] and unable to reach the shore as said in periya tirumoḻi 4.9.3 “*āsai ennum kadalil vīḻndu angu ayarttōm*” (fallen in the ocean of love and felt helpless).
- *ilangai seṟṟa ammānē* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) noticed that he has nothing in him, and hence looks up to sītāp pirātti who got her desires fulfilled; just as someone who has nothing in his hands, will look up to previously accumulated and available wealth.
- *ilangai seṟṟa ammānē* – Since [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is called as ammān (svāmy – lord), it is his gain if he delivers āḻvār. When svarūpam (true nature) shines in oneself, his responsibilities can be pushed to [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/), and he too has the aptness to eliminate the hurdles and embrace him just as he would do for his divine consorts.

When emperumān said “Yes I have done all of that. But now, the times have changed. rāmāvatāram is over long ago”, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says “you have solved that issue as well”.

- *tingaḷ …* – Unlike the avatārams where you leave at a particular time, are you not permanently residing in śrīvaramangala nagar where gem studded tall mansions reaching up to the moon are present?
- *tingaḷ sēr maṇimāda nīdu* – The gem studded tall mansions appearing to be rising up to the moon.

When asked “Even if he is present there, does he have the tools \[to eliminate the hurdles\]?”, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) replies,

- *sangu cakkarattāy* – Can we highlight such limitation? He is having a weapon in each of his hands. Does he lack something as it was mentioned in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 21.22 “*cāpamānaya saumitrē*” (Oh lakśmaṇa! bring my bow) \[No, he has all the weapons\]? Do you need to look for someone’s help here \[No\]? Furthermore, do you need the help of any tools \[weapons\] to have your desires fulfilled \[No\]? Why am I still missing out? Is it due to you not being present in close proximity? or due to your not having the ability? or due to not having the weapons? or are those weapons not in your reach?

[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) says “Everything is perfect on my side; but you too should not be lacking in anything \[i.e., you too should have the desire to attain me\]”, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) replies,

- *tamiyēnukku* – āḻvār is saying “there is nothing lacking in me too”. I am unlike the residents of paramapadam who have never separated from you. And I am unlike the residents of this world who have never separated from you. For people of this world, since they have no knowledge about you, they don’t feel the separation from you.
- *tamiyēnukku* – For me who has no companion other than you. You can discard me only if you consider my natural attachment towards you as my self-effort in pursuing you. Even if you remain the upāyam (means), should there not be someone who accepts you as upāyam \[I am one such qualified person who accepts you as upāyam\]?
- *tamiyēn* – \[lonely\] [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is differentiating himself from sītāp pirātti. There was at least trijadā who was favourable towards pirātti. Here āḻvār is so lonely that he says in [tiruvāimoḻi 5.1.9](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/05/thiruvaimozhi-5-1-9-avarar-thunai/) “*āvār Ar tuṇai*” (who is my companion?).

[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) asks “Alright. What shall I do now?”, āḻvār says,

- *aruḷāyē* – Did your mercy which was shown by you initially and which made me realise my emptiness and your completeness, disappear now? Did you, who bestowed your mercy when I did not ask for back then, do that to create the desire in me \[towards you\] and discard me? Can one person bestow the ruci (taste) and another person perform the subsequent pursuit \[as you bestowed the taste, you have to make sure that I am delivered too\]? If you cannot show your mercy to me who remains as said in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 5.4.1 “*ninnaruḷē purindirundēn*” (I desired for your mercy only), who else are you planning to show it?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.7.3. Karulap putkodi

*karuḷap putkodi cakkarappadai vāna nāda em kār mugil vaṇṇā poruḷ allāda ennaip poruḷ ākki adimai koṇḍāy teruḷ koḷ nān maṟai vallavar palar vāḻ sirīvaramangala nagarkku aruḷ seydangirundāy! aṟiyēn oru kaimmāṟē*

**Пословный перевод:**

karuḷan – garuda; puḷ – bird; kodi – as flag; cakkaram – divine chakra (disc); padai – as weapon; vānam – paramapadam (spiritual realm); nāda – have as kingdom; kār mugil – like a dark cloud (which does not expect anything from the recipient of its rain); em – bestowed for me; vaṇṇā – having a form; poruḷ – as an entity; allāda – cannot be considered, as said in “asannēva” (non-existent); ennai – me; poruḷ – to realize my nature; ākki – acknowledge; adimai – vācika kainkaryam (service by speech); koṇḍāy – being the one who accepted; teruḷ – great knowledge; koḷ – having; nāl – four types; maṟai – vēdams \[sacred texts\]; vallavar – who have mastered (at their will); palar – many; vāḻ – living (endowed with bhagavat anubhavam (experience of lord)); sirīvaramangala nagarkku – to śrīvaramangala nagar; aruḷ – infinite mercy; seydu – showed; angu – there; irundāy – oh one who is residing!; oru – a; kaimmāṟu – gratitude, return of favour; aṟiyēn – do not know that I have done

**Перевод:**

**emperumān is having garuda bird as his flag, divine chakra as his weapon and paramapadam as his kingdom; he is having a dark cloud like form which he bestowed to me; with that form, he transformed me who cannot be considered as an entity as said in “asannēva” (like acit) to realize my nature; he acknowledged and accepted my vācika kainkaryam; Oh you, who are residing in śrīvaramangala nagar where many who have mastered the four vēdams, having great knowledge, are living and showed your mercy there; I do not know of any gratitude, return of your favour, which I have done.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the third pāsuram, emperumān asks “What is the gain for me to accept you?”, and āḻvār replies “I cannot see any gain for you who are complete in all manner, in accepting me who am very inferior; you did only out of your mercy. In the same manner, please fulfil my desires too”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “I have not done any favour in return for the your favour of accepting me and engaging me in service of you who have distinguished symbols which manifest your supremacy”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Third pāsruam. emperumān says “You said ‘show me mercy’; Alright, we will do; nothing to worry there; but as said in pūrva mīmāmsā “śāstrapalam prayōktari” (When ātmā becomes kartā (doer), śāstram is of use) and in brahma sūtram “kartā śāstrārtavatvāt” (If śāstram is of use, ātmā should be the doer), those who receive the mercy should also have something in them”, and āḻvār replies “is this a rule only for what is to come? did I have anything previously \[when you blessed me originally\]? hence, give up the expectation of even a little bit from me and just do it out of your mercy”. āḻvār says “Just as you have acknowledged me out of your causeless mercy to get me thus far, you have to mercifully do the rest as well”. karuḷap putkodi cakkarappadai vāna nāda em kār mugil vaṇṇā poruḷ allāda ennaip poruḷ ākki adimai koṇḍāy teruḷ koḷ nān maṟai vallavar palar vāḻ sirīvaramangala nagarkku aruḷ seydangirundāy! aṟiyēn oru kaimmāṟē*

- *karuḷap putkodi* – did you bestow your mercy earlier upon me knowing you \[your greatness\] or me \[my lowliness\]!
- *karuḷap putkodi* – Is your supremacy such that, it needs anything more? Your supremacy is such that you have periya tiruvadi (garudāḻvār) as your flag. garudāḻvār is known as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.4.6](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/07/thiruvaimozhi-1-4-6-arulatha-nir/) “*aruḷ āḻip puḷ*” (garudāḻvār who is an ocean of mercy).
- *cakkarap padai* – Is the chakra present such that, there is need for garudāḻvār to appear \[No, chakra itself is sufficient to prove his supremacy\]? sudarśana chakra is said as in tiruviruttam 33 “*aruḷār tiruccakkarattāl*” (the chakra which is filled with mercy).
- *vāna nāda* – Should he be carried by something (garudāḻvār) or hold something (chakra)? Is his residence itself not sufficient? He is having periya tiruvadi as flag, divine chakra as weapon and paramapadam as residence. Riding on periya tiruvadi, holding chakra without getting tired and having paramapadam as his residence – these are the identification marks of the supreme lord; though just one of these is sufficient for him, it is explained here that he is complete in all aspects here.
- *karuḷap puḷ* – puḷ indicates bird species, and it is specifically highlighted as garuda bird. As “īdē” is written as “īḷē” in tamiḻ, garuda is written as karuḷa. Alternative explanation – karuḷ indicates black, which means anger and hence saying “garuda who is angry on the enemies”. It is said in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 4.9.3 “*karuḷudaiya poḻil marudu*” (the two angry maruda trees appearing like a garden).
- *em kār mugil vaṇṇā* – Did you see your supremacy or the entity \[me\] on which you are showering your mercy! Oh one who manifested your magnanimity all the way down to me! You did this without any expectation, without seeing my \[lowly\] nature.

When asked “What is the favour done by [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)?”, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says,

- *poruḷ allāda …* – Did you elevate a pre-existing entity? Prior to your acceptance, I was as said in taittirīya upaniśat “*asannēva sa bhavati*” (one who is ignorant of God, is considered to be non-existent) and you uplifted such me as said in the same passage “*santamēnam*” (the learned people accept him to exist).
- *adimai koṇḍāy* – You engaged me in service which is performed by nityasiddars (eternally free souls) as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 3.7.5](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/10/thiruvaimozhi-3-7-5-peru-makkal/) “*peru makkaḷ uḷḷavar*” (for the nityasūris who have greatness of having parama sāmyāpatti (having similar qualities to those of [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s)). Not only you created me, you also helped me live. This is how \[by accepting my service\] what he said in “*kārmugil*” (dark cloud), materialized \[like a cloud will give life to the crops etc\]. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) indicates what is said in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.1.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/03/thiruvaimozhi-1-1-1-uyarvara-uyarnalam/) “*adi toḻudeḻu*” (worship his divine feet and rise) by the term “*adimai koṇḍāy*“. As āḻvār who was divinely blessed by emperumān with knowledge and devotion speaks in this manner \[i.e., very lowly of himself\], it is to be understood that the result of true knowledge will make one highlight his/her own faults; being egotistic as said in “*īśvarōham*” (I am God) is the result of ignorance.
- *teruḷ koḷ nānmaṟai vallavar* – Those who have understood the essence of vēdam clearly. Those who are having great wisdom, and are able to excel in vēdam which is divided into four categories (namely rig, yajur, sāma, atarvaṇa).
- *palar –* Not just one or two, but many groups as seen in śrīvaikuṇṭam (the spiritual realm).
- *vāḻ* – Those who visualise and enjoy [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is the essence of vēdam. Though many creatures live in holy rivers, their sins do not get washed up since they lack knowledge \[about [self](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/), [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/), the sacred nature of the river they live etc\]; unlike these creatures, the residents of this divyadēśam have both knowledge and adequate practice.
- *sirīvaramangala nagarkku aruḷ seydu angu irundāy* – He is residing there giving himself to the residents there and considering such act of his as his own gain. It was not that the residents of sirīvaramangala nagar requested [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) to come and stay there, but out of his own natural compassion, he descended there.  Also explained as – you descended there to accept my \[[āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s\] service. You thought “We have brought āḻvār up to kainkaryam, and hence there should not be any break” and descended there.
- *aṟiyēn oru kaimmāṟē* – For all that you have done, I do not know if I have done anything \[in return\]. If you say that I have done something to trigger your mercy \[since I do not know what I have done\], still you have to fulfil the subsequent aspects. You cannot say “I helped you since you existed”, since I have already mentioned “*poruḷ allāda ennaip poruḷākki adimai koṇḍāy*” (You made me exist as an entity, when I remained like a non-existent entity, and then accepted my service).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.7.4. Maru ser padai

*māṟu sēr padai nūṟṟuvar manga ōr aivarkkāy anṟu māyap pōr paṇṇi nīṟu seyda endāy nilam kīṇḍa ammānē! tēṟu jñānattar vēda vēḷvi aṟāc cirīvaramangala nagar ēṟi vīṟṟirundāy unnai engeydak kūvuvanē?*

**Пословный перевод:**

māṟu – being inimical; sēr – gathered; padai – having armies; nūṟṟuvar – duryōdana and his brothers, one hundred of them; manga – to die; ōr – lonely; aivarkku – the five pāṇḍavas; āy – determined to help; anṟu – back then (when they were affected by duryōdana et al); māyam – amazing acts (such as changing day into night); pōr – battle; paṇṇi – performed; nīṟu – to become dust; seyda – made; endāy – being great benefactor; nilam – bhūmi (earth, which could do nothing like the pāṇḍavas); kīṇḍa – lifted it up during the danger of total deluge; ammānē – being the lord; tēṟu – having clarity (in prāypyam (goal) and prāpakam (means)); jñānattar – of those who have knowledge; vēdam – vaidika (as per vēdam); vēḷvi – worship of bhagvān \[vēḷvi – yāgam – worship of bhagavān\]; aṟā – happening continuously; sirīvaramangala nagar – in śrīvaramangala nagar; ēṟi – entered there (just as they have entered there); vīṟṟu – showing distinction (that he is vorśippable and they are the ones who worship him); irundāy – Oh one who is present!; unnai – you (who are engaged in protection without any expectation and who cannot be attained by any other means); engu – where; eyda – attain; kūvuvan – will I call out?

**Перевод:**

**Being great benefactor, back when duryōdana et al were inimical towards pāṇḍavas, you performed the battle with amazing acts with determination to help the lonely pāṇḍavas and kill duryōdana et al and changed them to dust; being the lord you lifted bhūmi up during the danger of total deluge; Oh one who entered śrīvaramangala nagar where worship of bhagavān is performed continuously as per vēdam by those who have clear knowledge, and is present there showing distinction! \[without your help\] How will I call out for you and attain you?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fourth pāsuram, āḻvār shows some examples where emperumān protects without any expectation and says “unless you protect me like that I cannot do anything”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “How can I attain you who are the saviour of your devotees, through my desire as means?”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Fourth pāsuram. emperumān says “You say that I should protect you with my causeless grace; have I done that anywhere before?” and āḻvār highlights a couple of examples and says “Did you not do those? You should do the same for me too”. māṟu sēr padai nūṟṟuvar manga ōr aivarkkāy anṟu māyap pōr paṇṇi nīṟu seyda endāy nilam kīṇḍa ammānē! tēṟu jñānattar vēda vēḷvi aṟāc cirīvaramangala nagar ēṟi vīṟṟirundāy unnai engeydak kūvuvanē?*

- *māṟu sēr padai nūṟṟuvar* – The hundred brothers who arrived with an inimical army. The army did not just come to help them, but were individually inimical towards kriṣṇa. padai – Army. Alternative explanation –  The hundred brothers who are inimical \[towards kriṣṇa\] with their weapons. padai – weapon. As said in mahābhāratam “*dviśadannam na bhōktavyam …*” (kriṣṇa said – Neither should one accept food from enemies nor should serve them food; Oh duryōdana! since you considered pāṇḍavas as your enemies and as pāṇḍavas are my life \[you are my enemy\]”), kriṣṇa considered them as his own enemies.
- *manga* – to die. He destroyed them to be not seen similar to darkness \[which cannot be seen\].
- *ōr aivarkkāy* – Though both kauravas and pāṇḍavas are equally related to kriṣṇa, he sided with the humbler side of pāṇḍavas. The five brothers who were so lonely that even kriṣṇa, their own sārati (charioteer), placed himself as secondary having vowed not to take up arms.
- *aivarkkāy* – kaṇṇan [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) remained fully at their disposal.
- *anṟu* – Back when the kauravas were ready to attack in the war.
- *māyap pōr paṇṇi* – It is said as amazing war as well as mischievous war; that is, his acts of changing day into night, vowing not to take up arms and still taking up arms, and showing the lifelines of the enemies.
- *nīṟu seyda* – Turned them (enemies) to ashes. As said in tiruvāimoḻi 6.10.2 “*kūṟāy nīṟāy nilanāgi*” (first will cut them, turn them into ashes and then flatten them fully to the ground).
- *endāy* – His considering the destruction of kauravas for the sake of pāṇḍavas, as his own gain.

[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) says “Whatever you said is correct. But were they \[pāṇḍavas\] all not obedient towards me?”, and [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) replies “You protected the earth, without even looking for such obedience”.

- *nilam kīṇḍa ammānē* – Alright, you can leave that aside since you can cite a reason in the case of pāṇḍavas; what can you say about this earth \[which is considered as an acētana – insentient, and hence cannot show obedience towards you\], which was consumed by deluge?
- *nilam kīṇḍa* – Did you not help earth which neither requested you to help to start with nor showed gratitude for your help? In this case, only you have attachment towards earth and the earth on its own cannot reciprocate.
- *ammānē* – Did you not help the earth out of your own mercy thinking “I cannot lose my property”?
- *tēṟu jñānattar …* – Those who are very clear in being able to treat anuśtānam (practice of principles) and ananuśtānam (disregard for principles and not putting them into practice) equally. That is, anananuśtānam is not the means \[to attain [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)\]. Just as knowing well that “engaging in forbidden activities is not a means to liberation”, they would remain “engaging in ordained activities is not a means to liberation”. But then, why do they practice ordained activities \[only\]? That is, to fulfil the orders of [īśvara](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/). Now, just as forbidden activities will stimulate one’s rajas (passion) and tamas (ignorance), ordained activities will stimulate one’s satvam (goodness); since a cētana cannot survive without engaging in actions \[it is better to engage in ordained activities\]. As said in śrī bhagavat gītā 14.17 “*satvāt sanjāyatē jñānam*” (activities in satva guṇam (mode of goodness) will lead to true knowledge), since sātvika activities lead to jñānam, these must be performed.
- *sirīvaramangala nagar ēṟi vīṟṟirundāy* – He too has arrived in this divyadēśam like those knowledgeable persons and is residing there amidst them.
- *vīṟṟirundāy* – Being seated joyfully, thinking “How fortunate am I to be living amidst these people!”.
- *unnai* – You who cannot be attained by any means other than yourself.
- *engu eydak kūvuvanē* – Only if I have done anything to have you in this manner in this divyadēśam, I can do something to attain my goal. As you have done so much until now, you should fulfil my subsequent desires too, out of your own mercy.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

adiyen saraty ramanuja dasan

## 5.7.5. Eydak kuvudal

*eydak kūvudal āvadē enakku? evvadevvat tuḷāyumāy ninṟu kaitavangaḷ seyyum karumēni ammānē! seyda vēḷviyar vaiyat tēvar aṟāc cirīvaramangala nagar kai toḻa irundāy adu nānum kaṇḍēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

enakku – for me (having the nature of not seeking any other protector); eyda – as means (for the attainment of my goal); kūvudal – desiring; āvadē – does it match?; evva – any type; tevattuḷ – the demoniac group who are inimical; āyumāy – assumed the forms such as budda et al and mingled; ninṟu – stood; kaitavangaḷ – deceptive acts (of decreasing their attachment in vēdam and increasing their attachment in worldly matters); seyyum – performed; karumēni – having dark forms (which bewilders their heart); ammānē – Oh lord!; seyda vēḷviyar – being krutakrutya (one who has fulfilled all duties); vaiyam – on earth; tēvar – comparable to nityasūris (eternal residents of paramapadam) in their wealth of jñānam (knowledge etc); aṟā – living without any break; sirīvaramangala nagar – all of śrīvaramangala nagar divyadēśam; kai toḻa – to be served; irundāy – remained there as the master; nānum – I too (who have comparable knowledge as they); adu – that presence; kaṇḍēn – have seen

**Перевод:**

**Does it match me to consider my desire as means to attain you? Oh lord who assumed the forms such as budda et al and mingled and stood amidst any type of demoniac groups who are inimical, and performed deceptive acts and who is having dark forms! You remained as the master of those who are krutakrutya and are comparable to nityasūris on earth and are living without any break in śrīvaramangala nagar divyadēśam and to be served by all of them; I too have seen that presence. It is implied by āḻvār “Hence, it is your duty to remove my hurdles and make me enjoy you”.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fifth pāsuram, emperumān asks “We have shown you our presence in śrīvaramangā divyadēśam, why are you being ungrateful?” and āḻvār replies “that is not sufficient”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says to emperumān “I have seen you who are of the nature of destroying the enemies of your devotees, descended here to be enjoyed by your devotees; is it apt for me to engage in self-efforts to attain you who are of such nature?”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Fifth pāsuram. emperumān says “I have manifested you my partiality towards my devotees and my presence in śrīvaramangala nagar. Why are you calling out saying ‘engu eydak kūvuvan‘, as if you have not received anything?”, and āḻvār says “I understand what you have bestowed on me so far, but I am not satisfied with that”. eydak kūvudal āvadē enakku? evvadevvat tuḷāyumāy ninṟu kaitavangaḷ seyyum karumēni ammānē! seyda vēḷviyar vaiyat tēvar aṟāc cirīvaramangala nagar kai toḻa irundāy adu nānum kaṇḍēnē*

- *eydak kūvudal āvadē enakku* – Leave it. Let it be so. Look at me, who am a śriya:pati \[This is explained as viparīta lakśaṇai, which means speaking the opposite while trying to explain something. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is citing himself as one who is having all the wealth/capabilities in a sarcastic way\], does it appear to you that “He (āḻvār) can engage in sādanam (means)”? I can only desire to attain you. I know myself better than you! Since āḻvār always considers his gain to be the result of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s mercy, he says “is there anything I can do \[No\]?”; when you give up on me, do I appear like you, who are śriya:pati (lord of [śrī mahālakśmi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/)) to engage in some means \[to attain you\]?
- *enakku* – \[When emperumān says “why don’t you pursue your own means to attain me?”\] [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) feels as if a mountain was placed on a weak person’s head. If you said as in śrī bhagavat gītā 9.34 “*mām namaskuru*” (worship me), āḻvār will cease to exist \[In this ślōkam, kriṣṇa tells arjuna to practice bhakti yōgam. Since practicing bhakti yōgam is contrary to the true nature of the soul which is totally dependent on lord, and only lord himself can be the means, āḻvār will not be able to accept that and survive\]. Now, one who is strong should discard those means, and tell “do not fear”.
- *evva* … – You broke the faith \[of being devoted to vēdam\] of those who were not devoted to you. Similarly, are you intent on breaking the faith of me \[of being who has no other refuge than you? \[simple meaning of the phrase\] Entering into any type of enemy camps.
- *evva* – any type. tevvar – enemies. tevvam – groups of enemies. It is said in perumāḷ tirumoḻi 10.3 “*tevvar anja*” (to frighten the enemies).
- *kaitavangaḷ seyyum* – Will perform deceptive acts. That is, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) entering the enemy camp as budda, standing in their amidst and eliminating their faith in vēdam \[As budda, emperumān preached against vēdam, to deceive the leaders of three towns who were demoniac yet were faithful towards vēdam and hence were drawing their strength from their practice of vaidika principles. Eventually rudra destroys the three towns and their leaders, by the grace of emperumān\].
- *kaitavangaḷ seyyum karu mēni ammānē* – By deceiving them through his speeches and tricks, and eliminating their faith in vēdam. For those who did not listen to him, he showed his \[beautiful\] form and shut them up. Through his speeches, he made them like dead bodies and made them the target of rudra’s arrow \[Though rudra shot the arrow, it was [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who facilitated the whole process and rudra was merely an instrument in the hands of emperumān\] .
- *ammānē* – Did you not finish those who are not devoted to you, for your devotees, while your relationship is the same with everyone? You are telling me who said “there is no other God” to do this \[engaging in bhakti yōgam\] just as you destroyed those who are saying “there are other Gods”. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) said in tiruvāsiriyam 7 “*oru mā teyvam maṟṟudaiyamō yāmē*” (Do we have any other greater God than you?). [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s act of engaging āḻvār in other means \[such as bhakti yōgam\] after reducing his faith in sidda sādanam (bhagavān, who is already existing/established means) is similar to his act of eliminating faith in vēdam for those demoniac people.
- *seyda vēḷviyar* – mahābhāratam says “*vidu: kriṣṇam brāhmaṇās tatvatōyē tēśām rājan sarva yajñāssamāptā:*” (Those brāhmaṇas who know kriṣṇa truly, have completed all the yajñas (sacrifices) they were to perform). While engaging in any other means, there will always be something which is left to be done. But those who accepted bhagavān as their means, are known as krutakrutya (one who has fulfilled all duties).
- *vaiyat tēvar* – bhūsura (celestial beings of this world). You remained in śrīvaramangala nagar which is occupied by such devotees and you considered their service as your sustenance. When emperumān asked “I who have the great abode of śrīvaikuṇṭam, have descended here for your sake and why are you still saying that I have not done anything?”, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) replies “I am not saying that I have not enjoyed anything; I am just saying that I am not satisfied with what I have enjoyed \[and I need more\]”.
- *adu nānum kaṇḍēnē* – Your highness have done a lot, there is no shortcoming in it; but that is not enough for me. The remainder of the pāsuram \[to be assumed\] is – I should perform continuous kainkaryam (service) at your divine feet.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.7.6. Enamay

*ēnamāy nilam kīṇḍa en appanē kaṇṇā! enṟum ennai āḷudai  vāna nāyaganē maṇi māṇikkac cudarē! tēnamām poḻil taṇ sirīvaramangalattavar kai toḻa uṟai vānamāmalaiyē adiyēn toḻa vandaruḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ēnamāy – (to handle the ocean of deluge) assuming the form of a varāha (pig, wild boar); nilam – earth; kīṇḍa – by the act of digging out; en – for me; appanē – being benefactor; kaṇṇā – (not just for a single entity earth, but for everyone) as kriṣṇa; enṟum – at all times; ennai – to make me sustain myself; āḷudai – accepting my service; vānam – accepting my kainkaryam (service) through speech which is as enjoyable as the bliss of paramapadam; nāyaganē – being the lord; maṇi – distinguished; māṇikkam – like a carbuncle \[ruby\]; sudarē – having greatly shining radiance; tēna – having honey; mām poḻil – having mango groves; taṇ – invigorating; sirīvaramangalattavar – the residents of śrīvaramangala nagar; kai toḻa – to be served; uṟai – eternally residing; vānam – to be enjoyed by the residents of paramavyōma (spiritual sky, paramapadam); mā – boundless; malaiyē – Oh one who is having a firm form resembling a mountain!; adiyēn – I who am a servitor; toḻa – to serve; vandu – giving up that posture, coming \[to me\]; aruḷ – mercifully

**Перевод:**

**emperumān being a benefactor for me by assuming the form of a varāha and digging out the earth, and as kriṣṇa; being the lord and accepting my service to make me sustain myself,  through speech which is as enjoyable as the bliss of paramapadam; having greatly shining radiance like a distinguished carbuncle, eternally residing in śrīvaramangala nagar which is having invigorating, honey bearing mango groves, to be served by the residents of the divyadēśam; Oh one who is having a firm form resembling a boundless mountain to be enjoyed by the residents of paramavyōma! Mercifully giving up that posture, come to me so that I, who am a servitor, can serve you.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the sixth pāsuram, emperumān asks “What else you desire for?” and āḻvār says “You should mercifully come to accept my service as desired by me”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “You who are greatly shining due to helping your devotee, should mercifully come for me to enjoy you and serve you”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Sixth pāsuram. āḻvār prays for the kainkaryam unsaid in the previous pāsuram \[mentioned in the last two lines in 5.7.5\]. ēnamāy nilam kīṇḍa en appanē kaṇṇā! enṟum ennai āḷudai  vāna nāyaganē maṇi māṇikkac cudarē! tēnamām poḻil taṇ sirīvaramangalattavar kai toḻa uṟai vānamāmalaiyē adiyēn toḻa vandaruḷē*

- *ēnamāy nilam kīṇḍa* – Your nature is such that those who are in danger need not inform you about their situation. When it comes to protecting others, you will not care for yourself.
- *ēnamāy nilam kīṇḍa en appanē kaṇṇā* – As mahāvarāha, you rescued bhūmi from mahāpraḷayam (the great deluge) and as kriṣṇa, you rescued me from the samsāra praḷayam (ocean of nescience).
- *ēnamāy nilam kīṇḍa en appanē kaṇṇā* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) considers [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s help to bhūmi which was consumed in praḷayam, as a help to āḻvār himself.
- *en appanē kaṇṇā* – Do you have to assume a different form or decoration to protect me \[like you had to do as varāha\]? \[Implies that, why don’t you just help me, since you don’t have to do anything special\]. As said in tiruvāimoḻi 7.7.8 “*kaṇṇan kōḷ iḻai vāḷ mugam*” (kriṣṇa’s face which is decorated by its own radiance), kriṣṇa’s face is [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s protection.
- *enṟum ennai āḷudai vāna nāyaganē* – Even while [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is with those who are matching his greatness \[i.e., nityasūris\], he thinks about āḻvār’s protection only. It is emperumān who personally ensured āḻvār’s sustenance etc.
- *maṇi māṇikkac cudarē* – emperumān is not just bringing fame for āḻvār after āḻvār sustains himself; instead right from the beginning, he cared for āḻvār, and once āḻvār acquired desire \[towards emperumān\], emperumān manifested to [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/), the form which he manifests to nityasūris.
- *maṇi māṇikkac cudarē* – the best among gems; alternative explanation – having the radiance of pearl and ruby.
- *tēna mām poḻil …* – Since there are honey bearing mango groves, śrīvaramangala nagar is invigorating. To accept the service of the residents of such abode, matching their true nature.
- *vāna mā malaiyē* – His presence in accepting service of the residents here is comparable to that of paramapadam where he is served by nityasūris. \[vānamāmalai means mountain reaching upto the sky. It is also the divine name of the [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) in this divyadēśam\].
- *adiyēn toḻa vandu aruḷē* – You should appear to accept my service and let me survive/live.
- *vandu aruḷē* – To let me serve \[and thereby survive/live\], you should walk up to me. Here serving means, as done in [tiruppāvai 24](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/01/thiruppavai-24-anru-ivvulagam/) “*anṟu ivvulagam aḷandāy adi pōṟṟi*” (Let the one with the divine feet which measured the world, live long), performing mangaḷāśāsanam (wishing well) for that beautiful walk.
- *vandu aruḷē* – You should accept my service by being in my vicinity.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.7.7. Vandaruli

*vandaruḷin en nenjidam koṇḍa vānavar koḻundē! ulagukkōr mundait tāy tanadaiyē! muḻu ēḻ ulagum uṇḍāy sendoḻilavar vēda vēḷvi aṟāc cirīvaramangala nagar andamil pugaḻāy! adiyēnai agaṟṟēlē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vandu aruḷi – mercifully arriving here (giving up paramapadam (spiritual realm) and kśīrābdi (milky ocean)); en – my (me who was facing away from you, lacking any desire); nenju – heart; idam – as residence; koṇḍa – having \[as residence\] and caring for my sustenance; vānavar – the sustenance of the residents of paramapadam; koḻundē – one who increases \[“koḻundu” is taken as “rising”\]; ulagukku – for this world; ōr – distinct (being the cause for sustenance); mundai – the primordial form; tāy – mother; tandaiyē – being the father; muḻu ēḻ ulagum – all worlds; uṇḍāy – consumed them, placed them in your stomach and protected them; sem – having honesty of existing for bhagavān only, in the form of engaging in kainkaryam (service); toḻilavar – those who are having activities, their; vēdam – vaidika (as per vēdam); vēḷvi – worship of bhagavān \[yajña is explained as worship of bhagavān\]; aṟā – continuing without any break; sirīvaramangala nagar – in śrīvaramangala nagar; andam – end; il – not having; pugaḻāy – oh one who is having great qualities!; adiyēnai – me (who am having the nature of totally existing for you, and not leaving you even if you shun me); agaṟṟēl – do not shun

**Перевод:**

**emperumān mercifully arrives and has my heart as his residence and cares for my sustenance and increases the sustenance of the residents of paramapadam; he is the distinct primordial mother and father for this world; he consumed all the worlds, placed them in his stomach and protected them; Oh emperumān who is having such endless great qualities who is residing in śrīvaramangala nagar where continuous worship of bhagavān as per vēdam, is performed by those who are having honesty of existing for him only, in the form of engaging in kainkaryam! Do not shun me.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the seventh pāsuram, since emperumān did not fulfil āḻvār‘s desire immediately, āḻvār thinks “Is he considering to shun me?” and says “kindly do not shun this servitor (me)”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “You who are total cause for my sustenance, should not separate from me and destroy my existence”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Seventh pāsuram. Since emperumān did not arrive on hearing āḻvār‘s words “adiyēn toḻa vandaruḷē“, āḻvār fears “may be emperumān is shunning me” and prays him “do not shun me”. vandaruḷin en nenjidam koṇḍa vānavar koḻundē! ulagukkōr mundait tāy tanadaiyē! muḻu ēḻ ulagum uṇḍāy sendoḻilavar vēda vēḷvi aṟāc cirīvaramangala nagar andamil pugaḻāy! adiyēnai agaṟṟēlē*

nampiḷḷai highlighted that nanjīyar used to explain this incident everytime he explained this pāsuram: bhattar, mercifully makes nanjīyar recite certain pāsurams \[to help bhattar use those pāsurams in lectures\] during the completion of śrī puśpa yāgam \[a yajña performed using flowers, at the end of brahmōtsavam\]; during one summer, he was seated on the divine streets of śrīrangam which were cooled down by pouring water, kindly requested nanjīyar to recite some pāsurams and he recites this pāsuram; bhattar meditates upon the pāsuram and subsequently he also recites the same pāsuram. He then said “The rock like hard minds/hearts which cannot be softened even by meditating about [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) in the mind after withdrawing the mind from external matters, and pursuing aśtānga yōgam through yama, niyama etc. Some most magnanimous persons ([āḻvārs](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/azhwars/)) left us these merciful words \[divya prabandams\] to melt such hard hearts”.

- *vandu aruḷi* – Mercifully arriving \[in me\] while I did not desire for that. Here entities from two different dvīpams (land masses) are uniting; i.e., [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) from paramapadam and [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) from samsāram are uniting. When āḻvār should have gone to the abode of his desired target \[emperumān\], even that did not happen, and they did not even travel equal distance and met each other in the middle. Here āḻvār is saying “vandaruḷi” with a melted heart \[“*vandaruḷi*” should be recited in very low pitch, matching āḻvār’s mood\]. āppān tiruvandūr aṟaiyar would pick up the tāḷam (cymbals) in his hand and would sing “*vandaruḷi*” repeatedly without moving on further.
- *vandu aruḷi* – As drvaya (entity) and guṇams (qualities) united \[[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) and [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) united\]. Now, both emperumān \[[paramātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)\] and āḻvār \[[jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)\] are dravyams (entities). Still, they both unite in some cases, as entity is seamlessly united with its qualities. \[Examples – ātmā being united with śarīram (body) and jñānam (knowledge) – where all three are dravyams; similarly, paramātmā is united with jīvātmā which is a dravyam; in all these cases, just like qualities are inseparable from the entity, here jīvātmās are also inseparable from paramātmā\].
- *en nenju* – This is the same heart which enjoyed matters other than [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) previously. [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) who is having śrīvaikuṇṭam as his divine assembly, is desiring to attain my heart \[[āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is amazed\]!
- *idam koṇḍa* – Even if some people come, they would say “my heart is elsewhere”; unlike those, emperumān remained as explained in śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam “*āvāsamtvahamiccāmi*” (śrī rāma to śarabanga riśi – I desire to stay here).
- *en nenju idam koṇḍa vānavar koḻundē* – emperumān is the leader of nityasūris! he is praying to get the \[inferior\] heart of mine; me, who am the leader of nitya samsāris (eternally bound souls)!
- *ulagukku ōr mundait tāy tandaiyē* – There \[in paramapadam\] both [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) and [nityasūris/mutktātmās](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) are naturally oriented towards each other; here only bhagavān is oriented towards us. śrīviṣṇu sahasranāmam “*bhūtānām yōvyaya:pitā*” (the imperishable father of all beings) – these worldly parents will perish one day like a staged drama will end, pirātti and [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) are imperishable parents. mahābhāratam āraṇya parvam “*sarvēśām Eva lōkānām pitā mātā ca mādava: \| gaccatvamēnam śaraṇam śaraṇyam puruśariśabhā:*” (Oh best among men! śrīman nārāyaṇan (indicated by the name “mādava”) is the mother and father for all beings in the world; you accept this saviour as the refuge). *gaccatvam* – Instead of just letting him pursue you in a one-sided manner, you too turn towards him. He is the distinct and primordial mother and father for the entire world.
- *muḻu ēḻ ulagum uṇḍāy* – The mother carries her child in the womb for ten months with the expectation “once he grows up, he will remove our sufferings”; unlike that, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) thinks “oh I am glad that I have protected them from being tormented \[in deluge\]” and consider that itself as the gain.
- *sem toḻilavar* – Those who do not say “*dēhi mē dadāmi*” (I give this to you, and you give something to me in return). Just like protecting others is his nature, the nature of the residents of this divyadēśam is to serve. If it is not like that, it is of no use. The activities of those who have the honesty of being ananya prayōjana (not seeking any ulterior benefits) and activities of such nature.
- *vēda vēḷvi aṟā* – The loud recital of vēdams and vaidika kriyā (rituals) go on continuously without any break. Since there are no hurdles in the prāpya (goal) and the prāpaka (means), it will go on like the embrace of the divine consorts. Only when there is a separate gain while embracing the dear consort, there can be a separate gain for kainkaryam. This kainkaryam continues forever since there is no separate gain, attaining which, one will stop the action \[kainkaryam\].
- *sirīvaramangala nagar andam il pugaḻāy* – If he remained in śrīvaikuṇṭam, there could be some limit for his qualities/greatness \[but since he is in śrīvaramangala nagar, there is no limit to them\].
- *adiyēnai agaṟṟēlē* – After reaching a different abode \[from your natural abode of śrīvaikuṇṭam\] and gaining great fame, do not end up being blamed for giving up a helpless person.
- *agaṟṟēlē* – \[Since [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is right here in śrīvaramangala nagar, arrived specifically for [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/), \] āḻvār is indicating that he cannot even wait for a moment to be with emperumān.  Those who cannot bear his separation even for a moment, will say like this.
- *adiyēnai* – Are you shunning me, because there is someone else apt to protect this [jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) (me)? \[No, I can only be protected by you\]

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.7.8. Agarra ni vaitta

*agaṟṟa nī vaitta māya val aim pulangaḷ ām avai nangaṟindanan agaṟṟi ennaiyum nī arunjēṟṟil vīḻtti kaṇḍāy pagark kadir maṇi māda nīdu sirīvaramangai vāṇanē! enṟum pugaṟkariya endāy puḷḷin vāy piḷandānē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

agaṟṟa – to banish (those who are turning away from you); nī vaitta – those which are created by you; māyam – having amazing nature (of not mixing with each other); val – not defeatable (by anyone); aim pulangaḷ Am avai – the five senses; nangu – (truly) well; aṟindanan – understood; ennaiyum – me too (who understand these and am fearful about these); agaṟṟi – pushing away (from you); nī – you; aru – difficult (to recoup and escape); sēṟṟil – mud (of worldly pleasures); vīḻtti kaṇḍāy – am fearing that you are pushing me into \[that mud\]; pagar – shining; kadir – having light; maṇi – carbuncles; mādam – mansions; nīdu – tall; sirīvaramangai – for sirīvaramangai divyadēśam; vāṇanē – controller; enṟum – ever; pugaṟku – to enter; ariya – difficult; endāy – being my lord; puḷḷin – bakāsura’s (who was a hurdle for those gōpikās who are dear to you); vāy – beak; piḷandānē – Oh one who tore!

**Перевод:**

**I have truly well understood the senses which are created by you, having amazing nature (of not mixing with each other) and not defeatable, to banish those who are turning away from you;  am fearing that you are pushing me away into the difficult mud; Oh controller of sirīvararamangai divyadēśam, which is having tall mansions with carbuncles which are having shining light. Oh one who being my lord, tore bakāsura’s beak; and who is difficult to enter. Implies that – āḻvār is saying “though emperumān is omnipotent in this manner, he did not help me and is pushing me away”.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the eighth pāsuram, emperumān asks “Did I banish you?” and āḻvār replies “You have placed me in this samsāram where the worldly pleasures such as śabda (sound) etc are active; is that not an act of banishing?”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. agaṟṟa nī vaitta māya val aim pulangaḷ Am avai nangaṟindanan agaṟṟi ennaiyum nī arunjēṟṟil vīḻtti kaṇḍāy pagark kadir maṇi māda nīdu sirīvaramangai vāṇanē! enṟum pugaṟkariya endāy puḷḷin vāy piḷandānē!*

- *agaṟṟa nī vaitta* – You who are omnipotent, have placed this as said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 7.14](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/7-14/) “*mama māyā duratyayā*” (my creation is difficult to crossover) for those who are not attached to you.
- *māya aim pulangaḷ Am avai* – The five senses which will capture everyone and which will engage all people of the world. You who are the [sarvēśvara](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/), have placed these to drive away those who are not attached to you.

When asked “How did you know these?”, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) replies

- *nangu aṟindanan* – Since I received unblemiśed knowledge and devotion as said in tiruvāimoḻi 1.1.1 “*mayarvaṟa madi nalam*“, I have understood this well.

[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) asks “If I kept them to banish those who are not devoted me, why does it bother you?”, āḻvār says,

- *agaṟṟi ennaiyum nī arum sēṟṟil vīḻtti kaṇḍāy* – You seem to be intent on separating me from you and pushing me too who cannot sustain myself without you into this worldly pleasure without any option to escape. Why is [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) who is seeking help from emperumān, blaming emperumān and highlighting him as a cruel person? āḻvār thinks – those who are merciful \[i.e., emperumān\] will help eventually thinking “this is going to cause great harm for my reputation”. While I have no connection \[attachment\] with my body, are you trying to keep me here and pushing me away from you?
- *pagark kadir* – pugar and pagar mean radiance/splendour. Oh leader of sirīvaramangai divyadēśam which is having tall mansions having great radiance, and precious gems studded in them.
- *pagaṟkadir* – If said this way, this line will mean – the mansions which rise upto the sun and having radiant gems. pagal – āditya – sun.
- *enṟum* … – Oh one who is unreachable for those who are not devoted to you. You banish those who are not devoted to you, and also destroy them!
- *endāy* – Do you have to do this to me who am distinguished \[i.e., having distinguished relationship with you\]?
- *puḷḷin vāy piḷandānē* – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) asks “What is stopping you from reaching me?” and [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says “As you destroyed bakāsuran, you mercifully destroy my connection to this world as well”.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.7.9. Pullin vay

*puḷḷin vāy piḷandāy! marudidai pōyināy! erudēḻ adartta en kaḷḷa māyavanē! karu māṇikkac cudarē! teḷḷiyār tiru nān maṟaigaḷ vallār mali taṇ sirīvaramangai uḷ irunda endāy! aruḷāy uyyumāṟenakkē.*

**Пословный перевод:**

puḷḷin vāy piḷandāy – (implying his elimination of the connection with samsāram for his devotees) killing bakāsura; marudu idai pōyināy – killing yamaḷa and arjuna (to imply his removal of pairs of sufferings); ēḻ erudu – seven bulls; adartta – killed; kaḷḷam – (in this manner, to have no one understand/know) confidential aspects; en – revealing to me; māyavanē – being amazing person; karu – blackish; māṇikka – carbuncle’s (precious gem); sudarē – having beautiful form shining like; teḷḷiyār – having clarity (in being protected by emperumān only); tiru – having the wealth that provides access to bhagavān’s true nature etc; nāl – four; maṟaigaḷ – the essence of vēdams; vallār – those who have them at their disposal; mali – living closely together; taṇ – invigorating, not being affected by the heat of this material realm; sirīvaramangai – sirīvaramangai divyadēśam; uḷ – inside; irunda – mercifully present to let me enjoy you; endāy – oh benefactor!; enakku – for me having no other refuge; uyyum – to uplift by attaining your divine feet; āṟu – means; aruḷāy – bestow on me mercifully

**Перевод:**

**You (emperumān), the amazing person, revealed confidential aspects by killing bakāsura, yamaḷa and arjuna and seven bulls; you are having the beautiful shining form like a blackish carbuncle; oh benefactor who are mercifully present to let me enjoy you, inside the invigorating sirīvaramangai divyadēśam which is populated by those who are having clarity and expertise in the essence of four vēdams (to have them at their disposal) which is having the wealth that provides access to bhagavān’s true nature etc! For me, having no other refuge, mercifully bestow the means to make me attain your divine feet and have me uplifted.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the ninth pāsuram, āḻvār says to emperumān “You who have captivated me with your divine pastimes etc and accepted my service, and who have mercifully descended to sirīvaramangala nagar, should also mercifully fulfil my remaining desires”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says to emperumān “you who are shining very radiantly due to destroying your enemies, should mercifully uplift me”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Ninth pāsuram. emperumān asks “What should I do to you who are fearing thinking ‘arunjēṟṟil vīztti kaṇḍāy’ (you have pushed me into this mud of samsāram (material realm) which is difficult to escape)“, āḻvār says “You who are capable and present here, should remove my hurdles and mercifully engage me in service at your divine feet”. puḷḷin vāy piḷandāy! marudidai pōyināy! erudēḻ adartta en kaḷḷa māyavanē! karu māṇikkac cudarē! teḷḷiyār tiru nān maṟaigaḷ vallār mali taṇ sirīvaramangai uḷ irunda endāy! aruḷāy uyyumāṟenakkē.*

- *puḷḷin vāy piḷandāy* – As a hungry person would recollect when he was fed by someone, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is recollecting and saying [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s previous assistance.
- *puḷ* … – You killed bakāsura, changed yamaḷārjunas to pieces, strangled the seven bulls together.
- *en kaḷḷa māyavanē* – You who are having amazing activities which cannot be comprehended by anyone, and revealed all those to me and captivated me.
- *karu mānikkac cudarē* – Oh one who eliminated nappinnaip pirātti’s hurdles, bestowed your divine form to her and also manifested the distinguished nature of that form to me!
- *teḷḷiyār* … – As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam 16.4 “*rāmasya vyavasāyajñā lakśmaṇasyā dīmata:*” (sītā heard the opinion of lakśamaṇa who is more knowledgeable than śrī rāma, and became pacified), this divyadēśam has many intelligent devotees who can correct you even if you are making some mistakes.
- *teḷḷiyār* – Those who are fully dependent on him, even when they themselves are capable. This is the purpose of their consciousness \[i.e., to be dependent on him\]. Their clarity of mind is the same as that of sītāp pirātti even when she was captured and placed alone in aśōka vanikām and as that of śrī vibhīśaṇāḻvān while he was surrendering to śrī rāma. \[Explanation for the clarity of śrī vibhīśaṇāḻvān\] śrī vibhiśaṇāḻvān was looking at sugrīva mahārāja and his angry assistants and was joyfully speaking to them as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 17.9 “*sugrīvam tāmśca samprekśya*” (He spoke to sugrīva beautifully), while they were saying “*vadyatām*” (he (vibhīśaṇa) deserves to be killed); this is similar to how a child will joyfully look at her mother’s face even though she may be scolding the child.
- *tiru nān maṟaigaḷ vallār* – Those who have understood the essence instead of running behind thousands of lines \[of śāstram\]. Those who remain as said in iraṇḍām tiruvandādi 39 “*mādavan pēr solluvadē ōttin surukku*” (the purpose of vēdam is to reveal the name of mādavan (śrīman nārāyaṇan)).
- *mali taṇ* … – Oh my lord who is residing along with those intelligent devotees who are in abundance in the invigorating sirīvaramangai divyadēśam.
- *aruḷāy uyyumāṟu enakkē* – Look at me \[enakkē – for me who is tormented in this samsāram\], and you have to mercifully bestow me kainkaryam at your divine feet. kainkaryam (rendering service) and ujjīvanam (uplifting) are not two separate concepts for [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/). If one does not have the urge \[to leave this samsāram\], it is implied that one does not have knowledge about [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s distinguished greatness; if one is living comfortably in this samsāram, it is implied that one has not understood the inferior nature of this samsāram.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.
