## 5.7.10. Arenakku

*āṟenakku nin pādamē śaraṇāgat tandoḻindāy unakkōr kaimāṟu nān onṟilēn enadāviyum unadē sēṟu koḷ karumbum perunjennelum mali taṇ sirīvaramangai nāṟu pūntaṇḍuḻāy mudiyāy! deyva nāyaganē*

**Пословный перевод:**

enakku – for me; āṟu – means to attain the goal; nin pādamē – your divine feet only; śaraṇāga – upāyam (means) which is the refuge; tandoḻindāy – you have bestowed; unakku – for you (who are such a benefactor); ōr – in any way; kaimāṟu – return favour; nān – I (who am akincana (empty-handed)); onṟu – anything; ilēn – do not have; enadu – my; āviyum – ātmā; unadu – (already) yours; sēṟu – in muddy field; koḷ – present; karumbum – sugarcane; peru – growing tall (taller than sugarcane); sennelum – paddy crop; mali – abundant; taṇ – invigorating; sirīvaramangai – present in sirīvaramangai; nāṟu – very fragrant; pū – having freshness; taṇ – invigorating; tuḻāy – decorated with tiruttuḻāy (tuḷasi); mudiyāy – having divine crown; deyvam – for nityasūris; nāyaganē – Oh leader!

**Перевод:**

**Oh leader of nityasūris who is in sirīvaramangai divyadēśam which has sugarcane and tall paddy crop in muddy field, wearing divine crown which is decorated with fresh invigorating tuḷasi! You (emperumān) have bestowed on me your divine feet only which are the means to attain the goal, as the upāyam (means) which is the refuge; I do not have anything to give you in return and my ātmā is yours.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the tenth pāsuram, āḻvār says “I cannot do anything in return for your favour of making me remain as ‘your divine feet are the only refuge’ even in dire situations”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, emperumān shows to āḻvār “My divine feet are the means to attain me” and  āḻvār says “I cannot do anything in return for this favour”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Tenth pāsuram. āḻvār said “aruḷāy uyyumāṟu enakku“, but he did not see emperumān coming and showering his mercy; he then says “even in such dire situations you have made me remain as ‘your divine feet are the only refuge’ – there is nothing which I can do in return for this favour”. āṟenakku nin pādamē śaraṇāgat tandoḻindāy unakkōr kaimāṟu nān onṟilēn enadāviyum unadē sēṟu koḷ karumbum perunjennelum mali taṇ sirīvaramangai nāṟu pūntaṇḍuḻāy mudiyāy! deyva nāyaganē*

- *āṟenakku* … – āṟu means vaḻi (path). vaḻi means upāyam (means/way). perumāḷ tirumoḻi 9.2 “*evvāṟu nadandanai*” (How did you walk?), nācciyār tirumoḻi 3.2 “*ippoygaikku evvāṟu vandāy*” (How did you come to this pond?). śaraṇ\[am\] – upēyam (goal). You made your own divine feet as the upāyam and upēyam – this is piḷḷān’s explanation. bhattar mercifully explains “both āṟu and śaraṇam indicate upāyam only”. You arranged such that your divine feet are my upāyam. āṟu – upāyam. Since it is explained in  śrī pāncarātram “… *upāyārtaika vācaka:*” (śaraṇam means upāyam (means), vīdu (house), rakśaka (protector); here it is explained as upāyam), śaraṇam means upāyam. By saying “*enakku*“, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is differentiating himself from followers of other upāyams \[such as karma jñāna bhakti yōgams\]. Since, this decad is focussed on highlighting āḻvār’s lack of any other means and establishing the real upāyam \[[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s divine feet\] starting with “*nōṟṟa nōnbilēn*“, here the same point is highlighted as the conclusion. By avadāraṇam \[emphasis\] (*pādam****E***), āḻvār thinks about \[and reminds us of\] “*ēka*” (only) padam in carama ślōkam. Instead of giving up other upāyams as a result of holding on to īśvara confidently, if we gave them up out of nāstikyam (lack of faith in śāstram), it will only lead to attachment towards worldly pleasures; one who has taken the antidote for serpent’s poison can boldly place his hand in serpent’s mouth; but if someone who has not taken the antidote and still places his hand in the serpent’s mouth, it will only lead to death. For you who bestowed this clarity in my mind, it is not just that there is no favour in return which matches your greatness, I who am an akincana (empty-handed) do not see even a favour which slightly matches your greatness.

[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) asks “Alright, why don’t you give your [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) (soul) then?”, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) replies,

- *enadu āviyum unadē* – I would have satisfied myself doing that; had you not bestowed me with unblemiśed knowledge and devotion, as someone stealing “*rājamahēndran padi*” (a divine ornament which is worn by namperumāḷ), considering it one’s own and offering it to perumāḷ, such act of ātmasamarpaṇam (presenting the [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) to [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)) will only reveal one’s robbery.

[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) asks “Why don’t you give your own [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)?”, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says,

- *nin pādamē – enadu āviyum unadē* – āppān tiruvaḻundūr aṟaiyar would recite “*nin pādamē!*” here to make it sound like āḻvār is vowing that his [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) is emperumān’s \[in this case [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying “You have given your divine feet (caraṇ) as āṟu (upāyam) – this is satyam (nin pādamē!)”\].
- *sēṟu koḷ …* – The cool sirīvaramangai, which has muddy fields of sugarcane, and abundance of  paddy crop which appears to be providing shade to the sugarcane.
- *nāṟu pūm taṇ tuḻāy mudiyāy …* – Fragrant attractive tuḷasi. Having a crown indicating that you are the leader of all these \[natural riches of sirīvaramangala nagar, having a tuḷasi garland as the crown\]. You remain as the controller of even those nityasūris who are very intelligent, and this being the case, what can I do anything in return for you? While you are favouring me greatly, I am not ignorant \[having known that I am already yours\]; even in this case, you are so complete that I cannot do something to satisfy you. Those who did not accept your favour \[i.e., your bestowing of true knowledge about the upāyam\], just roam around enjoying worldly pleasures; those who are ignorant \[about the fact that the ātmā is already owned by bhagavān\] remained saying “I have done something in return for his favour”; only if you are incomplete, we can consider to have done something, but you are complete; this being the case, can I do anything worthy? \[deyva nāyagan\] The leader of nityasūris. devaym – nityasūris.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.7.11. Deyva nayagan

*deyva nāyagan nāraṇan tirivikkiraman adi iṇai misai koy koḷ pūm poḻil sūḻ kurugūrc catakōpan seyda āyirattuḷ ivai taṇ sirīvaramangai mēya pattudan vaigal pāda vallār vānōrkkāravamudē*

**Пословный перевод:**

deyvam – leader of nityasūris; nāyagan – sarvēśvaran (supreme lord); nāraṇan – having motherly forbearance due to unconditional relationship \[this is the meaning of the term nārāyaṇa\]; tirivikkiraman – one who measures \[and accepts\] his subordinate entities so that they don’t develop ownership; adi iṇai misai – on the divine feet; koy koḷ – abundantly available to be plucked; pū – flowers; poḻil – gardens; sūḻ – surrounded by; kurugūr – leader of āḻvārtirunagari; satakōpan – nammāḻvār; seyda – mercifully spoke; āyirattuḷ – among the thousand pāsurams; taṇ – invigorating; sirīvaramangai – sirīvaramangai; mēya – aimed at; ivai – these; pattu – ten pāsurams; udan – agreeing with the meaning; pāda vallār – those who can sing; vānōrkku – for the residents of paramapadam (spiritual realm); vaigal – always; ārā – never-satisfying; amudu – eternally enjoyable like nectar

**Перевод:**

**sarvēśvaran who is the leader of nityasūris, having motherly forbearance due to unconditional relationship, measures \[and accepts\] his subordinate entities so that they don’t develop ownership; nammāḻvār, leader of āḻvārtirunagari which is surrounded by abundant flowers ready to be plucked, mercifully spoke on the divine feet of such emperumān, these ten pāsurams among the thousand pāsurams, aimed at the invigorating sirīvaramangai divyadēśam; those who can sing this decad agreeing with its meanings, will always be eternally enjoyable like never-satisfying nectar, for the residents of paramapadam.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the end, āḻvār says “those who recite this decad with intent and joy, will be always enjoyed by nityasūris”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. deyva nāyagan nāraṇan tirivikkiraman adi iṇai misai koy koḷ pūm poḻil sūḻ kurugūrc catakōpan seyda āyirattuḷ ivai taṇ sirīvaramangai mēya pattudan vaigal pāda vallār vānōrkkāravamudē*

- *deyva nāyagan* – sarvēśvaran (the supreme lord)
- *nāraṇan* – vatsalan (one who has motherly affection) who will not lose his belongings.
- *tirivikkiraman* – for those who begged him, he would fulfil their desires even at the cost of destroying his own supremacy.
- *adi iṇai misai* – on the divine feet
- *koy koḷ pūm poḻil sūḻ* – garden which is always pleasant. Flowers are always ready to be plucked.
- *kurugūrc catakōpan* – Different from [śrī bhagavat gītā](http://githa.koyil.org/). \[Recited by [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) who is a servitor of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), instead of emperumān himself reciting – so it has greater value\]
- *seyda āyiram* – Though the meanings are the same as in vēdam, unlike vēdam tiruvāimoḻi is not autorless. vēdam is similar to \[[bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s\] paratvam \[supreme form in paramapadam\]; itihāsams (epics) and purāṇams (ancient historical texts) are like [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s avatārams (incarnations); tiruvāimoḻi is like his arcāvatāram (deity forms). It is said as “*seyda āyiram*” (thousand pāsurams which were created) – just as emperumān became the son of daśarat to eliminate his worry of not having a father, here vēdam became a recital of [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) to eliminate its worry of not having an author.
- *udan – pāda vallār* – Those who can sing with intent. Those who can contemplate on āḻvār’s *upāyaśūnyatai* (total lack of any other upāyams) and sing.
- *vaigalum – vānōrkku ārā amudē* – They will remain eternally enjoyable by nityasūris. Just as the dēvas (celestial beings) become satisfied while receiving amrutam (nectar), nityasūris would become satisfied on receiving such persons. Since nityasūris who have taste towards [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) without attachment to any other means, like [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) who is similar to them, those who are able to recite these pāsurams in the same mood will become enjoyable for nityasūris.

## 5.8 5.8.1- aravamude

## 5.8.1. 5.8.1- Aravamude

*ārāvamudē adiyēn udalam ninpāl anbāyē nīrāy alaindu karaiya urukkuginṟa nedumālē! sīrār senneṟkavari vīsum seḻunīrt tirukkudandai ērār kōlam tigaḻak kidandāy kaṇḍēn emmānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

emmānē – one who is my unconditional lord; ārā – unquenchable (even after eternally enjoying); amudē – being eternally enjoyable; adiyēn – my (me who were captivated by such enjoyability); udalam – body; ninpāl – towards you; anbāyē – having love as the mood/form; nīrāy – losing firmness to become watery; alaindu – agitated (and not being steady); karaiya – to dissolve; urukkuginṟa – making it melt; nedumālē – Oh one who is having infinitely enjoyable greatness!; sīr – by weight; Ar – abundance; sennel – paddy crops; kavari vīsum – appearing like fans swaying; seḻu – rich; nīr – having water; tirukkudandai – in tirukkudandai; ēr – beauty; Ar – abundance; kōlam – decoration; tigaḻa – shining; kidandāy – resting; kaṇḍēn – enjoyed by seeing with my own eyes

**Перевод:**

**emperumān who is my unconditional lord, where my quench is never fulfilled even after eternally enjoying him; oh one who is having infinitely enjoyable greatness! You are agitating me to dissolve and melt my body which is having love as the mood/form towards you, losing firmness to become watery; you are resting in tirukkudandai which has abundance of heavy paddy crops which appear like fans swaying and having rich water; your abundant beauty and decoration are shining; I enjoyed these by seeing with my own eyes. This implies – āḻvār has only seen emperumān and has not interacted with him yet.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the first pāsuram, āḻvār says “I have seen you who are melting me with your beauty etc, mercifully reclining; but I have not seen you showering your merciful glance, embracing me etc”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*In the first pāsuram, āḻvār says “I have seen you reclining in tirukkudandai, making me melt being infinitely enjoyable by me with your beauty and your unconditional relationship”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. ārāvamudē adiyēn udalam ninpāl anbāyē nīrāy alaindu karaiya urukkuginṟa nedumālē! sīrār senneṟkavari vīsum seḻunīrt tirukkudandai ērār kōlam tigaḻak kidandāy kaṇḍēn emmānē*

- *ārāvamudē* \[*ārā amudē*\]- Even if one enjoys, how can one be relaxed when separated from an entity who cannot be simply enjoyed in order. The order of experience is – first to see, then to approach closely and then come in physical contact; [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is such that one cannot wait to these in order.
- *ārāvamudē* – To drink the salt water \[nectar retrieved from milky ocean\], one should be born as a celestial being, should practice celibacy and even after that it will be given only once; but this \[[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), the nectar\], is open for all, eternally enjoyable, even if there is shortcoming in one’s celibacy vow, it \[emperumān, the nectar\] will eliminate the shortcomings \[and accept the person who desires for him\]. lōkasārangamunigaḷ was residing in the uttara bhūmi (northern part of bhārata dēśam). A person \[devotee\] from here \[dakśiṇa bhūmi (southern part of bhārata dēśam)\] went there. lōkasārangamunigaḷ enquired from him “what is special in the dakśiṇa bhūmi?”, and he replies “a prabandam named tiruvāimoḻi has apppeared \[from [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)\], and the elders have accepted it and are greatly celebrating it”; lōkasārangamunigaḷ says “why don’t you recite a verse from what you know in it?” and he replied “I can recite this decad starting with ‘*ārāvamudē*‘”. Hearing that lōkasārangamunigaḷ said “While there are abundant names like nārāyaṇa etc for [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), how amazing that āḻvār is presenting us this beautiful name”, felt dissatisfied with his stay there and at once left for tirukkudandai saying “Let me go to the abode where these verses are recited”.
- *ārāvamudē* – \[śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 6.1 is explained here\] *sahapatnyā* – Just as one who steps into deep water will hold on to a support \[Along with sītāp pirātti, śrī rāma is vorśipping śrīman nārāyaṇan [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is his family deity\]. *patnyā saha* – Just as a person who is stepping into a river, will take the help of an expert, perumāḷ (śrī rāma) is setting out to worship periya perumāḷ \[śrīranganātan, śrīman nārāyaṇa, who is the family deity of śrī rāma’s clan\], with the help of sītāp pirātti. *visālākśyā* – sītāp pirātti became blissful seeing perumāḷ’s great love towards periya perumāḷ and her eyes expanded in wonder so much, even more than his embrace of her. *nārāyaṇamupāgamat* – But śrī rāma’s total control over his senses is such that he is not getting disturbed by her glance, and instead was focussed on periya perumāḷ. From this, it is explained – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s unquenchable nature is such that, even when he sets out to enjoy himself, he needs to have a companion.
- *ārāvamudē* – This word \[this nature of emperumān\] is the seed \[root cause\] for [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s craving in this decad.
- *adiyēn* – Here āḻvār is not identifying himself to be a servitor due to being bestowed unblemiśed knowledge \[as done in tiruvāimoḻi 1.1.1\] by emperumān, but is doing this being defeated by emperumān’s enjoyability. This is similar to lakhsmaṇa who first said in śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 15.7 “*paravānasmi*” (I am a servant), subsequently said in śrī rāmāyaṇam kiśkintā kāṇḍam 4.12 “*guṇair dāsyamubāgata:*” (I am his servant due to his auspicious qualities).
- *udalam nin pāl anbāyē* – When śēśatvam (servitorśip) is the nature of [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) \[and is realised\], the body being a hurdle for such servitude, is quashed. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) who was thinking “*aham*” (the independent, I am), is now saying “*adiyēn*” due to the enjoyable nature of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/); similarly, the body too, melted due to emperumān’s nature. The body, instead of pulling the ātmā which is the abode for servitude, towards it \[body\], followed the desire of ātmā. Not just the ātmā which is an embodiment of jñānam (knowledge) and ānandam (bliss, not just the mind which is the gateway of ātmā for the jñānam, but even the body which is made of skin, flesh etc also melted \[out of love for emperumān\]).
- *nin pāl anbāyē* – Towards you who can weaken both [cētana (sentient beings)](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) and [acētana (insentient entities)](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/09/thathva-thrayam-achith-what-is-matter/) with your love, the body, instead of being the abode of love, became an embodiment of love.
- *nīrāy alaindu* – The body became \[an embodiment of \] love, and that love became perturbed like water. First it starts with śravaṇam (hearing), then mananam (meditation), subsequently bhāvanā (deep contemplation) and finally it leads to visualisation which matches real experience; all of these happen due to [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s enjoyability.
- *nīrāy alaindu karaiya* – Water will dissolve the substance which falls in it, but will not dissolve itself; here it is unlike that, water (body which became like water) itself is dissolving. If love can become water, why can’t water dissolve?

If this is the state of [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/), what is the state of [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)?

- *urukkuginṟa* – He is set out to fully weakening ātmā. Just as a gold smith will melt the ornaments etc \[disregarding their worth, beauty etc\], emperumān is melting and destroying [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/). It is said in tiruvāimoḻi 4.3.2 “*tēsamāna aṇikalanum en kai kūppuc ceygaiyē*” (My salutations to him with joined palms are his ornaments).

Is it just [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) melting āḻvār’s body after weakening it? \[What happens to emperumān himself?\]

- *nedumālē* – \[Greatly loving\] Only after seeing the other person’s total meltdown, emperumān will start melting. If we consider emperumān’s emotions, the emotions of [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) will appear to be nothing. His melting cannot be explained using words as done for [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s melting and can only be said as “*nedumāl*“. māl means vyāmōham (infatuation/love). nedumāl means great infatuation/love. Alternate explanation – māl means great person, and when asked if he is like brahmā, rudra et al, no, he is as said in tiruvāimoḻi 8.4.5 “*manisarkkut tēvar pōlat tēvarkkum tēvāvō*” (as dēvas (celestials) exist in a higher platform for manuśyas (humans), [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) exists for dēvas). nedumāl means sarvēśvaran (supreme lord of all). His greatness is a tool to melt āḻvār.
- *sīrār* … – The fresh and heavy paddy crops, looking at the beautiful reclining posture of emperumān, sway to the sides as if servitors are fanning him. sīr means heavy and beautiful. kavari means cāmaram (a type of fan). Alternatively, sīrmai (greatness) for the fresh paddy is that it is used in preparing food for ārāvamudāḻvār. In that case, it is the greatness as explained in taittirīya upaniśat “*aham annam*” (I am the food).
- *kavari vīsum* – As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 127.17 “*akāla palinō vrukśā:*” (let the trees blossom even during non-season). vīsum is a term in present tense, indicating it is already serving [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) \[no need to wait for harvest\]. Like those who read his mind and serve him accordingly. The master \[emperumān\] considers all the activities of his servant as a task done to please him \[Even the paddy crop naturally swaying is considered as a service by emperumān\].
- *seḻu nīr* – In tirukkudandai which has abundance of water bodies matching emperumān’s beautiful reclining posture. *seḻu nīr* also implies *peru nīr* (huge water body).
- *ēr Ar kōlam* … – You reclined and rested to give more shine to your beautiful decorations. People of this world will have their bodily shortcomings hidden while they are roaming around; but when they settle and start sleeping, their ugliness will manifest to those who look at them; but in [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s case, it is unlike that; as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 38.24 “*samayābōditaśśrīmān*” (the prosperous lord who was sleeping, was awakened by me), even when he is in sleeping posture, he should be rid of evil eyes falling on him. He is such that one will fear “what will happen if he wakes up?” \[we will not be able to enjoy his beautiful sleeping posture\].
- *kidandāy kaṇḍēn* – as said in the same ślōkam “*sukhasupta:*” (blissfully resting), I have seen his beautiful sleeping posture, but did not enjoy the aspects which I desired. \[Looking at me\] Standing up, being seated, walking around, asking me “what did you do?”, embracing me etc did not happen.
- *emmānē* – I can remain relaxed if I don’t think “emperumān’s beauty is mine to enjoy”. Both emperumān’s beauty and aptness \[of being my master\] are torturing me. Should you torture me showing this aptness?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

adiyen saraty ramanuja dasan

## 5.8.2. Emmane

*emmānē en veḷḷai mūrtti! ennai āḷvānē! emmā uruvum vēṇḍum āṟṟāl āvāy eḻilēṟē! semmā kamalam seḻunīr misaik kaṇ malarum tirukkudandai ammā malark kaṇ vaḷarginṟānē! ennān seygēnē?*

**Пословный перевод:**

emmānē – being my lord (to have my activities at your disposal); en – for me to acquire satva guṇam (goodness); veḷḷai – very pure; mūrtti – having a form; ennai – to ensure that I don’t lose my existence; āḷvānē – one who lets me enjoy him; e – in all species (such as dēva (celestial), manuśya (human), tiryak (animal) and stāvara (plant), for the sake of his devotees); mā – great; uruvum – incarnations; vēṇḍum āṟṟāl – out of desire; āvāy – one who assumes; eḻil – with the beauty in those forms, capturing the hearts as said in “pumsām druśti cittāpahāriṇām”; ēṟē – appears majestic; sem – reddish; mā – big; kamalam – lotus flowers; seḻu – abundance; nīrmisai – on the water; kaṇ – everywhere; malarum – blossoming; tirukkudandai – in tirukkudandai; a – that; mā – distinguished; malar – lotus flower like; kaṇ – divine eyes; vaḷargiṇrānē – oh one who is resting \[with your closed eyes\]!; nān – I; en – what; seygēn – shall I do?

**Перевод:**

**emperumān who is my lord, is having a pure form for me to acquire satva guṇam; he is showing that form to let me enjoy him and to ensure that I don’t lose my existence; he assumes various incarnations in all species out of his own desire; with the beauty in those forms, capturing the hearts as said in “pumsām druśti cittāpahāriṇām” he appears majestic; oh one who is resting with your distinguished lotus flower like divine eyes in tirukkudandai where there is abundance of reddish big lotus flowers blossoming everywhere on the water! what shall I do? Implies that – while all lotus flowers are blossoming, your two lotus like flowers \[eyes\] are not blossoming on looking at me.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the second pāsuram, āḻvār informs emperumān the favours he mercifully did towards āḻvār himself and the favours he mercifully does to his devotees. and calls him out telling him “You, who are of such nature, are not mercifully fulfilling my desire” with grief.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “You who assumed many incarnation for the sake of your devotees, are not mercifully glancing at me; what shall I do?”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Second pāsuram. Even after āḻvār calling out in this manner \[as seen in previous pāsuram\], emperumān did not respond to him; seeing that āḻvār thinks that emperumān is thinking “You take care of your needs yourself”, and calls him out citing his previous favours. emmānē en veḷḷai mūrtti! ennai āḷvānē! emmā uruvum vēṇḍum āṟṟāl āvāy eḻilēṟē! semmā kamalam seḻunīr misaik kaṇ malarum tirukkudandai ammā malark kaṇ vaḷarginṟānē! ennān seygēnē?*

- *emmānē* – Who will conduct the owned – will it be the owner or the owned on its own? To have you say “You manage your own activities”, am I an independent person? emmānē – my nāta! \[my lord\]
- *emmānē en veḷḷai mūrtti* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) asks – Did I know that he is my lord through pramāṇams (authentic quotes from śāstram) such as in nārāyaṇa sūktam “*patim viśvasya*” (lord of the universe) and “*yasyāsmi*” (I am the servant of sarvēśvaran)? When asked “So, how did you know?”, he says – since [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is of pure nature, he himself showed all his qualities fully, considering it as his own gain, and I saw (understood) it. Had you left a little bit ignorance in me, while you bestowed unblemiśed knowledge, I would have remained relaxed.
- *ennai āḷvānē* – Bestowing full knowledge initially, will you discard me now by making me work on my own? \[No\] It was emperumān who sustained [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) by giving knowledge about his qualities and ridding āḻvār’s sorrows in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.4](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/07/thiruvaimozhi-1-4-anjiraiya/) “*anjiṟaiya mada nārāy*“, [tiruvāimoḻi 5.3](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/06/thiruvaimozhi-5-3-masaru-sodhi/) “māsaṟu sōdi” etc.
- *em mā uruvum* – Don’t you know all the hardships you take up for me and your devotees? Another explanation – Distinguished form in all aspects. As said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 4.6](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/4-6/) “*prakrutim svām adiśtāya*” (accepting distinguished forms (made of spiritual matter)), having divine forms.
- *vēṇḍum āṟṟāl* – Two explanations – 1) as said in tiruvāimoḻi 6.4.7 “*tanakku vēṇḍuruk koṇḍu*” (accepting forms which he likes), out of his own desire 2) as said in mudal tiruvandādi 44 “*tamar ugandadevvuruvam avvuruvam tānē*” (he accepts the forms which are desired by his devotees), out of the desire of his devotees.
- *evvurum vēṇḍum āṟṟāl āvāy* – Is there any form which you have not accepted for the sake of your devotees as said in tiruviruttam 1 “*enninṟa yōniyumāyp piṟandāy*” (You have appeared in every species).
- *em mā uruvum* – Because these forms are accepted by [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), they are glorious.That is, as said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 5.3.2 “*āvirbhūtam*” (appearing), emperumān super-imposes his divine spiritual form into this worldly species. It is said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 6.7.70 “*rūpam anyattarēr mahat*” ([bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s spiritual form is different from worldly matter).
- *vēṇḍum āṟṟāl āvāy* – Just as the [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) accepts births based on its karma \[past deeds\], emperumān appears based on his own mercy. Both ([bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) and [ātmās](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)) have births. When ātmā’s karma is exhausted, his birth will stop; ātmā’s karma will be eliminated when it surrenders at the divine feet of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/); but for emperumān, his births will go on forever. For emperumān, his anugraham (mercy) is the karma \[which triggers his birth\], and his mercy is eternal for him \[hence he will also be born repeatedly forever\]. For the ātmā, his birth is limited to his own scope; but emperumān is born for \[the uplifting of \] everyone. Since the ātmā’s birth is out of karma, it will be for his own sake; but since emperumān’s birth is out of his mercy, it will be for the sake of others. This is explained in [śrī bhagavat gītā 4.5](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/4-5/) “*bahūni mē vyatītāni janmāni tavaca*” (You too have many many births). *tavaca* (yours too) indicates the similarity in the births of both; emperumān is saying “just as your births are real, mine too are”. If this is not the case, the [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) cannot be confident \[in emperumān’s protection\].
- *eḻil ēṟē* – When [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) assumes births for his devotees would he lose his radiance? \[No\] He will acquire new radiance which was not present before. Only when one is born out of karma, it leads to a shortcoming. tiruvāimoḻi 1.3.2 “*pala piṟappāy oḷi varu muḻu nalam*” (by assuming many births, his qualities acquire new radiance). yajur vēdam 3.6.1 “*sa u śrēyān bhavati jāyamāna:*” (He becomes more radiant by accepting new births) – for everyone as they accept new birth their radiance will diminish, but for emperumān, it increases with every birth. He would externally look radiant, but would he feel sad for having to accept such births? \[No\] He would feel prideful thinking “Yes, I have accepted this birth”. emperumān remains restrained like a prince as said in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 3.6.3 “*vāniḷavarsu*” (prince of paramapadam (spiritual realm)) due to protocol there in paramapadam. But here in this samsāram (material realm), as said in nācciyār tirumoḻi 14.1″*patti mēyndōr kārēṟu*” (A dark coloured bull like emperumān who is roaming around everywhere), he would give up all inhibitions and happily roam around. Hence, only after being born here, he acquires beauty \[and radiance\]. When one who knows emperumān’s nature tells him as in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 120.13 “*bhavān nārāyaṇō dēva:*” (You are that śrīman nārāyaṇan), you are so attached to your incarnation that you reply to them as in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 120.11 “*ātmānam mānuśam manyē*” (I consider myself as a human being) and as in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 5.13.12 “*ahamvō bāndavō jāta:*” (I am your relative).
- *sem mā* … – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) descends to [kōyils (divyadēśams, divine abodes)](https://koyil.org/) and rests there to help those who missed his help during his incarnations.
- *semmā kamalam* … – As the fragrance \[of the lotus flowers\] hits the face, he sleeps in a relaxed manner. As the reddish big lotus flowers come out of the attractive water bodies and blossom, \[that light\] reveals his ocean-coloured form and his limbs.
- *sem mā kamalam* – The lotus flower which withers within a fraction of a moment cannot be a match for [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s eyes – so when it is cited as an example, lots of adjectives \[such as sem, mā etc\] need to be added.
- *am mā malark kaṇ vaḷarginṟānē* – I am not seeing the opening \[blossoming\] of his beautiful lotus flower like divine eyes.
- *am mā malar* – These two eyes appear to be the same species as those lotus flowers, and I am not seeing these eyes blossom \[while the lotus flowers blossom\].
- *en nān seygēnē* – What shall I who cannot sustain without the blossoming of these eyes, do? In tirukkudandai, the beetles drink the honey from the blossomed lotus flowers and are happy, but I who can drink the honey from his blossomed eyes, remain hungry.
- *en nān seygēnē* – Are you thinking “this calling out will go on forever” ? \[No\] It is at the finishing stage. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is suffering like this because he thinks “I will not drink any other honey \[than from [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s blossomed eyes\]”. Blossoming \[opening\] of his eyes means, bestowing his special and merciful glance. When he is not opening his eyes, āḻvār too would not \[if emperumān is not conscious, āḻvār too would be unconscious\].

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.8.3. En nan seygen

*en nān seygēn yārē kaḷaikaṇ ennai en seyginṟāy unnāl allāl yāvarālum onṟum kuṟai vēṇḍēn kannār madiḷ sūḻ kudandaik kidandāy adiyēn aruvāṇāḷ sennāḷ ennāḷ annāḷ una tāḷ pidittē selakkāṇē*

**Пословный перевод:**

nān – I (who have no control over my doerśip); en – what activity; seygēn – shall do; kaḷaikaṇ – protector; yār – who?; ennai – me (who am incapable); en seyginṟāy – what are you planning to do? (are you planning to engage me in difficult upāyams (means)? or are you considering to accept responsibility for me?); unnāl allāl – other than you (who are protector of all, apt and capable); yāvarālum – anyone else (who is not a protector, inapt and incapable); onṟu – anything; kuṟaiyum – desire; vēṇḍēn – I will not pray; kan – firmness; Ar – abundant; madiḷ – fort; sūḻ – surrounded; kudandai – in tirukkudandai; kidandāy – Oh one who is mercifully resting!; adiyēn – I who am your servitor; aru – ātmā; vāḻ – uplifting; nāḷ – time; sel – happening; nāḷ – day; e – how many; nāḷ – days; annāḷ – those days; una – your; tāḷ – divine feet; pidittē – holding on; sela – to be; kāṇ – kindly see to it

**Перевод:**

**What activity shall I do \[to protect myself\]! Who \[else\] is the protector! what are you planning to do to me? I won’t pray to anyone else other than you to fulfil any of my desires. Oh one who is mercifully resting in tirukkudandai which is surrounded by abundantly firm fort! You kindly see to it that I who am your servitor hold on to your divine feet until the time I am uplifted, for as many days as it may take. aru indicates ātmā which is atomic in nature.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the third pāsuram, since āḻvār did not have his desires fulfilled even after calling out like this, he thinks “Hopefully emperumān is not thinking that I will conduct my activities on my own” and says to emperumān “you should mercifully fulfil my desires”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “I who am an akincana (empty handed), do not want my desires fulfilled from anyone other than you; you who made me like this, should see that I serve at your divine feet forever”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. en nān seygēn yārē kaḷaikaṇ ennai en seyginṟāy unnāl allāl yāvarālum onṟum kuṟai vēṇḍēn kannār madiḷ sūḻ kudandaik kidandāy adiyēn aruvāṇāḷ sennāḷ ennāḷ annāḷ una tāḷ pidittē selakkāṇē*

\[In śrīvacana bhūśaṇa divya śāstram sūtram 46, “*en nān seygēn*” is quoted. In the previous sūtrams it is explained that one may surrender to [arcāvatāra emperumān](http://ponnadi.blogspot.in/p/archavathara-anubhavam.html) due to ajñānam (not having knowledge to practice other means), adika jñānam (being greatly knowledgeable about the nature of self being totally dependent on emperumān) and bhakti pāravaśyam (overwhelming devotion). This sūtram explains that [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) exhibits all these three qualities while surrendering to [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/). Let us see how this is explained by [piḷḷai lōkācāryar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/pillai-lokacharyar/) and [maṇavāḷa māmunigaḷ](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/mamunigal/).

- First, āḻvār says “what can I do?” to indicate that he has no knowledge to practice other means and hence he is surrendering to emperumān.
- emperumān asks “But I have bestowed you unblemiśed knowledge, so why don’t you use that and practice any of the means such as karma yōgam, jñāna yōgam, bhakti yōgam etc?”. For that, āḻvār says, “As you have bestowed me with unblemiśed knowledge, I realise that I am fully dependent on you and so I cannot practice any other means which are contrary to the total dependence; so, what can I do?”.
- Finally, he says “Had you just bestowed knowledge, even if it is contrary to the nature of the self, I could have practiced other means \[to attain you\]. But you have bestowed devotion which is a matured state of knowledge. So, every time I think about you I become overwhelmed with devotional emotions; so, what can I do?”

So, in this “*en nān seygēn*” itself, all these three moods are manifested by āḻvār in showing his helpless situation\]

- *en nān seygēn yārē kaḷaikaṇ ennai en seyginṟāy* – Have you left it to me to take care of myself? Are you leaving to others to protect me? ōr are you planning to protect me yourself?
- *en nān seygēn* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is not asking “what can I do?”, \[he is thinking\] there is no match between me and the actions that are to be done by me.
- *yārē kaḷaikaṇ* – Can a drowning person rescue another drowning person? How can those who are not even qualified for sharing of mutual experience as said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 10.9](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/10-9/) “*bōdayanta parasparam*” do anything?
- *ennai en seyginṟāy* – As said in periya tiruvandādi 6 “*neṟi kātti nīkkudiyō nin pāl karumā muṟi mēni kāttudiyō*” (Would you lead me to other upāyams and shun me, or would you show your beautiful form resembling dark leaf and uplift me?), what are you thinking to do?
- *en nān seygēn yārē kaḷaikaṇ ennai en seyginṟāy* -Don’t you know me? Don’t you know others? Don’t you know yourself? Looks like you are thinking of me to be an independent person who is capable of accomplishing his own goals!
- *yārē kaḷaikaṇ* – How can those who are not up to my level \[in attaining your mercy, or in knowledge/devotion\], protect me?
- *ennai en seyginṟāy* – Are you planning to fulfil my desires? ōr, are you going to shun me by telling me “engage in some sādanam (means) and attain me” as naḷa led damayanti \[to her parents’ place\].
- *en nān seygēn* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is withdrawing from his own protection.
- *yārē kaḷaikaṇ* – āḻvār is withdrawing from accepting others’ protection.
- *ennai en seyginṟāy* – Are you planning to tell me as in [śrī bhagavat gītā 9.34](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/9-34/) “*mādyāji mām namaskuru*” (worship me, bow down to me) \[i.e., engage me in bhakti yōgam\]? ōr are you planning to tell me as in śrī bhagavat gītā 18.66 “*mā suca:*” (do not worry) \[kriṣṇa telling “I will be your means”\]?
- *unnāl allāl yāvarālum onṟum kuṟai vēṇḍēn* – If you told me “*mām namaskuru*“, my grief will not disappear. Even to attain you, I would only do that through you; I would not want to attain you by me (my own efforts) or through others. Some explain this “*unnāl allāl*” in context of upēyam (goal) and say this as “Except for attaining you, I have no other desire”.
- *yāvarālum* – Instead of saying “*yāvaiyālum*” (by any means), [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying “*yāvarālum*” (by any one) due to the fact that upāyam is associated with a cētana (sentient) \[only a conscious person can be the trigger for any means and the means are simply processes which on their own have no standing\].
- *onṟum kuṟai vēṇḍēn* – Though other processes can \[eventually\] lead to fulfilment of one’s desires, since pursuing them is like having the deity of death decorating our finger with a ring, it is contrary to our nature, so I will not accept that. \[[āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is \] Just like [sītāp pirātti](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/) who did not reach [śrī rāma](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) riding on hanuman who was ready to cross the ocean and take her to śrī rāma \[attaining the goal through others\] or by cursing \[rāvaṇa to be destroyed, that is by her own efforts/abilities\]. That is, destroying the true nature of both \[[bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) and [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/), by doing what is contrary to their nature\]. I do not want anyone to remove any of me worries.
- *kannār madiḷ sūḻ kudandaik kidandāy* – The manner which āḻvār’s means ([emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)) is securely present. \[āḻvār is happy about emperumān being protected in the fort\] It is the responsibility of those who remain with emperumān as the upāyam and upēyam, to protect him due to overwhelming care towards him. As said by [periyāḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/periyazhwar/) in [tiruppallāṇḍu 1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/06/thiruppallandu-1-pallandu/) “*sevvadi sevvi tirukkāppu*” (let his divine reddish feet be protected\].
- *kannār madiḷ* – The fort which has abundance of activities, copper and firmness \[kan has these three meanings\].
- *adiyēn aru* – This ātmā which exists exclusively for you without even a tinge of self-interest.
- *vāḻ nāḷ sen nāḷ en nāḷ* – The day in which I will be uplifted.
- *an nāḷ* – Until that day.
- *una tāḷ pidittē selak kāṇē* – You should mercifully see that I am constantly beholding your divine feet. You should mercifully ensure that I don’t even leave them for a fraction of a second. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying – you did not come and fulfil my desire when I said “I don’t want anything from anyone”; I may get that experience some day; but until then you mercifully ensure that my faith does not diminish as said in “*unnāl allāl yāvarālum onṟum kuṟai vēṇḍēn*“. If he lets go of the divine feet, then his faith will diminish. One who lived by holding on to his divine feet, will not let them go now \[also, explained as, from the beginning, āḻvār was holding on to his divine feet and will not let go of them now\]. With this faith, āḻvār is a parama bhakti yuktar (fully situated in ultimate devotion), and so what is the reason for \[[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s\] delay? emperumān is keeping him here to nurture his bhakti further and to reform the world with his love-filled words.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.8.4. Selak kangirpar

*selak kāṇgiṟpār kāṇum aḷavum sellum kīrttiyāy! ulappilānē! ellā ulagum udaiya oru mūrtti! nalattāl mikkār kudandaik kidandāy unnaik kāṇbān nān alappāy ākāsattai nōkki aḻuvan toḻuvanē*

**Пословный перевод:**

sela – to go further; kāṇgiṟpār – those who have the ability to see; kāṇum aḷavum – as far as they can see; sellum – having greatness of going beyond the reach; kīrttiyāy – one who is having qualities, wealth etc; ulappu – end; ilānē – one without having; ellā ulagum – all of the world; udaiya – having at his service; oru – distinguished; mūrtti – having a form, which is the goal; nalattār mikkār – of those who have great love towards you; kudandai – in tirukkudandai; kidandāy – Oh one who is resting (for their enjoyment)!; unnai – you (who is greater than all, yet easily accessible for all); nān – I (who am very determined); kāṇbān – to see and enjoy as desired; alappāy – grieved; ākāsattai – the sky (from where you can descend); nōkki – looking at; aḻuvan – crying out like those who have great devotion; toḻuvan – vorśipping you (like those who have surrendered to you)

**Перевод:**

**emperumān is having endless qualities, wealth etc and greatness of going beyond the reach of those who have the ability to see further \[and further\], as much as they can see; he is having all of the world at his service; he is having a distinguished form which is the goal; oh such emperumān who is resting in tirukkudandai which is \[made up\] of those who have great love towards you! To see you and enjoy as desired, I am grieving and looking at the sky, crying out like those who have great devotion and those who worship you. Also explained as crying like a child and vorśipping like a matured person.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fourth pāsuram, āḻvār says “I am suffering having not been able to see you who have descended in tirukkudandai and resting here even after your being sarvēśvara (supreme lord) and I am having the desire to see you”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. selak kāṇgiṟpār kāṇum aḷavum sellum kīrttiyāy! ulappilānē! ellā ulagum udaiya oru mūrtti! nalattāl mikkār kudandaik kidandāy unnaik kāṇbān nān alappāy ākāsattai nōkki aḻuvan toḻuvanē*

- *sela* … – All your glories which were acquired through your auspicious qualities are going to be destroyed.
- *selak kāṇgiṟpār kāṇum aḷavum sellum kīrttiyāy* – Even if greatly knowledgeable persons acquire more knowledge and try to reach you, you will prove to be beyond their reach. As said in mūnṟām tiruvantādi 21 “*pēsuvār evvaḷavu pēsuvar avvaḷavē … vakkaranaik konṟān vadivu*” ([emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) the one who is wearing fragrant flower and tuḷasi garland, who is having radiant divine disc, divine conch, divine bow and the one who killed dantavktra; the nature and qualities of such emperumān match the ability of those who praise him) – his greatness keeps rising up to that level to which people speak of the greatness of his divine auspicious forms
- *ulappilānē* – While his true nature, form, qualities are beyond the reach of an individual’s intelligence, will he himself be limited in any sense? \[No\] “*ulappilānē*” (endless) – even he himself cannot see the boundary of his qualities \[This is an important point to understand clearly – if he does not know his boundary, it will be construed as a shortcoming of “his not knowing something”. But since there is no boundary for his greatness, he does not know of something which does not exist. So it is not a shortcoming, it only adds to his greatness of having endless glories\]. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) himself explains in tiruvāimoḻi 8.4.6 “*tanakkum than tanmai aṟivariyān*” ([emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) does not know his own greatness\].
- *ellā ulagum udaiya oru mūrtti* – One who manifests his beautiful form, captures all creatures and places them at his divine feet. When people see his form, they will know that he is the controller of everything. The term “mūrtti” indicates both vigraham (form) and aiśvaryam (control, wealth); in that case, this is understood as – distinguished [sarvēśvaran](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) who is the controller of all the worlds. What is the purpose of explaining these? [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying “you are setting out to destroy your own glories”; emperumān cannot say “the place wherein you are suffering is not within my reign” \[since everything is his\].
- *nalattāl mikkārk kudandaik kidandāy* – Had you remained put in your distinct nature, form etc in paramapadam, I would have remained relaxed. But you are holding on firmly to the divine abode \[of tirukkudandai\] which is dear to those who cannot exist without you.
- *nalattāl mikkār* – Those who are affectionate towards you without being able to follow the rules \[due to overwhelming devotion towards you\]. nalam – snēham – affection.
- *unnaik kāṇbān nān* – I am suffering with desire to see you who has śrīvaikuṇṭam as your divine assembly yet resting in tirukkudandai without leaving your devotees, in the manner in which you desire to see me. I who am greatly determined.
- *unnaik kāṇbān nān* – It is I who am seeing you; and you who are seen; in this case, how can I remain relaxed.
- *unnai* – Also explained as, you who are enjoyable as previously explained.
- *alappāy* – Being grieved. This ([emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)) is unlike casual sports/games like gambling, chess etc., which can be enjoyed sometimes and disregarded in other times. It is the unbearable suffering due to not seeing emperumān.
- *ākāsattai nōkki* – Three explanations – 1) Though tiruvadi’s (hanuman’s) voice was heard in one direction, sītāp pirātti looked around everywhere out of anxiety as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 31.19 “*sā tiryak ūrdvam ca*” (while the voice of hanuman came from up). While saying “*unnai”* (you, who are in front), why is he saying “*ākāsattai nōkki*“? This is the reaction of being bewildered as said in “*alappāy*” (being grieved). While emperumān is right in front of [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/), āḻvār is looking up in the sky since his desire was not fulfilled. He is looking up thinking “[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) will come for my rescue seeking my state, as he came for śrī gajēndrāḻvān”. 2) āṇḍān explains this as “seeing my helpless state” \[here ākāśam is cited to say that āḻvār is having no other support/refuge\]. 3) As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 13.16 “*gaganāsakta lōcana:*” (daśarata’s state after hearing kaikēyi’s words – having eyes pointing towards the sky), he is in such a sorrow state that his eyes cannot focus on emperumān who is in front of him.
- *aḻuvan toḻuvanē* – I am doing what is done by both upāsakas (bhakti yōga practitioners – crying out) and prapannas (those who have nothing in them and are fully surrendered – vorśipping); I am doing what is done by those who are having unfulfilled desires \[crying\] and also those who are having detachment \[vorśipping\].

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.8.5. Aluvan toluvan

*aḻuvan toḻuvan ādik kāṇban pādi alaṟṟuvan taḻuval vinaiyāl pakka nōkki nāṇik kaviḻndiruppan seḻu oṇ paḻanak kudandaik kidandāy sendāmaraik kaṇṇā toḻuvanēnai una tāḷ sērum vagaiyē sūḻ kaṇḍāy*

**Пословный перевод:**

aḻuvan – (due to being bewildered) cry; toḻuvan – (due to having clarity) worship; ādi – dance; kāṇban – see; pādi – (being overwhelmed with \[emperumān‘s\] qualities) sing; alaṟṟuvan – (due to grief) blabber; taḻu – embracing me; val vinaiyāl – this powerful sin of love; pakkam – directions (from where he can arrive); nōkki – look; nāṇi – feeling ashamed (due to not retaining the true nature \[having done all of these\] and not attaining the desire \[of emperumān‘s arrival\]); kaviḻndiruppan – hang my head down; seḻu – abundant; oṇ – attractive; paḻanam – having water rich fields; kudandai – in tirukkudandai; kidandāy – resting there (for the sake of your devotees); sem – reddish; tāmarai – lotus flower like; kaṇṇā – oh one who is having divine eyes!; toḻuvanēnai – (due to lacking any other refuge) I who am very needy \[of your protection\]; un – (you who are apt) your; tāḷ – (enjoyable) divine feet; sērum vagai – to reach; (nīyē) sūḻ kaṇḍāy – find out the appropriate means

**Перевод:**

**I cry, worship, dance and see, sing, blabber, look around in all directions due to this powerful sin of love which has embraced me, and hang my head down feeling ashamed. Oh one who is having reddish lotus flower like divine eyes, and resting in tirukkudandai which is having abundance of attractive water rich fields! You find out the appropriate means to reach your divine feet for me who am very needy \[of your protection\].**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fifth pāsuram, āḻvār says “Having the desire to see you, I have done many acts to invoke your mercy and yet I have not seen you; you should yourself see that I attain your divine feet”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. aḻuvan toḻuvan ādik kāṇban pādi alaṟṟuvan taḻuval vinaiyāl pakka nōkki nāṇik kaviḻndiruppan seḻu oṇ paḻanak kudandaik kidandāy sendāmaraik kaṇṇā toḻuvanēnai una tāḷ sērum vagaiyē sūḻ kaṇḍāy*

- *aḻuvan toḻuvan* – I am doing what is done by children \[crying\] and by those who have knowledge in vēdāntam (worship/surrender). It is said in perumāḷ tirumoḻi 5.1 “*maṟṟavaḷ than aruḷ ninaindē aḻum kuḻavi*” (the child which will cry and seek its mother’s mercy).
- *ādik kāṇban* – Just as a hungry person will dance if told “we will give you food, can you dance for us?”, I too will dance \[to seek his attention\]. \[kāṇban – dance and then see if it helped in attaining [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)\] [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) does not know how he will reach emperumān.
- *pādi alaṟṟuvan* – Overflowing love leading to singing, and that too in a disorderly manner.
- *taḻuval vinaiyāl* – This powerful sin which has come all along with me and stops me from seeing him, even after trying in so many ways like this. This powerful sin of love which stops me from embracing him. Here bhakti (loving devotion) is cited as sin, since sin is that which leads to unfavourable results.
- *pakkam nōkki* – Since [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) considers “[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) will arrive just on seeing āḻvār’s suffering”, he is looking at the direction of his arrival.
- *nāṇik kaviḻndiruppan* – Since emperumān does not arrive there, “I desired for him only to be dejected” and hangs his head in shame. Alternative explanation – *pakkam nōkki nāṇik kaviḻndiruppan* – āḻvār is feeling shy thinking about how emperumān will be censured by those who are there saying “this is how he helps those who desire him”.
- *seḻu oṇ paḻanak kudandaik kidandāy* – Oh one who is mercifully resting in tirukkudandai which is having huge beautiful water bodies.
- *sem tāmaraik kaṇṇā* – My life is sustained not by mukāntaram \[different face, different person/means\]. My life is sustained by your face with the reddish lotus flower like eyes. You are like the one who is having wealth \[here, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s face, eyes etc\], but not giving it to others.
- *toḻuvanēnai* – Two meanings. 1) krupaṇa – needy of your protection due to not having any other refuge and cannot exist without you; 2) I who am full of defects with interest in worldly pleasures.
- *una tāḷ …* – You should mercifully find out the means for me to reach your divine feet. Even I don’t need to know that means, I only need to reach you. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is thinking that his urge/haste in attaining [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is just his nature and not the means to reach emperumān. He considers the goal to be attained by emperumān only.
- *sūḻ kaṇḍāy* – Towards ananya prayōjanar (those who have no other desire than serving emperumān), even thinking about their uplifting is emperumān’s task.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.8.6. Sul kanday

*sūḻ kaṇḍāy en tollai vinaiyai aṟuttu un adi sērum ūḻ kaṇḍirundē tūrāk kuḻi tūrttu enai nāḷ aganṟiruppan vāḻ tol pugaḻār kudandaik kidandāy vānōr kōmānē! yāḻin isaiyē amudē aṟivin payanē ariyēṟē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vāḻ – due to enriched living (of experiencing bhagavān); tol – natural; pugaḻār – of those who are having glories; kudandai – in tirukkudandai; kidandāy – mercifully resting (to be enjoyed by them); vānōr – for nityasūris; kōmānē – being the controller (and enjoyed by them); yāḻin – the musical instrument yāḻ (an ancient string instrument, which is unlike the throat which may not function well at times); isaiyē – like the tune (enjoyable to the ears); amudē – like the eternally enjoyable nectar, one who is enjoyable to the tongue through stutis (praising songs) etc; aṟivin payanē – being enjoyable to the mind, since you are the result of knowledge; ariyēṟē – like the best among the lions, one who is great and hence cannot be comprehended; (nān) un – (I) your; adi – divine feet; sērum – to reach and exist exclusively for you; ūḻ – ancient aspect; kaṇḍirundē – having seen; tūrā – difficult to fill; kuḻi – the pit of inappropriate desires; tūrttu – dug (through inappropriate pleasures); enai – how many; nāḷ – days; aganṟu – being separate; iruppan – can I exist; en – my; tol vinaiyai – ancient sins; aṟuttu – sever; unnadi sērumpadi – to reach your divine feet which is apt for my true nature; sūḻkaṇḍāy – mercifully do it

**Перевод:**

**You are mercifully resting in tirukkudandai which is of those who are having natural glories due to enriched living (of experiencing bhagavān); you are the controller for nityasūris; you are like the most enjoyable tune of  the musical instrument yāḻ; you are like the eternally enjoyable nectar, one who is enjoyable to the tongue through stutis; you are enjoyable to the mind, since you are the result of knowledge; still, you are like the best among the lions, one who is great and hence cannot be comprehended; (I) having seen the ancient aspect of reaching your divine feet and existing exclusively for you, how many more days do I have to exist separated \[from you\] in this pit of inappropriate desires which is difficult to fill and is dug (through inappropriate pleasures)? Mercifully sever my ancient sins and help me reach your divine feet which is apt for my true nature.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the th pāsuram, āḻvār says “Since I having been captivated in your enjoyable nature and cannot exist with other worldly aspects, you have to eliminate the hurdles for me in attaining you, and find out the means to attain you and mercifully see to making it work for me even without my knowledge”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. sūḻ kaṇḍāy en tollai vinaiyai aṟuttu un adi sērum ūḻ kaṇḍirundē tūrāk kuḻi tūrttu enai nāḷ aganṟiruppan vāḻ tol pugaḻār kudandaik kidandāy vānōr kōmānē! yāḻin isaiyē amudē aṟivin payanē ariyēṟē*

- *sūḻ kaṇḍāy en tollai vinaiyai aṟuttu* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says “Please sever my ancient sins with their traces and ensure that you mercifully find out the means for me to reach your divine feet “. When [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) says “I will do it in proper sequence/order”, āḻvār asks “what is the reason for that?”.
- *un adi sērum ūḻ kaṇḍirundē* – Unlike the people of this world who don’t know about you, I know the means (ūḻ – path) to reach your divine feet.
- *tūrāk kuḻi tūrttu* – Feeding the sense organs which can never be satisfied.
- *enai nāḷ aganṟiruppan* – How long do I have to be here? Will you give a set date only for those who are like śrī bharatāḻvān?
- *vāḻ tol pugaḻār kudandaik kidandāy* – Those who don’t have the necessity to ask “how many days do we need to remain separated from you?”. Having the great glory of living in his vicinity. *tol pugaḻār* is also explained as “ancient glory”. When asked “Though [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) and they \[the residents of tirukkudandai\] have equal exposure to worldly pleasures, why is āḻvār celebrating them to be living gloriously?”. he explains that they need not call out for [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) as he is readily available for them.
- *vānōr kōmānē* – nityasūris are the residents of paramapadam which is not controlled by time.
- *yāḻin isaiyē* – The tune of yāḻ is unlike the throat, which gets troubled with infection etc at times due to one’s own karma. He is already explained in [tiruvāimoḻi 2.3.7](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/02/thiruvaimozhi-2-3-7-munnal-yazh/) “*yāḻ payil nūl narambin mudir suvaiyē*” (unlimitedly enjoyable like matured music played from the string of the musical instrument yāḻ, as per gītā śāstram (the set of sacred texts relating to music)).
- *amudē* – While he is pleasing to the ears, he is also enjoyable to the tongue, so that one need not search for something else for the tongue.
- *aṟivin payanē* – The joy which is the result of \[true\] knowledge. Being enjoyable for the mind.
- *ariyēṟē* – One who is great due to being different from all species. Also explained as one who is having great enjoyability which cannot be held by our eyes. While you are greatly enjoyable having given yourself to those who are here (in tirukkudandai) and there (paramapadam), how long do I have to remain separated, feeding my sense organs?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.8.7. Ariyere

*ariyēṟē ennam poṟcudarē sengatkarumugilē eriyē pavaḷak kunṟē nāl tōḷ endāy unadaruḷē piriyā adimai ennaik koṇḍāy kudandait tirumālē tariyēn ini un saraṇam tandu en sanmam kaḷaiyāyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ariyēṟē – one who is appearing majestic due to his uncontrollable independence; am – attractive; pon – like gold; sudar – radiance in his form; en – one who let me enjoy; sem – reddish; kaṇ – having divine eyes; karu mugilē – having dark cloud like form which is the abode for previously explained radiance; eriyē – reddish like fire; pavaḷak kunṟē – having a tall firm form like that of a pearl mountain; nāl tōḷ – manifesting four shoulders along with that form; endāy – being my lord who accepted me as his servant; unadu – your; aruḷ – mercy; piriyā – to never separate; adimai – services through speech etc; (ennai) koṇḍāy – accepted (me), and as the recipient of such service; kudandai – in tirukkudandai; tirumālē – oh one who appeared along with lakśmī!; ini – after (you being the benefactor along with pirātti); tariyēn – will not remain relaxed; un – your; saraṇam – caraṇam, the divine feet; tandu – bestow; en – my; sanmam – connection with this body; kaḷaivāy – eliminate with the traces

**Перевод:**

**emperumān is appearing majestic due to his uncontrollable independence, is having reddish divine eyes, is having dark cloud like form which is the abode for previously explained radiance, is having a fire like reddish tall firm form like that of a pearl mountain, is my lord who manifested four shoulders along with that form and accepted me as his servant; you accepted my services through speech etc to have me never separated from your mercy; oh one who is the recipient of my such service in tirukkudandai appearing along with lakśmī! I will not remain relaxed after this \[seeing you being the benefactor along with pirātti\]. Bestow me your divine feet and eliminate my connection with this body along with the traces.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the seventh pāsuram, āḻvār says “Just out of your mercy, you manifested your beauty etc and made me exist purely by serving you; now, as I cannot exist without your divine feet, please bestow me your divine feet and eliminate samsāram (my connection with this material realm) for me”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. ariyēṟē ennam poṟcudarē sengatkarumugilē eriyē pavaḷak kunṟē nāl tōḷ endāy unadaruḷē piriyā adimai ennaik koṇḍāy kudandait tirumālē tariyēn ini un saraṇam tandu en sanmam kaḷaiyāyē*

- *ariyēṟē* – The pride he acquired due to being the controller of all entities other than him.
- *en am pon sudarē* – When seen through that pride, one who is having attractive radiance similarly to that of distinguished and attractive gold. One who announced that greatness of that form to me.
- *sem kaṇ karu mugilē* – The cause for such radiance – the divine eyes and the divine body.
- *eriyē pavaḷak kunṟē* – eri – kēttai (jyēśta) star. His divine collective beauty appears like a tall pearl mountain risen up to the position of stars. Another explanation – appearing like reddish (fire like) pearl mountain. The thought behind such example is – splendour and attractiveness. For those who are unfavourable, he is like fire and for those who are favourable, he is attractive due to his splendour.
- *kunṟē* – immeasurable.
- *nāl tōḷ endāy* – Oh one who captured me to exist exclusively for you by manifesting your divine shoulders which appear like beautiful branches of kalpaka tree (a celestial tree). [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) was captivated by the same beautiful feature as tiruvadi (hanuman) was captivated.
- *unadu aruḷ* … – With your unconditional mercy, you have won over me as your servant fully.
- *aruḷē* – by the mercy.
- *kudandait tirumālē* – Oh one who descended along with periya pirāttiyār to tirukkudandai and mercifully rested there to accept me as your servant. Since it is not in the special abode of paramapadam \[and is in tirukkudandai\], there is no shortcoming in the place, and since he is śriya:pati \[[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) along with [pirātti](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/)\], there is no shortcoming in the aptness of the goal. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is also surrendering to emperumān, having pirātti as puruśakāram (one who recommends) as done by iḷaiya perumāḷ (lakśmaṇa) in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 31.25  “*bhavāmstu saha vaidēhyā girisānuśu ramsyatē*” (While you enjoy with sītā in the foothills of the mountain, I will serve you both in all ways).
- *tariyēn ini* – After seeing that togetherness, how can I sustain myself in separation? When the mother and father are present, and if they are wealthy and generous too, can their child remain hungry?

When asked “How long can you not sustain?”, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says,

- *un saraṇam tandu en sanmam kaḷaiyāyē* – Just as a mother will first suckle an ailing child and then give treatment for the child’s disease, āḻvār is saying “first bestow me your divine feet and then eliminate my bondage in this material realm”. [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is going to treat the wounded body and eliminate the karma (deeds); to do that, he should first sustain āḻvār (by bestowing his divine feet) and then eliminate it.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.8.8. Kalaivay tunbam

*kaḷaivāy tunbam kaḷaiyādoḻivāy kaḷaikaṇ maṟṟilēn vaḷai vāy nēmip padaiyāy kudandaik kidanda mā māyā taḷarā udalam enadāvi sarindu pōm pōdu iḷaiyāduna tāḷ orungappidittup pōda isai nīyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tunbam – sorrow (of not enjoying you); kaḷaivāy – eliminate; kaḷiyādoḻivāy – not eliminate; kaḷaikaṇ – eliminator of sorrows; maṟṟu – any other; ilēn – not having; vaḷai – round; vāy – having mouth; nēmi – divine chakra; padaiyāy – one who is having as weapon; kudandai – in tirukkudandai; kidanda – mercifully resting; māmāyā – oh one who is very amazingly beautiful!; udalam – body; taḷarā – weakened; enadu – my; āvi – prāṇa (life); sarindu – becomes shaken; pōm pōdu – the final stage of leaving the body arrives; iḷaiyādu – without losing the mental strength; una – your; tāḷ – divine feet; orunga – in a singular manner (as upāyam (means) and upēyam (goal)); pidittu – holding on; pōda – to conduct; nīyē – you only; isai – allow

**Перевод:**

**I am not having any other protector, whether you eliminate my sorrow or not; oh one who is very amazingly beautiful, who is mercifully resting in tirukkudandai and is having the divine chakra with rounded mouth as weapon; when my body becomes weakened, prāṇa becomes shaken and the final stage of leaving the body arrives, you only have to allow me to conduct myself holding on to your divine feet in a singular manner without losing the mental strength.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the eighth pāsuram, āḻvār became so perplexed that he could not think about emperumān since emperumān did not appear even after āḻvār saying “tariyēn” (I cannot sustain); he says “it does not matter whether you protect me or not; let that be so; but you should mercifully see that I am able to meditate upon your divine feet; this is what I need now”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. kaḷaivāy tunbam kaḷaiyādoḻivāy kaḷaikaṇ maṟṟilēn vaḷai vāy nēmip padaiyāy kudandaik kidanda mā māyā taḷarā udalam enadāvi sarindu pōm pōdu iḷaiyāduna tāḷ orungappidittup pōda isai nīyē*

- *kaḷaivāy tunbam kaḷaiyādu oḻivāy kaḷaikaṇ maṟṟilēn* – Whether you do your duty or not; I am not worried; I have no doubt in the principle of “*tvamēva upāya bhūtōmē bhava*”  (Let you be my only means);  whether you do or do not do your duty as said in śrī bhagavat gītā 18.66 “*sarva pāpēbhyō mōkśayiśyāmi*” (I will free you from all sins).

Since [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is not confirming that he will do so, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) highlights that emperumān’s presence is for āḻvār’s protection only.

- *vaḷai vāy nēmip padaiyāy* – Having the divine chakra which has mouth everywhere it is seen, as the weapon. Is there any limitation in your not eliminating my sorrows? Is there any part of the weapon in your hand, where there is no mouth? Don’t you need to have the purpose of having those mouths fulfilled? Can you say that you don’t have the tool \[to protect me\]? Is there the limitation of “I have nothing in my hands; I need to gather my weapons/army”?
- *nēmip padaiyāy kaḷaikaṇ maṟṟilēn* – Is there a weapon like that in my hand or in others’ hands or don’t you have any weapon?
- *kudandaik kidanda māmāyā* – You see this greatness \[of [arcāvatāra emperumān](http://ponnadi.blogspot.in/p/archavathara-anubhavam.html)\] for yourself after saying in śrī bhagavat gītā 18.66 “*mām*” \[kriṣṇa pointing to himself, saying “me” and revealing his ultimate simplicity\]. With this, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is establishing that [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s [arcāvatāram (deity form)](http://ponnadi.blogspot.in/p/archavathara-anubhavam.html) is even more easily accessible than his vibhavāvatārams (such as śrī rāma, kriṣṇa). īsn’t his merciful resting with amazing beauty in tirukkudandai is for the sake of his devotees? He cannot be said to be lacking in abilities. He cannot be said as “not easily accessible”. He cannot be said as “not the one who triggers our ruci (taste towards him)”.
- *taḷarā udalam* – when the body weakens.
- *enadu āvi sarindu pōm pōdu* – I have reached the stage where my life is going to end.
- *pōm pōdu* – The time of departure has arrived. Is this antima smruti \[thoughts \[about emperumān\] during the final moments is indicated as a means to attain the desired goal\]? It is not that āḻvār does not know \[i.e., [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) knows\] varāha [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s vow “*kāśta pāśāṇa sannibam*” (one who is unconscious like wood or stone) and “*aham smarāmi*” (during the last moments of such ātmās who had previously surrendered unto me, I will think about them and deliver them); he is also unlike such persons \[who use other means to attain emperumān\]. It is just due to the sorrow of separation from emperumān, now āḻvār’s body has become weakened and the ātmā has reached the stage of departing from the body.
- *iḷaiyādu …* – Even if I don’t have my desire fulfilled, you should mercifully ensure that my faith in your holding on to your divine feet to have my desire fulfilled, remains intact. Since he did not acquire the experience, he became fearful thinking “is my firm faith in the means which will fulfil the desire, diminishing?”, he asks [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) to mercifully ensure that such faith remains intact.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.
