## 5.8.9. Isaivittu ennai

*isaivittennai un tāḷiṇaik kīḻ iruttum ammānē asaivil amarar talaivar talaivā ādip perumūrtti! tisai vil vīsum seḻu mā maṇigaḷ sērum tirukkudandai asaivil ulagam paravak kidandāy kāṇa vārāyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ennai – me (who have turned away from you since time immemorial); isaivittu – to accept (my true nature of being your servitor); un – your; tāḷ iṇaik kīḻ – at divine feet, with the knowledge of them being both the means and the goal; iruttum – placing (me to exist exclusively for you); ammānē – being the lord; asaivu – disturbance; il – not having; amarar – nityasūris \[eternal residents of paramapadam\]; talaivar – leaders such as ananta \[ādiśēśan\] , garuda, viśvaksēna et al; talaivā – being the leader; ādi – being the cause for everything; peru – greater than all; mūrtti – having a form; tisai – in all directions; vil – radiance; vīsum – spreading; seḻu – attractive; mā – most expensive; maṇigaḷ – precious gems; sērum – reaching; tirukkudandai – in tirukkudandai; asaivu – shakiness due to doubt of difficulty \[in attaining him\]; il – being removed; ulagam – world; parava – to praise; kidandāy – oh one who is mercifully resting; kāṇa – to see (your beauty in walking posture); vārāy – should come

**Перевод:**

**You being the lord, made me to accept by placing me at your divine feet with the knowledge of them being the means and the goal; you are the leader of the leaders of nitysūris such as ananta, garuda, viśvaksēna et al who are free from disturbances; you are the cause for everything; you are having a form which is greater than all; oh one who is resting in tirukkudandai which is reached by most expensive, attractive precious gems which are spreading their radiance in all directions to be praised by the world which is removed of the shakiness due to doubt of difficulty  \[in attaining him\]! You should come for me to see. asaivu il ulagam – asaivu – the world that is swaying in the ocean of sorrow gets captivated in his beauty and praises him. It can also indicate the paramapadam which is unśakeable. ōr the world can said to be praising emperumān who is moving his divine body from left to right, while reclining.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the ninth pāsuram, āḻvār says “You being the sarvēśvaran, who descended to and mercifully rested in tirukkudandai to be surrendered to by everyone and made me accept your lordship and made me not to survive without servitude towards you, should also appear in front of me to be seen by me”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “You who bestowed me acceptance towards you and enjoyed me to consider your divine feet as the goal for me, should show me your beautiful walk just as you showed the beautiful reclining posture”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. isaivittennai un tāḷiṇaik kīḻ iruttum ammānē asaivil amarar talaivar talaivā ādip perumūrtti! tisai vil vīsum seḻu mā maṇigaḷ sērum tirukkudandai asaivil ulagam paravak kidandāy kāṇa vārāyē*

- *isaivittu ennai* – Making me accept. Making me who was turning away from you since long, accept in your service. While you can convince me, who was unconvinced, why is it difficult for you who are already favourable towards me, to help me \[now\]?
- *ennai* – I who am lower than nitya samsāri (eternally bound soul).
- *un tāḻiṇaik kīḻ iruttum* – Oh one who placed me at the divine feet which are served by nityasūris. [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who can place me at his divine feet to remain peaceful instead of craving for them \[due to not being there\]. Making [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) as his pādukā (sandals), that is, śrī śatakōpam (śrī śatāri) as said in periya tiruvandādi 31 “*niḻalum aditāṟum ānōm*” (we became your shadow and footprints). Like a small particle in a storm, āḻvār was previously as said in tiruviruttam 95 “*yādānum paṟṟi nīngum viradam*” (leaving emperumān by holding on to anything else).
- *ammānē* – While the benefit is for [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/), [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is making him accept, due to his eternal relationship with āḻvār.
- *asaivil amarar talaivar talaivā* – There are amaras (immortal persons) who have no disturbances. They are the nityasūris. The activities of śrī sēnāpati āḻvān (viśvaksēnar) who is the leader of nityasūris, are also at emperumān’s full disposal. Not having asaivu means – the immortality of nityasūris is unlike that of brahmā et al which are dependent on others. That is, they are only immortal until the mahā praḷayam \[total deluge\]. Not having asaivu also means – their knowledge being always expanded unlike that of dēvatās whose knowledge expands/contracts.
- *ādip peru mūrtti* – One who is the cause for sustenance of everyone. The supreme lord who is the cause of the universe. mūrtti – svāmi (lord).
- *tisai vil* … – He protected everyone; and instead of leaving it for them to take care of the subsequent aspects, he himself descended to take care of the subsequent aspects too. In tirukkudandai, which is reached by most expensive attractive  precious gems, the radiance of those, spreading in all directions. vil – tējas (radiance).
- *asaivil ulagam paravak kidandāy* – You mercifully rested to let the world surrender unto you without any difficulty. To stop the shakiness of the world which was due to the doubt of the difficulty in attaining [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/). Alternative explanation – there is an unśakeable world, i.e., paramapadam. emperumān rested here to facilitate the residents of paramapadam too to approach him. Another explanation – asaivu – changing posture from left side to right side. Seeing that, the world praised you and you remained accepting such praises.
- *kidandāy kāṇa vārāyē* – I enjoyed your beautiful reclining posture, and now please walk towards me to let me see your beautiful walking posture.
- *seḻu mā maṇigaḷ sērum tirukkudandai* – This is also explained as “tirukkudandai which is approached by puruśaratnams (gem among men) such as ārāvamudāḻvār ([emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) himself), [tirumaḻsaip pirān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/thirumazhisai-azhwar/) et al”.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.8.10. Vara aruvay

*vārā aruvāy varumen māyā māyā mūrttiyāy ārā amudāy adiyēn āvi agamē tittippāy tīrā vinaigaḷ tīra ennai āṇḍāy tirukkudandai ūrā unakkātpattum adiyēn innam uḻalvēnō*

**Пословный перевод:**

vārā – instead of walking towards us with your beautiful form to be seen by the eyes and enjoyed; aruvāy – without a \[physical\] form; varum – appearing inside me; en māyā – revealing your amazing qualities; māyā – free from decay and destruction; mūrttiyāy – having eternal auspicious form; ārā – unsatiated even after enjoying; amudāy – being enjoyable like nectar; adiyēn – me who am your servitor, my; āvi – the abode of my soul; agam – inside the heart; tittippāy – one who triggers great taste; tīrā – inexhaustible; vinaigaḷ – sins; tīra – to destroy; ennai – me; āṇḍāy – who accepted my service by speech; tirukkudandai – tirukkudandai; ūrāy – one who is having it as your distinguished abode and being present there; unakku – for you (who has such saulabhyam (easy accessibility) and saundaryam (beauty)); āḷ pattum – though being your servant; adiyēn – I who am existing exclusively for you and have no other refuge; innam – still, in future; uḻalvēnō – should I suffer with no interaction with you as desired?

**Перевод:**

**Instead of walking towards us with your  beautiful form to be seen by the eyes and enjoyed, you are appearing inside me without a \[physical\] form revealing your amazing qualities; \[on top of that\] you are also triggering great taste inside the heart of me who am your servitor, the heart which is the abode of my soul, with an eternal auspicious form which is free from decay and destruction; you accepted my service by speech to destroy my inexhaustible sins; oh one who is having tirukkudandai as your distinguished abode and being present there! Though being your servant, should I, who am existing exclusively for you and have no other refuge, still suffer with no interaction with you as desired?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the tenth pāsuram, āḻvār reached tirukkudandai thinking that all the sorrows will be removed and all his desires will be fulfilled; but that did not happen. So, he says “where else do I have to go and knock the doors?”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “You are present inside me and are greatly tasteful, but I am unable to see you physically; though you are present as the easily approachable arcāvatāram and I have surrendered to you, how long do I have to suffer in grief like this?”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. vārā aruvāy varumen māyā māyā mūrttiyāy ārā amudāy adiyēn āvi agamē tittippāy tīrā vinaigaḷ tīra ennai āṇḍāy tirukkudandai ūrā unakkātpattum adiyēn innam uḻalvēnō*

- *vārā aruvāy* – The formless lord \[that is, in the form that can not be perceived by our eyes\] who is not coming. [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is appearing in a form that is not perceivable by our eyes, but is not appearing for external/physical experience.
- *varum en māyā –* “*aruvāy”* should be recited with *“varum en māyā”* \[to indicate that he has come and made himself present internally as antarātmā which is not perceivable by our eyes\]. Oh amazing lord who is shining brightly in my heart to not let me forget and survive \[remembering [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) but not seeing is unsustainable for [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)\].
- *māyā mūrttiyāy* – One who is having eternal divine auspicious form. Every other entity’s (ātmā’s) body goes through different stages such as birth, death etc \[but emperumān’s forms do not go through such transformations\].
- *ārā amudāy* – Being infinitely enjoyable and hence cannot be forgotten by me.
- *adiyēn āvi agamē tittippāy* – You who have me as your belonging always and who manifested your enjoyable nature in my heart and let me enjoy that.
- *tīrā vinaigaḷ tīra ennai āṇḍāy* – Oh one who eliminated those sins which are impediments to enjoy you and which can only be exhausted either by experiencing their effects or by your mercy, and made me say “*adiyēn āvi agamē ttittippāy*“. Another explanation – You who eliminated my hurdles which are explained in [tiruvāimoḻi 4.6](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/02/thiruvaimozhi-4-6-thirpparai/) “*tīrppāraiyāmini*” etc as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 4.6.6](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/03/thiruvaimozhi-4-6-6-thaniyum-pozhudhillai/) “*piṇiyum oḻiginṟadillaip perugum iduvallāl*” (her disease is only worsening and she is not getting cured), and engaged me in your service.
- *tirukkudandai ūrāy* – You who descended to tirukkudandai to engage me in your service. Here it is highlighting the greatness of [arcāvatāram](http://ponnadi.blogspot.in/p/archavathara-anubhavam.html) in comparison to paratvam (his form in paramapadam), vyūham (his form in kśīrābdi) etc. While I have not come to you, you have come here and are resting for me. Have I surrendered to someone who does not even have a nattam (a town, as his belonging)? \[No – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) has tirukkudandai\].
- *unakku āḷ pattum* – Even after being captured by you who have descended to make the worldly people enjoy you.
- *adiyēn* – Whose belonging is suffering like this? \[I am your servant/belonging\].
- *innam uḻalvēnō* – I who have placed all my responsibilities at your divine feet and am considering that you would take care of those; how many divyadēśams should I go and knock at the door \[for your mercy\]?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.8.11. Ulalai enbil

*uḻalai enbin pēycci mulaiyūdu avaḷai uyir uṇḍān kaḻalgaḷ avaiyē śaraṇāgak koṇḍa kurugūrc catakōpan kuḻalin maliyac conna ōrāyirattuḷ ippattum maḻalai tīra vallār kāmar mānēy nōkkiyarkkē*

**Пословный перевод:**

uḻalai – resembling collection of wooden bars; enbu – having bones; pēycci – demoniac lady; mulaiyūdu – through her bosom; avaḷai – her; uyir uṇḍān – kriṣṇa sucked her life and eliminated the enemy/hurdle, his; avai – those which were revealed to āḻvār as means; kaḻalgaḷē – divine feet only; saraṇāga – means to fulfil the desire; koṇḍa – considered; kurugūr – leader of āḻvārtirunagari; satakōpan – nammāḻvār; kuḻalil – more than the flute which is the source for the sound and tune; maliya – having more sweetness; sonna – mercifully spoken; ōr – distinguished; āyirattuḷ – among the thousand pāsurams; ip pattum – this decad; maḻalai – their childishness, ignorance; tīra – to be rid of; vallār – those who can recite with the same emotion as āḻvār; mānēy – like a deer; nōkkiyarkku – those having eyes, i.e., divine celestial damsels who have beautiful moon like face; kāmar – will be cared by, while doing brahmālankāram \[when the liberated soul reaches paramapadam, many beautiful divine damsels will decorate the liberated soul before bringing that soul to bhagavān\]. This is also explained as – just as damsels would desire for their beloved, such devotees who recite this decad will be desired by śrīvaiṣṇavas

**Перевод:**

**kriṣṇa sucked the life through the bosom of the demoniac lady who had bones which resembled a collection of wooden bars and eliminated the enemy/hurdle; nammāḻvār, the leader of āḻvārtirunagari considered such kriṣṇa’s divine feet which were revealed to him as the only means to fulfil his desire; such āḻvār mercifully spoke this distinguished decad which is sweeter than the flute which is the source for the sound and tune, among the thousand pāsurams. Those who can recite this decad having been rid of their ignorance, with the same emotion as āḻvār, will be cared by those \[celestial damsels\] who are having eyes like that of deer, while doing brahmālankāram \[decorating the liberated soul\]. Also explained as – just as damsels would desire for their beloved, such devotees who recite this decad will be desired by śrīvaiṣṇavas.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the end, āḻvār says “those who learn this decad without any faults will be very enjoyable for śrīvaiṣṇavas just as a kāmuka (beloved boy) is desired by kāminis (beloved girls)”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. uḻalai enbin pēycci mulaiyūdu avaḷai uyir uṇḍān kaḻalgaḷ avaiyē śaraṇāgak koṇḍa kurugūrc catakōpan kuḻalin maliyac conna ōrāyirattuḷ ippattum maḻalai tīra vallār kāmar mānēy nōkkiyarkkē*

- *uḻalai enbil* … – kriṣṇa sucked through her bosom, the life of pūtanā who was having bones resembling wooden bars which were strung together.
- *kaḻalgaḷ avaiyē saraṇāgak koṇḍa* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) who firmly considered the divine feet of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who eliminated the enemies. avadāraṇam (“*avaiy****E***“) explains the divine feet as the only means for both iśta prāpti (fulfilling the desire) and aniśta nivrutti (elimination of unfavourables).
- *kaḻalgaḷ avaiyē saraṇāgak koṇḍa* – Whether the divine feet fulfil the desire or not, āḻvār will not give up on them.
- *kuḻalil maliya* – Even more than the music from the flute, will pierce the heart of those who hear it. There \[in kriṣṇa’s case\], it is said in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi “*marangaḷ ninṟum madudāraigaḷ pāyum*” (stream of honey will flow from the trees), but here \[in [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s case\] it is said in tiruvāimoḻi 6.5.9 “*marangaḷum irangum vagai*” (even the trees will pity); here the greatness of this decad is that it makes even us \[who are as hard-hearted as wood\] to melt. This distinguished decad among the thousand pāsurams.
- *maḻalai tīra vallār* – Those who are free of lethargy. That is, instead of remaining “if it comes, I will accept; but I won’t search for it myself”, those who can recite this decad with the same grief as [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/). His grief was as explained in [tiruvāimoḻi 5.8.5](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/08/thiruvaimozhi-5-8-5-azhuvan-thozhuvan/) “*aḻuvan toḻuvan ādik kāṇban*” (cry, worship, dance and see).
- *kāmar mānēy nōkkiyarkkē* – They will be like the dear beloved person for damsels who have the eyes resembling that of a deer’s. What does this mean? This is contradictory to what [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) himself said before in [tiruvāimoḻi 5.8.6](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/08/thiruvaimozhi-5-8-6-suzh-kanday/) “*tūrāk kuḻi tūṟṟu enai nāḷ aganṟiruppan*” (How long do I have to stay in this endless pit). So what does he imply? Just as one who is addicted to worldly pleasures will pursue that even after knowing “subsequently we will have to experience the results in hell”, those who learn this decad will be pursued as enjoyable entities by [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) and śrīvaiṣṇavas. If this is not the case, these will be a cheat’s words. āḻvār is a very bonafide person. So, the conclusion matches the context \[where emperumān descended to tirukkudandai for the sake of his devotees\]. But why is the word “*pōl*” (like) missing \[in the last line\]? That is because, this is of the style called “*muṟṟuvamai*” \[in tamiḻ grammar\], where the object which is explained through an example is cited as the example itself. āḻvār himself said in tiruvāimoḻi 6.9.9 “*tāvi vaiyam koṇḍa tadam tāmaraigatkē*” (for the broad lotus flowers which scaled and accepted the world) \[Here, lotus flowers directly imply the divine feet of emperumān\].

## 5.9 Maney nokku

## 5.9.1. Maney nokku

*mānēy nōkku nalleer! vaigalum vinaiyēn meliya vānār vaṇ kamugum madu malligai kamaḻum tēnār sōlaigaḷ sūḻ tiruvallavāḻ uṟaiyum kōnārai adiyēn adi kūduvadu enṟu kolō?*

**Пословный перевод:**

mān – deer’s eyes; ēy – matching; nōkku – having eyes; nalleer – those who are identified as well-wishers for me!; vinaiyēn – I who am having sin (which stops me from interacting with him as desired); vaigalum – always; meliya – to weaken me; vān – the sky; Ar – to cover; vaṇ – generous (to offer its own body as support to the jasmine creeper \[which is growing near it); kamugum – areca tree; madu – with flowing honey (due to being with the areca tree); malligai – jasmine \[creeper\]; kamaḻum – being fragrant; tēn – beetles which extract honey and the fragrant buds; Ar – filled with; sōlaigaḷ – gardens; sūḻ – surrounded; tiruvallavāḻ – in tiruvallavāḻ; uṟaiyum – eternally residing; kōnārai – unconditional lord; adiyēn – I who am a servitor (captivated by his supremacy); adi – his divine feet; kūduvadu – reach; enṟu kolō – when?

**Перевод:**

**Oh those who are identified as well-wishers for me and whose eyes match the eyes of deer! When will I, the servitor \[of emperumān\], who am sinful and am always weakened by emperumān who is eternally residing in tiruvallavāḻ which is surrounded by gardens which have the generous areca trees, fragrant jasmine \[creeper\] with flowing honey and are filled with beetles which extract honey and the fragrant buds, reach his divine feet? “vinaiyēn meliya” is recited with “vaṇ kamugu” \[indicating that the rich areca trees weaken her\] and “tiruvallavāḻ uṟaiyum” \[indicating that the emperumān who resides in tiruvallavāḻ weakens her\].**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the first pāsuram, this pirātti (parānguśa nāyaki) is grieving and her friends whose eyes resemble that of deer’s ask her “what are you thinking in your divine heart?”; she replies to them “When will I reach the divine feet of emperumān who is in tiruvallavāḻ?”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. mānēy nōkku nalleer! vaigalum vinaiyēn meliya vānār vaṇ kamugum madu malligai kamaḻum tēnār sōlaigaḷ sūḻ tiruvallavāḻ uṟaiyum kōnārai adiyēn adi kūduvadu enṟu kolō?*

- *mānēy nōkku nalleer* – piḷḷān explains this as – parānguśa nāyaki is requesting her friends to mercifully shower their cool glance to facilitate her reaching tiruvallavāḻ.
- *mānēy nōkku nalleer* – Oh those who have eyes matching those of a deer’s eyes and are well-wishers for me. Her friends thought “she is suffering due to separation, engaged in the beauty of the gardens and is weakened due to our advice; if she hears our words which stop her from her pursuit, she will become unconscious” and manifested their emotions with their eyes which resemble a deer’s eyes, and so she is calling them “*mānēy nōkku nalleer*“. For her, all it takes is to be as said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 9.1](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/9-1/) “*anasūyavē*” (not having hatred). “*idam tu tē guhya tamam pravakśyāmi*” (I shall explain to you this most secretive knowledge about upāsana (practicing bhakti yōga)) – I am explaining you this precious wealth \[of knowledge\]. Once there is no shortcoming in arjuna, will there be any limiting factor in kriṣṇa?
- *vaigalum vinaiyēn meliya* – Only those who can sustain after becoming weakened once on separation, can tolerate separation \[she is always weakened\].
- *vaigalum meliya* – For those who are interested in worldly pleasures, as time goes by, they lose interest in their object of interest; but this \[āḻvār’s love towards bhagavān\] is first meditated upon, followed by deep contemplation, and then vision, and then vision which matches physical experience and finally wait for the shedding of the body \[for the soul to reach bhagavān permanently\]. \[cāndōjña upaniśat ślōkam is highlighted here\] *tasya* (*mē*) – for (that person who is) me; this (*tasya*) should be read along with “*ata sampatsyē”*; *tāvadēva ciram* – the delay \[to reach bhagavān\] is only until that time \[when he sheds his body\]; *yāvanna mōkśē atasampatsyē* – subsequently I will become perfect (in liberated state). That is, as said in cāndōjña upaniśat “… *paramjyōti: upasampatya …*” (he reaches paramātmā and realises his true nature). This is the nature of those who are waiting to shed their bodies.
- *vaigalum vinaiyēn meliya* – I who am greatly sinful to be separated from emperumān, am very weak due to the suffering in separation constantly. She is so tender that she cannot even bear the weakening one day! Now she is suffering for many days. She is going through the same suffering as sītāp pirātti went through after tiruvadi (hanuman) met her and left \[to inform śrī rāma\]. tiruvadi could not bear witnessing her suffering for one night. śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 16.28 chapter – *imāmasitakēśāntām* – She has got beautiful hair which can be desired even by those who have hair as said in tiruneduntāṇḍagam 21 “*mai vaiṇṇa naṟungunji*” (dark and fragrant hair); *śatapatra nibhēkśaṇam* – one who is having dark eyes which deserve to be constantly seen by śrī rāma who is explained as “*kamalapatrākśa:*” (one who has lotus-petal like eyes); *sukārhām* – deserves to rest on the comfortable lap of emperumān; *du:khitām druśtvā* – having seen her in an undeserving state; *mamāpi vyatitammana:* – even my heart which is undisturbed by sorrow/joy became grieved. parānguśa nāyaki is also in the same state.
- *vinaiyēn* – I have committed such a sin that even after many days passing  by, my desire \[for emperumān\] is not reducing.
- *meliya* – Melting like ice.
- *vānār* … – As she was becoming weakened the other side grew proportionately. It appears that her weakening is the water (that nourishes) the garden there.
- *vānār* … – The areca trees are such that they cover the sky. Her abode is as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 59.4 “*apivrukśā: parivlānā:*” (the trees withered), and his abode is as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 127.17 “*akāla palinō vrukśā:*” (let the trees blossom even during non-season).
- *vaṇ kamugum* – attractive. As said in periya tirumoḻi 6.9.8 “*kulaiyārnda paḻukkāyum pasungāyum pāḷaimuttum talaiyārnda iḷangamugu*” (The areca trees with well ripened fruits, fruits which will ripe soon etc).
- *vaṇ kamugu* – Instead of the creeper having to reach out to the tree, the tree itself is leaning towards the creeper to facilitate spreading on it – such generosity. This is true generosity; also explained as generosity of giving one’s own body.
- *madu malligai kamaḻum* – Not a barren creeper! Due to embracing the areca tree, it is with vastness and flowers. The fragrance of the jasmine flowers which are having honey, reaches up to her abode and hits her.
- *tēnār sōlaigaḷ sūḻ* – Whatever explained previously are places but the town itself is filled with honey. The areca trees were tossed up and down in flood of honey, and suffered as mārkaṇḍēya riśi was tossed around during the deluge. The lord of tiruvallavāḻ who is residing in tiruvallavāḻ which is surrounded by the gardens which are flooded with honey. While both emperumān and I should together enjoy drinking the honey, I am suffering here while he is enjoying there. Alas! Should he not say that he won’t drink the honey as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 36.42 “*na cāpi madu sēvatē*” (he is not even drinking honey). The reason for āḻvār’s singing praises of the gardens even while suffering is due to the enjoyable nature of emperumān who is residing in the temple and the gardens etc. Just as emperumān who is the target of meditation, will present himself for those who \[are attached to him yet\] cannot meditate upon him, these \[beautiful aspects of tiruvallavāḻ\] too present themselves to parānguśa nāyaki. This is similar to emperumān who is the goal, also assumes the state of being the means. emperumān who is the eternal goal and is residing in paramapadam, assumes a divine form which is desired by his devotees and presenting himself for them, the residents of paramapadam too follow him, descend to these divyadēśams and assume immovable \[plants, assembly halls etc\], movable \[vāhanams etc\] and animal \[cow, elephant etc which serve emperumān in temples\] forms and remain close to him. nityasūris (eternal residents of paramapadam), muktātmās (liberated souls) and those baddātmās (bound souls) who have the devotion towards emperumān – all of these devotees are greatly attached to ugandaruḷina nilangaḷ (divyadēśams); in śrī rāmāvatāram lakśmaṇa et al (nityasūris), vānaras (dēvas, celestial beings assumed the forms of monkeys etc) and vibhīśaṇa et al (mumukśus, those bound souls who were desirous of mōkśam) were surrendered to śrī rāma. \[Why would anyone be born as stāvara (immovable plants)?\] for human and animal forms there is possibility of leaving the divyadēśam, but for plants, there is no such scope. When jananāta brahmarāyar was planning to cut a tree in śrīrangam, embār heard about that and told him “Oh lord (in a sarcastic way)! Are you trying to destroy bhagavān’s wealth?”; jananāta brahmarāyar enquired embār with curiosity “Is there any place which is not owned by bhagavān?” and embār mercifully explained “This place is unlike other places; just as an emperor and empress would maintain their own personal garden by watering the plants etc themselves, this place is personally created by periya perumāḷ and periya pirātti”. For those who have true faith in divyadēśams everything present there will be enjoyable. This samsāram (material realm) where one could not stand for even a moment, became enjoyable in one sense when it is considered as his wealth. When something is perceivable (through the senses), it is more believable, unlike the belief in pramāṇam (śāstram, authentic texts).  For āḻvār, like muktātmās, bhagavān’s ownership of everything is perceivable as he is seeing through his own eyes. For a bonafide person, unless it is in pramāṇam (śāstram), he will not believe it. \[An incident is cited to explain this\] nallān, a disciple of bhattar, was devoted to bhattar for a long time. During his last moments, bhattar mercifully arrived at his place and asked him “What are you thinking?”. nallān replied “I was thinking – when sarvaśakti (omnipotent emperumān) favours, he will greatly favour like this”. bhattar asked “Oh! You are away from your native town, your relatives etc. And you are going to reach emperumān’s divine feet after suffering like this. What is the favour in this?”. nallān replied “Being in a different place, I would have died as an unknown person. But he brought me over here to śrīrangam, made me take refuge at your divine feet, instigated my love towards him and made me shed my body in this divine abode in your presence \[what more is required?\]”. bhattar asked “Still, how could you think like this when the body which was considered as self is dying?”. nallān replied “I am thinking this based on pramāṇam”. For those who have pristine knowledge without any shortcoming, this is how they will think.
- *tēnār sōlaigaḷ sūḻ tiruvallavāḻ uṟaiyum kōnārai* – He is on his own, where he should enjoy with me too.
- *uṟaiyum* – Unlike \[vibhava\] avatārams \[like śrī rāma, kriṣṇa et al\], here \[in arcāvatāram\] he is not leaving.
- *kōnārai adiyēn* – \[Explains this as tirumantram\] As in the word “nārāyaṇa” and in praṇavam, it is not possible to explain emperumān without highlighting self; self cannot be explained without highlighting emperumān. kōnārai indicates the meaning of nārāyaṇa, adiyēn indicates praṇavam. praṇavam is focussed on jīvātmā \[where it says jīvātmā is exclusively existing for bhagavān, and it is an instruction for the jīvātmā\] and nārāyaṇa is focussed on īśvara (bhagavān) \[where it says emperumān is the abode of everything and emperumān is present in everything\]. “*adikūduvadu enṟu kolō*” reveals the meaning of caturti \[hidden “*āya*” in praṇavam\]; “*enṟu kolō*” indicates prārtanā \[prayer to emperumān for accepting our service, which is indicated in *nama:*\].
- *kōnārai adiyēn* – The lord is courageous \[kōn – leader\]; she is lacking in courage \[adiyēn – weak\].
- *adiyēn adi kūduvadu enṟu kolō* – Matching the nature \[of the soul\], it \[the pāsuram\] is ending with vibhakti \[*nārāyaṇāya*\]. Whatever state āḻvār may be in, his nature will not be lost. Whether he is singing as himself, or in the mood of a pirātti or any other mood beyond that, at all times, his true nature \[of being a servitor, who is attached to emperumān’s divine feet\] will not change; even if mrut (clay soil) takes the form of a block, pot or a container, it will still remain soil and that is never lost. In his own state, he will say as in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.1.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/03/thiruvaimozhi-1-1-1-uyarvara-uyarnalam/) “*adi toḻudu eḻu*” (worship the divine feet and be uplifted); while instructing others he will say as in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.2.10](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/05/thiruvaimozhi-1-2-10-en-perukku/) “*tiṇ kaḻal sēr*” (reach the firm divine feet); while sending messages he will say as in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.4.2](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/07/thiruvaimozhi-1-4-2-enseyya-thamaraikkan/) “*tiruvadik kīḻ kuṟṟēval*” (serving at the divine feet); while speaking about some one else, he will say as in [tiruvāimoḻi 2.1.2](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/11/thiruvaimozhi-2-1-2-kotpatta-sinthaiyaiyay/) “*tāḷ patta taṇḍhuḻāyt tāmam kāmuṟṟāyē*” (You desired for the tuḷasi garland which decorated emperumān’s divine feet); even while becoming bewildered and engaging in madal he will say as in [tiruvāimoḻi 5.3.7](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/06/thiruvaimozhi-5-3-7-valaiyul-agappaduththu/) “*talaiyil vaṇangavumāngolō*” (can we bow by our head?); while in a mad state of love for him, he will say as in [tiruvāimoḻi 4.4.8](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/02/thiruvaimozhi-4-4-8-thiruvudai-mannarai/) “*kaṇṇan kaḻalgaḷ virumbumē*” (will desire kriṣṇa’s divine feet) and as in [tiruvāimoḻi 4.4.7](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/02/thiruvaimozhi-4-4-7-eriya-piththinodu/) “*ēṟiya pittinōdu ellā ulagum kaṇṇan padiaippu*” (being maddened she will say everything is kriṣṇa’s creation).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.9.2. Enrukol

*enṟu kol tōḻimīrgāḷ! emmai nīr nalinden seydīrō? pon tigaḻ punnai magiḻ pudu mādavi mīdaṇavit tenṟal maṇam kamaḻum tiruvallavāḻ nagaruḷ ninṟa pirān adi nīṟ adiyōm koṇḍu sūduvadē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tōḻimīrgāḷ – Oh friends (who share my joy and grief)!; emmai – me (who am considering you all as companions for my desires); nalindu – torture (by stopping me from my pursuit); nīr – you all; en – what actions; seydīr – performing; pon – like gold; tigaḻ – shining pollen; punnai – punnai (a type of tree); magiḻ – magiḻ (a type of tree); pudu – fresh; mādavi – kurukkatti (a type of tree); mīdu – with their flowers on them; aṇavi – embracing; tenṟal – southerly breeze; maṇam – fragrance; kamaḻum – spreading; tiruvallavāḻ – tiruvallavāḻ; nagaruḷ – in the town of; ninṟa – standing \[residing\]; pirān – benefactor’s; adi nīṟu – dust of the divine feet; adiyōm – we, the servitors who benefit out of his favour of being present here; koṇḍu – accepting as a servitor would do; sūduvadu – holding on our head with reverence; enṟu kol – when?

**Перевод:**

**Oh friends! what are the actions you are all performing to torture me! When will we, the servitors who benefit out of his favour of being present here, be holding on our head with reverence the dust of the divine feet of the benefactor who is standing in the town of tiruvallavāḻ where the southerly breeze is embracing the flowers which are present on punnai, magiḻ and kurukkatti trees which have pollen shining like gold?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the second pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki tries to convince her friends who are not agreeing with her efforts and asks them “when will I enter tiruvallavāḻ and wear the dust of his divine feet?”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. enṟu kol tōḻimīrgāḷ! emmai nīr nalinden seydīrō? pon tigaḻ punnai magiḻ pudu mādavi mīdaṇavit tenṟal maṇam kamaḻum tiruvallavāḻ nagaruḷ ninṟa pirān adi nīṟ adiyōm koṇḍu sūduvadē*

- *enṟu kol tōḻimīrgāḷ* – [parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is asking those same friends who are stopping her saying “you should not have extreme attachment \[towards [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)\]”, to tell her the date on which she will have her desires fulfilled. They are stopping her fearing how people might accuse her; but she considers them to be the recipient of the same benefit and is hence asking them. They are tōḻimār (friends) – so they share her gain and loss.
- *tōḻimīrgāḷ* – Don’t you have the right to investigate when my desires will be fulfilled?
- *tōḻimīrgāḷ* – Don’t you who know my nature, have to follow me?
- *emmai* – Me who am beaten by your hands and feet.
- *nīr nalindu* – Your routine is to constantly look out for my uplifting. I who cannot sustain myself unless I enter that town \[of tiruvallavāḻ\]. And you who have always done what pleased me.
- *en seydīrō* – does this suit your nature? Does it suit my nature?
- *tōḻimīrgāḷ emmai nīr nalindu en seydīrō* – If you really want to torment some one, you should be tormenting the southerly breeze \[and not me\]. How can I withdraw myself while they \[the beautiful town, gardens etc\] stop me from withdrawing.
- *pon tigaḻ …* – Are they \[the different flower bearing trees\] not sufficient to torment me? How can you who are tender-hearted do what is done by hard-hearted persons?
- *pon tigaḻ punnai magiḻ* – punnai trees which shine like gold, and the same with magiḻ trees, as said in periya tirumoḻi 5.1.6 “*punnai ponnēy tādudirkkum*” (punnai trees shedding pollen which resemble gold).
- *pudu mādavi* – Freshly blossomed kurukkatti.
- *mīdaṇavit tenṟal maṇam kamaḻum* – The southerly breeze embracing them and bringing along the fragrance.
- *mīdaṇavi* – Considering that if it gets in contact with the deep insides of the flower the heat will get transmitted as well, the southerly breeze simply touched the top part of the flower and carried the fragrance. As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam kiśkintā kāṇḍam 1.71 “*padmakēsāsamsruśta:*” (along with the pollen in the lotus flower), without touching the flower just carrying its fragrance. It appears to be the nature of the entities of that abode, to grab the belongings of others and not giving their own belongings.
- *pon tigaḻ punnai magiḻ pudu mādavi mīdaṇavit tenṟal maṇam kamaḻum –* The nature of tender persons is such that they will not wear anything but kalambagan (a garland strung with many different flowers). Just as prideful princes would reject women with sagjñ bosoms, breeze will discard those flowers which blossomed later. Just as some one would search for pollen in the flower, here flowers are searched amidst the fragrance.
- *tenṟal maṇam kamaḻum* – Since the breeze is tormenting parānguśa nāyaki while without being visible to the eyes, her friend is not admitting that the breeze is tormenting her. Though the gain and loss are the same for her and her friend, since her friend has well-wishing thoughts for her, she is not realising the act of the breeze in tormenting parānguśa nāyaki. parānguśa nāyaki is thinking “even if you are not with me during my togetherness with emperumān, at least could you not be with me in separation?”. Though the gain and loss are common for both her and her friends, these sufferings are only applicable for parānguśa nāyaki.
- *pon tigaḻ punnai magiḻ enṟu* – It is attractive for the eyes.
- *tenṟal maṇam kamaḻum* – Feast for the senses of touch and smell.
- *tiruvallavāḻ nagaruḷ ninṟa pirān* – He does not reject us totally. When I am suffering in separation, instead of remaining in śrīvaikuṇatam (paramapadam), he has descended to tiruvallavāḻ and has remained close to me – what more favour can he do? As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 5.10 “*bahuvētat*” (śrī rāma says – this is great that sītā and I exist on this earth at the same time, this will help me sustain myself), here too [parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) feels pacified knowing about [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s existence in tiruvallavāḻ. *ēkām daraṇim āśritau* – resting on the same earth. As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 5.6 “*vāhi vāta*” (Oh wind! flow), though they were separated by the ocean stopping him from touching her, he felt pacified saying that he was fortunate to be present on the earth where she was present. His anguish in separation was so much that he begged the wind to fulfil his desire \[of bringing the fragrance from sītāp pirātti’s side\].
- *ninṟa pirān adi nīṟu adiyōm koṇḍu sūduvadu – enṟu kol* – When will I get to wear the pollen of the flowers from the divine feet of emperumān?
- *adi nīṟu adiyōm koṇḍu sūduvadu – enṟu kolō* – Like those who washed their hair and are waiting to wear the flowers on their hair.
- *adiyōm* – \[[parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying adiyēn in plural, to include her friends too\] Though they are staying separate from her now, while enjoying [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), they too will share that enjoyment. Even when he arrives, he will first glorify them before her.
- *adiyōm koṇḍu sūduvadu* – As said by śrī bharatāḻvān in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 98.8 “*yāvannacaraṇau …*” (I will not be at peace until I hold the divine feet of [śrī rāma](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) on my head), śrī rāma asked śrī bharatāḻvān “piḷḷāy (dear brother), when will your internal anguish be cured?”; śrī bharatāḻvān replied “when perumāḷ (you, śrī rāma) are coronated with the apt crown \[of the kingdom\] for him and when I am coronated with the apt crown (divine feet of śrī rāma) and when both are acting according to our nature, I will be relieved from the anguish”. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is of the nature as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 4.3.6](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/01/thiruvaimozhi-4-3-6-kala-chakkaraththodu/) “*kōlamām en sennikku un kamalam anna kurai kaḻal*” (Your lotus-like divine feet is the decoration for my head).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.9.3. Sudu malark kulaleer

*sūdu malark kuḻaleer! tuyarāttiyēnai meliyap pādu nal vēda oli paravait tirai pōl muḻanga māduyarndōmap pugai kamaḻum taṇ tiruvallavāḻ nīduṟaiginṟa pirān kaḻal kāṇḍungol niccalumē?*

**Пословный перевод:**

sūdu – worn; malar – having flower; kuḻaleer – oh those who are having hair!; tuyarāttiyēnai – me who is suffering in separation; meliya – to weaken; pādu – being sung; nal – noble (as said in “sāmavēdōsmi“, similar to the divine form for sarvēśvavan who is residing there); vēda oli – the sound of the sāma vēdam chanting; paravai – the ocean’s; tirai pōl – like the rising of the tides; muḻanga – tumultous; mādu – in the close vicinity; uyarndu – rising from the yāgam (sacrificial fire); ōmap pugai – the smoke from the hōmam (sacrificial altar); kamaḻum – spreading the fragrance of the sacrificial offerings; taṇ – invigorating; tiruvallavāḻ – in tiruvallavāḻ; nīduṟaiginṟa – eternally residing; pirān – great benefactor; kaḻal – divine feet; niccalum kāṇḍum kol – will I be able to eternally enjoy?

**Перевод:**

**Oh those who are having hair which is decorated with flowers! In tiruvallavāḻ the tumultous sound of the noble sāma vēdam is heard like the sound of rising tides in the ocean and in the close vicinity, the smoke from the hōmam in the yāgam is spreading the fragrance of the sacrificial offerings, both of which are occurring to weaken me; will I be able to eternally enjoy the divine feet of the great benefactor who is eternally residing in such invigorating tiruvallavāḻ?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the third pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki asks her friends “When will I see the divine feet of emperumān who is mercifully standing in tiruvallavāḻ?”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, parānguśa nāyaki asks “Will I be able to eternally enjoy the divine feet of emperumān who is doing the eternal favour of permanently residing in tiruvallavāḻ where the chants of vēdam and vaidika activities are conducted constantly?”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Third pāsuram. parānguśa nāyaki asks her friends “When will we get to enjoy him eternally?”. sūdu malark kuḻaleer! tuyarāttiyēnai meliyap pādu nal vēda oli paravait tirai pōl muḻanga māduyarndōmap pugai kamaḻum taṇ tiruvallavāḻ nīduṟaiginṟa pirān kaḻal kāṇḍungol niccalumē?*

- *sūdu malark kuḻaleer* – [piḷḷān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/pillan/) explains this as \[[parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) asking her friends\] “When will I see you all with your hair decorated with flowers?”. That is, when she is longing for the flowers, they would not be wearing flowers \[so it should be seen as something in future\]. Alternative explanation – since [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) celebrates his relationship with her by celebrating with her friends, they would be retaining those flowers which were given by him long ago \[when emperumān and parānguśa nāyaki were together\] even though they have lost their freshness. This is similar to those śrīvaiṣṇavas who would fold their lower/upper garments (doties and angavastrams) which were worn during periya tirunāḷ (adyayana utsavam) and hang them on the cloth liner without washing them even if they were dirty and cherish them for a long time; seeing those flowers, she became tormented being reminded with his memories. Even if she escapes the torture of the southerly breeze, she cannot escape the torture of this sight. She is being tormented by the breeze on one side and the hair on the other side. Even if he comes, he desires for those who are dear to her more than desiring for her. śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 16.3. *tatra kāśāyina:* – since they don’t care for themselves, they remain with dirty body and clothes. *vruttān* – In the anta:puram (private quarters), those who are older than ninety five years and are free from likes/dislikes will be employed. *vētra pāṇīn* – Just as perumāḷ (śrī rāma) is holding the bow, they are holding the stick. See the one who guards using his bow and the others who guard using their stick. *svalankrutān* – If they are not caring for their own clothes and are elderly, what is their decoration? perumāḷ goes to the palace of daśarata to bathe and eat and will return to the private quarters. At that time, since these elderly guards are as old as daśarata and have same affection towards perumāḷ, they will place him on their laps and affectionately smell his head; due to that their clothes will always be stained with the saffron paste and sandalwood paste which were applied on perumāḷ. Their decoration is unlike the \[fresh\] decoration of perumāḷ and pirātti. In this manner, they \[her friends\] remain as said in “*sūdu malark kuḻaleer*“.
- *tuyarāttiyēnai meliyap pādu nal vēda oli* – The brāhmaṇas are not doing these yāgams for any purpose other than to cause anguish to me. If they are brāmhaṇas, should they not be righteous? Why are they torturing the women?
- *tuyarāttiyēnai* – For those who torture others, don’t they need some target? Is the breeze not sufficient to torture \[me\]?  When tiruvadi (hanuman) met sītāp pirātti in the middle of the night and spoke a few words to her, without realizing who he is \[and assuming that it was rāvaṇa who has come as a monkey\], she said “previously you assumed the form of an ascetic and separated me from śrī rāma; now you are torturing me by assuming the form of a monkey and tormenting me with your words; this is not good for you”. śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 34.15 and 34.16. “*santāpam tanna śōbhanam*” (it is not fair to torment me) – Come on! you will also suffer in separation from those who are dear to you.
- *meliyap pādum* – Even if it is kartavyam (ordained duty \[for brāhmaṇas to engage in yāgam etc\]), should they not avoid it if it hurts others? In all the states \[whether singing as self, or with the mood of a pirātti\] [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) has the same attachment for vēdam. Right in the beginning he said in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.1.7](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/04/thiruvaimozhi-1-1-7-thidavisumbu-erivali/) “*uḷan sudarmigu surudiyuḷ*” ([bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is present in the radiant vēdam). That is \[irrespective of karma kāṇḍam (vēdam) or jñāna kāṇḍam (vēdāntam), everywhere only [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is mentioned\] – “*sarvē vēda yat padamāmananti*” (the one whose nature is spoken about in all of vēdam), “*sarvē vēda yatraikam bhavanti*” (the one on whom all the vēdam is singularly focussed upon), śrī bhagavat gītā 15.15 “*vēdaiśca sarvair ahamēva vēdya:*” (I am known from all of vēdam).
- *meliyap pādum* – \[The present tense in pādum is explained\] Unless they \[the students\] complete their studies, they wont leave their gurukulam (traditional resident school) \[so the chanting is going on\]; for her, when she hears the loud chants of vēdam, it is undesirable since it speaks about the glories of her lord. When this should be heard in their togetherness, hearing them when being in separation is undesirable. Even if he is glorified, the epic is glorified as “*sītāyām caritam mahat*” (this \[śrī rāmāyaṇam\] is the glorious history of sītā). And he joyfully hears those passages of vēdam which glorify her as in puruśa sūktam “*hrīścatē lakśmīśca patnyau*” (he is having śrī mahālakśmi and śrī bhūmi dēvi as his consorts), śrī sūktam “*īśvarīm sarvabhūtānām*” (she is the lord of all creatures) and yajur vēdam 4.4.37 “*asyēśānājagatō viṣṇu patnī*” (she is the lord of the universe and the consort of viṣṇu).
- *nal vēdam* – As said in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.1.7](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/04/thiruvaimozhi-1-1-7-thidavisumbu-erivali/) “*uḷan* ***sudarmigu*** *surudiyuḷ*” (bhagavān is present in the radiant vēdam), the greatness of vēdam over other pramāṇams (authentic texts); or it is the greatness explained in śrī bhagavat gītā 10.22 “*vēdānām sāma vēdōsmi*” (I am sāma vēdam amongst the four vēdams). Unless the svaram (tone) is not good, or not singing sāma vēdam which is sweetest, she may remain relaxed.
- *vēda oli paravait tirai pōl muḻanga* – The loud chant of the sāma vēdam resembles the tumultous sound of rising tides.
- *muḻanga* – On days other than amāvāsyai, paurṇami etc or in the morning, she can remain relaxed \[that is, on the days of amāvāsyai, paurṇami etc and in the nights the tides will be louder\].
- *mādu uyarndu ōmap pugai kamaḻum* – Where there is no loud chants of vēdam, they will be engaged in vaidika rituals.
- *uyarndu ōmap pugai kamaḻum* – The smoke rose up to the sky, filling it and made it difficult to enjoy the faces of those travelling in celestial vehicles in the sky.
- *uyarndu ōmap pugai kamaḻum* – These persons are the best among those who have knowledge in vaidika principles as said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 3.20](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/3-20/) “*karmaṇaiva hi samsiddim āstitā janakādaya:”* (Have janaka et al not attained the result of self-realization through karma yōga (and not jñāna yōga) only?); so, they will not practice these acts to attain a result and will stop on attaining the result \[present tense in kamaḻum is explained\].
- *kamaḻum* – The fragrance of the smoke from the hōmam and the sandalwood paste which is applied by [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who has arrived to accept the havis (sacrifice).
- *tiruvallavāḻ nīduṟaiginṟa pirān* – Unlike incarnations where emperumān returns to paramapadam after a while, arcāvatāra emperumān who is the benefactor eternally residing in the invigorating tiruvallavāḻ.
- *kaḻal kāṇḍum kol niccalumē* – If he is eternally residing here, we too can attain the same result \[right here in tiruvallavāḻ\] which is attained in paramapadam where he is eternally residing. There too, the result is explained as in viṣṇu sūktam “*sadā paśyanti*” (always seeing him).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.9.4. Niccalum tolimirgal

*niccalum tōḻimīrgāḷ emmai nīr nalinden seydīrō paccilai nīḷ kamugum palavum tengum vāḻaigaḷum maccaṇi mādangaḷ mīdaṇavum taṇ tiruvallavāḻ naccaravinaṇai mēl nampirānadu nannalamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tōḻimīrgāḷ – Oh friends (who always care for my likes)!; emmai – us (who have not fulfilled your desire); nīr – you; niccalum – always; nalindu – stopping me and torturing me; en – what actions; seydīr – are you doing?; pasu – green; ilai – having leaves; nīḷ – tall; kamugum – areca tree; paccilai nīḷ – similar; palavum – jack fruit tree; tengum – coconut tree; vāḻaigaḷum – plantain trees; maccu – upper storeys; aṇi – being complete; mādangaḷ – on the mansions; mīdu – on top of; aṇavum – spread (giving shade for those lands); taṇ – cool; tiruvallavāḻ – in tiruvallavāḻ; nanju – spitting poison (to stop the non-devotees); aravin aṇai mēl – reclining on the divine serpent bed; nam – revealed for us; pirānadu – the great benefactor’s; nal – abundance; nalam – goodness

**Перевод:**

**Oh friends! What actions are you doing by always stopping me and torturing me? My abundant goodness (also explained as, good ātmā) belongs to emperumān who manifested to me his reclining on the divine serpent bed which is splitting poison in cool tiruvallavāḻ which has tall areca trees with green leaves, jack fruit trees, coconut trees, plantain trees which are spread over mansions which are complete with upper storeys.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the 4th pāsuram, to her friends who stop her saying “desiring like this is not good”, parānguśa nāyaki says “my ātmā is with him, your blabbering is useless”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, parānguśa nāyaki says “While I am affectionate towards emperumān who is the benefactor for being with his eternal devotees in tiruvallavāḻ which has gardens and mansions, what is the use of your tormenting?”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. niccalum tōḻimīrgāḷ emmai nīr nalinden seydīrō paccilai nīḷ kamugum palavum tengum vāḻaigaḷum maccaṇi mādangaḷ mīdaṇavum taṇ tiruvallavāḻ naccaravinaṇai mēl nampirānadu nannalamē*

- *niccalum tōḻimīrgāḷ* – The friends would repeatedly say “you are not supposed to be like this”, still will have no result; but considering that they cannot lose her, they started saying the same thing again; [parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) said “if you are not going to stop tormenting me, please go and torment me where I am”. As my ātmā belongs to him, what is the use of your advice to me? Just as I have the desire to see him always, you have this desire to redeem me.
- *tōḻimīrgāḷ* – Are you speaking as yourself or are you speaking as mothers \[usually mothers advice their daughters to restrain them from reaching out to their beloved ones\]? There are such people who don’t have knowledge about their own nature. When some people tell something they should know who they are first.
- *emmai nīr* – You who will think about my well being even at the cost of your own loss, and me who cannot survive on hearing your advice.
- *nalindu en seydīrō* – Will I survive! Would that match your nature!
- *niccalum tōḻimīr …* – [piḷḷān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/pillan/) would explain “What did you gain by advising me from tiruvāimoḻi 5.3 ‘*māśaṟu sōdi*‘ up until now?”.
- *tōḻimīrgāḷ emmai nīr nalindu en seydīrō* – These friends would care for her even at their own expense, would they torment others?
- *en seydīrō* – An act is done for a particular result. Once the gain/loss is understood, should you not withdraw from your actions?
- *emmai nīr nalindu en seydīrō* – Should those who instigated the love initially \[in me\], not work for the result too?
- *paccilai …* – Would any one try to redeem me who is caught in [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s abode? Those who give advice should only do it where everything is green \[happy\]. Here everything is pale \[due to sorrow in separation\]. For those who have not separated, they will have their fresh \[natural\] colour \[Since the trees are present in the abode where emperumān is present, they are green\].
- *palavum* – Jack fruit tree. [nanjīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nanjiyar/) would mercifully explain “as said in ‘*nīḷ kamugum’,* uynda piḷḷai would add the adjective ‘*paccilai nīḷ*‘ (with fresh leaves and tall) to palavu, tengu and vāḻaigaḷ too”.
- *maccu aṇi mādangaḷ* – Mansions which appear well decorated due to having multiple storeys.
- *mīdu aṇavum* – As pampered children would have umbrella protection, these mansions have tall trees as protection.
- *taṇ tiruvallavāḻ* – The town which is invigorating due to having gardens. In cool tiruvallavāḻ where the complete multi-storeyed mansions are protected by the shades of the tall areca trees, jack fruit trees, coconut trees and plantain trees.
- *naccu aravin aṇai mēl* – As there are gardens above and in the surroundings, is it necessary to have them underneath too? \[Already, ādiśēśan is present as the mattress\] Here too, there is no shortcoming in coolness, fragrance and tenderness.
- *naccu aravu* – He is both the mattress and the protector \[as he spits poison on seeing the enemies\]. For the beautiful gardens, \[this is\] the town where bhōgis (those who are of enjoying nature, one who is lying on serpent) can reside constantly.
- *naccu aravu* – Just as perumāḷ (śrī rāma) and pirātti (sītā) enjoyed in the forest while iḷaiya perumāḷ (lakśmaṇa) protected them with the bow in his hands, here too he is protecting them as said in samkśēpa rāmāyaṇam “*ramamāṇā vanē traya:*“. This is multi-faceted protection \[since ādiśēśan has thousand hoods\]. When perumāḷ, iḷaiya perumāḷ and pirātti mercifully arrived at srungibhērapuram, śrī guhap perumāḷ told iḷaiya perumāḷ “perumāḷ and pirātti are resting; I have prepared a bed for you so that you can place your head at their divine feet; since we are forest dwellers and roaming around, we will not be able to sleep; since you are a prince, you are tender; don’t fear that bharata et al may come; you can rest peacefully; I am present along with my soldiers \[for your protection\]”; iḷaiya perumāḷ replied to him as in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 51.9 “*katā dāsaratau bhūmau śayānē sahasītayā*” (how can I rest, when śrī rāma is resting along with sītā on the ground?) – Come on! How can I sleep when the tender śrī rāma who was begot by emperor daśarata after sixty thousand years is resting on the ground? He had not even stayed under sage vaśiśta et al (those who were his teachers) \[due to his being the prince\], and that too he is resting there along with pirātti; this being the case, I am not consciously avoiding sleep; I am unable to do so \[due to being so heart-broken\]. \[All of these are explained to highlight how ādiśēśan constantly protects [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)\]
- *nam pirānadu nannalamē* – If it is as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 15.52 “*asyātēvyāmanas tasmin tasyacāsyāmpratiśtitam*” (the mind of sītā is with śrī rāma and śrī rāma’s mind is with sītā), will I not be relaxed? How can I be relaxed when my mind and ātmā both are with him?
- *nam pirānadu nannalamē* – My good self reached the emperumān who made me exclusively exist for him by showing his beautiful reclining form on ādiśēśan. It can also be said as – he made me exist exclusively for him as ādiśēśan is. When my good self is there with him, what is the point in giving advice just to my body? If you want, go to him and give your advice.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.9.5. Nannalat tolimirgal

*nannalat tōḻimīrgāḷ! nalla andaṇar vēḷvip pugai mainnalam koṇḍuyar viṇ maṟaikkum taṇ tiruvallavāḻ kannalam katti tannaik kaniyai in amudam tannai en nalam koḷ sudarai enṟu kol kaṇgaḷ kāṇbaduvē*

**Пословный перевод:**

nannalam – more caring towards me than myself; tōḻimīrgāḷ – Oh friends!; nalla – being exclusively devoted without any expectations and greatly attached \[to emperumān\]; andaṇar – vaidika (follower of vēdam); vēḷvi – karmas (rituals) such as agnihōtram etc which are part of vorśipping bhagavān; pugai – smoke; mai – dark pigment; nalam – good colour; koṇḍu – taking; uyar – rise; viṇ – sky; maṟaikkum – covers and makes it appear dark, providing shade; taṇ – cool; tiruvallavāḻ – residing in tiruvallavāḻ; kannal – sugarcane; am – without pulp; katti tannai – like a block \[of sugar\] which is sweet inside and outside; kaniyai – sweet like a ripened fruit which is to be enjoyed immediately; in – on top of that sweetness; amudam tannai – being the nectar which gives back the lost life; en – my; nalam – qualities of ātmā (self) and rūpam (form); koḷ – consumed \[enjoyed\]; sudarai – one who is having a form which acquired radiance due to that; kaṇgaḷ – my eyes which are suffering more than me; kāṇbadu – enjoy to its full satisfaction; enṟu kol – when?

**Перевод:**

**Oh friends who are more caring towards me than myself! In tiruvallavāḻ, vaidikas who are exclusively devoted without any expectations and greatly attached \[to emperumān\], are performing karmas (rituals) such as agnihōtram etc which are part of vorśipping bhagavān; the smoke from such rituals, taking the good colour of dark pigment rises up to the sky, covers it and makes it appear dark, providing shade and giving coolness. emperumān is residing in such tiruvallavāḻ and is like a pulpless block of sugar of the cane which is sweet inside and outside and on top of that sweetness, he is also like the nectar which gives back the lost life. When will my eyes which are suffering more than me, enjoy to their full satisfaction, such emperumān who enjoyed the qualities of my ātmā (self) and rūpam (form)?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fifth pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki says “Whatever I may be doing, when will my eyes see emperumān to have their fatigue removed?”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, parānguśa nāyaki says “When will our eyes see the infinitely enjoyable emperumān who is in tiruvallavāḻ where the best among the vaidikas (followers of vēdam) are engaged in agnihōtra (fire sacrifice), the smoke from which is covering the sky?”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. nannalat tōḻimīrgāḷ! nalla andaṇar vēḷvip pugai mainnalam koṇḍuyar viṇ maṟaikkum taṇ tiruvallavāḻ kannalam katti tannaik kaniyai in amudam tannai en nalam koḷ sudarai enṟu kol kaṇgaḷ kāṇbaduvē*

- *nannalat tōḻimīrgāḷ* – nannalam is the care they \[friends\] have towards her. That is, not being focussed on having their own desires fulfilled. This being the case, should you all not take my side instead of fearing that the mothers will blame them. \[Questioning her friendship with her friends through an example, explaining How śrī rāma and sugrīva are helping each other\] śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 35.2 sītā asks hanuman “*vānarāṇām narāṇām ca katam āsīt samāgama:*” – How come the monkeys who have no gurukula vāsam (formal education under a teacher) and the princes who are disciples of vaśiśta are together! only those who are bound by śāstram are qualified for formal education \[so monkeys are excluded from that\]. hanuman explains further – “*rāma sugrīvayōr aikyam tēvyēvam samajāyata*” – śrī rāma forgot himself and us and we are now at this current situation. \[Three explanations given here\] 1) That is, they have become so close to each other that, while iḷaiya perumāḷ (lakśmaṇa) is caring for śrī rāma constantly with the bow in his hand, \[instead of him\] I was sent for this most confidential service \[of being a messenger between śrī rāma and you\]. 2) When iḷaiya perumāḷ committed a mistake, hanuman became so confident that he helped to reunite sītā with śrī rāma. \[Did iḷaiya perumāḷ commit a mistake?\] It was because of his leaving sītā alone, they ended up getting separated from each other. 3) “*ēvam samajāyata”* – They were trying to increase each others wealth. śrī rāma ensured that sugrīva became the ruler of the forest. Such was their friendship; so too are \[her\] friends.
- *nalla andaṇar* – brāhmaṇas who are ananyaprayōjanars (who have no ulterior motives except kainkaryam); only these brāhamaṇas can serve matching [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s greatness; this being the case, should you (friends) also be not like them? The smoke from the yāgams of the ananyaprayōjana brāhmaṇas, leaving behind the residue, reaches up to the sky and covers it. The rising dark smoke reaches up and covers the sky and does not let those who accumulated virtuous deeds and ended up in the sky in celestial vehicles, to see and enjoy each other’s face. It appears that the residents of that abode are having the quality of not letting couples enjoy each other’s face. This is how they cause smoke \[also can be said as their jealousy\].
- *taṇ tiruvallavāḻ kannal katti tannai* – The block of sugar cane without any residue as said in “a block of this hill”.
- *kaniyai* – Already ripened instead of having to wait for it to ripe.
- *in amudam tannai* – That which is capable of building up the body. That is, giving strength to enjoy.
- *in amudam* – Unlike the salt water \[nectar\] consumed by dēvas, this is a nectar which can uplift the soul.
- *en nalam koḷ sudarai* – One who fully captured me and is radiant due to that.  Also explained as – one who is having the beauty which captivated me to be his servant. He is having a form which reveals that it was his gain to fully capture [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/).
- *enṟu kol kaṇgaḷ kāṇbaduvē* – As a mother would say “Let me suffer anyway, let my child live”, āḻvār is saying “when will my eyes be relieved of their suffering?”. āḻvār is the one who had his faculties fully desiring to enjoy [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) in [tiruvāimoḻi 3.8](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/10/thiruvaimozhi-3-8-mudiyane/) “*mudiyānē*“. Both his senses and himself will long for emperumān. śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 40.3 “*gātraiś śōkābhikarśita: samspruśēyam*” (I should be blessed to touch śrī rāma with my weakened limbs). When children live, those who are dear to them will be relieved \[similarly, if [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s eyes enjoy emperumān, that will relieve āḻvār from stress too\].

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.9.6. Kanbadu

*kānbadenjñānṟukolō? vinaiyēn kani vāy madavīr! pāṇ kural vaṇḍinodu pasum tenṟalum āgi engum sēṇ sinai ōngu marac ceḻum kānal tiruvallavāḻ māṇ kuṟaḷ kōlap pirān malart tāmaraip pādangaḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

pāṇ – in the form of song; kural – having rhythmic sound from the throat; vaṇḍinodu – with the beetles; pasum tenṟalum – fresh southerly breeze; āgi – be; engum – in all places; sēṇ – tall; sinai – having branches; ōngu – rising; maram – having trees; seḻu – attractive; kānal – having seaside gardens; tiruvallavāḻ – in tiruvallavāḻ; māṇ – celibacy (which highlights his seeking aspect); kuṟaḷ – and having dvarfness; kōlam – having attractive form; pirān – great benefactor’s; malar – blossomed; tāmarai – enjoyable like lotus; pādangaḷ – divine feet; kani – ripened like a fruit; vāy – having bright face with beautiful lips; madavīr – Oh friends who are obedient towards me!; vinaiyēn – having sin (to not interact with emperumān as much as I desired); kāṇbadu – seeing him; enjñānṟu kolō – when will the day be?

**Перевод:**

**tiruvallavāḻ is having attractive seaside gardens which are having rising trees with tall branches and is having the rhythmic sound of beetles in the form of song and fresh southerly breeze filled everywhere. Oh friends who are obedient towards me and are having bright face with beautiful lips which are ripened like a fruit! When will the day, I who am having sin, will see the enjoyable lotus like divine feet of the great benefactor  who is practising celibacy, having dvarflike and attractive form?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the sixth pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki says “When will I see the very attractive divine feet of śrī vāmana who is mercifully standing in tiruvallavāḻ?”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. kānbadenjñānṟukolō? vinaiyēn kani vāy madavīr! pāṇ kural vaṇḍinodu pasum tenṟalum āgi engum sēṇ sinai ōngu marac ceḻum kānal tiruvallavāḻ māṇ kuṟaḷ kōlap pirān malart tāmaraip pādangaḷē*

- *kāṇbadu enjñānṟu kolō vinaiyēn* – Let my faculties be, when will my hunger be gone.
- *vinaiyēn* – I have committed a sin which is distinct from everyone else’s in the world. [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is seen by even those who have committed the sin for not seeing him, is not seen by me who is having the qualification – I have committed such \[overwhelming\] sin. He is “*māṇ kuṟaḷ kōlap pirān*” (celibate, dvarflike beautiful lord) \[that is, even being an asura, mahābali saw him and even being a devotee I am not seeing him\].
- *kāṇbadu enjñānṟu kolō vinaiyēn* – Previously you were all in a hurry to show him to me, but today I am sinned to say “when will I see him”.
- *kanivāy madavīr* – When will I see you like before \[that is, with reddish lips\]? Her friends are  as said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 7.17](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/7-17/) “*priyōhi jñāninōtyartam*” (jñāni is most dear to me), to her. When she is as described in nācciyār tirumoḻi 1.8 “*māsudai udambodu talai ulaṟi vāyppuṟam veḷuttu*” (having dust covered body, with dry hair and pale mouth/lips), they would not decorate themselves well. She is praying to have them appear \[hale and healthy\] as previously \[when she was with emperumān\].
- *pāṇ kural vaṇḍinodu* – Their sound is never discarded due to being out of tune, and everywhere we hear their singing. That is, they are born with this melodious tune instead of learning to speak first and adding music later. Instead of saying “sweet song like honey”, if the song itself is an embodiment of honey, that will be very sweet. pāṇ kural – the voice is in the form of music.
- *pasum tenṟalum āgi engum* – Unpolluted breeze. Instead of touching many \[unwanted\] regions, arriving directly here.
- *pasum tenṟal* – Also explained as fresh \[young\] breeze.
- *sēṇ sinai* … – Having the gardens looking beautiful due to the branches of the trees having grown sideways and trees themselves standing tall.
- *seḻum kānal* – Attractive garden. kānal means seaside garden or seaside land.  sēn –  being tall; sinai – branch. Growth for the branches in sideways and for the tree, upwards.
- *māṇ kuṟaḷ kōlap pirān* – When will I see the most enjoyable divine feet of the [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is standing in tiruvallavāḻ? He is standing there as vāmana who begged to get his own belongings, making his greatly valuable form appear in a dwarf form, and letting his devotees enjoy his saulabhyam (simplicity) and beauty.
- *malart tāmaraip pādangaḷ* – The divine feet which are most enjoyable like freshly blossomed lotus flowers. He himself created the taste for [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) at first, and at his divine feet. The enjoyability of his divine feet is such that it will make one recite “adigaḷ, adigaḷ” constantly.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.9.7. Padangal melani

*pādangaḷ mēlaṇi pūntoḻak kūdungol? pāvai nalleer! ōda nedum tadattuḷ uyar tāmarai sengaḻunīr mādargaḷ vāṇmugamum kaṇṇum ēndum tiruvallavāḻ nādan injñālam uṇḍa nampirān tannai nādoṟumē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ōdam – like ocean; nedu – vast; tadattuḷ – in ponds; uyar – tall; tāmarai – lotus; sengaḻunīr – red lily; mādargaḷ – women; vāḷ – having radiance; mugamum – beauty of the face; kaṇṇum – beauty of eyes; ēndum – reflecting; tiruvallavāḻ – for tiruvallavāḻ; nādan – being the lord; i – this; jñālam – world; uṇḍa – with the incident of his consuming and protecting from total deluge; nam – for us; pirān tannai – appearing as our benefactor; nāḷ toṟum – eternally; pāvai – like a doll; nalleer – oh beautiful ladies who are having features!; pādangaḷ – divine feet; mēl – on; aṇi – wearing; pū – at least the flower; toḻa – to worship; kūdum kol – will it be possible?

**Перевод:**

**tiruvallavāḻ is having ponds which are vast like ocean, with tall lotus and red lily flowers which reflect the radiance from the beautiful face and eyes of the ladies. emperumān, who is the lord of such tiruvallavāḻ consumed and protected the world from total deluge. Hence he is appearing as our benefactor. Oh beautiful ladies who are having features like a doll! Will it be possible to at least worship the flower which is on the divine feet of such emperumān?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the seventh pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki says “Would we eternally pray by placing flowers at the divine feet of emperumān who is mercifully standing in tiruvallavāḻ?”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, parānguśa nāyaki says “Would we at least worship the flowers which were worn by āpatsakan (companion in difficult situations), the lord of tiruvallavāḻ which is having attractive ponds?”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. pādangaḷ mēlaṇi pūntoḻak kūdungol? pāvai nalleer! ōda nedum tadattuḷ uyar tāmarai sengaḻunīr mādargaḷ vāṇmugamum kaṇṇum ēndum tiruvallavāḻ nādan injñālam uṇḍa nampirān tannai nādoṟumē*

- *pādangaḷ mēlaṇi pūntoḻak kūdum kol* – Will it be possible for us the decorate his divine feet with flowers and worship him?
- *pāvai nalleer* – Three explanations – 1) The ladies who appear like doll to not have the ability to stop her. 2) They appear like an \[beautiful\] art work. 3) [parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is conversing happily with them since they are not stopping her.
- *ōdam …* – In the ponds which are as vast as the ocean, the tall lotus and red lily flowers reflect the radiantly beautiful faces and eyes of the ladies of the town \[both the flowers and beauty of ladies are comparable\]. Alternative explanation – as in a great scholarly assembly ignorant people will be discarded, the beauty of the town discards everything else \[such as the beauty of tall lotus and red lily flowers, the radiance of the beautiful faces and eyes of the ladies\].
- *mādargaḷ vāḷ mugamum kaṇṇum ēndum* – It is difficult to distinguish between the \[beauty of the\] town and fertile fields.
- *tiruvallavāḻ nādan* – Superior to śrīvaikuṇṭanātan. Being the lord of śrīvaikuṇṭam means being the lord of anta:puram (private quarters of the queen) only, since it is said in [tiruvāimoḻi 4.9.10](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/04/thiruvaimozhi-4-9-10-kandu-kettu/) “*oṇḍodiyāḷ tirumagaḷum nīyumē nilā niṟpa*” (While [śrīmahālakśmi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/), the one who is having distinguished forearms with ornaments like bangles, and you stand alone; but this samsāram (material relam) is unlike that, it is barren land where one person’s clothes are to be shared by seven persons \[and you are mercifully here to help everyone here\].
- *i jñālam uṇḍa* – Without considering his own supremacy, he will be the abode of those who are suffering. Just considering the danger, he would place everyone in his stomach and protect them.

When asked “Was this only heard in history?”, [parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) replies,

- *nam pirān* – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who rescued me who was consumed by the deluge of samsāram and brought me up to this stage.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.
