## 5.9.8. Nadorum vidinriye

*nādoṟum vīdinṟinṟiyē toḻak kūdum kol? nannudaleer! āduṟu tīm karumbum viḷai sennelum āgi engum māduṟu pūndadam sēr vayal sūḻ taṇ tiruvallavāḻ nīduṟaiginṟa pirān nilam tāviya nīḷ kaḻalē*

**Пословный перевод:**

engum – everywhere; ādu – swaying; uṟu – having; tī – sweet; karumbum – sugarcane; viḷai – well grown; sennelum – fresh paddy; āgi – becoming; mādu – proximity; uṟu – having; pūm tadam – ponds with blossomed flowers; sēr – together; vayal – fields; sūḻ – surrounded; taṇ – cool; tiruvallavāḻ – in tiruvallavāḻ; nīduṟaiginṟa – eternally residing; pirān – great benefactor’s; nilam – earth; tāviya – measured and accepted; nīḷ – growing to reach everyone’s head; kaḻal – divine feet; nal – being attractive due to such worship; nudaleer – having forehead!; nāḷ toṟum – everyday; vīdu – a momentary break; inṟiyē – without; toḻak kūdum kol – will it be possible to worship?

**Перевод:**

**The cool tiruvallavāḻ is surrounded by fertile fields which are filled with swaying sweet sugar canes and fresh paddy and are having ponds with blossomed flowers in close proximity. emperumān, the great benefactor who is eternally residing in such tiruvallavāḻ, measured and accepted the earth with his divine feet which grew to reach everyone’s head.  Oh friends who are having attractive forehead due to vorśipping such emperumān! Will it be possible for me to worship him everyday without even a momentary break?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the eighth pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki says “Will it be possible to serve him eternally?”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, parānguśa nāyaki says “Will it be possible to eternally enjoy the divine feet of emperumān who is eternally residing in tiruvallavāḻ which is surrounded by fertile fields?”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. nādoṟum vīdinṟinṟiyē toḻak kūdum kol? nannudaleer! āduṟu tīm karumbum viḷai sennelum āgi engum māduṟu pūndadam sēr vayal sūḻ taṇ tiruvallavāḻ nīduṟaiginṟa pirān nilam tāviya nīḷ kaḻalē*

- *nāḷ toṟum* … – “*nāḷ toṟum*” (always) differentiates it from “*darśa pūrṇa māsa …*” (in every pakśam (fortnight)) etc. “*vīdu inṟiyē*” (without a break) differentiates it from nitya agni hōtram (agni hōtram which is performed everyday \[but only at certain times of the day\]). [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is praying as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 3.3.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/08/thiruvaimozhi-3-3-1-ozhivil-kalam/) “*oḻivil kālam ellām*” (At all times). āḻvār is desiring for this continuous service to [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) due to his attachment as a result of his taste in servitorśip unlike us who desire for service based on the faith in our ācārya’s instructions.
- *nal nudaleer* – Will I see you with the dust particles on your forehead due to having paid obeisances to [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who has arrived? [parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) will worship emperumān as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 5.3.7](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/06/thiruvaimozhi-5-3-7-valaiyul-agappaduththu/) “*talaiyil vaṇangavumāngolō*” (can we bow to him with our head?), and they too will follow; just as she is happy in performing kainkaryam, they (her friends) are happy to see her desires fulfilled.
- *āduṟu tīm karumbum* – The sugar canes are always engaged in swaying. tī – sweetness. The fresh paddy is also ready to be harvested at all times. Everything there is ripened \[in devotion\].
- *māduṟu pū …* – In invigorating tiruvallavāḻ which is surrounded by fields which are close to ponds having flowers. The town is surrounded by ponds which are surrounded by fields – this is how the town remains cool.
- *nīdu …* – The greatness of this abode is – unlike the incarnations, specifically trivikrama avatāram where [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) placed his easily approachable divine feet on everyone’s end without checking their qualities or the lack of them, here in this divyadēśam, he is eternally residing and favouring everyone.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.9.9. Kalal valai

*kaḻal vaḷai pūrippa yām kaṇḍu kai toḻak kūdum kolō? kuḻalenna yāḻumennak kuḷir sōlai uḷ tēnarundi maḻalai vari vaṇḍugaḷ isai pādum tiruvallavāḻ suḻalin mali cakkarap perumānadu tollaruḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kuḷir – cool; sōlaiyuḷ – in the garden; tēn – honey; arundi – drink; maḻalai – young; vari – having stripes; vaṇḍugaḷ – beetles; kuḻalenna – to be said as flute; yāḻumenna – to be said as yāḻ (a string instrument); isai – music; pādum – sing; tiruvallavāḻ – one who is standing in tiruvallavāḻ; suḻalil – due to radiance of self; mali – greatly shining; cakkaram – one who is having the divine chakra (disc); perumānadu – sarvēśvaran’s; tol – natural; aruḷ – mercy; kaḻal – slipping from hands; vaḷai – bangles; pūrippa – to become complete (and remain on the hands); yām – us; kaṇḍu – see him; kai toḻa – to worship him with our hands; kūdum kolō – will it be possible?

**Перевод:**

**tiruvallavāḻ is having cool gardens where young beetles which are having stripes, have drunk honey and are singing music which can be said as the sound of flute and yāḻ. sarvēśvaran is standing in such tiruvallavāḻ, having divine chakra which is greatly shining due to radiance of self. Will it be possible that his natural mercy will make us see him and worship him with our hands to make my bangles complete and stop them from slipping from my hands?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the ninth pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki says “Will it be possible to receive his mercy to worship him, to retain the bangles which are slipping from my hands?”*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, parānguśa nāyaki says “Will we be able to enjoy him, by the mercy of sarvēśvaran who is having the divine chakra in his hand, in tiruvallavāḻ where the beetles who have drunk the honey, are swaying?”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. kaḻal vaḷai pūrippa yām kaṇḍu kai toḻak kūdum kolō? kuḻalenna yāḻumennak kuḷir sōlai uḷ tēnarundi maḻalai vari vaṇḍugaḷ isai pādum tiruvallavāḻ suḻalin mali cakkarap perumānadu tollaruḷē*

- *kaḻal vaḷai* – Like “veḷ vaḷai” (white bangles), here it is said as “kaḻal vaḷai” (bangles which are slipping from hands). “Slipping from hands” has become the adjective for the bangles. It is because of his abandoning of her, this slipping from hands is said as adjective for the bangles. pūrippa – to become complete. If he arrives, these bangles can be seen on her hands.
- *yām kaṇḍu kai toḻak kūdum kolō* – Subsequently comes the verb \[her action\].
- *yām* – \[Reason for saying yām in plural instead of yān\] Though only her bangles are slipping during separation, the situation is common for all.
- *kuḻalenna yāḻumenna* – The sound of the beetles can be compared to that of flute and yāḻ. One would feel that they heard everything that is sweet in the world. As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam bāla kāṇḍam 1.18 “*viṣṇunā sadruśō vīryē sōmavat priya darśana:*” (śrī rāma is similar to viṣṇu in his valour and in his looks he is attractive to see like the moon).
- *kuḷir sōlaiyuḷ tēn arundi* – \[The beetles\] drinking the honey to warm them up in the cool and invigorating gardens.
- *maḻalai vari vaṇḍugaḷ* – tiruvallavāḻ where young and attractive beetles, singing to express their joy. One who is standing there \[emperumān\].
- *isai pādum* – Just as those prideful and tender persons \[sons of very rich persons\] would wander around discarding sandalwood as waste wood and applying fragrant essences, these beetles will discard prose and will only sing the music.
- *suḻal …* – sarvēśvaran who is having the divine disc which is rotating fiercely with the intent of destroying the enemies.
- *suḻalin mali cakkaram* – Also explained as the disc which is shining like rotating.
- *tol aruḷ* – Due to the natural mercy – will it be possible for me to worship him with my hands and have my bangles be complete \[that is, remaining in my hands\].

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.9.10. Tol arul

*tol aruḷ nal vinaiyāl solak kūdum kol? tōḻimīrgāḷ! tol aruḷ maṇṇum viṇṇum toḻa ninṟa tirunagaram nal aruḷ āyiravar nalan ēndum tiruvallavāḻ nal aruḷ nam perumān nārāyaṇan nāmangaḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tol – natural; aruḷ – his benefactorśip; maṇṇum – residents of samsāram (material realm); viṇṇum – residents of paramapadam (spiritual realm); toḻa – to worship and enjoy; ninṟa – where he descended to and stood in; tiru – having prosperity; nagaram – town; nal – caring towards his devotees even more than himself; aruḷ – having mercy; āyiravar – thousand devotees; nalan – goodness in the form of knowledge about him, love towards him etc; ēndum – beholding; tiruvallavāḻ – in tiruvallavāḻ; nal – well; aruḷ – having mercy; nam – making us enjoy; perumān – being lord; nārāyaṇan – nārāyaṇan who is with all auspicious qualities and wealth, his; nāmangaḷ – divine names which express those qualities, wealth etc; tōḻimīrgāḷ – Oh friends (who are joyful to recite such divine names)!; tol – natural; aruḷ – mercy; nal vinaiyāl – virtuous aspects; solak kūdum kol – will we be able to recite?

**Перевод:**

**sarvēśvaran descended to and stood in prosperous tiruvallavāḻ to have the residents of both samsāram and paramapadam worship and enjoy his natural benefactorśip. There are thousand devotees who are caring towards his devotees even more than himself, who behold the goodness in the form of knowledge about him, love towards him etc. He is nārāyaṇan who is with all auspicious qualities and wealth, having mercy and letting us enjoy him. Oh friends! will we be able to recite his divine names which express those qualities, wealth etc, by the virtuous aspects which are his natural mercy? Also explained as – aruḷ also implies his favour. Will we be able to praise him by his virtuous deeds out of his mercy?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the tenth pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki says “Will I be able to see emperumān and recite his divine names out of love, by his natural mercy?”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, parānguśa nāyaki says “Will it be possible for us to recite the divine names of nārāyaṇa who is naturally related to us and is residing in tiruvallavāḻ which is the abode of distinguished personalities, by his mercy?”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. tol aruḷ nal vinaiyāl solak kūdum kol? tōḻimīrgāḷ! tol aruḷ maṇṇum viṇṇum toḻa ninṟa tirunagaram nal aruḷ āyiravar nalan ēndum tiruvallavāḻ nal aruḷ nam perumān nārāyaṇan nāmangaḷē*

- *tol aruḷ* – By his natural mercy.
- *nal vinaiyāl* – That is, by seeing him and as a result of that joy, will we be able to recite \[his divine names\]? Explained as – seeing him by his natural mercy, and being pleased with that, will we be able to recite his divine names; nalvinai – joy. Alternative explanation – By the virtuous deeds which are a result of his natural mercy, will we see him and recite his names? ammangi ammāḷ (an ācārya) would explain the meaning of the whole sentence as – “due to one’s sin, one’s tongue will be dry; [parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying ‘will we be fortunate to have saliva in our tongue and be able to recite his divine names?'”.
- *tol aruḷ* – The great town where he stood to have his unblemiśed mercy be vorśipped by the residents of both samsāram and paramapadam.
- *nal aruḷ āyiravar* – Those who are even more caring than [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) in protecting the citizens/children.
- *nalan* … – The town which lives by praising his auspicious qualities; the town which lives by performing mangaḷāśāsanam \[benediction\] out of love towards him.
- *nal aruḷ nam perumān* – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is having good mercy and is being our lord. good mercy – vātsalyam (motherly care). The meaning of the word nārāyaṇa includes vātsalyam \[his motherly care of being the antaryāmi of every entity\] and svāmitvam \[his supremacy of being the support for every entity\]. First [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) explains the meaning of the word nārāyaṇa and then recites the word “nārāyaṇa”.
- *nārāyaṇan nāmangaḷē* – The word “nārāyaṇa” ascertains [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) \[his true nature of being the antaryāmi and the support for all entities\]. All other names explain the qualities and activities of such [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is established by such specific aspects \[of being the antaryāmi and the support for all entities\].

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.9.11. Namangal ayiram

*nāmangaḷ āyiram udaiya namperumān adi mēl sēmam koḷ ten kurugūrc catakōpan terinduraitta nāmangaḷ āyirattuḷ ivai pattum tiruvallavāḻ sēmam koḷ tennagar mēl seppuvār siṟandār piṟandē*

**Пословный перевод:**

nāmangaḷ āyiram udaiya – having thousand names (which are amśam (representation) of the priamary name “nārāyaṇan”, as said in “pērāyiram koṇḍadōr pīdudaiyan nārāyaṇan“); nam perumān – sarvēśvaran who can be surrendered by everyone claiming “our lord”, his; adi mēl – on divine feet; sēmam – the firm faith in the form of intelligence of being the bestover of tranquillity; koḷ – having; then – orderly; kurugūr – the leader of āḻvārtirunagari; satakōpan – nammāḻvār; terindu – analysed and determined (that “these divine feet are the refuge”); uraitta – mercifully spoke; nāmangaḷ – like divine names which describe him; āyirattuḷ – among the thousand pāsurams; ivai – these; pattum – ten pāsurams; tiruvallavāḻ – tiruvallavāḻ; sēmam koḷ – protective; then – beautiful; nagar mēl – on this town; seppuvār – those who can recite; piṟandu – being connected with the material body; siṟandār – having the greatness of being able to enjoy bhagavān

**Перевод:**

**sarvēśvaran who is having thousand names, can be surrendered to by everyone claiming “our lord”. nammāḻvār, the leader of the orderly āḻvārtirunagari, having firm faith in the form of intelligence of such sarvēśvaran’s divine feet being the bestover of tranquillity, analyzed, determined and mercifully spoke the thousand pāsurams which resemble the \[thousand\] divine names which describe him. Those who can recite these ten pāsurams which are on the protective and beautiful town tiruvallavāḻ, will have the greatness of being able to enjoy bhagavān even while being connected with the material body.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the end, āḻvār says “Those who are experts of this decad, are best among everyone even while being in samsāram (material realm)”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*In the end, āḻvār explains the result of this decad as those who can recite this decad are born with qualification to enjoy bhagavān.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. nāmangaḷ āyiram udaiya namperumān adi mēl sēmam koḷ then kurugūrc catakōpan terinduraitta nāmangaḷ āyirattuḷ ivai pattum tiruvallavāḻ sēmam koḷ tennagar mēl seppuvār siṟandār piṟandē*

- *nāmangaḷ …* – As said in mahābhāratam “*dēvō nāma sahasravān*” (The shining [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who has thousand names), as he is having many divine names which describe his qualities and activities, he is well known as sarvēśvaran. nam – familiarity. perumān – sarvēśvaran.
- *adi mēl sēmam koḷ* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) who gave up all other bondage and held emperumān’s divine feet as his refuge.
- *terinduraitta nāmangaḷ āyirattuḷ ivai pattum* – ānalysed and spoken from the thousand pāsurams which reveal his qualities and activities as revealed by his divine names. Just as one will experience the divine qualities when reciting the thousand names, these pāsurams will also give the same experience. For those who recite this decad which is on the noble town of tiruvallavāḻ. tennagar – beautiful town.
- *siṟandār piṟandē* – For an [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/), accepting birth is the lowest point \[since he is forced into it by his karma (deeds)\], but for [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), his birth leads to increasing his radiance; similarly since these devotees are engaged in enjoying [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) right here, they too are the best. Is it not said in tiruviruttam 79 “*sīdanaiyē toḻuvār viṇṇuḷārilum sīriyarē*” (those who worship the cool emperumān, are greater than the [nityasūris](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/))? Those who can practice this decad, will enter the divya dēśams and enjoy emperumān unlike me who set out to go to his divya dēśam and suffered enroute due to lack of strength. Though their birth is due to their karma, since they are meant for him, their bodies are greater than that of [muktātmās (liberated souls)](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/). They are as great as bhagavān’s incarnations which are meant for his devotees.

## 5.10 Piranda arum

## 5.10.1. Piranda arum

*piṟanda āṟum vaḷarnda āṟum periya bāradam kai seydu aivarkkut tiṟangaḷ kātti ittuc ceydu pōna māyangaḷum niṟandanūdu pukkenadāviyai ninṟu ninṟu urukki uṇginṟa ic ciṟanda vān sudarē! unnai enṟu kol sērvaduvē*

**Пословный перевод:**

piṟanda – (as said in “ajāyamāna:“, “nārāyaṇāt” and “ajōpisan“, though being not bound by karma and having unfailing nature, born for the sake of protecting his devotees as one amongst the \[worldly\] species) born; āṟum – way; vaḷarnda – grew (to have his enemies destroyed and to sustain himself with the materials which are dear to his devotees); āṟum – way; periya bāradam – in mahābhārata \[war\]; kai seydu – arranging the armies; aivarkku – for the five pāṇḍavas; tiṟangaḷ – the means for victory; kātti ittu – revealing; seydu – completing the purpose of his incarnation (by favouring his devotees and destroying the others); pōna – returning to his own radiant abode; māyangaḷaum – amazing ways; niṟandan – for the inner region of my heart; ūdu – inside; pukku – entered; enadu – my; āviyai – ātmā; ninṟu ninṟu – moment after moment; urukki – melting to be fluid; uṇginṟa – consuming; i – being present for me always; siṟanda – matching; vān – infinite; sudarē – Oh one who is having radiance!; unnai – you; enṟu kol – when; sērvadu – will I reach?

**Перевод:**

**The way kriṣṇa was born, the way he grew up, the way he arranged the armies in mahābhāratam for the five pāṇḍavas and revealed the means for their victory, and the amazing ways of completing the purpose of his incarnation and returning to his own radiant abode have all entered inside the inner region of my heart and are melting my ātmā moment after moment to become fluid and consume me; oh one who is being present for me always, is having matching and infinite radiance! when will I reach you?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the first pāsuram, āḻvār mercifully explains the meaning of this decad briefly in this pāsuram saying “your birth etc touch my internal spot \[heart\] and weakens me; when will I be removed of this weakness and sustain myself to enjoy you?”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*In the first pāsuram, āḻvār mercifully explains the birth and activities of kriṣṇa briefly.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. piṟanda āṟum vaḷarnda āṟum periya bāradam kai seydu aivarkkut tiṟangaḷ kātti ittuc ceydu pōna māyangaḷum niṟandanūdu pukkenadāviyai ninṟu ninṟu urukki uṇginṟa ic ciṟanda vān sudarē! unnai enṟu kol sērvaduvē*

- *piṟanda āṟum* – He was born to break the shackles of his parents. Is there anyone who takes birth eliminating the bondage of the parents who give birth to him? They (vasudēva and dēvaki) thought that he was the one who was binding them \[just as anyone would think about a child bringing in restrictions in their lifestyle\]; unable to bear it, he eliminated their bondage. As said in periya tirumoḻi 8.5.1 “tandai kālil vilangaṟa”, did he not take birth to remove the knot in the feet of his parents?
- *piṟanda āṟum* – Dear child! Should there at least not be a lamp lit! you were yourself born as the light. As said in tiruppāvai 5 “*āyar kulattil tōnṟum aṇi viḷakku*” (the beautiful lamp which appeared in the covherd clan).
- *piṟanda āṟum* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is thinking about [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is not bound by karma, is taking birth as an individual bound by karma, having the protection of his devotees as his purpose while assuming such births, having their time of danger as the time for his birth, taking birth without minimizing any of his opulence, making his divine spiritual form available for everyone to enjoy and eliminating the birth of those who meditate upon his birth. āḻvār thinks about the various aspects such as “they \[parents of kriṣṇa\] being imprisoned and emperumān to be born to them, for our sake”.
- *piṟanda āṟum* – As said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 5.3 “*āvirbhūtam*“, why is [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) not saying “*tōṟṟinavāṟum*” (appearing) \[piṟanda is casual, tōṟṟina is more poetic and signifies divinity\]? āḻvār is using the term “piṟandvāṟum” since while samsāris live in womb for 10 months, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) as śrī rāma lived in the womb for 12 months as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam bāla kāṇḍam 18.8 “*tadaśca dvādaśēmāsē*” (in the 12th month of caitra), since his mother kausalyā suckled him and since śrī rāma suffered when he could not get mother’s milk, and since he placed himself in a humble position to be bound and beaten by his mother \[yaśōdā\]. Just as one who saw a pit in the morning, would fall in it in the night, āḻvār is so bewildered that he became unconscious thinking about kriṣṇa’s grown up \[growing up\] stage by saying previously in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.3.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/06/thiruvaimozhi-1-3-1-paththudai-adiyavar/) “*ettiṟam*” (how is it possible?); he is now getting to that same state by going further back \[up to  the stage of kriṣṇa’s birth\]. It is well known that āḻvār fell unconscious there saying “*ettiṟam*” and here saying “*piṟandvāṟum*“. śrī bharatāḻvān while being separated from śrī rāma, fell unconscious and was helplessly surrounded by his mothers and all, and śrī śatrugnāḻvān became frightened to near him and became dumb-founded on seeing his state as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 87.4 “*śatrugna: anantarastita:*” (śatrugna stood helplessly); similarly, [āḻvārtirunagari](http://azhwarthirunagari.koyil.org/) is praised in tiruviruttam 100 “*nallār navil kurugūr*” (kurugūr which is the abode for noble people), all the wise people (devotees) from all over the world came there and became bewildered seeing [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s state.
- *vaḷarnda āṟum* – If one thinks about kriṣṇa’s growing up, his birth seems relaxing. While he was born in the prison cell, was he given birth to be raised as one amongst the worldly children?
- *vaḷarnda āṟum* – He grew up to kill pūtanā et al and to nourish the devotion of yaśōdā et al as said in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 1.7.11 “*tāyar magiḻa onnār taḷarat taḷar nadai nadanda*” ([emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who walked like a child for the joy of his devotees and to weaken the others). They relished his actions as said in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 3.2.6 “*midaṟu meḻu meḻuttōda veṇṇey viḻungip pōy padiṟu pala seydippādi engum tiriya*” (Eating butter which is best for the throat and roaming around in this town).
- *vaḷarnda āṟum* – As he stretched his divine feet, both the unfavourable ones and favourable ones were freed from their bodies \[in case of unfavourable ones, they were killed; in case of favourable ones, their belongings were taken away and were eventually liberated to serve him eternally\]; as said in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 3.5.1 “*pottattuṟṟi*” (consuming quickly) and periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 2.9.1 “*veṇṇey viḻungi veṟum kalattai veṟpidai ittu*” (consuming the butter and breaking the pots by throwing them on the ground), he consumed the belongings of the favourable ones. In this manner he mercifully grew up to have the enemies bite the dust, himself consume ghee and his devotees enjoy by having his darśan.
- *periya bāradam* – Popularly known as mahābhāratam.
- *kai seydu* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is thinking about kaṇṇan [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) himself setting the army etc and other warfare activities.
- *aivarkkut tiṟangaḷ kātti ittu* – In his childhood days, his existence itself caused the enemies to die; darkness and light cannot co-exist; once he grew up, he became subservient to his favourable ones.
- *tiṟangaḷ kātti ittu* – āḻvār is explaining various acts of kriṣṇa \[during the war\] such as going as messenger, being the charioteer, picking up arms after vowing not to do so, changing day into night, revealing the life spots of enemies etc.
- *seydu* – doing so
- *pōna māyangaḷum* – The amazing act of leaving this samsāram (material realm) after some time instead of \[permanently\] residing here, where though he descended for the protection of his devotees and favour them by eliminating their dangers, they would fight with him instead of being grateful towards him. As said in mahābhāratam “*krutvāpārāvataraṇam prutivyā: prutulōcana: mōhayitvājagatsarvam katassvamstānam uttamam*” (The wide-eyed kriṣṇa, eliminated the burden of the earth, mesmerized the whole world and ascended to his divine abode) – mercifully incarnating here, fulfilling all the tasks for his favourable ones, smashing all his enemies with his stick, capturing his devotees with merciful glances, and \[in turn\] tormenting both favourable and unfavourable ones and finally leaving this abode! *svam stānam uttamam* – Just as everyone opposes [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) here \[in this material realm\], everyone accepts emperumān there \[spiritual realm\].
- *niṟandan ūdu pukku* – It is not a superficial thing, it pierces the internal/confidential heart and torments.
- *enadu āviyai* – Others, even after hearing about these subject matters, spent their lives eating, dressing up and roaming around.
- *āviyai ninṟu ninṟu urukki* – ātmā which is said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 2.24](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/2-24/) “*accēdya: … adāhya*:” (cannot be cut, burnt), is constantly being broken here.
- *ninṟu ninṟu urukki uṇginṟa* – Though these activities happened once, they are tormenting me repeatedly.
- *ic ciṟanda vān sudarē* – Oh one who is having matching infinite beauty! [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) acquires  more radiance as he takes on more births.
- *ic ciṟanda* – Though it happened in the past, for [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) everything appears in front of his eyes, as if it is happening in the present. Also said as, the bright light (emperumān) of the spiritual sky became the best after descending here. Everything upto “*ic ciṟanda vān sudarē*” can be construed as adjective for that \[*ic ciṟanda vān sudarē*\]. Another explanation is by saying “*urukki uṇginṟa*“, these are highlighted as qualities – that is, all these aspects are making āḻvār melt. This is the preferred explanation.
- *unnai enṟu kol sērvaduvē* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is praying to [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) to mercifully allow him to enjoy emperumān by sustaining himself. Alternative explanation – “*sērugai*” is construed as uniting of emperumān and āḻvār, and as āḻvār asking “when will I be free from getting weakened by meditating upon you in separation and unite with you without ever being separated?”.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.10.2. Vaduvai varttaiyul

*vaduvai vārttaiyuḷ ēṟu pāyndadum māya māvinai vāy piḷandadum maduvai vār kuḻalār kuravai piṇainda kuḻagum adu idu udu ennal āvana valla ennai un seygai naivikkum muduvaiya mudalvā! unnai enṟu talaip peyvanē?*

**Пословный перевод:**

vaduvai vārttaiyuḷ – when the marriage plan \[for nappinnaip pirātti\] came up; ēṟu – bulls; pāyndadum – jumped on them and killed them; māyam – deceptive and being possessed by demoniac qualities; māvinai – horse named kēśi; vāy – mouth; piḷandadum – tore; maduvai – honey; vār – flowing; kuḻalār – with girls who are having hair; kuravai – rāsa krīdā; piṇainda – playing together; kuḻagum – performing sweet activities; adu – that; idu – this; udu – the other thing; ennalāvana – to be specifically said; alla – not; ennai – me (who is greatly attached to you); un – your; seygai – activities; naivikkum – weakens; vaiyam – for the universe; mudu mudalvā – oh primordial cause!; unnai – you; enṟu – when; talaip peyvan – will I reach?

**Перевод:**

**Your acts of jumping on and killing the bulls when the marriage plan \[for nappinnaip pirātti\] came up, tearing the mouth and killing the horse named kēśi which is deceptive and is possessed by demoniac qualities, your playing rāsa krīdā together with girls who are having hair with flowing honey and performing sweet activities, are all weakening me without distinguishing between that activity, this activity or the other activity; oh primordial cause of the universe! when will I reach you? Implies – just as you created the universe which was destroyed in deluge, you should make me who is weak to stay steady.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the second pāsuram, āḻvār says “All your activities such as fighting the bulls etc have weakened me. You should make me sustain myself to enjoy you”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Second pāsuram. See nanjīyar‘s introduction. \[Why āḻvār is focussing on kriṣṇa’s growing up instead of his birth or other incarnations?\] If we analyse the other incarnations, they too would have similar qualities only and hence āḻvār would not go behind them and would not focus on kriṣṇa’s birth too and hence would engage in his growing up only; this is explained in periya tiruvantādi 16 “sīrāl piṟandu” (born in a royal manner). āḻvār cannot do anything when it comes to emperumān‘s birth since it is his choice; now, the devotees can care for him only in his growing up; so he is explaining that now. vaduvai vārttaiyuḷ ēṟu pāyndadum māya māvinai vāy piḷandadum maduvai vār kuḻalār kuravai piṇainda kuḻagum adu idu udu ennal āvana valla ennai un seygai naivikkum muduvaiya mudalvā! unnai enṟu talaip peyvanē?*

- *vaduvai vārttaiyuḷ* – vaduvai – marriage.
- *vārttaiyuḷ* – The popular discussion of “one who kills the seven bulls will be given nappinnaip pirātti in marriage”.
- *ēṟu pāyndadum* – Jumping on the bulls. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) feels that [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) had jumped in to the jaws of death, but emperumān feels that he had jumped into a pond. nappinnaip pirātti”s enjoyability is such that one will even jump into karumāri \[In the olden days, in kāmākśi temple, to fulfil one’s desire, one will jump into the pond which is planted with spears. If the person avoids the spears and jumps into the water, his desires will be fulfilled\].
- *māya māvinai vāy piḷandadum* – Sent by kamsa, assuming a deceptive form, the horse kēśi arrived. A demon appeared assuming the form of a deceptive horse with an open mouth. Just as small children would poke their hand into holes, he placed his hand into its mouth; due to the \[amazing\] unseen sight, his hands grew bigger and ended up tearing its mouth and it fell down in two pieces. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) feels similar to how śrī nārada bhagavān fell unconscious saying in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam “*jagadasmitam*” (the world is ending). śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 5.16.7 “*vyāditāsyō mahā raudras sōsura:kriṣṇabāhunā \| nipapātadvitābhūtō vaidyutēnayatādruma: \|\|*” (That fearsome demon with widely opened mouth fell down broken into two pieces by the divine hands of [kriṣṇa](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) just as a tree was cut into two by thunder bolt). In this way, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) eliminated the hurdles for the girls of śrīvrindāvanam.
- *maduvai vār kuḻalār …* – Girls who have honey-flowing hair. *maduvār kuḻalār* is written as *maduvaivār kuaḻalār*. In rāsakrīdā sport, emperumān made himself one in the game.
- *kuḻagum* – Eliminating their \[independent\] thinking and pride, and mingling as one amongst themselves. That is instead of being an outsider, he entered and stood in the group of covherd girls as one amongst them.
- *adu idu udu ennalāvana alla* – I have not specific requirement on this, that or the other activity.
- *ennai un seygai naivikkum* – Whichever activity, it does not make any difference to me; all it takes is them being your activities and me being there, to torment me. piḷḷān explains – “With this, three concepts are explained in this pāsuram; that is – his togetherness with his devotees \[embracing nappinnai\], his killing of the enemies \[kēśi\] and the protection of neutral persons \[covherd girls who are not as dear as nappinnai yet not inimical as kēśi\] are explained as adu, idu and udu”.
- *muduvaiya mudalvā* – His state is similar to that \[the universe which was consumed in deluge\]. Just as the universe which was consumed by deluge, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) too is totally broken, and he needs to be fully recreated. \[Two direct meanings\] The cause of ancient universe; the ancient cause of the universe.
- *unnai enṟu talaippeyvanē* – Instead of becoming weakened meditating upon you, you should make me sustain myself and meditate upon you. Also explained as – when will I reach you?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.10.3. Peyyum pungulal

*peyyum pūm kuḻal pēy mulai uṇḍa piḷḷait tēṟṟamum pērndōr sādiṟac ceyya pādam onṟāl seyda nin siṟuc cēvagamum ney uṇ vārttaiyuḷ annai kōl koḷḷa nī un tāmaraik kaṇgaḷ nīr malga paiyavē nilaiyum vandu en nenjai urukkungaḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

peyyum – wearing; pū – having flower; kuḻal – having hair; pēy – demon; mulai – bosom; uṇḍa – consumed \[milk\]; piḷḷai – in childish act; tēṟṟamum – clearly knowing it is not his mother’s bosom; ōr – being possessed by demon; sādu – wheel; pērndu – to be thrown; iṟa – and be finished; seyya – reddish; pādam – divine foot; onṟāl – by one; seyda – mercifully done \[kicked\]; nin – your; siṟuc cēvagamum – childish yet valourous act; ney – ghee \[clarified butter\]; uṇ – ate; vārttaiyuḷ – when such discussion came up; annai – mother yaśōdā; kōl – stick; koḷḷa – having; nī – you (the omnipotent who controls everything under your sceptre); un – matching your stature; tāmarai – lotus like; kaṇgaḷ – eyes; nīr – tears; malga – to flow; paiya – standing with fear; nilaiyum – that state; vandu – coming (from those days up to me); en – my; nenjai – desirous heart; urukkungaḷ – melting

**Перевод:**

**Your act of consuming milk from the bosom of the demon who is having flower decorated hair, in a childish act, while clearly knowing it is not your mother’s bosom; your childish valourous act of mercifully kicking the wheel possessed by the demon, by your reddish divine foot, to be thrown up and be finished; your act of standing with fear and tears flowing from your lotus like eyes which match your stature when mother yaśōdā held a stick when the discussion about your eating of ghee came up; these acts are coming up to me and are melting my desirous heart.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the third pāsuram, āḻvār says “Your childhood activities are greatly tormenting me”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. āḻvār is explaining further what was mentioned in first pāsuram “vaḷarndavāṟu” (the way emperumān grew up) saying that he grew up sustaining himself with the life of the enemies and the materials which are touched by his devotees.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. peyyum pūm kuḻal pēy mulai uṇḍa piḷḷait tēṟṟamum pērndōr sādiṟac ceyya pādam onṟāl seyda nin siṟuc cēvagamum ney uṇ vārttaiyuḷ annai kōl koḷḷa nī un tāmaraik kaṇgaḷ nīr malga paiyavē nilaiyum vandu en nenjai urukkungaḷē*

- *peyyum pūm kuḻal pēy mulai uṇḍa* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is explaining further what was mentioned in first pāsuram “*vaḷarndavāṟu*” (the way [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) grew up) saying that he grew up sustaining himself with the life of the enemies and the materials which are touched by his devotees. Mother yaśōdā gave a bath to kriṣṇa, decorated him, made him sleep and went away. At that time, pūtanā arrived.
- *peyyum pūm kuḻal* – This can be considered as an adjective for “*piḷḷai*” (baby kriṣṇa); alternatively, it can be seen as an adjective for “*pēy*” (demoniac pūtanā). She decorated herself and arrived there only to be killed. The mothers usually would decorate themselves nicely to avoid upsetting their toddlers. So, she too decorated herself nicely; she is said in periya tirumoḻi 1.3.1 “*peṟṟa tāy pōl vanda pēycci*” (she came dressed like his mother). The demon which was having hair decorated with flowers.
- *pēy mulai uṇḍa piḷḷait tēṟṟamum* – Instead of having knowledge about his control over everything etc, here it is talking about the knowledge of distinguishing between mother’s bosom and others’ bosom. Even at very toddler state, the babies would know their mothers’ bosom. Still, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) consumed the milk considering her to be his mother.
- *piḷḷait tēṟṟamum* – His clarity in that toddler state. That is – he performed the acts towards pūtanā which he would normally do after being pleased on consuming milk from mother yaśōdā. He both knows and knows not that she is dangerous for him, and his nature is such that whoever is inimical towards him, when they approach him, they will naturally be finished.
- *pērndu* – Furthermore.
- *ōr sādiṟa* – It \[the wheel\] cannot even be doubted to be inimical. At least in the case of pūtanā, one can doubt who she is, but this wheel was placed as protection for him. When some one sees \[real\] yaśōdā, one would at least doubt the identity of pūtanā.
- *ōr sādu* – There is no comparison for the enmity of the wheel towards kriṣṇa.
- *iṟa* – To break. As said in tiruvāimoḻi 6.9.4 “*taḷarndum muṟindum …*” (weakening and breaking into pieces).
- *seyya pādam* – Reddish divine feet. He eliminated the enemies using my \[āḻvār’s\] life. His life is always resting on [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s divine feet.
- *onṟāl* – We cannot say which divine foot he used. It is not that he was doing it with hatred/intent.
- *seyda nin siṟuc cēvagamum* – This is how you set out to perform valorous acts. As śrī rāma, you appeared as a prince, attained the right age, learned weaponry, followed vaśiśta et al, acquiring weapons from viśvāmitra et al and then only destroyed tādakā, mārīca, subāhu et al; all of those are happening without reaching mature age, here in kriṣṇāvatāram, with the mouth and feet. For one whose mouth is capable, he does not need anything more. There is no one who has stronger feet than him. That is why a flag is hoisted on his feet as said in [stōtra ratnam 31](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/01/sthothra-rathnam-31/) “*dvajāravaindānkuśavajralāncanam \| trivikrama! tvaccarṇāmbujadvayam”* (Oh my lord who incarnated as trivikrama! Having śankha (conch), chakra (disc), kalpaka vrukśa (kalpaka tree), dvaja/kodi (flag), arvainda/tāmarai (lotus), ankuśa (hook), vajrāyudam (a weapon) as identity! your two divine feet). Even at that time, it was his divine feet which rose against everything as said in tiruneduntāṇḍagam 5 “*avuṇan uḷḷahtu eṇ madiyum kadandu aṇḍamīdu pōgi”* (reaching beyond the thoughts of the demoniac king and up to the end of the oval shaped universe)*.*
- *ney uṇ …* – Just as he frightened his enemies even in his childhood, as he grew up, he was fearing his devotees.
- *ney uṇ vārttaiyuḷ* – Mother yaśōdā had placed the ghee safely with specific markings and had gone out; on returning she noticed that the markings were changed and said that it was stolen; at that time, kriṣṇa started looking at her with fear.
- *annai kōl koḷḷa* – Being a child, he does not understand that it was just his mother who has taken up the stick; it was her own words in periya tirumoḻi 10.4.8 “*un tam adigaḷ munivar*” (Your father will be angry) – dear child, if your father hears about your actions, he will be angry; her anger is as said in “*unnai nān en kaiyil kōlāl nondida mōdavum killēn*” (I cannot beat you with the stick in my hand, to hurt you); for one who is capable, they can use this stick to punish you and stop you from engaging in mischief further, but I am not capable to do so. As said in periya tirumoḻi 8.3.5 “*tāy edutta siṟu kōlukku uḷaindōdi*” (fleeing out of fear for the small stick (straw) which his mother took up to beat him). He does not realise that his mother just tries to frighten him and even if he was beaten with that stick it will not hurt. \[kriṣṇa’s thinking\] Even if the father takes up a stick, one can relax since it is apt due to his being intent on kriṣṇa’s well being. But if the mother who is always showering love, takes up a stick with anger, he could not bear it. But why did mother yaśōdā do this? When the ghee was stolen, there is no one to stop her anger which will make her take up the stick to beat him.
- *nī un tāmaraik kaṇgaḷ nīr malga* – As it is you deserve to be enjoyed, and if your eyes are well blossomed \[like a lotus flower\], shall we be patient!
- *un tāmaraik kaṇgaḷ* – Eyes matching your stature as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 16.15 “*rāghavōrhativaidēhīm*” (śrī rāma who matches sītā). It is said in [tiruvāimoḻi 5.5.5](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/07/thiruvaimozhi-5-5-5-pakkam-nokki/) “*takka tāmaraik kaṇ*” (matching lotus like eyes).
- *paiyavē nilaiyum* – When she lifted the stick in her hand to beat him, his state of looking at her and shedding tears, becoming pale and being anguished. Alternative explanation – when fearfully looking at her face, his mischievous acts being restless due to neither being able to step back nor being able to stay put.
- *vandu* … – These acts are tormenting me. At least you can escape from your situation, but in my case, they chase me wherever I go and torment me.
- *paiyavē nilaiyum vandu en nenjai urukkum* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says – They are binding my feet to make them not step away.
- *nenjai urukkum* – This is how those acts banged on āḻvār’s heart.
- *urukkum* – This is how [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) melted āḻvār’s heart.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.10.4. Kalla vedattai

*kaḷḷa vēdattaik koṇḍu pōyp puram pukkavāṟum kalandasurarai uḷḷam bēdam seydittu uyir uṇḍa upāyangaḷum veḷḷa nīrc cadaiyānum ninnidai vēṟalāmai viḷanga ninṟadum uḷḷam uḷ kudaindu en uyirai urukki uṇṇumē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kaḷḷa vēdattai – deceptive form (of budda who is outside the tenets of vēdam); koṇḍu – assuming; pōy – going (to become trustworthy by his beauty and maturity); puram – in tripura; pukka – enter; āṟum – way; asurarai – the demoniac residents there; kalandu – mingling inside; uḷḷam bēdam – confusion in mind; seydittu – created; uyir – their life; uṇḍa – taking away; upāyangaḷum – ways; veḷḷam – abundant; nīr – gangā water; sadaiyānum – rudra who is having in his matted hair; ninnidai – in you; vēṟalāmai – being inseparable (by śarīra śarīri bhāvam – body soul relationship); viḷanga – well known through śāstram; ninṟadum – stood; uḷḷam – in my heart; uḷ – all my intellectual acts (thoughts); kudaindu – engrossed; en – my; uyirai – ātmā; urukki – melting it into fluid state; uṇṇum – consumed

**Перевод:**

**The way in which you assumed the deceptive form \[of budda\] going to tripura and entered there, the way you mingled with the demoniac residents of the town and created confusion in their minds and taking their lives away; the way you remain inseparable from rudra who is having abundant gangā water in his matted hair to be well known through śāstram; these aspects engrossed in my intellectual thoughts in my heart and is melting my ātmā into a fluid state.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fourth pāsuram, āḻvār says “emperumān‘s incarnation as budda is tormenting me”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “His act of destroying the demons who were residing in tripuram (three towns), is breaking my ātmā”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. Previously āḻvār explained his stealing from favourable ones; here he is explaining the stealing from unfavourable ones. kaḷḷa vēdattaik koṇḍu pōyp puram pukkavāṟum kalandasurarai uḷḷam bēdam seydittu uyir uṇḍa upāyangaḷum veḷḷa nīrc cadaiyānum ninnidai vēṟalāmai viḷanga ninṟadum uḷḷam uḷ kudaindu en uyirai urukki uṇṇumē*

- *kaḷḷa vēdattaik koṇḍu* – As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 109.34 “*yatāhi cōras satatāhibudda:*” (Just as a thief should be driven out, one who rejects vēdam should also be driven out), assuming a mischievous form. [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is said as in śrī bhagavat gītā 15.15 “*vēdaiśca sarvair ahamēva vēdya:*” (the whole of vēdam speaks about me), assuming a form which rejects vēdam. Here [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is thinking the attractive form of budda which captures the hearts of those who see him, form which is dark, well built, stretched ears and holding a book. He captures them by his beauty to make them think that there is no other truth beyond what is explained by him.
- *pōy* – That is – walking very carefully fearing “whatever I step on will suffer”. While they (followers of budda) preach what is contradictory to \[vēda\] śāstram, to make it appear similar to vēdam, they will say “one cannot hurt others; one should not serve lowly entities; one should not speak mischievously; worldly attachment is not good etc”; these words match their deceptive form. perumāḷ (śrī rāma) mercifully set out to go in exile to the forest, jābālika spoke a few words \[contradictory to vēdam\] convincing him to return to the kingdom; perumāḷ angrily closed his ears and said “come on! you are arguing in favour of atheism in front of me to eliminate my faith in righteousness! what is the point in blaming you, when I should really be blaming my father who engaged you in his court”; jābāli responded “my lord! when you return and accept the throne, to have the tears removed from śrī bharatāḻvān’s eyes, you can see that I change from an atheist to a theist”; at that time everyone hailed as in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 108.1 “*jābālir brāhmaṇōttama:*” (jābāli is best among brāhmaṇas); \[they further said\] since we are wearing yajñōpavīdam, we are known as brāhmaṇas; as said in “*brahma sambandī brāhmaṇa:*” (one who is related to brahmam, is known as brāhmaṇa) – and only he is truly having that quality of being related to you. In this manner, jābāli explained lōkāyata (baudda) philosophy.
- *puram pukka āṟum* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is thinking about the acts of budda after reaching the town. That is – since [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is set out to equate vaidika himsā \[hurting which is allowed in vēdam for higher purpose\] to sāmānya himsā \[hurting which is done without the sanction of vēdam\], he walks carefully even while stepping over grass, not to hurt it.
- *kalandu* – He mingled as one amongst them and preached to them. To gain their trust, he mingled with them completely.
- *asurarai uḷḷam bēdam seydittu* – He preached them avaidika \[contrary to vēdam\] philosophy and eliminated their faith in vēdam. Did they have faith in vēdam? It is said in śrī rāmāyaṇam “*agnihōtrāśca vēdāśca rākśasānām gruhēgruhē*” (fire sacrifices and reciting of vēdam is seen in every rākśasa’s house). Everyone has some good aspects. [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) caused confusion in their minds and eliminated whatever faith they had in righteousness \[only after faith in vēdam is eliminated, they can be easily defeated\].
- *uyir uṇḍa upāyangaḷum* – The ways through which he finished them. Eliminating their faith in vēdam, he made them to be as good as dead bodies and can be easily defeated even by a bikśuka (beggar) and can have him glorified saying “I killed them”. Though emperumān did all of these, he ensured that he is not glorified for it! mahābhāratam karṇa parvam “viṣṇurātmā bhagavatō bhavasya amitatējasa: tasmāt danurjyā samsparśam saviśēhē mahēśvara:” (The omnipresent viṣṇu is the antaryāmi for Siva who is infinitely valourous and vorśippable; due to this fact, Siva was able to launch the arrow on the bow during the destruction of the three towns). For sarvēśvaran, there is no difference in getting things done through a cētana \[rudra\] or acētana \[bow and arrow\]. For [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), there is no difference between rudra and the bow in his hands. This is similar to how emperumān has [cit](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) and [acit](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/09/thathva-thrayam-achith-what-is-matter/) as the material cause in subtle state to effect their gross state \[during creation, the souls and matter from subtle state are transformed to gross state by emperumān\]. Previously, rudra tried to accomplish this himself; but he could not do it, and then emperumān as antaryāmi helped him accomplish it. Once a king had “rudra is supreme” written in a palm leaf and ordered the scholars to accept it and sign it. While many obliged, one scholar \[[kūrattāḻvān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/kuraththazhwan/)\] said “come on! can you establish rudra’s supremacy by preserving the palm leaf! śāstram is explaining that the greatness of your dēvatā is due to sarvēśvaran’s will; that being the case, I may write and agree what you say; but long after our time, a scholar may see this and will say ‘who is this fool to have written and signed this?’ and I don’t want to be laughed at; so you can do whatever you want”.
- *upāyangaḷum* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is thinking about [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s different thoughts from back then.
- *veḷḷa nīr* … – [tirumālai āṇḍān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/thirumalai-andan/) explained as heard from [āḷavandār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/alavandhar/) – this is explaining emperumān’s mischievous act of being present amidst brahmā and rudra. That is, emperumān appearing to be at par with brahmā and rudra. [emperumānār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/emperumanar/) mercifully heard this and said – that is nice; but do we have to go back in time so far? just see his great favour while destroying the three towns – is there any limit for such favours? is this not sufficient?
- *veḷḷa nīr* … – Your being present appearing inseparable from rudra who is having gangā water in his matted hair. That is – rudra being śarīram (body/form) for [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/). Why should it be explained like this? Why can’t rudra be explained as the same as viṣṇu? If we did that, the statement “*viṣṇurātmā*” will become useless. periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 4.7.2 “*nalam tigaḻ sadaiyān mudik konṟai malarum nāraṇan pādat tuḻāyum kalandiḻi punalāl pugar padu gangai*” (the gangā river which is shining with the water flowing down carrying konṟai flower from the pious rudra who is having matted hair and the tuḷasi from the divine feet of śrīman nārāyaṇan). [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying “this flooding gangā river is the proof for rudra’s servitorśip and emperumān’s lordship”. The konṟai flower from the matted hair of rudra and tuḷasi from the divine feet of sarvēśvaran are coming together.
- *uḷḷam uḷ kudaindu* – Entering into my heart and overwhelming it, and tormenting the ātmā which is said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 2.24](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/2-24/) “*accēdya: … adāhya*:” (cannot be cut, burnt). Entering through the mind which is the gateway for knowledge and melting the ātmā into fluid and finishing it.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.10.5. Unna vanavar

*uṇṇa vānavar kōnukku āyar oruppadutta adisil uṇḍadum vaṇṇamāl varaiyai eduttu maḻai kāttadum maṇṇai mun padaittuṇḍumiḻndu kadandidandu maṇanda māyangaḷ eṇṇum tōṟum ennenju erivāy meḻugokkum ninṟē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vānavar kōnukku – for indra who is with his assistants; uṇṇa – to eat; āyar – covherd people (who are engaged in herding cows); oruppadutta – prepared with intent; adisil – food; uṇḍadum – consuming it (assuming the form of gōvardana hill); vaṇṇam – colourful due to the presence of different minerals; māl – huge; varaiyai – hill; eduttu – lift; maḻai – rain (caused by indra having lost his worship); kāttadum – protected; maṇṇai – universe (which is indicated by earth); mun – initially; padaittu – created; uṇḍu – protecting it by placing it in his stomach during deluge; umiḻndu – (subsequently) spitting it out; kadandu – scaling it (to eliminate the ownership claim by others); idandu – rescuing it (during intermediary deluge, with the form of varāha); maṇanda – united with mother earth who was rescued from the deluge; māyangaḷ – these amazing qualities and activities; eṇṇum tōṟum – every time I meditate upon; en – my; nenju – heart; ninṟu – in a singular manner; erivāy – in fire; meḻugokkum – melting like wax

**Перевод:**

**You consumed the food which was prepared with intent by the covherd people for indra to eat; you lifted the huge gōvardana hill which is colourful due to the presence of different minerals and protected \[everyone\] from rain; you initially created the universe, protected it by placing it in your stomach during deluge, spat it out, scaled it, rescued it and united with mother earth who was rescued from the deluge; every time I meditate upon these amazing qualities and activities, my heart is melting like wax in fire in a singular manner.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fifth pāsuram, āḻvār says “Whenever I think about your activities which are done for the sake of your devotees, my mind melts”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. uṇṇa vānavar kōnukku āyar oruppadutta adisil uṇḍadum vaṇṇamāl varaiyai eduttu maḻai kāttadum maṇṇai mun padaittuṇḍumiḻndu kadandidandu maṇanda māyangaḷ eṇṇum tōṟum ennenju erivāy meḻugokkum ninṟē*

- *uṇṇa* … – The event where in his birth-place, some people were preparing food to offer to indra praying for rains, and he ate them. It is due to the jealousy of kriṣṇa thinking “who else can be vorśippable in the town where I was born?”; kriṣṇa said “come on! who is indra! Is one who is not seen by anyone, going to favour us? This being the case, this \[gōvardana\] hill which is the shelter for the clouds, having grass and water, and giving place for the cows, should be our vorśippable deity”. Since they are covherds, they would listen to others, and whatever he said could not be refuted; he said “place all your food offerings in front of the hill” and they mounted everything there; he then entered there and ate them all. Giving one’s exclusive belongings to others is similar to a king letting others enjoy the queen’s sweat. indra along with assistants, was waiting to consume the offering and be satisfied, but [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) consumed them all, in between. Out of rage, he started the heavy rains.
- *vaṇṇa māl varai* … – emperumān is not someone who gives false promise for protection and shies away from doing that. The act of protecting the cows and the covherds without even a drop of rain touching them for seven days by lifting up the inconceivable, huge mountain which appears colourful due to many minerals and holding it up, instead of going away after having his desire fulfilled \[that is, eating all the offerings\]. He also manifested compassion towards indra thinking “I cannot punish this celestial person indra; he acted like this due to his anger in losing his food; he himself will give up after a little while; until then let me protect my dependents”. indra was appointed as the administrator of the earth by kriṣṇa thinking that he is merciful and will protect them; but he became merciless \[being blinded by his ego\] and ended up committing this mistake.
- *maṇṇai* … – Now, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is talking about the favours done by [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) towards the whole universe instead of just a town where the residents set out to vorśipping indra. Creating the universe without anyone asking for it, protecting the ātmās by keeping them in his stomach during the imminent danger of deluge, releasing them thinking “they cannot vanish being inside”, redeeming the universe by scaling it when persons like mahābali claim ownership, rescuing the earth during intermediary deluge assuming the form of mahā varāha (great wild-boar) and since the earth is the abode of bhūmip pirātti, doing what is dear to her and uniting with her – such amazing activities.
- *maṇanda* – enjoying together.
- *eṇṇum tōṟum* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s eagerness to enjoy these activities is greater than [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s protection. āḻvār will neither think about him \[since he is totally weakened thinking about him\] nor avoid thinking about him \[as he cannot sustain himself without thinking about him\]. Just as emperumān is naturally set out for protecting others, āḻvār is set out to become finished.
- *en nenju* – Worldly people should have also constantly meditated upon these activities and spent their time \[but they did not do, only [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s heart was constantly thinking about it\].
- *erivāy meḻugu okkum* – Melted like wax placed near fire.
- *ninṟē* – It is not that it melts sometimes and becomes steady other times, it is constantly melting.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.10.6. Ninra arum

*ninṟavāṟum irundavāṟum kidandavāṟum ninaippariyana onṟalā uruvāy aruvāya nin māyangaḷ ninṟu ninṟu ninaiginṟēn unnai enganam ninaigiṟpan? pāviyēṟku onṟu nanguraiyāy ulagam uṇḍa oṇ sudarē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ninṟa āṟum – his standing ways; irunda āṟum – his sitting ways; kidanda āṟum – his resting ways; ninaippu – to think about; ariyana – difficult; onṟu – any single; alā – not restricted to; uruvāy – having form; aruvāya – not seen for me to experience; nin – your; māyangaḷ – amazing activities; ninṟu ninṟu – tormenting the already weakened heart at every stage; ninaiginṟēn – trying to fully think about; unnai – you (who are performing the activities which weaken me); enganam – how; ninaigiṟpan – can think about in a focussed manner?; pāviyēṟku – for me who am having sin (which stops me from meditating in a focussed manner); ulagam – universe which was getting destroyed in the deluge; uṇḍa – consumed and protected; oṇ sudarē – Oh one who became radiant!; onṟu – unique; nangu – distinguished means; uraiyāy – you should mercifully indicate

**Перевод:**

**Your ways of standing, sitting, and resting are difficult to think about; I am trying to fully think about the amazing activities of yours,  who are not restricted to having a single form, which are tormenting the already weakened heart at every stage; how can I,  who am a sinner, think about you in a focussed manner? ; oh one who became radiant by consuming and protecting the universe which was getting destroyed in the deluge! You should mercifully indicate the unique and distinguished means to save me. “ninṟavāṟum, irundavāṟum, kidandavāṟum” also is explained in context of kriṣṇa standing, sitting and resting in his cradle.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the sixth pāsuram, āḻvār says “I who have not seen all your activities, am not even capable of thinking about them; so, you should mercifully make me sustain myself and meditate upon you”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Sixth pāsuram, āḻvār says “I desired to see all your activities, and am not even capable of thinking about them; so, just as you protected the universe, you should mercifully protect me and make me meditate upon you”. ninṟavāṟum irundavāṟum kidandavāṟum ninaippariyana onṟalā uruvāy aruvāya nin māyangaḷ ninṟu ninṟu ninaiginṟēn unnai enganam ninaigiṟpan? pāviyēṟku onṟu nanguraiyāy ulagam uṇḍa oṇ sudarē*

- *ninṟa* … – Whatever [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is going through in bhagavat viśayam, we go through the same in worldly matters. A very good singer from North arrived in śrīrangam to worship the divine feet of śrīranganātan. That day being the tīrtavāri (the concluding day of brahmōtsavam), [āḻvār tiruvarangap perumāḷ araiyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/thiruvarangapperumal-araiyar/) sang [tirumālai](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/07/thirumalai/) in a melodious tune and praised [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) like taming an elephant and had him mesmerized; at the time he requested emperumān “My lord! A very good devotee of yours has arrived from a distant place to worship your divine feet; you should accept him and honour him”. perumāḷ obliged and invited him through the arcaka; emperumān mercifully ordered the arcakas to perform tirukkaittala sēvai (arcakas carrying emperumān with their bare hands) from tiruppunnai tree \[the divine tree at the banks of candra puskhariṇi, the ceremonial pond inside the temple campus\] up to where the devotee was standing, for a few meters. On completing the act, emperumān mercifully asked “Is this sufficient for this devotee who has arrived from distant location?” \[This explains emperumān’s divine walking activity\]. This is how you should console my heart by mercifully performing some acts. Once, the śrīvaiṣṇava vaśerman of the śrīrangam temple, washed the divine clothes of emperumān nicely, dried them, folded them and presented them to [emperumānār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/emperumanar/). Being very pleased, emperumānār at once took him along to perumāḷ and told him “My lord! Please see how neatly he has washed your divine clothes”; seeing that, emperumān mercifully speaks to emperumānār “for the sake of this vaśerman, I am forgiving the vaśerman of kamsa who committed offense towards me \[during kriṣṇāvatāram\]”.
- *ninṟa āṟum* … – Standing with the bow in his hand at the entrance of lankā; or standing with the bow in his hand after killing vāli; śrī rāmāyaṇam kiśkintā kāṇḍam 19.25 “*avaśtabya ca tiśtantam dadarśa danurūrjitam – śubhā*” (tārā saw śrī rāma who is standing majestically holding the bow, along with lakśmaṇa and sugrīva) – Due to the bow in his hand \[or liking towards him\], tārā felt pleased at her heart instead of seeing śrī rāma who killed her husband vāli and standing victoriously, along with lakhmaṇa who helped in that effort, and sugrīva who served them and is going to be crowned, as “they are our enemies”. Since vāli was demoniac by nature, he got destroyed by his own actions, just as some one will tie a rock in their neck and jump into a lake to kill oneself, while the lake was built to provide water for everyone. She remained “Did he (śrī rāma) commit any mistake?”. Would [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) let live anyone who attacked the one \[sugrīva\] who is as dear to him as his own life?
- *irunda āṟum* – Seated as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 99.25 “*utajē rāmām āsīnam*” (śrī rāma who was seated in the hermitage).
- *kidanda āṟum* – His reclining at the seashore as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 21.1 “*anjali prāng muka: krutvā pratiśiśyē mahōdadē*” (śrī rāma remained prostrated towards east direction with joined palms). “*pratiśiśyē*” – it appears that two oceans are present right across each other; kambanāttāḻvān \[poet kamban\] said “an ocean of mercy is facing the ocean of water”. That is, the arrow \[brahmāstram\] which he launched could have been easily shot by śrī rāma even previously; though he was having such arrow and well built shoulders, he was patiently reclining in front of the undeserving ocean \[king\] – such reclining is explained by [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) here; while it could have been said “*ninṟum irundum kidandum*” \[together\], āḻvār said “ninṟa āṟum”, “irunda āṟum”, “kidanda āṟum” individually since they tormented him individually. Alternate explanation – kriṣṇa’s lifting up of gōvardana hill can be considered for ninṟavāṟum, his being together with the covherd girls before rāsakrīdā can be considered for irundavāṟum, and his subsequent resting on the laps of the covherd girls can be considered for kidandavāṟum. When he stands, it is as said in periya tirumoḻi 6.9.8 “*nilaiyāra ninṟān*” (one who is standing firm) and will make one fear for his sitting and reclining postures \[that they will be even more attractive\]. While he is seated, it is said in tiruvāimoḻi 6.5.5 “*pirān irundamai kāttinīr*” (you showed the seated posture of the benefactor, kriṣṇa); when he is reclining, it is as said in [tirumālai 23](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/10/thirumalai-23/) “*kidandadōr kidakkai*” (the unique reclining posture). As said in tiruccanda viruttam 65 “*niṟpadum ōr veṟpagattirippa viṇ kidappadum naṟperum tiraik kadaluḷ*“, his standing posture in tirumalā (tiruppati), sitting posture in paramapadam and resting posture in tiruppāṟkadal (milky ocean) can also be considered. Another explanation – as said in tiruccanda viruttam 65 “*niṟpadum iruppadum kidappadum en nenjuḷē*” (he is standing, sitting and resting in my heart), in [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s divine heart, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is standing in āḻvār’s heart as said in tiruvāimoḻi 8.7.5 “*tigaḻumaṇikkunṟam onṟē ottu ninṟān*” (he is standing like a shining hill made of precious gems), sitting as said in tiruvāimoḻi 8.7.7 “*sevvāy muṟuvalōdu enaduḷḷattirunda avvāy anṟi yānaṟiyēn maṟṟaruḷē*” (I won’t know any other grace than that of the divine reddish smiling lips \[of emperumān who is seated in my heart\]) and resting as said in periya tiruvandādi 35 “*ninṟum irundum kidandum*” (standing, sitting and resting). Yet another explanation – while [āḻvār tiruvarangap perumāḷ araiyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/thiruvarangapperumal-araiyar/) explains as said in tiruccanda viruttam 64 “*ninṟadendai ūragattu irundadendai pādagattu anṟu vekkaṇaik kidandadu*” (my lord is sitting in tiruvūragam, seated in tiruppādagam and is reclining in tiruvekkā), [emperumānār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/emperumanar/) mercifully explained \[matching the context of the padigam which is focussed on kriṣṇāvatāram\], all of these are seen in the cradle \[of kriṣṇa\]. Baby kriṣṇa standing inside the cradle having the beam in the cradle as support, unable to stand after a while falling down and sitting, and even after unable to sit for a while, reclining and falling asleep – are explained here. Yet another explanation, as said in siṟiya tirumadal “*pōrār vēṟ kaṇ madavāḷ pōndanaiyum poy uṟakkam*” (kriṣṇa pretends to sleep until the spear-eyed yaśōdā leaves), his rising up and standing after she left, his sitting on hearing the sound of her return and reclining on seeing her approaching closer as said in “*mun kidanda tānattē ōrādavan pōl kidanda*” (kriṣṇa pretending to sleep at the same spot where he was before as if he knows nothing).
- *ninaippu ariyana* – Though these incidents occurred once, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is unable to think about these even today. He himself previously said in tiruviruttam 98 “*imaiyōr tamakkum – sevvē nenjāl ninaippaṟidāl veṇṇey ūṇennum īnac collē*” (even for the residents of paramapadam [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s butter eating activities are difficult to comprehend).
- *onṟalā uruvāy* – For āḻvār, just one such incident is enough to torment him forever. \[But here\] not just one, many such incidents are present.
- *aruvāya nin māyangaḷ* – Your amazing activities which are not visible to my eyes.
- *ninṟu ninṟu ninaiginṟēn* – Neither can he complete thinking about him nor can he avoid thinking about him. I will try hard to think about you, but unable to do so. Alternative explanation – while I desire to think about you, and hence am analysing “which is the means to think about you?”.
- *unnai enganam ninaigiṟpan* – You who are omniscient and omnipotent, are not showing me the means through which I can think about you. As said in periya tirumoḻi 8.2.8 “*toṇḍellām nin adiyē toḻudu uyyumākaṇḍu*” (Seeing that all your servitors are redeemed by vorśipping your divine feet) – that is all servitors, those who are desirous of wealth, those who are desirous of self-enjoyment and those who are desirous of serving your eternally including [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) himself go to [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), pray for what they require, acquire them and leave him after getting their desires fulfilled, went to emperumān as said in same pāsuram “*tān kaṇapuram toḻap pōyināḷ*” ([parakāla nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/thirumangai-azhwar/) went to worship emperumān at tirukkaṇṇapuram), thinking that “let me also be with emperumān, enjoy him and return”; would the self see emperumān only, and should it not see self too? Well, if one is going to emperumān seeking some benefits, one can return once that desire is fulfilled, but if one goes to emperumān considering emperumān only as the goal, there is no way they can return. This is the state of those who have extreme love towards [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) \[Here it is explained that, for those with self-interest, they can easily think about emperumān, pray to him, attain what they need and get back to their activities; but for devotees who are exclusively focussed on emperumān, cannot even think about emperumān easily since they don’t have any self interests\].
- *pāviyēṟku* – Except for me \[who has sins\], everyone else is able to think about you and have their desires fulfilled; everyone in the world as said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 1.17.78 “*smrutō yaccati śōbanam*” (one who bestows auspiciousness for those who think about him).
- *onṟu nangu uraiyāy* – Why can’t you tell me like you told a pacifying statement to arjuna \[as in śrī bhagavat gītā 18.66 “*mā suca:*” (do not worry)\]? [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s grief is much greater than arjuna’s grief. [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) declared “I am responsible for the attainment of the goal and the elimination of hurdles”. That is all which is required, and everything else will naturally follow. The real goal is realizing one’s own true nature, the result of such realisation is kainkaryam \[eternal service to emperumān in paramapadam\] and need not be explicitly explained and hence śāstram stops with highlighting the realisation of true nature \[as the initial goal\]. Whatever happens subsequent to that is not meant to be explained \[it is supposed to be experienced personally\]. In this manner, could you not tell me “I will accept responsibility for you”.
- *ulagam uṇḍa oṇ sudarē* – If one consumes food, the body will reflect that. Is desiring to think about, a mistake? Even if such thinking is difficult to do, should you not make that happen? When the universe was in great danger of being consumed by deluge and no one asked you for protection, you yourself consumed it and protected it by placing it in your stomach; while the universe does not realise the favour you did, you considered it as personal gain and remained radiant due to that.
- *ulagam uṇḍa on sudarē* – “You protected the universe considering it to be your personal gain” is truly revealed by your radiant form itself.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.
