## 5.10.7. Onsudarodu

*oṇsudarōdiruḷumāy ninṟavāṟum uṇmaiyōdinmaiyāy vandu en kaṇ koḷā vagai nī karandennaic ceyginṟana eṇ koḷ sindaiyuḷ naiginṟēn en kariya māṇikkamē! en kaṇgatkut tiṇ koḷḷa oru nāḷ aruḷāy un tiruvuruvē*

**Пословный перевод:**

uṇmaiyōdu – being present with the form which is shining in my heart; inmaiyāy – non-existing due to not being seen physically in a shining manner; vandu – came; oṇ – shining; sudarōdu – with radiance; iruḷumāy – as darkness; ninṟa – stood; āṟum – ways; en – my; kaṇ – eyes; koḷā vagai – to not enjoy you; karandu – hiding inside; nī – you; ennai – me; seyginṟana – these actions which you perform; eṇ – to think; koḷ – having; sindaiyuḷ – with heart; naiginṟēn – becoming weak; en – being the cause for my such weakened state; kariya māṇikkamē – Oh one who is having a form which resembles a blue gem!; un – your; tiru – apt and enjoyable; uru – form; en – my; kaṇgatku – for the eyes; tiṇ – having firmness; koḷḷa – to see; oru nāḷ – once; aruḷāy – kindly bless me

**Перевод:**

**Your ways of being present with the form which is shining in my heart and being non-existing due to not being seen physically in a shining manner, you came, stood as shining radiance with darkness; I am becoming weak as my heart thinks about your actions such as your hiding inside me to make my eyes not enjoy you; oh  one who is having a form which resembles a blue gem which is the cause for my such weakened state! you should kindly bless me to have firmness in my eyes to see your apt and enjoyable form once.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the seventh pāsuram, āḻvār says “Instead of becoming weak by only having internal experience and not seeing you physically, kindly bless me to see you to sustain myself and enjoy you”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. oṇsudarōdiruḷumāy ninṟavāṟum uṇmaiyōdinmaiyāy vandu en kaṇ koḷā vagai nī karandennaic ceyginṟana eṇ koḷ sindaiyuḷ naiginṟēn en kariya māṇikkamē! en kaṇgatkut tiṇ koḷḷa oru nāḷ aruḷāy un tiruvuruvē*

- *uṇmaiyōdinmaiyāy vandu – oṇsudarōdu iruḷumāy ninṟa āṟum* – Being truthful towards me, he would remain in my heart in a radiant manner; in my desire to see him externally, he remains non-existing and dark. Alternative explanation – he manifests all his aspects fully for his devotees and remains radiant and measurable by them; for others, he hides all his aspects and make them believe that he does not exist and remains dark to them. For the devotees he remains present with shining radiance and for the others he remains non-existing and dark.
- *vandu en kaṇ koḷā vagai nī karandu ennaic ceyginṟana* – Furthermore, the distinguished interactions of yours towards me. I am neither enjoying your radiance nor seeing the dark, but suffering in the middle. He \[āḻvār\] is neither in the group of muktars (liberated souls in paramapadam) nor in the group of samsāris (bound souls in this material realm), he is standing outside both the groups. Your tormenting of me by entering my heart and yet hiding from my eyes.
- *eṇ koḷ sindaiyuḷ naiginṟēn* – I am not satisfied with what I have attained \[the internal experience\]. And I am unable to see the means to attain the remaining aspects \[physical vision\] with what I already have. I become weak as soon as I start thinking about you.
- *en kariya māṇikkamē* – You revealed your beautiful form so that I don’t waste my time using my eyes in worldly matters.
- *en kariya māṇikkamē* – Did you think that those who separated from this form of yours can survive?
- *en kaṇgatku* – You know the thirst of my eyes; my eyes won’t remain happy, even if I experienced you – they have to see for themselves. They cannot be given something else to keep them happy.
- *tiṇ koḷḷa* – If you are saying “I have given you internal experience which is as good as physical experience”, I will not accept it.
- *tiṇ koḷḷa* – I have to firmly see you, and cannot just accept dream-like internal experience. When [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) asked “is that possible?”, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says “you remained always physically visible to some \[for nityasūris (eternally free souls in paramapadam) and muktātmās (liberated souls), as said in viṣṇu sūktam ‘*sadā paśyanti sūraya:’*\]”.
- *oru nāḷ aruḷāy* – He is not saying that it is sufficient to see emperumān once, but just saying how great his thirst to see [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is; just as a very thirsty person would say “let me wet my tongue with a little bit of water”. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying “once I attain you, I will let you go subsequently”.
- *un tiru uruvē* – Are these \[forms, qualities etc\] for your sake to carefully hide them! As said in jitantē stōtram “*na tē rūpam … bhaktānām*” (your form, qualities etc are not for your sake but for your devotees only).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.10.8. Tiru uruvu

*tiru uruvu kidanda āṟum koppūḻ sendāmarai mēl tisaimugan karu uḷ vīṟṟirundu padaittitta karumangaḷum poruvil un tani nāyagam avai kētkundōṟum en nenjam ninṟu nekku aruvi sōṟum kaṇṇīr en seygēn adiyēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tiru – beautiful; uruvu – divine form; kidanda āṟum – the way he reclines; koppūḻ – in the navel in such form; sem – reddish; tāmarai mēl – on lotus flower; tisai mugan – four headed brahmā; karu uḷ – inside the womb; vīṟṟu – being seated as the distinguished antarātmā (super-soul); irundu – present; padaittitta – (you) created (the universe to make it appear as “brahmā created it”); karumangaḷum – activities; poru – opponent; il – not having; un – your; tani nāyagam – highlighting your distinct supremacy; avai – those; kētkum tōṟum – every time I hear (through pramāṇam (authentic texts)); en – my; nenjam – heart; ninṟu – remaining focussed; nekku – loosened up; kaṇṇīr – tears; aruvi – like waterfall; sōrum – falling; adiyēn – I (who am totally subservient to you); en – what; seygēn – shall do?

**Перевод:**

**The way you are reclining with a beautiful divine form, and how four headed brahmā is seated in the lotus flower which is sprouting from your navel and how you are present inside such brahmā \[having him as the womb\] and created; every time I hear about such activities of yours, who is not having a matching opponent, and those activities which are highlighting your distinct supremacy, my heart remaining focussed, loosens up and tears are falling like waterfall; what shall I do?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the eighth pāsuram, āḻvār says “ēverytime I hear your qualities and activities, I am becoming weakened; what shall I do?”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. tiru uruvu kidanda āṟum koppūḻ sendāmarai mēl tisaimugan karu uḷ vīṟṟirundu padaittitta karumangaḷum poruvil un tani nāyagam avai kētkundōṟum en nenjam ninṟu nekku aruvi sōṟum kaṇṇīr en seygēn adiyēnē*

- *tiru uruvu kidanda āṟum* – How he is reclining and resting in the causal ocean with a radiant/attractive form.
- *koppūḻ* … – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) rested in the causal ocean with the intent to engage in creation and when the time was ripe, he created everything. He himself directly created up to the aṇḍams (universes) and created brahmā in the lotus in his divine navel, being the support for brahmā and subsequently he had brahmā as his support \[that is, being the antaryāmi, in-dwelling super soul of brahmā\], engaged in variegated creation \[creation of various entities such as celestial beings, humans, animals and plants, land masses, oceans etc\]. All these aspects overwhelm [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/).
- *tisai mugan karu uḷ vīṟṟu irundu* – Assuming the form of caturmukha (four-headed) brahmā. As said in viṣṇu darmam “*sruśtim tata:kariśyāmi tvāmāviśya*” (Oh brahmā! I will enter you and perform creation), and as said in nārāyaṇīyam nāmanirvacana adyāyam “*ētau dvau vibhutaśrēśtau*” (these two namely brahmā and rudra are best among dēvatās), as said in “having this particular throne” \[[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) assumed the form of brahmā to engage in creation\].
- *vīṟṟu irundu* – Being seated manifesting his greatness due to his opulence. Like a precious gem in a golden box.
- *padaittitta karumangaḷum* – The activities which were done by emperumān.
- *poruvil …* – Every time I hear about the activities which reveal the opulence of yours, who are matchless and distinguished, my heart loosens like a mountain loosening and tears flow like waterfall from my eyes.
- *en seygēn adiyēnē* – Are you letting me, a paratantran (one who is totally existing for you) to fulfil my own desires? ōr can I engage in any other activity to sustain myself? What shall I do?

## 5.10.9. Adiyai munrai

*adiyai mūnṟai iranda āṟum angē ninṟāḻ kadalum maṇṇum viṇṇum mudiya īradiyāl mudittuk koṇḍa mukkiyamum nodiyumāṟavai kētkum tōṟum en nenjam ninṟanakkē karaindugum kodiya val vinaiyēn unnai enṟu kol kūduvadē?*

**Пословный перевод:**

mūnṟu – three; adiyai – feet; iranda – humbly requested so that he \[mahābali\] cannot refuse; āṟum – way; angu – in that yajñavātam (the place of fire sacrifice) where he agreed and promised on water; ninṟē – standing; āḻ – deep; kadalum – oceans; maṇṇum – the earth which has seven islands; viṇṇum – the sky going up to brahma lōkam (the abode of brahmā); īradiyāl – with two feet; mudiya – to cover; mudittuk koṇḍa – fulfilled his desire; mukkiyamum – predominance; avai – those; nodiyum – to say; āṟu – way; kētkum tōṟum – every time I hear; en – my; nenjam – heart; nin tanakkē – Being avāpta samasta kāma (one how is having no unfulfilled desires), you became a seeker for the sake of your devotee – your qualities such as simplicity; karaindu – melt; ugum – flowing away; val – too strong to be atoned; kodiya – which cannot be wished away other than by experiencing; vinaiyēn – me who am having sin in the form of love (to not become broken), to steady myself and enjoy you; unnai – you; enṟu kol – when; kūduvadu – will I reach?

**Перевод:**

**The way emperumān humbly requested three feet \[of land\] so that he \[mahābali\] cannot refuse; his predominance of standing right in that yajñavātam and fulfilling his desire by covering with two feet the deep oceans, the earth which has seven islands and the sky going up to brahma lōkam; every time I hear anyone telling those aspects, my heart is melting and flowing away towards the qualities such as simplicity of yours, who are avāpta samasta kāma yet became a seeker for the sake of your devotee. When will I, who am having very strong unatonable sin in the form of love (to not become broken), reach you to steady myself and enjoy you?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the ninth pāsuram, āḻvār says “I have become very weak thinking about your incarnation of trivikrama. When will I sustain myself and enjoy you?”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. adiyai mūnṟai iranda āṟum angē ninṟāḻ kadalum maṇṇum viṇṇum mudiya īradiyāl mudittuk koṇḍa mukkiyamum nodiyumāṟavai kētkum tōṟum en nenjam ninṟanakkē karaindugum kodiya val vinaiyēn unnai enṟu kol kūduvadē?*

- *adiyai mūnṟai iranda āṟum* – Though these (worldly entities) do not pray for your mercy, not only you show your care towards them, you also ensure that the strong do not trouble the weak.
- *adiyai mūnṟai iranda āṟum* – Instead of directly attacking mahābali, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) prayed for three feet. Had emperumān only prayed for two feet, he could not have imprisoned mahābali \[The third step was placed on the head of mahābali to imprison him\].
- *angē ninṟu* – If he stepped away from the hermitage where the fire sacrifice was happening, some one could blame him “he cheated” \[hence, he scaled the worlds from right there\].
- *āḻ kadal …* – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) started taking the first step to melt [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s heart. He scaled the earth and the sky in his two steps and covered them all.
- *mukkiyamum* – Greatness (predominance). The greatness acquired due to cheating \[others\] for the sake of his devotees. Alternative explanation – the greatness of having everything other than himself under his divine feet.
- *nodiyumāṟu …* – nodidal – solludal (speaking). The great incident of trivikrama incarnation is narrated by great sages such as vyāsa et al – everytime I hear the way they explain it. I don’t need to speak about it \[just hearing is sufficient to melt me\].
- *en nenjam nin tanakkē karaindugum* – I am neither having generosity like mahābali nor ruling the worlds like indra; but my mind is becoming very weak towards you.
- *kodiya val vinaiyēn* – As said in śrīviṣṇu darmam mangalyastavam “*yannāma sankīrtanatō mahābayāt vimōkśamāpnōti*” (On reciting whose names, one becomes freed from great fear), while it is said that chanting of the divine names will relieve one from great sins, I am such a great sinner that, the same \[chanting of the divine names\] is causing my weakness.
- *unnai enṟu kol kūduvadē* – When will I sustain myself and enjoy you? When I reach you to enjoy you?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 5.10.10. Kudi nirai

*kūdi nīraik kadainda āṟum amudam dēvar uṇṇa asurarai vīdum vaṇṇangaḷē seydu pōna vittagamum ūdu pukkenadāviyai urukki uṇḍiduginṟa nin tannai nādum vaṇṇam sollāy naccu nāgaṇaiyānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kūdi – being together with dēvas (celestial persons) and asuras (demoniac persons); nīrai – making arrangements such as mortar, rope and base to churn the fluid in the milky ocean; kadainda – churned; āṟum – way; amudam – the amrutam (nectar) which appeared there; dēvar – dēvas; uṇṇa – to drink; asurarai – demons; vīdum – driving away; vaṇṇangaḷ – assuming the beautiful form of a damsel etc; seydu pōna – performed; vittagamum – amazing aspects; ūdu – inside; pukku – entered; enadu – my; āviyai – ātmā; urukki – melting to become fluid; uṇḍiduginṟa – consumed; nanju – hurdles for the experience; nāgam – with tiruvanantāḻvān (ādiśēśan); aṇaiyānē – one who is eternally together; nin tannai – you; nādum – enjoying eternally; vaṇṇam – way; sollāy – mercifully tell

**Перевод:**

**You remained together with dēvas and asuras, made arrangements such as mortar, rope and base to churn the fluid in the milky ocean and churned the ocean; the amazing aspects of your assuming the beautiful form of a damsel to let the dēvas drink the amrutam which appeared there and driving away the asuras; these amazing aspects entered inside my heart and melted my ātmā to become fluid and consumed it \[the ātmā\]. Oh one who is eternally together with tiruvanantāḻvān who can destroy the hurdles for my experience with you! Mercifully tell me the way to enjoy you eternally.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the tenth pāsuram, āḻvār prays to emperumān saying “I become weakened thinking about your amusing activity of churning the ocean; you should let me know the way to sustain myself and enjoy you”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. kūdi nīraik kadainda āṟum amudam dēvar uṇṇa asurarai vīdum vaṇṇangaḷē seydu pōna vittagamum ūdu pukkenadāviyai urukki uṇḍiduginṟa nin tannai nādum vaṇṇam sollāy naccu nāgaṇaiyānē*

- *kūdi nīraik kadainda āṟum* – The way [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) brought dēvas and asuras together telling them “we will divide the nectar amongst ourselves and consume it”. Only by churning the ocean, emperumān melted his heart.
- *amudam dēvar uṇṇa …* – When the result was to be reaped, emperumān fed the nectar to the dēvas and made the asuras ignore the nectar saying “throw that nectar to dogs \[with disregard\]”, by assuming a divine damsel form and have them \[asuras\] chasing that form – such amazing acts of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/). śrīviṣṇu purāṇam “*māyayā mōhayitvā tān viṣṇus strī rūpamāstita:*” (viṣṇu mesmerized the asuras with his māyā by assuming the form of a damsel). periya tirumoḻi 2.6.1 “*vānavaraip peṇṇāgi amudūttum perumānār*” (the great lord who assumed the form of a damsel to feed the nectar to the dēvas). By the way he churned the ocean and his other amazing acts.
- *ūdu pukku* – Instead of just being at the outer layer, entering into the inner most layer (heart).
- *enadu āviyai* – The ātmā which is explained as in [śrī bhagavat gītā 2.24](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/2-24/) “*accēdya: … adāhya*:” (cannot be cut, burnt).
- *urukki uṇḍiduginṟa nin tannai* – You who melted me to become fluid and finished me. I became weakened thinking about your auspicious qualities, wondering “why is the puruśōttama (best among men) doing like this?”. You should tell me a good means to sustain myself and enjoy you. When [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) asks “Can I sustain you?”, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) responds – Have you not let ādiśēśan (parambhōgi – great snake, great enjoyer) sustain and enjoy you? Similarly, you should mercifully let me also sustain and enjoy you.

## 5.10.11. Naganai misai

*nāgaṇai misai nampirān saraṇē saraṇ namakkenṟu nādoṟum ēka sindaiyanāyk kurugūrc catakōpan māṟan āga nūṟṟavandādi āyirattuḷ ivaiyum ōr pattum vallār māga vaikundattu magiḻveyduvar vaigalumē*

**Пословный перевод:**

nāgaṇai misai – resting on \[the lap of\] tiruvanantāḻvān (ādiśēśan); nam – our; pirān – lord; saraṇē – caraṇ (divine feet) only; saraṇ – śaraṇam, upāyam (means); namakku – for us; enṟu – that; nāḷ toṟum – always; ēka sindaiyanāy – having the desire in his mind; kurugūrc catakōpan māṟan – nammāḻvār \[the leader of āḻvārtirunagari\]; āga – to survive; nūṟṟa – mercifully spoke; andādi – in the \[poetic\] form of antādi \[ending of one pāsuram connecting with the beginning of the next pāsuram\]; āyirattuḷ – among the thousand pāsurams; ōr – distinguished; ivai – these; pattum – ten pāsurams; vallār – those who can practice; māgam – the great spiritual sky; vaigundattu – in śrīvaikuṇṭam; vaigalum – forever; magiḻvu eyduvar – will remain blissfully

**Перевод:**

**nammāḻvār always having the desire in his mind that only the divine feet of our lord who is resting on tiruvanantāḻvān are our upāyam and mercifully spoke these distinguished ten pāsurams among the thousand pāsurams in the form of antādi. Those who can practice this decad will forever remain blissfully in the great spiritual sky, śrīvaikuṇṭam.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the end, āḻvār says “Those who learn this decad will reach śrīvaikuṇṭam and will eternally enjoy emperumān there”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. nāgaṇai misai nampirān saraṇē saraṇ namakkenṟu nādoṟum ēka sindaiyanāyk kurugūrc catakōpan māṟan āga nūṟṟavandādi āyirattuḷ ivaiyum ōr pattum vallār māga vaikundattu magiḻveyduvar vaigalumē*

- *nāgaṇai …* – That, the divine feet of sarvēśvaran who is having tiruvanantāḻvān as his bed, are the means for us. Since anantaśāyitvam (resting on ādiśēśan) is a characteristic of the supreme lord, here [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) indicates that the supreme lord is the refuge (Here, it can be said that ādiśēśan’s puruśakāratvam (being the recommending authority) is highlighted \[highlighted explicitly in 24000 padi\]). Only those who are part of her ([śrī mahālakśmi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/)‘s) entourage, can do puruśakāram when [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) remains the upāyam. The bed (ādiśēśan) is available in the anta:puram (private quarters) \[where śrī mahālakśmi resides\].
- *nam pirān* – One who is the benefactor for his devotees.
- *saraṇē saraṇ enṟu* – \[caraṇē śaraṇ\] By the avatāraṇam (exclusivity – “*E*” in saraṇē), upāya nairapēkśyam (bhagavān not accepting any one/thing else as means) is explained. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s nature is such that even when tormented by materialistic sufferings, he will never give up the core principle. Not engaging in any other means is explained as mahāviśvāsam (unflinching faith). With this, “*ēka*” word \[of śrī gītā caramaślōkam\] is explained.
- *nāḷ toṟum ēka sindaiyānāy* – Eliminating other thoughts, having a singularly focussed mind. Those who go in search of wealth, remain faithful on a ship for four years, ten years etc \[in those days, merchants travelled in ships for long duration\], and if we look at the benefit that is received \[that is, kainkaryam to bhagavān\], should we not have as much faith \[in bhagavān\]? The true nature \[of a jīvātmā\] is to remain faithful even when tormented by worldly pains which is natural for this material world.
- *kurugūrc catakōpan māṟan* – His \[[āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s\] birth \[in [āḻvārtirunagari](http://azhwarthirunagari.koyil.org/)\] is the root cause for all his firm faith.
- *āga nūṟṟu andādi* – Those who can recite and practice this decad which was recited by [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) to sustain himself.
- *māga …* – in śrīvaikuṇṭam which is known as paramākāśam.
- *vaigalum – magiḻvu eyduvar* – Will eternally enjoy forever. Leaving behind the samsāram (material realm) where one needs to pray to have continuous experience, will reach paramapadam where there is no break for enjoying bhagavān.

## Sixth Centum

## 6.1 Vaigal pungalivay

## 6.1.1. Vaigal pungalivay

*vaigal pūngaḻivāy vandu mēyum kurginangāḷ! sey koḷ sennel uyar tiruvaṇvaṇḍūr uṟaiyum kai koḷ cakkarattu en kani vāyp perumānaik kaṇḍu kaigaḷ kūppic colleer vinaiyāttiyēn kādanmaiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vaigal – always; pū – beautiful; kaḻivāy – in canal close to the ocean; vandu – appearing in front of me; mēyum – grazing; kuruginangāḷ – oh group of storks!; sey – fertile land; koḷ – covering; sen nel – fresh paddy; uyar – growing tall; tiruvaṇvaṇḍūr – in tiruvaṇvaṇḍūr; uṟaiyum – one who is eternally residing; kai – in the hand; koḷ – seated; cakkaram – having the divine chakra; en – attracted me through such beauty and let me enjoy that; kani – \[reddish\] fruit like; vāy – having beautiful lips; perumānai – the paramaśēśi (great lord, who accepted me as his exclusive servitor); kaṇḍu – see; kaigaḷ kūppi – performing the action of a servitor matching his lordship; vinaiyāttiyēn – I who am having the sin which has caused this separation from him, my; kādanmai – great love; solleer – inform

**Перевод:**

**Oh group of storks who are appearing in front of me in the beautiful canal close to the ocean and grazing there! You go and see the paramaśēśi who is eternally residing in tiruvaṇvaṇḍūr, where the fresh paddy grows tall and covers the fertile land, who is having fruit like beautiful lips, who is having the divine chakra seated in his hand and who attracted me through such beauty and let me enjoy that; you perform the action of a servitor matching his lordship; and you inform him about my love, I who am having the sin which has caused this separation from him. For the birds, kaigaḷ kūppudal (joining the palm) means waving their wings. With this, the proximity of gatakas (ācāryas) due to being present in the same place \[as we\] and the activity towards the apt lord are implied.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the first pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki looks at some storks and requests them to go to tiruvaṇvaṇḍūr and inform her state to the emperumān there.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*In the first pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki thinks “emperumān, the lord, who showed his beauty and made me exist exclusively for him, may be focussed on something else due to the richness in tiruvaṇvaṇḍūr”, and sends the storks which were nearby as her messengers.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. vaigal pūngaḻivāy vandu mēyum kurginangāḷ! sey koḷ sennel uyar tiruvaṇvaṇḍūr uṟaiyum kai koḷ cakkarattu en kani vāyp perumānaik kaṇḍu kaigaḷ kūppic colleer vinaiyāttiyēn kādanmaiyē*

- *vaigal* – I am separated \[from [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)\] due to not having you all reaching the compassionate one \[emperumān\]; I am feeling that I can remedy all my loss through you. Unlike emperumān who united once and then separated from me, I am fortunate to be with you always here! How great is your compassion!
- *vaigal* – everyday.
- *pūm kaḻivāy* – In beautiful canal. Also explained as canal with blossomed flowers. You \[storks\] are appearing when the rakśaka (protectors) have discarded me and there is abundance of those entities which harm us \[even enjoyable aspects feel to be harming when in separation\]. Beautiful garden, cool southerly breeze, nice fragrance are all present. Not only emperumān who is separated, is harming, even the place where we are present is harming.
- *vandu* – As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam bāla kāṇḍam 1.58 “*pampā tīrē hanumatā sangata:*” (śrī rāma united with hanumān on the banks of pampā river). Just as you have arrived here when I am at the stage of sending messenger, and just as mother’s appearance will be soothing for a child who lost everything, tiruvadi (hanuman) appeared when śrī rāma was anguishing in separation of sītā. *hanumatā* – It is implying that when śrī rāma was weakened in separation, thinking “who will help us”, he united with the valourous hanuman. *vānarēṇa* – Unlike rāvaṇa who assumed the form of an ascetic to take away sītā and caused the separation, śrī rāma united with hanumān who is honest \[and willing to help, even though he himself had assumed an ascetic form\]. *ha* – riśi (sage vālmeeki) is celebrating the union. He is feeling blissful that they united to enjoy and feeling happy that they found some one who would care for their survival.
- *vandu* – Unlike him to whom I have to send messengers, you have arrived without my invitation. He needs to be awakened for her cause by sending messengers. These storks are similar to those who share the food and bed \[very close friends\] and go as messengers.
- *mēyum* – As said in mahābhāratam udyōga parvam “*gruhē bhuktam aśangitam*” (karṇa tells kriṣṇa – at home, everyone ate without any shyness).
- *kuruginangāḷ* – What a union as said in \[the same ślōkam quoted previously from\] mahābhāratam udyōga parvam “*darśitāni kaḷatrāṇi*” (the wives were shown).
- *vandu mēyum* … – Their nature is similar to those who along with their wives and children visit their natural \[unconditional/close\] relatives and joyfully eat at their place. The task is indicated by “*kuruginangāḷ – kaikūppic colleer*” (Oh storks! Join your palms and inform him). Previous ācārayas \[before [bhattar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/parasara-bhattar/)\] explained this decad saying that in the tenth pāsuram [parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is speaking with praṇaya rōśam (romantic quarrel). bhattar mercifully explained that all pāsurams are explained with praṇaya rōśam.
- *vandu mēyum kuruginangāḷ – kaigaḷ kūppic colleer* – Also, should you keep working to help others \[being in āḻvār’s association\]? Should you not perform your own activities \[like going to [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) and speaking to him on āḻvār’s behalf\]? Should you, who are healthy, not help me, who am weakened due to fasting \[in separation\]?
- *sey koḷ sem nel* – His nature is as said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 5.18.15 “*maturām prāpya gōvinda: katam gōkulam ēśyati\| nagarastrī kalālābamatu śrōtrēṇa pāsyati \|\|*” (How will kriṣṇa return to gōkulam after reaching maturā? He will be listening to honey like sweet songs of the city dwelling damsels”. Will he, who is captivated by the enjoyability of tiruvaṇvaṇḍur, think about us?
- *sey koḷ sem nel* – Just one paddy itself appears to cover the whole field.
- *uyar* – Since there is no limit, the paddy crop grows very tall. It is growing tall to reach the abode \[paramapadam (spiritual realm)\] of those who say as in taittirīya upaniśat “*aham annam*” (I am enjoyed by bhagavān as food).
- *tiruvaṇvaṇḍūr uṟaiyum* – The abode which need not be called out as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 5.10.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/09/thiruvaimozhi-5-10-1-pirandha-arum/) “*seydu pōna māyangaḷum*” (his amazing ways of completing the purpose of his incarnation and returning to his divine radiant abode) \[he is permanently residing in tiruvaṇvaṇḍūr\]. That is – the difference between arcā forms and incarnations.
- *kai koḷ cakkrattu* – Similar to the fresh paddy \[which is a decoration for the field\]. The chakra being the ornament for the hand.
- *en kani vāy* – One who gave his smile as the complete food for me.
- *perumān* – One who sustained my life by showing his lips and accepted me as his servant.
- *kai koḷ cakkarattu en kani vāyp perumān* – Similar to being won over by the multiple rings in the same finger of princes.
- *perumān* – She became fully captivated by his reddish lips and the combination of his hand and chakra, and offered her fully to him.
- *kaṇḍu* – You are going to enjoy the aspects which I desired to enjoy in him. For those who are associated with [parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/), their result is attained even before she attains it. This can be observed in the life of śrī vibhīśaṇa et al \[for example, hanuman who was sent by sugrīva to investigate śrī rāma and lakśmaṇa, got to see them first even before sugrīva could see\].
- *kaigaḷ kūppi* – Don’t consider yourself to be superior thinking about your royal heritage \[of being part of the prapanna kulam (the group of great devotees)\]. He is not the same old person we knew, but he is to be greatly respected. Offer your worships to him. She is of the nature as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 5.3.7](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/06/thiruvaimozhi-5-3-7-valaiyul-agappaduththu/) “*talaiyil vaṇangavum Am kolō*” (can we bow with our head?) and her entourage too is similar to her.
- *solleer* – On seeing you bow in front of him, he will look at your face. At that time you can tell him whatever is needed for you. Though he may have something lacking in his romantic aspects, he will still have his true nature \[of honouring those who worship him\].
- *solleer* – You please tell him everything starting with my bodily paleness \[due to separation\], my anguish etc to make him aware.

When asked “Should I not inform him these in a poem?”,

- *kādanmai solleer* – \[Just inform him my great love\] If you speak about my great love, he will consider that he too has such great love towards me; he remains “if there are two matching entities, the effect of such entities should also be matching \[both [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) and parānguśa nāyaki have equal love towards each other\]”. Like other greatness, the anguish in separation of [parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is greater.
- *vinaiyāttiyēn kādanmai solleer* – If he thinks “this is the distance between my abode and her abode”, I have so much sin that I cannot think the same way “this is the distance between my abode and his abode”. Though emperumān is able to sustain himself in her absence, I have committed sin that makes me unable to sustain in his absence. Also, I did not get the opportunity \[like sītāp pirātti\] to explain my plight to him through a messenger who came from him.
- *vinaiyāttiyēn kādal solleer* – The love of tender-hearted is not the same as that of the hard-hearted; inform him my love which is even greater than that of the tender-hearted. [parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) tells the storks – only due to lack of a messenger he has not arrived yet, if you go and inform him, he will certainly come.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.1.2. Kadal men pedai

*kādal men pedaiyōdu udan mēyum karu nārāy! vēda vēḷvi oli muḻangum taṇ tiruvaṇvaṇḍūr nādan jñālam ellām uṇḍa nam perumānaik kaṇḍu pādam kai toḻudu paṇiyīr adiyēn tiṟamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kādal – due to great love; men – being tender, unable to bear the separation; pedaiyōdu – with the spouse; udan – together; mēyum – grazing; karu – having blackish complexion; nārāy – oh crane!; vēda oli – the tumultuous sound of recital of vēdam; vēḷvi oli – the joyful vaidika rituals; muḻangum – sounding; taṇ – having coolness which will not allow the samsāratāpam (heat of this material realm) to enter; tiruvaṇvaṇḍūr – for tiruvaṇvaṇḍūr; nādan – being the lord; jñālam ellām – all the universe; uṇḍa – his companionship during danger of deluge by placing \[the universe\] in his stomach and protecting; nam – one who revealed to us; perumānai – the great person; kaṇḍu – seeing him to make me see him subsequently; pādam – towards his divine feet; kai toḻudu – performing anjali (joined palms); adiyēn – I who am his servitor, my; tiṟam – situation; paṇiyīr – inform him

**Перевод:**

**Oh black coloured crane who is tender being unable to bear the separation from the spouse and is grazing with the spouse! The great emperumān who is the lord for tiruvaṇvaṇḍūr where the tumultuous sounds of recital of vēdam and the joyful vaiodika rituals are resounding, revealed to us his companionship during danger of deluge by placing \[the universe\] in his stomach and protecting. You see him to make me see him subsequently, performing anjali towards his divine feet, inform him my situation,me who am his servitor. The usage of plural for the cranes implies that parānguśa nāyaki is addressing the crane along with its spouse. paṇiyīr indicates respectful ways of addressing. adiyēn (being a servitor) could also imply parānguśa nāyaki’s servitude towards gataka (ācārya). This implies that the companionship and the beauty of ācārya are desirable.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the second pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki says to some cranes “Please inform my plight to the most compassionate lord of tiruvaṇvaṇḍūr”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, parānguśa nāyaki sends a crane which is with its spouse towards the lord who is the companion during dangerous situations.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Second pāsuram. parānguśa nāyaki prays to a crane “inform my plight to emperumān who has vowed to protect the distressed ones”. kādal men pedaiyōdu udan mēyum karu nārāy! vēda vēḷvi oli muḻangum taṇ tiruvaṇvaṇḍūr nādan jñālam ellām uṇḍa nam perumānaik kaṇḍu pādam kai toḻudu paṇiyīr adiyēn tiṟamē*

- *kādal* … – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is not of the nature that one can wait thinking “those who have gone previously will bring him”; if that is the case, the prapatti (surrender) done previously is sufficient \[i.e., we are supposed to constantly recite dvaya mahā mantram which expresses our surrender towards him. This is due to our great affection towards emperumān\].
- *kādal men pediayōdu udan mēyum karu nārāy* – While sītāp pirātti said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 38.68 “*ūrdvam māsān najīviśyē*” (I will not survive beyond a month), śrī rāma said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 66.10 “*najīvēyam kśaṇamapi*” (I cannot even survive a moment). Unlike those who remain far away and saying for the sake of doing so, we have got those \[the crane couple\]  putting it in practice \[Also, implies that the ācārya makes the union happen unlike [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who just explains it\]. You are fortunate to have not joined hands with sarvajña \[my omniscient lord\]. emperumān will say “when it is inevitable that we will be together, why can’t you handle the separation for now”; these cranes are not intelligent like that.
- *kādal* – Embodiment of love and nothing beyond it \[Here the crane is explained as love itself instead of an entity which is having love\].
- *men pedaiyōdu* – So tender hearted that it cannot even bear/handle the union.
- *udan mēyum karu nārāy* – It is extraneous to explain that it cannot handle the separation when it is said that it cannot even handle the union. Due to that the female crane is roaming around with the male crane.
- *kādal men pedaiyōdu udan mēyum karu nārāy* – There is the male crane which understands the love of the female crane and is together with it \[unlike [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is ignoring me\].
- *udan mēyum* – They are roaming together as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam kiśkintā kāṇḍam 1.88 “*idam mētyam idam svādu*” (this is pure and this is reliśable). When the male crane picks up something with its beak and feeds it to the female crane, the female crane can instantly consume it without checking the same. There is a male crane which feeds the female crane, knowing its heart \[unlike emperumān who ignores me\].
- *udan mēyum karu nārāy* – \[[bhattar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/parasara-bhattar/)‘s view point of all pāsurams in distress\] [parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is trying to find fault in the crane to have her own desire accomplished \[that is, while you are with your spouse, I am suffering in separation\]. Like stopping one from consuming food from a vessel. Hearing her distressed voice, the food will not pass through the throat for the crane.
- *karu nārāy* – Since they are together, the crane is in dark completion without any paleness and is shining. For those who are together, they won’t become pale. Only [parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is pale.
- *vēda vēḷvi oli muḻangum taṇ tiruvaṇvaṇḍūr* – The benefit of their ignorance is explained. That is, they will not be attracted on hearing the vaidika chants and rituals. Her lord remains attracted in such chants and rituals and is hence not coming to her. śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam “*dāna yajña vivāhēśu*” (śrī rāma would be present where righteous charity, fire sacrifices and marriages happen). [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) would be present in yajña (fire sacrifice) at the appropriate places and times to facilitate righteous acts. He would be present there to engage people with honestly earned wealth and to remedy any shortcomings in the rituals. *vivāhēśu* – He will be present in the places of marriage to match the bride and groom, and to reconcile their difference of opinions, and to facilitate the fire sacrifice and complete the event successfully. *samājēśu mahatsuca* – In the great assemblies and festivals. *ca* – he will be present in all divine activities. “*nadrakśyāma: punar jātu*” – We are not seeing him in any of these places. He said “*dārmikam rāmam antarā”* (We have seen the righteous śrī rāmā in these places) – What is the purpose of his presence there? He will eliminate the doubts in the righteous principles and ensure that they are practiced properly. This is śrī rāma’s nature.
- *tiruvaṇvaṇḍūr nādan* – Greatness over “śrīvaikuṇṭanātan” is highlighted. The greatness of tiruvaṇvaṇḍūr nātan is unlike that of śrīvaikuṇṭanātan who remains in paramapadam enjoying fragrant sandal paste while the strong torment the weak. The invigorating town where the chants of the hymns and the fire sacrifices are well heard.
- *jñālam ellām uṇḍa nam perumānaik kaṇḍu* – When he descends with such supremacy, would he also carry along his unhelpful attitude? No, here in tiruvaṇvaṇḍūr, he is the protector and the companion during danger.
- *nam perumānaik kaṇḍu* – Seeing the one who showed his act of protecting during danger and accepted me exclusively.
- *pādam kai toḻudu* – Paying obeisances at the divine feet. [parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) said “*kaigaḷ kūppi*” (joining the palms) in previous pāsuram. Those who are vorśipping cannot simply stand \[they will fall at the divine feet at once\]. Previous ācāryas explain “Praying and not paying obeisances is like strangling one’s neck while he is eating”. [nanjīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nanjiyar/) mercifully explains “Only when I pay obeisances to a respectful śrīvaiṣṇava, would I feel like being relieved from hunger after eating”. Alternative explanation \[bhattar’s view\] – parānguśa nāyaki tells the crane, you go and fall at his divine feet such that your hands hit his divine feet highlighting my praṇaya rōśam (romantic anger)”.
- *paṇiyīr* – She cannot say the angry words to the crane \[ācārya\] as she would say to [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/). So, she is addressing them respectfully.
- *adiyēn* – I am not a servitor to the one who is going to accept me through you but a servitor to you who are going to eliminate my loss and unite me with him as said in [stōtra ratnam 2](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/12/sthothra-rathnam-2/) “*nitya yadīya caraṇau śaraṇam madīyam*” (śrīman nātamunigaḷ’s divine feet are always my refuge).
- *adiyēn tiṟamē* – My situation is not the same as his. You explain my situation to him, and it can last as long as mahābhāratam.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.1.3. Tirangalagi

*tiṟangaḷāgi engum seygaḷ ūduḻal puḷ inangāḷ! siṟanda selvam malgu tiruvaṇvaṇḍūr uṟaiyum kaṟangu cakkarak kaik kani vāyp perumānaik kaṇḍu iṟangi nīr toḻudu paṇiyīr adiyēn idarē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tiṟangaḷāgi – in flocks; engum – everywhere; seygaḷūdu – amidst the fertile fields; uḻal – roaming; puḷḷinangāḷ – Oh flocks of birds!; siṟanda – matching his greatness; selvam – wealth; malgu – existing in abundance; tiruvaṇvaṇḍūr – in tiruvaṇvaṇḍūr; uṟaiyum – eternally residing; kaṟangu – spinning around (due to the joy of experiencing bhagavān and setting out to destroy his enemies); cakkaram – having divine chakra (disc); kai – having divine hand; kani – infinitely enjoyable; vāy – having beautiful lips; perumānai – one who is having supremacy (acquired due to his protective and enjoyable nature); kaṇḍu – seeing; nīr – you; iṟangi – lowering yourself; toḻudu – vorśipping; adiyēn – me who am paratantra (to have my deeds accomplished as per your desire), my; idar – sorrow in separation; paṇiyīr – inform

**Перевод:**

**Oh flocks of birds roaming everywhere amidst the fertile fields in flocks! emperumān, the supreme lord who is having divine chakra which is spinning around in his divine hand and who is having infinitely enjoyable divine lips and who is eternally residing in tiruvaṇvaṇḍūr where abundant wealth matching his greatness exists. Seeing such emperumān there, lower yourself, worship him and inform him the sorrow in separation, of me who am paratantra.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the third pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki sees the flocks and flocks of birds, considers them to be flocking together to fulfil her desire, tells them “Please inform my sorrow to emperumān who is in tiruvaṇvaṇḍūr”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, parānguśa nāyaki sends some birds who are staying together to  emperumān who is greater than all in his protection and enjoyability.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. tiṟangaḷāgi engum seygaḷ ūduḻal puḷ inangāḷ! siṟanda selvam malgu tiruvaṇvaṇḍūr uṟaiyum kaṟangu cakkarak kaik kani vāyp perumānaik kaṇḍu iṟangi nīr toḻudu paṇiyīr adiyēn idarē*

- *tiṟangaḷāgi* – In flocks. [parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is thinking that these cranes are roaming around in flocks to help her. Due to her recollection from [tiruvāimoḻi 2.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/11/thiruvaimozhi-2-1-vayum/) “*vāyum tiraiugaḷum*“, she is thinking that they have all gathered unable to bear her sorrow. There – she was thinking that they were distressed not having fulfilled their own desires. Here – she is thinking that they are distressed for her not having fulfilled her desire. Is this possible? Well, if she is not able to understand “these are birds and really cannot fulfil our task”, then this too is possible.
- *tiṟangaḷāgi engum* – When śrī rāma was in sorrow due to separation from sītā, all the revered devotees (monkeys etc) went to all four directions searching for her. Similarly, here too the cranes are searching for [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/).
- *engum* – They searched everywhere, even in places where there is no scope of finding him. They \[monkeys\] even entered the pit which was self illuminous \[in search of sītā\].
- *uḻal puḷ inangāḷ* – The cranes are struggling just as the monkeys who searched in places where there is no scope of sītā’s presence, not seeing her there and vowing to fast until hanuman’s return. From the time of śrī rāmāvatāram, āḻvār thinks that tiryaks (animals, birds) are those who unite the separated couples.
- *siṟanda …* – It is not his fault. It is the richness of the town which stops from thinking about anyone else.
- *siṟanda selvam malgu* – Very opulent town.
- *tiruvaṇvaṇḍūr uṟaiyum* – Highlighting the difference from avatārams (incarnations) and paramapadam (spiritual realm).
- *siṟanda selvam* – Matching wealth. [parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) thinks – when [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) was with her together, he would say “you are my wealth”, but now having acquired rich wealth, he is not caring for her. By saying tiruvaṇvaṇḍūr, the distinction from paramapadam is highlighted. By saying uṟaiyum (reside eternally), the distinction from avatārams is highlighted. The wealth there made him forget about everything else as said in cāndōjña upaniśat 8.12.3 “*nōpajanam smaran idam śarīram*” ([ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) will not contemplate about the material body after reaching the spiritual realm).
- *kaṟangu cakkarak kai* – śarvēśvaran who is having in his hand, the divine chakra which is spinning around due to the urge in destroying the enemies. Alternative explanation – \[bhattar’s explanation\] [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) smiling with the chakra spinning in his hand with supremacy having captivated her.
- *kani vāyp perumānaik kaṇḍu* – Seeing [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who smiles revealing his internal bliss and captivating me with that. Though he has other wealth, for us there is no wealth other than him. He is praised in periya tirumoḻi 7.7.1 “*tiruvukkum tiruvāgiya selvā*” (Oh wealth of śrī mahālakśmi who is wealth personified herself).
- *iṟangi nīr toḻudu paṇiyīr* – She is telling them to worship him; don’t just stop with vorśipping, but since he is the lord, he will have his ministers with sticks close to him waiting to hit those who don’t fall at his divine feet; so you fall at his divine feet; if you fall at his divine feet, he will feel happy; so you give up your pride and fall at his feet – says [parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 116.3 “*nibruta: praṇata: prahva:*” (that hanuman with joined palms offered obeisances and mentally surrendered).
- *paṇiyīr* – She should address them the way [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) would address them when they arrive there from her. The way everyone else praises emperumān, emperuman praises those who arrive from her. If one respectfully addresses [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) due to his supremacy, there is nothing surprising in bhagavān respectfully addressing her messengers due to his love towards her.
- *adiyēn idar – paṇiyīr* – You have to inform him what he does not know. Had he known, would he have waited for the messengers for me?
- *adiyēn idar* – \[What if he knew?\] While both have similar joy during union, now I am the one in sorrow – so inform him about my suffering.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.1.4. Idaril bogam

*idaril bōgam mūḻgi iṇaindādum mada annangāḷ! vidalil vēda oli muḻangum taṇ tiruvaṇvaṇḍūr kadalin mēnip pirān kaṇṇanai nedumālaik kaṇḍu udalam naindorutti urugum enṟuṇarttuminē*

**Пословный перевод:**

idar – thought/talk about separation; il – not having; bōgam – enjoyment; mūḻgi – immersed; iṇaindu – without separation; ādum – to roam around; madam – obedient towards each other; annagāḷ – Oh swans!; vidal – break; il – not having; vēda oli – chants of vēdam; muḻangum – resounding; taṇ – invigorating; tiruvaṇvaṇḍūr – residing in tiruvaṇvaṇḍūr; kadal – attractive like ocean; mēni – form; pirān – as the one who presents me; kaṇṇanai – being obedient towards me; nedu – covering the limits of such obedience; mālai – the very great lord; kaṇḍu – on seeing; orutti – a unique woman; udalam – her body; naindu – weakened; urugum – melt; enṟu – that; uṇarttumin – inform him

**Перевод:**

**Oh swans who are immersed in enjoyment without any thought/talk about separation, to roam around without separation! emperumān is the one who is residing in the invigorating tiruvaṇvaṇḍūr where resounding chants of vēdam are heard; he is having attractive ocean like form and presents me such form; he is obedient towards me and is the very great lord where his greatness covers the limits of such obedience; on seeing such emperumān, inform him that a unique woman is having her body weakened and is melting \[in separation from him\]. By this, it is implied that the mutual comfort of the gatakas (ācāryas) and their mutual respectful dealings are to be desired \[by us\].**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fourth pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki tells some swans “Tell emperumān who is mercifully residing in tiruvaṇvaṇḍūr that here is a woman who has become weakened seeing him”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, parānguśa nāyaki sends some swans towards emperumān who is very beautiful and is obedient towards his devotees.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. idaril bōgam mūḻgi iṇaindādum mada annangāḷ! vidalil vēda oli muḻangum taṇ tiruvaṇvaṇḍūr kadalin mēnip pirān kaṇṇanai nedumālaik kaṇḍu udalam naindorutti urugum enṟuṇarttuminē*

- *idaril bōgam mūḻgi* – Immersed in the joy of union without any smell of separation. While I do what I do, I am seeing such united couples \[swans\] in this world \[she is amazed that couples remain united unlike she who is separated from her lord\]. She \[sītā\] got separated right in the beginning of her union with [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/). \[sītā’s plight\] If we remain in the palace, we should be answerable to śrī rāma’s parents; they should listen to the concerns of the citizens; so, they looked out for a secluded place in the forest to avoid all these extraneous activities and there came rāvaṇa \[to separate her from him\]; no such worries exist for the swans.
- *idaril bōgam mūḻgi* – They are not suffering my fate of seeking for union and ending up with separation.
- *mūḻgi* – The enjoyment is still unending \[present tense\].
- *iṇaindu ādum mada annangāḷ* – This is unlike the situation where one is enjoying while the other is suffering. Their hearts are so much in sync that one swan’s thought is perfectly followed by the other.
- *mada annangāḷ* – The obedience/humility which is explained for one is applicable for the other too. Usually, obedience/humility is attributed to the female swan only; but here it is explained for both male and female swans, due to the involvement in the union matching for both of them.
- *vidalil vēda oli muḻangum* – This town \[where I am\] is not having recitals of vēdam \[unlike tiruvaṇvaṇḍūr where there is constant recitals of vēdam happening\]. The clan of janaka is where there is no one present to recite vēdam. [śrī bhagavat gītā 3.20](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/3-19-5/) “*karmaṇaiva hi*” (only through karma yōga) \[Even such righteous town has become devoid of chanting of vēdam\].
- *muḻangum* – Do we need any other landmark to identify tiruvaṇvaṇḍūr? Would we not be guided by the resounding chants of vēdam? And aren’t you all vēdamārga anusāri (followers of the path of vēdam)?
- *kadal mēnip pirān* – One who is having invigorating form like that of an ocean, fully presenting it to us for our enjoyment, and further having great love thinking “I have not done anything for them”. Alternative explanation \[[bhattar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/parasara-bhattar/)‘s view\] – initially letting us enjoy his cool form like an obedient person \[manifesting simplicity\] and now being unreachable \[manifesting supremacy\]. Even back then, he did not unite with me for my pleasure, but only to capture me; had he united with me for my pleasure back then, would he not want to do it still?
- *udalam naindu* – Tell him – Don’t wait thinking “She may be affected emotionally; but I will help her before it affects her body”.
- *udalam naindu* – This body is capable of weakening part by part \[as seen in [tiruvāimoḻi 3.8](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/10/thiruvaimozhi-3-8-mudiyane/) “*mudiyānē*“\]. [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) himself will know that [parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) who united with him with that body, cannot sustain in separation with that same body.
- *orutti* – \[not specifically named\] If informed “this doe is hurt being shot in this forest”, the hunter who shot the arrow will know \[similarly, emperumān will know if you just tell him “a woman”\].
- *orutti urugum* – Just inform that he does not have the same emotions like her.
- *uṇarttuminē* – Remind him that he has forgotten her. Those who are unaware \[[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)\] should be made aware. It is the duty of the swan to bring awareness \[emperumān, in hamsāvatāram awakened everyone through vēdam\]; even previously he did that as said in periya tirumoḻi 5.7.3 “*piṟangiruḷ niṟam keda orunāḷ annamāy anṟangarumaṟai payandān*” (emperumān bestowed the great vēdam to eliminate the darkness).
- *orutti urugum enṟu uṇarttuminē* – Inform him that this is the suffering of one woman.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.1.5. Unarttal udal

*uṇarttal ūdal uṇarndu udan mēyum mada annangāḷ! tiṇartta vaṇḍalgaḷ mēl sangu sērum tiruvaṇvaṇḍūr puṇartta pūndaṇ tuḻāy mudi nam perumānaik kaṇḍu puṇartta kaiyinarāy adiyēnukkum pōṟṟuminē*

**Пословный перевод:**

uṇarttal – the difficulty in communicating to the spouse \[after a quarrel\]; ūdal – the suffering in romantic quarrel; uṇarndu – realising; udan – without separating; mēyum – grazing; madam – having attachment towards each other; annangāḷ – oh swans!; tiṇartta – well grown; vaṇḍalgaḷ mēl – on the sand banks; sangu – conces; sērum – reaching; tiruvaṇvaṇḍūr – in tiruvaṇvaṇḍūr; puṇartta – strung; pū – beautiful; taṇ tuḻāy – having fresh divine tuḷasi; mudi – one who is wearing divine crown; nam – our; perumānai – lord; kaṇḍu – on seeing; puṇartta – performing anjali (joining the palms); kaiyinarāy – having hands; adiyēnukkum – on behalf of me who am servitor for you; pōṟṟumin – offer some words in praise of him

**Перевод:**

**Oh swans who are having attachment towards each other, grazing without separating, after realising the difficulty in communicating to the spouse and the suffering in romantic quarrel! Our lord is the one who is wearing divine crown having beautiful fresh divine tuḷāsi strung around it and is residing in tiruvaṇvaṇḍūr where the conces reach the well grown sand banks. On seeing such emperumān,  performing anjali with your hands, on behalf of me who am servitor for you, offer some words in praise of him.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fifth pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki tells some swans “tiruvaṇvaṇḍūr will make those who enter there forget everything else, and so, while you enter there, remember me too”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, parānguśa nāyaki sends some more swans towards the supreme lord who is complete in enjoyability and lordship.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. uṇarttal ūdal uṇarndu udan mēyum mada annangāḷ! tiṇartta vaṇḍalgaḷ mēl sangu sērum tiruvaṇvaṇḍūr puṇartta pūndaṇ tuḻāy mudi nam perumānaik kaṇḍu puṇartta kaiyinarāy adiyēnukkum pōṟṟuminē*

- *uṇarttal* … – ṟealising well the nature of communication between them and romantic quarrels, the swans are roaming together. They are roaming together knowing well the sufferings in separation. Now, the way of enjoyment is in three forms. They are: tamiḻ scholars explained three results in love as said in tirukkuṟaḷ 1109 “*ūdal uṇardal puṇardal ivai kāmam kūdiyār peṟṟa payan*” (romantic quarrel, compromising by sweet talks and reunion are the results obtained in love). In this ūdal is – incidental fights when being united with the spouse. That is as seen in “You bathed without me, you looked at the flower without me, your body is having nice fragrance \[may be due to uniting with some one else\] and so on”. uṇarttal is – sweet talks to resolve the quarrel such as “I bathed just for you”, “I looked at the flower to pick it up for you”, “I decorated myself just for you” and so on. Subsequent to these too is kalavi (puṇardal, reunion). These are seen in her lord too.
- *uṇarttal ūdal uṇarndu udan mēyum* – thinking “who can separate, who can suffer in separation and who can try to compromise”, they roam around without separating. Their philosophy is “Only if one commits a mistake, one needs to try and correct it”.
- *udan mēyum* – They said as in śrī rāmāyaṇam kiśkindā kāṇḍam 1.88 “*idam mētyam idam svādu*” (this is pure and this is reliśable). Among the three viz ūdal, uṇarttal and puṇardal, these swans are only engaged in puṇardal.  They are so close that they eat from the same vessel and will never eat in separation from each other. I did not realise what is coming. That is – when [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) said “this separation will improve our union”, I did not stop him saying “only for those who are capable of handling separation, such desire for enhanced enjoyment can exist”. These swans who lack intelligence are acting smartly, but I who have intelligence \[being blessed by emperumān himself with unblemiśed knowledge\] did not act smartly.
- *mada annangāḷ* – Their forms reveal the fatigue which came about due to enjoyment in union.
- *uṇarttal* … – Should those who are knowledgeable about the future and avoid the separation, not help those who are not knowledgeable and get caught in separation. By this, it is understood that ūdal (romantic quarrel) is present in a subdued manner.
- *tiṇarttal* … – His not coming is not his fault. On raised sand banks. The conces reach the sand banks when the water bothers them.
- *sangu sērum* – This town is so enjoyable that even acētana (nonsentient) objects are so attached to it.
- *sērum* – Not having any other refuge. Reaching the state of no return as said in cāndōjña upaniśat “*na ca punar āvartatē*” (there is no return). The tenderness and coolness make one not to think about anything else.
- *sangu sērum* – The town which retains even those who are not bound by śāstrams \[conces don’t have any knowledge to understand and abide by śāstram\]. The nature of the town which attracts even the veḷḷai \[veḷḷai, white which means both conch and detached persons\].
- *puṇartta …* – On seeing [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is wearing the crown which has the attractive, invigorating tuḷasi which is strung as a garland, and who made me exist exclusively for him. All you need to do is to go and inform me, he has already decorated and is ready to come to me. Alternative explanation \[[bhattar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/parasara-bhattar/)‘s view\] – one who manifests his supremacy of captivating me by wearing garland on his crown.
- *pūm taṇ tuḻāy mudi nam perumānaik kaṇḍu* – On seeing the one who manifests his decoration and supremacy to us.
- *puṇartta kaiyinarāy* – \[In line with [bhattar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/parasara-bhattar/)‘s view\] Instead of waiting to worship him after reaching there, start performing anjali (joining your palms) before reaching there. Perform anjali even while being on the way; otherwise, as said in māhābhāratam sabhā parvam “*avaśā: pratibētirē*” (being emotionally charged, without their knowledge, they performed anjali etc \[persons in the court of dritarāśtra, vorśipped kriṣṇa even after duryōdana stops them from doing so\]), he will consider you also to be like them.
- *adiyēnukkum pōṟṟuminē* – Don’t forget me like he did; after reaching there, do remember me. That is – since that town will captivate all who enter there and engage them in it, there is no reason for you to think about me. It remains as explained in cāndōjña upaniśat 8.12.3 “*nōpajanam smaran idam śarīram*” ([ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) will not contemplate about the material body after reaching the spiritual realm).
- *adiyēnukkum pōṟṟuminē* – You should inform about my purpose too to him.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.1.6. Porri yan iranden

*pōṟṟi yān irandēn punnai mēl uṟai pūm kuyilgāḷ sēṟṟil vāḷai tuḷḷum tiruvaṇvaṇḍūr uṟaiyum āṟṟal āḻi am kai amarar perumānaik kaṇḍu māṟṟam koṇḍaruḷīr maiyal tīrvadoru vaṇṇamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

punnai mēl – on the punnai tree which is green in colour with multi coloured flowers providing nice contrast; uṟai – eternally residing on the tree, like those who hold on to the auspicious abode \[of emperumān\]; pū – having radiant forms due to that; kuyilgāḷ – Oh cuckoos!; pōṟṟi – performing mangaḷāśāsanam (praying for the well-being of your auspicious residing on the tree and your beauty); yān – I who am depending for my life on your words; irandēn – praying as those without any refuge would do; sēṟṟil – being joyful due to living in its natural habitat \[i.e., swamps\]; vāḷai – \[a type of\] fish; tuḷḷum – jumping; tiruvaṇvaṇḍūr – in tiruvaṇvaṇḍūr; uṟaiyum – one who is residing; āṟṟal – very majestic; āḻi – with the divine chakra; am – decorated; kai – divine hand; amarar – ruling over the nityasūris; perumānai – the supreme lord; kaṇḍu – seeing; maiyal – my bewilderment; tīrvadu – the means to eliminate; oru vaṇṇam – in a way; māṟṟam – reply; koṇḍu – bringing; aruḷīr – mercifully give

**Перевод:**

**Oh cuckoos who are eternally residing on the punnai tree which is green in colour with multi coloured flowers providing nice contrast, like those who hold on to the auspicious abode and are having radiant forms due to that! I, who am depending for my life on your words, am performing mangaḷāśāsanam and praying as those without any refuge would do; seeing emperumān who is residing in tiruvaṇvaṇḍūr, where fish are joyfully jumping due to living in its natural habitat, and who is having divine hand decorated with the very majestic chakra; seeing that supreme lord who is ruling over the nityasūris, bring the reply message from him with the means to eliminate my bewilderment and mercifully give \[that to me\]. āṟṟal implies peace and honour. In this, the sweet speech and deep meanings in such speech of the gatakas (ācāryas) are seen.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the sixth pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki tells some cuckoos “Mercifully go to tiruvaṇvaṇḍūr, see the emperumān there, inform him my state, bring a return message from him and eliminate my bewilderment”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, parānguśa nāyaki sends some cuckoos to emperumān who is enjoyed by nityasūris due to his great enjoyability.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. pōṟṟi yān irandēn punnai mēl uṟai pūm kuyilgāḷ sēṟṟil vāḷai tuḷḷum tiruvaṇvaṇḍūr uṟaiyum āṟṟal āḻi am kai amarar perumānaik kaṇḍu māṟṟam koṇḍaruḷīr maiyal tīrvadoru vaṇṇamē*

- *pōṟṟi yān irandēn* – As the vaimānikas (those who travel in the celestial aerial vehicles) remain high in the sky in their vehicles to eliminate the heat of the samsāram, some cuckoos were staying in the punnai tree; [parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is loudly saying “pōṟṟi” to make them hear her cry of sorrow. It appears she is calling out to make them see her face. She also feels that once the cuckoos hear her cry, they cannot avoid helping her anymore.
- *yān* – I who have the greatness to be prayed by him. Usually it is he who sends messenger and prays to others \[as he did in śrī rāmāvatāram etc\].
- *yān irandēn* – Another explanation – as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 31.12 “*sītām uvāca*” (lakśmaṇa spoke towards sītā), I \[parānguśa nāyaki, as a consort of lord\] who am usually prayed to by others to have them recommended to be connected with [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), am now praying here. I am not ordering here, but praying. I am praying since those who pray should be answered and their desires fulfilled.
- *irandēn* – She is hurting their hearts \[by explaining her situation and making them feel bad\].
- *punnai mēl uṟai pūm kuyilgāḷ* – Like those vaimānikas, these cuckoos who stay above the level of humans and which remain radiant due to being together. Sending you as messengers is not righteous \[since I am interfering in your enjoyment\], but I am doing it due to my unbearable sorrows – says [parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/).
- *pōṟṟi* – Just as rāvaṇa interfered when perumāḷ (śrī rāma) and pirātti (sītā) went to the forest to enjoy in a secluded place, it appears that I have arrived to disturb your enjoyment; hopefully there is no suffering for your enjoyment by this \[act of mine\].
- *punnai mēl* – [piḷḷai amudanār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/amudhanar/) asked tiruvirundavaraimārban “How did [bhattar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/parasara-bhattar/) mercifully explain this section?” and he replied “bhattar mercifully explained – parānguśa nāyaki crying out loudly to have her sorrow reach their ears”. amudanār further questions “In neydal (seashore) land, punnai tree will be low lying, does it \[crying out loudly\] make sense?”. tiruvaraimārban went to bhattar and said to him “amudanār asked in this manner”. bhattar mercifully replied “That the punnai tree is tall is established by the tune \[high meter\]; that is – when saying pōṟṟi would you say it meekly or loudly? \[Obviously, it will be recited loudly\]”.
- *sēṟṟil vāḷai tuḷḷum* – The vāḷai fish which would pridefully jump and create slush even in the total deluge like elephant calves. As said in periya tirumoḻi 11.4.1 “*alai kadal nīr kuḻamba agadāda ōdi agal vān urunju mudugil malaigaḷai mīdu koṇḍu varu mīnai*” (matsyāvatāra [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who carries mountains on his back and torments the ocean during the total deluge), the abode where both [cētanas (sentient beings)](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) and [acētanas (nonsentient entities)](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/09/thathva-thrayam-achith-what-is-matter/) are enjoying. I am sending messenger in separation while the entities in this town are enjoying pridefully.
- *āṟṟal āḻi am kaip perumānaik kaṇḍu* – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who does everything for his devotees and yet remains in sorrow thinking “I have not done anything for them”, having the divine chakra which is the tool for their protection in his hand, and the who is manifesting such beautiful combination of his hand and the chakra which was desired to be seen by me, to others who have no such desire. *āṟṟal āḻi* – āṟṟal is explained as an adjective for the divine chakra, that is, the one who is having the divine chakra which is even more merciful than emperumān himself in protecting his devotees, in his hand. Alternative explanation \[[bhattar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/parasara-bhattar/)‘s view\] – āṟṟal is explained as an adjective for emperumān himself, that is, [sarvēśvaran](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) who is not bothered about our separation, who is having the beautiful combination of his hand and the divine chakra.
- *māṟṟam koṇḍu aruḷīr* – Kindly bring a message from him. When asked “How should we bring it?”, she says – you have seen my state, so you find the means to eliminate the problem and tell me that. As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam bāla kāṇḍam 1.78 “*druśtā sītā*” (sītā was seen).
- *maiyal tīrvadu oru vaṇṇam māṟṟam koṇḍu aruḷīr* – Mercifully come here with the words that highlight the means to eliminate my sorrow. \[Explaining the respectful addressing of the cuckoos by saying “aruḷīr”\] Even if I am sītāp pirātti who is sending the messenger, or the messengers are animals, those who are gatakas (connectors) in bhagavat viśayam should only be addressed respectfully in this manner.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.
