## 6.1.7. Oru vannam

*oru vaṇṇam senṟu pukku enakkonṟurai oṇ kiḷiyē seru oṇ pūm poḻil sūḻ sekkar vēlait tiruvaṇvaṇḍūr karu vaṇṇam seyya vāy seyya kaṇ seyya kai seyya kāl seru oṇ cakkaram sangu adaiyāḷam tirundak kaṇḍē*

**Пословный перевод:**

oṇ – having physical beauty which makes you comparable to him; kiḷiyē – Oh parrot!; seru – fighting with each other \[healthy competition\]; oṇ – beautiful; pū – creating flowers; poḻil – garden; sūḻ – surrounded by; sekkar – reddish; vēlai – having periods \[during sun rise and sun set, or having the ocean which appears reddish\]; tiruvaṇvaṇḍūr – in tiruvaṇvaṇḍūr; oru vaṇṇam – in a straight way; senṟu – go; pukku – enter; karu – blackish; vaṇṇam – form; seyya – reddish; vāy – mouth; seyya – reddish; kaṇ – eyes; seyya – reddish; kai – hands; seyya – reddish; kāl – feet; seru – having enmity towards the enemies of those who are engaged in enjoying him; oṇ – having enjoyable form; cakkaram – divine chakra \[disc\]; sangu – śrī pāncajanya \[conch\]; adaiyāḷam – characteristics; tirunda – in front; kaṇḍu – seeing; enakku – on behalf of me who am waiting to see that form; onṟu – a word; urai – please tell

**Перевод:**

**Oh parrot who is having physical beauty which makes you comparable to him! You go in a straight way to tiruvaṇvaṇḍūr which is surrounded by garden which is creating beautiful flowers which compete with each other and enter the town which is having reddish periods \[during sun rise and sun set\]; emperumān is present with the characteristics such as a blackish form and reddish mouth, eyes, hands and feet; he is having the enjoyable divine chakra which is having enmity towards the enemies of those who are engaged in enjoying him and the śrī pāncajanya; seeing him in front of you, please tell a word on behalf of me who am waiting to see that form.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the seventh pāsuram, when the parrots asked parānguśa nāyaki “how can we identify him?”, she explains them his characteristics and tells them “you locate him clearly as per these characteristics and inform him about me on my behalf”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, parānguśa nāyaki sends a parrot towards emperumān who is having exclusively beautiful characteristics.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. oru vaṇṇam senṟu pukku enakkonṟurai oṇ kiḷiyē seru oṇ pūm poḻil sūḻ sekkar vēlait tiruvaṇvaṇḍūr karu vaṇṇam seyya vāy seyya kaṇ seyya kai seyya kāl seru oṇ cakkaram sangu adaiyāḷam tirundak kaṇḍē*

- *oru vaṇṇam senṟu pukku* – Two explanations are mercifully given for this. \[bhattar’s view\] If you go there \[just for your enjoyment\] forgetting my separation, great elders will be present; they will beat you with canes; you have to tolerate that and enter in there. Alternative explanation \[previous ācāryas’ view\] – there are many enjoyable aspects enroute; entering in there instead of getting attracted towards those. śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 19.1 “*satadanta:pura dvāram samatītya*” (sumantra walked through the familiar private quarters which is filled with people). As said in periya tirumadal “*ponniyalumādak kadandu pukku*” (passing through the golden mansions). śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 68.14 “*sarāmsi  ca supullāni nadīśca vimalōdakā: \| nirīkśamāṇā …*” (Focussed on their task they walked through the ponds which have blossomed flowers and the fresh water rivers). *kāryavaśāt jagmu:* – they were walking focussed on their task. Since there is abundance of enjoyment, entering in there without getting attracted in this will be very difficult.
- *enakku* – Am I in a state that you can worry about getting insulted there? As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 6.16 “*ēhi paśya śarīrāṇi*” (riśis to śrī rāma – See our bodies which are botched by the rākśasas) and as in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 17.17 “*nivēdayata mām*” (vibhīśaṇāḻvān telling sugrīva – please inform about me to śrī rāma), [parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is showing her \[weakened\] form. After seeing me, are you interested in the enjoyment or are you worrying about getting insulted there? Can those who are engaged in helping others, worry about such aspects?
- *onṟurai* – You tell one word. Alternative explanation – I am telling this due to my anguish; he is of the nature that it is extraneous to inform him more than once. It is just that he is immersed in the enjoyment there. Once he knows that I am ([parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)) suffering, neither he can enjoy nor he can refuse to come to me.
- *enakku onṟu urai* – You tell one thing about my situation/purpose.
- *oṇ kiḷiyē* – You are similar to him in his appearance, that is, your childishness, sweet talks, reddish mouth, and greenish form; instead of seeing and enjoying you, I am going to lose you as well \[since you too will remain there seeing the enjoyment there\].
- *seru oṇ pūm poḻil sūḻ* – Surrounded by flower garden which causes fights. For the couples there, there is constant suspicion. That is – there will be constant fights between the couples saying “instead of seeing me, you are satisfied in seeing the flower; you plucked the flowers which I was planning to pluck; even before I embraced you, nice fragrance is smelt on your body”. Also explained as the plants rubbing with each other and making flowers blossom as said in periya tirumoḻi 3.9.1 “*salam koṇḍu malar soriyum*” (absorbing the water and giving out the flowers).
- *cekkar vēlait tiruvaṇvaṇḍūr* – Having a reddish shade due to the pollens and colours from the flowers which has fallen on the sand banks. Since it is the seashore, it is explained to be having the sand. All of these imply that the town is having the qualities for enjoyment.
- *karu vaṇṇam* – This is the nature of the form which accepted [parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) exclusively.
- *seyya vāy* – To make the form look extraneous, the divine lips which are ready to say “I am for you”.
- *seyya kaṇ* – The divine eyes which indicates “it is not just said for the sake of it, even internally I feel that way”. The divine eyes are the ones which reveal what is inside. The hands which put such thoughts into action \[by embrace etc\]. The divine feet, where one falls after being captivated with these features.
- *seru oṇ cakkaram sangu* – The divine weapons which protect and nurture such beauty, doubting where it is unnecessary and attacking the enemies by leaving his hands \[chakra\], and being close without ever leaving the hands to protect \[Sanka\]. The divine weapons which mesmerises those who see them as said in periya tirumoḻi 10.10.9 “*innār enṟaṟiyēn*” (I don’t know who he is).
- *adaiyāḷam* – Just like the divine limbs, his divine weapons too are exclusive symbols of him. śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 34.3 “*yāni rāmasya cihnāni lakśmaṇasya ca yānivai*” (I have seen the features of śrī rāma and lakśmaṇa. Listen to me).
- *tirundak kaṇḍē* – Unlike me who is seeing everything through my internal vision, you see them through your external eyes. In bhagavān, the vision is the result \[viṣṇu sūktam – “*sadā paśyanti sūraya:*” (the nityasūris are constantly seeing him)\]. You have got it before me. When engaged in serving sītāp pirātti \[in being the messenger\], he got the result before her. śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 1.13 “*pariśvangō hanumata:*” (śrī rāma embraced hanuman).
- *tirundak kaṇḍē* – To remove all the anguish in seeing my pale complexion \[due to suffering in separation\], you will see the form which remains unchanged in union and separation. It is not just said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 1.2.1 “*sadaikarūpa rūpāya*” (one who is having unchanging divine auspicious form) for the sake of saying \[praising\], but you will practically see the form which manifests such quality.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.1.8. Tirundak kandu

*tirundak kaṇḍu enakkonṟuraiyāy oṇ siṟu pūvāy! serundi jñāḻal magiḻ punnai sūḻ taṇ tiruvaṇvaṇḍūr perundaṇ tāmaraikkaṇ peru nīṇ mudi nāṟṟadandōḷ karundiṇ mām mugil pōl tirumēni adigaḷaiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

oṇ – attractive; siṟu – having a small form as said in “pulan koḷ māṇ” (dwarf which can be captured by the eyes); pūvāy – Oh maina!; serundi jñāḻal magiḻ punnai – by four types of flower-bearing trees; sūḻ – surrounded by; taṇ – invigorating; tiruvaṇvaṇḍūr – in tiruvaṇvaṇḍūr; peru – very broad; taṇ – cool; tamarai – like lotus flower; kaṇ – divine eyes; peru – huge; nīḷ – tall; mudi – having the divine crown; tadam – well rounded; nāl – four; tōḷ – divine shoulders; karu – having dark complexion; tiṇ – remaining very firm instead of fading away eventually; mā mugil pōl – like a great cloud; tirumēni – having a divine form; adigaḷai – the sarvasvāmi (supreme lord of all); tirunda – properly; kaṇḍu – see; enakku – for me who is desiring to know his opinion; onṟu – a message; uraiyāy – bring me

**Перевод:**

**Oh attractive maina who is having a small form as said in “pulan koḷ māṇ“! The sarvasvāmi who is in invigorating tiruvaṇvaṇḍūr which is surrounded by four types of flower-bearing trees, is having very broad, cool lotus like divine eyes, huge and tall divine crown, four well rounded divine shoulders, and is having divine cloud like form which is having dark complexion which remains very firm instead of fading away eventually. You see him properly and bring a message for me who is desiring to know his opinion. jñāḻal – a type of greenish creeper. With this, it is explained that the compact stature of the gatakas (ācāryas) and their presentation of truth as they have seen it \[without any dilution\], are to be enjoyed.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the eighth pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki says to a maina “You see him properly and tell him a message so that if I hear his argument I can give him a proper response”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, parānguśa nāyaki sends a maina towards emperumān who is having the symbols of dominance/supremacy.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. tirundak kaṇḍu enakkonṟuraiyāy oṇ siṟu pūvāy! serundi jñāḻal magiḻ punnai sūḻ taṇ tiruvaṇvaṇḍūr perundaṇ tāmaraikkaṇ peru nīṇ mudi nāṟṟadandōḷ karundiṇ mām mugil pōl tirumēni adigaḷaiyē*

- *tirundak kaṇḍu* – You see him as I have identified him. Don’t just see for yourself, but see that you can explain to others.
- *enakku* – for me who is going to survive hearing your message.
- *onṟu uraiyāy* – You don’t need to tell me everything about him, but just one aspect is sufficient. \[Now\] She is not seeking to enjoy but merely to sustain herself. When said as in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 34.3 “*yāni rāmasya cināni*” (śrī rāma’s features), one cannot avoid saying about everything. Explained as – see him clearly and give me a message. Also explained as – please give me a message for my sake. Thus, by these two explanations, there is no other option than sustaining oneself by hearing ācārya’s words or sustaining by his grace.
- *oṇ siṟu pūvāy* – On seeing your efforts I realise that my request is extraneous! Your action says that you are set out to help others!
- *siṟu pūvāy* – Their compact form is convenient unlike hanuman who had to assume a huge form while crossing the ocean and a small form form while entering the palaces of the enemies in lankā. oṇmai – their attractive beauty.
- *serundi* … – One need not even consider his beautiful features, just the joyful abode is sufficient \[to bind oneself there\]. His non-arrival is not his fault, but is due to the joyful nature of the land.
- *serundi jñāḻal magiḻ punnai sūḻ* – He will come if there is one or two aspects that bind him there; when they surround him from all four directions, how can he come? It appears that each side is having a type of tree.
- *perum taṇ tāmaraik kaṇ* – The invigorating eyes which are broader than those who can enjoy; having well-blossomed form, freshness, coolness, fragrance etc.
- *peru nīḷ mudi* – One who is crowned as the lord for both nitya vibhūti (spiritual realm) and leelā vibhūti (material realm). Also explained as – his lordship of tiruvaṇvaṇḍūr is greater than being the lord of both realms. Alternative explanation – as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 37.108 “*yasya sā janakātmajā*” (for that śrī rāma whom sītā is the consort), the crown which he is wearing after captivating her.
- *peru nīḷ* – great growth.
- *nāl tadam tōḷ* – The shoulders which have expanded like the branches of kalpaka (celestial) tree, on embracing her. The divine shoulders which four in number and well rounded.
- *karum tiṇ …* – His form is similar to a dark, firm and great cloud. Alternative explanation \[[bhattar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/parasara-bhattar/)‘s view\] – a form that resembles a firm, infinitely huge cloud, which is having an invigorating complexion. Only the colour is comparable to the cloud; his hardened heart is his special feature. Only if we find a dark cloud which is also hard-hearted, it can match him ([emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)).
- *tirumēni adigaḷaiyē* – Without having to explain anything else, just on seeing his divine form, he will make one think “he is the lord for everything”. Alternative explanation \[[bhattar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/parasara-bhattar/)‘s view\] – having such divine form, and yet keeping such form for his own enjoyment.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.1.9. Adigal kai toludu

*adigaḷ kai toḻudu alar mēl asaiyum annangāḷ vidivai sangolikkum tiruvaṇvaṇḍūr uṟaiyum kadiya māyan tannaik kaṇṇanai nedumālaik kaṇḍu kodiya val vinaiyēn tiṟam kūṟumin vēṟu koṇḍē*

**Пословный перевод:**

alar mēl – on flower; asaiyum – swaying due to the blowing wind, as those who sleep on a mattress; annangāḷ – Oh swans!; vidivai – highlighting the sunrise; sangu – conch; olikkum – blowing; tiruvaṇvaṇḍūr – in tiruvaṇvaṇḍūr; uṟaiyum – one who resides; kadiya – being firm on his interests overcoming the opponent \[devotees\]; māyan tannai – having amazing activities which capture the opponent; kaṇṇanai – having great obedience towards such opponents who were captured; nedu mālai – having great attachment which is the cause for his such actions; kaṇḍu – seeing him humbly instead of manifesting your supremacy; adigaḷ – towards his divine feet; kai toḻudu – engaging in devotional activities; kodiya – very pitiable; val – very strong; vinaiyēn – I who am having sin in the form of this love \[towards him\], my; tiṟam – in my matter; vēṟu koṇḍu – in a private location; kūṟumin – inform him

**Перевод:**

**Oh swans who are swaying on the flower due to the blowing wind, as those who sleep on a mattress! emperumān who is firm on his interests overcoming the opponent \[devotees\], having amazing activities which capture the opponent and having great attachment which is the cause for his such actions, is in tiruvaṇvaṇḍūr where the sunrise is highlighted by the blowing conch; on seeing him, humbly engage in devotional activities towards his divine feet instead of manifesting your supremacy, in a private location, inform him about me who am having very pitiable and strong sin in the form of this love. By this, the greatness of the birth of gatakas (ācāryas) and their pride due to the distinguished union with emperumān are implied.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the ninth pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki tells some swans “When you reach tiruvaṇvaṇḍūr and see him, instead of informing my state to him in public, do it in private”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, parānguśa nāyaki sends some distinguished swans towards emperumān who is very attached to his devotees.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Ninth pāsuram. parānguśa nāyaki tells some swans “You inform him my state in private with the presence of the one \[śrī mahālakśmi\] who says ‘na kaścinnāparādyati‘ (who does not commit mistakes?)”. adigaḷ kai toḻudu alar mēl asaiyum annangāḷ vidivai sangolikkum tiruvaṇvaṇḍūr uṟaiyum kadiya māyan tannaik kaṇṇanai nedumālaik kaṇḍu kodiya val vinaiyēn tiṟam kūṟumin vēṟu koṇḍē*

- *adigaḷ kai toḻudu* – Worśipping his lotus feet with the hands. Performing service which he cannot refuse.
- *adigaḷ kai toḻudu – kūṟumin* – Inform him so that both you and him are focussed on the subject instead of looking elsewhere. So what if he delayed his arrival, he will not become someone else. He may be little bit careless due to the romantic quarrel, but there is no lacking in his natural compassion. That will remain in him forever.
- *alar mēl asaiyum annangāḷ* – While I am longing for the flower \[from [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)\], does it fit for you to enjoy staying on the flower? While I am suffering staying on the ground, will you derive pleasure on the flower? Only if you unite me with emperumān on his flower like soft mattress, you will have real joy.
- *alar mēl asaiyum annangāḷ* – By your deed, he cannot avoid arriving here. You will not be your true self, if you don’t unite us together. This being the case, is it apt for me to suffer like this? Oh swans who are swaying due to being together on the flower!
- *vidivai …* – As you set out to go there, you will hear the sound of the blowing conch. There in tiruvaṇvaṇḍūr, it is unlike here \[here the night is stretching too long and hence there is no sound of conch\], and if it is similar there to here, vouldn’t he have come? vidivai – during every sunrise.
- *vidivai sangolikkum tiruvaṇvaṇḍūr* – In tiruvaṇvaṇḍūr, both day and night are seen. As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam bāla kāṇḍam 77.26 “*rutūn bahūn*” (different seasons), [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is enjoying different aspects matching the different seasons with different tools fitting the grand assembly there; sage vālmeeki could have said “vatsarān” (years) but he said “rutūn” to indicate the variegated enjoyment for different seasons.
- *vidivai sangolikkum* – The abode of [parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is having dawn-less night.
- *tiruvaṇvaṇḍūr uṟaiyum* – He placed me in the place where there is no dawn; and he remains in a place where there is dawn. Where he is, there will be dawn. It is said in iraṇḍām tiruvandādi 81 “*pagal kaṇḍēn nāraṇanaik kaṇḍēn*” (I saw the dawn, and I saw nārāyaṇan).
- *kadiya māyan tannai* – One who has amazing skills in destroying the enemies of his devotees.
- *kaṇṇanai* – one who gives himself to his devotees by being their servitor.
- *nedumālai* – one who has so much love thinking “I have done nothing for my devotees” even after doing so much. Alternative explanation \[bhattar’s view\] – kadiya māyan implies the one who is cruel not to know about the suffering of those who are in separation from him.
- *kaṇṇanai nedumālai* – Humility/obedience is present at times, but supremacy is present at all times. Now, even his assuming of humble form is not done naturally, but only done to hurt me.
- *kodiya val vinaiyēn* – I have committed sins which no one else have committed in this world. The sin of others will be removed by getting close to [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/), but I have committed such a great sin that close proximity to bhagavān ended up tormenting me \[in separation\].
- *tiṟam* – my situation is like mahābhāratam \[so big to explain\].
- *kūṟumin vēṟu koṇḍē* – Don’t tell him in the assembly where he may not hear it, but tell him privately. That is, inform him where he and śrī mahālakśmi, both are present. That is – āḻvār always addresses perumāḷ and pirātti together as seen in tiruvāimoḻi 6.8.10 “*en tirumārvaṟkkennai*” (me who is for my lord who has śrī mahālakśmi in his chest), tiruvāimoḻi 1.4.7 “*en tirumālārkku en piḻaittāḷ*” (What wrong she did towards my lord who is the lord of śrī mahālakśmi) and in tiruvāimoḻi 9.7.6 “*mādarait tam mārvagattē vaittārkku*” (for the one who has [śrī mahālakśmi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/) in his chest).
- *vēṟu koṇḍē – kūṟumin* – As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 15.6 “*sītā samakśam kākutstam*” (lakhmaṇa spoke to śrī rāma, in the presence of sītā), please inform this message in the presence of the one who will make it happen. Inform him where he is along with the one \[śrī mahālakśmi\] who will give him good advice.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.1.10. Veru kondu

*vēṟu koṇḍu ummai yān irandēn veṟi vaṇḍinangāḷ! tēṟu nīrp pambai vadapālait tiruvaṇvaṇḍūr māṟil pōr arakkan madiḷ nīṟeḻac ceṟṟuganda ēṟu sēvaganārkku ennaiyum uḷaḷ enmingaḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

veṟi – as said in “brahamaganda: praviśati” (attaining the fragrance of brahmam), that is, once ātmās become mukta (by reaching paramapadam), they will be decorated with the garland from the divine feet of emperumān, which decorate the nityasūris, you \[beetles\] who are an embodiment of fragrance from the flowers which you enjoy; vaṇḍinangāḷ – oh groups of beetles!; ummai – you; vēṟu koṇḍu – treating distinctly unlike all others; yān – I who am sustaining based on your distinguished nature; irandēn – I am submitting the same prayers which are submitted towards emperumān, who is the apt goal, towards you who will unite me with him; tēṟu – pristine; nīr – having water; pambai – for pampā river; vadapālai – northern bank; tiruvaṇvaṇḍūr – in tiruvaṇvaṇḍūr; māṟu – comparison; il – not having; pōr – having battle; arakkan – rāvaṇa who is having rākśasa (demoniac) birth which causes cruelty in battle; madiḷ – the fort which is built for protection; nīṟ eḻa – to become dust; seṟṟu – destroy; uganda – being joyful due to that and feeling as “krutakrutya” (one who has accomplished the tasks); ēṟu – abundance, irrespective for favourable or unfavourable persons; sēvaganārkku – for the one who is having valour; uḷaḷ – I who am other than the one whom he attained by destroying his enemies; ennaiyum – me; enmingaḷ – tell him

**Перевод:**

**Oh groups of beetles who are an embodiment of fragrance from the flowers which you enjoy as said in “brahamaganda: praviśati” (attaining the fragrance of brahmam), that is, once ātmās become mukta (by reaching paramapadam), they will be decorated with the garland from the divine feet of emperumān which decorates the nityasūris! I who am sustaining based on your distinguished nature, am treating you distinctly unlike all others and submitting the same prayers which are submitted towards emperumān who is the apt goal, towards you who will unite me with him. śrī rāma is in tiruvaṇvaṇḍūr which is on the northern bank of the pampā river which is having pristine water. He destroyed the fort of lankā, which was headed by rāvaṇa who has no comparison in battle and is having rākśasa (demoniac) birth which causes cruelty in battle, to become dust and became joyful due to that and feeling as “krutakrutya” . You tell such śrī rāma, who is having abundance of valour, irrespective of favourable or unfavourable persons, “I who am other than the one whom he attained by destroying his enemies, am still waiting”. With this gataka’s (ācāryas’), the fame acquired by his attachment to bhagavān is revealed. veṟi implies radiance and splendour.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the tenth pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki speaks towards some beetles with anguish due to emperumān forgetting about her – “instead of thinking ‘she is requesting to us as she requested to everyone else’, consider my task as your responsibility and go to emperumān who has destroyed the enemies and protected the devotees, and is remaining fully satisfied; and inform him that I too, who am one amongst those who are to be protected by him, am present to be protected”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, parānguśa nāyaki sends some beetles towards emperumān who is having the ability to eliminate the enemies which is an act in love towards his devotees.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Tenth pāsuram. āḷavandār mercifully explained – parānguśa nāyaki tells some beetles “he will think that I am not even alive, and you tell him that I am alive too”. emperumānār mercifully explained – parānguśa nāyaki tells the beetles “When I am not alive, he too will not be alive; for the one who thinks ‘I have protected all women’ and remains fully satisfied, tell him that I too am part of those who are to be protected and am waiting \[to be protected\]”. vēṟu koṇḍu ummai yān irandēn veṟi vaṇḍinangāḷ! tēṟu nīrp pambai vadapālait tiruvaṇvaṇḍūr māṟil pōr arakkan madiḷ nīṟeḻac ceṟṟuganda ēṟu sēvaganārkku ennaiyum uḷaḷ enmingaḷē*

- *vēṟu koṇḍu* – While śrī rāma \[through sugrīva\] sent the monkey soldiers in all directions, he specially gave tiruvadi (hanuman) his divine ring; similarly I am treating you separately. As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam kiśkindā kāndam “*viśēhśēṇa tu sugrīvō hanūmat artam uktavān*” (sugrīva mahārajar specially informed the message to hanuman).
- *ummai* – You who cannot rest until you complete the task which you were requested to do.
- *nān* – This is similar to how śrī rāma requested sugrīva to help him.
- *yān irandēn* – She is of the nature that he should have come and requested her. He remains obedient towards her. Why should she specifically request these beetles? This is because they are having \[six\] feet and are capable of accomplishing the task patiently; another reason – the beetles don’t have stage fear and can speak freely in an assembly; \[another reason\] beetles are compared as the ideal example for [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) as said in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 1.8.2 “*tēn uṇṇum pōl vaṇḍē pōl pangigaḷ*” (your hair which resemble the honey-drinking beetle \[very dark coloured\]).
- *vēṟu koṇḍu ummai yān irandēn* – Just as our ācāryas have more attachment towards dvayam over the vyāpaka mantrams \[nārāyaṇa mantram, vāsudēva mantram and viṣṇu mantram\]. These beetles too are śadpadam \[six feet/parts – beetles have six feet and dvaya mahā mantram has six parts\].
- *veṟi vandu inangāḷ* – You manifest the mood where you cannot resist helping us. Your body reveals the emotions which you went through in union. veṟi – fragrance. Having fragrance. Your fragrance appears to be the food for you during your journey. You can travel along just smelling your own pleasant bodily fragrance. Since they are referred to as “inangāḷ” (groups), there is no separation for them. [parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) who previously embraced [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is mentioned as “*sarvaganda:*” (the root of all fragrances) has even forgotten that fragrance of emperumān and is amazed about the fragrance of these beetles.
- *tēṟu nīrp pambai* – As soon as you cross the border of this \[my\] town, you will see pristine entities. Where she is, everything is confused \[due to suffering in separation\]. śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 59.5 “*upataptōdakā:nadya:*” (the rivers became very hot). Thinking in this manner, considering “for a person who is anguished, by immersing in water, the heat will be eliminated”, and went to the \[sarayu\] river “would this river help in cooling me down from the heat of separation of śrī rāma?”, only to find out that even the shore is hot. They then checked if the ponds are cool , but even those were hot. *pallavāni sarāmsi ca* – In separation from śrī rāma, everything including trees, vaśiśta etc were suffering. This is how it feels like where [parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is.
- *vadapālait tiruvaṇvaṇḍūr* – In the northern side. āḻvār is able to realise where the town is and where the river is. parānguśa nāyaki is similar to sītāp pirātti who remained in the south side of the ocean \[in lankā\].
- *māṟil …* – It is only due to lack of messenger; there is no specific hurdle \[for [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) to come and rescue me\].
- *māṟil pōr arakkan* – The crook who was treated as an enemy by cakravarati tirumagan (śrī rāma, the son of emperor daśarata), who has incomparable valour. For emperumān who turned rāvaṇa, who had no equal opponent due to the strength of his boons and shoulders and the protective fort he had built around lankā, into dust, and subsequently became joyful.
- *ēṟu sēvaganārkku* – While there is a slight delay \[in his arrival\], we cannot blame him for his valour which was praised even by the enemies as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam bāla kāṇḍam 18.26 “*ratacaryāsu sammata:*” (praised even by the enemies for his skill in driving the chariot etc).
- *ennaiyum uḷaḷ enmingaḷē* – Tell him that there are still some who are suffering. tirumālai āṇḍān explains as heard from [āḷavandār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/alavandhar/) – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) has not arrived thinking “those who are separated from me will not survive”. Inform him that I still exist. [emperumānār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/emperumanar/) mercifully heard that and said – This is fine; yet, in tamiḻ literature, there is a principle called “*inṟiyamaiyāmai*” (total loving dependence on each other and survival of each other based on that); that is, \[in a couple\] one will survive only when the other is surviving; either both will survive or both will perish. Per this principle, as emperumān exists, he is sure to know that [parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is also surviving; hence, inform emperumān who destroyed the enemies \[rāvaṇa et al\] and crowned the favourable ones \[vibhīśaṇa et al\] and feeling accomplished thinking “there is nothing more to do”, that there is still someone remaining to be protected.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.1.11. Min kol

*min koḷ sēr puri nūl kuṟaḷāy agal jñālam koṇḍa van kaḷvan adi mēl kurugūrc catakōpan sonna paṇ koḷ āyirattuḷ ivai pattum tiruvaṇvaṇḍūrkku in koḷ pādal vallār madanar minnidaiyavarkkē*

**Пословный перевод:**

min – splendour; koḷ – having; sēr – matching his divine form and glory; puri nūl – having divine yajñōpavīdam (sacred thread); kuṟaḷāy – as vāmana (dwarf); agal – expansive; jñālam – earth; koṇḍa – having exclusively for himself; van – very strong, to be agreed upon by the one who gives and the people of the world; kaḷvan – having mischief; adi mēl – on the divine feet; kurugūrc catakōpan – nammāḻvār; sonna – mercifully spoke; paṇ – tune; koḷ – consuming the words in it; āyirattuḷ – among the thousand pāsurams; tiruvaṇvaṇḍūrkku – for tiruvaṇvaṇḍūr; in – sweetness; koḷ – having; pādal – song; ivai pattum – this decad; vallār – who can practice; min – shining/thin like lightning; idaiyavarkku – those who have waist portion; madanar – desirable

**Перевод:**

**emperumān as vāmana is wearing splendorous, divine yajñōpavīdam which is matching his divine form and glory, possessing the expansive earth exclusively for himself, being mischievous, to be agreed upon by the one who gives and the people of the world. nammāḻvār mercifully spoke on the divine feet of such emperumān these thousand pāsurams where the tune consumes the words. Among those thousand pāsurams, this sweet decad is for tiruvaṇvaṇḍūr. Those who can practice this decad, will be desired by those who have waist portion which is shining/thin like lightning. With this – it is implied that those who are well versed in this decad will bring joy to the bhāgavatas who are radiant due to not surrendering to anyone else as explained in the middle portion of tirumantram.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the end, āḻvār says “Just as lovers are enjoyed by damsels, those who are well versed in this decad will be enjoyed by śrīvaiṣṇavas”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*In the end, āḻvār says “Just as lovers are enjoyed by damsels, those who are well versed in this decad will be enjoyed by sarvēśvaran”. min koḷ sēr puri nūl kuṟaḷāy agal jñālam koṇḍa van kaḷvan adi mēl kurugūrc catakōpan sonna paṇ koḷ āyirattuḷ ivai pattum tiruvaṇvaṇḍūrkku in koḷ pādal vallār madanar minnidaiyavarkkē*

- *min koḷ sēr puri nūl kuṟaḷāy* – As śrī vāmana who is wearing the divine sacred thread which is having a contrast colour with his dark complexion which outshines lightning \[in its shine\]. The reason for speaking about vāmana form is to highlight his humble entry in the vicinity of [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) to offer himself to āḻvār. It is like the precursor for [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s arrival which is said as in iraṇḍām tiruvandādi 81″*pagal kaṇḍēn*” (I saw the dawn) \[his approaching of parānguśa nāyaki in the next decad to pacify her\]. Not having the ability to send a messenger, he himself arrives in a dwarf form feeling fully ashamed of being separated from āḻvār.
- *agal jñālam koṇḍa van kaḷvan adi mēl* – On the divine feet of the greatly mischievous emperumān who grabbed everything from mahābali. It is like the sunrise for “minnidai madavār” (next decad where he comes looking to be accepted by [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)); that is, just as [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) removed the pride of mahābali and took everything from him, he united with parānguśa nāyaki eliminating her pride which she acquired out of romantic quarrel. But, the pride of the enemy is not the same as the pride of a lover. That can be destroyed, but this cannot be destroyed \[since these are intimate interactions\]. When some one manifests anger without any reason \[as in the case of romantic quarrel\], it only increases when the person \[who is the target of the anger\] appears in front. Her anger/pride will not decrease even in his presence.
- *paṇ koḷ āyiram –* As īḻam (an island such as lankā) was filled with bamboo shoots, the tune is abundant \[subduing the words\].
- *in koḷ pādal vallār* – Those who are well versed in these sweet pāsurams. There is no need for palaśruti (result of singing the pāsurams); singing this in itself is the enjoyable result.
- *madanar minnidaiyavarkkē* – Just like lovers are desired by damsels, those who practice this decad are desired by śrīvaiṣṇavas; if this is not the case \[i.e., if it is taken literally\],why would [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) who said in tiruvāimoḻi 6.9.9 “*pala nī kāttip paduppāyō*” (Are you trying to finish me showing various worldly pleasures?) and in tiruvāimoḻi 6.9.8 “*puṟattittu innam keduppāyō*” (are you planning to engage me in worldly pleasures and spoil me further), will now say that they will be enjoyed by women; he is saying that just as damsels enjoy their lovers, they \[those who sing these pāsurams\] will be enjoyed by [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) and śrīvaiṣṇavas; even previously, āḻvār just said “*tāmarai*” (the example) and left out emperumān’s divine feet \[this is explained in tamiḻ grammar as “*muṟṟuvamai*“, where the example is directly highlighted  without the object of the example as in tiruvāimoḻi 6.9.9 “*tāvi vaiyam koṇḍa tadam tāmaraigatku*” (the lotus flower which measured the world)\]; when an example is exactly matching the object of the example, the example itself can be cited \[without the object of the example\]; same principle can be explained using the words “*adu pōla*” (like that) and “*adu tān*” (only that).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.2 Minnidai madavargal

## 6.2.1. Minnidai madavargal

*minnidai madavārgaḷ nin aruḷ sūduvār munbu nān adanjuvan man udai ilangai araṇ kāynda māyavanē! unnudaiya suṇḍāyam nān aṟivan ini adu koṇḍu seyvaden? ennudaiya pandum kaḻalum tandu pōgu nambī!*

**Пословный перевод:**

min – slim like a lightning; idai – due to having waist, not having any shortcoming in beautiful form; madavārgaḷ – having humility etc which are qualities of the soul; nin – your; aruḷ – mercy; sūduvār – having acquired, them; munbu – in presence; nān – I who know your actions towards them; adu – about this act of yours which will make them shy away from you to weaken you; anjuvan – I fear; man udai ilangai arṇ kāynda – For us, is there any one other than you!; māyavanē – Oh such emperumān who is having the mischievous form to deceive the young girls and captivate them!; (adu – that); unnudaiya – your; suṇḍāyam – selfish nature; nān – I who know your thoughts, unlike others; aṟivan – know; ini – now; adu – that; koṇḍu – with; seyvadu – to do; en – is there anything?; nambī – Only I am missing \[he is known to have 16100 wives as said in “padinārām āyiravar dēvimār“, you should go there, so that they don’t hate me); ennudaiya – considered to be owned and possessed by me; pandum – ball; kaḻalum – anklet; tandu – give; pōgu – go

**Перевод:**

**Damsels have lightning like slim waist and hence do not have any shortcoming in beautiful form, and humility etc which are qualities of the soul, and have acquired your mercy. I who know your actions towards them, in their presence, fear about this act of yours which will make them shy away from you, to weaken you. emperumān asks “Haven’t you heard about my previous incarnation where I was an ēkadāra vratan (married and committed to only one wife) and I had eliminated the hurdles \[of the devotees\]?” Oh such emperumān who is having the mischievous form to deceive the young girls and captivate them! Unlike others, I know your thoughts, know your selfish nature. Is there anything to do now with that? While only I am missing \[in the group of persons protected by you\], return the ball and anklet which are considered to be owned and possessed by me, and go. She thought “he will give up the possessions of those who claim ownership”; but emperumān thought “her facing off is due to her overwhelming love, so whatever is related to her, is desirable for me”. Ball is made of red, black and white threads \[prakruti which is made of three qualities – rajō, tamō and satva guṇam\], and anklet has five metal pearls in it \[indicating the five senses\]. He liked them desiring to take ownership of āḻvār‘s body which is made of the three qualities and the five senses; she asked him to return the same indicating that if she does not attain him, she will remain with the previous body and senses \[in this material realm\].**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*First pāsuram. emperumān delayed his arrival not because he can live without parānguśa nāyaki; he arrived quickly, picked up the ball and anklet, stood there being grateful for finding a rare treasure and manifested all the love he has towards her on them. Seeing his emotions, parānguśa nāyaki thinks “he is not doing this for us; he is doing all this thinking that these are the possessions of those he united and separated; why should I not talk to him?” and says “Come on!  These are not owned by those who you think about; they belong to us who are discarded by you; you return these to us and go to them”. He says “ōK! I shall do it”. He said “it appears that a cloud \[ parānguśa nāyaki‘s beautiful upper body\] is held by a lightning \[her slim waist\]”, and parānguśa nāyaki and friends said “minnidai madavārgaḷ” \[reminding emperumān about the other damsels\]. Considering him to be going towards those damsels and saying these things in between to them which is temporary, they said “If you spent too much time for us who don’t like you, those many damsels who like you will torment you greatly. What is their nature? What amazing qualities they have in their physical body and soul!”. minnidai madavārgaḷ nin aruḷ sūduvār munbu nān adanjuvan man udai ilangai araṇ kāynda māyavanē! unnudaiya suṇḍāyam nān aṟivan ini adu koṇḍu seyvaden? ennudaiya pandum kaḻalum tandu pōgu nambī!*

- *minnidai* – Sample for all other qualities of their physical form.
- *madavārgaḷ* – This is a sample for the virtues of the soul such as nāṇam (shyness), madam (humility), accam (fear) and payirppu (modesty). By the plural in madavār – his non-commitment to a single woman is highlighted. They make you bewildered and confuse us with them. She is assuming their beauty by his anguish. Oh my bad! Who made you torment thinking about their waist?
- *minnidai madavārgaḷ* – How amazing that [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is praising the virtues of the physical form and the soul of those who are related to him as śubhāśrayam (auspicious target)! Though she is having romantic anger externally, internally she is happy for him only. Even if one thinks [parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is having hatred in her heart, she can only speak the truth \[about those damsels who are dear to [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)\]; even while speaking out of hatred, sūrpaṇakā could only say as in śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 19.14 “*taruṇau rūpa sampannau*” (youthful, well grown).
- *minnidai madavārgaḷ* – They (parānguśa nāyaki and friends) very well know, when emperumān comes to them, he says “what a beautiful waist! what wonderful qualities you have!” and becomes engrossed in these aspects; so they think “even when he goes to these other damsels, he would tell them the same”. Otherwise, she has not seen the others \[so, she is saying based on assumption\].

When asked “are there those who are like this?”, she says

- *nin aruḷ sūduvār* – Those who are target of your mercy. At this stage, it is apt for her to say “those who are qualified \[greatly fortunate\] to place their feet on your head”; but she would not say that; because that will give him further opportunity; that is, he will take her feet and place them on his head. She who is not even manifesting their relationship \[due to anger\], would not say that. Since it is a union out of attachment \[of [parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) towards [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)\], their thoughts too arise out of emperumān’s desire and since there is no explicit question from emperumān, we have to assume that emperumān raised a question.

\[emperumān asks\] Alright! But they are not here \[why are you speaking about them\]!

- *munbu* – You treat us like them. She is telling “we are not different from them”. While she should have said “Whatever they have, I have them too”, why is she talking about others? [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is waiting to develop the conversation, will not stop with one statement then; he sustains himself by engaging them in conversation.
- *munbu* – \[in front of them\] whatever you do cannot be concealed. We know whatever you did there; similarly whatever you do here will also be known to them. See, for them, there is no external seeking out, like you are doing. Don’t think about them like yourself. Those who united with you and separated from you, will constantly have your image in front of them; they remain as said in periya tiruvandādi 50 “*pirindonṟu nōkkādu tammudaiya pinnē tirinduḻalum sindanaiyār*” (those who are constantly thinking about you and not looking at anything else after getting separated from you). Since they have nothing else to think about, you are their only focus.

[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) said “So what, when you say that you have no relationship with me, how does it bother you?”.

- *nān adu anjuvan* – We are not like you. If you spend a little extra time here and get delayed there, and if they face off from you even for a fraction of a moment, you will be anguished and suffer; I cannot bear that; only you can separate after uniting and can see others suffer; we cannot bear the suffering of others \[emperumān\]. Though we say that we are not related to you, we cannot bear your suffering; when some one falls into a well and cries out for help, should we be related to them to feel sorry for them? She is saying that she cannot tolerate emperumān’s suffering in facing off with the other damsels.

[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) said “I cannot survive without you even for a fraction of a moment; why are you portraying me as a liar and an outsider and speaking like this?”.

- *man udai ilangai araṇ kāynda māyavanē* – She asked “Why! Are you not a liar?”. He asked “With those who engaged with me, whom did I lie to?”; she asked “who did you ever remain truthful to?”; he replied “why are you saying like this? As said in nācciyār tirumoḻi 11.7 ‘*uṇṇādu uṟangādu oru kadalai ūdaṟuttu’* (Without eating and sleeping, cutting through the sea), I remained an ēka dāra vrata (committed to one wife) and suffered; were they all false?”. She replied “Did you do it with full-heart? Did you not do it thinking ‘if I don’t even protect my wife, all other women cannot be captured by me as a group’? Was that not a trick to capture the helpless women?”.
- *man udai ilangai araṇ kāynda*  – Destroyed the town of the crook, where the town by nature instills valour in the citizens – destroying those who lived there; moreover, it is the town which was protected by rāvaṇa like a lion’s den as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 1.39 “*lankām rāvaṇa pālitām*” (lankā which is protected by rāvaṇa) – destroyed such town.
- *man udai* – having mannan (king).
- *māyavan* – One who is having mischievous activities.

[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) said “Alright! You have atleast highlighted one of my truthful acts; will I not repeat the same here to have further goals fulfilled?”, she replied

- *unnudaiya suṇḍāyam nān aṟivan* – You only remain truthful towards those other damsels who are truthful to you; I know all your actions from the beginning; it is sītāp pirātti, the divine daughter of king janaka who remains “whatever you do is truthful”; I know your mischievous activities.

[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) said “How does it matter whether you know about my mischievous acts or not; my task \[of talking to you\] is accomplished”.

- *ini adu koṇḍu seyvadu en* – He said “My task is accomplished”; she replied “there is no benefit of such accomplishment” \[he says “I have made you talk to me”; she says “there is nothing more happening beyond the talk”\].
- *ennudaiya pandum kaḻalum* – He greatly cherished the ball and the anklet which were touched by her. She said “My bad! What are you doing to those ball and anklet, which should be done elsewhere?  They do not belong to those who you think; they are mine”. He said “That is true”; that is what he desires too. As said in mahābhāratam udyōga parvam “*yasyaitē tasya taddanam*” (to the one who owns a person, his property also belongs to the same owner), everything else will become [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s possession subsequently. Now, in the pravēśam (introduction of this decad), there was a passage about [parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) wanting to finish herself; that is seen in this word “*ennudaiya*” (mine). In his presence, there is nothing more devastating than claiming ownership \[of his properties\]; it is said in śrī pāncarātram “*dvayakśarastu bhavēn mrutyu:*” (the two syllable word, mama (mine) leads to death). For [śrī bhagavat gītā 1.1](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/1-1/) “*māmakā pāṇḍavaś caiva*” (my sons and pāṇḍu’s sons), siṟiyāttān’s explanation – He differentiated between his own sons and pāṇḍu’s sons. That led to total devastation. This principle is not just philosophical, but even applicable between lovers; while in union, one should not say “this is mine, this is yours”, which will lead to break in relationships.
- *ennudaiya pandum kaḻalum* – As said in “*ātmatyēvatu gruhṇīyāt*” (one should meditate on paramātmā considering him as self), during meditation upon brahmam, there is so much proximity that jīvātmā and paramātmā appear to be one. When one’s knowledge expands fully, there is no difference between saying “*nān*” (I) or “*adiyēn*” (humble I – servitor).
- *tandu pōgu nambī* – You are delaying here; they would start disliking you without understanding the reason; you better go before that.
- *nambī* – You are not familiar to me and you also remain a leader; so you better go there quickly. periya mudaliyār (āḷavandār) explains “It has been so long since they had been together which makes her say like this \[that she does not even remember him\]”. She said “*ennudaiya pandum kaḻalum*” to make him drop them. And she said “*tandu pōgu*” to indicate that she can survive only with those objects that are liked by him.
- *nambī* – As said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 5.31.17 “*śōdaśastrī sahasrāṇi*” (kriṣṇa is married to sixteen thousand one hundred women), wherever you go, there is no lack of enjoyment for you, but we won’t have you; now, we have to survive by keeping the objects which were touched by you; hence, you give them to us and leave. Like those who say “preserve my life and go”. Knowing well that he will not leave them and go, she says “give them and go” since she knows the inner heart of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

adiyen saraty ramanuja dasan

## 6.2.2. Pogu nambi

*pōgu nambī! un tāmarai purai kaṇṇiṇaiyum sevvāy muṟuvalum āgulangaḷ seyya aḻidaṟkē nōṟṟōmē yām? tōgai mā mayilārgaḷ nin aruḷ sūduvār sevi ōsai vaitteḻa āgaḷ pōga vittuk kuḻal ūdu pōy irundē*

**Пословный перевод:**

nambī – Oh you who are complete!; pōgu – (why are you not leaving even after being asked to go? From our proximity,) go; un – you are smiling at us; your; tāmarai purai – attractive like a lotus flower; kaṇṇiṇaiyum – eyes; sem – reddish; vāy – in your mouth; muṟuvalum – smile (we are not fortunate to see that and be happy); yām – us (hurting our posture); āgulangaḷ – anguish; seyya – manifest; aḻidaṟku – to be finished; nōṟṟōmē – have we not vowed?; tōgai – with expanded feathers; mā – nice; mayilārgaḷ – having hairdo like peacock; nin – your; aruḷ – mercy; sūduvār – don’t they have?; (when asked – are they not absent from here?); ōsai – sound; sevi vaittu – on hearing; eḻa – to rise and arrive; āgaḷ – cows; pōga vittu – driving them far away; pōy – going there; irundu – staying there; kuḻal – flute; ūdu – play

**Перевод:**

**Oh you who are complete! Go. You are smiling at us; your eyes which are attractive like a lotus flower and the smile manifested in your reddish mouth cause us anguish and we have vowed to be finished \[by that\]; are those damsels who have hairdo which is similar to expanded feathers of nice peacock, not having your mercy? You play your flute to make them hear the sound to rise and arrive here. \[Don’t do it directly so everyone can know your intentions\] Drive away the cows far from you, and play the flute after going and staying there. Implies to emperumān that, don’t think “can I not do the same here?”.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, emperumān does not leave even after parānguśa nāyaki tells him to do so; he smiles gently towards her and her mind becomes weakened seeing that; she says “instead of tormenting us, you go near those who are dear to you and wait for them playing your flute”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Second pāsuram. One \[emperumān\] who did not get them to notice him, saw their face; one who could not get them to speak, got them to say “go”; now he is very grateful for that. When she says “go”, he does not just see that word, but knows what is going on in her heart. uynda piḷḷai araiyar sang this quoting perumāḷ tirumoḻi 6.8 “innam en kaiyagattīngu oru nāḷ varudiyēl en sinam tīrvan nānē” (if you still come close to my hands’ reach, I will vent my anger by beating you up), and showing in action, how she will kick him with her feet and push him away with her hands; embār mercifully heard that and showed him how she would turn her face away from him saying “it is not like that; if he gets such beatings, he will be happy since he is praying for her touch since long; so, that is not the meaning”. He mercifully said “Whatever you did staying away from me, she is saying that she will do it in his presence”. It is well known that, as embār was totally detached from worldly pleasures, he would learn the specific details about the aspects/emotions of women from singappirān; piḷḷai uṟangā villi dāsar would say – such embār, while explaining “minnidai madavārgaḷ” decad, would make us wonder “why is this sanyāsi (ascetic) blabbering \[romantic aspects\] like this”.  This is how amazing his interest in matters relating to bhagavān! Those who are engaged in inferior worldly pleasures, remain blissful; what to speak of the emotions of those who are engaged for a long time in emperumān who has incomparable auspicious qualities. embār used to say “in this samsāram where it is rare to find some one who would say ‘come’ (when īśvaran appears in front of them), we have parānguśa nāyaki who says ‘go’ (since he delayed his arrival)”. pōgu nambī! un tāmarai purai kaṇṇiṇaiyum sevvāy muṟuvalum āgulangaḷ seyya aḻidaṟkē nōṟṟōmē yām? tōgai mā mayilārgaḷ nin aruḷ sūduvār sevi ōsai vaitteḻa āgaḷ pōga vittuk kuḻal ūdu pōy irundē*

- *pōgu nambī* – Since [parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is repeating “*pōgu nambī*“, it implies that emperumān would have come closer by a couple of steps.  \[She says\] Come on! I don’t know how many other damsels you have touched; stay away so that your clothes don’t touch me. What will one who comes closer when said “go”, feel when said “don’t touch me”?
- *nambī* – Would you do what is done by lowly people? āren’t you desireless?
- *nambī* – Are you having any shortcoming to be waiting for us like this? Do you need us? [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) try to finish himself in [tiruvāimoḻi 4.8](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/03/thiruvaimozhi-4-8-eralum/) “*ēṟāḷum iṟaiyōnum*“, saying “*uyirināl kuṟaivilam*” (I don’t need this self if not desired by him); but he did not die, since emperumān is existing. In [tiruvāimoḻi 5.4](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/06/thiruvaimozhi-5-3-masaru-sodhi/) “*māsaṟu sōdi*“, āḻvār tried to finish [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) \[i.e., emperumān’s great qualities, by performing madal\]; here, when emperumān arrives, āḻvār says “gō”; I \[nampiḷḷai\] don’t know what is the reason \[āḻvār’s mind is too difficult to understand\]. They are saying “*nambī*” because, he is disqualified to be in that group \[of damsels\]; where one should be humble, it is not apt to manifest one’s supremacy.
- *un tāmarai purai kaṇṇiṇaiyum sevvāy muṟuvalum* – The eyes which had become dry due to not seeing her, cooled down and became fresh on seeing her; the internal bliss led to his joyful smile. This is the change in his form on hearing their nectarean words of rejection. In this samsāram where there is no one inviting him to come, it is even more difficult to tell him to leave \[out of such great love\]. While being in this world where there is no one even to pray to him for worldly benefits, it is rare to see someone who surrendered to him exclusively and go through such emotions due to that.
- *āgulangaḷ seyya* – āgulam means pūsal (romantic quarrel), varuttam (sadness) and du:kham (sorrow). While there are two causes (eyes and smile), all the senses are weakening \[for her\]. For him, it was just one or two features \[in his body\] which changed; but for them, all the features changed. There is a difference between aṇu (miniscule ātmā) melting and vibhu (great paramātmā) melting. [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) asked “you told me that you have nothing to do with me; but you are speaking like those who have emotional attachment with me; this is contradictory! you said ‘*pōgu nambī*‘; but are also saying ‘*āgulangaḷ seyya*‘; what is the reason for this?”. They replied “Oh! Do you think that we are having emotional attachment towards you? Does the candrakāntā stone (moon-stone) melt on seeing the moon due to any emotional attachment? \[it is just unavoidable\] As said in ‘*avaśyamanubhōktavyam*‘ (must be experienced), can we avoid our destiny?”.
- *aḻidaṟkē nōṟṟōmē yām* – This is our nature. Only when iḷaiyaperumāḷ skips going along with you to the forest, can we avoid our destruction. It is said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 40.5 “*sruśtastvam vanavāsāya*” (sumitrā says to lakśmaṇa – “you are given birth to accompany (and serve) śrī rāma in the forest”). nōnbu – that which is carried over from previous birth. Hearing them saying that, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) thinks “such destruction will lead to union” and tells them “While you have changed so much on seeing me, why not continue on further?”; they replied “is that what you are thinking! we are not them \[those other damsels\]! we are destined to finish in this manner!”.
- *yām* – She is saying “there are others who pray to unite with you when separated from you”. He simply stood there manifesting his bliss of hearing them speak for a long time. she thought “our sight is relaxing for him” and turning her face away from him, stepped back; at that time, his heart became attached to her distinguished hairdo.
- *tōgai mā mayilārgaḷ* – she continued to think “he is not going to see our paleness and teary eyes; we cannot stop what he is seeing by divine sanction!”; and that benefited him. Overcoming the destruction caused by his eyes and smile, her survival led to his enjoyment of her. He remained “our goal is completed first” \[also explained as, I got to see their hairdo\]. As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 19.3 “*ūrubhyām udaram cādya bāhubyānca bayōdarau*” (sītāp pirātti sat there with fear covering her body with her hands and thighs \[legs\]), as she covered her body hiding them from the sight of demonic people, here she is covering herself to hide from the sight of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/). That is how much romantic anger she is having.
- *tōgai mā mayilārgaḷ* – As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 15.25 “*neelanāgābayā vēṇyā*” (hair which resembles a dark serpent), he saw her hair which was not cared for; “it does not matter where you are facing; what beautiful hair you have!”. She is very knowledgeable \[and having beautiful hair\]; since he is desirous \[and well aware of the different types of hair\], he praises her hair. Those other girls are so great that they make him think on seeing our hair that it is their hair! They said “When one is separated from his dear consort, he sees her everywhere and in everything”. Those damsels who have nice hairdo which resembles the expanded feathers of a peacock.

[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) asks “is there anyone like that?”, [parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says,

- *nin aruḷ sūduvār* – Those who united with you before and are driving you crazy in their separation. Instead of suffering in separation from them, go and unite with them.

[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) asks “Alright! Until I find the way to get them, let me remain here for some time”; they said “do you know the means to get them? Why don’t you practice what you are an expert at \[using what you have in your hand\]?”; emperumān asks “what is that?”, they reply,

- *sevi ōsai vaitteḻak kuḻalūdu* – They are as said in perumāḷ tirumoḻi 6.9 “*engaḷukkē oru nāḷ vandu ūda un kuḻalinnisai pōdarādē*” (would you not come and play your flute for us at least one day); when you play your flute, they will hear that; then they will come. As the serpents came and entered the sarpa yāgam (fire sacrifice performed by janamējayan to kill all serpents), all the covherd girls would come and fall at your divine feet! They are waiting to hear the sound of your flute; those who are separated from you have all their senses focussed on you only. When you start playing your flute, will anyone stay away as said in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 3.6.1 “*tūvalampuri udaiya tirumāl tūya vāyail kuḻalōsai vaḻiyē kōvalar siṟumiyar iḷam kongai kudugalippa udaluḷ aviḻndengum kāvalum kadandu kayiṟu mālaiyāgi vandu kaviḻndu ninṟanar*” (On hearing the divine flute music of śrīman nārāyaṇan who is having sudarśana chakra in his hand, the young covherd girls broke their barriers, had the protective ropes as garlands, with cherishing youthful bosoms, came running and stood with shyness in front of him)! All of them will come and fall at your feet! So you play your flute – [parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/). He said “That is not my approach; everyone will complain that I called them by playing my flute to unite with those girls as said in perumāḷ tirumoḻi 6.9 ‘*kongu naṟum kuḻalārgaḷōdu kuḻaindu kuḻal inidūdi vandāy’* (mingling with girls who have fragrant, beautiful hair and playing flute); it is well known that I play the flute to invite the girls; so I cannot do that”.

They said “Alright. Listen. We will give you a good idea”.

- *āgaḷ pōga vittu* – Let the cows go away and then play the flute to call them back. She said “Those who don’t know \[your trick\] will think that you are playing the flute to bring the cows back; the girls who know your intention, will reach you. And this also matches your family duty. It is said in tiruvāimoḻi 6.4.2 ‘*tīnguḻal ūdiṟṟum nirai mēyttadum*‘ (Played sweet music in his flute and tended the cattle). So you do that”. [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) thought “Now, we have understood the means to be followed; also got instructed on how to practice the means; now, we won’t miss out on the goal; there is no more shortcoming for us”, and started playing his flute. Now, he does not violate the rules; they said “tōgai mā mayilārgaḷ … sevi ōsai vaitteḻa” (sing to those girls who have beautiful, peacock feather like hairdo); they did not explicitly identify the location! So, he started playing the flute from there itself. They said “If we give you an idea, why are you trying to play it upon us?”.
- *kuḻal ūdu pōyirundē* – You go and play the flute where you have the opportunity to attract the girls.
- *tōgai mā mayilārgaḷ* – \[It appears a śrīvaiṣṇava may have arrived for the upanyāsam \[lecture\]\[ a bit late; so nampiḷḷai starts and explains it again\] Since [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is greatly knowledgeable \[well aware of the types of hair\], he started praising; they think “since he does not understand whose hair it is, he is praising without knowing – he is talking like a mad man”. They are discarding his best speeches \[or his speeches about their hair\].
- *sevi ōsai vaitteḻa* – Having the music from the flute in their ears and arriving there.
- *āgaḷ pōgavittuk kuḻal ūdu* – You send the cows and then play the flute. When you play the flute, your goal will be achieved and the cows too will have their stomach filled \[by your divine flute music\]. He said “their having the music of flute in their ears and rising is the result; my playing the flute is the means; should I not do it for my dearest persons? Let me sing staying right here” and started playing the flute.
- *pōy irundē kuḻal ūdu* – When we say one thing, you don’t do something else; you go to fertile lands where your dearest ones will assemble, stay there and play the flute.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.2.3. Poy irundu

*pōy irundu nin puḷḷuvam aṟiyādavarkku urai nambī! nin seyya  vāy irum kaniyum kaṇgaḷum viparīdam in nāḷ vēy irum tadam tōḷinār ittiruvaruḷ peṟuvār yavar kol? mā irum kadalaik kadainda perumānālē*

**Пословный перевод:**

(emperumān asks – Why are you asking me to go elsewhere thinking that there are others? Who else is there for me other than you? īsn’t your presence my abode? They reply – other than this place where you have entered in close proximity); nambī – you who are complete (in mischief); pōy – leaving (from our proximity); irundu – staying (in proximity of your dear ones); nin – your; puḷḷuvam – mischief; aṟiyādavarkku – those who don’t know; urai – tell (these mischievous words); nin – your; seyya – reddish; vāy – lips; iru – best; kaniyum – fruit; kaṇgaḷum – eyes (which are naturally having the tendency to finish others); innāḷ – nowadays; viparīdam – are causing pain; mā – deep; iru – vast; kadalai – ocean; kadainda – churned; perumānālē – by him who has wondrous abilities; it tiruvaruḷ – the mercy which makes his heart go crazy and praise; peṟuvār – those who attain; vēy – like bamboo shoots; iru – well rounded; tada – tall; tōḷinār – those who are having shoulders; yavar kol – who?

**Перевод:**

**You who are complete should leave and stay where those who don’t know your mischief exist and tell them those words; your reddish fruit like best lips and eyes are causing pain nowadays \[to us\]. Who are those having shoulders which are like tall, well rounded bamboo shoots, who have the mercy of you to make your heart go crazy and praise you who churned the deep, vast ocean?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, when parānguśa nāyaki said “pōyirundu … kuḻalūdu” (Go and play your flute), he still remained and said some enticing words, and praised her hands for the way she waved them to send him; she wonders “who showed their shoulders and bewildered you who agitated the unśakeable ocean?”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Third pāsuram. \[emperumān says\] You are telling me “kuḻalūdu pōyirundu“; I should follow your words. Now, you said “you go and play your flute where there are many girls”; that is good. Which is such place? Can you not identify that?”; saying this he entered a few steps inside, stood firmly and started engaging in sweet talks which were sweeter than his flute. His talks are not just as sweet as the sound from his flute \[it is much greater\]! \[He says\] Alright, Let me do as you say, \[but\] I am not understanding why you said “seviyōsai vaitteḻa – kuḻalūdu pōyirundu” (go and play the flute, to have the girls rise on hearing his flute sound); isn’t this just an action matching my family duty \[i.e., it is not aimed at attracting girls – here, emperumān is just developing the conversation further\]?”. pōy irundu nin puḷḷuvam aṟiyādavarkku urai nambī! nin seyya  vāy irum kaniyum kaṇgaḷum viparīdam in nāḷ vēy irum tadam tōḷinār ittiruvaruḷ peṟuvār yavar kol? mā irum kadalaik kadainda perumānālē*

- *pōy irundu nin puḷḷuvam aṟiyādavarkku urai nambī* – Your lies will not work with us who are familiar with them; you leave from here, reach the assembly of those who don’t know your misciefs and tell there. Since there are five lakh families with girls, you will find some people who don’t know about the disharmony between your mind and speech. Should you not tell them these words, since they believe your lies to be truth? You will find those who say as in periya tirumoḻi 9.4.5 “*pōy kēttu irundēn*” (I remained listening to the lies of [tiruppullāṇi](http://thiruppullani.koyil.org/) [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)).
- *nambī* – āren’t you complete \[in all aspects\]? Is there any shortcoming for you when you don’t have us?

On hearing these nectarean words of rejection from them, his face showed gaiety.

- *nin seyya vāy irum kaniyum kaṇgaḷum viparīdam innāḷ* – They asked – previously, we never observed this reddish lips and beautiful eyes; why are these like this? He replied – aren’t you talking about something above the neck \[just for the sake of praising\]! leave that; how beautiful your shoulders are!
- *vēy irum tadam tōḷinār it tiruvaruḷ peṟubavar yavar kol?* – Are their shoulders so beautiful that, they make you bewilder when seeing some other shoulders to make you think those to be their shoulders!
- *ittiruvaruḷ peṟuvār yavar kol* – They have got you to torment like this! When they said “*seyya vāy irum kaniyum kaṇgaḷum*“, it shows their loving attachment towards him; when he said “*vēy irum tadam tōlinār*“, it shows his loving attachment towards them. He realised his loving attachment towards them through his face (lips and eyes). They realised their loving attachment towards him through their shoulders.
- *yavar kol* – Are they most dear to you? Though she says some harsh words towards them due to romantic anger, in reality, whoever may be associated with him, are held with great reverence, as the goal, by her.
- *mā irum kadalaik kadainda perumānālē – ittiruvaruḷ peṟuvār yavar kol* – Those who are having such beautiful shoulders which are desired by [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is praised in nācciyār tirumoḻi 9.1 “*mandaram nātti anṟu madurak koḻunjāṟu koṇḍa sundarat tōḷudaiyān*” (emperumān with beautiful shoulders, who fixed the mantara mountain as pestle and brought out the nectar)! There are those who have such beautiful shoulders which torment emperumān who himself torments every woman with his beautiful shoulders! They are capable of tormenting emperumān in their hands, in the same way the great ocean was tormented by the great emperumān! Another explanation – as said in “*vaikuṇṭadōr bhramitamandara mūdapātam*“, being tormented to be not able to speak about it clearly. Alternative explanation – we did not observe such beauty in emperumān when he churned the ocean with mantara mountain and acquired periya pirāttiyār (śrī mahālakśmi)! Acquiring someone new ([parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) ) is not the same as acquiring some one old ([śrī mahālakśmi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/) who is already his consort).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.
