## 6.2.4. Alinililai

*ālinīḷilai ēḻulagum uṇḍu anṟu nī kidandāy un māyangaḷ mēlai vānavarum aṟiyār ini em paramē? vēlinēr tadam kaṇṇinār viḷaiyādu sūḻalaic cūḻavē ninṟu kāli mēykka vallāy! emmai nī kaḻaṟēlē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ēḻulagum – all worlds; uṇḍu – consuming them (to keep them in his small stomach); ālin – the banyan’s (which makes one wonder “where did this spring from”); nīḷ – stretched (having blossomed); ilai – on the leaf; anṟu – on that day (when all worlds were not present due to the total deluge); nī – you (who has childishness of not knowing that you may slip and fall into the deluge); kidandāy – did you not lie down without any worries!; un – your; māyangaḷ – mischievous acts; mēlai – those who are without any contact with materialistic aspects; vānavarum – nityasūris (permanent residents of paramapadam); aṟiyār – will not know (as they let you go and seek out for butter as said in tiruviruttam 21 “ōr māyaiyināl īttiya veṇṇey toduvuṇṇap pōndu“); ini – now; em – to speak about (this); paramē – is it possible?; vēlin nēr – destroying people like a spear; tadam – vast; kaṇinār – those who are having eyes; viḷaiyādu – playing; sūḻalai – sand hill; sūḻa – surrounding; ninṟē – standing there; kāli – cattle; mēykka vallāy – aren’t you greatly skilled to accomplish the impossible tasks such as tending the cows to their stomach’s full satisfaction?; emmai – we who know your mischief; nī – you; kaḻaṟēl – don’t try to fool us (by saying “why are you blaming me for telling lies, when I had gone to tend the cattle?”)

**Перевод:**

**Once upon a time, did you not lie down on the stretched banyan leaf without any worries, after consuming all the worlds! Even the nityasūris who are without any contact with materialistic aspects will not know your mischievous acts; now, is it possible to speak about it? āren’t you greatly skilled to accomplish the impossible tasks such as standing around the sand hills which are part of the playing arena for those who are having vast spear like eyes and tending the cows to their stomach’s full satisfaction? You don’t try to fool us who know your mischief.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, emperumān angrily said “As I delayed a little bit to go to tend the cows, should you consider me to be focussed on something else?”, parānguśa nāyaki says “For you who can make the impossible happen, what can not be said?”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Fourth pāsuram. emperumān thought “They are misunderstanding whatever I am saying due to the anguish in separation and inability to tolerate my fractional delay” and said “Can you speak to me like this? Am I not obedient to my parents? Can I refuse to them if they hand over a cane to me to tend the cows?”. She replied “Is this how one who is obedient towards his parents and goes to tend the cows behaves? Only when your acts remain truthful, your words will remain truthful!”. ālinīḷilai ēḻulagum uṇḍu anṟu nī kidandāy un māyangaḷ mēlai vānavarum aṟiyār ini em paramē? vēlinēr tadam kaṇṇinār viḷaiyādu sūḻalaic cūḻavē ninṟu kāli mēykka vallāy! emmai nī kaḻaṟēlē*

- *ālin nīḷ ilai ēḻulagum uṇḍu anṟu nī kidandāy* – A banyan leaf, which is only stretched as much as it has blossomed; on that, you slept having the seven (all) worlds in your stomach, and rested when even yaśōdā et al were not there for your protection. āren’t you the one who places the whole creation inside your stomach and having a small form and resting alone during total deluge! Is it difficult to handle these matters when you can unite those aspects which cannot be united? Whatever you say \[about being obedient towards parents\] cannot work in the group of lovers; here you should mingle along as said in “*pitā nāma mūrdnaś śirō rōga:*” (the great disease named father) and śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 5.18.22 “*kurava:kim kariśyanti*” (what would the elders do to us). You should remain as said in 5.3.6 “*annai en seyyilen? Ur en sollilen?*” (What shall we do if mother does something? What shall we do if the people of the town say something?). Will they satisfy our needs by pouring water as said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 5.18.22 “*dagdānām virahāgninā*” (I am burnt by this fire of separation)? You should not tell these reasons to me while you should be coming to us without their knowledge!
- *un māyangaḷ mēlai vānavarum aṟiyār* – \[vānavar\] Not the created beings such as indra et al, but even nityasūris don’t know your mischief. Though it is said in “*brahmābinivēda nārāyaṇam prabhum*” (Even brahmā does not know śrīman nārāyaṇan, the sarvēśvaran) to indicate that brahmā et al also have ignorance about [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), since the current context is talking about emperumān ignoring his dear ones, it is more apt to talk about nityasūris (who are most dear to him); while they wait to worship him with the necessary paraphernalia as said in tiruviruttam 21 “*sūttu nanmālaigaḷ tūyana ēndi*” (carrying the best garlands),  he went seeking for butter “*īttiya veṇṇey toduvuṇṇap pōndu*“; then he gave up the butter and went seeking nappinnaip pirātti as said in “*kōttidai ādiṟṟu adalāyar kombinukkē*“. The current situation is where he is discarding the older consorts and seeking newer consorts. \[He is\] like those who manifest the desire for the newly married wives.
- *ini em paramē* – They are considering themselves on a par with nityasūris. Is it possible for us to understand what is inconceivable by them? You tell those details to some one else other than us. He asks “Why? Are you saying that I did not tend the cows? ōr are you saying that you don’t know? ōr are you saying me that I am telling lies?”; \[they said\] even if we agree that you tended cows, is this how you did it?
- *vēlin nēr tadam kaṇṇinār viḷaiyādu sūḻalaic cūḻavē ninṟu kāli mēykka vallāy* – It appears that you are captivated by the beautiful eyes of the girls, while tending the cows! Having vast, beautiful eyes which are lot greater in capacity than those who can enjoy them. [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who torments the girls who saw his beautiful eyes as said in nācciyār tirumoḻi 14.4 “*kārttaṇ kamalak kaṇṇennum nedum kayiṟu paduttennai, īrttuk koṇḍu viḷaiyādum īsan tannaik kaṇḍīrē*” (Have you seen my lord who is binding me with the lengthy rope of his cool cloud like eyes and attracting me), is now tormented by these girls with their eyes.
- *viḷaiyādu sūḻalaic cūḻavē ninṟu kāli mēykka vallāy* – Did your parents not say “You should not return until your stomach gets filled \[with the food that is given to you\] and the stomachs of the cattle also get filled”? Did they tell you to tend the cows at a particular location? If you are to do something different from what they instructed \[that tending cows within our vision\], could you not do it here? We see not even a blade of grass, and you are tending the cows where these girls are playing with the sand hills; it is unbelievable that you could fill the stomachs of the cattle. As you filled the stomachs of the cattle where there is no opportunity to do that, this can also be considered as a special skill of yours in accomplishing impossible tasks as explained previously \[in resting on the banyan leaf\].
- *vallāy* – She is saying – aren’t you the one who only does what you like irrespective of anyone telling you to do anything! Instead of understanding their sarcasm, he thought “they are praising my ability” and tried to speak about his own greatness; she remained “we spoke for a while to stop him from arguing; and he is speaking more”. śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 36.31 *itīva* – Previously hanuman spoke at length; sages \[hanuman et al\] would not understand what is going on in the minds of the lovers; he is saying “in this manner”. *dēvī* – an outsider \[hanuman\] will not understand the exchanges between the lovers. *vacanam mahārtam* – not only for outsiders, even the visionary leaders \[śrī rāma\] will not know \[what sītāp pirātti is thinking\]. *tam vānarēndram* – There is none comparable to hanuman; though sugrīva mahāraja was crowned for his śēśatvam (servitude), hanuman was the epitome of pāratantriyam (being totally dependent on śrī rāma). Among everyone present, even sugrīva did not have the opportunity to meet sītāp pirātti and speak to her. *madurārtam* – one cannot withdraw from speaking \[due to the words being very sweet\]. *uktvā* – she spoke to have him \[hanuman\] and his \[hanuman’s\] entourage sustain. *śrōtum punas tasya vacōbirāmam* – she herself saw that “he can bring back dead people to life”; she wanted to hear hanuman speak about śrī rāma who she quashed \[by blaming him previously\]. *rāmārta yuktam* – for the benefit of śrī rāma; knowing that only he can fulfil her desire; *virarāma* – as she spoke at length and also cannot speak overriding the words about her svāmi (śrī rāma), she stopped speaking and let him speak. *rāmā* – we are not fortunate to see śrī rāma directly witnessing this beautiful quiet moment instead of her lengthy speech. \[In this manner\] He ([emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)) tried to argue \[with [parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)\].
- *emmai nī kaḻaṟēlē* – Would those who tormented, try to finish us as well?
- *emmai* – we who are suffering in separation from you,
- *nī* – You who never separate from us, You who are not bothered by the separation.
- *kaḻaṟēlē* – don’t keep arguing with us; you cannot speak like this. When it is just you \[who has committed offense of discarding us\] and us \[who are suffering\], how apt is it for you to argue with us? You are speaking considering us to be cētana (one who has knowledge)!  That too you are speaking more and more. Only those who have helped in difficult times, can speak \[as you have not helped, you cannot speak like this\]!

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.2.5. Kalarel nambi!

*kaḻaṟēl nambī! un kaitavam maṇṇum viṇṇum nangaṟiyum tiṇ cakkara niḻaṟu tol padaiyāy! unakku onṟu uṇarttuvan nān maḻaṟu tēn moḻiyārgaḷ nin aruḷ sūduvār manam vādi niṟka em kuḻaṟu pūvaiyodum kiḷiyōdum kuḻagēlē*

**Пословный перевод:**

nambī – (as said in “poy nambi” (complete in lies)) you who are complete (in lies)!; kaḻaṟēl – don’t argue with me (saying “why are you calling me a liar?”); tiṇ – firm (being a great support for falsely transforming day into night); cakkaram – divine disc; niḻaṟu – emitting radiance; tol padaiyāy – oh one who is having distinguished weapon!; un – your; kaitavam – mischievous acts; maṇṇum – (during the mahābhārata battle times) the princely people who gathered on earth; viṇṇum – dēvas, the residents of higher worlds, without any distinction; nangu – clearly; aṟiyum – know; unakku – for you; nān – I; onṟu – one thing; uṇarttuvan – inform you, listen; nin – your; aruḷ – mercy; sūduvār – born to behold; maḻaṟu – very fresh; tēn – honey like; moḻiyārgaḷ – those with voice; manam – heart; vādi – to wither; niṟka – to stand; em – ours (instead of theirs); kuḻaṟu – (unlike them who speak clearly to you) speaking incohesively; pūvaiyodum – with maina; kiḷiyōdum – and parrot; kuḻagēl – don’t play joyfully

**Перевод:**

**Oh you who are complete! Don’t argue with me; oh one who is having the firm, divine disc which is a distinguished weapon, emitting radiance! The princely people who gathered on earth and dēvas, the residents of higher worlds, without any distinction, clearly know your mischievous acts; I have one thing to inform you, listen; while the hearts of those who are born to behold your mercy who are with very fresh honey like voice, are withering, don’t play joyfully with our maina and parrot which are speaking incohesively. Here maina and parrot indicate the dear śiśyas who are the dear companions of emperumān’s devotees, having enjoyable attitude and are exclusively protected by them \[the ācāryas\].**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, parānguśa nāyaki says “You who have great support in the form of your entourage, do not engage in praising our speech for the sake of it, and praising our maina and parrot who speak sweetly”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Fifth pāsuram. emperumān said “Among friends, faults are considered as good qualities; when there is no friendship, even good qualities are seen as faults; good qualities and faults are dependent upon the person we are dealing with; hence, whatever I told you will appear as faulty for you all; still, we should accept what is highlighted by a mediator \[neutral person\]”. kaḻaṟēl nambī! un kaitavam maṇṇum viṇṇum nangaṟiyum tiṇ cakkara niḻaṟu tol padaiyāy! unakku onṟu uṇarttuvan nān maḻaṟu tēn moḻiyārgaḷ nin aruḷ sūduvār manam vādi niṟka em kuḻaṟu pūvaiyodum kiḷiyōdum kuḻagēlē*

- *kaḻaṟēl nambī* – As emperumān repeats what he was doing previously, they said “do not show your supremacy and talk over us strongly”.
- *nambī* – You cannot win over us showing your greatness!

emperumān said – I cannot accept the words of those (you all) who have hatred in their heart; are there others who have witnessed my mischief?

- *un kaitavam maṇṇum viṇṇum nangaṟiyum* – Your mischief is not limited to us; it is well known across worlds. Due to [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s memories from [tiruvāimoḻi 2.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/11/thiruvaimozhi-2-1-vayum/) “*vāyum tiraiyugaḷum*” \[in this decad, āḻvār sees everything to be suffering in separation from [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)\], he is thinking “all the universe is thinking like himself”. When the relationship \[with emperumān\] is common for all, it can be thought like that. Alternative explanation – when the lord is on one side, all the servitors will unite and speak with a single voice; when one has many servitors, they will mutually discuss with each other and represent a common cause. Both the residents of the higher worlds and the earth know his mischief clearly. Both the knowledgeable ones and the ignorant ones without any distinction, know this.

[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) said “Would you cite those who are ignorant? āren’t these people of the earth ignorant as said in tiruvāimoḻi 4.8.6 “*aṟivināl kuṟaivillā agal jñālattavar*” (the ignorant people of this world who don’t even know that they are ignorant)?

- *viṇṇum nangaṟiyum* – emperumān says “Alright! You make \[at least\] one of them highlight my lies”; they said “we will show you one of them who was partial towards you, on your hand itself”;
- *tiṇ cakkara niḻaṟu tol padaiyāy* – You listen to the one who considers \[your\] fault as an auspicious quality! It is he who stands by you in support of your mischief, who knows about them! he remains seated in your hand knowing your heart; when asked “would you transform day into night”, he would say “yes” and hide the sun; this is his activity.
- *tiṇ cakkaram* – Even if we can change [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s lies, we cannot do that with sudarśana chakra. emperumān, being svatantra (independent), will act depending upon the situation; but sudarśana chakra does not have that independence \[he works exclusively per emperumān’s desire\].
- *niḻaṟu tol padiyāy* – niḻaṟu – conducting. That is, sustaining him by implementing his thoughts even though he violated his own vow \[of not taking up arms\].
- *tol padaiyāy* – He is being an ancient servitor for such acts.

Hearing her words, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) hung his head in shame thinking “we are having some witness \[against us\] in our own entourage”.

- *unakku onṟu uṇarttuvan nān* – Listen! Don’t be speechless; I will give you a good advice. If he heard that, he can neither refute that nor he would have an option to argue back; emperumān still remained quiet and said “how is your speech so sweet?”.
- *maḻaṟu tēn moḻiyārgaḷ* – Oh my bad! you are listening our speech and are bewildered relating that to someone else! maḻaṟu tēn – fresh honey. Those who sweetly speak like nicely mixed honey. Since his presence does not change, their agitation also does not change. He would say “I am seeing that right here”.
- *moḻiyārgaḷ* – \[plural\] How many such girls do you have?
- *nin aruḷ sūduvār* – Those who are so great that, when you hear others speak, you think that they are speaking. Those who agitate you, who can pacify others by just saying a word \[śrī bhagavat gītā 18.66 “*mā suca:*” (do not worry)\] as seen in śrī bhagavat gītā 18.73 “*stitōsmi gata sandēha:*” (arjuna says – My mind has become stable; my doubts are gone). He asked “so what?”; she said “they are not like us \[who can neither live nor die in separation from you for so long\]; while you are standing here without any expectation, their hearts will wither thinking about your presence here, unable to bear the separation; they are as said in nācciyār tirumoḻi 8.7 ‘*kongai mēl kungumattin kuḻambaḻiyap pugundu orunāḷ tangumēl en āvi tangum*‘ (I will survive only on that day when he comes and unites with me to melt the kumkum on my bosom); this being the case, if you don’t go and protect them, they will suffer; can you tolerate that?” and remained quiet. He shifted his focus to her maina and parrot and started praising them saying “more than your speech, I sustain myself by hearing their speech”! caring for some one means, caring for their possessions which are dear to that person.

When he started praising them, she said “Who do you think are their owners? They are not the ones who you think to be!”.

- *em kuḻaṟu pūvaiyodum kiḷiyōdum kuḻagēlē* – They are not speaking to you specifically! They just naturally keep speaking!
- *kuḻagēlē* – Though we are talking with something else in mind, you are talking exclusively to us without any other refuge; similarly, their words mean something else \[not directed towards you\]!
- *kuḻaṟu pūvai* – The maina which is speaking incohesively. *kuḻagudal* – trying to mingle playfully.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.2.6. Kulagi engal

*kuḻagi engaḷ kuḻamaṇan koṇḍu kōyinmai seydu kanmam onṟillai paḻagiyām iruppōm paramē ittiruvaruḷgaḷ? aḻagiyār ivvulagu mūnṟukkum dēvimai taguvār palar uḷar kaḻagam ēṟēl nambī! unakkum iḷaidē kanmamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kuḻagi engaḷ kuḻamaṇan koṇḍu – picking up our doll which is used in our play; kōyinmai seydu – feeling superior due to the pleasure of having got hold of it; onṟu – any; kanmam – use; illai – not there; yām – we; paḻagi – previously used; iruppōm – to it; i – these; tiru – great; aruḷgaḷ – mercies; paramē – we cannot handle; aḻagiyār – having beauty (fitting to receive your mercy); i – (target of your supremacy,) these; ulagu mūnṟukkum – for the three worlds; dēvimai – to be crowned along with you; taguvār – deserving; palar – many (as said in “dēvyas sahasram“); uḷar – are present; nambī – aren’t they fitting for you who are complete in all qualities!; kaḻagam – in our assembly; ēṟēl – do not mingle; unakkum – for you (who have the nature of only harming others); kanmam – this act; iḷaidu – childish

**Перевод:**

**There is no use in picking up our doll which is used in our play and feeling superior due to the pleasure of having got hold of it; we are previously used to it; we cannot handle your great mercies; there are many who are having beauty fitting to receive your mercy, deserving to be crowned along with you for these three worlds; aren’t they fitting for you who are complete in all qualities! do not mingle in our assembly; this act is childish for you \[to do\]. By highlighting the doll, it implies that the devotees’ play items are also desirable for him.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, parānguśa nāyaki says to emperumān who manifested his greatness and picked up her doll “don’t show your supremacy to us; you show it to those who deserve that”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Sixth pāsuram. parānguśa nāyaki and her friends were hiding what is going on in their mind and remaining to be not overcome; seeing them, emperumān manifested facial expressions, emotional words and pleasing acts which matched such speech, and changed their mind. Now, having them dumbfounded to not object to his actions, he approached closer to them and picked up their doll, which is part of their play. kuḻagi engaḷ kuḻamaṇan koṇḍu kōyinmai seydu kanmam onṟillai paḻagiyām iruppōm paramē ittiruvaruḷgaḷ? aḻagiyār ivvulagu mūnṟukkum dēvimai taguvār palar uḷar kaḻagam ēṟēl nambī! unakkum iḷaidē kanmamē*

- *kuḻagi engaḷ kuḻamaṇan koṇḍu* – *kuḻagugai* means the \[crazy\] acts of youth which are done to unite with their counterparts when they are not honouring their attempts to speak to them. Whether by showing supremacy or humility; he set out to somehow approach them, change their mind and pick up their doll.
- *engaḷ kuḻamaṇan koṇḍu* – Who did you think is its owner? It is not owned by those who you think, but it is ours. There is no use for you with this. They said “as soon as we said ‘it belongs to us’, you should drop it and leave”; but that itself led to his pursuit of it.

When they asked “don’t you need our permission to take it?”, he said “Is there any one who can question me! Can I not do do what I like to do?”. They said,

- *kōyinmai seydu kanmam onṟu illai* – There is no use of whatever improper acts you do. Here karma implies karma palam (result of the action). Don’t do here what is done in a headless region. At least if there is any benefit, you can do it. kōyinmai seygai means grabbing their doll without their permission, not giving it back to them etc.
- *kanmam onṟu illai* – You cannot carry these along to where you are going; you don’t need them; and these are dear to us; hence, what is the use of this act \[of picking those up\]? Even if you carry those there, since they are not their belongings, they won’t care for them; since these don’t belong to those who are dear to you, you don’t need them, and since you took them without our permission, it \[the act\] does not please us as well! They said “Hence, there is no use of this act”.

He said “leave it aside; previously we were like minded; I too have no specific expectation and I did not do this expecting any other benefit; this itself is my benefit; can there be any benefit for a benefit; if we try to imagine such benefit that will lead to an endless chain”. They said,

- *paḻagi yām iruppōm* – āren’t we used to your lies! You cannot tell these to us! They said – Why don’t you go and tell these to those who believe your lies to be truth.

[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), acted as if saying “I cannot sustain without you”. They said,

- *em paramē it tiruvaruḷgaḷ* – You are showing great love towards us. Are your such acts bearable for us, just as the ocean cannot be placed in small spot? They said “there are others who can tolerate all your actions”.

He asked them “who are they?”. They said,

- *aḻagiyār ivvulagu mūnṟukkum* – śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 16.14 “*trailōkya rājyam sakalam sītāyānāpnuyāt kalām*” – if the three worlds and [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who himself is called by the term “viśva” are placed in one side of the weighing scale, they will not match a fraction of sītāp pirātti’s beauty.

He asked them “What are their qualities?”. They said,

- *dēvimai taguvār* – They are qualified to be crowned along with you.

He said “But I also need some one to dislike”. They said,

- *palar uḷar* – There are some who are present there to be rejected by you too. When something is natural for a person, it will not change even when he goes to a different place; similar to what he did to their own group, they imply that he would reject some persons there too. They said “You are not limited to a few of us; you have many persons! You go to them”. He said “Alright! But I need to know how to go there and what to do after reaching there and I need to hear that from you; it is usually instructed only to antēvāsis (close śiśyas); those who heard from learned persons are explained in [śrī bhagavat gītā 4.34](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/4-34/) ‘*paripraśṇēna sēvayā*‘ (by asking questions with proper attitude and by performing service)” and hence entered the assembly of [parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) and her friends.
- *kaḻagam ēṟēl nambi* – Let them be the primary ones; is it possible for us to assume a teacher’s position? First, you don’t enter our assembly. Here [bhattar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/parasara-bhattar/) mercifully explains – sarvēśvaran who is filled with all auspicious qualities, the lord of both spiritual and material realms, greater than all and controller of all, is unable to resist entering the assembly of a few covherd girls, and they say “you cannot enter here” He feels shackled and is neither able to leave nor able to stay and stumble upon there – such is his sauśeelyam (quality of mingling with inferior persons without any hesitation) – vyāsa et al documented this \[in purāṇams\] – who did they think are going to celebrate this great quality of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)?”. When one says “the controller of all, assumed such a simple position to be controlled by a few”, there will be no one who thinks “it is true”. When all of śāstram distinguishes between the supreme lord and the subordinate entities, here the roles are reversed! periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 3.6.11 “*sādu gōttiuḷ koḷḷap paduvār*” (will be accepted in the assembly of vaiṣṇavas) – when someone enters an assembly of vaiṣṇavas, it is apt for him to not manifest great pride and instead mix as water mixes with water, and them accepting him naturally; this is not just for vaiṣṇavas but applicable for emperumān too; as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam bāla kāṇḍam 4.31 “*sa cāpi rāma pariśad gataśśanair bubhūśaya āsaktamanā babhūva*” (śrī rāma with the desire to enjoy the singing of kuśa and lava, entered amidst the audience and listened from there) – śrī rāma arranged kuśa and lava’s singing in the royal assembly to be heard by greatly knowledgeable scholars and himself, being seated on the royal throne; but their being in a lower platform and his being in a higher platform, was not pleasing to his heart; so he quietly slid down from the throne, and entered the audience. That is because – if we rose making noise, the assembly will be disturbed; it is said in the ślōkam “to avoid that, he quietly stepped down from the throne”. What is the need for that? *anububhūśayā* implies “to enjoy being amidst the audience” and “*bavitumiccayā*” implies “to sustain himself”.
- *nambī* – See the great difference between you and us! Is there anything that you have to ask and get? They said “For you, who is a lord, is it apt to enter our place?”. He said “Good! It does not matter whether I am the lord or a small \[child like insignificant\] person; don’t you know me! I am known as said in nācciyār tirumoḻi 2.1 “*tīmai seyyum sirīdaran*” (śrīdara, who is engaged in mischievous acts)? Thus, isn’t it natural for me to engage in mischievous acts wherever girls are present?
- *unakkum iḷaidē kanmamē* – Even for you who are an expert in mischievous acts, this is childish. Some relationship is necessary between you and the ones who are affected by your mischievous acts – isn’t it?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.2.7. Kanmam anru

*kanmam anṟu engaḷ kaiyil pāvai paṟippadu kadal jñālam uṇḍitta ninmalā! nediyāy! unakkēlum piḻai piḻaiyē vanmamē  solli emmai nī viḷaiyādudi adu kētkil ennaimār tanma pāvam ennār oru nānṟu tadi piṇakkē*

**Пословный перевод:**

engaḷ – our; kaiyil – in the hand; pāvai – doll; pārippadu – touching and grabbing; kanmam – apt acts; anṟu – not; kadal – submerged in the causal ocean; jñālam – world; uṇḍitta – consumed and protected by placing in stomach; ninmalā – Oh one who is having radiance due to doing that as a great accomplishment!; nediyāy – Oh one who is having greatness (of letting them out and protecting them thinking “what I have done is not sufficient”)!; unakkum – even for you (who are having such greatness); piḻai – mistake (of touching and grabbing the doll from us, the helpless girls); piḻaiyē – is a disgrace; nī – you (who are great in this manner); vanmam – (saying “Shall I touch you? Who were you thinking before?”, reminded us about our previous union) secrets (which cannot be thought about or spoken about by us); emmai – towards us; solli – telling; viḷaiyādudi – teasing playfully; ennaimār – our brothers; adu kētkil – if they hear that; tanmapāvam – will not analyse whether it is right or wrong; ennār – will not prove; oru nānṟu – one day they will come; tadi – picking up a stick; piṇakku Am – will engage in fight

**Перевод:**

**Touching and grabbing the doll in our hand are not apt acts; oh one who consumed the world and protected it by placing in stomach when it was submerged in the causal ocean, and is having radiance due to doing that as a great accomplishment! Oh one who is having greatness! Even for you, such an act is a disgrace; you are telling us secrets and teasing us playfully; if our brothers hear that, they will not analyse and prove whether it is right or wrong; one day they will come with a stick and engage in fight \[with you\].**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, parānguśa nāyaki says “It is inapt for you who are having the greatness of protecting all the worlds without expecting any benefit in return, to touch us and grab our doll”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Seventh pāsuram. emperumān went through all difficulties which śrī bharatāḻvān had gone through by pursuing many means towards him, with parānguśa nāyaki and her friends. śrī bharatāḻvān struggled greatly to bring śrī rāma back as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 82.19 “vinivartayitumbalāt” (I am going to pursue all means to bring śrī rāma back). I will make sure that he himself will show his mercy; should he hear it from anyone else? – śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 111.14 “śēśyē purastāt śālāyā yāvan mēna prasīdati” (I shall remain lying down at the entrance of śrī rāma’s hut until he returns to ayōdyā); he said “purastāt” (in front) \[so his efforts are clearly visible to śrī rāma\]. Similarly, though emperumān tried hard various means, they remained firm to not let him get closer; he thought “what shall we do next?”; he determined “let us accomplish this task by force”, and set out to pick up their doll; as said in “prēkśitajñāstu kōsalā:” (the residents of kōsala kingdom will read the thoughts of others based on the way they see), since they can read emperumān’s thoughts, everyone picked up her doll; emperumān thought “this is what we wanted too”. He thought “now, I don’t have to go and try with every one of them \[since they have all collectively taken their doll\]”. He did not have to hold everyone’s hand individually \[by assuming multiple forms\] as he did in tirukkuravai (rāsa krīdai); he thought “this is a good opportunity” and went and grabbed their doll. kanmam anṟu engaḷ kaiyil pāvai paṟippadu kadal jñālam uṇḍitta ninmalā! nediyāy! unakkēlum piḻai piḻaiyē vanmamē  solli emmai nī viḷaiyādudi adu kētkil ennaimār tanma pāvam ennār oru nānṟu tadi piṇakkē*

- *kanmam anṟu* – They said “Come on! It is not apt for you do this”.

He asked “Why is it not apt for me to do?”, they said,

- *engaḷ kaiyil pāvai paṟippadu* – They said “Who did you think are the owners of this? It does not belong to those you think it belongs to! It is ours!”. He said “that is true!”; mahābhāratam udyōga parvam “*yasyaitē tasya taddanam*” (to the one who owns a person, his property also belongs to the same owner). The reason for his liking towards the doll is their claim of ownership. His goal is to make them claim ownership of the doll; their goal is to tell him that it is not owned by those who he thinks to be its owner.
- *engaḷ kaiyil pāvai paṟippadu* – He is grabbing as if he is leaving part of the doll in their hands! If they fully leave it, there is no use for him; only when they have part of it and he has part of it, it is enjoyable like \[closely related persons\] eating out of the same plate.
- *kaiyil pāvai paṟippadu* – While there is so much to do, it is not proper for you to grab the doll from our hands. You are doing what is not allowed to be done; there is no use in doing it – they said. Hence, what is understood from this? When a vaiṣṇava claims ownership for a particular object, that is what is desirable for [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/).

emperumān asks – How come you are telling me “you are doing what is not allowed to be done”! īsn’t it I who set the rules of what can be done and what cannot be!”.

- *kadal jñālam uṇḍitta* – Did I not protect all of these objects during the dangers such as praḷayam (deluge) etc? But their situation \[danger\] is not as limited as that of the worlds \[i.e., it is greater\]. Their state is such that, had he not gone and grabbed the doll, they would have been finished. But this world would still exist \[in a subtle form\] even during deluge; for them, in his absence, their existence itself is destroyed! He said “Am I not āpatrakśaka (saviour when in danger)! Hence, all my acts will be without any expectation; hence, this itself is my benefit! when there is a benefit for benefit, it will lead to anavastā (unending chain); only when I consider this as means, I will look for a separate result”; they said “you cannot talk like this; while we don’t accept your approach, you are forcefully doing this and calling yourself ‘āpatrakśaka’ is not acceptable; now, this will only lead to a faulty quality in you”.
- *ninmalā nediyāy!* – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) asked “While I have so many auspicious qualities, do you only see this one fault in me?”.
- *ninmalā! nediyāy!* – Even for candra (moon) who is known as ninmala (pure), there is scar! So, where the auspicious qualities shine, the faults shine too!! Oh one who is opposite of all faults and filled with unlimited, great qualities!
- *unakkēlum piḻai piḻaiyē* – Even for you who have unlimited auspicious qualities, a fault remains a fault.

On hearing this from them, as he could not give an apt reply, he set out to whisper in their ears, what could not be shared with others; they are saying “*vanmamē solli*” (saying secrets). Only their hearts and his heart know about those; and it cannot be explained explicitly.

- *emmai nī viḷaiyādudi* – When you tell those secrets, should you not tell knowing about you who tells and us who hear \[only when we have a good relationship, you can tell such things\]. (When some devotees asked embār, “what secrets did he tell”, [embār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/embar/) mercifully replied “when [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) who was divinely blessed with unblemiśed knowledge and devotion himself just says ‘vanmam’ (secret), how can you expect me to explain what secrets are they?”).
- *viḷaiyādudi* – He transformed himself \[minimizing his stature\] and told a secret; but they consider it as his playful act; they ask “when you tell something just for the sake of it, what is the benefit?”.

He again tried to say something.

- *adu kētkil ennaimār* – If our relatives hear your words, it will lead to undesirable results. ennaimār – brothers.
- *tanma pāvam ennār* – They do not know that we have no attachment for you. On seeing you coming at us, they will harm you without thinking about what can be done and cannot be.

[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) asked “So what? Would they know that? They are not here now!”, they said,

- *oru nānṟu* – Oh! Now they may not know, but some day they will come to know.

He asked “Alright! What would they do when they come to know?”, they said

- *tadi piṇakkē* – It will end up in fights and tussles. As he would use his bow in śrī rāmāvatāram for everything, in kriṣṇāvatāram, he would use his stick for everything \[so they would also fight him with their sticks\].

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.2.8. Pinakki yavaiyum

*piṇakki yāvaiyum yāvarum piḻaiyāmal bēdittum bēdiyādadu ōr kaṇakkil kīrtti veḷḷak kadir jñāna mūrttiyināy! iṇakki emmai em tōḻimār viḷaiyādap pōdumin ennap pōndōmai uṇakki nī vaḷaittāl en sollār ugavādavarē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

yāvarum yāvaiyum – all cētanas (sentient beings) and acētanas (insentient entities); piṇakki – mixing (at the time of deluge not to have name and form); piḻaiyāmal – without causing (any effect to karmas (deeds) of those cētanas); bēdittum – while causing differences in the form of dēva (celestials), manuśya (humans), tiryak (animals), stāvara (plants); bhēdiyādadu – not to have the true nature impacted (due to the defects in those forms); ōr – unparallel; kaṇakku il – unlimited; kīrtti veḷḷam – having ocean of glories; kadir – in the form of rays (radiance); jñānam – jñānam (knowledge) in the form of sankalpa (will); mūrttiyināy – oh you who are having as form!; em – belonging to the same category \[as we\] and having equal sorrow \[as we\]; tōḻimār – friends; emmai iṇakki – convincing us; viḷaiyāda – “to play; pōdumin – go”; enna – as they told us, considering such playing as the reason; pōndōmai – us who came here (without knowing that you are here, just to play); uṇakki – make us wither, being unable to even eat; nī – you; vaḷaittāl – block us; ugavādavar – those people who don’t like this; en – what; sollār – will they say?

**Перевод:**

**You (emperumān) mixed with all cētanas and acētanas causing differences in the form of dēva (celestials), manuśya (humans), tiryak (animals), stāvara (plants) without causing any effect in their karmas, not to have the true nature impacted; oh you who are having jñānam (knowledge) in the form of radiant sankalpa (will) as form which is having unlimited ocean of glories! As our friends belonging to the same category \[as we\] and having equal sorrow \[as we\] convinced us saying “go and play”, considering such playing as the reason, we came here; if you make us wither, being unable to even eat, and block us, what will those people who don’t like  this, say?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, parānguśa nāyaki and her friends thought “only if we remain in his presence, he will discuss secrets with us” and set out to leave, and he blocked their way; seeing him they said – if you who are sarvajña (omniscient) forcefully stop us as said in “don’t you who know everything, know this?”, what would those who are unfavourable say?.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Eighth pāsuram. He approached them and tried to trouble them; they thought “only if we remain here, we have to go through these”. One by one, they started to leave; he thought “is this what you are planning” and blocked their way. Since it is a garden, there is only a small pathway. When nanjīyar was mercifully explaining this pāsuram, āppān \[tiruvaḻundūr araiyar\] asked “What will he do if they just cross over him?”, he mercifully said “Who is going to benefit out of it? \[emperumān only\] He blocked the way thinking either one of two will happen \[i.e., if they remained,  his desire will be fulfilled, and if they crossed, the objective of his efforts to unite will fructify, because they will come in contact with him while crossing\]”. You are standing in our way; when others see what you do, they will think that you are related to us and doing such things out of such relationship; is there any limit to your playful acts towards everyone? You are such that, you will bring in transformation for everything else other than you and will remain unchanged; similarly you have charged us emotionally and you remain unchanged! piṇakki yāvaiyum yāvarum piḻaiyāmal bēdittum bēdiyādadu ōr kaṇakkil kīrtti veḷḷak kadir jñāna mūrttiyināy! iṇakki emmai em tōḻimār viḷaiyādap pōdumin ennap pōndōmai uṇakki nī vaḷaittāl en sollār ugavādavarē!*

- *yāvaiyum yāvarum piṇakki* – Mixing with those \[insentient\] entities which have no consciousness to recognise their togetherness with him and with those \[sentient\] entities which consciously do not recognise their togetherness with him, and remaining indistinguishable from them as said in subhāla upaniśat 2 “*tama: parē dēva ēkī bhavati*” (the primordial matter mixes with paramātmā).
- *piḻaiyāmal bēdittum* – Separating them without missing anything. Protecting them by keeping them in his stomach \[during intermediary deluge\] and then letting them free, and letting them free after a \[total\] deluge. Just as those who migrated from a place during disturbed times, would return to their original residence once peace returns, and would continue with their routines. Separating the ātmās and karmas from him, such that one person’s karma does not get consumed by some one else.
- *bēdiyādadu ōr kaṇakkil kīrtti veḷḷak kadir jñāna mūrttiyināy* – Though it is the same brahmam which is the effect and the cause, it remains with ēkarūpa (singular form), advitīya (without second), unlimited ocean of glories and knowledge in the form of radiance and divine will, without manifesting the differences such as subtle transformation of acit (insentient), ignorance of the cit (sentient), acit’s nature of the object itself transforming into some other form and cit’s nature of having changes in qualities. Oh such empermān! He is said in tiruvāimoḻi 1.5.2 “*ellāp poruḷgatkum vittāy mudalil sidaiyāmē manam sey jñānam*” (being the seed for all entities, without losing any of his attributes, in the form of knowledge). With this – it is explained that [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) remains ēkarūpa – without grief in separation and joy in union.
- *kaṇakkil kīrtti veḷḷam* – If one sets out to say “he is of such qualities”, he will only become tired in trying to measure it fully.
- *kadir jñāna mūrttiyināy* – Having no shortcoming in knowledge even when entities unite with him or get separated.
- *kadir jñāna mūrttiyināy* – Not losing the shine after completing the task; shine increases as he engages in his tasks.
- *kadir jñāna mūrttiyināy* – Oh one who is an embodiment of knowledge!
- *iṇakki …* – Speaking to convince. They said “that is a place to which kriṣṇa does not come”
- *emmai* – Us who don’t know that it is dangerous to be united with you.
- *en tōḻimār* – What is the point in hating you? Is there any fault in you? All this is due to those who united us with you! It is implied that one will celebrate those who do favours in bhagavat viśayam, when one understands about the distinguished nature of bhagavān. Both here \[in material realm\] and there \[in spiritual realm\], everything is due to them as said in [stōtra ratnam 2](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/12/sthothra-rathnam-2/) “… *nityam yadīya caraṇau śaraṇam madīyam*” (My salutations to [śrīman nātamunigaḷ](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nathamunigal/) whose divine feet are always my refuge in this world and the other world as well).
- *en tōḻimār* – Only those belonging to same clan will unite \[us\].
- *viḷaiyādap pōdumin ennap pōndōmai* – We did not know that they are actually helping you. We believed their words and did not look deep into their heart. If we knew that you were here, we would not have thought of coming here; we did not know that you are seeing us through them.

[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) asked “Leave that aside; so what? If you had come here on their advice, what have you lost now?”; they said,

- *uṇakki nī vaḷaittāl* – uṇakkugai means making them wither to be unable to sustain themselves. What else do we need to get now? Neither we are able to leave from here; nor we are able to come close to you and enjoy your face.

They asked – \[Others – people of the town\] What would those who don’t like to see this \[our interaction\] say? emperumān replied – What shall I say? As I am considered “īśvara” (supreme lord), and you are just “lowly covherd girls”, what is there to say \[there is no real match for us to be discussed by others\]. They said – You being the sarvēśvara and we being covherd girls is the reason why they will speak about us. \[Another view. Others – those other girls who are attached to [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)\] To be spoken at par with īśvara, they are not like nappinnai pirātti. emperumān asked “If you consider yourself not having any attachment towards me, what is there to worry about this?”.

- *en sollār ugavādavarē* – Would those who don’t like our interaction know that we do not have attachment towards you? As you delay a little bit here, would they not cite this as the reason saying “they are being together now”? Would they speak knowing about you who are blocking and us who are blocked?
- *en sollār ugavādavarē* – Your dear girls who have lightning like waist would speak to you harshly. What will those who cannot tolerate your separation say?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.2.9. Ugavaiyal nenjam

*ugavaiyāl nenjam uḷ urugi un tāmarait tadangaṇ viḻigaḷin agavalaip paduppān aḻittāy un tiruvadiyāl tagavu seydilai engaḷ siṟṟilum yām adu siṟu sōṟum kaṇḍu nin muga oḷi tigaḻa muṟuval seydu ninṟilaiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ugavaiyāl – due to the internal joy; nenjam – heart; uḷ urugi – melted; un – your; tāmarai – lotus like; tada – broad; kaṇ – eye’s; viḻigaḷ – glance; valai – in the net; agappaduppān – to capture; engaḷ – our; siṟṟilum – sandcastle; yām – we; adugiṟa – heating; siṟu sōṟum – food; kaṇḍu – seeing; nin – your; mugam – in the divine face; oḷi tigaḻa – to have shining glow; muṟuval – smile; seydu – doing; ninṟilai – instead of standing and observing; un – your; tiruvadiyāl – with the divine feet; aḻittāy – destroyed; tagavu seydilai – you did this mercilessly

**Перевод:**

**To have our heart melt with internal joy and to be captured in the net of the glance of your broad eye, we are building the sandcastle and heating our food; instead of seeing that, standing there and smiling to show the shining glow in your divine face, you destroyed those with your divine feet mercilessly. With this, it is implied that emperumān will destroy the attachment of devotees in the material realm.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, as he blocked the way, parānguśa nāyaki and her friends went away from him and started building a sand castle; he became angry thinking “instead of acknowledging me, they are ignoring me” and knocked their sand castle; they become upset saying “instead of letting us build the sand castles while looking at your beautiful face, you destroyed it!”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Ninth pāsuram. parānguśa nāyaki and her friends thought “Only when we interact with him as per his desire, there is benefit for his blocking us”. They remained silent thinking “We will not look at his face” as muktar (liberated persons) would remain unrelated to samsāris (worldly persons) in certain places (paramapadam); they further thought “if we remained like this, he would think that we are thinking about him” and said “let us engage in building a sand castle to show that we are focussed on something else” and set out to do that; he became angry thinking “Not only are you ignoring me, you have also started focussing on some other activity” and kicked and destroyed the sand castle and their food; they in turn became angry and started speaking to him forgetting their vow \[of not speaking to him\]. Even his own desires get fulfilled with the help of his divine feet only. Whoever has the divine feet can have his desires fulfilled. ugavaiyāl nenjam uḷ urugi un tāmarait tadangaṇ viḻigaḷin agavalaip paduppān aḻittāy un tiruvadiyāl tagavu seydilai engaḷ siṟṟilum yām adu siṟu sōṟum kaṇḍu nin muga oḷi tigaḻa muṟuval seydu ninṟilaiyē*

- *ugavaiyāl nenjam uḷ urugi* – Come on! Your task is useless; you are really looking to create joyful melting of our heart instead of melting of our heart due to your hurting us in separation; you cannot do that.
- *un tāmarai …* – He will capture us by trapping in the same pit which we fell in the day time \[i.e., capturing us showing the same eyes as done previously\]; it is by this bonding through his glance that he makes one exist fully for him. To capture by the net in the form of the glance of the divine eyes which have lotus like fragrance, coolness, redness and enjoyability which cannot be fully enjoyed by the enjoyers.
- *agavalai* – Inside the net. agavalai can also be construed as agaviya valai (vast net). It is said in nācciyār tirumoḻi 14.4 “*kaṇṇennum nedum kayiṟu*” (the vast net in the form of your eye). If one gets caught in such an eye, he will blabber like being affected by fever \[which causes shivers\];  as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 2.6.3](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/04/thiruvaimozhi-2-6-3-thamaraik-kannanai/) “*tāmaraik kaṇṇanai viṇṇōr paravum talai maganai*” ([emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is lotus-eyed, and \[hence\] being the leader, vorśipped by nityasūris (permanent residents of paramapadam)).
- *aḻittāy un tiruvadiyāl* – His own sandcastle \[material realm\] is destroyed just by his will; but their sandcastle needs to be destroyed by his physical touch; can you not use the same tool as you do for your sandcastle? He causes deluge using his sankalpam (will) only. Just as the śēśabhūta (servitor) desires for the divine feet, the beloved girls in separation too desire for the divine feet.
- *aḻittāy* – You did not just destroy our sandcastle; but you destroyed our heart too; nācciyār tirumoḻi 2.9 “*siṟṟilōdu engaḷ sindaiyum sidaikka*” (will you destroy our sandcastle and heart?). They are saying – you destroyed the sandcastle with your divine feet and our objective with your eyes.
- *tagavu seydilai* – You did not behave like a merciful person. Did you not discard the love while separating from us? Now, you are also not behaving like one who is having kaṇ (eye, mercy). īsn’t it the purpose of having eye to see good things ? nācciyār tirumoḻi – “*un mugattana kaṇgaḷallavē*” (āren’t those \[beautiful\] eyes in your face?).

He asked “What mistake did I commit?”, they said,

- *engaḷ siṟṟil …* – Is our sruśti (creation) unacceptable like yours? īsn’t it acceptable? He asks “How is my creation unacceptable and yours acceptable?”; Did we create this according to karma (collective deeds of the souls), using fire and air, sunshine and droplets? īsn’t this built as said in nācciyār tirumoḻi 2.3 “*vaṇḍal nuṇmaṇal teḷḷi yām vaḷaik kaigaḷāl siramappattōm*” (Putting efforts with our hands having bangles, built with the sand from the sand banks).
- *yām adu siṟu sōṟum kaṇḍu* – The food you cook \[material realm\] cannot be consumed by anyone else; it is consumable only by you as in the case of nirmālyatvam (food remnants of other dēvatās); isn’t the food we cook, consumed together as said in tiruppāvai 27 “*mūda ney peydu muḻangai vaḻivārak kūdi irundu*” (Covered with ghee which drips through the forearm, it is eaten together)?
- *kaṇḍu nin muga oḷi tigaḻa muṟuval seydu ninṟilaiyē* – You are not standing with a radiantly shining, smiling face, being pleased upon seeing our amazing activity; they become grieved that he is not showing his mercy on seeing their efforts.
- *tagavu seydilai* – You are not allowing us to enjoy your radiantly shining face and smile with our peripheral vision, pretending to be building the sandcastle. If we looked at you straight, it will be common for everyone; doesn’t one see her beloved with her peripheral vision only? How did they even build the sandcastle without seeing!

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.2.10. Ninrilangu mudiyinay!

*ninṟilangu mudiyināy! irubattōrukāl arasu kaḷai katta venṟi nīḷ maḻuvā! viyan jñālam mun padaittāy! inṟivvāyar kulattai vīduyyat tōnṟiya karu māṇikkac cudar! nin tannāl nalivē paduvōm enṟum āycciyōmē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ninṟu – to remain firmly; ilangu – shining; mudiyināy – wearing divine crown; irubattōrkāl – twenty one generations; arasu – kings; kaḷai katta – destroyed; venṟi – victorious; nīḷ – big; maḻuvāl – one who is having the axe!; viyal – vast; jñālam – world; mun – during sruśti (creation); padaittāy – one who created; inṟu – now as well; i – this; āyar kulam – covherd clan; vīdu – with their families; uyya – to uplift; tōnṟiya – one who appeared; karu māṇikkac cudar – oh one who is having the form which is radiant like blue gem!; nin tannāl – by you (since you are the protector in all ways, you being our lord who eliminated our anger, and brought us back to life, and having relationship with us and are having an enjoyable form); āycciyōm – we who are born in this ignorant covherd clan; enṟum – always; nalivu – suffering; paduvōmē – will go through – she is recollecting and telling about the previous sufferings after being pacified

**Перевод:**

**Oh one who is wearing the shining, divine crown to remain firmly! Oh one who is having the big, victorious axe which destroyed twenty one generations of kings! Oh one who is having the form which is radiant like blue gem, who created the vast world during sruśti and now appeared in the covherd clan to uplift them with their families! We who are born in this ignorant covherd clan will always go through suffering caused by you – she is recollecting and telling about the previous sufferings after being pacified. The plural used in all the pāsurams after “nānadunjuvan” (I fear for that) in the first pāsuram \[as singular\], can be construed as “royal we” \[treating oneself respectfully\] or speaking on behalf of self and her friends.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, after looking at his face and saying “muga oḷi tigaḻa muṟuval seydu ninṟilaiyē“, they forgot their internal anger, and thinking about his many efforts to turn them favourable towards him, being pacified, parānguśa nāyaki says “We are tormented by you who are the protector in all ways!”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Tenth pāsuram. They stood there saying “nin muga oḷi tigaḻa muṟuval seydu ninṟilaiyē” without seeing what is coming; he did not destroy just their sandcastle but the anger in their heart; once that anger was eliminated, they looked up and observed him from his divine feet to his divine head; he stood there with the joy of winning over them; they are now talking about the greatness of such form. ninṟilangu mudiyināy! irubattōrukāl arasu kaḷai katta venṟi nīḷ maḻuvā! viyan jñālam mun padaittāy! inṟivvāyar kulattai vīduyyat tōnṟiya karu māṇikkac cudar! nin tannāl nalivē paduvōm enṟum āycciyōmē*

- *ninṟu ilangu mudiyinay* – Before winning them \[[parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) and her friends\], the crown remained heavy as mere weight on his divine head; only then, it started shining. Just as some kings will wear crowns of valour and victory after winning over other kings, though [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) was crowned before, before winning over them, it was insignificant. Winning over the beloved consorts is unlike winning over rāvaṇa et al \[this is much more pleasing\]. Only after eliminating their hesitation and accepting them, his crown became significant, having supremacy and radiance. śrī rāmāyaṇam bāla kāṇḍam 1.85 “*abhiśicya ca lankāyām rākśasēndram vibhīśaṇam krutakrutya: …*” (śrī rāma crowned śrī vibhīśaṇa as the king of lankā and felt fulfilled and relieved from shivers) – śrī rāma became pale thinking “What if śrī vibhīśaṇa too refuses to be crowned and requests me to take care of the kingdom as done by śrī bharatāḻvān?”; “at least one major weight is eliminated; what if this \[kingdom of lankā\] also had become my responsibility?”. It is natural for the descendants of ikśvāku to shy away from the throne \[Here śrī vibhīśaṇa is also considered as descendant of ikśvāku since he was accepted by śrī rāma as brother\]. It is our true nature to accept the divine feet of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) and shy away from the throne.

emperumān said “Leave that aside; Have I not eliminated your hesitation and won over you?”.

- *irubattōr kāl …* – For you who had won over 21 generations of prideful kings, is it difficult to win over us who are helpless girls? For you who can easily win over those who consider them to be their own, is it a great thing to win over us who are fully existing for you? Oh one who uprooted the demonic kings who tormented the citizens! For you who won over the kings, is winning over the covherd girls a great thing?
- *viyan jñālam mun padaittāy* – Just as you recreated the earth which was totally destroyed during deluge, you have brought us back to life after we became totally destroyed by the romantic anger. viyan – amazing. Just as you lifted up the earth which was consumed by the deluge, you lifted us up from the deluge of the suffering in separation. You protected the earth there since there was none to reject your help \[considering earth to be insentient\], but here, have you not brought our life back even while we stopped you saying “*kaḻagam ēṟēl*” (Don’t enter our assembly)?
- *inṟu* … – Should we go searching \[for your helpful acts\] in general creation as said in taittirīya upaniśat “*bahusyām*” (Let me be many)? Have you not taken birth in our own covherd clan and protected everyone in this clan by showing your divine form? Your partiality towards your devotees, which you did as your own benefit, is well manifested in your form.
- *vīduyya* – To uplift everyone along with their descendants as said in “*saputra pautras sagaṇā:*” (With the belongings such as sons, grandsons et al).
- *tōnṟiya* – Appeared. They are saying “*karu māṇikkac cudar*” (shining like blue gem) since he united with those who were refusing to unite with them due to praṇaya rōśam (romantic anger).
- *nin tannāl …* – It has so happened that we are being tormented by you instead of either getting killed as enemies or moving away from you as materialistic people! Now, these words are spoken by [parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) after she united with [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) and in embrace with him. Until now, she was talking about her victory, and only now she has accepted defeat at his hands.
- *nalivē paduvōm* – Did we really achieve this \[union\]? We will only get what we usually have. What they usually have is suffering only as said in tiruviruttam 16 “*kūdilum nīngilum yām melidum*” (we are weakened both in union and separation).
- *āycciyōmē* – We who don’t even know the difference between left hand and right hand.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.2.11. Aycci agiya

*āycci āgiya annaiyāl anṟu veṇṇey vārttaiyuḷ sīṟṟam uṇḍaḻu kūtta appan tannaik kurugūrc catakōpan ēttiya tamiḻ mālai āyirattuḷ ivaiyum ōr pattu isaiyodum nāttannāl navila uraippārkku illai nalguravē*

**Пословный перевод:**

āycci āgiya – born in covherd clan; annaiyāl – by mother yaśōdā; anṟu – then; veṇṇey vārttaiyuḷ – when the news about butter theft came about; sīṟṟamuṇḍu – angered upon; aḻu – cried and performed sit-ups \[as punishment\]; kūttan – one who is having joyful pastime; appan tannai – one who is the benefactor for the world; kurugūrc catakōpan – nammāḻvār; ēttiya – mercifully spoke in the form of praises; tamiḻ mālai – in the form of a garland in drāvida (tamiḻ) language; āyirattuḷḷum – among the thousand pāsurams; ivai – these (distinguished pāsurams which turned the unfavourable to be favourable); ōr pattum – ten pāsurams (decad); isaiyodum – with tune; nāttannāl – as a benefit for the tongue; navila – well; uraippārkku – for those who recite; nalguravu – the poverty of bhagavat alābham (not having bhagavān); illai – is not there

**Перевод:**

**Back then, kaṇṇan emperumān was having the joyful pastime of crying and performing sit-ups when angered upon by mother yaśōdā who is born in covherd clan. nammāḻvār mercifully spoke about such emperumān who is the benefactor for the world, in the form of praises and a garland in drāvida (tamiḻ) language, in these ten pāsurams among the thousand pāsurams. Those who recite this decad well, with tune, as a benefit for their tongue, will not have the poverty of bhagavat alābham (not having bhagavān).**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the end, āḻvār says “Those who learn this with intent will not go through the suffering I had gone through”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār mercifully says “For those who recite this decad, there is no poverty of bhagavat alābham (not having emperumān)”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*In the end āḻvār says “Those who learn this with intent will not have lack of bhagavān \[i.e., lack of bhagavat anubhavam/kainkaryam\]”. āycci āgiya annaiyāl anṟu veṇṇey vārttaiyuḷ sīṟṟam uṇḍaḻu kūtta appan tannaik kurugūrc catakōpan ēttiya tamiḻ mālai āyirattuḷ ivaiyum ōr pattu isaiyodum nāttannāl navila uraippārkku illai nalguravē*

- *āycci āgiya annaiyāl* – āḻvār is specifically highlighting the covherd mother since kaṇṇan emperumān had one kśatriya (kingly) mother and another idaicci (covherd) mother. If dēvakip pirātti beats him, it will not hurt so much. He remained perplexed thinking that she is going to scold him \[for his misdeeds\] as said in periya tirumoḻi 8.3.5 “*tāy edutta siṟu kōlukkuḷaindōdi*” (Feeling perplexed about the stick which mother yaśōdā carried and ran out of fear). dēvaki’s motherhood was only known to God \[since no one else knew it at the time of birth\]; but he was nursed and nurtured here \[in gōkulam\] only.
- *anṟu veṇṇey vārttaiyuḷ* – Some one said in the town “butter was stolen”; at once emperumān started crying thinking “we will have to bear the brunt for this”. \[An example is cited for such act of emperumān. A huge coultry \[free dormitory\] is managed by a person. Someone comes and asks him “Who will clean such big coultry?”; \[the manager replied\] “*aśrōtriyan*” \[a dumb, ignorant person\]; \[an ignorant person who was there, at once said\] “can I clean this whole place on my own?”, similar to that \[emperumān will start crying as soon as he hears about butter theft\]. His mischief is such that whatever anyone else does, he only gets blamed; as said in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 2.8.5 “*pallāyiravar ivvūril piḷḷaigaḷ tīmaigaḷ seyvār ellām un mēl anṟip pōgādu*” (Though many thousands of children exist in this town and they all may commit mischief, you will be the only one blamed for all such mischief).
- *sīṟṟamuṇḍu aḻu kūtta appan tannai* – As the mother shows her anger, his trembling posture with tears in eyes, and standing as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 5.10.3](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/09/thiruvaimozhi-5-10-3-peyyum-punguzhal/) “*paiyavē nilaiyum*” (that fearful posture), looks like a seasoned dancer’s posture. Alternatively, it can be construed as the great benefactor who is having the pastime of crying. This proves one thing – this highlights how he, who is free from any expectation, stood fearfully instead of leaving, when they said “*pōgu nambī*” (Oh complete lord! Go!), and “*kaḻagam ēṟēl nambī*” (Oh complete lord! Don’t enter our assembly!).
- *appan tannai* – Manifesting such qualities and attracting/accepting him and bringing him back to life.
- *kurugūrc catakōpan ēttiya tamiḻ mālai* – As the “*praṇaya rōśam*” (romantic anger) disappeared, the angry words such as “*pōgu nambī*“, “*kaḻagam ēṟēl nambī*“, “*un puḷḷuvam aṟiyādavarkku urai nambī*” etc turned to be praises.
- *āyirattuḷ ivaiyum ōr pattu* – This distinguished decad which revealed his special relationship with his devotees.
- *isaiyodum* – Just with the mouth \[even without understanding the meanings\].
- *navila uraippārkku* – For those who say with intent/emotions.
- *illai nalkuravē* – There is no poverty. That is – sending messengers to him and when he comes, one need not suffer saying “we will not allow you to enter”. Here it is not talking about food and clothing; it is saying that one will not be deprived of enjoyment in spiritual matters; this is because, deprivation for āḻvār who remains “*uṇṇum sōṟu parugu nīr tinnum veṟṟilaiyum ellām kaṇṇan*” (kaṇṇan is everything to me – the food that nurtures, the water that sustains and the betel leaf that is enjoyed), is only related to spiritual matters. One’s food and beverages are based on his nature. Those who say as in perumāḷ tirumoḻi 3.4 “*uṇḍiyē udaiyē ugandōdum im maṇḍalattodum kūduvadillai yān*” (I won’t mingle with these materialistic people who are chasing food and clothes), will not consider worldly matters as wealth. As said in nānmugan tiruvandādi 61 “*senṟu onṟi ninṟa tiru*” (emperumān, the wealth, which came on its own and settled in me), emperumān would himself come to them and they would eternally enjoy him. For “*aḻu kūtta appan*“, we can recollect perumāḷ tirumoḻi 7.8 “*muḻudum veṇṇey aḷaindu tottuṇṇum*” \[this pāsuram beautifully explains in detail, how kaṇṇan emperumān steals butter, how he is caught by mother yaśōdā, how she scolds and beats him and how he stands trembling in front of her\].

## 6.3 Nalguravum selvum

## 6.3.1. Nalguravum selvum

*nalguravum selvum naragum suvarggamumāy vel pagaiyum natpum vidamum amudamumāyp pal vagaiyum paranda perumān ennai āḷvānaic celvam malgu kudit tiruviṇṇagark kaṇḍēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

nalguravum – the poverty of having contracted forms; selvum – the wealth of having expanded forms; naragum – hell which is the abode of sorrow; suvarggamum – heaven which is the abode of joy; āy – being \[having as his form/attribute\]; vel – knocking down the opponents; pagaiyum – hostility; natpum – friendship which is the opposite of that; vidamum – poison which finishes \[the one who consumes it\]; amudamum – amrutam (nectar, which gives immortality) which redeems the life; āy – being \[having as his form/attribute\]; pal vagaiyum – in many ways; paranda – one who has permeated; perumān – greater than all; ennai – manifesting such forms to me; āḷvānai – the master (who accepted me as a servitor); selvam – the wealth of experiencing bhagavān; malgu – abundant; kudi – having group of virtuous people; tiruviṇṇagar – in tiruviṇṇagar \[oppili appan temple\]; kaṇḍēn – I have seen

**Перевод:**

**emperumān is having the poverty of having contracted forms, the wealth of having expanded forms, hell which is the abode of sorrow, heaven which is the abode of joy, hostility which knocks down the opponents, friendship which is the opposite of that, poison which finishes \[the one who consumes it\] and amrutam which redeems the life, as his forms/attributes. I have seen such emperumān who has permeated in many ways \[in all these aspects\], who is greater than all and the master who is manifesting such forms to me, in tiruviṇṇagar which is having abundant group of virtuous people who are having the wealth of experiencing bhagavān.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the first pāsuram, āḻvār says “I have seen sarvēśvaran who is having contrary entities as his wealth/form, in tiruviṇṇagar”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*In the first pāsuram, āḻvār says “I have seen emperumān who is sarvavyāpaka (omnipresent)  and is having contrary entities which cause pleasure/pain, as his wealth/form, in tiruviṇṇagar”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. nalguravum selvum naragum suvarggamumāy vel pagaiyum natpum vidamum amudamumāyp pal vagaiyum paranda perumān ennai āḷvānaic celvam malgu kudit tiruviṇṇagark kaṇḍēnē*

- *nalguravum selvum* – Poverty and its opposite, wealth.
- *naragum suvarggamum* – Hell which is the abode of sorrow, and heaven which is the abode of joy.
- *vel pagaiyum natpum* – Hostility which eliminates any scope of truce and \[friendly\] relationship which is opposite of that.
- *vidamum amudamum āy* – Poison which will kill and nectar which will bring back life in a dead person. The nectar both redeems lost life and is also enjoyable. āḻvār likes both poverty which is undesired and wealth which is desired, considering them both to be owned by emperumān. “*āy*” (being) is added to every word \[i.e., nalguravumāy, selvumāy and so on\].
- *pal vagaiyum paranda perumān* – Even emperumān who is most knowledgeable withdrew saying in [śrī bhagavat gītā 10.19](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/10-19/) “*nāstyantō vistarasya mē* ” (there is no end to the full expansion of my wealth), while trying to explain his wealth; such wealth cannot be spoken by āḻvār who is in the mood of loving devotion. Yet, he should speak at least a little bit. An entity is not seen without its attributes; he is not speaking māyāvāda philosophy which speaks about brahmam without any attributes, as in “*nirviśēśam vastu*” (entity (brahmam) is devoid of any attributes). If that is the case \[i.e., entity is devoid of attributes\], there is no need for mōkśa śāstram (the sacred text which speaks about liberation \[which leads to eternal kainkaryam to bhagavān\]). When accepting the existence of an entity, the attribute will only show the differentiation \[between this entity and others\]. When something becomes an attribute for an entity, the attribute cannot be explained unless it is considered as anyayōga vyavaccēdam (exclusive distinction – an attribute which is exclusively held by this entity) \[“rāma is the only archer” – this establishes the exclusive nature of archery in rāma\]; since all other entities are his \[emperumān’s\] attributes, anyayōga vyavaccēdam is inapplicable; but, how can contrary attributes be present in a single entity? It is applicable as per ayōga vyavaccēdam (co-existing distinction) \[“rāma is archer only” – this implies, he is not the only archer, but archery is his main skill, and he will have other qualities as well\] and āḻvār is setting out to enjoy such emperumān. What is the purpose of his explaining such contrary attributes in him? That is to see him truly and enjoy him. For a prince, both his father’s grand assembly which is the enjoyable spot and the prison house are equally treated as “my father’s wealth”. āḻvār’s meditation here \[in this samsāram\] is similar to that of the muktātmā’s (liberated souls) about the material realm. Though it is said in cāndōjña upaniśat 8.12.3 “*nōpajanam smaran idam śarīram*” ([ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) will not contemplate about the material body after reaching the spiritual realm), for the muktātmā, this material realm is desirable when considered as bhagavān’s wealth; for āḻvār too, similar to muktātmās, to have his views only based on the thinking that, this material realm is owned by bhagavān, emperumān removed his ignorance. When looked at it from own perspective, it is seen to be tyājyam (given up); one will urge to give up this world where there is room for both knowledge and ignorance, and to reach the spiritual abode where there is no scope for ignorance.
- *pal vagaiyum paranda perumān* – emperumān who is expanded in multifarious ways through his wealth.
- *paranda perumān ennai āḷvānai* – āḻvār thinks that emperumān has permeated everything to capture him; just as a town is rounded up to capture a single person.
- *selvam malgu kudit tiruviṇṇagark kaṇḍēnē* – Like seeing an oasis in a desert.
- *selvam malgu kudi* – tiruviṇṇagar which is having greatly opulent communities. As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam bāla kāṇḍam 18.28 “*lakśmaṇō lakśmī sampanna:*” (lakśmaṇa who is endowed with wealth of kainkaryam), like iḷaiya perumāḷ (lakśmaṇa) who had the same relationship with śrī rāma as śrī bharatāḻvān, he served śrī rāma, while bharatāḻvān could not – similar to such lakśmaṇa.
- *tiruviṇṇagark kaṇḍēnē* – Just as one gets food when/where he is hungry, āḻvār enjoyed per his desire \[of seeing emperumān\] right here \[in tiruviṇṇagar\], instead of assuming a different body, reaching a different \[spiritual\] abode and seeing emperumān there. As said in periya tirumoḻi 6.8.1 “*nān senṟu naṟaiyūril kaṇḍēnē*” (I went to tirunaṟaiyūr and saw the emperumān there).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.
