## 6.3.2. Kanda inbam

*kaṇḍa inbam tunbam kalakkangaḷum tēṟṟamumāy taṇḍamum taṇmaiyum taḻalum niḻalumāyk kaṇḍukōdaṟkariya perumān ennai āḷvānūr teṇ tiraip punal sūḻ tiruviṇṇagar nannagarē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kaṇḍa – seen in this world; inbam tunbam – joy and sorrow; kalakkangaḷum – the mental worries which arise from such sorrows; tēṟṟamum āy – being the serenities which arise from joy; taṇḍamum – the anger (which arises from such worries); taṇmaiyum – clarity (which arises from such serenities); taḻalum – fire (which has anger-like heat); niḻalum – shadow (which has serene coolness); āy – being; kaṇḍukōdaṟku – to be seen similar to other species; ariya – one who is difficult; perumān – being sarvēśvaran (supreme lord); ennai – me; āḷvān – one who accepted as servitor; Ur – divine abode; teṇ – pristine; tirai – having rising tides; punal – water; sūḻ – surrounded; tiruviṇṇagar – tiruviṇṇagar; nal nagar – beautiful town

**Перевод:**

**emperumān being the joy and sorrow which are seen in this world, the mental worries which arise from such sorrows and the serenities which arise from joy, the anger and clarity, the fire and shadow,  and who is difficult to be seen similar to other species; such sarvēśvaran who accepted me as servitor is residing in the divine abode of tiruviṇṇagar, a beautiful town which is surrounded by pristine water having rising tides.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the second pāsuram, āḻvār says “emperumān who is having expansive and contrary wealth, and is being very great not to be seen by anyone due to his mighty shoulders, yet accepted my service; such emperumān’s abode tiruviṇṇagar is better than all of his other divine abodes”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. kaṇḍa inbam tunbam kalakkangaḷum tēṟṟamumāy taṇḍamum taṇmaiyum taḻalum niḻalumāyk kaṇḍukōdaṟkariya perumān ennai āḷvānūr teṇ tiraip punal sūḻ tiruviṇṇagar nannagarē*

- *kaṇḍa inbam* – Limited joy as said in “*aingaruvi kaṇḍa inbam*” (the joy experienced by the five senses).
- tunbam – the sorrow which is the same as “joy” \[in this material realm\], but having a different name.
- *kalakkangaḷum tēṟṟamumāy* – The worries which accumulate due to non-achievement of worldly pleasures and the clarities which arise from such achievement.
- *taṇḍamum taṇmaiyum* – anger and serenity.
- *taḻalum niḻalumāy* – fire which causes heat and shadow which gives coolness.
- *kaṇḍukōdaṟkariya perumān* – By all these, his immeasurable nature is explained. \[nampiḷḷai becomes amazed at āḻvār’s knowledge and devotion\] What expansive knowledge [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) has \[i.e., he is seeing everything as [brahmam](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)\]! While speaking about [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s attributes, he is speaking about him saying “emperumān is inconceivable”; previously, while highlighting some aspects he said in the first pāsuram “*pal vagaiyum paranda perumān*” (emperumān who permeated in many ways); what an amazing way of meditating/speaking! Nothing exists without [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/). While nallār and śrī sēnāpati dāsar were going to tirumalai (tiruvēngadam) \[most likely while walking on the mountain\], śrī sēnāpati dāsar hit some bushes with a stick \[to clear the path\]. nallār’s saying of “While you have no enmity towards these bushes due to earning wealth or enjoyment, why are you hurting the belongings of īśvara unnecessarily!” should be remembered.
- *ennai āḷvānūr* – The abode of emperumān who suffered in tiruvāimoḻi 6.2 “minnidai madavār”, not willing to lose me.
- *teṇ tirai …* – The beautiful town of tiruviṇṇagar which is surrounded by water having clear tides.
- *teṇ tiraip punal sūḻ* – The town is having the river which is a replica of the divine river virajā. If [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) himself descends from paramapadam to here, nothing stops other things to follow him.
- *tiruviṇṇagar nannagarē* – As śrīvaikuṇṭam is still not seen, should it even be considered as an abode? The abode \[tiruviṇṇagar\] which is dear to him is our destination.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.3.3. Nagaramum nadugalum

*nagaramum nādugaḷum jñānamum mūdamumāy nigaril sūḻ sudarāy iruḷāy nilanāy visumbāyc cigara mādangaḷ sūḻ tiruviṇṇagar sērnda pirān pugar koḷ kīrtti allāl illai yāvarkkum puṇṇiyamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

nagaramum – city which has many knowledgeable persons; nādugaḷum – countryside which has many ordinary persons; jñānamum – knowledge; mūdamum – foolishness; āy – being; nigar – match; il – not having; sūḻ – expansive; sudar – radiance; āy – being; iruḷ – darkness (which is lacking such radiance); āy – being; nilan – (abode of such darkness) earth; āy – being; visumbu – (abode of radiance) sky; āy – being; sigaram – having peaks; mādangaḷ – mansions; sūḻ – surrounded; tiruviṇṇagar – in tiruviṇṇagar; sērnda – one who is residing well; pirān – sarvēśvaran’s; pugar – radiance; koḷ – having; kīrtti – glorious qualities; allāl – other than; yāvarkkum – for everyone; puṇṇiyam – fortune which leads to uplifting; illai – not there

**Перевод:**

**sarvēśvaran who is being \[having forms as\] city which has many knowledgeable persons and countryside which has many ordinary persons, knowledge and foolishness, matchless, expansive radiance and darkness, earth and sky, is residing well in tiruviṇṇagar which is surrounded by mansions having peaks; for everyone, there is no other fortune which leads to uplifting, than such emperumān‘s radiant, glorious qualities.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the third pāsuram, āḻvār says “There is no means \[for being uplifted\] other than the auspicious qualities of emperumān who descended to tiruvinṇṇagar”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. nagaramum nādugaḷum jñānamum mūdamumāy nigaril sūḻ sudarāy iruḷāy nilanāy visumbāyc cigara mādangaḷ sūḻ tiruviṇṇagar sērnda pirān pugar koḷ kīrtti allāl illai yāvarkkum puṇṇiyamē*

- *nagaramum nādugaḷum* – City people who are engaged in enjoyment and countryside people who work hard to earn their livelihood. Alternatively – this could imply limited (urban) and unlimited (rural) aspects.
- jñānamum mūdamumāy – Knowledge which facilitates true understanding of objects, and ignorance which leads to misunderstanding the objects.
- *nigaril sūḻ sudarāy iruḷāy* – Being the all-pervading radiance which is incomparable and the darkness which is the opposite to that.
- *nilanāy visumbāy* – Earth which has \[a beautiful\] form and sky which is formless. Also explained as earth which is hard and sky which is light.
- *sigaram …* – The benefactor who is residing perfectly in tiruviṇṇagar which is surrounded with mansions which are having terraces which resemble mountain peaks.
- *pugar koḷ kīrtti allāl illai* – His glories are diminished in paramapadam; \[that is because\] there is no one lesser than him there; everyone is equal to him in paramapadam as said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 14.2](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/14-2/) “*mama sādarmyam āgatā:*” (having attained equanimity with me), muṇḍaka upaniśat “*paramam sāmyam upaiti*” (Attaining complete equanimity) and periya tirumoḻi 11.3.5 “*tammaiyē okka aruḷ seyvar*” (He will bless his devotees to become equal to him). Wouldn’t one’s glories shine only when helping inferior persons?
- *yāvarkkum puṇṇiyamē* – Other than his glories, there is no means for the uplifting of everyone. Whatever one seeks for one’s own uplifting will only be a hurdle in reality; in “minnidai madavār”, as he was coming, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) said “don’t come” and was going to be finished; the means sought by [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) is a hurdle for himself; the means shown by [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) will bind emperumān himself \[for uplifting; this is the firm nature of the upāyam \[means\].

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.3.4. Punniyam pavam

*puṇṇiyam pāvam puṇarcci pirivenṟiyavaiyāy eṇṇamāy maṟappāy uṇmaiyāy inmaiyāy allanāy tiṇṇa mādangaḷ sūḻ tiruviṇṇagar sērnda pirān kaṇṇanin aruḷē kaṇḍu koṇmingaḷ kaitavamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

puṇṇiyam pāvam – puṇyam and pāpam which lead to desirable and undesirable results respectively; puṇarcci pirivu – the union and separation with such results; enṟu – that; ivai āy – being these; eṇṇam – thoughts about such union and separation; āy – being; maṟappāu āy – being the forgetful state about the same; uṇmai āy inmai āy – being the existence and non-existence of those aspects; allan āy – being free from bondage of such aspects; tiṇṇam – firm; mādangaḷ – mansions; sūḻ – surrounded; tiruviṇṇagar – in tiruviṇṇagar; sērnda – reached \[descended\]; pirān – supreme lord; kaṇṇan – kriṣṇa’s; in – greatly enjoyable, without any expectation; aruḷē – mercy only; kaṇḍu koṇmingaḷ – know that this is the glorious means which was explained previously; kaitavamē – is there any mischief in this?

**Перевод:**

**The supreme lord kriṣṇa, who is residing in tiruviṇṇagar which is surrounded by firm mansions, is puṇyam and pāpam which lead to desirable and undesirable results respectively, the union and separation with such results, the thoughts about such union and separation, the existence and non-existence of those aspects, and is free from bondage of such aspects; know that, such emperumān’s greatly enjoyable mercy only which does not expect anything, is the glorious means which was explained previously. Is there any mischief in this? Implied that, this is the highest truth.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fourth pāsuram, āḻvār says “All his wealth/forms which appear in the form of puṇyam (virtues), pāpam (vices) etc, were created due to his mercy; you can analyze and understand that none of those is false “.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “The radiant glories which were explained previously are all kriṣṇa’s nirhētuka krupai (causeless mercy) who is having all objects which have puṇyam and pāpam as his wealth”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. puṇṇiyam pāvam puṇarcci pirivenṟiyavaiyāy eṇṇamāy maṟappāy uṇmaiyāy inmaiyāy allanāy tiṇṇa mādangaḷ sūḻ tiruviṇṇagar sērnda pirān kaṇṇanin aruḷē kaṇḍu koṇmingaḷ kaitavamē*

- *puṇṇiyam pāvam* – puṇyam which is means to joy and pāpam which is means to sorrow,
- *puṇarcci pirivu* – union which is result of puṇyam and separation which is result of pāpam.
- *eṇṇamāy maṟappāy* – Remembrance in desired aspects and forgetfulness in undesired aspects.
- *uṇmaiyāy inmaiyāy* – Being what is explained by the words “asti” (exists) and “nāsti” (does not exist). Also explained as existence and non-existence. Also explained as cētanas (sentient beings) and acētanas (insentient objects).
- *allanāy* – Being the controller of puṇyam and pāpam, and not being bound by them.
- *tiṇṇam …* – kriṣṇa, the benefactor who has descended to tiruviṇṇagar which is surrounded by firm mansions which will not be destroyed even during deluge as said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 5.38.9 “*vāsudēva gruham dvēkam naplāvayati sāgara:*” (the ocean \[which breached its shores\] did not destroy kriṣṇa’s palace alone).
- *innaruḷē* – Everything which appears as his wealth/forms in the form of puṇyam and pāpam, occurs due to his mercy. Is pāpam too his mercy? Yes – since it occurs based on cētana’s previous karma, that is also his mercy only. Irrespective of what he does, can bad things happen due to his mercy? As he shows the bad effects to reform the individual and lead him into good path, that can also be considered as part of his mercy.
- *in aruḷ* – Causeless pursuit \[merciful act towards the jīvātmā to accept it\].
- *kaitavamē* – There is no exaggeration in what I explain here.
- *kaṇḍu koṇmingaḷ* – You all can see for yourself.

Alternatively,

- *kaitavamē* – all that are krutaka (this world which is recreated during partial deluge), are created due to his causeless pursuit.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.3.5. Kaitavam semmai

*kaitavam semmai karumai veḷumaiyumāy mey poy iḷamai mudumai pudumai paḻamaiyumāy seyda tiṇ madil sūḻ tiruviṇṇagar sērnda pirān peyda kāvu kaṇḍīr perundēvudai mūvulagē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kaitavam – (inferior) dishonesty; semmai – (superior) honesty; karumai veḷumaiyum āy – being \[having as his forms\] black and white colours; mey poy – the truth which is form for superior and lie which is form for inferior; iḷamai mudumai – youth and old-age; pudumai paḻamai āy – being modern and ancient; seyda – well crafted; tiṇ – firm; madiḷ – fort; sūḻ – surrounded by; tiruviṇṇagar – in tiruviṇṇagar; sērnda – descended; pirān – sarvēśvaran; peyda – placed; kāvu kaṇḍīr – this is the garden where he enjoys his sport; perum dēvu – dēvatās starting with the great brahmā; udai – inhabited by; mūvalugu – the three layered world

**Перевод:**

**sarvēśvaran being dishonesty and honesty, black and white colours, the truth which is superior and lie which is inferior, youth and old-age, new and old, descended in tiruviṇṇagar which is surrounded by well crafted, firm fort; such emperumān placed this three layered world which is inhabited by dēvatās starting with the great brahmā as the garden where he enjoys his sport – see it.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fifth pāsuram, āḻvār says “The benefactor of tiruviṇṇagar is the protector for all irrespective of whether they are great or small”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “For sarvēśvaran who is having superior and inferior entities as his forms, the whole world is a garden for his sport”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyā35kyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. kaitavam semmai karumai veḷumaiyumāy mey poy iḷamai mudumai pudumai paḻamaiyumāy seyda tiṇ madil sūḻ tiruviṇṇagar sērnda pirān peyda kāvu kaṇḍīr perundēvudai mūvulagē*

- *kaitavam semmai* – dishonesty and honesty.
- *karumai veḷumai* – black and white.
- *mey poy* – truth and lie.
- *iḷamai mudumai* – youth and old-age.
- pudmai paḻamai – modern and ancient.
- *seyda …* –  highlights the craftsmanship in facilitating a fresh look in it \[fort\], even after passing ages.
- *peyda kāvu kaṇḍīr* – Look! This is the garden placed by [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/).
- *perum dēvudai mū ulagē* – The three layered world which has dēvatās who considered themselves to be lords. mū ulagu – the world which has higher, middle and lower layers. The principle explained by this – the garden will not know to ask for protection; having the nature of withering after a while, and the one who created it himself taking care of it subsequently; similarly irrespective of one being a lord \[dēvatā\] or controlled \[humans etc\], everything is working per his directive. ([āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is implying that even his romantic fight with emperumān was not done by āḻvār’s sanction \[but occurred per the will of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)\].)

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.3.6. Mu ulaganlumay

*mū ulagangaḷumāy allanāy ugappāy munivāy pūvil vāḻ magaḷāyt tavvaiyāyp pugaḻāyp paḻiyāy dēvar mēvit toḻum tiruviṇṇagar sērnda pirān pāviyēn manattē uṟaiginṟa paranjudarē*

**Пословный перевод:**

mū ulagangaḷum āy – being \[having as form\] the three layered world (this samsāram, material realm, which is having inferior attributes such as being created, being bound by karma and having the three qualities viz satva (goodness), rajas (passion) and tamas (ignorance)); allan āy – being with nitya vibhūti (spiritual realm) which is opposite of the aforementioned samsāram; ugappu āy munivu āy – being such liking and hatred of such fantastic and inferior entities respectively; pūvil vāḻ magaḷāy – being the desirable lakshmi \[śrī dēvi\]; tavvai āy – being the undesirable jyēśtā (elder sister of lakshmi \[who is popularly known as mūdēvi\]); pugaḻ āy – being the fame; paḻi āy – having blame as his form too; dēvar – nityasūris (eternal residents of paramapadam); mēvi – fitting well; toḻum – praying; tiruviṇṇagar – in tiruviṇṇagar; sērnda – descended; pirān – sarvēśvaran; pāviyēn – I who am having sins which make me turn away from him even when he pursues me rigorously, my; manattē – in the heart; uṟaiginṟa – residing eternally; param sudar – having great radiance due to that

**Перевод:**

**emperumān is being the three layered world and with the nitya vibhūti which is opposite of the aforementioned samsāram, is being such liking and hatred of such fantastic and inferior entities respectively, being the desirable lakshmi \[śrī dēvi\]  and the undesirable jyēśtā, being the fame and having blame as his form too; such sarvēśvaran who is prayed by nityasūris who descended in tiruviṇṇagar, fitting well, is having great radiance due to residing eternally in my heart, who am having sins which make me turn away from him even when he pursues me.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the sixth pāsuram, āḻvār says “Look! Though I rejected him, it was the benefactor who is in tiruviṇṇagar, who united with me by manifesting his qualities and activities to make me never forget him, and became radiant feeling satisfied”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “sarvēśvaran who is having fantastic and inferior entities as his wealth/forms, is having the radiance acquired through humility towards his devotees”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. mū ulagangaḷumāy allanāy ugappāy munivāy pūvil vāḻ magaḷāyt tavvaiyāyp pugaḻāyp paḻiyāy dēvar mēvit toḻum tiruviṇṇagar sērnda pirān pāviyēn manattē uṟaiginṟa paranjudarē*

- *mū ulagangaḷum āy* – Being the controller for the three worlds. \[Three worlds are \] Also explained as krutaka \[The bottom seven layers – atala to pātāla and the three middle layers – bhūr lōka, bhuva lōka and svarga lōka; these are completely destroyed as part of avāntara praḷayam (intermediary deluge at the end of brahmā’s day) and subsequently recreated\], akrutaka \[The top three layers – satya lōka, tapa lōka and jana lōka; these remain in tact during avāntara praḷayam with their residents\] and krutākrutaka \[mahar lōka; this remains in tact during avāntara praḷayam, but the residents shift up to higher layers at that time\].
- *allan āy* – Being the controller for all other worlds. Since it specifically explains these worlds \[of material realm\] and negates it, this implies [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s ownership of nitya vibhūti \[spiritual realm\].
- *ugappāy munivāy* – His mercy and reprimand.
- *pūvil magaḷāyt tavvaiyāy* – śrī \[śrī mahalakśmi, the deity for fortune\] and aśrī \[her elder sister who is the deity for misfortune\].
- *pugaḻāyp paḻiyāy* – The fame acquired by those who are blessed by śrī. The blame acquired by those who are blessed by aśrī.
- *dēvar …* – dēvatās such as indra, while accepting the sacrificial offerings, would stand three yōjanam (1 yōjana is approximately 9 miles) above the ground, turning their face away from the earth, and vomiting \[due to their dislike for the earth\]; but nityasūris, who can’t tolerate even the smell of such dēvatās, reside firmly \[happily\] in tiruviṇṇagar, since it is present in this earth. The benefactor who is residing in such tiruviṇṇagar.
- *pāviyēn manattē* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/), thinking about how emperumān rigorously pursued him in [tiruvāimoḻi 6.2](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/10/thiruvaimozhi-6-2-minnidai/) “*minnidai madavār*“, and how he pulled back, is blaming himself as “*pāviyēn*” (sinner/unfortunate). While nityasūris pursue [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), he pushed them aside and instead pursued me – it was in such situation, I rejected him.
- *manattē uṟaiginṟa* – Now, leaving those nityasūris and their presence in such divine assembly, he arrived in my heart and is staying there permanently.
- *param sudarē* – While there are many abodes for him, instead of thinking of his arrival in my heart as a favour for me, he thinks it is a fortune for himself and hence is shining radiantly. This is the newly acquired beauty in his form after initially worrying in [tiruvāimoḻi 6.2](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/10/thiruvaimozhi-6-2-minnidai/) “*minnidai madavār*” that “what if [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) slips from me!”, subsequently attaining āḻvār and is appearing as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 6.2.10](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/11/thiruvaimozhi-6-2-10-ninrilangu-mudiyinay/) “*ninṟilangu mudiyināy*” (wearing divine crown which is shining firmly).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.3.7. Paranjudar udambay

*paranjudar udambāy aḻukkup paditta udambāy karandum tōnṟiyum ninṟum kaidavangaḷ seydum viṇṇōr sirangaḷāl vaṇangum tiruviṇṇagar sērnda pirān varangoḷ pādam allāl illai yāvarkkum van saraṇē*

**Пословный перевод:**

param sudar udambu āy – Divine form which is enjoyed by his devotees; aḻukku – to be rejected; paditta – complete; udambu āy – having the form of this material universe; karandum – (for the non-devotees) not shining; tōnṟiyum – (for the devotees) shining; ninṟum – being firm (where he is shining); kaidavangaḷ seydum – being uncertain (in other places); āy – being; viṇṇōr – brahmā rudra et al; sirangaḷāl – with their heads; vaṇangum – to bow down; tiruviṇṇagar – in tiruviṇṇagar; sērnda – descended; pirān – sarvēśvaran’s; varam – greatness of not having any thing equal or greater; koḷ – having; pādam – divine feet; allāl – other than; yāvarkkum – for every sentient being; van – very strong, to give protection; saraṇ – refuge; illai – not there

**Перевод:**

**emperumān is having a divine form which is enjoyed by his devotees and a form of this material universe, which are shining and not shining, firm and uncertain; such emperumān descended to be bowed down by brahmā rudra et al with their heads in tiruviṇṇagar; for every sentient being, there is no other refuge than such emperumān’s very strong, divine feet, which are having the greatness of not having any thing equal or greater.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the seventh pāsuram, āḻvār says “Even for the greatest persons, there is no other firm refuge than him”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “The divine feet of sarvēśvaran who has distinct forms for his devotees and others, are the popular refuge for everyone”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. paranjudar udambāy aḻukkup paditta udambāy karandum tōnṟiyum ninṟum kaidavangaḷ seydum viṇṇōr sirangaḷāl vaṇangum tiruviṇṇagar sērnda pirān varangoḷ pādam allāl illai yāvarkkum van saraṇē*

- *param sudar udambāy* – Having distinguished, divine form which is made of sudda satvam (pure goodness). śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 1.9.67 “*tējasām rāśimūrjitam*” (collection of radiance).
- *aḻukkup paditta udambāy* – Having the material realm which is bound by the three qualities (satvam (goodness), rajas (passion) and tamas (ignorance)), as his body.
- *karandum* – Though he is present as antarātmā (in-dwelling super soul) for the material realm, he is protecting them, being unnoticed by them as said in bruhadāraṇyaka upaniśat “*yamātmā na vēda*” (The ātmā who is unaware of paramātmā).
- *tōnṟiyum* – To be seen by those who remain as said in tiruvāimoḻi 8.5.2 “*kāṇa vārāy enṟu enṟu kaṇṇum vāyum tuvarndu*” (those who have their eyes and mouth dried up, pleading for [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s arrival to see them), incarnating as śrī rāma, kriṣṇa et al.
- *ninṟum* – remaining for hundred years, ten thousand years etc during such incarnations.
- *kaidavangaḷ seydum* – Engaging in mischief. That is, while having incarnated, not making śisupāla et al realise his divinity and to let his devotees realise his divinity.
- *viṇṇōr* … – The benefactor who is standing in tiruviṇṇagar who is bowed down upon by brahmā et al thinking “we have fulfilled the purpose of having head”.
- *varam koḷ pādam allāl illai* – the great divine feet  which can be approached by even the most inferior persons.
- *yāvarkkum* … – Even for the greatest of the greats, there is no stronger refuge than those divine feet. All saviours other than [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), will drown along with the bound soul; other than emperumān’s divine feet, there is no stronger refuge. Only those who take shelter of his divine feet, will survive.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.3.8. Van saran surarkkay

*van saraṇ surarkkāy asurarkku vengūṟṟamumāy tan saraṇ niḻaṟkīḻ ulagam vaittum vaiyādum ten saraṇ tisaikkut tiruviṇṇagar sērnda pirān en saraṇ en kaṇṇan ennai āḷ udai ennappanē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

surarkku – for the dēvas (celestial beings) who are favourable; van – indestructible; saraṇ – refuge; āy – being; asurarkku – for the asuras (demoniac) who are unfavourable; vem – cruel; kūṟṟamum – mrutyu (death); āy – being; ulagam – worldly humans who are classified in this manner; than – his; saraṇ niḻal kīḻ – in the shadow of his divine feet; vaittum – placing; vaiyādum – not placing; āy – being; then tisaikku – for the southern direction; saraṇ – refuge; tiruviṇṇagar – in tiruviṇṇagar; sērnda – descended; pirān – being sarvēśvaran; en – to accept me; kaṇṇan – as kriṣṇa; ennai – me; āḷ udai – accepting my service; ennappan – my lord; en – for me; saraṇ – natural refuge

**Перевод:**

**emperumān is the indestructible refuge for dēvas and cruel death for asuras; he is placing and not placing the worldly humans who are classified in this manner, in the shadow of his divine feet; such sarvēśvaran, who has descended into tiruviṇṇagar which is the refuge for the southern direction, accepted me as kriṣṇa and accepted my service as my lord; he is the natural refuge for me.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the eighth pāsuram, āḻvār says “tiruviṇṇagar emperumān is not just my refuge but everything”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “kriṣṇa, who is sarvēśvaran and \[yet\] humble towards his devotees, who has certain aspects for both favourable and unfavourable ones, is the distinguished refuge for me”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. van saraṇ surarkkāy asurarkku vengūṟṟamumāy than saraṇ niḻaṟkīḻ ulagam vaittum vaiyādum then saraṇ tisaikkut tiruviṇṇagar sērnda pirān en saraṇ en kaṇṇan ennai āḷ udai ennappanē!*

- *van saraṇ surarkku āy* – Being the strong protector for dēvas, by himself accepting the arrows shot at them.
- *asurarkku vem kūṟṟamum āy –* For the demoniac people, he is the cruel death personified as said in “*antakan taṇṇīr*” (yama (deity for death) is cool, implying that he is more cruel than death itself).
- *than saraṇ* … – Having the favourable ones such as arjuna et al in the shadow of his divine feet, and pushing away the unfavourable ones such as duryōdana et al, though they have the same relationship with him.
- *then saraṇ tisaikku* – As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 11.82 “*dakśiṇā dik krutāyēna śaraṇyā puṇya karmaṇā*” (The southern direction which was made as a \[sacred\] abode, by that sage agastya who has an auspicious/virtuous history), the benefactor who descended to tiruviṇṇagar, which is considered as the refuge for the southern direction.
- *en saraṇ* – my refuge.
- en kaṇṇan – kriṣṇa who is humble towards me.
- *ennai āḷ udai* – one who is naturally qualified to accept my service
- *en appan* – my benefactor.

ulagam (world) indicates “the elders and the learned persons” who live there.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.3.9. Ennappan enakkay

*en appan enakkāy iguḷāy ennaip peṟṟavaḷāy pon appan maṇi appan muttappan en appanumāy minnap pon madiḷ sūḻ tiruviṇṇagar sērnda appan tan oppārillappan tandanan tana tāḷ niḻalē*

**Пословный перевод:**

enakku – being distinguished for me; en – the cause for my sustenance; appan – father; āy – being; iguḷ – the step mother, who is having the femininity which is opposite to such masculinity; āy – being; ennaip peṟṟavaḷ āy – being my distinguished, real mother who is unlike the step mother who just raises the child; pon appan – manifesting his attractive nature which resembles gold; maṇi appan – manifesting his radiant nature resembling a precious gem (which is greater than gold in radiance and great worth); muttu appan – manifesting the coolness resembling a pearl (which is greater than precious gem in the coolness); en appan um – the benefactor for me (in many ways); āy – being; minna – to shine; pon – golden; madiḷ – by fort; sūḻ – surrounded; tiruviṇṇagar – in tiruviṇṇagar; sērnda – living; appan – being the lord of all; than – for him; oppār il – having no match; appan – great benefactor; than – his; tāḷ – divine feet’s; niḻal – shadow; tandanan – mercifully bestowed

**Перевод:**

**emperumān being distinguished for me, being my father who is the cause for my sustenance, being my step mother, who is having the femininity which is opposite to such masculinity, being my distinguished, real mother who is unlike the step mother who just raises the child, manifesting his attractive nature which resembles gold, manifesting his radiant nature resembling a precious gem, manifesting the coolness resembling a pearl, being the benefactor for me, is living in tiruviṇṇagar which is surrounded by shining golden fort; being the lord of all there, having no match for him, the great benefactor mercifully bestowed me the shadow of his divine feet.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the ninth pāsuram, āḻvār says “While I rejected him, emperumān forcefully gave the shadow of his divine feet, to remove all my fatigue”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “sarvēśvaran who is having contrary entities which are related to him and attractive entities, and who is having no match for his benefactorśip, mercifully bestowed the shadow of his divine feet to me”*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. en appan enakkāy iguḷāy ennaip peṟṟavaḷāy pon appan maṇi appan muttappan en appanumāy minnap pon madiḷ sūḻ tiruviṇṇagar sērnda appan than oppārillappan tandanan tana tāḷ niḻalē*

- *en appan enakkāy* – Being a distinguished lord for me, and the father who is the cause for my sustenance. That is, unlike a father who would sell his child during famine to survive, emperumān is a father who would protect me even at the cost of transforming himself and losing his identification.
- *iguḷ āy* – iguḷai is a way of addressing a friend. It is indicated as “iguḷ” here. This implies – being my friend with whom I can have discussions.
- *ennaip peṟṟavaḷ āy* – Unlike the step mother who will just raise the child, you are being a mother who carries the child for ten months, caring for it and delivering it.
- *pon appan* … – There are some entities which remain the benefactor, but will lead to other enjoyable aspects \[like gold, gems, pearls\]; emperumān favoured me so that he himself remains as all such enjoyable aspects.
- *minnap pon … –* The benefactor who lives in tiruviṇṇagar which is surrounded by a shining golden fort.
- *than oppār il appan* – The great benefactor who has no match when it comes to favouring certain things to others. nanjīyar mercifully gives an explanation to this – when he rigorously pursued me in tiruvāimoḻi 6.2 “*minnidai madavār*“, I pushed him away saying “I don’t want you”; at that time he gave himself saying “Do you know what is good for you? You really need me”.
- *tandanan tana tāḷ niḻalē* – I tried to move away from him saying “I will be alright even with the heat of sunshine, staying away from you”, as said in “*aḻittāy un tiruvadiyāl*” (destroyed with your divine feet), he eliminated my ego with your divine feet, and bestowed the shadow of his divine feet to me. As soon as being touched by the divine feet, one would give up the objects which he considered as his.

## 6.3.10. Nilal veyyil

*niḻal veyyil siṟumai perumai kuṟumai nedumaiyumāy suḻalvana niṟpana maṟṟumāy avai allanumāy maḻalai vāy vaṇḍu vāḻ tiruviṇṇagar mannu pirān kaḻalgaḷ anṟi maṟṟōr kaḷaigaṇ ilam kāṇmingaḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

niḻal – shade which reduces the heat; veyyil – sunshine which causes heat; siṟumai – atomic form which is the ultimate state of smallness; perumai – universal form which is the ultimate state of largeness; kuṟumai – shortness; nedumaiyum – longness; āy – being; suḻalvana niṟpana – movable and immovable; maṟṟum – all other entities; āy – being (sarvaśarīrī – having everything as his body); avai – their qualities; allanum – not having \[unaffected\]; āy – being; maḻalai – babyish; vāy – having sounds; vaṇḍu – beetles; vāḻ – living due to the enjoyment; tiruviṇṇagar – in tiruviṇṇagar; mannu – eternally residing; pirān – sarvēśvaran’s; kaḻalgaḷ – divine feet; anṟi – than; maṟṟu – other; ōr – one; kaḷaigaṇ – protection; ilam – we are not having; kāṇmingaḷ – you can determine (this) for yourself

**Перевод:**

**emperumān is the shade which reduces the heat and the sunshine which causes heat; he is having atomic form which is the ultimate state of smallness and universal form which is the ultimate state of largeness; he is having shortness and longness as his qualities; he is all other movable and immovable entities and yet remains unaffected by such qualities; such sarvēśvaran is eternally residing in tiruviṇṇagar which is inhabited by beetles having babyish sounds, due to the enjoyment there; we are not having any protection other than such sarvēśvaran’s divine feet; you can determine for yourself.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the tenth pāsuram, āḻvār says “Know that there is no protection other than his divine feet”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār completes his instructions saying “We have as our protection, nothing but the divine feet of sarvēśvaran, who is having as his wealth/forms, all movable and immovable entities which are contrary to each other; you analyse and understand”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. niḻal veyyil siṟumai perumai kuṟumai nedumaiyumāy suḻalvana niṟpana maṟṟumāy avai allanumāy maḻalai vāy vaṇḍu vāḻ tiruviṇṇagar mannu pirān kaḻalgaḷ anṟi maṟṟōr kaḷaigaṇ ilam kāṇmingaḷē*

- *niḻal veyyil* – shade which causes coolness and sunshine which causes heat.
- *siṟumai perumai* – atomic and universal qualities.
- *kuṟumai nedumai* – shortness and longness which are part of intermediary dimension.
- *maṟṟumāy* – whatever is left out to be said; everything which is not mentioned explicitly.
- *suḻalvana niṟpana* – animal and plant species.
- *maṟṟumāy* – all other entities which have not been mentioned.
- *avai allanumāy* – Has it not been already explained that emperumān will remain unaffected by the defects of all these entities which are his forms? So, what is being explained here? Here, it says that emperumān does not have the states of transformations which these entities go through. That is, for the cētanas (sentient beings), the emotions (joy, sorrow etc) and for the acētanas (insentient objects), the changes in their forms.
- *maḻalai vāy vaṇḍu vāḻ* – Due to their youthful nature, the beetles which are living in tiruviṇṇagar have very sweet sounds; other than the divine feet of emperumān who is residing in such tiruviṇṇagar, we have no protector.
- *kaḻalgaḷ anṟi maṟṟōr kaḷaigaṇ ilam* – Instead of saying emperumān is our refuge, as he himself said in śrī bhagavat gītā 18.66 “*mām ēkam śaraṇam vraja*” (surrender unto me only), āḻvār is saying that the divine feet are his protection \[bhagavān’s devotees, bhāgavatas are said to be the divine feet of emperumān; so, it can be seen here that āḻvār is highlighting the devotees as his protection\].
- *kānmingaḷē* – This is not exaggeration; you can see for yourself.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.3.11. Kanmingal ulagir

*kāṇmingaḷ ulagīr enṟu kaṇ mugappē nimirnda tāḷiṇaiyan tannaik kurugūrc catakōpan sonna āṇai āyirattut tiruviṇṇagarp pattum vallār kōṇai inṟi viṇṇōrkku enṟum āvar kuravargaḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ulagīr – Oh people of this world!; kāṇmingaḷ – see this; enṟu – saying that; kaṇ mugappē – in front of those who are contrary to each other; nimirnda – grew; tāḷiṇaiyin tannai – sarvēśvaran who permeated into contrary entities in many ways, as he did during the incarnation as trivikrama, who has the divine feet; kurugūr – the leader of āḻvārtirunagari; satakōpan – nammāḻvār; sonna – mercifully spoke; āṇai – in the form of bhagavat ājñā (bhagavān’s commandments); āyirattu – among the thousand pāsurams; tiruviṇṇagar – for tiruviṇṇagar; pattum – decad; vallār – experts; kōṇai – difficulty; inṟi – without; viṇṇōrkku – for nityasūris; enṟum – always; kuravargaḷ – admirable; āvar – will become

**Перевод:**

**sarvēśvaran, permeated into contrary entities in many ways as he did during the incarnation as trivikrama, who has the divine feet, saying “Oh people of this world! see this”, grew in front of those who are contrary to each other; nammāḻvār, the leader of āḻvārtirunagari, mercifully spoke this decad for tiruviṇṇagar among the tousanda pāsurams, in the form of bhagavat ājñā; those who are experts in this decad will always be admired by nityaśūris without any difficulty.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the end, āḻvār says “Those who are well versed in this decad, will become enjoyable for ayarvaṟum amarargaḷ (nityasūris who do not have any ignorance)”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār explains the benefit as “those who can practice this decad will become eternally admired by nityasūris”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. kāṇmingaḷ ulagīr enṟu kaṇ mugappē nimirnda tāḷiṇaiyan tannaik kurugūrc catakōpan sonna āṇai āyirattut tiruviṇṇagarp pattum vallār kōṇai inṟi viṇṇōrkku enṟum āvar kuravargaḷē*

- *kāṇmingaḷ ulagīr enṟu kaṇ mugappē nimirnda tāḷiṇaiyan tannai* – trivikraman [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is having the divine feet which grew in front of them \[people of the world\] after having tricked them as a magician since they won’t agree if he said “I am going to place my feet on your head! Come closer!”.
- *kāṇmingaḷ* – Since they will pull back if he places his divine feet on their heads, he tricked them with the amazing act \[of growing tall suddenly\].
- *kurugūrc catakōpan sonna* – This is considered trustworthy since it is spoken by [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) who enjoyed [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s saulabhyam \[easily approachable\].
- *āṇai āyirattu* – Those who are experts in this decad which explains emperumān’s orderly conduct of this world. *viṇṇōr* – nityasūris, will admire them forever. There is no kōṇai – difficulty/shortcoming in it. How is this possible? How come a nityasamsāri who learns this \[and masters it\] becomes admirable for nityasūris who are untouched by the defects of samsāram? Even while being in paramapadam, muktātmās (liberated persons) can meditate on the material realm considering it to be [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘s wealth and become blissful. This person who is in this material realm, can experience the same feeling while being in this material realm itself. nityasūris will eternally glorify such persons thinking “While being in material realm, how can someone have such experience!”.

In the next article we will enjoy the next decad.

## 6.4 Kuravai aycciyarodu

## 6.4.1. Kuravai aycciyarodu

*kuravai āycciyarōdu kōttadum kunṟam onṟēndiyadum uravu nīrp poygai nāgam kāyndadum uḷpada maṟṟum pala aravil paḷḷip pirān tan māya vinaigaḷaiyē alaṟṟi iravum nan pagalum tavirgilam enna kuṟaivu enakkē*

**Пословный перевод:**

āycciyarōdu – with the covherd girls; kuravai – in tirkkuravai (rāsa krīdā in vrindāvanam); kōttadum – uniting (holding hands with all girls by inserting himself in between each of them, in the shape of a garland strung with different flowers); onṟu – a; kunṟam – hill; ēndiyadum – lifted it up and stood there holding it up for seven days effortlessly; uravu – matured; nīr – having water; poygai – in the pond; nāgam – kāḷiya serpent; kāyndadum – the way he angrily tamed; uḷpada – like those; maṟṟum – other; pala – many \[such acts\]; aravil paḷḷi – the serpent bed on which he was resting; pirān than – kriṣṇa, the benefactor who left it behind, his; māyam – amazing; vinaigaḷaiyē – activities; alaṟṟi – reciting out of overwhelming love; nan – having goodness to facilitate us to think about his qualities; iravum – night; pagalum – day; tavirgilam – not stopping; namakku – for us; enna – what; kuṟai – shortcoming; uṇḍu – present?

**Перевод:**

**kriṣṇa united with the covherd girls in tirukkuravai; he lifted up a hill and stood there holding it up for seven days effortlessly; he angrily tamed the kāḷiya serpent in the pond having matured water; we are reciting these and many such acts of kriṣṇa, the benefactor who left behind the serpent bed on which he was resting, without stopping through night and day which are having the goodness to facilitate us to think about his qualities; what shortcoming is present in us \[who have such experience\]? Implies that there is no shortcoming of limited experience and experience which is stopped.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the first pāsuram, āḻvār says “Induced by love, night and day (continuously), I got to enjoy the activities of kriṣṇa; do I have any shortcoming?”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*In the first pāsuram, āḻvār says “Being induced by love, we continuously spoke and enjoyed the activities of kriṣṇa who has anantaśāyitvam (the quality of resting on serpent bed) which is the root cause for all incarnations; do we have any shortcoming?”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. kuravai āycciyarōdu kōttadum kunṟam onṟēndiyadum uravu nīrp poygai nāgam kāyndadum uḷpada maṟṟum pala aravil paḷḷip pirān than māya vinaigaḷaiyē alaṟṟi iravum nan pagalum tavirgilam enna kuṟaivu enakkē*

- *kuravai āycciyarōdu kōttadum* – Why is [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) directly enjoying this activity of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), instead of starting with his birth in “*piṟandavāṟum*“? Since emperumān’s act of eliminating āḻvār’s romantic anger in “minnidai madavār” and uniting with him subsequently resembles emperumān’s act of giving joy to the covherd girls by performing rāsa krīdā with them, āḻvār is starting with this particular act of emperumān here. Only when āḻvār enjoys them with his own effort, he can go in sequence! When emperumān himself makes āḻvār experience according to his will, āḻvār’s experience would only be random \[as in here\]; emperumān manifested his union with the covherd girls in rāsa krīdā first. The joy emperumān acquired by uniting with the covherd girls from 5 lakh families in vrindāvanam, is acquired just by his uniting with this one āḻvār. Due to his great desire to be with each of the covherd girls, he made himself secondary in the array of covherd girls and held their hands. He is enjoying now as he previously desired in [tiruvāimoḻi 5.10.2](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/09/thiruvaimozhi-5-10-2-vadhuvai-varththaiyul/) “*kuravai piṇainda kuḻagum*“. He mingled with them as one amongst them while staying in between the covherd girls. Usually, girls will hold with each other while playing. Just as the girls could not sustain without kriṣṇa in rāsa krīdā, in “minnidai madavār”, he could not sustain without [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/). kōkkai – stringing together. kuravaik kūttu (rāsa krīdā) is a dance which is done, holding hands together \[forming a circular array\].
- *kunṟam onṟu ēndiyadum* – There is an abode named svargam (heaven) which is focussed on enjoyment; and there exists a person named indra who is reaping the fruits of his puṇya (virtuous deeds) by enjoying with apsaras girls (celestial dancers) ; seeing that kriṣṇa is having the same enjoyment with the covherd girls without any constraints in earth, he becomes jealous and citing “kriṣṇa stopped my feast” as a reason, sent hailstorm; at that time, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) lifted a hill which was within his hands’ reach and stood with it. indra is of the nature that if he sees someone in earth holding their nose (doing anuśtānams, yōga), he will fear for the safety of his throne and will try to disturb him as much as possible by sending these dancer girls. He does not realise that the one who enjoys in this manner is sarvēśavaran (supreme lord) himself; that is because emperumān presented himself as a covherd boy, one amongst the covherd clan. emperumān eliminating the danger for the cows and covherds during that hailstorm is much smaller compared to eliminating the danger for āḻvār in “*minnidai madavār*” \[i.e., āḻvār shunning emperumān\].
- *ēndiyadum* – Since this was done to help others, the hill appears like an ornament for his hand and does not trouble him at all. It appears as if [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is holding a flower in his hand. How amazing that a seven year old boy held up the hill for seven consecutive days!
- *kunṟam onṟu ēndiyadum* – He remained as a sagōtri \[close family member with paternal link\] so that one need not worry “How are we going to pay him back for holding the hill up for seven days when he is only seven years old?”.
- *uravu nīr* – The water having pride due to the depth of the river for which the bottom cannot be easily seen; or, due to the poison from kāḷiya, the water is so strong and unapproachable by anyone; or, since it is an ancient river, the water is strong due to its age.  uravu also means poison.
- *nāgam kāyndadum* – Driving the kāḷiya serpent away. It is after this deed of overcoming kāḷiya that he engaged in water-sports with the covherd girls.
- *uḷpada maṟṟum pala* – There is no count for such activities of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/). In “*piṟandavāṟum*“, he \[āḻvār\] could not speak about all activities due to his weakened state; here he is unable to speak due to overwhelming bliss. There were many such hurdles to unite with the covherd girls, which were eliminated by emperumān.
- *aravil paḷḷip pirān* – The sleep of worldly people is for selfish purpose and due to their tamō guṇam (lethargy, ignorance etc); emperumān’s sleep \[yōga nidrā\] is for the protection of others. He is known as in [tiruvāimoḻi 5.4.11](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/07/thiruvaimozhi-5-4-11-uranguvan-pol/) “*uṟanguvān pōl yōgu seyda perumān*” (emperumān who pretends to be sleeping but really meditating). When he sleeps, it is for the protection of others; when he is awake too, it is for the same purpose. How amazing is his benefactorśip!
- *aravil paḷḷip pirān* – Previously his mismatch with a serpent was explained; here his union with a serpent is explained. There, his discarding of the bhōga (serpent/enjoyment) is explained; here his attachment towards bhōga is explained. He drove away kāḷiya who was inimical; he has as his bed, ādiśēśa who is friendly. ādiśēśa performs services in many different ways and emperumān too accepts his services in many ways. ādiśēśa is known as in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 4.3.10 “*āyiram paindalaiya anantan*” (the thousand hooded ananta).
- *aravil paḷḷip pirān* – Since tiruppāṟkadal (kśīrābdi – milk ocean) is the root for all incarnations, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is explaining it here; alternatively – āḻvār is re-emphasising what he said previously in [tiruvāimoḻi 5.10.11](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/09/thiruvaimozhi-5-10-11-naganai-misai/) “*nāgaṇai misai nampirān saraṇē saraṇ*” (the lotus feet of our lord who is resting on ādiśēśa, is our refuge).
- *than māya vinaigaḷaiyē alaṟṟi* – Praising his amazing activities in the form of stōtrams.
- *iravu nan pagalum tavirgilam* – When \[day and night are\] not favourable for bhagavat anubhavam, they are felt as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 2.1.4](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/11/thiruvaimozhi-2-1-4-kadalum-malaiyum/) “*sudar koḷ irāp pagal*” (night and day which are identified by the radiance (heat) of moon and sun); since these nights and days are favourable for bhagavat anubhavam, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is prefixing them with “*nal*” (good). In separation, they feel like molten fire being poured on.
- *enna kuṟaivu enakkē* – Am I having the shortcoming of having to prepare food \[to consume during the journey\] to go seek for paramapadam where day and night have no effect as said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam “*na kālas tatravai prabhu:*“? In paramapadam, only singular experience \[enjoying his supremacy\] is present; but here, as said śrī rāmāyaṇam bāla kāṇḍam 77.26 “ … *vijahāra bahūn rutūn*” (śrī rāma enjoyed with sītāp pirātti in different seasons without any restraint), I enjoyed [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) matching every season; in such case, do I have any shortcoming? There in paramapadam, only paratva anubhavam (experience of his supremacy) exists; his śeela guṇa anubhavam (simplicity and other qualities) is only available here.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.4.2. Keyat tingulal

*kēyat tīnguḻal ūdiṟṟum nirai mēyttadum keṇḍai oṇ kaṇ vāsap pūnguḻal pinnai tōḷgaḷ maṇandadum maṟṟum pala māyak kōlap pirān tan seygai ninaindu mananguḻaindu nēyattōdu kaḻinda pōdu enakku evvulagam nigarē?*

**Пословный перевод:**

kēyam – using songs (which appear humble); tīm – to be sweet; kuḻal – flute; ūdiṟṟum – played; nirai – cattle; mēyttadum – herded; keṇḍai – like keṇḍai \[a dark coloured fish\]; oṇ – youthful/tender; kuḻal – having divine lock (hair on the head); pinnai tōḷgaḷ – with the divine shoulders of nappinnaip pirātti; maṇandadum – embraced; maṟṟum – further; pala – many pleasant aspects; māyam kōlam – having amazing form; pirān than – kriṣṇa’s; seygai – eternally enjoyable activities; ninaindu – thinking; manam – heart; kuḻaindu – having melted; nēyattōdu – with love; pōdu – time; kaḻindu – spent; enakku – for me; e – which; ulagam – world; oppu – match?

**Перевод:**

**kaṇṇan emperumān played sweet songs with his flute; he herded the cattle; he embraced the divine shoulders of nappinnaip pirātti who is having divine lock which resembles youthful/tender keṇḍai fish; thinking about the eternally enjoyable activities of kriṣṇa who is having an amazing form and many such enjoyable aspects, having a melted heart, I spent my time with love towards him; for me \[who is having such experiences\], which world will be a match? Implies that even paramapadam is not a match. \[Note; kaṇ (eyes) and vāsam (fragrance) are missing in the word-by-word translation\].**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the second pāsuram, āḻvār says “Is there anyone who is comparable to me in tirunādu (paramapadam)?” since his desire was fulfilled as he prayed in triuvāimoḻi 5.9.10 “tollaruḷ nal vinaiyāl solak kūdungol” (Will we be able to praise him by his virtuous deeds out of his mercy?).*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “My time is spent in lovingly meditating upon the heart-melting activities of kriṣṇa who is having an amazing form; are the residents of distinguished paramapadam, where there is constant enjoyment of bhagavān, a match to me?”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. kēyat tīnguḻal ūdiṟṟum nirai mēyttadum keṇḍai oṇ kaṇ vāsap pūnguḻal pinnai tōḷgaḷ maṇandadum maṟṟum pala māyak kōlap pirān than seygai ninaindu mananguḻaindu nēyattōdu kaḻinda pōdu enakku evvulagam nigarē?*

- *kēyat tīm kuḻal ūdiṟṟum* – kēyam (gēyam) – song; tīm – sweetness; sweet songs. He would play songs in the flute which rhyme with the names of the covherd girls he desires to invite.
- *nirai mēyttadum* – He uses the same tool (flute music) to invite the covherd girls and to herd the cows; as he plays his flute, the cows will feel their hunger is satisfied. Just as cakravartit tirumagan (śrī rāma, son of daśarata cakravarti) had mastered the bow in his hand, kriṣṇa has mastered the flute.
- *keṇḍai …* –  sītāp pirātti embraced śrī rāma to heal his wounds after he defeated kara, as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 30.39 and 30.40  “*bhartāram pariśasvajē*“ (embraced her husband); similarly here nappinnaip pirātti glanced at him with her beautiful eyes to relieve him of the fatigue of herding cows, adding fragrance to his divine form with the fragrance from her divine lock and embraced him.
- *keṇḍai oṇ kaṇ* – Cool glance of her very youthful/tender eyes like keṇḍai \[fish\], which feels like flow of nectar.
- *vāsap pūm kuḻal* – One who has specially great lock which is even greater than what is explained in tiruvāimoḻi 10.10.2 “.*.. vāsam sey pūm kuḻalāḷ*” (śrī mahālakśmi who has fragrant lock and who resides in the chest of emperumān).
- *pinnai tōḷgaḷ maṇandadum* – The manner in which emperumān embraced her shoulders. She is known as “*tōḷi*“, one who has overwhelmingly beautiful shoulders.
- *maṟṟum pala* – The manner in which he embraced his other consorts. Just as cakravaratit tirumagan (śrī rāma) has adyayanam (education), ācārya sēvai (serving the preceptors), astra śastra abhyāsa (learning weaponry and military science) , kriṣṇa is always engaged in enjoying his consorts and covherd girls.
- *māyak kōlap pirān* – The amazing decoration of the benefactor who is anointed with the turmeric paste which was passed on from nappinnaip pirātti’s divine body when he embraced her.
- *māyak kōlap pirān* – It can also imply his beautiful posture of being anointed with the turmeric paste and sandalwood paste from the bosoms of his other consorts who are explained in nācciyār tirumoḻi 10.8.7 “*kongai mēl kungumattin kuḻambaḻiyap pugundu orunāḷ tangumēl ennāvi tangum*” (I will sustain myself the day on which he comes and embraces me \[so tightly\] to erase the vermillion paste on my bosoms).
- *than seygai ninaindu manam kuḻaindu nēyattōdu kaḻinda pōdu* – As I start thinking about his activities, my heart will start melting uncontrollably. The state of āḻvārs is as said in tiruvāimoḻi 9.6.2 “*ninai toṟum sollum toṟum nenjidindugum*” (my thoughts, words and mind will tremble).
- *nēyattōdu kaḻindapōdu* – When the time was spent in a sweet manner due to the sweetness of the one who was thought about.
- *enakku evvulagam nigarē* – Is there anyone comparable to me even in a dēśa viśēśam (paramapadam, the divine abode)? Who is a match for me who has sweet bliss during the time of meditation itself as it happens during the actual experience? Are those residents of the spiritual sky a match for me? Since ulagam (lōkam) indicates the noble personalities of the world, here it indicates “nityasūris”.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.4.3. Nigaril mallarai

*nigaril mallaraic ceṟṟadum nirai mēyttadum nīḷ nedungaic cigaramā kaḷiṟattadum ivai pōlvanavum piṟavum pugar koḷ sōdip pirān tan seygai ninaindu pulambi enṟum nugara vaigal vaigap peṟṟēn enakku en ini nōvaduvē?*

**Пословный перевод:**

nigar – match; il – not having; mallarai – wrestlers; seṟṟadum – killed; nirai – behind the cows; mēyttadum – herding them with a stick; nīḷ – tall; nedu – long; kai – having trunk; sigaram – strong like a mountain peak; mā – great; kaḷiṟu – elephant; attadum – killed; ivai pōlvanavum – enjoyable acts like these; piṟavum – many other acts; pugar koḷ sōdi – very radiantly glowing; pirān than – kriṣṇa’s; seygai – activities; ninaindu – meditating upon; pulambi – reciting in a disorderly manner; enṟum – everyday; nugara – to consume; vaigal – time; vaiga – very long; peṟṟēn – got; ini – now; enakku – for me; en – why; nōvadu – would there be any suffering?

**Перевод:**

**kriṣṇa killed the matchless wrestlers; he herded the cows going behind them with a stick; he killed the great elephant which was tall, strong like a mountain peak and having long trunk; I got to consume enjoyable acts like these and many other acts of very radiantly glowing kriṣṇa, meditating upon them and reciting them in a disorderly manner everyday for a very long time; now, for me \[who has such enjoyment\], why would there be any suffering? Am I going to suffer due to lack of time for such experience? ōr am I going to suffer due to the experience lacking enjoyment?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the third pāsuram, āḻvār says “I got to spend all my time enjoying kriṣṇa’s activities; I need not worry thinking that there is something which I have not acquired”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. nigaril mallaraic ceṟṟadum nirai mēyttadum nīḷ nedungaic cigaramā kaḷiṟattadum ivai pōlvanavum piṟavum pugar koḷ sōdip pirān than seygai ninaindu pulambi enṟum nugara vaigal vaigap peṟṟēn enakku en ini nōvaduvē?*

- *nigrail mallaraic ceṟṟadum* – The way he killed the wrestlers who had no match for their strength. There were two boys who are tender-natured due to their herding the cows; they destroyed the wrestlers who were strong like a mountain due to their consuming forbidden foods and their knowledge in warfare/weaponry; just as the movement of worms may lead to art/letters on the sand, this happened naturally \[by divine will\]; otherwise, it is not possible for these two children to overcome the great wrestlers. On that day, everyone feared for [kriṣṇa](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s safety as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 103.6 “*na samam yuddam ityāhu*” (they said that it was a battle between unequal persons). periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 4.2.6 is quoted here. *ēviṟṟuc ceyvān ēnṟedirndu vanda mallarai* – Only if they were independently coming at kriṣṇa, they could step back and withdraw. Since they were subordinate to kamsa and were coming on his orders, if they lost the battle here with kriṣṇa, they would be killed by kamsa; hence, they thought “instead of dying like a coward, we could have a valiant death fighting kriṣṇa” and came at him; *sāvat tagartta sāndaṇi tōḷ caturan* – He fought with them without disturbing the sandalwood paste on his body that was anointed by kūni (the hunchback woman) . Even while wrestling them with his whole body, he ensured that the marks of sandalwood paste did not get disturbed. On top of the anointed sandalwood paste, many girls placed their glance and those cannot be wiped off even by him. Marking their glance on his sandalwood paste anointed body means – applying the marks of their fish, spear etc like eyes on his shoulders. Even if they got disturbed while fighting the wrestlers, they would think that he lost them elsewhere (while enjoying with other girls). If he lost those marks, he would then not be included in the assembly of those girls. ēnṟu edirdu – coming at him with the angry intent to kill him.
- *nirai mēyttadum* – His activities matching his first birth \[as kśatriya, the son of vasudēva\] and the second birth \[as vaiśya, the son of nandagōpa\]; matching his kingly birth, he fought the wrestlers; and matching his covherd birth, he tended the cows. His effort to tend the cows was greater than defeating the wrestlers.
- *nīḷ nedum kai sigaramā kaḷiṟu attadum* – Even if he could escape the wrestlers, he could not  have escaped this huge elephant.
- *nīḷ nedum kai* – Having a lengthy trunk to pull from distance, the individual who tries to escape. While “nedum kai” itself is sufficient to say the lengthy nature of the trunk, “nīḷ” is added to emphasise the great length of the trunk.
- *sigara mā kāḷiṟu attadu* – Does it even need the trunk \[to capture and trash the individual\]? Is it not sufficient to just see the elephant \[and die out of fear\]? It is said in tiruvāimoḻi 8.4.1 “*ānai mā malai*” (the great mountain like elephant) – it is as huge as a mountain peak.
- *attadum* – the manner in which he killed it.
- *ivai pōlvanavum piṟavum* – His acts such as this, killing kēśi (the demoniac horse) etc.
- *pugar koḷ sōdi* – The radiance he acquired after killing kuvalayāpīdam, the mad elephant.
- *pirān* – Benefactor. This is as said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 5.20.54 “*sakya: paśyata*” (The girls who were seeing kriṣṇa kill the elephant said – Friends! See!). \[As said in the same ślōkam\] “… *svētāmbu kaṇikācitam*” (Friends! See kriṣṇa’s divine face which is covered with sweat) – should he sweat like this while fighting with the elephant? \[The girls were relating to how [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) would sweat when he embraced them and thinking\] Both embracing our bosoms and angrily taking on the elephant appear to be the same for him.
- *than seygai ninaindu pulambi* – Thinking about the benefactor’s activities and blabbering it due to overwhelming emotions.
- *enṟum nugara vaigal vaigap peṟṟēn* – Enjoying his activities everyday, I got to spent my time. vaigal – time; vaiga – spending. Alternative explanation – To experience this, the time extended. In this explanation, vaigal means time and vaiga means extending.
- *enakku en ini nōvaduvē* – Do I have the dissatisfaction of not finding a place where the time for enjoyment is contracting or expanding?
- *enakku en ini nōvaduvē* – Whatever suffering [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) undergoes, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) considers that to be his own; that got eliminated. emperumān’s suffering is the suffering for āḻvār whose suffering is eliminated by emperumān himself. When emperumān’s suffering is eliminated, āḻvār’s suffering is eliminated too. Alternative explanation – the suffering which is for the soul \[emperumān\] will also affect the body \[āḻvār\].

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.4.4. Nova aycci

*nōva āycci uralōdārkka irangiṟṟum vanjap peṇṇaic cāvap pāl uṇḍadum ūr sagadam iṟac cādiyadum dēvak kōlap pirān tan seygai ninaindu mananguḻaindu mēvak kālangaḷ kūdinēn enakku en ini vēṇḍuvadē?*

**Пословный перевод:**

nōva – to hurt; āycci – the covherd woman \[mother yaśōdā\]; uralōdu – with the mortar; ārkka – binding him tightly; irangiṟṟum – being immersed in that experience; vanjam – came with mischief (assuming the motherly form); peṇṇai – pūtanā, the demoniac woman; sāva – to kill; pāl – breast milk; uṇḍadum – consumed; Ur – moving towards him, being possessed by a demon; sagadam – wheel; iṟa – to break; śādiyadum – kicked with his divine feet; dēvak kōlam – with divine form; pirān than – kriṣṇa‘s; seygai – activities; ninaindu – thinking about; manam – heart; kuḻaindu – melted; mēva – to fit well; kālangaḷ – times; kūdinēn – attained; enakku – for me; en – what else is; ini – now; vēṇḍuvadu – needed?

**Перевод:**

**kriṣṇa was bound tightly to the mortar by mother yaśōdā, the covherd woman, with the intent to hurt him, and he immersed himself in that experience; he killed pūtanā, the demoniac woman who came with mischief, by consuming her breast milk;  he broke the wheel which moved towards him, being possessed by a demon, by kicking it with his divine feet; thinking about the divine activities of kriṣṇa, my heart melted and had the time to fit well in them; now, what else is needed for me? Implied that the eternal enjoyment itself is the goal.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fourth pāsuram, āḻvār says “For me who got to enjoy kriṣṇa who is obedient to mother yaśōdā and who killed the enemies during such time, there remains nothing to be attained”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “I got to enjoy the childhood activities of kriṣṇa who has a divine form; is there anything more for me to desire for?”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. nōva āycci uralōdārkka irangiṟṟum vanjap peṇṇaic cāvap pāl uṇḍadum Ur sagadam iṟac cādiyadum dēvak kōlap pirān than seygai ninaindu mananguḻaindu mēvak kālangaḷ kūdinēn enakku en ini vēṇḍuvadē?*

- *nōva āycci uralōdu ārkka irangiṟṟu* – When [nanjīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nanjiyar/) explains this pāsuram, the way he says “*nōva*” is very beautiful. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying “*nōva*” as if he the rope was tied to his own divine form and bothered him.
- *āycci uralōdu ārkka irangiṟṟum* – She is not binding him with hatred, but is angry on him out of love; so, as long as there is love, anger would also remain. As said in periya tirumoḻi 8.3.5 “*tāyedutta siṟu kōlukku uḷaindōdi*” (running out of fear for the small stick held by his mother) and in periya tirumoḻi 6.7.4 “*viḷiyāvārkka vimmiyaḻudān*” (due to being angrily bound by his mother, he sobbed) – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is grieving since [kriṣṇa](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) could not even cry out loud \[out of fear\].
- *āycci uralōdu ārkka* – periya tirumoḻi 2.10.6 “*taṟiyārnda karungaḷiṟē pōla ninṟu tadangaṇgaḷ pani malgum tanmaiyānai*” ([emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who appears like a black elephant and having expansive, teary eyes) – it appears as if an elephant is tied to the mortar! He is of the nature where he stood crying there even when bound by a helpless woman, instead of freeing himself. She said as in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 5.6.15 “*yadiśaknōśi*” (free yourself up, if you can).
- *uralōdu ārkka irangiṟṟum* – He became immersed on seeing her binding him to the mortar; if duryōdana \[or some unfavourable person\] binds him, he will think about freeing himself up.
- *irangiṟṟum* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) thinks about [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s grief. irakkam – his attachment \[towards his mother\].
- *vanjap peṇṇaic cāvap pāl uṇḍadum* – Oh my god! what will I \[[āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)\] do, if he remains like that towards the fake mother too?
- *sāvap pāl uṇḍadum* – Unlike rāmāvatāram, where he just caused disability to sūrpaṇākā which caused further harm, here [kriṣṇa](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) killed her completely.
- *pāl uṇḍadum* – Just as he would consume mother yaśōdā’s milk to sustain himself, here too, he consumed pūtanā’s milk to sustain himself \[by killing her\]. He is said in periya tirumoḻi 1.3.1 “*peru mulaiyūdu uyirai vaṟṟa vāngi uṇḍa vāyan*” ([emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who has the mouth which sucked her life through her huge bosom). He consumed her milk as a child would do; but due to his nature, she, who was unfavourable towards him, died.
- *Ur sagadam iṟac cādiyadum* – Instead of being triggered by someone else, \[the demon in the form of\] the wheel, came itself towards him and tried to kill him. If he \[the demon\] is coming in a human form, he may be stopped. From this \[Ur – moving on its own\] we can understand that the demon is trying to fiercely attack [kriṣṇa](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) on his own without the help of anyone else.
- *iṟac cādiyadum* – It is said in tiruvāimoḻi 6.9.4 “*taḷarndum muṟindum sagadavasurar udal vēṟāp piḷandu*” (the body of demon in the wheel, became tired and broke into pieces).
- *cādiyadum* – Though [kriṣṇa](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) effortlessly lifted his divine feet, since its a child’s act, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is praising it greatly. It is said in [tiruvāimoḻi 5.10.3](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/09/thiruvaimozhi-5-10-3-peyyum-punguzhal/) “*pērndōr sādiṟac ceyya pādam onṟāl seyda nin siṟuc cēvagamum*” ( your childish valorous act of mercifully kicking the wheel possessed by the demon, by your reddish divine foot, to be thrown up and be finished).
- *dēvak kōlap pirān than* – He did not do all of these as a worldly person. Since he performed these acts during infant stage, his form appears to be divine for him.
- *than seygai ninaindu manam kuḻaindu mēvak kālangaḷ kūdinēn* – Enjoying his activities, having a melted heart, I got to spend my time without any other expectation. Having melted heart, with the heart focussing well on his activities, I got to spend my times.
- *enakku en ini vēṇḍuvadē* – Now, there is nothing to be attained for me.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.
