## 6.4.5. Vendit tevar irakka

*vēṇḍit tēvar irakka vandu piṟandadum vīngiruḷvāy pūṇḍu anṟu annai pulambap pōy angōr āyk kulam pukkadum kāṇḍal inṟi vaḷarndu kanjanait tunja vanjam seydadum īṇḍu nān alaṟṟap peṟṟēn enakkenna igal uḷadē?*

**Пословный перевод:**

dēvar – dēvas (celestial beings); irakka – prayed; vēṇḍi – out of own desire; vandu – descended (from kśīrārṇavam (milk ocean)); piṟandadum – the way he incarnated; anṟu – on that same day; annai – mother dēvaki who gave birth to him; pūṇḍu – (out of fear towards kamsa) lifted him up and embraced him; pulamba – cried out; vīngu – abundance; iruḷvāy – in darkness; pōy – went; angu – in a place which was under the reign of kamsa; ōr – distinguished (to hide him and raise him, without fear towards kamsa); āyk kulam – in covherd clan; pukkadum – the way he entered; kāṇḍal – the sight of such kamsa; inṟi – not to have; vaḷarndu – grow up; kanjan – kamsa; tunja – to finish; vanjam – mischief; seydadum – did; īṇḍu – from here; nān – I; alaṟṟa – to speak out; peṟṟēn – got; enakku – for me; enna – what; igal – hurdle; uḷadu – is there?

**Перевод:**

**dēvas prayed and emperumān descended out of his own desire and incarnated; on that same day, when mother dēvaki who gave birth to him, cried out, lifted him up and embraced him,  he went into abundant darkness and entered into the distinguished covherd clan, in a place which was under the reign of kamsa; he grew up hiding from the sight of kamsa to finish him through mischief; I got to speak out about all these from here; what hurdle is there from me? If there is any hurdle, it will meet the same end as that of kamsa.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fifth pāsuram, āḻvār says “After mercifully incarnating as kriṣṇa, he grew up without the knowledge of kamsa and killed him; for me who got to enjoy this today, is there any poverty? Also explained as “is there any match for me?”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. vēṇḍit tēvar irakka vandu piṟandadum vīngiruḷvāy pūṇḍu anṟu annai pulambap pōy angōr āyk kulam pukkadum kāṇḍal inṟi vaḷarndu kanjanait tunja vanjam seydadum īṇḍu nān alaṟṟap peṟṟēn enakkenna igal uḷadē?*

- *vēṇḍit tēvar irakka vandu piṟandadum* – It should be read as “*dēvar irakka vēṇḍi vandu piṟandadum*” (As the dēvas prayed, he incarnated willingly). dēvas with great anguish went and prayed to [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) “Without understanding our own strengths and weaknesses, we gave boons to a person to uplift him; but now our residences have been attacked”. And he became desirous to be fathered by some one and took birth as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam bāla kāṇḍam 15.30.1 and 15.30.2 “*pitaram rōcayāmāsa*” (he desired to have daśarata as his father). It is as said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 4.6](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/4-6/) “*ātma māyayā*” (by my will); this means “*ātmēccayā*” (by my own desire); nigaṇḍu (dictionary) “*māyā vayunam jñānam*” (māyā, vayunam, jñānam are synonyms and they all mean emperumān’s amazing ability). [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is anguished by the act of emperumān taking birth, without considering the \[inferior\] state of those who pray for his incarnation and without considering his own \[superior\] state. He would fulfil the desire of his devotee by assuming the form of a mendicant, would not hesitate to do anything for such devotees when he takes birth.
- *piṟandum vīngiruḷvāy* – As said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 5.3.7 “*madya rātrē akilādārē jāyamānē janārdanē*” (the supporter of all worlds, appeared at midnight), piḷḷai uṟangā villi dāsar used to say “kriṣṇa was caught without knowing the dangers, fear for kamsa was well present, and it was due to the darkness, we all survived \[kriṣṇa survived, so, we his dependents also survived\]! So, let us surrender to this darkness”. The same fear which was like death for [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) \[due to separation from [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)\], is now reliśable \[as it was the darkness which saved kriṣṇa\]. This can also be read as “*vīngiruḷvāy pūṇḍu anṟannai pulambap pōy*“; as said in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 5.3.1 “*makkaḷ aṟuvaraik kallidai mōda iḻandavaḷ*” (One who lost her six children by kamsa’s hitting them on rock), she lost her children one after other, as soon as giving birth to them, thinking “I may lose this child as well” and started crying, holding on to his feet. While out of motherly love she cried like that, since he was not nursed by her until then, he left her \[and went to gōkulam\]. *vīngiruḷ* – growing darkness.
- *angu ōr āykkulam pukkadum* – In that situation, there he found a place to grow up, which gives refuge to the fearful!
- *āykkulam* – Those who don’t fear thinking “kamsa is harmful”. They will say “if he lives along peacefully with the citizens, we will let him live, otherwise we will kill him with the plough”.
- *kāṇḍal inṟi vaḷarndu* – How amazing that he grew up hiding from kamsa and his harmful associates!
- *kanjanait tunja vanjam seydadum* – As soon as śrī nārada bhagavān informed, kriṣṇa went immediately without any delay and finished kamsa and his mischievous thoughts. Unlike śrī rāmāvatāram where śrī rāma fought righteous war only, kriṣṇa killed kamsa through mischievous ways.
- *īṇḍu nān alaṟṟap peṟṟēn* – Unlike mother dēvaki who suffered being present at the same time as that of kamsa, now I am able to enjoy without any fear.
- *enakku enna igal uḷadē* – After kamsa is destroyed, do I have any other enemies? igal – enemy. Also said as [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) saying “for me who enjoyed today how he killed kamsa, there is no grief”.

## 6.4.6. Igal kol

*igal koḷ puḷḷaip piḷandadum imilēṟugaḷ seṟṟaduvum uyar koḷ sōlaik kurundosittadum utpada maṟṟum pala agal koḷ vaiyam aḷanda māyan ennappan tan māyangaḷē pagalirāp paravap peṟṟēn enakkenna manap parippē?*

**Пословный перевод:**

igal – in the battle; koḷ – came with focus; puḷḷai – bakāsura (the demon in the form of a crane); piḷandadum – tore his beak; imil – having (prideful) hump; ēṟugaḷ – bulls; seṟṟaduvum – angrily killed; uyar – tallness; koḷ – having; sōlai – well grown; kurundu – kurundu (a type of tree); osittadum – broke; utpada – including; maṟṟum – other; pala – many activities relating to killing the enemies; agal – expansiveness; koḷ – having; vaiyam – earth; aḷanda – measured and eliminated the ego of mahābali; māyan – amazing as trivikrama; en – manifesting the similarity between that trivikrama avatāram and kriṣṇavatāram for me; appan than – the great benefactor, kriṣṇa’s; māyangaḷ – amazing activities; pagal irā – day and night, without any difference; parava – to praise; peṟṟēn – got; enakku – for me; enna – what; manapparippu – grief is there?

**Перевод:**

**emperumān tore the beak of bakāsura who came focussed in battle; he angrily killed the bulls which were having humps; he broke the tall and well grown kurundu tree; including these and many other activities relating to killing of enemies were manifested to me by the great benefactor, kriṣṇa who measured the expansive earth as trivikrama to eliminate the ego of mahābali; having got to praise these amazing activities day and night, without any difference, what grief is there? Implies that only when bhagavat anubhavam is absent, grief will be present.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the sixth pāsuram, āḻvār says “There is no mental grief for me who got to enjoy kriṣṇa’s activities of killing the enemies”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “There is no mental grief for me who got to enjoy kriṣṇa’s activities of killing the enemies and won over the three worlds in his previous incarnation, to eliminate the ego of mahābali”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. igal koḷ puḷḷaip piḷandadum imilēṟugaḷ seṟṟaduvum uyar koḷ sōlaik kurundosittadum utpada maṟṟum pala agal koḷ vaiyam aḷanda māyan ennappan than māyangaḷē pagalirāp paravap peṟṟēn enakkenna manap parippē?*

- *igal koḷ puḷḷaip piḷandadum* – (igal – battle) It just did not appear as a bird, but also was fiercely focussed to fight with kriṣṇa, and kriṣṇa killed it. Though the demon came to kill kriṣṇa, he assumed a bird’s form which will not threaten anyone so that others would not mistake him to be coming to harm kriṣṇa, as said in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 2.5.4 “*paḷḷattil mēyum paṟavai uruk koṇḍu*” (assuming the form of a bird which is gazing in the shallow area).
- *imil ēṟugaḷ seṟṟaduvum* – how he killed the bulls with the humps.
- *uyar koḷ sōlaik kurundu osittadum* – Breaking the kurundu tree which was tall and bushy. It grew out nicely thinking “this will be attractive for children”; kriṣṇa broke it into pieces thinking “let me break it”.
- *utpada maṟṟum pala* – There are many such destroying of enemies by him in this manner.
- *agal koḷ vaiyam …* – Many such amazing activities only of such emperumān who effortlessly measured the expansive earth.
- *pagal irāp paravap peṟṟēn* – Wordly people have divided the time into day and night, to engage in worldly pleasures; for me who got to enjoy emperumān’s activities during both day and night, is there the same mental grief of those who enjoy worldly pleasures? parivu \[paribu\] – grief; even if paribu is read as parippu, it has the same meaning.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.4.7. Manap parippodu

*manap parippōdu aḻukku mānida sādiyil tān piṟandu tanakku vēṇḍuruk koṇḍu tān tana sīṟṟattinai mudikkum punat tuḻāy mudi mālai mārban en appan tan māyangaḷē ninaikkum nenjudaiyēn enakkini yār nigar nīḷ nilattē?*

**Пословный перевод:**

manap parippōdu – with anguish in heart; aḻukku – to be rejected; mānida sādiyil – in human species; tān – himself (who is hēya pratyanīka (opposite to any such defects, rejectable aspects)); piṟandu – even while born as one amongst them; tanakku vēṇḍu – that which he desires; uru – dear forms; koṇḍu – accepting; tān – he (who is caring towards his devotees); tana – his; sīṟṟattinai – anger; mudikkum – one who brings it to an end; punam – having freshness as if being present in its natural place; tuḻāy – having tuḷasi garland; mudi – crown; mālai – that divine garland; mārban – being the one who has the divine chest; en – manifesting such beauty to me; appan than – benefactor’s; māyangaḷ – amazing activities; ninaikkum – obedient, to contemplate; nenju – heart; udaiyēn – me who am having it in a distinguished manner; enakku – for me; ini – now; nīḷ nilattu – in this great earth; nigar – match; Ar – who?

**Перевод:**

**Even while being born as one amongst the human species which is to be rejected with anguish in heart, he accepts dear forms which he desires and brings an end to his anger; he is having tuḷasi garland which is having freshness as if being present in its natural place, on his crown and on his divine chest; for me who am having the amazing activities of such benefactor in my distinguished, obedient heart to contemplate, is there any match in this great earth now?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the seventh pāsuram, āḻvār says “For me who is having the heart which contemplates the activities of emperumān who appeared with his divine entourage being unable to bear the sufferings of his devotees and destroyed their enemies, who is equal in this expansive world?”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. manap parippōdu aḻukku mānida sādiyil tān piṟandu tanakku vēṇḍuruk koṇḍu tān tana sīṟṟattinai mudikkum punat tuḻāy mudi mālai mārban en appan than māyangaḷē ninaikkum nenjudaiyēn enakkini yār nigar nīḷ nilattē?*

- *manap parippōdu aḻukku mānida sādiyil tān piṟandu* – He who eliminates this rejectable human body of the worldly people, himself took birth in such human species. When a child falls into a well, a mother will jump in with anguish and rescue the child. Similarly, he takes birth with anguish thinking “I have not helped them sufficiently”.
- *tān piṟandu* – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is opposite of all defects, entered the womb along with his divine entourage; he who is free from karma, took birth in species which are hated even by those who are bound by karma \[and pushed to such births\]; the reason for this is his kāruṇyam (mercy).
- *tanakku vēṇḍuruk koṇḍu* – With his divine entourage. When he is born like that, would it be limited! People would wonder “dvibhujōvā caturbhujōvā” (Is he with two shoulders or four shoulders!). Only after he gave up his supremacy, he was given space here \[when kriṣṇa was born, vasudēva asks him to hide his four shouldered form and asks him to appear as a normal child, and [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) obliges\]. Since these forms are assumed by him for his devotees, he would like them. They are also based on his own desire.
- *tān tana sīṟṟattinai mudikkum* – While he eliminates the enemies of his devotees, he would feel that his own anger was eliminated; just as a mother would eliminate her anger on those who harmed her child, by harming them. śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 50.136 “*kōpasya vaśamē ivān*” (On seeing hanuman being severely hurt by rāvaṇa, śrī rāma became engulfed with anger).
- *punat tuḻāy mudi mālai mārban* – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) was given a sacred bath after he killed the enemies of the devotees, and was decorated with tuḷasi (tiruttuḻāy) garland on his crown and chest. The tuḷasi garland having come in contact with his divine body, acquired freshness as if standing in its own abode \[plant\]. And, he captured me with such decoration.
- *than māyangaḷē ninaikkum nenjudaiyēn* – I am having a distinguished heart which is contemplating his divine activities unlike an ordinary heart which is said as in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 6.7.28 “*mana Eva manuśyāṇām kāraṇam banda mōkśayō:*” (For humans, mind is the cause for bondage and liberation).
- *enakku ini yār nigar nīḷ nilattē* – Across this expansive earth, is there anyone matching me? Here, he is not considering anyone in paramapadam; since there is no one who can sing verses in praise of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is asking “for me who can serve emperumān through my verses right in this material world, is there any match?”.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.4.8. Nil nilattodu

*nīṇilattodu vān viyappa niṟai perum pōrgaḷ seydu vāṇanāyiram tōḷ tuṇittadum utpada maṟṟum pala māṇiyāy nilam koṇḍa māyan ennappan tan māyangaḷē kāṇum nenjudaiyēn enakkini enna kalakkam uṇḍē?*

**Пословный перевод:**

nīḷ – expansive; nilattodu – earth; vān – sky; viyappa – to the amazement; niṟai – with many strong associates (while bāṇa himself was the real enemy, even those who came to support him such as rudra, subrahmaṇya et al); perum pōrgaḷ – great battles; seydu – performing; vāṇan – bāṇa’s; āyiram tōḷ – the thousand shoulders (which were craving for battle); tuṇittadum – the way he severed; utpada – including; maṟṟum – other; pala – many; māṇiyāy – as a brahmacāri (celibate boy, as a person seeking alms); nilam – earth; koṇḍa – accepted; māyan – mischievous; en – manifesting such mischief to me; appan than – the benefactor, kriṣṇa’s; māyangaḷ – amazing activities; kāṇum – to see in front of me and enjoy the same; nenju – heart; udaiyēn – having; ini – now; enakku – for me; enna kalakkam – what bewilderment; uṇḍu – present?

**Перевод:**

**To the amazement of the expansive earth and sky, performing great battles with bāṇa and his many strong associates, kriṣṇa severed the thousand shoulders of bāṇa; as a brahacāri, he accepted the earth through a mischievous way and manifested that mischief to me; I am having the heart to see in front of me and enjoy these and many other amazing activities of kriṣṇa, the benefactor; now, for me what bewilderment is present? Only for those who don’t have an obedient mind, there would be bewilderment such as svarakśaṇē svānvayam (protecting oneself through self efforts), anyarakśyatvam (being protected by others) etc.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the eighth pāsuram, āḻvār says “For me who is having the heart which constantly thinks about kriṣṇa’s activities starting with his victory over bāṇa, is there any bewilderment?”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “emperumān fulfilled his desire even by accepting alms ; For me who is having the heart which constantly thinks about  the activities of such kriṣṇa starting with his victory over bāṇa, is there any bewilderment?”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. nīṇilattodu vān viyappa niṟai perum pōrgaḷ seydu vāṇanāyiram tōḷ tuṇittadum utpada maṟṟum pala māṇiyāy nilam koṇḍa māyan ennappan than māyangaḷē kāṇum nenjudaiyēn enakkini enna kalakkam uṇḍē?*

- *nīḷ nilattodu vān viyappa* – To the amazement of the residents of earth and heaven. To the amazement of both humans who get amazed easily and celestial beings who remain unchanged for anything due to considering themselves to be great. It appears similar to “*manjākrōśanti*” \[a statement which says that the cot is making noise implying the persons on the cot are making noise\], as “*viyappa*” (amazed) is present subsequently \[earth and sky on their own cannot be amazed due to lacking jñānam, but the residents of earth and sky have knowledge to be amazed\].
- *niṟai perum pōrgaḷ seydu* – Engaging in a great battle without any shortcoming. That is waging a war which made even rudra et al who consider themselves to be supreme to run away after losing the battle.
- *vāṇan āyiram tōḷ tiṇittadum* – The way he eliminated the thousand shoulders of bāṇa which were engaged in unnecessary activities \[of vorśipping other dēvatās\]. [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) eliminated his hands thinking “due to the craving of his hands, he went and vorśipped everyone”.
- *vāṇan …* – emperumān made those hands to be prey for his chakra/army thinking “He wanted to worship someone and hence ended up vorśipping rudra to lose his hands”.
- *vāṇan …* – To make the people of this world engage in apt worship for their hands, he made bāṇa lose his hands as he was vorśipping other dēvatās. This dēham (body) was given to the ātmā (soul) to engage it in the service of bhagavān as said in  śrīviṣṇu darmam “*vicitrā dēhasampattir īśvarāya nivēditum \| pūrvamēva krutā brahman hastapādādisamyutā \|\|*” (Oh brāhmaṇa! To offer oneself and other materials, [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) previously got connected to the amazing body with hands and legs). It is natural for īśvara to punish those who do not use their hands in an apt way. sarvēśvara gave the hands to bāṇa (ātmā) only for surrendering unto him. He then punished thinking “he has not fulfilled it; he tried to overcome me”. For taking shelter of other dēvatā, he got punished immediately. bāṇa did not take shelter of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) not due to lack of ability (hands) but out of pride.
- *utpada maṟṟum pala* – kriṣṇa drove away event those who stood in support of bāṇa. Only after rudra said as in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 5.33.41 “*kriṣṇa kriṣṇa mahābāhō*” (kriṣṇa! kriṣṇa! Oh mighty armed!), bāṇa knew kriṣṇa’s true greatness.
- *māṇiyāy nilam koṇḍa māyan* – Assuming a form which is most apt for accepting alms, where he will survive if he got alms and will meet his end if he did not. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is not usually attracted to śrī vāmanāvatāram \[i.e., any avatāram other than kriṣṇāvatāram\]; but seeing the similarity between vāmana and kriṣṇa in their unmatched beauty, mingling with everyone without any restriction, partiality towards his devotees and the great deeds done by him \[for his devotees\], [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is enjoying śrī vāmana.
- *nilam koṇḍa māyan en appan* – āḻvār thinks that emperumān measured the three worlds only to capture āḻvār himself.
- *appan than māyangaḷai kāṇum nenjudaiyēn* – [nanjīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nanjiyar/) used to say – [piḷḷān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/pillan/) explains “since āḻvār is known to have his heart and senses independently desire for [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 3.8](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/10/thiruvaimozhi-3-8-mudiyane/) ‘*mudiyānē*‘, his heart will independently think and see”. Another explanation – as said in “*katkaṇ*” (external eye) and “*utkaṇ*” (internal eye), heart/mind is also said as “internal eye” – this could also imply that.
- *enakku ini enna kalakkam uṇḍē* – Do I have the bewilderment of “I have not got to see [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)“? Another explanation – I don’t have the bewilderment of considering dēvatāntarams (other dēvatas) as saviours, the bewilderment of doubting emperumān’s saviourśip and the bewilderment of “I can protect myself”.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.4.9. Kalakka el kadal

*kalakka ēḻ kadal ēḻ malai ulagēḻum kaḻiyak kadāy ulakkat tēr kodu senṟa māyamum utpada maṟṟum pala valakkai āḻi idakkaic cangam ivai udai māl vaṇṇanai malakku nāvudaiyēṟku māṟuḷadō immaṇṇin misaiyē?*

**Пословный перевод:**

ēḻ – seven; kadal – oceans; ēḻ – seven; malai – mountains; ēḻ – seven; ulagum – worlds; kalakka – to be fitting well (so that there is no difference between land and water); kaḻiya – to reach beyond the top of the oval shaped universe; kadāy – bring over; tēr – chariot which is a part of the resulting material world; kodu – using; ulakka – upto the end; senṟa – went; māyamum – amazing act; utpada – including; maṟṟum – other; pala – many other activities (such as bringing back the sons of vaidika without any delay etc); valakkai āḻi idakkaic cangam ivai – these distinguished symbols of the chakra (disc) in the right hand and Sanka (conch) in the left hand; udai – having; māl vaṇṇanai – one who is with dark form; malakkum – bewildering him out of bliss; nā – powerful tongue; udaiyēṟku – for me who is having; i – this; maṇṇin – earth; misai – on; māṟu – opposition; uḷadō – is there?

**Перевод:**

**emperumān used the chariot which is a part of the resulting material realm to reach beyond the top of the oval shaped universe which has seven oceans, seven mountains and seven worlds fitting well in it, and reaching up to the end and performed many other such amazing activities. For me who is having the powerful tongue which can bring bliss and bewilderment to emperumān who is having a dark form and having these distinguished symbols of the chakra (disc) in the right hand and Sanka (conch) in the left hand, is there any opposition on this earth? Implies that there is no one who has the speech which steals the heart of īśvara.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the ninth pāsuram, āḻvār says “For me who is having a power of speech which will even cause bewilderment to sarvēśvara, is there any match on this earth?”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “For me who is having the tongue to praise the superhuman activities of kriṣṇa who is having distinguished symbols of supremacy, such as bringing back the children of vaidika, is there any match on this earth?”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. kalakka ēḻ kadal ēḻ malai ulagēḻum kaḻiyak kadāy ulakkat tēr kodu senṟa māyamum utpada maṟṟum pala valakkai āḻi idakkaic cangam ivai udai māl vaṇṇanai malakku nāvudaiyēṟku māṟuḷadō immaṇṇin misaiyē?*

- *kalakka ēḻ kadal ēḻ malai ulagu ēḻum kaḻiyak kadāy* – To cross over the seven oceans, seven mountains and the seven worlds. kalakka – in the same manner. That is, while riding the chariot, he rode it without any distinction on water, mountain or land. Alternative explanation – if kalakka is considered as an attribute for the seven oceans, it is explained as ocean with tides. Another explanation – while crossing over the seven oceans, seven mountains and seven worlds, he agitated them very much.
- *ulakkat tēr kodu senṟa māyamum* – His amazing of skill of riding the chariot which is an effect into the layer of mūla prakruti (primordial matter) which is the cause, without losing its form. ulakka – end.
- *utpada maṟṟum pala* – The amazing acts of how the infant children of the vaidika \[brāhmaṇa\] were carried from here \[to paramapadam\], and how they were brought back in the same manner \[without aging etc\] and how he completed all of these between the morning session and noon session.
- *valakkai …* – When [bhattar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/parasara-bhattar/) was mercifully explaining this, a śrīvaiṣṇava named vaṇ tuvaraip perumāḷ from kanjanūr asked “Is it not sufficient to say ‘*māl vaṇṇanai malakku nāvudaiyēn*‘? What is the hidden reason for [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) using the adjective ‘*valakkai āḻi idakkaic cangam ivai udai*‘? bhattar mercifully replied “āḻvār is saying ‘I am going to shake cōḷēndra singan (the elephant on which [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) rides)’!”. Sanka and chakra are the identities for the supreme lord. āḻvār is saying “I am having the powerful tongue to emotionally charge the supreme lord who is said as in cāndōjña upaniśat 3.14 ‘*avākyanādara:’* (does not speak, ignores \[in paramapadam\])”.
- *māl vaṇṇanai* – The sarvēśvara who is dark in complexion.
- *malakku nā udaiyēṟku* – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is of the nature to be bewildered on hearing [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s words. Just as āḻvār is apt to be bewildered speaking about emperumān, emperumān is apt to be bewildered hearing his words.
- *māṟuḷadō immaṇṇin misaiyē* – āḻvār would not consider the experience in paramapadam as significant since it is natural there \[everyone will be able to enjoy [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) anywhere at all times\].
- *immaṇṇin misai – māṟuḷadō* – To even hypothetically say that there is some one to compare or not, it is possible only in nitya vibhūti (paramapadam) \[So, there is none to compare in this realm\]!

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.4.10. Man misai

*maṇ misaip perum bāram nīnga ōr bhāradamā perum pōr paṇṇi māyangaḷ seydu sēnaiyaip pāḻ pada nūṟṟittup pōy viṇ misait tana dāmamē puga mēviya sōdi tan tāḷ naṇṇi nān vaṇangap peṟṟēn enakkār piṟar nāyagarē?*

**Пословный перевод:**

maṇ – earth’s; misai – on top; peru – great (unbearable even for the all-bearing mother earth); bāram – burden; nīnga – to eliminate; ōr – unique; bhāradam – bhārata; A – that; peru – great; pōr – battle; paṇṇi – causing; māyangaḷ – amazing activities (such as taking up arms giving up his own vow, transforming day into night etc); seydu – performing; sēnaiyai – all the armies; pāḻ pada – to destroy; nūṟṟittu – finishing by surrounding; pōy – ascending on completion of his task; viṇ misai – on the paramākāśam (supreme sky); tana – his distinguished; dāmamē – in the abode; puga mēviya – entered; sōdi than – kriṣṇa who is in a radiant form; tāḷ – divine feet; naṇṇi – approach; nān – I; vaṇanga – serve; peṟṟēn – got to; enakku – for me (who got this throne of servitude and became an emperor of servitude); piṟar – any other; nāyagar – controller; Ar – who?

**Перевод:**

**kriṣṇa who is in a radiant form, caused the great bhāratam battle in order to eliminate the great burden on earth; he performed amazing activities to destroy all the armies by surrounding them; and on completion of his task, he ascended to his distinguished abode on the paramākāśam; I got to approach and serve the divine feet of such emperumān; is there any other controller for me?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the tenth pāsuram, āḻvār says “I do not have the defect of needing another controller as I got to enjoy emperumān‘s merciful descending  into this material realm and returning to the danger-free tirunādu (paramapadam)”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “I got to enjoy kriṣṇa who is of param jyōti (supremely radiant) nature, and who arranged the mahābhārata war to eliminate the burden on earth, and then ascended to his distinguished abode \[of paramapadam\]; is there any other controller for me?”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. maṇ misaip perum bāram nīnga ōr bhāradamā perum pōr paṇṇi māyangaḷ seydu sēnaiyaip pāḻ pada nūṟṟittup pōy viṇ misait tana dāmamē puga mēviya sōdi than tāḷ naṇṇi nān vaṇangap peṟṟēn enakkār piṟar nāyagarē?*

- *maṇ misaip perum bāram nīnga* – The evil persons increased so much that even mother earth who is known as viśvambarā (all-bearing), kśamā (forbearance), poṟai (mercy) and who can tolerate everything could not tolerate them. In tripād vibhūti (paramapadam, which is 3 times bigger than material realm), though there are heavy persons as said in puruśa sūktam 1.18 “… *yatra pūrvē sādyās santi dēvā:*” (Those dēvas in parama padam know that abode as a great one), there is no burden, since they do not have any ahankāram (ego, pride). They have already placed all their burdens on [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/).
- *ōr bhāradamā perum pōr paṇṇi* – Performing the unique, great battle of mahābhāratam.
- *māyangaḷ seydu* – Performing acts such as transforming day into night, taking up arms after vowing not to do so, revealing the secrets of the enemies etc.
- *sēnaiyaip pāḻ pada nūṟṟittup pōy* – Vowed to turn the armies into dust. It is said in mahābhāratam rājasūya parvam “*yasya mantrī ca gōptā ca suhrutcaiva janārdana:*” (janārdana who is the lord of all the worlds and is the minister, protector and friend of arjuna). Since they said “we will not let kriṣṇa take up arms”, he defeated them through cunning ways.
- *pōy viṇ misait tana dāmamē puga mēviya sōdi than tāḷ* – āḻvār is rejoicing thinking “He ascended to paramapadam leaving their \[devotees\] abode \[samsāram\] only after eliminating their enemies!”. Leaving this abode where they place a fake throne \[to kill him\], they hurl insults on him etc and ascending to the abode where everyone cares for him only! mahābhāratam mauśala parvam “*krutvā pārāvataraṇam …*” \[The wide eyed kriṣṇa eliminated the burden of the earth\]. *prutivyā: pārāvataraṇam – krutvā – prutu lōcana: – mōhayitvā jagat sarvam –* He flattened the unfavourable ones with his stick and the favourable ones with his divine eyes. *gatas svam stānam uttamam* – \[ascended to his supreme abode\] *viṇ misait tana dāmamē puga*. *uttamam* – Instead of having to fear for the dangers caused by kamsa, duryōdana et al, entered the abode where everyone cares for him. On a tīrtam day \[tīrtavāri – the last day of utsavam\], mudaliyāṇḍān and embār met, said “[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) came with his most tender divine \[arcā (deity)\] form, went around for 10 days amidst many crores of people who are filled with ahankāram (ego) and mamakāram (possessiveness)”, offered obeisances to each other and embraced each other – nanjīyar mercifully used to say that he personally witnessed it.
- *naṇṇi nān vaṇangap peṟṟēn* – Unlike kālayavana and jarāsanda who approached [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) to fight with him, I approached him properly \[with humble attitude\].
- *enakkār piṟar nāyagarē* – Who \[else other than emperumān\] is the controller for me who could enjoy starting with his birth, his favours to his devotees by escaping the dangers which were aimed at him, and finally entered his own divine abode? It appears that āḻvār has forgotten what he said in [tiruvāimoḻi 3.7.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/09/thiruvaimozhi-3-7-1-payilum-sudaroli/) “*payilum tiruvudaiyār yavarēlum*” (anyone who has the wealth of vorśipping emperumān); but then, āḻvār does not treat them as others \[i.e., different from himself\].

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.4.11. Nayagan

*nāyagan muḻu ēḻulagukkumāy muḻu ēḻulagum tan vāyagam pugavaittumiḻndavaiyāy avai allanumām kēsavan adi iṇai misaik kurugūrc catakōpan sonna tūya āyirattu ippattāl pattarāvar tuvaḷ inṟiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

muḻu ēḻ ulagukkum – for all worlds; nāyagan – controller; āy – being; muḻu ēḻ ulagum – the worlds which are controlled; than – his; vāyagam – inside his mouth; puga – to enter; vaittu – keep; umiḻndu – spit out; avaiyāy – having them as his body; avai allanum – being untouched by their defects; Am – being; kēsavan – kriṣṇa, who killed kēśi (the demon in the form of a horse); adi iṇai misai – on the divine feet; kurugūrc catakōpan – āḻvār; sonna – mercifully spoke; tūya – faultless; āyirattu – thousand pāsurams; ip pattāl – by this decad (which highlights the kriṣṇāvatāram); tuvaḷ inṟip pattar āvar – will be endowed with ananya prayōjana bhakti (devotion without any other expectation) towards kriṣṇa

**Перевод:**

**nammāḻvār mercifully spoke this decad among the thousand pāsurams on the divine feet of kriṣṇa, who killed kēśi. kriṣṇa, who is the controller of all worlds, made the worlds which are controlled, enter through his mouth, kept them safely and spat them out, having all of them as his body and still being untouched by their defects; by this decad, one will be endowed with ananya prayōjana bhakti towards kriṣṇa.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the end, āḻvār says “Those who learned this decad which speaks about kriṣṇa’s activities, will become an exclusive devotee of kriṣṇa like himself”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār explains the result as becoming an exclusive devotee of bhagavān on having connection with this decad.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. nāyagan muḻu ēḻulagukkumāy muḻu ēḻulagum than vāyagam pugavaittumiḻndavaiyāy avai allanumām kēsavan adi iṇai misaik kurugūrc catakōpan sonna tūya āyirattu ippattāl pattarāvar tuvaḷ inṟiyē*

- *nāyagan* … – Being the controller of all cētanas (sentient beings) and acētanas (insentient entities) , protecting them all by placing them in his divine stomach during deluge, letting them out so that they are not compressed for space inside, having them all as his body to have them identified as “tān” (himself) in all states and forms, and being untouched by their defects even when he has them all as his body.
- *kēsavan adi iṇai misai* – On the divine feet of sarvēśvara who is the killer of kēśi. It is explained \[by [pūrvācaryas](http://acharyas.koyil.org/)\] that “[āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is speaking together the supremacy which was explained in the previous decad and kriṣṇāvatāram where emperumān killed kēśi which is explained in this decad and concludes here in this manner”. Another explanation – also explained as speaking about kriṣṇa’s aspects/activities only as said in mahābhāratam sabhā parvam 38.23 “*kriṣṇa Eva hi lōkānām*” (kriṣṇa is the cause for all worlds).
- *tūya āyirattu ippattāl pattar āvar tuvaḷ inṟiyē* – Those who practice this decad will become like [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/). Due to the presence of this decad, the thousand pāsurams are having purity; alternatively – among the thousand pāsurams, since this decad speaks about kriṣṇa’s activities, it can be said as the decad which is having purity.
- *tuvaḷ inṟiyē pattar āvar* – tuvaḷ means defect. That is, instead of seeking out other incarnations of emperumān, they will immerse in kriṣṇāvatāram only.

In the next article we will enjoy the next decad.

## 6.5 Tuvalil ma mani madam

## 6.5.1. Tuvalil ma mani madam

*tuvaḷil mā maṇi mādam ōngu tolaivillimangalam toḻum ivaḷai nīr ini annaimīr! umakkāsai illai viduminō tavaḷa oṇ sangu cakkaram enṟum tāmarait tadangaṇ enṟum kuvaḷai oṇ malark kaṇgaḷ nīr malga ninṟu ninṟu kumuṟumē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tuvaḷ il – unblemiśed; mā – precious/valuable; maṇi – built with ruby; mādam – mansions; ōngu – highrise; tolaivillimangalam – tiruttolaivillimangalam; toḻum – vorśipping; ivaḷai – parānguśa nāyaki; nīr – you who brought her over and showed her; ini – after she having become greatly attached; annaimīr – who remain “we who have given birth to her can order her”; umakku – for you; āsai – desire to control her; illai – should not have; vidumin – give up the thought that she is obedient; tavaḷam – \[davaḷa\] having white colour; oṇ – attractive; sangu – divine conch; cakkaram – divine disc; enṟum – saying; tāmarai – like a lotus; tadam – very expansive; kaṇ – divine eyes; enṟum – saying; kuvaḷai – neydal plant’s; oṇ – beautiful; malar – flower like; kaṇgaḷ – eyes; nīr – tears; malga – to overflow; ninṟu ninṟu – sustaining (the self, moment after moment); kumuṟum – weep internally being unable to cry out loudly to express her sorrow

**Перевод:**

**Oh mothers! You brought parānguśa nāyaki over to tiruttolaivillimangalam which is built with highrise mansions built with unblemiśed, precious/valuable ruby gems and showed her the same; subsequently she has become greatly attached to that \[divine abode\]; you who remain “we who have given birth to her can order her” should not have the desire to control her and give up the thought that she is obedient; talking about the attractive white divine conch and divine disc and very expansive, lotus, divine eyes \[of emperumān\], she is having tears in her beautiful neydal flower like eyes, sustaining herself and is weeping internally being unable to cry out loudly to  express her sorrow. davaḷa (whiteness) and oṇmai (attractiveness) can be considered as attributes for Sanka and chakra respectively.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the first pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki‘s friend says to the divine mothers of parānguśa nāyaki “You who showed her tiruttolaivillimangalam knowing her nature well, trying to advice her now \[to come back\] is of no use”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*In the first pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki‘s friend says to the divine mothers of parānguśa nāyaki “You should not desire for her who has enjoyed the tiruttolaivillimangalam  where aravindalōcanan emperumān is residing and got captured in his distinguished symbols, please give up”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*In the first pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki‘s friend says to the divine mothers of parānguśa nāyaki “You who showed her tiruttolaivillimangalam not knowing her nature well, trying to advice her now \[to come back\] is of no use”. tuvaḷil mā maṇi mādam ōngu tolaivillimangalam toḻum ivaḷai nīr ini annaimīr! umakkāsai illai viduminō tavaḷa oṇ sangu cakkaram enṟum tāmarait tadangaṇ enṟum kuvaḷai oṇ malark kaṇgaḷ nīr malga ninṟu ninṟu kumuṟumē*

- *tuvaḷil* – Are you trying to pull back someone who is engaged with [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is in śrīvaikuṇṭam saying “he will not come due to the great distance”, or emperumān’s avatārams saying “they are from different times” or emperumān who is residing inside the divya dēśams which are his dear abodes? How can we pull her back who is attached to the nearby tiruttolaivillimangalam? How can she, who is in ultimate state, be pulled back by those who are in beginner’s state? tuvaḷ – blemish. Not having that. Only if there is any blemish in the matters related to this divya dēśam, she can be pulled back. Here, tuvaḷil indicates that the gems did not have any blemish to start with. While both jīvātmās \[muktātmās (liberated souls)\] and paramātmā (emperumān) have eight qualities such as apahatapāpmatvam (free from defects), for jīvātmās, there were defects and were eliminated \[as part of liberation\] by bhagavān’s grace; but paramātmā is untouched by defects ever; the gems on the mansions of this divya dēśam are similar to paramātmā.
- *mā maṇi* – Not just its radiance, even its price is quite high.
- *ōngu* – The shadow from the mansions in tiruttolaivillimangalam will reach up to āḻvārtirunagari. The lord went away from her \[to tiruttolaivillimangalam\] saying “its just close by”. He separated from her, while they were under the shadow of the palace. She remained constantly looking at the divya dēśam, the mansions and the gems in those mansions, right from the day he separated, without even blinking.
- *tolaivillimangalam* – She liked everyone in the divya dēśam.
- *toḻum ivaḷai* – “toḻugai” (vorśipping with joined palms) is the identity for her as said in “he is blackish, he is whitish and so on”. As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 4.42 “*prānjalim prahvamāsīnam*” (lakśmaṇa who has joined palms and is seated); as said in periya tirumoḻi 8.2.9 “*kaṇapuram kai toḻum piḷḷai*” (the child who is vorśipping tirukkaṇṇapuram with joined palms).
- *ivaḷai* – How come you are trying to pull her back! If you realize her state/form, would you try to pull her back!
- *toḻum ivaḷai* – Why are you trying to pull her back even after seeing her state yourself?
- *ivaḷai nīr* – She is setting out to be blamed \[as being totally dedicated to [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)\] and you are trying stop her from such blame.
- *ini* – One should try to pull back a person before such person acquires vorśipping emperumān as the exclusive daily routine.
- *annaimīr* – īsn’t there some thing called fully immersing in bhagavat viśayam? Should you only see controller-controlled mood? Though you are her mothers, can you engage in undesirable aspects?
- *umakku āsai illai* – Do the parents have any scope over youthful children? Should you try to pull her back instead of being attached to her likes?
- *viduminō* – It will be apt for you to give up now. Mothers will not easily give up if they are told “give up now”; they further requested the friend to help and she said “you see her emotions; don’t be a block in her experience”. When asked “why are you telling us to give up?”, the friend explains “Do you see anything in her speech or mind about us or me? Her state is as explained in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 17.14 ‘*tyaktvā putrāmśca dārāmśca*‘ (vibhīśaṇa has given up his children and wife)”.
- *tavaḷa oṇ sangu* – The Sanka (conch) which has a contrasting white colour to his black complexion and which is beautiful as said in nācciyār tirumoḻi 7.8 “*uṇbadu sollil ulagaḷandān vāyamudam*” (The divine conch’s food is the nectar from the mouth of trivikrama who measured the world).
- *cakkaram* – The disc which is having unlimited beauty which cannot be explained with just one or two attributes \[as done for Sanka\].
- *enṟum* – She is unable to say “I want to see them”; she is unable to say “I want him to come with these”, due to lack of strength.
- *tāmarait tadam kaṇ enṟum* – The divine eyes which expand up to those āḻvārs \[conch and disc which are nityasūris and immersed in bhagavān\]; lotus is no match to his eyes, yet used as a simile; they are much more enjoyable than what the enjoyers can enjoy,
- *enṟum/enṟum (repetition)* – Speaking sporadically with breaks in between each word, feeling heavy as if lifting up a mountain. [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) won over her by manifesting his divine weapons and divine eyes.
- *kuvaḷai* … – If one sees her eyes, they will wonder “Is it fair to let tears flow from these lotus like expansive eyes?”, “Is it fair for you to remain undisturbed seeing her state with teary eyes?”. śrīviṣṇu tatvam “*āhlāda śīta nētrāmbu:*” (One who is having cool happy tears due to blissful experience of bhagavān etc – the purpose of everyone is to see such persons). We need not go to paramapadam to keep seeing \[divine sight of [parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is right here\]. While she crossed her femininity \[of seeking out external experience\], how can you pull her back? Crying out with tears is explained as crossing the limits of femininity \[one should be able to control herself\].
- *ninṟu ninṟu kumiṟumē* – How can you pull her back as she stopped speaking and started crying and even beyond that staggering \[being unsteady\]? In a king’s assembly, when some said “ugum, iṟum” \[melt, fall down out of fatigue – when words are separated as ninṟugum, ninṟiṟum\], vikramasinga said “No, that is not the case. Here, she is controlling her tears out of great internal sorrow. Just as a mother cow will suffer internally due to her calf which is tied down separately not consuming its milk, here she is suffering internally \[and not able to even cry out anymore\]”. Just as a twirl in a flood \[which works within\], she too will control her emotions and not reveal them. By “*tolaivillimangalam toḻum*“, her physical servitude is explained. By saying “*tavaḷa oṇ sangu cakkarama enṟum tāmarait tadam kaṇ enṟum*“, her servitude through speech is explained. By “*kumiṟum*“, her servitude through mind is explained.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.5.2. Kumirum osai

*kumiṟum ōsai viḻavolit tolaivillimangalam koṇḍu pukku amudamen moḻiyāḷai nīr umakku āsai inṟi agaṟṟinīr timir koṇḍāl ottu niṟkum māṟṟivaḷ dēva dēva pirān enṟē nimiyum vāyodu kaṇgaḷ nīr malga nekkosindu karaiyumē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kumiṟum – profound; ōsai – having many different sounds; viḻavoli – having grand festivities; tolaivillimangalam – in tiruttolaivillimangalam; koṇḍu – brought; pukku – entered; amudam – nectar-like reliśable; men – tender; moḻiyāḷai – parāṇguśa nāyaki who is having \[such tender\] speech; nīr – you (who know the sweetness of her speech); umakku – for you; āsai – desire (for that sweet speech); inṟi – due to not having; agaṟṟinīr – made her lose your relationship; ivaḷ – she; timir koṇḍāl ottu – like being proud; niṟkum – remained silent; maṟṟu – (if she speaks) otherwise; dēvar – nityasūris who are divine beings; dēvar – viśvaksēna et al who are leaders; pirān – the benefactor who lets them enjoy; enṟē – only utters those words reflecting; nimiyum – curved; vāyodu – having mouth; kaṇgaḷ – eyes; nīr – tears; malga – to overflow; nekku – being broken; osindu – weakened; karaiyum – melted

**Перевод:**

**You brought parāṇguśa nāyaki who is having nectar-like reliśable and tender speech and entered tiruttolaivillimangalam which is having grand festivities with many different profound sounds, due to not having desire (for such sweet speech), and made her lose your relationship; she remained silent as if being proud; otherwise she is having a curved mouth which only utters those words reflecting the benefactor who lets viśvaksēna et al who are leaders of nityasūris who are divine beings, enjoy him. She has overflowing tears in her eyes, being broken, weakened and melted.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the second pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki‘s friend says “Would any one bring her to tiruttolaivillimangalam during festivals?”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, parānguśa nāyaki‘s friend says “You have brought her to the great festival at tiruttolaivillimangalam where dēvapirān who is enjoyed by nityasūris, is mercifully residing, and let her slip away”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. kumiṟum ōsai viḻavolit tolaivillimangalam koṇḍu pukku amudamen moḻiyāḷai nīr umakku āsai inṟi agaṟṟinīr timir koṇḍāl ottu niṟkum māṟṟivaḷ dēva dēva pirān enṟē nimiyum vāyodu kaṇgaḷ nīr malga nekkosindu karaiyumē*

- *kumiṟum ōsai viḻavoli* – The grand festivities have the reverberating sounds of those who recite vēdam, those who sing classical music, those who sing songs, those who recite pāsurams etc which make it impossible for one to distinguish among letters, words and meanings as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 6.8 “*tēśām puṇyāhagōśōta gambhīra madurasvana: \| ayōdyām pūrayāmāsa tūryānādānunādita: \|\|*” (The sound of vēda mantram recitations of the vaidikas along with the sound of the musical instrument tūriya, spread everywhere in ayōdyā). My goodness! Should one not retain their daughters on hearing this sound! It appears that the sound implies “this place will take away your child”. Seeing the town, the residents of the town and the festivities which are enjoyed there, would any one bring her there?
- *koṇḍu pukku* – You knowing well about her and still bringing her there.
- *amuda men moḻiyāḷai* – Her speech is such that, it will give immortality to those who listen to that \[implies that those who listen to tiruvāimoḻi will reach paramapadam and will not return\]. You have become unfortunate not to hear her speech. That is, after entering tiruttolaivillimangalam, she stopped talking to them. Her speech is as described in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 66.15 “*madurā madurālāpā*” (one who is beautiful and speaking sweet words). One who desired to listen to her speech, acquired her.
- *men moḻi* – Difference from amrutam (nectar). amrutam cannot be heard; it can only be tasted. Tenderness is only present in this \[her speech\].
- *nīr umakku āsai inṟi agaṟṟinīr* – You who have heard her speak and have let her slip from you.
- *timir koṇḍāl ottu niṟkum* – She remained silent being unable to enjoy the enjoyable emperumān as said in “*stabdōsi*” (stunned). Also explained as having become fully enlightened and remained silent as said in “*stabdōsyuta*” (stunned).
- *maṟṟu ivaḷ* – If she speaks anything more now …
- *dēva dēva pirān enṟē* – Even while seeing emperumān here she only thinks “the lord of nityasūris who doesn’t have any ignorance, appeared here being easily approachable”. Is it possible to redeem her, whose speech matches emperumān’s supremacy?
- *enṟē nimiyum* – Starting to speak about his simplicity saying “Such great emperumān is manifesting such simplicity here”, she will be unable to complete the words, and have her lips twirl. With twirling lips and teary eyes.
- *nekku* – becoming broken
- *osindu* – becoming overwhelmed with emotions
- *karaiyum* – melted to become fluid.
- *nekku osindu kariyumē* – As the bank will lose its form during a great flood after loosening and giving up its strength, parānguśa nāyaki too melted to be not seen in her whole form.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.5.3. Urai kol

*karai koḷ paim poḻil taṇ paṇait tolaivillimangalam koṇḍu pukku urai koḷ in moḻiyāḷai nīr umakkāsai inṟi agaṟṟinīr tirai koḷ pauvattuc cērndadum tisai jñālam tāvi aḷandadum niraigaḷ mēyttadumē pidaṟṟi nedungaṇ nīr malga nīṟkumē*

**Пословный перевод:**

karai – the divine porunal \[another name of tāmirabharaṇi river\] bank; koḷ – to consume \[overshadow\]; pai – expansive; poḻil – garden; taṇ – cool; paṇai – fertile field, water body; tolaivillimangalam – in tiruttolaivillimangalam; koṇḍu – bringing; pukku – entering; urai koḷ – praised by the world; in – sweet; moḻiyāḷai – one who is having speech; nīr – you (who know the greatness of her speech); umakku – for you; āsai – desire in that; inṟi – without; agaṟṟinīr – you made her go far away; tirai – the waves which kept rising due to coming in contact with him; koḷ – having; pauvattu – in the ocean; sērndadum – how he rested there (for the protection of his devotees); tisai – having directions; jñālam – earth; tāvi – extending his leg; aḷandadum – how he measured and made it exist for himself; niraigaḷ – herds of cow; mēyttadumē – the simplicity of tending them; pidaṟṟi – blabbering it (being emotionally overwhelmed); nedu – expansive; kaṇ – eyes; nīr – tears; malga – to overflow; niṟkum – remained stunned

**Перевод:**

**tiruttolaivillimangalam is having cool fertile field, water body and expansive garden which consumes the divine porunal \[another name of tāmirabharaṇi river\] bank; you entered there bringing her who is having sweet speech which is praised by the world, and you made her go afar, without any desire in such speech; and she remained stunned with tears overflowing in her expansive eyes, blabbering about how he rested in the ocean which is having the waves which kept rising due to coming in contact with him, how he measured the earth having different directions by extending his legs and made it exist for himself, and his simplicity of tending the herds of cows.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the third pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki‘s friend says “While you bring her to tiruttolaivillimangalam, you brought her through the divine garden and spoiled her further \[in her engagement with the divya dēśam\]”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, parānguśa nāyaki‘s friend says “You have shown her the divya dēśam which is having garden and fertile field which is inhabited by sarvēśvaran who is having activities for the protection \[of his devotees\]”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. karai koḷ paim poḻil taṇ paṇait tolaivillimangalam koṇḍu pukku urai koḷ in moḻiyāḷai nīr umakkāsai inṟi agaṟṟinīr tirai koḷ pauvattuc cērndadum tisai jñālam tāvi aḷandadum niraigaḷ mēyttadumē pidaṟṟi nedungaṇ nīr malga nīṟkumē*

- *karai koḷ paim poḻil* – The garden has consumed the divine banks of tāmirabharaṇi river. Just as the garden has consumed the river bank, she is consumed by [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s qualities. Only when you can shake that divine garden with your advice, you can shake her state of mind! Entering into tiruttolaivillimangalam  which has vast garden and cool water bodies, bringing her along.
- *urai koḷ in moḻiyāḷai* – Instead of enjoying her sweet speech, you yourself pushed her away. Five meanings explained for this.
   - Sweetness of the speech which will overshadow śrī rāmāyaṇam which is glorified as in bāla kāṇḍam 4.8 “*pātyē gēyē ca maduram*” (sweet for reading and singing with tune).
   - Instead of having to understand the meanings, just the speech itself is sufficient \[to enjoy\].
   - The speech which is praised by the world as “amazing words! amazing speech!”.
   - The speech which has no alternative to win over it.
   - The speech which fits the poetry rules quite well.
- *umakku āsai inṟi agaṟṟinīr* – Bringing her to tiruttolaivillimangalam is the same as giving up attachment towards her \[since she will not come back from there\]. So, you brought her there with the intent of not having her anymore.
- *tirai koḷ …* – The manner in which he mercifully rested in tiruppāṟkadal (milk ocean) which has rising waves due to coming in contact with him, to hear the cries of brahmā et al; and the manner in which he measured the world to redeem the property of indra after hearing their cries.
- *tisai jñālam tāvi aḷandaduvum* – How he accepted alms and measured the earth with different directions,
- *tisai jñālam tāvi aḷandaduvum* – He measured the earth with the desire to protect indar et al. tisai – dik – desire. The earth is desiring “let me be touched with his divine feet”. The desire of earth stretches up to its directions. Not just that, in addition to other incidents, [parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) called him out by highlighting in an disorderly manner his tending of cows which are prime example for ignorance \[We can recollect “*jñānēna hīna: paśubhis samāna:*” (an ignorant human is as good as an animal), here paśu means animal, yet bodes well with the explanation\].
- *nedum kaṇ nīr malga* – The expansive eyes became filled with tears everywhere.
- *niṟkumē* – Being unable to even utter anything, she remained stunned as if this teary eyed form is her natural form.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.5.4. Nirkum nanmarai vanar

*niṟkum nānmaṟai vāṇar vāḻ tolaivillimangalam  kaṇḍa pin aṟkam onṟum aṟavuṟāḷ malindāḷ kaṇḍīr ivaḷ annaimīr kaṟkum kalvi ellām kadal vaṇṇan kaṇṇa pirān enṟē oṟkam onṟum ilaḷ ugandugandu uḷmagiḻndu kuḻaiyumē*

**Пословный перевод:**

niṟkum – being eternal; nāl – classified into four; maṟai – in vēdams; vāṇar – experts; vāḻ – living well (due to bhagavat anubhavam); tolaivillimangalam – tiruttolaivillimangalam; kaṇḍa pin – after seeing; aṟa – good; aṟkam – control; onṟum – any; uṟāḷ – not having; ivaḷ – she; malindāḷ – became uncontrollable; annaimīr – you who gave birth to her and raised her; kaṇḍīr – have seen!; kaṟkum – reciting; kalvi – words; ellām – everything; karu – blackish; kadal – like an ocean; vaṇṇan – having the form; kaṇṇan – kriṣṇa who is humble towards his devotees; pirān – great benefactor; enṟē – as; onṟum – in any manner; oṟkam – control; ilaḷ – not having; ugandu ugandu – becoming more joyful due to meditating upon such aspects; uḷ – in heart; magiḻndu – with great joy; kuḻaiyum – weakened

**Перевод:**

**After seeing tiruttolaivillimangalam which is inhabited by experts in eternal vēdam which is classified into four, she is not having control in anything and has become uncontrollable.  You \[her mothers\], who gave birth to her and raised her, have seen! Everything she recites is about kriṣṇa, the great benefactor who is humble towards his devotees and is having an ocean like blackish form; she is not having any control and is becoming more joyful due to meditating upon such aspects; with great joy in her heart, she has weakened.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fourth pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki‘s friend says “The day she saw tiruttolaivillimangalam and the abundance of śrīvaiṣṇavas there, she broke her shackles”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, parānguśa nāyaki‘s friend says “After seeing tiruttolaivillimangalam which is the abode of his distinguished devotees, she became uncontrollable”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. niṟkum nānmaṟai vāṇar vāḻ tolaivillimangalam  kaṇḍa pin aṟkam onṟum aṟavuṟāḷ malindāḷ kaṇḍīr ivaḷ annaimīr kaṟkum kalvi ellām kadal vaṇṇan kaṇṇa pirān enṟē oṟkam onṟum ilaḷ ugandugandu uḷmagiḻndu kuḻaiyumē*

- *niṟkum nānmaṟai* – The four vēdams which are eternal. nityatvam (eternal) means the way it is propagated by one person who teaches it as heard previously and the other who person  repeats it, and it goes on like this forever. Hence vēdam is eternal. Since it is apauruśēyam (not created by any one), it is free from defects.
- *vāṇar* – Those who can claim the vyāsāsanam \[the seat of vēda vyāsa who divided the vēdam into four and explained brahma sūtram\].
- *vāḻ* – Those who can visualize bhagavān who is explained through vēdam and hence live joyfully.
- *vāḻ tolaivillimangalam* – The town where bhagavān who is the meaning of vēdam, is visualized. Those who are in the higher platform of yōgam as said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 6.6.2 “*yōgāt svādyāyam āmanēt*” (Through yōgam, desiring to study the portions which are not yet studied) instead of just being as said in the same ślōkam “*svādyāyāt yōgam āsīta*” (studying the vēdam since it is ordained to do so).
- *kaṇḍa pin* – You spoiled her by showing the togetherness of emperumān and vaiṣṇavas in that town.
- *aṟkam onṟum aṟavurāḷ* – aṟkam – humility/control. She gave up being obedient to our instructions.
- *malindāḷ* – She became too engaged to be redeemed by our advice. She became unqualified to be redeemed.
- *malindāḷ kaṇḍīr ivaḷ* – She became so great in attachment towards bhagavān, which is beyond my comprehension.
- *annaimīr* – In knowing her state, there is no difference between you who try to redeem her and me who thinks I know her. Only if samsāris \[materialistic persons\] can know about the activities of nityasūris \[eternally free assistants of emperumān in paramapadam\], we can understand her state.
- *kaṟkum …* – Whatever she speaks, they only related to his divine names, that too, those which are related to his physical beauty and his obedience towards his devotees. It is well known that “kriṣṇa is obedient towards his devotees”.
- *pirān* – The benefactor who let me enjoy his physical beauty making himself available to me.
- *enṟē oṟkam onṟum ilaḷ* – She is not feeling any fatigue due to continuously reciting his divine names. While it is said “due to the unfortunate situation of being separated, she will not even be able to recite his divine names completely”, she kept reciting without any fatigue. It appears that the divine name itself will make her sustain and recite it; it is said in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.7.10](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/09/thiruvaimozhi-1-7-10-agalil-agalum/) “*pādi iḷaippilam*” (I have no reason to take a break from glorifying his incomparable auspicious qualities). oṟkam – midi (poverty); not having fatigue; alternative explanation – oṟkam – obedience; that is, not feeling shy to speak in this manner in front of the mothers.
- *ugandu ugandu* – Becoming more and more joyful by meditating upon his beauty, simplicity through his divine names.
- *uḷ magiḻndu kuḻaiyumē* – Due to the great loving joy, the ātmā itself becomes weak.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.5.5. Kulaiyum val

*kuḻaiyum vāḷ mugattēḻaiyait tolaivillimangalam koṇḍu pukku iḻai koḷ sōdic cendāmaraik kaṇ pirān irundamai kāttinīr maḻai peydāl okkum kaṇṇa nīrinodu anṟu tottum maiyāndu ivaḷ nuḻaiyum sindaiyuḷ annaimīr toḻum attisai uṟṟu nōkkiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kuḻaiyum – having natural tenderness; vāḷ – shining; mugattu – having face; ēḻaiyai – her (who is having desire to deeply enjoy emperumān); tolaivillimangalam – in tiruttolaivillimangalam; koṇḍu pukku – brought her; iḻai koḷ – with the decorations of divine ornaments; sōdi – having radiance; sem – reddish; tāmarai – like lotus; kaṇ – one who is having eyes; pirān – the benefactor who manifested such eyes to his devotees for their enjoyment; irundamai – how we was present there; kāttinīr – you showed; annaimīr – Oh mothers!; anṟu tottu – from that day onvards; ivaḷ – parānguśa nāyaki; maḻai peydāl okkum – like rain; kaṇṇa nīrinodu – with tears from her eyes; maiyāndu – being bewildered; nuḻaiyum – immersing in his beauty; sindaiyaḷ – having the heart; a – where he resides; tisai – the direction; uṟṟu – well; nōkki – looking into; toḻum – perform anjali \[joined palms\]

**Перевод:**

**You \[mothers\] brought parānguśa nāyaki, who is having a shining face with natural tenderness, to tiruttolaivillimangalam and showed her emperumān who is having reddish lotus like eyes and with the radiant decorations of divine ornaments and who is the benefactor who manifested such eyes to his devotees for their enjoyment, and showed her how he was present there in this manner; oh mothers! From that day onvards, parānguśa nāyaki, with rain like tears from her eyes, having the heart which is bewildered and immersed in his beauty, is looking well into the direction where he resides and performs anjali.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fifth pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki‘s friend says “Knowing her nature quite well, you \[mothers\] brought her to tiruttolaivillimangalam, showed her emperumān‘s beauty and spoiled her”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently,  parānguśa nāyaki says “You showed her the decorated beauty of arvaindalōcana in tiruttolaivillimangalam; from that day she is emotionally charged”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. Alternative explanation – after showing her the nature of the residents of tiruttolaivillimangalam, should you also show her what \[emperumān\] sustains them? kuḻaiyum vāḷ mugattēḻaiyait tolaivillimangalam koṇḍu pukku iḻai koḷ sōdic cendāmaraik kaṇ pirān irundamai kāttinīr maḻai peydāl okkum kaṇṇa nīrinodu anṟu tottum maiyāndu ivaḷ nuḻaiyum sindaiyuḷ annaimīr toḻum attisai uṟṟu nōkkiyē*

- *kuḻaiyum* … – She is naturally tender and does not need a union \[before separation\] to weaken; being with radiance acquired by bhagavat anubhavam (experience of [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)) as said in the previous pāsuram “*ugandu ugandu uḷ magiḻndu kuḻaiyum*” (enjoying [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s qualities, her heart will become very weakened) and remains with the same desire without giving up even if she were told “you will not get him”.
- *tolaivillimangalam koṇḍu pukku* – As it is impossible to avoid bringing her to the abode which is pursued by bhagavān, aren’t you supposed to bring her to paramapadam where his supremacy is manifested? Would anyone bring her to tiruttolaivillimangalam \[divya dēśam\] where his ultimate simplicity is manifested? vāḷ – radiance.
- *iḻai koḷ sōdi* – \[[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is\] Explained as a) having the radiance of the divine ornaments; b) without separately needing any other ornaments, he himself is radiant; c) having natural radiance which subdues the radiance of the ornaments.
- *sem tāmaraik kaṇ pirān* – The divine eyes which can be compared to the lotus for their blossomed state, fragrance etc. The divine eyes which reveal his heart’s compassion.
- *pirān* – The form which is explained to be present for his devotees as in jitantē stōtram “*bhaktānām*” (for the devotees).
- *irundamai kāttinīr* – You spoiled her. It was you who showed her these aspects which she did not know initially.
- *irundamai* – It appears that his majestic seating posture is fully manifested there. If he is standing \[in a divya dēśam\], they \[āḻvārs\] will say as in periya tirumoḻi 6.9.8 “*nilaiyāra ninṟān*” (he stood firmly); if he is reclining, they will say as in [tirumālai 23](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/10/thirumalai-23/) “*kidandadōr kidakkai*” (amazing reclining posture); also explained as “you have showed her, his nature”.
- *kāttinīr* – You showed her saying “Look at his glance, look at his smile”.

When they ask “How does it matter now?”, she replies,

- *maḻai peydāl okkum kaṇṇa nīrinodu* – Look at her eyes overflowing with rain like tears on seeing such [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)! After [āḷavandār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/alavandhar/) heard about emperumān from [maṇakkāl nambi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/manakkal-nambi/) \[through his bhagavat gītā lectures\], he asked “there is no higher upāyam \[means\] than this; is there any way I can see emperumān right now?”. \[maṇakkāl nambi brings him to periya perumāḷ sannidi and shows his eyes\] Upon seeing emperumān, āḷavandār had overflowing tears in his eyes.

She is explaining the term “*ēḻai*” now.

- *anṟu tottum* – From that day you showed him to her.
- *maiyāndu* – being bewildered.

She is explaining the term “*kuḻaiyum*” now.

- *ivaḷ nuḻaiyum sindaiyuḷ* – She is having the heart which is immersed in emperumān’s qualities. Instead of focussing on [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s true nature and natural qualities, she is focussed on the qualities of his divine form. She remained thinking “What a beautiful form! how beautifully he is decorated! What a beautiful pair of eyes!” and so on.
- *annaimīr* – You are only focussed on redeeming her \[instead you should let her be with emperumān\].
- *toḻum* – She would look in to the direction \[of the town\] without even blinking and stand vorśipping it as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 16.25 “*ēkasta hrudayā nūnam rāmam Eva anupaśyati*” (she is seeing śrī rāma with single-focussed mind). Her vorśipping is not limited to just one direction too \[being bewildered, she worships in different directions\].

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.5.6. Nokkum pakkam ellam

*nōkkum pakkam ellām karumbodu sennolōngu sendāmarai vāykkum taṇ porunal vadagarai vaṇ tolaivillimangalam nōkkumēl attisai allāl maṟu nōkkilaḷ vaigal nādoṟum vāykkoḷ vāsagamum maṇivaṇṇan nāmamē ivaḷ annaimīr!*

**Пословный перевод:**

nōkkum pakkam ellām – wherever seen; karumbodu – with sugarcane; sennel – paddy crop; ōngu – tall (enough to give shade to the crops); sem tāmarai – reddish lotus flower; vāykkum – to be abundant; taṇ – cool; porunal vadakarai – in the northern banks of the divine porunal (tāmirabharaṇi) river; vaṇ – not having any shortcoming in urban wealth; tolaivillimangalam – tiruttolaivillimangalam; nōkkumēl – if parānguśa nāyaki sees; a – that; tisai – direction; allāl – other than; maṟu nōkkilaḷ – will not see anything else; vaigal – always; nāḷ toṟum – everyday; ivaḷ – she; vāy – in her speech; koḷ – having; vāsagamum – words; annaimīr – Oh mothers (who made her like this)!; maṇi – like a blue gem which is handy and can be enjoyed as desired; vaṇṇan – having physical beauty; nāmamē – divine names which reveal his simplicity, beauty etc

**Перевод:**

**tiruttolaivillimangalam is on the northern banks of the cool, divine porunal (tāmirabharaṇi) river, having abundance of sugarcane, paddy crop and reddish lotus flower, wherever seen, and is not having any shortcoming in urban wealth; if parānguśa nāyaki sees in that direction, she will not see anything other than that; oh mothers! she is always, everyday having in her speech, the words relating to the divine names which reveal the simplicity, beauty etc of emperumān who is having physical beauty which resembles a blue gem which is handy and can be enjoyed as desired.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the sixth pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki‘s friend says “Even in this bewildered state, parānguśa nāyaki will not look at anything else after seeing tiruttolaivillimangalam”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, parānguśa nāyaki‘s friend says “Not seeing anything else after seeing tiruttolaivillimangalam, whatever parānguśa nāyaki speaks, they end up being the comprehensively beautiful emperumān‘s divine names”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. nōkkum pakkam ellām karumbodu sennolōngu sendāmarai vāykkum taṇ porunal vadagarai vaṇ tolaivillimangalam nōkkumēl attisai allāl maṟu nōkkilaḷ vaigal nādoṟum vāykkoḷ vāsagamum maṇivaṇṇan nāmamē ivaḷ annaimīr!*

- *nōkkum pakkam ellām* – Wherever seen. Some sing as “*tirupporunal nōkkum pakkam ellām*” (wherever seen in the divine porunal river) too.
- *karumbu* … – Sugarcane, the paddy crops which grow along with them and the reddish lotus flowers which provide shade to those two.
- *vāykkum* – Implies abundance as well as the fertility of the land where whatever is sowed, brings out plenty of output.
- *taṇ porunal …* – tiruttolaivillimangalam which is having great wealth of being on the northern banks of the invigorating divine porunal river.
- *nōkkumēl* – First she is too weak to see; but once she saw with great effort, she is not taking her eyes off that direction.
- *vaigal nāḷ toṟum* – Every day which passes by.
- *vāyk koḷ vāsagamum* – Words which come out of her mouth.
- *maṇivaṇṇan nāmamē* – She uttered the words which reveal his physical beauty only. Instead of speaking about his qualities or his wealth, she speaks to imply that she was captivated by his physical beauty. What is her state? What is our state? Your svarūpa jñānam \[understanding about his true nature, that we should wait for him and not cross any limits\] is as good as her rūpa jñānam \[attachment towards his physical beauty which makes her cross all limits\].

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.
