## 6.5.7. Annaimir

*annaimīr! aṇi mā mayil siṟu mān ivaḷ nammaik kaivalindu enna vārttaiyum kētkuṟāḷ tolaivillimangalam enṟallāl munnam nōṟṟa vidikolō? mugil vaṇṇan māyangolō? avan cinnamum tirunāmamum ivaḷ vāyanagaḷ tirundavē*

**Пословный перевод:**

annaimīr – Oh mothers who gave birth to her and raised her!; aṇi – beautiful; mā – having dark complexion; mayil – very beautiful like peacock; siṟu – young; mān – like a deer; ivaḷ – your little girl; nammai – us; kaivalindu – overruling; tolaivillimangalam – tiruttolaivillimangalam; enṟu – as; allāl – other than; ena – any; vārttaiyum – word; kētka – to hear; uṟāḷ – does not; munnam – previously; nōṟṟa – done; vidikolō – fortune?; mugil – like a cloud which is magnanimous; vaṇṇan – done by one who is having the form; māyangolō – amazing act?; avan – his; cinnamum – symbols (such as his ornaments); tirunāmamum – divine names (which reveal his magnanimity); tirunda – to become more glorious; ivaḷ vāyanagaḷ – being spoken by her

**Перевод:**

**Oh mothers who gave birth to her and raised her! Your little girl who is having a beautiful dark complexion, is very beautiful like peacock and is like a young deer, is overruling us and is not hearing any word other than tiruttolaivillimangalam; is it due to her previous fortune? ōr is it due to an amazing act done by one who is having a cloud like magnanimous form? His symbols and divine names are becoming more glorious on being spoken by her.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the seventh pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki‘s friend says “His symbols and divine names became more glorious after having been highlighted by her”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, parānguśa nāyaki‘s friend says “sarvēśvaran, the great benefactor has acted on her in an amazing way that she is not hearing anything other than his divine symbols and divine names and they become more glorious on being spoken by her”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. annaimīr! aṇi mā mayil siṟu mān ivaḷ nammaik kaivalindu enna vārttaiyum kētkuṟāḷ tolaivillimangalam enṟallāl munnam nōṟṟa vidikolō? mugil vaṇṇan māyangolō? avan cinnamum tirunāmamum ivaḷ vāyanagaḷ tirundavē*

- *annaimīr* – This is her age; it’s amazing that she is overruling us. This resembles how parāśara riśi lovingly says “*maitrēya*“.
- *aṇi mā mayil siṟu mān* – The girl who is having beautiful complexion. Also explained as the girl who appears to be praiseworthy like a peacock.
- *siṟu mān ivaḷ nammaik kaivalindu* – One who previously felt shy to repeat the divine names clearly we taught her, is now beyond our reach.
- *kavalindu* – going beyond our reach.
- *ena vārttaiyum kētkuṟāḷ* – Even if I told her what she is already thinking, she is not listening to me thinking that I am trying to pull her back; if I said tiruttolaivillimangalam, she will listen; ena vārttai – my words.
- *munnam nōṟṟa vidikolō* – We were born together and raised together and I have not seen her engage in any activities \[to get to this stage\]. This must be a virtue from previous births!  It is said as “*vidir vidānam*” (puṇya is synonymous with vidi:, vidānam). For the means she pursued, the result cannot be so great; this must be “*sidda dharma palam*” (the result of an established means, i.e., bhagavān); and thus,
- *mugil vaṇṇan māyangolō* – Did he show his green necklace and divine form? The doubt in the first thought \[munnam nōṟṟa vidikolō\] is, there is no way such a great result can be attained by pursuing any insentient means \[such as karma yōga, jñāna yōga, bhakti yōga etc\]. The doubt in the second thought \[mugil vaṇṇan māyangolō\] is, we have not seen anyone attaining such result in this manner.
- *avan cinnam* … – The symbols as said in “*tavaḷa oṇ sangu cakkaram*” and the divine names such as “aravindalōcanan”, “dēvapirān” etc.
- *ivaḷ vāyanagaḷ tirundavē* – Though they were glorious to start with, by being spoken by her, they became alive \[more glorious\]. Just as the divine names acquire more glory when [bhattar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/parasara-bhattar/) \[lovingly\] says “[*aḻagiya maṇavāḷap perumāḷ*](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)“, [sōmāsiyāṇḍān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/somasiyandan/) \[lovingly\] says “[emperumānār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/emperumanar/)” and [anantāḻvān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/ananthazhwan/) \[lovingly\] says “[tiruvēngadamudaiyān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)“; as said in samkśēpa rāmāyaṇam “*yētvayā kīrtitā guṇā:*” (the qualities explained by you).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.5.8. Tirundu vedamum

*tirundu vēdamum vēḷviyum tirumāmagaḷirum tām malindu irundu vāḻ porunal vadagarai vaṇ tolaivillimangalam karundadangaṇṇi kai toḻuda annāḷ todangi innāḷtoṟum irundirundu aravindalōcana! enṟenṟē naindirangumē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tirundu – having clarity (in revealing bhagavat svarūpa (true nature) rūpa (form) guṇa (qualties) vibhūti (wealth)); vēdamum – vēdam; vēḷviyum – yajña and other rituals (which are revealed in such vēdam as ways to vorśipping emperumān); mā – the one who nurtures the wealth which is apt (for such yajña etc); tirumagaḷirum – lakshmi; tām – they; malindu – being abundant (due to togetherness with bhagavān); irundu – being well established; vāḻ – living; porunal vada karai – on the northern banks of the divine porunal (tāmirabharaṇi) river; vaṇ tolaivillimangalam – tiruttolaivillimangalam; karu – blackish; tadam – expansive; kaṇṇi – having eyes; kai toḻuda annāḷ todangi – from the day she started vorśipping; i – now; nāḷtoṟum – until this day; irundu irundu – (being unable to sustain in grief due to the distress) remaining; aravindalōcana – Oh aravindalōcana!; enṟenṟē – calling out repeatedly; naindu – becoming weak; irangum – had her heart melted

**Перевод:**

**tiruttolaivillimangalam is on the northern banks of the divine porunal river; those who are well established in vēdam which is having clarity and yajña and other rituals are living in abundance there; lakshmi who nurtures the wealth which is apt \[for those rituals\] is also living there; from the day parānguśa nāyaki who is having blackish expansive eyes, started vorśipping such divya dēśam until now, she remains calling out “Oh aravindalōcana!” repeatedly, becoming weak and is having her heart melted. “tām” can also imply bhagavān himself \[i.e., bhagavān is living along with lakshmi in tiruttolaivillimangalam\].**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the eighth pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki‘s friend explains how parānguśa nāyaki became weak since the day she started vorśipping tiruttolaivillimangalam until today.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently,  parānguśa nāyaki‘s friend says “since the day she started vorśipping tiruttolaivillimangalam, forever, she is becoming weak, reciting the divine name aravindalōcanan”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. tirundu vēdamum vēḷviyum tirumāmagaḷirum tām malindu irundu vāḻ porunal vadagarai vaṇ tolaivillimangalam karundadangaṇṇi kai toḻuda annāḷ todangi innāḷtoṟum irundirundu aravindalōcana! enṟenṟē naindirangumē*

- *tirundu vēdamum* – vēdam became organized only after the residents of this town pursued it. They are the ones who analyzed vēdam in various angles such as
   - svarūpa jñāna mātra śruti – parts of vēdam which are focussed on knowledge on true nature of bhagavān
   - jñātrutva śruti – parts of vēdam which are focussed on the expansive knowledge of bhagavān
   - bhēda abēda śruti – parts of vēdam which discuss duality and non-duality
   - saguṇa śruti – parts of vēdam which speak about bhagavān having \[auspicious\] qualities
   - nirguṇa śruti – parts of vēdam which speak about bhagavān being free from \[inauspicious\] qualities
- *vēḷviyum* – The vaidika worship of emperumān. Putting into practice what is learned.
- *tirumāmagaḷirum tām* – This is the completeness of the one (śrīman nārāyaṇan) who is being vorśipped.
- *tirumāmagaḷirum* – wealth \[provided by lakshmi\] (The abode where those who are having in abundance vēdam, yajñam and rituals, lakshmi who provides wealth for such yajñam; due to having togetherness with bhagavān, they are well established).
- *tirumāmagaḷirum tām* – Alternative explanation – The togetherness of śrī mahālakśmi and śrīman nārāyaṇan. tām – tān – him. The divine abode where pramāṇam (Scripture – śāstram/vēdam), pramēya (goal – priātti and emperumān) and pramātā (preceptors – śrīvaiṣṇavas) are in abundance (The presence of pramātā is implied).
- *malindirundu* – He is remaining here without the internal grief which he was having while staying in paramapadam \[in paramapadam, some of his qualities are not revealed since everyone is pure and committed to him; so his qualities like mercy etc are not shining there; but here everything is shining\].
- *porunal vada karai* – as it is said in “beyond virajā river” \[the river crossing which one will reach paramapadam\].
- *karum tadam kaṇṇi* – For the beauty of her eyes, she is comparable to asitēkśaṇā \[sītāp pirātti is called as asitēkśaṇā (blackeyed) in śrī rāmāyaṇam\].
- *tadam kaṇṇi* – The difference between sītāp pirātti and parānguśa nāyaki. sītāp pirātti acquired her beautiful eyes by vorśipping him; but parānguśa nāyaki’s beautiful eyes were acquired by the divine couple of śrī mahālakśmi and śrīman nārāyaṇan \[so its much more beautiful\]; even while being vorśipped, it would be apt to be vorśipped by beautiful persons.
- *kai toḻud annāḷ todangi* – From the day she vorśipped until today; another explanation – from the day she became enlightened \[in bhagavat viśayam\] until today. The previous state is explained as in taittirīya upaniśat “*asannēva*” (ātmā as good as acit (matter) when it lacks true knowledge) and in tiruccanda viruttam 64 “*anṟu nān piṟandilēn*” (I was not born then). It is neither in his hand, nor in others’ hand, but is in her hand – this is how she sustains \[her vorśipping by performing anjali\]! It is said in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.1.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/03/thiruvaimozhi-1-1-1-uyarvara-uyarnalam/) “*toḻudeḻu*” (worship and rise).
- *irundu irundu aravaindalōcana enṟu enṟē* – By the time she completes reciting “aravindalōcana” once, one can eat several times \[it takes so much effort for her\].
- *enṟu enṟē* – While thinking “would she not complete reciting the name due to lack of strength?”, she recites the name. He is aravindalōcanan and she is karundadangaṇṇi – both are caught in the same aspect \[lotus eye\].
- *naindirangumē* – She became weakened. Not just bodily deterioration, even her heart is  deteriorating.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.5.9. Irangi naltorum

*irangi nāḷtoṟum vāy vereei ivaḷ kaṇṇanīrgaḷ alamara marangaḷum irangum vagai maṇivaṇṇavō! enṟu kūvumāl turangam vāy piḷandānuṟai tolaivillimangalam enṟu tan karangaḷ kūppit toḻum avvūrt tirunāmam kaṟṟadaṟ pinnaiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ivaḷ – parānguśa nāyaki; nāḷtoṟum – everyday; irangi – with melted heart; vāyvereei – (emotionally) blabbering; kaṇṇa nīrgaḷ – tears; alamara – flow and make her tired; marangaḷum – even the trees (which are insentient); irangum vagai – to pity; maṇi – beautiful like a blue gem; vaṇṇavō – saying “Oh one who is having form!”; kūvum – calls out; turangam – kēśi who came in the form of a horse; vāy – mouth; piḷandān – kriṣṇa who tore; uṟai – residing; tolaivillimangalam – tiruttolaivillimangalam; enṟu – as; avvūrt tirunāmam – the divine name of that abode; kaṟṟadan pinnai – after learning; than karangaḷ – her hands; kūppi – joins palms; toḻum – worships

**Перевод:**

**Everyday, parānguśa nāyaki is blabbering with melted heart and tears flow and make her tired; even the trees pity her when she calls out saying “Oh one who is having a beautiful blue gem like form!”; after learning the divine name of that abode as tiruttolaivillimangalam where kriṣṇa who tore the mouth of kēśi who came in the form of a horse is residing, she joins her palms and worships it.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the ninth pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki‘s friend says “parānguśa nāyaki’s mind, action and speech have become greatly attached to emperumān”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, parānguśa nāyaki‘s friend says “She is calling out his divine name which reveals his beauty etc, identifying tiruttolaivillimangalam, the divine abode of the remover of hurdles, and is performing anjali \[joined palms\]”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. irangi nāḷtoṟum vāy vereei ivaḷ kaṇṇanīrgaḷ alamara marangaḷum irangum vagai maṇivaṇṇavō! enṟu kūvumāl turangam vāy piḷandānuṟai tolaivillimangalam enṟu than karangaḷ kūppit toḻum avvūrt tirunāmam kaṟṟadaṟ pinnaiyē*

- *irangi* – With a melted heart.
- *vāy vereei* – The speech was incoherent. Unlike as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 32.11 “*vicintya vācā bruvatī tamēva*” (perceiving with the intellect and speaking with the mouth), she is speaking without mind’s help.
- *nāḷtoṟum* – \[always\] It appears that when she was blessed with unblemiśed knowledge and devotion as mentioned in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.1.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/03/thiruvaimozhi-1-1-1-uyarvara-uyarnalam/), she also acquired this bewilderment.
- *ivaḷ kaṇṇa nīrgaḷ alamara* – The way her eye is also longing to see him. By “*nāḷtoṟum vāyvereei*” (blabbering forever) implies the calling out started from tiruviruttam 1 “*poynninṟa jñālamum*” until here.
- *marangaḷum irangum vagai* – Seeing her calling, irrespective of being sentient or insentient, everyone will show pity upon her and grieve for her. When embār was asked “can trees feel the grief too?”, he mercifully replied “We don’t know how many impure persons have recited these verses from the day that these were divinely spoken; that being the case, the stone like hearts which cannot be reformed even through yama, niyama etc \[aśtānga yōgam\], are now melting; seeing this, it is easy to believe that the trees which existed back then during parānguśa nāyaki’s time, grieved for her”. Whatever emotions the trees went through during kriṣṇāvatāram as said in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 3.6.4 “*marangaḷ ninṟu madudāraigaḷ pāyum malargaḷ vīḻum vaḷar kombugaḷ tāḻum*” (Honey will flow from the trees, the flowers will fall down and the well grown branches will lower themselves), they went through the same on hearing the grief-stricken calling of her. As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 59.10 “*apivrukśā: parimlānā:*” (Even the trees withered), whatever grief the trees went through in separation of śrī rāma, they went through the same grief on hearing her words. The words of those who are engrossed in bhagavān’s qualities are even more powerful than the qualities themselves, to melt others.
- *maṇi vaṇṇan enṟu kūvumāl* – Are you trying to pull her back! She is calling out identifying his qualities \[being too attached to them\]!
- *turangam …* – The abode where emperumān who previously helped \[the covherd clan\] has descended to help \[her\]. The abode where emperumān who effortlessly tore the mouth of kēśi, dwells.
- *tolaivillimangalam enṟu than karangaḷ kūppit toḻum* – She is born to be vorśipped by performing an anjali everytime anyone hears the name of her town, āḻvārtirunagari; such parānguśa nāyaki is now vorśipping emperumān with an anjali saying his abode; it appears that she is thinking “one who sees my hands will automatically worship me”. \[Is it wrong for her to worship like this?\] It is not apt for her being a woman to perform anjali like this \[visibly\].

When asked “since when is she vorśipping like this?”, she says

- *avvūrt tirunāmam kaṟṟadan pinnaiyē* – After she learned to speak, everyone in āḻvārtirunagari is learning “tiruttolaivillimangalam” only. Her learning words and reciting divine names are not two different activities. Just as those who are in kōyil (śrīrangam) learn the words “kōyil”, “perumāḷ” etc. parānguśa nāyaki’s friend is saying “avvūr” (that town) \[instead of tiruttolaivillimangalam\] since she does not feel it to be as sweet as how parānguśa nāyaki says the same. What! ḍidn’t she say previously? Yes – she did, and since it did not feel the same, this time she says “avvūr”.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.5.10. Pinnaikol

*pinnaikol? nilamāmagaḷkol? tirumagaḷkol? piṟandittāḷ enna māyangolō? ivaḷ nedumāl enṟē ninṟu kūvumāl munnivandavan ninṟirunduṟaiyum tolaivillimangalam senniyāl vaṇangum avvūrt tirunāma kētpadu sindaiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

pinnaikol – is she nappinnaip pirātti who is infinitely enjoyable?; nilam – being the controller of earth; mā – laudable; magaḷkol – is she bhūmip pirātti?; tirumagaḷkol – Is she lakshmi who is the infinite wealth for emperumān?; piṟandittāḷ – one who is born in this manner; enna – how; māyangolō – amazing!; ivaḷ – she; nedumāl enṟē – speaking about his great love; ninṟu – remaining; kūvum – she is calling out \[for him\]; avan – he; munni – before/first; vandu – arriving; ninṟirundu – standing and sitting; uṟaiyum – eternally residing; tolaivillimangalam – tiruttolaivillimangalam; senniyāl – with the head; vaṇangum – bows; avvūrt tirunāmam – the divine name of that town; kētpadē – hearing from others; sindai – focussed on

**Перевод:**

**Is parānguśa nāyaki who is born in this manner, nappinnaip pirātti who is infinitely enjoyable? Is she the laudable bhūmip pirātti who is the controller of the earth? Is she lakshmi who is the infinite wealth for emperumān? How amazing! She remains speaking about his great love and calling out for him. emperumān himself arrived first and is eternally residing in tiruttolaivillimangalam and is sitting and standing there; she is bowing with her head towards such town and is focussed on hearing the divine name of that town from others.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the tenth pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki‘s friend sees parānguśa nāyaki‘s great attachment towards emperumān and how she cannot sustain herself without him, and sees that there is no one comparable to her; doubts if she is one among emperumān’s divine consorts.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. pinnaikol? nilamāmagaḷkol? tirumagaḷkol? piṟandittāḷ enna māyangolō? ivaḷ nedumāl enṟē ninṟu kūvumāl munnivandavan ninṟirunduṟaiyum tolaivillimangalam senniyāl vaṇangum avvūrt tirunāma kētpadu sindaiyē*

- *pinnaikol …* – Did nappinnai take birth? ōr did śrī bhūmip pirātti take birth? ōr did śrī mahālakśmi who gives such greatness to everyone take birth herself? \[Another explanation\] Did śrī mahālakśmi who is the wealth of [sarvēśvaran](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) take birth? Did śrī bhūmip pirātti who is the fertile ground for the growth of such wealth take birth? Did nappinnaip  pirātti who is the harvest of such fertile land take birth?

Alternative explanation,

- *piṟandittāḷō?* – Since none of them is like [parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/), they are no match for her; has she taken birth to uplift the entire world? As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam bāla kāṇḍam 1.18 “*viṣṇunā sadrusō viryē*” (śrī rāma is as good as viṣṇu in valour), since each consort of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) has some comparable aspects with parānguśa nāyaki, her friend is highlighting such match with each of them. As said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 1.15.156 “*upamānam aśēśāṇām sādūnām yassadā bhavat*” (prahlāda is the best representative for the devotees of bhagavān), āḻvār can be compared to many personalities and yet no one is as good as āḻvār.
- *enna māyangolō* – In bhagavān’s wealth nothing is impossible! How amazing!
- *ivaḷ nedumāl enṟē ninṟu kūvum* – Ignoring her own love \[towards him\], she is calling him out citing his love \[towards her\].
- *Al* – Sound made due to amazement; also present to fill the necessary letter count in the verse.
- *munni* … – This is how he worked to nurture her great love. He arrived there long before her and is eternally residing there with his standing and sitting postures. Just as a hungry person will sit and wait, if the food preparation takes longer than expected.
- *senniyāl vaṇangum* – Even “*than karangaḷ kūppit toḻugai*” (joining her palms to worship) is also becoming difficult; now, she can only bow her head signalling her worship.
- *avvūr* … – She only desires to hear the divine name of the town, tiruttolaivillimangalam. Now, the friend is saying “avvūr”, because the actual name itself does not sound as good as it was said by [parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/). Then why did she say before? Yes, she said once, but then realised that it did not sound well, so she avoided subsequently.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.5.11. Sindaiyalum

*sindaiyālum sollālum seygaiyinālum dēvapirānaiyē tandai tāy enṟadainda vaṇ kurugūravar catakōpan mundai āyirattuḷ ivai tolaivillimangalattaic conna sendamiḻ pattum vallār adimai seyvār tirumālukkē*

**Пословный перевод:**

dēvapirānaiyē – Only dēvapirān; tandai – father; tāy – and mother; enṟu – determined; sindaiyālum sollālum seygaiyinālum – with the three faculties \[mind, speech and actions\]; adainda – having attained; vaṇ – those who are surrendered to self \[āḻvār\] like śrī madurakavigaḷ who said in kaṇṇinuṇ ciṟut tāmbu 4 “annaiyāy attanāy”; kurugūravar – the leader of the residents of āḻvārtirunagari; catakōpan – nammāḻvār; mundai – revealing the meanings of the ancient vēdam; āyirattuḷ – among the thousand pāsurams; tolaivillimangalattai – tiruttolaivillimangalam; sonna – mercifully spoke; sem – being honest in revealing the meanings; tamiḻ – tamiḻ pāsurams; ivai pattum – this decad; vallār – those who can practice; tirumālukku – for śriya:pati who is sarvēśvara; adimai seyvār – will become servitors

**Перевод:**

**Determining dēvapirān only as father and mother, and having attained him with the three faculties, nammāḻvār, the leader of the residents of āḻvārtirunagari, who are surrendered to self \[āḻvār\] like śrī madurakavigaḷ who said in kaṇṇinuṇ ciṟut tāmbu 4 “annaiyāy attanāy” mercifully spoke this decad in the form of tamiḻ pāsurams which honestly reveal the meanings and are among the thousand pāsurams, revealing the meanings of the ancient vēdam; those who can practice this decad will become servitors for śriya:pati who is sarvēśvara.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the end, explaining the purpose of this decad, āḻvār says “Those who learned this decad will get to perform matching kainkaryam”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*In the end, āḻvār explains the result as “Those who are able to practice this decad will become eternal servitors of śriya:pati (consort of śrīmahālakhsmi)”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. sindaiyālum sollālum seygaiyinālum dēvapirānaiyē tandai tāy enṟadainda vaṇ kurugūravar catakōpan mundai āyirattuḷ ivai tolaivillimangalattaic conna sendamiḻ pattum vallār adimai seyvār tirumālukkē*

- *sindaiyālum* … – āḻvār’s mind, speech and body are attached to emperumān in harmony. This decad explained āḻvār’s great attachment as seen in “*irangi*” \[mind\], “*maṇivaṇṇavō*” \[speech\] and “*than karangaḷ kūppit toḻum*” \[body\].
- *dēvapirān* … – Determined that emperumān who is said to be “*ayarvaṟum amarargaḷ adipati*” (the leader of nityasūris), has magnanimously descended to tiruttolaivillimangalam manifesting his simplicity, is also all types of relative to self, and attained him.
- *vaṇ kurugūravar catakōpan* – Just as emperumān is every type of relative for āḻvār, the residents of āḻvārtirunagari consider āḻvār as every type of relative. They remain as said in kaṇṇinuṇ ciṟut tāmbu 4 “*annaiyāy attanāy ennai āṇḍidum tanmaiyān*” (one who rules me being my mother and father) and in stōtra ratnam 4 “*mātā pitā yuvatayastanayā vibhūtis sarvam*” (everything – mother, father, wife, children, wealth).
- *mundai āyiram* – Since it reveals the meanings of the ancient vēdam. Just as sarvēśvaran appeared as a mortal being, vēdam to descended through āḻvār in tamiḻ language.
- *sem tamiḻ …* – Honest tamiḻ, fresh tamiḻ. Reveals the meanings elaborately. Those who can practice this will get to serve śrīya:pati. Just as iḷaiyaperumāḷ (lakśmaṇa) served perumāḷ and pirātti together, they will also get to serve emperumān who is with pirātti.

## 6.6 Malukku

## 6.6.1. Malukku

*mālukku vaiyam aḷanda maṇāḷaṟku neelak karu niṟa mēganiyāyaṟku kōlac cendāmaraik kaṇṇaṟku en kongalar ēlak kuḻali iḻandadu sangē*

**Пословный перевод:**

mālukku – one who is identified by his love for his devotees; vaiyam – earth; aḷanda – measured and owned (to avoid anyone claiming ownership); maṇāḷaṟku – being her enjoyer due to manifesting such activities; neela – glossy; karu – blackish; niṟam – having complexion; mēganiyāyaṟku – one who has a form which is similar to cloud; kōlam – attractive form; sem – reddish; tāmarai – lotus like; kaṇṇaṟku – one who is having eyes; en – my; kongu – having honey; alar – having flower; Elam – refreshingly fragrant like cardamom; kuḻali – having lock \[of hair\]; iḻandadu – lost; sangu – bangle

**Перевод:**

**My daughter who is having lock \[of hair\] with honey laden flower which is refreshingly fragrant like cardamom, lost her bangle for the one who is identified by his love for his devotees, who is her enjoyer due to manifesting activities such as measuring and owning the earth, who has a glossy blackish coloured form which is similar to cloud and who is having attractive, reddish lotus-like eyes.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the first pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki‘s mother says “parānguśa nāyaki lost her bangles being captivated by the qualities of emperumān who mercifully measured the earth”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*In the first pāsuram parānguśa nāyaki‘s mother says “My daughter who is having an unlimitedly enjoyable form for emperumān who performed actions out of love \[towards his devotees\], has lost her bangles”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. mālukku vaiyam aḷanda maṇāḷaṟku neelak karu niṟa mēganiyāyaṟku kōlac cendāmaraik kaṇṇaṟku en kongalar ēlak kuḻali iḻandadu sangē*

- *mālukku* – In [tiruvāimoḻi 6.2](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/10/thiruvaimozhi-6-2-minnidai/) “*minnidai madavār*“, āḻvār said he does not need emperumān, and emperumān in turn said he needs him, and āḻvār remained bewildered and he tormented her further by manifesting this \[beautiful vāmana\] form. If he manifested his supremacy, she would not be so perturbed! (For the one who is having love).
- *vaiyam aḷanda maṇāḷaṟku* – His love is such that, he would not even give up on those who are unfavourable towards him. As said in [tiruvāimoḻi 6.2.9](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/11/thiruvaimozhi-6-2-9-ugavaiyal-nenjam/) “*aḻittāy un tiruvadiyāl*“, he placed her beneath his divine feet and accepted her. She is the only one who became fully surrendered for such act; she says as in periya tirumoḻi 9.4.2 “*mūvadi maṇ koṇḍaḷanda mannan saridaikkē mālāgip pon payandēn*” (My complexion changed after becoming attached to the king who accepted three feet of land and measured the earth); he begged for alms and got the earth, and she acquired golden complexion having become pleased with his act. Whatever is the result of joy, will be like gold.
- *maṇāḷan* – ēnjoyer.
- *neelak karu niṟa mēganiyāyaṟku* – One who is like cloud which is laden and dark. niyāmam – similarity. Providing without any expectation and when not satisfied with what was given, becoming pale. Even if he has no love, he cannot be given up due to his beautiful form and magnanimity.
- *neelak karu niṟa mēganiyāyaṟku* – Just as he manifested his beautiful form and grabbed the earth from mahābali, he captured her by manifesting his beautiful form. This is black-pigment with which he decorated his body to drive her crazy. It is said in tiruviruttam 94 “*maippadi mēni*” (dark coloured form).
- *kōlac chem tāmaraik kaṇṇaṟku* – For the who has divine eyes which are attractive, reddish due to motherly forbearance, expansive etc. He captured her by showing his eyes as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 6.2.9](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/11/thiruvaimozhi-6-2-9-ugavaiyal-nenjam/) “*tāmarait tadangaṇgaḷin agavalaip paduppān*” (he caught us in the net of his expansive lotus like eyes). Since “*kku*” (for) is present in every quality, her being captivated in individual aspects is explained.
- *māl* … – She is counting the \[love\] arrows which were shot at her daughter. Like “this is punch”, “this is a cut”, “this is an arrow” etc.
- *en kongu alar ēlak kuḻali* – My daughter who is having flower which has flowing honey and beautiful fragrance. kongu – honey. alar – flower. Elam – fragrance. emperumān who becomes deeply immersed being captivated in her lock is now finishing her! Like many soldiers surrounded the lonely abhimanyu and killed him!
- *iḻandadu sangē* – She lost what he would lose on seeing her beautiful lock.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.6.2. Sangu vil

*sangu vil vāḷ taṇḍu cakkarak kaiyaṟku senganivāyc ceyya tāmaraik kaṇṇaṟku kongalar taṇṇanduḻāy mudiyānukku en mangai iḻandadu māmai niṟamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

sangu vil vāḷ taṇḍu cakkaram – one who is having the lofty divine five weapons as part of the incarnation to measure the world; kaiyaṟku – having divine hands; sem – reddish; kani – like a fruit; vāy – divine lips; seyya – reddish; tāmarai – like a lotus; kaṇṇaṟku – one who is having eyes; kongu alar – having blossomed with fragrance; taṇ – invigorating; am – attractive; tuḻāy – decorated with tiruttuḻāy (tuḷasi); mudiyānukku – one who is wearing divine crown; en mangai – my daughter who is at the age which attracts him; iḻandadu – lost; māmai niṟam – the beautiful complexion which is exclusive for her femininity

**Перевод:**

**emperumān was having the lofty divine five weapons, as part of the incarnation to measure the world, in his divine hands; his divine lips were reddish like a fruit; he was having reddish lotus like eyes; he was wearing a divine crown which is decorated with tiruttuḻāy which is invigorating, attractive and blossomed with fragrance; my daughter who is at the age which attracts him, lost her beautiful complexion which is exclusive for her femininity. kongu means both honey and fragrance.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the second pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki‘s mother says “My daughter lost her beautiful complexion being captivated by the beauty of divine five weapons and ornaments of the emperumān who mercifully measured the world”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. sangu vil vāḷ taṇḍu cakkarak kaiyaṟku senganivāyc ceyya tāmaraik kaṇṇaṟku kongalar taṇṇanduḻāy mudiyānukku en mangai iḻandadu māmai niṟamē*

- *sangu* … – She became immersed in the combined beauty of all his five weapons. How many ornaments \[weapons\] did he wear and show her to get just one of her ornaments \[her beautiful complexion\]? \[That too\] He showed his five ornaments on his hand to get her one ornament. \[Are these weapons or ornaments?\] These weapons behave both like weapons \[for unfavourable ones\] and ornaments \[for favourable ones\]!
- *sem kani vāyc ceyya tāmaraik kaṇṇaṟku* – Did he have to place something on his hand to attract her? Are his smile and glance not sufficient to attract her?
- *kongu alar …* – One who is having honey flowing tiruttuḻāy on the divine crown which reveals his total supremacy. He captured her beautiful complexion by showing the decorative garland. How much does he have to do to get her complexion – beautiful ornaments, his part-by-part beauty, other decorations etc!
- *en mangai* – One who can defeat him with her age now lost her complexion! māmai niṟam – beautiful complexion. māmai – beautiful. She lost her beautiful complexion.

## 6.6.3. Niram kariyanukku

*niṟangariyānukku nīdulaguṇḍa tiṟangiḷar vāyc ciṟuk kaḷvar avarkku kaṟangiya cakkarak kaiyavanukku en piṟangirungūndal iḻandadu pīdē*

**Пословный перевод:**

niṟam kariyānukku – being the one with dark complexion; nīdu ulagu – the great worlds; uṇḍa – consumed; tiṟam – manner; kiḷar – revealing; vāy – being the one with divine lips; kaṟangiya – (setting out to destroy the enemies of the world) spinning and moving; cakkaram – having the divine chakra (disc); kaiyavanukk – for the one who is having the hand; en piṟangu irum kūndal – my daughter who has well grown, collection of locks; iḻandadu – lost; pīdu – pride

**Перевод:**

**My daughter who has well grown, collection of locks \[of hair\] lost her pride for the one who is with dark complexion, is having the divine lips which reveal the manner in which he consumed the great worlds and is having the hand with the divine chakra which is spinning and moving.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the th pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki‘s mother says “My daughter lost her pride being captivated by the beauty etc of emperumān who, mercifully rested on the banyan leaf”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, parānguśa nāyaki‘s mother says “My daughter lost her pride for emperumān who gives protection through his resting on banyan leaf”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. niṟangariyānukku nīdulaguṇḍa tiṟangiḷar vāyc ciṟuk kaḷvar avarkku kaṟangiya cakkarak kaiyavanukku en piṟangirungūndal iḻandadu pīdē*

- *niṟam kariyānukku* – She said “*iḻandadu māmai niṟam*” \[in previous pāsuram\]; since that complexion went and settled on him, he is doubly shining. He got a unique complexion on top of his natural one. No need to say “*neelak karu niṟa mēganiyāyaṟku*” anymore, since there is no match for his complexion anymore. She is talking about the glossy, cool and invigorating form.
- *nīdulagu …* – Having the divine lips which reveal how we consumed the expansive earth and placed it in his divine stomach. kiḷarugai – speaking; It is said in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 1.1.6 “*vaiyamēḻum kaṇḍāḷ piḷḷai vāyuḷē*” (Mother yaśōdā saw the entire world in kriṣṇa’s mouth). The divine lips which reveal his saviourśip.
- *siṟuk kaḷvar avarkku* – One who secures the huge worlds in his small stomach and hence having inconceivable activities.
- *nīdulaguṇḍa niṟam kiḷar vāy* – Instead of having to hear from someone else’s mouth, she could hear directly from his mouth.
- *siṟuk kaḷvar avarkku* – Having small form, but great eagerness to protect others. He captivated her by manifesting his saviourśip and the ability to perform impossible tasks.
- *kaṟangiya cakkarak kaiyavanukku* – kaṟangugai – spinning; one who is having the divine disc in his hands, which is always spinning due to the eagerness to destroy the enemies; not only he is a saviour, his entourage is also eager to protect. Whoever he has in his hands, will be eager to protect. Even śrī pāncajanyāḻvān (divine conch) prays to [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) “When a hurdle comes about, please blow me and eliminate the hurdle”.
- *en piṟangu irum kūndal* – My daughter has nicely rounded and length hair. Also explained as her having very lengthy hair. irumai – greatness; here the greatness is due to the length. piṟangudal – abundance. kūndal – hair. aimbāl, kūndal, kuḻal are all synonyms for hair. One who defeats the opponent with her hair, has lost her pride. pīdu – greatness. She lost the greatness which she brings about to him as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 37.18 “*yasyasā janakātmajā – apramēyam hi tattēja:*” (One cannot measure the greatness of the one who is married to the daughter of śrī janaka).

## 6.6.4. Pidudai nanmuganai

*pīdudai nānmuganaip padaittānukku mādudai vaiyam aḷanda maṇāḷaṟku nādudai mannarkkut tūdu sel nambikku en pādudai algul iḻandadu paṇbē*

**Пословный перевод:**

pīdu – having the greatness with respect to knowledge etc which match his ability to create; udai – having; nānmuganai – caturmuka brahmā; padaittānukku – being the creator; mādudai – opulent; vaiyam – earth; aḷanda – by the act of measuring; maṇāḷaṟku – the enjoyer who makes her exist exclusively for him; nādu – for the kingdom; udai – leader; mannarkku – for pāṇḍavas, the kings; tūdu – being the messenger; sey – performed; nambikku – for the one who became fully complete; en pādudai algul – my daughter who has an expansive waist; iḻandadu – lost; paṇbu – her distinguished quality

**Перевод:**

**emperumān is the creator of caturmuka brahmā who is having the greatness with respect to knowledge etc which match his ability to create; he is the enjoyer who makes her \[parānguśa nāyagi\] exist exclusively for him by his act of measuring the opulent earth; he went as the messenger on behalf of pāṇḍavas, the kings who are the leaders of the kingdom and hence became fully complete. My daughter who has an expansive waist lost her distinguished quality for such emperumān.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fourth pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki‘s mother says “My daughter lost her qualities for the quality of emperumān who in spite of being the creator of brahmā, fulfilled the desires of his devotees, disregarding his own supremacy”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. pīdudai nānmuganaip padaittānukku mādudai vaiyam aḷanda maṇāḷaṟku nādudai mannarkkut tūdu sel nambikku en pādudai algul iḻandadu paṇbē*

- *pīdudai* … – The creator of caturmuka brahmā who has the ability to create the 14 layered universe. pīdu – greatness.
- *mādu* … – mādu – wealth. Opulent earth; mādu also means spacious implying expansive earth. For the one who captured her through his mischievous act of mercifully measuring the world and made her exist exclusively for himself.
- *nādu* … – The one who went as the messenger for pāṇḍavas who owned the kingdom and hence became complete. Here āḻvār is highlighting pāṇḍavas as “*nādudai mannarkku*” based on bhagavān’s opinion, while duryōdana et al were ruling the kingdom saying “we will not even give a small town for pāṇḍavas”. sankśēpa rāmāyaṇam 85 “*abhiśiśyaca lankāyām*” (śrī rāma crowned vibhīśaṇa as the king of lankā and felt satisfied).
- *nambikku* – By the act which is highlighted in periya tirumoḻi 2.2.3 “*innār tūdan ena ninṟān*” (He stood as a certain person’s messenger), he stood with pride. He captured her qualities by manifesting his qualities such as creating the universe to start with, redeeming it by measuring it when some one claims ownership and making it exist for his devotees by performing menial acts.
- *en pādudai algul* – One who is having spacious waist/thigh region. pādu – space. The physical beauty which will even melt women as seen in mahābhāratam “*pumbhāvam manasā yuyu:*” (The women who saw the waist region of draupadi acquired masculinity). Just as [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) being explained as in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 3.29 “*pumsām druśti cittāpahāriṇam*” (śrī rāma’s beauty will even attract the eyes and mind of men).

## 6.6.5. Panbudai vedam

*paṇbudai vēdam payanda paranukku maṇpurai vaiyam idanda varāgarku teṇpunaṟpaḷḷi em dēva pirānukku en kaṇpunai kōdai iḻandadu kaṟpē*

**Пословный перевод:**

paṇbu – the noble quality of revealing bhagavān’s svarūpam etc as is; udai – having; vēdam – vēdam; payanda – providing it to brahmā et al; paranukku – the supreme lord who is revealed by it; maṇ – land mass; purai – having abundance; vaiyam – earth; idanda – lifted up; varāgaṟku – one who is in the form of a varāha (wild boar); teṇ – clear; punal – in the causal ocean containing water; paḷḷi – resting with the thoughts to protect the universe; em – for us; dēvar – and brahmā et al, without any distinction; pirānukku – for the one who is the benefactor; en kaṇ punai kōdai – my daughter who is wearing a garland which captivates the eyes of those who see her; iḻandadu – lost; kaṟpu – her knowledge

**Перевод:**

**The supreme lord who revealed the vēdam which is having the noble quality of revealing bhagavān’s svarūpam etc as is, who lifted up the earth which is having abundant land mass, is resting with the thoughts to protect the universe, in the causal ocean containing clear water. My daughter who is wearing a garland which captivates the eyes of those who see her, lost her intelligence for such emperumān who is the benefactor for us and brahmā et al.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fifth pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki‘s mother says “My daughter lost her knowledge for emperumān who did favours such as revealing vēdam”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. paṇbudai vēdam payanda paranukku maṇpurai vaiyam idanda varāgarku teṇpunaṟpaḷḷi em dēva pirānukku en kaṇpunai kōdai iḻandadu kaṟpē*

- *paṇbudai vēdam* – vēdam which is having the quality of revealing īśvara truly.
- *payanda* – Teaching brahmā as per *supta prabudda nyāyam* (logic where a person waking up from sleep will remember everything naturally) \[This is to indicate that the vēdam was never created and was only remembered/recollected from previous times\].
- *paranukku* – The one who is supreme due to bestowing brahmā the eyes to understand vēdam and due to being known from vēdam only as said in śvētāśvatara upaniśat “*yō brahmāṇam vidadāti pūrvam yōvai vēdāmśca prahiṇōti tasmai*” (bhagavān, before creating the universe, created brahmā and instructed vēdam to him). One who bestows knowledge to the ignorant, has destroyed her knowledge now.
- *maṇ purai vaiyam* – Earth which has abundant land mass.
- *idanda varāgaṟku* – Without distinguishing between earth and sky, he protected everything on his own. To redeem the true nature of others, he minimizes his own nature. Even the form he assumes to minimize his nature, is so attractive. It is said in nācciyār tirumoḻi 11.8 “*mānamilāp panṟiyām tēsu*” (the radiance of having the most humble pig form). The abundance of land mass is indicated to highlight the difficulty in lifting it up.
- *varāgaṟku* – Unlike his other acts of protection, this act is most important for everyone; as said in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 5.2.3 “*eyiṟṟidai maṇ koṇḍa endai irāp pagal ōduvittu ennaip payiṟṟip paṇi seyyak koṇḍān*” (My lord who lifted up earth on his tusk, instructed me day and night and engaged me in his service), the one who bestowed knowledge to some one similar to my daughter \[bhūmip pirātti\], has now destroyed her knowledge.
- *teṇ punal paḷḷi* – One who has the causal ocean which is having clear water, as his mattress. For the one who is resting on the ocean to create the universe which was destroyed previously, and is about to bestow knowledge to the entities who are created. One who is engaged in redeeming the existence and bestowing knowledge is himself taking back the knowledge that was bestowed by him!
- *em dēva pirānukku* – One who is the benefactor for brahmā, īśāna (rudra, Siva) et al. If one remains “īśvarōham” (I am supreme) \[like the dēvatās\], one need not lose the knowledge \[only those who are fully subservient lose their knowledge and become bewildered like this\].
- *en kaṇ punai kōdai* – Since her lock \[of hair\] binds the eyes of those who see it, she is having those eyes as the decoration for her lock. That is – those who see her lock, cannot take their eyes off it. The target of the eyes is her head.
- *iḻandadu kaṟpē* – parānguśa nāyaki is so knowledgeable that she can bestow knowledge to emperumān who bestows knowledge to all; such parānguśa nāyaki lost her knowledge! śrī rāmāyaṇam ayodāya kāṇḍam 26.4 “*abhijñārājadarmāṇām*” (One who knows the identities of kings). kaṟpu – kalvi (education), that is knowledge.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.6.6. Karpagak kavana

*kaṟpagak kāvana naṟpala tōḷaṟku poṟcudark kunṟanna pūndaṇmudiyaṟku naṟpala tāmarai nāṇmalark kaiyaṟku en viṟpuruvak kodi tōṟṟadu meyyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kaṟpagam kā ana – like a garden of kaṟpaga tree (a celestial wish-fulfilling tree); nal – more distinguished; pala – many; tōḷaṟku – one who has shoulders; sudar – having radiance; pon kunṟanna – like a golden hill; pū – attractive; taṇ – favourable; mudiyaṟku – wearing a divine crown; nal – beautiful; pala – many; tāmarai – lotus varieties; nāḷ malar – like a fresh flower; kaiyaṟku – one who his having hands; en vil puruvak kodi – my tender creeper like daughter who is having bow like eyebrow; tōṟṟadu – lost; mey – the body which was obedient towards her. Implies that her body is no longer under her control

**Перевод:**

**emperumān who has many shoulders which resemble a garden of kaṟpaga tree and are more distinguished than such a garden, is having the radiance of a golden hill; he is wearing an attractive and favourable divine crown; he is having many hands which are like fresh lotus flowers; for such emperumān, my tender creeper like daughter who is having bow like eyebrow has lost the body which was obedient towards her. Implies that her body is no longer under her control.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the sixth pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki‘s mother says “My daughter lost her body to the physical beauty of emperumān who is resting on the causal ocean”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. kaṟpagak kāvana naṟpala tōḷaṟku poṟcudark kunṟanna pūndaṇmudiyaṟku naṟpala tāmarai nāṇmalark kaiyaṟku en viṟpuruvak kodi tōṟṟadu meyyē*

\[Since no incarnation of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is separately highlighted here, it is considered to be focussing on the emperumān who is resting on causal ocean who was highlighted in the previous pāsuram.\]

- *kaṟpagak kāvu* … –  [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) showcased his divine limbs and captured her body.  Like a garden of kaṟpaga tree, having many shoulders which are even more beautiful than such a garden.
- *poṟcudar* … – Wearing a divine crown which matches his divine head which resembles a radiant and attractive golden hill. pū could also mean flower garland, implying that his crown is decorated with garland. This is representative for all his ornaments.
- *naṟpala* … – One who is having many beautiful, divine hands which are like fresh lotus flower.
- *en viṟpuruvak kodi* – My daughter who is having bow like eyebrow (and like a tender creeper). Like someone who had brahmāstram \[the greatest weapon\] at their disposal yet got defeated, she lost even with the presence of her eyebrow!
- *tōṟṟadu meyyē* – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) showed his form which is said as in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 40.10 “*ūrdvam māsān na jīviśyē*” (sītāp pirātti says – I will not survive for more than a month without seeing śrī rāma), and won over her form which is said as in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 66.10 “*na jīvēyam kśaṇamapi*” (śrī rāma says – I will not survive even for a moment without seeing sītā). Implies that her body is no longer under her control.

## 6.6.7. Meyyamar

*meyyamar palgalan nangaṇindānukku paiyaravinaṇaip paḷḷiyinānukku kaiyodu kāl seyya kaṇṇapirānukku en taiyal iḻandadu tannudaic cāyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

mey – with the divine form; amar – fitting well; pal – countless; kalan – ornaments; nangu – to be beautiful; aṇindānukku – having worn; pai – having expanded hoods; aravin aṇai – on the serpent bed; paḷḷiyinānukku – mercifully resting; kaiyodu – with divine hands; kāl – divine feet also; seyya – being reddish; kaṇṇan – obedient towards his devotees; pirānukk – for the benefactor; en – my; taiyal – very beautiful daughter; iḻandadu – lost; tannudai – her distinguished; cāy – collective beauty

**Перевод:**

**My very beautiful daughter lost her distinguished collective beauty for emperumān who is wearing countless beautiful ornaments which are fitting well with his divine form, who is mercifully resting on the serpent bed which is having expanded hoods, who is having reddish divine hands and divine feet and who is obedient towards his devotees.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the seventh pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki‘s mother says “My daughter being captivated by the ornaments of emperumān, who is resting in the milky ocean, lost her beauty”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. meyyamar palgalan nangaṇindānukku paiyaravinaṇaip paḷḷiyinānukku kaiyodu kāl seyya kaṇṇapirānukku en taiyal iḻandadu tannudaic cāyē*

- *mey amar pal kalan* – The ornaments starting with crown and ending with anklets which appear to have naturally grown out of his divine body \[such perfectly fitting ornaments\].
- *nangaṇindānukku* – The apt beauty due to the ornaments being worn by the one who qualifies to wear them.
- *pai aravu* … – ādiśēśa (serpent) who is having his hoods expanded due to coming in contact with [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) and who is having fragrance, softness, coolness etc as his nature. emperumān who is having such ādiśēśa as his mattress and who is mercifully resting on it. Even ādiśēśa appears to be an ornament for him; an ornament with endless faces. The mattress which highlights the decorations which were explained previously.
- *kaiyodu kāl* … – kriṣṇa who is having the reddish divine hands and feet which have contrasting complexion to his blackish divine body, and who is the benefactor. Due to his togetherness with tiruvanantāḻvān (ādiśēśan), his limbs become complete.
- *en taiyal* … – My daughter lost her collective beauty which improves her look, just as a gem appears attractive due to its radiance. He manifested his removable ornaments and took away her irremovable ornament \[her collective beauty\]. taiyal – girl; cāy – lāvaṇyam (collective beauty).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.6.8. Sayak kurundam

*sāyak kurundam ositta tamiyaṟku māyac cakadam udaitta maṇāḷaṟku pēyaip piṇam padap pāluṇ pirānukku en vāsak kuḻali iḻandadu māṇbē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kurundam – the kurundu tree which is possessed by a demon; sāya – to be uprooted; ositta – broke; tamiyaṟku – being independently valourous; sakadam – wheel; māya – to be finished; udaitta – kicked; maṇāḷaṟku – one who made me exist exclusively for him and became my enjoyer by such act; pēyai – pūtanā, the demoniac lady; piṇam – dead body; pada – to fall down as; pāl – breast milk; uṇ – consumed; pirānukku – for the great benefactor; en vāsak kuḻali – my daughter who has ultimate fragrant hair; iḻandadu – lost; māṇbu – her femininity

**Перевод:**

**My daughter who has ultimate fragrant hair lost her femininity to the great benefactor kriṣṇa who independently broke and uprooted the kurundu tree which was possessed by a demon, who kicked the wheel to finish it and made me exist exclusively for him and became my enjoyer by such act, who consumed the breast milk of pūtanā, the demoniac lady to make her fall down as a dead body. māyac cakadam also means mischievous wheel.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the eighth pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki‘s mother says “My daughter lost her femininity for kriṣṇa who has the history of destroying enemies”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. sāyak kurundam ositta tamiyaṟku māyac cakadam udaitta maṇāḷaṟku pēyaip piṇam padap pāluṇ pirānukku en vāsak kuḻali iḻandadu māṇbē*

- *sāyak kurundam ositta tamiyaṟku* – The one who on his own uprooted and felled the kurundu tree which had well grown branches due to being possessed by a demon. For the one who demonstrated his valour, in the absence of nambi mūttapirān (balarāma). parānguśa nāyaki thinks [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) will help her too in her loneliness.
- *māyac cakadam udaitta maṇāḷaṟku* – \[māya has two meanings – mischievous, to finish\] Implies mischievous wheel; to completely destroy the wheel as said in tiruvāimoḻi 6.9.4 “*taḷarndum muṟindum sagadavasurar udal vēṟāp piḷandu*” (the body of demon in the wheel, became tired and broke into pieces).
- *maṇāḷaṟku* – Just as śrī rāma broke the bow and captivated the divine daughter of śrī janaka, he manifested this activity to [parāṇguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) and made her exist exclusively for himself.
- *pēyaip piṇam pada pāl uṇ pirānukku* – The great benefactor kriṣṇa who consumed the milk of pūtanā and killed her, unlike śrī rāma who let sūrpaṇakā go free to cause harm in future.
- *en vāsak kuḻali* – For my daughter who has naturally fragrant hair. This is the cause for calling emperumān as “*sarvaganda:*” (root of all fragrances). tiruvāimoḻi 10.10.2 “*vāsam sey pūnguḻalāḷ*” (One who has very fragrant hair).
- *iḻandadu māṇbē* – He manifested his masculine aspects \[valourous acts\] and captured her femininity. māṇbu also implies beauty.

## 6.6.9. Manbamai

*māṇbamai kōlattu em māyak kuṟaḷaṟku sēṇ sudark kunṟanna senjudar mūrttikku kāṇ perum tōṟṟattu en kāgutta nambikku en pūṇ punai men mulai tōṟṟadu poṟpē*

**Пословный перевод:**

māṇbu – beauty; amai – present; kōlam – having form; em māyam – one who deceived mahābali and us to fulfil his desire; kuṟaḷaṟku – being vāmana; sēṇ – lofty due to having his desire fulfilled; sudar – radiant; kunṟanna – like a mountain; sem – reddish; sudar – having splendour; mūrttikku – one who is having the form; kāṇ – attractive for everyone; peru – having unlimited greatness; tōṟṟam – having the appearance; em – to be enjoyed by us; kāguttan – cakravarti tirumagan (śrī rāma, son of emperor daśarata); nambikku – one who is complete; en pūṇ punai men mulai – my daughter whose bosoms are tender to bear the separation and are decorated with ornaments; tōṟṟadu – lost; poṟpu – her beauty

**Перевод:**

**emperumān is having a beautiful form, who being vāmana deceived mahābali and us to fulfil his desire; he is having the form which is lofty due to having his desire fulfilled like a radiant mountain and is having reddish splendour; he is having the appearance which is attractive for everyone and is having unlimited greatness, to be enjoyed by us; my daughter whose bosoms are tender to bear the separation and are decorated with ornaments, lost her beauty for  such emperumān who is complete as cakravarti tirumagan.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the ninth pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki‘s mother says “My daughter lost her beauty being captivated by the divine beauty of emperumān who incarnated as śrī vāmana et al”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. māṇbamai kōlattu em māyak kuṟaḷaṟku sēṇ sudark kunṟanna senjudar mūrttikku kāṇ perum tōṟṟattu en kāgutta nambikku en pūṇ punai men mulai tōṟṟadu poṟpē*

- *māṇbu* … – For śrī vāmana who has beautiful decoration and amazing form. māṇbu – aḻagu – beauty. māyam can also mean mischief.
- *sēṇ sudar* … – As he was given water \[by mahābali\], he grew. For the one who has a form which is having beautiful splendour like a lofty, radiant mountain.
- *kāṇ perum tōṟṟattu* – tōṟṟam – aḻagu – beauty. Said to be having a form which is pleasing to the eyes and infinitely enjoyable. It can also imply the greatness of the incarnation as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam bāla kāṇḍam 3.10 “*janma rāmasya sumahat*” (The great incarnation of śrī rāma).
- *em kāgutta nambikku* – cakravarttit tirumagan who is complete in all qualities. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is the one who says as in [tiruvāimoḻi 3.6.8](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/09/thiruvaimozhi-3-6-8-thuyarame-tharu/) “*tayarataṟku magan tannai anṟi maṟṟilēn*” (I won’t exist for any one other than the son of daśarata). śrī rāmāyaṇam kiśkintā kāṇḍam 15.21 “*guṇānām ākarō mahān*” (the abode of all good qualities).
- *en pūṇ punai men mulai* – One who is having bosoms which are decorated with ornaments and which cannot bear the separation \[of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)\].
- *tōṟṟadu poṟpē* – poṟpu means aḻagu (beauty). Since it is said “*pūṇ punai men mulai*“, she lost the beauty which was acquired by the decoration. My daughter who will give joy to him by making him not think about anyone else due to her beautiful bosoms as said in mūnṟām tiruvandādi 3 “*malarāḷ tanattuḷḷān*” (one who resides in the bosom of śrī mahālakśmi who resides in the flower), has now been defeated here.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.6.10. Porpamai

*poṟpamai nīḷmudip pūndaṇ tuḻāyaṟku maṟporu tōḷudai māyap pirānukku niṟpana pal uruvāy niṟkumāyaṟku en kaṟpudaiyātti iḻandadu kattē*

**Пословный перевод:**

poṟpu – beauty; amai – present; nīḷ – tall; mudi – crown; pū – attractive; taṇ – invigorating; tuḻāyaṟku – one who is having tiruttuḻāy (tuḷasi); mal – with the mighty strong wrestlers; poru tōḷudai – wrestled with them carefully, not to lose the sandalwood paste on his shoulders; māyam – amazing; pirānukku – one who let the women of maturā enjoy his beauty; niṟpana – having their existence established through pramāṇam (authentic scriptures); pala – variegated; uru – objects; āy – having as his body; niṟkum – remaining untouched by their defects; māyaṟku – for the amazing emperumān; en kaṟpudaiyātti – my intelligent daughter; iḻandadu – lost; kattu – her feminine limits

**Перевод:**

**My intelligent daughter lost her feminine limits for emperumān who is wearing beautiful, tall crown and attractive, invigorating tiruttuḻāy, who amazingly wrestled with the mighty strong wrestlers carefully, not to lose the sandalwood paste on his shoulders and let the women of maturā enjoy his beauty, who is having variegated objects which are  having their existence established through pramāṇam, as his body and yet amazingly remaining untouched by their defects.**

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the tenth pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki‘s mother says “My daughter lost her femininity for emperumān who is śrīvaikuṇṭanāta, who destroyed the unfavourable ones in his incarnations such as kriṣṇa and who is having the universe as his body”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. poṟpamai nīḷmudip pūndaṇ tuḻāyaṟku maṟporu tōḷudai māyap pirānukku niṟpana pal uruvāy niṟkumāyaṟku en kaṟpudaiyātti iḻandadu kattē*

- *poṟpamai* … – For the [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is wearing tuḷasi garland which indicates his control/wealth \[over everything\] on the beautiful, divine crown which highlights his supremacy.
- *pūm taṇ tuḻāy* – Due to coming in contact with him, the tuḷasi appears blossomed and invigorating.
- *maṟporu* – incarnating, having suitable shoulders for wrestling.
- *māyappirānukku* – The amazing way he fought the wrestlers, without losing the sandalwood paste he was anointed with.
- *pirānukku* – Being the benefactor for the women of śrī maturā in presenting his beauty for  them to enjoy. He is said as in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 4.2.6 “*sāvattagartta sāndaṇi tōḷ caduran*” (the capable lord with sandalwood paste on his shoulder who killed the wrestlers). Also implies, for the one who performed many amazing favours.
- *niṟpana* … – While being the [antaryāmi](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) for stāvara (immovable entities), jangama (movable entities) etc, remaining untouched by their defects – such amazing personality.
- *en kaṟpudaiyātti* – My daughter who is greatly intelligent. Her knowledge makes her remain as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 39.30 “*tatdasya sadruśam bhavēt”* (śrī rāma saving me and accepting me will match his stature).
- *iḻandadu kattē* – He manifested what he had directly and accepted what she had. kattu – fully. kattu also means norms formed in the society. Implies that she crossed those norms.

## 6.6.11. Kattelil solai

*katteḻil sōlai nal vēngada vāṇanai katteḻil ten kurugūrc catakōpan sol katteḻil āyirattu ippattum vallavar katteḻil vānavar bōgam uṇbārē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kattu – of abundance; eḻil – having beauty; sōlai – having garden; nal – having the goodness of revealing bhagavān’s saulabhyam (simplicity) etc; vēngadam – for the tiurvēnkata (tirumalā) hill; vāṇanai – chief; katteḻil – having beautiful forts; then – attractive; kurugūr – chief of āḻvārtirunagari; satakōpan – nammāḻvār; sol – mercifully spoke; katteḻil – having beautifully arranged; āyirattu – thousand pāsurams; ippattum – this decad; vallavar – those who can recite well; katteḻil – being bound by the divine will of bhagavān; vānavar – nityasūris’; bōgam – enjoyment; uṇbār – will enjoy

**Перевод:**

**emperumān is the chief of tiurvēnkata hill which is having gardens with abundance of beauty  and having the goodness of revealing bhagavān’s saulabhyam (simplicity) etc; nammāḻvār, the chief of the attractive āḻvārtirunagari which is having beautiful forts, mercifully spoke about such emperumān in this decad among the beautifully arranged thousand pāsurams; those who can recite these well will enjoy the enjoyment of nityasūris who are bound by the divine will of bhagavān. katteḻil also implies completely beautiful/orderly in all the four lines.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the end, āḻvār says “Those who are experts of this decad will enjoy the bliss of ayarvaṟum amarargaḷ (residents of parampadam)”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. katteḻil sōlai nal vēngada vāṇanai katteḻil then kurugūrc catakōpan sol katteḻil āyirattu ippattum vallavar katteḻil vānavar bōgam uṇbārē*

- *katteḻil* … – kadi is changed to kattu implying fragrant, beautiful garden.
- *nal vēngadam* – tirumalā which is apt for both śēśa (servitor) and śēśi (lord).
- *vāṇanai* – Chief, controller. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) praised tiruvēngadamudaiyān only. He himself said in tiruvāimoḻi 3.9.1 “*en nāvil in kavi yān oruvarkkum kodukkilēn*” (The songs from my tongue will not be submitted to anyone other than śrīnivāsa).
- *katteḻil then kurugūr* – kattu – araṇ – fort. Fortified [āḻvārtirunagari](http://azhwarthirunagari.koyil.org/).
- *katteḻil āyiram* – kattu – todai – poetic rule. Having poetic beauty.
- *katteḻil vānavar* – (The great) nityasūris who are fully in the mode of goodness. “katteḻil” can also be an attribute for bhōgam (enjoyment). In the samsāram (material realm), due to being bound by karma, all enjoyment will be both insignificant and temporary.  In paramapadam, since they match the nature of ātmā and bhagavān, they will be abundant and eternal.

In all the four lines, kattu could mean “completeness”. tirumalā which is the ultimate abode for his simplicity, is the place for surrendering unto him; paramapadam which is the ultimate abode for his supremacy, is the place for enjoyment; tiruvēngadam is said as in tiruvāimoḻi 9.3.8 “*onṟiyākkai pugāmai uyyak koḷvān ninṟa tiruvēngadam*” (tirumalā is the abode of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who does not let us get a materialistic birth and will uplift us).
