## 6.7 Unnum soru

## 6.7.1. Unnum soru

*uṇṇum sōṟu parugu nīr tinnum veṟṟilaiyum ellām kaṇṇan emperumān enṟenṟē kaṇgaḷ nīr malgi maṇṇinuḷ avan sīr vaḷam mikkavanūr vinavi tiṇṇam en iḷa mān pugumūr tirukkōḷūrē ḷisten*

**Пословный перевод:**

uṇṇum – To be continuously consumed to sustain oneself; sōṟum – rice \[food\]; parugum – To be drunk to nourish oneself by quenching the thirst; nīr – water; tinnum – to be consumed for pleasure; veṟṟilaiyum – betel leaves; ellām – all objects (which give sustenance, nourishment and enjoyment); kaṇṇan – being kriṣṇa, the son of vasudēva as said in śrī bhagavat gītā 7.19 “vāsudēva sarvam” (Everything is kriṣṇa); em – for me; perumān – he who is the lord; enṟu enṟē – repeating many times; kaṇgaḷ – eyes; nīrgaḷ – tears; malgi – overflow; maṇṇin uḷ – in the earth (where he descended to manifest himself to his devotees); avan – his; sīr – qualities such as saulabhya (easy approacability), saundarya (beauty), sauśeelya (simplicity) etc; vaḷam – due to abundance of consorts; mikkavan – one who is complete; Ur – town; vinavi – \[probing about\] not just thinking about it herself (due to overwhelming love, asking others as if being ignorant, to have good companion during the journey); en – due to being my daughter; iḷam – young; mān – due to being at the ignorant age, like a deer, she cannot go far; pugum – enter; Ur – town; tirukkōḷūrē – tirukkōḷur only; tiṇṇam – certain

**Перевод:**

**My daughter repeats many times “kriṣṇa, my lord who is the son of vasudēva as said in śrī bhagavat gītā 7.19 “vāsudēva sarvam” , is the food which is continuously consumed to sustain myself, water which is drunk to nourish me by quenching the thirst and betel leaves which are consumed for pleasure, and all other objects”.  Saying this with overflowing tears, probing about the qualities such as saulabhya, saundarya, sauśeelya etc and the earthly town of emperumān who is complete due to having abundance of consorts, due to being my daughter and at the ignorant age, like a young deer, she cannot go far; it is certain that she entered tirukkōḷūr.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the first pāsuram, as parānguśa nāyaki‘s mother does not see her daughter in her palace, since she is her own daughter and knowing about her nature, determines that she would have gone to tirukkōḷūr only.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*In the first pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki‘s mother firmly says “She would have gone to tirukkōḷūr which is the abode of kriṣṇa who is the dāraka (sustenance), pōśaka (nourishment), bhōjña (enjoyment) etc”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. uṇṇum sōṟu parugu nīr tinnum veṟṟilaiyum ellām kaṇṇan emperumān enṟenṟē kaṇgaḷ nīr malgi maṇṇinuḷ avan sīr vaḷam mikkavanūr vinavi tiṇṇam en iḷa mān pugumūr tirukkōḷūrē Listen*

- *uṇṇum sōṟu parugu nīr tinnum veṟṟilaiyum ellām kaṇṇan* – Did she go searching for a greater experience! Did she survive with food and water here and go searching for [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) to sustain herself! For those who live as said in taittirīya upaniśat “*ahamannam … ahamannāda:*” (I am the food and I am the consumer of food – residents of parampadam are enjoyed by emperumān and they in turn enjoy emperumān), is it necessary to go anywhere else? Is it not sufficient to say “*sōṟu, taṇṇīr, veṟṟilai*“? What is the need for the qualifying words such as “*uṇṇum, parugum, tinnum*“? tiruvaḷḷuvar too said in kuṟaḷ 1105 “*vētta poḻudil avai avai pōlumē tōttār kaduppināḷ tōḷ*” (Her shoulders which are decorated with flowers, give the pleasure I need, then and there) (That is – the food, water, betel leaves when in need, give a lot more pleasure than normally – this is how the dear shoulders of the beloved person will feel). Similarly, these objects will sometimes be undesirable; to [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar), bhagavat viśayam (matters relating to [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)) will always feel like the desirable state of these sustaining, nourishing and pleasure giving objects.
- *ellām kaṇṇan* – She feels everything is kriṣṇa as said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 7.19](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/7-19/) “*vāsudēva sarvam*” (Everything is kriṣṇa). Since it is said “uṇṇum sōṟu” (food being consumed, present tense), it appears that other food will reduce in quantity when consumed, and this food (bhagavat viśayam) will never reduce in quantity even if consumed. It is said in periya tiruvandādi 78 “*kaṇai nāṇil ōvāt toḻil sārngan tol sīrai nannenjē ōvāda ūṇāga uṇ*” (Oh good heart! Enjoy the unending qualities of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is valorously engaged with his endless arrows and bow). This (bhagavat viśayam) can be consumed endlessly and will never dry up; this is as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 2.5.4](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/03/thiruvaimozhi-2-5-4-epporulum-thanay/) “*appoḻudaikkappoḻudu en ārāvamudam*” (my unending nectar for every moment) and in [tiruvāimoḻi 4.7.2](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/03/thiruvaimozhi-4-7-2-kolla-mala/) “*koḷḷa māḷā inba veḷḷam*” (endless ocean of bliss to consume).
- *emperumān* – There is nothing in this list, which he can’t be. He himself, the apt lord, remains these to me. Just her presence is sufficient for us \[mothers\].
- *enṟu enṟē* – Only if she considers something else capable of sustaining her, she will talk about something else. Reciting this only. He is not such \[inferior\] matter that she can recite about him once and then engage in eating, sleeping etc.
- *kaṇgaḷ nīrgaḷ malgi* – This is their \[mothers’\] “*uṇṇum sōṟu, parugu nīr, tinnum veṟṟilai etllām*“. They sustain just by seeing her face. Should she who has gone to sustain herself take away our sustenance? When a person is too immersed in bhagavat viśayam with flowing tears, isn’t it apt just to see him? If one is a cētana (sentient being), one should perform mangaḷāśāsanam (pray for well-being) to such persons as said in tiruviruttam 2 “*aḻunīr tuḷumba alamaruginṟana vāḻiyarō*” (she is stumbling upon with tears in her eyes due to separation from her lord; long live!). nanjīyar mercifully used to say “I heard tiruvāimoḻi from piḷḷai tirunaṟaiyūr araiyar thrice; I don’t remember anything from that; but, when he starts explaining a pāsuram, he would become weak and start crying and I would remember that posture fondly”. śrīviṣṇu tatvam ślōkam is explained here: *āhlāda śīta nētrāmbu –* Unlike the hot tears due to separation, these are cool tears due to enjoying [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/); *pulakī kruta gātravān* – having goosebumps all over the body; *paraguṇāviśta:* – being immersed in bhagavān’s qualities as being possessed by good spirits; such person is *sarva dēhibi: draśtavya:* – to be seen by everyone who has a body. The whole purpose of accepting a body is to see such a person; *sadā draśtavya:* –  Should one go to paramapadam to constantly see \[bhagavān as said in *sadā paśyanti*\]? When [anantāḻvān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/ananthazhwan/) saw a śrīvaiṣṇava who was working in a farm land in cōḻakulāndagan (a village), he asked “which is your native place?” and he replied “my native place is tirukkōḷūr”. anantāḻvān asked “Why did you leave that town and come here?” and he replied “I could not have my livelihood there”. anantāḻvān said “Could you not herd some donkeys there and live there? You have lost the eternal livelihood \[[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)\]”.
- *kaṇṇan emperumān enṟu enṟē kaṇgaḷ nīrgaḷ malgi* – This could be understood as joyful tears due to immense experience; or it could be overflowing tears due to constant meditation.
- *maṇṇinuḷ* … – In this earth, tirukkōḷūr is the apt place to reach. In paramapadam, a particular place need not be specifically mentioned \[since everything is enjoyable there\].
- *avan sīr vaḷam mikkavan Ur* – The town which has his auspicious qualities and unlimited wealth. As said in taittirya upaniśad ānandavalli “*sōśnutē sarvān kāman saha brahmaṇā*” (He experiences all auspicious qualities of [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) who is omniscient) as one has [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) and his qualities as goal, the abodes which are dear to him are also part of the goal.
- *avan sīr* – His auspicious qualities. That is, those qualities which he manifests to attract her.
- *vaḷam mikkavan Ur* – While paramapadam is the grand assembly, the abode where he acquires what he desires is the real abode! It is said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 41.4 “*kim kāryam sītayā mama*” (What is the use of bringing sītā back \[at the cost of losing of sugrīva\]”. Even more than paramapadam, the abode of his devotees is his real abode and that which is well fitting for his divine heart.
- *vaḷam mikkavan* – Also known as very capable in loving affection. That is, he made her give up her residence and come all the way to his abode.
- *vinavi* – Asking those who cross her “how far is tirukkōḷūr?’, they said “it is just close by” , she uses those \[comforting\] words as pastime during her journey. “*pādēyam puṇḍarikākśa nāma sankīrtanāmrutam*” (Chanting of the divine names of the lotus-eyed lord is the food/pastime during the journey). Her divine mother is grieving because when she asks “How far is tirukkōḷūr”, her divine lips are lacking freshness \[due to the grief of separation\].
- *en iḷa mān pugumūr tirukkōḷūrē* – Due to having been born as my daughter and due to her nature, the mother is certain that she would have gone to tirukkōḷūr only. One will naturally inherit the qualities of one’s mother. Even the omniscient bharatvāja ruśi \[though this is said by śrī guhap perumāḷ, since bharatvāja ruśi too has same thoughts, here it is said to be the ruśi’s words\] saw śrī bharatāḻvān who cannot sustain himself without śrī rāma, and said as in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 85.7 “*kaccin na duśtō vrajasi*” (Are you coming with any evil intent? I have doubts in your intent seeing your great army), based on the qualities of his mother \[kaikēyi\] and asked him “You have sent him to the forest; are you following him here to trouble him further thinking ‘if perumāḷ (śrī rāma) survives, it is like a tumour in the lower abdomen'”; though he saw bharatāḻvān’s mood, he doubted him due to his mother’s nature; hunters perfectly determine the scenario on observing the nature of the objects; so, when śrī bharatāḻvān entered their region, he felt happy and said “you have come to this abode of the servitors”; still, he thought “when kings enter the region of hunters, they would only do so for enquiry” and spoke to śrī bharatāḻvān with both humility and authority and doubted him due to his mother’s nature. Similarly, the divine mother too, considering [parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) being her daughter, is certain that she would have entered tirukkōḷūr only. Would śrī rāma’s arrow miss its target \[it would certainly capture her daughter\]! So, she says “my daughter’s destination is tirukkōḷūr only”.
- *iḷa mān* – While eliminating the shyness from her who is very young, it should be [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) there!
- *en iḷa mān* – One who did not follow the rules. \[Also\] She rushed to tirukkōḷūr disregarding her own tender nature.
- *pugum Ur* – Just as a person who got caught in a forest fire, would run towards pond and garden, for the one who is caught in the forest fire in the desert land of samsāram (material realm), the divine abodes which are dear to [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) ([divya dēśams](https://koyil.org/)) are the ponds and gardens. Since it is said as “pugum Ur”, it is implied that those who enter this town will never return. When [emperumānār (bhagavat rāmānujar)](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/emperumanar/) went on a pilgrimage down south \[from śrīrangam\], he saw a girl coming out of tirukkōḷūr and asked “Where are you coming from?” and she replied “from tirukkōḷūr”. He mercifully said to her “Would any girl who entered this town, leave from there!”. My daughter certainly went to tirukkōḷūr – I am sure about it. When children are lost, people will go straight to the temple to find them there \[such a wonderful abode of emperumān\].

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.7.2. Urum nadum

*ūrum nādum ulagamum tannaip pōl avanudaiya pērum tārgaḷumē pidaṟṟak kaṟpuvān idaṟi sērum nal vaḷam sēr paḻanat tirukkōḷūrkkē pōrungol? uraiyīr kodiyēn kodi pūvaigaḷē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

ūrum – the town (where she resides); nādum – the country (which encompasses the town); ulagamum – the world (which encompasses the country); tannaip pōl – like herself; avanudaiya – his; pērum – name; tārgaḷum – garland; pidaṟṟa – blabbering (in many ways); vān – boundless like the sky; kaṟpu – feminine modesty; idaṟi – crossing over; nal – distinguished; vaḷam – with opulence; sēr – having; paḻanam – having water bodies; tirukkōḷūrkkē – to tirukkōḷūr; sērum – reaching; kodiyēn – my daughter who has given the suffering of separation to me; kodi – my daughter who cannot sustain herself without him like a creeper which requires support; pōrum kol – would she return?; pūvaigaḷē – Oh mynās! (birds belonging to the Starling family); uraiyīr – please tell

**Перевод:**

**Oh mynās! My daughter who has given the suffering of separation to me and who cannot sustain herself without him like a creeper which requires support, making the town, the country and the world blabber his name and garland, crossed the feminine modesty which was boundless like sky, and reached tirukkōḷūr which is having distinguished opulence and water bodies. Would she return? Please tell.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the second pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki‘s mother asks the mynā birds “Would my daughter who entered tirukkōḷūr ever return?”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. ūrum nādum ulagamum tannaip pōl avanudaiya pērum tārgaḷumē pidaṟṟak kaṟpuvān idaṟi sērum nal vaḷam sēr paḻanat tirukkōḷūrkkē pōrungol? uraiyīr kodiyēn kodi pūvaigaḷē!*

- *ūrum nādum* … – What is the shortcoming in her situation here?  Did she have some shortcoming here and go there to eliminate such shortcoming? \[ōr\] Did she not have good companions here as said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 10.9](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/10-9) “*bōdayanta: parasparam*” and go searching for a special abode seeking out for such companion as said in puruśa sūktam 1.18 “… *yatra pūrvē sādyās santi dēvā:*” (Those dēvas in paramapadam know that abode as a great one)? Similar to how [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) made those who are in paramapadam as good as he is, as said in muṇḍaka upaniśat 3.1.3 “*niranjana: paramam sāmyam upaiti*” ([jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) attains equality (in eight qualities) with supreme lord), she too made everyone as good as herself here.

\[Did she transform others to be like her?\]

- *ūrum nādum ulagamum tannaip pōl* – The town she lived ([āḻvārtirunagari](http://azhwarthirunagari.koyil.org/)), the region which encompasses that town (pāṇḍiya nādu) and the world which encompasses it. \[Mother is\] saying “In śrī rāmāvatāram, only one town (ayōdyā) got reformed; but here the whole material realm got reformed!”. Her effect is so great that it has reached even up to us. Saying that it climbed all kinds of lands as said in stōtra ratnam 3 ” *lōkē’vatīrṇa paramārta samagra bhakti yōgāya*” (one who has incarnated in this world, being the ultimate benefit and being complete and having bhakti yōga).
- *ūrum nādum* … – As said in nācciyār tirumoḻi 9.8 “*kālai eḻundirundu kariya kuruvik kaṇangaḷ mālin varavu solli*” (The blackish sparrows, waking up early in the morning, inform the arrival of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)) – during brahma muhūrta (early morning hours) even the birds wake up and inform her how emperumān is arriving with lots of love towards her. Informing about how emperumān who should be visited by everyone, is visiting her.
- *tannaip pōl avanudaiya pērum tārgaḷumē pidaṟṟa* – Her blabbering is the result of his bestowing her with unblemiśed knowledge and devotion! Their blabbering is the result of her \[state\]!
- *pidaṟṟa* – Making her speak incoherently after being immersed in bhagavat viśayam, unlike spoken coherently after thinking through what to speak.
- *avanudaiya pērum tārgaḷum* – Her saying “*sangennum cakkamennum tuḻāyennum*” (his conch, disc and tuḷasi garland), “dēva dēvapirān” (dēvapirān the lord of all dēvas) , and “*virai mattalar taṇḍhuḻāy*” (fresh, honey filled tuḷasi garland).
- *pidaṟṟa* – As said in mahābhāratam mōkśa darmam 34 “*śrutōyamartō rāmasya jāmadagnyasya jalpata:*” (This principle is heard from the blabbering of paraśurāma who is the son of jamadagni).
- *kaṟpuvānidaṟi* – Stepping over the feminine modesty which is as lofty as sky. Crossing over the modesty which cannot be crossed by anyone. Stepping over the mountain like modesty like stepping over a lowly stone and as a great flood will flow over high and low lying lands in the same manner, going to tirukkōḷūr, disregarding nāṇ (shyness), madam (humility), accam (fear) etc.
- *kaṟpu vānidaṟi* – Also said as strong knowledge and great knowledge. In this case, kaṟpu means kalvi (knowledge). Thus, knowledge is said with kaṟpu and its strength is said with vān. Alternatively, kaṟpu means kalvi and vān means pride/fame, indicating great knowledge. Only when there is a limit to the desire, there will be hurdles. They are of the nature of saying as in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 3.6.1 “*kāvalum kadandu*” (crossing the barrier). śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 5.13.19 “*yayau ca kācit prēmāntā*” – a woman \[from gōkulam\] left \[seeking kriṣṇa\]. Who took her? Guided by the darkness of love, she went. śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 5.18.22 “*kurava:kim kariśyanti dagdānām virahāgninā*” (what would the elders do to us. I am burnt by this fire of separation) – When said “they are elders, you have to listen to them”, she said “can they pour water on this fire of separation to cool it down?”.
- *sērum* … – She who is waited here by her dear ones \[like [madurakavi āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/madhurakavi-azhwar/) et al\] has left for there to satisfy her own desire! She who lived here to reform others is now seeking a reformed abode \[divya dēśam with [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)\]! She who is looked up for their sustenance here, is now seeking him for her sustenance!
- *sēru nal vaḷam* … – Only to tirukkōḷūr which is having matching wealth and water bodies.
- *tirukkōḷūrkkē pōrum kol* – pōrum kol implies pugum kol (enter). Alternative explanation – She is saying about her daughter’s heart which reached there before her and is looking for her safe arrival. Another explanation – She is asking the mynās if her daughter would return.
- *kodiyēn* – Though I am fortunate to have her as my daughter, I have committed sins to ask you about her.
- *kodi* – Without the support, my daughter will stay on the ground like a creeper. [iraṇḍām tiruvandādi 27](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/10/irandam-thiruvandhadhi-27/) “*kōl tēdiyōdum koḻundadē pōnṟadē māl tediyōdum manam”* (my heart which is seeking [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is resembling a creeper which seeks a supporting pole).
- *kodiyēn kodi* – I have committed a great sin that she gave me  up, who gave birth to her and ended up searching for some one else. It appears that “leaving the mother” is a hereditary quality for this clan \[of [āḻvārs](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/azhwars/) as seen in periya tirumoḻi 3.7.1 “kaḷvan kol” and in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 3.8.1 “*nalladōr tāmaraip poygai*”.
- *pūvaigāḷ – pōrungol – uraiyīr* – She is looking at herself and thinking “one can leave one’s mother but one can never leave one’s children”. She would not want me to know about her plans to go but she would have shared the same with you. \[You, the mynās, are like her children\] One cannot hide anything from one’s children.
- *uraiyīr* – She thinks that while her daughter informed them about her plans, they are not revealing the same to her.
- *pōrum kol* – The reason for her doubt on whether her daughter will return or not is – since I am here, she may not return; but since you are here, she may return for you; would my strong sins stop her from returning? ōr would she return on seeing you? Please tell! \[But\] If she had told you before leaving as said in śrī rāmāvatāram, the whole world would have followed her! ḍidn’t they all follow śrī rāma as said in perumāḷ tirumoḻi 8.6 “*suṟṟam ellām pin todara …*” (followed by all the kinsmen, śrī rāma entered the forest)

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.7.3. Puvai paingiligal

*pūvai paingiḷigaḷ pandu tūdai pūmbuttilgaḷ yāvaiyum tirumāl tirunāmangaḷē kūvi eḻum en pāvai pōy init taṇ paḻanat tirukkōḷūrkkē kōvai vāy tudippa maḻaik kaṇṇodu en seyyungolō?*

**Пословный перевод:**

puvai – mynās; pai – green; kiḷigaḷ – parrots; pandu – ball; tūdai – small wooden pot; pū – to place the flowers; puttilgaḷ – baskets; yāvaiyum – (to acquire the same joy which is acquired from) all these; tirumāl – śrīman nārāyaṇan’s; tirunāmangaḷē – divine names only; kūvi – reciting; eḻum – uplifting oneself through that; en – my; pāvai – daughter; ini – even after this joy of reciting the divine names is available \[here\]; taṇ – cool; paḻanam – having water bodies; tirukkōḻūrkkē – to tirukkōḷūr only; pōy – went; kōvai – like kōvai (a reddish) fruit; vāy – lips; tudippa – to tremble; maḻai – have lots of tears like rain; kaṇṇōdu – standing with eyes; en seyyum kolō – what will she do?

**Перевод:**

**My daughter who is uplifting herself only through the recital of śrīman nārāyaṇan‘s divine names in place of the joy acquired by the mynās, green parrots, ball, small wooden pot and the baskets used to keep the flowers, even after this joy of reciting the divine names is available, only went to tirukkōḷūr which is having cool water bodies; what will she do standing there with her trembling kōVai fruit like lips and the eyes which have lots of tears like rain?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the third pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki‘s mother says “How will she grieve when she nears tirukkōḷūr?”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, parānguśa nāyaki‘s mother says “How will parānguśa nāyaki who considers recital of bhagavān’s divine names to be as good as all the joy she acquires while playing with her beautiful objects such as mynā, ball etc, be grieving on not having her desires fulfilled after reaching tirukkōḷūr?”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. pūvai paingiḷigaḷ pandu tūdai pūmbuttilgaḷ yāvaiyum tirumāl tirunāmangaḷē kūvi eḻum en pāvai pōy init taṇ paḻanat tirukkōḷūrkkē kōvai vāy tudippa maḻaik kaṇṇodu en seyyungolō?*

- *pūvai* … – She who should be enjoying with playful things, is sustaining herself with recital of the divine names, and has gone! Did she have something else to sustain while she was here and go there to sustain herself by him? Whatever bliss she should acquire with her mynā etc, as said in [dvaya mahā mantram](http://ponnadi.blogspot.in/2015/12/rahasya-thrayam.html), she acquired the same by reciting the divine names of śriya:pati (śrīman nārāyaṇan). \[Now, a few contrary opinions are rejected and to confirm that the aforementioned principle is the actual meaning\]. peṟṟi asked nampiḷḷai – as said in \[the previous pāsuram\] “*ūrum nādum ulagamum tannaip pōl*“, can we say that all the entities which she uses in her play-time, are reciting [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s divine names? nampiḷḷai replied “That cannot be said since her belongings include pandu (ball), tūdai (small pot) etc, which cannot recite the names”. peṟṟi was satisfied with the explanation. Can we say that she named them with emperumān’s divine names and called them? No, that will also not fit her great love for him as said in the first pāsuram “*uṇṇum sōṟu parugu nīr tinnum veṟṟilaiyum*” \[So the original explanation stands out as the correct one\].
- *pūvai* … – After tasting the divine names, she would not like to see her belongings which she uses in her play; this is similar to śrī bharatāḻvān becoming averse to seeing his own kingdom. The morning after completing the final rites for daśarata cakravarati, śrī bharatāḻvān set out thinking “The citizens may think that I am also in agreement with kaikēyi’s wrong-doings; I should announce that I have no such defects”. While the whole ministry had come together thinking “we have lost the emperor; the apt one to succeed has left for the forest; now we should run the country with the help of the remaining princes” and arranged for playing of auspicious drums and musical instruments. On hearing this śrī bharatāḻvān went through the torment which [parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s friend went through on hearing the beating of the drums to announce the groom-seeking event for parāngusa nāyaki as seen in tiruvāimoḻi 8.9 “*karumāṇikka malai*“. śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam ślōkams 82.10 and 82.12 are explained \[śrī bharatāḻvān is addressing vaśiśta\].
   - *vilalāpa sabhā madyē –* He is not losing his svarūpam in seclusion \[but in the grand assembly\]. śēśatvam (servitude) is his svarupam \[true nature\]; they are trying to deprive him of that true nature!
   - *jagarhēca* – Like those who are late for sandyāvandanam would be reprimanded by the elders.
   - *purōhitam* – While we are here to take care of our traditions \[of elder son taking the throne\], it is amusing that you are trying to change those traditions.
   - *sabhā madyē jagarhē* – He violated the principle mentioned in āpastamba darmam “*niyamātikramam rahasibōdayēt*” (when ācāryas commit mistakes intentionally or unintentionally, they must be enquired humbly in private) since they lost their purōhitatvam \[purōhita means one who has a long term vision\].
   - *rājyam ca aham ca rāmasya* – When there are dependent entities, can one of them rule over the other? If that is the case, let the kingdom rule me.
   - *darmam vaktum ihārhasi* – In this world there are some who kill their fathers or elder brothers to take over the kingdom; don’t think that “I will be like that too”; know my nature and speak accordingly.
   - *katam daśaratājjātō bhavēt rājyāpahāraka:* – How will I, who am born as the son of daśarata who gave up his life on separation of śrī rāma, think about taking over the kingdom? If I take over the kingdom, which he gave up …
   - *namasyāmi krutānjali:* – śrī bharatāḻvān is atoning for having to hear such inappropriate words from vaśiśta.
- *en pāvaiyē ini* – My daughter who was fully obedient to me, has now left me. Also, explained as “my daughter who has natural femininity”.
- *ini pōy* – She is already thinking that [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) gives her everything which is given by her play things. What more will she get by going to tirukkōḷūr?
- *taṇ paḻanat tirukkōḷūrkkē –* To tirukkōḷūr which has invigorating water bodies.
- *kōvai vāy tudippa* – To have her reddish fruit like lips tremble. Her lips are twitching to tell him “You said you won’t leave but left me; you said you will come but did not come; you left me alone in separation; you waited until I arrived there and so on”.
- *kōvai vāyt tudippa maḻaik kaṇṇodu* – The tears rolling down her eyes are stopping her from revealing her mind! Being broken, due to her tears, she could not reveal her mind. As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 99.38 “*uktvāryēti sakrut dīnam punar nōvāca kincana*” (śrī bharatāḻvān said in a meek voice “ārya” and remained silent after that).
- *en seyyum kolō* – She will not speak; won’t stop speaking; won’t stop crying; what suffering is  she going through? We are fortunate to witness her beautiful posture of enjoying his divine names giving up us and others! But we are unfortunate not to witness her enjoying him. The emotional reactions are not the same when meditating and directly seeing; it is as said in nānmugan tiruvandādi 78 “*kāman udal koṇḍa tavattāṟku umai uṇartta vaṇḍalambum tāralangal nīḷ mudiyān than peyarē kēttirundu angāralangalānamiyāl – kaṇḍu vaṇanginārkku*” (rudra who burnt down manmata was informed by his wife pārvati about [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s divine name; immediately upon hearing the divine names of emperumān who is wearing a tall crown which is decorated with a flower garland which resounds the humming sound of beetles, he became immediately charged emotionally; if we analyse this what will happen to those who see and worship him directly?). The mother is saying “I have seen her posture of being in separation but have not seen her posture after her attaining him”.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.7.4. Kollai enbarkolo

*kollai enbar kolō? guṇam mikkanaḷ enbar kolō? cillai vāyp peṇḍugaḷ ayaṟcēri uḷḷārum ellē! selvam malgi avan kidanda tirukkōḷūrkkē mellidai nudanga iḷamān sella mēvinaḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

selvam malgi – being the one who is having great wealth; avan – emperumān; kidanda – mercifully resting; tiukkōḷūrkkē – to tirukkōḷūr; mel – slender; idai – waist; nudanga – to sway; iḷa – young; mān – my daughter who appears like a deer; sella – to go; mēvinaḷ – has her heart fixated; sillai – being naturally quarrel-mouthed; vāy – having mouth; peṇḍugaḷ – women who are in close proximity; ayaṟcēri – in the near-by town; uḷḷārum – the residents; kollai – crossed the limits; enbarkolō – would they condemn?; guṇam mikkanaḷ – having great qualities (which induce us to greatly like her); enbarkolō – would they praise?; ellē – alas!

**Перевод:**

**My young deer like daughter has her heart fixated, with her slender waist swaying, to go to tirukkōḷūr where emperumān who is having great wealth is mercifully resting; Would the naturally quarrel-mouthed women who are in close proximity and the residents of the near-by town condemn my daughter saying she crossed the limits or praise her saying she is having great qualities? Alas! \[Crying out in sorrow\]**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fourth pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki‘s mother says “Seeing my daughter’s activities, will the quarrel-mouthed residents of our town and the near-by town and the other women condemn her by saying that she is lacking good qualities or praise her by saying that she is having auspicious qualities?”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, parānguśa nāyaki‘s mother says “She has decided to go to tirukkōḷūr which is the abode of emperumān who has unsurpassed opulence; what would the residents of the town speak of her?”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. kollai enbar kolō? guṇam mikkanaḷ enbar kolō? cillai vāyp peṇḍugaḷ ayaṟcēri uḷḷārum ellē! selvam malgi avan kidanda tirukkōḷūrkkē mellidai nudanga iḷamān sella mēvinaḷē*

- *kollai enbarkolō* – Would they say that she crossed the limits stepping out of the home, she performed a forbidden act, she acted crossing the limits? kollai means acts which cross the limits.
- *guṇam mikkanaḷ enbarkolō* – Would they praise her saying she acted like someone who is of great qualities?
- *kollai enbarkolō guṇam mikkanaḷ enbarkolō* – Would they say she ignored the rules; or would they understand the truth and say that? Would they say that her act is inapt based on certain rules and regulations; or would they say that it is apt based on her taste and the greatness of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)? Would they stumble upon thinking about the rules of sādana (bhagavān as the only upāyam); or would they be clear understanding one’s true nature? Would they see the nature of the upāyam and say this is not correct; or would they see nature of the one who is attaining and what one is attaining and say this is correct? When one thinks about one’s nature of being totally dependent on bhagavān, one cannot step out; but if one meditates upon the goal which matches the true nature, one cannot stop from going there. Would they censure her citing the rules; or would they praise her seeing the statements which support divine love? tārā \[wife of vāli\] said to iḷaiya perumāḷ (lakśmaṇa) “Why are you who is detached, tormenting us who are attached to love?” as in śrī rāmāyaṇam kiśkintā kāṇḍam 33.55 “*na kāma tantrē tava buddirasti*“.
- *sillai vāyp peṇḍugaḷ* – The women who keeps chattering. Those women who consider that which happens due to the greatness of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) also as ordained rules. Only when something is done considering such act as upāyam (means), it is bound by rules; when one is driven by the qualities of emperumān, rules will not apply.
- *ayal cēri uḷḷārum* – (The chattering women from our town and other women from nearby town) Those who who are totally different from the residents of her town.
- *ellē* – Indicates calling out those who were mentioned previously or being amazed by the situation.
- *selvam* … – She made his arrival as good as the insentient wealth. She took a few steps and made the one who arrived before to become insignificant when compared to her. She destroyed his nature. He gave up paramapadam, vyūham (kśīrābdi – milky ocean) etc and is resting here, only to help her \[but he has not done that so far\].
- *selvam malgi avan kidanda tirukkōḷūrkkē* – To tirukkōḷūr where he arrived to make it  abundantly opulent. Only when the leader engages in protecting those who are to be protected, his opulence will shine brightly.
- *avan kidanda* – Instead of she waiting for his arrival, he is waiting for her arrival – such is his nature.
- *mel idai nudanga* – Does she at least know about her own nature well even if she does not know about his nature? Her ignorance is common \[both in her own case and his case\]! Had she known about her own waist, would she even have started? Her mistake is due to her not knowing about her own middle portion (waist) \[also indicates, her lack of knowledge in nama: – that he is the means and we should not try to reach him on our own\].
- *mel idai nudanga* – To trouble her slender waist. If she sets out to walk with such waist, should he not have arrived right across her?
- *iḷa mān* – She is not matured enough to understand the dangers enroute and her own nature!
- *sella mēvinaḷē* – Set out to go there. The attaining of the result is neither in her hands nor in their \[mothers\] hands; it is in his hands; in her side, she only has firm faith. Previously the mother said “*pōnāḷ*” (she left) and here  she is saying “*pōkkilē oruppattāḷ*” (set out to leave); how does this match? The mother says “she has left” as soon as “she sets out to leave”.
- *iḷa mān sella mēvinaḷ – kollai enbarkolō, guṇam mikkanaḷ enbarkolō?* – She has made up her mind; what do we achieve by questioning? Only if she heard our good advice while she was here, she will bother about the blame while going there. When she goes, she would only hear the praises and will ignore the blames.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

adiyen saraty ramanuja dasan

## 6.7.5. Mevi naindu

*mēvi naindu naindu viḷaiyādaluṟāḷ en siṟut tēvi pōy init tan tirumāl tirukkōḷūril pūviyal poḻilum tadamum avan kōyilum kaṇḍu āvi uḷ kuḷira enganē ugakkungol inṟē?*

**Пословный перевод:**

mēvi – thinking (about his beauty, easy approacability etc) with mind; naindu naindu – weakening every moment; viḷaiyādal – in play; uṟāḷ – being not interested; en siṟut tēvi – my daughter who is adolescent yet having distinguished nature; pōy – leaving from here; than – one who is specially existing for her; tirumāl – śrīmān’s (one who has śrī mahālakśmi as his divine consort); tirukkōḷūr – in tirukkōḷūr; pū – flower; iyal – naturally having; poḻilum – gardens; tadamum – the ponds (which give freshness to the gardens); avan – his (along with lakshmi) residence; kōyilum – the temple which is the abode of enjoyment; ini – now; kaṇḍu – on seeing; āvi – the abode of prāṇa (life); uḷ – heart; kuḷira – to cool down; inṟu – today (which is a good dawn for me); enganē – how; ugakkum kol – enjoying?

**Перевод:**

**My daughter who is adolescent yet having distinguished nature, is thinking (about his beauty, easy approacability etc) with mind, weakening every moment and being not interested in play, is leaving from here towards the śrīmān who is specially existing for her and who is residing in tirukkōḷūr which is with gardens which are naturally having flowers, ponds and his residence, the temple which is the abode of enjoyment; now, on seeing it, cooling down her heart which is the abode of her life, how is she enjoying it today?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fifth pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki‘s mother says “How \[well\] will my daughter like the gardens, ponds and his temple which decorate tirukkōḷūr?”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. mēvi naindu naindu viḷaiyādaluṟāḷ en siṟut tēvi pōy init than tirumāl tirukkōḷūril pūviyal poḻilum tadamum avan kōyilum kaṇḍu āvi uḷ kuḷira enganē ugakkungol inṟē?*

- *mēvi* – Focussing on the qualities of bhagavān.
- *naindu naindu* – Like fire which destroys its own base, the qualities destroy her heart; as said in tiruvāimoḻi 9.6.2 “*ninaidoṟum sollum toṟum nenjidindugum*” (my thoughts, words and mind will tremble). She did not approach an entity which is nirguṇa (devoid of qualities); is she not engaged with one who is said in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.1.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/03/thiruvaimozhi-1-1-1-uyarvara-uyarnalam/) “*uyarvaṟa uyar nalam udaiyavan*” (the one who has great, auspicious qualities)?
- *mēvi* – Even while she was here, she did not engage with us.
- *naindu naindu* – She would not stop weakening; will not sustain herself.
- *viḷaiyādal urāḷ* – She gave up the activities which match her age. She had not just given up her playful activities, approached him and had become weakened; instead she fully immersed in him, and then gave up everything else. As said in [mūnṟām tiruvandādi 14](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/03/munram-thiruvandhadhi-14/) “*māṟpāl manam suḻippa mangaiyar tōḷ kaivittu*” (as one focusses on [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), he will give up sensual pleasures), as she focussed on bhagavān’s qualities, she gave up other pleasures. When there are good and bad aspects, one should naturally give up the bad aspects and pursue good aspects. As said in bhārhaspatya smruti “*paramātmani yōrakta: virakta: aparamātmani*” (one who is having great attachment towards paramātmā and great detachment towards all other aspects) and [iraṇḍām tiruvandādi 42](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/11/irandam-thiruvandhadhi-42/) “*manaippāl piṟandār pirāndu eydum pērinbam ellām* *tuṟandār toḻudārat tōḷ*” (Those who worship the divine shoulders of emperumān will detest the small \[worldly\] pleasures which are attained by those who are born in samsāram (materialistic realm)).
- *mēvi naindu naindu viḷaiyādal uṟāḷ* – She is not of the type where one becomes more detached after growing up. She is not of the type where one learns from śāstram “the sensual pleasures are to be given up” and gives them up and pursues bhagavān thinking “bhagavat viśayam is good” \[Here, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s special status of being fully blessed with divine knowledge and devotion by bhagavān himself is implied\].
- *en siṟut tēvi* – Here the mother is saying “younger goddess” since subsequently the “older goddess” is highlighted by “tirumāl” (divine consort of [śrī mahālakśmi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/)).
- *en siṟut tēvi* – Though she is not grown up, she is comparable to the divine consorts of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), who are the crowned queens. She does not consider her to be merely her own daughter. periya tirumoḻi 8.2.9 “*kaṇapuram kai toḻum piḷḷaiyaip piḷḷai enṟu eṇṇap peṟuvarē*” (a child who worships tirukkaṇṇapuram sourirājap perumāḷ, even if it is one’s own child, it should be revered instead of being treated like a small child). Here she is saying that she should purify her tongue which advised her.
- *ini pōy* – She has the mood of enjoying [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) in the \[adolescent \] stage when one desires to enjoy sensual pleasures. With such maturity did she go there seeking anything better?
- *ini* – If one gets the mood as said in cāndōjña upaniśat 8.12.3 “*nōpajanam smaran idam śarīram*” ([ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) will not contemplate about the material body after reaching the spiritual realm), is there anything more to enjoy after reaching there?
- *than tirumāl tirukkōḷūril* – Just as [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is too attached to [śrī mahālakśmi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/), he has the same attachment towards [parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) too. The relationship/conduct with one’s beloved \[wife\] is unlike his lord-servant relationship in the world. He cannot interact with those who are dear, as stated in nārāyaṇa sūktam “*patim viśvasya*” (The lord of the universe). In the town where her wealth, śriya;pati (divine lord of śrī mahālakśmi) is resting.
- *pūviyal poḻilum* – Instead of being with leaves, stem, creepers etc, the garden being filled with flowers only. Eternally blooming garden.
- *tadamum* – The pond which is spread all over the garden and is helping to nourish the garden.
- *avan kōyilum kaṇḍu* – Seeing the temple where he joyfully resides, for the full satisfaction of the eyes as said in periya tirumoḻi “*mā maṇik kōyilē vaṇangi*” (Worśipping the tanjaimāmaṇik kōyil, temple which is greatly decorated with gems). Just as his divine nature is revealed by his divine form, both his divine nature and form are revealed brightly in the temple. As soon as one sees the temple, one can vouch for the entity inside the temple. Just as a beautiful jewel box for the gold inside.
- *kaṇḍu* – Seeing to the full satisfaction of her who only experienced him internally and became anguished \[due to not seeing him\]. [nanjīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nanjiyar/) used to mercifully explain “I saw and enjoyed from behind, how  piḷḷai tirunaṟaiyūr araiyar and [bhattar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/parasara-bhattar/) were slowly going around the temple and were seeing the temple walls/structure etc as if eating them with their eyes”. When āccān and āṇḍān were going east \[to tirukkudandai\], they would neither cross over tiruppērnagar nor enter the town, but would just see the temple from outside and enjoy it.
- *āvi uḷ kuḷira* – When [parāśara bhattar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/parasara-bhattar/) was mercifully explaining this section briefly, [sīrāmap piḷḷai (vēda vyāsa bhattar)](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vedha-vyasa-bhattar/) who was present there said “jīyā (Oh learned)! Do you not remember how [embār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/embar/) used to mercifully explain this in detail?”. Just as a dry land becomes flooded with water all over the place.
- *enganē ugakkum kol* – The mother is saying – when she was not matured, she gave up everything else and became weakened meditating upon him – I saw that and enjoyed it; but when she physically sees him and enjoys him – I am not seeing that.
- *inṟē* – When I am grieving here today, she is having great enjoyment! How is the same day bringing different emotions to different persons! The reaction is based on the object \[she is enjoying due to attaining him, and I am suffering due to losing her\].

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.7.6. Inru enakku

*inṟu enakku udavādaganṟa iḷamān inip pōy ten tisait tiladam anaiya tirukkōḷūrkkē senṟu tan tirumāl tirukkaṇṇum sevvāyum kaṇḍu ninṟu ninṟu naiyum nedum kaṇgaḷ pani malgavē*

**Пословный перевод:**

enakku – to me (who is suffering in separation from her); inṟu – now; udavādu – without helping; aganṟa – left; iḷa mān – my little daughter; pōy – went with anguish; then tisai – for the southern direction; tiladam anaiya – decoration like a tilak (a beautiful symbol on the forehead); tirukkōḷūrkkē – in tirukkōḷūr; senṟu – entered; ini – now (after entering); than – one who eliminated her relationship with her relatives (by bestowing union with him which is dear to her); tirumāl – śrīmān’s (consort of śrī mahālakśmi); tiru – glancing lovingly; kaṇṇum – divine eyes; sem – shining radiantly due to the welcoming words; vāyum – lips; kaṇḍu – after seeing; nedu – wide; kaṇgaḷ – eyes; pani malga – filled with happy tears due to great bliss; ninṟu ninṟu – every moment; naiyum – weakens

**Перевод:**

**Without helping me, my little daughter left me with anguish now and entered tirukkōḷūr; now, after seeing the śrīmān who eliminated her relationship with her relatives, lovingly glancing with his divine eyes and the lips shining radiantly due to the welcoming words, she is becoming weak every moment with her wide eyes filled with happy tears due to great bliss.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the sixth pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki‘s mother says “After reaching tirukkōḷūr and seeing his friendly glance etc, my daughter, out of great joy, weakens more”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. She will feel happy only when her daughter enters tirukkōḷūr and sustains herself. In the previous pāsuram, she said “how will she enjoy” and in this pāsuram she is explaining how she enjoys. This is the struggle of the divine mother of parānguśa nāyaki – on the one hand she is meditating on the target (emperumān) of her daughter; on the other hand, she is meditating upon the state of her daughter! inṟu enakku udavādaganṟa iḷamān inip pōy then tisait tiladam anaiya tirukkōḷūrkkē senṟu than tirumāl tirukkaṇṇum sevvāyum kaṇḍu ninṟu ninṟu naiyum nedum kaṇgaḷ pani malgavē*

- *inṟu enakku udavādu aganṟa* – One gives birth to a child and nurtures the child, so that the child helps when in danger \[need\]. Is there any greater danger than being lonely in separation from her daughter and the current situation? She is not helping me now! śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 59.26 “*atō nu kim du:khataram sōham ikśvāku nandanam \| imām avastām āpanna nēha paśyāmi rāghavam \|\|*” (Having attained this state, I am not seeing śrī rāma, the scion of ikśvāku dynasty; what is more sorrowful than this?) – “Did I not perform penance for long time and beget you as my son, to have you at this juncture of suffering in separation? Alas! I have lost you today!” said daśarata.
- *enakku udavādu* – This is the difference between \[daśarata\] cakravarti and self \[mother\]; as said in nācciyār tirumoḻi 9.9 “Remaining helpless”; did I treat you like other mothers would do? I always considered your happiness as mine. And she is the mediator for her daughter’s dear lord. [tiruvāimoḻi 6.7.6](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/02/thiruvaimozhi-6-5-5-kuzhaiyum-val/) “*pirān irundamai kāttinīr*” (you showed the lord), periya tirumoḻi 3.7.7 “*annaiyum attanum enṟu adiyōmukku irangiṟṟilaḷ*” (She did not show mercy upon us (parents) who considered ourselves as her servitor). Should one who plans to leave, cause us blame while leaving? Should she consider us servitors as her controller? Why did she leave us who would have accompanied her!
- *aganṟu* – Why did she leave us in this manner! At least she could have remained in the same town as we!
- *iḷa mān* – She is in the adolescent stage where she did not realise “I have left my own mother”! What can we do if it is her age doing it!
- *inip pōy* – There is none closer/greater than mother among the relatives! While she has great attachment towards [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) even to discard her own mother, what more is she seeking there? After giving up the unnatural aspects, should we need to separately pursue that which is natural?
- *then tisai* … – The southern direction which is known as “mleccā bhūmi”, is looked down upon by the āryas (the wise); though it is said like that, just as one nice ornament will make other ornaments to shine, due to the presence of tirukkōḷūr, the whole southern direction became laudable. śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 11.82 “*dakśiṇa dik krutā yēna śaraṇyā puṇya karmaṇā*” (The southern direction was made to be the refuge for everyone by agastya who has glorious history).
- *tirukkōḷūrkkē senṟu* – It appears great for the divine mother.  For her daughter, the journey, entry into the town and seeing him – all of these are desirable. Just as the journey through arcirādi gati (the path which leads to paramapadam), the paramapadam itself and [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is constantly seen/enjoyed after entering in there are desirable and part of the goal \[for an ātmā\].
- *than tirumāl* – As said in mahābhāratam “*sarvēśāmēva lōkānām pitā mātā ca mādava:*” (śrīman nārāyaṇan is the father and mother for all the creatures in the world) – whatever relations she gave up here, he becomes all of them. He being the goal is in the form of the divine lord of śrī mahālakśmi. She cannot focus on anything other than [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s form with his divine consort.
- *tirukkaṇṇum sevvāyum kaṇḍu* – To beg for pardon for making her come before he could have gone there, he glances gently, and the lips which tremble to say some kind words. This is how [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s “*kōvai vāy tudippa maḻaik kaṇgaḷ*” ([tiruvāimoḻi 6.7.3](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/03/thiruvaimozhi-6-7-3-puvai-paingiligal/) – trembling reddish lips and eyes with rain like tears) is.
- *ninṟu ninṟu naiyum* – Will break into pieces as days go by. When she sees him, she can no longer remember the separation; she becomes immersed in the emotions of emperumān. She remains as said in tirukkuraḷ 1286 “*kāṇungāl kāṇēn tavaṟāna kāṇākkāl kāṇēn tavaṟallavai*” (When I see my beloved, I do not see any faults, but when I do not see him, I do not see anything but his faults).
- *nedum kaṇgaḷ pani malgavē* – My whole eyes become filled with tears.
- *ninṟu ninṟu naiyum* – Weakened continuously. Like the shore which will give in when there is a flood.
- *nedum kaṇgaḷ pani malgavē* – Just as the heart becomes weakened, the eyes become teary. When she goes to see him, the tears in his eyes become a hurdle for her. There is no difference between happy tears or sad tears; whatever stops, that becomes enemy; I got to enjoy the entity which is said in bruhadāraṇyaka upaniśat 6-5-6 “*draśtavya:*” (one who is to be seen).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.7.7. Malgu nir

*malgu nīrk kaṇṇōdu maiyaluṟṟa manattanaḷāy allum nan pagalum nedumāl enṟaḻaittu inippōy selvam malgi avan kidanda tirukkōḷūrkkē olgi olgi nadandu enganē pugungol osindē?*

**Пословный перевод:**

malgu – overflowing (due to separation); nīr – having tears; kaṇṇodu – with the eyes; maiyal – confusion; uṟṟa – attained; manattanaḷ āy – one who is having the heart; nan – having goodness (to speak about him); allum – night; pagalum – day; nedumāl – Oh one who has great love!; enṟu – saying that; aḻaittu – calling out; ini – further to such longing; olgi – contracting; olgi – swaying; nadandu – walking; osindu – weakening; pōy – left; selvam malgi – having abundance of wealth; avan – he; kidanda – resting; tirukkōḷūrkkē – to tirukkōḷūr only; enganē – how; pugum kol – will she reach there?

**Перевод:**

**My daughter who is having eyes with overflowing tears, confused heart, is calling out “Oh one who has great love!” during night and day which are having goodness; further to such longing, she is contracting, swaying, walking and weakening, and left for tirukkōḷūr where he is resting and is having abundance of wealth; how will she reach there?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the seventh pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki‘s mother thinking about her daughter’s tender nature and her weakened state due to the separation from emperumān, says “we need to think about what she will go through on entering there, only if she can reach there”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. malgu nīrk kaṇṇōdu maiyaluṟṟa manattanaḷāy allum nan pagalum nedumāl enṟaḻaittu inippōy selvam malgi avan kidanda tirukkōḷūrkkē olgi olgi nadandu enganē pugungol osindē?*

- *malgu nīrk kaṇṇodu maiyal uṟṟa manattanaḷāy* – While both the senses which, as said in periya tiruvandādi 23 “*enṟēnum katkaṇṇāṟkāṇāda avvuruvai nejennum ut kaṇṇēṟkāṇum*” (The form which cannot be seen by the external eyes, can be seen by the heart which is the internal eye), are unstable, how will she reach there? Eyes became abundantly teary; heart became confused. If both the internal vision and external vision become covered in darkness, how will she go there? Due to the tears in the eyes, she cannot see with her eyes; due to being blinded by love, she cannot see with her heart.
- *malgu nīrk kaṇṇodu maiyal uṟṟa manattanaḷāy* – The tears identify the eyes and the confusion identifies the heart.
- *maiyal uṟṟa manattanaḷāy nedumāl enṟu aḻaittu* – She called out even without the help of the heart.
- *allum nan pagalum* – Since this is the time when she calls out for bhagavān, being engaged in his matters, she calls it good night and good day. While the worldly people are engaged in lowly sensual pleasures and call out for such pleasures, this is the time when she calls out saying “*ellām kaṇṇan*” (everything is kriṣṇa).
- *nedumāl enṟu aḻaittu* – Calling him out highlighting his great love towards her.
- *inip pōy* – After calling him out highlighting his great love towards her, now she is going there to highlight her great love towards him. At this stage of being with eyes which don’t see and heart which is captivated \[by him\], is she going to enjoy anything else going there?
- *selvam malgi avan kidanda tirukkōḷūrkkē* – It is due to his arrogance of being very wealthy, he did not come half way across, glance at her and embrace her! If he did not have such arrogance, would he not have come all the way towards her? She is saying that he could have enjoyed her even during the journey but lost the opportunity due to his arrogance.
- *selvam malgi avan kidanda* – As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 3.24 “*samayā bōdita: śrīmān …*” (śrī rāma, who was blissfully sleeping, was awakened by me), where he is very beautifully resting.
- *avan kidanda* – She went to see his beautiful resting posture which is said in the same ślōkam “*sukasupta:*” (blissfully sleeping); it is said in [tirumālai 23](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/10/thirumalai-23/) “*kidandadōr kidakkai*” (beautiful resting posture).
- *avan kidanda* – How amazing! Instead of her waiting for his arrival, he is awaiting her arrival!
- *olgi olgi nadandu* – It appears that she has to walk ten steps to cross distance of one sep.
- *osindu* – becoming weakened.
- *olgi olgi nadandu – osindu – enganē pugum kol* – Walking with great difficulty, becoming weakened even being unable to walk in that manner, how will she reach there?
- *nadandu enganē pugum kol* – The mother is thinking that even if her daughter walks, she will not reach. \[Why?\] She is thinking that since her daughter walks like a swan as said in periya tirumoḻi 11.2.5 “*annamennadaip pūnguḻali*” (one who gracefully walks like a swan and has beautiful hair), she will not reach there.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.7.8. Osinda nunnidai

*osinda nuṇṇidai mēl kaiyai vaittu nondu nondu kasinda nenjinaḷāyk kaṇṇa nīr tuḻumbac collungol! osinda oṇ malarāḷ koḻunan tirukkōḷūrkkē kasinda nenjinaḷāy emmai nītta em kārigaiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

osinda – being weakened (like a flower which withered due to being sucked out of its honey); oṇ – being distinguished; malarāḷ – of the one who resides in lotus flower; koḻunan – lord (who is greatly desirable); tirukkōḷūrkkē – to tirukkōḷūr; kasinda nenjinaḷāy – having dampened heart; emmai – me; nītta – who left; em kārigai – my beautiful daughter; osinda – previously weakened; nuṇ – slender; idai mēl – on the waist; kaiyai – hand; vaittu – placed; nondu nondu – feeling grief more and more; kasinda nenjinaḷāy – having such dampness \[indicating melted heart\] as companion; kaṇṇa nīr – tears; tuḷumba – to overflow; sellum kol – will she go there?

**Перевод:**

**Will my beautiful daughter who has a dampened heart and who left me for tirukkōḷūr which is the abode of the lord of the distinguished and weakened one \[śrī mahālakśmi\] who resides in lotus flower, placing her hand \[to support\] the previously weakened slender waist, feeling grief more and more, having such dampness \[indicating melted heart\] as companion and with overflowing tears, go there?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the eighth pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki‘s mother says “Will my daughter who discarded me and left from here due to her attachment towards tirukkōḷūr, not reach there having such attachment as her companion?”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, parānguśa nāyaki‘s mother says “Will my daughter who discarded me and left from here due to her attachment towards tirukkōḷūr which is the abode of the one who is dear to the greatly enjoyable lakshmi, not reach there having such attachment as her companion?”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. osinda nuṇṇidai mēl kaiyai vaittu nondu nondu kasinda nenjinaḷāyk kaṇṇa nīr tuḻumbac collungol! osinda oṇ malarāḷ koḻunan tirukkōḷūrkkē kasinda nenjinaḷāy emmai nītta em kārigaiyē*

- *osinda* … – Her waist is so slender that even if she does not walk, one should worry for it!
- *nuṇ idai mēl kaiyai vaittu* – She does not realise that there is nothing \[waist, hurdle\] in the middle. Her waist cannot even bear the weight of her own hand; her waist is so slender and one should worry for it even if she goes along with him as said in periya tirumoḻi 3.7.7 “*minnaiyum vanjiyaiyum venṟilangum idaiyāḷ*” (the waist which is thinner than a creeper and lightning). osindu – withered, slender, straight waist. To put it simply – it is so thin that we can say there is no waist. That is, to fear for it thinking “oh, its breaking, fully broken now” \[Generally, waist indicates attachment to worldly matters, slender waist means totally detached\].
- *osinda nuṇṇidai mēl kaiyai vaittu* – Is there anyone who does not know what is coming! The waist can only bear the hand of her lord and not her own. It is said in tiruviruttam 37 “*todungāl osiyum idai*” (the waist which will wither as soon as touched). From the beginning \[tiruviruttam 1st pāsuram\], her waist \[body\] is bothering her.
- *kaiyai vaittu* – as if placing a mountain on her waist.
- *nondu nondu* – She would neither take her hands off nor will stop feeling the grief. One can survive enemies who are born with self, but cannot survive the trouble from outsiders \[explained next\]!
- *nondu nondu* – Feeling very grieved; from the beginning, she is bearing the weight of her bosom \[bosom indicates bhakti generally\] which are suffering in separation, but now does she have to even bear the weight of hands?
- *kasinda nenjinaḷāy* – While the waist is weakened, is the heart well nourished? No, her heart is also very grieved.
- *kaṇṇa nīr tuḷumba* – That (heart) is the source for the \[tears in the\] eyes.
- *sellum kol* – Now, there is no scope of returning for her. Can she overcome the troubles on her way?
- *osinda …* – If the one \[[śrī mahālakśmi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/)\] who is united with [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) herself is withered, what can we say about the one who is in separation! The one who is residing in the distinguished lotus flower, is withered \[due to the union with emperumān\] as a flower which was sucked out of its honey by a beetle. To the abode of the beloved consort of such śrī mahālakśmi.
- *kasinda nenjinaḷāy* – Having a heart which is friendly towards her. She will only pursue that town and will even give up her own mother.
- *oṇmalarāḷ koḻunan tirukkōḷūrkkē kasinda nenjinaḷāy* – Is she the one who is caught in her romance, going to return? Being the beloved lord of [śrī mahālakśmi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/) who resides in the flower, is his greatness. The benefactor who has the fame of being the independent lord of śrī mahālakśmi as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.6.9](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/08/thiruvaimozhi-1-6-9-tharuma-arum/) “*tirumagaḷār tanik kēḷvan*“.
- *emmai nītta em kārigaiyē* – As she kept losing her mamākaram here \[possessiveness towards her mother\], that itself became the reason for her mother’s growing attachment towards her. This explains the ultimate stage of being immersed in bhagavat viśayam, giving up other attachments and how such persons are most desirable. All she needs is the knowledge about the one who made her leave everything else! All her mother needs is her relationship!
- *kasinda nenjinaḷāy emmai nītta em kārigai – osinda oṇmalarāḷ koḻunan tirukkōḷūrkkē – kasinda nenjinaḷāyk kaṇṇa nīr tuḷumbac cellum kol* – Would the great desire which made her leave me, not let her enter into the town too? The mother knows firmly that “she has left”; but she is doubting about her reaching there; would the desire/love not accomplish both? It may induce pāravaśyam (totally helpless state) and leave her in between; or it may bring her to tirukkōḷūr.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.7.9. Kariyam nallanagal

*kāriyam nallanagaḷ avai kāṇil en kaṇṇanukkenṟu īriyāy iruppāḷ idellām kidakka inip pōy sēri pal paḻi tūuy iraippat tirukkōḷūrkkē nēriḻai nadandāḷ emmai onṟum ninaittilaḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

nallanagaḷ – good; kāriyam – that which is known \[having form, name\]; avai – objects; kāṇil – when seen; en – one who is obedient to me; kaṇṇanukku – for kriṣṇa; enṟu – saying that; īriyāy – kind-hearted; iruppāḷ – one who is; nēr – thin; iḻai – she who is wearing ornaments; idu – this material realm which is created for that; ellām – all; kidakka – while they exist; ini – now; pōy – leaving me; sēri – the residents of the town; pal – in many ways; paḻi – accusations; tūuy – saying; iraippa – shouting loudly; tirukkōḷūrkkē – certainly to tirukkōḷūr; nadandāḷ – walked; emmai – me; onṟum – in any manner; ninaittilaḷ – did not think about

**Перевод:**

**My kind-hearted daughter, who is wearing thin ornaments, when seeing good objects which are known,thinks that they exist for kriṣṇa; while all this material realm which is created for that is existing, she is now leaving me; the residents of the town are shouting loudly and accusing her, and she certainly walked to tirukkōḷūr; she did not think about me in any manner. Implies that she neither thought her mother as a co-resident nor as one who lived with her as her mother.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the ninth pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki‘s mother says “My daughter who is greatly attached to emperumān, is considering the accusations thrown at her by the residents of the town as her companion and is going to tirukkōḷūr”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, parānguśa nāyaki‘s mother says “My daughter who considers anything good she sees to be existing for kriṣṇa, who is easily accessible to her, is ignoring the accusations of the residents of the town, and is going to tirukkōḷūr”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. kāriyam nallanagaḷ avai kāṇil en kaṇṇanukkenṟu īriyāy iruppāḷ idellām kidakka inip pōy sēri pal paḻi tūuy iraippat tirukkōḷūrkkē nēriḻai nadandāḷ emmai onṟum ninaittilaḷē*

- *kāriyam nallanagaḷ avai kāṇil* – She does not see anything to start with; but if she sees something good in objects, she will say that this is for kriṣṇa who presented himself to me, and become melted and will remain like that. She says similar to whatever śrī rāma said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 36.45 “*druśtvā palam vā puśpam vā*” (Whenever he sees fruits and flowers, he calls out for you – said hanuman to sītā). She is seeking out something greater than just thinking that everything good she sees is for kriṣṇa! His simplicity is the manner he descended to tirukkōḷūr for her and remained there.
- *idellām kidakka* – \[First explanation – giving up all these play tools\] As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 16.19 “*sarvān bhōgān parityaya*” (giving up all enjoyments). \[Second explanation – giving up all the bhagavat anubhavam here\] As said in [tiruvaimoḻi 6.7.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/03/thiruvaimozhi-6-7-1-unnum-soru/) “*uṇṇum sōṟu parugu nīr tinnum veṟṟiai ellām kaṇṇan*“, [tiruvāimoḻi 6.7.2](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/03/thiruvaimozhi-6-7-2-urum-nadum/) “*ūrum nādum ulagamum tannaip pōl avanudaiya pērum tārgaḷumē pidaṟṟak kaṟpuvān idaṟi*“, [tiruvāimoḻi 6.7.3](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/03/thiruvaimozhi-6-7-3-puvai-paingiligal/) “*pūvai paingiḷigaḷ pandu tūdai pūmputtilgaḷ yāvaiyum tirumāl tirunāmangaḷē kūviyeḻum*“. Giving up these unlimited wealth \[kainkaryaśrī\] here which exist for kriṣṇa only.
- *inip pōy* – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) will feel indebted to one who simply becomes fully faithful to him. For such emperumān, she went to offer something and has her worries eliminated. He remains as said in yajur vēdam “*tē bhūyiśtām*” (We are reciting “nama:” which is too much to handle for you). ḍoesn’t it befit her to remain here if we look at his nature?
- *sēri pal paḻi tūuyiraippa* – As she got companion \[accusations of the townspeople\], she left there. Not just one or two! Also, each one says different accusations.
- *pal paḻi tūuyiraippa* – First she made herself exist for him; that was not sufficient; she left for going there; she did not consider her mother; she did not consider the accusations of the townspeople; [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) should have come to her seeing any of these – but he has not done anything. As said in tirukkuṟaḷ 1141 “*alareḻil āruyir niṟkum*” (the accusations of townspeople will sustain her life).
- *nēriḻai nadandāḷ* – Her mother is also desiring to follow her daughter’s beautiful ornaments.
- *nadandāḷ* – Though she is talking about her own daughter, once she took a few steps towards tirukkōḷūr, her acts should be expressed only in a polite language \[she could have said “*pōnāḷ*“, but is using more respectful term\]. How respectfully she is treating her own daughter! Though own children or disciples, those who are immersed in bhagavat viśayam should be treated respectfully. Once [nanjīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nanjiyar/) greatly praised his disciple [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/) in an assembly and said “don’t think that I am praising my own disciple”! He mercifully continued to say – even previously there were those who said as in periya tirumoḻi 8.2.9 “*kaṇapuram kai toḻum piḷḷaiyaip piḷḷai enṟu eṇṇap peṟuvarē*” (a child who worships tirukkaṇṇapuram sourirājap perumāḷ, even if it is one’s own child, it should be revered instead of being treated like a small child). ammuṇi āḻvān \[an ācārya\] would often offer obeisances to his disciple; when asked “what are you doing?”, he replied “we need to analyse the actions of other śrīvaiṣṇavas to know about them! but I praise my śiśyas having known their vaiṣṇava qualities very well”.
- *emmai onṟum ninaittilaḷē* – Even if she did not take me along as a companion, should she not have at the least thought about me?
- *onṟum ninaittilaḷē* – Should she not consider me as one amongst those who receive her there, or those who accompany her? The mother remains “Her thoughts about me are what I need”. The care of those who are close to [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is that which is desirable/necessary.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.7.10. Ninaikkilen deyvangal!

*ninaikkilkēn deyvangāḷ! nedungaṇ iḷa mān inip pōy anaittulagum udaiya aravindalōcananai tinaittanaiyum vidāḷ avan sēr tirukkōḷūrkkē manaikkuvān paḻiyum ninaiyāḷ sella vaittanaḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

deyvangāḷ – Oh Gods!; ninaikkilēn – I cannot comprehend (her out of bound activities); nedu – huge (to behold all his greatness in it); kaṇ – having eyes; iḷam – young; mān – she who appears like a deer; ini – now (though she is having beautiful eyes herself); pōy – go; anaittulagum – for all worlds; udaiya – to be the apt lord; aravindalōcananai – aravindalōcanan; tinaittanaiyum – even for a moment; vidāḷ – not leaving; avan – his; sēr – residence; tirukkōḷūrkkē – to tirukkōḷūr only; sella vaittanaḷ – left at once; manaikku – for the family; vān – big; paḻi – blame; ninaiyāḷ – did not consider

**Перевод:**

**Oh Gods! I cannot comprehend the activities of my young deer like daughter who is having huge eyes who left at once and is now going to tirukkōḷūr, which is the residence of aravindalōcanan, the apt lord for all worlds and is not going to leave him even for a moment; she did not consider the great blame which befell upon the family.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the tenth pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki‘s mother says “Not considering the blame which will befall the family. she is determined to go to tirukkōḷūr and never leave him”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. ninaikkilkēn deyvangāḷ! nedungaṇ iḷa mān inip pōy anaittulagum udaiya aravindalōcananai tinaittanaiyum vidāḷ avan sēr tirukkōḷūrkkē manaikkuvān paḻiyum ninaiyāḷ sella vaittanaḷē*

- *ninaikkilēn* – It is impossible to see the shore of an ocean. There are so many aspects – the way she left leaving the mother behind, the trouble enroute, and the torment she will go through after entering tirukkōḷūr.
- *deyvangāḷ* – This cannot be told to those who are blaming her \[mother\] by saying as in in [tiruvāimoḻi 6.7.4](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/03/thiruvaimozhi-6-7-4-kollai-enbarkolo/) “*kollai*“. \[Why would she call out for dēvatās, though she is totally dependent on [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)\] dēvatās have the following similarities with her – they are also not blaming and they are also not sleeping \[as they are known as animiśa (those who don’t close their eyes)\] like those who become friends while staying in prison, she is calling out for them.
- *deyvangāḷ – ninaikkilēn* – This is said in a helpless state.
- *nedum kaṇ iḷa mān inip pōy* – She left, not knowing what is coming in the future! Those who are seen by her eyes, will come to her with all their greatness as all the serpents fell in to the sarpa yāgam (fire sacrifice performed by janamējayan to kill all the serpents in revenge for his father’s killing by a serpent\].
- *inip pōy* – Who is doing whose job! How can she be having beautiful eyes and yet go to tirukkōḷūr \[seeking beautiful eyed [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)\]! Her true nature is sufficient for her to not go there \[by nature, one should be fully dependent for emperumān to come\].
- *anaittulagum udaiya aravindalōcananai* – His eyes have just won over ubhaya vibhūti (his two realms – spiritual realm and material realm). But her eyes are capable of winning over himself. He is aravindalōcanan who owns all worlds! She is the who is having huge eyes \[which own him\]. He along with his two realms can reside in a corner of her expansive eyes. The remaining portion of her eyes and her age have no specific use.
- *tinaittanaiyum vidāḷ* – She cannot even bear a little bit relaxation during an embrace. Due to the sufferings she went through here, she cannot even bear him say “I won’t separate from you” \[i.e., she cannot even hear the word “separation” from him, not even to say “I won’t separate”\]. Even if he needs to go away for specific tasks, he needs to explain clearly that it is done for good reasons.
- *manaikku vān paḻiyum ninaiyāḷ* – She \[[parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)\] is not considering even the greatest blame for the family. Not only is she disregarding the apt means \[of waiting for him\], but is considering that to be a hurdle. The mother considers “going towards him on her own” is a blame! mahābhārata ślōkam where dharma dēvatā instructs yudiśtra is explained here. *ata pātaka bhīta: tvam sarva bhāvēna bhārata* – in this manner, dharma dēvatā is instructing yudiśtra who performed many rāja sūya yajñams, yet had to visit naraka (hell) for telling a lie once. Here it implies that both sat karma (righteous act) and asat karma (unrighteous act) are hurdles, and kriṣṇa only is the true refuge. *vimuktānya samārambha*: – don’t fall apart by just holding on to rituals which are insentient. *nārāyaṇa parōbhava* – Try to hold on to [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is befitting your true nature.
- *sella vaittanaḷē* – Two explanations – a) she placed her heart in going there, b) she went there to be seen by all of us. That is – a) she set out to go there; b) as she reached there, not to return, she made us also reach there.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.
