## 6.7.11. Vaitta ma nidiyam

*vaitta mā nidiyām madusūdanaiyē alaṟṟi kottalar poḻil sūḻ kurugūrc catakōpan sonna pattu nūṟṟuḷ ippattu avan sēr tirukkōḷūrkkē cittam vaitturaippār tigaḻ ponnulagāḷvārē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vaitta – preserved; mā nidiyām – like great wealth; madusūdanai – one who eliminates the hurdles of enjoyment; alaṟṟi – blabbering due to sorrow (of not attaining); kottu – flower bunch; alar – blossoming; poḻil – by garden; sūḻ – surrounded; kurugūr – leader of āḻvārtirunagari; satakōpan – nammāḻvār; sonna – mercifully spoken; pattu – (revealing different meanings) ten; nūṟṟuḷ – centums; ippattu – this decad which highlights the great urge to attain the goal; avan – he; sēr – residing; tirukkōḷūrkkē – to tirukkōḷūr; cittam – heart; vaittu – placing; uraippār – those who can recite; tigaḻ – having the radiance of bhagavat anubhavam; pon – laudable; ulagu – paramapadam (spiritual realm); āḷvār – will rule over to their full desire

**Перевод:**

**nammāḻvār, the leader of āḻvārtirunagari which is surrounded by garden having blossoming bunches of flower, out of sorrow, blabbered about emperumān who eliminates the hurdles of enjoyment and is the great wealth which is preserved; he mercifully spoke in this decad which highlights the great urge to attain the goal, amongst the ten centums, about emperumān who is residing in tirukkōḷūr; those who can recite this decad placing their heart into it, will rule over to their full desire, the laudable paramapadam which is having the radiance of bhagavat anubhavam.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the end, āḻvār says “tirunādu (spiritual realm) will be at the disposal of those who are experts in this decad”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. vaitta mā nidiyām madusūdanaiyē alaṟṟi kottalar poḻil sūḻ kurugūrc catakōpan sonna pattu nūṟṟuḷ ippattu avan sēr tirukkōḷūrkkē cittam vaitturaippār tigaḻ ponnulagāḷvārē*

- *vaitta mā nidiyām* – This is the reason for her lone journey and leaving the mother behind. While the accumulated wealth is already present, who would let it perish and not enjoy it!
- *vaitta mā nidi* – Here [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is said as nidi (wealth) due to the following reasons – being the preserved wealth as said in periya tirumoḻi 7.10.4 “*eyppinil vaippinaik kāsinai maṇiyai*” (the wealth when one is helpless, the gold and gems), that which makes one hold onto their life when heard about its presence \[just as one would get their life back when one accepts the existence of [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)\], that which makes everyone fall at the feet of the owner \[even the dēvatās will fall at the feet of bhāgavatas who have bhagavat bhakti\], that which lets one live off it \[when an ācārya teaches about bhagavān to a śiśya, the śiśya would give offerings\], where no one would blame the owner for living off the wealth \[no one would blame for accepting such offerings\] and would bring great honour \[such ācāryas who have great knowledge about bhagavān are praised greatly\], such possessor need not worry about anything \[one who has bhagavān in his heart, need not worry about anything\], one can get anything with that \[one can get anything with bhagavān’s presence\], and one can enjoy all types of enjoyment with its presence. mānidi means highly valued wealth. That is, even after getting everything with it, it remains the same – imperishable. The worldly wealth will perish over time.
- *madusūdanaiyē alaṟṟi* – madusūdana implies he protects himself. The goal itself can eliminate the hurdles and let us enjoy it.
- *kottalar poḻil* – As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 127.5 “*sarvanca kuśalam gruhē*” (everyone is well at home). Just as śrī bharatāḻvān was having his heart getting closer to perumāḷ (śrī rāma), the whole of śrī ayōdyā became green with blossomed flowers realising that he is arriving soon, [āḻvārtirunagari](http://azhwarthirunagari.koyil.org/) too became green with blossomed flowers due to [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s mind acquiring clarity due to his being fully focussed on [emperumān,](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) not having the time to think about the separation anymore. When there is so much urge in here \[[āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/), [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)\], would there be any shortcoming in facilitating the goal there \[[bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)\]? It changed from the state as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 59.5 “*apivrukśā:*” (the trees withered) to the state as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 127.19 “*akāla palinō vrukśā:*” (the trees blossomed in non-season).
- *pattu nūṟṟuḷ ippattu* – Like nectar in the ocean, this decad among the thousand pāsurams.
- *avan sēr …* – Placing their heart on tirukkōḷūr where he firmly resides.
- *uraippār* – those who recite.
- *tigaḻ pon ulagu āḷvārē* – Instead of having one person (mother) calling out and another person (daughter) going alone, they would enter the abode where they can eternally enjoy. Instead of having to travel alone, they would travel towards the distinguished abode, being witnessed by the residents of arcirādi gati (the multi layered path which leads to paramapadam).

## 6.8 Ponnulagaliro

## 6.8.1. Ponnulagaliro

*ponnulagāḷīrō? bhuvani muḻudāḷīrō? nannalap puḷḷinangāḷ vinaiyāttiyēn nān irandēn mun ulagangaḷ ellām padaitta mugil vaṇṇan kaṇṇan en nalangoṇḍa pirān tanakku en nilaimai uraittē*

**Пословный перевод:**

nal nalam – having distinguished friendship etc towards those who pray \[to you\]; puḷ inangāḷ – Oh flocks of birds (who have wings which help in your acts)!; vinaiyāttiyēn – who am having sins to be separated from him and sending message to him; nān – I; irandēn – praying to you as his devotees pray to him; mun – in the beginning; ulagangaḷ – world; ellām – all; padaitta – created; mugil – like black cloud; vaṇṇan – one who is having divine form; kaṇṇan – being easily approachable for his devotees \[as kriṣṇa\]; en – my; nalam – all distinguished features; koṇḍa – took ownership; pirān tanakku – to the benefactor; en – my; nilaimai – state; uraittu – informing; pon – eternally desirable; ulagu – paramapadam; āḷīrō? – would you rule?; bhuvani – highlighted by the earth; muḻudu – entire material realm; āḷīrō – rule

**Перевод:**

**Oh flocks of birds (who have wings which help in your acts) having distinguished friendship etc towards those who pray \[to you\]! I who am having sins to be separated from him and sending message to him, am  praying to you as his devotees pray to him; inform my state to the benefactor who created all worlds in the beginning, who is having divine black cloud like form, who is easily approachable for his devotees and who took ownership of my distinguished features; \[after both of us become united after you inform him\] would you rule the eternally desirable paramapadam and the material realm which is highlighted by the earth? Implies that both the realms are at your disposal. By saying inangāḷ (flocks), she feels confident that with so many of birds, the task in hand will be easily accomplished.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the first pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki prays to some birds saying “inform him about my state and \[in turn\] I will bestow you paramapadam (spiritual realm) and samsāram (material realm) for you to rule over”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. ponnulagāḷīrō? bhuvani muḻudāḷīrō? nannalap puḷḷinangāḷ vinaiyāttiyēn nān irandēn mun ulagangaḷ ellām padaitta mugil vaṇṇan kaṇṇan en nalangoṇḍa pirān tanakku en nilaimai uraittē*

- *pon ulagu āḷīrō* – [parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is thinking that īśvara’s wealth (spiritual and material realms) are there to be gifted to those who united her with him, when she was suffering in separation. Both the realms are at the disposal of the \[divine\] couple. One can say this when  she reaches that state \[being the consort of the lord\]. She is thinking that while sarvēśvaran is present, this is being a ruler-less kingdom \[so, she is asking the birds to rule over\]. Whatever one will acquire after being freed from material bondage and reaching paramapadam, she is offering that right here. This is the nature of the one \[[āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)\] who bestows paramapadam while being in bondage and the one \[[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)\] who bestows paramapadam after freeing one \[[ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)\] from bondage. When two persons \[emperumān and parānguśa nāyaki\] are separated from each other and suffering, it is natural for both to give \[but the approach is different, as explained here\]. The nature of those who help in uniting is – some give up their body in trying to unite \[like periya udaiyār, jatāyu\] and some others who unite being with their bodies \[like these birds\].
- *pon ulagu āḷīrō bhuvani muḻudu āḷīrō* – Should your kingdoms also suffer as I am suffering now \[i.e., being without the lord\]? [parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) who is separated from her beloved consort, and is seeking out a messenger, is offering both realms to the messenger! This is based on her dependence on him. She is not with some lowly person who would make himself and his belongings hers while being united and take them away when separated. He made himself and his belongings exist fully for her so that she can give them to anyone she desires, even in his absence. When [aruḷāḷap perumāḷ emperumānār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/arulala-perumal-emperumanar/) \[a disciple of [bhagavat rāmānujar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/emperumanar/)\] was ill, [āḻvān \[kūrattāḻvān\]](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/kuraththazhwan/) went to see him along with [piḷḷai uṟangā villi dāsar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/pillai-uranga-villi-dhasar/) \[another disciple of bhagavat rāmānujar\]. aruḷāḷap perumāḷ emperumānār said “The heartache caused by āḻvān \[in not praying to [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) to make him bestow me mōkśam, though he is capable of doing so\] will be cured only when I attain the divine feet of [āḷavandār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/alavandhar/) \[who is in paramapadam already\]”.
- *pon ulagu āḷīrō bhuvani muḻudu āḷīrō* – She thinks that just as śrī rāma broke the bow and kriṣṇa killed the bulls to attain sītā and nappinnai respectively, here the birds will get to rule both realms of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) for uniting her with emperumān.
- *āḷīrō* – She is in total possession that some one \[i.e., [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)\] need not make her the owner newly. perumāḷ (śrī rama) himself said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 18.34 “*dattam asya abhayam mayā*” (he was given protection by me); similarly, [parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) too bestows both the realms just as the birds turn favourable to become messengers. As they are really fulfilling [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s benefit, she need not inform him before giving the gift to them. She too is working for his benefit. As they go as messengers, she will survive; as she survives, emperumān too, who is her owner, will survive. Now, she is giving them her own private wealth \[which she acquired due to being with emperumān\].
- *āḷīrō* – You should not just be engaging in your own activities; you should also work for my benefit. Ruling the realms means taking care of her activities. When asked “If she gives both the realms to them, when he arrives, where would both of them live?”, anantāḻvān said “They will live in a place which is given by the bird”.
- *pon ulagu āḷīrō – bhuvani muḻudu āḷīrō* – \[Reasons for giving paramapadam first\] One would give that which is at closer reach first and then the others next. She is giving in the order which she received them from [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/). emperumān bestowed [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) nitya vibhūti (paramapadam) first and then leelā vibhūti (samsāram). First āḻvār sang \[based on emperumān’s revelation\] his having paramapadam in tiruvāimoḻi 1.1.1 “*ayarvaṟum amarargaḷ adipati*” (lord of tireless nityasūris) and then only his having leelā vibhūti in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.1.3](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/03/thiruvaimozhi-1-1-3-ilanathu-udaiyanithu/) “*ilanadu udaiyanidu*” ([emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) cannot be limited to saying that he is far from an object or close to an object). Even while being here, when one acquires knowledge, paramapadam appears closer; [periyāḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/periyazhwar/) too said in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 5.3.7 “*akkarai ennum anattak kadaluḷ aḻundi un pēraruḷāl ikkarai ēṟi iḷaittu irundēn*” (While I was previously suffering in the disastrous ocean, with your great mercy, I have now reached this shore and am remaining peaceful) – he highlighted paramapadam as his current abode and samsāram as the other shore. At the time of attaining the goal, paramapadam only will be in forefront; only because of samsāram being a possession of emperumān, it will be desirable. Though it is said in cāndōjña upaniśat 8.12.3 “*nōpajanam smaran idam śarīram*” ([ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) will not contemplate about the material body after reaching the spiritual realm), one will consider that emperumān’s possession should be enjoyed fully, and only due to that reason, one will consider samsāram to be desirable. Otherwise, with any other reason \[such as materialistic enjoyment\], it will not be fully enjoyable \[as it is said “*bhuvani* ***muḻudu*** *(fully) āḷīrō*“\]. *ponnulagu āḷīrō – bhuvani muḻudu āḷīrō* – This \[material\] realm is contrary to servitude, but paramapadam is natural fit for servitude. paramapadam is the primary abode of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is the target of the message. leelā vibhūti is his possession too \[Since paramapadam is his primary abode, it is said first\].
- *bhuvani muḻudu āḷīrō* – Why did she, who gave the desirable paramapadam, also give leelā vibhūti which is to be given up? Being overwhelmed by the help of the birds, she gives leelā vibhūti too without realising what she is doing. Even those who became bewildered previously did the same thing as said in  śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 68.29 and 68.30 “*aparāvartināmyāca yāca bhūmipradāyinām*” (For those who never return to this world and for those who have given the earth in charity). Only when the love is limited, one will be clear. \[When sītāp pirātti became overwhelmed with affection towards hanuman for announcing the victory of śrī rāma\] she became bewildered and said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 116.20 “*hiraṇyamvā suvarṇamvā ratnānivividānivā \| rājyamvā triśu lōkēśu rājyam naitadarhati bhāśitam \|\|*” (All of silver, gold, many varieties of gems, the reign of the three worlds would not be a match for the sweet words you rendered). Both the realms are present equally at the disposal of the couple \[[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) and [parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)\].
- *nal nalap puḷ inangāḷ* – Your quality \[two explanations – collection of all good qualities, compassion\], is greater than his, how amazing! Instead of being like him who needs to be sent a messenger even at this situation, you are present in front of me! I have seen your qualities – you have carried my message and brought him over to me! We thought he is famous due to his qualities; but it appears that you have greater qualities than he – says [parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/). Instead of realising about your qualities, due to my urge, I troubled you saying “accept this (paramapadam)! accept that (samsāram)!” and so on! On seeing you even [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is praised in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 116.28 “*guṇāstvayyēvaśōbhanā:*” (these qualities are shining in you only), is to be overlooked. piḷḷai amudanār used to say “For your greatness his qualities are like aṟugu (grass) and tāḷi flowers”. Did I do anything for you! Haven’t you done all of these out of your mercy! Your mercy is similar to how kriṣṇa went as messenger for pāṇḍavas and how maṇakkāl nambi reformed āḷavandār!
- *nal nalap puḷ inangāḷ* – Explained as “Oh flock of birds who are having good qualities!” and “Oh flock of birds who are being very affectionate!” They remained confident saying “would we do anything short of uniting both of you?”; (hanuman says to sītāp pirātti) śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 116.24 “*artatasca mayāprāptā dēvarājyādayō guṇā: \| hataśatrum vijayinamrāmam paśyāmi sustitam \|\|*” (On seeing the victorious śrī rāma, I attained the greatness of ruling the heaven etc).
- *nal nalam* – You have mercifully helped me and made me shiver thinking “what will I do in return” forever. \[nalam is explained as mercy\] śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 1.11 is explained. śrī rāma says to hanuman.
   - *aham ca raghuvamśaśca* … – I who remain as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 66.10 “*na jīvēyam kśaṇamapi*” (śrī rāma says – I will not survive even for a moment without seeing sītā) and brother bharata who cannot survive without me and lakśmaṇa who is our life.
   - *vaidēhyā:* – to say that all of these words are apt \[finding of vaidēhi\].
   - *darmata: parirakśitā:* – Is there anything in return that will match your help? You have done this only due to your righteousness.
- *puḷ* – You who are having such great mercy, are having wings which help you travel! Due to recollecting the act of the monkeys in śrī rāmāyaṇam, she remains thinking “the job of the animals/birds is to unite those who are separated from each other”.
- *inangāḷ* – Even those who say as in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 116-45 “*nakaścin nāparādyati*” (there is none who has not committed a wrongful deed), are present \[in the flocks\].
- *inangāḷ* – Like the body and soul (wife and husband) are together! Having those who walk ahead saying as \[sītāp pirātti said\] in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 27.9 “*agratastē gamiśyāmi*” (I will go before you).
- *inangāḷ* – Also explained as in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 30.3 “*dikśu sarvāsu mārgantē*” (searching in all directions), the flocks are present to go in every direction.
- *vinaiyāttiyēn* – I have sinned so much that I lost the [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who was with me, and am now falling at your feet. Just as you have good qualities as your nature (main characteristic), I have misfortune as my nature.
- *nān* – He remains as said in “*darmata: parirakśitā:”*! She is thinking “I am sending messenger with the same greatness of the divine daughter of śrī janakarāja!”.
- *nān irandēn* – The tables have turned (Previously, śrī rāma prayed towards hanuman/sugrīva and now [parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying the words towards birds).
- *irandēn* – Previously, [nammāḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) surrendered to emperumān in four decads (tiruvāimoḻi 5.7, tiruvāimoḻi 5.8, tiruvāimoḻi 5.9, tiruvāimoḻi 5.10); now, he is surrendering to [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s devotees; even if those failed, this would not fail. There is no hurdles in this approach. \[Where is śaraṇāgati?\] śaraṇāgati is said as “*prārtanā mati*” (the state of praying). He is pursuing the means which has no failings.
- *inangāḷ – irandēn* – For couples, the nature of those who request will be well known. While these birds with great mercy will even give up their own lives for the sake of those who surrendered unto them \[as illustrated by śrī rāma to sugrīva and others while accepting śrī vibhīśaṇāḻvān – a pigeon sacrificed its own life to feed the hungry hunter who previously killed the pigeon’s pair\], my situation is too pathetic even for the most cruel murderers.
- *nal nalap puḷ inangāḷ irandēn* – How complete he is to give refuge!
- *nān irandēn* – First he only surrendered to sugrīva as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam kiśkintā kāṇḍam 4.19 “*sugrīvam śaraṇamgata:*” (śrī rāma surrendered to sugrīva); only then, she (sītāp pirātti) said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 40.3 “*tatā kuru dayām mayi*” (you have to bestow your mercy in this manner).
- *vinaiyāttiyēn nān irandēn* – Even after giving everything to the birds, she remains dissatisfied feeling that she has not done nothing to them. Only when their favour is limited, she can find a matching favour in return and give it to them. Even after giving everything, as said in mahābhāratam “*krutsnamvā prutivīm dadyān na tattulyam katancana*” (while serving the ācārya, for the favour done by the ācārya, the śiśya can never repay it even if he can offer the entire world), one remains only with the feeling that whatever offered is not enough. One should not stop with thinking as said in āpastamba sūtram “*tasmai na druhyēt*” (I should not betray him); instead one should think as said in mahābhāratam udyōga parvam “*krutam asya jānan*” (one should be grateful for his favour). Only when one withdraws from being grateful, he should be told not to betray the benefactor. When the birds asked “Do we have to explain these to him? Only if he has it in him to come, we can inform him”, she replied “I lost him due to my misfortune only and if we look at his qualities, would I lose him?”.
- *mun ulagam* … – He can create everything from the beginning after being destroyed! I am too in a dilapidated state. Who created this world for me to feel broken in separation and send him a messenger? He did this purely out of his mercy! Previously (during creation), one need not send him a messenger to protect everyone!
- *mun ulagangaḷ ellām padaitta em mugil vaṇṇan* – He who previously created everything without distinguishing between water and land, through his sankalpa jñānam as said in taittirīya upaniśat “*bahu syām*” (let me become many)!
- *mugil vaṇṇan* – Even if he protects with favouritism, his form is so beautiful that he cannot be given up; can also be construed as [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) helping for his own sake \[like cloud, instead of expecting anything from us\].
- *mugil vaṇṇan kaṇṇan* – Explaining the audāryam (magnanimity) etc which is the reason for jagat kāraṇatvam (his being the cause of everything) and avatārams (incarnations); alternatively – it can be construed as saying how emperumān descended with his spiritual divine form.
- *en nalam koṇḍa pirān* – Why should we re-dig an old well \[why going back to emperumān who created the world long ago\]? He is the one who fully captured me; he made me surrender unto you. Except for being separated from me now, whatever he has done is good! Before uniting with us he would have many good qualities, but now he only has beautiful qualities.
- *mugil vaṇṇan* *en nalam koṇḍa* – Instead of me being the recipient of the water of that cloud \[[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)\], I became the place from where he fetches water \[i.e., captured me\].
- *tanakku en nilaimai* – When the birds asked “Though he will come on his own, what should we tell him?”, she said “my state” and showed her own form just as the daṇḍakāraṇya riśis showed their bodies with cut-off limbs to śrī rāma in śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam “*ēhi paśya śarīrāṇi*” (Look at our bodies). As you have seen me, you can yourself speak about my situation to him \[I need not tell you what to tell him\]. She spoke about his jagat kāraṇatvam, avatārams and the special mercy he showered upon her without any shortcoming; but her own nature of being fully immersed in his qualities cannot be spoken by her similar to [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is said as in tiruvāimoḻi 8.4.6 “*tanakkum than tanmai aṟivariyān*” (emperumān does not himself know the limits of his greatness).
- *uraittu* – She is confident that these birds can speak about her situation, which are difficult to comprehend for himself. Since they stand on the shore \[unlike me who is drowned in his qualities\], they can do it. Why did she not tell the birds “inform him, and bring him along” \[and stopped at saying “inform him”\]? She remains “How can I ask him to act in a particular way? It is his choice”; we can only inform him our needs; rest is his responsibility.
- *en nilaimai uraittu – pon ulagu āḷīrō* – You try to rule after ensuring my suffering cry \[it will be unfair for you to enjoy while I am suffering\]! While daśarata cakravarti was eagerly awaiting the coronation of perumāḷ (śrī rāma), śrī rāma did not have his heart attached to the kingdom due to the sufferings of the sages at the hands of the demons and hence he left for the forest; similarly, she thinks that the birds will not rule the two realms if they keep hearing the defeat of the women and their cry.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

adiyen saraty ramanuja dasan

## 6.8.2. Maiyamar

*mai amar vāḷ nedum kaṇ mangaimār munbu en kaiyirundu ney amar in adisil niccal pālodu mēvīrō kai amar cakkarattu en kanivāyp perumānaik kaṇḍu mey amar kādal sollik kiḷigāḷ! viraindōdi vandē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kiḷigāḷ – Oh parrots (who are enjoyable for both parānguśa nāyaki and emperumān due to their physical beauty and sweet talks)!; kai amar cakkaram – having the beautiful combination of his hand and the divine disc; kani – enjoyable like a ripened fruit; vāy – having beautiful lips; en perumānai – the lord who has accepted me as his servitor; kaṇḍu – (you who are fortunate to see him before me,) on seeing; mey – with the divine form; amar – to enjoy in abundance; kādal – great desire; solli – telling; viraindu – in a speedy manner; ōdi vandu – arriving quickly; mai – black pigment; amar – aptly; vāḷ – radiant; nedu – expansive; kaṇ – having eyes; mangaimār munbu – in the presence of the girl friends who are of the same age; en – my; kai – hand; irundu – being present; ney – with ghee; amar – together; in – sweet; adisil – rice; pālodu – with milk; niccal – eternally; mēvīr – accept

**Перевод:**

**Oh parrots! On seeing the lord who is having the beautiful combination of his hand and the disc, who has accepted me as his servitor, having beautiful lips which are enjoyable like a ripened fruit, telling him my great desire to enjoy in abundance with his divine form, and in a speedy manner, arriving quickly to me who is in the presence of the girl friends who are of the same age, having black pigment aptly anointed, radiant, expansive eyes, eternally accept the sweet rice which is with ghee and milk together in my hand.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the second pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki prays to some parrots saying “You should acknowledge the joyful celebrations of my friends and me, after informing my state to emperumān and returning to us”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, parānguśa nāyaki says to some parrots “You should acknowledge my glorification of you in front of my friends after you inform my helplessness to emperumān who has enjoyable symbols, and return to me”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. mai amar vāḷ nedum kaṇ mangaimār munbu en kaiyirundu ney amar in adisil niccal pālodu mēvīrō kai amar cakkarattu en kanivāyp perumānaik kaṇḍu mey amar kādal sollik kiḷigāḷ! viraindōdi vandē*

- *mai amar* – In the first pāsuram, she offered \[the birds\] his wealth; in this pāsuram she is offering something which is greater than that. His wealth – ubhaya vibhūti (spiritual and material realms); the wealth which is greater than that is herself who is dear to him. Even while offering herself, instead of doing it secretively, she is offering right on her own hand.
- *mai amar vāḷ nedum kaṇ mangaimār munbu en kai irundu* – Are those who are praised by her same as those who were praised by him \[śrī rāma praised hanuman for being a messenger for him, here she is praising the parrots\]! Those who reside in the inner-quarters have similar qualities; they all can be seen with the same vision. As said in periya tirumoḻi 11.3.5 “*tammaiyē nāḷum vaṇangit toḻuvārkku tammaiyē okka aruḷ seyvar*” ([emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)  will bless those who worship him to become similar to him), she too has given them her qualities.
- *mai amar* – They too have the greatness which is explained in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 16.5 “*asitēkśaṇā*” (one who is having beautiful dark eyes), [tiruvāimoḻi 6.5.8](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/02/thiruvaimozhi-6-5-8-thirundhu-vedhamum/) “*karundadangaṇṇi*” (one with black, expansive eyes). It can be explained as [parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) highlighting their natural darkness like her own eyes; alternatively, it can be highlighting about the black pigment which is applied for auspiciousness. When she is at loss \[of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)\], they cannot be decorating their eyes with black pigment; when you arrive you see it in their eyes \[i.e., they have decorated their eyes expecting his arrival\]! vāḷ – radiance. Even that has disappeared. When her form has lost the radiance, their eyes cannot have it.
- *nedum kaṇ* – The whole expansive eyes become purposeful only when that happens \[when emperumān arrives\]. Otherwise, its just a burden as said in periya tirumoḻi 11.7.1 “*kāṇādār kaṇ enṟum kaṇ alla*” (the eyes which don’t see [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) are never considered as eyes).
- *mai amar vāḷ nedum kaṇ* – Implies “Seeing your arrival, I become happy and acknowledge that ‘his arrival is certain’, and decorate myself; seeing that, you have decorated yourself and are having radiant, expansive eyes”.
- *mangaimār* – Just as he has his apt friends as said in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 3.1.1 “*tannērāyiram piḷḷaigaḷ*“, she is having apt friends.
- *mangaimār* – Just as muktātmās (liberated souls) will have an ever youthful form of twenty five years old.
- *mangaimār munbu* – They won’t be behind her!
- *mangaimār* – Not just one or two, but everyone will come into the forefront. As tiruvadi (hanuman) was praised by the monkeys as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 57.31 “*hanūmantam mahātmānam parivāryōpatastirē*” (the best among the monkeys surrounded hanuman and praised him). *mahātmānam* – is four persons surrounding and praising a great thing? The monkey leaders offered fruits and roots and praised hanuman as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 57.33 “*upāyanāni upādāya mūlā ca palāni ca*” (monkeys presented fruits and roots as gifts to hanuman); similarly here too sweet rice with ghee and all are present. There people with well-rounded faces were present as said in “*bējirē vipulānanā:*“, and here everyone has “*mai amar vāḷ nedum kaṇ*“.
- *en kai irundu* – Though they are said to be sharing the joys and sorrows as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam kiśkintā kāṇḍam 5.18 “*ēkam du:kham sukham ca nau*“, only one who is hungry needs to eat! So, this is their assembly; let my hand be their abode. I will make my hand which is a decoration to his crown, as your seat. As said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 5.13.54 “d*hadau bāhulatām skandē*” (she placed her hand on kriṣṇa’s shoulder like a creeper spreading on a supporting stick), the hand which is fully offered to him. His presence on her hand is not the same as being on his serpent bed which is explained in paryanga vidyā. What is prayed in by her in “*aṇi migu tāmaraik kai*” (Considering his lotus like hand as decoration on me), is applicable in his case too. She is saying “*mey amar kādal solli kiḷigāḷ! viraindōdi vandu, en kai irundu ney amar in adisil niccal pālodu mēvīrō!*“. Why śouldn’t she praise the birds while they are going?  For that, she needs some ability; she remains as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 40.3 “*gātraiśśōkābikarśitai:*” (she is having very tired limbs) and tiruvāimoḻi 7.2.4 “*itta kāl itta kaiyaḷāy irukkum*” (unable to move her feet and hands); also, she needs her friends to praise them! But they too remain as said in tiruvāimoḻi 9.9.5 “*emmin mun avanukku māyvarālō*” (they fall for him even before me).
- *ney amar …* – She has no ownership over her own body to offer it to them unlike [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who embraced hanuman as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 1.13 “*ēśa sarvasva bhūtastu*“. As I give the sweet rice which is mixed with ghee and milk everyday, you should accept them and uplift me. She who remains as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 6.7.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/03/thiruvaimozhi-6-7-1-unnum-soru/) “*uṇṇum sōṟu parugu nīr tinnum veṟṟilaiyum ellām kaṇṇan*” (sustaining food, nourishing water and pleasure-giving betel leaves are all kriṣṇa), is seeking and offering what is dear to them! What is explained by this? For those who do favours in bhagavat viśayam \[for the ācārya, śrīvaiṣṇavas who nurture our knowledge, devotion etc\], one should not be satisfied with just sharing a portion of whatever one has. One should seek out what is dear to them and offer those. In case of [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/), it is said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 103.30 “*yadanna:puruśō bhavati …*” (whatever one partakes, it must be offered to his vorśippable deities) \[In case of bhagavān, it is sufficient to offer whatever is fit to be consumed by us. But for ācāryas/śrīvaiṣṇavas, we should seek out the materials which are desirable for them and offer them\].
- *niccal* – The connection happens once, but the enjoyment is eternal. As said in stōtra ratnam 2 “*atra paratra cāpi nityam yadīya caraṇau śaraṇam madīyam”* (in this world and in the other world as well, always the divine feet of that śrīman nātamunigaḷ are my refuge).
- *kai amar cakkarattu en kani vāyp perumānaik kaṇḍu* – She is trying to feed those who already consumed \[on seeing [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)\]. By this it is explained that – those who are related to [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/), will attain the desires of āḻvār even before āḻvār attains them; [nānmugan tiruvandādi 18](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/07/nanmugan-thiruvandhadhi-18/) “*vēṟāgavē ēttiyiruppārai vellumē maṟṟavaraic cāttiyiruppar tavam*” (the penance (means) of those who depend on the devotees of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s devotees is greater than that of emperumān’s devotees).
- *kai amar cakkaram* – Being with the disc on his hand always.
- *en kani vāy* – Manifesting the divine beauty of his hand and the disc is equivalent to showing his smile. I was captured by his smile which he let out while separating from him thinking “let her sustain herself thinking about this smile”.
- *en kani vāy* – Hand is fully enjoyed by the divine disc; his lips are fully enjoyed by her. His (cakkarattāḻvār’s) life is eternally sustained \[since he never separates from the hand\]; but my sustenance is occasional only.
- *kaṇḍu* – Unlike me who has everything in the mind, you can see him. For her, she can only see through their eyes and see them; for her it is as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 5.6 “*tām spruśtvā*” (I touch her through the wind which touched her) and “*candrē druśti samāgama:*” (I see her through the moon which was seen by her).
- *mey amar kādal solli* – She is saying “my love is such that I want to embrace your divine form”; or she is saying “my love is such that I want you to embrace my body”. śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 40.3 “*gātraiś śōkābhikarśita: samspruśēyam*” (I should be blessed to touch śrī rāma with my weakened limbs). Tell him not to think “She will live when I live” or “She will sustain by thinking about my qualities” \[[āṇḍāḷ](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/andal/) sustained herself by thinking about emperumān’s qualities as said in nācciyār tirumoḻi 8.3 “*en gōvindan guṇam pādi … āvi kāttiruppēnē*” (I will sing about my gōvinda’s qualities and sustain myself)\]. There were others who sustained themselves like that. Even when shown the māyā śiras (replica of śrī rāma’s head), sītāp pirātti cried like a materialistic person would do, yet sustained herself saying “I would have died the moment śrī rāma died. The fact that I am living implies that he is alive too”. śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 21.15 “*ananyā rāghavēṇāham bhāskarēṇaprabhāyatā*” (I am inseparable from śrī rāma like the rays are inseparable from the sun); unless there is sun, there cannot be any rays. There is  contraction and expansion only due to certain reasons \[such as sītāp pirātti crying or being joyful based on her situation in her avatāram\]. While \[[ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)\] being a dravya (entity), it can also be a prakāra (attribute) \[of [paramātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)\]. Here it is not like that; for those who separated after the embrace, they cannot sustain without embracing again.
- *mey amar kādal* – [piḷḷān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/pillan/) explains this as “Don’t think our love is fake like yours” \[mey is explained as truth\]. Alternatively,
- *mey amar kādal* – Love attached to the [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) \[here mey is explained as ātmā\], that is, love which is naturally fitting with ātmā. In [tirumālai 38](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/12/thirumalai-38-part-1/) “*meymmaiyē miga uṇarndu*“, mey indicates ātmā only. True love.
- solli – When one does not know something oneself, one should hear it from others. If he had the same feeling, he would not have let me send a messenger. It appears that informing her state to him is more important than actually seeing him.
- *kiḷigāḷ! viraindu ōdi vandē* – You should come ahead like the monkey elders who returned with the joyful news to perumāḷ (śrī rāma) after seeing pirātti and like hanuman who rushed ahead to bring joy to śrī bharatāḻvān while śrī rāma was returning.
- *kiḷigāḷ! viraindu ōdi vandē* – After informing him, don’t wait to come along with him. hanuman, when went searching for pirātti, spent a whole lot of time since he was given sufficient time, reached lankā, saw her and then returned on the same day saying “The purpose of seeing sītāp pirātti will be fulfilled only when we inform him when he is alive”; the reason for such thoughts – while leaving śrī rāma, he saw his great sorrow and thought “it is difficult to see him alive when we return”; perumāḷ too said “My dear! Don’t see my current sustaining state when you are present here and think that I will be the same later too; please act according to my situation”.
- *viraindu ōdi vandē* – Only when the joy of your prior arrival settles, he should come. If you arrive with him, I cannot praise you freely \[naturally, when [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is there, he is the center of attraction; even ācāryas will take the backseat\]; hence, you arrive so that I can enjoy properly! Ensure that I first fall at the divine feet of you, the benefactors, before falling at his feet. This is why, our elders first recite guruparamparā \[mantram\] before reciting [dvaya mahā mantram](http://ponnadi.blogspot.in/2015/12/rahasya-thrayam.html)! Now, only when the ācārya is present with a physical body in this material world, the śiśya can serve him affectionately \[Refer [upadēśa rattina mālai 64](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/02/upadhesa-raththina-malai-64/)\]; subsequently, both will engage in bhagavat anubhavam together. Only when the ācārya remains “for me” \[in this material world\], the śiśya can serve him thinking “for you”.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

adiyen saraty ramanuja dasan

## 6.8.3. Odi vandu

*ōdi vandu en kuḻal mēl oḷi mā malar ūdīrō? kūdiya vaṇḍinangāḷ! kuru nādudai aivargatkāy ādiya mā nedundērp padai nīṟeḻac ceṟṟa pirān sūdiya taṇḍuḷabam uṇḍa tūmadu vāygaḷ koṇḍē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kūdiya – mutually close; vaṇḍu inangāḷ – swarm of bees!; kuru nādudai – the leaders of kurukśētra; aivargatku āy – for the five pāṇḍavas; ādiya – having beautiful movements; mā – horses; nedu – tall; tēr – chariots; padai – army; nīṟu eḻa – to become dust particles; seṟṟa – destroyed; pirān – kriṣṇa, the great benefactor; sūdiya – decorated on his divine hair; taṇ – invigorating; tuḷabam – from the tiruttuḻāy; uṇḍa – drank; tū – pure; madu – having honey; vāygaḷ – mouth; koṇḍu – having; ōdi vandu – coming here immediately; en – my; kuḻalmēl – on hair; oḷi – radiant; mā – best; malar – in flower; ūdīr – suck it as you sucked the honey

**Перевод:**

**Oh swarm of bees who are mutually close to each other! Having drunk the pure honey from the invigorating tiruttuḻāy which is decorating the divine hair of kriṣṇa, the great benefactor, who destroyed the horses which were having beautiful movements, tall chariots and the army to become dust particles, for the five pāṇḍavas who were the leaders of kurukśētra! Coming here immediately with the same mouth, suck the best flower which is on my radiant hair.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the third pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki says to a swarm of bees “You inform my state to emperumān, return to me and live on top of my head”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, parānguśa nāyaki says to some swarm of bees “As you go on behalf of me, kriṣṇa, the destroyer of the enemies of his devotees, will behold you on his head; you would become refreshed; you return to me and suck the fresh flowers on my hair, which were decorated thinking ‘he is coming’ “.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. ōdi vandu en kuḻal mēl oḷi mā malar ūdīrō? kūdiya vaṇḍinangāḷ! kuru nādudai aivargatkāy ādiya mā nedundērp padai nīṟeḻac ceṟṟa pirān sūdiya taṇḍuḷabam uṇḍa tūmadu vāygaḷ koṇḍē*

- *ōdi vandu* – You should return soon. As you have seen my state, you should arrive when I am alive. Alternatively, she is asking them to return soon due to the urge in enjoying them.
- *en kuḻal mēl* – She would know the greatness of her hair based on how a great personality (emperumān) is attracted to it. Why is she speaking like those who pay fees after completing a task in saying “sūdiya taṇḍuḷabam uṇḍē tūmaduvāygaḷ koṇḍu ōdi vandu en kuḻal mēl oḷi mā malar ūdīrō”? For the bees, there should be something in her hair. Now, the honey has dried out and the hair is withered; only when they return \[with happy news\], her hair will become fresh again.
- *en kuḻal mēl* – This is the greatness of these bees who go as her messenger, over those \[monkeys\] who went as his messenger \[with respect to the gift they got after going as messenger\]. There sugrīva mahārāja’s maduvanam (the orchard) was destroyed; here she is saying “I am giving my forest like hair which is dear to him, to you”. aḷagādavi (hair-forest) is the top most gift (as it is on the head, and it is the best). There is no dadimuka et al who can be a hurdle here \[dadimuka was the guard for maduvanam, who tried stopping hanuman and others from enjoying\]. The peaceful hanuman said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 62.2 “*aham āvārayiśyāmi yuśmākam paripantina:*” (Enjoy the honey! I will keep off your enemies). Though sugrīva mahārāja did not know about hanuman’s sighting of sītāp pirātti, as soon as he heard about maduvanam’s ransacking, he smashed his tail on the riśyamuka parvatam \[monkeys smash their tail when they are joyful\]. As they are ransacking maduvanam even though the time limit given to them is over, they must have spotted sītāp pirātti. bhattar mercifully used to say “If the maduvanam was not present, the joy of the monkeys in finding pirātti would have reflected on the back of the princes” \[patting the back in joy is a common act – every monkey would have joyfully patted the back of śrī rāma and lakśmaṇa\].
- *en kuḻal mēl oḷi mā malar ūdīrō –* The bees should always be drinking the honey from her hair. tiruvāimoḻi 9.9.4 “tūvi am puḷ udait teyva vaṇḍu” (the divine bee (emperumān) who has pure, beautiful garuda) or these bees. She is saying “Can emperumān only give sāmyāpatti (a type of mōkśa, where emperumān gives his devotees all his qualities)? I too will give you sāmyāpatti (equality) with him \[in enjoying my hair\]”. As said in taittirīya upaniśat “sōśnutē …” (the liberated soul enjoys with bhagavān), I will feed \[give pleasure to\] you both \[emperumān and the bees\] from the same container \[her hair\]. This is the topmost food.
- *en kuḻal mēl oḷi mā malar ūdīrō –* In my hair which became fresh on your arrival, would you drink the honey from the best, radiant flower?
- *ūdīrō* – Due to the abundance of honey, like someone who hesitates to enter flood waters, the bees are hesitating. While it is your duty \[to inform emperumān\] and it is a help to others \[me\], why are you waiting?
- *kūdiya vaṇḍinangāḷ* – There is no need for you to assemble the army like sugrīva mahārāja had to do. You have all already assembled to help me. sugrīva ordered his army only after iḷaiyaperumāḷ (lakśmaṇa) went to the entrance of kiśkindā and praised \[chastised\] him.
- *kuru nādu udai aivargatkāy* – emperumān is of the nature that he will feel sorry for the wives of others \[pāṇḍavas\] whose hair is not well maintained \[due to sorrow\]; as said in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 4.9.6 “*maittunar mār kādaliyai mayir mudippittu avargaḷaiyē mannarākki*” (Helping the wives of his cousins tie their hair \[after their husbands became victorious\] and crowning his cousins). He thinks that pāṇḍavas are the owners of the kingdom and considers himself to be their servitor.
- *kuru nādu udai aivar* – duryōdana and his brothers were like someone who climbed the ceremonial elephant without the permission of the elephant’s caretaker. As said in [tiruvāimoḻi 6.6.4](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/02/thiruvaimozhi-6-6-4-pidudai-nanmuganai/) “*nādudai mannar*“, pāṇḍavas are the real owners of the kingdom. āḻvār is speaking based on bhagavān’s opinion which is “the current regime under duryōdana et al is unlawful”; āḻvār’s thoughts follow emperumān’s thoughts.
- *ādiya mā nedum tēr* – With the huge chariot that has horses with beautiful steps; with the chariot that is described in [śrī bhagavat gītā 1.14](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/1-14/) “*mahati syandanē stitau*” (seated in the huge chariot).
- *padai nīṟeḻac ceṟṟa pirān* – Since he was not allowed to take up arms, he rode the chariot wheels to destroy the army into pieces.
- *ceṟṟa pirān* – Favouring others even at the cost of obliterating himself, is his natural quality. She considers that he reduced himself as the charioteer due to a particular reason \[not his natural quality\].
- *ceṟṟa pirān* – arjuna et al are similar to his weapons; emperumān himself declared in [śrī bhagavat gītā 11.33](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/11-33/) “*mayaivaitē nihatā: pūrvam Eva*” (as I have vowed to finish them already).
- *sūdiya taṇ tuḷabam uṇḍa* – The bees which drink the honey from the garland which he wore while riding arjuna’s chariot. Whatever garlands he wears in his incarnations, tiruttuḻāy (tuḷasi) assumes such garland forms to favour emperumān.
- *tū madu vāygaḷ koṇḍē* – Having their mouth purified and sweetened after drinking the honey from that garland; it can also mean – the bees which have sweet speech.
- *tū madu vāygaḷ koṇḍē – ōdi vandu en kuḻal mēl oḷi mā malar ūdīrō* – śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 5.6 is explained here. *vāhivāta* – As you \[wind\] cannot be seen by eyes, what did you get? *tvayimē gātra samsparśa:* – Contact with sītāp pirātti for my senses, is through you. I only get to touch you who touched her. *candrē druśti samāgama:* – Touch is similar to vision for me \[I can only see the moon that was seen you\]. \[Another meaning – mouth is pure\] With the mouth which makes that which fell apart to stick together \[when draupadi was in the forest, due to her purity, on hearing her words, a mango which fell from the tree went back to the tree and stuck to it\]. Like hanuman said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 65.10 “*druśtā sītā*” (I have seen sītā) \[and eventually united sītāp pirātti and śrī rāma\], you make me drink this honey and you too drink it.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.8.4. Tu madu

*tū madu vāygaḷ koṇḍu vandu en mullaigaḷ mēl tumbigāḷ! pū madu uṇṇac cellil vinaiyēnaip poy seydaganṟa māmadu vār taṇḍuḻāy mudi vānavar kōnaik kaṇḍu yāmiduvō takkavāṟu enna vēṇḍum kaṇḍīr nungatkē*

**Пословный перевод:**

en – raised by me; mullaigaḷ – jasmine; mēl – seated on; tumbigāḷ – dragonflies!; tū – pure; madu – having honey as identity; vāygaḷ – mouths; koṇḍu – with; vandu – arriving; pū – flower’s; madu – honey; uṇṇa – to drink; sella – if you set out; vinaiyēnai – me who is having the sin which caused the separation \[from emperumān \]; poy – mischievous union; seydu – performed; aganṟa – separated; mā – greatly flowing; madu – honey; vār – dripping; taṇ – cool; tuḻāy – decorated with tiruttuḻāy; mudi – donning the divine crown; vānavar – for nityasūris (eternal associates of emperumān in paramapadam); kōnai – one who is the ruler; kaṇḍu – on seeing; nungatku – for you (who are present in such prosperous situation); yām – your highness; iduvō – should manifest your supremacy like this?; takkavāṟu – fitting your merciful stature?

**Перевод:**

**Oh dragon flies seated on the jasmines raised by me! Having pure honey-mouths as your identity, if you have arrived to drink the honey from those jasmine flowers, you first go to emperumān who performed mischievous union with me and separated, and who is donning the divine crown which is decorated with cool tiruttuḻāy in which honey is greatly flowing and dripping, and who is ruling over the nityasūris; on seeing him, you tell him “Your highness! Should you manifest your supremacy like this? Is this fitting your merciful stature?”. Implies, only then, me as well as my jasmine flowers will become fresh and you can drink the honey from them.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fourth pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki mercifully tells some dragonflies “Go and inform emperumān who is in paramapadam ‘is it fitting for you to torment her there while you are enjoying with garland on your crown, in the unreachable abode?’ “.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. tū madu vāygaḷ koṇḍu vandu en mullaigaḷ mēl tumbigāḷ! pū madu uṇṇac cellil vinaiyēnaip poy seydaganṟa māmadu vār taṇḍuḻāy mudi vānavar kōnaik kaṇḍu yāmiduvō takkavāṟu enna vēṇḍum kaṇḍīr nungatkē*

- *tū madu vāygaḷ koṇḍu vandu* – Going with the mouth which is pure and having sweet speech. *vandu* (coming) means *senṟu* (going). With the sweet speech which will sustain those who are in anguish.
- *en mullaigaḷ mēl tumbigāḷ* – You too remain hungry like those who suffer along. Both the flowers in her hair and in the nearby garden are in a withered state; as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 59.10 “*apivrukśā: parimlānā:*” (Even the trees withered).
- *pū madu uṇṇac cellil* – Since you have the tendency to extract honey, you will go to places where flowers are present. Only those flowers in her side will be withered; but flowers in his side will be fresh; he is said as “*mā madu vār taṇ tuḻāy mudi vānavar kōn*“. The only difference between them (nityasūris) and him is his divine crown and the garland. Unlike the bees here, those who are there need not remain hungry.
- *mā madu vār taṇ tuḻāy* – Even in separation, he remains fresh.
- *pū madu uṇṇac cellil* – Once the flower in hair withered and the honey dried up, she thinks that the same would be the case throughout this material realm; she thinks that now if honey is present anywhere it will only be in [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s side.
- *vinaiyēnai* – I who have committed sins to think that his sweet talks and his love towards me are truthful.
- *vinaiyēnaip poy seydu* – Knowing that if he left suddenly she will die unable to bear that, he remained saying “I will never separate from you; I cannot bear your separation”, but suddenly made me realise that he was gone; and I didn’t understand how he did that. Had I known I would have held him and not let him go!
- *poy seydu* – This is how dissatisfied she is even in the union. [āḻvārs](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/azhwars/) are of the nature that even after spending a long time with [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) , they will feel “everything happened \[quickly\] like a dream”, since union always ends with separation. Unfulfilled enjoyment is highlighted as dream, magic or fake.
- *poy seydu aganṟa* – This is his reason to separate. Pretending to be together, not having fulfilling time together and leaving mischievously.
- *mā madu vār taṇ tuḻāy mudi* – Since honey seen is present there too, it will be doubly delightful. That is the best honey too. Seeing him \[his quality\], it (honey) will remain consistent both in union and separation too.
- *vānavar kōnaik kaṇḍu* – Seeing [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is presenting himself to those who care for themselves. Seeing emperumān who is ignoring his own words as in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 41.4 “*tvayi kincit samāpannē kim kāryam sītayā mama*” (even if you were insulted a little bit, what is the use of my getting back sītā?), he is pampering his old relatives \[nityasūris who are with him forever\].
- *yām* – \[calling him out respectfully\] Since he feels guilty, he would pretend to be conducting the grand assembly and will be difficult to be drawn attention to; without fearing his supremacy, draw his attention. On being called, he will have to look into your face; before he turns his face away, you ask him if his act is proper. ḍidn’t you tell someone as in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 40.41 “*ānrusamsyam parōdarma:*” (being compassionate is the ultimate darmam). That was visible in your form as in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 36.42 “*naivadamśān na maśakān*” (He will not drive away the flies and mosquitoes), and śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 36.41 “*namāmsam rāghavō bhungtē nacāpi madu sēvatē*” (he is neither indulging in meat nor in alcohol) \[But here you seem to be enjoying well\].
- *iduvō takkavāṟu* – Is hurting a woman and being garlanded in a grand assembly, your compassion?
- *enna vēṇḍum kaṇḍīr* – After seeing this grand assembly and his supremacy, you cannot remain compassionate thinking “how can we destroy this?”; in that situation, you think about me and speak.
- *nungatkē* – You who are not him, should do all of this. Otherwise, there is no difference between you who appeared in front of me in this sorrowful state and him.
- *nungatkē* – āren’t you residing in my jasmines! You have to preserve your own nature \[of helping me\]; he caused hurt to a woman (me) and is enjoying the grand assembly without considering the damage done to his nature; I am lying down \[waiting for him\]; now, you have to avoid causing damage to your own nature.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.8.5. Nungatku

*nungatku yān uraikkēn vammin yān vaḷartta kiḷigāḷ! vengatpuḷḷūrndu vandu vinaiyēnai nenjangavarnda sengaṇ karumugilaic ceyya vāyc ceḻungaṟpagattai enguc cenṟāgilungaṇḍu iduvō takkavāṟu enminē*

**Пословный перевод:**

yān – I; vaḷartta – grew up by my raising; kiḷigāḷ – Oh parrots!; vammin – come (not ignoring me due to your familiarity towards me); yān – I (who am going to benefit by you who are raised by me); nungatku – to you (who will live if I live); uraikkēn – telling (you what you already know and do); vem – staring at the enemies; kaṇ – having eye; puḷ – periya tiruvadi (garudāḻvān); ūrndu – riding him (to reveal his urge); vandu – arriving (near me); vinaiyēnai – me who is having the sin to be separated from him now; nenjam kavarnda – having captured my heart; sem – reddish; kaṇ – eye; karumugilai – having a blackish-form (contrast to that red colour, being seated in an apt way on the shoulders of periya tiruvadi as said in “pon malaiyin mīmisaik kārmugil pōlē” (like a dark cloud on a golden mountain)); seyya – reddish (due to being pleased with the accomplishment of the desire); vāy – having beautiful lips; seḻum kaṟpagattai – the great benefactor, who is like a distinguished kalpaka (desire fulfilling) tree (for letting me enjoy this beauty as a benefit for him); engāgilum – any location/state such as para (paramapadam), vyūha (milky ocean), vibhava (incarnations) etc; senṟu – go; kaṇḍu – see; iduvō – this act of capturing her heart and making her feel lonely; takkavāṟu – apt; enmin – ask that!

**Перевод:**

**Oh parrots who were raised by me! I am telling you; emperumān is riding periya tiruvadi whose eye is staring at the enemies, has arrived near me who is having the sin to be separated from him now and has captured my heart; if you go and see emperumān, the great benefactor, who is like a distinguished kalpaka tree, who is having reddish eye, a blackish-form and very reddish lips, in any location/state such as para, vyūha, vibhava etc., you ask “is this act of capturing her heart and making her feel lonely, apt?”.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fifth pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki tells her parrots “Wherever you go and see him, whether it is paramapadam or divya dēśams, ask him if this is how his compassion is”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. nungatku yān uraikkēn vammin yān vaḷartta kiḷigāḷ! vengatpuḷḷūrndu vandu vinaiyēnai nenjangavarnda sengaṇ karumugilaic ceyya vāyc ceḻungaṟpagattai enguc cenṟāgilungaṇḍu iduvō takkavāṟu enminē*

- *nugatku yān uraikkēn* – They too are sorrowful and being ahead of her; is this something I have to tell you \[You are already working to go to emperumān on my behalf\]? My sorrow makes me tell you this.
- *nugatku yān uraikkēn* – This is not to be told to you; I should not be the one saying this. While the parrots already are ready to eliminate my sorrow, I am talking as if I am someone else who doesn’t understand that.
- *vammin* – For you who are thinking “How will we make her sustain herself?”, I will give you the means, come on.
- *yān vaḷartta kiḷigāḷ* – For you who are born to me \[like my children\], is there time to be prideful like his associates? Were you born to be prideful like this!
- *nungatku* – For you who remain as in śrī rāmāyaṇam kiśkintā kāṇḍam 5.18 “*ēkam du:kham sukham ca nau*“ (sharing sorrow and joy).
- *yān* – I who have placed all my burden upon you.
- *uraikkēn* – I am not telling something you don’t know; I am telling because of my sorrowful state.
- *yān vaḷartta* – You who were raised by me by feeding sweet rice with milk and ghee.
- *kiḷigāḷ* – As said in tiruneduntāṇḍagam 14 “*vaḷarttadanāl payan peṟṟēn*” (I have attained the purpose of raising you), I could listen to his divine names from your mouth; and because it leads to more sorrow as said in “*kaṇṇan nāmamē kuḻaṟik konṟīr*” (you are killing me by reciting the names of kriṣṇa). I am looking to send you as messenger to him.
- *vem kaṇ puḷ* … – Coming on the bird which has angry eyes. Explaining the eyes to be angry due to his eliminating the hurdles while coming; alternatively the eyes are said to be angry due to the cruel way of separating emperumān from her and carrying him away as said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 5.18.30 “*akrūra: krūra hrudaya:*” (cruel-hearted akrūra).
- *vem kaṇ puḷ ūrndu vandu* – Like a prince who would come riding his ceremonial elephant to capture the girl he likes. āḻvār first sent a messenger to emperumān saying in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.4.6](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/07/thiruvaimozhi-1-4-6-arulatha-nir/) “*aruḷ āḻip puḷ kadavi avar vīdi oru nāḷ*” (taking a stroll on the street where she lives, on garudāḻvār who is an ocean of mercy, at least one day), and he obliged.
- *vinaiyēnai* – I have committed sin not to have dual heart like his; I am not having one heart to be finished while in union and another to sustain while in separation.
- *nenjam kavarnda* – emperumān who enlightens the mind of people has now destroyed my heart! Being a sāragrāhi (one who is capable of extracting the essence) he took the essence and left behind the residue; like those who carry the garland and leave behind the container. āḻvār’s heart is full of fragrance \[comparing it to a flower\]; he himself said in [tiruvāimoḻi 4.3.2](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/01/thiruvaimozhi-4-3-2-pusum-sandhu/) “*pūsum sāndu en nenjamē*” (my heart is the sandalwood paste you apply).
- *sem kaṇ karu mugilai* – His posture of looking with comforting eyes and presenting his divine form fully. Alternatively – explaining the completeness emperumān acquired after uniting with parānguśa nāyaki. Another explanation – informing that he was leaving, he stood looking with comforting eyes ready, to shed tears \[like a cloud\].
- *seyya vāy* – The smiling mouth which spoke many hundreds of words.
- *seḻum kaṟpagattai* – Distinguished kalpaka tree; here the distinguishing factor of emperumān from a desire fulfilling kalpaka tree is, emperumān himself would give, out of his own desire. kalpaka tree would neither bestow itself nor desire to help voluntarily; but he is capable of giving himself. He who gave himself in such a manner that, even when I am separated from him, he gave me the ability to bestow the two realms (spiritual and material) to whoever I desire to.
- *enguc cenṟāgilum kaṇḍu* – Already said “*vānavar kōnai*” (lord of nityasūris). Hearing that a messenger is coming, he would leave the grand assembly and enter the private quarters \[in paramapadam\]. Alternatively – you enter \[and search\] all the places where air will enter; that is para, vyūha, arcāvatārams; all places where he is hiding as said in bruhadāraṇyaka upaniśat “*yamātmā na vēda*” (The ātmā who is unaware of paramātmā). As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 1.40 “*anēnaiva hivēgēna gamiśyāmi surālayam*” (If I don’t find sītāp pirātti in lankā, I will reach svarga (heaven) with the same speed). You cannot return saying “he is not seen in paramapadam”.
- *iduvō takkavāṟu enminē* – Wherever he is, you words should be the same. Does it fit your mercy to steal the heart of others and keep yours as well? If we say that he does not have ānruśamsyam (mercy), that means he himself does not exist. As \[his\] compassion which is part of such mercy is not seen by us in us, tell him that he does not have that. For the one who is boasting of his compassion, there is nothing more damaging than this; so tell him this only.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.8.6. En minnu nul

*en minnu nūl mārvan en karum perumān en kaṇṇan tan mannu nīḷ kaḻal mēl taṇ tuḻāy namakkanṟi nalgān kanmingaḷ enṟu ummai yān kaṟpiyā vaitta māṟṟam solli senmingaḷ tīvinaiyēn vaḷartta siṟu pūvaigaḷē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

tī – cruel (instead of my serving you, I am making you serve me); vinaiyēn – I (who am having sin); vaḷartta – raised; siṟu – young; pūvaigaḷē – Oh mynās!; en minnu nūl mārvan – one who let me enjoy his divine chest which is having the divine yajñōpavīdam which is shining contrarily to his black coloured divine body; en karum perumān – my lord who let me enjoy (not only the part-by-part beauty, but also) his wholly beautiful dark-coloured body and my svāmy (Lord) who made me his servitor; en – totally obedient to me; kaṇṇan – kriṣṇa; than – his; nīḷ – which stretch up to the location of his devotees; kaḻal – divine feet; mēl – on; mannu – fittingly present; taṇ – invigorating; tuḻāy – tiruttuḻāy; namakku – to us; anṟi – but; nalgān – will not give joyfully (to anyone else); kanmingaḷ – Learn now!; enṟu – that; ummai – you (who are young and prideful); yān – I (who am ready to accept your service); kaṟpiyā vaitta – taught (saying “en minnu nūl mārvan … nalgān”); māṟṟam – words; solli – saying that; senmingaḷ – go!

**Перевод:**

**Oh mynās raised by cruel (person like) me! I have taught you saying “Learn now! kriṣṇa, who let me enjoy his divine chest which is having the divine yajñōpavīdam which is shining contrarily to his black coloured divine body, who is my lord and made me his servitor, who let me enjoy his wholly beautiful dark-coloured body, who is totally obedient to me , will joyfully give the invigorating tiruttuḻāy which is fittingly present on his divine feet which stretch up to the location of his devotees”; now you go \[to him\] saying the words I taught you.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the sixth pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki says to some mynās “Since emperumān is enjoying together with his devotees, he will fulfil our desires; you go to him and inform him if this matches his mercy”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, parānguśa nāyaki says to some mynās which she raised “kriṣṇan who is totally obedient will certainly give the tiruttuḻāy (tuḷasi) from his lotus feet for us; you go and tell him what I have taught you”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. en minnu nūl mārvan en karum perumān en kaṇṇan than mannu nīḷ kaḻal mēl taṇ tuḻāy namakkanṟi nalgān kanmingaḷ enṟu ummai yān kaṟpiyā vaitta māṟṟam solli senmingaḷ tīvinaiyēn vaḷartta siṟu pūvaigaḷē!*

- *en minnu nūl mārvan* … – One who made me fully exist for him by manifesting the divine yajñōpavīdam (sacred thread) as if it is shining in my heart. Even while my belonging ([emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)) is separated from me, would he offer my belonging (his tiruttuḻāy) to others?
- *en minnu nūl mārvan* – One who eradicated the darkness from my heart by manifesting the beauty of his divine yajñōpavīdam. By manifesting the nūl (thread) on his chest, he made me follow in line with the nūl (śāstram).
- *en karum perumān* – He acquired me by manifesting his divine dark form which contrasts with the bright yajñōpavīdam like a lightning in a cloud.
- *en kaṇṇan* – Accepting me by manifesting these aspects and then offered himself fully to me. Due to individual attachment towards the beauty of his decoration, divine form and simplicity, āḻvār is repeatedly saying “en” in every one of these aspects.
- *than mannu nīḷ kaḻal mēl taṇ tuḻāy namakkanṟi nalgān* – Whatever he does, he would not offer that which is said in jitantē stōtram “*bhaktānām*” (for the devotees), to others. This is the main pāsuram in this decad. Since [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is āśrita paratantran (submissive towards his devotees), [parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is sending a messenger considering his *aikarasyam* (being fully attached to his devotes), thinking “he will come to me if we inform him, after he becomes owned by his devotees).
- *than – nīḷ kaḻal – mannu – taṇ tuḻāy namakkanṟi nalgān* – He will never offer the invigorating tiruttuḻāy which is fittingly placed on his boundlessly reliśable divine feet, to others. śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 37.57 “*mayi jīvitam āyattam rāghavasya mahātmana:*” (My life is dedicated to śrī rāma, his brothers and the dynasty) – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) made himself and his belongings to exist for me. She is not thinking about self and speaking like this; but she is thinking about emperumān’s nature and speaking like this; he spoke like this in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 18.25 “*kim puna: mad vidōjana:*” (How much more should I do for those who surrender unto me) \[śrī rāma explains to sugrīva and his associates that a female pigeon gave its life to feed a hungry hunter who previously hunted its male companion\]. During the final moments of [aruḷāḷap perumāḷ emperumānār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/arulala-perumal-emperumanar/), he was asked “what are you thinking about now?”; he replied “I am thinking about how a bird hurt the feelings of perumāḷ (śrī rāma)”. For this, [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/) mercifully explains – Our act of surrender is not going to get us the result; yet, due to the great qualities of emperumān who accepts our surrender, we have no shortcoming. (Hurting the feelings of perumāḷ is explained as – when śrī vibhīśaṇa surrendered to perumāḷ, instead of accepting him at once, there was a delay and others wanted him to be killed too – this caused great hurt in [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s divine heart where he thought “I could not even do what a pigeon who does (save the surrendered person)”.
- *namakku anṟi nalgān* – He will not enjoy the sweet tuḷasi alone.
- *kanmingaḷ enṟu ummai yān kaṟpiyā vaitta* – When the heart is stable, she will teach them what sustains her. Just as our ācāryas would teach dvayam to their children, grand children et al. I who am the protector, taught you who are the protected.
- *māṟṟam* – That is – what I taught you always saying “*namakku anṟi nalgān*“, or what I taught saying that you ask him “*iduvō takkavāṟu*“.
- *sollic cenmingaḷ* – This is what you have as company for your journey; don’t become dumbfounded when you reach there. Don’t wait until he starts speaking about it, you inform him as soon as you reach there.
- *tī vinaiyēn* – forget about you going there, speaking to him, his arrival etc; see my sin – I have become like the one who lost one’s child. Instead of him and I both being together, celebrating you, I am sinful enough to get my desire fulfilled through you. There is nothing inferior to sending one’s own children to bring over the one who is very dear \[Here, the birds are considered as [parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s children, and [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) as her consort\].

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.
