## 6.8.7. Puvaigal

*pūvaigaḷ pōl niṟattan puṇḍarīgangaḷ pōlum kaṇṇan yāvaiyum yāvarumāy ninṟa māyan en āḻippirān māvai val vāy piḷanda madusūdaṟken māṟṟanjolli pāvaigaḷ! tīrkkiṟṟirē vinaiyāttiyēn pāsaṟavē*

**Пословный перевод:**

pūvaigaḷ pōl – (beautiful) like pūvaippū (blue coloured flower); niṟattan – having complexion; puṇḍarīgangaḷ pōlum – like lotus flowers; kaṇṇan – having eyes; yāvaiyum – all acētanas (insentient objects); yāvarum – all cētanas (sentient beings); āy – having as body/form, in those forms; ninṟa – being untouched by their defects; māyan – (while being amazingly present everywhere) being able to be aloof; en āḻip pirān – the great benefactor who let me enjoy his beautiful combination of hand and divine chakra (disc), earlier; māvai – kēśi, the horse (who was a hurdle for the gōpikās who were enjoying him); val – very strong; vāy – mouth; piḷanda – one who tore; madusūdaṟku – for madusūdana (who is naturally the eliminator of enemies); en māṟṟam – the words I taught to the parrots and mynās; solli – telling; pāvaigaḷ – Oh dolls (who remain here unable to bear my sorrow, unlike the birds who flew away)!; vinaiyāttiyēn – me who is sinful to be forced to get my desire fulfilled through you; pāsaṟavu – loss of fresh complexion; tīrkkiṟṟirē – can you remedy?

**Перевод:**

**emperumān is having complexion like pūvaip pū and eyes like lotus;  he is able to remain aloof while having all acētanas and cētanas as body/form, and remaining untouched by their defects in those forms; he is the great benefactor who let me enjoy his beautiful combination of hand and divine chakra (disc), earlier; he is madusūdana who tore the very strong mouth of kēśi, the horse; oh dolls! I am sinful to be forced to get my desire fulfilled through you. Telling him the words I taught to the parrots and mynās, can you remedy my loss of fresh complexion?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the seventh pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki thinks “if we sent cētanas \[sentient – birds etc\] as messengers, it is not helping the cause and they are abandoning me like emperumān due to their having knowledge” and prays to her dolls “can you eliminate my sorrow?”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, parānguśa nāyaki our of her great sorrow tells some dolls ignoring that they are acētanas (insentient) “Can you remedy my pale complexion by informing my words to emperumān who is very beautiful, indvelling soul of all and the one who eliminates the hurdles of his devotees?”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. She has become so desperate and helpless that she thinks even a doll can help her. pūvaigaḷ pōl niṟattan puṇḍarīgangaḷ pōlum kaṇṇan yāvaiyum yāvarumāy ninṟa māyan en āḻippirān māvai val vāy piḷanda madusūdaṟken māṟṟanjolli pāvaigaḷ! tīrkkiṟṟirē vinaiyāttiyēn pāsaṟavē*

- *pūvaigaḷ pōl niṟattan* – He has such beautiful complexion which makes a man become woman to pursue him. As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 3.29 “*pumsām druśti cittāpahāriṇam*” (śrī rāma’s beauty will attract the eyes and mind of even men). He has such beauty that one will even fall at the feet of a doll to attain him. One who has the complexion of pūvaippū.
- *puṇḍarīgangaḷ pōlum kaṇṇan* – His body and eyes appear to be a flower growing out of another flower \[as his divine body is compared to a flower too\]; it appears that a lotus flower grew out of kāyāmpū (pūvaippū). He has such beautiful eyes which make every [cētana](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) and [acētana](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/09/thathva-thrayam-achith-what-is-matter/) fall at his feet.
- *yāvaiyum yāvarumāy ninṟa māyan* – When he pervades some \[all\], he becomes them. The one who remains the in-dwelling soul of cētanas and acētanas. taittirīya upaniśat “*tatsruśtvā tadēvānuprāviśat tadanupraviśya saccatyaccābhavat*” (He created everything and entered in them; by pervading them, he became the sentient and insentient entities); one who becomes indistinguishable when uniting \[with his dear ones\].
- *māyan* – While mingling in such manner, he remains without acquiring any blemish; while being the antaryāmi (in-dwelling soul) of all, being untouched by their blemishes as said in rig vēdam “*anaśnannanyō abhiśākaśīti*” (paramātmā who is different from jīvātmā is shining radiantly due to not experiencing the results of actions). While having the whole jagat (universe) as his body and being inseparable from them, he is untouched by the transformational quality of acit (matter) and the aspect of going through joy/sorrow by cit (soul). Here she is saying *“yāvaiyum yāvarumāy ninṟa māyan*” to indicate that just as he united with her and still remained aloof, he is present in all [cētanas](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) and [acētanas](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/09/thathva-thrayam-achith-what-is-matter/) yet being untouched by their blemishes; otherwise this is not required for the current context \[of explaining her separation\].

Now she is explaining the difference between “*aḻukkup paditta udambu*” (his material body – i.e., all cētanas and acētanas) and “*paranjudar udambu*” (spiritual body, the divine form) \[as indicated in [tiruvāimoḻi 6.3.7](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/11/thiruvaimozhi-6-3-7-paranjudar-udambay/) \].

- *en āḻip pirān* – One who presented his distinguished form to me. After saying “*yāvaiyum yāvarumāy ninṟu*“, she is saying “*en āḻip pirān*“; this is how she became involved in his divine form. \[Similarly\] He himself said in tiruvāimoḻi 6.9.1 “*nīrāy nilanāy*” (one who became water, earth etc) and then said “*kūrār āḻi veṇ sangēndi adiyēn pāl vārāy*” (you come to me carrying your sharp chakra (disc) and white Sanka (conch)). Except for the fact that everything is pervaded by [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) and so he is called us “jagat śarīra” (one who has the universe as his body), would the samsāram be as desirable as his divine form? That is why his divine form is praised as  being opposite of all blemishes as in “*paranjudar udambu*” (spiritual body, the divine form) and the universe is explained as mixed with blemishes as in “*aḻukkup paditta udambu*” (his material body – i.e., all [cētanas](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) and [acētanas](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/09/thathva-thrayam-achith-what-is-matter/)) .
- *māvai …* – Whatever comes as a hurdle to enjoy his beauty, he eliminates them; and that does not happen just occasionally \[but always\].
- *madusūdaṟku* – His eliminating of enemies is perpetual and not accidental like alphabets being formed as a worm crawls.
- *en māṟṟam solli* – Whatever I have taught you.
- *pāvaigaḷ tīrkiṟṟirē* – The [paramacētanan (supreme sentient)](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) has abandoned me; these birds who have caitanyam (consciousness) have not done the job; now, can you eradicate my sorrow? She is trying to get her task done considering their inseparable nature only.
- *vinaiyāttiyēn* – I have attained the sorrow of getting you to fulfil my desire instead of praising you; I have become greatly sinful to try and eliminate my sorrow which was caused by [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who said in [śrī bhagavat gītā](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/contents/) 18.66 “*mā śuca:”* (do not grieve), with the help of [acētanas](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/09/thathva-thrayam-achith-what-is-matter/) (insentient entities). pāsaṟavu – sorrow.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.8.8. Pasaraveydi

*pāsaṟaveydi innē vinaiyēn enai ūḻi naivēn? āsaṟu tūvi veḷḷaik kurugē! aruḷ seydoru nāḷ māsaṟu neelac cudar mudi vānavar kōnaik kaṇḍu ēsaṟum nummai allāl maṟu nōkkilaḷ pērttu maṟṟē*

**Пословный перевод:**

āsu – any shortcoming in flying; aṟu – not having; tūvi – having wings; veḷḷai – having white colour which reflects the internal purity; kurugē – Oh heron!; vinaiyēn – I who am sinful not seeing the end of this suffering in separation; pāsaṟavu eydi – losing my complexion; innē – in this manner; enai ūḻi – many kalpa (day of brahmā); naivēn – will remain broken; māsu – fault; aṟu – not having; neelac cudar – having blue radiance; mudi – having hair; vānavar – for nityasūris; kōnai – the supreme lord, who is the leader; kaṇḍu – on seeing; ēsu – blemish; aṟum – not having; nummai – you; allāl – other than; pērttu – further; maṟṟu – other; maṟu nōkkilaḷ – not having the option to see; oru nāḷ – one day; aruḷ sey – give your mercy

**Перевод:**

**Oh heron which is having wings which have no shortcoming in flying and are white in colour reflecting the internal purity! I who am sinful in not seeing the end of this suffering in separation, will remain broken for many kalpa, losing my complexion in this manner; on seeing the supreme lord, who is having faultless hair with blue radiance and who is the leader of nityasūris, you should give your mercy one day by saying to him “\[for parānguśa nāyaki\] there is no option to see, other than you who are free from any blemish”.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the eighth pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki mercifully says to a heron which is in front of her “Tell him that there is a girl who cannot sustain herself without you, like nityasūris (eternal residents of paramapadam) and is suffering due to not having attained you”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, parānguśa nāyaki prays to a heron “Tell him that there is a girl who does not look for anything other than you, the supreme lord who is served by nityasūris and hence you should bestow your mercy upon her for a day”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. pāsaṟaveydi innē vinaiyēn enai ūḻi naivēn? āsaṟu tūvi veḷḷaik kurugē! aruḷ seydoru nāḷ māsaṟu neelac cudar mudi vānavar kōnaik kaṇḍu ēsaṟum nummai allāl maṟu nōkkilaḷ pērttu maṟṟē*

- *pāsaṟavu* … – Am I in a state where it can be thought “let us wait for some more time to inform him”?
- *pāsaṟavu eydi* – pāsu means freshness; which implies nīrmai (good complexion), losing that means, becoming pale.
- *innē* – When asked “how did you acquire this pale complexion?”, she says – I don’t need to explain to you who are already seeing me. Only if an object is of limited nature, this \[suffering\] will be limited. I cannot explain my suffering in words; I can only show my body. Being unable to explain it through words, she is pointing to her body.
- *vinaiyēn* – My viślēśam (separation) from him is not the same as the samślēśam (union) with him; that (samślēśam) is occasional; this (viślēśam) is perpetual.
- *vinaiyēn* – I am sinful not to withdraw from him when there is no opportunity to be with him.
- *enai ūḻi naivēn* – How many kalpa can I spend in this broken state? Those who separated previously only had to wait for fourteen years \[bharatāḻvān\], ten months \[sītāp pirātti\] etc.
- *āsaṟu tūvi veḷḷaik kurugē* – Having unblemiśed wings, and pure mind/heart which will not let you bear others’ sufferings.
- *veḷḷaik kurugē* – Just like he is dark inside and outside \[i.e., having cruel heart\] to separate from me, you are white inside and outside to unite me with him.
- *aruḷ seydu oru nāḷ* – Shower your mercy once. There is no greater mercy that showing your presence here; you did this purely out of your mercy.
- *māsaṟu* … –  Seeing him who is having blemiśless, shining hair cared for / enjoyed by nityasūris \[she is saying this with grief\]. This is similar to a cloud which is pouring rain on the ocean while there is a \[dry\] lake \[which would feed many\].
- *ēsaṟum* – She is suffering; also implies that she has gone beyond the state of worrying for people’s accusations.  Also implies – show your form. That is, you assume my pale complexion on your form and show it to him.
- *nummai allāl maṟu nōkkilaḷ* – There is no other cooler eyes than yours. Even to share my story, there is none other than you \[for her\]; even the state explained in “*sakībissukamāsva*” (be happy with your friends) has been crossed.
- *nummai allāl* – She cannot bear even if someone is sent in advance saying [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is coming as in the case of śrī bharatāḻvān \[hanuman came ahead to announce the arrival of śrī rāma\].
- *nummai allāl* – She cannot sustain herself by meditating about the qualities of your true nature \[She can only sustain herself when she sees your divine form\].
- *maṟu nōkkilaḷ* – She has even crossed the state of being cared by the relatives \[she has given up all of them\] and only you can do it.

There is no verb \[action word/phrase\] in this pāsuram \[for the heron\]. It should be assumed from previous pāsuram or next pāsuram. tamiḻ scholars explain this as “vinai eccam”. That is, “*maṟu nōkkilaḷ pēṟttu maṟṟē*” should be suffixed with “enṟu sollungōḷ” (you tell him).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.8.9. Perttu marru

*pērttu maṟṟōr kaḷaikaṇ vinaiyāttiyēn nān onṟilēn nīrttirai mēl ulavi irai tērum pudāvinangāḷ! kārttiraḷ mā mugil pōl kaṇṇan viṇṇavar kōnaik kaṇḍu vārttaigaḷ koṇḍaruḷi uraiyīr vaigal vandirundē*

**Пословный перевод:**

nīr – water’s; tirai – tide; mēl – on top; ulāvi – moving around; irai – prey (which is dear to you); tērum – searching; pudāvinangāḷ – oh big cranes!; vinaiyāttiyēn – having sin (since the one who is supposed to help, is not helping); nān – I; pērttu – other than you; maṟṟu – other; ōr – unique; kaḷaikaṇ – saviour; onṟu – one; ilēn – not having; kār – in rainy season; tiraḷ – gathered; mā mugil pōl – (beautiful) like huge clouds; kaṇṇan – very obedient to his devotees through his incarnation; viṇṇavar – letting (such beauty) to be enjoyed by the residents of paramapadam; kōnai – the supreme lord; kaṇḍu – on seeing; vārttaigaḷ – (his merciful) message; koṇḍu – bringing; aruḷi – showering that mercy upon me; vandu irundu – coming and residing here; vaigal – for a long time (to have this as our activity); uraiyīr – speak

**Перевод:**

**Oh big cranes who are moving around atop the water suppressing the tide, in search of prey! I who am having sin, not having any other saviour than you the unique ones; on seeing the supreme lord who is like huge clouds gathered during rainy season, who is very obedient to his devotees through his incarnation, and who is letting (such beauty) to be enjoyed by the residents of paramapadam, bring his message and shower your mercy upon me , come and reside here, and speak for a long time.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the ninth pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki says to some big cranes “When you go to emperumān, even if he does not come here, you can bring his message from there to me and repeat that everyday to sustain me”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. pērttu maṟṟōr kaḷaikaṇ vinaiyāttiyēn nān onṟilēn nīrttirai mēl ulavi irai tērum pudāvinangāḷ! kārttiraḷ mā mugil pōl kaṇṇan viṇṇavar kōnaik kaṇḍu vārttaigaḷ koṇḍaruḷi uraiyīr vaigal vandirundē*

- *pērttu maṟṟōr kaḷaikaṇ vinaiyāttiyēn nān onṟilēn* – She has crossed the state of passing her time along with her associates. Even towards his devotees, one should manifest his hollowness. I have no other saviour than you.
- *maṟṟu ōr kaḷaikaṇ* – For sītāp pirātti, even in lankā, she had trijadā; even when she was left alone in the forest, there was vālmīkī bhagavān; when the husband abandons, one should at the least have a father \[she does not have any one\].
- *vinaiyāttiyēn* – Usually the husband will be the saviour; I am so sinful to have such husband abandon me.
- *nīrt tirai mēl ulavi* – The cranes are capable of crossing over the ocean surrounding the universe and the virajā river \[which is the boundary between spiritual realm and material realm\].
- *ulavi* – They are moving around water as they would do on land.
- *irai tērum* – Just like their walk, their search for prey is also complete.  While I am fasting here \[not having [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)\], you cannot consume your food; I will sustain only when I too have food like you.
- *pudā* – big crane.
- *kārt tiraḷ mā mugil pōl kaṇṇan* – All the fatigue will be removed when his divine form is  seen! For her eyes – everything appears black. One who appears like a cluster of blackness; also said as a great cloud gathered around in rainy season.
- mā mugil – The cloud which can give continuously.
- *kaṇṇan* – His compassion inside the heart is \[white/pure\] unlike the black external form.
- *viṇṇavar kōnaik kaṇḍu* – While there are thirsty people here \[in material realm\], he is feeding water to fishes. On seeing the [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is presenting himself to nityasūris who have no scope for separation from him.
- *vārttaigaḷ koṇḍu* – Even if he does not come, he would have something to say. More than seeing him, you are going to hear his words.  [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is the one who says in [tiruvāimoḻi 4.7.3](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/03/thiruvaimozhi-4-7-3-iviladha-thivinaigal/) “*pāvi nī enṟu onṟu sollāy*” (you are not telling me that I am a sinner). Now [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) would even hear his words of refusal.

How can I wait forever to hear from you?

- *vārttaigaḷ – koṇḍaruḷi – vandirundu – vaigalum – uraiyīr* – You go to him once, hear his words, being merciful and come to me, uplift me forever by speaking about that to me! Alternative explanation – seeing kriṣṇa, the lord of nityasūris, hearing the words “*mā śuca:*” (do not worry) which lead to the result, show your compassion towards me  by coming here and share with me those words forever.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.8.10. Vandirundu

*vandirundu ummudaiya maṇic cēvalum nīrum ellām andaram onṟuminṟi alar mēl asaiyum annangāḷ! en tirumārvaṟku ennai innavāṟivaḷ kāṇmin enṟu mandirattonṟuṇartti uraiyīr maṟu māṟṟangaḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vandu – coming here (without any expectation); irundu – remaining here (with full focus); ummudaiya – your pleasant; maṇi – best; sēvalum – pairs; nīrum – you all; ellām – all the relatives; onṟum – any; andaram – hurdle; inṟi – without; alar mēl – on top of the flowers; asaiyum – moving around; annangāḷ – Oh swans!; em – lord for those girls like me; tiru – lakshmi; mārvaṟku – having in his chest; ennai – me; ivaḷ – she; innavāṟu – in this manner; ānāḷ – has become; kāṇmin – see; enṟu – saying that; mandirittu – in his (and her) private abode; onṟu – a word; uṇartti – informing him; maṟu māṟṟangaḷ – reply (he mercifully gives); uraiyīr – tell me

**Перевод:**

**Oh swans coming here and remaining here who are coming along with your pleasant, best pairs and relatives, and moving around atop the flowers without any hurdle! Go to the private abode of emperumān who is the lord for those girls like me, who is having lakshmi in his divine chest and tell him a word about me “see her situation and what she has become” and tell me his reply.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the tenth pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki says to swan couples which move around her “You go to the abode where emperumān and pirātti are privately enjoying, explain my situation and bring me a message”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, parānguśa nāyaki prays to some swans “Go to emperumān who is having śriya:patitvam (being the lord of śrīmahālakśmi) which is the cause for his supremacy and simplicity, tell him privately my situation, and bring me his message”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. vandirundu ummudaiya maṇic cēvalum nīrum ellām andaram onṟuminṟi alar mēl asaiyum annangāḷ! en tirumārvaṟku ennai innavāṟivaḷ kāṇmin enṟu mandirattonṟuṇartti uraiyīr maṟu māṟṟangaḷē*

- *vandirundu* – What a help in need! How kind-hearted you are! You did not have to be forcefully invited through iḷaiya perumāḷ \[as he angrily drew the attention of sugrīva\].
- *vandirundu* – Just as śrī rāma voluntarily went to sugrīva mahārāja, enquired his situation and provided a solution, you remained together during these sorrowful times.
- *ummudaiya maṇic cēvalum nīrum ellām* – Though ātmās assume different masculine and feminine forms in paramapadam, all of those forms are meant for service to lord \[not just for physical distinction\]; similarly, she considers these varieties \[swans, their pairs, relatives etc\] to be present to accomplish her task.
- *maṇic cēval* – What a beautiful \[male\] spouse! Her beautiful spouse \[[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)\] is staying away from her, making her become pale and still remains without any sorrow.
- *ellām* – As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam bāla kāṇḍam 1.99 “*sa putra pautras sagaṇa:*” (with children, grandchildren and relatives); like those who set out to help others along with wife, children et al.
- *andaram onṟum inṟi* – Unlike me who is having separation after union; not even having separation which leads to union.
- *alar mēl asaiyun annangāḷ* – You who are couples, are able to move atop flowers too. Your pride is such that you can step on flowers too. This is how you remain without any shortcoming.
- *en tirumārvaṟku* – Am I suffering due to lack of support for me there? As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 15.6 “*sītā samakśam kākutstam*” (He spoke to śrī rāma in the presence of sītāp [pirātti](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/)), you inform him where your words will become worthy; you approach him like I did.
- *ennai innavāṟu ivaḷ kāṇmin enṟu* – Her situation is beyond the scope of speech.
- *ennai* – me who desired to serve that divine couple. [nanjīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nanjiyar/) would mercifully explain “they can show her pale complexion in their body highlighting her pathetic situation”. Alternatively – tell him “Is she your privately vorśippable deity! isn’t she an associate \[of [periya pirātti](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/)\] in your private quarters?”. \[dēvāram\] arccai (deity at home) – is she totally dependent like vorśippable deity at home?
- *mandirattu onṟu uṇartti* – Don’t inform him in the grand assembly; there would be those who would say as in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 17-29 “*vadyatām*” (let vibhīśaṇan be killed). You inform him where her words will have value \[that is while [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) and [pirātti](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/) are enjoying together\].
- *uraiyīr māṟṟangaḷē* – When he replies without the same urge \[like me\], you, not being satisfied with that, inform in front of the one \[[pirātti](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/)\] who tells as in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 116-44 “*na kaścinnāparādyati*” (There is none who has not committed a sin).
- *mandiram* – praṇavam.
- *onṟu* – the middle portion in it \[ukāram\]; informing my ananyārhatai (not existing for anyone else).
- *uraiyīr maṟu māṟṟangaḷē* – Hearing the words speak seeing my previous offenses, and the words she speak on seeing our relationship and my situation, and inform them to me.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.8.11. Marrangal

*māṟṟangaḷ āyndu koṇḍu madusūda pirān adi mēl nāṟṟangoḷ pūmpoḻil sūḻ kurugūrccatakōpan sonna tōṟṟangaḷ āyirattuḷ ivaiyum ōr pattum vallār ūṟṟin kaṇ nuṇ maṇal pōl urugā niṟpar nīrāyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

māṟṟangaḷ – distinguished words; āyndu koṇḍu – analysing; madusūdan – one who destroyed madu who robbed the vēdam which is the cause for knowledge; pirān – benefactor’s; adi mēl – on the divine feet; nāṟṟam koḷ – with fragrance; pū – having flower; poḻil – gardens; sūḻ – surrounded by; kurugūr – leader of āḻvārtirunagari; satakōpan – āḻvār who won over bāhya (those who reject vēdam) and kudruśti (those who misinterpret vēdam) philosophers; sonna – mercifully spoke; tōṟṟangaḷ – incarnation of vēdam like bhagavān’s incarnations; āyirattuḷ – among the thousand pāsurams; oru – unique; ivai – these; pattum – ten pāsurams; vallār – those who can recite with meditation; ūṟṟinkaṇ – in a spring; nuṇ – tiny; maṇal pōl – like sand particles (which will get sucked in due to the water); nīrāy urugā niṟpar – (with overwhelming emotions) will melt

**Перевод:**

**āḻvār, the leader of āḻvārtirunagari, which is surrounded by fragrant flower filled gardens, who won over bāhya and kudruśti philosophers, analysing with distinguished words, mercifully spoke these ten pāsurams among the thousand pāsurams which are incarnation of vēdam like bhagavān’s incarnations, on the divine feet of the benefactor who destroyed madu who robbed the vēdam which is the cause for knowledge; those who can recite with meditation, will melt like tiny sand particles in a spring.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the end, āḻvār says “Those who meditate upon my sorrow in this decad, will melt like tiny sand particles in a spring (ground water source)”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār explains the result of this decad “Those who recite this decad, due to having great love towards its meanings, will have the nature of fluid”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. māṟṟangaḷ āyndu koṇḍu madusūda pirān adi mēl nāṟṟangoḷ pūmpoḻil sūḻ kurugūrccatakōpan sonna tōṟṟangaḷ āyirattuḷ ivaiyum ōr pattum vallār ūṟṟin kaṇ nuṇ maṇal pōl urugā niṟpar nīrāyē*

- *māṟṟangaḷ āyndu koṇḍu* – For those who are drenched in devotion, like for those who are climbing hills, cannot speak/sing coherently; the words themselves become aligned properly; through noble words.
- *madusūda pirān adi mēl* – On the divine feet of the one who has virōdi nirasanam (elimination of enemies) as a natural attribute.
- *nāṟṟam koḷ …* – The gardens too became evergreen as [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) sustained himself thinking “We will surely succeed as we have sent a messenger to his private quarters”. [āḻvārtirunagari](http://azhwarthirunagari.koyil.org/) surrounded by gardens filled with fragrant flowers.
- *tōṟṟangaḷ āyiram* – They are not spoken as said in “*mana:pūrvō vāguttara:*” (first in mind, then in speech) \[they were spontaneously spoken by the grace of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)\]. Though he spoke with bewilderment, they appeared like bhagavān’s incarnations. tōṟṟam – āvirbhāvam (incarnation). Just as riśis will see the mantrams \[through their internal vision\]. As said in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.10.11](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/10/thiruvaimozhi-1-10-11-maniyai-vanavar/) “*sol paṇi sey āyiram*” (the thousand pāsurams served by words), entering [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s speech, words thought “let me enter āḻvār’s speech, be born there, serve āḻvār purely”, request āḻvār saying “accept me! accept me!”. The blemish of entering the speeches of avaidikas is removed only now. As they have now been used by āḻvār, past and future blemishes for the words will be eliminated as said in [tiruppāvai 5](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2014/12/thiruppavai-05-mayanai/) “*pōya piḻaiyum pugutaruvān ninṟanavum tīyinil tūsāgum*” (previous sins and future sins will be eliminated just as cotton is burnt down to ashes by fire),
- *ūṟṟinkaṇ* … – These pāsurams have not been learnt before \[[āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) only revealed them\]. That is, āḻvār is saying “with my sorrowful cry, I have melted the whole world”. \[Explaining the present tense in “urugā niṟpar”\] āḻvār’s sorrow will end when [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) appears in front of him; but since these pāsurams are eternal, those who hear them, will not be able sustain themselves; they will melt like tiny sand particles in a spring, and become broken-hearted. What is the result of this? As melting on hearing the words of great devotees of [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is also part of the goal, this itself (melting) is the result \[for this decad\].

In the next article we will enjoy the next decad.

## 6.9 Niray nilanay

## 6.9.1. Niray nilanay

*nīrāy nilanāyt tīyāyk kālāy nedu vānāy sīrār sudargaḷ iraṇḍāy sivanāy ayan ānāy kūrār āḻi veṇ sangēndik kodiyēnpāl vārāy! oru nāḷ maṇṇum viṇṇum magiḻavē*

**Пословный перевод:**

nīr – having importance as said in manu smruti “apa Eva sasarjātau” (He first created water); āy – having as body; nilan – earth (which is an effect of water); āy – having as body; tī – fire (which is the cause for both water and earth, which is given great importance in cāndōjña upaniśat); āy – having as body; kāl – air (which is the cause for fire); āy – having as body; nedu – very expansive; vān – ether; with all these, the samaśti (initial creation); āy – create, enter inside and be the antaryāmi for them; sīrār – being the primary person for vyaśti sruśti (variegated creation) (as said in “sūryā candramasau dātā yatāpūrvamakalpayat” (Sun, moon etc get created as before by the lord); iraṇḍu sudargaḷ – moon and sun (benefactors due to providing heat and coolness); āy – having as body; sivan – rudra; āy – having as body; ayan – brahmā; ānāy – Oh one who is having them as body by being their antarātmā (indvelling soul)!; kūr – sharpness (in eliminating the enemies); Ar – having; āḻi – divine chakra (disc); veṇ – having pure white complexion (which is enjoyable for the devotees); sangu – śrī pāncajanyam (the divine conch); ēndi – holding; maṇṇum – leelā vibhūti (material realm) which is highlighted by the earth; viṇṇum – nitya vibhūti which is highlighted by the term “parama vyōma” (supreme sky); magiḻa – to be delighted; kodiyēnpāl – for I who am having cruelty (of forcing you to show your distinguished form); oru nāḷ – at least on one day; vārāy – should arrive

**Перевод:**

**Oh emperumān who is having water which is having importance as said in manu smruti “apa Eva sasarjātau“, earth, fire, air and the very expansive ether as his body as part of the samaśti sruśti, creating them, entering inside them and being the antaryāmi for them! Oh one who is the primary person for vyaśti sruśti, having moon and sun as his body! Oh one who is having rudra and brahmā as body by being their antarātmā! You should arrive at least on one day for me who am having cruelty and to the delight of leelā vibhūti and nitya vibhūti, holding the divine chakra which is having sharpness and śrī pāncajanyam which is having pure white complexion.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the first pāsuram,  emperumān says “I have shown my universal form”  and āḻvār replies “that is not sufficient, I want to see your distinguished form”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*In the first pāsuram, āḻvār says “You who are having the entire cosmos as your body, should appear with your distinguished symbols”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. nīrāy nilanāyt tīyāyk kālāy nedu vānāy sīrār sudargaḷ iraṇḍāy sivanāy ayan ānāy kūrār āḻi veṇ sangēndik kodiyēnpāl vārāy! oru nāḷ maṇṇum viṇṇum magiḻavē*

- *nīray nilanāy …* – āḻvār is praying to emperumān with what he knows already, so that emperumān does not think that āḻvār is desiring for him without knowing the truth.
- *nīrāy* – He says that he already knew that emperumān is nārāyaṇa (one who resides in water). He previously said in tiruvāimoḻi 1.1.10 “*nīrtoṟum paranduḷan*” (he is pervading every water droplet).
- *nīrāy* – As said in manu smruti “*apa Eva sasarjātau*” (He first created water), he first created water and subsequently created land etc; while using them (five great elements) \[in pancīkaraṇam, for further creation of the oval shaped universes\], more of the yet to be created ones are required than the already created ones. Creation is done as said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 1.2.54 “*samētya anyōnya samyōgam paraspara samāśraya:*” (five great elements with each other; they are related to each other); they are not a single element; while they are being several individual elements they should be combined into a single element and used further; while doing that, just as a potter would mix soil, water and mud, beat them well, and would create pots etc, emperumān would first create water, and since it is fluid, would mix land which is firm, with it, and as it is still not tight, would create fire to harden it, and since it starts burning, would create air to dry it, and would finally create ether to provide space for air to move around. Up until this point, he created the oval shaped universe, with his pratama sankalpam (first vow); now after creating a huge mansion, it cannot be left in darkness; so he created moon and sun as two lamps. Both sun and moon were created to deal with removing wetness and keeping cool respectively.
- *sivanāy ayanānāy* – Created brahmā and rudra to remain inside the universe and manage creation and annihilation. Why is rudra highlighted first? That is because annihilation precedes creation always. As “*nīrāy nilanāy*” and “*sīrār sudargaḷ iraṇḍāy*” are read along the same lines, it is clear that both cētana (sentient beings) and acētana (insentient objects) are subservient to bhagavān just like body is to soul as said in bruhadāraṇyaka upaniśat “*yasya ātmā śarīram, yasya prutivī śarīram*” (for the one who has Souls as his body, for the one who has earth etc as his body). As “*sīrār sudargaḷ iraṇḍāy*” and “*sivanāy ayanānāy*” are read along the same lines, it is explained that both the controlled entities and those who consider themselves as controllers are both subservient to bhagavān; \[āḻvār thinks\] ḍidn’t emperumān perform jagat sruśti (creation) for my purpose? Only if you did some favour me, your action is purposeful! The purpose of sruśti is to place the eternally sorrowful ātmā in the abode of unlimited bliss. While that is the case, should you not attain the purpose of your creation? By saying “*nīrāy nilanāyt tīyāyk kālāy neduvānāyc cīrār sudargaḷ iraṇḍāy sivanāy ayanānāy*“, it is clear that he recollects īśvara’s wealth similar to someone counting to the digit.
- *kūrār āḻi veṇ sangēndi* – śrī chakra’s sharpness is as desirable as the whiteness of the śrī pāncajanyam for āḻvār.
- *kūrār āḻi* – śrī chakra’s sharpness increases as it destroys the enemies. The identification of his beautiful form is the combination of his divine hand and divine chakra.
- *kodiyēn* – I am forced to such situation! What I am doing is contrary to my true nature! I have not got the nature of śrī bharatāḻvān who stayed back in ayōdyā when śrī rāma told him to do so; I have got the nature of iḷaiya perumāḷ (lakśmaṇa) who forced śrī rāma saying “*kuruśva*” (you should accept me as your servitor and order), when śrī rāma told him to stay put in ayōdyā!
- *vārāy* – Even if desired only those who are able, can walk along;

When you say “vārāy”, should he keep coming!

- *oru nāḷ* – (to sustain me.) As a very thirsty person would say “just quench my thirst once”.
- *maṇṇum viṇṇum magiḻavē* – Even if you don’t come for me, you come to ensure that your wealth does not get finished. If you remain thinking “why should I do anything if this material realm gets finished, like the decorations during navarātri utsavam get recreated every year?”, your spiritual realm will also be finished; when this realm gets finished, that too will be considered as finished; even while the spiritual realm was there, during the annihilation phase of this material realm, it was said as in “*sa ēkākī na ramēta*” (that supreme lord was unhappy feeling loneliness). When it says that the spiritual realm will not be finished during praḷayam (in material realm), it does not mean that the spiritual realm will not be finished for my sorrow.
- magiḻavē – to avert the destruction and survive.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.9.2. Mannum vinnum

*maṇṇum viṇṇum magiḻak kuṟaḷāy valangātti maṇṇum viṇṇum koṇḍa māya ammānē! naṇṇi unai nān kaṇḍugandu kūttāda naṇṇi oru nāḷ jñālattūdē nadavāyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

maṇṇum – earth; viṇṇum – the higher worlds; magiḻa – to the delight; kuṟaḷāy – as vāmana (who shrunk his huge form); valam – the omnipotency; kātti – manifesting; maṇṇum – earth; viṇṇum – the higher worlds; koṇḍa – measured; māyam – having amazing activity; ammānē – Oh lord!; unai – you (who are having beauty which was manifested to those with ulterior motives); nān – I (who am having the extreme desire ); naṇṇi – reaching (with that beauty); kaṇḍu – (not just through internal vision but ) physically seeing; ugandu – being pleased; kūttāda – to dance; naṇṇi – arrive here (just as you arrived at the sacrificial arena; oru nāḷ – one day; jñālattūdē – in the earth; nadavāy – should walk

**Перевод:**

**Oh lord who manifested as vāmana to the delight of earth and the higher worlds and who manifested amazing omnipotency by measuring the earth and higher planets! You should arrive one day on the earth and walk here, so that I can reach you and physically see you to my delight and to make me dance.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In second pāsuram, emperumān says “I will do as you say in paramapadam (spiritual realm) only” and āḻvār replies “āren’t you the one who manifested your beauty to be enjoyed by everyone, by mercifully taking birth in this samsāram (material realm) as śrī vāmana? So, you should mercifully fulfil my desire right here”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “You who are having amazing power of reinstating undisputed ownership of the entire universe by manifesting your beauty to mahābali, should arrive here to my delight”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. maṇṇum viṇṇum magiḻak kuṟaḷāy valangātti maṇṇum viṇṇum koṇḍa māya ammānē! naṇṇi unai nān kaṇḍugandu kūttāda naṇṇi oru nāḷ jñālattūdē nadavāyē*

- *maṇṇum viṇṇum magiḻak kuṟaḷāy* – To the extent that both the realms would have been finished had you not appeared as śrī vāmana, you appeared to the delight of even the unfavourable ones just as all the entities will freshen up with a heavy rainfall.
- *valam kātti* – Since mahābali had a little bit of audārya (magnanimity), he could not be killed by arrows like emperumān did to rāvaṇa et al; so [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) stunned him with the strength of his beauty. Even while śukrācārya et al were trying to stop, mahābali was won over by the beauty and was offering \[what vāmana asked\].
- *kuṟaḷāy* – He had become very small to be easily enjoyed, just like huge measurement was shrunk into a small measurement \[without losing the essence\].
- *maṇṇum viṇṇum koṇḍa* – One who placed earth and the sky under his feet. Instead of saying it was given to indra, here it is said that he took it because – since mahābali is demoniac in nature, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) took it himself (instead of accepting from mahābali) and since his devotee indra and emperumān are inseparable.
- *māya ammānē* – Here, the following amazing aspects are implied – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) being the divine consort of śrī mahālakśmi \[wealth personified\] and still prayed to mahābali; stunning mahābali with his beauty, speaking incoherently like a child as said in “*koḷvan nān māvali*” (mahābali! I will accept), showing little feet first and while accepting the offering enlarging the feet etc.
- *ammānē* – Wasn’t it his normal lordship as explained in jitantē stōtram 2 “*dēvānām dānavām ca sāmānyamadidaivatam*” ([emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is equal toward dēvas \[celestial persons\] and demons) that made him do that?
- *naṇṇi unai nān kaṇḍu ugandu kūttāda* – Unlike indra et al, I have no desire for kingdom! I won’t become satisfied with the worldly favours you have done. You have to arrive to make me dance on seeing you. It is his responsibility to come here; [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s only responsibility is to become joyful on his arrival.
- *nān kaṇu ugandu kūttāda* – I am unlike mahābali who had something to give; and I am unlike indra who was waiting to accept something from you; would you only interact and give/accept things with those who claim “mine” and “for me”? Could you not manifest yourself to those who become joyful only on seeing you? [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is only interested in what is explained in mahābhāratam udyōga parvam “*sambramais tuśya gōvinda ētanna: paramam danam*” (vidura says – Oh kriṣṇa! You become joyful seeing our nervousness \[on seeing you\]; this is our biggest wealth).
- *naṇṇi* – You must arrive where I am located.
- *oru nāḷ* – Should you not do this again once more? Would you only walk to the delight of earth and sky, in front of an asura (demon)? Could you not do that in front of an ananya:prayōjana (one who has no desire other than seeing you)?
- *jñālattūdē nadavāyē* – Should you walk in front of mahābali who manifested his magnanimity instead of enjoying your beautiful walk? Could you not walk in front of me who sustains only by your internal and external beauty of your walk?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

adiyen saraty ramanuja dasan

## 6.9.3. Jnalattude

*jñālattūdē nadandum ninṟum kidandirundum sālap pala nāḷ ugandōṟuyirgaḷ kāppānē! kōlat tirumāmagaḷōdu unnaik kūdādē sālap pala nāḷ adiyēn innum taḷarvēnō?*

**Пословный перевод:**

ugandōṟu – every yuga; jñālattūdē – descending on earth; nadandum – mercifully walked as said in “cacāra vasudātalē”; ninṟum – stood (holding the bow with the arrow ready to be launched as said in “avaśtabya ca tiśtantam dadarśa danurūrjitam“); kidandum – mercifully rested (like an ocean in front of another ocean as said in “pratiśiśyē mahōdadē:“); irundum – being nicely seated along with pirātti (as said in “ēvam āstē sa darmātmā sītayā saharāghava:“); sālap pala nāḷ – for a long time (as said in “daśa varśa sahasrāṇi daśa varśa śatāni ca“); uyirgaḷ – creatures; kāppānē – Oh one who protects!; kōlam – one who appears matching your beautiful form as said in “viṣṇōr dēhānurūpām vai karōtyēśā’tmanastanūm”; tiru mā magaḷōdu – with lakshmi; unnai – you; kūdādē – without reaching and enjoying; sālap pala nāḷ – for the times to come; adiyēn – I (who knows our \[lord-servant\] relationship); innum – even after acquiring the taste \[for bhagavat viśayam\]; taḷarvēnō – should I suffer due to not acquiring the experience?

**Перевод:**

**Oh one who protected creatures for a long time by descending on earth every yuga and mercifully walking as said in “cacāra vasudātalē“, stood, mercifully rested and by being nicely seated along with pirātti! Without reaching and enjoying you along with lakshmi who appears matching your beautiful form as said in “viṣṇōr dēhānurūpām vai karōtyēśā”tmanastanūm” for the times to come, should I suffer due to not acquiring the experience, even after acquiring the taste?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the third pāsuram, āḻvār says “Instead of considering that you have taken an incarnation like that \[referring to vāmana avatāram\] by chance, you have the natural quality of protecting the universe by manifesting different heart captivating activities during rāma, kriṣṇa et al incarnations in every yuga; why should I suffer for such a long time, without seeing you?”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “You are having activities which are meant for the protection of devotees in all manners; would I suffer forever without enjoying you along with your divine consort lakshmi?”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*āḻvār says “It is not sufficient that you have manifested your universal form; you should manifest your distinguished form”; emperumān says “I will manifest that to you in the special abode of paramapadam”; āḻvār replies “did you not manifest that in a worldly form before?”; emperumān replies “that was like a flash flood which occurs rarely”; āḻvār says “You cannot say that to be rare as you have the natural quality of protecting in every yuga as rāma, kriṣṇa et al; why should I still suffer \[by not seeing your divine forms\]?”. jñālattūdē nadandum ninṟum kidandirundum sālap pala nāḷ ugandōṟuyirgaḷ kāppānē! kōlat tirumāmagaḷōdu unnaik kūdādē sālap pala nāḷ adiyēn innum taḷarvēnō?*

- *jñālattūdē nadandum* – The walk which is manifested in front of those \[residents of parampadam\] who constantly see him, is carried out in front of these worldly people who don’t even look at, even if [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) appears rarely! Like walking in front of a blind person. Walked as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 11.1 “*agrata: prayayau rāma:*” (śrī rāma walks first), mahābhāratam āraṇya parvam “*ata dāśaratirvīrō rāmōnāmamahābala: \| viṣṇurmānuśarūpēṇa cacāra vasudātalē*” (Subsequently, viṣṇu assumed a human form as the divine son of emperor daśarata, with great strength and with well known name śrī rāma, and roamed around on earth). A very good singer from North arrived in śrīrangam to worship the divine feet of śrīranganātan. That day being the tīrtavāri (the concluding day of brahmōtsavam), [āḻvār tiruvarangap perumāḷ araiyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/thiruvarangapperumal-araiyar/) sang [tirumālai](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/07/thirumalai/) in a melodious tune and praised [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) like taming an elephant and had him mesmerised; at that time araiyar requested emperumān “My lord! A very good devotee of yours has arrived from a distant place to worship your divine feet; you should accept him and honour him”. perumāḷ obliged and invited him through the arcaka; emperumān mercifully ordered the arcakas to perform tirukkaittala sēvai (arcakas carrying emperumān with their bare hands) from tiruppunnai tree \[the divine tree at the banks of candra puskhariṇi, the ceremonial pond inside the temple campus\] up to where the devotee was standing, for a few meters. On completing the act, emperumān mercifully asked “Is this sufficient for this devotee who has arrived from distant location?”; this is how emperumān should feel in his divine heart for my loss, and mercifully present himself to me to eliminate such suffering.
- *ninṟum* – śrī rāmāyaṇam kiśkintā kāṇḍam 19.25 “*avaśtabya ca tiśtantam dadarśa danurūrjitam \| rāmām rāmānujam caiva bartuścaivānujam śubhā*” (tārā \[vāli’s wife\] saw śrī rāma who was standing majestically holding the bow, along with lakśmaṇa and sugrīva) – tārā instead of blaming śrī rāma who killed her husband, said “Is it śrī rāma’s fault? How can one avoid eliminating the enemies of the one who took refuge? Had vāli remained favourable towards him, would he have not protected him as well? Just as a person who drowned in a lake which was dug to provide water, vāli got killed due to his own mistake!”. In this manner [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) stood with the bow in his hand in the most attractive manner to be praised even by the wives of those who were unfavourable towards him!
- *kidandum* – His lying down in front of the ocean appears to win over lankā as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 21.1 “*bāhum bhujagabhōgābham upadāyārisūdana*” (the annihilator of enemies, is having the hand resembling the body of a serpent as his pillow). śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 21.1 “*anjali prāng muka: krutvā pratiśiśyē mahōdadē*” (śrī rāma remained prostrated towards east direction with joined palms). “*pratiśiśyē*” – it appears that two oceans are present touching each other. The ocean thought itself as too great and to eliminate that pride [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) laid himself down as a competitor and hence it appeared that an ocean (of salt water) is present adjacent to another ocean (of mercy); as said in kamba rāmāyaṇam varuṇanai vaḻi vēṇḍu padalam 5 “*karuṇai am kadal tuyinṟanai karungadal nōkki*“.
- *irundum* – Seated as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 16.8 “*upaviśtam svalankrutam*” (one who is decorated and seated) and śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 99.25 “*utajē rāmām āsīnam*” (śrī rāma who was seated in the hermitage). \[second ślōkam is explained\] His secluded assembly \[in citrakūtam\] seems greater than his assembly in śrī ayōdyā. śrī bharatāḻvān who could approach him in that assembly in ayōdyā, could himself not approach śrī rāma in citrakūtam; \[same ślōkam\] “*apita:bhāvakōpamam*” (like being surrounded by fire) – as one cannot approach burning fire, śrī rāma remained unable to be overcome.
- *sālap pala nāḷ* – Is your protection not from time immemorial? Alternative meaning – has your protection not been going for hundred, thousand etc years?
- *ugandōṟu* – as said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 4.8](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/4-8/) “*sambhavāmi yugē yugē*” (I appear in every yuga).
- *uyirgaḷ* – Your protection is not only for tiruvadi (hanuman),  tiruvanantāḻvān (ādi śēśa) and pirātti (śrī mahālakhsmi), but for the well-being of all!
- *kāppānē* – Just as they have the nature of destroying themselves, he has the nature of protecting them. I have withdrawn; if you don’t want to be blamed for being careless in your guarding, you protect me. śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 25.33 “*rāma lakśmaṇa guptāsāsugrīvēṇa ca vāhinī*” (sugrīva along with his army was protected by śrī rāma and lakśmaṇa) – when everyone was on the seashore close to lankā to protect perumāḷ (śrī rāma), all leaders such as his own brother lakśmaṇa, sugrīva mahārāja, mainda, dvivida et al watched the sky and were guarding perumāḷ like those who protect their wealth; when they all fell asleep at one point, perumāḷ took up his bow and arrows, circled them and guarded them. One should just close his own eyes to be protected by [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/). Considering ourselves to be his guardians is only an illusion; when we truly realise, we will understand that he is the true protector.
- *kōlat tirumā magaḷōdu unnaik kūdādē* – It looks like a nursing baby which is struggling due to lack of milk, being unable to reach the mother and father who are in close proximity! For [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/), the goal is their divine togetherness as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 21.15 “*ananyā rāghavēṇāham”* (I am inseparable from śrī rāma).
- *innam taḷarvēnō – sālap palanāḷ* – While I have lost it since time immemorial, should I lose him again for unlimited time?
- *adiyēn* – While that is there, are you planning to abandon me saying “you lost because of yourself \[i.e., your lack of knowledge about our relationship\]”?
- *innam taḷarvēnō* – Should I suffer even after knowing that the divine couple is the goal? Not knowing “you are the protector”, considering “I have some other refuge”, considering “I can protect myself”, not knowing “the lord of lakshmi is the goal”, considering “I own myself” – did I do any of these to lose you? Can I lose you even after acquiring taste \[for you\]? With this pāsuram, the meaning of akāram (“a” in praṇavam) is sequentially elaborated.
   - “*ava – rakśaṇē*” is the dātu (root). While protecting, he should protect in all manners; he should protect at all times; while doing so, he should be the protector for all; while protecting like this without any restriction, the one (pirātti) who says as in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 116-44 “*na kaścinnāparādyati*” (There is none who has not committed a sin) and the one ([emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)) who says as in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 4.9.2 “*ennadiyār atu seyyār*” (My devotees would not do anything wrong) are present together; thus, akāram indicates the divine couple.
   - By “*jñālattūdē …*“, his protection in all manners is explained.
   - By “*sālap pala nāḷ …*“, his protection in all times is explained.
   - By “uyirgaḷ”, his protection for all is explained.
   - By “*kōlat tiru mā magaḷōdu unnaik kūda*“, śrīya:pati (lord of śrī mahālakśmi) is the goal, is explained.
   - \[Subsequently\] [tirumantram](http://ponnadi.blogspot.in/2015/12/rahasya-thrayam.html)‘s meaning \[i.e., [arta pancakam](http://ponnadi.blogspot.com/2015/12/artha-panchakam.html)\] which is the expansion of akāram is explained.
      - By “*kōlat tiru mā magaḷōdu*“, true nature of [brahmam (God)](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is explained.
      - By “*adiyēn*“, true nature of [ātmā (soul)](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) is explained.
      - By “*uyirgaḷ kāppān*“, upāyam (means) is explained.
      - By “*unnaik kūda*“, palam (result) is explained.
      - By “*unnaik kūdādē – taḷarvēnō*“, virōdi (hurdle) is explained.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.9.4. Talarndum murindum

*taḷarndum muṟindum sakatavasurar udal vēṟā piḷandu vīyat tirukkāl āṇḍa perumānē! kiḷarndu biraman sivan indiran viṇṇavar sūḻa viḷanga oru nāḷ kāṇ vārāy viṇmīdē*

**Пословный перевод:**

sakata asurar – śakatāsura’s; udal – body; taḷarndum – losing firmness; muṟindum – splitting into two; vēṟā – to become different pieces; piḷandu – broke; vīya – to lose its form; tirukkāl – divine foot; āṇḍa – engaged; perumānē – Oh lord!; kiḷarndu – being active (with desire, giving up their ego of considering themselves as the lords); biraman – brahmā; sivan – rudra; indiran – indra; viṇṇavar – dēvas; sūḻa – surround and worship; viḷanga – manifesting the splendour (of being their lord); oru nāḷ – one day; viṇ mīdu – on the sky; kāṇa – to be seen; vārāy – you should appear!

**Перевод:**

**Oh lord who engaged your divine foot to make śakatāsura’s body lose its form by losing firmness, splitting it into two to become different pieces and to break it! Just as you appeared manifesting the splendour to be surrounded and vorśipped by brahmā, rudra, indra and dēvas, you should appear on the sky one day to be seen \[by me\]!**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fourth pāsuram, āḻvār says “If there are hurdles, you should mercifully eliminate them and appear in front of me to remove my sorrow”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*emperumān says “Don’t grieve; though I can eliminate your sorrow, the hurdles are huge”; āḻvār responds “Oh! Is my hurdle greater than śakatāsura?” āḻvār says “as soon as they (hurdles) see your foot, will they not run away?”. The hurdles think “What will happen if the feet touch us?”, and run away as said in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 5.4.3 “summenādē kaivittōdum” (will run away being unable to breathe). taḷarndum muṟindum sakatavasurar udal vēṟā piḷandu vīyat tirukkāl āṇḍa perumānē! kiḷarndu biraman sivan indiran viṇṇavar sūḻa viḷanga oru nāḷ kāṇ vārāy viṇmīdē*

- *taḷarndum …* – To finish śakatāsura eliminating the firmness of his body, to split it and to turn it into pieces; śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 94.22 “*cinnam binnam śarair dagdam prabagnam śastra pīditam*” (They saw the army of rākśasas who were cut, blown away, burnt and destroyed by the arrows of śrī rāma). Subsequently disappearing to not even be able to see the particles. While he could have simply said “śakatāsura was destroyed”, he is saying “taḷarndum”, “muṟindum” etc individually since he relishes the destruction of the enemies and each of those steps is sweet for him.
- *tirukkāl āṇḍa* – If the servitors (divine feet) are engaged, they will help when in danger. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying “While he \[cētana, sentient entity\] remained silent due to his infancy, it was the divine feet which protected us!”. As said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 5.6.1 “*stanyārtī brarurōdaha*” (desiring for mother’s milk, he cried and lifted his feet), out of anger in not getting fed by his mother with her milk, he \[kriṣṇa\] lifted his divine feet; at that time, the wheel \[came in contact with the divine feet and\] turned into pieces; as said in periya tirumoḻi 10.8.3 “*uruḷaccagadam adu uṟakkil nimirttīr*“, he did not do it intentionally either. While knowingly engaging \[in destroying the enemies\], his divine weapons will help; if those are not there, his own hands will help; even if his hands are not helping, at that stage, the divine feet will come to the rescue. Not only for our dangers, even for his own danger, only his feet help him. As his divine form exists for his devotees, it remains the cause to eliminate their hurdles too.
- *perumānē* – For you \[emperumān’s divine feet\] who protected the lord back then, is it a huge task to protect the servitor? As he is the prakāri (entity), the attributes will survive too.
- *kiḷarndu …* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is praying to [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) – being surrounded by ananyaprayōjanas (those who desire benefits other than emperumān himself) who are said to be as mentioned in tiruvāimoḻi 3.5.4 “*kumbidu nattam ittādi*” (dancing up and down), being not in control of self, entities such as brahmā, rudra, dēvatās et al, irrespective of superiority/inferiority, like a water body which surrounds everything, and like a lamp in darkness as said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 1.9.67 “*tējasām rāśimūrjitam*” (collection of radiance); with such radiant form, like you appeared for the elephant, you should appear covering the whole sky.
- *viḷanga* – In his presence, the radiance of brahmā, rudra et al, is like darkness.
- *oru nāḷ* – Did I pray for hundred years or thousand years!
- *kāṇa vārāy* – Is he thinking that I am saying “*nīḷ nagar nīḷ eri vaittaruḷāy*“!
- *viṇ mīdē* – Did I ask you to descend to earth?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.9.5. Vin midiruppay

*viṇ mīdiruppāy! malai mēl niṟpāy! kadaṟsērppāy! maṇ mīduḻalvāy! ivaṟṟuḷ engum maṟianduṟaivāy! eṇ mīdiyanṟa puṟavaṇḍattāy! enadāvi uḷ mīdādi urukkāttādē oḷippāyō?*

**Пословный перевод:**

viṇ mīdu – in paramapadam (which is the ultimate manifestation of his supremacy); iruppāy – residing there (superior to everyone); malai mēl – in tirumalā (which is the ultimate manifestation of his simplicity); niṟpāy – standing there (in arcā (deity) form); kadal – in tiruppāṟkadal (kśīrābdi – milky ocean); sērppāy – reclining mercifully (assuming the anirudda form); maṇ mīdu – incarnating on earth; uḻalvāy – roaming around (along with the mortals there); ivaṟṟuḷ – in this universe; engum – in all objects; maṟaindu – being invisible to the senses (being the antarātmā (in-dwelling super-soul)); uṟaivāy – residing; eṇ – count; mīdu – beyond; iyanṟa – to go; puṟam – other; aṇḍattāy – you who are present in oval shaped universes; enadu – my; āvi uḷ – in the heart (which is the abode for prāṇa (vital air)); mīdādi – after being fully present; uru – form; kāttādē – not making visible for my eyes; oḷippāyō – why are you hiding \[from me\]?

**Перевод:**

**You (emperumān) are residing in paramapadam; standing in tirumalā; reclining mercifully in tiruppāṟkadal; incarnating on earth and roaming around; residing in all objects in the universe being invisible to the senses; why are you, who are present in the other countless oval shaped universes, after being fully present in my heart, not making your form visible for my eyes and hiding from me?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fifth pāsuram, āḻvār says “While you are present everywhere, and are shining in my heart brightly too, can I sustain myself if you are not visible to my eyes?”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “Should you, who are letting your devotees enjoy you in the five forms starting with paratvam, hide your form from my eyes while revealing the same in my heart?”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. viṇ mīdiruppāy! malai mēl niṟpāy! kadaṟsērppāy! maṇ mīduḻalvāy! ivaṟṟuḷ engum maṟianduṟaivāy! eṇ mīdiyanṟa puṟavaṇḍattāy! enadāvi uḷ mīdādi urukkāttādē oḷippāyō?*

- *viṇ mīdu iruppāy* – This is how he presents himself to those who see him constantly. For [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/), emperumān’s presence in paramapadam appears before his presence here \[in samsāram\].
- *malai mēl niṟpāy* – The abode where nityasūris (eternal residents of paramapadam) and nityasamsāris (bound souls) worship him together without any distinction. Being the one who initiates taste (towards himself) to make the residents of this world realise his greatness. He is said as in periya tirumoḻi 2.1.9 “*vēngadattādu kūttan*” (one who dances in tiruvēngadam hill).
- *kadal sērppāy* – Reached tiruppārkadal and reclined there for the benefit of brahmā, rudra et al who are able to access this abode. By saying *viṇ mīdu iruppāy*, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) highlighted his majestic sitting posture; and by *malai mēl niṟpāy*, the distinguished standing posture is highlighted by him.
- *kadal sērppāy* – the reclining beauty rests in the milky ocean.
- *maṇ mīdu uḻalvāy* – Oh one who descends and roams around in front of the samsāris (worldly people) who cannot reach such abodes!
- *uḻalvāy* – This samsāram has those favourable ones and unfavourable ones who bind him as said in periya tiruvandādi 18 “*tāmbāl āppuṇḍālum attaḻumbu tān iḷagap pāmbāl āppuṇḍāṟṟalum*” (He toiled by the binding of kāḷiya snake to make the binding by yaśōdā look insignificant).
- *ivaṟṟuḷ engum maṟaindu uṟaivāy* – For those who show their anger when seeing him with their eyes, Oh one who resides within them without their being able to see you! Like a mother who would engage someone dear to her son who is interested only in worldly matters and says “I won’t be with you”, to care for him. That is – even when śiśupāla et al show their envy towards him, he resides inside them as their antaryāmi and protects them.
- *eṇ mīdu iyanṟa puṟa aṇḍattāy* – Oh one who resides in the other countless such oval shaped universes! It is said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 2.7.97 “*kōti kōti śatanica*” (there are hundreds and hundreds  of crores of such universes).
- *enadu āvi uḷ mīdādi* – Saying “Roaming around in my heart without any shortcoming”; alternatively saying “roaming inside and outside my heart”.
- *uruk kāttādē oḷippāyō* – When not seeing your form, I cannot forget you and sustain myself too. Only for those who sustain themselves with the knowledge about his qualities, sustenance without seeing his form is possible!

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.9.6. Payoradi

*pāyōradi vaittu adan kīḻp paravai nilam ellām tāy ōradiyāl ellā ulagum tada vanda māyōn! unnaik kāṇbān varundi enai nāḷum tīyōdudan sēr meḻugāy ulagil tirivēnō?*

**Пословный перевод:**

ōr – one; adi – divine foot; pāy – spread; vaittu – kept; adan kīḻ – to be underneath it; paravai – with the ocean; nilam ellām – the whole earth; tāy – measured; ōr – with the other; adiyāl – divine foot; ulagu – higher world; ellām – all; tada vanda – touched; māyōn – amazing lord!; unnai – you; kāṇbān – to see; enai nāḷum – at all times; varundi – grieved; tīyōdu – with fire; udan – near; sēr – present together; meḻugāy – like wax; ulagil – in this world; tirivēnō – will grieve?

**Перевод:**

**Oh amazing lord who spread your one divine foot to keep the whole earth which is with the ocean, to be underneath it and measured and touched all of the higher world with the other foot! Will I grieve in this world to see you at all times like wax which is present together with fire?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the sixth pāsuram, āḻvār thinks that emperumān abandoned him saying “you are unqualified to see me”, and says “Is there anyone who can miss out on you who measured the whole universe without considering the qualification of anyone”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “I am melting like wax near fire, desiring to see you who mingled with those who were qualified and unqualified, without any distinction”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Sixth pāsuram. emperumān says “We will fulfil your desire. There is no doubt; still, since the benefit is for you, you should also put in some effort” and āḻvār responds “Since when you started having this practice”. Alternatively – See nanjīyar‘s introduction. pāyōradi vaittu adan kīḻp paravai nilam ellām tāy ōradiyāl ellā ulagum tada vanda māyōn! unnaik kāṇbān varundi enai nāḷum tīyōdudan sēr meḻugāy ulagil tirivēnō?*

- *pāy ōr adi vaittu* – Did the worldly people grieve to have your divine feet placed on their heads? Did you not do that without discriminating between vaśiśta (most learned) and caṇḍāḷa (most downtrodden), purely out of your grace?
- *pāy ōr adi vaittu* – Spreading one divine foot.
- *adan kīḻ* – underneath that foot.
- *paravai nilam ellām tāy* – All of the world which is surrounded by ocean. tāvi – scaled, measured. He did not just do it out of his sankalpam (vow/will), but physically scaled by spreading his divine feet and measured the same. He is as said in tiruccanda viruttam 32 “*parakka vaittu aḷandu koṇḍa paṟpapādan*” (the one with lotus foot who spread it to measure).
- *ōr adiyāl ellā ulagum tada vanda* – Extended the other divine foot up to brahma lōkam and touched it.
- *ellā ulagum* – all worlds in between \[earth and brahma lōkam\].
- *tada vanda* – like how southerly wind gently caresses.
- *māyōn* – One who shows great love to touch his own belongings.
- *unnaik kāṇbān varundi* – Why are you making me pray in my case? Have we changed roles \[before you were desiring to touch everyone, now you are making me pray to be touched by you\]?
- *enai nāḷum* – at all times. The short period in between the day āḻvār was blessed with “*mayarvaṟa madi nalam*” and the day he attains the goal \[reaching paramapadam\]. This short period looks like lengthy period, the time span before emperumān tried to catch āḻvār as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 2.7.6](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/05/thiruvaimozhi-2-7-6-madhusudhanai-anri/) “*edir sūḻal pukku*” (comes across from the opposite side and catches).
- *tīyōdu udan sēr meḻugāy* –  I am neither getting finished by entering into fire nor staying away and being safe; I am melting and grieving. Melting and grieving out of internal experience and due to lack of external (physical) experience. As the *nasai* (desire to attain) makes him grieve, *āsai* (the extreme situation caused by lack of experience which makes him unable to sustain himself) makes him melt.
- *ulagil tirivēnō* – Unable to either be finished or survive happily, I am grieving here like a yātanāśarīram (the subtle body) which is tormenting in hell.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.9.7. Ulagil tiriyum

*ulagil tiriyum karuma gadiyāy ulagamāy ulagukkē ōr uyirum ānāy! puṟa aṇḍattu alagil polinda tisai pattāya aruvēyō alagil polinda aṟivilēnukku aruḷāyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ulagil – in the world; tiriyum – engaged; karumam – leading to result; gati – for the means; āy – being the controller; ulagam – for the doers of those means; āy – being the promoter (by being the antarātmā); ulagukku – for all the worlds; ōr uyirum – being the singular soul; ānāy – being the one; puṟa aṇḍattu – those who remain outside the oval shaped universe; alagil polinda – with countless (endless) nature; pattu – ten; tisai – in directions; āya – pervaded; aruvē – Oh one who is having the muktātmās (liberated souls) as prakāram (form)!; alagil polinda – countless \[endless\]; aṟivilēnukku – me who is not having the means to attain you, due to my ignorance; aruḷāy – should shower your mercy (to have you as the means and end)

**Перевод:**

**Oh emperumān who is the controller of everything engaged in this world leading to result for the means! Oh one who is the promoter for the doers of those means! Oh one who is the singular soul for all the worlds! muktātmās (liberated souls) who remain outside the oval shaped universe, with endless nature, pervaded in ten directions; oh one who is having such muktātmās as prakāram (form)! You shower your mercy on me who is not having the means to attain you, due to my ignorance.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the seventh pāsuram, emperumān says “You too should put in some effort” and āḻvār responds “Am I counted outside your vow of protecting everyone?”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “You who are the antarātmā (in-dwelling super-soul) for all worldly entities which are doers or actions, should bestow your mercy upon me who do not know the means to attain you”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.\`*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Seventh pāsuram. emperumān says “There is a streak of independence in you based on the fact that you are grieving for this world” and āḻvār responds “While the means and the doers are at your disposal, this grief is just a natural quality \[in separation\]”. Alternatively – see nanjīyar‘s introduction. ulagil tiriyum karuma gadiyāy ulagamāy ulagukkē ōr uyirum ānāy! puṟa aṇḍattu alagil polinda tisai pattāya aruvēyō alagil polinda aṟivilēnukku aruḷāyē*

- *ulagil tiriyum karuma gatiyāy* – The means which is practiced in this world. Is there any one other than you who can bestow the results?
- *ulagamāy* – Are the practitioners independent? \[They are controlled by you too\] “*ulagam enbadu uyarndōr mādu*” (the term world implies the learned elders residing in the world); this can also mean all residents of the world.
- *ulagukkē ōr uyirum ānāy* – Just as a body is considered as the possession of an ātmā, oh one who is the singular soul of all objects! yajur āraṇyakam 3-11-21 “*anta:praviśtaśśāsta janānām sarvātmā*” ([emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) pervades all *janas* (those who are born) and controls them). One who bestows the result himself remains the doer, the action and the instruments. When both (karma and kartā) are at your disposal, how can we survive without you?
- *puṟa aṇḍattu* – As said in “*aṇḍātbahi:*” (outside the oval shaped universe).
- *alagil podinda tisai pattāya aruvēyō* – Oh one who is the controller for the countless ātmās (muktātmās) who pervade in all ten directions with their jñānam just as [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) pervades everything with his true nature, who are without \[material\] form unlike entities with \[material\] form! Are the muktas independent? \[No\] Would paramapadam have ten directions? Since [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying this from here, he is saying like that. Alternatively – when muktas think about the leelā vibhūti (samsāram), they will experience it as it is seen here.
- *alagil polinda aṟivilēnukku* – āḻvār is saying that even if he can comprehend bhagavān’s svarūpa, rūpa, guṇa, vibhūti etc, he cannot comprehend his own ignorance. This is the conclusion of the one who attained unblemiśed knowledge/devotion from bhagavān himself.
- *aruḷāyē* – As I have the prerequisite (not having anything in me), what stops you from bestowing your mercy! As said in stōtra ratnam 24 “*anuttamam pātram idam dayāyā:*” (You now have the best recipient for your mercy).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.
