## 6.9.8. Arivilenukku arulay

*aṟivilēnukkaruḷāy aṟivār uyirānāy! veṟi koḷ sōdi mūrtti! adiyēnedumālē! kiṟi seydennaip puṟattittu innam keduppāyō? piṟidonṟaṟiyā adiyēn āvi tigaikkavē*

**Пословный перевод:**

aṟivār – for the distinguished wise persons; uyir – dāraka (sustainer); ānāy – you are; veṟikoḷ – totally fragrant; sōdi – radiant; mūrtti – having divine form; adiyēn – you who made me totally exist for you to desire for you; nedumālē – Oh one who is having great attachment!; aṟivilēnukku – for me who does not know the means (to enjoy such beautiful form); aruḷāy – you should let me enjoy it by your mercy; piṟidu – other than you; onṟu – any other goal; aṟiyā – without knowing; adiyēn – me (who is having the nature to be at your disposal); āvi – heart; tigaikka – to become worried; kiṟi – by some means; seydu – having planted the taste; ennai – me (who knows the greatness of your beautiful form); puṟattu – worldly matters; ittu – engage; innam – even today (when I have the desire for you); keduppāyō – are you planning to torment me?

**Перевод:**

**You are the sustainer for the distinguished wise persons; oh one who is having totally fragrant, radiant, divine form, who made me totally exist for you to desire for you and who is having great attachment! You should let me who does not know the means, enjoy such form by your mercy. You have planted the taste by some means in me to have my heart become worried without knowing any goal other than you; would you engage me in worldly matters and are you planning to torment me even today? veṟi koḷ sōdi – also implies radiance which blinds the eyes of the one who sees.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the eighth pāsuram, as āḻvār‘s desire is not fulfilled immediately, he says “Are you trying to do something to keep me, who cannot survive without you, away? Instead of doing that, you should protect you by your mercy”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “Are you planning to push me into worldly matters and trouble me more instead of letting me enjoy your lustrous form?”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. aṟivilēnukkaruḷāy aṟivār uyirānāy! veṟi koḷ sōdi mūrtti! adiyēnedumālē! kiṟi seydennaip puṟattittu innam keduppāyō? piṟidonṟaṟiyā adiyēn āvi tigaikkavē*

- *aṟivilēnukku aruḷāy* – As said in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 5.4.1 “*nin aruḷē purindirundēn*” (I am looking for your mercy only), you should shower your mercy upon me who does not know anything other than your mercy, āḻvār would remain as said in tiruvāimoḻi 9.9.6 “*avvaruḷ allana aruḷum alla*” (any other grace is not consider as grace). [mudal tiruvandādi 15](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/06/mudhal-thiruvandhadhi-15/) “*vaiyagattup pallār aruḷum paḻudu*” (world’s many others’ grace is of no use). (For me who is having ignorance, you who are jñānap pirān should shower your grace).
- *aṟivār uyir ānāy* – Saying “Oh life of the wise persons \[great devotees\]!”; saying “Oh the one who is having the wise persons as your life!”. As said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 7.18](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/7-18/) “*jñāni tvātmaiva mē matam*” (but the jñāni is the one who sustains me – this is my opinion). As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 4.43 “*dvitīyammēntarātmānam*” (You who are my second soul).
- *veṟi koḷ sōdi mūrtti* – The beauty which will not let me give up on you even if you do not shower your mercy. As said in “*sarvaganda:*” (root of all fragrances). Oh one who is having the physical beauty with fragrance and endless radiance!
- *adiyēn nedumālē* – Saying “Oh one who is beyond my reach now!”; or saying “Oh one who manifested your beauty and created great attachment in me!”.
- *kiṟi seydu* – As you are not helping now, whatever \[favours\] you have done previously appear to be a plan to torment me \[by neither making me fit in this samsāram nor helping me reach you at once\]!
- *ennaip puṟattittu* – Like you let sītāp pirātti stay in aśōka vanam, you have left me in samsāram where bhagavat viśayam is not seen and sensual pleasures are rampant.
- *innam keduppāyō* – Is whatever I have lost so far, not sufficient? Would you trouble me even after knowing “samsāram should be discarded” and “bhagavat viśayam is good”? Is it not said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 2.63](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/2-63/) “*buddi nāśāt praṇāśyati*” (due to destruction of intelligence, the person himself perishes)?
- *piṟidonṟu …* – Confusing my mind, would you plan and keep me, who has no other refuge and no interest towards others, away and torment me further?

## 6.9.9. Avi tigaikka

*āvi tigaikka aivar kumaikkum siṟṟinbam pāviyēnaip pala nī kāttip paduppāyō? tāvi vaiyam koṇḍa tadandāmaraigatkē kūvik koḷḷum kālam innam kuṟugādō?*

**Пословный перевод:**

āvi – heart; tigaikka – to tremble; aivar – the five senses; kumaikkum – torturing saying “give me more”; siṟu – insignificant; inbam – sweet pleasures; pala – in many varieties; kātti – revealing; nī – you (who have the ability to destroy these); pāviyēnai – me who is a sinner (to be residing in this sorrowful place while being qualified to be joyful endlessly); paduppāyō – are you planning to finish me?; vaiyam – earth; tāvi – measured to claim full ownership; koṇḍa – accepted; tadam – infinitely enjoyable; tāmaraigatku – to engage in the divine lotus feet; kūvik koḷḷum – to invite me; kālam – the time; innam – even at this stage (when I have realised that even the sight of worldly pleasures is the cause to disaster); kuṟugādō – Will it not happen soon?

**Перевод:**

**Are you planning to finish me who is a sinner, by revealing the many varieties of insignificant, sweet pleasures which are causing my heart to tremble by saying “give me more” and torturing the five senses? Your infinitely enjoyable, divine lotus feet measured the earth to claim full ownership and accepted it. Will the time to invite me to engage in those divine feet, not happen soon, even at this stage?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the ninth pāsuram, āḻvār explains emperumān‘s act to finish āḻvār as “by showing the worldly pleasures and keeping me away from your divine feet”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “Are you planning to keep me in this samsāram where the senses which are under your control, are rampant, and to finish me? Will the day I reach your divine feet not arrive soon?”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*In the ninth pāsuram, āḻvār expands upon his words from previous pāsuram “puṟattittu innam keduppāyō?” and says “Will the day I reach your divine feet not arrive soon?”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Ninth pāsuram. emperumān asks “How did I trouble you here?” and āḻvār responds “If you keep me in this world where one gets sucked into the visually appealing aspects, is there anything you need to separately do to trouble me?”. He further says “When you decide to keep me here, is it not like you digging a pit and pushing me in there?”. As said in śrī bhagavat gītā 16.19 “tān aham dviśata: krūrān samsārēśu narādamān \| kśipāmi …” (I continuously push those (demoniac people) who are having hatred towards me (as explained previously), being cruel, being lowly amongst men, being inauspicious, in births (which contain repeated birth, death, old-age and disease), that too, in demoniac births). āvi tigaikka aivar kumaikkum siṟṟinbam pāviyēnaip pala nī kāttip paduppāyō? tāvi vaiyam koṇḍa tadandāmaraigatkē kūvik koḷḷum kālam innam kuṟugādō?*

- *āvi tigaikka* – To make the heart/mind, which is the root for the senses, tremble.
- *aivar kumaikkum* – \[Instead of saying “aindu” (as non-living thing), “aivar” (as living thing) is used\] Due to the level of cruelty, they are addressed like a cētana (sentient). Just as a weak person will be tortured by five strong persons, each sense will try to extract the best for its interest. Even if they torture like this, at least if there is some taste, one can accept.
- *siṟṟinbam* – Like \[non-existing\] honey in muḷḷi flower. They are as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 3.2.6](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/07/thiruvaimozhi-3-2-6-kirpan-killen/) “*aṟpa sārangaḷ*” (insignificant pleasures). Even if you were to be discarded, at least there should be a lot more to enjoy \[even that is not there\].
- *pāviyēnai* – I who am born to enjoy endless great pleasure as said in tiruvāimoḻi 10.9.11 “*andamil pērinbam*“, am caught in enjoying such insignificant pleasures. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) who said in [tiruvāimoḻi 4.5.3](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/02/thiruvaimozhi-4-5-3-vivil-inbam/) “*vīvil inbam miga ellai nigaḻndanan*” (one who is in the ultimate state of continuous bliss), is saying this now.
- *pala* – I am not so weak to be just bound by one aspect – so there are many aspects.
- *nī kāttip paduppāyō* – Are you, the saviour, yourself showing these to finish me?
- *kāttip paduppāyō* – The same aspects without which the worldly people cannot survive, are causing [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) bewilderment at the very sight of them. There is a particular species of birds named “asuṇamā”. These birds cannot be easily caught. Those who try to catch them will first sing and hearing that, the birds will become attracted and melt. At that time, they will beat the drums loudly. Unable to tolerate the sound, they will fall. Similarly, āḻvār melts on enjoying bhagavān’s guṇas (qualities). At that time, if he sees worldly matters, he will fall. The nature of worldly pleasures is such that – even after enjoying a pleasure for many days, when being away for some time from that, one cannot meditate upon that and explain the nature of that experience clearly; in spite of such nature, one becomes attracted to them due to the abundance of sins.
- *tāvi …* – While speaking about something else ([emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s act of measuring the world), [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is establishing his goal.
- *tāvi vaiyam koṇḍa* – Explains the potency of emperumān in fulfilling what he desires. Explains how effortlessly he measured the entire earth.
- *tadam tāmaraigatkē* – In the divine feet which have infinite enjoyability. With this – the goal is explained. By saying “*kūvik koḷḷum kālam*” (the time you will invite me), the nature of the means is explained. By saying “*innam kuṟugādō*” (has it not arrived yet), [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s taste/craving is explained. Would you still delay even after the stage where I will be finished on seeing worldly matters and not giving up attachment to your divine feet knowing well their enjoyable nature? During the final days of [piḷḷān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/pillan/), [nanjīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nanjiyar/) goes to him to enquire about his health. piḷḷān keeps saying ” *kūvik koḷḷum kālam innam kuṟugādō?*“. Hearing that nanjīyar starts crying. Seeing that piḷḷān says to nanjīyar “Why are you crying? Does it appear that what I am going to get in paramapadam is any lesser than our current situation here?” \[piḷḷān indicates that nanjīyar should not be crying and should instead be relishing the thought that he will be in paramapadam soon\].

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.9.10. Kuruga nila

*kuṟugā nīḷā iṟudi kūdā enai ūḻi siṟugā perugā aḷavilinbam sērndālum maṟugāl inṟi māyōn! unakkē āḷāgum siṟu kālattai uṟumō? andō! teriyilē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kuṟugā nīḷā – without expansion or contraction in true nature; iṟudi kūdā – without an end; enai ūḻi – at all times; siṟugā perugā – without decay and growth; aḷavil – without any limit; inbam – bliss of self; sērndālum – even if attained; māyōn – Oh the amazing one whose momentary experience is greatly distinguished!; teriyil – if analysed; maṟugāl – repeat; inṟi – not having; unakkē – for you only; āḷ āgum – being a servitor and enjoying that servitude; siṟu kālattai – that small fraction of time; andō – alas!; uṟumō – is it a match?

**Перевод:**

**Oh the amazing one whose momentary experience is greatly distinguished! Even if the bliss of self which has no expansion or contraction, which is endless, which is without decay or growth at all times, is attained; alas! If analysed, it is not a match for being a servitor to you only and enjoying that servitude even if attained for a small fraction of time without a repeat experience,.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the tenth pāsuram, emperumān says to āḻvār “If you think worldly pleasures are alpam (insignificant) and astiram (temporary), why don’t you pursue kaivalyam (being freed from material realm to eternally enjoy the self)”, āḻvār says “since that will not lead to kainkaryam at your divine feet, I don’t need it”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “Is the distinguished benefit of enjoying the self a match to a momentary servitude towards you who are greatly distinguished?”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. āḻvār says “I am not discarding something just because they are bad and pursuing something just because they are good; I am pursuing you because its you and I am discarding everything else, because they are not you”. He says “I got to see good qualities, beauty etc in the apt entity (i.e. emperumān)”. kuṟugā nīḷā iṟudi kūdā enai ūḻi siṟugā perugā aḷavilinbam sērndālum maṟugāl inṟi māyōn! unakkē āḷāgum siṟu kālattai uṟumō? andō! teriyilē*

- *kuṟugā nīḷā* – Not contracting and expanding.
- *iṟudi kūdā* – Not having complete destruction.
- *enai ūḻi* – Not having the contraction and expansion which are caused as an effect of time.
- *aḷavil inbam sērndālum* – In this manner, even if this endless bliss of [self](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) enjoyment is attained.
- *maṟugāl inṟi* – bhagavat anubhavam (experiencing bhagavān) is unique everytime.
- *māyōn* – Here [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s being with auspicious qualities which make him undiscardable even if he is enjoyed only once.
- *unakkē āḷ āgum siṟu kālattai uṟumō* – Considering “servitude at your divine feet is the goal” is irrevocable. Even if it is experienced for a fraction of a moment, would it be comparable to endless bliss of [self](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) enjoyment? \[No, servitude to [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s divine feet even for a fraction of a moment is much greater\].

Seeing this \[[āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says\],

- *andō* – \[Alas!\] Why am I in a situation of comparing a mountain with a small pebble!
- *teriyilē* – When we speak without thinking, we cannot do anything; but if we speak after analysis, this can be the only situation. Why is this even needed to be instructed! \[It is very obvious\].

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.9.11. Teridal ninaidal

*teridal ninaidal eṇṇal āgāt tirumālukku uriya toṇḍar toṇḍar toṇḍar satakōpan teriyac conna ōr āyirattuḷ ippattum uriya toṇḍarākkum ulagam uṇḍāṟkē*

**Пословный перевод:**

teridal – having clarity (through hearing); ninaidal – thinking (firmly through contemplation); eṇṇal – even if fixed in mind (through repeated meditation); āgā – without any limit; tirumālukku – for emperumān who is the consort of śrī mahālakśmi; uriya toṇḍar – for those who became exclusive servitors; toṇḍar – for those who are servitors; toṇḍan – servitor; satakōpan – nammāḻvār; teriya – in detail; sonna – mercifully spoke; ōr āyirattuḷ ippattum – this decad among the thousand pāsurams; ulagam uṇḍāṟku – one who protected everything; uriya toṇḍar – exclusive servitor; ākkum – will make

**Перевод:**

**Even if fixed in mind after having clarity and thinking upon, emperumān who is the consort of śrī mahālakśmi, is beyond limits; nammāḻvār who is the servitor for those servitors of the exclusive servitors of such emperumān, mercifully spoke in detail in this decad among the thousand pāsurams; one who practices this decad will be made an exclusive servitor of emperumān who protected everything.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the end, āḻvār says “Those who learned this decad will become confidential servitors for emperumān“.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār explains the result as “This decad will make those who are connected to it to be unflinching servitors to the one who is the protector of all”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. teridal ninaidal eṇṇal āgāt tirumālukku uriya toṇḍar toṇḍar toṇḍar satakōpan teriyac conna ōr āyirattuḷ ippattum uriya toṇḍarākkum ulagam uṇḍāṟkē*

- *teridal* … – For śrīman nārāyaṇa who cannot be restricted within any limits by śravaṇa (hearing), manana (contemplation) and nididyāsitavya (repeated meditation). As said in katōpaniśat 1.2.23 “*nāyamātmā pravacanēna labhya:*” (This [paramātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) cannot be attained by mere hearing, meditation etc without devotion) – he is beyond conception for mere hearing etc; otherwise (when hearing etc were performed with love) these will lead to experience.
- *tirumālukku* – The reason for this (his inconceivable nature) is his being the consort of śrī mahālakśmi; this is the identity of being the supreme lord.
- *tirumālukku uriya toṇḍar toṇḍar toṇḍar satakōpan* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) who is an exclusive servitor of sarvēśvara who is the consort of śrī mahālakśmi. Due to the cruelty of having contemplated upon the nature of this material realm and due to the overwhelming emotions of having immersed in bhagavat viśayam, just as a very thirsty person will plunge into a pond, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is engaging in the ultimate stage of servitude (i.e. being the servitor of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s servitors). This is the nature of āḻvār’s aham buddi (thinking about self). When one is a dēhātmābhimāni (considering body as soul), one would have his/her aham buddi on the body; when one knows that there is something different from the body, one would have his/her aham buddi on ātmā; when one contemplates oneself to be a servitor of [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/), one would stop at the layer of prakāra (forms/attributes) of emperumān, and would leave after accepting wealth etc; when one considers “śēśatvam” (servitude) is the goal, one should consider oneself to be a servitor of emperumān’s servitors. After [tiruvāimoḻi 3.7](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/09/thiruvaimozhi-3-7-payilum/) “*payilum sudaroḷi*“, āḻvār’s aham buddi stretches upto being a servitor of servitors of emperumān. Only if one reaches this stage, he is in ananyārha śēśatvam (exclusive servitude).
- *teriyac conna …* – This decad which explains the greatness of [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) and the defect of this material realm in detail.
- *uriya toṇḍarākkum ulagam uṇḍārkkē* – This decad will make one become an exclusive servitor of sarvēśvara who is the protector of all.
- *uriya toṇḍarākkum* – True servitors are those who will not discard bhagavat viśayam even if it turns bad and this material realm turns good.

## 6.10 Ulagam unda

## 6.10.1. Ulagam unda

*ulagam uṇḍa peru vāyā ulappil kīrtti ammānē! nilavum sudar sūḻoḷi mūrtti nediyāy adiyēn āruyirē! tiladam ulkagukkāy ninṟa tiruvēngdattemperumānē! kula tol adiyēn una pādam kūdumāṟu kūṟāyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ulagam – the world; uṇḍa – while consuming; peru – having great eagerness (more than the world which is to be protected); vāyā – having divine lips/mouth which is the tool to protect; ulappu – end; il – not having; kīrtti – glory (of all auspicious qualities such as jñāna, śakti etc); ammānē – being the one with natural lordship; nilavum sudar sūḻ – revealing the complete radiance of natural beauty etc; oḷi – filled with divine splendour; mūrtti – being with divine form; nediyāy – having unbounded glory (for the aforementioned nature, form, qualities and activities); adiyēn – for me (who is at your disposal); Ar uyirē – being my perfectly complete vital air; ulagukku – for the whole world; tiladam – like a tilak which is applied on the forehead in the form of ūrdvapuṇḍram (upwards pointing symbol); āy – being; ninṟa – (firmly) stood; tiruvēngadattu – on tirumalā; em – to me; perumānē – Oh one who stood revealing your lordship!; kulam – coming in famous lineage; tol – ancient; adiyēn – I (servitor); un – (lord, protector and enjoyable) your; pādam – divine feet; kūdum – attaining; āṟu – means; kūṟāy – mercifully tell!

**Перевод:**

**Oh emperumān who is having divine lips/mouth which is the tool to protect the world with great eagerness \[during deluge\] by consuming it! Oh the one with endless glory and natural lordship! Oh one who is having divine form filled with divine splendour, revealing the complete radiance of natural beauty etc and having unbounded glory! Oh one who is being my perfectly complete vital air (life)! Oh one who stood revealing your lordship to me on tirumalā like a tilak which is applied on the forehead in the form of ūrdvapuṇḍram for the whole world! For me, the servitor who is coming in an ancient lineage, mercifully tell the means to attaining your divine feet!**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the first pāsuram, āḻvār says “You should mercifully ensure that I who have no refuge other than you, to reach your divine feet”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*In the first pāsuram, āḻvār says “You who are having the qualities to protect all the world and are present in tirumalā, should mercifully show the way to attain you to me who is having natural servitude towards you”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. ulagam uṇḍa peru vāyā ulappil kīrtti ammānē! nilavum sudar sūḻoḷi mūrtti nediyāy adiyēn āruyirē! tiladam ulkagukkāy ninṟa tiruvēngdattemperumānē! kula tol adiyēn una pādam kūdumāṟu kūṟāyē*

- *ulagam uṇḍa peru vāyā* – Would the danger of ten deluges match my sorrow of not reaching the divine feet of your highness? Oh one who has more eagerness \[to protect\] than those who wish to be protected! īsn’t there a match between your eagerness and my agony? āren’t you the one who protects based on the relationship and the danger alone! Would you only protect if the whole world is in danger! Would you not protect if I am inflicted with the same danger that affected the whole world? Would you only protect those who drowned in the ocean of deluge! Would you not protect those who are drowning in the ocean of samsāram (material realm) ? Would you only protect those who did not request you to do so! Would you not help those who request you to do so? Would you only protect when there is danger for the body! Would you not protect when there is danger for the soul? Would you only protect those who are caught in the deluge of water! Would you not help those who are caught in the deluge of separation? Would you only protect when endangered by others! Would you not protect when endangered by you? Is there any rule that you only protect those who have not surrendered! Would you not protect those who have surrendered? For you who cannot relax even after protecting someone, is it possible to not even think about protecting me? āren’t you of the nature that even after protecting those who were caught in the danger of deluge, you will check with those who were present saying “is there anything great I have done for them?”, and subsequently will feel disturbed thinking “I have not done anything worthy for them” and feel dejected!
- *peru vāyā* – This is how the nature of the one who has more eagerness \[to protect\] than those who wish to be protected is. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) thinks [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) has the same amount of disregard for himself as the amount of eagerness in protecting the universe.
- *peru vāyā* – draupadi said “śaraṇam” (I take shelter of you) only once. Having that in his divine heart, he eliminated the insult that was to happen for her in the assembly, destroyed duryōdana et al, crowned daramaputra, and had her hairlock tied \[she vowed not to tie her hair until duryōdana et al were killed\]. Still being unsatisfied as said in mahābhāratam udyōga parvam 58.22 “*ruṇam pravruttam iva mē*” (I feel like I owe you so much), while ascending to paramapadam, he departed with a wounded heart as said in “*nātis svasta manā:*” (my heart is not in peace).
- *ulappil kīrtti ammānē* – I am not praising him considering that his protection is an unnatural and occasional activity; this act of protecting the world and acquiring endless glory as a result of that is explained in tirunedundāṇḍagam 10 “*poḻilēḻum kāval pūṇḍa pugaḻ ānāy*” (He has the glory of protecting the 7 worlds). Oh sarvēśvara who is having glorious qualities! Your glory is not just advised as said in “*tasya nāma mahatyaśa:*” (paramātmā’s glory is great), śrī rāmāyaṇam kiśkindā kāṇḍam 15.19 “*yaśasaścaikabājanam*” (He is the abode of glory), but is even popularly celebrated in the enemy’s camp as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 21.20 “*vidita:*” (he is well known)! Your commandment is such that the one which is tortured \[sumukha, the snake\] is well protected in the presence of the one who tortures \[garuda, the eagle\]! When he desires, the torturer will care for the tortured.
- *ulappil kīrtti ammānē* – There is no end for his qualities which are explained in śrī rāmāyaṇam kiśkindā kāṇḍam 15.21 “*guṇānām ākarō mahān*” (one who is the abode for auspicious qualities), mātsya purāṇam “*tatā guṇāhi anantasya*” (His qualities are endless), mahābhāratam karṇa parvam “*varśāyutair yasya guṇānaśakyā:*” (Even if spoken for ten thousand years, kriṣṇa’s qualities cannot be explained fully) and śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 2.26 “*bahavō nrupa kalyāṇa guṇā: putrasya santitē*” (Oh emperor! You son (śrī rāma) has many auspicious qualities). If one tries to see the end of it, they cannot; they will retract due to lack of intellect. ([āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) became captivated by [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), not for his true nature but for his qualities.)
- *nilavum sudar sūḻ oḷi mūrtti* – Even if he is a butcher instead of a protector, his beautiful form will not let us leave him.
- *nilavum* – It is not something which he acquires based on some karma, and will lose it on exhausting of the same \[i.e. it is eternal\].
- *sudar sūḻ oḷi mūrtti* – Instead of inside being dirt and outside being radiant, he is made of radiant material as said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 1.9.67 “*tējasām rāśimūrjitam*” (collection of radiance);. He is said as in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.7.4](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/09/thiruvaimozhi-1-7-4-mayarvu-ara/) “*uyarvinaiyē tarum oṇ sudark kaṟṟaiyai*” (one who bestowed me increase in my knowledge, devotion, etc., and has a radiantly shining form). Unlike forms which are made of rajas (passion) and tamas (ignorance), his form is made of śudda satva (pure goodness), unlimited radiance, and like boiled ghee \[which has a golden colour\], full of luster both inside and outside. His divine form is explained both as “*pancaśaktimayam*” (made of five divine elements \[which are different from the five elements which make material forms\]) and “*śādguṇya vigraham*” (form having six auspicious qualities); but if analysed, his forms are made by five divine elements only; but when said as “*śādguṇya vigraham*“, that is because the divine form reveals those qualities unlike material forms which conceal the qualities. His forms are as explained in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 34.30 “*rūpavān subakaś śrīmān gandarpa ivamūrtimān*” (He is having divine form like cupid and having radiance) and in śrī bhāgavatam 10.32.2 “… *tāsāmāvirabūt …*” (He appeared amidst the covherd girls like the cupid for cupids).
- *nediyāy* – Even if there is an end for the previously explained qualities, one cannot see the end for his qualities such as part-by-part beauty, wholesome beauty etc. As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam kiśkindā kāṇḍam 15.20 “*mahān*” (the great), every aspect of his qualities is boundless.
- *adiyēn Ar uyirē* – Oh one who manifested your physical beauty and qualities and made me not sustain myself in separation! This should be read along with “*tiruvēndattemperumānē*” (lord of tiruvēngadam hill).
- *tiladam ulagukkāy ninṟa* – Just as some women become complete with the tilak on their face, tirumalā is for the earth.
- *adiyēn Ar uyirē* – Oh one who arrived and stood in tirumalā, taught me my servitude towards you, and made me unsustainable without you!

Until here, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) explained [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s nature, and now he starts speaking about his own nature.

- *kula tol adiyēn* – I, who am a servitor, since long, along with all my ancestors. He is not highlighting his greatness, rather he is highlighting his lack of any other refuge. When one exists for only one person, no one else will protect that person.
- *una pādam kūdumāṟu kūṟāyē* – As my nature is this, you kindly ensure that I attain the goal which fits my nature.
- *adiyēn una pādam kūdumāṟu* – When a servitor wants to unite with you, it is expressed only as “uniting with your divine feet”.
- *una pādam kūdumāṟu* – This is how [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s sāyujyam \[the aspect of liberation, where one remains eternally united with the lord\] is.
- *kūṟāyē* – Your one word leads to realising my true nature. When [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) speaks a single word, āḻvār’s confusions will be eliminated. \[āḻvār is asking\] You should say as in [śrī bhagavat gītā 18.66](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/18-66/) “*mā śuca:*” (do not grieve).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.10.2. Kuray niray

*kūṟāy nīṟāy nilanāgik kodu val asurar kulam ellām sīṟā eriyum tirunēmi valavā! deyvak kōmānē! sēṟār sunait tāmarai sendī malarum tiruvēngadattānē! āṟā anbil adiyēn un adi sēr vaṇṇam aruḷāyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kodu – being cruel; val – very strong; asurar – demons; kulam – group; ellām – all; kūṟu āy – to be cut into many pieces; nīṟu āy – to turn into dust; nilan āgi – while being flattened; sīṟā – showing anger; eriyum – shining; tiru – having the wealth of valour; nēmi – tiruvāḻi, divine chakra (divine disc); valavā – being the omnipotent who can control; deyvam – for nityasūris; kōmānē – being the lord; sēṟu – by mud (for the lotus to stay in); Ar – filled; sunai – pond; tāmarai – reddish lotus; sem – reddish; tī – acquiring the complexion of fire; malarum – blossoming; tiruvēngdattānē – Oh one who is residing in tirumalā!; āṟā – ever endless; anbu – love; il – having; adiyēn – I, who am a servitor; un – your; adi – divine feet; sēr vaṇṇam – to reach; aruḷāy – kindly bless

**Перевод:**

**Oh omnipotent emperumān who can control the shining chakra which cuts the cruel, very strong demons into pieces, to turn them into dust, and which shows its anger even after flattening them and which is having the wealth of valour! Oh lord of nityasūris! Oh one who is residing in tirumalā which is having muddy ponds with reddish lotus flowers which have the complexion of reddish fire and which are blossoming! Kindly bless me who is a servitor, having ever endless love for you, to reach your divine feet.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the second pāsuram, āḻvār says “If there are any hurdles, you should yourself eliminate them and accept me at your divine feet”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. kūṟāy nīṟāy nilanāgik kodu val asurar kulam ellām sīṟā eriyum tirunēmi valavā! deyvak kōmānē! sēṟār sunait tāmarai sendī malarum tiruvēngadattānē! āṟā anbil adiyēn un adi sēr vaṇṇam aruḷāyē*

- *kūṟāy …* – What is the match between your hand being inseparable from the chakra and I still having my hurdles? [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s divine weapons which are indestructible, would destroy all his ([ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)‘s) hurdles and uplift him; they can also eliminate the hurdles which are caused by emperumān himself. viṣṇu darmam 70 “*rakśanti sakalāpatbya:*” (protecting from all dangers); he \[emperumān\] himself is included in this word “*sakala*” (all).  Now, sins are the result of his anger over the ātmā due to the defects in the ātmā; these weapons are capable of eliminating even such hurdles. The reason for this is because they (weapons) keep thinking about emperumān’s initial mercy towards the ātmā. These weapons were previously told by emperumān himself “Even if I see some faults in these ātmās and manifest my anger towards them, you don’t abandon him; you see my initial, natural mercy towards him and protect him due to that”. The chakra is explained as in tiruviruttam 33 “*aruḷār tiruccakkaram*” (the divine disc which is filled with mercy). They (weapons) would have seen his initial mercy and hence even if he changes his position towards the ātmās, the weapons would not change \[and continue to protect them\]. This is why, those who were bestowed with his mercy, would consider the sharpness of his divine chakra as their refuge.
- *kūrāy nīrāy nilanāgi* – His divine arrows which act as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 94.22 “*cinnam binnam śarair dagdam prabagnam śastra pīditam*” (They saw the army of rākśasas who were cut, blown away, burnt and destroyed by the arrows of śrī rāma), have guṇa (guṇa means the String as well as mercy). Unlike those arrows, his chakra is most cruel. \[While the arrows will cut the entity into portions directly\] the chakra will cut it into two pieces and then will turn the entity into dust and finally will make it disappear as well.
- *āgi* – Implies both making and to become.
- *kodu val asurar* – This is the reason for his anger. Those demons who act in a cruel manner and who are very strong which makes it impossible for anyone to defeat them.
- *kulam ellām* – Just one person’s mistake makes the whole clan to be destroyed and hence [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) destroyed the whole town along with the residents. Whether it is the favourable ones or the unfavourable ones, no one escapes his curly chakra. As said in tiruviruttam 70 “*vaḷaivāyt tiruccakkarattengaḷ vānavanār*” (our lord in paramapadam who has the curvy and rounded chakra) – only after being caught in his chakra, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) was uplifted.

What was the reason for his act to cut the demons and finish them?

- *sīṟā eriyum tirunēmi valavā* – Even after completing the tasks, his chakra will shine continously like a snake which has not found its prey.
- *tirunēmi valavā* – While you are carrying the divine chakra on your right hand, I am \[still\] carrying agony \[how do these two match?\]!
- *deyvak kōmānē* – Such [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who takes up so much care/suffering to protect his devotees, is not without any support. He is as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.1.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/03/thiruvaimozhi-1-1-1-uyarvara-uyarnalam/) “*ayarvaṟum amarargaḷ adipati*” – lord of indefatigable nityasūris. There (paramapadam), only those who enjoy his beautiful combination of hand and chakra are available; but it is here (samsāram) that he has people to be cut into two pieces. Only his divine chakra rules both the realms. As said in tiruviruttam 33 “*agal visumbum nilanum iruḷār vinai kedac cengōl nadāvudir*” (You are having your sceptre which eliminates the darkness and rules over the spiritual sky and the material world); the chakra rules over everyone there (paramapadam) with its beauty; it rules over everyone here (samsāram) with its sharpness. Sharpness is subdued there; beauty is subdued here. For those who are there, just its presence on his hand will uplift them; but for those who are here, only after eliminating the enemies, they will be uplifted. Those who are there always depend upon his hand (him), but here people don’t have such faith.
- *sērār sunai …* – In the muddy ponds, lotus flowers blossom like reddish fire. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is desiring to enjoy water-lamp instead of oil-lamp. The reddish lotus flowers appear to be fire on top of water!
- *āṟā anbil adiyēn* – This \[love\] is āḻvār’s identity. Only when the water dries out in the pond \[which never happens\], will āḻvār’s love dry out. This love originated from [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s blessing of unblemiśed knowledge and devotion. The love which does not wait for any rules.
- *un adi sēr vaṇṇam aruḷāyē* – You should bestow your mercy upon me to have me engaged in service at your divine feet. See that the purpose of your standing in tirumalā is fulfilled! See that my love is properly fed!

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.10.3. Vannam arul kol

*vaṇṇam aruḷ koḷ aṇi mēga vaṇṇā! māyavammānē! eṇṇam pugundu tittikkum amudē! imaiyōr adipadiyē! teṇṇal aruvi maṇi pon muttalaikkum tiruvēngadattānē! aṇṇalē! un adi sēra adiyēṟkāvāvennāyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vaṇṇam – complexion; maruḷ – madness; koḷ – to cause; aṇi – having beauty; mēgam – like cloud; vaṇṇā – having form; māyam – with amazing qualities; ammānē – being greater than all; eṇṇam – in the heart; pugundu – entered; tittikkum – being sweet; amudē – being nectar; imaiyōr – letting nityasūris enjoy; adipadiyē – \[adipati\] having supremacy; teḷ – having clarity; nal – attractive; aruvi – waterfalls; maṇi – gemstones; pon – gold; muttu – pearl; alaikkum – toss around; tiruvēngadattānē – being present in tirumalā; aṇṇalē – Oh one who effortlessly manifesting your lordship!; un – your; adi – apt, divine feet; sēra – to reach; adiyōrkku – for us, the servitors; A A – alas! alas! \[taking pity on us\]; ennāy – you should manifest your mercy

**Перевод:**

**emperumān who is greater than all, is having cloud like form with amazing qualities and a complexion which causes madness; he has entered the heart and is sweet nectar; he is letting nityasūris enjoy \[such form\]; he is having supremacy and is present in tirumalā which has clear, attractive waterfalls which toss around gemstones, gold and pearls; Oh one who effortlessly manifests your lordship in such tirumalā! Taking pity on us, you should manifest your mercy for us to reach your divine feet which are apt for us!**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the third pāsuram, emperumān says “While you have not put in any effort, how can I do whatever you ask for?”; āḻvār replies “While you already have many distinguished personalities who enjoy you, you pursued me; similarly, purely out of your mercy, you should fulfil my desires”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. vaṇṇam aruḷ koḷ aṇi mēga vaṇṇā! māyavammānē! eṇṇam pugundu tittikkum amudē! imaiyōr adipadiyē! teṇṇal aruvi maṇi pon muttalaikkum tiruvēngadattānē! aṇṇalē! un adi sēra adiyēṟkāvāvennāyē*

- *vaṇṇam …* – vaṇṇam means prakāra (attributes), Oh one who is having mercy, and is having an attractive form which resembles a cloud! Alternatively – vaṇṇam means form, Oh one who is having the form which blinds the heart of those who see you! His form is explained in tiruviruttam 94 “*maippadi mēni*” (dark coloured form). Another explanation – His divine form is manifesting so much mercy that the heart of a cloud is hard like a rock.
- *māya ammānē* – Oh one who is great in your qualities and activities too, apart from having a great form!
- *eṇṇam pugundu tittikkum amudē* – Unlike being born in a distinguished birth, performing a particular sādana anuśtānam (means such as bhakti yōga), and finally attaining bliss through that and enjoying it, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) himself descends into someone’s heart without checking the individual’s nature and gives enjoyment. He is said as in 8.6.3 “*uḷḷum tōṟum tittikkum amudu*” (sweet like nectar everytime he is thought about).
- *imaiyōr adipadiyē* – Like beetles, these nityasūris sustain themselves with this enjoyment only.
- *teṇṇal aruvi …* – Oh sarvēśvara who is standing on tirumalā where clear, beautiful waterfalls toss around gemstones, gold and pearls!
- *aṇṇalē* – Oh one who descended in tirumalā and eliminated any doubt in your supremacy! [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying “Though you are the lord of the nityasūris, you remain the one with beautiful cloud-like form, amazing lord, and being tiruvēngadattān who resides in tirumalā where waterfalls have gemstones, gold, pearls etc, and being my lord”.
- *un adi sēra adiyēṟku A A enṟāyē* – As you came close to me and revealed me the process, please make me attain the goal as well! Taking pity on me and manifesting your mercy, ensure that I, who have no other refuge, attain your divine feet! āren’t those your divine feet? Manifest your mercy such that I reach your divine feet which are the means, goal and the enjoyable object!

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.10.4. Ava ennadu

*āvā! ennādu ulagattai alaikkum asurar vāṇāḷ mēl tīvāy vāḷi maḻai poḻinda silaiyā! tirumā magaḷ kēḷvā dēvā! surargaḷ munik kaṇangaḷ virumbum tiruvēngadattānē! pūvār kaḻalgaḷ aruvinaiyēn porundumāṟu puṇarāyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ulagattai – world; A A – alas! alas! \[taking pity\]; ennādu – not showing mercy; alaikkum – those who torment; asurar – demons; vāṇāḷ mēl – on life; tīvāy – fire-faced; vāḷi – arrows; maḻai – like rain; poḻinda – shooting; silaiyā – oh one who is having śrī śārnga bow; tiru mā magaḷ – for lakshmi who is being the valourous consort and who is pleased after his eliminating such enemies; kēḷvā – being the aptly beautiful consort; dēvā – shining due to that; surargaḷ – dēvas (celestial beings); muni – riśis (sages); kaṇangaḷ – groups; virumbum – to be desired; tiruvēngadattānē – Oh one who resides in tirumalā!; pū – by flowers (offered by groups of celestial beings and sages); Ar – filled; kaḻalgaḷ – divine feet; aru – unconquerable; vinaiyēn – I, who am having sins; porundum – to reach; āṟu – means; puṇarāy – mercifully teach me

**Перевод:**

**Oh emperumān who is having śrī śārnga bow which is shooting fire-faced arrows like rain targeting the lives of demons who torment the world instead of showing mercy, taking pity on it! Oh one who is the aptly beautiful consort for lakshmi who is being the valourous consort and who is pleased after his eliminating such enemies, and is shining due to that! Oh one who resides in tirumalā to be desired by groups of dēvas and riśis! I am having unconquerable sins which stop me from reaching your divine feet filled with flowers; mercifully teach me the means to reach them.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fourth pāsuram, āḻvār says “I don’t have any means in me which will lead to you; hence you should find out a means and mercifully bestow that to me”. Also explained as āḻvār saying “You who eliminate everyone’s hurdles and protect them without any restriction, should mercifully ensure that I reach your divine feet”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. āvā! ennādu ulagattai alaikkum asurar vāṇāḷ mēl tīvāy vāḷi maḻai poḻinda silaiyā! tirumā magaḷ kēḷvā dēvā! surargaḷ munik kaṇangaḷ virumbum tiruvēngadattānē! pūvār kaḻalgaḷ aruvinaiyēn porundumāṟu puṇarāyē*

\[karma yōga, jñāna yōga, bhakti yōga and prapatti/śaraṇāgati are explained as the first four means. It is generally considered that [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) \[śaraṇāgati to him\] is the ultimate means. But ācārya abhimānam (mercy of ācārya) is explained as the fifth means in śrīvaiṣṇava sampradāyam. As ācārya is considered as the divine feet of bhagavān, this ācārya abhimānam is considered as the extension of the fourth upāyam. A conversation between [nanjīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nanjiyar/) and [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/) is highlighted by [vadakkut tiruvīdip piḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadakku-thiruvidhi-pillai/) in relation to ācārya abhimānam which is also known as pancamōpāyam (fifth upāyam)\]

Once nampiḷḷai mercifully asked nanjīyar “It is said that there is a pancamōpāyam; is it seen in this world?”. nanjīyar mercifully replied “I don’t know; as [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) is the fourth upāyam, talking about the fifth upāyam is similar to some people talking about vyōmātīta \[vyōmātīta is a claim made by pāśupata followers; they say that rudra is the antaryāmi for bhagavān śrīman nārāyaṇa, which is unfounded in śāstram\]; I have not heard about this” \[The principle here is, nanjīyar did not want to reveal about the secretive fifth upāyam in public\].

But while he was mercifully explaining this pāsuram, nampiḷḷai again asked “It appears that [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is asking [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) to present a separate means to him”, and nanjīyar mercifully responded “Oh! You have misunderstood the concept here; the meaning for āḻvār’s words is – while you (emperumān) are present, why I am still not attaining my goal” \[nanjīyar is categorically saying that there is no scope for any upāyam other than [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) in this case, as āḻvār is simply lamenting about the delay\]. mahābhāratam “*sāham kēśagraham prāpta – tvayijīvatyapiprabhō*” – \[draupadi said\] While you (kriṣṇa) were present, I was insulted by someone who dragged me by my hair!  Where is the match for your existence and my insult? *prabhō* – I could remain relaxed if you too were a woman like me; while you are capable of eliminating the insults, was I not still insulted!

\[The role of prapatti, our surrender is clarified through another conversation. Here it is explained that though [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is always present as the means, in the initial stages, our surrender acts as the qualification for the result and in the end, it becomes part of the result/goal\]

A disciple of nanjīyar asked him “While [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is the means, I am not seeing what we accomplish through our prapatti”, nanjīyar, closing his ears \[in anguish\], replied to him “The most confidential principle, which was explained by our ācāryas starting from nātamunigaḷ through succeeding disciples, has to be explained by me who is a great sinner, to you who do not understand its greatness!”, beating on his head \[again in anguish\] and brought him into the sanctum of emperumān.

Just as [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s divine form, the qualities of such divine form and the qualities of his true nature, are part of the goal for the [nityasūris](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) and [muktātmās](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/), for a qualified mumukśu (one who is desirous of liberation), the [dvayam](http://ponnadi.blogspot.in/2015/12/rahasya-thrayam.html) \[which emphasises on surrender\] itself is part of the goal.

- *A A ennādu* – To please [īśvara](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) means to show compassion towards his world. nanjīyar mercifully says “If one cannot tolerate the suffering of others, one can oneself determine ‘I have connection with [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)‘; but if one considers ‘it is alright for others to suffer’, then one can withdraw saying ‘I have no connection with bhagavān’ “.  Here, others means everyone other than self. But should we show compassion towards the unfavourable? Yes, that is the opinion of [āḻvārs](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/azhwars/)/[ācāryas](http://acharyas.koyil.org/). We should remain \[concerned for them too\] thinking “Oh they have not lost their evil interests and become favourable”. When [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) himself says in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 18.34 “*yadi vā rāvaṇa svayam*” (Even if rāvaṇa had come \[bring him along, he too is given refuge\]), should those who live in his world not have the same attitude? But how does it align with what is said in tiruvāimoḻi 10.7.5 “*naṇṇā asurar naliveyda*” (emperumān appears to destroy the demons who show hatred)? Well, when the hatred is deeply imprinted in them, he slays them. Just as the sacrifices done in yajñas such as agnīśōmīya are good for the animal that is sacrificed, this killing of demoniac persons is also good for them, since he rids the soul of the body which facilitates hatred and leads the soul into the path of goodness.
- *A A ennādu (ulagattai alaikkum)* – While the demons should take pity \[on the sufferers\], they will further torment them. It cannot be thought “they are fighting for wealth and lust; both are desirable \[and so are fighting\]”; instead of that, they are just tormenting the world. They would torment others just as they eat, wear clothes etc., i.e. as a natural activity.
- *asurar* – The reason for this is they are demoniac by nature.
- *vāṇāḷ mēl* – While their valourous decorations remain intact, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) attacked their life. That is, eliminating their life span.
- *tīvāy vāḷi* – When perumāḷ (śrī rāma) launches, it can be said as arrow. But once it reaches the target, it will be like fire ball piercing through. When the arrow leaves the string of śrī śārnga bow, it will travel like a branch of fire growing out. This is how it is when his qualities are subdued \[also said as, when the arrow leaves the string\]. śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 16.22 \[vibhīśaṇa tells rāvaṇa\] “*dīpta pāvaka sankāśai:*” (resembling blazing fire) – this is how it feels when the arrow hits someone. *śitai:* (Sharp) – Before realising being hit, it will pierce through and fall down on the other side of the body. *kāncana bhūśaṇai:* (adorned with gold) – they have two different manifestations (being ornament as well as weapon). As said in periya tirumoḻi 7.3.4 “*sarangaḷāṇḍa taṇḍāmaraik kaṇṇanukkanṟi en manam tāḻndu nillādu*” (My heart will not wait for anyone but śrī rāma who has reddish lotus like eyes and who controls the arrows), it is his bow and arrow which help capture the favourable ones too. *na tvām iccāmi* (do not wish to see you killed) – while one can live being the target of such beauty, I do not wish to see you being killed. I don’t know what you are thinking. When I see him standing with the firm bow and the arrow, he looks so beautiful to me; just as one will drown in a lake which was dug to quench the thirst, I can’t see you fight with him and get killed instead of enjoying his beauty. He is known as a lake as said in tiruvāimoḻi 10.1.8 “*dayaradan peṟṟa maragada maṇit tadam*” (the green-gem like pond who is born to daśarata).
- *vāḷi maḻai poḻinda silaiyā* – As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 94.18 “*śaravarśam vavarśaha*” (did he not pour down a rain of arrows?), he poured down arrows heavily.
- *tiru mā magaḷ kēḷvā* – Here [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is speaking about the one who joyfully embraces after seeing him defeat the enemies. One who does as in śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 30.39 “*bartāram pariśasvajē*” (embraced her husband).
   - *tam druśtvā* – She saw [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), who should be warded off evil eyes even normally, in his valourous form after defeating the enemies.
   - *śatruhantāram* – Not only he slaughtered them without any impact for his own body, he also cut them into pieces. Previously when they were in śrī ayōdyā, she would hear from the relatives about his hunting trips “when he went for hunting, he fought like this; he stabbed a tiger, he stabbed a lion”. She witnessed all such acts when he started fighting.
   - *maharśīṇām sukāvaham* – one who eliminated the enemies of the sages and let them live there peacefully. For those who knew their true nature – while they could have defeated the demons using the power of their penances, they depended fully on śrī rāma. śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 1.21 “*garbabhūtās tapōdanā:*” – those who fully depend on emperumān even when they lost their prime wealth. While they had the wealth of their penance, they were also like foetus in the womb (fully dependent). While the foetus can try on its own, when it is in the womb, only the mother will have to protect it; similarly these sages were also fully dependent on [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) for his protection. emperumān protects the favourable ones and annihilates the unfavourable ones, only for pirātti’s pleasure.
   - *babhūva* – On seeing his lone battle with the fourteen thousand powerful demons, she remained frightened and lifeless thinking “what will happen now?”, but now she regained her life. *bhū sattāyām* – The root of the word bhūta, that which exists.
   - *hruśtā* – As she regained her life, the bliss which naturally exists there also manifested.
   - *vaidēhi* – Just as the daughters of the teachers who teach vēdam would have memorized vēdam just by hearing their fathers teach the students, sītā (vaidēhi) is born in the vidēha clan/dynasty which knows the nature of valour; how will my father, who gave me in marriage to him just for breaking a bow, feel when he sees his victory over fourteen thousand demons on his own!
   - *bartāram* – Previously, as śrī rāma was tender-hearted, she considered him to be immature and embraced him thinking “I am subservient to him since my father gave me in marriage to him”; only now, she embraced him thinking to be a true man;
   - *pariśasvajē* – Fourteen thousand demons who were equivalent to rāvaṇa in strength and were respected by him, shot arrows on śrī rāma and hence his body was full of scars of war; she pressed all those spots with her divine bosom to comfort him.
- *tiru mā magaḷ kēḷvā* – Am I losing you due to your lack of strength? ōr is it due to lack of puruśakāram (recommendation from pirātti)?
- *dēvā* – The radiance which he acquired after her embrace \[divu – radiance\]. Alternatively, it could highlight the radiance acquired on eliminating the enemies. (The divine abode tirumalā which is considered and glorified by the dēvas and riśis thinking “This is the abode where the slayer of our enemies resides” and hoping that their desires too will be fulfilled).
- *surargaḷ …* – The divine abode where all the favourable ones wait for him patiently.
- *pū Ar kaḻalgaḷ* – Explained as the divine feet which cannot sustain without the flowers. Also explained as divine feet which are similar to flowers.
- *aruvinaiyēn* – He is capable of eliminating the hurdles; I have unlimited desire; his divine feet are infinitely enjoyable; still, I am having sin to not reach there and enjoy the same.
- *porundumāṟu puṇarāyē* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is considering himself to be similar to sītā in aśōka vanam.
- *puṇarāyē* – āḻvār says “you should create the means to make me reach your divine feet” or “you should ensure that I reach your divine feet”.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

adiyen saraty ramanuja dasan

## 6.10.5. Punara ninra

*puṇarā ninṟa maram ēḻ anṟeyda oru vil valavāvō! puṇarēy ninṟa maram iraṇḍin naduvē pōna mudalvāvō! tiṇarār mēgam enak kaḷiṟu sērum tiruvēngadattānē! tiṇarār sārngattuna pādam sērvadadiyēn ennāḷē?*

**Пословный перевод:**

puṇarā ninṟa – standing as a collection; maram – marāmarams (ebony trees); ēḻ – seven; anṟu – on that day (when sugrīva mahārāja doubted śrī rāma’s ability); eyda – shot (to instill faith in him); oru vil valavā – being the unique archer; puṇar – togetherness; ēy – to fit well; ninṟa – standing; maram iraṇḍin – two trees; naduvē – in between; pōna – crawled; mudalvā – being the primary cause of the universe; tiṇar – density; Ar – abundance; mēgam – clouds; ena – to say; kaḷiṟu – elephants; sērum – residing together; tiruvēngadattānē – one who is present in tirumalā!; tiṇar – greatness (of filling the hands which hold on); Ar – having; sārngam – śrī sārnga bow; una – your; pādam – divine feet; adiyēn – I who am a servitor (being captivated by your valorous history); sērvadu – reaching; ennāḷ – when?; O – revealing the agony of not uniting yet

**Перевод:**

**emperumān being the unique archer, shot the seven marāmarams on that day; being the primary cause for the universe, he crawled between the two trees which were standing together, fitting well; Oh one who is present in tirumalā where the elephants, which are said to be like dense clouds, reside together! When am I, a servitor, will reach the divine feet of you who is having the great śrī sārnga bow!?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fifth pāsuram, emperumān mercifully says “I will fulfil all your desires” and āḻvār asks “When will that happen?”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “When will I reach your divine feet which carry out effortless functions for the protection of the devotees?”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. puṇarā ninṟa maram ēḻ anṟeyda oru vil valavāvō! puṇarēy ninṟa maram iraṇḍin naduvē pōna mudalvāvō! tiṇarār mēgam enak kaḷiṟu sērum tiruvēngadattānē! tiṇarār sārngattuna pādam sērvadadiyēn ennāḷē?*

- *puṇarā* … – Don’t the kśatriyas (warriors) uphold the bow to not hear the sorrowful cries? śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 10.3 “*kśatriyair dāryatē cāpam nārtaśabdōbavēditi*” (A warrior upholds the bow so that crying sound is not heard). Oh brave one who straightened the seven crowded trees by your strength and stance and shot at them!
- O – O highlights the great sorrow. You who proved your abilities to those who doubted your protection, are not helping me who is desirous of you! samkśēpa rāmāyaṇam 63 “*sugrīvaś śankitaścāsīt …*” – From the day he saw perumāḷ (śrī rāma) and until he shot down the seven ebony trees, sugrīva kept doubting perumāḷ’s abilities. Should you who protected him after eliminating his doubt, not protect me who is holding on to you without any doubt?
- *puṇarā …* –  Piercing through the seven ebony trees which stood together, like someone who could casually go through a door, Oh you who protected yourself who is the root of the universe! He did not create the universe after the deluge; only today. He was present then, so he could easily create the universe; but here his existence was threatened \[had he been destroyed, the universe which sustains on him would have also been destroyed\].
- *mudalvā O!* – Oh one who created the universe! Here he protected himself who is the root of the universe; as said in cāndōjña upaniśat 6.2.1 “*sadēva sōmya idam agra āsīt*” (Only sat existed before creation, there was nothing else). Only when he exists, the universe will also exist. Would he only save himself from such danger! \[Implies – would he not save me from such danger!\]
- *tiṇar …* – Oh one who is mercifully standing in tirumalā where elephants which resemble dense clouds are residing together! Since clouds and elephants are totally similar, clouds can be considered as elephants and elephants can be considered as clouds. nācciyār tirumoḻi 8.9 “*mada yānai pōl eḻunda māmugilgāḷ*” (Oh great clouds which rise like mad elephants). āḻvār is not talking about anyatā jñānam (misunderstanding an object to be something else) in that abode, but everything is enjoyable for him there.
- *tiṇar Ar sārngattu una pādam* – The divine feet of you who are having the great śrī sārnga bow. The divine feet which are the refuge as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 94.17 “*śaraṇyam śaraṇam yātā rāmam daśaratātmajam*” (reached the divine feet of the son of daśarata, which are the apt refuge). Whatever is picked up by the sons of emperor daśarata, that turns into bow.
- *tiṇar Ar sārngam* – Capturing the enemies in his curved bow.
- *una pādam* – Those who are not captured by the bow \[i.e. the favourable ones\], will be captured by his feet.
- *sērvadu adiyēn en nāḷē* – Since you have the bow in your hands, we won’t lose you fearing for the hurdles; now, you just need to inform when I will attain you.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.10.6. En nale

*en nāḷē nām maṇ aḷanda iṇait tāmaraigaḷ kāṇbadaṟkenṟu en nāḷum ninṟu imaiyōrgaḷ ētti iṟainji inam inamāy mey nā manattāl vaḻipādu seyyum tiruvēngadattānē! mey nān eydi en nāḷ un adikkaṇ adiyēn mēvuvadē?*

**Пословный перевод:**

maṇ – all worlds indicated by earth; aḷanda – measured and mingled with everyone, having overwhelming simplicity; tāmaraigaḷ – divine lotus feet; iṇai – both; nām – we (who enjoy his supremacy); kāṇbadaṟku – to see; e – that; nāḷēm – having the day; enṟu – that; imaiyōrgaḷ – nityasūris who have unfailing knowledge; en nāḷum – always; ninṟu – standing; ētti – praising in this manner; iṟainji – vorśipping; inam inamāy – in groups; meyn nā manattāl – with the body, speech and mind; vaḻipādu – serve; seyyum – to perform; tiruvēngadattānē – Oh one who is present in tirumalā!; adiyēn – being an exclusive servitor; nān – I (who am desirous); mey – seen in dream; eydi – attain; un – your; adikkaṇ – at the divine feet; mēvuvadu – fit properly; en nāḷ – when!

**Перевод:**

**Groups of nityasūris are always standing and praising emperumān saying “when will we get to see both of your divine feet which measured all worlds indicated by earth and mingled with everyone,  and are having overwhelming simplicity”. Oh one who is present in tirumalā to be vorśipped in this manner and to be served by them! When will I, being an exclusive servitor, attain your divine feet like seeing \[clearly\] in a dream, and fit there properly.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the sixth pāsuram, emperumān says “īsn’t performing kainkaryam to me in śrīvaikuṇṭam the goal for all?” and āḻvār responds “āren’t those from śrīvaikuṇṭam descending to tirumalā with great desire and serving you? When will I get to serve you in tirumalā completely?”. Also explained as āḻvār asking “When will I truly attain your divine feet which are attractive to be served even by dēvas who are not exclusively devoted to you?”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. en nāḷē nām maṇ aḷanda iṇait tāmaraigaḷ kāṇbadaṟkenṟu en nāḷum ninṟu imaiyōrgaḷ ētti iṟainji inam inamāy mey nā manattāl vaḻipādu seyyum tiruvēngadattānē! mey nān eydi en nāḷ un adikkaṇ adiyēn mēvuvadē?*

- *en nāḷē nām maṇ aḷanda iṇait tāmaraigaḷ kāṇbadaṟku enṟu* – Just as those who are here \[[āḻvārs/ācāryas](http://acharyas.koyil.org/)\] desire to go to paramapadam to serve him as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 3.2.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/07/thiruvaimozhi-3-2-1-munnir-gyalam/) “*ennāḷ yān unnai ini vandu kūduvanē*” (When will I reach you there?), those who are there (nityasūris) desire to see his saulabhyam (simplicity) here in tirumalā. When will I get to see the most easily accessible [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s divine feet? The divine feet which effortlessly measured the earth and seeing such act, one would desire to keep those feet on his/her head due to their enjoyability.
- *en nāḷum* – They \[āḻvārs\] would never have anything else to do at any time.
- *imaiyōrgaḷ …* – nityasūris, would praise him forever and then fall at his divine feet, and like those who venture as groups into flooded river ….
- *meyn nā …* – … surrender unto him \[in groups\] with their mind, speech and body. Alternative explanation – they would worship with their mind, speech and body. That is, they will surrender unto him with their faculties which are exclusively devoted to him. When “*imaiyōrgaḷ*” implies nityasūris, their acts are considered as kainkaryam (service); when it is said in the context of dēvas such as brahmā et al, their acts are considered as upāsanā (worship \[to get something other than [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)\]).
- *meyn nān eydi …* – I will not be satisfied by just meditating upon your qualities and enjoying you in my heart/mind; When will I fully reach your divine feet, and not be ever separated? Even if [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) loses grip of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s one divine foot, his existence will become doubtful.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.10.7. Adiyen mevi

*adiyēn mēvi amarginṟa amudē! imaiyōr adipadiyē! kodiyā adu puḷ udaiyānē! kōlak kani vāyp perumānē! sediyār vinaigaḷ tīr marundē! tiruvēngadattemperumānē! nodiyār poḻudum una pādam kāṇa nōlādāṟṟēnē.*

**Пословный перевод:**

adiyēn – I (who have natural servitude towards you); mēvi – approach; amarginṟa – to experience eternally; amudē – eternally enjoyable; imaiyōr – for them (nityasūris); adipadiyē – \[adipati\] having the supremacy to control them; adu – being the one who eliminates the enemies of devotees; puḷ – periya tiruvadi (garudāḻvān); kodiyā – as flag; udaiyānē – one who is having; kōlam – having beauty etc which increase such enjoyability; kani – reddish like a ripened fruit; vāy – having beautiful lips; perumānē – having greatness of unlimited enjoyability; sedi – like bush; Ar – dense; vinaigaḷ – sins; tīr – to eliminate; marundē – being the best medicine; tiruvēngadattu – residing on tirumalā; em – me; perumānē – oh one who accepted as servitor!; una – your; pādam – divine feet; kāṇa – to see; nōlādu – without any effort; nodi – a fraction; Ar – of; poḻudu – moment; āṟṟēn – cannot bear

**Перевод:**

**emperumān is eternally enjoyable for me to approach and experience him; he is having the supremacy to control the nityasūris; he is having garudāḻvān who eliminates the enemies of devotees, as his flag; he is having beautiful lips which are like reddish ripened fruit with beauty etc which increase such enjoyability and is having greatness of such unlimited enjoyability; oh one who is residing on tirumalā, being the best medicine to eliminate the dense bush like sins of mine, and who accepted me as your servitor! While I have not put in any effort to see your divine feet, I cannot bear even a fraction of a moment \[without seeing them\].**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the seventh pāsuram, āḻvār says “While I have not pursued any means to attain you, I cannot sustain even for a moment without experiencing your enjoyability”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Seventh pāsuram. emperumān says “You have acquired this knowledge to say ‘meynnāneydi‘; that will certainly lead to the result; why not you be patient then?”, āḻvār responds “Your enjoyability does not let me wait patiently; I cannot sustain without you”. adiyēn mēvi amarginṟa amudē! imaiyōr adipadiyē! kodiyā adu puḷ udaiyānē! kōlak kani vāyp perumānē! sediyār vinaigaḷ tīr marundē! tiruvēngadattemperumānē! nodiyār poḻudum una pādam kāṇa nōlādāṟṟēnē.*

- *adiyēn mēvi amarginṟa amudē* – This \[nectar\] is unlike the salt water of dēvas; and it is not enjoyed in groups collectively \[it is enjoyed by me\]; this is the nectar which is enjoyed by the exclusive devotees of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)!
- *imaiyōr adipadiyē* – There is a group waiting to accompany while enjoying this nectar there \[in paramapadam\].
- *kodiyā adu puḷ udaiyānē* – Oh one who is having periya tiruvadi who has eliminating the enemies as a natural quality, as your flag!
- *kōlak kani vāyp perumānē* – Oh one who mesmerized and captured me by showing the reddish complexion of your beautiful, ripened lips! [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) was captured by his lips \[or just the physical beauty\]. It appears that [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) has hoisted the garuda flag to let his devotees enjoy his beauty.
- *sedi Ar vinaigaḷ tīr marundē* – sedi – sin; Oh one who is the medicine to remove the sorrows caused by vices which are filled with sins! Eliminating the hurdles to let one enjoy his beauty. Alternative explanation – Oh one who is the medicine for the karma (vices) which are dense and deep! The nectar itself is the medicine. There is no medicine other than him as said in [mūnṟām tiruvandādi 4](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/02/munram-thiruvandhadhi-4/) “*marundum poruḷum amudamum tānē*” (He (his divine feet) is the medicine, wealth and nectar) and in tiruvāimoḻi 9.3.4 “*marundē nangaḷ bōga magiḻccikku*” (He is the medicine for our enjoyment); he is as said in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 5.3.6 as “*maruttuvanāy ninṟa māmaṇivaṇṇan*” (The great maṇivaṇṇan, who is a doctor).
- *tiruvēngadattu emperumānē* – For those who consume that nectar, it is like a medicine from the mountain.  For those who consume that nectar, it remains like a jar (from which water is poured from the top) which is nicely placed on a high position. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying “Being the lord of nityasūris, having garuda as his flag, being the medicine for deep/dense sins, being the lord of tirumalā, being the one with reddish, beautiful, ripened lips – Oh the nectar who is approached and enjoyed by me!”. When bhattar was asked “in \[[emperumānār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/emperumanar/)‘s\] nitya grantam \[a grantam describing the home [tiruvārādanam](http://ponnadi.blogspot.in/2012/07/srivaishnava-thiruvaaraadhanam.html) process\], when it says ‘while offering food to emperumān, recite these stōtrams (verses in praise), which pāsurams/ślōkams are indicated there?”, he mercifully explains “Recite pāsurams such as ‘*adiyēn mēvi amarginṟa amudē*‘, [tirumālai 2](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/08/thirumalai-2-part-2/) ‘*paccai mā malai pōl mēni*‘ etc”.
- *nodi Ar poḻudum* – Even the moment which can be filled with a second.
- *una pādam kāṇa nōlādu āṟṟēnē* – While I have not pursued any means to see your divine feet, I cannot bear even for a moment \[not seeing them\]. I am in anguish as if I have pursued the means and am waiting for the result. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is in agony due to not having any means on his own \[such as karma, jñāna, bhakti yōgas\]. For a person who pursued other means \[than [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) himself\], he can remain patient thinking “Once I complete the process, I will get the result” or “Due to the shortcomings in the pursuit, the result is being delayed”; but for āḻvār who considers emperumān only as the means, when the result is delayed, he becomes frightened thinking “Am I so unfortunate that even his mercy is not flowing on me successfully!”.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.
