## 6.10.8. Noladarren

*nōlādāṟṟēn una pādam kāṇavenṟu nuṇṇuṇarvin neelār kaṇḍattammānum niṟai nānmuganum indiranum sēlēy kaṇṇār palar sūḻa virumbum tiruvēngadattānē! mālāy mayakki adiyēnpāl vandāy pōlē vārāyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

una – your; pādam – divine feet; kāṇa – to see; nōlādu – without pursuing any means; āṟṟēn – I am not able to bear; enṟu – saying this; nuṇ uṇarvil – since he is omniscient, being able to see subtle things; neela – black colour; Ar – fully; kaṇḍam – having throat; ammānum – rudra, who became important one in the universe due to that; niṟai – being the father of such rudra, and having complete knowledge to create etc; nānmuganum – four-headed brahmā; indiranum – indra who has the wealth of three worlds (bhū:, bhuva: and svarga worlds); sēl ēy – like a fish; kaṇṇār – having eyes; sūḻa – being in their proximity; virumbum – surrender with desire; tiruvēngadattānē – Oh one who is residing in tirumalā!; māl āy – having dark complexion; mayakki – mesmerising everyone with the qualities and activities; vandāy pōlē – like you came; adiyēnpāl – towards me who is exclusively devoted to you and cannot sustain without you; vārāy – you should come!

**Перевод:**

**rudra who is omniscient, being able to see subtle things and hence became the important one in the universe and is having throat that is fully having black colour, four-headed brahmā who is the father of such rudra, and having complete knowledge to create etc and indra who has the wealth of three worlds say \[to emperumān\] “Even without pursuing any means to see your divine feet, I am unable to bear”;  Oh one who is residing in tirumalā and who is offered such prayers and surrendered with desire by such dēvas along with their women folk such as umā (pārvati), sarasvatī, śaci et al who have fish like eyes, in their proximity! Just as you came \[as kriṣṇa\] with dark complexion, mesmerising everyone with the qualities and activities, you should come towards me who is exclusively devoted to you and cannot sustain without you!**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the eighth pāsuram, emperumān asks “When you have not put in any effort and say ‘I cannot bear’, would you get the result?” and āḻvār responds “ḍidn’t brahmā et al who are with limited ability, get their desires fulfilled by citing their ākincanyam (lack of anything in them)? So, kindly come and eliminate my sorrow”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. nōlādāṟṟēn una pādam kāṇavenṟu nuṇṇuṇarvin neelār kaṇḍattammānum niṟai nānmuganum indiranum sēlēy kaṇṇār palar sūḻa virumbum tiruvēngadattānē! mālāy mayakki adiyēnpāl vandāy pōlē vārāyē*

- *nōlādu …* – They (dēvas) all individually say “I have not pursued any means to see your divine feet, yet I cannot bear without you”. When they \[Siva and others\] lose in a battle like the one \[of kriṣṇa\] with bāṇa, without any other refuge, they say like this. \[Why do they behave in this contradictory manner?\] When rajas (passion) and tamas (ignorance) are on the rise, they would consider as in [śrī bhagavat gītā 16.14](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/16-14/) “*īśvarōham*” (I am the lord); when they are defeated, they would praise him as in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 5.33.41 “*kriṣṇa kriṣṇa mahābāhō jānētvām puruśōttamam*” (kriṣṇa! kriṣṇa! Oh mighty armed! I know you as the best among the men); śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 1.9.65 “*śaraṇam tvām anuprāptās samastā dēvatā gaṇām*” (Oh lord! all the dēvas who were defeated by the army of asuras are surrendering unto you with folded hands). rudra who considers himself as the primary entity in the universe due to his power of holding the poison in his throat, the four-headed brahmā who is the father of rudra and who has even greater knowledge and powers than rudra, indra who is the controller of the three worlds; \[āḻvār is following the pattern of vēdāntam\] nārāyaṇa sūktam “*sa brahmā sa śivas sēndra:*” (he is brahmā, he is Siva, he is indra). When asked though they are like this, we considered their words in ahirbudnya samhitā as authentic instructions, it is because they spoke those words when their satva guṇam (goodness) was on the rise. Just because their words are accepted, it does not mean that they are to be pursued; bhattar used to explain mercifully “It is said by periyāḻvār ‘*kākkai vāyilum katturai koḷvār*‘ (one would even hear from a crow)”.
   - An āḻvār \[tirumaḻisai āḻvār\] said in nānmugan tiruvandādi 84 “*pidrumanam ilēn*” – I do not have a confused mind; “*pinjagan tannōdu edirvan*” – I am comparable to rudra in his knowledge; “*avan enakku nērān*” – yet he is not a match for me \[in my exclusive servitude to [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)\]; why is that? “*adirum …*” – for me who has placed my heart only in matters related to bhagavān, would rudra who has his interest in various matters, be comparable?
   - \[Next, brahmā’s ākincanyam is highlighted\] nānmugan tiruvandādi 9 “*kuṟai koṇḍu*” – having lack of anything in him, as the tool; “*nānmugan kuṇḍigai nīr peydu*” – without brahmā’s intention, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s divine feet reached there; he did not have any tool to worship them. \[Hence\] dharma dēvatā became the water in his pot; with that, “*maṟai koṇḍa mandirattāl vāḻtti*” – praised emperumān with the portions of vēdāntam \[such as puruśa sūktam\] which sing the glories of bhagavān; “*kaṟai koṇḍa kaṇḍattān senni mēl ēṟak kaḻuvinān*” – brahmā let that water flow on to the head of Siva, just like a father would sprinkle śrīpāda tīrtam (sacred water) on his disobedient children \[to purify them\].
- *nun uṇarvil* – When satvam is on the rise, they would only praise [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/). It is said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 14.17](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/14-17/) “*satvāt sanjāyatē jñānam*” (satva guṇam leads to knowledge).
- *neelār kaṇḍattu ammānum* – rudra who considers himself the lord due to holding the poison in his throat.
- *niṟai nānmuganum* – brahmā who is the father of such rudra and who is complete in knowledge.
- *indiranum* – Though he is not involved in creation or annihilation similar to brahmā and rudra, he is still counted along with them as said in nārāyaṇa sūktam “*sa brahmā sa śivas sēndra:*” (he is brahmā, he is Siva, he is indra).
- *sēl ēy kaṇṇar …* – When some one has some greatness, he would not remain humble in front of women; \[but\] when in danger they would come along with their women folk and surrender unto him. They will take shelter of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) along with their wives as seen in hari vamśam 279.15 “*umā sārdam īśāna:*” (rudra along with his wife umā, with joined palms, desired to speak the glories of viṣṇu), śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 5.7.57 “*bartru bikśā pradīyatām*” (wife of kāliya, the snake, prayed to kriṣṇa “spare my husband from your wrath”), samkśēpa rāmāyaṇam 79 “*samudras saritām pati:*” (samudrarāja, the lord of rivers appeared) and śrī rāmāyaṇam kiśkindā kāṇḍam 33.40 “*kim kōpa mūlam*” (tārā asked lakśmaṇa “what is the cause of your anger?”).
- *tiruvēngadattānē* – His presence in tirumalā which is easily accessible for such persons \[who are looking for a refuge\].
- *mālāy mayakki* – māl as per tamiḻ dictionary means “*mayangalum kūdalum kalaviyum*” (bewilderment, moment before uniting, the union); explained as āḻvār saying “you should arrive to bewilder me”; or as saying “you should arrive in a mesmerising form to make me mad”; but these are not the correct meanings here. māl indicates black, by which āḻvār thinks about kriṣṇa. Just as you appeared as kriṣṇa and made those who were with you to become mad for you, you should come for me too once; as said in nācciyār tirumoḻi 14.3 “*mālāy piṟanda nambiyai, mālē seyyum maṇāḷanai*” (the complete one who was born as kriṣṇa, who caused madness in others).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.10.9. Vanday pole

*vandāy pōlē vārādāy vārādāy pōl varuvānē sendāmaraik kaṇ sengani vāy nāṟṟōḷamudē enaduyirē sindāmaṇigaḷ pagarallaip pagal sey tiruvēngadattānē andō adiyēn una pādam agalagillēn iṟaiyumē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vandāy pōlē – as if arrived and being within reach; vārādāy – being unreachable; vārādāy pōl – due to ākincanyam (lack of anything) in self, while thinking “there is no possibility of his arrival”; varuvānē – arriving and being fully subservient; sem – reddish; tāmarai – attractive like lotus (will make one say “jitam” (victory)); kaṇ – divine eyes; sem – reddish; kani – enjoyable like fruit; vāy – the divine lips which say “māmēkam śaraṇam vraja”; nāl – four; tōḷ – having divine shoulders; amudē – being eternally enjoyable for the devotees; enadu – manifesting to me; uyirē – became my sustaining force; sindā – \[cintā\] wish fulfilling; maṇigaḷ – valuable gemstones; pagar – radiance; allai – night; pagal – day; sey – making; tiruvēngadattānē – Oh one who resides in tirumalā!; andō – alas!; una – your; pādam – divine feet; adiyēn – the totally subservient me, who has no other refuge; iṟaiyum – not even a moment; agala – to leave; killēn – unable to do

**Перевод:**

**You are unreachable while appearing to have arrived and being within reach; due to ākincanyam (lack of anything) in self, while thinking “there is no possibility of his arrival”, you will arrive and be fully subservient. You are manifesting to me your beautiful form with reddish, attractive, lotus-like divine eyes, divine lips which are enjoyable like reddish fruit and which say “māmēkam śaraṇam vraja“, four divine shoulders which embrace devotees saying “sugādam pariśasvajē” and are eternally enjoyable for the devotees, and have become my sustaining force; Oh one who is residing on tirumalā where the radiance of valuable, wish fulfilling gemstones make night to be like day! Alas! I, who am totally subservient to you, without any other refuge, am unable to leave your divine feet even for a moment. andō implies āḻvār wondering “Even after having so much sorrow in separation, I have to even manifest my desire separately!”.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the ninth pāsuram, since āḻvār did not see emperumān as soon as he desired, he says “If I don’t see you immediately, I will not survive even for a moment”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “I will never leave your divine feet which are having most enjoyable beauty”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. vandāy pōlē vārādāy vārādāy pōl varuvānē sendāmaraik kaṇ sengani vāy nāṟṟōḷamudē enaduyirē sindāmaṇigaḷ pagarallaip pagal sey tiruvēngadattānē andō adiyēn una pādam agalagillēn iṟaiyumē*

- *vandāypōlē vārādāy* – Due to the overwhelming internal experience, one would feel “we have got external experience” and be satisfied, and would consider that to be real and stretch his/her hand to embrace him – at that time [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) would be unreachable.
- *vārādāypōl varuvānē* – When one thinks “he will never be reachable”, he quickly arrives and is at one’s disposal. Alternative explanation – In the case of those who are not surrendered, when they think “he is within our reach”, he will remain outside their reach, and in the case of those who are surrendered, when they think “he is unreachable”, he would arrive and be at their disposal.
- *sem tāmarai …* – Oh one who is enjoyable due to having cool, divine eyes which will remove all sufferings, reddish, ripened, divine lips, and divine shoulders which appear like branched out kalpa taru (wish-fulfilling, celestial tree)!
- *enaduyirē* – Oh one who let me enjoy this beautiful form and made me to not sustain myself in separation from you!
- *sindā maṇigaḷ …* – The radiance of distinguished gemstones which turned night into day; eliminating the difference between day and night. periya tirumoḻi 4.10.8 “*maṇigaḷin oḷiyāl vidi pagal iravenṟāṟivaridāya*” (due to the radiance of the gemstones, unable to differentiate between day and night). With this, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is thinking about experiencing the bliss of paramapadam which is described as “*na kāla: tatravai prabhu:*” (Time is not the controller in paramapadam), right here in tirumalā itself.
- *andō* – While there is infinite enjoyment, he is also present here and I am also having great desire, I am unable to reach him and enjoy him! \[What a pity!\]
- *adiyēn una pādam agalagillēn iṟaiyumē* – You are not realising my state on seeing my true nature; while seeing your divine feet, I cannot even take my eyes off for a moment, where such act will enhance the experience, while seeing again.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 6.10.11. Adikkil amarndu

*adik kīḻ amarndu pugundu adiyīr! vāḻmin enṟenṟaruḷ kodukkum padikkēḻ illāp perumānaip paḻanak kurugūrc catakōpan mudippān sonna āyirattut tiruvēngadattukkivai pattum pidittār pidittār vīṟṟirundu periya vānuḷ nilāvuvarē*

**Пословный перевод:**

adiyīr – Oh servitors!; adik kīḻ – under my divine feet; amarndu – being ananya sādanar (not pursuing any means other than emperumān) and ananya prayōjanar (not desiring for anything other than kainkaryam); pugundu – enter; vāḻmin – eternally enjoy!; enṟu enṟu – saying so; aruḷ – his mercy; kodukkum – bestowing; padi – the manner in which; kēḻ – match; illā – not having; perumānai – towards emperumān who is greater than all; paḻanam – having invigorating water bodies; kurugūr – leader of āḻvārtirunagari; satakōpan – nammāḻvār; mudippān – to fulfil all his desires; sonna – mercifully spoke; āyirattu – among the thousand pāsurams; tiruvēngadattukku – focussed on tirumalā; ivai – these; pattum – ten pāsurams; pidittār – those who hold on to the pāsurams; pidittār – those who hold on to the meanings of the pāsurams (all of them); periya – having infinite greatness; vānuḷ – paramapadam which is indicated by the term “parmavyōma” (great sky); vīṟṟirundu – being present in a distinguished manner (to highlight their connection with this decad); nilāvuvar – live there with eternal enjoyment

**Перевод:**

**emperumān who is greater than all is bestowing his mercy in a matchless manner saying “Oh servitors! Enter under my divine feet and eternally enjoy being ananya sādanar and ananya prayōjanar”; nammāḻvār, the leader of āḻvārtirunagari which is having invigorating water bodies, mercifully spoke about such emperumān to fulfil all his desires in these ten pāsurams among the thousand pāsurams; those who hold on to these pāsurams and their meanings, will be present in the infinitely great paramapadam which is indicated by the term “parmavyōma”, in a distinguished manner and live there with eternal enjoyment.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the end, āḻvār says “All those who learn this decad will reach paramapadam, be crowned for servitude and will get to engage in service”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. adik kīḻ amarndu pugundu adiyīr! vāḻmin enṟenṟaruḷ kodukkum padikkēḻ illāp perumānaip paḻanak kurugūrc catakōpan mudippān sonna āyirattut tiruvēngadattukkivai pattum pidittār pidittār vīṟṟirundu periya vānuḷ nilāvuvarē*

- *adik kīḻ …* –  Saying “īsn’t this what you desire for? Hold on to this, be fully immersed and remain as one who accomplished everything that needs to be done”.
- *aruḷ kodukkum padik kēḻ illāp perumānai* – sarvēśvara who has no match in bestowing his mercy towards his devotees. Even kriṣṇa who said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 18.66](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/18-66/) “*mā śuca:*” (do not worry) is not a match for tiruvēngadamudaiyān’s mercy.
- *paḻanak kurugūrc catakōpan* – [nammāḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/), the leader of [āḻvārtirunagari](http://azhwarthirunagari.koyil.org/) which has fine water bodies.
- *mudippān …* – This decad for tirumalā among the thousand pāsurams which were mercifully spoken with great enthusiasm in his divine heart to eliminate the hurdles of this samsāram (material) which were explained in [tiruvāimoḻi 6.9.9](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/06/thiruvaimozhi-6-9-9-avi-thigaikka/) “*pala nītti kattip paduppāyō*” (are you planning to finish me by revealing varieties of pleasures?). As said in “*ratnahārīca pārtiva:*” (one who owns the most precious gemstone is the king).
- *pidittār pidittār* – Those who hold on to the ones who hold on to [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/); those who surrendered to the devotees of emperumān.
- *vīṟṟirundu* – Attaining the throne is not the same for both (jīvātmā and paramātmā) as said in cāndōjña upaniśat 7.25 “*sasvarāt bhavati*” (muktātmā becomes independent). The liberated soul acquires bliss by being the servitor of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who has everyone other than himself as his servitors. The ātmā who becomes blissful by the mercy of emperumān as said in taittirīya upaniśat ānandavalli 7 “*ēśahyēvānandayāti*” (he – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) – himself makes jīvātmā ecstatic).
- *periya vānuḷ nilāvuvarē* – They will get to reside in paramapadam which is known as “*mahāgam*” (great) and “*paramākāśam*” (supreme sky). This is not the heavenly sky which is inhabited by indra et al \[part of the materialistic realm\]. They will enter the abode where one need not perform surrender to attain the goal and one simply will enjoy there eternally. His surrender is sufficient for all of us; we need not surrender separately; just by reciting this pāsuram, one can attain the goal. Just as a cow will provide milk on seeing a made-up calf in place of the real calf, īśvara will be delighted seeing those who learn this decad, thinking about [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/). śrī vībhīśaṇāḻvān’s surrender was sufficient for the four soldiers who accompanied him \[when he went to śrī rāma to surrender\]. All that is needed is to make [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) believe that we belong to such āḻvār \[āḻvārs, ācāryas\].

## Seventh Centum

## 7.1 Unnilaviya

## 7.1.1. Unnilaviya

*uṇṇilāviya aivarāl kumai tīṟṟi ennai un pāda pangayam naṇṇilā vagaiyē nalivān innam eṇṇuginṟāy eṇṇilāp peru māyanē! imaiyōrgaḷ ēttum ulagamūnṟudai aṇṇalē! amudē! appanē! ennai āḷvānē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

uḷ – inside; nilāviya – being the internal enemy due to residing permanently; aivarāl – with the senses; kumai tīṟṟi – torture; ennai – me (who surrendered unto you fearing them); un – you who are apt, enjoyable; pāda pangayam – divine feet; naṇṇilā vagaiyē – to not reach; innam – even after having acquired the urge (as said in tiruvāimoḻi 6.9.9 “kāttip paduppāyō” (are you planning to finish me by revealing varieties of pleasures?)); nalivān – torment (by placing in samsāram); eṇṇuginṟāy – you are thinking; eṇṇilā – countless; peru – unlimited; māyanē – having the amazing prakruti tatvam (matter) as prakāram (form); imaiyōrgaḷ – by nityasūris (who are untouched by samsāram and have unfailing knowledge); ēttum – praised; mūnṟu ulagam – three types of cētanas (sentient beings) and acētanas (insentient entities); udai – having them as subservient entities; aṇṇalē – being the lord; amudē – naturally having eternal enjoyability; appanē – being a benefactor right from the beginning; ennai – me; āḷvānē – one who controls in all of these aspects!

**Перевод:**

**Oh one who is having the countless, unlimited, amazing prakruti tatvam as your form, who is praised by nityasūris, who is having the three types of cētanas and acētanas as subservient entities! Oh lord who is naturally having eternal enjoyability! Oh one who is a benefactor right from the beginning and who controls me in all of these aspects! You who are apt and enjoyable, are thinking to torture me with the senses which are internal enemy due to residing inside permanently and are stopping me from reaching your divine feet. āḻvār is blaming emperumān who is the benefactor, out of his relationship with emperumān. The senses are addressed as sentient entities, due to their ability to act. eṇṇilāp peru māyanē could also mean one with countless, unlimited, amazing qualities.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the first pāsuram, āḻvār becomes upset saying “Why are you tormenting me with the senses even after I have surrendered unto your divine feet, being unable to sustain myself without you”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “You who are having the relationship \[with me\] to eliminate my hurdles, are tormenting me with the senses and making me not reach your divine feet”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. uṇṇilāviya aivarāl kumai tīṟṟi ennai un pāda pangayam naṇṇilā vagaiyē nalivān innam eṇṇuginṟāy eṇṇilāp peru māyanē! imaiyōrgaḷ ēttum ulagamūnṟudai aṇṇalē! amudē! appanē! ennai āḷvānē!*

- *uṇṇilāviya …* – Instead of having the presence of the saviour I am having the presence of the tormentor. Is your highness thinking that you have placed my enemies outside?
- *nilāviya* – Though they are inside, if they travel outside and return, we can fight with them at the right time.
- *nilāviya* – Residing. The tormentors are remaining in close proximity and hurting. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is not realising “there is ātmā (soul) which is different from dēham (body)”; he is thinking that the senses are only residing.
- *aivarāl* – Even if being tormented, we can remedy the situation if it is just one or two persons. But we have four of them \[eyes, ears, nose, tongue\] tormenting together and one \[skin\] is present all over the body. While the saviour is one, tormentors are five in number. While the senses are insentient, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) uses the term “*aivar*” (five persons) instead of “*anju*” (five objects), due to their resembling cētanas (sentient beings) in tormenting. āḻvār is not realising that there is an ātmā (self), that the mind is the gateway for the self’s knowledge and that these senses are subservient to them.
- *kumai tīṟṟi* – tormenting \[being consumed\]. Just as the one who insists those who tied a slingshot loosely to tighten it up, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is thinking that [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is not letting the senses relax and is making them torment him heavily. Based on the way they torment, if we address them like addressing sentient beings, is there any fault in them? Even when they are tormenting, he \[emperumān\] is not absent. Nor are they uncontrollable by him. Is he not known as hruśīkēśa (one who controls everyone’s senses)?
- *ennai* – Me who will be finished in their \[senses’\] presence as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 6.9.9](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/06/thiruvaimozhi-6-9-9-avi-thigaikka/) “*pala kāttip paduppāyō*” (are you planning to finish me by revealing varieties of pleasures?) and , [tiruvāimoḻi 6.9.8](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/06/thiruvaimozhi-6-9-8-arivilenukku-arulay/) “*innam keduppāyō*” (will you torment me further?).
- *un pāda pangayam* – Your divine feet which are said as in tiruvāimoḻi 6.9.9 “*tāvi vaiyam koṇḍa tadam tāmaraigaḷ*” (The expansive divine feet which measured the world) and tiruvāimoḻi 6.10.4 “*pūvār kaḻalgaḷ*” (divine feet filled with flowers).
- *un pāda pangayam* – Should I not highlight my helpless state? You don’t know your own greatness \[i.e. enjoyability of your divine feet\]! Are you pushing me away without knowing about you! \[Your divine feet\] periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 1.2.1 “*pēdaik kuḻavi pidittuc cuvaittuṇṇum pādak kamalam*” (The divine foot which is joyfully suckled by the ignorant toddler (kriṣṇa)). The enjoyable divine feet which cannot be discarded by even those who have not given up the inclination towards samsāra. The divine feet are said as in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.5.5](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/08/thiruvaimozhi-1-5-5-maney-nokki/) “*tēnē malarum tiruppādam*” (the divine foot which is the origin for honey).
- *naṇṇilā vagaiyē* – Not just occassionally to stay away, but doing that \[staying away\] as natural act. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) thinks “Can I ever reach [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) ?”.
- *nalivān* – For āḻvār, “not reaching him” and “being tormented” are not two separate aspects; they both are the same; not reaching [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s divine feet is the real torture for ātmā. This is what is torture.
- *innam* – Even after saying in tiruvāimoḻi 6.10.10 “*agalagillēn iṟaiyum enṟu alarmēl mangai uṟai mārbā … un adik kīḻ amarndu pugundēn*“.
- *eṇṇuginṟāy* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) thinks “īśvara has nothing else to do \[other than torturing me\]”. As he cared for pāṇḍavas as said in mahābhāratam rājasūya parvam “*yasya mantrī ca gōptā ca suhruccaiva janārdana:*” (janārdana who is the lord of all the worlds and is the minister, protector and friend of arjuna), he is thinking about tormenting me while I am actually being tormented as well. āḻvār thinks “[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is thinking how to push āḻvār away”.
- *eṇṇilāp peru māyanē* – Oh you who are able to perform many activities as said in upaniśat “*asmān māyī srujatē viśvamētat*” (īśvara creates the universe from the primordial matter) and in [śrī bhagavat gītā 7-13](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/7-13/) “*mama māyā duratyayā*” (it is difficult to crossover my primordial matter), are having the prakruti (material realm) as the prison to torment those whom you don’t like! Alternative explanation – pīḷḷān used to explain it as “Oh one who is having countless, amazing qualities!”. How does it fit your having such qualities and tormenting me? \[Why is he praising [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is tormenting him\] While someone is tormented using slings, in between they would be offered water, similarly, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is praising emperumān’s qualities here \[while blaming him\].
- *imaiyōrgaḷ ēttum* – Is the nitya vibhūti present to praise emperumān saying “Oh here is someone \[emperumān\] who has abandoned one \[āḻvār\] who cannot sustain without him”? āḻvār is thinking “Because of their \[nityasūris\] favourable attitude towards empeurmān, he has not arrived here”. Had his grand assembly protested like trisangu’s assembly did, could he stay away from me? \[trisangu reached svarga (heaven) on the order of viśvāmitra eventually to be pushed down and a new heaven was constructed by viśvāmitra for him in the sky\]
- *ulagam mūnṟu udaiya aṇṇalē* – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) manifested his greatness thinking that [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) would remain patiently knowing “emperumān will act when he wishes to”; āḻvār thinks “He manifested his greatness to make me think ‘would such saviour torment me?’ and then tormented me”.
- *amudē* – āḻvār thinks “He did not manifest his enjoyability to let me enjoy him, but to make me suffer not liking anything else”.
- *appanē* – āḻvār thinks “Making me believe ‘such benefactor will not torment me’ and then caused me suffering”.
- *ennai āḷvānē* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) thinks “He manifested his lordship to prove that he previously helped me. He did those to make me think ‘Did he rule over me previously based on any of my effort/act? \[No – he voluntarily did\] Similarly, he will care for me’; but his actual intent is different”.
- *ennai āḷvānē* – \[Alternative explanation based on piḷḷai tirunaṟaiyūr araiyar’s view which was explained in the [pravēśam](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/07/thiruvaimozhi-7-1-unnilaviya/)\] Being my lord, why are you thinking to torment me?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.1.2. Ennai alum

*ennai āḷum vankō ōraindivai peydu irāp pagal mōduvittittu unnai nān aṇugā vagai seydu pōdi kaṇḍāy kannalē! amudē! kār mugil vaṇṇanē! kadal jñālam kākkinṟa minnu nēmiyināy! vinaiyēnudai vēdiyanē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

kannalē – having complete sweetness; amudē – not just that, but being the sustainer, and with enjoyability; kār mugil vaṇṇanē – having the generosity without any restriction like dark clouds which help everyone; kadal – surrounded by ocean; jñālam – world; minnu – radiant; nēmiyināy – having divine chakra; kākkinṟa – being the protector, nouriśer; vinayēnudai – to be heard by me who is having the sin which stops me from attaining you; vēdiyanē – oh one who is revealed by vēdam only!; ennai – me (who is your servitor); āḷum – to be ruled over by them to be obedient; van – very strong; kō – having independence; ōr – distinguished; ivai – these; aindu – five senses; peydu – using them against me to harm me; irāp pagal – continuously throughout day and night; mōduvittittu – to be affected; unnai – you who are apt and enjoyable; nān – I (who know your greatness); aṇugāvagai – to not reach; seydu – do; pōdi kaṇḍāy – gone away from me

**Перевод:**

**Oh one who is having complete sweetness, not just that, but being the sustainer, and with enjoyability, who is having the generosity without any restriction like dark clouds which help everyone, who is having divine chakra which is radiant in the world surrounded by ocean, who is being the protector and nouriśer, who is revealed by vēdam only, to be heard by me who is having the sin which stops me from attaining you! You are using these distinguished, very strong, independent five senses against me to harm me continuously throughout day and night and to be ruled over by them, to be obedient towards them; being affected by them, you who are apt and enjoyable, have affected me and stopped me from reaching you and have gone away from me.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the second pāsuram, āḻvār says “You are tormenting me who is weak, with the senses throughout the day and night to stop me from reaching you and you are not even present to be informed about my suffering”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. ennai āḷum vankō ōraindivai peydu irāp pagal mōduvittittu unnai nān aṇugā vagai seydu pōdi kaṇḍāy kannalē! amudē! kār mugil vaṇṇanē! kadal jñālam kākkinṟa minnu nēmiyināy! vinaiyēnudai vēdiyanē!*

- *ennai āḷum van kō* – While you care for my sustenance, there are others who are using my service. While the fact is, there is [īśvara](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/), [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) is subservient to such īśvara, manas (mind) is a confidential instrument for the ātmā, and indriyas are subservient to the mind, here the senses are ruling over me as it happens during chaotic scenarios.
- *van kō* – I am disgusted having served the very strong senses who are unnatural inhabitants on my body. vanmai – forceful. periya tirumoḻi 7.7.9 “*kōvāy aivar en mey kudiyēṟik kūṟai sōṟivai tāvenṟu kumaittup pōgār*” (these five senses occupied my body as rulers, and pestered me for clothing, food etc). Why is [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who has good qualities, avoiding to be the śēśi (master)! vanmai – hard-hearted. Instead of emperumān who is with all auspicious qualities being the master, these cruel senses became the masters.
- *ōr aindu* – Instead of each sense individually tormenting based on its own nature, they are together tormenting me. The state of being the servitor of the apt lord is gone. emperumān who is said in nārāyaṇa sūktam as “*patim viśvasya*” (the lord of the universe) and [tiruvāimoḻi 6.7.10](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/04/thiruvaimozhi-6-7-10-ninaikkilen-dheyvangal/) “*anaittulagum udaiya aravindalōcanan*” (the lotus-eyed lord who owns all the worlds) is not the master.
- *aindu* – That we are servitors to one single master is no longer true.
- *ivai peydu* – How can we blame the senses? āren’t you the one who is tormenting us with them? Just as hiraṇya sent the snakes to torment śrī prahlāda, you are tormenting me with these senses.
- *irāp pagal mōduvittittu* – What a \[bad\] way to spend my time! I desired to serve you as said in tiruvāimoḻi 3.3.1 “*oḻivil kālam ellām*” (at all times, without a break). I prayed in [tiruvāimoḻi – 2.3.10](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/02/thiruvaimozhi-2-3-10-kalippum-kavarvum/) “*adiyārgaḷ kuḻāngaḷai udan kūduvadu enṟu kolō*” (When will I be amidst the nityasūris?), but now I have been united with these senses!
- *unnai nān* – You who are to be attained to survive, and I who cannot survive without reaching you. You who are infinitely enjoyable and I who cannot sustain without enjoying you.
- *aṇugā vagai seydu* – Stopping me from reaching you.
- *pōdi kaṇḍāy* – This is similar to how you separated sītāp pirātti, who was fully inclined to enjoy you, from you by showing her the mystical deer, and led her to the ēkākśi (one-eyed rākśasi), ēkakarṇikā (one-eared rākśasi) et al.
- *kannalē amudē* – Am I satisfied with just some sort of enjoyability? He is said in “*sarvaganda: sarvarasa:*” (root of all fragrance and taste), being unlimited as in [tiruvāimoḻi 4.7.2](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/03/thiruvaimozhi-4-7-2-kolla-mala/) “*koḷḷa māḷā inba veḷḷam*” (flood of bliss which cannot be easily held). kannal – block of sugar. amudu – enjoyable and that which leads to immortality.
- *kār mugil vaṇṇanē* – He bestows such enjoyability for his own sake \[without any other expectation\]. He is said to be most generous. Alternative explanation – saying “like clouds in rainy season, oh one who is having an attractive form!”.
- *kadal jñālam …* – Now you are away – but did you protect the worlds on anyone’s request! Did anyone pray to you saying “we are tormented by the senses” to have you protect them! Would you not protect even those who don’t know that you are enjoyable? Are you not having the nature of protecting the world which is surrounded by ocean, under your watchful eyes?
- *kākkinṟa* – Is protecting others an occasional activity for you?
- *minnu nēmiyināy* – As you have the ability, would you simply protect using your vow? Don’t your protect with your hand readily holding the weapon! It is said in tiruviruttam 33 “*aruḷār tiruccarattāl agal visumbum nilanum iruḷār vinai kedac cengōl nadāvudir*” (With your merciful divine chakra, you are conducting the vast sky and earth by removing the ignorance and thus having your sceptre ruling over everything). Would you not protect by not placing the sword in it’s sheath? The shining divine chakra.
- *vinaiyēnudai vēdiyanē* – While you are equally placed towards everyone as said in jitantē stōtram 2 “*dēvānām dānavām ca sāmānyamadidaivatam*” ([emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is equal toward dēvas \[celestial persons\] and demons) and [mūnṟām tiruvandādi 88](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/05/munram-thiruvandhadhi-88/) “*podu ninṟa ponnam kaḻal*” (the divine feet which are equal towards everyone), when it comes to me, you are being *vēdaikasamadigamyan* (known through vēdam only), and I am being sinful to hear about you only through the scriptures \[and not having your darśan\].

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.1.3. Vediya nirkum

*vēdiyā niṟkum aivarāl vinaiyēnai mōduvittu un tiruvadic cādiyā vagai nī taduttu en peṟudi! andō! ādiyāgi agalidam padaittu uṇḍumiḻndu kadandidanditta sōdi nīḷ mudiyāy! toṇḍanēn madusūdananē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

ādi – the root cause; āgi – being; agal – very expansive; idam – universe; padaittu – create; uṇḍu – protect by placing in stomach (during deluge); umiḻndu – spit out (subsequently); kadandu – measured (to eliminate others’ claim of ownership); idandu – dig out (as varāha during intermediary deluge); sōdi – radiance (revealing his supremacy over all); nīḷ – having tallness; mudiyāy – one who is wearing the crown; toṇḍanēn – to me who is desirous of enjoying you; madusūdananē – oh one who is capable of eliminating my hurdles like you eliminated \[the demon\] madu!; vēdiyā niṟkum – those who pierce through me to torment me; aivarāl – with the five senses; vinaiyēnai – me who is sinner (in being unable to be protected by you); mōduvittu – to be affected; un – you (who is protector of all); tiruvadi – divine foot; sādiyā vagai – to not attain; nī – you; taduttu – stopping; en – what benefit; peṟudi – you get?; andō – alas! Implying “the saviour has turned to be the tormentor”

**Перевод:**

**emperumān being the root cause of the expansive universe, created it, protected by placing in his stomach, spat it out, measured it and dug it out; oh one who is wearing the tall, radiant crown! Oh one who is capable of eliminating my (me who is desirous of enjoying you) hurdles like you eliminated madu! What benefit do you get by having me, the sinner, affected with the five senses which pierce through me to torment me and stopping me from attaining your divine feet? Alas! Implying “the saviour has turned to be the tormentor”.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the third pāsuram, āḻvār says “While you are the protector for the universe in all manner, what benefit is there for you to torment me with the senses and stop me from attaining your divine feet?”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. vēdiyā niṟkum aivarāl vinaiyēnai mōduvittu un tiruvadic cādiyā vagai nī taduttu en peṟudi! andō! ādiyāgi agalidam padaittu uṇḍumiḻndu kadandidanditta sōdi nīḷ mudiyāy! toṇḍanēn madusūdananē!*

- *vēdiyā niṟkum* – I happily desired to serve him in all manners. Whatever I prayed for in [tiruvāimoḻi 3.3.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/08/thiruvaimozhi-3-3-1-ozhivil-kalam/) “*udanāy manni*” (staying together), is to serve these senses!
- *vēdiyā niṟkum* – Those which engage in constant torture. While it is said in yajur vēdam “*yāvajjīvam agnihōtram juhuyāt*” (as long as one is alive, one should do agni hōtram (fire ritual)), it also allocates certain times of the day for doing that, as in “*sāyam prāta:*” (morning and evening); unlike that, whatever I spoke of desiring to serve in all manners to emperumān, have ended up with these senses.
- *vinaiyēnai* – Whatever I longed for enjoyment, has become the cause for suffering.
- *un tiruvadic cādiyā vagai nī taduttu* – What a strong relationship! Their \[āḻvār – emperumān\] relationship is such that, āḻvār can blame emperumān for his own fault. āḻvār is speaking as if he performed sādanam \[bhakti yōga etc\] and someone is holding up the results. Stopping me from attaining your divine feet.
- *en peṟudi* – Do you want to only destroy my nature? If you attain some benefit by my suffering, that is what I need; my aim is to live for you only. iḷaiya perumāḷ (lakśmaṇa) who previously said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 53.31 “*muhūrtam api jeevāva: jalān matsyā vivōtrutau”* (if we separate from you we will die like a fish out of the water), when sage durvāsa arrived \[and wanted lakśmaṇa to interrupt śrī rāma’s meeting which will finish him\], he bid farewell without seeing self’s suffering, saying “I cannot allow disrepute to perumāḷ (śrī rāma)”.
- *en peṟudi* – You separated śrī bharatāḻvān to prove that you abide by your promises; what is the benefit in my case?
- *andō* – I have taken such a birth that I am tormented only for the sake of causing disaster to others instead of being at your service. emperumān who is having “protection of others” as his sole aim, is now acting like cruel person!

\[Following section is as per piḷḷai tirunaṟaiyūr araiyar’s view which was highlighted in the [pravēśam](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/07/thiruvaimozhi-7-1-unnilaviya/)\]

- *ādi* … – Are you not of the nature that you will protect someone even if there is no benefit for you in doing so! This being the case, does your act fit your nature? While you wear divine ornaments such as the divine crown etc which reveal your supremacy and remain amidst the nityasūris, being the root cause for the universe, you created the expansive earth, you placed it in your stomach and protected it when the danger of deluge loomed, subsequently you spat them out, and then you measured the boundaries and reclaimed it when mahābali claimed ownership of it, dug it out during intermediary deluge; are you not having the nature to protect everyone in these manners?
- *toṇḍanēn* … – Do we have to seek out for previous incidents to prove that he is the protector?  Is he not the one who eliminated my attachment towards my senses, just as he eliminated madu, the demon? toṇḍan – one who is attached to sensual pleasures. My only complaint is, after manifesting his greatness and eliminating my attachment towards other aspects, now he is still out of my reach.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.1.4. Sudu nan

*sūdu nān aṟiyā vagai suḻaṟṟi ōr aivaraik kātti un adip pōdu nān aṇugā vagai seydu pōdi kaṇḍāy yādum yāvarum inṟi nin agampāl odukki ōr ālinīḷilai mīdu sēr kuḻavi! vinaiyēn vinai tīr marundē*

**Пословный перевод:**

yādum – all acētanas (insentient entities); yāvarum – all cētanas (sentient beings); inṟi – without leaving anything behind; nin – your; agampāl – inside your divine stomach; odukki – placing them in a corner; ōr – a (one which cannot be traced to a location where it sprouted from); ālin – banyan tree’s; nīḷ – stretched out (due to having blossomed); ilai – the leaf; mīdu – on top of; sēr – reclining (without realising that he is in the dangerous deluge); kuḻavi – having childishness; vinaiyēn – my, who is embodiment of sin; vinai – sin; tīr – eliminating; marundē – oh one who is the medicine!; ōr – having distinguished strength; aivarai – the five senses; kātti – showing; nān – I (who am having the qualification for the ultimate goal); sūdu – apt goal; aṟiyāvagai – to not know; suḻaṟṟi – to bewilder in the worldly pleasures; un – your (you, the companion in dangerous times); adip pōdu – infinitely enjoyable divine foot which is like a lotus; nān – I (who has no other refuge); aṇugā vagai – to not reach; seydu – do; pōdi kaṇḍāy – moved away from my vision

**Перевод:**

**emperumān is placing all acētanas and cētanas in his divine stomach in a corner, without leaving anything behind and is reclining on top of a banyan tree’s leaf, with childishness; oh such emperumān who is the medicine for eliminating the sin of me, who is an embodiment of sin! You are showing me the five senses which have distinguished strength, to not know the apt goal and to bewilder me in the worldly pleasures; you ensured that I do not reach your infinitely enjoyable divine foot and have moved away from my vision.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fourth pāsuram, āḻvār says “You are bewildering me by manifesting the sensual pleasures through śabda (sound) etc to make me not know that you are the infinite goal”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “You who are able to accomplish impossible tasks, are bewildering my mind with the senses and are ensuring that I don’t reach your enjoyable divine feet”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. sūdu nān aṟiyā vagai suḻaṟṟi ōr aivaraik kātti un adip pōdu nān aṇugā vagai seydu pōdi kaṇḍāy yādum yāvarum inṟi nin agampāl odukki ōr ālinīḷilai mīdu sēr kuḻavi! vinaiyēn vinai tīr marundē*

- *sūdu* …. – apt goal. That is “For this [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/), attachment towards worldly pleasures will lead to destruction and experiencing [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) will uplift”. To ensure that I do not realise this.
- *ōr aivaraik kātti – suḻaṟṟi* – Manifesting the worldly pleasures derived from śabda (sound) etc, and bewildering me; like consuming bewilderment-inducing food item.
- *un adip pōdu nān aṇugā vagai seydu* – Ensuring that I don’t reach your divine feet, which are like fresh flowers. Like someone who stops a person, who washed his/her hair to decorate with flowers, from wearing those flowers.
- *pōdi kaṇḍāy* – If you remain in close proximity, I will not suffer like this! Like those who move away thinking “if we remained here, we cannot avoid showing compassion”.

emperumān says “It is difficult for me to do whatever you are saying”; āḻvār responds “Yes, \[as if\] you have never accomplished any difficult task”.

- *yādum yāvarum …* – Placing all cētanas and acētanas in your stomach, reclining on a closed \[non-blossomed\] banyan tree leaf, you assumed a form and rested there, as if you need a protector. Did you not do that?

Do we need to highlight a historical incident to prove that you can do the impossible tasks? \[We have one example in myself\]

- *vinaiyēn vinai tīr marundē* – Oh one who is the medicine to cure the sin of me who is an embodiment of sin! Have you not eliminated my attachment towards the worldly pleasures through śabda etc, and made me suffer \[in separation like this\]!

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.1.5. Tir marundu

*tīr marundinṟi aindu nōyadum sekkil ittut tirikkum aivarai nēr marungudaittāvadaittu negiḻppānokkinṟāy ār marundini āguvār! adalāḻi ēndi asurar vankulam vēr marungaṟuttāy! viṇṇuḷār perumānēyō!*

**Пословный перевод:**

adal – being set out to fight (to destroy the enemies of devotees); āḻi – tiruvāḻi (divine chakra); ēndi – holding; asurar – asuras (demons) who are unfavourable; van – very strong; kulam – groups; marungu vēr – with the roots in sideways; aṟuttāy – being the one who severed; viṇṇuḷār – for the residents of paramapadam; perumānē – Oh leader who is infinitely enjoyable!; tīr – pacifier; marundu – remedial medicine; inṟi – to not have; aindu – five types of; nōy – by diseases (subtle elements such as śabda (sound), sparśa (touch), rūpa (form), rasa (taste) and ganda (smell)); adum – which can finish; sekkil – in the mortar of body, which can cause bewilderment; ittu – placing; tirukkum – bewildering; aivarai – five senses; nēr – in front of me; marungu – in the side; udaittā – to have; adaittu – placing; negiḻppān okkinṟāy – you are breaking me; ini – now (after you who are the eliminator of hurdles, are nurturing the hurdles); marundu – medicine; āguvār – be; Ar – who?

**Перевод:**

**Oh leader who is infinitely enjoyable for the residents of paramapadam, who held the divine chakra which is set out to fight and severed the groups of very strong asuras along with their roots even in sideways! You are breaking me by placing  the five types of diseases \[pleasures derived from śabda etc\] which are not having any pacifier which is a remedial medicine, in the mortar of body, which can cause bewilderment, and the bewildering senses in front of me, and in the sides; now, who will be my medicine? Will the sensual pleasures which are the diseases be the medicine? Will I, the sufferer be the medicine? Will the senses which torment me, be the medicine? āḻvār becomes very anguished thinking “being comparable to nityasūris to enjoy emperumān, I am being inflicted with diseases and experiencing the trouble” and highlights it with “O”.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fifth pāsuram, āḻvār says “Will there be any other protector for me if you leave me to become unresponsive by tormenting me with the worldly pleasures and senses?”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. tīr marundinṟi aindu nōyadum sekkil ittut tirikkum aivarai nēr marungudaittāvadaittu negiḻppānokkinṟāy Ar marundini āguvār! adalāḻi ēndi asurar vankulam vēr marungaṟuttāy! viṇṇuḷār perumānēyō!*

- *tīr marundu inṟi* – If there is any other option, one can be pacified; even if sarvaśakti ([emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is all capable) tries, it is not possible to eliminate \[i.e. the disease is so powerful\].
- *aindu nōy adum sekkil ittu* – With the disease of pleasures which are derived from śabda (sound) etc, placing in the body which finishes the soul.
- *tirukkum aivarai* – Senses such as śrōtra (ear), eye, nose, tongue and skin which torment. Placing the soul in the body, showing the pleasures and tormenting with the senses.
- *nēr marungu udaittā adaittu* – Being placed in front and the sides \[fully surrounding\]. Just as many great warriors/charioteers surrounded to attack the child abhimanyu, \[[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)\] had the senses under his control.
- *negiḻppān okkinṟāy* – You appear to be diminishing my faith in you while I was thinking “Would this torment remain forever?”, “Would this suffering go on forever?” \[i.e. the senses will naturally torment and this will stop after some time surely\].

[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) said “This being my state now, why don’t you seek out for some remedy?”.

- *Ar marundu ini āguvār* – Would I seek any other protector? When others and I cannot protect myself, you are there; who will protect when you abandon? \[another explanation\] [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) asks “Can you not protect yourself?”; can I not protect myself if I too have divine chakra in my hand? Would we not need a cētana (sentient being) to become the medicine? \[no other insentient means could remedy my situation\]. As said in mūnṟām tiruvandādi 4 “*marundum poruḷum amudamum tānē*” (medicine, that which will bestow the result and nectar are all emperumān), everything is emperumān only.
- *adal āḻi ēndi asurar van kulam vēr marungu aṟuttāy* – Oh one who is holding up the divine chakra which is set out to fight, and destroyed the clan of asuras along with their roots! Is that habit \[of tormenting the enemies of devotees\] making you torment me?
- *viṇṇuḷār perumānēyō* – Just as an imprisoned person would feel anguished due to his absence from his family, when his parents and brothers engage in joyful activities, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) ponders over [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s presence along with [pirātti](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/) and nityasūris in paramapadam and calls out to make them his hear his plight. Just as sītāp pirātti cried out when she was alone as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 28.8 “*hā rāma hā lakśmaṇa hā sumitrē*” (Oh rāma! Oh lakśmaṇa! Oh sumitra!), āḻvār is calling out to shake the grand assembly in paramapadam.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.1.6. Vinnular

*viṇ uḷār perumāṟkadimai seyvāraiyum seṟum aimpulan ivai maṇ uḷ ennaip peṟṟāl en seyyā maṟṟu nīyum vittāl? paṇ uḷāy! kavi tan uḷāy! pattiyin uḷḷāy! param īsanē! vanden kaṇ uḷāy! nenjuḷāy! sol uḷāy! onṟu sollāyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

viṇ uḷār – being residents of paramapadam; perumāṟku – to you who are greater than all; adimai seyvāraiyum – those who serve, like vainadēya (garudāḻvān); maṇ uḷ – this world, which is a natural habitat \[for the senses\]; seṟum – overcome and torment; ivai – these; aimpulan – five senses; ennai – me who lacks strength to overcome them; peṟṟāl – when they find; maṟṟum – further; nīyum – you (who are the controller); vittāl – if abandon me; en – what; seyyā – will not do?; en – my (who is calling you with involvement); paṇ – the tune of my wailing; uḷ āy – being inside; kavi than – the poem which is the placeholder for the tune; uḷ āy – being inside; pattiyin – of the desire (which is the cause for such poem); uḷḷāy – being the object; param – being supreme (so that everything is at your disposal); īsanē – being the controller (lord); kaṇ – eye; uḷāy – being inside; nenju – heart; uḷāy – being inside; sol – speech; uḷāy – being present inside; vandu – arriving here; onṟu – a word; sollāy – mercifully speak

**Перевод:**

**These five senses will overcome and torment in this world, which is a natural habitat \[for the senses\], even the residents of paramapadam like vainadēya et al \[when they descend here\] who serve you who are greater than all; what will they not do when they find me who lacks strength to overcome them and if you abandon me too? Oh one who is inside the tune of my wailing, the poem which is the placeholder for the tune and is the object of my desire! Being inside my eyes, heart and speech, you arrive here \[physically\] and mercifully speak a word. “sollāyē” implies “why are you not speaking?” highlighting how emperumān abandoned āḻvār. “en seyyā” indicates “they will do anything, just as a leaderless country will be tormented by evil people”.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the sixth pāsuram, āḻvār says “If you abandon me who is very weak, would the senses which can torture even the most knowledgeable, not lead me to total disaster?”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. viṇ uḷār perumāṟkadimai seyvāraiyum seṟum aimpulan ivai maṇ uḷ ennaip peṟṟāl en seyyā maṟṟu nīyum vittāl? paṇ uḷāy! kavi than uḷāy! pattiyin uḷḷāy! param īsanē! vanden kaṇ uḷāy! nenjuḷāy! sol uḷāy! onṟu sollāyē*

- *viṇ uḷār perumāṟku …* – These senses will even torment those who serve the lord of nityasūris.
- *perumāṟku adimai seyvāraiyum seṟum* – There are those who are born along with [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) and serve him continuously like iḷaiya perumāḷ (lakśmaṇa). These senses made even tiruvadi (garuda) think “For me” \[with ego\]. When a snake named sumuka took refuge of emperumān’s divine feet, periya tiruvadi (garuda) ran to emperumān and said “Why are you protecting this snake which is my prey?” Feeling upset he further said “I carried your highness and your consorts for a long time and travelled around; what have I received in return?” This is the nature of this samsāram (material realm). Just as emperumān incarnates and feels anguished, bewildered etc \[i.e. pretending to be so\], they \[nityasūris\] too feel anguished, bewildered etc. Alternative explanation – These are the senses which can torment even the [mumukśus](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) (liberation seekers) in this samsāram who are fully engaged in service to the lord of nityasūris. We have seen that in viśvāmitra, sugrīva et al. Even the very wise sage viśvāmitra had fallen in the trap of worldly pleasure for a long duration; sugrīva mahārāja who was caring towards perumāḷ (śrī rāma), captivated in sensual enjoyment and even forgetting the route to śrī rāma’s residence, let perumāḷ suffer in lightning and thunder during the four months of rainy season.
- *maṇ uḷ …* – Is [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) not someone from the paramapadam? \[No – it appears like that based on his glories\] This is the natural habitat for the senses; I have placed myself in this trap and tightened the noose; when they catch me in this manner, what would they not do?
- *maṟṟu nīyum vittāl* – When everyone else abandons, one would fall upon you who will sustain; but if you too abandon there is no hope. Had you protected me, could I not have won over the senses as sugrīva won over vāli? arjuna too said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 6.34](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/6-34/) “*tasyāham nigraham manyē vāyōr iva suduśkaram”* (I think that it is very difficult to restrain it, like controlling a fierce storm). Only if we can bind wind in a particular place, could the mind be controlled. If you who said “If you say ‘it is difficult to control my senses’, then place your mind in me”, abandon me now?

[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) said “I have not abandoned you! How can I abandon you?”; [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says “am I losing you due to your absence or lack of ability?”

- *paṇ uḷāy* – You are not deaf to the tune of my anguished wail!
- *kavi than uḷāy* – You are not deaf to the words which are filled with my anguish.
- *pattiyin uḷḷāy* – You are not ignorant about the root cause of my anguish.
- *param īsanē* – There is nothing which is impossible for you. Is there any place where your lordship does not rule?

(You are also the lord of the senses) [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying “Aside, is there anything you have not done previously?” [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) says “but, there is nothing more to do”; āḻvār says “I am not blaming you in what you have already done; but I am just highlighting what you have not done yet”.

- *en kaṇ uḷāy nenjuḷāy sol uḷāy* – Is there any other target for my external and internal senses? They always remain as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 3.9.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/10/thiruvaimozhi-3-8-1-mudiyane/) “*nediyānē*” (Oh great lord!), [tiruvāimoḻi 3.8.4](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/10/thiruvaimozhi-3-8-4-kaigalal-ara/) “*unnai mey koḷḷak kāṇa virumbum*” (desire to see you in front of me), [tiruvāimoḻi 3.8.2](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/10/thiruvaimozhi-3-8-2-nenjame/) “*vanjanē*” (Oh mischievous one!) “*kavi than uḷāy*” indicates the pāsuram (poem); “*sol uḷāy*” indicates the sense of speech.

When [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) asked “what should I do?”,

- *vandu – onṟu sollāyē* – You take a few steps towards me, and drive away my fear saying as in [śrī bhagavat gītā 18.66](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/18-66/) “*mā śuca:*” (do not grieve). [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says “Is there any doubt in me about your existence? \[No\] My only desire is see you arriving in front of me and speaking to me”.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.1.7. Onru solli

*onṟu solli oruttinil niṟkilāda ōr aivar van kayavarai enṟu yān velgiṟpan un tiruvaruḷ illaiyēl anṟu dēvar asurar vānga alai kadal aravam aḷāvi ōr kunṟam vaitta endāy! kodiyēn parugu innamudē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

anṟu – on that day (when he surrendered unto you having faith in your nityatva (eternity)); dēvar – dēvas; asurar – asuras (who united with them for the nectar); vānga – to pull; alai – having rising waves; kadal – in the ocean; aravam – snake named vāsuki; aḷāvi – coiled around; ōr – distinguished; kunṟam – mantara mountain; vaitta – manifesting the magnanimity of how you anchored it firmly; endāy – being my master; kodiyēn – having the anguish (of desiring to enjoy you only) unlike them who were satisfied with getting the nectar; parugu – to drink; in amudē – Oh one who is eternally enjoyable!; un – your; tiruvaruḷ – infinite mercy; illaiyēl – if not present; onṟu – find something and give; solli – saying; oruttinil – in a steady manner; niṟkilāda – without being focussed; ōr – individually independent and not matching together; aivar – five senses; van – very strong; kayavarai – though being together \[with me\], the unknown evil entities; yān – I who am weak; enṟu – when; velgiṟpan – will win over?

**Перевод:**

**emperumān anchored the distinguished mountain mantara firmly in the ocean with rising waves and coiled it around with the snake named vāsuki, to be pulled by dēvas and asuras on that day; oh my master who manifested such magnanimous act and is eternally enjoyable to drink for me who is having the anguish unlike them who were satisfied with getting the nectar! When will I who am weak, win over my very strong, five senses which are individually independent and not matching together and though being together \[with me\], they \[sense\] are the unknown evil entities, without a steady mind saying “find something and give, if not present”, .**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the seventh pāsuram, āḻvār says “If you abandon me, would I have any means to win over the most powerful senses?”*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. onṟu solli oruttinil niṟkilāda ōr aivar van kayavarai enṟu yān velgiṟpan un tiruvaruḷ illaiyēl anṟu dēvar asurar vānga alai kadal aravam aḷāvi ōr kunṟam vaitta endāy! kodiyēn parugu innamudē!*

- *onṟu solli* – Am I fearful even after having surrendered to [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is said as in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 18.30 “*rāmō dvirnābhibhśatē*” (śrī rāma is not double-tongued , i.e. does not change his stand)? Since it is said so (that he does not change his stand), his statement in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 18.33 “*ētat vratam mama*” (This is my vow) will not go waste.
- *onṟu solli oruttinil niṟkilāda* – When a word is said, but even the meaning of the word is not followed. A word is said, and even before it is realised, it will not remain there. oruttu – concentration/focus.
- *ōr aivar* – There are many who are like this.
- *van kayavarai* – Those who became cruel while getting friendly/used to them.
- *enṟu yān velgiṟpan* – Are you (emperumān) thinking “If he (āḻvār) does not win over them today, he will win tomorrow. He will come here, after winning over them, on his own”?
- *un tiruvaruḷ illaiyēl* – If his mercy is there, we can win over them. periya tirumoḻi 6.2.4 “*aruḷ ennum oḷ vāḷ uruvi eṟindēn aimpulangaḷ*” (I pulled out the shining sword of his mercy and threw out the five senses). Only when pāṇḍavas could win duryōdana et al without your help, can I win over my senses. arjuna won over his enemies by taking shelter of kriṣṇa. mahābhāratam drōṇa parvam “*kriṣṇāśraya: kriṣṇa balā: kriṣṇa nātāśca pāṇḍavā:*” (for the pāṇḍavas, kriṣṇa is the final goal to be attained, kriṣṇa is their strength and kriṣṇa is their Lord).
- *anṟu dēvar asurar vānga* – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) \[again\] asks “Is there anyone \[else\] who became victorious after getting my mercy?” [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says “When durvāsa cursed dēvas, did they not churn the ocean after having your mercy? Implies that when dēvas and asuras gave up, he churned the ocean. Alternative explanation – vāngudal – pulling. He facilitated them to churn the ocean.
- *alai kadal …* – In the ocean with high waves, having a sentient snake vāsuki as the rope and an unshakable mantara mountain as the mortar, he coiled vāsuki around the mantara and made it easy for everyone to churn; \[everyone includes us too\] even we would have been able to churn it.
- *endāy* – Since [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is also seeking some benefit (kainkaryam), he is considering it \[such favour of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) to dēvas\] as a favour to himself.
- *kodiyēn parugu in amudē* – I am not satisfied with accepting what came out of the churning effort. While I should be satisfied with whatever you have done, I am having the sin to insist you as in the case of \[rudra saying\] “*attadu oḻiyac cuttadu koṇḍu vā*” (place this flesh aside and bring what is burning in the stove) \[rudra tested the faith of one of his devotees, to make him cook the flesh of his own son and offer as feast\].

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.1.8. Innamudu

*in amudenat tōnṟi ōr aivar yāvaraiyum mayakka nī vaitta munna māyam ellām muḻu vērarindu ennai un cinnamum tirumūrttiyum sindittēttik kai toḻavē aruḷ enakku en ammā! en kaṇṇā! imaiyōr tam kula mudalē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

en – for me; ammā – being the natural lord; en kaṇṇā – manifesting your simplicity to me; imaiyōr tam kulam – for the group of nityasūris; mudalē – Oh one who is the cause for the sustenance etc!; ōr – distinguished; aivar – by the five senses; in – sweet; amudu – nectar; ena – appear to be enjoyable like; tōnṟi – manifesting; yāvaraiyuum – even brahmā et al who are very knowledgeable; mayakka – to cause bewilderment; nī – you (who are omnipotent); vaitta – (created and) placed; munnam – since time immemorial; māyam – matters known by the term māyā, since they cause ignorance; ellām – all; muḻu – fully; vēr – root; arindu – sever; ennai – me who is fearful of samsāram; un – your; cinnamum – distinguished symbols such as Sanka, chakra etc; tiru – decorated by them; mūrttiyum – the divine form; sindittu – think with my mind; ētti – praise with my speech; kai – with the hand; toḻa – to worship; enakkē – specially for me; aruḷ – bestow your mercy

**Перевод:**

**Oh one who is my natural lord. who is manifesting your simplicity to me and who is the cause for the sustenance for the group of nityasūris! Since time immemorial you have placed matters known by the term māyā, since they cause ignorance, and are manifesting the five distinguished senses which appear to be enjoyable like sweet nectar to cause bewilderment even in brahmā et al who are very knowledgeable; you bestow your mercy specially for me who is fearful of samsāram, to fully sever all those matters along with their root, and let me think with my mind, praise with my speech and worship with my hand(s) your distinguished, divine form which is decorated with symbols such as Sanka, chakra etc**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the eighth pāsuram, āḻvār says “You should bestow your mercy to sever my relationship with this material realm and ensure that I enjoy you eternally through my mind, speech and body”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. in amudenat tōnṟi ōr aivar yāvaraiyum mayakka nī vaitta munna māyam ellām muḻu vērarindu ennai un cinnamum tirumūrttiyum sindittēttik kai toḻavē aruḷ enakku en ammā! en kaṇṇā! imaiyōr tam kula mudalē!*

- *in amudu enat tōnṟi* – If the end result matches the initial appearance, I could give it up. It is said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 18.38](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/18-38/) “*agrē’mrutōpamam*” (in the beginning stages (of enjoyment), it feels like nectar); at the end, it turns out to be poison. If the true nature is visible in the beginning, one can at least avoid indulging in it. Even if one is to acquire blame, neglect of duty and subsequent attainment of hell, it is difficult to avoid indulging in them. All the worldly matters have this nature; similar to drudarāśtra. While he lacked virtuous inclination in his heart, he too spoke favourable words.
- ōr aivar – The five worldly pleasures acquired through śabda etc \[śabda, sparśa, rūpa, rasa, ganda\] which are very strong individually.
- *yāvaraiyum mayakka* – To bewilder everyone from the lowly human beings to the wisest brahmā et al.
- *nī vaitta* – Placed by you who are omnipotent. brahmā himself becomes attracted to these worldly pleasures thinking “there is something enjoyable in them” without realising that they were created by him in first place.
- *munna māyam ellām* – all of samsāram which are anādi (beginning-less)
- *muḻu vēr arindu* – eliminating with the vāsanā (inclination)
- *ennai* – I who am fearful of samsāram. emperumān is satisfied with whatever he has already done. He remains thinking “we have bestowed knowledge”; but that is not sufficient; āḻvār desires to be fully freed from samsāram.
- *un cinnamum tirumūrttiyum* – The divine weapons and the matching divine form as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 6.5.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/02/thiruvaimozhi-6-5-1-thuvalil-ma-mani-madam/) “*tavaḷa oṇ sangu cakkaram*” (white coloured radiant conch and chakra), [tiruvāimoḻi 6.4.9](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/01/thiruvaimozhi-6-4-9-kalakka-ezh-kadal/) “*valakkai āḻi idak kaic cangam*” (chakra in right hand and conch in the left hand) and [tiruvāimoḻi 6-5-10](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/02/thiruvaimozhi-6-5-10-pinnaikol/) “*aravinda lōcanan*” (lotus eyed lord).
- *sindittu …* –  You should mercifully enable me to meditate upon these in my heart, praise you with my speech as a result of the overwhelming experience and to fall at your divine feet. You should mercifully ensure that my mind, speech and body are engaged in you instead of the mouth saying something and the heart thinking something else, or the mouth saying “I am your servitor” but the body serving someone else.
- *en ammā* – Oh one who is caring towards me like a mother! “*ammē*” is generally used to call out (sambhōdana (samskrutam), viḷi (tamiḻ)) and also to refer to sentient entity; here ammā is used in place of ammē.
- *en kaṇṇā* – Oh one who gave meaning to that word (ammā) by practically manifesting it \[as kriṣṇa\]!
- *imaiyōr tam kula mudalē* – Are you not presenting yourself to the \[spiritual\] world? Can you not present yourself to me who has the desire of everyone put together?
- *en ammā …* – Being my lord, who appeared as kriṣṇa thinking “I cannot let others harm my belongings” and protected me! While emperumān’s incarnation is common for all, āḻvār thinks it was done specifically for him. While you have engaged the mind, speech and body of the entire \[spiritual\] world in you, what stops you from engaging me in the same manner?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.1.9. Kula mudal

*kula mudal adum tīvinaik kodu van kuḻiyil vīḻkkum aivarai vala mudal kedukkum varamē tandaruḷ kaṇḍāy nila mudal ini evvulagukkum niṟpana selvana enap poruḷ pala mudal padaittāy! en kaṇṇā! en paranjudarē*

**Пословный перевод:**

nilam – earth; mudal – starting with; ini – further; evvulagukkum – for all worlds; niṟpana selvana ena – immovable and movable; poruḷ – objects; pala – many; mudal – in the beginning; padaittāy – being the creator; en kaṇṇā – manifesting simplicity of appearing as kriṣṇa (for the protection of the world) to me; en – being enjoyable to me; param sudarē – oh one who is having infinitely radiant form!; kulam – clan; mudal – with the primary ancestor; adum – capable of destroying fully; tī – burning; vinai – nurturing sins; kodu – cruel; van – strong sensual pleasures; kuḻiyinil – deep pit; vīḻkkum – able to push; aivarai – five senses; vala mudal – with the evil inclination which is the cause for one’s strength; kedukkum – finishing; valamē – strength only; tandu aruḷ kaṇḍāy – kindly bestow

**Перевод:**

**emperumān created all worlds starting with the earth, and many immovable and movable objects in those world in the beginning; oh one who is manifesting simplicity of appearing as kriṣṇa to me, who is enjoyable by me and who is having infinitely radiant form! The five senses are capable of pushing one into the deep pit of strong sensual pleasures which are having the cruelty of burning sins which will destroy one along with his whole clan starting with the primary ancestor; you should kindly bestow the strength to finish those senses along with the evil inclination which is the cause for one’s strength \[for such sins\]. Here valam indicates his mercy which is very strong.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the ninth pāsuram, āḻvār says “Mercifully see that I am not tormented by the senses which lead me to sins which will destroy me along with others who are related to me”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. kula mudal adum tīvinaik kodu van kuḻiyil vīḻkkum aivarai vala mudal kedukkum varamē tandaruḷ kaṇḍāy nila mudal ini evvulagukkum niṟpana selvana enap poruḷ pala mudal padaittāy! en kaṇṇā! en paranjudarē*

- *kula mudal* … – Nurturing sins which not only cause harm to self but also to the whole clan, being cruel where there is no end to the experience, being a very strong pit – the senses which are strong, and which will push us into the pit of worldly pleasures from which it is impossible to come out. mālyavān advised rāvaṇa in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam “*nahi dharma viruddēṣu bahvapāyēśu karmasu \| mūlakādiśu sajjantē buddimantō bhavadvidā: \|\|*” – Wise men like you would not engage in acts which are forbidden, which are having danger which is beyond what is explained as the result, which will uproot the whole clan!
- *valamudal kedukkum varamē tandu aruḷ kaṇḍāy* – You should bestow your mercy which will eliminate their strength in the early stages itself.

[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) asks “Can I do all of that by myself?” and [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) replies

- *nilamudal …* – Who assisted you when you created the universe etc? \[No one\]. īsn’t the liberation \[of souls\] the purpose of creation? Would you not want to have that purpose accomplished? You created the immovable and movable entities in the earth and other worlds in the beginning.
- *(ini maṟṟum) en kaṇṇā, en param sudarē!* – Not only being common protector for all, you specifically incarnated as kriṣṇa as an obedient person towards me and oh one who manifested your beautiful form to me! Oh one who let me enjoy the beautiful form which is enjoyed by all the residents of paramapadam! For you who created what was destroyed \[previously in deluge\], is it difficult to manifest your auspicious qualities to me who is already existing?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.
