## 7.1.10. En paranjudare

*en paranjudarē! enṟunnai alaṟṟi un iṇait tāmaraigatku anburugi niṟkum adu niṟkac cumadu tandāy van parangaḷ eduttu aivar tisai tisai valitteṟṟuginṟanar mun paravai kadaindu amudangoṇḍa mūrttiyō!*

**Пословный перевод:**

mun – previously; paravai – the expansive ocean; kadaindu – churned; amudam – nectar (which is the essence of that ocean); koṇḍa – accepting and offering it (to dēvas); mūrtti – Oh one who is having lordship!; en – for me; param sudarē – Oh infinitely radiant enjoyable entity!; enṟu – saying so; unnai – seeing you; alaṟṟi – calling you incohesively due to \[my\] attachment; un – your; iṇai – mutually fitting; tāmaraigatku – for the pair of divine feet; anbu – out of love; urugi – becoming fluid; niṟkum – remaining; adu – that state of perfect essence; niṟka – while that is the nature; sumadu – body which is a baggage \[burden\]; tandāy – you gave; van – very strong; parangaḷ – sensual pleasures; eduttu – using; aivar – five senses; tisai tisai – the directions of their liking; valittu – pulling; eṟṟuginṟanar – tormenting; O – what a disaster!

**Перевод:**

**While I have attained the ultimate, fluid \[melted\] state out of love towards your mutually fitting pair of divine feet, saying incohesively due to attachment “Oh one who previously churned the expansive ocean, accepting the nectar and offering it to the dēvas, and who is having lordship! Oh infinitely radiant enjoyable entity for me!” , you gave this body which is a baggage; due to that, the five senses are using the very strong sensual pleasures to torment me by pulling me to the directions of their liking. What a disaster!**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the tenth pāsuram, āḻvār cries out with great anguish saying “You gave me this body which is a hurdle to serve you and is apt for worldly enjoyment; due to that, these five senses are tormenting me immensely; you should mercifully eliminate them”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. en paranjudarē! enṟunnai alaṟṟi un iṇait tāmaraigatku anburugi niṟkum adu niṟkac cumadu tandāy van parangaḷ eduttu aivar tisai tisai valitteṟṟuginṟanar mun paravai kadaindu amudangoṇḍa mūrttiyō!*

- *en param sudar …* – Calling you saying incohesively “Oh one who is favouring me by manifesting your beautiful form”.
- *un iṇait tāmarai …* – It is the true nature of this ātmā to be in a fluid \[melted\] state having experienced the enjoyability of your divine feet which appear like a pair of fresh flowers which are mutually fitting.
- *adu niṟkac cumadu tandāy* – While this is my true nature, you gave me this body which would push me away from you and engage me in worldly pleasures; you gave me this body to let me enjoy you; but the same body led to my loss. If the crown of a prince was removed and a baggage \[which is a burden\] was placed on his head, those who don’t know that he is prince, will use him in their service. \[Similarly\] The body you gave me to experience you, is now serving the senses. You gave this body, which is the baggage.
- *van parangaḷ …* – Am I fearing that I am engaged in inappropriate matters? \[No\] If I am given manageable burden, can I not bear it? Placing heavy baggage.
- *aivar* – I can manage if they were just one or two \[but they are five\].
- *tisai tisai valittu* – Will I not move slowly, at least if they all pulled me in the same direction?
- *eṟṟuginṟanar* – \[present tense\] If one is the owner, one may pause for a bit before harming again. These senses will place heavy baggage on a weak person, will surround him from all sides and pull from all directions.
- *mun paravai …* –  Oh one who is having great shoulders to churn the ocean, extract the nectar from it and distribute them to the dēvas who were interested in ulterior aspects \[instead of kainkaryam to emperumān\]! You have not driven out my senses fully and manifested the beautifully decorated form which you assumed during the churning of the ocean!

## 7.1.11. Konda murtti

*koṇḍa mūrtti ōr mūvarāyk kuṇangaḷ padaittaḷittuk kedukkum ap puṇḍarīgak koppūḻp punaṟpaḷḷi appanukkē toṇḍar toṇḍar toṇḍar toṇḍan satakōpan sol āyirattuḷ ippattum kaṇḍu pāda vallār vinai pōm kangulum pagalē*

**Пословный перевод:**

guṇangaḷ – qualities (in the form of satva (goodness), rajas (passion) and tamas (ignorance)); koṇḍa – having; mūrtti – having forms (of brahmā, viṣṇu and rudra); ōr – distinguished; mūvar – three (causal) individuals; āy – being; padaittu – creates (as antaryāmi of brahmā); aḷittu – protects (as viśnū who is an incarnation of śrīman nārāyaṇa); kedukkum – one who annihilates (as antaryāmi of rudra); a – being the root for all of these, as known in scriptures; puṇḍarīgam – having puṇḍarīka (lotus); koppūḻ – having divine navel; punal – in the causal ocean; paḷḷi – resting; appanukku – for the great benefactor; toṇḍar – those who became related; toṇḍar – those who got related; toṇḍar – those who related; toṇḍan – servitor; satakōpan – nammāḻvār; sol – mercifully spoke; āyirattuḷ – among the thousand pāsurams; ippattum – this decad; kaṇḍu – seeing the meanings; pāda vallār – those who can sing being triggered by love; kangulum pagal – at all times whether day or night; vinai – sin which puts hurdle for experiencing bhagavān; pōm – will be freed

**Перевод:**

**emperumān is manifesting himself as three distinguished individuals with the forms having adequate qualities to perform creation, sustenance and annihilation; being the root of all these, as known in scriptures, he is resting in the causal ocean with the lotus flower on his divine navel; nammāḻvār is the servitor of those who are related to in a chain of servitors of such emperumān; he spoke this decad among the thousand pāsurams; those who can sing this decad with the meanings, being triggered by love, at all times whether day or night, will be freed from sin which puts hurdle for experiencing bhagavān.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the end, āḻvār says “Those who practice this decad will be freed from the eternal torment of senses to the ātmā“.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “For those who sing this decad joyfully with its meaning, all sins will be eliminated”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. koṇḍa mūrtti ōr mūvarāyk kuṇangaḷ padaittaḷittuk kedukkum ap puṇḍarīgak koppūḻp punaṟpaḷḷi appanukkē toṇḍar toṇḍar toṇḍar toṇḍan satakōpan sol āyirattuḷ ippattum kaṇḍu pāda vallār vinai pōm kangulum pagalē*

- *koṇḍa mūrtti ōr mūvarāyk kuṇangaḷ* – “*guṇangaḷ koṇḍa mūrtti ōr mūvarāy”* – being the three individuals having the form matching the qualities such as satva, rajas and tamas. Creation etc which match the particular quality will manifest in each of those forms. Among the three forms, in two forms \[brahma and rudra\], he pervades through other [jīvātmās](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/).
- *padaittu* … – Engaged in creation with rajō guṇam, annihilation with tamō guṇam and protecting all of these with satva guṇam.
- *appuṇḍarīgam …* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is speaking about [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s lying on the causal ocean to do all of these. Only for the benefactor who reclined himself on the causal ocean to engage in the creation of the universe, with the lotus flower in his divine navel which is well known \[as the source of creation\]. By “*appuṇḍarīgak koppūḻ*“, emperumān being the cause and brahmā and rudra being the effect is explained. The creation of one individual \[brahmā\] only needs to be proven; as said in vēdam “*brahmaṇa:putrāya jyēśtāya śrēśtāya*” (rudra, who is the eldest son and the best), the creation of other person will be naturally explained. After saying in [nānmugan tiruvandādi 1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/06/nanmugan-thiruvandhadhi-1/) “*nānmuganai nārāyaṇan padaittān*” (śrīman nārāyaṇa created brahmā), [tirumaḻisai āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/thirumazhisai-azhwar/) would further explain the creation of others. In this manner, this is explained by vēdam as well as vaidikas.
- *toṇḍar …* – To overcome the anguish of meditating upon the sensual pleasures and the senses, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is focussing on the ultimate state of śēśatvam (servitude) \[i.e. servitude towards the devotees of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) and their devotees\]; just as someone who experienced heat will delve deep into a pond to refresh himself.
- *kaṇḍu pāda vallār* – Can those who meditate upon [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s state, sing? \[No – they will also melt\].
- *kaṇḍu* – Considering these pāsurams to be our refuge.
- *vinai pōm kangulum pagalē* – Sins \[which cause attachment to senses\] will be eliminated from day and night. Difficulties explained in [tiruvāimoḻi 7.1.2](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/07/thiruvaimozhi-7-1-2-ennai-alum/) “*irāp pagal mōduvittittu*” will be eliminated.

In the next article we will enjoy the next decad.

## 7.2 Kangulum pagalum

## 7.2.1. Kangulum pagalum

*kangulum pagalum kaṇ tuyil aṟiyāḷ kaṇṇa nīr kaigaḷāl iṟaikkum sangu cakkarangaḷ enṟu kai kūppum tāmaraik kaṇ enṟē taḷarum enganē darikkēn unnai vittennum iru nilam kai tuḻāvirukkum sengayal pāy nīrt tiruvarangattāy ivaḷ tiṟatten seyginṟāyē?*

**Пословный перевод:**

kangulum – night (when worldly people sleep); pagalum – day (when those who are in love sleep); kaṇ – eyes; tuyil – to sleep; aṟiyāḷ – does not even realise; kaṇṇa nīr – tears; kaigaḷāl – with her hands; iṟaikkum – removing them; sangu cakkarangaḷ – Sanka (conch) and chakra (disc); enṟu – saying; kai kūppum – she would perform anjali which she would do upon his arrival; tāmarai – lotus like; kaṇ – eye; enṟē – saying that; taḷarum – would become tired; unnai – you (who have such beautiful weapons and limbs); vittu – without; enganē – how; darikkēn – will I sustain?; ennum – will say; iru nilam – the whole ground; kai – with her hand; tuḻā – search; irukkum – will remain in an inactive state (due to not having strength for searching the land too); sem – reddish due to youthful state; kayal – fish; pāy – jumping around; nīr – having water; tiruvarangattāy – oh one who is residing in kōyil (śrīrangam)!; ivaḷ tiṟattu – this girl who is having these amazing emotions; en – what; seyginṟāy – are you planning to do?

**Перевод:**

**My daughter’s eyes do not even realise to sleep in night and day; she is removing the tears from her eyes with her hands; saying Sanka and chakra, she would perform anjali which she would do upon his arrival; saying “lotus like eye”, she would become tired; she would say “how will I sustain without you”; she would search the ground with her hand and will remain in an inactive state; oh one who is residing in kōyil (śrīrangam) which is having water bodies in which youthful, reddish fishes jump around! What are you planning to do for this girl who is having these amazing emotions?  Implies “are you planning to eliminate the sorrow or increase the same?”**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the first pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki‘s mother informs her daughter’s unconscious state to periya perumāḷ and asks him “What are you going to do to her?”*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. kangulum pagalum kaṇ tuyil aṟiyāḷ kaṇṇa nīr kaigaḷāl iṟaikkum sangu cakkarangaḷ enṟu kai kūppum tāmaraik kaṇ enṟē taḷarum enganē darikkēn unnai vittennum iru nilam kai tuḻāvirukkum sengayal pāy nīrt tiruvarangattāy ivaḷ tiṟatten seyginṟāyē?*

- *kangulum pagalum kaṇ tuyil aṟiyāḷ* – When are you planning to make her sleep? The boundary of day and night was set up to give a break to the continuous sorrow of those who are suffering in separation; that is not helping her. In the night, one would spend the time by engaging in the pleasures, and in the day, one would spend time thinking “it is getting closer to night”; since she is saying “*enganē darikkēn unnai vittu*” (How can I sustain without you?) she cannot sustain herself like that. She does not even realise the day and night which are meant to pacify her. Even the day became useless like the night.
- *pagal* – (for those who are in love) when they enter the adolescent stage, as they are constantly engaging with their beloved person, they would not sleep in the night; to compensate for the lack of sleep in the night, they would sleep well in the morning! She is not even getting such sleep. [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) made her to be like him as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 36.44 “*anidras satatam rāma:*” (śrī rāma never sleeps). This is how he gave his sāmyāpatti (equivalence) to her as said in muṇḍaka upaniśat 3.1.3 “*niranjana: paramam sāmyam upaiti*” ([jīvātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) attains equality (in eight qualities) with supreme lord). Instead of saying “*kaṇ tuyil koḷḷāḷ*” (she would not sleep), here it is said as “*kaṇ tuyil aṟiyāḷ*” (she would not know about sleep) because, in samślēśam (union), he would not let her sleep and in viślēśam (separation) her sorrow in separation will not let her sleep; so, in both cases, she does not get to sleep \[hence, she does not even know about sleep\]. Even if she would have slept during union, the mother who observes her current suffering, would not consider that sleep as significant! The mother would not consider that sleep as significant since it is a rehearsal for her subsequent suffering. Just as someone who was born in a prison cell and was raised there, would think about that suffering even after getting released and living comfortably.
- *aṟiyāḷ* – While being together with śrī rāma in the forest, lakśmaṇa considering sleep to be a hurdle, gave it up. This is the distinguished nature of [parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) even more than such servitors. Though ādiśēśa \[previous form of lakśmaṇa\] never knew sleep, to play the role of lakśmaṇa properly, he pretended to give up the sleep.
- *kaṇṇa nīr kaigaḷāl iṟaikkum* – But her ignorance is not manifested all the times! Thinking “at this stage, my lord will certainly come, and I cannot be with teary eyes or have tired posture when he comes; I should see from the time he enter this place” she is trying to hide her tears. How amazing! She thinks that she can stop her tears and starts working on it. It is said in tiruviruttam 18 “*kadal koṇḍa kaṇṇīr*” (tears like ocean). She is thinking that she can fetch the water from the ocean using a kōkuḷ leaf and empty the ocean! She is trying to empty the tears using her own hands. It is as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 33.4 “*kimartam tavanētrābhyām*” (why are tears flowing from the eyes of your highness?).
- *sangu* – She is thinking about the divine form which will appear in front of her, once she stops the tears. She is desiring to see him with his divine weapons as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 6.5.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/02/thiruvaimozhi-6-5-1-thuvalil-ma-mani-madam/) “*tavaḷa oṇ sangu cakkaram*” (white coloured radiant conch and chakra)! Only for those unfavourable ones, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) should remain two-handed. arjuna who desired to his original form, said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 11.46](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/11-46/) “*tēnaivarūpēṇa caturbhujēna*” (your original four handed form). She desires to say “*kūrārāḻi veṇ sangēndi*” , but is unable to complete that due to her weakness; just as a thirsty person would request water using sign language \[being unable to speak\], here [parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) performs an anjali \[to indicate her desire to see him with his weapons\].
- *tāmaraik kaṇ enṟē taḷarum* – While trying to say how his eyes expand up to those āḻvārs \[Sanka, chakra et al are all nityasūris who are known as āḻvārs (immersed in bhagavat anubhavam) with certain forms\] and manifest their beauty, she became weakened. Setting out to say as in tiruvāimoḻi 9.2.1 “*un tāmaraik kaṇgaḷāl nōkkāy*” (you glance at me with your lotus eyes), she became weakened. As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 26.37 “*rāmam raktānta nayanam apaśyantī du:khitā*” (I have become anguished due to not seeing śrī rāma’s eyes which are red in their ends).

Why are you becoming weakened? Why can’t you spend your time doing something else? ..

- *enganē darikkēn unnai vittu ennum* – Can I be pacified that I desired for param (bhagavān’s form as paravāsudēva in śrīvaikuṇṭam) or vyūham (bhagavān’s form in kśīrābdi) \[and rightfully did not get to see them due to the distance\]?
- *unnai vittu enganē darikkēn ennum* – She is asking if she was caught in worldly pleasures in the absence of which she could engage in \[casual\] gambling, chess etc? \[No. She is caught in the most distinguished [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), so she cannot sustain herself in his absence\]. If you knew your own greatness “Should you not know that those who get separated from me will not survive?”
- *unnai vittu enganē darikkēn ennum* – Have you not seen yourself in the mirror? If you have seen yourself, you will not separate \[from yourself\]; if you separated, you too will suffer like her.

As [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) did not arrive even after saying “*enganē darikkēn*” (how will I survive?),

- *iru nilam kai tuḻā irukkum* – (due to the mud which was created from the tears) the great earth became a semi-solid state like sandalwood paste in a small container.
- *sem kayal* – Even the animals (fish in this case) are well nourished! They are healthy and active; but she lost her complexion. One which held on to nāra (water) is living happily; but why is my daughter who held on to [nārāyaṇa](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) in distress?
- *sem kayal* – Beautiful fish. Only if that fish can survive without water, she can survive without you. She is mentioned in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 53.31 “*muhūrtam api jeevāva: jalān matsyā vivōtrutau”* (if we separate from you, we will die like a fish out of the water).
- *ivaḷ tiṟattu* – As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 6.16 “*ēhi paśya śarīrāṇi*” (Look at our bodies), since her state is not explainable through words, the mother is showing her body to [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/). Just as the riśis (sages) showed the bodies which were partly consumed by rākśasas \[reference here is to śrī rāma when he came for the first time to daṇḍakāraṇya forest\], here the mother is showing her daughter’s body which is consumed by the sorrow in separation.
- *en seyginṟāyē* – What are you planning to do for her? Should she not become as happy as the creatures \[like fish\] in your town, for seeking you?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.2.2. En seyginray

*en seyginṟāy en tāmaraik kaṇṇā ennum kaṇṇīr malga irukkum en seygēn eṟi nīrt tiruvarangattāy ennum vevvuyirttuyirtturugum mun seyda vinaiyē mugappadāy ennum mugil vaṇṇā taguvadō ennum mun seydivvulagam uṇḍumiḻndaḷandāy en kolō mudiginṟadivatkē*

**Пословный перевод:**

en – (first) making me existing for you only; tāmarai – very enjoyable (to cause desire in me); kaṇṇā – Oh one who is having eyes!; en seyginṟāy – what are you thinking to do?; ennum – says; kaṇ – eye; nīr – tears; malga – to overflow; irukkum – remain put being unable to move; eṟi – with rising waves; nīr – having water; tiruvarangattāy – Oh one who resides in kōyil (śrīrangam)!; en – what; seygēn – shall I do?; ennum – says; vev – (due to inward heat) to become hot; uyirttu uyirttu – repeatedly breathing heavily; urugum – will melt due to that situation; mun – previously; seyda – (I) committed; vinaiyē – karma (virtues/vices); mugappadāy – appearing in front; ennum – says considering the karma to be a cētana (sentient being) due to its act of causing harm; mugilvaṇṇā – Oh one who is magnanimous like clouds which pour the rain without distinguishing between land and water!; taguvadō – does it match (such magnanimity)?; ennum – says; i – this; ulagam – world; mun – first; seydu – created; uṇḍu – consumed (during deluge); umiḻndu – spat out; aḷandāy – Oh one who measured and accepted!; ivatku – for her (who cannot survive without you); en – how; mudiginṟadu kolō – is it going to end?

**Перевод:**

**She says “Oh one who is having very enjoyable eyes which are making me exist for you only! What are you thinking to do?” With tearful eyes, she would remain put; she says “Oh one who resides in kōyil (śrīrangam) which is having water with rising waves! what shall I do?” She will repeatedly breathe \[heavily\] to become hot inwardly and will melt due to that situation; she says that her previous karma is appearing in front of her, considering the karma to be a cētana due to its act of causing harm; she says “Oh one who is magnanimous like clouds which pour the rain without distinguishing between land and water! Does it match your magnanimity \[to not appear in front of me\]?” \[the mother asks\] Oh one who first created, consumed, spat out, measured and accepted the world! How is it going to end for her? Implies “Is she going to be included in the group of those who are protected by you, to end her distress? ōr is she going to be pushed out to be kept away?”**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the second pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki‘s mother says “Where will this girl’s state lead her to?”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently,  parānguśa nāyaki’s mother says “While you are the protector in all manners, where is her state leading to?”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. en seyginṟāy en tāmaraik kaṇṇā ennum kaṇṇīr malga irukkum en seygēn eṟi nīrt tiruvarangattāy ennum vevvuyirttuyirtturugum mun seyda vinaiyē mugappadāy ennum mugil vaṇṇā taguvadō ennum mun seydivvulagam uṇḍumiḻndaḷandāy en kolō mudiginṟadivatkē*

- *en seyginṟāy* – As the anguish increases, they will only ask him \[for a solution\].
- *en tāmaraik kaṇṇā ennum* – She is saying “Can you not shower your mercy like cloud pouring into dried out crop which is seeking water?” It is said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 1.20.16 “*avalōkana dānēna bhūyōmām pālaya*” (Oh lord! protect me with your glance). She said “*tāmaraik kaṇ enṟē taḷarum*“; while becoming conscious too, she would blabber the same thing. When she approached him \[previously\], he said through his eyes “My belongings and I are at your disposal”; only based on that, she fully submitted herself. Thinking about how he would glance at her and how he would embrace her with his hands, she would be overwhelmed with emotions and remain with tears in the eyes, as he she united with him and separated.
- *en seygēn …* – She says “Can you not throw me into the wavy waters to eliminate my suffering?”. The water of divine kāvēri river would remain hot like moon for those who are in separation \[in separation, even the coolness of moon will be unbearable\].
- *en seygēn* – What shall I do to reach you? As she did not attain him immediately, she would sigh thinking “This is how nicely we attained him” \[being sarcastic\]. As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 17.29 “*dahantīm iva niśvāsair vrukśān pallava dāriṇa:*” (she who appears to be burning the tender shoots of the trees, with her sighing), she is trying use her sigh to eliminate her enemies. Her enemy now is the trees with tender shoots \[they are fresh, while she is suffering\]. They would all stand together and torment her. Even rākśasi would sometimes sleep \[and give break for their torment\] but these trees stand firm all the time. They remain firm all the time.
- *urugum* – She will remain there while melting.  She would melt so much that there is no entity to sigh anymore. She would breathe heavily with heat for long time and will melt due to that heat.
- *mun seyda vinaiyē* – Seeing the means to firm up \[from the melted state\]. She says “Oh my perviously committed sins! Please stand in front of me”. If you stand in front of me, I will stop asking him “tāmaraik kaṇṇā – en seyginṟāy” (oh lotus eyed lord! what are you planning to do?). She remains “As my suffering is a result of my own sins, who can I blame for that?” Both the divine daughter of king janaka and [parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) have the same situation; both remain “everything good is because of him; and everything bad is because of me”. sītāp pirātti said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 38.48 “*mamaiva duśkrutam kincit mahadasti na samśaya:*” (My sins are huge; there is no doubt).
- *mugil vaṇṇā taguvadō ennum* – My sins aside, would you only act based on my karma? taguvadō – will it fit your magnanimity? She says “For your magnanimity due to which you shower mercy towards all like a cloud which pours rain on water and land, is this a fitting conduct?” She says “[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is capable of manifesting himself saying ‘is this sin really powerful in my presence? Did I not cause it in the first place?’ ” Though this overwhelming attachment is a result of bhakti (love/devotion), since it is stopping her from enjoying bhagavān, she is highlighting it to be a sin. Whatever causes unfavourable results, that is called sin. When the text is read as “*tagavidō*“, she says “If the result of my sin is to be experienced by me, what is the purpose of your mercy?” By saying “*mun seyda vinaiyē mugappadāy*“, the opinion of those \[pūrva mīmāmsaka\] who say “the karma will remain as adruśta (invisible) and give the result later” is expressed; by saying “*mugilvaṇṇā*“, it is the opinion of vēdāntis who say “result can be bestowed only by the supreme lord’s mercy”. The previous statement is similar to the words of sugrīva et al who said “those who are with defects do not belong in śrī rāma’s group”; subsequent words are like the philosophy of śrī rāma as in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 18.3 ‘*dōśō yadyapi tasya syāt’* (Even if faults are there in him, let them be). The previous statement is similar to [śrī bhagavat gītā 9.34](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/9-34/) “*mām namaskuru*” (worship me) \[onus is on ātmā\]; “*tagavidō*” is like [śrī bhagavat gītā 18.66](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/18-66/) “*mā śuca:*” (do not grieve) \[onus is on bhagavān\].

[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) asks “Where did you see my magnanimity fructifying to say “mugilvaṇṇā”?”

- *mun seydu* … – You performed creation etc out of your natural inclination; did you not create these and protect them when there was no tool for the ātmās to say “*tagavidō*“? During the danger of deluge, did you not secure them in your stomach, release them out when it was apt and measure the world by walking all over and hence protect in all manners!
- *en kolō mudiginṟadu ivatkē* – It appears that the entity ([parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)) will be finished. Are you seeing or not, the difference between the earth which you protect and her? (she has placed all her responsibility on you and is helpless;) Is it her karma or your mercy which is going to win? (Implies, what are you going to do for her? or what is going to happen to her state?).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.2.3. Vatkilal

*vatkilaḷ iṟaiyum maṇivaṇṇā! ennum vānamē nōkkum maiyākkum utkudai asurar uyir ellām uṇḍa oruvanē! ennum uḷḷurugum katkilee unnaik kāṇumāṟaruḷāy kāguttā! kaṇṇanē! ennum titkodi madiḷ sūḻ tiruvarangattāy! ivaḷ tiṟatten seydittāyē?*

**Пословный перевод:**

iṟaiyum – even a little bit; vatku – shyness which is her identity; ilaḷ – she is not having; maṇivaṇṇā – Oh one who is obedient to me like a blue gem which can be placed in the pocket!; ennum – says; vānamē – sky; nōkkum – looks up; maiyākkum – becomes unconscious; utku – pride; udai – having; asurar – demoniac person’s; uyir – life; ellām – without any remainder; uṇḍa – swallowed; oruvanē – oh independently valorous person!; ennum – says; uḷ – inside; urugum – breaks down; katku – by the eye; ilee – oh one who is difficult to be seen!; unnai – you (who cannot be missed to be seen for my survival); kāṇumāṟu – to be seen; aruḷāy – kindly be merciful; kāguttā – as the divine son of daśarata who manifested himself to those belonging to cities and forests as said in “pumsām druśti cittāpahāriṇām” and “dadruśu: vismitākārā:” respectively; kaṇṇanē – did you not incarnate as kriṣṇa who manifested your beauty to covherd girls as said in “tāsām āvirabhūt“?; ennum – says; tiṇ – firm; kodi – having flag; madiḷ – fort; sūḻ – surrounded; tiruvarangattāy – oh one who is residing in kōyil (śrīrangam)!; ivaḷ tiṟattu – to put her in sorrow; en seytittāy – what did you do?

**Перевод:**

**My daughter is not having shyness which is her identity, even a little bit; she says “Oh one who is obedient to me like a blue gem which can be placed in the pocket!” She looks up the sky and becomes unconscious; she says “Oh independently valorous person who swallowed the life of the prideful, demoniac persons without any remainder!” She breaks down inside her; she says “Oh one who is difficult to be seen by the eye! kindly be merciful to be seen by me”; she says – did you not incarnate as the divine son of daśarata who manifested himself to those belonging to cities and forests as said in “pumsām druśti cittāpahāriṇām” and “dadruśu: vismitākārā:” respectively and kriṣṇa manifesting your beauty to covherd girls as said in “tāsām āvirabhūt“? \[mother says\] Oh one who is residing in kōyil (śrīrangam) which is having the firm flag on the surrounding fort! What did you do to her to put her in such sorrow?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the third pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki’s mother says “What did you do to her, to have her reach this state?”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently,  parānguśa nāyaki’s mother says “Being the one who has incarnations which are focussed on eliminating the enemies of the devotees, what did you do to her, to have her reach this state? “.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. vatkilaḷ iṟaiyum maṇivaṇṇā! ennum vānamē nōkkum maiyākkum utkudai asurar uyir ellām uṇḍa oruvanē! ennum uḷḷurugum katkilee unnaik kāṇumāṟaruḷāy kāguttā! kaṇṇanē! ennum titkodi madiḷ sūḻ tiruvarangattāy! ivaḷ tiṟatten seydittāyē?*

- *vatkilaḷ iṟaiyum* – nanjīyar mercifully explains this as “she is finished”. vatku – lajjā (shyness). A woman will be known by her shyness. If a quality which is close to the identity is lost, the entity itself will also be lost. Without the quality which identifies an entity, the entity will not exist.

What is the clue for her loss of shyness?

- *maṇivaṇṇā ennum* – She is saying the name of her husband. She is describing the beauty of her husband in the presence of her mother. She is revealing those matters which she would hide even if I enquired her about the same. A girl who is in love, will obviously like his physical beauty; she is describing the feature in which she became captivated. She has now acquired the nature of thinking about his form, speaking about his form and enjoying his form! She prays towards him for the same thing as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 7.1.8](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/07/thiruvaimozhi-7-1-8-innamudhu/) “*un cinnamum tirumūrttiyum sindittēttik kai toḻavē aruḷ enakku*”  (Bless me to worship your divine form which is decorated with distinguished symbols such as Sanka, chakra etc).
- *maṇivaṇṇā ennum* – She kept highlighting his beautiful form and simplicity. His form and qualities cannot be spoken about whatever may be one’s state as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 58.35 “*adruśta pūrva vyasanā mruduśeelā manasvinī \| tēna du:kēna rudatī naivamākincit abhravīt \|\|*” (sītāp pirātti who is tender, grave and in great sorrow which was never seen by her previously, was crying due to that sorrow and could not speak to me).
- *vānamē nōkkum* – He is incapable to remain there after hearing the cry “*maṇivaṇṇā!*“. As he appeared through that sound \[sky/ether which is the element which carries sound\] for śrī gajēndrāḻvān, she is looking up at the sky to see his arrival. She is in an even more dangerous state than śrī gajēndrāḻvān’s state which is said in viṣṇu darmam “*paramāpadam āpanna:*” (one who was caught in great danger).

As she is not seeing his arrival there,

- *maiyākkum* – becoming unconscious; becoming bewildered.

Would becoming unconscious help in eliminating the hurdles? \[No\]

- *utkudai …* – When I try to come to you, the hurdles appear too. But if you come to me, who will be able to stop that? utku – pride. For him to destroy the enemies, they should be prideful and many.
- *uṇḍa* – As said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 1.19.24 “*babau janārdana: krutta:*” ([bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/), with anger, consumed the wind named aticōśaṇam).
- *oruvanē ennum* – Even if there is comparison for his beauty, there is nothing comparable to his valour.
- *utkudai …* – She is speaking like a vīrapatni (wife of a valorous person). She is the one who said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 22.16 “*tvam nīca śaśavat smruta:*” (You are like an inferior rabbit in front of śrī rāma).
- *uḷ urugum* – She would become broken thinking “Why am I losing [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) while there is no shortcoming?” As there is no reason for the delay, she will melt like ice due to not attaining emperumān. Others \[such as mother et al\] will question “just because she melts, would he who is beyond the senses, become visible?”; but she remains “is there any such rule for the one who gets him by his mercy?” What is said in taittirīya upaniśat as “*na cakśuśā paśyati*” is for those who try to see him with their own effort; it is not difficult when emperumān himself shows him as said in upaniśat “*tasyaiśa ātmā vivruṇutē tanūm svām*” ([paramātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) shows his form to those who are blessed by him). Did he not bestow divine eyes and show himself to arjuna et al?
- *katkilee* –  Oh one who is not visible for the eyes!
- *unnaik kāṇumāṟu aruḷāy* – It is difficult to see you for those who try to see you on their own; is it difficult to see you even for those who get to see you by your mercy?

[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) asks “Who did I show myself to with my mercy?”

- *kāguttā* – Did you not show yourself to the residents of the city and the forest as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 3.29 “*rūpaudāryaguṇai:*” (his form, magnanimity and simplicity) and śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kaṇḍam 1.1 “*rūpam samhananam lakśmīm*” (his form, beauty and tenderness)?

[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) asks “Are you just saying this based on my one-off act?”

- *kaṇṇanē* – Did you not show your form to those girls who were born in the same clan? śrī bhāgavatam 10.32.2 is explained.
   - *tāsām āvirabhūt* – Like a heavy down pour on the crop in a drought-hit field.
   - *smayamāna mukhāmbuhuja:* – On appearing in front of them, his face acquired new freshness.
   - *pītāmbaradaras sragvī* – He changes the minds of the girls by showing off his well-worn clothes and the garland on the shoulder.
   - *sākśāt manmada manmada:* – Whatever the world goes through with cupid, cupid goes through with [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)!
   - *titkodi …* – When asked “You did not help me during your incarnations!” emperumān says “Have I not mercifully reclined here (śrīrangam) for those who missed out during my incarnations?” I have hoisted the flag and am waiting to show myself to those who are favourable towards me. The firmness could be an adjective for both the fort and flag; titkodi also means that which is never replaced. The flag which is hoisted to indicate “whoever desires to come is welcome”.
   - *ivaḷ tiṟattu en seydittāyē* – What did you do to her to have her go mad at you in this manner? He would apply a medicine without her knowledge. The medicine is his face only as said in nācciyār tirumoḻi 2.4 “*maiyal ēṟṟi mayakka un mugam māya mandiram tānkolō*” (Your face is the medicine which will drive me mad). When asked “what does she need now?” she says that, as a retaliation, parānguśa nāyaki who is like pirātti as said in sundara kāṇḍam 16.14 “*trailōkya rājyam sakalam sītāyā nāpnuyāt kalām*” (the three worlds, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is indicated by the term world, and everything else is no match for sītā), should be placed in front of emperumān, and make him go through the same torment she went through.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.2.4. Itta kal

*itta kāl itta kaiyaḷāy irukkum eḻundulāy mayangum kai kūppum kattamē kādal enṟu mūrccikkum kadal vaṇṇā! kadiyai kāṇennum vatta vāy nēmi valangaiyā ennum vandidāy enṟenṟē mayangum sittanē! seḻu nīrt tiruvarangattāy! ivaḷ tiṟatten sindittāyē?*

**Пословный перевод:**

itta itta – wherever placed; kāl – leg; kaiyaḷ – and hand; āy – having; irukkum – remains; eḻundu – stands up, after regaining consciousness; ulāy – walks around; mayangum – subsequently becomes unconscious; kai kūppum – performs anjali (joined palms); kādal – love; kattamē – is difficult to handle; enṟu – becoming upset; mūrccikkum – loses conscious; kadalvaṇṇā – oh one who is like immeasurable ocean which secures everything inside it!; kadiyai kāṇ – You are being cruel towards me!; ennum – says; vatta vāy – wholesome; nēmi – divine chakra; valam kaiyā – oh one who is having in your right hand!; ennum – says; vandidāy – come here with the divine chakra in your hand; enṟu enṟē – repeatedly requesting; mayangum – loses her mind thinking “I lost my nature due to repeatedly calling him, and lost the desire/goal as he did not come”; sittanē – pretending to be a reputed person; seḻu nīrt tiruvarangattāy – oh one who is reclining on the beautiful banks of the river \[kāvēri\]!; ivaḷ tiṟattu – in her case (where she is bewildered in separation); en – what; sindittāy – are you thinking?

**Перевод:**

**My daughter’s leg and hand remain \[unmoved\] wherever they were placed; after regaining consciousness, she stands up, walks around and subsequently becomes unconscious; she performs anjali; becoming upset saying “love is difficult to handle”, she loses consciousness; she says “Oh one who is like immeasurable ocean which secures everything inside it! You are being cruel towards me!” She says “oh one who is having the wholesome divine chakra in your right hand!”; She is repeatedly requesting him saying “come here with the divine chakra in your hand” and loses her mind thinking “I lost my nature due to repeatedly calling him, and lost the desire/goal as he did not come”; oh one who is reclining on the beautiful banks of the river, pretending to be a reputed person! What are you thinking in her case? Implies, “Are you thinking to only keep her bewildered? ōr are you planning enlighten her?”**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fourth pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki’s mother requests periya perumāḷ “What are you mercifully thinking to do for this girl?”*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. itta kāl itta kaiyaḷāy irukkum eḻundulāy mayangum kai kūppum kattamē kādal enṟu mūrccikkum kadal vaṇṇā! kadiyai kāṇennum vatta vāy nēmi valangaiyā ennum vandidāy enṟenṟē mayangum sittanē! seḻu nīrt tiruvarangattāy! ivaḷ tiṟatten sindittāyē?*

- *itta kāl itta kaigaḷāy irukkum* – You need not present your form to her, it is sufficient if you can make her limbs obey her command. She will remain where her friends placed her as said in “*sakībhi: nyasta prakīrṇa paratantra vipāṇḍurāngī*” (One who has pale limbs which were spread by her friends, who is unconscious). As she is unconscious, she would remain the way her friends placed her legs and hands.
- *eḻundulāy mayangum* – Like a lamp which will shine brightly before going off, she is having baseless rising and roaming around; just as the lamp will be off as it starts shining brightly, she too fell unconscious.
- *kai kūppum* – She does not perform anjali (vorśipping with joined palms) only while awakening and does remain without vorśipping while unconscious, since does not do the worship as a means; but she cannot avoid vorśipping when in distress.
- *kattamē kādal enṟu …* – If she is performing anjali as a means, she would not say that it is difficult. Since the love is the cause for torment in separation, she is saying it is difficult.
- *kadal vaṇṇā kadiyai kāṇ ennum* – The ocean will contain everything in it, and will ensure that one creature does not trouble another creature; she says “such you (emperumān) have become cruel”. Alternative explanation – she says “you who have a form without which those who are separated cannot sustain themselves, have now become cruel like a murderer”.
- *vatta vāy nēmi* – She has crossed the stage of saying “*sangu cakkarangaḷ*“. Though invisible now, the thought of the chakra causes hatred; wherever touched one can feel its mouth (opening). You are not without the tools to eliminate the hurdles.
- *vandidāy enṟenṟē mayangum* – She is unable to remain if it is said that you will be coming soon. A thirsty person would cry out repeatedly saying “water” until his thirst is quenched;  similarly, parānguśa nāyaki says “vandidāy! vandidāy!”; she does not know anything else.
- *mayangum* – she will recite it repeatedly having her inclination as the teacher \[who makes her repeat it\].
- *enṟenṟē* – Just as the sound of bell metal will keep echoing.
- *sittanē* – \[condemning his act\] Here śrīman nārāyaṇa is said to be the śiśta (reputed). Saying that he has great love towards pirātti; also explained as one who drives pirātti crazy on him and torments her; your conduct is very nice \[sarcastic\]. Helpless women will be finished if there were a few reputed persons like you. You are nicely showering your mercy \[sarcastic\]. Your act resembles that of those who do abominable acts such as killing brāhmaṇas, but walking around wearing bright yajñōpavīdam (sacred thread), having pavitram (a sacred ornament made out of darbha grass) and reciting vēdams.
- *seḻu nīrt tiruvarangattāy* – kōyil (śrīrangam) which has invigorating water bodies. Your reclining here is like the presence of a murderer in a water booth \[which is placed during summer time to distribute water\].
- *ivaḷ tiṟattu en sindittāyē* – The mother thinks that even emperumān who is sarvajña (omniscient) has to ponder on a remedy for her daughter’s state; this is the clarity of the divine mother of parānguśa nāyaki. She is praying at his divine feet thinking “emperumān’s thoughts can only lead to solution”. He is the one who thinks for the favourable ones as said in “*śrēyō dyāyati kēśava:*” (kēśava looks out for the well-being of the favourable ones). Will you just keep thinking like this, and will you not give a firm solution?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.2.5. Sindikkum tisaikkum

*sindikkum tisaikkum tēṟum kai kūppum tiruvarangattuḷḷāy ennum vandikkum āngē maḻaik kaṇ nīr malga vandidāy enṟenṟē mayangum andip pōdavuṇan udal idandānē! alai kadal kadainda āramudē! sandittun caraṇam sārvadē valitta taiyalai maiyal seydānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

andi – sandyā (dusk); pōdu – in the particular time; avuṇan – hiraṇya, the asura (demon), his; udal – body; idandānē – one who tore apart; alai – having waves; kadal – ocean; kadainda – churned; āramudē – being infinitely enjoyable; sandittu – meeting, to have external experience; un caraṇamē – your divine feet only; sārvadu – to unite and enjoy; valitta – having perfectly fit form; taiyalai – this girl; maiyal seydānē – oh one who bewildered!; sindikkum – thinks about how you united with her previously; tisaikkum – (since she cannot experience it immediately) becomes bewildered; tēṟum – regains composure; kai kūppum – performs anjali; tiruvarangattu – in kōyil (śrīrangam); uḷḷāy – Oh one who is reclining!; ennum – calls saying \[that\]; vandikkum – (thinking about your beauty) she bows her head; angē – remaining there itself; maḻai – cool; kaṇṇīr malga – to have eyes filled with tears; vandidāy – come and accept me; enṟu enṟē – repeatedly saying; mayangum – becomes unconscious (since her desire is not fulfilled)

**Перевод:**

**You (emperumān) tore apart the body of hiraṇya, the asura in the particular time of sandyā and being infinitely enjoyable, churned the ocean having waves; oh one who bewildered this girl who has a perfectly fit form and is desiring to unite with you to have external experience of enjoying your divine feet only! She thinks about how you united with her previously, becomes bewildered, regains composure and performs anjali; she calls you saying “Oh one who is residing in kōyil!” and bows her head; remaining there itself, with eyes filled with cool tears, repeatedly saying “come and accept me” she becomes unconscious. Implies that she goes through all kinds of transformations with respect to romantic interactions with emperumān.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fifth pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki’s mother informs the transformations her daughter is going through every moment and says “Would it befit your qualities such as āśrita vātsalya (motherly affection towards devotees) etc to torment her in this manner?”*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. sindikkum tisaikkum tēṟum kai kūppum tiruvarangattuḷḷāy ennum vandikkum āngē maḻaik kaṇ nīr malga vandidāy enṟenṟē mayangum andip pōdavuṇan udal idandānē! alai kadal kadainda āramudē! sandittun caraṇam sārvadē valitta taiyalai maiyal seydānē*

- *sindikkum* – She thinks about your qualities such as saundaryam (beauty) and your previous unions with her. Previously she was not even able to think about these; this is also a transformation like being unconscious.
- *tisaikkum* – becomes bewildered since she does not see you immediately.
- *tēṟum* – without any reason, suddenly she acquired clarity in mind. This is frightening me; while she is unconscious, the sudden awakening as if her desire was fulfilled, is frightening. \[Usually\] one acquires clarity in his/her final moments – so her sudden awakening should be feared. Whenever uynda piḷḷai araiyar recited this pāsuram, nanjīyar would mercifully say “My bad! she is now saying ‘tēṟum’ “.
- *kai kūppum* – This is her nature. Previously it was said “*mayangum kai kūppum*” (she will become unconscious and perform anjali) and here it is saying “*tēṟum kai kūppum*” (she realises and performs anjali); while rest of the aspects are changing, this \[vorśipping him\] is a constant factor since it is part of her nature. It is said in mahābhāratam mōkśa darmam “*nityānjali putā hruśtā:*” (they are always performing anjali). The existence is present in both unconscious and awakened states; the true nature is as explained in tiruvāimoḻi 3.3.1 “*vaḻuvilā adimai seyya vēṇḍu nām*” (we should serve continuously). That which is constantly performed is the goal.
- *tiruvarangattu uḷḷāy ennum* – nanjīyar would mercifully say “*perumāḷē ennum*“. [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is desired only due to his presence in this divya dēśam.
- *vandikkum* – Having “*tiruvarangattuḷḷāy*” fixated in her heart, she praises “What a face! What a smile! What a garland he is wearing!”; alternative explanation – devoid of any pride, she would remain at his divine feet.
- *āngē* – in that state.
- *maḻaik kaṇṇīr …* – With cool tears, she would say “have you come” and will lose her mind.

Will he come as soon as one thinks about him?

- *andip pōdu* – Would you only help those who have clarity as said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 1.19.85 “*mattas sarvam aham sarvam mayi sarvam sanātanē*” (prahlāda said “Everything originated from me and everything subdued into me, who is eternal”)? Can you not help those who are bewildered? Did you not tear the demoniac hiraṇya’s body arriving at the time which was contrary to the boon he acquired? Would you only help if the father becomes an enemy? Can you not help when you are the enemy? There is no greater enmity than not helping even at this stage.

[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) says “I helped the child once. Is there any other incident?” and the mother responds “Did you not help subsequently?”

- *alai kadal kadainda* – Did you not churn the ocean even for the prayōjanāntaraparars (those who are looking for other benefits from you)? Would you only help those who would use you to fulfil their own desires? Can you not help those who consider you as the only benefit?
- *āramudē* –  They churned the ocean with [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s nectar \[[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)\].
- *sandittu …* – You are playing with the mind of this girl who desires to reach you and be at your divine feet! Alternative explanation – the girl who is holding on to her life to reach you and finish herself in your presence. valitta – having firm faith. She remains as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 36.30 “*tāvadyaham dūta jijīviśēyam*” (Oh hanuman! I wish to be alive until I hear about my beloved lord’s activity to save me).
- *maiyal seydānē* – Even for my daughter who desired for you, the result is bewilderment.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.2.6. Maiyal seydu

*maiyal seydu ennai manam kavarndānē! ennum māmāyanē! ennum seyya vāy maṇiyē! ennum taṇ punal sūḻ tiruvarangattuḷḷāy ennum veyya vāḷ taṇḍu sangu cakkaram vil ēndum viṇṇōr mudal! ennum pai koḷ pāmbaṇaiyāy! ivaḷ tiṟattaruḷāy pāviyēn seyaṟpāladuvē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ennai – me; maiyal seydu – causing bewilderment; manam – heart; kavarndānē – oh one who stole!; ennum – says; māmāyanē – having infinite, amazing activities in order to cause bewilderment in me; ennum – says; seyya – reddish; vāy – having beautiful lips; maṇiyē – oh one who is easy to handle like a precious gemstone!; ennum – says; taṇ – (to reach you and eliminating my suffering, being) cool; punal – water; sūḻ – surrounded; tiruvarangattu – in kōyil (śrīrangam); uḷḷāy – oh one who is residing!; ennum – says; veyya – very angry towards enemies; vāḷ taṇḍu sangu cakkaram vil – the five divine weapons; ēndum – carrying them always as someone who cannot delay the protection of the surrendered ones; viṇṇōr – letting the nityasūris enjoy; mudal – oh one who is the cause for their existence etc!; ennum – says; pai – expanded hoods, due to being in contact with you; koḷ – having; pāmbu – tiruvanantāḻvān (who is having infinite enjoyability due to its natural tenderness, coolness, fragrance); aṇaiyāy – oh one who is having as mattress!; ivaḷ tiṟattu – towards her (who is suffering due to lying on the ground, while you are comfortably resting on the mattress); pāviyēn – I who am having sins which made me witness her such pathetic state; seyaṟpāladu – the act; aruḷāy – mercifully say

**Перевод:**

**My daughter says “oh one who stole my heart, causing bewilderment!”; she says ” oh one who is easy to handle like a precious gemstone and is having reddish beautiful lips!”; she says “oh one who is residing in kōyil (śrīrangam) which is surrounded by beautiful water bodies”; she says “oh you are carrying the five divine weapons always as someone who cannot delay the protection of the surrendered ones”; she says “oh one who is the cause for the existence etc of nityasūris! and oh one who is having tiruvanantāḻvān as his mattress!” I am having sins which made me witness her such pathetic state. Mercifully tell me “What is your act towards her?”**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the sixth pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki’s mother says “She is suffering like this and you are not eliminating her suffering; the reason for this  is my karma (virtues/vices)”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently,  parānguśa nāyaki’s mother says “You who are having the necessary weapons to protect your devotees still made my daughter suffer, should tell me what should I do for her”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. maiyal seydu ennai manam kavarndānē! ennum māmāyanē! ennum seyya vāy maṇiyē! ennum taṇ punal sūḻ tiruvarangattuḷḷāy ennum veyya vāḷ taṇḍu sangu cakkaram vil ēndum viṇṇōr mudal! ennum pai koḷ pāmbaṇaiyāy! ivaḷ tiṟattaruḷāy pāviyēn seyaṟpāladuvē*

- *maiyal seydu* – If she is in the awakened state, she will feel the loss in her heart \[so he bewildered her\]. Just as one will wait for a lax moment in the enemy camp to enter and capture their fort \[emperumān entered her and captured her\].
- *ennai* – She is saying “me” as one would say “he has reached the ocean bed”.
- *manam kavarndānē* – As the scent extracted from civet \[a type of cat\] is used and the container is thrown out.
- *maiyal …* – As someone would kill and rob the wallet.
- *mā māyanē ennum* – The way he bewildered and captured her. She is thinking about the amazing acts done by emperumān during their union such as remaining obediently towards her, massaging her hands and feet etc. His obedient postures during romance is appearing to be similar to his natural supremacy. She would say “Oh one who performed amazing acts during our union!”.
- *seyya vāya maṇiyē ennum* – This is one of the amazing aspects. Giving up his pride, he said “I am yours” and the lips manifested redness at that time. It is said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 5.17.21 “*savilāsasmitādāram*” (one who has the smiling, beautiful lotus-like mouth/lips).
- *maṇiyē* – Just as a flower will appear fresh when it blossoms, the whole of his divine form appears fresh when he smiles.
- *taṇ punal* – Just as the coolness in his smile, the town is cool as well. Just as the coolness of the mouth, the divya dēśam is cool as well.
- *veyya vāḷ …* – Just as the divine weapons are used to destroy the enemies, they are also used to destroy the romantic damsels. They are winning over the favourable and the unfavourable ones equally. He has placed them in his front side to be seen by others. You who are holding up the divine weapons which defeat the enemies who see them, are not manifesting yourself after eliminating my enemies.
- *viṇṇōr mudal ennum* – As emperumān manifests his divine beauty of his carrying his divine weapons, the whole of paramapadam sustains with that vision. Otherwise, there is no reason for him to carry the divine weapons there as enemies are not present in paramapadam.
- *pai koḷ …* – His smile, his divine weapons, his being together with nitya vibhūti (paramapadam), his reclining on tiruvanantāḻvān (ādiśēśan) etc are all desirable. Oh one who is having ādiśēśan who has expanded hoods due to being in constant contact with bhagavān’s divine form, as your mattress! While she is lying on the ground, why are you reclining alone on ādiśēśan?
- *ivaḷ tiṟattaruḷāy* – Even if you don’t accept her on your bed, should you not at least shower the mercy which is common for everyone?
- *ivaḷ tiṟattu* – On my daughter who is in sorrow.
- *aruḷāy* – You who are seeking those who are expecting your mercy, are letting her who cannot survive without your mercy, to suffer on the ground!
- *pāviyēn* – Neither are you not showering your mercy, nor will she survive without your mercy; this is all due to my sin. As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam “*matpāpamēvātra nimittam āsīt*” (the reason for the current situation is my sin only).
- *seyaṟpāladu* – It is my acts which caused you not to bestow your mercy upon her. There is no fault either on my daughter or on you, it is the sin of me who desires to see your togetherness, which is the cause for this situation.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.2.7. Pala tunbangal

*pāla tunbangaḷ inbangaḷ padaittāy! paṟṟilār paṟṟa ninṟānē! kāla cakkarattāy! kadal idam koṇḍa kadalvaṇṇā! kaṇṇanē! ennum sēl koḷ taṇ punal sūḻ tiruvarangattāy! ennum en tīrttanē! ennum kōla mā maḻaik kaṇ pani malga irukkum ennudaik kōmaḷak koḻundē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ennudai – my; kōmaḷam – tender natured; koḻundu – my daughter who is like a slender creeper; pāla – in every place; tunbangaḷ – sorrows for those who are not surrendered; inbangaḷ – joy for the surrendered ones; padaittāy – one who created; paṟṟu – attachment; ilār – like jayanta who did not have; paṟṟa – to surrender; ninṟānē – one who stands as the refuge for those who don’t have refuge; kāla cakkarattāy – being the controller of the wheel of time (to ensure that the apt time for the surrendered ones be at his disposal, having the units such as month, season, year etc); kadal – in the divine milk ocean; kadal vaṇṇā – like an ocean reclining on another ocean; idam koṇḍa – mercifully resting; kaṇṇanē – Oh one who appeared as kriṣṇa for the protection \[of devotees\]!; ennum – says; sēl – fish; koḷ – having; taṇ – cool; punal – water \[kāvēri\]; sūḻ – surrounded; tiruvarangattāy – Oh one who is residing in kōyil (śrīrangam)!; ennum – says; en – for me to immerse; tīrttanē – Oh one who is like a ghat!; ennum – says; kōlam – beautiful; mā – expansive; maḻai – cool; kaṇ – eye; pani – tears; malga – to be filled; irukkum – remains inactive

**Перевод:**

**My tender natured daughter who is like a slender creeper says “You created sorrows for those who are not surrendered and joy for the surrendered ones in every place; you stand as the refuge for those who don’t have refuge even for those who did not have attachment like jayanta, to surrender; you are the controller of the wheel of time; you are mercifully resting in the divine milk ocean, like an ocean reclining on another ocean; oh one who appeared as kriṣṇa for the protection \[of devotees\]! Oh one who is residing in kōyil (śrīrangam) which is surrounded by cool water \[kāvēri\] having fish in it! Oh one who is like a ghat for me to immerse into!” She then remains inactive with tears filled in her beautiful, expansive eyes.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the seventh pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki’s mother says “My daughter is saying – you consider the nature of entities and give them joy and sorrow as much as they can handle; how can you torment me?” Alternative explanation – “Has your nature changed from protecting the followers and tormenting the unfavourable ones?”*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, parānguśa nāyaki’s mother says “My daughter is in anguish speaking about emperumān’s qualities, such as reclining on the ocean for the protection of his devotees”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction – those were piḷḷān’s opinions. parānguśa nāyaki’s mother is thinking “Due to her relationship with me, this tender shoot like girl, has to go through this type of suffering in the presence of emperumān who has the qualities to protect those helpless people who surrender unto him”. pāla tunbangaḷ inbangaḷ padaittāy! paṟṟilār paṟṟa ninṟānē! kāla cakkarattāy! kadal idam koṇḍa kadalvaṇṇā! kaṇṇanē! ennum sēl koḷ taṇ punal sūḻ tiruvarangattāy! ennum en tīrttanē! ennum kōla mā maḻaik kaṇ pani malga irukkum ennudaik kōmaḷak koḻundē*

- *pāla* … – Oh one who created joy and sorrow appropriate to the place! pāl – place; as “*appāl*“, “*ippāl*” means that place, this place respectively. pāla – at every place. If you give the suffering of all those who are in separation from you, to my daughter, can she tolerate that? Alternative explanation – Have you not made arrangements for protection of the surrendered ones and the suffering of those who have not surrendered? pāl – method. Are you not of the nature as mentioned in [tiruvāimoḻi 2.6.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/04/thiruvaimozhi-2-6-1-vaikundha-manivannane/) “*seygundā arum tīmai un adiyārkkut tīrttu asurarkkut tīmaigaḷ seygundā*” (oh one who has the weapon named kunda, who does not hesitate bestowing results on your devotees by elminating cruel sins and transferring them to those who are demoniac causing them disaster!). Is the previously established methods not applicable for her? pāl means part, nature, place and method. When that which cannot be tolerated by himself was pursued by emperumān himself, can we do anything about it?

Considering emperumān is saying “There is no fault in me, you should also have something in you to attain the result”,

- *paṟṟilār paṟṟa ninṟānē* – Have you not descended here and mercifully reclined to be the refuge for those who have nothing in them? Is this reclining posture for nityasūris? \[No\] Are you not the refuge for persons like jayanta (indra’s son) who disowned you! āren’t you explained as the refuge in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 38.34 “*tamēva śaraṇam gata:*” (He surrendered to śrīrāma only)?

emperumān says “Alright! But there is a time for that”,

- *kāla cakkarattāy* – īsn’t the wheel of time under your disposal? Did you not turn day into night for your devotee?

Alternative explanation – emperumān is saying “But there are hurdles”,

- *kāla cakkarattāy* – You are having the divine chakra to eliminate such enemies.

Even if you have the weapon, you cannot say “I live too far away from you”!

- *kadal idam koṇḍa kadal vaṇṇā* – You have arrived closer to us and are reclining in milk ocean to protect us. Did you not beautifully lie down on the milk ocean, like one ocean lying on top of another?

emperumān asks “So, can you not come there?”

- *kaṇṇanē* – Did you not come and help as kriṣṇa to those covherd men and women who could not hear \[reach\] your presence there?
- *kaṇṇanē ennum* – Did you not leave that reclining posture and accept this abode as said in hari vamsam 113.62 “*nāgaparyankamutsrujya hyāgatō maturāmpurīm*” (he descends from the serpent bed to the town of maturā)?

emperumān says “but you have missed it”, she says “did you not arrive in kōyil (śrīrangam) and mercifully recline here to make that kriṣṇāvatāram look like paratvam (form in paramapadam)?”

- *sēl koḷ …* – īsn’t said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 53.31 “*muhūrtam api jeevāva: jalān matsyā vivōdrutau”* (if we separate from you, we will die like a fish out of the water); only if the creatures which live in water can live on land, she can survive without you. Having taken up this town as your abode, does it fit your nature to not manifest yourself to her?
- *en tīrttanē ennum* – She is saying “oh one who made me fully exist for you even when you disregard me!”; (ōr she is talking about how emperumān’s purity which made it impossible for her to mingle with others;) also her saying “the ghat where I immerse into”.
- *kōlam …* – She stood in an attractive manner, with her eyes filled with tears which eliminate her stress. This beautiful form of hers is wasted like a moon shining in a forest! Instead of shedding tears like this, she could have engaged in some sādanam \[such as bhakti yōgam\] and could have lost it at the time of getting the result!
- *ennudaik kōmaḷak koḻundē* – Can my daughter who is too tender to unite with him, tolerate this separation from him? nanjīyar would mercifully say “Just as one would not see the eyes/face of the doctor when the muscle tightens \[as part of the treatment\], the mother is speaking to periya perumāḷ avoiding eye-contact”.
- *koḻundu* – When the creeper is looking for a support, it is being laid on the ground. śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 118.34 “*pati samyōga sulabham vaya:*” (my apt age to be married to a man). vangi purattu nambi explains the reason for lack of specific conclusion \[request to periya perumāḷ as in previous pāsurams\] is – the mother is feeling the anguish thinking “She has crossed the boundary of redemption, what can I tell him?”

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.2.8. Kolundu vanavargatku

*koḻundu vānavaragatku! ennum kunṟēndik kōnirai kāttavan! ennum aḻum toḻum āvi anala vevvuyirkkum anjana vaṇṇānē! ennum eḻundu mēl nōkki imaippilaḷ irukkum enganē nōkkugēn? ennum seḻum tadam punal sūḻ tiruvarangattāy! en seygēn en tirumagatkē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vānavargatku – for the nityasūris; koḻundu – being the head; ennum – says; kunṟu – hill; ēndi – effortlessly lifted; kōnirai – cows; kāttavan – Oh one who performed the super-human task and protected!; ennum – says; aḻum – remains with teary eyes like those who are immersed in devotion; toḻum – performs anjali like a surrendered person; āvi – the soul which cannot be burnt; anal – to be burnt; vev – hot; uyirkkum – breathes; anjana vaṇṇanē – Oh one who is having dark-coloured form which caused anguish!; ennum – says; mēl – up; eḻundu – rise; nōkki – see; imaippilaḷ – without blinking the eyes; irukkum – remains; enganē – how; nōkkugēn – will I see?; ennum – says; seḻu – beautiful; tadam – vast; punal – water; sūḻ – surrounded; tiruvarangattāy – Oh one who is residing in kōyil (śrīrangam)!; en – my; tirumagatku – daughter who is comparable to lakshmi; en – what; seygēn – shall I do?

**Перевод:**

**My daughter says “he is the head of nityasūris”; she says “Oh one who performed the super-human task to protect the cows by lifting the hill!” She remains with teary eyes like those who are immersed in devotion; she  performs anjali like a surrendered person; she breathes hot to burn the soul which cannot be burnt; she says “Oh one who is having dark-coloured form which caused anguish!” She rises up to see \[him\] and remains without blinking; she says “How will I see?” Oh one who is residing in kōyil (śrīrangam) which is surrounded by the beautiful, vast water body! What shall I do to my daughter who is comparable to lakshmi? Can I control her love which causes the suffering? ōr can I make you who are not arriving, to arrive? Implies that both are impossible.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the eighth pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki’s mother says “How will I remedy the sufferings which keep coming at my daughter?”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. koḻundu vānavaragatku! ennum kunṟēndik kōnirai kāttavan! ennum aḻum toḻum āvi anala vevvuyirkkum anjana vaṇṇānē! ennum eḻundu mēl nōkki imaippilaḷ irukkum enganē nōkkugēn? ennum seḻum tadam punal sūḻ tiruvarangattāy! en seygēn en tirumagatkē*

- *koḻundu vānavaragatku ennum* – She says “Oh one who is the head of nityasūris!”. Alternative explanation – She says “nityasūris are the root and he is the shoot” (i.e. sustaining himself by them).
- *kunṟēndi* – Do we have to search for his activities in other worlds? Did he not help the cows and the covherd men who are like cows? She says “Am I losing him due to his lack of supremacy or simplicity?”
- *aḻum* – Can you who lifted the hill to stop the rain, not stop this rain \[of tears\]? Can you not stop these tears, as explained as in [stōtra ratnam 49](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/02/sthothra-rathnam-49/) “*bahudā santata du:khavarśiṇi*” (pouring down sorrows continuously in many ways)?
- *aḻum* – she is doing what children would do; also, she is doing what friends would do.
- *toḻum* – she is doing what is done by those who have no other refuge; also, she is doing what is done by those who have knowledge in vēdānta.
- *āvi anala vevvuyirkkum* – As [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) did not arrive even after performing anjali, she thinks “my ultimate weapon also failed” and starts breathing heavily to burn the ātmā which cannot be burnt as said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 2.24](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/2-24/) “*adāhya*“; as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 117.6 “*dīrgam uṣṇam ca niśvasya*” (she breathed hot and heavy).
- *anjana vaṇṇanē ennum* – She is saying “You are not appearing with your cool form, just as water is poured on fire”. His form is as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 83.8 “*mēga śyāmam*” (having dark bluish complexion like cloud); did they \[residents of ayōdyā who came to see śrī rāma in the forest\] not say that after going through the anguish in hearing the words of kaikēyi, only by seeing śrī rāma’s form, will they be relieved from the stress?
- *eḻundu …* – Rising up on thinking about his divine form, and starts seeing the direction from which he may arrive. She remains without blinking the eyes seeing there thinking “I should see him from the time he enters”;
- *enganē nōkkugēn ennum* – As he did not arrive in the direction where she looked, she turns around thinking “he may come from behind and embrace me”.
- *eḻundu mēl nōkki* – On thinking about his divine form, she will rise even with the fatigue, and look up thinking “he will descend from the sky as he did for the elephant”; and will remain without blinking the eye thinking “I should see him from the time he enters”;
- *engagnē nōkkugēn ennum* – As he did not appear still, she asks “What means can I pursue to see you?”
- *seḻum tadam punal sūḻ tiruvarangattāy* – Oh one who is having this kōyil (śrīrangam) which is surrounded by beautiful, vast water body! Did you not arrive and recline in this invigorating abode looking for her? Have the roles reversed? \[i.e. instead of you looking for her, she is looking for you now\]
- *en seygēn* – Whatever she needs to do, she has done them. Now, what shall I do? Is your darśanam (arrival and vision) achievable through other means?
- *en tirumagatkē* – Can you lose her? ḍoesn’t she \[śrī mahālakśmi\] only have the greatness of exclusively desiring for you? īsn’t my daughter the only one who has the greatness of desiring for both of you together? She can be compared exactly with lakshmi.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.
