## 7.2.9. En tirumagal

*en tirumagaḷ sēr mārbanē! ennum ennudai āviyē! ennum nin tiruveyiṟṟāl idandu nī koṇḍa nilamagaḷ kēḷvanē! ennum anṟuruvēḻum taḻuvi nī koṇḍa āy magaḷ anbanē! ennum ten tiruvarangam kōyil koṇḍānē! teḷigilēn mudivu ivaḷ tanakkē*

**Пословный перевод:**

en – my lady lord; tirumagaḷ – lakshmi; sēr – being united, as her desirable place; mārbanē – Oh one who is having the divine chest!; ennum – says; ennudai – for me; āviyē – Oh one who remained in my heart as the sustaining life!; ennum – says; nin – your; tiru eyiṟṟāl – with the divine tusk; idandu – (submerging into the deluge, from the wall of the oval shaped universe) dug it out; nī – you; koṇḍa – kept as your beloved one; nila magaḷ – śrī bhūmip pirātti; kēḷvanē – matching consort!; ennum – says; anṟu – when the bulls were placed as a challenge; uru – the bulls which roared like the thunder causing fear; ēḻum – seven; taḻuvi – (effortlessly as done with the beloved ones) embraced; nī – you; koṇḍa – accepted like finding and keeping a treasure; āy magaḷ – nappinnaip pirātti who appeared in a matching clan for you; anbanē – Oh one who has fixed affection!; ennnum – says; then – well protected; tiruvarangam – śrīranga kśētram; kōyil – as the abode; koṇḍānē – Oh one who acknowledged!; ivaḷ tanakku – for her; mudivu – means to end her suffering; teḷigilēn – I am unaware

**Перевод:**

**My daughter says “Oh one who is having the divine chest which is the desirable abode of lakshmi, my lady lord, where she is united with you!” She says “Oh the matching consort of śrī bhūmip pirātti who you dug out with your divine tusk and accepted as your beloved one!” She says “Oh one who has fixed affection for nappinnaip pirātti who appeared in a matching clan for you and was accepted by you like finding and keeping a treasure, by embracing the seven bulls  which roared like thunder, causing fear when they were placed as a challenge!” Oh one who acknowledged the well protected śrīranga kśētram as your abode! I am unaware of the means to end her suffering.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the ninth pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki’s mother sees the state of her daughter and says “I am not seeing an end to her suffering”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently,  parānguśa nāyaki’s mother says “I cannot fulfil the desire of my daughter who is captivated by the overwhelming love of you who are the divine consort of lakśmī, bhūdēvi and nīḷā dēvi”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. en tirumagaḷ sēr mārbanē! ennum ennudai āviyē! ennum nin tiruveyiṟṟāl idandu nī koṇḍa nilamagaḷ kēḷvanē! ennum anṟuruvēḻum taḻuvi nī koṇḍa āy magaḷ anbanē! ennum then tiruvarangam kōyil koṇḍānē! teḷigilēn mudivu ivaḷ tanakkē*

- *en tirumagaḷ sēr mārbanē ennum* – She is asking “Am I losing my result due to lack of puruśakāram \[pirātti as the one who recommends to [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) for us\]?” Here, the “en” (my) is not meant for viśiśta (entity) but on viśēśaṇa (attribute); that is, it is meant for tirumagaḷ (pirātti) and not for mārban (one who holds her on his chest). [anantāḻvān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/ananthazhwan/) named his daughter “*en tirumagaḷ*“. bhattar prayed to perumāḷ “consider me in your divine heart as one who came along with pirātti as strī danam (a servant maid who is gifted along during marriage); I too will think about you as ‘he (emperumān) is dear to our nāycciyār’ and hence we should think that you are ‘*aḻagiya maṇavāḷap perumāḷ*‘ (the lord who is the most beautiful bride groom)”.
- *sēr mārbanē* – In the rahasyam \[secret [dvaya mahā mantram](http://ponnadi.blogspot.in/2015/12/rahasya-thrayam.html)\], this indicates the nitya yōgam \[“math” which indicates their eternal togetherness\]; only if she separates for a moment, is there a  reason for the delay in my result? It was mercifully said “[bhattar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/parasara-bhattar/) called [nanjīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nanjiyar/) to hear from him some pāsurams which he could recite in front of perumāḷ subsequently; he was eating when nanjīyar starts reciting this decad; while reciting this pāsuram, nanjīyar mercifully recited ‘*en tirumagaḷ sēr mārbanē ennum ennuadai āviyē ennum’* without any break in between; hearing that, bhattar stopped eating, cried out ‘śrīranganāta’ and mercifully lay down on the mattress” \[When recited together, it implies that [parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s life sustaining entity is śrīman nārāyaṇan, instead of seeing the two phrases independent of each other. bhattar becomes overwhelmed in emotions thinking about how nanjīyar presented the subtle truth in his recital\]. nanjīyar mercifully said “I became frightened seeing bhattar’s state, wondering if he attained the divine feet of [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)“.
- *ennudai āviyē ennum* – For āḻvār, the vital air is not the sustaining force but the divine couple. Oh one who remains my sustaining life, being the one who is having śrī mahālakśmi on your chest!
- *nin …* – īsn’t it natural for you to even transform your stature to fulfil the desire of your beloved one? Can you gain acceptance of śrī bhūmip pirātti, only by caring for her wealth? “*tiru*” in “*tiru eyiṟu*” indicates the beauty of your tusk.
- *idandu nī koṇḍa* – The one you dug out and accepted. Oh one who is dear to śrī bhūmip pirātti!
- *anṟu …* – Could you, who helped long ago, not help now? Here “*anṟu*” indicates the \[helpless and loving\] state of nappinnaip pirātti. Not one or two, but embracing all the seven bulls. Since it \[winning over them\] is the means to attain her, he feels embracing the bulls to be embracing her divine bosom. uru – thunder, implying that they roared like thunder. uru – pride, implying that they appeared to be embodiment of pride.
- *āy magaḷ anbanē ennum* – She is saying “How will you get the acceptance of my lady lords if you abandon me?”
- *then tiruvarangam kōyil koṇḍānē* – Oh one who is having the śrīranga kśētram which is the best in southern direction, as your abode! Is there the shortcoming of his not presenting himself during the incident of killing the seven bulls? Unlike \[vibhava\] avatārams, aren’t you residing eternally here to help those who are here after the period of incarnations? He accepted this abode of śrīrangam not have to say as in mahābhāratam “*gatas svam stānam uttamam*” (He reached his own ultimate abode).
- *teḷigilēn* … – When there is no shortcoming there \[i.e. eternally residing in śrīrangam\], there should be clarity that “the result will not be missed”, but I am unable to have that clarity. When you practically demonstrate the statement in [śrī bhagavat gītā 18.66](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/18-66/) “*mā śuca:*” (do not worry) by reclining here, should I not remain as said in śrī bhagavat gītā 18.73 “*stitō’smi gatasandēha:*” (being freed from doubts, I am standing firm, with realisation of truth)? But I am unable to do so.  I am unable to give a solution for her. Shall we be satisfied with the realisation, while her state is such?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.2.10. Mudivu ival

*mudivu ivaḷ tanakkonṟaṟigilēn ennum mūvulagāḷiyē! ennum kadikamaḻ konṟaic cadaiyanē! ennum nānmugak kadavuḷē! ennum vadivudai vānōr talaivanē! ennum vaṇ tiruvarangaē! ennum adi adaiyādāḷ pōl ivaḷ aṇugi adaindanaḷ mugil vaṇṇan adiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ivaḷ – my daughter (who is visibly anguished); tanakku – for her anguished state; mudivu – solution; onṟu – a; aṟigilēn – don’t know; ennum – says; mū ulagu āḷiyē – Oh one who ruled over the worlds by being the antarātmā of indra who is the lord of the three worlds \[bhū:, bhūva:, suva:\]!; ennum – says; kadi kamaḻ – fragrant; konṟai – having konṟai (Indian laburnum tree) garland; cadaiyanē – Oh one who remains the antarātmā of rudra who has matted hair, to be meditated upon by him!; ennum – says; nānmugan – (the master for these aforementioned dēvatās) the four-headed; kadavuḷē – Oh one who is the antarātmā of the dēvatā!; ennum – says; vadivu udai – having matching form; vānōr – for nityasūris; talaivanē – Oh one who is the lord!; ennum – says; vaṇ – having magnanimity (to present himself to those who desire); tiruvaranganē – Oh one who is the controller of kōyil (śrīrangam)!; ennum – says; adi – his divine feet; adiayādāḷ pōl – who appeared to be not reaching; ivaḷ – my daughter; mugil – like a dark cloud which pours the rain on land and water; vaṇṇan – due to the great generosity of the one who is having the form; adi – his divine feet; aṇugi – approached; adaindanaḷ – attained

**Перевод:**

**My daughter says “I don’t know a solution”; she says “Oh one who ruled over the worlds by being the antarātmā of indra who is the lord of the three worlds \[bhū:, bhūva:, suva:\]!” She says “Oh one who remains the antarātmā of rudra who has matted hair which is having fragrant konṟai garland, to be meditated upon by him!” She says “Oh one who is the antarātmā of the four-headed dēvatā!” She says “Oh one who is the lord of nityasūris who are having a matching form like yours!” She says “Oh one who is the controller of kōyil (śrīrangam) having magnanimity!” My daughter who appeared to be not reaching the divine feet of emperumān who is having the form like a dark cloud which pours the rain on land and water, approached and attained his divine feet due to his great generosity.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the tenth pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki’s mother says “My daughter who became distressed to appear that she may not unite with periya perumāḷ, reached his divine feet and united with him”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, as sarvēśvaran who is the antarātmā (in-dwelling super soul) of those \[dēvatās\] who consider themselves to be the lord, knowing her suffering/urge, out of his great simplicity etc, magnanimity and his physical beauty, grants her the external experience while in separation, and that leads to parānguśa nāyaki acquiring faith; seeing this her mother speaks in a satisfied manner.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. mudivu ivaḷ tanakkonṟaṟigilēn ennum mūvulagāḷiyē! ennum kadikamaḻ konṟaic cadaiyanē! ennum nānmugak kadavuḷē! ennum vadivudai vānōr talaivanē! ennum vaṇ tiruvarangaē! ennum adi adaiyādāḷ pōl ivaḷ aṇugi adaindanaḷ mugil vaṇṇan adiyē*

- *mudivu ivaḷ tanakku onṟu aṟigilēn ennum* – As the mother is repeating her daughter’s words she is saying “I don’t know the solution for my situation”. She is saying that she does not see the bottom of this ocean of sorrow; or she is saying that she does not know the means to finish herself to escape from this situation.
- *mū ulagu …* – tirumālai āṇḍān explains this as “*mūvulagāḷiyē! kadikamaḻ konṟaic cadaiyanē! nānmugak kadavuḷē! ennum vadivudai vānōrkkut talaivanē ennum!*” (Oh one who is the leader of the dēvatās who are in the form of indra, rudra and brahmā!) implying the principle of vaiyadikaraṇam (dealing with different entities – i.e. emperumān being the lord of different dēvatās). emperumānār (bhagavat śrī rāmānuja) mercifully heard this and mercifully explained it in the context of sāmānādikaraṇam (dealing with different entities which have a common base – i.e. emperumān being the antarātmā of all these dēvatās). “She is saying ‘Oh one who is the antaryāmi of indra, the controller of the three worlds and manages his abilities!  Oh one who is the antaryāmi of rudra, the one who is having konṟai garland in his matted hair and manages his abilities! Oh one who is the antaryāmi of the four-headed brahmā who is the leader of all these dēvatās and others in this material realm!”
- *vadivudai …* – She is saying “Oh one who is the lord of nityasūris who have the form which manifests bliss of enjoying bhagavān!” For [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/), there is no difference in saying that emperumān is the lord of nityasūris, or is \[the antaryāmi of\] indra, the leader of the three worlds, or rudra, the one who is having konṟai flower in his matted hair, or the four-headed brahmā; as he was bestowed unblemiśed knowledge and devotion by bhagavān himself, he does not just stop at the external form; he has fully realised that emperumān is the controller of all.
- *vaṇ tiruvaranganē ennum* – You descended and mercifully reclined here in śrīrangam so that not only the nityasūris get to enjoy you, but even the eternally bound souls will not miss out on you. She is saying “Should I not get the result of your reclining here?” vaṇ relates to emperumān’s magnanimity of presenting himself to those who desire for him.
- *adi adaiyādāḷ …* – Some explain this as “like someone who is surviving, but suddenly finishing”; but this is mercifully explained \[by emperumānār\] as “if she dies at this stage, this prabandam will not be completed, so it should be explained as – she appeared to be not attaining \[seeing\] divine feet, but ended up attaining them properly”. This is a type of [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s mānasa anubhavam (internal experience).
- *adi adaiyādāḷ pōl* – This is explained as “It appears that she would not reach his divine feet immediately; she will remain here for some more time; but she is becoming finished”. Alternative explanation – She who was anguished to be thought “would she ever unite with emperumān?” reached him and united with him. It is explained that she reached the divine feet of periya perumāḷ who appears like dark cloud.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.2.11. Mugil vannan

*mugil vaṇṇan adiyai adaiundaruḷ sūdi uyndavan moy punal porunal tugil vaṇṇat tūnirc cērppan vaṇ poḻil sūḻ vaṇ kurugūrc catakōpan mugil vaṇṇan adi mēl sonna sol mālai āyirattip pattum vallār mugil vaṇṇa vānattu imaiyavar sūḻa iruppar pērinba veḷḷattē*

**Пословный перевод:**

mugil vaṇṇan – periya perumāḷ who is having magnanimity as his nature, as a cloud, his; adiyē – divine feet only; adaindu – attained; aruḷ – his mercy; sūdi – beholding; uyndavan – one who got uplifted; moy – abundant; punal – having water; porunal – the divine tāmirabharaṇi river, its; tugil – rich cloth; vaṇṇam – like the complexion; tū – very pure; nīr – having water; sērppan – having as abode, at the banks of; vaṇ – with greatness of having honey, flowers etc; poḻil – by gardens; sūḻ – surrounded; vaṇ – with infinite opulence; kurugūr – the leader of āḻvārtirunagari; satakōpan – nammāḻvār; mugil – like a dark cloud; vaṇṇan – infinitely beautiful periya perumāḷ; adi mēl – on the divine feet; sonna – mercifully spoken; sol – having words; mālai – garlands; āyirattu – among the thousand pāsurams; ippattum – this decad; vallār – one who can practice with the true emotions; mugil – dark bluish like cloud; vaṇṇam – having complexion; vānattu – paramapadam; imaiyavar – nityasūris; sūḻa – to be surrounded; pēr inba veḷḷattē – in the infinite ocean of bliss; iruppar – will remain

**Перевод:**

**The divine tāmirabharaṇi river is filled with abundant, pure water which is having the complexion of a rich cloth; infinitely opulent āḻvārtirunagari is on the banks of this river and is surrounded by gardens which have the greatness of having honey, flowers etc; nammāḻvār, the leader of such āḻvārtirunagari, got uplifted by attaining the divine feet of periya perumāḷ who has the qualities of generous cloud; he mercifully spoke this decad in the thousand pāsurams as garlands of words, on the divine feet of infinitely beautiful, cloud-like periya perumāḷ; one who can practice this decad with the true emotions will remain in the infinite ocean of bliss in the paramapadam which is dark-bluish coloured, to be surrounded by the nityasūris.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the end, āḻvār says “Those who practice this decad will not be tormented like me and will reach paramapadam \[spiritual realm\] where they will remain with infinite bliss, surrounded by nityasūris”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. mugil vaṇṇan adiyai adaiundaruḷ sūdi uyndavan moy punal porunal tugil vaṇṇat tūnirc cērppan vaṇ poḻil sūḻ vaṇ kurugūrc catakōpan mugil vaṇṇan adi mēl sonna sol mālai āyirattip pattum vallār mugil vaṇṇa vānattu imaiyavar sūḻa iruppar pērinba veḷḷattē*

- *mugil vaṇṇan …* –  āḻvār who reached the divine feet of periya perumāḷ and attained uplifting with his mercy. As āḻvār had even lost his existence in the previous state, here the word “*uyndavan*” (attained uplifting) is used. *moy* indicates abundance and strength. Here, the strength acquired by the flow of water is considered. One who owns the abode on the banks of tāmirabharaṇi which is having water with strong currents and purity of a rich cloth. sērppan – tuṟaivan (owner); the chieftain of *neydal* (area near water body) land. While saying water with strong currents, it is also said as tū nīr (pure water), since the water remains clear even with the strong currents in it. The chief of the magnanimous āḻvārtirunagari which is having beautiful gardens as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam bāla kāṇḍam 2.5 “*ramaṇīyam prasannāmbu san manuśya manōyatā*” (Look at this pure, clear water which resembles the heart of great people).
- *mugil* … – Those who can practice with true emotions, this decad which is among thousand pāsurams in the form of garlands made of words, on periya perumāḷ who appears infinitely beautiful like a dark cloud. nampiḷḷai mercifully said “All the thousand pāsurams in tiruvāimoḻi were submitted at the divine feet of periya perumāḷ. And then, it was distributed to other divya dēśams as said in ‘tirumōgūrkkīnda pattu’ (decad submitted to tirumōgūr), ‘*tiruvēngadattukkivai pattu*‘ (this decad submitted to tiruvēngadam) and so on; this is similar to bhōgam (food to be offered) first placed for periya perumāḷ and subsequently allocated to emperumāns of other divya dēśams”.
- *mugil vaṇṇa vānattu* – Explaining that due to the shade of the emperumān (who has dark complexion) who is present there, the \[spiritual\] sky is also dark in colour; alternatively, it is explained as the sky of of mugil vaṇṇan (emperumān who has dark complexion).
- *imaiyavar …* – To compensate for the suffering of \[those who also became anguished\] seeing the mother cry out while the daughter remained unconscious, they will be made to be present with joy and without any responsibility \[other than eternal service\] amidst the group of nityasūris and enjoy there.

In the next article we will enjoy the next decad.

## 7.3 Vellaic curiu sangu

## 7.3.1. Vellaic curiu sangu

*veḷḷaic curi sangodāḻi ēndi tāmaraik kaṇṇan en nenjinūdē puḷḷaik kadāginṟa āṟṟaik kāṇīr en soillic collugēn annaimīrgāḷ! veḷḷac cugamavan vīṟṟirunda vēda oliyum viḻā oliyum piḷḷaik kuḻā viḷaiyāttoliyum aṟāt tiruppēreyil sērvan nānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

annaimīrgāḷ – Oh those who try to keep me away from him thinking “we are your mothers \[so we know what is good for you\]” (without realising my internal emotions which are beyond the expression of words)!; veḷḷai – having white colour; curi – having curliness; sangodu – with śrī pāncajanya; āḻi – divine chakra; ēndi – holding; tāmaraik kaṇṇan – one who is having lotus eyes (which made me fully exist for him); en – my; nenjin – heart; ūdē – inside; puḷḷai – periya tiruvadi (garudāḻvār); kadāginṟa – riding (to his desire); āṟṟai – way; kāṇīr – you don’t know!; en solli – through which words; sollugēn – Will I be able to explain?; veḷḷac cugam – having the flood of bliss due to experiencing him; avan – one who shines in my heart; vīṟu – manifesting his greatness; irunda – the divine abode where he is; vēda oliyum – the loud chants of vēdam by those who enjoy such beautiful sitting posture of emperumān; viḻā – due to the ever occurring utsavams (festivals); oliyum – sound of the musical instruments etc; piḷḷaik kuḻā – group of children; viḷaiyādu – play; oliyum – loud noise; aṟā – are heard continuously without a break; tiruppēraiyil – in tiruppēreyil; nān – I; sērvan – will reach

**Перевод:**

**Oh those who try to keep me away from him thinking “we are your mothers!” emperumān who is having lotus eyes and holding the white, curly śrī pāncajanya and the divine chakra, is inside my heart riding periya tiruvadi and you don’t know how he does that! Will I be able explain it through words? emperumān who is shining in my heart which is having the flood of bliss as a result of experiencing him, is manifesting his greatness in the divine abode, tiruppēreyil; the loud chants of vēdam by those who enjoy such beautiful sitting posture of emperumān, the sound of the musical instruments etc due to the ever occurring utsavams and the loud noise of the playing of the group of children, are heard continuously without a break; when will I reach there?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the first pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki is informing that she desires to go to tentiruppērai due to the suffering she is going through, which is beyond words, to her mother who is enquiring about her state.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently,  parānguśa nāyaki is telling her determination to go to tentiruppērai where emperumān resides, due to his manifesting his form with the enjoyable weapons, limbs and periya tiruvadi (garudāḻvān) in her heart.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. veḷḷaic curi sangodāḻi ēndi tāmaraik kaṇṇan en nenjinūdē puḷḷaik kadāginṟa āṟṟaik kāṇīr en soillic collugēn annaimīrgāḷ! veḷḷac cugamavan vīṟṟirunda vēda oliyum viḻā oliyum piḷḷaik kuḻā viḷaiyāttoliyum aṟāt tiruppēreyil sērvan nānē*

- *veḷḷaic curi sangodu āḻi ēndi* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) constantly engages in the beauty of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s divine hand and chakra combination as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 6.5.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/02/thiruvaimozhi-6-5-1-thuvalil-ma-mani-madam/) “*tavaḷa oṇ sangu cakkaram*” (white coloured radiant conch and chakra),  [tiruvāimoḻi 6.9.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/05/thiruvaimozhi-6-9-1-niray-nilanay/) “*kūrār āḻi veṇ sangu*” (sharp chakra and white conch), [tiruvāimoḻi 7.2.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/07/thiruvaimozhi-7-2-1-kangulum-pagalum/) “*sangu cakkarangaḷ enṟu kai kūppum*” (she performs anjali saying “Sanka, chakra”). He is known as mugilvaṇṇan (one who has complexion of cloud); holding the conch which is curly and white, contrasting with the complexion of his divine form, and the beautiful chakra which does not need any additional adjectives.
- *tāmaraik kaṇṇan* – She is reminiscing what is said in [tiruvāimoḻi 7.2.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/07/thiruvaimozhi-7-2-1-kangulum-pagalum/) “*tāmaraik kaṇ enṟē taḷarum*” (becomes tired by just saying “lotus eyes”). Just as his divine shining form is represented by his divine weapons, his glance highlights his internal qualities. Naturally, the compassion in the heart is revealed through the eyes. Just as the eyes appear to be enemies for the unfavourable ones, similar to the divine weapons, for the favourable ones, his divine weapons are seen as adding beauty to his divine form similar to the divine eyes. The favourable ones will enjoy the divine eyes along with the divine weapons and the divine weapons along with the divine eyes. The divine weapons are recited along with the divine eyes to indicate how [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) won over her; they will make one say as in jitantē stōtram 1 “*jitantē*” (victory!). The eyes are recited along with the weapons, to highlight his beauty. Here nanjīyar mercifully used to highlight the words of nilāttukkuṟi pagavar \[this can be seen in [tiruvāimoḻi 3.7.2](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/09/thiruvaimozhi-3-7-2-alum-paramanai/)\]. Just as the āḻvārs \[Sanka, chakra\] are ornaments to decorate the hands, the eyes are ornaments for the face. As said in [mūnṟām tiruvandādi 1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/02/munram-thiruvandhadhi-1/) “*tirukkaṇḍēn ponmēni kaṇḍēn tigaḻum arukkan aṇi nirṟamum kaṇḍēn serukkiḷarum ponnāḻi kaṇḍēn purisangam kaikkaṇḍēn ennāḻi vaṇṇan pāḷ inṟu*” (I had the fortune to worship śrī mahālakśmi, his beautiful divine form,the beautiful, resplendent radiance shining like a sun from his form, his beautiful divine disc which is bursting out in the battle field and his beautiful divine conch which is curling towards the right), the divine weapons too appear as decoration, along with his physical beauty. As āḻvārs (Sanka and chakra) have decorated his hands, they are known as ornaments.
- *en nenjin ūdē* – Since it is not in their\[mothers’\] heart, they will say “this is not acceptable”.
- *en nenjin ūdē puḷḷaik kadāginṟa* – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) bestowed [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) unblemiśed knowledge and devotion and made his heart to be said as in [tiruvāimoḻi 3.8.2](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/10/thiruvaimozhi-3-8-2-nenjame/) “*nenjamē nīḷ nagar*” (considering my heart as a big divine city); while there is sufficient space in paramapadam \[which is three times the size of material realm\], as he would climb the shoulders of tiruvadi (garudāḻvār) and ride along to sustain the dwellers of paramapadam, here emperumān is manifesting the same inside his heart.
- *nenjin ūdē* – They will say “Would whatever is present inside, be not seen outside as well?”. mahābhāratam “*nirguṇa: paramātmāsau dēham tē vyāpya tiśtati*” (The paramātmā is fully pervaded in your body). She will say “if he is not present in my heart, I too can be considered as non-existing”. [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is roaming around in parānguśa nāyaki’s divine heart with the āḻvārs (Sanka, chakra) as hamsa (swan), cakravāga (another bird) on a pond, the divine limbs as fully spread out, blossomed lotus, the divine form which is like the water and lotus leaves in that pond, periya tiruvadi (garudāḻvār) holding emperumān as mount mēru holding that pond. This is how emperumān engages with his dear devotees. nanjīyar was once travelling to kōyil (śrīrangam) and meets piḷḷān on the way; nanjīyar asks piḷḷān “Does īśvara only have svarūpa vyāpti (pervading everywhere with his subtle antaryāmi form) or does he also have vigraha vyāpti (present in the heart, with a visible antaryāmi form)? piḷḷān replied “[bhāśyakārar (emperumānār)](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/emperumanar/) primarily explained svarūpa vyāpti in his commentaries; yet, [embār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/embar/) (disciple of emperumānār) told me once ‘I have heard from emperumānār once that emperumān is present with a visible form in the heart of his devotees for their worship’ ” Just as it is said in taittirīya āraṇyaka “*guhāyām*” (one who resides in the cave of mind/heart), katōpaniśat “*gahvarēśtam purāṇam*” (the ancient person who resides in the mind/heart), periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 5.2.10 “*aravattamaḷiyinōdum aḻagiya pāṟkadalōdum aravindap pāvaiyum tānum agam padi vandu pugundu*” ([emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) entered my heart with his serpent bed, beautiful milky ocean and śrī mahālakśmi) and śrī rāmāyaṇam “*ēśām indīvara śyāmō hrudayē supratistita:*” (In whose hearts dark-coloured bhagavān is firmly present),  “*en nenjinūdē puḷḷaik kadāginṟa*” is also similar to these. In śubhāśraya prakaraṇams \[sections which explain meditation on the auspicious form of emperumān\], as said in muṇḍaka upaniśat 3.2.3 “*tasyaiśa ātmā vivruṇutē tanūmsvām*” (bhagavān shows his true form to those who are dear to him), his divine form as the target of meditation is explained; subsequently he presents his form only to them as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 1.13 “*ēśa sarvasva bhūtastu*” (This embrace of mine is equivalent to everything else). Let the others say whatever they like; but there is nothing greater than this path which is shown by our [āḻvārs](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/azhwars/); even those who \[sections of vēdāntam\] say “there is something inside/beyond the \[divine\] form”, are only speaking about the true nature of bhagavān; they are not negating the form.
- *puḷḷaik kadāginṟa* – garudāḻvār would eagerly wonder “Are we going to be roaming around inside [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s heart only?” [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) would tap him to speed him up saying “Yes! How did you know?” and garudāḻvār would continue his run inside; \[is garudāḻvār more eager to protect āḻvār than emperumān?\] as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 16.4 “*dīmata:*” (one who is conscious, his \[it is in context of lakśmaṇa being more protective of sītāp pirātti, than śrī rāma\]), garuda’s duty is to unite the devotees with emperumān.
- *kadāginṟa* – \[present tense\] not recollecting what happened in the past and not talking about future. Is there any specific instruction needed for what is happening now?
- *kāṇīr* – You are not seeing. Even what is happening at present, is not fulfilling the purpose due to your efforts to stop it. Are you not hearing the noise of garudāḻvār’s flying? It is unfortunate that I have to explain about what is well known.
- *kāṇīr* – Are you trying to stop me, even after having eyes and ears? You too see this using your internal vision! They said “We have not seen it; you who have seen it, explain it to us!”
- *en sollic collugēn* – I cannot explain it; what can I say and which words can I use? Just as it is beyond your vision, it is beyond my speech. It appears that the experience which filled his heart cannot be fitted in to his speech!
- *en sollic collugēn* – I am not speaking due to my weakness; due to his unlimited greatness, we cannot speak about him. I need not speak since you are not going to believe me anyway.
- *annaimīrgāḷ* – If you are like me \[like minded\], based on what is already known, we can do as said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 10.9](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/10-9/) “*bōdayanta: parasparam*” (discuss with each other) \[but you are much older than I\].
- *en sollic collugēn annaimīrgāḷ* – I cannot express my anguish through words; you are stopping me in your old ways due to lack of understanding my situation; do I need only those who constantly stop me?

They ask “If we don’t have the eyes to see and the ears to hear, what are you planning to do?” She says I am going to the town where those who advice and try to withdraw me from him are not present. This abode \[tentiruppēreyil\] is an abode which will not let one think about those \[parents, friends etc\] who separated as said in cāndōjña upaniśat 8.12.3 “*nōpajanam smaran idam śarīram*” ([ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) will not contemplate about the material body after reaching the spiritual realm).

- *veḷḷac cugam avan* – One who has a flood of bliss. One who retains the infinite bliss which originated during the union, even during separation. The bliss he gave during union remains even in separation.
- *veḷḷai* – When it is read as “*veḷḷai*“, it means faultless bliss \[pure bliss, without suffering\]. It should be recited as “*avan vīṟṟirunda – tentiruppēreyil*“. This is the opposite to what is said in her case in [tiruvāimoḻi 7.2.4](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/07/thiruvaimozhi-7-2-4-itta-kal/) “*itta kāl itta kaiyaḷāy irukkum*” (she remains with her leg and hand placed wherever they were). While she is suffering here, he is seated jofyfully manifesting his opulence there.
- *avan vīṟṟirunda* – Being seated victoriously after winning her over. If he remains forgetting the situation, should we also remain like that? If he remains complete and prideful there, should we who are with faults and are suffering, remain quiet? If he remains ignoring the rules, should we also not break the rules? If only we were united with someone whose separation is bearable, we can remain tolerant. Should we not break the rules, and even pursue madal \[an act of crying out in public complaining about the beloved person\]? īsn’t it said in periya tirumoḻi 9.3.9 “*namakkē nalam ādalin*” (if it is good for us)?
- *vēda oliyum* – Being heartless, he is hearing the ancient praises. That is, he is hearing about his previous successes. That is, the praises such as in jitantē stōtram 1 “*jitantē puṇḍarikākśa*” (Oh lotus-eyed lord! Victory for you).
- *viḻā oliyum* – It appears like celebration for winning her over.
- *aṟā* – Immediately after the tīrttavāri (concluding) day, they will perform tirumuḷaiccāṟṟu (commencement of the next utsavam). Just as akrūra performed aśvamēda yāgams continuously after acquiring the syamantka maṇi (a precious gemstone), for makaranedunguḻaik kādar, there are continuous utsavams; parānguśa nāyaki is a strī ratnam (gem among women). But the celebrations are not held where she is present \[instead they are in tentiruppēreyil\].
- *piḷḷaik kuḻā viḷaiyāttoliyum aṟā* – She is saying that she would leave the town where even aged \[matured\] persons are stopped \[from engaging in bhagavat viśayam\] and to the town where even young children \[who are not matured\] are engaged in bhagavat viśayam constantly, are present.  Even young children would be immersed in makaranedunguḻaikkādan’s beauty and would constantly utter about that as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 6.16 “*bālā api krīdamānā gruha dvārēśu sangaśa: \| rāmābhiśtava samyuktāścakrurēva mita: katā: \|\|*” (Children who are in playing-stage will assemble at the entrance and sing about the glories of śrī rāma).  uttara rāmāyaṇa ślōkam “*rāmō rāmō rāma iti*” (Saying rāma, repeatedly) is beautifully explained here by nampiḷḷai.
   - *rāmō rāmō rāma iti* –  Like some say “*sōṟu sōṟu sōṟu*” (food, repeatedly)
   - *prajā nām abhavan katā:* – this is the recital for everyone who has taken birth
   - *rāma bhūtam jagata bhūt* – The whole kingdom became rāmādvaitam (everyone was seeing śrī rāma everywhere). What is the reason for feeling the experience of nitya vibhūti (spiritual realm), here?,
   - *rāmō rājyam praśāsati* – The dwellers of ayōdyā are not enjoying the result of their karma; they are enjoying the mercy of śrī rāma. As said in samkśēpa rāmāyaṇam, “*nacāgnijam bayam kincit*” – fire never gets hotter than it is necessary to cook rice. “*nāpsu majjanti jantava:*” – the water which will drown objects, will make them float. Water \[ocean\] has already seen the prowess of śrī rāma. tiruccanda viruttam 31 “*vēlai vēva vil vaḷaitta*” (launched his bow to heat the water of the ocean).
- *tiruppēreyil sērvan nānē* – It is natural that the loser reaches the abode of the winner. As said in “*tāmaraik kaṇṇan en nenjinūdē*“, she will sing “*jitantē*” and fall there \[at his divine feet\].

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

adiyen saraty ramanuja dasan

## 7.3.2. Nanak karungulal

*nānak karunguḻal tōḻimīrgāḷ! annaiyargāḷ! ayaṟcēriyīrgāḷ! nān ittanai nenjam kākka māttēn en vasamanṟidu irāp pagal pōy tēn moytta pūm poḻil taṇ paṇai sūḻ tentiruppēreyil vīṟṟirunda vānap pirān maṇi vaṇṇan kaṇṇan sengani vāyin tiṟattaduvē*

**Пословный перевод:**

nānam – fragrant due to application of fragrant materials; karu – black; kuḻal – hair; tōḻimīrgāḷ – oh friends!; annaiyargāḷ – oh mothers (who control them and me)!; ayaṟ cēriyīrgāḷ – oh neighbours (who have arrived to enquire about the situation)!; nān – I (who am very attached to emperumān); tani – independent (and having more attachment than I); i – this; nenjam – heart; kākka māttēn – unable to stop (from leaving me); en – to me; vasam – obedient; anṟu – not; idu irāp pagal – night and day; pōy – leaving me; tēn – beetles; moytta – swarming; pūmpoḻil – having flower gardens; taṇ – cool; paṇai – water bodies; sūḻ – surrounded; then – fortified; tiruppēreyil – in tentiruppēreyil; vīṟṟu – manifesting his greatness; irunda – residing; vānam – resident of paramapadam; pirān – supreme; maṇi – like a radiant gemstone; vaṇṇan – one who is having form; kaṇṇan – kriṣṇa (who is obedient towards his devotees); sem – reddish; kani – like a fruit; vāyil – beautiful lips; tiṟattadu – became attached

**Перевод:**

**Oh friends who have black, fragrant hair due to application of fragrant materials! Oh mothers! Oh neighbours! I am unable to stop this independent heart of mine; it is not obedient to me; night and day, it is leaving me and is becoming attached to the reddish fruit like beautiful lips of kriṣṇa who is having a radiant gemstone like form, who is the resident of paramapadam with supremacy, and is now residing, manifesting his greatness, in the fortified tentiruppēreyil, which is surrounded by cool water bodies and is having flower gardens which are swarmed by beetles.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the second pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki‘s friends et al say “should you be anxious? should you not sustain yourself by holding your heart tight?” and she replies “my heart which became immersed in the divine lips of the emperumān who is mercifully residing in tentiruppēreyil, is not under my control”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently,  parānguśa nāyaki says to her friends, mothers and neighbours “I am unable to control my heart which became attached to emperumān who has infinite supremacy, simplicity etc”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Second pāsuram. In the previous pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki spoke to her mother directly; thinking “she cannot be stopped anymore”, the mothers, friends and the neighbours came together and started advicing her. She replies to them “I am unable to hear your advice since my heart is out of my control as it has become attached to emperumān who has infinite supremacy and simplicity, and hence cannot stop it; you see, my heart is consumed by the ocean \[of love\]” nānak karunguḻal tōḻimīrgāḷ! annaiyargāḷ! ayaṟcēriyīrgāḷ! nān ittanai nenjam kākka māttēn en vasamanṟidu irāp pagal pōy tēn moytta pūm poḻil taṇ paṇai sūḻ tentiruppēreyil vīṟṟirunda vānap pirān maṇi vaṇṇan kaṇṇan sengani vāyin tiṟattaduvē*

- *nānak karum kuḻal tōḻimīrgāḷ* – nānam – nice fragrance. She is highlighting it as a blame for them. As they are with the best fragrance, she is unable to bear it like a deer which will die if a hair falls off it \[in separation, she cannot just bear her own decorations, she cannot even bear others’ decorations\]. Would I not stay here itself, if you were not here \[decorating yourself like this\]? Their hair reminds her of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s dark hair. Should the friends not be in the same state like her as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam kiśkintā kāṇḍam 5.18 “*ēkam du:kham sukham ca nau*“ (sharing sorrow and joy)? While she is not even caring for her hair and will perish if she sees the fragrance, can her friends use fragrances? As he engages with her in union, whatever flowers etc they discard, are given fully by her to her friends only. Since it was his merciful gift, even if those flowers become dry, they will continue to keep them in their hair! That reminds her of him and tortures her. Alternative explanation – they do use fragrances too. That is, they decorate themselves since if they remain morose without decoration, that will cause more anxiety to her. They will work to uplift her mood even at the cost of ignoring their own suffering \[of decorating in such situations\]. While [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) who is indicated by “a” in praṇavam and [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) who is indicated by “ma” in praṇavam are both present since time immemorial, the ātmā was not uplifted. Now, the act of uniting them is that which uplifts him; in this manner, they need to convince her to uplift her. They will not bother about their own suffering, they remain “we should bring glory for the lord”; this is similar to iḷaiya perumāḷ (lakśmaṇa) who is more anguished than perumāḷ (śrī rāma) \[during separation from sītāp pirātti\], would sustain himself with care for the protection of perumāḷ. iḷaiya perumāḷ is said to be parama bhōgi \[great enjoyer, great serpent\]. śrī rāmāyaṇam kiśkindā kāṇḍam 1.60 “*saumitrē paśya pampāyā:*” (Oh lakśmaṇa! See this pampā river banks) – though he could see the enjoyability there, he turned away from the scenery to distract perumāḷ; \[so perumāḷ says\] brother! look at this.
- *nānak karum kuḻal* – A tamiḻ scholar said “since nānam is an adjective for kuḻal, this means hair which appears like nāvi (musk, civet scent)”. This also implies fragrance only.
- *tōḻimīrgāḷ* – Those who speak priyam (favourable sweet words) have gone to the group of those \[mothers\] who speak hitam (advice)!
- *tōḻimīrgāḷ! annaiyargāḷ! ayaṟcēriyīrgāḷ! –* The three stages are highlighted here – a) I know some secret and not even share it with the friends b) the friends and I know of it and the mothers don’t know about it and c) friends, mothers and I know but others don’t know; crossing all these stages, things have become so public that, she is calling for everyone. She need not tell anyone; this being the case, she is so anguished that even the enemies will pity her state. śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 21.18 “*mām samānaya du:khitām*” (unite me who is suffering, with śrī rāma) – sītāp pirātti tells rāvaṇa to unite her with śrī rāma. As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam “*tadākuru dayām mayi*” (show mercy to me), sundara kāṇḍam 39.10 “*vācā darmam avāpnuhi*”  (become righteous through your speech), she is speaking the words that should be spoken to tiruvadi (hanuman) et al, to the one who separated her from śrī rāma.
- *tōḻimīrgāḷ …* – \[Being my friends\] How you liked what I liked! How you looked out for my priyam and hitam! How you remain indifferent towards me!

The friends ask “What is our fault? As you crossed your limits, we too crossed our limits”, she says

- *nān ittani nenjam kākka māttēn* – Do you have any reason like I do, to cross your limits?
- *nān* – Did you lose your heart \[to any one\]? Implies her situation is not the same as theirs.
- *it tani nenjam* – Just as I have become distinguished from you, my heart has become distinguished from me.
- *tani nenjam* – Independent heart which does not obey me. Even the heart of sītāp pirātti who is said to be śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 39.40 “*tat tasya sadruśam bhavēt*” (it will be fitting if śrī rāma could come on his own and take me) is not a match for her heart.
- *kākka māttēn* – (I don’t have the ability to protect myself) She can only say as in periya tiruvandādi 1 “*munduṟṟa nenjē iyaṟṟuvāy emmodu nī kūdi*” (Oh heart which is rushing towards perumāḷ before me! wait, let us pray together), and cannot stop it. It left me without seeing anyone else as said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 5.18.22 “*kurava:kim kariśyanti dagdānām virahāgninā*” (what would the elders do to us. I am burnt by this fire of separation); it is not returning after hearing something from him; from “*māttēn*“, it appears that she tried to stop the heart, but it went without listening and she gave up. Just as samsāris (materialistic people) won’t withdraw themselves from worldly pleasures derived from śabda (sound) etc, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) will not withdraw himself from bhagavat viśayam.

Can someone say “māttēn” (I won’t stop)? Should the heart not be submissive to the self in all cases?, she says

- *en vasam anṟu idu* – What shall I do if it ends up separating the child from the mother? Only when śrī bharatāḻvān listens to kaikēyi’s words and rules the kingdom, she will listen to her mother’s words and withdraw herself. Am I am not your daughter now? My heart too is like me. Instead of being present for my sake, it made me follow it.

When asked “even if the heart is not obedient generally, should you not advice it when it is obedient?” She says

- *irāp pagal pōy* – I am not seeing any moment when I can advice it, in the available time; her attachment is unlike \[that of materialistic people\] where one is sometimes attached to bhagavat viśayam and other times to worldly pursuits. Only if it is here for a moment, we can advice it.
- *tēn moytta …* – Did it get captivated in a matter from which it can be withdrawn? Can we withdraw those who are captivated by the enjoyability of the town itself? tēn indicates beetle.
- *pūm poḻil …* – In tentiruppēreyil which has blossomed gardens and water bodies.
- *vīṟṟirunda* – Manifesting his seated posture of paramapadam, as it is, in here. Is this town like that paramapadam? This place is such that, one person’s clothes will be worn by many \[such inferior abode\]; this abode is the place from where both the paramapadam and samsāram are perfected.
- *vānap pirān* – This implies the faultless supremacy.
- *tentiruppēreyil vīṟṟirunda vānap pirān* – The benefactor who manifested the posture of śrīvaikuṇṭam in this abode.
- *maṇi vaṇṇan* – The beautiful form which will make us hold him tight, even if he lacks the supremacy.
- *kaṇṇan* – One who lets the residents of this samsāram to enjoy the form which is enjoyed by the residents of paramapadam.
- *vānap pirān …* – Is it possible to measure the supremacy, beauty or simplicity?
- *sem kani vāyin tiṟattaduvē* – Just as one will get caught in the swirl during floods, she got caught in his lips; vouldn’t one return only when the boundary of the desired matter is found? It got captivated in the reddish, fruit like lips; only when it returns to me, can I listen to your advice.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

adiyen saraty ramanuja dasan

## 7.3.3. Sengani vayin

*sengani vāyin tiṟattadāyum senjudar nīḷ mudi tāḻndadāyum sangodu cakkaram kaṇḍugandum tāmaraik kaṇgaḷukku aṟṟut tīrndum tingaḷum nāḷum viḻā aṟāda tentiruppēreyil vīṟṟirunda nangaḷ pirānukku en nenjam tōḻī! nāṇum niṟaiyum iḻandaduvē*

**Пословный перевод:**

sem – reddish; kani – enjoyable like a fruit; in – attractive due to the sweetness etc; vāy – divine lips; tiṟattadāyum – plunged into; sem – reddish; sudar – radiant; nīḷ – tall; mudi – in the divine crown; tāḻndadāyum – residing humbly matching the supremacy; sangodu cakkaram – the divine ornaments which confirm such supremacy; kaṇḍu ugandum – becoming joyful; tāmarai – like a greatly enjoyable lotus; kaṇgaḷukku – for the divine eyes; aṟṟu – without attachment to anything else; tīrndum – existing exclusively; en nenjam – my heart; tōḻī – Oh friend who helped our union previously!; tingaḷum – every month; nāḷum – every day; viḻā – festivals; aṟāda – happening continuously without a break; tentiruppēreyil – in tentiruppēreyil; vīṟṟu – highlighting his distinguished nature; irunda – one who is mercifully residing; nangaḷ – manifesting himself to people like us; pirānukku – benefactor who is easily approachable in this arcāvatāram (deity form); nāṇum – natural shyness; niṟaiyum – obedience; iḻandadu – lost

**Перевод:**

**Oh friend who helped our union previously! My heart is plunged into emperumān’s enjoyable, reddish fruit like lips; it is residing humbly under the reddish, radiant, tall, divine crown, matching its \[crown’s\] supremacy; it is becoming joyful seeing the divine ornaments which confirm such supremacy; it is existing exclusively for the greatly enjoyable lotus like divine eyes; it has lost its natural shyness and obedience to the benefactor who is easily approachable in this arcāvatāram, highlighting his distinguished nature, mercifully residing in tentiruppēreyil where festivals are happening continuously without a break, every day and month, manifesting himself to people like us.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the third pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki‘s friends ask “Is your act in line with our shyness and honour?” and she replies “after being captivated by his beauty, my heart lost all of those”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Third pāsuram. Everyone except one of her friends withdraw themselves saying “this is not possible for us”; that one friend said “this is not good for us; should you not control your heart and sustain yourself?”, parānguśa nāyaki replies “What can that heart do now? It has lost everything it had by being captivated by his beautiful limbs etc”. sengani vāyin tiṟattadāyum senjudar nīḷ mudi tāḻndadāyum sangodu cakkaram kaṇḍugandum tāmaraik kaṇgaḷukku aṟṟut tīrndum tingaḷum nāḷum viḻā aṟāda tentiruppēreyil vīṟṟirunda nangaḷ pirānukku en nenjam tōḻī! nāṇum niṟaiyum iḻandaduvē*

parānguśa nāyaki is saying “*sengani vāyin tiṟattadāyum, senjudar nīḷ mudit tāḻndadāyum, sangodu cakkaram kaṇḍugandum, tāmaraik kaṇgaḷukku aṟṟut tīrndum – nenju nāṇum niṟaiyum iḻandadu kāṇ!*“. A muni (sage) named śaubhari, with his special power, assumed fifty forms. The one with whom she united, could do a lot more than that. Just as emperumān could fully pervade every entity, her heart too could be captivated individually in his every limb. \[Alternative explanation\] The multifarious forms acquired during experience with bhagavān as said in cāndōjña upaniśat “*sa ēkadā bhavati tridā bhavati*” (he assumes one form, three forms and so on), is happening to the heart in separation.

- *sem kani vāyin tiṟattadāyum* –  Being captivated in the divine lips which are trying to say “Whether I am away from you in separation or present in your vicinity, am I not your belonging?” That too she is not even going into in-depth experience of the divine lips \[just seeing the lips from outside is captivating her\].
- *vāyin tiṟattadāyum* – Is this experience not as big as mahābhāratam?
- *sem sudar …* – When emperumān spoke about the separation and stood a few steps away from her, she saw the divine crown which is highlighting his supremacy, revealing that he is the lord of both nitya vibhūti and leelā vibhūti (spiritual and material realms), and fell flat on the ground and held his divine feet.
- *sangodu …* – She then saw the āḻvārs (Sanka and chakra) which are the tools for him to eliminate the enemies when in separation, and which are so beautiful not to take our eyes off them, and became joyful.
- *tāmaraik kaṇgaḷukkaṟṟut tīrndum* – If one escapes for his words “*tavāsmi*” (I am yours), he/she will be captivated by his eyes; she became totally existing for him for those eyes. While separating from her, he glanced at her in such a manner that she was uplifted, to not exist for anyone else. Just as emperumān assumed eight forms \[being the antaryāmi for dēvas, asuras, vāsuki (the serpent) and mantara (the mountain); kūrmam (tortoise), antarikśāvatāram (the form which appeared on top), upēndram and the form which held the mountain from falling off), \] while churning the ocean, her heart took several forms to experience emperumān’s different features. All his abilities can occur for her heart too.
- *tingaḷum nāḷum …* – While festivals are celebrated on a daily basis in the desirable abode, would the heart remain with us in suffering! \[the abode\] where monthly festivals and daily festivals never stop.
- *vīṟṟirunda nangaḷ pirānukku* – The benefactor who is manifesting such benevolent presence to us. paratvam (his presence in paramapadam) is for nityasūris and muktātmās; vyūham (his presence in kśīrābdi) is for for those who are comparable to muktātmās; vibhavam (his incarnations such as śrī rāma, kriṣṇa et al) is for the virtuous ones; but this arcāvatāram is for the samsāris who have committed sins.
- *en nenjam* – His favours, beauty etc are like diamond-melters \[which can melt my heart which is hard like diamond\]. \[Oh friend!\] You know the hard nature of my heart. Both the heart and he are perfectly aligned \[he is attached to the devotees, it is attached to him\].
- *nangaḷ pirānukku en nenjam* – as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 16.15 “*rāghavōrhativaidēhīm*” (śrī rāma who matches sītā).
- *tōḻī* – You can understand the hardness of my heart, and now you too are siding with him.
- *nāṇum niṟaiyum iḻandaduvē* – Is there anything which it has not lost? See what happened by his separation for a fraction of a moment! I lost myself; mothers and friends lost me; my heart lost its shyness and obedience.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.3.4. Ilanda em mamai

*iḻanda em māmai tiṟattup pōna en nenjinārum angē oḻindār uḻandiniyāraik koṇḍu en usāgō! ōdak kadal oli pōla engum eḻunda nal vēdattoli ninṟōngu tentiruppēreyil vīṟṟirunda muḻangu sangak kaiyan māyat tāḻndēn annaiyargāḷ ennai en munindē*

**Пословный перевод:**

iḻanda – previously lost; em – my; māmait tiṟattu – for the complexion; en – my; nenjinārum – heart; angē – in close proximity there; oḻindār – due to the connection with emperumān, he remained with him; ini – now; uḻandu – being anguished; ārai – those who are ignorant about my state; koṇḍu – with; en – what principles (which are beyond them); usāgō – will discuss?; ōdam – having rising waves; kadal oli pōla – like the sound of the ocean; engum – everywhere; eḻunda – rose; nal vēdattoli – the loud sounds of sāma vēdam recital; ninṟu – present (always); ōngu – rising; tentiruppērēyil – in tentiruppērēyil; vīṟṟirunda – one who is mercifully seated; muḻangu – blowing (along with the vēdam recital); sangam – śrī pāncajanya; kaiyan – who holds it in his divine hand; māyattu – in amazing activities which reveal his simplicity, beauty etc; āḻndēn – immersed; annaiyargāḷ – Oh mothers (who consider themselves having the experience and relationship to stop her)!; ennai – you (who is engaged in him, without any companion); munindu – being angry; en – what is the benefit?

**Перевод:**

**My heart which reached in close proximity there seeking my previously lost complexion, remained with him due to the connection with emperumān; now, being anguished, what principles will I discuss with those who are ignorant about my state? I am immersed in the amazing activities which reveal his simplicity, beauty etc of the one who is holding the blowing śrī pāncajanya in his divine hand and is mercifully seated in tentiruppērēyil where the loud, rising sounds of sāma vēdam recital which resemble the sound of the rising waves of the ocean everywhere, are present always; oh mothers! What is the benefit of your being angry?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fourth pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki‘s mothers angrily say “Should you not pass your time thinking about something in anguish?” and she replies “even my heart was stolen by him; how can I pass my time?”*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. iḻanda em māmai tiṟattup pōna en nenjinārum angē oḻindār uḻandiniyāraik koṇḍu en usāgō! ōdak kadal oli pōla engum eḻunda nal vēdattoli ninṟōngu tentiruppēreyil vīṟṟirunda muḻangu sangak kaiyan māyat tāḻndēn annaiyargāḷ ennai en munindē*

- *iḻanda emmāmait tiṟattup pōna* – Saying “*nāṇum niṟaiyum iḻanda*” (lost my shyness and obedience), implies the other aspects which were lost; while reiterating, she is highlighting the loss of her complexion explicitly. Her heart thought “While we should steal everything he has, how can he steal some of our aspects”, went to him saying “I will bring those back from him immediately”, only to remain there.
- *en nenjinārum angē oḻindār* – emperumān transformed the one who entered there to be like him. He who said “I will never separate from you” is now there without thinking about me.
- *nenjinār* –  My heart is remaining there with his disturbed clothes, becoming a close confidante to him.
- *nenjinār* – As in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 19.23 “*pravēkśyāmi ca vāhinīm*” (I will also enter the army), śrī vibhīśaṇāḻvān told that he will fight along with śrī rāma \[came from the opponent’s side only to become a confidante of emperumān, similarly, my heart said that it will fight for me, but ended up staying with him\].
- *iḻanda* … – My heart which went saying that it will bring back my complexion etc, ended up staying there. Just as one will eliminate the foundation of the enemy, emperumān gave my heart rewards and sāmyāpatti (equivalence to himself) too. As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 28.27 “*rājāhyēśa vibhīśaṇa:*” (īsn’t this vibhīśaṇa the king?), my heart got its reward. Why are śukha and śāraṇa who grew up eating the food provided by rāvaṇa, hailing śrī vibhīśaṇāḻvān as the king in front of rāvaṇa himself? \[In samskritam language\] while a letter may exist, if a dot were placed on top of it, the letter would not be counted for the total number of letters in a sentence/verse. Here, as śrī vibhīśaṇāḻvān was already crowned by śrī rāma, who is the emperor \[who crowns other kings\], rāvaṇa no longer is counted as a king. Still, why would they address śrī vibhīśaṇāḻvān as the king, knowing well the cruelty of rāvaṇa? They thought “would an image harm us?” \[as rāvaṇa became delinquent already\]. One would think “let us use this capable person to eliminate the enemy” and reward him.
- *en nenjinārum angē oḻindār* – One who went to bring back my complexion became like the one who stole my complexion. The heart which went there seeing my emptiness became like the one who left me seeing my completeness. Everyone who leaves her tells her while leaving that they are going to fulfil her purpose! emperumān left her saying “our love for each other should increase”; my heart left me seeing my emptiness, to save me. What is the point in hating them? As said in cāndōjña upaniśat 8.12.3 “*nōpajanam smaran idam śarīram*” ([ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) will not contemplate about the material body after reaching the spiritual realm), after entering the abode where there is no return from?
- *angē oḻindār* – They remained there saying “I will fill the gaps in an ocean”.
- *uḻandu …* – Did those who lost their hearts previously, become pained but sustained themselves by crying along with others? Could you also not spend your time in anguish with some?
- *uḻandu* – being anguished
- *ini* – after losing my heart. Now, being anguished, what could I discuss with whom, to pass my time? Even for the one who was held captive in lankā, there was a person (śrī vibhīśaṇāḻvān) and a family (his daughter, trijadā); I don’t even have that! śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 37.11 “*jyēśtā kanyānalā nāma vibhīśaṇa sutā*” (nalā, the eldest maiden daughter of vibhiśaṇa) – \[sītāp pirātti tells hanuman\] while she is here, she really belongs there \[to us\]! “*kapē”* – just as you are helpful at times, she too is helpful. To be precise, she is comparable to you!
- *āraik koṇḍu en usāgō* – Would I be able to pass my time with samsāris (materialistic people) who are dēhātmābhimānis (considering soul to be the same as body)? Would I be able to pass my time with brahmā, īśāna (rudra) et al who consider themselves to be the lords as said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 16.14](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/16-14/) “*īśvarōham*” (I am the lord)? Would I be able to pass my time with nityasūris who never think about anything other than bhagavat viśayam? Would I be able to pass my time with emperumān who even stole my clothes and left me? With whom can I pass my time?
- *en usāgō* – sītāp pirātti could at least say as in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 33.17 “*samā dvādaśa tatrāham*” (I enjoyed blissfully with śrī rama for twelve years). Is there anything like that for me? This is how insufficient her \[parānguśa nāyaki’s\] union \[with him\] is.
- *āraik koṇḍu* – Is there anyone who is as compatible as the heart?

When asked “So, what can be done?” She says,

- *ōdak kadal …* – Since the continuous celebrations which happen there \[in paramapadam\], are now happening here \[in tentiruppēreyil\], we should also go there. The one who is seated in tentiruppēeryil where the loud sound of vēdam recital resembles the sound of rising waves in an ocean, is spreading everywhere.
- *nal vēdam* – Everywhere, the sound of sāma vēdam which is hailed in [śrī bhagavat gītā 10.22](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/10-22/) “*vēdānām sāmavēdō’smi*” (I am sāma vēdam among the vēdams), is seen everywhere. Just as the muktātmās would sing sāmagānam seeing emperumān’s posture there.
- *muḻangu cakkarak kaiyan* – As the śrī pāncajanya hears the sound of vēdam recital there, it would release its sound.
- *māyattu āḻndēn* – I got captured deeply, not to return, in his smile, glance etc.
- *annaiyargāḷ ennai en munindē* – Would you be angry with me only due to being my mother and having the right to do so? Should there not be someone present to receive your wrath? You have to show anger only when the entity (I) would exist!
- *māyattāḻndēn – ennai en munindē* – There is benefit only if you show your anger on the one you controls! \[I have already become emperumān’s property – so you cannot show your anger on me\]

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.3.5. Munindu sagadam

*munindu sagadam udaittu māyap pēy mulai uṇḍu marudidai pōyk kaninda viḷavukkuk kanṟeṟinda kaṇṇa pirānukku en peṇmai tōṟṟēn munindini en seydīr annaimīrgāḷ? munni avan vandu vīṟṟirunda kaninda poḻil tiruppēreyiṟkē kālam peṟa ennaik kāttuminē*

**Пословный перевод:**

munindu – showing his anger due to the delay in getting mother’s milk; sagadam – the wheel; udaittu – kicked; māyam – came in the form of mother; pēy – demoniac woman; mulai uṇḍu – drank from the bosom; marudu idai – between the \[twin\] arjuna trees; pōy – (finding the route and) went; kaninda – ripened; viḷavukku – on the demon who stood as a wood apple fruit; kanṟu – the demon who came as a calf; eṟinda – threw; kaṇṇan – kriṣṇa; pirānukku – great benefactor; en – my; peṇmai – femininity; tōṟṟēn – lost; ini – now; annaimīrgāḷ – oh mothers!; munindu – controlling me; en – what; seydīr – did you accomplish; avan – him; munni – taking the initiative; vandu – arrived; vīṟṟirunda – mercifully seated; kaninda – well blossomed; poḻil – having garden; tiruppēreyiṟkē – to tiruppēreyil; ennai – me (who cannot wait to attain the goal); kālampeṟa – without any delay; kāttumin – take me there and show me

**Перевод:**

**I lost my femininity to kriṣṇa, the great benefactor who kicked the wheel showing his anger due to the delay in getting mother’s milk, drank from the bosom of the demoniac woman who came in the form of his mother, went between the \[twin\] arjuna trees and threw the demon who came as a calf on the demon who stood as a wood apple fruit. Now, oh mothers! what did you accomplish by controlling me? Take me to tiruppēreyil which is having well blossomed garden and where he is mercifully seated after arriving there on his own initiative, without any delay and show him to me.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fifth pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki‘s mother scolds her saying “This urging does not fit your femininity” and she says “I have lost it long back; instead of taking me there when there is no use, you leave me in tentriruppēreyil now”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. munindu sagadam udaittu māyap pēy mulai uṇḍu marudidai pōyk kaninda viḷavukkuk kanṟeṟinda kaṇṇa pirānukku en peṇmai tōṟṟēn munindini en seydīr annaimīrgāḷ? munni avan vandu vīṟṟirunda kaninda poḻil tiruppēreyiṟkē kālam peṟa ennaik kāttuminē*

- *munindu …* – Think about my thoughts \[and situation\]; Will I, who am already caught in his anger, escape your anger? Will I, who am caught in the anger which is both hitam (well being) and priyam (pleasing), escape the anger which is neither? \[[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s anger is both hitam and priyam since it is done with his divine will for the benefit of his devotees\]
- *munindu sagadam udaittu* – The wheel broke into pieces after being touched by the divine feet which was angrily stretched out due to the delay in mother yaśōdā’s arrival to feed him. It is said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 5.6.1 “*stanyārtī brarurōdaha*” (desiring for mother’s milk, he cried and lifted his feet).
- *māyap pēy mulai uṇḍu* – Finishing the evil demon who assumed the form of his mother to feed him as he showed his anger due to delay in getting mother’s milk.
- *marudu idai pōy* – As a baby is fed, it will start crawling. Unlike those demons who came from outside to kill him, the yamaḷārjuna trees stood right in their yard and planned to kill him – he broke them into pieces.
- *kaninda …* – Due to being possessed by demons, one stood as a wood apple, and another as a calf; he picked up one of them and threw at the other one to kill both of them.
- *kaṇṇa pirānukku en peṇmai tōṟṟēn* – He finished both the perishable ones \[acit – the various demoniac forms\] and the imperishable one \[my femininity\]. He finished them with his prowess and finished her with his gentle nature.
- *pirānukku* – She is writing herself off to him for the favour of escaping from the clutches of those demons and saving himself and presenting himself to her. He preserved himself who is the lord and made me to remain in the ultimate state of servitude. The actions he performed in this kriṣṇāvatāram are as vast as the many incarnations which are explained in [śrī bhagavat gītā 4.5](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/4-5/) “*bahunimē vyatītāni janmāni*” (I have gone through many births). His anger is a result of his motherly affection towards his followers.
- *kaṇṇa pirānukku en peṇmai tōṟṟēn* – He stole her femininity manifesting his masculinity \[of being the puruśōttama\] which is explained in [śrī bhagavat gītā 15.18](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/15-18/) “*atō’smi lōkē vēdē ca pratita: puruṣhōttama:*” ( I am reputedly known as puruśōttama in śruti and smruti) and in [śrī bhagavat gītā 15.19](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/15-19/) “*jānāti puruśōttamam*” (knows as the one who is greater than bound souls and liberated souls for many reasons)!
- *peṇmai tōṟṟēn* – I lost that which can never be won over!
- *munindu ini …* – Are you thinking that I can be withdrawn now? Should you not have tried to withdraw me before I became aware of his \[amazing\] activities?
- *en seydīr* – Neither you remained favourable for me nor could you withdraw me.
- *annaimīrgāḷ* – You who know may nature from my birth, are trying to withdraw me! You are angry at me due to not knowing the favours he has done to me.

The mothers said ” You think about him, if you cannot forget his favours. But you should also think about our favours of giving birth to you and raising you!” She replies

- *munni avan vandu vīṟṟirunda* – See, he came first to favour me \[even before you\].
- *munni* – being the first one; as said in jitantē stōtram 1 “… *pūrvaja*” (one who puts in the initial effort for the uplifting of [jīvātmās](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)); [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is seated in a distinguished manner to get me.
- *kaninda poḻil …* – the problem is only with those who take me there; everything which is present there is well-ripened. The garden where one need not fear for the presence of demons when seeing a well-ripened tree \[as in the case of kriṣṇāvatāram wood apple incident\].
- *kālampeṟa ennaik kāttuminē* – There is only one solution for me and our family. Please avoid takiing me there later; you should try to do it when I am alive. Instead of taking me there later like building a dam after the flood water drained, show me when I am alive.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.3.6. Kalampera ennai

*kālampeṟa ennaik kāttumingaḷ kādal kadalin migap peridāl neela mugil vaṇṇattemperumāniṟku munnē vanden kaikkum eydān jñālattavan vandu vīṟṟirunda nān maṟaiyāḷarum vēḷvi ōvā kōlac cenneṟkaḷ kavari vīsum kūdu punal tiruppēreyiṟkē*

**Пословный перевод:**

neela mugil – like a dark cloud; vaṇṇam – manifesting the beautiful form which is magnanimous by nature; em – one who enslaved me; perumān – lord; munnē – in front of me; vandu – arrived; niṟkum – stood as visualised \[by me\]; en – my; kaikkum – for hand; eydān – beyond my reach (like such cloud); kādal – love; kadalil – more than the ocean; miga – much; peridu – became larger; jñālattu – in the world; vandu – arriving (with that physical beauty); avan – he; vīṟṟu – manifesting his generosity; irunda – abode; nān maṟaiyāḷarum – distinguished persons who are experts in four vēdams; vēḷvi – in vaidika practices which are a form of worship of emperumān; ōvā – occurring continuously; kōlam – beautiful; senneṟkaḷ – paddy crops; kavari – like fan; vīsum – swaying; kūdu – matching that; punal – having abundance of water bodies; tiruppēreyiṟkē – to tiruppēreyil; ennai – me (who cannot tolerate any further delay); kālampeṟa – at once; kāttumingaḷ – take me and show me

**Перевод:**

**My lord who enslaved me by manifesting the dark cloud like beautiful form which is magnanimous by nature, arrived in front of me and stood as visualised \[by me\]; yet he was beyond the reach of my hand; my love became much larger than the ocean; take me at once to tiruppēreyil where he has arrived and is manifesting his generosity in this world, and where vaidika practices which are a form of worship of emperumān are occurring continuously  in the presence of distinguished persons who are experts in four vēdams, and which is having beautiful paddy crops which are swaying like fans and abundant water bodies.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the sixth pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki says “I am not at the stage where you can enquire ‘should we take her there or not’; my desire has crossed the limits; I cannot sustain myself here; take me to tentiruppēreyil at once”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. kālampeṟa ennaik kāttumingaḷ kādal kadalin migap peridāl neela mugil vaṇṇattemperumāniṟku munnē vanden kaikkum eydān jñālattavan vandu vīṟṟirunda nān maṟaiyāḷarum vēḷvi ōvā kōlac cenneṟkaḷ kavari vīsum kūdu punal tiruppēreyiṟkē*

- *kālampeṟa ennaik kāttumingaḷ* – Though this is not the solution for the family, there is no other solution for me. There is no fault in me any more.

When asked “Why do you want to go immediately?”, she says,

- *kādal kadalin migap peridāl* – Is my love bounded? You see the word which I used \[kadal – ocean\]. You are thinking “previously she said in [tiruvāimoḻi 5.3.4](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/06/thiruvaimozhi-5-3-4-uravar-kavvai/) ‘kadal puraiya’ (ocean like)”. But, this love did not occur to fulfil a particular purpose, it has occurred naturally in me \[so, there is no boundary, it keeps growing\].

They said “still, should you not restrain your love, listen to us and follow us?” She says,

- *neela mugil vaṇṇattu emperumān* – Should I follow you? ōr should I follow him? When he appears in front of me to accept me, how can I withdraw myself from him? When he engages me with his divine form, will I listen to your advice? He appeared in front of me with an invigorating form and increased my love. It is his form, which nurtures my love. As seen in [tiruvāimoḻi 5.3.4](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/06/thiruvaimozhi-5-3-4-uravar-kavvai/), my love grew to the size of an ocean due to his dark coloured form only.
- *niṟkum munnē vandu* – Had he not arrived near me, would I not have withdrawn myself listening to your advice?

They asked “Is he reachable for you?”, she says,

- *en kaikkum eydān* – Nice, it will be good if I get him. Not just he is not talking and embracing, he is not even reachable to my hand; they asked “what are you doing now?”, she says “instead of enjoying him through visualisation, I desired to go to the abode where I can physically enjoy him”.
- *jñālattavan vandu vīṟṟirunda* – Instead of having to travel far and seeing him, he is manifesting all the opulence of paramapadam here in tentiruppēreyil.
- *nānmaṟaiyāḷarum vēḷvi ōvā* – Even the experts in the principles of vēdam are engaged in vorśipping him perpetually. Those who are similar to me, will be engaged in kainkaryam (service) which fit them \[instead of doing the worship for other benefits, they will do it as kainkaryam\].
- *kōlac cennel …* – The abode is such that they need not put in any effort to get rain, food etc. They will get them consequentially; it is said in perumāḷ tirumoḻi 5.9. “*nīḷ selvam vēṇḍādān tannaiyē tān vēṇḍum*” (Like the wealth that will desire to reach the one who does not desire for the wealth and desiring for you only) and in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 5.1.4 “*angangē avai pōdarum*” (they will get food, clothes etc naturally). Beautiful paddy crop will sway like a fan for that abode.
- *kūdu punal tiuppēyiṟkē* – Having abundance of water due to the confluence of river water, ground water and rain water.
- *tiruppēreyiṟkē* – Please take me to the invigorating abode and leave me there to eliminate my fatigue. Just as the paddy crop is sustained by water there, she will be sustained by the sight of that abode.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.
