## 7.3.7. Pereyil sul

*pēreyil sūḻ kadal ten ilangai seṟṟa pirān vandu vīṟṟirunda pēreyiṟkē pukken nenjam nādip pērttu vara engum kāṇa māttēn ārai ini ingudaiyam tōḻī! en nenjam kūda vallārum illai ārai inik koṇḍu en sādikkinṟadu en nenjam kaṇḍaduvē kaṇḍēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

pēr – big; eyil – by the fort; sūḻ – being surrounded; kadal – having the ocean (as a moat surrounding the fort); then – well organized; ilangai – lankā; seṟṟa – one who destroyed; pirān – benefactor; vandu – arrived (to rest); vīṟu irunda – mercifully seated manifesting that valour; pēreyiṟkē – to tentiruppēreyil; pukku – went and reached; en – my; nenjam – heart; nādi – seeking him; pērttu – return; engum – anywhere; vara – to come; kāṇamāttēn – I am not seeing; ini – now; tōḻī – oh friend (who shares my grief)!; ingu – in this state; ārai – whom; udaiyam – are we having?; (pōna – went); en – my; nenjam – heart; kūva – to bring back; vallārum – capable ones; illai – not present; ini – now (after the heart is not helping, and you have given up); ārai – whom; koṇḍu – with; en – what benefit; sādikkinṟadu – can accomplish?; en – my; nenjam – heart; kaṇḍaduvē – whatever seen; kaṇḍēn – I have also seen

**Перевод:**

**I am not seeing my heart returning to come here, after it went and reached tentiruppēreyil seeking emperumān, the benefactor, where he has arrived and mercifully seated manifesting his valour with which he destroyed lankā which was surrounded by big fort and the ocean and was well organised; now, oh my friend! whom are having in this state, as company? there is no one capable who is present here to bring back my heart; now, what benefit can be accomplished with whom? I have also seen what my heart had seen \[i.e. going to tentriuppēreyil is the only way\].**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the seventh pāsuram, after perumāḷ (śrī rāma) bids farewell to iḷaiya perumāḷ (lakśmaṇa), as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam uttara kāṇḍam “lakśmaṇēna gatām gatim” (I will follow the path taken by lakśmaṇa), perumāḷ set out to follow lakśmaṇa. Similarly, parānguśa nāyaki too says to her friend “Just as my heart reached tentiruppēreyil to sustain itself, I too will reach there”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently,  parānguśa nāyaki says “I am not seeing my heart returning from the abode where the one who destroyed lankā which was the great hurdle for the result, resides; now, I will also go there”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. pēreyil sūḻ kadal then ilangai seṟṟa pirān vandu vīṟṟirunda pēreyiṟkē pukken nenjam nādip pērttu vara engum kāṇa māttēn ārai ini ingudaiyam tōḻī! en nenjam kūda vallārum illai ārai inik koṇḍu en sādikkinṟadu en nenjam kaṇḍaduvē kaṇḍēnē*

- *pēreyil …* – She is saying “as my state has crossed the limits of tolerance, this is what I am planning to do now”. pēr eyil – big fort.
- *sūḻ kadal* – The ocean is a protective layer surrounding the fort. The benefactor who trashed such town which frightened everyone.
- *vandu vīṟṟirunda* – To compensate the avoidance then, he has arrived in close proximity to embrace me. As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 117.36 “*vimala śaśānka nibhānanā*” (pure, moon like, cool) – even while perumāḷ (śrī rāma) was very angry and cannot be seen, sītāp pirātti remained with a pure moon like, coolness in her face. śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 118.17 “*dīpōnētrā dūrasyēva pratikūlāsimē drudam*” (śrī rāma says – certainly, you appear to be unfavourable for me as a lamp for the one with an eye-disease); āḷavandār mercifully explained this as “the defect is in the eyes and not in the lamp”.
- *seṟṟa pirān vandu vīṟṟirunda* – He has arrived here after becoming tired while eliminating the enemies; as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 30.40  “*bhartāram pariśasvajē*“ (embraced her husband), he should be cooled down.
- *pēreyiṟkē …* – I am not seeing my heart returning after entering tentiruppēreyil seeking him. Even tiruvadi (hanuman) who entered lankā where one can never return from, returned; but I am not seeing my heart returning from this nearby town! When the heart itself has not returned, we need not say explicitly that he will not come \[it is implied\]. Her eyes become dizzy due to looking out for the arrival of her heart for a long time.
- *māttēn* – I should not perish here itself without seeing him, instead of sustaining myself by seeing him.

Her friend asked “Should you not wait for your beloved lord until he comes, by singing sorrowful songs?”, she says,

- *ārai ini ingudaiyam tōḻī* – Who is here to accompany me, when my heart itself is lost?
- *tōḻī* – If you asked “Am I different from your heart?”, you are my friend \[you would fall for him before me\].

Her friend asked “Am I not here?”, she says,

- *en nenjam kūva vallārum illai* – You should be present to bring my heart back; you who created the attachment in my heart for him, should be the one who brings it back to me; but your state is such that you cannot be even take a step forward; and the others don’t have the urge to bring my heart back to me; so, who will bring my heart back?
- *ārai inik koṇḍu en sādikkinṟadu* – With whom shall I accomplish? What can be accomplished? When the heart and he arrive here, should I not be present? Here, the situation is very bad \[I have almost perished\].

When asked “So, what are you trying to do now?”, she says,

- *en nenjam kaṇḍaduvē kaṇḍēnē* – I am also trying to follow the path which was taken by my heart. As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam uttara kāṇḍam “*adyaivāham gamiśyāmi lakśmaṇēna gatām gatim*” (I am going to follow lakśmaṇa’s path immediately), I am seeking to follow the path taken by my heart.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.3.8. Kandaduve kondu

*kaṇḍaduvē koṇḍellārum kūdik kārk kadal vaṇṇanōdu en tiṟattuk koṇḍu alar tūṟṟittadu mudalāk koṇḍa en kādal uraikkiṟtōḻī maṇ tiṇi jñālamum ēḻ kadalum nīḷ visumbum kaḻiyap peridāl teṇṭhirai sūḻndu avan vīṟṟirunda tentiruppēreyil sērvan senṟē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kaṇḍaduvē – the external changes only; koṇḍu – with; ellārum – everyone (mothers and townspeople); kūdi – together; kār – dark; kadal – invigorating like ocean; vaṇṇanōdu – being with the one who is having the form; en tiṟattu – my weakness; koṇḍu – considering; alar – accusations; tūṟṟiṟṟadu – throwing; mudalā – as reason; koṇḍa – present; en – my; kādal – love; tōḻī – oh friend (who first caused)!; uraikkil – if I see (to explain it through words); maṇ – land; tiṇi – abundant; jñālam – earth; kadal ēḻum – seven oceans; visumbum – ether; kaḻiya – beyond them, having consumed them; peridu – remained huge; teḷ – clear; tirai – invigorating due to having waves; sūḻndavan – one nurtured the great love; vīṟṟirunda – residing; tentiruppēreyil – tentiruppēreyil; senṟu – go there (to pacify my suffering); sērvan – will reach there

**Перевод:**

**Oh friend! If I try to speak about the love in me which is present due to the accusations thrown at me by everyone seeing my external changes only and my weakness due to desiring to be with emperumān who is having invigorating ocean like form, it remains huge, beyond the earth which is abundant with land, seven oceans and ether, having consumed them all; I will go to tentiruppēreyil where one who nurtured my great love is residing, and which is invigorating due to having clear water and waves, and reach there.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the eighth pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki says “my desire to see him is not just greater than ocean, but it has become extreme; hence, if you don’t give your consensus, I will myself go and enter tentiruppēreyil which is having abundance of water and where he is mercifully seated manifesting his greatness”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. kaṇḍaduvē koṇḍellārum kūdik kārk kadal vaṇṇanōdu en tiṟattuk koṇḍu alar tūṟṟittadu mudalāk koṇḍa en kādal uraikkiṟtōḻī maṇ tiṇi jñālamum ēḻ kadalum nīḷ visumbum kaḻiyap peridāl teṇṭhirai sūḻndu avan vīṟṟirunda tentiruppēreyil sērvan senṟē*

- *kaṇḍaduvē koṇḍu* – she would recite his name, perform a praṇāmam (obeisance) as said in “*talayil vaṇangavumāngolō?*“; seeing that only, if they become so worried for just these external aspects, what would they feel if they come to know her internal emotions?
- *ellārum kūdi* – Those \[friends\] who care for her, those \[mothers\] who look for her well-being, and the others \[townspeople\] will all unite together. \[Why would the townspeople come along?\] For blaming someone, even those who don’t normally unite, will unite.
- *kārk kadal vaṇṇanōdu en tiṟattuk koṇḍu* – As she has paled, should she not have lost her complexion to him? Does his complexion not appear as if the ocean flooded and drained subsequently? Uniting my urge with him who is having an invigorating complexion.
- *alar tūṟṟittadu mudalāk koṇḍa en kādal uraikkil* – Would I not remain happy had they not spoken? They are throwing accusations at me to make me withdraw from him fearing their accusations.
- *alar tūṟṟiṟṟu* – They threw accusations at me.
- *adu mudal …* – Having that as the cause, my love expanded manifolds like a tree with hundreds of branches.
- *kādal uraikkil* – Even she can’t explain her love. Even if [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s qualities which are said in taittirīya upaniśat as “*yatō vācō nivartantē*” (The speech returned unable to understand and glorify emperumān), can be explained, her love cannot be explained through words. Her love will consume even emperumān who is the target of her love. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) himself, in tiruvāimoḻi 10.10.10, first explained emperumān’s bliss as “*sudar jñāna inbam*” (radiant knowledge and bliss) and then said “*adanil periya en avā*” (my love which is greater than that).
- *tōḻī* – You know the efforts which went in to have this love nurtured; now see the result of it.
- *maṇ tiṇi jñālam …* – We said “*kādal kadalil migap peridāl*” without analysing; so, how can we explain that? We can only say that it is larger than the largest aspects, but cannot explain it precisely. Earth which has abundance of land. The seven oceans which surround that and the ether which gives space for everything. Beyond all of these.

Her friend asked “If the love overflows like this, what are you going to do?” She says,

- *teḷ tirai …* – She will reach the place where the [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who will enjoy this love is present. She will go to tentiruppērai which is surrounded by clear waves, and reach there. We will go to the abode where there is scope for enjoyment as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 38.14 “*tasyōpavana śaṇḍēśu nānā puśpa sugandiśu \| vihrutya salilaklinnā tavāngē samupāviśam \|\|*” (sītāp pirātti says to śrī rāma – I will sweat on playing around the many gardens in the citrakūta hill which is filled with the fragrance of many flowers, and then rest on your lap).
- *sērvan senṟē* – Now, just the words are not sufficient, I will really go there. I will not send a messenger, and will not wait for his arrival.
- *senṟē sērvan* – Even if I meet him on the way, I will not return. My desire is not to be with him, but to reach the abode \[divyadēśam is given greater importance than the emperumān who resides there\].

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.3.9. Servan senru

*sērvan senṟu ennudait tōḻimīrgāḷ! annaiyargāḷ ennait tēṟṟa vēṇḍā nīrgaḷ uraikkinṟadu en idaṟku? nenjum niṟaivum enakku ingillai kār vaṇṇan kārk kadal jñālam uṇḍa kaṇṇa pirān vandu vīṟṟirunda ēr vaḷa oṇ kaḻanip paḻanat tentiruppēreyil mā nagarē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ennudai – while sharing my grief, setting out to advice me; tōḻimīrgāḷ – friends!; annaiyargāḷ – oh mothers (who always advice me)!; ennai – me; tēṟṟa vēṇḍā – need not console me; idaṟku – for this state; nīngaḷ – you; en – what words; uraikkinṟadu – can you speak?; nenjum – heart (which will remain pacified); niṟaivum – completeness; enakku – for me; ingu illai – not present; kār – dark; vaṇṇam – form; kārk kadal – consumed by deluge; jñālam – world; uṇḍa – his quality of protecting in danger, of consuming; pirān – who has the obedience of being the benefactor for his followers; kaṇṇan – kriṣṇa; vandu – arrived; vīṟṟirunda – having as residence; ēr – plough’s; vaḷam – having abundance; oṇ – beautiful; kaḻani – fields; paḻanam – having water bodies; tentiruppēreyil – tentiruppēreyil; mā nagar – big city; senṟu sērvan – will reach

**Перевод:**

**Oh friends who are setting out to advice me while sharing my grief! Oh mothers! You need not console me; what can you speak for this state? My heart and completeness are not present; kriṣṇa, who is having dark form and who has the quality of protecting the world from being consumed by deluge, by consuming it, arrived at tentiruppēreyil and having it as residence; I will reach this big city which is having abundance of ploughs, beautiful fields and water bodies.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the ninth pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki says “You cannot console me; I will go and enter tentiruppēreyil”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. sērvan senṟu ennudait tōḻimīrgāḷ! annaiyargāḷ ennait tēṟṟa vēṇḍā nīrgaḷ uraikkinṟadu en idaṟku? nenjum niṟaivum enakku ingillai kār vaṇṇan kārk kadal jñālam uṇḍa kaṇṇa pirān vandu vīṟṟirunda ēr vaḷa oṇ kaḻanip paḻanat tentiruppēreyil mā nagarē*

- *sērvan senṟu* – They say “though you are speaking in anguish, is this practically possible?” she says “I will certainly reach there”.
- *ennudait tōḻimīrgāḷ …* – Those who exist for me \[friends\] and those who think I exist for them \[mothers\] need not say anything. To be unable to console her, there is no difference between friends and mothers. Can ignorant persons instruct wise person and save them? Can those who consider my love towards him which is due to his nature, to be a means, advice me? She is forgetting herself and speaking with her focus on him; they are forgetting him, and focussing on themselves, trying to withdraw her.
- *nīrgaḷ uraikkinṟaden idaṟku* – Can those who are confused \[friends and mothers\], console the one who is clear \[parānguśa nāyaki, who is clear on her goal\]? What is your state? And what is my state? How can you who consider my leaving as a fault/blame, advice me who is determined to go to him?
- *idaṟku* – For my state.

They say “Still, is this how one who has a heart and obedience will speak? Should you not listen to advice and follow us?” She says,

- *nenjum niṟaivum enakku ingu illai* – If you want to say that, you go there and say that. My heart and obedience have reached him. niṟaivu – obedience. nenju – the container of that.
- *kār vaṇṇan …* – Is his form such that my heart and obedience will be under my disposal?
- *kār vaṇṇan* –  One who has a beautiful form which makes me disregard the words of mothers and friends.

When asked “Does he only have physical beauty?” She says,

- *kārk kadal jñālam uṇḍa* – The saviour for the suffering ones.

When asked “would he just protect during dire situations and leave subsequently?” She says,

- *kaṇṇā pirān* – The benefactor who places himself at the disposal of others.
- *vandu vīṟṟirunda* – Being present there manifesting all his opulence.
- *ēr …* – I will reach the great city of tentiruppēreyil which is having abundance of ploughs \[implying fertile lands\], beautiful fields and water bodies. I will neither withdraw myself seeing the hurdles you place nor will I remain on the way \[looking at the beauty\]. Don’t console me.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.3.10. Nagaramum nadum

*nagaramum nādum piṟavum tērvēn nāṇ enakkillai en tōḻimīrgāḷ! sigara maṇi nedu māda nīdu ten tiruppēreyil vīṟṟirunda makaranedunguḻaikādan māyan nūṟṟuvarai anṟu manga nūṟṟa nigaril mugil vaṇṇan nēmiyān en nenjam kavarndenai ūḻiyānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

enakku – for me; tōḻimīrgāḷ – in the name of friends, you are giving advice; sigaram – having peaks; maṇi – having abundance of gemstones; nedu – tall; mādam – having mansions; nīdu – present for long time; tentiruppēreyil – in tentiruppēreyil; vīṟṟirunda – mercifully seated; makaram – in the form of a fish; nedu – huge; kuḻai – having ornament; kādan – one who is having ears; māyan – just as the beauty with the ornaments, one who has amazing activities; nūṟṟuvarai – duryōdana et al, who are the enemies of his followers; anṟu – back then (during mahābhārada war); manga – to be finished; nūṟṟa – wove his magic; nigar il – matchless; mugil – like a dark cloud; vaṇṇan – having radiance in his form; nēmiyān – one who is having the divine chakra (which is protective towards followers); en nenjam – my heart; kavarndu – stole; enai ūḻiyān – one who did long ago; nagaramum – the town (where he resides); nādum – the region (which is along that town); piṟavum – other cities; tērvēn – will go and search; nāṇ – shyness (which is apt for women, i.e. thinking “why am I doing this in the presence of these people who are blaming me?”); enakku illai – I don’t have

**Перевод:**

**Oh friends who are starting to advice me! emperumān who is having ears which are wearing huge ornament in the form of a fish and who is mercifully seated in tentiruppēreyil which is present for a long time, having tall mansions with abundance of gemstones, and who has amazing activities just as the beauty with the ornaments, wove his magic and finished duryōdana et al, who are the enemies of his followers, back then; he is having dark cloud like matchless radiance in his form and the divine chakra; he stole my heart long ago; I will go and search for him in the town, the region and other cities; I don’t have shyness.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the tenth pāsuram, when parānguśa nāyaki‘s friends say “would everyone not accuse you?” she says “Am I not searching for them as well?”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently,  parānguśa nāyaki says “makaranedunguḻaikkādan, who is the eliminator of enemies of his followers, residing in tentiruppēreyil has stolen my heart long ago; I will myself go and search for the towns, countryside and regions where he resides; I have no shyness”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. nagaramum nādum piṟavum tērvēn nāṇ enakkillai en tōḻimīrgāḷ! sigara maṇi nedu māda nīdu then tiruppēreyil vīṟṟirunda makaranedunguḻaikādan māyan nūṟṟuvarai anṟu manga nūṟṟa nigaril mugil vaṇṇan nēmiyān en nenjam kavarndenai ūḻiyānē*

- *nagaramum nādum …* – Friends ask her “Looking at your determination, the rural people, urban people and all others are accusing you”, she replies “Do I really seek [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)? No. I only seek the accusations of the town, region and cities” \[It is their accusations which work like manure in providing nutrition to my love towards him – Refer to [tiruvāimoḻi 5.3.4](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/06/thiruvaimozhi-5-3-4-uravar-kavvai/) “*ūravar kavvai eru vittu*“\].
- *tērvēn* – She is saying that she is searching. As you are not uniting me with him, and as he is not arriving himself, it is these people who throw accusations of speaking about me and him being together and they only sustain me; even tiruvaḷḷuvar said in tirukkuṟaḷ “*alar eḻa āruyir niṟkum*” (I will survive as the accusations keep coming). piṟavum – all other places.
- *nāṇ enakku illai* – I am not having shyness just here; even after reaching there I won’t have shyness. That is, there is no shyness in [parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) from the beginning.
- *en tōḻi mīrgāḷ* – It is unfortunate that I have to explain this to you!
- *sigaram …* – Mercifully seated in the huge tentiruppēreyil which has tall mansions which are filled with gemstones and which appear as if peaks where brought and placed here.
- *makara nedum kuḻaik kādan* – One who is having ears which are decorated with makara shaped ornament. If some one becomes immersed in his limbs, can he/she be retrieved?
- *māyan* – She is thinking about the radiance in his form and internal qualities, which have not been explicitly stated here.
- *māyan* – His favouritism towards his followers.
- *nūṟṟuvarai anṟu manga nūṟṟa* – One who destroys without leaving anyone remaining when he thinks to do so. One who wove his magic to destroy duryōdana et al during the mahābhārata war.
- *nigaril mugil vaṇṇan* – His matchless physical beauty which appears like that of a dark cloud. With this – she is implying that his beauty is so hard to ignore that one cannot leave him even if it nurtures the enemies.
- *nēmiyān* – One who is having the instruments to turn day into night, while destroying the enemies. He lifted his chakra and even chased bhīśma et al.
- *nigaril mugil vaṇṇan* – While he remained like lightning and thunder for duryōdana et al, he was like soothing rain for pāṇḍavas to eliminate their suffering.

When asked “When he is not thinking to eliminate your enemies and unite with you, could you not weave your magic at him to make him fall at your feet?” she says,

- *en nenjam kavarndu enai ūḻiyānē* – How long can I survive after losing the instrument \[my heart\] to do that? How long has it been since he stole my heart showing his beautiful form and his being with weapons?
- *enai ūḻiyānē* – It has been many eons. How long has he been planning to steal my heart just as he planned to destroy duryōdana et al?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.3.11. Ulidoruli

*ūḻitōṟūḻi uruvum pērum seygaiyum vēṟavan vaiyam kākkum āḻi nīr vaṇṇanai accudanai aṇi kurugūrc catakōpan sonna kēḻil andādi ōr āyirattuḷ ivai tiruppēreyil mēya pattum āḻiyangaiyanaiyē ētta vallār avar adimait tiṟattāḻiyārē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ūḻi ūḻi tōṟu – every kalpa (a day of brahmā); pērum uruvum seygaiyum – activities relating to name and form; vēṟavan – being the origin; vaiyam – universe; kākkum – being the protector; āḻi nīr – greenish colour like that of the ocean water; vaṇṇanai – being the one who has distinguished form; accudanai – acyuta, who never abandons those who are to be protected; aṇi – as an ornament for the universe; kurugūr – controller of āḻvārtirunagari; satakōpan – nammāḻvār; sonna – mercifully spoke; kēḻ – match; il – not having; ōr andādi āyirattuḷ – the thousand distinguished pāsurams in the form of andādi (having connection between the ending of one pāsuram and the beginning of the next pāsuram); tiruppēreyil – tentiruppēreyil; mēya – for; ivai pattum – this decad; koṇḍu – having; āḻi am kaiyanai – sarvēśvara who has beautiful chakra in his hands; ētta – praise; vallār avar – experts; adimait tiṟattu – in activities related to servitude \[towards him\]; āḻiyārē – immersed in

**Перевод:**

**acyuta, who never abandons those who are to be protected, is the origin for all activities relating to name and form during every kalpa; he is the protector of the universe and has a distinguished form with greenish colour like that of the ocean water; nammāḻvār, the controller of āḻvārtirunagari, an ornament for the universe, mercifully spoke the matchless, distinguished thousand pāsurams in the form of andādi; among these, this decad is for tentiruppēreyil; those who are experts in praising sarvēśvara who has beautiful chakra in his hands, with this decad, will be immersed in activities related to servitude.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the end, āḻvār says “Those who learn this decad will be immersed in servitude”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. ūḻitōṟūḻi uruvum pērum seygaiyum vēṟavan vaiyam kākkum āḻi nīr vaṇṇanai accudanai aṇi kurugūrc catakōpan sonna kēḻil andādi ōr āyirattuḷ ivai tiruppēreyil mēya pattum āḻiyangaiyanaiyē ētta vallār avar adimait tiṟattāḻiyārē*

- *ūḻi* … – In every kalpa, for the protection of his followers, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) assumes variety of divine forms, divine names and activities.

What is the result of it?

- *vaiyam kākkum* – To protect the universe. \[It can be understood that the explanation for this point is in the previous point. i.e. protecting the universe means protecting his followers in the universe\]
- *ūḻitōṟu ūḻi …* – Unless he protects the universe like this, nobody will consider him as rakśaka (protector).
- *āḻi nīr vaṇṇanai* – Even if he does not protect and engages in torture, he is so beautiful that one cannot leave him. Here [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is talking about [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) having a distinguished form in paramapadam to be vorśipped by the residents of paramapadam constantly.
- *accudanai* – Indicating that his form is imperishable; also indicates that he does not abandon those who surrender unto him.
- *aṇi kurugūr* – [āḻvārtirunagari](http://azhwarthirunagari.koyil.org/) which is an ornament.
- *kēḻil andādi* – Matchless andādi \[anta + ādi – a type of poem where last word/letter of one pāsuram is connected with the first word/letter of the next pāsuram\]. This decad is matchless since it reveals [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s great faith in bhagavat viśayam where he could not be withdrawn by either self or others. Also explained as – with this decad which is meant for tiruppēreyil among the matchless thousand pāsurams.
- *āḻi am kaiyanai ētta vallār* – With all of these, it is explained how he became captivated by his beautiful hand and divine chakra combination. While all other beauty is one level, this beauty is on a different \[higher\] level. It can be seen and enjoyed on \[his\] hand \[visibly\].
- *avar adimait tiṟattu āḻiyārē* – Implies that they will have the nature of divine chakra while engaging in service \[will serve based on [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s will\]; also implies – they will become so immersed in servitude that no one can withdraw them from that.

In the next article we will enjoy the next decad.

## 7.4 Ali ela

## 7.4.1. Ali ela

*āḻi eḻac cangum villum eḻat tisai vāḻi eḻat taṇḍum vāḷum eḻa aṇḍam mōḻai eḻa mudi pādam eḻa appan ūḻi eḻa ulagam koṇḍavāṟē*

**Пословный перевод:**

āḻi – the divine chakra, who is the chief \[among the weapons\]; eḻa – appearing to rise to the front; sangum – śrī pāncajanya (conch); villum – śrī śārnga (bow); taṇḍum – the maze; vāḷum – the sword; eḻa – as they all appear; tisai – present in every direction; vāḻi – the tumultuous sound of mangaḷāśāsanam (wishing well by dēvas, manuśyas etc); eḻa – to rise; aṇḍam – breaking the top portion of the oval shaped universe; mōḻai – bubble; eḻa – to rise; mudi – the divine crown; pādam – the risen, divine feet; eḻa – to rise together; ūḻi – distinguished times; eḻa – to commence; appan – sarvēśvaran, who is the lord of all; ulagam – the world; koṇḍa – measured and accepted; āṟu – method; E – this is how \[amazing\] it was!

**Перевод:**

**The divine chakra appears to rise to the front, along with the conch, the bow, the maze and the sword; the tumultuous sound of mangaḷāśāsanam was raised by those who are present in every direction; the divine crown and the divine feet rose together to break the top portion of the oval shaped universe and the bubbles \[from the water\] rose; this is how amazing, the method by which sarvēśvaran, who is the lord of all measured and accepted the world, to commence the distinguished times!**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the first pāsuram, āḻvār meditates about emperumān‘s divine act of measuring the world and becomes blissful.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. āḻi eḻac cangum villum eḻat tisai vāḻi eḻat taṇḍum vāḷum eḻa aṇḍam mōḻai eḻa mudi pādam eḻa appan ūḻi eḻa ulagam koṇḍavāṟē*

As said in “*dēvās svāstānamāyānti nihatā daitya dānavā: \| nabhayam vidyatē kincit jitam bhagavatā jagat \|\|*” (dēvas are returning to their residences; asuras were killed; there is no fear left; bhagavān won over the universe) \[This is how jāmbavān celebrated [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s tirvikrama avatāram\], this is the act of emperumān redeeming the universe for himself. Unlike in the case of rāvaṇa where he was made an enemy and killed. as mahābali had a few good qualities, he was won over in a natural manner.

Would the servitors not help in bringing victory to the master?

- *āḻi eḻa* – Only sarvēśvara would have the total inclination to have the whole universe under his divine feet; though such desire is not found in his paraphernalia they set out to do that first. This is similar to iḷaiya perumāḷ (lakśmaṇa) decorating himself and getting ready to go to forest when perumāḷ (śrī rama) was only asked to go, as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 33.28 “*pūrva jasyānuyātrārtē drumacīrairalankruta:*” (the virtuous iḷaiya perumāḷ decorated himself with tree-bark clothes to follow śrī rāma).
- *āḻi eḻa* – Commencing with a kingly battle; he is known as hētirāja. tiruvāḻi (divine chakra) is the chief among the divine weapons. While the army remained still, sugrīva mahārjāja jumped at rāvaṇa, being unable to tolerate the situation, thinking “How can this lowly person stand in front of śrī rāma wearing a crown! It will imply that there are two kings”. śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 40.29 is explained here \[sugrīva went to attack rāvaṇa even before śrī rāma did\].
   - *ata harivara nāta:* – There were many valiant \[monkey\] warriors like him \[sugrīva\].
   - *prāpya sangrāma kīrttim* – He could not just fight along with those who were there. He wanted to have special glory for him in the battle field. He assumed the greatness of perumāḷ (śrī rāma) in the battle field, on himself.
   - *niśicara patim* – Even on the other side \[rāvaṇa’s side\], there were many great warriors. But he directly set out to fight rāvaṇa considering no one else in their side as equals.
   - *ājau* – Unlike them (the enemies) who attacked them (śrī rāma’s army) in illegal ways, he attacked rāvaṇa in an upfront manner.
   - *yōjayitvā śramēṇa* – Gave him the suffering which he had never tasted before.
   - *gaganamati viśālam lankayitvā* – He crossed the expansive sky effortlessly with his skills;
   - *arkasūnu:* – He returned without others realising about his return. He acted according to his heritage \[he is the son of sūrya\]. Sky is his natural habitat. One cannot know how the sun travels from one place to another.
   - *harivara gaṇa madyē* – He went and stood among the monkey warriors not desiring to distinguish himself from them.
   - *rāma pārśvam jagāma* – He stood near śrī rāma thinking “only those who have performed respectable feats in the battle field will stand in the front”.
- *āḻi eḻa* – As said “the little one of a bird which can fly at thousand feet, will practice flying at five hundred feet”, the divine chakra first rose. Will those who fear for his safety even where there is no danger, be fearless in this abode \[material realm\] where there is scope for danger? His greatness is such that they will fear for his safety even where there is no danger. Being paranoid \[about his own palace\], vidura checked the mattress in his own palace, when he saw how duryōdana et al tried mischievously to harm kriṣṇa; mahābhāratam udyōga parvam “*samspruśan āśanam śaurē: viduras sa mahāmati:*” (the wisest vidura checked the mattress \[which was placed by himself\] on which kriṣṇa was seated) – as an ocean will be agitated to its capacity \[i.e. vidura became fearful based on his love towards kriṣṇa\]. piḷḷai uṟangāvilli dāsar asked “Does ‘mahāmati:’ indicate losing one’s mind?” During namperumāḷ’s puṟappādu, piḷḷai uṟangāvilli dāsar would hold up his knife and worship him saying “if there is even a slight shaking for namperumāḷ, I will kill myself” \[indicating that perumāḷ should be carried very carefully\]; our elders, the śrīvaiṣṇavas, would call him as “mahāmati”. Real wisdom means losing one’s mind in matters relating to bhagavān.
- *āḻi eḻa* – Looking at [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s inclination to grow, tiruvāḻi (chakra) feared “he cannot rise alone” and started to rise.
- *sangum villum eḻa* – Just as the junior warriors will follow the senior warriors entering the war, other āḻvārs (weapons) too started rising from the other hand. Those who keep roaring where there is no prey \[i.e. no war in paramapadam\], will not abandon one another where there is prey \[opponents in samsāram\]. \[Alternative explanation\] Just as the relatives will come and surround someone who became rich, all the divine weapons started to rise along with sudarśana chakra. [iraṇḍām tiruvandādi 71](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/01/irandam-thiruvandhadhi-71/) is explained here.
   - “*idangai valampuri ninṟārppa*” (the conch in his left hand stood firm and blew vociferously), meditating upon emperumān’s beauty śrī pāncajanya blew vociferously.
   - *eri …* – Unlike having opportunity to make vociferous sound like śrī pāncajanya, spitting fire. The divine chakra which wanted to consume namuci \[son of mahābali who challenged [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) while measuring the universe\] et al.
   - *vidangālum …* – tiruvanantāḻvān (ādiśēśan) could only remain where he is and spit poisonous fire on the enemies.
   - *aravaṇai mēl tōnṟal* – The chief who has ādiśēśan as his mattress.
   - *tisai aḷappān pūvāradi nimirtta pōdu* – He measured the forests, plains and plateaus with his tender flower like feet. He measured the bhū (earth) with his pū (lotus like divine feet). If emperumān who fits in the tender mattress and is having such tender form set out to measure this rough world, would they \[his divine weapons\] not be agitated like this? They cannot remain silent, when he sets out to measure the world like this.
- *tisai vāḻi eḻa* – The divine weapons rise thinking “what danger is falling upon him?” Others were fearing for them and singing mangaḷāśāsanam (well wishes) thinking “what danger is falling upon them?” as said in [tiruppallāṇḍu 2](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/06/thiruppallandu-2-adiyomodum/) “*vadivār sōdi valattuṟaiyum cudarāḻiyum pallāṇḍu* *padaipōr pukku muḻangum appānjasanniyamum pallāṇḍē”* (Long live the radiant chakra which is on the right hand! Long live the conch which is blowing vociferously while entering the war!) As said in [tiruppāvai 22](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/01/thiruppavai-24-anru-ivvulagam/) “*nin kaiyil vēl pōṟṟi*” (Long live the spear in your hand), even the spear should be cared for. The “vāḻi vāḻi” wishes of the favourable ones are rising from all directions. As [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is reciting the rising of mangaḷāśāsanam amidst the rising of the divine weapons, it can be construed that he thinks such mangaḷāśāsanams are greater protection than the divine weapons for him.
- *tisai vāḻi eḻa* – He is as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 2.2.11](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/02/thiruvaimozhi-2-2-11-eththa-ezhulagum/) “*ētta ēḻ ulagum koṇḍa kōlak kūttan*” (The beautiful dancer who measured the worlds to be praised by everyone). śrī viṣṇu purāṇam 5.5.17 “*trivikrama: kramākrānta trailōkyas spuratāyuda:*” (the weapons rose when [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) set out to measure the worlds).
- *taṇḍum vāḷum eḻa* – The remaining ones too started rising thinking “If they follow the emperumān in the battle, only they will be glorified”; this is how every one of emperumān’s weapons thought “we are lagging behind; we are lost”; this is similar to many persons fighting for a single person’s food. Those who said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 17-29 “*vadyatām*” (let vibhīśaṇan be killed) when a favourable person entered, will not remain quiet where the enemies are present. namuci, son of mahābali, held emperumān’s divine feet and said “my father does not know your mischief. You should measure with the little feet you had before” as said in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 1.9.8 “*en idu māyam en appan aṟindilan munnaiya vaṇṇamē koṇḍaḷavāy*“. As this is an act of emperumān who was born on a particular day and grew up immediately, there is good reason for everyone to care for him. periya tiruvandādi 16 “*sīrāl piṟandu siṟappāl vaḷarādu pēr vāmanan …*” (not being cared while he was born and raised) – do you have to accept this world in this manner, while you have toyed with the world in many ways like how cotton seed goes through twelve types of evolution.
- *aṇḍam mōḻai eḻa* – He started to stretch his foot thinking to measure the three worlds (bhū:, bhuva:, svarga) for indra’s sake; but as his will was not just, he stretched his foot upto the top of the oval shaped universe. His divine foot reached upto the external shell of the universe and pierced through it as said in [tiruneduntāṇḍagam 5](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/06/thirunedunthandakam-5/) “*oṇ midiyil punal uruvi oru kāl niṟpa*“. The water surrounding the universe rises. The oval shaped universe is simply like a seed in the causal water. His anger at that time in measuring the world made everyone fear thinking “is his act of protection causing danger?”. mōḻai – bubble.
- *mudi pādam eḻa* – The divine feet \[foot\] rise upto the level of his divine crown. Also recited as “*mudi mēlē pādam eḻa*” (the foot going over the crown) to highlight his dancing posture.
- *appan ūḻi eḻa* – The bad times of mahābali’s inapt regime ends and the apt, good times commenced; to have the good times rise.
- *appan – ulagam koṇḍa āṟē* – Saying “How amazing is it that sarvēśvaran, the great benefactor, accepted the world!” Alternative explanation – asking “How did he accept the world?” Also said that [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is becoming blissful saying “appan” repeatedly.
- *appan* – āḻvār is saying “[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) made me exist by the act of presenting the kingdom to indra”.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.4.2. Aru malaikku

*āṟu malaikku edirndōdum oli ara vūṟusulāy malai tēykkum oli kadal māṟu suḻanṟu aḻaikkinṟa oli appan sāṟu pada amudam koṇḍa nānṟē*

**Пословный перевод:**

appan – sarvēśvara, the great benefactor; sāṟu – great festivity; pada – to occur; amudam – amruta (nectar); koṇḍa – obtained; nānṟu – day; āṟu – rivers; malaikku – towards the mountain (which is the origin for them); edirndu – in the opposite direction; ōdum – flowing; oli – sound; aravu – vāsuki, the serpent, its; ūṟu – body; sulāy – coiled; malai – on mantara (a celestial mountain); tēykkum – rubbing; oli – sound; kadal – ocean; māṟu – turning around; suḻanṟu – whirling; aḻaikkinṟa – calling; oli – sound (occurred)

**Перевод:**

**On that day when sarvēśvara, the great benefactor, caused great festivity for the dēvas and obtained the nectar, the following sounds occurred – a) the sound of rivers flowing in the opposite direction towards the mountain, b) the sound of the rubbing of the body of vāsuki, the serpent, which is coiled around the mantara mountain and c) the sound of the calling \[noise\] of the ocean turning around and whirling.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the second pāsuram, āḻvār is enjoying emperumān‘s act of churning the ocean.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. āṟu malaikku edirndōdum oli ara vūṟusulāy malai tēykkum oli kadal māṟu suḻanṟu aḻaikkinṟa oli appan sāṟu pada amudam koṇḍa nānṟē*

- *āṟu malaikku edirndu ōdum oli* – As the mountain *mantara* was anchored into the ocean, the ocean became agitated, the mountain went in deep and a pit was created; water, will naturally flow towards the lower regions. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is hearing the sound of the rivers flowing in the opposite direction, towards the mountain. [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) blessed [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) with divine knowledge so that āḻvār sees everything from past, present and future, in front of his eyes.
- *aravu ūṟu sulāy malai tēykkum oli* – ūṟu – body. sulāy – coiling. The sound which arises when the body of vāsuki was engaged in churning.
- *kadal māṟu suḻanṟu aḻaikkinṟa oli* – When *mantara* mountain was anchored and churned, the bottom of the ocean came up and the top of the ocean went down. This sound of the waves smashing at each other was like a battle between bulls.
- *appan* – benefactor.
- *sāṟu pada* – The nectar which came out of the ocean, to make the water as residue.  Alternative explanation – sāṟu means utsavam (festival). Saying “the bring in festivity in the dēvas camp”. Implying that the as nectar touched the water, and festivities occurred.
- *amudam koṇḍa āṟē* – All of these occurred during the churning \[of the ocean\] for nectar.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.4.3. Nanrila

*nānṟila ēḻ maṇṇum tānattavē pinnum nānṟila ēḻ malai tānattavē pinnum nānṟila ēḻ kadal tānattavē appan ūnṟi idandu eyiṟṟil koṇḍa nāḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

appan – the great benefactor (who transformed himself as a wild boar which does not shy away from \[muddy\] water); ūnṟi – pushed it into the shell of universe; idandu – dug it; eyiṟṟil – on the tusk; koṇḍa – kept; nāḷ – at that time; ēḻ – in the form of seven islands; maṇṇum – different regions of land; nānṟila – without slipping; tānatta – became established in their original locations; pinnum – further; ēḻ malai – the seven main mountains; nānṟila – without shaking; tānatta – became rooted in their original locations; pinnum – further; ēḻ kadal – the seven oceans; nānṟila – without breaching their shores; tānatta – became situated in their original locations

**Перевод:**

**At the time when earth was submerged in the deluge, emperumān, the great benefactor, pushed it into the shell of universe, dug it out and kept it on his tusk; the different regions of land in the form of seven islands became established in their original locations, without slipping; further, the seven main mountains, became rooted in their original locations, without shaking; further, the seven oceans, became situated in their original locations, without breaching their shores.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the third pāsuram, āḻvār is reminiscing the incarnation of mahāvarāha (great boar).*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. nānṟila ēḻ maṇṇum tānattavē pinnum nānṟila ēḻ malai tānattavē pinnum nānṟila ēḻ kadal tānattavē appan ūnṟi idandu eyiṟṟil koṇḍa nāḷē*

- *nānṟila ēḻ maṇṇum tānattavē* – Picking up the seven lands without shaking. While picking up mother earth, who has seven islands within her, he picks them up without shaking and places them in their original location. While performing great tasks, he does it without any deficiency as before, with everything continuing to happen as usual. As the one who is the support is present, they will not have any worries. The seven islands did not shake, and went back to their location.
- *pinnum* – Further.
- *nānṟila ēḻ malai tānattavē* – The seven main mountains which appear to be nailed on earth, went back to their original location. There was not even a small damage for the mountains. The reason for repeatedly saying “pinnum” with each situation, is to imply “emperumān could have just any one of those! But he did all of these”.
- *nānṟila ēḻ kadal tānattavē* – We could say due to their hard nature, the mountains remained in tact; but these \[oceans\] do not have that hardness; water is a fluid matter; he placed them in such a manner that even the oceans went back to their exact previous location. It is implied “The hardness in the mountain and the fluid nature of the water are irrelevant; whatever he wills, that is what will happen”.

When asked “Do they all remain in tact in this manner, when he protects them carefully?”, he says,

- *ūnṟi idandu eyiṟṟil koṇḍa nāḷē* – Piercing the earth with his tusk fully, taking it out of the wall of the universe and lifting it up, and while lifting it up with his tusk \[these entities were not disturbed even a little bit\]. When he sets out to protect them properly as said in periya tirumoḻi 3.4.3 “*maṇṇellām idandeduttu madangaḷ seydu*” (digging out the earth and lifting it up and performing wild acts), would they miss out \[on his protection\]? Both immovable objects and movable objects went back to their original positions.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.4.4. Nalum ela

*nāḷum eḻa nila nīrum eḻa viṇṇum kōḷum eḻa eri kālum eḻa malai tāḷum eḻac cudar tānum eḻa appan ūḷi eḻa ulagam uṇḍa ūṇē*

**Пословный перевод:**

nāḷum – the division between day and night; eḻa – to be subdued; nila nīrum – land and water; eḻa – to be subdued; viṇṇum – sky; kōḷum – planets; eḻa – to be subdued; eri kālum – fire and air; eḻa – to be subdued; malai – mountains; tāḷ – base; eḻavum – to be subdued; sudar tānum – radiant objects such as stars; eḻa – to be subdued; appan – the great benefactor who helps during deluge; ūḷi eḻa – as said in “he ate with great hunger” \[making sound will eating\]; ulagam – world; uṇḍa – consumed; E – how amazing it was!

**Перевод:**

**How amazing the way emperumān, the great benefactor, consumed the world as said in “he ate with great hunger” to subdue the division between day and night, land and water, sky and planets, mountain bases and shining objects such as stars!**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Fourth pāsuram. āḻvār is mercifully explaining the way emperumān protects during mahā praḷayam (total deluge). Some ācāryas mercifully explain that āḻvār is mercifully talking about the intermediary deluge as per purāṇam which says “mārkaṇḍēya witnessed everything which is seen outside, inside the divine stomach of emperumān”. nāḷum eḻa nila nīrum eḻa viṇṇum kōḷum eḻa eri kālum eḻa malai tāḷum eḻac cudar tānum eḻa appan ūḷi eḻa ulagam uṇḍa ūṇē*

- *nāḷum eḻa* – To subdue the division of time. As said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 1.2.25 “*nāhō narātri:*” (no day and no night). eḻa – pēra (to remove). Due to sun’s movement and stagnation, differences such as year, month, day, minute, second etc occur; when sun who divides the time gets consumed, these divisions will also follow him and cease to exist.
- *nila nīrum eḻa* – To have everything enter him, without distinction between cause and effect.  We have seen that both cause \[primordial matter\] and effect \[manifested matter in the form of great elements etc\] exist at the same time; while highlighting the \[mūla\] prakruti tatva (primordial matter) tiruvāimoḻi 10.7.10 “*māmāyai mangavottu”*  (relieve me from matter), he also highlighted “*ingu ivvuyirēy pirakiruti*” (the manifested matter which is together with soul). He said this to differentiate between the mūla prakruti and his śarīram (body). He said “*uyirēy prakruti*” (soul with matter), to highlight the matter which is with soul. \[This is to explain that [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is talking about intermediary deluge and not total deluge).
- *viṇṇum kōḷum eḻa* – To subdue the sky and the planets in there.
- *eri kālum eḻa* – To subdue the fire and air.
- *malai tāḷum eḻa* – To subdue the mountains along with their bases;  to uproot them fully.
- *sudar tānum eḻa* – To subdue those other radiant objects which are not enlisted here.
- *appan ūḷi eḻa* – ūḷi – sound. eḻa – to appear. Just as the sound which occurs while everyone enters into śrīrangam through the gates of adaiyavaḷaindān (the last layer of the seven layers) during dangerous times. When the creatures enter the divine stomach of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), many sounds occur due to the interaction between them; alternative explanation – ammāḷ explains this sound as “the sound of him sucking all of these into his mouth!”; with this it is thought that emperumān is joyfully protecting them \[by descending into this material realm\] instead of pridefully sitting as the supreme lord \[in paramapadam\] and protecting.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.4.5. Unudai

*ūṇudai mallar tadarnda oli mannar āṇudaic cēnai nadungum oli viṇṇuḷ ēṇudait tēvar veḷippatta oli appan kāṇudaip pāratam kaiyaṟai pōḻdē*

**Пословный перевод:**

appan – kriṣṇa who is partial towards his followers; kāṇudai – attractive; bhāratam – mahābhārata war; kai – joining his hands; aṟai – clapped \[to stimulate the war\]; pōḻdu – at that time; Un – muscles which give strength; udai – having; mallar – great wrestlers; tadarnda – banging at each other and falling; oli – sound; mannar – kings’; āḷ – brave soldiers; udai – having; sēnai – armies; nadungum – trembling; oli – sound; viṇ uḷ – on the sky; ēṇ – their respective positions; udai – having; dēvar – prime dēvatās; veḷippatta – appearing and celebrating; oli – sound (occurred)

**Перевод:**

**When kriṣṇa who is partial towards his followers, joined his hands and clapped them to conduct the mahābhārata war, the following sounds were heard – a) the great wrestlers who have muscles which give strength, banging each other and falling down, b) the trembling of the kings’ armies which are having great soldiers and c) the appearance and celebration of prime dēvatās per their respective positions, on the sky.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fifth pāsuram, āḻvār is enjoying the mahābhārata war which was conducted to eliminate the burden of earth.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. ūṇudai mallar tadarnda oli mannar āṇudaic cēnai nadungum oli viṇṇuḷ ēṇudait tēvar veḷippatta oli appan kāṇudaip pāratam kaiyaṟai pōḻdē*

- *ūṇ udai mallar tadarnda oli* – The banging sound of duryōdana’s prideful soldiers who were specifically paid extra allowances to purchase and consume food to strengthen themselves.  mal – pride. Saying “prideful army”. duryōdana fed them alcohol and meat to give them strength and sent them in to the battle field only to have them killed; knowing that pāṇḍava army soldiers were destroying those evil persons by driving their chariots over them – the sound of that. After hailing their strength, āḻvār is putting them down by saying “they were broken into pieces”, to highlight that they were destroyed effortlessly like freshly made pots.
- *mannar …* – The army which is having greatly valorous kings. The fearful sound of those kings who became frightened thinking “we are finished” on hearing “kriṣṇa has taken the position of charioteer \[for arjuna\]”. bhīśma, drōṇa et al are experts in warfare \[and these are the kings who became frightened\].
- *viṇ uḷ ēṇ udait tēvar veḷippatta oli* – The dēvas who are counted along with sarvēśvara and consider themselves to be the lords, having their own abodes. The sound of their visible hailing of emperumān. Those who are recited together as said in nārāyaṇa sūktam “*sabrahmā sa śivas sēndra:*” (He is \[the antaryāmi of\] brahmā, he is \[the antaryāmi of\] Siva, he is \[the antaryāmi of\] indra). Due to his saulabhyam (simplicity), he will let these lowly dēvatās \[who are dwellers of sky\] along with him!
- appan – The benefactor, who eliminated the burden of earth,
- *kāṇ udai …* – The purpose of his bestowing us senses such as eyes etc is only to see his such form. The form where he is with the dust of the army, having the stick and rope in his hands \[to conduct the horses of the chariot\] and with the firmly placed divine foot. This is the form indicated by him in [śrī bhagavat gītā 18.66](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/18-66/) “*mām*” (me). The attractive mahābhārata war.
- *kai aṟai pōḻdu* – These sounds were heard when he walked around the army waving and clapping his hands and instructing them “You have to do this! We will do this!” and so on.

## 7.4.6. Poldu melinda

*pōḻdu melinda pun sekkaril vān tisai sūḻum eḻundu udirap punalā malai kīḻdu piḷanda singam ottadāl appan āḻ tuyar seydu asuraraik kollumāṟē*

**Пословный перевод:**

pōḻdu – day; melinda – when ended; pun – young; sekkaril – reddish, during dusk; vān – sky; tisai – directions; sūḻum – surrounded; eḻundu – rise; udirap punal – pool of blood; A – to create; appan – emperumān in the form of narasimha, who helps his followers; āḻ tuyar – great sorrow; seydu – caused; asurarai – hiraṇya, the demon; kollum – killing; āṟu – method; malai – mountain; kīḻdu – to put down; piḷanda – tore; singam – lion; ottadu – similar

**Перевод:**

**When the day was ending, emperumān rose in the form of narasimha, who helps his followers, to create a pool of blood in the youthfully reddish sky at dusk and the surrounding directions, and killed hiraṇya, the demon; the method through which he killed the demon looked similar to a lion tearing down a mountain.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the sixth pāsuram, āḻvār  is mercifully explaining the incident of killing of hiraṇya, which is the reason for uplifting of devotees.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. pōḻdu melinda pun sekkaril vān tisai sūḻum eḻundu udirap punalā malai kīḻdu piḷanda singam ottadāl appan āḻ tuyar seydu asuraraik kollumāṟē*

- *pōḻdu melinda* – As the day was coming to an end as said in “*palita prāyō vāsara:*” (Most part of the day was gone).
- *pun sekkaril* – While the sky is reaching the point of dusk. The time between the day and the dusk which was discounted in the boon which hiraṇya got from brahmā. He got a boon saying “I cannot be killed in the day and in the night”.
- *vān tisai sūḻum eḻundu udirap punalā* – The expansive sky and all the directions became filled with a pool of blood, just as all low-lying regions will be filled with flood waters.
- *malai kīḻdu piḷanda singam ottadāl* – Saying “a lion placing a mountain underneath it and tearing it apart”; alternatively saying “lion which tore it apart, a lion which joyfully tore it apart”. It is said in tiruccanda viruttam 62 “*iraṇḍu kūṟu seyduganda singam*” (narasimha, the lion god, who tore hiraṇya into two pieces and became joyful). Like a lion which tore apart a mountain in to two equal pieces.
- *appan āḻ tuyar seydu* – Looking at the rough face of narasimha, hiraṇya experienced everything which he will experience after his death. That is, within a fraction of moment, he experienced the great suffering,  matching all the unfavourable actions he did with regard to bhagavān and bhāgavatas. Causing great sorrow.
- *asuraraik kollum āṟē* – This is how [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) killed the demon. The following principle is explained with this incident. Apart from his common disposition towards all, he would also be the vatsala (one with motherly affection), through the father, mother et al towards the children; if that motherly affection is not present, the same father will become an enemy; even at that stage, only emperumān will remain the saviour. With this, it is explained that empeurmān will come and protect immediately as the danger becomes greater. If emperumān protects when the father himself turns to be an enemy, should we have to explicitly say that he will protect when one becomes an enemy for self? As said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 6.5](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/6-5/) “*ātmaiva ripurātmana:*” (mind alone is one’s enemy), one is an enemy to oneself \[when attached to worldly pleasures\].

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.4.7. Maru niraittu

*māṟu niraittu iraikkum sarangaḷ ina nūṟu piṇam malai pōl puraḷa kadal āṟu maduttu udirap punalā appan nīṟu pada ilangai seṟṟa nērē*

**Пословный перевод:**

māṟu – facing each other; niraittu – being organised; iraikkum – making sound; sarangaḷ – by the arrows; inam – in groups; nūṟu – hundreds and hundreds of; piṇam – dead bodies of the rākśasas; malai pōl – like a mountain; puraḷa – to fall; āṟu – through the rivers; maduttu – being filled; kadal – ocean; udirap punal – flood of blood; A – to become; appan – cakravartit tirumagan (śrī rāma, divine son of the emperor daśarata), who is the benefactor of his followers; ilangai – lankā; nīṟu pada – to become ashes; seṟṟa – fought; nēr – honesty

**Перевод:**

**The groups of arrows which were shot, were making great sounds; they caused hundreds and hundreds of dead bodies of the rākśasas to fall like mountains falling down; the ocean became filled with a flood of blood through the rivers; this is how cakravartit tirumagan, who is the benefactor of his followers, fought the war honestly, to bring lankā down to ashes.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the seventh pāsuram, āḻvār is enjoying how rāvaṇa was killed.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. māṟu niraittu iraikkum sarangaḷ ina nūṟu piṇam malai pōl puraḷa kadal āṟu maduttu udirap punalā appan nīṟu pada ilangai seṟṟa nērē*

- *māṟu niraittu iraikkum sarangaḷ* – This is how quickly śrī rāma traversed the battle field. The sound of the arrows which were shot from different directions banged on each other and created huge sound, like the sound of the \[turbulent\] ocean. In the speed at which śrī rāma traversed in the battle field, his own arrows which were shot from different directions, banged at each other and caused huge sounds.
- *ina nūṟu piṇam malai pōl puraḷa* – The many groups of hundreds and hundreds of dead bodies, due to having been pierced fiercely by the arrows, were split into two and both parts of each body were shaking as the soul was interlocked between both the parts.
- *kadal āṟu maduttu udirap punalā* – The ocean which is said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 2.70](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/2-70/) “*āpūryamāṇam acala pratiśtam*” (naturally full and motionless), became filled with a flood of blood, and was flowing out through rivers. [tirumangai āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/thirumangai-azhwar/) said in periya tirumoḻi “*vaiymūdu peru nīrin mummai peridē*” (Three times greater than the deluge which covers the world).
- *nīṟu pada* – To turn them into ashes as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 26.26 “*smaśāṇa sadruśī*” (similar to a crematorium).
- *ilangai seṟṟa nērē* – nēr indicates time. At the time when he destroyed lankā. In this case, the pāsuram should be read as “*ilangai seṟṟa poḻudu – māṟu niraittu iraikkum sarangaḷ*“. Alternative explanation – \[nēr indicates his skill\] the manner in which he destroyed lankā. Instead of mystical warfare, he fought straight and destroyed lankā. Another explanation – nēr – honestly. Here it means, he destroyed lankā through honest means only.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.4.8. Ner sarindan

*nēr sarindān kodik kōḻi koṇḍān pinnum nēr sarindān eriyum analōn pinnum nēr sarindān mukkaṇ mūrtti kaṇḍīr appan nēr sari vāṇan tiṇ tōḷ koṇḍa anṟē*

**Пословный перевод:**

appan – kriṣṇa who helped anirudda \[kriṣṇa’s grandson\]; nēr sari – sided; vāṇan – bāṇa’s; tiṇ – strong as a result of the boon etc; tōḷ – shoulders; koṇḍa – won over; aṇru – on that day; kōḻi – peacock; kodi – as flag; koṇḍān – subrahmaṇya, who has; nēr sarindān – fell down, unable to resist; pinnum – further; eriyum – with rising flame (having the cruelty of rudra); analōn – agni (fire); nēr sarindān – fell down, unable to resist; pinnum – further; mukkaṇ – having great power due to having three eyes; mūrtti – rudra, the chief among dēvatās; nēr serindān – ran away from the battlefield; kaṇḍīr – see \[it is well known\]!

**Перевод:**

**On that day when kriṣṇa who helped anirudda, won over the strong shoulder’s of bāṇa who sided \[with rudra et al\], subrahmaṇya, who has peacock flag, fell down, unable to resist; further, agni, with rising flame, fell down, unable to resist; further, rudra, the chief among dēvatās, having great power due to having three eyes, ran away from the battlefield; aren’t these well known?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the eighth pāsuram, āḻvār is reminiscing \[kriṣṇa’s\] victory over bāṇa.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. nēr sarindān kodik kōḻi koṇḍān pinnum nēr sarindān eriyum analōn pinnum nēr sarindān mukkaṇ mūrtti kaṇḍīr appan nēr sari vāṇan tiṇ tōḷ koṇḍa anṟē*

- *nēr sarindān kodik kōḻi koṇḍān* – subrahmaṇya who has peacock as his flag, is the commander-in-chief of dēvas, like a colt (young one of a horse) in the battlefield, lost in the beginning itself.
- *pinnum …* – At that time, the forty nine agni dēvatās appeared with great fervour, only to run away.
- *pinnum …* – rudra hiding his flag thinking “our son pridefully showed his flag only to be insulted in the end” arrived there; immediately he lost the battle and was running away, covering his third eye. While he ran, hiding his eye, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) catches him red-handed by saying “*mukkaṇ mūrtti kaṇḍīr*” (see the one with the third eye) and reveals his identity to everyone. Whatever one may do, one cannot hide one’s main bodily identity. This sorrow is beyond words and cannot be even said as “the sorrow inflicted upon me when bāṇa’s thousand shoulders were severed”. appan – causeless protector.
- *nēr sari vāṇan* – Now the chief, bāṇāsura is coming; he too runs away from the battlefield – says āḻvār; or āḻvār is saying “he is turning around from wherever he is standing to look away \[indicating that he has given up fighting\]”. Those who dropped the weapons and those who showed their hair \[i.e. their back, turning away from the battle\] cannot be killed.
- *tiṇ tōḷ koṇḍa anṟē* – bāṇāsura remained firmly as if remaining in a fort, holding on to a dēvatā (demigod) who is as good as himself. He remained free from fear holding on to rudra, who has skull attached to his palm \[due to a curse\], similar to those who are surrendered to the supreme lord. He pretended similar to those who remain as said in taittirīya upaniśat “*na bibēti kutaścana*” (Those who are surrendered to sarvēśvaran do not fear anything).
- *tiṇ tōḷ koṇḍa* – Considering “uśā cannot become fatherless”, he just severed bāṇa’s hands. It is due to his having many hands, he fell at the feet and vorśipped any dēvatā he saw. Due to this, kriṣṇa severed his hands and made him lord-less. While it is ordained that one should use the body and limbs in the service of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) as said in śrīviṣṇu darmam “*yau tat pūjā karau karau*” (only those hands which worship emperumān are called hands) and śrīviṣṇu darmam “*vicitrā dēhasampattir īśvarāya nivēditum …*” (Oh brāhmaṇa! To offer oneself and other materials, [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) previously got connected to the amazing body with hands and legs), he engaged his thousand hands in inapt matters and hence emperumān severed them. As the dēvatā (rudra) himself came begging and prayed to emperumān “Can you who made me a dēvatā, invalidate it? If you kill my devotee, no one else will come and surrender unto me”, he let bāṇa live. śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 5.33.41 “*kriṣṇa kriṣṇa mahābāhō jānētvām puruśōttamam*” (kriṣṇa! kriṣṇa! Oh mighty armed! I know you as the best among the men) – \[rudra says\] without realising your true nature, I just saw your shooting posture and thought that you were just a warrior; like those who say “only after aiming and marking my neck, I realised the true nature”. With this, it is explained – everyone other than īśvara, while they are doing well, they will consider themselves to be the protectors and when they are in danger, they will lead the danger to their devotees and they will escape; it is explained that since in every situation, [sarvēśvaran](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) will protect his followers by transforming himself, even in dire situations, he is the only one who is fit to be surrendered unto; others are not to be surrendered.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.4.9. Anru man

*anṟu maṇ nīr eri kāl viṇ malai mudal anṟu sudar iraṇḍu piṟavum pinnum anṟu maḻai uyir dēvum maṟṟum appan anṟu mudal ulagam seydadumē*

**Пословный перевод:**

appan – the great benefactor, who is the creator of the universe; mudal – initially; ulagam – universe; seydadum – created; anṟu – during that initial creation; maṇ nīr eri kāl viṇ – the five elements starting with earth etc which are the causes; malai mudal – the mountains etc which are worldly objects; seydadum – created; anṟu – during that time; sudar – moon and sun; iraṇḍu – both; piṟavum – other radiant objects; seydadum – created; anṟu – during that time; pinnum – further; maḻai – rain; uyir – creatures which depend on the rain; dēvum – the dēvas who grant the rain; maṟṟum – other creatures; seydadum – created; anṟu – during that time

**Перевод:**

**During the initial creation, the great benefactor, who is the creator of the universe, created the universe; he created the five elements starting with earth etc which are the causes and the mountains etc which are worldly objects; he created both moon and sun and other radiant objects; further he created rain, creatures which depend on the rain, the dēvas who grant the rain and other creatures. Implies that āḻvār is talking about the initial creation after total deluge instead of subsequent creation.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Ninth pāsuram. As sruśti (creation) is also distinct for bhagavān \[and not done by anyone else\], āḻvār is considering it to be a victorious act. As per “appan – mudal ulagam seydadum – anṟu“, the great benefactor initially created the universe \[material realm in manifested state\] during the first sruśti \[i.e. after total deluge, the creation begins once again\]. To support this concept “maṇ nīr …”  \[the creation of five great elements which is part of samaśti sruśti \[initial creation up to five great elements, before the variegated creation commences\]\] is highlighted here; alternative explanation –  as the previous pāsuram and next pāsuram talk about kriṣṇa’s activities, we can construe that as āḻvār is thinking that only after winning over bāṇa, the universe came into existence \[previously, it was as good as non-existing\], he is talking about that here; it is not sufficient to just raise the crops; only when the crops are protected, they are said to be created. anṟu maṇ nīr eri kāl viṇ malai mudal anṟu sudar iraṇḍu piṟavum pinnum anṟu maḻai uyir dēvum maṟṟum appan anṟu mudal ulagam seydadumē*

- *anṟu* … – He created both cause \[five great elements\] and effect \[variegated creation\].
- *sudar iraṇḍu* – He created the moon and sun.
- *piṟavum* – Other radiant objects such as starts etc, and further, the cloud which pours rain;
- *maḻai mēgam* – Other souls which survive based on the rain, and the dēvas who create rain, and other animals/plants.
- *appan* – the creator of all.
- *anṟu mudal ulagam seydadumē* – Do I have to identity all of these individually? On the day, emperumān punished bāṇa and eliminated multiple kings \[and remained as a singular king for all\], he created these; alternative explanation – on the day when the state was as said in taittirīya upaniśat “*sadēva*” (only sat existed, and emperumān vowed “*bahusyām*” (let me become many)).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.4.10. Mey nirai

*mēy nirai kīḻ puga mā puraḷac cunai vāy niṟai nīr piḷiṟic coṟiya ina ānirai pādi angē odunga appan tī maḻai kāttuk kunṟam eduttānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

mēy – grazing; nirai – cows; kīḻ – underneath; puga – to take shelter; mā – the animals residing on the hill; puraḷa – to roll down and fall; sunai – ponds’; vāy – up to the top; niṟai – filled; nīr – water; piḷiṟi – with tumultuous sound; soriya – to pour; inam – groups of; āy nirai – having covherds and cows; pādi – tiruvāyppādi (gōkulam); angē – there; odunga – to take shelter; appan – kriṣṇa, who eliminates danger; tī – causing disaster; maḻai – rain; kāttu – stopped; kunṟam – gōvardana hill; eduttān – lifted up

**Перевод:**

**kriṣṇa, who eliminates danger, lifted up the gōvardana hill, stopped the disaster-causing rain, for the grazing cows to take shelter underneath it, to have the animals residing on the hill roll down and fall, to have the ponds which have water filled up to the top, pour down with a tumultuous sound, and to have the groups of cows and covherds of tiruvāyppādi take shelter there.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the tenth pāsuram, āḻvār is enjoying emperumān‘s act of lifting up the gōvardana hill and protecting \[the covherds and cattle\].*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. mēy nirai kīḻ puga mā puraḷac cunai vāy niṟai nīr piḷiṟic coṟiya ina ānirai pādi angē odunga appan tī maḻai kāttuk kunṟam eduttānē*

- *mēy nirai kīḻ puga* – To have the grazing cows enter underneath the hill, while continuing to chew the grass which they ate, without spitting them out.
- *mā puraḷa* – Due to lifting up the hill and placing it upside down, the animals which were residing there started rolling down.
- *sunai vāy niṟai nīr piḷiṟic coriya* – The water filled in the pond started falling with a sound similar to that from a pot filled with water turned upside down; while trying to save from a rain, he caused many little rains to pour there.
- *ina ānirai pādi angē odunga* – To have the herds of cows and \[the residents of\] tiruvāyppādi take shelter there.
- *appan* – the benefactor, who helps during disaster.
- *tī maḻai kāttu* – As the rain was sent down to bring upon the end, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying “*tīmaḻai*” (fire rain). āḻvār is considering himself to be suffering then, beyond the covherds and cows.
- *kunṟam eduttānē* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying “the great benefactor who lifted the hill and saved everyone”. [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) held the hill for seven days thinking “only until indra’s anger out of hunger subdues, he will pour the rain” and protected everyone. Only if it were rāvaṇa et al, could they have been killed? Since it is an unfavourable act by a favourable person (indra, a devotee), emperumān could only do this. With this, it is explained that even if a devotee commits a mistake, emperumān will tolerate that and protect him.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.
