## 7.4.11. Kunram edutta

*kunṟam edutta pirān adiyārodum onṟi ninṟa satakōpan urai seyal nanṟi punainda ōr āyirattuḷ ivai venṟi tarum pattum mēvik kaṟpārkkē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kunṟam edutta – one who lifted gōvardana; pirān – for kriṣṇa, the great benefactor; adiyārodum – bhāgavatas who are distinguished servitors; onṟi – united; ninṟa – having the nature; satakōpan – āḻvār’s; urai seyal – the act through speech; ōr – unique; āyirattuḷ – among the thousand pāsurams; nanṟi – the goodness of revealing the victories of sarvēśvaran; punainda – having; ivai pattum – this decad; mēvi – with the meanings; kaṟpārkku – those who practice; venṟi – victory in every aspect; tarum – will grant

**Перевод:**

**āḻvār remained united with and having the same nature as the bhāgavatas who are distinguished servitors for kriṣṇa, the great benefactor, who lifted gōvardana; those who practice with the meanings, such āḻvār’s this decad among the thousand pāsurams, which is having the goodness of revealing the victories of sarvēśvaran, will be granted victory in every aspect, by this decad itself.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the end, āḻvār says “Those who learn with their hearts this decad,  which enlists emperumān’s victories, will be granted victories by this decad itself”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. kunṟam edutta pirān adiyārodum onṟi ninṟa satakōpan urai seyal nanṟi punainda ōr āyirattuḷ ivai venṟi tarum pattum mēvik kaṟpārkkē*

- *kunṟam edutta …* – āḻvār becoming pleased being together with the bhāgavatas who are engaged in emperumān’s quality of lifting up the gōvardana hill, and the beauty at that time, recited this pāsuram as an outlet for that joy.
- *nanṟi punainda ōr āyiram* – The thousand pāsurams which classified sarvēśvaran’s paratvam (supremacy) and saulabhyam (simplicity). nanmai (goodness) means telling the samsāri (materialistic person) that emperumān is the sarvēśvaran, he is easily approachable by all and he is the refuge for all; this is what has been mercifully explained by āḻvār from the first decad. This decad which enlists the victories of sarvēśvaran.
- *mēvik kaṟpārkku – venṟi tarum* – This decad will grant victories to those who learn this with great attachment. For aiśvaryārti (those who seek wealth), it will eliminate the hurdles for acquiring wealth; for kaivalyārti (the one who seeks self-enjoyment), it will eliminate the hurdles \[in that pursuit\]; for bhagavat caraṇārti (those who seek bhagavān’s divine feet) – for upāsanka (one who pursues karma, jñāna or bhakti yōgam), it will grant control over senses; for prapanna, it will grant victory over hurdles in performing kainkaryam.

In the next article we will enjoy the next decad.

## 7.5 Karpar iramapiranai

## 7.5.1. Karpar iramapiranai

*kaṟpār irāma pirānai allāl maṟṟum kaṟparō? puṟpā mudalāp pul eṟumbādi onṟinṟiyē naṟpāl ayōttiyil vāḻum sarāsaram muṟṟavum naṟpālukku uyttanan nānmuganār peṟṟa nāttuḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

pā – sprouted and spread; pul – grass; mudalā – starting with; pul – very lowly; eṟumbu – ant; ādi – etc; naṟpāl – the good place (where śrī rāma’s qualities are observed); ayōttiyil – in śrī ayōdyā; vāḻum – those who are living, with the joy of enjoying the qualities \[of śrī rāma\]; sarāsaram – in the form of cara (mobile) and acara (immobile); muṟṟavum – all entities; nānmuganār peṟṟa – created by brahmā; nāttuḷē – in the universe; onṟu – any means to be uplifted; inṟiyē – while not having; naṟpālukku – the apt land \[paramapadam\], which is a good place; uyttanan – placed; kaṟpār – those who desire to learn something which is priyam and hitam; irāman – cakravartit tirumagan (the son of emperor daśarata and who is too desirable, and who is embodiment of dharma); pirānai – great benefactor; allāl – other than; maṟṟum – any entity; kaṟparō – will they learn?

**Перевод:**

**Those who are living in the good place, in śrī ayōdyā, with the joy of enjoying the qualities \[of śrī rāma\], all entities in the form of cara (mobile) and acara (immobile) created in the universe by brahmā, starting with the sprouted and spread out grass, very lowly ant etc, who were not having  any means to be uplifted, were all placed in the apt land, which is a good place, by śrī rāma; those who desire to learn something which is priyam and hitam, will they learn about any entity other than the great benefactor, cakravartit tirumagan (śrī rāma)?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the first pāsuram, āḻvār says “Would those who analyse about priyam (aspects which give pleasure) and hitam (aspects which do good), learn about anyone other than the great benefactor śrī rāma, who, out of his own will, made the residents of śrī ayōdyā feel happy/sad in his union/separation?”*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. kaṟpār irāma pirānai allāl maṟṟum kaṟparō? puṟpā mudalāp pul eṟumbādi onṟinṟiyē naṟpāl ayōttiyil vāḻum sarāsaram muṟṟavum naṟpālukku uyttanan nānmuganār peṟṟa nāttuḷē*

- *kaṟpār* … – āḻvār is considering that anything other than learning about śrī rāma, will not be counted as learning. Did the riśi not say in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 6.5.84 “*tat jñānam ajñānam atōnyatuktam*” (that is knowledge and everything else is ignorance)? The knowledge which helps one reach bhagavān is knowledge; everything else is said to be ignorance only.
- *kaṟpār* – One learns something because “it is pleasing at the time of learning” or “it will lead to something good in the future”; since it is said “*irāma pirānai*” (śrī rāma, the benefactor), both the aspects are found here only and nowhere else. rāma indicates the beauty which will bind oneself fully to him without going anywhere; pirān indicates how he makes cētanas become exclusively existing for him manifesting that beauty and his magnanimity of presenting his beauty for the sake of others only as done by moon, southerly breeze, sandalwood and water. śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 2.32 “*priyavādīca*” – when perumāḷ (śrī rāma) mercifully speaks, one cannot do anything but listen to that; when heard, his words will only be sweet. When asked “for whom?”, it is said “*bhūtānām*” – for all creatures which have existence; one only needs to be different from insentient objects \[i.e. one should simply be sentient\]. When asked “would it be pleasing then but lead to something else?”, *satyavādīca* – whatever he says will not be anything other than for the well-being of everyone. If his one word is praised like this, it is obvious for the rest of his words. He captivated the entire kingdom to be as said in uttara rāmāyaṇa ślōkam “*rāmō rāmō rāma iti*” (Saying rāma, repeatedly). perumāḷ’s existence is the cause for the ātmā’s existence; rest of the aspects \[of perumāḷ) are for the enjoyment of the ātmā. The pāsuram says “will those who are interested in priyam and hitam, seek anyone other than śrī rāma?” śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 2.29 “*sākśāt rāmāt vinirvruttō darmaścāpi śriyāsaha:*” (Only śrī rāma can make both righteousness and wealth combine truly) – the pāsuram says that śrī rāma is both the means and goal, being inseparable from each other.
- *kaṟpār irāma pirānai* – His goal is not to say kaṟpār (learners); his goal is to say that “others are not worthy to be learnt”. When it is done out of love, one will naturally learn about śrī rāma only; thus, one should simply avoid engaging in others. āḻvār does not eliminate vorśipping other dēvatās etc by saying “*maṟṟu*” (others), but is discriminating between the different forms of the vorśippable lord. āḻvār is not of the nature to eliminate the unworthy dēvatās, but is eliminating emperumān’s paratvam (paramapada nātan) and other incarnations.
- *maṟṟum kaṟparō* – As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam uttara kāṇḍam 40.16 “*bhāvō nānyatra gaccati*” (hanuman says – my mind will not focus on anyone else). \[This ślōkam is explained in detail\]
   - *snēhō mē parama:* – When śrī rāma was mercifully returning to paramapadam, he enquired hanuman “Would you follow me?”, hanuman replies “my love is not limited to that”. As said in [iraṇḍām tiruvandādi 100](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/02/irandam-thiruvandhadhi-100/) “*en than aḷavanṟāl yānudaiya anbu*” (my love is greater than me) and tiruvāimoḻi 9.6.1 “*uyirin param anṟip perugumāl vētkaiyum*” (my love stretches beyond myself).
   - *rājamstvayi* – It was not acquired by myself. Grammar says “*ranjcayatīti rājā”.*
   - *nityam pratiśtita:* – Since it is about holding on to emperumān, it cannot be done as said in “I will hold on to one form now and another form later”.
   - *bhaktiś ca niyatā* – snēham is the state of daśarata cakravarti who gave up his life unable to bear the separation of perumāḷ; bhakti is the state of iḷaiya perumāḷ (lakśmaṇa) who surrendered properly when perumāḷ said “stop; remain here in ayōdyā”, he said to him “*kuruśva*” (you should accept me as your servitor and order).
   - *vīra* – You could have been victorious elsewhere with your valour, but cannot defeat me here. Since hanuman too is valorous, he is talking about the way śrī rāma won over him \[by showing his valour\].
   - *bhāva: na anyatra gaccati* – Even if you take me along, you cannot redeem my heart. As said in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.7.8](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/09/thiruvaimozhi-1-7-8-ennai-negizhkkilum/) “*ennudaiya nal nenjam tannai agalvikkat tānum killān ini*” (it will be impossible for himself to separate my heart which has become partial towards him), even the omnipotent emperumān cannot redeem his heart.
   - *anyatra na gaccati* – As said in amalanādipirān 10 “*kaṇḍa kaṇgaḷ maṟṟonṟinaik kāṇāvē*” (the eyes which have seen śrīrangānāta will not see anything else). anyatra implies, he does not even like to utter the name of the other forms. As said in [siṟiya tirumadal](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/03/siriya-thirumadal/) “*maṟṟārānum uṇḍenbār*” (ignorant ones say that there is a goal named mōkśam), here āḻvār is saying “*maṟṟum kaṟparō*” .
- *kaṟparō* – īsn’t he \[āḻvār\] a cētana? He considers everyone to be himself; as those who say “how will the children of this town eat without rich/pure sugar as the side dish?” \[A story is narrated in the arumpadam to explain this – once, a prince was tired and ended up in a house looking for food. The lady of the house offered him some rice. He asked for a side dish and the lady give him some salt/pickle. The prince at once wondered “How would children in this town eat without rich/pure sugar?”, considering everyone to be having a royal lifestyle like himself\].

Further, the reason for learning about śrī rāma, giving up everything else, is explained.

- *pul pā mudalā* – pā indicates material, pul (grass) being that material; alternatively – pā indicates spreading out, implying well spread out grass. Being beyond the reach of the mouth of the cows. This implies wheat grass etc.
- *pul eṟumbādi* – Starting with the lowest of animals, ant. Ant is usually recited along with brahmā \[to indicate highest and lowest forms of living beings\]. āḻvār is not highlighting any specific importance to grass, ant etc; he is saying that they were the ones to receive the attention of śrī rāma first; just as flood will flow into low-lying areas first. Lowest of plant life is grass; lowest of animal life is ant; since they are cited together here, it eliminates the principle of “jñānam (knowledge) leads to mōkśam”.  It also emphasises that having \[evolved\] consciousness or not, is irrelevant for perumāḷ’s compassion. It emphasises that the differences due to their karma are also irrelevant; with respect to the unconditional lord, one needs to have apratiśēdam (not stopping emperumān from helping) only for the result to fructify. Looking at the state of śrī bharatāḻvān, while the people were crying, the trees which were neck-deep in water, also withered as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 59.4 “*apivrukśā: parimlānā:*” (Even the trees withered). śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 59.5 is explained; “*upataptōdakā nadya:*” – there is no difference between the water and those who fall into the water. upatapta means one cannot even reach the banks. “*palvalāni sarāmsica*” – there is no difference between small and big entities. As said in “*vanāni upavanānica”* – forests and gardens \[were drowned\].
- *onṟu inṟiyē* – Not saying everything \[every creature\]; since there is “*muṟṟavum*” subsequently which indicates all creatures. Now, “*onṟu inṟiyē*” implies that they do not have any sādana (means) which will lead them to the goal. When one observes the inferior nature of self and the superior nature of the result attained, one will realise that one has nothing in self. Looking at the \[great\] result that is achieved, one cannot claim anything in the self, whether one gets the result through parama bhakti or bhagavān. Now, when there is no means in anyone when emperumān acknowledged everyone, he who gave the result, is the sādanam (means) \[Even “*dēśōyam sarvakāmaduk*” (residence in divyadēśam will grant all wishes), is only said for glorification\]! He granted this great result to them just because they resided there without leaving.
- *naṟpāl ayōtti* – In śrī ayōdyā which has good places. pāl – place. With this, it is implied that just being in this town, will bring bhakti towards śrī rāma. It is said “*dēśōyam sarvakāmaduk*” (residence in divyadēśam will grant all wishes). But it is said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 7.1 “*jñāti dāsī yatō jātā*” (servant maid of relatives of kaikēyi, residing with her since birth). What is the explanation for that? \[i.e. why was mantarā evil minded, even after being in ayōdyā?\] One who is born in this town will not have any enmity towards perumāḷ. As she was born elsewhere, she just remained an unknown person. udāli (one of the primary commentators for śrī rāmāyaṇa) explained this as “*yata:kutaścijjātā*” (She was born somewhere). Not taking birth in this land of śrī ayōdyā, has become the enemy for her. The divine abode itself can bring in all goodness. While the residents of this town (śrīrangam), eat, wear clothes, celebrate emperumān, talk with each other and roam around \[like everyone else\], when there is a hurdle/danger for perumāḷ (emperumān), they will consider their own bodies as that of the enemies, and even give them up. As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam “*rāgavārtē parākrāntā na prāṇē kurutēdayām*” (The army which has surrounded to support śrī rāma, does not have any love towards their own life), as the prāṇas (lives), due to having been together for so long, seek acknovledgement \[from the soldiers\], they said “when we should choose between the owner (śrī rāma) and you, would we choose you?” When śrī rāma says in uttara kāṇḍa 18.18 “*prāṇān parityajya*” (I will protect my devotees even at the cost of my own life), why would anyone see their own life?
- *ayōttiyil vāḻum* – Instead of saying “*varttikkum*” (residing), āḻvār has said “*vāḻum*” (living gloriously), since in ayōdyā, there is no such difference \[everyone lives gloriously there\]; as said in nācciyār tirumoḻi 8.9 “*vēngadattaip padiyāga vāḻvīrgāḷ*” (live gloriously having tiruvēngadam as your abode) and nācciyār tirumoḻi 11.5 “*nallārgaḷ vāḻum naḷir arangam*” (the śrīrangam where many noble people live gloriously). Since once residing in the apt abode itself is redemption, āḻvār is saying “*ayōttiyil vāḻum*“. The eternally apt emperumān is having his presence here always. Our experience happens once in a while due to our connection with acit (body); due to the same emperumān \[who is present in paramapadam\], being present here, there is no shortcoming in the divine abode.
- *naṟpālukku uyttanan* – He changed them to have noble qualities. That is making them feeling happy/sad based on union/separation. If joy/sorrow occurs based on one’s karma, it is limited. But as they occurred by his grace, it leads to goodness for everyone. For śrī rāma who could liberate one from the bondage here and grant him the supreme bliss in paramapadam as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 68.80 “*mayātvam samanujñātō gacca lōkān anuttamān*” (Being ordained by me, you shall reach the supreme abode), it is not difficult to instill such quality of being unable to sustain in his absence.
- *nānmuganār peṟṟa nāttuḷē – naṟpālukkuyttanan* – When an emperor makes one of his confidantes as a king for a small kingdom, he will ensure that his own orders and independent desires will be implemented in the kingdom. Similarly, in this materialistic realm which is under the control of four-headed brahmā who is the chief for the samsāri cētanas (materialistic people), emperumān eliminated brahmā’s independence, and reformed the dependence of the residents of ayōdyā on their karma, by manifesting his qualities, and made them survive when they have him and feel sad in his absence. This being the case, would one learn anything other than śrī rāma?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

adiyen saraty ramanuja dasan

## 7.5.2. Nattil pirandavar

*nāttil piṟandavar nāraṇaṟkāḷ anṟi āvarō nāttil piṟandu padādana pattu manisarkkā nāttai naliyum arakkarai nādit tadindittu nāttai aḷittuyyac ceydu nadandamai kēttumē*

**Пословный перевод:**

nāttil – in the place where his greatness is not understood; piṟandu – taking birth (based on the request of the followers, just as those who are bound by karma take birth); padādana pattu – going through sufferings which even they (the samsāris) do not undergo; manisarkkā – for those ungrateful men who blame him subsequently; nāttai – the place where they live; naliyum – torment; arakkarai – rākśasas; nādi – seeking them in their own places; tadindittu – killing; nāttai – the place; aḷittu – protecting; uyyacceydu – uplifting them to spare them from rebirth; nadandamai – (as said in “saśarīras sahānuga:“, with that form and paraphernalia) the way he presented himself; kēttum – after having heard through śrī rāmāyaṇam; nāttil – in the abode (where his qualities are observed); piṟandavar – those who are born; nāraṇaṟku – (as said in “bhavān nārāyaṇa dēva:“) to cakravarti tirumagan (śrī rāma, the divine son of emperor daśarata) who has unconditional relationship; āḷ – to become a servitor; anṟi – other than; āvarō – will they become servitor of anyone else?

**Перевод:**

**After having heard through śrī rāmāyaṇam about emperumān taking birth in the place where his greatness is not understood, going through sufferings which even they do not undergo, for those ungrateful men who blame him subsequently, seeking the rākśasas who torment them where they live, in their own places and killing them, protecting the place and uplifting them to spare them from rebirth and the way he presented himself, will those who are born, become the servitor of anyone else other than cakravarti tirumagan, who has unconditional relationship?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the second pāsuram, āḻvār highlights śrī rāma’s greater quality in comparison with what was explained in the previous pāsuram. While in the previous pāsuram, āḻvār explained how śrī rāma captivated everyone in ayōdyā with his qualities, in this pāsuram, āḻvār explains how śrī rama did not leave anyone behind while ascending to paramapadam and how he took them there along with him.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār explains how emperumān protected by remaining in ayōdyā for eleven thousand years instead of ascending to paramapdam immediately after accomplishing the task cut out for the particular avatāram.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Second pāsuram. Some explain the greatness of the qualities explained in the subsequent pāsurams as “Desiring to speak about the qualities \[of emperumān\] which are explained in the subsequent pāsurams, āḻvār says that the quality explained in the previous pāsuram is not so great”. In this pāsuram, āḻvār says “Is it just that he made the residents of śrī ayōdyā to be fully sustaining themselves by śrī rāma’s qualities? Did he not eliminate the hurdles of the residents of śrī ayōdyā and protect them?” \[Implying that his subsequent act/quality of uplifting everyone is greater\] nāttil piṟandavar nāraṇaṟkāḷ anṟi āvarō nāttil piṟandu padādana pattu manisarkkā nāttai naliyum arakkarai nādit tadindittu nāttai aḷittuyyac ceydu nadandamai kēttumē*

- *nāttil piṟandavar* – Everyone takes birth in some place. Here, the emphasis is on having taken birth in the abode where śrī rāma’s qualities are observed. \[Should he say where perumāḷ’s qualities are observed?\] But there is no place outside the boundary of perumāḷ’s kingdom. śrī rāmāyaṇam kiśkindā kāṇḍam 18.6 “*ikśvākūṇām iyam bhūmis saśaila vana kānanā*” (This earth with mountains, forests are under the reign of ikśvāku dynasty). sītāp pirātti too said to rāvaṇa in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 21.20 “*viditassa hi darmajña:*” (Have you not heard of perumāḷ’s qualities?) If only there is a place where his qualities are not observed, that place will be outside his reign. Being born in the kingdom means being born within the boundary of his kingdom and taking shelter under his shoulder.
- *nāraṇaṟku āḷ anṟi āvarō* – Implies “Would they not become a servitor of perumāḷ?” Even brahmā et al praised perumāḷ in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 120.13 “*bhavān nārāyaṇō dēva:*” (You are that lord nārāyaṇa). As said in “Would those who lived off a person, serve someone else?”
- *naraṇaṟku* – The name “nārāyaṇa” implies the following qualities in perumāḷ – mingling with everyone without any restriction, placing himself for the sake of his followers, accepting arrows on his chest for their sake, eliminating their enemies, being like a mother for the followers, not leaving them on seeing their defects. Due to these qualities, it is apt to call perumāḷ as “nārāyaṇa” \[here the term *perumāḷ* refers to śrī rāma\].
- *āḷ anṟi āvarō* – In the previous pāsuram, it was said “kaṟparō” (will they learn?), and in this pāsuram it is said “*āḷ anṟi āvarō*” (will they not become servitor?) – this implies that the result of learning, is to become a servitor.
- *piṟandavar – āḷ anṟi āvarō* – as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 40.5 “*sruśtastvam vanavāsāya*” (the purpose of your birth is to send you to the forest \[along with śrī rāma\]; saying “would those who have taken birth, lose the purpose of that? For [āḻvārs](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/azhwars/) who know the greatness of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), they will consider total dependence on emperumān, the apt lord, as the goal; \[for us\] due to having engaged in inapt aspects, it \[total dependence\] looks impractical and makes us wonder “is this the goal?”
- *nāttil piṟandu* – One who is totally untouched by the samsāra \[bondage\], taking birth in the place which is hated by even those who are bound by karma. \[śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 1.7 is explained here\] *sa hi dēvai: …*
   - *sa: jajñē hi* – One who is well known from the authentic scriptures that he has no birth due to karma, has taken birth which is beyond the imagination of even those bound by karma. What is the reason for his birth?
   - *artita:* – due to the prayer of the dēvas; their prayers caused his desire since it is said that he took birth out of his own desire in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 6.5.84 “*iccā gruhīta*” (he incarnated out of his desire).
   - *dēvai:* – He took birth for those who begged him for fulfilling their task and one the task was completed, would say “*īśvarōham*” (I am the lord)! They prayed as in tiruviruttam “*nīḷ nagar nīḷ eri vaittaruḷāy*” (mercifully burn down this great lankā).
   - *udīrṇasya rāvaṇasya* – The lowly rāvaṇa who caused fear in them; [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) himself had to descend and kill rāvaṇa who became very powerful due to the boons he acquired.
   - *vadārtibhi:* – due to the sufferings they went through, they requested him to do what is not acceptable to his divine heart. He only killed him thinking “if we killed this one person, the whole place will survive”.
   - *artita:* – He felt their prayer until he returned to his divine abode of paramapadam.
   - *artita:* – they did not perform any upāsana, but just prayed.
   - *mānuśē lōkē* – The dēvas who were created \[by bhagavān\], would hate the smell of humans, vomit on looking at them and with great dislike to step on earth, remain one and half yōjanā (about 15 miles) from the ground and accept the offerings given to them in yajñas (rituals); [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) in front of whom those dēvas look like manuśyas in front of them, himself descended here. It is said in tiruvāimoḻi 8.1.5 “*manisarkkut tēvar pōla dēvarkkum dēvāvō*” (just as dēvas are for manuśyas, you are dēva for the dēvas).
   - *jajñē* – It was not mere āvirbhūtam (manifesting directly); if the worldly people go through ten months in the womb, he spent twelve months in the womb; it is said in śri rāmāyaṇam bāla kāṇḍam 18.10 “*tataśca dvādaśē māsē*” (subsequently, on the twelfth month of caitra, śrī rāma took birth) and śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 5.3.14 “*jatōham yattavōdarāt” (*I was born from your womb).
   - *viṣṇus sanātana:* – the eternal lord, viṣṇu.
- *nāttai aḷittu – “nāttil piṟandu … manisarkkā”* – \[A summary up to this point\] [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), who is not bound by karma, took birth in this world along with the souls who are bound, went through sufferings which are even beyond their sufferings such as being separated from the daughter of janakarāja, with his soul on the other side of the ocean \[along with sītā\] and his mere body remained here, lost jatāyu, etc. Further, for the sake of the ungrateful people, going to the places of demoniac enemies such as rāvaṇa et al who harm the harmless people, as said in perumāḷ tirumoḻi 9.5 “*porundār kai vēl nudi pōl paraṟpāya melladigaḷ kurudi sōra – virumbāda kān virumbi*” (desiring the undesirable forest where the sharp stones would tear his tender feet to let the blood flow out from there) and perumāḷ tirumoḻi 9.2 “*evvāṟu nadandanai em irāmāvō*” (Oh my dear rāma! how did you walk in the forest?). Subsequently, when he mercifully stood victorious at the entrance of lankā, all the dēvas starting with brahmā arrived there and said as in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 117.29 “*tadidam na: krutam kāryam – prahruśtō divamākrama:*” (purpose of your birth is accomplished – return to your divine abode with joy) – indicating “Your highness have fulfilled our prayers without seeing our lowliness; now, you can return to your splendorous abode”; at that time rudra said “the whole of śrī ayōdyā is greatly suffering in separation from you; you should return to śrī ayōdyā and spend some loving time with your divine mothers, divine brothers and the residents of the sacred abode and protect them”; “*nāttai aḷittu*” implies [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s loving reign of his kingdom stretching for eleven thousand years as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 4.8.5](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/03/thiruvaimozhi-4-8-5-thalir-niraththal/) “*kadal jñālattu aḷi mikkān*” (with great compassion towards the world surrounded by ocean). Due to this reason,vālmikī maharishi called the three-eyed rudra as in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 117.3 “*śadarda nayanaśrīmān*” (the three-eyed śrīmān (wealthy person)) \[here the wealth in him was to desire for emperumān’s presence in this world, beyond the selfish interest of dēvas\]; otherwise, there is no reason to call a *bhikśuka* (mendicant) as śrīmān.
- *uyyac ceydu* – this is talking about how emperumān cared for them \[the residents of śrī ayōdyā\] for a long time being together to make them unsustainable in his absence and took them along \[to paramapadam\] instead of leaving them behind, and uplifted everyone.
- *nadandamai kēttumē* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is talking about perumāḷ taking everyone along with him as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam uttara kāṇḍam 109.22 “*tiryak yōni gatāścāpi sarvē rāmamanuvratā:*” (all the animals followed śrī rāma), “*vivēśa vaiṣṇavam tējas saśarīrassahānuka:*” ([emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) ascended to paramapadam with a spiritual form along with the residents of śrī ayōdyā). [kulaśēkarāḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/kulasekarazhwar/) has mercifully eliminated all doubts about the place where they reached; taking them along to paramapadam as said in perumāḷ tirumoḻi 10.10 “*anṟu sarāsarangaḷai vaigundattēṟṟi*” (lifting all the mobile and stationary entities to śrīvaikuṇṭam on that day \[when he ascended there\]).
- *nadandamai kēttumē* – Even after hearing this travelogue. That is taking along those who are hungry \[for bhagavat viśayam\] and helpless \[in attaining him\]. The companion for the pilgrimage is “*puṇḍarīkākśa nāma sankīrtanāmrutam*” (the nectarean names of lotus eyed lord). ṭravelling along saying as in jitantē stōtram 1″*jitantē puṇḍarīkākśa*” (lotus eyed lord has won us over). It is said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 35.8 “*rāma: kamalapatrākśa:*” (śrī rāma who has eyes like lotus petals). Would one not become the servitor of nārāyaṇa even after hearing how he uplifted everyone as śrī rāma? In the previous pāsuram, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) said that [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) descended and captivated the samsāris (materialistic people) who were engaged in worldly pleasures and who would hear about sarvēśvara from anyone \[without proper analysis of the principle/source\], with his beauty and qualities and transformed them to be fully dependent on him; in this pāsuram – was that great? After transforming someone to be totally dependent on him and leaving them behind, is as good as being a cruel murderer; instead of doing that, the quality of taking them along with him and protecting them is such a great quality – says āḻvār.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

adiyen saraty ramanuja dasan

## 7.5.3. Ketpargal kesavan

*kētpārgaḷ kēsavan kīrtti allāl maṟṟum kētparō kētpār sevi sudu kīḻmai vasavugaḷē vaiyum sētpāl paḻam pagaivan sisupālan tiruvadi tāḷ pāl adainda tanmai aṟivārai aṟindumē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kētpār sevi – for the ears of those who are desirous to hear about defects in bhagavān’s qualities; sudu – to cause burning sensation of fire; kīḻmai – causing lowliness; vasavugaḷē – saying harsh words; vaiyum – scolding; sētpāl – from distant past; paḻam pagaivan – being an age-old enemy; sisupālan – śiśupāla; tiruvadi – the unconditional lord, kriṣṇa, his; tāḷ pāl – at divine feet; adainda – attained sāyujyam (eternal togetherness); tanmai – distinguished nature; aṟivārai – those very wise persons; aṟindum – even after knowing; kētpārgaḷ – those who are supposed to be hearing (about the path for salvation); kēsavan – kriṣṇa, the killer of kēśi (the demoniac horse), his; kīrtti – greatness (of liberating the one who kept committing offenses birth after birth); allāl – other than; maṟṟum – any other entity who liberated those who did not avoid his help; kētparō – will they hear?

**Перевод:**

**śiśupāla, an age-old enemy from distant past kept saying lowly, harsh words and scolded kriṣṇa, the unconditional lord, to cause burning sensation for the ears of even those who are desirous to hear about defects in bhagavān’s qualities; \[yet\] he attained sāyujyam at the divine feet of such kriṣṇa; even after knowing those very wise persons who know the distinguished nature of kriṣṇa, will those who are supposed to be hearing (about salvation), hear the greatness of any other entity who liberated those who did not avoid his help, than that of kriṣṇa, the killer of kēśi?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the third pāsuram, āḻvār is meditating upon emperumān‘s acceptance of śiśupāla which is greater than bringing along those who don’t think about anything other than emperumān himself.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār explains emperumān‘s greatness of liberating śiśupāla who performs unfavourable acts, beyond just eliminating the unfavourable aspects and protecting \[the followers\].*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Third pāsuram. āḻvār says “Will those who have heard and known about emperumān‘s great compassion of even accepting śiśupāla at his divine feet, hear anything other than the glories of kēśi hantā (kriṣṇa who killed kēśi)?” kētpārgaḷ kēsavan kīrtti allāl maṟṟum kētparō kētpār sevi sudu kīḻmai vasavugaḷē vaiyum sētpāl paḻam pagaivan sisupālan tiruvadi tāḷ pāl adainda tanmai aṟivārai aṟindumē*

- *kētpārgaḷ* – Previously, āḻvār said “*kaṟparō*” (will they learn?). That is, to ensure that he is firmly placed in the heart, in the beginning, during the course and at the end; now, hearing means when someone who has him firmly placed in his heart \[ācārya\] instructs, faithfully pondering upon it and accepting it. Though one may not have full clarity in the heart during the course of time, at the end, the result will be the same for both \[the ācārya who instructs and the śiśya who hears\]. Even if one is not learned, at least he should have heard it \[kuṟaḷ 414 reflects this same meaning\]. Being faithful upon hearing what was learnt and fully understood. Though one is not fully learned and not engaged in the kainkaryam which is the culmination of such learning, at least if one hears these principles from an ācārya, it will help when one is in danger. Now \[during the course of time here\], the loss for self is to be unable to explain these principles to others and not having full clarity in the heart.
- *kētpārgaḷ* – One who has an opening in the ear \[i.e. everyone\]. The only purpose of ears is to hear bhagavat viśayam; it is said in periya tirumoḻi 11.7.2 “*kēḷāc cevigaḷ ceviyalla kēttōmē*” (we have heard that, those ears which do not hear bhagavat viśayam, are not considered as ears); it is only like a rat hole.
- *kēsavan kīrtti allāl* – Would they hear the glories of anyone other than kriṣṇa who is the eliminator of enemies? He did not wait until becoming a youth to eliminate the enemies; right from the toddler stage he started eliminating enemies such as pūtanā et al. He did not eliminate the enemies intentionally, but it was an act of sustaining himself. Poison kills not due to having knowledge \[it is just its nature\]. śrī viṣṇu purāṇam 5.16.14 “*vyāditāsyō mahāraudras sōsura kriṣṇabāhunā …*” (having widely open mouth, and looking very frightening, the demon horse fell down being torn apart by kriṣṇa, like a tree felled by thunder strike) – kēśi had his mouth open and appeared to instill fear on those who saw him. Toddlers usually place their hand in any hole, playfully. In that manner, kriṣṇa stretched his hand into its mouth, and due to the new experience, the hand grew; at that time, kēśi fell down in two pieces like a tree which was struck down by thunder.
- *maṟṟum kētparō* – Would they even listen to the incidents of śrī rāma’s life which was explained previously? How amazing is āḻvār’s nature! Previously he said “*irāma pirānai allāl maṟṟum kaṟparō*” (would one learn anyone other than śrī rāma, the benefactor?) Here, he is saying “kēsavan kīrtti allāl maṟṟum kētparō”; what is the reason for this? When āḻvār enjoys rāmāvatāram he says in [tiruvāimoḻi 3.6.8](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/09/thiruvaimozhi-3-6-8-thuyarame-tharu/) “*tayaradaṟku magan tannai anṟi maṟṟilēn tanjamāga*” (other than such śrī rāma, who appeared as the son of daśarati cakravarti, I will not have any one, even another form of [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/), as my refuge); when he enjoys kriṣṇāvatāram he says in [tiruvāimoḻi 2.2.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/01/thiruvaimozhi-2-2-1-thinnan-vidu/) ” *nam kaṇṇan kaṇṇallatu illai ōr kaṇṇē*” (kriṣṇa is the supreme controller for the universe and there is no other controlling entity that exists); in this manner, he is the only one who is capable of immersing in the particular incarnation he enjoys. Just as when one immerses in one quality of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), he cannot pursue other qualities of same emperumān, when one immerses in a particular incarnation, he cannot pursue other incarnations as well.
- *kētpār sevi sudu kīḻmai vasavugaḷē vaiyum* – Here, it is not explained in the same way as “*kētpār*” was explained previously \[i.e. as all those who have ears\]; here, this means, those who are interested to hear the lowly scoldings only. Speaking such harsh words that even those lowly people who would pay to accuse bhagavān, would become disturbed, would close their ears and say “You are speaking so harshly; you cannot speak like this”.
- *vasavugaḷē vaiyum* – Even the followers of emperumān, due to being associated with a \[material\] body and due to forgetfulness, would sometimes engage in unfavourable acts; similarly, would he sometimes, accidentally say a good word? With the “*ēvakāram*” \[i.e. the long syllable *E* in *vasavugaḷ****E***\], it is emphasised that, there is no such possibility.

The reason for this is explained further.

- *sētpāl paḻam pagaivan* – Having great enmity right from his birth; not just this birth, even from previous births, he has been an enemy; there is no end to the offenses he committed in every birth; there were many such births. Due to long standing enmity, the lengthy duration of each of such births and the abundance of offenses committed in those births are considered. Even if he is speaking unknowingly, due to his vāsanā (inclination), it will end up being offensive only.  A new born calf will itself seek the udder of the mother cow, due to the inclination from previous births; similarly, his enmity in this birth is due to the inclination from previous births.
- *tiruvadi tāḷ pāl adainda* – Attained proximity to the divine feet of sarvasvāmi (lord of all). It is defining the nature of sāyujya mōkśam. That is to engage in eternal kainkaryam, without any break, being in close proximity of the divine feet. sāyujya does not mean merging of ātmā and brahmam – that \[principle of merging\] is not what is explained in muṇḍaka upaniśat 3.2 “*brahma vēdam brahmaiva bhavati*” (one who knows brahmam, becomes similar to that), muṇḍaka upaniśat 3.1.3 “*paramam sāmyam upaiti*” (he attains supreme equivalence), periya tirumoḻi 11.3.5 “*tammaiyē nāḷum vaṇangit toḻuvārkku tammaiyē okka aruḷ seyvar*” ([emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)  will bless those who worship him to become similar to him), [śrī bhagavat gītā 14.2](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/14-2/) “*mama sādarmyam āgatā:*” (having attained equanimity with me) and bōdāyana vrutti “*samānō jyōtiśā*” (Similar to paramātmā); instead it speaks about the equivalence in the resulting enjoyment between emperumān and the ātmā; since it is said in brahma sūtram 4.4.17 “*jagat vyāpāra varjam*” (they (nityas, muktas) have all capabilities except engaging in activities related to material realm) and brahma sūtram 4.4.21 “*bhōga mātra sāmya lingātca*” (Having similar identity in enjoyment only), sāyujyam does not mean as in [rāmānusa nūṟṟandādi 58](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/11/ramanusa-nurranthadhi-58/) “*avanōdu onṟām*” (becoming one with  him), but it means “serving his divine feet” as it is also said in parama samhitā “*sāyujyam pratipannāyē tīvra bhaktāstapasvina: \| kinkarā mama tē nityam bhavanti nirubatravā:*” (Those great devotees, who performed upāsana and who became uplifted attaining equivalence with me, will be freed from all hurdles and will always be my servitors).
- *tanmai aṟivārai aṟindumē* – Identifies the target for those who should hear. Will those who know persons with such knowledge and hear from them, hear anything other than kēśava’s glories? How did śiśupāla attain [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s divine feet? He angrily shouted saying the divine names, and could have remembered the beautiful posture of emperumān with his divine chakra in his hand, at the final moment \[before being killed by kriṣṇa using his chakra\]. If we superficially analyse, we could highlight some reasons in this manner. If we try to highlight a reason for this, that will minimize the greatness of his krupā (mercy). āḻvārs, riśis and everyone would explain “śiśupāla attained sarvēśvaran’s divine feet by his grace”. Even if he acquires up to parama bhakti (ultimate state before liberation), veren’t the faculties given by īśvaran himself? As even this reason becomes irrelevant, it is not meant for us to try and highlight a non-existing reason. \[Another view point on śiśupāla’s attaining mōkśam\] āḷavandār mercifully said “śiśupālan did not get liberated”. When asked “How do you say that?’, he mercifully replied “since he did not have the means \[i.e. desire\] to go to paramapadam; to stop him from harming the world, emperumān picked him up and threw him into a corner \[of paramapadam, as a criminal would be banished and thrown out from the kingdom\]”. Here it is simply saying that the vastness of emperumān’s qualities \[mainly krupā\] will become minimized, if we say that śiśupāla angrily recited emperumān’s divine names and hence got mōkśam, or kākāsura was pardoned due to falling at his divine feet, since it is said in śrīrangarājastavam 3.97 “*balibhuji śiśupālē tādrugākaskarē vā guṇalavasahavāsāt tvatkśamā sankucantī*” (Your patience which became minimised due to some good aspects in kākāsura and śiśupāla). periyāḻvār too said in 4.3.5 “*pala pala nāḻam sollip paḻitta sisupālan tannai – alaivalaimai tavirtta aḻagan*” (The beautiful emperumān who eliminated the blabbering of śiśupāla who accused emperumān in many ways). tiruccanda viruttam 111 “*vaidu ninnai vallavā paḻittavarkkum*” (attainable even for the one accused you with faults). The greatness in this pāsuram – Is it great to say that śrī rāma took along those who could not live without him or is it great to say that emperumān gave the same result to even śiśupāla who committed grave offense against him?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.5.4. Tanmai aribavar

*tanmai aṟibavar tām avaṟkāḷ anṟi āvarō? panmaip padar poruḷ ādumil pāḻ nedum kālattu nanmaip punal paṇṇi nānmuganaip paṇṇit tan uḷḷē tonmai mayakkiya tōṟṟiya sūḻalgaḷ sindittē*

**Пословный перевод:**

panmai – having variations such as dēva (celestial beings) etc; padar – expansive in the form of puṇya (virtues) and pāpa (vices); poruḷ – entities; ādum – any; il – not present; pāḻ – remained as śūnya (void); nedum kālattu – for a long period stretching thousand catur yugas; nanmai – having goodness (of being together with other bhūtas \[creations\] and being the cause for subsequent creation); punal – causal water; paṇṇi – created (as said in “apa Eva sa sarjātau“); (as per “tadaṇḍamabhavatddaimam – tasminjajñē svayam brahmā“, in the oval shaped universe which was created in that water); nānmuganai – brahmā; paṇṇi – created; tonmai – to erase the previous inclinations; than uḷḷē – in a small portion of his svarūpam (true nature); mayakkiya – (as said in “ēkībhavati“) all the entities which were in a subdued state inside him; tōṟṟiya – (through creation, to become manifold) created; sūḻalgaḷ – ways/efforts (such as merciful glance, creation, pervading, giving name and form etc); sindittu – meditated (through vēdānta); tanmai – his nature (distinguished identity, of being the cause); aṟibavar – those who know; tām – their; avaṟku – for kriṣṇa, who is the cause of universe (as said in “kriṣṇa Eva hi lōkānām utpatti:“); anṟi – other than; āḷ āvarō – will they become servitor?

**Перевод:**

**When none of the entities which are expansive in the form of puṇya and pāpa, having variations such as dēva etc is present and everything remained void for a long period stretching thousand catur yugas, emperumān created water which is having goodness, and then brahmā and subsequently created all the entities which were in a subdued state inside him in a small portion of his svarūpam, having erased the previous inclinations; having meditated upon the ways/efforts of his nature, will they \[materialistic people\] become a servitor of anyone other than kriṣṇa, who is the cause of universe?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fourth pāsuram, āḻvār is meditating upon emperumān‘s great quality of recreating the universe after it was in a subdued state with the \[collective\] offenses \[of everyone\] during deluge, which makes his quality of accepting śiśupāla, who already existed, with his transgressions, look inferior.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār mercifully meditates upon his greatness of recreating the universe which became subdued.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. There are many samsāris who are equal to śiśupāla. tanmai aṟibavar tām avaṟkāḷ anṟi āvarō? panmaip padar poruḷ ādumil pāḻ nedum kālattu nanmaip punal paṇṇi nānmuganaip paṇṇit than uḷḷē tonmai mayakkiya tōṟṟiya sūḻalgaḷ sindittē*

- *tanmai aṟibavar tām* – Those who know the nature of truth. That is, those who understand that this creation is for his purpose; similar to śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 40-5 “*sruśtatvam vanavāsāya*” (you were sired by me only to follow śrī rāma to the forest). Those who know that the cause of the universe is the one to be meditated upon; it is said in cāndōjña upaniśat “*kāraṇam tu dyēya:*” (meditate upon the origin/cause); in brahma sūtram too, after saying in 1.1.1 “*atātō brahma jijñāsā*” (then, one enquires into brahmam), the riśi said in 1.1.2 “*janmādi asya yata:*” (that which is the cause for creation etc).
- *avaṟku āḷ anṟi āvarō* – He gave the senses and body, only to use them in his service.
- *panmaip padar poruḷ ādum il pāḻ nedum kālattu* – being manifold, differentiated by being dēva etc \[dēva, manuśya, tiryak, stāvara\], having entities which are expansive due to their karma; during the time when such variations don’t exist for a very long time. īśvaran will annihilate the universe and keep it void for a long time just to hear the sound of voidness. Just as a farmer will store water on a field for a long time, to eliminate the saltiness in the cultivable land, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) will keep them \[various sentient and insentient entities\] in their subtle forms to eliminate the evil inclinations, for the same duration that was spent in manifested \[created\] state \[While brahmā’s day is engaged in creation, his nights are quiet, with no such activity\]. In that time, when there is not even a small piece of matter, as far as one can see, and everything is in the state of “sat” (existence only).
- *nanmaip punal paṇṇi* – This is not like the water during deluge. As said in manu smruti “*apa Eva sasarjātau*“ (first, he created water). Until then, he directly engages with acit \[this state of samaśti sruśti, where emperumān performs advāraka sruśti, direct creation; subsequently he creates sadvāraka sruśti, variegated creation, through others\] and thinks “now that these two work according to my will, let me engage cit too in creation”, and creates brahmā \[i.e. selects the most pious ātmā and gives him the post of brahmā\]. Both cit and acit are subservient to [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) as said in “*yasya ātmā śarīram*” (All ātmās are my bodies), “*yasya prutivī śarīram*” (this material nature is my body) and so on. Like those who say “he has made a doll” \[effortless accomplishment\], as said in śvētāsvatara upaniśat “*yō brahmāṇam vitadādi pūrvam*” (one who created brahmā first), “*nanmaip punal paṇṇi, nānmuganaip paṇṇi*“.
- *than uḷḷē* – In a tiny fraction of his divine will.
- *tonmai …* – Back then, how he encompassed everything to be implied by the term “*sadēva*” (sat only) and subsequently, engaged in creation as said in taittirīya upaniśat “*bahu syām*” (let me become many) and the ways through which he manifested. Will those who know his true nature, become servitor of anyone other than kriṣṇa? tanmai – uṇmai (truth). punal (water) is representative of other elements. tōṟṟiya – created.

Previous pāsuram stated that he gave his divine feet to his enemy śiśupāla – is this great? ōr is his greatness of having simplicity \[magnanimity\] to create the enemies and let them trouble himself, great?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.5.5. Sulalgal sindikkil

*sūḻalgaḷ sindikkil māyan kaḻal anṟic cūḻvarō? āḻap perum punal tannuḷ aḻundiya jñālattai tāḻap padāmal tan pāl oru kōttidait tān koṇḍa kēḻal tiru uru āyiṟṟuk kēttum uṇarndumē*

**Пословный перевод:**

peru – boundless; punal than uḷ – in the ocean \[water\] of deluge; āḻa – deep at the shell of the universe; aḻundiya – submerged; jñālattai – earth; tāḻap padāmal – not to lose its form, due to the delay in time; than pāl – a small area in his divine form; ōr kōttidai – on the tusk; koṇḍa – (dug it out and) kept; kēḻal – śrī varāha as said in “kōla varāham” (beautiful boar); tiru – beautiful; uru – form; āyiṟṟu – one who is having; kēttum – even after hearing through vēdam, itihāsa, purāṇa etc; uṇarndum – even after meditating upon; sūḻalgaḷ – noble paths which will be the means for salvation; sindikkil – when thinking to analyse; māyan – the one with the varāha form, who performs amazing acts (as said in tiruviruttam 99 “jñānap pirānai allāl illai nān kaṇḍa nalladuvē“, helping during the danger of deluge and also the one who uplifts us from the ocean of samsāra); kaḻal – divine feet; anṟi – other than; sūḻvarō – will consider as refuge?

**Перевод:**

**emperumān appeared in the beautiful form of śrī varāha as said in “kōla varāham“, dug out the earth, not to lose its form due to the delay in time, which went deep down to the shell of the universe, being submerged in the boundless ocean of deluge, with his tusk which is a small area in his divine form and kept it there. Even after hearing about this through vēdam, itihāsa, purāṇa etc and even after mediating upon the noble paths which will be the means for salvation, when thinking to analyse, will one consider as refuge anything other than the divine feet of the one with the varāha form, who performs amazing acts?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fifth pāsuram, āḻvār is meditating upon the great quality of emperumān who assumed the form of an animal \[boar\] as per the need and saved the earth instead of abandoning it thinking “let me create a new universe like this”,  when the universe, created by him, was consumed by deluge.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār mercifully explains the incident of śrī varāha, who is the friend-in-need, who transformed himself to save the earth, beyond recreating the universe after deluge.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. sūḻalgaḷ sindikkil māyan kaḻal anṟic cūḻvarō? āḻap perum punal tannuḷ aḻundiya jñālattai tāḻap padāmal than pāl oru kōttidait tān koṇḍa kēḻal tiru uru āyiṟṟuk kēttum uṇarndumē*

- *sūḻalgaḷ sindikkil* – When thinking about the means to eliminate self-dependence and to be uplifted. \[Alternative explanation\] When thinking about the means to fulfil one’s desires.

(There are many upāyams (means), but for an adiyān (servitor), the scope is limited to adi \[his tiruvadigaḷ – divine feet\])

- *māyan kaḻal anṟic cūḻvarō* – When all the entities to be protected are together \[in a helpless state\], [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) will ignore about caring for himself and will focus on protecting others. Will they seek as refuge anything other than such emperumān’s divine feet?
- *āḻap perum punal than uḷ aḻundiya jñālattai* – Saying “earth being submerged in deep ocean”, “deeply submerged in the vast ocean”.
- *aḻundiya jñālattai* – The earth which went and got stuck to the wall of the universe.
- *tāḻap padāmal* – not to hit the ocean bed; not to lose its form. After having submerged inside and losing some portions, not desiring to lose the existence itself.
- *than pāl oru kōttidait tān koṇḍa* – One who kept the expansive universe on his tusk like a blue gem; placing the earth in a small area on his tusk. Just as a generous person will cook for hundred persons while desiring to feed only forty persons, the tusk is so great that it is much larger than what is to be protected; instead of protecting through someone else, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) protected the earth himself.
- *tān koṇḍa* – It was not done by him as a result of a prayer from the earth which was losing its portions \[done by him on his own desire\].
- *kēḻal tiru uru āyiṟṟu* – The form emperumān assumed to cause disrepute to himself, became so beautiful that one has to ward-off evil eyes. As emperumān cares less for his appearance for the protection of his devotees, that itself gives him more radiance; as said in nācciyār tirumoḻi 11.8 “*mānam ilāp panṟiyām tēsu*” (radiance due to his assuming the form of a humble pig). “*māsudambil nīr vārā*” (muddy water dripping from his dirty form) – assuming a form, where all the dirt is on his body. “*mānam ilāp panṟiyām”* – his supremacy is not even visible slightly. [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is having such internal emotions that when other pigs get closer to him, and smell him, they become convinced that “this is one among our herd”. When mārīca assumed the form of the mystical deer, other deer which smelt it, ran away sensing the demoniac smell. “*panṟiyām tēsudaiya dēvar*” – Had he not assumed this form, he would have lost all the hard earned radiance/fame. The greatness of lowering himself which is greater than presenting himself for the nityasūris in paramapadam.
- *kēttum uṇarndumē* – Will those who analyse the means, by hearing and meditating, surrender unto anything other than the divine feet of māyan (amazing [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/))? In comparison to giving up his own divine form and assuming a lowly form, to save the earth which was consumed by deluge, is the act of creating the universe with his divine vow, without minimising any of his qualities such as being the cause of the universe etc, a match?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.5.6. Kettum unarndavar

*kēttum uṇarndavar kēsavaṟkāḷ anṟi āvarō? vāttamilā vaṇ kai māvali vādikka vādippuṇḍu īttam koḷ dēvargaḷ senṟirandārkkidar nīkkiya kōttam kai vāmananāyc ceyda kūttukkaḷ kaṇḍumē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vāttam ilā – never diminishing; vaṇ – having magnanimity; kai – having hand; māvali – mahābali; vādikka – (out of pride) torment; vādippuṇḍu – suffered; īttam koḷ – grouped together, without any enmity between each other; dēvargaḷ – dēvas, who are generous; senṟu – went (where emperumān was mercifully seated); irandārkku – those who surrendered through their prayers (as said in “śaraṇam tvām anuprāptā:“); idar nīkkiya – eliminating the sorrow in their mind (by vowing to act); kōdu – due to accepting alms; am – acquiring beauty; kai – having hand; vāmananāy – attracting him with his vāmana (dwarf) form; seyda – performed; kūttukkaḷ – acts; kaṇḍum – meditating as if seeing physically; kēttum – hearing (this incident, through purāṇas etc); uṇarndavar – those who are sentient; kēsavaṟku – for vāmana who is having beautiful locks of hair which are elegantly swaying; anṟi – other than; āḷ – servitor; āvarō – will they become?

**Перевод:**

**The generous dēvas, having suffered by the torment of mahābali, who has never diminishing magnanimous hand, grouped together, without any enmity between each other, went to emperumān and surrendered to him through their prayers; eliminating the sorrow in their mind, emperumān having a hand which acquired beauty due to accepting alms, attracting mahābali with his vāmana (dwarf) form, performed acts; will those sentient beings who are meditating as if seeing physically, and hearing these acts, become servitor for anyone other than vāmana who is having beautiful locks of hair which are elegantly swaying? kēsavan (kēśava) also means the master of brahmā and rudra, with one \[brahmā\] washing his divine feet and the other \[rudra\] accepting that holy water on his head.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the sixth pāsuram, āḻvār is meditating upon the great quality of emperumān giving up his supremacy and accepting alms, which is greater than previously enjoyed qualities and the act of mercifully digging out the earth with his ability.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār mercifully speaks about emperumān‘s artitva sāmartyam (ability to seek alms), where he has lowered his natural quality \[supremacy\] which is beyond just assuming a humble form.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. kēttum uṇarndavar kēsavaṟkāḷ anṟi āvarō? vāttamilā vaṇ kai māvali vādikka vādippuṇḍu īttam koḷ dēvargaḷ senṟirandārkkidar nīkkiya kōttam kai vāmananāyc ceyda kūttukkaḷ kaṇḍumē*

- *kēttum uṇarndavar* – When an ācāryan instructs a meaning, hearing that and remaining with clarity as said in “*ēvam jñātvā bhavitum arhati*” (after knowing that, acting accordingly).
- *kēsavaṟku āḷ anṟi āvarō* – Would they become servitor of anyone other than the one who became the refuge, without letting anyone else to be the refuge? kēśava means as in mahābhāratam harivamśam “*ka iti brahmaṇō nāma īśōham sarva dēhinām \| āvām tavāngē sambhūtau tasmāt kēśava nāmavān \|\|*” (both of us, brahmā (ka) and rudra (īśa), originated from the divine body of your highness; thus you are called kēśava” and due to having beautiful locks.
- *vāttam ilā vaṇ kai* – Instead of giving and withdrawing after sometime, the hand which keeps giving. [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) did not severe his \[mahābali’s\] head like he did to rāvaṇa et al since there is a reason \[of mahābali being magnanimous\].
- *māvali vādikka vādippuṇḍu* – Having this \[magnanimity\] as the reason, he tormented the dēvas and they suffered.
- *īttam koḷ dēvargaḷ* – Like village-heads, they will not tolerate one another’s greatness, and are of the nature that one person \[rudra\] severs another person’s head and another person \[brahmā\] has his head severed; as great danger loomed, such envious people gave up their pride, came together and fell at the divine feet of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/).
- *senṟu irandārkku idar nīkkiya* – \[reason for “senṟu” – they went to emperumān, is explained here\] When maṇiyakārar (administrative chief) is in the temple, he would think “what is wrong if the īśvaran (lord) himself has to come to me?”; similarly, these dēvas think “everyone should come to us”, but the great danger which was looming, made them unite and come here – thinking like this in his divine heart, emperumān eliminated their sorrow. \[Would the dēvas think like that?\] When [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) broke a weak bow, the dēvas thought him to be great as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam bāla kāṇḍam 75.19 “*adikam mē nirē viṣṇum*” (they thought viṣṇu to be superior to rudra); at other times they remain as said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 16-14](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/16-14/) “*īśvarōham*” (I am the controller of everything). When such dēvas come begging, emperumān eliminated their sorrow.
- *kōttam kai vāmananāy* – Having beautifully cupped hands to accept the water; as said in nācciyār tirumoḻi 11.5 “*pollāk kuṟaḷ uruvāy poṟkaiyil nīrēṟṟu*” (in the form of a beautiful dwarf, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) accepted water in his golden hands), since mahābali is troubling the dēvas, he should be killed; but since he has noble qualities, emperumān won’t kill him; so, emperumān, the protector, should find out an apt means to satisfy both situations. poṟkai – hand which acquired beauty. Beautiful hand. The hand which grew, by giving; as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 21.7 “*gō sahasra pradātāram*” (the hand which grew, by donating thousands of cows) and in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 33.25 “*dadyān na pratigruhṇīyāt*” (perumāḷ (śrī rāma) would give but not accept any charity).
- *seyda kūttukkaḷ kaṇḍumē* – For [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/), his ([emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) as vāmana) acts of being born on one day, growing up on the same day, setting out to seek alms on the same day, and going all the way to the sacrificial arena of mahābali, walking in a tense manner to cause disturbance to the earth and entering there, standing there humbly with kriṣṇājinam (deer skin), yajñōpavīdam (sacred thread) and munji (darbā grass) and asking childishly “I will accept”, and showing little feet but measuring with huge feet etc appear like dance by expert dancers. In comparison to his simplicity of becoming an alms-seeker while having all the supremacy and being śriya:pati (husband of śrī mahālakśmi), to protect his followers, is protecting the earth from the deluge, a match?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.5.7. Kandum telindum

*kaṇḍum teḷindum kaṟṟār kaṇṇaṟkāḷ anṟi āvarō? vaṇḍuṇ malart tongal mārakkaṇḍēyanukku vāḻu nāḷ iṇḍaic cadai mudi īsanudan koṇḍusāc cella koṇḍangut tannodum koṇḍu udan cenṟaduṇarndumē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vaṇḍu – beetles; uṇ – drinking honey from; malar – having flower; tongal – due to wearing garland; mārkkaṇḍēyanukku – for mārkaṇḍēya; vāḻu nāḷ – the time of salvation; iṇḍai – garland which indicates his being the enjoyer; sadai mudi – having matted hair which indicates his being the upāsaka (one who is pursuing the means); īsan – rudra who considers himself to be the lord; udan – together; koṇḍu – took along; usā – to mingle with emperumān who is greater than all; sella – went; angu – in that situation; koṇḍu – considering (him to be protected in his divine heart); tannodum – with self; koṇḍu – taking along; udan – not to separate, forever; senṟadu – the manner in which it was done; uṇarndumē – learning through purāṇa etc; kaṇḍum – visibly seeing the greatness of emperumān over other dēvatās; teḷindum – acquiring clarity as said in “adikam mē nirē viṣṇu:”; kaṟṟār – those who have the knowledge acquired through distinguished personalities; kaṇṇaṟku – sarvēśvara who causes joy; anṟi – other than; āḷ – servitor; āvarō – will they become?

**Перевод:**

**Youthful mārkaṇḍēya wearing flower garland from which beetles drink honey, was a vorśipper of rudra who considers himself to be the lord, wearing garland which indicates his being the enjoyer and is having having matted hair which indicates his being the upāsaka; at the time of \[seeking\] salvation, rudra took mārkaṇḍēya along with him to mingle with emperumān who is greater than all; in that situation, emperumān took mārkaṇḍēya along, not to separate from him, forever; will those who learned through purāṇa etc the manner in which it was done, who have visibly seen the greatness of emperumān over other dēvatās, who have acquired clarity as said in “adikam mē nirē viṣṇu:” and have the knowledge acquired through distinguished personalities, become the servitor of anyone other than sarvēśvara who causes joy?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the seventh pāsuram, āḻvār is meditating upon the distinguished quality of emperumān’s acceptance of mārkaṇḍēya who is a devotee of dēvatāntaram (other dēvatā, rudra) and is to be discarded for that, which is greater than his being śriya:pati yet fulfilled the desires of his devotees even by seeking alms.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. kaṇḍum teḷindum kaṟṟār kaṇṇaṟkāḷ anṟi āvarō? vaṇḍuṇ malart tongal mārakkaṇḍēyanukku vāḻu nāḷ iṇḍaic cadai mudi īsanudan koṇḍusāc cella koṇḍangut tannodum koṇḍu udan cenṟaduṇarndumē*

- *kaṇḍum teḷindum kaṟṟār* – (kaṟṟu – teḷindu – kaṇḍār (learn – have clarity – see)) Learning in a disciplined manner from a person (ācarya) and having clarity in that, will ensure that sākśātkāram (true visualisation) is attained. śravaṇa (hearing), manana (meditation) will naturally lead to true visualisation.
- *kaṇṇaṟku āḷ anṟi āvarō* – Will those who are intent on meditating, move away from the real target of such meditation \[i.e. emperumān\]?
- *vaṇḍu uṇ malar …* – Saying “For the salvation of śrī mārkaṇḍēya who is wearing a garland from which the beetles are drinking honey”; also, should be read as “*vāḻu nāḷ usāc cella*” (to spend the remaining time together). The parents of mārkaṇḍēya decorated him and let him play outside, at that time a voice from the sky announced “he will die soon”, and the parents became very anguished. mārkaṇḍēya said to his parents “Do not fear, I will take care of this” and went and surrendered to rudra. rudra accepted his service until the day when death arrived for mārkaṇḍēya. rudra, feeling uneasy about the situation, shut the front doors and the back doors, spread out his matted hair and told mārkaṇḍēya “Look, I am also in the same situation as you; you saw my garland \[and considered me as a dēvatā\], instead of seeing my matted hair \[which indicates I am also a upāsaka (one who is praying)\]” and further said “as you served for long, you cannot be left in a helpless situation; let me show you the refuge” and took him to sarvēśvaran, while sharing emperumān’s qualities such as saulabhyam (simplicity) etc with him.
- *koṇḍu angu* – Feeling pity in his divine heart thinking “Alas! You came fearing for death!”, not looking down upon him thinking “was he brought along by this prideful person \[rudra\]!”, he accepted him as he would accept those who were recommended by pirātti. Also explained as “*nenjil koṇḍu*” (accepting mārkaṇḍēya in his heart).
- *tannodum koṇḍu* – Fulfilled the purpose he came for and subsequently gave sāmyāpatti (equivalence with him).
- *udan senṟadu uṇarndumē* – He took mārkaṇḍēya along with him just as he took [parakāla nāyaki (tirumangai āḻvār in feminine mood)](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/thirumangai-azhwar/) as explained in periya tirumoḻi 3.7 “*kaḷvan kol*“. As said in periya tirumoḻi 5.8.4 “*pinnai enṟum nin tiruvadip piriyā vaṇṇam eṇṇiya*” (How you thought about keeping me at your divine feet without ever getting separated), not to consider him as a “separate person”, he let mārkaṇḍēya enjoy the bliss along with him – having this in the mind.

Will those who have seen, have clarity and learnt about it, become servitor of anyone other than kriṣṇa? \[a nice summary by nampiḷḷai\] Is it so great to lower himself for indra who surrendered to him? While emperumān said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 7.14](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/7-14/) “*mām Eva yē prapadyantē māyām ētām taranti tē*” (Only those who surrender unto me will cross over this material nature/realm \[by my grace\]), mārkaṇḍēya vorśipped other dēvatā \[rudra\]. Further, had rudra as puruśakāram (recommendation authority), since emperumān had the quality of saulabhyam (easy approacability). emperumān thought “What could he \[rudra\] do! instead of abandoning the one who surrendered unto him, at least he showed me and protected mārkaṇḍēya”. Associating with those who have tamō guṇam will lead to abandonment by emperumān; associating with those who have satva guṇam will lead to acceptance by emperumān; while this is the case, even while mārkaṇḍēya approached emperumān through rudra \[who has tamō guṇam\], he was uplifted. How amazing!

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.5.8. Sella unarndavar

*sella uṇarndavar selvan tan sīr anṟik kaṟparō? ellai ilāda perum tavattāl pala seymiṟai allal amararaic ceyyum iraṇiyan āgattai mallal ari uruvāyc ceyda māyam aṟindumē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ellai ilāda – boundless; perum tavattāl – with great tapasyās (penances); pala – various ways; sey – made; miṟai – causing trouble to the world; amararai – for dēvas who grant results; allal – sorrow; seyyum – giving; iraṇiyan – hiraṇya’s; āgattai – body; mallal – huge as said in “mahāviṣṇum”; ari uruvāy – assuming narasimha form; seyda – effortlessly tore; māyam – amazing act; aṟindum – even after learning from pramāṇams (authentic texts); sella – to go up to the boundary of his partiality towards his followers which is the essence of that incarnation; uṇarndavar – those who realise; selvan than – the śrīmān who has narasimha form; sīr – the glorious, valorous history; anṟi – other than; kaṟparō – will they learn?

**Перевод:**

**emperumān, assuming the huge narasimha form as said in “mahāviṣṇum“, effortlessly tore the body of hiraṇya who was giving sorrow to dēvas who grant results and was causing trouble to the world in various ways due to his boundless, great tapasya; even after hearing this amazing act of emperumān from pramāṇams, will those who realise to go up to the boundary of his partiality towards his followers which is the essence of that incarnation, learn anything other than the glorious, valorous history of the śrīmān who has narasimha form?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the eighth pāsuram, āḻvār meditates upon emperumān‘s assuming of a form which is part-human and part-lion, at once, due to the urge in protecting of his devotee which is greater than the quality of accepting the one who vorśipped another dēvatā.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. sella uṇarndavar selvan than sīr anṟik kaṟparō? ellai ilāda perum tavattāl pala seymiṟai allal amararaic ceyyum iraṇiyan āgattai mallal ari uruvāyc ceyda māyam aṟindumē*

- *sella uṇarndavar* – Those who realised to go up to the ultimate result of serving bhagavān instead of stopping at the superficial results like worldly wealth and ātma prāpti (kaivalyam). Those who desire to enjoy eternally with him. Instead of stopping at the initial stage such as bodily matters, those who go up to serving bhagavān, with true realisation of the true nature of the self.
- *selvan than sīr anṟik kaṟparō* – Will they learn anything other than the auspicious qualities of śrīmān (the opulently beautiful [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/))? It is said “*innam sollāy sīmānai*” (Tell more about śrīmān).
- *ellai ilāda perum tavattāl* – By boundless, great tapasyā.  The boons were so powerful that the dēvas were driven out from their own residences.
- *pala sey miṟai allal amararaic ceyyum* – the body of hiraṇya who is troubling them in many ways, not to let the dēvas stay in their residences, and giving them sorrow. The effect of his troubles is sorrow.
- *mallal ari uruvāy* – mallal – greatness. As said in narasimha mantram “*mahāviṣṇum*” (The great viṣṇu), assuming a huge form, to make hiraṇya’s form look very small. \[Alternative explanation\] mallal – wealth, implying “*lakshmi narasimha*” (narasimha with śrī mahālakśmi); as said in “*nārayaṇō nrusimhas tu śaktis tvam amarēśvari*” (nārāyaṇa is narasimha and you are his power), he can not remain without her ever.
- *seyda māyam aṟindumē* – Knowing well the amazing acts of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who appeared on the vow of the child \[prahlādāḻvān\] instantaneously and tearing apart hiraṇya’s body into two.

What is so great about protecting someone who approaches emperumān with puruśakāram (recommendation) of another person? \[the reference here is to the previous pāsuram where mārkkaṇḍēyā’s narrative was mentioned\] Is it comparable to the quality of narasimhan [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s protection with lion’s head and human’s body, when one’s own father \[prahlāda’s father\] has become inimical? This is the quality of protecting as said in periya tirumoḻi “*peṟṟār peṟṟoḻindār pinnu ninṟadiyēnukku uṟṟānāy vaḷarttu*” (after my parents abandoned me, you remained my relative and raised me).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.
