## 7.5.9. Mayam aribavar

*māyam aṟibavar māyavaṟku āḷanṟi āvarō? tāyam seṟum oru nūṟṟuvar manga ōr aivarkkāy tēsam aṟiya ōr sāradiyāyc cenṟu sēnaiyai nāsam seydittu nadanda nal vārttai aṟindumē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tāyam – the portion of the kingdom which is hereditary right for pāṇḍavas; seṟum – forcefully captured; oru – unique; nūṟṟuvar – the hundred brothers starting with duryōdana; manga – to perish; ōr – isolated; aivarkku – for the five pāṇḍavas; āy – himself becoming all types of relatives; tēsam aṟiya – to be popularly known everywhere; ōr – unique; sāradiyāy – as a sārati (charioteer); senṟu – moved around; sēnaiyai – all the armies; nāsam seydittu – destroyed; nadanda – revealing how he mercifully returned to his own radiant abode; nal vārttai – the good literature of mahābhāratam; aṟindum – even after knowing; māyam – the amazing essence of such mahābhāratam, which is his being obedient towards his followers; aṟibavar – those who know; māyavaṟku – the amazing emperumān (who performs menial services to his devotees, disregarding his own greatness); anṟi – other than; āḷ – servitor; āvarō – will they become?

**Перевод:**

**emperumān became all types of relatives and renowned, unique charioteer for the five pāṇḍavas who were isolated. and moved around, destroyed all the armies to finish the unique, hundred brothers starting with duryōdana who forcefully captured the portion of the kingdom which is hereditary right for pāṇḍavas; even after knowing the good literature of mahābhāratam which reveals how he mercifully returned to his own radiant abode, will those who know the amazing essence of such mahābhāratam, which is his being obedient towards his followers, become servitor of anyone?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the ninth pāsuram, āḻvār meditates upon emperumān‘s act of carioting which is greater than assuming the form of narasimha for the sake of his devotees.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. māyam aṟibavar māyavaṟku āḷanṟi āvarō? tāyam seṟum oru nūṟṟuvar manga ōr aivarkkāy tēsam aṟiya ōr sāradiyāyc cenṟu sēnaiyai nāsam seydittu nadanda nal vārttai aṟindumē*

- *māyam aṟibavar* – Those who know that all his acts are for the sake of his followers and are amazing.
- *māyavaṟku āḷ anṟi āvarō* – Would they become servitor of anyone other than the one who is totally dependent on his followers?
- *tāyam seṟum oru nūṟṟuvar manga* – To destroy the evil duryōdana et al due to their refusal to fulfil the pāṇḍava’s hereditary rights. \[Why should he destroy them?\] Did they trouble kriṣṇa himself? kriṣṇa considers their troubling pāṇḍavas who are favourable towards him, as troubling himself.
- *oru nūṟṟuvar, ōr aivar* – This is how those who trouble and those who are troubled remain.
- *ōr aivarkkāy* – While all the evil forces have ganged up together, the pāṇḍavas remain with the sārati (kriṣṇa, the charioteer) as their only support. He destroyed those who did not follow him and protected those who knew none other than him alone, by minimising his own stature for them. While the pāṇḍavas and duryōdana et al had the same relationship with [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), he protected those who bowed their heads at him. mahābhāratam udyōga parvam “*arjunānga gatau pādau kēśavasya upalakśaya \| arjunasya tu kriṣṇāyā: subhāyā: ca angagāvupau \|\|*” (I saw, kriṣṇa’s divine feet on arjuna’s lap and arjuna’s feet on the lap of draupati, the most chaste woman) – when kriṣṇa and satyabāmā, and arjuna and draupati, were resting privately, the guards came in and informed “sanjaya has arrived”, kriṣṇa said “let him, in; he would be rejoiced seeing this; also, he will narrate it beautifully to break the hearts of the unfavourable ones; so, allow him to come inside”. Just as the unfavourable ones cannot see such intimate moments, favourable ones cannot miss out on the joy on seeing them; this is how he remained with pāṇḍavas.
- *tēsam aṟiya ōr sāradiyāy* – As said \[by [emperumānār\]](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/emperumanar/) in [śrī gītā bhāśyam](http://githa.koyil.org/) “*pārtam ratinam ātmānam ca sāratim sarvalōka sākśikam cakāra*” (Having arjuna as the master of the chariot and himself as sārati (charioteer)), and in periya tirumoḻi 2.2.3 “*innār tūdan ena ninṟān*” (he stood to be identified as pāṇḍavas’ messenger). Generally, we observe that svātantriyam (independence) and pāratantriyam (dependence) are manifested in uncertain places and in private only; \[example\] the husband massages his wife’s feet in private only. Still, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) placed himself at a subservient position \[to arjuna\] to be well known to the world.
- *senṟu sēnaiyai nāsam seydittu* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying that it was not the arrows of arjuna et al which killed the enemies. As he was prayed to \[and had vowed\] not to take up arms during the battle, he killed the enemies just by riding the chariot in a skillful manner.
- *nadanda nal vārttai aṟindumē* – Even after knowing the great message that he left this lowly earth where he was attacked with a rain of arrows and ascended to his divine abode of paramapadam where those who are eager to see him were waiting for his arrival. mahābhāratam mausala parvam “*krutvā bhārāvataraṇam …*” (after accomplishing the task of eliminating the burden of earth, kriṣṇa ascended to paramapadam) – he reached the abode where duryōdana et al \[impure ātmās\] don’t exist.

He did all the previous acts \[as explained in previous pāsurams\], while he was supremely independent. In narasimhāvatāram, he at least had his nails for his protection; it is not like that here; he transformed himself to be totally subservient to his followers; instead of caring for his own divine body, he accepted the arrows of the enemies; will the previously explained qualities match his simplicity explained here?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.5.10. Varttai aribavar

*vārttai aṟibavar māyavaṟkāḷ anṟi āvarō pōrtta piṟappodu nōyodu mūppodu iṟappivai pērttup perum tunbam vēraṟa nīkkit tan tāḷin kīḻc cērttu avan seyyum sēmattai eṇṇit teḷivuṟṟē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vārttai – the good instruction “mām ēkam śaraṇam vraja aham tvā sarva pāpēbhyō mōkśayiśyāmi”; aṟibavar – those who know; pōrtta – concealed the soul (with ignorance, such that the dawning of true self realisation is prevented); piṟappodu – birth \[with a material body\]; nōyodu – the disease which accompanies that body; mūppodu – old-age (which is incurable unlike disease); iṟappu – the (unavoidable) death; avai – the six types of changes; pērttu – to be eliminated; perum tunbam – sufferings such as \[life in\] the womb, hell etc which are in the form of endless sorrow; vēr aṟa – to be eliminated with the karma (puṇya/pāpa), the root of such sorrow; nīkki – eliminated; than tāḷin – at his divine feet; kīḻ – underneath; sērtti – united; avan – one who eliminated the sorrow (saying “mā śuca:“); seyyum – doing (not to return as said in “na ca punar āvartatē“); sēmattai – protection; eṇṇi – meditate upon; teḷivuṟṟu – having ascertained; māyavaṟku – amazing emperumān (who is the refuge and the one who eliminates enemies for them); anṟi – other than; āḷ āvarō – with they become servitor?

**Перевод:**

**Will those who know the good instruction “mām ēkam śaraṇam vraja aham tvā sarva pāpēbhyō mōkśayiśyāmi“, and who have meditated upon and ascertained about the one who eliminated the sorrow and gave protection, become servitor of anyone other than the amazing emperumān who eliminated birth, disease which accompanies that body, old-age, death and the six types of changes, which concealed the soul, and who eliminated sufferings such as \[life in\] the womb, hell etc which are in the form of endless sorrow, along with the karma, which is the root of such sorrow and to unite the soul underneath his divine feet?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the tenth pāśuram – the favours done previously by emperumān are those done while the cētanas (sentient beings) remain in this samsāram (material realm); beyond that, here āḻvār mercifully explains emperumān’s great favour of accepting the cētanas at his divine feet to not to have to take birth in this samsāram ever again.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. vārttai aṟibavar māyavaṟkāḷ anṟi āvarō pōrtta piṟappodu nōyodu mūppodu iṟappivai pērttup perum tunbam vēraṟa nīkkit than tāḷin kīḻc cērttu avan seyyum sēmattai eṇṇit teḷivuṟṟē*

- *vārttai aṟibavar* – With the whole of mahābhāratam, there is only one instruction given. That which leads to result is known as instruction/word; āḻvār is considering śrī bhagavat gītā 18.66 “*mām ēkam*” as the word here. Whatever he spoke previously \[in śrī gītā\], is like ocean; and this is like the amrutam (nectar).
- *māyavaṟku āḷ anṟi āvarō* – When he himself says “surrender unto me only”, will these āḻvārs surrender unto anyone else? (māyavan – one who has great love) He revealed all the confidential matters, just to have draupati tie her hair \[she had vowed that she will not tie her hair until duryōdana et al were killed\].
- *pōrtta piṟappu …* – Various births which surround and bury the ātmā not to have self realisation, like a cobweb, disease which follows the body wherever it goes, old-age which does not let him live even with that disease like the striking of a thunderbolt, death which is disliked by him and which does not let him live even with that old-age; all of these.
- *pērttu* – They are so powerful that even īśvara (lord) himself needs to identify a means to eliminate them; destroying it as a skilled worker will bring down a huge wall.
- *perum tunbam vēr aṟa nīkki* – Eliminating with traces, the great sorrow of kaivalyam (self enjoyment) which is the next step after subsequent births are eliminated. The nature of this kaivalyam is such that it makes one think “the previous state of repeated births is better”; in there, at least one may acquire another body, and may surrender unto bhagavān; but this kaivalyam is eternal destruction.
- *than tāḷin kīḻc cērttu* – uniting the ātmā underneath the divine feet to be like the lines at the bottom of the feet.
- *avan seyyum sēmattai eṇṇi* – Subsequently he \[emperumān\] ensures that the salvation of the ātmā is his own responsibility. He perfectly synchronizes the heart of the ātmā and his own divine will. \[As a cētana (sentient being), would the ātmā not have his own desire?\] Though he is a cētana, the ātmā’s very many thoughts and acts are at emperumān’s disposal, once he becomes liberated \[similarly, here too, once the ātmā fully accepts emperumān as his everything, emperumān takes full responsibility for him\]. To free the ātmā from fear, even when he is left on his own to make his decisions \[as those will be perfectly in sync with emperumān’s divine will\].
- *eṇṇit teḷivuṟṟu* – Thinking about this and becoming clear. Having clarity in where he first said “surrender unto me only” and said in the end \[of carama ślōkam\] “I will eliminate all the hurdles myself and give you myself”; would they become a servitor of anyone but him? The qualities \[of emperumān\] which were explained previously were like when a child \[which is ignorant\] cries and says “I want to eat the soil/dust”, allowing it to do so and giving adequate medication subsequently; here, seeing the well-being of the ātmās, he is eliminating all sorrows starting from samsāram (bondage) and protecting them by placing them at his divine feet; will those previously explained qualities be a match for this great quality? Other \[previous\] remedies within samsāram are similar to a cure while the tumour remains; the quality explained here is similar to that of a doctor who gives medication which completely eliminates the tumour. The remedies explained in previous pāsurams were done by emperumān as per the desire of the samsāris \[those who are bound in this material realm\]; this \[granting of eternal kainkaryam, after liberation\], is done by īśvara’s desire.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.5.11. Telivurru vivinri

*teḷivuṟṟu vīvinṟi ninṟavarkku inbak kadi seyyum teḷivuṟṟa kaṇṇanait ten kurugūrc catakōpan sol teḷivuṟṟa āyirattuḷ ivai pattum vallār avar teḷivuṟṟa sindaiyar pāmaru mūvulagattuḷḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

teḷivu – clarity (that emperumān is both upāyam (means) and upēyam (goal)); uṟṟu – acquire; vīvu – break; inṟi – without; ninṟavarkku – those who remain (firm); inbam – in the form of unlimited bliss; gati – goal; seyyum – one who grants; teḷivuṟṟa – (even when ātmās are unclear in this principle) he who protects with clarity in this principle; kaṇṇanai – kriṣṇa who is easily approachable for his followers; then – attractive; kurugūr – leader of āḻvārtirunagari; satakōpan – nammāḻvār; sol – mercifully spoken; teḷivuṟṟa – which bring clarity in those who relate to \[by learning, reciting\]; āyirattuḷ ivai pattum – this decad among the thousand pāsurams; vallāravar – those who are capable of practicing; pā – vastness restricted by karma; maru – having; mūnṟu – having differences due to the three qualities (satva, rajas, tamas); ulagattuḷḷē – in the universe; teḷivu – full expansion of knowledge, which is a result of śudda satva guṇam (pure goodness); uṟṟa – having; sindaiyar – will have the heart

**Перевод:**

**Having acquired the clarify, those who remain without break in that state, are granted the goal in the form of unlimited bliss by kriṣṇa who is easily approachable for his followers and who protects with clarity in this principle of his being the means/goal; nammāḻvār, the leader of the attractive āḻvārtirunagari, mercifully spoke this decad among the thousand pāsurams which bring clarity in those who relate to them; those who are capable of practicing this decad, will have the heart which has full expansion of knowledge, which is a result of śudda satva guṇam, while being in this universe which has vastness restricted by karma and having differences due to the three qualities.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the end, āḻvār says “Those who practice this decad, are pure-natured even while being in samsāram”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. teḷivuṟṟu vīvinṟi ninṟavarkku inbak kadi seyyum teḷivuṟṟa kaṇṇanait then kurugūrc catakōpan sol teḷivuṟṟa āyirattuḷ ivai pattum vallār avar teḷivuṟṟa sindaiyar pāmaru mūvulagattuḷḷē*

- *teḷivuṟṟu …* –  For those who have firm faith in “Only [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is the prāpya (goal) and prāpaka (means)”, and subsequently do not waver seeing the actions of the worldly people or superficial words \[of other philosophers\]. In mahābhārata war, \[after explaining the important principles in [śrī bhagavat gītā](http://githa.koyil.org/)\] kriṣṇa asked arjuna “Did you understand what I explained or not?”, arjuna replied in [śrī gītā 18.73](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/18-73/) “*stitō’smi*” (standing firm, with realisation of truth); emperumān asked “So, how are you going to perform my work?”, arjuna replied “*kariśyē vacanam tava*” (will act according to your instructions) – “I will act according to the orders of your highness”. nampiḷḷai asked nanjīyar “Did arjuna get emperumān \[i.e. did he get liberated\]?” nanjīyar mercifully replied “How does it matter to you? As the one \[emperumān\] who spoke this, is common to all, and as bhagavān’s words are certain, one will get according to their acts and desire; we are not trying to surrender unto him analysing who else has got it”. When a thirsty person sees cool water, to drink it and quench his thirst, he does not wait for someone else to quench his thirst first.
- *inbak kadi seyyum* – he will grant the reward of unlimited bless.
- *teḷivuṟṟa kaṇṇanai* – To compensate the lack of clarity in him (ātmā), kriṣṇa who is very clear in granting eternal kainkaryam to him. As said in varāha carama ślōkam “… *aham smarāmi …*” (When my devotee surrenders to me when he is stable, I will think about him and uplift him at the time of death when he can neither think nor say my names).
- *teḷivuṟṟa āyiram* – Just as water, which is muddy in mountain, will become clear after travelling and reaching certain spots, and be usable for everyone, the principles of vēdam which are to be pursued only by qualified persons \[brāhmaṇa, kśatriya and vaiśya – males\], and are mixed with chaff and sticky substances which makes it difficult to separate the real principles from the extraneous ones, became pursued by all, and cleared of all doubts, only after being revealed by [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/).
- *ivai pattum vallāravar teḷivuṟṟa sindaiyar* –  Those who can practice this decad, will have a clear heart/mind like this āḻvār.

When asked “Would we have such clarity once we reach paramapadam?” āḻvār says,

- *pāmaru mūvulagattuḷḷē* – “pāpa” is shortened to be “pā” – implies the land which has abundance of sins. The clarity one will acquire after reaching paramapadam, will be acquired in this samsāram itself, which is contrary to paramapadam; those who will acquire clarity in this samsāram itself where even when [sarvēśvaran](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) descends, he is put through sorrows and bewilderment; they will become pure-natured while being in this samsāram which will bring [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) himself who is opposite to all defects, in line with its nature.

In the next article we will enjoy the next decad.

## 7.6 Pamaru muvulagum

## 7.6.1. Pamaru muvulagum

*pāmaru mūvulagum padaitta paṟpanābāvō! pāmaru mūvulagum aḷanda poṟpapādāvō! tāmaraik kaṇṇāvō! taniyēn tani āḷāvō! tāmaraik kaiyāvō! unnai enṟukol sērvaduvē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

pā – vastness; maru – having; mūvulagam – the universe which has three types of worlds such as krutaka, akrutaka, krutākrutaka; padaitta – created; paṟpam – having lotus flower; nābā – oh one who has divine navel!; pā maru mūvulagam – such universe; aḷanda – measured to claim exclusive ownership; paṟpam – infinitely enjoyable like lotus flower; pādā – oh one who has divine feet!; tāmarai – attractive like lotus; kaṇṇā – oh one who has divine eyes!; tāmarai – distinguished like a lotus; kaiyā – oh one who has hands!; taniyēn – due to abundance of hurdles I am helpless, my; tani – being unique in eliminating hurdles; āḷā – oh master who can rule me!; unnai – you who are apt, enjoyable and protector, in this manner; enṟu kol – when; sērvadu – reach?

**Перевод:**

**Oh one who has divine navel which is having lotus flower, and who created the vast universe which has three types of worlds such as krutaka, akrutaka, krutākrutaka! Oh one who has the infinitely enjoyable lotus flower like divine feet which measured such universe to claim exclusive ownership! Oh one who has attractive lotus like divine eyes! Oh one who has distinguished lotus like hands! Oh master who is unique in eliminating hurdles and can rule me, who is helpless due to abundance of hurdles! When will I reach you who are apt, enjoyable and protector, in this manner? The presence of “O!” at the end of each line indicates the great sorrow.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the first pāsuram, āḻvār is calling out for emperumān saying “When will I reach you who are infinitely enjoyable due to your favours such as creation etc?”*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*In the first pāsuram, āḻvār says “When will I reach you who have distinguished relationship with me due to being the cause etc?”*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. pāmaru mūvulagum padaitta paṟpanābāvō! pāmaru mūvulagum aḷanda poṟpapādāvō! tāmaraik kaṇṇāvō! taniyēn tani āḷāvō! tāmaraik kaiyāvō! unnai enṟukol sērvaduvē!*

- *pāmaru mūvulagum padaitta paṟpanābāvō* – pā indicates an entity, implying abundance of entities; that is – the three worlds which have abundance of entities. pāmaru can be seen as a single word, and in that case, it would mean the three worlds which are filled with pāpa (sins). (another explanation – pā indicates vast, indicating worlds which have vastness). mūvulagam indicates the worlds which are in the top, middle and bottom layers; alternatively, it could mean krutaka, akrutaka and krutākrutaka.
- *padaitta paṟpanābāvō* – Like calling out “oh my mother!” Does he only have the aptness \[natural relationship\]? Would I not be relaxed if he did not have the enjoyability? \[i.e. he has an enjoyable form with beautiful lotus flower in his divine navel\] Did you create these only to destroy them? Why are you destroying the existing entity \[me\], while you are creating new entities \[during creation\]?
- *pāmaru mūvulagaḷanda* – Would I not be relaxed if you created them and let them fend for themselves? You are carefully protecting them, like a mother. While I who have great desire as said in tiruvāimoḻi 9.2.2 “*padikkaḷavāga nimirnda nin pāda pangayamē talaikkaṇiyāy*” (Your divine, lotus feet which rose matching your form are the decoration on my head), you are placing your divine feet on those who have no desire! Are you not the one who would redeem this earth by crossing the boundary, when those persons such as  mahābali et al capture the worlds like an eagle catching its prey?

[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) asks “Yes, I have done that. What do you need now?” [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says,

- *tāmaraik kaṇṇāvō* – We depend on you for our creation, nurturing and life on you only; āḻvār is saying to emperumān that he should glance with his divine eyes as said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 1.20.16 “*avalōkana dānēna bhūyōmām pālaya*” (Oh lord! protect me with your glance). So, he meditated upon the beauty of the divine eyes; but he did not see his presence amidst the nityasūris who consider the beauty of those divine eyes as their life; so, he identifies himself to be *taniyēn* (lonely one).
- *taniyēn tani āḷāvō* – Oh one who rules me by placing in a third position beyond the material realm where everyone sustains himself by the glance of women and the spiritual realm where everyone sustains himself by your divine glance! Alternative explanation – as I am fully dependent on your mercy, you made me the full (lone) target of your eyes and are ruling me!
- *tāmaraik kaiyāvō* – Would I get like akrūra? śrīviṣṇu purāṇam “*sōpyēnam …*” (akrūra kept thinking about kriṣṇa’s features throughout his travel and was embraced by kriṣṇa when they met) – kriṣṇa touched him such that all the features of his divine hands were imprinted on akrūra’s body and as akrūra stood dumbfounded by that touch, he himself picked up akrūra’s hand, and embraced him so tightly that two persons were not seen there. As said in hari vamśam 275.15 “*karēṇa mrudunā dēva: pāpānni: mōcayan hari:*” (With his tender hand, kriṣṇa touched the body of gaṇṭākarṇan).
- *unnai enṟukol sērvaduvē* – Would you only fix a date for your younger brothers as in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 127.1 “*pūrṇē caturdaśē varśē pancamyām*” (on the pancami (fifth day) after fourteen years)? Should you not specify a date for your distinguished servitors saying “you will get it on this particular day”? A servitor should wait for the master to grant it on the day he (master) wishes. But I am unable to be patient in that manner.
- *taniyēn – unnai enṟukol sērvaduvē* – A nāra (sentient) cannot live being separated from nārāyaṇa (the lord); now, reaching/uniting means – uniting with the assembly of nityasūris as said in [tiruvāimoḻi – 2.3.10](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/02/thiruvaimozhi-2-3-10-kalippum-kavarvum/) “*adiyārgaḷ kuḻāngaḷai udan kūduvadu*“. How will we derive this meaning when [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says “*unnai enṟukol sērvadu*” (when will I reach you)? Since it is said in [tiruvāimoḻi 4.9.10](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/04/thiruvaimozhi-4-9-10-kandu-kettu/) “*oṇḍodiyāḷ tirumagaḷum nīyumē nilā niṟpa*” (While [śrīmahālakśmi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/), the one who is having distinguished forearms with ornaments like bangles, and you stand alone), this meaning will be naturally derived \[i.e. in paramapadam, while innumerable nityasūris (eternal associates) including other consorts of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) and muktātmās (liberated souls) are present, in this pāsuram only emperumān and pirātti are said to be present – this implies that everyone is subservient to them. Similarly, when emperumān is mentioned, it implies the assembly of his devotees\].

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.6.2. Enrukol servadu?

*enṟukol sērvadu? andō! aran nānmugan ēttum seyya nin tiruppādattai yān nila nīr eri kāl viṇ uyir enṟivai tām mudalā muṟṟumāy ninṟa endāyō! kunṟeduttu ānirai mēyttu avai kātta em kūttāvō!*

**Пословный перевод:**

nilam nīr eri kāl viṇ – five elements which are earth, water, fire, air and ether; uyir – creatures with material bodies; enṟu – viz; ivai tām – these; mudalā – starting with; muṟṟum – all entities; āy – having as prakāra (form); ninṟa – be; endāy – my lord; ānirai – herds of cows; mēyttu – tending them; kunṟu – mountain; eduttu – lifted; avai kātta – protected them; em kūttā – oh one who manifested heart-capturing activities!; aran – rudra; nānmugan – brahmā; ēttum – to praise; seyya – attractive; nin – your; tiruppādattai – divine feet; yān – I (who am devoted to you without any other expectation); sērvadu – reach; enṟukol – when?; andō – alas!

**Перевод:**

**My lord tended herds of cows and protected them by lifting the mountain; having all entities starting with five great elements which are earth, water, fire, air and ether, and all creatures with material bodies, as his prakāra (form); oh one who manifested such heart-capturing activities! When will I reach your divine feet which are attractive to be praised by \[even\] brahmā and rudra? Alas! Implies “I, who seek no other benefit from you, have to call out to reach the divine feet which are easily approachable even for those seek other benefits from you”.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the second pāsuram, āḻvār calls out with great anguish saying “Even brahmā et al who are focussed on other goals, are attracted to your lotus feet; when will I reach there?”*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “You are the ātmā of all creatures and the companion during disasters; when will I reach your divine feet?”*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. enṟukol sērvadu? andō! aran nānmugan ēttum seyya nin tiruppādattai yān nila nīr eri kāl viṇ uyir enṟivai tām mudalā muṟṟumāy ninṟa endāyō! kunṟeduttu ānirai mēyttu avai kātta em kūttāvō!*

- *enṟukol* – In the previous pāsuram, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) was just saying “*enṟukol sērvadu*” (when will I reach), desiring to be touched by his divine hand; as, there was no response from him, now he is saying \[again\] “*enṟukol sērvadu*” with great anguish!
- *andō* – now, there will be no one who would call out saying “*enṟukol sērvadu?*” āḻvār is saying that he will perish \[soon\]. By the tone of “*andō!*“, he is revealing his deep distress.
- *aran nānmugan ēttum seyya nin tiruppādattai* – The divine feet which give joy to the destroyer as well as creator, without any difference. When will I, an ananyaprayōjana (one who seeks no other benefit), reach your divine feet which captivate even the prayōjanāntaraparas (those who seek other benefits)? When will I, who am fully focussed on you, reach your attractive, reddish, divine feet which captivate and make brahmā et al who are engaged in their own tasks to be fully focussed on you and praise? When will I reach your reddish divine feet which are praised by rudra and brahmā?
- *nilam nīr …* – Unlike a step-mother who cares for the child which is already born, acting like a real \[biological\] mother who will prepare/suffer even prior to giving birth to the child, before sruśti starts with trivrut karaṇam (mixing of 3 primary elements – earth, water and fire) and ends with pancī karaṇam (mixing of five elements – earth, water, fire, air and ether, to engage in creation), creating them all, pervading into the created entities through jīvātmās, for their existence and differentiating by name \[and form\] and such aspects. By “*muṟṟum āy ninṟa*” (being fully themselves), his being the meaning for the combination of acit (matter), jīvātmā (soul) who is the caretaker for acit and the [paramātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) ([emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)) who is the antaryāmi of jīvātmā, and how any of those acit will eventually lead to the paramātmā who is pervading inside, is indicated.

When asked, “while they don’t realise his presences, why is he toiling for their benefit?”, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says,

- *endāyō* – The relationship which is the cause for such care is explained. āḻvār is saying that after creating the entities, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) does not leave them to fend for themselves during dangers; instead, he toils to a great extent for their protection.
- *kunṟeduttu* – He lifted the mountain and protected them.
- *ānirai mēyttu* – While protecting, he protected the cows fully without any restrictions.
- *avai kātta em kūttāvō* – he lifted the mountain to protect the cows which were affected by the rain; at that time, he stood in a tribangi \[with three bends\] form; as that form looks very attractive like that of an expert dancer, for [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/), he says “*em kūttāvō*“.

Thus, with the previous pāsuram and this pāsuram, his attractive nature and being the goal is explained; with the next five pāsurams, his being the means will be explained.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.6.3. Katta enguttavo

*kātta engūttāvō! malai ēndik kal māri tannai pūttaṇḍuḻāy mudiyāy punai konṟai anjenjadaiyāy vāytta en nānmuganē! vandu ennāruyir nīyānāl ēttarungīrttiyināy! unnai engut talaippeyvanē*

**Пословный перевод:**

malai – mountain; ēndi – holding; kal māri tannai – hailstorm; kātta – while protecting; em kūttā – one who has the attractive posture of an expert dancer; pū – wearing blossomed flower garland, which reveals supremacy; taṇ – invigorating; tuḻāy – tiruttuḻāy (tuḷasi) garland; mudiyāy – one who is having on your divine crown; punai – (similarly, considering to be like that) wearing; konṟai – konṟai flower garland; am – having acquired beauty due to that; sem – (revealing his penance to become such lord) reddish; sadaiyāy – one who is having rudra who has matted hair, as your prakāra (form); vāytta – (being the father of such rudra) born (from emperumān himself); en nānmuganē – one who revealed the state of having brahmā as his prakāra (form); ētta – to praise (seeing the ultimate state of paratva (supremacy) and saulabhya (simplicity)); arum – difficult; kīrttiyināy – oh one who is having glories!; en – for me; Ar uyir – complete sustainer; ānāl – due to being; unnai – you (who are greater than all and easily approachable to all); engu – how; talaippeyvan – will reach and enjoy!; O – alas!

**Перевод:**

**Oh one who has the attractive posture of an expert dancer, who held the mountain and protected \[everyone\] from hailstorm, who is wearing blossomed flower garland, which reveals supremacy and who is having invigorating tuḷasi garland on his divine crown! Oh one who is having rudra who is wearing konṟai flower garland, who is having acquired beauty due to that and who has matted hair, as your prakāra! Oh one who revealed the state of having brahmā who is born from you, as your prakāra! Oh one who is having such glories which are difficult to be praised even by rudra and brahmā! As you sustain me fully, how will I reach you and enjoy you! Alas! Implies “you who were attained by those who consider themselves to be lords and by those who are ignorant, are difficult to reach by me who is fully sustained by you and calling out for you!”**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the third pāsuram, āḻvār says “You who are the cause for brahmā et al, came to me without any reason, and made me fully sustain by you only; now, you should fulfil the remaining task as well”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “When will I reach you, while I cannot sustain without you who are easily approachable by all and greater than all?”*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*In the previous two pāsurams, his being the cause of the universe and his attractive nature are explained; previously, his being the goal is explained; now his being the means is explained. See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. kātta engūttāvō! malai ēndik kal māri tannai pūttaṇḍuḻāy mudiyāy punai konṟai anjenjadaiyāy vāytta en nānmuganē! vandu ennāruyir nīyānāl ēttarungīrttiyināy! unnai engut talaippeyvanē*

- *kātta em kūttāvō* – previously, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) spoke about kriṣṇa’s activities “*ānirai mēyttu avai kātta em kūttāvō*“; after saying “*ettiṟam*“, he would repeatedly say “*ettiṟam*” and be immersed in it; being reminded by what he said previously, he is saying “*kātta em kūttāvō*“.
- *malai ēndik kal māritannai* – As it was a hailstorm (raining stones/rocks), he lifted the mountain \[stone\] and protected; had he \[indra\] rained with water, he would have lifted up the ocean and protected. Did the cows lift up the mountain to protect themselves? \[Np\]
- *pūt taṇḍuḻāy …* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is explaining the specific identity for each entity.
- *pūt taṇ tuḻāy mudiyāy* – this tuḷasi garland is the most revealing aspect of his opulence; this garland is the identity for the entity \[[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)\] who has full control over its existence \[and does not depend on anyone else\]. What did he get by highlighting this point? āḻvār is implying “Just as you have full control of your existence, my existence is also under your full control; hence, why should I engage in pursuing other means to reach you?”
- *punai konṟai am sem sadaiyāy* – Are the existence of others, free from your control? Just as the existence of the cows is under your control, isn’t the existence of those who consider themselves to be lords, under your control as well?
- *punai …* – rudra, who has beautiful, reddish matted hair which is decorated with konṟai garland, is at your disposal.
- *vāytta en nānmuganē* – Just as the garlands are distinguished identities for the respective entity, as explained in the previous phrases \[for emperumān and rudra\], for brahmā, his four faces are specifically given for the task he is set out for \[i.e. creation\]. Further, even if īśvara vows “let me create this way”, it will be impossible to do, looking at brahmā’s apt creation \[vāytta nānmugan – brahmā, the apt person for creation\].
- *en* – for this, the focus is on viśēśya ([emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is the object who has the viśēśaṇa (attribute)). While speaking in context of vaiyadikaraṇam (dealing with different entities – i.e. emperumān being the lord of different dēvatās), it will lead to bewilderment to separate him from the dēvatās and also to consider it to be talking about kēvala bēdam (simple difference) only; but when explained in context of sāmānādikaraṇam (dealing with different entities which have a common base – i.e. emperumān being the antarātmā of all these dēvatās), it will highlight the lord/servant relationship. So, the result of both vaiyadikaraṇam and sāmānādikaraṇam, is his total control over others; yet, there is special reason in explaining this in the context of sāmānādikaraṇam. As said in śrīrangarāja stavam 2.87 “*svam uddiśya*“, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) did all these for his own sake only. As said in this ślōkam “*upāttē sattā stiti niyamana ādyai: cidacitau svam uddiśya*” (upaniśats are saying that śrīman nārāyaṇan accepts the existence, protection and control of all cit (sentient beings) and acit (insentient entities), for his own sake), since starting from existence to everything else is at his disposal, one’s total dependence on emperumān is such that one cannot engage in pursuing other means separately.
- *vandu en Ar uyir* – Should I speak about your favours towards others? Is it not sufficient to see the favours you have done for me? By revealing your form/nature to me, you brought me to the state where I cannot exist without you, whereas previously I was totally engaged in worldly activities and had not even see you in my dream.
- *ānāl* – after this being the situation
- *ētta arum kīrttiyināy* – When I who was made to exist by you, set out to praise you, would it be possible for me to praise you?
- *ānāl* – That is your \[superior\] nature and this is my \[inferior\] nature; now
- *unnai engut talaippeyvanē* – How will I pursue some means and reach you? Is there even anything like that \[myself pursuing and reaching you\]?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.6.4. Engut talaippeyvan

*engut talaippeyvan nān eḻil mūvulagum nīyē angu uyar mukkaṇ pirān pirama perumān avan nī vengadir vaccirakkai indiran mudalāt teyvam nī kongalar taṇṇanduḻāy mudi ennudaik kōvalanē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kongu – having honey; alar – blossomed; taṇ am tuḻāy – decorated with fresh, beautiful tiruttuḻāy (tuḷasi); mudi – having hair; ennudai – manifesting to me (such beauty); kōvalanē – oh obedient kriṣṇa!; eḻil – having distinguished beauty; mū ulagum – world with three classifications; nīyē – at your disposal; angu – in that world; uyar – appearing to be great in jñānam (knowledge) and śakti (power); mukkaṇ pirān – three-eyed rudra (who considers himself to be lord); piraman perumānavan – the famous lord of such rudra who is well known as brahmā; nī – at your disposal; vem kadir – greatly radiant and unconquerable by enemies; vacciram – vajra (thunderbolt weapon); kai – having in hand; indiran – indra; mudal A – starting with; deyvam – group of dēvatās; nī – at your disposal; nān – I; engu – how; talaippeyvan – will reach?

**Перевод:**

**Oh obedient kriṣṇa who is having hair which is decorated with fresh, blossomed, honey-laden, beautiful tiruttuḻāy and who manifested that beauty to me! You have the world with three classifications, which is having distinguished beauty, at your disposal; in that world, the three-eyed rudra who is appearing to be great in jñānam and śakti, and the famous lord of such rudra who is well known as brahmā, are at your disposal; group of dēvatās starting with indra who is having vajra which is greatly radiant and unconquerable by enemies, in his hand, are at your disposal; how will I reach you?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fourth pāsuram, āḻvār says “You are the one who granted greatness for brahmā, īśāna et al. Similarly you should fulfil my desires too as I cannot do anything on my own”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “How will I who have nothing in me, reach you who are greater than all, who are obedient to your devotees and who are greatly enjoyable?”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Fourth pāsuram. In the previous pāsuram, it was said that the svarūpam (true nature) is at emperumān‘s disposal; here it is said that the glories which result from such svarūpam are also at his disposal. engut talaippeyvan nān eḻil mūvulagum nīyē angu uyar mukkaṇ pirān pirama perumān avan nī vengadir vaccirakkai indiran mudalāt teyvam nī kongalar taṇṇanduḻāy mudi ennudaik kōvalanē*

- *engut talaippeyvan nān* – If a weak person is told “lift the mountain”, would he able to complete that task?
- *eḻil mū ulagum nīyē* – all the greatness in this three-fold world is at your disposal.
- *angu uyar mukkaṇ pirān* – In that universe, in comparison to other dēvatās, rudra has special greatness. That greatness, is at your disposal.
- *pirama perumān avan nī* – brahmā has the greatness of being the father of such rudra, and the lord of the fourteen layered universe. That greatness, is at your disposal.
- *vem kadir …* – As said in bruhat śautrāmaṇi “*vajra hasta: purandara:*” (one who has vajrāyuda in his hand and is known as purandara) – all the greatness of dēvatās starting with indra who has hot, radiant vajra, are at your disposal.
- *kongu alar …* – You who have at your disposal, the greatness of all entities other than yourself, have placed your greatness at my disposal. Oh obedient kriṣṇa who is having hair which is decorated with fresh, blossomed, honey-laden, beautiful tiruttuḻāy and who manifested that beauty to me! By “*kongu alar taṇ am tuḻāy mudi*“, the overwhelming enjoyability is explained; by “*ennudaik kōvalanē*“, obedience towards followers is explained.

## 7.6.5. Ennudaik kovalane

*ennudaik kōvalanē en pollāk karu māṇikkamē unnudai undi malar ulagam avai mūnṟum parandu unnudaic cōdi veḷḷattagampāl unnaik kaṇḍu koṇḍittu ennudai āruyirār enganēkol vandeyduvarē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ennudaik kōvalanē – Oh one who revealed to me your obedience towards your followers to be ordered by them saying “go, tend the cows”!; pollā – unused; en karu māṇikkamē – oh one who is enjoyable to me like a perfect blue gem!; unnudai – your; undi – in the divine navel; malar – blossomed; ulagam avai mūnṟum – in matters relating to the (popular) three-fold qualities \[satva, rajas, tamas\] of the worlds; parandu – immersed; ennudai āruyirār – my (dear) self; unnudai – your; sōdi veḷḷam – glow which is in the form of collection of splendorous rays; agampāl – inside; unnai – you who are the ultimately attainable goal; kaṇḍu koṇḍittu – as said in “sadā paśyanti” (always seeing) (like someone who found a treasure); vandeyduvar – attaining; enganēkol – how is it possible?

**Перевод:**

**Oh one who revealed to me your obedience towards your followers to be ordered by them saying “go, tend the cows”! Oh one who is enjoyable to me like a perfect, unused, blue gem!  While my dear self is immersed in the matters related to the three-fold qualities of the worlds which blossomed in your divine navel, how is it possible for me to attain you who are the ultimately attainable goal inside your glow which is in the form of collection of splendorous rays, as said in “sadā paśyanti“? Implies “What is the means for me who is fully immersed in worldly pleasures?”**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fifth pāsuram, āḻvār says “How will I, who am used to objects which are created by you, who are greatly distinguished, sever my attachment from them and reach your divine feet on my own?”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Fifth pāsuram. emperumān says – whatever may be said \[about greatness of emperumān\], isn’t it said “śāstrapalam prayōktari” (śāstram becomes purposeful only when jīvātmā has doerśip)? As the result is for you, you should also not put in some effort. See nanjīyar‘s introduction. ennudaik kōvalanē en pollāk karu māṇikkamē unnudai undi malar ulagam avai mūnṟum parandu unnudaic cōdi veḷḷattagampāl unnaik kaṇḍu koṇḍittu ennudai āruyirār enganēkol vandeyduvarē*

- *ennudaik kōvalanē* – He became to me as he was for pāṇḍavas; this is how his simplicity is.
- *en pollāk karu māṇikkamē* – This is how his physical beauty is. If āḻvār says “*aḻagidu*” (beautiful), then it will just be understood as worldly beauty, he is using a contrary word “*pollā*” (bad) \[this is explained as viparīta lakśaṇā – example – *nalla pāmbu* (very poisonous snake)\]; alternatively – it is explained as a gem without a hole \[i.e. previously unused\]. Saying “a gem which is very worthy of enjoyment”.
- *unnudai …* – While your nature/form is such, I became immersed in the beauty and qualities of objects other than you. I became individually attached to the three \[layers of\] worlds which blossomed from your divine navel. Due to my desire, I became immersed in every entity which is pervaded by you, by your omnipotence. This is my state now. On top of this, you were dwelling in a place which was unattainable for me.
- *unnudaic cōdi …* – You are present in śrīvaikuṇṭam which is your exclusive abode, which is greatly radiant and is as said in mahābhāratam āraṇya parvam “*atyarkānaladīptam tat stānam*” ([śrīman nārāyaṇan](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)’s divine abode parampadam is many thousands of times more radiant than the sun and moon); I have to sever my relationship with matter and material aspects, travel a long distance, acquire a fitting \[spiritual\] body \[matching paramapadam’s nature\], reach paramapadam and enjoy you who are in such abode; thus, this is my state and that is your state; this is how the desire \[to reach you\] is in my heart; this being the case, how quickly will my respected self reach you? (āḻvār is using viparīta lakśaṇā and chastising his own self as “respected self” due to his attachment to worldly pleasures) Thus, everyone’s svarūpam (true nature) is at your disposal; everyone’s greatness is also at your disposal; this is my state and that is your state; there is desire in my heart; this being the case, is there anything such as myself pursuing some means to reach you? \[No, you have to make me reach you, seeing my helpless state, your greatness and my desire\]

## 7.6.6. Vandeydumaru ariyen

*vandeydumāṟu aṟiyēn malgu neelac cudar taḻaippac cenjudarc cōdigaḷ pūttoru māṇikkam sērvadupōl andaramēl sempattōdu adi undi kai mārbu kaṇ vāy senjudarc cōdi vidavuṟai en tirumārbanaiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

malgu – in abundance; neelac cudar – bluish radiance; taḻaippa – spreading; sem – reddish; sudar – having radiance; sōdigaḷ – splendorous lustre; pūttu – blossomed; oru māṇikkam – a bluish gem; sērvadupōl – as fitting perfectly; andaramēl – in supreme sky (paramapadam); sem – reddish; pattōdu – with the divine pītāmbaram (yellow garment); adi – divine feet; undi – divine navel; kai – divine hand; mārbu – divine chest; kaṇ – divine eye; vāy – divine mouth; sem – reddish; sudar – having radiance; sōdi – light; vida – to spread; uṟai – his merciful presence; en – revealing to me; tirumārbanai – śrīmān (divine consort of śrīmahālakśmi); vandu – coming there and; eydum – reaching; āṟu – means; aṟiyēn – don’t know

**Перевод:**

**I don’t know the means to reach the śrīmān who revealed his merciful presence in the supreme sky, spreading the radiant, reddish light with the reddish, divine pītāmbaram, divine feet, divine navel, divine hand, divine chest, divine eye and divine mouth which are fitting perfectly like a bluish gem with well spread, abundant bluish radiance interleaved with blossomed, radiant, splendorous lustre. Implies “You who know the means, should come here and take me there”.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the sixth pāsuram, āḻvār says “I have no means in me to attain you who are infinitely enjoyable; you should accept me yourself”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. vandeydumāṟu aṟiyēn malgu neelac cudar taḻaippac cenjudarc cōdigaḷ pūttoru māṇikkam sērvadupōl andaramēl sempattōdu adi undi kai mārbu kaṇ vāy senjudarc cōdi vidavuṟai en tirumārbanaiyē*

- *vandu eydum āṟu aṟiyēn* – I don’t know the means to come and reach you there. When you yourself manifest your physical beauty, I should not reject it; but I cannot pursue any means and reach you. When asked “what if you lost me?”; [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) responds “Is your form such that, I will lose you”.
- *malgu neelac cudar taḻaippa* – Should I give up due to lack of physical beauty in him? Should I give up due to lack of puruśakāram (recommendation) to attain him? Should I give up due to lack of desire in me?
- *malgu neelac cudar* – abundant bluish radiance
- *taḻaippa* – since it \[radiance\] is not acquired due to karma, it grows infinitely; it keeps growing to let us not define it within certain boundaries.
- *sem sudarc cōdigaḷ pūttu* – The lustre which is having reddish radiance, blossomed like a flower which blossoms at various times of the day.
- *oru māṇikkam sērvadupōl* – To be enjoyed, like a gemstone resting. “*malgu neelac cudar taḻaippa*” indicates the beautiful complexion; “*sem sudarc cōdigaḷ pūttu*” indicates the divine limbs; “*oru māṇikkam sērvadupōl*” indicates the divine form which is the abode for both the complexion and the limbs. It is seen here that, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s features are explained in a concealed manner, subsequently, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is explaining them in an explicit manner.
- *andaramēl …* –  andaram – middle portion. Middle portion for the body is waist. The divine feet with the divine waist decorated with the divine pītāmbaram; divine navel, divine hands, the reddish divine chest which is comparable to these aforementioned limbs, due to the merciful presence of periya pirāttiyār, divine eyes, divine mouth/lips.
- *sem sudarc cōdi vida* – to release the lustre with reddish radiance.
- *uṟai en tirumārbanaiyē* – this \[presence of periya pirāttiyār on his chest\] also appears to be a divine ornament; one who has my lady lord, periya pirāttiyār on his divine chest. As [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) mercifully reclines on tiruvanantāḻvān (ādiśēśan) having him as the mattress on tiruppāṟkadal (milky ocean) so that the water does not bother him, periya pirāttiyār is staying on emperumān \[his chest\] who is seen as a multi-coloured bed-spread.  It is said śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 38.20 “*paryāyēṇa prasupta:*” (Due to being very tired, I was resting on śrī rāma’s lap).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.6.7. En tirumarban

*en tirumārban tannai en malai magaḷ kūṟan tannai enṟum en nā magaḷai agampāl koṇḍa nānmuganai ninṟa sasīpatiyai nilangīṇḍeyin mūnṟeritta venṟu pulan turanda visumbāḷiyaik kāṇēnō?*

**Пословный перевод:**

en tirumārban tannai – one who revealed to me his śriya:patitvam (being the divine consort of śrī mahālakśmi) which highlights his lordship; en malai magaḷ kūṟan tannai – one who revealed to me his having rudra who has pārvati in half of his body, as prakāra (form); enṟum – always; en nā magaḷai agampāl koṇḍa nānmuganai – one who revealed to me his having four-headed brahmā who has sarasvati, the deity for tongue (knowledge) as his confidential consort, as prakāra; ninṟa – standing (in equality with them); sasīpatiyai – one who is having indra, the consort of sasī, as prakāra; nilam kīṇḍu – lifting up the earth; mūnṟu eyil eritta – burning down the three towns; pulan – senses; venṟu – win over; turandu – driving away; visumbu āḷiyai – protecting by ruling the heaven; kāṇēnō – will I not see?

**Перевод:**

**Will I not see emperumān who revealed to me (a) his śriya:patitvam (being the divine consort of śrī mahālakśmi) which highlights his lordship, (b) his having rudra who has pārvati in half of his body, as prakāra (form), (c) his having four-headed brahmā who has sarasvati, the deity for tongue (knowledge) always as his confidential consort, (d) his having indra \[who is standing  equally with brahmā and rudra\], the consort of sasī, as prakāra, (e) who lifted up the earth, who burnt down the three towns \[as being the antaryāmi of rudra\], and who drove away and won over the senses \[as being the antaryāmi of brahmā\] and who protected by ruling the heaven \[as being the antaryāmi of indra\]? Implies “I who am considering this seeing of emperumān who is protector in all manner, as goal, am not seeing him!” eyil – fort, implying town inside the fort.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the seventh pāsuram, āḻvār says “Will I see emperumān who is the cause for the enjoyment of brahmā et al starting with their wives, and their super-human activities?”*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “Will I see emperumān who protects in all manner, both directly and through other agents?”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Seventh pāsuram. The expected result is at emperumān’s disposal. ātmā has pāratantriyam (total dependence) which makes it inapt to try on its own; there is no shortcoming to acquire the result by emperumān’s grace; looking at not having attained the result yet, āḻvār says “Will I perish with this longing to get the result?” en tirumārban tannai en malai magaḷ kūṟan tannai enṟum en nā magaḷai agampāl koṇḍa nānmuganai ninṟa sasīpatiyai nilangīṇḍeyin mūnṟeritta venṟu pulan turanda visumbāḷiyaik kāṇēnō?*

- *en tiru mārban tannai* – Here, “*en*” (my) is focussed on viśēśaṇāmśam (attribute) \[i.e., tiru is the attribute, and mārban is the entity\]; as seen in tiruvāimoḻi 7.2.9 “*en tiru magaḷ sēr mārban*“, here it means, one who has my lady lord periya pirāttiyār in his divine chest.
- *en malai magaḷ …* – Starting here, “en” is focussed on the viśēśyam (emperumān, the underlying entity of the dēvatās). Except to speak about them as his wealth, āḻvār who remains as said in [nānmugan tiruvandādi 68](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/08/nanmugan-thiruvandhadhi-68/) “*maṟandum puṟam toḻā māndar*” (those who don’t worship any one other than emperumān), will not consider these dēvatās to be related to him \[to identify them with some relation saying “my …”\].
- *en malai magaḷ kūṟan tannai* – emperumān who has at his disposal, rudra, who has the daughter of himavān, pārvati on one side of his body.
- *enṟum …* – one who is the antaryāmi of four-headed brahmā who always has sarasvati along with him.
- *ninṟa sasīpatiyai* – one who is the antaryāmi of indra, who is comparable in wealth, to be counted along rudra and brahmā. One who is the antaryāmi of indra, who is recited along in nārāyaṇa sūktam as “*sēndra:*” (he is indra) while reciting “*sa:brahmā sa:Siva:*” (he is brahmā, he is rudra) and is supported to stand along with them. What is the purpose of highlighting these? Previously, their true nature and greatness were at emperumān’s disposal; here, as a father would find a suitable bride for his marriage-ready son et al, their wives were also granted by sarvēśvaran only and not acquired on their own.
- *nilam kīṇḍu …* – Further, it is explained that their activities too are at his disposal.
- *nilam kīṇḍu* – Just as when mother earth became drowned into the ocean of deluge and became stuck to the wall of the oval shaped universe, emperumān assumed the form of a mahāvarāha (great wild-boar), lifted her up and had total control over the situation, their \[rudra et al\] activities are also under his full control.
- *eyil mūnṟu eritta* – One who burnt down three forts. It is said in mahābhāratam karṇa parvam “*viṣṇur ātmā*” (viṣṇu remained as the antaryāmi); that \[act\] was also at his disposal.
- *venṟu pulan tuṟanda* – One who won over the senses, as part of creation. One who drove away the senses, winning over them.
- *visumbu āḷiyai* – One who fully rules svargam. (Here āḻvār is reciting emperumān along with the agents of this world to emphasise that since all actions are at his disposal, āḻvār’s desire should also be fulfilled by him only).
- *kāṇēnō* – \[Will I not see?\] Hence, it is concluded; attaining the desired goal is at his disposal; my actions are also at his disposal, to not let me try on my own. Now, only if the result is acquired by my effort, there is reason for delay; as the result is at his disposal, there should not be any delay. Even after this being the case, as āḻvār is seeing himself not having attained the result, becomes anguished thinking “Will I perish with this longing?”

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.6.8. Aliyaik kan pariyay

*āḷiyaik kāṇ pariyāy ari kāṇ nariyāy arakkar ūḷaiyittu anṟu ilangai nadandu pilambukkoḷippa mīḷiyam puḷḷaik kadāy viṟan māliyaik konṟu pinnum āḷuyar kunṟangaḷ seydu adarttānaiyum kāṇḍungolō?*

**Пословный перевод:**

āḷi – yāḷi (a historical lion-faced beast, with four feet and a trunk); kāṇ – seen; pariyāy – like a horse; ari – lion; kāṇ – seen; nari – like a jackal; arakkar – rākśasas; anṟu – when the war started; ūḷaiyittu – screaming out of great fear; ilangai – lankā; kadandu – fleeing; pilam – holes in ground; pukku – entering; oḷippa – to hide (in pātāḷa (netervorld)); mīḷi – being very prideful; am – attractive; puḷḷai – periya tiruvadi (garudāḻvār); kadāy – riding; viṟal – well-known; māliyai konṟu – killing māli; pinnum – further; āḷ – brave warriors; (konṟu – killing them); uyar – tall; kunṟangaḷ – as mountains; seydu – created; adarttānaiyum – upēndra (viṣṇu, who appeared as brother of indra) who killed them; kāṇḍungol – will I see?

**Перевод:**

**Will I see upēndra (viṣṇu) who rode very prideful, attractive garudāḻvār, and killed the well-known demoniac people such as māli et al who were screaming out of fear when the war started and fleeing lankā, entering the holes in the ground to hide in pātāḷam, like a horse which saw a yāḷi and a jackal which saw a lion, and created tall mountains \[of their dead bodies\]?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the eighth pāsuram, āḻvār says “I am not able to see sarvēśvaran who killed enemies such as māli et al”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. Eighth pāsuram. In the first two pāsurams, āḻvār explained that emperumān is the goal; in the next five pāsurams, āḻvār explained that emperumān is the means to reach him; in this pāsuram and the next pāsuram, his quality of eliminating enemies is explained, and that he will himself remove all the hurdles, is explained. āḷiyaik kāṇ pariyāy ari kāṇ nariyāy arakkar ūḷaiyittu anṟu ilangai nadandu pilambukkoḷippa mīḷiyam puḷḷaik kadāy viṟan māliyaik konṟu pinnum āḷuyar kunṟangaḷ seydu adarttānaiyum kāṇḍungolō?*

\[This incident is narrated in śrī rāmāyaṇam uttara kāṇḍam, where viṣṇu kills many demons in lankā, long before the birth of rāvaṇa\]

- *āliyaik kāṇ pariyāy* – Like a horse which saw a yāḷi.
- *ari kāṇ nariyāy* – Like a jackal which saw a lion. In śrīrāmāyaṇam, how the rākśasas feared is explained through various examples; āḻvār is highlighting a couple of them here.
- *arakkar ūḷaiyittu* – As āḻvār said “nari” (jackal) previously, he is saying “*ūḷaiyittu*” (howling of a jackal) in that context.
- *anṟu …* – Being unable to fight the war directly in the battlefield, they left lankā and hid in the pātāḷam (netervorld). Just as an anthill (where snakes live) will never be free from snakes, lankā is always filled with rākśasas, and hence the likes of māli, sumāli, mālyavān were residing there; it is explained that emperumān arrived there riding the garudāḻvār and destroyed them. āḻvār is speaking about that here.
- *pilam pukku oḷippa* – It is not ethical to kill those who dropped their weapons and those who fled the battlefield; hence, those who fled from there and hid in the pātāḷam, eventually perished there.
- *mīḷiyam puḷḷaik kadāy* – *miḷiyam* is considered as a single word, where it means, powerful; saying “one who rides the powerful garudāḻvār”; it could be considered as “*mīḷi am puḷ*“, as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 3.10.2](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/11/thiruvaimozhi-3-10-2-kuraivil-thadam-kadal/) “*kaṟai aṇi mūkkudaip puḷḷaik kadāvi*” (riding garudāḻvār who is having a stain as ornamental decoration on its divine beak), one who rides garudāḻvār who is having an attractive form for the favourable ones and who remains as mrutyu (death) for the unfavourable ones, as said in periya tirumoḻi 6.8.3 “*tūvāya puḷ ūrndu*” (riding the bird with wings). āḻvārs seek for the beautiful sight of emperumān riding on garudāḻvār and appearing in front of them. mīḷi means vali (strength), mrutyu (death) and the leader of a desert kingdom.
- *viṟal māliyaik konṟu* – Thus, one of the prominent ones is highlighted here.
- *pinnum …* – Further, killed many brave men and created a mountain of dead bodies. Increasing the height of the mountains with the dead bodies on top of them.
- *adarttānaiyum kāṇḍungolō* – Just as he destroyed the demoniac forces, would we see him after he eliminates our hurdles, and will we end up seeing him?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.6.9. Kandungolo? nenjame!

*kāṇḍungolō? nenjamē! kadiya vinaiyē muyalum āṇ tiṟal meeḷi moymbil arakkan kulattait tadindu mīṇḍum avan tambikkē viri nīr ilangai aruḷi āṇḍu tan sōdi pukka amarar ari ēṟṟinaiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kadiya – very cruel; vinaiyē – only actions leading to harm for others; muyalum – think about and perform the great task; āṇ – having valorous, prideful masculinity; tiṟal – bravery which hurts others; mīḷi – like a lion; moymbil – having huge pride; arakkan – rāvaṇa who is a demoniac person by birth, his; kulattai – clan (including brother kumbakarṇa, son indrajit et al); tadindu – severed without any trace; mīṇḍum – further; avan tambikkē – for vibhīśaṇa; viri – expansive; nīr – having oceanic water; ilangai – lankā; aruḷi – granting the kingdom; āṇḍu – mercifully returning to śrī ayōdyā, ruling over the kingdom as the crowned emperor for eleven thousand years; than – his exclusive; sōdi – paramapadam which is in the form of lustrous light; pukka – return and stay there; amarar – for nityasūris \[eternal associates of emperumān\]; ari – like the best among lions; ēṟṟinai – one who mercifully remains seated revealing his supremacy; nenjamē – Oh heart (which colluded with him for the separation)!; kāṇḍungolō – will see?

**Перевод:**

**rāvaṇa a demoniac person by birth, was very cruel, and was thinking about and performing the great task of actions leading to harm for other, was having valorous, prideful masculinity, and lion like bravery which hurts others, and was having huge pride;  emperumān severed such rāvaṇa’s clan without any trace; further he granted the kingdom of lankā with expansive oceanic water to rāvaṇa’s brother vibhīśaṇa; he mercifully returned to śrī ayōdyā, ruled over the kingdom as the crowned emperor for eleven thousand years; he returned and remained in his exclusive abode, paramapadam which is in the form of lustrous light; oh heart! will we see him mercifully seated revealing his supremacy, like the best among the lions \[as a leader\] for nityasūris? Implies – just as he killed rāvaṇa, kumbakarṇa et al along with their descendants and granted the lankā kingdom to vibhīśaṇa, he will eliminate my anyatā jñāna (misunderstanding the attribute of a particular entity incorrectly) and viparīta jñāna (misunderstanding the entity itself incorrectly) which are caused by rajas (passion) and tamas (ignorance), and kāma (lust), krōda (anger) which are caused by such anyatā jñāna and viparīta jñāna, and grant me full expansion of knowledge which is caused by sudda satva (pure goodness). Will we see such emperumān who is served by nityasūris?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the ninth pāsuram, āḻvār says “Oh heart! Will we see the son of daśarata who killed rāvaṇa et al?”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār mercifully says to his heart “Will we see emperor daśarata’s divine son, who eliminated the clan of rāvaṇa without a trace due to his partiality towards vibhīśaṇa, who crowned vibhīśaṇa as the king of lankā, who himself became coronated and ruled over the kingdom of ayōdyā, and ascended to paramapadam, with that greatness?”*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. kāṇḍungolō? nenjamē! kadiya vinaiyē muyalum āṇ tiṟal meeḷi moymbil arakkan kulattait tadindu mīṇḍum avan tambikkē viri nīr ilangai aruḷi āṇḍu than sōdi pukka amarar ari ēṟṟinaiyē*

- *kāṇḍungolō nenjamē* – Will you who accompanied me to hug and cry out loud in separation, be with me and see him together when we enjoy him without anything else to do?
- *kadiya vinaiyē muyalum* – He separated perumāḷ (śrī rāma) and pirātti (sītā) and made them live separately, similar to separating mother and father \[which is a very cruel act\]. There is nothing lower than his such lowly act. His cruel acts are such that sarvēśvaran cannot remain peaceful thinking “let me punish you in the course of time”. As said in dharma śāstram “*ihaiva palam aśnutē*” (for greatly pious acts and greatly vile acts, one will reap the rewards/punishment in this birth itself). By the avadāraṇam (“E” in *vinaiy****E***), it is clear that he does not have any noble qualities at all.
- *āṇ tiṟal …* – A demoniac person who is like a valorous lion, in masculinity. meeḷi – lion. Alternative explanation – eliminated the clan of rāvaṇa who has valour, ability to hurt others and pride of death. Eliminated the whole clan as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 64.66 “*kariśyē maitilee hētōr apiśācam arākśasam*” (For the sake of sītā, I will eliminate the clans of ghosts and demons).
- *avan tambikkē viri nīr ilangai aruḷi* – \[Is being rāvaṇa’s brother, a reason for emperumān’s acknovledgement?\] His comforting words in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 18.34 “*yadi vā rāvaṇa svayam*” (Even if rāvaṇa had come \[bring him along, he too is given refuge\]), look good. śrī rāma was patiently waiting to hear “it is not just someone related to rāvaṇa is here, but rāvaṇa himself is here”. Is it not sufficient if someone from lankā was accepted? Why is he expecting rāvaṇa himself to arrive and surrender? If someone related to rāvaṇa is accepted, only he along with few others who accompanied him will benefit; but if rāvaṇa himself arrived looking for refuge, the whole town will be protected; now, though rāvaṇa was too advanced in unfavourable thoughts, he is most desired by emperumān to be protected. Now, emperumān’s anguish in not having rāvaṇa take refuge was eliminated only after accepting vibhīśaṇa. As vibhīśaṇa introduced himself as in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 19.4 “*anujōrāvaṇasyāham*” (I am the brother of rāvaṇa), emperumān too accepted him considering him to be “rāvaṇa’s brother”.
- *viri nīr ilangai aruḷi* – Bestowing him the kingdom of lankā which is surrounded by oceanic water.
- *mīṇḍum – āṇḍu* – After the killing of rāvaṇa, brahmā and other dēvatās said to śrī rāma “We have accomplished our task, by placing your highness as the target of arrows; now your highness can ascend to paramapadam”; at that time rudra said “Your highness shall not do that; as your coronation was stopped, your divine mothers are all anguished; the whole kingdom is suffering; śrī bharatāḻvān is also in grief; hence, as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 122.4 ‘*āśvāsya bharatam dīnam*‘ (to pacify śrī bharatāḻvān who is suffering and others), you should mercifully return to śrī ayōdyā to eliminate the suffering of śrī bharatāḻvān et al, become crowned and uplift the kingdom”, and as that was pleasing to his divine heart, he remained there for eleven thousand years and mercifully uplifted the kingdom.
- *than sōdi pukka* – leaving the abode where he can be attacked with arrows and ascending to his distinguished, infinitely radiant abode of paramapadam.
- *amarar ari ēṟṟinaiyē* – Will we see his presence amidst nityasūris who are favourable by nature and focussed on service to him only, instead of hurling arrows at him? Just as a bull will walk around pridefully amidst a herd of cows, as the nityasūris praise him, his prideful presence there is explained. The goal is to see emperumān’s divine presence in the assembly of nityasūris.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.
