## 7.6.10. Errarum vaigundattai

*ēṟṟarum vaigundattai aruḷum namakku āyar kulattu īṟṟiḷam piḷḷai onṟāyp pukku māyangaḷē iyaṟṟi kūṟṟiyal kanjanaik konṟu aivarkkāyk kodunjēnai tadindu āṟṟal mikkān periya paranjōdi pukka ariyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

īnṟu – on birth; iḷam – being an infant; piḷḷai – child; āyar kulattu – in covherd clan; onṟāy – becoming one with them; pukku – entered; māyangaḷē – very amazing acts such as killing putanā, śakata, yamaḷārjuna et al; iyaṟṟi – engaged in; kūṟṟu – death which separates body and soul; iyal – having the nature; kanjanai – kamsa (who separated kriṣṇa, who is the life for śrī vasudēva and dēvaki, from them); konṟu – killed; aivarkku – for pāṇḍavas; āy – for the sake of; kodum – cruel; sēnai – duryōdana’s army; tadindu – destroyed; mikka – great; āṟṟalān – with patience; periya – having infinite glories; paranjōdi – in paramapadam which is known by the term “param jyōti”; pukka – to enter (after eliminating the burden of earth); ari – kriṣṇa who is like a great lion; ēṟṟarum – having nature/qualities which are inconceivable even by the mind and speech of great yōgis; vaigundattai – śrīvaikuṇṭam; namakku – for us; aruḷum – will bestow (by his grace)

**Перевод:**

**Being a very infant child, kriṣṇa entered the covherd clan and became one with them; he was engaged in very amazing acts such as killing putanā, śakata, yamaḷārjuna et al and killed kamsa who was having the nature of death which separates body and soul; he destroyed cruel duryōdana’s army for the sake of pāṇḍavas; with great patience, having infinite glories, he set out to enter into paramapadam which is known by the term “param jyōti”; such kriṣṇa who is like a great lion, will bestow śrīvaikuṇṭam which is having nature/qualities which are inconceivable even by the mind and speech of great yōgis, for us. emperumān who is the eliminator of all hurdles as said in “sarvapāpēbhyō mōkśayiśyāmi“, will also bestow the result to us to eliminate our suffering as said in “mā śuca:“.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the tenth pāsuram, āḻvār sustains himself thinking “kriṣṇa who is the young toddler of covherd clan, without checking āḻvār’s qualities/defects due to his childish ignorance, will bestow śrīvaikuṇṭam which is difficult to attain”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “kriṣṇa who protected his own people such as śrī vasudēva, pāṇḍavas et al by eliminating their enemies, will bestow śrīvaikuṇṭam to me”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Tenth pāsuram. āḻvār explains that emperumān is the goal, he is the means to attain himself, and he is the one who eliminates the hurdles; as there is no shortcoming to obtain the result in this manner, āḻvār determines that emperumān will bestow himself to self. ēṟṟarum vaigundattai aruḷum namakku āyar kulattu īṟṟiḷam piḷḷai onṟāyp pukku māyangaḷē iyaṟṟi kūṟṟiyal kanjanaik konṟu aivarkkāyk kodunjēnai tadindu āṟṟal mikkān periya paranjōdi pukka ariyē*

- *ēṟṟarum vaigundattai aruḷum* – He himself will bestow śrīvaikuṇṭam which is unattainable by one’s own effort, to us \[who will get it from him only\].

When asked “though you know his nature fully and remain confident that he will bestow it to us, will he not look at the nature of us who are to be the recipients”? [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) responds,

- *āyar kulattu īṟṟiḷam piḷḷai* – He is a toddles who cannot see our nature \[i.e. faults\]. It is said in [stōtra ratnam 63](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/03/sthothra-rathnam-63/) “*mugda sāyujyadō’bhū:*” (Oh kriṣṇa who doesn’t know \[care for\] any defects! You bestowed śiśupāla with liberation). Here, the words can be split in a couple of ways; a) having īṟu at the end, as in “īṟāna iḷam piḷḷai” – meaning infant. Alternatively, as in “*īnṟiḷam piḷḷai*” – which is “*kaṟṟiḷam piḷḷai*“. In both usage, the meaning remains “infant” only.
- *onṟāyp pukku* –  kamsa, kriṣṇa’s maternal uncle invited him mischievously for “vil viḻavu” (archery festival), and kriṣṇa too mischievously considering himself to be the main participant, went in. Alternatively – kriṣṇa entered maturā having the archery festival as a reason to go in there.
- *māyangaḷē iyaṟṟi* – Performing amazing acts such as entering the weapon storage area and breaking the weapons, killing the vaśerman and wearing the clothes he had, breaking the tusk of kuvalayāpīdam, the elephant, killing the wrestlers etc. As kamsa heard kriṣṇa’s actions, he rose angrily like the deity of death.
- *kūṟṟu iyal kanjanaik konṟu* – kriṣṇa dragged kamsa who was seated on the throne to have his face hit the ground and killed him. ammāḷ explained the meaning of śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 5.20.84 “*vigaḷat krīdamavanītalē pātayāmāsa*” (kriṣṇa, pushed kamsa to ground to have him lose his crown) as, “as when one kills traitors (coming in the dynasty), one will withdraw their royal symbols and then kill them; here kriṣṇa killed kamsa after taking his crown away”. As kamsa was allowed to be king by [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) only, he first withdrew the royal symbols, to let others have faith in the royal system. Hence, in the early life, emperumān escaped from those who were sent by kamsa and kamsa himself. Once he became old enough and realised himself, he helped pāṇḍavas.
- *aivarkkāyk kodum sēnai tadindu* – As those who were angry at pāṇḍavas were screaming “sārati” repeatedly and were running towards him, he rode over them with his chariot and killed them.
- *āṟṟal mikkān* – Even after uprooting the enemies, crowning dharma putra (yudiśtra) and having draupadi tie her hair, he mercifully returned to paramapadam saying “*nātisvastamanā:*” (I am not having a satisfied mind). āṟṟal indicates poṟai (patience). Alternatively, it means vali (strength). Implies, he has the strength to destroy everything.
- *periya paranjōdi pukka ariyē* – Even after reaching paramapadam where kamsa, duryōdana et al are not present, instead of thinking “we are amidst the nityasūris”, he remained with the same anger of dealing with kamsa, duryōdana, karṇa et al and holding the weapon.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.6.11. Pukka ariyuruvay

*pukka ari uruvāy avuṇan udal kīṇḍuganda sakkarac celvan tannaik kurugūrc catakōpan sonna mikka ōr āyirattuḷ ivai pattum vallāravarait tokkup pallāṇḍisaittuk kavari seyvar ēḻaiyarē*

**Пословный перевод:**

a – very wonderful; ari uruvāy – having lion form; pukku – setting out towards the enemy; avuṇan – hiraṇya, the demon, his; udal – body; kīṇḍu – tore; uganda – became pleased due to effortlessly eliminating prahlāda’s enemy; sakkarac celvan tannai – having the divine disc which is part of his beauty and wealth; kurugūr – leader of āḻvārtirunagari; satakōpan – nammāḻvār; sonna – mercifully spoke; mikka – having greatness of presenting the qualities and activities of bhagavān clearly; ōr – distinguished; āyirattuḷ – among the thousand pāsurams; ivai pattum – this decad; vallāravarai – those who are able to practice; ēḻaiyar – “madi muga madandaiyar” (beautiful-faced damsels) who are servitors of bhagavān and are eager to serve bhāgavatas; tokku – in group; pallāṇḍu isaittu – performing mangaḷāśāsanam; kavari – cāmara (fan) kainkaryam (which is done for bhagavān) etc; seyvar – will serve

**Перевод:**

**emperumān, having a very wonderful lion form, set out towards the enemy hiraṇya, the demon, and tore his body and became pleased due to effortlessly eliminating prahlāda’s enemy; nammāḻvār, leader of āḻvārtirunagari, mercifully spoke about such emperumān who is having the divine disc which is part of his beauty and wealth, in this decad, among the distinguished thousand pāsurams which are having greatness of presenting the qualities and activities of bhagavān clearly; those who are able to practice this decad will be performed mangaḷāśāsanam by “madi muga madandaiyar” who are servitors of bhagavān and are eager to serve bhāgavatas and be served with cāmara (fan) etc.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the end, āḻvār says “Those who learn this decad will be praised with ‘tiruppallāṇḍu’ by beautiful-faced damsels”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. pukka ari uruvāy avuṇan udal kīṇḍuganda sakkarac celvan tannaik kurugūrc catakōpan sonna mikka ōr āyirattuḷ ivai pattum vallāravarait tokkup pallāṇḍisaittuk kavari seyvar ēḻaiyarē*

- *pukka ari uruvāy* – avvari uruvāy pukku. We can only say “*avvari uruvu*” (that lion form) \[it’s beyond description\]. Assuming the human-lion form and entering into the place of the enemy. Alternatively – the fierce anger with which [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) tore and moved forward. Instead of someone from outside doing that, it appeared as if a lion came out of hiraṇya’s body tearing it apart; āḻvār is speaking about that.
- *avuṇan …* – After tearing apart hiraṇya’s body, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) became pleased thinking “the enemy of the child is gone”.
- *sakkarac celvan tannai* – As hiraṇya’s body could only partly satisfy the divine nail \[which is an incarnation of sudarśana chakra\], it was only present for adding beauty.
- *kurugūr …* – Those who learnt this decad among the thousand pāsurams which are mercifully spoken by āḻvār, which reveal bhagavat viśayam fully.
- *tokku …* – As people will enter flood waters in a group instead of entering alone, madi muga madandaiyar (beautiful-faced damsels) will perform mangaḷāśāsanam saying “poliga, poliga”, and serve in a distinguished manner just as they will serve sarvēśvaran, to those who practice this decad. They will be praised so much that they will be relieved of the sufferings which they went through in this samsāram since time immemorial.

## 7.7 Elaiyar avi

## 7.7.1. Elaiyar avi

*ēḻaiyar āvi uṇṇum iṇaik kūṟṟangolō aṟiyēn āḻiyangaṇṇa pirān tirukkaṇgaḷkolō aṟiyēn sūḻavuntāmarai nāṇmalarpōl vandu tōnṟungaṇḍīr tōḻiyargāḷ annaimīr! en seygēn tuyarāttiyēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ēḻaiyar – girls’ (who are desirous); āvi – life; uṇṇum – consuming; iṇai – pair (matching each other); kūṟṟam kolō – death personified?; aṟiyēn – I am unable to determine (them as eyes due to their causing harm); āḻi – like ocean (which has hidden gems); am – being distinguished (infinite); kaṇṇan – being obedient; pirān – kriṣṇa (who favoured by uniting); tiru – distinguished; kaṇgaḷ kolō – are they divine eyes?; aṟiyēn – I am unable to determine (them as \[agents of\] death due to their attractive nature); sūḻavum – surrounding (not to move away); tāmarai – lotus’; nāḷ malar pōl – like fresh flower; vandu – come; tōnṟum – appeared; kaṇḍīr – see; tōḻiyargāḷ annaimīr – oh friends (who are close, but cannot see the internal anguish) and mothers (who gave birth to me, and raised me knowing my nature well), who are controlling me!; tuyarāttiyēn – I who am with anguish (which is only known to me); en seygēn – what remedy will do (to eliminate the anguish)?

**Перевод:**

**I am unable to determine if these are “a pair of death personified which consume the life of girls? or “the distinguished, divine eyes of obedient kriṣṇa who resembles a distinguished ocean”. They came and appeared like fresh lotus flower which is surrounding everywhere; see them; oh friends and mothers who are controlling me! What remedy will I who am anguished, do? Implies, I will neither hide the divine eyes which appear in front of me, nor will I enjoy them by getting close.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the first pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki is speaking about how emperumān‘s divine eyes oppress her.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. ēḻaiyar āvi uṇṇum iṇaik kūṟṟangolō aṟiyēn āḻiyangaṇṇa pirān tirukkaṇgaḷkolō aṟiyēn sūḻavuntāmarai nāṇmalarpōl vandu tōnṟungaṇḍīr tōḻiyargāḷ annaimīr! en seygēn tuyarāttiyēnē*

- *ēḻaiyar āvi …* – Are these two death personified which will finish the lives of those helpless girls who develop desire towards certain matters and are unable to sustain themselves? Will these death personified finish the helpless girls so that they can remain neither for [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who caused the anguish by separating nor for the elderly mothers who try to redeem the girls by advising “this is not proper”? He is not aware of the beauty of his eyes! Would he not come, if they harmed him as well? Has he not seen them in the mirror?
- *āvi uṇṇum* – Like śrī rāma’s arrows, while the decorations remain intact, they would take away the life.
- *iṇaik kūṟṟam kolō* – The harm caused by the divine eyes is like two death personified which discussed between each other and arrived.
- *aṟiyēn* – Why is she saying arīyēn (I don’t know)? Even if two persons discuss between themselves and arrive, they need not kill helpless girls; she is doubting due to this reason.
- *āḻi am kaṇṇa pirān tirukkaṇgaḷ kolō aṟiyēn* – Alternatively – would they only torment the girls? One cannot escape thinking “only others (unfavourable ones) will torment”, were these divine eyes not the ones which established the initial relationship? This means – the ocean like eyes of kriṣṇa, the benefactor; and also means – the divine eyes of kriṣṇa, the benefactor who has ocean like invigorating form.
- *aṟiyēn* – Since she has not experienced separation previously, she does not realise that the eyes could torment. Have we not heard previously in periya tirumoḻi 7.1.9 “*uyirkkellām tāyāy aḷikkinṟa taṇ tāmaraik kaṇ*” (the cool lotus eye which protects everyone like a mother)? The whole universe sustains by this merciful glance. Now, it is contrary to what we have heard.

When asked “but, is it possible to escape?”, [parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) replies

- *sūḻavum …* – On the final day when śrī rāma was fighting rāvaṇa, just as wherever one saw, only śrī rāma was visible, it has become similar here; is it that only when rākśasas could escape from śrī rāma’s arrow, could the helpless girls escape from the beauty of his eyes? It is said in tiruviruttam 39 “*puṇḍarīka nedundadangaḷpōlap polindemakkellā idattavum*” (for us, everywhere it appears that his expansive lotus ponds like eyes are shining). It is similar to one’s fear for snake. Wherever she tried to move away, there too she only saw his eyes. Why is she saying “*tāmarai nāḷ malarpōl*” (like fresh lotus flower)? She is talking about the freshness during the union. \[Explains why they cannot be fresh, in separation\] śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 35.44 “*mahatājvalatā nityamagni nēvāgni parvata:*” (Oh sītāp pirātti! As śrī rāma has not seen you, he is burning like fire garland which is surrounded by great fire), śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 36.42 “*naivatamśān namaśakān*” – perumāḷ (śrī rāma) is not aware of what crawls over him and what bites him; when asked for the reason for that, it is said in same ślōkam “*tvat gatēnāntarātmanā*” – as perumāḷ \[his soul\] has moved here \[to lankā, near pirātti\], who will realise these there?  said hanumān. His \[[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s\] anguish in separation is not the same as her \[āḻvār as [parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)\] anguish. She is not realising that. She only knows how he fresh he was after having fully united with her and then separated; that is what is deep-rooted in her heart; she does not know how he felt afterwards; that is why she is saying “fresh flower like eyes”.
- *vandu tōnṟum* – Just as in real, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) will arrive on his own will, even in uruvu veḷippādu (visualisation), he appears on his own will.
- *kaṇḍīr* – Are you not seeing this?
- *tōḻiyargāḷ annaimīr* – Her state is not such that she can reveal this to some and hide it from others. She is not at the state where she can reveal it to her friends but cannot reveal it to mothers. That is the special state she was in.
- *en seygēn* – Should I try to escape it or try to experience it – what shall I do?
- *tuyarāttiyēnē* – While I should remain as said in taittirīya upaniśat “*ānandam brahmaṇō vidvān nabhibhēti kutaścana*” (One who realised bhagavān’s bliss, will not fear anything), I started going through previous state of sorrow as said in “*avaśyam anubhōktavyam*” (must be experienced).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.7.2. Attiyum turriyum

*āttiyum tūṟṟiyum ninṟu annaimīr ennai nīr nalinden? māttuyar kaṟpagattin valliyō koḻundō aṟiyēn īttiya veṇṇey uṇḍān tiru mūkku enadāviyuḷḷē māttiya val viḷakkin sudarāy niṟkum vāliyadē*

**Пословный перевод:**

annaimīr – mothers (who are focussed on pleasing me); nīr – you; āttiyum – (advising and) not letting me remain where I am; tūṟṟiyum – (outside) accusing me; ninṟu – remain (firm); ennai – me; nalindu – due to tormenting; en – what is the benefit?; māttu – in close proximity; uyar – tall; kaṟpagattin – kalpa (celestial variety) tree’s; valliyō – creeper; koḻundō – shoot; aṟiyēn – I don’t know; īttiya – (churned and) gathered; veṇṇey – butter; uṇḍān – one who mercifully ate (by stealing); tiru mūkku – divine nose; enadu – my; āvi uḷḷē – in the heart; māttiya – raised; vāliyadu – being big; val – firm; viḷakkin sudarāy niṟkum – shining like the flame of a lamp

**Перевод:**

**Oh mothers! You are not letting me remain where I am and you remain firm in accusing me. What is the benefit in doing so? I don’t know if it is tall kalpa tree’s creeper or shoot, in close proximity – the divine nose of the one who mercifully ate the gathered butter is shining like a raised, big, firm flame of a lamp in my heart.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the second pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki speaks about how emperumān‘s beautiful, divine nose is tormenting her.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, parānguśa nāyaki says “The nose of kriṣṇa who became butter thief due to his desire for the belongings of devotees, is shining in my heart”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*In second pāsuram, as her friends are of the same age, knowing her suffering, they avoided scolding her; mothers, beyond scolding, set out to discuss about it in public as well; parānguśa nāyaki says “the beauty of his nose, being close to the divine eyes, is tormenting me”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Second pāsuram. The way the divine nose torments her is explained as “While I \[the nose\] am positioned in between the two eyes, why are they rushing? Is this what is our \[nose’s\] strength?” āttiyum tūṟṟiyum ninṟu annaimīr ennai nīr nalinden? māttuyar kaṟpagattin valliyō koḻundō aṟiyēn īttiya veṇṇey uṇḍān tiru mūkku enadāviyuḷḷē māttiya val viḷakkin sudarāy niṟkum vāliyadē*

- *āttiyum tūṟṟiyum* – āttugai means scolding with accusations. tūṟṟugai means accusing in public. It is natural to try and withdraw someone by scaring him/her once; unlike that,
- *ninṟu* – continuously doing the same thing even when there is no success in previous attempts
- *annaimīr ennai nīr nalindu en* – Why are you who are focussed on pleasing me, now tormenting me like fathers who are focussed on advising me? How can you, who only look at my pleasure, torment me?
- *nalinden* – Are you trying to stop that visualisation or are you trying to withdraw me? Would you engage in something which has no benefit? What are you trying to do even after knowing the strength of his nose?

When asked “If there is no benefit for our advice, what will be beneficial?”, she responds

- *māttu uyar …* – If you are capable, please eliminate this doubt of mine. mādu – near by, i.e. near one’s eyes. The way the divine eyes and the nose are positioned, it appears like a creeper which grows near an ocean, having the ocean spring as the sustenance.
- *uyar* – As said in [stōtra ratnam 32](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/01/sthothra-rathnam-32/) “*unnasam*” (great).
- *kaṟpagattin valliyō koḻundō* – Looking at its length, it can be termed as a creeper. Due to the consistent shape, it can be termed as a shoot. She is saying “*aṟiyēn*“, since it is difficult to determine what exactly is it; and due to total equivalence \[to both\].
- *īttiya …* – When asked “would we know? You who enjoy it deeply, tell us”
- *īttiya …* – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), being unable to sustain without the object that was in contact with the favourable ones, engaged in stealing the butter and got caught, and to negate his stealing, he would apply the remaining butter on his face; for her, while visualising, she even smells the fragrance of butter. The visualisation was so realistic, the smell of the butter was experienced.

When said “whatever you are seeing, we are not seeing the same”, she responds,

- *enadu āvi uḷḷē* – this is inside my heart.
- *māttiya* – Implies radiant, lit.
- *val viḷakkin sudarāy* – The lamp which would not be put off by viraha (suffering in separation). They would mercifully explain saying “A tamiḻ scholar used to say ‘*ēṟṟiya peru viḷakku*‘ (huge lamp which was lit)”
- *niṟkum vāliyadē* – Will remain firm and torment. dīpa (lamp) is generally kśaṇika (transient) and prādēśika (limited); unlike that, this is permanent and omnipresent; this is word uttered after considering the extent of torment.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.7.3. Valiyador kanikol

*vāliyadōr kani kol? vinaiyāttiyēn valvinai kol? kōlandiraḷ pavaḷak koḻunduṇḍangolō aṟiyēn neela nedu mugil pōl tirumēni ammān toṇḍai vāy ēlundisaiyuḷ ellām vandu tōnṟrum en in uyirkkē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vāliyadu – having goodness (of not taking to time fructify); ōr – distinguished (due to its tenderness, complexion and sweetness); kanikol – is it like a fruit?; vinaiyāttiyēn – having sin (of not enjoying it at once), my; val – difficult to eliminate (by reaping the results); vinaikol – has my sin assumed a form?; kōlam – beauty, easy approacability, tenderness, enjoyability etc; tiraḷ – together; pavaḷam – coral; koḻum – pure; tuṇḍanm kolō – is it like a piece?; aṟiyēn – unable to know (decisively); neelam – blackish; nedu – huge; mugilpōl – like a cloud; tirumēni – having beautiful form; ammān – lord’s; toṇḍai – having complexion of toṇḍai (a reddish) fruit; vāy – divine lips; ēlum – wherever seen; tisai uḷ ellām – in all directions; en – my; in – sweet; uyirkku – towards my soul; vandu – arrive; tōnṟum – appeared

**Перевод:**

**Is it like a distinguished fruit having goodness? Has my sin which is difficult to eliminate, assumed a form? Is it like a piece of pure coral which is having beauty, easy approacability, tenderness, enjoyability etc? I am unable to know. In all directions, wherever I see, the divine lips (which are having toṇḍai (a reddish) fruit like complexion) of my lord who is having a huge cloud like blackish form, are arriving towards my sweet soul and appear.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the third pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki speaks about how the beauty of his divine lips is tormenting her.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, parānguśa nāyaki says “His beautiful lips which remain a contrast for the complexion of his blackish form, is seen everywhere”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Third pāsuram. parānguśa nāyaki mercifully speaks about how the beauty of his divine lips torment her thinking “if we keep quiet while the nose is showing its strength, others may scold us thinking if this is all the mouth is capable of” vāliyadōr kani kol? vinaiyāttiyēn valvinai kol? kōlandiraḷ pavaḷak koḻunduṇḍangolō aṟiyēn neela nedu mugil pōl tirumēni ammān toṇḍai vāy ēlundisaiyuḷ ellām vandu tōnṟrum en in uyirkkē*

- *vāliyadu ōr kani kol* – Some fruits first start out as buds, then fructify and finally become unusable; unlike that, is this a fruit which is always enjoyable? As his enjoyability is not a progressive one, the suffering here is also not progressive \[it is always present in same form\].
- *vinaiyāttiyēn valvinaikol* – The enjoyable entity has become the tormentor due to the sins of those who are set out to enjoy it; I have performed sins which have turned even nectar into poison. Did the sins of mine, who is a sinner, assume a ripened form there? Being present there, it will make us reap the results. Being bhagavān’s anger, it will make us suffer here. As the sins are based on actions, they will be gone once performed. For the sins committed by him \[ātmā\], they don’t have the independent ability to give the results.
- *val vinai kol* – The sins which cannot be exhausted by enduring the results.
- *kōlam tiraḷ …* – Is this a pure piece of pearl which has “accumulated beauty”? I don’t know. It is said as “piece” to highlight that there is no dirt; the broken piece will appear radiant and well shaped.
- *neelam …* – while these (limbs) always existed, they were not tormenting previously; as they have teamed up, they have started tormenting. sarvēśvara who is having a dark, enjoyable, infinite-sized cloud like form, his.
- *toṇḍai vāy* – toṇḍai – kōvai fruit. The divine lips are ripened and well-shaped like kōvai fruit. They don’t see their internal differences \[body and lips are contrasting in complexion\], while tormenting her. There is no equal for both \[when two independently strong persons have enmity against another person, they will gang up and attack this other person; similarly [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s form and lips gang up and torment parānguśa nāyaki\].

When asked “when they appear to torment, can you try to escape?”, she responds “the strength of the lips is such that, we cannot escape”.

- *ēlum tisaiyuḷ ellām* – I too tried to find the means to escape to a place where they cannot torment; but they (lips) appeared in every such place. Wherever I saw, the lips were present.

When asked “why are they appearing like that?”, she responds,

- *en in uyirkkē* – To finish my good soul.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.7.4. Innuyirkku

*innuyirkkēḻaiyar mēl vaḷaiyum iṇai neela viṟkol? manniya sīr madanan karuppuc cilai kol? madanan tan uyirt tādai kaṇṇa perumān puruvam avaiyē en uyir mēlanavāy aduginṟana enṟu ninṟē*

**Пословный перевод:**

in – good; uyirkku – life (to steal); ēḻaiyar mēl – on girls (who are desirous); vaḷaiyum – (themselves) bend and torment; neelam – having dark complexion; iṇai – pair; viṟkol – are these bows; manniya sīr – having qualities such as firmness, beauty etc; madanan – cupid’s; karuppuc cilai kol – is this the sugarcane bow (which torments those who are in love)?; madanan than – for that cupid; uyir – being the life giver; tādai – being the father; kaṇṇan – kriṣṇa; perumān – greater than all; puruvam avaiyē – divine eye brows (like the bow in his hand); en – my; uyir mēlanavāy – (being desirous) on my soul; enṟum – always; ninṟē – remaining firm; aduginṟana – tormenting

**Перевод:**

**Are they two bows which are having dark complexion when themselves bend and torment the good life of girls? Is this the sugarcane bow of cupid who is having qualities such as firmness, beauty etc? They are the divine eye brows of kriṣṇa who is life giver and the father for cupid, and is greater than all; they are always remaining firm in tormenting my soul.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fourth pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki says “His distinguished, divine eye brows are tormenting so much that it makes me think that previous torments are pleasures”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, parānguśa nāyaki says “The divine eye brows of kriṣṇa who is the real cupid and the cause for kāma (cupid) are tormenting my soul”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Fourth pāsuram. āḻvār is mercifully explaining how the divine brows are tormenting him asking “What! Have the divine lips become great now?” innuyirkkēḻaiyar mēl vaḷaiyum iṇai neela viṟkol? manniya sīr madanan karuppuc cilai kol? madanan than uyirt tādai kaṇṇa perumān puruvam avaiyē en uyir mēlanavāy aduginṟana enṟu ninṟē*

- *in uyirkku* – to take away my good soul.
- *ēḻaiyar mēl vaḷaiyum* – While there is none to bend and no reason to bend – it bent due to no reason and no one to bend. As it says “*ēḻaiyar*” (helpless), there is no reason to bend, as there is none set out to bend, there is no kartā (doer). Are these two bows which are bending (to hurt) helpless girls? As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam kiśkindā kāṇḍam 3.9 “*śakracāpa nibēcāpē gruhītvā śatru nāśanē*” (Holding on to bows similar to indra’s bow which can destroy enemies). For indra’s bow, there is no restriction that it should only torment helpless girls.
- *manniya sīr …* – Is it the bow of cupid which only torments girls? That too, this must be the bow in his hand, before he lost his form at the hands of rudra.
- *karuppuc cilai kol* – Being unreal to the eyes and the harm is firmly placed in the heart. The bow in the hand of cupid who has royal heritage of having [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) as his father, will not do such harm. These must be the divine eye brows of kriṣṇa who is the father of such cupid.
- *madanan …* – As āṇḍāḷ says in nācciyār tirumoḻi 14.6 “*than kaic cārngam aduvē pōl puruva vattam aḻagiya*” \[wife knows better\], these must be the divine eye brows of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) which resemble his own śārnga bow. \[Explaining the meaning of this pāsuram\] “*darumam aṟiyāk kuṟumbanai*” – Should he not be born as the son of a crowned king, to know darmam? yādavas are not direct rulers. kriṣṇa does not know mercy at all. śrī nandagōpar begot a son who would roam around as he pleased \[without any rules\]. “*than kai …*” – when one saw the bow in the hand, he would say “what was in his face \[eye brows\] is now present in his hand!” Similarly on seeing the eye brows in the face, “what was in his hand is now present in his face!” Saying “*aduvē pōl*” indicates the equivalence between the eye brows and the bow. His divine form is so beautiful that even if he does not know any darmam, we have to hold on to him. “*poruttamiliyai*” – some objects, when the complexion is nice, will still be unusable; similarly, he \[and his eye brows\] have such beautiful form, he will not let us enjoy him. “*kaṇḍīrē*” – though he does not want to unite with us, can we give up, if we don’t want to unite with him? His dislike makes us follow him more.
- *puruvam avaiyē* – The suffering inflicted by the eye brows is such that it makes us think that the previous torments are pleasures.
- *en uyir mēlanavāy* – While they are present in his face, their target is me. They remain as said in tiruvāimoḻi 2.6.2 “*engum pakkam nōkkaṟiyā*” (they don’t look at anything else).
- *aduginṟana* – they are killing us.
- *enṟu ninṟē* – While some objects are harmful, they are temporary too. Unlike those, these (the eye brows) are constantly tormenting me. They have assumed permanence to torment me; that which is said as “*nityam nityā krutitaram*” (that which is permanent and assumed permanence) is tormenting me.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.7.5. Enru ninre

*enṟu ninṟē tigaḻum seyyavīn sudar veṇ minnukkol? anṟi en āvi adum aṇi muttangolō? aṟiyēn kunṟam edutta pirān muṟuval enadāvi adum onṟum aṟiginṟilēn annaimīr! enakkuyvidamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

enṟum – always; ninṟē – remaining fixed; tigaḻum – shining; seyya – reddish; In – gave birth; sudar – having radiance; veṇ – white; minnukkol – is it a lightning?; anṟi – otherwise; en – my; āvi – life; adum – tormenting; aṇi – set in a row; muttam kolō – are they like pearls?; aṟiyēn – I am unable to determine; kunṟam – gōvardana; edutta – lifted and protected; pirān – great benefactor’s; muṟuval – smile (which occurred due to the joy of protecting); enadu – my; āvi – soul; adum – burning; annaimīr – Oh mothers (who are advising even at this stage)!; enakku – for me; uyvidam – a place to escape; onṟum – any; aṟiginṟilēn – I don’t know

**Перевод:**

**Is it a white lightning with radiance which gives birth to reddish shine which always remains fixed? Otherwise, are they like pearls set in a row, which are tormenting my life? I am unable to determine; the smile of the great benefactor who lifted gōvardana and protected, is burning my soul; oh mothers! I don’t know any place for me to escape.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fifth pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki says “kriṣṇa’s smile is greatly tormenting me”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, parānguśa nāyaki says “The gentle smile of kriṣṇa who effortlessly lifted gōvardana, is tormenting me; I am not seeing any place where I can escape and save myself”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Fifth pāsuram. āḻvār is mercifully explaining how his divine smile torments him saying “While I am present at the entrance of the face, how can these go first?” enṟu ninṟē tigaḻum seyyavīn sudar veṇ minnukkol? anṟi en āvi adum aṇi muttangolō? aṟiyēn kunṟam edutta pirān muṟuval enadāvi adum onṟum aṟiginṟilēn annaimīr! enakkuyvidamē*

- *enṟum* … – Always shining, is this a white lightning which gives birth to reddish radiance? While the redness in the divine lips appear together with the whiteness in the row of his divine teeth, it appears that the redness in the divine lips was given birth by the white teeth. This is said as “*acirāmśu:*” (lightning – which appears and disappears). When said to harm others, the teeth are tightening up and coming at us.
- *anṟi* – Otherwise, is this the row of his pearl like divine teeth, which are aimed at finishing me?
- *aṇi muttam kolō* – It appears like an elephant which is decorated and has appeared.
- *aṇi muttam* – Beautiful teeth. Previously, it was explained in “*veṇ minnukkol*“, how the teeth tormented due to being together with the divine lips; here, its independent torment is highlighted.
- *kunṟam edutta …* – The smile of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who lifted the mountain and protected the covherd girls from the rain, has become harmful only to me. Did he not protect the cows? It is said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 5.11.13 “*gōgōpijana sankulam \| atīvārtam*” (cows, covherd boys and girls are all suffering, he started thinking immediately \[for their protection\]). He removed the sorrow caused by the rain, by lifting the mountain, and stood smiling to remove their anguish.

When asked “But, can you not find a place where it (smile) is not present?”, she responds,

- *onṟum* … – She is saying “I started searching ‘if there is any place where I can escape and be saved’; but I am not seeing any such place”; alternatively, she is saying “I can only see the previously explained beauty causing harm, but not finding any place to escape”.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.7.6. Uyvidam elaiyarkkum

*uyvidam ēḻaiyarkkum asurarkkum arakkargatkum evvidam? enṟirangi makarandaḻaikkundaḷirkol? paividap pāmbaṇaiyān tirukkuṇḍalak kādugaḷē kaividal onṟum inṟi aduginṟana kāṇmingaḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ēḻaiyarkkum – for helpless girls (who desired without discriminating between favourable and unfavourable aspects); asurarkkum arakkargatkum – for asuras and rākśasas (demoniac persons, who oppose emperumān); uyvidam – place of escape; evvidam – which?; enṟu – asking; ilangi – having (great) radiance; makaram – in the form of fish; taḻaikkum – well grown; taḷirkol – like sprout; pai – having hoods (which are expanded due to being in contact with emperumān‘s divine form); vidam – having poison (which cannot be handled by enemies); pāmbu aṇaiyān – one who is having tiruvantāḻvān (ādiśēśan) as mattress; tiru – attractive; kuṇḍalam – having earrings; kādugaḷē – ears; onṟum – in any manner; kaividal inṟi – without giving up; aduginṟanan – tormenting; kāṇmingaḷ – you all see

**Перевод:**

**The divine ears having attractive earrings which are in the form of fish and are like well grown sprouts, of one who is having hooded, poisonous tiruvantāḻvān as his mattress, are tormenting me in all manner without giving up saying “which is the place of escape for helpless girls, asuras and rākśasas?” – you all see. The enjoyable earrings are harmful for enemies due to their \[ear rings\] being unable to bear their \[enemies\] sight. She is saying “kāṇmingaḷ” (see for yourself), thinking they will also have that vision.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the sixth pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki mercifully explains how emperumān‘s divine makara kuṇḍalam (ear ring) and divine ears are tormenting her.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, parānguśa nāyaki mercifully explains how the root of such avatārams, anantaśāyi’s (emperumān in milky ocean) divine makara kuṇḍalam (ear rings) are tormenting her.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Sixth pāsuram. parānguśa nāyaki is explaining how the beauty of his ear is tormenting her thinking “while we are in the ears, how did we allow these other limbs to go ahead?” They would usually shake their ears and speak! uyvidam ēḻaiyarkkum asurarkkum arakkargatkum evvidam? enṟirangi makarandaḻaikkundaḷirkol? paividap pāmbaṇaiyān tirukkuṇḍalak kādugaḷē kaividal onṟum inṟi aduginṟana kāṇmingaḷē*

- *uyvidam* … – Is this a radiant sprout, which is a fish shaped earring, asking “which is the place of escape and survival for asuras, rākśasas and helpless girls?” asuras et al will perish as they cannot see the beauty and tolerate it; helpless girls will perish due to not attaining the same. A tamiḻ scholar explained this as “as the helpless girls are tormented, the earrings will develop attachment in asuras and rākśasas, and will harm them in the end”; nanjīyar mercifully heard this and said “this explanation is nice; but, this does not match the context of this decad; here the focus is not to explain that earrings will harm asuras and rākśasas; so, it is not required to be explained in this manner”.
- *paividam …* – Having tiruvanantāḻvān who is having the hoods which are expanded due to being in contact with him ([emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)) and the poison which will kill the unfavourable ones, as his mattress; such emperumān’s ears which are decorated with earrings in the form of fish. Just as the beauty of the divine ears have become harmful, his togetherness with ādiśēśan too has become harmful \[in separation\]. I am suffering here even while ananta (ādiśēśan) is present as puruśakāram \[a recommendatory role on behalf of jīvātmās\]! The way the ears torment, makes previous anguish to be considered as pleasure. It appears that the previous limbs placed water-shelters to care for the self; as said in tiruvurittam 35 “*mālai  … nalgiṟṟaiyellām*” \[first evening time grabbed everything; subsequently the breeze harmed further to make one thing that the evening was better\].
- *kai vidal onṟum inṟi* – Without taking a break; would not leave once and harm later \[will harm continuously\].
- *aduginṟana* – my soul is perishing.
- *kāṇmingaḷē* – She is assuming that they too can see everything through uruveḷippādu (visualisation); because [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s nature \[of considering everyone to be similar to self\] is explained already in [tiruvāimoḻi 2.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/11/thiruvaimozhi-2-1-vayum/) “*vāyum tirai*“.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.7.7. Kanmingal annaiyargal!

*kāṇmingaḷ annaiyargāḷ! enṟu kāttum vagai aṟiyēn nāḷ mannu veṇ tingaḷkol? nayandārgatku naccilaikol? sēṇ mannu nāl tadandōḷ perumān tan tirunudalē kōḷ manni āvi adum kodiyēn uyir kōḷ iḻaittē*

**Пословный перевод:**

annaiyargāḷ – Oh mothers!; kāṇmingaḷ – “(you) see”; enṟu – saying; kāttum – to show; vagai – means; aṟiyēn – I don’t know; nāḷ – with the day (ending with aśtamī (eighth day after no moon and full moon)); mannu – fitting well; vēṇ – whitish (without any blemish due to being half in size); tingaḷkol – is it moon?; nayandārgatku – for those who desired; naccu – in the form of poison; ilaikol – is it not?; sēṇ – tallness; mannu – having; nāl – four types; tadam – branched out; tōḷ – with the shoulders; perumān than – the great kriṣṇa’s; tiru – attractive; nudalē – divine forehead itself; kōḷ – pride; manni – assuming; kodiyēn – me who is pathetic (where his beauty itself starts harming me); uyir – life; kōḷ – having; iḻaittu – determined; āvi – my soul; adum – tormenting

**Перевод:**

**Oh mothers! I don’t know the means to show you saying “(you) see” \[my suffering\]; Is it the whitish moon which is fitting with the day? Is it not a form of poison for those who desired?  The attractive, divine forehead of kriṣṇa who is having greatness of having four types of branched out, tall shoulders, assuming pride, being determined to have the life of me who is pathetic, is tormenting my soul.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the seventh pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki explains how emperumān‘s divine forehead is tormenting her.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, parānguśa nāyaki explains how mighty-shouldered kriṣṇa’s divine forehead is tormenting her.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Seventh pāsuram. āḻvār is mercifully explaining how the beauty of emperumān‘s divine forehead is tormenting her thinking “can these limbs stand in front of him? are we not in forefront of all of these?” kāṇmingaḷ annaiyargāḷ! enṟu kāttum vagai aṟiyēn nāḷ mannu veṇ tingaḷkol? nayandārgatku naccilaikol? sēṇ mannu nāl tadandōḷ perumān than tirunudalē kōḷ manni āvi adum kodiyēn uyir kōḷ iḻaittē*

- *kāṇmingaḷ …* – The mothers said “You are saying that his forehead is tormenting you; we are not seeing it; can you explain us in a manner which will make us understand that”,
- *kāṇmingaḷ …* – I don’t know the means through which I can say “You too see this”. Only if I can catch hold of him or if you also experience the *uruveḷippādu* (visualisation), can I show it to you?
- *annaiyargāḷ* – Only if I can show it to men, I can show it to you who have become older.
- *nāḷ mannu veṇ tingaḷ kol* – Is this pūrvāśtamī candra (moon, which is just reaching the eight day)? To be very young, to grow further and to be attractive.
- *nayandārgatku naccu ilaikol* – Is this like poisonous herb for those desired for it? Alternative meaning – \[naccu illai is explained as not to be desired\] Is this not to be desired by those who desired for it? [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) who previously said [tiruvāimoḻi 3.4.5](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/08/thiruvaimozhi-3-4-5-achchudhan-amalan/) “*naccu mā marundam*” (the medicine which is desired), Instead of having to know that it is in a particular mountain and having to go and fetch from there with great effort \[like hanuman had to bring the sanjīvini herb\], it \[[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)\] is a remedy which will work by just smelling it,  mā marundam – medicine which does not have any specific diet along with it. It is not a medicine which will blame the consumer having failed to work; it is the best medicine from paramapadam, which has now become like a poisonous herb for her.
- *sēṇ …* – The divine forehead of emperumān who is having tall, well rounded shoulders like the branches of kalpa taru (celestial tree) and who acquired me by those beautiful shoulders. She is also caught in the same aspect in which tiruvadi (hanuman) got caught as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam kiśkindā kāṇḍam 3.14  “*āyatāśca suvrutāśca …*“ (one who is having the shoulders which are long, well rounded and cannot be overcome by anyone).
- *kodiyēn uyir kōḷ iḻaittu – kōḷ manni āvi adum* – It desired to destroy the beauty of my life and finished my soul.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.7.8. Kol ilait tamaraiyum

*kōḷ iḻait tāmaraiyum kodiyum pavaḷamum villum kōḷ iḻait taṇ muttamum taḷirunguḷir vān piṟaiyum kōḷ iḻaiyā udaiya koḻunjōdi vattangol? kaṇṇan kōḷ iḻai vāṇmugamāyk kodiyēn uyir koḷginṟadē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kōḷ – (its own) radiance; iḻai – having as ornament (for itself); tāmaraiyum – lotus flowers \[divine eyes\]; kodiyum – creeper \[divine nose\]; pavaḷamum – coral \[divine lips\]; villum – bow \[divine eye brows\]; kōḷ – (its own) radiance; iḻai – having as ornament (for itself); taṇ – cool; muttamum – pearl \[divine teeth\]; taḷirum – sprouts \[divine ears\]; kuḷir – cool; vān – beautiful; piṟaiyum – crescent \[divine forehead\]; kōḷ – to have; iḻaiyā – as ornament (for self); udaiya – having; koḻum – complete; sōdi vattangol – is it a jyōtirmaṇḍalam (a sphere of radiance)?; kaṇṇan – kriṣṇa’s; kōḷ – radiance; iḻai – to be the ornament; vāḷ – radiant; mugamāy – as the divine face; kodiyēn – me who is having cruel sin (of being tormented by his beauty), my; uyir – life; koḷginṟadu – is stealing

**Перевод:**

**Is it a complete jyōtirmaṇḍalam with lotus flowers, creeper, coral, bow, cool pearl, sprouts, cool beautiful crescent having its own radiance as ornament? kriṣṇa’s radiant divine face which is itself an ornament, is stealing the life out of me, who is having cruel sin.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the eighth pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki explains how the beauty of his face starting with his divine eyes along with all the previously explained limbs, is tormenting her.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Eighth pāsuram. “Thinking ‘We cannot leave everything to the forehead’, all the previously explained limbs are tormenting me together” says āḻvār. When the enemies arrive, as one would gather all the scattered armies and push forward at the enemies, āḻvār is explaining how all the limbs which individually tormented are now coming together to torment him. kōḷ iḻait tāmaraiyum kodiyum pavaḷamum villum kōḷ iḻait taṇ muttamum taḷirunguḷir vān piṟaiyum kōḷ iḻaiyā udaiya koḻunjōdi vattangol? kaṇṇan kōḷ iḻai vāṇmugamāyk kodiyēn uyir koḷginṟadē*

- *kōḷ iḻait tāmaraiyum* – Though the species of all lotus is the same, there are different internal varieties such as poṟkāl tāmarai, nūṟkāl tāmarai etc; here it is talking about nūṟkāl tāmarai (iḻai – nūl – string/thread); alternatively, saying “lotus which is focussed on stealing”; another explanation – lotus which is having its beauty itself as an ornament; another explanation – lotus which is having its radiance as an ornament. Divine eyes.
- *kodiyum* – divine nose.
- *pavaḷamum* – divine lips.
- *villum* – divine eyebrows.
- *kōḷ iḻait taṇ muttamum* – The cool divine teeth which are having their radiance as an ornament. Alternative explanation – The cool divine teeth which appear like pearls strung on a thread.
- *taḷirum* – divine ears.
- *kuḷir vān piṟaiyum* – divine forehead. The eyes, the one who said “I am the strong nose”, the one \[lips\] who spoke about the mouth, the eyebrows which bent saying “did the lips become great?”, the one remained at the forefront \[teeth/smile\], the ears which stood up on hearing the name, the forehead which thought itself as the leader of all, together tormented.
- *kōḷ iḻaiyā …* – Is it a jyōtirmaṇḍalam which is having many ornaments? Allegorical. Alternative explanation – Is it a jyōtirmaṇḍalam which is having its own beauty as an ornament?
- *kaṇṇan kōḷ iḻai …* – Having kriṣṇa’s beauty itself as an ornament and having radiant face, as the reason.
- *kodiyēn uyir koḷginṟadē* – It is so tragic that I have performed sin to make me lose my life when I should get it \[by seeing his beauty\]. The radiant sphere of light which is decorated, is stealing the life out of me who is having the sin which makes me perish while I should be living.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.7.9. Kolginra kolirulai

*koḷginṟa kōḷ iruḷaic cugirnditta koḻunjuruḷin uḷ koṇḍa neela nannūl taḻaikol? anṟu māyan kuḻal viḷginṟa pūndaṇḍhuḻāy virai nāṟa vandu en uyirai kaḷginṟavāṟu aṟiyīr annaimīr kaḻaṟā niṟṟirē*

**Пословный перевод:**

koḷginṟa – to contain (the whole world); kōḷ – having pride; iruḷai – darkness; sugirnditta – (to eliminate all blemishes) reformed; koḻum – dense; suruḷin – collection’s; uḷ – inside; koṇḍa – (spun and) kept; neelam – having dark complexion; nal – beautiful; nūl taḻaikol – is it a bunch of thread?; anṟu – it is not like that (due to kriṣṇa’s hair being curly); māyan – kriṣṇa who is having amazing form, his; kuḻal – (matchless) divine hair; viḷginṟa – blossomed; pū – having flower; taṇ – having freshness; tuḻāy – tiruttuḻāy’s (tuḷasi); virai – fragrance; nāṟa – to spread; vandu – come; en – my; uyirai – soul; kaḷginṟa – stealing; āṟu – means; aṟiyīr – you don’t know; annaimīr – being the mothers; kaḻaṟā niṟṟīr – you are ordering me (without knowing my state)

**Перевод:**

**Is kriṣṇa’s hair a bunch of beautiful thread, which is having prideful darkness to contain the whole world, which is reformed and is a dense, internal collection of such darkness kept with dark complexion? it is not like that. The divine hair of kriṣṇa who is having an amazing form, which is having blossomed flowers and having fresh tuḷasi, which is spreading its fragrance, has come to steal my heart; you don’t know the means by which it does this; being my mothers, you are ordering me.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the ninth pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki explains how the beauty of his divine hair which is beyond this world, is tormenting her.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, parānguśa nāyaki explains how the matchless, divine hair of kriṣṇa who has an amazing form, is tormenting her.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Ninth pāsuram. parānguśa nāyaki is explaining how the beauty of his divine hair is tormenting her saying “It is for this purpose \[to torment her\] that we are decorated with flowers and fragrant substances”. koḷginṟa kōḷ iruḷaic cugirnditta koḻunjuruḷin uḷ koṇḍa neela nannūl taḻaikol? anṟu māyan kuḻal viḷginṟa pūndaṇḍhuḻāy virai nāṟa vandu en uyirai kaḷginṟavāṟu aṟiyīr annaimīr kaḻaṟā niṟṟirē*

- *koḷginṟa* … – Starting to give an example for his divine hair, and since the example does not match his hair, the example is getting decorated \[to make it a match\]. The darkness which consumed everything and pervaded everything, during praḷayam (deluge) where there is no difference between day and night; kōḷ means pride, implying prideful darkness. sugirdal means reforming it. After extracting the reformed, dense portion, and eliminating the extraneous aspect (the internal diamond-like strong dark pigment is extracted) – is this such a bunch of dark coloured thread?
- *anṟu māyan kuḻal* – She saw his beautiful hair in her heart. Only after decorating the example, it can be compared. Still, she is saying that it is the divine hair of kriṣṇa who has an amazing form. Will these extraneous decorations bring any comparability to his naturally divine hair?
- *viḷginṟa …* – The fragrance from the blossoming, fresh and cool tuḷasi is appearing to hit her face. For the beauty of his divine hair, the fragrance of the tuḷasi becomes the army and is causing harm.
- *en uyiraik kaḷginṟavāṟu aṟiyīr* – kaḷginṟa – stealing. While you all remain happy, you will not know how it is specifically coming to me and stealing my soul. What does it mean by stealing? Taking it away without the acceptance of the soul. It is emperumān who is stealing. The roles have reversed \[i.e. usually, ātmā claims ownership of self, which is considered as stealing of emperumān’s property\]. One can stop if an inapt person steals, but if emperumān who is apt \[to have our soul\] steals, there is no stopping. Once he gets a hold of the soul, he will then start talking with authentic texts to justify his act.
- *annaimīr kaḻaṟā niṟṟirē* – You, being angry, are scolding me thinking that I am assisting in his theft. \[Instead\] Can you help me by stopping this uruveḷippādu (visualisation)? Does being my mother where you can control me, give you rights to scold me? kaḻaṟal – hurting by words.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.7.10. Nirri murrattul

*niṟṟi muṟṟattuḷ enṟu neritta kaiyarāy ennai nīr suṟṟiyum sūḻndum vaidir sudarc cōdi maṇi niṟamāy muṟṟa im mū ulagum viriginṟa sudar mudikkē oṟṟumaik koṇḍaduḷḷam annaimīr! nasai en nungatkē*

**Пословный перевод:**

muṟṟattuḷ – in the courtyard; niṟṟi – standing there; enṟu – saying; neritta – pressed \[in anger\]; kaiyarāy – having hand; ennai – me; nīr – you; suṟṟiyum – surrounding; sūḻndum – (due to anger) tricking; vaidir – scolding me; sudar – spreading as radiance; sōdi – having shining; maṇi – gems; niṟamāy – having complexion; im mū ulagu – the world which has three types of cētanas (sentient beings) and acētanas (insentient objects); muṟṟavum – all; viriginṟa – pervading; sudar – having radiance; mudikkē – in the divine crown; uḷḷam – heart; oṟṟumaik koṇḍadu – became attached; annaimīr – oh mothers!; nungatku – for you (who are scolding me); nasai – having desire (towards me); en – what is the use?

**Перевод:**

**You are saying “you are standing in the courtyard”, having hands pressed, surrounding me, tricking me and scolding me; my heart became attached to the radiant, divine crown \[of emperumān\] which is spreading like radiance, having the complexion of shining gems and pervading the world which has three types of cētanas and acētanas;  oh mothers! what is the use for you to have desire towards me?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the tenth pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki says “My heart is captivated by the beauty of his crown; your scolding me has no purpose”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, parānguśa nāyaki explains how her heart became attached to his divine crown which reveals his supremacy.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Tenth pāsuram. parānguśa nāyaki explains how the beauty of his divine crown is tormenting her thinking “even the śrīya:pati (lord of śrī mahālakśmi) is wearing me on his head, for this situation \[to torment her\]”. niṟṟi muṟṟattuḷ enṟu neritta kaiyarāy ennai nīr suṟṟiyum sūḻndum vaidir sudarc cōdi maṇi niṟamāy muṟṟa im mū ulagum viriginṟa sudar mudikkē oṟṟumaik koṇḍaduḷḷam annaimīr! nasai en nungatkē*

- *niṟṟi* … – Unless she tells them to give up attachment towards her, it appears that they won’t give up on her.
- *niṟṟi muṟṟattuḷ enṟu* – They will say “Why are you standing in the courtyard?” They thought “instead of staying in the bed, she has risen and is standing in the courtyard to be seen by everyone – what is more shameful than this?” śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 33.7 “*yā naśakyā*” (one (sītāp pirātti) who was not seen even by those who wander in the sky). They are thinking her act to be similar to that which is mentioned in the same ślōkam “*rājamārgagatājanā:*” (those who are walking on the road are seeing her). They are pressing their hands in anger for her courageous act of stepping out to the courtyard.
- *ennai nīr* – I who was brought out to the courtyard by the uruvu veḷippādu (visualisation) and you who are fortunate to remain unharmed by this visualisation. I who was brought out to the courtyard by him, and you who have nothing to do with this.
- *suṟṟiyum sūḻndum vaidir* – ānalysing within your heart thinking “how to make her escape from this situation?” and standing around me, being unable to leave. Alternative explanation – you are scolding me, going in and out of the place.
- *sudarc cōdi …* – Unlike them who are standing in a particular place trying to help her escape, it (the divine crown) remains everywhere tormenting her. She is saying “my heart became fully attached to the divine crown which is pervading its radiance everywhere we see and is having the radiance of a very shining gemstone”. Alternatively, saying “I have written myself off for the divine crown”.
- *annaimīr nasai en nungatkē* – You mothers should give up attachment towards me. The mothers should beget the girl, raise her and once she becomes enjoyable, should leave her with the one who married her and stay away. Instead should they show anger and scold? As one becomes a matured adult, should the mothers try to advice and withdraw the girl, just because they have given birth?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.7.11. Katkariya piraman

*katkariya piraman sivan indiran enṟivarkkum katkariya kaṇṇanaik kurugūrc catakōpan sonna utkudai āyirattuḷ ivaiyum oru pattum vallār utkudai vānavarōdu udanāy enṟum māyārē*

**Пословный перевод:**

katku – for the eyes (of humans et al); ariya – difficult to see; piraman sivan indiran – brahmā, rudra, indra et al; enṟu – as told; ivarkkum katku – for their eyes; ariya – difficult to see; kaṇṇanai – kriṣṇa; kurugūrc catakōpan – āḻvār (who experienced through visualisation); sonna – mercifully spoke; utku – strength (to reveal bhagavān’s svarūpa (true nature), rūpa (forms), guṇa (qualities) etc); udai – having; āyiurattuḷ – among the thousand pāsurams; oru – distinguished (due to revealing bhagavān’s great beauty); ivaiyum pattum – this decad; vallār – those who can practice; utku udai – those with strength (to eternally experience bhagavān); vānavarōdu – with the residents of paramapadam; enṟum – always; udanāy – to be known as equals; māyār – will live (without destruction in nature of self which is in the form of bondage in samsāram)

**Перевод:**

**āḻvār mercifully spoke this distinguished decad among the thousand pāsurams which are having strength \[to reveal bhagavān’s true nature, forms, qualities etc\] and which are on kriṣṇa who is difficult to be seen by the eyes of brahmā, rudra, indra et al who are told to be difficult to be seen by the eyes of humans et al. Those who can practice this decad will be always known as equals to the residents of paramapadam who have the strength to eternally experience bhagavān and will live with them.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the end, āḻvār says “Those who know this decad, will not go through the sufferings which I endured in this decad, and will eternally associate with ayarvaṟum amarargaḷ (nityasūris)”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. katkariya piraman sivan indiran enṟivarkkum katkariya kaṇṇanaik kurugūrc catakōpan sonna utkudai āyirattuḷ ivaiyum oru pattum vallār utkudai vānavarōdu udanāy enṟum māyārē*

- *katkariya …* – kriṣṇa who cannot be seen by the eyes of dēvatās such as brahmā et al who cannot be seen by the eyes of humans. kriṣṇa, who cannot be seen by brahmā et al, revealed himself to āḻvār through visualisation so that āḻvār cannot forget him and kriṣṇa chased and surrounded āḻvār wherever he went. Just as he made it difficult for the eyes of brahmā et al to see him, he manifested himself to āḻvār, as said in “*sūḻavum tāmarai nāṇmalarmēl vandu tōnṟum*” (he came and appeared like fresh lotus flower).
- *kurugūrc catakōpan sonna* – Mercifully spoken by āḻvār.
- *utkudai āyirattuḷ …* – Among the thousand pāsurams which have the strength to reveal the subject matter as it is, those who can practice this decad, will become united with the nityasūris who have the qualification to keep enjoying bhagavān while eternally experiencing him.
- *enṟum māyārē* – āḻvār is considering uruveḷippādu (visualisation) and māygai (separation) as synonyms. māyār – will not separate. They will become part of the assembly of devotees as said in [tiruvāimoḻi – 2.3.10](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/02/thiruvaimozhi-2-3-10-kalippum-kavarvum/) “*adiyārgaḷ kuḻāngaḷai – udan kūduvadu*“. Unlike sufferings inflicted by bhagavat apacāram (offenses committed towards bhagavān) and bhāgavata apacāram (offenses committed towards bhāgavatas), this suffering \[of āḻvār\] is caused after getting acceptance of bhagavān and not having that joy perpetually. As in deluge, āḻvār’s eyes is directly covered by [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s eyes \[not letting him see anything else and hence suffering. Such suffering will not be there for those who practice this decad\].
- *sūḻavum* – \[trick\] All of these are done by him over his neck \[i.e – suffering inflicted by his facial beauty; this would also mean that he inflicted this suffering just from his mouth and not from his heart\].

## 7.8 Maya! vamanane!

## 7.8.1. Maya! vamanane!

*māyā! vāmananē! madusūdā! nī aruḷāy tīyāy nīrāy nilanāy visumbāyk kālāy tāyāyt tandaiyāy makkaḷāy maṟṟumāy muṟṟumāy nīyā nī ninṟavāṟu ivai enna niyāyangaḷē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

māyā – Oh one who has naturally amazing abilities; vāmananē – (matching such ability, one who requested for alms in a tiny form as the huge mēru mountain was shrunk into a small stone) being vāmana; madusūdā – Oh one who destroys (like you destroyed madu to eliminate the doubts of those who doubted your variegated abilities)!; nī – yourself; aruḷāy – should kindly explain the way you have your variegated wealth; tī nīr nilan visumbu kāl – five great elements which are the cause for the spherical universe; tāy tandai makkaḷ maṟṟum – mother, father, children et al (who are all residents in the universe and are unique in their own ways); muṟṟum – all entities which are connected to mother, father, children et al; āy – having them as prakāram (form) to have them at your full disposal; nīyāy – being the one with distinguished form; nī – you; ninṟa – remaining; ivai āṟu – this manner; enna – what; niyāyangaḷ – are under \[what\] principles?

**Перевод:**

**Oh one who has naturally amazing abilities! Oh vāmana! Oh destroyer of madu! You should kindly explain the way you have your variegated wealth; under what principles, are you remaining in this manner with the five great elements which are the cause for the spherical universe, mother, Father, children et al and all entities which are connected to them, as your form and being the one with a distinguished form as well? āḻvār is mercifully saying “since the causal entities are themselves present as effectual entities, bhagavān who is the antaryāmi of everyone/everything, without being contaminated with the faults of those entities, should himself mercifully explain these confidential principles of vēdāntam”.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the first pāsuram, āḻvār mediates upon emperumān having variegated causes and effects as his wealth, and asks emperumān “how is this!” in amazement.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. māyā! vāmananē! madusūdā! nī aruḷāy tīyāy nīrāy nilanāy visumbāyk kālāy tāyāyt tandaiyāy makkaḷāy maṟṟumāy muṟṟumāy nīyā nī ninṟavāṟu ivai enna niyāyangaḷē!*

- *māyā* – This one word is the essence of this decad.
- *vāmananē* – The meaning of the word māyā is well manifested here. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying “born on one day, grew up on the same day, went to mahābali and stood in front of him, mercifully spoke so convincingly that he will follow every word of it, showed small feet and measured the world with huge feet, and oh vāmana who thought about all of these ahead!”
- *madusūdā* – Just as vāmanāvatāram is for amazing acts, madusūdanāvatāram is for eliminating hurdles.
- *madusūdā nī aruḷāy* – Just as you killed madu, you should mercifully eliminate my doubts as well.
- *tīyāy …* – The variegatedness which is seen in the effect, will be seen in cause as well. That is, each one is distinct in nature. In this manner, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is the controller of the five great elements.
- *tāyāy …* – Even the effectual entities, what is done by mother is not done by father; the help done by father is not done by the sons; the help done by the sons is not done by the relatives; in this manner, being all types of relatives.
- *muṟṟumāy* – Oh controller of all those related entities in the form of cētanas (sentient beings) and acētanas (insentient objects) who are not mentioned here!
- *nīyāy* – His distinguished form is unlike \[much more glorious than\] the universal form. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) acquired great knowledge that [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s presence in paramapadam being enjoyed by the nityasūris and his having universal form, are equally enjoyable.
- *nī ninṟavāṟu* – The manner in which you remained with these variegated forms.
- *ivai enna niyāyangaḷē* – How amazing these forms are! Though in the beginning itself āḻvār has enjoyed [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s wealth, he is enjoying emperumān’s wealth as if he has never experienced them, just as while experiencing emperumān’s qualities is ever fresh as mentioned in [tiruvāimoḻi 2.5.4](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/03/thiruvaimozhi-2-5-4-epporulum-thanay/) “*appoḻudaikku appoḻudu en ārāvamudamē*” (every moment, emperumān is like infinitely reliśable nectar).
- *ivai enna niyāyangaḷē nī aruḷāy* – You should kindly explain this. Just as you cleared the doubt of arjuna as said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 6.39](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/6-39/) “*tvadanya: samśayasyāsya cēttā na hyupapadyatē*” (none other than you are qualified to clear this doubt), you should clear my doubt as well.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.8.2. Angan malar

*angaṇ malart taṇḍuḻāy mudi accudanē! aruḷāy tingaḷum jñayiṟumāyc ceḻum pal sudarāy iruḷāy pongu poḻi maḻaiyāyp pugaḻāyp paḻiyāyp pinnum nī vengaṇ vengūṟṟamumām ivai enna vicittiramē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

am – distinguished; kaḷ – having honey; malar – having flower; taṇ – invigorating; tuḻāy – decorated with tiruttuḻāy (tuḷasi); mudi – having hair; accudanē – Oh acyuta who does not fail (due to complete lordship acquired after accomplishing the desired task); aruḷāy – you should mercifully explain!; tingaḷum – moon; jñāyiṟumāy – being sun; seḻum – distinguished; pal – many; sudarāy – luminous objects such as planets, stars; iruḷāy – darkness (in which, creatures cannot see the objects); pongu – in abundance (for the growth of such creatures); poḻi – pouring; maḻaiyāy – being rain; pugaḻāy – glories (which were earned by the crop etc which grew abundantly due to the rain \[and were shared to others\]); paḻiyāy – blame (due to inapt recipient etc); pinnum – further; vem kaṇ – being with cruel eyes (to destroy them); vem – with cruelty; kūṟṟamumām – being death personified; ivai – these aspects; enna vicitram – how variegated?

**Перевод:**

**Oh acyuta who is having hair which is decorated with distinguished, honey filled, flowered tiruttuḻāy and who does not fail! You should mercifully explain! How variegated your aspects are? You are being moon, sun and many distinguished, luminous objects such as planets, stars; you are being darkness; you are being the rain which is pouring in abundance; you are being glories and blame, and further being with cruel eyes as cruel death personified.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the second pāsuram, āḻvār is mercifully explaining how emperumān is having entities such as candra (moon), sūrya (sun) etc as his wealth.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “Your highness who has the completeness acquired by fulfilling your desire, should mercifully explain your variegated nature of having candra, sūrya etc as your wealth”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. angaṇ malart taṇḍuḻāy mudi accudanē! aruḷāy tingaḷum jñayiṟumāyc ceḻum pal sudarāy iruḷāy pongu poḻi maḻaiyāyp pugaḻāyp paḻiyāyp pinnum nī vengaṇ vengūṟṟamumām ivai enna vicittiramē!*

- *am kaḷ malar …* – Oh one who is having beautiful tiruttuḻāy which has honey and flower, on your divine hair and having that beauty eternally without any change ever! Experiencing bhagavān’s wealth is as enjoyable for āḻvār, as his garland on his hair. piḷḷān explains, āḻvār is reminiscing what he said in the previous decad as in tiruvāimoḻi 7.7.9 “*viḷginṟa pūntaṇḍuḻāy virai nāṟa vandu*” (to spread the fragrance of tiruttuḻāy which has blossomed flower). Here, āḻvār is enjoying [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s hair through sākśātkāram (internal vision) instead of being harmed by uruveḷippādu (visualisation) as said in previous decad “*māyan kuḻal viḷginṟa pūndaṇḍhuḻāy virai nāṟa vandu*“.
- *tingaḷum jñāyiṟumāy* – As said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 5.10.13 “*sūryāmśu janitam tāpam ninyē tārāpatiś śamam*” (The heat caused by sun’s rays was removed by the moon, you are being the moon which refreshes cētanas (sentient beings) by eliminating the heat caused by sun’s rays, and being the sun which eliminates the wetness caused by moon.
- *seḻum pal sudarāy* – being the stars which have movements which determine the gain and loss of cētanas.
- *iruḷāy* – being the darkness which helps in enjoyment of cētanas.
- *pongu poḻi maḻaiyāy* – Being the rain which helps producing crops which help all creatures.
- *pugaḻāy* – fame which is desired by all
- *paḻiyāy* – blame which should be eliminated by struggling hard by everyone
- *pinnum* – further
- *vem kaṇ vem kūṟṟamumām* – As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 65.4 “*purābhūtvā mrudurdānta: sarva bhūta hitē rata: \| na krōda vaśām āpanna: prakrutim hātum arhasi \|\|*” (śrī rāma should not give up his natural calmness and assume anger, after previously being very kind hearted, being in full control over his senses and being desirous of doing good to all creatures), once their conduct becomes too bad, instead of showering his cool glance, he himself shows his cruel glance.
- *vem kūṟṟam* – Being very cruel-hearted to make demoniac persons cry for water. This explains how [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) becomes the antaryāmi of rudra etc during samhāram (annihilation).
- *ivai enna vicittiramē* – How variegated are these! Kindly explain.
