## 7.8.3. Cittirat ter

*cittirat tēr valavā! tiruccakkarattāy aruḷāy ettanai ōr ugamum avaiyāy avaṟṟuḷ iyalum otta oṇ pal poruḷgaḷ ulappillanavāy viyavāy vittagattāy niṟṟi nī ivai enna vidamangaḷē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

cittiram – in many ways; tēr – chariot; valavā – one who can conduct; tiruccakkarattāy – similarly, oh one who is having the weapon, divine chakra, which can transform day into night!; aruḷāy – you should mercifully explain; ettanai – having variations \[in yugas\] such as kruta, trētā, dvāpara and kali; ōr – distinguished to be incomparable with one another; ugamum – being the controller of yugas; avaiyāy – being the time; avaṟṟuḷ – in it; iyalum – occurring; otta – being the same in being the embodiment of knowledge; oṇ – having distinguished aspects such as being self-illuminating, being knowledgeable etc; pal – having distinguished natures as said in “ēkō bahūnām”; ulappillana – innumerable; poruḷgaḷ – cit (sentient) and acit (insentient) entities; āy – having them as your form; viyavu – for the differences (in them such as dēva, manuśya forms which conceal the equality of the souls); āy – being the controller; vittagattāl – being amazing due to being unaffected by their defects as said in “namaksnigdāni bhūtāni”; nī niṟṟi – you remain; ivai enna vidamangaḷ – what kind of uniqueness is this?

**Перевод:**

**Oh one who can conduct your chariot in many ways and who is having the weapon, divine chakra, which can transform day into night! You should mercifully explain; your are being the controller of yugas which are having variations such as kruta, trētā, dvāpara and kali, and are distinguished to be incomparable with one another; you are being the time and having as your form, the innumerable cit (sentient) and acit (insentient) objects which are existing within the scope of such time, being the same in being the embodiment of knowledge, having distinguished aspects such as being self-illuminating, being knowledgeable etc and having distinguished natures as said in “ēkō bahūnām“; you are being the controller for their differences; yet, you remain amazing due to being unaffected by their defects as said in “namaksnigdāni bhūtāni“; what kind of uniqueness is this?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the third pāsuram, āḻvār says “emperumān is the one who is having the many yugas starting with krut yuga, and all the dēvas (celestial beings), manuśyas (human beings) et al who exist in those times, as his wealth”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “Being great and yet being subservient towards your followers, and while remaining as all entities starting with time, you should mercifully explain your uniqueness of being unconnected with them”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. cittirat tēr valavā! tiruccakkarattāy aruḷāy ettanai ōr ugamum avaiyāy avaṟṟuḷ iyalum otta oṇ pal poruḷgaḷ ulappillanavāy viyavāy vittagattāy niṟṟi nī ivai enna vidamangaḷē!*

- *cittirat tēr valavā* – Oh one who can conduct the chariot in amazing ways! His amazing acts include – when drōṇa arranged the armies and waited at the entrance, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) went around him and placed the chariot beyond his reach, stopping him from being able to fight; bhīśma can aim for distant target, and arjuna’s arrow will fall short; hence when bhīśma takes aim, emperumān will drive the chariot too far away from his sight and when arjuna takes him, he will drive the chariot to be too close to bhīśma; this ability of driving the chariot makes āḻvār praise emperumān as “*cittirat tēr valavā*“.
- *tiruccakkarattāy* – Oh one who is having the weapon which can transform day into night \[as done while killing jayadrada\]!
- *ettanai ōr ugamum avaiyāy* – being the controller of yugas such as kruta etc.
- *avaṟṟuḷ iyalum* – residing within the time frame of the yugas.
- *otta …* – Being equal in one aspect, and at the same time being different in another aspect, having distinguished, many types of objects – having many such objects as your prakāra (form). Being equal by the species such as dēva, manuśya et al, but being different due to being individual entities. While all ātmās will be equal due to being embodiment of knowledge, due to the individual identity, they will all be separate/different from one another.
- *vittagattāy niṟṟi nī* – You remain causing amazement for everyone.
- *ivai enna vidamangaḷē* – What kind of togetherness of unrelated objects is this!

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.8.4. Kallavil tamarai

*kaḷ aviḻ tāmaraik kaṇ kaṇṇanē! enakkonṟaruḷāy uḷḷadum illadumāy ulappillanavāy viyavāy veḷḷat tadangadaluḷ vida nāgaṇai mēl maruvi uḷḷap pal yōgu seydi ivai enna upāyangaḷē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

kaḷ – honey; aviḻ – sprouting; atāmarai – like fresh lotus flower; kaṇ – having divine eyes; kaṇṇanē – Oh kriṣṇa!; enakku – for me; onṟu – one; aruḷāy – you should mercifully tell; uḷḷadum – being eternal (due to being nityam) \[cit (sentient beings)\]; illadumāy – being transient (due to having forms which keep changing) \[acit (insentient objects)\]; ulappillanavāy – being innumerable; viyavāy – having entities which have differences, as your prakāra (form); veḷḷam – fully; tadam – having space; kadal uḷ – in milk ocean; vidam – spitting out poison (being invincible by enemies); nāgaṇai mēl – on the mattress called tiruvanantāḻvān; maruvi – fitting well; uḷḷam – in your divine heart; pal – many types; yōgu – thoughts for protection; seydi – contemplating; ivai – these; enna – what; upāyangaḷ – means!

**Перевод:**

**Oh kriṣṇa who is having divine eyes which appear like fresh lotus flowers which sprout honey! you should mercifully tell me one thing; you are having innumerable eternal and transient entities which have differences, as your prakāra; you are contemplating many types of thoughts in your divine heart for the protection of such entities, while fitting well on the mattress called tiruvanantāḻvān who is spitting out poison, in the fully, spacious milk ocean; what means are you contemplating! I am not sure about what is going on in your divine heart. Are you thinking to incarnate? Are you thinking about how to eliminate the hurdles? Are you thinking about how to fulfil the desires \[of such entities\]? Are you thinking about uniting with your devotees? Are you thinking to become victorious? You should firmly and mercifully explain which is the one that you are thinking about.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fourth pāsuram, āḻvār mercifully explains how emperumān is having nitya (eternal) and anitya (transient) entities as his wealth.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “You are having lotus eyes which reveal your enjoyability in the form of supremacy and simplicity, and you are having eternal and transient entities as your wealth; how do you meditate about the protection of such entities?”*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. kaḷ aviḻ tāmaraik kaṇ kaṇṇanē! enakkonṟaruḷāy uḷḷadum illadumāy ulappillanavāy viyavāy veḷḷat tadangadaluḷ vida nāgaṇai mēl maruvi uḷḷap pal yōgu seydi ivai enna upāyangaḷē!*

- *kaḷ aviḻ …* – Oh one who is having divine eyes which resemble freshly blossomed lotus flower and who is obedient! [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s wealth is attractive to āḻvār just as his divine eyes. Alternative explanation – just as his divine eyes is hurting āḻvār, experiencing his wealth too is causing hurt. What is causing hurt here? When one has a doubt due to lack of clarity on a particular subject, one will be distressed, and that would cause hurt. piḷḷān explains “āḻvār is reminiscing what he said in previous decad ‘*sūḻavum tāmarai nāḷ malar pōl vandu tōnṟum*‘ (They came and appeared like fresh lotus flower which is surrounding everywhere)”. Hearing this nanjīyar mercifully said “it will be nice if this too is similar to the experience āḻvār had previously; but this being in a different taste, as the context here is āḻvār being awakened from his previous bewilderment, that principle will not fit here”.
- *uḷḷadum …* – Being the controller for the innumerable ātmās (souls) which are said as existing \[sat\] and the variegated acit (matter) which are said as non-existing \[asat\]. As said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 2.13.96 “*yattu kālāntarēṇāpi nānya samjñām upaiti vai \| pariṇāmādi sambhūtām tat vastu nrupatacca kim \|\|*” (Oh king! That which has no changes such as growth or shrinkage, is called vastu; you analyse about that), since acit is transitory it can be said as non-existing; and since ātmā is always singular in form, it is said as existing.
- *veḷḷat tadam kadal uḷ …* – In milk ocean, fitting well on tiruvanantāḻvān who is spitting poison to stop unfavourable ones from getting close. ādiśēśa would have his fear placed in inappropriate place \[where there is no reason for fear\] and spit poison as said in [nānmugan tiruvandādi 10](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/06/nanmugan-thiruvandhadhi-10/) “*āngāravaram adu kēttu aḻal umiḻum – pūngār aravaṇaiyān*” ([emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) has the furious ādiśēśan as his mattress, who is spitting fire on hearing the praises of brahmā et al during trivikrama avatāram, mistaking it to be an army of attackers).
- *uḷḷap pal yōgu seydi* – You are having many thoughts in your divine mind for our protection. Just as there are so many different cētanas (ātmās), his thoughts are also so variegated and vast. How is this fitting with the preceding and succeeding sections \[this is related to [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) being upāyam, while rest of the pāsuram, decad is focussed on āḻvār enjoying emperumān’s wealth\]? acit, being transitory, should be given up; ātmā \[cit\], being singular in nature, should be pursued; īśvara would be the controller for both acit and cit; such emperumān thinks “This cētana has karma which he performs and has his own desires; unless he develops desire to reach me, he will not have the means to reach me; as he does not have that, what shall be done” and is resting there, thinking about the means to uplift him thinking “what shall we do to make him reach me, while he does not have the desire and does not say as in tiruviruttam 1 ‘inninṟa nīrmai ini yām uṟāmai’ (I cannot bear this lowly life)” as if he said that.
- *ivai enna upāyangaḷē* – As the cētanas are many, their protection will also be in many forms; and since [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is sarvajña (omniscient) he will know all such means; what \[amazing\] means are these!

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.8.5. Pasangal nikki

*pāsangaḷ nīkki ennai unakkē aṟak koṇḍittu nī vāsa malart taṇḍhuḻāy mudi māyavanē! aruḷāy kāyamum sīvanumāyk kaḻivāyp piṟappāyp pinnum nī māyangaḷ seydu vaitti ivai enna mayakkukkaḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ennai – me (who is totally subservient to you, who is fully protected by you); pāsangaḷ – inapt aspects; nīkki – eliminating; unakkē aṟa – to exist exclusively for your sake; koṇḍittu – accepting; vāsam – having great fragrance manifesting total subservience; malar – having flower; taṇ tuḻāy – decorated with fresh tiruttuḻāy (tuḷasi); mudi – having hair; māyavanē – Oh amazingly enjoyable one!; nī – you (who are protector and the enjoyable one); kāyamum – the body which binds; sīvanum – bound soul; kaḻivu piṟappu – the death and birth (which occur to these); āy – while at your disposal; pinnum – further; (nī – you); māyangaḷ – deceptions such as avidyā (ignorance), karma (puṇya/pāpa), vāsanā (impressions), ruci (taste); seydu – created; vaitti – and placed; ivai – these; enna mayakkukkaḷ – what kind of bewildering acts!; aruḷāy – mercifully explain

**Перевод:**

**Oh amazingly enjoyable one who eliminated inapt aspects from me and accepted me to exist exclusively for your sake, who is having hair which is decorated with fresh tiruttuḻāy having flower and great fragrance manifesting total subservience! While the body \[matter\] which binds and the souls which are bound, and their death and birth, at your disposal, you further created deceptions such as avidyā, karma, vāsanā, ruci and placed them. What kind of bewildering acts are these! Mercifully explain.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fifth pāsuram, āḻvār merciful explains the main principle of this decad saying “You have eliminated my attachment towards material aspects and fully sustain on you, yet it is amazing that you are leaving me in this material world”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. pāsangaḷ nīkki ennai unakkē aṟak koṇḍittu nī vāsa malart taṇḍhuḻāy mudi māyavanē! aruḷāy kāyamum sīvanumāyk kaḻivāyp piṟappāyp pinnum nī māyangaḷ seydu vaitti ivai enna mayakkukkaḷē*

- *pāsangaḷ nīkki* – Eliminating ignorance. Eliminating avidyā etc and the bondage of tight ropes which are in the form of karma.
- *ennai* – me who is engaged in worldly pleasures.
- *unakkē aṟak koṇḍittu* – Made me to be as said in tiruvāimoḻi 1.1.1 “*tuyar āṟu sudaradi toḻudeḻu*” (to rise after vorśipping the divine feet which eliminate sorrows).

What did [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) manifest to eliminate the bondage and to make [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) exist fully for him?

- *vāsa malar …* – He manifested the tuḷasi garland on his hair and eliminated āḻvār’s attachment to worldly pleasures and made āḻvār exist fully for him.
- *aruḷāy* – Did you develop me into such \[advanced\] state to torment me by keeping me here?
- *kāyam …* – Body and soul, and birth and death.
- *pinnum …* – After granting knowledge about you, you are still placing me in this samsāram where I don’t fit anymore.
- *ivai enna mayakkukkaḷē* – What kind of inconceivable acts are these! I thought that you accepted me since you eliminated my attachment towards worldly pleasures and developed my attachment towards you; but I am thinking that you are planning to abandon me since you have still kept me in this samsāram; what kind of bewilderment is this!

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.8.6. Mayakka! vamanane!

*mayakkā! vāmananē! madiyām vaṇṇam onṟaruḷāy ayarppāyt tēṟṟamumāy aḻalāyk kuḷirāy viyavāy viyappāy venṟigaḷāy vinaiyāyp payanāyp pinnum nī tuyakkāy nī ninṟavāṟu ivai enna tuyarangaḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

mayakkā – Oh one who mesmerized mahābali’s heart by your form, walk and speech vāmananē – Oh vāmana!; madiyām vaṇṇam – to grant knowledge (after eliminating my confusions); onṟu – one thing; aruḷāy – mercifully explain; ayarppu – forgetfulness; tēṟṟamum – clarity; āy – having at your disposal; aḻal – heat; kuḷir – coolness; āy – having at your disposal; viyavu – amazement; viyappu – objects which cause amazement; āy – having at your disposal; venṟigaḷ – victorious abilities in this world; āy – having at your disposal; vinai – deeds in the form of puṇya (virtues) and pāpa (vices); payan – their respective results; āy – having at your disposal; pinnum – further; tuyakku – the bewilderment of cētanas in these aspects; āy – having at your disposal; (nī – you); ninṟa – in this manner, being the enjoyer of such aspects; āṟu – means; enna – what; tuyarangaḷ – kind of sufferings!

**Перевод:**

**Oh vāmana who mesmerized mahābali’s heart by your form, walk and speech! Mercifully explain one thing to me to grant me knowledge. You are having at your disposal, forgetfulness and clarity, heat and coolness, amazement and objects which cause amazement, victorious abilities in this world, deeds in the form of puṇya and pāpa and their respective results, and the bewilderment of cētanas in these aspects. What kind of sufferings do your means of being the enjoyer of such aspects, cause to this universe!**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the sixth pāsuram, āḻvār becomes astonished enjoying emperumān having contrasting aspects starting with forgetfulness, as his wealth.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. mayakkā! vāmananē! madiyām vaṇṇam onṟaruḷāy ayarppāyt tēṟṟamumāy aḻalāyk kuḷirāy viyavāy viyappāy venṟigaḷāy vinaiyāyp payanāyp pinnum nī tuyakkāy nī ninṟavāṟu ivai enna tuyarangaḷē*

- *mayakkā* – Oh one who mesmerizes anyone who approaches you irrespective of who they are!

When asked “Where did we see that?” [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) explains

- *vāmananē* – Oh you who mesmerized mahābali himself to willingly pour the water and give you the worlds after having his heart melted even though he was torturing the dēvas (celestial beings) on whose behalf you went to him! As said in periya tirumadal “*mannai manam koḷḷa vanjittu nenjurukki*” ([emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) deceived mahābali, the emperor to captivate his heart, by melting it).
- *madiyām …* – You should bring clarity in me so that I don’t get confused between favourable and unfavourable aspects.
- *ayarppāyt tēṟṟamumāy* – He himself said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 15.15](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/15-15/) “*matta: smrutir jñānam apōhanam ca*” (knowledge to identify any entity and forgetfulness originate from me). Being forgetfulness and clarity. Here, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is not focussing contrasting aspects of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s wealth but the variegated nature of the same \[since contrasting aspects are already explained in [tiruvāimoḻi 6.3](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/11/thiruvaimozhi-6-3-1-nalguravum-selvum/) “*nalguravum selvum*“\].
- *aḻalāyk kuḷirāy* – coolness and heat.
- *viyavāy viyappāy* – amazement and objects which cause amazement.
- *venṟigaḷāy* – victories.
- *vinaiyāyp payanāy* – puṇya and pāpa, and their respective result.
- *pinnum nī tuyakkā* – Further, to cause bewilderment even in those who taken refuge in you, you give them anyatā jñānam (understanding an object to be something else) and viparīta jñānam (understanding the object’s attributes incorrectly).
- *nī ninṟa āṟu* – The way you remain.
- *iuvai enna tuyarangaḷē* – You are having these as enjoyable sport; but these are causing us great sorrow.

## 7.8.7. Tuyarangal seyyum

*tuyarangaḷ seyyyum kaṇṇā sudar nīḷ mudiyāy! aruḷāy tuyaram sey mānangaḷāy madanāgi ugavaigaḷāy tuyaram sey kāmangaḷāyt tulaiyāy nilaiyāy nadaiyāy tuyarangaḷ seydu vaitti ivai enna suṇḍāyangaḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tuyarangaḷ – sorrows as per karma; seyyyum – while doing that; kaṇṇā – in his incarnation; sudar nīḷ mudiyāy – oh one who conducts without differentiation in your supreme state!; tuyaram sey – being the cause of sorrow; mānangaḷāy – pride caused by being born in high family heritage etc; madanāgi – (as said in “ētēmadā:“) arrogance which is caused by pride etc; ugavaigaḷāy – pleasures derived from those arrogance etc; tuyaram – sorrows such as affection \[towards such pleasures\]; sey – causing; kāmangaḷāy – lust in the form of thirst for such pleasures; tulaiyāy – the evolution which cause variations in such objects; nilaiyāy nadaiyāy – their existence and movements; tuyarangaḷ – sorrows; seydu – created; vaitti – and placed; ivai – these; enna suṇḍāyangaḷ – what kind of selfish acts which lead to sorrow to others?; aruḷāy – mercifully explain

**Перевод:**

**Oh one who conducts without differentiation in your supreme state and in your incarnation, in giving sorrows as per karma! You have created sorrows such as pride which are caused by being born in high family heritage etc which cause sorrow, the arrogance which is caused by such pride etc, pleasures derived from those arrogance etc, lust in the form of thirst for such pleasures which cause sorrows such as affection etc, the evolutions which cause variations in such objects, their existence and movements, and placed them; what kind of selfish acts are these which lead to sorrow to others? Mercifully explain.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the seventt pāsuram, āḻvār meditates upon emperumān having variegated aspects such as abhimānam (pride) etc which lead to sorrow.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. tuyarangaḷ seyyyum kaṇṇā sudar nīḷ mudiyāy! aruḷāy tuyaram sey mānangaḷāy madanāgi ugavaigaḷāy tuyaram sey kāmangaḷāyt tulaiyāy nilaiyāy nadaiyāy tuyarangaḷ seydu vaitti ivai enna suṇḍāyangaḷē*

- *tuyarangaḷ …* – Oh kriṣṇa who causes sorrows!
- *sudar nīḷ mudiyāy* – Meditating upon his wealth is also as harmful as his divine crown. piḷḷān explains this as āḻvār reminiscing what he experienced previously in [tiruvāimoḻi 7.7.10](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/10/thiruvaimozhi-7-7-10-nirri-murraththul/) “*muṟṟa im mū ulagum viriginṟa sudar mudikkē oṟṟumaik koṇḍadu*” (my heart became attached to the radiant, divine crown \[of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)\] which is spreading like radiance, having the complexion of shining gems and pervading the world which has three types of cētanas and acētanas). Because it has to be enquired and learned from him, it is said to be tormenting.
- *tuyaram sey …* – The pride of being “*dāsōham*” (I am a servitor) is priceless. Unlike that, the pride which causes sorrow by thinking “*sōham*” (I am he \[supreme lord\]).
- *madan …* – Arrogance caused by worldly joy, and the lust which leads to destruction as said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 2.62](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/2-62/) and [śrī bhagavat gītā 2.63](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/2-62/) “sangāt sanjāyatē kāma: … *buddināśāt praṇaśyati*” (from attachment occurs lust … due to destruction of intelligence, he himself perishes). bhagavat kāmam is unlike that \[it leads to uplifting\].
- *tulaiyāy* – as pramāṇam (authentic text) which measures \[one’s state/progress\].
- *nilaiyāy nadaiyāy* – Explains stāvara \[plants, stationary\] and jangama \[animals, mobile\]. Also explains existence and movements \[of previously explained aspects\]. You are causing sorrows in this manner!
- *ivai enna suṇḍāyangaḷē* – This is enjoyable sport for you. But this is causing sorrow for us.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.8.8. Enna sundayangalal

*enna suṇḍāyangaḷāl ninṟittāy ennai āḷungaṇṇā? innadōr tanmaiyai enṟu unnai yāvarkkum tēṟṟariyai munniya mū ulagum avaiyāy avaṟṟaip padaittum pinnum uḷḷāy! puṟattāy ivai enna iyaṟkaigaḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

enna suṇḍāyangaḷāl – with what selfish, sportive activities; enganē – in what manner; ninṟittāy – you remain; en kaṇṇā – oh kriṣṇa who is obedient towards me!; innaduōr – this; tanmaiyai – having particular nature; enṟu – as; unnai – you who are inconceivable; yāvarkkum – even for the most intelligent persons; tēṟṟa – to determine; ariyai – and difficult to know; munniya – being without a beginning and continuously flowing; mū ulagum – three types of worlds such as krutaka, akrutaka and krutākrutaka; avaiyāy – being antaryāmi for them; avaṟṟai – those; padaittu – create; pinnum – further; uḷ – pervading inside as antaryāmi; puṟam – pervading outside as the support; āy – you are having; ivai – these; enna – what; iyaṟkaigaḷ – nature of acts?

**Перевод:**

**Oh kriṣṇa who is obedient towards me!  With what kind of selfish, sportive activities you remain! You are inconceivable to determine saying “you are of this particular nature” even for the most intelligent persons, and are difficult to know. Being the antaryāmi of the three types of worlds such as krutaka, akrutaka and krutākrutaka, which are without a beginning and continuously flowing, you created them, and further pervaded them inside as antaryāmi and outside as the support; of what nature are these acts?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the eighth pāsuram, āḻvār says “How amazing that emperumān creates all the universes, pervades inside and outside and controls everything, and yet he is difficult to comprehend!”*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. enna suṇḍāyangaḷāl ninṟittāy ennai āḷungaṇṇā? innadōr tanmaiyai enṟu unnai yāvarkkum tēṟṟariyai munniya mū ulagum avaiyāy avaṟṟaip padaittum pinnum uḷḷāy! puṟattāy ivai enna iyaṟkaigaḷē*

- *enna …* – Oh kriṣṇa who has enslaved me! What \[amazing\] activities are you having!
- *innadōr …* – You remain as the cause for everything, and cannot be estimated to be of particular nature, even by the most intelligent persons; as said in “*brahmāpi na vētti alpam prayatnata:*” (Even brahmā  does not know a little bit about sarvēśvaran even after trying hard).
- *munniya mū ulagum avaiyāy* – Being the controller for the three worlds which are continuously existing since time immemorial \[and being ancient due to that\].  The term ‘three worlds’ would refer to three types of cētanas \[badda (bound), mukta (liberated), nitya (eternally free)\] or three types of worlds \[krutaka, akrutaka and krutākrutaka\].
- *avaṟṟaip padaittu* – When it is in the context of wealth \[worlds\], it means creating them; when it is in the context of cētanas, it means bestowing them knowledge.
- *pinnum uḷḷāy puṟattāy* – Oh one who pervades as said in nārāyaṇa sūktam “*antar bahiśca*” (pervading inside and outside).
- *ivai enna iyaṟkaigaḷē* – You have them as your sport, and for us they remain amazing.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.8.9. Enna iyarkaigalal

*enna iyaṟkaigaḷāl enganē ninṟittāy en kaṇṇā! tunnu kara saraṇam mudalāga ellā uṟuppum unnu suvai oḷi ūṟoli nāṟṟam muṟṟum nīyē unnai uṇaravuṟil ulappillai nuṇukkangaḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ennai – me; āḷum – enslaving; kaṇṇā – Oh kriṣṇa!; enna iyaṟkaigaḷāl – In which manner; ninṟittāy – you mercifully remain?; tunnu – well seated (in the body); kara saraṇam mudalāga – karmēndriya and jñānēndria such as hands, feet etc; ellā uṟuppum – all organs; unnu – to have the mind deeply engage with; suvai oḷi ūṟu oli nāṟṟam – rasa (taste), rūpa (form), sparśa (touch), śabda (sound) and ganda (smell); muṟṟum – all pleasures; nīyē – to be you only; unnai – you (who are the antaryāmi of them); uṇara uṟil – if we set out to prove; nuṇukkangaḷ – subtle aspects; ulappu – boundary; illai – not present

**Перевод:**

**Oh kriṣṇa who enslaved me! In which manner, you mercifully remain? If we set out to prove that you are the organs such as karmēndriya and jñānēndria such as hands, feet etc which are well seated in the body and all pleasures such as rasa, rūpa, sparśa, śabda and ganda which engage the mind deeply, there is no boundary for the subtle aspects.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the ninth pāsuram, āḻvār meditates upon emperumān having jñānēndriyams (organs of knowledge), karmēndriyam (organs of action) and pleasures such as śabda etc, as his wealth.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. enna iyaṟkaigaḷāl enganē ninṟittāy en kaṇṇā! tunnu kara saraṇam mudalāga ellā uṟuppum unnu suvai oḷi ūṟoli nāṟṟam muṟṟum nīyē unnai uṇaravuṟil ulappillai nuṇukkangaḷē*

- *enna iyaṟkaigaḷāl enganē ninṟittāy en kaṇṇā* – With what type of nature and in what forms, do you remain? Oh kriṣṇa who is obedient towards me!
- *tunnu …* – You are the controller for all the organs such as karmēndriyam and jñānēndriyam which are closely located, and for the pleasures such as śabda etc which are meditated upon and desired for.
- *unnai uṇara uṟil* – If we set out to know you.
- *ulappu illai nuṇukkangaḷē* – There is no end for your greatness. As said in “*aṇīyāmsam aṇīyasām*” (one who is very subtle), ātmās have pervaded acit (insentient objects) everywhere, and [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is pervading both ātmās and acit, in a subtle manner.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.8.10. Illai nunukkangale

*illai nuṇukkangaḷē idanil piṟidennum vaṇṇam tollai nannūlil sonna uruvum aruvum nīyē allit tuḻāy alangal aṇi mārba! en accudanē! valladōr vaṇṇam sonnāl aduvē unākkām vaṇṇamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

idanil – than this; piṟidu – other; nuṇukkangaḷ – subtler; illai – not present; ennum vaṇṇam – to say; tollai – being anādi (beginningless); nal – having qualities such as apauruśēyatvam (not authored by any one) etc; nūlil – in vēda śāstram; sonna – mentioned by the term “tamas” (primordial matter); uruvum – acit (insentient objects); aruvum – cit (sentient beings); nīyē – you became them \[i.e. their antaryāmi\] as mentioned in “sadēva”; alli – having flower string; tuḻāy alangal – tiruttuḻāy (tuḷasi) garland; aṇi – having as decoration; tirumārba – having the divine chest; en – my; accudanē – oh one who is having divine form, and who never lets your devotees fail!; valladōr vaṇṇam – the great way; sonnāl – even if said by vēdam etc; unakku – for you; aduvē vaṇṇam – the manner; Am – it is (you remain obedient towards your devotes)

**Перевод:**

**To say that there is nothing subtler than these \[acit and cit in subtle state\], you became the acit and cit which are mentioned by the term tamas as mentioned in “sadēva“, in the vēda śāstram which is anādi and having qualities such as apauruśēyatvam (not authored by any one) etc; oh my lord who is having divine form with tiruttuḻāy garland (strung with flowers) decorated divine chest, and who never lets your devotees fail! Even if vēdam etc explain your great ways, that is the way it is for you.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the tenth pāsuram, āḻvār is meditating upon emperumān being known through vēdam only, being the cause and having the subtle cētana (sentient) and acētana (insentient) entities as his wealth.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. illai nuṇukkangaḷē idanil piṟidennum vaṇṇam tollai nannūlil sonna uruvum aruvum nīyē allit tuḻāy alangal aṇi mārba! en accudanē! valladōr vaṇṇam sonnāl aduvē unākkām vaṇṇamē*

- *illai nuṇukkam …* – That there is no subtler entity than these. That is, cētanas (sentient) and acētanas (insentient) entities, which are not having any name and form on their own and are indicated only by brahmam’s name and form, which are in causal form, are at your disposal.
- *tollai nannūlil sonna* – taittirīya upaniśat \[which is part of ancient vēda śāstram\] said “*sadēva sōmya idam agra āsīt*” (dear child! there was only sat in the beginning \[during *sruśti*, creation\]). Thus, his being the cause of jagat (universe) is explained.
- *allit tuḻāy …* – bhagavān being with nitya vibhūti (paramapadam) is explained. Having divine chest which is decorated with tiruttuḻāy garland which has flowers in them; oh one who manifests such permanent presence in paramapadam, to me!
- *valladōr …* – This is explained in two ways. When an ātmā talks about bhagavān with all his capability, that will still mean that only a few aspects of yours are spoken, since you cannot be defined in a certain way; at that time, would that \[explained by the ātmā\] be your nature? āḻvār says that it is not so \[not limited to the ātmā’s understanding/explanation\]. Another explanation – those who are friendly \[affectionate\] towards you, though they may not be intelligent, if they say something about [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), instead of thinking “I cannot be comprehended and spoken about by nityasūris amidst whom I reside in śrīvaikuṇṭam. How can a very lowly bound soul in samsāram speak about me as if he knows me well?” and becoming angry, emperumān would \[mercifully\] think that whatever that ātmā spoke about, is his nature.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.8.11. Am vannam

*ām vaṇṇam innadonṟenṟu aṟivadariya ariyai ām vaṇṇattāl kurugūrc catakōpan aṟinduraitta ām vaṇṇa oṇ tamiḻgaḷ ivai āyirattuḷ ippattum ām vaṇṇattāl uraippār amaindār tamakkenṟaikkumē*

**Пословный перевод:**

Am – apt; vaṇṇam – mode; innadu onṟu – of this particular type; enṟu aṟivadu – to know; ariya – one who is difficult; ariyai – sarvēśvara; kurugūrc catakōpan – āḻvār who was granted unblemiśed knowledge and devotion; Am vaṇṇattāl – truly; aṟindu – knew; uraitta – mercifully spoke (matching śrīvaikuṇṭam’s greatness); vaṇṇam – poetic meter; Am – having; oṇ – having goodness of being pursued by everyone; tamiḻgaḷ – in tamiḻ; ivai āyirattuḷ – among the thousand pāsurams; ippattum – this decad; Am vaṇṇattāl – to their ability; uraippār – those who can recite; tamakku – for them; enṟaikkum – for eternal experience; amaindār – prepared

**Перевод:**

**āḻvār who was granted unblemiśed knowledge and devotion truly knew sarvēśvara who is difficult to be known as “he is in the apt mode of this particular type” and mercifully spoke thousand tamiḻ pāsurams which are having poetic meter and goodness of being pursued by everyone; those who can recite this decad among those thousand pāsurams, to their ability, will be prepared for eternal experience \[of bhagavat kainkaryam in paramapadam\].**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the end, āḻvār truly knew sarvēśvaran who cannot be known by anyone and in any way, and mercifully spoke in an apt way for his greatness in paramapadam, in these thousand pāsarams; āḻvār says “Those who can recite this decad among such thousand pāsurams, to the extent possible, will be considered as krutakrutya (one who accomplished the task that needs to be done) always”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. Am vaṇṇam innadonṟenṟu aṟivadariya ariyai Am vaṇṇattāl kurugūrc catakōpan aṟinduraitta Am vaṇṇa oṇ tamiḻgaḷ ivai āyirattuḷ ippattum Am vaṇṇattāl uraippār amaindār tamakkenṟaikkumē*

- *Am vaṇṇam* … – āḻvār sung sarvēśvara who is difficult to be known by anyone as having a particular nature. Even vēdam returned being unable to speak about him \[his qualities\] as said in taittirīya upaniśat “*yatō vācō nivartantē*” (the speech returned).
- *Am vaṇṇam …* – The pāsurams which are mercifully spoken by āḻvār matching [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s greatness.

When it is said “*aṟivadariya ariyai*” (hari who is difficult to be known), how can it be said “*Am vaṇṇattāl uraitta*” (truly knew and spoke)? āren’t these contradictory?

- *aṟindu uraitta* – Because emperumān granted him unblemiśed knowledge and devotion as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.1.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/03/thiruvaimozhi-1-1-1-uyarvara-uyarnalam/) “*mayarvaṟa madinalam aruḷinan*” and āḻvār spoke due to that. When someone tries to know [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) on his own efforts, emperumān is difficult to know; but there is no shortcoming when one tries to know emperumān through the knowledge given by him. Those who try to know emperumān on their own are only rejected in [mudal tiruandādi 4](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/06/mudhal-thiruvandhadhi-4/) “*neṟivāsal tanē āy ninṟānai aindu poṟivāsal pōrkkadavam sātti – aṟivānām”* (Would one who closes the doors of five sensory organs which are difficult to close, know [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is both the path and the goal?)
- *Am vaṇṇam oṇ tamiḻgaḷ …* – Beautiful tamiḻ \[pāsurams\] which match his greatness; another explanation – tamiḻ pāsurams having apt poetic meter and goodness of being pursued by everyone. vaṇṇam – candas (poetic meter). Alternative explanation – vaṇṇam – tone. Pure tamiḻ pāsurams which are having nice tone.
- *tamiḻgaḷ ivai āyirattuḷ ippattum* – This decad among the thousand pāsurams in tamiḻ.
- *Am vaṇṇattāl uraippār* – Now, would those who recite this pāsurams be also blessed by [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) with unblemiśed knowledge and devotion, and recite them in a manner matching his greatness? No – those requirements are only for āḻvār; for the others who recite this decad, it is sufficient if they recite them to their ability.
- *amaindār tamaku enṟaikkumē* – For them, until eternity, they don’t need the left over water \[prasādam – grace\] of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/); it is sufficient for them to have the acceptance of āḻvār. They will remain fully prepared always for the eternal experience.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.9 Enraikkum ennai

## 7.9.1. Enraikkum ennai

*enṟaikkum ennai uyyak koṇḍu pōgiya anṟaikkanṟu ennait tannākki ennāl tannai in tamiḻ pādiya īsanai ādiyāy ninṟa en sōdiyai en solli niṟpanō?*

**Пословный перевод:**

enṟaikkum – Acknowledging first time so that it (such acknovledgement) is eternal; pōgiya – conducting; anṟaikkanṟu – forever; ennai uyyakkoṇḍu – specially blessing me; ennai – me; tannākki – causing the craving in me to exist only for him; ennāl – having me who doesn’t have knowledge etc to sing praises, as the reason; tannai – him (who is having such glories that even vēdam etc give up praising him); in – pāsurams themselves being very sweet; tamiḻ – tamiḻ pāsurams (which are pursuable by all); pādiya – sang; īsanai – natural lord; ādiyāy – being the root cause due to remaining inside me and singing; ninṟa – becoming stable due to that; en sōdiyai – one who revealed his having a radiant form; en – what; solli – say; niṟpan – hold myself together

**Перевод:**

**Acknowledging first time so that it is eternal, specially blessing me and conducting me forever, causing the craving in me to exist only for him, having me who doesn’t have knowledge etc to sing praises, as the reason and being the root cause due to remaining inside me and singing, and  becoming stable due to that, he, the natural lord sang himself in these very sweet tamiḻ pāsurams. What will I say about the one who revealed his having a radiant form, and held myself together? Should I say that he has not acknowledged me first to become favourable towards him? Should I say that he has not carried that forward? Should I say that he has not made me exist fully for him? Should I say that he has not sung these to be claimed as sung by me? Should I say that he has not become radiant due to that? Implies “Saying what, can I hold myself together?”**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the first pāsuram, āḻvār says “You have made me who is very lowly to be the most knowledgeable and engaged me in singing tiruvāimoḻi; I cannot hold myself together thinking about the favour you have done to me”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. enṟaikkum ennai uyyak koṇḍu pōgiya anṟaikkanṟu ennait tannākki ennāl tannai in tamiḻ pādiya īsanai ādiyāy ninṟa en sōdiyai en solli niṟpanō?*

When asked “What favour has he done to melt you like this?”, āḻvār says,

- *enṟaikkum ennai uyyak koṇḍu* – When sarvēśvara pursues and accepts a person once, that person could meditate upon that acceptance forever and be uplifted. As said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 18.77](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/18-77/) “*tacca samsmrutya samsmrutya*” (thinking about it every time) – subsequently thinking about it forever one can sustain oneself. Just as those who were hit by śrī rāma’s arrows will keep talking about incessantly as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 60.3 “*smaran rāghava bāṇānām*” (remembering śrī rāma’s arrow, I became anguished), those who are hit by his qualities will also keep talking for ever about the same. The wound caused by arrow can be healed, but there is no antidote for the mark caused by his qualities. Hence, when sarvēśvara pursues a person once, that can be thought about forever.

When asked “Did he discard after accepting once?” āḻvār says,

- *pōgiya anṟaikkanṟu* – Day after day, he pursued in this manner. Seeing the nature of both [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) and āḻvār, it cannot be handled. If we see the nature of āḻvār who became the target of his pursuing, he cannot handle it \[being overwhelmed\]; if we see emperumān, just as a person who steals from a close friend will feel anguished thinking “Oh! what have I done”, emperumān will feel “I have not done anything for him” even after doing everything, as if he has not done anything.
- *ennait tannākki* – āḻvār is saying that he who was ignorant and incapable as said in “*aṟivilēn*” (ignorant), was transformed to have jñānam (knowledge) and śakti (power) matching [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) himself.
- *ennait tannākki* – \[another explanation\] making him to belong to emperumān.
- *ennāl tannai* – By me who was given strength by emperumān who is beyond the reach of śruti (vēdam), smruti and itihāsa etc. He who is beyond the conception of pramāṇams (tools to gain knowledge) as said in taittirīya upaniśat “*yatō vācō nivartantē*” (Speech returned), and in kauśīdakī upaniśat “*yasyā matam tasya matam – avijñātam vijānatām*” (one who thinks he cannot know, can know and one who thinks he knows, does not know).
- *in tamiḻ pādiya* – While the meanings and emotions are great in this, even the mere words themselves are so sweet.
- *pādiya* – Saying “he made me sing” or “he sang”. As said in taittirīya upaniśat “*ētat sāma gāyannāstē*” (The liberated soul is singing sāma gānam), having experienced togetherness with āḻvār, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) will become blissful and sing saying “*tennā*“.

When asked “How did this sweet prabandam appear?”, āḻvār says

- *īsanai* – Should we say explicitly? Is sarvēśvaran not capable of doing anything! Is this difficult for him?

When asked “You are singing his praises! Why are saying that he is the singer?” āḻvār says,

- *ādiyāy ninṟa* – He became the reason for my singing of poems – I sang due to him.

When asked “How did he become the cause?”, āḻvār says,

- *en sōdiyai* – He disrobed the shawl he was wearing and manifested his divine beauty. Just as many will sing the praises when the curtain is raised, I too called out for him and that ended up as tiruvāimoḻi. By manifesting his divine physical beauty, he placed the inner meaning for the pāsurams.

When asked “If you had also sung praises on him, why would you suffer like this?” āḻvār says,

- *en solli niṟpanō* –  Did I also walk towards him and end up being pursued by him? \[No, he himself pursued first\] Alternatively – Am I feeling content due to the limited result? \[No unlimited experience is the result\] As those who pursued various paths will have \[some\] reward, did I also pursue some means and consider myself to be deserving of the result? Am I relaxed to let me feel content after getting the reward? How will I hold myself together? This is as said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 3.4.4 “*kriṣṇa dvaipāyanam vyāsam viddi nārāyaṇam priyam\| kōhyanya: puṇḍarīkākśān mahābhārata krutbhavēt \|\|*” (Know that kriṣṇa dvaipāyana vyāsa, is nārāyaṇa himself; Who else other than the lotus-eyed lord can write mahābhāratam!). [āḷavandār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/alavandhar/) explains this in this manner – “When [sarvēśvara](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) sets out to do something, is there anything difficult?” Alternatively, [emperumānār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/emperumanar/) says “If āḻvār sings this, he will stop at some point; if emperumān himself speaks, it will go on infinitely; when a young child starts writing, he will write something and stop; if the father or the teacher writes, it will make some sense \[as proper writing\]; but if emperumān gets āḻvār to write, just as in the example of parent-child writing case, the father will pull it to one side and the child will pull it to the other side and will end up being meaningless scribbles; in this manner, while he engaged me in this singing exercise, he made me sing, without being affected by the defects caused by my singing”.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.9.2. En solli nirpan?

*en solli niṟpan? en in uyir inṟonṟāy en sollāl yān sonna in kavi enbittut tan sollāl tān tannaik kīrttitta māyan en mun sollum mū uruvām mudalvanē*

**Пословный перевод:**

en – my; in – attached to worldly pleasures; uyir – ātmā (soul); inṟu – today; onṟāy – as his belonging; ‘en – my; sollāl – words; yān – I, as the author; sonna – spoke; in kavi – sweet poem’; enbittu – making it popular in the world; than – his; sollāl – words; tān – being the author; tannai – having him as the object of the poem; kīrttitta – one who sang praises; en – being inside me; mun sollum – reciting pāsurams before me \[so that I can repeat them\]; māyan – amazing lord; mū uruvāy – having three forms; mudalvan – the causal lord who is present as one; en solli niṟpan – what will I tell to hold myself together?

**Перевод:**

**Considering my ātmā which is attached to worldly pleasures as his belonging today, emperumān made it popular in the world that this sweet poem has been spoken by me, and he himself, being the author, sang praises having him as the object of the poem; what will I tell about the causal lord who is present as one, having three forms, who is the amazing lord residing in me and reciting the pāsurams before me, to hold myself together? Implies that this pāsuram is no match for his favour.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the second pāsuram, āḻvār says “He himself sings his praise and makes it popularly known in the world that I sang them” and becomes blissful seeing emperumān‘s amazing ability thinking “How amazing his quality is”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. āḻvār says “I have been totally lost, due to my ahankāram and mamakāram since time immemorial and was facing away from him; emperumān pursued me without any reason and changed me to be favourable towards him; if I think about this act, how can I hold myself together?” en solli niṟpan? en in uyir inṟonṟāy en sollāl yān sonna in kavi enbittut than sollāl tān tannaik kīrttitta māyan en mun sollum mū uruvām mudalvanē*

- *en solli niṟpan* – Should I say his pursuit of me to be nirhētukam (without any reason) or sahētukam (due to some reason \[action from my side\])? When [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) analyses the self, he does not see any reason; when he analyses [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), he does not see any reason; \[that is\] he does not see any reason for emperumān to abandon him since time immemorial; he does not see any reason for emperumān to suddenly accept him today. Now, what could be the reason? Shall we say “since he is the owner, he could accept his belonging \[ātmā\], when he chooses to do so”? That cannot be said; not only emperumān thinks he merely accepted his own belonging, but he made āḻvār sing his praises, and hearing that, he considers himself and his wealth to come into existence; due to this reason, āḻvār is not able to hold himself together.
- *in uyir* – \[[āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is praising his own self\] as per bhagavān’s opinion ; he is saying in this manner due to being part of the cause to be accepted by bhagavān; alternatively – he is condemning his own self using viparīta lakśaṇā \[using contradictory term to explain a principle\].
- *inṟu onṟāy* – He did not consider his own self to exist before this day \[inṟu – the day when he got unblemiśed knowledge and devotion from bhagavān\]; only on this day, his ‘self’ came to be counted as an entity.

When asked “What did he do with you after accepting you?”, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says,

- *en sollāl …* – He made it popular in the world that the words are mine, that I am the composer and that the poem is very sweet. Any word will only refer / belong to sarvēśvara and not for the lowly samsāri (materialistic person). Now, a cētana does not qualify to have his own independent action or inaction; since his true nature and existence are under the disposal of emperumān. He made this tiruvāimoḻi to be popular in the world as *iniya kavi* (sweet poem); as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.5.11](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/08/thiruvaimozhi-1-5-11-male-maya/) “*pālēy tamiḻar isaikārar pattar paravum āyiram*” (sweet milk like pāsurams which are celebrated by those who are well-versed in tamiḻ, those who are well-versed in music and can sing this and those devotees who understand the meaning); just as kriṣṇa won the war, but stood along with others and praised arjuna for the victory. periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 2.1.2 “*malai purai tōḷ mannavarum …*” ([emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) stood in the chariot witnessing arjuna killing great warriors). *sengaṇ alavalai* (reddish eyed chattering kriṣṇa) one who remains quiet and aloof in paramapadam as said in cāndōjña upaniśat “*avākyanādara:*“, gave up such qualities and started praising arjuna continuously.

When asked “*you said inkavi enbittu,* is it in this manner?”, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says “No” and when asked “How”, he says,

- *than sollāl* … – Words are his, they are spoken by him and he spoke about himself. Only if I am the object of the praise, I could have sung it.

When asked “If he sang on himself, how did he make it popular in the world that you sang about him”, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says,

- *māyan* – Should I tell about it? Does he not have amazing abilities? He had me as a tool and sang himself.

When asked “How did he have you as a tool and sing?”, āḻvār says,

- *en mun sollum* – As he first recites, I would recite after him. If he directly spoke, it will end up like [śrī bhagavat gītā](http://githa.koyil.org/) which is difficult to understand. nambi tiruvaḻudi nādu dāsar would mercifully say “If an expert in śrī bhagavat gītā arrives in an assembly, after the recital/explanation, he will be given some rice and sent off; he would not be invited inside; but if an expert in tiruvāimoḻi recital/discourse arrives, sarvēśvaran himself and the villagers will welcome him themselves, present their own residences for his use and honour him”.

When asked “how did he do that?”, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says,

- *mū uruvā mudalvanē* – Just as [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) created brahmā, taught him vēdam, and made him transfer the knowledge to dēvas and would honour him saying “brahmā gave knowledge to dēvas” and being antarātmā (in-dwelling super soul) of rudra, making him burn down the three towns and would honour him saying “rudra is the tripurāntaka”, emperumān himself sang this prabandam, and then claimed that I did it and gave me the honour. Doing the work himself but honouring others is an ancient habit of his! svētāsvatara upaniśat “*yō brahmāṇam vidadāti pūrvam yō vai vēdāmśca prahinōti*“ ([emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) creates brahmā and imparts vēdam unto him initially) and mahābhāratam karṇa parvam “*viṣṇurātmā bhagavatō bhavasya amitatējasa: tasmāt danurjyā samsparśam saviśēhē mahēśvara:*” (The omnipresent viṣṇu is the antaryāmi for Siva who is infinitely valorous and vorśippable; due to this fact, Siva was able to launch the arrow on the bow during the destruction of the three towns). When asked “Why did he himself do it?” āḻvār says that just as he would directly engage in activities \[as viṣṇu\], he would also have brahmā, rudra et al as his body and would engage in sruśti (creation), samhāram (annihilation) etc and would give the honour to them. Similarly, he sang the prabandam himself and gave the authorship to me.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.9.3. Amudalvan ivan

*āmudalvan ivan enṟu tantēṟṟi en nā mudal vandu pugundu nallinkavi tū mudal pattarkkut tān tannaic conna en vāy mudal appanai enṟu maṟappanō?*

**Пословный перевод:**

mudalvan – he, the causal lord; ivan Am – to be sung by him; enṟu – saying; than – him; tēṟṟi – determined in his mind (upon me); mudal – first; en nā – in my tongue; vandu pugundu – entered; nal – having no shortcoming in the meanings and the words; in – being very reliśable; kavi – poem; tū – having satva śuddi (purity of goodness); mudal – etc; pattarkku – to be enjoyed by those who have bhakti; tān – he himself; tannai – about himself; sonna – spoke; en vāy – for my speech; mudal – cause; appanai – benefactor; enṟu maṟappan – will I forget?

**Перевод:**

**emperumān, the causal lord said “I should be sung by him \[āḻvār\]” and determined in his mind. He first entered my tongue and spoke \[sang\] about himself the most reliśable poem which is having no shortcoming in the meanings and the words, which is having satva śuddi etc, and is to be enjoyed by those who have bhakti. How will I forget the benefactor who is the cause for my speech? Implies that only if his benefactorśip is not shining ever \[which will not happen – it will always be shining\], could he be forgotten. Also this can be construed as making me understand that he is the apt one to be praised. vāy mudal could also mean the apt cause. tū mudal pattar could also mean the main bhaktas (devotees) who are ananya prayōjanas (those who don’t expect anything other than kainkaryam).**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the th pāsuram, āḻvār says “There is no means to forget the great benefactor who used me as a tool and sang about himself”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. āmudalvan ivan enṟu tantēṟṟi en nā mudal vandu pugundu nallinkavi tū mudal pattarkkut tān tannaic conna en vāy mudal appanai enṟu maṟappanō?*

- *āmudalvan ivan enṟu than tēṟṟi* – Bringing in clarity in me that he is the primordial lord; bringing clarity in me to know that he is the one who is spoken about as the upāsyan (target of meditation/worship) in kāraṇa vākyams (portions of vēdam which establish the cause of everything); alternatively – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) bringing clarity about his svarūpam etc in me saying “we are trying to reform samsāram to become like paramapadam; and you are the chosen one”. \[An incident from āḷavandār’s life is highlighted, contextually\] An explanation is mercifully given here – when āḷavandār was mercifully present near the kariya māṇikkāḻvār (kariya māṇikkap perumāḷ sannidi in kāncīpuram), he noticed udaiyavar (iḷaiyāḻvār then) arriving at the eastern side of the sannidi, and he mercifully said ‘*āmudalvan ivan*‘ (he is the leader who will bring glories to our sampradāyam)”.
- *en nā mudal vandu pugundu* – Unlike in the case of śrī vālmeeki bhagavān authoring śrī rāmāyaṇam where first sarvēśvaran blessed brahmā who in turn ordered sarasvati as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam bāla kāṇḍam 2.31 “*maccandādēva tē brahman pravruttēyam sarasvatī*” (Oh sage! sarasvatī has arrived by my grace! You shall write the history of śrī rāma now) to bless śrī vālmeeki bhagavān and made him author śrī rāmāyaṇam, without any intermediaries, he himself entered my tongue directly. Alternatively, it is saying, he became the root for my tongue.
- *nal in kavi* – While all the expected qualities are present in the poem, the words in the poem themselves are so attractive.
- *tū mudal pattarkku* – For the nityasūris, who are untouched by the defects of samsāram ever, as said in tiruvāimoḻi 10.7.11 “*kēttu ārār vānavargaḷ*“, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) spoke to be praised by such nityasūris. Alternatively – it is for the mumukśus (liberation seekers) who are primary in this samsāram.
- *tān tannaic conna* – Instead of him directly authoring it and instead of me authoring it on my own, he entered my tongue and spoke about himself.
- *en vāy mudal appanai* – Saying “my apt benefactor who is the causal lord”; also it could be considered as [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) repeating what he said in “*en nā mudal*” and saying that [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) being the cause for his speech.
- *enṟu maṟappanō* – Since I had previously forgotten him from time immemorial, would I forget even if the future which is available for me to think about him is changed to make me forget him? As it was difficult for me to think about him previously, now it is difficult for me to forget him; now, will I be able to forget him ever?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.9.4. Appanai enru marappan

*appanai enṟu maṟappan en āgiyē tappudal inṟit tanaik kavi tān solli oppilāt tīvinaiyēnai uyyak koṇḍu seppamē seydu tiriginṟa sīr kaṇḍē*

**Пословный перевод:**

en āgiyē – in me; tappudal inṟi – without missing; tanai – him; tān – himself; kavi solli – singing praises; oppu ilā – matchless; tī – cruel; vinaiyēnai – me, the sinner; uyya – to be uplifted; koṇḍu – accepted; seppamē – honestly; seydu tiriginṟa – acting and interacting; sīr – quality (simplicity); kaṇḍu – on seeing; appanai – one who is benefactor in this manner; enṟu – even if he becomes harmful; maṟappan – will I forget?

**Перевод:**

**emperumān accepted me, the matchless cruel sinner; being within me, he sang praises on him, without missing \[anything\], and uplifted me. On seeing his quality of having honest actions and interactions, even if such benefactor becomes harmful, will I forget him?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fourth pāsuram, āḻvār says “There is nothing amazing if he sings his glories himself; but he got me who is unqualified, to do it; I have no means to forget this favour”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. appanai enṟu maṟappan en āgiyē tappudal inṟit tanaik kavi tān solli oppilāt tīvinaiyēnai uyyak koṇḍu seppamē seydu tiriginṟa sīr kaṇḍē*

- *appanai enṟu maṟappan* – When will I forget the benefactor? \[Never\]

When asked “Now, will you be able to forget him even if he causes harm to you? And, what favour did he do which makes you never forget him?”, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says,

- *en āgiyē tappudal inṟit tanaik kavi tān solli* – When having me as a tool to sing, he sang in such a manner that he is unaffected by my defects.
- *en āgiyē* – Being with me; [embār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/embar/) mercifully gives an explanation for this – if he himself sings, it will be excellent; if I sang too, I will try hard and somehow complete it. But, even while having me as a tool and singing, he completed it without getting affected by my defects.
- *tanaik kavi tān solli* – he sang matching the object \[himself\] of praise.
- *oppu ilāt tī vinaiyēnai uyyak koṇḍu* – For having me as a tool and making me sing this, how much did I change from my previous \[materialistic\] state? Have I progressed even a little bit since then?
- *oppu ilāt tī vinaiyēnai uyyak koṇḍu* – āḻvār is saying “I am comparable to him”. Just as there is no match for his omniscience and omnipotence, there is no match for my ignorance and incapability.
- *uyyak koṇḍu* – Accepting me to uplift me as said in taittirīya upaniśat “*santamēnam*” (the learned people accept him to exist).
- *seppamē seydu tiriginṟa* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying “with me who has a mischievous heart, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) interacted honestly just as he would interact with nityasūris who are unaffected by the defects of samsāram”; or he is saying “emperumān who protects me”.
- *sīr kaṇḍē* – On meditating upon such qualities such as seelam (simplicity) etc, when will I forget my benefactor?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.9.5. Sir kandu

*sīr kaṇḍu koṇḍu tirundu nallinkavi nēr pada yān sollum nīrmaiyilāmaiyil ērvilā ennait tannākki ennāl tannai pār paravinkavi pādum paramarē*

**Пословный перевод:**

sīr – his qualities which were revealed; kaṇḍu – seeing; koṇḍu – meditating upon them; tirundu – (to be revealed) being reformed; nal – words and meaning being well formed; in – sweet to listen; kavi – poems; nērpada – to occur; yān – I; sollum – to sing; nīrmai – nature of having knowledge, ability etc; ilāmaiyil – due to not having; ērvilā – inept; ennai – me; than – towards him; ākki – making me to have such knowledge, devotion etc; ennāl – by me; tannai – him; pār – the whole earth which is hard; paravu – to praise; in – sweet; kavi – poem; pādum – due to singing; paramar – is great

**Перевод:**

**Since I did not have knowledge, ability etc to sing the poems which have well formed words and meaning, which are sweet to listen and are reformed to see his qualities which were revealed to meditate upon them, he made me who is inept, to have such knowledge, devotion etc towards him; due to his using me to sing the sweet poem which made the whole earth which is hard, to praise him, he is great.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fifth pāsuram, āḻvār says “While I don’t have the quality and desire to sing his praises, he engaged me as a tool in singing his praises, to have me celebrated by the world! What a supreme lord he is!”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. sīr kaṇḍu koṇḍu tirundu nallinkavi nēr pada yān sollum nīrmaiyilāmaiyil ērvilā ennait tannākki ennāl tannai pār paravinkavi pādum paramarē*

- *sīr kaṇḍu koṇḍu* – Being immersed in his auspicious qualities.
- *tirundu …* – The poems which are orderly, proper (in words and meanings) and sweet.
- *nērpada …* – Even if these qualities are lacking, based on the goodness of the composer of the poem, the poem will also have some goodness; but I don’t have such goodness in me. Hence …
- *ērvilā ennai* – ēr – beauty; I who don’t have it.
- *tannākki* – Saying “making me as good as him”; or saying “making me exist \[exclusively\] for him”.
- *ennāl tannai …* – Having me as a tool, he sung sweet poems, so that everyone in the world praises him \[[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)\]. He made everyone, irrespective of being wise or ignorant, praise him.
- *paramarē* – We need not know his greatness through the phrase in śvētāsvatara upaniśat “*na tat samaśca*” (there is none equal to him); just by seeing him use me as a tool to sing his glories, one can understand his greatness.

## 7.9.6. In kavi padum

*in kavi pādum parama kavigaḷāl tan kavi tān tannaip pāduviyādu inṟu nangu vandu en udan ākki ennāl tannai van kavi pādum en vaigunda nādanē*

**Пословный перевод:**

in – infinitely sweet; kavi – poems; pādum – those who sing; parama kavigaḷāl – by the great poets such as parāśara, pārāśara (vyāsa), vālmeeki et al who have none greater, mudalāḻvārgaḷ (et al); than – matching him; kavi – poem; tān – him (being the instigator); tannai – himself who has infinite greatness; pāduviyādu – instead of making them sing ever; inṟu – today; nangu – with intent; vandu – came; ennudan – with me; ākki – made; en – for me; vaigunda nādanē – manifesting his greatness of being śrīvaikuṇṭanāta (lord of śrīvaikuṇṭam); ennāl – through me; tannai – him who has such greatness; van – perfectly; kavi pādum – will sing poems

**Перевод:**

**Instead of making great poets such as parāśara, pārāśara (vyāsa), vālmeeki et al who sing great, infinitely sweet poems to sing poems which match him, about himself who has infinite greatness, today, with intent, he has come to me, manifesting his greatness of being śrīvaikuṇṭanāta and will perfectly sing poems on him who has such greatness, through me.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the sixth pāsuram, āḻvār becomes blissful thinking “Instead of getting the likes of parāśara, vyāsa, vālmeeki to sing about you, you are using me as a tool to sing perfect poems!”*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. in kavi pādum parama kavigaḷāl than kavi tān tannaip pāduviyādu inṟu nangu vandu en udan ākki ennāl tannai van kavi pādum en vaigunda nādanē*

- *in kavi pādum parama kavigaḷāl* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says “Now, if he wanted to have some one praise him through poems, he could have engaged śrī vēda vyāsa bhagavān, śrī parāśara bhagavān, śrī vālmeeki bhagavān et al, and if he wanted more such poets, mudalāḻvārgaḷ who are glorified as “*sendamiḻ pāduvār*” (pure tamiḻ poets) are also present; leaving them all aside, he engaged me in this task. What an amazing quality is this!” When one \[[bhūtattāḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/bhuthaththazhwar/)\] among the first three āḻvārs was asked to sing a poem, he beautifully sang [iraṇḍām tiruvandādi 75](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/01/irandam-thiruvandhadhi-75/) “*perugu mada vēḻam”* pāsuram. It is explained in detail here:
   - *perugum* … – The male elephant which is letting out (exulting) fluid which is flowing like flood waters.
   - *māppidikku mun ninṟu* – Its \[the female elephant’s\] greatness is such that it can enslave such majestic male elephant which comes at it.
   - *mun ninṟu* – The male elephant stood in front of the female elephant being ready to complete any task saying “What shall I do for you?”
   - *iru kaṇ iḷa mūngil vāngi* – Pulling the young bamboo shoot with two nodes; though it runs around with pride in the forest, due to the great attachment towards the female elephant, it pulled the bamboo shoot carefully
   - *arugirunda tēn kalandu* – Just as all raw materials will be kept ready for tirumanjanam (sacred bathing of the lord), dipping the bamboo shoot in the honey which is readily available in the mountain caves. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is mercifully saying “*kalandu*” as if mixing two fluid substances.
   - *nīttum* – As the male elephant is willingly offering it to the female elephant, the female element stands as if saying “you give it to the one who likes to receive it from you”.
   - *vān kalandu …* – Just as the bamboo shoot and honey are mixed, cloud and [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s divine body complexion are mixed. By the great poets (such as mudalāḻvārgaḷ) who can sing such beautiful poems.
- *than kavi tān tannaip pāduviyādu* – The poem is his. He is the poet. And he is the one who reveals it. Not having them \[such poets\] to reveal his glories with his own words, being the one who reveals it.
- *inṟu nangu vandu* – Saying “Arriving here today to uplift me”. Alternatively, it is read as “*nangu uvandu*” (being well pleased); that is considering it as a pleasure to sing this poem.
- *en udan ākki* – Having me as an inseparable tool.
- *van kavi pādum* – Having rich words, as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 4.5.2](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/02/thiruvaimozhi-4-5-2-maiya-kannal/) “*moyya sollāl*” (made with words which are collected together), instead of being lax (untied).
- *en vaigunda nādanē* – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) thought “as we have the eternal unśakeable paramapadam as the residence, I should make [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) sing thousand pāsurams which remain eternal like vēdam without perishing ever”. He thought that the greatness acquired by being the object of these poems is at par with having paramapadam as residence.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.
