## 7.9.7. Vaigunda nadan

*vaigunda nādan en valvinai māyndaṟac ceykundan tannai ennākki ennāl tannai vaigundanāgap pugaḻa vaṇḍhīngavi seykundan tannai ennāḷ sindittārvanō?*

**Пословный перевод:**

vaigunda nādan – Having the greatness of being śrīvaikuṇṭanāta; val – very strong; en vinai – my sin; māyndaṟa – to destroy; sey – doing; kundan – having the nature; tannai – him; ennākki – making him to be understood by me; ennāl – having me as a tool; tannai – he who is having such greatness; vaigundanāga – not to cause any blemish for his nature; pugaḻa – to praise; vaṇ – magnanimously; tīm – sweet; kavi – poem; sey – to do; kundan – having the nature of favouring; tannai – him; sindittu – think; ennāḷ ārvan – when will I get satisfaction?

**Перевод:**

**Having the greatness of being śrīvaikuṇṭanāta, emperumān had me as a tool, making him to be understood by me, having the nature of destroying my very strong sin, having such greatness of favouring me to sing magnanimous, sweet poem to praise him and not to cause any blemish for his nature; when will I get satisfaction by thinking about such emperumān? Implies, that he will never get full satisfaction. “valvinai māyndaṟac cey kundan” is also explained as one who has the weapon named “kunda” to eliminate the enemies. “kavi sey kundan” is also explained as one who is pure in nature, like “kunda” flower.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the seventh pāsuram, āḻvār says “For this great favour of using me as a tool to sing this infinitely enjoyable poems, I will not be satisfied even if I enjoy him forever”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. vaigunda nādan en valvinai māyndaṟac ceykundan tannai ennākki ennāl tannai vaigundanāgap pugaḻa vaṇḍhīngavi seykundan tannai ennāḷ sindittārvanō?*

- *vaigunda nādan* – Should I be satisfied that the one who favoured me is at par with me? How can I stay calm when the leader of nityasūris comes and pursues me, who is a samsāri? It is even greater than what is explained in śrī rāmāyaṇam kiśkindā kāṇḍam 4.18 “*lōkanāta: purā bhūtvā sugrīvam nātam iccati*” (One who is the lord of the universe, is now desiring to have sugrīva as his leader). He first became lord of the universe to qualify to have śrī sugrīva mahārāja. Whether he attains it or not, he desired for that. Usually, one desires for unattainable goals only. As said in  śrī rāmāyaṇam kiśkindā kāṇḍam 4.21 “*sarāmō vānarēndrasya prasādam abikānkśatē*” (Such śrī rāma desired with noble thoughts, the grace of sugrīva).
- *en val vinai māyndaṟa* – Me who does not desire to eliminate my very strong sin.He said in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.1.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/03/thiruvaimozhi-1-1-1-uyarvara-uyarnalam/) “*mayarvaṟa madinalam aruḷinan*” (mercifully bestowed unblemiśed knowledge and devotion) and did not say “mercifully bestowed unblemiśed knowledge and devotion **to me**” since he did not see himself as an entity before receiving that mercy; the previous state is explained as in taittirīya upaniśat “*asannēva bhavati*” (he does not exist).
- *val vinai māyndaṟa* – The sin is so strong that one would wonder whether even the omnipotent lord can remove it.
- *māyndaṟac cey kundan* – One who was having the ability to eliminate my strong enemy; it is said in [tiruvāimoḻi 2.6.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/04/thiruvaimozhi-2-6-1-vaikundha-manivannane/) “*adiyārkkut tīrttu asurarkkut tmaigaḷ sey kundā*” (He destroys the cruel sins for those who are his servitors, passes them on to those demoniac individuals causing them disaster). It can be construed that “*mukundā*” is cut short in the beginning \[tamiḻ grammar – talaik kuṟai\]. Alternatively kundan could be considered as a divine name of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/). As seen in śrīviṣṇu sahasranāmam “*kumuda: kundara: kunda:*“, kundan is a divine name of emperumān. It is explained there \[in sahasranāmam\] as his great ability of his partiality towards his devotees which makes him collect the vices of his devotees and place them on the demoniac persons. “*tannai ennākki*” implies two meanings – making him \[[āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)\] at par with emperumān and making him \[āḻvār\] fully exist for emperumān.
- *ennāl tannai vaigundanāgap pugaḻa* – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s action is similar to that of a father who gives a cow through charity to his son and will get it back from the son as charity.
- *vaigundanāgap pugaḻa* – paramapadam is called nitya vibhūti (which always exists); but still he thinks that he acquired it due to [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s praises. This is similar to how ātmā is explained in taittirīya upaniśat as “*asannēva*” (non-existing) and “*santamēnam*” (to be existing), while ātmā is eternal. It is seen \[in the world\] that “one becomes great due to being praised by so and so person”; similarly, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) thinks that only after āḻvār’s praises, he feels comfortable in paramapadam.
- *vaṇ tīm kavi …* – One who is having the purity of singing poems which are magnanimous and sweet, and considers such praises as his desired results. As said in tiruvāimoḻi 1.1.1 “*tuyar aṟu sudaradi*” (the divine feet which eliminate sorrow), his sorrows became eliminated after being sung by [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/). Once āḻvār’s sorrows were eliminated, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) thought that he himself had sorrow and got that sorrow eliminated. When the body becomes afflicted with some disease, it is the soul which suffers \[bhagavān being the soul of everyone/everything hence anguishes\]. śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 2.42 “*vyasanēśu manuśyāṇām”* (He feels the pain of the suffering of lowest of humans) – would he be anguished when his divine consorts in their private quarters or his mothers become anguished? “*manuśyāṇām bhruśam bhavati du:kita:*” (the pain of the suffering of lowest of humans). He is not just anguished, but he feels like an elephant which gets stuck in mud. “*du:kitō bhavati*” – for them, they will feel the pain one day but will be healed the next day; but he will feel the pain freshly every day. If the disaster is for the individual, should the resulting sorrow also be for the same individual? Why is [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) anguishing here? emperumān thinks “His suffering is not due to his carelessness but my carelessness” and hence he will feel the anguish freshly everyday. It is said in śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 10.10 “*hrīrēśā hi mamātulā*” (this is a great shame for me). emperumān feels more shame than the ātmā.
- *ennāḷ sindittu ārvanō* – His favour is so great; there is not enough time to show the gratitude; what will I do? After leaving this body, as one will be immersed in experiencing [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), there will not be enough time to show the gratitude; the time we are here, there is not enough time; his favour is great; what will I do?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.9.8. Arvano aliyangai

*ārvanō āḻi am kai em pirān pugaḻ pār viṇ nīr muṟṟum kalandu parugilum ērvilā ennait tannākki ennāl tannaic cīr peṟa in kavi sonna tiṟattukkē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ērvu – jñānam, śakti etc which are required for singing poem; ilā – lacking; ennai – me; tannākki – granting jñānam etc in matters related to him; ennāl – by me; tannai – he who is perfect; sīr – qualities such as śeela (simplicity); peṟa – to acquire; in – sweet; kavi – poem; sonna – spoke; tiṟattukku – manner; āḻi am kai – manifesting beautiful combination of hand and divine chakra; em pirān – my lord who bestowed knowledge and made me realise the relationship with him; pugaḻ – abundance of qualities; pār – in his abodes of incarnations which is highlighted by earth; viṇ – the supreme abode which is in the form of spiritual sky; nīr – in vyūha state of milk ocean; muṟṟum – all cētanas (sentient beings); kalandu – together; parugilum – even if enjoyed; ārvanō – will I be satisfied?

**Перевод:**

**For the manner in which emperumān who is perfect and who granted jñānam etc in matters related to him, to me who is lacking jñānam, śakti etc which are required for singing poem, and who spoke sweet poems to acquire qualities such as śeela etc, even if I enjoyed the abundance of qualities with the ability of all cētanas who are in his abodes of incarnations which is highlighted by earth, in the supreme abode which is in the form of spiritual sky and in vyūha state of milk ocean, will I be satisfied?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the eighth pāsuram, āḻvār says “You got me to sing tiruvāimoḻi; even If I acquire the ability of everyone in the spiritual and material realms to enjoy, and even if I acquired matching faculties such as speech etc and enjoy your such great quality, I will not be satisfied”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Eighth pāsuram. āḻvār say “Am I worried that I cannot feel grateful enough until my existence alone? Will I be satisfied even if I enjoy \[his qualities\] along with all cētanas who have not interest in bhagavat viśayam, with my gratitude and desire, for a long time?” ārvanō āḻi am kai em pirān pugaḻ pār viṇ nīr muṟṟum kalandu parugilum ērvilā ennait tannākki ennāl tannaic cīr peṟa in kavi sonna tiṟattukkē*

- *ārvanō* … – Even if I enjoyed the auspicious qualities of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) with divine disc in his hand, along with the cētanas of the earth and sky \[material and spiritual realm\] – would I be satisfied? The auspicious qualities of emperumān who made his svarūpa (true nature), rūpa (form), guṇa (qualities), vibhūti (wealth) as the object of my poem. He is saying in [tiruvāimoḻi 3.9.9](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/10/thiruvaimozhi-3-9-9-vay-kondu/) “*vāy koṇḍu mānidam pāda vanda kaviyēn allēn āy koṇḍa sīr vaḷḷal āḻip pirān enakkē uḷan”* (I am not a poet who have come to sing manuśya with my mouth which is the sensory organ for speech; the most generous emperumān whose qualities such as ānandam etc are examined in vēdāntam, who is a great benefactor having divine chakra, is present for me exclusively as the distinguished one). Will I be satisfied even if I enjoyed forever with the ability of speech etc, ability to enjoy and the strength of those who are on land, in the sky and in the sea? kalakkai – being together with them. Alternatively – pār and viṇ could be construed as indicating material realm and spiritual realm, and nīr indicates nīrmai (quality), implying “even I enjoyed with the strength and ability to enjoy, of the residents of both realms”.

When asked “What favour did he do, which makes you remain unsatisfied even after enjoying with the ability of everyone, forever?” [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says,

- *ērvu …* – Here, it is indicating that he has no goodness in him. Previously (in fifth pāsuram), he indicated that he did not even have the desire to sing him; here, he says that he does not even have the qualification which is the root for that desire. While it is said in bruhadāraṇyaka upaniśat 6.4 “*brāhmaṇā vividiśanti*” (brāhmaṇas desire to know about brahmam), the qualification is explained subsequently there “*yajñēna dānēna tapasānāśakēna*” (by yajña (sacrifice), dāna (charity), tapas (penance) etc); here, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying that he even lacks that qualification.
- *ennāl tannaic cīr peṟa in kavi sonna* – The poem which brings about greatness to [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is perfect in all auspicious qualities. sarvēśvaran was thinking that by this song of mine, he will acquire new glories. The sweetness of the poem is such that even if the qualities are not highlighted properly.
- *in kavi sonna tiṟattukku* – For the manner in which the sweet poems were spoken. Other qualities become useless \[in comparison to this quality of making me sing his glories\].

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.9.9. Tirattukke tuppuravam

*tiṟattukkē tuppuravām tirumālin sīr iṟappedir kālam parugilum ārvanō? maṟappilā ennait tannākki ennāl tannai uṟappala in kavi sonna udavikkē*

**Пословный перевод:**

maṟappu ilā – not having forgetfulness; ennai – me; tannākki – granting knowledge which will ensure that I don’t forget him; ennāl – through me; tannai – him; uṟa – continuous words \[without break\]; pala – in the count of thousand; in – sweet; kavi – poem; sonna – spoke; udavikku – for the favour; tiṟattukku – the acts in which he engaged; ēy – matching; tuppuravu Am – one who has śakti (ability); tirumālin – śriya:pati’s (divine consort of śrī mahālakśmi); sīr – qualities such as audārya (magnanimity), śeela (simplicity), saulabhya (easy approacability) etc; iṟappu edir kālam – having the ability of all cētanas from past and future; parugilum – even if enjoyed; ārvanō – will I be satisfied?

**Перевод:**

**emperumān spoke the sweet poem \[prabandam\] which has thousand continuous pāsurams through me who is not having forgetfulness \[due to not remembering him previously\] by granting knowledge which will ensure that I don’t forget him; for his such favour and the śakti who has matching the acts in which he engaged, will I be satisfied even if I enjoyed the qualities such as audārya, śeela, saulabhya etc,  having the ability of all cētanas from past and future?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the ninth pāsuram, āḻvār says “Even if I enjoyed the great benefactor who made me sing his glories, with the ability of all cētanas (sentient beings), I will not be satisfied”*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

Ninth pāsuram. Previously, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) said “Even if I enjoyed the great benefactor who sung him through me, with the enjoyability of all cētanas forever, I will not be satisfied?” Here, he is saying “even if I enjoyed with that ability to enjoy, in past and future, I will not be satisfied”.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. tiṟattukkē tuppuravām tirumālin sīr iṟappedir kālam parugilum ārvanō? maṟappilā ennait tannākki ennāl tannai uṟappala in kavi sonna udavikkē*

- *tiṟattukkē …* – In any situation, if he needs to just use a blade of grass to complete a task, he has the ability to do so. tuppuravu – sāmartyam – ability. What is the reason for such ability? Since he is śriya:pati, he has the ability to accomplish any task.  Such śriya:pati’s auspicious qualities \[are to be enjoyed\]. When a person starts a task and when it takes shape towards completion, people would say “he has auspicousness, when a śrīmān (auspicious person) starts something, it will complete successfully”.
- *iṟappu edir …* – Even if I try to enjoy after acquiring the tools like speech etc of all cētanas and their ability to enjoy etc, since the time left for me to live is short, there won’t be enough time to just show my gratitude. Instead of having to say as in tiruvāimoḻi 7.9.7 “*ennāḷ sindittārvanō*” (when will I think and be satisfied?), will I ever be satisfied even if I have the tools of everyone and even if I enjoyed in the past and the future?

When asked “Which favour of his are you thinking about which will leave you unsatisfied even if you enjoyed with the tools of everyone forever?” [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says,

- *maṟappilā …* – I who am not forgetful. āḻvār is mercifully saying in this manner to indicate that he has not thought about him \[[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)\] ever to start with, only then one can forget. But should he say “*maṟappilā*“? Only where there is remembrance, there is forgetfulness. Hence, he is saying “I never think about him”.
- *maṟappilā ennait tannākki* – Did he pursue me ignoring my occasional remembrance which was followed by forgetfulness? Engaging me who never had any thought about him to start with, in his service.
- *ennāl* – Engaging me who is not even atoning as said in periya tirumoḻi 6.2.2 “*maṟandēn unnai munnam*” (I previously forgot you).
- *tannai uṟap pala in kavi sonna* – nanjīyar mercifully explains this as follows – The way [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) clearly explained [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) and his qualities which were even given up by vēdam as in taittirīya upaniśat “*yatō vācō nivartantē*” (the speech returned). piḷḷān explains “Matching sarvēśvara’s stature”.
- *pala in kavi sonna* – As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam bāla kāṇḍam 4.2 “*catur vimśat sahasrāṇi ślōkānām uktavānruśi:*” (Sage vālmeeki recited twenty four thousand ślōkams), āḻvār is amazed thinking “In this samsāram, emperumān has sung these thousand distinguished pāsurams \[through me\]!”. For such favour, even if enjoyed śrīman nārāyaṇan’s qualities in the past and future, will I be satisfied?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.9.10. Udavik kaimmaru

*udavik kaimmāṟu en uyir enna uṟṟeṇṇil aduvumaṟṟāngavan tannadu ennāl tannai padaviya in kavi pādiya appanukku eduvum onṟum illai seyvadu ingum angē*

**Пословный перевод:**

udavi – for the favour of engaging me in singing tiruvāimoḻi; kaimmāṟu – favour in return; en uyir – my soul; enna – as; uṟṟu – aptly; eṇṇil – if we tried to determine; āngu – in that state of favouring in return; aduvum – that soul; maṟṟu – further; avan tannadu – as it is exclusively subservient to him; ennāl – through me; tannai – him; padaviya – soft; in – sweet; kavi – poem; pādiya – sang; appanukku – for the benefactor; ingum – in this \[material\] realm; angum – in that spiritual realm; seyvadu – can be done; eduvum – anything even infinitesimal; onṟum illai – not present

**Перевод:**

**For emperumān‘s favour of engaging me in singing tiruvāimoḻi, if we aptly tried to determine \[offering\] my soul as the favour in return, in that state of favouring in return, since that soul is exclusively subservient to him, what infinitesimal act can be done in this material realm and that spiritual realm for the great benefactor who made me sing soft, sweet poem on him? Implies, after acquiring knowledge, for the ātmā which is always subservient to bhagavān, irrespective of whether in the state of being mumukśu (one who is desiring of liberation) or a mukta (one who is liberated), there is no eligibility for offering itself.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the tenth pāsuram, āḻvār is feeling anguished for not being able to carry out a favour in return for emperumān‘s great favour of engaging āḻvār in singing tiruvāimoḻi.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Tenth pāsuram. When asked “Instead of grieving that you don’t have enough time to show your gratitude to him, can you not give something, which you own, in return, and sustain yourself?” āḻvār says “I could do that, if I also have some belongings like īśvaran is having; but I don’t have any such belongings”. udavik kaimmāṟu en uyir enna uṟṟeṇṇil aduvumaṟṟāngavan tannadu ennāl tannai padaviya in kavi pādiya appanukku eduvum onṟum illai seyvadu ingum angē*

- *udavi* – udavi – favour; kaimmāṟu – favour in return for that.
- *en uyirenna* – ātmā which is eternal, has jñāna (knowledge) and ānanda (bliss) as identity, and is praiseworthy; can it be offered? Had emperumān not blessed unblemiśed knowledge and devotion to start with, we can do that; first he gave knowledge; this act of seeking to do a favour in return on thinking about his favour, is similar to *ātma samarpaṇam* (offering oneself) during bewildered state. While being bewildered, one should offer oneself; but on acquiring clarity, one cannot remain saying “I have offered myself to him”; considering “I have offered my belonging, i.e. myself to him” is lower than the *ātmāpahāram* (illegal claiming of self as independent instead of considering self to be dependent on bhagavān) which was being done since time immemorial. If that was done, the previous state of stealing of bhagavān’s belonging continues; also, it is false to say that one has acquired real knowledge. To avoid sarva mukti prasangārtam (to eliminate the question of everyone getting liberated) one has to offer the soul; but when one acquires clarity in the heart/mind, one will accept bhagavān’s belonging \[ātmā\] to be his. [āḷavandār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/alavandhar/) too said in stōtra ratnam ślōkams [52](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/02/sthothra-rathnam-52/) and [53](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/02/sthothra-rathnam-53/) “… *mayā samarpita: , … atavā kinnu samarpayāmi tē*” (I have offered myself … (After knowing that everything is yours) what can I offer to you?) [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) too said in [tiruvāimoḻi 2.3.4](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/02/thiruvaimozhi-2-3-4-enadhu-aviyul/) “*enadāvi tandoḻindēn*” (I submitted my self unto him) and “*enadāvi yār yān Ar*” (neither the actions of the ātmā nor the doerśip of the ātmā that is submitting are under my control). As one acquires true knowledge and gets closer to the goal, one will observe both aspects. Hence, this explains the ātmā’s exclusive/deep subservience which highlights that it is inapt for the ātmā to offer itself and then show gratitude \[since ātmā is always owned by bhagavān\].
- *uṟṟeṇṇil* – If one look at this superficially, one can offer oneself; but when a little bit of knowledge is acquired in the heart, and when the true nature of the self is analysed, one cannot offer oneself.
- *aduvum* – ātmā too.
- *maṟṟu* – others, i.e. the belongings of the ātmā.
- *āngu avan tannadu* – It is [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s, when one needs to sustain oneself by doing something in return.
- *ennāl …* – By me who is not supposed to even show gratitude, and he who is a great benefactor.
- *padaviya in kavi pādiya appanukku* – The benefactor who sang this poem to cause new glories for himself, who is the object of the poem.
- *eduvum onṟum illai seyvadu* – There is nothing to be done.

When asked “When one is here in this material realm, he cannot do anything due to limited knowledge \[and ability\]; but is there any restriction in doing something in return after being liberated and acquiring full knowledge \[and ability\]” [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says,

- *ingum angē* – at least here in material realm, due to dēhātmābhimānam \[identifying body with the soul\], as one roams around thinking “I, mine”, one may think “there is something to be done”; but there, in spiritual realm, after having eliminated all such limitations \[with fully expanded knowledge\], it is not necessary to explain that one need not do anything \[it is obvious that one will have clear understanding of that\]; as said in cāndōjña upaniśat 8-12-2 “*svēnarūpēṇa abhiniśpadyatē*” (realises his basic nature) – where one acquires true knowledge about self, hurdles will naturally be removed.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.9.11. Ingum angum

*ingum angum tirumālanṟi inmai kaṇḍu anganē vaṇ kurugūrc catakōpan inganē sonna ōr āyirattippattu enganē sollilum inbam payakkumē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ingum – during the time of surrender, while in this leelā vibhūti (material realm); angum – during the time of kainkaryam (service), while in the nitya vibhūti (spiritual realm); tirumāl – one who has śriya:patitva (being the lord of śrī mahālakśmi) which is part of both pūrva vākya (first sentence) and uttara vākya (second sentence) \[of dvaya mahā mantram\]; anṟi – other than; inmai – not present; kaṇḍu – thinking about; anganē – having such state; vaṇ – magnanimous; kurugūrc catakōpan – āḻvār; sol – accepting service by speech; inganē – in this manner; sonna – mercifully spoke; ōr āyirattu – among the thousand pāsurams; ippattum – this decad; enganē – leaving out the meaning in the form of his gratitude; sollilum – even if \[one\] just recited the words; inbam – endless bliss caused by experiencing bhagavān; payakkum – will grant

**Перевод:**

**The magnanimous āḻvār thinks about none other than the one who has śriya:patitva (being the lord of śrī mahālakśmi) which is part of both pūrva vākya (first sentence) and uttara vākya (second sentence) \[of dvaya mahā mantram\] being present during the time of surrender, while in this leelā vibhūti and during the time of kainkaryam (service), while in the nitya vibhūti; and in that state, he mercifully spoke about emperumān accepting his service by speech, in this decad among the thousand pāsurams; even if one recites the mere words of such decad, leaving out the meaning in the form of his gratitude, the decad will grant endless bliss caused by experiencing bhagavān.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the end, āḻvār says “Whichever way this decad is recited, it will bring about pleasure”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. ingum angum tirumālanṟi inmai kaṇḍu anganē vaṇ kurugūrc catakōpan inganē sonna ōr āyirattippattu enganē sollilum inbam payakkumē*

- *ingum angum tirumāl inṟi inmai kaṇḍu* – Meditating upon the principle that for the ātmā, both while pursuing the means and attaining the apt goal, in this realm and the other realm, there is no refuge other than śriya:pati; while engaging in service, one should approach bhagavān through pirātti as said in tiruvāimoḻi 9.2.1 “*paṇḍai nāḷālē pangayattāḷ tiruvaruḷum nin tiruvaruḷum koṇḍu nin kōyil sīyttu*” (with the ancient, divine mercy of śrī mahālakśmi who is seated on a lotus flower and your divine mercy, cleaning your temple); even while surrendering to [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), one should approach him through her. She is the one with great compassion to place some goodness even on the rākśasis (demoniac maids of rāvaṇa) saying “Just because they troubled me as per rāvaṇa’s orders, would they do it now?” as seen in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 116.41 “*hatē tasmin na kuryu:*“.
- *anganē …* – We too, when we are with a sadācāryan (true ācārya) who instructs that there is no refuge for us other than śriya:pati, will hear and agree at that time \[other times, we may deviate\]; unlike that, āḻvār has apt actions always matching that thought.

When asked “But, are the mind, speech and body in harmony?” āḻvār says,

- *inganē …* – All the thousand pāsurams were spoken with the same mood.

When asked “These pāsurams were mercifully spoken by you with mind, speech and body in harmony; for those who recite these pāsurams, is it necessary that their mind, speech and body be withdrawn from worldly pleasures? You were in the state of being fully focussed as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 6.5.11](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/02/thiruvaimozhi-6-5-11-sindhaiyalum/) ‘*sindaiyālum sollālum seygaiyinālum dēvapirānaiyē tandai tāy enṟadainda’* (Determining dēvapirān only as father and mother, and having attained him with the three faculties); is the same expected from others who recite these pāsurams?” āḻvār says “that restriction is only for me; those who learn this are not required to be so”.

- *enganē sollilum inbam payakkumē* – It will cause bliss whichever way it is recited. īsvaran mercifully glances at those who learned my pāsurams just because they learned them; otherwise, if one can engage with his mind, speech and body, that is ideal; this is explained to emphasise that even when recited without such attitude, there is no difference in the result.
- *inbam payakkumē* – As said in taittirīya upaniśat ānandavalli 7 “*ēśahyēvānandayāti*” (he – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) – himself makes jīvātmā ecstatic), the bliss acquired by eternal bhagavat anubhavam will be granted.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.10 Inbam payakka

## 7.10.1. Inbam payakka

*inbam payakka eḻil malar mādarum tānum ivvēḻulagai inbam payakka inidudan vīṟṟirundu āḷginṟa engaḷ pirān anbuṟṟamarnduṟaiginṟa aṇi poḻil tiruvāṟanviḷai anbuṟṟamarndu valanjeydu kai toḻu nāḷgaḷum āgungolō?*

**Пословный перевод:**

eḻil – having qualities such as saundaryam (beauty); malar mādarum – lakshmi who is enjoyable due to lotus being her residence; tānum – him (who is distinguished to be pursued by such enjoyable persons); inbam – (mutually) blissful act; payakka – to cause; inidudan – in a joyful state; vīṟṟirundu – present (manifesting his supremacy); ivvēḻulagai – the worlds which are seven categories (four types of acētanas namely vyakta (manifested matter), avyakta (unmanifested matter), kāla (time) and sudda satva (matter made of pure goodness) and three types cētanas namely nitya (eternally free), mukta (liberated), badda (bound) souls); inbam payakka – to cause great bliss; āḷginṟa – accepting service; engaḷ pirān – the great benefactor who accepted our service too, through the faculty of speech; anbuṟṟu – desiring (that this is a peaceful abode to accept our service); amarndu – fitting well (even better than in paramapadam, kśīrābdi etc); uṟaiginṟa – residing (forever); aṇi – beautiful; poḻil – garden; sūḻ – surrounded; tiruvāṟanviḷai – tiruvāṟanviḷai; anbuṟṟu – desiring (that this is a nearby abode to serve him); amarndu – fitting well (instead of leaving away, searching for other benefits); valam seydu – performing activities (which match our nature); kai toḻum – enjoying with joined palms; nāḷgaḷum – days; āgum kol – will they occur?

**Перевод:**

**lakshmi who is enjoyable due to lotus being her residence, and who is having qualities such as saundaryam and emperumān himself, are seated in a joyful state to cause blissful acts; such great benefactor who accepted the service of the worlds which are in seven categories to cause bliss and our service too, is desirously residing in tiruvāṟanviḷai fitting well, which is surrounded by beautiful garden; will those days of performing activities for him and enjoying him with joined palms occur for us?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the first pāsuram, āḻvār yearns thinking “this is the apt time to enter tiruvāṟanviḷai and serve emperumān blissfully”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*In the first pāsuram, āḻvār says “Will this be the apt time for me to enjoy and serve the perfect lord who is mercifully residing in tiruvāṟanviḷai along with lakshmi”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. inbam payakka eḻil malar mādarum tānum ivvēḻulagai inbam payakka inidudan vīṟṟirundu āḷginṟa engaḷ pirān anbuṟṟamarnduṟaiginṟa aṇi poḻil tiruvāṟanviḷai anbuṟṟamarndu valanjeydu kai toḻu nāḷgaḷum āgungolō?*

- *inbam payakka* – Just as [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is explained in vēdam “*ānandamaya:*” (totally blissful), will acquire new bliss when he unites with samsāri cētana (bound soul) who is filled with sorrow, acquires bliss when he unites with pirātti \[who is equally enjoyable as himself\]; he will be bewildered due to the union with pirātti as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 3.10.8](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/11/thiruvaimozhi-3-10-8-allalil-inbam/) “*alli malar magaḷ bōga mayakkukkaḷāgiyum  niṟkum ammān*” (standing with blissful form due to union with śrī mahālakśmi, the best among women, who is infinitely enjoyable due to having lotus flower as her abode). \[śrī rāmāyaṇam bāla kāṇḍam 77.26 is explained here to highlight that there is great bliss when perumāḷ and pirātti unite. The same is explained briefly in [tiruvāimoḻi 2.3 pravēśam](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/02/thiruvaimozhi-2-3-unil-vazh/) too\] *rāma:* – śrī rāma, who rid śrī paraśurāmāḻvān of his pride, arrived at the capital city śrī ayōdyā, remained obedient towards cakravarti daśarata and the great sages, and conducted himself most righteously. *tu* – After serving his parents etc, when he started romancing pirātti, he was totally different to be thought f as “Has he previously learned vātsyāyanam (a text on the art of love) and engaged in the art of love!” Previously when we was engaged in righteous activities, he conducted himself to be thought of as “Has he ever experienced the art of love?” but now he makes one think “Has he ever learnt to conduct himself righteously?” *sītāyā sārdam* – pirātti, not being boron to a lady, was a great match for [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) in paramapadam in not having any shortcoming in the freshness after uniting with him; still, even when emperumān transforms himself by incarnating as a human, he remained primary in enjoyment even pushing her to the background; what is the reason for that? It is due to his being a prince who is focussed on just enjoyment. *vijahāra* – It is just eagerness, and he has not even started the enjoyment; it took time to setup the scene; there was not enough time to even start. *bahūnrutūn* –  Though he enjoyed for twelve years as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 33.17 “*samādvādaśa tatrāham*“, he is using it to identify using the word “*rutu*” to imply how he enjoyed each season with the apt flowers etc; he is implying how he enjoyed with apt materials for winter and summer seasons. *manasvī* – When it comes to romance, her eagerness in comparison to his eagerness in his heart is like placing a horse in front of an elephant \[though elephant can chase the horse, it can never reach it\]. *tatgata:* – Unlike an entity unites with another entity of the same kind, he united with pirātti as jāti (species) and guṇas (qualities) remain together with an entity; both said as seen in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 21.6 “*ananyā rāghavēṇāham*” (I always remain united with śrī rāma) and śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 122.19 “*ananyāhi mayā sītā*” (Does sītā not remain united with me always?). “*tasyānityam hrudi samarpita:*” – As sītā knew śrī rāma’s nature before he engaged with her, she thought “this great person, standing humbly in front of me, is the greatest! What a quality!” and since he is always thinking about her, and as she too is having her heart attached to him only, he remained in a manner that she offers herself to him fully. By “*tatgata:”*, how he placed himself at her disposal, is explained. By “*nityam hrudi samarpita:*“, how she placed herself at his disposal, is explained. In this manner, they were mutually enjoying each other every moment, as if a person who never enjoyed bliss before finds bliss.
- *eḻil malar mādarum* – sītāp pirātti has become as mentioned in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 16.5 “*raghavōrhati vaidēhim*” (śrī rāma suits sītā pirātti in all aspects),
- *tānum* – emperumān too has become as mentioned in śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 34.18 “*yasya sītā bhavēt bhāryā*” (to whom, sītā would become wife) and śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 37.18 “*yasya sā janakātmajā*” (janaka’s daughter sītā, who is the wife of).
- *ivvēḻulagai inbam payakka* – As said in samkśēpa rāmāyaṇam 1.89 “*rāmas sītām anuprāpya rājyam punar avāptavān \| prahruśtamuditō lōka:*” (After redeeming sītā, śrī rāma also got back his kingdom; the world became joyful), when the mother and father remain together and care for the children, the children will have no worries. Thus, as there is joy in their union, and as the world becomes joyful seeing their togetherness, they \[emperumān and pirātti\] became \[more\] joyful seeing that, just as a mother will become joyful seeing her child drink her milk.
- *inidudan vīṟṟirundu āḷginṟa* – emperumān who brings great joy to the world by his presence, feels great joy as if he has found something valuable, resides joyfully thinking “we have now got a divine abode which is suitable for us to hear tiruvāimoḻi”.
- *engaḷ pirān* – \[reason for “*engaḷ*” – plural\] After \[singing\] [tiruvāimoḻi 2.7](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/04/thiruvaimozhi-2-7-kesavan-thamar/) “*kēśavan tamar*” padigam, he was no longer a loner \[as he considered to be in association of many devotees\]. The benefactor who engaged me in singing tiruvāimoḻi.
- *anbuṟṟu* – Manifesting his liking towards the divyadēśam thinking “we will get a divine abode to hear tiruvāimoḻi”
- *amarndu* – desiring it so much that he did not expect anything other than residing there
- *uṟaiginṟa* – Unlike avatārams (incarnations) where he leaves for paramapadam (in a short duration), residing eternally.
- *aṇi poḻil sūḻ tiruvāṟanviḷai* – tiruvāṟanviḷai which appears similar to the apt abode (of paramapadam), having the vastness to let him and his associates from paramapadam to reside and hear, and which is surrounded by beautiful garden. Whatever abode is desirable for [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) will be desirable for his followers too as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 17.15 “*tēnatētam anuvratā:*” (hence everyone was devoted to śrī rāma).
- *anbuṟṟu* – As emperumān felt “we found a suitable place to hear tiruvāimoḻi”, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) too became greatly attached to this divyadēśam thinking “we found a suitable place to make him hear tiruvāimoḻi”.
- *amarndu* – Without seeking any other benefit than being in that abode.
- *valam seydu* – Performing circumambulation etc.
- *kai toḻu nāḷgaḷum āgum kolō* – śrī kausalyā said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 24.37 “*apīdānīm sakālssyāt*” (It will be good, if the day of your return from the forest is today itself); just as seen there “if he cannot avoid his trip to the forest, let the day of his return be today”, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying “would this day of yearning become the day of enjoyment?”

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.10.2. Agungol

*āgungol? aiyam onṟinṟi agalidam muṟṟavum īradiyē āgum parisu nimirnda tirukkuṟaḷappan amarnduṟaiyum māgam tigaḻ kodi mādangaḷ nīdu madiḷ tiruvāṟanviḷai māganda nīr koṇḍu tūvi valanjeydu kai toḻak kūdungolō?*

**Пословный перевод:**

onṟu – a; aiyam inṟi – without doubt; āgum kol – will occur?; agal – vast; idam – worlds; muṟṟavum – all; īradiyē āgum parisu – to be consumed in two feet; nimirnda – mercifully grew; tirukkuṟaḷ – śrī vāmana; appan – great benefactor; amarndu – seated (firmly even more than dēva lōkam (heaven) where he was born as śrī vāmana); uṟaiyum – residing; mā – vast; kam – in the sky; tigaḻ – shining; kodi – having flags; mādangaḷ – mansions; nīdu – tall; madiḷ – having forts; tiruvāṟanviḷai – tiruvāṟanviḷai; mā – distinguished; gandam – having fragrance; nīr – water; koṇḍu – with; tūvi – sprinkling; valam seydu – circumambulating; kai toḻa – to perform anjali (joined palms); kūdungolō – would it be possible?

**Перевод:**

**śrī vāmana, the great benefactor, mercifully grew to consume all the vast worlds under his divine feet; such emperumān is seated and residing in tiruvāṟanviḷai which is having  mansions with flags which are shining in the vast sky and tall forts; will it be possible to sprinkle water with distinguished fragrance, circumambulate and perform anjali there? Will it occur without a doubt? It appears that, āḻvār is subsequently highlighting that it is indeed possible. “Without a doubt” can be associated with emperumān measuring the world too.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the second pāsuram, āḻvār says “Will I be able to sprinkle wondrously fragrant water, circumambulate and worship with joined palms in tiruvāṟanviḷai!”*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. āgungol? aiyam onṟinṟi agalidam muṟṟavum īradiyē āgum parisu nimirnda tirukkuṟaḷappan amarnduṟaiyum māgam tigaḻ kodi mādangaḷ nīdu madiḷ tiruvāṟanviḷai māganda nīr koṇḍu tūvi valanjeydu kai toḻak kūdungolō?*

- *āgum kol aiyam onṟu inṟi* – Instead of being assertive, this more appears to be highlighting [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s longing. Will it be possible for us without a doubt? Alternatively – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) measured the worlds with two steps, without any doubt. Due to his childishness, though he is capable to do everything, he initially thought “will this be possible for us or not?”.
- *agalidam muṟṟavum* – Grew to have the vast earth and heavenly worlds in two steps. He measured earth, heaven etc with two steps, thinking that he would capture mahābali with the other step \[as he requested three steps of land\].
- *tirukkuraḷappan* – śrī vāmana, the great benefactor.
- *amarnduṟaiyum* – Unlike in śrī vāmanāvatāram, where he returned to tiruppāṟkadal and reclined there immediately after helping indra, here he is residing permanently.
- *māgam tigaḻ …* – tiruvāṟanviḷai which has mansions having flags which shine in the vast sky, measured by his divine feet, and having tall forts.
- *māganda nīr …* – śrī śatrugnāḻvān poured fragrant, cool water from śrī nandigrāmam to śrī bharatvāja bhagavān’s āśramam \[to welcome śrī rāma\] as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 130.6 “*sincantu vasūdām krutsnām himaśītēnavāriṇā*” (Let the earth be drenched with cool water); similarly will I also be able to sprinkle greatly fragrant water and engage in favourable activities there?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.10.3. Kudungol?

*kūdungol? vaigalum gōvindanai madusūdanaik kōḷariyai ādu paṟavai misaik kaṇḍu kaitoḻudanṟi avan uṟaiyum pādum perum pugaḻ nānmaṟai vēḷviyaindu āṟangam panninar vāḻ nīdu poḻil tiruvāṟan viḷai toḻa vāykkungol? niccalumē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vaigalum – always; kūdum kol – will this occur?; gōvindanai – one who is crowned to protect the cows; madusūdanai – being the destroyer of madu (who was an enemy of the protected ones); kōḷariyai – one who cannot be overcome for the enemies, like a very radiant splendorous lion; ādu – having attractive movements; paṟavai misai – on periya tiruvadi (garuda); kaṇḍu – see; kai toḻudu – performing anjali; anṟi – not stopping with that; avan uṟaiyum – his residence; pādum – sung (to be praised); peru – great; pugaḻ – having the glory of bhagavān’s qualities; nānmaṟai – four vēdas (in the form of rig, yajur, sāma and atarvaṇa); aindu vēḷvi – panca mahā yajñas, the five great sacrifices (offered to celestial beings, ancestors, \[other\] creatures, humans and bhagavān); angam – ancillary subjects (such as śīkśā, niruktam, vyākaraṇam, candas, kalpa and jyōtiśa); āṟu – six; panninar – those who analyse in detail; vāḻ – live (enjoying bhagavān); nīdu – huge; poḻil – having garden; tiruvāṟanviḷai – tiruvāṟanviḷai; toḻa – to worship; niccalum – eternally; vāykkungol – will it occur?

**Перевод:**

**I would like to see emperumān who is crowned to protect the cows, who is the destroyer of madu, who cannot be overcome for the enemies, like a very radiant splendorous lion, and to perform anjali; will this occur eternally? Not stopping with that, I would like to worship tiruvāṟanviḷai which is having huge garden which is inhabited by those who analyse in detail the four vēdas, panca mahā yajñas, the five great sacrifices and six ancillary subjects and which is his residence, and sung as having great glory of bhagavān’s qualities; will it eternally occur?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the 3rd pāsuram, āḻvār says “Even if the emperumān from tiruvāṟanviḷai mercifully arrives here on his garuda vāhanam, will I get to worship tiruvāṟanviḷai forever, leaving him aside?”*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. kūdungol? vaigalum gōvindanai madusūdanaik kōḷariyai ādu paṟavai misaik kaṇḍu kaitoḻudanṟi avan uṟaiyum pādum perum pugaḻ nānmaṟai vēḷviyaindu āṟangam panninar vāḻ nīdu poḻil tiruvāṟan viḷai toḻa vāykkungol? niccalumē*

- *kūdum kol vailgalum* – This is emphasised by āḻvār, yearning if this will occur everyday.
- *gōvindan …* – When we see the emperumān who is present there, we will observe three important aspects – having motherly forbearance towards his devotees, quality of eliminating the enemies of his devotees and being unable to be overcome by the unfavourable ones.
- *kōḷari* – As said in narasimha mantram “*jvalantam*” (splendorous).
- *ādu paṟavai misaik kaṇḍu* – Seeing him on top of the victorious bird. ādu – victory. Alternatively, due to the bliss of being the carrier/vehicle of sarvēśvaran, periya tiruvadi who is blissfully dancing like those who drink too much honey; seeing emperumān on the shoulder of such garuda. Just as we head to tiruvāṟanviḷai considering it to be the goal \[due to emperumān’s presence there\], he would come towards āḻvārtirunagari considering it to be the goal \[due to āḻvār’s presence there\].
- *kaṇḍu* – on seeing him on the way.
- *kai toḻudu* – Even if there is no use of him \[as we are more attached to the divyadēśam\], we should worship him on approaching him; hence, he should be vorśipped properly \[This implies that, even for carama parva niśtars who are focussed on the divyadēśam, ācārya and bhāgavatas, emperumān is vorśippable\].
- *anṟi* – leaving him.
- *avan uṟaiyum* – let us go and enter the abode where he stays in the night \[i.e. his permanent residence\]; \[Why should we go to his abode leaving him? Is his abode the goal?\] while sarvēśvaran is the goal, there is a principle that one goes to the special abode \[of paramapadam\] and enjoy \[him\] there.
- *pādum perum pugaḻ nānmaṟai* – The four vēdams which praise his auspicious qualities.
- *vēḷvi aindu* – panca mahā yajñas.
- *āṟu angam* – The six ancillary subjects. “panninar” means those who are experts in these. We should go and unite with those who are residing there as said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 10.9](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/10-9/) “*bōdayanta: parasparam*” (sharing with each other).
- *vāḻ* – Those who are living \[gloriously\] there, understanding and enjoying emperumān who is the essence of vēdam.
- *nīdu poḻil tiruvāṟanviḷai toḻa* – To worship tiruvāṟanviḷai which is having huge garden.
- *vāykkungol niccalumē* – Will I get to eternally enjoy with the śrīvaiṣṇavas there?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.10.4. Vaykkungol niccalum

*vāykkungol niccalum eppoḻudum manattu īngu ninaikkap peṟa vāykkum karumbum perunjennelum vayal sūḻ tiruvāṟanviḷai vāykkum perum pugaḻ mūvulagīsan vada maduraip piṟanda vāykkum maṇiniṟak kaṇṇapirān tan malaradip pōdugaḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vāykkum – (abundantly) rising; karumbum – sugarcane; peru sennelum – tall, red paddy crop; vayal – field; sūḻ – surrounded; tiruvāṟanviḷai – in tiruvāṟanviḷai; vāykkum – due to being present; perum – well established; pugaḻ – having glory; mū ulagu – for three types of cētanas (sentient beings) and acētanas (insentient entities); īsan – being the lord; vada madurai – at śrī maturā; piṟanda – incarnated; vāykkum – being apt (to be enjoyed by devotees); maṇi – like a blue gem; niṟam – having divine complexion; kaṇṇan – kriṣṇa; pirān than – great benefactor’s; malar – blossomed; adip pōdugaḷ – lotus feet; īngu – from here; manattu – in the heart; ninaikka – to meditate; niccalum – forever; peṟa – to get; vāykkum kol – will it happen?

**Перевод:**

**emperumān is having well established glory due to being present in tiruvāṟanviḷai which is surrounded by field which is having rising sugarcane and tall, red paddy crop; being the lord of three types of cētanas (sentient beings) and acētanas (insentient entities),  he incarnated in śrī maturā as kriṣṇa who is being apt with the divine complexion of a blue gem; will I get to meditate upon the lotus feet of such great benefactor forever, in my heart?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the third pāsuram, āḻvār says “If we are unable to reach tiruvāṟanviḷai, can we at least eternally get to meditate upon, even if we are here, the divine feet of emperumān who is standing there?”*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. vāykkungol niccalum eppoḻudum manattu īngu ninaikkap peṟa vāykkum karumbum perunjennelum vayal sūḻ tiruvāṟanviḷai vāykkum perum pugaḻ mūvulagīsan vada maduraip piṟanda vāykkum maṇiniṟak kaṇṇapirān than malaradip pōdugaḷē*

- *vāykkum kol niccalum* – We should get this benefit everyday.
- *eppoḻudum* – Even in that, it should not be like nitya agnihōtram, where the ritual is only performed at certain times of the day (though the name of the ritual suggests “*nitya*” (eternal)), but it should happen in all states.
- *manattu īngu ninaikkap peṟṟa* – I don’t need to go there and enjoy; I can meditate upon the interactions I would have with [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) from here itself and be content with that. As he says “peṟa”, it is clear that [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is not looking for any other benefit/result, beyond this yearning in his heart. \[a ślōkam from jitantē stōtram is explained here\] *durgatāvapi* – one goes through great suffering during death; I am not praying for that; as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 2.9.3](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/06/thiruvaimozhi-2-9-3-seyyel-thivinai/) “*aiyār kaṇḍam adaikkilum nin kaḻal eyyādu ētta aruḷ sey*” (even when my throat is filled with mucus and I become speechless, you should mercifully bless me exclusively to praise your divine feet without getting tired). *tvadgatōmē manōrata:* – Did you think that it will be possible for me? *yadināśam na vindēta* – since, such yearning will never perish. *tāvatāsmi krutīsadā* – People in general, would explain yearning and experiencing as two separate aspects; but I don’t need any of these; I am satisfied with this yearning itself. *sadā* – I consider this as the goal instead of being freed from the material body, reaching paramapadam and enjoying there gloriously. \[An anecdote is cited for such yearning\] Long ago, there was a person named idaiyāṟṟukkudi nambi. He would visit during every utsavam (festival), and until the next utsavam, he would just meditate upon the utsavam he witnessed \[being in his residence\]. Once, during an utsavam, he was enjoying the \[first day\] utsavam within himself, those who were nearby him said “it is time for dinner”, he said “oh then, it is time to get bed, we should reach for the \[second day\] utsavam early in the next morning” \[he was so deep into the thoughts about the utsavam, he thought it to be really happening\]. He was hundred years old and became weak. He did not arrive in time for the utsavam this time for tirumuḷāiccāṟṟu \[a ceremony of sprouting of seeds for the utsavam, usually conducted before the commencement of the utsavam\]. [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) mercifully searched for him and felt in his divine heart “This is our grand utsavam, how come idaiyāṟṟukkudiyān has not arrived yet?” idaiyāṟṟukkudiyān finally arrived on the 6th day of the utsavam, and emperumān noticed him and mercifully asked “What shall I do for you?” he replied “I have used my body which was mercifully given by your highness, in your service as much as possible; now, it has become too weak to move around”; emperumān said “if that is the case, you just remain here \[no need to move around\]”; after emperumān crossed the the middle gate, idaiyāṟṟaukkudi nambi gave up his body and mercifully ascended to paramapadam \[as per emperumān’s desire\].
- *vāykkum …* – Everything in that abode is abundant. In tiruvāṟanviḷai which is surrounded by field which has well grown sugarcane, the tall, red paddy crop which gives shade to that sugarcane.
- *vāykkum perum pugaḻ* – Since everything present there becomes abundant, the one (emperumān) who desired that abode also became filled with abundant auspicious qualities.
- *mū ulagu īsan …* – Being the supreme lord of all worlds, for the sake of protecting saintly people, emperumān descended to śrī maturā.
- *vāykkum maṇi niṟak kaṇṇa pirān than* – bhagavān presented his divine, spiritual form into human form; hence, forever, will I get to meditate upon the blossomed, divine feet which are like fresh flowers, of the great benefactor, kriṣṇa, who is having beautiful, blue gem like complexion?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.10.5. Malaradip podugal

*malaradip pōdugaḷ ennenjatteppoḻudum irutti vaṇanga palar adiyār munbaruḷiya pāmbaṇai appan amarnduṟaiyum malarin maṇi nedu mādangaḷ nīdu madiḷ tiruvāṟanviḷai ulagamali pugaḻ pāda nam mēl vinai onṟu nillā nedumē*

**Пословный перевод:**

malar – (to be greatly enjoyed) blossomed; adip pōdugaḷ – divine, lotus feet; en – my; nenjattu – in heart; eppoḻudum – always; irutti – place; vaṇanga – to worship (due to that joy of having them in the heart); palar – many different (such as nityasūris (eternal associates of emperumān), sages such as parāśara et al, and his devotees); adiyār – servitors; munbu – in the presence of; aruḷiya – granting his (unlimited) grace; pāmbaṇai appan – anantaśāyi (who is having the quality of being together with his devotees, as he is always with ādiśēśa); amarndu – without any distraction (of taking care of the universe); uṟaiyum – being the residence (where he thinks the stay there itself as the goal); malaril – having flower garlands; maṇi – filled with gem stones; nedu – tall; mādangaḷ – mansions; nīdu – tall; madiḷ – having fort; tiruvāṟanviḷai – tiruvāṟanviḷai’s; ulagam – in the world; mali – abundance; pugaḻ – glories; pāda – as we sing (with joy); nam – our; mēl – tormenting upon; vinai – sins (themselves); onṟum – any (on us); nillā – without; kedum – will leave for unknown destination

**Перевод:**

**anantaśāyi emperumān granted his grace in the presence of his many different servitors to me to have his blossomed, divine, lotus feet in my heart always and to worship them; as we sing the abundant glories in the world for such tiruvāṟanviḷai where he is residing without any distraction and which is having tall mansions which are decorated with flower garlands and gem stones, and having tall forts, our sins which are tormenting us, will leave without any trace for unknown destination.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fifth pāsuram, āḻvār says “As we sing the abundant glories of tiruvāṟanviḷai, all our sorrows will leave us”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. malaradip pōdugaḷ ennenjatteppoḻudum irutti vaṇanga palar adiyār munbaruḷiya pāmbaṇai appan amarnduṟaiyum malarin maṇi nedu mādangaḷ nīdu madiḷ tiruvāṟanviḷai ulagamali pugaḻ pāda nam mēl vinai onṟu nillā nedumē*

- *malaradip pōdu …* – To make me place the fresh flowers which are his blossomed, divine feet in my heart always, and due to the overwhelming emotions, to fall at his divine feet without any pride.
- *palaradiyār munbaruḷiya* – How amazing that he has showered his special grace upon me while śrī vēda vyāsa bhagavān, śrī vālmeeki bhagavān, śrī paraśāra bhagavān and mudalāḻvārgaḷ who are known as in [tiruvāimoḻi 7.9.6](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/11/thiruvaimozhi-7-9-6-in-kavi-padum/) “*in kavi pādum parama kavigaḷ*” (the great poets who sing sweet pāsurams) are present! Just as how śrī rāma showered his grace upon tiruvadi (hanuman) when all the devotees were there as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 64.39 “*bahūmānēna mahatā hanūmantamavaikśata*” (Subsequently śrī rāma, being happy, looked at hanuman with pride), [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) was bestowed with special grace by [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/). \[A beautiful incident is narrated here\] [emperumānār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/emperumanar/) was once worried and was mercifully thinking “As kings from the east are trying to harm śrīrangam, what shall we do?”; he informed [periya namb](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/periya-nambi/)i “we are caring for this divyadēśam continuously; but demoniac people are trying to destroy this abode; what shall we do?”; periya nambi says “Let me circumambulate the town fully and I need one of your disciples to follow me”; emperumānār asked “who is fit for that?”; periya nambi says “while following me, he should not think ‘I am following someone’ and follow me like my shadow”; when emperumānār again asked “who would fit that description?” periya nambi said “can you not send [āḻvān \[kūrēśa\]](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/kuraththazhwan/)?” \[such was kūrattāḻvān’s greatness that he was honoured by periya nambi himself in the presence of emperumānār and his śiśyas\]
- *palar adiyār munbu aruḷiya* – Just as periya nambi requested emperumānār to send āḻvān while there were many great ācaryas in the assembly.
- *pāmbaṇai appan amarndu uṟaiyum* – sarvēśvaran who is having tiruvanantāḻvān (ādiśēśan) as his mattress as said in paryanka vidyā, tiruvāṟanviḷai became dearer to emperumān than ādiśēśan.
- *malarin maṇi nedu mādangaḷ* – tiruvāṟanviḷai which is having the tall mansions which are covered with the flowers poured by the dēvas and are radiant due to the gem stones on the walls, and having a tall fort.
- *ulaga mali pugaḻ pāda* – As we sing his auspicious qualities being triggered by the love towards him, which is overflowing out of the world, like a flood in a small area \[which overflows\].
- *nam mēl vinai onṟum nillā kedumē* – We need not do anything separate to eliminate the sins; just as a disease gets cured by drinking milk \[which is sweet too\], the sins will themselves get destroyed.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.10.6. Onru nilla

*onṟu nillā kedum muṟṟavum tīvinai uḷḷit toḻumin toṇḍīr! anṟangamar venṟu uruppiṇi nangai aṇi nedundōḷ puṇarndān enṟum eppōdum ennenjam tudippa uḷḷē irukkinṟa pirān ninṟa aṇi tiruvāṟanviḷai ennum nīṇagaram aduvē*

**Пословный перевод:**

anṟu – that day (when śiśupāla gathered the army to marry rukmiṇi); angu – when chased; amar – in war; venṟu – defeated; nangai – complete in enjoyability; uruppiṇi – rukmiṇi’s; aṇi – decorated; nedu – very enjoyable; tōḷ – divine shoulders; puṇarndān – one who embraced (as said in “bhartāram pariśasvajē“); enṟum – always; eppōdum – without a break even for a moment; en nenjam – my heart; tudippa – (enjoy and) to praise; uḷḷē – inside me; irukkinṟa – present; pirān – great benefactor; ninṟa – mercifully standing (to be enjoyed by everyone); aṇi – beautiful; tiruvāṟanviḷai – tiruvāṟanviḷai; ennum – well known as; nīḷ nagaram adu – the great city; toṇḍīr – you who have desire to enjoy; uḷḷi – meditate; toḻumin – worship; tī – cruel; vinai – sins; onṟum – all; nillā – being shaken (to not remain); muṟṟavum – fully; kedum – will be destroyed

**Перевод:**

**emperumān embraced the decorated, very enjoyable, divine shoulders of rukmiṇi who is complete in enjoyability, after defeating rukma in the war, on that day when he chased emperumān. Such great benefactor is always inside me to be praised by my heart without a break even for a moment; you who have the desire to enjoy him, who is mercifully standing in the great city which is well known as beautiful tiruvāṟanviḷai, meditate and worship him; all your sins will be shaken up and be fully destroyed.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the sixth pāsuram, āḻvār says “Oh those who desire for emperumān! You think about tiruvāṟanviḷai and reach it, to eliminate all your sorrows”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. onṟu nillā kedum muṟṟavum tīvinai uḷḷit toḻumin toṇḍīr! anṟangamar venṟu uruppiṇi nangai aṇi nedundōḷ puṇarndān enṟum eppōdum ennenjam tudippa uḷḷē irukkinṟa pirān ninṟa aṇi tiruvāṟanviḷai ennum nīṇagaram aduvē*

- *onṟu nillā kedum muṟṟavum tīvinai* – Only when the individual tries to eliminate his sins, it will go slowly like the dirt from a new cloth; but [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is sarvaśakta (omnipotent) eliminates them, they will go without a trace. \[viṣṇu darmam 78th ślōkam is explained\] *mēru mantaramātrōpi* – the sins which are as heavy as mēru mountain and mantara mountain placed on top of each other; as a disease will be cured certainly when the physician treats it, the sins which were addressed by emperumān who is said in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 5.3.6 “*maruttuvanāy ninṟa māmaṇivaṇṇan*” (emperumān who is like a doctor, with beautiful gemstone like complexion). He said in śrī bhagavat gītā 18.66 “*sarva pāpēbhyō mōkśayiśyāmi*” (I will free you from all sorrows). It is said in cāndōjña upaniśat 5.24 “*sarva pāpmāna: pradūyantē*” (All sins are destroyed). Whatever is said for him applies to his abode as well \[Quoted pramāṇams highlight that emperumān eliminates the sins. But here it is said that the divine abode itself will eliminate the sins. So, this implies that when āḻvār talks about the divine abode of emperumān, it is in context of emperumān and his full paraphernalia\].
- *uḷḷit toḻumin toṇḍīr* – Oh those who are interested in bhagavat viśayam! Think about the abode and reach there.
- *anṟu …* – He is the one who appears to fulfil the desires of those who desire for anything!
- *anṟu* – When śiśupāla was actively participating in the svayamvara (rukmiṇi’s selection of her groom).
- *angu* – He was eager, but rukmiṇi was thinking “would the real owner not come and accept me”, he appeared there as he appeared from the pillar \[as narasimha\].
- *amar venṟu* – Accepting arrows in his chest, for her.
- *uruppiṇi nangai* – She was so complete in all qualities, that one would not hesitate to do anything for her.
- *aṇi …* – One who embraced the most enjoyable shoulders of rukmiṇi which were like ornaments for themselves.
- *enṟum …* – āḻvār’s heart is fully thinking about the auspicious qualities of rukmiṇip pirātti. The benefactor who is in my heart, to be praised by my heart always in all situations.
- *ninṟa …* – Oh devotees! worship the great city, the beautiful tiruvāṟanviḷai, where one can see and enjoy [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) to remain fearless thinking “he is there for us”, unlike the antaryāmi (indvelling super soul) state where he is shining in the heart yet invisible. If he is yearning to serve emperumān, why is he instructing others saying “uḷḷit toḻumin”? For āḻvār, his own experience will always be mixed with instructions to others; \[but can he not just interact with his own heart as said in the first pāsuram of tiruvāimoḻi?\] there is no difference between his interactions with his heart and his calling out for the devotees.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.10.7. Ninagaram aduve

*nīṇagaram aduvē malarc cōlaigaḷ sūḻ tiruvāṟanviḷai nīṇagarattuṟaiginṟa pirān nedumāl kaṇṇan viṇṇavarkōn vāṇapuram pukku mukkatpirāṇait tolaiya vem pōrgaḷ seydu vāṇanai āyiram tōḷ tuṇittān saraṇanṟi maṟṟonṟilamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

nīṇagaram (nīḷ nagaram) – the great city (which is famously known in śruti (vēdam) as ayōdyā, aparājitā); aduvē – to be that (arcāvatāra stalam); malar – having flowers; sōlaigaḷ – gardens; sūḻ – surrounded; tiruvāṟanviḷai – tiruvāṟanviḷai; nīṇagarattu – in the great city; uṟaiginṟa – eternally residing; pirān – being great benefactor; nedumāl – being greatly attached towards his devotees; kaṇṇan – one who incarnated as kriṣṇa; viṇṇavar kōn – the master of nityasūris; vāṇapuram – into bāṇa’s town (where anirudda was confined); pukku – entered; mukkaṇ pirānai – rudra (who has the third eye which indicates his power and who pridefully considers himself as the lord); tolaiya – to stop him (from protecting his devotee); vem – greatly valorous; pōrgaḷ – battles; seydu – performed; vāṇanai – bāṇa’s; āyiram tōḷ – thousand shoulders; tuṇittā – one who severed; saraṇ – means (to attain the divyadēśam); anṟi – than him; maṟṟu – other than him; onṟu – means; ilam – we are not having

**Перевод:**

**tiruvāṟanviḷai, the great city which is surrounded by flower-filled gardens, can be said as the great city, paramapadam; emperumān, the great benefactor who is eternally residing in this divyadēśam, who is greatly attached towards his devotees, who incarnated as kriṣṇa, the master of nityasūris, entered bāṇa’s town, stopped rudra, performed greatly valorous battles, and severed the thousand shoulders of bāṇa; other than such emperumān, we are not having any means (to attain the divyadēśam).**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the seventh pāsuram, when asked “īsn’t tirunādu (paramapadam) our goal?” āḻvār says “tiruvāṟanviḷai is our goal and emperumān who is present there, is our means”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “kriṣṇa who eliminated anirudda’s enemy bāṇa amd severed his shoulders, is the apt means for us”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Seventh pāsuram. When asked “You said tiruvāṟanviḷai is the goal; but isn’t emperumān the goal?”; āḻvār says “Am I capable to say no? Can you not listen to my philosophy?” and elaborates the same as “Whatever is attained as a result of upāsanam (means) becomes part of the result \[example – the path leading to paramapadam, reaching divyadēśam etc\]; whatever helps to enhance the result, is also part of the result \[example – kainkaryam to bhagavān, kainkaryam in divyadēśam etc\]; hence, that divyadēśam itself is the goal; bhagavān is the means who brings us there; this is my philosophy”. nīṇagaram aduvē malarc cōlaigaḷ sūḻ tiruvāṟanviḷai nīṇagarattuṟaiginṟa pirān nedumāl kaṇṇan viṇṇavarkōn vāṇapuram pukku mukkatpirāṇait tolaiya vem pōrgaḷ seydu vāṇanai āyiram tōḷ tuṇittān saraṇanṟi maṟṟonṟilamē*

- *nīḷ nagaram aduvē* – This is the ultimate destination which is eternal residence for those who entered there and where there is no bewilderment as said in [mūnṟām tiruvandādi 51](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/04/munram-thiruvandhadhi-51/) “*kalangāp perunagar*” (paramapadam which is without any bewilderment), and from where there is no return as said in cāndōjña upaniśat 8.15 “*na ca punarāvartatē*” (there is no return).
- *malar …* – It appears as the ultimate destination for [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) himself too. The benefactor who resides in the great city of tiruvāṟanviḷai which is surrounded by evergreen gardens.
- *nedumāl …* – Being the lord of nityasūris, incarnating as kriṣṇa due to the affection towards those who have inclination towards him in this samsāram, travelling from one ocean \[west coast – dvārakā\] to another ocean \[east coast – cōṇitapuram\], eliminating the pride of rudra who considered himself to be the lord and who vowed to protect bāṇa fully, and engaged in valorous battles to make rudra think “I will never consider myself as a dēvatā to vouch for the protection of anyone”. śrī viṣṇu purāṇam 5-33-41 “*kriṣṇa kriṣṇa mahābāhō jānētvām puruśōttamam* ” (rudra says – Oh kriṣṇa, with mighty arms! I know that you are the greatest among all souls). As said in “*ānaikkum tanakkut takka vādam*” (elephant has problems matching its size), dēvatās are more ignorant than us \[humans\]. \[Are they ignorant?\] When [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) broke a weak bow, the dēvas thought him to be great as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam bāla kāṇḍam 75.19 “*adikam mē nirē viṣṇum*” (they thought viṣṇu to be superior to rudra).
- *vāṇanai āyiram tōḷ tuṇittān* – He eliminated the shoulders and let bāṇa live thinking “uśā cannot become fatherless”.
- *saraṇ* – He is the gataka (connector – means) and tiruvāṟanviḷai is the prāpyam (goal). As [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is the prāpyan (goal) himself arrived and remained in that divyadēśam, there is nothing wrong in highlighting the abode to be the goal. A sarvādika (supreme entity) should be the means and the one who grants the result; hence he is the means, and the result is that divyadēśam.
- *anṟi maṟṟu onṟu ilamē* – We will not consider anything else as the means and goal.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.
