## 7.10.8. Anri marronrilam

*anṟi maṟṟonṟilam nin caraṇē enṟu agalirum poyigaiyin vāy ninṟu tan nīḷ kaḻal ēttiya ānaiyin nenjidar tīrtta pirān senṟanguiniduṟaiginṟa seḻum poḻil sūḻ tiruvāṟanviḷai onṟi valanjeyya onṟumō? tīvinai uḷḷattin sārvallavē*

**Пословный перевод:**

nin – your; caraṇ – divine feet; anṟi – without; maṟṟu – other; onṟu – any; ilam – we are not having; enṟu – thinking that; agal – vast; irum – deep; poygaiyin vāy – in the pond; ninṟu – standing (being caught by the crocodile); than – his; nīḷ – stretch up to those who are in danger; kaḻal – divine feet; ētthiya – praised (saying “nārāyaṇā” highlighting the eternal relationship); ānaiyin – elephant’s; nenju idar – the sorrow in the heart (“we are not able to offer the flower before it loses its freshness); tīrtta – one who eliminated; pirān – great benefactor; senṟu – went (to help his devotees); angu – there; inidu – sweetly; uṟaiginṟa – being the residing place; seḻum – very enjoyable; poḻil – garden; sūḻ – surrounded; tiruvāṟanviḷai – tiruvāṟanviḷai; onṟi – reach; valam seyya – as we circumambulate; onṟumō – will it occur?; tī – cruel; vinai – sins; uḷḷattin – the heart’s; sārvu – fit in; allavē – won’t have

**Перевод:**

**gajēndrāḻvān, the elephant, while standing in the vast, deep pond thinking “we are not having anything other than your divine feet”, praised emperumān’s divine feet which stretch up to those who are in danger; the great benefactor who eliminated the elephant’s sorrow in its heart, went to tiruvāṟānviḷai which is surrounded by very enjoyable garden and had it as his sweet residing place; will we reach there and circumambulate the place? If that happens, cruel sins won’t fit in our heart \[they will leave\].**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the eighth pāsuram, āḻvār says “as we enter tiruvāṟanviḷai, all our sorrows will disappear”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. anṟi maṟṟonṟilam nin caraṇē enṟu agalirum poyigaiyin vāy ninṟu than nīḷ kaḻal ēttiya ānaiyin nenjidar tīrtta pirān senṟanguiniduṟaiginṟa seḻum poḻil sūḻ tiruvāṟanviḷai onṟi valanjeyya onṟumō? tīvinai uḷḷattin sārvallavē*

- *anṟi maṟṟu onṟu ilam nin caraṇē enṟu* – should be read as “*nin caraṇē anṟi maṟṟu onṟu ilam enṟu*” – there is no hold for me other than your divine feet; eliminating the bewilderment of considering others as saviours. Also eliminating the thought of self as saviour as said in viṣṇu darmam 68 “*gaja ākarśatē tīrē grāha ākarśē jalē*” (the elephant was pulling to the shore and the crocodile was pulling to the water). As it says in viṣṇu darmam 68 “*manasā cintayat*” (thinking in the mind), it has crossed the stage where crying out will help. When we see emperumān, ” the self” will also be similar to “others” when it comes to protecting oneself. This is why while the middle word (*ukāram*) is present in *praṇavam*, the middle word of *tirumantram* (*nama:*) also survives \[*ukāram* explains that ātmā is not for self and others – it only exists for emperumān. *nama:* specifically explains that ātmā does not belong to self. This is explained in mumukśuppadi in detail especially in sūtrams 65, 78 to 80 and 91. Can be heard in detail at [https://pillai.koyil.org/index.php/2017/12/learn-mumukśuppadi/](https://pillai.koyil.org/index.php/2017/12/learn-mumukshuppadi/) \].
- *agal irum poygaiyin vāy* – As it fits to speak about the vastness and depth, irum indicates depth there \[generally, iru means big\]. What is the purpose of highlighting the vastness and depth? To indicate that there is no other way than getting protected by him and perishing due to the lack of his protection.
- *agal irum poygaiyin vāy ninṟu* – The vastness and depth made it so helpless that it remained still in the dangerous place, as if standing in a safe place. At this stage, the act of crocodile pulling into the water and the act of elephant pulling to the shore stopped, and the crocodile only was pulling the elephant into the water.
- *than nīḷ kaḻal* – The divine feet which stretches up to the other person’s helplessness. Even when caught by the crocodile, on meditating upon emperumān, one can remain fearless. It is said in taittirīya upaniśat “*ānandam brahmaṇō vidvān na bibēti*” (One who knows bhagavān’s bliss, will not fear). *kutaścana* – one can remain fearless, not just for unintentional mistakes, but even for intentional mistakes. When emperumān says as in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 4.9.2 “*seydārēl nanṟu seydār*” (even if my devotees committed mistake, they did it properly only). When intentional mistakes are not to be feared \[as explained in the aforementioned pāsuram\], unintentional mistakes are naturally not to be feared. Even in bhakti yōga, one need not fear for unintentional mistakes \[the speciality of śaraṇāgati is that, one need not even fear for intentional mistakes\].
- *ēttiya* – Just as one would spontaneously cry out “*ammē*” (Oh mother) on stepping on a thorn, the elephant naturally cried out to emperumān.
- *ānaiyin nenju idar tīrtta pirān* – It was such a desperate situation that, even its trunk was going into the pond; emperumān was waiting for the elephant’s effort to stop \[so that he can help\]; as the elephant gave up its efforts, emperumān jumped to its help.
- *ānaiyin nenju idar tīrtta pirān* – He eliminated the elephant’s sorrow “I am not able to offer this flower before it loses its freshness!”; alternatively – it is the sorrow “emperumān is going to acquire disrepute because of me”. That is, the elephant thought “What if people would think ‘While the elephant is suffering, this is how emperumān is protecting it! We are thinking that he is the saviour!’ “. emperumān arrived at the shore of the pond, tore apart the mouth of the crocodile, and eliminated the sorrow of the elephant, to eliminate the sorrow for both as said in [nānmugan tiruvandādi 12](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/06/nanmugan-thiruvandhadhi-12/) “*iraṇḍum pōy iraṇḍin vīdu*” (relieving both the elephant and crocodile from their previous state, and liberating them both). bhattar explains mercifully this in this manner – when a prince was imprisoned, even his guard will be given royal food. Both got liberated! The crocodile was liberated from the curse and the elephant was liberated from this material world.
- *pirān* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is thinking about emperumān eliminating the sorrow of the elephant, as emperumān doing a favour for āḻvār himself, instead of helping the elephant. Only when one has such attitude, can one be a śrīvaiṣṇava. One will have śrīvaiṣṇavatvam (the quality of being a śrīvaiṣṇava) only when one thinks about a favour to a devotee as a favour to self and a disaster to a devotee as a disaster to self.
- *senṟu angu inidu uṟaiginṟa* – Just as the elephant grieves when sarvēśvaran does not help its cause, sarvēśvaran grieves when he does not reach this divyadēśam. Performing circumambulation etc in tiruvāṟanviḷai where he has arrived and residing with great eagerness and which is surrounded by beautiful garden.
- *onṟumō* – Will that occur?
- *tī vinai uḷḷattin sārvallavē* – When that happens, cruel sins will not remain in our heart. Will light and darkness reside together? When emperumān eternally resides in the heart, is there any place for the cruel sins?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.10.9. Tivinai ullattin

*tīvinai uḷḷattin sārvallavāgit teḷivisumbēṟal uṟṟāl nāvin uḷḷum uḷḷattuḷḷum amainda toḻilin uḷḷum navinṟu yāvarum vandu vaṇangum poḻil tiruvāṟanviḷai adanai mēvi valanjeydu kai toḻak kūdungol? ennum en sindanaiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tī – cruel; vinai – sins; uḷḷattin – in the heart; sārvu allavāgi – without fitting; teḷi – having clarity (to cause self realisation); visumbu – supreme sky; ēṟal – to climb/reach; uṟṟāl – even if got; en – my; sindanai – heart; nāvin uḷḷum uḷḷattuḷḷum – in mind and speech; amainda – matching; toḻilin uḷḷum – in acts; navinṟu – with harmony; yāvarum – residents of all realms (both spiritual and materialistic); vandu – come; vaṇangum – to be vorśipped; poḻil – having garden (which highlights the enjoyability); tiruvāṟanviḷai – tiruvāṟanviḷai; adanai – that abode itself; mēvi – reach; valam seydu – by engaging in favourable acts; kai toḻa – to worship by joined palms; kūdum kol – will it occur?; ennum – thinking

**Перевод:**

**As the cruel sins no longer fit in the heart, even if I get to reach the supreme sky which has clarity, my heart which is in harmony with the mind, speech and matching acts is thinking to  reach the abode of tiruvāṟanviḷai which is reached and vorśipped by residents of all places and which is having garden, and to worship with joined palms by engaging in favourable acts; will it occur?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the ninth pāsuram, āḻvār says “If I were to get both śrīvaikuṇṭam (paramapadam) and tiruvāṟanviḷai, my heart will choose tiruvāṟanviḷai which is desired and reached by the residents of paramapdam itself”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. tīvinai uḷḷattin sārvallavāgit teḷivisumbēṟal uṟṟāl nāvin uḷḷum uḷḷattuḷḷum amainda toḻilin uḷḷum navinṟu yāvarum vandu vaṇangum poḻil tiruvāṟanviḷai adanai mēvi valanjeydu kai toḻak kūdungol? ennum en sindanaiyē*

- *tīvinai* … – when asked “You are talking about tiruvāṟanviḷai as the goal due to the shrunk knowledge while being here; when the knowledge expands, you will change paramapadam to be your goal”, āḻvār says “it is not like that; would you like to hear how I would be when my knowledge expands?”
- *tī vinai uḷḷattin sārvallavāgi* – The previously carried out avidyā (ignorance), karma (acts), vāsanā (impressions) and ruci (tastes) stopped touching the ātmā.
- *teḷi visumbu ēṟal uṟṟāl* – While setting out to reach tirunādu (paramapadam).
- *nāvin uḷḷum …* – tiruvāṟanviḷai which is eternally, perfectly enjoyable, to be desired by those most wise souls who are present in paramapadam and reach out here with their mind, speech and body.
- *mēvi …* – I should go and reach that abode of tiruvāṟanviḷai and engage in favourable acts.
- *kai toḻak kūdum kol ennum en sindanaiyē* – My heart is not obedient to me, as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam uttara kāṇḍam 40.16 “*bhāvō nānyatra gaccati*” (hanuman says – my mind will not focus on anyone else).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.10.10. Sindai marronrin

*sindai maṟṟonṟin tiṟattadallāt tanmai dēva pirān aṟiyum sindaiyināl seyvadān aṟiyādana māyangaḷ onṟum illai sindaiyināl sollināl seygaiyāl nilattēvar kuḻu vaṇangum sindai magiḻ tiruvāṟanviḷai uṟai tīrttanukkaṟṟa pinnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

sindaiyināl sollināl seygaiyāl – with mind, body and speech; nilat tēvar – bhāgavatas’, who are the vorśippable entities in this world; kuḻu – group; vaṇangum – to worship; sindai – heart (of the enjoyers); magiḻ – bring joy; tiruvāṟanviḷai – in tiruvāṟanviḷai; uṟai – residing; tīrttanukku – for the purest emperumān; aṟṟa pin – after having dedicated (to totally exist for him); sindai – heart; maṟṟu onṟin – anything else; tiṟattadu allā – not considering as goal; tanmai – nature; dēvan – master of nityasūris; pirān – the omniscient emperumān himself; aṟiyum – knows; sindaiyināl – with the mind; seyya – done; māyangaḷ – hidden acts; tān – he; aṟiyādana – unknown; onṟum illai – there is nothing

**Перевод:**

**The purest emperumān is residing in tiruvāṟanviḷai to be vorśipped by and to bring joy for the group of bhāgavatas, who are vorśippable themselves, with their mind, body and speech; after having dedicated myself to such emperumān, the omniscient emperumān knows himself the nature of my heart which does not consider anything else as goal; no hidden act which is done in the mind, is unknown to him.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the tenth pāsuram, āḻvār says “As one remains with tiruvāṟanviḷai as the goal, there is nothing unknown”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “After emperumān knows that my heart is focussed on his presence in tiruvāṟanviḷai, he himself will know that my heart will not seek anything else”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*In tenth pāsuram, when asked “You consider tiruvāṟanviḷai as the goal; what if emperumān gives your tirunādu (paramapadam)?” āḻvār says “he is sarvajña (omniscient); will he not know \[my heart\]?”*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Tenth pāsuram. Some explain this as – when asked “Are you just saying this? What if your heart really desires for paramapadam?” āḻvār explains “You should ask this question to sarvēśvaran who is at the origin of my thoughts”. Alternatively, piḷḷān explains – when asked “You are considering tiruvāṟanviḷai to be the goal; but isn’t īśvaran independent? What if he grants you paramapadam?” āḻvār says “īsn’t he omniscient? Will he not know? Does he not grant puruśārtam? He would only grant that which is desired by puruśa \[soul\]. sindai maṟṟonṟin tiṟattadallāt tanmai dēva pirān aṟiyum sindaiyināl seyvadān aṟiyādana māyangaḷ onṟum illai sindaiyināl sollināl seygaiyāl nilattēvar kuḻu vaṇangum sindai magiḻ tiruvāṟanviḷai uṟai tīrttanukkaṟṟa pinnē*

- *sindai maṟṟu onṟin tiṟattadu allāt tanmai dēva pirān aṟiyum* – sarvēśvaran knows that my heart will not even think about paramapadam. tanmai – nature. maṟṟu indicates that even reciting the name “paramapadam” is undesirable.

When asked “While we are asking you, why are you bringing sarvēśvaran as witness?” āḻvār says,

- *sindaiyināl …* – While emperumān thinks first, which is followed by ātmā’s thought, is there anything which emperumān does not know? Is he not said in [tirumālai 34](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/11/thirumalai-34/) “*uḷḷuvār uḷḷiṟṟū ellām udan irundu aṟidi*” (being together with everyone, the thoughts of those who are thinking, are known to you)? ātmā can think only if emperumān thinks first! Whatever is done by heart, there is nothing mischievous, which is unknown to him.
- *sindaiyināl …* – Just as nityasūris, this is the abode where mumukśus (liberation seekers) also come and take shelter. The abode where the śrīvaiṣṇavas who are known as bhūsuras (vorśippable personalities in this world) gather in group and serve through their mind, speech and body.
- *sindai magiḻ tiruvāṟanviḷai* – The divine abode which will turn anyone entering there to be come perfectly blissful. It appears to be the “*prāpya bhūmi*” (ultimate destination). It can be enquired from sarvēśvaran who has arrived and is residing in tiruvāṟanviḷai.

When asked “since when do you have this clarity?” āḻvār says,

- *tīrttanukku aṟṟa pin* – Since the day when emperumān manifested his great enjoyability, eliminated my attachment towards all other aspects and made me exist exclusively for him; from the day he uplifted me; \[before that special mercy of emperumān fell upon me\] since time immemorial, I was suffering in this material realm.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 7.10.11. Tirttanukku arrapin

*tīrttanukkaṟṟa pin maṟṟōr saraṇ illai enṟenṟeṇṇit tīrttanukkē tīrtta manattananāgic ceḻungurugūrc catakōpan sonna tīrttangaḷ āyirattuḷ ivai pattum vallārgaḷait tēvar vaigal tīrttangaḷē enṟu pūsittu nalgi uraippar tam dēviyarkkē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tīrttanukku – for emperumān (who is the one who instructs the means); aṟṟa pin – after becoming an exclusive servitor; maṟṟu – other; ōr – any; saraṇ – means; illai – not having; enṟu eṇṇi – determined; tīrttanukkē – for emperumān (who has the supreme purity to free us from all our sins); tīrtta – fully submitted; manattananāgi – with the heart; seḻum – beautiful; kurugūr – leader of tirunagari (āḻvārtirunagari); satakōpan – nammāḻvār; sonna – mercifully spoke; tīrttangaḷ – individually being the abode of knowledge; āyirattuḷ – among the thousand pāsurams; ivai pattum – this decad; vallārgaḷai – those who can practice; dēvar – nityasūris; vaigal – always; tam – their; dēviyarkku – divine consorts; pūsittu – offering gifts; nalgi – friendship; tīrttangaḷē – as purifying personalities (who remove the sins of samsāram); enṟu – as; uraippar – will hail

**Перевод:**

**nammāḻvār, the leader of beautiful āḻvārtirunagari, after becoming an exclusive servitor for emperumān, determined that there is no means other than emperumān, with fully submitted heart for him, mercifully spoke the thousand pāsurams which are individually abodes of knowledge; among those thousand pāsurams, those who can practice this decad, will always be hailed as purifying personalities by nityasūris to their divine consorts in a friendly manner, offering gifts.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the end, āḻvār says “Those who are well versed in this decad will be celebrated by ayarvaṟum amarargaḷ (nityasūris)”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. tīrttanukkaṟṟa pin maṟṟōr saraṇ illai enṟenṟeṇṇit tīrttanukkē tīrtta manattananāgic ceḻungurugūrc catakōpan sonna tīrttangaḷ āyirattuḷ ivai pattum vallārgaḷait tēvar vaigal tīrttangaḷē enṟu pūsittu nalgi uraippar tam dēviyarkkē*

- *tīrttan …* – Instead of specifically saying “[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is pure for certain persons”, he is the pure one for everyone other than him \[as there is no adjectives for the first “*tīrttan*“\]. tīrttam means one who is pure himself, and also will purify those who come in contact with him. As brahmā washed the divine feet of emperumān who measured the world as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 2.8.6](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/05/thiruvaimozhi-2-8-6-thirththan/) “*tīrttan ulagaḷanda sēvadi*“, that holy water was held by rudra in his matted hair, to purify himself. rudra is known as in [tiruveḻukūṟṟirukkai](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/07/thiruvezhukurrirukkai-7/) “*āṟupodi sadaiyōn*” (one with matted hair, which has a river in it). He is known as gangādaran. Now, all we need to do is to find the origin for that gangā; when analysed, one will find it to be connected to the divine feet \[of emperumān\]; periya tirumoḻi 4.2.6 “*gangai pōdarak kāl nimirttaruḷiya kaṇṇan*” (kriṣṇa who raised his foot to emanate gangā from it).
- *tīrttanukku aṟṟa pin* – Also said as “after becoming an exclusive servitor for the one who manifested his great enjoyability and eliminated the taste for everything other than him”.
- *maṟṟu ōr saraṇ illai enṟu eṇṇi* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) became clear that there is no other saviour than [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/).
- *tīrttanukkē tīrtta manattanan āgi* – Having the heart which is fully handed over to emperumān who eliminated the taste in worldly pleasures. He himself said previously in [tiruvāimoḻi 2.6.4](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/04/thiruvaimozhi-2-6-4-vallale-madhusudhana/) “*unai ninaindu eḷgal tanda endāy*” (Oh lord! meditating upon you, you bestowed on me detachment from worldly pleasures). Once the heart is placed on emperumān, it will not go anywhere as said in [mūnṟām tiruvandādi 14](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/03/munram-thiruvandhadhi-14/) “*māṟpāl manam suḻippa mangaiyar tōḷ kaivittu*” (as one’s heart becomes attached to śrīman nārāyaṇa, his worldly desires will disappear) and in bhārhaspatya smruti “*paramātmani yō rakta: viraktōparamātmani*” (as one becomes attached to paramātmā, he becomes detached from everything else). His beauty will not let us enjoy worldly pleasures as said in [iraṇḍām tiruvandādi 42](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/11/irandam-thiruvandhadhi-42/) “*manaippāl piṟandār pirāndu eydum pērinbam ellām tuṟandār toḻudārat tōḷ*” (those who worship [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s divine shoulders will detest the small pleasures which are attained by those who are born in samsāram).
- *seḻum kurugūrc catakōpan sonna* – Mercifully spoken by [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) who has the apt birth place \[for becoming such servitor of emperumān\].
- *tīrttangaḷ āyiram* – The thousand pāsurams are thousand pure objects. Those who can practice this decad will be hailed as “always purest persons” by dēvar, i.e. nityasūris like tiruvadi (garudāḻvār), tiruvanantāḻvān (ādiśēśa), sēnai mudaliyār (viśvaksēna) et al, while they enjoy with their dear consorts.
- *nalgi uraippār tam dēviyarkku* – When the nityasūris serve along with their dear consorts, to śrīvaikuṇṭanāta, and when they reach an ecstatic state out of great bliss, which is explained as “*ōdam ēṟṟik kūli koḷḷum daśai*” (Some boatmen will allow passengers to board the boat without discussing the fare, and will negotiate the same when the boat reaches midway, where the passenger will not have an option to bargain), they will reveal everything to their consorts and explain the greatness of such śrīvaiṣṇavas. Here, “*ōdam ēṟṟik kūli koḷḷum daśai*” means, assisting in kainkaryam \[consorts will assist in the kainkaryam of nityasūris and become joyful\]. That is, as seen in how [caramaślōkam](http://ponnadi.blogspot.in/2015/12/rahasya-thrayam.html) was protected and carefully taught \[In tirukkōśtiyūr, [emperumānār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/emperumanar/) revealed the principles of the most confidential carama ślōkam (which was given to him by [tirukkōśtiyūr nambi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/thirukkoshtiyur-nambi/) after severe tests), for those who assisted him to serve emperumān with great joy, being satisfied with their service\].
- *vaigalum pūsittu* – As in “one cannot touch the ocean during aparva \[days other than māsa pravēśam, amāvāsyai, paurṇami, pratamai and ēkādaśi\]”, there is no such rule. vaigal also means time. Just as āḻvār prayed as in [tiruvāimoḻi 3.3.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/08/thiruvaimozhi-3-3-1-ozhivil-kalam/) “*oḻivil kālam ellām udanāy manni*” (being together at all times) in bhagavān related matters, nityasūris who are well learned in this principle, will engage in the matters of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s devotees.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## Eighth Centum

## 8.1 Devimar avar

## 8.1.1. Devimar avar

*dēvimār āvār tirumagaḷ bhūmi ēva maṟṟamarar ātceyvār mēviya ulavam mūnṟavai ātci vēnduvēṇḍuruvam nin uruvam pāviyēn unnai aduginṟa kamalakkaṇṇadu ōr pavaḷa vāy maṇiyē! āviyē! amudē! alai kadal kadainda appanē! kāṇumāṟaruḷāy*

**Пословный перевод:**

dēvimār – your consorts (who match your beauty and greatness); tirumagaḷ – lakshmi (who is your great wealth); bhūmi – bhūmi dēvi (who is the presiding deity of all wealth); maṟṟu – others (further); Eva – as you order (as said in “kriyatām iti mām vada“); ātceyvār – will perform kainkaryam (service); amarar – nityasūris (eternal residents of paramapadam); mēviya – fitting well (to be inseparable from you); mūnṟavai – having the three folded (i.e. matter, souls and time); ulagam – worlds; ātci – follow your orders; vēṇḍu – as per the situations (for their protection); vēṇḍu – as per his own desire; uruvam – forms; nin – for you; uruvam – (distinguished) forms; pāviyēn tannai – sinful me (who could not enjoy this form); aduginṟa – torturing (like those who kill); kamalam – (most enjoyable) lotus like; kaṇṇadu – eye; ōr – unique; pavaḷam – coral like; vāy – having beautiful lips; maṇiyē – attractive like a blue gem; āviyē – being the life (without which one cannot survive); amudē – being the (most enjoyable) nectar (which brings back life); alai kadal kadainda appanē – oh great benefactor who performed difficult tasks and helped!; kāṇumāṟu – to see and enjoy; aruḷāy – show your mercy

**Перевод:**

**nityasūris will perform kainkaryam as you and your divine consorts śrī dēvi, bhūmi dēvi and others order; the three-folded worlds which are fitting well with you, follow your orders; you have distinguished forms as per the situation and your desire; oh great benefactor who performed difficult tasks and helped others! You are torturing me who is sinful, with your lotus like eyes, unique coral like lips and attractive blue gem like form; you are my life; you are the most enjoyable nectar; show your mercy to me, to see and enjoy you.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the first pāsuram, āḻvār says “you who are the most enjoyable such that one cannot bear your separation, should shower your mercy so that I can see you”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. dēvimār āvār tirumagaḷ bhūmi Eva maṟṟamarar ātceyvār mēviya ulavam mūnṟavai ātci vēnduvēṇḍuruvam nin uruvam pāviyēn unnai aduginṟa kamalakkaṇṇadu ōr pavaḷa vāy maṇiyē! āviyē! amudē! alai kadal kadainda appanē! kāṇumāṟaruḷāy*

- *dēvimār …* – What is the reason for me to suffer while those \[consorts\] who would say as in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 116-45 “*nakaścin nāparādyati*” (there is none who has not committed a wrongful deed) are near you? śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 21-19 “*mitramaupayikam kartum rāma: stānam parīpsatā, vadam ca aniccatā ghōram tvayā asau puruśarśabha:* ” (śrī rāma  who is the best among all *puruśas* (souls) is the apt person to make friends for you who would like to remain in this world and who would not like to die a horrible death) is explained here in detail.
   - *mitram aupayikam* – As rāvaṇa stood in front of sītāp pirātti and started uttering some foolish words, the mother would not become angry when the child torments her! Being the mother, seeing his downfall, she gives good advise to him. If she told him to surrender unto śrī rāma’s divine feet, he may consider that as an insult and will not agree to it; hence, she says “become friendly with śrī rāma”; śrī rāma said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 18.3 “*mithra bhāvēna*” (even if you (rāvaṇa) approach me as a friend); pirātti is saying “*mitram aupayikam*“. Even while reaching paramapadam, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) grants parama sāmyāpatti (supreme equivalence in eight qualities) to ātmās. rāvaṇa asks “Why would I have friendly relationship with my enemies?”
   - *stānam parīpsatā* – Too bad. Even for those who engage in robbery, they should be able to stay on some place and do it; so, if you would like to preserve your place, you have to do this. Thinking that rāvaṇa is saying “I don’t need the land, I can even fly”, she continues,
   - *vadam cāniccatā* – Will śrī rāma’s arrows not reach the sky?
   - *gōram* – Even if you desire to be killed in a merciful way instead of a very horrible way, you have to reach out to him.
   - *tvayā* – What is the use of explaining so much? You need his help.
   - *asau* – Are you not seeing him in front of you? Due to visualisation, she sees śrī rāma in front of her; and due to fear, rāvaṇa sees śrī rāma in front of him. rāvaṇa asks “Will he accept me who has committed so many offences?”
   - *puruśarśabha*: – He is puruśōttama (best among men) – he will not consider your offences.
- *dēvimār āvār tirumagaḷ bhūmi* – periya pirātti and āṇḍāḷ who are so dear to him that he will act upon the direction of their eyebrows; [śrī mahālakśmi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/) is the teacher who teaches compassion to him as said in “*nakaścin nāparādyati*” and [bhūmi dēvi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/andal/) is the fertile field where that compassion grows, as she asks “what do you have to tolerate? did he even commit an offence?” While they are present, what is there for me to lose?
- *Eva* – It is explained that just as kainkaryam is the goal, their ordering us to engage in kainkaryam is also part of the goal; śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 15.7 “*kriyatāmiti mām vada*” (lakśmaṇa to śrī rāma – order me in what should be done); his voice would be as deep as the sound of a thunderous cloud, pouring rain.
- *maṟṟu amarar ātceyvār* – nityasūris are the ones who remain close and serve [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) and his divine consorts. maṟṟu indicates *tulyavikalpa* (exact variation); that is whatever pleasure derived by his divine consorts when he embraces them, will be derived by the nityasūris who serve the togetherness; as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam bāla kāṇḍam 1.31 “*ramamāṇā vanē traya:*” (all 3 – śrī rāma, sītā and lakśmaṇa enjoyed together in the forest), the pleasures match the individual’s true nature; the pleasure derived by perumāḷ (śrī rāma) and (sītā) pirātti in their union, will be derived by iḷaiya perumāḷ (lakśamaṇa) by seeing their togetherness.
- *amarar ātceyvār* – As said in [tiruvāimoḻi 4.6.8](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/03/thiruvaimozhi-4-6-8-vedham-vallargalai/) “*vēdam vallārgaḷaik koṇḍu*” (with the help of those who are well versed in vēdam), nityasūris also remain as puruśakārabhūtar \[those who present our case to [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), like pirātti\].

Even if his consorts are present, and the nityasūris who are comparable to his consorts are also present, we can say that he will not fulfil our desire, if he has some limitation in his wealth/control,

- *mēviya …* – Indicating the three layers of worlds; or indicating the three types of cētanas \[nityasūris (eternal residents of paramapadam), muktātmās (liberated souls), baddātmās (bound souls)\].
- *mēviya* – Indicating that if we said he is the protector for the worlds, it will be apt; or saying his reign fits well for him. śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 2.13 “*trailōkyamapi nātēna yēna syānnātavattaram*” (In śrī rāma, all the three worlds have an apt leader) – even if the three worlds are taken together, that which is to be protected will be small and his desire to protect them will be great.
- *vēṇḍu vēṇḍuruvam nin uruvam* – As necessary for the protection; or as said in śrī viṣṇu purāṇam 6.5.84 “*iccā gruhītābhimatōru dēha:*” (many forms assumed by bhagavān out of his own desire); or it is saying that [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) will accept the forms which are desired by his devotees for him.
- *pāviyēn tannai* – Me who has committed such sins to lose you even after having puruśakāram, wealth, and divine forms which are under the control of his devotees; I became outside his family!
- *aduginṟa* – perishing. Oh one who is having cool eyes which give motherly protection to everyone!
- *pavaḷa vāy* – Oh one who has beautiful smile as said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 5.17.21 “*savilāsasmitādāram bibhrāṇam mukapankajam*” (one who has the lotus like face which has smiling, beautiful lotus-like mouth/lips)!
- *maṇiyē* – Just as one would let out cool water towards the face of a tired person, oh one who has an invigorating form! These features of yours sustain me.
- *āviyē* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s life is not just a type of air \[prāṇa (vital air)\]; his life is [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) with his divine consorts, nityasūris and his beautiful form with beautiful eyes and lips.
- *amudē* – Being the vital air which makes him sustain himself, āḻvār also has emperumān as the most enjoyable nectar not having to search for enjoyment elsewhere. As he is the enjoyment, emperumān remains the upāyam (means) as well, so that [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) need not put any effort to attain him.
- *alai kadal kadainda appanē* – Oh one who performs great task even for those who are with worldly desires!

[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) asks “What shall I do for you?” [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says,

- *kāṇumāṟu aruḷāy* – You don’t need to churn the ocean for me, but it is sufficient if you show me that divine form. (kāṇumāṟu) Seeing his divine form is the prāpyam (goal); (aruḷ) his mercy is the prāpakam (means). Would you not fulfil the desire of those who feel “you are the goal and the means”?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

adiyen saraty ramanuja dasan

## 8.1.2. Kanumararulay

*kāṇumāṟaruḷāy enṟenṟē kalangik kaṇṇa nīr alamara vinaiyēn pēṇumāṟellām pēṇi nin peyarē pidaṟṟumaṟaruḷenakkandō! kāṇumāṟaruḷāy kāguttā! kaṇṇā! toṇḍanēn kaṟpagak kaniyē! pēṇuvāramudē! periya tadam punal sūḻ perunilam edutta pērāḷā!*

**Пословный перевод:**

kāṇumāṟu – to be able to see you; aruḷāy – show your mercy; enṟu enṟu – saying this repeatedly; kalangi – (being unable to see him) becoming bewildered; kaṇṇa nīr – tears; alamara – as it spreads; vinaiyēn – me who is sinful to not see you; pēṇum – engaging in (even after losing self and belongings of self, by surrendering many times, becoming bewildered etc); āṟu – methods; ellām – all; pēṇi – engaged; nin – your; peyarē – divine names only; pidaṟṟumāṟu – to recite incohesively and call out; enakku – (doing this) for me; aruḷ – mercy; andō – alas!; kāguttā – Being born as a descendant of kaktsta (raghu vamśam, and presented yourself to those who were in forest and city); kaṇṇā – being born as kriṣṇa (and made yourself easily approachable and enjoyable to the covherd girls); toṇḍanēn – for me who is desirous; kaṟpagam – you are generous (to manifest yourself to me); kaniyē – being a ripened fruit (which is to be consumed immediately); pēṇuvār – for those who are desirous; amudē – the eternally enjoyable nectar which helps one sustain the self; periya – boundless; taṇ – cool; punal – water of the deluge; sūḻ – drowned; perunilam – the huge earth; edutta – dug out; pērāḷā – oh great personality!; kāṇumāṟu – to be seen and enjoyed (by me); aruḷāy – shower your mercy

**Перевод:**

**Alas! You have shown your mercy upon me to recite your divine names incohesively and call out for you after repeatedly saying “show your mercy upon me to be able to see you”, having tears spread in my eyes and engaging in all methods which are to be engaged; oh great personality who dug out the huge earth which was drowned in the cool, boundless water of the deluge! You are generous;  you are a ripened fruit; you are the eternally enjoyable nectar which helps one sustain the self, for those who are desirous; you shower your mercy upon me to see you and enjoy you;**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the second pāsuram, āḻvār says “Did you mercifully wait to see me saying ‘when will I see you?’ in suffering? Alas! Instead of making me suffer like that, you should mercifully let me see you”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār thinks about the enjoyability of emperumān‘s forms in “vēṇḍuvēṇḍuruvam ninnuruvam” and requests emperumān to show mercy upon him to stop his suffering.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. kāṇumāṟaruḷāy enṟenṟē kalangik kaṇṇa nīr alamara vinaiyēn pēṇumāṟellām pēṇi nin peyarē pidaṟṟumaṟaruḷenakkandō! kāṇumāṟaruḷāy kāguttā! kaṇṇā! toṇḍanēn kaṟpagak kaniyē! pēṇuvāramudē! periya tadam punal sūḻ perunilam edutta pērāḷā!*

- *kāṇumāṟu aruḷāy* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is not of the type to say “let me try on my own to attain him” when he asks [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) to appear infront of him and emperumān does not do so. Like the cātaka bird which sustains itself only with direct rain water, āḻvār looks for emperumān’s mercy only. Hence, he again says “*kāṇumāṟu aruḷāy*“.
- *enṟu enṟē* – These are his words always. Only if there is another refuge, he can take shelter of that.
- *kalangi* – bewilderment only increases; śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 100.1 “*jatilam cīravasanam prānjalim patitam bhuvi\| dadarśa rāmō durdarśam yugāntē bhāskaram yatā \|\|*” (Having matted hair, wearing tree-bark-robes, having joint palms, lying flat on the earth. [śrī rāma](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) unable to bear that vision that is like the radiant sun during dissolution).
- *kaṇṇa nīr alamara* – Just as a filled lake will overflow, the internal torment comes overflowing as tears.
- *vinaiyēn* – Until now, there has been no one who has desired for [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) but ended with tears! I am so sinful that I have desired to see him who wipes the tears of even those who have a little desire to see him, and ended up with tearful eyes.
- *pēṇumāṟu ellām pēṇi* – pēṇugai – desiring. First considered self to be unqualified to be with him and left him; then said that there is no use of self and belongings of self, when not desired by him; then with great sorrow, performed madal; surrendered in many ways; showed romantic anger and so on.
- *nin peyarē pidaṟṟumāṟu aruḷ enakku* – as you tried to shower your mercy upon me, I have ended up incohesively reciting your names; is this what your mercy is – to make me call out your divine names in sorrow of not attaining you? Are you remaining silent thinking “as I have made [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) to call out for me instead of hankering for worldly pleasures”? Am I desiring to just be different from samsāris (worldly people)? Should I not have my goal attained?
- *vinaiyēn pēṇumāṟu ellām pēṇi* – pēṇudal – desiring. Desiring in all manner. Are there many ways to desire? Yes; \[two types of desires\] desiring for apt aspect and desiring for aspect which we like. For āḻvār, both apt aspect and desirable aspect are the same. In case of apt aspect, the desire will be in proper order, and in desirable aspect, the desire will be without any boundary. For the apt aspect, one needs to surrender unto [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) to get it; he did that too in [tiruvāimoḻi 5.7](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/08/thiruvaimozhi-5-7-norra-nonbilen/) “*nōṟṟa nōnbu*“, [tiruvāimoḻi 5.8](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/08/thiruvaimozhi-5-7-aravamudhe/) “*ārāvamudu*“, [tiruvāimoḻi 5.9](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/09/thiruvaimozhi-5-9-maney-nokku/) “*mānēnōkku*“, [tiruvāimoḻi 5.10](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/09/thiruvaimozhi-5-10-pirandhavarum/) “*piṟandavāṟu*” and [tiruvāimoḻi 6.10](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/06/thiruvaimozhi-6-10-ulagamunda/) “*ulagamuṇḍa peruvāyan*“. For the desire in desirable aspect, one needs to do starting with sending a messenger and ending with performing madal (public display of dejection); he did that too starting with [tiruvāimoḻi 1.4](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/07/thiruvaimozhi-1-4-anjiraiya/) “*anjiṟaiya mada nārāy*” up to [tiruvāimoḻi 5.3](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/06/thiruvaimozhi-5-3-masaru-sodhi/) “*māsaṟu sōdi*“, [tiruvāimoḻi 6.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/10/thiruvaimozhi-6-1-vaigal/) “*vaigal pūngaḻivāy*“, [tiruvāimoḻi 6.8](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/04/thiruvaimozhi-6-8-ponnulagu/) “*ponnalagāḷīr*“. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying “in this manner, after pursuing all types of desires towards you, your mercy has only landed me into reciting your name incohesively”.
- *andō* – You have not tasted separation from yourself, and you have not seen those who are separated from you. nityasūris never separate from you, and samsāris don’t realize that they are separated from you; hence I am the only one who is having such sorrow.
- *kāṇumāṟu aruḷāy* – Either you bring tiruvāṟanviḷai near me or give me the strength to go there.

[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) asks “Why are you forcing me like this? Where did you see me show my mercy?”, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says

- *kāguttā* – śrī viṣṇu purāṇam 4.2.77 “*kakutsta vamśē vimukā:prayānti*” (Are you not born in kakutsta vamśam?) śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 1.13 is explained here – *rūpa samhananam* – your physical beauty, *lakśmīm* – your collective beauty, *saukumāryam* – even favourable persons cannot stare at you \[your body cannot tolerate that\]. *suvēśatām –* this ascetic appearance, *dadruśūr vismitākārā:* – the internal senses of those who saw you, became astonished. Who are they? *vanavāsina:* – The forest-dwellers who survived by eating dry leaves saw this amazing form of yours, which was not even seen by the residents of ayōdyā, the capital city.

[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) says “That was long back. Just because I did it back then, are you forcing me now?” [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says,

- *kaṇṇā* – Not just for riśis (sages), but did you not manifest yourself even for covherd girls and boys as said in śrī bhāgavatam 10.32.2 “… *tāsāmāvirabūt …*” (He appeared amidst the covherd girls like the cupid for cupids).

Further, Why should you search outside?

- *toṇḍanēn kaṟpagak kaniyē* – Oh one who fully gave yourself to me who was engaged in worldly matters and was only searching for them, by eliminating those desires from me!
- *pēṇuvār amudē* – Oh one who is perfectly enjoyable for those who don’t push you aside when you come and help them!
- *periya …* – Who prayed to you to make you rescue the universe from the deluge and protect it? Oh great personality who uplifted the great earth which was surrounded by the water during the deluge! Did you not protect the universe which neither desired you nor requested you to do so? Would you not protect as soon as you come to know about the danger?
- *pērāḷā* – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s desire to protect is much greater than that which is to be protected.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.1.3. Edutta peralan

*edutta pērāḷan nandagōpantan innuyirc ciruvanē! asōdaikku adutta pērinbak kula viḷangaḷiṟē! adiyanēn periya ammānē! kadutta pōr avuṇan udal iru piḷavāk kai ugir āṇḍa engadalē! aduttadōr uruvāy inṟu nī vārāy enganē tēṟuvar umarē?*

**Пословный перевод:**

edutta – acquired (you like an impoverished person finding great wealth); pērāḷan – great; nandagōpantan – for nandagōpa; in – perfectly enjoyable; uyir – being the life; siṟuvanē – having childishness (being very obedient); asōdaikku – for yaśōdā; adutta – attained; pērinbam – one who gave perfect joy (as said in “tollai inbattiṟudi“); kulam – for that clan; iḷam kaḷiṟē – living pridefully like an elephant calf; adiyanēn – for me, the servitor; periya – unreachable (by manifesting your greatness); ammānē – being my lord; kadutta pōr – having great desire for warfare; avuṇan – hiraṇyāsura’s; udal – body; iru piḷavu A – to become two pieces; kai – in the hand; ugir – nail; āṇḍa – had as the instrument; em kadalē – oh one who is an ocean (of care towards your devotees)!; inṟu – today too; aduttadu – matching; ōr uruvāy – having a form; vārāy – not arriving; umar – those who depend upon you; enganam – how; tēṟuvar – will have faith?

**Перевод:**

**The great nandagōpa acquired you as the perfectly enjoyable child and had you as his life; you were attained by yaśōdā and gave perfect joy to her, living pridefully like an elephant calf of that clan; being my lord, you are unreachable for me, the servitor; oh one who is an ocean (of care towards your devotees)! you had the nail as an instrument in your hand to tear the body of hiraṇyāsura, who was having great desire for warfare, into two pieces; you are not arriving today with a matching form; how will those who depend upon you, have faith in you?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the third pāsuram, āḻvār says “If you, who are easily approachable by your followers, do not come today and eliminate my danger, how will your devotees who sustain themselves by your qualities, survive?”*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. edutta pērāḷan nandagōpantan innuyirc ciruvanē! asōdaikku adutta pērinbak kula viḷangaḷiṟē! adiyanēn periya ammānē! kadutta pōr avuṇan udal iru piḷavāk kai ugir āṇḍa engadalē! aduttadōr uruvāy inṟu nī vārāy enganē tēṟuvar umarē?*

- *edutta pērāḷan* – The most fortunate one who begot you as a son, like someone finding treasure. As both nandagōpa and vasudēva prayed to have [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) as son, vasudēva was unfortunate not to see kriṣṇa \[for more than a short period\] even after dēvaki gave birth to him, while nandagōpa saw kriṣṇa’s face like finding treasure. Just as a poor man who suddenly starts living luxuriously will be called “*ivan eduppeduttān*” (he must have found treasure), here [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says “*edutta*“.
- *pērāḷan* – Great personality. His greatness is the same as my smallness; would you only show your face to those who desire to have you as their son? kriṣṇa is the embodiment of śrī nandagōpa’s life.
- *asōdaikku adutta* – Though both \[dēvaki and yaśōdā\] prayed in the same manner, for dēvaki who physically gave birth to kriṣṇa, the suffering was greater; yaśōdā, enjoyed kriṣṇa, though she did not go through the trouble of labour. She got to see kriṣṇa as he himself came closer to her as said in śrī viṣṇu purāṇam 5.4.23 “*dadarśa prabudda sā yaśōdā jātam ātmajam*” (yaśōdā, having attained clarity, saw kriṣṇa, who appeared with the complexion of a blue lotus petal).
- *pērinbam* – One who caused perfect joy for her; as said in perumāḷ tirumoḻi 7.8 “*tollai inbattu iṟudi kaṇḍāḷē*” (yaśōdā enjoyed the ultimate state of supreme bliss), he gave her great bliss; he made the endless bliss in paramapadam look small when compared to the joy he gave her.
- *kula iḷam kaḷiṟē* – Oh one who is enjoyable elephant calf for the covherd clan! Also said as a wild elephant which is having great heritage and is attractive due to its youthful state, and is uncontrollable by yaśōdāp pirātti; but if gets caught, he is \[obedient\] like an elephant calf; when caught he would be like an elephant tied to a pole as said in periya tirumoḻi 2.10.6 “*taṟiyārnda karungaḷiṟē pōla ninṟu*” (standing like a dark elephant tied to a pole). \[periya tirumoḻi 2.10.6 is further explained\] “*tadangaṇgaḷ pani malgum*” (will have teary eyes) – when she says as in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 5.6.14 “… *yadi śaknōśi gacca tvam …*” (yaśōdā tied the mischievous [kriṣṇa](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) into a mortar with a rope and angrily told him “Oh one with mischievous activities! if you are capable, free yourself and go now”), he has no other option than standing with teary eyes; to be controlled by her, does it not mean sarvaśakta (omnipotent [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)) should remain aśakta (incapable)? *tanmaiyānai* – one who has the nature of being subservient to his devotees?
- *adiyanēn periya ammānē* – Would you only help those who think of you as their son? Would you not help those who understand the true relationship between them and you? As I stand in proper state towards you, you are not responding properly. While I said “*adiyēn*” (servitor), you are not remaining as īśvara (lord).
- *kadutta …* – To split the body of hiraṇyāsura who had craving for warfare, into two pieces.
- *kai ugir āṇḍa* – As said in “*padai āṇḍān*” (rules over the army).
- *em kadalē* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) considers [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s help to prahlāda arriving with great zeal as said in narasimha mantram “*mahāviṣṇum*” (the great viṣṇu), as help for āḻvār himself.
- *aduttadu ōr uruvāy* – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) stood everywhere in this form, since he could not guess the place which will be pointed out by hiraṇya. As hiraṇya put too many conditions, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) assumed a form spontaneously at that time; also explained as assuming a form which evades his boons as said in mahābhāratam “*narasyārda tanum krutvā simhasyārda tanum tatā*” (half human body and half lion body); also explained as, emperumān in a hurry, picked up the head of one creature and the body of another, and assumed a form with that. He assumed a matching form and split the body of the demon who was eager for warfare.
- *inṟu nī vārāy* – Is your help not needed both then and now? You helped then, but not now. You helped the one who had viparīta jñānam \[nandagōpa who considered you as his son\]; you helped the one who had yatā jñānam \[prahlāda who considered you as his lord properly\]; am I outside both these groups? You helped the one who was bewildered that you are his son; you helped the one who had clarity in saying as in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 1.19.85 “*mattas sarvam aham sarvam mayi sarvam sanātanē*” (prahlāda said “Everything originated from me and everything subdued into me, who is eternal”); would you only not help me who is also bewildered saying ‘”*enṟenṟē kalangi*” \[previous pāsuram\]? Even if you don’t show up, for those who would like to survive, they have to fall at your feet.

emperumān says “Leave that aside; why are you worried now?”, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says

- *enganam tēṟuvar umarē* – If you don’t come even now, would those who sustain themselves by your qualities, survive? That is, saying “How will those who consider ‘your qualities are our refuge’ have faith in you?”

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.1.4. Umar ugandu

*umar uganduganda uruvam nin uruvam āgi untanakku anbarānār avar ugandamarnda seygai un māyai aṟivonṟum sangippan vinaiyēn amar adu paṇṇi agalidam pudai sūḻ adu padai avitta ammānē! amarar tam amudē! asurargaḷ nanjē! ennudai ār uyirēyō!*

**Пословный перевод:**

adu – world famous through his acts of going as a messenger etc; amar – war; paṇṇi – caused; agal – expansive; idam – earth’s; pudai – surroundings; sūḻ – covered; adu – engaged in killing; padai – army; avitta – destroyed (without any trace); ammānē – being the lord; amarartam – for (favourable) dēvas; amudē – being very enjoyable; asurargaḷ – for (unfavourable) asuras; nanjē – being poison (which will destroy them); ennudai – for me; Ar uyirē – oh one who sustains me!; umar – your exclusive servitors; ugandu uganda – always enjoyed; uruvam – form; nin – your; uruvamāgi – being your form; untanakku – in that form; anbarānār avar – those who have love; ugandu – with the desire; amarnda – without any other expectation; seygai – to engage in service; un – your; māyai – amazing activities; aṟivu onṟum – even this knowledge with which I know; sangippan – am doubting; vinaiyēn – I who have sin to doubt the very principle which is our refuge; O – alas! (highlighting his loss)

**Перевод:**

**emperumān, being the lord, caused the world famous war, which had his acts of going as a messenger etc, destroyed the army which covered the surroundings of the expansive earth; he is enjoyable for dēvas and is like poison for asuras; oh such emperumān who sustains me! You are having as your form, the form that is always enjoyed by your exclusive devotees; your amazing activities make your exclusive devotees who love such form of yours, to desirously engage in service without any other expectation; I who have the sin to doubt the very principle of such knowledge which is our refuge, am doubting that principle now; alas!**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fourth pāsuram, āḻvār says “I who sustained myself by thinking that you will be pleased by your forms and activities which are pleasing to your devotees, am doubting if my understanding is true”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. umar uganduganda uruvam nin uruvam āgi untanakku anbarānār avar ugandamarnda seygai un māyai aṟivonṟum sangippan vinaiyēn amar adu paṇṇi agalidam pudai sūḻ adu padai avitta ammānē! amarar tam amudē! asurargaḷ nanjē! ennudai Ar uyirēyō!*

- *umar ugandu uganda uruvam nin uruvamāgi* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying “You are having the form that is desired by those who are your exclusive devotees, as your divine form”; or āḻvār is saying “you desire a particular form since it is desired by those who are favourable towards you and that becomes your form”. As said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 4.11](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/4-11/) “*yē yatā mām prapadyantē tāms tataiva bhajāmyaham*” (I reach those who surrender unto me, In whichever way they desire me, in the same way which they desired), mudal tiruvandādi 44 “*tamar ugandadu evvuruvam*” (forms desired by devotees).
- *untanakku anbaranār avar* – those who are overwhelmingly affectionate towards you.
- *ugandu* – showing great love.
- *amarnda seygai un māyai* – Your amazing activities, which make them approach and serve you without any expectation.
- *aṟivu onṟum sangippan vinaiyēn* – this  knowledge about [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s qualities is that which sustains [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/); now, he is having unnecessary doubt in that only.
- *vinaiyēn* – Just because I become worried and doubt unnecessarily, it does not make his qualities non-existent; my unnecessary doubt is due to my own sin; sītāp pirātti too said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 26.13 “*kyāta: prājña: krutajñaśca sānukrōśaśca rāghava: \| satvruttō niranukrōśaś śankē madbhājña sankśayāt \|\|*” – for śrī rāma who has such great qualities, my unnecessary doubts will not mean that he does not have those qualities; it is only my misfortune, which makes me unnecessarily doubt like this \[this ślōkam is explained in detail in the introduction section of this decad\].
- *amar adu paṇṇi* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is showing an example to highlight that [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is partial towards his devotees; making “that” war happen. It is known as “*mahābhāratam*“; it caused discomfort for the whole earth.
- *sūḻ adu padai avitta* – Destroyed the army which surrounded in all directions to kill him. All the evil minded persons united and rose like forest fire, and arrived shouting “sārati! sārati!”, and [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) put them out \[like putting out the fire\]. kriṣṇa, the dark cloud as said in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 3.4.1 “*maḻaikolō varuginṟadu*” (arriving like rain), rose and put them out.
- *ammānē* – Being sarvasvāmi (lord of all), due to partiality towards his devotees, he eliminated the enemies.
- *amarar tam amudē* – Being perfectly enjoyable for the dēvas, since he accepted arrows on him from asuras for them.
- *asurargaḷ nanjē* – Oh one who is like unbearable poison for those who are demoniac by birth and those who are demoniac by qualities!
- *ennudai Ar uyirēyō* – Oh one who is the reason for my sustenance! [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) being enjoyable for dēvas and poisonous for asuras, is that which sustains [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.1.5. Aruyireyo!

*āruyirēyō! agalidamuḻudum padaittidandu uṇḍumiḻndu aḷanda pēruyirēyō! periya nīr padaittu anguṟaindadu kadaindadaittudaitta sīriyarēyō! manisarkkut tēvar pōlat tēvarkkum dēvāvō! ōruyirēyō! ulagangatkellām unnai nān engu vanduṟugō!*

**Пословный перевод:**

āruyirē – being my perfect life; agal – expansive; idam – world; muḻudum – all; padaittu – created; idandu – dug it out (without getting destroyed in deluge); uṇḍu – protected it by placing it in stomach; umiḻndu – spit it out (to let it see outside); aḷanda – measured and accepted (to eliminate the claim of ownership by others); pēruyirē – being the lord who is greater than all; periya nīr – the singular \[causal\] ocean which is a huge water body; padaittu – created; angu – there; uṟaindu – mercifully rested; adu – kśīrārṇavam (milk ocean, which is a transformed state of that causal ocean); kadaindu – churned; adaittu – built a bridge (across another ocean which is of the same kind); udaitta – broke (to provide fresh water for samsāris (worldly people) by his danuśkōti (edge of his bow)); sīriyarē – being the best (like the soul, in protecting his devotees); manisarkku – for humans et al; tēvarpōla – like dēvas who are desirable \[object of worship\]; tēvarkkum – for dēvas; dēvā – being the (desirable) refuge; ulagangatkellām – for all the creatures (which are sustained by prāṇa); ōruyirē – Oh singular ātmā!; unnai – Other than you (who are the singular ātmā \[paramātmā\] unlike the jīvātmās who are many in count and who remain the dāraka (one who sustains), śēśi (lord), parivan (caretaker), uddēśya (desirable) for their bodies); nān – I (who am dārya (sustained), śēṣabhūta (servitor), rakśya (protected), āśraya (depend on), niyāmya (controlled) by/for you only); engu – where; vandu – come; uṟugō – will attain you?

**Перевод:**

**Being my life and being the lord who is greater than all, you created all the expansive world, dug it out, protected it by placing it in stomach, spat it out, measured and accepted it; you being the best, created the singular \[causal\] ocean which is a huge water body and mercifully rested there; you churned kśīrārṇavam, built a bridge and broke the ocean; just like dēvas are desirable for humans et al, you are desirable for dēvas; oh singular ātmā who is being the refuge for all the creatures! Where else other than you, will I come and attain? āḻvār is implying “While you who are supremely independent can put in some effort and that will lead to the result, if I who am fully dependent on you put in some effort, there is no possibility of getting the result”. “O” in the end of the worlds reveals āḻvār’s anguish thinking “how can paramātmā suggest the ātmā to put in some effort!”**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fifth pāsuram, when emperumān says “you perform the necessary sādanānuśtānam (means) and come and see me”, āḻvār responds “there is no such thing that I put in some effort to reach you and see you; you, who are the controller of all, should show me yourself”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Fifth pāsuram. emperumān says “As the result is for you as said in pūrva mīmāmsā ‘śāstrapalam prayōktari (When ātmā becomes kartā (doer), śāstram is of use), should the effort also be in you?” āḻvār responds “There is nothing which can be seen and attained by my effort”. āruyirēyō! agalidamuḻudum padaittidandu uṇḍumiḻndu aḷanda pēruyirēyō! periya nīr padaittu anguṟaindadu kadaindadaittudaitta sīriyarēyō! manisarkkut tēvar pōlat tēvarkkum dēvāvō! ōruyirēyō! ulagangatkellām unnai nān engu vanduṟugō!*

- *āruyirēyō* – When you are my life, what sādanānuśtānam can I perform to reach you? īsn’t the protection of the śarīram (body), the responsibility of the ātmā (soul)? Will the body protect itself?

[āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) asks “Is it just the relationship? Have you also not demonstrated?”

- *agal idam muḻudum padaittu* – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) created the expansive world through his sankalpam as stated in taittirīya upaniśat “*bahusyām*” (let me become many), dug it out as mahāvarāha when it was tormenting in deluge, protected it by placing it in his stomach during the subsequent deluge, spat it out so that it does not suffocate inside for a longtime, walked up and measured it when it was snatched by mahābali. Should you who help others in difficult times without them calling out for you, not help me as well?
- *pēruyirēyō* – Oh great lord!
- *periya nīr …* – He is indifferent towards all kinds of help irrespective of whether it is done for all or his own dear consort, śrī mahālakśmi.
- *periya nīr padaittu angu uṟaindu* – Created the causal ocean and rested there for the purpose of creation.
- *adu kadaindu …* – He churned the ocean to acquire her \[śrī mahālakśmi\]; he then built a bridge to unite with her and subsequently broke it so that the rākśasas from there will not be able to cross over the ocean to trouble the devotees.
- *sīriyarēyō* – Oh one who has the greatness of equally accepting pirātti who is eternally united with you and others!
- *manisar …* – Just as dēvas are with respect to manuśyas with respect to their wealth/opulence and greatness, sarvēśvaran is superior with respect to those dēvas.
- *ōr uyirēyō ulagangatkellām* – Will the body or the ātmā think about the well-being? \[ōr – distinguished\] If there is any other entity like you, I can engage in sādanānuśtānam to attain you. What will I who am a body for you who are my soul, do as means, to attain you? While the ātmā can care for the well-being of the body, can the body itself care for it? How can I, who am supported by you, controlled by you and servitor to you, protect while you, who are the support, controller and lord, exist? As ātmā has the identity of being śarīra (body) for bhagavān due to ādāra – ādēya (support – supported) and niyantru – niyāmya (controller – controlled) relationships, the consciousness in the ātmā is only present to accept that “You are the means” and not to individually engage in sādanānuśtānam.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.1.6. Engu vandurugo?

*engu vanduṟugō? ennai āḷvānē! ēḻulagangaḷum nīyē angavarkkamaitta deyvamum nīyē avaṟṟavai karumamum nīyē pongiya puṟambāl poruḷuḷavēlum avaiyumō nī innē ānāl mangiya aruvām nērppamum nīyē vān pulan iṟandadum nīyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ennai – me; āḷvānē – (to reach up to this stage) oh one who ruled!; ēḻ ulagangaḷum – all worlds (wherein those who engage in sādanānuśtānam (means to attain emperumān) do their practice, and where they get their results); nīyē – at your disposal; angu – in those worlds; avarkku – vorśippers (who desire for results); amaitta – made (for the fulfilment of their wishes and for their worship); deyvamum – \[demi\] gods; nīyē – at your disposal; avaṟṟavai – towards those demigods; karumamum – rituals (of worship); nīyē – at your disposal; pongiya – overflowing (beyond these worlds); puṟambāl – outside; poruḷ – all entities (such as mahat (the great element) etc); uḷavēlum – as they are present (as explained popularly in pramāṇams (authentic texts)); avaiyum – those as well; nī – at your disposal; mangiya – without name and form (during the state of deluge); aruvām nērppamum – cit (sentient entities) and acit (insentient entities) in subtle state; nīyē – at your disposal; vān – in supreme sky (paramapadam); pulan iṟandadum – the group of muktātmās who are beyond our senses; nīyē – at your disposal; innē – in this manner; ānāl – as you are the antaryāmi of all entities; nān – I (who am under your exclusive control); unnai – you; engu – where; vandu uṟugō – will come and attain?

**Перевод:**

**Oh one who ruled me! All worlds are at your disposal; all the demigods who are created for the vorśippers, are at your disposal; all the rituals towards those demigods are at your disposal; all entities which are present outside these worlds as well are at your disposal; all cit and acit in subtle state without name and form are at your disposal; the group of muktātmās who are beyond our senses, in supreme sky, are at your disposal; as you are the antaryāmi of all entities in this manner, where will I come and attain you?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the sixth pāsuram, āḻvār elaborates what was highlighted in the previous pāsuram.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “Since you are the antaryāmi of both causal and effectual entities, where can I come and attain you?”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. engu vanduṟugō? ennai āḷvānē! ēḻulagangaḷum nīyē angavarkkamaitta deyvamum nīyē avaṟṟavai karumamum nīyē pongiya puṟambāl poruḷuḷavēlum avaiyumō nī innē ānāl mangiya aruvām nērppamum nīyē vān pulan iṟandadum nīyē*

- *engu vanduṟugō* – Can a lame person reach one who is on top of the peak of the mēru \[a huge mountain which anchors the universe\]?
- *ennai āḷvānē* – Only if I reached this stage on my own, I could aim to reach you \[on my own\]?
- *ēḻulagangaḷum nīyē* – Oh one who has all the worlds at your disposal! Unlike me who has desire, those others who are indifferent towards you only are under your control!
- *angavarkku amaitta deyvamum nīyē* – The dēvatās (demigods) who rule over the residents of those worlds, are under your control.
- *avaṟṟavai karumamum nīyē* – Are the responsibilities and actions of those dēvatās under their own control? \[No – they are also under your control\] Thus, it is expalined that all the effectual entities are under your control.
- *pongiya …* – More expansive when compared to one another, mahat etc which are beyond these worlds, are also under your control.
- *mangiya …* – Even the avyakta (unmanifest matter) which has attained the subtle state after deluge is under your control.
- *vān pulan iṟandadum nīyē* – Unlike these, like the ether which can pervade avayakta, which is beyond the senses such as cakśur (eyes) etc, the whole group of ātmās are also under your control. āḻvār is saying “all the bound souls are also at your disposal”.
- *innē ānāl … engu vanduṟugō* – As this is the true reality, where will I come and attain you?

piḷḷān explains that “*mangiya aruvām nērppam*” means whole group of bound souls and “*vān pulan iṟandadu*” means whole group of liberated souls. In that case, the \[bound\] souls in subtle state which are as good as acit \[during deluge\], and the \[liberated\] souls in paramapadam which are beyond the senses, are explained. What is implied through this? Whether it is causal state, effectual state or in liberated state, everyone is looking for your support. Hence, is there anything I can do here?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.1.7. Irandadum niye

*iṟandadum nīyē edirndadum nīyē nigaḻvadō nī innē ānāl siṟanda nin tanmai adu idu udu enṟu aṟivonṟum sangippan vinaiyēn kaṟanda pāl neyyē! neyyin in suvaiyē! kadalinuḷ amudamē! amudil piṟanda in suvaiyē! suvaiyadu payanē! pinnai tōḷ maṇanda pērāyā!*

**Пословный перевод:**

kaṟanda – even while extracted; pāl – milk (which is having natural taste); neyyē – ghee (which is the essence of milk); neyyin – ghee’s; in – sweet; suvaiyē – being the taste; kadalinuḷ – came from the \[milk\] ocean; amudamē – being nectar; amudil – in that nectar; piṟanda – originated from; in suvaiyē – sweetness (which is greater than what is found in this earth); suvaiyadu – caused by such sweetness; payanē – the resulting pleasure; pinnai – nappinnaip pirātti; tōḷ – with her divine shoulders; maṇanda – united; pērāyā – oh great kriṣṇa!; vinaiyēn – I who am having sins (which stop me from enjoying your eternal enjoyability); iṟandadum nīyē edirndadum nīyē nigaḻvadu O nī – all entities (individually) from past, future and present are at your disposal; innē – in this manner; ānāl – being the case; adu – far; idu – close by; udu – all entities which are present in between; siṟanda – distinguished; nin – your; tanmai – attributes; enṟu – as; aṟivu – this true knowledge of knowing; onṟum – everything; sangippan – I doubt if that will be lost

**Перевод:**

**Oh great kriṣṇa who united with nappinnaip pirātti’s divine shoulders! You are the naturally tasty milk, ghee and the sweet taste of ghee; you are the nectar which came from the ocean, the sweetness originated from that nectar and the resulting pleasure from that sweetness; I have true knowledge of knowing that all entities (individually) from past, future and present are at your disposal and all the entities which are present far away, close by and in between, are the  attributes of you who are distinguished; due to my sins, I doubt if that knowledge too will be lost.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the seventh pāsuram, āḻvār says “I, who am sustaining myself with the knowledge that the whole cosmos is subservient to you, am doubting whether this is false due to my own karma \[sinful deeds\]”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. iṟandadum nīyē edirndadum nīyē nigaḻvadō nī innē ānāl siṟanda nin tanmai adu idu udu enṟu aṟivonṟum sangippan vinaiyēn kaṟanda pāl neyyē! neyyin in suvaiyē! kadalinuḷ amudamē! amudil piṟanda in suvaiyē! suvaiyadu payanē! pinnai tōḷ maṇanda pērāyā!*

- *iṟandadu …* – Can you say “I am in charge, as of now, and there are others who will take care of other times”? All entities of past, future and present are at your disposal. This has to be read along with \[the previous pāsuram\] “*innē ānāl … engu vanduṟugō*” (this being the case, where can I attain you?)
- *siṟanda nin tanmai adu idu udu enṟu* – All entities which are at a distance, close by and in between are prakāra (attribute) for you who are distinguished due to your lordship. This is explained in two ways – a) as entities from all three times (past, future and present) are at your disposal, it can be said that all entities are your attributes; b) as entities which are at a distance, close by and in between are your attributes, all entities of past, future and present are at your disposal.
- *enṟu aṟivonṟum sangippan* – āḻvār sustains himself by the knowledge that as everything other than himself are his attributes \[reference is to [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)\], if anything happens to them, he would feel that he is impacted and care for them; as that has not materialized for me, I am doubting that knowledge itself.
- *vinaiyēn* – as I doubt unnecessarily due to my bewilderment, he will not lose his nature; I am having this confusion due to my own sins. śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 26.13 “*śankē madbhājña sankśayāt*” (it is only my misfortune, which makes me unnecessarily doubt like this) – there is a huge difference between the doubt here and the doubt in the fourth pāsuram. If there is an unnecessary doubt in [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s quality of being āśrita paratantra (fully dependent on his devotees), one can convince oneself that there may be some shortcoming in the devotee’s surrender towards him; but here the unnecessary doubt is in his intrinsic nature itself. His existence is based on having everything as attributes; all other entities exist due to being his attributes.

When asked “Why are you having unnecessary doubt in his intrinsic nature itself?” āḻvār explains

- *kaṟanda pāl …* – The reason for my unnecessary doubt is due to your enjoyability which makes one think the whole universe has dissolved, in your separation.
- *kaṟanda pāl* – āḻvār is thinking about the natural taste even while extracting; there is no milk which is not extracted \[so no need to specifically say “*kaṟanda pāl*“\]; here āḻvār is distinguishing the taste acquired by other reasons \[such as boiling it, adding sugar etc\].
- *neyyē* – the essence of milk, ghee.
- *neyyin in suvaiyē* – Oh one who is the sweet taste of ghee!
- *kadalinuḷ amudamē* – Oh one who is enjoyable like the nectar which is the essence acquired by churning the great ocean!
- *amudil piṟanda in suvaiyē* – āḻvār is talking about the taste of the nectar.
- *suvaiyadu payanē* – Oh one who is the embodiment of the pleasure acquired by enjoying the taste of nectar!

After explaining the intrinsic taste in a step by step manner \[starting from milk, up to the pleasure of nectar\], since that was not satisfying, āḻvār is highlighting [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) himself directly.

- *pinnai tōḷ maṇanda pērāyā* – āḻvār’s enjoyment rests on the divine couple. As emperumān gives pleasure to samsāris \[worldly people to attract them\], nappinnaip pirātti gives pleasure to the blissful emperumān. For āḻvār, their beautiful togetherness is the object of enjoyment.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.
