## 8.1.8. Mananda peraya

*maṇanda pērāyā! māyattāl muḻudum valvinaiyēnai īrginṟa guṇangaḷai udaiyāy ! asurar vankaiyar kūṟṟamē! kodiya puḷ uyarttāy! paṇangaḷ āyiram udaiya painnāgap paḷḷiyāy! pāṟkadal sēṟppā! vaṇangumāṟaṟiyēn manamum vāsagamum seygaiyum yānum nī tānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

māyattāl – by amazing activities; muḻudum – all entities; maṇanda – being close with his dear consort, and giving joy; pērāyā – being kriṣṇa having greatness; val vinaiyēnai – me who is having powerful sins to not be united in that manner; īrginṟa – always tormenting; guṇangaḷai – qualities (such as simplicity, easy approacability, beauty etc); udaiyāy – (naturally) having; van kai asurar – for powerful asuras (who are enemies of devotees); kūṟṟamē – being death; kodiya – (on seeing, the enemies will) perish; puḷ – periya tiruvadi (garuda); uyarttāy – having (as flag); āyiram paṇangaḷ – thousand hoods; udaiya – having; pai – very expansive; nāgam – tiruvanantāḻvān (ādiśēśan); paḷḷi – mattress; āy – having; pāṟkadal – in milk ocean; sērppā – oh one who is mercifully resting!; manamum vāsagamum seygaiyum – senses in the form of mind, speech and body; yānum – me too (who is the abode for those senses); nī tānē – appear to be you; vaṇangum – to worship; āṟu aṟiyēn – don’t know any doer or faculties (senses)

**Перевод:**

**kriṣṇa is having greatness of giving joy to all entities, by being close with his dear consort and engaging in amazing activities; he is having the qualities which are always tormenting me who is having powerful sins to not be united in that manner; he is having garudāḻvān who is like death for powerful asuras who will perish on seeing him \[garuda\], as his flag; oh one who is resting on the mattress of ādiśēśan who is having very expansive thousand hoods, in milk ocean! I and my senses in the form of mind, speech and body appear to be you \[your attributes\]; hence I don’t know any doer or faculties to worship you.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the eighth pāsuram,  emperumān asks “Still, should you not put in some effort?” and āḻvār responds “Since the ātmā (self) and its belongings are all yours, and I have nothing in me, I cannot do anything; you being capable of giving protection, and having the nature to protect others, should yourself come and accept me”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. maṇanda pērāyā! māyattāl muḻudum valvinaiyēnai īrginṟa guṇangaḷai udaiyāy ! asurar vankaiyar kūṟṟamē! kodiya puḷ uyarttāy! paṇangaḷ āyiram udaiya painnāgap paḷḷiyāy! pāṟkadal sēṟppā! vaṇangumāṟaṟiyēn manamum vāsagamum seygaiyum yānum nī tānē*

- *maṇanda pērāyā māyattāl* – Oh great kriṣṇa who embraced nappinnaip pirātti’s shoulders with great desire! \[greatness\] Covherd qualities are much greater in kriṣṇa than in nappinnaip pirātti.
- *muḻudum val vinaiyēnai īrginṟa guṇangaḷai udaiyāy* – Oh one who is having all the qualities which torment me, unlike some qualities tormenting and other qualities helping me to sustain myself! The reason for the torment is due to those being your qualities and the recipient being me,
- *val vinaiyēn* – While some \[like āṇḍāḷ who said in nācciyār tirumoḻi 8.3 “*en gōvindan guṇam pādi … āvi kāttiruppēnē*” (I will sing about my gōvinda’s qualities and sustain myself)\] sustain themselves by his qualities, I am having sins to have those qualities torment me.
- *īrginṟa* – They not only harm me; wound caused by arrow can be healed by applying medicine, but there is no remedy for the disease caused by his qualities.
- *asurar van kaiyar kūṟṟamē* – Oh one who is like death personified for the most prideful asuras similar to most cruel persons praying for a little bit of water from someone who is more cruel than they are!
- *kodiya puḷ uyarttāy* – Oh one who has garudāḻvān who will destroy the enemies on being seen by them, as your flag! To destroy the enemies, emperumān is not needed; mere sighting of his flag by them will lead to their destruction.
- *paṇangaḷ …* – tiruvanantāḻvān is having expanded hoods due to coming in contact with emperumān, is having many heads to release his internal bliss of enjoying emperumān, and is having vast space to let sarvēśvaran and his divine consorts to enjoy freely; oh one who is having such ādiśēśa as your mattress!
- *pāṟkadal sērppā* – Oh one who is resting in the milk ocean to hear the cries of your devotees!
- *vaṇangum āṟu aṟiyēn* – I don’t know any means to perform a kincitkāram (small service) to you who are ahead in giving protection to me by descending from paramapadam to kśīrābdi.

emperumān asks “How can you say that you don’t know the means? You have mind, speech and body, and you who are the abode for them, are there; why can’t you worship me?” āḻvār says

- *manamum …* – There should be a heart, speech and act which exist for me; there should be an I, who exist for me; but everything is at your disposal. I have the desire to worship you, but do not know the means.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.1.9. Yanum nidane

*yānum nīdānē āvadō meyyē arunaragavaiyum nī ānāl vān uyar inbam eydilen? maṟṟai naragamē eydilen? eninum yānum nīdānāy teḷidoṟum nanṟum anjuvan naragam nān adaidal vān uyar inbam manni vīṟṟirundāy! aruḷu nin tāḷgaḷai enakkē*

**Пословный перевод:**

yānum – I too (indicated as self); nīdānē – remain as you (as I am your prakāram (attribute)); āvadu – this principle; meyyē – is the ultimate truth; aru – insurmountable; naragu avaiyum – the entities in this greatly sorrowful samsāram; nī – your attributes; ānāl – this being the case; vān – in paramapadam (which matches the state of ātmā, the servitor for you who are distinguished); uyar – great; inbam – bliss; eydil en – what if we get it?; maṟṟai – (due to being inferior, nurturing independence and filled with sorrow) contrasting that \[i.e. bliss in paramapadam\]; naragamē – this naraka (hell) of samsāram (material realm); eydil – if we get; en – so what?; eninum – though this principle is prevalent in the world; yānum – I (who am distinguished, being identified by jñāna (knowledge) and ānanda (bliss)); nīdānāy – being you since it \[the self\] is an attribute for you (who are the opposite to all defects and the abode of all auspicious qualities); teḷidoṟum – when realised; naragam – this hellish samsāram; nān – I; adaidal – reaching \[remaining\]; nanṟum – very; anjuvan – scared; vān – in paramapadam (which is indicated by the word “paramavyōma” (supreme sky)); uyar – great (beyond speech and mind); inbam – bliss; manni – having; vīṟu – manifesting your distinguished nature of being the lord of all; irundāy – oh one who is mercifully seated!; nin – your; tāḷgaḷai – divine feet; enakku – for me; aruḷu – mercifully give

**Перевод:**

**This principle “I too remain as you” is the ultimate truth; the entities in this insurmountable, greatly sorrowful samsāram are your attributes; this being the case, though the principle “so what if I remain in paramapadam with great bliss or I remain in this hellish samsāram, which contrasts paramapadam?”  is prevalent in the world, whenever I realised that I am you because of being your attribute, I feel very scared to remain in this hellish samsāram. Oh one who is mercifully seated in paramapadam manifesting your distinguished nature of being the lord of all, having great bliss! Mercifully give your divine feet to me.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the ninth pāsuram, āḻvār says “Since every entity is subservient to you, though there is no difference being with this knowledge in this samsāram (material realm) or tirunādu (paramapadam – spiritual realm), I am scared to remain in samsāram which is a hurdle for this knowledge of subservience (towards you); hence, you should take me to tirunādu, which is favourable for such knowledge”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. yānum nīdānē āvadō meyyē arunaragavaiyum nī ānāl vān uyar inbam eydilen? maṟṟai naragamē eydilen? eninum yānum nīdānāy teḷidoṟum nanṟum anjuvan naragam nān adaidal vān uyar inbam manni vīṟṟirundāy! aruḷu nin tāḷgaḷai enakkē*

- *yānum nīdānē āvadō meyyē* – I am your attribute to be considered as implied by the word “You”, this meaning of I being indicated by the word “brahma” is truth. muktātmās always recite as said in bruhadāraṇyaka upaniśat “*ātmatyēvatu gruhṇīyāt*” (one should meditate on paramātmā considering him as self).
- *meyyē* – There is no doubt in it.
- *aru naragu avaiyum nī* – This samsāram which is unbearable for me and cannot resist leaving it, is also at your disposal. āḻvār is saying this now to indicate “You cannot eliminate this samsāram for me when you please \[you have to do it now\]”. Hence, this samsāram, which is a hurdle for me, and I are your attributes.
- *ānāl* – as this is the general principle.
- *vān uyar inbam eydil en* – So what if we attain perfect bliss after reaching paramapadam with knowledge of servitude?
- *maṟṟai naragamē eydil en* – So what if we remain in samsāram which is contrary to bliss and knowledge of servitude? There is a principle that one should remain where the owner places him/her.
- *eninum* – Though this principle is there.
- *nānum nīdānāyt teḷidoṟum* – Instead of thinking that this samsāram is outside your desire, as I get the clarity of “I am your confidential servitor”.
- *nanṟum anjuvan naragam nān adaidal* – Your highness thinks “As you have acquired knowledge of servitude, should the servitor not see what the master desires and remain as per his limits? Can the servitor force me?” Though you are thinking like this, I am very scared about existence is this samsāram since this samsāram is contrary to one’s faith in servitude.

[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) asks “Can I do anything just because you are scared?” āḻvār says

- *vān uyar inbam manni vīṟṟirundāy …* – Instead of being here \[in this samsāram\], you have a particular presence in nityavibhūti (paramapadam) where you remain perfectly blissful, manifesting your supremacy; you should invite me there and grant me distinguished interactions with you.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.1.10. Talgalai enakke

*tāḷgaḷai enakkē talait talaic ciṟappat tanda pērudavik kammāṟā tōḷgaḷai ārat taḻuvi en uyirai aṟavilai seydanan sōdī! tōḷgaḷ āyirattāy! mudigaḷ āyirattāy! tuṇai malark kaṇgaḷ āyirattāy! tāḷgaḷ āyirattāy! pērgaḷ āyirattāy! tamiyanēn periya appanē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

tāḷgaḷai – those divine feet; enakkē – to be there exclusively for me; talait talai – more and more; siṟappa – to shine; tanda – mercifully granted; pērudavi – for the great favour; kaimmāṟā – as gratitude \[return of favour\]; en – my; uyirai – self \[soul\]; tōḷgaḷai – shoulders; Ara – to have full satisfaction; taḻuvi – showing great love as if embracing (as if a physical entity); aṟavilai – unconditional offering; seydanan – I did; sōdī – oh one who is having radiance! (As I offered myself in bewilderment due to being grateful, without retracting as in “aduvum maṟṟu āngavan tannadu“, you accepted it blissfully as if accepting someone else’s belonging \[while the self is already your belonging\]); tōḷgaḷ āyirattāy – (not just the radiance, as said in “āyiram tōḷāl“, you are having) thousand shoulders (which themselves are a favour to me); mudigaḷ āyirattāy – having thousand divine heads (as said in “sahasra śīrśā“); tuṇai malark kaṇgaḷ āyirattāy – (as said in “sahasrākśa:“) having thousand eyes which appear like matching flowers; tāḷgaḷ āyirattāy – (as said in “sahasrapād“) having thousand divine feet; pērgaḷ āyirattāy – (as said in “nāma sahasravān“) having thousand divine names; tamiyanēn – for me (who started doubting even my own intelligence and became lonely); periya appanē – Oh lord who favoured matching your greatness!

**Перевод:**

**Showing great love as if embracing the shoulders of my own self, to have full satisfaction , I unconditionally offered it \[soul\] as a gratitude for emperumān who greatly favoured me by granting his divine feet to exist exclusively for me, to have me shine more and more; oh one who is having radiance! You are having thousand shoulders! You are having thousand divine heads! You are having thousand eyes which appear like matching flowers! You are having thousand divine feet! You are having thousand divine names! Oh lord who favoured matching your greatness for me! Implies “Oh one who is having such radiance and greatness! You have become greatly benevolent towards me”.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the tenth pāsuram, āḻvār says “As you have greatly favoured me by granting your divine feet, in fulfilling my desire, I am offering myself to you as gratitude”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār mercifully explains the radiance and greatness acquired by emperumān on seeing āḻvār’s gratitude for emperumān’s favour matching āḻvār’s desire.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. Granting his divine feet implies emperumān making āḻvār realise his incompatibility with samsāram and inability to cope in emperumān’s separation tāḷgaḷai enakkē talait talaic ciṟappat tanda pērudavik kammāṟā tōḷgaḷai ārat taḻuvi en uyirai aṟavilai seydanan sōdī! tōḷgaḷ āyirattāy! mudigaḷ āyirattāy! tuṇai malark kaṇgaḷ āyirattāy! tāḷgaḷ āyirattāy! pērgaḷ āyirattāy! tamiyanēn periya appanē!*

- *tāḷgaḷai enakkē talait talaic ciṟappat tanda* – As said in [tiruvāimoḻi 7.10.5](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/11/thiruvaimozhi-7-10-5-malaradip-podhugal/) “*palar adiyār munbaruḷiya*” (granting his grace in the presence of many servitors) – even as śrī vālmeeki bhagavān, mudalāḻvārgaḷ et al are present, you granted your special grace upon me to have me shine greatly; saying “fully granting your grace”.
- *pēr udavi* – Not granting according to the level of me who is accepting, but granting according to your level \[of greatness\].
- *kaimmāṟā* – as pratyupakāram (return of favour).
- *tōḷgaḷai ārat taḻuvi* – As one would embrace his daughter and present her to the groom, here too, the formless ātmā acquired feet, shoulders etc out of gratefulness, so that [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) can embrace it and offer it. Due to the delight, āḻvār forgot about his own words such as in [tiruvāimoḻi 2.3.4](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/02/thiruvaimozhi-2-3-4-enadhu-aviyul/) “*enadāvi yār? yān Ar?*” (neither the actions of the ātmā nor the doerśip of the ātmā that is submitting are under my control) and in [tiruvāimoḻi 8.1.8](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/02/thiruvaimozhi-8-1-8-manandha-peraya/) “*manamum vāsagamum seygaiyum yānum nīdānē*” (my mind, speech, body and self are all your attributes).
- *en uyirai aṟavilai seyydanan* – I unconditionally gave myself to your highness to exclusively exist for you.
- *sōdī* – As [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) submitted in bewilderment something which does not belong to him as his own belonging, he too, accepted it in bewilderment as if he received something which does not already belong too him, and became radiant; he remained as said in samkśēpa rāmāyaṇam 85 “… *vijvara: …*” (having his fever removed, śrī rāma is happy).
- *tōḷgaḷ …* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is praising [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) after seeing his completeness which is acquired by him on seeing āḻvār who previously called out for him due to the loss, but now engaging with him out of gratitude. Just as āḻvār’s self grew feet and shoulders due to thinking about his favours, emperumān’s sadēka rūpa (immutable form) became śata śākam (with thousands of limbs). Is it believable that sarvēśvaran who is avāpta samasta kāman (one who has no unfulfilled desires) will become blissful like this on attaining a samsāri (āḻvār who was engaged previously in worldly activities)? Though one may be an emperor who rules over the world and may have nothing new to be attained, when it comes to his consort, will he not have desires? As avāpta samasta kāmatvam (being with no unfulfilled desires) is found in authentic scriptures, so is his āśrita vātsalyam (motherly care towards his devotees), and hence can both not be accepted as they are? āḻvār praises emperumān saying “Giving joy to me and seeing that joy, he is becoming blissful!”
- *tamiyanēn* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is thinking about his loneliness in doubting [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s svarūpam \[7th pāsuram\] and āśrita pāratantriyam \[4th pāsuram\].
- *periya appanē* – Your favour is not limited! You did not show your mercy due to any noble quality that is present in me, but due to the prāpti (natural connection/responsibility).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.1.11. Periya appanai

*periya appanaip piraman appanai uruttiran appanai munivarkku uriya appanai amarar appanai ulagukkōr tani appan tannai periya vaṇ kurugūr vaṇ satakōpan pēṇina āyirattuḷḷum uriya sol mālai ivaiyum pattu ivaṟṟāl uyyalām toṇḍīr! nangatkē*

**Пословный перевод:**

periya appanai – being the lord of all; piraman – for brahmā (who is the creator of all \[within a particular universe\]); appanai – being the creator; uruttiran – for rudra (who is the annihilator); appanai – being the creator; munivarkku – for sages (such as sanaka et al who are very wise); uriya appanai – being the distinguished lord; amarar – for (the remaining) dēvas (celestial beings); appanai – being the creator; ulagukku – for all worlds; ōr – unique; tani appan tannai – being the primary lord; periya – huge; vaṇ – having wealth; kurugūr – being the leader of āḻvārtirunagari; vaṇ – great benefactor (due to composing this prabandam); satakōpan – nammāḻvār; pēṇina – spoke with great desire; āyirattuḷḷum – among the thousand pāsurams; uriya – apt; sol mālai – having garland of words; ivai pattum – this decad; ivaṟṟāl – by these; toṇḍīr – oh those who are addicted (to worldly pleasures); nangatku – for us (who have focussed elsewhere since time immemorial); uyyalām – shall be uplifted

**Перевод:**

**emperumān is the lord of all, the creator of brahmā, creator of rudra, the distinguished lord of the sages, creator of the dēvas, and is the unique, primary lord for all words; the great benefactor nammāḻvār who is the leader of āḻvārtirunagari which is having huge wealth, very desirously spoke about such emperumān in this apt decad having garland of words, among thousand pāsurams; oh those who are addicted to worldly desires, we shall be uplifted with this decad.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the end pāsuram, āḻvār summarizes what was explained in this decad and says “those who learn this decad will attain emperumān and be uplifted”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār explains “this decad will uplift the self” as the result.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. periya appanaip piraman appanai uruttiran appanai munivarkku uriya appanai amarar appanai ulagukkōr tani appan tannai periya vaṇ kurugūr vaṇ satakōpan pēṇina āyirattuḷḷum uriya sol mālai ivaiyum pattu ivaṟṟāl uyyalām toṇḍīr! nangatkē*

- *periya appanai* – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is with nitya vibhūti (spiritual realm) and leelā vibhūti (material realm).
- *piraman appanai* – Creator of brahmā, lord of the fourteen layered universe.
- *uruttiran appanai* – The lord of such brahmā’s son, rudra.
- *munivarkku uriya appanai* – As sages starting with sanaka et al are fully in brahma bhāvanai (focussed on bhagavān), uriya indicates emperumān’s closeness to them.
- *amarar appanai* – Creator of dēvas.
- *ulagukku ōr tani appan tannai* – What is the need to individually highlight his lordship over everyone? He is the singular lord of the whole cosmos. It is said in [śrīviṣṇu sahasranāmam](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/10/srivishnu-sahasranamam-preface-part-5/) “*bhūtānām yō’vyaya:pitā*” (the imperishable lord of all creatures). So, why is [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) individually identifying his lordship? As someone who found treasure will say “I found this, I found that” and so on, āḻvār who had unnecessary doubt in [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s intrinsic nature \[7th pāsuram\] and qualities \[4th pāsuram\], felt totally lost and having found them again, he is joyfully revealing [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s greatness \[intrinsic nature\] individually. “*munivarkkuriya appanai*” indicates emperumān’s subservience towards his devotees \[quality\].
- *periya vaṇ kurugūr* – The reason for unnecessarily doubting when emperumān the protector delays and feeling blissful out of gratitude \[when he manifests himself\] is due to having been born in this divyadēśam.
- *vaṇ satakōpan* – His generosity of composing this as a prabandam \[tiruvāimoḻi\], instead of just enjoying it in his own heart.
- *pēṇina āyirattuḷḷum uriya sol mālai ivayiyum pattu* – The decad where [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) explained how he desired for [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/).
- *uriya sol mālai* – These pāsurams are aptly explaining bhagavān’s qualities unlike vēdam which retracted as in taittirīya upaniśat “*yatō vācō nivartantē*” (the speech returned).
- *ivaṟṟāl uyyalām toṇḍīr nangatkē* – For us who were facing away from [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) since time immemorial, being engaged in worldly pleasures, and remained as said in taittirīya upaniśat “*asannēva*” (he does not exist), there is hope for redemption as said in taittirīya upaniśat “*santamēnam*” (to exist).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.2 Nangal varivalai

## 8.2.1. Nangal varivalai

*nangaḷ varivaḷai āyangāḷō! nammudai ēdalar munbu nāṇi nungatku yānonṟuraikkum māṟṟam nōkkuginṟēn engum kāṇa māttēn sangam sarindana sāyiḻandēn tada mulai pon niṟamāyt taḷarndēn vengaṇ paṟavaiyin pāgan engōn vēngadavāṇanai vēṇḍic cenṟē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vari – having stripes; vaḷai – having bangles; nangaḷ – our; āyangāḷō – oh friends!; ēdalar – others (mothers who advice and try to withdraw me and hence are inimical); munbu – in front of; nāṇi – feeling shy (to speak); nungatku – for you (who are close to me); yān uraikkum – what I can say; onṟu – one; māṟṟam – word; nōkkuginṟēn – I am trying to see; engum – in all ways; kāṇa māttēn – I am not seeing; vem – cruel (to destroy the enemies of devotees); kaṇ – having sight; paṟavaiyin – riding periya tiruvadi (garudāḻvān); pāgan – controller; em – one who enslaved me; kōn – being the lord; vēngadam – in tirumalai; vāṇanai – one who has arrived and stood in an easily approachable manner; vēṇḍi – desired (in these forms); senṟu – went; sangam – (my) bangles made of conch; sarindana – slipping \[from my hands\]; sāy – (natural) bodily glow; iḻandēn – I lost; tadam – huge; mulai – bosom; pon niṟamāy – attaining golden complexion (due to the disease of separation); taḷarndēn – became weak-bodied

**Перевод:**

**Oh friends who are wearing bangles with stripes! I am trying to see if there is any word which I can tell you, which I cannot speak in front of others feeling shy; but I am not seeing any such word in all ways; emperumān who is the controller of periya tiruvadi having cruel sight and riding him, who enslaved me by being my lord, who has arrived in tirumalai and stood there in an easily approachable manner; I desired him, and my bangles made of conch, slipped from my hands; I lost my bodily glow; my huge bosom attained golden complexion and I became weak-bodied. Implies that emperumān rides the faultless pramāṇam \[garudāḻvān who represents vēdam\], has natural relationship and very easily approachable nature.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the first pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki desired for emperumān and she could not have her desire fulfilled even after going to divyadēśams; as she remained with sorrow, her friends told her “Should you not feel shy only in front of unfavourable ones? Should you feel shy in front of us? Tell us what you are going through” and she says “I am not able to find those words which I want to share with you, which I cannot tell others due to feeling shy”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, parānguśa nāyaki informs her friends “I desired for tiruvēndamudaiyān who is easily approachable by all, but only ended up losing my beautiful ornaments and my physical beauty”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. nangaḷ varivaḷai āyangāḷō! nammudai ēdalar munbu nāṇi nungatku yānonṟuraikkum māṟṟam nōkkuginṟēn engum kāṇa māttēn sangam sarindana sāyiḻandēn tada mulai pon niṟamāyt taḷarndēn vengaṇ paṟavaiyin pāgan engōn vēngadavāṇanai vēṇḍic cenṟē*

- *nangaḷ varivaḷai* – Previously, all of you and I had the same bangles. You who said as in śrī rāmāyaṇam kiśkintā kāṇḍam 5.18 “*ēkam du:kham sukham ca nau*“ (sharing sorrow and joy), are now changing your stance when it comes to practice! When asked “What is the change when it comes to practice?” [parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says “Have you not seen our hands? I have no bangles on my hands. You have bangles on your hands”.
- *vari vaḷai* – Striped bangles or attractive bangles. To sustain her, they sustain themselves in spite of their sorrow. Though iḷaiya perumāḷ (lakśmaṇa) had double the sorrow when sītāp pirātti separated from perumāḷ (śrī rāma) thinking that it was due to his own lethargy in guarding her, he would sustain himself thinking that perumāḷ will feel more sorrow seeing his sorrow. Similarly, they kept their bangles in tact.
- *āyangāḷō* – Though the friends and mothers should have different attitude, now everyone is together in trying to stop [parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) \[hence, she is calling them all together\].
- *āyangāḷ* – Oh friends!
- *O* – Highlights her great sorrow. After calling them, she becomes filled with sorrow even before starting to speak to them.

Her friends say “You need not express the reason of this sorrow to others, but should you not tell us? Please tell us your state”, [parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says

- *nammudai …* – Though the friends are starting to give advice \[which is done by mothers\] and are trying to withdraw her \[from him\], as they will be together with her while getting the result, she is saying “*nammudai ēdalar*” (our enemies). ēdalar – enemies. She does not have any enemies; her mothers who advice her and bring her back, are her enemies.
- *ēdalar munbu nāṇi* – Feeling shy in front of the enemies.
- *nungatku* – for all of you, my friends.
- *yān …* – I analysed if there is something I could share with you.
- *engum kāṇa māttēn* – When I tried to find some words to express my feelings, I am unable to do that.

When asked “Why are you fully rejecting everyone? Why can’t you hide it from most of your friends and express it to just a few of them?”, [parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says

- *sangam sarindana* – From whom shall I hide this and to whom shall I reveal this? It appears as said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam “*jagadasmitam*” (the world is ending). When she is not attained, the nāyakan ([emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), lord) ceases to exist; when the lord is not  there, both spiritual realm and material realm will cease to exist. That is – when she is not with the bangles on her hands, emperumān will not exist; both the realms which exist in the presence of the divine couple, will also cease to exist.
- *sāy iḻandēn* – I lost my beauty which was acquired by uniting with him and which is the reason for my sustenance until he arrives.
- *tada mulai …* – The reason for his sustenance \[my bosom which are there for his enjoyment\] is also lost and hence there is no use of his arrival too.
- *tada mulai* – My huge bosom which give unending pleasure to [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/).
- *pon niṟamāy* – became pale. Like a beautiful palace going to ruins.
- *taḷarndēn* – I have become so weak that even if I regained the lost features, there is no ability to support them.
- *vengaṇ paṟavaiyin pāgan em kōn …* – She is highlighting the reason for her loss.
- *vengaṇ paṟavai* – periya tiruvadi who is having cruel eyes. Saying “where he arrives, he will remove the obstacles there as well”. Also saying “one who would take emperumān away while he is united with her”; śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 5.18.30 “*akrūra: krūra hrudaya:*” (cruel-hearted akrūra).
- *paṟavaiyin pāgan em kōn* – He enslaved me fully, by manifesting his presence on periya tiruvadi.
- *vēngada vāṇanai* – I did not desire for his form in paramapadam; I desired for his form, where he arrived to give audience to us.
- *vēṇḍic cenṟē* – Going with desire to him who arrived here with desire towards us; saying “we went there with desire”. Instead of waiting for his arrival, we went to his abode and still did not have our desire fulfilled, hence the bangles slipped.
- *senṟu* – \[Alternative explanation\] Gone there and totally remained there \[without returning\].

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.2.2. Vendic cenru

*vēṇḍic cenṟu onṟu peṟugiṟpāril ennudait tōḻiyar nungatkēlum īṇḍiduraikkum padiyai andō! kāṇginṟilēn idarāttiyēn nān kāṇḍhagu tāmaraik kaṇṇān kaḷvan viṇṇavar kōn nangaḷ kōnaik kaṇḍāl īṇḍiya sangum niṟaivum koḷvān ettanai kālam iḷaikkinṟēnē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

senṟu – going (towards him); onṟu – something; vēṇḍi – prayed; peṟugiṟpāril – those who want to get; ennudai – those who are greater than I; tōḻiyar – friends; nungatkēlum – for you too; īṇḍu – here; idu – the reason for this exhausted state; idarāttiyēn – filled with sorrow; nān – I; uraikkum padiyai – way to tell; andō – alas!; kāṇginṟilēn – I am not seeing; kāṇ – to see (always); tagu – fitting; tāmarai – like a lotus (having expansive form, freshness, coolness, fragrance); kaṇṇan – having eyes; kaḷvan – being mischievous (who captured me fully by showing his obedience through his glance); viṇṇavar – all of the nityasūris (eternal residents of paramapadam); kōn – one who torments; nangaḷ – me too; kōnai – one who engaged; kaṇḍāl – while seeing; īṇḍiya – (from me) went there; sangum – my striped bangles; niṟaivum – my complete femininity; koḷvān – to retrieve; ettanai – how long; kālam – time; iḷaikkinṟēn – becoming weak and anguishing

**Перевод:**

**Alas! I am filled with sorrow here and am not seeing the way to tell the reason for my exhausted state to you too who are my friends who are greater than I am in going to emperumān and praying to get \[what you need\]; he is having lotus like eyes which are fit to be seen, is mischievous, torments all of the nityasūris and who engaged me too; I am becoming weak and anguished thinking about “how long will it take to retrieve my striped bangles and complete femininity which went to him?” when I see him.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the second pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki‘s friends ask her “Is your suffering not to be shared even with us who are very close to you?” and she responds “I don’t know how to tell you due to my excessive sorrow”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, parānguśa nāyaki says “How long have I been suffering to get back the bangles etc which were taken away by him who is having enjoyable form? I don’t know how to tell this even to you”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. vēṇḍic cenṟu onṟu peṟugiṟpāril ennudait tōḻiyar nungatkēlum īṇḍiduraikkum padiyai andō! kāṇginṟilēn idarāttiyēn nān kāṇḍhagu tāmaraik kaṇṇān kaḷvan viṇṇavar kōn nangaḷ kōnaik kaṇḍāl īṇḍiya sangum niṟaivum koḷvān ettanai kālam iḷaikkinṟēnē!*

- *vēṇḍic cenṟu onṟu peṟugiṟpāril …* – Even to you, my friends who are primary among those who pray and receive from me.
- *ennudait tōḻiyar* – best friends. senṟu indicates vandu (arriving at my location).

Alternatively, splitting the word \[as “*perugiṟpār il*“\]

- *vēṇḍic cenṟu onṟu peṟugiṟpāril –* There is no one who went and got anything by praying to [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/); māngalya stavam “*sakala pala pradōhi viṣṇu:*” (īsn’t viṣṇu the one who grants all wishes), a tamiḻ scholar said “That ‘he will give everything’ is only for words sake \[and not truth\]”
- *īṇḍu* – Now. Though I have shared with you previously, now I am not seeing what to tell you.
- *idu* – Though I am able to speak about everything else, I am unable to speak about “this” (sorrow).
- *uraikkum padiyai* – It is spread in the heart like how poison spreads everywhere; yet I am unable to express it in words.
- *andō kāṇginṟilēn* – More than you, I desire to share my emotions to you to relieve myself, yet, I am unable to find the words. uttara rāmāyaṇam “*pralābhairēva dāryatē*” (sustaining by sharing the grief).
- *idarāttiyēn nān* – I who am suffering. Neither for my sorrow nor for you who insist “tell us, tell us”, \[for\] I who am suffering.
- *kāṇ tagu tāmaraik kaṇṇan* – One who has the eyes which are fit to be seen. The eyes which are fit to be seen always; due to its \[lotus’\] expansive nature, freshness, coolness and fragrance, they are comparable to a lotus.
- *kaḷvan* – Manifesting his unbearability \[without me\], he who captured myself and my belongings.
- *viṇṇavar kōn nangaḷ kōnai* – One who enslaved me similar to nityasūris.  He tormented me the way he tormented the whole spiritual realm.
- *kaṇḍāl* – If we get to see him.
- *īṇḍiya sangum* – The well-rounded bangles. Among thousand conces, one valamburi (curled towards right side) conch will reach there \[[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s hand\]. periya tirumoḻi “*valamburi āḻiyan vēngada vēdiyan*” (śrī vēnkatēśa, who is present in tiruvēngadam, who is known from vēdams and who has conch curled towards right).
- *niṟaivum* – obedience too.
- *koḷvān* – To have. parānguśa nāyaki thinks emperumān is the refuge for anything which does not stay with her. Her wealth is in him only.

When asked “Is this how brave you are? Would you not give up and retract yourself after a while?” she says

- *ettanai kālam iḷaikkinṟēnē* – Will I be convinced by your words? How long can I remain with this desire and become weak?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.2.3. Kalam ilaikkil

*kālam iḷaikkil allāl vinaiyēn nān iḷaikkinṟilan kaṇḍu koṇmin jñālam aṟiyap paḻi sumandēn nannudaleer! ini nāṇittānen? neela malar nedunjōdi sūḻnda nīṇḍa mugil vaṇṇan kaṇṇan koṇḍa kōla vaḷaiyodu māmai koḷvān ettanai kālamum kūdac cenṟē*

**Пословный перевод:**

neelam – bluish; malar – well blossomed; nedum – endless; sōdi – by radiance; sūḻnda – surrounded; nīṇḍa mugil – like a huge cloud; vaṇṇan – having complexion; kaṇṇan – kriṣṇa; koṇḍa – captured and kept; kōlam – attractive; vaḷaiyodu – with the bangles; māmai – my complexion; ettanai kālamum – forever; kūdac cenṟē – even going with; koḷvān – to get them \[back\]; jñālam – world; aṟiya – to know; paḻi – blame (of setting out to go on her own boldly); sumandēn – acquired; nal – beautiful; nudaleer – oh friends who are having forehead!; ini – now; nāṇittān – feeling shy; en – what benefit is there?; kālam iḷaikkil allāl – time will become weak and perish; vinaiyēn – having sin (of pursuing him even after his being difficult to attain); nān – I; iḷaikkinṟinlan – will not give up becoming weak; kaṇḍu koṇmin – see this for yourself!

**Перевод:**

**kriṣṇa who is surrounded by a bluish, well blossomed, endless radiance and having complexion of a huge cloud, captured my attractive bangles and complexion; I acquired the blame by going with him forever to get them back, to be known by the world; oh friends who are having beautiful forehead! What benefit is there in feeling shy now? I who am having sin, will not give up becoming weak, even time becomes weak and perishes; see this for yourself!**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the third pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki‘s friends say “Though you would not withdraw from the pursuit of emperumān as per our advice, would you give up over time, becoming weak?” she says “even the eternal time may end, but I will not give up until I see him”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, parānguśa nāyaki says “While trying to reach the most beautiful emperumān and retrieve my bangles etc from him, even if you stop me saying ‘he is difficult to attain’ I will not give up even if the eternal time comes to an end”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Third pāsuram. parānguśa nāyaki‘s friends say “we are not saying that engagement in bhagavat viśayam is inferior; though you would not withdraw from the pursuit of emperumān as per our advice, you would give up over time, since he is difficult to attain; in that case, why not give up based on our advice?” she says “even the eternal time may end, but I will not give up until I see him”. kālam iḷaikkil allāl vinaiyēn nān iḷaikkinṟilan kaṇḍu koṇmin jñālam aṟiyap paḻi sumandēn nannudaleer! ini nāṇittānen? neela malar nedunjōdi sūḻnda nīṇḍa mugil vaṇṇan kaṇṇan koṇḍa kōla vaḷaiyodu māmai koḷvān ettanai kālamum kūdac cenṟē*

- *kālam* – Unless time which is said as in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 1.2.28 “*anādir bhagavān kālōnāntōsya*” (This time is huge and endless) ends, I will not become weak and give up.
- *nān iḷaikkinṟilan* – Will I, who consumed with great desire, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), who is beyond time as said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam “*na kāla: tatravai prabhu:*“ (Time is not the controller in paramapadam), give up?
- *vinaiyēn* – parānguśa nāyaki is saying “I who am having sin to pursue emperumān who is said to be difficult to attain”; or she is saying “I who am having sin which makes me remain deaf to your words”.

When told “Though you are saying like this, you are continuing to pursue him”, she says

- *kaṇḍu koṇmin* – Should we hear from others what is perceivable by us?

When told “as you have boldly set out to do this, the whole world is blaming you”, she says

- *jñālam aṟiyap paḻi sumanden* – Am I being blamed only today? Was I not blamed back when I said in [tiruvāimoḻi 5.3.10](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/06/thiruvaimozhi-5-3-10-yamadalurndhum/) “*nādum iraikkavē*” (the whole world is angrily shouting)?

When asked “Is this how you speak? Should you not care for your shyness which is an important aspect of femininity?” she says

- *nannudaleer ini nāṇittān en* – Should we not care for the beauty only until it is present? As this has become well known in the world, what is the benefit of feeling shy now?
- *nannudaleer* – nudal – forehead. As you have your facial beauty, have you not seen that I have lost mine! Should you not speak after observing this difference? Let it be;

Now, she is saying that his beauty will not let us act as we please.

- *neela malar …* – Having bluish complexion.
- *malar* – well blossomed
- *nedu* – huge, endless.
- *sōdi sūḻnda …* – To get back the attractive bangles and complexion which mesmerizes him who is surrounded by radiance, having the complexion of a huge dark cloud, making it available for others, I went along forever and was blamed by the world. Oh friends with beautiful forehead! What is the benefit in feeling shy anymore?
- *ettanai kālamum kūdac cenṟu* – Having pursued him for too long, to unite with him.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.2.4. Kudac cenren

*kūdac cenṟēn ini en kodukkēn? kōl vaḷai nenjat todakkam ellām pādaṟṟoḻiya iḻandu vaigal pal vaḷaiyār mun parisaḻindēn mādak kodi madiḷ ten kuḷandai vaṇ kudapāl ninṟa māyak kūttan ādal paṟavai uyartta vel pōr āḻi valavanai ādarittē*

**Пословный перевод:**

mādam – mansions; kodi – having flags; madiḷ – having fort; then – beautiful; kuḷandai – in tirukkuḷandai; vaṇ – beautiful; kudapāl – in the western side; ninṟa – standing; māyak kūttan – having amazing activities; ādal – having beautiful movements (due to joy); paṟavai – periya tiruvadi (garudāḻvār); uyartta – being atop; vel – being victorious; pōr – having battles; āḻi – tiruvāḻi (sudarśana chakra); valavanai – having in his right hand; ādarittu – with desire; kūda – to unite; kōl – beautiful; vaḷai – bangles; nenjam – heart; todakkam ellām – etc; pādu – in me; aṟṟu – without being subservient; oḻiya – to leave; iḻandu – lost; pal – many; vaḷaiyār – girls having bangles; mun – in front of; vaigal – for long time; parisu – my nature; aḻindēn – lost; ini – now; en – what; kodukkēn – shall I give?

**Перевод:**

**emperumān who is having amazing activities is standing in the beautiful tirukkuḷandai in the beautiful western side having mansions and forts with flags; he is atop periya truvadi who is having beautiful movements; in his right hand, he is having the divine chakra which has been victorious in battles; with the desire to unite with him, I lost my ancient nature in front of the girls with bangles as my beautiful bangles, heart left me without being subservient; what shall I give now? āḻi valavan is also said as āḻi vallavan (one who is an expert in using the chakra); nenjat todakkam is also recited as nenjat tuḷakkam indicating the loss of relationship with the heart.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fourth pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki‘s friends say “While you are bold, you will lose everything” and as she could not have her desire to unite with him fulfilled, she says “What is there to lose? I have lost everything already”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, parānguśa nāyaki says “Desiring to reach emperumān who has the completeness in weapons for the elimination of hurdles of his devotees, I have lost everything; now what can I give him!”*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. kūdac cenṟēn ini en kodukkēn? kōl vaḷai nenjat todakkam ellām pādaṟṟoḻiya iḻandu vaigal pal vaḷaiyār mun parisaḻindēn mādak kodi madiḷ then kuḷandai vaṇ kudapāl ninṟa māyak kūttan ādal paṟavai uyartta vel pōr āḻi valavanai ādarittē*

- *kūdac cenṟēn* – [parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying “I have given up my body here and reached him in paramapadam and only he exists now” or saying “I have reached there desiring for union with him”.
- *ini en kodukkēn* – After losing everything already, what is there to lose now?
- *kōl vaḷai …* – Beautiful bangles, heart etc left me without a trace and  I have lost them all; Just as his wealth, her belongings are also quite vast.
- *vaigal pal vaḷaiyār mun parisaḻindēn* – In front of those who have not lost the separable ornaments, I lost my inseparable ornament which is my shyness.
- *mādak kodi madiḷ then kuḷandai* – In the beautiful [tirukkuḷandai](http://thirukkulanthai.koyil.org/) which has mansions and forts with flags.
- *vaṇ kudapāl ninṟa* – Standing in the beautiful western side. It appears that standing in the western side also is a reason for his supremacy \[arumpadam – Just as riding garuda, having divine chakra are indications of his supremacy, being in tirukkuḷandai itself is another indication of his supremacy\].
- *māyak kūttan* – One who has amazing activities.
- *ādal paṟavai uyartta* – Being seated on periya tiruvadi who is dancing joyfully due to being the vehicle of sarvēśvara.
- *vel pōr āḻi valavanai* – Desiring for sarvēśvaran who is having in his right hand, the divine sudarśana chakra which wins every battle it enters.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.2.5. Ali valavanai

*āḻi valavanai ādarippum āngavan nammil varavum ellām tōḻiyargāḷ! nammudaiyamē tān? solluvadō ingariyadu tān ūḻi tōṟūḻi oruvanāga nanguṇarvārkkum uṇaralāgā sūḻaludaiya sudarkoḷādit tollaiyanjōdi ninaikkungālē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ninaikkungāl – while seeing (with analysis); nangu – well; uṇarvārkkum – those who can understand truly; ūḻi tōṟūḻi – forever; oruvanāga – as someone with a particular nature; uṇaralāgā – not to perceive and know; sūḻal – mischievous activities (which capture his devotees); udaiya – having; sudar – radiance (of not being affected by the transformation in cit (sentient beings) and acit (insentient objects), being the material cause without impacting the true nature, and being the efficient cause); koḷ – having; ādi – being the cause; tollai – eternally distinguished; am – divine; sōdi – having radiant form; āḻi valavanai – sarvēśvara who has tiruvāḻi (divine chakra) in his hand; ādarippum – surrendering with intent; āngu – in that state of surrender; avan – he (who has supremacy and simplicity); nammil – towards us (who are surrendered unto him); varavum – arrival (and fulfilling our desires); ellām – these; nammudaiyamē tān – happening according to our abilities?; tōḻiyargāḷ – Oh friends (who know the value of this like I do)!; solluvadō – speaking about the difficulty to attain him which is his another aspect; ingu – here; ariyadu tān – is it difficult?

**Перевод:**

**sarvēśvara is having mischievous activities to be not perceived and known by those who can well understand him truly even if seen forever; he is having radiance; he is being the cause; he is having eternally distinguished form; he is having divine chakra in his hand; are these such as surrendering with intent unto him and his arrival towards us happening according to our abilities? Oh friends! Is it difficult to speak about the difficulty to attain him which is his another aspect, here?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fifth pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki‘s friends say “You are trying to reach the inconceivable, unreachable emperumān and feeling anguished” and she says “Irrespective of how distinguished and inconceivable he is, is this norm of approaching him and to be accepted by him, established by me? īsn’t it ancient norm?”*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. āḻi valavanai ādarippum āngavan nammil varavum ellām tōḻiyargāḷ! nammudaiyamē tān? solluvadō ingariyadu tān ūḻi tōṟūḻi oruvanāga nanguṇarvārkkum uṇaralāgā sūḻaludaiya sudarkoḷādit tollaiyanjōdi ninaikkungālē*

- *āḻi valavanai ādarippum* – Surrendering unto emperumān who has the divine chakra in his right hand.
- *āngu* – at that time.
- *avan* – One who has both supremacy and simplicity.
- *nammil varavum ellām* – These acts such as arriving where we are and accepting us.
- *tōḻiyargāḷ* – Have you also not immersed in these aspects like I have done?
- *nammudaiyamē tān* – Is it as per our ability? Is this norm of surrendering unto him and his fulfilling the desires \[of those who surrendered\], a new one established after creating us?
- *solluvadō ingu ariyadu tān* – While the actual meaning may be different, it is difficult to speak as you understand it! Should you speak whatever you like since there is no one to stop you?

When the friends ask “Is he not difficult to attain?” she says “don’t you like to hear from me about that?”

- *ūḻi …* – Even when tried to understand by the group of most intelligent persons forever, he will not be understandable. Highlighting that, emperumān is with such quality.
- *sūḻal udaiya* – One who has the tactics to capture those who surrender unto him.
- *sudarkoḷ* – Having countless auspicious qualities starting with tējas (radiance).
- *ādi* – the one who is the cause of the whole world.
- *tollai am sōdi* – Having natural, perfectly radiant, totally distinguished, divine form which is different from other forms.
- *ninaikkungāl* – If we set out to analyse his greatness. If the distinguished emperumān becomes easy to approach, can I pursue him or give him up?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.2.6. Tollai anjodi

*tollai anjōdi ninaikkungāl en sol aḷavanṟimaiyōr tamakkum ellai ilādana kūḻppuc ceyyum attiṟam niṟka emmāmai koṇḍān alli malart taṇ tuḻāyum tārān ārkkidugō inip pūsal? solleer valli vaḷa vayal sūḻ kudandai mā malark kaṇ vaḷarginṟa mālē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ninaikkungāl – if we try to analyse; tollai – distinguished; am – unlimited; sōdi – his radiance; en – my; sol aḷavu – within my speech; imaiyōr tamakkum – for (greatly knowledgeable) brahmā et al; ellai ilādana – endless; kūḻppu – doubt; seyyum – cause; a – that; tiṟam – greatness; niṟka – be; valli – flower bearing creeper; vaḷam – beautiful; vayal – fields; sūḻ – surrounded; kudandai – in tirukkudandai; mā – great; malar – lotus like; kaṇ – divine eyes; vaḷarginṟa – mercifully resting; māl – having great affection towards devotees; em – my; māmai – complexion; koṇḍān – captured; alli – flower garland’s; malar – blossom; taṇ tuḻāyum – tuḷasi garland too; tārān – not giving; ini – now (after being tormented by him); ārkku – for whom; pūsalidugō – will call out; solleer – Please tell!

**Перевод:**

**If we try to analyse his unlimited, distinguished radiance, it is not within my speech; his greatness causes endless doubt in brahmā et al; emperumān who is mercifully resting in tirukkudandai which is surrounded by flower bearing creepers and beautiful fields, who is having great affection towards his devotees, captured my complexion; he is not giving his tuḷasi garland which resembles a blossomed flower garland; now, oh friends! Please tell! For whom will I call out?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the sixth pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki‘s say “he is not easily approachable as you say, but is unreachable” and she says “Whether he is difficult to attain or easy to attain, instead of calling out for emperumān who inflicted this suffering upon us, can we be upset with those who are unrelated to us?”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. tollai anjōdi ninaikkungāl en sol aḷavanṟimaiyōr tamakkum ellai ilādana kūḻppuc ceyyum attiṟam niṟka emmāmai koṇḍān alli malart taṇ tuḻāyum tārān ārkkidugō inip pūsal? solleer valli vaḷa vayal sūḻ kudandai mā malark kaṇ vaḷarginṟa mālē*

- *tollai am sōdi ninaikkungāl* – If we try to analyse, \[we will understand that\] he has a distinguished form which is not seen in any other species.
- *en sol aḷavu anṟu* –  His greatness is not limited to my speech.

Is it because of my being a helpless girl that it is difficult to speak about his greatness?

- *imaiyōr …* – Even for brahmā et al who are most knowledgeable, his greatness will cause unlimited doubts. śrī viṣṇu purāṇam 1.9.55 “*yannāyam bhagavān brahmā jānāti paramam padam*I *tannatā: sma jagaddāma tava sarvagadācyuta* īī” (Oh all pervading acyuta! We bow down to that supreme dwelling place of yours which even bhagavān brahmā does not know and which is the sustaining entity for the universe), mahābhāratam mōkśa parvam “*na sa śakyas tvayā draśtum mayānyair vāpi sattama* I *sarvēśām sākśibhūtō’sau na  grāhya kēnacit kvacit* īī” (Oh child, rudra! That [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is not capable of being seen by you, me or anyone else. Even though he sees everyone, he cannot be seen by anyone at any time); alternatively, imaiyōr implies nityasūris; while they wait to worship him with the necessary paraphernalia as said in tiruviruttam 21 “*sūttu nanmālaigaḷ tūyana ēndi*” (carrying the best garlands),  he went seeking butter “*īttiya veṇṇey toduvuṇṇap pōndu*“.
- *attiṟam niṟka em māmai koṇḍān* – While he was having such greatness, he manifested his beauty etc and captured my complexion \[i.e. I became pale in his separation\]. Did he, who cannot sustain without uniting with me, not accept my complexion, due to not seeing his greatness?
- *alli malart taṇ tuḻāyum tārān* – After capturing my complexion, should he at least not give something which has had direct contact with him \[tuḷasi garland\] and uplift me? He is not doing that either. At least if he did that, I can remain satisfied thinking “I offered my complexion to get his garland”.
- *ārkkidugō inip pūsal solleer* – Instead of calling out at the gates of the one who tormented else. whose gates should we go to and call out? Please tell me!
- *valli …* – sarvēśvaran who is mercifully resting in tirukkudandai which is surrounded by gardens filled with flower bearing creepers and fertile fields.
- *mā malark kaṇ vaḷarginṟa māl* – I am not seeing the apt lord’s blossomed lotus like flower, blossoming towards me. Implying, his eyes have not given their special glance towards her. Implying that [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is present to hear our cries.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.2.7. Mal ari kesavan

*māl ari kēsavan nāraṇan sīmādavan gōvindan vaigundan enṟenṟu ōlamida ennaip paṇṇi vittittu onṟum uruvum suvadum kāttān ēla malark kuḻal annaimīrgāḷ! ennudait tōḻiyargāḷ! en seygēn? kalam pala senṟum kāṇbadāṇai ungaḷōdu engaḷ idaiyillaiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

māl – one who is affectionate towards his devotees; ari – having the nature of taking their sins away; kēsavan – having beautiful locks; nāraṇan – having natural relationship (which is the foundation for the previously explained qualities); sīmādavan – the lord of śrī mahālakśmi (who nurtures such qualities); gōvindan – being obedient towards his devotees; vaigundan – one who has the perfect abode to grant (to those who surrendered unto him seeing his obedience); enṟu enṟu – repeatedly saying these aspects; ōlam ida – to call out in great sorrow; ennai – me; paṇṇi – doing; vittu – pushing aside; ittu – leaving; onṟum – in any way; uruvum – his form; suvadum – any trace of reaching him; kāttān – not showing; Elam – having invigorating fragrance like cardamom; malar – having flower; kuḻal – having locks; annaimīrgāḷ – oh mothers!; ennudai – my distinguished; tōḻiyargāḷ – oh friends!; en seygēn – he said “what can I do?”; pala kālum – forever; senṟum – even if it goes on; āṇai – vow; kāṇbadu – I will see him; ungaḷōdu – with you (who are trying to weaken my determination); engaḷ – for me; idai – any relationship; illai – not there

**Перевод:**

**emperumān has made me repeatedly say “emperumān who is affectionate towards his devotees, is having the nature of taking their sins away, is having beautiful locks, is having natural relationship, is the lord of śrī mahālakśmi, is obedient towards his devotees and has the perfect abode to grant \[to his devotees\]” and call him out in great sorrow; he pushed me aside and left me, without showing his form in any way and any trace of reaching him. Oh mothers having locks with flower which is having invigorating fragrance like cardamom! Oh my distinguished friends! He said “what can I do?” Even if it goes on forever, I will vow to see him; there is no relationship for me with you.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the seventh pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki’s relatives condemn her saying “It is difficult to see him, you should give up this thought” and she says “Even if it takes forever, I who am captivated in his beauty etc, will not give up seeing him; if you pose hurdles for that, I will sever my relationship with all of you”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. māl ari kēsavan nāraṇan sīmādavan gōvindan vaigundan enṟenṟu ōlamida ennaip paṇṇi vittittu onṟum uruvum suvadum kāttān ēla malark kuḻal annaimīrgāḷ! ennudait tōḻiyargāḷ! en seygēn? kalam pala senṟum kāṇbadāṇai ungaḷōdu engaḷ idaiyillaiyē*

- *māl* – One who is an embodiment of affection towards his devotes. His affection of favouring āḻvār to arrive up to this stage of calling out to him, starting from tiruviruttam 1 “*poyn ninṟa jñānam*“.
- *ari* –  One who is capable of eliminating the enemies.
- *kēsavan* – He has such beautiful locks that even if one enjoyed him forever, one will not feel contented.
- *nāraṇan* – One who has motherly care towards his devotees.
- *sīmādavan* – Being the lord of śrī mahālakśmi which is the  cause for such motherly care towards his devotees.
- *gōvindan* – Due to his togetherness with her, he is subservient towards his devotees.
- *vaigundan* – One who has the supremacy for all of these aforementioned qualities.
- *enṟu enṟu* – forever.
- *ōlam ida* – Calling out loudly to get his attention.
- *ennaip paṇṇi* – As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 40.5 “*sruśtastvam vanavāsāya*” (the purpose of your birth is to send you (lakśmaṇa) to the forest \[along with śrī rāma\]), making this to be my routine.
- *vittu* – separating me from him.
- *ittu* – discarding me like an insentient object.
- *onṟum uruvum suvadum kāttān* – He is neither showing his form nor the hint for his location; showing his form as said in śrī bhāgavatam 10.32.2 “… *tāsāmāvirabūt …*” (He appeared amidst the covherd girls like the cupid for cupids); when śrī bharatāḻvān went to see śrī rāma, he identified the hermitage of śrī rāma from a distance, by the smoke coming of the fire sacrifice etc. He is neither showing his form nor his location as seen in these examples.
- *ēla malark kuḻal annaimīrgāḷ* – When will I see you as you were \[favourable towards me\] before?
- *ēla malar* – Flower which has fragrance similar to that of cardamom.
- *ennudait tōḻiyargāḷ* – Your duty is not to give me advice and withdraw me from him but to speak what is pleasing to me.
- *en seygēn* – What will I do now since I don’t see any hint?

They say “you can ask us” and she says

- *kālam pal senṟum kāṇbadu* – Even if this goes on forever, I will not come back without seeing him.

They say “That is impossible” and she says

- *āṇai* – One who is going to give up will not vow. She is vowing on him.

Still they continued to advice her and hence she says

- *ungaḷōdu …* – I have no relationship with all of you and hence you need not advice me.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.2.8. Idai illai

*idai illai yān vaḷartta kiḷigāḷ! pūvaigāḷ! kuyilgāḷ! mayilgāḷ! udaiya nam māmaiyum sangum nenjum onṟum oḻiya ottādu koṇḍān adaiyum vaigundamum pāṟkadalum anjana veṟpum avai naṇiya kadaiyaṟap pāsangaḷ vitta pinnai anṟi avan avai Kāṇ kodānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

yān – I; vaḷartta – raised; kiḷigāḷ – oh parrots!; pūvaigaḷgāḷ – Oh mynahs!; kuyilgāḷ – Oh cuckoos!; mayilgāḷ – Oh peacocks!; idai – space/posture; illai – not there; nammudaiya – our; māmaiyum – complexion; sangum – bangles; nenjam – heart; onṟum – a; oḻiya – to remain; ottādu – to not fit; koṇḍān – one who captured; adaiyum – being present in the unreachable; vaigundamum – paramapadam; pāṟkadalum – tiruppāṟkadal (milk ocean); anjana veṟpum – tirumalai (tiruvēngadam); avai – those desirable, apt abodes; naṇiya – there is no shortcoming in reaching and enjoying; pāsangaḷ – worldly attachments (in other aspects); kadaiyaṟa – with the trace; vitta – leaving; pinnnai – after; anṟi – otherwise; avan – the apt lord; avai – those enjoyable abodes; kāṇ kodān – will not show us

**Перевод:**

**Oh parrots who were raised by me! Oh mynahs! Oh cuckoos! Oh peacocks! There is no space for you near me! emperumān who captured our complexion, bangles and heart to not fit with us and remain here, is present in the unreachable paramapadam, tiruppāṟkadal and tirumalai; there is no shortcoming in reaching and enjoying him in those desirable, apt abodes; if we don’t leave the worldly attachments without a trace, he, the apt lord, won’t show us those enjoyable abodes.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the eighth pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki highlights her detachment towards her playmates such as parrot, mynah etc.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, as emperumān will not be easily approachable for anyone other than those who are fully detached, parānguśa nāyaki after previously highlighting her detachment towards her relatives, is now speaking about her detachment towards her toys such as parrot, mynah etc.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. idai illai yān vaḷartta kiḷigāḷ! pūvaigāḷ! kuyilgāḷ! mayilgāḷ! udaiya nam māmaiyum sangum nenjum onṟum oḻiya ottādu koṇḍān adaiyum vaigundamum pāṟkadalum anjana veṟpum avai naṇiya kadaiyaṟap pāsangaḷ vitta pinnai anṟi avan avai Kāṇ kodānē*

- *idai illai* – You have no space with me.
- *yān vaḷartta kiḷigāḷ* – Showing your familiarity with me, you are trying to get close to me.
- *pūvaigaḷ …* – These birds etc which were desirable for her previously, will become part of his playmates as well; yet, she became detached from all of them as well.
- *udaiya …* – She is highlighting the reason for her detachment towards everything else; he captured everything from us without leaving a trace, both external aspects such as complexion, bangles and internal aspects such as heart.
- *adaiyum vaigundamum* – paramapadam which is the abode he reaches. She is saying “having captured everything from me, he is reaching the abode which is unreachable for us and is celebrating his victory there”.
- *pāṟkadalum* – tiruppāṟkadal (kśīrābdi, the milk ocean) which is \[relatively\] closer to such paramapadam.
- *anjana veṟpum* – tirumalai is also said to be comparable to paramapadam.
- *avai naṇiya* – I have attained the desirable abodes.

When asked “What stops you from enjoying it?” She responds “He is very possessive; when one has attachment towards other aspects as well, he will not grant his enjoyment”.

- *kadai* … – Unless one’s worldly attachments are completely given up without the trace, he will not manifest the enjoyable abodes. Previously she gave up *prāpaka ābhāsangaḷ* (false means) by saying “*vaṇangum āṟu aṟiyēn*“; he she is giving up *prāpya ābhāsangaḷ* (false goals).

## 8.2.9. Kan koduppan allan

*kāṇ koduppān allan ārkkum tannaik kaiseyappāladōr māyam tannāl māṇ kuṟaḷ kōla vadivu kātti maṇṇum viṇṇum niṟaiya malarnda sēṇ sudart tōḷgaḷ pala taḻaitta dēvapirāṟku en niṟaivinōdu nāṇ koduttēn ini en kodukkēn? ennudai naṇṇudal nangaimīrgāḷ*

**Пословный перевод:**

ārkkum – even for the most knowledgeable ones; tannai – him; kāṇ koduppān allan – being the one who does not manifest himself to be seen by them; māyam tannāl – by his deceit; kai sey – to create; appāladu – beyond; ōr – unique; kōlam – having beauty; māṇ – alms seeking; kuṟaḷ vadivu – assuming the vāmana (dwarf) form; kātti – and manifesting it; maṇṇum – earth; viṇṇum – higher worlds; niṟaiya – to be filled; malarnda – blossomed; sēṇ – tall; sudar – radiant; pala – many; tōḷgaḷ – shoulders; taḻaitta – branched out; dēva pirāṟku – to emperumān who is the lord of brahmā, rudra et al; ena – my; niṟaivinōdu – complete femininity and; nāṇ – shyness; koduttēn – gave; ennudai – being related to me; nal – radiant; nudal – having forehead; nangaimīrgāḷ – oh faultless ones \[mothers\]!; ini – now; en – what; kodukkēn – shall I give?

**Перевод:**

**emperumān does not manifest himself to be seen by even the most knowledgeable ones; but such emperumān, by his deceit, assumed the unique, beautiful, alms seeking vāmana form which is beyond the capacity for anyone to create, and manifested it; he then blossomed to fill the earth and the higher worlds, branched out with many tall and radiant shoulders; , I gave my complete femininity and shyness to such emperumān who is the lord of brahmā, rudra et al; oh faultless ones who are related to me and having radiant forehead! What shall I give to him now?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the ninth pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki‘s mothers say “If you are determined like this, will you not lose everything you have?” and she says “Already I have lost my femininity and shyness; what is there to lose anymore?”*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. kāṇ koduppān allan ārkkum tannaik kaiseyappāladōr māyam tannāl māṇ kuṟaḷ kōla vadivu kātti maṇṇum viṇṇum niṟaiya malarnda sēṇ sudart tōḷgaḷ pala taḻaitta dēvapirāṟku en niṟaivinōdu nāṇ koduttēn ini en kodukkēn? ennudai naṇṇudal nangaimīrgāḷ*

- *kāṇ koduppān allan ārkkum tannai* – He is of such nature that he will not show himself to those who try to see him with their own efforts, even if they are most knowledgeable.
- *kai sey …* – Showing his beautiful alms seeking dwarf form which is beyond creation. māyam tannāl – krutrima (deceit). Here the deceit is – arriving as a mendicant while he is the lord of spiritual and material realms, making himself as a seeker of alms while he is the lord of śrī mahālakśmi and showing small feet, but measuring the world with large feet.
- *kai seyappāladāna kōla vadivu* – Having a form which is having beauty beyond creation. Implying natural beauty. Alternatively, implying that it is like a beautiful art which acquired life.
- *māṇ kuṟaḷ vadivu* – Being a prideless alms seeker with a beautiful vāmana form.
- *kōla vadivu* – The form which was assumed by emperumān to minimize his greatness, is in itself so great that one would seek to ward off evil eyes.
- *kātti* – Manifesting the natural alms seeking dwarf form to mahābali to deceive him.
- *maṇṇum viṇṇum niṟaiya malarnda* – Grew out to fill all the worlds immediately after receiving the water in his hands.
- *sēṇ sudart tōḷgaḷ pala taḻaitta* – Having well grown, many shoulders which resemble well-branched kalpataru (wish fulfilling celestial tree).
- *dēva pirāṟku* – One who became the benefactor for dēvas (celestial entities) by redeeming the kingdom which was lost by indra.
- *en niṟaivinōdu nāṇ koduttēn* – I lost two kingdoms \[femininity and shyness\]. indra regained his kingdom. mahābali manifested his generosity. But I lost my obedience and shyness which are my great wealth.
- *ini en kodukkēn* – What more can I give now?
- *ennudai nannudal nangaimīrgāḷ* – Since you don’t realise my suffering, you can remain beautiful, with complete femininity and can also advice me. Previously in the fourth pāsuram she said “*ini en kodukkēn?*“; what is the difference between her statement here and there? There, she lost herself to emperumān’s presence on periya tiruvadi and his holding the divine chakra in his hand, became attached to māyakkūttan emperumān and went to unite with him, but did not get that and hence felt lost there; here she is saying that she lost herself to śrī vāmana’s beauty and simplicity and lost everything like mahābali.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.2.10. Ennudai nannudal

*ennudai nannudal nangaimīrgāḷ! yān inic ceyvaden? en nenju ennai nin idaiyēn allēn enṟu nīngi nēmiyum sangum irukaik koṇḍu pannedunjūḻ sudar jñāyiṟṟō? pāl madi ēndi ōr kōla neela nannedungunṟam varuvadoppān nāṇmalarp pādam adaindaduvē*

**Пословный перевод:**

en – obedient towards me; nenju – heart; nin – for you (who separated from emperumān); idaiyēn allēn – will not be your limb; enṟu – saying; ennai – me (who is the abode of such limbs); nīngi – leaving; nēmiyum – divine chakra; sangum – śrī pāncajanya, conch; irukai – in two divine hands; koṇḍu – holding; pal – manifold; nedum – expansive; sūḻ – surrounded; sudar – having radiance; jñāyiṟṟōdu – with the sun; pāl – having milky white colour; madi – moon; ēndi – holding on the peaks; ōr – unique; kōlam – with attractive form; neelam – having blue colour; nal – being distinguished due to having minerals etc; nedu – tall; kunṟam – mountain; varuvadu – walking; oppāna – like; nāḷ – fresh; malar – lotus like; pādam – divine feet; adaindadu – reached; ennudai – being related to me; nal nudal – by physical beauty and noble qualities; nangaimīrgāḷ – oh those who are complete!; yān – I (interested in emperumān, unlike all of you); ini – after losing my heart and having become helpless; en – what; seyvadu – shall I do?

**Перевод:**

**My heart which was obedient to me indicated that it will no longer be my limb and left me and reached the fresh lotus like divine feet of emperumān who is holding divine chakra and conch in his two hands, and walking towards me like a unique, attractive, tall, bluish, distinguished mountain with special minerals, herbs etc, having expansive sun surrounded with manifold radiance and moon having milky white colour, on its peaks. Oh those who are related to me, who are complete in having physical beauty and noble qualities! What shall I do after losing my heart and having become helpless? Implies, only those who have heart can sustain.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the tenth pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki‘s friends say “Can you behave like this? Why don’t you sustain yourself?” and she says “My heart left me and became captivated by emperumān‘s beauty. Now, I can’t do anything”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. ennudai nannudal nangaimīrgāḷ! yān inic ceyvaden? en nenju ennai nin idaiyēn allēn enṟu nīngi nēmiyum sangum irukaik koṇḍu pannedunjūḻ sudar jñāyiṟṟō? pāl madi ēndi ōr kōla neela nannedungunṟam varuvadoppān nāṇmalarp pādam adaindaduvē*

- *ennudai nannudal nangaimīrgāḷ* – You are free from sorrows since you are complete in physical beauty and femininity, though you are related to me.
- *yān* – I am suffering, having lost everything.
- *inic ceyvaden* – This being the case, what can I do! Can I redeem my belongings or control him?

When asked “Don’t you at least need to sustain yourself in all manner?” she says “Do I not need my heart for that?”

- *en nenju* – My heart which is obedient in all situations.
- *ennai* – me who sustains with its help.
- *nin idaiyēn allēn enṟu nīngi* – Leaving me saying that it is not fitting with me. As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 17.1 “*ityuktvā paruśam*” (saying harsh words in this manner), it left. It left me saying “*sanyastam mayā*” (I have given you up completely) so that I cannot redeem it highlighting our apt relationship. Just as I am treating you now, my heart treated me in the same manner and left far away from me.
- *nēmiyum …* – It reached the ocean \[of bhagavān’s divine feet\] so that I cannot follow it. [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is holding the āḻvārs (Sanka and chakra) in his hands which are on their own so attractive that one would ward off evil eyes from them. He is walking around with those Sanka and chakra āḻvārs, like a boundless mountain with sun which is having manifold radiance which permeates everywhere and moon which has milk like radiance, having cool physical form in blue colour which contrasts such bright radiance and having many untold beauty.
- *nāḷ malarp pādam adaindaduvē* – It reached like a beetle reaching a fresh flower – what can I do now?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.
