## 8.2.11. Padam adaivadan

*pādam adaivadan pāsattālē maṟṟavan pāsangaḷ muṟṟa vittuk kōdil pugaḻk kaṇṇan tan adi mēl vaṇ kurugūrc catakōpan sonna tīdil andādi ōr āyirattuḷ ivaiyum ōr pattu isaiyodum vallār ādum ōr tīdilarāgi ingum angum ellām amaivārgaḷ tāmē*

**Пословный перевод:**

pādam – divine feet; adiavadan – to reach; pāsattālē – due to the desire; maṟṟa – other matters; van – strong; pāsangaḷ – desires; muṟṟa – directly; vittu – giving up; kōdu – defect; il – without; pugaḻ – having glories; kaṇṇan than – kriṣṇa’s; adimēl – on divine feet; vaṇ – having great generosity (of documenting his pure actions); kurugūrc catakōpan – āḻvār; sonna – mercifully spoken by; tīdu – defect (of speaking about other matters); il – without having; andādi – in antādi type \[where end of one pāsuram relates to the beginning of the next pāsuram\]; ōr – unique; āyirattuḷ – among the thousand pāsurams; ōr – (like finding pearl in the ocean) unique; ivai – these; pattum – ten pāsurams; isaiyodum – with tune; vallār – those who can practice; ādum – any; ōr – one; tīdu – defect; ilarāgi – without having; ingum – in this material realm (as said in “tuśyanti ca ramanti ca“, being fully engaged in enjoying emperumān‘s qualities); angum – in the spiritual realm (as said in “sōśnutē sarvān kāmān“, being fully satisfied in enjoying all aspects in relation to emperumān and being present exclusively for him); ellām amaivārgaḷ tāmē – will become complete in all aspects

**Перевод:**

**Due to the desire to reach the divine feet of kriṣṇa, the greatly generous āḻvār directly gave up the strong desires towards other matters and mercifully spoke this unique decad among the unique, defect free, thousand pāsurams in andādi type, on the divine feet of kriṣṇa which are having defect free glories; those who can practice this decad with tune, will remain without any defect in this material realm and the spiritual realm, and become complete in all aspects.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the end, āḻvār says “those who are experts in this decad will be freed from all defects such as avidyā, karma etc and be the chief in the material realm and the spiritual realm”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. pādam adaivadan pāsattālē maṟṟavan pāsangaḷ muṟṟa vittuk kōdil pugaḻk kaṇṇan than adi mēl vaṇ kurugūrc catakōpan sonna tīdil andādi ōr āyirattuḷ ivaiyum ōr pattu isaiyodum vallār ādum ōr tīdilarāgi ingum angum ellām amaivārgaḷ tāmē*

- *pādam* … – Due to the attachment towards reaching the divine feet, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) gave up strong attachments towards other matters completely; this is what is explained in this decad. He is not the one who gave all the attachments first and then desired for the divine feet; as said in mūnṟām tiruvandādi 14 “*māṟpāl manam suḻippa mangaiyar tōḷ kaivittu*” (as one’s mind goes towards śrīman nārāyaṇa, one will get rid of the desire to embrace the shoulders of women”, due to attachment towards his divine feet, he eliminated these incidental worldly attachments.
- *kōdil pugaḻ* – The reason for the attachment towards his divine feet is his auspicious qualities. Defect for qualities is to be such that one can like them and other aspects as well \[[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s qualities are such that when one likes them, one will not like anything else\].
- *kaṇṇan than adi mēl* – The most generous [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) mercifully spoke on kriṣṇa who has such auspicious qualities.
- *tīdu il* … – Defect for a prabandam is to speak about matters other than bhagavān. While śrī rāmāyaṇam was meant to speak about śrī rāma’s history, it ended up speaking about the birth of subrahmaṇya, narration of puśpaka vimāna etc; after saying mahābhāratam to be “*nārāyaṇa katām imām*” (this is the story of śrīman nārāyaṇa), it ended up narrating warfare strategies etc.
- *ōr āyirattuḷ ivaiyum ōr pattu isaiyodum vallār* – Those who joyfully recite this decad among the unique thousand pāsurams.
- *ādum ōr tīdu ilarāgi* – Defects such as avidyā etc will be removed. Though [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) did not have any attachment towards worldly pleasures, he remained in this world to complete this prabandam; for those who recite those prabandams, even such difficulty is not there.
- *ingum angum ellām amaivārgaḷ tāmē* – They will remain without any defects in both this realm and spiritual realm. In this world, they will remain content as said in mahābhāratam “*kruta krutyā pradīkśantē*” (Having performed everything required of them, they are eagerly awaiting yama, the deity of death); in paramapadam, they will remain without any defect as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 31.25 “*aham sarvam kariśyāmi*” (I will serve you both in all ways).
- *tāmē* – \[They need not depend on īśvara\] They will be the chief for both material and spiritual realms.

In the next article we will enjoy the next decad.

## 8.3 Angum ingum

## 8.3.1. Angum ingum

*angum ingum vānavar tānavar yāvarum engum inaiyai enṟu unnai aṟiyagilādalaṟṟi anganjērum pūmagaḷ maṇmagaḷ āymagaḷ sangu cakkarak kaiyavan enbar saranamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

angum – in the higher worlds (heaven etc); ingum – in earth; engum – in all regions (such as pātāḷa etc); vānavar – (favourable) dēvas (celestial beings); tānavar – (unfavourable) asuras (demoniac beings); yāvarum – humans and all (in the same manner); unnai – you (who are with the enjoyable consorts); inaiyai – such enjoyable person; enṟu – as; aṟiyagilādu – without knowing; alaṟṟi – calling out (highlighting his omnipotence etc which are useful for his protection); pūmagaḷ – lakshmi who is an embodiment of the fragrance of flower; maṇmagaḷ – bhūmi dēvi (who is an embodiment of enjoyment due to being fragrant); āymagaḷ – nīḷā dēvi (who has high family heritage); angam – his divine form; sērum – remaining inseparable and enjoying; sangu cakkaram – (enjoyable) āḻvārs; kaiyavan – emperumān who holds them in their hands; saraṇam – one who is the means for fulfilling our desires (due to having complete puruśakāram (recommendation) \[in pirāttis\]); enbar – will say

**Перевод:**

**In the higher worlds, the earth and all regions, the dēvas, asuras, humans and all, without knowing that emperumān is such an enjoyable person, would call out for him as the one who remains inseparable from lakshmi who is an embodiment of the fragrance of flower, bhūmi dēvi and nīḷā dēvi, and being enjoyed by them, who is having the āḻvārs (Sanka and chakra) in his hand, and will say “he is the means for fulfilling our desires”. Since emperumān’s lordship is common for the unfavourable asuras also, being their refuge to fulfil their desires is also present in him. āḻvār is upset that even those who seek other benefits from him are not thinking about his beauty, tenderness etc and caring for him.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the first pāsuram, āḻvār is condemning the seekers of wealth saying “In this samsāram irrespective of being knowledgeable or not, instead of considering your tender nature and caring for you, they are considering you to be the means to attain their desirable goals”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. angum ingum vānavar tānavar yāvarum engum inaiyai enṟu unnai aṟiyagilādalaṟṟi anganjērum pūmagaḷ maṇmagaḷ āymagaḷ sangu cakkarak kaiyavan enbar saranamē*

- *angum ingum …* – In the higher worlds and earth.
- *engum* – pātāḷa etc which are not explicitly mentioned here.
- *vānavar* – favourable ones.
- *tānavar* – dānava – unfavourable ones.
- *yāvarum* – humans who are both favourable and unfavourable.
- *inaiyai enṟu unnai* – Knowing you to be of this particular nature – you who are the lord of all, to be having perfect tenderness. āḻvār always thinks about [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s tenderness only. Not knowing your nature of being like a tender bluish flower.
- *aṟiyagilādu* – not knowing – to not know to care for you. Whether it is the favourable dēvas or unfavourable asuras or manuśyas who are both favourable and favaourable, everyone is the same when it comes to caring for emperumān. āḻvār thinks that everyone should care for him.
- *alaṟṟi* – They would cry out highlighting those statements from śāstram which help them in getting his protection as in muṇḍaka upaniśat “*yassarvajña: sarvavit*” (one who knows the basic nature and basic qualities of all entities) and in śvētāśvatara upaniśat “… *parāsya śaktir vividaiva śrūyatē śvābhāvikī jñāna bala kriyāca”* (that supreme bhagavān who has full ability and natural knowledge, strength etc). They don’t know that you are to be protected and cared for.
- *angam sērum …* – Further, his tenderness and beauty are highlighted.
- *pūmagaḷ maṇmagaḷ āymagaḷ … angam sērum* – They would say that they have the pirāttis’ puruśakāram to attain him. They would say – the one (śrīdēvi) who says as in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 116-45 “*nakaścin nāparādyati*” (there is none who has not committed a wrongful deed), the one (bhūmi dēvi) who says “What is the point in tolerating the wrongful deeds? Should you even see the wrong deed?” and the one (nīḷā dēvi) who manifests her enjoyability so that he does not see anyone’s wrong deeds, are all present. But there is none who would perform mangaḷāśāsanam for their togetherness as seen in tiruppallāṇḍu 1 “*vadivāy nin vala mārbinil vāḻiginṟa mangaiyum pallāṇḍu*” (Long live śrī mahālakśmi who resides in the right side of your beautiful divine chest).
- *sangu cakkarak kaiyavan* – There is none who is present to enjoy the divinely beautiful combination of his hand and the divine chakra. They would say “he is having the divine weapons to destroy our enemies”. āḻvārs think as in tiruppallāṇḍu 1 “*vadivār sōdi valattuṟaiyum sudarāḻiyum pallāṇḍu*” (Long live the most beautiful and radiant chakra which is in his right hand”.
- *enbar saraṇamē* – They would say that he is the means to fulfil their desires. There is none who realises that he is the desirable goal and is most tender-natured; \[instead\] they will send him to seek alms and face the arrows of the enemies.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.3.2. Saranamagiya

*saraṇamāgiya nān maṟai nūlgaḷum sārādē maraṇam tōṟṟam vān piṇi mūppenṟu ivai māyttōm karaṇap pal padai paṟṟaṟavōdum kanal āḻi araṇat tiṇ padai ēndiya īsaṟku āḷāyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

saraṇamāgiya – refuge; nāl – having four divisions; maṟai – vēdas; nūlgaḷum – śāstras; sārādē – instead of depending upon (in the superficial meanings as said in śrī bhagavat gītā 2.42 “vēda vāda ratā: pārta nānyadastīti vādina:“); karaṇam – harmful tools; pal – many types; padai – enemy armies; paṟṟu – faith; aṟa – to lose; ōdum – to flee; kanal – fiery; āḻi – tiruvāḻi āḻvān (śudarśana chakra); araṇam – protection; tiṇ – firm; padai – weapon; ēndiya – one who is holding; īsaṟku – for sarvēśvara; āḷāy – being the servitor; maraṇam – death; tōṟṟam – birth; vān – great; piṇi – disease; mūppu – old age; enṟu – as said; ivai – the six types of changes; māyttōm – we have got rid of them

**Перевод:**

**Instead of depending upon the śāstras i.e. vēdas having four divisions, which are said to be the refuge, we have got rid of the six types of changes as said in death, birth, great disease, old age etc by being the servitor of sarvēśvara who is holding the fiery, firm weapon śudarśana chakra which makes the enemy armies having many harmful tools to lose faith and flee. Implies “while the ātmā should exist fully for emperumān, is it matching its nature to be selfish?”**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the second pāsuram, āḻvār condemns the seekers of kaivalyam (enjoying the self eternally).*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār considering the seekers of kaivalyam also to be subservient to emperumān, condemns them as they simply try to eliminate their old age, death etc through emperumān who is capable of destroying the enemies.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*The seekers of kaivalyam say “Unlike material wealth, this (kaivalyam) is not temporary; isn’t this permanent?” āḻvār condemns them here. saraṇamāgiya nān maṟai nūlgaḷum sārādē maraṇam tōṟṟam vān piṇi mūppenṟu ivai māyttōm karaṇap pal padai paṟṟaṟavōdum kanal āḻi araṇat tiṇ padai ēndiya īsaṟku āḷāyē*

- *saraṇam* … – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is condemning saying – instead of engaging in pūrvabāgam (karma kāṇḍam) which explains the means to attain wealth as said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 2.45](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/2-45/) “*traiguṇya viśayā vēdā:*” (vēdams which are focussed on the well-being of the ones having the three qualities), pursuing vēdānta (jñāna kāṇḍa) which focusses on  liberation, surrendering unto sarvēśvaran, we have eliminated our bodily connection!
- *saraṇamāgiya* – The knowledge which shows wealth and the means to attain such wealth.
- *nānmaṟai nūlgaḷ* – śāstram in the form of four vēdams. nūl – śāstram. It can also be considered as explaining āgamas etc separately by the word “*nūl*“. It is usually said in this manner as śāstram in the form of vēdam. It is seen in ārśam “*vēda śāstrā virōdinā*“.
- *maraṇam tōṟṟam* – All we have done is to have attained the state of not having six types of changes such as birth, death, strong/well-known diseases, old age etc. This praising is in the mood of condemnation.
- *karaṇap pal padai …* – Explained as shining, fiery śudarśana chakra which remains to make the enemy armies which have have many divisions and harmful weapons flee without a trace; alternatively explained as shining, fiery śudarśana chakra which remains to make the groups of sense organs flee from the worldly pleasures without a trace.
- *araṇat tiṇ padai* – Being the protection for devotees, and being invincible by the enemies.
- *tiṇ padai* – Even if īśvara fails his devotees, śudarśana chakra will not fail [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s devotees.
- *ēndiya īsaṟku* – Because of holding śudarśana chakra, he has become sarvēśvaran. For such emperumān.
- *āḷāyē* – Why are they considered as servitors? Just as those who desire to serve bhagavān, they too had *bhagavat bhajanam* (vorśipping him) and they too had *antima smruti* (thoughts in the final moments before death).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.3.3. Alumalar

*āḷum āḷār āḻiyum sangum sumappār tām vāḷum villum koṇḍu pin selvār maṟṟillai tāḷum tōḷum kaigaḷai ārat toḻak kāṇēn nāḷum nāḷum nāduvan adiyēn jñālattē*

**Пословный перевод:**

jñālattu – in this world (where people like rāvaṇa, duryōdana et al live); āḷum – servitors (who care); āḷār – not recognising (to have); tām – he (who is so tender to even be stared at); āḻiyum – tiruvāḻi (divine chakra); sangum – tiruccangu (divine conch); sumappār – carrying (as if holding a mountain); vāḷum – nandaka (sword); villum – śrī śārngam (bow); koṇḍu – carrying; pin selvār – to follow; maṟṟu – anyone else; illai – not there; tāḷum – divine feet (walking as said in “matta mātanga gāminam“); tōḷum – divine shoulders (which give shade as said in “bāhuccāyām avaśtabda:“); kaigaḷai – with my hands; Ara – fully; toḻa – to worship and serve; kāṇēn – I am not seeing (with my eyes); adiyēn – I (who have servitude as my nature) am; nāḷum nāḷum – everyday; nāduvan – searching

**Перевод:**

**emperumān is not recognising any servitors in this world; there is no one else \[other than lakśmaṇa\] to follow him carrying his divine chakra, divine conch, sword and bow; I am not seeing how I can fully worship and serve his divine feet and divine shoulders with my hands; I am searching \[for this opportunity to serve\] everyday.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the third pāsuram, āḻvār says “emperumān would descend in this material realm where people will oppose him without realising his nature and act based on the selfish prayer of some prayōjanāntaraparar (seeker of benefits other than kainkaryam); I am unable to help him during those times”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. āḷum āḷār āḻiyum sangum sumappār tām vāḷum villum koṇḍu pin selvār maṟṟillai tāḷum tōḷum kaigaḷai ārat toḻak kāṇēn nāḷum nāḷum nāduvan adiyēn jñālattē*

- *āḷum āḷār* – There is none to care for him in both the realms \[spiritual and material\] as he is focussed on ruling over only one person \[[āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)\]. nityasūris are focussed on enjoying bhagavān and samsāris are focussed on enjoying worldly pleasures.
- *āḻiyum sangum sumappār tām* – The weapons which are like ornaments for [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), appear to be heavy mountain for āḻvār. They appear as weapons for enemies and ornaments for devotees.
- *tām* – Should he not care for himself? āren’t these his specific identities as said in [periya tiruvandādi 87](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/02/periya-thiruvandhadhi-87/) “*eppōdum kai kaḻalā nēmiyān*” (one who has the inseparable chakra in his hand)? Are they heavy for him? They are heavy when he \[who is most tender\] carries them.
- *vāḷum villum koṇḍu* – Would it not be apt if someone like iḷaiya perumāḷ follows him carrying them? [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying “*āḷum āḷār, sumappār tām, pin selvār maṟṟillai*” so that [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) says “Should you who cares for me do that?” and engages him in service.
- *tāḷum tōḷum* – His divine feet which make beautiful steps will make one become very attracted and sing praises hailing his beautiful walk. It is said in śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 11.1 “*agrata: prayayau rāma:*” (śrī rāma walks first). And the shoulders which are swaying.
- *kaigaḷai Ara* – similar to those who say “*vayir****Ara*** *uṇṇa*” (to eat to the full satisfaction of the stomach).
- *toḻak kāṇēn* – It appears that vorśipping and caring are synonyms \[for [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)\]. I am not getting to worship him. “*nama:*” indicates exclusive existence for [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/). Saying “*nama:*” represents vorśipping \[Hence vorśipping is the same as caring for him exclusively\] .
- *nāḷum nāḷum nāduvan* – Meditating upon his loneliness, I will anaylse “what will happen to him” everyday. As the relationship \[between bhagavān and ātmā\] is eternal, the resulting care toward bhagavān is also eternal.
- *adiyēn* – I who am having knowledge about the true nature of the self. I who understand that it is natural for the servitor to bring about glories to the lord.
- *jñālattē* – Am I unnecessarily fearing for [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), while being in paramapadam? Why vouldn’t I fear when he is present in this world which has those who shoot brahmāstram at him, who bind him with the nāgapāśam (a type of weapon), who deceitfully invite him to make wrestlers attack him and who offer him a false throne \[which leads to a deep pit\].

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.3.4. Jnalam ponagam

*jñālam pōnagam paṟṟi ōr muṟṟā uruvāgi ālam pērilai anna vasam seyyum ammānē! kālam pērvadu ōr kāriruḷ ūḻi ottuḷadāl un kōlam kār eḻil kāṇaluṟṟu āḻum kodiyēṟkē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ōr – being unparalleled; muṟṟā – very tender; uruvāgi – having a form; jñālam – the great universe; pōnagam – as food; paṟṟi – consumed; Al – pipal; pēr – to be said; ilai – on a leaf; anna vasam seyyum – mercifully resting in sideways; ammānē – Oh lord!; kār – dark cloud’s; eḻil – having the beauty; un – your; kōlam – physical beauty; kāṇaluṟṟu – forcing to see; āḻum – becoming immersed (due to fear); kodiyēṟku – for me who has cruel sin; pērvadu – between one moment and the next; kālam – time duration; ōr – unparalleled; kār iruḷ – having deep darkness; ūḻi ottu – like a kalpa (a night of brahmā); uḷadu – is

**Перевод:**

**Oh lord who is having an unparalleled and a very tender form, who consumed the great universe as food and is mercifully resting in sideways on the pipal leaf! Your form has the beauty resembling the same of a dark cloud; I am having cruel sins to force you to show such form for me to see and be immersed in it; for me, this time duration between one moment and the next, is like a kalpa which is having deep darkness. Implies āḻvār saying “your prowess of agadita gatanā samārtyam (ability to unite contradicting aspects, ability to accomplish impossible tasks) and ability to protect everyone ends up causing more fear in me”.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fourth pāsuram, āḻvār meditates about emperumān‘s dangerous resting on the pipal leaf without anyone protecting him and thinks “what will happen to him?”*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Fourth pāsuram. Seeing āḻvār‘s fear \[in previous pāsuram\], emperumān says “Am I not the one who protected the universe by digging it out of the ocean of deluge and placing it in my stomach? Don’t fear for me” and shows his form of being the protector of all; seeing that, āḻvār fears further thinking “such protector of all, is now caught in the ocean of deluge”. jñālam pōnagam paṟṟi ōr muṟṟā uruvāgi ālam pērilai anna vasam seyyum ammānē! kālam pērvadu ōr kāriruḷ ūḻi ottuḷadāl un kōlam kār eḻil kāṇaluṟṟu āḻum kodiyēṟkē*

- *jñālam pōnagam paṟṟi* – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) consumed the whole of earth without realising “I won’t be able to digest it”. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) would think that emperumān can’t even digest butter.
- *ōr muṟṟā uruvāgi* – He is so young that when milk spills on one cheek it will be visible in the other cheek. He is in a younger stage than the stage of nursing under mother yaśōdā. āḻvār’s heart is not focussing on emperumān protecting everything during the danger of deluge and his amazing ability to rest on the pipal leaf after consuming the universe; āḻvār is only looking at his tender nature.
- *ālam pēr ilai* – There \[under yaśōdā’s care\] he was at least resting on a cradle, but here he is dangerously resting on a tender pipal leaf.
- *pēr ilai* – \[other meanings for “*pēr*“\] Moving leaf; blossoming leaf; “*katanvayam śiśuśśētē lōkē nāśam upāgatē \| śākāyām vata vrukśasya pallavētviti vismita: \|\|*” (When the worlds were annihilated, this small child is resting on the tender leaf of a pipal tree. How amazing!). As said in periya tirumoḻi 2.10.1 “*iḷan taḷiril kaṇ vaḷarnda*” (mercifully resting on a tender leaf), “*Al ilai*” is just for namesake. *pēr ilai* (big leaf) is also explained as viparīta lakśaṇā (sarcasm), indicating that it is a small leaf.
- *anna vasam seyyum* – After consuming the worlds, he is uncomfortably moving around on the leaf \[due to indigestion\]. Whatever he did in mother yaśōdā’s cradle, he is doing the same here \[causing fear in [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s mind that he will fall into the ocean of deluge\]. In the cradle he did as said in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 1.1.9 “*kidakkil tottil kiḻiya udaittidum*” (while resting he would kick the cradle to break it). Being very childish to know “this will not digest”, mercifully resting on the small leaf in the ocean of deluge, moving around while being on such small leaf are all causing fear for āḻvār.
- *ammānē* – Oh protector of all! Also, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is fearing because this has not occurred to some anonymous person but for the protector of all.
- *kālam …* – As I keep thinking about your loneliness, the duration between one moment and the next feels like the unending dark kalpa (night of brahmā).
- *un kōlam kār eḻil kāṇaluṟṟu* – āḻvār is saying “your dark, beautiful form”; alternatively [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying “your beauty which resembles that of a cloud”.
- *kāṇaluṟṟu āḻum kodiyēṟku* – For me, the great sinner who desires to see your beautiful form to perform mangaḷāśāsanam (wishing for well being), yet not getting to see the same and suffering due to that. The fear in samsāram will be eliminated as one takes refuge of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/); but I have committed such a great sin that I have this fear \[for emperumān’s well being\] which will go on eternally without an end. There is no end for the fear of thinking “What will happen to the protector of all?”

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.3.5. Kodiyar mada

*kodiyār mādak kōḷūragattum puḷingudiyum madiyādinnē nī tuyil mēvi magiḻndadudān adiyār allal tavirtta asaivō? anṟēl ip padidān nīṇḍu tāviya asaivō? paṇiyāyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kodi – flags; Ar – abundantly present; mādam – having mansions; kōḷūr – tirukkōḷūr; agattu – inside; puḷingudiyum – in tiruppuḷingudi; madiyādu – to not leave; innē – in this (composed) manner; tuyil mēvi – due to mercifully resting; nī – you; magiḻndadudān – being pleased in this manner; adiyār – devotees; allal – sorrow; tavirtta – eliminated; asaivō – due to the fatigue?; anṟēl – otherwise; i – this; paditān – earth; nīṇḍu – growing that day; tāviya – measured and accepted; asaivō – fatigue?; anṟēl – if it is not due to that; i – this; padidān – earth; nīṇḍu – growing one day; tāviya – measured; asaivō – fatigue?; paṇiyāy – mercifully tell

**Перевод:**

**You are pleased to be mercifully resting in this composed manner in tirukkōḷūr which is having mansions with abundance of flags and in tiruppuḷingudi, to not leave from there;  are you resting here due to the fatigue of eliminating the sorrows of your devotees or due to the fatigue of growing that day to measure and accept this world? Mercifully tell me. āḻvār‘s aim is to hold on to the divine feet which measured the world and the shoulders which won over the enemies.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fifth pāsuram, as emperumān mercifully shows his merciful resting posture in tirukkōḷūr and tiruppuḷingudi to remove āḻvār’s fears, āḻvār asks him out of fear “instead of engaging in activities, why are you being pleased in mercifully resting like this?”*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “Are you resting in tirukkōḷūr and tiruppuḷingudi without any distress, due to the fatigue from destroying the enemies and the activity in the incarnation of trivkirama?”*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. kodiyār mādak kōḷūragattum puḷingudiyum madiyādinnē nī tuyil mēvi magiḻndadudān adiyār allal tavirtta asaivō? anṟēl ip padidān nīṇḍu tāviya asaivō? paṇiyāyē*

- *kodi Ar mādak kōḷūr agattum* – In tirukkōḷūr which is having mansions with flags atop; should you rest here with the flags atop which will let your enemies know your presence and attack you? No one fears for kodi (flag) like [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) \[kodi also means woman in tamiḻ – as āḻvār is detached from worldly matters, this is highlighted in cādu (double meaning)\]. Should you not remain as in the case where your presence was kept secret due to fear for kamsa? In the previous pāsuram, this fear is not there, since both favourable and unfavourable were in annihilated state there \[here, they are abundantly available\].
- *puḷingudiyum* – This is also a reason for āḻvār’s fear. āḻvār thinks that [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is resting in many places due to his overwhelming fatigue.
- *madiyādu* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying that emperumān is resting uncomfortably; alternatively, madi – laziness; indicating he is resting without laziness. That is, though knowing well that he is there for us, he does not give up thinking “there is no one approaching me and caring for me”.
- *innē* – In this manner. Other than saying as in [tirumālai 23](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/10/thirumalai-23/) “*kidandadōr kidakkai*” (unparalleled resting posture), there are no words to describe him.
- *nī tuyil mēvi magiḻndadu tān* – Why have you who are *avikāri* (immutable), mercifully rested and become pleased? [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) thinks that [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is having a relaxed face and the reason for that is he was fatigued before and those who are fatigued will look relaxed as they get sufficient sleep.
- *adiyār allal tavirtta asaivō* – Is it the fatigue of destroying rāvaṇa et al for the sake of indra et al who surrendered at you divine feet, and eliminating their sorrows?
- *anṟēl* – otherwise.
- *ippadi …* – Did your tender divine feet become tired due to measuring the uneven world after growing up quickly on the same day of birth \[as vāmana\]?
- *paṇiyāyē* – Did your divine feet or shoulders become tired? Mercifully tell me; kindly grant me the opportunity to massage your shoulders or the divine feet whichever are tired. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is asking [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) to speak so that he can find out the fatigue from the pitch of his tone. āḻvār is thinking – even in divyadēśams, nothing is impossible for him; it is just that he has vowed not to speak, he is remaining silent.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.3.6. Paniya amarar

*paṇiyā amarar paṇivum paṇbum tāmēyām aṇiyār āḻiyum sangamum ēndum avar kāṇmin taṇiyā vennōy ulagil tavirppān tiruneela maṇiyār mēniyōdu en manam sūḻa varuvārē*

**Пословный перевод:**

paṇiyā – not to bow to (anyone’s foot for any reason); amarar – nityasūris’ (who are not ruled by anyone \[other than emperumān\]); paṇivum – (natural, fitting their nature) humility; paṇbum – their qualities (such as jñāna (knowledge), prēma (love) etc); tāmēyām – being the target himself; aṇi – in the form of ornaments; Ar – having enjoyability; āḻiyum – divine chakra; sangum – divine conch; ēndum – holding (to be enjoyable for such nityasūris); avar kāṇmin – see him; ulagil – in this world; taṇiyā – occurring without reduction; vem – causing great heat; nōy – diseases (in the form of avidyā (ignorance), karma (virtues and vices), vāsanā (impressions), ruci (taste) and prakruti sambandam (bondage)); tavirppān – to eliminate; tiru – opulence (of perfect beauty, tenderness etc to be enjoyed by such nityasūris); Ar – having; neela maṇi – like a blue gem; mēniyōdu – with divine form; en – my; manam – mind; sūḻa – to be bewildered; varuvār – descends in this samsāram

**Перевод:**

**sarvēśvaran himself remains the target for the humility and qualities of nityasūris so that they need not bow to (anyone else), is holding the divine chakra and divine conch in the form of ornaments to be enjoyed by them; to bewilder my mind, such emperumān descends in this samsāram with the opulent, blue gem like divine form to eliminate the never-reducing diseases which cause great heat.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the sixth pāsuram, āḻvār says “sarvēśvaran who is mercifully present in paramapadam to be cared by nityasūris who have pure knowledge and devotion, has descended in this samsāram to eliminate the disease of bondage for all ātmās here, causing fear in my heart”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Sixth pāsuram, when asked “Why are you fearing for emperumān like this? īsn’t he the protector of all?” āḻvār says “even when he is in paramapadam, enjoyed by nityasūris, he is of the nature that one fears for his safety unnecessarily; why would I not fear for him when he appears with such form in this world?” paṇiyā amarar paṇivum paṇbum tāmēyām aṇiyār āḻiyum sangamum ēndum avar kāṇmin taṇiyā vennōy ulagil tavirppān tiruneela maṇiyār mēniyōdu en manam sūḻa varuvārē*

- *paṇiyā amarar* – Unlike others, nityasūris never had any scope to bow to anyone. They are unlike those who previously vorśipped inapt persons, atoned for such acts one fine day, atoned thinking as in tirukkurundāṇḍagam 12 “*aḻukkudambu eccilvāy*” (dirty body \[bowing to others\] and contaminated mouth \[praising others\]) and eventually bowed to the apt persons \[[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), pirāttis, ācāryas\]; that is those who did not engage in praising or serving others. With this, nityasūris are differentiated from muktātmās.
- *paṇivum paṇbum tāmēyām* – For their subservience and qualities such as jñāna (knowledge), emperumān remains the target.
- *aṇi Ar āḻiyum sangamum ēndum* – While emperumān holds the divine weapons, these divine weapons appear like all ornaments, and manifest his divine form to the nityasūris; the nityasūris would fear unnecessarily and perform mangaḷāśāsanam (well-wishing prayers) to him. Even they go through the same emotions as I do.
- *avar kāṇmin* – It is such [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who descends into this fearful abode. Is he coming here for his own benefit?
- *ulagil taṇiyā vennōy … tavirppān* – The never ending tāpa trayam (three types of sufferings viz ādi baudika (caused by other creatures), ādi daivika (caused by divine/natural forces), ādi ātmika (caused by self)).
- *tiru neela maṇi Ar mēniyōdu* – With invigorating, very tender form resembling a blue gem. Even if he decides to descend here, should he descend with such divine form?
- *en manam* – My mind which has understood that he is roaming around in this samsāra with such tender form.
- *sūḻa varuvārē* – one who descends to make my mind spin in bewilderment.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.3.7. Varuvar selvar

*varuvār selvār vaṇ parisārattirunda en tiruvāḻ mārvaṟku en tiṟam sollār seyvaden? uruvār cakkaram sangu sumandu ingu ummōdu oru pāduḻalvān ōr adiyānum uḷan enṟē*

**Пословный перевод:**

varuvār – those who come (from there); selvār – those who go (from here); vaṇ – having distinguished wealth; parisārattu – in tirupparisāram; en – to accept my service; irunda – mercifully present; tiruvāḻmārvaṟku – for śrīmān (the lord of śrī mahālakśmi); uru – by physical beauty; Ar – matching; cakkaram – tiruvāḻi (divine chakra); sangum – tiruccangu (divine conch); sumandu – carrying; ingu – in this material realm; ummōdu – with you; orupādu – remaining in close proximity to you; uḻalvān – travel along; ōr – (unparalleled) one; adiyānum – servitor; uḷan – is available; enṟu – as; en – my; tiṟam – matters; sollār – not informing; seyvadu – can be done; en – (becoming upset) how?

**Перевод:**

**To accept my service, śrīmān (the lord of śrī mahālakśmi) is mercifully present in tirupparisāram which has distinguished wealth; though many devotees come and go, there is no one present to inform my matters to such emperumān that there is a servitor (me) who is available to carry your divine chakra and divine conch which match your physical beauty and travel along with you in this material realm, remaining in close proximity to you. Since those who come do not bring him and those who go do not hear any response, āḻvār thinks that they come and go for their own sake and hence says that they are not informing. āḻvār is becoming upset thinking “what can be done?”**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the seventh pāsuram, āḻvār says “I am unable to help him there \[in his incarnations\] and becoming anguished due to that; further there is no one like me who travels along with emperumān, to inform the presence  of me, the servitor, in the presence of periya pirāttiyār, my female lord (svāmini) in tirupparisāram (tiruvaṇparisāram) and help me attain emperumān”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. varuvār selvār vaṇ parisārattirunda en tiruvāḻ mārvaṟku en tiṟam sollār seyvaden? uruvār cakkaram sangu sumandu ingu ummōdu oru pāduḻalvān ōr adiyānum uḷan enṟē*

- *varuvār selvār* – People walk from āḻvārtirunagari to tirupparisāram considering it to be a lengthy/great route. āḻvār thinks about those who are going there for their own purpose to be going there to inform his state and those who are arriving from there to be coming to invite him. He is not remaining inactive \[instead he is waiting for them\]. \[āḻvār thinks\] We should care for tirupparisāram; further, we should care for emperumān’s togetherness with pirātti there. āḻvār’s state of mind here is that he desires to serve both emperumān and pirātti, following them everywhere as iḷaiya perumāḷ (lakśmaṇa) said/did in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 31.25  “*bhavāmstu saha vaidēhyā girisānuśu ramsyatē*” (While you enjoy with sītā in the foothills of the mountain, I will serve you both in all ways).
- *en tiṟam sollār* – They are not informing my state due to the absence of the one \[pirātti\] who makes him listen to our requests! \[there is some other reason\]
- *en tiruvāḻ mārvaṟku* – Because it is the abode where my female lord (*svāmini*) is present, whatever is informed will have value.
- *seyvadu en* – What shall I do in this situation?

When asked “If they are going for their own sake, what would they say there?” āḻvār says

- *uru Ar cakkaram …* – They are saying 1) One who is desirously carrying the beautiful āḻvārs (Sanka and chakra), 2) One who is carrying the āḻvārs who appear like ornaments and who negate the need for any other ornament.
- *ingu* – In this samsāram where there is none to care for you.
- *ummōdu oru pādu uḻalvān* – Following you on one side without ever leaving you. There is already iḷaiya perumāḷ for one side.
- *ōr adiyānum uḷan enṟē* – Saying that there is a person (me) who is ananyaprayōjana (one who does not expect anything but kainkaryam). They would remain resigned thinking that there is none as said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 7.19](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/7-19/) “*sa mahātmā sa durlabha:*” (Such large-hearted souls are rare to attain); there is no one to inform my matters saying “don’t think like that, there is one person (āḻvār)”; what shall I do?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.3.8. Enre ennai

*enṟē ennai un ērār kōlat tirundadikkīḻ ninṟē ātceyya nī koṇḍaruḷa ninaippadudān? kunṟēḻ pārēḻ sūḻ kadal jñālamuḻuvēḻum ninṟē tāviya nīḷ kaḻal āḻit tirumālē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

ēḻ kunṟu – the seven anchoring mountains; ēḻ pār – seven islands; sūḻ – surrounded; kadal – the respective ocean; ēḻ jñālamum – seven worlds starting from bhūmi \[i.e. bhū:, bhuva:, suva:, maha:, jana, tapa, satya lōkams\]; muḻu – fully; ninṟē – in his standing posture; tāviya – measured; nīḷ – lengthy; kaḻal – one who is having divine feet; āḻi – having tiruvāḻi (divine chakra, which highlights his lordship); tirumālē – Oh śriya:pati (lord of śrī mahālakśmi)!; ennai – me (who is a caring servitor for you); un – your (tender, enjoyable); ēr – beautiful; Ar – abundant; kōlam – having decorated with ornaments; tirundu – naturally beautiful; adikkīḻ – under the divine feet; ninṟē – remaining (without ever separating); ātceyya – to serve (by performing mangaḷāśāsanam matching your śriya:patitva (being the lord of śrī mahālakśmi), saukumārya (tenderness) etc); nī – you; koṇḍaruḷi – acknowledging (in your divine heart); ninaippadudān – mercifully think (to make these occur); enṟu – when?

**Перевод:**

**Oh śriya:pati who remained in standing posture and is having the lengthy divine feet which fully measured the seven anchoring mountains, seven islands, the respective ocean which surrounds those islands and the seven worlds starting from bhūmi and who is having the divine chakra! When are you mercifully thinking to acknowledge me to remain under your divine feet which are naturally beautiful and are decorated with abundantly beautiful ornaments and serve them? koṇḍaruḷi is also recited as koṇḍaruḷa.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the eighth pāsuram, āḻvār asks emperumān “When are you going to have me under your divine feet permanently?”*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. enṟē ennai un ērār kōlat tirundadikkīḻ ninṟē ātceyya nī koṇḍaruḷa ninaippadudān? kunṟēḻ pārēḻ sūḻ kadal jñālamuḻuvēḻum ninṟē tāviya nīḷ kaḻal āḻit tirumālē!*

- *enṟē* – When [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) said “we will fulfil your desire” [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) asks “when?”
- *ennai* – Me who cannot remain without caring for you.
- *un …* – Under your naturally beautiful divine feet which are decorated with abundantly beautiful ornaments. The divine feet which must be performed mangaḷāśāsanam.
- *ninṟē ātceyya* – Instead of accepting favours and leaving as said in yajur vēdam “*dēhimē dadāmi tē*” (I will do something for you and you grant me something), to serve continuously.
- *nī koṇḍaruḷa* – Unlike my climbing on a resting elephant , you should consider in your divine heart that I should be engaged in some service.
- *ninaippadudān* – Only [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s thought/desire will lead to results. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) considers that his own desire is useless.
- *kunṟēḻ …* – When emperumān’s seated posture in tiruvaṇparisāram itself as said in previous pāsuram “*vaṇ parisārattirunda*” deserves to be performed mangaḷāśāsanam, when he performs super-human activities, should he not be performed mangaḷāśāsanam? Oh śriya:pati who is having the lengthy divine feet which measured the seven anchoring mountains, seven islands, the seven oceans which surround them and the seven types of worlds, in standing posture itself and who is having the divine chakra in his hand! When will I pamper and massage your tender divine feet to relax them, which measured the uneven earth though you are the śriya:pati who are carrying the divine weapons such as Sanka, chakra etc? Alternatively, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying “You who can accomplish most difficult tasks, should mercifully think that I should reach your divine feet and serve there”.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.3.9. Tirumal!

*tirumāl! nānmugan senjadaiyān enṟivargaḷ em perumān tanmaiyai yār aṟigiṟpār? pēsi en? orumā mudalvā! ūḻip priān! ennai āḷudai karumā mēniyan enban en kādal kalakkavē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tiru – for periya pirāttiyār (śrī mahālakśmi); māl – Oh lord who is distinguished to be loved!; nānmugan – brahmā (who is engaged in multifaceted creation); sem sadaiyān – rudra (who is engaged in penance); enṟu – well known in this manner; ivaragaḷ – these personalities; emperumān – you who are my lord and greater than all; tanmaiyai – distinguished aspects such as beauty, tenderness etc; aṟigiṟpār – those who are capable of knowing; Ar – who?; en – my; kādal – love; kalakka – bewilder (my heart); oru – distinguished; mā mudalvā – Oh supreme cause!; ūḻi – as per the time; pirān – oh benefactor!; ennai – me; āḷudai – engaged in service; karu – dark; mā mēniyan – Oh one with distinguished form!; enban – I keep saying; pēsi en – How can I explain?

**Перевод:**

**I keep saying “Oh lord who is distinguished to be loved by periya pirāttiyār! Who among the well-known, great personalities such as brahmā, rudra et al know the distinguished aspects of you, who are my lord and greater than all? Oh distinguished, supreme cause! I am bewildered by the love towards you. Oh benefactor as per the occasion! Oh one with a distinguished dark form who engaged me in service!” How can I explain your tenderness!**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the ninth pāsuram, emperumān mercifully says “When brahmā et al, dakśa et al are all present, why are you fearing” āḻvār says “They don’t know about your saukumāryam (tenderness) etc; due to my affection towards you, I have become bewildered and am crying out”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. tirumāl! nānmugan senjadaiyān enṟivargaḷ em perumān tanmaiyai yār aṟigiṟpār? pēsi en? orumā mudalvā! ūḻip priān! ennai āḷudai karumā mēniyan enban en kādal kalakkavē*

- *tirumāl* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is calling out with determination \[that śrīman nārāyaṇan is the supreme\] saying “tirumāl”. Would they perform mangaḷāśāsanam \[wishing well\] for your togetherness with pirātti?
- *nānmugan* – One who has multiple faces to engage in creation, and is fully focussed on creation.
- *sem sadaiyān* – rudra who has the form of one who is pursuing some means; he too is focussed on getting what he desires.
- *emperumān tanmaiyai* – Tenderness of you who is [sarvēśvara](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/).
- *Ar aṟigiṟpār* – Can it be known by some people? Will those who are focussed on other aspects know your tenderness? Can your tenderness be known by those who are focussed on other aspects?
- *pēsi en* –  What is the use of speaking about this? Can we make them care for you? \[No\] Can we make your tenderness to be limited? \[No\] When asked “If they are focussed elsewhere and do not know about me, why don’t you speak about me?” [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says “Am I able to do it now?” \[No\]
- *oru mā mudalvā* – Oh distinguished supreme cause!
- *ūḻip pirān* – Oh one who is the lord of all entities including time!
- *ennai …* – Oh one who is having the form which made me exclusively exist for you, while I was focussed on other aspects previously!
- *enban* – I too can only say this. You being the controller of all and accepting me by manifesting your physical beauty, have bewildered me.
- *en kādal kalakkavē* – My love makes me worry and fear for you, and I spoke out of such bewilderment caused by your beauty and greatness; I did not speak, having seen the ultimate level of your tenderness. I have spoken being blinded by love and not with heart’s intent. Neither the care of prayajōnāntaraparas (those who seek other benefits) such as brahmā et al, is a match for you nor the care of me who is blinded by love.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.3.10. Kalakkam illa

*kalakkam illā nal tava munivar karai kaṇḍōr tuḷakkam illā vānavar ellām toḻuvārgaḷ malakkam eyda mā kadal tannaik kadaindānai ulakka nām pugaḻgiṟpadu en seyvadu? uraiyīrē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kalakkam – bewilderment (which is natural in this samsāram (material realm)); illā – not having; nal tavam – having tapas (penance) in the form of jñānam (knowledge); munivar – sages sanaka et al; karai kaṇḍōr – (as said in “sōdvana: pāram āpnōti“) muktātmās (liberated souls) who have reached the other shore (after crossing samsāra); tuḷakkam – wavering \[thoughts\]; illā – not having; vānavar – nityasūris (eternally free souls); ellām – all; toḻuvārgaḷ – worship and perform mangaḷāśāsanam (wishing well with care); mā – boundless; kadal tannai – ocean; malakkam eyda – to agitate; kadaindānai – omnipotent emperumān who churned; nām – us; ulakka – to see fully; pugaḻgiṟpadu – and this ability to praise him; en seyvadu – how to do?; uraiyīr – Please tell – āḻvār asks the worldly people

**Перевод:**

**Sages such as sanaka et al who are not having any bewilderment and are having tapas in the form of jñānam, muktātmās who have reached the other shore \[liberated\] and all of the unwavering nityasūris worship and perform mangaḷāśāsanam to the omnipotent emperumān who churned the boundless ocean to agitate it; how can we fully see and praise him? Please tell – āḻvār asks the worldly people.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the tenth pāsuram, emperumān mercifully says “There are many who think about my tenderness etc and care for me; I am also too strong to be cared by anyone”; āḻvār thinks about it and becomes joyful being relieved from his fear.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. Whatever was causing fear in āḻvār previously, now becomes the reason for the removal of fear and hence āḻvār becomes joyful. We cannot understand what will cause fear in āḻvār at a particular time and what will remove the fear at that time. kalakkam illā nal tava munivar karai kaṇḍōr tuḷakkam illā vānavar ellām toḻuvārgaḷ malakkam eyda mā kadal tannaik kadaindānai ulakka nām pugaḻgiṟpadu en seyvadu? uraiyīrē*

- *kalakkam illā nal tava munivar* – Sages such as sanaka et al who are meditators having great penance, and not having any bewilderment which are acquired by worldly pleasures.
- *karai kaṇḍōr* – muktātmās.
- *tuḷakkam illā vānavar* – tuḷakkam – shivering. The nityasūris who have no connection with samsāram. tuḷakkam – wavering. That is, contraction \[in their knowledge\].
- *ellām toḻuvārgaḷ* – mumukśus (liberation seekers), muktātmās and nityasūris are those who serve [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/). As service means bringing glories to the lord, it is mangaḷāśāsanam only.
- *malakkam …* – The greatly capable lord due to churning the great ocean to agitate it. He is so capable that even those who care for him, are protected by him only.
- *ulakka …* – While we cannot understand his nature fully, how can we care for him and speak about him fully? Please tell. While [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) manifested the same valour previously, āḻvār did not believe that and feared for it, but why is he feeling satisfied seeing the same now? This is because āḻvār should complete this prabandam or it can be due to īśvara not sustaining himself \[by āḻvār being satisfied, emperumān will sustain himself\].

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.3.11. Uraiya vennoy

*uraiyā vennōy tavira aruḷ nīḷ mudiyānai varaiyār māda mannu kurugūrc catakōpan urai ēy sol todai ōr āyirattuḷ ippattum niraiyē vallār nīdulagattup piṟavārē*

**Пословный перевод:**

uraiyā – to be beyond speech; vem – causing heat/suffering; nōy – disease (of bewilderment); tavira – to eradicate; aruḷ – showing his completeness of wealth and ability; nīḷ mudiyānai – emperumān, the lord who is greater than all; varai – mountain; Ar – like densely present; mādam – mansions; mannu – being firmly present; kurugūr – leader of āḻvārtirunagari; satakōpan – nammāḻvār‘s; urai – in the manner of speech; ēy – dense; sol todai – having string of words; ōr – distinguished; āyirattuḷ – among the thousand pāsurams; ippattum – this decad; niraiyē – in proper sequence; vallār – those who can recite; nīdu – vast; ulagattu – in this samsāra (where there is none who cares for bhagavān); piṟavār – will not take birth

**Перевод:**

**emperumān, the lord who is greater than all, showed his completeness of wealth and ability to eradicate the disease which is causing suffering which is beyond speech; nammāḻvār, the leader of āḻvārtirunagari which has firmly present mansions which resemble densely present mountains, composed this decad among the distinguished thousand pāsurams, which have string of words in the manner of dense speech, on such emperumān; those who can recite this decad in proper sequence, will not take birth in this vast samsāra.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the end, āḻvār says “Those who are expert in this decad, will not take birth in this samsāram where emperumān’s loneliness is feared”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. uraiyā vennōy tavira aruḷ nīḷ mudiyānai varaiyār māda mannu kurugūrc catakōpan urai ēy sol todai ōr āyirattuḷ ippattum niraiyē vallār nīdulagattup piṟavārē*

- *uraiyā vennōy* – Very cruel disease which is beyond words. Not only it caused suffering for us, it also made us wonder “what will happen to bhagavān who is the lord of ubhaya vibhūti (spiritual and material realms)?”
- *tavira aruḷ nīḷ mudiyānai* – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), who is ubhaya vibhūti nātan, who showered his grace to eradicate such disease. ammangi ammāḷ says “emperumān nodded his head in agreement saying ‘we will fulfil your desire’, to eradicate [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s fear”. Only after eradicating āḻvār’s fear, emperumān’s crown which highlights his protection for both realms, became firmly seated on his head.
- *varai Ar …* – Once his fear was removed, āḻvārtirunagari too became abundantly rich and stable.
- *urai ēy …* – The distinguished thousand pāsurams which are having string of words of \[[āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s\] speech.
- *ippattum niraiyē vallār* – Those who can recite this decad in proper sequence; due to the bewilderment he acquired, āḻvār is thinking, those who recite this decad will also be unable to recite it in proper sequence.
- *nīdulagattup piṟavārē* – They will not be born in this realm where if one looks around the vast earth, one will not find anyone to care for [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/); they will get to reach paramapadam where the whole realm performs mangaḷāśāsanam for emperumān and enjoys him eternally.

## 8.4 Varkada aruvi

## 8.4.1. Varkada aruvi

*vār kadā aruvi yānai mā malaiyin maruppu iṇaik kuvadu iṟittu urutti ūr koḷ tiṇ pāgan uyir seguttu arangin mallaraik konṟu sūḻ paraṇ mēl pōr kadā arasar puṟakkida mādam mī misaik kanjanait tagartta sīr koḷ siṟṟāyan tiruccengunṟūril tirucciṟṟāṟu engaḷ sel sārvē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vār – flowing; kadā – exultation; aruvi – fluid falling down; ānai – elephant; mā – huge; malaiyin – mountain’s; maruppu – tusks; iṇai – pair; kuvadu – peaks; iṟuttu – broke; urutti – rolling (the elephant effortlessly); Ur koḷ – to guide the elephant to walk (even in that state of broken tusk); tiṇ – one who is having the ability; pāgan – mahout’s; uyir – life; seguttu – destroyed; arangil – those who were present in the middle of the wresting arena; mallarai – wrestlers (cāṇūra and muśtika); konṟu – killed; sūḻ – around (the arena); paraṇmēl – in the balconies (those who are standing); pōr – battle; kadā – those who can conduct; arasar – kings; puṟakkida – to flee; māda mīmisai – present on the highest platform; kanjanai – kamsa; tagartta – tore him apart (like knocking off unburnt pot); sīr – wealth of valour; koḷ – having; siṟu – child; āyan – where kriṣṇa is present; tiruccengunṟūril – in tiruccengunṟūr; tirucciṟṟāṟu – tirucciṟṟāṟu; engaḷ – for us; sel – to go and approach; sārvu – abode of refuge

**Перевод:**

**kriṣṇa broke the peaks, i.e. the tusks of the mountain, i.e. the elephant which has waterfalls i.e. the exultation fluid flowing, and rolled it; he then destroyed the life of the mahout who was having the ability to guide the elephant to walk; he then killed the wrestlers who were present in the middle of the wresting arena; he then tore apart kamsa who was on the highest platform to make the kings who were standing in the balconies around the arena, flee the place; tirucciṟṟāṟu in tirucengunṟūr where such young child kriṣṇa, who is having the wealth of valour is present, is the abode of refuge for us to go and approach.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the first pāsuram, āḻvār says “tiruccengunṟūr tirucciṟṟāṟu which is the divine abode of the glorious young covherd who destroyed enemies such as kuvalāyāpīdam (elephant), wrestlers et al, is the refuge which removes our fear”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. வார் கடா அருவி யானை மா மலையின் மருப்பு இணைக் குவடு இறுத்து உருட்டி ஊர் கொள் திண் பாகன் உயிர் செகுத்து அரங்கின் மல்லரைக் கொன்று சூழ் பரண் மேல் போர் கடா அரசர் புறக்கிட மாடம் மீ மிசைக் கஞ்சனைத் தகர்த்த சீர் கொள் சிற்றாயன் திருச்செங்குன்றூரில் திருச்சிற்றாறு எங்கள் செல் சார்வே vār kadā aruvi yānai mā malaiyin maruppu iṇaik kuvadu iṟittu urutti Ur koḷ tiṇ pāgan uyir seguttu arangin mallaraik konṟu sūḻ paraṇ mēl pōr kadā arasar puṟakkida mādam mī misaik kanjanait tagartta sīr koḷ siṟṟāyan tiruccengunṟūril tirucciṟṟāṟu engaḷ sel sārvē*

- *vār kadā aruvi yānai mā malaiyin* – The mountain of elephant having flowing waterfalls of exultation fluid. kadā – madam (exultation). kamsa made the elephant consume fluids which caused it madness, and placed it at the entrance, yet he pretended to be sober and was planning to cry for [kriṣṇa](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) \[if he gets killed by the elephant\] as a maternal uncle would do, identifying it to be an accident. periya tirumoḻi 6.5.6 “*puguvāy ninṟa pōdagam vīḻap porudān*” (kriṣṇa who battled to kill the elephant which was placed in the entrance by kamsa).
- *maruppu iṇaik kuvadu iṟuttu* – Breaking the pair of peaks, i.e. pair of tusks; effortlessly breaking the tusks which resemble mountain peaks. Just as breaking two peaks from that mountain.
- *urutti* – As it lost its tusks, it lost its strength as well; so emperumān knocked it off effortlessly with his divine feet.
- *Ur koḷ tiṇ pāgan* – The mahout was still conducting the elephant as if it was alive; being an able mentor, he was conducting the elephant.
- *uyir seguttu* – Though the elephant was knocked off, unless the mahout was killed, it cannot be considered as dead.
- *arangin mallaraik konṟu* – As [kriṣṇa](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) and balarāma entered the arena pridefully carrying the tusks of the elephant which was killed; unable to bear their pride, cāṇūra and muśtika attacked them only to be killed. kamsa thought “as the elephant was an animal, it died without knowing how to kill kriṣṇa; but we have the wrestlers who will kill kriṣṇa” and kriṣṇa ended up killing them as well. As those who were present, including the girls, were becoming fearful as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 103.5 “*na samam yuddam ityāhu:*” (this is not an even battle), he effortlessly killed the wrestlers to eradicate their fear.
- *sūḻ paraṇ mēl* – Those who were standing on the balconies around the arena.
- *pōr kadā arasar puṟakkida* – Those kings who can motivate a demotivated army, to conduct \[and win\] battles; as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 1.29 “*sēnānaya viśarata:*” (one who is capable of leading the army), these kings who will not return without victory in battle field, were fleeing.
- *māda mīmisai* – Being seated in the tallest balcony/platform as said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 5.20.26 “*tunga manja vyavastita:*” (he was seated in the highest throne). He raised the platform to the extent of his fear.
- *kanjanait tagartta* – He jumped up to the place where kamsa was seated, knocked him down by pulling him by his hair and tore him apart like breaking a fresh pot (which is not burnt yet) as said in periya tirumoḻi 3.10.3 “*kanjan kunji pidittaditta pirān*” (the benefactor who knocked kamsa by grabbing his hair); as said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 5.20.91 “*avajñayā hatam druśtvā kriṣṇēna maturēśvaram*” (subsequently, seeing [kriṣṇa](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) effortlessly killing kamsa). śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 5.20.86 “*kēśēśvākruśya vigaḷat kirītam avanītalē \| kaim sampātayāmāsa tasyōparipa pātaca \|\|*” (That kriṣṇa knocked the crown on kamsa’s head, grabbed his hair and pushed him to the ground; kriṣṇa landed on him) – ammangi ammāḷ explains “When traitors of the kingdom are killed, their medals/honours will be revoked and be killed then – similarly, emperumān revoked the crown conferred by him to kamsa and killed him”.
- *sīr koḷ siṟṟāyan* – While not old enough, not having any shortcoming in the wealth of valour.
- *tiruccengunṟūril tiucciṟṟāṟu* – Just as a bush where a tiger resides, the town which is feared by enemies.
- *engaḷ* – For us, who care for emperumān, such as [periyāḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/periyazhwar/), śrī vidura, self ([āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)), [piḷḷai uṟangā villi dāsar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/pillai-urangavilli-dhasar/), and others who are similar.
- *sel sārvē* – The refuge where they can enter and remain without any fear. That, the fear he was having previously is gone, can be seen in his clear \[jubilliant\] tone/recital.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.4.2. Engal sel sarvu

*engaḷ sel sārvu yāmudai amudam imaiyavar appan en appanpongu mūvlagum padaittu aḷittu aḻikkum porundu mūvuruvan em aruvansengayal ugaḷum tēm paṇai pudai sūḻ tiruccengunṟūrt tirucciṟṟāṟuangamarginṟa ādiyān allāl yāvar maṟṟu en amar tuṇaiyē?*

**Пословный перевод:**

engaḷ – for us; sel – to go and surrender; sārvu – refuge; yām – our; udai – having; amudam – enjoyablility; imaiyavar – for nityasūris (who have unfailing knowledge); appan – being the benefactor; en – for me; appan – being the benefactor; pongu – rich; mū ulagum – three worlds; padaittu – create; aḷittu – protect; aḻikkum – being the one who annihilates; porundu – matching (for this); mū uruvan – having three forms; em – for me; aruvan – being the antarātmā (indvelling super soul); sem – reddish (due to being youthful); kayal – fish; ugaḷum – to jump joyfully; tēm – filled with honey; paṇai – maruda (cropland) region; pudai sūḻ – surrounded; tiruccengunṟūr – in tiruccengunṟūr; tirucciṟṟāṟu – tirucciṟṟāṟu; angu – in that distinguished abode; amarginṟa – one who resides fittingly; ādiyān – one who is the cause for sustenance of all; allāl – other than; maṟṟu – any one; en – for me; amar – matching; tuṇai – companion; yāvar – who is?

**Перевод:**

**tirucciṟṟāṟu, in tiruccengunṟūr, which is surrounded by  maruda region which is filled with honey to make the reddish fish jump joyfully is the distinguished abode where emperumān who is my antarātmā, who is having three matching forms to create, protect and annihilate the three worlds, who is the benefactor for our nityasūris and me, and who is the refuge to go and surrender, and the enjoyable aspect, resides fittingly; who else is a matching companion for me other than such emperumān who is the cause for sustenance of all? paṇai also indicates neydal (water and areas close to water).**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the second pāsuram, āḻvār says “There is none other than emperumān, who is capable of creating the universe etc and is mercifully standing in tiruccengunṟūr, who is my companion”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. எங்கள் செல் சார்வு யாமுடை அமுதம் இமையவர் அப்பன் என் அப்பன்பொங்கு மூவுலகும் படைத்து அளித்து அழிக்கும் பொருந்து மூவுருவன் எம் அருவன்செங்கயல் உகளும் தேம் பணை புடை சூழ் திருச்செங்குன்றூர்த் திருச்சிற்றாறுஅங்கு அமர்கின்ற ஆதியான் அல்லால் யாவர் மற்று என் அமர் துணையே? engaḷ sel sārvu yāmudai amudam imaiyavar appan en appanpongu mūvlagum padaittu aḷittu aḻikkum porundu mūvuruvan em aruvansengayal ugaḷum tēm paṇai pudai sūḻ tiruccengunṟūrt tirucciṟṟāṟuangamarginṟa ādiyān allāl yāvar maṟṟu en amar tuṇaiyē?*

- *engaḷ sel sārvu* – The refuge for those who are favourable to remain fearless.
- *yāmudai amudam* – Not just being the refuge, he is also the enjoyable aspect which need not be searched elsewhere. “engaḷ, yām” indicates plural because after [tiruvāimoḻi 2.7](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/04/thiruvaimozhi-2-7-kesavan-thamar/) “*kēsavan tamar*” [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is not alone, he is always in the group of devotees. These are words spoken by āḻvār being together with devotees as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 7.4.11](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/09/thiruvaimozhi-7-4-11-kunram-eduththa/) “*kunṟam edutta pirān adiyārodum onṟi ninṟa satakōpan*” (āḻvār remained united with and having the same nature as the bhāgavatas who are distinguished servitors for kriṣṇa, the great benefactor, who lifted gōvardana).
- *imaiyavar appan en appan* – One who enslaved me just as he enslaved the nityasūris; being the cause for sustenance to nityasūris who have no faults and to me who is the ultimate abode of faults.
- *pongu …* – One who creates, protects and annihilates the three expansive worlds.
- *porundu mū uruvan* – One who is having matching forms for those activities; remains as the antaryāmi of brahmā and creates; remains as the antaryāmi of rudra and annihilates; remaining in his original form \[as viṣṇu\], he protects. Fitting well would indicate that he does not any difference between brahmā et al who are filled with rajas (passion) and tamas (ignorance), and his own divine form.
- *em aruvan* – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) eradicated my fear by revealing to me “the activities of others are at my disposal and not the other way around” and sustained me. As said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 1.9.36 “*utpattistiti nāśānām ahētum hētum īśvaram*” (Surrender unto īśvara who has no separate origin for himself, and who is the cause for creation, sustenance and annihilation), he manifested that everything other than himself acts according to his thoughts and he does not act according to anyone else’s will, and sustained me.
- *sem kayal ugaḷum* – The abode where the fish which are reddish due to their youthful nature, jump around and play joyfully. Unlike [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) who first feared thinking that [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) does not have anyone who cares for him in in previous decad, and became joyful on reciting “*vār kadā aruvi*“, the abode where all entities remain joyful always.
- *tēm paṇai sūḻ* – Saying that the abode is surrounded with water bodies having honey, or abode that is surrounded with fertile fields.
- *angu amarginṟa* – Unlike avatārams where he leaves for his divine abode after the incarnation is completed, he remains here eternally – such an abode.
- *ādiyān* – Saying that one who is the cause for everything or one who is the cause for my sustenance; just as a mother who remains in close proximity of her child, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who looks after my sustenance.
- *allāl yāvar maṟṟu en amar tuṇaiyē* – There is no one else other than emperumān who is a matching companion. Others pretend like companion, but end up strangling my neck, only to lead me to disaster.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.4.3. En amar peruman

*en amar perumān imaiyavar perumān iru nilam idanda em perumān munnai val vinaigaḷ muḻududan māḷa ennai āḷginṟa em perumān ten disaikku aṇi koḷ tiruccengunṟūril tirucciṟṟāṟṟangarai meepāl ninṟa em perumān adi allāl saraṇ ninaippilum piṟidillai enakkē*

**Пословный перевод:**

imaiyavar – for nityasūris; perumān – like being the lord; en – for me; amar perumān – being the matching lord; iru nilam – the great earth; idanda – one who dug out and lifted up (to not get caught in the danger of deluge); emperumān – being my lord; munnai – ancient \[since time immemorial\]; val – strong; vinaigaḷ – sins; muḻudu – all; udan – at once; māḷa – to be destroyed; ennai – me; āḷginṟa – mercifully accepting my service; emperumān – being the one who has greatness; then tisaikku – for southern direction; aṇi – as decoration; koḷ – considered; tiruccengunṟūril – in tiruccengunṟūr; tirucciṟṟāṟṟangarai – on the banks of tirucciṟṟāṟu; mīpāl – on the western direction; ninṟa – in the beauty of standing posture; emperumān – one who enslaved me, his; adi – divine feet; allāl – other than; enakku – my; ninaippilum – even while thinking; piṟidu – anything else; saraṇam – refuge; illai – not there

**Перевод:**

**emperumān is my matching lord just as he remains the lord of nityasūris, dug out and lifted the great earth, having greatness of mercifully accepting my service to at once destroy the ancient, strong sins of mine; he is having a beautiful standing posture in the western direction on the banks of tirucciṟṟāṟu in tiruccengunṟūr which is considered as a decoration for the southern direction, using which he enslaved me; other than such emperumān’s divine feet, even while thinking, I have no other refuge.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the third pāsuram, āḻvār says “I don’t have even in my mind any other refuge than the divine feet of emperumān who is mercifully standing in tiruccengunṟūr after mercifully rescuing earth from the ocean of deluge”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. என் அமர் பெருமான் இமையவர் பெருமான் இரு நிலம் இடந்த எம் பெருமான் முன்னை வல் வினைகள் முழுது உடன் மாள என்னை ஆள்கின்ற எம் பெருமான் தென் திசைக்கு அணி கொள் திருச்செங்குன்றூரில் திருச்சிற்றாற்றங்கரை மீபால் நின்ற எம் பெருமான் அடி அல்லால் சரண் நினைப்பிலும் பிறிது இல்லை எனக்கே en amar perumān imaiyavar perumān iru nilam idanda em perumān munnai val vinaigaḷ muḻududan māḷa ennai āḷginṟa em perumān then disaikku aṇi koḷ tiruccengunṟūril tirucciṟṟāṟṟangarai meepāl ninṟa em perumān adi allāl saraṇ ninaippilum piṟidillai enakkē*

- *en amar perumān imaiyavar perumān* – He is being the lord of nitysūris and my matching lord. One who eliminated my fear and conducted my servitude by manifesting how nityasūris are caring for him.
- *iru nilam …* – One who manifested his ability in protecting the great earth which was consumed by deluge, and enslaved me. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying that [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) manifested his act of rescuing the earth to highlight that everyone is under his protection, and eradicated āḻvār’s fear.
- *munnai …* – The lord who eradicated the ancient, strong sins with their impressions and enslaved me. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying that [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) manifested his beauty, valour etc and enslaved him by eradicating all the fears he previously had. Here valvinai indicates “great loving devotion” since that was the factor which caused āḻvār to fear thinking “what will happen to emperumān who is omnipotent?”.
- *then tisai …* – The abode which is the decoration for the southern direction which was despised by āryas (great personalities) \[due to this region being infested with atheism even back in olden days\].
- *mīpāl ninṟa emperumān* – His presence in the western direction is a cause for greatness as per [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) and the reason for the eradication of fear for him. His supremacy is depending on the direction \[being the lord of paramapadam, the higher world, highlights his supremacy\].
- *adi …* – Even in my thoughts, there is nothing other than his divine feet, which will be considered as refuge.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.
