## 8.4.4. Piridillai enakku

*piṟidillai enakkup periya mūvulagum niṟaiyap pēr uruvamāy nimirnda kuṟiya māṇ emmān kurai kadal kadainda kōla māṇikkam en ammān seṟi kulai vāḻai kamugu tengu aṇi sūḻ tiruccengunṟūr tirucciṟṟāṟu aṟiya meymmaiyē ninṟa em perumān adi iṇai alladu ōr araṇē*

**Пословный перевод:**

periya – having vast space; mū ulagum – three worlds; niṟaiya – to be filled; pēr – big; uruvamāy – being with form; nimirnda – grew; kuṟiya māṇ – as a vāmana brahmacāri (dwarf celibate); emmān – being my lord; kurai – having great noise; kadal – ocean; kadainda – churned; kōlam – attractive; māṇikkam – form which resembles a precious gem; en – (manifesting) for me; ammān – being the lord; seṟi – dense; kulai – branches; vāḻai – banana tree; kamugu – areca tree; tengu – coconut trees; aṇi – rows; sūḻ – surrounded; tiruccengunṟūr – in tiruccengunṟūr; tirucciṟṟāṟu – those who reside in tirucciṟṟāṟu divyadēśam; aṟiya – to know (him) truly; meymmaiyē ninṟa – mercifully standing revealing his true state; emperumān – sarvēśvara’s; adi iṇai – divine feet; alladu – other than; piṟidu – any; enakku – for me; ōr – slightest; araṇ – protector; illai – not there

**Перевод:**

**My lord as vāmana brahmacāri grew to have a big form to fill the three worlds having vast space; being my lord he manifested the precious gem like attractive form with which he churned very noisy ocean; he is mercifully standing in tiruccengunṟūr, tirucciṟṟāṟu divyadēśam which is surrounded with rows of banana trees with dense branches, areca trees and coconut trees, revealing his true state to those who reside in there; other than the divine feet of such sarvēśvara, there is no other slightest protector for me.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fourth pāsuram, āḻvār says “Other than the divine feet of emperumān who is mercifully standing in tiruccengunṟūr after eliminating the dangers of his devotees by defeating mahābali and churning the ocean, there is no other protection for me”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. பிறிது இல்லை எனக்கு பெரிய மூவுலகும் நிறையப் பேர் உருவமாய் நிமிர்ந்த குறிய மாண் எம்மான் குரை கடல் கடைந்த கோல மாணிக்கம் என் அம்மான் செறி குலை வாழை கமுகு தெங்கு அணி சூழ் திருச்செங்குன்றூர்த் திருச்சிற்றாறு அறிய மெய்ம்மையே நின்ற எம் பெருமான் அடி இணை அல்லது ஓர் அரணே piṟidillai enakkup periya mūvulagum niṟaiyap pēr uruvamāy nimirnda kuṟiya māṇ emmān kurai kadal kadainda kōla māṇikkam en ammān seṟi kulai vāḻai kamugu tengu aṇi sūḻ tiruccengunṟūr tirucciṟṟāṟu aṟiya meymmaiyē ninṟa em perumān adi iṇai alladu ōr araṇē*

- *piṟidillai enakku* – There is no protector other than emperumān, for me.
- *periya mū ulagum niṟaiyap pēr uruvamāy nimirnda* – grew up to fill the space available in brahma lōka \[top most layer of an oval shaped universe\]; he grew due to the joy of completing the task that was begun.
- *kuṟiya māṇ emmān* – He enslaved me by manifesting the dwarf form which facilitates growth, and his being an alms-seeker. This is how he eradicated the fear in me, by manifesting the form which was assumed by him to defeat mahābali.
- *kurai kadal kadainda* – He churned the ocean to bring out great noise from there.
- *kōla māṇikkam* – He churned the ocean with a form which resembles an expensive gem.
- *en ammān* – One who enslaved me showing the skill of churning the ocean and his beauty.
- *seṟi kulai vāḻai* – The town which is surrounded with banana trees which are having dense branches, and similar areca and coconut trees. The special feature and fort are not two separate aspects for this town. Due to being well surrounded and having densely branched trees, the enemies cannot enter this town.
- *tirucciṟṟāṟu aṟiya* – For the residents of the town to know that he is sarvēśvara. \[ticciṟṟāṟu implies the residents of the town\] As said in “*manjā: krōśannivat*” (the cot is making noise, implying those who are on the cot, are making noise).
- *meymmaiyē ninṟa emperumān* – My lord who stood there fully revealing himself unlike in śrī rāmāvatāram or kriṣṇāvatāram where he hid his identity as seen in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 120.11 “*ātmānam mānuśam manyē*” (I consider myself as a human being) and in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 5.13.12 “*ahamvō bāndavō jāta:*” (I am your relative) respectively.
- *adi iṇai alladu ōr araṇē* – Nothing else other than his divine feet, is our protection.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.4.5. Allador aranum

*alladu ōr araṇum avanil vēṟu illai adu poruḷ āgilum avanai alladu en āvi amarndu aṇaigillādu ādalāl avan uṟaiginṟa nalla nān maṟaiyōr vēḷviyuḷ madutta naṟum pugai visumbu oḷi maṟaikkum nalla nīḷ mādat tiruccengunṟūril tirucciṟṟāṟu enakku nal araṇē*

**Пословный перевод:**

alladu – any (other than tiruccengunṟūr); ōr araṇum – the refuge (of many arcāvatāra stalams – divyadēśams etc); avanil – other than him; vēṟu – other; illai – not there; adu – that only; poruḷ – is the principle; āgilum – still; avanai – one who is standing (in tiruccengunṟūr); alladu – other than; en – my; āvi – soul; amarndu – fittingly; aṇaigillādu – will not remain; ādalāl – hence; avan – he; uṟaiginṟa – being the eternal abode; nalla – having abundant love; nān maṟaiyōr – caturvēdis (those who are expert in four vēdams); vēḷvi uḷ – in yāgam (sacrifice in fire) etc; madutta – offered through the fire; naṟum – having the fragrance of the havis (offering); pugai – smoke; visumbu – in the sky; oḷi – the light of sun etc; maṟaikkum – to hide; nalla – distinguished; nīḷ – tall; mādam – having mansions; tiruccengunṟūril – in tiruccengunṟūr; tirucciṟṟāṟu – tirucciṟṟāṟu; enakku – for me; nal – fearless; araṇ – refuge

**Перевод:**

**Other than emperumān in tiruccengunṟūr there is no other refuge; this is the only principle. Still, my soul will not fittingly remain anywhere other than him who is standing there. Hence, my fearless refuge is emperumān who is in the divine abode tirucciṟāṟu in tiruccengunṟūr which is having distinguished, tall mansions where the fragrant smoke of the havis offered in the yāgam through fire, is hiding the light of the sun in the sky.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fifth pāsuram, āḻvār says “Though other divyadēśams where he desirously descended are his, and though he himself is mercifully residing there, my heart will not be together with anything other than tiruccengunṟūr and anyone other than the emperumān who is present there”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. அல்லது ஓர் அரணும் அவனில் வேறு இல்லை அது பொருள் ஆகிலும் அவனை அல்லது என் ஆவி அமர்ந்து அணைகில்லாது ஆதலால் அவன் உறைகின்ற நல்ல நான் மறையோர் வேள்வியுள் மடுத்த நறும் புகை விசும்பு ஒளி மறைக்கும் நல்ல நீள் மாடத் திருச்செங்குன்றூரில் திருச்சிற்றாறு எனக்கு நல் அரணே alladu ōr araṇum avanil vēṟu illai adu poruḷ āgilum avanai alladu en āvi amarndu aṇaigillādu ādalāl avan uṟaiginṟa nalla nān maṟaiyōr vēḷviyuḷ madutta naṟum pugai visumbu oḷi maṟaikkum nalla nīḷ mādat tiruccengunṟūril tirucciṟṟāṟu enakku nal araṇē*

- *alladu ōr araṇum avanil vēṟillai* – Other abodes are not different from him \[his abode tiruccengunṟūr tirucciṟṟāṟu\].
- *adu poruḷ* – This is the principle.
- *āgilum* – Still.
- *avanai alladu en āvi amarndu aṇaigillādu* – My heart will not fit well with anyone other than emperumān who is mercifully standing in tiruccengunṟūr; did tiruvadi (hanuman) say in śrī rāmāyaṇam uttara kāṇḍam 40.16 “*bhāvō nānyatra gaccati*” (hanuman says – my mind will not focus on anyone else) because śrīvaikuṇṭanāta is not the lord or it is inapt \[to attain him\]? Similarly, āḻvār is also associating himself only with the emperumān in tiruccengunṟūr. *amarndaṇaigai* – fitting well without any internal anxiety.
- *ādalāl* – Because he is of this nature.
- *avan uṟaiginṟa* – tiruccengunṟūr where he is eternally residing.
- *nalla nānmaṟaiyōr* – brāhmaṇas who are ananyaprayōjanars (those who don’t seek anything other than kainkaryam).
- *vēḷvi uḷ madutta naṟum pugai* – The smoke which carries the fragrance of the havis which was offered in the yāgam (sacrifice). If they are ananyaprayōjanars, why are they engaging in yāgams? It is svayam prayōjanam (for the sake of performing those yāgams as kainkaryam) or they are doing this as abhicāram (exorcising) to destroy the enemies of bhagavān – the brāhmaṇas of this town are similar to emperumānār (emperumānār, while being at tirunārāyaṇapuram, arranged an abhicāra yāgam to destroy kirumi kaṇḍa cōḷa who was causing lot of troubles to bhagavān and bhāgavatas\].
- *visumbu oḷi maṟaikkum* – This is saying, the smoke will hide the luminous objects in the sky such as sun, or saying, the smoke will hide the light in the sky.
- *nalla nīḷ mādam* – No need for any of these karma \[yāgams etc\], the fortified town itself will remain very difficult to penetrate for the enemies.
- *tiruccengunṟūril tirucciṟṟāṟu* – As said in periya tirumoḻi 2.3.1 “*mādamāmayilait tiruvallikkēṇi*” ([tiruvallikkēṇi](http://thiruvallikkeni.koyil.org/) area inside the fortified town of tirumayilai).
- *enakku nal araṇē* – For me who is fearing in unnecessary situation, other than tirucciṟṟāṟu in tiruccengunṟūr, there is no other abode where my fear will be eradicated. tirucciṟṟāṟu is the name of the divyadēśam as well as the river.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.4.6. Enakku nallaranai

*enakku nal araṇai enadu ār uyirai imaiyavar tandai tāy tannait tanakkum tan tanmai aṟivu ariyānait tadam gadal paḷḷi ammānai manakkoḷ sīr mūvāyiravar vaṇ sivanum ayanum tānum oppār vāḻ kanak koḷ tiṇ mādat tiruccengunṟūril tirucciṟṟāṟu adanuḷ kaṇḍēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

enakku – for me; nal – to remain fearless; araṇai – being the refuge; enadu – for me; Ar uyirai – sustenance; imaiyavar – for them; tandai tāy tannai – being the father and mother; tanakkum – even for himself (who is sarvajña (omniscient)); than – his; tanmai – greatness; aṟivu ariyānai – difficult to know; tadam – expansive; kadal – in the ocean; paḷḷi – mercifully resting; ammānai – sarvēśvara; manam – in the heart; koḷ – held; sīr – having qualities of bhagavān; mū āyiravar – three thousand; vaṇ – having wealth of knowledge etc; sivanum – rudra; ayanum – brahmā; tānum – himself (who is sarvēśvara); oppār – to match (each one of them is capable of the creation etc of the universe); vāḻ – being the abode where they have wonderful life (of being engaged in bhagavat anubhavam and not having interest in activities such as creation etc as said in brahma sūtram “jagat vyāpāra varjanam“); ganam – density; koḷ – having; tiṇ – firm; mādam – having mansions; tiruccengunṟūril – in tiruccengunṟūr; tirucciṟṟāṟu adanuḷ – in the distinguished abode of tirucciṟṟāṟu; kaṇḍēn – got to see

**Перевод:**

**I got to see sarvēśvara, who is the refuge for me to remain fearless, who is my sustenance, who is the father and mother for the nityasūris, whose greatness is difficult even for himself to know, and who is mercifully resting in the expansive ocean, who is in the distinguished abode of tirucciṟṟāṟu in ticuccengunṟūr, which has dense, firm mansions, and whose qualities are held in the hearts of three thousand persons who are having wealth of knowledge etc, and are a match to rudra, brahmā and himself and are having wonderful life in this divine abode.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the sixth pāsuram, āḻvār says “emperumān is having such great nature which cannot be understood even by himself, he is all kinds of relatives for nityasūris, he is mercifully resting in tiruppāṟkadal (kśīrābdi – milk ocean) as the refuge for brahmā et al; I got to see such emperumān in tirucciṟṟāṟu in tiruccengunṟūr which is safe, to not fear thinking ‘what will happen to him?’*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. எனக்கு நல் அரணை எனது ஆர் உயிரை இமையவர் தந்தை தாய் தன்னை தனக்கும் தன் தன்மை அறிவு அரியானை தடம் கடல் பள்ளி அம்மானை மனக்கொள் சீர் மூவாயிரவர் வண் சிவனும் அயனும் தானும் ஒப்பார் வாழ் கனக் கொள் திண் மாடத் திருச்செங்குன்றூரில் திருச்சிற்றாறு அதனுள் கண்டேனே enakku nal araṇai enadu Ar uyirai imaiyavar tandai tāy tannait tanakkum than tanmai aṟivu ariyānait tadam gadal paḷḷi ammānai manakkoḷ sīr mūvāyiravar vaṇ sivanum ayanum tānum oppār vāḻ kanak koḷ tiṇ mādat tiruccengunṟūril tirucciṟṟāṟu adanuḷ kaṇḍēnē*

- *enakku nal araṇē* – One who became a refuge which removes the fear for me who fears for matters as explained in taittirīya upaniśat ānandavalli “… *atasō bhayangatō bhavati*” (when he attains [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) with devotion to be without fear for samsāram, he gets rid of fear of samsāram).
- *enadu Ar uyirai* – One who became my sustainer by manifesting his protection.
- *imaiyavar tandai tāy tannai* – One who is all kinds of relatives for the nityasūris who fear for emperumān unnecessarily. It is said in [tiruppallāṇḍu 12](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/11/thiruppallandu-12-pallandu-enru/) “*sūḻndirundu ēttuvar pallāṇḍē*” (In paramapadam, everyone will surround him and perform mangaḷāśāsanam\[wishing well\] for him).
- *tanakkum than tanmai aṟivariyānai* – Even for the naturally omniscient [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), his glories cannot be comprehended. To start with there is no scope for fear; only if one can comprehend someone can they trouble that person.
- *tadam kadal paḷḷi ammānai* – One who mercifully rested in tiruppāṟkadal, for the śvēta dvīpa residents to take shelter of him, to destroy demons such as madu kaitabha et al and to let brahmā et al care for him.
- *manak koḷ mū āyiravar* – There are three thousand brāhmaṇas who behold bhagavān’s qualities in their heart and unnecessarily fear for his safety thinking “what is going to happen to such [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) with great qualities?” Even the brāhmaṇas of this town are of [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s nature; they are similar to the great sage śrī bharatvāja muni as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 127.1 “*vavandēni yatō munim*” (śrī rāma who is having his mind, speech and action in harmony, vorśipped śrī bharatvāja muni). śrī bhatvāja bhagavān was constantly fearing for their \[śrī rāma, sītā and lakśmaṇa\] safety as soon as they left him, until they came back after killing rāvaṇa.
- *vaṇ sivanum ayanum tānum oppār vāḻ* – They are all individually capable of performing the duties of brahmā, rudra and viṣṇu. This is the greatness of these brāhmaṇas over the three main deities.
- *kanak koḷ tiṇ mādam* – Even they are extraneous as the fortified town itself will deter anyone from entering.
- *tirucciṟṟāṟu adanuḷ kaṇḍēnē* – As one’s fear removed inside the place where such fear existed, there is an abode which makes us feel fearless within this samsāram (material realm) – I got to see [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) there.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.4.7. Tiruccengunruril

*tiruccengunṟūril tirucciṟṟāṟu adanuḷ kaṇḍa at tiruvadi enṟumtiruc ceyya kamalak kaṇṇum sevvāyum sevvadiyum seyya kaiyumtiruc ceyya kamala undiyum seyya kamala mārvum seyya udaiyumtiruc ceyya mudiyum āramum padaiyum tigaḻa en sindai uḷānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tiruccengunṟūril – in tiruccengunṟūr; tirucciṟṟāṟu adanuḷ – residing in tirucciṟṟāṟu; kaṇḍa – seen (by me); attiruvadi – that svāmi (lord); seyya – reddish; kamalam – lotus like; tiruk kaṇṇum – divine eyes; sem – reddish; vāyum – divine lips; sem – reddish; adiyum – divine feet; seyya – reddish; kaiyum – divine hands; seyya – reddish; kamalam – having lotus; tiru undiyum – divine navel; seyya – having reddish divine form; kamalai – having lakshmi; mārvum – divine chest; seyya – reddish; udaiyum – divine clothes; seyya – reddish; tiru mudiyum – divine crown; āramum – divine ornaments; padaiyum – divine weapons; tigaḻ – to shine; enṟum – always; en sindai – in my heart; uḷān – became present

**Перевод:**

**That lord I have seen residing in tirucciṟṟāṟu in tiruccengunṟūr has entered my heart, become present there to shine always, with his reddish lotus like divine eyes, reddish divine lips, reddish divine feet, reddish divine hands, reddish lotus on his divine navel, lakshmi having reddish form in his divine chest, reddish clothes, reddish divine crown, divine ornaments and divine weapons.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the seventh pāsuram, āḻvār says “The young covherd with auspicious qualities, who is mercifully standing in tiruccenguinṟūr, has entered my heart with his divine beauty so that I never forget him”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. திருச்செங்குன்றூரில் திருச்சிற்றாறு அதனுள் கண்ட அத் திருவடி என்றும்திருச் செய்ய கமலக் கண்ணும் செவ்வாயும் செவ்வடியும் செய்ய கையும்திருச் செய்ய கமல உந்தியும் செய்ய கமலை மார்பும் செய்ய உடையும்திருச் செய்ய முடியும் ஆரமும் படையும் திகழ என் சிந்தையுளானே tiruccengunṟūril tirucciṟṟāṟu adanuḷ kaṇḍa at tiruvadi enṟumtiruc ceyya kamalak kaṇṇum sevvāyum sevvadiyum seyya kaiyumtiruc ceyya kamala undiyum seyya kamala mārvum seyya udaiyumtiruc ceyya mudiyum āramum padaiyum tigaḻa en sindai uḷānē*

- *tiruccengunṟūril …* – My svāmi who mercifully stood to be seen by me in tirucciṟṟāṟu in tiruccengunṟūr which is a safe abode. tiruvadi – svāmi (lord).
- *tirucceyya kamalak kaṇṇum* –  Divine eyes which are beautiful, reddish and resembling lotus due to its blossomed form, freshness etc.
- *sevvāyum* – The smile which fully purchases the relationship which was attained by the glance.
- *sevvadiyum* – The divine feet at which one falls after being won over by the smile.
- *seyya kaiyum* – The divine hands which lift up and embrace those who fall at his divine feet.
- *tirucceyya kamala undiyum* – The divine navel which is eternally enjoyable for those who embraced him, being the ultimate abode of beauty and which manifests that it is the origin of everything.
- *seyya kamala mārvum* – The divine chest which is reddish due to being the abode of pirātti (śrī mahālakśmi) who is the hold for even those who have no connection with bhagavān. kamala is also recited as kamalai \[since kamalā is a divine name of pirātti, indicating that the chest is pirātti’s abode\].
- *seyya udaiyum* – The divine pītāmbaram (yellow garment) which contrasts his complexion and highlights his masculinity.
- *tirucceyya mudiyum* – The divine crown which is also contrasting the complexion of his divine body and highlights his protection to eradicate the fear of others.
- *āramum* – The divine ornament which matches his vast, divine chest as said in [mūnṟām tiruvandādi 55](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/04/munram-thiruvandhadhi-55/) “*periya varai mārbil pēr āram pūṇḍu*” (wearing a length ornament on his mountain like chest).
- *padaiyum* – The divine weapons which act as weapons in battle and as ornaments during enjoyment.
- *tigaḻa* – Shining as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 38.15 “*śobayan daṇḍakāraṇyam*” (śrī rāma’s divine form’s radiance spread through the forest and lit up the whole forest).
- *enṟum … en sindai uḷānē* – As he eternally resides in my heart, there is no room for fear.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.4.8. Tigala en sindaiyul

*tigaḻa en sindaiuḷ irundānaic ceḻu nilat tēvar nānmaṟaiyōr tisai kai kūppi ēttum tiruccengunṟūril tirucciṟṟāṟṟang karaiyānaip pugar koḷ vānavargaḷ pugalidam dannai asurar van kaiyar vem gūṟṟaip pugaḻumāṟu aṟiyēn porundu mūvulagum padaippodu keduppuk kāppavanē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tigaḻa – to be radiant; en sindai uḷ – in my heart; irundānai – one who resides; seḻu – distinguished; nilat tēvar – being the divine personalities of this material world; nānmaṟaiyōr – experts in four vēdams; tisai – in every direction; kai kūppi – with joined palms; ēttum – to praise; tiruccengunṟūril – in tiruccengunṟūr; tirucciṟṟāṟṟangaraiyānai – residing on the banks of tirucciṟṟāṟu river; pugar – glow; koḷ – having; vānavargaḷ – for dēvas (celestial beings); pugal idam tannai – being the refuge; vankaiyar – very strong; asurar – for demons; vem – cruel; kūṟṟai – being death personified; porundu – inseparable (from him); mū ulagum – three worlds; padaippodu – with creation; keduppuk kāppavanē – having annihilation and protection; pugaḻum āṟu – to praise (in a particular manner); aṟiyēn – I don’t know

**Перевод:**

**emperumān is residing in my heart to be radiant and is residing on the banks of tirucciṟṟāṟu in tiruccengunṟūr, to be praised by the distinguished, divine personalities of this material world in every direction, who are experts in four vēdams; he is the refuge for dēvas who are having glow; he is cruel death personified for the strong demons; I don’t know how to praise such emperumān who is inseparable from the three worlds which are created, annihilated and protected by him.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the eighth pāsuram, āḻvār says “In this manner having immersed in the beauty and qualities of the young covherd I enjoyed, I don’t know how to praise him”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. திகழ என் சிந்தையுள் இருந்தானை செழு நிலத் தேவர் நான்மறையோர் திசை கை கூப்பி ஏத்தும் திருச்செங்குன்றூரில் திருச்சிற்றாற்றங் கரையானை புகர் கொள் வானவர்கள் புகலிடம் தன்னை அசுரர் வன் கையர் வெம் கூற்றை புகழுமாறு அறியேன் பொருந்து மூவுலகும் படைப்பொடு கெடுப்புக் காப்பவனே tigaḻa en sindaiuḷ irundānaic ceḻu nilat tēvar nānmaṟaiyōr tisai kai kūppi ēttum tiruccengunṟūril tirucciṟṟāṟṟang karaiyānaip pugar koḷ vānavargaḷ pugalidam dannai asurar van kaiyar vem gūṟṟaip pugaḻumāṟu aṟiyēn porundu mūvulagum padaippodu keduppuk kāppavanē*

- *tigaḻa en sindai uḷ irundānai* – This is also a reason for āḻvār’s eradication of fear. The presence of emperumān in his heart is like being present in a well fortified area. Fear of emperumān being inside the heart of unfavourable ones is also eradicated; āḻvārs are of the nature to say as in periya tirumoḻi 7.2.7 “*inip pōyp piṟar oruvar vannenjam pukkirukka ottēn vaḷaittu vaittēn*” (I have completely surrounded you so that you cannot go to the hard heart of anyone else now).
- *seḻu nilat tēvar …* – Distinguished vaiṣṇavas who are experts in four vēdams, and who are divine personalities in this material world. emnperumān is residing on the banks of tirucciṟṟāṟu in tiruccengunṟūr, where such vaiṣṇavas are standing in every direction and praising him by joining their palms. Residing in the fortified town which is not accessible for the unfavourable ones.
- *pugar koḷ …* – Being the refuge for dēvas such as brahmā et al, who have the radiance of being the refuge for everyone else, when they are in danger themselves.
- *asurar vankaiyar vem kūṟṟai* – For the demons who have strong arms, he is like cruel death personified, as in *andagan taṇṇīr* (he is so cruel that he makes a cruel destroyer feel like cool water).
- *pugaḻum āṟu aṟiyēn* – There is no shortcoming in him and I don’t know the way in which I can praise him and feel fulfilled; at the same time, I cannot desist from praising him as well;

When asked “so what can be done?” āḻvār says

- *porundu …* – I can only say collectively that he is the one who engages in creation etc of the universe which is subservient to him; I cannot individually highlight each aspect completely. I can only briefly explain about him.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.4.9. Padaippodu keduppu

*padaippodu keduppuk kāppavan pirama param paran sivap pirān avanē idaippukku ōr uruvum oḻivu illai avanē pugaḻ illai yāvaiyum tānē kodaip perum pugaḻār inaiyar tan ānār kūriya viccaiyōdu oḻukkam nadaip pali iyaṟkait tiruccengunṟūril tirucciṟṟāṟu amarnda nādanē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kodai – generosity (of sharing knowledge etc); perum – great; pugaḻār – having fame; enaiyar – many; than ānār – those who are complete in jñāna (knowledge), śakti (power) etc to be said as emperumān himself; kūriya – subtly spread; viccaiyōdu – with scholarship; oḻukkam – practice; nadai – daily routine; pali – bhagavat ārādanam (vorśipping of bhagavān); iyaṟkai – having as nature; tiruccengunṟūril – in tiruccengunṟūr; tirucciṟṟāṟu – in tirucciṟṟāṟu; amarnda – standing; nādan – svāmi (lord); padaippodu keduppuk kāppavan – being the controller of creation, sustenance and annihilation of universe; param paran – as said in “brahmādyavastābhi: aśēśa mūrti:“, being the one who is beyond indra et al who are desired by humans et al, as the para:para (most supreme); piraman – brahmā (who is creator); sivap pirān – rudra, who is also known as īśvara (who is having qualities such as purity etc due to engaging in annihilation, having bhagavān as antarātmā); avanē – to be considered as himself (due to being the prakāri (antarātmā) \[for them\]); idai – in between (these two, brahma and rudra); pukku – entering (as protector); ōr – single; uruvum – entity; oḻivu illai avanē – remaining without leaving any; yāvaiyum – all entities (which are created, sustained and annihilated); tānē – being him (due to being the antarātmā of everything, and having everything as prakāra (form)); pugaḻvu – praising (in the form exaggeration); illai – not there

**Перевод:**

**emperumān is standing in tirucciṟṟāṟu in tiruccengunṟūr accepting the daily tiruvārādanam (worship) of many of those who are as famous as emperumān himself, who are complete in subtly spread jñānam and śakti, who are having scholarship and practice, and all of these as nature; he is the controller of creation, sustenance and annihilation of universe as said in “brahmādyavastābhir aśēśa mūrti:“, being brahmā who is beyond indra et al who are desired by humans et al, as the para:para, and rudra, who is also known as īśvara, and entering in between them as well \[as viṣṇu\] and remaining as every entity not leaving a single entity and all entities being himself; in this, there is no praising (exaggeration).**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the ninth pāsuram, āḻvār says “It is not an exaggeration to say that emperumān who is mercifully standing in tiruccengunṟūr is the one who creates, sustains and annihilates all entities starting from brahmā to an ant; this is the truth”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. படைப்பொடு கெடுப்புக் காப்பவன் பிரம பரம் பரன் சிவப் பிரான் அவனே இடைப்புக்கு ஓர் உருவும் ஒழிவு இல்லை அவனே புகழ்வு இல்லை யாவையும் தானே கொடைப் பெரும் புகழார் இனையர் தன் ஆனார் கூரிய விச்சையோடு ஒழுக்கம் நடைப் பலி இயற்கைத் திருச்செங்குன்றூரில் திருச்சிற்றாறு அமர்ந்த நாதனே padaippodu keduppuk kāppavan pirama param paran sivap pirān avanē idaippukku ōr uruvum oḻivu illai avanē pugaḻ illai yāvaiyum tānē kodaip perum pugaḻār inaiyar than ānār kūriya viccaiyōdu oḻukkam nadaip pali iyaṟkait tiruccengunṟūril tirucciṟṟāṟu amarnda nādanē*

- *padaippodu …* – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is the one who is having sruśti (creation), samhāram  (annihilation) and pālanam (sustenance) at his disposal.
- *pirama param paran* – Just as indra et al are greater than humans et al, brahmā, the foremost dēva (celestial being) is greater than indra et al.
- *sivap pirān* – Similarly the most capable among the dēvas, that is rudra. Both of them are at emperumān’s disposal as well.
- *idaip pukku …* – In between, there is no independent entity; everything will be prakāra (form) and he remains the prakāri (substratum).
- *yāvaiyum tānē* – What is the need to unnecessarily highlight the individual entities? Every cētana (soul) and every acētana (matter) are at his disposal.
- *pugaḻvu illai* – This is not just for artavādam (praising/exaggeration). Even for brahmā et al, such greatness is attributed occasionally and that is merely for upacāram (honour).  But in case of bhagavān, there is no question of exaggeration.

When asked “who is that person who has everything at his disposal?” [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says “*tirucciṟṟāṟu amarnda nādan*” (the lord who is in tirucciṟṟāṟu).

- *kodaip perum pugaḻār* – The residents of this town are famous for their generosity. They are capable of even attracting their enemies by their generosity. dāna (charity) is also one among sāma (talks), dāna (charity), bhēda (tricks), daṇḍa (violence) \[the means to attract/convince others\]. perum pugaḻ (great fame) indicates jñāna dānam (giving knowledge) as said in “*vidyā dānam viśiśyatē*“.
- *inaiyar* – Those who are famous as in “innār” (this person), “innār” (that person) and so on; as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam bāla kāṇḍam 7.15 “*vidēśēśvapi vijñātā:*” (those who are famous even in other countries), since they are famous even in enemy countries, they will think that if they come here, they cannot return safely to their place, and hence will not enter this town. When it is recited as “*ēnaiyar*“, it indicates that there are many such personalities here.
- *than ānār* – Those who are comparable to [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/). Just like him, they will not return without completing the task they take up.
- *kūriya viccaiyōdu oḻukkam* – Good knowledge and, conduct which matches that knowledge. Knowledge to know about enemies and destroy them, and being free from bad conduct which will facilitate their enemies to win over them. To destroy the womb \[of diti\], indra used her misconduct as an opportunity. “*śatru daṇḍassuvruttatā*” (Having good conduct is in itself a punishment for enemies).
- *nadaip pali* – Daily bhagavat samārādanam (worship). nadai – continuous occurrence.
- *pali* – pūjā (worship).
- *iyaṟkai* – Having this as their daily routine.
- *tiruccengunṟūril …* – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is eternally residing in tirucciṟṟāṟu in tiruccengunṟūr is the one who performs creation, sustenance and annihilation.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.4.10. Amarnda nadanai

*amarnda nādanai avar avar āgi avarkkaruḷ aruḷum ammānai amarnda taṇ paḻanat tiruccengunṟūril tirucciṟṟāṟṟang karaiyānai amarnda sīr mūvāyiravar vēdiyargaḷ tambati avani dēvar vāḻvu amarnda māyōnai mukkaṇ ammānai nānmuganai amarndēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

amarnda – being apt (controller of all souls); nādanai – having (natural) lordship; mukkaṇ ammānai – rudra who has three eyes; nānmuganai – brahmā who has four heads/faces; avaravar – those personalities (who pray and acquire their wealth); āgi – becoming one with them (as said in “samētya pratinandya ca“); avarkku – for them; aruḷ – the tools to fulfil their wishes; aruḷum ammānai – being the one who bestows; amarnda – dense; taṇ – invigorating; paḻanam – having water bodies; tiruccengunṟūril – in tiruccengunṟūr; tirucciṟṟāṟṟangaraiyānai – one who is having the banks of tirucciṟṟāṟu as his residence; amarnda – fitting; sīr – ātma guṇams (internal qualities); mū āyiravar – three thousand in count; vēdiyargaḷ – vaidikas (followers of vēdam); tam padi – being the distinguished abode; avani dēvar – bhāgavatas who are bhūsuras (celesital beings of this world); vāḻvu – being the abode having the wealth of bhagavat anubhavam; amarnda – living fittingly (considering their wonderful life as his own); māyōnai – amazing emperumān; amarndēn – I got to fit with him (without any other expectation)

**Перевод:**

**emperumān who is having apt lordship, who is hailed as rudra who has three eyes and brahmā who has four heads/faces, due to being their antarātmā, and also being one with these personalities, being the one who bestows the tools to fulfil their wishes, is residing on the banks of tirucciṟṟāṟu in tiruccengunṟūr which is having dense, invigorating water bodies; this is the distinguished abode for three thousand vaidikas and the abode having the wealth of bhagavat anubhavam for bhāgavatas who are bhūsuras; I got to fit with such amazing emperumān who is living there fittingly. Also explained as emperumān having apt amazing activities for the enjoyment of vaidikas and other divine personalities of this world (bhāgavatas) who live in tirucciṟṟāṟu in tiruccengunṟūr, along with him.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the tenth pāsuram, āḻvār becomes pleased saying “Being sarvēśvara, to be the refuge for all creatures, he mercifully arrived at tiruccengunṟūr and mercifully stood there; I got to enjoy such emperumān”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “Since emperumān is the natural lord, he is having the existence of incidental lords such as brahmā, rudra et al at his disposal and considering their benefit as his own, he offers them his wealth, and is residing in tiruccengunṟūr; I got to unite with such amazing emperumān”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. அமர்ந்த நாதனை அவர் அவர் ஆகி அவர்க்கு அருள் அருளும் அம்மானை அமர்ந்த தண் பழனத் திருச்செங்குன்றூரில் திருச்சிற்றாற்றங் கரையானை அமர்ந்த சீர் மூவாயிரவர் வேதியர்கள் தம்பதி அவனி தேவர் வாழ்வு அமர்ந்த மாயோனை முக்கண் அம்மானை நான்முகனை அமர்ந்தேனே amarnda nādanai avar avar āgi avarkkaruḷ aruḷum ammānai amarnda taṇ paḻanat tiruccengunṟūril tirucciṟṟāṟṟang karaiyānai amarnda sīr mūvāyiravar vēdiyargaḷ tambati avani dēvar vāḻvu amarnda māyōnai mukkaṇ ammānai nānmuganai amarndēnē*

- *amarnda nādanai* – One who remains fitting to be identified as the natural lord of both spiritual and material realms. As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 2.13 “*trailōkyamapi nātēna yēna syānnātavattaram*” (In śrī rāma, all the three worlds have an apt leader) – even if the three worlds are taken together, that which is to be protected will be small and his desire to protect them will be great. *yēna  – nātēna – nātavattaram – syāt*.
- *avaravar āgi* – As seekers approach them, the dēvatās \[rudra, brahmā et al\] would try to be benevolent towards those seekers; similarly, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is benevolent towards them. As the dēvatās would think “we need these”, emperumān too thinks “they need these”. Alternatively – The dēvatās seek to get something; he is seeking to keep granting and their acceptance. They feel joyful on receiving what they desired; emperumān feels joyful in giving.
- *avarkku aruḷ aruḷum* – Granting their wishes as if he himself is benefitting; granting with the same seeking mood of the dēvatās who seek from him; as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 16.27 “… *sa sarvāṇartinō druśtvā samētya pratinandya ca \|\|*” (That śrī rāma, looking at those who came to accept alms from him, welcomed them, gave them joy and united with his friends).
- *ammānai* – sarvēśvara; identifying [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) as pūrṇa (complete) or prāpta (apt).
- *amarnda taṇ paḻanam …* – One who mercifully stood on the banks of tirucciṟṟāṟu in tiruccengunṟūr which is having dense, cool water bodies.
- *amarnda sīr* – Three thousand brāhmaṇas who are having apt qualities. As he is having perfect lordship, they are having apt glories which are highlighted.
- *vēdiyargaḷ tam padi* – Not just the three thousand brāhmaṇas, but this is the abode for all the brāhmaṇas.
- *avani dēvar vāḻvu* – The ultimate destination for the vaiṣṇavas who are bhūsuras.
- *amarnda māyōnai* – sarvēśvara, the amazing lord who is eternally residing in that abode.
- *mukkaṇ ammānai nānmuganai amarndēnē* – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is the controller for the existence of brahmā et al. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is repeating brahmā and rudra several times to highlight emperumān’s lordship and not to miss out on any one of the controlled entities. Alternatively – considering “*amarnda māyōn*“, and since the pāsuram is ending with brahmā and rudra, as those words which rest on the same personality, will point to that underlying personality, it indicates that emperumān is the prakāri (substratum).
- *amarndēnē* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying that he has attained. śrī viṣṇu purāṇam 2.12.38 “*bhūtāni viṣṇu:*” (Every creature is viṣṇu) etc.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.4.11. Tenai nan palai

*tēnai nan pālaik kannalai amudait tirundu ulagu uṇḍa ammānaivānai nānmuganai malarnda taṇ koppūḻ malar misai padaitta māyōnaikōnai vaṇ kurugūr vaṇ satakōpan sonna āyirattuḷ ip pattumvānin mīdēṟṟi aruḷ seydu mudikkum piṟavi mā māyak kūttinaiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tēnai – being honey (which has a combination of all tastes); nan – naturally tasty; pālai – being milk; kannalai – sugarcane (which is sweet in every part); amudai – being nectar (amrutam which brings one’s life back from death); tirundu ulagu – distinguished great world; uṇḍa – protected by consuming (so that it does not get destroyed in deluge); ammānai – being the lord; vānam – resident of higher world; nānmuganai – brahmā; malarnda – blossomed; taṇ – fresh; koppūḻ malar misai – in the lotus flower in the divine navel; padaitta – created; māyōnai – amazing emperumān; kōnai – (due to that) being the natural lord; vaṇ – having unsurpassed wealth; kurugūr – being the leader of tirukkurugūr (āḻvārtirunagari); vaṇ – greatly magnanimous; satakōpan – āḻvār; sonna – mercifully spoke; āyirattuḷ – among the thousand pāsurams; ippattum – this decad; vānin mīdu – on paramapadam; ēṟṟi – will help those practice it to reach; aruḷ – acceptance by bhagavān (of kainkarya sāmrājyam (engaging in constant service)); seydu – facilitate; piṟavi – in the form of this bondage in material realm; mā māyak kūttinai – amazing drama; mudikkum – will finish

**Перевод:**

**emperumān is like honey, naturally tasty milk, sugarcane and nectar; being the lord, he protected the distinguished great world by consuming it; such amazing emperumān created brahmā in the blossomed, fresh lotus flower in his divine navel and is hence the natural lord; the greatly magnanimous āḻvār of tirukkurugūr which is having unsurpassed wealth mercifully spoke about such emperumān in this decad among the thousand pāsurams; this decad will will help those who practice it to reach paramapadam and facilitate acceptance by bhagavān and will finish this amazing drama in the form of this bondage in material realm.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the end, āḻvār explains the creation etc which are the key principle of sāmānādikaraṇyam (emperumān being the subtratum of all), which is explained in this decad and highlights the results for those who learn this prabandam.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*In the end, āḻvār says “for those who practice this decad, this decad itself will take them to paramapaham first and will eliminate this great drama of samsāra (material realm)”. தேனை நன் பாலை கன்னலை அமுதை திருந்து உலகு உண்ட அம்மானைவான நான்முகனை மலர்ந்த தண் கொப்பூழ் மலர் மிசைப் படைத்த மாயோனைகோனை வண் குருகூர் வண் சடகோபன் சொன்ன ஆயிரத்துள் இப் பத்தும்வானின் மீது ஏற்றி அருள் செய்து முடிக்கும் பிறவி மா மாயக் கூத்தினையே tēnai nan pālaik kannalai amudait tirundu ulagu uṇḍa ammānaivānai nānmuganai malarnda taṇ koppūḻ malar misai padaitta māyōnaikōnai vaṇ kurugūr vaṇ satakōpan sonna āyirattuḷ ip pattumvānin mīdēṟṟi aruḷ seydu mudikkum piṟavi mā māyak kūttinaiyē*

- tēnai … – The reasons for [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s fear are highlighted; [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s reliśable nature is that which causes fear in āḻvār. emperumān who is reliśable for me in all manner. He is said as “*sarvarasa:*” (root of all taste).
- *tirundulaguṇḍa …* – The reasons for the removal of fear are explained. The great lord who consumed the organised world to be not destroyed in deluge by placing it in his stomach and protecting it.
- *vānam …* – The amazing lord who created brahmā who is in the sky \[higher world\] in the lotus flower in his \[emperumān’s\] divine navel, which has freshness which is necessary for creation.
- *kōnai* – The natural lord. It is clear that the oneness of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) with brahmā et al which was highlighted previously are not in direct entity itself, but in a cause-effect relationship \[bhagavān being the cause and everyone else being effect\]. Being the companion when needed during dangerous times, being capable of re-creating those vhc were annihilated and being the apt lord.
- *vaṇ kurugūr …* – When a country become leaderless, the prince \[who was previously prisoned for some reason\] will be crowned first and then his shackles will be cut off; similarly, this decad will first grant paramapadam and then eliminate this great drama of samsāra.

In the next article we will enjoy the next decad.

## 8.5 Mayak kutta

## 8.5.1. Mayak kutta

*māyak kūttā! vāmanā! vinaiyēn kaṇṇā! kaṇ kai kāl tūya seyya malargaḷāc cōdic cevvāy mugiḻadā sāyal sāmat tirumēni tan pāsadaiyā tāmarai nīḷ vāsat tadam pōl varuvānē! oru nāḷ kāṇa vārāyē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

māyam – amazing activities that reveal your simplicity; kūttā – having heart-captivating activities; vāmanā – having vāmana (dwarf) form (which is enjoyable as if the huge mēru mountain is shrunk into a small seed); vinaiyēn – for me who is having sin (of not being to enjoy you as I desire); kaṇṇā – being kriṣṇa (who was born in a nearby place, yet remaining far from reach); kaṇ – divine eyes (which acknowledge those who desire to enjoy him); kai – divine hand (which gives refuge); kāl – divine feet (which are approachable through surrender); tūya – pure; seyya – reddish; malargaḷ A – as (blossomed) flowers; sōdi – shining due to gentle smile; sem – reddish; vāy – divine lips; mugiḻadu A – as a bud; sāyal – having radiance; sāmam – blackish; tirumēni – divine form; taṇ – cool; pāsadai A – with dense greenish leaves; tāmarai – having (blossomed) lotus flowers; nīḷ – huge; vāsam – with abundant fragrance; tadam pōl – like a pond (which walks); varuvānē – oh one who is coming!; oru nāḷ – one day; kāṇa – to be seen; vārāy – mercifully come

**Перевод:**

**emperumān is having amazing activities which reveal his simplicity and is having heart-captivating activities in a vāmana form; for me who is having sin, he is being kriṣṇa, who is having divine eyes, divine hand, divine feet, reddish divine lips which are shining due to his gentle smile, as pure reddish flowers; his blackish, divine form which is radiant as a bud; oh one who is coming like an abundantly fragrant pond with huge lotus flowers and is with dense greenish leaves! Mercifully come to be seen one day \[by me\].**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the first pāsuram, āḻvār says “You should appear like a lotus flower filled pond, to remove my fatigue”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. māyak kūttā! vāmanā! vinaiyēn kaṇṇā! kaṇ kai kāl tūya seyya malargaḷāc cōdic cevvāy mugiḻadā sāyal sāmat tirumēni than pāsadaiyā tāmarai nīḷ vāsat tadam pōl varuvānē! oru nāḷ kāṇa vārāyē!*

- *māyak kūttā* – Oh one who is having amazing aspects and heart-captivating activities! To fulfil indra’s wish, oh one who is having heart-captivating activities such as taking birth one day, growing up the same day and going to beg for alms on the same day, going to the sacrificial arena of mahābali and calling him like a child “*māvali*“! His walk appears to [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) like an expert dancer’s dance.
- *vāmanā* – One who begged and who grants whatever one asks him is the one who is making me who is having “seeing him” as the goal, to beg for that and still not granting me my wish.
- *vinaiyēn kaṇṇā* – āḻvār thinks that just as [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) incarnated as vāmana for indra, he incarnated as kriṣṇa for āḻvār. Unlike other incarnations, kriṣṇāvatāram is closer \[to āḻvār\] in proximity by time; hence he is saying “kaṇṇā”. Alternatively, it can be said that āḻvār is saying “kaṇṇā” since this incarnation is by emperumān who is common to all, and kriṣṇa allows himself to be claimed as “mine” by those who desire for him. Here āḻvār is saying “*vinaiyēn*” (sinner), since he appeared just a little after kriṣṇa’s ascending to paramapadam similar to someone trying to put something in his mouth which hits the teeth and falls down.
- *kaṇ kai kāl tūya seyya malargaḷā* – The eyes which establish first relationship with those who approach him, the hand which embraces those who become defeated by his glance, the divine feet at which one will fall after being won over by the embrace, and while being there enjoying those lotus like divine feet and looking up, the divine form which has a contrasting complexion of dark greenish colour.
- *sōdic cevvāy mugiḻadā* – The divine lips which are radiant, which appear like budding. Since bhagavān is explained in cāndōjña upaniśat 3.14 ‘*avākyanādara:’* (does not speak, ignores \[in paramapadam\]), due to his unfathomable nature, his smile will expand and he will not show any further signs; that is why it is explained as budding.
- *sāyal sāmat tirumēn taṇ pāsadaiyā* – Being radiant, dark divine form which appears like cool greenish leaves; As said in varāha purāṇam “*puruśa: puṇḍarīkākśa:*” (the supreme lord is lotus eyed) and in tiruvāimoḻi 9.7.3 “*akkamalattu ilai pōlum*” (like the petals of lotus flower).
- *tāmarai nīḷ vāsat tadam pōl varuvānē* – Like a pond which has blossomed lotus flowers everywhere, being expansive like an ocean filled with a single pond. It appears that such a huge pond filled with fragrance is walking, when he walks as his fragrance comes and hits us. He is said as “*sarvaganda:*” (root of all fragrances).
- *varuvānē* – Oh one who has the nature of coming! [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is highlighting how [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) came to him before, with gratitude.
- *oru nāḷ* – Like those who say “*oru kāl nākku nanaikka*” (let me wet my tongue once).
- *kāṇa* – When he comes, this is the benefit for āḻvār – that is to see him. This constant seeing is the activity even in paramapadam. To get that benefit here.
- *vārāyē* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is of the nature that he will see only when [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) voluntarily comes; as said in muṇḍaka upaniśat 3.2.3 “*tasyaiśa ātmā vivruṇutē tanūmsvām*” (bhagavān shows his true form to those who are dear to him), he considers that approaching bhagavān and seeing him with his own effort is against the true nature of the self.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.5.2. Kana varay

*kāṇa vārāy enṟenṟu kaṇṇum vāyum tuvarndu adiyēn nāṇi nannāttalamandāl irangi oru nāḷ nī andō! kāṇa vārāy karu nāyiṟudikkum karu mā māṇikka nāḷ nal malai pōl sudaṟcōdi mudi sēr senni ammānē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

karu – dark; nāyiṟu – sun; udikkum – has appeared and started; mā – great; karu māṇikkam – being a blue gem; nāḷ – fresh; nal – attractive; malai pōl – like a mountain; sudar – having rays (which spread); sōdi – having radiance; mudi – with hair; sēr – being together; senni – having head; ammānē – oh svāmi!; kāṇa – “(your beauty) to be seen by me; vārāy – you should come”; enṟu enṟu – looking out and calling in this manner repeatedly; kaṇṇum – eyes (which are looking out); vāyum – the mouth (which calls out); tuvarndu – drying up; nāṇi – feeling ashamed (thinking how will his desire be fulfilled); nal – having their wish fulfilled; nādu – in the place; adiyēn – me who has śēśatvam (servitude) as the identity; alamandāl – if I become anguished (in this manner); oru nāḷ – one day; irangi – showing your mercy; nī – you (who is so beautiful to be even separated for a moment); kāṇa – to give me the benefit of seeing you; vārāy – not coming; andō – alas!

**Перевод:**

**Oh svāmi who is having divine head along with radiant hair having rays like a great blue-gem like fresh, attractive mountain having a dark sun appearing and starting from it! After looking out and calling out repeatedly saying “you should come to be seen by me”, my eyes and mouth dried up, and feeling ashamed in this place where everyone is having his/her wish fulfilled, even if I who have śēśatvam as my identity, become anguished,  you are not coming one day and showing your mercy to give me the benefit of seeing you. Alas!**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the second pāsuram, āḻvār says “You should mercifully appear with your beautiful hair, to remove my faitgue”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. kāṇa vārāy enṟenṟu kaṇṇum vāyum tuvarndu adiyēn nāṇi nannāttalamandāl irangi oru nāḷ nī andō! kāṇa vārāy karu nāyiṟudikkum karu mā māṇikka nāḷ nal malai pōl sudaṟcōdi mudi sēr senni ammānē!*

- *kāṇa vārāy enṟu enṟu* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is not of the nature to remain peaceful if [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) does not appear after calling out once saying “*kāṇa vārāy*“; he will repeatedly say “*kāṇa vārāy, kāṇa vārāy*“.
- *kāṇṇum vāyum tuvarndu* – Since āḻvār does not know as to from where emperumān will come, he looks at every direction and gets his eyes to dry up. He has even crossed the stage as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 7.2.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/07/thiruvaimozhi-7-2-1-kangulum-pagalum/) “*kaṇṇa nīr kaigaḷāl iṟaikkum*” (removing the tears with her hands). His mouth too dried up by calling out repeatedly.
- *adiyēn nāṇi* – I who have the relationship with [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) to feel ashamed for emperumān’s defects considering them to be our own, felt ashamed. Feeling ashamed thinking as to what the townspeople will say about him \[for not coming\]; alternate explanation – instead of calling out to seek other benefits, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) called out to see [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), which is the proper attitude; for such state of āḻvār, emperumān’s act was good \[i.e. viparīta lakśaṇā (sarcasm) – he acted improperly by not showing himself\] – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) thought about that and felt ashamed.
- *nal nādu* – Three meanings.
   - viparīta lakśaṇā (sarcasm) – the abode which is filled with endless sorrow.
   - the abode where one lives joyfully due to worldly enjoyment
   - piḷḷān explains “this is the abode where one can attain [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) and enjoy; if not why would they \[[āḻvārs](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/azhwars/) and other devotees\] called for him.
- *alamandāl* – If I become anguished.
- *irangi* – Even if you don’t have interest, should you not show your mercy seeing other’s suffering? Don’t you even have the compassion which the riśis \[like vālmeeki\] had?
- *oru nāḷ* – Am I asking you to come for many days?
- *nī* – You who are having distinguished nature to be constantly seen.
- *andō* – You neither understand your greatness nor my suffering!
- *kāṇa vārāy* – Am I calling you seeking other benefits?
- *karu nāyiṟu udikkum* – rising of the dark sun.
- *karu māṇikka nāḷ nal malai pōl* – The mountain from where such sun rises from. Like a mountain made of bluish expensive gem.
- *nāḷ nal malai* – Like a “nātpū” (fresh flower), fresh, attractive mountain. Should be recited as “*karu māṇikkam – nan malai mēl – karu nāyiṟu udikkum – poḻudu – pōl – mudi sēr senni ammān*“. nāḷ – poḻudu (time).
- *sudar sōdi mudi* – Very radiant hair. In line with the simile “*karu nāyiṟu udikkum*“, mudi here means hair \[generally, mudi means crown\].
- *sēr senni* – The divine form on which the hair rests, appears like a mountain of gem.
- *ammānē* – Oh sarvēśvara! When a samsāri \[bound soul\] becomes a muktātmā \[liberated soul\], to remove his sorrow, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) manifests his divine hair to him \[muktātmā\]. It is said “*kēśava: klēśa nāśana:*” (kēśava is the one who destroys the sorrows).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.5.3. Mudi ser senni amma!

*mudi sēr senni ammā! nin moy pūndāmat taṇ tuḻāy kadi sēr kaṇṇip perumānē! enṟenṟēngi aḻudakkāl padi sēr magarak kuḻaigaḷum pavaḷa vāyum nāl tōḷum tudi sēr idaiyum amaindadu ōr tū nīr mugil pōl tōnṟāyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

mudi – with the divine crown (which reveals his supremacy due to his being the lord of paramapadam (spiritual realm) and samsāram (material realm)); sēr – well fitting; senni – having divine head; ammā – being the lord; nin – your distinguished; moy – dense; pū – attractive; dāmam – radiant; taṇ – cool; tuḻāy – tiruttuḻāy (tuḷasi); kadi sēr – very fragrant; kaṇṇi – wearing garland; perumānē – Oh greatest of all!; enṟenṟu – saying so; ēngi – sob; aḻudakkāl – while crying; padi – for the form; sēr – matching; magarak kuḻaigaḷum – divine ear rings; pavaḷam – coral like; vāyum – divine lips; nāl – four; tōḷum – divine shoulders; tudi sēr – like a damaru/udukkai (hour-glass shaped drum, where the middle portion is thin); idaiyum – having waist; amaindadu – present; tū – pure; nīr – being complete in simplicity; ōr – being an unseen; mugil pōl – like a cloud (to manifest your benefactorśip); tōnṟāy – you should appear

**Перевод:**

**As I am sobbing and crying, saying “Oh emperumān who is greatest of all, being the lord with the divine crown which is well fitting your divine head, who is wearing distinguished, dense, attractive, radiant, cool, very fragrant tiruttuḻāy garland!” you should appear like a pure, unseen cloud with the form that has matching divine ear rings, coral like divine lips, four divine shoulders, waist which resembles a damaru/udukkai.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the third pāsuram, āḻvār says “You should come and appear in front of me like an invigorating, distinguished, pure rain cloud, to eliminate my sorrow”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. mudi sēr senni ammā! nin moy pūndāmat taṇ tuḻāy kadi sēr kaṇṇip perumānē! enṟenṟēngi aḻudakkāl padi sēr magarak kuḻaigaḷum pavaḷa vāyum nāl tōḷum tudi sēr idaiyum amaindadu ōr tū nīr mugil pōl tōnṟāyē*

- *mudi sēr senni ammā* – Oh sarvēśvara who is having divine head which is with a divine crown which reveals your supremacy over everyone else!
- *nin moy pūm dāmat taṇ tuḻāy* – Oh sarvēśvara who is wearing an invigorating tuḷasi garland, which is densely strung together, which is heart-captivating, radiant, and having its fragrance increasing, as days pass!
- *enṟu enṟu* – Are you remaining inactive thinking that I will recite this once and leave it?
- *ēngi aḻudakkāl* – As I sob and cry. As you hear my helplessness in my cry, should you not come and immediately present yourself?
- *padi sēr magarak kuḻaigaḷum* – Fitting as part of the divine form, or fitting well on the divine form; also explained as naturally fitting, and fitting on the divine form. It is said in mudal tiruvandādi 85 “*padi kaṇḍaṟidiyē*” (Have you not seen and enjoyed his divine form?) \[this explains that padi refers to form\].
- *pavaḷa vāyum* – The divine lips which manifest the relationship/attachment.
- *nāl tōḷum* – The four shoulders which resemble well-branched kalpa taru (celestial wish-fulfilling tree), which are available to embrace us.
- *tudi …* – His form appears like a cloud which is having damaru like waist. Since these attributes are not present in a cloud, this is called abhūtōpamā (a non-existing simile).
- *tū nīr mugil* – Cloud which has absorbed pure water. You should present yourself so that all your internal coolness and compassion are visible in your form itself.

## 8.5.4. Tu nir mugil

*tū nīr mugil pōl tōnṟum nin sudar koḷ vadivum kanivāyum tēnīr kamalak kaṇgaḷum vanden sindai niṟaindavā! mānīr veḷḷi malai tan mēl vaṇ kār neela mugil pōlat tūnīrk kadaluḷ tuyilvānē! endāy! solla māttēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

mā – vast; nīr – in the ocean (which is present); veḷḷi malai than mēl – atop a silver mountain; vaṇ – magnanimous; kār – during rainy season; neela mugil pōl – like a dark cloud; tū – white; nīr – having fluid; kadal uḷ – in kśīrārṇava (milk ocean); tuyilvān – one who mercifully rests; endāy – oh my lord!; tū – pure; nīr – filled with water; mugil pōl – like a cloud; tōnṟum – shining; nin – your; sudar – radiance; koḷ – having; vadivum – form; kani – like a ripened fruit; vāyum – divine lips; tēn nīr – having honey; kamalam – like a lotus; kaṇgaḷum – divine eyes; vandu – coming (here); en – my; sindai – heart; niṟaindavā – the manner in which they filled; solla māttēn – I cannot express (in words)

**Перевод:**

**Oh my lord who is mercifully resting in kśīrārṇava having whitish fluid, like a magnanimous dark cloud during the rainy season atop a silver mountain in the vast ocean! I cannot express the manner in which your divine form which is having the shining radiance of cloud filled with pure water, your ripened fruit like divine lips, your divine eyes like a lotus having honey, are all coming and filling my heart. tēnīrk kamalam also implies lotus having the \[sweet\] nature of honey. With the example of veḷḷi malai (silver mountain), the serpent mattress can be inferred. ōr it can also be considered as the risen milk ocean as said in the best, easily approachable, silver mountain.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fourth pāsuram, āḻvār presents to emperumān saying “I am unable to completely express how your beauty enters in my heart, fills it and torments me”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. tū nīr mugil pōl tōnṟum nin sudar koḷ vadivum kanivāyum tēnīr kamalak kaṇgaḷum vanden sindai niṟaindavā! mānīr veḷḷi malai than mēl vaṇ kār neela mugil pōlat tūnīrk kadaluḷ tuyilvānē! endāy! solla māttēnē*

- *tū nīr mugil pōl tōnṟum* – emperumān appears like a rain cloud which will remove the fatigue as soon as it is seen.
- *nin sudar koḷ vadivum* – Since emperumān’s divine form is made of pure goodness having perfect radiance, a cloud which is made of worldly matter cannot be cited as example. He is as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.7.4](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/09/thiruvaimozhi-1-7-4-mayarvu-ara/) “*oṇ sudark kaṟṟaiyē*” (a radiant beam of rays).
- *kani vāyum* – His mouth appears like a well ripened fruit which will tempt one to consume it immediately upon seeing it.
- *tē nīrk kamalak kaṇgaḷum* – Eyes which resemble lotus which has honey as its water. With this, the freshness is thought about. Also said as the eyes which are having the nature of honey. That is, his eyes are available to be drunk by our eyes.
- *vandu en sindai niṟaindavā* – āḻvār is saying “I cannot express how emperumān entered and filled my heart”. Worldly matters can be enjoyed but will be forgotten; matters relating to emperumān will remain etched in the heart.
- *mā nīr veḷḷi malai than mēl* – In the vast water body, on top of a silver mountain.
- *vaṇ kār neela mugil pōla* – Like a magnanimous, darkiś, loaded cloud floating \[on that mountain\]. ōr like a magnanimous, rainy season cloud floating \[on that mountain\].
- *tū nīrk kadal pōl tuyilvānē* – Oh one who is mercifully resting on tiruvanantāḻvān (ādiśēśa) in the pure water! As *veḷḷi malai* (silver mountain) is highlighted in the example, it can be inferred in the actual object as well.
- *endāy* – The apt relationship which makes us not to leave him even if he does not have any of the distinguished aspects explained previously.
- *endāy – vandu en sindai niṟandavā – solla māttēn* – His shining form in my heart is causing sorrow and I cannot express it. In separation, thinking about his qualities will lead to sorrow only. His reclining on the pure ocean indicates that emperumān arrived and reclined there ahead of time, for those \[dēvas\] who don’t even have the desire to see him.

## 8.5.5. Solla matten

*solla māttēn adiyēn un tuḷangu sōdit tiruppādam ellaiyil sīr iḷa nāyiṟu iraṇḍu pōl ennuḷḷavā! allal ennum iruḷ sērdaṟku upāyam ennē? āḻi sūḻ mallai jñālamuḻuduṇḍa mānīrk koṇḍal vaṇṇanē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

āḻi – by ocean; sūḻ – surrounded; malllal – big; jñālam – universe; muḻudu – fully; uṇḍa – placing in stomach (so that it is not consumed by the deluge); mā – filled; nīr – having water; koṇḍal – like a dark cloud; vaṇṇanē – oh one who is having the form!; adiyēn – I who am enslaved (by your help when needed); solla māttēn – I cannot express in words; un – your; tuḷangu – shining; sōdi – having radiance; tiruppādam – divine feet; ellai il – boundless; sīr – having beauty; iḷa nāyiṟu – youthful suns (which are seen early in the morning); iraṇḍu pōl – like two of them; en – my; uḷḷa A – remained inside me; allal – as sorrow; ennum – to be said; iruḷ – darkness (of forgetfulness); sērdaṟku – to attain; upāyam – means; ennē – what? (you should tell)

**Перевод:**

**Oh one who is having a form which is like a dark cloud filled with water, who fully placed the big universe surrounded by ocean, in your stomach! I who am enslaved by you cannot express in words \[the reason why you are shining in me\]; your divine feet having shining radiance remained in me like two youthful suns having boundless beauty; what means is there to attain the darkness to be said as sorrow? While the divine feet are shining, since āḻvār does not get to enjoy them physically, he prefers forgetting them. Since, the previous pāsurams and the subsequent pāsurams in this decad reveal his sorrow, this pāsuram should also be seen in this context only.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fifth pāsuram, āḻvār says “Your beauty remains in my heart constantly reminding me \[about it\] and tormenting me; you should tell me a way to forget it”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. solla māttēn adiyēn un tuḷangu sōdit tiruppādam ellaiyil sīr iḷa nāyiṟu iraṇḍu pōl ennuḷḷavā! allal ennum iruḷ sērdaṟku upāyam ennē? āḻi sūḻ mallai jñālamuḻuduṇḍa mānīrk koṇḍal vaṇṇanē!*

- *solla māttēn* – I cannot express in words the manner in which you remain in my heart and torment me.
- *adiyēn* – Due to our relationship \[you being the master and I being the servitor\] I cannot avoid you.
- *un tuḷangu …* – What is that \[I cannot avoid\]? Your divine feet with shining radiance.
- *ellai …* – They are tormenting me by remaining in my heart like two youthful suns with boundless beauty. Here they are said to be youthful suns, since they can be seen without straining the eyes, and they are in the starting stage of their tormenting.
- *iḷa nāyiṟu* – As they torment me, their youthfulness keep increasing.
- *(en uḷḷavā solla māttēn* – I cannot express in words, how they do it)
- *allal …* – bhattar would mercifully explain “When you hide yourself and make it difficult for me to see you, worldly people will ignorantly say ‘he is inferior’; how can I get such ignorance?”, since āḻvār would want to forget emperumān and survive. ammāḷ would explain it as “While the divine feet are shining in my heart, is there any means to acquire ignorance which leads to sorrow?” If there is such an option, I can also be engaged in worldly matters like the worldly people.
- *āḻi …* – Oh great benefactor who placed the great universe surrounded by the ocean, in your stomach and protected it from the deluge! āḻvār is saying “emperumān is having a form which resembles a cloud which absorbed a huge singular ocean”.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.5.6. Kondal vanna!

*koṇḍal vaṇṇā! kudak kūttā! vinaiyēn kaṇṇā! kaṇṇā! en aṇḍa vāṇā! enṟu ennai āḷak kūppittaḻaittakkāl viṇ tan mēl tān maṇ mēl tān viri nīrk kadal tān maṟṟut tān toṇḍanēn un kaḻal kāṇa oru nāḷ vandu tōnṟāyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

koṇḍal – like a cloud (which removes fatigue); vaṇṇā – oh one who is having form!; kudak kūttā – Oh one who dances with pots (which is heart-captivating)!; vinaiyēn – for me who is having the sin (to be unable to see and enjoy that); kaṇṇā – Oh one who is the vision!; kaṇṇā – Oh one who descended as kriṣṇa (to manifest your obedience towards the devotees)!; en – to be my attainable goal; aṇḍa vāṇā – Oh one who remains as the controller of paramapadam!; enṟu – in this manner (mentioning your basic nature, repeatedly); ennai – me; āḷa – to enslave; kūppittu – calling out (due to my great sorrow/urge); aḻaittakkāl – When I call; viṇ than mēl tān – being in paramapadam; maṇ mēl tān – or being in this world (as incarnations and arcā vigrahams); viri nīr kadal tān – or being in kśīrārṇavam (as viṣṇu, who is the source of the incarnations); maṟṟut tān – or being in my heart (as antaryāmi); toṇḍanēn – me who is greatly desirous; un – your; kaḻal – divine feet; kāṇa – to see; oru nāḷ – one day; vandu – come; tōnṟāy – and be present

**Перевод:**

**When I call out for you to enslave me in this manner saying “Oh one who is having cloud like form! Oh one who dances with pots! Oh one who is the vision for me, who is having sin! Oh one who descended as kriṣṇa to be my attainable goal! Oh one who remains as the controller of paramapadam!” one day you come and be present for me who is greatly desirous to see your divine feet,  being in paramapadam or being in this world or being in kśīrārṇavam or being in my heart.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.Highlights from nanjīyar‘s introduction In the sixth pāsuram, āḻvār says “As I think about your beauty etc and call out saying ‘I want to see you’, you should mercifully come and appear somewhere for my upliftment”.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. koṇḍal vaṇṇā! kudak kūttā! vinaiyēn kaṇṇā! kaṇṇā! en aṇḍa vāṇā! enṟu ennai āḷak kūppittaḻaittakkāl viṇ than mēl tān maṇ mēl tān viri nīrk kadal tān maṟṟut tān toṇḍanēn un kaḻal kāṇa oru nāḷ vandu tōnṟāyē*

- *koṇḍal vaṇṇā* – Oh one who has a form which will remove the fatigue of those who see you!
- *kudak kūttā* – Oh one who has heart-captivating activities!
- *vinaiyēn kaṇṇā kaṇṇā* – Oh kriṣṇa who is my vision!
- *vinaiyēn* – I have committed sin to lose my vision.
- *en aṇḍa vāṇā enṟu* – Oh one who became the lord of the universe to accept me! āḻvār says “Just as his being with auspicious qualities is for the sake of his devotees, his having wealth of these spiritual and material realms is for me”.
- *ennai āḷa* –  Am I calling you for any worldly benefits? Am I not calling you for engaging me in eternal service?
- *kūppittu aḻaittakkāl* – Are you delaying your arrival thinking I can wait to attain you in due course of time? Are you thinking “let me go in due course of time” and remaining there even after hearing my sorrowful cry?
- *viṇ than mēl tān* – You can appear in the sky where the water-filled cloud is moving around.
- *viṇ than mēl tān* – You can appear in front of me manifesting your presence as in paramapadam.
- *maṇ mēl tān* – You can appear by incarnating \[in this world\].
- *viri nīr kadal tān* – You can appear in front of me manifesting your merciful reclining posture in kśīrābdi. (milky ocean)
- *maṟṟut tān* – You can appear in front of me as you appeared from within the pillar (as narasimha) or as you appeared for the elephant, gajēndrāḻvān.
- *toṇḍanēn* – I who am desirous in serving your divine feet.
- *un kaḻal kāṇa* – To see your divine feet which sustain me.
- *oru nāḷ vandu tōnṟāyē* – Am I insisting that you do this (showing me your divine feet) for many days? To sustain me, you should mercifully appear one day.

## 8.5.7. Vandu tonray

*vandu tōnṟāy anṟēl un vaiyam tāya malar adik kīḻ mundi vandu yān niṟpa mugappē kūvip paṇi koḷḷāy sendaṇ kamalak kaṇ kai kāl sivanda vāy ōr nāyiṟu andam illāk kadir parappi alarndadokkum ammānē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

sem – reddish; taṇ – cool; kamalam – like a lotus; kaṇ – eye; kai – hand; kāl – foot; sivanda – reddish; vāy – having mouth; ōr – a; karu nāyiṟu – dark bluish sun; andam – end; illā – not having; kadir – rays; parappi – spreading; alarndadu okkum – resembling well expanded; ammānē – Oh lord (who has physical beauty)!; vandu – coming (with that beauty); tōnṟāy – you should appear; anṟēl – otherwise; vaiyam – the whole universe; tāya – united (without any limitation); malar – like a blossomed lotus; adik kīḻ – under the divine feet; mundi – coming forward; yān – I; vandu – come; niṟpa – to stand (by sustaining myself); un – your; mugappē – in divine presence; kūvi – calling; paṇi – service; koḷḷāy – should mercifully engage me

**Перевод:**

**Oh lord who are resembling a well expanded dark bluish sun which is having reddish, cool lotus like eye, hand, foot and reddish mouth, which has endless rays which are spreading! You should come and appear in front of me; otherwise, you should call me to make me come forward and stand under your blossomed lotus like divine feet which united with the whole universe and mercifully engage me in service in your divine presence.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the seventh pāsuram, āḻvār says “Either you should come here and bless me or if there is a reason for your non-arrival, you should take me there and engage me in service”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. vandu tōnṟāy anṟēl un vaiyam tāya malar adik kīḻ mundi vandu yān niṟpa mugappē kūvip paṇi koḷḷāy sendaṇ kamalak kaṇ kai kāl sivanda vāy ōr nāyiṟu andam illāk kadir parappi alarndadokkum ammānē!*

- *vandu tōnṟāy* – You should appear in my sight. āḻvār is calling emperumān who is praised as in periya tirumoḻi 8.5.1 “*tandai kālil vilangaṟa vandu tōnṟiya tōnṟal*” (the lord who appeared to break the shackles of his father), to come and appear in front of him.
- *anṟēl* – If you don’t see my suffering and your compassion, and present yourself to me. Also explained as, if you don’t see my inferiority and your supremacy, and present yourself to me.
- *un vaiyam tāya malar adi* – The divine feet which did not discriminate between vaśiśta (great scholar) and caṇḍāḷa (dog-eater).
- *malar adi* – With your fresh flower like divine feet, you measured the world which has forests and rough terrains.
- *malar adik kīḻ mundi vandu yān niṟpa* – To make me come forward and stand in front of the infinitely enjoyable divine feet.
- *mugappē* – in your vicinity.
- *kūvip paṇi koḷḷāy* – You feed me and engage me in service. As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 15.7 “*kriyatāmiti mām vada*” (lakśmaṇa to śrī rāma – order me in what should be done), you should mercifully engage me in service in your vicinity. I am not like śrī bharatāḻvān who could sustain himself by meditating upon emperumān’s qualities; you should engage me who is like iḷaiya perumāḷ (lakśmaṇa) who said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 53.31 “*muhūrtam api jeevāva: jalān matsyā vivōtrutau”* (if we separate from you, we will die like a fish out of the water), in service. I will not remain wherever I am placed saying as in [tiruvāimoḻi 3.3.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/08/thiruvaimozhi-3-3-1-ozhivil-kalam/) “*vaḻuvilā adimai seyya vēṇḍum*” (I should perform continuous service) and in [tiruvāimoḻi 2.3.7](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/02/thiruvaimozhi-2-3-7-munnal-yazh/) “*ninnalāl ilēn*” (I have no existence without you). Does āḻvār not say as in [tiruvāimoḻi 8.1.9](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/02/thiruvaimozhi-8-1-9-yanum-nidhane/) “*nanṟum anjuvan naragam nān adaidal*” (I am very scared in reaching the samsāram).
- *sem taṇ …* – You should appear like a dark bluish sun which is having reddish, cool lotus like eye, hand, foot and reddish mouth, which has endless rays unlike being limited by thousand rays, which are spreading.
- *ammānē* – Either you should see your supremacy and take me to paramapadam and engage me in service there, or if you don’t desire to be finished, you should come here and accept my service.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.
