## 8.5.8. Okkum amman

*okkum ammān uruvam enṟu uḷḷam kuḻaindu nāṇāḷum tokka mēgap pal kuḻāngaḷ kāṇum tōṟum tolaivan nān takka aivar tamakkāy anṟu īraimpadinmar tāḷ sāyap pukka nal tērt tanip pāgā! vārāy iduvō poruttamē?*

**Пословный перевод:**

“ammān – svāmy’s (lord); uruvam – physical beauty; okkum – is apt”; enṟu – saying this; uḷḷam – heart; kuḻaindu – being broken; nāḷ nāḷum – everyday; tokka – gathered; mēgam – clouds’; pal – many; kuḻāngaḷ – groups; kāṇum tōṟum – whenever I see; nān – I; tolaivan – will remain anguished; takka – having takkōrmai (justice, honesty) (to have you as all types of relatives); aivar tamakku – for the five pāṇḍavas; āy – being their servitor; anṟu – on that day (when mahābhārata war was waged); īr aim padinmar – \[2 \* 5 \* 10 = 100\] the hundred persons (enemies); tāḷ sāya – to be uprooted; pukka – entered (into the armies); nal – best (due to your presence); tēr – for the chariot; tanip pāgā – Oh distinguished charioteer (where the owner of the chariot can hide behind your back)!; vārāy – you are not coming (with that beauty); iduvō – is this; poruttam – your matching conduct (towards your devotee’s matters)?

**Перевод:**

**Saying “lord’s physical beauty is apt”, having my heart broken, I will remain anguished everyday, whenever I see the groups of gathered clouds; oh distinguished charioteer who entered the armies and rode the best chariot to uproot the hundred persons by being the servitor for the five pāṇḍavas who were having honesty! You are not coming ; does this match your conduct?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the eighth pāsuram, āḻvār says “While I am suffering seeing the cloud which is similar to you, you are not coming and mercifully uniting with me; is this your nature?”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. okkum ammān uruvam enṟu uḷḷam kuḻaindu nāṇāḷum tokka mēgap pal kuḻāngaḷ kāṇum tōṟum tolaivan nān takka aivar tamakkāy anṟu īraimpadinmar tāḷ sāyap pukka nal tērt tanip pāgā! vārāy iduvō poruttamē?*

- *okkum ammān uruvam enṟu* – While knowing well “sarvēśvara is distinct from all other entities”, [āḻvārs](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/azhwars/) would consider clouds which are made of smoke, light, water and air as said in mēga sandēśam 1.5 “*dūma jyōti salilam marutām sannipāda: kva mēga:*“, to be similar to [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/).
- *uḷḷam kuḻaindu* – This is not just extenal, the heart itself is broken.
- *nāḷ nāḷum* – This broken state is not occassional, but occurring continuously without break.
- *tokka mēgap pal kuḻāngaḷ* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) will not become broken when he sees part of the clouds; but will become broken everytime he sees groups of gathered clouds.
- *nāḷ nāḷum tolaivan* – I am neither dead, nor able to survive.
- *nān* – The sight of the clouds will bring peace for the townspeople. \[But for me, it brings anguish\]
- *takka aivar* – For which sight of clouds, did the pāṇḍavas become weak, to be protected by [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)? The five pāṇḍavas who have the honesty and goodness to say “our clan should survive, please give five villages, that is sufficient for us”.
- *tamakkāy* – To be a servitor for arjuna to order kriṣṇa saying as in [śrī bhagavat gītā 1.21](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/1-21/) “*ratam stāpaya*” (Position the chariot).
- *anṟu* – The day when they remained isolated.
- *īraimpadinmar* – To uproot the hundred brothers who said “we will not survive along with the relatives \[namely pāṇḍavas\]”.
- *pukka* – to enter into the battle field.
- *nal tēr* – The chariot which became greatly celebrated due to having [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) as the sāraty (charioteer).
- *tanip pāgā* – Oh one who handled it on your own! They did not see the raty (arjuna who is seated in the chariot); they are only seeing the sāraty who carefully engaged arjuna who said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 1.32](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/1-32/) “*na kānkśē vijayam kriṣṇa*” (Oh kriṣṇa! I don’t desire victory).
- *vārāy* – Could you who positioned the chariot amidst the two armies when arjuna said as in [śrī bhagavat gītā 1.21](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/1-21/) ”  *sēnayōrubhayōr madyē ratam stāpaya mē’cyuta*” (Oh acyuta! position my chariot in between the line ups of both armies), not conduct your chariot amidst the clouds? Would you only help if there are five persons suffering and hundred persons tormenting them? Would you not help if I am alone and tormented by countless groups of clouds?
- *iduvō poruttam* – Is this how you aptly mingled with devotees previously? Were your acts, such as going as a messenger, being a charioteer, vowing to not take up arms and breaking that vow and changing day into night, all false? [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying that vyāsa who said “*nārāyaṇa katām imām*” (I am going to recite the stories of nārāyaṇa) accepted some remuneration and sang about [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/). āḻvār is saying “unless emperumān helps me, all these are not true”.
- *vārāy* – Should I suffer all of these? Can you not show your face?

## 8.5.9. Iduvo poruttam?

*iduvō poruttam? min āḻip padaiyāy! ēṟum irunjiṟaip puḷ aduvē kodiyā uyarttānē! enṟenṟēngi aḻudakkāl eduvē āgak karudungol? immā jñālam poṟai tīrppān maduvār sōlai uttara maduraip piṟanda māyanē*

**Пословный перевод:**

“min – having radiance as ornament; āḻi – tiruvāḻi (divine chakra); padaiyāy – Oh one who is having as weapon!; ēṟum – as vehicle; iru – huge; siṟai – having wings; puḷ aduvē – periya tiruvadi (garudāḻvār) himself; kodi A – as flag; uyarttānē – one who hoisted!; iduvō – is this; poruttam – befitting (even with them)?”; enṟu enṟu – saying repeatedly in this manner; ēngi – sobbing; aḻudakkāl – while crying; i – this; mā jñālam – the vast earth’s; poṟai – burden; tīppān – to eliminate; madu – honey; vār – flowing; sōlai – having garden; uttara madurai – in vadamadurai (śrī maturā of the north); piṟanda – descended manifesting his sarvēśvaratva (supremacy); māyan – amazing personality; eduvēyāga – in what way; karudum – is he mercifully thinking?

**Перевод:**

**As I am saying repeatedly “Oh one who is having divine chakra which has radiance as its ornament, as a weapon! Oh one who hoisted periya tiruvadi, who is your vehicle with huge wings, as your flag! Is this befitting?” and while sobbing and crying, emperumān, the amazing personality, descended into śrī maturā which is having garden with flowing honey, to eliminate the burden of the vast earth. In what way is emperumān mercifully thinking?”**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the ninth pāsuram, āḻvār says “kriṣṇa who has amazing qualities, mercifully descended to śrī maturā to eliminate the sufferings of everyone fully; what is such kriṣṇa mercifully thinking to do for me who is suffering after desiring to see him?”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. iduvō poruttam? min āḻip padaiyāy! ēṟum irunjiṟaip puḷ aduvē kodiyā uyarttānē! enṟenṟēngi aḻudakkāl eduvē āgak karudungol? immā jñālam poṟai tīrppān maduvār sōlai uttara maduraip piṟanda māyanē*

- *iduvō poruttam* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) seeing that [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) has still not showed up even after calling out in this manner, rolls his eyes and again says “*iduvō poruttam*” (is this befitting your nature?)
- *min āḻip padaiyāy* – Oh one who is having the divine chakra which destroys the enemies of the devotees and which resembles lightning in a cloud! Could you not eliminate my hurdles using that divine chakra?
- *ēṟum …* – Oh one who hoisted on his own vehicle, the garuda bird which has rising wings as his flag! Is he not the one who engages his devotees in all types of services?
- *enṟu enṟu ēngi aḻudakkāl* – if I keep sobbing and crying throughout this pāsuram
- *eduvēyāgak karudum kol* -Is he thinking to present himself for this crying out? ōr is he thinking that I will keep crying out? Alternative explanation – How is his divine heart feeling hurt for this crying out?
- *immā jñālam poṟai tīrppān* – To eliminate the burden of this vast earth.
- *madu vār sōlai* – Having garden which has flowing honey.
- *uttara madurai* – Oh one who took birth amidst the enemies such as kamsa et al in śrī maturā of the north! Oh one who remained in the womb and took birth as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam bāla kāṇḍam 18.10 “*tataśca dvādaśē māsē*” (subsequently, on the twelfth month of caitra, śrī rāma took birth) instead of āvirbhāvam (appearing spontaneously)! [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) has the nature of descending as one amongst the humans to eliminate the enemies of his devotees having *bhūbhāra nirasanam* (eliminating the burden of the earth) as the reason. What is such emperumān thinking for my crying out?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.5.10. Piranda maya

*piṟanda māyā! bhāratam poruda māyā! nī innē siṟanda kāl tī nīr vān maṇ piṟavumāya perumānē kaṟanda pāl uḷ neyyē pōl ivaṟṟuḷ engum kaṇḍu koḷ iṟandu ninṟa perumāyā! unnai engē kāṇgēnē?*

**Пословный перевод:**

piṟanda – incarnating with his true nature as said in “ajō’pisann”; māyā – being an amazing person; bhāratam – while engaging in mahābhārata war; poruda māyā – Oh one who conducted it with amazing activities (such as taking up arms after vowing not to do so, changing day to night etc)!; nī – you; innē – while being easily approachable; siṟanda – having the greatness (due to being the cause of the universe); kāl tī nīr vān maṇ – five elements; piṟavum – other worldly objects; āya – having as prakāra (form); perumānē – being greater than all; kaṟanda – extracted; pāl – milk; uḷ – inside; neyyē pōl – like ghee; kaṇḍu koḷ – to see; iṟandu – to be difficult; ivaṟṟuḷ – in all these objects; engum – everywhere; ninṟa – one who remains; perumāyā – Oh greatly amazing one!; unnai – you (who are beyond senses in this manner); engē – where; kāṇgēn – will I see?

**Перевод:**

**Oh one who is an amazing person incarnating with your true nature as said in “ajō’pisann“, who conducted the mahābhārata war with amazing activities! You are having greatness while being easily approachable, being greater than all, having the five great elements and other worldly objects as your prakāra (form); Oh greatly amazing one who remains everywhere, yet is difficult to be seen in all these objects like ghee inside extracted milk! Where will I see you?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the tenth pāsuram, āḻvār says “Where will I see you who are amazing to be present in close proximity yet disallowing me from seeing you?”*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Tenth pāsuram. āḻvār says “I am subsequent to your incarnations and you as antaryāmi cannot be seen by my external eyes; where will I see you?” piṟanda māyā! bhāratam poruda māyā! nī innē siṟanda kāl tī nīr vān maṇ piṟavumāya perumānē kaṟanda pāl uḷ neyyē pōl ivaṟṟuḷ engum kaṇḍu koḷ iṟandu ninṟa perumāyā! unnai engē kāṇgēnē?*

- *piṟanda māyā* – Oh amazing lord who being akarmavaśya (being uncontrolled by karma), incarnated as a human with the original spiritual, divine form!
- *bhāratam poruda māyā* – This battle is as amazing as his birth! It is the amazing aspect where satya pratijña (one who stands by his vows) became asatya pratijña (one who ignored his own vows). He vowed not to take up arms but ended up doing so \[momentarily against bhīśma\] and he turned day into night.
- *nī innē* – While you remain sulabha (easily approachable).
- *siṟanda …* – For the five causal elements such as prutivi (earth) etc.
- *piṟavum* – for the effect of the five elements such as dēva etc \[variegated forms\].
- *āya perumānē* – Oh sarvēśvara who is the ātmā \[of all such entities\]! The speciality of air \[siṟanda kāl\] is, while it is one among the causal elements, it is also that which sustains all beings.
- *kaṟanda …* – Oh greatly amazing lord who is present in every entity yet invisible to the external eyes just as the invisible ghee which is present in the visible milk! It is said in brahmavit upaniśat “*gavāmanēka varṇānām kśīrasyatvēka varṇatā \| kśīravat paśyati jñānam linginas tu gavāmyatā \|\| grutamiva payasi nigūdam bhūtē bhūtē ca vasati vijñānam \| satatammantē tavyam manasā mandā na bhūtēna \|\| sarva bhūtāti vāsamayat bhūtēśu ca vasatyapi \| sarvānugrāhakatvēna tadasmayaham vāsudēva iti*” (The milk of different coloured cows remain the same; similarly ātmā which is made of jñānam should be seen; bodily differences such as dēva etc are similar to \[differently coloured\] cows; just as ghee remains hidden in the milk, bhagavān is hidden inside all entities; one should churn with the mortar named mind; that which is the abode of all entities and that which resides in every entity, is the one which gives the strength for all entities; I am that vāsudēva \[who gives strength to every entity\]).
- *kaṟanda pāl* – The ghee which appears over time and due to the churning, will not be visible while extracting the milk \[from the cow\]; [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying “unless one has the samskāram (effect) of having totally surrendered to [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), one cannot easily see him”.
- *unnai engē kāṇgēnē* – To see you in paramapadam, my bodily connection should be eliminated; I am subsequent to your incarnations; I am not attaining arcāvatāra [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) as I desire; your being antaryāmi is invisible for my external eyes; now, I can only perish with this craving to see you.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.5.11. Enge kangen!

*engē kāṇgēn! īn tuḻāy ammān tannai yān? enṟenṟu angē tāḻnda soṟkaḷāl andaṇ kurugūrc catakōpan sengēḻ sonna āyirattuḷ ivaiyum pattum vallārgaḷ ingē kāṇa ippiṟappē magiḻvar elliyum kālaiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

“In – ultimately enjoyable; tuḻāy – wearing tiruttuḻāy (tuḷasi) garland; ammān tannai – sarvēśvara; yān – I (who have great urge/sorrow); engē – where; kāṇgēn – will see”; enṟu enṟu – saying this repeatedly; angē – towards his enjoyability and lordship; tāḻnda – loving; soṟkaḷāl – with the words; am – attractive; taṇ – invigorating; kurugūr – leader of āḻvārtirunagari; satakōpan – āḻvār; sengēḻ – with honesty; sonna – mercifully spoke; āyirattuḷ – among the thousand pāsurams; ivaiyum pattum – this decad; vallārgaḷ – those who can recite with true emotions; ingē – in this world itself; kāṇa – to be seen (by all); ippiṟappē – in this birth itself; elliyum kālai – without a break, in night and day; magiḻvar – will acquire the joy caused by experiencing bhagavān

**Перевод:**

**āḻvār, the leader of attractive, invigorating āḻvārtirunagari was repeatedly saying “where will I see sarvēśvara who is wearing ultimately enjoyable tuḷasi garland?” mercifully spoke with loving words towards his enjoyability and lordship, with honesty, this decad among the thousand pāsurams. Those who can recite it with true emotions will acquire the joy caused by experiencing bhagavān, without a break, in night and day, in this world itself to be seen by all, in this birth itself.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the end, āḻvār says that those who are expert in this decad, without going through the suffering of āḻvār, will attain emperumān in this world, in this birth itself and will remain eternally joyful.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. engē kāṇgēn! In tuḻāy ammān tannai yān? enṟenṟu angē tāḻnda soṟkaḷāl andaṇ kurugūrc catakōpan sengēḻ sonna āyirattuḷ ivaiyum pattum vallārgaḷ ingē kāṇa ippiṟappē magiḻvar elliyum kālaiyē*

- *In tuḻāy ammān tannai engē kāṇgēn* – Where will I who cannot sustain without seeing him who is wearing the divine tuḷasi garland which highlights his opulence, see him?
- *enṟu enṟu* – I who did not attain your various forms such as paratva \[in paramapadam\] etc, saying repeatedly. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is not of the nature to say once and remain satisfied feeling “I have stated my desire”; he will repeat until his desire is fulfilled.
- *angē tāḻnda soṟkaḷāl* – The words which were engrossed in his shoulders and the garland on his shoulders, and his lordship.
- *am taṇ kurugūrc catakōpan* – As said by bhīśma in mahābhāratam “*upatiśtantumām sarvē vyādaya: …*” (let all diseases inflict me; let me reach viṣṇu’s paramapadam having cleared all my debts), [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) who tolerated such suffering – this is āḷavandār’s explanation.
- *sengēḻ sonna …* – This decad among the thousand pāsurams which were spoken with mind, speech and body in harmony.
- *vallārgaḷ* – those who can recite.
- *ingē …* – In this world itself, in this current birth itself, they will become joyful due to experiencing bhagavān continuously in day and night without any break; īśvara who did not present himself for [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) when āḻvār called him saying in [tiruvāimoḻi 8.5.6](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/03/thiruvaimozhi-8-5-6-kondal-vanna/) “*āḷak kūppittaḻaittakkāl*” (when I call out for you to enslave me) and was blamed for that, eliminated that blame by quickly presenting himself for those who recite this decad; this is similar to a husband who had a fight with his wife, would praise the children to get her attention.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.6 Elliyum kalaiyum

## 8.6.1. Elliyum kalaiyum

*elliyum kālaiyum tannai ninaindeḻa nalla aruḷgaḷ namakkē tandaruḷ seyvān alliy andaṇṇanduḻāy mudi appan ūr selvargaḷ vāḻum tirukkadittānamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

elliyum kālaiyum – without any distinction between night and day; tannai – him (who is the benefactor); ninaindu – remembering; eḻa – to be uplifted; nalla – distinguished; aruḷgaḷ – unconditional mercies (for arrival in close proximity, entering in the heart, eliminating hurdles, giving experience etc); namakkē – exclusively for us; tandu – granting; aruḷ – mercy; seyvān – bestow; alli – having flowers; am – attractive; taṇṇam – cool; tuḻāy – being decorated with tiruttuḻāy (tuḷasi) garland; mudi – having divine crown; appan – lord, the benefactor’s; Ur – (distinguished) abode; selvargaḷ – bhāgavatas (who have the wealth of kainkaryam to bhagavān); vāḻum – (due to continuous experience, joyfully) living; tirukkadittānam – tirukkadittānam

**Перевод:**

**emperumān exclusively grants us his unconditional mercies to uplift me by making me remember him without any distinction between night and day and further bestows his mercy; the abode of such lord, the benefactor who has divine crown decorated with attractive, cool tiruttuḻāy garland with flowers, is tirukkadittānam where bhāgavatas are living.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the first pāsuram, āḻvār says “sarvēśvara (lord of all) is the one who would mercifully eliminate my sufferings; his abode is tirukkadittānam”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*In the first pāsuram, āḻvār says “The abode of sarvaśēśi (lord of all) who has come to do unsurpassed favours, is tirukkadittānam”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. elliyum kālaiyum tannai ninaindeḻa nalla aruḷgaḷ namakkē tandaruḷ seyvān alliy andaṇṇanduḻāy mudi appan Ur selvargaḷ vāḻum tirukkadittānamē*

- *elliyum kālaiyum* – To be uplifted always thinking without any distinction between night and day about emperumān, who is the benefactor.
- *nalla aruḷgaḷ* – The mercy which was granted by emperumān for his own sake, without seeing my faults and his omniscience. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is not just thinking that emperumān is granting this mercy to eliminate the suffering he went through in the previous decad “*māyakkūttā”*.
- *namakkē tandu aruḷ seyvān* – āḻvār thinks that even nityasūris have not received such benediction from emperumān as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 7.10.5](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/11/thiruvaimozhi-7-10-5-malaradip-podhugal/) “*palar adiyār munbaruḷiya*” (granting his grace in the presence of many servitors).
- *alli am taṇṇam tuḻāy mudi* – emperumān manifested the form which was desired by [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) in the previous decad as in tiruvāimoḻi 8.5.3 “*moy pūndāmat taṇ tuḻāy kadi sēr kaṇṇip perumānē!*” (Oh [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is greatest of all, being the lord with the divine crown which is well fitting your head, who is wearing distinguished, dense, attractive, radiant, cool, very fragrant tiruttuḻāy garland!).
- *Ur* – Since such benefactor is residing there, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying that tirukkadittānam is the ultimate destination for us.
- *selvargaḷ vāḻum* – Those who constantly enjoy [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) unlike [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) who had “māyakkūttā” (suffering in separation) and “*elliyum kālaiyum*” (joy in union); as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam bāla kāṇḍam 18.28 “*lakśmaṇō lakśmī sampanna:*” (lakśmaṇa who is endowed with wealth of kainkaryam), these are the ones who have the wealth of kainkaryam.
- *elliyum …* – this is the abode of appan (benefactor); tirukkadittānam is the abode of those who have the wealth of kainkaryam; the benefactor who is wearing a crown decorated with cool, attractive tuḷasi, will grant us distinguished mercies and shower his grace upon us.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.6.2. Tirukkadittanamum

*tirukkadittānamum ennudaic cindaiyum orukkaduttu uḷḷē uṟaiyum pirān kaṇḍīr serukkaduttu anṟu tigaitta arakkararai urukkeda vāḷi poḻinda oruvanē*

**Пословный перевод:**

seru – in war; kaduttu – with great pride; anṟu – that day (when they committed offense to cause anger in śrī rāma like fire rising out of ash); tigaitta – bewildered (thinking who will win); arakkar – rākśasas (demons); uru – bodies; keda – to become broken and destroyed; vāḷi – rain of arrows; poḻinda – poured; oruvan kaṇḍīr – he is the lone warrior; tirukkadittānamum – in tiurukkadittānam tiruppati (divyadēśam (divine abode)); ennudai sindaiyum – my heart; orukkaduttu – holding together; uḷḷē – in both of them; uṟaiyum – living; pirān – great benefactor

**Перевод:**

**The lone warrior who poured a rain of arrows to break the bodies and destroy the bewildered rākśasas who were in the war with great pride on that day, is holding tirukkadittānam tiruppati and my heart together and is the great benefactor who is living in both of them. Alternative explanation – he is holding on to both tirukkadittānam and my heart but living in me.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the second pāsuram, āḻvār says “emperumān himself eliminated the hurdles which were stopping his arrival towards me and showed same love towards tirukkadittānam and my heart, and resided in me”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. tirukkadittānamum ennudaic cindaiyum orukkaduttu uḷḷē uṟaiyum pirān kaṇḍīr serukkaduttu anṟu tigaitta arakkararai urukkeda vāḷi poḻinda oruvanē*

- *orukkaduttu* – To treat equally. Desiring for tirukkadittānam and my heart equally.
- *uḷḷē uṟaiyum* – He is eternally residing in my heart.

When asked “What happened to the hurdles?” āḻvār says “they met with the same fate of the rākśasas”.

- *serukkaduttu* – Having the urge for the war.
- *anṟu* – The day when rāvaṇa said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 36-11 “*na namēyam*” (I will not worship him).
- *tigaitta arakkarai* – The foolish rākśasas who thought they could win against cakravartit tirumagan (śrī rāma, the son of emperor daśarata).
- *uruk keda* – as said in in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 94.22 ‘*cinnam binnam śarair dagdam’* (cut, blown away, burnt and destroyed by the arrows of śrī rāma).
- *vāḷi poḻinda* – as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 94.18 “*śaravarśam vavarśaha*” (did he not pour down a rain of arrows?)
- *oruvan* – emperumān who remained as the lone warrior.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.6.3. Oruvar iruvar

*oruvar iruvar ōr mūvar ena ninṟu uruvu karandu uḷḷundōṟum tittippān tiruvamar mārvan tirukkadittānattai maruvi uṟaiginṟa māyap pirānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

oruvar – (first) as one; iruvar – (subsequently) as two; mūvar ena – (further) to be said as three; ninṟu – standing; ōr – distinguished; uruvu – form; karandu – being beyond sense perception (to not take aim at); tiru – lakshmi; amar mārvan – having in his divine chest; tirukkadittānattai – tirukkadittānam; maruvi – fitting well; uṟaiginṟa – one who resides eternally; māyap pirān – being amazing benefactor; uḷḷum tōṟum – everytime he is thought about; tittippān – he feels sweet

**Перевод:**

**emperumān (śrī rāma) stood with one, two and subsequently three distinguished forms and remained beyond sense perception, having lakshmi in his divine chest, resides eternally in tirukkadittānam, fitting well there. ēverytime such amazing benefactor is thought of, it feels sweet.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the third pāsuram,  āḻvār says “emperumān who descended to tirukkadittānam along with pirātti, and resides their fittingly well, is greatly attached to me and is very sweet everytime I think about him”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. oruvar iruvar ōr mūvar ena ninṟu uruvu karandu uḷḷundōṟum tittippān tiruvamar mārvan tirukkadittānattai maruvi uṟaiginṟa māyap pirānē*

- *oruvar …* – When asked “how did śrī rāma shoot his arrows?” [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says “this is how he did it”.
- *oruvar iruvar ōr mūvar ena ninṟu uruvu karandu* – He first appeared as one, and then as two and then as three and then moved so swiftly to be beyond sense perception. This is to be recited along with the previous pāsuram as in “*oruvar iruvar ōr mūvar ena ninṟu uruvu karandu – serukkaduttanṟu tigaitta arakkarai urukkeda vāḷi poḻinda oruvan avan – tirukkadittānamum ennudaic cindaiyum orukkaduttu uḷḷē uṟaiyum pirān kaṇḍīr*“.
- *tiru amar mārvan* – He came along with pirātti who says as in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 116-45 “*nakaścin nāparādyati*” (there is none who has not committed a wrongful deed).
- *tiru amar mārvan tirukkadittānattai maruvi uṟaiginṟa māyap pirān uḷḷum tōṟum tittippān* – Whenever I think of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is having the divine chest where periya pirātti eternally resides, who fittingly resides in tirukkadittānam and who shows amazing love towards me, he feels sweet as a new person every time.

## 8.6.4. Mayap piran

*māyap pirān ena val vinai māyndaṟa nēsattināl nenjam nādu kudi koṇḍān tēsattamarar tirukkadittānattai vāsap poḻil mannu kōyil koṇḍānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tēsam – those who have (unsurpassed) tējas (glow); amarar – destination for the nityasūris (eternal residents of paramapadam); vāsam – very fragrant; poḻil mannu – having garden; tirukkadittānattai – tirukkadittānam; kōyil – as temple/abode; koṇḍān – one who had; māyap pirān – amazing benefactor; ena – my; val – strong; vinai – sins; māyndu aṟa – to destroy; nēsattināl – due to great attachment towards me; nenjam – my heart; nādu – the vast place; kudi – as residence (for him); koṇḍān – acquired

**Перевод:**

**The amazing benefactor who had tirukkadittānam which is having a very fragrant garden and is the destination for nityasūris who have unsurpassed glow, as his abode, acquired the vast place of my heart as his residence, to destroy my strong sins, due to great attachment towards me.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fourth pāsuram, āḻvār says “emperumān is having tirukkadittānam as his day time residence only, and is having my heart as his most beloved and mercifully resides in there eternally”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. māyap pirān ena val vinai māyndaṟa nēsattināl nenjam nādu kudi koṇḍān tēsattamarar tirukkadittānattai vāsap poḻil mannu kōyil koṇḍānē*

- *māyap pirān* – The benefactor who has amazing qualities and activities.
- *ena val vinai māyndu aṟa* – To destroy all my sufferings in separation from him; to eliminate all the sufferings which I underwent in māyakkūttā saying in [tiruvāimoḻi 8.5.2](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/03/thiruvaimozhi-8-5-2-kana-varay/) “*kāṇa vārāy enṟu kaṇṇum vāyum tuvarndu*” (saying “you should come to be seen by me”, my eyes and mouth dried up) with its trace,
- *nēsattināl* – due to the attachment he had towards me.
- *nenjam nādu* – \[How is it that the miniscule heart became so vast?\] [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) made [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s divine heart to be like paramapadam \[which is three times bigger than this material realm\], by his union and separation.
- *kudi koṇḍān* – He eternally resided there along with his paraphernalia; as said in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 5.2.10 “*aravattamaḷiyinōdum …*” (emperumān arrived with his serpent mattress, śrī mahālakśmi et al into my heart).
- *tēsattu amarar tirukkadittānattai* – tirukkadittānam, the ultimate destination for nityasūris who have the glow due to their eternal experiencing of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/).
- *vāsap poḻil mannu* – Having fragrant garden. To be recited as “*tēsattamarar tirukkadittānattai kōyil koṇḍān, nēsattināl nenjam nādu kudi koṇḍān*“.

## 8.6.5. Koyil kondan

*kōyil koṇḍān tan tirukkadittānattaik kōyil koṇḍān adanōdum en nenjagam kōyil koḷ deyvam ellām toḻa vaigundam kōyil koṇḍa kudak kūtta ammānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kōyil koḷ – having distinguished tower; deyvam ellām – nityasūris; toḻa – to worship; vaigundam – paramapadam (the ultimate destination); kōyil – as abode; koṇḍa – one who has; kudak kūtta – (having the heart-captivating activity) of kūdak kūttu (dancing with pots); ammān – (kriṣṇa, the) svāmy (lord); tirukkadittānattai – tirukkadittānam; than kōyil – as his distinguished abode; koṇḍān – accepting it; adanōdum – along with that; en – my; nenjam – heart too; kōyil – as (his) abode; koṇḍān – accepted

**Перевод:**

**emperumān who is in paramapadam where nityasūris who have distinguished towers worship him, who is the lord having kudak kūttu, accepted tirukkadittānam as his distinguished abode; along with that, he accepted my heart too as his abode.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fifth pāsuram, āḻvār says “due to the great love towards me, emperumān mercifully entered my heart too, along with being present in tirukkadittānam”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. kōyil koṇḍān than tirukkadittānattaik kōyil koṇḍān adanōdum en nenjagam kōyil koḷ deyvam ellām toḻa vaigundam kōyil koṇḍa kudak kūtta ammānē*

- *kōyil koṇḍān …* – He accepted tirukkadittānam as his distinguished abode.
- *kōyil …* – Thinking “*seruppu vaittut tiruvadi toḻuvāraip pōlē āga oṇṇādu*” (one cannot peacefully worship [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), having his / her sandals outside the temple), along with tirukkadittānam, he mercifully entered my heart too \[here it implies that emperumān cannot remain peaceful by just staying in tirukkadittānam as he is looking to enter [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s heart mainly\].
- *kōyil koḷ …* – Every one of them \[nityasūris\] will have his/her own abodes/temples – tiruvadi (garudāḻvār), tiruvanantāḻvān (ādiśēśa), sēnai mudaliyār (viśvasēnar) and so on; sarvēśvara who has Śrīvaikuṇṭha as his abode/temple to be vorśipped by all of them. Such sarvēśvaran incarnated as kriṣṇa and danced with pots; to eliminate that fatigue, he accepted tirukkadittānam as his abode; along with that, he accepted my heart as his abode; as said in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 5.2.10 “*aḻagiya pāṟkadalōdum*” (along with the milk ocean), since his presence in tirukkadittānam was to attain me; just as one discards the means after attaining the goal, since [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) attained me by being in that abode, he entered in my heart along with that abode.

## 8.6.6. Kutta amman

*kūtta ammān kodiyēn idar muṟṟavum māytta ammān madusūda amman uṟai pūtta poḻil taṇ tirukkadittānattai ētta nillā kuṟikkoṇmin idarē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kūtta – with heart-captivating activities; ammān – being the lord (of the universe); kodiyēn – me who is having cruelty (of calling him repeatedly saying “kāṇa vēṇum“); idar – sorrow in heart; māytta – eliminated; ammān – one who enslaved; madusūdan – eliminated just as he eliminated madu \[demon\]; ammān – lord; uṟai – abode where he resides; pūtta – with abundance of flowers; poḻil – having garden; taṇ – cool; tirukkadittānattai – tirukkadittānam; ētta – as we praise; idar – sorrows; muṟṟavum – fully; nillā – destroyed; kuṟik koṇmin – keep (this) in your mind

**Перевод:**

**sarvēśvaran, being the lord with heart-captivating activities eliminated the sorrow in my heart and enslaved me who is having cruelty; he is the lord who eliminated the sorrows just as he eliminated madu and who resides in cool tirukkadittānam having garden with abundance of flowers; as we praise that abode, our sorrows will be fully destroyed; keep this in your mind.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the sixth pāsuram, āḻvār joyfully tells others “Praise tirukkadittānam which is the eternal abode of sarvēśvara who eliminated my suffering of not seeing him, just as he eliminated madu, kaitaba et al; all your sorrows will be gone; keep this in your mind”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. kūtta ammān kodiyēn idar muṟṟavum māytta ammān madusūda amman uṟai pūtta poḻil taṇ tirukkadittānattai ētta nillā kuṟikkoṇmin idarē*

- *kūtta ammān* – sarvēśvaran, who has heart-captivating activities.
- kodiyēn – my; me who is a great sinner.
- *idar muṟṟavum māytta ammān* – my lord who eliminated all the sorrows in separation of him, along with the trace.
- *madusūdan …* – the abode where sarvēśvara who has the quality of eliminating enemies, resides.
- *pūtta poḻil* – Due to his eternal presence, the garden remains with blossomed flowers always. Only if his merciful glance stops, will the flowers stop blossoming.
- *taṇ tirukkadittānattai* – Invigorating tirukkadittānam.
- *ētta nillā idar* – As one engages in praising emperumān, the sorrows will think “this is not the place for us” and will flee without making any noise.
- *kuṟik koṇmin* – Keep this in your mind, instead of thinking that this is just said for the assembly.

## 8.6.7. Konmin idar keda

*koṇmin idar keda uḷḷattuk kōvindan maṇ viṇ muḻudum aḷanda oṇ tāmarai maṇṇavar tām toḻa vānavar tām vandu naṇṇu tirukkadittāna nagarē*

**Пословный перевод:**

gōvindan – emperumān who is having the radiance of being sarvasulabha (easily approachable by all), his; maṇ – earth; viṇ – higher world; muḻudum – without leaving anything; aḷanda – measured and accepted; oṇ – greatly enjoyable; tāmarai – divine lotus feet; maṇṇavar – residents of earth; tām – considering to be exclusively enjoyable for them; toḻa – as they worship; vānavar – the residents of paramapadam (who eternally enjoy emperumān); tām – them too; vandu – arriving here (to enjoy his great simplicity); naṇṇu – to attain him; tirukkadittānam – tirukkadittānam; nagarai – town; idar – sorrows; keda – to eliminate; uḷḷattu – in the heart; koṇmin – try to keep

**Перевод:**

**The greatly enjoyable divine lotus feet of emperumān measured and accepted his own earth and higher world without leaving anything; as the residents of this world worship them considering them to be exclusively enjoyable for them and as the residents of paramapadam too arrive here to attain him at tirukkadittānam, you try to keep that town in your heart to eliminate all your sorrows.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the seventh pāsuram, āḻvār says “You think about tirukkadittānam in your heart to get rid of all your sorrows”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Seventh pāsuram. You need not even praise tirukkadittānam to eliminate your sorrows; just thinking about it is sufficient – says āḻvār. koṇmin idar keda uḷḷattuk kōvindan maṇ viṇ muḻudum aḷanda oṇ tāmarai maṇṇavar tām toḻa vānavar tām vandu naṇṇu tirukkadittāna nagarē*

- *koḷmin …* – Think about tirukkadittānam in your heart; that will eliminate all your sorrows.
- *gōvindan* – sarvasulabhan’s.
- *maṇ viṇ muḻudum aḷanda oṇ tāmarai*  – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) measured and accepted the earth and the sky with a lotus flower.
- *maṇṇavar tām toḻa* – to be vorśipped by the residents of earth, who don’t know to distinguish between left and right hands; as paramapadam remains exclusively for nityasūris \[and muktātmās\], divya dēśams \[which are said in tamiḻ as ugandaruḷina nilam\] remain exclusively for samsāris (worldly people).
- *vānavar …* – thinking about [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s simplicity of manifesting himself for the sake of samsāris, nityasūris too approach tirukkadittānam – keep it in your heart/mind to eliminate your sorrows fully. The residents of samsāram (material realm) go to paramapadam to enjoy his supremacy; the residents of paramapadam (spiritual realm) come to samsāram to enjoy his simplicity.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.6.8. Tana nagargal

*tāna nagargaḷ talaic ciṟandengengum vānin nilam kadal muṟṟum em māyaṟkē āna idattum en nenjum tirukkadit tāna nagarum tanadāyap padiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vān – paramapadam; i – this; nilam – earth; kadal – kśīrārṇava (milk ocean); engengum – in all places; tānam – residing place; nagargaḷ – towns; muṟṟum – all; talai – great; siṟandu – having glories; em māyaṟkē – for my amazing lord; Ana idattum – though they are there; en – my; nenjum – heart; tirukkadittānam nagarum – this town tirukkadittānam (where he first came before arriving in my heart); tana – for him; tāyam – hereditary; padiyē – remain as distinguished abodes

**Перевод:**

**Though there are many towns as residing places in many distinguished abodes with great glories such as paramapadam, this earth, kśīrārṇavam, for my amazing lord, my heart and this town tirukkadittānam remain as distinguished, hereditary abodes.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the eighth pāsuram, āḻvār says “While emperumān has many distinguished abodes, he is considering my heart and tirukkadittānam as hereditary/native abode and shows great affection”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. tāna nagargaḷ talaic ciṟandengengum vānin nilam kadal muṟṟum em māyaṟkē Ana idattum en nenjum tirukkadit tāna nagarum tanadāyap padiyē*

- *tāna nagar …* – In the higher worlds, in earth, in the ocean and wherever we see, he has many distinguished towns as abodes; such amazing lord who has great desire towards me.
- *Ana idattum* – Still, he desired my heart and this town tirukkadittānam as his native/hereditary abode.

## 8.6.9. Tayap padigal

*tāyap padigaḷ talaic ciṟandengengum māyattināl manni vīṟṟirundān uṟai tēsattamarar tirukkadittānattuḷ āyarkkadipadi aṟpudan tānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tēsam – radiant; amarar – ultimate destination for nityasūris; tirukkadittānattuḷ – in tirukkadittānam; uṟai – residing; āyarkku – for covherd boys; adipadi – ultimate lord; aṟupudan tān – one who has amazing qualities and activities; tāyam – distinguished; padigaḷ – arcāvatara stalams (many divya dēśams / divine abodes); engu engum – everywhere; talai – great; siṟandu – having qualities such as śeelam (simplicity) etc; māyattināl – with amazing physical qualities such as beauty etc; manni – fitting well; vīṟṟu – in a distinguished manner (different from other forms such as para (paramapadam), vyūha (milk ocean) etc); irundān – remains

**Перевод:**

**The ultimate lord of the covherd boys, the lord who has amazing qualities and activities, remains in tirukkadittānam which is the ultimate destination for the radiant nityasūris; he is fitting well in a distinguished manner having great qualities such as śeelam (simplicity) etc, and with amazing physical qualities such as beauty etc, and is the one who is present in distinguished arcāvatara stalams everywhere.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the ninth pāsuram, when asked “āren’t all these abodes mentioned in previous pāsuram, hereditary for him?” āḻvār says “he is attached to tirukkadittānam since it facilitates his union with me”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. tāyap padigaḷ talaic ciṟandengengum māyattināl manni vīṟṟirundān uṟai tēsattamarar tirukkadittānattuḷ āyarkkadipadi aṟpudan tānē*

- *tāyap padigaḷ …* – In all the greatly distinguished, ancient abodes.
- *māyattināl* – With attachment, with desires. As said in dictionary “*māyā vayunam jñānam*” (māyā is synonymous with knowledge, desire etc).
- *manni vīṟṟirundān* – He mercifully remained in this divaydēśam manifesting all his opulence, desirously. Alternative meaning – one who remained there with the greatness of his opulence.
- *uṟai* – eternally residing.
- *tēsattu amarar …* – In tirukkadittānam which is the ultimate destination for the radiant nityasūris.
- *āyarkku adipadi* – One who incarnated in the covherd clan and became their leader.
- *aṟpudan* – One who has amazing forms/qualities. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying “though [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) has desire for all divyadēśams, he mercifully remained in tirukkadittānam manifesting his supremacy and simplicity, to attain me”.

## 8.6.10. Arpudan narayanan

*aṟpudan nārāyaṇan ari vāmanan niṟpadu mēvi iruppaden nenjagam naṟpugaḻ vēdiyar nānmaṟai ninṟadir kaṟpagac cōlait tirukkadittānamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

aṟpudan – being with (enjoyable) amazing activities; nārāyaṇan – having the relationship (matching that); ari – being the one who eliminates the hurdles to experience him; vāmanan – one who comes as a seeker and gives enjoyment; mēvi – fitting well; iruppadu – residing; en – my; nenjagam – in heart; niṟpadu – (coming as a part of that and) standing; nal pugaḻ – having the greatness of being ananya prayōjana (not seeking any other benefits); vēdiyar – vaidikas (followers of vēdas); nāl – four; maṟai – vēdams; ninṟu – stand; adir – chanting loudly; kaṟpagam – filled with kalpaka (celestial wish fulfilling) trees; sōlai – having garden; tirukkadittānam – tirukkadittānam

**Перевод:**

**emperumān who is with (enjoyable) amazing activities, who is having the apt relationship, who is the one who eliminates the hurdles to experience him, and who is the one who comes as a seeker and gives enjoyment, is residing in my heart, fitting well there; he is standing in tirukkadittānam which is having garden filled with kalpaka trees and vaidikas who are having the greatness of being ananya prayōjana and who stand and chant four vēdams loudly.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the tenth pāsuram, āḻvār says “Until he attained me, he mercifully remained in tirukkadittānam; once he united with me, he is standing and sitting in my heart”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. aṟpudan nārāyaṇan ari vāmanan niṟpadu mēvi iruppaden nenjagam naṟpugaḻ vēdiyar nānmaṟai ninṟadir kaṟpagac cōlait tirukkadittānamē*

- *nārāyaṇan* – vatsala (one with motherly forbearance) who will not give up his belongings \[[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is related to everyone, is the support for everyone and is the antaryāmi of everyone – this is indicated by the name nārāyaṇa\].
- *ari* – one who is capable of eliminating the hurdles.
- *vāmanan* – one who will minimize himself to fulfil all the desires of his devotees.
- *aṟpudan* – due to these aspects, he is amazing.
- *nal pugaḻ …* – First explanation – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is standing in tirukkadittānam which is having kalpaka tree forest which resounds with the four vēdams chanted by vaidikas who are ananya prayōjanas, and further, he is seated in my heart; alternative explanation – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is nārāyaṇan, ari, vāmanan and aṟpudan who is from tirukkadittānam, is standing and fittingly residing in my heart.

## 8.6.11. Solait tirukkadittanattu

*sōlait tirukkadittānattu uṟai tiru mālai madiḷ kurugūrc catakōpan sol pālōdamudanna āyirattippattum mēlai vaigundattattu iruttum viyandē*

**Пословный перевод:**

sōlai – having gardens; tirukkadittānattu – in tirukkadittānam; uṟai – eternally residing; tirumālai – to surrender unto śriya:pati (divine consort of śrī mahālakśmi); madiḷ – having fort (which is a protection); kurugūr – leader of āḻvārtirunagari; satakōpan – nammāḻvār‘s; sol – word; pālōdu amudu anna – resembling a mixture of milk and nectar; āyirattu – among thousand pāsurams; ippattum – this decad; mēlai – high abode; vaigundattu – in paramapadam; viyandu – being pleased; iruttum – will make them stay put

**Перевод:**

**This decad among the thousand pāsurams which resemble a mixture of milk and nectar, composed by the words of nammāḻvār, the leader of the fortified āḻvārtirunagari, to surrender unto śriya:pati who is eternally residing in tirukkadittānam which is having gardens, will make those who have connection with this decad to stay put, being pleased, in the high abode of paramapadam.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the end, āḻvār says “This decad, by itself, will carry those who learn it, to paramapadam”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. sōlait tirukkadittānattu uṟai tiru mālai madiḷ kurugūrc catakōpan sol pālōdamudanna āyirattippattum mēlai vaigundattattu iruttum viyandē*

- *sōlai …* – śriya:pati who is eternally residing in tirukkadittānam which is having invigorating, attractive gardens.
- *madiḷ kurugūr* – [āḻvārtirunagari](http://azhwarthirunagari.koyil.org/) which is surrounded by fort which stops the sorrows of this samsāram from entering inside.
- *satakōpan sol* – As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam bāla kāṇḍam “*raghuvara caritam muni praṇītam*” (History of śrī rāghava (śrī rāma) spoken by the sage vālmīkī bhagavān \[who only speaks about śrī rāma\]). The thousand pāsurams which resemble a mixture of milk and nectar; or this decad which resemble a mixture of milk and nectar. This indicates the proper match between the words and the meanings. [āḷavandār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/alavandhar/)‘s explanation – pāl (milk) indicates [tirumāl (śrīman nārāyaṇa)](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who resides in tirukkadittānam. amudu (nectar) indicates [nammāḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s words.
- *ippattum viyandu mēlai vaigundattu iruttum* – This decad would think “It is amazing that in this samsāram (materialistic world) there is someone who recites this decad” and will place that person in the supreme abode, śrīvaikuṇṭam. It will place such person in the supreme abode where one need not go through the suffering as in previous decad “*māyakkūttā*” and will grant eternal experience to such person.

## 8.7 Iruttum viyandu

## 8.7.1. Iruttum viyandu

*iruttum viyandu ennait tan ponnadik kīḻ enṟu aruttittu enaittōr pala nāḷ aḻaittēṟkup poruttam udai vāmanan tān pugundu endan karuttai uṟa vīṟṟirundān kaṇḍu koṇḍē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ennai – me (who cannot survive without him); viyandu – being astonished; “than – his; pon – perfectly enjoyable; adik kīḻ – under the divine feet; iruttum – will place”; enṟu – that; aruttittu – seeking; enaittu – for a long time; ōr pala nāḷ – everyday; aḻaittēṟku – who called out; enakku – for me; tān – he; poruttam – love; udai – having; vāmanan – as vāmana; pugundu – entered (as he voluntarily went to the sacrificial arena of mahābali); en than – my; karuttai – heart (which is seeking); uṟa – to remain firmly; vīṟu – manifesting the distinction (of his love over mine); kaṇḍu koṇḍu – fully seeing me; irundān – resided

**Перевод:**

**emperumān being astonished at me who was calling out every day for a long time seeking him saying “he will place me at his perfectly enjoyable divine feet”, entered my heart as loving vāmana to remain firmly, manifesting his distinction, and resided there, fully seeing me.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the first pāsuram, āḻvār mercifully mentions in brief as to how emperumān came and united with him.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “To eliminate all my suffering as I called out as a seeker, he entered my heart as a seeker and resided there as some one who attained a great benefit”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. iruttum viyandu ennait than ponnadik kīḻ enṟu aruttittu enaittōr pala nāḷ aḻaittēṟkup poruttam udai vāmanan tān pugundu endan karuttai uṟa vīṟṟirundān kaṇḍu koṇḍē*

- *ennait than pon adik kīḻ – viyandu – iruttum enṟu* – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) would place me who was interested in worldly pleasures without knowing his greatness, at his glorious divine feet, feeling astonished thinking “in this samsāra (material world) which has been given up by me as said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 7.19](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/7-19/) ‘*sa mahātmā sa durlabha:’* (Such large-hearted souls are rare to attain), there is someone who is desiring me” and make me inseparable and engage me in service. With this, prāpya (goal) and prāpaka (means) are explained. The nature of prāpyam is explained by “*than pon adik kīḻ*” (emperumān’s enjoyable divine feet); by saying “*iruttum*” (he will place), it is explained that emperumān himself is the means.
- *viyandu iruttum* – Would place me there as a benefit for him.
- *aruttittu* – To be a cētana entity (sentient) one should at least have this \[seeking to reach him\].
- *enaittu ōr pala nāḷ* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is stating what he said in [tiruvāimoḻi 8.5.8](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/03/thiruvaimozhi-8-5-8-okkum-amman/) “*nāḷ nāḷum*” (everyday).
- *aḻatittēṟku* – āḻvār is stating what he said in [tiruvāimoḻi 8.5.6](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/03/thiruvaimozhi-8-5-6-kondal-vanna/) “*ennai āḷak kūppittaḻaittakkāl*” (When I call out for you to enslave me). piḷḷān explains – āḻvār is saying “Without knowing his great love, I considered him to be delaying and I am having great desire towards him, and called out for him”. When we think about his love, starting with our seeking, everything seems superfluous; it is said in tiruvāimoḻi 9.3.9 “*eḻudum ennum idu migai*” (vorśipping him and rising are also superfluous).
- *poruttam udai* – I said in [tiruvāimoḻi 8.5.8](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/03/thiruvaimozhi-8-5-8-okkum-amman/) “*iduvō poruttam*” (is this matching?) towards the one who has such matching love.
- *vāmanan* – What have I done seeking from him? He was the one who became a seeker himself to regain his own belonging.
- *tān pugundu* – To get me, he entered my heart as a seeker.
- *en than karuttai uṟa* – He accepted my thoughts as I said in tiruvāimoḻi 2.9.4 “*tanakkēyāga enaik koḷḷum īdē*” (he should accept me for his own sake).
- *vīṟṟirundān* – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) manifested the distinction in his physical form after having attained [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) and remained as kruta krutya (one who completed the task that has to be completed).
- *kaṇḍu koṇḍē* – Just as parents would lovingly keep seeing their child who survived a great disease, emperumān is seeing āḻvār as he escaped the suffering he went through in [tiruvāimoḻi 8.5](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/03/thiruvaimozhi-8-5-mayakkuththa/) “*māyak kūttā*“.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.7.2. Irundan kandu kondu

*irundān kaṇḍu koṇḍu enadēḻai nenjāḷum tirundāda ōr aivarait tēyndaṟa mannip perundātkāḷiṟṟukku aruḷ seyda perumān tarundān aruḷ tān ini yān aṟiyēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

enadu – my; ēḻai – desirous; nenju – heart; āḷum – ruling over; tirundāda – uncontrollable; ōr – distinguished; aivarai – five senses; tēyndu – wane; aṟa – to perish; manni – entered \[in the heart\] to remain firm; kaṇḍu koṇḍu – like those who watch carefully (after finding a treasure); irundān – emperumān who remained without leaving; peru – huge; tāḷ – having feet; kaḷiṟṟukku – for the elephant; aruḷ seyda – showed mercy (by eliminating the sorrow inflicted by a crocodile); perumān – lord, greater than all; tān – he; tarum – granted (that elephant); aruḷ tān – favour; yān aṟiyēn – I don’t know (that as mercy)

**Перевод:**

**While the uncontrollable, distinguished five senses were ruling over my desirous heart, emperumān entered my heart to make them wane and perish, and remained firm in there, watching me; \[after seeing such favour\] the favour of the lord who is greater than all, who showered his mercy for the elephant with huge feet, does not look like a favour. Implies “the favour you have done to me who was caught by the crocodile of five senses, is far greater”.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the second pāsuram, āḻvār says “Even emperumān’s elimination of the danger of gajēndrāḻvān is not a match for his great favour of accepting me by manifesting his beauty and eliminating my attachment towards my senses”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. irundān kaṇḍu koṇḍu enadēḻai nenjāḷum tirundāda ōr aivarait tēyndaṟa mannip perundātkāḷiṟṟukku aruḷ seyda perumān tarundān aruḷ tān ini yān aṟiyēnē*

- *irundān kaṇḍu koṇḍu* – Just as an impoverished person finding treasure would keep watching it, emperumān keeps watching me. śrī rāmāyaṇam kiśkindā kāṇḍam 5.18 “*anyōnyam abhivīkśantau na truptim upajagmatu:*” (śrī rāma and sugrīva were gazing at each other without getting fully satisfied), āḻvār is not seeing himself \[as he is fully engrossed in emperumān seeing him\].
- *enadu ēḻai nenju āḷum* – The senses tormented my heart which runs after everything it sees, due to that same reason. As my heart was not surrendered to a strong person, the senses started dominating it.
- *tirundāda* – They are so cruel that they cannot be reformed even by the omnipotent sarvēśvara since time immemorial.
- *ōr aivarai* – You cannot find another set of five entities like these. Due to the suffering inflicted by them, āḻvār is highlighting his senses with respect.
- *tēyndaṟa manni irundān* – To diminish the attachment towards worldly matters which are visible to the eyes, he stood there presenting his beauty. Everyone becomes attached to worldly matters due to their beautiful forms only. As kings would kill their enemies with the strength of their seat/throne, emperumān entered my heart thinking “we should win over them with our presence”. He is as said in [tirumālai 16](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/09/thirumalai-16/) “*pōdarē enṟu sollip pundiyil pugundu than pāl ādaram peruga vaitta aḻagan*” (Calling out “come here”, the beautiful emperumān entered my heart and increased my attachment towards him).
- *perum tāḷ …* – sarvēśvaran who showered his mercy on the elephant which had huge feet. The huge body indicates the unbearability of the pain.
- *perumān – tān – tarum – aruḷ tān* – The mercy he granted. Since the mercy keeps flowing at all times \[past, present and future\], he says “*tarum*” (in present tense). As he thinks that whatever favours done by emperumān to his devotees are done for himself, he speaks in this way.
- *ini yān aṟiyēn* – After he helped me, I don’t consider that \[help to gajēndrāḻvān\] as help. The elephant suffered for thousand years, the pond is limited in size and there is one crocodile; I have been suffering since time immemorial, caught in the samsārārṇava (ocean of nescience) and there are five crocodiles \[five senses\]. Is the great quality of helping me only as good as helping gajēndrāḻvān? āḻvār highlighted emperumān’s help to śrī gajēndrāḻvān and highlighted how that is greater than his help for others; and then, he highlights the help to āḻvār himself and highlighted how that is greater than his help to gajēndrāḻvān.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.7.3. Arul tan

*aruḷ tān ini yān aṟiyēn avan ennuḷ iruḷ tān aṟa vīṟṟirundān idu allāl poruḷ tān enin mū ulagum poruḷ alla maruḷ tān īdō? māya mayakku mayakkē*

**Пословный перевод:**

avan – one who is greatly attached to me; en uḷ – in my heart; iruḷ tān – darkness (of ignorance etc); aṟa – to be gone; vīṟṟu – with greatness; irundān – was seated; idu – this presence; allāl – other than; poruḷ tān – other goals; enil – if attained; mū ulagum – three types of subservient cit (sentient beings) and acit (insentient objects); poruḷalla – are not considered as benefit; ini – now; aruḷ tān – as a favour; yān – I; aṟiyēn – do not consider; īdu tān – this; maruḷō – is this hallucination; māyam – amazing; mayakku – deceitful activities; mayakkē – is he causing bewilderment?

**Перевод:**

**emperumān who is greatly attached to me, became seated with greatness in my heart to have my darkness eliminated; other than this presence, even if other goals such as the three types of subservient cit (sentient beings) and acit (insentient objects) are attained, he does not consider them as benefits; now, I do not consider this as a favour. Is this hallucination? ōr is he causing bewilderment with his amazing deceitful activities?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the third pāsuram, āḻvār doubts thinking “sarvēśvaran showing unsurpassed affection in this manner is impossible to attain; hence, is this experience my hallucination?”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. aruḷ tān ini yān aṟiyēn avan ennuḷ iruḷ tān aṟa vīṟṟirundān idu allāl poruḷ tān enin mū ulagum poruḷ alla maruḷ tān īdō? māya mayakku mayakkē*

- *aruḷ tān ini yān aṟiyēn* – I did not consider his act of eliminating my attachment towards my senses, as something worthy.

When asked “Why so?” āḻvār says,

- *avan …* – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) remained in my heart in a distinguished manner having attained an impossible benefit, to eliminate all my ignorance; will anything else be visible to me?
- *idu allāl …* – [tirumālai āṇḍān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/thirumalai-andan/)‘s explanation – Worldly people identify the wealth of owning the three worlds as the best among all available wealth; āḻvār says “even that is not considered worthy by me”; [emperumānār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/emperumanar/)‘s merciful explanation – other than being present in my heart, if we see emperumān would consider his presence as mentioned in [tiruvāimoḻi 4.5.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/02/thiruvaimozhi-4-5-1-virrirundhu/) “*vīṟṟirundu ēḻulagum tanikkōl sella*” (controlling all the worlds by sitting in paramapadam itself) as opulence, he would not consider even that as worthy. emperumānār’s explanation is the one which matches the context of this pāsuram.
- *maruḷ tān īdō* – It does not fit well to say that [sarvēśvaran](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) will blissfully remain in this manner after attaining a samsāri cētana (bound soul); am I saying this due to my confused mind?
- *māya mayakku mayakkē* – ōr, did he manifest his amazing deceitful acts and bewilder me? For a long time he bewildered me with this prakruti (worldly matter) and now he is bewildering me with his love.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.7.4. Maya mayakku

*māya mayakku mayakkān ennai vanjittu āyan amararkkari ēṟu enadammān tūya sudarccōdit tanadennuḷ vaittān tēsandigaḷum tan tiruvaruḷ seydē*

**Пословный перевод:**

āyan – being obedient as one among the ignorant covherd boys; amararkku – for (the knowledgeable) nityasūris (eternal residents of paramapadam); ari ēṟu – having unbounded supremacy; enadu ammān – my svāmy (lord, who manifested such supremacy and simplicity to me); tēsam tigaḻum – popular in the world; than – his; tiru – distinguished; aruḷ – mercy; seydu – showering unconditionally; tanadu – his distinguished; tūya – pure; sudar – very radiant; sōdi – glowing divine form; en – in my; uḷ – inside heart; vaittān – (firmly) placed; ennai – me (who does not know anyone other than him); vanjittu – deceived (as he would deceive the unfavourable ones); māya mayakku – amazing deceitful acts; mayakkān – will not bewilder me

**Перевод:**

**My svāmy being obedient as one among the ignorant covherd boys and having unbounded supremacy for the nityasūris, unconditionally showered his distinguished mercy which is popularly known in this world,  and placed his distinguished, pure, very radiantly glowing divine form inside my heart; he will not bewilder me by deceiving me with his amazing, deceitful acts.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fourth pāsuram, āḻvār says “emperumān, being with a form which cannot be easily seen even by the nityasūris, being the apt lord who enslaved me as kriṣṇa, the covherd boy, will not bewilder me; there is no doubt that he entered in me and mercifully united with me”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. māya mayakku mayakkān ennai vanjittu āyan amararkkari ēṟu enadammān tūya sudarccōdit tanadennuḷ vaittān tēsandigaḷum than tiruvaruḷ seydē*

- *ennai vanjittu māya mayakku mayakkān* – emperumān as kriṣṇa, told the unfavourable ones such as duryōdana et al “I won’t take up arms” but took to arms; turned day into night and deceived them; but did he do any such thing towards pāṇḍavas? \[No\] Hence, he will not bewilder me who fully exists for him, through his amazing, deceitful acts.

When asked “What is the reason for your saying this?” āḻvār says,

- *āyan amararkku ari ēṟu enadu ammān* – Though he is having supreme greatness over nityasūris, he, my ultimate well-wisher, incarnated as kriṣṇa and accepted my servitude; \[hence\] he will not bewilder me with his deceitful acts.

When asked “How did you get this benefit?” āḻvār says,

- *tēsam tigaḻum than tiruvaruḷ seydu – tūya sudarc cōdit tanadu ennuḷ vaittān* – He arrived inside me and showered his mercy, to be well known all over the world.
- *than tiruvaruḷ* – The distinguished mercy which is seen only in him and no one else. He placed his distinguished divine form which is opposite to all defects, having great radiance and is in pure goodness state, inside me. He manifested his divine form which manifests that he is ananyasādya (not attained by the effort of anyone else) as said in muṇḍaka upaniśat 3.2.3 “*tasyaiśa ātmā vivruṇutē tanūmsvām*” (bhagavān shows his true form to those who are dear to him).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.7.5. Tigalum tan

*tigaḻum tan tiruvaruḷ seydu ulagattār pugaḻum pugaḻ tān adu kāttit tandu ennuḷ tigaḻum maṇik kunṟam onṟē ottu ninṟān pugaḻum pugaḻ maṟṟenakkum ōr poruḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tigaḻum – radiant (for both emperumān and āḻvār, being nirhētuka (unconditional) and niravadika (infinite)); than – his; tiruvaruḷ – divine mercy; seydu – showering; ulagattār – people of the world; pugaḻum – praising (seeing this); adu – that; pugaḻ – (popular) glory; tān – he; kāttit tandu – revealing to me; en uḷ – inside me; tigaḻum – shining; onṟu – a; maṇik kunṟam ottu – like a ruby hill; ninṟān – he stood; enakku – for me; maṟṟu – other; pugaḻum – praising (him); pugaḻum – glory; ōr – a; poruḷē – is it worthy?

**Перевод:**

**emperumān is standing inside me as a shining ruby hill, revealing to me his radiant, divine mercy which is praised by the people of the world;  is there any other glory such as praising him, worthy for me?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fifth pāsuram, āḻvār says “emperumān mercifully stood inside me to make everyone praise me saying ‘what a benefit he has got’; for such emperumān, I will not consider any glory other than the glory acquired by this act, as worthy”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. tigaḻum than tiruvaruḷ seydu ulagattār pugaḻum pugaḻ tān adu kāttit tandu ennuḷ tigaḻum maṇik kunṟam onṟē ottu ninṟān pugaḻum pugaḻ maṟṟenakkum ōr poruḷē*

- *tigaḻum than tiruvaruḷ seydu* – Unlike limited mercy of others, he showered his \[unlimited\] mercy which brings glory to both him and me.
- *ulagattār …* – emperumān showed how the people of world are praising the benefit I got. emperumān is making the whole world to praise as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.5.11](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/08/thiruvaimozhi-1-5-11-male-maya/) “*pālēy tamiḻar isaikārar pattar paravum āyiram*” (sweet milk like pāsurams which are celebrated by those who are well-versed in tamiḻ, those who are well-versed in music and can sing this and those devotees who understand the meaning). As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam bāla kāṇḍam 4.32 “*imau munī pārtiva lakśaṇānvitau kuśeelavau cāpi mahātapasvinau …*” (śrī rāma says – the narration by these saintly kuśa and lava, who are having kingly feature and are great hermits, is bringing good fortune to me; listent to this greatly virtuous legend), the whole world is praising.
- *en uḷ …* – Entering in me, considering to have attained the impossible benefit, remaining firmly without leaving and with great glow, stood like a shining ruby hill.
- *pugaḻum pugaḻ* – Other than this great quality of standing in me, I will not consider any other glory as worthy. I will not even consider his elimination of my attachment towards my senses as something worthy \[in comparison to being inside me\].
