## 8.7.6. Porul marru

*poruḷ maṟṟenakkum ōr poruḷ tannil sīrkkat tarumēl pinnai yārkku avan tannaik kodukkum? karumāṇikkak kunṟattut tāmarai pōl tirumārvu kāl kaṇ kai sevvāy undiyānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

karu māṇikkak kunṟattu – on top of a dark carbuncle hill; tāmarai pōl – reddish/fresh like a blossomed bush of lotus flowers; tirumārvu – divine chest; kāl – divine feet; kaṇ – divine eyes; kai – divine hands; sem – reddish; vāy – divine lips; undiyān – one who has divine navel; maṟṟu – other; poruḷ tannil – among the goals/benefits; enakkum – for me; ōr – a; poruḷ – benefit; sīrkka – in the best way; tarum ēl – if he gives; pinnai – then; avan – he; tannai – himself (who is the ultimate goal); ārkku – to whom; kodukkum – will he give?

**Перевод:**

**emperumān resembles a dark carbuncle hill with a reddish/freshly blossomed lotus flower bush, with his divine chest, divine feet, divine eyes, divine hands, reddish divine lips and divine navel; If such emperumān bestows a benefit among the other goals/benefits in the best way to me, then, to whom will he give himself? Implies that emperumān did not bestow other benefits \[and bestowed himself\] to āḻvār due to not having an apt entity who can receive him, but due to his mercy.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the sixth pāsuram, āḻvār says “emperumān gave himself to me due to his great desire towards me and not because there would be no one to enjoy him, who has greatly distinguished beauty, if he gave me some other benefit”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. poruḷ maṟṟenakkum ōr poruḷ tannil sīrkkat tarumēl pinnai yārkku avan tannaik kodukkum? karumāṇikkak kunṟattut tāmarai pōl tirumārvu kāl kaṇ kai sevvāy undiyānē*

- *poruḷ …* – If he bestows another superior benefit among the puruśārtams (goals/benefits).
- *pinnai yārkku avan tannaik kodukkum* – Is there any one who can quickly accept him?

When asked “Why? Is there no one who can accept him?” [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says,

- *karu māṇikkam …* – Would any one accept such neem juice \[āḻvār is sarcastically highlighting [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) as neem juice which is bitter\]?
- *karu māṇikkak kunṟattu* – \[dark carbuncle hill\] The example for emperumān, who is the refuge.
- *tāmarai pōl* – \[lotus flower\] The example for his individual limb-wise beauty.
- *tiru mārvu* – The divine chest where pirātti, who is the puruśakāram \[one who presents the situation of ātmās to [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) and recommends on their behalf\], resides.
- *kāl* – The divine feet one will fall at, after being won over by the divine togetherness of emperumān and pirātti.
- *kaṇ …* – The eyes which shower their cool glance at those who fall at the feet, the eyes which will lift them up and embrace them, the lips which will speak sweet words and the divine navel which is enjoyable for them. ḍidn’t [tiruppāṇāḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/thiruppanazhwar/) say in amalanādipirān 3 “*undi mēladanṟō*” (my mind is fully dependent on your navel).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.7.7. Sevvay undi

*sevvāy undi veṇ pal sudark kuḻai tammōdu evvāyc cudarum tammil mun vaḷāyk koḷḷac cevvāy muṟuvalōdu enaduḷḷattirunda avvāyanṟi yān aṟiyēn maṟṟaruḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

sem – reddish; vāy – mouth; (sem) undi – reddish divine navel; veṇ – whitish; pal – divine teeth; sudar – having radiance; kuḻai tammōdum – divine ear rings, along with these; evvāy – all limbs; sudarum – radiance; tammil – with each other; mun – competing; vaḷayk koḷḷa – surrounded; sem – reddish; vāy – divine lips’; muṟuvalōdu – with the smile; enadu – my; uḷḷattu – in my heart; irunda – present; a – that; vāy – manner; anṟi – other than that; maṟṟu – any other; aruḷ – form; yān aṟiyēn – I don’t think

**Перевод:**

**The radiance of every limb of emperumān‘s such as reddish mouth, reddish divine navel, whitish divine teeth, radiant divine ear rings, competing with each other, surrounded me; I cannot think of any form other than the manner in which such emperumān is present with the smile in his reddish divine lips.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the seventh pāsuram, āḻvār becomes very pleased on enjoying the beautiful smile of emperumān which occurred after emperumān‘s union with āḻvār.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. sevvāy undi veṇ pal sudark kuḻai tammōdu evvāyc cudarum tammil mun vaḷāyk koḷḷac cevvāy muṟuvalōdu enaduḷḷattirunda avvāyanṟi yān aṟiyēn maṟṟaruḷē*

- *sevvāy …* – Along with the reddish divine lips, divine navel, whitish divine teeth, radiant divine ear rings.
- *evvāyc cudarum* – The radiance of every other limb. vāy – place.
- *tammil mun vaḷāyk koḷḷa* – Each one of them highlighting itself, competing with each other, surrounded me saying “I, I”. Implies each one of them highlighting itself and surrounding me. Alternative explanation – each one of them competes with me and is surrounding me.
- *sevvāy muṟuvalōdu enadu uḷḷattirunda* – The entity who is explained in cāndōjña upaniśat 3.14 ‘*avākyanādara:’* (does not speak, ignores \[in paramapadam\]), is similing here highlighting that attaining [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is for his benefit. As a flower blossoms, freshness will be seen all over the flower; similarly he smiled to have an impact in all of his limbs \[to become reddish\].
- *avvāy anṟi* – Other than this place. Other than this smiling form. In śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 63.12, first the nature of sītāp pirātti is said as “*kāntasmitā*” (one who has a gentle smile) and was then said as “*jātahāsā*” (smiling) to differentiate the change in her state after becoming joyful at that time.  I don’t know about any other mercy of his. Implies, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is satisfied with this and does not need anything else.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.7.8. Ariyen marrarul

*aṟiyēn maṟṟaruḷ ennai āḷum pirānār veṟidē aruḷ seyvar seyvārgatku ugandu siṟiyēnudaic cindaiyuḷ mūvulgum tan neṟiyā vayiṟṟil koṇḍu ninṟoḻindārē*

**Пословный перевод:**

maṟṟu – anything else; aruḷ – as favour; aṟiyēn – I don’t think; ennai – me; āḷum – enslaved; pirānār – great benefactor; seyvārgatku – to whom he thought of helping; veṟidē – without any cause; ugandu – happily; aruḷ – favour; seyvar – will do; siṟiyēnudai – me who is very lowly; sindaiyuḷ – in heart; mū ulagum – three worlds; neri A – without disregarding the protector-protected relationship; than vayiṟṟil – inside him; koṇḍu – having; ninṟoḻindār – he stood

**Перевод:**

**I don’t think about anything as his favour; the great benefactor who enslaved me, will happily do favours without any cause, to whom he thought of helping; he who is having the three worlds inside him without disregarding the protector-protected relationship, stood in my heart, in me who is very lowly. \[Implies – because of this great favour, I don’t consider anything else as favour\]**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the ninth pāsuram, āḻvār says “For emperumān to come and unite with me in this manner, there is no reason other than his mercy”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. aṟiyēn maṟṟaruḷ ennai āḷum pirānār veṟidē aruḷ seyvar seyvārgatku ugandu siṟiyēnudaic cindaiyuḷ mūvulgum than neṟiyā vayiṟṟil koṇḍu ninṟoḻindārē*

- *aṟiyēn maṟṟu aruḷ* – I don’t know any other favour of his.
- *ennai āḷum pirānār* – The benefactor who accepts my service.
- *veṟidē aruḷ seyvar* – Will shower his nirhētuka krupai (causeless mercy).

When asked “to whom?” [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says,

- *seyvārgatku* – To those he considered to pursue as said in kata upaniśat 1.2.23 “*yamēvaiśa vruṇutē*” (one who is desired by the supreme lord). If he only helps those who put in some effort, then [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) would not have said “*veṟidē*” (causelessly). But should there not be some reason for this mercy? (His) Happiness is the reason; it is said in śrī bhāśyam “*priya tama Eva hi varaṇīyō bhavati*” (īsn’t the one who is desired by [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), pursued by emperumān?) Even when a cētana has ruci (taste/intent) towards bhagavān, that is only considered as a distinguished nature of the sentient being and not considered as means for the goal.

When asked “Where did you find his causeless mercy?” [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says “should I seek outside?”

- *siṟiyēnudaic cindaiyuḷ* – I am so lowly; still I see him in my heart.
- *mū ulagum …* – An owner will care for his possessions due to the relationship (owner – owned). One who properly cares for his belongings, remained in my heart and interacted with me improperly. Due to considering himself as lowly, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) considers [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s interactions with him to be improper. emperumān considers āḻvār to be greater than the three worlds; āḻvār considers himself to be lower than the three worlds.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.7.9. Vayirril kondu

*vayiṟṟil koṇḍu ninṟoḻindārum yavarum vayiṟṟil koṇḍu ninṟoru mūvulagum tam vayiṟṟil koṇḍu ninṟa vaṇṇam ninṟa mālai vayiṟṟil koṇḍu manna vaittēn madiyālē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vayiṟṟil koṇḍu – being a protector (just as a mother would protect a foetus in the womb); ninṟu oḻindārum – kśatriyas (kings); yavarum – brahmā et al (who are greater than the kings); vayiṟṟil – in a fraction of his svarūpa (true nature); koṇḍu – having; ninṟu – standing; oru – distinguished; mū ulagum – three worlds; tam – in his; vayiṟṟil – in a fraction of his vow; koṇḍu – holding; ninṟa vaṇṇam – with the svarūpam (which was there prior to that state); ninṟa – stood; mālai – the supreme lord; madiyālē – with the permission (which was granted by him first as said in tiruvāimoḻi 5.8.9 “isaivittu ennai“); vayiṟṟil – inside me; koṇḍu – having; manna – to not leave; vaittēn – I placed

**Перевод:**

**Having the kśatriyas, brahmā et al who were all considered as protectors, in a fraction of his svarūpa, beholding the distinguished three worlds in a fraction of his vow, the supreme lord stood with his svarūpam; by giving my persmission, I placed such emperumān inside me to not leave from there.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the ninth pāsuram, when āḻvār is asked “What did you do to be accepted by emperumān in this manner?” he says “I allowed him to do so”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “I firmly placed his protection in all manner, in my heart”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. vayiṟṟil koṇḍu ninṟoḻindārum yavarum vayiṟṟil koṇḍu ninṟoru mūvulagum tam vayiṟṟil koṇḍu ninṟa vaṇṇam ninṟa mālai vayiṟṟil koṇḍu manna vaittēn madiyālē*

- *vayiṟṟil koṇḍu ninṟu oḻindārum* – kśatriyas et al who would care for their citizens just as a mother would have her child (foetus) in her womb and care for it.
- *yavarum* – brahmā et al who would care for such kśatriyas as well.
- *vayiṟṟil …* – brahmā et al, kśatriyas et al and the three worlds which are all inside him.
- *tam vayiṟṟil koṇḍu* – Conducting them in one thousandth fraction of his vow; alternative explanation – having those protectors who care for others, and the three worlds in his stomach, and protecting them.
- *ninṟa vaṇṇam ninṟa mālai* – sarvēśvara who stood there without any impact to his form even after having all of these in him. I placed sarvēśvara who is along with his wealth, in my heart, to not let him leave from there.
- *madiyālē* – \[ammangi\] ammāḷ explains this as āḻvār saying “I have known about emperumān’s nature” \[mati is explained as jñānam\]. Alternatively, parāśara bhattar explains “*mati:* implies *anumati:* (permission) – I simply gave him permission”. That is, āḻvār saying “When he entered, I simply did not stop him” \[When emperumān tries to help us, if we don’t stop him, that is sufficient for him to shower his grace. This is termed as apratiśēdam, vilakkāmai – non-prohibition\].

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.7.10. Vaitten madiyal

*vaittēn madiyāl enaduḷḷattagattē eyttē oḻivēn allēn enṟum eppōdum moyttēy tirai mōdu taṇ pāṟkadaluḷāl paittēy sudarp pāmbaṇai nam paranaiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

moyttu – being dense; ēy – matching; tirai – waves; mōdu – rising; taṇ – invigorating; pāṟkadaluḷ – in kśīrābdi (milky ocean); paittu – with hoods which are expanding; ēy – natural; sudar – having radiance; pāmbu – tiruvantāḻvān; aṇai – having as mattress; nam – for us; paranai – lord; madiyāl – with my permission; enadu – my; uḷḷattu agattē – in my heart; vaittēn – I placed; enṟum – all days; eppōdum – at all times; eyttē oḻivēn allēn – will not separate from him and suffer

**Перевод:**

**With my permission, I placed in my heart, our lord who is having the naturally radiant tiruvanantāḻvān who is having hoods which are expanding, as his mattress, in the invigorating kśīrābdi which has dense, matching and rising waves; I will not separate from him at any day, any time and suffer \[due to such separation\].**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the tenth pāsuram, āḻvār says “emperumān has arrived in my heart along with his retinue; I will never separate from him and suffer”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. vaittēn madiyāl enaduḷḷattagattē eyttē oḻivēn allēn enṟum eppōdum moyttēy tirai mōdu taṇ pāṟkadaluḷāl paittēy sudarp pāmbaṇai nam paranaiyē*

- *vaittēn madiyāl enadu uḷḷattu agattē* – I placed him in my heart with my permission; just for a simple permission, what a great benefit I attained!
- *eyttē oḻivēn allēn* – From now onvards, I will never become weakened and suffer.

When asked “How long will this remain true?” [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says,

- *enṟum eppōdum* – On all days and in all states.
- *moyttu ēy tirai* – In the invigorating kśīrābdi, where the waves gather together and flow in a matching manner. Even if a small drop falls on [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) \[and ādiśēśan\], his tenderness is such that it makes one say “huge wave hit him”.
- *paittēy sudarp pāmbaṇai* – ādiśēśa who is having expanded hoods which stop the waves from hitting [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s divine form, and is having matching radiance due to \[constant\] enjoyment of bhagavān; emperumān having greatness due to resting on such ādiśēśa.
- *nam paranai* – One who revealed such greatness to us; [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) entered [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s divine heart as said in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 5.2.10 “*aravattamaḷiyinōdum aḻagiya pāṟkadalōdum”* (emperumān arrived with his serpent mattress, śrī mahālakśmi et al into my heart)

## 8.7.11. Sudarp pambanai

*sudarp pāmbaṇai nam paranait tirumālai adic cēr vagai vaṇ kurugūrc catakōpan mudippān sonna āyirattu ippattum sanmam vidat tēyndaṟa nōkkum tan kaṇgaḷ sivandē*

**Пословный перевод:**

sudar – having perfect radiance; pāmbu – tiruvantāḻvān (ādiśēśa); aṇai – having as mattress; nam – for us; paranai – lord; tirumālai – śriya:pati (śrīman nārāyaṇa); adi – in the divine feet; sēr vagai – the way to reach; mudippān – to fulfil; vaṇ – having unlimited wealth; kurugūr – leader of āḻvārtirunagari; satakōpan – nammāḻvār; sonna – mercifully spoke; āyirattu – among the thousand pāsurams; ippattum – this decad; sanmam – birth (which causes hurdles in enjoying bhagavān); aṟa – very; tēyndu – weaken; vida – to be destroyed; than – his; kaṇgaḷ – eyes; sivandu – becoming reddish; nōkkum – will see

**Перевод:**

**To fulfil the way of reaching the divine feet of our lord, śriya:pati, who is having perfectly radiant ādiśēśa as mattress, nammāḻvār, the leader of āḻvārtirunagari which is having unlimited wealth, mercifully spoke this decad among the thousand pāsurams; with his eyes becoming reddish, this decad \[personified\] will look at birth \[of his devotee\] to weaken it very much and destroy it. The decad itself is spoken as a man personified due to its ability to destroy the birth.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the end, āḻvār says “for those who learn this decad, it will be the poison for their samsāram \[bondage in this material realm\]”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. sudarp pāmbaṇai nam paranait tirumālai adic cēr vagai vaṇ kurugūrc catakōpan mudippān sonna āyirattu ippattum sanmam vidat tēyndaṟa nōkkum than kaṇgaḷ sivandē*

- *sudarp pāmbaṇai nam paranait tirumālai* – The eradication of birth is explained as the result/benefit for those who learn this decad; the goal attained as a result of such eradication of birth is explained here – as explained in paryanka vidyā, the benefit attained by muktātmās is to see and enjoy [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s merciful presence in the lap of tiruvanantāḻvān along with periya pirāttiyār.
- *adic cēr vagai …* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) who has the nature of being together with emperumān’s divine feet. For āḻvār, jñānam (knowledge) and ānandam (bliss) are not the identity; śēśatvam (servitude) is.
- *mudippān sonna …* – Also explained as – this decad which was spoken to eradicate the bondage in the material realm, will fulfil the goal of reaching the divine feet of empeurmān. It will ensure that the birth is eliminated.

While doing that,

- *ippattum – than kaṇgaḷ sivandu – nōkkum* – That is, this decad is druśti viśam (poison which kills on being seen) for samsāram. That is, the presence of this decad and birth together are contradictory.

## 8.8 Kangal sivandu

## 8.8.1. Kangal sivandu

*kaṇgaḷ sivandu periyavāy vāyum sivandu kanindu uḷḷē veṇ pal ilagu sudar ilagu vilagu magara kuṇḍalattan koṇḍal vaṇṇan sudar mudiyan nāngu tōḷan kuni sārngan oṇ sangadai vāḷ āḻiyān oruvan adiyēn uḷḷānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kaṇgaḷ – divine eyes; sivandu – becoming reddish; periya āy – being expansive; vāyum – divine lips; sivandu – becoming reddish; kanindu – being well ripened; uḷḷē – inside \[the mouth\]; veṇ – whitish; pal – the divine teeth line; ilagu – shining; sudar – radiance; ilagu – greatly splendorous; vilagu – swaying; magara kuṇḍalattan – having makara kuṇḍalam (a fish shaped ear ring); koṇḍal – dark cloud’s; vaṇṇan – having a beautiful form with the complexion \[of such cloud\]; sudar – having great radiance; mudiyan – having divine crown; nāngu tōḷan – (matching such supremacy) having four divine shoulders; kuni – bent; sārngam – śrī śārngam (bow); oṇ – attractive; sangu – śrī pāncajanyam (conch); gadai – kaumōdaki (mace); vāḷ – nandakam (sword); āḻiyān – having the divine weapon of tiruvāḻi (chakra); oruvan – one with a distinguished form (due to these beautiful limbs, beautiful ornaments and beautiful weapons); adiyēn – me, the servitor (who is immersed in such beauty), my; uḷḷān – radiantly residing in me

**Перевод:**

**emperumān is having expansive, divine eyes which are becoming reddish; his divine lips are becoming reddish and well ripened; his divine, whitish teeth line, inside the mouth, are shining radiantly; he is having swaying ear rings; he is having a beautiful form with the complexion of a dark cloud; he is having a greatly radiant divine crown; he is having four divine shoulders; he is holding the bent śrī śārngam, attractive śrī pāncajanyam, kaumōdaki, nandakam and the divine weapon, tiruvāḻi; such emperumān with a distinguished form is radiantly residing in me, who is a servitor.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the first pāsuram, āḻvār enjoys emperumān showing his fresh appearance with beauty etc after uniting with āḻvār.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. After enjoying emperumān‘s divine form, our āḻvārs will not engage in his svarūpam (true nature) and guṇam (qualities); śāstram says that once a person holds on to emperumān’s divine form as the auspicious abode, he/she will engage further \[in his true nature and qualities\] – but it does not instruct him/her to engage further, giving up the divine form of emperumān; it is saying that to highlight that emperumān’s true nature and qualities are also to be meditated upon. It does not matter whether it is for himself, his divine consorts or his servitors; his divine form is very dear to everyone. kaṇgaḷ sivandu periyavāy vāyum sivandu kanindu uḷḷē veṇ pal ilagu sudar ilagu vilagu magara kuṇḍalattan koṇḍal vaṇṇan sudar mudiyan nāngu tōḷan kuni sārngan oṇ sangadai vāḷ āḻiyān oruvan adiyēn uḷḷānē*

- *kaṇgaḷ sivandu* – As said in cāndōjña upaniśat 1.6 “*tasya yatā kapyāsam puṇḍarīkam ēvam akśinī*” (The divine eyes of śrīman nārāyaṇa, the supreme lord, resemble the lotus flower which has been freshly blossomed by the rays of the sun), [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s eyes will be reddish; this being the case, due to the separation experienced in “*māyak kūttā*“, they became pale; and due to the union experienced in “*iruttum* *viyandu*“, they got back their original reddish colour. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) being engrossed in emperumān’s eyes and not moving away, can be seen in the tone of this pāsuram.
- *periya āy* – They are having expansion and contraction. While it says in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 1.2.1 “*sadaikarūpa rūpāya*” (one who is having unchanging divine auspicious form), it implies – there is no change in him due to karma (deeds, puṇya/pāpa (virtue/vice)), but there is no negation of changes due to uniting with his devotees; if that happens (he remains unchanging), that means he will cease to exist. Even he will change according to his own greatness.
- *vāyum sivandu* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying – not just the eyes, even the divine lips accquired their natural complexion. āḻvār is recollecting what he said in [tiruvāimoḻi 8.6.7](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/04/thiruvaimozhi-8-6-7-konmin-idar-keda/) “*sevvāy – veṇpal sudarkkuḻai*” (reddish lips, whitish teeth, radiant ears).
- *kanindu* – This redness, being fully immersed, appears well ripened.
- *uḷḷē* – The difficulty in leaving the reddish divine lips and entering inside, is observed here.
- *veṇ pal ilagu sudar* – The teeth line having white complexion which is contrasting the reddish lips, and having well surrounded radiance.
- *ilagu vilagu magara kuṇḍalattan* – One who is having the swaying, divine makara kuṇḍalam which has contrasting complexion to the darkness in his divine hair. It appears that [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is joyfully nodding his head thinking “we have acquired the union with [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)” \[which caused his earrings to sway\]. He became very joyful just as an ocean broke its barriers.
- *koṇḍal vaṇṇan* – His divine form became very dark like a rain cloud. Previously his divine form was pale in complexion \[due to separation\].
- *sudar mudiyan* – One who is having a divine crown which will override the beauty of everything else with its beauty. Only after eliminating [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s suffering in “*māyakkūttā*“, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) was crowned. āḻvār called him in [tiruvāimoḻi 8.5.3](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/03/thiruvaimozhi-8-5-3-mudi-ser-senni-amma/) “*mudi sēr senni ammā*” (oh lord with well fitting divine crown).
- *nāngu tōḷan* – After embracing [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/), [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s shoulders swelled \[due to the joy\].
- *kuni sārngan* – Just as it is said in “*magara kuṇḍalattan*“, even these \[weapons\] appear like ornaments for him. In the hands of valorous persons, the bow will be bent even when there is no battle.
- *oṇ sangu* – The attractive conch which is praised in nācciyār tirumoḻi 7.8 “*uṇbadu sollil … un selvam sāla aḻagiyadē*” (what you eat is \[[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s nectarean saliva\] … you are so wealthy).
- *gadai vāḷ āḻiyān* – one who holds the mace, sword and chakra.
- *oruvan* – The distinguished one due to being puṇḍarīkākśa (lotus-eyed), kāḷa mēga śyāma (having dark cloud like complexion), caturbhuja (four handed) and one who has divine weapons such as Sanka, chakra etc.
- *adiyēn* – Just as his lordship is distinguished, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s servitude is also distinguished. That is – āḻvār is saying that he is a servitor not due to having true knowledge about the self, but due to [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s beauty.
- *uḷḷānē* – As the mind which was focussed outward is turned  inward \[towards the self\], emperumān whose beauty is generally heard in “*yuvākumāra:*” (youth and adolescent), is śiningly visible with his beautiful limbs, beautiful ornaments and beautiful weapons as in a box containing diamonds.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.8.2. Adiyen ullan

*adiyēn uḷḷān udal uḷḷān aṇḍattagattān puṟattuḷḷān padiyē iduvenṟuraikkalām padiyan allan param paran kadi sēr nāṟṟattuḷḷālai inbattunbak kaḻi nērmai odiyā inbap perumaiyōn uṇarvil umbar oruvanē*

**Пословный перевод:**

aṇḍattu – for all entities inside the oval shaped universe; agattān – being the antarātmā (indvelling soul); puṟattu – outside the universe, the entities such as avyakta (unmanifested matter), mahat (the great element), ahankāra (the ego); uḷḷān – being the ātmā; iduvē – this itself; padi – form; enṟu – as; uraikkalām padiyan – one who has the form to say; allan – not being; param paran – being the one who is greater (than nityasūris and muktātmās who are greater than these entities here in samsāram); kadi sēr nāṟṟattuḷḷālai – fully immersed and enjoyed the collection of great fragrances; inbam – joy’s; tunbam – (due to being insignificant and impermanent) sorrow’s; kaḻi – having the elimination; nērmai – the subtle aspect’s; odiyā – eternal (due to having no breaks); inbam – joy’s; perumaiyōn – having the boundless nature; uṇarvil – in knowledge; umbar – being superior (like the joy which is eternal, boundless etc); oruvan – one; adiyēn – I (inside what is said as aham (I) which is identified exclusively by servitude); uḷḷān – is present as antarātmā inside; udal – in śarīram (body, which is to be rejected); uḷḷān – is residing in the heart too

**Перевод:**

**emperumān is the antarātmā for all entities inside the oval shaped universe and the entities such as avyakta (unmanifested matter), mahat (the great element), ahankāra (the ego) outside the universe; yet he cannot be said to be present in this form only \[not limited to few qualities/definitions\]; he is greater than all; he is having the greatness of subtle, eternal, unbounded joy, which is like the joy of being fully immersed and enjoyed the collection of great fragrances, after eliminating all the sorrow; his knowledge is greater than the superior ones’ (who have such joy as explained before); such great emperumān is present in me, the servitor; he is also inside the heart in my body. “padiyē idu” indicates the lack of similes for emperumān. The example of joy derived from fragrance, is given to instill faith in us \[to understand that bhagavān will be pure, without any blemish\] since there is no example for emperumān who is with ubhayalingam \[two aspects – with auspicious qualities, without any blemish\], with great knowledge/bliss which is distinguished from all other entities.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the second pāsuram, āḻvār says “emperumān who is greatly distinguished, not only mercifully entered me, he also mercifully entered my body”. Since āḻvār uses the word “adiyēn uḷḷān” (present in me, the servitor) where he should be using “en uḷḷān” (present in me), I and adiyēn are understood to be synonyms.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. adiyēn uḷḷān udal uḷḷān aṇḍattagattān puṟattuḷḷān padiyē iduvenṟuraikkalām padiyan allan param paran kadi sēr nāṟṟattuḷḷālai inbattunbak kaḻi nērmai odiyā inbap perumaiyōn uṇarvil umbar oruvanē*

- *adiyēn uḷḷān* – kūrattāḻvān, after serving tirukkōśtiyūr nambi for six months, was about to leave \[Once in [emperumānār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/emperumanar/)‘s kālakśēpam, a question arose on the true identity of ātmā – whether it is knowledge/bliss or servitude; emperumānār instructed [kūrattāḻvān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/kuraththazhwan/) to go to [tirukkōśtiyūr nambi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/thirukkoshtiyur-nambi/) and have the doubt clarified; he had gone there and spent six months serving [nambi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/thirukkoshtiyur-nambi/), but nambi never asked [āḻvān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/kuraththazhwan/) why he had come; thinking of returning to śrīrangam, being unable to handle the separation from [emperumānār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/emperumanar/), he decided to leave\]; nambi said to him “āḻvān! ? Have you not seen [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) saying ‘*adiyēn uḷḷān*‘?” āḻvān said “I am grateful for this insight”. Where āḻvār should have said “***en*** *uḷḷān*“, he said “***adiyēn*** *uḷḷān*“. This is because, ātmā is not identified by jñānam (knowledge) and ānandam (bliss); but is identified by śēśatvam (servitude). Implies that – servitude towards bhagavān is more intrinsic than knowledge and bliss.
- *udal uḷḷān* – Just as for the cētana (sentient being), bhagavān’s divine auspicious form is more desirable than bhagavān’s true nature, for īśvara, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s divine form is more desirable than āḻvār’s true nature; this is similar to prideful persons having desire for the dirt/sweat of their beloved ones. With this – the view points such are “jīva-para bhēdam (difference between jīvātmā and paramātmā), jīva paraspara bhēdam (difference among jīvātmās) and śēśa-śēṣi sambandam (servant-master relationship between jīvātmā and paramātmā) are false principles” are negated naturally.

When asked “who desires your divine form?” [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says,

- *aṇḍattu agattān puṟattuḷḷān* – One who is present in the entities which are present inside the oval shaped universe and outside it. Implies that, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is omnipresent, became captivated in an entity (āḻvār), that too in a small part (heart) of that entity.
- *padiyē idu* – “Is this his nature?”  He does not have a fully matching simile. Only if there is another entity which is omnipresent and which controls every other entity, can we cite that entity as a simile.

When asked “how can we explain him then?” [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says,

- *param paran* – One who is superior to all superior entities. As said in bruhadāraṇyaka upaniśat 4.3 “*nēti nēti’”*(not like this, not like this – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) cannot be understood in any specific way), we can only that he is unlike anything else.

When asked “Still, how can we try to understand him?” [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says,

- *kadi sēr nāṟṟattuḷ ālai* – ālai – madu (honey). Both kadi and nāṟṟam indicate parimaḷa (fragrance) – meaning “greatly fragrant”. Also, kadi could mean freshness, meaning “freshly fragrant”. Since parimaḷa is not a physical substance, the nāṟṟam (scent) of it is indicated.
- *inbat tunbak kaḻi nērmai* – There is pure enjoyment of that experience, which is the subtle joy – where all the sorrows from it are eliminated \[in this world, with every joy, there is an aspect of sorrow – eliminating that aspect\]. Since the fragrance in the flower is highlighted as the example, the sorrowful aspect \[blemish\] in that is its insignificant and temporary in nature; the subtle joy which is derived after eliminating such blemish; that is unblemiśed joy.
- *odiyā inbap perumaiyōn* – The uninterrupted and great joy. One who has eternal and perfect joy; as said in taittirīya upaniśat “*ānandamaya:*” (one who is filled with bliss).
- *uṇarvil umbar oruvanē* – One who is superior in knowledge. Saying that [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who has distinguished jñānam and ānandam.
- *odiyā inbap perumaiyōn uṇarvil umbar oruvan – adiyēn uḷḷān – udal uḷḷān* – One who is greatly desirable for everyone, is the one who desires my body.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.8.3. Unarvil umbar

*uṇarvil umbar oruvanai avanadaruḷāl uṟal poruttu enuṇarvil uḷḷē iruttinēn aduvum avanadinnaruḷēuṇarvum uyirum udambum maṟṟulappilanavum paḻudēyāmuṇarvaip peṟa ūrndiṟavēṟi yānum tānāy oḻindānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

uṇarvil – having abundant knowledge; umbar – being the full controller of nityasūris; oruvanai – distinguished one; avanadu – by his; aruḷāl – grace; uṟal poruttu – to reach; en – my; uṇarvinuḷḷē – in knowledge which is in the form of desire; iruttinēn – placed; aduvum – that desire too; avanadu – his; in aruḷē – was caused by his causeless mercy; “uṇarvum – knowledge in the form of actions; uyirum – five types of prāṇa (namely prāṇa, apāna, vyāna, udāna, samāna which facilitate actions); udambum – different types of body (for the different types of prāṇa); maṟṟu – further; ulappilanavum – (countless) mahat (the great element), ahankāra (ego), indriyas (senses) etc; paḻudu – to be given up”; Am – this; uṇarvai peṟa – to realise; uṇarndu – conducted; iṟa ēṟi – reaching up to (distinguished ātmā); yānum – consciousness and intelligence (which relate to the ātmā); tān āy oḻindān – had ātmā as his prakāram (form), to have it fully engage in him

**Перевод:**

**To reach emperumān, by his grace, I placed him, the distinguished one who is the controller of nityasūris who are having abundant knowledge, in my knowledge which is in the form of desire; that desire too was caused by his causeless mercy; he conducted himself to make me realise “the knowledge in the form of actions, five types of prāṇa , different types of body, mahat, ahankāra and indriya are all to be given up”, reaching up to the distinguished ātmā to have my consciousness and intelligence, and had me \[ātmā, self\] as his prakāram, to have it fully engage in him.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the third pāsuram, āḻvār says “emperumān purely out of his own mercy created desire in me towards him, united with me, showed the nature of ātmā having knowledge, bliss and purity and being sustained with servitude towards him, to make such union remain firm”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. uṇarvil umbar oruvanai avanadaruḷāl uṟal poruttu enuṇarvil uḷḷē iruttinēn aduvum avanadinnaruḷēuṇarvum uyirum udambum maṟṟulappilanavum paḻudēyāmuṇarvaip peṟa ūrndiṟavēṟi yānum tānāy oḻindānē*

- *uṇarvil umbar oruvanai* – nityasiddas (nityasūris, eternal residents of paramapadam) who are knowledgeable; the distinguished one who has the existence etc of the most knowledgeable nityasūris, at his disposal. With this, the nature of the prāpyam (goal), is explained. The attainable goal is [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), who is as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.1.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/03/thiruvaimozhi-1-1-1-uyarvara-uyarnalam/) “*ayarvaṟum amarargaḷ adipati*” (the lord of nityasūris). [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) too prayed in [tiruvāimoḻi – 2.3.10](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/02/thiruvaimozhi-2-3-10-kalippum-kavarvum/) “*adiyārgaḷ kuḻāngaḷai udan kūduvadu enṟu kolō*” (When will I be amidst the nityasūris?)
- *avanadu aruḷāl* – With his mercy. Just as there is a preference that bhagavān is the goal, the means is also his mercy.
- *uṟal poruttu* – To attain.

When asked “If he is the goal as well as the means, what is your part?” [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says,

- *en uṇarvin uḷḷē iruttinēn* – I made him the object of my knowledge. He already said in tiruvāimoḻi 8.7.10 “*vaittēn madiyāl*” (I placed him in my intelligence). Implies “I desired”.

When asked “Is that desire, under your control?” [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says,

- *aduvum avanadu in aruḷē* – Even that desire occurred in me due to his mercy. His kind heart is such that, at every step āḻvār will recollect and say “this occurred due to his mercy”. After saying in [tiruvāimoḻi 8.7.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/04/thiruvaimozhi-8-7-1-iruththum-viyandhu/) “*than ponnadik kīḻ – iruttum viyandum*” (will place me at his divine feet – being astonished) that he is the goal and means, āḻvār said “*aruttittu*” (seeking him); he is saying the same thing here.

Up to here, in these two and half pāsurams, the greatness of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) has been explained; subsequently, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says that emperumān has shown the greatness of the nature of the ātmā.

- *uṇarvum* – knowledge about matter.
- *uyirum* – Five prāṇas.
- *udambum* – body
- *maṟṟu ulappilanavum* – the other aspects such as the inconceivable mahat and its many transformed states, and prakruti (primordial matter).
- *paḻudēyām uṇarvaip peṟa ūrndu* –  conducting in such a manner that I acquire the knowledge which highlights “all of these are to be rejected”; just as riding a chariot \[just as a king will ride his own chariot in search of wealth during difficult situations, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) himself took control and made me understand this; alternative meaning – arjuna’s chariot is the victorious caritot; just as [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) became the charioteer for that chariot and eliminated bhīśma et al, emperumān rode [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s body which is the chariot, by being in his heart and eliminated the worldly knowledge etc\]. That is – there is a knowledge which highlights that everything else is apuruśārtam (not a goal) – this knowledge is called mayarvaṟa mati (unblemiśed knowledge); he gave that knowledge to me.
- *iṟa ēṟi* – Not just to highlight that matter and material aspirations are not goals, but to completely eliminate them. Showing that the ātmā is made of knowledge and bliss and is fully focussed on servitude towards bhagavān only.
- *iṟa ēṟi* – Lifting me up to that top level of understanding.
- *yānum tānāy oḻindānē* – He did not stop at that; he showed me that I am his prakāram (form) to the extent that if a word indicates me, that word would indicate him too. When some one calls me “āḻvīr!”, before I could respond, īśvara would say “What?” He showed that the word “*aham*” (I) and the understanding of that word indicate him. \[In cāndōjña upaniśat vākyam (phrase) “*tatvamasi*” (that is you)\] just as “tat” (that) indicates bhagavān with qualities, “*tvam*” (you) stretches up to the antaryāmi (indvelling supersoul) of the ātmā which is with the acit (body).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

adiyen saraty ramanuja dasan

## 8.8.4. Yanum tanay

*yānum tānāy oḻindānai yādum yavarkkum munnōnai tānum sivanum piramanumāgip paṇaitta tani mudalait tēnum pālum kannalum amudumāgit tittittu en vānil uyiril uṇarvinil ninṟa onṟai uṇarndēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

yādum yavarkkum – for all cētanas (sentient beings) and acētanas (insentient objects) in the samaśti (collective) form; munnōnai – being the cause (who exists in the previous moment \[before the manifestation\]); tānum – himself (who is in charge for rakśaṇam (protection) as part of the vyaśti (variegated) sruśti (creation) etc); sivanum – rudra (who is in charge for samhāram (annihilation)); piramanum āgi – being brahmā (who is in charge for sruśti (creation)); paṇaitta – who expanded; tani mudalai – primordial causal entity; tēnum pālum kannalum amudum āgi – being enjoyable as per his desire; tittittu – relish; en – my; ūnil – in the body; uyiril – in my prāṇa (vital air); uṇarvinil – in my jñāna (knowledge); ninṟa – remaining exclusively in an inseparable manner; onṟai – ātma svarūpa (true nature of the self); yānum – the meaning of the word “aham” (I); tān āy oḻindānai – one who is; uṇarndēn – I understood

**Перевод:**

**emperumān, the primordial causal entity, being the cause for all cētanas and acētanas , expanded as himself, rudra and brahmā; being enjoyable as per his desire to relish, he remains exclusively in an inseparable manner in my body, prāṇa, jñāna with my ātmā; I understood him who is the meaning of the word “aham” (I).**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fourth pāsuram, āḻvār says “emperumān mercifully showed that this ātmā is very enjoyable for him”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “I have understood the inseparable relationship of emperumān with ātmā which is enjoyable in all manners to emperumān who is the cause of all, as said in ‘aham annam‘ (I am the food)”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. yānum tānāy oḻindānai yādum yavarkkum munnōnai tānum sivanum piramanumāgip paṇaitta tani mudalait tēnum pālum kannalum amudumāgit tittittu en vānil uyiril uṇarvinil ninṟa onṟai uṇarndēnē*

- *yānum tānāy oḻindānai* – Due to his liking in the previously explained *ananyārha śēśatvam* (exclusive servitude), [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is repeating the same.
- *yādum …* – By “*yādum yavarkkum*“, āḻvār explains the cētanas and acētanas in causal state.
- *munnōnai* – Cause is that which explains in the previous moment of the effect. \[Hence [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is rightly said as munnōn – one who is there first\]
- *tānum …* – He who incarnated amidst brahmā and rudra. One who is the distinguished cause who expanded as the effectual entities such as brahmā, rudra et al; when all the cētanas and acētanas were in the annihilated state \[during deluge\] he protected them by keeping them attached to his body in a subtle form like subdued rays in their energy form. At the time of creation, he separated them from his body. He performs up to the creation of universes himself \[directly\]. He creates brahmā et al \[prajāpatis (progenitors)\] who are primary beings among the residents of the universes. He remains with his own divine form \[viṣṇu\] and engages in protection, while performing creation and annihilation by being the controller of the bodies and souls of brahmā and rudra. In this manner, he is the one who conducts his own activities and the activities of brahmā, rudra et al without any distinction.
- *tēnum* – For whom is this \[[ātmā/cētana](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)\] enjoyable? Just as [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is enjoyable for the cētana as said in “*sarvarasa:*” (the source of all tastes), for īśvara, this \[ātmā\] is enjoyable. For īśvara, it will be reliśable since he considers it to be his belonging. For cētana, it will be reliśable since he considers it to be īśvara’s belonging. Even prior to understanding that the self is “*īśvara paratantran*” (one who is totally subservient to īśvara), it is reliśable to make one think “let me enjoy myself”.
- *en ūnil …* – I came to know about [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who has the distinguished [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) which is pervading in my body, vital air and knowledge, as his body. “*ninṟa onṟu*” indicates the jīvātmā; here [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is stretching it up to īśvara who is the substratum \[prakāri, for that ātmā\]. Since āḻvār is not focussed on self, he will always point up to the indvelling bhagavān. Here, ātmā’s enjoyability is explained; but how is his kāraṇatvam (being the cause) explained? \[āḻvār says to reveal that\] He created the cētanas \[gave appropriate bodies to them\] according to their karma; he bestowed wealth for brahmā et al who are seekers of wealth; for me, he revealed that acit aspects (body etc) are to be given up, wealth is not an apt benefit and ātmā is exclusively subservient to him and greatly enjoyable by him. Similar to [tiruvāimoḻi 1.1.6](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/04/thiruvaimozhi-1-1-6-ninranar-irunthanar/) “*ninṟanar irundanar*” pāsuram, here too, the focus is on sāmānādikaraṇyam (sāmānādikaraṇyam means more than one aspect/attribute having one common substratum. It also means two or more words focussed on explaining a single entity. A simple example is mrud gatam (clay pot). This talks about gatam (pot) being the substratum and having two attributes – being made of mrud (soil/clay) and gatatvam (being a pot). Another example is “śukla: pata:” (white cloth). This talks about patam (cloth) being the substratum and having two attributes – śukla (white color) and patatvam (being a cloth). Similarly, [brahmam](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)/[bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) being the substratum of all entities is explained through this principle of sāmānādikaraṇyam. This is a separate and detailed subject which can be learned from scholars who are well versed in samskruta vyākaraṇam and vēdāntam) based on the enjoyability which is an attribute. Even for the vaiyadikaraṇyam (vaiyadikaraṇyam means two or more aspects having different substratum. For example, a chair may be held by the earth and a flower pot may be held by a table. It also means two or more words that are focussed on explaining different entities), the pure difference \[among cit, acit and īśvara\] which is explained generally by people is not the meaning; for the sāmānādikaraṇyam too, svarūpa aikyam (jīvātmā and paramātmā literally being the same) is not the meaning. pāsuram should be recited as “*yādum yavarkkum munnōnai … en ūnil uyiril uṇarvinil ninṟa onṟana … yānum tānāy oḻindānai … uṇarndē*“

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.8.5. Ninra onrai

*ninṟa onṟai uṇarndēnukku adanuḷ nērmai adu idu enṟu onṟum oruvarkku uṇaral āgādu uṇarndu mēlum kāṇbaridu senṟu senṟu param paramāy yādum inṟit tēyndaṟṟu nanṟu tīdenṟaṟivaridāy nanṟāy jñānam kadandadē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ninṟa onṟai – ātmā which is eternal (and made of knowledge only); uṇarndēnukku – for me who saw it (as he showed as his prakāra (form)); adanuḷ – its; nērmai – subtle, distinguished nature; onṟum – any; oruvarkku – even for those who are fully knowledgeable; adu idu enṟu – to be in a particular manner; uṇaral āgādu – cannot be known (through śravaṇam (hearing), mananam (meditation) etc); uṇarndum – even if known (with great efforts); mēlum – even while gone upto the level of samādi (trance); kāṇbu aridu – will be difficult to see directly; param paramāy – going further over every entity; senṟu senṟu – passing through; yādum – with their nature (such as change); inṟi – without having; tēyndu – being very subtle; aṟṟu – eliminating (their connection); nanṟu tīdu – having virtues and vices (which occur based on their desires); enṟu – as; aṟivu aridu āy – being difficult to know; nanṟu āy – having distinguished knowledge and bliss ( which is distinguished in all manners); jñānam – for the knowledge (which supports them); kadandadu – beyond

**Перевод:**

**The ātmā which is eternal and seen by me – its subtle, distinguished nature cannot be known  to be in a particular manner even for those who are fully knowledgeable; even if known and pursued up to the level of samādi, it will be difficult to see it directly; passing through and going further over every entity (namely body, senses, mind, vital air, knowledge), without having any change, being very subtle and eliminating the connection with such entities, being difficult to know as having virtues and vices, having distinguished knowledge and bliss, the ātmā remains beyond the reach of knowledge. In this pāsuram, the distinguished nature of ātmā is explained through the philosophy of sānkhya.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fifth pāsuram, āḻvār says “This ātmā (self) which I realised by bhagavān‘s prasādam (mercy) cannot be known by anyone; even if known, it cannot be realised”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Fifth pāsuram. embār mercifully explains “Previously – ātmā was explained as bhagavān‘s prakāram (form/attribute); from here onvards, just as the whiteness on a cloth will be explained separately using separate words, up to the pāsuram ‘em pemmānōdu‘, ātmā’s distinctive nature is explained”. mudaliyāṇḍān says “ātmā is explained as prakāram of  bhagavān”. In the ātmā which is explained as “ninṟa onṟai“, it is highlighted by āḻvār “this ātmā which is seen by bhagavān’s mercy, cannot be known by anyone and even if one knows about it with great efforts, one cannot see it”. ninṟa onṟai uṇarndēnukku adanuḷ nērmai adu idu enṟu onṟum oruvarkku uṇaral āgādu uṇarndu mēlum kāṇbaridu senṟu senṟu param paramāy yādum inṟit tēyndaṟṟu nanṟu tīdenṟaṟivaridāy nanṟāy jñānam kadandadē*

- *ninṟa onṟai* – The [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) which is different from body, senses, mind, vital air and knowledge, the one which remains alive in a singular form even when these perish, being the controller for these, and distinguished.
- *uṇarndēnukku* – For me who analysed. Since [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is the one who immersed in emperumān’s auspicious qualities as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.1.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/03/thiruvaimozhi-1-1-1-uyarvara-uyarnalam/) “*uyarvaṟa uyarnalam*” (most superior, auspicous qualities), he did not focus on the nature of the self which appears like firefly in front of emperumān, until now; since his tools are jñāna in the form of bhakti, he did not have time to engage in self.

When asked “How did you feel about it when you analysed it?” āḻvār says,

- *adanuḷ nērmai* – It’s greatness.
- *adu idu enṟu* – It cannot be known as what is realised or experienced.
- *onṟum oruvarkku uṇaral āgādu* – Even for those with great knowledge, the slightest aspect of it cannot be understood.
- *uṇarndu mēlum kāṇbaridu* – As said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 11.54](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/11-54/) “*… jñātum draśtum ca tatvēna …*” (Oh arjuna! One who roasts the enemies! Only with the assistance of bhakti, I, like this, can be truly known, seen and attained), it cannot be known, and even if known, it cannot be seen.
- *senṟu senṟu param paramāy* – Going step by step, being greater than one after the other. Being beyond the different layers such as annamaya (layer of body), prāṇamaya (layer of vital air) and manōmaya (layer of mind).
- *yādum inṟit tēndaṟṟu* – Not having any of their qualities \[such as change etc\] and being totally disconnected from them.
- *nanṟu tīdu enṟu aṟivaridāy* – As senses are greater than body, mind is greater than senses, vital air is greater than mind and so on, it will be difficult to be comprehended as good or bad based on material conceptions.
- *jñānam kadandadē* – Will be beyond the knowledge acquired through senses. In acit (matter), though each entity is distinguished from one another, they have equality in being perceivable by physical senses; even that is not possible for [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/). Thus, in this pāsuram, the manner in which the ātmā is described in sānkhya philosophy through entity numbering system, and the difficulty in understanding the same are explained.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.8.6. Nanray jnanam

*nanṟāy jñānam kadandu pōy nallindiriyam ellām īrttu onṟāyk kidandu arum perum pāḻ ulappil adanai uṇarnduṇarndu senṟānginbat tunbangaḷ seṟṟuk kaḷaindu pasai aṟṟāl anṟē appōdē vīdu aduvē vīdu vīdāmē*

**Пословный перевод:**

nanṟu āy – having purity (of being free from attachment towards materialistic objects); jñānam – knowledge (which relates to such matters); kadandu – escaping; pōy – moving away (far from them); nal – having goodness (of engaging him with such worldly knowledge \[and eventually leading to spiritual matters\]); indiriyam – senses; ellām – all; īrttu – eliminate; onṟāyk kidanda – being together with cētana (to be unable to distinguish from each other as said in “tilatailavat dāruvahnivat” \[like oil present inside sesame seed and fire present inside firewood\]); arum – unfathomable; peru – being unlimited (as said in “anantasya na tasyānta: sankyānam vāpi vidyatē“); ulappil pāḻ – being countless; pāḻ adanai – prakruti tatvam (primordial matter); uṇarndu uṇarndu – knowing well repeatedly (through śravaṇam (hearing), mananam (meditation) etc); senṟu – going; angu – in that ātmā related matters; inbat tunbangaḷ – joy and sorrow (which are resulting from previous virtues and vices); seṟṟuk kaḷaindu – eliminating along with the cause; pasai – attachment (in those matters such as vāsanā (impressions), ruci (taste)); aṟṟāl – when eliminated; anṟē – on that day; appōdē – at that moment; vīdu – will be freed (from all defects of this samsāram); aduvē – that is; vīdu – ātmānubhava mōkśam (liberation of enjoying the self); vīdāmē – ātmā being prakāra to bhagavān and being distinguished, it is reasonable to say that this self enjoyment is also part of the goal

**Перевод:**

**If those who are pure, escape worldly knowledge and move away, eliminating all of the good senses \[attachment to sense organs\], knowing well repeatedly about the unfathomable, unlimited, variegated \[countless\] prarkuti (primordial matter) which is being together with cētana, go in to those ātmā related matters and eliminate joy and sorrow, along with their cause, and eliminate the attachment towards them, on that day, at that moment itself they will be freed; that is ātmānubhava mōkśam; ātmā being prakāra to bhagavān and being distinguished, it is reasonable to say that this self enjoyment is also part of the goal.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the sixth pāsuram, āḻvār says “In yōga śāstram, overcoming the senses etc are highlighted as a means for realising ātmā; through that, with great difficulty, one can realise the ātmā which is free from matter”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. nanṟāy jñānam kadandu pōy nallindiriyam ellām īrttu onṟāyk kidandu arum perum pāḻ ulappil adanai uṇarnduṇarndu senṟānginbat tunbangaḷ seṟṟuk kaḷaindu pasai aṟṟāl anṟē appōdē vīdu aduvē vīdu vīdāmē*

- *nanṟāy jñānam kadandu pōy* – Having distinguished goodness \[nanṟāy\]; since it \[[ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/)\] is beyond the comprehensions of the senses, it is repeated here. \[Another explanation\] \[Here, jñānam is treated as worldly pleasures such as śabda etc which are understood by jñānam\] While the pure ātmā is present, escaping the worldly pleasures. As per “*jñāyata iti jñānam*“, here the worldly pleasures are said as jñānam; whatever is perceived by jñānam, is indicated by the word jñānam here.
- *nal indiriyam ellām īrttu* – Even if one escapes the pleasures, the senses which have the ability to reach out to those pleasures, are present; eliminating those senses too.
- *onṟāyk kidanda …* – acit tatvam (prakruti, the primordial matter) which remains present along with the cētana, which is difficult to crossover by anyone as said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 7-13](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/7-13/) “*mama māyā duratyayā*” (it is difficult to crossover my primordial matter), having expansive nature in its mahat (the great element), ahankāram (ego) forms, which facilitates enjoyment and liberation, and which is eternal both in pravāharūpam (continuous existence) and svarūpam (true nature); knowing well that prakruti remains both in causal and effectual state.
- *āngu nanṟāy senṟu* – Instead of focussing on such prakruti which will cause the attitude of enjoyment, reaching up to the true nature of self.
- *inbat tunbam …* – Even if one gives it up considering it to be given up, if the puṇya and pāpa which cause joy and sorrow remain, that will again lead to the same routine; giving them up.

Even if these are given up, if ruci and vāsanā remain, they will again come up.

- *pasai aṟṟāl* – if ruci and vāsanā too are given up.
- *anṟē appōdē* – On that same day, at that same moment.
- *vīdu* – The connection with matter and matter related aspects will be eliminated. There is none like prakruti in shyness and tenderness. It does not care for those who give it up.
- *aduvē vīdu* – As said in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.2.5](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/05/thiruvaimozhi-1-2-5-arrathu-parru/) “*aṟṟadu paṟṟenil uṟṟadu vīduyir*” (When attachments towards aspects outside bhagavat viśayam are given up, [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) is fit to attain (kaivalya) mōkśam), once attachment towards worldly pleasures are eliminated, one will attain ātma prāpti mōkśam (liberation of self enjoyment). There is nothing more to be done.
- *vīdāmē* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) thinks [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) to be a prakāram of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) and in that manner considers it to be the goal. Even for those who see this self enjoyment and remain at this level without reaching up to [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/), it remains as an option! – says āḻvār. Previously āḻvār laughed at this \[in [tiruvāimoḻi 4.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/11/thiruvaimozhi-4-1-orunayagamay/), as an inferior goal\] since it was considered as the ultimate goal \[by others\], though it is only a small aspect of āḻvār’s goal \[of eternal enjoyment of emperumān\].

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.8.7. Aduve vidu

*aduvē vīdu vīdu pēṟṟu inbandānum adu tēṟi eduvē tānum paṟṟinṟi yādumiligaḷāgiṟkil aduvē vīdu vīdu pēṟṟu inbandānum adu tēṟādu eduvē vīdu? ēdinbam enṟeyttār eyttār eyttārē*

**Пословный перевод:**

aduvē – the enjoyment of self (who is a form of bhagavān, as explained previously); vīdu – is mōkśam (liberation); vīdu pēṟu – attained from that liberation; inbam tānum adu – the joy itself; tēṟi – determined; eduvē tānum – all matter and material aspects; paṟṟu – attachment (in them being enjoyment, the tools for enjoyment and the abodes for enjoyment); inṟi – eliminating; yādum – ruci (taste) and vāsanā (impression) (which came about from that attachment); iligaḷ āgiṟkil – when eliminated; aduvē – that ātmā anubhavam (self enjoyment, which was highlighted previously); vīdu – liberation; vīdu pēṟu – caused by that liberation; inbam tānum – bliss; adu – that is; tēṟādu – without determining (the ātmā to be a form of bhagavān); ‘edu – what is; vīdu – liberation?; inbam – joy (attained from that); edu – what is?’; enṟu – as; eyttār – those who have mental weakness; eyttār eyttārē – will suffer due to entering into womb and hell \[remain for ever in samsāram\]

**Перевод:**

**The enjoyment of self is mōkśam; having determined that the joy attained from that liberation as the goal, when attachment from all matter and material aspects and ruci and vāsana are eliminated, that is liberation and the bliss caused by such liberation; those who have mental weakness, being unable to determine “what is liberation? what is joy?” will suffer due to entering into womb and hell.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the seventh pāsuram, āḻvār says “If one can give up ātmā instead of pursuing it as said here \[previously, as an independent entity instead of considering it to be bhagavān’s subservient entity\], that will be the liberation and the joy acquired through such liberation”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “Those who don’t pursue ātmā as explained previously, will suffer in samsāram without experiencing ātmā”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Seventh pāsuram. āḻvār says “Those who don’t attain ātmā with the help of the means explained previously, having doubts in that, will suffer greatly”. aduvē vīdu vīdu pēṟṟu inbandānum adu tēṟi eduvē tānum paṟṟinṟi yādumiligaḷāgiṟkil aduvē vīdu vīdu pēṟṟu inbandānum adu tēṟādu eduvē vīdu? ēdinbam enṟeyttār eyttār eyttārē*

- *aduvē vīdu* – Whatever has been explained previously is the liberation of attaining self realisation/enjoyment.
- *vīdu pēṟṟu inbam tānum adu* – That is the joy acquired while attaining such libertaion.
- *tēṟi* – having clarity in this manner
- *eduvē tānum paṟṟu inṟi* – Being detached from matter and material aspects.
- *yādum iligaḷ āgiṟṟil* – When freed from ruci and vāsanā in them. Practicing karma \[yōga\], having jñāna \[yōga\], attaining the state of “*stita prajña*” \[Can be seen in śrī bhagavat gītā 2nd chapter from [ślōkam 54](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/2-54/)\], being established in yōga, when one attains self realisation.
- *aduvē vīdu* – That ātma prāpti (attaining self) explained previously, is liberation.
- *vīdu pēṟṟu inbam tānum adu* – The joy acquired in that liberated state is also part of that self enjoyment.
- *tēṟādu* – Not having clarity in this manner.
- *eduvē vīdu ēdu inbam enṟu eyttār* – Those who become weak thinking “What is mōkśam? What is the joy acquired in that state of mōkśam?”
- *eyttār eyttārē* – They will greatly suffer by repeatedly weakening; meditating upon the true nature of ātmā without the proper practice of yōga śāśtram or without being supported by [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/), is of no use.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.8.8. Eyttar eyttar

*eyttār eyttār eyttār enṟu illattārum puṟattārum moyttu āngalaṟi muyangat tām pōgumbōdu unmattar pōl pittē ēṟi anurāgam poḻiyum pōdu embemmānōdu ottē senṟu anguḷḷam kudak kūdiṟṟāgil nal uṟaippē*

**Пословный перевод:**

eyttār – became weak (to not have their limbs engage in activities); eyttār – became weak (to have the senses lose the ability to grasp matters); eyttār – became weak (to even stop breathing); enṟu – as; illattārum – the wife, children et al in the house; puṟattārum – and other relatives; moyttu – gathered; āngu – in that stage; alaṟi – wailing and crying out; muyanga – as they approach; tām – they; pōgumbōdu – in that final moments; unmattar pōlē – like an intoxicated person; pittē ēṟi – being bewildered; anurāgam – attachment; poḻiyumpōdu – when it pours out; em pemmānōdu ottē senṟu – as īśvara, my lord considers him \[the soul\] to be a servitor, the soul too should meditate that he is servitor to emperumān; angu – towards emperumān; uḷḷam – (his) heart; kūdak kūdiṟṟāgil – if it went and united; nal – good; uṟaippu – stability

**Перевод:**

**As the wife, children et al in the house and the other relatives gather around saying “he has become weak in his limbs, senses and breath” and wailed, crying out and approached the ailing persons, they remained like an intoxicated person in the final moments, being bewildered; when attachment pours out to those family members and relatives in those final moments, if the ātmā places its heart towards emperumān, meditating upon him considering him as the lord, as īśvara, and considers himself \[ātmā\] to be emperumān’s servitor, and goes and unites with emperumān, that is good stability. One will attain the self which is a prakāra (form) of bhagavān. Implies āḻvār saying “emperumān easily revealed such state of self realisation which is difficult to attain”.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the eighth pāsuram, āḻvār says “Even if one becomes an expert in the hard-earned knowledge, without antimasmruti (remembrance at the final moments), all the difficulties one went through to earn that knowledge will go in vain”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. eyttār eyttār eyttār enṟu illattārum puṟattārum moyttu āngalaṟi muyangat tām pōgumbōdu unmattar pōl pittē ēṟi anurāgam poḻiyum pōdu embemmānōdu ottē senṟu anguḷḷam kudak kūdiṟṟāgil nal uṟaippē*

- *eyttār eyttār eyttār enṟu* – Since many people would like for him \[the person highlighted here\] to die even before his time is up, they would repeatedly say “he has become weak”. Instead of bringing clarity in his mind during his bewildered state so that he can meditate upon the apt aspect, they would keep saying “he has become weak” \[to bewilder him further\].
- *illattārum puṟattārum* – His wife et al would think “Why is he still alive with his great paraphernalia? Can we not share his wealth after he dies quickly?” since he did not give them anything while he was alive.
- *puṟattārum* – Other relatives would think “it would be nice if he dies” since they cannot bear seeing his presence along with his family.
- *moyttu* – They will gather around during difficult times \[even without invitation, to see his suffering\] while they never attended any auspicious occassions even after being invited.
- *āngu alaṟi* – They will cry out so hard that he loses whatever clarity he has; when there is hope for his survival, they will cry out so hard that he will die out of fear.
- *muyanga* – To embrace. To eliminate his remaining life which did not leave even after such crying out, they will embrace just as friends would do.
- *tām pōgumbōdu* – While the heart pulls toward them thinking “Why do I have to leave them \[family, relatives\] and this wealth?” they will leave their body themselves since there is no way to stop death. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says “*tām pōgumpōdu*“, thinking about the great suffering at that last moment.
- *unmattar …* – Even those who are free from attachment, will become bewildered as if in an intoxicated state; being bewildered in that state when one should acquire clarity and think about self and sarvēśvara.
- *anurāgam poḻiyumpōdu* – They will dress up the younger wife with golden ornaments and make her stand in front of him. He will start showing great affection towards his children, for the days he missed on showing his affection towards them. While living comfortably, due to his greed, he will not do anything for them; but now, he will show overwhelming affection thinking “I should have brought all the buried wealth out and decorated them with the ornaments”.
- *em pemmānōdu ottē senṟu …* – If one understands the principle of meditaing upon the self to be as pure as [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) himself, at this bewildering time, with clarity. To think “emperumān is identified with his jñānam (knowledge) and ānandam (bliss); this [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) is also identified with jñānam and ānandam”. If one understands the principle of having the heart focussed on the ātmā.
- *nal uṟaippu* – Good opportunity. Otherwise, whatever was done thus far, will go in vain. If one become beviledered like an intoxicated person, their desired result will not be attained; if one shows overwhelming attachment towards family, relatives and wealth, one will become like a deer as it occurred to ādibharata \[a great jñāna yōgi, who took birth as a deer, since he remembered the deer which he raised, at his final moments\]. mudaliyāṇḍān’s explanation – from “*ninṟa onṟai uṇarndēnukku*” pāsuram, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is highlighting not just the [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) exclusively, but ātmā as a servitor of bhagavān; in this pāsuram, antima smruti (remembrance during final moments) as said in “*em pemmānōdu ottē senṟu anguḷḷam kūdak kūdiṟṟāgil”* and “just as [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) considers this ātmā to be his servitor, the ātmā should reciprocate emperumān’s thought and meditate upon his servitude towards emperumān, to have a good chance to unite with him”. Why is āḻvār who is overwhelmingly immersed in bhagavān’s qualities thinking/speaking about these aspects? This is due to his gratitude towards emperumān thinking “emperumān revealed me such ātmā which is so difficult to attain”.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.
