## 8.8.9. Kudirragil

*kūdiṟṟāgil nal uṟaippu kūdāmaiyaik kūdināl ādaṟpaṟavai uyar kodi em māyan āvadu adu aduvē vīdaip paṇṇi oru parisē edirvum nigaḻvum kaḻivumāy ōdit tiriyum yōgigaḷum uḷarum illai allarē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kūdiṟṟāgil – if it is possible (that the jīvātmā who is a nitya samsāri is the same as brahmam who is greatly distinguished); nal – good; uṟaippu – will it not be an unacievable feat that is attained?; kūdāmaiyai – seen as impossible to occur in this world, such as rabbit having a horn; kūdināl – only if those occur; adu – that jīvātmā; ādal – having beautiful movements (due to close proximity to bhagavān); paṟavai – periya tiruvadi (garudāḻvār); uyar kodi – having as great flag (highlighting emperumān’s greatness); em – enjoyable by his devotees; māyan āvadu – will become sarvēśvara who has amazing svarūpa (nature), rūpa (form), guṇa (qualities); aduvē – that jīvātmā will remain itself; oru parisē – by the individual’s intelligence; vīdai – mōkśam (liberation); paṇṇi – imagined; edirvum – future times; nigaḻvum – present times; kaḻivum – past times, without any distinction; āy – being in the same state; ōdi – running (swiftly as said in “samsāra padavīm vrajan“); tiriyum – those who roam around; yōgigaḷum – yōgis; uḷarum – are present; illai allarē – they are not absent

**Перевод:**

**If it is possible \[for ātmā to become sarvēśvara\], will it not be an unacievable, good feat that is attained? Only if those which are seen as impossible to occur in this world, such as rabbit having a horn, occur, that jīvātmā will become sarvēśvara who has amazing svarūpa (nature), rūpa (form), guṇa (qualities), who is enjoyable by his devotees, who is having periya tiruvadi who is having beautiful movements, as his great flag; that jīvātmā will remain itself; yōgis who imagine such mōkśam \[of ātmā becoming brahmam\] by their intelligence, who remain in the same state in future, present and past times and who run and roam around, are present; they are not absent. Implies that even such great yōgis \[who imagine ātmā to become brahmam\] exist and condemns them.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the ninth pāsuram, while explaining antima smruti (remembrance during final moments), the presence of īśvara and ātmā is emphasised; māyāvādis (those who propound the philosophy of everything other than brahmam being illusion) say “there is no such difference between these entities; this ātmā and brahmam are the same” highlighting the cētana who is a nitya samsāri (one who has been in samsāra eternally) to be the same as brahmam, āḻvār condemns them.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. kūdiṟṟāgil nal uṟaippu kūdāmaiyaik kūdināl ādaṟpaṟavai uyar kodi em māyan āvadu adu aduvē vīdaip paṇṇi oru parisē edirvum nigaḻvum kaḻivumāy ōdit tiriyum yōgigaḷum uḷarum illai allarē*

- *kūdiṟṟāgil nal uṟaippu* – Re-emphasising.
- *kūdāmai …* – If non-existing entities such as rabbit horn, lotus on the sky, sterile woman’s son comes to existence, samsāri cētana (bound soul) can become the one having periya tiruvadi who is dancing blissfully due to being sarvēśvara’s vehicle, as his flag, having amazing qualities and activities, and one decorating the shoulders of periya tiruvadi.
- *adu aduvē* – [ātmā](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) will remain itself; an entity cannot become another entity.

When asked “Is there someone who speaks about samsāri cētana to be the one \[emperumān\] who is greater than nityasiddas (eternal residents of paramapadam)?” [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says,

- *vīdaip paṇṇi oru parisē* – Instead of basing it from śāstram, just based on their intelligence, imagining that the elimination of ignorance is liberation \[māyāvāda philosophy says when the ātmā gets rid of ignorance, it becomes brahmam\].
- *edirvum nigaḻvum kaḻivumāy* – Those who are present in past. future and present times.
- *ōdit tiriyum yōgigaḷum uḷarum* – The great yōgis who roam around without any \[worldly\] expectation are present.
- *illai allarē* – Their absence is inapplicable. Time is eternal; there is no end to the sins which are committed. In this should there not be such great yōgis \[[āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) being sarcastic\]? Is there anything impossible in samsāram?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.8.10. Ularum illai

*uḷarum illai allarāy uḷarāy illai āgiyē uḷar em oruvar avar vandu en uḷḷattuḷḷē uṟaiginṟār vaḷarum piṟaiyum tēy piṟaiyum pōla asaivum ākkamum vaḷarum sudarum iruḷum pōl teruḷum maruḷum māyttōmē*

**Пословный перевод:**

illai – for the word “No” in matters relating to his devotees; allarāy – not being applicable; uḷarum – always being present; illai āgiyē – as absent (for those who are not devoted towards him); uḷarāy – being present; em – for us (with his true nature, form and qualities); oruvar – being distinguished; uḷar – revealed; avar – he; vandu – arrived (with intent); en – my; uḷḷattuḷḷē – in heart; uṟaiginṟār – is eternally residing; vaḷarum piṟai pōla – like waxing moon; ākkamum – creation; tēy piṟaiyum pōla – like waning moon; asaivum – annihilation; vaḷarum sudarum pōl – like sun with growing radiance; teruḷum – jñānam (knowledge); iruḷum pōl – like darkness; maruḷum – ignorance; māyttōm – we destroyed

**Перевод:**

**emperumān revealed his distinguished nature of being always present for his devotees and not being applicable for the word “No” for them, and being always absent for others; he arrived in my heart and is eternally residing there; (due to that) I destroyed the creation which is like a waxing moon and annihilation which is like a waning moon, and jñānam which is like a sun with growing radiance and ignorance which is like darkness. Implies that the incidental growth and decay, knowledge and ignorance were eliminated, and saw the ātmā which is in a singular nature.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the tenth pāsuram, āḻvār says “As emperumān who is my lord, saved me from entering in to kudruśti matams (philosophies which misinterpret vēdam) such as sānkhya etc, and eternally united with me, all my sorrows were eliminated”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. uḷarum illai allarāy uḷarāy illai āgiyē uḷar em oruvar avar vandu en uḷḷattuḷḷē uṟaiginṟār vaḷarum piṟaiyum tēy piṟaiyum pōla asaivum ākkamum vaḷarum sudarum iruḷum pōl teruḷum maruḷum māyttōmē*

- *uḷarum illai allarāy* – sēśvara sānkhya matam \[the sānkhya matam which accepts the existence of god) explains “īśvara is present. He simply exists so that he cannot be nullified”; it says – just as a bhartā (husband) who lacks the ability to order/refrain \[the members of family\], īśvara merely exists without the ability to control the universe.
- *uḷarāy illai āgiyē* – nirīśvara sānkhya matam \[the sānkhya matam which rejects the existence of god) says “The truth of īśvara is that he does not exist”; [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is rejecting these view points. Alternative explanation in the context of devotees and others – for devotees, he will be present, and will not remain as non-existent; and for others he will be present but remain non-existent.
- *uḷar em oruvar* – Being the distinguished, complete one with qualities, wealth etc, who pursued me showing them.
- *avar vandu en uḷḷattuḷḷē uṟaiginṟār* – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is great in qualities, arrived at me and eternally resided in my heart which was reformed by him as said in tiruvāimoḻi 1.1.1 “*mayarvaṟa madinalam aruḷinan*” (one who bestowed faultless knowledge and devotion).
- *vaḷarum …* – Just as darkness will not remain in the presence of light, as he eternally resides in my heart, the growth and decay which are similar to the waxing and waning of the moon, and the worldly knowledge and ignorance which are similar to the repeated occurrence of sun and darkness, were destroyed for me.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.8.11. Terulum marulum

*teruḷum maruḷum māyttut tan tirundu sempoṟkaḻal adik kīḻ aruḷi iruttum ammānām ayanām sivanām tirumālāl aruḷappatta satakōpan ōrāyirattuḷ ippattāl aruḷi adik kīḻ iruttum nam aṇṇal karu māṇikkamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

teruḷum maruḷum – worldly knowledge and ignorance; māyttu – eliminating; than – themselves accepting the devotees; tirundu – having correctness; sem – reddish; pon – golden; kaḻal – wearing anklet of bravery; adik kīḻ – under the divine feet; aruḷi – showering his mercy (as said in tiruvāimoḻi 6.10.11 “adik kīḻ amarndu pugundu adiyīr vāḻmin“); iruttum – placing (me, not to move away); ammānām – being the lord; ayanām sivanām – being the antaryāmi of brahma, rudra et al (who are in charge of creation, annihilation etc of the universe); tirumālāl – by śriya:pati (śrīman nārāyaṇa, divine consort of śrī mahālakśmi); aruḷap patta – blessed divinely (with faultless knowledge and devotion); satakōpan – āḻvār‘s; ōr – distinguished; āyirattuḷ – among the thousand pāsurams; ippattāl – in the context of this decad; nam – our; aṇṇal – being lord; karu māṇikkam – having complexion of blue carbuncle; aruḷi – showing his unlimited mercy; adik kīḻ – under his divine feet; iruttum – will place

**Перевод:**

**emperumān is wearing reddish golden anklet of bravery on his divine feet which will eliminate the worldly knowledge and ignorance and have the greatness of themselves accepting the devotees; he is my lord who is showering his mercy to place me at his divine feet; he is śriya:pati, who is the antaryāmi of brahma, rudra et al; āḻvār who is blessed by such emperumān, composed this decad among the distinguished thousand pāsurams; such emperumān, our lord, who is having the complexion of blue carbuncle, showing his unlimited mercy, will place those who are connected with this decad, under his divine feet.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the end, āḻvār says “Those who learn this decad will be pursued by emperumān himself and be placed at his divine feet, just as he pursued me”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. teruḷum maruḷum māyttut than tirundu sempoṟkaḻal adik kīḻ aruḷi iruttum ammānām ayanām sivanām tirumālāl aruḷappatta satakōpan ōrāyirattuḷ ippattāl aruḷi adik kīḻ iruttum nam aṇṇal karu māṇikkamē*

- *teruḷum maruḷum māyttu* – Eliminating kudruśti jñānam (inapt knowledge) \[different philosophies which misinterpret vēdam\] which arose due to brahmā’s rajas (passion) and bāhya jñānam such as āgama etc \[different philosophies which reject vēdam\] which arose due to rudra’s tamas (ignorance); eliminating the knowledge about worldly matters which hinder self enjoyment, along with their trace.
- *than tirundu sem pon kaḻal adik kīḻ* – Under the divine feet which are attractive and which have anklets of bravery, and which don’t let his devotees bow at the feet of anyone else. The context of the bravery here is – not leading those who surrendered through pirātti, to themselves or others.
- *aruḷi iruttum* – Will place due to his exclusive mercy.
- *ammānām ayanām sivanām tirumālāl* – by śriya:pati, sarvēśvara who is the controller of all ātmās starting with brahma, rudra et al.
- *aruḷap patta satakōpan* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) who became an object of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s mercy as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.1.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/03/thiruvaimozhi-1-1-1-uyarvara-uyarnalam/) “*mayarvaṟa madinalam aruḷinan*” (blessed faultless knowledge and devotion). It is being said that the entry point for such mercy is pirātti, śrī mahālakśmi.
- *ōr āyirattuḷ ippattāl – nam aṇṇal karu māṇikkamē – aruḷi adik kīḻ iruttum* – sarvēśvara who is controller of all, who is having attractive physical beauty and qualities, will himself bless and accept at his divine feet. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying that those who practice this decad, will get the same beneft as he got.

## 8.9 Karu manikka malai

## 8.9.1. Karu manikka malai

*karu māṇikka malai mēl maṇittadandāmaraik kādugaḷ pōl tirumārvu vay kaṇ kai undi kāl udai ādaigaḷ seyya pirān tirumāl emmān seḻu nīr vayal kutta nāttut tiruppuliyūr aru māyan pēr anṟip pēccilaḷ annaimīr! idaṟken seygēnō?*

**Пословный перевод:**

karu – having blackish complexion; māṇikka malai mēl – atop a carbuncle hill; maṇi – having (attractive) glow; tadam – expansive; tāmaraik kādugaḷ pōl – like lotus forests; tirumārvu – divine chest (which holds lakśmī and kaustuba gem); vāy – divine lips; kaṇ – divine eyes; kai – divine hands; undi – divine navel; kāl – divine feet; udai ādaigaḷ – divine clothes’; seyya – having the red complexion; pirān – being the benefactor who lets his devotees enjoy; tiru – of pirātti (who eternally enjoys such beauty); māl – being the dear consort; emmān – one who is our lord (due to such beauty); seḻu – beautiful; nīr – having water; vayal – having fields; kuttanāttut tiruppuliyūr – in kuttanāttut tiruppuliyūr \[a divine abode in modern day kēraḷam\]; aru – difficult to attain; māyan – amazing lord’s; pēr – divine name; anṟi – other than; pēccu – any other word; ilaḷ – is not uttering; annaimīr – Oh mothers!; idaṟku – for her state; en – what; seygēnō – shall I do? – \[parānguśa nāyaki‘s friend\] announces her inner torment

**Перевод:**

**parānguśa nāyaki‘s friend announces her inner torment – emperumān appears like expansive lotus forests atop a blackish carbuncle hill with reddish divine chest, divine lips, divine eyes, divine hands, divine navel, divine feet and divine clothes; emperumān is the benefactor who lets his devotees enjoy him, is the dear consort of pirātti and is our lord residing in kuttanāttut tiruppuliyūr having fields with beautiful water; parānguśa nāyaki is not uttering any word other than the divine name of such difficult to attain, amazing lord; oh mothers! What shall I do for her state?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the first pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki‘s friend says “Having seen emperumān‘s beautiful limbs, she became immersed in that beauty, not to know anything else”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. karu māṇikka malai mēl maṇittadandāmaraik kādugaḷ pōl tirumārvu vay kaṇ kai undi kāl udai ādaigaḷ seyya pirān tirumāl emmān seḻu nīr vayal kutta nāttut tiruppuliyūr aru māyan pēr anṟip pēccilaḷ annaimīr! idaṟken seygēnō?*

- *karu māṇikka malai mēl* – Atop a perfectly enjoyable hill, which is having darkness to cool down the hearts of those who enjoy and is glowing abundantly. Also said as a dark hill which will remove the darkness. This is called abhūtōpamā (simile implying an impossibility).
- *maṇit tadam tāmaraik kādugaḷ pōl* – His divine form and divine limbs appear to be a crystal clear pond atop such a hill, having forests of lotus flowers.
- *tirumārvu* – The divine chest where pirātti, our hold/hope, resides. The redness in the chest is due to the auspicious presence of pirātti there.
- *vāy* –  For those who established their relationship with [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) through her, the divine lips will give favourable speech.
- *kaṇ* – The eye which will fulfil the remaining aspects with its glance, when the lips fumble to speak sweet words, due to having seen the dear ones.
- *kai* – The hands which will embrace those who are won over by his glance.
- *undi* – The divine navel which can captivate those who fall at the apt target \[divine feet\]; it is the swirl which captures everyone in the middle.
- *kāl* – The divine feet where one will fall after having been won over by all these aspects.
- *udai ādaigaḷ* – The divine clothes which are engaged while remaining at the divine feet; \[In amalanādipirān, tiruppāṇāḻvār said\] in pāsuram 1 “*kamala pādam*” (lotus foot) and then in pāsuram 2 “*sivanda ādai*” (reddish clothes).
- *pirān* – One who remains with such beauty as said in jitantē stōtram “*bhaktānām*” (for the devotees).
- *tirumāl* – Not just beauty; he has supremacy matching pirātti’s qualities as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 37.18 “*yasyasā janakātmajā – apramēyam hi tattēja:*” (One cannot measure the greatness of the one who is married to the daughter of śrī janaka).
- *emmān* – \[[parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s\] friend is saying – When one asks “please give parānguśa nāyaki \[in marriage\] to [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)“, he remains great, so that one need not wonder “Is he a good match for her?” How great is my lord!
- *seḻu nīr …* – Surrounded with fields which have abundance of beautiful water.
- *kutta nāttut tiruppuliyūr* – The name of the region is kuttanādu \[tiruppuliyūr is the name of the divyadēśam which is inside this region\].
- *aru māyan* – Amazing lord who is difficult to attain.
- *pēr anṟip pēccu ilaḷ* – She is not even uttering the divine names which indicate other states of emperumān such as para ([emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) in paramapadam), vyūha (emperumān in kśīrābdi) and vibhava (emperumān’s incarnations). She is not even uttering the divine names of emperumān in other divyadēśams.
- *annaimīr idaṟku en seygēnō* – To make it appear as if she also found out about it along with the relatives now, [parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s friend is asking “what shall I do now?”

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.9.2. Annaimir!

*annaimīr idaṟken seygēn? aṇi mēruvin mīdulavum tunnu sūḻ sudar nāyiṟum anṟiyum pal sudargaḷum pōl minnu nīḷ mudi āram palgalan tānudai emperumān punnai am poḻil sūḻ tiruppuliyūr pugaḻum ivaḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

annaimīr – Oh mothers!; idaṟku – for her state (which occurred without our knowledge); en – what; seygēn – shall I do?; aṇi – beautiful; mēruvin – mēru mountain’s; mīdu – atop; ulavum – roaming; tunnu – dense; sūḻ – surrounded; sudar – having radiance; nāyiṟum – sun; anṟiyum – not just that; pal – many types; sudargaḷumpōl – like the radiance of planets and stars; minnu – having glow; nīḷ – tall; mudi – divine crown; āram – necklace (etc); pal – many types; kalan tān – ornaments; udai – one who is wearing; emperumān – the sarvādika (greater than all) who enslaved us (showing such beauty); punnai – having punnai tree; am – beautiful; poḻil – by gardens; sūḻ – surrounded; tiruppuliyūr – tiruppuliyūr; ivaḷ – she; pugaḻum – is praising

**Перевод:**

**Oh mothers! emperumān is wearing a glowing, tall divine crown which resembles the sun surrounded with densely radiant rays atop the beautiful mēru mountain and not just that, resembling the planets and stars which have many types of radiance, and many types of ornaments; she is praising tiruppuliyūr which is surrounded by beautiful gardens having punnai trees, which is the abode of such sarvādika (greater than all) who enslaved us. What shall I do for her state? aṇi mēru is a simile for emperumān’s reddish form.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the 2nd pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki‘s friend says “She is captivated by emperumān‘s beautiful ornaments”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. annaimīr idaṟken seygēn? aṇi mēruvin mīdulavum tunnu sūḻ sudar nāyiṟum anṟiyum pal sudargaḷum pōl minnu nīḷ mudi āram palgalan tānudai emperumān punnai am poḻil sūḻ tiruppuliyūr pugaḻum ivaḷē*

- *annaimīr idaṟken seygēn* – This situation was neither created by you nor by me; what shall I do for this?
- *aṇi …* – Distinguished sun who has radiance which is not limited to what we see but is dense and fully surrounding the sun, which is roaming atop the beautiful mēru mountain.
- *anṟiyum pal sudargaḷum pōl* – And other luminous objects such as stars etc which have similar radiance.
- *minnu nīḷ mudi* – The divine crown which was explained as “*tunnu sūḻ sudar nāyiṟu*” (sun with well surrounded radiance).
- *āram* – The divine necklace which is explained as in [tiruvāsiriyam 1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/07/thiruvasiriyam-1/) “*am sudar madiyam pūṇḍu*” (wearing the moon which has beautiful cool rays).
- *pal kalan* – Other divine ornaments.
- *emperumān* – Loving way of addressing \[addressing him as [parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) would do\]. My lord who remains truthful to these aspects.
- *punnai am poḻil sūḻ* – She is speaking about the pleasing gardens \[in that town\]. These are the words of one \[[parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)\] who united with [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) in the garden \[This is why she is praising the gardens\].
- *tiruppuliyūr pugaḻum ivaḷē* – Dear child \[the friend speaking in exclamation\]! How did she know about this town? Does she not appear to be immersed in the gardens in the town, the town itself just as she is immersed in his beautiful ornaments?

## 8.9.3. Pugalum ival

*pugaḻum ivaḷ ninṟirāp pagal poru nīrk kadal tīppattu engum nigaḻum eriyōdu selvadoppac ceḻungadirāḻi mudal pugaḻum poru padai ēndip pōr pukkasuraraip ponṟuvittān tigaḻumaṇi nedu māda nīdu tiruppuliyūr vaḷamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

poru – moving in an agitated manner (due to rising tides); nīr – having water; kadal – ocean; tīppattu – lit fire; engum – everywhere; tigaḻum – shining; eriyodu – with flames; selvadu oppa – occurring like; pugaḻum – to be praised (even by enemies); seḻum – very; kadir – having radiance; āḻi – tiruvāḻi (divine chakra); mudal – etc; poru – well fitting; padai – weapons; ēndi – holding; pōr – in battle; pukku – entered; asurarai – demons; ponṟuvittān – one who destroyed; tigaḻum – shining; maṇi – having carbuncles; nedu – tall; mādam – having mansions; nīdu – being expansive; tiruppuliyūr – tiruppuliyūr’s; vaḷam – beauty; ivaḷ – she; irāp pagal – night and day; ninṟu – continuously; pugaḻum – is praising

**Перевод:**

**Just as an ocean having water which is moving in an agitated manner which appears like being on fire everywhere with shining flames, emperumān who is praised even by the enemies, entered the battle holding the well fitting weapons such as the very radiant divine chakra etc and destroyed the demons; through night and day, parānguśa nāyaki is continuously praising the beauty of the expansive tiruppuliyūr which is the residence of such emperumān and which is having tall mansions with shining carbuncles. “poru padai” also could mean weapons which are ready to battle.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the third pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki‘s friend says “Being captivated by the masculinity of emperumān in tiruppuliyūr, she is enthusiastically reciting the divine names of his which relate to his valour etc”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Third pāsuram. When asked “Even the sages explain about emperumān’s beauty; how is her explanation indicative of their union?” parānguśa nāyaki‘s friend says “Her words resemble those of sītāp pirātti who embraced perumāḷ (śrī rāma) after seeing his valour as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 30.40 ‘bhartāram pariśasvajē’ (tightly embraced her husband)”. pugaḻum ivaḷ ninṟirāp pagal poru nīrk kadal tīppattu engum nigaḻum eriyōdu selvadoppac ceḻungadirāḻi mudal pugaḻum poru padai ēndip pōr pukkasuraraip ponṟuvittān tigaḻumaṇi nedu māda nīdu tiruppuliyūr vaḷamē*

- *pugaḻum ivaḷ ninṟu irāp pagal* – She is not at the stage of understanding his valour and becoming attached to him for that; did she hear this from someone and say it once? \[No\] She keeps repeating this night and day.
- *pugaḻum* – Did she just think about it in her heart? \[No\] Did she not give up her shyness and keep praising him?
- *poru nīrk kadal tīp pattu* – Setting fire on an ocean with agitated tides.
- *engum tigaḻum eriyodu selvadu oppa* – The radiance acquired by him from the weapons and his divine form make him appear to be walking with blazing fire on such ocean.
- *pugaḻum poru padaiyāna seḻum kadir āḻi mudal ēndi* – His divine weapons are praising him as said in raghuvamśam 10 “*hētibhi: cētanāvatbhiru dīritajayasvanam*” ([emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is eulogised by his weapons which have knowledge); alternative explanation mercifully given by [emperumānār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/emperumanar/) –  even his enemies are praising him saying “how perfectly the weapons fit in his hands!” as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 106.6 “*śatrō:prakyāta vīryasyaranjanīyasya vikramai:*” (śrī rāma who is well-known for bringing joy by his valour and bravery).
- *poru padai* – Weapon which is ready for battle.
- *seḻum kadir* – Holding weapons such as the very radiant sudarśana chakra etc.
- *pōr pukku asuraraip ponṟuvittān* – Entered the battle with weapons and destroyed the miscreants.
- *tigaḻum …* – She will praise the beauty of tiruppuliyūr which has tall mansions with radiant carbuncles, and which remains until the end of kalpa (brahmā’s day). vaḷam – beauty. To stop the enemies from approaching him, even he is not needed, just the town is sufficient. Just as sītāp pirātti will ignore śrī mitilā and praise śrī ayōdyā as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 33.17 “*rāghavasya nivēśanē*” (the abode of śrī rāma), [parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is praising the glories of tiruppuliyūr ignoring āḻvārtirunagari. Just as she thinks about paramapadam which is explained as “*ayōdyā aparājitā*” (paramapadam which is invincible by enemies), she is thinking about tiruppuliyūr. Even for paramapadam āḻvār is saying in tiruvāimoḻi 9.3.7 “*māga vaigundam kāṇbadaṟku en manamēgam eṇṇum irāp pagal inṟiyē*” (My heart will continuously think about seeing paramapadam).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.9.4. Ur valam

*ūr vaḷangiḷar sōlaiyum karumbum perum sennelum sūḻndu ēr vaḷangiḷar taṇpaṇaik kutta nāttut tiruppuliyūr sīr vaḷangiḷar mū ulaguṇḍumiḻ dēvapirān pēr vaḷangiḷarndanṟip pēccilaḷ inṟip punai iḻaiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

Ur – for the town; vaḷam – being the wealth; kiḷar – tall; sōlaiyum – garden; karumbum – sugarcane (which is comparable to the garden); peru – tall (bigger than the sugarcane); sennelum – great paddy crops; sūḻndu – surrounded; ēr – plough’s; vaḷam – beauty; kiḷar – increasing; taṇ – cool; paṇai – having water bodies; kuttanāttut tiruppuliyūr – in kuttanāttut tiruppuliyūr; sīr – qualities (which help him in protecting others); vaḷam – abundance; kiḷar – to be seen; mū ulagu – three worlds; uṇḍu – consumed; umiḻ – spat out; dēvapirān – one who is enjoyable by nityasūris, his; pēr – divine names’; vaḷam – abundance; punai – decorated; ivviḻai – she, who is having ornaments; inṟu – now; kiḷarndu anṟi – without enthusiasm; pēccilaḷ – not speaking

**Перевод:**

**emperumān, who is enjoyable by nityasūris, who consumed and spat out the three worlds, remains in kuttanāttut tiruppuliyūr which has cool water bodies with increasing beauty of the plough, which is surrounded by tall garden which reveals the wealth of the town, sugarcane and tall, great paddy crops, to let others see his qualities. parānguśa nāyaki who is wearing ornaments of abundance of divine names of such emperumān, is now not speaking without enthusiasm \[i.e., speaking with enthusiasm\]. “ēr vaḷam kiḷar” indicates “revealing the beautifully abundant \[water bodies\]” as well; “Ur vaḷam kiḷar sōlai” indicates “the garden which reveals the town’s wealth” as well.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fourth pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki‘s friend says “She is immersed in tiruppuliyūr emperumān‘s qualities”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Fourth pāsuram. When asked “Is it sufficient to have masculinity? Does he have the quality of helping in desperate times?” parānguśa nāyaki‘s friend says “Does he have any shortcoming in that aspect?” \[No\] She is talking about “punal taru puṇarcci” (a woman falling in love with a man who saved her from drowning in water). Ur vaḷangiḷar sōlaiyum karumbum perum sennelum sūḻndu ēr vaḷangiḷar taṇpaṇaik kutta nāttut tiruppuliyūr sīr vaḷangiḷar mū ulaguṇḍumiḻ dēvapirān pēr vaḷangiḷarndanṟip pēccilaḷ inṟip punai iḻaiyē*

- *Ur vaḷam kiḷar sōlaiyum* – The garden which reveals the wealth of the town; alternative explanation – the garden which reveals the greatness which are claimed for the towns.
- *karumbum perum sennelum sūḻndu* – Surrounded with fertile field which is filled with sugarcane, and the great paddy crops which give shade to sugarcane.
- *ēr vaḷam kiḷar* – Having the beauty acquired from the plough; alternative explanation – the collection of ploughs. Implies – the active farming in the town.
- *taṇ paṇai* – maruda nilam (cropland and areas around cropland) or beautiful water bodies. By saying cropland, fertile fields are highlighted.
- *sīr vaḷam kiḷar mū ulagu uṇḍu umiḻ* – The leader of the blemiśless nityasūris, who revealed the goodness of his qualities through his acts, by placing the three worlds in his stomach and subsequently spitting them out.
- *pēr vaḷam* – The beauty of his divine names; alternative explanation – the collection of his divine names.
- *kiḷarndu anṟip pēccilaḷ* – She is very enthusiastically uttering the divine names which reveal his qualities and activities, just as a roaring ocean will throw up the tides. Is she uttering the divine names as we do? \[No. Her bhāvam (mood) is totally different from ours\]
- *inṟu* – This enthusiasm and goodness were not seen yesterday.
- *ip punai iḻaiyē* – Every time she utters the divine name, it looks as if she becomes decorated with one more ornament.

## 8.9.5. Punai ilaigal

*punai iḻaigaḷ aṇivum ādai udaiyum pudukkaṇippum ninaiyum nīrmai adanṟu ivatkidu ninṟu ninaikkap pukkāl sunaiyinuḷ tadandāmarai malarum taṇ tiruppuliyūr munaivan mūvulagāḷi appan tiruvaruḷ mūḻginaḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

punai – (previously) worn; iḻaigaḷ – ornaments; aṇivum – having worn (now with added beauty); ādai udaiyum – the beauty of her clothes; pudukkaṇippum – freshness (acquired in her form); ninṟu – staying (as long as we exist); ninaikkap pukkāl – even if we try to enjoy; ivatku – for her; idu – this greatness; ninaiyum – to think (as per worldly order); nīrmai adu anṟu – not of the nature; sunaiyinuḷ – inside the ponds; tadam – huge; tāmarai – lotus flowers; malarum – blossomed; taṇ – invigorating; tiruppuliyūr – of tiruppuliyūr; munaivan – being the primary leader; mū ulagu – for the universe; āḷi – being the lord; appan – benefactor’s; tiruvaruḷ – divine, unlimited favour; mūḻginaḷ – she immersed

**Перевод:**

**Even if we stay and try to enjoy her greatness in the way she is wearing the previously worn ornaments \[with added beauty now\], the beauty of her clothes and her freshness, it is beyond our thoughts; she is immersed in the divine, unlimited favour of the primary leader of the invigorating tiruppuliyūr, which has huge blossomed lotus flowers in ponds, and who is the lord of the universe and the benefactor.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fifth pāsuram, when asked “Are we not talking about emperumān‘s qualities such as beauty etc? Shall we not consider that she is also speaking in this manner?” parānguśa nāyaki‘s friend says “For those who have seen her form, it is understandable that she became immersed in his qualities such as opulence and united with him”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. punai iḻaigaḷ aṇivum ādai udaiyum pudukkaṇippum ninaiyum nīrmai adanṟu ivatkidu ninṟu ninaikkap pukkāl sunaiyinuḷ tadandāmarai malarum taṇ tiruppuliyūr munaivan mūvulagāḷi appan tiruvaruḷ mūḻginaḷē*

- *punai iḻagaḷ aṇivum* – Do you think the ornaments appear to have been decked by us on her? \[They appear to be disturbed due to embracing by [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)\]
- *ādai udaiyum* – Are these clothes worn according to emperumān’s desire? \[Yes\]
- *pudukkaṇippum* – Look at her freshness which resembles freshly watered field!
- *ninaiyum nīrmai adanṟu ivatku idu ninṟu ninaikkap pukkāl* – Not just starting to think and leaving it subsequently, even if analysed forever, one cannot understand the beauties which she has acquired. Even if one can comprehend the greatness of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) which is incomprehensible as declared by vēda puruśa in taittirīya upaniśat “*yatō vācō nivartantē*” (the speech returned), her state cannot be comprehended.

When asked “What did you comprehend from all of these?” [parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s friend says

- *appan tiruvaruḷ mūḻginaḷ sunaiyinuḷ tadam tāmarai malarum* – Each flower will blossom to appear that it is spreading all over the pond. She is saying that the residents of this town will not accommodate others. There is no other go for her.
- *tiruppuliyūr munaivan* – The main leader of this town.
- *mū ulagu āḷi* – The controller of all worlds. One need not seek anyone else for wealth.
- *appan* – She is saying “appan” \[benefactor\] due to being satisfied by having acquired all the necessary wealth \[from him\].
- *tiruvaruḷ mūḻginaḷē* – How can we retrieve something which is drowned in the ocean? Is it possible for you to redeem her who has drowned in the ocean of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s mercy?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.9.6. Tiruvarul mulgi

*tiruvaruḷ mūḻgi vaigalum seḻunīr niṟak kaṇṇa pirān tiruvaruḷgaḷum sērndamaikku adaiyāḷam tirunda uḷa tiruvaruḷ aruḷāl avan senṟu sēr taṇ tiruppuliyūr tiruvaruḷ kamugoṇ paḻattadu melliyal sevvidaḻē*

**Пословный перевод:**

seḻu nīr – of the great ocean (with abundant water); niṟam – having the complexion; kaṇṇa pirān – the great benefactor kriṣṇa (who is easily approachable by his devotees); tiruvaruḷ – (infinite) magnanimity; vaigalum – repeatedly; mūḻgi – immersed; tiruvaruḷgaḷum – his greatly magnanimous acts (during the union); sērndamaikku – what she got; tirunda – insuppressible; adaiyāḷam – signs; uḷa – are present; tiruvaruḷ – (his causeless) divine mercy; aruḷāl – to bestow; avan – he; senṟu – went; sēr – reached; taṇ – invigorating; tiruppuliyūr – in tiruppuliyūr; tiruvaruḷ – as a target for his merciful glance; kamugu – areca tree’s; oṇ – well rounded, reddish; paḻattadu – like a fruit; mel – slender; iyal – having nature; sem – reddish; idaḻ – her leaf like lips

**Перевод:**

**Being immersed repeatedly in magnanimity of kriṣṇa, the great benefactor  who is having the complexion of great ocean, and the greatly magnanimous acts she received from him are seen through the insuppressible signs on her form; her slender, reddish lips resemble the well rounded, reddish fruit of the areca tree which is the target of his merciful glance in the invigorating tiruppuliyūr where he went and reached to bestow his divine mercy.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the sixth pāsuram, when asked “could her recently acquired beauty be due to her amazing activities and her age?” parānguśa nāyaki‘s friend says “Being captivated by emperumān‘s magnanimity and united with him, is visibly seen in her form \[that is the reason for her recently acquired beauty\]”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. tiruvaruḷ mūḻgi vaigalum seḻunīr niṟak kaṇṇa pirān tiruvaruḷgaḷum sērndamaikku adaiyāḷam tirunda uḷa tiruvaruḷ aruḷāl avan senṟu sēr taṇ tiruppuliyūr tiruvaruḷ kamugoṇ paḻattadu melliyal sevvidaḻē*

- *vaigalum tiruvaruḷ mūḻgi* – Immersed in his mercy for a long time, repeatedly. We only know what we see now. Would we know, since how long he has been voluntarily pursuing her and interacting with her?
- *seḻu nīr niṟak kaṇṇa pirān* – He captivated her by manifesting his saundaryam (beauty) and saulabhyam (easy approacability).
- *tiruvaruḷgaḷum sērndamaikku* – For all of his mercy to have reached her.
- *adaiyāḷam tirunda uḷa* – His pursuit upon her is visibly seen through the signs on her form.

When asked “How did you know this?” [parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s friend says,

- *tiruvaruḷ aruḷāl* – To bestow his quality of \[magnanimously\] blessing others without checking the qualities \[being good or bad\] of others; to bestow his divine mercy. *Al* is present for sound, and has no specific meaning here.
- *avan senṟu …* – While he has the paramapadam which is hailed in [mudal tiruvandādi 51](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/04/munram-thiruvandhadhi-51/) “*kalangāp perunagaram*” (paramapadam, the great town, which has no bewilderment) as his audience, he came here and presented himself. There are some areca trees which are said to be “*tiruvaruḷ kamugu*“. That is, instead of growing with water, they grow by the merciful glance of [periya pirāttiyār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/) and [sarvēśvaran](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/); the tender-natured [parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s lips resemble the fruit of such areca trees. Her situation is known from her mouth which is quite beautiful.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.9.7. Mellilaic celva

*mellilaic celva vaṇ kodip pulga vīngiḷandāḷ kamugin mallilai madal vāḻai īn kani sūḻndu maṇangamaḻndu pullilait tenginūdu kāl ulavundaṇ tiruppuliyūr mallalanjelvak kaṇṇan tāḷ adaindāḷ immadavaralē*

**Пословный перевод:**

mel – tender; ilai – rich leaves; selvam – having wealth of beauty; vaṇ – having generosity (by supporting those which needs support); kodi – betel creeper; pulga – as it embraces; vīngu – being well-grown (due to the union); iḷam – very soft; tāḷ – having the bottom portion; kamugin – being close to the areca tree; mal – dense; ilai – leaf; madal – having flower petal (which appears to be a tool for service); vāḻai – plantain trees; In – charming, infinitely enjoyable; kani – ripened fruits; sūḻndu – due to being in contact with; maṇam kamaḻndu – greatly fragrant; pul – dense; ilai – having leaf; tengin – (tall) coconut trees; ūdu – in between; kāl – southerly wind (which travels as per its desire); ulavum – to roam around; taṇ – invigorating; tiruppuliyūr – in tiruppuliyūr; mallalam selvam – having great wealth of love; kaṇṇan – kriṣṇa; tāḷ – divine feet; im madavaral – this young-hearted parānguśa nāyaki; adaindāḷ – reached and enjoyed

**Перевод:**

**In invigorating tiruppuliyūr, as the betel creeper which has rich, tender leaves and wealth of beauty and generosity, embraces the well-grown areca tree which has very soft bottom portion, \[which appears to be served by\] the plantain tree which is having dense leaves and flower petal, with charming, infinitely enjoyable, ripened fruits, being in contact with the greatly fragrant coconut trees with dense leaves, and southerly wind roams around between these trees; this young-hearted parānguśa nāyaki reached and enjoyed the divine feet of kriṣṇa who is having great wealth of love, in such tiruppuliyūr.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the seventh pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki‘s friend says “Even the plants of tiruppuliyūr are affectionate towards each other and sustain themselves by union, due to his love and she became drowned in it”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. mellilaic celva vaṇ kodip pulga vīngiḷandāḷ kamugin mallilai madal vāḻai In kani sūḻndu maṇangamaḻndu pullilait tenginūdu kāl ulavundaṇ tiruppuliyūr mallalanjelvak kaṇṇan tāḷ adaindāḷ immadavaralē*

- *mellilai …* – There is generous creeper which is having tender leaves; it appears that this creeper will fully present itself to its bhartā (husband), the areca tree.
- *vīngu iḷam tāḷ kamugin* – As the creeper embraces the tree, it keeps growing and having its bottom portion loosening. As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 37.18 “*yasyasā janakātmajā – apramēyam hi tattēja:*” (One cannot measure the greatness of the one who is married to the daughter of śrī janaka). As said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 5.13.54 “*dadau bāhulatām skandē gōpī madu nighātina:*” (A covherd girl placed her creeper like hand on the shoulders of [kriṣṇa](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is the killer of madu, the demon).
- *kamugin mallilai madal vāḻai* – Adjacent to the areca tree, there exists a plantain tree which has huge leaves and flower petals. The plantain tree will provide shade for the betel creeper and areca tree, protecting them from sun.
- *In kani sūḻndu* –  Many bunches of banana fruit will be present around the tree.
- *maṇam kamaḻndu* – The wind, without realising the result, with the desire to grasp the fragrance, entered inside, picked up the fragrance, got stuck in the dense presence of plantain trees, subsequently entered in the garden of coconut trees where there is some gap between trees, and roamed around.
- *pul ilai* – \[three explanations\] 1) leaves which are close to each other; coconut trees which have leaves which are embraced by one another; 2) the coconut trees which have their leaves touching the plantain trees; 3) the leaves which became straightened out due to the dense nature of the garden.
- *mallalam selvak kaṇṇan* – [kriṣṇa](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who has wealth of infinite beauty.
- *tāḷ adaindāḷ* – She reached his divine feet being captivated by his loving quality.
- *im madavaral* – She who was obedient towards me previously, is now saying she cannot be rescued by anyone.

## 8.9.8. Madavaral annaimirgatku

*madavaral annaimīrgatku en sollic collugēn? mallaic celva vadamoḻi maṟai vāṇar vēḷviyuṇey aḻal vān pugai pōy tida visumbil amarar nāttai maṟaikkum taṇ tiruppuliyūr padavaravaṇaiyān tan nāmam allāl paravāḷ ivaḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

annaimīrgatku – for you, mothers; en – what words; solli – by telling; solluvēn – will explain?; mallai – huge; selvam – having wealth; vadamoḻi – samskrutam language (which is uttered during worship); maṟaivāṇar – experts in vēdam (which reveals the methods of worship), their; vēḷviyuḷ – in rituals such as yāgam (fire sacrifice) etc (which are forms of worship); ney – the offerings made in the form of ghee etc; aḻal – fire’s; vān – huge; pugai – smoke; pōy – rising; tidam – firm; visumbil – in the sky; amarar – dēvas’; nāttai – abode; maṟaikkum – covering (like surrounding it with a screen); taṇ – invigorating; tiruppuliyūr – in tiruppuliyūr; padam – having hoods (which are expanded due to coming in contact with him); aravu aṇaiyān than – one who is resting on the mattress, tiruvanantāḻvān (ādiśēśa), to be vorśipped by such rituals; nāmam – divine name; allāl – other than; ivaḷ madavaral – this obedient girl; paravāḷ – will not speak

**Перевод:**

**With what words will I explain to you, mothers? In the invigorating tiruppuliyūr, emperumān is resting on the hooded tiruvanantāḻvān, the mattress, to be vorśipped by rituals such as yāgam (fire sacrifice) etc by the very wealthy experts in samskrutam language and vēdam, where the offerings made in the form of ghee etc by them in the fire gives rise to huge smoke which reaches the abode of dēvas, in sky and covers it. This obedient girl will not speak about any name other than the divine name of such tiruppuliyūr emperumān.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the eighth pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki‘s friend says “due to tiruppuliyūr emperumān‘s wonderful conduct, she is attracted towards him”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*When said “Just being with great love is not sufficient. Our family is situated in good conduct as said in ‘karmaṇaiva hi samsiddim āstitā janakādaya:‘ (Have janaka et al not attained the result of self-realisation through karma yōga only?) So tiruppuliyūr emperumān should also have good conduct”, parānguśa nāyaki‘s friend says “Have you not heard about the conduct of the residents of tiruppuliyūr?” madavaral annaimīrgatku en sollic collugēn? mallaic celva vadamoḻi maṟai vāṇar vēḷviyuṇey aḻal vān pugai pōy tida visumbil amarar nāttai maṟaikkum taṇ tiruppuliyūr padavaravaṇaiyān than nāmam allāl paravāḷ ivaḷē*

- *madavaral* – Her obedience; how she was obedient towards me; also implies, she will not give up on whatever she holds on to.
- *annaimīrgatku* – For you, who introduced her to me first.
- *en sollic collugēn* – Shall I say that she is following my advice? Shall I say that she is obedient towards me?
- *mallai …* – brāhmaṇas who are having infinite wealth, who are experts in samskruta \[purāṇas etc\] and vēdam, engage in yāgam where they offer ghee, which gives rise to smoke that goes up.
- *tida visumbil amarar nāttai maṟaikkum* – It will cover the dēvalōkam (abode of dēvas) which is in the firmly remaining sky. It will cover the vaimānikas (pilots of the planes) in svargam (heaven) and will stop the apsaras (damsels) from seeing their faces. It can also be considered to be putting up a curtain for their enjoyment in privacy.
- *taṇ tiruppuliyūr* – His nature is as said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 3.24](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/3-24/) “*utsīdēyur imē lokā na kuryām karma cēd aham \| sankarasya ca kartā syām upahanyām imā: prajā: \|\|*” (If I did not perform the actions, the residents of this world (who follow my discipline) will be ruined; I would be the one who caused mixture (impurity in the families of dedicated followers); thus, I would be the cause for the downfall (in the future too) of these people).
- *pada aravu …* – She does not repeatedly utter any name other than the divine name of tiruppuliyūr [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is resting on tiruvantāḻvān whose hoods are expanded due to being in contact with emperumān. While I am with her, she speaks about the beauty of his mattress, which she enjoyed during her union with him.
- *ivaḷ* – She who does not know to interact with anyone other than me.

## 8.9.9. Paraval ival

*paravāḷ ivaḷ ninṟirāp pagal pani nīr niṟak kaṇṇa pirān viravār isai maṟai vēdiyar oli vēlaiyininṟolippak karavār tadandoṟum tāmaraik kayam tīvigai ninṟalarum puravār kaḻanigaḷ sūḻ tiruppuliyūrp pugaḻanṟi maṟṟē*

**Пословный перевод:**

pani – cool; nīr niṟam – having complexion of water; kaṇṇan – kriṣṇa; pirān – the great benefactor’s; viravu – spread; Ar – filled; isai – having tune; maṟai – by vēdams starting with sāma vēdam; vēdiyar – vaidakas \[followers of vēdam\]; oli – tumultuous chants; vēlaiyil – like ocean; ninṟu – stand; olippa – as they are recited; karavu – crocodiles; Ar – filled; tadam toṟum – in every pond; tāmarai – lotus flower’s; kayam – area; tīvigai – like lamps which are lit; ninṟu – remain; alarum – blossoming; puravār – well organised; kaḻanigaḷ – fields; sūḻ – surrounded; tiruppuliyūrp pugaḻ anṟi – other than the glories of tiruppūliyūr; maṟṟu – anything else; ivaḷ – she; ninṟu – remaining firm; irāp pagal – night and day; paravāḷ – will not sing

**Перевод:**

**The tumultuous chants by vaidikas, of vēdams, starting with the musical sāma vēdam in a well spread, filled manner which is \[speaking the glories\] of kriṣṇa, the benefactor, who is having the complexion of cool water, appear like the sound of ocean. The blossomed lotus flowers on the many ponds which are filled with crocodiles, appear like lamps which are lit, in tiruppuliyūr which is surrounded with well organised fields. parānguśa nāyaki is not singing anything other than the glories of such tiruppuliyūr, remaining firm through night and day. tolkāppiyam “tadamum kayavum naḷiyum perumai” (greatness is indicated by the words tadam, kayavu, naḷi). tadam can be considered as banks. In this sense, it could be “lotus filled ponds with crocodiles on the banks”.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the ninth pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki‘s friend says “She is always singing about emperumān as the one who is having knowledge about all principles of vēdam starting with sāma vēdam”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*When asked “Is good conduct sufficient? Will one know about the conduct without studying the literature explaining such conduct? īsn’t the nature of the descendants of this clan as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam bāla kāṇḍam 13.21 ‘niśtitam sarva śāstrēśu sarva vēdēśu niśtitam‘ (janaka who has deeply analysed all literature and vēdams)? So, he should have true knowledge in vēdāntam matching the good conduct” parānguśa nāyaki‘s friend says “There is no shortcoming in that as well”. paravāḷ ivaḷ ninṟirāp pagal pani nīr niṟak kaṇṇa pirān viravār isai maṟai vēdiyar oli vēlaiyininṟolippak karavār tadandoṟum tāmaraik kayam tīvigai ninṟalarum puravār kaḻanigaḷ sūḻ tiruppuliyūrp pugaḻanṟi maṟṟē*

- *paravāḷ ivaḷ ninṟu irāp pagal* – She is speaking in an incohesive manner; she is speaking through night and day. Should we search for any other pramāṇam (proof) for this? Her words are pramāṇam themselves.
- *pani nīr niṟak kaṇṇa pirān* – kriṣṇa who has cool form and qualities \[heart\].
- *viravār isai maṟai* – viravi – spreading everywhere. ārndu – abundance. Well spread, abundant vēdam which is having tune. Alternative explanation – considering it to be “*viraivār*“, virai – enjoyable, vār – abundance, isai maṟai – sāma vēdam \[which is very enjoyable\].
- *vēdiyar oli* – The chants of vēdam and the sounds of those who are discussing vēdāntam.
- *vēlaiyil ninṟu olippa* – Being louder than the sound of the ocean.
- *karavār tadam toṟum* – In ponds which are filled with crocodiles.
- *tāmaraik kayam* – kayam implies group and greatness.
- *tīvigai* – Lamp. The group of blossomed lotus flowers appears like collection of lamps which are well lit.
- *puravār kaḻanigaḷ sūḻ* – Fields where there are lots of arguments. parāśara bhattar mercifully explains “While the brāhmaṇas are arguing and fighting with each other while discussing vēdam, āḻvār is glorifying the town”.
- *tiruppuliyūr pugaḻ anṟi maṟṟu paravār ivaḷ ninṟu irāp pagal* – She is constantly talking incohesively about the vēdam chants of the residents of the town, the loud arguments on vēdāntam by the residents of the town and the enjoyable nature of the town.

## 8.9.10. Anri marror upayam

*anṟi māṟṟōr upāyam en? ivaḷ andaṇ tuḻāy kamaḻdal kunṟa mā maṇi māda māḷigaik kōlak kuḻāngaḷ malgi tendisait tiladam purai kuttanāttut tiruppuliyūr ninṟa māyap pirān tiruvaruḷām ivaḷ nērpattadē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kunṟam – like a hill; mā – best; maṇi – filled with precious gems; mādam – mansions’; māḷigai – palaces’; kōlam – attractive; kuḻāngaḷ – rows; malgi – densely present; then tisai – for the southern direction; tiladam purai – decoration like a tilak (a beautiful symbol on the forehead); kuttanāttut tiruppuliyūr – in kuttanāttut tiruppuliyūr; ninṟa – standing; māyap pirān – amazing lord’s; tiruvaruḷām – divine mercy only; ivaḷ – she; nērpattadu – attained; anṟi – other than (that); ivaḷ – she; am – beautiful; taṇ – cool; tuḻāy – tiruttuḻāy (divine tuḷasi); kamaḻdal – to have that fragrance on her; maṟṟu – any; ōr – a; upāyam – means; en – what?

**Перевод:**

**parānguśa nāyaki attained the divine mercy of the amazing lord who is standing in kuttanāttut tiruppuliyūr which is a decoration like tilak for the southern direction, which has densely located, beautiful rows of hill like mansions and palaces which are filled with best precious gems. What other means is there for her who is having the fragrance of beautiful, cool tiruttuḻāy?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the tenth pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki‘s friend says “Is his greatness limited to our speech? It is most amazing” and highlights the signs of her union with him to convince them.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. anṟi māṟṟōr upāyam en? ivaḷ andaṇ tuḻāy kamaḻdal kunṟa mā maṇi māda māḷigaik kōlak kuḻāngaḷ malgi tendisait tiladam purai kuttanāttut tiruppuliyūr ninṟa māyap pirān tiruvaruḷām ivaḷ nērpattadē*

- *anṟi maṟṟu ōr upāyam en ivaḷ am taṇ tuḻāy kamaḻdal* – Can there be any other reason for this beautiful, cool tiruttuḻāy’s fragrance on her? Would anyone have the fragrance of the sandalwood paste, without embracing the prince? Is my body or your body having this fragrance of tiruttuḻāy? Inner, true meaning – this “*andaṇ tuḻāy kamaḻdal*” implies their acknovledgement of the union of [parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) and tiruppuliyūr [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/).
- *kunṟam …* – Having attractive, abundant collection of mansions and palaces which are as tall as hills, being built with precious gems. The amazing lord who is standing in kuttanāttut tiruppuliyūr which looks like a tilak for the southern direction. He is with great qualities to be said as “she is not a match for him”. You are thinking that he is not a good match for her; but the residents of this town think that she is not a good match for him.
- *tiruvaruḷām ivaḷ nērpattadē* – She attained him by his divine mercy. When asked “Is his divine mercy the only sign for their union? Is there any other sign?” [parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s friend says “*anṟi maṟṟōr upāyamen ivaḷ andaṇ tuḻāy kamaḻdal*“.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.9.11. Nerpatta nirai

*nērpatta niṟai mūvulagukkum nāyagan tan adimai nērpatta toṇḍar toṇḍar toṇḍar toṇḍan satakōpan sol nērpatta tamiḻ mālai āyirattuḷ ivai pattum nērpattāravar nērpattār nedumāṟkadimai seyyavē*

**Пословный перевод:**

niṟai – fully complete; mū ulagukkum – for three types of cētanas (sentient beings) and acētanas (insentient entities); nērpatta – apt; nāyagan than – lord, sarvēśvara’s; adimai – for kainkaryam; nērpatta – apt; toṇḍar – great devotees, their; toṇḍar toṇḍar – related in any manner; toṇḍan – servitor; satakōpan – āḻvār‘s; sol nērpatta – having good words; tamiḻ – in drāvida (tamiḻ) language; mālai – made as a garland; āyirattuḷ – among the thousand pāsurams; ivai pattum – this decad; nērpattāravar – those who practiced and attained; nedumāṟku – for sarvēśvara who is greatly attached to his devotees; adimai seyya – to serve; nērpattār – will get

**Перевод:**

**āḻvār is a servitor of those who are related in any manner to the apt, great devotees engaged in service of sarvēśvaran, the apt lord of the three types of cētanas (sentient beings) and acētanas (insentient entities) which are fully complete; those who practiced and attained this decad among the thousand pāsurams which are having the garland of words of āḻvār, in tamiḻ language, will get to serve sarvēśvara who is greatly attached to his devotees.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the end, āḻvār says “Those who learnt this decad will get to perform bhagavat kainkaryam which is the perfect goal for this ātmā”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. nērpatta niṟai mūvulagukkum nāyagan than adimai nērpatta toṇḍar toṇḍar toṇḍar toṇḍan satakōpan sol nērpatta tamiḻ mālai āyirattuḷ ivai pattum nērpattāravar nērpattār nedumāṟkadimai seyyavē*

- *nērpatta niṟai mū ulagukkum nāyagan than adimai* – The apt lord for the three worlds which have no shortcoming. śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 2.13 “*trailōkyamapi nātēna yēna syānnātavattaram*” (In śrī rāma, all the three worlds have an apt leader) – even if the three worlds are taken together, that which is to be protected will be small and his desire to protect them will be great. With this, the nature of the lord is explained as said in “*anurūpassavaināta:*” (that śrī rāma is the apt leader).
- *adimai nērpatta toṇḍar toṇḍar toṇḍar toṇḍan satakōpan* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is talking about his own nature. Just as emperumān is the ultimate entity for lordship, āḻvār is the ultimate entity for servitude.
- *sol nērpatta tamiḻ mālai* – Matching such [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), this tamiḻ garland of thousand pāsurams. Among those thousand pāsurams, those who are well versed in this decad.
- *nedumāṟku adimai seyya nērpattār* – This means “those who recite these pāsurams, will get to engage in [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s activities \[of singing emperumān\]”. nērpadugai – to be spoken about; implies, they are spoken about. Thus, with this pāsuram, āḻvār explained the true nature of sarvēśvara, the true nature of self, the greatness of this prabandam which reveals about these aspects and the greatness of the result which is attained by those who recite this decad.

## 8.10 Nedumarkadimai

## 8.10.1. Nedumarkadimai

*nedumāṟkadimai seyvēn pōl avanaik karuda vanjittu tadumāṟṟa tīkkadigaḷ muṟṟum tavirnda sadir ninaindāl kodu mā vinaiyēn avan adiyār adiyē kūdum iduvallāl vidumāṟenbaden? andō! viyan mūvulagu peṟinumē ḷisten*

**Пословный перевод:**

nedu – unlimited; māṟku – for sarvēśvara (who has great love for his devotees); adimai seyvēnpōl – as to serve; avanai – him; karuda – as I thought; tadumāṟṟam – wavering; aṟṟa – remaining in me, to eliminate; tīkkadigaḷ – the evil ways (which are in the form of avidyā \[ignorance\], causing sorrow); muṟṟum – all; vanjittu – deceiving me (without my knowledge); tavirnda – left me (as said in “kānō orungiṟṟum kaṇḍila māl“); sadir – apt; ninaindāl – if we see; avan – for him (who has motherly affection towards devotees); adiyār – bhāgavatas, who are his servitors; adiyē – divine feet only; kūdum idu allāl – other than attaining; viyan – vast; mū ulagu – wealth of three worlds; peṟinum – even if attained; kodu – to highlight the difference between aisvaryam (wealth) and tadīya śēśatvam (being subservient to devotees); mā vinaiyēn – I who am having great sin; vidum – leaving; āṟu – as ways; enbadu – saying; en – why?; andō – alas!

**Перевод:**

**As I thought to serve the unlimited sarvēśvara, he remained in me to eliminate the wavering in me and ensured that the evil ways left me through deception; if we see what is apt, other than attaining the divine feet of bhāgavatas who are his servitors, why is attaining the vast wealth of three worlds said as ways for me who is having great sin (to highlight the difference between aisvaryam (wealth) and tadīya śēśatvam (being subservient to devotees), to leave the divine feet of such bhāgavatas?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the first pāsuram, āḻvār says “Even more than ruling over the amazing three worlds, serving bhāgavatas is most enjoyable for me”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*First pāsuram. āḻvār says “It is not even worthy to say that worldly wealth which is considered as the goal by worldly people cannot be compared to the goal I have pursued”. nedumāṟkadimai seyvēn pōl avanaik karuda vanjittu tadumāṟṟa tīkkadigaḷ muṟṟum tavirnda sadir ninaindāl kodu mā vinaiyēn avan adiyār adiyē kūdum iduvallāl vidumāṟenbaden? andō! viyan mūvulagu peṟinumē Listen*

- *nedumāṟku* – For *nedumāl*. *māl* means the great. By saying *nedu*, the greatness is emphasised; implies “very great person”. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is seeking the ultimate state of his lordship, since he is focussed on the ultimate state of servitude. Alternative explanation – *māl* indicates love, and *nedu* the greatness of that. His love is such that he does not just place \[me\] at him but leads \[me\] up to his devotees; amalanādipirān “*adiyārkkennai ātpadutta vimalan*” (the pure lord who made me serve his devotees).
- *adimai seyvēn pōl avanaik karuda* – As I considered him similar to those who serve him. It is only mithra bhāva (superficial friendship) and when deeply analysed, being a liar.
- *tadumāṟṟu aṟṟa tīkkadigaḷ muṟṟum tavirnda* – Since I have not performed any virtuous activity which will remove my ignorance, all of such ignorance etc were eliminated. How were those eliminated? By deception. Just as naḷa who said to damayanti in the day time “we will live together forever”, ate together in the night from the same plate, slept together under lit lamp, but left her without her knowledge. Could also be recited as “*adimai sēvēn pōl avanai – vanjittu – karuda*” (To deceive him as if I am serving his devotees).
- *muṟṟum tavirnda* – Only when I eliminate my ignorance etc, they will go gradually. When he does, it will be as said in cāndōjña upaniśat 5.25 “*ēvam hāsya sarvē pāpmāna: pradūyantē*” (For one with such true knowledge in vēdāntam, all his sins will be destroyed like dust thrown into fire) and in [śrī bhagavat gītā 18.66](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/18-66/) “*sarva pāpēbhyō mōkśayiśyāmi*” (I will free you from all sorrows).
- *sadir ninaindāl* – As we think about how all our evil effects were removed on surrendering at his divine feet, should we not pursue the ultimate state of puruśārtam (i.e. being surrendered to bhāgavatas)? Should we not be surrendered to bhāgavatas if we see what is apt?
- *kodumā vinaiyēn* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is speaking with great bliss just as someone who becomes immersed in hearing a song, exclaims “*pāviyēn*” (Oh I am a sinner!) when the notes become jarring. Alternative explanation – āḻvār is saying that he did not get to serve the ultimate state (bhāgavatas) in the initial stage itself.
- *avan adiyār adiyē kūdum idu allāl* – If emperumān shows great love towards those who are surrendered to his divine feet, should we also not desire for those who are desired by him? If he is greatly attached to his devotees should we also not pursue what is pleasing to him? By the avadāraṇa (exclusivity – “E” in adiyē), it is explained that [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) does not consider himself to be equivalent to those who are surrendered to [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s divine feet; as emperumān is the ultimate state of lordship, āḻvār stands at the ultimate state of servitude.
- *adiyē kūdum* – āḻvār is not desiring to enjoy along with the bhāgavatas, but is of the nature to hold on to their divine feet.
- *vidum āṟu enbadu en* – Can I deal with this aspect (serving bhāgavatas) as I pursue or give up worldly aspects? \[One should pursue this with utmost sincerity\]
- *andō* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying “alas!” feeling “I am trying to compare aiśvaryam which is way below the goal I pursued \[bhāgavata śēśatvam\]”
- *viyan mū ulagu peṟinum* – Even if the forests and hills in the three worlds were cleared and the three worlds were made to be enjoyable, and placed at my full disposal, how can I think about leaving bhāgavata śēśatvam! āḻvār is saying “This aiśvaryam is not comparable to the goal I have pursued”, since it \[aiśvaryam\] is desired by worldly people, even though it is totally incomparable to bhāgavata śēśatvam.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.10.2. Viyan muvulagu

*viyan mūvulagu peṟinum pōyt tānē tānē ānālum puyal mēgam pōl tirumēni ammān punai pūngaḻal adik kīḻ sayamē adimai talai ninṟār tiruttāḷ vaṇangi immaiyē payanē inbam yān peṟṟadu uṟumō pāviyēnukkē? ḷisten*

**Пословный перевод:**

viyan – huge; mū ulagu – the wealth of three worlds; peṟinum – even if attained; pōy – going (without attachment in that); tānē – being self; tānē – exclusively being self (without enjoying īśvara); ānālum – if enjoyed; puyal – ready to rain; mēgam pōl – like cloud (having the quality of being generous towards devotees); tirumēni – having divine form; ammān – sarvēśvara’s; punai – worn; pū – flower; kaḻal – having anklets of bravery; adik kīḻ – under the divine feet; sayamē – without any other expectation; adimai – servitude; talai – in ultimate state; ninṟār – those who remained; tiru – distinguished; tāḷ – divine feet; vaṇangi – offering praṇāmams (matching that servitude); immaiyē – in this world itself; payanē – as result; yān – I; peṟṟadu – attained; inbam – for the bliss; pāviyēnukku – for me who has committed sins (of having to highlight the greatness of bhāgavata śēśatvam over other results); uṟumō – would those aiśvarya and kaivalya results fit me?

**Перевод:**

**sarvēśvaran has rain-cloud like divine form and his divine feet are decorated with flower and anklets of bravery. There are bhāgavatas \[followers of emperumān\] who are in the ultimate state of servitude to those divine feet, without any expectation. Even If I were to get the huge wealth of three worlds and go on to enjoy exclusively such aiśvaryam and kaivalyam, will these fit me who has committed sins when I offer praṇāmams (salutations) to such bhāgavatas? It implies that these \[aiśvaryam and kaivalyam\] are no match for carrying out kainkaryam to bhāgavatas.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the second pāsuram, āḻvār says “Even if aiśvaryam (worldly wealth) and kaivalyam (self enjoyment) were attained together, it will not be comparable to bhāgavata śēśatvam (servitude towards bhāgavatas), the goal that I have attained”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. viyan mūvulagu peṟinum pōyt tānē tānē ānālum puyal mēgam pōl tirumēni ammān punai pūngaḻal adik kīḻ sayamē adimai talai ninṟār tiruttāḷ vaṇangi immaiyē payanē inbam yān peṟṟadu uṟumō pāviyēnukkē? Listen*

- *viyan mū ulagu peṟinum* – Even if the astonishing wealth of the three worlds are exclusively given to me.
- *pōyt tānē tānē ānālum* – Being relieved from bondage in samsāram, and even if exclusively enjoyed the self. Repetition of *tānē* (self) implies being freed from enjoyment in this samsāram along with the children, grandchildren et al and not enjoying in paramapadam as said in taittirīya upaniśat “*aham annam aham annam aham annam*” (I am the food enjoyed by bhagavān – repetition implies emphasis), and enjoying self alone.
- *puyal …* – [sarvēśvaran](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) enslaved the whole world by showing his divine form which appears like a rain cloud. His divine feet are decorated with flower and anklets of bravery. Implies that [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) has such strong relationship that even if he is ugly, he cannot be given up.
- *sayamē adimai talai ninṟār* – Those who serve him without any expectations. Alternative explanation – those who serve him in all manners, being won over by his beauty.
- *sayam* – May mean either svayam (without expectation) or jayam (victorious).
- *tiruttāḷ vaṇangi* – Even more than attaining ātmā which is greater than body and eternal, a limb of those who are won over by his beauty, is sufficient – says [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/).
- *immaiyē payanē inbam* – Instead of having to shed the body here and go somewhere else to enjoy, I got the bliss of enjoying in this world itself. I got it already instead of having to perform some sādanam (means) and attain it in the future.
- *uṟumō* – Are they \[aiśvaryam and kaivalyam\] comparable to this?
- *pāviyēnukkē* – I have committed the sin of having to compare the ultimate goal which is eternal and that which cannot even be considered as goal. Since it is not temporary as aiśvaryam, ātma prāpti (kaivalyam) is considered to be eternal puruśārtam; but since it does not involve bhagavat viśayam (engaging in bhagavān), it is considered as apuruśārtām (not a valid goal);.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.
