## 8.10.3. Urumo paviyenukku

*uṟumō pāviyēnukku ivvulaga mūnṟum udan niṟaiyasiṟu mā mēni nimirtta en sendāmaraik kaṇ tirukkuṟaḷannaṟu mā virai nāṇmalar adik kīḻp pugudal anṟi avan adiyārsiṟu mā manisarāy ennai āṇḍār ingē tiriyavē*

**Пословный перевод:**

i – these (not aware of itself); ulagam mūnṟum – three worlds; udan – in a single effort; niṟaiya – to fill; siṟu – being small (to become small and enjoy him); mā – attractive, having distinguished greatness; mēni – divine form; nimirtta – one who made it grow; en – being perfectly enjoyable for me; sem – reddish; tāmarai – lotus like; kaṇ – having eye; tirukkuṟaḷan – śrī vāmana’s; naṟu – fragrant; mā – best; virai – having honey; nāṇ(L) malar – like a fresh flower; adik kīḻ – (serving) under the divine feet; pugudal – attaining; avan – for such vāmana; adiyār – servitors; siṟu – though they appear to be small due to having human form; mā manisarāy – being great personalities (of having greatness beyond that of nityasūris); ennai – me; āṇḍār – those who enslaved me; ingē – in this world itself; tiriya – visibly remaining; anṟi – other than this; pāviyēnukku – for me who is having the sin (to distinguish between tadīya śēśatvam (servitude towards bhāgavatas) which is the ultimate state and tat śēśatvam (servitude towards bhagavān) which is the initial state); uṟumō – does it fit?

**Перевод:**

**śrī vāmana made his small, attractive distinguished divine form grow in a single effort to fill these three worlds, is having reddish lotus like eye which is perfectly enjoyable for me; for me who is having the sin, does it fit to attain such vāmana’s fragrant, best, divine feet which resemble fresh flower with honey, while such vāmana’s servitors who appear to be small due to having human form but are great personalities, who enslaved me, are visibly remaining in this world itself?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the third pāsuram, āḻvār says “Even if I attained bhagavat prāpti (reaching bhagavān and serving him) which is distinguished from aiśvaryam (wealth) and kaivalyam (soul enjoying itself), that would not match serving bhāgavatas in this world”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. āḻvār says that while the śrīvaiṣṇavas, who are dear to the divine feet which measured the world, engage me in their service, service to the divine feet which measured the world is not apt. uṟumō pāviyēnukku ivvulaga mūnṟum udan niṟaiyasiṟu mā mēni nimirtta en sendāmaraik kaṇ tirukkuṟaḷannaṟu mā virai nāṇmalar adik kīḻp pugudal anṟi avan adiyārsiṟu mā manisarāy ennai āṇḍār ingē tiriyavē*

- *uṟumō pāviyēnukku* – āḻvār is reciting the words which he used in context of ātmānubhavam (enjoying self) and aiśvaryam (worldly wealth).
- *uṟumō pāviyēnukku* – But this \[bhagavat viśayam\] cannot be discarded like those; it is discarded since it is not the ultimate state of the puruśārtam (attainable goal).
- *pāviyēn* – I have committed the sin to be highlighting the difference between initial state and ultimate state. *ulgamuūnṟudan niṟaiya … nāṇmalar adik kīḻp pugudal uṟumō*?
- *ivvulagam mūnṟum udan niṟaiya* – Just as clouds will rain to fill some dried out lakes which have no knowledge about being dry, to fill the three worlds which have no knowledge about his greatness.
- *siṟu mā mēni nimirtta* – Reducing his size to be very small so that one can enjoy him within one’s own eyes, increased the size of his divine form which has unlimited greatness.
- *em* – As said in [iraṇḍām tiruvandādi 61](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/11/irandam-thiruvandhadhi-61/) “*unnaip piramāṇittār peṟṟa pēṟu*” (is the great benefit that all those who believed you, got), this was done for the benefit of your devotees.
- *sem tāmarai …* – Under the divine feet, which appear like a fresh flower with beautiful fragrance, of śrī vāmana who has beautiful eyes which have vastness, freshness and coolness to be compared to a lotus flower.
- *naṟu mā virai* – Very abundant fragrance; āḻvār is discarding such wonderful divine feet as bitter neem drink saying “*uṟumō*“. As āḻvār holds on to bhāgavata viśayam which is the essence of bhagavat viśayam, he discards the pulp (of exclusive bhagavat viśayam without bhāgavata viśayam).
- *anṟi* – discarding that.
- *avan adiyār* – śrīvaiṣṇavas who are captivated by śrī vāmana. They are those who remain as said in periya tirumoḻi 9.4.2 “*munnam kuṟaḷuruvāy mūvadi maṇ koṇḍaḷanda – mannan saridaikkē mālāgip pon payandēn*” (I became bewildered and acquired paleness on hearing the incident of emperumān previously accepting three feet of land and measuring the world).
- *siṟu mā manisarāy* – Those who have small form but vast greatness. When parāśara bhattar was young, he enquired kūrattāḻvān “How can contrary qualities of being small and big be applicable in the same entity?” āḻvān explained “mudaliyāṇḍān, aruḷāḷap perumāḷ emperumānār, śrī gōvindap perumāḷ (embār) are siṟu mā manisar since they appear to be similar to us \[in being small\] by their dependence of food, water for sustenance but are comparable to nityasūris in their devotion towards bhagavān”.
- *ennai āṇḍār* – Those who have enslaved me.
- *ingē tiriya* – While they are present in front of me.
- *anṟi* – discarding them.
- *naṟu mā virai nāḷ malar adik kīḻp pugudal – uṟumō pāviyēnukku* – This is nammāḻvār’s kaṇṇinuṇ ciṟut tāmbu \[just as madurakavi āḻvār exclusive focussed on nammāḻvār in his prabandam, nammāḻvār is exclusively focussing on bhāgavatas in this decad\]. śrī madurakavi also is in this same state. After fully learning from tiruviruttam 1 “*poy ninṟa jñānam*” to tiruvāimoḻi 10.10 \[last decad\] “*muniyē nānmuganē*“, madurakavi āḻvār accepted as his refuge, the decads which nammāḻvār highlighted as his goal [tiruvāimoḻi 3.7](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/09/thiruvaimozhi-3-7-payilum/) “*payilum sudaroḷi*” and [tiruvāimoḻi 8.10](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/05/thiruvaimozhi-8-10-nedumarkadimai/) “*nedumāṟkadimai*“. It is said in taittirīya upaniśat “*yānyasmākam sucaritāni*” (The ācārya instructs the śiśyas, what are considered as good conduct and what are to be pursued by the śiśyas).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.10.4. Inge tirinderku

*ingē tirindēṟkiḻukkuṟṟēn? iru mā nilam mun uṇḍumiḻndasengōlatta pavaḷa vāyc cendāmaraik kaṇ en ammānpongēḻ pugaḻgaḷ vāyavāyp pulan koḷ vadiven manattadāyangēy malargaḷ kaiyavāy vaḻipattōda aruḷilē*

**Пословный перевод:**

iru – expansive; mā – praiseworthy; nilam – universe; mun – during the danger of deluge; uṇḍu – consumed; umiḻnda – while spitting it out (subsequently); sem – reddish; kōlatta – having beauty; pavaḷam – like coral; vāy – divine lip; sem – reddish; tāmarai – like lotus; kaṇ – having divine eye; en – my; ammān – lord; pongu – actively; ēḻ – rising; pugaḻgaḷ – his qualities; vāyavāy – to be the target of my speech; pulan koḷ – captivating all the senses; vadivu – form; en – my; manattadāy – to be in my heart; angu – there; ēy – matching; malargaḷ – flowers; kaiyavāy – to be in hands; vaḻi – in the path (of service done by bhāgavatas with the three faculties); pattu – being aligned; ōda – and act; aruḷil – if he blesses; ingē – in this world; tirindēṟku – for me who is moving around; en – what; iḻukkuṟṟu – is the insult?

**Перевод:**

**emperumān, my lord, is having beautiful, coral-like, reddish, divine lips which consumed the expansive, praiseworthy universe during the danger of deluge and spat it out, and is having reddish, lotus-like, divine eye; what is the insult if he blesses me who is moving around in this world, to be aligned and act in the path to have his actively rising qualities to be the target of my speech, his form which captivates all my senses to be in my heart and to hold flowers matching his greatness in my hands?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fourth pāsuram, āḻvār says “If I get to praise and serve emperumān to please śrīvaiṣṇavas, the ultimate goal for me is to remain here in this world itself which is praiseworthy due to their moving around here”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. ingē tirindēṟkiḻukkuṟṟēn? iru mā nilam mun uṇḍumiḻndasengōlatta pavaḷa vāyc cendāmaraik kaṇ en ammānpongēḻ pugaḻgaḷ vāyavāyp pulan koḷ vadiven manattadāyangēy malargaḷ kaiyavāy vaḻipattōda aruḷilē*

- *ingē tirindēṟku* – You said in previous pāsuram “*siṟu mā manisar*” and “*ingē*“; but isn’t this world said as in tiruvāimoḻi 10.6.1 “*iruḷ taru mā jñālam*” (the world which gives darkness/ignorance)? īsn’t it in paramapadam where one gets to engage in bhagavat anubhavam (enjoying [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)) which leads to bhāgavata kainkaryam (service to bhāgavatas)? [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying “What is wrong to live here, if we get the same bhagavat anubhavam by his mercy here itself?” Implies āḻvār saying – even for our experience in paramapadam, his mercy is the reason; if that is received here itself, what is wrong?
- *iḻukkuṟṟu en* – What is the inferiority?
- *iru mā nilam mun uṇḍu umiḻnda* – During deluge, placing the greatly expansive universe in his stomach and protecting it, and releasing it during creation.
- *sem kōlatta pavaḷa vāy* – One who is having beautiful divine lips which will make one not to let go of him even if he pushes one in to the deluge. Reddish, beautiful coral-like divine lips.
- *sem tāmaraik kaṇ en ammān* – One who made me say “jitam” (you have won) by his glance. One who enslaved me by the qualities and beauty mentioned here.
- *pongēḻ …* – pongi – spreading out; kēḻ – beauty. To have his actively rising auspicious qualities in my mouth. The qualities which have the agitation of a flood, which can agitate those who entered \[to enjoy them\].
- *pulan koḷ vadivu en manattadāy* – To have his form which captivates all the senses, in my mind.
- *angēy malargaḷ kaiyavāy* – To have flowers matching his form, in my hands.
- *vaḻipattōda aruḷil* – If we are blessed to follow the path properly; if we get his mercy so that we get to serve his divine feet with my mind, speech and body.
- *ingē tirindēṟku iḻukkuṟṟu en* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying that if he gets bhagavat kainkaryam which is pleasing to bhāgavatas, in this world itself, by his mercy, that will be considered as his puruśārtam (attainable goal).

## 8.10.5. Valipattoda

*vaḻipattōda aruḷ peṟṟu māyan kōla malar adik kīḻ suḻipattōdum sudarc cōdi veḷḷattu inbuṟṟirundālum iḻipattōdum udalinil piṟand tan sīr yān kaṟṟu moḻipattōdum kavi amudam nugarcci uṟumō? muḻudumē ḷisten*

**Пословный перевод:**

vaḻipattu – being engaged properly; ōda – to go on; aruḷ – his mercy; peṟṟu – attained; māyan – sarvēśvara who has amazing nature, form, qualities and wealth, his; kōlam malar – ultimately enjoyable; adik kīḻ – under the divine feet; suḻipattu – whirling; ōdum – continuously running; sudar – having radiance; sōdi veḷḷattu – in paramapadam which is in the form of clusters of splendour; inbuṟṟu – being very blissful; irundālum – even if I remained; muḻudum – even if I acquired previously explained aiśvaryam, kaivalyam etc; iḻipattu – in inferiority; ōdum – very lowly; udalinil – in body; piṟandu – taking birth; than – (most enjoyable) his; sīr – qualities; yān – I (who am very distant for them); kaṟṟu – learn; moḻipattu – as words (caused by the joy of such experience); ōdum – flowing; kavi – poem; amudam – amrutam (nectar); nugarcci – to enjoy (along with the devotees); uṟumō – will it match?

**Перевод:**

**sarvēśvara has amazing nature, form, qualities and wealth; even if I attained such sarvēśvara’s mercy to be engaged properly and go on to remain very blissfully under his ultimately enjoyable divine feet in paramapadam which has whirling and continuously running radiance, and even if I acquired the previously explained aiśvaryam, kaivalyam etc, would those be a match for taking birth in this inferior, lowly body, learning his qualities and singing nectarean poems as flowing sequence of words and enjoying them?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fifth pāsuram, āḻvār says “Even if I go to tirunādu (paramapadam) and attain the ultimate goal of serving him there and even if I get all of the previously mentioned aiśvaryam (worldly wealth) etc, would they match taking birth in this samsāram and singing tiruvāimoḻi for the pleasure of śrīvaiṣṇavas?”*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. vaḻipattōda aruḷ peṟṟu māyan kōla malar adik kīḻ suḻipattōdum sudarc cōdi veḷḷattu inbuṟṟirundālum iḻipattōdum udalinil piṟand than sīr yān kaṟṟu moḻipattōdum kavi amudam nugarcci uṟumō? muḻudumē Listen*

- *vaḻipattu ōda aruḷ peṟṟu* – Acquiring his mercy to engage in nitya kainkaryam (eternal service) in the proper manner.
- *māyan* – One who is amazing due to his beauty, simplicity etc.
- *kōlam malar adik kīḻ* – Under the divine feet which appear like attractive flower.
- *suḻipattu ōdum sudarc cōdi veḷḷattu* – In paramapadam which has waves of radiance which whirls around like a flood. It is said in mahābhāratam āraṇya parvam “*atyarkānaladīptam tat stānam*” ([śrīman nārāyaṇan](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)’s divine abode parampadam is many thousands of times more radiant than the sun and moon).
- *inbuṟṟu irundālum* – As said in taittirīya upaniśat ānandavalli 7 “*ēśahyēvānandayāti*” (he – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) – himself makes jīvātmā ecstatic), even if he gives joy and I become the enjoyer.
- *muḻudum* – Even if the previously explained aiśvaryam etc are included along.
- *iḻipattu ōdum udalinil piṟandu* – Taking birth in this body which is considered as the most lowly.
- *than sīr* – The auspicious qualities which will even drown the nityasūris.
- *yān kaṟṟu* – I who am a nityasamsāri (eternally bound in this material world), who am not qualified to learn them, learn and know them.
- *moḻipattu ōdum* – As they cannot be held inside, they overflow as words.
- *kavi amudam nugarcci uṟumō* – Would all of those match enjoying this nectar of tiruvāimoḻi?
- *sudarc cōdi veḷḷattu inbuṟṟu irundālum muḻudum* – He himself said “*avan adiyār siṟu mā manisarāy ennai āṇḍār ingē tiriya – naṟu mā virai nāṇmalar adik kīḻ pugudal uṟumō*” (when his great devotees are present here, would it be apt to go under the divine feet of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)); leaving even that, he is saying “*kavi amudam nugarcci uṟumō muḻudum*” (would all of those match enjoying tiruvāimoḻi?). Is [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) leaving that (serving devotees)? No. Since he has said in tiruvāimoḻi 9.4.9 “*toṇḍarkkamuduṇṇac col mālaigaḷ sonnēn*” (I recited these garlands of words, to have the devotees drink them as nectar), this is how āḻvār is serving them.

## 8.10.6. Nugarcci urumo?

*nugarcci uṟumō? mūvulagin vīdu pēṟu tan kēḻil pugarc cem mugatta kaḷiṟatta pon āḻik kai en ammān nigarc cembangi eri viḻigaḷ nīṇḍa asurar uyir ellām tagarttuṇḍuḷalum putpāgan periya tani māp pugaḻē ḷisten*

**Пословный перевод:**

than – for him; kēḻ – match; il – not having; pugar – having radiance; sem – become red (due to anger); mugatta – having face; ānai – elephant; atta – destroyed; pon – attractive; āḻi – having divine ring; kai – one who is having divine hands; en – my; ammān – being the lord; nigar – matching its species; sem – reddish; pangi – (hanging) hairs; eri – like fire disc; viḻigaḷ – having eyes; nīṇḍa – having well built bodies; asurar – asuras’ (demons’); uyir ellām – all their vital airs; tagarttu – attacked; uṇḍu – consumed; uḻalum – roaming; puḷ – for periya tiruvadi (garudāḻvār); pāgan – controller, his; periya – unlimited; tani – distinguished; mā – greatly enjoyable; pugaḻ – collections of auspicious qualities; nugarcci – enjoying through tiruvāimoḻi which is pleasing to bhāgavatas; mū ulagin – of the three worlds; vīdu – ability to create; pēṟu – lordship which has; uṟumō – is it a match?

**Перевод:**

**emperumān, my lord, is having divine hands with attractive divine ring, which were used to destroy the elephant having incomparable radiance and reddish face; he is the controller of periya tiruvadi (garudāḻvār) who roams around attacking the vital airs and consuming the well built asuras (demons) who are having reddish hair and fire disc like eyes; would the lordship which has the ability to create the three worlds be a match for enjoying such emperumān’s unlimited, distinguished, greatly enjoyable collections of auspicious qualities through tiruvāimoḻi which is pleasing to bhāgavatas?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the sixth pāsuram, āḻvār says “Only if aiśvarya (worldly wealth), kaivalya (self enjoyment), bhagavat anubhava prīti (joy of experiencing bhagavān) and bhagavat ānandam (bhagavān’s bliss) were attained, would those match the recital of tiruvāimoḻi for the pleasure of his devotees?”*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. āḻvār says “To enjoy the huge, incomparable, distinguished qualities of putpāgan (rider of garuda) through tiruvāimoḻi, even the all pervading bhagavān‘s bliss is not a match”. nugarcci uṟumō? mūvulagin vīdu pēṟu than kēḻil pugarc chem mugatta kaḷiṟatta pon āḻik kai en ammān nigarc cembangi eri viḻigaḷ nīṇḍa asurar uyir ellām tagarttuṇḍuḷalum putpāgan periya tani māp pugaḻē Listen*

- *nugarcci uṟumō* – Would those match enjoying [bhagavān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s qualities through tiruvāimoḻi?
- *mū ulagin vīdu pēṟu* – Would the ability to create/annihilate the universe in a fraction of one’s vow/will be a match for that \[tiruvāimoḻi enjoyment\]? [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) considers that as aiśvaryam (wealth/ability); [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) considers it is only a puruśārtam (goal, that too an inferior one). As said in “*jagat vyāpāra varjam*” (the liberated soul will not engage in worldly activities such as creation, annihilation etc though he will be capable of them), would only that which is matching the nature of the self, be not considered as puruśārtam?
- *than kēḻil …* – Finished the the elephant, kuvalayāpīdam, which was having matchless pride, and having radiance and a red face due to anger.
- *pon āḻik kai* – One whose divine hand is decorated with beautiful divine ring. While hitting the elephant’s temple and cheeks, this is how his divine hand with the ring appeared to be.
- *en ammān* – One who showed his divine form with the divine hand decorated with the ring and enslaved me. He finished the enemies with his strength and the devotees with his beauty.
- *nigar …* – Routinely attacking and consuming the lives of the well built demons having reddish hair, eyes which appear like burning fire matching their demoniac birth. [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) rides such garudāḻvār; would anything match enjoying the unlimited, matchless, auspicious qualities of such emperumān through tiruvāimoḻi?
- *mū ulagin vīdu pēṟu* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying that even the joy of being seated on the throne ruling over the whole universe, will not match the joy of enjoying tiruvāimoḻi.

## 8.10.7. Tanimap pugale

*tani māp pugaḻē enjñānṟum niṟkumpadiyāt tān tōnṟi muni māp pirama mudal vittāy ulagamūnṟum muḷaippitta tanimāt teyvat taḷir adik kīḻp pugudal anṟi avan adiyār nani māk kalavi inbamē nāḷum vāykka nangatkē ḷisten*

**Пословный перевод:**

tani – distinguished; mā – great; pugaḻē – his qualities which highlight his kāraṇatva (being the cause); enjñānṟum – always; niṟkumpadiyā – to firmly remain (as highlighted popularly in vēdāntam); tān – himself; tōnṟi – incarnating with the intent to engage in creation (as said in “prārturāsīttamōnuta:“); muni – to meditate upon creation (as said in the vow “bahusyām“); māp piramam – being explained by the term “para brahmam”; mudal – primary; vittāy – material cause; ulaga mūnṟum – the three worlds; muḷaippitta – created; tani māt teyvam – the distinguished supreme lord’s; taḷir – very tender; adik kīḻ – under the divine feet; pugudal anṟi – instead of attaining; avan adiyār – for the bhāgavatas who were enslaved by his such qualities; nani – very; mā – best; kalavi inbamē – the joy of being united with them; nangatku – for us; nāḷum – always; vāykka – should occur

**Перевод:**

**emperumān, incarnates with the intent to engage in creation, to have his distinguished, great qualities which highlight his kāraṇatva, remains firmly always, meditating upon creation, being explained by the term “para brahmam”, created the three worlds which are the primary material causes; instead of attaining the presence under the very tender divine feet of such distinguished supreme lord, to have the joy of being united with the very best bhāgavatas who were enslaved by his such qualities should always occur for us.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the seventh pāsuram, āḻvār says “I don’t need the bhagavat anubhavam (enjoying bhagavān) which is considered as the independent goal; but I would like to unite with bhāgavatas and engage in bhagavat anubhavam for the pleasure of bhāgavatas”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. tani māp pugaḻē enjñānṟum niṟkumpadiyāt tān tōnṟi muni māp pirama mudal vittāy ulagamūnṟum muḷaippitta tanimāt teyvat taḷir adik kīḻp pugudal anṟi avan adiyār nani māk kalavi inbamē nāḷum vāykka nangatkē Listen*

- *tani mā …* – To have the incomparable, best qualities remain forever.
- *tān* – one who has primordial matter as his body.
- *tān tōnṟi* – Being complete while there is no one who could pray to him to engage in creation, for his own satisfaction, appeared saying as in taititirīya upaniśat “*bahu syām*” (let me become many).
- *muni māp pirama mudal vittāy* – Being the parabrahma, the ultimate cause, which vows. muni – desireless. As a mother would worry for her son who has gone to a distant country, parabrahma himself being the three causes (upādāna kāraṇa (material cause), nimitta kāraṇa (ancillary cause) and sahākāri kāraṇa (instrumental cause)) worrying for the jīvātmās who are in subdued state.
- *ulaga mūnṟum muḷaippitta* – He made sure that all the resulting entities blossom from him; this is how his sankalpam of creating many universes was.
- *tani …* – Entering under the divine feet of the unparalelled supreme lord; this is the objective of creation. For a cētana (sentient being), it is apt to surrender unto the divine feet of the benefactor.
- *anṟi* – leaving that aside.
- *avan adiyār …* – To eternally have the greatly distinguished union with such śrīvaiṣṇavas who have offered themselves to him seeing such benefactorśip.
- *nangatkē* – For us who desire for this and think “this is the ultimate goal”, this should occur forever.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.10.8. Nalum vaykka

*nāḷum vāykka nangatku naḷir nīrk kadalaip padaittut tan tāḷum tōḷum mudigaḷum samanilāda pala parappi nīḷum padar pūngaṟpagak kāvum niṟai pannāyiṟṟin kōḷum udaiya maṇimalaipōl kidandān tamargaḷ kūttamē ḷisten*

**Пословный перевод:**

naḷir – naturally cool; nīr – having water; kadalai – causal ocean; padaittu – created (as said in “apa Eva sasarjātau“); than – (that itself) being distinguished as revealed in vēdam; saman – match; ilāda – without having; tāḷum – divine feet; tōḷum – divine shoulders; mudigaḷum – divine crowns/heads; pala – as many (to be in count of thousands); parappi – spreading out; nīḷum – rising; padar – grown; pū – beautiful; kaṟpagak kāvum – garden of kaṟpaka (kalpa – celestial) trees; niṟai – dense; pal – many (rays); nāyiṟṟin kōḷum – the radiance of the sun; udaiya – having; maṇi malai pōl – like a carbuncle hill; kidandān – one who is resting, his; tamargaḷ – of the servitors; kūttam – union; nangatku – for us; nāḷum – forever; vāykka – should occur

**Перевод:**

**emperumān created the causal ocean with naturally cool water, and is resting in it as revealed in vēdam, having distinguished, matchless, many divine feet, divine shoulders and divine crowns/heads similar to a carbuncle hill having gardens of rising, beautiful, well grown kaṟpaka trees and a radiant sun with many dense rays; union with servitors of such emperumān should occur for us, forever. kūttam – sērtti – union. Alternatively, kūttam means sangam (crowd), and here āḻvār prays for the presence of such crowd in front of him.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the eighth pāsuram, āḻvār says “Do I even need to unite and interact with bhāgavatas? Just being present with them is sufficient. ōr just seeing the groups of them, is sufficient”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. nāḷum vāykka nangatku naḷir nīrk kadalaip padaittut than tāḷum tōḷum mudigaḷum samanilāda pala parappi nīḷum padar pūngaṟpagak kāvum niṟai pannāyiṟṟin kōḷum udaiya maṇimalaipōl kidandān tamargaḷ kūttamē Listen*

- *nāḷum vāykka …* – For us who have this as the puruśārtam (goal), this should occur forever.
- *naḷir nīrk kadalaip padaittu* – Creating the ocean which has coolness as its nature. Also implies the water that is apt for his resting.
- *saman ilāda tāḷum tōḷum mudigaḷum* – His limbs which have no similes.
- *pala parappi* – Decorating the whole ocean with his form to eliminate the vacuum in there.
- *nīḷum padar pūm kaṟpagak kāvum* – Divine feet which resemble ultimately enjoyable flower and divine shoulders which resemble a garden of kaṟpaka tree. This is how his divine feet and shoulders are.
- *niṟai pal nāyiṟṟin kōḷum* – This resonates with what is said in [tiruvāimoḻi 8.8.10](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/02/thiruvaimozhi-8-1-10-thalgalai-enakke/) “*mudigaḷāyirattāy*” (having thousand divine heads). kōḷ – tējas (radiance). The head which appears to be made of millions of suns together. kōḷ – graham (planet). Since planets emit light, here also kōḷ implies radiance.
- *maṇi malai pōl kidandān* – His resting looks like a carbuncle hill which is laid down.
- *tamargaḷ kūttamē nāḷum vāykka* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is not praying for eternal occurrence of \[seeing\] such [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is resting so beautifully that one cannot take one’s eyes off him; āḻvār is saying that he should be part of those śrīvaiṣṇavas who are captivated in his beauty of resting as said in [tirumālai 23](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/10/thirumalai-23/) “*kidandadōr kidakkai*” (unparalleled resting posture); or he is saying that it is sufficient to just see such groups of śrīvaiṣṇavas. Just as a hungry person will say “bring me lot of rice”, āḻvār is saying \[“want to see the groups of śrīvaiṣṇavas”, instead of just saying “want to see śrīvaiṣṇavas”\] matching is desire. It is said in mārkaṇḍēya purāṇam “*sadbhirēva sahāsīta*” (should be with elders) and in perumāḷ tirumoḻi 2.1 “*īttam kaṇḍidak kūdumēl*” (if we can see the presence of bhāagvatas). Previously, āḻvār said “I would like to unite with śrīvaiṣṇavas who are captivated by his benefactorśip”; here he is saying “it is sufficient to just see the groups of śrīvaiṣṇavas who are captivated by his resting posture”.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.10.9. Tamargal kutta

*tamargaḷ kūtta val vinaiyai nāsam seyyum sadir mūrtti amargoḷ āḻi sangu vāḷ vil taṇḍādi pal padaiyan kumaran kōla aingaṇai vēḷ tādai kōdil adiyar tam tamargaḷ tamargaḷ tamargaḷām sadirē vāykka tamiyēṟkē ḷisten*

**Пословный перевод:**

tamargaḷ – devotees; kūttam – occurring for the group; val – strong; vainaiyai – sins; nāsam – (total) destruction; seyyum – to do; sadir – having ability; mūrtti – being the lord; amar – engaging in battle to eliminate the enemies; koḷ – having; āḻi sangu vāḷ vil taṇḍu ādi – starting with śrī pancāyudam (disc, conch, sword, bow and mace); palpadaiyan – being the one with many types of innumerable weapons; kumaran – being youthful (which highlights his ability to eliminate the enemies); kōlam – having great physical beauty; aingaṇai – one who has five arrows; vēḷ – for kāmadēva (cupid); tādai – having the greatness of being the father; kōdu – blemish (of seeking benefits other than kainkaryam); il – not having; adiyār tam – for the devotees; tamargaḷ – for servitors; tamargaḷ – for servitors; tamargaḷām – having the wealth of servitude; sadir – mercy; tamiyēṟku – for us who are helpless in samsāra; vāykka – should occur

**Перевод:**

**emperumān, the lord, is having the ability to cause destruction of the strong sins occurring to the group of his devotees; he is having many types of innumerable weapons starting with śrī pancāyudam; he is having the greatness of being the father of the youthful kāmadēva who has great physical beauty and five arrows; for us who are helpless in samsāra having the wealth of servitude towards the servitors of servitors of the blemiśless devotees of such emperumān, his mercy should occur. The term kūtta val vinai also implies sins derived through attachment \[to worldly pleasures\]. When recited as “cadu mūrtti” (instead of sadir mūrtti), it implies the different forms of emperumān.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the ninth pāsuram, āḻvār says “Do we even need to live with them? It is sufficient to be at the ultimate servitude towards them”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. tamargaḷ kūtta val vinaiyai nāsam seyyum sadir mūrtti amargoḷ āḻi sangu vāḷ vil taṇḍādi pal padaiyan kumaran kōla aingaṇai vēḷ tādai kōdil adiyar tam tamargaḷ tamargaḷ tamargaḷām sadirē vāykka tamiyēṟkē Listen*

- *tamargaḷ kūtta val vinaiyai nāsam seyyum* – One who would destroy the strong sins that enter the group of śrīvaiṣṇavar. Alternative explanation – one who would destroy the collective strong sins of his servitors. Another explanation – as the servitors increase their sins, he will destroy them. Just as it is natural for the servitor to increase his sins \[due to being in this material world\], it is natural for [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) to always destroy them.
- *cadu mūrtti* – emperumān will assume many apt forms to destroy the enemies \[of devotees\]. Just as the ātmā \[in liberated state\] will assume many forms to engage in service, emperumān will assume many forms to engage in protecting the devotees.
- *amar koḷ …* – One who has divine weapons such as tiruvāḻi (divine chakra) etc which are ready to battle, for the elimination of the enemies.
- *kumaran* – He remains eternally youthful.
- *kōlam …* – One who is the father of kāmadēva who has five arrows. It is said that even the beauty of kāmadēva who thinks “There is none beyond me for beauty” is originating from [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) himself. āḻvār is saying that he should be at the ultimate state of servitude for the śrīvaiṣṇavas who are ananya prayōjanas (who expect nothing but service) towards emperumān being captivated by his charming youth and beauty.
- *sadirē vāykka* – This ultimate goal should occur eternally.
- *tamiyēṟkē* – Even in the past, one needs to search and locate śrī śatrugnāḻvān for such bhāgavata śēśatvam (servitude towards bhāgavatas, in this case, śrī bharatāḻvān) and in the present there is none who matches āḻvār’s nature, āḻvār is saying “for us who are lonely”. In the previous pāsuram, āḻvār said “*nangatku*” (for us) since he is not lonely after singing [tiruvāimoḻi 2.8](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/04/thiruvaimozhi-2-7-kesavan-thamar/) “*kēsavan tamar*“; here āḻvār is saying “*tamiyēṟku*” (us who are lonely) since there is no match for him among samsāris (worldly people).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 8.10.10. Vaykka tamiyerku

*vāykka tamiyēṟku ūḻi tōṟūḻi ūḻi mākāyām pūk koḷ mēni nāngu tōḷ pon āḻik kai en ammān nīkkam illā adiyār tam adiyār adiyār adiyār em kōkkaḷ avarkkē kudigaḷāyc cellum nalla kōtpādē ḷisten*

**Пословный перевод:**

mā – having greatness of being attractive; kāyām pū – the complexion of kāyām (a dark purple coloured) flower; koḷ – having; mēni – divine form; nāngu tōḷ – the four divine shoulders (which are the resting place for the devotees); pon – attractive; āḻi – and tiruvāḻi (divine chakra); kai – having divine hand; en – one who enslaved me showing this physical beauty; ammān – lord; nīkkam – separation; illā – enjoying without; adiyār tam – for the servitors; adiyār adiyār adiyār – in the distinguished lineage of servitors; em – for my associates and I; kōkkaḷ – lords; avarkkē – for them only; kudigaḷāy – being the clan which engage in service; sellum – to be; nalla – praiseworthy; kōtpādu – act of pursuing; ūḻi tōṟūḻi – occuring in every mahā kalpa (brahmā’s one day which is made of thousand four yuga cycles); ūḻi – even in the intermediary kalpas; tamiyēṟku – for me (who has no match for being devoted towards devotees); vāykka – should occur

**Перевод:**

**emperumān enslaved me by the showing his attractive, great, physical beauty of his divine form having the complexion of kāyām (a dark purple coloured) flower, four divine shoulders and his divine hand having the attractive, divine chakra; for my associates and I, the servitors who are enjoying such lord without any separation, are my lords; it should occur for me to be in the clan which engage in service exclusively for them and to be in the praiseworthy act of pursuing them even in the intermediary kalpas which occur in every mahā kalpa.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the tenth pāsuram, āḻvār says “Both my associates and I should get this result \[of bhāgavata śēśatvam (servitude towards devotees)\]”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. vāykka tamiyēṟku ūḻi tōṟūḻi ūḻi mākāyām pūk koḷ mēni nāngu tōḷ pon āḻik kai en ammān nīkkam illā adiyār tam adiyār adiyār adiyār em kōkkaḷ avarkkē kudigaḷāyc cellum nalla kōtpādē Listen*

- *vāykka tamiyēṟku* – For me who has no simile due to being immersed in the ultimate state of puruśārtam (goal), I should get this result only.
- *ūḻi tōṟūḻi ūḻi* – Forever, without a break, this is the goal, as long as the ātmā exists.
- *mā kāyām pū …* – He made me totally exist for him by showing his beautiful kāyām flower like divine form, divine shoulders which resemble a well branched out kaṟpaka (celestial) tree, and the divine chakra which resemble a blossomed kaṟpaka flower.
- *nīkkam illā adiyār* – When [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) plans to separate, as seen in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 31.22 “*kuruśva mām*” (lakhsmaṇa to śrī rāma – You should make me follow you \[otherwise I will not be able to live\]), such devotees who are the ultimate ones in being unable to separate from him, are my lords. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is starting with those who were explained in previous pāsuram as “*adiyār adiyār adiyār*“. [tiruvāimoḻi 8.10.2](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/05/thiruvaimozhi-8-10-2-viyan-muvulagu/) “*sayamē adimai talai ninṟār”* (serving without any expectaion) are those who are like śrī bharatāḻvān \[who acted for the pleasure of śrī rāma exclusively\]. tiruvāimoḻi 8.10.9 “*kōdil adiyār*” (blemiśless servitors) are those who are like śrī śatrugnāḻvān \[who did not indulge in rāma bhakti\]. *nīkkam illā adiyār* (inseparable servitors) are those who are like iḷaiya perumāḷ \[lakśmaṇa, who served without separating from [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)\].
- *avarkkē kudigaḷāy* – Instead of being irukaraiyar (those who hold on to emperumān and devotees), it is apt to be as said in “*nacēt rāmānujēt ēśā caturā caturakśarī \| kāmavastām prapadyantē jantavō hantamādruśa: \|\|*” (If this great, four-lettered mantra of rāmānuja is not there, I don’t know the most fallen state persons like me will reach).
- *avarkkē …* – Let this good order of being exclusively devoted to them occur for us (my associates and I).

## 8.10.11. Nalla kotpattulagangal

*nalla kōtpāttulagangaḷ mūnṟin uḷḷum tān niṟainda allik kamalak kaṇṇanai andaṇ kurugūrc catakōpan sollap patta āyirattuḷ ivaiyum pattum vallārgaḷ nalla padattāl manai vāḻvar koṇḍa peṇḍir makkaḷē ḷisten*

**Пословный перевод:**

nalla – distinguished; kōtpādu – having space; ulagangaḷ mūnṟin uḷḷum – in the three worlds; tān – he; niṟainda – pervading; alli – blossomed; kamalam – lotus flower like; kaṇṇanai – on kriṣṇa; am – attractive; taṇ – invigorating; kurugūr – controller of āḻvārtirunagari; satakōpan – nammāḻvār; solla – by the merciful words; patta – created; āyirattuḷ – among the thousand pāsurams; ivaiyum pattum – this decad; vallārgaḷ – those who can practice; koṇḍa – accepted; peṇḍir makkaḷē – being with wife, children et al; nalla – distinguished; padattāl – in the state of tadīya śēśatvam (servitude towards devotees); manai – in gruhastāśramam (married life); vāḻvar – will live

**Перевод:**

**emperumān is pervading in the expansive three worlds and is having lotus flower like eyes; those who can practice this decad among the thousand pāsurams which were created from the merciful words of nammāḻvār, the controller of beautiful, invigorating āḻvārtirunagari, will live in gruhastāśramam along with their accepted wife, children et al in the distinguished state of tadīya śēśatvam.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the end, āḻvār says “Those who are expert in this decad, will acquire bhāgavata śēśatvam (servitude towards devotees) which is explained here and live happily with their families”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. nalla kōtpāttulagangaḷ mūnṟin uḷḷum tān niṟainda allik kamalak kaṇṇanai andaṇ kurugūrc catakōpan sollap patta āyirattuḷ ivaiyum pattum vallārgaḷ nalla padattāl manai vāḻvar koṇḍa peṇḍir makkaḷē Listen*

- *nalla kōtpāttu ulagangaḷ* – It appears that only after [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) mercifully spoke “*nedumāṟkadimai*” revealing that bhāgavata śēśatvam is the ultimate goal, the world became well orgainsed/established.
- *mūnṟin uḷḷum tān niṟainda* – It became fresh, even without the need for [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s all pervasive existence.
- *allik kamalak kaṇṇanai* – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s divine eyes too acquired more reddiśness and freshness as [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) increasingly became attached to his devotees.
- *am taṇ kurugūr* – Even the town became attractive and invigorating.
- *satakōpan sollap patta āyiram* – Unlike vēdam which has no author, being authored by [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/). vēdam is similar to [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s paratvam \[he is ever existing, without any cause\] and tiruvāimoḻi is similar to his avatārams \[where he gets a father and mother\].
- *ivaiyum pattum vallārgaḷ* – Those can practice this decad.
- *nalla …* – nalla padam (good position) means bhāgavata śēśatvam, since [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) established this principle in this decad; and further.
- *manai vāḻvar* – They will get to practice gruhasta darmam (being in married life, following vaidika principles).
- *koṇḍa …* – Instead of being in a situation where one thinks one way and one’s family thinks the opposite way, they will live along with their families for the purpose of serving bhāgavatas. \[A beautiful incident is narrated here to highlight how the whole family should be like minded in serving bhāgavatas\] A group of śrīvaiṣṇavas was travelling to tiruvanantapuram. On the way, they were in tirukkōśtiyūr, where they entered the tirumāḷigai (residence) of selvanambi \[the minister of pāṇḍiya king; [periyāḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/periyazhwar/) considered selvanambi as his mentor and had great reverence for him\]. At that time, selvanambi was away and his dharma patni (wife) took the paddy grains which were preserved safely for the subsequent year’s seeding, since there were no other grains there. She cooked a meal with those grains, offered that to [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) and fed the śrīvaiṣṇavas to their satisfaction. On the next day, nambi returned and was shocked to see the grains missing. He asked his wife “where are those grains?” and she said “I sowed them so that we can reap them in paramapadam” \[needless to say, selvanambi was overwhelmed with joy\]. There were some great personalities like toṇḍanūr nambi, eccān et al – the whole purpose of their life was to serve bhāgavatas; \[those who are well versed in this decad will acquire their qualities\].

## Ninth Centum

## 9.1 Konda pendir

## 9.1.1. Konda pendir

*koṇḍa peṇḍir makkaḷ uṟṟār suṟṟattavar piṟarum kaṇḍadōdu pattadallāl kādal maṟṟu yādum illai eṇḍhisaiyum kīḻum mēlum muṟṟavum uṇḍa pirān toṇḍarōmāy uyyal allāl illai kaṇḍīr tuṇaiyē ḷisten*

**Пословный перевод:**

koṇḍa – those who consider us as relative in their heart; peṇḍir – wife; makkaḷ – children et al; uṟṟār – close relatives, like in-laws; suṟṟattavar – other relatives; piṟarum – friends, servants et al; kaṇḍadōdu – when they see something to be received from us; pattadu allāl – they will agree with us, other than that; maṟṟu – in other situations; yādum – even a little bit; kādal illai – have no love for us; eṇ tisaiyum – with all directions; kīḻum – earth and nether worlds; mēlum – higher worlds; muṟṟavum – everything; uṇḍa – mercifully consumed and protected from deluge; pirān – for the great benefactor; toṇḍarōmāy – being servitors; uyyal allāl – other than being uplifted; illai tuṇai – no other refuge

**Перевод:**

**Those who consider us as relative in their heart such as wife, children et al, close relatives, like in-laws and other relatives, friends, servants et al will agree with us when they see something to be received from us and in other situations, they don’t have even a little bit of love for us. Hence, other than being the servitors of the great benefactor who mercifully consumed the earth with all its directions, the nether worlds, the higher worlds and everything and protected all of them from deluge, and being uplifted, there is no refuge for us.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the first pāsuram, āḻvār says “Since everyone’s relationship is incidental, one should pursue emperumān, the natural relative, and be uplifted”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. koṇḍa peṇḍir makkaḷ uṟṟār suṟṟattavar piṟarum kaṇḍadōdu pattadallāl kādal maṟṟu yādum illai eṇḍhisaiyum kīḻum mēlum muṟṟavum uṇḍa pirān toṇḍarōmāy uyyal allāl illai kaṇḍīr tuṇaiyē Listen*

- *koṇḍa peṇḍir …* – Wife et al who are considered by the individual in his heart as relatives.
- *koṇḍa peṇḍir* – Wife et al who were accepted due to wealth etc instead of accepting naturally. \[koṇḍa is explained as “having”\] Alternative explanation – wife who is considered as everything having offered all his wealth to her at the cost of making his parents suffer, and having her as refuge in his heart. Also explained as – having her as the ācārya, bhagavān, aiśvaryam (wealth) etc. Considering that her presence is the cause for everything. Another explanation – koṇḍa is applied to all entities \[wife, children et al\], implying wife et al who are considered by him as relatives.
- *makkaḷ* – The children who were begotten by destroying her youth.
- *uṟṟār* – The in-laws who were appreciated as equals for self.
- *suṟṟattavar* – The blood relatives who are respected by such in-laws.
- *piṟarum* – others; there is not much difference between these and the previously explained ones.
- *piṟarum* – Also explained as friends, servants et al.
- *kaṇḍadōdu pattadu allāl* – They will be friendly during physical presence; also explained as – will be friendly when they see our wealth.
- *kādal maṟṟu yādum illai* – They will be agreeable while they see some benefit for them; otherwise they will have no friendship towards us. Also explained as – when not present physically, they will not have true friendship. \[maṟṟu – otherwise\] The opposite of presence is absence.
- *kādal maṟṟu* – Saying  that there is no friendship and no enmity, which is the opposite for friendship or saying that there is no friendship and no relationship \[which causes such friendship\].
- *eṇ tisaiyum …* – One who protected all the cētanas who are present in all ten directions without missing any one of them; one who protects them even when they have nothing to offer. To protect them during deluge, they neither have the means to pursue nor the prayer to be protected; for his protection, the looming danger which he is aware of and his relationship are the requirements. They don’t have the ability to reject his protection \[so he protects\].
- *pirān* – One who is the benefactor.
- *toṇḍarōmāy uyyal allāl* – We need not offer anything to him from our side other than being his servitor and be uplifted. When śēśatvam (servitude) is svarūpam (true nature, for the self) losing that is vināśam (destruction).

In addition to the affirmation, āḻvār is showing the same meaning in negation as well.

- *illai kaṇḍīr tuṇaiyē* – āḻvār is not instructing to hold on to emperumān when there is someone else to protect during danger; one can sustain oneself by holding on to him or cease to exist.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 9.1.2. Tunaiyum sarvum

*tuṇaiyum sārvum āguvār pōl suṟṟattavar piṟarumaṇaiya vanda ākkam uṇḍēl attaigaḷ pōl suvaipparkaṇai onṟālē ēḻ maramum eyda em kārmugilaipuṇai enṟuyyap pōgal allāl illai kaṇḍīr poruḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tuṇaiyum – companions; sārvum – the refuge; āguvār pōl – pretending to be; suṟṟattavar – relatives; piṟarum – others; aṇaiya – their; vanda – getting; ākkam – benefit; uṇḍēl – if present; attaigaḷ pōl – like leeches; suvaippar – pretending to be doing favour for him, but will suck out completely; kaṇai onṟālē – with an arrow; ēḻ maramum – seven ebony trees; eyda – the benefactor who shot; em – one who makes us faithful too; kārmugilai – one who has the nature of a dark cloud; puṇai enṟu – considering as refuge; uyyap pōgal allāl – other than being uplifted; poruḷ – benefit; illai – not there

**Перевод:**

**The relatives and others, pretending to be companions and refuge, and pretending to be doing favour for the individual, will completely suck out like leeches if some benefit is present. Other than considering the benefactor who shot seven ebony trees with an arrow, who makes us remain faithful and who has the nature of a dark cloud, as refuge and being uplifted, there is no other benefit.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the second pāsuram, āḻvār says “Instead of the discardable ones who pretend to be benevolent but only look out for personal benefits, hold on to the son of daśarata who is only focussed on being benevolent towards others”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. tuṇaiyum sārvum āguvār pōl suṟṟattavar piṟarumaṇaiya vanda ākkam uṇḍēl attaigaḷ pōl suvaipparkaṇai onṟālē ēḻ maramum eyda em kārmugilaipuṇai enṟuyyap pōgal allāl illai kaṇḍīr poruḷē*

- *tuṇai …* – tuṇai means being a companion and sharing the joy and sorrow as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam kiśkintā kāṇḍam 5.18 “*ēkam du:kham sukham ca nau*“ (sharing sorrow and joy); sārvu means when there is no other refuge, themselves being the refuge. This is as how kriṣṇa remained the companion where he presented himself while the pāṇḍavas were living alone in the forest during their vanavāsam, and how he went to the workshop of the potter where pāṇḍavas were staying while taking draupadi away, stayed with them and cried along with them as said in mahābhāratam sambava parvam “*jagāma tām bhārgava karmaśālām*” (kriṣṇa went along with balārāma to the potter’s workshop). He remained as a refuge when he faced the arrows shot by bagadatta which were aimed at arjuna.
- *āguvār pōl* – Since they are not really related, instead of staying away, they will come close and remain in vicinity as if they are the protectors.
- *suṟṟattavar piṟarum* – Blood relatives and others.
- *aṇaiya …* – When there is wealth in their reach. Explained as – they pretend that there is some benefit for them in him. Also explained as – they pretend that there is some benefit for him in them.
- *attaigaḷ pōl suvaippar* – While sucking the blood, the leeches appear to be doing good to the individual on whom they are present; similarly, these people will remain as if he is benefitting from them while in reality they are benefitting from him. They will advice him “If you keep the wealth, someone will take them away from you. You give them to me and I will keep them safe for you” and survive.
- *kaṇai …* – With a random arrow as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam bāla kāṇḍam 1.66 “*ēkēna mahēśuṇā*” (With a single arrow, śrī rāma pierced the seven ebony trees and the lower worlds). When sugrīva māhārāja was alone in the forest, in a distressed state, with his own brother becoming an enemy, he saw perumāḷ (śrī rāma) and iḷaiya perumāḷ (lakśmaṇa) from a distance, and feared that they were sent by vāli, he sent tiruvadi (hanumān) and became introduced to them; at that time perumāḷ pacified him saying “We are capable of fulfilling your desire” and did the same.
- *ēḻ maramum eyda* – When sugrīva’s doubt would have been cleared by shooting down one or two trees, he shot all seven trees.
- *em kār mugilai* – *em* (we) could mean devotees; or it could be “royal we” (self), where [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is thinking that whatever favour done for sugrīva as done for self.
- *kār mugilai* – The great benefactor.

When asked “When this is his nature, what are we supposed to do for him?” [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says,

- *puṇai …* – There is nothing to offer to him. Just a word is sufficient. We only need to pray “my burden is your responsibility”.
- *illai kaṇḍīr poruḷē* – By holding on to others, there is no benefit. There are some who become worried, when we surrender unto them; but there is nothing which gives benefit.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 9.1.3. Porul kaiyunday

*poruḷ kai uṇḍāyc cellak kāṇil pōṟṟi enṟēṟṟeḻuvar iruḷ koḷ tunbattinmai kāṇil ennē! enbārum illai maruḷ koḷ seygai asurar manga vada maduraip piṟandāṟku aruḷ koḷ āḷāy uyyal allāl illai kaṇḍīr araṇē ḷisten*

**Пословный перевод:**

kai – in hand; poruḷ – wealth; uṇḍāy sella – present; kāṇil – when they see; pōṟṟi enṟu – performing mangaḷāśāsanam; ēṟṟu – accepting (whatever was given by him (the individual)); eḻuvar – leave (as they desire); iruḷ koḷ – abundance of ignorance and darkness; tunbattu – very sorrowful; inmai – poverty; kāṇil – when they see; ennē – alas!; enbārum – showing compassion saying; illai – not there; maruḷ koḷ – heart wrenching; seygai – having activities; asurar – demons; manga – to destroy them; vada madurai – in northern maturā; piṟandāṟku – for kriṣṇa who incarnated in; aruḷ koḷ – being the target of his mercy; āḷāy – being servitors; uyyal allāl – other than being uplfited; araṇ – other refuge; illai – not there

**Перевод:**

**When they (relatives) see the presence of wealth in his (individual’s) hand, they will perform mangaḷāśāsanam, accept what is given by him and leave; when they see very sorrowful poverty which has abundance of ignorance and darkness, they won’t be there to show compassion saying “alas!”; hence, other than being uplifted by being servitors and being the target of the mercy of kriṣṇa who incarnated in northern maturā to destroy the demons who were having heart-wrenching activities, there is no other refuge.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the third pāsuram, āḻvār says “All others but emperumān would pretend as relatives when there is a benefit for them and will abandon when there is danger; hence, worship kriṣṇa who is the natural āpatsaka (companion during danger) for all”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. poruḷ kai uṇḍāyc cellak kāṇil pōṟṟi enṟēṟṟeḻuvar iruḷ koḷ tunbattinmai kāṇil ennē! enbārum illai maruḷ koḷ seygai asurar manga vada maduraip piṟandāṟku aruḷ koḷ āḷāy uyyal allāl illai kaṇḍīr araṇē Listen*

- *poruḷ kai uṇḍāyc cellak kāṇil* – This individual will open the bag, close the bag and save certain things. When such wealth is actively being accessed by him and seen \[by others\]…
- *pōṟṟi enṟu* – They will speak as if they are fully focussed on the welfare of others. They will say “your wealth should increase further”. He will affectionately look at them thinking “there is someone who is fully caring towards us!”

Knowing that he will never become merciless towards them,

- *ēṟṟu eḻuvar* – They will rise saying “We are leaving. Should you not give us something?”
- *iruḷ …* – When looking at poverty which causes ignorance and sorrow,
- *ennē enbārum illai* – There is no one to even say “alas!” piḷḷai tirunaṟaiyūr araiyar would explain – An individual gives \[wealth\] to another person and in the end becomes poor; the one who received and became rich even would not come and enquire “how are you doing?” Not just that, if that person who became rich visits the one who initially gave him wealth and spends some time, at least others would think “Oh! This (poor) person is related to that (rich) person” and the poor person can survive with that reputation; but the second person would not even do that.
- *maruḷ …* – Now, it is explained that [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is akarmavaśya (not affected by any karma) incarnates and helps his devotees even when they did not have any wealth to offer, to eliminate their sufferings. For one who incarnated without anyone praying to do so, to destroy the demoniac clan which engages in activities which cause bewilderment in the hearts of cētanas (sentient beings).

what should we do for him?

- *aruḷ koḷ …* – Other than being the target of his mercy, and becoming uplifted, all one needs to do is to not reject [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s mercy; emperumān is of the nature that he will praise those who accept his mercy as in [śrī bhagavat gītā 7.18](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/7-18/) “*udārā*:” (magnanimous persons). There is nothing in the individual to accept; for emperumān, there is nothing more to be done, since emperumān is pūrṇa (complete in himself). The relationship \[between paramātmā and jīvātmā\] is natural; if the individual decides to pursue emperumān, emperumān considers it as his own gain; hence *vilakkāmai* (non-rejection) is the only requirement.
- *illai kaṇḍīr araṇē* – This is the only protection; everything else will end up as disaster only. Any other means which are considered as protection is similar to a child considering fire to be a bundle of gems. “*ādarēṇa yadāstauti danavanta danēccayā \| tadācēt viśvakartāram kōna mucyēdabandanāt \|\|*” (If one who gleefully praises a wealthy person with the desire to acquire wealth, praises the creator of the world with such great desire, why would he not be freed from bondage?) – since he is used to praising others, he would praise highly. But is he praising a magnanimous person? \[No\] danavantam – useless blade of grass; there is no real love in him. And who prayed to him? *danēccayā* (those who are interested in wealth). If the same desire is shown towards emperumān who is the owner of everything, who is much greater than the wealthy person explained previously, emperumān will not place this individual in a position to praise a mortal person for wealth.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 9.1.4. Aranamavar

*araṇām āvar aṟṟa kālaikku enṟenṟamaikkap pattār iraṇangoṇḍa teppar āvar inṟi ittālum ahdē varuṇit tennē? vada maduraip piṟandavan vaṇ pugaḻē saraṇ enṟuyyap pōgal allāl illai kaṇḍīr sadirē ḷisten*

**Пословный перевод:**

aṟṟa kālaikku – for the times when we have no means (help); araṇam āvar – being the refuge; enṟu enṟu – thinking like this repeatedly; amaikkap pattār – those who were captivated by offering wealth etc; iraṇam – debt; koṇḍa – like those who had; teppar āvar – will leave; inṟi ittālum – even if we don’t consider; ahdē – their non-helping nature is well established; varuṇittu – highlighting their ungrateful nature; ennē – what is the use?; vada madurai – in northern maturā; piṟandavan – the one who is born, his; vaṇ – causeless favour; pugaḻē – qualities such as śeela (simplicity), saulabhya (easy approacability) etc; saraṇ – refuge; enṟu – thinking as; uyya – being uplifted; pōgal allāl – instead of doing; sadir – activity; illai – not present

**Перевод:**

**Those who were repeatedly thought to be the refuge for the times when we have no means and those who were captivated by offering wealth etc will leave us like those who owe us something. Their non-helping nature is well established even if we don’t consider that; what is the use in highlighting their ungrateful nature? Instead of being uplifted by thinking about the qualities such as śeela (simplicity), saulabhya (easy approacability) etc which are causeless favours of the one who was born in norten maturā, no other activity is present.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fourth pāsuram, āḻvār says “Even after considering ‘these people will protect us during dangers’, giving them wealth etc and be surrendered to them for a long time, they would abandon us during dangerous times; hence you surrender unto emperumān, the āpatsaka (companion during dangerous times) would himself mercifully incarnate \[to protect us\] even when we have not surrendered unto him”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. araṇām āvar aṟṟa kālaikku enṟenṟamaikkap pattār iraṇangoṇḍa teppar āvar inṟi ittālum ahdē varuṇit tennē? vada maduraip piṟandavan vaṇ pugaḻē saraṇ enṟuyyap pōgal allāl illai kaṇḍīr sadirē Listen*

- *aṟṟa kālaikku araṇam āvar enṟu enṟu amaikkap pattār* – Considering deeply that there should be someone as protector for the times when we have no help, during good times, offering something, surrendering unto them and holding them as refuge. Those who were prepared as help in this manner.

When asked “How would those who were captivated by wealth etc, help us in dangerous times?” [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says,

- *iraṇam koṇḍa teppar āvar* – Not only would they be ungrateful to the one who did all of these, they would consider having received what is rightful for them, and would feel angry for the days when that person was unable to offer something – such lowly persons who accepted whatever was offered to them. teppar – tapra – capra.
- *inṟi ittālum ahdē* – Even if we don’t offer something and surrender unto them, when there is danger, we will find many who would abandon us. There is no use in surrendering unto those who would abandon us in dangerous times. Alternative explanation – in this manner, if the one who offered thought “here is a protector for us” and surrendered unto that person, and that if that person could die in the meantime, we will end up with the same result.
- *varuṇittu ennē* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying “What is the use of explaining this?” being disgusted with those who harm the ones who first helped them. \[perumāḷ’s (śrī rāma) reaction to iḷaiya perumāḷ (lakśamaṇa) getting angry on kaikēyi is explained here\] śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 71.10 “*ātma kāmā sadā caṇḍī krōdanā prājña māni nī*” (iḷaiya perumāḷ blamed kaikēyi along the lines of śrī bharatāḻvān blaming her to be self centered and cruel); perumāḷ said “Come on son! You are talking about our middle mother in this manner”; as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 16.37 “*na tēmbā madya mātāta karhitavyā katancana*” (Son, you cannot degrade your middle mother like this) – you should not speak like this about your mother. *tāmēva* (Only those) – You should only apply the well known remedy. “*ikśvāku nātasya bharatasya*” (ikśvāku clan’s king bharata’s) – father has died; bharata is the leader of this clan, who would properly maintain the kingdom which we have abandoned. “*bharatasya katām kuru”* (speak about bharata) – speak those words which will melt our tongue. Hence, what is the use of speaking about those who consider the favourable acts of an individual to be harmful?

[āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says “Even if you don’t offer anything, there is someone who comes forward and helps when there is a need; you surrender unto him and be protected!”

- *vada madurai …* – Instead of considering that the auspicious qualities such as sauśeelya, saulabhya etc of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who incarnated himself in śrī maturā for the protection of everyone when no one went and requested him to do so, and being uplifted.
- *illai kaṇḍīr sadirē* – \[Other acts/means\] Involving too much effort with very little benefit – inferior; where there is less effort and best benefit – that is best. Saying “*namō*” (śaraṇāgati) is the effort \[means\]; “*samankoḷ vīdu*” (attaining śrīvaikuṇṭam) is the benefit.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 9.1.5. Saduram enru

*saduram enṟu tammait tāmē sammadittu inmoḻiyār madura bōgam tuṟṟavarē vaigi maṟṟonṟuṟuvar adir koḷ seygai asurar manga vadamaduraip piṟandāṟku edir koḷ āḷāy uyyal allāl illai kaṇḍīr inbamē ḷisten*

**Пословный перевод:**

saduram – (to attract the beloved person) having sadir (ability); enṟu – as; tammai – self; tāmē – oneself; sammadittu – speaking to; in – pleasant; moḻiyār – women who have speech, their; maduram – sweet; bōgam – enjoyability; tuṟṟavarē – those who enjoyed; vaigi – in other times; maṟṟu onṟu – contrary results such as insult etc; uṟuvar – will get; adir koḷ – causing great torment; seyrai – having as nature; asurar – demons; manga – to be annihilated; vada madurai – in northern maturā; piṟandāṟku – to kriṣṇa, who incarnated; edir koḷ – persons who go towards; āḷāy – being servitors; uyyal allāl – other than being uplifted; inbam – ultimate joy; illai – not there

**Перевод:**

**Those peope who enjoyed the sweet enjoyability of women who have pleasant speech, who speak within themselves saying “we are capable”, will be insulted at other times; other than being uplifted by being servitors who go towards kriṣṇa, who incarnated in northern maturā to annihilate demons who were causing great torment, there is no other ultimate joy.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fifth pāsuram, āḻvār says “The friendly women who cannot survive without being with them, will insult them during dangerous times; hence, you surrender unto emperumān who is always friendly”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. saduram enṟu tammait tāmē sammadittu inmoḻiyār madura bōgam tuṟṟavarē vaigi maṟṟonṟuṟuvar adir koḷ seygai asurar manga vadamaduraip piṟandāṟku edir koḷ āḷāy uyyal allāl illai kaṇḍīr inbamē Listen*

- *saduram enṟu* – As living smartly. They would consider themselves to be capable as they are saying “We are capable, we are capable”.
- *tammait tāmē sammadittu* – Agreeing among themselves. Even one who has little bit of wealth will tell the women “I will make everyone in public think about me as capable; you can second that”; there is no one else ready to help for such acts; they have to do it themselves.
- *inmoḻiyār* – Of those who have pleasant speech. While inside their heart they may be like a sharp knife, they can attract others with loving speech.
- *madura bōgam tuṟṟavarē* – Intimately experienced sweet enjoyments with them.
- *vaigi maṟṟonṟu uṟuvar* – The youthful state which is apt for enjoyment and the wealth which is the principal for such enjoyment will go; still the desire will not change; while going to the same women, being a hurdle for their enjoyment with other \[youthful\] persons, and those women will tell him respectfully “can you go away for sometime?”; this person will say “I am going” but will remain there; then they will send their servant maid and insult him; he will still not go; subsequently, they will order him to leave; he will still not go; then they will pull his legs and try to pull him away from their residence; he will hold on to the pillar and remain there; in this manner he will be insulted by them; thinking about the insult which is attained and feeling disgusted about it, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says “*maṟṟu onṟu*” (another one), not willing to explicitly speak about those.

āḻvār says “Instead, hold on to the one who will lead to good result and be uplifted”.

- *adir …* – To the one who incarnated in northern maturā to destroy the demoniac clan which has activities causing torment to the hearts of cētanas (sentient beings).
- *edir koḷ āḷāy uyyal allāl* – Instead of being devotees who acknowledge him and be uplifted; this is what we need to do to him – when he pursues us, we should not turn our face away from him. mahābhāratam udyōga parvam 89.13 “*anyat pūrṇāt apām kumbāt*” – when drutarāśtra said a few words indicating “kriṣṇa who is partial towards pāṇḍavas is coming; let us give some land and gold to him and make him become favourable towards us”; he implied “by this, we can take him in our side”. But he lacks harmony since he thinks one thing but speaks something else; knowing this sanjaya \[his charioteer and friend\] said “the one who is coming is not of that nature; all he needs is a little bit; he is the one who gives coolness to water which he drinks; just placing such water in a pot in the route he comes, is sufficient”. When a guest comes to our home, sāmānya śāstram (basic rules) ordains that he should be offered water to wash his feet; there is nothing more needed matching his greatness. *anyat pādāvanē janāt* – Placing water in a pot is sufficient to wash his feet. Nothing more is needed. *anyat kuśala sampraśnāt* – For the one who has arrived travelling so far, it is apt to enquire as in tiruccanda viruttam 61 “*nadanda kālgaḷ nondavō*” (Are your feet hurting due to the long walk?) *nacēccati* – For one who has already eaten, it is not possible to eat more; in this manner, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) will become satisfied on seeing the individual’s efforts and become full; whatever done by the individual subsequently will be extraneous.
- *illai kaṇḍīr inbamē* – While there are some sorrows which appear like joy, there is nothing which is true joy. The joy derived by samsāris (materialistic persons) here is similar to the joy of a person facing death sentence becoming thirsty, drinking water and feeling satisfied. The joy for such samsāri is like resting under the hood of a swaying snake and being joyful thinking that it will give shade instead of knowing that it will swallow him.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 9.1.6. Illai kandir

*illai kaṇḍīr inbam andō! uḷḷadu ninaiyādē tollaiyārgaḷ ettanaivar tōnṟik kaḻindoḻindār mallai mūdūr vadamaduraip piṟandavan vaṇ pugaḻē solli uyyap pōgal allāl maṟṟonṟillai surukkē ḷisten*

**Пословный перевод:**

inbam – that which is in the form of joy; illai kaṇḍīr – not there; andō! – alas!; uḷḷadu – the true nature of bhagavān who is eternal and blissful; ninaiyādē – instead of thinking; tollaiyārgaḷ – those who were there in ancient times; ettanaivar – many persons; tōnṟik kaḻindu oḻindār – they were fully engaged in birth and death repeatedly; mallai – with abundance of perfect wealth; mudu – ancient (connected with emperumān since vāmanāvatāram); Ur – town; vadamadurai – in northern maturā; piṟandavan – one who incarnated; vaṇ – refreshing; pugaḻ – qualities; solli – praising; uyyap pōgal allāl – other than being uplifted; maṟṟu – any other; surukku – that which is to be stated briefly; onṟu illai – there is none

**Перевод:**

**There is no joy; alas! Many persons of ancient times were fully engaged in birth and death repeatedly without knowing the true nature of bhagavān who is eternal and blissful; other than being uplifted by praising the refreshing qualities of the one who incarnated in the abundantly wealthy, ancient town of northern maturā, there is nothing more which is to be stated in a brief manner.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the sixth pāsuram, āḻvār says “Many perished without knowing the principle of emperumān being the ultimate goal; without perishing like this, you surrender unto sarvēśvara who incarnated in śri maturā for his devotees; there is nothing better than this for the ātmā; I have stated this briefly here”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. illai kaṇḍīr inbam andō! uḷḷadu ninaiyādē tollaiyārgaḷ ettanaivar tōnṟik kaḻindoḻindār mallai mūdūr vadamaduraip piṟandavan vaṇ pugaḻē solli uyyap pōgal allāl maṟṟonṟillai surukkē Listen*

- *illai kaṇḍīr inbam* – In this samsāram which is said as in “*sarvam du:khamayam jagat*” (the whole world is filled with sorrow), there is not even a trace of joy.
- *andō!* – I have to explain this to you who are enjoyers \[experiencing the sorrow already\]! āḻvār is instructing this since their real time experience did not make them realise that.
- *uḷḷadu ninaiyādē* – Instead of thinking about the real goal. Instead of thinking “bhagavat viśayam is eternal and blissful”. It can also be read along with previous phrase and understood as “instead of thinking about the obvious non-existence of joy”.
- *tollai …* – For many persons from ancient times, as the birth led them to death, they perished without using the time in-between for the real goal. Just as some grass would perish where it sprouted from, these people too died without knowing anything.
- *mallai …* – Opulent, and being his eternal abode which was known as siddāśramam when śrī vāmana was mercifully present, which was held as the capital city by śrī śatrugnāḻvān, and where kriṣṇa incarnated; in this manner, maturā is constantly having bhagavat sambandam.
- *mūdu Ur* – Very ancient town; instead of praising the great glories of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who incarnated there and be uplifted.
- *maṟṟu onṟu illai surukkē* – Being present and explaining it elaborately, this cannot be stated briefly.
