## 9.1.7. Marronrillai

*maṟṟonṟillai surungac connōm mānilattevvyuirkkum siṟṟa vēṇḍā sindippē amaiyum kaṇḍīrgaḷ andō! kuṟṟamanṟengaḷ peṟṟattāyan vadamaduraip piṟandān kuṟṟam il sīr kaṟṟu vaigal vāḻdal kaṇḍīr guṇamē ḷisten*

**Пословный перевод:**

maṟṟu – other; onṟu illai – there is nothing to say; surunga – briefly; sonnōm – we told (you); mā – vast; nilattu – in earth; ev uyirkkum – for all ātmās; siṟṟa vēṇḍā – no need to sweat heavily; sindippē – mere thoughts; amaiyum – are sufficient; kaṇḍīrgaḷ – you have seen (isn’t it well known as said in “āyāsa: smaraṇē kō’sya“); andō – alas!; kuṟṟam – disaster; anṟu – not; engaḷ – obedient towards devotees; peṟṟam – for (ignorant) cows; tāyan – being protector; vada madurai – in northern maturā; piṟandān – one who incarnated, his; kuṟṟam il – without any expectation, exclusively for the result of protecting his devotees; sīr – qualities; kaṟṟu – understanding them (through instructions); vaigal – enjoying the qualities forever (as said in “sarvān kāmān sō’śnutē“); vāzdal kaṇḍīr – live!; guṇam – natural and apt

**Перевод:**

**Other than what we have briefly told, there is nothing more to say; all ātmās in this vast earth need not sweat it out heavily; mere thoughts are sufficient; you have seen already; alas! There is nothing disastrous; it is natural and apt for all of you to understand the qualities of the one who, without any expectation, is obedient towards devotees and protects them and who incarnated in northern maturā to be the protector of cows and to live enjoying the qualities forever!**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the seventh pāsuram, āḻvār mercifully states about the simplicity and sweetness of surrendering unto bhagavān.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says “By enjoying the qualities of kriṣṇa who is easily approachable just by thoughts, one can remain joyfully forever”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. maṟṟonṟillai surungac connōm mānilattevvyuirkkum siṟṟa vēṇḍā sindippē amaiyum kaṇḍīrgaḷ andō! kuṟṟamanṟengaḷ peṟṟattāyan vadamaduraip piṟandān kuṟṟam il sīr kaṟṟu vaigal vāḻdal kaṇḍīr guṇamē Listen*

- *maṟṟu onṟu illai* – There is nothing which can be thought along with this; altenative explanation – one need not think that we need to speak about this now and about something else later.
- *surungac connōm* – We stated this briefly without going into detail. Instead of explaining it in a manner which does not instil faith, we have explained it in a manner which you can grasp easily.
- *mānilattu* – Those who are qualified for this principle are in samsāra (material realm). Though the experts of this principle are present in paramapadam (spiritual realm), those who are qualified to receive the instructions are in samsāra.
- *ev uyirkkum* – This is not meant for an elite group; everyone is qualified to receive this.
- *siṟṟa vēṇḍā* – Need not sweat it out. siṟṟudal – wavering, saying no need to waver. Implies that no physical action is required.
- *sindippē amaiyum kaṇḍīrgaḷ* – Just the thought, without uttering a word, is sufficient.
- *andō* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying “alas!” thinking even good aspects \[such as singing [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s glories etc when done as means instead of service\] need to be given up.
- *kuṟṟam anṟu* – Even if it lacks any of the aforementioned good aspects, and even if this is said, nothing bad will occur. “*yōvasādassa ucyatām – prātar dēvēti kriṣṇēti*” (Will there be any shortcoming for those who recite dēva, kriṣṇa, gōvinda in morning, noon and evening respectively?) Even if there is no separate result for this upāyam (means), it will remain the benefit itself.
- *engaḷ peṟṟattu āyan vada maduraip piṟandān* – It appears that he was a covherd even before incarnating as kriṣṇa – implies that there is no shortcoming in his will to be be born as kriṣṇa. Implies kriṣṇa, who was born in maturā, who tended the cows. *peṟṟattu āyan* – covherd.
- *kuṟṟam il sīr kaṟṟu* – Meditating upon his auspicious qualities which are opposite to all defects; alternative explanation – he will be fully immersed in his birth and activities. śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 5.13.12 “*ahamvō bāndavō jāta:*” (I am your relative).
- *vaigal vāḻdal kaṇḍīr guṇamē* – Will learn once and joyfully live eternally; only this is apt; everything else is inapt.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 9.1.8. Valdal kandir

*vāḻdal kaṇḍīr guṇamidu andō māyavan adi paravi pōḻdu pōga uḷḷagiṟkum punmai ilādavarkku vāḻ tuṇaiyā vadamaduraip piṟandavan vaṇ pugaḻē vīḻ tuṇaiyāp pōm idanil yādum illai mikkadē ḷisten*

**Пословный перевод:**

vāḻdal – living; idu – isn’t this; guṇam – natural (for everyone)!; kaṇḍīr – īsn’t this world renowned!; andō – alas!; māyavan – sarvēśvara who has amazing qualities and activities; adi – divine feet; paravi – praising due to being pleased; pōḻdu pōga – to spend the time; uḷḷagiṟkum – being able to think; punmai – inferiority (relationship with other benefits); ilādavarkku – for those who don’t have; vāḻ – life matching the true nature; tuṇaiyā – to be upāyabhūta (means); vadamadurai – in northern maturā; piṟandavan – kriṣṇa who incarnated, his; vaṇ – enjoyable for his devotees; pugaḻē – qualities only; vīḻ – loving; tuṇaiyā – as companion for enjoyment; pōm – occurring; idanil – in this; mikkadu – greater; yādum – any other live; illai – not there

**Перевод:**

**īsn’t this natural living! īsn’t this world renowned! Alas! sarvēśvara who has amazing qualities and activities incarnated in northern maturā, for those who think about praising his divine feet due to being pleased and to spend the time without any inferiority, to be the means for their life matching their true nature; there is nothing greater than this life of having only his qualities which are enjoyable for his devotees, as the companion for enjoyment.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the eighth pāsuram, āḻvār explains the reason for emperumān‘s divine incarnation to shower his mercy and says “Other than holding on to him considering him as protector, there is no other benefit for anyone”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. vāḻdal kaṇḍīr guṇamidu andō māyavan adi paravi pōḻdu pōga uḷḷagiṟkum punmai ilādavarkku vāḻ tuṇaiyā vadamaduraip piṟandavan vaṇ pugaḻē vīḻ tuṇaiyāp pōm idanil yādum illai mikkadē Listen*

- *vāḻdal kaṇḍīr guṇam idu* – It is apt to live meditating upon his qualities.
- *andō* – Just as having to pay to make someone eat sugarcane, I have to pray this to them \[samsāris, the dwellers of this materialistic realm\]. While the glorious life is for you, it is I who has to beg to you to make use of it!
- *māyavan …* – Those great devotees who have the goodness of being won over by his amazing qualities such as saundarya (beauty), sauśeelya (simplicity) etc, due to being pleased, who praise his divine feet in an inorderly manner, and spend their time in this way. śrīvaiṣṇavas who seek no other benefits. Those who are as said in [nānmugan tiruvandādi 63](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/08/nanmugan-thiruvandhadhi-63/) “*teritteḻudi vāsittum kēttum vaṇangi vaḻipattum*” (meditating upon, writing, reading, hearing, bowing down and carrying out [*tiruvārādanam*](http://ponnadi.blogspot.in/2012/07/srivaishnava-thiruvaaraadhanam.html) [(elaborate worship)](http://ponnadi.blogspot.in/2012/07/srivaishnava-thiruvaaraadhanam.html)). parāśara bhattar would say “Those who don’t have the inferiority of praising this māyavan to be passing time as playing chess and gambling” \[that is, it is done as timepass instead of real enjoyment\].
- *vāḻ tuṇai …* – Even for those who feel inferior, he will eliminate that inferiority and make it an enjoyment for them; if this is the case, for those who have no such defect, there is no benefit other than [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s union with his devotees. emperumān who incarnated in northern maturā to let them enjoy his qualities and to be their companion, his. The purpose of his incarnation is as explained in [śrī bhagavat gītā 4-8](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/4-8/) “*paritrāṇāya sādūnām*” (to protect the good people).
- *vaṇ pugaḻ …* – Other than desirously holding on to his auspicious qualities as the companion.
- *vīḻ tuṇai* – The companion who is desired. vīḻ – to fall. Those who are desirous are explained as “fallen” as said in kuṟaḷ 1191 “*tām vīḻvār tam vīḻap peṟṟavar*” (those who love someone and in turn was loved by that person).
- *idanil* – Greater than this.
- *yādum illai mikkadē* – Only if there is something greater than this, it needs to be identified; tṭhere is nothing greater than this.

## 9.1.9. Yadum illai

*yādum illai mikkadanil enṟenṟadu karudikādu seyvān kūdai seydu kadai muṟai vāḻkkaiyum pōmmādugilin kodik koḷ māda vadamaduraip piṟandatādu sēr tōḷ kaṇṇan allāl illai kaṇḍīr saraṇē*

**Пословный перевод:**

adanil – more than that; mikku – greater benefit; yādum – any thing; illai – not there; enṟu enṟu – repeatedly; adu – the other benefits in the form of aiśvaryam (worldly wealth) and kaivalyam (self enjoyment); karudi – considered; kādu seyvān – trying to pierce the ear; kūdai seydu – (even the base getting affected) becoming damaged; kadai muṟai vāḻkkaiyum – the lowly benefits which are already present; pōm – will perish; mā – huge; tugilin – made of cloth; kodi – flags; koḷ – having; mādam – having mansions; vada madurai – in northern maturā; piṟanda – one who incarnated; tādu sēr – decorated with garlands of tuḷasi, vaijayanti etc; tōḷ – having shoulders; kaṇṇan – kriṣṇa; allāl – other than; saraṇ – refuge for the goal; illai – not there; kaṇḍīr – this can be seen by those who understand it

**Перевод:**

**There is no other benefit greater than that \[kainkaryam\]; those who are repeatedly considering the other benefits in the form of aiśvaryam (worldly wealth) and kaivalyam (self enjoyment) will perish just as one who tries to pierce his ear will end up damaging the ear itself; hence, there is no refuge for the goal other than kriṣṇa who incarnated in northern maturā having mansions with flags made of huge clothes and is having  shoulders decorated with garlands of tuḷasi, vaijayanti etc; this can be seen by those who understand it.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the ninth pāsuram, āḻvār says “Those who considered something other than emperumān as rakśaka (protector) and surrendered unto that entity, will become a disaster losing their previous position too; hence, there is no refuge other than him”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. yādum illai mikkadanil enṟenṟadu karudikādu seyvān kūdai seydu kadai muṟai vāḻkkaiyum pōmmādugilin kodik koḷ māda vadamaduraip piṟandatādu sēr tōḷ kaṇṇan allāl illai kaṇḍīr saraṇē*

- *yādum …* – Holding on to something other than bhagavān, saying “there is no refuge other than this” and considering it as the refuge. Having the faith which is explained in “*samartō druśya tē kaścit*” (only [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is capable of removing dangers and granting wealth), in worldly aspects.
- *kādu seyvān kūdai seydu* – Just as someone tries to pierce the ear, but ends up mutilating the whole ear.
- *kadai muṟai vāḻakkaiyum pōm* – There is a lowly life – this is the life with children, with lots of ups and downs in this samsāram; even that will be spoilt. During dangerous times, other dēvatatās will not be of any help; having placed the burden on those dēvatās, the individual will lose everything, even those aspects which could have been fulfilled by self.
- *mā tugil …* – While kamsa is living \[a rich life\], [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is considering the flags which are hoisted by kamsa as those which are hoisted to celebrate kriṣṇa’s birth. While śiśupāla performed all rituals meant for pāṇigrahaṇam (marriage with rukmiṇi pirātti), kriṣṇa considered those rituals to be for his own sake and married \[rukmiṇi pirātti\].
- *tādu …* – One whose divine shoulders are decorated with garlands such as vaijayanti etc. No other benefit is required \[this divine sight itself is sufficient\].
- *allāl illai kaṇḍīr saraṇē* – There is no other entity who can be our refuge.

When explained in context of *kaivalya* (self enjoyment),

- *yādum …* – Thinking “there is nothing greater than this self enjoyment”, though there is the joy of enjoying bhagavān, the individual focusses on self enjoyment; just as a person who tries to pierce the ear, trying many times and ends up even losing the ear, the individual who is in samsāram where there is scope for surrendering unto bhagavān, ends up even losing the option to enjoy in worldly pleasures \[by attaining kaivalyam\]; hence, kriṣṇa, who is greater than everyone, is the ultimate goal.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 9.1.10. Kannan allal

*kaṇṇan allāl illai kaṇḍīr saraṇ adu niṟka vandu maṇṇin bāram nīkkudaṟkē vadamaduraip piṟandān tiṇṇamā num udaimai uṇḍēl avan adi sērttuymminō eṇṇa vēṇḍā nummadādum avan anṟi maṟṟillaiyē ḷisten*

**Пословный перевод:**

kaṇṇan – kriṣṇa; allāl – other than; saraṇ – other prāpya (goal) and prāpaka (means); illai kaṇḍīr – not there; adu – that nature of his being prāpya and prāpaka; niṟka – to be established in the world; maṇṇin bāram – the burden of demoniac people who are the enemies; nīkkudaṟku – to eliminate; vandu – leaving the nāga paryanka (ādiśēśa mattress); vadamadurai – in northern maturā; piṟandān – incarnated; num – whatever you are claiming as yours; udaimai – object; uṇḍēl – if it is there; avan adi – at his divine feet; tiṇṇamā – firmly; sērttu uymminō – offer them; eṇṇa vēṇḍā – need not analyse; nummadu – your; ādum – all aspects in the form of prāpya and prāpaka; avan anṟi – other than bhagavān who is all kinds of relative as said in “mātā pitā bhrātā nivāsaś śaraṇam suhrud gatir nārāyaṇa:”; maṟṟu – any thing which is owned by self; illai – not there

**Перевод:**

**There is no prāpya and prāpaka other than kriṣṇa; leaving the nāga paryanka, he incarnated in northern maturā to have that nature of his being prāpya and prāpaka established and to eliminate the burden of demoniac people who are the enemies; offer whatever object you are claiming as yours, if present, firmly at his divine feet; you need not analyse this; there is nothing which is owned by self in all aspects in the form of prāpya and prāpaka, other than bhagavān who is all kinds of relative as said in “mātā pitā bhrātā nivāsaś śaraṇam suhrud gatir nārāyaṇa:”**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the tenth pāsuram, āḻvār says “Surrender unto the divine feet of kriṣṇa who mercifully incarnated to establish the principle of his being the refuge for all”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. kaṇṇan allāl illai kaṇḍīr saraṇ adu niṟka vandu maṇṇin bāram nīkkudaṟkē vadamaduraip piṟandān tiṇṇamā num udaimai uṇḍēl avan adi sērttuymminō eṇṇa vēṇḍā nummadādum avan anṟi maṟṟillaiyē Listen*

- *kaṇṇan …* – To establish the principle that there is none other kriṣṇa who is refuge, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) divinely incarnated to eliminate the burden of the earth; hence, you too, offer whatever you consider as yours, quickly at his divine feet as his property! [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is not saying “*undēl*” (if present) based on his own opinion, but based on the misplaced knowledge of the individuals who consider themselves to be the owner.
- *eṇṇa vēṇḍā* – No need to analyse “if this is his or ours”; you and your belongings are all owned by him only.
- *maṟṟu illaiyē* – There is nothing else. Alternatively – whatever efforts you put in for which you are responsible, are not at your disposal; everything is at his disposal.
- *maṟṟu illai* – The means for the goal cannot be without him. You need not put your share in the effort as said in “*samitai pādi sāvitri pādi*” \[While doing gāyatri japam during āvaṇi avittam (yajur upākarmā) for certain count like 1008, some brahmacāris would recite the mantra 500 times and count 500 offerings of samit (wooden stick offered in fire sacrifice)\]

## 9.1.11. Adumillai

*ādum illai maṟṟavanil enṟaduvē tuṇindu tādu sēr tōḷ kaṇṇanaik kurugūrc catakōpan sonna tīdilāda oṇ tamiḻgaḷ ivai āyirattuḷ ippattum ōda valla pirākkaḷ nammai āḷ udaiyārgaḷ paṇḍē ḷisten*

**Пословный перевод:**

avanil – other than him; maṟṟu – any other; ādum – an entity who is prāpya (goal) or prāpaka (means); illai – not there; enṟaduvē – only this; tuṇindu – faithfully; tādusēr – decorated with garland; tōḷ – having divine shoulders and being perfectly enjoyable due to that; kaṇṇanai – kriṣṇa who is obedient towards his devotees; kurugūrc catakōpan – āḻvār; sonna – mercifully spoken; tīdu – defect in poem or its meanings; ilāda – not having; oṇ – having many good qualities; tamiḻgaḷ – in drāmida (tamiḻ); ivai āyirattuḷ – among the thousand pāsurams; ip pattum – this decad; ōda valla – able to recite; pirākkaḷ – benefactors; paṇḍē – starting with the time of accepting body to recite these pāsurams; nammai – for us; āḷ udaiyārgaḷ – lords

**Перевод:**

**With faith in “There is no other entity who is prāpya (goal) or prāpaka (means) other than emperumān“, āḻvār mercifully spoke this decad among the tosand tamiḻ pāsurams which are not having any defect in poem or its meanings and are having many good qualities, on kriṣṇa whose divine shoulders are decorated with garland and are perfectly enjoyable due to that and who is obedient towards his devotees; those benefactors who are able to recite this decad are the lords for us starting with the time of accepting body to recite these pāsurams.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the end, āḻvār says “those who practice this decad are dear to me” as emperumān said in śrī bhagavat gītā 18.70 starting with “adyēśyatē ca ya imam” (One who recites the śāstram which was a conversation about the means for liberation between the two of us, has vorśipped me with the jñāna yajña; this is my opinion).*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. ādum illai maṟṟavanil enṟaduvē tuṇindu tādu sēr tōḷ kaṇṇanaik kurugūrc catakōpan sonna tīdilāda oṇ tamiḻgaḷ ivai āyirattuḷ ippattum ōda valla pirākkaḷ nammai āḷ udaiyārgaḷ paṇḍē Listen*

- *ādum illai maṟṟu avanil enṟu aduvē tuṇindu* – Being faithful that there is no prāpyam and prāpakam other than [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/).

When asked “Who gave such faith to [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)?”, āḻvār says “Could that be anything other than his divine shoulders and the garland which decorates them?”

- *tādu sēr …* – It is his beauty which made āḻvār become firmly faithful.
- *tīdu ilāda …* – Being without any discussion other than the actual subject matter.
- *oṇ tamiḻgaḷ* – The poems which fully reveal the underlying meanings. Also expalined as being without any fault and with many good qualities.
- *ōda valla pirākkaḷ* – Those benefactors who can recite/practice this decad. The inferior nature of this samsāram and īśvara being prāpya and prāpaka are explained in this decad; by meditating upon these, one will give up bad path and start pursuing the good path. They cannot do any greater favour than this for [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/).
- *nammai āḷ udaiyārgaḷ paṇḍē* – Even if they become qualified to recite this in a particular birth, they will be our lord from previous times. \[Alternative explanation\] As said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 18.70](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/18-70/) “*adyēśyatē*” (recites), from the time one becomes qualified to recite this decad, he will be my lord.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 9.2 Pandai nalale

## 9.2.1. Pandai nalale

*paṇḍai nāḷālē nin tiruvaruḷum pangayattāḷ tiruvaruḷum koṇḍu nin kōyil sīyttup pal padigāl kudi kudi vaḻi vandātceyyum toṇḍararōrkkaruḷic cōdivāyt tiṟandun tāmaraik kaṇgaḷāl nōkkāy teṇḍiraip porunal taṇpaṇai sūḻnda tiruppuḷingudik kidandānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

teṇ – clear; tirai – having tides; porunal – having tirupporunal (tāmirabharaṇi river); taṇ – cool; paṇai – vaterbodies; sūḻnda – surrounded; tiruppuḷingudi – in tiruppuḷingudi; kidandānē – oh one who is mercifully resting!; nin – (natural relative) your; tiruvaruḷum – divine mercy; pangayattāḷ – śrī mahālakśmi who is in lotus flower (who makes you shower your mercy); tiruvaruḷum – divine mercy; paṇḍai nāḷālē – from the time of creation; koṇḍu – having (as ours); nin – where you are joyfully present; kōyil – in divyadēśam; sīyttu – doing apt services; pal padigāl – since long ago; kudi kudi vaḻi – coming as per family traditions (without deviating from the path of śāstram forever along with son, grandson et al); vandu āḷ seyyum – those who come and serve; toṇḍarōrkku – for us, servitors; aruḷi – showing his mercy fully; sōdi – radiant; vāy – divine lips; tiṟandu – open; un – your distinguished; tāmarai – lotus like; kaṇgaḷāl – with divine eyes; nōkkāy – should mercifully glance at us fully

**Перевод:**

**Oh one who is mercifully resting in tiruppuḷingudi which is having tirupporunal with clear tides and is surrounded by cool vaterbodies! In this divyadēśam, where you are joyfully present, we are having the divine mercy of both yours and śrī mahālakśmi’s, who is in lotus flower, from the time of creation, and are doing apt services since long ago as per family traditions; you should show your mercfy fully to us, open your radiant, divine lips \[to speak a few words\] and should mercifully glance at us fully with your distinguished, lotus like, divine eyes.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the first pāsuram, āḻvār tells emperumān to mercifully say a few words to people like him who have nowhere else to go and to mercifully look at them with his divine eyes to get rid of their longing.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. paṇḍai nāḷālē nin tiruvaruḷum pangayattāḷ tiruvaruḷum koṇḍu nin kōyil sīyttup pal padigāl kudi kudi vaḻi vandātceyyum toṇḍararōrkkaruḷic cōdivāyt tiṟandun tāmaraik kaṇgaḷāl nōkkāy teṇḍiraip porunal taṇpaṇai sūḻnda tiruppuḷingudik kidandānē*

- *paṇḍai nāḷālē nin tiruvaruḷum* – The merciful glance that you have been showering for a long time. Is this \[our state\] the result of your recent efforts? Is this not the result of your hardvork for many days as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 2.7.6](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/05/thiruvaimozhi-2-7-6-madhusudhanai-anri/) “*edir sūḻal pukku*” (comes across from the opposite side and catches)? Did you try for so long to give up when it is bearing fruit?
- *pangayattāḷ tiruvaruḷum* – With the merciful glance of periya pirāttiyār which is the cause for your mercy. The mercy which will eliminate the independence in his mercy. It is the pāratantriyam (dependence) out of love which will eliminate the independence in his mercy. Acquiring your mercy as said in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 4.9.2 “*ennadiyār adu seyyār*” (My devotees would not do anything wrong) and her mercy as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 116-44 “*na kaścinnāparādyati*” (There is none who has not committed a sin). Also explained as, the mercy of yours who are subservient to your own mercy as said in śrī rāmāyaṇa ślōkam sundara kāṇḍam 38.34 “*krupayā paryapālayat*” (protected out of his mercy), and her mercy which is the cause of your dependence.
- *pangayattāḷ tiruvaruḷum* – Her mercy is the one which eliminates the binding of your mercy with your independence. Her mercy will ensure that he does not follow his independence. One need not fear thinking “Is his dependence on her not based on his love? Would it remain always? Is he not naturally independent?” When she is present next to him, his independence will not remain. This is why, in the first part \[of dvaya mahā mantram\] we pursue him with her puruśakāram (recommendation/support).
- *nin kōyil sīyttu* – Doing distinguished services in divyadēśams where he mercifully resides with great joy. Those who acquired bhagavān’s mercy through their own pious deeds will care for their family; those who acquired bhagavān’s mercy through pirātti’s puruśakāram, will care for divyadēśams. śrīviṣṇu darmam “*nakincit api kurvāṇa: viṣṇō: āyatanē vasēt*” (One should remain in viṣṇu’s temples without engaging in any \[other\] activity) – even for those who should not cut a piece of grass, should remain attached to a divyadēśam. One who realises that the service which he desires to get after shedding the body can be done with this body itself, will never leave it. tiruvāimoḻi 10.2.7 “*vayal aṇi anantapuram kadaittalai sīykkap peṟṟāl kadu vinai kaḷaiyalāmē*” (when one gets to clean the floors of tiruvanantapuram temple surrounded by fertile fields, one’s hurdles will be removed) – as one attains the goal, the hurdles will naturally be removed. When [tirukkaṇṇamangai āṇḍān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/thirukkannamangai-andan/) swept the floor under a tirumagiḻam tree which had leaves, an atheist who studied with him asked him “\[your view is\] bhagavān is the means; we have no other expectation; now, what is the benefit of your effort?” āṇḍān showed the side of the floor which had leaves and other side which did not have leaves and said “after seeing the two places, do you still think that there is no benefit?” \[Implies that the cleaning of the floor is a service and hence it must be done\].
- *palpadigāl* – Did it start happening today? Did it not start on the day you started showering your mercy \[long ago\]?
- *kudi kudi* – with family members.
- *vaḻi vandu* – As per the ways explained in śāstram properly.
- *āḷ seyyum toṇḍarōrkku aruḷi* – Showering your mercy upon us who are serving.
- *sōdi vāy tiṟandu* – The freshness which appears on your face when your open your mouth and speak, resembles a blossoming flower. akrūra only enjoyed [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s speech as said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 5.17.12 “*māmakrūrēti vakśyati*” (kriṣṇa will call me “*Oh akrūra!*“). The freshness in the divine face at that time is also desirable for [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/).
- *un tāmaraik kaṇgaḷāl nōkkāy* – You should shower your cool merciful glance so that I can understand our bondage which was not understood by your words; as said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 1.20.16 “*avalōkana dānēna bhūyōmām pālaya*” (Oh lord! protect me with your glance). If you get hiccups while trying to speak, you should manifest the feelings through your divine eyes. When piḷḷai dēvap perumāḷ araiyar repeated multiple times saying “*un tāmaraik kaṇgaḷāl nōkkāy*, *nōkkāy*“, [āḻvār tiruvarangap perumāḷ araiyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/thiruvarangapperumal-araiyar) stood up and mercifully told him “Son! Why are you forcing emperumān like this hurting emperumān’s divine heart? He has given you sweet voice, good pāsurams, children, wealth and so on; why are you feeling sorrowful as if he has not given something to you?”
- *teṇ tirai …* – You got to mercifully rest in tiruppuḷingudi which has abundance of water, matching the tender nature of your divine form. What you have done – you are mercifully resting in tiruppuḷingudi which is close to tirupporunal which has clear tides and is surrounded by vaterbodies.
- *un tāmaraik kaṇgaḷāl nōkkāy* – It is apt for a qualified devotee to be grateful for what is already done by [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) and to pray for what is to be done by emperumān.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 9.2.2. Kudik kidandu

*kudikkidandākkam seydu nin tīrtta adimaik kuṟṟēval seydu un ponnadikkadavādē vaḻi varuginṟa adiyarōrkkaruḷi nī oru nāḷ padikkaḷavāga nimirtta nin pāda pangayamē talaikkaṇiyāy kodikkoḷ pon madiḷ sūḻ kuḷir vayaṟcōlait tiruppuḷingudik kidandānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kodik koḷ – decorated with flags; pon – golden; madiḷ – by fort; sūḻ – surrounded; kuḷir – cool; vayal – fields; sōlai – having garden; tiruppuḷingudi – in tiruppuḷingudi; kidandānē – oh one who is mercifully resting (to be enjoyed by your devotees)!; kudik kidandu – remaining without ignoring the norms of the clan of servitude; ākkam seydu – being engaged in services which will enhance such servitude; tīrtta – eliminating other attachments; nin – towards you; adimai – services; kuṟu ēval – confidential services; seydu – performed; un – your; pon – attractive; adikkadavādē – other than the divine feet; vaḻi – the path of pāratantriyam (total dependence); varuginṟa – following without fail; adiyarōrkku – for us, servitors; aruḷi – showering your mercy; nī – you (who are a natural relative); oru nāḷ – on the day (when mahābali claimed ownership of earth); padikku – for that; aḷavāga – matching; nimirtta – lifted, measured and accepted; nin – your; pāda pangayam – perfectly enjoyable divine lotus feet; talaikku – for my head; aṇiyāy – you should mercifully decorate

**Перевод:**

**Oh one who is mercifully resting in tiruppuḷingudi which is having cool fields and garden and is surrounded by golden fort decorated with flags! You should shower your mercy upon us who are remaining without ignoring the norms of the clan of servitude and being engaged in services which will enhance such servitude, eliminating other attachments and performing confidential services unto your attractive divine feet without expecting self enjoyment, and following the path of pāratantriyam without fail; you should mercifully decorate my head with your perfectly enjoyable divine lotus feet which you lifted and measured and accepted the earth matching its size on the day when it was claimed by mahābali.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the second pāsuram, āḻvār says “You should mercifully place your divine feet which are easily approachable for all, on my head”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. kudikkidandākkam seydu nin tīrtta adimaik kuṟṟēval seydu un ponnadikkadavādē vaḻi varuginṟa adiyarōrkkaruḷi nī oru nāḷ padikkaḷavāga nimirtta nin pāda pangayamē talaikkaṇiyāy kodikkoḷ pon madiḷ sūḻ kuḷir vayaṟcōlait tiruppuḷingudik kidandānē*

- *kudik kidandu* – Acting according the traditions of the family. Acting without giving up the family traditions. śrī bharatāḻvān said “in ikśvāku vamśam, when the elder brother is present, younger brothers will not take up the throne”.
- *ākkam seydu* – Bringing new glories which were not present previously in the clan; this can be seen from,
   - śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 127.5 “*panka dikdastu jatilō bharatastvām pratīkśatē \| pādukē tē puraskrutya sarvanca kuśalam gurhē \|\|*” (śrī bharatāḻvān is eagerly waiting for your arrival with matted hair and dirty clothes; he is ruling over the kingdom with your sandals at the forefront; everyone is fine there)
   - śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 100.1 “*jatilam cīravasanam*” (wearing matted hair and tree-bark clothes)
   - śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 70.4 “*nahi tē rājaputrantam kāśāyāmbaradāriṇam \| paribhōktum vyavasyanti paurāvai darmavatsalam \|\|*” (The residents of the town did not like to see śrī bharatāḻvān who is very righteous and the son of daśarata cakravarti, with saffron clothes) – Though he was in their close proximity, they did not like to see and enjoy him. The reason for that is – *rājaputram –* They thought “was he not the son of daśarata who died after perumāḷ (śrī rāma) left śrī ayōdyā? At least, he will remain here for us”. *dharma vatsalam* – For his desire towards righteousness, he will match his father; he tormented himself to protect dharma.
   - śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 101.12 “*ēpiśca sacivaissārdam*” – while it was sufficient for him to go alone, he took along many who were in sorrow; the reason for that is – “instead of just seeing my tears, would he not return if he sees the tears of many?” He even took along elephants, horses etc like going to wage a war. In his entourage, everyone was at par with him in sorrow of separation from śrī rāma. *śirasā yācitō mayā* – Would he refuse when I pray by bowing my head at him? Even perumāḷ said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 24.19 “*śirasā yācatastasya vacanam na krutam mayā*” (I did not fulfil the request of śrī bharatāḻvān who bowed his head and prayed to me) – “He did what was apt for him and I did what was apt for me”. perumāḷ’s divine heart became hurt since he refused śrī bharatāḻvān’s prayer even after he bowed his head and prayed. *bhrātu:* – as said in manu dharma śāstram “*bhrātā svā mūrtirātmana:*” (A brother is like one’s body), is he (perumāḷ) not thinking me (śrī bharatāḻvān) as his divine body? Remaining ślōkam should be understood as explained previously. In this manner, bringing a lot of new glories to the clan. Previously the clan members remained “when the elder brother is present, younger ones cannot accept the throne”; but there was none who remained with great sorrow, teary eyes, grew matted hair and wore tree-bark clothes other than śrī bharatāḻvān.
- *nin tīrtta adimaik kuṟṟēval seydu* – Engaging in confidential services to emperumān who can eliminate the taste in other aspects with the help of his own enjoyability.
- *un ponnadik kadavādē* – śrī bharatāḻvān was not just forcing upon perumāḷ out of his own desire but also went to bring back perumāḷ, with the puruśārtam (recommendation) of śrī vasiśta bhagavān et al; after hearing perumāḷ saying “We will be satisfied only after completing the task ordered by our father, so you remain in the kingdom and rule it for fourteen years”, he returned joyfully as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 112.25 “*ārurōha ratam hruśta:*” (bharata climbed the chariot happily along with śatrugna); in the same manner, without violating your order. Without ignoring your divine feet. Alternative meaning – being without knowing anything other than your attractive divine feet. That is, being ananya prayōjana (without any other expectation).
- *vaḻi varuginṟa adiyarōrkku aruḷi* – Showering your mercy upon us who are helpless and are properly engaged in your service.
- *nī oru nāḷ …* – Will that nature of yours be present one day and dry up after that? Is having ruci (taste) in that, extraneous over apratiśēdam (non-rejection) \[Should I also be like those who did not reject you when you placed your divine feet on them\]? Can you not place your divine feet which were placed on everyone’s head without checking their qualities or defects, on my head?
- *padikku aḷavāga* – Is having them \[divine feet\] grow to consume the earth difficult for you? ōr is stopping the stretching of your divine feet beyond the size of the earth more difficult for you to do than stretching it? Do I have to worry about these being difficult for you to do? Don’t you just have to place them on my head?
- *nin pāda pangayamē* – He measured the world which is filled with rough terrains with these fresh flowers \[divine feet\].
- *talaikku aṇiyāy* – All of your efforts to measure the world were with a hidden purpose \[of placing your divine feet on my head\]; so, can you not place the divine feet which were stopped at the size of the earth, at the size of my head?
- *talaikku aṇiyāy* – Should you not place the divine feet on those who say as in [tiruvāimoḻi 4.3.6](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/01/thiruvaimozhi-4-3-6-kala-chakkaraththodu/) “*kōlamām en sennikku …*” (your infinitely enjoyable lotus flower like divine feet which make sounds of bravery are the shining radiant decoration for my head). āḻvār is saying as in [stōtra ratnam 31](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/01/sthothra-rathnam-31/) “*kadā*” (when).
- *kodi …* – śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 36.47 “*sārāma sankīrtana vītaśōkā rāmasya śōkēna samāna śōkā*” (That sītāp pirātti who has the same grief as śrī rāma, on hearing the glorification about śrī rāma, remained like moon in the night covered by the autumn clouds) – There was grief due to doubt on perumāḷ’s existence. There was another grief due to separation from perumāḷ. The first grief was eliminated after seeing tiruvadi (hanuman) \[but the other grief remained\]; similarly, emperumān’s merciful resting in tiruppuḷingudi which is well protected, was to eliminate the fear of āḻvār who thinks “what will happen to emperumān”; now, the only remaining issue is your pursuit of mine; you should mercifully rectify this issue as well.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 9.2.3. Kidanda nal

*kidanda nāḷ kidandāy ehtanai kālam kidatti un tiruvudambasaiyat todarndu kuṟṟēval seydu tolladimai vaḻi varum toṇḍarōrkkaruḷit tadangodāmaraik kaṇ viḻittu nī eḻundun tāmarai mangaiyum nīyum idangoḷ mūvulagundoḻa irundaruḷāy tiruppuḷingudik kidandānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tiruppuḷingudi – In tiruppuḷingudi; kidandānē – oh one who is mercifully resting for the sake of your devotees!; kidanda nāḷ – starting from the day you reclined to rest; kidandāy – you have remained in the same posture; un tiruvudambu – your divine form; asaiya – to strain; ettanai kālam – for how long more; kidatti – will you remain in this resting posture?; todarndu – following (you who are presenting yourself as per our desire); kuṟṟēval – confidential service; seydu – doing; tol – since time immemorial; adimai vaḻi – in the path of servitude; varum – coming; toṇḍarōrkku – for us who are exclusively subservient to you; aruḷi – showing compassion; tadam – pond; koḷ – huge to be seen as consuming; tāmarai – like lotus; kaṇ – divine eyes; viḻittu – opening widely; eḻundu – get up (from your mattress); un – your inseparable; tāmarai – having enjoyability due to being born in flower; mangaiyaiyum – śrī mahālakśmi who is youthful; nīyum – you too; idam koḷ mū ulagum – the vast three-layered world; toḻa – to see and enjoy (like those who are exclusively subservient to you); irundu aruḷāy – you should be mercifully seated

**Перевод:**

**Oh one who is mercifully resting in tiruppuḷingudi for the sake of your devotees! You have remained in the same posture starting from the day you reclined to rest; for how long more will you remain in this same resting posture to strain your divine form? You should show your compassion towards us who are following you, doing confidential services and coming in the path of servitude since time immemorial by widely opening your divine eyes which appear like a huge lotus consuming the pond \[in which it is present\], by getting up and by being mercifully seated here with your inseparable divine consort śrī mahālakśmi who is having enjoyability due to being born in flower and is youthful, to be seen and enjoyed by the vast three-layered world.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the third pāsuram, āḻvār says “Instead of resting in the same posture straining yourself, open your divine eyes for your servitors like us, get up and be present along with your divine consort who is seated on lotus flower, to enliven the whole world”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. kidanda nāḷ kidandāy ehtanai kālam kidatti un tiruvudambasaiyat todarndu kuṟṟēval seydu tolladimai vaḻi varum toṇḍarōrkkaruḷit tadangodāmaraik kaṇ viḻittu nī eḻundun tāmarai mangaiyum nīyum idangoḷ mūvulagundoḻa irundaruḷāy tiruppuḷingudik kidandānē*

- *kidanda nāḷ kidandāy* – You are mercifully resting since the day when one person \[toṇḍaradippodi āḻvār\] desired to see your resting posture as said in [tirumālai 23](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/10/thirumalai-23/) “*kidandadōr kidakkai*” (the beautiful resting posture).
- *ettanai kālam kidatti* – \[It seems\] You will remain in this posture without getting up, until another person \[like tirumaḻisai āḻvār\] comes and tells as said in tiruccanda virtuttam 61 “*kidandavāṟu eḻundirundu pēsu*” (wake up and speak to me). You cannot avoid having all your activities for the sake of your devotees as said in jitantē stōtram “*bhaktānām*” (for the devotees).
- *un tiru udambu asaiya* – To strain your tender divine form. Would you just see \[the desire of\] those seekers \[āḻvārs\] and not \[the desire of\] yourself?
- *todarndu kuṟṟēval seydu* – Performing confidential services saying “this has to be done at this stage, this has to be done at this stage and so on”. Just as when perumāḷ (śrī rāma) was not expressing his desires iḷaiya perumāḷ (lakśmaṇa) forced him saying “please accept this service, please accept this other service” as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 15.7 “*mām vada*” (please order me), engaging in confidential services in this manner.
- *tol adimai* – Since this is natural service for the ātmā, it is considered as ancient service. It is said in aśta ślōki 3 “*avastāsvāvisyu: mama sahaja kainkaryavidaya:*” (In all states, all times and places, my natural servitude should occur).
- *vaḻi varum toṇḍarōrkku aruḷi* – Showering your mercy upon us who are helpless and are coming in proper servitude. It appears that, āḻvār is speaking about his own qualification \[deserving nature\] in these three pāsurams. It is not so. He is talking about his lack of refuge as in “if a person exists for one master only, no one else will look at him”.
- *tadam koḷ tāmaraik kaṇ viḻittu* – Like a pond which becomes filled with a lotus flower, mercifully glancing with his vast divine eyes.
- *nī eḻundu* – Getting up. As said in [tiruppāvai 23](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/01/thiruppavai-23-mari-malai-muzhainjil/) “*sīriya singam aṟivuṟṟu*” (the great lion waking up), I wish to see the beauty of your waking up.
- *un tāmarai mangaiyum nīyum* – As said in “those who start pursuing bhagavān, will have to go through pirātti’s recommendation”, previously he said in first pāsuram “*pangayattāḷ tiruvaruḷ*“; now āḻvār is speaking about serving pirātti and emperumān together.
- *idam koḷ mū ulagum* – Residents of all the vast worlds.
- *toḻ irundu aruḷāy* – To worship you properly as done by ananyaprayōjana (those who have no expectation) and to see and enjoy that.
- *tiruppuḷingudik kidandānē* – Since you are easily approachable, you should mercifully do all of these. If you have mercifully decided to fulfil my desires, after doing some, should you not do the remaining as well?
- *tiruppuḷingudik kidandānē* – *irundaruḷāy* – You mercifully showed your beautiful reclining posture; you should also show your beautiful seated posture!

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 9.2.4. Pulingudik kidandu

*puḷingudik kidandu varaguṇamangai irundu vaigundattuḷ ninṟu teḷinda en sindai agangaḻiyādē ennai āḷvāy! enakkaruḷi naḷirnda sīr uḷagam mūnṟudan viyappa nāngaḷ kūttādi ninṟārppa paḷingu nīr mugilin pavaḷampōl kanivāy sivappa nī kāṇa vārāyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

puḷingudi – in tiruppuḷingudi; kidandu – resting; varaguṇamangai – in tiruvaraguṇamangai; irundu – sitting; vaigundattuḷ – in śrīvaikuṇṭam; ninṟu – standing; teḷinda – having clarity (that these are done for us); en – my; sindai agam – standing in my heart; kaḻiyādē – without leaving; ennai – me; āḷvāy – oh one who enslaved!; enakku – for me; aruḷi – granting special mercy; naḷirnda – cool; sīr – qualities such as śeela etc; ulagam mūnṟu – the three worlds; udan – with a single voice; viyappa – to the amazement saying “what a partiality towards his devotees!”; nāngaḷ – us (who are going to see you, being an ananya prayōjana (without any expectation)); kūttādi – dancing out of joy; ninṟu – stand; ārppa – to make huge noise of celebration; paḷingu – pure; nīr – filled with water; mugilin – in dark cloud; pavaḷampōl – like a coral creeper which is spread out; kani – having friendly colour; vāy – divine lips; sivappa – to manifest the reddiśness; kāṇa – to be seen and enjoyed by us; nī vārāy – you should mercifully walk towards us

**Перевод:**

**Oh one who enslaved me by mercifully resting in tiruppuḷingudi, sitting in tiruvaraguṇamangai and standing in śrīvaikuṇṭam, and standing in my heart which is having clarity! Granting your special mercy to me, to the amazement of the three worlds which glorify your qualities such as cool śeela etc, with a single voice saying “what a partiality towards his devotees!” and to have us dancing out of joy and stand to make huge noise of celebration, you should mercifully walk towards us to be seen and enjoyed by us, by manifesting the reddiśness in your friendly lips which appear like a coral creeper which is spread out in a dark cloud filled with pure water.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fourth pāsuram, āḻvār says “Just as you have presented yourself in divyadēśams starting with tiruppuḷingudi, kindly fulfil my other desires too”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. puḷingudik kidandu varaguṇamangai irundu vaigundattuḷ ninṟu teḷinda en sindai agangaḻiyādē ennai āḷvāy! enakkaruḷi naḷirnda sīr uḷagam mūnṟudan viyappa nāngaḷ kūttādi ninṟārppa paḷingu nīr mugilin pavaḷampōl kanivāy sivappa nī kāṇa vārāyē*

- *puḷingudi …* – Did you do all of these after I requested you to do so? \[No – he did these out of his own free will\] [parāśara bhattar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/parasara-bhattar/) was very upset in \[tottiyam\] tirunārāyaṇapuram \[after [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s divine form was attacked by miscreants, and piḷḷai tirunaṟaiyūr araiyar gave up his life saving emperumān’s divine form\] and said in anger “You could do \[unpleasant\] activities out of your freewill towards strong personalities such as [emperumānār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/emperumanar/) who can bear your such activities and they still remained faithful towards you; how can you do such activities towards me who is very weak-hearted? Whatever is done towards most faithful personalities who remain firm as said in “*mahāviśvāsa pūrvakam*” (with unflinching faith), they will think ‘even if we have to suffer, it is not because of anything other than our own previous sins’, could you do the same towards weak-hearted persons who would become weaker in their faith?” \[[āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says\] Did you not sustain me by showing the beauty of your reclining posture in tiruppuḷingudi as said in [tirumālai 23](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/10/thirumalai-23/) “*kidandadōr kidakkai*” (the beautiful resting posture), the beauty of your sitting posture in varaguṇamangai as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 6.7.6](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/02/thiruvaimozhi-6-5-5-kuzhaiyum-val/) “*pirān irundamai kāttinīr*” (you showed the merciful presence of our benefactor) and the beauty of your standing posture in śrīvaikuṇṭam as said in periya tirumoḻi 6.9.8 “*nilaiyāra ninṟān*” (he stood firmly)?
- *teḷinda en sinda agam kaḻiyādē* – To not move away saying “ayōjña” (unqualified). After bringing clarity in my mind in tiruvāimoḻi 8.8 “*kaṇgaḷ sivandu*“, you remained eternally with me to retain that clarity in me.
- *ennai āḷvāy* – You made me survive by thinking upon your qualities instead of letting me leave saying “I am unqualified” or finishing myself in sorrow of separation.
- *enakku aruḷi* – After stopping me from moving away, if you also did not give me life, how can I sustain myself?
- *naḷirnda …* – The quality of śeela which cools down the one who meditated upon such quality. The auspicious quality of “fulfilling the desire of [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)“.
- *ulagam mūnṟu udan viyappa* – To the enjoyment and amazement of everyone who is ignorant and who is intelligent.
- *nāngaḷ …* – Not only we are amazed, but to have us emotionally charged. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) does not have time for amazement \[he is emotionally charged to dance already\]
- *paḷingu nīr mugilin pavaḷampōl kanivāy sivappa* – The reddiśness in his divine lips resemble a coral creeper spreading out on an attractive cloud filled with pure water. This is [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s smile on seeing āḻvār’s dance.
- *nī kāṇavārāyē* – You should come in front of me to let me see you. This is how his dance is. The way he walks placing step by step, resembles the dance of an expert dancer. Once namperumāḷ (śrīranganāta) invited piḷḷai aḻagiya maṇavāḷa araiyar and told him “I will walk here; you dance matching my steps” and araiyar replied to that saying “tampirānē (Oh lord)! Can I dance matching your steps? periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 3.6.4 ‘*kānagam padi ulāvi ulāvi*‘ (walking around the forest) … – as they heard your highness’ divine flute music, they stopped their songs; they stopped their expert dance on seeing your natural walk; can I compete with you in dance with these inferior limbs?”

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 9.2.5. Pavalampol kanivay

*pavaḷampōl kani vāy sivappa nī kāṇa vandu nin pal nilā muttam tavaḻ kadir muṟuval seydu nin tirukkaṇ tāmarai tayanga ninṟaruḷāy pavaḷa nan padark kīḻc canguṟai porunal taṇ tiruppuḷingudik kidandāy kavaḷa mā kaḷiṟṟin idar kedat tattuk kāysinap paṟavai ūrndānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

pavaḷam – coral’s; nan – dense; padark kīḻ – under the creeper; sangu – conces; uṟai – where they are present; porunal – tirupporunal’s (tāmirabharaṇi river); taṇ – invigorating; tiruppuḷingudi – in tiruppuḷingudi; kidandāy – mercifully resting; kavaḷam – one who is used to having lot of food; mā – huge; kaḷiṟṟin – gajēndra’s; idar – the sorrow of fighting for thousand dēva (celestial) years, without any food; keda – to eliminate; tadattu – in that pond; kāy – cruel (on the enemies); sinam – having anger; paṟavai – periya tiruvadi (garuda); ūrndānē – oh one who arrived by riding!; pavaḷampōl – just as there is abundance of creeper of corals and conces in tirupporunal; kani – glossy; vāy – divine lips; sivappa – appearing reddish; nin – your; pal – as tooth; nilā – remaining; muttam – as we see the pearls; kadir – radiance; tavaḻ – having; muṟuvalseydu – smiling; kāṇa – to be seen (by me); nī vandu – you should arrive; nin – your; tiru – beautiful; kaṇ – divine eyes; tāmarai – lotus; tayanga – to shine; ninṟaruḷāy – should mercifully stand revealing your joy

**Перевод:**

**Oh one who is mercifully resting in invigorating tiruppuḷingudi which is having tirupporunal which is the abode of conces under the densely present creeper of corals and who arrived by riding greatly angry periya tiruvadi at the pond where the huge śrī gajēndrāḻvān who is used to having lot of food, to eliminate its sorrow of fighting for thousand dēva (celestial) years, without any food! Just as there is abundance of creeper of corals and conces in tirupporunal, your glossy divine lips which appear reddish and the tooth remaining insided appear like pearls; you should arrive with your radiant smile to be seen by me; you should mercifully stand revealing your joy with your beautiful divine lotus like eyes shining.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fifth pāsuram, āḻvār says “You should mercifully appear in front of me as you appeared for śrī gajēndrāḻvān”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. pavaḷampōl kani vāy sivappa nī kāṇa vandu nin pal nilā muttam tavaḻ kadir muṟuval seydu nin tirukkaṇ tāmarai tayanga ninṟaruḷāy pavaḷa nan padark kīḻc canguṟai porunal taṇ tiruppuḷingudik kidandāy kavaḷa mā kaḷiṟṟin idar kedat tattuk kāysinap paṟavai ūrndānē*

- *pavaḷam …* – You who are explained as uncangeable in cāndōjña upaniśat 3.14 ‘*avākyanādara:’* (does not speak, ignores \[in paramapadam\]), should smile due to seeing your favourable devotee and revealing the internal connection through your smile.
- *nin pal nilā muttam* – The teeth lining which has the \[crescent\] moon of teeth.
- *tavaḻ kadir muṟuval seydu* – “*kadir tavaḻ muṟuval seydu*” – the radiance is sneaking out being uncontrollable inside. In the lips, the moon like teeth are floating. muttam – lips. Smiling to emanate radiance.
- *nin tirukkaṇ tāmarai tayanga ninṟu aruḷāy* – This is the smile of the eyes. tayangugai – the fresh radiance or the swaying of the eyes like that of the ocean.
- *ninṟu aruḷāy* – I should see how you take a few steps and after that being unable to do anything, just remain stunned.
- *pavaḷam …* – Oh one who is mercifully resting in invigorating tiruppuḷingudi which is having the tāmirabharaṇi river which has the conces under the creepers of corals! padar – tūṟu – bushes. In this town, the entities will not live in fear of harmful entities. While this is the nature of the town, why am I fearing “Will I attain you? ōr not?” in this town?
- *kavaḷam …* – Elephant which is always joyful. By this, it is implied that the elephant was mad.  The elephant which had not gone through sorrows previously.
- *idar keda* – As said by gajēndrāḻvān himself in siṟiya tirumadal “*vārāy en Ar idarai nīkkāy*“, this is the huge nature of the sorrow it went through. [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s heart itself became broken hearing about the great suffering the elephant went through as identified in “*ānaiyin tuyaram*” (elephant’s sorrow).
- *tadattu* – To eliminate the danger of being caught by a lowly crocodile, since water is not the natural habitat for the elephant. tadam – shore and pond.
- *kāy sinap paṟavai ūrndānē* – periya tiruvadi (garuda) has great anger on enemies. Did you not carry such periya tiruvadi on yourself since you considered that he was not fast enough for you \[to remove the danger of gajēndrāḻvān\] and arrive \[at the pond\]? My state is the same as that of the elephant! You should mercifully appear in front of me just as you did for the elephant.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 9.2.6. Kaysinap paravai

*kāy sinap paṟavai ūrndu pon malaiyin mīmisaik kārmugilpōl māsina māli māli mān enṟu angavar padakkananṟu mun ninṟa kāy sina vēndē! kadir mudiyānē! kali vayal tiruppuḷingudiyāy! kāy sina āḻi sangu vāḷ vil taṇḍhēndi emmidar kadivānē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

pon – golden; malaiyin – the great mēru’s; mīmisai – lying atop; kārmugilpōl – like a dark cloud; kāy – cruel (on enemies); sinam – having anger; paṟavai – periya tiruvadi (garudāḻvār); ūrndu – riding; kāy – like the fire of death upon enemies; sinam – having anger; āḻi sangu vāḷ vil taṇḍu – the five divine weapons; ēndi – carrying; mā – great; sinam – having anger; māli – māli; mān – great; māli – sumāli; enṟu – well known as; avar – those demons; angu – in the battle field; pada – to kill; kananṟu – with great anger; mun – in front of (the unfavourable ones); ninṟa – standing (showing this beauty); kāy – that which burns the enemies; sinam – having anger; vēndē – being the lord; kadir – shining due to the destruction of enemies; mudiyānē – one who is having the divine crown; kali – abundant; vayal – having fields; tiruppuḷingudiyāy – one who is residing in tiruppuḷingudi; em – our; idar – sorrow of being unable to enjoy; kadivānē – oh one who is there to eliminate!

**Перевод:**

**emperumān riding the very angry periya tiruvadi resembles a dark cloud lying atop the golden mountain of great mēru; he is carrying the five divine weapons which are having anger which resembles the fire of death upon enemies, and is standing with great anger in front of those well-known demons such as the angry māli, the great sumāli, to kill them; he is being the lord who is having anger which burns the enemies, and who is having the divine crown which is shining due to the destruction of enemies, and who is residing in tiruppuḷingudi which is having abundant fields; oh one who is there to eliminate our sorrow of being unable to enjoy! Implies, he should mercifully be present with that vāhana (vehicle), weapons and divine crown, and the shining divine eyes, to be seen by me!**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the sixth pāsuram, when emperumān says “There are hurdles to fulfil your desires” āḻvār says “Just as you eliminated the demons such as as māli with the divine weapons which you are donning to eliminate the dangers of your devotees, you should mercifully eliminate my hurdles as well”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. kāy sinap paṟavai ūrndu pon malaiyin mīmisaik kārmugilpōl māsina māli māli mān enṟu angavar padakkananṟu mun ninṟa kāy sina vēndē! kadir mudiyānē! kali vayal tiruppuḷingudiyāy! kāy sina āḻi sangu vāḷ vil taṇḍhēndi emmidar kadivānē!*

- *kāy sinap paṟavai ūrndu* – Even if you are lenient towards the enemies, periya tiruvadi is not; riding such periya tiruvadi.
- *pon malaiyin mīmisaik kārmugilpōl* – This is how he appears while riding periya tiruvadi. Resembles a dark cloud lying atop mount mēru. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying this now, to see [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s divine presence on the back of periya tiruvadi.
- *mā sina māli* – māli who came with great anger.
- *māli mān* – The great māli. That is, sumāli.
- *enṟu angu avar pada* – To kill all of those.
- *kananṟu mun ninṟa* – Standing in front of them with great anger. His valour is such that the enemies will perish just on seeing his angry form.
- *kāysina vēndē* – Divine name. Oh controller who has anger which roasts the enemies!
- *kadir mudiyānē* – Oh one who has a shining divine crown! While you are crowned to protect others, will it be apt for me to lose your protection?
- *kali vayal tiruppuḷingudiyāy* – Am I losing it because of your presence in a far away abode? Oh one who is mercifully resting in tiruppuḷingudi which has abundant fields!
- *kāy sina āḻi …* – Did you not take up the greatly angry, divine weapons such as tiruvāḻi (divine chakra) etc to eliminate the dangers of your devotees? The connection with the previous pāsuram is as seen in “*em idar kadivānē – tirukkaṇ tāmarai tayanga ninṟaruḷāy*“.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 9.2.7. Em idar kadindu

*em idar kadindingennai āḷvānē! imaiyavar tamakkumānganaiyāy! semmadal malarundāmaraip paḻanat taṇ tiruppuḷingudik kidandāy! nammudai adiyar kavvai kaṇḍugandu nām kaḷittuḷa nalangūra immadavulagar kāṇa nī oru nāḷ irundidāy engaḷ kaṇ mugappē*

**Пословный перевод:**

em – our; idar – all sorrows caused by avidyā (ignorance) etc; kadindu – eliminate; ingu – in this world; ennai – me; āḷvānē – being the one who accepts my service; imaiyavar tamakkum – for brahmā et al who don’t blink their eyes; āngu – there; anaiyāy – being the protector who first removes the hurdles and then fulfils their desires; sem – reddish; madal – petal; malarum – blossoming; tāmarai – having lotus; paḻanam – having water bodies; taṇ – cool; tiruppuḷingudi – in tiruppuḷingudi; kidandāy – oh one who is mercifully resting for your devotees!; nammudai – so as to say “our people”; adiyar – your distinguished devotees, nityasūris; kavvai kaṇḍu – seeing the celebration (caused by experience); nām – us; ugandu – being pleased; kaḷittu – being joyful; uḷam – in heart; nalam – affection; kūra – to have; madam – ignorant; i – this; ulagar – residents of this world; kāṇa – to see; nī – you (who always gives joy to nityasūris); oru nāḷ – at least one day; engaḷ kaṇmugappē – in front of our eyes; irundidāy – should mercifully reside

**Перевод:**

**Oh one who is mercifully resting for your devotees in the cool tiruppuḷingudi which has water bodies with lotus blossoming with reddish petals, to eliminate all our sorrows caused by avidyā and to accept our services in this world, and to protect brahmā et al who don’t blink their eyes, first by removing their hurdles and then fulfilling their desires! You should mercifully reside in front of our eyes at least one day, for us to see the celebration of nityasūris, your distinguished devotees, to identify them as “our people”, and for us to be pleased and joyful to have affection in our heart, and for the ignorant residents of this world to see.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the seventh pāsuram, āḻvār says “You who are the protector of the able and the weak, should remain in front of our eyes for one day to make us sustain ourselves”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. em idar kadindingennai āḷvānē! imaiyavar tamakkumānganaiyāy! semmadal malarundāmaraip paḻanat taṇ tiruppuḷingudik kidandāy! nammudai adiyar kavvai kaṇḍugandu nām kaḷittuḷa nalangūra immadavulagar kāṇa nī oru nāḷ irundidāy engaḷ kaṇ mugappē*

- *em idar kadindu* – Eliminating all our worldly sorrows.
- *ingu ennai āḷvānē* – Oh one who engages me in your service in this world which is not a place for knowledge about [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/)!
- *imaiyavar tamakkum ānganaiyāy* – Not only for us who are akincana (helpless), oh one who is the controller for brahmā et al who consider themselves to be supreme as said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 16-14](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/16-14/) “*īśvarōham*” (I am the controller)!
- *sem madal …* – Oh one who is mercifully resting in the invigorating tiruppuḷingudi which has water bodies where blossoming lotuses with reddish petals exist! There is lotus everywhere – both inside and outside \[[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) himself has lotus eyes, lotus feet etc\].
- *nammudai …* – We should become pleased seeing how your devotees enjoy you, that pleasure should reach its peak \[as joy\] and due to that the affection in our heart towards you should grow.
- *immada ulagar kāṇa* – To be seen even by the ignorant residents of this world, who don’t know to differentiate between left and right hands.
- *nī oru nāḷ irundidāy engaḷ kaṇ mugappē* – You should mercifully remain in front of our eyes at least for one day. Should you, who are giving constant audience to nityasūris, not present yourself to our eyes at least for one day? Should your audience be available for qualified persons only?

## 9.2.8. Engal kanmugappe

*engaḷ kaṇmugappē ulagargaḷ ellām iṇaiyadi toḻudeḻudiṟainjit tangaḷ anbārat tamadu sol valattāl talait talaic ciṟandu pūsippat tingaḷ sēr mādat tiruppuḷingudiyāy! tiruvaigundattuḷḷāy dēvā! ingaṇmā jñālattidanuḷum oru nāḷ irundidāy vīṟṟidangoṇḍē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tingaḷ – moon (who resides at the upper boundary of dēvalōka); sēr – very tall to make contact; mādam – having mansions; tiruppuḷingudiyāy – one who resides in tiruppuḷingudi; tiruvaigundattu – in śrīvaikuṇṭam; uḷḷāy – one mercifully resides; dēvā – Oh one who is having this radiance of easy approacability!; engaḷ kaṇmugappē – in front of us; ulagargaḷ – residents of this world; ellām – everyone; adi – your divine feet; iṇai – both; toḻudu – worship; eḻudu – and rise; iṟainji – bewildered in manifesting their dependence towards you; tangaḷ – their; anbu – bhakti (devotion); Ara – while present; tamadu – their; sol valattāl – with the strength of their speech; talait talaic ciṟandu – competing with each other in reaching emperumān; pūsippa – to praise in many ways; i – this; kaṇ – vast; mā – praiseworthy (matching your arrival); jñālattu – in earth; idanuḷum – in this tiruppuḷingudi; vīṟṟu (vīṟu) idam koṇḍu – to have your supremacy well manifested; oru nāḷ irundidāy – you should mercifully remain for one day

**Перевод:**

**Oh one who is having the radiance of easy approacability of residing in tiruppuḷingudi which has tall mansions which reach to the moon and who resides in śrīvaikuṇṭam! You should mercifully remain for one day in front of us in this tiruppuḷingudi in the vast, praiseworthy earth, to have your supremacy well manifested, for all the residents of this world to worship your divine feet, rise, be bewildered in manifesting their dependence towards you and to have their bhakti towards you, and to compete with each other in reaching emperumān and praising him in many ways with the strength of their speech.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the eighth pāsuram, emperumān says “I can only fulfil your desire in tirunādu (paramapadam)” and āḻvār says “You should mercifully rest here at least for one day manifesting your greatness in front of our eyes, to be praised by all worlds”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. engaḷ kaṇmugappē ulagargaḷ ellām iṇaiyadi toḻudeḻudiṟainjit tangaḷ anbārat tamadu sol valattāl talait talaic ciṟandu pūsippat tingaḷ sēr mādat tiruppuḷingudiyāy! tiruvaigundattuḷḷāy dēvā! ingaṇmā jñālattidanuḷum oru nāḷ irundidāy vīṟṟidangoṇḍē*

- *engaḷ* … – You should be in front of our eyes. At that time, everyone in this world should see the beauty of the togetherness of your divine feet, bow to them and rise, and surrender unto you.
- *tangaḷ anbu Ara* – To increase their love.
- *tamadu sol valattāl* – The words matching their strength; or, as best as they can say; it is said in śrī nārāyaṇīyam “*yatā jñānam tu vakśyāmi puruśantam sanātanam*” (I am telling about the ancient lord as much as I know). That is, saying as in “Let you live for hundred years, let you wear golden sacred thread”. When vangippurattu nambi said “viyayasva” (Let you be victorious), recollect āṇḍān’s words \[Once during a puṟappādu, nambi stood along with the covherd girls and vorśipped namperumāḷ. āṇḍān asked him “why are you standing there?” and nambi replied “[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s merciful glance will fall upon them directly. That is why I stood with them”. āṇḍān asked “What did they say and what did you say?” nambi said “they said ‘Let you drink lot of milk; let you eat lot of fruits; let you live for hundred years, Let you wear golden sacred thread” and I said “vijayasva”. Hearing that āṇḍān said “when you are in their group, you should speak like them only”\].
- *talait talaic ciṟandu pūsippa* – Competing with each other, surrendering unto you and praising you.
- *tingaḷ …* – The mansions are so tall that the moon can rest on them after roaming around; one who is present there.
- *tiruvaigundattu uḷḷāy* – Further, you are also mercifully standing in śrīvaikuṇṭam.
- *dēvā* – The radiance acquired due to remaining in this samsāram, which is greater than that in paramapadam.
- *ingaṇ mā jñālattu idanuḷum oru nāḷ irundidāy* – In this great earth, you should mercifully remain for one day in tiruppuḷingudi.

While remaining here,

- *vīṟṟu idam koṇḍu* – You should remain here similar to being in paramapadam, manifesting your greatness. What is the intent of āḻvār saying “*idanuḷum*” (in here, as well)? For āḻvārs, when they see [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s beautiful resting posture, they will think “how will he look, if he sits?”, “how will he look, if he stands?” In this manner they will acquire new desires; for us these will be in a different way. We have the same desire in aspects which lead to hell; we won’t experience them in bhagavat viśayam. Being unsatisfied with whatever is acquired, and seeking further experience will occur in worldly matters for us. We can only know that such experience is available in bhagavat viśayam \[as we cannot fully experience it\].

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.
