## 9.2.9. Virridangondu

*vīṟṟidangoṇḍu viyan koḷ mā jñālattidanuḷum irundidāy adiyōm pōṟṟi ōvādē kaṇṇiṇai kuḷirap pudu malar āgattaip paruga sēṟṟiḷa vāḷai sennel ūdugaḷum seḻum paṇait tiruppuḷingudiyāy! kūṟṟamāy asurar kulamudal arinda koduvinaip padaigaḷ vallānē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

sēṟu – due to growing in mud which is natural habitat; iḷam vāḷai – youthful fish; sennelūdu – in between the great paddy crops; ugaḷum – jumping around and living happily; seḻu – abundant; paṇai – having water bodies; tiruppuḷingudiyāy – one who is residing in tiruppuḷingudi; kūṟṟamāy – being death to enemies; asurar kulam – the demoniac clan; mudal – from the womb; arinda – one who destroys; kodu vinai – having cruel acts matching that; padaigaḷ – weapons; vallānē – Oh one who has under your control!; adiyōm – We who are exclusively devoted to you; pōṟṟi – to perform mangaḷāśāsanam; ōvādē – continuously; kaṇṇiṇai – pair of eyes; kuḷira – to cool down from the heated state; pudu malar – very tender like a fresh flower; āgattai – your form; paruga – to enjoy, in the form of quenching my thirst; vīṟṟu idam koṇḍu – manifesting the greatness (acquired from your supremacy) and being present; viyan koḷ – vast; mā – praiseworthy; jñālattu idanuḷum – in this world too; irundidāy – you should mercifully remain

**Перевод:**

**You are residing in tiruppuḷingudi which is having abundant water bodies where youthful fish are jumping around and living happily in between great paddy crops, due to growing in mud which is natural habitat for the fish. Oh one who has under your control the weapons which are having cruel acts matching those weapons, and who is like death to enemies and who destroys the demoniac clan including those who are in the womb! You should mercifully remain in this vast, praiseworthy world too, manifesting your very tender fresh flower like form and your greatness for us who are exclusively devoted to you, to enjoy, in the form of quenching our thirst, and to perform mangaḷāśāsanam continuously and to see you to cool down our pair of eyes from their heated state.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the ninth pāsuram, emperumān says “Why should I remain in this samsāram which does not understand my supremacy?” āḻvār says “You do that to be seen by us who are desirous, and for us to be uplifted”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. vīṟṟidangoṇḍu viyan koḷ mā jñālattidanuḷum irundidāy adiyōm pōṟṟi ōvādē kaṇṇiṇai kuḷirap pudu malar āgattaip paruga sēṟṟiḷa vāḷai sennel ūdugaḷum seḻum paṇait tiruppuḷingudiyāy! kūṟṟamāy asurar kulamudal arinda koduvinaip padaigaḷ vallānē!*

- *vīṟṟiudam koṇḍu* – Manifesting the greatness acquired by śēśitvam (lordship).
- *viyan koḷ …* – Remain in this amazing, great earth, which is in this samsāra (material realm) which does not see your purpose.
- *idanuḷum irundidāy* – Please remain in this divyadēśam named tiruppuḷingudi as well. Is it sufficient if you remain in the presence of those \[nityasūris\] who cannot live without you?
- *idanuḷum irundidāy* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) mercifully recollects [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s beautiful reclining posture. \[āḻvār says\] Now, you mercifully let us enjoy your sitting posture. bhattar mercifully explains “We can see everything here \[in śrīrangam\] itself; merciful reclining posture can be seen in periya perumāḷ; merciful standing posture can be seen in namperumāḷ; merciful sitting posture can be seen in periya pirāttiyār”.

[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) asks “What will you get by my presence here?” [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says,

- *adiyōm …* – adiyōm – we, the servitors, who will sustain ourselves when you manifest your form to us.
- *pōṟṟi* – Performing mangaḷāśāsanam saying that, this experience should be present eternally.
- *ōvādē* – Without any break.
- *kaṇṇiṇai kuḷira* – To have our eyes which are drought-stricken due to not seeing you, to have all the fatigue removed and be cooled.
- *pudu malar …* – To enjoy the divine form which resembles a fresh flower. To enjoy the form which is like a tender flower, as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 21.6 “*lōcanābhyām pibanniva*” (Like drinking through eyes).
- *sēṟṟu iḷam …* – All the entities in this town will be joyful having fulfilled their desires. Having beautiful vaterbodies, where in the mud which remains in between great paddy crops, the fish jump around in joy like muktātmās who remain twenty five years old always \[in paramapadam\].
- *seḻum paṇai* – Also explained as beautiful marudam (farm lands).
- *kūṟṟamāy …* – Holding divine weapons which appear like death for the enemies; alternative explanation – being death for enemies, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who destroys their clan along with the trace, and having the divine weapons which perform such cruel acts, to destroy such enemies. Now, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying this to highlight as an example of eliminating his \[āḻvār’s\] enemies previously; or to say “Why should I lose you as if you have some limitation?”

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 9.2.10. Koduvinaip padaigal

*kodu vinaip padaigaḷ vallaiyāy amararkkidar keda asurargatkidar sey kadu vinai nenjē! ennudai amudē! kali vayal tiruppuḷingudiyāy vadiviṇai illā malar magaḷ maṟṟai nila magaḷ pidikkum mel adiyai kodu vinaiyēnum pidikka nī oru nāḷ kūvudal varudal seyyāyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kodu vinai – cruel acts towards enemies; padaigaḷ – weapons; vallaiyāy – able (to engage them); amararkku – for dēvas who are favourable; idar – sorrow; keda – to eliminate; asurargatku – for asuras who are unfavourable; idar – sorrow; sey – while causing; kadu – quick; vinai – having actions; nanjē – being poison; ennudai – for me (who is ananyaprayōjana (not expecting anything else) and ananyagati (not having any other refuge)); amudē – oh nectar (which is difficult to attain); kali – rich; vayal – having fields; tiruppuḷingudiyāy – Oh one who is mercifully resting in tiruppuḷingudi!; vadivu – for beauty; iṇai illā – having great beauty for which even your beauty is not a match; malar magaḷ – śrīmahālakśmi who resides in lotus; maṟṟai – having similar greatness; nila magaḷ – śrī bhūmip pirātti; pidikkum – massaging (with their naturally tender hands); mel – very tender; adiyai – divine feet; kodu vinaiyēnum – I who am having great sin (to lose this opportunity even after your being apt master for me); pidikka – to massage; nī kūvudal – you calling me there; varudal – or mercifully coming here (as I desired); oru nāḷ seyyāy – should do it one day

**Перевод:**

**Oh one who is mercifully resting in tiruppuḷingudi, who is able to engage the weapons which have cruel acts towards enemies, who is like poison which is having quick actions to cause sorrow to asuras who are unfavourable which will in turn eliminate sorrows for dēvas who are favourable and who is like nectar for me! You should either call me there or mercifully come here one day to let me who is having great sin, to massage your very tender divine feet which is massaged by śrīmahālakśmi who resides in lotus, who is having great beauty for which, even your beauty is not a match and śrī bhūmip pirātti who is having similar greatness.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the tenth pāsuram, āḻvār says “You should either take me there or arrive here so that I can serve your most enjoyable divine feet”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. kodu vinaip padaigaḷ vallaiyāy amararkkidar keda asurargatkidar sey kadu vinai nenjē! ennudai amudē! kali vayal tiruppuḷingudiyāy vadiviṇai illā malar magaḷ maṟṟai nila magaḷ pidikkum mel adiyai kodu vinaiyēnum pidikka nī oru nāḷ kūvudal varudal seyyāyē*

- *kodu vinaip padaigaḷ vallaiyāy* – Just as fire rising out of water, you become angry (very rarely) on those who show enmity towards you even though they are subservient to you, and are capable of taking up arms against them. He cannot destroy anyone \[due to his merciful nature\]; he is of the nature to say as in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 18.19 “*yadivā rāvaṇasvayam*” (even if it is rāvaṇa himself, bring him). Building a bridge in the ocean, surrounding lankā, subsequently sending angadap perumāḷ as messenger of peace, and when rāvaṇa was caught, śrī rāma said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 59.144 “*gaccānujānāmi*” (Leave now and return tomorrow) and let him escape. emperumān waited thinking “would he become favourable now?” When rāvaṇa was firm on his thoughts and stood in front of emperumān as if saying “I want to be killed”, emperumān killed him with tears in his eyes. He only kills them due to their unfavourable acts and does not kill them willingly.
- *amarar …* – To eliminate the sorrows caused by asuras to dēvas, he will cause sorrows to the asuras.
- *kadu vinai nanjē* – Oh one who is an irreversible poison which will kill immediately!
- *ennudai amudē* – That same poison is nectar for [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/). This is unlike the brackish water (amrutam) which was desired by dēvas.
- *kali vayal …* – To get this amrutam, we need not churn the ocean or go to svargam; it is the nectar which is present in tiruppuḷingudi.
- *kali vayal* – having abundant fields
- *vadivu iṇai …* – There is no match for her form. Even bhagavān is no match for her; she is fully glorified in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 16.5 “*tanjēyam asitēkśaṇā*” (one who is having beautiful dark eyes and a good match for perumāḷ).
- *maṟṟai nila magaḷ* – śrī bhūmip pirātti who is equally glorious.
- *pidikkum mel adiyai* – Even when they massage his divine feet, they would do it carefully thinking “will they be hurt?” due to their tender nature; such divine feet.
- *kodu vinaiyēnum pidikka* – After [tiruvāimoḻi 8.8](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/04/thiruvaimozhi-8-8-kangal-sivandhu/) “*kaṇgaḷ sivandu*“, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) would not consider his lowliness \[since emperumān highlights that ātmās are very dear to him\]. He is saying as in “*pāviyēn*” (My bad!) thinking “They are present there, I have the right to serve, yet I am unable to serve”.
- *nī oru nāḷ kūvudal varudal seyyāyē* – You who are greatly enjoyable and are present in tiruppuḷingudi, to sustain us, should invite me there or mercifully come here. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) did not say “varudal” (you should come) first, since he did not want to disturb his togetherness with pirāttis there. \[Even while giving it as second choice\] Since they would not send him alone towards desirous persons, āḻvār is calling emperumān, thinking that they will come together.

## 9.2.11. Kuvudal varudal

*kūvudal varudal seydidāy enṟu kurai kadal kadaindavan tannai mēvi nangamarnda viyan punal porunal vaḻudinādan satakōpan nāviyal pādal āyirattuḷḷum ivaiyum ōr pattum vallārgaḷ ōvudal inṟi ulaga mūnṟaḷandān adiyiṇai uḷḷattōrvārē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kurai – having great noise; kadal – ocean; kadaindavan tannai – savrvēśvara who churned; kūvudal – inviting me there; varudal – coming (to where I am); seydidāy – do it; enṟu – desired in this manner; mēvi – acquiring his acceptance; nangu – well; amarnda – one who sustained; viyan – abundant; punal – having water; porunal – having divine porunal (tāmirabharaṇi) river; vaḻudinādan – leader of tiruvaḻudinādu (āḻvārtirunagari and surroundings); satakōpan – āḻvār‘s; nā iyal – activity of the tongue; pādal āyirattuḷḷum – in thousand pāsurams; ōr – distinguished; ivaiyum pattum – this decad also; vallārgaḷ – experts; mūnṟu ulagam – three worlds; aḷandān – sarvēśvaran, who measured; adi – divine feet; iṇai – both; ōvudal – ending; inṟi – without; uḷḷattu – in heart; ōrvār – will get to enjoy

**Перевод:**

**āḻvār said to sarvēśvara who churned the very noisy ocean “invite me there or come here”, desired to acquire his acceptance and sustained himself; he is the leader of tiruvaḻudinādu (āḻvārtirunagari and surroundings) which has divine porunal/tāmirabharaṇi river with abundance of water; those who are experts in this decad among the thousand pāsurams which are the result of the activity of such āḻvār’s tongue, will get to endlessly enjoy in their heart, both the divine feet of sarvēśvara who measured the three worlds.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the end, āḻvār says “Those who learn this decad will perpetually enjoy emperumān“.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. kūvudal varudal seydidāy enṟu kurai kadal kadaindavan tannai mēvi nangamarnda viyan punal porunal vaḻudinādan satakōpan nāviyal pādal āyirattuḷḷum ivaiyum ōr pattum vallārgaḷ ōvudal inṟi ulaga mūnṟaḷandān adiyiṇai uḷḷattōrvārē*

- *kūvudal …* – āḻvār said “*kurai kadal kadaindavan tannai kūvudal varudal seydidāy*” (the one who churned the noisy ocean should invite me there or arrive here). Either in proper manner or in improper manner, the end result is to see him only.
- *kurai kadal …* – He desired for [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who undertook the trouble himself to churn the ocean and give the nectar to those who did not have such desire.
- *mēvi nangu amarnda* – Due to thinking about such nature of emperumān, āḻvār remained firmly.
- *viyan …* – āḻvār, the leader of tirvaḻudinādu which has tirupporunal with amazing water.
- *nā iyal pādal* – āḻvār spoke \[spontaneously\] without the help of his mind.
- *ōvudal …* – One who got to perpetually enjoy the divine feet of the one who is easily approachable by his devotees. All along, as āḻvār was saying to [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) “You should mercifully glance with your divine eyes, you should mercifully place your divine feet on my head; I should see the merciful sitting posture of your highness; I should see the togetherness of your consorts and your highness; I should see you walk around; I should see your gentle smile” and desiring for them without getting those desires fulfilled, it appears that, this longing desire is the goal; even for those who recited this decad, this longing desire will continue all along – says āḻvār as said in jitantē stōtram “*yadināśam navindēta tāvadāsmi krutīsadā*” (I will remain satisfied forever, if my heart which is placed on you remains the same forever).

## 9.3 Orayiramay

## 9.3.1. Orayiramay

*ōrāyiramāy ulagēḻaḷikkum pēr āyiram koṇḍadōr pīdudaiyan kārāyina kāḷa nan mēniyinan nārāyaṇan nangaḷ pirān avanē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ōr – every divine name; āyiramāy – in thousand ways; ulagēḻu – all types of cētanas \[sentient beings\] and acētanas (insentient objects\]; aḷikkum – protecting; pēr – divine names; āyiram – thousand; koṇḍadu – having; ōr – distinguished; pīdu – greatness; udaiyan – one who is having; kāḷa kār āyina – dark like a black cloud; nan – spiritual; mēniyinan – having a divine form; nārāyaṇan avanē – one who has the primary name, nārāyaṇa, which is the root of all of those names; nangaḷ – for us; pirān – benefactor

**Перевод:**

**emperumān is having thousand distinguished divine names where each one of them is protecting all cētanas and acētanas in thousand ways; he is our benefactor having a divine spiritual dark form like that of a black cloud, and has the primary name, nārāyaṇa, which is the root of all of those names.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the first pāsuram, āḻvār mercifully says to his own divine heart “īsnt’ he nārāyaṇa? He will certainly fulfil our desire”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. ōrāyiramāy ulagēḻaḷikkum pēr āyiram koṇḍadōr pīdudaiyan kārāyina kāḷa nan mēniyinan nārāyaṇan nangaḷ pirān avanē*

- *ōr āyiramāy* – Each divine name is capable of protecting in a thousand ways. As said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 6.5.74 “*aiśvaryasya samagrasya vīryasya yaśaśśriya: …*” (Since bhaga means having aiśvarya (opulence), vīrya (valour), kīrti (fame), sampat (wealth), jñānam (knowledge) and vairājñam (detachment)) – by differences based on etymological interpretation of the word, there can be several ways of protection.
- *ulagu* – While protecting, instead of doing it individually, he will protect everyone.
- *ēḻu* – Even in that, instead of protecting one world only, he will protect all the worlds. [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) would only protect his devotees; such restriction is not there for his divine names.
- *aḷikkum* – There is a possibility for emperumān to say as in [śrī bhagavat gītā 16.19](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/16-19/) “*kśipāmi*” (I push them \[in demoniac births\]) on seeing their sins; but his names are naturally focussed on protection only.
- *pēr* – Just one name is enough for protection.

When asked “How many such names does he have?” [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says,

- *āyiram koṇḍadu ōr pīdu udaiyan* – As said in mahābhāratam “*dēvō nāma sahasravān*” (The shining [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who has thousand names) just as saying “he has many cows”. Just as one who desires to feed everyone will provide abundance of rice and water, īśvara who thought about protecting the universe, has thousand names as tool for that. Recollect the words of parāśara bhattar when kōyil āyttān lost his son, came to him and fell at his divine feet, with great agony \[kōyil āyttān was a disciple of bhattar. He named his son as bhattar in memory of his ācārya. When that son died, he came to bhattar with great agony. At that time bhattar said “Don’t worry for the loss of your son who had my name” and made a sculpture of himself and gave that to kōyil āyttān saying “Now, you keep this for you; I will be with you in this name and form” – this is to highlight that the divine name will be the refuge even in dire situations\] One who has the greatness of having thousand names.

Even if his thousand names are spread out like cauvery river without shores, his form will be such that the names can be brought together, to be enjoyed.

- *kār āyina kāḷa nan mēniyinan* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) thinks of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) as cloud itself as the similarity is so close. Being similar to a very dark, black cloud; even this is said since one who steps in to a flooded river will search for a boat to sustain oneself \[here āḻvār compares emperumān’s form to a dark cloud\], when explaining emperumān’s form, a similar object is highlighted; but if we look at his divine form, it has no match otherwise.

When asked “who is this person?” [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says

- *nārāyaṇan* – While jñāna (knowledge), śakti (ability) etc are all his qualities, jñāna (knowledge), ānanda (bliss), amalatva (being pure) etc are *svarūpa niṟupaka* (that which identifies him); similarly, when asked “Who is *pērāyiram koṇḍadu ōr pīdudaiyan*?” – where it is said “*innān*” (this person), āḻvār says “*nārāyaṇan*” – hence this name is his primary identity. Highlighting thousand names, there are three mantrams (nārāyaṇa, vāsudēva, viṣṇu mantrams) which are said to be primary being vyāpaka mantrams (those mantrams which highlight his all pervasiveness); since the other two \[vāsudēva and viṣṇu\] are now pushed along with the rest of the names, the predominance of this name can be understood. [tirumangai āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/thirumangai-azhwar/) said in [tirunedundāṇḍagam 4](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/06/thirunedunthandakam-4/) “*andaṇar māttu andi vaitta mandirattai*” (sarvēśvaran, the secret entity who is kept safely in the knots of vēdāntams which are the wealth of brāhmaṇas), periya tirumoḻi 8.10.3 “*nin tiruvetteḻuttum kaṟṟu nān uṟṟadum*” (I understood after learning your aśtākśaram), periya tirumoḻi 1.1.1 “*nārāyaṇa ennum nāmam*” (the name, nārāyaṇa) and periya tirumoḻi 6.10.1 “*namō nāraṇam*” (I worship nārāyaṇa); [nammāḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) too stated in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.2.10](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/05/thiruvaimozhi-1-2-10-en-perukku/) “*vaṇ pugaḻ nāraṇan*” (nārāyaṇa, who is with auspicious qualities) and recited this name only throughout tiruvāimoḻi. This is the path taken by vēdams, [āḻvārs](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/azhwars/) and our [ācāryas](http://acharyas.koyil.org/); even for us, there is nothing wrong in pursuing this even now; did we not discard the other two vyāpaka mantrams because they were pursued by śudras et al \[śaivas and others who were unfavourable towards bhagavān\] and others \[such as māyāvādis\]? We have to only pursue the path taken by our ācāryas.
- *nangaḷ pirān avanē* – He is the only benefactor who will protect us. By the avadāraṇam (exclusivity indicated by “***E***” in *avanē*), it is indicated that it is not apt for us to pray for our result saying “*kūvudal varudal seydidāy*“.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 9.3.2. Avane agal jnalam

*avanē agal jñālam padaittidandān avanē ahdu uṇḍu umiḻndān aḷandān avanē avanum avanum avanum avanē maṟṟellāmum aṟindanamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

agal – expansive; jñālam – universe; padaittu – one who created; idandān – entered and rescued it when there was the danger of deluge; avanē – he who does not expect any help; avanē ahdu – he himself, the earth; uṇḍu – protecting by placing in his stomach; umiḻndān – spat out after the deluge; aḷandān – one who measured so that others don’t claim ownership; avanum avanum avanum – those who are capable of sruśti (creation), samhāra (annihilation) and rakśaṇa (protection); avanē – only he; maṟṟu – all other bound entities; ellāmum – all cētanas (sentient beings) and acētanas (insentient objects); avanē – to be only him; aṟindanam – we knew (with the help of the knowledge given by him)

**Перевод:**

**He is the one who created the expansive universe; he who does not expect any help is the one who entered and rescued it when there was the danger of deluge;  he himself protected the great earth by placing it in his stomach; he spat it out after the deluge; he is the one who measured so that others don’t claim ownership; he is the one who is capable of sruśti, samhāra and rakśaṇa; he is all other bound entities; we knew him to be all cētanas and acētanas;**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the second pāsuram, āḻvār mercifully explains the meaning of the word nārāyaṇa.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. avanē agal jñālam padaittidandān avanē ahdu uṇḍu umiḻndān aḷandān avanē avanum avanum avanum avanē maṟṟellāmum aṟindanamē*

- *avanē agal jñālam padaittu idandān* – He is the one who created the expansive earth and as mahāvarāha (the great boar) rescued the earth which was consumed by deluge. By the avadāraṇam (exclusivity in *avan****E***), his sahakāri nairapēkśyam (not seeking any help) in activities such as creation etc, is explained.
- *avanē …* – Picking up the earth and placing it in his stomach to save it from the deluge, spitting it out to let it see outside, and when it was stolen by mahābali, walking over the boundary and reclaiming it – all of this done by [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) himself. By the avadāraṇam (exclusivity in *avan****E***), his sahakāri nairapēkśyam  in qualities such as āpatsakatvam (helping in dangerous times), rakśakatvam (protection) etc, is explained.
- *avanē …* – The svarūpa (nature), stiti (existence) and pravrutti (actions) of brahmā, rudra, indra et al are all at his disposal. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying as per the well known phrase in nārāyaṇa sūktam “*sa brahmā sa śivas sēndra*” (he is brahmā, he is rudra, he is indra). āḻvār is saying “sa: sa: sa:” \[*avanum avanum avanum*\].
- *avanē maṟṟu ellāmum* – As said in nārāyaṇa sūktam “*sōkśara: parama svarāt*” (he is the great, immutable liberated soul), irrespective of the predominant ones or the others, all cētana and acētana entities are at his disposal.
- *aṟindanamē* – When asked “While brahmā et al consider themselves as lords as said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 16-14](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/16-14/) ‘*īśvarōham’* (I am the controller) and their followers too consider them to be lords, why are you saying ‘*avanē*‘ (bhagavān only)?” [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says “Since I was divinely blessed with knowledge and devotion by bhagavān himself, I am able to say this”.

Thus, with these two pāsurams, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) considered \[and explained\] the tirumantram and its meanings.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 9.3.3. Arindana veda

*aṟindana vēda aruḷ poruḷ nūlgaḷ aṟindana koḷga arum poruḷādal aṟindanar ellām ariyai vaṇangi aṟindanar nōygaḷ aṟukkum marundē*

**Пословный перевод:**

aṟindana – knowledgeable as said in “vēdāhamēdam”; vēdam – vēdams; arum – difficult be known; poruḷ – that which determines the nature of entities; nūlgaḷ – śāstrams such as braham sūtram, itihāsams, purāṇams etc; arum – difficult to be known; poruḷādal – as an entity; aṟindana – as known; koḷga – can be accepted; aṟindanar – vaidika puruśas who knew as said in “aham vēdmi mahātmānam”; ellām ariyai – sarvēśvara who annihilates all sins; vaṇangi – surrender; nōygaḷ – (their) great disease of samsāra (bondage in material realm); aṟukkum – to sever; marundē – as the great medicine; aṟindanar – only knew as much

**Перевод:**

**śāstrams such as brahmasūtram, itihāsam, purāṇam etc help in knowing the nature of entities which are difficult to be known through vēdams alone, even though vēdams are expected to be knowledgeable as mentioned in the saying vēdāhamēdam. bhagavān is an entity who is difficult to be known even through these śāstrams (brahmasūtram etc). vaidika puruśas (followers of vēdams), as mentioned in the saying aham vēdmi mahātmānam, who knew sarvēśvara, the annihilator of all sins, knew only that he is the great medicine to sever the great disease of samsāra. But, unlike them, we have learnt his quality of being enjoyable as well as other qualities such as śeelam etc as manifested by him. This has to be read along with the word aṟindanam, mentioned in the pāsuram.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the third pāsuram, āḻvār becomes pleased saying “emperumān who is beyond the knowledge of vēdams and riśis, revealed himself completely to me”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. aṟindana vēda aruḷ poruḷ nūlgaḷ aṟindana koḷga arum poruḷādal aṟindanar ellām ariyai vaṇangi aṟindanar nōygaḷ aṟukkum marundē*

- *aṟindana …* – vēdams, the śāstrams, which have knowledge about the subjects which are most difficult to know; alternate explanation – śāstrams such as brahmasūtram, itihāsams, purāṇams etc determine the meanings of entities which are difficult to understand in vēdams.
- *aṟindana koḷga* – One can only know that “he is difficult to be known” as said in taittirīya upaniśat “*yatō vācō nivartantē*” (the speech returned), kauśīdakī upaniśat “*yasyā matam tasya matam”* (one who thinks he does not know, knows) and kauśīdakī upaniśat “*avijñātam vijānatām*” (one who thinks he knows, does not know).
- *aṟindanar ellām* – The greatly knowledgeable sages such as parāśara, vyāsa, vālmīki.
- *ariyai vaṇangi* – vaṇangi – āśrayaṇa (surrender). Surrendering unto the one who removes all sorrows.
- *aṟindanar, nōygaḷ aṟukkum marundē* – They only knew that [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is “*samsāra durita bhēśajam*” (the quick medicine to eliminate samsāra); “*samsāra sarpa sandaśta  naśta cēśtaika bhēśajam*” (Those who are bitten by the snake of samsāra and remain unconscious, will be freed as soon as they hear the name of kriṣṇa). They did not immerse in his enjoyability; another explanation – they did not immerse in his being the unconditional means.

## 9.3.4. Marunde nangal

*marundē nangaḷ bōga magiḻccikku enṟu perundēvar kuḻāngaḷ pidaṟṟum pirān karundēvan emmān kaṇṇan viṇṇulagam tarundēvanaic cōrēl kaṇḍāy manamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

nangaḷ – our; bōgam – enjoyment’s; magiḻccikku – for the increase; marundē – enriching medicine; enṟu – as; peru – great; dēvar – nityasrūis’; kuḻāngaḷ – groups; pidaṟṟum – due to overwhelming joy, praising in a disorderly manner; pirān – being the great benefactor who brings joy to them; karu – having darkness; dēvan – being the one with divine form; emmān – one who enslaved me (by showing that form); kaṇṇan – as kriṣṇa who is sarvasulabha (very easily approachable for all); viṇ ulagam – the enjoyment of paramapadam; tarum – one would give; dēvanai – refuge; manamē – Oh heart!; cōrēl kaṇḍāy – (due to your external focus or due to considering yourself to be inferior) do not lose!

**Перевод:**

**To make the groups of great nityasūris praise in a disorderly manner due to overwhelming joy saying “you are the enriching medicine to increase our enjoyment”, emperumān, the great benefactor, brings joy to them; having a dark, divine form, he enslaved me as kriṣṇa who is very easily approachable for all, and is my refuge, who would give the enjoyment of paramapadam. Oh heart! Do not lose him! marundu is also explained as the medicine which will be the remedy to contain the over-enjoyment.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fourth pāsuram, āḻvār says to his divine heart “sarvēśvaran who is enjoyable even for nityasūris, divinely incarnated as kriṣṇa, accepted me as a servitor and is ready to give paramapadam; don’t you lose him!”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. marundē nangaḷ bōga magiḻccikku enṟu perundēvar kuḻāngaḷ pidaṟṟum pirān karundēvan emmān kaṇṇan viṇṇulagam tarundēvanaic cōrēl kaṇḍāy manamē*

- *marundē nangaḷ bōga magiḻccikku enṟu* – Oh one who is the enhancer of the bliss acquired by experiencing you!

When asked “Who says this?” [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says,

- *perum dēvar* – Those nityasūris who are untouched by samsāra.
- *kuḻāngaḷ* – They would immerse in [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) in groups just as people would step in to a flooded river in groups.
- *pidaṟṟum* – Just as one who is affected with fever, they would call out in a disorderly manner.
- *karum dēvan* – Having a divine form, with the complexion of a dark cloud.
- *emmān* – One who enslaved me showing that form. He showed me the form which he showed to nityasūris!
- *kaṇṇan* – Instead of favouring from his high position, he incarnated as kriṣṇa and favoured me.
- *viṇ ulagam tarum dēvanai* – [sarvēśvara](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) who is ready to bestow paramapadam.
- *cōrēl kaṇḍāy manamē* – Oh heart! Don’t make him become pale! It appears that, ātmā leaving bhagavān is a loss for bhagavān. His efforts will go in vain; \[why would anyone lose him?\] otherwise, instead of realising his greatness, don’t ignore him considering him to be “*sulabhan*” (easily approachable!)

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 9.3.5. Maname unnai

*manamē unnai valvinaiyēn irandu kanamē sollinēn idu sōrēl kaṇḍāy punamēviya pūndaṇ tuḻāy alangal inamēdum ilānai adaivadumē*

**Пословный перевод:**

manamē – Oh heart!; unnai – you (who are more speedy in this matter); val vinaiyēn – I am having great sin to be unable to tolerate the delay; due to my desire; irandu – prayed; kanamē – firmly; sollinēn – told; idu – this; sōrēl kaṇḍāy – don’t let go; punam – in its own habitat; mēviya – due to growing; pū – fresh; taṇ tuḻāy – tiruttuḻāy (tuḷasi); alangal – one who has as garland; ēdum – in any manner; inam – match; ilānai – having greatness of not having \[a match\]; adaivadum – this aspect of reaching

**Перевод:**

**Oh heart! I am having great sin to be unable to tolerate the delay; due to my desire I prayed to you and firmly told “don’t let go of this”; \[don’t let go of\] this aspect of reaching emperumān who is having the greatness of not having a match in any manner and who is having tiruttuḻāy garland which is fresh due to growing in its own natural habitat \[emperumān’s divine body\].**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fifth pāsuram, āḻvār dearly prays to his heart “Do not leave the greatly enjoyable emperumān“.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. manamē unnai valvinaiyēn irandu kanamē sollinēn idu sōrēl kaṇḍāy punamēviya pūndaṇ tuḻāy alangal inamēdum ilānai adaivadumē*

- *manamē unnai* – Am I not calling you as if you are slow, while you are the cause for my mōkśam and is ahead of me in reaching him? While love towards bhagavān is natural for you, I am telling you this due to my helpless state.You who are ahead of me and who need to be slowed down by me as said in [periya tiruvandādi 1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/10/periya-thiruvandhadhi-1/) “*munduṟṟa nenjē iyaṟṟuvāy emmodu nī kūdi*” (Oh heart who has gone ahead (of me)! You too join me and praise him with me).
- *val vinaiyēn* – I have committed the sin of being unable to wait for the eventual attaining of bhagavat viśayam. I don’t need to pray to you \[because of any shortcoming in you\]; I am praying only due to my great desire.
- *irandu kanamē sonnēn* – I held on to your divine feet and firmly told. He is similar to maṇakkāl nambi in praying and instructing \[maṇakkāl nambi showed great mercy to āḷavandār by praying for an opportunity to teach him\].
- *idu sōrēl kaṇḍāy* – Even if I told you “Love towards bhagavān is not beneficial; give it up”, don’t lose it! kanam – gold. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says “I have told you the highest principle”. As said in [periya tiruvandādi 14](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/10/periya-thiruvandhadhi-14/) “*sāyāl kariyānai* …” (āḻvār telling his mind – How lowly are you to approach [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is so great?)
- *idu sōrēl* – His mind asks āḻvār “What are you talking about here?”,
- *punam …* – Reaching the greatly enjoyable emperumān. Due to wearing the garland made of tiruttuḻāy which grew on its own land, he has no match. One who has this tuḷasi garland on his shoulder, is hailed as sarvādika (the greatest of all). Once during tirumuḷaic cāṟṟu (ankurārpaṇam which marks the commencement of a major utsavam), nanjīyar  mercifully recited this pāsuram. Since he had the previous day’s celebration, *kaiyār cakkaram* (*āḻvār tirunāḷ* – [sēnai mudaliyār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vishwaksenar/) puṟappādu to check the streets) fresh in his mind, he mercifully said “To be *‘punamēviya pūndaṇ tuḻāy alangal inam ēdum ilān*‘ is because he was mercifully seen in yesterday’s puṟappādu” \[here nanjīyar sees and enjoys [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) through sēnai mudaliyār\]. *adaivadu sollinēn – idu sōrēl kaṇḍāy* – is the kriyā (active instruction); also, when asked “what are you saying to not lose?” – here āḻvār saying “*inam ēdum ilānai adaivadu*” can be considered as the kriyā.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 9.3.6. Adaivadum aniyar

*adaivadum aṇiyār malar mangai tōḷ midaivadum asurarkku vembōrgaḷē kadaivadum kadaluḷ amudam en manam udaivadum avaṟkē orungāgavē*

**Пословный перевод:**

malar – high family heritage of residing in lotus; mangai – lakshmi who is youthful, her; aṇi – by the ornaments; Ar – decorated; tōḷ – divine shoulder; adaivadum – to embrace; asurarkku – for asuras (who are unfavourable), difficult; vem – cruel; pōrgaḷē – battles; midaivadum – to engage in; kadaluḷ – in the ocean; amudam – amrutam (nectar); kadaivadum – churn; avaṟkē – for him only (who is with lakshmi, who is the remover of hurdles and bestover of desirable aspects); en manam – my heart; orungāgavē – in a singular manner; udaivadum – is breaking

**Перевод:**

**emperumān embraces the shoulders of lakshmi who has high family heritage of residing in lotus, who is youthful and whose shoulders are decorated with ornaments;  he engages in cruel battles which are difficult to face by asuras; he churned the ocean in the ocean; my heart is breaking in a singular manner for such emperumān only.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the sixth pāsuram, āḻvār becomes pleased thinking about how his mind meditates upon emperumān‘s activities and becomes weak, as he prayed.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. adaivadum aṇiyār malar mangai tōḷ midaivadum asurarkku vembōrgaḷē kadaivadum kadaluḷ amudam en manam udaivadum avaṟkē orungāgavē*

- *adaivadum aṇiyār malar mangai tōḷ* – To embrace the beautiful divine shoulder of periya pirāttiyār. Even if assumes viśvarūpam (universal form), he cannot move beyond her shoulder \[in other words, he is not superior to the beauty of pirātti’s shoulders\].
- *aṇiyār malar mangai* –  He would embrace the shoulder of periya pirāttiyār as said in tiruvāimoḻi 10.10.2 “*mārvattu mālai*” (garland on his chest); she will remain the ornament for his divine chest, without any shortcoming in enjoyability.
- *midaivadum asurarkku vem pōrgaḷ* – This is the offering he gives to make her embrace him. She embraces as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 30.40 “*bhartāram pariśasvajē”* (tightly embraced her husband) \[after killing the rākśasas\]. Also said as – he engages in cruel battles with the enemies of his devotees; also said as – he is constantly thinking about the ways to annihilate them.
- *kadaivadum kadaluḷ amudam* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying “[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is churning the ocean for the benefit of those who see worldly benefits” or “he churned the ocean to get periya pirāttiyār for himself”. āḻvār explained how emperumān embraces pirātti, the offering given for that and the efforts he takes up to attain her. These are the reasons for āḻvār’s heart-break.
- *en manam …* – My heart becomes broken in a singular manner for [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who has such activities. As he churned the snow \[milk\] ocean, his heart started breaking apart. A very skillful person, while trying to grab the wealth of a cowardly person, would first grab the wealth of a brave person by force, which will make the cowardly person  hand over his wealth voluntarily; similarly, as emperumān placed a pestle in the middle of the ocean, which is a huge entity and grabbed its life \[nectar\], [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s divine heart started breaking.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 9.3.7. Agam ser

*āgam sēr narasingam adāgi ōr āgam vaḷḷugirāl piḷandān uṟai māga vaigundam kāṇbadaṟku en manam ēgam eṇṇum irāp pagal inṟiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

āgam – in a form; sēr – placed; narasingam adu āgi – having both naratva (human’s aspects) and simhatva (lion’s aspects); ōr – unparalleled; āgam – chest; vaḷ – bent; ugirāl – with nail; piḷandān – one who tore apart; uṟai – residing; māga vaigundam – śrīvaikuṇṭam; kāṇbadaṟku – to see; en manam – my heart; irāp pagal – night and day; inṟi – without any difference; ēgam – in a singular manner; eṇṇum – desired

**Перевод:**

**emperumān having placed both human’s aspects and lion’s aspects in a form, tore apart hiraṇya’s unparalleled chest with his bent nail; my heart without any difference between night and day desired in a singular manner to see śrīvaikuṇṭam which is the residence of such emperumān.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the seventh pāsuram, āḻvār says “My heart desires to go to paramapadam which is unreachable for anyone, and where such emperumān with many qualities, is residing. What shall I do for its desire?”*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. āgam sēr narasingam adāgi ōr āgam vaḷḷugirāl piḷandān uṟai māga vaigundam kāṇbadaṟku en manam ēgam eṇṇum irāp pagal inṟiyē*

- *āgam sēr …* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying most aptly joined narasimha form with human’s aspects and lion’s aspects just as an appropriate mixture of milk and sugar; also explained as, āḻvār saying, how narasimha’s form has been placed in his heart; as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 60.1 “*smaran rāghava bāṇānām*” (thinking about rāghava’s arrows), how [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) was placed in his heart without any scope for forgetting him; or āḻvār saying when emperumān appeared with a combined human form and lion form, how pleasing that was for his heart.
- *ōr āgam* – Unparalleled strong body.
- *vaḷ ugirāl* – Sharp nail; or bent nail.
- *piḷandān uṟai* – The eternal abode of the one who effortlessly tore apart hiraṇya.
- *māga vaigundam* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s heart desired to see the cave where such narasimham is residing. It is said as “*paramākāśam*” (supreme sky) \[mā kam – great sky\]. My heart, without any break, is constantly desiring for this.
- *irāp pagal inṟiyē* – For worldly people, there are different tasks for night and day; for [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/), this is the only activity at all times; as sītāp pirātti thought about śrī ayōdyā as her own residence as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 33.17 “*samā dvādaśa tatrāham rāghavasya nivēśanē*” (I enjoyed all pleasures in śrī rāma’s residence for twelve years), āḻvār’s heart considers paramapadam to be its own residence.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 9.3.8. Inrip poga

*inṟip pōga iru vinaiyungeduttu onṟi ākkai pugāmai uyyak koḷvān ninṟa vēngadam nīḷ nilattuḷḷadu senṟu dēvargaḷ kai toḻuvārgaḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

iru vinaiyum – karma in the form puṇya (virtues) and pāpa (vices); inṟi – losing its existence; pōga – to eliminate; keduttu – destroy; onṟi – attached with acit, to be not seen separately; ākkai pugāmai – to not enter bodies of dēva (celestial) etc \[manuśya (human), tiryak (animal), stāvara (plant)\]; uyyak koḷvān – one who enslaves and uplifts; ninṟa – standing to act; vēngadam – tirumalā; nīḷ nilattu – in this praiseworthy earth; uḷḷadu – is present; senṟu – reaching; kai toḻuvārgaḷ – those who worship; dēvargaḷ – (they are not humans;) aren’t they dēvas?

**Перевод:**

**emperumān will destroy and eliminate karma in the form of puṇya (virtues) and pāpa (vices) to lose its existence, and will make the ātmās not enter bodies of dēva (celestial) etc which are attached with acit, to be not seen separately; such emperumān who enslaves and uplifts everyone, is standing to act \[as necessary\] in tirumalā, in this praiseworthy earth; aren’t those who reach and worship him there, dēvas?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the eighth pāsuram, āḻvār meditates upon emperumān‘s act of presenting himself in tirumalā which is at close proximity, so that one who desires to see him need not go all the way up to tirunādu (paramapadam), praises those who have the ability to walk up to tirumalā and reveals his lack of ability to do so.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. inṟip pōga iru vinaiyungeduttu onṟi ākkai pugāmai uyyak koḷvān ninṟa vēngadam nīḷ nilattuḷḷadu senṟu dēvargaḷ kai toḻuvārgaḷē*

- *inṟip pōga iru vinaiyum keduttu* – To fully destroy and eliminate karma which is in the form of puṇya and pāpa, along with the trace. Only when one tries with his own efforts to eliminate karma will there be residue.
- *onṟi …* – Even after that, if the ruci (taste) and vāsanā (impressions) remain, ātmā will go and mix with acit (matter), enter a body and will have to undergo the troubles which arise from that; not having to go through that.
- *uyyak koḷvān* … – As said in tiruviruttam 1 “*uyir aḷippān*” (give life), tirumalā where he is standing with the vow to protect everyone.
- *nīḷ nilattuḷḷadu* – Since the earth has tirumalā on it, it is praiseworthy; being on such earth.

When asked “what is the benefit?” [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says,

- *senṟu …* – Those who can walk up to tirumalā are greatly fortunate; as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 64.69 “*natē manuśyā dēvāstē …*” (Those who will see śrī rāma’s beautiful form after fifteen years, are not manuśyas, but dēvas), āḻvār is meditating upon [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s śeela guṇam (quality of simplicity) and saying. For those who are blinded by love, being unable to reach is the same irrespective of the destination being paramapadam or tirumalā.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 9.3.9. Toludu mamalar

*toḻudu mā malar nīr sudar dūbangoṇḍu eḻudum ennum idu migai ādalin paḻudil tol pugaḻp pāmbaṇaip paḷḷiyāy! taḻuvum āṟaṟiyēn una tāḷgaḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

mā – praiseworthy; malar – flower; nīr – water in the form of arghya (offering to wash hands) etc; sudar dūbam – dīpa (lamp) and dūpa (incense); koṇḍu – gathering; toḻudu – to worship; eḻudu – we will set out; ennum idu – this; migai ādalin – due to being superfluous; paḻudu – fault (of being difficult to worship); il – not having; tol pugaḻ – having natural, ultimate simplicity; pāmbu – tiruvantāḻvān (ādi śēśa); aṇai – having as mattress; paḷḷiyāy – Oh one who is resting, being eternally united with ādi śēśa!; una tāḷgaḷ – your divine feet; taḻuvum – being united; āṟu – method; aṟiyēn – I don’t know

**Перевод:**

**Since it is superfluous to think “we will set out to worship you by gathering praiseworthy flower, water in the form of arghya etc, lamp and incense”, you are not having any fault (of being difficult to worship) but you are having natural, ultimate simplicity; I don’t know the method to unite with your divine feet, Oh one who is resting on tiruvanantāḻvān (ādi śēśa) and having him as mattress and being eternally united with him!**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the ninth pāsuram, āḻvār says “Even if I surrender unto your divine feet, as said in ‘anyat pūrṇāt apām kumbāt’, as you become pleased easily even by the favourable attitude of the one who surrendered, it is difficult to perform any service for you due to your simplicity”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. Alternatively – some explain “āḻvār is speaking about his disqualification in these three pāsurams \[8, 9, 10\]”; but that is not there for āḻvār after tiruvāimoḻi 8.8 “kaṇgaḷ sivandu“. Some others explain “āḻvār is speaking about the upāya bhāvam (being the means) of emperumān, where praying to him to attain something, is itself considered superfluous \[he will do even without praying\]”. These are not the focus here. Our ācāryas explain this as “āḻvār speaking about emperumān’s śeela guṇam (simplicity) which will make one melt in his presence and hence one will not be able to serve him properly”. toḻudu mā malar nīr sudar dūbangoṇḍu eḻudum ennum idu migai ādalin paḻudil tol pugaḻp pāmbaṇaip paḷḷiyāy! taḻuvum āṟaṟiyēn una tāḷgaḷē*

- *toḻudu …* – When we think “Let us offer praiseworthy flower etc, serve him and seek uplifting”, doesn’t your simplicity make such efforts look superfluous? You are as explained in mahābhāratam udyōga parvam 89.13 “*anyat pūrṇāt apām kumbāt*” (kriṣṇa does not desire for anything more than a pot filled with water).
- *ādalin* – Since you are ultimately simple. Instead of having the fault of “being difficult to worship”, you are having the natural greatness of being easily vorśippable. Oh one who is being united with ādiśēśa due to such simplicity!
- *taḻuvum āṟu aṟiyēn* – I don’t know the means to unite with your divine feet. Due to my weakness, it is difficult to reach first; even if I reach, I will be unable to do any service, thinking about your ultimate simplicity.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 9.3.10. Tala tamaraiyan

*tāḷa tāmaraiyān unadundiyān vāḷ koḷ nīḷ maḻuvāḷi unnāgattān āḷarāyt toḻuvārum amarargaḷ nāḷum en pugaḻgō un seelamē?*

**Пословный перевод:**

tāḷa – having stem; tāmaraiyān – brahmā who was born in lotus; unadu – your; undiyān – has your navel as the abode; vāḷ – glow; koḷ – having; nīḷ – big; maḻu – axe; āḷi – rudra who rules over; un āgattān – is on one side of your divine form; āḷar āy – servitors like nityasūris; toḻuvārum – those who worship; amarargaḷ – groups of other dēvatās who are prayōjanāntaraparas (seekers of benefits other than kainkaryams); un – your; seelam – simplicity; nāḷum – even if tried forever; en – how; pugaḻkō – will I praise?

**Перевод:**

**Simple translation (based on vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar‘s 12000 padi)**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the tenth pāsuram, āḻvār says “You are being the refuge even for lowly dēvas who don’t know about servitude; the simplicity of your divine feet cannot be praised enough even if I tried forever”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. pāsuram tāḷa tāmaraiyān unadundiyān vāḷ koḷ nīḷ maḻuvāḷi unnāgattān āḷarāyt toḻuvārum amarargaḷ nāḷum en pugaḻgō un seelamē?*

- *tāḷa tāmaraiyān un undiyān* – brahmā who has lotus flower as his birth place, resides on your navel. You gave your body to the one who has the pride of being born in lotus flower.
- *vāḷ …* – rudra, who has the glowing axe which will complete any task which is taken up, resides on one part of your divine body. He is not exclusively surrendered to you with flowers as said in [tiruppaḷḷiyeḻucci 10](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/01/thiruppalliyezhuchchi-10-kadimalar/) “*todai otta tuḷavamum kūdaiyum*” (properly prepared tiruttuḻāy and flower basket).
- *āḷar āyt toḻuvārum amarargaḷ* – dēvatās seek refuge unto you as servitors. The service of nityasūris is carried out by dēvas due to being comparable as “*amara*” (immortal) \[nityasūris are eternally immortal, but dēvatās are immortal for a certain limited period of time\], though they consider themselves to be lords.
- *nāḷum …* – Even if all the times to come are combined and presented to me, to let me praise you, is your śeela guṇam such that it could be easily praised to the full extent?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 9.3.11. Seelam ellaiyilan

*seelam ellai ilān adimēl aṇi kōla nīḷ kurugūrc catakōpan sol mālai āyirattuḷ ivai pattinin pālar vaigundam ēṟudal pānmaiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

seelam ellai ilān – one who has boundless simplicity/qualities; adi mēl – on the divine feet; aṇi – decorated; kōlam – beautiful form; nīḷ – very vast; kurugūr – leader of āḻvārtirunagari; satakōpan – āḻvār‘s; sol – with words; mālai – being garland; āyirattuḷ – among thousand pāsurams; ivai pattinin – this decad’s; pālar – those who have close proximity (either by learning the pāsurams or their meanings); vaigundam – in śrīvaikuṇṭam; ēṟudal – ascending; pānmai – this is natural

**Перевод:**

**āḻvār, the leader of very vast āḻvārtirunagari, which has a decorated, beautiful form, spoke this decad which is a garland of words among the thousand pāsurams, on the divine feet of one who has boundless simplicity/qualities; for those who have close proximity to such decad, ascending to śrīvaikuṇṭam is natural.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the end, āḻvār says “For those who learnt this decad, it is not surprising to reach paramapadam; it is apt”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. seelam ellai ilān adimēl aṇi kōla nīḷ kurugūrc catakōpan sol mālai āyirattuḷ ivai pattinin pālar vaigundam ēṟudal pānmaiyē*

- *seelam ellai ilān* – On the divine feet of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who has boundless simplicity/qualities. His great simplicity is what is explained in this decad; [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is summarising it here.
- *aṇi kōla nīḷ kurugūrc catakōpan sol mālai* – āḻvār who has tirunagari which is abundantly beautiful. Alternatively – as “*kōḷ nīḷ*” is present, “*aṇi*” can be read along in “*adi mēl aṇi – mālai*” (the garland which decorates the divine feet).
- *āyirattuḷ ivai pattinin pālar* – Those who are close to this decad. By having some proximiity through plain recital, memorising it or meditating upon the meanings.
- *vaigundam …* – Ascending to paramapadam is apt \[sure to go\]. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) greatly desired to go to paramapadam as said in tiruvāimoḻi 9.3.7 “*māga vaigundam kāṇbadaṟku ēgam eṇṇum*“; for those who are associated with this pāsuram, it need not be prayed for, but it will occur certainly. The wealth of the father will naturally belong to the son, due to the relationship \[we will inherit whatever āḻvār attained, as his children/descendants\].

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 9.4 Maiyar karunganni

## 9.4.1. Maiyar karunganni

*maiyār karungaṇṇi kamala malar mēl seyyāḷ tirumārvinil sēr tirumālē! veyyār sudarāḻi suri sangam ēndum kaiyā! unnaik kāṇak karudum en kaṇṇē*

**Пословный перевод:**

maiyār – having decorated with black pigment (for the eyelashes); karu – having natural darkness to be said as in “asitēkśaṇā”; kaṇṇi – one who is having divine eyes; kamala malar mēl – residing on a lotus flower; seyyāḷ – lakshmi who is having reddish complexion (due to being in the colour of lotus); tirumārvinil – (being immersed) in the beauty of his divine chest; sēr – to be united; tiru – towards her; mālē – being the one who shows great affection; vey Ar – very cruel; sudar – having fire; āḻi – tiruvāḻi (divine chakra); suri – having circular marks (where the appearance itself will destroy the enemies and bring enjoyment for the devotees); sangam – śrī pāncajanyam (divine conch); ēndum – carrying; kaiyā – Oh one who is having divine hands!; unnai – you (who are śriya:pati and the possessor of Sanka, chakra and gadā); en – my; kaṇ – (desirous) eyes; kāṇa – to see constantly (like nityasūris do); karudum – are desiring

**Перевод:**

**lakshmi who is having divine eyes which are naturally dark to be said as in “asitēkśaṇā” and are decorated with black pigment, who is residing on a lotus flower and is having reddish complexion, is united in your beautiful divine chest; you show great affection towards her; oh one who is having divine hands carrying the very cruel, fiery divine chakra and śrī pāncajanyam which is having circular marks! My eyes are desiring to see you constantly.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the first pāsuram, āḻvār mercifully highlights the desire of his cakśu: (eyes) which feel “I should see emperumān who is śriya:pati (consort of śrī mahālakśmi)”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. maiyār karungaṇṇi kamala malar mēl seyyāḷ tirumārvinil sēr tirumālē! veyyār sudarāḻi suri sangam ēndum kaiyā! unnaik kāṇak karudum en kaṇṇē*

- *maiyār karum kaṇṇi* – Those who desire to attain him, seek him through her and when they attain him, they would serve in that togetherness only.
- *maiyār karum kaṇṇi* – The divine eyes are so beautiful naturally that nothing else is needed for decoration; now, the black pigment \[anjanam\] is applied for auspiciousness. When it is already said as “karungaṇṇi” (dark-eyed), “maiyār” (decorated with black pigment) is said to indicate that the black pigment is applied only for auspiciousness.
- *kamala malar mēl seyyāḷ* – This is how tender she is.
- *tirumārvu …* – Oh one who has the chest which can hold her feet if the fragrance and pollen (of lotus) become too hot for her to remain! Even after having such greatness, she will not look beyond his chest. Since the whole chest is so enjoyable, one need not look beyond it.
- *tirumālē* – He too, will be madly in love with all of her limbs just as she is with his chest. His eyes are reddish. Since he is constantly glancing at her, the redness from his eyes becomes fixed on her divine body and hence her divine body is reddish in colour; since she is constantly glancing at him, the blackness from her eyes becomes fixed on his divine body and hence his divine body is blackish in colour. Her eyes are cool \[hence the black colour\]; his eyes have abundance of vātsalyam (motherly forbearance) \[hence the red colour\]; it is due to their togetherness, he has abundance of vātsalyam. Hence both of them will have both coolness and motherly forbearance, due to their love for each other. When the messenger (hanuman) desired to destroy the servants of rāvaṇa, she said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 116-45 “*nakaścin nāparādyati*” (there is none who has not committed a wrongful deed); with her \[who is so compassionate\], he argues saying as in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 4.9.2 “*ennadiyār adu seyyār*” (My devotees would not do anything wrong);  hence, both of them have both the qualities perfectly. Even while in separation, these qualities will remain perfectly in them.
- *tirumārvinil sēr* – While enjoying his divine chest eternally, she would worry as someone who newly attained him will feel, saying as in tiruvāimoḻi 6.10.10 “*agalagillēn iṟaiyum*” (I will not leave even for a moment). This is shown by “*sēr*” (uniting), being in present tense.
- *veyyār …* – Just as the lotus in her hand is enjoyable for him, the divine weapons in his hands are pleasing to her. They are the tools with which he destroys the enemies of his devotees, for her pleasure. The radiant divine chakra which will manifest great cruelty on the enemies and śrī pāncajanyam which can be seen without taking the eyes off and not having to do anything other than its presence.
- *ēndum kaiyā* – Neither just the weapons, nor just his hands; [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) desires for the combination of both. He says in [tiruvāimoḻi 6.9.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/05/thiruvaimozhi-6-9-1-niray-nilanay/) “*kūrārāḻi veṇ sangēndi – vārāy*” (you come, holding the sharp chakra and white conch).
- *unnai* – You who are having lakshmi as your consort, divine weapons and divine form. This is how [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s desirable entity is.
- *kāṇak karudum* – My eyes desire to see your divine form which is described in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 114.15 “*Sanka chakra gadādara: – śrīvatsa vakśā:*” (maṇḍōdari says “One who is holding conch, disc and mace, who has śrīvatsa mole on your chest”). Those who desire for him, do not desire him to fulfil some goal, but just to see him. It is said in [nānmugan tiruvandādi 39](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/07/nanmugan-thiruvandhadhi-39/) “*tiruvēngadattānaik kāṇa*” (to see tiruvēngadamudaiyān) and in siṟiya tirumadal “*kārār tirumēni kāṇumaḷavum pōy*” (going to see the dark, divine form of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)). nityasūris too, constantly see emperumān’s divine form only. Those who are here \[in material realm\] will be fully focussed on seeing his divine form as said in amalanādipirān 10 “*aṇi arangan en amudinaik kaṇḍa kaṇgaḷ maṟṟonṟinaik kāṇāvē*” (My eyes which have seen you, śrī ranganāta, my nectar, will not see anything else); those who are there \[in spiritual realm\] will also be focussed on seeing his divine form as said in cāndōjña upaniśat “*ētadēvāmrutam druśtvā trupyanti*” (dēvas (nityasūris) do not eat; they drink this nectar and remain satisfied).
- *en kaṇṇē* – The difference between samsāris’ \[materialistic perons’\] desire and [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s desire is the same as āḻvār’s desire and his eyes’ desire. They have the greatness of being āḻvār’s eyes \[the primary sense\].

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 9.4.2. Kanne! unnai

*kaṇṇē! unnaik kāṇak karudi ennenjam eṇṇē koṇḍa sindaiyadāy ninṟiyambuim viṇṇōr munivarkkenṟum kāṇbariyāyai nāṇṇādoḻiyēn enṟu nān aḻaippanē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kaṇṇē – Oh my vision (being the one who helps me see)!; unnai – you (who are the means) only; kāṇa – to constantly see and enjoy; karudi – considered; en nenjam – my heart; eṇṇē koṇḍa – in many ways; sindaiyadāy – desiring; iyambum – will cry out; nān – I (who am the owner of the senses); viṇṇōr – for brahmā et al; munivarkku – for sanaka et al; enṟum – always; kāṇbu ariyāyai – you who are difficult to be seen; naṇṇādu oḻiyēn – will not give up before attaining; enṟu – being determined; aḻaippan – will call out (due to the great eagerness)

**Перевод:**

**Oh my vision! My heart will cry out only considering to see you and enjoy you, desiring in many ways. I will call up being determined and say “I will not give up before attaining you, who are always difficult to be seen by brahmā et al and sanaka et al”.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the second pāsuram, āḻvār mercifully explains his and his heart’s desire.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. kaṇṇē! unnaik kāṇak karudi ennenjam eṇṇē koṇḍa sindaiyadāy ninṟiyambuim viṇṇōr munivarkkenṟum kāṇbariyāyai nāṇṇādoḻiyēn enṟu nān aḻaippanē*

- *kaṇṇē* – Oh my vision!
- *unnaik kāṇak karudi* – To see you who are greatly enjoyable.  He is planning to see his eyes \[[bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) who is his vision\] with his \[external\] eyes. He says that the means to see [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) and the object that is seen are both emperumān himself; it is said in subhālōpanisat “*cakśuśca draśtavyanca nārāyaṇa:*” (both the eyes and the object which is seen are nārāyaṇa). [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is of the nature to attain emperumān through himself. For āḻvār, just as there is a norm for the goal which is attained, there is a norm for the means as well.
- *en nenjam* – The heart of samsāris will be the cause for bondage and will remain too eager in worldly pleasures; the heart of those who were blessed with divine knowledge and devotion by [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) himself as said in tiruvāimoḻi 1.1.1 “*mayarvaṟa madinalam aruḷinan*“, will say as in tiruvāimoḻi 1.1.1 “*toḻudeḻu*” (worship and rise).
- *eṇṇē …* – Having countless desires; having many desires such as “I should see, I should have sorrows of not seeing him, removed and I should serve him”.
- *ninṟu iyambum* – Will constantly call out. It \[mind\] is assuming the actions \[of soul\] upon itself. By “*kaṇṇē*“, it is established that he is the means; by “*unnaik kāṇa*“, it is established that he is the goal; by “*eṇṇē koṇḍa*“, the practice of a qualified person who thinks “I should attain the goal through the means”, is explained.
- *viṇṇōr …* – Am I giving up thinking that this is the situation only for my heart? Will I not attain you who are always difficult to be seen for brahmā et al and sanaka et al? I am calling out thinking “I will certainly attain him”. How is he thinking that he will certainly attain him? I am calling out thinking “Since they are living in distinguished abodes and are having their own abilities, there is a possibility for delay in attaining him; but for those who have no abilities, will there be any delay?”
- *naṇṇādu oḻiyēn* – I cannot sustain myself if I don’t attain him.  This is āyttān’s explanation. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is revealing his mahāviśvāsam (unflinching faith) in “*naṇṇādu oḻiyēn*“. Since they \[brahmā et al\] are residing in distinguished abodes, they can be rescued through a proper process \[such as bhakti yōgam, which will take a long time to fructify\]; unlike them, āḻvār who is caught in samsāram, should be rescued quickly. I am in the place which is apt for rescue; I also desired to be rescued; he is the saviour; if he protected me, he will be the beneficiary; this being the situation, what is the reason \[for me to suffer here\]?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 9.4.3. Alaikkinra adinayen

*aḻaikkinṟa adi nāyēn nāy kūḻai vālāl kuḻaikkinṟadupōla en uḷḷam kuḻaiyum maḻaikku anṟu kunṟam eduttu ānirai kāttāy! piḻaikkinṟadaruḷ enṟu pēduṟuvanē*

**Пословный перевод:**

aḻaikkinṟa – calling out (out of great desire); adi – being without refuge and having such relationship with you; nāyēn – me who is inferior to cause disrepute to you, my; en uḷḷam – my heart which is filled with sorrow; nāy – dog; kūḻai – small; vālāl – wagging its tail; kuḻaikkinṟadupōla – as it will reveal; kuḻaiyum – breaking; anṟu – that day (when he caused distress through hail); maḻaikku – as a remedy for that rain; kunṟam – hill; eduttu – lifted; A – cows (which don’t even know to pray for protection); nirai – herds; kāttāy – oh one who protected!; aruḷ – boundless mercy; piḻaikkinṟadu – ignoring; enṟu pēduṟuvan – I am worried

**Перевод:**

**I am calling out for you, being without refuge and having such relationship with you; I am inferior to cause disrepute to you and my heart is filled with sorrow; as a dog will reveal its thoughts by wagging its small tail, my heart is breaking; oh one who protected the herds of cows by lifting the hill as a remedy for the rain on that day! I am worried to see that your boundless mercy is ignoring me. Also implies that you are missing your mercy \[towards me\].**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the third pāsuram, after āḻvār called out to see emperumān, he was with great distress and still emperumān did not arrive; he feels pained thinking “is he not having the quality of protecting those who are without means and anguished?”*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. aḻaikkinṟa adi nāyēn nāy kūḻai vālāl kuḻaikkinṟadupōla en uḷḷam kuḻaiyum maḻaikku anṟu kunṟam eduttu ānirai kāttāy! piḻaikkinṟadaruḷ enṟu pēduṟuvanē*

- *aḻaikkinṟa adi nāyēn …* – Being unqualified and inferior, I am still calling out for you due to my distress. He cannot avoid calling out for him, due to the taste towards him. But if he attains, he thinks he will cause disrepute to [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/). A dog will reveal its desire to its owner by its tail only; if the tail is small, it will be difficult to inform its thoughts; similarly, my heart is paining here. With this, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying that his sorrow is beyond words. Also implies that though āḻvār is not having any means, he is still desiring for emperumān.
- *maḻaikku …* – Oh one who protected the covherds and the cows by seeing their distress as the reason, when indra rained hail!
- *piḻaikkinṟadu aruḷ enṟu pēduṟuvanē* – [āḷavandār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/alavandhar/) mercifully explains “I am worried ‘you are going to lose your great quality of protecting everyone by not help me’ “. [emperumānār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/emperumanar/) mercifully heard that and said – the meaning is nice; but, it does not fit [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s current state of mind; hence āḻvār is saying “I am worried thinking ‘Am I outside this great quality of lifting the hill to protect the cows and covherds from getting affected by the rain?’ “

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.
