## 9.4.4. Uruvadidu enru

*uṟuvadu idu enṟu unakkātpattu nin kaṇ peṟuvadedukol enṟu pēdaiyēn nenjam maṟugal seyyum vānavar tānavarkkenṟum aṟivadariya ariyāya ammānē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

vānavar – dēvas, celestial beings who are favourable; tānavarkku – and dānavas, demoniac beings who are unfavourable, without any difference; enṟum – always; aṟivadu – to know; ariya – being difficult; ari āya – being narasimha; ammānē – Oh lord!; idu – this state of śēśatvam (servitude); uṟuvadu – apt; enṟu – establishing well; unakku – for you (who is the recipient of such servitude); ātpattu – allowing me to be a servitor; nin kaṇ – towards you (who is the lord); peṟuvadu – to get the result; edu kol – which one (kainkaryam matching my nature or being in this samsāra)?; enṟu – as; pēdaiyēn – ignorant me (who cannot accept that whatever you grant is apt), my; nenjam – heart; maṟugal seyyum – is becoming agitated

**Перевод:**

**Oh lord narasimha who is always difficult to know for dēvas, celestial beings who are favourable and dānavas, demoniac beings who are unfavourable, without any difference! Establishing well that this state of śēśatvam is apt, allowing me to be a servitor for you, being an ignorant person, my heart is becoming agitated thinking “which result will I get towards you?”**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fourth pāsuram, āḻvār says “Seeing that you are difficult to be attained by dēvas and asuras, my heart is becoming agitated”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. uṟuvadu idu enṟu unakkātpattu nin kaṇ peṟuvadedukol enṟu pēdaiyēn nenjam maṟugal seyyum vānavar tānavarkkenṟum aṟivadariya ariyāya ammānē!*

- *uṟuvadu idu enṟu* – Considering that this servitude is best.
- *unakku ātpattu* – Engaging in service to you. If one knows “our true nature is to be subservient to bhagavān”, the natural result is service to such bhagavān.
- *nin kaṇ peṟuvadu edu kol enṟu* – Wondering what I am going to get from you. What is the reason for [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) who has full understanding about his own nature, who knows that kainkaryam (service to bhagavān) is the best, who knows “īśvara will not give anything else \[other than kainkaryam\] for ananyaprayōjana (one who does not seek any other benefit)”, to say “what will I get from you?” ? āḻvār is really wondering “Will [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) let me remain in this samsāram saying ‘I will liberate you when the time is ripe’ or will he manifest himself quickly understanding my great desire?”
- *pēdaiyēn nenjam maṟugal seyyum* – My heart which does not have the knowledge “I will get the result that was desired by me”, became agitated.

When asked “What is the reason for such agitation?” [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says “Heart’s lack of knowledge is the reason; and you ([emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)) too are a reason”

- *vānavar …* – As said in jitantē stōtram “*dēvānām dānavānām*” (for the celestials and the demoniac people), being the lord for both of them, he is difficult to be known by both dēvas and asuras, but still, in that same state, you revealed yourself to a small child (prahlādāḻvān); not knowing, which group am I part of? This is similar to arjuna asking kriṣṇa “Which group am I part of?” after kriṣṇa explained the difference between dēvas and asuras in śrī bhagavat gītā. What was the remedy  given by [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) for this? He manifested his saulabhyam (easy approacability). emperumān says – as you say that I am easily approachable for my devotees, and if you are in that group of devotees, is it not clear that you can easily attain me?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 9.4.5. Ariyaya ammanai

*ariyāya ammānai amarar pirānaip periyānaip piramanai mun padaittānai varivāḷ aravin aṇaip paḷḷikoḷginṟa kariyān kaḻal kāṇak karudum karuttē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ari āya – one who destroys the enemies; ammānai – being the lord; amarar – nityasūris who have no enemies; pirānai – being the one who gives joy; periyānai – having the glory of not being able to be enjoyed by them too, by estimating the limits; mun – even before, first; piramanai – brahmā; padaittānai – who created; vari – stripes; vāḷ – radiance; aravin aṇai – in the divine serpent mattress; paḷḷi koḷginṟa – mercifully resting; kariyān – (contrasting the mattress’s complexion) having black form; kaḻal – on the divine feet; kāṇa – to see; karuttu – my buddi (intellect); karudum – is thinking

**Перевод:**

**emperumān being the lord who destroys the enemies and who gives joy to nityasūris who have no enemies, who first created brahmā, is mercifully resting on the serpernt mattress which has stripes and radiance; my intellect is thinking to see the divine feet of such emperumān. kariyānai is shortened as kariyān. kariyāntanai is also an accepted way of reciting \[in place of kariyān kaḻal\].**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fifth pāsuram, āḻvār says “My heart desires to see the divine feet of sarvēśvara who is naturally inclined towards being with his devotees”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. ariyāya ammānai amarar pirānaip periyānaip piramanai mun padaittānai varivāḷ aravin aṇaip paḷḷikoḷginṟa kariyān kaḻal kāṇak karudum karuttē*

- *ammānai* – [sarvēśvara](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/).
- *amarar pirānai* – The benefactor who reveals himself to nityasūris and lets them to enjoy him.
- *periyānai* – Their svarūpa (nature), stiti (existence) are at his disposal and he cannot be conceived by them \[fully\].
- *piramanai mun padaittānai* – One who is the father of caturmukha (brahmā), “*ari āya”* (as narasimha) should be recited after these. In the created world, when prahlādāḻvān vowed \[for the presence of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) in the pillar\], immediately, emperumān incarnated, transforming himself \[into a lion-human form\]
- *vari vāḷ …* – Not only he helps his devotees, he is also naturally inclined towards being together with them.
- *vari vāḷ aravu* – The serpent which has beauty and radiance. vari – beauty.
- *kariyān* – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) mercifully rests just as a dark cloud is resting on whitish complexioned tiruvanantāḻvān.
- *kāṇak karudum karuttē* – My mind was eager to see. It is desiring to see his divine feet which are having contrasting complexion \[red colour\] to his divine form \[black colour\] which in turn is having contrasting complexion \[white colour\] of the mattress.

## 9.4.6. Karutte! unnai

*karuttē! unnaik kāṇak karudi en nenjattu iruttāga iruttinēn dēvargatkellām viruttā! viḷangum sudarc cōdi uyarattu oruttā! unnai uḷḷum en uḷḷam ugandē*

**Пословный перевод:**

karuttē – Oh strength of my heart who gives me strength and does not let me become weak!; unnaik kāṇa – to see you and enjoy you; karudi – desired; en nenjattu – in my heart; iruttāga – to not get up (and leave); iruttinēn – placed; dēvargatku ellām – for all nityasūris; viruttā – being the eldest leader; viḷangum – radiant; sudar – having lustre; sōdi – luminous; uyarattu – in paramapadam, which is the supreme abode (as said in “viśvata: pruśtēśu saravata: pruśtēśu“); oruttā – oh one who is present as the distinguished lord!; en – my; uḷḷam – heart; unnai – you (who is the ultimate goal); ugandu – with great love; uḷḷum – enjoyed internally

**Перевод:**

**Oh strength of my heart who gives me strength and does not let me become weak! I desired to see you and enjoy you and placed you in my heart to not let you get up and leave. Oh one who is the eldest leader of all nityasūris, who is the luminous entity having radiant lustre and who is present as the distinguished lord in paramapadam which is the supreme abode! My heart enjoyed you internally with great love.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the sixth pāsuram, āḻvār mercifully explains how his heart is joyfully enjoying emperumān who mercifully entered his heart while he was desiring to see emperumān.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. karuttē! unnaik kāṇak karudi en nenjattu iruttāga iruttinēn dēvargatkellām viruttā! viḷangum sudarc cōdi uyarattu oruttā! unnai uḷḷum en uḷḷam ugandē*

- *karuttē unnaik kāṇak karudi* – You manifested yourself as I desired to see you, who are my strength; [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying that to attain [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), taste \[for him\] is the only requirement. Previously āḻvār said “*kaṇṇē unnaik kāṇak karudi*“; here, he is saying “*karuttē unnaik kāṇak karudi*“. āḻvār is desiring to physically see the entity \[emperumān\] who needs to be explained through artāpatti (inference from circumstances) due to anupapatti (lack of conclusive proof) \[since there should be someone with amazing knowledge to create this universe. prabhākara – philosopher who propagated artāpatti\] or who needs to be explained as beyond our senses through anumānam (inference) \[establishing through arguments that bhagavān is beyond our senses\]. For āḻvār, emperumān is the eyes \[knowledge\] and intellect \[strength\].
- *en nenjattu iruttāga iruttinēn* – I placed the steady lord in my unsteady heart just as he is present in paramapadam. If [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who was worried thinking “I have not got [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s acceptance to stay in his heart”, gets āḻvār’s acceptance, he will not leave even if he were pushed out. perumāḷ (śrī rāma) said in śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 94.15 “*yatīha śarata: anēkās tvayā sārdam aninditē*” (Oh faultless sītā! If I live with you and lakśmaṇa here for many years, I won’t have any sorrow) and śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 15.19 “*iha vatsyāmi saumitrē sārdamētēna pakśiṇā …*” (Oh lakśmaṇa! This abode is very pious; pure; has animals and birds; I will live with jatāyu here) – \[perumāḷ said\] we thought we will live under the care of our father; to fulfil the desire of our middle mother (kaikēyi), we could not do that; now, let us at least try to live under the care of jatāyu \[who is like our father\].
- *iruttāga* – Alternative explanation – I only pretend to be friendly towards [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 18.3 “*mithra bhāvēna*” (even if you (rāvaṇa) approach me as a friend).
- *dēvargatku ellām viruttā* – Oh one who is superior to even those who are considered as the most superior! In tamiḻ literature, the hero and heroine are referred to as “*kiḻavanum kiḻattiyum*” (viruttā – vrudda – elder). [āḻvārs](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/azhwars/) too have said as in tiruccanda viruttam 55 “*malark kiḻatti*” (śrī mahālakśmi who resides in the flower).
- *viḷangum sōdi* – As said in “*ata yadata:parō divō jyōtir dīpyatē*” (bhagavān is shining radiantly in paramapadam which is atop the prakruti maṇḍalam (material relam)), oh distinguished one who is residing in the radiant paramapadam which is always shining! prakāri (bhagavān) is only one, but prakāram (forms/bodies) are many.
- *unnai …* – My agitated heart joyfully enjoyed you who arrived quickly. The purpose for adjectives such as “*dēvargatkellām viruttā*“, “*viḷangum sudarccōdi uyarattoruttā*” is to explain that my heart became pleased after you let it enjoy you just as the leader of the superior ones in paramapadam you let them enjoy you.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 9.4.7. Ugande unnai

*ugandē unnai uḷlum en uḷḷattu agampāl agandān amarndē idangoṇḍa amalā! migundānavan mārvagalam iru kūṟā nagandāy narasingam adāya uruvē*

**Пословный перевод:**

agam tān – in the heart; amarndu – fitting well; idam koṇḍa – remained there considering it as your abode (and that is the goal); amalā – being luminous; migum – very strong boons, strength and arms; dānavan – hiraṇya, the asura, his; mārvu – in the chest; agalam – the vast space; iru kūṟā – to become two parts; nagam – nail; tāy – made to jump; narasingam adāya – narasimha; uruvē – oh one who has the form!; en uḷḷattu – in my heart; agampāl – inside; unnai ugandē – being pleased with you; uḷḷum – enjoyed

**Перевод:**

**You remained luminous in my heart fitting well and considering it as your abode.  Oh one who has the form of narasimha who made your nail to jump in the vast space of the chest of hiraṇya, the asura who has very strong boons and arms, and tore it to become two parts! My heart being pleased with you, enjoyed you inside.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the seventh pāsuram, āḻvār is praising emperumān, being pleased with his merciful act of eliminating āḻvār’s distress just as he mercifully eliminated śrī prahlādāḻvān’s distress.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. ugandē unnai uḷlum en uḷḷattu agampāl agandān amarndē idangoṇḍa amalā! migundānavan mārvagalam iru kūṟā nagandāy narasingam adāya uruvē*

- *ugandē unnai uḷḷum* – Instead of the joy which will end in sorrow of separation, my heart will enjoy you with singular focus.
- *en uḷḷattu* – My heart which is said as in tiruvāimoḻi 9.4.2 “*eṇṇē koṇḍa sindaiyadāy*” (desiring in many ways).
- *agam pāl agam tān* – Inside the heart. As said in [tiruvāimoḻi 2.4.7](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/03/thiruvaimozhi-2-4-7-ullul-avi/) “*uḷḷuḷ āvi*” (the soul which is inside the heart), the dried soul to become wet again.
- *amarndē* – Showing great desire as if it is his goal.
- *idam koṇḍa* – He fully pervaded in all the space available.
- *amalā* – Not only seeking for any goal other than the presence in [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s heart, but also not being present for any particular reason. “*eṇṇē koṇḍa sindaiyadāy*” is not considered as means.
- *migum dānavan* – The dānava who is unfavourable without any limit. Not only he negated the existence of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), he also hurt emperumān’s life line \[śrī prahlādāḻvān\]; it is said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 7.18](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/7-18/) “… *jñānītvātmaiva mē matam*” (All \[four\] of them are generous, but the jñāni is the one who sustains (me) – this is my principle) .
- *mārvu agalam iru kūṟā nagandāy* – Oh one who has the nail which can tear apart the vast-cested hiraṇya into two pieces! nagattāy is written as nagandāy.
- *narasingam adāya uruvē* – You are having the form which is described as in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 1.2.1 “*sadaikarūpa rūpāya*” (one who is having unchanging divine auspicious form), in this manner! You are having two forms \[lion and human\]! With this, it is explained that since [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) will arrive immediately on the vow of his devotees, just as he appeared from within a pillar, he pervaded everywhere in my ([āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s) heart, and similar to watering the dry lands, you fully allowed me to enjoy you.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 9.4.8. Uruvagiya

*uruvāgiya āṟu samayangatkellām poruvāgi ninṟān avan ellāp porutkum aruvāgiya ādiyait tēvargatkellām karuvāgiya kaṇṇanaik kaṇḍu koṇḍēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

uru āgiya – present based on superficial appearance; āṟu samayangatku ellām – for six bhāhya matams (philosophies which reject vēdam) namely cārvāka, baudda, kśapaṇa, vaiśēśika, sānkhya and pāśupata; poru āgi – as said in tiruveḻukūṟṟirukkai “aṟuvagaic camayamum aṟivaru nilaiyinai” (you were such that the 6 philosophies which reject vēdam, could not know about you), being the enemy; ninṟānavan – being unshakable; ellāp porutgatkum – for all entities; aru āgiya – being the antarātmā (in-dwelling soul which is invisible); ādiyai – being the primordial lord; dēvargatku ellām – including dēvas such as brahmā et al; karu āgiya – being the origin; kaṇṇanai – one who incarnated as kriṣṇa to protect the devotees; kaṇḍu koṇḍēn – saw and enjoyed

**Перевод:**

**As said in tiruveḻukūṟṟirukkai “aṟuvagaic camayamum aṟivaru nilaiyinai“, being the enemy, emperumān remains unshakable and the enemy for six bhāhya matams (philosophies which reject vēdam) namely cārvāka, baudda, kśapaṇa, vaiśēśika, sānkhya and pāśupata which are present in a superficial manner; he is the antarātmā for all entities, the primordial lord and the origin for everyone including dēvas such as brahmā et al; I saw and enjoyed such emperumān who incarnated as kriṣṇa to protect the devotees.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the eighth pāsuram, āḻvār becomes pleased saying “I have seen emperumān“.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. uruvāgiya āṟu samayangatkellām poruvāgi ninṟān avan ellāp porutkum aruvāgiya ādiyait tēvargatkellām karuvāgiya kaṇṇanaik kaṇḍu koṇḍēnē*

- *uru āgiya āṟu samayangatku ellām* – By all of the bhāhya matams which superficially appear to be the same, but order certain aspects, restrain certain other aspects and having some people who explain the remedy for the performance of such restrained aspects and those who listen to that.
- *poru āgi ninṟanavan* – poru – hurdle. [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) remained unaffected, not to be nullified by these matams.
- *ellāp porutkum aru āgiya ādiyai* – Being the antarātmā for all entities and being the controller, he is the primordial lord.
- *dēvargatku ellām karu āgiya* – One who is the origin for dēvas such as brahmā et al.
- *kaṇṇanai* – Being the effect of one of his effects \[bhagavān is the cause, all entities are born from him; he took birth as the son of vasudēva (who is one of his own creations)\]
- *kaṇḍu koṇḍēnē* – Though [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s times are subsequent to kriṣṇāvatāram, he is saying “I have seen”; for those whose mind and vision are filled with love, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) can be seen always; for śiśupāla et al, even during kriṣṇavatāram, they could not see emperumān \[as he is\]. āḻvār is saying “I have seen emperumān who is beyond the comprehension of bhāhya matams, the antarātmā of all, the controller of all, the origin for brahmā et al and easily approachable for the devotees”.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 9.4.9. Kandu kondu

*kaṇḍu koṇḍu en kaṇṇiṇai ārak kaḷittu paṇḍai vinai āyina paṟṟōdaṟuttu toṇḍarkkamuduṇṇac col mālaigaḷ sonnēn aṇḍattamarar perumān adiyēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

en kaṇgaḷ – my eyes (which are with jñānam (knowledge) and prēmam (love)); iṇai – pair; Ara – to be fully satisfied; kaṇḍu koṇḍu kaḷittu – saw and felt joyful; paṇḍai – ancient; vinai āyina – all hurdles such as ahankāra, mamakāra etc; paṟṟōdu – with the trace; aṟuttu – eliminated; aṇḍattu – in paramapadam; amarar perumān – the apt lord who is the leader of nityasūris; adiyēn – I (who am an eternal servitor); toṇḍarkku – for his servitors; amudu uṇṇa – to joyfully experience; sol mālaigaḷ – the vācika kainkaryam (service in the form of speech), in the form of a garland of words; sonnēn – I did

**Перевод:**

**I saw and felt joyful to have my pair of eyes to be fully satisfied; all my ancient hurdles such as ahankāra, mamakāra etc with the trace, were eliminated; I did vācika kainkarayam in the form of a garland of words for the joyful experience of the servitors of the apt lord who is the leader of nityasūris in paramapadam. In this pāsuram, the following aspects are explained:**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the ninth pāsuram, āḻvār becomes pleased saying “I got to enjoy emperumān and got to sing tiruvāimoḻi to be enjoyed by śrīvaiṣṇavas”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. kaṇḍu koṇḍu en kaṇṇiṇai ārak kaḷittu paṇḍai vinai āyina paṟṟōdaṟuttu toṇḍarkkamuduṇṇac col mālaigaḷ sonnēn aṇḍattamarar perumān adiyēnē*

- *kaṇḍu koṇḍu* – Saw \[[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)\] to have all my suffering, which was said in [tiruvāimoḻi 9.4.2](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/07/thiruvaimozhi-9-4-2-kanne-unnai/) “*nān aḻaippan*” (I call out), eliminated.
- *en kaṇ iṇai Ara* – To have the suffering of my eyes, which was said in [tiruvāimoḻi 9.4.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/07/thiruvaimozhi-9-4-1-maiyar-karunganni/) “*karudum en kaṇṇē*” (My eyes desire), removed
- *kaṇ iṇai Ara – kaṇḍu koṇḍu* – Like a hungry person would say “*vayiṟāra uṇḍu*” (eating to the full satisfaction of the stomach).
- *kaḷittu* – Bringing joy in the heart which was agitated.
- *paṇḍai vinai āyina paṟṟōdu aṟuttu* – Eliminating, along with the trace, the previously accumulated karma which was the hurdle for this joy.
- *toṇḍarkku amudu uṇṇac col mālaigaḷ sonnēn* – Not just enjoying myself, but also became a benefactor for vaiṣṇavas, similar to those who would say “I ate, my limbs lived and became capable to feed my relatives as well”.
- *sol mālaigaḷ sonnēn* – I got the benefit of serving your devotees. Looking at the result which is attained, this could not have been achieved by my own efforts.
- *aṇḍattu amarar perumān adiyēnē* – I was accepted by sarvēśvaran.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 9.4.10. Adiyan ivan

*adiyān ivan enṟu enakkāraruḷ seyyum nediyānai niṟai pugaḻ anjiṟaip puḷḷinkodiyānaik kunṟāmal ulagamaḷandaadiyānai adaindu adiyēn uyndavāṟē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

ivan adiyān – he (āḻvār) is my natural servitor; enṟu – having this in tiruvuḷḷam (divine heart); enakku Ar – complete for me; aruḷ – mercy; seyyum – while showering; nediyānai – being great and feeling as though he has done nothing and having eagerness to do more; niṟai – matching this protection; pugaḻ – having great qualities starting with śeela (simplicity), saulabhya (easy approacability), jñāna (knowledge), śakti (ability) etc; am – distinguished; siṟai – having wings; puḷḷin – periya tiruvadi (garudāḻvār); kodiyānai – having as flag to manifest his great protection; kunṟāmal – to eliminate the shortcoming of being claimed by others; ulagam – world; aḷanda – measured and accepted; adiyānai – one who has the divine feet which reveal the eternal relationship; adaindu – reached; adiyēn – I who have the nature of servitude, which is displayed; uynda āṟē – got uplifted!

**Перевод:**

**emperumān is having in his tiruvuḷḷam (divine heart) “he (āḻvār) is my natural servitor”, while showering his complete mercy, remained great and felt as though he has done nothing and was having eagerness to do more; he is  having great qualities starting with śeela (simplicity), saulabhya (easy approacability), jñāna (knowledge), śakti (ability) etc matching this protection; he is having periya tiruvadi who is having distinguished wings as his flag to manifest his great protection; he measured and accepted the world to eliminate the shortcoming of being claimed by others, with his divine feet which reveal the eternal relationship; I who have the nature of servitude, which is displayed, reached such divine feet and got uplifted!**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the tenth pāsuram, āḻvār says “I am grateful having attained emperumān“.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. adiyān ivan enṟu enakkāraruḷ seyyum nediyānai niṟai pugaḻ anjiṟaip puḷḷinkodiyānaik kunṟāmal ulagamaḷandaadiyānai adaindu adiyēn uyndavāṟē!*

- *adiyān ivan enṟu* – To say “my subsequent generosity towards you is apt”, he favoured me highlighting that I am his servitor.
- *enakku Ar aruḷ seyyum nediyānai* – sarvēśvara who favoured to his ability instead of my capacity \[to accept\]. It is said in tiruvāimoḻi 10.6.1 “*aruḷ peṟuvār adiyār*” (devotees who receive his mercy). Children only get to claim their share \[of mercy\]; but servitors will have theirs in everything. \[An incident is highlighted to explain that [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/) will greatly bless his devotees\] piḷḷai agaḷanga brahma rāyar desired to pacify [parāśara bhattar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/parasara-bhattar/) \[piḷḷai agaḷanga brahma rāyar is a disciple of [kūrattāḻvān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/kuraththazhwan/), but committed an offense towards bhattar, which led bhattar to go to tirukkōśtiyūr and stay there for some time, being distressed\]; he sent a very dear devotee of namperumāḷ named “*iru kai madavāraṇam*” (a weaver) thinking that bhattar’s heart will be joyed at seeing him; as iru kai madavāraṇam arrived there and had a conversation with bhattar, bhattar became blissful; those who were there said “appears that your divine heart is cherishing his vaiṣṇavatvam” and bhattar said “Should we even say it? Are these devotees not garbhadāsas (devotees from the time of conceiving)?” and mercifully continued to recite this pāsuram.
- *Ar aruḷ seyyum* – Instead of showering his mercy to my accepting capacity, he did to his ability.

When asked “What is his greatness?” [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says,

- *nediyānai* – He can only be said as “sarvēśvaran” \[cannot be explained further\].
- *niṟai …* – Do I have to explain this today? Is it not visible from the flag he has hoisted? periya tiruvadi has great qualities such saurya (valour), vīrya (strength) etc and has a beautiful form due to constant enjoyment of [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/); one who has such periya tiruvadi as his flag. One who accepted me just as he accepted periya tiruvadi.

When asked “What is the goodness in you for being accepted by bhagavān?” [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says,

- *kunṟāmal ulagam aḷanda adiyānai* – Just as he mercifully measured the world \[and touched everyone with his divine feet\] without checking the qualities of anyone, he did it without any reason. One who has the divine feet which measured every inch of the vast earth. He allowed me to enjoy his greatness and simplicity.
- *adaindu adiyēn uynda āṟē* – How did I become uplifted just due to my śēśatvam (servitude)? Is there so much benefit for the śēśatva jñānam (knowledge about one’s servitude towards [bhagavān](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/12/thathva-thrayam-iswara-who-is-god/))?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 9.4.11. Ara mada yanai

*āṟā mada yānai adarttavan tannai sēṟār vayal ten kurugūrc catakōpan nūṟē sonna ōr āyirattuḷ ippattum ēṟē tarum vānavar tam innuyurkkē*

**Пословный перевод:**

āṟā – uncontrollable forever; madam – intoxicated; yānai – the elephant named kuvalayāpīdam; adarttavan tannai – on kriṣṇa who annihilated; sēṟu – mud; Ar – abundance; vayal – having fields; then – beautiful; kurugūr – controller of āḻvārtirunagari; satakōpan – āḻvār; nūṟē – in hundreds; sonna ōr āyirattuḷ ippattum – this decad among the thousand pāsurams; vānavar tam – for the nityasūris; in – dear; uyirkku – reaching the heart; ēṟē tarum – will climb

**Перевод:**

**This decad which is one among the thousand pāsurams which are composed in \[collections of\] hundreds by āḻvār, who is the controller of āḻvārtirunagari which is having fields with abundant mud, on kriṣṇa who annihilated the elephant, kuvalayāpīdam which was uncontrollably intoxicated, will reach the dear heart of nityasūris and climb there. Also explained as, this decad will grant sarvēśvaran who is the lord of the dear heart of nityasūris.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the end, āḻvār says “This decad will cause pain in the hearts of nityasūris, due to its enjoyability”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. āṟā mada yānai adarttavan tannai sēṟār vayal then kurugūrc catakōpan nūṟē sonna ōr āyirattuḷ ippattum ēṟē tarum vānavar tam innuyurkkē*

- *āṟā mada yānai adarttavan tannai …* – One who annihilated kuvalayāpīdam which was uncontrollably intoxicated forever. One who eliminated my hurdles just as he annihilated it.
- *sēr Ar vayal* – That kuvalayāpīdam was working in the fields here \[making it to remain muddy\]!
- *nūṟē sonna ōr āyiram …* – Just as gifts are given in separate packages, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) sang these pāsurams in hundreds. Just as we see kāṇḍam, parvam etc in mahābhāratam, śrī rāmāyaṇam etc, āḻvār composed this prabandam in hundreds to facilitate easy memorising/understanding for the readers. This decad will cause pain in the hearts of nityasūris \[This is to say that their hearts will be captured by this decad – as being captured is painful in worldly aspects, similar narration is done by āḻvār\]; alternative explanation – this will bestow the lord of nityasūris.

## 9.5 Innuyirc cevalum

## 9.5.1. Innuyirc cevalum

*innuyirc cēvalum nīrum kūvik koṇḍu ingettanai ennuyir nōva miḻaṟṟēnmin kuyiṟpēdaigāḷ ennuyirk kaṇṇa pirānai nīr varak kūvugileer ennuyir kūvik koduppārkkum ittanai vēṇḍumō?*

**Пословный перевод:**

kuyil pēdaigāḷ – Oh female cuckoos!; in uyir – that which is enjoyable and which sustains you, like prāṇa (life) being outside; sēvalum – male cuckoo; in uyir nīrum – you who are a female like me and who is the dear life for that male cuckoo; kūvik koṇḍu – calling out (to unite with each other); ingu – in front of me; ettanai – greatly; en uyir – my prāṇa (life); nōva – to hurt; miḻaṟṟēnmin – don’t make incoherent sounds!; en – for me; uyir – who sustains me; kaṇṇan – kriṣṇa; pirānai – benefactor; nīr – you; varak kūvugileer – not inviting!; en uyir – my prāṇa; kūvi – steal; koduppārkkum – to those who give it to him; ittanai – so many activities; vēṇḍumō – are they required?

**Перевод:**

**Oh female cuckoos! Don’t make incoherent sounds in front of me greatly hurting my prāṇa, by calling out the male cuckoo which is like prāṇa \[for you\] being outside, which is enjoyable and which sustains you. You are a female like me and you are the dear life for that male cuckoo! You are not inviting kriṣṇa who sustains me and is the benefactor for me! Are so many activities required for those who steal my prāṇa and give it to him?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the first pāsuram, āḻvār says to some female cuckoos “should you be so enthusiastic in finishing me off?”*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. innuyirc cēvalum nīrum kūvik koṇḍu ingettanai ennuyir nōva miḻaṟṟēnmin kuyiṟpēdaigāḷ ennuyirk kaṇṇa pirānai nīr varak kūvugileer ennuyir kūvik koduppārkkum ittanai vēṇḍumō?*

- *in uyirc cēvalum* – The male cuckoo which is as dear as the good life itself. It is moving around in front of the female cuckoo as if it is the embodiment of prāṇa. Unlike the male ([emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)) who separated from parānguśa nāyaki and torments her, this male cuckoo sustains the female cuckoo! There is a male who is enjoyable and who sustains!
- *nīrum* – You who are like the dear life of the male cuckoo.
- *kūvik koṇḍu* – On top of showing your togetherness and tormenting me \[who is separated from emperumān\], should you also torment me with your talks? Having special names for each other for the sake of your union.
- *ingu ettanai* – Is there any scope for so many activities? Here I am in separation. What is there to enthuse you? As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam kiśkindā kāṇḍam “*adikam śōbatē*” (This beautiful pampā river is increasing my love), it is tormenting me; alternatively,
- *ettanai en uyir nōva miḻaṟṟēlmin* – Don’t carry out your sweet talks to increase my sorrow in separation, when I am already weak. By saying “*uyir nōva*” (tormenting my life), she indicates that her body is already gone. Your sound resembles the arrows of śrī rāma which can pierce the life. By saying “*en uyir*“, she is differentiating it from [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who would enjoy the sweet talks of the cuckoos. miḻaṟṟugai – nirambā mensol – sweet talks which are left incomplete during union.
- *nōva miḻaṟṟēl min* – Should you not remain quiet if you know that when she hears these talks, she will be finished? Should one not retract, if the action \[speech\] leads to hurting women?
- *kuyil pēdaigāḷ* – Should you also do what is done by those belonging to the other species \[male\]? Even while thinking to achieve a task with the help of male cuckoo, one has to bow at the feet of the female cuckoo and get the desired task accomplished.
- *en uyirk kaṇṇa pirānai* – She assumes the birds asking her “Why are you talking about us as if we are murderers?” she says “You are not inviting kriṣṇa who sustains me”; that which sustains is different for each entity; grass sutains \[some\] animals, food sustains humans, nectar sustains dēvas and kriṣṇa sustains parānguśa nāyaki; did she not say in [tiruvāimoḻi 6.7.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/03/thiruvaimozhi-6-7-1-unnum-soru/) “*ellām kaṇṇan*” (everything is kriṣṇa for me).
- *kaṇṇa pirānai* – One who places himself for the sake of others.
- *nīr* – Should you, who understand the taste in union, not understand the pain in separation?
- *varak kūvugileer* – If you go in front of him and make noise, would he not understand my pain and arrive? You are not doing that. You are engaging in actions which torment me but not the actions which will unite me with him. She thinks that the birds which can finish her off can also rejuvenate her by uniting her with him. She is thinking that their mouths are the only hope for her survival.
- *en uyirk kūvik koduppārkkum ittanai vēṇḍumō* – When you are not ready to unite us, your aim is to finish off me only; should you be so enthusiastic for that? As your aim is to take away my life which is already gone, and hand it over to him, should you be so enthusiastic for that? Do you need to do all of these such as being together, having union, calling each other lovingly, making sweet talks etc? īsn’t enlivening those who are down, more difficult to achieve\[should you not do that, to bring me to life\]? Is there anything great in finishing them \[in this case, me\] off?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 9.5.2. Ittanai venduvadu

*ittanai vēṇḍuvadanṟandō! anṟil pēdaigāḷ! ettanai nīrum num śēvalum karaindēngudir vittagan gōvindan meyyan allan oruvarkkum attanaiyām ini ennuyir avan kaiyadē*

**Пословный перевод:**

anṟil pēdaigāḷ – Oh female curlews (who cannot live in separation from your spouses); nīrum – you (who interact according to the desires of your spouses); num sēvalum – your spouses (which interact according to your desires); ettanai – in how many ways; karaindu – melting inside due to the enjoyment in union; ēngudir – making sounds?; ittanai – this over-action; vēṇḍuvadu anṟu – not required; andō – alas!; vittagan – one who has amazing acts; gōvindan – kriṣṇa who attracts the world by manifesting his simplicity in protecting cows; oruvarkkum – for any one (irrespective of townspeople or noble ones); meyyan allan – will not interact truthfully; ini en uyir – now, my life; avan kaiyadē – depends on him

**Перевод:**

**Oh female curlews! In how many ways, your spouses and you are melting inside due to the enjoyment in union and making sounds? This over-reaction is not required; alas! kriṣṇa who attracts the world by manifesting his simplicity in protecting cows and who has amazing acts, will not interact with any one truthfully. Now, my life depends on him.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the second pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki prays to some female curlews saying “Don’t torment me with love-fights, being with your spouses”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. ittanai vēṇḍuvadanṟandō! anṟil pēdaigāḷ! ettanai nīrum num śēvalum karaindēngudir vittagan gōvindan meyyan allan oruvarkkum attanaiyām ini ennuyir avan kaiyadē*

- *ittanai vēṇḍuvadu anṟu* –  You should not be so enthusiastic to finish me off. While she \[[āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) in the mood of [parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)\] was saying “Should you be so enthusiastic!” to the cuckoos, she was tormented by the sound of curlews; she was in a state to repeat the same words to the curlews too. When \[sugrīva\]  mahārājar and vāli were fighting, perumāḷ (śrī rāma) shot the shining arrow; similarly, when she was arguing with the cuckoos saying “don’t make noise” and they were making loud noise and so on, the curlews came in between them and started making noise as if pouring fire through the ears; she understood their intent and said “are the cuckoos not enough! are you needed too!” They continued to make noise even while she was telling them to stop.
- *andō* – She is saying “Your attitude is similar to someone filling with arrows, the mouth of the one who surrenders saying ‘śaraṇam’! Alas!”
- *anṟil pēdaigāḷ* – I am not seeing any difference between the female cuckoos and you.  I am not seeing any difference between your spouses and you as well. When it comes to tormenting me, you are worse than sajātīya (your own kind – female cuckoos) and vijātīya (others – males of your species).

They ask “What did we do?” [parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says,

- ettanai – very much
- *nīrum num sēvalum* – You who act according to the thoughts of your spouses and your spouses which act according to your thoughts. As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam bāla kāṇḍam 77.2 “*antarjātam abhivyaktam*” (As perumāḷ is in the heart of sītāp pirātti, she knows her thoughts clearly), the male curlews which act according to the desire of the female curlews.
- *karaindu ēngudir* – One cannot hurt oneself to torment others! They are interacting with each other and manifesting how weakened they are due to their love for each other. Is this the time for your union? Even if you unite, should you express your inner emotions?
- *vittagan …* – They ask “If he is delaying a little bit, should you say that he is tormenting you through us?” She responds “Listen to me about his qualities!”
- *vittagan* – Amazing personality. Now, he is so amazing to be known by the favourable ones.
- *gōvindan* – rakśaka (protector) of all. With this, \[it is said that\] he pretends to be the protector of all but really hurts \[the favourable ones\].  He can neither be surrendered to considering him to be the protector nor be ignored considering him to be the offender.
- *meyyan allan oruvarkkum* – Even you, who thought of him to be “very loving, protector of all” and engaged in his cause, will end up with disappointing results. You are thinking him to be śrī rāma who said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 18.30 “*rāmō dvirnābhibhśatē*” (śrī rāma is not double-tongued , i.e. does not change his stand), śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 8.3 ‘*natyajēyam*‘ (I will not abandon even if he has faults) and śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 18.33 “*ētat vratam mama*” (This is my vow); but the acts of kriṣṇa are such as changing day into night, taking up arms after vowing not to do so etc. The curlews said “His truth in rāmāvatāram and his lies in kriṣṇāvatāram are the refuge for his devotees; what if he is truthful or a liar? We will accept him joyfully whichever way he is” and were focussed on their acts.
- *attanaiyum ini …* – She is saying “Now, they should not be like this! Due to their focus, I am ending up with his thoughts only!” As my life is in his hands, why should I hold on to your feet for my protection?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 9.5.3. Avan kaiyade

*avan kaiyadē enadāruyir anṟil pēdaigāḷ! evan solli nīr kudaindādudir pudai sūḻavē tavam seydillā vinaiyāttiyēn uyir inguṇḍō? evan solli niṟṟum? num ēngu kūkkural kēttumē*

**Пословный перевод:**

anṟil pēdaigāḷ – Oh female curlews!; avan kaiyadē – in the hands of gōvinda, who is having simplicity; enadu Ar uyir – my prāṇa (life); nīr – you; evan solli – speaking in many distinct ways; kudaindu – uniting as if you are inside each other; pudai sūḻavē – in my proximity; ādudir – moving around!; tavam – unlike him who is having the fortune of being undisturbed in separation; seydillā – instead of having; vinaiyāttiyēn – me who is having the sin of suffering on seeing similes, my; uyir – life; ingu uṇḍō – is it here?; num – your; ēngu – weakened by the union; kūkkural – on hearing the sounds; evan – what; solli niṟṟum – shall I say?

**Перевод:**

**Oh female curlews! My life is in the hands of gōvinda, who is having simplicity; you are speaking in many distinct ways, uniting as if you are inside each other and moving around in my proximity! Unlike him who is having the fortune of being undisturbed in separation, I am having the sin of suffering on seeing similes to him; is my life present here? What shall I say on hearing your sounds which are weakened by the union?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the third pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki is again praying to the female curlews saying “don’t torment me who is already suffering greatly”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. avan kaiyadē enadāruyir anṟil pēdaigāḷ! evan solli nīr kudaindādudir pudai sūḻavē tavam seydillā vinaiyāttiyēn uyir inguṇḍō? evan solli niṟṟum? num ēngu kūkkural kēttumē*

- *avan kaiyadē enadu āruyir* – My life is in his hands. For a couple, isn’t it natural to have their lives in each other? Can you not understand this?
- *anṟil pēdaigāḷ* – Should you who understand the joy of union, not understand the pain of separation?
- *evan solli* – Saying something. It appears that her mouth will burn if she repeats the words of the female curlews.
- *nīr kudaindu* – Immersing in each other.
- *ādudir* – You are interacting and enjoying.
- *pudai sūḻavē* – You are moving around in my surroundings. Just as those who try to capture a kingdom will surround the fort. Can I escape this by closing my ears or eyes! She feels that this is similar to perumāḷ (śrī rāma) and his army surrounding lankā to destroy it.  Oh I am a sinner! There is nothing available in me for your enthusiasm.
- *tavam seydillā* – I am not fortunate since I don’t have my life here to favour you. piḷḷān would explain “I am not fortunate like him to be undisturbed in separation”.
- *uyir ingu uṇḍō* – She is saying “is it here!” and showing her heart, just as someone will show the light to a murderer.
- *evan solli niṟṟum* – What can I say to sustain myself?
- *num …* – While surviving in separation, after hearing the sounds of all of you who are immersed in union, will I able to survive that sound! Would your sound, not finish off those who hear it! Are you calling out, after closing your ears? \[Are you not hearing your own voice?\] śrī rāmāyaṇam kiśkindā kāṇḍam 80.10 “*nisvanam cakravāgānām niśamya sahacāriṇām \| puṇḍarīka viśālākśī katam ēśā bhaviśyati \|\|*” (perumāḷ said – How will sītāp pirātti, the one with a huge lotus like eyes, feel after hearing the sweet sounds of female cakravāka birds with their spouses?)

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 9.5.4. Kukkural kettum

*kūkkural kēttum nangaṇṇan māyan veḷippadān mēṟkiḷai koḷḷēnmin nīrum sēvalum kōḻiigāḷ! vākkum manamum karumamum namakkāngadē ākkaiyum āviyum andaram ninṟuḻalumē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kōḻigāḷ – Oh peahens!; kūkkural – Your calling out for each other; kēttum – while it is audible even in his abode; nam – obedient (to be considered by everyone as “our own”); māyan – one who engages those who approach him, with his amazing qualities and acts; kaṇṇan – kriṣṇa; veḷippadān – he is not coming; num – your; sēvalum nīrum – your spouse and yourself together; mēl – further; kiḷai koḷḷenmin – don’t call out as a group!; namakku – for us; vākkum manamum karumamum – speech, mind and body; āngadē – reached him; ākkaiyum – body; āviyum – life; andaram ninṟu – in between; uḻalumē – being tormented

**Перевод:**

**Oh peahens! Though your calling out for each other is audible even in his abode, the obedient kriṣṇa who engages those who approach him, with his amazing qualities and acts, is not coming; your spouse and yourself together don’t call out as a group, further! Our speech, mind and body have reached him; the body and the life are being tormented in between. kōḻi – peahen; kiḷaittal – making sound.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fourth pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki says to hens “Don’t torment me by making loud noise”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*Subsequently, āḻvār says to \[pea\]hens “Don’t torment me by making loud noise”. kriṣṇa, who has amazing activities, is not appearing yet.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. kūkkural kēttum nangaṇṇan māyan veḷippadān mēṟkiḷai koḷḷēnmin nīrum sēvalum kōḻiigāḷ! vākkum manamum karumamum namakkāngadē ākkaiyum āviyum andaram ninṟuḻalumē*

- *kūkkural kēttum* – Even after hearing the way you make your sound. She is thinking that there is not a single place where this sound cannot reach.
- *nam kaṇṇan* – His obedience is as popular as vatayakśa prasiddi \[a ghost is present in this banyan tree – imaginary\].
- *māyan* – amazing personality; pretending to be truthful during union.
- *veḷippadān* – He is not arriving, thinking that “she won’t survive \[in my absence\]”; he is said as in śrī bhāgavatam 10.32.2 “… *tāsāmāvirabūt …*” (He appeared amidst the covherd girls like the cupid for cupids)! riśi (sage) said “*āvirabhūt*” (appeared) and she is saying “*veḷippadān*” (not appearing).
- *mēl kiḷai koḷḷēnmin* – High pitch. Don’t make high pitched sound which matches your species and your romantic situation. As she was being engaged, it increased its pitch.
- *nīrum sēvalum* – When the peahen started, the peacock continued it and completed it.
- *kōḻigāḷ* – Should you come as a clan to defeat a woman? kōḻi – mayil – peahen.

[parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) considers the birds to be saying “Are we going to be bothered about your statement ‘do not torment me’? Would we stop without taking away all of your faculties? We need to complete the task we have taken up” and says “for that, you have to go there”.

- *vākkum manamum karumamum namakku āngadē* – All my faculties (mind, speech and body) are with him now, She is saying this thinking “these birds will go there and make sound, which will make it unsustainable for him, and he will arrive”.

When asked “if they are there, how can you speak and act in this manner?” She says

- *ākkaiyum āviyum andaram ninṟu uḻalumē* – Due to the previous sorrows, my body and life are suffering in between \[neither here, nor there\]. Like a horn which was held and released, we only have the impressions. There is something which is needed here to be tormented \[by you\], but the faculties which can be tormented are not here.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 9.5.5. Andaram ninru

*andaram ninṟuḻalginṟa yānudaip pūvaigāḷ ! nundiṟattēdum idai illai kuḻaṟēnminō indira jñālangaḷ kātti ivvēḻulagum koṇḍa nandirumārvan nam āvi uṇṇa nangeṇṇinān*

**Пословный перевод:**

andaram ninṟu – standing in between; uḻalginṟa – being agitated needlessly; yānudaip pūvaigāḷ – Oh mynās whom I considered to be mine!; num tiṟattu – in your matters; ēdum idai illai – there is no reason; kuḻaṟēnmin – don’t make incoherent sounds!; indira jñālangaḷ kātti – showing his clairvoyant qualities, form and activities to make us think them to be true; i ēḻ ulagum – these seven worlds; koṇḍa – having it (as his own for them to exist without claim of ownership by others and self); nam tirumārvan – captivated us by showing his love towards pirātti who is on his divine chest; nam – our; āvi – prāṇa (life); uṇṇa – to consume; nangu eṇṇinān – planned clearly

**Перевод:**

**Oh mynās whom I considered to be mine, who are standing in between and needlessly being agitated! There is no reason for you to torment me; don’t make incoherent sounds! emperumān who is showing his clairvoyant qualities, form and activities to make us think them to be true, is having these seven worlds, has captivated us by showing his love towards pirātti who is on his divine chest and as planned clearly, to consume our life.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fifth pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki tells her own mynās which torment her “He is looking for a good means to finish me off; it is not apt for you to do the same”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. andaram ninṟuḻalginṟa yānudaip pūvaigāḷ ! nundiṟattēdum idai illai kuḻaṟēnminō indira jñālangaḷ kātti ivvēḻulagum koṇḍa nandirumārvan nam āvi uṇṇa nangeṇṇinān*

- *andaram ninṟu uḻalginṟa* – While you have nothing to torment here, you are feeling agitated needlessly here.
- *yānudaip pūvaigāḷ* – Oh my mynās! Can you, who are my belonging, do what is done by common persons? It appears that whenever I claim something as mine, that is sufficient to be tormented \[by that\]! Even he remained mine and tormented me!
- *num tiṟattu ēdum idai illai* – on your side, there is no reason to torment me; also implies her saying “there is nothing left in me for your enthusiasm”.
- *kuḻaṟēnmin* – Don’t finish me off with your incoherent sounds! Only if he remains relaxed in his efforts, you should be trying hard in this manner! Did he leave any opportunity for you!
- *indira jñālangaḷ kātti* – Showing his beautiful form which cannot be ignored by anyone, his qualities (simplicity) and activities. Since these are ever changing, she is saying “*poygaḷ*” (illusion). indirajñālam and poy (false) are synonyms.
- *ēḻ ulagum koṇḍa* – While setting out to take away others’ belongings, he will completely take them away without leaving anything for them.
- *nam tirumārvan* – Showing me the fame he acquired by his love. He did not engage with pirātti due to his love; it is only to attract others by showing that relationship. Also explained as her saying – just as he told a few lies to \[re\]claim the earth, he pretended to engage with me and separate from me, as a means to finish me off.
- *nam āvi uṇṇa nangu eṇṇinān* – He looked out for a good means to finish us off. You have nothing to do here. Are you thinking that there is some shortcoming in the acts of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is sarvaśakti (omnipotent) and trying to help him! Also said as – she is feeling distressed and saying “he gave a deadly glance to finish me off”.

## 9.5.6. Nangenni

*nangeṇṇi nān vaḷartta siṟu kiḷip paidalē in kural nī miḻaṟṟēl en uyirk kāguttan nin seyya vāyokkum vāyan kaṇṇan kai kālinan nin pasum sāma niṟattan kūttuṇḍu nīnginān*

**Пословный перевод:**

en Ar uyir – being my prāṇa (life) who cannot be sustained in separation; kāguttan – cakravartit tirumagan (śrī rāma, son of the emperor) who is said as “maṟṟilēn tanjamāgavē” (cannot sustain without your refuge); nin – your; seyya – reddish; vāy – mouth; okkum vāyan – having matching mouth; kaṇṇan – having matching eyes; kai kālinan – having matching hands and feet; nin – your; pasum sāmam – fresh black colour like; niṟattan – having dark complexion; kūttuṇḍu – united (with me); nīnginān – separated; nangu – having goodness (of helping me during dangers); eṇṇi – thinking; nān vaḷartta – I raised; siṟu – having small form; paidal – young; kiḷiyē – oh parrot!; in – attracting me with the sweetness; kural – voice; nī – you (who are tormenting me by reminding me of his form); miḻaṟṟēl – don’t make beautiful sounds with deep meanings!

**Перевод:**

**cakravartit tirumagan (śrī rāma, son of the emperor) who is said as “maṟṟilēn tanjamāgavē“, who is my prāṇa, who cannot be sustained in separation, who is having fresh black colour like dark complexion, and having reddish mouth, eyes hands and feet, matching yours, united with me and separated; oh young parrot with a small form whom I raised to have the goodness of helping me during dangers! Don’t make beautiful sounds with deep meanings, with your attractive sweet voice!**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the sixth pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki stops her pet parrot which tells the divine names without understanding her state saying “I raised you to please me by reciting the divine names, when I am in stable condition. Don’t tell the divine names, when I am in this unmanageable state!”*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. nangeṇṇi nān vaḷartta siṟu kiḷip paidalē in kural nī miḻaṟṟēl en uyirk kāguttan nin seyya vāyokkum vāyan kaṇṇan kai kālinan nin pasum sāma niṟattan kūttuṇḍu nīnginān*

- *nangeṇṇi* – Did I not raise you to recite the divine names when I can handle them and refrain while I cannot handle them?
- *nān vaḷartta* – I raised you as a mother, who raises a single child, would care so much for that child; it seems that if I show love towards something, it will move away from me! Even he is obedient to me like the parrot \[only to leave me\].
- *siṟu kiḷip paidalē* – siṟumai – age. paidal – not having the right growth for that age as well. It is due to your childish nature that you are tormenting me.
- *in kural* – It is like saying “*kūriya vēl*” (sharp spear).
- *nī miḻaṟṟēl* – Don’t finish me off with your soft words with deep meanings! Is there any one who tries to kill one’s own mother?
- *en Ar uyirk kāguttan* – He united with me so intimately that I am unable to sustain myself in separation. He remains thinking as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 3.6.8](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/09/thiruvaimozhi-3-6-8-thuyarame-tharu/) “*tayarataṟku magan tannai anṟi maṟṟilēn*” (I won’t exist for any one other than the son of daśarata).
- *nin seyya vāy okkum vāyan* – He has a mouth similar to that of yours. We can highlight a simile to his limbs but cannot fully comprehend the greatness of his limbs.
- *kaṇṇan kai kālinan* – One who has reddish eyes, hands and divine feet.
- *nin pasum sāma niṟattan* – He has your cool blackish complexion.
- *pasum sāmam* – Instead of being very dark (hard on the eyes), it is cool black complexion. Why is he having so many enemies for me in his divine form \[every limb is tormenting her\]?
- *kūttuṇḍu nīnginān* – He united with me, and separated knowing my nature quite well; aren’t your ways/acts enjoyable only when he is with me? Wouldn’t only rāvaṇa et al torment those who are separated? Would the favourable ones torment too?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 9.5.7. Kuttundu ningiya

*kūttuṇḍu nīngiya kōlat tāmaraik kaṇ sevvāy vāttamil en karumāṇikkam kaṇṇan māyanpōl kōttiya villodu minnu mēgak kuḻāngaḷgāḷ kāttēnmin nummuru ennuyirkku adu kālanē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kūttuṇḍu – united with me to make us look like a single entity; nīngiya – in the state of separation; kōlam – attractive; tāmarai – lotus like; kaṇ – eyes; sem – reddish; vāy – having lips; vāttamil en karu māṇikkam – having blue carbuncle like form which is in my memory always; kaṇṇan – (obedient) kriṣṇa; māyanpōl – who is like an amazing personality; kōttiya – bent; villodu – with rainbow/lightning; minnum – shining; mēgak kuḻāngaḷgāḷ – oh groups of clouds!; en – my; uyirkku – for prāṇa; adu kālan – that is like death; num uru – your form; kāttēnmin – don’t show

**Перевод:**

**Oh shining groups of clouds which have bent rainbows/lightning which resemble kriṣṇa who is like an amazing personality who is having attractive lotus like eyes, reddish lips and is with a blue carbuncle like form which is in my memory always, who separated from me after uniting with me to make us look like a single entity! Your form looks like death for my prāṇa; don’t show it.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the seventh pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki sees the gathering of clouds which have the same complexion as he has and being unable to bear it, says “don’t show your form to me and finish me off”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. kūttuṇḍu nīngiya kōlat tāmaraik kaṇ sevvāy vāttamil en karumāṇikkam kaṇṇan māyanpōl kōttiya villodu minnu mēgak kuḻāngaḷgāḷ kāttēnmin nummuru ennuyirkku adu kālanē*

- *kūttuṇḍu …* – After uniting to be said as a single entity, and separated, this is how his limbs are shining; alternative explanation – this is the shine he acquired after uniting with her.
- *kōlat tāmaraik kaṇ sevvāy* – One who has beautiful lotus like divine eyes and reddish lips.
- *vāttam …* – The freshness \[in him\] which was there during the union, will not disappear even in separation; it only doubled after flattening me.
- *en karu māṇikkam* – Having the complexion of a blue carbuncle which cannot be forgotten even after getting separated from it. While he remains as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 36.42 “*naivadamśān na maśakān*” (He will not drive away the flies and mosquitoes), she is saying this word just for his momentary delay!
- *kaṇṇan māyan pōl* – Like the amazing kriṣṇa; while uniting, he was obedient in massaging the hands and feet.
- *kōttiya vil* – Oh groups of clouds which are shining with rainbow/lightning! Just  as kaustuba jewel adds lustre to his divine form, the rainbow/lightning is adding luster to the groups of clouds.
- *kāttēnmin num uru* – Don’t show your form which resembles death! There is no difference between emperumān who tries to abandon me with such form and you!

When asked “How is that?” She says,

- *en uyirkku adu kālanē* – It is like death for my prāṇa which is consumed by separation and has become weak. After saying “*kuḻāngaḷgāḷ kāttēnmin num uru*” (in first person), she is saying “*adu*” (in third person), since she has turned her face away not desiring to see them.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 9.5.8. Uyirkkadu kalan

*uyirkkadu kālan enṟu ummai yān irandēṟku nīr kuyiṟpaidalgāḷ! kaṇṇan nāmamē kuḻaṟik konṟīr tayirp paḻanjōṟṟodu pāl adisilundandu sol payiṟṟiya nal vaḷamūttinīr paṇbudaiyīrē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

nān – I; adu – that \[his names\]; uyirkku – for my prāṇa; kālan enṟu – saying that it is death personified; ummai – towards you; irandēṟku – for me who prayed; kuyil paidalgāḷ – young cuckoos!; nīr – you; kaṇṇan nāmamē – the divine names of obedient kriṣṇa; kuḻaṟi – speaking incoherently; konṟīr – finished me!; tayirp paḻam sōṟṟodu – giving old rice with curd for breakfast; pāl adisilum – rice with milk for lunch; tandu – gave (you); sol – words (that represent his divine names); payiṟṟiya – taught; nal vaḷam – good wealth; ūttinīr – let me enjoy!; paṇbu – good quality; udaiyīr – you are having!

**Перевод:**

**Oh young cuckoos to whom I prayed saying that his names are death personified for my prāṇa! You have finished me by incoherently speaking the divine names of obedient kriṣṇa! You have let me enjoy this good wealth for giving you old rice with curd for breakfast and rice with milk for lunch and teaching these words! You are having such good quality! \[sarcasm\]**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the eighth pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki says to some cuckoos “Even after my prayers to stop, you recite his divine names further and torment me; this is the result I get for raising you” and becomes upset.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. uyirkkadu kālan enṟu ummai yān irandēṟku nīr kuyiṟpaidalgāḷ! kaṇṇan nāmamē kuḻaṟik konṟīr tayirp paḻanjōṟṟodu pāl adisilundandu sol payiṟṟiya nal vaḷamūttinīr paṇbudaiyīrē!*

- *uyirkku adu* – She is saying it “that”, since she cannot spell it out as it does not stop at hurting her externally.
- *kālan enṟu* – Feeling that they don’t stop with tormenting but will finish her.
- *ummai* – You who pray to serve me.
- *nān* – Me who is the irrefutable mother.
- *irandēṟku* – Did I order you? For me who surrendered unto you due to my unbearable situation.
- *nīr* – You who are controlled by me. You became the murderers of those who surrendered unto you.
- *kuyil paidalgāḷ* – Your childishness ended up taking away my life! Though you are not matured, should you not know your mother?

When they asked “What did we do?” She says,

- *kaṇṇan nāmamē kuḻaṟik konṟīr* – You finished me by incoherently saying kriṣṇa’s divine names which have no remedy. Could you not have spoken at least once, śrī rāma’s qualities which are said to be “*mrutasanjīvanam*” (medicine which will bring back life in a dead person)?
- *tayir …* – I gave curd and old rice, milk and freshly cooked rice at the proper times and taught you the divine names and you have returned the favour nicely for that!
- *nal vaḷam ūttinīr* – You made me enjoy this good wealth! I cared for you all along; and you have come here and tormented me. Did these cuckoos ended up having annadōśam (poisoned food)?
- *paṇbudaiyīrē* – While there is apt relationship and odedience, you are having great humility! \[sarcasm\] You are being merciless towards your protector!

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 9.5.9. Panbudai vandodu

*paṇbudai vaṇḍodu tumbigāḷ! paṇ miḻaṟṟēnmin puṇpurai vēl kodu kuttāl okkum num in kural taṇ peru nīrt tadandāmarai malarndāl okkum kaṇ perungaṇṇan nam āviyuṇḍeḻa naṇṇinān*

**Пословный перевод:**

paṇbudai – having the good quality tunes; vaṇḍodu tumbigāḷ – dragonflies which are with the beetles!; num in kural – your sweet voice; puṇ purai – in a wound; vēl kodu – with a spear; kuttāl okkum – feels like piercing; paṇ miḻaṟṟēnmin – don’t sing sweet tunes!; taṇ – cool; peru – filled; nīr – having water; tadam – pond; tāmarai malarndāl okkum – like a lotus blossoming; perum kaṇ – having greatness of eyes; kaṇṇan – kriṣṇa; nam – our; āvi – prāṇa; uṇḍu – stealing; eḻa naṇṇinān – planning to leave

**Перевод:**

**Oh dragonflies which are with the beetles, having good quality tunes! Your sweet voice feels like a spear piercing in a wound; don’t sing sweet tunes! kriṣṇa who is having the great eyes which look like a blossoming lotus in cool, water filled pond, is planning to steal our prāṇa and leave. When paṇbudai is recited as paṇburai, it implies “having natural sound”.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the ninth pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki says to some singing honey-drunken beetles and dragonflies “Your sounds are causing sorrow; don’t sing”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. paṇbudai vaṇḍodu tumbigāḷ! paṇ miḻaṟṟēnmin puṇpurai vēl kodu kuttāl okkum num in kural taṇ peru nīrt tadandāmarai malarndāl okkum kaṇ perungaṇṇan nam āviyuṇḍeḻa naṇṇinān*

- *paṇbudai vaṇḍodu tumbigāḷ* – Oh dragonflies which are with beetles having good quality \[simplicity\]!
- *paṇ miḻaṟṟēnmin* – Don’t hum abundant tunes! When it is recited as “*paṇburai*“, it indicates paṇbāna urai (humming noble sounds); it could also mean, humming tunes.
- *puṇ purai vēl kodu kuttāl okkum num in kural* – I am already hurt with the sounds of other birds etc; your humming feels like piercing a spear into that wound.
- *taṇ peru nīr …* – kriṣṇa who has eyes which look greater than a blossoming lotus in a cool, water filled pond.
- *nam …* – He showed his beauty to finish me off and left me.

## 9.5.10. Ela nanni

*eḻa naṇṇi nāmum nam vāna nādanōdonṟinōm paḻana nannāraik kuḻāngaḷgāḷ payinṟennini iḻai nalla ākkaiyum paiyavavē puyakkaṟṟadu taḻai nalla inbam talaippeydu engum taḻaikkavē*

**Пословный перевод:**

nāmum – we are also; eḻa naṇṇi – setting out to leave; nam vāna nādanōdu – with emperumān who is in paramapadam which is the apt destination for us; onṟinōm – have become like-minded; paḻanam – in water-bodies; nal – being attractive; nāraik kuḻāngaḷgāḷ – Oh groups of cranes (which have gathered)!; ini payinṟu en – what is the benefit of analysing me, while gathering together?; iḻai nalla – attractive like an ornament (for him); ākkaiyum – body; paiyavē – in proper sequence; puyakkaṟṟadu – trying to leave; engum – all places; taḻai – vastly; nalla inbam – good joy; talaippeydu – having attained; taḻaikka – let them be enriched

**Перевод:**

**Having become like-minded with emperumān who is in paramapadam which is the apt destination for us, we are also setting out to leave; oh groups of attractive cranes in water-bodies! What is the benefit of analysing me, while gathering together? My body which is attractive like an ornament \[for emperumān\], is trying to leave in proper sequence. Let all places, attaining vast, good joy, become enriched.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the tenth pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki assuming that the group of cranes is discussing within itself to finish her off, says to the cranes “I am already dead; what is the benefit of your gathering together?”*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. eḻa naṇṇi nāmum nam vāna nādanōdonṟinōm paḻana nannāraik kuḻāngaḷgāḷ payinṟennini iḻai nalla ākkaiyum paiyavavē puyakkaṟṟadu taḻai nalla inbam talaippeydu engum taḻaikkavē*

- *eḻa naṇṇi* – Setting out to leave.
- *nāmum nam vāna nādanōdu onṟinōm* – Just like containing an ocean in a small space, he presented himself, flattened me and left. We too thought “We have become one in heart with the leader of nityasūris. As he planned along with nityasūris to finish us off, we accepted. Instead of his deciding to finish us and we deciding to live, as he tries to twist the arm in clockwise direction and we twist in anti-clockwise, we too decided perish. Since nityasūris are eternally related to him, they too have the same thoughts as he.
- *paḻana nal nāraik kuḻāngaḷgāḷ* – Oh groups of cranes who live in water-bodies and have the ability to complete the tasks which you take up!
- *payinṟu en ini* – What is the use of your gathering now? Wouldn’t your mantram be of value only when I differ from his thoughts? She is thinking that just as the mudaligaḷ (vānara elders) gathered together and analysed the means to unite perumāḷ (śri rāma) and pirātti (sītā), these cranes are gathering together and analysing the means to separate her from [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/). Due to her impressions from rāmāvatāram, she is thinking “the task of tiryak (animals/birds) is to unite with him those who are desired by him and to separate from him those who are rejected by him”. Due to mentioning “*vāna nādan – nāraik kuḻāngaḷgāḷ*” (paramapadanātan (spiritual realm) and cranes (material realm), she is wondering “Are both realms required to finish off a helpless girl?”
- *iḻai nalla ākkaiyum* – Implies a) body which looks beautiful due to being decorated with ornaments, or b) distinguished body which appears like a body decorated with ornaments.
- *paiyavē puyakkaṟṟadu* – Saying a) lost its strength progressively or b) started leaving in proper sequence. puyattal – leaving, puyakka – attractive.
- *taḻai nalla …* – She says “īśvara’s wealth should become abundant”. [āḷavandār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/alavandhar/) explains this as – She is saying like those who try to kill themselves will say ‘long live this world’. [emperumānār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/emperumanar/) explains this as – She is saying “The world should not go through my suffering”. bhattar explains this as – She is saying “While I am getting finished, the world will survive without suffering for my sorrow”.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.
