## 9.5.11. Inbam talaippeydu

*inbam talaippeydu engum taḻaitta pallūḻikkut tan pugaḻ ēttat tanakkaruḷ seyda māyanait ten kurugūrc catakōpan sol āyirattuḷ ivai onbadōdonṟukkum mūvulagum urugumē*

**Пословный перевод:**

inbam talaippeydu – causing joy; engum taḻaitta – spread everywhere; than pugaḻ – his glorious qualities; pal ūḻikku – forever; ētta – to praise; tanakku – for āḻvār; aruḷ seyda – showered infinite grace; māyanai – amazing lord; then – organised; kurugūr – leader of āḻvārtirunagari; satakōpan sol – mercifully spoken by āḻvār; āyirattuḷ – among thousand pāsurams; ivai onbadōdu onṟukku – for the first nine pāsurams filled with one level of sorrow and the tenth pāsuram which is filled with greater level of sorrow; mū ulagum – three worlds; urugum – will become fluid due to the love

**Перевод:**

**āḻvār, the leader of āḻvārtirunagari, was showered with the amazing lord’s infinite grace, to praise forever, his glorious qualities which are spread everywhere causing joy; the three worlds will become fluid due to the love in this decad, among the thousand pāsurams, where the first nine pāsurams are filled with one level of sorrow and the tenth pāsuram is filled with greater level of sorrow.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the end, āḻvār says “Whosoever understands the goodness in this decad, will not be able to sustain”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. inbam talaippeydu engum taḻaitta pallūḻikkut than pugaḻ ēttat tanakkaruḷ seyda māyanait then kurugūrc catakōpan sol āyirattuḷ ivai onbadōdonṟukkum mūvulagum urugumē*

- *inbam talaippeydu engum taḻaitta* – *engum taḻaitta inbam talaippeydu* – Having unlimited love which is spread all over the world.
- *pal ūḻikkut than pugaḻ ētta* – To praise his qualities forever.
- *tanakku aruḷ seyda* – For [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) who was one among the samsāris \[worldly people\], bestowing “*mayarvaṟa madinalam*” (blemiśless knowledge and devotion).
- *māyanai* – The amazing lord who specially blessed only me among all of the samsāris.
- *inbam talaippeydu engum taḻaitta – than pugaḻ ētta – pal ūḻikku – tanakkaruḷ seyda māyanai –* Alternative explanation – He made me enjoy forever his auspicious qualities which are spread everywhere and which give infinite joy to those who enjoy them. It is said that [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) sustained himself with this “*than pugaḻ ētta tanakkaruḷ seyda*” only. āḻvār considered the experience of nityasūris and his own similarity with them in attaining the goal, and became anguished; but looking at samsāris who have lost this opportunity forever, he consoled himself saying “even this anguish is as good as the ultimate result”. As [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) speaks about himself in third person as in “*satakōpan sol*“, he could address himself as “*tanakku aruḷ seyda*” ([emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who blessed āḻvār) \[instead of *enakku aruḷ seyda*\]; this is similar to what is said \[by vālmīki bhagavān himself\] in śrī rāmāyaṇam “*vālmīki bhagavān riśi:*” (Sage vālmīki bhagavān).
- *onbadōdu onṟukkum* – This decad where the first nine pāsurams which are considered to be filled with sorrow, appear to be filled with joy in comparison to the tenth pāsuram which is filled with great sorrow. In the first nine pāsurams, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) felt great anguish while being alive, due to being reminded by the entities which are similar to [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/); but in the tenth pāsuram, he lost all interest in living itself.
- *mū ulagum urugumē* – No one will be able to sustain. After āḻvār said “this world should not be destroyed hearing my cry”, the residents of this world ended up breaking down \[seeing his anguish\].

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 9.6 Urugumal nenjam

## 9.6.1. Urugumal nenjam

*urugumāl nenjam uyirin paramanṟi perugumāl vētkaiyum en seygēn toṇḍanēn teru ellām kāvi kamaḻ tirukkātkarai maruviya māyan tan māyam ninaidoṟē?*

**Пословный перевод:**

teru ellām – in every street; kāvi kamaḻ – having the fragrance of sengaḻunīr (red lily); tirukkātkarai – in tirukkātkarai; maruviya – residing firmly; māyan than – amazing lord’s; māyam – very amazing qualities such as saundarya (beauty), śeela (simplicity) etc; ninaidoṟum – every time I think about; nenjam – my heart (which is the first tool for enjoyment); urugum – became fluid after breaking down; uyirin param anṟi – to be unbearable for the ātmā (self); vētkai – affection; perugum – is growing greatly; toṇḍanēn – I who am very desirous; en seygēn – what shall I do? (Shall I change the breaking of the heart, shall I control my affection, shall I avoid the qualities etc which are enjoyable or shall I avoid the desire towards him?)

**Перевод:**

**Every time I think about the very amazing qualities such as saundarya, śeela etc of the amazing lord who is residing firmly in tirukkātkarai which is having the fragrance of sengaḻunīr in every street, my heart breaks down and becomes fluid; the affection has grown greatly to be unbearable for the ātmā; what shall I, who am very desirous, do? The “Al” sound (at the end of urugumāl and perugumāl) indicates the amazement.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the first pāsuram, āḻvār says “My heart breaks greatly every time I think about the amazing interaction of emperumān in tirukkātkarai”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. உருகுமால் நெஞ்சம் உயிரின் பரமன்றி பெருகுமால் வேட்கையும் என் செய்கேன் தொண்டனேன் தெருவு எல்லாம் காவி கமழ் திருக்காட்கரை மருவிய மாயன் தன் மாயம் நினைதொறே? urugumāl nenjam uyirin paramanṟi perugumāl vētkaiyum en seygēn toṇḍanēn teru ellām kāvi kamaḻ tirukkātkarai maruviya māyan than māyam ninaidoṟē?*

- *urugumāl nenjam* – The heart which is the first tool for enjoyment is breaking down. One needs the heart to enjoy and to become satisfied with such enjoyment. Just as a \[supporting\] boat capsizes on entry into the river for a person who sets out to swim, the heart which is the entry point for enjoyment, breaks down. The heart is required for āḻvār to say as in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.1.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/03/thiruvaimozhi-1-1-1-uyarvara-uyarnalam/) “*toḻudeḻu*” (worship and rise) and in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.10.6](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/10/thiruvaimozhi-1-10-6-niyum-nanum/) “*nīyum nānum innēr niṟkil*” (when both of us stand in this manner without rejecting his favour). He \[emperumān\] does not understand that he should create the partner for union! He is not thinking that two persons are required for a union!
- *uyirin param anṟip perugumāl vētkaiyum* – The affection grew so much that the ātmā could not bear it. Oh dear! The affection is not limited to the atomic size of this ātmā, but it keeps growing like a flood.
- *Al* – Indicates the greatness of the anguish. āḻvār is saying “*nenjam urugumāl, vētkaiyum perugumāl*” to highlight the uncontrollable anguish.
- *en seygēn* – Should I stop the heart from breaking? Should I stop the affection from growing? ōr shall I avoid his qualities which are the cause for these?
- *toṇḍanēn* – Shall I eliminate my desire which is the cause for such breaking of the heart and increasing of affection? The desire is not letting me withdraw saying that he is beyond us, and his greatness is not letting me forget him and survive.
- *teru ellām kāvi kamaḻ* – āḻvār is highlighting the reason for his heart break and increase in affection.
- *teru ellām* – Not limiting to main streets, the fragrance of red lily is present everywhere in smaller lanes as well as main streets. \[Alternative explanation\] Since the ponds are present in every part of the town, both inside and outside are equally very fragrant. The fragrance of red lily in the streets and “*sarvaganda:*” (root of all fragrance) is inside.
- *tirukkātkarai maruviya* – With this, the greatness over paratvam (his presence in paramapaddma) and avatāram (incarnations) is explained. paratvam is too far away; \[vibhava\] avatāram is limited by time \[but arcāvatāram is eternal\].
- *māyan* – One who can drive others crazy with his beauty, simplicity etc.
- *māyam* – His interaction while being together. He interacted with āḻvār as a needy person will interact with a generous, rich person.
- *ninaidoṟē* – While thinking about the town, while thinking about the beauty and while thinking about his simplicity of behaving as if he does not have an abode and beauty.
- *ninaidoṟum* – How long did he think? How long he avoided thinking? emperumān is capable of giving enjoyment to millions of contradictory entities; āḻvār is capable of enjoying a single quality of emperumān forever, immersing fully every moment in that quality as if it is fresh every time; he says in [tiruvāimoḻi 2.5.4](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/03/thiruvaimozhi-2-5-4-epporulum-thanay/) “*appoḻudaikku appoḻudu en ārāvamudam*” (every moment, emperumān is like infinitely reliśable nectar).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 9.6.2. Ninaidorum

*ninai toṟum sollum doṟum nenju idindu ugum vinai koḷ sīr pādilum vēm enadu ār uyir sunai koḷ pūnjōlait ten kātkarai en appā! ninaigilēn nān unākku ātceyyum nīrmaiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

sunai koḷ – having ponds; pūm sōlai – having flower gardens; then – attractive; kātkarai – in tirukkātkarai; en appā – oh one who is standing as my eternal relative!; vinai koḷ – revealing your activities relating to the great union; sīr – qualities such as śeela (simplicity), saulabhya (easy approacability) etc; ninai toṟum – thinking about it, every moment; nenju – the tool which is used for such thinking; idindu – becoming broken; sollum toṟum – every moment, I speak; urugum – the heart will melt and become fluid; pādilum – even if I tried to sustain myself by singing (as said in tiruvāimoḻi 1.7.10 “pādi iḷaippilam” (I have no reason to take a break from glorifying his incomparable auspicious qualities)); enadu Ar uyir – my ātmā (self) which is the abode of the senses; vēm – became burnt; nān – I (who am like this); unakku ātceyyum – to perform service to you; nīrmai – form/aspect; ninaigilēn – unable to even think

**Перевод:**

**Oh one who is standing as my eternal relative in attractive tirukkātkarai which is having ponds in flower gardens! My heart which is the tool for thinking about you, becomes broken and is melting and becoming fluid, every moment I think and speak about your qualities such as śeela, saulabhya etc which are revealed in your activities relating to the great union; even if I tried to sustain myself by singing, my ātmā which is the abode of the senses becomes burnt; I am unable to think about the form/aspect to perform service to you.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the second pāsuram, āḻvār tells emperumān in tirukkātkarai “I cannot think about the interactions I had with you”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. நினை தொறும் சொல்லும் தொறும் நெஞ்சு இடிந்து உகும் வினை கொள் சீர் பாடிலும் வேம் எனது ஆர் உயிர் சுனை கொள் பூஞ்சோலைத் தென் காட்கரை என் அப்பா! நினைகிலேன் நான் உனக்கு ஆட்செய்யும் நீர்மையே ninai toṟum sollum doṟum nenju idindu ugum vinai koḷ sīr pādilum vēm enadu Ar uyir sunai koḷ pūnjōlait then kātkarai en appā! ninaigilēn nān unākku ātceyyum nīrmaiyē*

- *ninai toṟum* – He will set out to meditate; but he will lose strength to continue meditating upon [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), still he will not forget; again he will set out to meditate; will not be able to complete; how long did he think? How long did he stop?
- *sollum toṟum* – It is obvious that what cannot be meditated, can also be not spoken about. \[But how will [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) speak about emperumān\] Unlike as said in “*mana:pūrvōvāguttara:*” (first in mind and then speech), but as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 3.8.2](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/10/thiruvaimozhi-3-8-2-nenjame/) “*kuṟaḷāgiya vanjanē ennum eppōdum en vāsagam*” (I will always say “Oh mischievous one who assumed the form of a vāmana!”) āḻvār’s mouth will always speak about emperumān; due to this impression, he will speak without even thinking; and that will enter his heart through his ears, soak there and will melt his heart, since it is on emperumān who has great qualities.
- *nenju idindu ugum* – The heart melts and becomes fluid. Just as a flood will erode the banks and consume them as well, the heart dissolved and became invisible.
- *vinai koḷ …* – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s auspicious qualities which will eliminate sins. The qualities which eliminate the sins of everyone, ended up destroying me only; alternatively, sīr – simplicity, vinai – activity, that is, emperumān’s humble interactions which are a result of his simplicity. It is said in śrī rāmāyaṇam kiśkindā kāṇḍam 4.18 “*lōkanāta: purā bhūtvā sugrīvam nātam iccati*” (One who is the lord of the universe, is now desiring to have sugrīva as his leader).
- *pādilum* – Other than incoherently speaking, one will enthusiastically sing as well; even while doing that.
- *vēm enadu Ar uyir* – Not only my mind, it even burnt the soul which cannot be burnt. Just as snow which cools down everything will wither a lotus only, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s qualities which eliminate the sins of everyone, are harmful to me only.
- *vēm enadu Ar uyir* – When [śrī bhagavt gītā 2.24](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/2-24/) said “*adāhyam*” (cannot be burnt), it meant that the ātmā cannot be burnt by fire, but does not apply to bhagavān’s qualities.
- *sunai …* – The places which immersed [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) \[in [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)\]. Oh one who is present as the eternal relative in tirukkātkarai which is having ponds and attractive gardens!
- *ninaigilēn nān unakku ātceyyum nīrmaiyē* – I am unable to think how I can serve you.
- *nān* – I who remained as said in tiruvāimoḻi 3.3.1 “*vaḻuvilā adimai seyya vēṇḍu nām*” (I am desiring to perform continuous service).
- *unakku* – To you who are the apt lord. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying about the way [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) humbly interacted with him by saying “*ātceyyum nīrmai*” due to his (āḻvār’s) humility \[as it was an intimate, confidential interaction\]. While emperumān humbly interacted with āḻvār, āḻvār is saying in this manner, to not lose this opportunity of expression as well. When embār was asked “Why is āḻvār saying that he does not know how to serve emperumān, while it was emperumān who humbly served āḻvār?” embār replies “will he lose this opportunity of expression also?”

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 9.6.3. Nirmaiyal nenjam

*nīrmaiyāl nenjam vanjittup pugundu ennai īrmai seydu en uyir āy en uyir uṇḍān sīr malgu sōlait ten kātkarai en appan kār mugil vaṇṇan tan kaḷvam aṟigilēn*

**Пословный перевод:**

nīrmaiyāl – due to revealing the quality of svasvāmi sambandam (property-owner relationship); nenjam – my heart; vanjittu – owning me; pugundu – entering me; ennai īrmai seydu – melting me; en uyir āy – (with these two aspects) being the one who sustains me; en uyir uṇḍān – being the one who consumes me; sīr malgu – having abundance of honey and flowers; sōlai – having garden; then – beautiful; kātkarai – due to the presence in tirukkātkarai; en appan – being my benefactor; kār mugil vaṇṇan than – the monsoon-cloud like greatly generous emperumān‘s; kaḷvam – his mischievous act where the means and end are different; aṟigilēn – I don’t understand it to be in a particular manner

**Перевод:**

**emperumān owned me and entered my heart by revealing the quality of svasvāmi sambandam; he melts me, he is the one who sustains me and consumes me; he is my benefactor due to being present in tirukkātkarai which is having beautiful garden with abundance of honey and flowers; I don’t understand the monsoon-cloud like greatly generous emperumān’s mischievous act where the means and end are different, to be in a particular manner.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the third pāsuram, āḻvār says “I cannot think about the ways emperumān mischievously made me loyal to him and saying ‘I will accept your service’, entering me and fully taking me with his qualities and disorderly activities”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. நீர்மையால் நெஞ்சம் வஞ்சித்துப் புகுந்து என்னை ஈர்மை செய்து என் உயிர் ஆய் என் உயிர் உண்டான் சீர் மல்கு சோலைத் தென் காட்கரை என் அப்பன் கார் முகில் வண்ணன் தன் கள்வம் அறிகிலேன் nīrmaiyāl nenjam vanjittup pugundu ennai īrmai seydu en uyir āy en uyir uṇḍān sīr malgu sōlait then kātkarai en appan kār mugil vaṇṇan than kaḷvam aṟigilēn*

- *nīrmaiyāl nenjam vanjittup pugundu ennai īrmai seydu* – He convinced me that we should interact in a manner that he is the lord and I am the servitor, and entered my heart through deception; if he had told that their interactions will be contrary to that, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) would not have agreed. krutrima (deception) means saying one way and doing it differently.

When asked “What was that?” āḻvār says,

- *nīrmaiyāl ennai īrmai seydu* – nīrmai means his humble interactions, and śeelam (simplicity) which is the cause for that.
- *ennai* – I who was thinking “he will arrive for proper interaction” as truth.
- *īrmai seydu* – Make me melt. Saying that [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) melted him with his humble actions; or saying that he is causing compassion in my heart; or to make me become fluid.
- *en uyirāy en uyir uṇḍān* – He entered me as if he will sustain me, but ended up finishing me off. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) would not have agreed for his entry if he entered to cause harm! While both united, emperumān ended up being the sole enjoyer;
- *en uyirāy en uyir uṇḍān* – Alternative explanation – he made me to be totally dependent on him and consumed me.
- *sīr malgu sōlai* – Very beautiful garden. The completeness he acquired by uniting with me, is showcased by the garden in his town itself.
- *then kātkarai en appan* – One who is sulabha (easily approachable \[due to be being in tirukkātkarai\]) and nirupādika bandu (eternal relative \[due to being my father\]); one who is present here highlighting the relationship which says that he is determined to fulfil my desire.
- kār mugil vaṇṇan – Due to his union with me, he acquired freshness in his divine form similar to a monsoon season cloud which has absorbed the whole ocean. Just as he desired in [tiruvāimoḻi 8.5.3](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/03/thiruvaimozhi-8-5-3-mudi-ser-senni-amma/) “*tū nīr mugil pōl tōnṟāyē*” (you should appear like a pure cloud), [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) appeared and allowed [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) to enjoy him, this is how fresh emperumān was.
- *than kaḷvam aṟigilēn* – I don’t understand his actions which are different in the beginning and the end. I don’t understand his act of serving me while he set out to accept service from me.
- *aṟigilēn* – The lord who is greater than everyone else should not interact in this humble manner; am I confused? [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is talking about what is said in [tiruvāimoḻi 8.7.3](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/04/thiruvaimozhi-8-7-3-arul-than/) “*maruḷ tān īdō*” (is this hallucination?) in union.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 9.6.4. Arigilen tannuyir

*aṟigilēn tannuḷ anaittu ulagum niṟka neṟimaiyāl tānum avaṟṟuḷ niṟkum pirān veṟi kamaḻ sōlait ten kātkarai en appan siṟiya en āruyir uṇḍa tiru aruḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tannuḷ – in a fraction of his vow; anaittulagum – all entities of all worlds; niṟka – to remain firmly; tānum – he too; neṟimaiyāl – in proper manner (of servitor-master which is a result of body-soul relationship); avaṟṟuḷ – in them; niṟkum – remaining; pirān – being the benefactor; veṟi kamaḻ – spreading distinguished fragrance; sōlai – having garden; then kākarai – standing in tirukkātkarai; en appan – my lord; siṟiya en – very lowly me, my; Ar uyir – ātmā (soul); uṇḍa – intently enjoyed; tiru aruḷ – favour of sauśeelyam (simplicity); aṟigilēn – I am unable to precisely understand

**Перевод:**

**emperumān supports all entities of all the worlds to remain firmly in a fraction of his vow and remains in them firmly as well; my lord, being the benefactor, is standing in tirukkātkarai which is having garden spreading distinguished fragrance; I, who am very lowly, am unable to precisely understand his favour of sauśeelyam with which he intently enjoyed my ātmā.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fourth pāsuram, āḻvār says “It is impossible for me to understand the love shown towards me who is very lowly by emperumān who mingles with everyone properly even as he is the lord and all the entities in the entire world are his servitors”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. அறிகிலேன் தன்னுள் அனைத்து உலகும் நிற்க நெறிமையால் தானும் அவற்றுள் நிற்கும் பிரான் வெறி கமழ் சோலைத் தென் காட்கரை என் அப்பன் சிறிய என் ஆர் உயிர் உண்ட திரு அருளே aṟigilēn tannuḷ anaittu ulagum niṟka neṟimaiyāl tānum avaṟṟuḷ niṟkum pirān veṟi kamaḻ sōlait then kātkarai en appan siṟiya en āruyir uṇḍa tiru aruḷē*

- *aṟigilēn* – I don’t understand if he \[[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)\] did it out of joy or to destroy me.
- *tannuḷ anaittulagum niṟka* – He is only doing favours for everything other than me! While all the worlds depend on a fraction of his vow, he is remaining in all of them due to his being the lord; such emperumān interacted only with [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) in this improper manner \[where he served āḻvār\]! āḻvār is speaking about what is said in [tiruvāimoḻi 8.7.8](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/04/thiruvaimozhi-8-7-8-ariyen-marrarul/) “*mūvulgum than neṟiyā vayiṟṟil koṇḍu – siṟiyēnudaic cindaiyuḷ – ninṟoḻindārē*” (he who is having the three worlds inside him without disregarding the protector-protected relationship, stood in my heart, in me who is very lowly). One who protected the whole universe during the danger of deluge, destroyed only me. He will destroy the enemies with arrow and his followers with his qualities. He is protecting in a neutral manner! Wound caused by arrow can be healed; but there is no remedy for the wound caused by his qualities.
- *verṟi …* – There is something \[myself\] desired by one who is having such beautiful town! Garden which has rising fragrance.
- *en appan* – My creator himself destroyed me!
- *siṟiya en Ar uyir uṇḍa* – The good soul of this lowly person – my self, where I am very lowly. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is thinking that just as there is no limit for [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s supremacy, there is no limit for his own inferiority.
- *en Ar uyir uṇḍa* – He is thinking himself to be very small \[*siṟiyēn*\]; emperumān is thinking āḻvār to be greater than nityasiddas (nityasūris) \[*Ar uyir*\]. emperumān thinks “What is the use if he thinks himself to be small? Does he know about himself?” and pursues āḻvār with great intent.
- *tiru aruḷ aṟigilēn* – This is not an act in true knowledge; would one not stop at proper limit when acting per true knowledge? Love will destroy all rules.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 9.6.5. Tiruvarul seybavanpola

*tiru aruḷ seybavan pōla ennuḷ pugundu uruvamum ār uyirum udanē uṇḍān tiru vaḷar sōlait ten kātkarai en appan karu vaḷar mēni en kaṇṇan kaḷvangaḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tiruvaruḷ – the great favour (of accepting my service, as I prayed in tiruvāimoḻi 3.3.1 “adimai seyya vēṇḍunām“); seybavanpōla – like those who do; ennuḷ – in my heart; pugundu – entered; uruvamum – my body (which is to be given up by me); Ar uyirum – and the soul which is pervading (in the body); udanē uṇḍān – he desired without discriminating between what is to be given up and what is to be pursued!; tiruvaḷar – most beautiful; sōlai – having garden; tenkātkarai – in tirukkātkarai; en appan – being my lord; karuvaḷar mēni – having form with dark complexion (due to uniting with me); en kaṇṇan – my very obedient kriṣṇa’s; kaḷvangaḷē – deceptive acts are!

**Перевод:**

**emperumān entered my heart like those who will do great favour, and desired for my body and the soul which is pervading, without discriminating between what is to be given up and what is to be pursued! This is how deceptive the acts of my obedient kriṣṇa who is my lord having form with dark complexion and residing in tirukkātkarai having most beautiful garden, are! Some of his acts are coming as an enjoyable person to favour me, benefited being the enjoyer, coming to me as if he will highlight the difference between body and soul to me, enjoying my body and my soul without discriminating between them and becoming radiant due to that.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fifth pāsuram, āḻvār becomes blissful thinking “emperumān‘s greatness is such that he entered in me as if accepting my service but consumed my body and soul!”*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. திரு அருள் செய்பவன் போல என்னுள் புகுந்து உருவமும் ஆர் உயிரும் உடனே உண்டான் திரு வளர் சோலைத் தென் காட்கரை என் அப்பன் கரு வளர் மேனி என் கண்ணன் கள்வங்களே tiru aruḷ seybavan pōla ennuḷ pugundu uruvamum Ar uyirum udanē uṇḍān tiru vaḷar sōlait then kātkarai en appan karu vaḷar mēni en kaṇṇan kaḷvangaḷē*

- *tiruvaruḷ seybavanpōla* – He entered me as if presenting himself fully and accepting my service. For what is said in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.1.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/03/thiruvaimozhi-1-1-1-uyarvara-uyarnalam/) “*tuyaraṟu sudaradi toḻugai*” (worshiping his radiant divine feet), he entered as “*mayarvaṟa madinalam aruḷvār*” (blessing faultless knowledge and devotion). Here “*pōla*” (like) indicates, that emperumān did not shower his mercy on [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/), rather, he accepted the mercy of āḻvār.
- *ennuḷ pugundu* – Entering me who desired to perform eternal service as said in tiruvāimoḻi 3,3,1 “*vaḻuvilā adimai*“.
- *uruvamum* – First [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) desired for [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s body which was known as dirty body as said in tiruviruttam 1 “*aḻukkudambu*“; before emperumān’s acceptance of āḻvār, āḻvār had liking for this same body; after emperumān accepted āḻvār, emperumān started liking āḻvār’s body. āḻvār’s interaction with emperumān led to āḻvār’s svarūpa jñānam (knowledge about true nature of the self); emperumān’s interaction with āḻvār led to emperumān’s dēhātmābhimānam (considering body and soul (of āḻvār) to be equally enjoyable).
- *uruvamum* – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) thinks “Do I need [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)? Is it not sufficient for me to enjoy what is considered as āḻvār’s belonging?”
- *Ar uyirum* – Stretching up to the ātmā, since his love in āḻvār’s divine body will not stop there. Since the body cannot be separated from soul, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s desire to enjoy cannot be stopped at the body.
- *udanē uṇḍān* – He did not consume them showing discrimination between them.
- *uṇḍān* – He himself became enjoyer, without giving any opportunity for me.
- *tiruvaḷar sōlait tenkātkarai en appan* – The garden in this town, which has its beauty increasing and his own beauty are revealing how he enjoyed [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) fully.
- *karu vaḷar mēni* – His form where his darkness keeps increasing. We are not seeing here, what is explained about his form in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 1.2.1 “*sadaikarūpa rūpāya*” (one who is having unchanging divine auspicious form).
- *nam kaṇṇan* – kriṣṇa who is obedient towards his devotees.
- *kaḷvangaḷ* – His acts which appear one way on the face and different inside; entering the heart as if he is accepting [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s service, but ending up serving āḻvār; entering the heart saying that he will eliminate the body which is a hurdle, but ending up enjoying āḻvār’s body and soul (ātmā) without any discrimination; entering as the enjoyable person but ending up being the enjoyer; entering to favour me but ending as being the one receivied my favour and revealing all of these in his divine form. [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) eliminated my ātmāpahāram (claiming ownership of self) by himself claiming ownership of my soul.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 9.6.6. Engannan kalvam

*en kaṇṇan kaḷvam enakkuc cemmāy niṟkum am kaṇṇan uṇḍa en ār uyirk kōdu idu punkaṇmai eydip pulambi irāp pagal en kaṇṇan enṟu avan kātkarai ēttumē*

**Пословный перевод:**

em kaṇṇan – kriṣṇa who has great love towards me, his; kaḷvam – deceptive acts (which are one way on the face and other way in the inside); enakkuc cemmāy irukkum – look truthful to me; angaṇṇan – being desirous, due to his love; uṇḍa – due to consuming; kōdu – faulty; en Ar uyir idu – my soul; punkaṇmai eydi – attaining a miserable state; en kaṇṇan enṟu – saying that he is obedient to me; irāp pagal pulambi – lamenting in night and day; avan kātkarai – tirukkātkarai where he is residing; ēhtum – praising

**Перевод:**

**The deceptive acts of kriṣṇa who has great love towards me look truthful to me. My faulty soul considering his being lovingly desirous and consuming of it, attaining a miserable state, saying that he is obedient towards it, lamenting in night and day, is praising tirukkātkarai where he is residing. punkaṇmai is also explained as being very less intelligent.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the sixth pāsuram, āḻvār says “When I see kriṣṇa who greatly torments me after coming to me as if accepting my service, I will consider his deceptive acts to be truthful acts”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. என் கண்ணன் கள்வம் எனக்குச் செம்மாய் நிற்கும் அம் கண்ணன் உண்ட என் ஆர் உயிர்க் கோது இது புன்கண்மை எய்தி புலம்பி இராப் பகல் என் கண்ணன் என்று அவன் காட்கரை ஏத்துமே en kaṇṇan kaḷvam enakkuc cemmāy niṟkum am kaṇṇan uṇḍa en Ar uyirk kōdu idu punkaṇmai eydip pulambi irāp pagal en kaṇṇan enṟu avan kātkarai ēttumē*

- *em kaṇṇan kaḷvam enakkuc cemmāy niṟkum* – The deceptive acts of kriṣṇa who appears to be obedient towards me, look truthful to me. If I get caught in his deception once, I will never retract. As he is in front of me, all his acts appear truthful to me. A tamiḻ scholar explained “*enakkuc cemmāy irukkum*” as “*enakkuc cēmamāy irukkum*” (will be my protection). Though it ends in previous pāsuram as “*nam kaṇṇan kaḷvangaḷ*“, it starts here as “*em kaṇṇan kaḷvangaḷ*“, since nām and yām are synonyms, and here the type of antādi (andādi) is known as “*poruḷ isai andādi*” (where the meaning of the words are connected together). If it ended in previous pāsuram as “*em kaṇṇan kaḷvangaḷ*“, that would be “*iyal isai andādi*” (words are connected together directly).
- *angaṇṇan uṇḍa* – Enjoyed by the most desirous. Very desirous persons are known as “*angaṇṇar*“.
- *en Ar uyirk kōdu idu* – My ātmā which is like chaff. He interacted with the soul to turn it into chaff.
- *punkaṇmai* – pēgaṇippu (sorrow); saying that he had an evil glance. bhattar explains this as “surviving again”. nampiḷḷai mercifully explained – nanjīyar said “This does not match the word; how can we relate the word with the meaning which we heard \[from bhattar\]?” I replied “What has become chaff, needs to be enlivened again to feel the sorrow; this can be explained in that sense”. nanjīyar heard that and became very pleased.
- *em kaṇṇan enṟu irāp pagal pulambi* – Calling out in day and night saying “kriṣṇa was obedient to me previously”, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) praised tirukkātkarai which is the abode of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/); as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 33.17 “*rāghavasya nivēśanē*” (śrī rāma’s residence).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 9.6.7. Katkarai ettum

*kātkarai ēttum adanuḷ kaṇṇā! ennum vētkai nōy kūra ninaindu karaindu ugum ātkoḷvān ottu en uyir uṇḍa māyanāl kōḷ kuṟaipattadu en ār uyir kōḷ uṇḍē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ātkoḷvān ottu – entering in as if accepting my service; en uyir – my ātmā (soul); uṇḍa – consumed inside him; māyanāl – by the amazing personality; kōḷ uṇḍē – even after being consumed; kōḷ – enjoyment; kuṟaipattadu – said to be remainder; en Ar uyir – my soul; kātkarai – tirukkātkarai (where he is residing); ēttum – will praise; adanuḷ – standing in there; kaṇṇā ennum – will call him who is obedient, as “kaṇṇā”; vētkai nōy – desire to enjoy; kūra – to increase; ninaindu – thought (about his interactions); karaindu – becoming broken; ugum – will melt to become fluid

**Перевод:**

**emperumān, the amazing personality, entered me as if accepting my service and consumed my ātmā and kept me inside; even after doing that, my ātmā which appears to have some enjoyment remaining in it, will praise tirukkātkarai; it will stand in there and call him who is obedient, as “kaṇṇā”; it will think about increasing the desire to enjoy, become broken and will melt to become fluid.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the seventh pāsuram, āḻvār says “emperumān entered me as if accepting my service, consumed my soul fully and still remained hungry”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. காட்கரை ஏத்தும் அதனுள் கண்ணா! என்னும் வேட்கை நோய் கூர நினைந்து கரைந்து உகும் ஆட்கொள்வான் ஒத்து என் உயிர் உண்ட மாயனால் கோள் குறைபட்டது என் ஆர் உயிர் கோள் உண்டே kātkarai ēttum adanuḷ kaṇṇā! ennum vētkai nōy kūra ninaindu karaindu ugum ātkoḷvān ottu en uyir uṇḍa māyanāl kōḷ kuṟaipattadu en Ar uyir kōḷ uṇḍē*

- *kātkarai ēttum* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) will praise [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s abode even more than praising emperumān himself.
- *adanuḷ kaṇṇā ennum* – The greatness acquired after entering this town, which is greater than his paratvam (supremacy). As he says “en kaṇṇā”, he will praise kātkarai; as he praises the town, he will then praise emperumān; he does not go anywhere beyond him and his town.
- *vētkai nōy kura ninaindu* – Meditating to increase the desire to enjoy.
- *karaindugum* – Will become broken, and melt to make others think that there is no form.
- *ātkoḷvān ottu en uyir uṇḍa māyanāl* – By the amazing personality who entered me as if accepting my service and flattened me; [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is explicitly revealing what he concealed previously saying “*tiruvaruḷ*” (divine mercy). The amazing aspect is – when [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) was together with āḻvar, he remained humble and interacted blissfully with āḻvār.
- *en Ar uyir kōḷ uṇḍē – kōḷ kuṟaipattadu* – Even after consuming my ātmā fully (there was some remainder in me); [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is thinking that there is still some enjoyment left in self, since [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is still pursuing āḻvār; since āḻvār remains in anguish still, he thinks that there is still something left in self. āḻvār is thinking that a sarvajña (omniscient) \[lord\] will not show so much love in something which does not exist.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 9.6.8. Kol undan

*kōḷ uṇḍān anṟi vandu en uyir tān uṇḍān nāḷum nāḷ vandu ennai muṟṟavum tān uṇḍān kāḷa nīr mēgat ten kātkarai en appaṟku āḷ anṟē pattadu? en ār uyir pattadē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kōḷ uṇḍān anṟi vandu – coming unconditionally instead of being pursued (by me); en uyir – my ātmā (soul); tān – he; uṇḍān – eagerly consumed; nāḷu nāḷ vandu – arriving fresh everyday; ennai – me (soul, qualities and body) (with great affection); muṟṟavum tān uṇḍān – consumed me without any remainder; kāḷa – black coloured; nīr – risen after extracting water; mēgam – like a dark cloud; then kātkarai – residing in tirukkātkarai; en appaṟku – for my lord; ātpattadau anṟē – did I not become a servitor?; en Ar uyir pattadē – my ātmā became a servitor!

**Перевод:**

**emperumān came unconditionally instead of being pursued by me and eagerly consumed my soul. He is arriving fresh everyday and consuming me without any remainder. Did I not become a servitor for my lord who is residing in tirukkātkarai, who is like a black coloured dark cloud which has risen after extracting water? My ātmā became a servitor!**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the eighth pāsuram, āḻvār says “I am unable to bear his great quality of consuming me as if it is a rare accomplishment, though he is enjoying me everyday”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. கோள் உண்டான் அன்றி வந்து என் உயிர் தான் உண்டான் நாளும் நாள் வந்து என்னை முற்றவும் தான் உண்டான் காள நீர் மேகத் தென் காட்கரை என் அப்பற்கு ஆள் அன்றே பட்டது? என் ஆர் உயிர் பட்டதே kōḷ uṇḍān anṟi vandu en uyir tān uṇḍān nāḷum nāḷ vandu ennai muṟṟavum tān uṇḍān kāḷa nīr mēgat then kātkarai en appaṟku āḷ anṟē pattadu? en Ar uyir pattadē*

- *kōḷ uṇḍān anṟi vandu en uyir tān uṇḍān* – Many merciful explanations are given for this.
   - Instead of accepting any favour from me, he enjoyed my ātmā unconditionally.
   - He eagerly enjoyed me as if he has never got any such enjoyable entity.
   - While I have not attained him, he attained me.
- *nāḷu nāḷ vandu* – Did he retract saying “have we not enjoyed him already?” after consuming me for one day? \[No\] He arrived everyday and enjoyed [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/). This is the way [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) thinks about āḻvār, just as āḻvār had said of emperumān in [tiruvāimoḻi 2.5.4](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/03/thiruvaimozhi-2-5-4-epporulum-thanay/) “*appoḻudaikku appoḻudu en ārāvamudamē*” (every moment, emperumān is like infinitely reliśable nectar).
- *ennai muṟṟavum tān uṇḍān* – emperumān who is vibhu (omnipresent) fully enjoyed [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) (ātmā) who is miniscule, and he considered it to be his fortune/greatness and praised āḻvār. āḻvār said in [tiruvāimoḻi 9.6.4](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/08/thiruvaimozhi-9-6-4-arigilen-thannuyir/) “*siṟiya en Ar uyir*” looking at himself; he is now saying this way, looking at [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s experience.
- *kāḷa nīr mēgat tenkātkarai ennappaṟku* – For emperumān, the unconditional relative who is having dark, water-filled cloud like form, and who is residing in tirukkātkarai as if such cloud rained there. This is his physical beauty; his residence; still why is he hankering so much as if he is lacking in something!
- *āḷ anṟē pattadu* – Did I not become his servitor? Did I fight with him like rāvaṇa et al?
- *en Ar uyir pattadē* – This is the struggle of an ātmā! Those who opposed will lose their body or apply medicine to the wounds caused by him; but here ātmā itself has been harmed; there is no remedy for the harm caused by his qualities which affected the ātmā itself.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 9.6.9. Aruyir pattadu

*ār uyir pattadu enadu uyir pattadu? pēr idaḻt tāmaraik kaṇ kani vāyadu ōr kār eḻil mēgat ten kātkarai kōyil koḷ sīr eḻil nāl tadam dōḷ deyva vārikkē*

**Пословный перевод:**

pēr idaḻ – having large petal; tāmarai – like a lotus; kaṇ – eyes; kani – reddish like a fruit; vāyadu – having lips/mouth; ōr – distinguished; kār eḻil – having dark beauty; mēga – like a cloud; then – beautiful; kātkarai – tirukkātkarai; kōyil koḷ – having as residence; sīr eḻil – having vīraśrī (bravery) and beauty; nāl – four different; tadam – huge; tōḷ – having divine shoulders; deyvam – for dēvatās; vārikku – being the ocean which is the originating place; enadu uyir – my ātmā; pattadu – being immersed as the enjoyable object; Ar uyir pattadu – did the nityasūris who enjoy him eternally immerse in the same way?

**Перевод:**

**emperumān is having eyes which resemble a lotus with large petal; his lips/mouth resemble a reddish fruit; he resembles a beautiful cloud having dark beauty; he is having tirukkātkarai as his residence; he is having four huge, divine shoulders which are having vīraśrī (bravery) and beauty; he is the ocean which is the originating place for dēvatās; did nityasūris, who enjoy such emperumān, eternally immerse in him the same way that my ātmā immersed in him as the enjoyable object? Implies that the experience with new/beloved person is more enjoyable than prevailing/married person.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the ninth pāsuram, when asked “Would he not indulge in this manner with whosoever he interacts with?” āḻvār says “Did nityarsūris who are fully immersed in his qualities go through what I went through?”*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. ஆர் உயிர் பட்டது எனது உயிர் பட்டது? பேர் இதழ்த் தாமரைக் கண் கனி வாயது ஓர் கார் எழில் மேகத் தென் காட்கரை கோயில் கொள் சீர் எழில் நால் தடம் தோள் தெய்வ வாரிக்கே? Ar uyir pattadu enadu uyir pattadu? pēr idaḻt tāmaraik kaṇ kani vāyadu ōr kār eḻil mēgat then kātkarai kōyil koḷ sīr eḻil nāl tadam dōḷ deyva vārikkē*

- *Ar uyir pattadu enadu uyir pattadu* – Did nityasūris become immersed as I did in him? Did nityasūris who reside in nityavibhūti (paramapadam) get the experience I got in this material realm which is no place for enjoying bhagavān? [emperumānār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/emperumanar/) says “*ingu enaduyir pattadu angu āruyir pattadu*?” (whatever I experienced here, did anyone experience it there?). [nanjīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nanjiyar/) mercifully explained – I asked \[[parāśara bhattar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/parasara-bhattar/)\] “īsn’t everyone engaged in enjoying [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s qualities? Why is this distinguished experience for āḻvār?” he explained “Just a newly married woman will sweat and have goosebumps when coming in contact with her husband, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is feeling this way since this experience is new to him \[got it in this birth only\]”

Subsequently, āḻvār explains how his life was finished.

- *pēr idaḻt tāmaraik kaṇ kanivāyadu ōr* – One who is having eyes which resemble a lotus with large petal and reddish lips/mouth.
- *kār eḻil mēgat tenkātkarai kōyil koḷ* – Having a form which resembles dark and beautiful cloud, and having tirukkātkarai as his abode.
- *sīr eḻil nāl tadam tōḷ* – Having four, well-rounded, divine shoulders which resemble well branched out kalpa taru (celestial tree), having vīraśrī (bravery) and beauty.
- *deyva vārikku* – vāri – ocean. The ocean which is the origin for dēvatās. The creator of dēvatās. One who is the creator of prideful dēvatās, finished me who has no pride! He finished [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) by showing his beauty and his presence in this town.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 9.6.10. Varik kondu

*vārik koṇḍu unnai viḻunguvan kāṇil enṟu ārvu uṟṟa ennai oḻiya ennil munnam pārittut tān ennai muṟṟap paruginān kār okkum kātkarai appan kadiyanē*

**Пословный перевод:**

unnaik kāṇil – if I see you; vārik koṇḍu – without leaving anything such as your svarūpam (true nature), rūpam (form), guṇa (qualities), vibhūti (wealth), behind; viḻunguvan enṟu – vowing to swallow completely; ārvuṟṟa – desired; ennai oḻiya – more than me; ennil munnam – before me (from the time of my existence); pārittu – being eager; tān – he (who is beyond limits); ennai – me (who is insignificant); muṟṟa – fully; paruginān – drank; kār okkum – like a dark cloud (which drinks ocean); kātkarai appan – the benefactor who is standing in tirukkākarai; kadiyan – is very quick (in not allowing others to enjoy)

**Перевод:**

**I desired and vowed to swallow you fully without leaving anything such as your svarūpam (true nature), rūpam (form), guṇa (qualities), vibhūti (wealth), behind, if I see you; being more eager than I, he fully drank me before me; the benefactor who is standing like a dark cloud in tirukkākarai, is very quick.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the tenth pāsuram, āḻvār is mercifully explaining that emperumān who united with āḻvār has more desire than āḻvār himself.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. வாரிக் கொண்டு உன்னை விழுங்குவன் காணில் என்று ஆர்வு உற்ற என்னை ஒழிய என்னில் முன்னம் பாரித்துத் தான் என்னை முற்றப் பருகினான் கார் ஒக்கும் காட்கரை அப்பன் கடியனே vārik koṇḍu unnai viḻunguvan kāṇil enṟu ārvu uṟṟa ennai oḻiya ennil munnam pārittut tān ennai muṟṟap paruginān kār okkum kātkarai appan kadiyanē*

- *vārik koṇḍu* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) thought “Let me fully consume [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) so that there is no remainder of him for others”. That is he was eager as per his prayer in [tiruvāimoḻi 3.3.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/08/thiruvaimozhi-3-3-1-ozhivil-kalam/) “*vaḻuvilā adimai seyya vēṇḍunām*” (We should serve continuously). He thought “I will not let ananta, vainadēya et al serve him”; as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 31.25 “*aham sarvam kariśyāmi*” (I will serve you both (perumāḷ and pirātti) in all ways).
- *unnai* – You who is sarvaśēśi (lord of all).
- *viḻunguvan* – For a śēśabhūta (servitor), kainkaryam (service) is the sustainer.
- *kāṇil* – If I see you.
- *enṟu ārvuṟṟa* – Desired in this manner, i.e. had desire.
- *ennai oḻiya* – Instead of seeing my insignificance.
- *ennil munnam pārittu* – Having more eagerness than I, and desiring for me even before I desired for you. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s eagerness \[to consume [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)\] was only after he was accepted by ācārya \[in āḻvār’s case, emperumān himself is the ācārya\]; since there is no hurdle for the relationship \[between bhagavān and ātmā\], his eagerness is natural.
- *tān ennai* – He who is vibhu (omnipresent) and independent, \[consumed\] me who is aṇu (atomic) and dependent.
- *muṟṟap paruginān* – He melted me by manifesting his qualities and activities, and drank me without any remainder; as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 16.65 “*vacasā sāntvayitvainam lōcanābhyām pibanniva*” (śrī rāma pacified vibhīśaṇa by speaking and seeing as if swallowing vibhīśaṇa through the eyes); implies that [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) interacted with [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) consuming him fully. Previously āḻvār explained how emperumān ate him \[8th pāsuram – muṟṟavum tān uṇḍān\]; after eating, one will desire for water; so, āḻvār explains how emperumān drank him. This is emperumān’s “*uṇṇum sōṟu pargu nīr*” (food that is eaten and water that is drunk).
- *kār okkum kātkarai appan* – One who appeared in close proximity as a greatly magnanimous personality.
- *kadiyanē* – He will be quick to enjoy. When both try to enjoy each other, he will not leave any opportunity for the other person.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 9.6.11. Kadiyanay

*kadiyanāyk kanjanaik konṟa pirān tannaik kodi madiḷ ten kurugūrc catakōpan sol vadivu amai āyirattu ip pattināl sanmam mudivu eydi nāsam kaṇḍīrgaḷ em kānalē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kadiyanāy – being ahead of kamsa’s thoughts; kanjanaik konṟa – one who killed kamsa; pirān tannai – kriṣṇa, the great benefactor; kodi madiḷ – wall around fort, having flag; then kurugūr – leader of āḻvārtirunagari; satakōpan – nammāḻvār; sol – mercifully spoke; vadivu amai – rich, due to presenting bhagavān’s qualities in a nice form; āyirattu – among the thousand pāsurams; ippattināl – by this decad; em – our; sanmam – births; mudivu eydi – reaching the end; kānal – samsāra, the mirage; nāsam kaṇḍīr – will be destroyed

**Перевод:**

**nammāḻvār, the leader of āḻvārtirunagari which is having wall around its fort, with flag, mercifully spoke this decad among the thousand pāsurams which are rich due to presenting bhagavān’s qualities in a nice form, about kriṣṇa, the great benefactor who killed kamsa being ahead of kamsa’s thoughts; by this decad, our births will reach the end and samsāra, the mirage will be destroyed.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the end, āḻvār says “Those who are well versed in this decad among the thousand pāsurams composed by me, will have their \[worldly\] birth ended and the samsāra (bondage) which is the root-cause of such birth will be destroyed”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. கடியனாய்க் கஞ்சனைக் கொன்ற பிரான் தன்னை கொடி மதிள் தென் குருகூர்ச் சடகோபன் சொல் வடிவு அமை ஆயிரத்து இப் பத்தினால் சன்மம் முடிவு எய்தி நாசம் கண்டீர்கள் எம் கானலே kadiyanāyk kanjanaik konṟa pirān tannaik kodi madiḷ then kurugūrc catakōpan sol vadivu amai āyirattu ip pattināl sanmam mudivu eydi nāsam kaṇḍīrgaḷ em kānalē*

- *kadiyanāyk kanjanaik konṟa pirān tannai* – emperumān finished kamsa without anyone else knowing kamsa’s evil thoughts.
- *kadiyanāy* – Implies, this is not his natural attribute; it is said in periya tirumoḻi 5.8.3 “*koṇḍa sīṟṟam*” (anger which was voluntarily assumed).
- *pirān tannai* – One who was the benefactor previously, has now finished me! Finishing the favourable ones is harmful; finishing the enemies is favour.
- *kodi madiḷ tenkurugūr* – It was āḻvārtirunagari which celebrated the victory of kriṣṇa over kamsa, by hoisting the flag; isn’t it natural for the servitors to hoist the flag in their abodes, for the victory of their master?
- *vadivu amai āyiram* – Having collective beauty. Being fully beautiful. Since there is victory, there will be praises.
- *sanmam mudivu eydi* – Attaining an end for the series of births.
- *nāsam kaṇḍīrgaḷ em kānalē* – The samsāra which is the root-cause for birth will also be finished. kānal – mirage. Instead of taking birth here anymore, they will enter where bhagavān’s qualities can be enjoyed to the full satisfaction.

In the next article we will enjoy the next decad.

## 9.7 Enganal agangalivay

## 9.7.1. Enganal agangalivay

*engānal agangaḻivāy irai tērndinginidamarum sengāla mada nārāy! tirumūḻikkaḷatturaiyum kongār pūnduḻāy mudi engudakkūttarkken tūdāy nungālgaḷ en talai mēl keḻumīrō numarōdē*

**Пословный перевод:**

em kānal agam kaḻivāy – residing in the salt pan inside the garden on the seashore, to be considered as ours, to be engaged in your service; irai tērndu – with liking towards the food here, highlighting your great relationship; ingu – in my presence; inidu – with romantic love; amarum – residing; sem – being reddish as if a decoration for my head; kāl – having feet; madam – having humility to be ordered to fulfil our desire; nārāy – Oh cranes!; tirumūḻikkaḷattu – in tirumūḻikkaḷam; uṟaiyum – eternally residing there as āśrita sulabha (easily approachable for devotees); kongu Ar – with abundance of honey; pū – attractive; tuḻāy mudi – wearing divine crown which is decorated with tiruttuḻāy (tuḷasi); em kudak kūttarkku – one who is greatly enjoyable for us due to his heart-captivating activity of kudak kūttu (dancing with pots); en tūdāy – going as my messenger; numarōdē – with your wife and children (who are related to you, as said in “guruvad guruvargaśca drastavya:“); num kālgaḷ – your divine feet which walked for my sake; en talai mēl – on my head, which is the top most limb, which is the apt target for them; keḻumīr – should unite

**Перевод:**

**Oh cranes who are residing in the salt pan inside the garden on the seashore, to be considered as ours, to be engaged in your service, with liking towards the food here, highlighting your great relationship, with romantic love , having reddish feet as if a decoration for my head and having humility to be ordered to fulfil our desire! emperumān who is greatly enjoyable for us due to his heart-captivating activity of kudak kūttu (dancing with pots), is eternally residing in tirumūḻikkaḷam as āśrita sulabha and is wearing divine crown which is decorated with attractive tiruttuḻāy with abundance of honey; after going to such emperumān as my messenger, your divine feet which walked for my sake, along with your wife and children should unite on my head, which is the top most limb, which is the apt target for them. Though ācārya is the only upakāraka (benefactor), the gratitude for such favour should stretch up to his descendants. “nārāy” which is in singular, indicates the whole clan.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the first pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki tells some cranes how emperumān won over her by manifesting his beauty and activities and tells them “Please inform him my current state and on return, please place your divine feet on my head”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. engānal agangaḻivāy irai tērndinginidamarum sengāla mada nārāy! tirumūḻikkaḷatturaiyum kongār pūnduḻāy mudi engudakkūttarkken tūdāy nungālgaḷ en talai mēl keḻumīrō numarōdē*

- *em kānal* – While it is apt to enjoy together with the upakāraka (ācārya, the benefactor), here [parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying “*em*” (mine) to indicate the gratitude for the favour, of being unable sustain oneself without claiming ownership and handing it over \[to the one who did the favour\]. mamakāra (ownership) which occurs for the sake of helping others is desirable. It is the gratitude which made her say like this even though all her belongings are his from the day she surrendered to him. This is the reason for ātma samarpaṇam (offering oneself to bhagavān) too. kānal – garden on the seashore or land near the sea.
- *agam kaḻivāy* – In the salt pan which is located inside. They are so close that they don’t need permission to enter the private quarters. They are residing there as said in mahābhāratam udyōga parvam “*katitāni rahasyāni*” (secret matters were told).
- *irai tērndu* – Searching for food; as said in the same ślōkam “*gruhē bhuktam aśangitam*” (they took food without shyness); she is highlighting how they helped her previously, to make them help again.
- *ingu* – Unlike [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who stayed away from me to make me give up my own nature and send messenger to you, you are in my close proximity.
- *inidu amarum* – Living with us in a pleasing manner; also said as, living with distinguished pleasures.
- *sem kāla* – having reddish feet; the divine feet which I am planning to keep on my head resemble those which I was keeping in my lap (previously, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s divine feet).
- *mada nārāy* – Oh obedient cranes!
- *tirumūḻikkaḷattu uṟaiyum* – Has more greatness than paramapadam in tirumūḻikkaḷam due to being located in close proximity for those who come to you as messengers.
- *kongu Ar pūm tuḻāy mudi en kudakkūttarkku* – One who presented his decoration and heart-captivating activities for me. “em” is common for both his beauty and activities. “*em*” is *ātmani bahuvacanam* (calling oneself with resepect, what is said as “royal we”).
- *en tūdāy* – Engaging as the messenger for me who is won over by his decoration and activities, who will survive on attaining him and will perish on not attaining him.
- *num kālgaḷ en talai mēl* – The feet of yours, who are the benefactor on the head of mine, who will survive with your help; like those who wash the hair and wait for flowers to decorate the same. Their feet were seeking her head; and her head was waiting for their feet; both were existing for each other.
- *keḻumīrō* – Here it need not be done as a strict rule; as soon as I am made his, I will become yours too. Why don’t you unite your feet with my head?
- *numarōdē* – As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam bāla kāṇḍam 1.99 “*saputra pautra: sagaṇa:*” (along with children, grand children and other relatives), with all relatives. It is said in āpatstamba dharma “*ācāryavat ācārya putrē vrutti:*” (one should treat ācārya’s son as the ācārya himself).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 9.7.2. Numarodum piriyade

*numarōdum piriyādē nīrum num sēvalumāy amarkādal kuruginangāḷ! aṇimūḻikkaḷattuṟaiyum emarālum paḻippuṇḍu ingu en? tammāl iḻippuṇḍu tamarōdanguṟaivārkkut takkilamē? kēḷīrē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

numarōdum – with those who are related to you and who follow your heart; piriyādē – without separating; nīrum – you (who are obedient towards your spouses); num sēvalum – your spouses who are obedient towards you; amar kādal – having love to live together; kurugu inangāḷ – Oh groups of herons!; aṇi – attractive; mūḻikkaḷattu – in tirumūḻikkaḷam; uṟaiyum – eternally residing; tammāl – by him; iḻippuṇḍu – being abandoned after momentary union; emarālum – by those who are related to me; paḻippuṇḍu – being insulted; ingen – what is the use of the presence here!; tamarōdu – with the distinguished associates; angu – there; uṟaivārkku – for him who is eternally residing; takkilamē – would we not be acceptable?; kēḷīrē – You ask him

**Перевод:**

**Oh groups of herons who are having love to live together with your spouses who are obedient towards you, without separating, with those who are related to you and who follow your heart! What is the use of my presence here after being abandoned after momentary union by emperumān who is eternally residing in tirumūḻikkaḷam, and after being insulted by those who are related to me! Ask him “Would we not be acceptable for him who is eternally residing there?”**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the second pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki calls some herons and tells them “Go and ask emperumān in tirumūḻikkaḷam ‘Have I lost the opportunity to enjoy tirumūḻikkaḷam emperumān’s presence along with his devotees?’ ”*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. numarōdum piriyādē nīrum num sēvalumāy amarkādal kuruginangāḷ! aṇimūḻikkaḷattuṟaiyum emarālum paḻippuṇḍu ingu en? tammāl iḻippuṇḍu tamarōdanguṟaivārkkut takkilamē? kēḷīrē!*

- *numarōdum piriyādē* – [parānguśa nāyaki](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) thinks about prāpya vastu (bhagavān, who is the goal) as “*tamarōdanguṟaivār*” (one who resides there with his devotees); these herons are also happily living in that manner. Should those who are fully satisfied not help those who are not satisfied! It is apt for one who ate to satisfy the hunger of the hungry person.
- *nīrum num sēvalumāy* – You and your spouse who interact according to the desires of each other. Should you who understand the pleasure of union not understand the sorrow of the separated one!
- *amar kādal kurugu inangāḷ* – Love which is well placed in each other. In desire, isn’t there the desire which does not lead to separation! To begin with, you have complete desire, without any separation, and you are also interacting with mutual understanding! Though she started calling them “*kuruginangāḷ*“, due to lack of strength she could not even complete her sentence and became sorrowful thinking about her state.
- *emarālum paḻippuṇḍu – aṇimūḻikkaḷattu uṟaiyum tammālum paḻippuṇḍu* – Due to the momentary union, the relatives abandoned her; due to the same union, he too abandoned her. He should have accepted me due to having been abandoned by my relatives; he should have accepted me since he descended here to present his audience to those who have missed him previously; both of these have become the reasons for his abandoning of me!
- *ingu en* – What is the purpose of my presence here? Have I attained him or do I have my relatives? Should he not keep me in his protection after those who are here have abandoned me? Would these samsāris (materialistic people) not abandon one, the day one starts entering into bhagavat viśayam (spiritual matters)?

Leaving such sorrow at that, again, due to her sorrow, she starts telling them (herons),

- *tamarōdu angu uṟaivārkku* – Ask him “Would we not be acceptable for [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is residing there with his devotees?” Ask him “Would those who remain as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 2.3.10](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/02/thiruvaimozhi-2-3-10-kalippum-kavarvum/) ‘*adiyār kuḻāngaḷ udan kūduvadu enṟukolō*‘ (when will I unite with the groups of devotees in paramapadam?) be not acceptable for this beautiful presence of emperumān along with his devotees?”

## 9.7.3. Takkilame? kelirgal

*takkilamē? kēḷīrgaḷ tadam punalvāy irai tērum kokkinangāḷ kuruginangāḷ kuḷir mūḻik kaḷattuṟaiyum sekkamalattalarpōlum kaṇ kai kāl senganivāy akkamalattilaipōlum tirumēni adigaḷukkē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tada – vast; punalvāy – in the pond; iraitērum – seeking your prey; kokku inangāḷ kurugu inangāḷ – Oh groups of cranes and herons!; kuḷir – invigorating; mūḻikkaḷattu – in tirumūḻikkaḷam; uṟaiyum – eternally residing; sem – reddish; kamalattu – lotus’; alarpōlum – like a blossomed flower; kaṇ – eyes (which make one say “jitantē“); kai – hands (which embrace as prayed by “apyēśa pruśtē mama hastapadmam kariśyati“); kāl – divine feet (which are surrendered unto as said in “caraṇadvandvam vrajāmi“); sem kani vāy – divine lips (which pacify by saying “māśuca:”) which are like reddish fruit; akkamalattu – contrasting \[the complexion of\] such lotus flower; ilai pōlum – dark like a dense leaf; tirumēni – having divine form; adiugaḷukku – the one who became my lord by showing such beautiful form; takkilamē – are we not qualified (to enjoy that beauty); kēḷīrgaḷ – you ask

**Перевод:**

**Oh groups of cranes and herons who are seeking your prey in the vast pond! You ask emperumān who is eternally residing in the invigorating tirumūḻikkaḷam having eyes, hands, divine feet and divine lips which are like reddish blossomed lotus flower, and a contrasting divine dark form like a dense leaf, and who became my lord by showing such beautiful form, if we are not qualified to enjoy that beauty.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the third pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki tells some cranes and herons “Ask him if we are not qualified to see his beauty?”*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. takkilamē? kēḷīrgaḷ tadam punalvāy irai tērum kokkinangāḷ kuruginangāḷ kuḷir mūḻik kaḷattuṟaiyum sekkamalattalarpōlum kaṇ kai kāl senganivāy akkamalattilaipōlum tirumēni adigaḷukkē*

- *takkilamē kēḷīrgaḷ* – You ask him so that we can fully make up our mind in our decision. You ask him and find out from him so that if he is inclined to accept us, we will look after ourselves with anguish and if he is inclined to reject us, we will decide to finish ourselves.
- *tadam punalvāy irai tērum* – Your situation is such that you are searching for prey in the water in the pond which is having abundance of water. Unlike me who is as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 15.18 “*tatō manlinasamvītām rākśasībhis samāvrutām \|  upavāsakruśām dīnām ni:śvasantīm puna: puna: \|\|*” (Thereafter, (hanuman saw) sītā pirātti who is wearing ragged clothes, surrounded well by rākśasis, looking lean due to abstaining from eating, fearful and frequently breathing heavily), you are well-built to push the prey down your throat!
- *kokku inangāḷ kurugu inangāḷ* – kurugu – a type of stork. Just as it is mentioned in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 30.3 “*yām kapīṇām sahasrāṇi*” (sītāp pirātti who is searched by thousands of monkeys), she is sending everything she sees, as messengers. [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is not of the nature that one can remain satisfied after sending some messengers thinking that one’s desire will be fulfilled.
- *kuḷir mūḻikkaḷattuṟaiyum* – For me who is suffering in separation, reaching this cool town is difficult!
- *sekkamalam …* – The fragrant pond inside \[the town\] which is the root cause for the coolness there; [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is having divine limbs such as eyes which resemble blossomed red lotus; his eyes which establish the first relationship; the eyes which embrace those who are won over by that glance; the divine feet one falls at, after being won over by the embrace; the smile which will pacify those who fall at the divine feet.
- *akkamalattu ilaipōlum tirumēni* – the form which uplifts them. The divine form is having a complexion which is contrasting to the complexion of the limbs. Here she is saying “*akkamalam*” (that lotus) to signify that it is a distinguished red lotus and not a regular white lotus.
- *adigaḷukku* – One who enslaved me by showing the beauty of the individual limbs and the wholesome beauty of the divine form. You ask him “Is the one who became pale after being won over by your physical beauty, not qualified to be there \[with you\]?” When he is puruśōttama (best among men), she should be *nārīṇāmuttamā* (best among women).

## 9.7.4. Tirumeni adikalukku

*tirumēni adigaḷukkut tīvinaiyēn vidu tūdāy tirumūḻikkaḷam ennum seḻu nagarvāy aṇi mugilgāḷ! tirumēni avatkaruḷīr enṟakkāl ummait tan tirumēni oḷi agaṟṟit teḷivisumbu kadiyumē*

**Пословный перевод:**

aṇi – having an attractive form; mugilgāḷ – Oh clouds!; tirumūḻikkaḷam ennum – tirumūḻikkaḷam which is popularly known as said in tirunedundāṇḍagam 10 “pinnānār vaṇangum sōdi”; seḻu nagarvāy – residing in distinguished abode; tirumēni adigaḷukku – one whose form reveals his lordship over everyone as said in “rūpamēva asya ētanmahimānam vyācaśtē”; tīvinaiyēn – I who am having cruel sin (to have a relationship with him, yet being unable to enjoy him); vidu – sending; tūdāy – going as messenger; ‘avatku – for her; tirumēni – your perfectly enjoyable divine form; aruḷīr – mercifully grant her’; enṟakkāl – when you make a statement; ummai – all of you (who spoke for my sake); than tirumēni oḷi – radiance of his divine form (which he previously gave); agaṟṟi – eliminating it; teḷi visumbu kadiyumē – will he reject your stay in the distinguished sky \[paramapadam\]?

**Перевод:**

**Oh clouds which are having attractive form! emperumān whose form reveals his lordship over everyone as said in “rūpamēva asya ētanmahimānam vyācaśtē“, is residing in tirumūḻikkaḷam which is popularly known as said in tirunedundāṇḍagam 10 “pinnānār vaṇangum sōdi”. When you go to him since I, who am having cruel sin, am sending you as my messenger and when you make a statement “mercifully grant her your perfectly enjoyable divine form”, will he eliminate the radiance of his divine form which he previously gave to you and reject your stay in the distinguished sky? She is saying “for emperumān who bestows this favour to those who request it for themselves, eliminating sārūpyam (having similar form as bhagavān) and viṣṇupadāśrayatvam (residing in paramapadam) for requesting on my behalf, does not fit”.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fourth pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki says to some clouds “Will he punish you if you inform my words to him?”*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. tirumēni adigaḷukkut tīvinaiyēn vidu tūdāy tirumūḻikkaḷam ennum seḻu nagarvāy aṇi mugilgāḷ! tirumēni avatkaruḷīr enṟakkāl ummait than tirumēni oḷi agaṟṟit teḷivisumbu kadiyumē*

- *tirumēni adigaḷukku* – One who is manifesting his lordship in his physical beauty itself, other than the same which is seen in his svarūpa (nature), rūpa (form), guṇa (qualities) and vibhūti (wealth); also said as one who won over the whole universe with his physical beauty. His form is attractive even for unfavourable ones as said in mahābhāratam sabhā parvam “… *avaśā pratipēdirē*” (On seeing kriṣṇa, they offered respects etc without realising it).
- *tīvinaiyēn vidu tūdāy* – Engaging as my messenger, where I am so sinful to have lost [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s form which is available for everyone, and to fall at your feet.
- *tirumūḻikkaḷam ennum* – The abode which is popularly known to be the place where emperumān is standing to protect the suffering ones.
- *seḻu nagar* – Greatness \[of tirumūḻikkaḷam\] over paramapadam. Three meanings explained – a) Oh beautiful clouds present in the distinguished abode! b) Inform the lord who is in the distinguished abode c) Go to the distinguished abode and inform.
- *tirumēni avatkaruḷīr* – You tell him “Can you not present your divine form which is existing for the sake of others, to those who desire for it?” You tell him that his divine form belongs to those who desired for it as said in jitantē stōtram “*bhaktānām*” (for the devotees); for a kāmini (lady in love with a man), there is more desire for her man’s form than his true nature etc.
- *aruḷīr* – After losing your love for me, have you lost your krupai (mercy) also?
- *enṟakkāl* – As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 39.10 “*vācā darmam avāpnuhi*”  (become righteous through your speech), don’t you just need to speak a word?
- *ummai* – All of you who are my benefactors.
- *than tirumēni oḷi agaṟṟit teḷivisumbu kadiyumē* – Would he eliminate the radiance in your form and drive you away from the pure sky? Instead of giving you that which you don’t have, would he take away what you already have and punish you? Would he not give full equivalence as said in muṇḍaka upaniśat 3.1.3 “*paramam sāmyam upaiti*” (he attains supreme equivalence) instead of minimal equivalence and presence in supreme sky (śrīvaikuṇṭam) other than the \[material\] sky? How can you be relaxed while your words will lead to same result for both you and me?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.
