## 9.7.5. Teli visumbu

*teḷi visumbu kadidōdit tīviḷaittu minnilagumoḷimugilgāḷ! tirumūḻikkaḷattuṟaiyum oṇsudarkkut teḷi visumbu tirunādāt tīvinaiyēn manattuṟaiyumtuḷivārgatkuḻalārkku en tūduraittal seppuminē*

**Пословный перевод:**

teḷi visumbu – in the pure sky; kadidu ōdi – quickly running (as if walking quickly on the ground, showing urge for my sake); tī vaḷaittu – like a ring of fire carried around; min ilagum oḷi mugilgāḷ – Oh clouds which are having increased beauty due to the presence of lightning which is shining!; tirumūḻikkaḷattu – in tirumūḻikkaḷam; uṟaiyum oṇsudarkku – due to the eternal presence there, one who is having distinguished radiance of qualities such as sauśeelyam, saulabhyam etc; teḷi visumbu – pure divine sky; tirunādā – as one who is having perfect wealth; tīvinaiyēn manattu – in my heart; I who am having the sin of being pained after union \[due to the separation\]; uṟaiyum – residing in a concealed manner; tuḷi – sprouted; vār – and flowing; kaḷ – having honey; kuḻalārkku – for the one who is manifesting his beautiful hair; en tūduraittal – the message saying “You, being kēśava, are to eliminate my klēśa (sorrow)”; seppumin – please convey!

**Перевод:**

**Oh clouds which are having increased beauty due to the presence of lightning which is shining and which are quickly running in the pure sky like a ring of fire carried around! emperumān is having distinguished radiance of qualities such as sauśeelyam, saulabhyam etc due to the eternal presence in tirumūḻikkaḷam; he is having the perfect wealth which is the pure divine sky; I am having the sin of being pained after union and he is residing in my heart in a concealed manner; please convey the message to such emperumān who is manifesting his beautiful hair having honey which is sprouted and flowing, saying “You, being kēśava, are to eliminate my klēśa (sorrow)”**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fifth pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki says to the clouds “If you ask me ‘would he acknowledge us if we speak to him on your behalf?’ I would say ’emperumān who showed me the love he shows towards paramapadam, will acknowledge; hence you put forth my request to him’ “*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. teḷi visumbu kadidōdit tīviḷaittu minnilagumoḷimugilgāḷ! tirumūḻikkaḷattuṟaiyum oṇsudarkkut teḷi visumbu tirunādāt tīvinaiyēn manattuṟaiyumtuḷivārgatkuḻalārkku en tūduraittal seppuminē*

- *teḷi visumbu kadidu ōdi* – In the sky which is pure and supportless, moving quickly as if walking quickly on the ground. She considers their urge to be for her sake.
- *tī vaḷaittu min ilagum* – Lightning is shining like a ball of fire. The clouds are with lightning just as someone who is dark will carry a lamp along to reveal the presence.
- *oḷi mugilgāḷ* – Oh clouds which are having beautiful form due to the contrasting colours!
- *tirumūḻikkaḷattu uṟaiyum oṇsudarkku* – One who has increased radiance due to his eternal residing in tirumūḻikkaḷam. Your form resembles his form.
- *teḷi visumbu …* – He is showing the love he has for parampadam, towards my heart and resides there.
- *tī vinaiyēn* – I have committed sin which makes me unable to see him though he is shining in my heart. For this, siṟṟāḷ koṇḍān explains “Just as one would discuss about the rate of the garment, while the cotton is still in the plant, while he has paramapadam as his royal assembly, ignoring it, to remain in front of me, he is shining in my heart”. But this does not fit with the overall theme of this decad; it is just a statement based on a momentary experience.
- *tuḷi vār kaḷ kuḻalārkku* – For the one who has hari in which hair is overflowing; when an expert wears flowers, we can see the overflowing honey instead of the flower itself.
- *en tūdu uraittal seppuminē* – Please go an inform the message of me who is having withered flowers in my head, to him. Inform him my state of having to send messenger while he had lovingly said that he will come himself.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 9.7.6. Tuduraittal

*tūduraittal seppumingaḷ tūmoḻivāy vaṇḍinangāḷ! pōdiraittu madu nugarum poḻil mūḻikkaḷattuṟaiyum mādarait tam mārbagattē vaittārkku en vāy māṟṟam tūduraittal seppudirēl sudar vaḷaiyum kalaiyumē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tū moḻi vāy – having faultless speech; vaṇḍinangāḷ – Oh groups of beetles!; pōdu iraittu – celebrating due to the bliss while the flowers are blossoming; madu nugarum – for you to drink the honey; poḻil – having garden; mūḻikkaḷattu – in tirumūḻikkaḷam; uṟaiyum – one who resides; mādarai – lakshmi who is the best among women; tam mārbagattē vaittārkku – one who made her eternally reside in his enjoyable, divine chest saying “agalagillēn”; en vāy māṟṟam – words of my speech; tūdu uraittal – message; seppudirēl – if you set out to speak; sudar – radiant; vaḷaiyum – bangles; kalaiyum – clothes; tūduraittal – as the matter of my message; seppumingaḷ – please tell

**Перевод:**

**Oh groups of beetles having faultless speech! tirumūḻikkaḷam is having garden for you to celebrate due to the bliss while the flowers are blossoming and drink the honey from them; emperumān is a resident of such tirumūḻikkaḷam  and made lakshmi, the best among women, to eternally reside in his enjoyable, divine chest saying “agalagillēn“; when you set out to speak the message which is made up of the words of my speech, please tell him about the radiant bangles and clothes as the matter of my message.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the sixth pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki tells some beetles “While you inform my situation to emperumān, you do it in the presence of pirātti so that your words lead to the apt result”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. tūduraittal seppumingaḷ tūmoḻivāy vaṇḍinangāḷ! pōdiraittu madu nugarum poḻil mūḻikkaḷattuṟaiyum mādarait tam mārbagattē vaittārkku en vāy māṟṟam tūduraittal seppudirēl sudar vaḷaiyum kalaiyumē*

- *tūdu uraittal seppumingaḷ* – You just need to inform my message to him; you need not bring him.
- *tū moḻi vāy vaṇḍinangāḷ* – Oh beetles with sweet speech! Even if he disregards me, your voice is such that if he hears it, he will come. When perumāḷ (śrī rāma) and iḷaiya perumāḷ (lakśmaṇa) were coming with their bows, sugrīva mahārāja thought “Are they coming at the behest of vāli?” and became frightened and ran away to a distant place; but he returned and became friends with śrī rāma to be said as in śrī rāmāyaṇam kiśkindā kaṇḍam 5.17 “*ēkam du:kham sukancanau*” (we share joy and sorrow) irrespective of being different from each other, due to the sweet words of hanuman as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 17.48 “*ata samskāra sampanna:*” (being well trained in śāstram).
- *pōdu iraittu madu nugarum poḻil* – Saying that the garden where the beetles are drinking honey spilling it over on the flowers \[pōdu – flower\]; another explanation – pōdu – time. You need not bring him here; there is no one to protect the garden like dadimuka (who was protecting sugrīva’s garden); you can just drink honey along with those who are already drinking.
- *mādarait than mārbagattē vaittārkku* – All you need to do is to just inform him. There is \[pirātti’s\] puruśakāram (recommendation) to listen to your words and to praise your words.
- *en vāy māṟṟam* – When you set out to convey my message, speak about how my beautiful bangle and garment have become broken! If you are speaking about me, that itself is my radiant bangle and garment. As soon as he is informed, he will arrive.

## 9.7.7. Sudar valaiyum

*sudar vaḷaiyum kalaiyum koṇḍu aru vinaiyēn tōḷ tuṟanda padar pugaḻān tirumūḻikkaḷattuṟaiyum pangayakkaṇ sudar pavaḷa vāyanaik kaṇḍu oru nāḷ ōr tūy māṟṟam padar poḻil vāyk kuruginangāḷ! enakkonṟu paṇiyīrē*

**Пословный перевод:**

padar – spread out; poḻilvāy – residing in the garden; kurugu inangāḷ – Oh groups of herons!; sudar – radiant; vaḷaiyum – bangles; kalaiyum – garment; koṇḍu – taking; aruvinaiyēn – me who is having sins which are difficult to overcome, my; tōḷ tuṟanda – one who very lovingly embraced my shoulders, and abandoned them subsequently; padar – spread in the world; pugaḻāna – as greatness; tirumūḻikkaḷattu uṟaiyum – eternally residing in tirumūḻikkaḷam (to increase my sorrow by remaining in close proximity); pangayak kaṇ – having lotus like divine eyes (which remain fresh during union and separation); sudar – radiant; pavaḷam – coral like; vāyanai – one who is having divine lips; kaṇḍu – see; enakku – for me (who is manifesting my sorrow in my body); oru nāḷ – one day (unlike nitya agnihōtram which is to be done everyday); ōr – distinguished (due to being for protection of suffering ones); tūy māṟṟam – best words due to the clarity; onṟu – to remain crisp (without wavering); paṇiyīrē – you should tell

**Перевод:**

**Oh groups of herons residing in the spread out garden! emperumān took the radiant bangles and garments from me who is having sins which are difficult to overcome and very lovingly embraced my shoulders, and abandoned them subsequently. He is eternally residing in tirumūḻikkaḷam with such greatness which is spread in the world, having lotus like divine eyes and radiant coral like divine lips. You see him for me one day and tell him in distinguished, best words due to the clarity in them to remain crisp. She is requesting them humbly to highlight her reverence towards them.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the eighth pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki says to some groups of herons “You ask emperumān ‘is it sufficient to bask in the glory of uniting with some and separating from them?’ ”*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. sudar vaḷaiyum kalaiyum koṇḍu aru vinaiyēn tōḷ tuṟanda padar pugaḻān tirumūḻikkaḷattuṟaiyum pangayakkaṇ sudar pavaḷa vāyanaik kaṇḍu oru nāḷ ōr tūy māṟṟam padar poḻil vāyk kuruginangāḷ! enakkonṟu paṇiyīrē*

- *sudar vaḷaiyum kalaiyum …* – He took what is useful for him and abandoned me; he took what sustains him and abandoned the other aspects; he took away what can be held in the hand and my waist garment.
- *aruvinaiyēn* – I have committed sin to be abandoned by one who showed great love.
- *tōḷ tuṟanda* – He will show all such love towards my shoulders and will not go beyond them.
- *padar pugaḻān* – Having this aspect of “there is none who can abandon in this manner those who cannot sustain without him” as his fame, he is remaining glorious with flag and pomp.
- *tirumūḻikkaḷattu uṟaiyum* – One who is remaining in tirumūḻikkaḷam which is nearby and hence we cannot be relaxed thinking he is staying too far away.
- *pangayak kaṇ sudar pavaḷa vāyanai* – One who is having beautiful limbs which do not allow one to leave him alone, after having been abandoned by him; also implies – one whose limbs appear fresh having tormented me in this manner.
- *kaṇḍu* – You have attained the result before me, having seen his glance and smile.
- *oru nāḷ* – Just \[informing him\] one day is enough and no need for another day. She thinks it is an insult to inform him again \[Surrender should be performed only once\].
- *ōr tūy māṟṟam* – A distinguished, good word. This is the word to uplift a helpless lady who is perishing.
- *padar poḻil vāyk kurugu inangāḷ* – Oh groups of herons who are residing in the vast garden! While I am fasting \[without enjoyment\], is it apt for you to remain alive and enjoy? If I die, who will protect this vast garden for you?
- *enakku* – You have seen my form.
- *onṟu paṇiyīrē* – No need to speak another word.
- *paṇiyīrē* – Even if one is born in janaka’s clan and even if the other entity is an animal, this is how gataka (messenger/ācārya) for bhagavān should be addressed.

## 9.7.8. Enakkonru paniyirgal

*enakkonṟu paṇiyīrgaḷ irum poḻilvāy irai tērndu manakkinbam padamēvum vaṇḍinangāḷ tumbigāḷ kanakkoḷ tiṇ madiḷ pudai sūḻ tirumūḻikkaḷattuṟaiyum punakkoḷ kāyāmēnip pūnduḻāy mudiyārkkē*

**Пословный перевод:**

iru – vast; poḻilvāy – in the garden; irai tērndu – seeking the enjoyable honey; manakkku – for the mind; inbam pada – to cause joy; mēvum – uniting and residing; vaṇḍu inangāḷ tumbigāḷ – Oh groups of beetles and dragonflies!; kanam koḷ – heavy; tiṇ – firm; madiḷ – fort; pudai – surrounding; sūḻ – surrounded; tirumūḻikkaḷattu – in tirumūḻikkaḷam; uṟaiyum – one who is eternally residing; punam koḷ – staying in its own habitat; kāyā mēni – having the complexion of kāyām pū (a purple coloured flower); pū tuḻāy mudiyārkku – one whose divine crown is decorated with attractive tiruttuḻāy (tuḷasi); enakku – for me; onṟu – a word; paṇiyīr – should tell

**Перевод:**

**Oh groups of beetles and dragonflies who are seeking the enjoyable honey in the vast garden and uniting and residing there to cause joy for the mind! You should tell a word for me to emperumān who is eternally residing in tirumūḻikkaḷam which is surrounded by heavy and firm fort, who is having the complexion of kāyām pū which is staying in its own habitat, and whose divine crown is decorated with attractive tiruttuḻāy.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the eighth pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki says to some beetles and dragonflies “emperumān is mercifully residing in a well-protected abode so that we need not fear for his beauty. Now, the only desire is to eliminate my suffering. Hence, inform him about my suffering”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. enakkonṟu paṇiyīrgaḷ irum poḻilvāy irai tērndu manakkinbam padamēvum vaṇḍinangāḷ tumbigāḷ kanakkoḷ tiṇ madiḷ pudai sūḻ tirumūḻikkaḷattuṟaiyum punakkoḷ kāyāmēnip pūnduḻāy mudiyārkkē*

- *enakku onṟu paṇiyīrgaḷ* – My position is such that if you don’t say a word on my behalf I will die.
- *irum poḻilvāy irai tērndu* – Entering the vast garden and searching for food.
- *manakku inbam pada mēvum* – You are uniting to bring joy in the mind. They united nicely so that I don’t feel my sorrow in separation – they united in such an intimate manner that even while separated their bliss will not become extinct.
- *kanak koḷ …* – For the one who is eternally residing in tirumūḻikkaḷam which is surrounded by heavy and firm fort on all sides. When one thinks about his beauty, one will seek protection \[for him\] certainly.  A deep sorrow will affect one when not being united with him; another sorrow will affect one on thinking about the danger that will befall him; one such sorrow is eliminated first \[since the town is well protected\].
- *punak koḷ kāyā mēnip pū tuḻāy mudiyārkkē* – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s complexion resembles the complexion of kāyām pū (purple coloured flower) in its natural habitat. for the one who is also beautifully decorated on top of that physical beauty. This is his physical beauty; this is his decoration. Please tell on behalf of me who enjoyed that physical beauty and decoration and separated from him.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 9.7.9. Pundulay mudiyarkku

*pūnduḻāy mudiyārkkup ponnāḻik kaiyārukku ēndu nīr iḷangurugē! tirumūḻikkaḷattārukku ēndu pūṇ mulai payandu enniṇai malark kaṇ nīr tadumba tām tammaik koṇḍagaldal tagavanṟenṟuraiyirē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ēndu nīr – not being feared by water, sustaining the water; iḷa – being youthful (which is required for ability to travel); kurugē – Oh heron!; pū tuḻāy mudiyārkku – having attractive tiruttuḻāy (tuḷasi) on his crown (to highlight his supremacy over everyone); pon – attractive; āḻi – tiruvāḻi (divine chakra); kaiyārkku – having in in his hand; tirumūḻikkaḷattārkku – one who is present nearby in tirumūḻikkaḷam; pūṇ – ornament; ēndu – holding; mulai – bosom; payandu – having paleness; en iṇai malar kaṇ – my eyes which are like a pair of flowers (which blossom on seeing him); nīr tadumba – filled with sad tears (due to separation); tām – he (who is having subservience, enjoyability and simplicity); tammaik koṇḍu – knowing him; agaldal – moving away; tagavu anṟu enṟu – that it does not match his mercy; uraiyīrē – tell – she says in respectable way

**Перевод:**

**Oh youthful heron which does not fear water but sustains by that water! You tell  emperumān who is present nearby in tirumūḻikkaḷam having attractive tiruttuḻāy on his crown and divine chakra in his hand, that I am having paleness in my bosom which is holding ornament and my eyes which are like a pair of flowers are filled with sad tears and that moving away from me does not match his mercy after knowing himself.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the ninth pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki says to a heron which can complete the task it thinks  “You ask emperumān ‘should you who are perfectly enjoyable not take her along while leaving?'”*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. pūnduḻāy mudiyārkkup ponnāḻik kaiyārukku ēndu nīr iḷangurugē! tirumūḻikkaḷattārukku ēndu pūṇ mulai payandu enniṇai malark kaṇ nīr tadumba tām tammaik koṇḍagaldal tagavanṟenṟuraiyirē*

- *pū tuḻāy mudiyārkku* – This is the decorative garland on the crown.
- *pon āḻik kaiyārkku* – This is the decorating ring (chakra) for the hand.
- *ēndu nīr iḷam kurugē* – Oh young heron who can walk on vast water, like walking on land! I am trying to attain the result of your ability to travel. Even if this water remains a hurdle for you, don’t hesitate.
- *tirumūḻikkaḷattārkku* – Just as the garland and the ornament, his presence in the town is also adding to his beauty. Just as those \[garland, ornament\] are ornaments for his form, his simplicity is an ornament for his svarūpam (true nature). Beauty and qualities relate to particular entity.
- *ēndu pūṇ mulai payandu* – The bosom which is supposed to wear ornament is now wearing paleness. Ornaments are removed during union; but this paleness will not go unless there is union. This is the natural quality of a woman in separation; if this is not the case, a woman cannot be differentiated from a man.
- *en iṇai malark kaṇ nīr tadumba* – My eyes which resemble a pair of flowers. My eyes which are focussed on his beauty are now the abode of sad tears. As she knows about her eyes from him, she is speaking like this; otherwise it is not apt to praise one’s own aspects.
- *tadumba* – My eyes which deserve to get joyful tears are now filled with sorrowful tears.
- *tām* – After saying pūnduḻāy mudiyār, ponnāḻik kaiyār and tirumūḻikkaḷattār, now she is saying tām (him). By saying “*pūnduḻāy mudiyārkkup ponnāḻik kaiyārkku*“, she highlighted his physical beauty; by saying “*tiumūḻikkaḷattārkku*“, she highlighted his qualities \[such as easy approacability\]; he who is having such beauty and qualities.
- *tammaik koṇḍu agaldal* – If he wants to go, should he not leave his form and go, thinking “those who separate from this form cannot live”? He knows about his own form having seen it in the mirror. He has seen his own form to help those who separate from him; as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 59.26 “*atō nu kim du:khataram sōham ikśvāku nandanam \| imām avastām āpanna nēha paśyāmi rāghavam \|\|*” (Having attained this state, I am not seeing śrī rāma, the scion of ikśvāku dynasty; what is more sorrowful than this?) one’s sorrow will make one say everything. He is there for the sake of presenting himself, caressing me and protecting me by being close to me when I am in distress. There is no sorrow for me which is greater than being separated from him. daśarata said “I am still not seeing perumāḷ (śrī rāma).

ālernatively,

- *tām tammaik koṇḍu agaldal* – While he can take me along and leave, can he leave just by himself? If he desires to leave himself, should he leave behind what is owned by him \[me\] and take along what is owned by others \[his forms\]? His form remains as said in jitantē stōtram “*bhaktānām*” (for the  sake of devotees). ātmā remains as said in tiruvāimoḻi 2.9.4 “*tanakkēyāga enaik koḷḷum īdē*” (he should accept me for his own sake).
- *tagavu anṟu enṟu uraiyīrē* – While he has love and tenderness, you inform him that this is an act of a merciless person. You inform him that he did what is done by one who does not fear killing a woman.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 9.7.10. Tagavanru

*tagavanṟenṟuraiyīrgaḷ tadam punal vāy irai tērndu miga inbam pada mēvum mennadaiya annangāḷ miga mēni meliveydi mēgalaiyum īdaḻindu en aga mēni oḻiyāmē tirumūḻikkaḷattārkkē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tada – vast; poḻilvāy – in the garden; irai – food; tērndu – acquired; miga – great; inbam – bliss; pada – to attain; mēvum – living together; mel nadaiya – having gentle gait; annangāḷ – Oh swans!; mēni – body; miga – greatly; melivu eydi – weakened; mēgalaiyum – garment; īdaḻindu – losing its tightness; en agamēni – my inherent nature; oḻiyāmē – to not lose; tirumūḻikkaḷattārkku – for the one who is standing in tirumūḻikkaḷam to bless his devotees; tagavu anṟu enṟu – this is not the effect of your mercy since the purpose of standing there is not attained; uraiyīrgaḷ – inform him – says parānguśa nāyaki

**Перевод:**

**Oh swans who have acquired your food in the vast garden and are living together to attain great bliss and are having a gentle gait! My body greatly weakened and my garment lost its tightness; you go and inform the one, who is standing in tirumūḻikkaḷam to bless his devotees, before I lose my inherent nature “this is not the effect of your mercy since the purpose of standing there is not attained”.**

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. tagavanṟenṟuraiyīrgaḷ tadam punal vāy irai tērndu miga inbam pada mēvum mennadaiya annangāḷ miga mēni meliveydi mēgalaiyum īdaḻindu en aga mēni oḻiyāmē tirumūḻikkaḷattārkkē*

- *tagavu anṟu enṟu uraiyīrgaḷ* – You tell him that he is not merciless to destroy his own existence. That is – he is being merciless. Since mercy is his identity and since she knows his secret, she is saying that he is merciless.
- *tadam punalvāy irai tērndu* – Searching for food in very flooded ponds. They are engaged in activities which only lead to union.
- *miga inbam pada mēvum* – You are uniting to have overwhelming bliss. They are uniting so intimately to have both parties become lost.
- *men nadaiya annangāḷ* – They were walking around in such a manner that we can observe their abundance of union in their steps.
- *miga mēni melivu eydi* – You have lost your intimate walks; you have seen my state; are you able to sustain yourself after seeing my state? My body’s weakness is in line with your abundant union.
- *mēgalaiyum īdaḻindu* – Garment also loosened; when it hangs loosely, it needs support.
- *en aga mēni oḻiyāmē* – Everything outside is gone; now, before the inner nature also goes; she is saying “before I die”.
- *tirumūḻikkaḷattārkku* – One who is remaining here to protect those who cannot live without him.
- *tirumūḻikkaḷattārkku – tagavu anṟu enṟu uraiyīrgaḷ* – Enough of pampering him and speaking with sugar-coated words; now, you inform him about his nature directly. When asked “If she did that previously”, when her venerable mother said as in [tiruvāimoḻi 2.4.5](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/03/thiruvaimozhi-2-4-5-ival-irap-pagal/) “*ena tavaḷa vaṇṇar tagavugaḷ*” (In what manner your qualities such as compassion etc exist?), she could not tolerate that and said as in [tiruvāimoḻi 2.4.6](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/03/thiruvaimozhi-2-4-6-thagavudaiyavane/) “*tagavudaiyavanē*” (he is compassionate) and said “Oh! will he give up his mercy?”; she is speaking about that now.

## 9.7.11. Olivinri

*oḻivinṟit tirumūḻikkaḷattuṟaiyum oṇsudarai oḻivillā aṇi maḻalaik kiḷi moḻiyāḷ alaṟṟiya sol vaḻuvillā vaṇ kurugūrc catakōpan vāynduraitta aḻivillā āyirattu ippattum nōy aṟukkumē*

**Пословный перевод:**

oḻivu inṟi – to not separate (ever); tirumūḻikkaḷattu – in tirumūḻikkaḷam; uṟaiyum – due to eternally residing; oṇ sudarai – one who is having distinguished radiance; oḻivillā – unable to sustain in separation; aṇi – beautiful; maḻalai – gibberish \[childish speech\]; kiḷi moḻiyāḷ – one whose speech matches a parrot’s; alaṟṟiya – spoke incoherently due to her sorrow; sol – pāsuram; vaḻu illā – without any shortcoming (in that love); vaṇ kurugūr – leader of the distinguished āḻvārtirunagari; satakōpan – nammāḻvār; vāyndu uraitta – spoken after approaching and enjoying (emperumān‘s qualities); aḻivu illā – not leaving the hearts of the enjoyers; āyirattu ippattum – this decad among the thousand pāsurams; nōy – the disease of samsāra (which is the cause for separation from bhagavān); aṟukkum – will eradicate

**Перевод:**

**nammāḻvār, who is the leader of the distinguished āḻvārtirunagari, whose beautiful childish speech matches a parrot’s speech, incoherently spoke these pāsurams without any shortcoming, due to his \[her\] sorrow of being unable to sustain in separation from emperumān who is eternally residing in tirumūḻikkaḷam to not separate from there and is distinguiśably radiant due to that. This decad among the thousand pāsurams which are spoken after approaching and enjoying emperumān’s qualities, which are not leaving the hearts of the enjoyers, will eradicate the disease of samsāra.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the end, āḻvār says “This decad will eradicate the samsāra durita (difficulties in bondage) which is the equivalent of separation from perumāḷ, for those who learn/practice it”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. oḻivinṟit tirumūḻikkaḷattuṟaiyum oṇsudarai oḻivillā aṇi maḻalaik kiḷi moḻiyāḷ alaṟṟiya sol vaḻuvillā vaṇ kurugūrc catakōpan vāynduraitta aḻivillā āyirattu ippattum nōy aṟukkumē*

- *oḻivinṟit tirumūḻikkaḷattu uṟaiyum* – One who eternally resides in this town without ever contemplating to leave.
- *oṇ sudar* – This is the radiance acquired due to his presence in this town as said in [tirunedundāṇḍagam 10](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/11/thirunedunthandakam-10-part-2/) ‘*pinnānār vaṇangum sōdi tirumūḻikkaḷam*‘ (the radiant lord in tirumūḻikkaḷam who is vorśipped by those who are of later times); the radiance acquired due to the enjoyability in the town and his presence for the sake of those who are of later times.
- *oḻivillā* – Just as [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) cannot sustain without this town , parānguśa nāyaki cannot sustain without him; she is of the nature to say as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 53.31 “*na ca sītā tvayā hīnā nacāhamapi rāghava*” (Oh rāghava! I too will not sustain in separation from you just as sītā would not).
- *aṇi maḻalaik kiḷi moḻiyāḷ* – One who is having speech which is similar to that of a beautiful, young parrot.
- *alaṟṟiya sol* – The words which were spoken incoherently due to her sorrow.
- *vaḻu illā vaṇ kurugūrc catakōpan* – āḻvār who is no less than pirātti (śrī mahālakśmi) herself in any aspect.
- *vāyndu uraitta* – approached and spoke; implying that it was spoken with great emotions considering the intimate relationship.
- *aḻivu illā āyirattu ippattu* – This decad which will stay forever in the hearts of those who heard it. For those who heard this decad, it will bring in the emotions every time, as if it is happening in the present.
- *nōy aṟukkumē* – It will eradicate the disease of separation from bhagavān; one need not unite and separate, and then suffer by falling at the feet of animals/birds; one will enter the abode where there is no separation.

## 9.8 Arukkum vinai

## 9.8.1. Arukkum vinai

*aṟukkum vinaiyāyina āgattu avanai niṟuttum manattonṟiya sindaiyinārkku veṟit taṇ malarc cōlaigaḷ sūḻ tirunāvāy kuṟukkum vagai uṇḍukolō? kodiyēṟkē*

**Пословный перевод:**

āgattu – in (their) heart; avanai – sarvēśvara (who is the eliminator of all hurdles and who is perfectly enjoyable); niṟuttum – to hold; manattu – in heart; onṟiya – singular; sindaiyinārkku – those who have desire; vinaiyāyina – all hurdles for enjoyment such as avidyā (ignorance), karma (activities), vāsanā (impression), ruci (taste); aṟukkum – to eliminate; veṟi – abundantly fragrant; taṇ – invigorating; malar – filled with flowers; sōlaigaḷ sūḻ – having gardens; tirunāvāy – tirunāvāy; kodiyēṟku – me having the cruelty (of not being able to enjoy as per desire); kuṟukkum vagai uṇḍukolō – is there any means to reach?

**Перевод:**

**Is there any means for me, who is having cruelty, to reach tirunāvāy which is having gardens filled with abundantly fragrant, invigorating flowers and where sarvēśvara is present to eliminate all hurdles for enjoyment such as avidyā (ignorance), karma (activities), vāsanā (impression), ruci (taste) of those who have singular desire to hold him in their hearts?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the first pāsuram, āḻvār says “Is there any means for me to reach tirunāvāy?”*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. aṟukkum vinaiyāyina āgattu avanai niṟuttum manattonṟiya sindaiyinārkku veṟit taṇ malarc cōlaigaḷ sūḻ tirunāvāy kuṟukkum vagai uṇḍukolō? kodiyēṟkē*

- *aṟukkum vinaiyāyina* – everything which falls under the category of vinai (sin) will be eradicated; hurdles in taste, hurdles in means, hurdles in attaining the goal and those hurdles which do not stop at the current body but will delay the attainment of goal due to the presence of remainder of such sins. Hence, hurdles occur in every stage. Just as the dirt in new garment is removed step by step, when one tries to eradicate the hurdles, it will be done step by step; when the sins are removed by bhagavān’s mercy, they will be eradicated at once; it is as said in viṣṇu darmam 78th ślōkam *“mēru mantaramātrōpi*” (the sins which are as heavy as mēru mountain and mantara mountain placed on top of each other), cāndōjña upaniśat 5.24 “*sarva pāpmāna: pradūyantē*” (All sins are destroyed) and śrī bhagavat gītā 18.66 “*sarva pāpēbhyō mōkśayiśyāmi*” (I will free you from all sorrows). When one performs atonement for brahma hatyā (killing a brāhmaṇa), he also needs to perform atonement  separately for gō hatyā (killing a cow) ; this is not required when getting the sins removed with the help of bhagavān’s mercy \[they will all go at the same time\].

When asked “To whom, does he show mercy in this manner?” [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says,

- *āgattu …* – Those who have the singular desire to place him in their hearts, due to the firm believe in that.
- *veṟi …* – The abode is such that, it cannot be abandoned even if he increased our sins instead of eradicating them. tirunāvāy which is surrounded with fragrant, invigorating gardens which give the feel of eternal spring.
- *kuṟukkum vagai uṇḍukolō* – \[Three meanings are explained\] a) What is the means which will make me attain it? b) what is the means to reach it? c) kuṟukkum – local language (something being in close proximity). \[Third meaning is explained with an example\] [emperumānār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/emperumanar/) was mercifully going towards tirunāvāy and mercifully asked those who were coming towards him “How far is tirunāvāy?” and they replied “*kuṟukkum*” (it is in close proximity); hearing that emperumānār became blissful and mercifully said “[āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is mercifully using the local language \[since his mother is from tiruvaṇparisāram which is a malayāḷa divyadēśam\]!”
- *kodiyēṟku* – For the cruel me. While this town remains reachable even for those who have a little bit of desire, I have committed sin to suffer in not reaching there even after having overwhelming desire.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 9.8.2. Kodiyer idai

*kodiyēr idaik kōganagattavaḷ kēḷvan vadivēl tadangaṇ madappinnai maṇāḷan nediyān uṟai sōlaigaḷ sūḻ tirunāvāy adiyēn aṇugap peṟu nāḷ evaikolō?*

**Пословный перевод:**

kodi ēr idai – having creeper like (slender) waist; kōganagattavaḷ – for lakshmi who is perfectly enjoyable having been born in lotus flower; kēḷvan – being a match; vadi vēl – having radiance and sharpness of a well made spear; tadam kaṇ – having vast eyes; madam – and having humility; pinnai – for nappinnaip pirātti; maṇāḷan – being the enjoyer; nediyān – one who is having endlessly great enjoyability; uṟai – residing (abode); sōlaigaḷ – with many different gardens; sūḻ – surrounded; tirunāvāy – tirunāvāy; adiyēn – I (who cannot enjoy anything else); aṇugap peṟum nāḷ – days of reaching; evaikolō – when?

**Перевод:**

**emperumān is the match for lakshmi who is perfectly enjoyable having been born in lotus flower and is having a creeper like (slender) waist; he is the enjoyer of nappinnaip pirātti who is having vast eyes which have radiance and sharpness of a well made spear and is having humility; he is having endlessly great enjoyability and is residing in tirunāvāy which is surrounded with many different gardens; when are the days of my reaching such tirunāvāy? vadi also indicates a type of mango, where the eyes appear like cut mango or a spear.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the second pāsuram, āḻvār says “When will I enter tirunāvāy?”*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. kodiyēr idaik kōganagattavaḷ kēḷvan vadivēl tadangaṇ madappinnai maṇāḷan nediyān uṟai sōlaigaḷ sūḻ tirunāvāy adiyēn aṇugap peṟu nāḷ evaikolō?*

- *kodi ēr …* – [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is the beloved consort of pirātti who is having creeper like slender waist and who took birth from the buds of the lotus flower. [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is asking “should I lose him even while pirātti who said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 116-45 “*nakaścin nāparādyati*” (there is none who has not committed a wrongful deed) is present with him?”
- *vadi vēl tadam kaṇ madap pinnai maṇāḷan* – nappinnaip pirātti is having such a sharp spear like eyes where one glance will win over anyone and is having enjoyability beyond anyone’s enjoying ability; [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) appears to be born only to enjoy nappinnaip pirātti’s freshness.
- *nediyān* – One who cannot be comprehended by such divine consorts and associates.
- *uṟai …* – tirunāvāy which is surrounded by vast gardens which give space to him and his wealth without any limitation.
- *adiyēn* – When perumāḷ \[śrī rāma\] and \[sītāp\] pirātti set out to leave for the forest, iḷaiya perumāḷ (lakśmaṇa) also set out to perform all services as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 31.25  “*bhavāmstu saha vaidēhyā girisānuśu ramsyatē*” (While you enjoy with sītā in the foothills of the mountain, I will serve you both in all the ways), here [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) set out to serve them here. Unlike in the case of iḷaiya perumāḷ there is no shortage of those who can engage āḻvār in service. There, it was only the divine daughter of śrī janakarāja \[here both consorts are present\],
- *aṇugap peṟu nāḷ evaikolō* – When will I reach that abode \[of tirunāvāy\]?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 9.8.3. Evaikol anuga

*evaikol aṇugap peṟu nāḷ enṟeppōdum kavaiyil manam inṟik kaṇṇīrgaḷ kaluḻvan navaiyil tirunāraṇan sēr tirunāvāy avaiyuḷ pugalāvadu ōr nāḷ aṟiyēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

aṇugap peṟu nāḷ – the day I reach; evaikol enṟu – when; eppōdum – all times; kavaiyil manam inṟi – without having the heart to focus on anything else (with total focus); kaṇṇīrgaḷ – tears; kaluḻvan – will shed; navai il – without defect (of being difficult to attain, being conditional); tirunāraṇan – (being easy to attain, being unconditional relative as) nārāyaṇa who is śriya:pati (lord of śrī mahālakśmi); sēr – residing; tirunāvāy – in tirunāvāy; avaiyuḷ – in his divine assembly; pugalāvadu – to enter; ōr nāḷ – one day; aṟiyēnē – I don’t know

**Перевод:**

**Thinking at all times “when will I reach”, without having the heart to focus on anything else, I will shed tears; I don’t know the day I will enter the divine assembly of the defectless nārāyaṇa, who is śriya:pati, in tirunāvāy.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the third pāsuram, āḻvār becomes anguished saying “I don’t know when I will enter the divine assembly of emperumān in tiruvāy?”*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. evaikol aṇugap peṟu nāḷ enṟeppōdum kavaiyil manam inṟik kaṇṇīrgaḷ kaluḻvan navaiyil tirunāraṇan sēr tirunāvāy avaiyuḷ pugalāvadu ōr nāḷ aṟiyēnē*

- *evaikol …* – Thinking “When will I reach there?”
- *eppōdum* – Am I saying this once and doing other things at other times?
- *kavaiyil manm inṟi* – Even in that, am I engaged in this and worldly matters simultaneously? Without having double-minded heart.
- *kaṇṇīrgaḷ kaluḻvan* – I will shed a flood of tears.
- *navai il tirunāraṇan* – nārāyaṇa who is śrīmān and who has no defects such as being difficult to attain etc. One who has arrived and is easily approachable in tirunāvāy along with pirātti who is the cause for his easy approacability. While [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) is present in the great assembly in tirunāvāy, I don’t know, when I, who desired in [tiruvāimoḻi – 2.3.10](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/02/thiruvaimozhi-2-3-10-kalippum-kavarvum/) “*adiyārgaḷ kuḻāngaḷai udan kūduvadu enṟu kolō*” (When will I be amidst the nityasūris?), will reach in that divine assembly?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 9.8.4. Nalel ariyen

*nāḷēl aṟiyēn enakkuḷḷana nānum mīḷā adimaip paṇi seyyap pugundēn nīḷār malarc cōlaigaḷ sūḻ tirunāvāy vāḷēy tadangaṇ madappinnai maṇāḷā!*

**Пословный перевод:**

nīḷ – tall; Ar – full; malar – having flower; sōlaigaḷ – gardens; sūḻ – surrounded; tirunāvāy – in tirunāvāy; vāḷ ēy – having huge radiance like sword; tadam kaṇ – having expansive eyes; madappinnai – for nappinnaip pirātti who is complete in all qualities; maṇāḷā – Oh perfect enjoyer!; nānum – I am also; mīḷā adimaip paṇi seyya – to perform eternal kainkaryam without any break; pugundēn – engaged; enakku – for me; uḷḷana – ordained; nāḷ ēl – the day; aṟiyēn – I don’t know (them)

**Перевод:**

**Oh perfect enjoyer of nappinnaip pirātti who is complete in all qualities, who is having expansive eyes with huge radiance like sword, residing in tirunāvāy surrounded with gardens having tall and full flowers! I am also engaged to perform eternal kainkaryam without any break; I don’t know the day which is ordained for me to perform such kainkaryam.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fourth pāsuram, āḻvār is becoming restless saying “For you who are present along with nappinnaip pirātti in tirunāvāy which has divine gardens which are suitable to accept all service, when will I who am accepted by you to perform true service, engage in service of your divine feet”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. nāḷēl aṟiyēn enakkuḷḷana nānum mīḷā adimaip paṇi seyyap pugundēn nīḷār malarc cōlaigaḷ sūḻ tirunāvāy vāḷēy tadangaṇ madappinnai maṇāḷā!*

- *nāḷēl aṟiyēn enakku uḷḷana* – He is saying “I don’t know the day when I will get this opportunity”; or saying “I don’t know as to how long I need to wait for this”.

When asked “While the result is guaranteed, why the anxiety?” [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) says,

- *nānum mīḷā adimaip paṇi seyyap pugundēn* – Did I not engage in the true service which is performed by nityasūris?  Am I remaining relaxed as a person who would seek any benefit? ōr am I remaining relaxed due to not knowing the taste of servitude?
- *nīḷār malarc cōlaigaḷ* – The abode where the gardens have tall, well blossomed flowers. The abode which has no shortage of flowers etc which are useful in service; alternative meaning – The abode where nappinnaip pirātti and [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) can pluck the flowers and enjoy them fully.
- *vāḷ ēy tadam kaṇ* – Radiant, expansive eyes; expansive eyes which are like sword in destroying others; one who has beautiful eyes which will make him fully exist for her.
- *madappinnai maṇāḷā* – Oh beloved consort of nappinnaip pirātti who not only has phyiscal beauty but also internal qualities which will immerse you in her! Just as a son who went to a different town, while returning to the home town, as the home town gets closer, will think about the mother, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) too thinks about the pirāttis individually and together, as the prāpya dēśam (the apt destination) gets closer.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 9.8.5. Manalan

*maṇāḷan malar mangaikkum maṇ madandaikkum kaṇṇāḷan ulagattuyir dēvargatkellām viṇṇāḷan virumbi uṟaiyum tirunāvāy kaṇṇārak kaḷikkinṟadingenṟukol kaṇḍē*

**Пословный перевод:**

malar mangaikkum – for lakshmi who is seated on lotus flower; maṇ madandaikkum – for śrī bhūmip pirātti; maṇāḷan – being the enjoyer; ulagattu – in the world; uyir dēvargatku ellām – for all creatures, dēvas et al; kaṇṇāḷan – being the controller; viṇ āḷan – one who accepts the service of the residents of paramapadam which is known as parama vyōma (supreme sky); virumbi – (in these two worlds) desirously; uṟaiyum – residing; tirunāvāy – tirunāvāy; kaṇ – eyes; Ara – to become complete; kaṇḍu – see; ingu – here; kaḷikkinṟadu – to become perfectly blissful; enṟukol – when?

**Перевод:**

**When will my eyes see emperumān who is the enjoyer of lakshmi who is seated on lotus flower and śrī bhūmip pirātti, who is the controller of all creatures, dēvas et al in the \[material\] world, who accepts the service of the residents of paramapadam which is known as parama vyōma and who is residing desirously in tirunāvāy, to become complete and to become perfectly blissful here?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fifth pāsuram, āḻvār says “When will I see tirunāvāy to eliminate the craving of my eyes and be satisfied?”*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. maṇāḷan malar mangaikkum maṇ madandaikkum kaṇṇāḷan ulagattuyir dēvargatkellām viṇṇāḷan virumbi uṟaiyum tirunāvāy kaṇṇārak kaḷikkinṟadingenṟukol kaṇḍē*

- *maṇāḷan …* – One who is dear to periya pirāttiyār (śrī mahālakśmi) and śrī bhūmip pirāttiyār. Should I lose even after the presence of the one who performs puruśakāram (śrī mahālakśmi, who recommends us to him) and the one (śrī bhūmi dēvi) who teaches compassion to him?
- *kaṇṇāḷan …* – One who is the controller of humans, celestial beings et al in this world. It is because of his connection with his divine consorts that he is protecting everyone.
- *viṇṇāḷan* – This is how his private quarter is; one who controls the nityasūris by remaining in the divya paryankam (divine throne/cot) in paramapadam along with his divine consorts.
- *virumbi uṟaiyum tirunāvāy* – The lord of both worlds (spiritual and material realm) is residing in tirunāvāy as if it is a rare commodity to get. Other than the place he desires, there is no other apt destination.
- *kaṇ Ara* – The eyes which acquired fatigue due to the craving in seeing him. Ara – to become full/complete.
- *kaḷikkinṟadu ingu enṟu kol* – Apart from becoming blissful in paramapadam as said in taittirīya upaniśat “*aham annam aham annam aham annam*” (I am the food enjoyed by bhagavān – repetition implies emphasis), when will I become blissful here itself?
- *kaṇḍē* – Due to firm belief in seeing bhagavān, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying “when will I become blissful seeing you?” instead of just saying “when will I become blissful?”

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 9.8.6. Kande kalikkinradu

*kaṇḍē kaḷikkinṟadingenṟukol kaṇgaḷ toṇḍē unakkāy oḻindēn turisinṟi vaṇḍār malarc cōlaigaḷ sūḻ tirunāvāy koṇḍē uṟaiginṟa engōvalar kōvē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vaṇḍu Ar – filled with beetles; malarc cōlaigaḷ – gardens with flowers; sūḻ – surrounded; tirunāvāy – tirunāvāy; koṇḍu – having (in his divine heart, as residence); uṟaiginṟa – one who is eternally residing; em kōvalr kōvē – Oh kriṣṇa who manifested your simplicity to covherd boys and me, and became our lord!; turisu inṟi – without deception; unakkē – for you only; toṇḍē oḻindēn – became desirous; kaṇgaḷ – my eyes; ingu – here; kaṇḍē kaḻikkinṟadu – eternally enjoying by seeing; enṟukol – when?

**Перевод:**

**Oh kriṣṇa who manifested your simplicity to covherd boys and me, and became our lord, who are having in your divine heart and eternally residing in tirunāvāy which is surrounded with gardens with flowers filled with beetles! I became desirous for you only, without deception; when will my eyes eternally enjoy by seeing you here?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the sixth pāsuram, āḻvār says to emperumān in tirunāvāy “When will my eyes see you and become blissful?”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. kaṇḍē kaḷikkinṟadingenṟukol kaṇgaḷ toṇḍē unakkāy oḻindēn turisinṟi vaṇḍār malarc cōlaigaḷ sūḻ tirunāvāy koṇḍē uṟaiginṟa engōvalar kōvē*

- *kaṇḍē kaḷikkinṟadu ingu enṟukol kaṇgaḷ* – Let me do whatever I can; when will the fatigue of my eyes end?

When asked “Certainly [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) will see him one day; now, what is the reason to force him?” āḻvār says,

- *toṇḍē unakkāy oḻindēn …* – Without any diversion, I have become fully desirous on your divine feet. My desire is so much that I cannot lose this even for a fraction of a moment. turisu – contact with undesirable aspects for the mind.
- *vaṇḍu …* – Just as the buds/fragrance, even the beetles are present in the flowers. The town which is having such gardens with beetle-filled flowers. Greatly enjoyable town which would not let those who entered it, leave it, as said in cāndōjña upaniśat 8.15 “*na ca punarāvartatē*” (there is no return).
- *koṇḍē uṟaiginṟa* – The town which is celebrated in his divine heart thinking “This is the apt abode where my devotees and I can interact as desired” and where he is residing.
- *em kōvalar kōvē* – Just as you incarnated as kriṣṇa and became easily approachable for the covherd clan, you arrived in tirunāvāy and became easily approachable for me!

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 9.8.7. Kovagiya mavaliyai

*kōvāgiya māvaliyai nilangoṇḍāy dēvāsuram seṟṟavanē tirumālē nāvāy uṟaiginṟa en nāraṇa nambī! āvā adiyān ivan enṟaruḷāyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kōvāgiya – one who considered himself as the lord (of three worlds, up to svarga lōka); māvaliyai – mahābali; nilam koṇḍāy – became the lord to eliminate any claim of ownership on it by others by requesting and getting the world and making it to exist only for you; dēvāsuram – the enmity caused due to the differentiation of dēvas (saintly people) and asuras (demoniac people); seṟṟavanē – one who eliminates and makes everyone be surrendered unto you; nāvāy uṟaiginṟa – one who is eternally residing in tirunāvāy; en – my; nāraṇa nambī – one who is having completeness due to having all qualities and wealth; tirumālē – Oh one who is having the distinguished cause of being śriya:pati (lord of śrī mahālakśmi) which is the reason for your completeness in being the lord, protector and apt goal!; A A – alas!; ivan adiyān enṟu – saying “he is our servitor”; aruḷāyē – you should shower your mercy seeing the three types of relationship (ananyārha śēśatva, ananya śaraṇatva, ananya bhōjñatva) \[with me\]

**Перевод:**

**You \[emperumān\] became the lord \[again\] to eliminate any claim of ownership on it by others by requesting and getting the world from mahābali who considered himself as the lord. You  eliminated the enmity caused due to the differentiation of dēvas (saintly people) and asuras (demoniac people) and made everyone be surrendered unto you. You are eternally residing in tirunāvāy. You are having completeness due to having all qualities and wealth. Oh one who is having the distinguished cause of being śriya:pati (lord of śrī mahālakśmi) which is the reason for your completeness in being the lord, protector and apt goal! Alas! You should shower your mercy seeing the three types of relationship saying “he is our servitor”.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the seventh pāsuram, āḻvār says “Oh nāraṇa nambi who is eternally residing in tirunāvāy! You should mercifully shower your mercy upon me considering ‘alas! he has no other refuge’ ”*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. kōvāgiya māvaliyai nilangoṇḍāy dēvāsuram seṟṟavanē tirumālē nāvāy uṟaiginṟa en nāraṇa nambī! āvā adiyān ivan enṟaruḷāyē*

- *kōvāgiya māvaliyai nilam koṇḍāy* – sarvēśvaran made indra the leader of the three worlds (up to svarga lōka); mahābali pushed indra away, grabbed the throne and proclaimed himself to be the leader. He was thinking “you \[[emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)\] need not give me; I am the controller myself” and remained prideful; emperumān mercifully saw and thought “when he does not have anything on his own, he is claiming ownership like this; if we let him really be the leader, the world will not survive” and redeemed indra’s belongings from mahābali.
- *dēvāsuram seṟṟavanē* – When he saw that dēvas and asuras were harming each other, [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) destroyed asuras and provided comfortable living for the dēvas.
- *tirumālē* – His being śriya:pati is the reason for giving protection to his devotees and destroying the enemies of such devotees.
- *nāvāy uṟaiginṟa* – One who is eternally residing in tirunāvāy which is in close proximity so that he can visibly protect his devotees.
- *en nāraṇa nambī* – One who remains as the antaryāmi of all to protect the devotees.
- *nāraṇa nambī* – Oh one who is āśrita vatsala (one who has motherly love towards devotees) which is the cause for protecting them, and who is complete due to protecting them all!
- *A A …* – As said in taittirīya bhruguvalli 10.5 “*krupāmātra manōvrutti:*” (with the divine heart filled with grace), you should mercifully shower your mercy upon me thinking “Alas! He has no other refuge; he has no one to surrender unto”.
- *adiyān* – [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is highlighting the relationship \[of self being a servitor of bhagavān\] which makes him \[bhagavān\] shower his mercy and makes āḻvār \[ātmā\] accepting such mercy.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 9.8.8. Aruladolivay

*aruḷādoḻivāy aruḷ seydu adiyēnaip poruḷākki un ponnadik kīḻp pugavaippāy maruḷē inṟi unnai ennenjattiruttum teruḷē taru ten tirunāvāy en dēvē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

aruḷādu oḻivāy – you may not shower your mercy (thinking let him do whatever he likes); adiyēnai – me (who has no other refuge, and who remains for you); aruḷ seydu – showering your infinite mercy; poruḷ ākki – making me have an existence; un pon adik kīḻ – under your attractive divine feet; puga – to enter; vaippāy – you may place me; then – well-organised; tirunāvāy – in tirunāvāy; en dēvē – Oh my ultimate goal!; maruḷē inṟi – without a trace of ignorance; unnai – you (who are complete and enjoyable in all manner); en nenjattu – in my heart (greatly desirous me); iruttum – to place and enjoy; teruḷē – clear knowledge; taru – you should mercifully give me

**Перевод:**

**You may not shower your mercy; or you may shower your infinite mercy upon me, making me have an existence by placing me under your attractive divine feet. Oh my ultimate goal who is present in the well-organised tirunāvāy! You should mercifully give me clear knowledge to place you in my heart and enjoy you, without a trace of ignorance.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the eighth pāsuram, āḻvār became anguished since he did not attain the result as desired; hence he prays saying “It does not matter whether you wish to shower your mercy or  you wish to avoid me; now mercifully allow me to think about you without getting bewildered”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. aruḷādoḻivāy aruḷ seydu adiyēnaip poruḷākki un ponnadik kīḻp pugavaippāy maruḷē inṟi unnai ennenjattiruttum teruḷē taru then tirunāvāy en dēvē!*

- *aruḷādu oḻivāy* – You can remain without showering your mercy upon me considering “let him suffer”.
- *aruḷ seydu* – ōr, you can see my pitiful state and bless me.
- *adiyēnai …* – To turn me who is as good as asat \[acit (insentient) matter\] to become a vastu \[cit (sentient matter)\] as said in taittirīya upaniśat “*santamēnam*” (to exist), and place me under your perfectly enjoyable divine feet, if you desire so.
- *maruḷē inṟi …* – Just as you gave unblemiśed knowledge and devotion as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.1.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/03/thiruvaimozhi-1-1-1-uyarvara-uyarnalam/) “*mayarvaṟa madinalam aruḷinan*” (blessed unblemiśed knowledge and devotion), to have you in my mind always without a trace of ignorance, you should give me the clarity which is explained in [tiruvāimoḻi 2.9.4](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/06/thiruvaimozhi-2-9-4-enakke-atchey/) “*tanakkēyāga enaik koḷḷum īdē*” (he should accept me for his own sake). *then tirunāvāy en dēvē – teruḷē taru* – is the operational phrase; alternatively – piḷḷān explains this as “*maruḷē inṟi unnai en nenjattu iruttum teruḷē taru then tirunāvāy en dēvē! aruḷādu oḻivāy, aruḷ seydu adiyēnaip poruḷākki un ponnadik kīḻp pugavaippāy*; (Oh my lord in the well-organized tirunāvāy! Without a trace of ignorance, give me the clarity to place you in my heart; whether you bless me by making me an entity and placing me at your divine feet or not bless me, do it as per your divine heart’s wish”.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 9.8.9. Devar munivarkku

*dēvar munivarkku enṟum kāṇḍaṟkariyanmūvar mudalvan oru mūvulagāḷidēvan virumbi uṟaiyum tirunāvāyyāvar aṇugap peṟuvār ini andō?*

**Пословный перевод:**

dēvar munivarkku – for all dēvatās and for sages such as sanaka et al; enṟum – at all times; kāṇḍaṟku – to see; ariyan – difficult; mūvar – brahma, rudra et al; mudalvan – one who is the cause for sustenance; oru – distinguished; mū ulagau – three worlds; āḷi – being the controller (with his sankalpam (vow)); dēvan – īśvara who is the abode of all auspicious qualities; virumbi – with great affection; uṟaiyum – residing; tirunāvāy – tirunāvāy; andō – alas!; ini – now; aṇugap peṟuvār yāvar – who will reach there?

**Перевод:**

**īśvara who is difficult to be seen for all dēvatās and for sages such as sanaka et al, who is the cause for sustenance of brahmā, rudra et al, who is the controller of distinguished three worlds, is residing in tirunāvāy with great affection. Alas! Who will reach there now? Implies that when it is not attainable with such great love and intent, is it possible to attain it ever?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the ninth pāsuram, āḻvār says “I am perishing here  in not seeing tirunāvāy. Now, who are those fortunate ones who enjoy tirunāvāy?” as daśarata cakravarti said in “natēmanuśyā: dēvā:“.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. dēvar munivarkku enṟum kāṇḍaṟkariyanmūvar mudalvan oru mūvulagāḷidēvan virumbi uṟaiyum tirunāvāyyāvar aṇugap peṟuvār ini andō?*

- *dēvar munivarkku enṟum kāṇḍaṟku ariyan* – One who is difficult to be seen for brahmā et al \[dēvas\] and for sanaka et al \[sages\] always, by their own efforts.
- *mūvar mudalvan* – Incarnating amidst brahmā and rudra \[as viṣṇu\] and controlling them; or being the controller of brahmā, rudra and indra.
- *oru mū ulagu āḷi* – Ruling over the three worlds \[bhū:, bhuva: and svarga\] through indra; or being the distinguished leader of the three layered universe.
- *dēvan* – One who is different from all entities.
- *virumbi uṟaiyum tirunāvāy* – The abode where such [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who is the controller of all, greatly relishes and stays in the abode as if he has no place to stay, thinking “This is the apt abode to protect my devotees”.
- *yāvar aṇugap peṟuvār ini* – I am perishing here; now who will get this! As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 64.69 “*natēmanuśyā:*” (they are not humans), they cannot be counted along with humans. With “*ini*“, it is highlighted that “I am finished”. With “*andō*“, it is implied that “Why is he not going through my state?”. “*natēmanuśyā:*” – they can not be counted along the mortal beings. “*dēvā:”* – They have to be counted along with those who can eternally enjoy bhagavān. “*yē cāru śubha kuṇḍalam …*” – Who is that most fortunate person who will get to see the decorated face of [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) after surviving for fourteen years \[bharatāḻvān waiting for śrī rāma\]? Those who enjoy emperumān here at a particular time are greater than nityasūris who enjoy him constantly; tiruviruttam 79 “*viṇṇuḷārilum sīriyarē*” (those who constantly worship emperumān here in this word are greater than nityasūris\]. “*varśē panca daśē puna:*” – Only those who remain in the fifteenth year from now, after spending fourteen years, will get to see śrī rāma. daśarata cakravarti thinks that his time is up.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 9.8.10. Ando! anugapperunal

*andō! aṇugap peṟunāḷ enṟu eppōdumsindai kalangit tirumāl! enṟaḻaippankondār malarc cōlaigaḷ sūḻ tirunāvāyvandē uṟaiginṟa em maṇivaṇṇā*

**Пословный перевод:**

kondu Ar – filled with bunches; malarc cōlaigaḷ – gardens having flowers; sūḻ – surrounded; tirunāvāy – in tirunāvāy; vandē – (abandoning paramapadam etc) having arrived and standing here; uṟaiginṟa – one who is eternally residing; em mā maṇivaṇṇā – Oh one who is having a divine form which resembles perfectly enjoyable blue gem!; andō – alas!; aṇugap peṟu nāḷ enṟu – asking “When will I reach you?”; eppōdum – always; sindai kalangi – with a bewildered heart; tirumāl enṟu – saying “Oh śrīmān!”; aḻaippan – I am calling out

**Перевод:**

**Oh one who is having a divine form which resembles perfectly enjoyable blue gem, who has arrived and is eternally residing in tirunāvāy which is surrounded with gardens filled with bunches of flowers! Alas! Always asking “When will I reach you?”, I am calling out with a bewildered heart saying “Oh śrīmān!”**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the tenth pāsuram, āḻvār says “Even if I don’t attain you after desiring for you, I will be bewildered and call out ‘tirumālē!’ “.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. andō! aṇugap peṟunāḷ enṟu eppōdumsindai kalangit tirumāl! enṟaḻaippankondār malarc cōlaigaḷ sūḻ tirunāvāyvandē uṟaiginṟa em maṇivaṇṇā*

- *andō aṇugap peṟu nāḷ enṟu eppōdum* – Due to lack of strength in completing the sentence which he started, [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) is saying andō (alas). He thought of saying “aṇugap peṟu nāḷ yavaikol”.
- *eppōdum* – Instead of giving up after trying to say it once and becoming weakened, he keeps saying it always.
- *sindai kalangi …* – having his heart bewildered; just as an anguished son will call out the names of his mother and father, I will call out “*tirumāl*” (beloved lord of śrī mahālakśmi).
- *kondu Ar …* – In tirunāvāy which is surrounded by gardens filled with bunches of flowers. Since the abode has gardens in permanent spring season, it can be said as perfectly enjoyable.
- *vandē uṟaiginṟa* – Oh one who is eternally residing here for the sake of your devotees with the form that can be seen in paramapadam! Implies “Until you show that form to me, your arrival is as good as false”.

## 9.8.11. Vannam manimada

*vaṇṇam maṇi māda nal nāvāy uḷḷānai tiṇṇam madiḷ tenkurugūrc catakōpan paṇṇār tamiḻ āyirattippattum vallār maṇṇāndu maṇam kamaḻvar malligaiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vaṇṇam – having many colours; maṇi – made with carbuncles; mādam – having mansions; nal – perfectly enjoyable; nāvāy uḷḷānai – on the one who is residing in tirunāvāy; tiṇ – firm; am – beautiful; madiḷ – having fort; tenkurugūr – leader of āḻvārtirunagari; satakōpan – nammāḻvār’s; paṇ Ar – filled with tune; tamiḻ āyirattu – among thousand tamiḻ pāsurams; ippattum – this decad; vallār – those who can practice; maṇ – leelā vibhūti (material realm) which is indicated by bhūmi; āṇḍu – ruling as per their desire for bhagavān and in nitya vibhūti (spiritual realm) with knowledge in enjoying bhagavān; malligai – being very pure like jasmine; maṇam kamaḻvar – will remain famous, fragrant and be blossomed

**Перевод:**

**nammāḻvār, the leader of āḻvārtirunagari which is having firm, beautiful fort composed this decad among the thousand tamiḻ pāsurams filled with tune on emperumān who is residing in perfectly enjoyable tirunāvāy having mansions made with carbuncles of many colours. Those who can practice this decad will rule this leelā vibhūti (material realm) which is indicated by bhūmi as per their desire for bhagavān and will remain famous, fragrant and be blossomed like a very pure jasmine and in nitya vibhūti (spiritual realm) with knowledge in enjoying bhagavān**

*In the end, āḻvār explains the results for those who learn this decad.*

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*In the end, āḻvār explains that those who learn this decad will enjoy all pleasures in this world and other world. vaṇṇam maṇi māda nal nāvāy uḷḷānai tiṇṇam madiḷ tenkurugūrc catakōpan paṇṇār tamiḻ āyirattippattum vallār maṇṇāndu maṇam kamaḻvar malligaiyē*

- *vaṇṇam maṇi māda nal nāvāy uḷḷānai* – One who is mercifully standing in the perfectly enjoyable tirunāvāy which is having mansions which are made with precious gems of many colours.
- *tiṇṇam …* – Mercifully spoken by [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) who is the leader of [āḻvārtirunagari](http://azhwarthiunagari.koyil.org/) which is having firm fort. It appears that tirunāvāy has its protection in the fort of āḻvārtirunagari. \[Two explanations\] Since āḻvār is caring towards tirunāvāy, that care is the protection for the town; alternate explanation – since āḻvār is [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s wealth and since fort is required where the wealth is, āḻvārtirunagari is fortified and protected \[hence emperumān is also protected since his main wealth is protected\].
- *paṇ Ar tamiḻ* – tamiḻ pāsurams which have abundance of tune.
- *maṇ āṇḍu* – Being opulent with śrīvaiṣṇavaśrī (the wealth of kainkaryam) in this world.
- *maṇam kamaḻvar malligaiyē* – Will be fragrant as jasmine. This is highlighted as a representative to indicate that they will attain sāmyāpatti (equivalence) with bhagavān who is said to be  “*sarvaganda:*” (root of all fragrance). It is said that [āḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/)‘s desire is the reason for their attainment of the ultimate goal.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 9.9 Malligai kamal

## 9.9.1. Malligai kamal

*malligai kamaḻ tenṟal īrumālō! vaṇ kuṟinji isai tavarumālō! sel kadir mālaiyum mayakkumālō! sekkar nan mēgangaḷ sidaikkumālō! alliyam tāmaraik kaṇṇan emmān āyargaḷēṟariyēṟu emmāyōn pulliya mulaigaḷum tōḷum koṇḍu pugalidam aṟigilam tamiyamālō!*

**Пословный перевод:**

malligai kamaḻ – having the fragrance of jasmine; tenṟal – southerly breeze; īrum – piercing me in all ways like a sword applied with poison!; vaṇ – pleasing to the ears and easily graspable even for non-inquisitive ones; kuṟinji isai – music with the tune of kuṟinji; tavarum – pierces deep into the self; sel – focussed on setting; kadir – having sun; mālaiyum – evening time; mayakkum – causes bewilderment (to destroy the knowledge and not be able to even call out); sekkar – during the evening time, having reddish complexion; nal – attractive; mēgangaḷ – clouds; sidaikkum – harming my body by reminding me his form with golden garment; alli – blossomed; am – beautiful; tāmaraik kaṇṇan – one who is having lotus flower like beautiful eyes; emmān – being the lord (who won over us for us to say “jitam” (victory) by that); āyargaḷ ēṟu – having pride which attracts even the gōpas (covherd boys) who belong to the same clan; ari ēṟu – one who is proud like the best lion (due to winning over women and men without any distinction); em māyōn – one who is having amazing activities (of interacting with us humbly during the state of union); pulliya – embraced (being greatly desirous towards me); mulaigaḷum – bosom; tōḷum – shoulders; koṇḍu – having; tamiyam – we who are alone (after being separated from him); pugalidam – refuge; aṟigilōm – we don’t know

**Перевод:**

**The southerly breeze having the fragrance of jasmine is piercing me in all ways like a sword applied with poison! The music with the tune of kuṟinji which is pleasing to the ears and is easily graspable even for non-inquisitive ones, pierces deep into the self; the evening time which is having the sun focussed on setting causes bewilderment; the attractive clouds which are having reddish complexion during the evening time, are harming my body by reminding me of his form with golden garment; we who are alone here after having our bosom and shoulders embraced by emperumān who is having blossomed, beautiful lotus flower like beautiful eyes, being the lord, who is having pride which attracts even the gōpas (covherd boys) who belong to the same clan, who is proud like the best lion and is having amazing activities, don’t know any refuge. The protector is not here; we are helpless; we have a lot of harmful enemies around us; we don’t know how to protect and present him the aspects he likes. Al and O \[ālō\] indicate the great sorrow. He was called out in every line, due to the great sorrow.**
