## 9.10.3. Tondar! nundam

*toṇḍar nundam tuyar pōga nīr ēkamāy viṇḍu vādā malar ittu nīr iṟainjumin vaṇḍu pādum poḻil sūḻ tirukkaṇṇapurattu aṇḍa vāṇan amarar perumānaiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vaṇḍu – beetles; pādum – joyfully humming; poḻil – garden; sūḻ – surrounded; tirukkaṇṇapurattu – in tirukkaṇṇapuram; aṇḍa vāṇan – being the resident of paramapadam; amarar perumānai – one who remained there being enjoyed by nityasūris; toṇḍar – Oh you who are all desirous for all kainkaryams!; num tam tuyar – your sorrow of not enjoying him; pōga – to be eliminated; nīr – all of you; ēkam āy – having a common focus; viṇḍu – looking to blossom; vādā – remaining fresh; malar ittu – offering flowers; nīr iṟainjumin – worship him matching your śēśatvam (servitude)

**Перевод:**

**emperumān, the resident of paramapadam who remained there being enjoyed by nityasūris, is now in tirukkaṇṇapuram surrounded by garden which is having joyfully humming beetles. Oh you who are all desirous for all kainkaryams! To have your sorrow of not enjoying him eliminated, all of you, having a common focus, worship him matching your śēśatvam, offering fresh flowers which are set to blossom.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the third pāsuram, āḻvār says “Oh you who are desirous! Being ananyaprayōjana (without any expectation other than kainkaryam) surrender unto emperumān who is the lord of spiritual and material realm and who is mercifully standing in tirukkaṇṇapuram,  to have your sorrows eliminated”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. toṇḍar nundam tuyar pōga nīr ēkamāy viṇḍu vādā malar ittu nīr iṟainjumin vaṇḍu pādum poḻil sūḻ tirukkaṇṇapurattu aṇḍa vāṇan amarar perumānaiyē*

- *toṇḍar* – You who have a little bit of desire; you who are born for service as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 31.25 “*aham sarvam kariśyāmi*” (I will serve you both (perumāḷ and pirātti) in all the ways).
- *num tam tuyar pōga* – Even their sorrows can be different; it could be sorrows due to not getting worldly desires fulfilled; or the sorrow due to not praying to emperumān.
- *nīr ēkamāy* – Being ananyaprayōyana; being like-minded. As “toṇḍar” (servitor) they could be having single voice/desire.
- *viṇḍu vādā malar* – The flowers which are starting to blossom and not the flowers which are dried. Saying that  you should approach emperumān with fresh flowers.
- *vaṇḍu pādum …* – The abode which is surrounded by garden having beetles being drunk with honey, and humming as said in taittirīya upaniśat “*ētat sāma gāyannāstē*” (The liberated soul is singing sāma gānam). Ultimately enjoyable abode.
- *tirukkaṇṇapurattu aṇḍa vāṇan amarar perumānaiyē* – The one who is easily approachable in tirukkaṇṇapuram is the lord of spiritual and material realms; saying – one who is resident of paramapadam, being as said in tiruvāimoḻi 1.1.1 “*ayarvaṟum amarargaḷ adipati*” (the lord of unblemiśed nityasūris); also saying – one who is the leader of leelā vibhūti (aṇḍa vānan) and nityasūris (amarar). One need not surrender here and reach a special abode after having the hurdles removed, to enjoy fully; he is manifesting qualities such as śeelam (simplicity) etc here in tirukkaṇṇapuram so that even nityasūris come and enjoy him here. In a place meant for blind persons, there is no use for people with good vision. That is not the case here. “*pratimāsu aprabuddānām*” (emperumān remains in deity form for the sake of the less intelligent). For this, āḷavandār mercifully explains – If emperumān can attract the less intelligent ones in his deity form, what to speak of those who have clear knowledge about him? \[They will obviously enjoy him lot more in deity form\].

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 9.10.4. Manai nokki

*mānai nōkki madap pinnai tan kēḷvanai tēnai vādā malar ittu nīr iṟainjumin vānai undum madiḷsūḻ tirukkaṇṇapuram tān nayanda perumān saraṇāgumē*

**Пословный перевод:**

mān – deer; nai – to feel anguished (having lost); nōkki – having eyes; madam – complete in all qualities; pinnai than – for nappinnaip pirātti; kēḷvanai – being the beloved lord; tēnai – being enjoyable like honey (as said in “rasōvaisa:“); vādā – fresh; malar ittu – with flowers; nīr – all of you; iṟainjumin – worship; vānai – sky; undu – tall to be pushing; madiḷ sūḻ – surrounded by fort; tirukkaṇṇapuram – tirukkaṇṇapuram; tān nayanda – desired himself; perumān – sarvēśvaran; saraṇ āgumē – in the form of being the refuge, will remain the recipient of your worship

**Перевод:**

**All of you worship emperumān who is the beloved lord of nappinnaip pirātti, who is complete in all qualities and is having eyes which will make deer feel anguished, with fresh flowers; sarvēśvaran in the form of being the refuge, will remain the recipient of your worship, is on his own desire in tirkkaṇṇapuram, which is surrounded by tall fort which is tall enough to be pushing the sky. “tēnai vādā malar” could mean flower which has ever-flowing honey.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fourth pāsuram, āḻvār says “Approach emperumān in tirukkaṇṇapuram with the puruśakāram (recommendation) of nappinnaip pirātti”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. mānai nōkki madap pinnai than kēḷvanai tēnai vādā malar ittu nīr iṟainjumin vānai undum madiḷsūḻ tirukkaṇṇapuram tān nayanda perumān saraṇāgumē*

- *mānai nōkki* – One who is having eyes which make deer feel anguished. Her eyes are such that, deer will feel ashamed having lost to her.
- *madap pinnai than kēḷvan* – One who is the beloved lord of nappinnaip pirātti who has qualities such as femininity.
- *tēnai* – One who is ultimately enjoyable. I am asking you to drink this neem juice \[sarcasm\].
- *vādā malar ittu nīr iṟaijumin* – Offer fresh flowers and approach him. Approaching him is as tasteful as mixing honey and fresh flowers.
- *vānai …* – The town which is surrounded by fort which appears to be scraping the sky and pushing it. Saying that the town is well-protected and cannot be approached by evil entities.
- *tān nayanda perumān* – sarVēśvaran residing here with eagerness thinking “this is the apt place to engage with my devotees”.
- *saraṇ āgumē* – He is your protector. Just as the fort protects him, he will be the fort for you.

## 9.10.5. Saranam agum

*saraṇam āgum tana tāḷ adaindārkkellām maraṇam ānāl vaigundam kodukkum pirān araṇ amainda madiḷ sūḻ tirukkaṇṇapurat taraṇiyāḷan tanadanbarkku anbāgumē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tana tāḷ adaindārkku ellām – for all those who performed prapatti (surrender) unto his divine feet; saraṇam āgum – himself being the means; maraṇam ānāl – in their final moments; vaigundam – the abode from where there is no return; kodukkum – who grants; pirān – being the great benefactor; araṇ amainda – being as a protective layer; madiḷ sūḻ – fortified; tirukkaṇṇapuram – in tirukkaṇṇapuram; taraṇi āḷan – one who is standing there to protect the earth; tanadu anbarkku – for those who are having love towards his divine feet; anbu āgum – will remain as an embodiment of love \[towards them\]

**Перевод:**

**Being the means for all those who performed prapatti (surrender) unto his divine feet, during their final moments, he will be the great benefactor, granting them the abode from where there is no return. Such emperumān is standing in the well-protected, fortified tirukkaṇṇapuram to protect the earth. For those who are having love towards his divine feet, he will remain as an embodiment of love \[towards them\]. “saraṇam āgum tana tāḷ” could also mean divine feet which are the means. taraṇiyāḷan could also mean the beloved lord of śrī bhūmip pirātti.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fifth pāsuram, āḻvār mercifully explains how emperumān mercifully delivers those who are unable to engage in bhakti yōgam but hold on to his divine feet as the means.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. saraṇam āgum tana tāḷ adaindārkkellām maraṇam ānāl vaigundam kodukkum pirān araṇ amainda madiḷ sūḻ tirukkaṇṇapurat taraṇiyāḷan tanadanbarkku anbāgumē*

- *saraṇam āgum tana tāḷ adaindārkku ellām* – Even if someone is inferior by birth, activities and knowledge, if he/she holds on to [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)‘s divine feet as the means, emperumān will remain his/her protector. bhakti yōga which was explained previously (in three pāsurams) is adikrutādikāram (only qualified persons can pursue), but prapatti which is explained in this pāsuram, is sarvādikāram (anyone can pursue); it is said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 9.29](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/9-29) “*samōham sarva bhūtēśu*” (I am equally disposed towards all creatures). bhagavat viśayam (matters related to bhagavān) is like sparśavēdi (touch stone); in kaiśika purāṇam, the conversation of a brāhamaṇa with caṇḍāḷa who was a devotee of bhagavān led to being the remedy for the shortcomings in the brāhmaṇa’s ritualistic conduct; this is the principle which is explained in those incidents.
- *maraṇam ānāl vaigundam kodukkum pirān* – The benefactor who cannot tolerate the separation of the person who performed bharanyāsam (surrender), based on the taste of the individual, waited until his body falls down and grants paramapadam to him at that time. Here the \[elongated\] tone of “*maraṇamānāl*” indicates that while [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) should have taken the person on the day the person surrendered at his divine feet, the time between that day of surrender and the day of death, is as said in tiruvāimoḻi 10.3.1 “*oru pagal āyiram ūḻi*” (one day feels like an eon). “*maraṇamānāl*” indicates – there is no incapability in emperumān, the prapanna (surrendered person) has nothing more to do, yet emperumān lets the prapanna stay in this world, based on the prapanna’s desire. The elaborate explanation given in the introductory section of this decad is based on this meaning explained for “*maraṇamānāl*“.
- *araṇ amainda* – One need not fear thinking “one who is under the care of nityasūris is present here; what danger may befall him?” Made to be a protective layer.
- *taraṇi āḷan* – Leader of the earth. Indicating that he is the protector of the samsāris (worldly people).
- *tanadu anbarkku anbāgumē* – He will be greatly affectionate towards those who are devoted to him.
- *anbāgum* – He will be an embodiment of love, instead of saying “he has love” where he and love can be individually seen.

## 9.10.6. Anban agum

*anbanāgum tana tāḷ adaindārkkellām sembon āgattu avuṇan udal kīṇḍavan nanpon ēynda madiḷ sūḻ tirukkaṇṇapurattu anban nāḷum tana meyyarkku meyyanē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tana tāḷ adaindārkku ellām – for those who surrendered unto his divine feet; anban āgum – being with ultimate vātsalyam (motherly forbearance); sem – reddish; pon – like gold; āgattu – having form; avuṇan – hiraṇya, the demon’s; udal – body; kīṇḍavan – one who effortlessly tore apart; nan pon – by pure gold; ēynda – made; madiḷ sūḻ – surrounded by fort; tirukkaṇṇapurattu – in tirukkaṇṇapuram; anban – one who desirously resides; than meyyarkku – for those who consider emperumān as the ultimate goal; nāḷum – always; meyyan – (he too, towards them) will consider them as the ultimate goal

**Перевод:**

**emperumān being with ultimate vātsalyam for those who surrendered unto his divine feet, who effortlessly tore the body of hiraṇya, the demon who was having reddish gold like form, is desirously residing in tirukkaṇṇapuram which is surrounded by fort made of pure gold. For those who consider emperumān as the ultimate goal, he will always consider them as his ultimate goal.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the sixth pāsuram, āḻvār says “emperumān in tirukkaṇṇapuram will eliminate the hurdles of those who surrender unto him and will be affectionate towards them”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. anbanāgum tana tāḷ adaindārkkellām sembon āgattu avuṇan udal kīṇḍavan nanpon ēynda madiḷ sūḻ tirukkaṇṇapurattu anban nāḷum tana meyyarkku meyyanē*

- *anban …* – For those who hold his divine feet as the means, as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 21.20 “*śaraṇāgata vatsala:*” (sītā says – śrī rāma shows motherly love towards those who surrender unto him), he will have great love towards them where he will not see their faults; śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 18.3 ‘*dōśō yadyapi tasya syāt’* (Even if faults are there in him, let them be). What does he do to their hurdles? They will see the same fate as prahlāda’s hurdles. One who effortlessly tore apart the body of the demon, hiraṇya.
- *nan pon ēynda madiḷ* – Fort made of pure gold; attractive fort.
- *tirukkaṇṇapurattu anban* – The abode where he resides thinking “this is the apt place to protect my devotees”.
- *nāḷum tana meyyarkku meyyanē* – For those who are ananyaprayōjana (not having any expectation other than kainkaryam) towards him, he too remains ananyaprayōjana (not having any expecation other than being with them). For those who have friendly attitude \[even if it is superficial\], he will remain as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 8.3 ‘*natyajēyam*‘ (I will not abandon even if he has faults).

## 9.10.7. Meyyan agum

*meyyan āgum virumbit toḻuvārkkellām poyyan āgum puṟamē toḻuvārkkellām seyyil vāḷai ugaḷum tirukkaṇṇapurattu aiyan āgattaṇaippārgatku aṇiyanē*

**Пословный перевод:**

virumbit toḻuvārkku ellām – for those who desirously surrender unto him, having him as the goal; meyyan āgum – he will shine manifesting his ultimate form of being the goal; puṟamē toḻuvārkku ellām – for those who surrender unto him seeking other benefits; poyyan āgum – will hide himself after granting those benefits; seyyil – the fields, which are the natural habitat; vāḷai – vāḷai fish; ugaḷum – jumping around; tirukkaṇṇapurattu – in tirukkaṇṇapuram; aiyan – being the natural relative for both categories of persons; āgattu aṇaippārgatku – for those who consider him as the means, in their heart; aṇiyanē – (while being a natural relative) he remains distinguiśedly easily approachable

**Перевод:**

**For those who desirously surrender unto him having him as the goal, he will shine manifesting his ultimate form of being the goal; for those who surrender unto him seeking other benefits, he will hide himself after granting those benefits; for those who consider him as the means, in their heart, being the natural relative for both categories of persons, he remains distinguiśedly easily approachable in tirukkaṇṇapuram where the vāḷai fish are jumping around in the fields, which are their natural habitat.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the seventh pāsuram, āḻvār says “For ananyaprayōjana (those who expect nothing but kainkaryam) he remains easily approachable and for prayōjanāntarapara (those who seek other benefits) he fulfils their desires and remains away from them”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. meyyan āgum virumbit toḻuvārkkellām poyyan āgum puṟamē toḻuvārkkellām seyyil vāḷai ugaḷum tirukkaṇṇapurattu aiyan āgattaṇaippārgatku aṇiyanē*

- *meyyan āgum …* – For those who are ananyaprayojana, whoever they may be, he will completely fulfil their desires; for those who surrender unto emperumān seeking other benefits, he will eagerly grant those benefits which lead to bondage and keep himself away from them. For those who remain as said in mahābhāratam drōṇa parvam “*kriṣṇāśraya: kriṣṇa balā: kriṣṇa nātāśca pāṇḍavā:*” (for the pāṇḍavas, kriṣṇa is the final goal to be attained, kriṣṇa is their strength and kriṣṇa is their Lord), he will remain truthful; as he gave his nārāyaṇa sēnai (army of his associates) and gōpāla sēnai (army of covherds) to duryōdana who came praying for army, he remained with pāṇḍavas and destroyed duryōdana et al and hence remained untruthful to them.
- *seyyil …* – emperumān, the supreme relative who is standing in tirukkaṇṇapuram where the fish are jumping around and living joyfully in the fields. Implies that the abode is so enjoyable that even the animals are living there joyfully. For those who keep him in their hearts, he will be their servitor; for those who are ananyaprayōjana, he will remain as said in  śrī rāmāyaṇam bāla kāṇḍam 31.4 śrī rāma tells viśvāmitra “*imau sma muniśārdūla! kinkarau sampastitau \| ājñāpaya yatēśtam vai śāsanam karavāva kim \|\|*” (Oh best among sages! We are near you to serve your highness. You can order us. What should we do?)

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 9.10.8. Aniyan agum

*aṇiyan āgum tana tāḷ adaindārkkellām piṇiyum sārā piṟavi keduttāḷum maṇi pon ēynda madiḷ sūḻ tirukkaṇṇapuram paṇimin nāḷum paramētti tan pādamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tana tāḷ – ultimately enjoyable divine feet; adaindārkku ellām – those who attained; aṇiyan āgum – (he) will remain very close and enjoy \[them\]; piṇiyum – disease in the form of other benefits; sārā – will disappear; piṟavi – (being the cause for that) connection with birth \[in material realm\]; keduttu – eliminating it so that there is no need to take birth; āḷum – will accept the service \[from them\]; maṇi – precious gems; pon – gold; ēynda – placed; madiḷ sūḻ – surrounded by fort; tirukkaṇṇapuram – in tirukkaṇṇapuram; paramētti than pādam – divine feet of one who is present, like he is present in paramapadam; nāḷum – eternally; paṇimin – see that you worship and enjoy

**Перевод:**

**To those who attained emperumān’s ultimately enjoyable divine feet, he will remain close and enjoy them; your disease in the form of other benefits will disappear. He will eliminate your connection with birth so that there is no need to take birth, and accept your service. See that you eternally worship the divine feet of emperumān, who is present in tirukkaṇṇapuram which is surrounded by fort having precious gems and gold placed on it,  just as he is present in parampadam, and enjoy them \[emperumān’s divine feet\].**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the eighth pāsuram, āḻvār says “Surrender unto sarvēśvaran; he will eliminate your sorrows and samsāra (bondage in material realm) which is the root cause of your sorrows”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. aṇiyan āgum tana tāḷ adaindārkkellām piṇiyum sārā piṟavi keduttāḷum maṇi pon ēynda madiḷ sūḻ tirukkaṇṇapuram paṇimin nāḷum paramētti than pādamē*

- *aṇiyan āgum tana tāḷ adaindārkku ellām* – For those who surrender unto his divine feet, he will become easily approachable without any restrictions. He is the one who said, as in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 41.4 “*tvayi kincit samāpannē kim kāryam sītayā mama*” (even if you were insulted a little bit, what is the use of my getting back sītā?) towards a newly surrendered animal \[sugrīva mahārāja\].
- *piṇiyum sārā* – All your sorrows will disappear.
- *piṟavi keduttu āḷum* – Birth which is the cause for such sorrows, will be eliminated by him and he will accept your service.
- *maṇi pon ēynda madiḷ sūḻ tirukkaṇṇapuram* – It should be seen as “in tirukkaṇṇapuram” which is surrounded by fort made of precious gems and gold.
- *paramētti than pādamē* *– paṇimin nāḷum* – He remains here without losing any aspect of his in paramapadam. Perform the activities which are natural for the self, at his divine feet. As emperumān, who is served by nityasūris there, has arrived here, you also try to surrender unto his divine feet.

## 9.10.9. Padam nalum

*pādam nāḷum paṇiyat taṇiyum piṇi ēdam sārā enakkēl ini en kuṟai? vēda nāvar virumbum tirukkaṇṇapurattu ādiyānai adaindārkku allal illaiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

pādam – his divine feet; nāḷum – always; paṇiya – to enjoy; piṇi – previous sorrows; taṇiyum – will go; ēdam – any other sorrow; sārā – will not occur; ini – hence; enakku en kuṟai – what worry do I have?; vēda nāvar – those who have reciting vēdam as the hallmark for their tongues; virumbum – desired (due to residing as per “vēda vēdyē“); tirukkaṇṇapurattu – in tirukkaṇṇapuram; ādiyānai – the primordial cause who is known only through vēdam; adaindārkku – for those who attained; allal – sorrow; illaiyē – will not be there

**Перевод:**

**As his divine feet are enjoyed always, previous sorrows will go; further sorrows will not occur; hence, what worry do I have? For those who attained emperumān, the primordial cause who is known only through vēdam, residing in tirukkaṇṇāpuram which is desired by those for whom reciting vēdam is the hallmark for their tongues, there will not be any sorrow. piṇi and ēdam could also imply pūrvāgam (sins before śaraṇāgati) and uttarāgam (sins after śaraṇāgati).**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the ninth pāsuram, āḻvār becomes pleased saying “without anyone instructing me, I surrendered unto emperumān and became joyful”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. pādam nāḷum paṇiyat taṇiyum piṇi ēdam sārā enakkēl ini en kuṟai? vēda nāvar virumbum tirukkaṇṇapurattu ādiyānai adaindārkku allal illaiyē*

- *pāda nāḷum paṇiyat taṇiyum piṇi* – As one surrenders to emperumān’s divine feet, the previous sins which were accumulated since time immemorial will be eliminated. As the pleasing aspect is done, the sins which are the hurdles will be eliminated.
- *ēdam sārā* – The future sins \[after śaraṇāgati\] will not remain.
- *enakkēl ini en kuṟai* – Is there any worry for me, as all my sufferings will be eliminated on bowing at his divine feet?
- *vēda nāvar …* – The primordial cause of the universe who is present in tirukkaṇṇapuram which is the beloved abode of those who are experts in the principles of vēdam. vēda nāvar indicates the likes of tirumangai āḻvār et al. virumbugai (desiring) means as said in periya tirumoḻi 8.9.3 “*kaṇṇapuram onṟu udaiyānukku adiyēn oruvarkku uriyēnō*” (Do I, the servitor of the lord of tirukkaṇṇapuram, belong to anyone else?) pramāṇam (authentic source of knowledge) is vēdam and pramēyam (ultiamte goal) is jagat kāraṇam (the primordial cause of the universe). The entity to be meditated upon is as said in cāndōjña upaniśat “*kāraṇam tu dyēya:*” (meditate upon the origin/cause).
- *ādiyānai adaindārkku allāl illaiyē* – It is certain that there is no sorrow for the one who reclined on the lap of the mother.

## 9.10.10. Illai allal

*illai allal enakkēl ini en kuṟai? alli mādar amarum tirumārbinan kallil ēynda madiḷ sūḻ tirukkaṇṇapuram solla nāḷum tuyar pādu sārāvē*

**Пословный перевод:**

alli – having lotus as the abode; mādar – lakshmi who is best among women; amarum – eternally residing; tirumārbinan – one who is having divine chest; kallil ēynda – with abundant rocks; madiḷ sūḻ – surrounded by fort; tirukkaṇṇapuram – tirukkaṇṇapuram; solla – as one says; nāḷum – always; tuyar – sorrows; pādu – close; sārā – will not come; enakku – for me; allal – sorrow of lacking enjoyment; illai – will not have; ini – now; en kuṟai – what is there to worry?

**Перевод:**

**lakshmi, who is the best among women and is having lotus as her abode, is eternally residing in the divine chest of emperumān who is residing in tirukkaṇṇapuram which is surrounded by fort made of abundant rocks; as one says “tirukkaṇṇapuram”, sorrows will never come close. I will not have the sorrow of lacking enjoyment; now, what is there to worry?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the tenth pāsuram, āḻvār again explains his own benefit out of great joy and says “if one is not able to perform bhakti or prapatti, one can simply say tirukkaṇṇapuram to have all the sorrows eliminated”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. illai allal enakkēl ini en kuṟai? alli mādar amarum tirumārbinan kallil ēynda madiḷ sūḻ tirukkaṇṇapuram solla nāḷum tuyar pādu sārāvē*

- *illai allal* – All sorrows will disappear.
- *enakkēl ini en kuṟai* – What is there to worry for me, now? Since all the hurdles for enjoying bhagavān, which are the sorrows, have been eliminated, do I need to go and find the special abode \[of paramapadam\] for my enjoyment?
- *alli …* – One who has the divine chest which is the permanent abode of periya pirāttiyār. The one \[śrī mahālakśmi\] who says as in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 116-45 “*nakaścin nāparādyati*” (there is none who has not committed a wrongful deed) is with him, so that he would not abandon those who surrender unto him, finding faults in them. As one says the name of the town “tirukkaṇṇapuram” \[their sorrows will be eliminated\]. Those who do not have the tools/faculties to engage in bhakti yōgam and those who do not have the firm faith to perform prapatti, can simply say “tirukkaṇṇapuram” to have all their sorrows eliminated.

## 9.10.11. Padu sara

*pādu sārā vinai paṟṟaṟa vēṇḍuvīr! māda nīdu kurugūrc catakōpan sol pādalāna tamiḻ āyirattuḷ ippattum pādi ādip paṇimin avan tāḷgaḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vinai – all worldly sorrows; pādu sārā – not in your proximity; paṟṟu aṟa vēṇḍuvīr – if you desire to get rid of them; mādam – mansions; nīdu – tall; kurugūr – leader of āḻvārtirunagari; satakōpan – nammāḻvār; sol – mercifully spoken by; pādalāna – in musical form; tamiḻ – in drāvida (tamiḻ) language; āyirattuḷ – among the thousand pāsurams; ippattum – this decad too; pādi – singing due to the joy; ādi – dancing due to the bliss; avan tāḷgaḷ – the divine feet of sarvēśvaran who is easily approachable; paṇimin – try to worship and enjoy

**Перевод:**

**nammāḻvār, the leader of āḻvārtirunagari which has tall mansions, mercifully spoke thousand pāsurams; if you desire to get rid of all worldly sorrows and not have them in your proximity, due to joy, sing this decad too which is among those thousand pāsurams, which is in musical form and in drāvida language. Dance due to the bliss, try to worship the divine feet of sarvēśvaran who is easily approachable, and enjoy them. Implies that as one enjoys bhagavān through this decad, one’s sorrows will be eliminated without a trace.**

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. pādu sārā vinai paṟṟaṟa vēṇḍuvīr! māda nīdu kurugūrc catakōpan sol pādalāna tamiḻ āyirattuḷ ippattum pādi ādip paṇimin avan tāḷgaḷē*

- *pādu sārā vinai paṟṟu aṟa vēṇḍuvīr* – If you desire to have all the sorrows eliminated from your proximity completely without a trace.
- *māda nīdu …* – Mercifully spoken by āḻvār who is the leader of tirunagari which is having eternal mansions. Since this is the advice of trustworthy person, there is no artavādam (exaggeration) in what is explained in tiruvāimoḻi.
- *pādal …* – This decad is so enjoyable, even if an untrustworthy person tells this. As a flower blossoms with fragrance, this decad is sung with music.

## Tenth Centum

## 10.1 Tala tamarai

## 10.1.1. Tala tamarai

*tāḷa tāmarait tada maṇi vayal tirumōgūr nāḷum mēvi nangamarndu ninṟu asurarait tagarkkum tōḷum nāngudaic curi kuḻal kamalak kaṇ kani vāy kāḷamēgattai anṟi maṟṟonṟilam gadiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tāḷa – having the strength of the stem; tāmarai – lotus flowers; tadam – ponds; aṇi – decorating; vayal – having fields; tirumōgūr – in tirumōgūr; nāḷum mēvi – eternally residing; nangu – very; amarndu ninṟu – standing firmly with joy of self satisfaction; asurarai – demoniac persons, who are enemies; tagarkkum – to torment; nāngu tōḷudai – one who is having four divine shoulders; suri kuḻal – (pacifying our sufferings, and being qualified to be the companion) having curly, dense hair; kamalak kaṇ – one who is having lotus like eyes; kani vāy – one who is having friendly coral like divine lips; kāḷamēgattai anṟi – other than the one who is having a magnanimous form resembling a dark cloud; maṟṟu onṟu gadi – any other refuge which is our destination; ilam – we do not have

**Перевод:**

**To torment the demoniac persons who are the enemies, kāḷamēgam emperumān is eternally residing and standing very firmly with the joy of self satisfaction, in tirumōgūr which is having fields decorated with ponds with lotus flowers having strong stem. He is having four divine shoulders, curly, dense hair, lotus like eyes and friendly coral like divine lips. Other than such emperumān who is having a magnanimous form resembling a dark cloud, we do not have any other refuge which is our destination.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the first pāsuram, āḻvār says “We do not have any refuge other than kāḷamēgam emperumān who has the nature of destroying the hurdles”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. tāḷa tāmarait tada maṇi vayal tirumōgūr nāḷum mēvi nangamarndu ninṟu asurarait tagarkkum tōḷum nāngudaic curi kuḻal kamalak kaṇ kani vāy kāḷamēgattai anṟi maṟṟonṟilam gadiyē*

- *tāḷa tāmarai* – Lotus where the stem is carrying the greatness of the flower with great difficulty as if carrying a mountain. It is said in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 4.9.8 “*uram peṟṟa malark kamalam ulagaḷanda sēvadipōl uyarndu kātta*” (the strongly stemmed lotus appearing tall like emperumān’s divine feet which measured the world). Lotus which is having strong stem due to the nature of the mud.
- *tadam aṇi* – The pond appears to be decorated with such flowers; when recited as “*uram peṟṟa malark kamalam ulagaḷanda sēvadipōl uyarndu kātta*“, it implies that the strongly stemmed lotus, due to the nature of the mud, grew tall and blossomed, appearing like the divine feet which mercifully measured the world. \[For the fields\] When it is recited as “*varambuṟṟa …*“, it implies that the well stretched paddy crops resemble dēvas stretching their feet, bowing their head and offering obeisances to emperumān’s divine feet as said in śrīviṣṇu darmam “*sankaissurāṇām*” (When trivikrama measured the world with his foot, he was vorśipped by dēvas, humans and other celestial beings). tirumōgūr which is having such rich ponds and fields. The enjoyability of the town is seen in the fields.
- *nāḷum mēvi* – Having great desire everyday. Every dawn in that town, he feels as said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 5.17.3 “*suprabātā mē niśā*” (Today is a good day for me).
- *nangamarndu ninṟu* – He is standing there without considering any other goal than residing in this divya dēśam.
- *asurar …* – One who is having four divine shoulders which show that he can conduct himself well by winning over the demoniac persons and eliminate the hurdles. nampiḷḷai asked \[nanjīyar\] “How would āḻvār know this \[that emperumān can eliminate the enemies\]?” and nanjīyar mercifully answered “Though one may not have earring now, it can be seen that he was wearing them before, based on the scars”.
- *suri kuḻal* – emperumān’s hair will eliminate the long-term suffering one went through in this samsāram. As emperumān who is walking ahead,  gently sways his divine hair and as the one who follows looks at it, he will feel “*kēśava: klēśa nāśana:*” (the one with beautiful hair, will eliminate our sorrows).
- *kamalam* … – āḻvār is talking about the relief one gets after seeing the true glance and true smile, after having been tormented by the glance and smile of inferior entities \[since time immemorial\].
- *kāḷa mēgattai* – Just as water is sprinkled on the path which is taken by the kings, as kāḷamēgam emperumān walks ahead sprinkling the nectar of his beauty, one can follow him, enjoying such coolness.
- *anṟi maṟṟu onṟu ilam gadiyē* – There is no companion other than kāḷamēgam for our journey.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 10.1.2. Ilam gadi

*ilam gadi maṟṟonṟu emmaikkum īn taṇ tuḻāyin alangalangaṇṇi āyiram pērudai ammān nalangoḷ nānmaṟai vāṇargaḷ vāḻ tirumōgūr nalangaḻal avanadi niḻal tadam anṟi yāmē*

**Пословный перевод:**

In – makes the flowers which are strung to become enjoyable; taṇ – cool; tuḻāyin – having tiruttuḻāy (tuḷasi); alangal – swaying; am – beautiful; kaṇṇi – one who is having garland; āyiram pērudai – having countless divine names which are enjoyable; ammān – being the unconditional lord; nalam koḷ – having distinguished qualities such as compassion; nānmaṟai – for the four vēdas; vāṇargaḷ – experts; vāḻ – having an enriched life due to enjoying his qualities such as being the protector etc; tirumōgūr – residing in tirumōgūr; nalam kaḻalavan – one who is having divine feet which are decorated with valorous anklets which can be used by him to reach us without discriminating between his devotees; adi niḻal – shade of his divine feet; tadam anṟi – other than the pond; yām – us; emmaikkum – in all births; gadi – as destination; maṟṟu onṟu – anything else; ilam – do not have

**Перевод:**

**kāḷamēgam emperumān is decorated with beautiful, swaying tiruttuḻāy garland which makes the flowers which are strung to become enjoyable, with its coolness; he is the unconditional lord having countless divine names which are enjoyable; he is residing in tirumōgūr where experts of four vēdas, who are having distinguished qualities such as compassion and are having an enriched life due to enjoying his qualities such as being the protector etc, are residing; in all births, we do not have any destination other than the shade of the pond; in other words, his divine feet which are decorated with valorous anklets which can be used by him to reach us without discriminating between his devotees.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the second pāsuram, āḻvār says “Forever, we have no refuge other than the rejuvenating divine feet of emperumān who has divine names which remove the fatigue of his devotees with his enjoyability and which uplift them”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. ilam gadi maṟṟonṟu emmaikkum In taṇ tuḻāyin alangalangaṇṇi āyiram pērudai ammān nalangoḷ nānmaṟai vāṇargaḷ vāḻ tirumōgūr nalangaḻal avanadi niḻal tadam anṟi yāmē*

- *ilam gadi maṟṟu onṟu emmaikkum* – (emmaikkum – maṟṟu onṟu – ilam gadi) This statement is not for just this birth, but for all my births. Forever, we will have no refuge other than his divine feet.
- *en …* – Beautiful garland which has the radiance of tuḷasi which has coolness and string of flowers.
- *alangal* – radiance, swaying; as one follows him, one will observe the swaying of the garland on his head, when he places his steps; the radiance is due to being on his divine form.
- *āyiram pērudai* – As one sets out to glorify him seeing his shoulders and the garland on the shoulders, he has countless divine names in his every aspect, just like one sees steps wherever one enters a river \[from the bank\] to have a bath .
- *ammān* – Instead of having to be involved in praising inapt entities just seeing their physical beauty \[he is the apt lord for us too\]. As said in [periya tiruvandādi 82](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/02/periya-thiruvandhadhi-82/) “*āḻiyangai ammānai ēttādu ayarttu* *– vāḷā irunduoḻindēn*” (I remained ignorant without praising [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who had in his beautiful hand, the signet ring, spending the time purposelessly), he is of the nature, that one needs to worry for the days spent without praising him.
- *nalam koḷ …* – The eternal abode of those who have understood the essence of vēdam as “*ānruśamysamē vēdārtam*” (the main purport of vēdam is compassion), who can take up the vyāsapadam (seat of vēda vyāsa). Mere residence in this town leads to enrichment in life. Due to residing here, īśvara too becomes firm on the principle of “protecting my devotees is my ultimate duty”. Those who say as in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 18.38 “*asmābhis tulyō bhavatu*” (you are equal to us) to those who come here to surrender unto emperumān.
- *nalam kaḻal avan* – The divine feet which do not discriminate between the noble qualities and faults of the devotees. Even if they \[devotees\] say as in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 17.27 “*vadyatām*” (he deserves to be killed), being blinded by love, he will say as in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 18.8 “*natyajēyam*” (I will never abandon).
- *avan adi niḻal tadam anṟi yāmē* – *avan* (he/his) is read in both sections (previous as well as here). Other than the shade of his divine feet, which is the pond, we have no other gati (destination).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 10.1.3. Anri yam

*anṟi yām orui pugalidam ilam enṟenṟalaṟṟi ninṟu nānmugan aranodu dēvargaḷ nāda venṟu immūvulagaḷittu uḻalvān tirumōgūr nanṟu nām ini naṇugudum namadidar kedavē*

**Пословный перевод:**

anṟi – other than you; yām – we; oru pugalidam – another refuge; ilam – do not have; enṟu enṟu alaṟṟi – calling out many times while becoming weak every time; ninṟu – standing (until result is attained); nānmugan aranodu – with brahmā and rudra; dēvargaḷ – celestial beings; nāda – as \[they\] seek and approach; venṟu – winning over the enemies; immūvalagu – this three layered universe; aḷittu uḻalvān – one who has such protection \[of everyone\] as his routine; tirumōgūr – tirumōgūr; nām – we; namadu – our; idar keda – to eliminate the mental stress (of seeking a companion for the final journey); ini – after (the presence of the protector); nanṟu – being ananya prayōjanar (one who is without any expectation); naṇugudum – will reach him

**Перевод:**

**Calling out many times “Other than you, we do not have any other refuge” while becoming weak every time, as the celestial beings stand along with brahmā and rudra, seek emperumān and approach him, let us reach tirumōgūr which is the abode of the one who wins over his enemies in this three layered universe and who has such protection \[of everyone\] as his routine, to eliminate our mental stress; being ananyaprayōjanar, we will reach him.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the third pāsuram, āḻvār says “Let us reach tirumōgūr where sarvēśvara who is having all auspicious qualities dwells, to have all our sorrows eliminated; this is good advice”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. anṟi yām orui pugalidam ilam enṟenṟalaṟṟi ninṟu nānmugan aranodu dēvargaḷ nāda venṟu immūvulagaḷittu uḻalvān tirumōgūr nanṟu nām ini naṇugudum namadidar kedavē*

- *anṟi …* – Even prayōjanāntarapara (those who expect benefits other than kainkaryam) are speaking the words of ananyaprayōjana, to have his presence. Forever calling out incoherently saying “Other than your highness, we have no refuge”.
- *ninṟu* – Remaining put there, until they accomplish the task just as the ananyaprayōjanas would do.
- *nānmugan …* – caturmuka (four-headed) brahmā, rudra and all the celestial beings approach him.
- *venṟu …* – This is the abode of the one who has as his main routine, protecting \[the surrendered ones\] from their enemies, protecting this three-layered universe which is meant for them.
- *nanṟu nām ini naṇgudum* – (ini nām nanṟu naṇugudum (now, we will approach him well)) – as he is the protector of all, we, who have desire to be protected, should approach him well. We will approach him as ananyaprayōjana unlike kālayavana, jarāsanda et al who approached kriṣṇa in śrī maturā and unlike brahmā et al who approached kśīrābdi (milk ocean) as said in tiruviruttam 92 “*nīṇagar nīḷeri vaittaruḷāy*” (Please burn down the great town of lankā).
- *namadu idar kedavē* – The sorrow of us who are as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 5.1.9](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/05/thiruvaimozhi-5-1-9-avarar-thunai/) “*āvār Ar tuṇai*” (who will be my companion?).

## 10.1.4. Idar keda

*idar keda emmaip pōndaḷiyāy enṟenṟēttic cudar koḷ sōdiyait tēvarum munivarum todarap padar koḷ pāmbaṇaip paḷḷi koḷvān tirumōgūr idar keda adi paravudum toṇḍīr! vamminē*

**Пословный перевод:**

idar keda – “to have the sorrows caused by enemies, eliminated; pōndu – mercifully arriving here; emmai – us; aḷiyāy – protect us”; enṟu enṟu – saying repeatedly revealing the weakness; ētti – praising him; sudar koḷ – having great radiance; sōdiyai – very luminous divine form; dēvarum – dēvas who consider themselves to be lords; munivarum – sages (who perform penance as seekers of wealth); todara – to follow and surrender; padar koḷ – having expansion due to being in contact with him; pāmbu aṇai – on the divine serpent mattress which has softness, coolness, fragrance fitting the nature of the serpent species; paḷḷi koḷvān – one who is mercifully reclining, his; tirumōgūr – in tirumōgūr; idar – (our) sorrows which are impossible to be removed; keda – to rid of; toṇḍīr – Oh you who have desire to surrender unto him; adi – his divine feet; paravudum – let us praise; vammin – please do come!

**Перевод:**

**emperumān who is having greatly radiant luminous form, who is mercifully reclining on the divine serpent mattress which has softness, coolness, fragrance fitting the nature of the serpent species, which is having expansion due to being in contact with him, is followed, surrendered and repeatedly praised by dēvas who consider themselves to be lords and sages, by saying “Protect us by arriving here to eliminate all the sorrows caused by enemies”. Such emperumān is in tirumōgūr now. Please do come! Oh you who have desire to surrender unto him! Let us praise his divine feet.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fourth pāsuram, āḻvār is inviting śrīvaiṣṇavas saying “Come, let us surrender unto emperumān in tirumōgūr to have all our sorrows eliminated”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. idar keda emmaip pōndaḷiyāy enṟenṟēttic cudar koḷ sōdiyait tēvarum munivarum todarap padar koḷ pāmbaṇaip paḷḷi koḷvān tirumōgūr idar keda adi paravudum toṇḍīr! vamminē*

- *idar keda …* – The words of those who consider themselves as lords (dēvas) and sages who can both inflict their curse and bestow blessing are as in “*emmai idar keda pōndu aḷiyāy*” (bless us to have our sorrows eliminated). To have the sorrows mentioned in [stōtra ratnam 13](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/12/sthothra-rathnam-13/) “*vēdāpahāra …*” (stealing of vēdas), to be eliminated.
- *emmai* – Those who previously considered themselves to be, as said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 16-14](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/16-14/) ‘*īśvarōham’* (I am the controller), when afflicted with dangers, will present their emptiness as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 6.16 “*ēhi paśya śarīrāṇi*” (Look at our bodies).
- *pōndu aḷiyāy* – They (āḻvārs) will tell him that he should descend and protect them. Those \[dēvas\] who were previously ignoring, when met with danger, will ask him “why are you resting, while we are suffering here?” just as one would question the village chief.
- *enṟu enṟu ētti todara* –  To continuously praise him and forcefully surrender unto him due to their dangerous situation.
- *sudar koḷ sōdiyai* – emperumān is appearing radiant thinking “at least, they come to me when they are in danger”. Another explanation – due to his distinguished beauty, he should be pursued for his beauty alone, but he is only considered as the eliminator of hurdles.
- *dēvarum munivarum todara* – dēvas and riśis. Those who remain “*īśvarōham*” and those who pursue wealth.
- *padar koḷ pāmbaṇaip paḷḷi koḷvān* – One who accepts the service of ananyaprayōjanars (those who expect nothing but kainkaryam) is mercifully resting in kśīrābdi (milky ocean) for the sake of prayōjanāntaraparars (those who seek other benefits)!
- *padar koḷ pāmbu* – tiruvanantāḻvān (ādiśēśa) who expands by the touch of emperumān.
- *paḷḷi koḷvān* – tiruvanantāḻvān is capable of making the sarvajña (omniscient lord) becoming captivated by sleep due to coming in contact with him.
- *tirumōgūr* – He mercifully stood in tirumōgūr to be easily approachable for us as well just as he remained easily approachable for dēvas (in kśīrābdi).
- *idar keda adi paravudum* – Let us surrender unto his divine feet to have all our sorrows eliminated.
- *toṇḍīr vamminē* – All those who are sagōtris (sharing the same gōtram of prapanna kulam (the clan of servitors)) should gather around.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 10.1.5. Tondir! vammin

*toṇḍīr! vammin nam sudaroḷi oru tani mudalvan aṇḍamūvulagaḷandavan aṇi tirumōgūr eṇḍhisaiyum īn karumbodu perunjennel viḷaiyak koṇḍa kōyilai valanjeydu ingu ādudum kūttē*

**Пословный перевод:**

nam – being enjoyable for us; sudar – having endless radiance; oḷi – having luminous divine form; oru tani mudalvan – being the three types of causes viz nimitta (efficient), upādāna (material) and sahakāri (ancillary) kāraṇa (causes) himself; aṇḍam – present inside the created oval shaped universe; mū ulagu – three layers of worlds; aḷandavan – one who measured and accepted; aṇi – beautiful; tirumōgūr – in tirumōgūr; eṇ disaiyum – in all directions; In – sweet; karumbodu – with sugarcane; perum sennel – tall and reddish paddy; viḷaiya – to flourish; koṇḍa – accepted; kōyilai – temple; ingu – in this world; valam seydu – circumambulating; kūttādudum – out of overwhelming love, we will dance; toṇḍīr – Oh you who are desirous!; vammin – Come!

**Перевод:**

**Oh you who are desirous! Come! emperumān who is enjoyable for us, who is having endlessly radiant luminous divine form, who is himself the three types of causes viz efficient cause, material cause and ancillary cause, who measured and accepted the three layers of worlds which are present in the created oval shaped universe, has accepted the temple in tirumōgūr as his abode, which has flourishing sweet sugarcane and tall and reddish paddy in all directions. In this world itself, let us circumambulate such temple and dance out of overwhelming love.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fifth pāsuram, āḻvār says “Come to surrender unto tirumōgūr where emperumān has mercifully arrived and stood”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. toṇḍīr! vammin nam sudaroḷi oru tani mudalvan aṇḍamūvulagaḷandavan aṇi tirumōgūr eṇḍhisaiyum In karumbodu perunjennel viḷaiyak koṇḍa kōyilai valanjeydu ingu ādudum kūttē*

- *toṇḍīr vammin* – Oh those who are desirous in bhagavat viśayam! Come!
- *nam sudar oḷi oru tani mudalvan* –  One who is endlessly radiant and who is himself the three types of causes. “nam” indicates the well-known nature of the pramāṇam (source of knowledge). Alternatively it indicates that he is the one who revealed his physical beauty and his aptness due to being the cause.
- *aṇḍam mū ulagaḷandavan* – One who is beyond the oval-shaped universe. One who measured and accepted the three kinds of worlds inside the universe which were stolen by mahābali. Not only does he create the universe, but he also protects it by walking all the way when the created universe is claimed by strong persons.
- *aṇi tirumōgūr* – The abode which is a decoration for him; or, the abode which is a decoration for the material realm.
- *eṇ disaiyum …* – To have sweet sugarcane and paddy crops growing in all directions.
- *koṇḍa kōyil* – The abode which was accepted by him in his divine heart. The paddy crop appears to be giving shade for the sugarcane \[it is that tall\]. Due to his presence, the town remained as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 127.19 “*akāla palinō vrukśā:*” (the trees blossomed in non-season).
- *valam seydu* – circumambulating etc.
- *ingu ādudum kūttē* – We will enjoy at tirumōgūr, the same enjoyment which will be enjoyed there in paramapadam as said in taittirīya upaniśat “*ahamannam ahamannam ahamannam:*” (I am the food and I am the consumer of food\[repeated thrice\] – residents of parampadam are enjoyed by emperumān and they in turn enjoy emperumān).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 10.1.6. Kuttan kovalan

*kūttan kōvalan kudaṟṟu vallasurargaḷ kūṟṟamēttum nangatkum amararkkum munivarkkum inbanvāytta taṇ paṇai vaḷa vayal sūḻ tirumōgūrāttan tāmarai adi anṟi maṟṟilam araṇē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kūttan – one who beautifully walks like an expert dancer; kōvalan – one who follows those who need protection, and protects them; kudaṟṟu – those tormentors who can torture by biting; val – very strong; asurargaḷ – for demoniac persons such as kēśi, dēnuka et al; kūṟṟam – being death personified; ēttum – praising as ananyaprayōjana (those who seek nothing but kainkaryam); nangatkum – for us (who have no pride); amararkkum – for nityasūris who eternally enjoy him; munivarkkum – for sages; inban – being enjoyable; vāytta – abundant; taṇ – cool; paṇai – by water bodies; vaḷa vayal – and by beautiful fields; sūḻ – surrounded; tirumōgūr – in tirumōgūr; āttan – the most trustworthy emperumān who is standing there for the devotees to surrender; tāmarai adi anṟi – other than the ultimately enjoyable lotus like divine feet; maṟṟu araṇ ilam – we have no other protection

**Перевод:**

**emperumān beautifully walks like an expert dancer; follows those who need protection, and protects them; he is death personified for very strong, demoniac persons such as kēśi, dēnuka et al who are tormentors who can torture by biting; he is enjoyable for us who praise him without any expectation other than kainkaryam, for nityasūris who eternally enjoy him and for sages. We have no other protection than the ultimately enjoyable lotus like divine feet of the most trustworthy emperumān who is standing for the devotees to surrender, who is residing in tirumōgūr which is surrounded by abundantly cool vaterbodies and beautiful fields.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the sixth pāsuram, āḻvār says “There is no protection for us other than the divine feet of the most trustworthy emperumān who is mercifully standing in tirumōgūr”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. kūttan kōvalan kudaṟṟu vallasurargaḷ kūṟṟamēttum nangatkum amararkkum munivarkkum inbanvāytta taṇ paṇai vaḷa vayal sūḻ tirumōgūrāttan tāmarai adi anṟi maṟṟilam araṇē*

- kūttan – When he starts walking, it will resemble the dance of an expert dancer. As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 11.1 “*agrata: prayayau rāma:*” (śrī rāma walks first), when he walks, it will be apt to hold an umbrella for him. Following him when he vallks in the front would mean watching a dance while going. It is said in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi “*ādal pādal avai māṟinar tāmē*” (Dancers and singers gave up their dance and song) – when he played his divine flute, the apsaras (celestial dancers) stopped singing on hearing that; they stopped dancing when they saw his beautiful walk.
- *kōvalan* – One who degrades himself to protect his devotees. He led a piśāśa \[gaṇṭākarṇan\] to paramapadam, being the grantor of liberation.
- *kudaṟṟu val asurargaḷ kūṟṟam* – He is death personified for very prideful demons who torment others.
- *ēttum …* – One who is \[equally\] enjoyable for us who surrender unto him today and to those who are eternally surrendered to him as said in “*vaigundattamararum munivarum*” (those who are amarar (engaged in kainkaryam) and munivar (engaged in meditation)).
- *vāytta …* – The ultimate relative who is mercifully standing in tirumōgūr which has beautiful water bodies and fertile fields. The most trustworthy emperumān who says in varāha carama ślōkam “*aham smarāmi math bhaktam nayāmi*” (I will remember my devotee and liberate him) for those who are unconscious during their last moments, under whom one can place one’s burden and remain free, when one is in danger.
- *tāmarai adi anṟi* – His divine feet are so enjoyable that they cannot be ignored even if he is untrustworthy.
- *maṟṟilam araṇē* – We have no other persons as our protection. We have no other refuge even if he is not enjoyable.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 10.1.7. Marrilam aran

*maṟṟilam arān vān perum pāḻ tani mudalā suṟṟum nīr padaittu adan vaḻit tol muni mudalā muṟṟum dēvarōdu ulagu seyvān tirumōgūr suṟṟi nām valam seyya nam tuyar kedum kadidē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tani – having uniqueness (of not being created etc as said in “ajāmēkām“); vān – having ultimate greatness (to have all the effects in a fraction of himself); peru – having the ability to create all effects; pāḻ mudalā – starting with prakruti (primordial matter); suṟṟum – pervading everywhere; nīr – causal water; padaittu – creating; adan vaḻi – through that; tol – being ancient (since he is existing prior to the creation of the worlds inside the oval shaped universe); muni mudalā – brahmā who contemplates the creation process and others; muṟṟum dēvarōdu – with all dēvatās; muṟum ulagu – the whole material realm; seyvān – one who creates, his; tirumōgūr – tirumōgūr; suṟṟi valam nām seyya – as we (joyfully) perform favourable acts such as circumambulation etc; nam – our; tuyar – suffering due to the loneliness; kadidu – immediately; kedum – will go; maṟṟu araṇ ilam – we don’t have any other protection

**Перевод:**

**emperumān is having uniqueness, ultimate greatness and the ability to create all effects in the whole material realm, creates everything starting with primordial matter, the all-pervading causal water, and creates the ancient brahmā who contemplates the creation process, and others including dēvatās; as we perform favourable acts such as circumambulation etc in his tirumōgūr, our suffering due to the loneliness will immediately go. Hence, we don’t have any other protection.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the seventh pāsuram, āḻvār says “As we approach tirumōgur which is the abode of emperumān who is the cause of all and hence cannot avoid protecting us, all our sorrows will be immediately eliminated”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. maṟṟilam arān vān perum pāḻ tani mudalā suṟṟum nīr padaittu adan vaḻit tol muni mudalā muṟṟum dēvarōdu ulagu seyvān tirumōgūr suṟṟi nām valam seyya nam tuyar kedum kadidē*

- *maṟṟilam araṇ* – We don’t have any other refuge.  When asked “can he protect us?” āḻvār says “this is his nature” in the remaining portion of the pāsuram.
- *vān …* – Starting with the distinguished mūla prakruti (primordial matter) which remains strong even if all the material entities which are the effects, get annihilated.
- *suṟṟu nīr padaittu* – As said in manu smruti “*apa Eva sasarjātau*“ (first, he created water), creating the causal water which surrounds everything.
- *adan vaḻit tol muni mudalā* – Through that, creating dēvatās starting with caturmuka (four-headed) brahmā who is ancient and who engages in contemplation.
- *muṟṟum dēvarōdu ulagu sevyān tirumōgūr* – tirumōgūr, the abode of emperumān who creates all celestial species and all worlds.
- *suṟṟi nām valam seyya* – As we reach there and engage in circumambulation etc.
- *nam tuyar kedum kadidē* – Our sorrow of thinking that we have no companion in our \[final\] journey will immediately go. It is said in taittirīya upaniśat ānandavalli 6,7 “*atasō bhayam gatō bhavati*” (he will get rid of fear of samsāram); hence, there is no need for any other protection.

## 10.1.8. Tuyar kedum

*tuyar kedum kadidadaindu vandu adiyavar! toḻumin uyar koḷ sōlai oṇ tada maṇi oḷi tirumōgūr peyargaḷ āyiram udaiya vallarakkar pukkaḻundat dayaradan peṟṟa maradaga maṇit tadattinaiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

uyar koḷ – tall; sōlai – gardens; oṇ – distinguished; tadam – ponds; aṇi – having as decoration; oḷi – shining due to that; tirumōgūr – in tirumōgūr; āyiram – countless; peyargaḷ udaiya – having honorary titles/names; val – very strong; arakkar – rākśasas; pukku aḻunda – to enter and drown; dayaradan peṟṟa – sired by daśarata; maradaga maṇi – having dark complexion like an emerald gem; tadattinai – pond; adiyavar – all of you who are as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam kiśkindā kāṇḍam 4.12 “guṇairdāsyam upāgata:” (I am serving him, being overwhelmed by his qualities says lakśmaṇa about śrī rāma); vandu adaindu – reaching here; toḻumin – worship him; tuyar – your sorrows, without your effort; kadidu – immediately; kedum – will be destroyed

**Перевод:**

**emperumān, who is in tirumōgūr which has tall gardens and distinguished ponds as decoration and is shining due to that, who was sired by daśarata, is like a pond having complexion of emerald gem, to drown the very strong rākśasas who are having countless honorary titles/names; all of you who are as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam kiśkindā kāṇḍam 4.12 “guṇairdāsyam upāgata:”, reach here and worship him. Your sorrows, will be immediately destroyed, without your effort. The example of maradaga gem which eliminates poison and is also an ornament, implies emperumān being the eliminator of enemies and being the refuge for devotees.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the eighth pāsuram, āḻvār says “As we surrender unto the masculine son of daśarata, who is mercifully standing in tirumōgūr, all our sorrows will go”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. tuyar kedum kadidadaindu vandu adiyavar! toḻumin uyar koḷ sōlai oṇ tada maṇi oḷi tirumōgūr peyargaḷ āyiram udaiya vallarakkar pukkaḻundat dayaradan peṟṟa maradaga maṇit tadattinaiyē*

- *tuyar kedum kadidu* – Our sorrows will immediately go away, even we don’t desire for that.
- *adaindu vandu* – vandu adaindu – coming here and reaching.
- *adiyavar toḻumin* – You who are suffering thinking that there is no companion for the \[final\] journey, please take shelter and worship him.
- *uyar …* – tirumōgūr which has the shine based on the decoration of tall gardens and beautiful ponds. When we see the garden, it will remind us of his beautiful form. When we see the ponds, it will remind us of how he eliminates our fatigue. He is said to be coming \[walking\] like a fragrant pond as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 8.5.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/03/thiruvaimozhi-8-5-1-mayak-kuththa/) “*vāsat tadam pōl varuvān*“.
- *peyargaḷ āyiram udaiya* – Just as īśvara acquired many names by protecting others, these rākśasas acquired many names by harming others; “yajñaśatru” (enemy of fire sacrifice), “brahmaśatru” (enemy of brāhmaṇa) etc are some of their names.
- *val arakkar pukku aḻunda* – To drown the greatly prideful rākśasas.
- *dayaradan …* – Reach and surrender unto the son of daśarata cakravarty, who is like a pond which resembles blue gem. emperumān protects the favourable ones as said in “*badi taru maru vāpī vārivat sarva bhōjñam*” (one who is pleasing to the trees enroute, water in dry lands and all) and destroys the unfavourable ones as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 14.20 “*kākutsta pātālamukē patansa:*” (rāvaṇa who enters into the fire of śrī rāma). īsn’t he the one who guides even a bird \[to mōkśam\] as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 68.30 “*mayātvam samanujñātō gacca lōkān anuttamān*” (With my permission, you shall reach the highest abode).

## 10.1.9. Manittadattadi

*maṇittadattadi malark kaṇgaḷ pavaḷac cevvāy aṇikkoḷ nāl tadandōḷ deyvam asurarai enṟum tuṇikkum vallarattan uṟai poḻil tirumōgūr naṇittu nammudai nallaraṇ nām adaindanamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

maṇit tadattu – (cool) like a clean pond; adi – divine feet; malar – like a blossomed lotus flower; kaṇgaḷ – divine eyes; pavaḷam sevvāy – one who is having reddish coral like divine lips; aṇikkoḷ – deserving to be decorated with all ornaments; nāl – four kinds of; tadam – huge; tōḷ – one who is having divine shoulders; deyvam – one who is having a divine form; asurarai – demoniac persons; enṟum – at all times; tuṇikkum – severs; val arattan – very prideful, strong one; uṟai – eternal abode; poḻil – having (enjoyable) garden; tirumōgūr – tirumōgūr; nammudai – our; nal araṇ – abode of distinguished protection; naṇittu – is in very close proximity; nām – we (who are alone in seeking companion); adaindanam – we have reached

**Перевод:**

**kāḷamēgam emperumān is having a divine form with clean pond like divine feet, blossomed lotus flower like divine eyes, reddish coral like divine lips and is having four huge, divine shoulders which deserve to be decorated with all ornaments. He, who is a very prideful, strong and always severs the demoniac persons, is having tirumōgūr which is having enjoyable garden, as his eternal abode, Such tirumōgūr, which is our abode of distinguished protection is in very close proximity; we have reached here.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the ninth pāsuram, āḻvār speaks about his own benefit of reaching tirumōgūr which is his protection.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. maṇittadattadi malark kaṇgaḷ pavaḷac cevvāy aṇikkoḷ nāl tadandōḷ deyvam asurarai enṟum tuṇikkum vallarattan uṟai poḻil tirumōgūr naṇittu nammudai nallaraṇ nām adaindanamē*

- *maṇit tadattu adi* – His divine feet resemble a clean pond. Rejuvenating divine feet.
- *malark kaṇgaḷ* – The divine eyes resemble a flower blossomed in such pond.
- *pavaḷac cevvāy* – The celestial lord who has coral like reddish divine lips and four huge divine shoulders which appear like their own ornaments. When we travel along with him in his company, his rejuvenating form, his smile, glance etc which reveal his joy, his divine shoulders, which give shade, where we can take shelter and remain fearlessly as if we are inside a stone fort. He always travels with the desire for victory; he will always be having his hand in the weapon thinking “what hurdle we may face enroute?”
- *asurarai enṟum tuṇikkum val arattan* – Very prideful/strong person who always severs the demoniac persons.
- *uṟai poḻil tirumōgūr* – tirumōgūr, the abode which has garden and where he eternally resides. Just as saying “The den where the lion dwells”.
- *naṇittu* – We have reached – it is very close.
- *nammudai nal araṇ* – The abode which gives us protection.
- *nām adaindanamē* – We, who are seeking protection, have reached.

## 10.1.10. Nam adainda

*nām adainda nal araṇ namakkenṟu nallamarar tīmai seyyum vallasurarai anjic cenṟadaindāl kāma rūpangoṇḍu eḻundaḷippān tirumōgūr nāmamē navinṟu eṇṇumin ēttumin namargāḷ!*

**Пословный перевод:**

“namakku – exclusively for us; nām adainda – one we surrendered unto; nal araṇ – distinguished protection”; enṟu – considering this way; nal amarar – dēvas (celestial beings) who know the noble aspects; tīmai seyyum – those who engage in evil deeds; val – very strong; asurarai – towards the asuras (demoniac persons); anjic cenṟu adaindāl – when taken shelter, out of fear; kāma rūpam koṇḍu – assuming apt, desirable form; eḻundu – tumultuously; aḷippān – one who protects; tirumōgūr – tirumōgūr’s; nāmamē – glorious fame; namargāḷ – all of you who are related to us; navinṟu – speak; eṇṇumin – and think; ēttumin – praise out of love

**Перевод:**

**When dēvas who know the noble aspects, become fearful of the very strong asuras who engage in evil deeds and take shelter of emperumān considering “he is our exclusive, distinguished protector whom we surrendered unto”, he tumultuously protects us assuming an apt, desirable form. Oh all of you who are related to us! Speak and think about the glorious fame of tirumōgūr which is such emperumān’s abode; praise it out of love. kāma rūpam also indicates emperumān’s feminine form in mōhini avatāram to give nectar to dēvas.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the tenth pāsuram, āḻvār says \[to people at large\] “Oh you who are related to me! Have attachment towards tirumōgūr where sarvarakśakan (protector of all) is mercifully residing, think about it and praise it”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. nām adainda nal araṇ namakkenṟu nallamarar tīmai seyyum vallasurarai anjic cenṟadaindāl kāma rūpangoṇḍu eḻundaḷippān tirumōgūr nāmamē navinṟu eṇṇumin ēttumin namargāḷ!*

- *nām adainda …* – The dēvas sing saying “Our good protection, which we have taken shelter unto”.
- *nal amarar* – āḻvār is praising them as “nal amarar” (good dēvas) since they know that he is the means when they are faced with dangerous situations. This is the distinguishing factor from the asuras \[asuras won’t depend on bhagavān ever\].
- *tīmai seyyum …* – When they fear for asuras who are always engaged in harming others, and surrender unto emperumān.
- *kāmam …* – tirumōgūr, which is the abode of emperumān who assumes a form which is apt for the protection.
- *nāmamē navinṟu* – Oh those who are related to me! Recite the name of the town, think about it and praise it, out of overwhelming love.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 10.1.11. Ettumin namargal

*ēttumin namargāḷ! enṟu tān kudamādu kūttanaik kurugūrc catakōpan kuṟṟēvalgaḷ vāytta āyirattuḷ ivai vaṇ tirumōgūrkku ītta pattivai ētta vallārkku idar kedumē*

**Пословный перевод:**

namargāḷ – those who are related to us; ēttumin enṟu – saying “praise me (revealing your bliss)”; tān kudamādu kūttanai – on the dancer, who danced with pots; kurugūr – leader of āḻvārtirunagari; satakōpan – nammāḻvār’s; kuṟṟēvalgaḷ – as confidential services; ivai – these (apt services for īśvara); vāytta – occurred; āyirattuḷ – among the thousand pāsurams; vaṇ tirumōgūrkku – for the distinguished tirumōgūr; ītta pattu ivai – submitted decad; ētta vallārkku – for those who can recite, out of love; idar kedumē – sorrow (of not having companion during the final journey) will be eliminated

**Перевод:**

**nammāḻvār, the leader of āḻvārtirunagari, presented the thousand pāsurams as confidential services to the dancer who said “Those who are related to us! Praise me” and danced with pots; among those, this decad is submitted to the distinguished tirumōgūr. For those who can recite this decad out of love, their sorrow will be eliminated.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the end, āḻvār says “For those who like this decad which is submitted to tirumōgūr, all their sorrows will be eliminated”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. ēttumin namargāḷ! enṟu tān kudamādu kūttanaik kurugūrc catakōpan kuṟṟēvalgaḷ vāytta āyirattuḷ ivai vaṇ tirumōgūrkku ītta pattivai ētta vallārkku idar kedumē*

- *ēttumin* – emperumān said “Those who enjoy my activities should see me and sing to fulfil the purpose of having a mouth” and danced for that purpose, with pots.
- *kurugūrc catakōpan kuṟṟēvalgaḷ* – āḻvār’s confidential service. Meditating upon his dance with pots, he engaged in service through speech.
- *vāytta āyirattuḷ ivai* – This decad occurred among the thousand pāsurams which are meant for sarvēśvaran.
- *vaṇ tirumōgūrkku ītta pattu* – The decad which is submitted to the most magnanimous tirumōgūr. As said in “*ratnahārīca pārtiva:*” (one who owns the most precious gemstone is the king), due to the sweetness in this decad, he offered it to tirumōgūr.
- *ivai ētta vallārkku idar kedum* – For those who can recite and practice this decad, at the time of death, kāḷamēgam emperumān will become the companion so that one need not worry thinking “I have no companion in this journey”.
