## 10.2 Kedum idaraya

## 10.2.1. Kedum idaraya

*kedum idarāya ellām kēsava enna nāḷum kodu vinai seyyum kūṟṟin tamargaḷum kuṟugagillār vida mudai aravil paḷḷi virumbinān surumbalaṟṟum tadamudai vayal anantapura nagar pugudum inṟē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kēsavā enna – as we just recite the name kēśava; idar āya ellām – all sorrows; kedum – will be eliminated and driven out (to unseen place); nāḷum – eternally; kodu vinai – cruel tortures; seyyum – doing; kūṟṟin tamargaḷum – servitors of yama (by the recital of the name of lotus-eyed lord as said in “itīrayanti“, as said in “tyaja pata dūratarēṇa“, as said in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi “kōlādi kuṟugappeṟā\[dē\]” (he cannot come close to where I rule) and in periya tirumoḻi 8.10 .8 “kaḷḷar pōl“); kuṟugagillār – will run away; vidam udai – having abundant poison; aravil – on the divine mattress; paḷḷi virumbinān – one who mercifully rests, manifesting his desire to be united with his devotees; surumbu – beetles which have drunk honey; alaṟṟum – making sounds in a disorderly manner; tadam – flower filled ponds; udai – having; vayal – having fields; anantapuranagar – tiruvanantapuram; inṟē – (without any further delay) today itself; pugudum – reach

**Перевод:**

**As said in “vaikuṇṭha nāma śravaṇam aśēśāga vināśanam“, as we recite the divine name of kriṣṇa who has excellent hair, all our sorrows will be eliminated and driven away; servitors of yama, who are eternally doing cruel tortures, will run away; emperumān is mercifully resting on the divine serpent mattress which is having abundant poison, in tiruvanantapuram which is having fields with flower filled ponds which has beetles which have drunk honey and are making sounds in a disorderly manner; let us reach there today itself.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the first pāsuram, āḻvār invites śrīvaiṣṇavas saying “All the hurdles in reaching tiruvanantapuram which is the destination, will be gone. Please come! Let us recite this divine name ‘kēśava’ which is pleasing to us and go there”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. kedum idarāya ellām kēsava enna nāḷum kodu vinai seyyum kūṟṟin tamargaḷum kuṟugagillār vida mudai aravil paḷḷi virumbinān surumbalaṟṟum tadamudai vayal anantapura nagar pugudum inṟē*

- *kedum idarāya ellām* – Anything which is known as sorrow will be eliminated. If one performs a yajña for twelve years as atonement for brahma hatyā (killing of a brāhmaṇa), the same person needs to perform another atonement for another sin; here \[while reciting the divine name, kēśava\] that is not required as said in viṣṇu darmam “*pāpēntanāgni:”* (He is like fire for the firewood of sins).

When asked “Would the atonement also be many?”, āḻvār says,

- *kēsavā enna* – As we speak about how he eliminated a particular enemy, anything known as enemies will be eliminated just as the whole clan of rākśasas got destroyed due to rāvaṇa’s unfavourable acts.
- *ellām* – All future and past sins will be destroyed as said in [tiruppāvai 5](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2014/12/thiruppavai-05-mayanai/) “*pōya piḻaiyum pugu taruvān ninṟanavum*” (past sins and future sins).
- *enna* – Just the recital is required since it will lead to the result fully; alternative explanation – – if we speak about his having excellent hair, our sorrows will be eliminated as said in mahābhāratam “*kēśava: klēśa nāśana:*“. Another explanation – he is the controller of brahmā and rudra; still the first explanation is most important.
- *nāḷum …* – Even those confidential servitors of yama who are engaged in cruel activities on a daily basis, will not come close. Even if they are yama’s servitors, can they come close to sarvēśvaran’s devotees? śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 8.7.13 “*svapuruśam abhivīkśya pāśahastam vadati yama kila tasya karṇa mūlē* I *parihara madusūdanapprapannān prabhur ahamanyanruṇām na vaiṣṇavānām*  īī” \[ślōkam is explained subsequently\]; śrīviṣṇu darmam “*tasya yajña varāhasya …*” (yama says “I repeatedly worship those who worship the greatly capable yajña varāha) – in this, did yama not say “*praṇāmam yēpi kurvanti*” (I repeatedly worship)? [nānmugan tiruvandādi 68](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/08/nanmugan-thiruvandhadhi-68/) “*iṟainjiyum sāduvarāyp pōdumingaḷ*” (yama said “praying to them, leave their presence softly”) – \[yama says\] When you see them, don’t just think that we have no control over them, instead, approach them, offer your prayers and service, and then leave! *svapuruśam* –  yama observes his servitor going with rope, spear and dog and thinks “bhāgavatas and others will all be present; what if he goes in front of bhāgavatas like this?” and speaks with anxiety. *svapuruśam* – as he is speaking to his confidential servitor, he is speaking about his own inferior nature instead of speaking about his own greatness, as it is unavoidable now. *abhivīkśya* – he has only some control over the situation \[as given by bhagavān\]; before starting to instruct his servitor, he lovingly glances at him. *madusūdana prapannān* – When the servitor asks “what is the problem for bhagavān, if we torment this bhāgavata?”; \[yama says\] these bhāgavatas have placed their responsibilities upon him; if something happens to them, he will come forward, beating his chest. The servitor asks “For us, who are your servitors, if we need to fear for someone else, who are you to command us?” \[yama says\] *prabhur aham anya nruṇām* – Will there not be shortcoming in me, only if I don’t have a say under those who are under my control? Should we analyse the aspect in which we have no control? \[yama is saying that he has control over everyone other than bhāgavatas\] The same incident is explained by tirumaḻisaip pirān as well in [nānmugan tiruvandādi 68](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/08/nanmugan-thiruvandhadhi-68/) “*tiṟambēnmin* …”. [mudal tiruvandādi 55](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/08/mudhal-thiruvandhadhi-55/) “*avan tamar evvinaiyar…*” (Even the most sinful persons, if they are devotees of bhagavān, will not be checked by the servitors of yama). These are the messages which they \[yama and his servitors\] discuss among themselves. [tiruccanda viruttam 116](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2024/03/thiruchchandha-viruththam-116/) “*māṟu seyda …*” (If śrī rāma who destroyed lankā for the sake of sītāp pirātti does not abandon me, can yama check my historical sins and punish me?) Does he have the ability to check the servitors of śrī rāma, the son of emperor daśarata. \[An incident from the life of parāśara bhattar is explained\] During an utsavam, bhattar was with a great assembly of śrīvaiṣṇavas. Some śrīvaiṣṇavas come and inform him “It is time for sandyāvandanam”. bhattar responded “We are immersed in the divine beauty of perumāḷ; if we delay our duty a little bit, can yama consider this as a mistake and question us? When a king is listening to the accounts and balances of various people, and if the name of a close confidante of the king is read out, the king would say ‘Alright! Skip that name and read further’ and thereafter that close confidante’s name will never be read out”; in this context, tirumangai āḻvār mercifully said in periya tirumoḻi 6.3.9 “*unakkāgit toṇḍu patta nallēnai vinaigaḷ naliyāmai nambu nambī*” (Oh perfect lord! Ensure that I who am fully existing for you and serving you, am not bothered by my sins). periya tirumoḻi 8.10 .8 “*vaḷḷalē un tamarkku enṟum naman tamar kaḷḷar pōl*” (Oh generous lord! For your devotees, the servitors of yama are like lowly beings) – both of them \[i.e., your devotees and yama’s servitors\] cannot travel in the same route. periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 5.4.4 ‘*kodumai seyyum …*‘ (yama who gives out cruel punishments cannot enter where I rule) – when asked “What if yama’s servitors happen to cross the path of your devotees?” – as said in same pāsuram “*tadavarait tōḷ cakkara pāṇī sārngavil sēvaganē*” (Oh one who has vast mountain like shoulders, divine chakra in the hand and the valorous one with śārnga bow), he will send his divine chakra and remove the shoulder, shoot an arrow to knock down the head and so on. They will go through the same fate as bāṇāsura and rāvaṇa. periya tirumoḻi 10.6.5 “*vēṇḍāmai naman tamarai en tamar vinavap peṟuvār alar enṟu ulagēḻāṇḍān*” (He protected the worlds, to highlight that yama’s servitors cannot question his devotees, since it was his own wish) – yama’s servitors cannot question my devotees. What is the reason for that? vēṇḍāmai – he himself wished that it does not happen. Can a general clerk enter the private quarters of the king and assess the situation there? emperumān who says as in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 4.9.2 “*seydārēl nanṟu seydār*” (even if they commit mistakes, it was done for good purpose), will not lead his devotees to yama’s servitors. [tirumālai 1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/07/thirumalai-1-part-1/) “*nin nāmam kaṟṟa āvalippudaimai – naman tamar talaigaḷ mīdē – nāvalittuḻitaruginṟōm*” (with victorious war-cry, we walk on the heads of yama and his servitors, due to the pride of learning your divine names). As said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 8.7.14 “*prabavati samyamanē”* (he can punish me too) – he who is controlling me, is unlike me who can control \[just\] you; I can only assess someone when they are present in front of me; but he is present everywhere.
- *nāḷum kodu vinai seyyum kūṟṟin tamargaḷum kuṟugagillār* – Can they approach me due to being used to torment me previously, even after I have taken my first step towards bhagavān?
- *kuṟugagillār* – mahābhāratam “*nirdōśam viddi tam*” (he should be thought as defectless) – even if we took birth and died, having accomplished nothing, and even if he has committed unpardonable sins; still he should be thought as defectless only. When there are defects, why should we consider in this manner? *prabhāvāt* – Should we see him? \[No\] Should we not see whom he has surrendered unto? \[Yes\] If we analyse him, that means, we are limiting bhagavān’s mercy.
- *killār* – Is there anyone who goes near burning fire? It is not that they wont approach him based on the orders of bhagavān, the controller; but would one not want to save oneself?
- *vidam udai …* – Now prāpyam (attainable goal) is explained further.
- *vidam udai* – Like a thorn fence for tender coconut, no one can get close to him; as said in [mūnṟām tiruvandādi 66](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/05/munram-thiruvandhadhi-66/) “*vāynda madu kaidabarum vayiṟurugi māṇḍār*” ( those demons madu and kaitabha who came there got killed by having their bowels rotting), the enemies will be finished.
- *aravu* – It would have softness, coolness, fragrance etc matching the serpent species.
- *paḷḷi virumbinān* – He is mercifully resting there as explained in paryanka vidyā \[Explained in detail in [tiruvāimoḻi 2.8](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/05/thiruvaimozhi-2-8-anaivadhu/) “*aṇaivadu aravaṇai mēl*” decad\]. As said in “*tamēmvamvit pādēnādyārōhati*” (knowing him thus, he sets foot on ādiśēśa and climbs there) – one can climb on the serpent bed, by stepping on it.
- *surumbu alaṟṟum* – The beetles will do what is done by muktas as said in taittirīya upaniśat “*ētat sāma gāyannāstē*” (The liberated soul is singing sāma gānam).
- *tadam udai vayal* – The ponds will resemble virajā river and other divine water bodies.
- *anantapura nagar* – This abode resembles kalangāp peru nagaram (the unshakable great abode – paramapadam).
- *pugudum inṟē* – It is not possible to remain peaceful thinking “let us reach there in due course”; let us go and reach there today itself, when we have acquired the desire.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 10.2.2. Inru poy

*inṟu pōyp pugudirāgil eḻumaiyum ēdam sārā kunṟu nēr māda mādē kurundu sēr serundi punnai manṟalar poḻil anantapura nagar māyan nāmam onṟum ōrāyiramām uḷḷuvār umbar ūrē*

**Пословный перевод:**

inṟu – without any delay, on the same day when the desire is acquired; pōy – go; pugudir āgil – if you reach; eḻumaiyum – forever; ēdam – the defect of samsāra; sārā – will not affect; kunṟu nēr – like a mountain; mādam – mansions; mādē – in the proximity; kurundu sēr – with kurundu tree; serundi – serundi flower tree; punnai – punnai tree; manṟu – in the centre of the town; alar – blossoming; poḻil – being enjoyable, having garden; anantapura nagar – in the town of tiruvanantapuram; māyan – (having qualities such as saundarya (beauty), sauśeelya (simplicity), saulabhya (easy approacability) etc which are enjoyed by his devotees) the amazing lord’s; nāmam – the names which highlight such qualities; onṟum – any one of them; ōr – being distinguished; āyiram A – in thousand ways; uḷḷuvārkku – for those who determine; umbar Ur – paramapadam

**Перевод:**

**If you go without any delay on the same day when the desire is acquired, and reach tiruvanantapuram, the defect of samsāra will forever not affect you; in tiruvanantapuram, blossoming gardens are present in the centre of the town which has proximity of mountain like mansions, kurundu trees, along with serundi trees and punnai trees; for those who determine in thousand ways, any one of the names which highlight the qualities of the amazing lord in such tiruvanantapuram, that town itself is paramapadam. Implies that paramapadam can be given up. manṟu also implies manṟal (spreading), meaning the garden which spreads fragrance.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the second pāsuram, āḻvār says “Reciting a single divine name is sufficient to eliminate the hurdles;  that itself is a protection in thousand ways”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. inṟu pōyp pugudirāgil eḻumaiyum ēdam sārā kunṟu nēr māda mādē kurundu sēr serundi punnai manṟalar poḻil anantapura nagar māyan nāmam onṟum ōrāyiramām uḷḷuvār umbar ūrē*

- *inṟu pōy pugudirāgil* – If you go and reach there, today itself when you acquired the desire to go. “To become a qualified person, is it not required to have detachment towards worldly aspects etc? Is it enough to have the desire alone?” Yes. They are required for the matter \[bhakti yōgam etc\] where such qualifications are expected as said in jābāli smruti “*yadaharēva virajēt tadaharēva pravrajēt*” (one should accept sanyāsam as soon as one acquires vairājñam \[detachment\]); for that matter (emperumān related matter) which is common for all, which is apt, and which is already desiring for him and waiting for his desire, such desire alone is required; since he cannot earn the qualification matching emperumān’s greatness and emperumān as said in [nānmugan tiruvandādi 60](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/08/nanmugan-thiruvandhadhi-60/) “*āḷpārttuḻi taruvāy kaṇḍu*” (Oh! Lord you are in search of a person who has surrendered unto your divine feet), nothing else is required. He is of the nature to say as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 18.19 “*yadivā rāvaṇasvayam*” (even if it is rāvaṇa himself, bring him); \[śrī rāma says\] don’t come back empty handed, even if rāvaṇa had come carrying the name “vibhīśaṇa”. When asked “Why?” \[śrī rāma says\] Don’t think whether it is not enough if we accepted someone who came from lankā. Only those who have shortcomings are desired by us; that (shortcomings) is present in rāvaṇa. Since vibhīśaṇa has good qualities as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 17.23 “*vibhīśaṇastu darmātmā*’ (vibhīśaṇa is of noble character) , he can even come in the future; isn’t rāvaṇa the one who is in a dangerous situation where even if he delays a fraction of a moment, he will see disaster? Hence, should we not accept rāvaṇa first? Now, if we accept vibhīśaṇa, these four assistants will also benefit along with him; but if we accept rāvaṇa, we can accept the whole of rākśasa clan; just as we accepted sugrīva mahāraja, leading to the uplifting of the whole monkey clan.
- *eḻumaiyum ēdam sārā* – Calamities will never befall us.
- *sārā* – Even he need not specifically think about it. As said in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 5.4.3 “*summenādē kaivittōdum*” (will run away being unable to breathe), they will not come close thinking “this is not the abode for us”; due to our relationship with the royal clan \[of emperumān\], they will flee; [periiya tiruvandādi 54](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/01/periya-thiruvandhadhi-54/) “*vānō maṟikadalō* …” (After vorśipping the divine feet of kriṣṇa who killed vatsāsura and kapittāsura, I don’t know where my sins went. Did they hide in the sky? Did they dissolve in the ocean? Did they merge in the wind? Did they melt in the fire? Did they hide in the forest?)
- *kunṟu …* – The enjoyability of the wealth in the town is such that even if we are affected with the sufferings, we will desire to go there. The mansions which seem to be carved out of mountains, the kurundu, serundi and punnai trees which are in close proximity as if giving shade for the mansions; they are located close to each other.
- *manṟalar poḻil* – The gardens which are blossomed in the surroundings of the town. Alternatively, manṟu – manṟal which means fragrance, and alar means spreading, indicating the gardens where the fragrance is well spread.
- *kunṟu nēr mādam* – nanjīyar would mercifully say “I saw with reverence, piḷḷai tirunaṟaiyūr araiyar and bhattar entering \[the śrīrangam town with sapta prākāram – seven layers\] and circumambulating the same; others would do it quickly, but these two would see the divine palaces \[residences\] and divine towers as if drinking through their eyes; seeing that, I thought ‘while the act of circumambulation is the same for all, what a great distinction they have over others’ “.
- *sēr serundi* – It is as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 16.5 “*raghavōrhati vaidēhim*” (śrī rāma suits sītā pirātti in all aspects). Here āḻvār is talking about the plants/trees while subsequently he talks about nityasūris. In divyadēśams, due to all of them being desirable for emperumān, āḻvārs/ācāryas would think that there is no difference between distinguished personalities and plants/trees; for nityasūris, there is scope to go to paramapadam; while they will not think like that due to their great love towards divyadēśam out of knowledge; but they do have the ability to think like that; but, for these plants, they don’t even have that scope \[so, they are most fortunate to remain in divyadēśams forever\]. \[An incident is explained\] Think about embār’s merciful words when piḷḷai jananāta brahmarāyār was organizing a tree cutting event in śrīrangam \[This incident is explained in detail in [tiruvāimoḻi 5.9.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/09/thiruvaimozhi-5-9-1-maney-nokku/)\]. When āccān tiruvāli nādu dāsar gave some high quality betel nuts to bhattar, bhattar mercifully said “How are they looking so good? Did they grow in tiruvaruḷ kamugu (areca trees which received the divine mercy of emperumān)?” They were not grown with water but with his merciful glance.
- *anantapura nagar māyan* – His great simplicity of leaving śrīvaikuṇṭam and arriving here thinking “Let me give audience to lowly persons” and not leaving tiruvanantapuram, is spoken here.
- *nāmam onṟum ōr āyiramām* – It is said that even his single name will eliminate all the hurdles; in the same manner, one who has thousand divine names, which will protect in thousand ways.
- *uḷḷuvārkku* – Desirability is abundantly available; now, those who can meditate upon that are required.
- *uḷḷuvārkku* – Those who can meditate upon emperumān’s quality of simplicity in thinking “let me give audience to lowly persons” and residing here joyfully, while he, as sarvēśvaran, lives amidst nityasūris in śrīvaikuṇṭam.
- *umbar ūrē* – For those who meditate upon the divine names, their residence itself is paramapadam; alternatively – the abode which those who meditate upon the divine names attain is paramapadam. paramapadam is desirable due to his eternal presence there. Now, when one who has darmaikyam (being the same in paramapadam and tiruvanantapuram), is residing here, there is nothing wrong to say that this abode is desirable.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

adiyen saraty ramanuja dasan

## 10.2.3. Urum putkodiyum

*ūrum putkodiyum ahdē ulagellām uṇḍumiḻndān sērum taṇ anantapuram sikkenap pudirāgil tīrum nōy vinaigaḷ ellām tiṇṇam nām ariyac connōm pērum ōr āyirattuḷ onṟu nīr pēsuminē*

**Пословный перевод:**

puḷ – periya tiruvadi (garudāḻvār); ūrum – will ride; kodiyum – the flag hoisted for protecting; ahdē – is also that; ulagu ellām – whole world; uṇḍu – consumed (and protected by placing in the stomach); umiḻndān – spat it out after deluge; sērum – mercifully resting to give audience to those who are of subsequent times; taṇ – invigorating; anantapuram – tiruvanantapuram; sikkena – with firm faith in not expecting anything other than kainkaryam; pugudirāgil – if you reach; nōy – disease (of taste for worldly pleasures); vinaigaḷ ellam tīrum – all karmas (which are the root for such disease) will be eliminated; nām – we, who are experts in this principle; aṟiya – to know; tiṇṇam – firmly; sonnōm – told; pērum ōr āyirattuḷ – among his enjoyable thousand divine names; onṟu – anyone; nīr – you; pēsumin – recite

**Перевод:**

**emperumān will ride periya tiruvadi (garudāḻvār); the flag hoisted for protection is also the same garudāḻvār. emperumān consumed the whole world, spat it out after the deluge, and is mercifully resting to give audience to those who are of subsequent times in invigorating tiruvanantapuram. If you reach there with firm faith in not expecting anything other than kainkaryam, your diseases and all karmas will be eliminated. We, who are experts in this principle, have firmly told this for you to know. You can recite any one among his enjoyable thousand divine names. While all his names are enjoyable, no names are to be considered as primary or secondary.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the third pāsuram, āḻvār says “No particular divine name is required to eliminate the hurdles, anyone among the thousand is enough”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. ūrum putkodiyum ahdē ulagellām uṇḍumiḻndān sērum taṇ anantapuram sikkenap pudirāgil tīrum nōy vinaigaḷ ellām tiṇṇam nām ariyac connōm pērum ōr āyirattuḷ onṟu nīr pēsuminē*

- *ūrum puḷ* – He will ride periya tiruvadi, as his vehicle.
- *kodiyum ahdē* – This is a sample for nityasūris too. This is highlighted to show that the variegated forms/aspects acquired by those nityasūris who are untouched by samsāram as said in [mudal tiruvandādi 53](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/08/mudhal-thiruvandhadhi-53/) “*senṟāl kudaiyām*” (becomes umbrella when emperumān walks), will be applicable even for emperumān who reached tiruvanantapuram \[i.e., nityasūris will serve arcāvatāra emperumān also in the same way\]. Even if the servitor says as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 31.25 “*aham sarvam kariśyāmi*” (I will serve you both (perumāḷ and pirātti) in all the ways), there is no use, unless emperumān accepts it as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 31.22 “*kuruśva mām*” (lakhsmaṇa to śrī rāma – You should make me follow you). For the servitor, when he does not engage in small services, he cannot retain his svarūpam (true nature). emperumān who has no expectation, will take up an inferior position and eliminate the servitor’s shortcomings. He will remain an expectant (of the servitor’s service) and make the servitor become devoid of expectation. emperumān should remain devoid of any expectation and yet make the servitor retain his true nature. When he minimizes his own stature to have the servitor’s true nature established, that will help in retaining his non-expectant nature. Only after remaining as said in periya tirumoḻi 2.2.3 “*innār tūdan ena ninṟān evvuḷ kidandānē*” (He who stood there to be said as ‘he is the messenger of pāṇḍavas’ is now resting in tiruvevvuḷ”), his true nature (of being subservient towards his devotees) was established.
- *ulagu …* – Not only does he accept service from those who are untouched by samsāra, he also consumes the world during the danger of deluge, protects it by placing in his stomach and releases it subsequently by spitting it out so that it does not struggle inside.
- *sērum taṇ anantapuram* – During the danger of deluge, the world was in anxiety till it entered emperumān’s stomach; he had the same anxiety until he entered this divyadēśam; it is saying that this the abode where he, who protected us during the danger of delug,e has reached, or is saying that he is mercifully resting here without any worries.
- *taṇ anantapuram* –  It is not because of his bewilderment, he is desirous of this town; he cannot leave it due to its enjoyability. Since it is known as “*ugandaruḷina nilam*” (emperumān dwells there with great eagerness), should it not be like this? It is said in [tirunedundāṇḍagam 6](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/09/thirunedunthandakam-6-part-1/) “*tānuganda Ur*” (the abode which is dear to him). paramapadam is dear to both himself and nityasūris; here it is only his desire; even when they don’t manifest the same desire, he is eagerly waiting here.
- *sikkena* – As said in cāndōjña upaniśat 8.15 “*na ca punarāvartatē*” (there is no return), if you reach there with irreversible taste.
- *tīrum …* – The sorrows and their cause will be eliminated.
- *tiṇṇam* – As said in itihāsams/purāṇams “*satyam satyam punas satyam …*” (I declare the truth again and again).
- *nām aṟiyac connōm* – We who have seen it our ourselves, are firmly telling you who don’t understand the greatness, to not lose it.
- *nām* – āḻvār has suffered a lot previously and finally has seen the shore now.
- *sonnōm* – We have told so that we are not blamed for not informing; if they \[worldly people\], being bound, do not believe it and continue to suffer, let them do that.

You told that reaching tiruvantapuram is to be done. What do we recite after having reached there?

- *pērum ōr …* – We have already told that he is having thousand names where each of those names will protect in thousand ways; among those, you can recite any one of the names, which you like.
- *pēsuminē* – You don’t even need to do it with heart’s consent – just plain recital is enough.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 10.2.4. Pesumin kusaminri

*pēsumin kūsam inṟip periya nīr vēlai sūḻndu vāsamē kamaḻum sōlai vayal aṇi anantapuram nēsam seyduṟaiginṟānai neṟimaiyāl malargaḷ tūvip pūsanai seyginṟārgaḷ puṇṇiyam seydavāṟē*

**Пословный перевод:**

periya – abundant; nīr – having water; vēlai – by ocean; sūḻndu – surrounded; vāsamē kamaḻum – spreading the fragrance; sōlai – gardens; vayal – fields; aṇi – having as decoration; anantapuram – in tiruvanantapuram; nēsam seydu – showing ultimate vātsalyam (motherly love) (to manifest himself to the devotees); uṟaiginṟānai – one who is eternally residing; neṟimaiyāl – in proper means matching his being the lord; malargaḷ – tools such as flowers; tūvi – offering (being overwhelmed by love); pūsanai seyginṟārgaḷ – those who worship; puṇṇiyam – fortune; seyda āṟu – the way they got; kūsam inṟi – without seeing (your) disqualification and without feeling shy (seeing the overwhelming motherly love of those who worship the vatsalan (emperumān who is like a mother); pēsumin – try to praise

**Перевод:**

**emperumān is showing ultimate vātsalyam and eternally residing in tiruvanantapuram which is having fields and gardens spreading the fragrance, as decoration and is surrounded by ocean having abundant water; try to praise those who offer such emperumān in proper means matching his being the lord with tools such as flowers considering the way they got that fortune, without seeing your disqualification and without feeling shy.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fourth pāsuram, to trigger the taste in those who surrender, āḻvār says “What noble deeds would those, who serve emperumān in tiruvanantapuram without any expectation, have done previously?” Alternatively, āḻvār is saying “Speak about the fortune of those who serve emperumān in tiruvanantapuram without any expectation”*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. pēsumin kūsam inṟip periya nīr vēlai sūḻndu vāsamē kamaḻum sōlai vayal aṇi anantapuram nēsam seyduṟaiginṟānai neṟimaiyāl malargaḷ tūvip pūsanai seyginṟārgaḷ puṇṇiyam seydavāṟē*

- *pēsumin kūsam inṟi* – Speak without feeling shy, seeing your disqualification. Though āḻvār was mercifully blessed by emperumān with divine knowledge and devotion, having been in samsāram since time immemorial, due to that impression, he felt shy speaking about emperumān saying “*aruvinaiyēn*” (sinful me); āḻvār thinks the same is applicable for even those who are coming now to speak about emperumān. While speaking about bhagavat viśayam one need not feel shy; one was not speaking since there was no faith; as one understands the aptness of it, then one can speak without any shyness.
- *periya nīr …* – Being surrounded by ocean which is having abundance of water, and having garden which has fragrance. The ocean is surrounding the garden like a fort to not let out the fragrance.
- *vāsamē kamaḻum* – The fragrance of the garden suppresses the bad smell emitted by the ocean; tiruvanantapuram which is decorated with fields which have such garden. It can also be recited along with previous phrase as in “*nēsam seydu uṟaiginṟānai – pēsumin kūsaminṟi*“. In that case, it will highlight āḻvār’s amazement as in “*nēsam seyduṟaiginṟānai – pūsanai seyginṟārgaḷ puṇṇiyam seydavāṟē*“. Alternatively, it can also be recited starting with “*periya nīr*” and ending with “*pūsanai seyginṟārgaḷ puṇṇiyam seydavāṟṟai – pēsumin kūsaminṟi*“, implying “praise without feeling shy, as to how fortunate are those who are vorśipping such emperumān”; in that case, “*kūsaminṟip pēsugai*” means – bhāgavatas cannot be praised casually unlike the case of bhagavān \[hence, they have to be praised with great care/love\].
- *nēsam seydu uṟaiginṟānai* – He remains in paramapadam since it is unavoidable for him. He resides here showing the defects in paramapadam; as seen in “if there is a place where there is no scope for protecting the suffering ones, what is the point in residing there!”, he desirously resides here considering this abode to be the apt place for protecting the suffering ones; śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 95.12 “*adikam puravāsācca*” (residing in this citrakūtam is greater than residing in ayōdyā).
- *neṟimaiyāl malargaḷ tūvi* – Offering flowers etc at his divine feet with the understanding of “sarvēśvaran is the lord; this ātmā is his servitor”; alternative explanation – as he desirously resides in this abode, we too, desirously offer these flowers; another explanation – as he arrived here considering this place to be dear to him, due to their presence here, they also surrender unto him without expecting anything else from him \[other than kainkaryam\].
- *puṇṇiyam seyda āṟē* – Is the service of nityasūris who served as said in tiruviruttam 21 “*sūttu nanmālaigaḷ tūyana ēndi*” (carrying the best garlands), a service! They \[residents of paramapadam\] are like śrī bharatāḻvān; these \[residents of tiruvanantapuram\] are like iḷaiya perumāḷ (lakśmaṇa). Even after emperumān leaves them \[in paramapadam\], they remain there due to their pāratantriyam (total dependence).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 10.2.5. Punniyam seydu

*puṇṇiyam seydu nalla punalodu malargaḷ tūvi eṇṇumin endai nāmam ippiṟappaṟukkum appāl tiṇṇam nām aṟiyac connōm seṟipoḻil anantapurattu aṇṇalār kamala pādām aṇuguvār amararāvār*

**Пословный перевод:**

puṇṇiyam seydu – performing bhakti which is enjoyable; nalla – that which is dear to him, due to being with bhakti; punalodu malargaḷ – water, flowers etc; tūvi – offer (with love); endai – creator’s; nāmam – divine names; eṇṇumin – meditate upon them always and enjoy them; ippiṟappu – this birth, which hurts when seen; aṟukkum – will ensure the eradication; appāl – further; seṟi poḻil – having rich garden; anantapurattu – in tiruvanantapuram; aṇṇalār kamala pādam – divine feet of the unconditional lord; aṇuguvār – those who approach in a friendly manner (as said here); amarar āvār – will become one among nityasūris; nām – we (who are well versed); tiṇṇam – firmly; aṟiya – to know; sonnōm – told

**Перевод:**

**Performing bhakti which is enjoyable, offering water, flowers etc which are dear to him, due to being with bhakti, meditate upon the divine names of the creator always and enjoy them; that will ensure the eradication of this birth, which hurts when seen; further, those who approach in a friendly manner, the divine feet of the unconditional lord in tiruvanantapuram which is having rich garden, will become one among nityasūris; we firmly tell this for you to know.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fifth pāsuram, āḻvār praises those who surrender unto tiruvanantapuram to be comparable to nityasūris and says “You also surrender like that”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. puṇṇiyam seydu nalla punalodu malargaḷ tūvi eṇṇumin endai nāmam ippiṟappaṟukkum appāl tiṇṇam nām aṟiyac connōm seṟipoḻil anantapurattu aṇṇalār kamala pādām aṇuguvār amararāvār*

- *puṇṇiyam seydu* – Showing devotion. \[How does puṇya indicate bhakti?\] That is because, bhakti has dyānam, varṇāśrama darmam etc as ancillary aspects; hence, the jñāna in the form of bhakti (devotion), which is a result of righteous karma is indicated. [śrī bhagavat gītā 9.34](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/9-34/) “*madbhaktō … man manā bhava …*” (be my devotee, think about me).
- *nalla punalodu malargaḷ tūvi* – Being overwhelmed with love, offering flowers with pure water. With this, arcanai \[a mode of worship\] etc are indicated. “*madyāji mām namaskuru*” (worship me, offer me obeisances) are said in the same ślōkam.
- *eṇṇumin* – It is said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 9.14](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/9-14/) “*satatam kīrtayanta:*” (always engage in singing).
- *endai nāmam* – One need not seek any qualification to recite the divine name, since it is similar to someone stumbling upon and crying out “ammē!” (mother); nanjīyar asked paraśara bhattar “Should one purify oneself before reciting the divine name?” bhattar mercifully replied “Should one who is going to take a dip in gangā, take a dip in another pond to purify oneself? Will the divine name which bestows all goodness subsequently, not bestow the qualification to recite it as well?” One only needs taste to recite the divine name; only those \[with desire\] are qualified persons.
- *ippiṟappu aṟukkum* – Have we not seen the state of this body which is like a garment stitched together!  One will hang the head down, while seeing the inside of the body; one will naturally develop detachment \[when the inside is seen\]. The power of previous impressions makes it difficult to develop detachment even after this being physically observable by the senses. Some śrīvaiṣṇavas introduced a cetty (scholar) to bhattar and told him “He is a well known tamiḻ scholar”; bhattar asked him “If you have any questions, why don’t you ask?” He asked “Some say ‘beyond the body which is seen, there is no ātmā, there is no darmam/adarmam and there is no īśvara’; others see the defects in the body and say ‘this body is impermanent; we should hold on to something which is permanent, and beyond this body’; while the body is the same, why are there multiple views?” bhattar mercifully explained “īśvara has arranged it as per individual’s karma, in such a way that the fortunate ones will see the defects in the body and shed it, and the unfortunate ones will enjoy the body and drown in it, as said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 7-14](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/7-14/) ‘*mama māyā duratyayā’* (it is difficult to crossover my primordial matter) and ‘*māyām ētām tarantitē’* (they cross over this ocean of samsāra \[by my grace\])” It will be as said in [iraṇḍām tiruvandādi 66](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/01/irandam-thiruvandhadhi-66/) “*idu kaṇḍāy*” (This birth in samsāram itself is hellish – see for yourself); it is not good because we think in that manner; the true state of this body is the knowledge of “this is insignificant, this is impermanent” which was given by īśvara.
- *ippiṟappu aṟukkum* – Will eradicate the connection with the body, which is to be known to understand its defective nature.
- *seṟi poḻil …* – Those who reach the ultimately enjoyable divine feet of the lord of all who is mercifully resting in tiruvanantapuram which is having rich garden.
- *appāl – amarar āvār* – Even those \[nityasūris with divine bodies\] who are with body which cannot be said as “*ippiṟappu aṟukkum*“, are serving the divine feet of one who is mercifully resting in tiruvanantapuram. Thus, with this, this tiruvanantapuram which not only eliminates the hurdles but also facilitates attaining the desired goal, is said to be the abode of refuge.
- *tiṇṇam* – This is confirmed.
- *nām aṟiyac connōm* – We are blessed by emperumān with “*mayarvaṟa madinalam*” (unblemiśed knowledge and devotion); we are telling this to you who are all considering your body as the self, to make you aware, seeing your disastrous state.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 10.2.6. Amararay

*amararāyt tiriginṟārgatku ādi sēr anantapurattu amarar kōn arccikkinṟu angagap paṇi seyvar viṇṇōr namargaḷō! sollak kēṇmin nāmum pōy naṇuga vēṇḍum kumaranār tādai tunbam tudaitta gōvindanārē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kumaranār tādai – rudra, the father of subrahmaṇya, his; tunbam tudaitta – eliminated the sorrow; gōvindanār – as kriṣṇa; amarar āy – as other dēvatās; tirginṟārgatku – those who roam around; ādi – being the creator; sēr – mercifully resting; anantapurattu – in tiruvanantapuram; amarar kōn – sēnai mudaliyār (viśvaksēnar); arccikkinṟu – for the worship; angu – arriving in that abode; agap paṇi seyvar – those who perform confidential services in assisting him in such worship; viṇṇōr – are the residents of paramapadam; namargaḷō – Oh our people!; sollak kēṇmin – listen to what I say; nāmum pōy – let us also go (along with them); naṇuga vēṇḍum – should reach

**Перевод:**

**emperumān as kriṣṇa eliminated the sorrow of rudra, the father of subrahmaṇya and is the creator of those who roam around as dēvatās; such emperumān is mercifully resting in tiruvanantapuram; sēnai mudaliyār has arrived at this abode to worship such emperumān along with those residents of paramapadam who perform confidential services, assisting him in such worship. Oh our people! Listen to what I say; let us also go and reach there.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the sixth pāsuram, āḻvār says “Even nityasūis come and serve in tiruvanantapuram; thus, tiruvanantapuram is an even more apt goal than paramapadam; hence, let us go and serve him”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. amararāyt tiriginṟārgatku ādi sēr anantapurattu amarar kōn arccikkinṟu angagap paṇi seyvar viṇṇōr namargaḷō! sollak kēṇmin nāmum pōy naṇuga vēṇḍum kumaranār tādai tunbam tudaitta gōvindanārē*

- *amararāyt tiriginṟārgatku* – Just as māmbaḻa uṇṇi (an insect, whose name means mango-eater) has no relation to mango, these amaras (dēvas) who are in this material world, who live a little bit longer than humans and eventually die, and who are still called as amara (immortal) even though there is an end to their life, are pridefully roaming around as if they are immortal.
- *tiriginṟār* – Though the bondage is heavy, they roam around without any worry. Their situation is not as simple as the ātmā in a human body. For a human being, all that he needs to give up is his own body and a woman (his wife); but for brahmā, he needs to give up the whole universe which is under his control.
- *ādi sēr anantapurattu* – For dēvas and nityasūris, the only commonality towards bhagavān is bhagavān being the cause for all. For nityasūris, he ensures their existence; for the dēvas, he unites the body and soul, and conducts them by recreating the body every moment that it decays. tiruvanantapuram where the cause of the universe is eternally residing.
- *amarar kōn …* – śrī sēnāpati āḻvān (viśvaksēna) is performing eternal kainkaryam; nityasūris will assist him.
- *namargaḷō sollak kēṇmin* – Oh all of those who are eternally related to me as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 3.3.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/08/thiruvaimozhi-3-3-1-ozhivil-kalam/) “*vaḻuvilā adimai seyya vēṇḍunām*” (We should serve continuously)! Listen to my words. One should share kind words with relatives.
- *nāmum* – We are desirous to serve and should join the nityasūris to be in their group to go and serve.
- *pōy naṇuga vēṇḍum* – It is not enough that we just dream of it from here, but we should reach there.

When asked “Would it be possible for us, who are samsāris, to be in their group?” āḻvār says,

- *kumaranār …* – He is the saviour for us when we are in a dangerous situation of being attacked by dēvas and asuras together; thus, should it be difficult for us to reach that abode? Will he, who removes the sorrows of the prideful persons, make it difficult for us who are without any pride, to reach him? He remains the eliminator of sorrows for rudra et al; he remains subservient to cows and covherds. We should reach such gōvinda.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 10.2.7. Tudaitta govindanare

*tudaitta gōvindanārē ulaguyir dēvum maṟṟum padaitta em parama mūrtti pāmbaṇaip paḷḷi koṇḍān madaittalai vāḷai pāyum vayalaṇi anantapuram kadaittalai sīykkap peṟṟāl kadu vinai kaḷaiyalāmē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ulagu – worlds; uyir – creatures (such as humans); dēvum – dēvatās (celestial beings); maṟṟum – and other entities such as mahat (the great element) etc; tudaitta – one who created them all and annihilated them too; gōvindanārē – (as said in “tama: parēdēva ēkī bhavati“, as he has a shining form in that stage) one who is known as gōvinda, himself; padaitta – one who created; em – one who revealed this kāraṇatvam (his being the cause); parama mūrtti – lord who is greater than all; pāmbu aṇai – in the serpent mattress; paḷḷi koṇḍān – one who is mercifully resting, his; madait talai – in the entrance of the canals; vāḷai pāyum – the (schools of fish) jumping around joyfully; vayal aṇi – having the field as decoration; anantapuram – in tiruvanantapuram; kadaittalai – in the divine entrance; sīykkap peṟṟāl – if we engage in sweeping the floor etc; kadu vinai – great sorrow (of not attaining opportunity to do kainkaryam); kaḷaiyalām – can be eliminated

**Перевод:**

**emperumān, who is known as gōvinda, himself created the worlds, the creatures, dēvatās and other entities such as mahat and annihilated them too; being the creator, lord who is greater than all, who revealed this kāraṇatvam, is mercifully resting on the serpent mattress. If we engage in sweeping the floor etc at the divine entrance of his tiruvanantapuram which is having farm-field as decoration with (the schools of) fish jumping around joyfully in the entrance of the canals, our great sorrow, of not doing kainkaryam until now, can be eliminated. gōvinda could also indicate kriṣṇa as said in “kriṣṇa ēvahi lōkānām utpattirapi cābyaya:” .**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the seventh pāsuram, āḻvār says “As one goes and serves sarvēśvaran who is mercifully resting in tiruvanantapuram, our sorrow of not serving him previously will be eliminated immediately”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. tudaitta gōvindanārē ulaguyir dēvum maṟṟum padaitta em parama mūrtti pāmbaṇaip paḷḷi koṇḍān madaittalai vāḷai pāyum vayalaṇi anantapuram kadaittalai sīykkap peṟṟāl kadu vinai kaḷaiyalāmē*

- *tudaitta gōvindanārē …* – tudaikkai – annihilating. Annihilation precedes creation. mahābhāratam sabhā parvam 38.23 “*kriṣṇa Eva hi lōkānām utpattirapicābyaya:*” (kriṣṇa is the cause for all worlds), periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 1.1.6 “*vaiyam ēḻum kaṇḍāḷ piḷḷai vāyuḷē*” (mother yaśōdā saw the whole creation in kriṣṇa’s mouth).
- *ulagu uyir …* – One who created the world, celestial beings and other sentient beings. When they started violating their limits, he annihilated them, and subsequently he gave them the senses/bodies which are necessary to attain the puruśārtam (goal), and protected them.
- *em parama mūrtti* – sarvēśvaran who is humble towards his devotees.
- *pāmbaṇaip paḷḷi koṇḍān* – One who mercifully reclined on tiruvanantāḻvān (ādiśēśa) in the created world, for the protection of the residents of the world. His,
- *madaittalai …* – In the abode which is decorated with fields where the (schools of) fish joyfully jump around and reside in the entrance of the canals, due to the abundant availability of water; just as muktātmās reside in paramapadam singing sāma gānam, even the animals reside joyfully in this abode.
- *kadaittalai sīykkap peṟṟāl* – If we get to perform divine sweeping kainkaryam at the sannidi entrance.
- *kadu vinai kaḷaiyalāmē* – All the sorrows due to not performing service will be eliminated. After acquiring śēśatva jñānam (knowledge of being a servitor), the sorrow of not having done service cannot be eliminated by prāyaścittam (atonement) \[it will only go by engaging in kainkaryam fully\].

## 10.2.8. Kadu vinai

*kadu vinai kaḷaiyalāgum kāmanaip payanda kāḷai ida vagai koṇḍadenbar eḻil aṇi anantapuram padamudai aravil paḷḷi payinṟavan pādangāṇa nadaminō namargaḷ uḷḷīr! nām umakkaṟiyac connōm*

**Пословный перевод:**

kadu vinai – cruel sins (which are the reasons for delay in attaining the result); kaḷaiyal āgum – can be eliminated; kāmanai – kāma (cupid, who is famous for his beauty); payanda – one who created; kāḷai – kriṣṇa who did not lose his youth (even after that); ida vagai – as his abode; koṇḍadu – had; eḻil – beauty; aṇi – having; anantapuram – tiruvanantapuram; enbar – is said; padam udai – having hoods (which are expanded due to being in contact with emperumān); aravil – in the divine serpent mattress; paḷḷi – in mercifully resting; payinṟavan – of the one who is very involved; pādam – divine feet; kāṇa – to see and enjoy; namargaḷ uḷḷīr – oh our people; nadaminō – start walking; nām – we (who know the greatness of emperumān); umakku – for you; aṟiya – to know; sonnōm – have told

**Перевод:**

**Cruel sins can be eliminated. It is said that kriṣṇa who did not lose his youth even after creating kāma, is having beautiful tiruvanantapuram as his abode. Oh our people! Start walking towards such tiruvanantapuram to see and enjoy the divine feet of the one who is very involved in mercifully resting on the divine serpent mattress with hoods. We have told this for you to know.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the eighth pāsuram, āḻvār invites śrīvaiṣṇavas saying “Please go to tiruvanantapuram to see the divine feet of sarvēśvaran who is mercifully resting there”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. kadu vinai kaḷaiyalāgum kāmanaip payanda kāḷai ida vagai koṇḍadenbar eḻil aṇi anantapuram padamudai aravil paḷḷi payinṟavan pādangāṇa nadaminō namargaḷ uḷḷīr! nām umakkaṟiyac connōm*

- *kadu vinai kaḷaiyal āgum* – We can get rid of the cruel sins which cannot be eliminated by our own efforts.
- *kāmanaip payanda kāḷai* – I have to instruct you only until you see him! He is the one who created kāma who bewilders the whole world with his beauty. When both (kriṣṇa and kāma) are seen together, one will think “kāma is mistakenly identified as beautiful”. Even what is said in “*prasavāntanca yauvanam*” (youth remains only until one becomes pregnant), is not applicable here.
- *ida vagai koṇḍadu enbar* – All the learned ones say that he has taken this place as his abode and will remain blissful; “*padmanābham vidurbudā:*” (Learned ones know about padmanānābha).
- *eḻil aṇi anantapuram* – Nothing new can be done in paramapadam; this is the unique greatness here over there \[here, the town can be newly decorated\].
- *padam udai aravil* – The blossoming which happens when sarvēśvaran reclines on him, is highlighted here in “*padam udai aravu*“.
- *paḷḷi payinṟavan* – The mattress is so cozy that even the naturally omniscient lord will become unconscious while resting on it.
- *pādam …* – All of you who are my brethren in thinking to see his divine feet as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 9.4.5](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/07/thiruvaimozhi-9-4-5-ariyaya-ammanai/) “*vari vāḷ aravinaṇaip paḷḷi koḷginṟa kariyān kaḻalē kāṇak karudum karuttu*” (Dark-hued emperumān is mercifully resting on the serpent mattress which has stripes and radiance; my intellect is thinking to see the divine feet of such emperumān). During an adyayana utsavam, when araiyar recited this pāsuram, āḷavandār heard it and thought “We should have a connection with āḻvār \[by following his instructions\]” and immediately gathered śrīvaiṣṇavas who are his disciples, and mercifully went to tiruvanantapuram.
- *nām* – We who know the nature of his merciful resting posture and say as in [tiruvāimoḻi 3.7.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/09/thiruvaimozhi-3-7-1-payilum-sudaroli/) “*yavarēlum avar – emmai āḷum paramar*” (anyone who has the wealth of vorśipping emperumān, is my lord).
- *umakku aṟiyac connōm* – We have told you, who are having the desire to see such form of emperumān, to know about it.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 10.2.9. Nam umakku

*nām umakkaṟiyac conna nāḷgaḷum naṇiyavāna sēmam nangudaittuk kaṇḍīr seṟi poḻil anantapuram tūma nal virai malargaḷ tuvaḷaṟa āyndu koṇḍu vāmanan adikkenṟētta māyndaṟum vinaigaḷ tāmē*

**Пословный перевод:**

nām – us; umakku – for you; aṟiyac conna nāḷgaḷum – the days of the end of the body, which were informed; naṇiya Ana – are coming close; seṟi poḻil – having dense garden; anantapuram – tiruvanantapuram; nangu – good; sēmam – protection; udaittuk kaṇḍīr – is having!; tūmam – fragrant smoke, which is an aide in the worship; nal – good; virai – having fragrance; malargaḷ – flowers; tuvaḷ aṟa – to be without defect; āyndu koṇḍu – preparing; vāmanan adikku enṟu – vowing them to be for the divine feet of śrī vāmana who is naturally inclined towards union with his devotees; ētta – (for such acceptance) praising his qualities such as śeelam (simplicity) etc; vinaigaḷ – karmas which are hurdles for kainkarayam; tānē – on their own; māyndu aṟum – will be destroyed

**Перевод:**

**The days of the end of the body, which were informed for you by us are coming close; tiruvanantapuram which is having dense garden, is having good protection! As we engage in preparing fragrant smoke which is an aide in the worship, flowers which are having good fragrance and vowing them to be for the divine feet of śrī vāmana who is naturally inclined towards union with his devotees, and praise his qualities such as śeelam etc, our karmas which are hurdles for kainkarayam, will be destroyed on their own.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the ninth pāsuram, āḻvār says “The time which was identified as in tiruvāimoḻi 9.8.4 ‘nāḷēl aṟiyēn enakkuḷḷana’ (I don’t know the date fixed for me) and tiruvāimoḻi 9.10.5 ‘maraṇam ānāl’ (at the end of this body), has arrived; as we quickly reach tiruvanantapuram and engage in service, the karmas which are hurdles for our service will be eliminated”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. nām umakkaṟiyac conna nāḷgaḷum naṇiyavāna sēmam nangudaittuk kaṇḍīr seṟi poḻil anantapuram tūma nal virai malargaḷ tuvaḷaṟa āyndu koṇḍu vāmanan adikkenṟētta māyndaṟum vinaigaḷ tāmē*

- *nām umakku* – The days I said in [tiruvāimoḻi 9.8.4](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/08/thiruvaimozhi-9-8-4-nalel-ariyen/) “*nāḷēl aṟiyēn enakkuḷḷana*” (I don’t know the date fixed for me) and [tiruvāimoḻi 9.10.5](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/09/thiruvaimozhi-9-10-5-saranam-agum/) “*maraṇam ānāl*” (at the end of this body), have arrived near. Did he advice others in this manner? Yes. In [tiruvāimoḻi 9.10](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/09/thiruvaimozhi-9-10-malainanni/) “*mālai naṇṇi*“, āḻvār found out īśvara’s opinion in “*maraṇam ānāl*” and instructed the same to others. Here also, āḻvār is instructing others. mahābhāratam “*tasmin atamitē …*” \[kriṣṇa tells this ślōkam to yudiśtra\] – bhīśma is dying and he mercifully started explaining these since there won’t be anyone who will hear these words subsequently – āḻvār is mercifully repeating the same advice now. *astamitē* – There are two suns, viz the sun who illuminates the eyes and the sun who illuminates the heart; tiruccanda viruttam 114 “*jñānamāgi jñāyiṟāgi*” (being the knowledge and sun). *jñānānyalpī bhaviśyati* – just as svarūpam (the self, which is also known as darmi jñānam), dharma bhūta jñānam (knowledge which helps understand other aspects) is also eternal \[but it is considered insignificant due to depending upon the mind\]; now, the dawn and dusk for this depend on the tool which receives such knowledge. If bhīśma dies, there won’t be anyone to give and receive this knowledge. parijñai appar (a śrīvaiṣṇava) highlights what is mercifully explained by bhattar “unless a respectable person has this and teaches this, teachers and students will cease to exist and such knowledge will become worthless”. *tasmāt tvām cōdayāmyaham* – This is why I am urging to go to bhīśma and hear from him.
- *sēmam nangudaittuk kaṇḍīr seṟi poḻil anantapuram* – This perfectly enjoyable abode is the protection for our final moments.
- *tūma nal virai malargaḷ* – Nicely fragrant smoke, fragrant and good flowers.
- *tuvaḷ aṟa …* – Making them distinguished to be apt for us and him.
- *vāmanan …* – Praising the divine feet of emperumān who became a mendicant to get back his own property, and offering to such divine feet.
- *māyndu aṟum vinaigaḷ tānē* – As the ātmā engages in activity which is apt for his true nature, all the hurdles will be eliminated \[i.e. the kainkaryam is not a means, but is a natural activity\]

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 10.2.10. Mayndarum vinaigal

*māyndaṟum vinaigaḷ tāmē mādavā! enna nāḷum ēynda pon madiḷ anantapura nagar endaikkeṟnu sāndodu viḷakkam dūbam tāmarai malargaḷ nalla āyndu koṇḍētta vallār andamil pugaḻinārē*

**Пословный перевод:**

mādavā! enna – the moment that emperumān is referred to as śriya:pati (husband of śrī mahālakśmi); vinaigaḷ – hurdles; tāmē – on their own; māyndu aṟum – will be eliminated; nāḷum – forever; ēynda – rich; pon madiḷ – having golden fort; anantapura nagar – in the city of tiruvanantapuram; endaikku – for the lord; enṟu – vowing in this manner; nalla – good; sāndodu – with sandalwood paste; viḷakkam – lamp; dūbam – fragrant smoke; tāmarai malargaḷ – lotus flowers; āyndu koṇḍu – preparing (to not being touched by attachment towards result, doerśip and ownership which are like dry leaves, hair and worms); ētta vallār – those who can praise emperumān, fulfilled with the feeling of having been acknowledged by him; andam il – endless; pugaḻinār – will have greatness in servitude

**Перевод:**

**The moment that emperumān is referred to as “śriya:pati” (husband of śrī mahālakśmi), hurdles will be eliminated on their own; those who can praise emperumān, fulfilled with the feeling of having been acknowledged by him, preparing good sandalwood paste, lamp, fragrant smoke and vowing that all of these are for the lord, in the city of tiruvanantapuram which is having golden fort forever,  have endless greatness in servitude.**

## 10.2.11. Andamil pugal

*andamil pugaḻ anatapura nagar ādi tannai kondalar poḻil kurugūr māṟan sol āyirattuḷ aindinōdaindum vallār aṇaivar pōy amar ulagil paindodi madandaiyar tam vēy maru tōḷiṇaiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

andam il pugaḻ – being with endless qualities; anantapura nagar – residing in tiruvanantapuram; ādi tannai – the cause of all; kondu – flower bunches; alar – blossoming; poḻil – surrounded by garden; kurugūr – controller of āḻvārtirunagari; māṟan – nammāḻvār; sol – mercifully spoke; āyirattuḷ – among the thousand pāsurams; aindinōdu – along with the five pāsurams (which are advice for others); aindum – the five pāsurams where he adviced others as well as self; vallār – those who can practice; pōy – going (in arcirādi mārgam (path leading to paramapadam)); amar ulagil – in the abode of paramapadam, which is the dwelling place of “ayarvaṟum amarargaḷ” (nityasūris, muktātmās); paindodi – being decorated with ornaments in their arms; madandaiyar tam – divine apsaras (celestial damsels), their; vēy maru – distinguished like bamboo; tōḷiṇai – the brahmālankāram (ultimate decoration) which is done by their shoulders (hands); aṇivar – will get to accept

**Перевод:**

**nammāḻvār, the controller of āḻvārtirunagari, which is surrounded by garden with blossoming flower bunches, mercifully spoke on emperumān, the cause of all, who is residing in tiruvanantapuram with endless qualities, five pāsurams as advice for others and five pāsurams as advice for others and self, among the thousand pāsurams; those who can practice this decad will go and reach the abode of paramapadam , which is the dwelling place of “ayarvaṟum amarargaḷ“, to accept the brahmālankāram (ultimate decoration) which is done by the distinguished bamboo like shoulders of the divine apsaras who are decorated with ornaments in their arms. todi – bangles.**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. andamil pugaḻ anatapura nagar ādi tannai kondalar poḻil kurugūr māṟan sol āyirattuḷ aindinōdaindum vallār aṇaivar pōy amar ulagil paindodi madandaiyar tam vēy maru tōḷiṇaiyē*

- *andam il …* – On the one who is the cause of the universe, who is present with endless qualities in tiruvanantapuram; those who surrender are with endless qualities; the one who accepts the surrender is also with endless qualities. Since he left parampadam, arrived in tiruvanantapuram and is mercifully resting there, there is no end for his qualities/greatness; for the devotees, since they became detached from samsāram and engaged in service in ugandaruḷina nilangaḷ (divya dēśams, where he is desirously living), there is no end for their qualities/greatness. Due to accepting service from such ātmā \[from samsāram\], there is no end to emperumān’s greatness; due to serving emperumān, there is no end for the greatness of such devotees. Only if emperumān is glorified only while being in samsāram, ātmā will also be glorified while reaching paramapadam. As the ātmā increases his detachment in this world, he acquires greatness; similarly, as emperumān increases his detachment in paramapadam, he acquires greatness. For both \[ātmā and emperumān\], both \[paramapadam and samsāram, respectively\] are difficult to attain.
- *kondu alar poḻil kurugūr …* – Mercifully spoken by nammāḻvār who has āḻvārtirunagari which is in spring season always.
- *aindinōdu aindum vallār* – Just as making a necklace with gems knowing their nature very well and glorifying the necklace, āḻvār is enjoying five pāsurams at a time.
- *aṇaivar …* – Reach śrīvaikuṇṭam and will become the target of the care of the apsaras (celestial damsels) as said in kauśīdaki upaniśat “… *śatam mālā hastā:*” (With garlands in their hands, hundred apsaras will welcome the muktātmā (liberated soul) who enters paramapadam). There is no difference between what is said in tiruvāimoḻi 10.9.8 “*mudiyudai vānavar muṟai muṟai edir koḷḷa*” (the crowned nityasūris will welcome the liberated soul) and “*vēy maru tōḷiṇai aṇaivar*“. It is said in tiruvāimoḻi 10.9.10 “*madimuga madandaiyar ēndinar vandē*” (Ladies with moon like face, with auspicious pots in their hands, came to welcome the liberated soul).

## 10.3 Vey maru tol inai

## 10.3.1. Vey maru tol inai

*vēy maru tōḷ iṇai meliyumālō! melivum en tanimaiyum yādum nōkkāk kāmaru kuyilgaḷum kūvumālō! kaṇa mayil avai kalandālumālō! āmaru ina nirai mēykka nī pōkku oru pagal āyiram ūḻiyālō! tāmaraik kaṇgaḷ koṇḍu īrdiyālō! tagavilai tagavilaiyē nī kaṇṇā!*

**Пословный перевод:**

vēy maru – Like bamboo; tōḷ iṇai – pair of shoulders; meliyum – became lean (to reveal the inside); en melivum – the weakness of my body (which is the abode); en tanimaiyum – my loneliness (where I cannot bear the separation); yādum – anything; nōkkā – ignoring; kāmaru – attractive; kuyilgaḷum – cuckoos; kūvum – making sounds (to unite among themselves); kaṇa mayil avai – muster of peacocks; kalandu – uniting (among themselves); Alum – are dancing; A – cows; maruvu inam – abundantly available matching their species; nirai – herds; mēykka – to tend them; nī – you; pōkku – going for a leelā (sport); oru pagal – the day time; āyiram ūḻi – felt like thousand yugas (as said in “trudi yugāyatē“); tāmarai – attractive like lotus; kaṇgaḷ koṇḍu – with the eyes; īrdi – you are piercing me; kaṇṇā – Oh kriṣṇa (who is here to hurt the hearts of girls)!; nī tagavilai – You don’t have the common mercy not to torment (the girls); tagavilai – Also, you don’t have the specific mercy (of not tormenting the already suffering ones)

**Перевод:**

**Pair of shoulders which resemble bamboo, became lean; ignoring the weakness of my body and my loneliness, the attractive cuckoos are making sounds; the muster of peacocks is uniting and dancing; in the day time, when you go for the leelā of tending the herds of cows which are abundantly available matching their species, it feels like thousand yugas; you are piercing me with your eyes which are attractive like lotus. Oh kriṣṇa! You neither have the common mercy not to torment the girls nor the specific mercy of not tormenting the already suffering ones. Implies that this cruelty has become a natural quality for him. She is saying “vēy maru tōḷ iṇai” just as he would praise her beauty. kāmaru kuyil – beautiful cuckoo or cuckoo which is in the garden. “ālō” indicates the overwhelming sorrow.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the first pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki is in pain of separation thinking that emperumān is leaving and further becomes anguished by the sounds of birds such as cuckoo etc and by the glance of emperumān; she informs this state to him as if informing it to her friends.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. vēy maru tōḷ iṇai meliyumālō! melivum en tanimaiyum yādum nōkkāk kāmaru kuyilgaḷum kūvumālō! kaṇa mayil avai kalandālumālō! Amaru ina nirai mēykka nī pōkku oru pagal āyiram ūḻiyālō! tāmaraik kaṇgaḷ koṇḍu īrdiyālō! tagavilai tagavilaiyē nī kaṇṇā!*

- *vēy …* – Due to having nice circumference and freshness, the shoulders can be compared to bamboo – such shoulders are becoming lean – says parānguśa nāyaki, just as informing to a prideful prince “your garden is getting destroyed”. Her becoming weak is directly being witnessed by kriṣṇa instead of hearing from others (like before), by looking at her shoulders. Thinking about her bewilderment, just as one would step into a flood, the shoulders became lean even while he was present there. Even his physical presence is of no use, when there is separation in the heart; the weakness which is a result of such separation, cannot be stopped from occurring. She is informing about the weakening of her shoulders as if saying “your shoulders are becoming weak”! This ātmā remains a prakāra (attribute) for bhagavān to not differentiate between dēvadatta (a jīvātmā) and vāsudēva (paramātmā). When you unite with me where will you relax yourself? Usually he will rest on her shoulders and relax as said in tirunedundaṇḍagam 13 “*melliyal tōḷ tōyndāy*” (drowned in the shoulder of tender sītā).
- *iṇai* – See the torment undergone by the pair of shoulders which are praised by your for their beautiful togetherness! She is of the nature of praising her own beauty; she is repeating what she heard from him. Now, they are as good as acit (matter) even if you arrive.
- *ālō!* – The great sorrow is revealed by *ālō*.
- *melivum en tanimaiyum* – My weakness and loneliness are unlike those of the worldly people. They are unlike your weakness and loneliness; this is the loneliness when you are with me and the weakness when we are together. This is much beyond what is explained in [tiruvāimoḻi 4.2.10](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/12/thiruvaimozhi-4-2-10-en-seygen/) “*pon sey pūṇ men mulaikkenṟu meliyumē*” (She desires such tuḷasi to decorate her withered bosom which has pale complexion; since her desire is not fulfilled, she has become weak), [tiruvāimoḻi 9.7.10](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/08/thiruvaimozhi-9-7-10-thagavanru/) “*miga mēni meliveydi*” (body greatly wizened) and [tiruvāimoḻi 9.9.2](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/09/thiruvaimozhi-9-9-2-pugalidam-arigilam/) “*tamiyamālō*” (lonely us). They were all felt in his absence; now, the sorrow is felt in his presence. For the one who says as in [tiruvāimoḻi 9.7.9](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/08/thiruvaimozhi-9-7-9-pundhuzhay-mudiyarkku/) “*tām tammaik koṇḍagaldal tagavanṟu*” (moving away from me does not match his mercy after knowing himself) that if he leaves he has to place himself there and leave \[which is impossible\], due to her loving attitude towards him, she can say that he has left, while he is present there with her. Neither has he left to return nor is he thinking to leave; it is not possible for him to leave her. Even he starts wondering “Have we really separated from her?” looking at her body truly becoming weak. As, both of them are crazy for each other as if eating ūmattangāy (a plant product, which causes hallucination), there is no scope for either of them to acquire clarity. This is his great fortune. He had not seen her sufferings previously; he has only heard from her friends and others; śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 5.6 *“vāhivāta …”* (Oh wind!) etc; now he is seeing it with his own eyes. Now, she is telling whatever she would share with her friends usually.
- *yādum nōkkā* – Not considering anything. Not seeing the weakness in the shoulders, her loneliness etc.
- *kāmaru kuyilgaḷum* – kāmarudal – desire. Since their union will not lead to separation, such unions are desirous. They don’t have the fear of their union ending in separation.
- *kuyilgaḷum* – Not only you, even these cuckoos have become harmful. You seem good when compared to the entities you send to harm me.
- *kūvumālō* – Should they not shut their mouth seeing my state? Seeing my sorrow in separation, should they not avoid making sounds thinking “our sound will be like poison for her”? śrī rāmāyaṇam kiśkindā kāṇḍam 3.33 “*kasya nārādayatē cittam*” (whose heart does not become enchanted) – her state is such that one will place the sword back in its pouch on seeing her.
- *kaṇa mayil* – Unlike those \[like rāma\] would remain alone in suffering and torment others by keeping them lonely, these peacocks are together.
- *avai* – Since they appear like druśtiviśam (like a snake’s poison which harms on being seen), she is saying “those” by keeping her face away, since she is not able to tolerate seeing them. They are tormenting her being in a group.
- *kalandu* – They are not retracting thinking “at this stage, if we unite that will kill that girl”.
- *ālumālō* – After physically observing the peacocks dancing as a result of the bliss of their union, she is turning her face away and saying “*avai*“. First part of śrī rāmāyaṇam kiśkindā kāṇḍam 1.40 is explained here. *mayūrasya* – āḻvār is thinking that rāvaṇa is separating anything seen in pairs. Did he not carry away the spouse of the peacock? *vanē* – He did not separate them in śrī ayōdyā! He separated them in the secluded forest where they are meant to enjoy with each other. *rakśasā na hrutā priyā* – Only these were spared from separation by this cruel killer!
- *āmaruvu …* – At this stage, he should have been thinking as in śrī rāmāyaṇam kiśkindā kāṇḍam 30.10 “*katam ēśā bhaviśyati*” (how is she doing now), instead of doing that, he is setting out to protect his dependents. There are herds of cattle which move around with you – they are cows; to tend them. As said in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 3.6.9 “*mēynda pullum kadaivāy vaḻi sōra*” (to let the gazed grass slip out of the mouth), the cattle sustain themselves by being with kriṣṇa and nothing else.
- *inam* – Even if we are in the group which is protected by him, he will only think about protecting everyone together; he protects only those who are in groups.
- *nī pōkku oru pagal* – The daytime in which you go; or the daytime when you are away; another explanation – the daytime in which you stay away from me to go and protect the cows.

When asked “īsn’t it just one daytime!” she says,

- *āyiram …* – Don’t think about us to be like you. For those who are always craving for your togetherness, there is no separate desire for night time and day time. śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 5.13.59 “*yatābda kōti pratima: kśaṇastēna vinābavat*” (When separated from kriṣṇa, a moment will feel like millions of years).

emperumān thought “We did not leave; we did not think about leaving as well; while we are here, she is thinking that I have left and is being tormented by these entities! What an amazing love she has for me?” and mercifully glanced at her. She says,

- *tāmaraik kaṇgaḷ koṇḍīrdiyālō* – It is better if you go to tend the cows rather than glancing at me like this. Some explain this as parānkuśa nāyaki explaining emperumān’s glance from previous occasions; but “*īrdi*” (piercing, in present tense) indicates that she is talking about present only.

Even after parānkuśa nāyaki says this, he does not take his eyes off her. She says,

- *tagavilai* – You have no mercy towards the world; there is none who can stop his mercy. While emperumān is tormenting us, why is she upset towards those who are inimical towards us? One has annadōśam (defect in the food consumed) and the other has samsarga dōśam (defect in friendship); hence, isn’t it natural that they will be inimical towards us? Peacock, being subrahmaṇya’s vehicle, has defect in friendship; cuckoo, due to consuming crow’s food, has defect in its food.
- *nī tagavu ilai* – You have no mercy. She who called him in [tiruvāimoḻi 2.4.6](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/03/thiruvaimozhi-2-4-6-thagavudaiyavane/) “*tagavudaiyavanē*” (oh merciful one!), is now saying *tagavilai* in his presence. You are merciless. The first tagavilai says that he is merciless and the second indicates that he has mercy for worldly people; alternatively – both tagavilai mean he is merciless. The reason for the repetition is to indicate that she is working to establish that emperumān is merciless as said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 5.18.30 “*ēvam ārtāsu yōśitsu krupā kasya na jāyatē*” (If the girls are suffering like this, who will not have mercy?)

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.
