## 10.3.2. Tagavilai

*tagavilai tagavilaiyē nī kaṇṇā! tada mulai puṇardoṟum puṇarccikkārāccuka veḷḷam visumbiṟandu aṟivai mūḻkkac cūḻndu adu kanavena nīngi āngēaga uyir agam agandōṟum uḷ pukku āviyin param alla vētkai andō!miga miga ini unnaip pirivaiyāmāl vīva nin pasu nirai mēykkap pōkkē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kaṇṇā – Oh kriṣṇa (who is known to be obedient towards girls)!; nī – you; tagvilai tgavilaiyē – are not having mercy in any manner (matching such obedience); tada – expansive (to be praised by you); mulai – bosoms; puṇardoṟum – every moment you embrace; puṇarccikku – for that embrace; ārā – uncontrollable, great; suka veḷḷam – ocean of bliss; visumbu iṟandu – going beyond (endless) sky; aṟivai – intellect too; mūḻkka – to be subdued; sūḻndu – surrounded; adu kanavena – as a dream; nīngi – faded away; āngē – in that situation; aga uyir – where the prāṇa (vital air) which is inside; agam agam tōṟum – in every spot; uḷ pukku – entering inside; āviyin – for the ātmā (which is the abode); param alla – intolerable; vētkai – desire (increased); andō! – alas! (I am unfortunate to inform this to you who are with me now!); ini – now; miga miga – further; unnai – you; pirivaiyām Al – to handle the separation; nin – your; pasu nirai mēykkap pōkku – going to tend the cows for their grazing; vīva – should avoid

**Перевод:**

**Oh kriṣṇa! You are not having mercy in any manner; every moment you embrace my expansive bosoms, I am surrounded with uncontrollable, great ocean of bliss which goes beyond the sky, and my intellect is subdued too; but that experience faded away as a dream, and my desire increased in the ātmā to become intolerable as it entered inside every spot  where the prāṇa is present; alas! Now, to handle separation from you, you should avoid any further intent on going to tend the cows for their grazing.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the second pāsuram, as parānguśa nāyaki speaks in this manner, to sustain her, emperumān embraces her repeatedly. Seeing that, she says “while I get ultimate bliss in your union, when I think that you will leave, all that bliss becomes illusion like waking up from a dream in the sleep, and hence I am suffering”. This can also be considered as speaking about previously occurred union.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. tagavilai tagavilaiyē nī kaṇṇā! tada mulai puṇardoṟum puṇarccikkārāccuka veḷḷam visumbiṟandu aṟivai mūḻkkac cūḻndu adu kanavena nīngi āngēaga uyir agam agandōṟum uḷ pukku āviyin param alla vētkai andō!miga miga ini unnaip pirivaiyāmāl vīva nin pasu nirai mēykkap pōkkē*

- *tagavilai …* – (You kriṣṇa, have no mercy) kriṣṇa is popularly known to be the property of girls. But you, who are the property of girls, remain merciless.

kriṣṇa says “You are telling me that I am merciless! I did not think about leaving you and neither have I left you” and tightly embraced her to sustain her.

- *tada mulai …* – Even if he embraced her million times, she will think “he is embracing me to separate from me” and her body will become pale when his hands relaxed from the tight embrace; he will see that and embrace her to pacify her and this will keep repeating. Though this could mean the union in the past, it is more apt to speak about the union in present only.
- *tada mulai* – emperumān is going through the same emotions which those who try to know him, go through \[her bosoms are so expansive to be able to easily comprehend\]; one cannot enjoy them fully; the ultimate enjoyability which cannot be fully enjoyed even by emperumān himself who is the ultimate enjoyer.
- *puṇarccikku ārāc cuka veḷḷam* – The ocean of bliss which cannot be controlled even after the union. The bliss matches the nature of the couple uniting. Just as his svarūpam cannot be determined to be in a particular manner, his excellent enjoyability cannot be determined; her desire is as explained in tiruvāimoḻi 10.10.10 “*adanil periya avā*” (my desire which is greater than everything).
- *puṇardoṟum puṇarccikku ārāc cuka veḷḷam* – Alternative explanation – That is, union happens rarely, but the bliss remains eternally. It is said in kuṟundogai 3 “*nilattinum peridē vāninum uyarndanṟu, nīrinum āraḷavinṟē sāral, karungōl kuṟinjip pūk koṇḍu perundēn iḻaikkum nādanodu natpē*” (The heroine says – my love for nādan (her beloved) is longer than earth, taller than sky and deeper than ocean. Just as honey extracted from the kuṟinji flower will be taken to bee-hive, I will be taken home by him). Just as honey is extracted from kuṟinji flower to be enjoyed.

When asked “How big is this bliss?” She says,

- *visumbu …* – ākāsam (ether) is the one which gives space for all entities; even making that look very small, and further, the bliss makes the knowledge which was acquired by the divine blessing of emperumān also look very small. Alternative explanation – visumbu indicates paramapadam – mōkśam (ultimate bliss) is explained in tirukkuṟaḷ 1103 as “*tāmaraik kaṇṇan ulagu*” (the abode of lotus eyed lord). Hence – going beyond tripād vibhūti \[paramapadam which is three times the size of samsāram\], it subdued ubhaya vibhūti (both spiritual and material realms) and my intelligence.
- *adu kanavena nīngi* – It faded away just as a dream will disappear. On seeing its vastness, I thought there is no end to it; on seeing it disappear, it felt like a flood drained and the ground underneath became hot. One who united in such manner, separated. The endless union is explained as dream and magic; this union too remains endless.
- *āngē* – In that situation.
- *aga uyir* – The heart which is the abode of prāṇa.
- *agam agandōṟum* – Every spot in the heart. \[Will the mind be expansive to have many spots?\] Due to previous, special unions, the heart remains expansive. The union and separation will cause space in the heart; sorrow will fill in all of those spots.
- *āviyin param alla vētkai* – The eagerness is not limited to the atomic nature of the ātmā; bhūtattāḻvār too said in [iraṇḍām tiruvandādi 100](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/02/irandam-thiruvandhadhi-100/) “*enṟan aḷavanṟāl yānudaiya anbu*” (my love is not limited to my size); the desire is beyond the abode \[ātmā\] on which it exists. There are three states in an ātmā – sukham (in the state of joy), du:kham (in the state of sorrow) and svarūpēṇāvasti (neutral state); did I get to remain in the neutral state!
- *andō!* – It is sad that you have to learn this from me! While both of us enjoy in union, in separation, I have to explain the sorrow to you! While the union is equal for both, the sorrow is just for me!

When asked “So, what needs to be done?” she says,

- *nin pasu nirai mēykkap pōkku – vīva* – You should not go to tend your cows.

When asked “Why should I not go?” she says,

- *miga miga ini unnaip pirivaiyāmāl* – Since it will lead to further separation from you.
- *pirivai* – This is poetic way of saying pirivu. Avoid going to tend the cows, which will lead to separation. pōkku is singular. Just as it is said “*pasu vandana*” (cow\[s\] came, where pasu is singular indicating the group, vandana is in plural), pōkkugaḷ (travels, plural) is mentioned as pōkku (travel, singular).
- *ini vīva* – Though you have gone previously, at least going forward, you should avoid going.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 10.3.3. Vivan nin

*vīvan nin pasu nirai mēykkap pōkku vevvuyir koṇḍu enadāvi vēmāl yāvarum tuṇai illai yān irundu un anjana mēniyai āttam kāṇēn pōvadanṟu oru pagal nī aganṟāl poru kayaṟkaṇṇiṇai nīrum nillā sāvadu ivvāykkulattāycciyōmāyp piṟanda ittoḻuttaiyōm tanimai tānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

nin pasu nirai mēykkap pōkku – In your going to tend the cows (which you consider as your activity matching your dharma); vīvan – I will perish; vevvuyir koṇḍu – breathing hot (due to this disease of separation); enadu āvi – my ātmā (soul); vēm – is burning due to that; tuṇai – companion; yāvarumillai – there is no one; yān – I; irundu – alive; un anjana mēniyai – your form which is attractive like dark pigment; āttam – activity; kāṇēn – not seeing; nī aganṟāl – if you go; oru pagal – that one day time alone; pōvadu anṟu – will remain without moving; poru – fighting (with each other); kayal – like a fish; kaṇ iṇai – pair of eyes which you praise; nīrum nillā – tears are not stopping; ivvāyk kulattu – in this covherd clan (in which you are born); āycciyōmāyp piṟanda – being born as covherd girl instead of covherd boy; toḻuttaiyōm – we who are lowly, our; it tanimai tānē – being alone in this manner; sāvadu – should end

**Перевод:**

**I will perish if you go to tend the cows; as I am breathing hot, my ātmā is burning due to that; there is no companion for me; I am alive but not seeing the activity of your form which is attractive like dark pigment; if you go, that day time will remain without moving; tears are not stopping in the pair of eyes which you praise and which resemble fish fighting with each other; we are born lowly as covherd girls instead of covherd boys; our loneliness should end. Implies – since loneliness is natural for them, ending it means ending themselves. Also implies that loneliness is as good as death.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the third pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki says “This one sided love, of your ignoring us and our liking you, should perish”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. vīvan nin pasu nirai mēykkap pōkku vevvuyir koṇḍu enadāvi vēmāl yāvarum tuṇai illai yān irundu un anjana mēniyai āttam kāṇēn pōvadanṟu oru pagal nī aganṟāl poru kayaṟkaṇṇiṇai nīrum nillā sāvadu ivvāykkulattāycciyōmāyp piṟanda ittoḻuttaiyōm tanimai tānē*

- *vīvan …* – Having your going to tend the cows as the reason, I will perish. If you think “isn’t it my duty?”, then you will end up doing strīvadam (killing of woman).

When asked “How do you know that you are reaching the end?” she says,

- *vevvuyir …* – Can you not see me? Due to your leaving, I am breathing heavily and having that as the reason, my heart has withered. I am burning by the fire of sorrow in separation; she is saying “Don’t you have the capability to pour water on this heart?”.
- *enadu āvi* – Don’t consider everyone to be like yourself \[I am suffering and you are not\].
- *yāvarum tuṇai illai* – You, who are my companion, have left; if you leave, naturally my friends who are my companions, would also leave; cuckoos, peacocks etc have also developed hatred towards me, like the townspeople.
- *yān irundu* – Did I get to experience that \[death\] which happens when you leave? Even after suffering everything, I am continuing to live one hundred years; the desire to see you somehow, will not let me die. emperumān who separated will neither let me die nor let me sustain; just as arjuna remained facing many insults after kriṣṇa ascended to paramapadam.
- *un anjana mēniyai āttam kāṇēn* – Did I get to enjoy the sustaining force of those who continue to live? She is desiring for the uruveḷippādu (visualisation) which she enjoyed in [tiruvāimoḻi 7.7](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/10/thiruvaimozhi-7-7-ezhaiyar/) “*ēḻaiyarāvi*“.
- *un* – You have not seen yourself in mirror. Had you seen, should you not think “those who are separated from me will not survive”?
- *mēniyai* – She in not interested to engage in his svarūpam (true nature) or guṇam (qualities); as an eager woman, she is desiring for his body!
- *āttam kāṇēn* – I did not get to see him walk around in front of me with his body.

He said “This is just for the day time”, and she says,

- *pōvadu anṟu …* – Don’t think that it is the same for us like for you. When you step away, even if 30 nāḻigai \[each nāḻigai is 24 minutes\] pass it will not move even a little bit, just as those firm malayāḷar (people from the present state of kēraḷam) who decide to get something from someone, will not move away until they get it; that is not due to the nature of the daytime.
- *nī aganṟāl* – It is because of your nature. If that is the nature of the daytime, even while you are together with us, it should stay still. Just as I cannot see night \[darkness\] when you are with me, I cannot see the daytime moving in your absence. When he is present, we cannot see night; [iraṇḍām tiruvandādi 81](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/01/irandam-thiruvandhadhi-81/) “*nāraṇanaik kaṇḍēn pagal kaṇḍēn*” (I saw nārāyaṇa, I saw light). He remains without saying “*pōvadu anṟu oru pagal*“; even previously she said that he said “I will not leave” \[but left. Hence, she will not trust him\].
- *poru kayal …* – I am unable to stop the tears which are flowing from my eyes, due to your leaving.
- *nīrum nillā* – Even if I can stop you, I cannot stop the tears. The suffering in thinking about the separation is similar to the fighting of the fish.

When asked “What should I do?” she says

- *sāvadu …* – Let the separation in this lowly life of being born as a girl in this covherd clan, be ended. Whether you go or remain here, let my loneliness end. She is speaking like sāvitri who told yama “I should get hundred children with him” \[When yama was taking her husband, satyavān, away, sāvitri prayed to yama and he agreed to give her a boon. She cleverly asked him to let her get hundred children with satyavān\]
- *tanimaidānē – sāvadu* – Alternative explanation. We don’t distinguish between loneliness and separation! Also implying that this loneliness itself is death. āḻvār says in [tiruvāimoḻi 2.3.7](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/02/thiruvaimozhi-2-3-7-munnal-yazh/) “*ninnalāl ilēn*” (I have no existence without you); even tirumangai āḻvār says in [tirunedundāṇḍagam 1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/06/thirunedunthandakam-1/) “*iṟappadaṟkē eṇṇādu*” (not thinking about death, that is kaivalyam, self enjoyment). Another explanation – this loneliness is very bad, and hence let this one sided love end. When a kaikkiḷait talaivi (heroine who is engaged in one sided love) loses patience, she will say anything.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 10.3.4. Toluttaiyom

*toḻuttaiyōm tanimaiyum tuṇai pirindār tuyaramum ninaigilai gōvindā nin toḻuttanil pasukkaḷaiyē virumbit tuṟandemmai ittu avai mēykkap pōdi paḻutta nal amudin in sāṟṟu veḷḷam pāviyen manam agandōṟum uḷ pukku aḻutta nin sengani vāyin kaḷvap paṇi moḻi ninaidoṟum āvi vēmāl*

**Пословный перевод:**

gōvindā – Oh one who is crowned as gōvinda (due to protecting covherd girls)!; toḻuttaiyōm – we the servitors (to be protected by you), our; tanimaiyum – loneliness; tuṇai – you, the companion; pirindār – separated; tuyaramum – sorrow; ninaigilai – not thinking; un – your; toḻuttanil – covśed; pasukkaḷaiyē – cows alone; virumbi – showed attachment; emmai – us (who are also to be protected by you); tuṟandu – abandoned; ittu – leave behind; avai – those; mēykka – to protect them only; pōdi – you are starting to leave; paḻutta – well ripen; nal amudin – pure nectar’s; in – sweet; sāṟṟu veḷḷam – flood of the essence; pāviyēn – I who am having sin to separate from you, my; manam agam tōṟum – every spot in my heart; uḷ pukku – entering; aḻutta – to strangle; nin – your; sem – reddish; kanivāyin – enjoyable divine lips which resemble a fruit; kaḷvam – mischievous; paṇi – humble; moḻi – words; ninaitoṟum – every time I think about; āvi – my soul; vēm – is burning

**Перевод:**

**Oh one who is crowned as gōvinda! You, our companion, are not thinking about the loneliness and sorrow of separation of ours, the servitors; showing attachment to the cows in your covśed, abandoning and leaving us behind, you are only starting to leave to protect them; you speak mischievously humble words from your enjoyable divine lips which resemble a reddish fruit; these words are like a flood of the essence of well ripened, sweet, pure nectar which enter into every spot in my heart and strangle it; every time I think about it, my soul is burning. paṇi moḻi means humble words as well as spoken words.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fourth pāsuram, as parānguśa nāyaki starts feeling the pain thinking emperumān is leaving, he mercifully says “is there any reason for me to leave?” and few other humble words; she says “these words only are finishing me”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. toḻuttaiyōm tanimaiyum tuṇai pirindār tuyaramum ninaigilai gōvindā nin toḻuttanil pasukkaḷaiyē virumbit tuṟandemmai ittu avai mēykkap pōdi paḻutta nal amudin in sāṟṟu veḷḷam pāviyen manam agandōṟum uḷ pukku aḻutta nin sengani vāyin kaḷvap paṇi moḻi ninaidoṟum āvi vēmāl*

- *toḻuttaiyōm tanimaiyum* – This is the loneliness of the girls of five lakh families in gōkulam. They are referring to themselves as “*toḻuttaiyōm*” and “*adicciyōm*” highlighting their being defeated \[by him\].
- *tuṇai pirindār tuyaramum* – That is those who have separated from you \[the companion\]. āccān would say “would companion not indicate presence of two persons?” These gōpikās will be his companions and he will be their companion; now, companionship remains on only one person; he is the only companion now; everyone else is like a wound in the neck \[hurdle\]; periya tirumoḻi 3.7.6 “*vantuṇai*” (strong companion). You are not thinking about our loneliness and the sorrow of those who are separated from you; you are not thinking that “we” \[your servitors\] are getting separated and are separating from “you” \[who is distinguished\].
- *gōvindā* – He was crowned as gōvinda for protecting the cows and covherd people \[during gōvardan leelā\]. Birth based duties will always remain. That is, even while his consort is suffering in separation, he would be desirous with his cows and look for fields which have grass and water to feed them.
- *nin …* – if yo have two classes of entities to be protected (cows and cow-herd girls), why do you show your love towards only one class? Would it not be acceptable to love both classes?
- *nin toḻuttanil* – Should you only protect the cows which are sheltered in a single place? Should you not protect those who are within your grasp? Even while going to tend the cows, you should embrace them \[the covherd girls\] and leave for grazing the cows.
- *pasukkaḷaiyē* – Should you be helping those \[cows\] who do not suffer in your separation?
- *virumbi* – Even while lying with the girls, embracing them, he will be saying “bring that rope”, “calves are leaving” and thinking about them only. Even while he is physically present here, his heart is with the cows. Here, he is faking the embrace only. piḷḷai amudanār would say “if a thorn pierces the foot of a cow, the head of the covherd boy will accumulate pus”. When something happens to the body, it is the ātmā who naturally experiences the pain and pleasure \[covherd boys and cows have such close relationship\].
- *tuṟandu emmai* – The gōpikās think that as his love increases for the cows, he becomes more detached from the gōpikās themselves.
- *emmai ittu* – Dropping us just like dropping insentient objects. Even while being with the gōpikās, he will think about the cows; but when he goes behind the cows, he will not think about the gōpikās.
- *avai mēykkap pōdi* – You will go for their protection. In protecting them, you would become tired, but to protect us, your mere presence is sufficient; your going to protect them will cause fear as said in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 3.2.6 “*idaṟa en piḷḷaiyaip pōkkinēn*” (I let my son go to make him suffer) and periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 3.2.2 “*eṟṟukken piḷḷaiyaip pōkkinēn*” (Why did I let my tender son go to roam around?) But in our protection, there is no fatigue involved, your presence here is sufficient.
- *paḻutta …* – He said some humble words such as “Will I go? Even if I go, will I forget you? Do you go through the same pain as I do? Am I not going to tend the cows since I am subservient to my parents and going as per their orders? Will my heart not remain here even if go there?” These words make us not forget you. Saying that the words are like an ocean of well ripened, sweet essence of distinguished nectar; alternatively – this can be a type of union. That is, the nectar from his mouth; it is said in periyāzvār tirumoḻi 1.7.4 “*vāyamudam tandu ennait taḷirppikkinṟān*” (bringing joy in me by giving his nectarean saliva).
- *pāviyēn* – I am having sins which turn nectar into poison. This act of saying “I won’t separate” thinking about the separation is similar to poison.
- *manam agam tōṟum …* – As it presses on every spot in my heart, your reddish fruit like mouth’s
- *kaḷvap paṇi moḻi* – This (your mouth) is the gateway for this flood of essence of bliss; lowly words which will captivate us. Since the words are spoken having the separation in mind, they will destroy my heart. His speech and mind are not in harmony.
- *ninai toṟum* – Will start meditating upon them considering “will these sustain us?” But they are harmful; still she cannot stop thinking; in this manner, it will go on forever.
- *āvi vēmāl* – ātmā which is the abode, is burning. Just as the fire burns the object on which it is present, the thoughts burn the ātmā on which they are present. Should be understood as “paḻutta nallamudinin sāṟṟu veḷḷamāna – nin sengani vāyin kaḷvap paṇi moḻi – pāviyēn manamagandōṟum uḷ pukkaḻutta … āvi vēmāl”.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 10.3.5. Pani moli

*paṇi moḻi ninaidoṟum āvi vēmāl pagal nirai mēykkiya pōya kaṇṇā! piṇiyaviḻ malligai vādai tūvap peru mada mālaiyum vandanṟālō maṇi migu mārvinin mullaip pōdu en vana mulai kamaḻvittun vāy amudam tandu aṇi migu tāmaraik kaiyai andō adicciyōm talai misai nī aṇiyāy!*

**Пословный перевод:**

paṇi moḻi – the words you say to pacify me; ninaidoṟum – every time I think about; āvi – heart; vēm – burning; pagal – the daytime fully; nirai mēykkiya – to tend the cows; pōya – gone; kaṇṇā – kriṣṇa!; piṇi – bound by the string; aviḻ – expanding; malligai – jasmine (which has honey); vādai – northerly wind; tūva – as it blows; peru – huge; madam – pride; mālaiyum – evening; vandanṟu – has arrived; maṇi – kaustuba gem; migum – very shining; mārvinil – in the divine chest; mullaip pōdu – jasmine flower; en vana mulai – on my beautiful bosom; kamaḻvittu – embracing me to spread the fragrance; un vāy amudam tandu – giving me your ultimately sweet nectar from your mouth; aṇi migu – attractive and well decorated; tāmarai – like a lotus flower; kaiyai – hand; adicciyōm talaimisai – on the head of ours, servitors; nī – you; aṇiyāy – indicates the desire for wild union saying “you should place your hand as decoration”; andō! – It is tragic that I have to explain my suffering to you!

**Перевод:**

**Every time that I think about the words you say to pacify me, my heart is burning. Oh kriṣṇa who has gone to tend the cows during the daytime fully! As the northerly wind blows the jasmine flowers bound by the string, expanding their fragrance, the hugely prideful evening has arrived; you should embrace my beautiful bosom to spread the fragrance of the jasmine flower which is in your chest having very shining kaustuba gem; you should give me your ultimately sweet nectar from your mouth; you should place your hand which is like an attractive and well decorated lotus flower, on the head of ours, servitors; indicates the desire for wild union. It is tragic that I have to explain my suffering to you!**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fifth pāsuram, emperumān mercifully asks parānguśa nāyaki “Why are you tormenting like this when I am here in front of you” and she says “Since you have to tend the cows, you will be leaving; after you leave, I am being tormented by entities which torment like the sandyā (evening time); hence you should do acts like embracing me etc and enliven me”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. paṇi moḻi ninaidoṟum āvi vēmāl pagal nirai mēykkiya pōya kaṇṇā! piṇiyaviḻ malligai vādai tūvap peru mada mālaiyum vandanṟālō maṇi migu mārvinin mullaip pōdu en vana mulai kamaḻvittun vāy amudam tandu aṇi migu tāmaraik kaiyai andō adicciyōm talai misai nī aṇiyāy!*

- *paṇi moḻi ninaidoṟum āvi vēmāl* – My words are unlike yours where you think about separation but say “I won’t leave you”; since your words are as in [tiruvāimoḻi 10.3.4](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/11/thiruvaimozhi-10-3-4-thozhuththaiyom/) “*kaḷvap paṇi moḻi*“, they are false, and since my words express my experience, they are truthful.

He asks “Did I go?” She says,

- *pagal …* – You went to tend the cows all through the daytime.
- *kaṇṇā* – She is calling him “*kaṇṇā*” and directly telling him! \[Commentator becomes amazed at āḻvār’s mood\]
- *mēykkiya* – To tend.
- *piṇi …* – As those harmful entities starting with as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 9.9.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/09/thiruvaimozhi-9-9-1-malligai-kamazh/) “*malligai kamaḻ tenṟal*” (southerly breeze fragrant with jasmine flavour) etc started tormenting me, hence it is certain that you have left. The northerly wind is spreading the fragrance of the blossoming jasmine. Just as rāvaṇa assumed the form of a sanyāsi and appeared, the northerly wind is harming me in the form of cool breeze.
- *tūva* – It is blowing on me by staying apart so that I don’t feel warm; śrī rāmāyaṇam kiśkindā kāṇḍam 1.17 “*padma kēsara samsruśta:*” (with the buds of lotus flowers) – just as a mad elephant would arrive with band music in front of it, the evening arrives following the northerly wind. Since the evening respects her, it is coming along with companions to torment her.
- *vandanṟālō* – It has arrived; it touched my body and left. Just as you faced the arrows shot by bhagadatta aimed at arjuna by covering him and accepting them in your chest, you come in front of me and face this. We are not fearing for very fierce evening to come, it has already arrived.

When asked “What shall we do?” She says,

- *maṇi migu mārvinil* – The chest which will add shine to śrī kaustuba jewel; alternative explanation – the whole chest will have the lustre of śrī kaustuba jewel. It is of such nature that even during embrace, it need not be removed as said in [śaraṇāgati gadyam 5th cūrṇikai](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/12/saranagathi-gadhyam-5-part-1/) “*niratiśaya sukha sparśa:*” (wondrously soft on emperumān’s body); just as her femininity is identified by her bosom, his masculinity is identified by śrī kaustubam. This is an identity of puruśōttama (supreme lord). Adding fragrance to my beautiful bosom with the jasmine garland on that chest. My bosom became an enjoyable tool for him on his chest just like śrī kaustuba and garland. She is explaining this wild union to have the fragrance of the jasmine garland on his shoulders to be transferred to her bosom. These bosoms are waiting to be decorated by the garland just as those who would take bath and wait for flowers to decorate their hair. Instead of letting these bosoms remain celibate, make these fragrant with the fragrance of the garland; you should transfer the fragrance of the garland here and leave the residue on your chest. It is not possible to have the fragrance of the garland on my bosoms without union/embrace; as said in “*kim mukham vanamālā sankramasya*” (how to attain the vanamālā of emperumān).
- *vāy amudam tandu* – As the union reaches ultimate stage, to sustain themselves there will be some romantic speech – that is highlighted here; alternatively, it is highlighting his necatrean saliva. Mainly, it is explained as speech.
- *aṇi …* – My tongue has become dry thinking about your leaving. As a remedy, can you please place your hand on my head? This is their mundirigai fruit (a type of fruit) which will remove dryness in mouth.
- *aṇi migu tāmaraik kai* – Hand which is well decorated with ornaments and which is an ornament in itself negating the need for any other ornament as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam kiśkindā kāṇḍam 3.15 “*sarvabhūśaṇa bhūśārhā:*” (the shoulders which bring about beauty for the ornaments which are worn by him). He will collect the ornaments showing his great attachment towards them saying “When I go to tend the cows, to sustain myself, give me your ornament \[to one gōpikā\], give me your ornament \[to another gōpikā and so on\]” and would wear them; she may also be talking about how he has decorated himself to go to tend the cows. As he gets decorated and gets ready to leave, she became broken.
- *tāmaraik kaiyai* – The hand which needs no ornament to make it look more beautiful.
- *andō* – I have to request this from you as if a thirsty person needs to be requested to drink cold water!
- *adicciyōm* – She is highlighting that he has won over her with his beauty.
- *talai misai nī aṇiyāy* – Just as his hand is for the ornament, her head is for his hand. They are trying to get their goal accomplished by holding his hand and falling at his feet as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 9.2.2](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/06/thiruvaimozhi-9-2-2-kudik-kidandhu/) “*pāda pangayamē talaikkaṇiyāy*” (your lotus feet are the decoration for my head) and “*adicciyōm talai misai nī aṇiyāy*“. They \[āḻvārs/ācāryas\] remain as said in [stōtra ratnam 31](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/01/sthothra-rathnam-31/) “… *madīya mūrdānam alankariśyati*” (when will my head be decorated with your divine feet?) He said “Who knows these conditions? If you desire so, you can take my hand and place it on your head yourself!” Will I have to put in my own effort to accomplish my goal, which is like letting kāla (death personified) to put a ring on my finger? Am I not of the nature that you will yourself desirously grant me that? They \[āḻvārs/ācāryas\] always accept any benefit only by bhagavān’s will and effort.
- *aṇiyāy* – Just because of overwhelming grief, we won’t do improper acts! Are we supposed to perform your duty?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 10.3.6. Adicciyom

*adicciyōm talai misai nīyaṇiyāy āḻiyangaṇṇā! un kōlappādam pidittadu naduvunakkarivaiyarum palar adu niṟka em peṇmai āṟṟōm vadittadangaṇṇiṇai nīrum nillā manamum nillā emakkadu tannālē vedippu nin pasu nirai mēykkap pōkku vēm emaduyir aḻal meḻugilukkē*

**Пословный перевод:**

āḻi – like an ocean (having the quality of immeasurability); am – attractive; kaṇṇā – oh kriṣṇa!; un – your; kōlap pādam – well decorated divine feet; adicciyōm talaimisai – on the head of ours, who fully exist for you; nī aṇiyāy – you should mercifully place; naduvu – in between (your going for the task); adu pidittu – holding your divine feet; arivaiyarum – those (girls) who think about themselves highly; unakku – for you; palar – there are many; adu niṟka – that aside; em peṇmai – our femininity; āṟṟōm – unable to control by pacifying it; vadi – beautiful like a split in a baby-mango; tada – vast; kaṇṇiṇai – in the pair of eyes (which you praise); nīrum nillā – tears are not stopping; manamum – heart; nillā – is not steady; adu tannālē – hence; nin – your; pasu nirai mēykkap pōkku – going to tend the cows; vedippu – leading to destruction; emadu uyir – our ātmā; aḻal – in fire; meḻugil – like wax; ukku – melting; vēm – and burning

**Перевод:**

**Oh kriṣṇa, you who are like an attractive ocean! You should place your well decorated divine feet on the head of ours, who fully exist for you; in between, there are many of those (girls) who think about themselves highly, remain for you, holding your divine feet; that aside, we are unable to control our femininity by pacifying it; tears are not stopping in the pair of eyes which are vast and beautiful like a split in a baby-mango; our heart is not steady; hence, your going to tend the cows, is leading to our destruction; our ātmā is melting like wax in fire and burning.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the sixth pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki says “You have many girls who are dear to you; you have no shortcoming; we cannot sustain in your separation; your leaving is undesirable for us”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. adicciyōm talai misai nīyaṇiyāy āḻiyangaṇṇā! un kōlappādam pidittadu naduvunakkarivaiyarum palar adu niṟka em peṇmai āṟṟōm vadittadangaṇṇiṇai nīrum nillā manamum nillā emakkadu tannālē vedippu nin pasu nirai mēykkap pōkku vēm emaduyir aḻal meḻugilukkē*

- *adicciyōm talai misai nī aṇiyāy āḻi am kaṇṇā* – Should the winner not be caring towards the loser?
- *āḻi am kaṇṇā* – Attractive eyes which are like ocean which rejuvenates. Since “*nī aṇiyāy*” is followed by “*āḻi am kaṇṇā*” – it implies he is saying – Am I not saying “You should mercifully glance at me with your divine eyes, you should touch me with your hand”? Do I have any other go? Even if I go, will I think of anything other than you? She says – Yes! Let that be! \[But we want you to glance us with your merciful eyes\]
- *un kōlam …* – There are many who hold on to your divine feet; don’t you have great festival wherever you go?
- *naduvu* – In between your tasks which you are going to attend.
- *arivaiyar* – Those who can engage you with their youth.
- *palar* – Are they just one or two? śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 5.13.18 “*śōdaśa strī saharsrāṇi*” (sixteen thousand wives), periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 4.9.4 “*padināṟāmāyiravar dēvimār*” (sixteen thousand wives).
- *adu niṟka* – That aside. Are we going to stop a herd of elephants marching on us? \[We cannot stop your engagement with the girls\]
- *em peṇmai āṟṟōm* – We are unable to suppress our sorrow with our femininity. We cannot survive if you leave.

When asked “If femininity is your nature, should you not sustain yourself till I come?” she says,

- *vadit tadam kaṇṇiṇai nīrum nillā* – Can you not see us? Do we have any sign of an alive person in us? Sharp, vast eyes are not stopping to shed tears. What a sharpness where the glance clearly shoots the targeted person! See the torment faced by the eyes which you praised “The enjoyability is beyond the capability of the enjoyers!”
- *nīrum nillā* – Even if you stop \[leaving\], the tears are not stopping. Even if I can stop you, I cannot stop the tears.

When asked “Why are you not stopping it forcefully?” she says “I have to stop at the source to stop the flow of the tears”. He asks “But, why can’t you force your heart?” she says,

- *manamum nillā* – Can you not see how we are suffering due to losing our courage?

When asked “you should try hard to control your heart and sustain” she says,

- *namakku* – You can do it; to separate and to sustain during separation, one has to be you as said in “*yāmudai āyan than manam kal*” (the covherd, kriṣṇa’s heart has become very hard).
- *adu tannālē* – Due this heart-broken situation.
- *vedippu nin pasu nirai mēykkap pōkku* – Your going to tend the cows is destruction for us.

When asked “Why is it destruction?” she says,

- *vēm …* – Our prāṇa (life) is melting like wax in close proximity of fire. Hence, your going to tend the cows is destruction for us.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 10.3.7. Vem emaduyir

*vēm emaduyir aḻal meḻugilukku veḷ vaḷai mēgalai kaḻanṟu vīḻa tu malark kaṇṇiṇai muttanjōrat tuṇai mulai payandena tōḷgaḷ vāda mā maṇivaṇṇā! un sengamala vaṇṇamen malaradi nōva nī pōy ā magiḻndugandavai mēykkinṟu unnōdasurargaḷ talaippeyyil yavan kol āngē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

veḷ vaḷai – white bangles; mēgalaiyum – waist clothes; kaḻanṟu vīḻa – slipping down, not fitting well; tū – blemiśless; malar – like fresh lotus flower; kaṇṇiṇai – the eyes which you liked; muttam – sorrowful tear drops; sōra – flowing uncontrollably; tuṇai mulai – the pair of bosoms which you praise; payandu – becoming pale; ena tōḷgaḷ – my shoulders; vāda – like a creeper which lost its support; māmaṇi – like a great blue gem (which can be owned); vaṇṇā – Oh one who is having a form!; sengamalam – like a reddish lotus; vaṇṇam – attractive; men malar – tender like a flower; un adi nōva – to hurt your divine feet; nī pōy – You (who can sustain during separation) going; A – for the cows; magiḻndu ugandu – being greatly blissful; avai mēykkinṟu – while tending them; unnōdu – with you who lead to chaos; asurargaḷ – demons (such as ariśtāsura, dēnukāsura et al); talaippeyyil – if they fight; yavan kol – what will happen? (thinking this); emaduyir – our ātmā; aḻal – in fire; meḻugil – like wax; ukku – melting; vēm – and burning

**Перевод:**

**Simple translation (based on vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar‘s 12000 padi)**

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the seventh pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki says “While we are suffering here, what disaster will befall you when you go to tend the cows such that you hurt your tender divine feet and some demons attack you?”.*

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. pāsuram vēm emaduyir aḻal meḻugilukku veḷ vaḷai mēgalai kaḻanṟu vīḻa tu malark kaṇṇiṇai muttanjōrat tuṇai mulai payandena tōḷgaḷ vāda mā maṇivaṇṇā! un sengamala vaṇṇamen malaradi nōva nī pōy A magiḻndugandavai mēykkinṟu unnōdasurargaḷ talaippeyyil yavan kol āngē!*

- *vēm …* – Even if you don’t understand due to lack of loving connection, can you not understand with our instructions? As she is saying “*emadu uyir vēm*” (Our ātmā is burning), she implies that he does not go through that emotion.
- *veḷ vaḷai …* – Bangles made of conch. Due to great weakness in separation, the bangles and waist clothes slip down. Even if they were adjusted without being noticed by others, due to lack of support, they will keep slipping; they cannot stay on ether; that is how lean the body has become.
- *tū malar …* – She spoke the words of her nāyaka (hero, emperumān). Did emperumān say like this? Yes, he said in tiruviruttam 67 “*kaṇgaḷāya tuṇai malar* – *kāviyum neelamum vēlum kayalum pala pala veṇṟirukkum*” (The pair of eyes which is like a pair of lotus flowers, is victorious over many entities like kāvi flower, neelam flower, spear, fish etc).
- *tū malark kaṇṇiṇai muttam sōra* – You can see something which is unseen before \[since he would not have witnessed her sorrowful tears during separation, now she is showing him the same while he is present\]; she is saying “don’t go”. Her tears in the eyes are like a pearl on lotus flower; the pearl which is primary or originated from the eyes. \[Does she know about the beauty of her eyes?\] She is saying based on how her friend explained this to emperumān. He himself said in tiruviruttam 11 “*jñālam eydaṟkuriyana oṇ muttum paimbonnum ēndiṟṟina*” (These eyes which can capture the world, are having beautiful pearls (tears) and gold (pale complexion) due to separation from me) as understood from her.
- *tuṇai mulai payandu* – My bosoms which are praised for their matching togetherness, are acquiring pale complexion; she is saying “emperumān’s kōyil kattaṇam (temple, residence) is getting destroyed”.
- *ena tōḷgaḷ vāda* – As the avayavi (body) weakens, naturally the pair of shoulder will also wither. What is the purpose in standing on pointless aspects and yearning for them? She talked about his loss \[since she belongs to him, whatever she lost is a loss for him\]. Subsequently, she talks about her loss.
- *mā maṇivaṇṇā* – Oh one who has a form resembling a blue gem! mā – black. Are you leaving , taking this form with you? Would your body tolerate the hot weather and winds? You don’t know how it feels to separate from you!
- *un …* – Due to the expansive nature etc, his divine feet can be compared to lotus flower. But there is no comparison for the tenderness of his divine feet.
- *nī pōy* – She is feeling that he should walk with her feet \[instead of his\]. She is the one who says \[as sītāp pirātti\] in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 27.7 “*agratastē gamiśyāmi mrutnandī kuśakatakān*” (I will precede you \[to the forest\] clearing the grass and thorns in the path) – if he does not avoid leaving, she will lead him in the path.

When asked “Should I not go, once the path is cleared?” she says,

- *nī pōy* – Are you śrī rāma, cakravarttit tirumagan (son of emperor daśarata) who goes in the proper path and returns promptly? You are of the nature to go and cause chaos wherever you go.
- *A magiḻndu* – You are not abandoning cows like you are doing to us.
- *ugandu avai mēykkinṟu* – Due to your desire towards them, you are joyfully tending them.
- *mēykkinṟu* – In that situation of grazing the cows, you are not fully focussed \[on external aspects\].
- *unnōdu asurargaḷ talaippeyyil* – Similar to karumugai garland and fire of death meeeting each other.
- *yavan kol āngē* – To be seen as “*āngu yavankol?”* – What will happen there? He will say wherever we go and whoever comes against us, we will remain victorious. But aren’t victory and loss seen as indeterminable as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 37.53 “*avyavastau hi druśyē tē yuddē jaya parājayau*” (In battles, victory or loss is indeterminable)? I am fearing for the undesirable result. What will happen if they come at you? Since she does not want to spell it out, she is saying “what will happen”?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 10.3.8. Asurargal talaippeyyil

*asurargaḷ talaippeyyil evankol? āngu enṟu āḻum ennāruyir ānpin pōgēl kasigaiyum vētkaiyum uḷ kalandu kalaviyum naliyum en kai kaḻiyēl vasi seyun tāmaraik kaṇṇum vāyum kaigaḷum pīdaga udaiyum kātti osi sey nuṇṇidai iḷavāycciyar nī ugakkum nallavarodum uḻi tarāyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

asurargaḷ – demoniac entities; talaippeyyil – if they attack; evankol āngu – whatever unexpected difficulties may occur; enṟu – thinking this; en Ar uyir – my ātmā; āḻum – will be immersed (as in drowning in an ocean) and be anguished; An pin pōgēl – don’t go beyond the cows; kasigaiyum – attachment (due to the love); vētkaiyum – (further) great affection; kalaviyum – union (matching such affection); uḷ kalandu – blending in my heart; naliyum – will torment me; en – my; kaikaḻiyēl – don’t leave; vasi sey – attractive; un – your; tāmarai – like lotus; kaṇṇum – divine eyes; vāyum – divine lips; kaigaḷum – divine hands; pīdaga udaiyum – beauty of the divine yellow clothes; kātti – showing; osi sey – that which will cause weakness (by its nature and embrace); nuṇ idai – those who are having slender waist; iḷam – having youth; āycciyar – covherd girls (born in matching clan); nī ugakkum – dear to you; nallavarodum – with those distinguished persons; uḻi tarāy – roam around

**Перевод:**

**My ātmā will be immersed and be anguished thinking “whatever unexpected difficulties may occur if the demoniac entities attack you”; don’t go beyond the cows; the attachment, great affection and union will blend in my heart and will torment me; don’t leave me; showing your attractive, lotus like divine eyes, divine lips, divine hands and the beauty of the divine yellow clothes which will cause weakness to those youthful covherd girls who are having slender waist, roam around with those distinguished persons who are dear to you, in my presence.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the eighth pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki says “I fear thinking ‘what may happen to you when you go to tend the cows?’ I am also unable to be separated from you; hence, you attract those who are dear to you and remain along with them in my sight and roam around here”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. asurargaḷ talaippeyyil evankol? āngu enṟu āḻum ennāruyir ānpin pōgēl kasigaiyum vētkaiyum uḷ kalandu kalaviyum naliyum en kai kaḻiyēl vasi seyun tāmaraik kaṇṇum vāyum kaigaḷum pīdaga udaiyum kātti osi sey nuṇṇidai iḷavāycciyar nī ugakkum nallavarodum uḻi tarāyē*

- *asurargaḷ …* – She is saying “Even if you return victorious, I will be dead before that; don’t you need me?”
- *āḻum* – Will immerse.

When asked “What shall I do now?” she says,

- *An pin pōgēl* – Don’t go behind the cows; please follow me. Can someone say “I am going to perform sandyāvandanam” when the beloved girl is with him? Should one perform one’s duties abandoning one’s own people?

When asked “How can I avoid my duty which is prescribed for my jāti (birth)? Should you not be patiently waiting?” she says “Did you unite with me in such a manner that I can remain patient?”

- kasigaiyum – love
- *vētkaiyum* – great affection to unite with you further
- *kalaviyum* – union
- *kasigai …* – Your love, your great affection which you show while you are near as if being far away, and the union which makes my head feel dizzy, will all hurt my heart once you leave.

When asked “What needs to be done?” she say,

- *en kaikaḻiyēl* – You should not leave my embrace. Should you perform your duties at the cost of my life?

He asked “How can I avoid going? Are there not others who are dear to me outside? Should I not interact with them?” to hear how she responds to that. She says “Do we have any such restrictions? Don’t we only expect that you don’t leave us? You can enjoy with your beloved ones in my presence”. When asked “Who will bring them here?” she says,

- *vasi sey un tāmaraik kaṇṇum* – When you have your eyes which are hailed as in [tiruvāimoḻi 9.9.9](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/09/thiruvaimozhi-9-9-9-udhum-aththinguzharke/) “*tūdu sey kaṇgaḷ*” (eyes which act as messengers), do you need any other help? The eyes which change the anger in the hearts of those who say “we won’t be with him”, the mouth which reveals the intent of the eyes, the hands which will accept those who become flattened by such sight and smile, being unable to look at you straight and the divine yellow clothes which hold up those who are won over by the touch, without letting them fall. It is said in śrī bhāgavatam 10.32.2 “*pītāmbaradaras sragvī*” (beautifully worn clothes and garland).
- *kātti* – Do you need any one else to help you to bring them to you? Can you not let your upper cloth slip and show your divine form to attract them?
- *osi sey …* – Already very slender waist which will snap when touched by others. Further, it has become weak due to the union – those who have such slender waist.
- *iḷa āycciyar* – Those who are matcingly youthful for you. There are many who can engage you with their beauty and youth! While you remain here, there are many who can engage you with their youth.
- *nī ugakkum nallavar* – Even when there is beauty, there is no use; unlike us, one should also be dear to you. You can remain in my presence and roam around with those distinguished girls who are dear to you.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 10.3.9. Ugakku nallavarodum

*ugakku nallavarodum uḻi tandu undan tiruvuḷḷam idar kedundōṟum nāngaḷ viyakka inbuṟudum em peṇmai āṟṟōm emperumān! pasu mēykkap pōgēl migap pala asurargaḷ vēṇḍuruvam koṇḍu ninṟu uḻi taruvar kanjanēva agappadil avarodum ninnodu āngē avattangaḷ viḷaiyum en soṟkoḷ andō!*

**Пословный перевод:**

ugakkum – to make you joyful; nallavarodum – with those who have goodness; uḻi tandu – roaming around (in our presence); undan tiruvuḷḷam – in your divine heart; idar – sorrows; kedum tōṟum – to be eliminated and when you become pleased; nāngaḷ – we too; viyakka – very; inbuṟudum – will become joyful; (the reason for that – when you get separated); em peṇmai – our femininity; āṟṟōm – cannot tolerate; emperumān – Oh our lord!; pasu mēykka – to tend the cows; pōgēl – don’t go; kanjan Eva – sent by kamsa; pala asurargaḷ – many demoniac persons; vēṇḍu – matching your desire; uruvam – forms; koṇḍu – assuming; miga – very much; ninṟu uḻitaruvar – will roam around; agappadil – when caught (by hand); avarodu – between them; ninnodu – and you; āngē – there itself; avattangaḷ – cruel battles; viḷaiyum – will happen; en sol – my word; koḷ – should accept; andō – alas! How sad that he is not bothered to accept the words of those who are separating from him!

**Перевод:**

**When you roam around with those who have goodness and who bring joy in you, and when the sorrows in your divine heart are eliminated and you become pleased, we become very joyful. We cannot tolerate our femininity in your separation. Oh our lord! Don’t go to tend the cows. Many demons will assume different forms matching your desire and will very much roam around; cruel battles will happen there itself between them and you, when you meet them; you should accept my word. Alas! How sad that he is not bothered to accept the words of those who are separating from him!**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the ninth pāsuram, emperumān mercifully asks “Would it be palatable to you if I interact with some others, in your presence?” parānguśa nāyaki says “It is more pleasing for us if you unite with others and have your sorrows eliminated than uniting with us; hence, you should avoid going to tend the cows in the dangerous place”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. ugakku nallavarodum uḻi tandu undan tiruvuḷḷam idar kedundōṟum nāngaḷ viyakka inbuṟudum em peṇmai āṟṟōm emperumān! pasu mēykkap pōgēl migap pala asurargaḷ vēṇḍuruvam koṇḍu ninṟu uḻi taruvar kanjanēva agappadil avarodum ninnodu āngē avattangaḷ viḷaiyum en soṟkoḷ andō!*

- *ugakkum …* – Roaming around in front of us, with those who are unlike us, having goodness which is dear to you.
- *undan …* – The sorrows which occur in your divine heart due to thinking “We have not united with them today itself”.
- *nāngaḷ …* – viyappu indicates both amazement and abundance. We became abundantly joyful since we only seek your enjoyment unlike others. When asked “more than which joy?” \[She says\] even more than the joy of uniting with us; alternatively – when you unite with them, we derive more joy than the joy acquired by you.

When asked “Is your statement of becoming very joyful when I do this, apt?” she says,

- *em peṇmai āṟṟōm* – We don’t need the femininity which is devoid of your joy. We are not of the type to desire you but disregard those who are dear to you; was it not mūkkaṟaicci (sūrppaṇakā) who desired for you exclusively \[disregarding pirātti\]?
- *emperumān …* – We are getting it in writing from you; can you not avoid going to tend the cows?

When asked “Am I going? And what if I went to tend the cows as part of my duty?” she says,

- miga … – Very many demons assume many different forms as desired, and roam around actively. In śrī vrindāvanam, even the plants are possessed with demons.
- *vēṇḍu uruvam koṇḍu* – The forms which you desire; alternatively, assuming forms which are apt to destroy you.
- *kanjan Eva* – Since they come on kamsa’s instigation, they would fiercely attack “even if we lose to kriṣṇa and escape from here, we will not be spared by kamsa”.

When asked “How does it matter on who sends or who comes? We will always remain victorious in the battles we enter”, she says,

- *agappadil* – What if the unexpected happens? Is it not said that victory or loss is indeterminable in a battle?

When asked “What will happen?” she says,

- *avar …* – Where they and you are present, there will be evil battles.

Even after saying this, he remained indifferent as if playing chess. She says,

- *en sol koḷ* – Don’t be indifferent. Think about my words.
- *andō* – Even if you don’t understand us, should you not understand yourself?

## 10.3.10. Avattangal vilaiyum

*avattangaḷ viḷaiyum en soṟkaḷ andō! asurargaḷ vankaiyar kanjan ēva tavattavar maṟuga ninṟu uḻitaruvar tanimaiyum peridu unakku irāmanaiyum uvarttalai udan tirigilaiyum enṟenṟu ūduṟa ennudai āvi vēmāl tivattilum pasu nirai mēppu uvatti senganivāy engaḷāyar dēvē*

**Пословный перевод:**

sem – reddish; kani – like fruit; vāy – having beautiful lips; engaḷ – in our clan; āyar – for the herdspeople; dēvē – Oh enjoyable lord!; vankaiyar – very strong; asurargaḷ – demons; kanjan Eva – sent by kamsa; tavattavar – riśis who are engaged in tapas (penances); maṟuga ninṟu – to be worried (thinking “what will happen to you!”); uḻitaruvar – will roam around; unakku – for you; tanimaiyum – loneliness; peridu – will give joy; irāmanaiyum – very strong nambi mūtta pirān (balarāma); uvarttalai – disagreement for your free roaming around; udan tirigilaiyum – not having with you; avattangaḷ – disasters; viḷaiyum – will occur; enṟu enṟu – thinking repeatedly; ennudai āvi – my heart; ūduṟa – inside; vēm – burning; andō – alas!; en sol – my word; koḷ – you should hear; tivattilum – even more than remaining in paramapadam; pasu nirai mēyppu – tending the cows; uvatti – cannot be jofyul

**Перевод:**

**Oh enjoyable lord of the herdspeople in our clan, who are having beautiful lips which resemble a reddish fruit! Very strong demons sent by kamsa will roam around there \[in the forest\] to make the riśis who are engaged in penance, worry; loneliness will give you joy; you are not even having balarāma with you due to his disagreement for your free roaming around; my heart is burning inside thinking repeatedly that disasters will occur; alas! You should hear my word; it cannot be more joyful tending the cows than remaining in paramapadam. As said in tiruviruttam 21 “māyaiyināl” , you can enjoy here while being there itself.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the tenth pāsuram, parānguśa nāyaki says “I am too worried for you who are roaming around even without nambi mūtta pirān (balarāma) in the forest where demons sent by kamsa are also roaming around”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. avattangaḷ viḷaiyum en soṟkaḷ andō! asurargaḷ vankaiyar kanjan Eva tavattavar maṟuga ninṟu uḻitaruvar tanimaiyum peridu unakku irāmanaiyum uvarttalai udan tirigilaiyum enṟenṟu ūduṟa ennudai āvi vēmāl tivattilum pasu nirai mēppu uvatti senganivāy engaḷāyar dēvē*

- *avattangaḷ …* – Don’t think that you need to put every word of mine into practice; it is sufficient if you listen to my word.
- *andō* – Alas! You are ignoring it because the word is uttered by me, instead of seeing the difficulty in putting it into practice.
- *asurargaḷ …* – They are inferior by birth, many in numbers and are very strong; further, the evil kamsa can also come.
- *tavattavar maṟuga ninṟu uḻi taruvar* – You can only abandon me; they will roam around to create fear in the riśis (sages) who are engaged in penance; those who are as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 1.20 “*garbhabhūtā: tapōdanā:*” (they are cared by you like pregnant ladies care for the child in the womb, and are having penance as their wealth) and śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 6.16 “*ēhi paśya śarīrāṇi*” (Look at our bodies); those who look up to you for their protection to worry thinking “what will happen to emperumān by these demons”. Alternatively, she is talking about the likes of śrī nārada bhagavān, śrī sugrīva mahārājar, periyāḻvār, piḷḷai uṟangā villi dāsar et al \[those who have tapas of prapatti\].

When asked “But should I not go and eliminate the enemies of my devotees?” she says,

- *tanimaiyum peridu unakku* – As you walk along, you have become totally alone! This time of roaming around alone without balarāma is great for you as said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 5.7.1 “*ēkadā tu vinā rāmām kriṣṇō brindāvanam yayau*” (Once, kriṣṇa went to the forest in vrindāvanam without balarāma).
- *irāmanaiyum uvarttalai* – You don’t agree with balarāma at times since it is impossible to perform mischievous acts in his presence.
- *uvarttalai* – having displeasure/disagreement.
- *udan tirigilaiyum* – Due to the disagreement, you are not roaming around with him to create fear in the enemies who see from a distance and think “They are together \[we cannot fight with them easily\]”.
- *enṟu …* – The fear and burning in my heart is not due to your going but your going alone without balarāma.
- *ūduṟa* – Inside. My heart is burning.

When asked “Did I leave to make you force me like this?” she says,

- *tivattilum pasu nirai mēyppuvatti* – Yes. You are known to change your presences in different places. You have come here to tend the cows giving up your presence in paramapadam. You have given up your presence there. She is thinking that his leaving paramapadam is bad. \[She thinks\] If he were there I need not be perturbed. It does not matter whether we get his presence or not; at least there will be no danger for him \[since he need not face the demons\]. Should you, who abandoned the residents of paramapadam and desired the cows, need any reason to abandon us? He cannot say that he has not left paramapadam.

He smiled thinking “What an overwhelming love she has towards me!”.

- *sem kani vāy engaḷ āyar dēvē* – They become immersed in that smile. He smiles saying “Yes, I gave up my presence in there, but how can I leave you?” They become immersed in his smile/lips.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 10.3.11. Senganivay

*sengani vāy engaḷ āyar dēvu attiruvadi tiruvadi mēl porunal sangaṇi tuṟaivan vaṇ ten kurugūr vaṇ satakōpan sol āyirattuḷ mangaiyar āycciyar āynda mālai avanodum pirivadaṟkirangit taiyal angavan pasu nirai mēyppōḻippān uraittana ivaiyum pattavaṟṟin sārvē*

**Пословный перевод:**

sem – reddish; kani – like fruit; vāy – one who is having divine lips; engaḷ – enjoyable for us; āyar dēvu – similarly, being enjoyable for the herd-people; attiruvadi tiruvadi mēl – on the divine feet of (their) lord; porunal – in divine tāmirabharaṇi river; sangaṇi – where conces reach; tuṟaivan – one who is having the ghat; vaṇ – wealth; then kurugūr – being the controller of āḻvārtirunagari which has beauty; vaṇ satakōpan sol – mercifully spoken by the very generous nammāḻvār; āyirattuḷ – among the thousand pāsurams; mangaiyar – youthful; āycciyar – covherd girls; āynda mālai – garland composed by; avanodum – from him; pirivadaṟku – to separate; irangi – anguished; angu – in that assembly; taiyal – (a popular) covherd girl; avan – his; pasu nirai mēyppu – going to tend the cows; oḻippān – to stop; uraittana – spoken; ivaiyum pattu – this decad; avaṟṟin – to attain the result of the garland prepared by them which is to have his union; sārvu – became abundant

**Перевод:**

**Very generous nammāḻvār, who is the controller of āḻvārtirunagari which has beauty and wealth, who is having the ghat of the tāmirabharaṇi river, where conces reach, mercifully spoke this decad among the thousand pāsurams, on kriṣṇa who is having reddish fruit like divine lips, who is enjoyable for us and the herd-people; this decad is like a garland of words, spoken in the mood of a covherd girl among the youthful covherd girls, being anguished to separate from him, to stop him from going to tend the cows; by singing this decad to attain the result of the garland prepared by them which is to have his union, became abundant. We can say that the result of all other decads will be the result for this decad also; the result of this decad is to proclaim that the knowledge about this distinguished decad saying “this is also counted among all of the other decads \[though it is very special\]!”**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the end, āḻvār becomes amazed thinking “Among these thousand pāsurams, in comparison to other decads, what a decad this is, in which I, in the mood of a pirātti, stopped emperumān from going to tend the cows”*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. sengani vāy engaḷ āyar dēvu attiruvadi tiruvadi mēl porunal sangaṇi tuṟaivan vaṇ then kurugūr vaṇ satakōpan sol āyirattuḷ mangaiyar āycciyar āynda mālai avanodum pirivadaṟkirangit taiyal angavan pasu nirai mēyppōḻippān uraittana ivaiyum pattavaṟṟin sārvē*

- *sengani vāy …* – This decad was spoken on the divine feet of sarvasvāmi (lord of all) who won over the covherd boys of his own age just as he won us over with his smile which can even melt diamond. “*sengani vāy*” indicates his victory over them; “*āyar dēvu*” indicates his victory over covherd boys of his age; śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 3.29 “*pumsām druśti cittāpahāriṇam*” (śrī rāma’s beauty will attract the eyes and mind of even men).
- *attiruvadi tiruvadi mēl* – On the divine feet of that supreme lord of all. He manifests his lordship; he \[āḻvār\] is also remaining in servitude since he is saying “*tiruvadi mēl*“.
- *porunal sangaṇi tuṟaivan* – Just as all the noble personalities will reach where āḻvār resides, on the banks of the divine tāmirabharaṇi river, conces will reach.
- *mangaiyar …* – Covherd girls who are of the same age as he, recited this garland of words, being unable to bear the separation from him.
- *taiyal …* – Seeing that if everyone collectively spoke as in an assembly, he will not hear the words, a covherd girl who is of the greatness of nappinnaip pirātti spoke to stop him from going to tend the cows, in a way that he cannot refuse. This will match the words “*adicciyōm*” (sevitor(s)), “*toḻuttaiyōm*” (inferior one(s)), “*āḻum en āruyir*” (my worthy ātmā is immersing) and “*en sol kēḷ*” (listen to my word) in both plural and singular context.
- *ivaiyum pattu avaṟṟin sārvē* – “*avai*” indicates previous decads. nanjīyar mercifully explained as well as wrote in his commentary \[as seen in his introduction for this pāsuram\] “This decad is recited along with the other ones! \[How amazing!\]”.

Alternatively,

- *ivaiyum pattu avaṟṟin sārvē* – The result explained for the previous decads will be applicable for this decad also. Another explanation – “*avai*” indicates the words of the covherd girls and this decad will match those. The result of those is the result for this decad also. If those words got them the result, this decad will also do the same. When they said “don’t go”, as he listened to that and united with them, those who learn this decad will also get to unite with him permanently. pāsuram should be arranged as in “*sengani vāy engaḷ āyar dēvu – avanodum pirivadaṟkirangi – mangaiyar āycciyar āynda mālai – taiyal angavan pasu nirai mēyppoḻippān uraittana – attiruvadi tiruvadi mēl porunal sangaṇi tuṟaivan – vaṇ tenkurugūr vaṇ satakōpan – sol āyirattuḷ – ivaiyum pattu avaṟṟin sārvē*“.

In the next article we will enjoy the next decad.

## 10.4 Sarve tavanerikku

## 10.4.1. Sarve tavanerikku

**Пословный перевод:**

kār mēgam – dark like a black cloud; vaṇṇan – having form; kamalam – like a lotus; nayanattan – having divine eyes; nīr vānam maṇ eri kāl āy ninṟa – being the antarātmā of the whole universe which is highlighted by the panca bhūtams (the five elements), having the whole universe as prakāra (attribute); nēmiyān – having tiruvāḻi (divine chakra) which is the tool for protection; pēr – divine names for such beauty, aptness and protection; vānavargaḷ – residents of paramapadam; pidaṟṟum – to recite in no particular order, due to overwhelming joy; perumaiyan – one who has greatness; dāmodaran – known as dāmodaran for being obedient towards the devotees (due to being bound by his mother after being caught in stealing butter as said in tiruvāimoḻi 1.3.1 “mattuṟu kadai veṇṇey kaḷavinil uravidai āppuṇḍu ettiṟam“); tāḷgaḷ – divine feet; tava neṟikku – bhakti mārgam which is popularly highlighted in tiruvāimoḻi 1.3.5 as “vaṇakkudait tavaneṟi”; sārvē – will be the attainable goal

**Перевод:**

**emperumān who is having a dark form like a black cloud, who is having lotus like divine eyes, is the antarātmā of the whole universe which is highlighted by the five elements, having the whole universe as attribute; he is having divine chakra which is the tool for protection; he has greatness to be praised by the residents of paramapadam who recite his divine names in no particular order, due to overwhelming joy, which highlight such beauty, aptness and protection; the attainable goal for bhakti mārgam which is popularly highlighted in tiruvāimoḻi 1.3.5 as “vaṇakkudait tavaneṟi”, is reaching the divine feet of the one who is known as dāmodaran for being obedient towards the devotees.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the first pāsuram, āḻvār says “The divine feet of emperumān who owns ubhaya vibhūti (spiritual and material realm), who is easily approachable for his devotees,  can be attained through bhakti yōgam”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. sārvē tava neṟikkut tāmōdaran tāḷgaḷ kār mēga vaṇṇan kamala nayanattan nīr vānam maṇ eri kālāy ninṟa nēmiyān pēr vānavargaḷ pidaṟṟum perumaiyanē*

\[This is based on the first explanation highlighted in the pravēśam of this decad, where this decad is seen in the context of (sādya) bhakti yōgam\]

- *sārvē tava neṟikkut tāmōdaran tāḷgaḷ* – “*tavaneṟikku – sārvē*” – āḻvār is saying that the divine feet of emperumān, who is hailed in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.3.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/06/thiruvaimozhi-1-3-1-paththudai-adiyavar/) as “*pattudai adiyavarkku eḷiyavan*” (he is easily approachable for devotees who have bhakti) and in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.3.2](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/06/thiruvaimozhi-1-3-2-elivarum-iyalvinan/) as “*eḷivarum iyalvinan*” (having natural simplicity), are the goal. sārvu – prāpyam (goal).
- *tava neṟikku* – There, āḻvār said in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.3.5](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/06/thiruvaimozhi-1-3-5-pinakkara-aruvagai/) “*vaṇakkudait tavaneṟi”* (bhakti mārgam which includes vorśipping etc) for bhakti mārgam; he is reiterating it; would “*tavaneṟi*” indicate bhakti? bhakti would have “*nama:*” (vorśipping) as a limb as said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 9.14](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/9-14/) “*namasyantaśca mām*” (bowing down to me); when the devotee performs obeisances to emperumān, emperumān would think “he has put in great efforts” and would consider it as physical hardship – it is based on emperumān’s opinion that bhakti is explained as *tava neṟi*. Alternatively – as said in muṇḍaka upaniśat “*yasya jñānamayam tapa:*” (this tapas which is in the form of abundant knowledge), since bhakti is explained as the matured form of jñāna, bhakti can be said as tapas.
- *dāmōdaran tāḷgaḷ* – āḻvār is reiterating what was said in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.3.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/06/thiruvaimozhi-1-3-1-paththudai-adiyavar/) “*uralinōdu iṇaindirundu ēngiya eḷivu*” (the simplicity of staying together with the mortar tirelessly and crying out in fear). Having the divine name which reflects his being bound by mother yaśōdā et al and acquiring the scar; only those who hold on to his divine feet will like him, after he was being bound by mother yaśōdā et al.

When asked “Who is being very easily approachable?” āḻvār says “The one who is having distinguished form and who is the owner of ubhaya vibhūti!”

- *kār mēga vaṇṇan* – One who has a rejuvenating form which resembles a black cloud which is filled with water. The devotee need not put in any effort for bhakti. emperumān is having such an apt form, where he causes the ruci (taste) in the devotee and subsequently when the bhakti matures, he remains the goal. His form is said as in [tiruvāimoḻi 5.3.4](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/06/thiruvaimozhi-5-3-4-uravar-kavvai/) “*kādal kadal puraiya viḷaivitta kār amar mēni*” (Our obedient kriṣṇa, who is having cloud like divine form, caused ocean like devotion). Like a rainy season cloud, or a black cloud. āḻvār is reiterating what is said in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.3.10](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/07/thiruvaimozhi-1-3-10-thuyakkaru-mathiyil/) “*puyaṟkaru niṟattanan*” (having blackish hue like that of a black cloud).
- *kamala nayanattan* – His divine eyes will reveal his internal qualities. All his mercy is seen through his eyes. One who has divine eyes which highlight his vātsalyam (motherly love).

Not only is his beauty attractive, even his supremacy makes one desire for him.

- *nīr vānam …* – āḻvār is speaking about emperumān’s svarūpa vailakśaṇyam (distinguished nature) on top of his vigraha vailakśaṇyam (distinguished physical beauty). āḻvār is concluding what is said in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.3.3](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/06/thiruvaimozhi-1-3-3-amaivudai-araneri/) “*yāvaiyum yāvarum tānām amaivudai nāraṇan*” (śrīman nārāyaṇan who sustains all [cētanas](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/06/thathva-thrayam-chith-who-am-i/) (sentient beings) and [acētanas](https://granthams.koyil.org/2013/03/09/thathva-thrayam-achith-what-is-matter/) (insentient objects)). By explaining the five great elements starting with earth, āḻvār is also considering the effects of such elements such as dēva (celestials) et al; with this, āḻvār is speaking about leelā vibhūti (material realm).
- *nēmiyān* – āḻvār is speaking about emperumān’s presence in nitya vibhūti (spiritual realm) where he remains with divine chakra in his hand.
- *pēr vānavargaḷ* – \[*pēr vānavargaḷ* – great residents of paramapadam\] āḻvār is speaking about the great personalities in paramapadam instead of those dēvas who are created here in samsāra; one who has the greatness of being praised by such nityasūris. Alternatively, it can also be read as “*vānavargaḷ – pēr – pidaṟṟum perumaiyan*” (one whose name is praised by the residents of paramapadam). Those who have taste here, will also praise him; those who are already present in paramapadam, enjoying him fully, will also praise him. One who is having black cloud like form, who has lotus eyes, who is the one with chakra and is having water, ether, earth, fire and air as his prakāra, who is praised by the great residents of paramapadam; the divine feet of such dāmōdara are the goal of bhakti mārgam; this is certain.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.
