## 10.4.2. Perumaiyane

*perumaiyanē vānattimaiyōrkkum kāṇḍaṟku arumaiyanē āgattaṇaiyādārkkenṟum tirumey uṟaiginṟa sengaṇ māl nāḷum irumai vinai kadindu ingennai āḷginṟānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vānattu – residents of higher worlds; imaiyōrkkum – brahmā et al; perumaiyan – having greatness (beyond them); āgattu – in the heart; aṇaiyādārkku – for those who don’t think; kāṇḍaṟku – to see; arumaiyan – one who is difficult; enṟum – always; tiru – lakshmi; mey – in the divine form; uṟaiginṟa – due to eternally residing; sem gaṇ – having reddish divine eyes which highlight ultimate wealth; māl – great lord; irumai vinai kadindu – eliminating my karma in the form of puṇya (virtues) and pāpa (vices); ingu – in this material realm; nāḷum – every day; ennai – me; āḷginṟān – accepting my service

**Перевод:**

**emperumān is having greatness beyond brahmā et al who are the residents of higher worlds; he is difficult to be seen by those who don’t think about him in their heart; since lakshmi is eternally residing in his divine form, he is the great lord who is always having reddish divine eyes which highlight ultimate wealth; every day, such emperumān is accepting my service in this material realm, after eliminating my karma in the form of puṇya and pāpa.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the second pāsuram, āḻvār speaks about his own benefit saying “sarvēśvaran who is the lord of śrī mahālakśmi eliminated my hurdles and is accepting my service in this world, everyday”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. perumaiyanē vānattimaiyōrkkum kāṇḍaṟku arumaiyanē āgattaṇaiyādārkkenṟum tirumey uṟaiginṟa sengaṇ māl nāḷum irumai vinai kadindu ingennai āḷginṟānē*

- *perumaiyanē vānattu imaiyōrkkum* – āḻvār is reiterating what was explained in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.3.3](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/06/thiruvaimozhi-1-3-3-amaivudai-araneri/) “*amaivudai mudalkedal odividai aṟanilam aduvām amaivudai amarar*” (dēvas such as brahmā et al have darmam (virtuous path) that leads to proper result, have attained high position to be engaged in creation, annihilation etc and are very capable/intelligent). While others are present in lower worlds, they are residing in distinguished worlds; they think highly of themselves as being responsible for creation etc; emperumān is so great that even such brahmā et al need to surrender unto him and retain their true nature.
- *vānattu* – This \[being in higher world\] is the only distinction they have; when compared with him, there is no difference between us and them. They are more heavily immersed in samsāram than we are. For us, we need to give up only what we hold on to, but for them, they need to give up the whole worlds which are under their control.
- *kāṇḍaṟku …* – When he himself pursues us, for those who reject him, it will not be possible to see him. No need to search for the sambandam (relationship \[between us and him\]) today; the difference lies in whether one desires to attain him or not. āḻvār is reiterating what is said in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.3.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/06/thiruvaimozhi-1-3-1-paththudai-adiyavar/) “*piṟargaḷukku ariya vittagan*” (difficult to attain for those others who are not interested in him).
- *enṟum tirumey uṟaiginṟa* – āḻvār is explaining the nitya yōgam (eternal togetherness indicated in “*math*“) in rahasyam (dvaya mahā mantram). [tiruvāimoḻi 6.10.10](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/06/thiruvaimozhi-6-10-10-agalagillen-part-1/) “*agalagillēn*” (I will not leave his chest even for a moment). āḻvār is reiterating what is said in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.3.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/06/thiruvaimozhi-1-3-1-paththudai-adiyavar/) “*malar magaḷ virumbum*” (one who is dear to śrī mahālakśmi). One who is always having periya pirāttiyār residing in his divine form.
- *sem kaṇ* – Due to eternal togetherness with her, his divine eyes are always fresh like watered green field.
- *māl* – The greatness acquired by having her as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 37.18 “*yasyasā janakātmajā – apramēyam hi tattēja:*” (One cannot measure the greatness of the one who is married to the daughter of śrī janaka); āḻvār is reiterating what is said in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.3.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/06/thiruvaimozhi-1-3-1-paththudai-adiyavar/) “*arum peṟal adigaḷ*” (our great lord, who is difficult to attain).
- *nāḷum …* – Eliminating my karmas which are in the form of puṇya and pāpa, he accepted the kainkaryam which will be done after leaving this samsāra and reaching paramapadam, in this samsāra, everyday. There he will conduct the sustenance of the ātmās by letting them experience his qualities; here we will sustain with the knowledge about his qualities.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 10.4.3. Alginran aliyan

*āḷginṟān āḻiyān ārāl kuṟaivudaiyam mīḷginṟadillaip piṟavit tuyar kadindōm vāḷ keṇḍai oṇ kaṇ madappinnnai tan kēḷvan tāḷ kaṇḍu koṇḍu en talai mēl punaindēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

āḻiyān – having the divine chakra in the divine hand; āḷginṟān – protecting us by eliminating the hurdles; piṟavit tuyar – all sorrows starting with birth etc; kadindōm – we got rid of; mīḷginṟadu illai – (they) won’t return; ārāl kuṟaivu udaiyōm – we have no worries caused by self or others; vāḷ – (due to sharpness and vastness) sword; keṇḍai – resembling keṇḍai fish (due to the coolness and splendour); oṇ – distinguished; kaṇ – having eyes; madam – complete with internal qualities such as shyness; pinnai than – for nappinnaip pirātti; kēḷvan – beloved lord’s; tāḷ – divine feet; kaṇḍu koṇḍu – saw; en talai mēl – on my head; punaindēn – held

**Перевод:**

**emperumān who is having the divine chakra in the divine hand, is protecting us by eliminating the hurdles; we got rid of all of our sorrows starting with birth etc; they won’t return; we have no worries caused by self or others; I saw the divine feet of the lord, who is the beloved consort of nappinnaip pirātti whose distinguished eyes resemble sword and keṇḍai fish, and who is complete with internal qualities such as shyness, and held those \[divine feet\] on my head.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the third pāsuram, āḻvār says “Eliminating my bondage in samsāra, seeing the divine feet of the lord of nappinnaip pirātti, I decorated my head with those divine feet”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. āḷginṟān āḻiyān ārāl kuṟaivudaiyam mīḷginṟadillaip piṟavit tuyar kadindōm vāḷ keṇḍai oṇ kaṇ madappinnnai than kēḷvan tāḷ kaṇḍu koṇḍu en talai mēl punaindēnē*

- *āḷginṟān āḻiyān* – emperumān, with his hand holding the weapon, eliminated my hurdles and accepted my service; the apt sarvēśvara is accepting the service. There are some who are engaging in other upāyams which anyway depend on him, who will decorate and indulge in those upāyams; there are some others who depend upon the sharpness of emperumān’s arrows as said in [nānmugan tiruvandādi 8](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/06/nanmugan-thiruvandhadhi-8/) “*kūrambanallāl*” and the sharpness of his divine chakra as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 2.4.9](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/03/thiruvaimozhi-2-4-9-patta-podhu/) “*sudar vatta vāy nudi nēmiyīr*“. Some incapable persons (those who engage in other upāyams) try to reach him through other upāyams which are to be performed by them; others (prapannas) try to reach him through sarvēśvaran who is omnipotent and already established. He weakened the role of other upāyams and said “You should surrender unto me” \[in carama ślōkam, [śrī bhagavat gītā 18.66](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/18-66/)\].
- *ārāl kuṟaivu udaiyam* – Am I depending on myself to lose it? Am I interested in being in this samsāram where I can be pursued by yama et al? Am I depending on other upāyams such as bhakti yōgam etc where even after pursuing them, we have to depend on him ultimately? āḻvār is saying “*ārāl*” (by whom?) since he has the firm understanding that the result will be granted by a cētana (sentient \[bhagavān\]).
- *mīḷginṟadu illai* – There is no return, anymore.
- *piṟavit tuyar kadindōm* – We drove away the sorrows of samsāram. vaidika putras (the sons of a brāhmaṇa), even after reaching paramapadam, since they did not go there with ruci (desire/taste \[for the goal\]), returned like a wooden log caught in the ocean tides. Is there any question of returning for āḻvār who has the taste to go there and has been granted paramapadam by emperumān himself as said in tiruvāimoḻi 1.1.1 “*mayarvaṟa madinalam aruḷinan*” (blessed unblemiśed knowledge and devotion)? āḻvār himself is saying “*kadindōm*” here; for the task which emperumān promised to fulfil, one can say as in [śrī bhagavat gītā 18.73](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/18-73/) “*stitō’smi*” (standing firm, with realisation of truth).
- *vāḷ …* – It appears that when his svātantriyam (free will) rises, enjoyable food containers will be blocked \[i.e. nappinnaip pirātti’s merciful glance will be blocked. That is, if he is not blessing me, he will not get nappinnaip pirātti’s merciful glance\]. Now, can I abandon him? \[No\] ōr, can he abandon me? \[No\] Unlike my pāratantriyam (total dependence), is his āśrita pāratantriyam (total dependence on his devotees) having any shortcoming? If his svātantriyam rises, he will lose his food \[that is, her merciful glance\]. \[Is nappinnaip pirātti’s merciful glance, his food?\] periya tirumoḻi 8.10.1 “*maṇa nōkkam uṇḍān*” (he consumed her glance). One who is the beloved consort of nappinnaip pirātti who is having radiant, fish like divine eyes from which one cannot take their eyes off after seeing once, and who is complete in internal qualities.
- *tāḷ kaṇḍu koṇḍu* – āḻvār is highlighting the reason for the merciful glance of nappinnaip pirātti.
- *en talai mēl punaindēn* – āḻvār is highlighting the enjoyability that is similar to one washing the hair and remaining ready to decorate the hair with flowers, as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.1.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/03/thiruvaimozhi-1-1-1-uyarvara-uyarnalam/) “*tuyaraṟu sudaradi toḻudeḻu*” (worship his radiant divine feet and rise), [tiruvāimoḻi 9.2.2](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/06/thiruvaimozhi-9-2-2-kudik-kidandhu/) “*pāda pangayamē talaikkaṇiyāy*” (your lotus feet are the decoration for my head) and [tiruvāimoḻi 4.3.6](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/01/thiruvaimozhi-4-3-6-kala-chakkaraththodu/) “*kōlamām en sennikku …*” (your infinitely enjoyable lotus flower like divine feet which make sounds of bravery are the shining radiant decoration for my head). I became fulfilled on attaining what I prayed for in [tiruvāimoḻi 2.9.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/06/thiruvaimozhi-2-9-1-emma-vittu/) “*nin semmā pādapaṟput talai sērttu*” (placing your reddish, divine lotus feet on my head),

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 10.4.4. Talai mel

*talai mēl punaindēn saraṇangaḷ ālin ilai mēl tuyinṟān imaiyōr vaṇanga malai mēl tān ninṟu en manattuḷ irundānai nilai pērkkalāgāmai niccittirundēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

saraṇangaḷ – his divine feet; talai mēl – on my head; punaindēn – have placed; ālin ilai mēl – on a banyan leaf; tuyinṟān – the protector of all, who is mercifully resting; imaiyōr – nityasūris; vaṇanga – to follow him and worship him; malai mēl – on tirumalai (tiruvēngadam); tān – without any other expectation; ninṟu – mercifully stood; en manattuḷ – entering my heart; irundānai – remained firm; nilai – the firmness in such presence; pērkkal āgāmai – unable to break; niccittu – determined; irundēn – (due to that) remained contented

**Перевод:**

**I have placed his divine feet on my head; the protector of all who is mercifully resting on a banyan leaf, mercifully stood on tirumalai without any expectation, to have the nityasūris follow him and worship him; I remained contented having determined that such emperumān has entered my heart, remained firmly there and that his firmness in such presence is unbreakable.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fourth pāsuram, āḻvār says “I remain contented having determined that no one can separate sarvēśvaran who is residing in my heart, from me”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. talai mēl punaindēn saraṇangaḷ ālin ilai mēl tuyinṟān imaiyōr vaṇanga malai mēl tān ninṟu en manattuḷ irundānai nilai pērkkalāgāmai niccittirundēnē*

- *talai mēl punaindēn saraṇangaḷ* – I got to decorate my head with those divine feet which are said in tirukkuṟundāndagam 6 as “*amarar sennippūvinai*” (the divine feet borne by nityasūris on their heads). Instead of just praying to have them, I got to keep those divine feet on my head.

Now, āḻvār is explaining the efforts of emperumān to facilitate āḻvār getting this result; emperumān performed penance staying in the beautiful pond \[deluge\] as said in periya tirumadal “*vaṇ tadattin uḷ kidandum*” to facilitate the āḻvār getting this result.

- *ālin ilai mēl tuyinṟān* – He did not see many who would pursue bhagavān to attain the result; he thought of engaging in an activity which will become famous; we have not seen anyone who would reject this. After becoming satisfied with such stay on the banyan leaf, he descended along with the nityasūris to tirumalai and stood there; after becoming satisfied with that also, he arrived and entered āḻvār’s heart; since there is no one to reject him here, he stood there like a plant/tree. emperumān entered āḻvār’s heart as said in [mūnṟām tiruvandādi 76](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/05/munram-thiruvandhadhi-76/) “*poruppidaiyē ninṟum punal kuḷittum*” (standing on the hilltop and taking bath in the river). He did as said in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 5.4.9 “*panikkadalil paḷḷi kōḷaip paḻaga vittu ōdi vandu en manak kadalil vāḻa valla*” (giving up the reclining posture on the ādiśēśa in kśīrābdi, he came running to the ocean of my heart). Such emperumān.
- *nilai pērkkal āgāmai* – I tried in many ways to drive him out, but he did not listen to that.
- *niccittirundēn* – I remained as said in taittirīya upaniśat “*na bibhēti*” (need not be afraid). When emperumān’s nature is known, there is nothing wrong for the ātmā to remain fearless. taittirīya upaniśat says “*ānandam brahmaṇō vidvān nabibhēti kutaścana iti*” – After knowing that one’s sorrow will be drowned in his bliss, there is nothing wrong in saying that one’s sorrow will be eliminated. *kutaścana* – one need not fear for mistakes committed knowingly \[Though such surrendered person will not commit mistakes knowingly\].

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 10.4.5. Niccittirunden

*niccittirundēn ennenjam kaḻiyāmai kaiccakkarattaṇṇal kaḷvam peridudaiyan meyccappadān piṟarkku mey pōlum poy vallan naccap padum namakku nāgattaṇaiyānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

en nenjam – my heart; kaḻiyāmai – nature of not leaving; niccittirundēn – I firmly believed; cakkaram – tiruvāḻi (sudarśana chakra which is both protection and enjoyable); kai – having in his hand; aṇṇal – being the distinguished lord; kaḷvam peridudaiyan – being in my heart, having joy in speaking about his favours done to me without my knowledge; piṟarkku meyccappadān – not glorified by others; mey pōlum – just as doing everything truthfully for his devotees; poy vallan – one who can be untruthful for others who are not devoted to him; nāgattaṇaiyān – anantaśāyi (one who is reclining on the serpent mattress) who is having the nature of being united with devotees; namakku – for us; naccap padum – is desirable as the ultimate goal

**Перевод:**

**I firmly believed in his nature of not leaving my heart; he is the distinguished lord, having the divine chakra in his hand, being in my heart, having joy in speaking about his favours done to me without my knowledge, and not glorified by others as much as I have done;  just as doing everything truthfully for his devotees, he can be untruthful for others who are not devoted to him; such anantaśāyi (one who is reclining on the serpent mattress) who is having the nature of being united with devotees, is desirable for us as the ultimate goal.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fifth pāsuram, āḻvār says “It is impossible for anyone to know what emperumān is mercifully thinking to do for me”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. niccittirundēn ennenjam kaḻiyāmai kaiccakkarattaṇṇal kaḷvam peridudaiyan meyccappadān piṟarkku mey pōlum poy vallan naccap padum namakku nāgattaṇaiyānē*

- *niccittu …* – I have firmly determined that he will never leave my heart since he performed penance for his own benefit by staying in water and standing on the mountain.
- *kaiccakkarattu aṇṇal* – sarvēśvaran who has the divine chakra in his hand. One who never abandons his devotees; it is said in [periya tiruvandādi 87](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/02/periya-thiruvandhadhi-87/) “*kai kaḻalā nēmiyān*“ (one who has the inseparable chakra in his hand).
- *kaḷvam peridu udaiyan* – Not only is he remaining in my heart without leaving from there, he is eagerly planning for glorious aspects without my knowledge. He was planning for glorious aspects for me such as setting out to take me to paramapadam, thinking about having amānava touch me, thinking to make moon-faced damsels welcome me at the entrance of paramapadam.

Don’t fear that “he does this for everyone”.

- *meyccappadān piṟarkku* – He does not place himself to be praised by others as he let me praise him highlighting his qualities; he remains unreachable for the others.
- *mey pōlum poy vallan* – He places himself equally in front of duryōdana et al just as he places himself in front of arjuna et al; but during the execution, he will pretend to act truthfully, but will deceive.

Don’t fear “what if he does the same with us?”

- *naccappadum namakku* – He would not do to us what he does to those who are unfavourable towards him.

When asked “How can we believe that?” āḻvār says,

- *nāgattu aṇaiyānē* – What is the point in seeing what he does towards those who are different from us? Our example is what he does towards those who are similar to us. īsn’t this how he interacts with one who is similar to us, as the reason for our goal?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 10.4.6. Nagattanaiyanai

*nāgattaṇaiyānai nāḷdōṟum jñānattāl āgattaṇaippārkku aruḷ seyyum ammānai māgattiḷa madiyam sērum sadaiyānai pāgattu vaittān tan pādam paṇindēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

nāgam – tiruvanantāḻvān who is eternal servitor; aṇaiyānai – one who is having as mattress; nāḷdōṟum – always; jñānattāl – through jñāna in the form of bhakti; āgattu – in the heart; aṇaippārkku – for the mumukśus (liberation seekers) who place and enjoy; aruḷ seyyum – doing favours, being ultimately enjoyable; ammānai – being the lord; māgattu – dwelling in the sky; iḷa madiyam – young crescent moon; sērum – uniting; sadaiyānai – due to having in his matted hair (and hence being enjoyer (due to having the moon) as well as being engaged in penance (due to having matted hair)); pāgattu – on one side \[of his divine form\]; vaittān than – the ultimately simple one who placed, his; pādam paṇindēn – I got to surrender unto the divine feet

**Перевод:**

**emperumān is having tiruvanantāḻvān who is an eternal servitor, as his mattress; he is the ultimately enjoyable lord who is doing favours for the mumukśus who place him in their hearts and always pursue him through jñāna in the form of bhakti, and who enjoy him; he is ultimately simple due to placing rudra who is having the young crescent moon, which usually dwells in the sky, in his matted hair, on one side of his divine form; I got to surrender unto the divine feet of such emperumān. The “ai” in the end of “aṇaiyānai, ammānai” is just for sound and has no specific meaning. Alternative recital – “pāgattu vaittānaip pādam paṇindēnē“.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the sixth pāsuram, āḻvār says “I got to surrender unto the divine feet of sarvēśvaran who is of the nature that he will accept those who surrender today without checking their qualities, as he would accept nityasūris”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. nāgattaṇaiyānai nāḷdōṟum jñānattāl āgattaṇaippārkku aruḷ seyyum ammānai māgattiḷa madiyam sērum sadaiyānai pāgattu vaittān than pādam paṇindēnē*

- *nāgattu aṇaiyānai* – He would accept those who are favourable towards him, as his mattress.
- *nāḷdōṟum …* – For those who embrace him in their hearts, with their jñāna, he will always shower his mercy. The mumukśu cannot always think about emperumān! To eliminate such shortcoming, emperumān who is in a singular form/state will always shower his mercy upon such mumukśu.
- *māgam …* – emperumān gave place to rudra, who is wearing the moon on his hair to pretend as an enjoyer and is having matted hair which reveals that he is a pursuer of some means, on one side of his divine form; I have surrendered unto the divine feet of such emperumān; is there anything to worry for me now?

## 10.4.7. Pani nenje

*paṇi nenjē! nāḷum parama param paranaipiṇi onrum sārā piṟavi keduttāḷummaṇi ninṟa sōdi madusūdan ennammānaṇi ninṟa sempon adalāḻiyānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

maṇi ninṟa sōdi – having complexion which resembles the radiance in a blue gem; madusūdan – eliminating the hurdles for enjoyment, just as he eliminated madu; en ammān – my lord who allowed me to enjoy that beauty; aṇi ninṟa – being an ornament for itself; sem pon – having an attractive form which resembles reddish gold; adal – having engagement in battle to kill the enemies of devotees; āḻiyān – one who has tiruvāḻi (divine chakra); piṟavi – our birth; keduttu – eliminate; āḷum – will accept our service; piṇi – the sorrows of samsāra; onṟum sārā – will not affect at all; parama param paranai – having none greater than he and being greater than brahmā et al; nenjē – Oh heart!; nāḷum – always; paṇi – worship and enjoy him

**Перевод:**

**emperumān who is having complexion which resembles the radiance in a blue gem, who eliminates the hurdles for enjoyment, just as he eliminated madu, allowed me to enjoy that beauty; he is having divine chakra which is like an ornament in itself, which is having an attractive form which resembles reddish gold and which is having engagement in battle to kill the enemies of devotees; he will eliminate our birth and accept our service; the sorrows of samsāra will not affect us at all. Oh heart! Always worship such emperumān who is having none greater than he and being greater than brahmā et al, and enjoy him.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the seventt pāsuram, āḻvār says “Oh heart! Enjoy sarvēśvaran everyday; he will eliminate the hurdles and accept our service”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. paṇi nenjē! nāḷum parama param paranaipiṇi onrum sārā piṟavi keduttāḷummaṇi ninṟa sōdi madusūdan ennammānaṇi ninṟa sempon adalāḻiyānē*

- *paṇi …* – Oh heart! Try to enjoy him everyday. There is good opportunity for that.
- *parama param paranai* – emperumān is the controller of nityasūris who are greater than brahmā et al, who are greater than indra et al.
- *piṇi onṟum sārā* – Sorrow will not touch us. He will uproot birth which is the root cause for such sorrows and will accept our nitya kainkaryam (eternal service).
- *maṇi ninṟa sōdi* – His physical beauty is such that we cannot abandon him even if causes us birth. One who is having a divine form which looks like an embodiment of the radiance of a blue gem.
- *madusūdan* – One who eliminates the hurdles of those who enjoy that beauty, just as he eliminated madu.
- *en ammān* – One who eliminated my hurdles in this manner and presented himself to me.
- *aṇi …* – One who has the divine chakra in his hand which will eliminate the hurdles of those who enjoy him, which is like an ornament for his divine hand, and which has a form which attracts those who enjoy him, and which is always ready for battle. One who is having the tool which is both the reason for enjoyment and elimination of hurdles.

## 10.4.8. Aliyan ali

*āḻiyān āḻi amararkkum appālān ūḻiyān ūḻi padaittān nirai mēyttān pāḻiyam tōḷāl varai eduttān pādangaḷ vāḻi en nenjē! maṟavādu vāḻ kaṇḍāy*

**Пословный перевод:**

āḻiyān – One who is having the tiruvāḻi (divine chakra); āḻi – deep natured; amararkkum – for nityasūris; appālān – who has greatness beyond; ūḻiyān – being alone during samhāram (annihilation); ūḻi padaittān – being the creator of all entities starting with time; nirai mēyttān – being the one who follows the created entities and protects them; pāḻi – prideful; am – enjoyable; tōḷāl – with the divine shoulder; varai – mountain; eduttān – lifted and protected, his; pādangaḷ – divine feet; en – my; nenjē – Oh heart!; maṟavādu – without forgetting; vāḻ kaṇḍāy – see that you live by enjoying eternally; vāḻi – let this last for a long time

**Перевод:**

**emperumān who is having divine chakra, whose greatness is beyond the deep-natured nityasūris, is alone during samhāram, is the creator of all entities starting with time and is the one who follows the created entities and protects them. He lifted with his prideful, enjoyable, divine shoulder and protected the covherd clan. Oh my heart! Without forgetting the divine feet of such emperumān, see that you live by enjoying eternally; let this last for a long time. āḻiyān also means one who is deep natured.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the eighth pāsuram, āḻvār says “Enjoy him” to his heart and seeing that the heart became pleased about it, he praises it and says “Oh heart! Enjoy him continuously”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. āḻiyān āḻi amararkkum appālān ūḻiyān ūḻi padaittān nirai mēyttān pāḻiyam tōḷāl varai eduttān pādangaḷ vāḻi en nenjē! maṟavādu vāḻ kaṇḍāy*

- *āḻiyān* – One who has the divine chakra which highlights that he is sarvēśvara (supreme lord).
- *āḻi …* – One who remains the controller of the svarūpa (nature), stiti (existence) etc of deep natured nityasūris as in the case of that tiruvāḻi āḻvān (cakkarattāḻvār).
- *ūḻiyān* – One who remains in paramapadam along with the nityasūris in the great assembly. When all the effectual entities here \[in samsāram\] become annihilated and when only time remains, he appears.
- *ūḻi padaittān* – He created all entities starting with time by his sankalpam as said in taittirīya upaniśat “*bahu syām*” (let me become many).
- *nirai mēyttān* – In this manner, he created all entities, and then incarnated as if someone else created him, would protect the cows. He protected the cows which do not know how to protect themselves and which do not reject his protection.
- *pāḻi am tōḷāl* – As he keeps protecting the cows, indra rained hail due to anger caused by hunger; he protected them by lifting the gōvardan mountain. pāḻi – strength, being spacious. āḻvār is talking about the strength of emperumān’s shoulders wherein one can take shelter and remain fearless as if being inside a fort while everyone outside is suffering; alternatively, āḻvār is talking about emperumān’s urge for protection where even after the five lakh families taking shelter under his shoulders, there is more space not just for tiruvāyppādi (śrī gōkulam) but ten such gōkulams; As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 34.31 “*bāhuccāyām avaśtabda: yasya lōkō mahātmana:”* (Under the divine shoulders of mahātmā śrī rāma, all the world has taken shelter), those who have taken shelter are small in number in comparison to the shade available there.
- *am tōḷ* – Beautiful shoulder. His shoulder’s beauty is such that one will start performing mangaḷāśāsanam (wishing well) as said in tiruppallāṇḍu 1 “*tiṇḍōḷ maṇivaṇṇā un sēvadic cevvi tirukkāppu*” (Oh one who is having complexion of a gem and strong shoulders! Let your reddish, fresh feet be protected”; *sundarat tōḷ* (beautiful shoulder).
- *pādangaḷ* – The divine feet of the one who lifted gōvardana mountain and protected.
- *vāḻi* – In between, āḻvār is performing mangaḷāśāsanam to his own heart so that it understands the principle which will be explained subsequently. Just as it is said in śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 67-15 “*yāmōśadimivāyuśman anvēśasi mahāvanē*” (May you live long! Whosoever you are searching for, just like looking for a rare medicine in a huge forest, that (sītā) dēvi and my life have both been usurped by rāvaṇa), āḻvār is saying “let this abundance always remain with you”.
- *en nenjē* – Everywhere else, the manas (heart) which is subservient to ātmā is pulling the ātmā away, but you, my heart, are following my ways! For everyone else, the heart which is one of the faculties for the ātmā is leading to bondage. Unlike that, you who are following my ways and are leading me to liberation!
- *maṟavādu* – As you have attained the benefit, do not do what is done in other matters \[remembering first and forgetting later\].
- *vāḻ kaṇḍāy* – Why should I beg at your feet for your life? I am begging at your feet to make you drink milk \[which is already nice\]. If we have to say “live your life without forgetting”, what is the purpose of the attributes highlighted previously \[such as āḻiyān, amararkkum appālān etc\]? \[It is to emphasise that\] One should not go elsewhere and try different means! We should hold on to the one who can be the protector. \[āḻiyān\] One who has the tool (divine chakra) for protection can only be the protector \[others cannot be\]; \[āḻi amararkkum appālān\] only the one who is controller, for the nature, existence etc, of those who have no other expectation can be the protector; \[ūḻiyān\] for the one who exists sometimes and does not exist at other times, one who always exists can only be the protector; \[ūḻi padaittān\] one who created all of these when they did not exist can only be the protector; \[nirai mēyttān\] after having created, one who protects even those who have no ability in protecting themselves, can only be the protector; knowing all of these, see if you can forget him!

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 10.4.9. Kanden

*kaṇḍēn kamala malarp pādam kāṇḍalumē viṇḍē oḻinda vinaiyāyina ellām toṇḍē seydu enṟum toḻudu vaḻiyoḻugap paṇḍē paraman paṇitta paṇi vagaiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

toṇḍē seydu – performing ultimate devotion towards him; enṟum – always; toḻudu – having activities matching the servitude; vaḻi oḻuga – to engage in that path as per his desire; paṇḍē – in previous times; paraman – sarvēśvara who is greater than all; paṇitta paṇi vagaiyē – by the mantra rahasya prakāram (ways of confidential mantras) mercifully explained; kamala malar – ultimately enjoyable like lotus flower; pādam – divine feet; kaṇḍēn – saw \[internally\], matching my servitude; kāṇḍalumē – as I acquired this knowledge; vinaiyāyina ellām – all sorrows such as ahankāram, mamakāram etc which are hurdles for enjoyment; viṇḍē oḻinda – went away, along with the traces

**Перевод:**

**Previously, sarvēśvaran who is greater than all, mercifully explained the mantra rahasya prakāram (ways of confidential mantras) to have me performing ultimate devotion towards him always, to have activities matching the servitude and to engage in that path as per his desire; I saw the ultimately enjoyable lotus flower like divine feet of such emperumān, matching my servitude; as I acquired this knowledge, all sorrows such as ahankāram, mamakāram etc which are hurdles for enjoyment, went away, along with the traces.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the ninth pāsuram, āḻvār speaks about the benefit he got saying “emperumān who is attained by bhakti yōgam which is a culmination of tapas (penance), jñāna (knowledge) etc which are done over a thousand births, is seen by me by his grace only”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. kaṇḍēn kamala malarp pādam kāṇḍalumē viṇḍē oḻinda vinaiyāyina ellām toṇḍē seydu enṟum toḻudu vaḻiyoḻugap paṇḍē paraman paṇitta paṇi vagaiyē*

- *kaṇḍēn* – I saw the emperumān who is always heard about only \[from śāstram\]. āḻvār is saying that he saw emperumān implying that his surrender led to its goal. With this, he is talking about jñāna sākśātkāram (seeing with internal eyes) which is at par with pratyakśa sākśātkāram (seeing with external eyes).
- *kamala malarp pādam* – The enjoyability \[of the divine feet\] is such that one is satisfied with the seeing through internal eyes, even without the actual attainment.
- *kāṇḍalumē* – Upon seeing.
- *viṇḍē oḻinda vinaiyāyina ellām* – We are acquiring this \[elimination of sins\] from him as said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 18.66](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/18-66/) “*sarva pāpēbhyō mōkśayiśyāmi*” (I will liberate you from all of your sins). All the sorrows thought “He is not alone, he is depending upon bhagavān’s lotus feet” and left.
- *toṇḍē …* – āḻvār is saying that even this \[what is explained in this pāsuram\] is also the meaning for that ślōkam. What is incidental will naturally go; upāyam will also lead to the result. The principle “Now, as the true nature of the self is established, the activities matching that nature will also remain eternally”, which is implied in that ślōkam, is explicitly explained here.
- *toṇḍē seydu enṟum toḻudu vaḻi oḻuga* – After the true nature is understood to be eternal, to also have the activities matching that nature, eternally.
- *paṇḍē paraman paṇitta paṇi vagaiyē – kaṇḍēn kamala malarp pādam* – As he said in \[the same ślōkam\] “*mām ēkam śaraṇam vraja*” (Surrender unto me as the only refuge), I got to see his divine feet.

## 10.4.10. Vagaiyal manam onri

*vagaiyāl manam onṟi mādavanai nāḷum pugaiyāl viḷakkāl pudu malarāl neerāl tisaidōṟu amarargaḷ senṟirainja ninṟa tagaiyān saraṇam tamargatku ōr paṟṟē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vagaiyāl – by ways explained in śāstram; manam – heart; onṟi – being focussed; mādavanai – emperumān, who is śriya:pati (consort of śrī mahālakśmi) for the fulfilment of their goal; nāḷum – everyday; pudu – distinguished; pugaiyāl viḷakkāl malarāl neerāl – smoke (incense), lamp, flower and water; disaidōṟu – in every direction; amarargaḷ – dēvas starting with brahmā; senṟu – go; iṟainja – to pray and surrender; ninṟa – stood; tagaiyān – one who is having the nature; saraṇam – divine feet; tamargatku – for the distinguished devotees who are ananyaprayōjanas (those who don’t seek any other benefit); ōr – being distinguished goal; paṟṟu – will be the good refuge

**Перевод:**

**dēvas starting with brahmā, being focussed in their hearts by ways explained in śāstram on emperumān, who is śriya:pati for the fulfillment of their goal, everyday, go in every direction with distinguished smoke (incense), lamp, flower and water; the divine feet of such emperumān who is standing to be prayed and surrendered by brahmā et al, are the distinguished goal and good refuge for the distinguished devotees who are ananyaprayōjanas.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the tenth pāsuram, āḻvār concludes with bhakti yōgam which is spoken about here, saying “The divine feet of sarvēśvaran, who is the refuge for prayōjanāntaraparas (those who see other benefits) also and who fulfills their desires, are the good refuge for bhaktimāns (followers of bhakti yōgam) and prapannas (those who performed prapatti) as well”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. vagaiyāl manam onṟi mādavanai nāḷum pugaiyāl viḷakkāl pudu malarāl neerāl tisaidōṟu amarargaḷ senṟirainja ninṟa tagaiyān saraṇam tamargatku ōr paṟṟē*

- *vagaiyāl manam onṟi* – Being focussed in the heart by the ways explained in śāstram.
- *mādavanai* – One need not fear for violating the rules and carelessness; whatever activities one performed to avoid the censure by people, one will not reap the results. The one (śrī mahālakśmi) who would say “Should you abandon him for not following the rules properly and not being careful?” is with emperumān. With this, the relationship with lakshmi is explained in that \[gītā carama\] ślōkam \[This pāsuram is further explaining carama ślōkam\]. The attributes which are part of one’s nature can either be explicitly mentioned or skipped; this is why in dvayam it is explicitly highlighted and in tirumantram it is implicitly understood. It is said in dramida bhāśyam “*antargata guṇāṇām Eva dēvatām bhajatē*” (only vorśipping the lord who has qualities which are hidden in his svarūpam (true nature)); as it is said that in such svarūpam of bhagavān itself, his qualities such as apahatapāpmatva (being untouched by sins) etc are present.
- *nāḷum …* – Without any time restriction. Not having any restriction in the materials used for the worship also, carrying the materials which they have, brahmā et al come and surrender just as devotees will arrive for periya tirunāḷ (brahmōtsavam, adyayana utsavam etc in śrīrangam) from all directions; such emperumān’s divine feet; for those who surrendered to his divine feet, there is no need for seeking any other refuge. For ananyaprayōjana bhakti yōga niśtas (who perform bhakti without any expectation), he will be the grantor of results and means; for prapannas (who surrendered to him only), he will be the direct means.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 10.4.11. Parrenru parri

*paṟṟenṟu paṟṟip parama param paranai mal tiṇ tōḷ mālai vaḻudi vaḷa nādan sol todai andādi ōr āyirattuḷ ippatutum kaṟṟārkku ōr paṟṟāgum kaṇṇan kaḻal iṇaiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

parama param paranai – the lord of all who has none greater than him; mal – in wrestling battle; tiṇ – strong; tōḷ – having shoulder; mālai – sarvēśvaran who is the prāpya (goal) and prāpaka (means), since he is infatuated towards his devotees; paṟṟu enṟu – determined as the good refuge for us; paṟṟi – surrendered; vaḻudi vaḷa nādan – nammāḻvār, who is the controller of tiruvaḻudi nādu (āḻvārtirunagari region); sol – mercifully spoke; todai – in the form of a garland of words; andādi ōr āyirattuḷ – among the distinguished thousand pāsurams which are in the style of antādi (ending word of one pāsuram relating to the beginning of next pāsuram); ippattum – this decad also; kaṟṟārkku – for those who learnt and practiced; kaṇṇān – kriṣṇa who is dāmōdara; kaḻal – divine feet; iṇai – pair; ōr – distinguished; paṟṟāgum – result

**Перевод:**

**sarvēśvaran is the prāpya (goal) and prāpaka (means), since he is infatuated towards his devotees, who is the lord of all who has none greater than him,  who is having strong shoulder in the wrestling battle; nammāḻvār, who is the controller of tiruvaḻudi nādu, determined that such emperumān is the good refuge for us, and mercifully spoke about him in distinguished thousand pāsurams which are in the form of a garland of words and are in the style of antādi; for those who learnt and practiced this decad among those thousand pāsurams, the distinguished pair of divine feet of kriṣṇa who is dāmōdara are the distinguished result.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the end, āḻvār says “For those who learn this decad, kriṣṇa’s divine feet are easily attainable”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. paṟṟenṟu paṟṟip parama param paranai mal tiṇ tōḷ mālai vaḻudi vaḷa nādan sol todai andādi ōr āyirattuḷ ippatutum kaṟṟārkku ōr paṟṟāgum kaṇṇan kaḻal iṇaiyē*

- *paṟṟu enṟu paṟṟip parama param paranai* – Surrendering unto sarvēśvaran considering him to be the goal and means.
- *mal tiṇ tōḷ mālai* – ātmā just needs to surrender unto him and have faith; there is no shortcoming in emperumān for protection. āḻvār is saying that emperumān has the strength and love to eliminate the hurdles of such surrendered persons.
- *vaḻudi …* – As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam bāla kāṇḍam 4.8 “*pātyē gēyē ca maduram pramāṇais tribhiranvitam*” (both words and music are sweet, in harmony with all three pramāṇams), those who learnt this decad among the thousand pāsurams which are strung in the form of a garland with beautiful words.
- *kaṇṇan kaḻal iṇai – ōr paṟṟu āgum* – As said in “*dāmōdaran tāḷgaḷ – tava neṟikku – oru sārvē*” (the divine feet of dāmōdara, are the result for bhakti yōgam), divine feet of kriṣṇa themselves will be the result, so that one need not seek anything else to hold on to.

## 10.5 Kannan kalalinai

## 10.5.1. Kannan kalalinai

*kaṇṇan kaḻal iṇai naṇṇum manam udaiyīr eṇṇum tirunāmam tiṇṇam nāraṇamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kaṇṇan – kriṣṇa who is easily approachable for all, his; kaḻal iṇai – divine feet which are present for his devotees; naṇṇum – to reach; manam – heart; udaiyīr – you who all have; eṇṇum – to meditate upon; tirunāmam – divine name; tiṇṇam – certainly; nāraṇamē – the word nārāyaṇa which is part of the primary mantra (as seen in the viṣṇu gāyatri)

**Перевод:**

**Oh you who all have the heart to reach the divine feet. which are present for his devotees, of kriṣṇa who is easily approachable for all! The divine name to be meditated upon is certainly the word nārāyaṇa which is part of the primary mantra. Also it can be considered as āḻvār saying “No need to worry about praṇava, namas and caturti \[āya\]. Just think about the divine name”.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the first pāsuram, āḻvār says “The divine name you should meditate upon to reach the divine feet of kriṣṇa is nārāyaṇa; this is certain”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. kaṇṇan kaḻal iṇai naṇṇum manam udaiyīr eṇṇum tirunāmam tiṇṇam nāraṇamē*

- *kaṇṇan kaḻal iṇai naṇṇum manam udaiyīr* – āḻvār is repeating once more what he explained previously, to instruct what they (people) should hear. He said in tiruvāimoḻi 10.4.1 “*sārvē tava neṟikkut tāmōdaran tāḷgaḷ*“; he says the same as “*kaṇṇan kaḻaliṇai*” here. Oh you who desire to reach the divine feet of kriṣṇa!
- *kaṇṇan kaḻal iṇai* – The divine feet of the one who is easily approachable, instead of having to go all the way to paramapadam to reach him. The divine feet which facilitate in he being the messenger, charioteer etc for his devotees.
- *naṇṇum* – It looks as if reuniting after separation; as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 17.1 “*ājagāma*” (he came).
- *manam udaiyīr* – As said in “*nidi udaiyīr*” (wealthy person), āḻvār is considering the intent as something great. No need to search for qualification, everyone who has taste is qualified. To attain svargam (heaven), one requires qualification and atonement; but for the apunarāvrutti mōkśam (irrevokable liberation), one does not need any such thing; this is because, one cannot earn the qualification matching the greatness of the goal attained in paramapadam.
- *eṇṇum tirunāmam* – The divine name to be meditated upon; since āḻvār is talking about bhaktimāns (those who practice bhakti yōgam), they would think “adu adu” (that name, that name repeatedly). āḻvār is saying *eṇṇum tirunāmam* instead of *eṇṇum tirumantram*, because, for \[reciting\] the divine name, one need not have any specific qualification and limbs \[ancillary rituals\]; this is to say that it is similar to a child calling out the mother’s name.

When asked “What is that divine name?” āḻvār says,

- *nāraṇam* – As this is the name of the svāmy (lord), this is similar to how one would say “*ammē!*” (Oh mother!).

When asked “Would something else also be required?” āḻvār says,

- *nāraṇamē* – This is sufficient.

When asked “For such great result, is this sufficient?” āḻvār says,

- *tiṇṇam* – Certainly. As said in itihāsams/purāṇams “*satyam satyam punas satyam …*” (I declare the truth again and again), āḻvār is saying with certainity. With the avadāraṇam (“*nāraṇam****E***” – ascertainment), āḻvār is saying that even without praṇavam, namas and caturti, this is complete on its own. As āḻvār said it as “nāraṇam” where he has included “m” in the end which is not in the original name \[nārāyaṇa\] and also shrunk the original name \[from nārāyaṇa to nāraṇa\], just as a salt pan will have salt everywhere, when anything is added to this name, that will be acceptable and even when a letter or two are missing, that will not lead to becoming a brahmarakśas due to missing some part or tune \[as it happens for general vēdam recital\], thereby establishing the distinguished nature of this name, nārāyaṇa.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 10.5.2. Naranan emman

*nāraṇan emmān pāraṇangāḷan vāraṇam tolaitta kāraṇan tānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

nāraṇan – the one who is known by the name “nārāyaṇa” as said in hari vamśam “ēśa nārāyaṇa:” (śrīman nārāyaṇa); emmān – being the controller of leelā vibhūti (material realm) due to being the lord of people like me; pār aṇangu āḷan – being the controller of nitya vibhūti (spiritual realm) due to being the dear consort of śrī bhūmip pirātti; varaṇam tolaitta – one who eliminated kuvalayāpīdam (which was an enemy); nāraṇan tānē – kriṣṇa himself, who is the origin of the whole world

**Перевод:**

**kriṣṇa himself, who is the origin of the whole world, who eliminated kuvalayāpīdam is the one who is known by the name “nārāyaṇa” as said in hari vamśam “ēśa nārāyaṇa:” (śrīman nārāyaṇa) and is the controller of leelā vibhūti (material realm) due to being the lord of people like me and nitya vibhūti (spiritual realm) due to being the dear consort of śrī bhūmip pirātti.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*In the second and third pāsurams, āḻvār explains the meaning of this divine name/mantram. Whenever tirumantram is highlighted, āḻvār always explains either the meaning first and then the name or the name first and then the meaning. This is seen in tiruvāimoḻi 1.2.10 “eṇ perukkannalattu oṇ poruḷ īṟila – vaṇ pugaḻ nāraṇan“,  tiruvāimoḻi 1.3.3 “yāvaiyum yāvarum tānām amaivudai nāraṇan” (śrīman nārāyaṇan who sustains all cētanas (sentient beings) and acētanas (insentient objects)) and tiruvāimoḻi 9.3.1 “nārāyaṇan nangaḷ pirān avanē” (nārāyaṇa is our only benefactor) followed by tiruvāimoḻi 9.3.2 “avanē agal jñālam padaittidandān” (He created this great world and dug it out also). nāraṇan emmān pāraṇangāḷan vāraṇam tolaitta kāraṇan tānē*

- *nāraṇan* – Thinking to explain the meaning of the name, āḻvār recites the name.
- *emmān* – My lord.
- *pār aṇangu āḷan* – śrī bhūmip pirātti is pāraṇangu. She is the controlling dēvatā for bhūmi (pār – earth). By pāraṇangāḷan, āḻvār explains emperumān’s nitya vibhūti yōgam (having spiritual realm); by emmān, āḻvār gives a sample for leelā vibhūti; hence, āḻvār explains that he is the lord of both nitya vibhūti and leelā vibhūti. emperumān has one vibhūti (spiritual realm) to forgive the faults \[of devotees\] and another vibhūti (material realm – bhūmip pirātti) to make him forgive the faults. As said in “*krutāgasa: kśāmyati*” (one who saves the sinners) – īśvara who saves those who have committed abundant sins and have no refuge; pirātti is of the nature that she will protect those who have abundant sins and do not atone for the same; śrī bhūmip pirātti would say \[in the context of what sītāp pirātti said in the case of kākāsura\] “Why punish him by asking to sever the head? Why ask for protection later? If you are going to punish him, why did she let him commit the mistake and then make him suffer and finally ask for his protection?”
- *vāraṇam tolaitta* – The enemies of those who desire to reach him will meet the same end as that of kuvalayāpīdam. Is elimination of hurdles explained in tirumantram? Protection is explained in it from the beginning \[akāram\]; protection should be done by removing the hurdles.  It is said as “*avarakśaṇē*” \[the root meaning of akāram is “giving protection” – hence it talks about eliminating the hurdles as well\].
- *kāraṇan tānē* – For tirumantram, he being the one who is the controller of svarūpa (nature), stiti (existence) etc of all entities, is also an important meaning.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 10.5.3. Tane ulagellam

*tānē ulagellām tānē padaittidandu ōtānē uṇḍumiḻndu tānē āḷvānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tānē – He (who is known by the name nārāyaṇa); ulagu ellām – one who can be said as the singular substratum for the entire cosmos as per sāmānādikaraṇyam (multiple entities having singular base) as said in “sarvam kalvidam brahma”; tānē – He (without any assistance from anyone); padaittu – created; idandu – digging it out from praḷayam (deluge); tānē – without anyone requesting; uṇḍu – placed in his stomach and protected; umiḻndu – spat it out subsequently; tānē – He (who is greater than all); āḷvān – will rule

**Перевод:**

**He is the one who can be said as the singular substratum for the entire cosmos as per sāmānādikaraṇyam (multiple entities having singular base) as said in “sarvam kalvidam brahma“, who created the world, dug it out from praḷayam, who placed it in his stomach without anyone requesting and protected it, who spat it out subsequently, and will rule the world.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*In the third pāsuram, āḻvār explains how emperumān is protecting in all ways matching his lordship. tānē ulagellām tānē padaittidandu ōtānē uṇḍumiḻndu tānē āḷvānē*

- *tānē ulagu ellām* – It is said in cāndōjña upaniśat 3-14-1 “*sarvam kalvidam brahma* ” (all these are brahmam), cāndōjña upaniśat “*tatvamasi*” (that is you). Since he is the one who created the world, dug it out from deluge and who controls/rules the world, he is referred to as the world; this is said in cāndōjña upaniśat 3-14-1 “*tajjalān*” (due to being created, sustained and ended in that brahmam). The sameness of nature identified here is not speaking about svarūpēṇa aikyam (brahmam and jīvātmā being the same by nature); it is speaking about sameness by śarīrātma bhāvam (brahmam being ātmā and all entities being his body \[just as ātmā and body are identified together, brahmam and ātmā are identified together\]). While talking about kāraṇatvam (emperumān being the cause), a doubt arises about how brahmam could have vikāram (change) and that doubt is clarified by explaining the changes through śarīrātma bhāvam \[changes are for body only i.e. cit and acit, not for brahmam\]. This is being explained here to highlight that just as childhood, adolescence, youth and old age which occur on the body will not affect the ātmā, the changes which occur on the entities, will not affect him \[emperum An\] and hence he is free from defects.
- *tānē padaittu* – As said in subhāla upaniśat 2 “*tama: parē dēva ēkī bhavati*” (the primordial matter mixes with paramātmā), īśvara who has cit and acit in subtle form (during deluge), himself created all the worlds. Since even ātmās are in the state of acit (insentient), there is no one to request him for creation, and hence out of great mercy in his heart, he himself created.
- *tānē  idandu* – The earth which was consumed by the deluge did not pray to emperumān to be rescued; yet he rescued it on his own desire.
- *tānē uṇḍu* – No one knows before the arrival of the deluge \[yet he himself consumed them \[all the cit and acit entities in all the worlds\] and placed in his stomach before deluge consumes them all\].
- *umiḻndu* – While they will be anguished inside the stomach, they would not know to pray “please let us go out”. He himself spat them out.

Since he engages in many ways of protection in this manner, he is

- *tānē ulagu ellām* – *sarvam kalvidam brahma* (all these are brahmam).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 10.5.4. Alvan alinir

*āḷvān āḻi nīrk kōḷ vāy aravaṇaiyān tāḷ vāy malar ittu nāḷ vāy nādīrē*

**Пословный перевод:**

āḻi nīr – the huge causal ocean; kōḷ vāy – one who has the mouth which is prideful and always praising emperumān; aravu aṇaiyān – having the divine serpent as mattress; āḷvān – the lord who is the controller of the world, his; tāḷ vāy – at the divine feet; malar ittu – offering flowers; nāḷ vāy nādīr – always desirously approach him

**Перевод:**

**The lord who is the controller of the world, has as his mattress, the divine serpent who has the mouth which is prideful and always praising him, in the huge causal ocean; offering flowers at the divine feet, always desirously approach him. kōḷ vāy could mean the strong mouth, which is the place of strength as said in stōtra ratnam 39 “prakruśta vijñāna balaika dāmani” (ādiśēśan who is the abode of great knowledge and ability); alternatively, kōḷ means radiance as said in the same ślōkam “paṇāmaṇivrāta mayūkha maṇḍala” (shining brightly as a result of the light emitted from the precious stones in his hoods).**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Fourth pāsuram. āḻvār says “There is an explanation for this \[aśtākśara mantram/nāmam\] as said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 1.4.6 ‘āpō nārā iti prōktā:’ (Water originated from paramapuruśa, hence it is called nāra); understand the tirumantram in this manner, recite it and approach him with flowers and anjali (joined palms)”. āḷvān āḻi nīrk kōḷ vāy aravaṇaiyān tāḷ vāy malar ittu nāḷ vāy nādīrē*

- *āḷvān* – One who accepts the service of everyone.
- *āḻi nīr āḷvān* – This is how he accepts the service. Mercifully reclining on the causal ocean with the intent to engage in creation, and protecting all the cētanas (sentient beings) at that time.
- *kōḷ vāy* – Prideful mouth; also said as the mouth which is like death for enemies.
- *aravu aṇaiyān tāḷ vāy malar ittu* – āḻvār is saying that emperumān is easily vorśippable. Offering fresh flowers at the divine feet of anantaśāyi (one who is resting on ādiśēśan).
- *nāḷ vāy nādīrē* – Approach him everyday; you will also get the same benefit as that tiruvanantāḻvān (ādiśēśan).

## 10.5.5. Nadir naldorum

*nādīr nāḷdōṟum vāda malar koṇḍu pādīr avan nāmam vīdē peṟalāmē*

**Пословный перевод:**

nāḷdōṟum – every day; vādā malar koṇḍu – with fresh flowers; nādīr – approach him (manifesting your state of seeking); avan nāmam – the divine name of such nārāyaṇa; pādīr – sing; vīdē – as mōkśam, the ultimate goal; peṟalām – can attain

**Перевод:**

**Every day, approach him with flowers; sing the divine name of such nārāyaṇa; you can attain the ultimate goal, mōkśam (which is nothing but such worship and singing).**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Fifth pāsuram. āḻvār says “With fresh flowers, recite his divine name as an outlet for the bliss; as you do that, you will acquire the activities which match your true nature”. nādīr nāḷdōṟum vāda malar koṇḍu pādīr avan nāmam vīdē peṟalāmē*

- *nādīr nāḷdōṟum* – As one would eat whenever one is hungry \[recite his name always\].
- *vādā malar koṇḍu* – With flowers which are as fresh as your affection towards him.
- *pādīr avan nāmam* – As muktātmās (liberated souls) would sing sāmagānam as said in taittirīya upaniśat “*ētat sāma gāyannāstē*” (The liberated soul is singing sāma gānam), sing his divine names with love. *nādīr* indicates the action of the mind; *vādā malar koṇḍu* indicates action of the body; *pādīr* indicates the action of the speech.
- *vīdē peṟalāmē* – As one engages in activities matching one’s true nature, one can get what is said in cāndōjña upaniśat 8.12.2 “*svēna rūpēṇābhiniśpadyatē*” (attains natural realisation/blossoming of self). As one engages in sweet activities, one can get great benefit.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 10.5.6. Meyan vengadam

*mēyān vēngadam kāyā malar vaṇṇan pēyār mulai uṇḍa vāyān mādavanē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kāyā malar – dark, like kāyām pū \[a purple coloured flower\]; vaṇṇan – having form; pēyār – pūtanā’s; mulai – bosom (filled with poison); uṇḍa – will eliminate our attachment here, as he fully sucked to extract her life; vāyān – one who has a nectarean mouth; mādavan – as said in “svāmi puśkariṇi tīrē ramayā sahmōdatē“, with alarmēlmangait tāyār \[śrī mahālakśmi\]; vēngadam mēyān – is eternally residing in tirumalā

**Перевод:**

**emperumān who is having dark form like that of kāyām pū (a purple coloured flower), will eliminate our attachment here, as he fully sucked pūtanā’s bosom to extract her life; he has a nectarean mouth; he is eternally residing in tirumalā with alarmēlmangait tāyār as said in “svāmi puśkariṇi tīrē ramayā sahmōdatē“.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Sixth pāsuram. When asked “We can do as you say only if we can see such approachable emperumān; shall we not first see him to approach him?” āḻvār says “emperumān is mercifully standing in tirumalā for us, who are of later times \[of incarnations\]; go and approach him”. mēyān vēngadam kāyā malar vaṇṇan pēyār mulai uṇḍa vāyān mādavanē*

- *mēyān vēngadam* – *vēngdam mēyān* – To accept your surrender, he is eternally residing in tirumalā.

When asked “Would one worship him as soon as one sees him?” āḻvār says,

- *kāyā malar vaṇṇan* – One who has such a beautiful form that even a wooden log will stand up and dance, without stopping, on seeing him.

When asked “What will the hurdles do?” āḻvār says,

- *pēyār mulai uṇḍa vāyān* – They will meet the same fate as pūtanā did.
- *mādavanē* – One \[śrī mahālakśmi\] who will make him accept us without seeing our previous actions, is present with him.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 10.5.7. Madavan enrenru

*mādavan enṟenṟu ōda valleerēl tīdonṟum adaiyā ēdam sārāvē*

**Пословный перевод:**

mādavan – the divine name mādava (of emperumān who is with lakśmī who is having the responsibility of puruśakāram (recommendation of us to emperumān) and kainkarya vardakatvam (improving our kainkaryams towards emperumān)); enṟu enṟu – meditating (as the refuge as indicated as the upāyam (means) in the first part of dvaya mahā mantram and as the goal as indicated as the upēyam (end) in the second part of dvaya mahā mantram); ōda – to recite; valleerēl – if you are able to do; tīdu onṟum – all the cruel sins accumulated so far; adaiyā – will not reach you to give results; ēdam sārā – future sins will not associate with us

**Перевод:**

**If you are able to recite the divine name mādava meditating upon it, all the cruel sins accumulated so far will not reach you to give results; as said in “dvayam āvartayēt nityam“, future sins will not associate with us. Implies that only joyful experience will be there, for the rest of the life as said in “sadaivam vaktā … sukhamāsva“.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*In the seventh pāsuram, āḻvār says “Those who are unable to lovingly approach him or sweetly recite the divine names, if they recite the name recited by those who are residing in his private quarters \[the abode of pirātti\], will get the result after perfect devotion”. mādavan enṟenṟu ōda valleerēl tīdonṟum adaiyā ēdam sārāvē*

- *mādavan enṟu enṟu ōda valleerēl* – Along with the divine name nārāyaṇa, try to recite this name also \[mādava\]. Previously āḻvār said in [tiruvāimoḻi 10.5.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/12/thiruvaimozhi-10-5-1-kannan-kazhalinai/) “*nāraṇamē*” (the name, nārāyaṇa \[now he is extending it to include the connection of pirātti (mā – lakshmi) to indicate he is śrīman nārāyaṇa\]).
- *ōda valleerēl* – Even if you don’t have ruci (taste), being encouraged by others, if you can recite it always.
- *tīdu onṟum adaiyā* – Past sins will be destroyed.
- *ēdam sārāvē* – Future sins will not affect. He will forget the past sins. He will not consider the future sins in his divine heart. If previously explained tirumantram and the śrīmat word indicated in this pāsuram \[in mādava\] will lead to results individually, it is obvious that those who recite these together \[in dvaya mahā mantram\] will certainly get the apt result.

## 10.5.8. Sara edangal

*sārā ēdangaḷ nīrār mugilvaṇṇan pērār ōduvār ārār amararē*

**Пословный перевод:**

sārā – (on their own) will not come close; nīr Ar – filled with water; mugil vaṇṇan – one who is having the complexion of a dark cloud, his; pēr – divine name; ārār – without being satiated; Ar – anyone (without seeing as per varṇāsrama rules, those who are only having the qualification of devotion); ōduvār – who recites; amararē – are \[comparable to\] nityasūris

**Перевод:**

**Sorrows themselves will not come close; anyone who recites the divine name of the one who is having the complexion of a dark cloud filled with water, without being satiated, is comparable to nityasūris. ārār also indicates those who will never get satiated.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*In the eighth pāsuram, āḻvār says “There is no qualification required; anyone who always recites the divine name, will be comparable to nityasūris”. sārā ēdangaḷ nīrār mugilvaṇṇan pērār ōduvār ārār amararē*

- *sārā ēdangaḷ* – No vices will come close.
- *nīrār mugil vaṇṇan* – One who has the complexion of a cloud which is filled with water.
- *pēr Ar ōduvār* – Those rare few who would recite his divine name always.
- *ārār amararē* – Irrespective of their birth or activities, as they are, they will be comparable to nityasūris. In such birth and state, they will remain comparable to nityasūris.

## 10.5.9. Amararkku ariyanai

*amararkku ariyānai tamargatku eḷiyānai amarattoḻuvārgatku amarā vinaigaḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

amararkku – for brahmā et al who are prayōjanāntaraparas (those who seek other benefits); ariyānai – one who is difficult to attain; tamargatku – for the ananyaprayōjanas (those who seek kainkaryam only) who have the knowledge about their relationship with bhagavān; eḷiyānai – one who is easy to attain; amara – to fit well; toḻuvārgatku – those who worship; vinaigaḷ – sins which are hurdles for the attainment of the goal; amarā – will not touch

**Перевод:**

**emperumān is difficult to attain for brahmā et al who are prayōjanāntaraparas and is easy to attain for the ananyaprayōjanas; for those who worship emperumān to fit well, sins which are hurdles for the attainment of the goal, will not touch.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*In the ninth pāsuram, when asked “When birth etc are immaterial, what will happen to the sins which lead to other results”  āḻvār says “if you surrender unto him without any other expectation, the sins will leave on their own”. amararkku ariyānai tamargatku eḷiyānai amarattoḻuvārgatku amarā vinaigaḷē*

- *amararkku ariyānai* – Even for most intelligent persons such as brahmā et al, he cannot be attained by their own efforts; śrī viṣṇu purāṇam 1.9.55 “*yannāyam bhagavān brahmā jānāti paramam padam*I *tannatā: sma jagaddāma tava sarvagadācyuta* īī” (Oh all pervading acyuta! We bow down to that supreme dwelling place of yours which even bhagavān brahmā does not know and which is the sustaining entity for the universe).
- *tamargatku eḷiyānai* – One who is easy to attain for ananyaprayōjana. Even for a monkey \[sugrīva\], a woman of the hunter clan \[śabari\], or riśis (sages), emperumān is easily approachable; as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam kiśkindā kāṇḍam 4.19 “*sugrīvam śaraṇamgata:*” (śrī rāma surrendered to sugrīva), śankśēpa rāmāyaṇam “*sa: abhyagaccat mahātējā:*” (the very radiant, valorous śrī rāma reached śabari); śrī rāmāyaṇam bāla kāṇḍam 31.4 “*imausma munisārdūla*” (śrī rāma to viśvāmitra – Oh best among sages! We are available to execute your orders).
- *amarat toḻuvārgatku* – For those who worship him without any expectation as ananyaprayōjana.
- *amarā vinaigaḷē* – The hurdles which are the cause for such seeking of other benefits will not come close.

## 10.5.10. Vinai vallirul

*vinai val iruḷ ennum munaigaḷ veruvippōm sunai nal malarittu ninaimin nediyānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vinai – karmas in the form of past and future sins; val iruḷ – very strong transformations in the form of anyatā jñānam (understanding an object to be something else) and viparīta jñānam (understanding the object’s attributes incorrectly); ennum – counted in this manner; munaigaḷ – bodily relationship with hurdles, instincts such as ruci (taste), vāsanā (impressions); veruvip pōm – will leave out of fear (on their own); sunai – in the pond (which is its own habitat); nal malar – fresh flowers; ittu – offering; nediyān – one who is a great benefactor for his devotees; ninaimin – try to think about him

**Перевод:**

**Those which are counted as karmas in the form of past and future sins, very strong transformations in the form of anyatā jñānam and viparīta jñānam, bodily relationship with hurdles, instincts such as ruci, vāsanā will all leave out of fear; offer the fresh flowers from the pond to emperumān, the great benefactor for his devotees, and try to think about him.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*In the tenth pāsuram, āḻvār says “Not just that \[elimination of sins which lead to other benefits\], the hurdles for kainkaryam will also be eliminated; hence, you surrender unto him”. vinai val iruḷ ennum munaigaḷ veruvippōm sunai nal malarittu ninaimin nediyānē*

- *vinai …* – vinai – karma.
- *val iruḷ* – very strong ajñānam (ignorance); bodily relationship which is the cause for such ajñānam; group of ruci, vāsanā etc which result from such relationship.
- *munai* – group.
- *veruvip pōm* – They will go away out of fear thinking “this is not the place for us”. Alternatively, munai – face. They will lose face and go away.
- *sunai nal malar ittu* – No need to seek for divine materials.
- *ninaimin* – [tiruvāimoḻi 9.1.7](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/06/thiruvaimozhi-9-1-7-marronrillai/) “*sindippē amaiyum*” (mere thoughts are sufficient). When it is convenient to you, think about him once as said in śrī varāha caramaślōkam “*smartā*” (for one who thinks when he is stable).
- *nediyānē* – Even If you think about him once \[and forget subsequently\], he will himself constantly think about you saying as in śrī varāha caramaślōkam “*aham smarāmi*” (I think about him); emperumān need not worry after thinking once unlike the jīvātmā. Being with all auspicious qualities, and being untouched by karma, he will constantly think about the jīvātmā.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 10.5.11. Nediyan arul

*nediyān aruḷ sūdum padiyān satakōpan nodi āyirattu ippattu adiyārkkaruḷ pēṟē*

**Пословный перевод:**

nediyān – sarvēśvara who is greater than all, his; aruḷ – (learning) his mercy in all ways; sūdum – enjoying; padiyān – having nature; satakōpan – āḻvār’s; nodi – word; āyirattu – among thousand pāsurams; ippattu – this decad; adiyārkku – for the servitors of bhagavān; aruḷ pēṟu – will lead to the result of his mercy

**Перевод:**

**āḻvār has the nature of enjoying in all ways, the mercy of sarVēśvara who is greater than all,. For the servitors of bhagavān, this decad among thousand pāsurams which are the words of such āḻvār, will lead to the result of his mercy.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*In the end, āḻvār says “Those who practice this decad will become the target of emperumān’s pursuit, as I was”. nediyān aruḷ sūdum padiyān satakōpan nodi āyirattu ippattu adiyārkkaruḷ pēṟē*

- *nediyān …* – āḻvār is exclusively having the nature of being the target of the mercy of sarvēśvaran. That is, previously āḻvār became blissful thinking about how emperumān gave āḻvār the experience of his qualities and activities in a step by step manner as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 4.5.5](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/02/thiruvaimozhi-4-5-5-arra-nalla/) “*āṟṟa nalla vagai kāttum ammān*” ([emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), being the natural lord, reveals his distinct attributes as much as acceptable); now, āḻvār has become expert in enjoying his repeated mercy. *nodidal* – speaking.
- *ippattu adiyārrku aruḷ pēṟē* – This decad, for those who practiced/recited it, will lead to sarvēśvaran’s mercy as said in “*nediyān aruḷ sūdum padiyān*“. If īśvaran can give sādarmyam (equivalence in some aspects), why can’t āḻvār do the same?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

adiyen saraty ramanuja dasan
