## 10.6 Arul peruvar

## 10.6.1. Arul peruvar

*aruḷ peṟuvār adiyār tam adiyanēṟku āḻiyān aruḷ taruvān amaiginṟān adu namadu vidi vagaiyē iruḷ taru mā  jñālattuḷ inip piṟavi yān vēṇḍēn maruḷ oḻi nī mada nenjē vāttāṟṟān adi vaṇangē*

**Пословный перевод:**

aruḷ – his endless mercy; peṟuvār – those who are identified by receiving; adiyār tam – for those who have knowledge about śēśatvam which is the cause for that; adiyanēṟku – for me who is distinguished servitor; āḻiyān – just as he never abandons tiruvāḻi āḻvān (cakkarattāḻvār); aruḷ – the great favour of previous experience on his aspects; taruvān – one who bestows; amaiginṟān – being prepared for; adu – that (instead of doing as per his independent desire); namadu vidi vagaiyē – (since it is puruśārtam – goal desired by individual) is happening as per our command; iruḷ taru – giving ignorance; mā – vast; jñālattuḷ – in this world; ini – after receiving (his acceptance); piṟavi – taking birth (even if it is taken for the pleasure of bhagavān and bhāgavatas as said in tiruvāimoḻi 8.10.5 “iḻipattōdum udalinil piṟandu than sīr yān kaṟṟu“); yān vēṇḍēn – I who know his thoughts, am not desiring; madam – having desire to not give up attachment; nenjē – Oh heart!; maruḷ – bewilderment (of desiring independently to enjoy arcāvatāram here which is contrary to his desire); nī oḻi – try to avoid; vāttāṟṟān – one who is standing in tiruvāttāṟu to fulfil our desires; adi – divine feet; vaṇangu – worship him, agreeing with my desire

**Перевод:**

**Just as emperumān never abandons tiruvāḻi āḻvān, he is prepared to bestow the great favour of previous experience on his aspects, to me who is a distinguished servitor for those who are identified by receiving his endless mercy and who have knowledge about śēśatvam which is the cause for that; that is happening as per our command. After receiving his mercy, I, who know his thoughts, am not desiring to take birth in this vast world which gives ignorance. Oh heart which is having desire to not give up attachment! Try to avoid the bewilderment; worship the divine feet of the one who is standing in tiruvāttāṟu to fulfil our desires, agreeing with my desire.**

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. அருள் பெறுவார் அடியார் தம் அடியனேற்கு ஆழியான் அருள் தருவான் அமைகின்றான் அது நமது விதிவகையே இருள் தரு மா ஞாலத்துள் இனிப் பிறவி யான் வேண்டேன் மருள் ஒழி நீ மட நெஞ்சே வாட்டாற்றான் அடி வணங்கே aruḷ peṟuvār adiyār tam adiyanēṟku āḻiyān aruḷ taruvān amaiginṟān adu namadu vidi vagaiyē iruḷ taru mā  jñālattuḷ inip piṟavi yān vēṇḍēn maruḷ oḻi nī mada nenjē vāttāṟṟān adi vaṇangē*

- *aruḷ peṟuvār adiyār tam adiyanēṟku* – This is the reason \[for emperumān fulfilling my desire\]. There are some who are the recipients of sarvēśvaran’s great mercy; they are our lords. āḻvār is saying that the mercy he showed towards them is ready to flood upon us also. When a child engages in evil deeds, the parents will scold him/her, as in śrī bhagavat gītā 16.19 “*tānaham dviśata: krūrān*” (I push those evil persons into demoniac births); there are some who remain the recipient of his anger; unlike them, there are some who are recipients of his mercy as said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 10.10](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/10-10/) “*dadāmi*” (I bestow \[the knowledge\]); he showered upon us the same mercy which was showered upon them. \[Another explanation\] Though the king will interact in a royal manner outside, for the queen, he offers all his wealth and himself at her disposal; similarly, there are some to whom he fully offers himself and makes himself subservient to them; he showered upon us the same mercy which was showered upon all of them.
- *aruḷ peṟuvār adiyār tam adiyanēṟku* – Identity for both \[emperumān and āḻvār\].  āḻvār is the devotee of those who receive his mercy; emperumān is āḻiyān (one who holds cakkarattāḻvār); hence both are identified by emperumān’s devotees.
- *adiyanēṟku* – He only considered my words as in [tiruvāimoḻi 8.10.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/05/thiruvaimozhi-8-10-1-nedumarkadimai/) “*vidumāṟenbaden*” (why consider the ways to leave them?), [tiruvāimoḻi 8.10.10](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/05/thiruvaimozhi-8-10-10-vaykka-thamiyerku/) “*nīkkam illā adiyār tam adiyār adiyār adiyār em kōkkaḷ*” (for my associates and me, the servitors who are enjoying such lord without any separation, are the lords) and [tiruvāimoḻi 8.10.9](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/05/thiruvaimozhi-8-10-9-thamargal-kutta/) “*tamargaḷ tamargaḷ tamargaḷām sadirē vāykka*” (for us who are helpless in samsāra having the wealth of servitude towards the servitors of servitors of the blemiśless devotees of such emperumān, his mercy should occur); āḻvār thinks about his own true nature as said in periya tirumoḻi 2.6.10 “*adigaḷ adiyē ninaiyum adiyavargaḷ tam adiyān*” (the servitor of those devotees who always think about the divine feet of emperumān).
- *āḻiyān aruḷ taruvān amaiginṟān* – sarvēśvaran is eager to shower his great mercy towards us with full focus; he is seeing the divine chakra with one eye and āḻvār with another eye; he is saying “only if I can abandon my divine chakra, can I abandon you as well” as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 2.10.11](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/06/thiruvaimozhi-2-9-11-vidalil-chakkaraththu/) “*vidalil cakkarattu aṇṇalai mēval vidalil*” (The most magnanimous [nammāḻvār](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nammazhwar/) who cannot bear leaving [emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), approached his lord/master emperumān who never puts away his divine chakra).
- *āḻiyān* – He is of the nature that, he identifies himself through his devotees. He showed the collective mercy which is showered upon all of those devotees, upon me as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 19.38 “*asmābhi: tulyō bhavatu*” (let vibhīśaṇa be equal to us). They are “*aruḷ peṟuvār adiyārāna adiyār*” (those servitors who receive his mercy); and he is “*aruḷ taruvān amaiginṟān*” (waiting to grant his mercy).
- *amaiginṟān* – Half the problem is solved. He makes himself readily available to shower his mercy.

When asked “Since he is eager to shower his great mercy, and since he is the sarvēśvaran, what is the shortcoming?” āḻvār says,

- *adu namadu vidi vagaiyē* – While doing that, he is desiring to do it as per my command.
- *adu namadu vidi vagaiyē* – Previous ācāryas explain this as “he does it as per our bhājñam (fortune)”. emperumānār mercifully heard this and mercifully said “this view does not match with the subsequent mood in this decad; āḻvār is saying that emperumān is waiting to do as per āḻvār’s command”. Just as the same lakśmaṇa who eagerly desired in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 31.25 “*aham sarvam kariśyāmi*” (I will serve you both (perumāḷ and pirātti) in all the ways), also eagerly desired in śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 15.7 “*kriyatāmiti mām vada*” (lakśmaṇa to śrī rāma – order me in what should be done), emperumān too is eagerly waiting to follow āḻvār’s command. Why is āḻvār saying “*vidi vagaiyē*” (per my command) instead of “*namadu sol vagaiyē*” (per our words)? emperumān is fearing just like those who violate the command will fear for the result. Though he has no shortcomings in him to do as he desires, he will not carry the ātmā \[to paramapadam\] without the ātmā having the desire for the same. Being puruśōttama (best among men), he will not do that which will cause disrepute to his masculinity \[forcing something upon someone who does not desire for that\].
- *namadu vidi vagaiyē* – stōtra ratnam 42 “*tadā’nujānantamudāravīkśaṇai:”* (you who approve of those actions, by your merciful glances, in the same manner as you approve of actions requested in any manner by such viśvaksēna). nanjīyar mercifully said “I heard it when bhattar mercifully explained this”. As sēnai mudaliyār arrived with his robe, beard and stick in his hand and was about to enter the private quarters where emperumān was enjoying independently with his nācciyārs, he stopped that enjoyment and nācciyārs went and hid behind the throne. emperumān also welcomed him humbly and treated him just as kings would treat elderly commanders with great respect. sēnai mudaliyār too thought “We cannot be bottleneck for their enjoyment” and quickly requested regarding what is needed to be taken care of. in the administration of the \[material\] universes. emperumān enjoys the presence of sēnai mudaliyār even more than being with his nācciyārs; it is said in the same ślōkam “*priyēṇa*” (beloved). sēnai mudaliyār would briefly enlist the tasks as in “such and such person should be made brahmā; this person should be replaced”; emperumān will autorise the requests with his merciful glance as if saying “Whatever your highness says, everything is fine”. When this was beautifully narrated by bhattar, kidāmbi āccān and others \[who are not śiśyas of bhattar\] were all deeply became immersed; kidāmbi āccān would have great affection for bhattar. iḷaiyāḻvān asked kidāmbi āccān “Why are you interacting with bhattar in a more obedient manner than his śiśyas?” kidāmbi āccān mercifully replied “You did not see the other day. emperumānār gave a book in the hand of bhattar, made him recite a ślōkam in the divine presence of periya perumāḷ \[inside the garbhagruham (inner sanctum)\], came out of the barricade in front of the inner sanctum, mercifully looked around and told ‘all of you, our followers, should treat him \[bhattar\] as you would treat me”.

When asked “If sarvēśvaran is the one who is showering the mercy, that too as per our command, what is the shortcoming still?” āḻvār says,

*iruḷ …* – Now, you \[āḻvār’s heart\] just need to agree with him; this \[refusal to agree\] is the only shortcoming. I have decided to go along in his way and you too should do the same! When āḻvār’s heart asked “Why should you follow his way?” āḻvār says – This world is giving ignorance. samsāra will increasingly give ignornace as we continue to reside here; this world made even śrī prahlādāḻvān to oppose and fight emperumān.

- *ini* – Previously I was bewildered to say as in [tiruvāimoḻi 8.1.9](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/02/thiruvaimozhi-8-1-9-yanum-nidhane/) “*vān uyar inbam eydilen? maṟṟai naragamē eydilen?*” (so what, if I remain in paramapadam with great bliss or I remain in this hellish samsāram, which contrasts paramapadam?) Now I have eliminated that. When asked “Why should that be eliminated?” āḻvār says – Due to facilitating śrīvaiṣṇava sahavāsam (being together with śrīvaiṣṇavas) and due to great interest towards ugandaruḷina nilangaḷ (divyadēśams \[divine abodes\] where emperumān himself is eagerly residing out of his mercy), previously we thought “So what, if we are in paramapadam or in samsāram?” and wanted to simply remain in a place which is under his boundary \[as he is present everywhere, we thought it was to remain anywhere\]; but instead of getting either of those two aspects, it ended up in a contrary manner. After pondering upon the nature of samsāra which will bind one to matter and will fully engage in worldly matters such as śabda (sound) etc, I have determined that I should eliminate this bewilderment.
- *yān vēṇḍēn* – I have given up the attachment in my intellect; but if he places me here, I cannot do anything about it.

When the heart asks “So, what should I do?” āḻvār says,

- *maruḷ oḻi nī* – You have a thought, try to eliminate that. After having roamed around in this world and having all the hurdles eliminated as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 7.10.9](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/11/thiruvaimozhi-7-10-9-thivinai-ullaththin/) “*tīvinai uḷḷattin sārvallavāgit teḷivisumbēṟal uṟṟāl nāvin uḷḷum uḷḷattuḷḷum amainda toḻilin uḷḷum navinṟu* *yāvarum vandu vaṇangum poḻil tiruvāṟanviḷai adanai mēvi valanjeydu kai toḻak kūdungol? ennum en sindanaiyē*” (As the cruel sins no longer fit in the heart, even if I get to reach the supreme sky which has clarity, my heart which is in harmony with the mind, speech and matching acts is thinking to reach the abode of tiruvāṟanviḷai which is reached and vorśipped by residents of all places and which is having garden, and to worship with joined palms by engaging in favourable acts; will it occur?), when it is said “this is the route for paramapadam and this is the route for tiruvāṟanviḷai”, you may become bewildered thinking “when the attainable goal (bhagavān) himself has arrived here, should we not happily serve him here?”; try to eliminate that bewilderment. maruḷ – ignorance.

- *mada nenjē* – Instead of only seeing “the desirable emperumān is present right here”, should you not see me also?
- *vāttāṟṟān adi vaṇangē* – You pursue the way of emperumān who has arrived here as a well-wisher for us, and try to enjoy him; his arrival and residing in ugandaruḷina nilangaḷ (his divine abodes, where he is eagerly residing) is to carry us to paramapadam; you also try to follow his divine heart/intention.
- *adi vaṇangē* – Worśipping the divine feet means eliminating the situation of dual kings \[let him be the king and we will simply follow his desire\].

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 10.6.2. Vattarran adi vanangi

*vāttāṟṟān adi vaṇangi mā jñālap piṟappu aṟuppān kēttāyē mada nenjē! kēsavan em perumānai pāttāya pala pādi paḻa vinaigaḷ paṟṟaṟuttu nāttārōdu iyalvu oḻindu nāraṇanai naṇṇinamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

mā jñālam – in the vast world; piṟappu – connection with birth; aṟuppān – to eliminate; vāttāṟṟān – being āśrita sulabha (easily approachable for devotees) in tiruvāttāṟu; adi vaṇangi – surrendering unto the divine feet; kēsavan – being the one who eliminated kēśi who was a hurdle for enjoyment; emperumānai – similarly, one who eliminated our hurdles and engaged us in service; pala pāttu āya – many different types of songs; pādi – performing the kainkaryam (service) of singing; paḻa vinaigaḷ – avidyā (ignorance), karma (virtues/vices) etc which are present since time immemorial; paṟṟu aṟuttu – eliminating them with the impressions; nāttārōdu – with the worldly people who are filled with ahankāram (considering self to be body) etc; iyalvu – co-existence; oḻindu – eliminating; nāraṇanai – nārāyaṇa (who is unconditional relative and is ready to give us the result now); naṇṇinam – we approached; madam – being obedient and agreeing with me; nenjē – Oh heart!; kēttāyē – You have asked (about these chain of favours done by emperumān)!

**Перевод:**

**Surrendering unto the divine feet of the āśrita sulabha in tiruvāttāṟu who is present there to eliminate the connection with birth in this vast world, performing the kainkaryam of singing many different types of songs on the one who eliminated kēśi who was a hurdle for enjoyment and who similarly eliminated our hurdles and engaged us in service, eliminating avidyā, karma etc which are present since time immemorial with their impressions and co-existence with the worldly people who are filled with ahankāram, we approached nārāyaṇa. Oh heart which is obedient and agreeing with me! You have asked (about these chain of favours done by emperumān)!**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Second pāsuram. When asked \[by the heart\] – Why are you saying that you got this result by bhagavān’s krupai only? Did we not pray originally in tiruviruttam 1 “inninṟa nīrmai iniyām uṟāmai“? āḻvār says “Did we receive only as much as we prayed for?” வாட்டாற்றான் அடி வணங்கி மா ஞாலப் பிறப்பு அறுப்பான் கேட்டாயே மட நெஞ்சே! கேசவன் எம் பெருமானைப் பாட்டு ஆய பல பாடி பழ வினைகள் பற்று அறுத்து நாட்டாரோடு இயல்வு ஒழிந்து நாரணனை நண்ணினமே vāttāṟṟān adi vaṇangi mā jñālap piṟappu aṟuppān kēttāyē mada nenjē! kēsavan em perumānai pāttāya pala pādi paḻa vinaigaḷ paṟṟaṟuttu nāttārōdu iyalvu oḻindu nāraṇanai naṇṇinamē*

- *mā jñālap piṟappu aṟuppān – vāttāṟṟān adi vaṇangi – kēsavan emperumānaip pāttāya pala pādip paḻa vinaigaḷ paṟṟāṟuttu nāttārōdiyalvoḻindu nāraṇanai naṇṇinam – kēttāyē mada nenjē!* – Did we receive all of these by his mercy? Did we receive these by our praying to him? We only prayed for elimination of hurdles; my bad, you are not realising what we prayed for.
- *mā jñālap piṟappu aṟuppān* – We surrendered unto the divine feet of sarvēśvara and only prayed “Our connection with samsāram should be eliminated”. But see! Beyond that, he has also accepted our service. He accepted our vācika kainkaryam (service by speech).
- *kēsavan emperumānai* – sarvēśvaran who is the killer of kēśi \[the demon who came in the form of a horse\]; one who is being our lord, by  eliminating our hurdles just as he eliminated kēśi and establishing our servitude; alternatively, one who showed his beautiful kēśa (hair) and accepted our service.

Is that all?

- *pāttāya pala pādi* – He made us sing his glories in these pāsurams to have great devotees who are praised in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.5.11](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/08/thiruvaimozhi-1-5-11-male-maya/) “*pālēy tamiḻar isaikārar pattar paravum āyiram*” (sweet milk like pāsurams which are celebrated by those who are well-versed in tamiḻ, those who are well-versed in music and can sing this and those devotees who understand the meaning), pursue him. You see, while we prayed “you should eliminate our hurdles and engage us in your service”, he engaged us in kainkaryam even while the hurdles \[this existence in samsāra\] were present.
- *pādip paḻa vinaigaḷ paṟṟaṟuttu* – As we engage in service for him, you have seen that all of hurdles for attainment of the goal, which were accumulated since time immemorial such as avidyā (ignorance) etc, are gone. This is the neem juice drink which he drank to eliminate his \[āḻvār’s\] hurdles \[sarcasm\]. viṣṇu darmam “*mēru mantara mātrō’pi rāśi: pāpasya karmaṇa:* ***kēśavam vaidyam****āsātya durvyātiriva nacyati* ” (just as a serious disease disappears on seeing a good medical practitioner, the bundles of sins of a person, even if they are as much as mēru mountain, will disappear once the person attains kēśavan) – the karma accumulated by the ātmā for a long time can be eliminated by sarvaśakta (omnipotent emperumān) in a moment.
- *nāttārōdu iyalvoḻindu* – You have seen that we have become detached from the people of this world who run around seeking food, clothes etc as said in perumāḷ tirumoḻi 3.4 “*uṇḍiyē udaiyē ugandōdum immaṇḍalattodum kūduvadillai yān*“. Our connection with those who are filled with ahankāram (considering body to be self) and mamakāram (considering oneself to be independent) as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 2-9-9](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/06/thiruvaimozhi-2-9-9-yane-ennai/) “*yānē endanadē enṟirundēn*” (I remained as if I were everything and everything were mine), was eliminated. You have seen that emperumān has made us say as in [tiruvāsiriyam 6](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/11/thiruvasiriyam-6/) “*Oh Oh ulaginadiyalvē*” (this is the nature of this world), [tiruvāimoḻi 4.9.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/04/thiruvaimozhi-4-9-1-nannadhar-muruvalippa/) “*ivai enna ulagiyaṟkai*” (how strange are these worldly aspects?), [tiruvāimoḻi 4.9.7](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/04/thiruvaimozhi-4-9-7-aye-ivvulagaththu/) “*kodu ulagam kāttēlē*” (hide the cruel world from me); he is the one who said in [tiruvāimoḻi 8.2.7](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/02/thiruvaimozhi-8-2-7-mal-ari-kesavan/) “*ungaḷōdu engaḷ idaiyillaiyē*” (there is no relationship for me with you).
- *nāraṇanai naṇṇinam* – Did we just stop at leaving the worldly relatives who were acquired due to karma? We also attained the unconditional relative \[bhagavān\]. He is pursuing those who were given by him, in a different form \[after giving up worldly people here, he still is connected with them through bhagavān, who is known as nārāyaṇa who is the antarātmā of all entities\].  It is for this reason that this world is enjoyable for muktātmās  (liberated souls). This \[pursuing emperumān nārāyaṇan\] is similar to giving up the thought of independent enjoyment, and enjoying \[all the wealth\] along with the  father \[who is the real owner of the wealth\]. Not pursuing nārāyaṇa even when he is readily available is similar to dying due to swollen heels while huge treasure is available right under one’s bed.
- *kēttāyē mada nenjē* – Thinking about the greatness of the result we have acquired, are you prideful that we have attained what is impossible to attain? Are you enjoying this? As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam “*saumitrē bhukśava*” (son of sumitrā! Enjoy as per your desire) and śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 94.18 “*vaidēhi ramasē kaścit*” (Oh descendant of janaka clan! Are you enjoying along with me in citrakūtam?).

Should be arranged as “*mā jñālap piṟappaṟuppān – kēsavan emperumānan – vāttāṟṟān adi vaṇangi – pāttāya pala pādip paḻa vinaigaḷ paṟṟaṟuttu nāttārōdiyalvoḻindu nāraṇanai naṇṇinam – kēttāyē mada nenjē*“.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 10.6.3. Nanninnam narayananai

*naṇṇinam nārāyaṇanai nāmangaḷ pala solli maṇ ulagil vaḷam mikka vāttāṟṟān vandu inṟu viṇ ulagam taruvānāy viraiginṟān vidi vagaiyē eṇṇinavāṟu āgā ik karumangaḷ ennenjē!*

**Пословный перевод:**

en nenjē – Oh heart which is a tool for my enjoyment!; pala nāmangaḷ – many divine names; solli – reciting; nārāyaṇanai – the unconditional relative who has the divine name nārāyaṇa (which is the root of all his divine names); naṇṇinam – got to surrender unto him; maṇ ulagail – on this earth; vaḷam – having the wealth of qualities such as śeelam (simplicity), saulabhyam (easy approacability) etc; mikka – having abundance; vāttāṟṟān – one who is standing in tiruvāttāṟu; vandu – arrived (without my prayer, on his own desire); inṟu – today (without any reason on my side); viṇ ulagam – paramapadam; vidi vagaiyē – with our permission; taruvān āy – to bestow; viraiginṟān – he is rushing; ikkarumangaḷ – these activities; eṇṇina āṟu āgā – instead of the ways we thought (our going towards him, our praying to him, our craving for it and our looking at his thoughts), it is happening in the way of his coming towards us, his desiring us, his craving for us and his looking at our thoughts

**Перевод:**

**Oh heart which is a tool for my enjoyment! We got to surrender unto the unconditional relative who has the divine name nārāyaṇa, reciting his many divine names; he has arrived on this wealth and is standing in tiruvāttāṟu with abundance of wealth of qualities such as śeelam, saulabhyam etc, and is rushing to bestow paramapadam to us with our permission; instead of the ways we thought, it is happening in the way of his coming towards us, his desiring us, his craving for us and his looking at our thoughts.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Third pāsuram. āḻvār says “Oh heart! While we remain thinking that emperumān is capable of pursuing us, why are the results different?”. நண்ணினம் நாராயணனை நாமங்கள் பல சொல்லி மண் உலகில் வளம் மிக்க வாட்டாற்றான் வந்து இன்று விண் உலகம் தருவானாய் விரைகின்றான் விதி வகையே எண்ணினவாறு ஆகா இக் கருமங்கள் என் நெஞ்சே! naṇṇinam nārāyaṇanai nāmangaḷ pala solli maṇ ulagil vaḷam mikka vāttāṟṟān vandu inṟu viṇ ulagam taruvānāy viraiginṟān vidi vagaiyē eṇṇinavāṟu āgā ik karumangaḷ ennenjē!*

- *nārāyaṇanai nāmangaḷ pala solli – naṇṇinam* – We attained the apt lord.
- *nāmangaḷ pala solli* – To attain the goal \[of liberation and eternal kainkaryam\], this divine name nārāyaṇa itself is enough as said in “*namō nārāyaṇāyēti mantras sarvārta sādaka:*” (This aśtākśara mantram is sufficient to attain all results). Triggered by the love, reciting many divine names.
- *maṇ ulagil …* – One who has tiruvāttāṟu which has more abundance \[of opulence\] than paramapadam, as his identity.
- *vaḷam* – Wealth. Since there are many entities to be protected, there is abundance of wealth for the rakśaka (protector), here; since there is no break in kainkaryam, there is abundance of wealth for the servitor, here.
- *vandu* – Arriving here through all the abodes which we would have had to travel to reach him.
- *inṟu* – Until yesterday, there was nothing on our side to get such result; we have seen this wonderful dawn today.
- *viṇ ulagam taruvānāy* – He is not stopping with just allocating some place for us in paramapadam. He is terminating the status quo of the abode being common for all as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 3.9.9](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/10/thiruvaimozhi-3-9-9-vay-kondu/) “*vānavar nādu*” (the spiritual realm which is owned by nityasūris) and tiruvāimoḻi 10.9.6 “*āṇmingaḷ vānagam*” (rule over the spiritual realm), and is eager to bestow it to us exclusively. emperumān’s thought is that āḻvār does not qualify to remain in this world which goes through creation and annihilation. Bestowing it on āḻvār exclusively means, giving him as he prayed in [tiruvāimoḻi 3.3.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/08/thiruvaimozhi-3-3-1-ozhivil-kalam/) “*vaḻuvilā adimai*” (continuous kainkaryam).
- *viraiginṟān* – He is not relaxed like us. We are relaxed at times as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 2.9.5](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/06/thiruvaimozhi-2-9-5-sirappil-vidu/) “*siṟappil vīdu – iṟappil eyduga eydaṟka*” (After shedding this body, let me reach paramapadam or not). \[On the other hand\] emperumān has packed all the luggage ahead of āḻvār, and when āḻvār was late, he went back to āḻvār and urged “āḻvīr! Are you ready? Are you ready?” As emperumān let āḻvār remain here for a particular purpose \[of singing tiruvāimoḻi\] and as that purpose is coming close to an end, emperumān is urging āḻvār to go. His urge is so much that, even after being sarvaśaktan, he cannot wait for orderly fulfilment of the purpose and āḻvār leaving after that. He is unable to remain patient for the task which was vowed by himself.

When asked “Let him accomplish what he desires; if he is sarvēśvaran who is omnipotent, why is he rushing here?” āḻvār says,

- *vidi vagaiyē* – He is thinking to bestow us paramapadam as per our command. āḻvār himself said in [tiruvāimoḻi 2.9.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/06/thiruvaimozhi-2-9-1-emma-vittu/) “*emmā vīttut tiṟamum seppam*” (I won’t ask for the form of liberation that is great in all ways); giving up such thought, if he forces emperumān to bestow liberation as he did in tiruvāimoḻi 10.10.6 “*uṇḍittāy ini uṇḍoḻiyāy*” (You enjoyed me before, now you enjoy me fully) and tiruvāimoḻi 10.10.2 “*tiruvāṇai ninnāṇai*” (I vow by śrī mahālakśmi, I vow by you – you should bestow, you should accept me), emperumān was willing to bestow it.
- *vidi vagaiyē – viṇṇulagam taruvānāy viraiginṟān* – Before āḻvār acquired the taste for emperumān, emperumān tried to corner āḻvār with great urge; after acquiring the taste, āḻvār pursued emperumān with great urge; seeing that emperumān acquired even greater urge, which is way beyond āḻvār’s urge; seeing that, āḻvār becomes amazed. emperumān remains relaxed only until ātmā acquires the taste for him; once the taste is acquired, emperumān will rush to make the ātmā attain the result fully. Wouldn’t the owner rush to acquire the owned?
- *eṇṇina āṟu āgā* – Did we not pray only for relief from suffering as said in tiruviruttam 1 “*inninṟa nīrmai ini yām uṟāmai*” (I cannot bear this lovlife any more)? Did we think that he would rush to attain me?
- *ikkarumangaḷ* – In bhagavat viśayam, the attainment of result is not as per one’s expectation. If we ask some worldly people to help us in accomplishing some task, we have to follow up with them until the task is accomplished; \[oh heart!\] do not think like that in bhagavat viśayam.
- *en nenjē* – Did we not get him to rush towards our task, due to your proper disposition towards him?  Did you not become the cause for mōkśam (liberation) instead of bandam (bondage)? Are you not the cause for this abundance?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 10.6.4. En nenjattul irundu

*en enjattu uḷ irundu ingu irum tamiḻ nūl ivai moḻinduval nenjattu iraṇiyanai mārvu idanda vāttāṟṟānman anja pāradattup pāṇḍavarkkāp padai tottānnal nenjē! nam perumān namakku aruḷ tān seyvānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

nal nenjē – Oh heart which has attachment for bhagavat viśayam!; vannenjattu – hard-hearted (which not only lacks attachment, but also is filled with hatred); iraṇiyanai – hiraṇya; mārvu idanda – plucked the heart where his mind is present; vāttāṟṟān – being present in tiruvāttāṟu; man – all the kings; anja – to fear; bāradattu – in mahābhārata battle; pāṇḍavarkku A – for pāṇḍavas; padai tottān – having the partiality to take up arms (after vowing not to do so); namperumān – being our lord (by these acts); en nenjattu – attracting my heart (which was focussed elsewhere); uḷ irundu – remaining fixed inside; ingu – in this stay; irum – huge (to be greatly distinguished); tamiḻ – in drāvida (tamiḻ) language; nūl – in the form of śāstram; ivai – this tiruvāimoḻi which is having imperceivable enjoyability; moḻindu – mercifully speaking, as the propagator; namakku – for us; aruḷ – great favours; tān seyvānē – was eager to do

**Перевод:**

**Oh heart which has attachment for bhagavat viśayam! emperumān who plucked the heart of the hard-hearted hiraṇya where his mind is present, is present in tiruvāttāṟu; he is our lord who created fear in all the kings by showing his partiality to take up arms during the mahābhārata battle; such emperumān, remaining fixed in staying inside my heart and attracting it, as the propagator, mercifully spoke this tiruvāimoḻi which is having imperceivable enjoyability, which is in the form of a great śāstram in tamiḻ language and was eager to do great favours for us.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.a

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Fourth pāsuram. When asked “Will sarvēśvaran’s commitment of fulfilling our desire as per our command, happen?” āḻvār says “If one considers his āśrita pāratantriyam (dependence on his devotees), nothing is impossible”. என் நெஞ்சத்து உள் இருந்து இங்கு இரும் தமிழ் நூல் இவை மொழிந்துவல் நெஞ்சத்து இரணியனை மார்வு இடந்த வாட்டாற்றான்மன் அஞ்ச பாரதத்துப் பாண்டவர்க்காப் படை தொட்டான்நல் நெஞ்சே! நம் பெருமான் நமக்கு அருள் தான் செய்வானே en enjattu uḷ irundu ingu irum tamiḻ nūl ivai moḻinduval nenjattu iraṇiyanai mārvu idanda vāttāṟṟānman anja pāradattup pāṇḍavarkkāp padai tottānnal nenjē! nam perumān namakku aruḷ tān seyvānē*

- *en nenjattu* – āḻvār is upset with his heart saying “*ennenju*” (my heart) since it was engaged in worldly pleasures based on śabdam (sound) etc in this samsāram (material realm) since time immemorial. But emperumān is falling head-over-heels on āḻvār’s heart since āḻvār claimed ownership, ignoring the goodness and faults of the heart. āḻvār tried to move out of his heart; emperumān considered that \[his ownership\] as the reason and tried to enter it.
- *uḷ* – Just as tired/thirsty person would push away the water from the top and immerse deeply into a river, emperumān entered the heart.
- *irundu* – He \[emperumān\] did not think that there is another abode \[paramapadam\] for him, and should go there. He remained in āḻvār’s heart, like a tree.
- *ingu* – He created new wealth here \[in samsāram\] which is not present there \[paramapadam\] \[That is, he revealed tiruvāimoḻi through āḻvār here\].
- *irum tamiḻ* – The goodness of this prabandam is so vast that it is even beyond the capacity of paramapadam. It is said in tiruvāimoḻi 10.6.11 “*kēttārār*” (They will never satiate hearing tiruvāimoḻi – would hear it repeatedly).
- *nūl* – This prabandam remains a role model for poets of subsequent times. Though āḻvār spoke this in sorrow, emperumān made āḻvār speak it with all necessary qualities.
- *ivai* – āmidst saying “emperumān did this”, āḻvār himself enjoys thinking about tiruvāimoḻi and says “ivai”.
- *moḻindu* – Even when one learns and recites poems of another author, he will have attachment and be possessive about the same; āḻvār is not even claiming such ownership. He is not even valuing his own words in [tiruvāimoḻi 7.9.2](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/11/thiruvaimozhi-7-9-2-en-solli-nirpan/) “*en mun sollum*” (emperumān who is reciting pāsurams before me \[so that I can repeat them\]).
- *vannenjattu …* – tiruvāttāṟṟān (emperumān in tiruvāttāṟu) who effortlessly plucked the hard heart of hiraṇya whose strong heart is so angry on hearing about bhagavat viśayam. āḻvār is implying that emperumān who helped the son when the father became inimical, will certainly help āḻvār too. He dug and plucked the spot \[heart\] where hiraṇya’s pride was present.
- *vāttāṟṟān* – One who is residing in tiruvāttāṟu to help the people of subsequent times. Just as he eliminated the sorrow of his \[hiraṇya’s, prahlāda’s\] heart, he is standing here to eliminate the sorrow in our hearts.
- *man anja* – To have the great warriors who are known as atirata and mahārata \[different titles for powerful warriors\] succumb just like a fox will do while seeing a lion. To instill fear in all of the kings.
- *pāṇḍavarkkāy* – Being their servitor to be said as in periya tirumoḻi 2.2.3 “*innār tūdan*” (their messenger).
- *padai tottān* – It is not that he took up arms \[chakra\] and then himself disarmed; he just abandoned his own vow \[of not using the arms\]; he just did not use them. \[How did you take up arms? Did you not vow not to take up arms?\] He is known as satya sankalpa (one with unfailing vow) only in the cases other than for his devotees; he gave up arms since arjuna prayed “It will cause disrepute to me that you launched arms, Why don’t you give up?” \[periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 4.2.7 is explained here\] *mannar maṟuga …* – When arjuna’s horses became tired, since kriṣṇa knows where to find water in the ground, he spotted it, shot vāruṇāstram on the ground to bring out the water, fed water to horses, caressed them, got them back on their feet and got them ready. All the kings saw this and became fearful thinking “How can we win over arjuna when kriṣṇa is so partial towards arjuna?” *mun angu ninṟu mōḻai eḻuvitta* – He got the water to bubble, to be seen by everyone. As the heart meditated upon his āśrita pāratantriyam, the heart became favourable.
- *nannenjē …* – You are there to say no; he is there to say yes; his krupai (mercy) is there to instigate him \[towards us\].
- *namperumān* – He who is our lord, will shower his mercy certainly; he will certainly bestow the result as said in “*viṇṇulagam taruvānāy viraginṟān*“; this is certain. You are there to agree; he is there to make us agree; the relationship is present to act according to the agreement; is there any shortcoming for our result now?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 10.6.5. Vanera valitanda

*vān ēṟa vaḻi tanda vāttāṟṟān paṇi vagaiyē nān ēṟap peṟuginṟēn naragattai nagu nenjē! tēn ēṟu malart tuḷavam tigaḻ pādan seḻum paṟavai tān ēṟit tirivāna tāḷiṇai en talai mēlē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vān ēṟa – to go to paramapadam; vaḻi tanda – created the arcirādi mārgam \[path\] and presented it (as said in tiruvāimoḻi 3.9.3 “pōm vaḻiyait tarum“); vāttāṟṟān – one who is residing in tiruvāttāṟu; paṇi vagaiyē – as said in tiruvāimoḻi 10.4.9 “paṇḍē paraman paṇitta paṇi vagaiyē”; nān – I (who follow his thought fully); ēṟa – to climb up; peṟuginṟēn – getting it; tēn – honey; ēṟu – being in abundance; malart tuḷavam – tiruttuḻāy (tuḷasi) having flower; tigaḻ pādan – one with divine feet where such tuḷasi shines freshly; seḻum paṟavai – periya tiruvadi (garudāḻvār) who has an attractive form; tān ēṟit tirivān – one who climbs and rides for the sake of his devotees, his; attāḷ iṇai – both of those enjoyable divine feet; en talai mēlē – have decorated my head; nenjē – Oh heart!; naragattai – this samsāra; nagu – see that you (disdainfully) laugh at

**Перевод:**

**emperumān who is residing in tiruvāttāṟu created the arcirādi mārgam and presented it to me to go to paramapadam; I am set to climb up there as said in tiruvāimoḻi 10.4.9 “paṇḍē paraman paṇitta paṇi vagaiyē“; my head is decorated with the enjoyable divine feet of emperumān who is adorning tiruttuḻāy (tuḷasi) having flower with abundance of honey, and who climbs and rides periya tiruvadi who has an attractive form, for the sake of his devotees. Oh heart! You see that you laugh at this samsāra.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Fifth pāsuram. āḻvār says “I am set to travel through the arcirādi gati (the illuminated path starting with arcis) which he has kept for his devotees to reach paramapadam; I also got to be accepted by him as an eternal devotee”. வான் ஏற வழி தந்த வாட்டாற்றான் பணி வகையே நான் ஏறப் பெறுகின்றேன் நரகத்தை நகு நெஞ்சே! தேன் ஏறு மலர்த் துளவம் திகழ் பாதன் செழும் பறவை தான் ஏறித் திரிவான தாள் இணை என் தலை மேலே vān ēṟa vaḻi tanda vāttāṟṟān paṇi vagaiyē nān ēṟap peṟuginṟēn naragattai nagu nenjē! tēn ēṟu malart tuḷavam tigaḻ pādan seḻum paṟavai tān ēṟit tirivāna tāḷiṇai en talai mēlē*

- *vān ēṟa …* – One who gave arcirādi mārgam to travel through and reach paramapadam. The fame of arcirādi mārgam is such that, even more than reaching paramapadam, the path itself is enjoyable. Its distinguished nature is that one will cherish the travel as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 3.9.3](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/10/thiruvaimozhi-3-9-3-ozhivonrilladha/) “*pōm vaḻiyait tarum*” (one who gives the path to travel to paramapadam).
- *vāttāṟṟān* – This is the abode where emperumān worked for this result.
- *paṇi vagaiyē* – As per his divine heart; that is, āḻvār is talking about śrī bhagavat gītā 18.66 “*māmēkam śaraṇam vraja*” (Surrender unto me only); he already said in [tiruvāimoḻi 10.4.9](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/11/thiruvaimozhi-10-4-9-kanden/) “*paṇḍē paraman paṇitta paṇi vagaiyē*” (Previously, sarvēśvaran who is greater than all, mercifully explained the mantra rahasya prakāram); āḻvār could also be talking about what is said in [tiruvāimoḻi 9.10.5](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/09/thiruvaimozhi-9-10-5-saranam-agum/) “*maraṇamānāl*” (when body falls, one will be liberated).
- *nān ēṟap peṟuginṟēn* – I, who would send you as messenger and wait for you as said in tiruviruttam 30 “*kaṇṇan vaigundanōdu ennenjināraik kaṇḍāl*” (If you see my honourable heart with kriṣṇa, the lord of śrīvaikuṇṭam), am saying these words now to you \[that I am going to śrīvaikuṇṭam\]!
- *nān …* – I am going to paramapadam.

When heart asked “What should I do now?” āḻvār says,

- *naragattai nagu nenjē* – Don’t rush thinking that you have attained the apt abode! Look at his samsāram which had us as citizens and humiliated us for a long time, and laugh at it. Recollect the words of piḷḷai aḻagiya maṇavāḷap perumāḷ araiyar, where he laughed at a wound and spoke \[that is, when he was ascending to paramapadam, he looked at the wound and said “I have defeated you”\]. samkśēpa rāmāyaṇam 68 “*tēna nātēna mahatā nirjagāma harīśvara:*” (Hearing the loud screaming of sugrīva, vāli, the king of monkeys, came out) – As sugrīva mahāraja shouted loud to call vāli, though tārā stopped vāli saying “sugrīva who was previously humiliated is now shouting out with confidence, this cannot happen without a reason; you should not leave at this bad time”, being a kśatriya, vāli came out since he cannot bear an insult and asked “Why are you shouting out so loud? You have given up the cowardice which you had and are confident; there must be a reason for this; still, you will be a good prey, in this manner”. *harīśvara:* (king of monkeys) – Previously he had never let anyone survive after shouting out at him. Similarly, drawing strength from emperumān, one will laugh at samsāram, patting on the arms and saying “I have won over you”. \[Only\] For the ignorant ones, naraka indicates the region controlled by yama et al. samsāram is indicated \[by āḻvār himself\] as in [tiruvāimoḻi 8.1.9](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/02/thiruvaimozhi-8-1-9-yanum-nidhane/) “*maṟṟai naragam*” (the other place, hellish samsāram); this \[narakam – samsāram\] is opposite to what is said in the same pāsuram as “*vānuyar inbam*” (the great bliss in paramapadam).

When asked “Did we attain the apt target, so that we can clap our hands and laugh at samsāram?” āḻvār says,

- *tēnēṟu …* – One who has the shining divine feet which has tiruttuḻāy with flower where honey flows increasingly as days go by, just as overflowing flood.
- *seḻum paṟavai* – tiruvadi (garudāḻvār) who has a cool and attractive form due to being together with emperumān. With this, the result of the togetherness with sarvēśvaran for the jīvātmā is highlighted.
- *tān ēṟit tirivāna* – Not just for the sake of garudāḻvār, but since it is pleasing for emperumān to be on garudāḻvār, he roams around on garudāḻvār.
- *tān ēṟit tirivāna tāḷ iṇai en talai mēlē* – emperumān placed his divine feet exclusively on my head instead of having them on the divine shoulder of garudāḻvār and my head. We need not feel bad for garudāḻvār’s loss, since it was garudāḻvār who brought emperumān and handed over to āḻvār. Hence garudāḻvār’s greatness only increased.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 10.6.6. Talaimela talinaigal

*talai mēla tāḷ iṇaigaḷ tāmaraikkaṇ en ammān nilai pērān en nenjattu eppoḻudum em perumān malai mādattu aravu aṇai mēl vāttāṟṟān madam mikka kolai yānai maruppu osittān kurai kaḻalgaḷ kuṟuginamē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tāḷ iṇaigaḷ – his divine feet; talai mēla – are on my head; tāmaraik kaṇ – having lotus like reddish divine eyes; en ammān – my svāmy (lord) who considers acquiring me as his great benefit; en nenjattu – in my heart; eppoḻudum – always; nilai pēṟān – not moving from his position; emperumān – being the greatest of all, due to remaining firm in me; malai – like a mountain; mādam – having mansions; vāttāṟu – in tiruvāttāṟu; aravaṇai mēlān – mercifully resting on the divine serpent mattress; madam mikka – heavily intoxicated; kolai – intent of killing; yānai – kuvalyāpīdam; maruppu osittān – just as he broke the tusks, he eliminated my hurdles too, his; kurai – the sound (of his valorous anklet); kaḻalgaḷ – divine feet; kuṟuginam – got to reach

**Перевод:**

**emperumān’s divine feet are on my head; my svāmy who is having lotus like reddish divine eyes and who considers acquiring me as his great benefit, is not moving from his position in my heart always; he is the greatest of all, due to remaining firm in me; he is mercifully resting on the divine serpent mattress in tiruvāttāṟu which is having mountain like mansions; I got to reach the resounding divine feet of such emperumān who eliminated my hurdles just as he broke the tusks of kuvalayāpīdam which was heavily intoxicated and was intent on killing.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Sixth pāsuram. āḻvār says “We got to reach the divine feet of emperumān who is present in tiruvāttāṟu and who will not let go of me in any way”. தலை மேல தாள் இணைகள் தாமரைக்கண் என் அம்மான் நிலை பேரான் என் நெஞ்சத்து எப்பொழுதும் எம் பெருமான் மலை மாடத்து அரவு அணை மேல் வாட்டாற்றான் மதம் மிக்க கொலை யானை மருப்பு ஒசித்தான் குரை கழல்கள் குறுகினமே talai mēla tāḷ iṇaigaḷ tāmaraikkaṇ en ammān nilai pērān en nenjattu eppoḻudum em perumān malai mādattu aravu aṇai mēl vāttāṟṟān madam mikka kolai yānai maruppu osittān kurai kaḻalgaḷ kuṟuginamē*

- *talai mēla tāḷ iṇaigaḷ* – As I prayed in [tiruvāimoḻi 2.9.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/06/thiruvaimozhi-2-9-1-emma-vittu/) “*nin semmā pāda paṟput talai sērttu*” (placing your reddish divine lotus feet on my head) and [tiruvāimoḻi 9.2.2](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/06/thiruvaimozhi-9-2-2-kudik-kidandhu/) “*pāda pangayamē talaikkaṇiyāy*” (your lotus feet are the decoration for my head), he decorated my head with his beautiful divine feet.
- *tāmaraik kaṇ ennammān* – He stood in front of me, gave a cool glance and won over me as said in “*jitam*” (victory).
- *nilai pērān en nenjattu* – He is doing all of these without leaving my heart. As saubari assumed 50 forms, as ātmā would assume many forms to enjoy him, emperumān assumed many divine forms to enjoy āḻvār.
- *eppoḻudum* – He pursued all the options which I pursued to enjoy him as I did in [tiruvāimoḻi 2.5.4](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/03/thiruvaimozhi-2-5-4-epporulum-thanay/) “*eppoḻudum nāḷ tingaḷ āṇḍu ūḻi ūḻi*” (every moment, day, month, year and yuga cycle). He manifested all of his omnipotence. He did everything such as remaining in my heart, standing in front of me, placing his divine feet on my head etc simultaneously.
- *emperumān* – The owner sustaining himself by acquiring his possession is \[higher and\] not the same as the property sustaining itself by acquiring the owner.
- *malai …* – emperumān who is mercifully resting on tiruvanantāḻvān (ādiśēśan) in tiruvāttāṟu  which is having mansions which appear as if they are carved out of mountains. With this, the attainable goal is explained as highlighted in paryanka vidyā \[scripture which narrates how śrīman nārāyaṇan is present on ādiśēśa throne\].
- *madam …* – All the hurdles for our enjoyment will see the same fate that was faced by kuvalayāpīdam. As emperumān eliminates the ātmā’s hurdles, the ātmā will get to enjoy him.
- *kurai kaḻalgaḷ kuṟuginam* – The sound of the ornaments is heard. We attained what we prayed in [tiruvāimoḻi 6.9.9](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/06/thiruvaimozhi-6-9-9-avi-thigaikka/) “*tadandāmaraigatkē kūvik koḷḷum kālam innam kuṟugādō?*” (Will the time to invite me to engage in those divine feet, not happen soon, even at this stage?)

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 10.6.7. Kurai kalalgal

*kurai kaḻalgaḷ kuṟuginam nam gōvindan kudi koṇḍān tirai kuḻuvu kadal pudai sūḻ ten nāttut tiladam anna varai kuḻuvu maṇi māda vāttāṟṟān malar adi mēl virai kuḻuvu naṟum tuḷavam meynninṟu kamaḻumē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kurai – distinguished; kaḻalgaḷ – divine feet; kuṟuginam – we got to reach; nam – obedient towards us; gōvindan – kriṣṇa; kudi – as his residence; koṇḍān – accepted; tirai – waves; kuḻuvu – well gathered; kadal – by ocean; pudai – in close proximity; sūḻ – surrounded; tennādu – for southern region; tiladam anna – like tilakam (decoration on forehead); varai kuḻuvu – resembling plenty of mountains; maṇi mādam – having gem-studded mansions; vāttāṟṟān – one who is mercifully residing in tiruvāttāṟu, his; malar adi mēl – on the divine feet which are ultimately enjoyable like blossomed lotus; virai – flower buds; kuḻuvu – well gathered; naṟum tuḷabam – nicely smelling tiruttuḻāy (tuḷasi); mey ninṟu – remaining firmly on my body; kamaḻum – fragrance is emanating

**Перевод:**

**We got to reach his distinguished divine feet; kriṣṇa who is obedient towards us accepted my heart as his residence; emperumān is mercifully residing in tiruvāttāṟu which is surrounded by ocean with well gathered waves, in close proximity, which is like the tilakam for southern region. and which is having gem-studded mansions which are resembling a range of mountains; the fragrance of the nicely smelling tiruttuḻāy with well gathered flower buds which are on such emperumān’s divine feet, which are ultimately enjoyable like blossomed lotus, is firmly remaining on my body and emanating from my body.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Seventh pāsuram. When asked “How do you know that you have reached him?” āḻvār says “Can’t you see that my body is smelling of the sandal wood paste applied on him?” குரை கழல்கள் குறுகினம் நம் கோவிந்தன் குடி கொண்டான் திரை குழுவு கடல் புடை சூழ் தென் நாட்டுத் திலதம் அன்ன வரை குழுவு மணி மாட வாட்டாற்றான் மலர் அடிமேல் விரை குழுவு நறும் துளவம் மெய்ந்நின்று கமழுமே kurai kaḻalgaḷ kuṟuginam nam gōvindan kudi koṇḍān tirai kuḻuvu kadal pudai sūḻ then nāttut tiladam anna varai kuḻuvu maṇi māda vāttāṟṟān malar adi mēl virai kuḻuvu naṟum tuḷavam meynninṟu kamaḻumē*

- *kurai kaḻalgaḷ kuṟuginam* – I am not saying we are getting close, we have already reached.
- *nam gōvindan* – kriṣṇa who is famously known as being owned by his devotees.
- *gōvindan kudi koṇḍān* – As said in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 5.2.10 “*aravattamaḷiyinōdum aḻagiya pāṟkadalōdum aravindap pāvaiyum tānum agam padi vandu pugundu*” (emperumān along with śrī mahālakśmi, entered my heart with his serpent mattress and beautiful milky ocean), kriṣṇa entered āḻvār’s heart with the five lakh families of tiruvāyppādi (gōkulam).
- *tirai …* – tiruvāttāṟu is surrounded by ocean filled with waves, is like tilakam for the southern region and is having gem-studded mansions which resemble closely packed mountains; sarvēśvaran is having such tiruvāttāṟu as his abode; such emperumān’s.
- *malar adi mēl* – Abundantly fragrant tiruttuḻāy which is on the divine feet which have freshness, coolness and fragrance.
- *mey ninṟu kamaḻumē* – My body is nicely smelling, forever. āḻvār is saying on his own words what was said in tōḻi bhāvam (mood of female friend) as in [tiruvāimoḻi 8.9.10](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/05/thiruvaimozhi-8-9-10-anri-marror-upayam/) “*anṟi maṟṟōr upāyam …*” (What other means is there for her who is having the fragrance of beautiful, cool tiruttuḻāy?) and in tāyār bhāvam (mood of mother) as in [tiruvāimoḻi 4.4.3](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/02/thiruvaimozhi-4-4-3-ariyum-sendhiyai/) “*veṟikoḷ tuḻāy malar nāṟum*” (tiruttuḻāy from her is emitting abundance of fragrance).
- *mey ninṟu kamaḻumē* – If you would like to know the truth in my words, can you not smell my body?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 10.6.8. Meynninru

*meynninṟu kamaḻ tuḷava virai ēṟu tirumudiyan kainninṟa cakkarattan karudum idam porudu punal mainninṟa varai pōlum tiru uruva vāttāṟṟāṟku en nanṟi seydēnō en nenjil tigaḻvaduvē?*

**Пословный перевод:**

mey ninṟu – remaining fully on the divine form; kamaḻ tuḷavam – tiruttuḻāy which is spreading the fragrance, its; virai – pleasing smell; ēṟu – rising; tirumudiyan – having crown; karudum idam – going where his divine heart desires; porudu – attack; kai ninṟa – (returning as said in “rāma pārśvam jagāma“) and staying on the divine hand; cakkarattan – being the one with the divine chakra; punal – like ocean water; ninṟa – firm; mai – having blackish complexion; varai pōlum – like mountain; tiru uruva – being with beautiful divine form; vāttāṟṟāṟku – one who is easily approachable in tiruvāttāṟu; en nanṟi – what virtuous deed; seydēnō – as I did to him; en nenjil tigaḻvadu – entering in my heart and shining there?

**Перевод:**

**tiruttuḻāy which is spreading the fragrance by remaining fully on his divine form, is rising up to his crown; he is having the divine chakra which goes where his divine heart desires, attacks the target and returns to stay on his divine hand; he is having a beautiful divine form which resembles a mountain having firm blackish complexion like dark ocean water; what virtuous deed did I do to the easily approachable emperumān at tiruvāttāṟu, for him to enter and shine in my heart?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Eighth pāsuram, āḻvār says “The most distinguished emperumān arrived in tiruvāttāṟu as a very easily approachable person, and arrived and entered in my heart and shone; what virtuous deed did I do, to get this?”. மெய்ந்நின்று கமழ் துளவ விரை ஏறு திருமுடியன் கைந்நின்ற சக்கரத்தன் கருதும் இடம் பொருது புனல் மைந்நின்ற வரை போலும் திரு உருவ வாட்டாற்றாற்கு எந் நன்றி செய்தேனா என் நெஞ்சில் திகழ்வதுவே? meynninṟu kamaḻ tuḷava virai ēṟu tirumudiyan kainninṟa cakkarattan karudum idam porudu punal mainninṟa varai pōlum tiru uruva vāttāṟṟāṟku en nanṟi seydēnō en nenjil tigaḻvaduvē?*

- *mey …* – One who is having divine crown where the fragrance of the tiruttuḻāy on his divine form, rises and reaches. Just as ocean water will climb up the mountain, the fragrance of the tiruttuḻāy on the divine feet covers the whole body and climbs up over his divine head.
- *kai …* – Since sudarśana cakram is bhāvajña (one who understands the mood), he will understand the divine heart of sarvēśvaran, enter into battle, destroy the enemies, will be victorious, and will return to emperumān’s hand as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 111.20 “*svatūṇīm punarāviśat*” (arrow re-entered its own quiver). As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 40.29 “*rāma pārśvam jagāma*” (he came back and stood next to śrī rāma). śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 40.29 is explained here \[sugrīva went to attack rāvaṇa even before śrī rāma did\].
   - *ata hari vara nāta:* – As the evil rāvaṇa was standing under a pearl umbrella \[highlighting his opulence\] against perumāḷ (śrī rāma), sugrīva mahārāja being unable to tolerate that, charged at rāvaṇa, attacked him for a long time and made him lose all his energy, and as he started engaging in māyā yuddam (illusory warfare), and thought “We will also be forced to fight in the same way; but that is not apt for us; we cannot cause harm to perumāḷ’s vow” and returned. \[Did perumāḷ make a vow?\] śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 51.32 “*rāmēṇa hi pratijñātam”* – perumāḷ who is satya sankalpa (one with unfailing vow) is vowing. “*haryrakśaṇa sannidau*” – he vowed amidst great warriors. Hence, sugrīva mahārāja thought that he should not cause harm to that vow.
   - *hari vara nāta:* – He did not do this since there is no one capable in his army to do so; he did it out of envy only \[he wanted to serve rāma in a distinguished manner\].
   - *prāpya sangrāma kīrtim* – There is a separate glory in battle; he has such fame.
   - *niśicara patim* – The evil one who is the shelter for those who engage in mischievous warfare. He separated the princes (śrī rāma and laskmaṇa) from sītā and kept her in a separate place.
   - *ājau* – In the righteous warfare which is not their field of interest.
   - *yōjayitvā śramēṇa* – he gave fatigue to rāvaṇa; and he himself acquired fame.
   - *gaganam ativiśālam lankayitvā* – He effortlessly crossed over the space in-between.
   - *arkkasūnu:* – He manifested that he was “arkkasūnu:” (son of sūrya). When sun appears in udayagiri (the mountain of dawn), it won’t stop moving until dusk.
   - *rāma pārśvam jagāma* – After leaving perumāḷ, as he thought that he did not do anything worthy there, instead of standing in front of perumāḷ, he stood on the side of perumāḷ.  He stood on the side thinking “Having not plucked the head of the evil rāvaṇa and placed at the divine feet of perumāḷ, how can I stand in front of him?”
- *punal …* – His form which resembles ocean, black pigment and firm mountain. ōr form which resembles a mountain which does not lose its black complexion. It is not vāttāṟṟārkku (for the respectable emperumān in tiruvāttāṟu) – which indicates respect. It is vāttāṟṟānukku (for emperumān in tiruvāttāṟu) \[which is recited as vāttāṟṟāṟku\].
- *en nanṟi seydēnō* – What virtuous deed did I do? Did I die in trying to protect sītā as done by periya udaiyār (jatāyu)? ōr did I come back as done by tiruvadi (hanumān) who said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 65.10 “*drustā sītā*” (sītā was seen)? ōr, did I observe all the ordained karma for me to say that I have followed your orders? Considering which virtuous deed of mine, has he entered my heart and is shining as if attaining impossible benefit? emperumān who is great in every aspect such as wearing tiruttuḻāy garland which highlights his opulence, having the weapon which will complete the tasks thought of by him, and having physical beauty, has entered and is remaining in my heart as if he has attained an impossible benefit.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 10.6.9. Tigalginra tirumarbil

*tigaḻginṟa tirumārbil tirumangai tannōdum tigaḻginṟa tirumālār sērvidam taṇ vāttāṟu pugaḻginṟa puḷ ūrdi pōr arakkar kulam keduttān igaḻvu inṟi en nenjattu eppoḻudum piriyānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tigaḻginṟa tirumārbil – in the naturally shining divine chest; tirumangai tannōdum – with lakshmi who is naturally young forever; tigaḻginṟa tirumālār – śriya:pati who is shining; sērvidam – the eternal abode (of his); taṇ – rejuvenating; vāttāṟu – tiruvāttāṟu; pugaḻ ninṟa – one who is the abode for the fame of servitude; puḷ – periya tiruvadi (garudāḻvār); ūrdi – one who rides; pōr – strong in warfare; arakkar – rākśasas’ (demons’); kulam – group; keduttān – one who destroyed; en nenjattu – in my lowly heart; igaḻvinṟi – without any detachment; eppoḻudum – always; piriyān – never separates

**Перевод:**

**tiruvāttāṟu is the rejuvenating, eternal abode of the shining śriya:pati who is with lakshmi who is naturally young forever, in his naturally shining divine chest; emperumān who rides periya tiruvadi who is the abode for the fame of servitude, destroyed the group of rākśasas who are strong in warfare; such emperumān never separates from my lowly heart and remains there without any detachment.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Ninth pāsuram. āḻvār says “emperumān who is very complete, is not leaving my heart ever, and is not despising me”. திகழ்கின்ற திருமார்பில் திருமங்கை தன்னோடும் திகழ்கின்ற திருமாலார் சேர்விடம் தண் வாட்டாறு புகழ்நின்ற புள் ஊர்தி போர் அரக்கர் குலம் கெடுத்தான் இகழ்வு இன்றி என் நெஞ்சத்து எப்பொழுதும் பிரியானே tigaḻginṟa tirumārbil tirumangai tannōdum tigaḻginṟa tirumālār sērvidam taṇ vāttāṟu pugaḻginṟa puḷ ūrdi pōr arakkar kulam keduttān igaḻvu inṟi en nenjattu eppoḻudum piriyānē*

- *tigaḻginṟa* … – śriya:pati, whose divine chest is naturally shining on its own, is shining further due to the togetherness with periya pirāttiyār who is mercifully residing there. Even others are called “śrīmān” as an honour; it is unlike that here \[it is perfectly true in emperumān’s case\]; since he is shining with śrī mahālakśmi, he is known as śriya:pati. The rēpam (“Ar”) in the end of tirumālār has no specific meaning; it just indicates he is “*tirumāl*” (one who has śrī mahālakśmi as his consort); as it is said in “*puḷḷūrdi*” (one who rides garudāḻvār).
- *sērvidam taṇ vāttāṟu* – Having this abode as his residence is as great as being śriya:pati.
- *pugaḻ …* – periya tiruvadi, the vehicle, who has all fame in him. All the fame remains in him; having this fame is his greatness.
- *pōr …* – He destroyed the whole clan of rākśasas in righteous warfare.
- *igaḻvu …* – Instead of holding back considering me to be a samsāri (bound soul), and instead of remaining in my heart for a purpose and leaving it afterwards, he never ever leaves my heart. Just as one who is suffering from bile disease will never give up sandalwood paste, he never leaves me even for a moment.

## 10.6.10. Piriyadatcey

*piriyādu ātcey enṟu piṟappu aṟattu āḷ aṟak koṇḍān ari āgi iraṇiyanai āgam kīṇḍān anṟu periyārkku ātpattakkāl peṟāda payan peṟumāṟu vari vāḷ vāy aravu aṇai mēl vāttāṟṟān kāttinanē*

**Пословный перевод:**

piriyādu – without separating forever; ātcey – perform kainkaryam; enṟu – saying; piṟappu – connection with birth, which is a hurdle for that (such kainkaryam); aṟuttu – eliminate; aṟa – fully; ātkoṇḍān – accepting my kainkaryam; anṟu – long ago (when prahlāda was tormented by his own father); ariyāgi – incarnated as narasimha; iraṇiyanai – hiraṇya’s; āgam – body; kīṇḍān – one who tore; vari – stripes; vāḷ – having radiance; vāy – having many faces; aravu aṇai mēl – on the divine serpent mattress; vāttāṟṟān – one who mercifully rests in tiruvāttāṟu; periyārkku – for great personalities; ātpattakkāl – when became servant; peṟāda – difficult to attain; payan – results; peṟum āṟu – the means to get; kāttinān – showed

**Перевод:**

**emperumān who incarnated as narasimha and tore hiraṇya’s body long ago, who is mercifully resting in tiruvāttāṟu on the divine serpent mattress which is having stripes and many radiant faces, said “Perform kainkaryam forever without separating”, fully eliminated my connection with birth, which is a hurdle for such kainkaryam and accepted my kainkaryam. He also showed the means to get results which are difficult to attain and which are attained when one becomes servant of great personalities.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Tenth pāsuram. āḻvār says “Great personalities when approached, will grant based on their standards instead of that of those who are requesting; this principle is manifested by the nāyanār (lord) in tiruvāttāṟu towards me”. பிரியாது ஆட்செய் என்று பிறப்பு அறுத்து ஆள் அறக் கொண்டான் அரி ஆகி இரணியனை ஆகம் கீண்டான் அன்று பெரியார்க்கு ஆட்பட்டக்கால் பெறாத பயன் பெறுமாறு வரி வாள் வாய் அரவு அணை மேல் வாட்டாற்றான் காட்டினனே piriyādu ātcey enṟu piṟappu aṟattu āḷ aṟak koṇḍān ari āgi iraṇiyanai āgam kīṇḍān anṟu periyārkku ātpattakkāl peṟāda payan peṟumāṟu vari vāḷ vāy aravu aṇai mēl vāttāṟṟān kāttinanē*

- *piriyādu …* – Mercifully saying “Serve me without separating”, eliminating my hurdles, he accepted my eternal service; he fulfilled our prayer which was in [tiruvāimoḻi 2.9](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/06/thiruvaimozhi-2-9-emmavidu/) “emmā vīdu” where we asked him to say in [tiruvāimoḻi 2.9.4](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/06/thiruvaimozhi-2-9-4-enakke-atchey/) “*enakkē ātcey*” (serve me only). He eliminated my birth as we prayed in tiruviruttam 1 “*poynninṟa jñānam*“, where we said “*inninṟa nīrmai ini yām uṟāmai*” (I cannot tolerate this lowly life anymore). He fully accepted our service as we prayed in [tiruvāimoḻi 2.9](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/06/thiruvaimozhi-2-9-emmavidu/) “emmā vīdu” saying in [tiruvāimoḻi 2.9.4](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/06/thiruvaimozhi-2-9-4-enakke-atchey/) “*tanakkēyāga*” (exclusively for him).
- *ariyāgi …* – āḻvār is recollecting emperumān’s previous favour for him. \[āḻvārs think about favours done to other devotees as favours done to them\]
- *ariyāgi* – As śrī narasimha, he effortlessly tore apart hiraṇya’s rough body.
- *anṟu* – He did it that way back then; now he is doing it this way. As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 15.7 “*kriyatāmiti mām vada*” (lakśmaṇa to śrī rāma – order me in what should be done), eliminating my hurdles, he accepted my eternal service. He also prayed saying in tiruvāimoḻi 8.5.7 “*mugappē kūvip paṇi koḷḷāy*” (you should call me and mercifully engage me in service in your divine presence).
- *periyār …* – The principle that one will get results which are difficult to attain by surrendering unto great personalities, was manifested towards me by vāttāṟṟān (emperumān in tiruvāttāṟu) who is mercifully resting on striped, radiant, many faced serpent mattress. viṣṇu purāṇam kśatrabandu upākyānam “*mahātmanām samśrayam abhyupētō naivāvasīdatyati durgatōpi*” (Oh viṣṇu! I have endured great suffering; show your mercy upon me; one who is ignorant and who has reached great personalities will not have any worries) – it is seen in the world that, after surrendering unto great personalities, such great personalities will not act seeing the lowliness of those who accept and the greatness of themselves who are granting; he manifested that towards me. Did he make prahlāda et al to sing his glories? \[That opportunity was only granted to me\]

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 10.6.11. Kattit tan

*kāttit tan kanai kaḻalgaḷ kadu naragam pugal oḻitta vāttāṟṟu ēm perumānai vaḷang kurugūrc catakōpan pāttāya tamiḻ mālai āyirattuḷ ip pattum kēttu ārār vānavaragaḷ sevikku iniya senjollē*

**Пословный перевод:**

than kanaikaḻalgaḷ – his divine feet (which are perfectly enjoyable due to having resounding anklets which reveal his valour); kātti – showing; kadu – unbearable; naragam pugal – entry in to this hellish samsāram (material realm); oḻitta – one who eliminated; vāttāṟu – in tiruvāttāṟu; emperumānai – on the lord; vaḷam – beautiful; kurugūr – controller of āḻvārtirunagari; satakōpan – nammāḻvār’s; pāttāy – song; tamiḻ mālai – tamiḻ garland; āyirattuḷ – among the thousand pāsurams; sevikku iniya – like a nectar to the ears; senjol – being honest words (due to all the three faculties viz mind, speech and body being in harmony); ip pattum – this decad; vānavargaḷ – nityasūris; kēttu ārār – will never become satiated, hearing this

**Перевод:**

**nammāḻvār, the controller of beautiful āḻvārtirunagari, composed thousand pāsurams in the form of a garland of song on the lord in tiruvāttāṟu who eliminated my entry in to this unbearable, hellish samsāram by showing his divine feet; nityasūris, hearing this decad among those thousand pāsurams, which is having honest words which are like nectar to the ears, will never become satiated.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*In the end, āḻvār says “nityasūris are the ones who can enjoy this decad”. காட்டித் தன் கனை கழல்கள் கடு நரகம் புகல் ஒழித்த வாட்டாற்று எம் பெருமானை வளங் குருகூர்ச் சடகோபன் பாட்டாய தமிழ் மாலை ஆயிரத்துள் இப் பத்தும் கேட்டு ஆரார் வானவர்கள் செவிக்கு இனிய செஞ்சொல்லே kāttit than kanai kaḻalgaḷ kadu naragam pugal oḻitta vāttāṟṟu ēm perumānai vaḷang kurugūrc catakōpan pāttāya tamiḻ mālai āyirattuḷ ip pattum kēttu ārār vānavaragaḷ sevikku iniya senjollē*

- *kāttit than kanai kaḻalgaḷ* – Without any reason, emperumān manifested his divine form which reveals his svarūpa (true nature), rūpa (forms), guṇa (qualities), vibhūti (wealth).
- *kadu naragam pugal oḻitta* – He fulfilled our desire as prayed in tiruviruttam 1 “*inninṟa nīrmai ini yām uṟāmai*” (I cannot tolerate this lowly life anymore).  For those who are wise, this samsāram is the unbearable hell.
- *vaḷam …* – āḻvār who owns the beautiful āḻvārtirunagari.
- *pāttāya …* – Hearing this decade among the thousand pāsurams which are well mixed with music as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam bāla kāṇḍam 4.8 “*pātyē gēyē ca maduram*” (both words and music are sweet).
- *ārār vānavargaḷ* – After hearing this, they \[nityasūris\] will say “recite again, recite again” and will never be satiated with what was heard. Those who just weep and stammer being unable to reveal their emotions after enjoying bhagavān’s qualities, will not leave these pāsurams after hearing them.

When asked “What is the reason for their ever unsatiated state? Is it due to experiencing his qualities such as simplicity?” āḻvār says “No, it is because of being won over by these pāsurams”.

- *sevikkiniya* – As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 31.1 “*samśravē maduram vākhyam*” (words which are sweet to hear), instead of becoming sweet after entering through the ear and reaching the heart, it is pleasing to the ear itself.

When asked “What is the reason for that?” āḻvār says,

- *senjollē* – It is because the thoughts, speech and action are in harmony. He himself said in tiruvāimoḻi 6.5.11 “*sindaiyālum sollālum seygaiyinālum dēvapirānaiyē*” (having attained him with the three faculties viz mind, speech and body) and “*sendamiḻ pattum*” (this decad in the form of tamiḻ pāsurams which honestly reveal the meanings) \[in the same pāsuram\].

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.
