## 10.7 Senjorkavigal

## 10.7.1. Senjorkavigal

*senjoṟkavigāḷ! uyirkāttātceymmin tirumālirunjōlai vanjak kaḷvan māmāyan māyak kaviyāy vandu en nenjum uyirum uḷ kalandu ninṟār aṟiyā vaṇṇam en nenjum uyirum avai uṇḍu tānēyāgi niṟaindānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tirumālirunjōlai – (to bless his devotees) being in tirumalai; vanjak kaḷvan – one who steals without the knowledge of those from whom he steals; mā māyan – one who has very amazing form, qualities etc (to attract others); māyak kaviyāy – one who remains with mischievous acts to make me sing poems; vandu – arriving at (where we are, with determination); en nenjuḷḷum – in my heart; uyir uḷḷum – in self; kalandu – mixing seamlessly; ninṟār – even lakshmi et al who remain with him; aṟiyā vaṇṇam – without the knowledge; avai – those; nenjum – my heart; uyirum – self \[ātmā\]; uṇḍu – consumed; tānē āgi – becoming the exclusive enjoyer; niṟaindān – became avāpta samasta kāma (one who has no unfulfilled desire); sem – having honesty (without any expectation); sol – with words; kavigāḷ – Oh all of you who can sing poems!; uyir kāttu – protecting (from his hand, your) selves and belongings from being stolen; ātceymmin – try to serve with your \[faculty of\] speech

**Перевод:**

**emperumān, being in tirumalai, who steals without the knowledge of those from whom he steals, who has very amazing form, qualities etc, who remains with mischievous acts to make me sing poems, is arriving in my heart and mixing in my heart and self even without the knowledge of lakshmi et al who remain with him; he consumed my heart and self, became the exclusive enjoyer and became avāpta samasta kāma. Oh all of you who can sing poems with honest words! Protect yourselves and your belongings from being stolen and try to serve him with your speech. Implies that for those who immerse in bhagavān as ananyaprayōjana (without any expectation other than kainkaryam), it is unavoidable to have the self and belongings to be stolen by him.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the first pāsuram, āḻvār says “emperumān entered my heart saying ‘I will make you sing tiruvāimoḻi’, but look at his love for me. Oh those who serve him! Don’t get drowned in the ocean of his qualities”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. senjoṟkavigāḷ! uyirkāttātceymmin tirumālirunjōlai vanjak kaḷvan māmāyan māyak kaviyāy vandu en nenjum uyirum uḷ kalandu ninṟār aṟiyā vaṇṇam en nenjum uyirum avai uṇḍu tānēyāgi niṟaindānē*

- *senjol* … – Oh poets who have honest words! Honesty for poet/poet is to remain ananya prayōjanam (without any expectation); having expecation is dishonesty for poems/poets; as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 7.9.6](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/11/thiruvaimozhi-7-9-6-in-kavi-padum/) “*in kavi pādum parama kavigaḷ*” (Instead of making great poets such as parāśara, pārāśara (vyāsa), vālmeeki, mudalāḻvārgaḷ et al who sing great, infinitely sweet poems to sing poems) and periya tirumoḻi 2.8.2 “*sendamiḻ pāduvār*” (those who sing beautiful tamiḻ pāsurams), āḻvār is thinking about mudalāḻvārgaḷ. ananya prayaōjanar are those who said in [iraṇḍām tiruvandādi 74](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/01/irandam-thiruvandhadhi-74/) “*perundamiḻan nallēn*” (I am an expert in great tamiḻ arts and am great) and in [mudal tiruvandādi 11](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/06/mudhal-thiruvandhadhi-11/) “*vāy avanai alladu vāḻttādu*” (My mouth will not praise anyone other than emperumān).
- *uyir kāttu ātceymmin* – You first protect yourselves and then sing the poems. Only if you are present, you can sing the poems. Only if ātmās are present, they can sing mangaḷāśāsanam for emperumān.
- *ātceymmin* – He is saying this because, singing poems is a vācika kainkaryam (service by speech). Protect yourselves since he will enter us to accept our service but will end up differently as said in tiruvāimoḻi 9.6.7 “*ātkoḷvān ottu ennuyir uṇḍa māyan*” ([emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/), the amazing personality, entered me as if accepting my service and consumed my ātmā). siṟṟāḷ koṇḍān says “just as those who immerse in deep water will place poles to mark the depth, āḻvār is also placing poles to highlight emperumān’s depth”. udaiyavar would say “since it is not mentioned whose life \[is to be protected\], \[āḻvār is saying that\] you protect emperumān’s life and serve him”. That is – when he himself voluntarily pursues us, if we move away from him, we will lose him; hence you should save his life \[by not leaving him\]. Just as expert swimmers will mark regions in a river saying “this spot is deep, this spot is shallow”, āḻvār who first humbly invited worldly poets who are not interested in bhagavat viśayam, saying in tiruvāimoḻi 3.9.6 “*vammin pulavīr*” (Oh poets! Come), is now stopping those who are immersed in bhagavān’s qualities such as simplicity. āḻvār himself is wounded by emperumān’s qualities such as śeela (simplicity) etc as said in tiruvāimoḻi 9.6.2 “*ninai toṟum sollundoṟum nenjidindugum*” (My heart which is the tool for thinking about you, becomes broken and is melting and becoming fluid, every moment I think and speak about your qualities such as śeela, saulabhya etc which are revealed in your activities relating to the great union) and tiruvāimoḻi 8.1.8 “*valvinaiyēnai īrginṟa* *guṇangaḷai udaiyāy*” (he is having the qualities which are always tormenting me who is having powerful sins). Instead of doing acts which will destroy you, please enjoy his opulence and sing poems on it, instead of thinking to enjoy his quality of śeela.
- *kavigāḷ uyir kāttu ātceymmin* – While saying “kavigāḷ”, naturally one would have to say “save yourself and sing poems”; instead he is saying “save yourself and serve him”; due to his impressions from [tiruvāimoḻi 3.4](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/08/thiruvaimozhi-3-4-pugazhum/) “*pugaḻu nal oruvan*” \[In this decad, āḻvār praised emperumān as everything, that is emperumān having every entity as śarīram\].

The reason for āḻvār forcefully saying “don’t immense in his śeela guṇam (quality of simplicity)” is – that is explained in the rest of the pāsuram. \[Main reason is\] I am not seeing my existence as said in “*tānēyāgi nirṟaindānē*” (He exclusively enjoyed me).

- *tirumālirunjōlai* – His presence in tirumalai is also an aspect of his simplicity.
- *vanjak kaḷvan* – He will steal to make us believe that he is truthful. As said in tiruvāimoḻi 9.6.6 “*engaṇṇan kaḷvam enakkuc cemmāy niṟkum*” (The deceptive acts of kriṣṇa who has great love towards me look truthful to me), even while the act of stealing is happening, it will appear truthful. He will steal the stealing itself. He will enter as if establishing śēśatvam (servitude) in the ātmā, but he will himself accept it \[śēśatvam\] and place śēśitvam (lordship) in the ātmā, and hold the ātmā on his head.

When asked “If you know his mischief, why don’t you escape from him?” āḻvār says,

- *mā māyan* – He is having amazing qualities and acts which stop us from escaping even after knowing his mischief; as said in [nācciyār tirumoḻi 2.4](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2024/06/nachchiyar-thirumozhi-2-4/) “*maiyalēṟṟi mayakka*” (To bewilder us by increasing our infatuation).

When asked “With his qualities and acts, how did he capture you?” āḻvār says,

- *māyak kaviyāy vandu* – emperumān entered me saying “Oh āḻvīr! I am looking at making you sing beautiful poems which are not seen in this world. We will do it”. He entered with the pretext of making me sing, just as one will enter the place of his beloved looking for water.
- *vandu* – He is the one who came. While I did not go to his place and request him saying “Please make me sing some poems”, he himself came. One who is to be attained, has himself come. This is what is called simplicity!

When asked “What torment did he do, after coming?” āḻvār says,

- *en nenjum uyirum* – nenju (Heart) indicates the whole body; uyir is ātmā (self).
- *uḷ kalandu* –  He seamlessly mixed; he immersed in my body and self without any difference.
- *ninṟār aṟiyā vaṇṇam* – He united with me even beyond the knowledge of pirātti, tiruvanantāḻvān (ādiśēśa), tiruvadi (garudāḻvār) et al who are experts in such interaction with emperumān. They are the ones who remain with emperumān in such union; even without their knowledge; as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 9.6.9](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/08/thiruvaimozhi-9-6-9-aruyir-pattadhu/) “*āruyir pattadu enaduyir pattadu?*” (Did nityasūris, who enjoy such emperumān, eternally immerse in him the same way that my ātmā immersed in him as the enjoyable object?)
- *en nenjum uyirum avai uṇḍu* – He is not able to differentiate between body and soul; as said in tiruvāimoḻi 9.6.5 “*uruvamum āruyirum udanē uṇḍān*” (enjoying my body and my soul without discriminating between them) – he consumed my body and self equally.
- *tānēyāgi* – āḻvār is not seeing himself anymore. emperumān entered as if sharing the enjoyment but ended up being the exclusive enjoyer. As said in [tiruvāimoḻi 9.6.10](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/08/thiruvaimozhi-9-6-10-varik-kondu/) “*ennai muṟṟap paruginān*” (he fully consumed me), the ātmā became the enjoyed. He interacted without considering the ātmā as a sentient; he made me become like acit (insentient) which purely exists for others’ enjoyment. He accepted as I prayed in [tiruvāimoḻi 2.9.4](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/06/thiruvaimozhi-2-9-4-enakke-atchey/) “*tanakkēyāga*” (exclusively for him). Just as there is intrinsic variety in enjoyable objects, the cētana also has become one such enjoyable object.
- *tānē āgi* – He eliminated dual lordship. He made the ātmā bite the dust and remained prideful.
- *niṟaindānē* – Though he was known as avāpta samasta kāman (one who has no unfulfilled desires), he became fully complete only after acquiring āḻvār. This is the quality of simplicity. That is – when a great personality unites with a lowly person, mixing seamlessly so that the greatness and lowliness of the individuals are invisible; as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam bāla kāṇḍam 1.85 “*krutakrutyastadā rāma:*” (After crowning vibhīśaṇa in lankā, śrī rāma felt as one who accomplished his own task, and became happy, being relieved from grief).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 10.7.2. Taneyagi niraindu

*tānēyāgi niṟaindu ellā ulagum uyirum tānēyāy tānē yān enbān āgit tannait tānē tudittu enakkut tēnē pālē kannalē amudē tirumālirunjōlaik kōnēyāgi ninṟoḻindān ennai muṟṟum uyir uṇḍē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ennai – me; muṟṟum – in all ways; uyir uṇḍu – enjoying the self; tānē āgi – being the primary one; niṟaindu – being complete; ellā ulagum – all worlds; uyirum – the creatures which are present in those worlds; tānē āy – to be himself (being the controller, by being the antarātmā (indvelling super soul), and not just that common principle); yān enbān – being I, the entity which is explained by the presence of consciousness; tānē āgi – to be himself (due to that inseparable nature); tannai – on him, who is praised; tānē tudittu – being the one who praises and praising him; enakku – due to revealing to me; tēnē pālē kannalē amudē – being honey, milk, sugar and nectar and all the taste in these objects; tirumālirunjōlai – mercifully residing in tirumālirunjōlai; kōnē āgi – being the lord, himself; ninṟoḻindān – remained here without leaving

**Перевод:**

**He is enjoying my self fully in all ways; he is primary and complete; he is all the worlds and the creatures in the worlds \[everything is his body\]; he is I, the entity which is explained by the presence of consciousness; he is the one who praises and one who is praised; due to revealing all these to me, being honey, milk, sugar and nectar and all the taste in these objects, he is the lord who is mercifully residing in tirumālirunjōlai, remaining there without leaving. Implies that he remained both the enjoyer and enjoyed.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the second pāsuram, āḻvār becomes pleased and enjoys the opulence emperumān acquired after uniting with him.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. tānēyāgi niṟaindu ellā ulagum uyirum tānēyāy tānē yān enbān āgit tannait tānē tudittu enakkut tēnē pālē kannalē amudē tirumālirunjōlaik kōnēyāgi ninṟoḻindān ennai muṟṟum uyir uṇḍē*

- *tānē āgi niṟaindu* – He entered saying that both of us will share the joy but ended up acquiring all the joy.
- *ellām …* – He remained as the worlds and all the creatures such as humans et al in those worlds. He became sarvēśvaran. When asked “Did he become sarvēśvaran now only?” Yes – only when he remains a rakśaka (saviour) his true nature is retained. Without protecting those who need to be protected, one cannot be niyantā (controller). Before acquiring āḻvār, his īśvaratva (lordship) was like bright light for a person with a troubled eye. While ātmā is eternal, when bhagavat jñānam (knowledge about bhagavān) is not dawned in him, he is said as in taittirīya upaniśat “*asannēva bhavati*” (he is as good as non-existing) and after getting such jñānam, he is said as in taittirīya upaniśat “*santamēnam tatōvidu:*” (he is known to be existing). bhagavān is also similar to that. Expecting a recipient is common to both \[jīvātmā and paramātmā\]. As said in [nānmugan tiruvandādi 7](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/06/nanmugan-thiruvandhadhi-7/) “*nānunnai anṟi ilēn kāṇḍāy nāraṇanē nī ennai anṟi ilai*” (Oh nārāyaṇa! I cannot exist without you and you cannot exist without me) – ātmā exists being a servitor and bhagavān exists being a lord.
- *tānē yān enbān āgi* – emperumān became the entity which is known as “I”. Beyond explaining emperumān to be the antaryāmi of everyone/everything, āḻvār is also explaining about emperumān being the antaryāmi of āḻvār himself.
- *yān enbān – tānē āgi* – I, who am existing for namesake, came to be known as emperumān himself. āḻvār tried to touch himself and feel him, but he is not seeing him. āḻvār is seeing emperumān holding him on the head and hence sees him only; emperumān is assuming subservience and is placing importance to āḻvār causing pride in āḻvār and hence sees āḻvār only. \[With the help of śarīra-śarīri bhāvam (soul-body relationship between bhagavān and all other entities), the essence is explained\] In the viśiśta vastu (bhagavān with attributes), due to viśēśya prādānyam (importance for bhagavān), āḻvār is not seeing himself who is viśēśaṇam (attribute/form). Both in effectual state and causal state, while brahmam is qualified \[with subtle and form entities\], that brahmam itself is called as upādānam (material cause). And due to the question of his having vikāram (transformation) etc, such vikāram etc are associated with the attributes to ensure that he is free from all defects \[arising out of such aspects\]. Still, brahmam can be said as only one; this is because, the natural relationship \[between bhagavān and all other entities\] is without any shortcomings. This is unlike pot, cloth etc which can exist separately; here, it is explained based on prakāra-prakāri bhāvam (relationship between attribute-form\[ which are inseparable – aprutak siddi\]); just as jāti (species) and guṇam (quality) are fully existing on the particular entity \[and cannot exist on their own\].

Since, bhagavān is like this,

- *tannait tānē tudittu* – As said in jitantē slōkam 1.7 “*vacasām vācyamuttamam*” (being the main meaning for words), just as the meaning of the word “aham” (I) goes all the way up to bhagavān, the word aham also goes all the way up to bhagavān. Though the pāsurams originate from āḻvār, it can be said that emperumān is the origin for the same \[based on this principle explained here\]. Only if I am the one who is praised, can I be the one who praises? \[emperumān is both the one who praises and the one who is praised\].
- *enakku …* – Beyond the common state as said in “*sarvarasa:*” (essence of all tastes), oh one who is perfectly enjoyable for me! As said in [tiruvāimoḻi 7.1.7](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/07/thiruvaimozhi-7-1-7-onru-solli/) “*kodiyēn paruginnamudē*” (oh my master who manifested such magnanimous act and is eternally enjoyable to drink for me who is having the anguish unlike them who were satisfied with getting the nectar!) When āḻvār said “*tannait tānē tudittu*“, he did not see himself there; now, he is seeing his presence and feeling that emperumān’s sweetness. āḻvār becomes pleased seeing that emperumān is pleased on hearing the pāsurams.
- *tirumālirnjōlaik kōnē* – The presence of emperumān in tirumalai is the same as the tasteful objects highlighted previously. It is said in periya tirumoḻi 7.3.6 “*tirumāirunjōlaiyangattiyaik karumbīnṟa insāṟṟai*” (the sugar block of tirumālirunjōlai and the juice of sugarcane).
- *tirumālirunjōlaik kōnē āgi* – The greatness of having tirumalai as his abode appears to be much bigger than the greatness of having ubhaya vibhūti (spiritual and material realm).
- *kōnē āgi* – His rakśakatvam (saviourśip) became complete, only after acquiring āḻvār. If this is not the case, there will be no difference between the presence in śrīvaikuṇṭam and in tirumalai \[presence in tirumalai is greater as explained previously, due to acquiring āḻvār, by being here\].
- *ninṟu oḻindān* – Only after arriving and standing here, he gave up his restlessness. He became krutakrutya (one who has accomplished his duties).
- *ennai muṟṟum uyir uṇḍē* – Fully consuming my self. āḻvār is in such a state that emperumān who is vibhu (great) acquired glories by consuming ātmā who is aṇu (miniscule).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 10.7.3. Ennai murrum

*ennai muṟṟum uyir uṇḍu en māya ākkai idanuḷ pukku ennai muṟṟum tānēyāy ninṟa māya ammān sēr tennan tirumālirunjōlait tisai kai kūppic cērnda yān innum pōvēnēkolō? enkol ammān tiruvaruḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ennai – me; muṟṟum – in all ways; uyir uṇḍu – enjoying my ātmā; en – my; māyam – being the cause for ignorance etc; ākkai idanuḷ – in this body (which is a product of prakruti (matter), which is having defects which are perceivable by senses and which binds); pukku – entered; ennai – me (who is the controlling ātmā for this body); muṟṟum – on body etc which are connected; tānē āy – being the controller (to eliminate the ahantā (ego) and mamatā (possessiveness)); ninṟa – one who stood (as krutakrutya (one who accomplished the duties)); māyam – one who has amazing qualities and acts; ammān – one who is the unconditional lord; sēr – the abode where he firmly resides; then – for the southern direction; nan – praiseworthy; tirumālirunjōlai – standing on tirumalai (divine hill) which is known as tirumālirunjōlai; tisai – towards the direction; kai kūppi – performing an act of servitude; sērnda yān – I who reached; innam – after acquiring the state (of vorśipping that direction too); pōvēnēkolō – will I go anywhere else thinking that there is a destination for me?; ammān – the unconditional lord’s; tiruvaruḷ – affection; enkol – how \[amazing\] is it?

**Перевод:**

**Enjoying my ātmā in all ways, emperumān entered my body which is the cause for ignorance etc, being the controller of me and my body etc which are connected, who has amazing qualities and acts, and who is the unconditional lord, is standing and firmly residing on the praiseworthy tirumalai which is in the southern direction; performing an act of servitude, I reached that divyadēśam;  after acquiring the state, will I go anywhere else thinking that there is a place to go for me? How \[amazing\] is the affection of my unconditional lord? Implies that emperumān is standing as if there is some other benefits and he is granting them. tennan could also indicate the king of that region.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the third pāsuram, āḻvār mercifully explains emperumān’s endless affection which keeps increasing towards him.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. ennai muṟṟum uyir uṇḍu en māya ākkai idanuḷ pukku ennai muṟṟum tānēyāy ninṟa māya ammān sēr tennan tirumālirunjōlait tisai kai kūppic cērnda yān innum pōvēnēkolō? enkol ammān tiruvaruḷē*

- *ennai muṟṟum uyir uṇḍu* – The greatness acquired by fully enjoying āḻvār is even greater than the greatness acquired as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 37.18 “*yasyasā janakātmajā – apramēyam hi tattēja:*” (One cannot measure the greatness of the one who is married to the daughter of śrī janaka).
- *en māya ākkai* – Did he stop with enjoying my ātmā (self)? āḻvār himself hated his body so much saying “this must be given up” as in tiruviruttam 1 “*aḻukkudambu*” (dirty body), [tiruvāimoḻi 3.2.3](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/07/thiruvaimozhi-3-2-3-kolla-makkol/) “*pollā ākkai*” (disastrous body) and [tiruvāimoḻi 5.1.5](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/05/thiruvaimozhi-5-1-5-kanna-piranai/) “*puṇṇai maṟaiya varindu*” (concealing the external faults, surrounding me forever) and started walking away from it; while āḻvār was despising his body, emperumān was pursuing it himself considering it to be his goal.
- *uḷ pukku* – āḻvār hated it wholeheartedly and started walking away from it. That is – āḻvār is remaining there until emperumān remains there and nods in agreement with āḻvār. emperumān entered there since he cannot leave from there until āḻvār says in tiruvāimoḻi 10.7.10 “*mangavottu*” (Agree to eliminate/destroy).
- *idan uḷ pukku* – ātmā is used to acit (matter) since time immemorial; bhagavān too remains in acit through cētana; such emperumān eagerly pursued āḻvār’s body. This body is a prakāra (inseparable attribute) for the ātmā which is a prakāra for emperumān. It is said in cāndōjña upaniśat 6.3 “*anēna jīvēna ātmanānupraviśya nāma rūpē vyākaravāṇi*” (all names and forms are created by my entry into acit through ātmās).
- *ennai muṟṟum tānē āy* – Since emperumān is pervaded everywhere both in ātmās and acit, there is nothing wrong in saying “*tānē*” (only him). emperumān accepted what is claimed by āḻvār as “*nān*” (I, ātmā) and his mamakāra viśayam (body which was considered by āḻvār as his belonging). āḻvār became so great that even īśvara (lord) cannot consume him fully and enjoy him.
- *ninṟa* – \[Being present with a divine form inside āḻvār\] Unlike the common state which is explained in nārāyaṇa sūktam “*antarbahiśca tat sarvam vyāypya nārāyaṇa stita:*” (nārāyaṇa is all pervading, both inside and outside).
- *māyam …* – The divine abode where even the sarvēśvaran, who has amazing qualities and activities, reaches with great eagerness like a thirsty person saying “water! water!” \[uncontrollable longing for something\]
- *tennan tirumālirunjōlai* – tennan indicates the king, and the land belongs to him; alternatively – the good abode in the southern direction.
- *tisai kaikūppic cērnda yān* – āḻvār desired the direction which was desired by emperumān. āḻvār likes to reach a particular direction. That is – desiring emperumān, through that, desiring the abode which he desired, and desiring the direction related to that divyadēśam, and in this manner, I have reached the state of desiring all that are related to him. This is similar to emperumān desiring for āḻvār, and the body which is related to āḻvār; āḻvār himself said previously in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.8.7](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/09/thiruvaimozhi-1-8-7-kondan-ezhvidai/) “*en eṇṭhān ānān*” (he started desiring for what I desire for).
- *innam pōvēnēkolō* – Is there any other destination for me beyond this direction? Will I, who have reached this direction, go anywhere beyond that, while he is restless for me in this manner? Now, going beyond here means giving up the connection with tirumalai.
- *enkol ammān tiruvaruḷē* – \[*ammān tiruvaruḷ enkol*\] \[āḻvār thinks – How amazing is his love? He is not going to abandon us since we are in our final days, yet we become bewildered thinking that he may do so\] On sarvēśvaran, would we not become bewildered without any reason? Alternatively – Why is he restless for me as if he has not done anything? Even after doing everything for āḻvār, he is remaining “what shall we do for him?” as if he has not done anything.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 10.7.4. Enkol amman

*enkol ammān tiruvaruḷgaḷ? ulagum uyirum tānēyāy nangen udalam kai vidān jñālattūdē nadanduḻakki tenkoḷ disaikkut tiladamāy ninṟa tirumālirunjōlai nangaḷ kunṟam kai vidān naṇṇā asurar naliyavē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ulagum – all the worlds; uyirum – all the creatures; tānē āy – to be himself (being antarātmā, by pervading everywhere); naṇṇā – not interested (in surrendering unto him); asurar – demoniac persons; naliya – to be destroyed; jñālattūdē – in the earth; nadandu uḻakki – walked around, stepping on it; then – south; koḷ – having; tisaikku – for the direction; tiladamāy ninṟa – one which is held on the head; tirumālirunjōlai – having the name tirumālirunjōlai; nangaḷ – enjoyable for those who are like us; kunṟam – divine hill; kaividān – not abandoning (considering it to be a favourable abode to acquire me); en udalam – my body; nangu – very much; kai vidān – not abandoning; ammān – lord’s; tiruvaruḷgaḷ – the acts of śeelam (simplicity) which favour us; enkol – how \[amazing\] are they?

**Перевод:**

**emperumān, being all the worlds and creatures, destroyed the demoniac persons who are not interested in him, stepped on the earth and walked around; he is not abandoning the divine hill named tirumālirunjōlai which remains atop the head of the southern direction and is enjoyable for those who are like us; he is also certainly not abandoning my body. How \[amazing\] are the acts of emperumān’s śeelam which favour us?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fourth pāsuram, āḻvār mercifully explains emperumān’s love towards āḻvār’s body and tirumalai due to its being the abode where emperumān can enjoy āḻvār.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. enkol ammān tiruvaruḷgaḷ? ulagum uyirum tānēyāy nangen udalam kai vidān jñālattūdē nadanduḻakki tenkoḷ disaikkut tiladamāy ninṟa tirumālirunjōlai nangaḷ kunṟam kai vidān naṇṇā asurar naliyavē*

- *enkol ammān tiruvaruḷgaḷ* – For sarvēśvaran, there is no scope for bewilderment without any reason! \[Even after doing so much for me, he is still thinking that he has not done anything for me\]
- *ulagu …* – Why is he anguishing as if he is having any shortcoming?
- *nangu en udalam kai vidān* – Just as a prideful prince will be at the gates of a lowly woman.
- *nangu en udalam* – sarvēśvaran will tell those who asked him “This is the divine body which gave āḻvār to us”.
- *nangu* – Well. Very much.
- *en udalam* – He remained “Whatever āḻvār considers as his, that is desirable for us”. He said “Is there anything that can be given up in my ‘*adangeḻil sampattu*‘ (fully beautiful wealth – [tiruvāimoḻi 1.2.7](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/05/thiruvaimozhi-1-2-7-adangu-ezhil/))?”
- *jñālattu …* – How long has he roamed around and tried to acquire this result? A cētana (sentient being) can say that the activities of the lord who is common to all, are for the cētana. \[On emperumān’s trivikrama avatāram\] It appears that whatever is said by indra as “I got my kingdom”, mahābali as “I got my magnanimity established”, and some say “I became pale” \[tirumangai āḻvār said periya tirumoḻi 9.4.2 “*munnam kuṟaḷuruvāy mūvadi maṇ koṇḍaḷanda – mannan saridaikkē mālāgip pon payandēn*” (I became bewildered and acquired paleness on hearing the incident of emperumān previously accepting three feet of land and measuring the world)\], are all making āḻvār say “he has done this for me”.
- *tenkoḷ …* – tirumālirunjōlai which is an ornament for the southern direction.
- *nangaḷ kunṟam* – The secluded place where the devotees interact with emperumān.
- *nangaḷ kunṟam kai vidān – nangu en udalam kai vidān* – emperumān considers tirumalai as prāpakam (means) and āḻvār’s divine body as prāpyam (goal). āḻvār’s divine body is the goal and his presence in tirumalai is for that purpose only.
- *naṇṇā asurar naliyavē* – As said in paḻamoḻi nānūṟu “*nedum pagai taṟceyyat tānē kedum*” (As one performs the right duties, the old enemies will be destroyed naturally), as emperumān resides in this abode without leaving, the demoniac clan got destroyed. pāsuram should be rearranged as “ulagum uyirum tānēyāy – jñālattūdē nadanduḻaki, tenkoḷ disaikkut tiladamāy ninṟa tirumālirunjōlai nangaḷ kunṟam – naṇṇā asurar naliya – kai vidān – nangennudalam kai vidān – enkol ammān tiruvaruḷgaḷ”.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 10.7.5. Nanna asurar

*naṇṇā asurar naliveyda nalla amarar poliveyda eṇṇādanagaḷ eṇṇum nanmunivar inbam talai siṟappap paṇṇār pādāl in kavigaḷ yānāyt tannait tān pādit tennāvennum ennammān tirumālirunjōlaiyānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

naṇṇā – those who remain as obstacle, not desiring to acquire (bhagavat viśayam); asurar – demoniac persons; nalivu eyda – to be destroyed (unable to bear this greatness); nalla amarar – the divine persons, who have devotion and are favourable; polivu eyda – to acquire opulence; eṇṇādanagaḷ – greatness which were never thought about previously over and above the qualities and wealth of emperumān who is avāpta samasta kāman (one who has no unfulfilled desires); eṇṇum – those who desire due to love \[towards him\]; nal – those who are with devotion; munivar – meditators (who meditate and enjoy); inbam talai siṟappa – being deeply joyful; paṇ Ar – filled with tune; pādal – having music; in kavigaḷ – sweet poems; yānāy – being I (who am his prakāra (attribute)); tannai – him (who is praiseworthy and who likes to be praised); tān pādi – being the one who praise, and sang; tirumālirunjōlaiyān – standing as the lord of tirumālirunjōlai; en ammān – my lord; tennā ennum – swaying his head, will sing

**Перевод:**

**To have those demoniac persons who remain as obstacle, not desiring to attain him, destroyed, to have the divine persons, who have devotion and are favourable, acquire opulence, and to give deep joy to very devoted meditators, who  due to love, desire greatness which were never thought about previously over and above the qualities and wealth of emperumān who is avāpta samasta kāman, my lord who is standing as the lord of tirumālirunjōlai, sang these sweet poems with music and filled with tune, on him, through me; he will sway his head and sing these pāsurams.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fifth pāsuram, āḻvār says “emperumān united with me, heard tiruvāimoḻi from my mouth and due to the uncontrollable, overflowing bliss on hearing tiruvāimoḻi, is singing like nityasūris and muktātmās, swaying his head”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. naṇṇā asurar naliveyda nalla amarar poliveyda eṇṇādanagaḷ eṇṇum nanmunivar inbam talai siṟappap paṇṇār pādāl in kavigaḷ yānāyt tannait tān pādit tennāvennum ennammān tirumālirunjōlaiyānē*

tiruvāimoḻi came into existence to destroy the demoniac persons, to give opulence to the devotees and to give deep joy to those meditators who desire for new greatness to emperumān. Just as the incarnation of the one \[emperumān\] is praised, the incarnation of the poems is also glorious; [śrī bhagavat gītā 4.8](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/4-8/) “*paritrāṇāya …*” (I am born in many ways in every yuga to protect the virtuous, to torture and destroy the wicked and to establish dharma firmly). As said in śrī viṣṇu purāṇam 5.3.2 “*akila jagat padma bōdāya*” (kriṣṇa, the sun, appeared to blossom all of the worlds which are like lotus).

- *naṇṇā …* – This \[tiruvāimoḻi\] remains the single tool to destroy the enemies, protect the favourable ones and to be the result for those who seek no other result than kainkaryam.
- *naṇṇā asurar nalivu eyda* – The son of the evil one who cannot be named \[krimikaṇṭacōḷa, who drove emperumānār out of śrīrangam and harmed periya nambi and kūrattāḻvān\], heard the acts of his father, despised them and said “how foolish he acted! Will that darśanam (śrīvaiṣṇava sampradāyam) be destroyed by just destroying a physical fort \[of tirukkaṇṇapuram\], while there are two great literature in the form of tiruvāimoḻi and śrī rāmāyaṇam?” In this way, this prabandam will break the heart of the enemies. \[Were those kings demoniac?\] It is said in śrī viṣṇu purāṇam “*viparītastatā’sura:*” (those who are not devotees of viṣṇu, are demons). To make the demoniac clan which cannot co-exist, bite the dust. Even demons are related to bhagavān, but the only shortcoming is their saying “We won’t accept and co-exist”.
- *nalla amarar polivu eyda* – It is said in śrī viṣṇu purāṇam “*viṣṇu bhakti parō dēva:*” (one who is devoted to viṣṇu, is divine). To make the favourable ones grow, even without consuming food. The goodness (nalla) in them – being devotee of bhagavān. [tiruvāimoḻi 9.4.9](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/07/thiruvaimozhi-9-4-9-kandu-kondu/) “*toṇḍarkkamuduṇṇac col mālaigaḷ sonnēn*” (I did vācika kainkarayam in the form of a garland of words for the joyful experience of the servitors of the apt lord).
- *eṇṇādana …* – There are some who think about those aspects which are not thought of by others. Instead of just remaining “sarvēśvaran is the saviour and everything other than him is protected by him”, there are some who think along the lines of “For the ubhayavibhūti yukta (one who is with spiritual and material realms), there should be some more wealth; for the one who is sarvaguṇa sampanna (one who is full in all qualities), there should be some more qualities”. Their,
- *inbam talai siṟappa* – After the advent of tiruvāimoḻi, they had their anguish of “he does not have enough wealth”, eliminated, and became ultimately joyful.
- *nanmunivar* – Those who meditate upon his opulence. Alternatively – those who become blissful thinking “we don’t need any other wealth than tiruvāimoḻi”.
- *paṇṇār pādal* – Song with tune. Just as a flower will blossom with fragrance, song \[poem\] is abundant with tune and music.
- *in kavigaḷ* – The poem is sweet on its own, even without the tune and music, just as a fruit is without the skin.
- *yānāyt tannait tān pādi* – Just as a father would grant a cow to his son, and will subsequently accept the same cow from the son; just as a father will teach some words to his son and will become joyful on hearing the son repeat those words. If he directly sang \[tiruvāimoḻi\], this would become like śrī gītā. nambi tiruvaḻudi dāsar, while explaining [kaṇṇinuṇ ciṟut tāmbu 8](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/02/kanninun-chiru-thambu-8-arul-kondadum/) “*aruḷ koṇḍādum*” pāsuram, said – When a scholar who is well trained in śrī gītā goes to an evening assembly \[in the maṇḍapam at the temple entrance\], many will give some rice, due to lack of faith in him, will tell him to stay in the veranda outside; when a scholar who is well trained in tiruvāimoḻi goes there, sarvēśvaran along with everyone else will come out to welcome him, and will honour him by giving their own residences and necessary food”. Even śrī gītā got its reputation by āḻvār’s acknovledgement in [tiruvāimoḻi 10.4.9](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/11/thiruvaimozhi-10-4-9-kanden/) “*paṇḍē paraman paṇitta*” (emperumān’s orders from long ago).
- *tennā ennum* – Due to joyful pride, emperumān will sing as in “tennā tennā” (swaying the head); just as a samsāri cētana (soul who is bound in this world), attains bhagavān, will sing sāma gānam as said in taittirīya upaniśat “*ētat sāma gāyannāstē*” (The liberated soul is singing sāma gānam), one \[emperumān\] who is said as in cāndōjña upaniśat 3.14 ‘*avākyanādara:’* (does not speak, ignores \[in paramapadam\]), gives up such state and will start singing.
- *en ammān* – Due to prāpti (the natural relationship), the child’s words are sweet; here the reason for such prāpti is explained.
- *tirumālirunjōlaiyānē* – This \[tirumālirunjōlai\] is the mukkōttai (mūkāmbikā kśētram which makes even the most ignorant person to sing wonderful poems) which made āḻvār sing. tirukkaṇṇapuram is the mukkōttai which made tirumangai āḻvār sing as said in periya tirumoḻi 8.10.9 “*pāttināl unnai en nenjattirundamai – kāttināy kaṇṇapurattuṟai ammānē*” (Oh lord residing in tirukkaṇṇapuram! You have revealed your presence in my heart through these songs). āḻvār thought about the sweetness of the pāsurams he sang and determined that such sweetness could not have been caused by self; he thought “what could be the reason?” and determined that emperumān having entered his heart, made him sing. āḻvār highlights the mukkōttai which made him sing as “*kaṇṇupurattuṟai ammān*“.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 10.7.6. Tirumalirunjolaiyane agi

*tirumālirunjōlaiyānē āgic ceḻumūvulagum tan oru mā vayiṟṟinuḷḷē vaittu ūḻi ūḻi talai aḷikkum tirumāl ennai āḷumāl sivanum piramanum kāṇādu arumāl eydi adi parava aruḷai īnda ammānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

sivanum – rudran (who is very knowledgeable); piramanum – and brahmā; kāṇādu – being unable to see; aru – difficult to attain; māl – very great devotion; eydi – being the one who is having; adi – divine feet; parava – to praise; aruḷai īnda – one who fulfilled the desire with his (endless) grace; ammān – being sarvādika (greater than all); seḻu – distinguished; mū ulagum – three worlds; than – one who can unite contrary aspects, his; oru – unique; mā – has skillful ability (to hide them from others’ vision); vayiṟṟin uḷḷē – in the divine stomach, in a particular way; vaittu – placing; ūḻi ūḻi – every kalpam; talai – primarily; aḷikkum – one who protects; tirumāl – one who is having śriya:patitvam (being the lord of śrī mahālakśmi, which is the cause for such śēśitvam and rakśaktvam); tirumālirunjōlaiyānē āgi – having his presence in tirumālirunjōlai; ennai – me; āḷum – to accept my service; māl – is very infatuated

**Перевод:**

**As rudra and brahmā could not see emperumān, they praised his divine feet with very great devotion which is difficult to attain, he fulfilled their desire with his grace; in every kalpam, such emperumān, who is greater than all, who primarily protects the distinguished three worlds by placing them in a particular way in his divine stomach which has the unique skillful ability to unite contrary aspects, who is having śriya:patitvam, is very infatuated, to accept my service, by having his presence in tirumālirunjōlai. orumā also indicates the insignificant, small portion \[in his stomach\].**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the sixth pāsuram, āḻvār says “śriya:pati (consort of śrī mahālakśmi) is mercifully standing in tirumalai and is very interested in ruling over me”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. tirumālirunjōlaiyānē āgic ceḻumūvulagum than oru mā vayiṟṟinuḷḷē vaittu ūḻi ūḻi talai aḷikkum tirumāl ennai āḷumāl sivanum piramanum kāṇādu arumāl eydi adi parava aruḷai īnda ammānē*

- *tirumālirunjōlaiyānē āgi – ennai āḷumāl* – One who stands having tirumālirunjōlai as his abode, is having a form which is an embodiment of the desire, to accept my service.
- *seḻu mū ulagum* – Well organized three layered world.
- *oru …* – Placing them in his unique small stomach, protects in every kalpam. Just as the world cannot sustain itself without emperumān, during the danger of deluge, he cannot sustain without me now.
- *tirumāl* – śriya:pati.
- *ennai āḷum māl* – One who has a form which is an embodiment of the desire, to accept my service.
- *sivanum piramanum …* – As brahmā, rudra et al, being unable to see sarvēśvaran, incohesively praised emperumān’s divine feet with great devotion, without appearing in front of them, he blessed them; such emperumān arrived in tirumālirunjōlai to be seen by me, and became mad to accept my service.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 10.7.7. Arulai i ennammane!

*aruḷai ī ennammānē! ennum mukkaṇ ammānum teruḷkoḷ piraman ammānum dēvarkōnum dēvarum iruḷgaḷ kadiyum munivarum ēttum ammān tirumalai maruḷgaḷ kadiyum maṇi malai tirumālirunjōlai malaiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

en ammānē – Oh my lord!; aruḷai I – mercifully grant (your) mercy; ennum – saying this; mukkaṇ ammānum – the three-eyed rudra (who thinks of himself as īśvara); teruḷ koḷ – one who has qualities such as jñānam etc (which helps his being the creator etc); piraman ammānum – brahmā who is the lord of the universe, by being the creator; dēvarkōnum – indra who is the controller of dēvas; dēvarum – dēvas (in the count of thirty three distinguished dēvatas and crores of other dēvas); iruḷgaḷ – darkness (such as jñāna abhāvam (lack of knowledge), anyatā jñānam (understanding an object to be something else) and viparīta jñānam (understanding the object’s attributes incorrectly) etc on svarūpa (true nature) and puruśārta (goal)); kadiyum – those who can eliminate through the instructions in the form of purāṇa etc; munivarum – great sages; ēttum – to praise; ammān – lord’s divine abode; tirumalai – tirumalai \[divine mountain\]; maruḷgaḷ – confusions such as avidyā (ignorance) etc which are hurdles for the goal; kadiyum – which can eliminate; maṇi – distinguished, to be ultimately enjoyable; malai – hill; tirumālirunjōlai – having the name, tirumālirunjōlai; malaiyē – the divine hill only

**Перевод:**

**emperumān is praised as “Oh my lord! Mercifully grant (your) mercy” by the three-eyed rudra who has qualities such as jñānam etc,  brahmā who has qualities such as jñānam etc and who is the lord of the universe, by being the creator, indra who is the controller of dēvas, dēvas and great sages who can eliminate darkness through instructions in the form of purāṇa etc.  The divine hill, which is the divine abode of such emperumān, which can eliminate confusions such as avidyā (ignorance) etc which are hurdles for the goal, which is distinguished to be ultimately enjoyable, is the one which is known as tirumālirunjōlai.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the seventh pāsuram, āḻvār praises tirumalai which is the cause for his \[āḻvār’s\] benefits.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. aruḷai I ennammānē! ennum mukkaṇ ammānum teruḷkoḷ piraman ammānum dēvarkōnum dēvarum iruḷgaḷ kadiyum munivarum ēttum ammān tirumalai maruḷgaḷ kadiyum maṇi malai tirumālirunjōlai malaiyē*

- *aruḷai I enbargaḷ* – They will pray to emperumān requesting to shower his mercy.
- *en ammānē* – Is there any other refuge for us if you don’t shower your mercy? They will say “You, who are apt for us, should shower your mercy”.

When asked “Who are those who pray for such mercy?” āḻvār says,

- *mukkaṇ …* – rudra, who is having an eye in the forehead and who considers himself to be the lord. caturmukha (brahmā) who is having the greatness of being the knowledge-giver and creator of such rudra, indra who checks the presence of dēvas every Saturday and Wednesday, dēvas who bring glory to indra by being his subjects. the meditating sages who eliminate the ignorance in the form of darkness along with the trace. This tirumālirunjōlai is the divine abode of such sarvēśvaran, who is praised in one tone by all of these entities, who comes and resides eagerly.
- *maruḷgaḷ kadiyum maṇi malai* – The abode which will completely eliminate the hurdles for the goal. That is – it will eliminate the thought of considering something other than tirumalai as the goal. When asked “Which entity does that?” āḻvār says, “Is there anything else? It is tirumālirunjōlai malai only”.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 10.7.8. Tirumalirunjolai malaiye

*tirumālirunjōlai malaiyē tiruppāṟkadalē en talaiyē tirumāl vaigundamē taṇ tiruvēngadamē enadudalē arumā māyattenaduyirē manamē vākkē karumamē orumā nodiyum piriyān en ūḻi mudalvan oruvanē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tirumālirunjōlai malaiyē – tirumālirunjōlai hill; tiruppāṟkadalē – tiruppāṟkadal (divine milky ocean); en talaiyē – my head; tirumāl – being śriya:pati as said in “śriyāsārdam“, residing in; vaigundamē – paramapadam (spiritual realm); taṇ – invigorating; tiruvēngadamē – periya tirumalai (main divine hill); enadu udalē – my body; aru – insurmountable; mā – great; māyattu – united with the amazing prakruti (matter); enaduyirē – my ātmā (self); manamē – mind; vākkē – speech; karumamē – action; oru mā nodiyum – even a fraction of a moment; piriyān – he is not separating; en ūḻi mudalvan – being the cause for all entities which are controlled by time, to acquire me; oruvanē – he is the distinguished one!

**Перевод:**

**emperumān, being the cause for all entities which are controlled by time, to acquire me, is not separating even for a fraction of a moment from tirumālirunjōlai hill, tiruppāṟkadal , my head, paramapadam where he is residing as śriya:pati as said in “śriyāsārdam“, invigorating periya tirumalai, my body, my ātmā which is united with the insurmountable, great, amazing prakruti, my mind ,speech and action. What a distinguished one he is! The ēkārams (long syllables, E in the end), indicate count or how he exclusively likes each of the aspects.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nampiḷḷai‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Eighth pāsuram. āḻvār says “All the desire he has towards temples starting with tirumalai, is being shown by him towards my limbs and is not separating from me even for a moment; what an amazing state is his!” tirumālirunjōlai malaiyē tiruppāṟkadalē en talaiyē tirumāl vaigundamē taṇ tiruvēngadamē enadudalē arumā māyattenaduyirē manamē vākkē karumamē orumā nodiyum piriyān en ūḻi mudalvan oruvanē*

- *tirumālirunjōlai malai …* – emperumān desired equally for tirumalai in southern direction, tiruppāṟkadal and āḻvār’s top-most limb; he desired equally for śrīvaikuṇṭam, tirumalai in northern direction and āḻvār’s divine form.
- *tirumāl vaigundam* – As said in Siva \[linga\] purāṇam “*vaikuṇṭē tu parē lōkē śriyāsārdam jagat patē*” (In the divine world of vaikuṇṭam, viṣṇu is present with śrī mahālakśmi, being served by nityasūris), the divine abode which matches the divine couple. Thus, emperumān showed all the desire he showed on the two tirumalais, para (paramapadam) and vyūha (kśīrābdi) on āḻvār’s divine form itself.
- *aru …* – emperumān desired equally for āḻvār’s ātmā and mind, speech and body. By the avadāraṇam (exclusivity in “E” in the end of each word), it is explained that even in such desire/enjoyment, emperumān is enjoying continuously without any break, in no particular sequence, assuming many forms like saubhari did.
- *aru …* – ātmā is remaining as sentient for namesake, but since time immemorial being united with acit (insentient, matter), he remained as acit only. Since it is said as “aru”, on ātmā which is united with acit which is difficult to cross over by anyone as said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 7-14](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/7-14/) ‘*mama māyā duratyayā’* (it is difficult to crossover my primordial matter).
- *manamē vākkē karumamē* – Previously, āḻvār explained how emperumān desired for the whole body together; here āḻvār is explaining how emperumān is desiring equally in each of the faculties.
- *oru mā nodiyum piriyān* – He will not separate even for a fraction of a moment. He is not taking himself off from one limb to other and enjoying it \[he is enjoying all of them at once\].
- *en ūḻi mudalvan oruvanē* – To enter me, he is remaining the distinguished, cause of all entities which are under the control of time. Just as during samhāram (annihilation) all the entities cannot sustain without emperumān, here emperumān is unable to sustain without āḻvār’s divine body. sarvēśvaran who has all cit and acit, both in causal and effectual states, to be under his control, is now having his sustenance under the control of my body.
- *en ūḻi mudalvan oruvanē!* – “This desirous person is known as īśvaran! What a distinguished one!” says āḻvār.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 10.7.9. Uli mudalvan

*ūḻi mudalvan oruvanē ennum oruvan ulagellām ūḻi tōṟum tan uḷḷē padaittuk kāttuk keduttuḻalum āḻi vaṇṇan en ammān andaṇ tirumālirunjōlai vāḻi manamē! kai vidēl udalum uyirum mangavottē*

**Пословный перевод:**

ūḻi – all entities which are under the control of time; mudalvan oruvanē – being the singular cause; ennum – as said in kāraṇa vākyams (statements which emphasise emperumān being the cause) such as “ēkamēva”; oruvan – being distinguished; ulagu ellām – all worlds; ūḻi tōṟum – all times which are favourable for creation etc; than uḷḷē – in a small portion of his divine will; padaittu – create; kāttu – protect; keduttu – annihilate; uḻalum – conducting these, having as routine; āḻi vaṇṇan – one who is unlimited; en ammān – being my lord due to this apt relationship; am – being beautiful; taṇ – invigorating; tirumālirunjōlai – tirumālirunjōlai; manamē – Oh heart!; udalum uyirum – our body, vital air etc are to be given up by us; manga – to be destroyed; ottu – go close and try to surrender unto; kai vidēl – do not give it up until our task is accomplished; vāḻi – you should live long by this

**Перевод:**

**Oh heart! To have our body, vital air etc, which are to be given up by us, destroyed, go close and surrender unto the beautiful, invigorating tirumālirunjōlai which is the abode of my lord due to this apt relationship. He is the distinguished, singular cause for all entities which are under the control of time as said in kāraṇa vākyams such as “ēkamēva“, who is unlimited and who routinely conducts creation, protection and annihilation of all worlds at all times which are favourable for creation etc, in a small portion of his divine will. Do not give it up until our task is accomplished. You should live long by this \[act of being surrendered unto the divine hill\]. āḻi vaṇṇan also indicates “he is the one with a divine form which is infinitely enjoyable”.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the ninth pāsuram, āḻvār tells his divine heart “We got all this wealth through tirumalai; hence, do not abandon this tirumalai” and tells emperumān seeing his desire to carry āḻvār with āḻvār’s body to tirunādu (paramapadam) “you should eliminate this body which should be given up and take me to paramapadam”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. ūḻi mudalvan oruvanē ennum oruvan ulagellām ūḻi tōṟum than uḷḷē padaittuk kāttuk keduttuḻalum āḻi vaṇṇan en ammān andaṇ tirumālirunjōlai vāḻi manamē! kai vidēl udalum uyirum mangavottē*

- *ūḻi mudalvan oruvanē ennum oruvan* – The one who is known as the cause of all the entities which are under the control of time, as said in taittirīya upaniśat “*sadēva sōmya idam agra āsīt*” (dear child! There was only sat in the beginning \[during *sruśti*, creation\]). One who takes and places all the effectual entities, when all of those were annihilated, on himself, is now coming and residing in my body. In the causal state, he remains the reason for the existence of all cit and acit; such emperumān is depending upon me for his existence.

When asked “If he ensures their existence in the causal state, will those entities manage themselves subsequently?” āḻvār says,

- *ulagu ellām …* – After giving name and form \[for these entities, as part of creation\], will they manage themselves? With this, it is explained that \[similarly\] emperumān cannot sustain himself without āḻvār at all times. Just as all the entities cannot sustain themselves during dangers such as deluge etc, emperumān cannot sustain himself without āḻvār.
- *āḻi vaṇṇan* – Implies that he is profound by nature; also explained as, one who rescued me from the deluge of samsāram, by showing his ocean-like invigorating form.
- *am taṇ tirumālirunjōlai* – The abode which is beautiful and invigorating even for such emperumān.
- *vāḻi manamē kai vidēl* – Oh heart! Let this opulence remain forever for you. This tirumalai is the cause for his overwhelming desire towards us. āḻvār tells his divine heart not to give up tirumālirunjōlai, ever. emperumān tells his divine heart “We got āḻvār in this divine body of his; so you also don’t give it up”; āḻvār is forcing emperumān “Oh benefactor! You cannot say that; you should give it \[my body\] up”.
- *udalum uyirum mangavottu* – You should agree for my body and vital air to be destroyed. This is not to be pursued as this tirumalai; this should be verily given up; you should agree for them to be destroyed. As āḻvār is saying “mangavottu”, it appears that āḻvār’s presence in samsāram is not due to the remainder of prārabda karma (the accumulated karma which has to be exhausted before ascending to paramapadam), but is due to bhagavat abhiprāyam (bhagavān’s wish). It highlights that āḻvār remained here since īśvara held on to āḻvār’s body without leaving it; he said in [tiruvāimoḻi 10.7.4](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2020/02/thiruvaimozhi-10-7-4-enkol-amman/) “*udalam kaividān*” (he is not abandoning my body).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 10.7.10. Mangavottu

*mangavottu un mā māyai tirumālirunjōlai mēya nangaḷ kōnē! yānē nīyāgi ennai aḷittānē! pongaimpulanum poṟiyaindum karumēndiriyam aimbūdam ingu ivvuyirēy pirakirudi mānāngāra manangaḷē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tirumālirunjōlai – in tirumālirunjōlai hill; mēya – eternally residing; nangaḷ kōnē – being the one who is the lord for those who are like me; yānē nī āgi – you being me without any difference between us, as if I am giving the remedy myself; ennai – me; aḷittāy – oh one who protected!; pongu – rising (due to the enjoyment); aim pulanum – five types of enjoyable aspects such as sound, touch, form, taste and smell; poṟi aindum – five traps – (the senses which trap in such aspects) eye, ear, nose, tongue and skin which are jñānēndriyams (senses of knowledge); karumēndiriyam – five karmēndriyams (senses of action) which help in engaging in such aspects; aim būdam – panca būtams (five great elements) such as earth, water, air, fire and ether which are the abodes for śabda etc and which are the cause for the body which holds the senses; ingu – in this samsāram; i uyir ēy – being closely bound with the ātmā; pirakiruti – mūla prakruti (primordial matter); mān – mahān which facilitates creation; āngāram – ahankāra which facilitates ego/intellect; manangaḷ – mind which is the cause for sankalpa (will); un mā māyai – your very amazing prakruti and effects of prakruti; mangavottu – mercifully agree to destroy them

**Перевод:**

**Oh one who is eternally residing in tirumālirunjōlai hill, being the one who is the lord for those who are like me, being me without any difference between us, as if I am giving the remedy myself, and who protected me! Mercifully agree to destroy your very amazing prakruti and effects of prakruti which constitute five types of rising, enjoyable aspects such as sound, touch, form, taste and smell, five traps such as eye, ear, nose, tongue and skin which are jñānēndriyams, five karmēndriyams (senses of action) which help in engaging in such aspects, panca būtams such as earth, water, air, fire and ether which are the abodes for śabda etc and which are the cause for the body which holds the senses, primordial matter which is closely bound with ātmā in this samsāram, mahān which facilitates creation, ahankāra which facilitates ego/intellect and mind which is the cause for sankalpa.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the tenth pāsuram, even after āḻvār praying to emperumān, emperumān did not accept āḻvār’s words due to his attachment towards āḻvār’s body; hence āḻvār informs emperumān about the prakruti which is made of twenty four elements, which is to be given up and requests emperumān to mercifully eliminate it, without having any desire for it.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Tenth pāsuram. Even after āḻvār’s insistence, emperumān was not listening to him as if he is playing chess; emperumān asks “What are you talking about! While applying sandalwood paste, would one break the container?” \[Hence\] āḻvār again says “let it be destroyed”. mangavottu un mā māyai tirumālirunjōlai mēya nangaḷ kōnē! yānē nīyāgi ennai aḷittānē! pongaimpulanum poṟiyaindum karumēndiriyam aimbūdam ingu ivvuyirēy pirakirudi mānāngāra manangaḷē*

- *un mā māyai mangavottu* – Agree to let this body which was bound by you so tightly, which cannot be removed by anyone, to be destroyed. emperumān says “If you understand that it has to be given up, why don’t you just leave it? Why should I agree for that?” \[āḻvār says\] “How can I, who am incapable, leave the bondage which was caused by sarvaśakti (omnipotent lord)? Did you not say in [śrī bhagavat gītā 7-14](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/7-14/) ‘*mama māyā duratyayā’* (it is difficult to crossover my primordial matter)”?
- *tirumālirunjōlai mēya nangaḷ kōnē* – Though having paramapadam as your divine assembly, did you not give it up and arrive in tirumālirunjōlai hill ahead of me, to follow my orders? If you were to do it as per your will, would you have not taken me from there itself? Oh one who arrived and stood in tirumālirunjōlai to announce to me your lordship and my servitude!
- *yānē āgi ennai aḷittānē* – Why are you, who carry my thoughts and act to fulfil them, remaining like this even after my prayers? All along, you have been protecting me even without my prayers. Even after āḻvār said in this manner, emperumān remained quiet, not willing to eliminate the body. āḻvār asked “Why are you remaining quiet as if you have not heard me even after my insistence?” emperumān says “I am not remaining quiet; what you identify as that which is to be given up, is desirable for me; hence we are unable to distinguish between what is to be given up and what is to be accepted; you who understand the truth should explain that to me so that I can eliminate the same”; āḻvār says “Alright! Why don’t you listen to me now?” and starts explaining.
- *poingaimpulan …* – What was carried out by emperumān towards āḻvār previously in [tiruvāimoḻi 8.8.3](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/04/thiruvaimozhi-8-8-3-unarvil-umbar/) “*uṇarvum uyirum udambum maṟṟulappilanavum paḻudēyām uṇarvaip peṟa ūrndu*” (he conducted himself to make me realise “The knowledge in the form of actions, five types of prāṇa , different types of body, mahat, ahankāra and indriya are all to be given up”), is now informed by āḻvār to emperumān. The result of vyāmōham (bhagavān’s love on retaining āḻvār’s body) can very will match the result of karma (one’s past virtues/vices); unlike the result of karma, the result of love is eternal. \[Hence āḻvār is forcefully praying emperumān to give up such love for āḻvār’s body\] Let all of these pleasures such as (a) śabda etc which can transform the cētanas to take them \[cētanas\] away from themselves, (b) the jñānēndriyams which can deeply engage and destroy the cētana in such pleasures just as rat-traps, which will certainly capture the rats etc by showing some food items, (c) karmēndriyams, (d) panca būtams starting with prutivi (earth). (e) mūla prakruti which holds on the effectual cit and acit entities, (f) mahān, (g) ahankāram and (h) manas, be destroyed. \[Would māmāyai, the primordial matter, point to body?\] The same prakruti which is causal state has become body in effectual state.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 10.7.11. Manangara manam

*mānāngāra manam keda aivar vankaiyar mangat tānāngāramāyp pukkut tānē tānē ānānait tēnāngārap poḻil kurugūrc catakōpan sol āyirattuḷ mānāngārattivai pattum tirumālirunjōlai malaikkē*

**Пословный перевод:**

mānāngāra manam – The connection with body through mahān, ahankāram and manas (mind); keda – to be destroyed; vankaiyar – very strong; aivar – five senses; manga – to be destroyed (along with their respective pleasure); tān āngāramāy – being with great abhimānam (pride); pukku – entered; tānē tānē ānānai – one who became my self and belongings; tēn āngāram – prideful due to having beetles; poḻil – having garden; kurugūrc catakōpan – nammāḻvār who is the leader of āḻvārtirunagari; sol āyirattuḷ – among the thousand pāsurams mercifully spoken by him; tirumālirunjōlai malaikkē – exclusively for tirumālirunjōlai hill; ivai pattum – this decad; mānāngārattu – focussed on all hurdles which are indicated by mahat and ahankāram

**Перевод:**

**emperumān with great abhimānam, to have the connection with body through mahān, ahankāram and manas and five senses destroyed, entered and became my self and belongings; nammāḻvār who is the leader of āḻvārtirunagari which is having prideful garden due to having beetles, mercifully spoke this decad exclusively for tirumālirunjōlai hill, among the thousand pāsurams; this decad is focussed on all hurdles which are indicated by mahat and ahankāram. Implies that for those who learnt this decad, hurdles such as mahat, ahankāra etc will leave naturally.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the end, āḻvār says “This decad which deals about mahat and ahankāram, is spoken of, on tirumalai”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. mānāngāra manam keda aivar vankaiyar mangat tānāngāramāyp pukkut tānē tānē ānānait tēnāngārap poḻil kurugūrc catakōpan sol āyirattuḷ mānāngārattivai pattum tirumālirunjōlai malaikkē*

- *mānāngāra manam keda* – To destroy those which are known as mahān, ahankāram and manas; this also implies \[mūla\] prakruti (primordial matter).
- *aivar vankaiyar manga* – This \[five jñānēndriyams – senses of knowledge\] also implies karmēndriyams (senses of action) and pleasures such as śabdam etc. Did he ask them to fade away? If he agrees to give up his forceful attachment, they will leave him. If he nods his head saying “I agree”, there is nothing wrong in saying that āḻvār’s desire is fulfilled.
- *tān …* – emperumān entered me as the controller for me; emperumān pridefully entered me.
- *tānē tānē ānānai* – emperumān eliminated my claim over my self and belongings and entered as the controller; alternatively – without expecting my request, he himself became the one who requested and became the exclusive controller.
- *tēn āngāram …* – āḻvār, who is the controller of āḻvārtirunagari, which is having garden,liked by beetles, mercifully spoke this decad among the thousand pāsurams, to destroy mūla prakruti which is the form of mahat, ahankāram etc; this decad which is spoken pridefully.
- *tirumālirunjōlai malaikkē* – This decad is spoken of, on tirumalai; if there is a section which is spoken about aḻagar emperumān, that should be considered as speaking about kalpakataru (heavenly wish-fulfilling tree). Anything which is on tirumalai, is desirable; kulaśēkarāḻvār also mercifully mentioned in perumāḷ tirumoḻi 4.10 “*emperumān pon malai mēl ēdēnum āvānē*” (Let me become anything on the golden tiruvēngadamalai).

## 10.8 Tirumalirunjolai malai

## 10.8.1. Tirumalirunjolai malai

*tirumālirunjōlai malai enṟēn ennat tirumāl vandu en nenju niṟaiyap pugundān kurumā maṇi undu punal ponnit tenpāl tirumāl senṟu sērvidam tentiruppērē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tirumālirunjōlai malai enṟēn enna – as I said tirumālirunjōlai; tirumāl – emperumān who is śriya:pati (consort of śrī mahālakśmi) and who is very complete; vandu – (like someone with an expectation) arrived; en nenjam – in my heart (which does not co-operate with the words which are spoken); niṟaiya – fully; pugundān – entered; tirumāl – (to arrive in my heart) one who is residing in the divine abode of paramapadam, along with her as said in “śriyāsārdam jagatpati:”; senṟu sērvidam – the abode where he reached and mercifully rested; kuru mā maṇi – very best precious gems; undu – pushing; punal – having water; ponni – on river ponni’s (cauvery’s); tenpāl – on the southern bank; then tiruppēr – beautiful tiruppēr

**Перевод:**

**As I said tirumālirunjōlai, emperumān who is śriya:pati and very complete, arrived in my heart and fully entered it. The abode where he, who is residing in the divine abode \[of paramapadam\] along with her as said in “śriyāsārdam jagatpati:“, reached and mercifully rested is the beautiful tiruppēr which is on the southern bank of river ponni, which is having water which pushes very best precious gems.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the first pāsuram, āḻvār says “Incidentally I said tirumālirunjōlai malai; having said that, emperumān, who is fully without any expectation, arrived along with pirātti and mercifully entered me”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. tirumālirunjōlai malai enṟēn ennat tirumāl vandu en nenju niṟaiyap pugundān kurumā maṇi undu punal ponnit tenpāl tirumāl senṟu sērvidam tentiruppērē*

- *tirumālirunjōlai …* – āḻvār is explaining the reason for īśvaran’s acceptance of āḻvār now, while īśvaran did not accept āḻvār since time immemorial. When hills in a town are identified, it is common to highlight the specific attribute of the hill; similarly I said “*tirumālirunjōlai malai*“.
- *enna* – Even my mind did not co-operate; I only spoke the words. empeumān remains thinking “As he is a śēśabhūta (servitor), as I am the means \[for his goal\], as his benefit is my benefit, and as it is sufficient to say a few words which highlight that he is a cētana (conscious person), what more is expected?” For emperumān, this is a distinguished hill. The words cannot be negated; he is not of the nature to analyse the root of the words. He who said to vibhīśaṇa, the brother of rāvaṇa “a friendly attitude is sufficient” will not expect anything more than this. emperumān thinks “While there are many hills, āḻvār specifically named this hill due to his great attachment towards it”. Thus this \[speech\] makes it look like there is nothing \[no reason\] in āḻvār \[from āḻvār’s point of view\] and there is something for emperumān \[from emperumān’s point of view\].
- *tirumāl* – āḻvār is saying that pirātti, who would change the words which were said without heart’s approval to heart-felt speech, is present in close proximity.
- *vandu* – āḻvār becomes amazed thinking “He has himself come!” and his words reflect “īsn’t it natural that a thirsty person will come to the place where there is water?” emperumān remained thinking “It is natural for a needy person to come to the best/resourceful person”. I have become approachable to the one who is approachable by all! As said in samkśēpa rāmāyaṇam 38 “*sōbhyagaccat – śabarīm*” (śrī rāma reached śabari).
- *en nenjam* – In my heart which is with those words.
- *niṟaiyap pugundān* – He entered so that there is no space for other \[worldly\] matters, just as śrī rāma stood humbly in atri bhagavān āśramam saying “I am rāma; this is mytili; this is lakśmaṇa”, offering obeisances. Just as the vacuum was eliminated in the forest, he entered my heart and eliminated the vacuum.
- *kuru …* – āḻvār is saying that while emperumān desirously reached the great abode tiruppēr, he entered my heart. One who is the goal of everyone is having me as his goal. On the southern bank of ponni (cauvery) which is having water which pushes very expensive, beautiful gems. Implies that it is a praiseworthy abode. As said in śrī rangarāja stavam pūrva śatakam 21 “*dugdābhdir janaka: …*” (Milky ocean is the father, I am the mother, lakshmi is daughter and śrīranganāta is the lord).
- *punal* – One who has an invigorating abode (tiruppēr), is entering my heart. \[This can also be seen as – one who has an invigorating abode (paramapadam), is entering tiruppēr\]
- *tirumāl senṟu sērvidam* – emperumān, who has rich tastes, reached tiruppēr desirously, along with pirātti. As soon as I uttered the words “tirumālirunjōlai malai” even without heart’s co-operation, he left his divine abode \[of tiruppēr\] and entered my heart. In the first instance when the term “*tirumāl*” is mentioned, pirātti’s puruśakāra bhāvam (being the one who recommends) is explained \[this is explained in the first half of dvaya mahā mantram\]; the “*tirumāl*” in the end implies the connection of lakshmi with emperumān in the second half \[of dvaya mahā mantram, which explains that pirātti is coexisting with emperumān to be the recipient of our kainkaryam\].

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 10.8.2. Pere uraiginra

*pērē uṟaiginṟa pirān inṟu vandu pēṟēn enṟu en nenju niṟaiyap pugundān kārēḻ kadalēḻ malai ēḻulaguṇḍum ārā vayiṟṟānai adangap pidittēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

pērē – in tiruppēr; uṟaiginṟa – one who is eternally residing; pirān – sarvēśvaran; inṟu vandu – (as if he were incomplete before) today (without any reason, as if he were with expectation) came; pērēn enṟu – saying “I will not leave” (even if we ask him to leave); en nenju – in my heart; niṟaiya – to make it very complete; pugundān – entered; kār ēḻ – seven types of clouds (such as puśkalāvartakam etc); kadal ēḻ – seven oceans; malai ēḻ – having the seven kulaparvatams (anchoring mountains); ulagu uṇḍum – even after consuming all the worlds; ārā vayiṟṟānai – one who has unfilled stomach; adanga – entering in me and becoming complete in all ways; pidittēn – got to enjoy

**Перевод:**

**sarvēśvaran who is eternally residing in tiruppēr came today saying “I will not leave” and entered my heart to make it very complete; even after consuming all the worlds, having seven types of clouds, seven oceans and seven anchoring mountains, he remained with unfilled stomach; I got to enjoy him who entered in me and became complete in all ways.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the second pāsuram, āḻvār says “Though he was sarvēśvaran previously too, due to not having united with me, he was having shortcomings, and after entering my heart without any reason, he became complete”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. pērē uṟaiginṟa pirān inṟu vandu pēṟēn enṟu en nenju niṟaiyap pugundān kārēḻ kadalēḻ malai ēḻulaguṇḍum ārā vayiṟṟānai adangap pidittēnē*

- *pērē uṟaiginṟa pirān* – sarvēśvaran who has arrived in tiruppēr and eternally residing there.
- *inṟu vandu* – āḻvār would have known previously that this will happen, had he performed any sādanānuśtānam (pursuit of means).
- *pērēn enṟu* – He kept repeating “I won’t leave”, though there was no one to ask him “Will you leave or stay?” He is saying the words which are said by pirātti about him, towards me \[pirātti’s words as in tiruvāimoḻi 6.10.10 “*agalagillēn iṟaiyum*” (I won’t leave even for a moment from his chest)\] Though there is no one to raise unnecessary doubts about his leaving, he keeps vowing saying “I won’t leave”; śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 19.21 “*tribhistai: bhrātrubhi: śapē*” (I take oath on my three brothers).
- *en nenju* – My heart which remains “It does not matter whether he leaves or stays”.
- *niṟaiyap pugundān* – Entered to become complete.
- *kār …* – Placing all the worlds containing seven types of clouds such as puśkalāvartakam etc, seven oceans, seven mountains, in his divine stomach and still remained “What \[good\] have I done?” just as one who stole from a person who faithfully resided with him. One who remains “I have not done anything \[good for you\]” even after performing all types of protection starting from sruśti (creation) to mōkśam (liberation) for the protected ones.
- *adangap pidittēnē* – I held him well to make him feel satisfied that “We have done everything good for him”. Rescuing the worlds from the deluge implies again engaging in samsāram deeply; he was feeling incomplete since he did not carry the ātmās to paramapadam; as I have become ready to be carried by him all the way to paramapadam, his desire has become fulfilled. I have become the target of his very complete acceptance.
