## 10.8.3. Piditten

*pidittēn piṟavi keduttēn piṇi sārēn madittēn manai vāḻkkaiyuḷ niṟpadōr māyaiyai kodik gōbura mādangaḷ sūḻ tiruppērān adiccērvadu enakku eḷidāyinavāṟē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kodi – having flags; gōpuram – on towers; mādangaḷ – on mansions; sūḻ – surrounded by; tiruppērān – one who is easily approachable and is having tiruppēr as his residence; adi – divine feet; sērvadu – reaching; enakku eḷidāyina āṟu – easily approachable way for me; pidittēn – got to reach (his divine feet without any reason at first); piṟavi – connection to birth; keduttēn – eliminated; piṇi – (caused by such birth) sorrows; sāṟēn – won’t have; manai vāḻakkai uḷ – in samsāram (bondage); niṟpadu – remaining; ōr māyaiayai – ignorance; madittēn – avoided

**Перевод:**

**Seeing the easily approachable way for me for reaching the divine feet of the one who is easily approachable and is having tiruppēr which is surrounded by mansions and towers having flags, as his residence, I got to reach the same; I eliminated my connection to birth; I won’t have any sorrows; I have avoided the ignorance of remaining in samsāram.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the third pāsuram, āḻvār meditates upon emperumān’s nirhētuka samślēśam (union without reason) and says “Such emperumān’s divine feet are easily available for me!”*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. pidittēn piṟavi keduttēn piṇi sārēn madittēn manai vāḻkkaiyuḷ niṟpadōr māyaiyai kodik gōbura mādangaḷ sūḻ tiruppērān adiccērvadu enakku eḷidāyinavāṟē*

- *pidittēn* – As he placed his divine feet on my head as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 10.6.6](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2020/01/thiruvaimozhi-10-6-6-thalaimela-thalinaigal/) “*talai mēla tāḷiṇaigaḷ*” (his divine feet on my head), I caught them firmly.
- *piṟavi keduttēn* – I eliminated the birth completely.
- *keduttēn* – I have not seen where it \[birth\] has gone.
- *piṇi sārēn* – I won’t acquire disease which will follow birth wherever it goes.
- *madittēn …* – mūīa prakruti is the māyā (ignorance) which makes one remain in samsāram (material realm) – I made it retract. Just as kriṣṇa made the nāgāstram (snake based weapon) to retract after knocking down arjuna’s crown. Once, emperumānār was walking and he mercifully turned around before reaching the end of the place; embār who was watching this from behind the doors, sneaked his head in and asked “are you meditating upon tirumālirunjōlai \[decad\] in your divine heart?” emperumānār mercifully said “yes, that is it”.
- *kodi …* – It has become easy for me to attain the divine feet of the one who is standing in tiruppēr which is having towers and mansions having flags! While śāstram instructs us to follow strenuous process saying “Close the eyes, placing bermuda grass on them, drink pancagavyam (five products given by cow), stay upside down, lift your leg up”, I have got this secret route!
- *enakku …* – One who was fully immersed in the worldly pleasures, is now seeing himself at emperumān’s divine feet.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 10.8.4. Elidayinavarenru

*eḷidāyinavāṟenṟu en kaṇgaḷ kaḷippak kaḷidāgiya sindaiyanāyk kaḷikkinṟēn kiḷi tāviya sōlaigaḷ sūḻ tiruppērān teḷidāgiya sēn visumbu taruvānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

en kaṇgaḷ – my thirsty eyes; eḷidu āyina āṟu enṟu – saying “the goal which is difficult to attain, has become easy!”; kaḷippa – to become joyful; kaḷidu āgiya – joyful; sindaiyanāy – being with the one who has the heart; kaḷikkinṟēn – I am enjoying; kiḷi tāviya – dense to let the parrots hop around; sōlaigaḷ sūḻ – surrounded by gardens; tiruppērān – one who is present as easily approachable in tiruppēr; teḷidu āgiya – being radiant, due to its being filled with great goodness; sēṇ visumbu – parama vyōma (supreme sky) which is higher (than the abode of brahmā); taruvān – is ready to bestow

**Перевод:**

**Being with the one who has the joyful heart, where my thirsty eyes are saying “the goal which is difficult to attain, has become easy!” to become joyful, I am enjoying; emperumān who is present as easily approachable in tiruppēr which is surrounded by dense gardens where the parrots hop around, is ready to bestow me parama vyōma which is higher and is radiant, due to its being filled with great goodness.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fourth pāsuram, āḻvār meditates upon the nature of emperumān who is ready to bestow tirunādu (paramapadam) to him, wonders “How easy it is!” and says “I am joyful with a mind which has enjoyed along with my senses”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. eḷidāyinavāṟenṟu en kaṇgaḷ kaḷippak kaḷidāgiya sindaiyanāyk kaḷikkinṟēn kiḷi tāviya sōlaigaḷ sūḻ tiruppērān teḷidāgiya sēn visumbu taruvānē*

- *eḷidāyina āṟu* – [iraṇḍām tiruvandādi 22](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/10/irandam-thiruvandhadhi-22/) “*ariyadeḷidāgum …*” (If emperumān decides to grant us mōkśam which is difficult to attain, we will easily attain it) – even the most difficult result will be easily attainable. Where did we see it? “*kariyadu …*” (\[By emperumān’s grace\] Did gajēndrāḻvān not come out victorious over the crocodile and serve emperumān with the lotus flower?) – Did the elephant not get emperumān to arrive at the shore of the pond without any proper decoration?
- *eḷidāyina āṟu enṟu …* – Saying “That which is difficult to attain has become easily attainable!”, my eyes which were thirsty as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 9.4.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/07/thiruvaimozhi-9-4-1-maiyar-karunganni/) “*kāṇak karudum en kaṇṇē*” (my eyes long to see him), became joyful.
- *kaḷidu āgiya sindaiyan āy* – Having a delighted mind. My heart which is said as in [tiruvaimoḻi 3.8.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/10/thiruvaimozhi-3-8-1-mudiyane/) “*nediyānē****e****! enṟu kidakkum en nenjamē*” (My heart will remain still meditating upon his qualities), got to become joyful.
- *kaḷikkinṟēn* – I, who said in [tiruvāimoḻi 3.8.7](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/10/thiruvaimozhi-3-8-7-aviye-aramudhe/) “*kūviyum kāṇap peṟēn*” (even after calling out many times, I have not seen and enjoyed you), am now enjoying. āḻvār who was greatly craving for emperumān, along with his \[āḻvār’s\] senses, has now got to enjoy emperumān with his \[āḻvār’s\] senses.
- *kiḷi tāviya …* – emperumān of tiruppēr which is surrounded by eternally blossoming gardens.
- *teḷidu …* – There is a high sky (higher world) reaching where, one will never leave that abode and which will bring clarity in mind unlike this material world which is said as in [tiruvāimoḻi 10.6.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2020/01/thiruvaimozhi-10-6-1-arul-peruvar/) “*iruḷ taru mā jñālam*” (the vast world which gives us ignorance) – that is, emperumān is determined to grant to me paramapadam, which is beyond the abodes of brahmā et al.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 10.8.5. Vane taruvan

*vānē taruvān enakkā ennōdu otti ūnēy kurambai idanuḷ pugundu inṟu tānē tadumāṟṟa vinaigaḷ tavirttān tēnēy poḻil tentiruppēr nagarānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tēn ēy – abundance of beetles; poḻil – having garden; then – beautiful; tiruppēr nagarān – one who resides in the city named tiruppēr; enakku – for me; vānē taruvān āy – vowing to bestow me paramapadam; ennōdu – with me; otti – taking oath; Un ēy – abundance of flesh; kurambai idan uḷ – inside this body which is a skeleton; inṟu – today; tānē – on his own; pugundu – arrived and entered; tadumāṟṟam – reason for the perplexity (in his separation); vinaigaḷ – puṇya (virtues), pāpa (vices); tavirttān – eliminated

**Перевод:**

**emperumān who is residing in the beautiful city named tiruppēr which is having garden filled with beetles, vowing to bestow me paramapadam, taking oath with me, on his own, arrived and entered inside my body which is a skeleton filled with abundance of flesh, and eliminated puṇya and pāpa which are the reason for our perplexity. tēn also indicates honey.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fifth pāsuram, āḻvār says “emperumān who is in tiruppēr nagar vowed to me that he has decided to bestow me tirunādu (paramapadam), and eliminated the hurdles which make me perplexed”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. vānē taruvān enakkā ennōdu otti ūnēy kurambai idanuḷ pugundu inṟu tānē tadumāṟṟa vinaigaḷ tavirttān tēnēy poḻil tentiruppēr nagarānē*

- *vānē taruvān enakkāy* – To be ready to bestow paramapadam to me. He stopped engaging me in his service here; saying “the abodes of brahmā et al do not fit āḻvār’s greatness”, he eliminated that as well; he decided to bestow the abode of nityasūris to me, a samsāri.
- *ennōdu otti* – Taking an oath along with me. Vowing along with me as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 21 “*arāvaṇam vā arāmam vā*” (You are going to see this world either without rāvaṇa’s presence or rāma’s presence), while I did not desire for it. Vowing with me saying “I will bestow you emmāvīdu (the great paramapadam)” to me who said in [tiruvāimoḻi 2.9.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/06/thiruvaimozhi-2-9-1-emma-vittu/) “*emmā vīttut tiṟamum seppam*” (I won’t ask for the form of liberation that is great in all ways).
- *Un ēy …* – emperumān says – if I delayed thinking “I would like to carry you to paramapadam with this body”, will I remain content to carry you without the body?
- *Un ēy …* – Just as a thirsty/tired person will immerse fully in a pond, emperumān immersed fully into my body instead of just superficially mixing with my body which is abundant with flesh and is the abode of the ātmā. Without separation even for a moment as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 10.7.8](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2020/02/thiruvaimozhi-10-7-8-thirumalirunjolai-malaiye/) “*enadudalē arumā māyattenaduyirē manamē vākkē karumamē orumā nodiyum piriyān*” (emperumān, being the cause for all entities which are controlled by time, to acquire me, is not separating even for a fraction of a moment from tirumālirunjōlai hill, tiruppāṟkadal , my head, paramapadam where he is residing as śriya:pati as said in “*śriyāsārdam*“, invigorating periya tirumalai, my body, my ātmā which is united with the insurmountable, great, amazing prakruti, my mind ,speech and action).
- *inṟu* – There was no such thought yesterday.
- *tānē* – emperumān who is not bound by karma. āḻvār had great attachment for body \[matter\] since time immemorial and never left it; now, as āḻvār developed attachment towards emperumān, emperumān who is not attached to matter, came and entered āḻvār’s body.
- *idan uḷ pugundu* – Only if āḻvār were unsure about next step like emperumān, will he not see the defects in this body? \[āḻvār is seeing his own body to be defective, while emperumān likes it\]
- *tānē …* – Does he voluntarily enter but subsequently let me also act favourably towards him \[for my benefits\]? \[No, he himself takes care of everything\]
- *tadumāṟṟa …* – He eliminated the sins which separate me from him and cause perplexity in me. They are explained as in [tiruvāimoḻi 10.7.10](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2020/02/thiruvaimozhi-10-7-10-mangavottu/) “*pongaim pulanum …*” (five types of rising, enjoyable aspects such as sound, touch, form, taste and smell, five traps such as eye, ear, nose, tongue and skin which are jñānēndriyams, five karmēndriyams (senses of action) which help in engaging in such aspects, panca būtams such as earth, water, air, fire and ether which are the abodes for śabda etc and which are the cause for the body which holds the senses, primordial matter which is closely bound with ātmā in this samsāram, mahān which facilitates creation, ahankāra which facilitates ego/intellect and mind which is the cause for sankalpa).
- *tēn ēy …* – emperumān who has tiruppēr nagar which is having garden with abundance of honey, has entered my body and is not leaving it even for a moment; what shortcoming he had to be fully engaged with me in this manner?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 10.8.6. Tirupper nagaran

*tiruppēr nagarān tirumālirunjōlaip poruppē uṟaiginṟa pirān inṟu vandu iruppēn enṟu en nenju niṟaiyap pugundan viruppē peṟṟu amudam uṇḍu kaḷittēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tiruppēr nagarān – in tiruppēr nagar; tirumālirunjōlai poruppē – in the divine hill named tirumālirunjōlai; uṟaiginṟa – one who is eternally residing; pirān – the great benefactor; inṟu – today (while there is no reason); vandu – himself arrived; iruppēn enṟu – vowing “let me stay here”; en nenju – my heart; niṟaiya – to become complete; pugundān – entered; viruppē peṟṟu – receiving (his perfect) gift; amudam uṇḍu – drinking the nectar (enjoying his qualities); kaḷittēn – I became joyful

**Перевод:**

**emperumān, the great benefactor who is residing eternally in tiruppēr nagar and in the divine hill named tirumālirunjōlai, arrived today vowing “let me stay here” and entered my heart to make it complete; receiving this gift, I became joyful, drinking the nectar.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the sixth pāsuram, āḻvār becomes pleased thinking “while emperumān has many merciful abodes, just like someone who has no place to stay, he arrived with the request ‘let me stay here’ and entered  my heart without any reason”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. tiruppēr nagarān tirumālirunjōlaip poruppē uṟaiginṟa pirān inṟu vandu iruppēn enṟu en nenju niṟaiyap pugundan viruppē peṟṟu amudam uṇḍu kaḷittēnē*

- *tiruppēr nagarān* – This divyadēśam is as great as tiruvayōdyai (śrī ayōdyā).
- *tirumālirunjōlai poruppē uṟaiginṟa pirān* – \[the presence in tirumālirunjōlai is greater than tiruppēr nagar\] As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 95.12 “*adikam puravāsācca*” (residing in this citrakūtam is greater than residing in ayōdyā); śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 57.38 “*jahau ca du:kam puravi pravāsāt*” (śrī rāma’s became joyful in seeing the river mālyavati and even forgot the sorrow of coming to the forest leaving ayōdyā). This is similar to what happened in tiructitrakūtam \[where śrī rāma became more joyful than in ayōdyā\]. śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 99.12 “*kubhēra iva nandanē*” (like kubhēra strolling around in a garden) – this is similar to a worry-less person strolling around in a garden. Only for a person who has no worries in all manner, is there scope for enjoyment in playful aspects. \[Similarly emperumān is enjoying in tirumālirunjōlai\]
- *inṟu vandu* – While there was no such thought, yesterday, to arrive in this manner, we have seen him arriving today.
- *iruppēn enṟu* – emperumān kept repeating “I will stay here”. śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 94.15 “*ihaiva śaratā anēkā: tvayā sārdam aninditē*” (Oh unblemiśed one! I will live here with you for many years) and śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 15.19 “*iha vatsyām saumitrē sārdam ētēna pakśiṇā:*” (Oh lakśmaṇa! I am going to live here along with jatāyu mahārāja) – śrī rāma said “We desired to live under the sceptre/order of our father, daśarata; but since that was not to the liking of kaikēyi, the second mother, we left ayōdyā; for the rest of our time in the forest, let us live under the shade of jatāyu mahārāja’s wings”.
- *en nenju niṟaiyap pugundān* – He entered my heart to fill it, which does not fully remain for such emperumān who desires to remain there.
- *viruppē peṟṟu* – Not residing due to the hatred of not fulfilling the commandments. There is a presence as said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 16.19](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/16-19/) “*tānaham dviśata: krūrān*” (I push those evil persons into demoniac births)**;** unlike that, being desirable by him.
- *amudam uṇḍu kaḷittēnē* – Unlike the enjoyment en route to the hell due to consuming poisonous food, I drank the nectar and became blissful (Implies enjoying by drinking the nectar of praising him; enjoying his nectarean qualities). Being inclined towards lowly pleasures, sowing the seeds for hellish after-life, and enjoying in between \[in this world\]. That is as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 4.1.5](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/11/thiruvaimozhi-4-1-5-panimin-thiruvarul/) “*aṇi men kuḻalār inbak kalavi amuduṇḍār*” (They enjoyed the nectar of blissful union of damsels who have tender hairs with decorations).
- *kaḷittēnē* – This bliss is the prideful bliss explained in [tirumālai 1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/07/thirumalai-1-part-2/) “*nāvalittu uḻitaruginṟōm*” (we keep walking with a victorious war-cry). I became blissful having placed my feet on the head of yama et al.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 10.8.7. Undu kalitterku

*uṇḍu kaḷittēṟku umbar en kuṟai? mēlait toṇḍu ugaḷittu andi toḻum sollup peṟṟēn vaṇḍu kaḷikkum poḻil sūḻ tiruppērān kaṇḍu kaḷippak kaṇṇuḷ ninṟu agalānē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vaṇḍu kaḷikkum – beetles which enjoy (drinking nectar); poḻil sūḻ – surrounded by garden; tiruppērān – emperumān residing in tiruppēr nagar; kaṇḍu kaḷippa – to be blissful by constantly seeing (him); kaṇ uḷ ninṟu – being the object of my sight; agalān – is not leaving; uṇḍu kaḷittēṟku – (in this manner) for me who enjoyed him eternally; umbar – enjoyment in going further to a special abode (paramapadam); en kuṟai – what worry is there?; mēlait toṇḍu – great servitude; ugaḷittu – acquiring great joy; andi – in the end; toḻum – (as said in “nama ityēva vādina:“) words indicating worship/surrender; sollu – to say the word “nama:”; peṟṟēn – got

**Перевод:**

**emperumān who is residing in tiruppēr nagar surrounded by garden having joyful beetles, who is the object of my sight to cause bliss in me by constantly seeing him, is not leaving. What worry is there for me who enjoyed him eternally about the enjoyment in going further to a special abode of paramapadam? In the end, I got to say the word “nama:” which indicates worship/surrender, after acquiring great joy by the great servitude. ugaḷittal – being in abundance.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the seventh pāsuram, āḻvār merciful explains his blessedness.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. uṇḍu kaḷittēṟku umbar en kuṟai? mēlait toṇḍu ugaḷittu andi toḻum sollup peṟṟēn vaṇḍu kaḷikkum poḻil sūḻ tiruppērān kaṇḍu kaḷippak kaṇṇuḷ ninṟu agalānē*

- *uṇḍu kaḷittēṟku umbar en kuṟai* – Is there any worry for me who has enjoyed and become blissful in this manner? āḻvār thinks that there is nothing more needed for him after enjoying emperumān’s qualities and being blessed by emperumān as said in tiruvāimoḻi 1.1.1 “*mayarvaṟa madinalam aruḷinan*” (emperumān bestowed unblemiśed knowledge and devotion). After attaining true knowledge, would one have the worry of having not reached the goal in paramapadam? umbar – further.
- *mēlait toṇḍu …* – Having abundance of great servitude. Enjoying the feeling as said in parama samhitā “*yēna yēna dātā gaccati tēna tēna saha gaccati*” (wherever the lord goes, the servitor follows). Unlike as said in manu smriti 4.6 “*sēvā śvavrutti:*” (serving others is dog’s job) , this servitude is matching the true nature of the self.
- *toṇḍu ugaḷittu* – Due to the service rendered, the joy reached its peak. In that ultimate stage, one will knowingly utter the words as said in mahābhāratam śānti parvam 344.45 “*nama ityēva vādina:*” (The definition of the residents of śvēta dvīpa applies to the muktātmās (liberated souls) as well. They are always performing anjali (joined palms out of reverence); they are blissful as a result of that; they constantly recite “*nama:*“). I got to recite those words. That is, getting to serve by rendering tiruvāimoḻi which is a result of words drenched in overflowing bhakti.
- *vaṇḍu …* – One who resides in tiruppēr which is surrounded by the garden where beetles enjoy by drinking honey. The divine abode where the most wise and animals/insects enjoy without any difference.
- *kaṇḍu kaḷippa* – To the joy of my eyes which craved as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 3.8.4](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/10/thiruvaimozhi-3-8-4-kaigalal-ara/) “*mey koḷḷak kāṇa virumbum en kaṇgaḷē*” (My eyes desire to see you in front of me).
- *kaṇ uḷ ninṟu agalānē* – Even if I ask him to leave, he is not leaving my sight; just as those who are desirous to enjoy their beloved ones will not leave the place, holding on to a pillar. For me who got to enjoy him and became blissful, is there any further worry?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 10.8.8. Kannul ninragalan

*kaṇṇuḷ ninṟagalān karuttin kaṇ periyan eṇṇil nuṇ poruḷ ēḻisaiyin suvai tānē vaṇṇa nan maṇi mādangaḷ sūḻ tiruppērān tiṇṇam en manattup pugundān seṟindinṟē*

**Пословный перевод:**

kaṇ uḷ ninṟu – being eternally enjoyable for my external eyes; agalān – not leaving; karuttin kaṇ – in the heart (seeing his thoughts, due to the eagerness in carrying āḻvār from here to the special abode of paramapadam and enjoying there); periyan – is great; eṇṇil – while thinking (saying “let us know him”); nuṇ poruḷ – having very subtle qualities; tānē – himself (while enjoying); ēḻ isaiyin suvai – having the sweetness of sapta svaram (the seven musical notes); vaṇṇam – in many colours; nanmaṇi – made with the best gems; mādangaḷ sūḻ – surrounded by mansions; tiruppērān – one who is residing in tiruppēr; en manattu – in my heart (which craved to attain him); tiṇṇam – without any reason; inṟu – today; seṟindu – to remain firm; pugundān – entered

**Перевод:**

**emperumān who is residing in tiruppēr, being eternally enjoyable for my external eyes, is not leaving me; he is great in the heart; while thinking about him, he is having very subtle qualities, he is having the sweetness of sapta svaram, and is residing in tiruppēr which is surrounded by mansions made with the best gems in many colours; today, such emperumān entered my heart without any reason to remain firmly, here.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the eighth pāsuram, āḻvār says “emperumān of tiruppēr nagar who is perfectly enjoyable and whose nature is beyond our mind/speech, is remaining the object of my eyes always, showing love to never leave, entered my heart; he is not stopping to favour me according to my level”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. kaṇṇuḷ ninṟagalān karuttin kaṇ periyan eṇṇil nuṇ poruḷ ēḻisaiyin suvai tānē vaṇṇa nan maṇi mādangaḷ sūḻ tiruppērān tiṇṇam en manattup pugundān seṟindinṟē*

- *kaṇ uḷ ninṟu agalān* – He is not knowing that there is some other opulence for his constant sight.
- *karuttin kaṇ periyan* – Eliminating the lack of focus due to having ubhaya vibhūti (spiritual and material realm as his wealth), emperumān was eager to carry āḻvār to paramapadam, to command the ādivāhikas (those who guide the ātmās in their journey towards paramapadam) and he himself coming ahead and carrying āḻvār. It is not possible to conceive his urge in fulfilling our objective; iyattārahitan (one who cannot be described as having certain qualities). This is not just implying the commonly known principle which is explained in kauśīdaki upaniśat “*yasyāmatam*” (for whom brahmam is not known). He remains in this manner for our task; because “*karuttin kaṇ periyan*” (too great to comprehend in my heart) should align with “*en manattup pugundān*” (entered my heart).
- *eṇṇil nuṇ poruḷ* – One can only understand emperumān if emperumān voluntarily reveals himself, otherwise, one cannot understand emperumān by self-effort. But one cannot give up the effort to understand him.
- *ēḻisaiyin suvai tānē* – He is of the nature that one should try very hard to enjoy him. This is how sweet he is.
- *vaṇṇam …* – This is how great he is.
- *en manattu – seṟindu – pugundān* – He entered in me to remain inseparable as he remains with his divine consort, sītāp pirātti as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 21.6 “*ananyā rāghavēṇāham*” (I always remain united with śrī rāma); as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 2.3.4](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/02/thiruvaimozhi-2-3-4-enadhu-aviyul/) “*enadāvi uḷ kalanda*” (mixed seamlessly in my ātmā). āḻvār unnecessarily doubted “Would emperumān who is greater than all, voluntarily pursue me like this?”;  he did not see any reason for that.
- *tiṇṇam* – Certainly. There is no failing in this.

## 10.8.9. Inrennaip porulakki

*inṟennaip poruḷ ākkit tannai ennuḷ vaittān anṟu ennaip puṟam pōgap puṇarttadu en seyvān kunṟennat tigaḻ mādangaḷ sūḻ tiruppērān onṟu enakkaruḷ seyya uṇarttal uṟṟēnē*

**Пословный перевод:**

inṟu – now (after the initial merciful glance occurred); ennai – me (who previously remained as said in “asannēva“); poruḷ ākki – made to be an entity (as said in “santamēnam“); tannai – him (who is distinguiśedly enjoyable); en uḷ – in my heart (which is to be given up); vaittān – (voluntarily brought and) placed; anṟu – previously (before such merciful glance occurred); ennai – me (who is fully at his disposal); puṟam pōga – to stay away, by being engaged in worldly pleasures (facing away from him); puṇarttadu – vowed; en seyvān – why?; kunṟenna – to be said as a hill; tigaḻ – shining; mādangaḷ sūḻ – surrounded by mansions; tiruppērān – emperumān who is in tiruppēr; onṟu – the reason for one (of these two scenarios); enakku aruḷ seyya – to mercifully explain to me; uṇarttal uṟṟēn – was focussed (saying “you should truthfully inform me”)

**Перевод:**

**Now, emperumān made me to be an entity and placed himself in my heart; previously, why did he have the vow to let me stay away by being engaged in worldly pleasures? I was focussed on making emperumān who is in tiruppēr which is surrounded by shining mansions which are like hills, mercifully explain the reason for either one of the scenarios. Implies that if the reason for one scenario is explained, other will be opposite to that. When the nirhētuka viśayīkāram (pursuit without any reason) is questioned, even bhagavān, the omniscient, does not have an answer.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the ninth pāsuram, āḻvār says “I wanted to ask emperumān, who announced himself to me today and firmly united with me, ‘why did you ignore me all along?’ “.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. inṟennaip poruḷ ākkit tannai ennuḷ vaittān anṟu ennaip puṟam pōgap puṇarttadu en seyvān kunṟennat tigaḻ mādangaḷ sūḻ tiruppērān onṟu enakkaruḷ seyya uṇarttal uṟṟēnē*

āḻvār is saying I was focussed on asking emperumān “Why did you mercifully accept me today and ignore me previously?” Alternatively – seing sarvēśvaran’s urge in carrying āḻvār to paramapadam, asks him “While your highness are urging much more than me, why did you remain relaxed in separation of me since time immemorial?” āḻvār says “If your urge today is true, you should not have remained relaxed previously”; as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 36.33 “*natvām ihastām jānītē*” (emperumān is not aware of your presence here), some one had to mediate in between; he remained relaxed only due to not knowing where you are mercifully present, had he known the location, would he have remained relaxed even for a moment? Do you have to know this from my words? *kamala lōcanē* – Is the beauty of your eyes not sufficient to prove this? *rāma:* – Do you have to be unaware of him? śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 66.10 “*na jīvēyam kśaṇamapi vinātām asitēkśaṇām*” (śrī rāma says – I will not survive even for a moment without seeing sītā who has dark eyes). *rāma: kamala lōcanē* –  It is not that you are unaware of him; also it is not that you have not seen yourself in a mirror. *kamala lōcanē* – Alternatively, why is the redness in the eyes and anger?

- *inṟu ennaip poruḷ ākki* – I, who was like asat (matter), have been transformed to be an entity today. He said in [tiruvāimoḻi 5.7.3](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/08/thiruvaimozhi-5-7-3-karulap-putkodi/) “*poruḷ allāda ennai*” (I who was like matter).
- *tannai* – He who is desired by even the noblest persons.
- *en uḷ vaittān* – He brought himself and placed inside me fully so that he is inaccessible for others.
- *anṟu* – āḻvār is speaking about all the earlier times, before acquiring his special mercy. inṟu (today) implies the time after acquiring unblemiśed knowledge and devotion as said in tiruvāimoḻi 1.1.1 “*mayarvaṟa madi nalam*“.
- *ennaip puṟam pōgap puṇarttadu en seyvān* – āḻvār remains “Both separation from him previously, and union with him now, are due to his desire”. Can ātmā which is paratantram (subservient) move away or come close, on its own?
- *kunṟu …* – Such praiseworthy person is the one who is residing in tiruppēr which is surrounded by shining mansions which resemble an array of hills.
- *onṟu enakku aruḷ seyya* – You can give the reason for abandoning me previously or accepting me now.
- *uṇarttal uṟṟēnē* – I stood to request him to impress upon his divine heart to give a response for this. emperumān said “Do we have to explain this? Don’t you already know?” āḻvār said “I don’t know; your highness, who are omniscient should mercifully explain”. emperumān said “That is because, you accepted my entry in to your heart and to reside there”; āḻvār asked “Is there anything like my acceptance? [tiruvāimoḻi 1.7.7](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/09/thiruvaimozhi-1-7-7-yan-otti/) ‘*yān otti ennuḷ iruttuvam enṟilan*‘ (I did not think about keeping him inside my heart with acceptance)” emperumān said “Even if you did not invite me, you vorśipped me after my entry”; āḻvār said “as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 2.7.7](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/05/thiruvaimozhi-2-7-7-thirivikkiraman/) ‘*maruvit toḻum manamē tandāy’* (you bestowed the mind that made me fit well at your enjoyable lotus feet and worship), even that was done by your highness”; emperumān said “Yes; even otherwise, at par with me, you did not desire for worldly pleasures”; āḻvār said “as said in  [tiruvāimoḻi 2.7.8](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/05/thiruvaimozhi-2-7-8-vamanan/) ‘*ennait tīmanam keduttāy* (you reformed my evil mind), even that was done by your highness”; emperumān said “even if you did not do any of these, you worked on increasing *‘madinalam’* (tiruvāimoḻi 1.1.1 – the knolvedge and devotion) which I bestowed on you”; āḻvār said “as said in tiruvāimoḻi 5.3.4 “*kādal kadal puraiya viḷaivitta kāramar mēni*” (made abundant ocean like devotion to occur by your cloud-like divine form), even that was done by your highness”; in this manner, as āḻvār kept following up with more questions, emperumān became speechless, as being consumed by an ocean. nanjīyar asked bhattar “What was the ultimate answer given by īśvaran for this question?” bhattar mecifully said – emperumān became shy thinking “How can I respond to āḻvār having not acquired him all along, placing the blame on him?” and stood drawing patterns with his toe on the ground – is there any other response which can be given by him? That is – emperumān will neither say “You did not have the desire before to reach me” nor say “You have not pursued any means previously”; but will this not lead to vaiśamya (partiality \[of selecting a particular individual randomly\]), nairgruṇya (cruelty \[letting ātmās suffer without any reason\]) for īśvara and sarvamukti prasangam (emperumān should have liberated all, if there is no specific aspect in the ātmā to attain the goal)? No. That does not occur. Since emperumān is working since time immemorial to create advēśam (no hatred) and iccā (desire) and is waiting for an opportune time for that to mature in every ātmā. Since emperumān did not respond any further, āḻvār thought “We have known the answer; this must be the reason for his favours now: when we are not considering his coming into contact with us as unfavourable, and he was looking for an opportunity for such time when we don’t avoid him. ōr, when we give up the pursuit of all other means and pursue emperumān himself as the means, he will bestow the result”. Now, why did emperumān not mercifully explain this as the answer?  emperumān would not explain this natural attribute of a cētana having consciousness, as a sādanam (means) to attain him; he is the only upāyam (means); he remained silent thinking “What can I, who blamed āḻvār (ātmā) all along, say?” He is the one who will feel shy for what will occur in the future as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 10.9 “*hrīrēśā hi mamātulā*” (this is immense shame for me, for not reaching out to you and helping these brāhmaṇas before they came to me); emperumān’s state is such that, he had to respond to āḻvār’s step-by-step questions. The desire which is a natural attribute of consciousness is not contrary to the true nature of the self. emperumān asked “Would you not be satisfied, if you acquired your desired goal?” āḻvār responded “Yes that is sufficient for me”. Would a thirsty person drink the tender coconut water only after analysing and finding out how the water entered the coconut in first place?

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 10.8.10. Urren ugandu

*uṟṟēn ugandu paṇi seydu una pādam peṟṟēn īdē innam vēṇḍavadu endāy kaṟṟār maṟai vāṇargaḷ vāḻ tiruppērāṟku aṟṟār adiyār tamakku allal nillāvē*

**Пословный перевод:**

uṟṟēn – without any reason \[effort from my side\], I reached your divine feet; ugandu – out of love; paṇi seydu – serving through speech; una pādam peṟṟēn – I attained the divine feet of yours, who are the ultimate goal; endāy – Oh one who is naturally related to me!; īdē – this service only; innam – forever; vēṇḍuvadu – desired; kaṟṟār – those who are learned (by knowing what is to be known, from preceptors); maṟai – meanings of vēdam, which are heard; vāṇargaḷ – those who are experts in conducting them; vāḻ – living with bhagavat anubhavam (enjoying bhagavān); tiruppērāṟku – for you, who are residing in tiruppēr; aṟṟār – ananyārha (exclusively existing); adiyār tamakku – for those devotees; allal – sorrows which stop the enjoyment; nillāvē – will naturally not stay

**Перевод:**

**Without any reason \[effort from my side\], I reached your divine feet; I attained the divine feet of yours, who are the ultimate goal, by serving through speech, out of love. Oh one who is naturally related to me! This service only is desired forever by me! The sorrows which stop the enjoyment will naturally not stay for those exclusive devotes of yours who are residing in tiruppēr where those who are learned in the meanings of vēdam, which are heard, and are experts in conducting them, are living with bhagavat anubhavam. Also said as aṟṟārukku adiyār (the devotees of those who exclusively exist for emperumān).**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the tenth pāsuram, emperumān did not have any answer to āḻvār‘s question and mercifully told him “Tell me what should be done for you”; āḻvār says “I got to serve you with love and to enjoy your divine feet. I just need this more”; emperumān says “Alright! Granted”. āḻvār, being pleased, says “For those who surrender unto the emperumān of tiruppēr nagar, there is no sorrow”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Tenth pāsuram. As emperumān remained silent without an answer for āḻvār’s question since he is not seeing the reason for the same, emperumān asked “What shall I do for you further?” āḻvār said “Out of love, I got to serve you; this is what is needed further”. When we say “It was done by emperumān”, would it not cause vaiśamyam (partiality) and nairgruṇyam (cruelty) for him and also sarva mukti prasangam?  (the question of “Why is everyone not liberated?”) Since emperumān is granting it based on the desire of the ātmā, those defects do not affect emperumān. When asked “Why did emperumān not give that as the answer?”  that ruci (desire) is not the upāyam (means); that which directly leads to the result, is upāyam; since this ruci is adikāri svarūpam (natural attribute of ātmā), it is only a qualifier for the ātmā. Since upāyam (bhagavān as the means) is devoid of any expectation for assistance, this ruci cannot be the upāyam. Since this is not the upāyam, we can say that āḻvār does not have any upāyam in him, and for a remedy for sarva mukti prasangam, it can be considered as an aspect which makes emperumān grant the result. uṟṟēn ugandu paṇi seydu una pādam peṟṟēn īdē innam vēṇḍavadu endāy kaṟṟār maṟai vāṇargaḷ vāḻ tiruppērāṟku aṟṟār adiyār tamakku allal nillāvē*

- *uṟṟēn* – I have reached your divine feet, just as a huge ship reaching the shores.
- *ugandu …* – Out of love, I sang tiruvāimoḻi and enjoyed your divine feet. ugandu paṇi seygai – āḻvār is not saying that at present singing tiruvāimoḻi is sādanam (means) and subsequently it will be sādyam (result), since both (singing of tiruvāimoḻi and reaching his divine feet) are present at once \[āḻvār’s tiruvāimoḻi recital is not the means but part of his kainkaryam to emperumān\].
- *īdē innam vēṇḍuvadu* – This should go on forever. \[śāstram recommends mōkśam which is attributed as “*na ca punar āvruttatē*” (the abode of no return) – why are you just desiring for tiruvāimoḻi singing?} Not coming back to samsāram means – not stopping kainkaryam.

When asked “Is this inapt?” āḻvār says,

- *endāy* – This experience is apt for the true nature of the self. Servitude for self and lordship for your highness are natural attributes.

As emperumān agrees to āḻvār’s request, being pleased, āḻvār speaks further:

- *kaṟṟār* – Those who studied under a preceptor.
- *maṟai vāṇargaḷ vāḻ* – The abode where those who can sit on vyāsapadam (vyāsa’s position) for vēdam, are living with enjoyment.
- *tiruppērāṟku* – āḻvār is taking his face off emperumān out of overwhelming joy, and addressing emperumān in third person, looking at self; or āḻvār is directly saying to emperumān “you who are in tiruppēr”.
- *aṟṟār adiyār* – Those devotees who are exclusively existing for tiruppēr nagarān; or those devotees of those who exclusively exist for emperumān in tiruppēr.
- *allal nillāvē* – Sorrows will not remain with them.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 10.8.11. Nilla allal

*nillā allal nīḷ vayal sūḻ tiruppēr mēlnallār palar vāḻ kurugūrc catakōpansollār tamiḻ āyirattuḷ ivai pattumvallār toṇḍar āḷvadu sūḻ pon visumbē*

**Пословный перевод:**

allal – for sorrow; nillā – being the abode of not letting stay; nīḷ vayal sūḻ – being surrounded by vast fields; tiruppēr mēl – on tiruppēr; nallār – distinguished personalities; palar – many; vāḻ – living while hearing tiruvāimoḻi; kurugūrc catakōpan – nammāḻvār, the controller of āḻvārtirunagari, his; sol Ar – strung with words; tamiḻ – tamiḻ; āyirattuḷ – among the thousand pāsurams; ivai pattum vallār – those who can practice this decad; toṇḍar – bhāgavatas (devotees); āḷvadu – conducting it, being the leader; sūḻ – pervading everywhere, being boundless; pon – radiant; visumbu – paramapadam, which is known as paramavyōma

**Перевод:**

**nammāḻvār, the controller of āḻvārtirunagari, where many distinguished personalities live hearing tiruvāimoḻi, sang this decad on tiruppēr, the abode which does not let sorrows stay there, and which is surrounded by vast fields, among the thousand tamiḻ pāsurams strung with words; those devotees who can practice this decad will become the leader and conduct paramapadam, which is known as paramavyōma, which is pervading everywhere, being boundless and radiant.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the end, āḻvār says “the distinguished, radiant tirunādu (paramapadam) will be at the disposal of those who are experts in this decad”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. nillā allal nīḷ vayal sūḻ tiruppēr mēlnallār palar vāḻ kurugūrc catakōpansollār tamiḻ āyirattuḷ ivai pattumvallār toṇḍar āḷvadu sūḻ pon visumbē*

- *nillā allal* – Sorrows will think “this is not our abode” and leave on their own.
- *nīḷ vayal …* – This decad was spoken on tiruppēr which is surrounded by vast fields.
- *nallār …* – This decad was mercifully spoken by āḻvār who owns tirunagari where those who are pleased enjoying āḻvār, are living. tiruviruttam 1 “*nallār navil kurugūr*” (tirukkurugūr where noble personalities reside). śankśēpa rāmāyaṇam “*sarvadā apigata: sadbhi:*” (One who is reached by great personalities, just as the rivers reach the ocean).
- *sol Ar …* – Thousand tamiḻ pāsurams which are strung by words; alternative explanation – the thousand tamiḻ pāsurams, where the words are sufficient for sweetness as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam bāla kāṇḍam 4.8 “*pātyē gēyē ca maduram*” (both words and music are sweet).
- *ippattum vallār toṇḍar* – Those who can practice this are śrīvaiṣṇavas who serve through words as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 10.7.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2020/02/thiruvaimozhi-10-7-1-senjorkavigal/) “*senjoṟkavigāḷ*” (Oh all of you who can sing poems with honest words!)
- *āḷvadu sūḻ pon visumbē* – They will rule over the perfectly radiant paramapadam! When those who practiced this decad reach paramapadam, those who remain there will say as in tiruvāimoḻi 10.9.6 “*āṇmingaḷ vānagam*” (Rule over these higher worlds).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 10.9 Sul visumbani

## 10.9.1. Sul visumbani

*sūḻ visumbaṇi mugil tūriyam muḻakkina āḻ kadal alai tirai kaiyeduttādina ēḻ poḻilum vaḷamēndiya ennappan vāḻ pugaḻ nāraṇan tamaraik kaṇḍugandē*

**Пословный перевод:**

en appan – being my distinguished relative; vāḻ pugaḻ – having great qualities which bring joy; nāraṇan tamarai – the devotees who are distinguished relatives of nārāyaṇa; kaṇḍu ugandu – becoming pleased on seeing; sūḻ visumbu – in ākāsa (sky) which surrounds all areas; aṇi mugil – the clouds which are gathered; tūriyam muḻakkina – made tumultuous sound of a musical instrument; āḻ kadal – the bottomless oceans; alai tirai – the rising tides; kai eduttu ādina – danced having as hands; ēḻ poḻilum – seven islands (of earth); vaḷam – wonderful objects in the form of gifts; ēndiya – presented

**Перевод:**

**Becoming pleased seeing the devotees who are distinguished relatives of nārāyaṇa who is my distinguished relative and has great qualities which bring joy, the clouds which are gathered in the sky which surrounds all areas, made tumultuous sound of a musical instrument; the bottomless oceans danced having the rising tides as hands; the seven islands presented wonderful objects in the form of gifts.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the first pāsuram, āḻvār mercifully explains the joy in the immovable and movable entities due to the great love on seeing the śrīvaiṣṇavas who are starting to ascend to tirunādu (paramapadam).*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. sūḻ visumbaṇi mugil tūriyam muḻakkina āḻ kadal alai tirai kaiyeduttādina ēḻ poḻilum vaḷamēndiya ennappan vāḻ pugaḻ nāraṇan tamaraik kaṇḍugandē*

- *sūḻ visumbu* – The sky which is spacious to surround the earth.
- *aṇi mugil* – The cloud which is an ornament \[for the sky\]; or the cloud which is present all over the vast sky.
- *tūriyam muḻakkina* – Made tumultuous sound of a musical instrument.
- *sūḻ visumbu …* – This resembled how the decorated gandarvas (celestial beings) would beat the drums in huge maṇḍapams (halls); as said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 5.3 “*mandam jagarjur jaladā:*” (the clouds gathered and made tumultuous sound), if this joy is due to emperumān’s arrival to carry him \[ātmā\], how joyful will the clouds be when the ātmā leaves? Alternatively, this can also imply the joy of the dēvatās such as indra, varuṇa, parjyanya et al who are the abhimānis (controller) of such cloud, ocean etc.
- *āḻ kadal …* – The deep ocean which can contain everything in it, gave up its fear and raised the tides as its hands and danced joyfully.
- *ēḻ poḻilum vaḷam ēndiya* – The seven islands became new; can also be explained as presenting gifts.

When asked “On seeing whom, are all of these happening?” āḻvār says,

- *en appan* – One who is ultimately related to me. When he is naturally connected to these śrīvaiṣṇavas, everything which is related to him should be enthused about them; just as all the citizens of the kingdom need to be enthused about a journey of the prince of the kingdom.
- *vāḻ pugaḻ nāraṇan* – sarvēśvaran who has the auspicious qualities which will uplift his devotees.

When asked “Is this joy on seeing him?” āḻvār says,

- *avan tamaraik kaṇḍu* – Seeing his devotees.

When asked “Are they being joyful in fear of bhagavān’s questioning if they did not do so?” āḻvār says,

- *ugandē* – Out of love.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 10.9.2. Naranan tamarai

*nāraṇan tamaraik kaṇḍugandu nalnīrmugil pūraṇa poṟkudam pūrittadu uyar viṇṇil nīraṇi kadalgaḷ ninṟārttana neduvarait tōraṇam niraittu engum toḻudanar ulagē*

**Пословный перевод:**

nāraṇan tamaraik kaṇḍu – seeing the devotees of nārāyaṇa who is natural lord \[of me/all\]; ugandu – being pleased; nal nīr mugil – clouds which are filled with pure water; uyar – high (as in pots with spout); viṇṇil – in sky; puṟaṇam – perfect; pon kudam – golden pots; pūrittadu – filled; nīr aṇi – having water; kadalgaḷ – oceans; ninṟu – standing (in a stable manner); ārttana – made tumultuous sound; nedu varai – tall mountains; tōraṇam niraittu – filling with welcome arches; ulagu – residents of the world; engum – everywhere; toḻudanar – vorśipped

**Перевод:**

**Being pleased on seeing the devotees of nārāyaṇa who is natural lord, clouds which are filled with pure water, filled the sky as perfect golden pots in the high sky; oceans having water, stood firm and made tumultuous sound; the tall mountains filled the world as welcome arches, the residents of the world vorśipped everywhere. With these first two pāsurams, the welcome given by earth up to the sky is shown by āḻvār. ulagam indicates the leaders of the world.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the second pāsuram, āḻvār mercifully explains the welcome given by the higher worlds.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. nāraṇan tamaraik kaṇḍugandu nalnīrmugil pūraṇa poṟkudam pūrittadu uyar viṇṇil nīraṇi kadalgaḷ ninṟārttana neduvarait tōraṇam niraittu engum toḻudanar ulagē*

- *nāraṇan …* – Seeing those who have the natural lord, the clouds which have pure water, being pleased, became the pūrṇa kumbam (golden pots which are given while welcoming revered personalities) on the high sky. Implies – first the clouds became joyful and then they became the pūrṇa kumbams. They did not remain content thinking “We raised tumultuous sound of a musical instrument once”. Alternatively, it is explained as the dēvatās who wander on the sky placing pūrṇa kumbams all over the sky.
- *nīr …* – Oceans which are having water, instead of remaining content thinking “We danced once”, danced joyfully continuously.
- *nedu varai …* – The residents of such worlds, planted welcome arches which resembled huge mountains and vorśipped too. As said in “*ulagam enbadu uyarndōr*” (world indicates the great personalities who live there), here the residents of such worlds are implied. As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 16.32 “*catra cāmara pāṇistu*” (lakśmaṇa protected śrī rāma by holding umbrella and fan in his hands and remained with him on the chariot), due to the bliss, they performed all services \[to the śrīvaiṣṇavas who are ascending to paramapadam\].

## 10.9.3. Toludanar ulagargal

*toḻudanar ulagargaḷ dūba nal malar maḻai poḻivanar būmi anṟaḷandavan tamar munnē eḻumin enṟu iru marungisaittanar munivargaḷ vaḻiyidu vaigundaṟku enṟu vandedirē*

**Пословный перевод:**

anṟu – when mahābali claimed as “mine”; būmi aḷandavan – one who measured the earth to remain exclusively for him, his; tamar – devotees’; munnē – in the presence; dūbam – starting with incense; nal malar maḻai – rain of good flowers; poḻivanar – showering; ulagargaḷ – the residents of those \[higher\] worlds; toḻudanar – performed anjali (joined palms in reverence) matching their servitude; munivargaḷ – those munivars who restrain their speech; vaigundarkku – to those who are ascending to śrīvaikuṇṭam; vaḻi idu enṟu – saying “this is the path”; edirē vandu – coming towards them; eḻumin enṟu – saying “could you mercifully come?”; iru marungu – standing on both sides; isaittanar – eagerly said

**Перевод:**

**The munivars who restrain their speech and are residents of those higher worlds, in the presence of the devotees of the one who measured the earth to remain exclusively for him when mahābali claimed it as “mine”, offered incense etc, showered rain of good flowers and performed anjali (joined palms in reverence) matching their servitude; coming towards those who are ascending to śrīvaikuṇṭam, saying “this is the path to śrīvaikuṇṭam”, they eagerly said “could you mercifully come?” standing on both sides of the path.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the third pāsuram, āḻvār mercifully explains how the residents of ādivāhika worlds (the abode of those who guide ātmās in the path to paramapadam) come forward to welcome the śrīvaiṣṇavas who are ascending to tirunādu (paramapadam) and praise them by showering flowers on them.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. toḻudanar ulagargaḷ dūba nal malar maḻai poḻivanar būmi anṟaḷandavan tamar munnē eḻumin enṟu iru marungisaittanar munivargaḷ vaḻiyidu vaigundaṟku enṟu vandedirē*

- *toḻudanar ulagargaḷ* – The residents of ādivāhika lōkams (worlds of those who guide the ātmā in the path leading to paramapadam), performed anjali considering “the purpose of having hands is fulfilled now”. They vorśipped with the help of incense and rain of good flowers.
- *būmi anṟu aḷandavan tamar munnē* – They are showing great respect considering these śrīvaiṣṇavas have become the devotees of śrī vāmana being won over by his act of mercifully measuring the world. There are those who say as in periya tirumoḻi 9.4.2 “*mūvadi maṇ koṇḍaḷanda mannan saridaikkē mālāgip pon payandēn*” (I became pale being infatuated by the incident of the king (emperumān) who measured and accepted the three worlds). They (ādivāhikas) show great respect due to the fact that these śrīvaiṣṇavas (who are ascending to paramapadam) fructified emperumān’s thought of mercifully measuring the world.
- *eḻumin enṟu iru marungu isaittanar* – They stood on both sides of the path and said “Kindly come here”. munivar \[derived from mounam\] indicates restraining of speech; they considered that their silence should be maintained elsewhere only \[and not here\].
- *vaḻi idu vaigundarkku enṟu vandu edirē* – They came forward \[from the opposite direction\] and said “this is the path for those who are going to paramapadam”. As said in [śrī bhagavat gītā 8.26](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/8-26/) “*jagata: śāśvatē*” (permanently ordained (in śruti/vēdam) for jñānis and pious persons), this path which is traversed by those who are intending to go to paramapadam, is not created today \[by them saying “this is the path”\]. They showed reverence by crossing their own boundaries and coming forward thinking “we should engage in a few kainkaryams for the bhāgavatas and sustain ourselves”.
- *vaigundarkku* – Just as a king who returns to his own kingdom after being away in other places, \[the *munivars* are identified as residents of śrīvaikuṇṭam saying vaigundarkku\] it appeared \[seeing their glory\] as if they left śrīvaikuṇṭam and are just returning there. \[The pāsuram should be arranged in the following sequence to acquire simple meaning\] “*būmi anṟaḷandavan tamar munnē – dūba nal malar maḻai poḻivanarāyk koṇḍu – munivarāna – ulagargaḷ – toḻudanar; vaigundarkku – vaḻi idu – enṟu – edirē – vandu – eḻuimin enṟu irumarungu isaittanar*“.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 10.9.4. Edir edir

*edir edir imaiyavar iruppidam vaguttanar kadiravar avar avar kainnirai kāttinar adir kural murasangaḷ alai kadal muḻakkotta madu viri tuḻāy mudi mādavan tamarkkē*

**Пословный перевод:**

madu viri – dripping honey; tuḻāy mudi – having tiruttuḻāy (tuḷasi) on the divine crown; mādavan tamarkku – for the servitors of śriya:pati (lord of śrī mahālakśmi); imaiyavar – (dēvatās) those who don’t blink their eyes; edir edir – in the path of śrīvaiṣṇavas going to paramapadam; iruppidam – palaces which are resting places; vaguttanar – made; kadiravar – the twelve ādityas; avaravar – in their respective ability; kai nirai kāttinar – gave their rays which are their hands as the decorative rows; murasangaḷ – the drums which they beat; adir kural – the tumultuous sound; alai kadal – in ocean with tides; muḻakkottana – matched loud noise

**Перевод:**

**dēvatās who don’t blink their eyes made palaces which are resting places for the servitors of śriya:pati, who is having tuḷasi, which is dripping honey, on the divine crown; the twelve ādityas in their respective ability, gave their rays which are their hands as the decorative rows; the tumultuous sound of the drums which they beat, matched the loud noise of the ocean with tides.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fourth pāsuram, āḻvār explains how the dēvatās of higher worlds arrange gardens everywhere for the śrīvaiṣṇavas to rest and how they make joyful sounds with the help of musical instruments etc in praise of śrīvaiṣṇavas.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. edir edir imaiyavar iruppidam vaguttanar kadiravar avar avar kainnirai kāttinar adir kural murasangaḷ alai kadal muḻakkotta madu viri tuḻāy mudi mādavan tamarkkē*

- *edir edir …* – Everywhere, with the expectation “Will they stay here? Will they stay here?” , dēvatās constructed rest houses. They are not referred to as imaiyavar (those who don’t blink) for their nature, but for their awakened state due to the urge in constructing the rest houses; just as iḷaiya perumāḷ (lakśmaṇa) remained awake \[in forest\] to serve perumāḷ (śrī rāma). They are constructing the rest houses fully knowing that these śrīvaiṣṇavas  will not rest there, but are constructing to engage in kincitkāram (a little service) for sustaining their own true nature; just as those who will construct welcome arches during festive season for the kings to notice the same and utter a word of praise “well done”.
- *kadir …* – ādityas showed their hands \[rays\] as decorative rows of lights saying “Please come in this way, please come in this way, please see, please see”.This kadiravar can also mean the groups of ādivāhikas who lead in the arcirādi mārgam. kadiravar – luminuous persons.
- *adir …* – Thinking that they may rest in the palaces constructed by the dēvatās, the residents of the \[even\] higher worlds, to stop the śrīvaiṣṇavas from hearing the welcoming words of the dēvatās, played the drums which give out tumultuous sound, resembling the sound of the ocean with tides; alternatively – they played loud music with the musical instruments with the expectation of making the śrīvaiṣṇavas stay there.
- *madu viri …* – As the musical instruments are played and the residents of various worlds along the path utter welcoming words, and as the śrīvaiṣṇavas are travelling in the path, emperumān along with pirātti, decorates himself again and again, to present himself along with pirātti to them.
- *mādavan tamarkkē* – emperumān is decorating himself thinking “Those who surrendered unto me with the puruśakāram (recommendation) of pirātti, are coming to serve me in the presence of pirātti”. Implies that these śrīvaiṣṇavas became fully devoted being captivated by the beautiful decoration of śriya:pati.
- *edir edir …* – How amazing that these śrīvaiṣṇavas were disrespected and not given rewards just because they were vaiṣṇavas in this world, are now being welcomed by the dēvatās and are offered wonderful abodes! miḷagāḻvān once went to the capital city of a kingdom hearing that the king is giving rewards to scholars. The king saw him and said “You are āntarāḷigan (one who is in between samsāri who is bound in this world and muktātmā who is liberated; i.e., he is being identified as mumukśu, liberation seeker); you will not be given any rewards”. miḷagāḻvān asked “Are you saying this due to any doubt in my knowledge, scholarship etc?” The king replied “There is no shortcoming in your qualities, but this is the only reason”. Hearing that miḷagāḻvān said “Though I don’t have the qualities of a proper vaiṣṇava, I am glad that they abandoned me citing me to be a vaiṣṇava” and threw his upper cloth on the sky in jubiliation and started dancing.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 10.9.5. Madavan tamar

*mādavan tamar enṟu vāsalil vānavar pōdumin emadidam puguduga enṟalum gīdangaḷ pādinar kinnarar kerudargaḷ vēda nal vāyavar vēḷviyuḷ maduttē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vānavar – ādivāhika dēvatās (those who guide the ātmā in their path to paramapadam) such as varuṇa, indra, prajāpati et al; vāsalil – standing at the entrances of their respective abode; mādavan tamar – servitors of śriya:pati (lord of śrī mahālakśmi); enṟu – showing reverence; pōdumin – “kindly come in this way”; emadu idam puguduga – please enter the places which are under our regime; enṟalum – as they say these words and honour them with gifts; vēda nal vāyavar – those who are having distinguished mouth/speech due to their recital of vēdam; vēḷvi – (their) karmas such as yāgam (fire sacrifice) etc; uḷ – with reverence thinking “our recitals have become purposeful”; maduttu – offered (at the lotus feet of the śrīvaiṣṇavas); kinnarar – kinnaras (celestial beings); gerudargaḷ – garudas (celestial beings); gīdangaḷ pādinar – sang songs

**Перевод:**

**ādivāhika dēvatās such as varuṇa, indra, prajāpati et al, standing at the entrance of their respective abode, showed reverence to servitors of śriya:pati and said “kindly come in this way, please enter the places which are under our regime”; as they say these words and honour them with gifts, those who are having distinguished mouth/speech due to their recital of vēdam, offered their karmas such as yāgam etc at the lotus feet of such  śrīvaiṣṇavas with reverence thinking “our recitals have become purposeful”; kinnaras and garudas sang songs.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fifth pāsuram, āḻvār mercifully explains the honours given to śrīvaiṣṇavas by varuṇa, indra et al who all perform the duty of ādivāhika (the one who guides the ātmā in the path leading to paramapadam).*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. mādavan tamar enṟu vāsalil vānavar pōdumin emadidam puguduga enṟalum gīdangaḷ pādinar kinnarar kerudargaḷ vēda nal vāyavar vēḷviyuḷ maduttē*

- *mādavan tamar enṟu* – They praise these śrīvaiṣṇavas as the ones who are confidential servitors of pirātti due to having surrendered to emperumān through pirātti’s puruśakāram (recommendation); they have not surrendered to emperumān who is brahmacāri (celibate, bachelor).
- *vāsalil vānavar* – The dēvatās who are present en route.
- *vāsal* – Path. They are varuṇa, indra and prajāpati.
- *pōdumin emadu idam puguduga enṟalum* – As they request saying “You should come this way; you should accept our kingdoms”.
- *gīdangaḷ pādinar kinnarar gerudargaḷ* – kinnaras and garudas sang songs. Those who reside in kinnara dēśam and garuda dēśam sang.
- *vēda nal vāyavar* – The vaidikas (those who practice vēdam) of the higher worlds, who worship bhagavān through yāgams etc, offered their worship at their divine feet. For the śrīvaiṣṇavas who are travelling towards paramapadam and have no other expectation, out of reference, dēvatās, kinnara and garudas, and vaidikas would offer their abodes, songs, the results of the yāgam respectively. As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam bāla kāṇḍam 4.20 “*prīta: kaścinmunistābhyām samsiddita: kalaśam dadau*” (A sage became pleased and gave them a pot; another renowned sage gave them tree barks), whatever is owned by one will naturally be offered to revered personalities.

## 10.9.6. Velviyul maduttalum

*vēḷviyuḷ maduttalum virai kamaḻ naṟum pugai kāḷangaḷ valampuri kalandengum isaittanar āṇmingaḷ vānagam āḻiyān tamar enṟu vāḷ oṇ kaṇ madandaiyar vāḻttinar magiḻndē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vēḷvi uḷ maduttalum – As the vaidikas offered all darmas; virai kamaḻ – emitting fragrance; naṟum – fragrant; pugai – incense; engum kalandu – spreading everywhere; kāḷangaḷ – wind instruments; valam puri – conces with curl towards the right side; isaittanar – blew; vāḷ – radiant; oṇ – beautiful; kaṇ – having eyes; madandaiyar – celestial women; āḻiyān – for sarvēśvaran who has tiruvāḻi (divine chakra); tamar – you who are servitors; vānagam – these abodes such as svarga (heaven) etc; āṇmingaḷ – should rule over; enṟu magiḻndu – being joyful in this manner; vāḻttinar – blessed

**Перевод:**

**As the vaidikas offered all dharma, fragrant incense emitting nice fragrance spread everywhere and wind instruments and conces with curl towards the right side were blown; celestial women having beautiful, radiant eyes blessed them,  being joyful, saying “You who are servitors of sarvēśvaran who has tiruvāḻi, should rule over these abodes such as svarga etc”.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the sixth pāsuram, āḻvār says “dēvastrīs (celestial women) joyfully welcomed śrīvaiṣṇavas and uttered blessings”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. vēḷviyuḷ maduttalum virai kamaḻ naṟum pugai kāḷangaḷ valampuri kalandengum isaittanar āṇmingaḷ vānagam āḻiyān tamar enṟu vāḷ oṇ kaṇ madandaiyar vāḻttinar magiḻndē*

- *vēḷviyuḷ maduttalum* – As the vaidikas offered the results of their yāgams, others engaged in burning fragrant incenses made of eagle-wood trees etc.
- *virai kamaḻ naṟum pugai* – Very desirable incense due to being very fragrant.
- *kāḷangaḷ …* – As these śrīvaiṣṇavas were accepting what was offered by the vaidikas and others, some others \[celestial persons\] started playing wind instruments and right-curled conces.
- *kalandu engum isaittanar* – They reverberated everywhere (While there is sound, there must be those who are making the sound).
- *āḻiyān tamar* *– āṇmingaḷ vānagam* – They are praising the śrīvaiṣṇavas saying “You who are servitors of sarvēśvaran, should rule over this place”. Even emperumān has his wealth for his devotees as said in jitantē stōtram “*bhaktānām*” (everything is for your devotees). They would ask “What stops you from ruling us?”
- *vāḷ oṇ kaṇ …* –  The consorts of those dēvatās who perform the duty of ādivāhika (guiding in the path leading to paramapadam), blessed the śrīvaiṣṇavas. Just as mothers would give their cool glance towards their children who are going away to far away lands,  these dēvastrīs glanced at the śrīvaiṣṇavas with their radiant, beautiful eyes.
- *magiḻndē* – They are not doing it as something ordained, just because their husbands are honouring them. They are doing it with affection. His (śrīvaiṣṇava’s) great fortune is in being honoured by those who are greater (due to being in higher worlds), after shedding the body, while the same śrīvaiṣṇava was insulted by much lower persons due to his relationship with bhagavān during his times in material realm!

## 10.9.7. Madandaiyar valttalum

*madandaiyar vāḻttalum marudarum vasukkaḷum todarndu engum tōttiram sollinar todu kadal kidanda engēsavan kiḷaroḷi maṇi mudi kudandai engōvalan kudi adiyārkkē*

**Пословный перевод:**

todu kadal kidanda – mercifully resting in the deep ocean; em kēsavan – being kēśava who is the creator of everyone such as people like me, dēvas starting with brahmā, and nityasūris; kiḷar oḷi – rising and radiant; maṇi mudi – having the divine crown which has abundance of precious gems; kudandaiyan – one who is mercifully resting in tirukkudandai; kōvalan – for kriṣṇa; kudi adiyārkku – on the servitors who are serving for generations; madandaiyar – (respective) consort; vāḻttalum – as they praised; marudarum – maruts; vasukkaḷum – aśta vasus (eight vasus); engum todarndu – following everywhere; tōttiram sollinar – uttered praises

**Перевод:**

**emperumān, mercifully resting in the deep ocean, being kēśava who is the creator of everyone such as people like me, dēvas starting with brahmā, and nityasūris, having rising and radiant divine crown which has abundance of precious gems, is mercifully resting in tirukkudandai as kriṣṇa; the consorts of maruts and aśta vasus praised the servitors who are serving such emperumān for generations; as they praised, the maruts and vasus followed the śrīvaiṣṇavas everywhere and uttered praises. todudal – tōṇḍudal (digging) – indicates the depth.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the seventh pāsuram, āḻvār says “Groups of marutas and vasus even crossed their boundaries, went as far as they could and praised the śrīvaiṣṇavas”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. madandaiyar vāḻttalum marudarum vasukkaḷum todarndu engum tōttiram sollinar todu kadal kidanda engēsavan kiḷaroḷi maṇi mudi kudandai engōvalan kudi adiyārkkē*

- *madandaiyar vāḻttalum …* – As the consorts of the dēvatās praised the śrīvaiṣṇavas, the groups of maruts and vasus.
- *todarndu engum* – Going wherever they could, beyond their own boundaries.
- *tōttiram sollinar* – Praised. As they can travel from one world to another within a moment, and as they were not satisfied with praising them \[śrīvaiṣṇavas\] within their boundaries, they followed them and praised them. Why are the śrīvaiṣṇavas travelling swiftly? This is due to their remaining as said in tiruviruttam 47 “*kaṇṇan viṇṇūr toḻavē sariginṟana sangam*” (My bangles are slipping due to having the desire to worship paramapadam which is the abode of kriṣṇa), [tiruvāimoḻi 5.9.6](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/09/thiruvaimozhi-5-9-6-kanbadhu/) “*kāṇbadenjñānṟukolō*” (When will the day of seeing him (arrive)?), [tiruvāimoḻi 9.3.7](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/07/thiruvaimozhi-9-3-7-agam-ser/) “*māga vaigundam kāṇbadaṟken manam ēgameṇṇum*” (my heart without any difference between night and day desired in a singular manner to see śrīvaikuṇṭam which is the residence of such emperumān) and [tiruvāimoḻi 2.3.10](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/02/thiruvaimozhi-2-3-10-kalippum-kavarvum/) “*udan kūduvadu enjñānṟukolō*” (When will I become part of the assemblies of nityasūris?), and since they understand the thought of emperumān who said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 66.10 “*na jīvēyam kśaṇamapi vinātām asitēkśaṇām*” (śrī rāma says – I will not survive even for a moment without seeing sītā who has dark eyes).
- *todu kadal kidanda* – emperumān who has paramapadam as his royal assembly, leaving that, arrived and mercifully rested in tiruppāṟkadal (milky ocean) to show his presence to brahmā et al.
- *todu kadal* – The ocean which was dug; deep ocean.
- *em kēsavan …* – emperumān who incarnated as kriṣṇa for the sake of his devotees and protected them.

To ensure that those who are subsequent to his incarnation, do not miss out, one who is mercifully resting in tirukkudandai,

- *em kōvalan* – kriṣṇa himself has come and is mercifully resting in tirukkudandai. maruts and vasus praise the śrīvaiṣṇavas saying that they are the results of emperumān’s efforts.
- *kiḷar oḷi maṇi mudi* – The divine crown which is very radiant and which reveals his supremacy over all. The dēvatās are showing reverence towards the śrīvaiṣṇavas considering that they have fully submitted themselves along with their descendants, having been won over by emperumān’s simplicity in mercifully resting in tirukkudandai.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.
