## 10.9.8. Kudi adiyar

*kudiyadiyār ivar gōvindan tanakkenṟu mudiyudai vānavar muṟai muṟai edirkoḷḷak kodiyaṇi nedu madiḷ gōpuram kuṟuginar vadivudai mādavan vaigundam pugavē*

**Пословный перевод:**

gōvindan tanakku – For kriṣṇa who incarnated for the sake of his devotees; kudi adiyār – devotees who belong to the clan which excusively exists; enṟu – saying; mudi udai – having similar form with crown etc as īśvara; vānavar – nityasūris; muṟai – as per their respective position; edir koḷḷa – come forward and welcome; vadivu udai – having a decorated form; mādavan – sarvēśvaran’s (who is present with lakshmi as said in “śriyāsārdam“); vaigundam – in śrīvaikuṇṭam; puga – to let them enter; kodi aṇi – being decorated with flags (as a mark of welcoming them, as decoration); nedu madiḷ – having tall fort; gōpuram kuṟuginar – arrived at the main entrance

**Перевод:**

**nityasūris having similar form, with crown etc, to īśvara, came forward and welcomed the  devotees considering them to belong to the clan which exists exclusively for kriṣṇa who incarnated for the sake of his devotees. They arrived at the main entrance of śrīvaikuṇṭam which is being decorated with flags and having tall fort, and which belongs to sarvēśvaran who is having a decorated form, to let the śrīvaiṣṇavas enter in there.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the eighth pāsuram, āḻvār explains how the nityasūris come forward and welcome the śrīvaiṣṇavas beyond the material realm and outside the boundary of paramapadam.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. kudiyadiyār ivar gōvindan tanakkenṟu mudiyudai vānavar muṟai muṟai edirkoḷḷak kodiyaṇi nedu madiḷ gōpuram kuṟuginar vadivudai mādavan vaigundam pugavē*

- *kudi adiyār …* – nityasūris revere these śrīvaiṣṇavas as they have submitted themselves along with their clan to emperumān having been captivated by his simplicity. Previously, āḻvār said “*kudandai engōvalan kudiyadiyār*” (the devotees for generations, for kriṣṇa who is in tirukkudandai); here he says “*kudiyadiyār ivar gōvindan tanakku*“. They praise them saying “They are surrendered to emperumān’s vibhavāvatārams (incarnations); they are surrendered to emperumān’s arcāvatārams (deity forms)”.
- *mudi udai vānavar* – nityasūris, who are as respectable as emperumān himself, are showing their reverence towards these śrīvaiṣṇavas. If the crowns of emperumān and nityasūris appear the same, what is the difference then? He is crowned for protecting others; nityasūris are crowned for their servitude.
- *muṟai muṟai edir koḷḷa* – Welcoming in a fitting manner. As said in puruśa sūktam “*yatra pūrvē sādyā:*” (where the elders and desirable ones are present) and in [tiruvāimoḻi 2.3.10](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/02/thiruvaimozhi-2-3-10-kalippum-kavarvum/) “*adiyār kuḻāngaḷai*” (the groups of nityasūris), they are desirable to those who desire for them.
- *kodi …* – They reached the divine tower at the entrance of the tall fort which is a boundary for the paramapadam and which is decorated with flags, looking forward to the arrival of the śrīvaiṣṇavas.
- *vadivu udai mādavan* – As said in the case of śrī vasudēva and dēvakip pirātti after kriṣṇa killed kriṣṇa as said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 5.20.52 “*yuvēva vasudēvōbhūt*” (vasudēva lost his old-age and became a youth again) and in the case of cakravarti (emperor, daśarata) who saw perumāḷ (śrī rāma) as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 12.105 “*punaryuvēva*” (daśarata regained his youth again) – śriya:pati (lord of śrī mahālakśmi) acquired a more youthful form due to the joy of their (śrīvaiṣṇavas) arrival; to enter into such emperumān’s paramapadam. As he heard about their arrival, his form and pirātti’s form acquired freshness.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 10.9.9. Vaigundam pugudalum

*vaigundam pugudalum vāsalil vānavar vaigundan tamar emar emadidam pugudenṟu vaigundattu amararum munivarum viyandanar vaigundam puguvadu maṇṇavar vidiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vaigundam pugudalum – As the śrīvaiṣṇavas entered śrīvaikuṇṭam; vāsalil vānavar – the divine gate keepers; vaigundan tamar – these śrīvaiṣṇavas, who have attained śrīvaikuṇṭanāta; emar – are desirable for us; emadu idam puga – they should enter our dominion; enṟu – considering this; viyandanar – became pleased; vaigundattu – in that abode; amararum munivarum – amarars (those who engage in kainkaryam) and munivars (those who engage in meditating on bhagavān’s qualities); maṇṇavar – those who were immersed in worldly pleasures on earth; vaigundam puguvadu – entering paramapadam; vidiyē – what a bhājñam (fortune)!; enṟu viyandanar – became pleased

**Перевод:**

**As the śrīvaiṣṇavas entered śrīvaikuṇṭam, the divine gate keepers thought “these śrīvaiṣṇavas, who have attained śrīvaikuṇṭanāta, are desirable for us”; considering “they should enter our dominion”, they became pleased; the amarars (those who engage in kainkaryam) and munivars (those who engage in meditating on bhagavān’s qualities) became pleased thinking “What a fortune for these śrīvaiṣṇavas who were immersed in worldly pleasures on earth, to enter paramapadam!”**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the ninth pāsuram, āḻvār says “After reaching the entrance of śrīvaikuṇṭam and being accepted by the elders, the nityasūris who are present there became amazed and wondered ‘How amazing that the samsāris (those who were in samsāra before) come to śrīvaikuṇṭam! What a fortune!’ “.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. vaigundam pugudalum vāsalil vānavar vaigundan tamar emar emadidam pugudenṟu vaigundattu amararum munivarum viyandanar vaigundam puguvadu maṇṇavar vidiyē*

- *vaigundam pugudalum …* – As the śrīvaiṣṇavas reached paramapadam, the divine gate keepers said “Those who are devotees of śrīvaikuṇṭanātan, are our lords; hence you should accept our abodes”. The residents of paramapadam also remain similar to āḻvār who said in [tiruvāimoḻi 3.7.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/09/thiruvaimozhi-3-7-1-payilum-sudaroli/) “*payilum tiruvudaiyār evarēlum – emmai āḷum paramar*” (Those who have the wealth of being together with bhagavān to be eternally engaged in him, even if they lack (high birth, knowledge, actions), even in that same state, they are the supreme masters having us as servitors in many births). The divine gate keepers will come forward and welcome the śrīvaiṣṇavas, hold the hands, take them to the regions which are under their control and hand over the stick, which is in their hands, to those śrīvaiṣṇavas. As the ultimate goal of those who reach paramapadam is kainkaryam and the routine of those who are already present there is also kainkaryam, they will give kainkaryam to the śrīvaiṣṇavas and the śrīvaiṣṇavs will also accept it. “puguda” – means “Come on! Enter!”
- *vaidattu amararum munivarum* – They are guṇa niśtar (munivars, who are engaged in meditating on bhagavān’s qualities) and kainkarya niśtar (amarars, who are engaged in service) just like śrī bharatāḻvān and iḷaiya perumāḷ (lakśmaṇa)respectively.
- *viyandanar* – Became amazed.
- *vaigundam puguvadu maṇṇavar vidiyē* – Became amazed thinking “Just as seavater set out to climb a mountain, samsāris got the bhājñam \[mercy of bhagavān\] of entering paramapadam!”

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 10.9.10. Vidi vagai

*vidi vagai pugundanar enṟu nal vēdiyar padiyinil pānginil pādangaḷ kaḻuvinar nidiyum naṟcuṇṇamum niṟai kuda viḷakkamum madi muga madandaiyar ēndinar vandē*

**Пословный перевод:**

vidi vagai – by the order of īśvara, in the form of our fortune; pugundanar – the śrīvaiṣṇavas arrived and entered; enṟu – being pleased; nal vēdiyar – the nityasūris who are well versed in vēdam (as said in puruśa sūktam “sādyāssandi dēvā:“) and having distinguished nature; padiyinil – in their respective abode; pānginil – in an honourable manner; pādangaḷ kaḻuvinar – cleansed the divine feet (of such śrīvaiṣṇavas); nidiyum – bhagavān’s pādukā which are said as the wealth for devotees as said in stōtra ratnam “danam madīyam”; nal suṇṇamum – distinguished tiruccūrṇam (fragrance powder, which acquired its greatness due to the contact with the divine form of bhagavān); niṟai kudam – pūrṇa kumbam (sacred pot filled with water); viḷakkam – mangaḷa dīpams (auspicious lamps); madi – shining like a full moon; mugam – having face; madandaiyar – divine damsels who have the humility revealing their subservience; vandu – coming forward; ēndinar – carried

**Перевод:**

**The śrīvaiṣṇavas arrived and entered paramapadam by the order of īśvara, in the form of our fortune; being pleased, the nityasūris who are well versed in vēdam and having distinguished nature cleansed the divine feet of such śrīvaiṣṇavas, in an honourable manner, in their respective abode; divine damsels who have the humility revealing their subservience and face shining like a full moon, came forward to welcome the śrīvaiṣṇavas, carrying bhagavān’s pādukā which are said as the wealth for devotees as said in stōtra ratnam “danam madīyam“, distinguished tiruccūrṇam, pūrṇa kumbams  and mangaḷa dīpams.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the tenth pāsuram, āḻvār mercifully explains the way the nitasūris praise the śrīvaiṣṇavas who went from samsāram to śrīvaikuṇṭam.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. vidi vagai pugundanar enṟu nal vēdiyar padiyinil pānginil pādangaḷ kaḻuvinar nidiyum naṟcuṇṇamum niṟai kuda viḷakkamum madi muga madandaiyar ēndinar vandē*

- *vidi vagai pugundanar enṟu* – Some consider that the words uttered by these nityasūris, that is “*vaigundam puguvadu maṇṇavar vidiyē!*” (What a bhājñam (fortune) for these śrīvaiṣṇavas to arrive here!) as not apt, and say “What fortune did we have for them to arrive here?” They would say “īsn’t it our fortune that these great personalities who remained as ananya prayōjanar (those who have no expectation other than kainkaryam) and enjoyed bhagavān’s qualities even while being in samsāram where worldly pleasures are abundant, and who are hailed as in tiruviruttam 79 ‘*viṇṇuḷārilum sīriyar*‘ (those who are greater than the residents of paramapadam)?” There, in the previous pāsuram, they (nityasūris) said “*vaigundam puguvadu \[maṇṇavar vidi\]*” \[Focus is on the bhājñam of śrīvaiṣṇavas to enter paramapadam\]; here, they are saying “*vidi vagai\] pugundanar*“; as “*pugundanar*” (entered) is in past tense, it is focussed on the bhājñam of the nityasūris.
- *nal vēdiyar* – Those who are revealed in vēdams as in yajur vēdam “*yatrarśya:pratamajāyē purāṇā:*” (those seers who are born in the beginning and are ancient), puruśa sūktam “*pūrvē sādyā: santi dēvā:*” (the dēvās (divine personalities) who are present everywhere and are the refuge) and rig vēdam – viṣṇu sūktam “*tadviprāsō vipanyavō jāgruvāgumsa: samindatē*” (The best, vast abode of viṣṇu, paramapadam, which is reached by nityasūris who are filled with wisdom, are always engaged in devotion and are careful).
- *padiyinil* – ananta, vainatēya et al taking the śrīvaiṣṇavas to their divine abodes.
- *pāngu …* – Without showing any discrimination thinking “he was a samsāri cētana (bound soul); we are aspruśta samsāra gandar (those who are untouched with the defects of samsāra)”, seating the śrīvaiṣṇavas on the throne, they would remain below aptly and clean their divine feet.
- *nidi …* – At that time, the divine damsels who serve bhagavān would come forward to welcome the śrīvaiṣṇavas. They will be carrying the pādukās which are the wealth for śrīvaiṣṇavas, tiruccuṇṇa prasādam (divine fragrant powder remnants), pūrṇa kumbams (divine pots filled with water) and mangaḷā dīpams (auspicious lamps).
- *madi muga madandaiyar* – The damsels whose faces are shining like a full moon due to the joy of seeing them just as the face of a mother will become on seeing her child returning from far away land.

## 10.9.11. Vandavar edir kolla

*vandavar edir koḷḷa māmaṇi maṇḍabattu andamil pērinbattu adiyarōdirundamai kondalar poḻil kurugūrc catakōpan sol sandangaḷ āyirattu ivai vallār munivarē*

**Пословный перевод:**

avar – he himself (who is with lakshmi); vandu edirkoḷḷa – as he comes forward and receives; mā maṇi maṇḍabattu – in tirumāmaṇi maṇḍapam (the divine assembly hall); andam il – endless; pēr – boundless; inbattu – having bliss; adiyarōdu – being with sūris (nityasūris, muktātmās); irundamai – in the way one is present; kondu alar – bunch of flowers blossoming; poḻil – having garden; kurugūr – controller of āḻvārtirunagari; satakōpan – nammāḻvār; sol – mercifully spoke; sandangaḷ – having different metres; āyirattu – among the thousand pāsurams; ivai – this decad; vallār – those who can practice well; munivar – will become those who meditate upon bhagavān’s auspicious qualities (in paramapadam)

**Перевод:**

**nammāḻvār, the controller of āḻvārtirunagari, mercifully spoke this decad which explains the way emperumān himself comes forward and receives the śrīvaiṣṇavas in the tirumāmaṇi maṇḍapam . The śrīvaiṣṇavas are present with the sūris who are having endless and continuous bliss, in this decad among the thousand pāsurams having different metres. Those who can practice this decad well, will become those who meditate upon bhagavān’s auspicious qualities. vandavar edirkoḷḷa could also imply the primary servitors such as viskhvasēnar et al.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the end, āḻvār says “Those who are well versed in this decad are comparable to the munivars of vaigundam (nityasūris in paramapadam who always meditate on emperumān)”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. vandavar edir koḷḷa māmaṇi maṇḍabattu andamil pērinbattu adiyarōdirundamai kondalar poḻil kurugūrc catakōpan sol sandangaḷ āyirattu ivai vallār munivarē*

- *vandu avar edirkoḷḷa* – emperumān along with pirātti, comes forward and receives the śrīvaiśnavas. It can also mean, the nityasūris who are divine by nature.
- *māmaṇi maṇḍabattu* – In the blissful tirumāmaṇi maṇḍapam.
- *andam il pēr inbattu* – paramapadam is the opposite of ananta klēśa bhājanam (samsāra – the abode of unlimited sorrows); in samsāra, what appears as joy is sorrow only, in reality. When pāṇḍu \[father of pāṇḍavas\] shot an arrow at a person (a sage who was trying to enjoy with his wife, where both were in the forms of deer), he said \[after being shot, in his final moments\] “in this samsāra, there is joy only for a fraction of a moment; you did not even let me enjoy that momentary joy”.
- *adiyarōdu irundamai* – Being with nityasūris as desired in [tiruvāimoḻi 2.3.10](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/02/thiruvaimozhi-2-3-10-kalippum-kavarvum/) “*adiyār kuḻāngaḷai udan kūduvadu enṟukolō?*” (when I will reach the divine assembly of nityasūris agreeing to their principles?)
- *kondu alar …* – Mercifully spoken by āḻvār who owns āḻvārtirunagari where it always feels likes spring season \[when the flowers are well blossomed\]. As āḻvār set out to travel to paramapadam, it appears that emperumān has made the whole route to be filled with garden, starting with āḻvārtirunagari itself.
- *sandangaḷ āyirattu* – Thousand pāsurams having different metres; alternatively, thousand forms in the form candam (vēdam).
- *ivai vallār munivarē* – Those who are capable of practicing this decad will be like the residents of paramapadam who enjoy bhagavān’s qualities, remain fully immersed in them and will not move away from them.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 10.10 Muniye nanmugane

## 10.10.1. Muniye nanmugane

*muniyē nānmuganē! mukkaṇṇappā! en pollāk kanivāyt tāmaraik kaṇ karu māṇikkamē! en kaḷvā! taniyēn āruyirē! en talai misaiyāy vandittu ini nān pōgalottēn onṟum māyam seyyēl ennaiyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

muniyē – (being unqualified to be distinguished by name and form, being in an annihilated state without any difference between cit (sentient beings) and acit (insentient entities), in that singular state of all entities as said in cāndōjña upaniśat “sadēva” and “ēkamēva“, as said in viṣṇu tatvam “īśvarāya nivēditum“, with merciful heart, set out to bestow body and senses to cētanas, to make them surrender unto him) one who meditates upon the ways of creation; nānmuganē – (after performing samaśti sruśti (initial creation up to creating the oval shaped universes) in transforming the primordial matter to mahat etc, to engage in vyaśti sruśti (variegated creation) inside the universes, as said in “sruśtim tata: kariśyāmi tvāmāviśya prajāpatē“) having four-headed brahmā as your body; mukkaṇ appā – (during annihilation, to assist in annihilation of the created universe, highlighting his power) three-eyed (with the assistance of the one who is having sense which helps in great activities) having rudra who is a benefactor, as your body; en – for me; kani – (to instill taste towards you, in me) enjoyable like a ripened fruit; vāy – lip; tāmarai – attractive like lotus flower; kaṇ – one who is having eye also; pollā – unpierced; karu māṇikkamē – having form which resembles a black gem; en – me (who stole the ātmā and claimed it as mine since time immemorial); kaḷvā – (without my knowledge, with that beauty) one who deceived and stole; taniyēn Ar uyirē – (having not attained) for me who am lonely (manifesting his qualities and turned me to a stage where I cannot sustain myself without him), one who became my complete prāṇa (life)!; en talai – for my head; misai āy – being on; vanditttu – arriving and remaining; ini – now, after (manifesting the defects of this samsāra and the goal, and creating the urge and deep interest); nān – I (who am with the love granted by you, greatly craving and understanding your urge); pōgalottēn – will not permit you to leave me as done previously; ennai – me (who will perish in separation from you); onṟum – even a little bit (as you placed me away by showing worldly pleasures when I was in bondage, and as you pacified me by showing me your qualities, after attaining taste for you); māyam seyyēl – you should not deceive me

**Перевод:**

**Oh one who meditates upon the ways of creation! Oh one who is having four-headed brahmā as your body! Oh one who is having three-eyed rudra who is a benefactor, as your body! Oh one who is having a form which resembles an unpierced black gem, whose lips are enjoyable like a ripened fruit, and eyes are attractive like lotus flower for me! Oh one who deceived and stole me! Oh one who became the complete prāṇa for me who am lonely! You have arrived and placed your divine feet on my head. Now, after all of these, I will not permit you to leave me as done previously; you should not deceive me even a little bit.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the first pāsuram, āḻvār says “As a result of your manifesting your qualities such as saundaryam (beauty) etc without any reason, I am unable to sustain without you; now you cannot remain away from me, keeping me in this samsāra, which is unbearable for me, by only letting me to enjoy your qualities by manifesting them”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. muniyē nānmuganē! mukkaṇṇappā! en pollāk kanivāyt tāmaraik kaṇ karu māṇikkamē! en kaḷvā! taniyēn āruyirē! en talai misaiyāy vandittu ini nān pōgalottēn onṟum māyam seyyēl ennaiyē*

- *muniyē* – bhagavān is the one with cit (sentient beings) and acit (insentient entities) \[as his prakāra (form/attribute)\] as said in cāndōjña upaniśat 3-14-1 “*sarvam kalvidam brahma tajjalāniti*” (all these are brahmam due to being created, sustained and ended in that brahmam), śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 1.2.67 “*sruśtau srujati cātmānam viṣṇu: bālyanca bātira: upasamhriyatē cāntē samhartāca svayam prabhu:*” (viṣṇu who is united with subtle cit and acit, transforms himself during creation to be with gross cit and acit; he protects himself; during annihilation he destroys himself being the destroyer \[reverting to subtle cit and acit\]), “*sa Eva srujyasya: sa ca sarga kartā sa Eva bātyattica pālyat ēca brahmādi avastyābhi: aśēśa mūrtti: viṣṇu: variśta: varada varēṇya:*” (he is the one who is created; he is the creator; he is the protector; he is the annihilator; he is the one who is protected; it is viṣṇu who has all forms such as brahmā, Siva et al as his body, he is superior, and is the bestover of the best boons), [śrī bhagavat gītā 15.7](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/15-7/) “*mamaivāmśō jīvalōkē*” (having my features. living in this material realm where bound souls live), śārīraka mīmāmsā 2.3.42 “*amśō nānā vyapadēśāt*” (jīvātmā is known as a feature of paramātmā); hence sruśti (creation), samhāra (annihilation) are at his disposal only; as said in śubāla upaniśat “*prutivyapsu praleeyatē, āpas tējasileeyantē, tējauvāyau leeyatē, vāyurākāśē leeyatē, ākāśam indriyēśu indriyāṇi tanmātrēśu tanmātrāṇi bhūtādau leeyantē, bhūtādir mahati leeyatē, mahān avyaktē leeyatē, avyaktam akśarē leeyatē, akśaram tamasi leeyatē, tama:parēdēva ēkībhavati*” (Earth dissolves into water, water dissolves into fire, fire dissolves into air, air dissolves into ether, ether dissolves into senses which in turn dissolve into tanmātrās (subtle form of senses) and tanmātrās dissolve into bhūtādi, bhūtādi dissolves into mahat, mahān dissolves into avyaktam and avyaktam dissolves into akśaram, akśaram dissolves into tamas (mūla prakruti – primordial matter) and tamas finally becomes one with bhagavān) – emperumān has made the divine vow as said in taittirīya upaniśat “*bahusyām*” (let me become many) and separated tamas which was attached to him, transformed it to what is known as tamas, transformed that into akśaram, created avyaktam from akśaram, created mahān from avyaktam, created ahankāram from mahān, created tanmātrās from ahankāram, culminated them into panca bhūtams (the great elements), engaged in jagat sruśti (creation of material realm) up to the creation of aṇḍam (oval shaped universe); he who is known as bhagavān, is known as parabrahma, paramātmā in vēdāntam, and is directly known as paramapuruśa.
- *muniyē* – As said in “*sa ēkākī na ramēta*” (that supreme lord was unhappy feeling loneliness) – as all the entities were without their names and forms and as brahmam’s name and form only were present, and everything else remained as acit, sarvēśvaran also remained like acit in separation from everything \[i.e. everything in subtle form and hence not being able to relish with them\].
- *muniyē* – As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 1.1 “*tatō  rāvaṇa nītāyā: sītāyā: śatrukarśaṇa:\| iyēśa padamandēśtum cāraṇācaritē pati \|\|*” (After that, hanuman, the destroyer of enemies, desired to travel in the sky where celestials like cāraṇas tread, to search for sītā, who was taken away by rāvaṇa) – as hanuman desired to search for sītā who was taken across the ocean, you meditated to create the citizens/children who have lost their forms! Should you who created me unconditionally, when I was non-existing, not help me today when I am present and suffering?
- *muniyē* – Like those who would call out “*ammē!*” (Oh mother!). That is, you created these entities when they were without body and senses; should you not help me who is desiring now \[for you\]? Will you only help when you desire for it? Should you not help when I desire for it? As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 59.45 “*śākāmrugā:* *rāvaṇa sāya kārtā:* *jagmuś śaraṇyam śaraṇam smarāmam*” (The monkeys fled the battlefield being tormented by rāvaṇa’s arrows and surrendered to śrī rāma who was their refuge) and śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 94.17 “*rākśasair vadyamānānām vānarāṇām mahacamū: \| śaraṇyam śaraṇam yātā rāmam daśaratātmajam \|\|*” (The great army of monkey warriors who were tormented by the army of demons, surrendered unto śrī rāma, the son of daśarata), āḻvār is saying “Won’t you help those who have no refuge other than you?”
- *nānmuganē* – Creating brahmā as said in śvētāśvatara upaniśat “*yō brahmāṇam vidadāti pūrvam*” (One who created brahmā first), pervading everywhere through jīvātmās, just as cētanas (sentient beings) would act and move around with the help of their respective acētana (insentient) body, being the antaryāmi for brahmā who is his body, through brahmā and his own sankalpa (vow), emperumān engaging in variegated creation in the form of dēva (celestial), tiryak (animals), manuśya (humans) and stāvara (immovable entities such as plants) is explained here. With this – it is explained that when emperumān desires, he can do anything with the help of any entity. brahmā is like the seat from which emperumān would engage in creation; for emperumān there is no difference between engaging in creation using mahat which is acētana and brahmā who is a cētana; though cētana and acētana are different from each other, both are same with respect to being subservient to bhagavān. Just as the words which indicate the different types of bodies such as dēva , tiryak, manuśya, stāvara and brāhmaṇa, kśatriya, vaiśya, śūdra, also indicate the ātmās inside those bodies, here also, as said in bruhadāraṇyaka upaniśat “*yasya ātmā śarīram, yasya prutivī śarīram*” (for the one who has souls as his body, for the one who has earth etc as his body), śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 117.26 “*jagat sarvam śarīram tē stairyam tē vasudātalam \| agni:kōpa: prasādastē sōmaś śrīvatsa lakśaṇa \|*\|” (The entire cosmos is your body. The earth constitutes your firmness. Fire is your anger. The moon constitutes your placidity. You are viṣṇu who bears the mark śrivatsa – a curl of hair on his chest), śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 1.22.86  “*yāni mūrtānyamūrtāni yānyatrānyatra vā kvacit \| santi vai vastujātāni tāni sarvāṇi tadvapu: \|\|*” (Whatever is with form or without form, the collection of all entities which are here, there and everywhere at any time, they are all body of that paramātmā) and śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 1.22.38 “… *tat sarvam vai harēstanu:*” (Whatever is created, they are all body of [hari](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/)) – as per the rule which says that the word which indicates the body would itself also indicate the soul which controls that body, the word *catumukha/nānmugan* which indicates the body of brahmā also indicates emperumān who is different from such brahmā and is the soul of brahmā; hence “*nānmuganē*” is also a calling for emperumān only.
- *mukkaṇ appā* – As said in katavalli upaniśat “*yasya brahmaca kśatranca ubhēbhavata ōdanam, mrutyur yasya upasēcanam*” (For whom, brāhmaṇa, kśatriya and all of the creation, become food \[during annihilation\], and for whom, the annihilator is like pickle \[which is used as side dish and finally eaten separately as well\]), for sarvēśvaran who annihilates everything along with the annihilator, with the name of the three-eyed \[rudra\] who is a body of sarvēśvara, emperumān who is different from rudra and who is the antarātmā (in-dwelling soul) of rudra, is invoked.
- *appā* – Favour; annihilation is a greater favour than creation. Even if creation happens after a little while, the existence of the ātmās will remain in tact. But due to the evil deeds performed by the ātmās, if annihilation does not happen immediately, the existence of ātmās will be lost. How is this so? Just as one will poke one’s own eye and cause harm, when the purpose of creation is forgotten and it becomes a reason for evil deeds, as the parents would put shackles on the hands and feet of their evil children, when the created universe becomes misused for the evil deeds, eliminating the body and senses as part of annihilation is seen as a favour; as said in jitantē stōtram “*tadā – samhāraka:*” (You are creator as well as annihilator of this universe). “*muniyē nānmuganē mukkaṇṇappā*” follows the section from mahānārāyaṇa upaniśat starting with “*ēkō ha vai nārāyaṇa āsīt – nabrahmā – nēśāna: nēmē dyāvā prutivī – nanakśatrāṇi – nāpōnāgnirnasōmōnasūrya: \|\| sa ēkākī naramēta – tasyadyānānanta sattasyaikā – kanyādaśēndriyāṇi*” (Only nārāyaṇa existed in the beginning; no brahmā; no rudra; this sky and earth were not there; no stars; no water; no fire; no moon; no sun; he felt anguished due to loneliness; for him, who is in meditation, there was a mind and ten senses) and “*atapunarēva nārāyaṇassōnyam kāmam manasādyāyīta – tasyadyānān tastasya lalādāt svēdōpatat tā imā āpa: – taddiraṇmayam aṇḍam abhavat – tatra brahmācaturmukhōjāyata \|\| ata punarēva nārāyāṇassōnyam kāmam manasā dyāyīta tasya dyānāntastasya* *lalādāt svēdōpatat – svēdōt budbudamabhavat – budbudāt tryakśaśśśulabhāpāṇi: puruśō jāyata*” (Again that nārāyaṇa meditated to vow something else; sweat oozed out of his forehead and fell on the ground; that is the water; that became the golden oval shaped universe; four-headed brahmā came into existence in that universe; again that nārāyaṇa meditated to vow something else; sweat oozed out of his forehead and fell on the ground; bubble appeared from that sweat; a three-eyed man appeared from that bubble with the spear in his hand). śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 1.2.23 “*sruśti stiti antakaraṇīm …*” (bhagavān janārdana assumes the names and forms of brahmā, viṣṇu and Siva to perform creation, sustenance and annihilation).
- *en pollāk kanivāyt tāmaraik kaṇ karumāṇikkamē* – In between creation and annihilation, if there is no protector, the evil ones will torment the individuals just as an eagle will catch its prey; for that, emperumān incarnates with his natural form as viṣṇu in between the primordial deities brahmā and rudra just as emperumān incarnated as one \[śrī rāma\] amongst the ikśvāku clan and one \[kriṣṇa\] amongst yadu clan; āḻvār is calling out that name viṣṇu here. Since creation and annihilation need to be done mercilessly, he would appoint agents for those tasks; since protection need to be done by himself, with mercy, he cannot appoint others; even if appointed, others cannot do this task as said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 1.22.21 “*na hi pālana sāmartyamrutē sarvēśvaram harim \| …*” (Oh wise person! Except for hari who is well situated in sustaining others, no one has the ability to give protection) and para samhitā “*na sampadām samāhārē vipadām vinivartanē \| samartō druśyatē kaścit tam vinā puruśōttamam \|\|*” (I have not seen any one other than puruśōttama who is capable of bestowing wealth and removing the dangers without a trace).
- *en pollā …* – While saying “*nānmuganē, mukkaṇṇappā*“, āḻvār closed his eyes and focussed on bhagavān who is the viśēśyam (substratum); here \[in the case of viṣṇu\] viśēśaṇam (form) itself is desirable, saying “*en pollāk kanivāyt tāmaraik kaṇ karumāṇikkamē*“. āḻvārs cannot move beyond bhagavān’s divine form; while the divine form is explained as *śubhāśrayam* (auspicious abode), vēdāntam instructs the ātmās to focus on the divyātma svarūpam (divine internal nature/qualities) of bhagavān leaving behind the divine form; the intent of vēdāntam is not to negate the divine form, but to push the ātmās up to the understanding of the true nature of bhagavān; *pollā* should be joined with *karumāṇikkam*. āḻvār could be warding off the evil eyes by saying “*pollā – karumāṇikkam*” (evil precious gem); alternatively, he is saying “*pollā*” to highlight the beauty of emperumān which is unseen in any other entity.
- *kani vāy* – sarvēśvaran who is said in cāndōjña upaniśat 3.14 ‘*avākyanādara:’* (does not speak, ignores \[in paramapadam\]), is giving up his firmness and smiling on seeing the favourable ones \[devotees\]; as said in śrī pauśkaram “*sva karmānala taptānām dyāyinām khēdaśāntayē*” (to remove the suffering of those who were experiencing the heat of the results of their karma).
- *tāmaraik kaṇ* – āḻvār is talking about the eyes which will further pacify us, if we start enquiring his smile and stutter with hiccups; as said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 1.20.16 “*avalōkana dānēna bhūyōmām pālaya*” (Oh lord! protect me with your glance).
- *karu māṇikkamē* – His divine body which embraces us to eliminate our fatigue in samsāram; as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 1.13 “*ēśa sarvasva bhūtastu*” (This embrace of mine is equivalent to everything else). His divine form resembles a smiling dark precious gem.
- *en kaḷvā* – Oh one who stole me without my permission! ātmā who steals the self which is īśvara’s property, without knowing about the ownership; emperumān steals the ātmā, by showing his own beautiful form. ātmā’s mamakāram (claiming bhagavān’s wealth to be owned by self) is so deep that, sarvēśvaran himself needs to steal the ātmā to reclaim the ownership. Just as emperumān \[as śrī rāma\] made janakarāja to hand over his daughter (sītāp pirātti) in marriage, he reclaims ātmā to be his own.
- *taniyēn Ar uyirē* – Not only you accepted me without my permission, you also informed your presence to me and manifested your qualities with which I sustain myself being unable to perish in separation from you.
- *taniyēn* – āḻvār’s presence amidst samsāris (worldly people) is similar to sītāp pirātti’s presence amidst rākśasis (demoniac women) in aśōka vanam, highlighting his inability to mix with samsāris and inability to reach paramapadam.
- *Ar uyirē* – For me who is suffering in this samsāram in separation from you, oh one who is the cause for my existence!
- *en talai misaiyāy vandittu* – Arriving completely as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 10.6.5](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2020/01/thiruvaimozhi-10-6-5-vanera-vazhithandha/) “*seḻum paṟavai tānēṟit tirivāna tāḷiṇai en talai mēlē*” (one who climbs and rides periya tiruvadi who has an attractive form, and arrives to be on my head) and [tiruvāimoḻi 10.6.6](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2020/01/thiruvaimozhi-10-6-6-thalaimela-thalinaigal/) “*talai mēla tāḷiṇaigaḷ*” (his divine feet on my head). Also implies that he arrived unconditionally, without any reason.
- *ini* – Not just showing yourself, revealing the nature of paramapadam. After this.
- *nān* – I who have come to know the path to paramapadam.
- *pōgalottēn* – āḻvār became qualified to stop him and force him, due to his sorrow in separation and his apt relationship with emperumān; as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 111.14 “*śēśyē purastāt śālāyā yāvan mēna prasīdati*” (I shall remain lying down at the entrance of śrī rāma’s hut until he returns to ayōdyā).
- *pōgalottēn* – You can arrive of your own freewill only; but while going, is that under your control? āḻvār is able to say like this due to a) the urge acquired by him under the supervision of sarvajña (omniscient lord) and b) since bhagavān will become shy in the delay in fulfilling āḻvār’s desire immediately as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 10.9 “*hrīrēśāhi mamātulā*” (I am feeling immensely ashamed).
- *onṟum māyam seyyēl* – Before I realised you, you showed me the aspects which are to be given up and made me remain satisfied with them; after realising you, you manifested your qualities and made me say in [tiruvāimoḻi 10.8.7](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2020/02/thiruvaimozhi-10-8-7-undu-kaliththerku/) “*umbar en kuṟai*” (What worry is there for me, who enjoyed him eternally, about the enjoyment in going further to a special abode of paramapadam?) and [tiruvāimoḻi 10.8.8](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2020/02/thiruvaimozhi-10-8-10-urren-ugandhu/) “*īdē innam vēṇḍavadu endāy*” (Oh one who is naturally related to me! This service \[by speech\] only is desired forever by me!) In this manner, by manifesting your qualities further, don’t make me think that I have attained the goal and deceive me.

When asked “Why are you asking like this?” āḻvār says,

- *ennaiyē* – As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 6.16 “*ēhi paśya śarīrāṇi*” (Look at our bodies), āḻvār shows his body which was eaten by viraham (sorrow in separation); there, for the riśis, the rākśasas ate only their limbs; here āḻvār is going through destruction of the svarūpam (true nature) itself.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

adiyen saraty ramanuja dasan

## 10.10.2. Mayam seyyel

*māyanjeyyēl ennai un tirumārvattu mālai nangai vāsanjey pūnguḻalāḷ tiruvāṇai ninnāṇai kaṇḍāy nēsanjeydu unnōdu ennai uyir vēṟinṟi onṟāgavē kūsanjeyyādu koṇḍāy ennaik kūvik koḷḷāy vandandō*

**Пословный перевод:**

ennai – me (who is in the state of perishing even in a moment of separation); māyam seyyēl – do not continue to deceive; un – for you; tiru – due to being your natural wealth, being the identity of your supreme nature over all; mārvattu – having a contrasting complexion to your divine chest (which is desired by her as said in tiruvāimoḻi 6.10.10 “agalagillēn“); mālai – like a golden garland; nangai – (due to her being complete in all qualities just as you are as said in “darpaṇa iva pracuram svadantē“, just as the shadow will appear in a mirror, these qualities) because of whose presence your qualities acquire more shine; vāsam sey – brings great fragrance (even to you who is hailed as “sarvaganda:“); pū – distinguished; kuḻalāḷ – having divine hair; tiru – (due to being an enjoyable entity, being the controller of wealth) lakshmi’s; āṇai – (honourable) order; nin – your (you who conduct the whole world by your order); āṇai – your order; kaṇḍāy – see; nēsam seydu – showing friendship (without any reason); unnōdu – with you (who are opposite of all defects); ennai – me (who is full of defects); uyir vēṟu inṟi – (as said in tiruvāimoḻi 4.3.8 “unnadu ennadāviyum ennadu unnadāviyum“) to have no difference between ātmās (jīvātmā and paramātmā); onṟu āgavē – (by the inseparable nature) to consider both to be one; kūsam seyyādu – without feeling disgusted (seeing my defects); koṇḍāy – (from the beginning) mercifully acknowledged me; ennai – me (who knows your acts in this manner); vandu – arriving (in front of me); kūvik koḷḷāy – mercifully invite me (with your divine voice saying “āḻvīr! Let us go”); andō! – Alas! I have to order for what you are craving already!

**Перевод:**

**Do not continue to deceive me; let the order of lakshmi, due to being your natural wealth, being the identity of your supreme nature over all, having a contrasting complexion to your divine chest like a golden garland, because of whose presence your qualities acquire more shine, who is having distinguished, divine hair which brings great fragrance, become your order; showing friendship, you mercifully acknowledged me without being disgusted with me, and to make it appear that both you and I have no difference between each other; arriving here, mercifully invite me. Alas! I have to order for what you are craving already!**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the second pāsuram, āḻvār vows on periya pirāttiyār to emperumān so that emperumān cannot avoid fulfilling āḻvār’s desires.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. māyanjeyyēl ennai un tirumārvattu mālai nangai vāsanjey pūnguḻalāḷ tiruvāṇai ninnāṇai kaṇḍāy nēsanjeydu unnōdu ennai uyir vēṟinṟi onṟāgavē kūsanjeyyādu koṇḍāy ennaik kūvik koḷḷāy vandandō*

- *māyam seyyēl* – What a sorrow āḻvār has to repeat the same words “*māyam seyyēl*” as in the previous pāsuram! Even after āḻvār forcefully pleaded, emperumān does not say “Alright! I won’t deceive you any further”; as emperumān did not say as in śrī bhagavat gītā 18.66 “*mā śuca:*” (do not grieve), āḻvār again pleads saying “don’t deceive me”.
- *ennai* – Just by delivering me, your leelā vibhūti (material realm) will not meet its end.
- *māyam seyyēl ennai* – Do not deceive me who believed your vow in [śrī bhagavat gītā 7.14](http://githa.koyil.org/index.php/7-14/) “*māmēva yē prapadyantē māyām ētām taranti tē*” (Only those who are surrendered to me, can cross over) and surrendered unto you saying as in tiruvāimoḻi 6.10.10 “*alarmēl mangai uṟai mārbā – un adikkīḻ amarndu pugundēnē*” (Oh one who has śrī mahālakśmi on your chest! I surrendered unto your divine feet and remained there)!

As emperumān does not say “mā śuca:”  even after āḻvār forcefully pleaded to him, āḻvār vows on periya pirāttiyār, which even he cannot refuse.

- *un tiru* – As said in śrī viṣṇu purāṇam 1.8.17 “*viṣṇōśrī:*” (Wealth of viṣṇu), for the whole world, he is the wealth and for him, she is the wealth. Alternatively, it can also be said as in “*viṣṇō:*” (viṣṇu’s belonging). \[Explanation for 1st view\] As said in periya tirumoḻi 7.7.1 “*tiruvukkum tiruvāgiya selvā*” (one who is the wealth for pirātti who is embodiment of wealth), [stōtra ratnam 45](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/02/sthothra-rathnam-45/) “*śriya:śriyam*” (one who is the wealth for pirātti who is embodiment of wealth) and Śrīvaikuṇṭha stavam 29 “*tvāmhi śriya: śriyam udāhu: udāravāca:*” (You are hailed by great devotees who have benevolent speech). \[Explanation for second view\] As per second view, being ādāra pradānam (being primary for bhagavān, the ādāram (substratum)) and ādēya pradānam (being primary among the supported aspects, like fragrance of flower) as said in vēdam “*śraddayā dēvō dēvatvamaśnutē* ” (due to pirātti, the supreme entity attains radiance) and śrī rāmāyaṇam āraṇya kāṇḍam 37.18 “*yasyasā janakātmajā – apramēyam hi tattēja:*” (One cannot measure the greatness of the one who is married to the daughter of śrī janaka); the ādēya (supported object/aspect) cannot exist without the ādāra (substratum); the nirūpyam (ādāra which is identified) cannot sustain its true nature without the nirūpaka (identity, ādēya); both cannot exist without each other; nācciyār tirumoḻi 8.4 “*tannāgat tirumangai tangiya sīr mārvaṟku*” (to emperumān in whose divine chest, śrī mahālakśmi has taken residence), śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 66.10 “*najīvēyam kśaṇamapi*” (I will not survive even for a moment if I don’t see sītā).
- *mārvattu mālai* – Not just the wealth but she is also the decorative garland for his divine chest. For the divine chest, she is the decoration and for her, the divine chest is the decoration; jitantē stōtram “*bhaktānām*” (everything is for your devotees).
- *nangai* – She is not just a decoration for his form, but his svarūpam (true nature), guṇa (qualities) and vibhūti (wealth) are also because of her. She is as good as bhagavān with respect to jñānam (knowledge).
- *nangai* – Even for the one who is hailed in nārāyaṇa sūktam “*patim viśvasya*” (lord of universe), her completeness brings in value. This is the main difference between him and others \[dēvatās like brahmā, rudra et al\]; those \[dēvatās\] who are without śrī cannot be a match for śrīmān \[bhagavān\].
- *vāsam sey pūnguḻalāḷ* – The hair which gives fragrance to the entity ‘fragrance’. The hair which adds fragrance to the one who is hailed as “*sarvaganda:*” (root of all fragrance). He got that fame of being known as “*sarvaganda:*” due to her only.
- *tiruvāṇai nin āṇai kaṇḍāy* – Since you are sarvādika (greater than all), for everyone, your order works for everyone; for you, your beloved one needs to order. Also explained as periya pirāttiyār’s order will be your order as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 112.27 “*mayā ca sītayācaiva śaptōsi raghunandana*” (śrī rāma said “Protect your mother without getting angry with her. You are taken this vow thus by me and sītā).

emperumān said “Your order is contradictory to your true nature; if you are a śēśabhūta (servitor), you should remain as per my desire”; āḻvār proves that it is not contradictory in the rest of this decad. That is, he remedies it by explaining the magnitude of his sorrow. When emperumān said “If your nature is pāratantriyam (to be totally subservient to me), you should remain as per the desire of the śēśi (lord, me)”, āḻvār’s helplessness is explained in the rest of the decad where āḻvār says “the servitor should exist for that in first place”. āḻvār asks “If pāratantriyam is the nature, are existing separately and appearing to be separate applicable?”

- *nēsam seydu* – You showed the affection towards me which was not even shown towards periya pirāttiyār. Did you do it based on my affection? \[No\] īsn’t my craving towards you, based on your initial craving towards me? \[Unlike in my case\] You showed great affection towards her due to her saying in tiruvāimoḻi 6.10.10 “*agalagillēn iṟaiyum*” (I cannot leave even for a moment).
- *unnōdu ennai* – Did you understand about you? Did you understand about me? You are as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 3.6.7](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/09/thiruvaimozhi-3-6-7-ezhumaikkum/) “*viḻumiya amarar munivar viḻungum kannaṟkani*” (One who is consumed by the best immortal personalities and sages of śrīvaikuṇṭam, who is perfectly sweet like a fruit mixed with sugar) and I am exact opposite to that; did you see “he is atomic, controlled; we are great, controller”?
- *uyir vēṟinṟi onṟāgavē* – Did you not accept me to not have any difference between yourself and myself? As said in [tiruvāimoḻi 4.3.8](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/01/thiruvaimozhi-4-3-8-ennadhavi/) “*unnadu ennadāviyum ennadu unnadāviyum*” (My ātmā’s nature is enjoyable for you and your divine ātmā’s nature is enjoyable for me), you held me in your head so that I cannot be seen separate from you. He enjoyed with me in the manner that even what is said in śrī rāmāyaṇam sundara kāṇḍam 21.15 “*bhāskarēṇa prabhāyatā*” (as sun is with the rays), cannot be compared here \[since sun and rays are still different\].
- *kūsam seyyādu koṇḍāy* – You who are sarvajña (omniscient), did not differentiate me while uniting with me. You accepted me without seeing my inferiority. At first you blessed me unblemiśed knowledge and devotion, without seeing my previous acts; in tiruvāimoḻi 1.5 “*vaḷavēḻulagu*” when I moved away from saying “I am unqualified”, you did not let me leave and accepted me by showing your sorrow in separation from me.  Had you not done it then, I would not be suffering now.
- *ennaik kūvik koḷḷāy vandu* – Now, try to come to me quickly. It is not sufficient to announce through śāstram; it is not sufficient to just manifest your qualities; it is not sufficient to have visualisation; you should ensure that I reach you and enjoy you.
- *andō* – You created this state of being unable to live without you in me, but now you are not showing your physical presence!

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 10.10.3. Kuvik kollay

*kūvik koḷḷḷāy vandandō! en pollāk karumāṇikkamē! āvikku ōr paṟṟuk kombu ninnalāl aṟiginṟilēn nān mēvit toḻum piraman sivan indiranādikkellām nāvik kamala mudaṟkiḻangē umbarandaduvē*

**Пословный перевод:**

en – being perfectly enjoyable for me; pollā – unpierced; karu māṇikkamē – having distinguished form like a precious gem; mēvit toḻum – those who are reaching and surrendering (to sustain their positions); piraman sivan indiran – brahmā, rudra and indra; ādikku ellām – and for others; mudal – origin; nāvik kamalam – for the divine lotus in the divine navel; kiḻangē – the root; umbar – for nityasūris; anda aduvē – oh one who is the controller of their nature, existence etc!; āvikku – for my ātmā; ōr – being the noble abode; paṟṟuk kombu – supporting pole; nin alāl – other than you; nān aṟiginṟilēn – I don’t know; vandu – (yourself) arriving; kūvi – inviting; koḷḷāy – mercifully accept me; andō! – Alas! I have to speak out your task! \[You should pursue me, but I am pursuing you here\]

**Перевод:**

**Being perfectly enjoyable for me, having distinguished form like an unpierced, precious gem, being the root for divine lotus in the divine navel, which is the origin for those brahmā, rudra, indra and others who are reaching and surrendering and oh one who is the controller of the nature, existence etc of nityasūris! I don’t know of any supporting pole which can be the noble abode for my ātmā other than you; arrive here, invite me and mercifully accept me. Alas! I have to speak out your task!**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the third pāsuram, āḻvār says “You who are the controller for the true nature, existence etc of the very prideful brahmā, īśāna et al, should, alas, accept me who has no other means for deliverance without you”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. kūvik koḷḷḷāy vandandō! en pollāk karumāṇikkamē! āvikku ōr paṟṟuk kombu ninnalāl aṟiginṟilēn nān mēvit toḻum piraman sivan indiranādikkellām nāvik kamala mudaṟkiḻangē umbarandaduvē*

- *kūvik koḷḷāy* – āḻvār who said “kūvik koḷḷāy” in previous pāsuram is repeating the same here, just like one who is thirsty would repeatedly say “water, water”. āḻvār has no other words to say, even though his sorrow keeps increasing. It is not sufficient if emperumān invites and accepts āḻvār; he has to come, invite and accept āḻvār. Even when my sorrow increases greatly, it is not proper for me to come and attain you; that will cause disrepute to you as well; śrī rāmāyaṇam yudda kāṇḍam 30.30 “*śaraistu sankulām krutvā lankām parabalātdana:, mām nayēdyadi kākutsta: tat tasya sadruśam bhavēt*” (it will be appropriate for śrī rāma, who is capable of annihilating enemies, to agitate lankā with his arrows and redeem me) – for the one who thinks as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 9.3.9](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/07/thiruvaimozhi-9-3-9-thozhudhu-mamalar/) “*eḻudum ennum idu migai ādalin*” (Since it is superfluous to think “we will set out to worship you”), it is not necessary to explicitly say that our going there is not desirable for him. It is apt for him only to arrive and accept us.
- *andō!* – It is sad that I have to explain that it is not apt for you!
- *en pollāk karumāṇikkamē* – If you are not you \[with such beautiful form\], we can say “we can go and see you when you invite us”. Were you to think that you will invite us and accept us in proper sequence at a later time, why did you manifest your beauty and make us fully exist for you?
- *en pollāk karumāṇikkam* – ūnpierced precious gem. Three explanations – a) precious gem which is not enjoyed so far by anyone; b) since his beauty is not comparable in this world and is totally different from the beauty of any other entity, it is known as pollā (very distinguished); c) that which will ward off evil eyes.

When asked “Even if I am so distinguished, should you not see your own svarūpam (true nature) and remain pacified?” āḻvār says “For that, first, should I not survive in your absence?”

- *āvikkōr paṟṟuk kombu ninnalāl aṟiginṟilēn nān* – A supporting pole is required. Can a creeper stand on its own without the supporting pole? Will it grow after cutting off its roots? I am not seeing any cause to uplift myself other than you; as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam ayōdyā kāṇḍam 53.31 “*na ca sītā tvayā hīnā nacāhamapi rāghava*” (Oh rāghava! I too will not sustain in separation from you just as sītā would not).

When asked “So, should you also not put in some effort for your result?” āḻvār says,

- *mēvi …* – Are the brahmā et al putting efforts for their own result! Oh one who is helping even those \[brahmā et al\] who don’t say “*āvikkōr paṟṟuk kombu*“! brahmā et al won’t say “*āvikkōr paṟṟuk kombu*“, because they do not know how to say that; nityasūris won’t say because they don’t have ego, and there is no need for them now.
- *mēvit toḻum* – On other times, they \[dēvatās\] will face off with each other; but when they are in trouble, they will gather together and worship emperumān. Oh one who is the root for the divine lotus on his divine navel which is the origin for all the dēvatās such as brahmā et al who worship without pride!
- *umbar anda aduvē* – Oh one who is the attainable goal for nityasūris who are greater than the dēvatās! “adu” indicates bhagavān being known in well established pramāṇam (śāstram). You who are the controller of nityasūris and dēvatās such as brahmā et al, should come, invite me and accept me.

By this pāsuram, āḻvār has mercifully explained that the sāmānādikaraṇyam (bhagavān being the substratum for everything) which is explained previously and subsequently, is by the cause-effect relationship; cāndōjña upaniśat 3-14-1 “*sarvam kalvidam brahma tajjalāniti*” (all these are brahmam due to being created, sustained and annihilated in that brahmam).

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 10.10.4. Umbar andan paleyo!

*umbar andaṇ pāḻēyō! adanuḷ misai nīyēyō! ambara naṟcōdi! adanuḷ piraman aran nī umbarum yādavarum padaitta munivan avan nī embaranjādikkaluṟṟu ennaip pōravittittāyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

umbar – being greater (than elements such as mahat etc , due to being the origin); am – distinguished, due to existing for your sport; taṇ – cool (due to the state where the three qualities satvam, rajas and tamas are in equal proposition); pāḻēyō – \[primordial matter, which is suitable\] to cause bhōgam (worldly enjoyment) and mōkśam (liberation); adanuḷ misai nīyēyō – (in this manner, being with cit and acit in subtle forms); ambaram – ākāśam (ether, which is the cause for oval shaped universe); nal – distinguished; sōdi – creating elements such as fire and having them as your forms; adan uḷ – in the oval shaped universe which originated from the elements; piraman aran – created brahmā, rudra et al and having them as forms; nī – you; umbarum – dēvas (celestial beings, who are greater than the creatures on earth); yādavarum – all types of sentient beings such as humans etc; padaitta munivanavan – the one who meditated upon such acts of creation and created; nī – you; em param – my body (I who am your form); sādikkal uṟṟu – after accepting the responsibility to control; ennai – me (who cannot live without you); pōra vittittāy – made me remain here

**Перевод:**

**You are great and distinguished since you control primordial matter, which is existing for your sport and which is cool. The primordial matter is suitable to cause bhōgam and mōkśam \[for cētanas for whom it is the abode\]. You subsequently create elements such as ether, distinguished fire etc and have them as your forms; you created the oval shaped universe which originated from the elements, and brahmā, rudra et al inside the universe and are having them as your forms; you meditated upon the creation of all types of sentient beings such as celestial beings, humans etc, and created them; after accepting the responsibility to control my body, you made me remain here. The sound “O” should be added to all places where “nī” is present, indicating the sorrow of āḻvār where āḻvār is feeling “there is every reason for you to protect me yet you abandoned me”.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fourth pāsuram, āḻvār says “If you, who are the controller of all, mercifully saw that I control my own situation, would it not mean that you have abandoned me?”*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. umbar andaṇ pāḻēyō! adanuḷ misai nīyēyō! ambara naṟcōdi! adanuḷ piraman aran nī umbarum yādavarum padaitta munivan avan nī embaranjādikkaluṟṟu ennaip pōravittittāyē*

This pāsuram is explained in sāmānādikaraṇam – bhagavān being one common ātmā, śarīri, prakāri (substratum) for having everything else (mūīa prakruti, ātmās, panca bhūtams etc) as his śarīra/prakāra (form), and bhagavān being the singular creator of everything else.

- *umbar am taṇ pāḻēyō* – Oh one who is the controller of mūla prakruti (primordial matter) which is superior due to being the cause for effects such as mahat, having the ability to create all the effectual elements from a fraction of itself, one which transforms in to variegated elements, one which is the abode for cētanas to engage in bhōgam and mōkśam!
- *am taṇ* – Being beautiful and cool.
- *pāḻ* – Being ready for cultivation/activity. Explaining that the primordial matter is in causal state which will facilitate bhōgam and mōkśam for cētanas, in its effectual state.
- *umbar am taṇ pāḻēyō* – It is said as “*pāḻēyō*” (primordial matter alone) \[in sāmānādikaraṇam\] instead of saying separately as in “whiteness of a cloth” \[cloth and whiteness are explicitly spoken\], since it cannot be separated from bhagavān who is having it as his prakāram. By saying “*umbar andaṇ pāḻēyō*“, it is said that there is no other controller than bhagavān even for acit which is devoid of cētana as said in śruti “*yasyātmā śarīram – yasya prutivī śarīram*” (for whom, the ātmās are bodies, for whom, the earth is a body), instead of primordial matter being the body of ātmās and ātmās being bodies of bhagavān. This word “*pāḻēyō*” decimates mīmāsakas who acknowledge śudda bhēdam (clear distinction between īśvara/brahmam, cit and acit \[without accepting śarīra-śarīri bhāvam\]) and māyāvādis who acknowledge brahmam to be the same as matter \[māyāvādi would generally consider brahmam to be the same ātmā, but not matter. Here, we have to see that even if someone tries to equate brahmam to be same as matter, that is also decimated\].
- *adanuḷ misai nīyēyō* – Oh one who is the controller of the distinguished ātmās which are bound in that matter! bhagavān’s causal state is explained since śarīrī (bhagavān, the substratum) with sūkśma cidacit (subtle sentient beings and insentient entities) is the cause. With this, it is explained that the opinion of nyāya \[naiyāyika\] and vaiśēśika who speak about the viśēśaṇa prādānyam (ātmā, which is an attribute, having independence) and apāramārtyam for viśēśaṇam (cit and acit are not real – there is only one brahmam), are not the opinions of āḻvār. By saying “*nīyēyō*” (only you), it is explained that ātmā does not exist without īśvara, just as acit does not exist without cit.
- *ambara nal sōdi* – ambaram – ākāśam (Ether). nal sōdi – distinguished fire. These are samples for the other elements; just as mentioning water in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 2.12 “*yat ambu vaiṣṇava: kāya:*” (the reason why viṣṇu’s body became water), implied other elements.
- *ahdanuḷ piraman aran nī* – āḻvār is saying – even brahmā, rudra et al who reside in the universe which is created as a result of pancīkaraṇam of bhūtams (the process of mixing the five elements to create the universe), are under your control.
- *umbarum yādavanum padaitta munivan avan nī* – You are the well-known muni (meditator) who created dēvas and all others. The sāmānādikaraṇyam explained in “*piraman aran nī*” is based on kārya kāraṇa bhāvam (relationship of cause – effect); as said in cāndōjña upaniśat 3-14-1 “*sarvam kalvidam brahma tajjalāniti*” (all these are brahmam due to being created, sustained and annihilated in that brahmam). One who meditates upon the previous karmas of all entities to create them as per their karma is the one who is muni; yajur vēdam “*tadasadēva sanmanō kurutasyāmiti*” (Only that brahma with subtle cit and acit which have no name and form, vowed “let me be with gross cit and acit which have names and forms). With this, bhagavān being the effect, due to being with gross cit and acit, is explained.
- *em param sādikkaluṟṟu ennaii pōra vittittāyē* – After assuming my burdens, neglecting that, leaving me like discarding insentient objects; you, who are controlling everything, considered that I can control my own destiny, neglected me by keeping me away from you.
- *ennai* – I who cannot survive without you.
- *pōra vittittāyē* – āḻvār is considering that he has separated from emperumān. āḻvār is saying “You pushed me into the place where your qualities cannot be observed”. Your act of granting me full knowledge but not leading me up to the destination resembles naḷa’s act of showing the path for damayanti and leaving her.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 10.10.5. Pora vittittu

*pōra vittittu ennai nī puṟam pōkkal uṟṟāl pinnai yān āraik koṇḍu ettai andō enadenbaden? yānenbaden? tīra irumbuṇḍa nīradu pōla en āruyirai ārap paruga enakku ārāvamudānāyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

tīra – to be cured (of its fever); irumbu – iron; uṇḍa – drank; nīradu – like water; en āruyirai – my ātmā’s; Ara – fully (to cure the fatigue); paruga – to drink; enakku – for me; ārā – insatiable; amudānāyē – you became nectar; nī – you (who revealed yourself to let me enjoy you knowing your greatness and to lead me to the goal); pōra vittu – discarding it (after destroying it); ittu – abandoning me (like an insentient object will be abandoned); ennai – me (who has no other refuge); puṟam – in worldly pleasures which is outside (of you); pōkkal uṟṟāl – if you think about doing it; pinnai – subsequently (after being abandoned by you who are omnipotent); yān – I (who am incapable); āraikkoṇḍu – with who else (who will lead me to the goal); ettai – which goal; andō – alas! (will attain); enadu enbadu en – I have no faculties which can be claimed as mine; yān enbadu en – there is no independent doer to be claimed as I

**Перевод:**

**Just as iron drank water to cure its heat, to eliminate the fatigue of my ātmā, you became the insatiable nectar for me to drink fully; if you think about discarding and abandoning me and making me to engage in worldly pleasures which is outside of you, subsequently which goal will I attain, and  with who else; alas! I have no faculties which can be claimed as mine and there is no independent doer to be claimed as I. Implies that there is nothing left. āḻvār becomes sad in saying the contrary words “āraikkoṇḍu ettai“. Also implies that āḻvār is saying “You revealed your enjoyability to fully drink me as said in ‘irumbuṇḍa nīrpōl en ātmāvai muṟṟap paruginān‘ “.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the fifth pāsuram, āḻvār says “If you are abandoning me considering that I can attain you with my own effort, is there anything known as I and mine? I will only perish”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. pōra vittittu ennai nī puṟam pōkkal uṟṟāl pinnai yān āraik koṇḍu ettai andō enadenbaden? yānenbaden? tīra irumbuṇḍa nīradu pōla en āruyirai ārap paruga enakku ārāvamudānāyē*

- *pōra vittu ittu* – Abandoning me and pushing me away from you.
- *ennai* – I, who have no other refuge.
- *nī* – You, who brought me up to this level starting from sruśti (creation); you who are the protector of all.
- *ennai* – I, who am the ultimate state of ignorance and inability.
- *nī* – You, who are complete in knowledge and ability. It looks like pushing someone who is not able to reach the shore, in to the river.
- *ennai nī* – There is one person who is blind and lame; there is another person who has fit eyes and legs; āḻvār is asking “who will lead whom?” As said in jitantē stōtram “*naiva kincit parōkśantē pratyakśōsi na kaścit*” (There is nothing that you are unaware of; you are not known by anyone).
- *nī* – You, who are said as in [nānmugan tiruvandādi 60](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/08/nanmugan-thiruvandhadhi-60/) “*āḷ pārttuḻi taruvāy*” (searches for devotees) and [tiruvāimoḻi 2.7.6](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/05/thiruvaimozhi-2-7-6-madhusudhanai-anri/) “*edir sūḻal pukku*” (comes across from the opposite side and catches).
- *puṟam pōkkal uṟṟāl* – If you are determined to engage me outside of you. If you abandon me considering that I can take care of my own destiny.
- *pinnai yān āraik koṇḍu ettai* – After being abandoned by you who are omnipotent, what means can I, who am unable, pursue, and to attain what goal? āḻvār is saying “*ārai*” (by whom) to indicate that the goal can be attained with the help of a sentient being and not merely with insentient activities \[such as karma, jñāna, bhakti yōgam\].
- *andō* – It is sad that I have to advice you who said in śrī bhagavat gītā 18.66 “*mām ēkam śaraṇam vraja*” (surrender unto me only)!
- *enadu enbaden yān enabden* – āḻvār is saying “I am gone”.
- *nīr …* – Just as a hot iron \[object like rod\] will absorb the water to reduce its fever \[heat\], you showed your perfectly enjoyable nature and captivated me, to fully enjoy my ātmā, .
- *en Ar uyirai ārap paruga* – I thought you united with me to eliminate my fatigue; but it seems that you showed yourself to me to eliminate your own fatigue. You showed yourself to me for your own sake. Alternative explanation – vibhakti vyatyayam (case should be changed) \[i.e. āruyirai should be changed to āruyir – dvitīyā vibhakti (accusative case) should be changed to pratamā (nominative case)\]; to have my ātmā drink you fully; in this case, it will mean “Just as hot iron will drink water to eliminate the heat, oh one who previously remained perfectly enjoyable for me and allowed me to drink you to eliminate all my heat!” \[in the first explanation, emperumān is equated to hot iron and in the alternative explanation, āḻvār is equated to hot iron\]
- *enadu enbaden yān enbaden* – When asked “If the result is yours, should you also not have a part in the means?” āḻvār says “Is there any separate faculty for me? Is there an entity named ‘I’ which can remain separate from you? Is there anyone else other than the śarīri (ātmā) who can protect the śarīra (body)? \[Here bhagavān is ātmā and āḻvār is the body\]”

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 10.10.6. Enakku aravamuday

*enakku ārāvavamudāy enadāviyai innuyirai manakkārāmai manni uṇḍittāy ini uṇḍoḻiyāy punakkāyā niṟatta puṇḍarīgak kaṇ sengani vāy unakkēṟkum kōlamalarp pāvaikkanbā! en anbēyō*

**Пословный перевод:**

punakkāyā – Like a kāyāmpū (purple coloured flower) in its own habitat; niṟattta – having complexion; puṇḍarīgam – like puṇḍarīka (lotus); kaṇ – divine eye; sem kani vāy – having reddish divine lips; unakku ēṟkum – matching your; kōlam – having divine form; malar – being perfectly enjoyable due to being born in flower; pāvaikku – for lakshmi who has internal qualities matching her femininity; anbā – being the beloved; en anbēyō – Oh you, who are the embodiment of my love!; enakku – for me; ārā amudāy – being perfectly enjoyable person; enadu āviyai – my nature/body (which is to be given up); in uyirai – my distinguished ātmā; manakku – for the heart; ārāmai – desiring so much to remain dissatisfied; manni – eternally; uṇḍittāy – enjoyed; ini – from now onvards; uṇḍoḻiyāy – you should let me enjoy further

**Перевод:**

**You are the beloved for lakshmi who has internal qualities matching her femininity, who is perfectly enjoyable due to being born in flower and is having divine form matching your form which is having the complexion of a kāyāmpū, having divine eyes which resemble lotus and reddish divine lips; oh you who are the embodiment of my love! You eternally enjoyed my nature/body and my distinguished ātmā, being perfectly enjoyable person for me and with your heart desiring so much to remain dissatisfied; from now onvards, you should let me enjoy further. It is natural for īśvara to be the natural enjoyer and cētana (ātmā, sentient being) to be the enjoyed; the ultimate state of the pleasure caused by such experience leads to cētana being the enjoyer and īśvara being the enjoyed. Hence, based on the true nature \[of ātmā\] as said in taittirīya upaniśat “ahamannam” (I am the enjoyed), by explaining ātmā being enjoyed and īśvara being the enjoyer as in “annamadantam“, ended with explaining ātmā being enjoyer \[and īśvara being the enjoyed\] due to the ultimate state of the sentient nature of the ātmā as said in “admi“.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the sixth pāsuram, āḻvār says “You, who are very determined towards me just as you are towards periya pirāttiyār, who showed great attachment even towards my body/nature, and consumed me, should mercifully accept me quickly, without neglecting me”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. enakku ārāvavamudāy enadāviyai innuyirai manakkārāmai manni uṇḍittāy ini uṇḍoḻiyāy punakkāyā niṟatta puṇḍarīgak kaṇ sengani vāy unakkēṟkum kōlamalarp pāvaikkanbā! en anbēyō*

- *enakku ārā amudāy* – You are unlike the worldly nectar, which is like saltwater enjoyed by the dēvatās. You, who are enjoyed even by all the nityasūris, granted yourself to me who is a samsāri.
- *enadu āviyai* – Having my claim of ownership as the only reason, you desired by body just as the sweat and dirt of the beloved woman will be desired by a kāmuka (man who is in love).
- *in uyirai* – In bhagavān’s opinion, ātmā is very fragrant. Alternatively, just as Tuesday is said as mangaḷavāram (auspicious day), āḻvār is sarcastically saying that the ātmā is inferior due to the connection with matter.
- *manakku ārāmai …* – For manas (mind/heart).
- *ārāmai* – Without getting satisfied.
- *manni uṇḍittāy* – You eternally enjoyed.
- *ini uṇḍoḻiyāy* – Don’t stop what you started, fully enjoy me. Did I assist you in any way for what you have done to me to bring me up to this stage? Should I pray to you to have you fulfil your own duty? It appears that āḻvār’s nectar is having the ability to be the enjoyer!
- *punak kāyā …* – Will it match your stature to like this ātmā (āḻvār) and its śarīram (body)? Will it match the stature of those \[pirātti et al\] who are dear to you?
- *punak kāyā niṟatta* – Your form resembles a well blossomed kāyāmpū in its natural habitat.
- *puṇḍarīgak kaṇ* – The eyes are showering the nectar of vātsalyam (motherly forbearance).
- *sem kani vāy* – Your smile resembles reddish fruit. These are your aspects which are dear to pirātti.
- *punak kāyā …* – It appears as if a kāyām tree is flowering as lotus and ripening into a reddish fruit. This is how his divine form, divine eyes and divine lips are.
- *unakkēṟkum* – She is so tender that she cannot even be explained through words as done in emperumān’s case. Oh you who are dear to pirātti who is having a comparable, beautiful form to you and who appears to be made of the buds of a flower! āḻvār is speaking about the beauty in saying “*unakkēṟkum kōlam*“. āḻvār is doing nyāyātidēśam (comparing a quality, that is beauty \[svarūpātidēśam – comparing the entity itself\]).
- *kōla malarp pāvaikku anbā! en anbēyō!* – Towards her, you are having love, but towards us, I cannot distinguish between love and you who are having such love; just as jñātā (knowledgeable person – ātmā) is said as jñānam (knowledge). śārīraka mīmāmsā 2.3.30 “*tat guṇa sāratvāt tatvyapadēśa:”* (for ātmā, since jñānam as a characteristic is the essence, it is referred to as jñānam itself, just as a person is called jñānavān (one with knowledge))
