## 10.10.7. Kola malarp pavaikku

*kōla malarp pāvaikku anbāgiya en anbēyō neela varai iraṇḍu piṟai kavvi nimirndadoppa kōla varāgam onṟāy nilam kōttidaik koṇḍa endāy! neelak kadal kadaindāy! unnaip peṟṟu inip pōkkuvanō*

**Пословный перевод:**

kōlam – physical beauty; malar – having enjoyability; pāvaikku – for pirātti; anbāgiya – due to the love; en – towards me as well; anbēyō – having great love; neela varai – blue mountain; iraṇḍu piṟai – two crescent moons; kavvi – holding; nimirndadu oppa – and as rising; kōlam – having distinguished physical beauty; onṟu – a unique; varāgamāy – being mahāvarāha (great boar); nilam – earth; kōttidaik koṇḍa – with the act of placing on the divine tusk; endāy – being my lord (who reveals how he will lift me up from the samsāra); neelam – bluish (due to your shadow falling on it); kadal – ocean; kadaindāy – oh one who churned and engaged in hard work to protect your devotees!; unnai – you (who are good to me and protect me through puruśakāram \[of pirātti\] in this manner); peṟṟu – having attained; ini – after fully having you in my hand; pōkkuvanō – will I let you escape?

**Перевод:**

**You are having great love towards me as well due to your love for the beautiful and enjoyable pirātti. Oh my lord who is having distinguished physical beauty in a unique, mahāvarāha form placing the earth on your tusk the act of which resembles a blue mountain holding two crescent moons and rising up! Oh one who churned the bluish ocean and engaged in hard work to protect your devotees! Having attained you and after having you fully in my hand, will I let you escape? “neelak kadal” could also mean ocean with bluish precious gems.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the seventh pāsuram, āḻvār says “You mercifully lifted me up from the ocean of samsāra and united with me since I am a servitor of periya pirātti, just as you lifted up śrī bhūmip pirātti who was drowned in the ocean of deluge and just as you churned the ocean and brought out periya pirāttiyār and united with them; will I let you escape after having attained you who showed great love towards me?”*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. kōla malarp pāvaikku anbāgiya en anbēyō neela varai iraṇḍu piṟai kavvi nimirndadoppa kōla varāgam onṟāy nilam kōttidaik koṇḍa endāy! neelak kadal kadaindāy! unnaip peṟṟu inip pōkkuvanō*

- *kōla malarp pāvaikku anbāgiya en anbēyō* – The words mercifully spoken by parāśara bhattar \[to nanjīyar\] during his final moments – Our followers should recite this pāsuram along with dvayam. Because he is friendly towards periya pirāttiyār, he is dear towards us who are her servitors. āḻvār is identifying the root cause for his love as said in “*tirumāl ennai āḷumāl*” (one who is having śriya:patitvam, is very infatuated). Am I not the confidential servitor of the private quarters?

āḻvār is asking “īsn’t there any cause for my love?”

- *neela varai …* – Just as a dark mountain is rising up with two crescent moons. The earth on the divine tusk resembles the mole in the crescent moon.
- *kōla varāgam* – emperumān’s form as explained in nācciyār tirumoḻi 11.8 “*māsudambil nīr vārā*” (muddy water dripping from his dirty body) is the cause for warding off evil eyes for āḻvār; as the beloved lady remained in dirt as said in “*pāsi tūrttuk kidanda pār magaḷ*” (śrī bhūmip pirātti, who was covered with algae), had emperumān arrived in his original form, it would have been a farewell for his love. The form which he assumed to reduce his glory, has made āḻvār ward off evil eye from him.
- *onṟāy* – āḻvār is saying, emperumān has only assumed the form of a wild boar; but he is distinguished, due to having grown to cover the three worlds.
- *nilam kōttidaik koṇḍa endāy* – Oh one who lifted me who was consumed by the ocean of samsāra just as you reached up to the wall of the universe to lift the earth which was consumed by the deluge and placed it on your tusk!
- *neelak kadal kadaindāy* – Oh one who churned the ocean to acquire pirātti!
- *neelak kadal* – It \[milky ocean, which is usually white\] has become dark due to the one who churns it; \[alternative explanation\] the change in complexion due to dropping all the herbs; \[another explanation\] by the blue colour, the blue precious gems are indicated and hence saying ratnākara (abode of gems) which has abundance of such gems.
- *unnaip peṟṟu inip pōkkuvanō* – Will I let you escape after you engaged in activities similar to attaining śrī bhūmip pirātti and periya pirātti, and attaining me? Am I going to abandon the wealth, after being involved in the result acquired by your effort?

## 10.10.8. Perrinip pokkuvano!

*peṟṟinip pōkkuvanō? unnai en tanip pēr uyirai uṟṟa iru vinaiyāy uyirāyp payanāy avaiyāy muṟṟa immūvulagum perundūṟāyt tūṟṟil pukku muṟṟak karandoḷittāy en mudal tani vittēyō!*

**Пословный перевод:**

uṟṟa – apt; iru vinai āy – being the controller of two types of karma, viz. puṇya (virtues) and pāpa (vices); uyir āy – being the controller (of ātmā who is bound by karma); avai āyp payan āya avai A – being the benefactor of the resulting joy and sorrow of such karmas; im mū ulagum – these three worlds; muṟṟa – fully; perum tūṟu āy – having the great bush \[primordial matter\] as your prakāra (body); tūṟṟil pukku – entering (out of his independence, through his vow) in this great bush (which does not let out those who enter in it due to their karma); muṟṟak karandu – to not know in any manner; oḷittāy – present in a concealed manner (in a subtle form); en – for me (to reach you); mudal tani vittēyō – Oh you who are the distinguished cause and who are the primary virtue!; unnai – you (who are incomparable and who are unlimited ātmā); peṟṟu – having attained; ini – after reaching the state of being unable to survive in your separation; pōkkuvanō – is there any means to let you go? The sound “O” indicates the sorrow of separation

**Перевод:**

**You are the controller of two types of karma, viz. puṇya and pāpa; you are the controller of ātmā; you are the benefactor of the resulting joy and sorrow of such karmas; you are having as your prakāram, this great bush of primordial matter which has all the three worlds fully; you have entered in this great bush and are present in a concealed manner to not be known by everyone in any manner; oh you who are the distinguished cause and who are the primary virtue for me! Having attained you, and after reaching the state of being unable to survive in your separation, is there any means to let you go? The sound “O” indicates the sorrow of separation.**

*No specific introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the eighth pāsuram, āḻvār says “There is no means to let you escape after attaining you who are very difficult to understand”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. peṟṟinip pōkkuvanō? unnai en tanip pēr uyirai uṟṟa iru vinaiyāy uyirāyp payanāy avaiyāy muṟṟa immūvulagum perundūṟāyt tūṟṟil pukku muṟṟak karandoḷittāy en mudal tani vittēyō!*

- *peṟṟinip pōkkuvanō unnai* – Am I going to worry about losing you like losing fake money? Will I, who am totally different from you, let you go, after attaining you, who are verily my sustainer?
- *unnai* – Do you not know about yourself?
- *en tanip pēr uyirai* – Are you just at the level of ātmā which can be accepted if realised and neglected if not?

āḻvār is explaining this “unnai” in the subsequent portion of the pāsuram. You who are the ātmā of all as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 8.1.5](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2019/01/thiruvaimozhi-8-1-5-aruyireyo/) “*ulgangatkellām ōr uyirēyō*” (Oh singular ātmā who is being the refuge for all the creatures!) By “*peṟṟinip pōkkuvanō*” – āḻvār highlights the greatness of the result being attained over all other results; by saying “*en tanip pēruyirai*“, āḻvār highlights the greatness of emperumān over self.

- *uṟṟa iru vinaiyāy* – Only if I considered karmas to be independent of you,  could I leave you. Being the controller of the karmas in the form of puṇya and pāpa which never leave the ātmā.
- *uyirāy* – Only if the performer of such karmas were beyond your control, could I leave you. Being the controller of ātmā who is the performer.
- *payanāy avaiyāy* – Only if I consider the fruits of the karma will be bestowed independent of you, could I leave you. Being the controller of the results of such karmas.
- *muṟṟa immūvulagum perum tūṟāy* – Only if I consider this samsāra which has to be given up, as independent of you,  could I leave you. It is explained as great bush, since one cannot know where one entered and from where one will leave in this samsāram.
- *tūṟāy* – creating this samsāram.
- *tūṟṟil pukku* – entering in it.
- *muṟṟak karandu* – Only if there is a place where you have not pervaded,  could I leave you.
- *oḷittāy* – You remained to be unknown by the entities you pervaded as said in bruhadāraṇyaka upaniśat “*yamātmā na vēda*” (The ātmā who is unaware of paramātmā). Will I not survive, if you become visible to my eyes?
- *en mudal tani vittēyō* – Oh you who revealed this to me while not revealing the same to others! \[What a benevolence towards me!\]
- *mudal tani vittēyō* – If I can take one step towards you on my own, I can remain patient \[You have done everything for me\]. Oh you who are my primary virtue!

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

adiyen saraty ramanuja dasan

## 10.10.9. Mudal tani vitteyo

*mudal tani vittēyō! muḻu mūvulagādikkellām mudal tani unnai unnai enai nāḷ vandu kūduvan nān mudal tani angum ingum muḻu muṟṟuṟu vāḻ pāḻāy mudal tani sūḻndaganṟāḻnduyarnda mudivileeyō!*

**Пословный перевод:**

muḻu mū ulagu ādikku ellām – for all the three worlds etc; mudal – being the primary efficient cause \[nimitta kāraṇa\]; tani vittēyō – (without expectation of any assistance) being the unique material cause \[upādāna kāraṇa\]; angum ingum – (in the universe in the effectual form) who are outside the oval shaped universe and inside; muḻu muṟṟuṟu – pervading all the entities completely; mudal tani – being the unique cause; vāḻ – the fertile field for prosperity (of attaining enjoyment and liberation); pāḻ āy – being the controller of mūla prakruti (primordial matter); mudal – (in controlling matter and all aspects of matter) being the primary; tani – incomparable (due to being different from acit (insentient objects)); sūḻndu aganṟu – pervading (through the dharma bhūta jñānam (knowledge which helps grasp external aspects)); āḻndu uyarnda – being present in all ten directions; mudivileeyō – Oh you who are the controller (of the collection of ātmās who are all eternal)!; mudal – being primary in all aspects; tani – being incomparable; unnai – you; unnai – you (who are having distinguished nature, form and qualities which are different from all, instead of seeing in that universal form); nān – I (who am greatly craving due to not attaining and enjoying you); enai nāḷ – when; vandu kūduvan – will come there and unite with you?

**Перевод:**

**Oh you who are the primary efficient cause for all the three worlds etc, who are the unique material cause, who are completely pervading all the entities which are outside the oval shaped universe and inside, who are the controller for mūla prakruti which is the unique cause and the fertile field for prosperity, who are the primary, incomparable controller who is pervading and present in all ten directions! When will I come there and unite with you who are primary in all aspects and are incomparable?**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the ninth pāsuram, emperumān asked “After having seen my state of having the whole universe as my form, what more would you like?” āḻvār says “That is not enough for me; I would like to see your presence in tirunādu (paramapadam) which is distinguished and fully complete”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*Ninth pāsuram. As said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 1.22.86 “tāni sarvāṇi tatvapu:” (everything is a śarīram (body) for that paramātmā), subāla upaniśat 7 “yasyātmā śarīram … yasya prutivī śarīram” (for whom, this ātmā is a body, this earth is a body) and śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 1.22.38 “… tat sarvam vai harēstanu:” (Whatever is created, they are all body of hari), emperumān says “I have showed you universal form so that you can see me everywhere”, āḻvār says “That is common for the favourable and unfavourable ones; only if you don’t have another \[distinguished\] form, could I remain thinking ‘this is enough’? You should manifest your distinguished form in tirunādu”. mudal tani vittēyō! muḻu mūvulagādikkellām mudal tani unnai unnai enai nāḷ vandu kūduvan nān mudal tani angum ingum muḻu muṟṟuṟu vāḻ pāḻāy mudal tani sūḻndaganṟāḻnduyarnda mudivileeyō!*

- *mudal tani vittēyō muḻu mū ulagu ādikku ellām* – Oh you who do not need the help of those who are protected by you, when you set out to protect them! Oh you who are all the three types of causes (upādāna (material), nimitta (efficient), sahakāri (instrumental)) for everything starting with the three worlds!
- *mudal* – nimitta kāraṇam.
- *tani* – sahakāri kāraṇam.
- *vittu* – upādāna kāraṇam.
- *mudal tani …* – When will I come and unite with you who are primary, incomparable and complete in qualities, wealth etc?
- *enai nāḷ vandu kūduvan* – Even for those who realised their true nature by the knowledge granted by him, they can speak like pirātti \[in desiring to unite with him\].
- *nān* – I who have understood the nature of paramapadam; I who desired for your distinguished form.
- *mudal tani angum ingum muḻu muṟṟuṟu vāḻ pāḻāy* – In mahat etc which are primary, incomparable and present everywhere.
- *muṟṟu* – everywhere.
- uṟu – pervading everywhere.
- *vāḻ pāḻāy* – the level playing field for cētanas to attain bhōgam (worldly enjoyment) and mōkśam (liberation).

\[The introduction section is repeated here and the pāsuram is explained once more from the beginning for the sake of a śrīvaiṣṇava who arrived late while nampiḷḷai was explaining the meaning of this pāsuram\]

- *mudal tani vittēyō* – *mudal* – nimitta kāraṇam, *tani* – sahakāri kāraṇam, *vittu* – upādāna kāraṇam.
- *muḻu mū ulagu ādikku ellām* – By “*mū ulagam*“, the three layered aṇḍam as in “*krutakam, akrutakam, krutakākrutakam*” is explained; by muḻu, the countless oval shaped universes as said in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam 2.7.27 “*aṇḍānānāntu sahasrāṇām sahasrāṇyayutāni ca – īdruśānānta tatra kōti kōti śatāni ca*” (In that mūla prakruti thousands of crores of oval shaped universes are present) are explained; by “*ādi*“, the āvaraṇams (covering layers) which are the causes for these aṇḍams are explained. Hence, oh you who are the cause for everything staring with the three worlds!

Note: krutaka \[The bottom seven layers of the universe – atala to pātāla and the three middle layers – bhūr lōka, bhuva lōka and svarga lōka; these are completely destroyed as part of avāntara praḷayam (intermediary deluge at the end of brahmā’s day) and subsequently recreated\], akrutaka \[The top three layers of the universe – satya lōka, tapa lōka and jana lōka; these remain in tact during avāntara praḷayam with their residents\] and krutakākrutaka \[mahar lōka; this remains in tact during avāntara praḷayam, but the residents shift to higher layers at that time\].

- *mudal …* – Being the primary, incomparable, complete in qualities and wealth, you who are having the universe as your body.

Thus, until now, bhagavān having leelā vibhūti (materialistic realm) is explained; subsequently – āḻvār says that he desires to see the divine beauty of emperumān’s divine form which is enjoyed by nityasūris.

- *unnai* – bhagavān having nitya vibhūti (spiritual realm) is explained. Will just saying “*unnai*” explain his having nitya vibhūti? Yes, it will; when emperumān and pirātti are mentioned as in [tiruvāimoḻi 4.9.10](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/04/thiruvaimozhi-4-9-10-kandu-kettu/) “*oṇḍodiyāḷ tirumagaḷum nīyumē nilā niṟpa – kaṇḍa sadir*” (While [śrīmahālakśmi](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sri-mahalakshmi/), the one who is having distinguished forearms with ornaments like bangles, and you stand alone – determined the best means), the whole of paramapadam is implied.
- *unnai* – You who are as said in tiruvāimoḻi 4.5.1 “*vīṟṟirundu ēḻulagum tanik kōl sella*” (sarvēśvaran, the lord of all, being distinct from every other entity, seated to conduct seven types of worlds with his matchless sceptre), having
   - divine crown which can be confused as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 3.1.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2016/07/thiruvaimozhi-3-1-1-mudichchodhiyay/) “*mudiccōdiyāy unadu mugaccōdi malarndaduvō*” (Did the radiance of your divine face rise upwards to become the radiance in your divine crown?)
   - divine hair as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 7.7.9](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/10/thiruvaimozhi-7-7-9-kolginra-kolirulai/) “*māyan kuḻal*” (divine hair of kriṣṇa who is having an amazing form), the beautiful divine face as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 7.7.8](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/10/thiruvaimozhi-7-7-8-kol-izhaith-thamaraiyum/) “*kōḷ iḻait tāmaraiyum kodiyum pavaḷamum villum* *kōḷ iḻait taṇ muttamum taḷirunguḷir vān piṟaiyum kōḷ iḻaiyā udaiya koḻunjōdi vattangol?*” (Is it a complete jyōtirmaṇḍalam with lotus flowers, creeper, coral, bow, cool pearl, sprouts, cool beautiful crescent having its own radiance as ornament? kriṣṇa’s radiant divine face which, in itself, is an ornament, is stealing the life out of me, who is having cruel sin)
   - divine neck which resembles the neck of youthful areca tree and conch, which are imprinted with the ornaments worn by the nācciyārs (divine consorts) in their hands
   - divine shoulders as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 6.6.6](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/02/thiruvaimozhi-6-6-6-karpagak-kavana/) “*kaṟpagak kāvana naṟpala tōḷ*” ([emperumān](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/sriman-narayanan/) who has many shoulders which resemble a garden of kaṟpaga trees)
   - divine chest which is like the palace of periya pirāttiyār, which will drive her crazy to say as in [tiruvāimoḻi 6.10.10](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2018/06/thiruvaimozhi-6-10-10-agalagillen-part-1/) “*agalagillēn*” (I cannot leave) while enjoying it eternally, which is said as in periyāḻvār tirumoḻi 1.3.10 “*kurumā maṇip pūṇ kulāvit tigaḻum tirumārbu*” (the divine chest where the kaustuba gem joyfully exists)
   - divine stomach which roams around in the hearts of nityasūris and muktātmās as said in amalanādipirān 4 “*uḷḷattuḷ ninṟu ulāginṟadē*” (staying in my heart and roaming around in there)
   - divine navel which resembles a whirl in the ocean of beauty
   - hip which cannot be explained any further as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 5.5.8](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/07/thiruvaimozhi-5-5-8-kaiyul-nanmugam/) “*algulum*” (hip)
   - slender waist
   - divine lower garment which appears to have branched out of his divine body, which resembles the sky in the dusk time as said in amalanādipirān 3 “*andi pōl niṟattādaiyum*” (the lower garment which resembles the complexion of dusk)
   - divine thighs which are profound as a plantain stem
   - divine shins which resemble the thorny stem of a lotus flower (due to having goosebumps)
   - divine feet which are having the symbols as said in [stōtra ratnam 31](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2017/01/sthothra-rathnam-31/) “*kadā punaś śankharatāngakalpaka dvajāravaindānkuśa vajralāncanam*” (Oh trivikrama! When will my head be decorated with your two divine feet which are having \[the marks of\] śankha , chakra , et al?), which are so tender to make the pirāttis hesitate to massage them, which are perfectly enjoyable as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 1-5-8](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/08/thiruvaimozhi-1-5-8-unday-ulagu/) “*tēnē malarum tiruppādam*” (the divine feet from which honey will drip)
- *enai nāḷ vandu kūduvan* – When will I come and reach you? Since he was granted unblemiśed knowledge and devotion by emperumān as said in [tiruvāimoḻi 1.1.1](https://divyaprabandham.koyil.org/index.php/2015/03/thiruvaimozhi-1-1-1-uyarvara-uyarnalam/) “*mayarvaṟa madinala aruḷinan*“, he can speak like pirātti.
- *nān* – I who desired to see that form.
- *mudal tani angum ingum muḻu muṟṟu uṟu vāḻ pāḻāy* – All of mahat etc, which are primary, incomparable and present everywhere.
- *muṟṟu* – Fully. Everywhere.
- *uṟu* – Pervading.
- *vāḻ pāḻāy* – Being the ātmā of prakruti (primordial matter) which is a level playing field to facilitate bhōga and mōkśa for cētanas (sentient beings).
- *mudal …* – Being the primary and controller for prakruti.
- *tani* – Incomparable.
- *sūḻndu* – Pervading primordial matter and the effectual entities of such matter.

While pervading,

- *aganṟu āḻndu uyarnda* – Pervading in ten directions with knowledge.
- *mudivileeyō* – Oh controller of the incomprehensible ātmās!
- *mudivilee* – mudivu – nāśam (destruction), being eternal unlike prakruti which gets destroyed (fully transformed).

I have seen you who are the cause and in-dwelling soul of all aspects of matter and ātmās; when will I see you who are enjoyed by nityasūris in paramapadam? It is not sufficient to enjoy you with your form of being the controller of cit and acit in both kāraṇa (causal) and kārya (effectual) state, as shown by you; I would like to enjoy you with your distinguiśded form in the special abode of paramapadam.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 10.10.10. Sulndu aganru

*sūḻndaganṟāḻnduyarnda mudivil perum pāḻēyō sūḻndadanil periya para nanmlarc cōdīyō sūḻndadanil periya sudar jñāna inbamēyō sūḻndadanil periya en avā aṟac cūḻndāyē*

**Пословный перевод:**

sūḻndu – surrounding (all of the effectual entities); aganṟu – vastly pervading; āḻndu uyarnda – being present in all directions, being present in lower and higher regions; mudivil – being eternal (due to not being subject to creation and annihilation); perum – being immeasurable (due to being beyond all the effectual entities); pāḻē – having the prakruti (primordial matter) which is a level playing field for bhōgam (worldly enjoyment) and mōkśam (liberation), as prakāra (attribute); sūḻndu – pervading with their jñānam; adanil – more than that; periya – being big; param – being superior (due to being in singular form); nal – having greatness such as svayam prakāśatvam (self-illuminating); malar – blossoming; sōdī – having ātmās which have rays of knowledge, as prakāra; sūḻndu – pervading this prakruti (matter) and puruśas (ātmās); adanil periya – bigger than them; sudar – radiant due to auspicious qualities; jñāna inbamē – Oh controller who is having the true nature identified by jñānam (knowledge) and ānandam (bliss)!; sūḻndu – Surrounding (these three tatvams viz acit, cit, īśvara); adanil periya – bigger than them; en avā – my deep affection; aṟa – to be satisfied; sūḻndāyē – You granted me sāyujya bhōgam of fully and joyfully remaining in you who have svarūpa (true nature), guṇa (qualities), vigraha (form), bhūśaṇa (ornaments), āyuda (weapons), mahiśī (divine consorts), parijana (servitors) and stāna (abode); O! – āḻvār becomes blissful in every line saying “Wow! How amazing!”

**Перевод:**

**Oh you who are having prakruti which is surrounding, vastly pervading, present in all directions being present in lower and higher regions, immeasurable and is a level playing field for bhōgam and mōkśam, as prakāra! Oh you who are having ātmās which are pervading with jñānam, bigger than prakruti, superior and having greatness such as svayam prakāśatvam, blossoming and are having rays of knowledge, as prakāra! Oh controller who is pervading this matter and ātmās, bigger than them, radiant due to auspicious qualities and having the true nature identified by jñānam and ānandam! You granted me sāyujya bhōgam of fully and joyfully remaining in you, who have true nature, qualities, form, ornaments, weapons, divine consorts, servitors and abode, to satisfy my deep affection which is surrounding those three tatvams and is bigger than them. In saying “O” in every line, āḻvār reveals his bliss saying “Wow! How amazing!”**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the tenth pāsuram, āḻvār vowed on periya pirāttiyār to not allow emperumān to remain satisfied without fulfilling āḻvār’s desire and cried out with great sorrow; emperumān arrived as prayed by āḻvār, being complete, and mercifully united with āḻvār; seeing that āḻvār says “you came and united with me to eliminate my craving which was greater than the immeasurable prakruti (matter), ātmās and your knowledge in the form of your sankalpam (vow); my desire has now been fulfilled”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. Also explained as – You caused so much craving in me for you but had more craving for me in you, and had your craving eliminated by uniting with me; as said in śrī rāmāyaṇam 130.89 “angē bharatam ārōpya mudita: pariśasvajē” (śrī rāma placed bharatāḻvān on the lap and embraced him) \[Only after meeting bharatāḻvān again, śrī rāma’s sorrow came to an end\]. sūḻndaganṟāḻnduyarnda mudivil perum pāḻēyō sūḻndadanil periya para nanmlarc cōdīyō sūḻndadanil periya sudar jñāna inbamēyō sūḻndadanil periya en avā aṟac cūḻndāyē*

- *sūḻndu … pāḻēyō* – Now āḻvār is speaking about prakruti and pursuśas to highlight that his affection is greater than those big entities. īśvara is also spoken about since prakruti and puruśa cannot sustain separately from īśvara. Oh you who are the ātmā for prakruti which is vastly pervading mahat etc which are its effects, present in all ten directions, eternal, immeasurable and is a level playing field for bhōgam and mōkśam for cētanas!
- *sūḻndu … sōdīyō* – Oh you who are the ātmā for ātmās who are pervading the matter, being bigger than it, being superior due to being the controller, being distinguished due to not undergoing transformation etc, being blossomed in a radiant form!
- *sūḻndu … inbamēyō* – Indicating the jñānam in the form of sankalpam (vow) – Oh you who are pervading both of them (matter and ātmās), being their controller and are having jñānam which is in the form of sankalpam and sukham (bliss)!  Alternative explanation – directly saying emperumān as one who  is in the form of radiance of bliss.
- *sūḻndu …* – You united with me to fulfil my deep affection which is bigger than the three tatvams to make them appear very small in front of my affection, by showing your even bigger affection towards me! You finally brought an end to my crying out! As said in śrī rāmāyaṇam 130.89 “*angē bharatam ārōpya mudita: pariśasvajē*” (śrī rāma placed bharatāḻvān on the lap and embraced him), just as śrī rāma returned to śrī ayōdyā, placed śrī bharatāḻvān on his lap and lovingly smelt the head and embraced him, emperumān united with āḻvār to eliminate āḻvār’s craving.

In the next article we will enjoy the next pāsuram.

## 10.10.11. Avavaraccul ariyai

*avāvaṟaccūḻ ariyai ayanai aranai alaṟṟiavāvaṟṟu vīdu peṟṟa kurugūrc catakōpan sonnaavāvil andādigaḷāl ivai āyiramum mudindaavāvil andādi ippattaṟindār piṟandār uyarndē*

**Пословный перевод:**

avā – deep affection (of devotees); aṟa – to be satisfied; sūḻ – due to engaging in endless union; ariyai – having the nature to destroy (the sorrow of separation); ayanai – being antarātmā (for hiraṇyagarbha (brahmā), as per the understanding in “kāryam jaimini:” \[identify the root cause for the result\], as expounded by pūrva pakśi (one with opposing view) and to be attained by muktātmās); aranai – being the ultimate goal and antarātmā of rudra who is the goal for followers of pāśupata school of thought; alaṟṟi – crying out (due to the urge in attaining him); avā aṟṟu vīdu peṟṟa kurugūrc catakōpan – nammāḻvār of āḻvārtriunagari whose desire was fulfilled and who got liberated; sonna avāvil andādigaḷāl ivai āyiramum – these thousand pāsurams which are mercifully spoken in antādi form; mudinda – ended (in the form of great parabhakti (stage of full visualisation)); avāvil – in the desire; andādi – antādi poems; ippattu – this decad too; aṟindār – those who meditated \[some portion missing here in the original text\]; piṟandār uyarndē – born great \[some portion missing here in the original text\]

**Перевод:**

**nammāḻvār of āḻvārtirunagari cried out with deep affection and became satisfied by the endless union of hari who is having the nature to destroy, antarātmā for brahmā and the ultimate goal and antarātmā of rudra who is the goal for followers of pāśupata school of thought; his desire was fulfilled and he got liberated; he mercifully spoke these thousand pāsurams in antādi form; those who meditated upon this decad of antādi poems, in the state of having his desire fulfilled, among those thousand pāsurams, are born great. “avāvaṟac cūḻ ari” is also explained as “one who fulfills the \[devotees’\] desire which captivates him by surrounding \[the devotee\] with his qualities, and accepts \[the devotee\]”.**

**Комментарий. Автор Tirukkurugaippiran Piḷḷān:**

*No specific introduction.*

See [vādi kēsari aḻagiya maṇavāḷa jīyar](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/vadhi-kesari-azhagiya-manavala-jiyar/)‘s translation.

**Комментарий. Автор Nañjīyar:**

*In the end – emperumān who is opposite to all defects, abode of all auspicious qualities, identified by jñānam and ānandam, having the best of qualities, wearing innumerable divine ornaments, having all weapons, the divine lord of lakshmi, bhūmi dēvi and nīḷā dēvi, having the divine feet which are always served by ananta, vainatēya et al who are fearing unnecessarily for him, residing in śrīvaikuṇṭam, lord of all, antarātmā (in-dwelling soul) of brahmā and rudra who are his properties, having the nature to unite with those who crave to see him and eliminate their cravings – āḻvār cried out for such emperumān and attained him and became free from sorrow and free from all hurdles; among the thousand pāsurams which came into existence due to āḻvār’s forceful devotion, this decad is born in the form of antādi (ending word in one pāsuram relating to beginning word of next pāsuram) due to āḻvār‘s paramabhakti which makes him unsustainable in separation from emperumān; such āḻvār says “those who are well-versed in this decad, being born in this samsāra, are at par with ayarvaṟum amarargaḷ (nityasūris)”.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Vādhi Kēsari Azhagiya Maṇavāḷa Jīyar:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

**Комментарий. Автор Periyavāccān Piḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction.*

See [nampiḷḷai](http://acharyas.koyil.org/index.php/nampillai/)‘s vyākhyānam.

**Комментарий. Автор Nampiḷḷai:**

*See nanjīyar‘s introduction. avāvaṟaccūḻ ariyai ayanai aranai alaṟṟiavāvaṟṟu vīdu peṟṟa kurugūrc catakōpan sonnaavāvil andādigaḷāl ivai āyiramum mudindaavāvil andādi ippattaṟindār piṟandār uyarndē*

- *avā aṟac cūḻ ariyai* – āḻvār is calling sarvēśvaran who is the benefactor of all desires, with the name hari (which means one who takes away) without any other adjective, since he came and united to eliminate \[fulfil\] āḻvār’s deep affection.
- *ayanai aranai* – One who is the antarātmā for brahmā and rudra who are part of his wealth. avā aṟac cūḻ means – uniting to eliminate the craving of those devotees who crave to see him. By saying “ayanai, aranai” in the context of sāmānādikaraṇyam (multiple aspects/forms having one common substraum), āḻvār decimates the doubt of lordship on brahmā and rudra. Since their nature, existence, activities and inaction are at the disposal of īśvara, their true nature is pāratantriyam (total dependence) only; their control \[over materialistic aspects in this world\] were granted by bhagavān based on their karma. There is another way to explain this to those who cannot understand this principle of sāmānādikaraṇyam. That is – “ayanai – aranai – avā aṟṟu – ariyai alaṟṟi – vīdu peṟṟā” (abandoning the desire for brahmā and rudra, crying out for hari and got liberated), or “ayanai aranai – avā aṟac cūḻ ariyai alaṟṟi, avā aṟṟu vīdu peṟṟa” (Crying out to hari who fulfils the desire of brahmā and rudra by surrounding them, got liberated after having his desire fulfilled).
- *alaṟṟi avā aṟṟu vīdu peṟṟu* – Mercifully spoken by āḻvār, cried out for him, attained him, had all the hurdles eliminated and became free from sorrow.
- *avāvil andādigaḷāl ivai ayiramum* – The thousand pāsurams resulted from āḻvār’s forceful devotion. āḻvār’s śrī maitrēya bhagavān is his avā (desire/affection) \[maitrēya riśi raised questions to parāśara riśi which resulted in śrīviṣṇu purāṇam\]. The thousand pāsurams which were conducted by the teacher, avā. There have been hundred thousand poets after the time of āḻvār; to consider their poems as good as the sound of the ocean and to ignore those poems and to pursue āḻvār’s pāsurams is due to these pāsurams being an outcome of āḻvār’s overwhelming devotion.
- *mudinda avāvil andādi ippattu* – This decad is the result of āḻvār’s paramabhakti which makes him unsustainable \[in separation from bhagavān\]. If īśvaran does not help āḻvār at this stage, his consciousness will be of no use. Up to the previous decad of tiruvāimoḻi 10.9 “sūḻ visumbaṇi mugil”, the pāsurams were conducted by āḻvār’s parabhakt \[clear knowledge about bhagavān\]; sūḻ visumbaṇi mugil decad was conducted by āḻvār’s parajñānam \[visualisation of bhagavān\]; this final decad was conducted by āḻvār’s paramabhakti \[unsustainable in separation\]. For those who are having both bhagavān’s grace and their own effort, at the end of the final body, these parabhakti, parajñānam and paramabhakti will occur; since āḻvār was divinely blessed with “*mayarvaṟa madinalam*” (unblemiśed knowledge and devotion) \[tiruvāimoḻi 1.1.1\], āḻvār experienced these in his lifetime itself. āḻvār’s parabhakti etc were acquired by sarvēśvaran’s mercy which stood in place of bhakti acquired through karma and jñāna.
- *aṟindār piṟandār uyarndē* – Those who are well versed in this decad, are at par with nityasūris, even while being born in this samsāra.
- *piṟandē uyarndār* – The birth of such persons is the same as the incarnation of sarvēśvaran.

With this, the English translation to most beautiful tiruvāimoḻi of the most exalted nammāḻvār, comes to an end.

My heart-felt gratitude to śrīman nārāyaṇan, āḻvārs and ācāryas for using me as an instrument in this enormous task.

This translation effort would not have been possible without the knowledge acquired from gōmatam śrī u vē sampatkumārācāryar’s bhagavat viśaya kālakśēpam. It is also important to recollect vēḷukkudi śrī u vē kriṣṇan svamy’s kālakśēpam (Cḍs) which were very helpful in times of need for clarity.

Special gratitude to puttūr śrī u vē kriṣṇasvāmy iyengār’s publications with arumpada urai (notes) which were very helpful during translation. The value of arumpadam is mostly underrated – but they greatly help in understanding complex aspects in the vyākhyānams.

prapanna vidvān śrīmān puruśōttama nāidu’s eettin tamiḻākkam (tamiḻ translation of eedu) played a significant role in this translation effort. All the pramāṇams are well gathered and explained in tamiḻ, which makes it easier to translate them in to English.

śrī vālmeeki rāmāyaṇam translation site ([http://www.valmikiramayan.net/](http://www.valmikiramayan.net/)) and our own bhagavat gītā site ([http://gita.koyil.org/](http://githa.koyil.org/)) were of significant use.

Finally, I am very thankful to śrī T N kriṣṇan svamy for his proof-reading which eliminated several typos and grammatical errors and his constant support in improving the translations.

Also, I am greatly elated that, by bhagavat sankalpam, this translation effort completed on panguni bharaṇi, on the monthly tirunakśatram of asmadācāryan, śrīmat paramahamsētyādi pattarpirān vānamāmalai rāmānuja jīyar, exactly one month before his annual tirunakśatram, citrai bharaṇi. Without his blessings, this would not have been possible.

Praying to emperumān, āḻvārs and ācāryas for more such kainkaryams.
